For if what he says, reads or hears concerns the torments or the forsaking of the wicked, he can conceive from it a holy fear, lest he too suffer the like; or thanksgiving and the kindling of love, because he sees that by God's mercy he has been preserved from such things; or a good sadness, if he considers that he has fallen into such evils as deserved to be tormented and forsaken for. But if what he says or hears concerns the perfection and beatitude of the just, he can be fired to imitate them and strengthened to hope.

paras.t: Igitur secundum hunc sensum dicat devotus vel pœnitens seu alius quilibet: Beatus vir qui non abiit in consilio impiorum: hocque dicendo, proponat nunquam malo consilio assentire; pœniteat quoque se unquam perversis consiliis acquievisse; et oret Deum ut in omnibus se dirigat ad inveniendum, et consentiendum sanis consiliis, sicut Tobias docet: Omni tempore benedic Deum, et pete ab eo ut viam tuam dirigat, et omnia consilia tua in ipso permaneant. Indigemus namque, ad hoc quod non abeamus in consilio impiorum, illuminari ac dirigi a Spiritu Sancto dono consilii, quemadmodum Sapiens dicit: Quis hominum potest scire consilium Dei? aut quis poterit cogitare quid velit Deus, nisi tu, Domine, dederis sapientiam, et miseris Spiritum tuum de cœlis?
paras.en: According to this sense, then, let the devout man, or the penitent, or anyone else say: [[1:1|Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly|Beatus vir qui non abiit in consilio impiorum]]; and in saying this let him purpose never to assent to evil counsel; let him also repent of ever having given way to perverse counsels; and let him pray God to direct him in all things to find sound counsels and consent to them, as Tobias teaches: [[Tob 4:20|Bless God at all times: and desire of him to direct thy ways, and that all thy counsels may abide in him|Omni tempore benedic Deum, et pete ab eo ut viam tuam dirigat, et omnia consilia tua in ipso permaneant]]. For, so as not to walk in the counsel of the ungodly, we need to be enlightened and directed by the Holy Ghost through the gift of counsel, as the Wise man says: [[Wis 9:13|who among men is he that can know the counsel of God? or who can think what the will of God is?|Quis hominum potest scire consilium Dei? aut quis poterit cogitare quid velit Deus]] [[Wis 9:17|except thou give wisdom, and send thy holy Spirit from above|nisi tu, Domine, dederis sapientiam, et miseris Spiritum tuum de cœlis?]]? [Denis joins Wis 9:13 to 9:17, as the margin notes, and reads “O Lord” and “thy Spirit from heaven”.]

paras.t: Per hunc modum formare debet homo suum affectum in singulis quæ sequuntur, secundum exigentiam singulorum verborum: sicut quum dicit, Et in via peccatorum non stetit, cogitet de cetero non peccare, et de operatione mala præterita doleat. Dum vero dicit, Et in cathedra pestilentiæ non sedit, proponat nullum inficere, nullum scandalizare, ne perdat animam ejus pro quo Christus mori dignatus est. Simili modo quum dicit, Sed in lege Domini voluntas ejus, studeat omnes evagationes abjicere, affectum suum a caducis rebus abstrahere, et ad divinæ legis observantiam omne desiderium suum erigere. Et ut ista adimpleat, bene advertat, et pro viribus agere studeat quod sequitur, Et in lege ejus meditabitur die ac nocte; hocque dicendo, omnes infructuosas et malas mentis suæ occupationes repellat, atque divinis meditationibus cor suum implere semper laboret, quemadmodum Dominus ait: Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis.
paras.en: In this way a man should form his affections in each of the things that follow, as each of the words requires. So when he says, [[1:1|nor stood in the way of sinners|Et in via peccatorum non stetit]], let him think of sinning no more, and grieve over his past evil-doing. When he says, [[1:1|nor sat in the chair of pestilence|Et in cathedra pestilentiæ non sedit]], let him purpose to infect no one, to scandalize no one, lest he destroy the soul of one for whom Christ deigned to die[[Rom 14:15||]]. In like manner, when he says, [[1:2|But his will is in the law of the Lord|Sed in lege Domini voluntas ejus]], let him strive to cast off all wanderings, to draw his affections away from perishable things, and to raise all his desire to the keeping of the divine law. And to fulfil this, let him pay good heed to what follows, and strive with all his strength to do it: [[1:2|and on his law he shall meditate day and night|Et in lege ejus meditabitur die ac nocte]]; and in saying this let him drive away all the fruitless and evil occupations of his mind, and labour always to fill his heart with divine meditations, as the Lord says: [[Is 1:16|take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]].

paras.t: Porro dum psallit, Et erit tanquam lignum quod plantatum est secus decursus aquarum, oret, cordialiterque desideret, ut sit sicut arbor bona, quæ bonos fructus facit: quatenus bene vivendo, alios verbo et exemplo ædificet, et non tam loquendo quam operando informet, ut illud Salvatoris adimpleat: Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant bona facta vestra, et glorificent Patrem vestrum qui in cœlis est. Dum vero ait, Et folium ejus non defluet, proponat se semper loquendo modestum et cautum habere. Quumque adjungit, Et omnia quæcumque faciet, prosperabuntur, cupiat in eorum consortio numerari, de quibus ait Apostolus: Scimus quoniam diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum.
paras.en: Further, when he sings, [[1:3|And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters|Et erit tanquam lignum quod plantatum est secus decursus aquarum]], let him pray and desire from his heart to be like a good tree that bears good fruit: so that by living well he may edify others by word and example, and form them not so much by speaking as by doing, and so fulfil that saying of the Saviour: [[Matt 5:16|So let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven|Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant bona facta vestra, et glorificent Patrem vestrum qui in cœlis est]]. When he says, [[1:3|And his leaf shall not fall off|Et folium ejus non defluet]], let him purpose always to keep himself modest and careful in speaking. And when he adds, [[1:3|and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper|Et omnia quæcumque faciet, prosperabuntur]], let him desire to be numbered in the company of those of whom the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:28|we know that to them that love God all things work together unto good|Scimus quoniam diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum]].

paras.t: Ex his vero quæ sequuntur, Non sic impii, non sic, solicitus fiat, ne ea quæ de impiis scripta sunt, sibi conveniant; sed in judicio discretionis a peccatis resurgat, et in consilio justorum permanere conetur.
paras.en: And from the words that follow, [[1:4|Not so the wicked, not so|Non sic impii, non sic]], let him become anxious lest what is written of the wicked should fit him; but let him rise again from his sins in the judgment of discernment, and strive to remain in the counsel of the just.

1.title: Expositio ejusdem primi psalmi secundum anagogicum intellectum
1.title_en: Exposition of the same first psalm according to the anagogical sense

paras.t: Anagogice insuper hic psalmus exponi potest, videlicet de comprehensoribus seu Beatis in patria, ut sciamus ex hujus psalmi expositione, quid de nobis ipsis sperare debeamus.
paras.en: This psalm can also be expounded anagogically [that is, of the life to come], namely of those who have attained, the Blessed in the fatherland, so that from the exposition of this psalm we may know what we ought to hope for ourselves.

paras.t: Ait ergo Scriptura: Beatus vir qui non abiit in consilio impiorum. Vir, hoc loco non a sexu, sed a cordis vigore vocatur: et ita angeli sancti viri dici possunt, quoniam ad omnia divina opera exercenda viriles atque fortissimi sunt. Unde de angelis dicitur: Ecce duo viri adstiterunt juxta illos. Et Gregorius: Angelus, inquit, rationale est animal, non quod sit materialis aut sensitivæ naturæ, sed propter intellectualem perfectionem. Angeli autem sancti non abierunt in consilio impiorum, quia non consenserunt consilio Luciferi atque cadentium angelorum. Nullus quoque Beatorum hominum abiit in consilio impiorum, in ipso finaliter permanendo, sed ab hac vita in bona dispositione discessit.
paras.en: Scripture says, then: [[1:1|Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly|Beatus vir qui non abiit in consilio impiorum]]. *Man* here is said not from sex but from vigour of heart: and so the holy angels can be called men, since they are manly and most strong for carrying out all divine works. Hence it is said of angels: [[Acts 1:10|behold two men stood by them|Ecce duo viri adstiterunt juxta illos]]. And Gregory: An angel, he says, is a rational animal, not because he is of a material or sensitive nature, but because of his intellectual perfection. And the holy angels did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, since they did not consent to the counsel of Lucifer and the falling angels. Nor did any of the blessed among men walk in the counsel of the ungodly by remaining in it to the end; but each departed this life in a good disposition.

paras.t: Itaque, Beatus vir, omnis electus, in virtutibus fortis, homo vel angelus, Deo jam feliciter fruens, qui non abiit in consilio impiorum, ruentium scilicet angelorum, aut hominum perversorum. Et in via peccatorum non stetit, id est, cum Lucifero aliisque Deo rebellibus non peccavit, contra Creatorem superbiendo, seu ejus similitudinem temerarie et præsumptuose ambiendo. Et in cathedra pestilentiæ non sedit, id est, alios ad peccandum non induxit, quemadmodum Lucifer et infectores proximorum suorum. Sed in lege Domini voluntas ejus. Hoc universis Beatis in patria plenissime convenit, quia præceptum de dilectione Dei perfectissime implent, et toto affectu ad Deum conversi sunt, eique inavertibiliter semper adhærent. Et in lege ejus, id est in præcepto quod ipsis a Deo præfixum est in diligendo et operando: in hac lege meditantur die ac nocte, id est in ævo, quod omne tempus includit, considerantes incessabiliter qualiter Deo reverenter adsistant, prompte obediant, atque in omnibus ordinem suum custodiant.
paras.en: So, [[1:1|Blessed is the man|Beatus vir]]: every elect one, strong in virtues, man or angel, already happily enjoying God, [[1:1|who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly|qui non abiit in consilio impiorum]], namely of the angels who fell, or of perverse men. [[1:1|nor stood in the way of sinners|Et in via peccatorum non stetit]], that is, did not sin with Lucifer and the others who rebelled against God, by being proud against the Creator, or by rashly and presumptuously reaching after likeness to him. [[1:1|nor sat in the chair of pestilence|Et in cathedra pestilentiæ non sedit]], that is, did not lead others into sin, as Lucifer did, and those who infect their neighbours. [[1:2|But his will is in the law of the Lord|Sed in lege Domini voluntas ejus]]. This befits all the Blessed in the fatherland most fully, since they fulfil the precept of the love of God most perfectly, and are turned to God with their whole affection, and cleave to him always without turning away. [[1:2|and on his law|Et in lege ejus]], that is, on the precept set them by God in loving and working: on this law [[1:2|he shall meditate day and night|meditantur die ac nocte]] [Denis paraphrases: *meditantur*, "they meditate"], that is, in eternity [*ævum*: the duration proper to angels and the blessed], which includes all time, considering without ceasing how they may stand reverently before God, obey promptly, and keep their order in all things.

paras.t: Et erit tanquam lignum, etc. Omnis Beatus Deo jam fruens, ligno juxta aquarum decursus plantato optime comparatur, quoniam inebriatur torrente divinæ voluptatis: sicque copiosissimum fructum affert, quia indesinenter sanctissimis actionibus occupatur, et nunquam otiosus aut infecundus est, sed in continua Divinitatis contemplatione ac dilectione æternaliter permanet. Et folium ejus non defluet, id est, laudatio qua Deum honorat, nunquam cessabit. Et omnia quæcumque faciet, prosperabuntur, id est, ad divinum honorem infallibiliter ordinantur; nec potest aliquid adversitatis eis accidere, sed perpetua securitate Deo conjuncti sunt.
paras.en: [[1:3|And he shall be like a tree|Et erit tanquam lignum]], etc. Every blessed one who already enjoys God is very well compared to a tree planted by the running waters, since he is inebriated with the torrent of divine pleasure[[35:9||]]: and so he bears most abundant fruit, since he is unceasingly busied with most holy actions, and is never idle or unfruitful, but abides eternally in the continual contemplation and love of the Godhead. [[1:3|And his leaf shall not fall off|Et folium ejus non defluet]], that is, the praise with which he honours God will never cease. [[1:3|and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper|Et omnia quæcumque faciet, prosperabuntur]], that is, they are ordered unfailingly to the honour of God; nor can any adversity befall them, but they are joined to God in everlasting security.

paras.t: Non sic impii, non sic: id est, apostatæ angeli hominesque injusti, non sic, id est, non sunt beati sicut jam de angelis et sanctis hominibus dictum est. Sed sunt tanquam pulvis quem projicit ventus a facie terræ. Nam angeli mali statim quum peccaverunt, cœlo projecti sunt, sicut in Evangelio ait Salvator: Videbam satanam sicut fulgur de cœlo cadentem. Et Isaias: Quomodo, inquit, cecidisti, Lucifer, qui mane oriebaris? Ideo non resurgunt impii in judicio. Dæmones enim non pœnitent, sed sunt obstinati in malo, sicut et omnes damnati. Ideo non resurgunt a sua pessima voluntate in judicio discretionis, se ipsos discutiendo et corrigendo. Quoniam novit Dominus viam justorum. Nam omnis operatio Beatorum in patria, Deo semper gratissima est et summe accepta. Et iter impiorum peribit. Iter cadentium angelorum, fuit desiderium ascendendi ad similitudinem Dei immoderate. Sed hoc iter, seu talis superbia peribit, quia nunquam adipiscentur quod adipisci optabant.
paras.en: [[1:4|Not so the wicked|Non sic impii]], [[1:4|not so|non sic]]: that is, the apostate angels and unjust men are [[1:4|not so|non sic]], that is, they are not blessed as has just been said of the angels and holy men. [[1:4|but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth|Sed sunt tanquam pulvis quem projicit ventus a facie terræ]]. For the bad angels, as soon as they sinned, were cast out of heaven, as the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Luke 10:18|I saw Satan like lightning falling from heaven|Videbam satanam sicut fulgur de cœlo cadentem]]. And Isaias: [[Is 14:12|How art thou fallen|Quomodo, inquit, cecidisti]], he says, [[Is 14:12|O Lucifer, who didst rise in the morning?|Lucifer, qui mane oriebaris]] [[1:5|Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment|Ideo non resurgunt impii in judicio]]. For the demons do not repent, but are obstinate in evil, as are all the damned. Therefore they do not rise from their most wicked will in the judgment of discernment, by examining and correcting themselves. [[1:6|For the Lord knoweth the way of the just|Quoniam novit Dominus viam justorum]]. For every work of the Blessed in the fatherland is always most pleasing to God and supremely accepted. [[1:6|and the way of the wicked shall perish|Et iter impiorum peribit]]. The way of the falling angels was the desire to climb immoderately to the likeness of God. But this way, that is, such pride, will perish, since they will never obtain what they longed to obtain.

paras.t: Porro ad hanc beatitudinem electorum in patria nos quoque perventuros speramus, si ea pro posse nostro quæ ipsi fecerunt, agamus, videlicet non abeundo in consilio impiorum, nec stando in via peccatorum, nec sedendo in cathedra pestilentiæ.
paras.en: Now we too hope to come to this blessedness of the elect in the fatherland, if we do, as far as we can, what they did: namely by not walking in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standing in the way of sinners, nor sitting in the chair of pestilence.

paras.t: Precatio. Auctor omnium bonorum Deus, reple nos, quæsumus, gratia tua, ut voluntas nostra dirigatur semper in lege tua; quatenus te inspirante, die ac nocte in ea sic meditemur, ut fructum æternæ felicitatis percipere mereamur.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, author of all good things, fill us, we beseech thee, with thy grace, that our will may be ever directed in thy law; so that by thy inspiration we may so meditate on it day and night as to deserve to receive the fruit of eternal happiness.

2.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SECUNDI: QUARE FREMUERUNT GENTES, ETC.
2.title_en: Literal exposition of the second Psalm: Why have the Gentiles raged, etc.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi nunc exponendi talis est: Psalmus David. Considerandum est autem (ut ait Hieronymus) quod liber Psalmorum est quasi magna domus, plures habens cellas sive cubicula, et quælibet cella propriam habet clavem ac januam. Ostium vero totius domus istius, est primus psalmus, cujus clavis est Spiritus Sanctus. Ceteri autem psalmi tanquam speciales cellulæ, proprias habent claves, id est titulos appropriatos. Nam sicut se habet clavis ad domum, et signum ad hospitium, ita se habent tituli psalmorum ad psalmos, quia per eos datur introitus ad intellectum psalmorum.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be expounded is this: A Psalm of David. Now it is to be considered (as Jerome says) that the book of Psalms is like a great house, having many cells or chambers, and each cell has its own key and door. The entrance of this whole house is the first psalm, whose key is the Holy Ghost. The other psalms, like particular little cells, have their own keys, that is, the titles proper to them. For as a key stands to a house, and a sign to an inn, so the titles of the psalms stand to the psalms, because through them entrance is given to the understanding of the psalms.

paras.t: Porro titulus psalmi præsentis varie explanatur, prout psalmus hic diversis modis exponitur. Quidam enim ipsum exponunt ad litteram de populo Judæorum a captivitate Babylonica redeuntium. Alii vero, de ipso David, asserentes David fecisse hunc psalmum ad laudem Dei propter victoriam Philistinorum, quos ipse devicit, quando ascenderunt contra eum, eo quod audissent eum unctum in regem totius Israeliticæ plebis. Et quamvis hic psalmus ad hunc sensum aliquo modo exponi posset ac trahi, hoc tamen improprie fit. Nam quod sequitur, Dominus dixit ad me, Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te, nec populo Judæorum, nec David proprie competit, maxime si profunde atque subtiliter exponatur, sicut patebit. Denique, si verum est quod Nicolaus de Lyra refert, nec omnes Judæorum magistri psalmum istum ita exponunt. Narrat enim Rabbi Salomonem, maximum Judæorum doctorem modernum, circa hunc psalmum testari ac dicere: Majores nostri hunc psalmum exposuerunt de rege Messia seu Christo, sed propter hæreticos exponatur de David. Vocat autem hæreticos, Judæos ad fidem Christi conversos. Unde patet quod ipse hunc psalmum exponit de David, ad evadendum argumenta quæ Judæi conversi sumpserunt ex psalmo isto pro christianæ fidei approbatione.
paras.en: Further, the title of the present psalm is explained in various ways, according as the psalm itself is expounded in different ways. For some expound it literally of the Jewish people returning from the Babylonian captivity. Others expound it of David himself, asserting that David made this psalm in praise of God for the victory over the Philistines, whom he overcame when they came up against him because they had heard that he was anointed king of the whole people of Israel. And although this psalm could in some way be expounded and drawn to this sense, it is done improperly. For what follows, [[2:7|The Lord hath said to me: Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee|Dominus dixit ad me, Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te]], does not properly fit either the Jewish people or David, above all if it is expounded deeply and subtly, as will be clear. Moreover, if what Nicholas of Lyra reports is true, not all the masters of the Jews expound this psalm so either. For he relates that Rabbi Salomon, the greatest of the modern doctors of the Jews, testifies and says of this psalm: Our elders expounded this psalm of the king Messias, that is, Christ; but because of the heretics let it be expounded of David. And by heretics he means the Jews converted to the faith of Christ. Hence it is plain that he expounds this psalm of David in order to escape the arguments which the converted Jews drew from this psalm in proof of the Christian faith.

paras.t: Verumtamen, quidquid sit de istis, nullum christianum expositorem decet vel licet hunc psalmum ad litteram exponere, nisi de Christo. Nam Act. iv, et ad Hebr. i, inducitur psalmus iste ad fidem probandam. Probatio autem fidei per sacram Scripturam, non valet ex sensu mystico, sed litterali dumtaxat, quemadmodum in epistola contra Vincentium Donatistam adstruit Augustinus.
paras.en: However that may be, it is neither fitting nor lawful for any Christian expositor to expound this psalm literally except of Christ. For in Acts 4[[Acts 4:25||]] and in Hebrews 1[[Heb 1:5||]] this psalm is brought in to prove the faith [the margin's verse for Hebrews is half read; it is Heb 1:5 that quotes this psalm]. And proof of the faith from sacred Scripture holds good only from the literal sense, not from the mystical, as Augustine establishes in the letter against Vincent the Donatist.

paras.t: Itaque, psalmum hunc de Christo litteraliter exponendo, titulus ejus prædictus sic intelligendus est: Psalmus, id est tractatus iste, qui dicitur psalmus, quoniam ad bene operandum hortatur, attribuitur David, id est Christo. David enim, manu fortis vel desiderabilis adspectu interpretatur: et hoc Christo potissimum convenit, quum ipse sit Dominus virtutum, qui principem hujus mundi devicit, et speciosus forma præ filiis hominum consistit.
paras.en: So, in expounding this psalm literally of Christ, its title given above is to be understood thus: A Psalm, that is, this treatise, which is called a psalm because it exhorts us to do good, is ascribed to David, that is, to Christ. For David is interpreted “strong of hand” or “desirable to behold”: and this befits Christ above all, since he is [[Ps 23:10|the Lord of hosts|Dominus virtutum]] [*Dominus virtutum*: literally “Lord of powers”, which Denis links with “strong of hand”], who overcame the prince of this world[[John 12:31||]], and is [[Ps 44:3|beautiful above the sons of men|speciosus forma præ filiis hominum]].

paras.t: Sanctus ergo David, Spiritu Sancto revelante prænoscens impietatem malignorum, Christum persequentium et occidentium, quasi admirans eorum malitiam, dicit: Quare fremuerunt gentes? id est, cur gentiles, cur Romani milites, cur Herodis ac Pilati ministri, tanquam feræ seu bestiæ, irrationabiliter malignati ac moti sunt, et hoc contra Filium Dei? Et populi, id est filii Israel, ad quos specialiter missus est Christus, meditati sunt inania, utpote cogitantes consilia quæ non potuerunt stabilire? Volebant namque exstinguere nomen Domini Jesu, interficiendo eum sicut seductorem et impium, quemadmodum de eis scriptum est: Mittamus (inquiunt) lignum in panem ejus, et eradamus eum de terra viventium. Sed hujus oppositum accidit, quia post mortem Christi, nomen ejus ubique innotuit, et fides ejus per totum mundum diffusa est. Unde et ipse ante passionem dixit: Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum.
paras.en: Holy David, then, foreknowing by the revelation of the Holy Ghost the impiety of the wicked who would persecute and kill Christ, and as it were marvelling at their malice, says: [[2:1|Why have the Gentiles raged|Quare fremuerunt gentes]]? that is, why have the Gentiles, why have the Roman soldiers, why have the servants of Herod and of Pilate, like wild beasts, been moved with unreasoning malice, and that against the Son of God? [[2:1|and the people|Et populi]], that is, the children of Israel, to whom Christ was specially sent, [[2:1|devised vain things|meditati sunt inania]], inasmuch as [[Ps 20:12|they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish|cogitantes consilia quæ non potuerunt stabilire?]]? For they wished to blot out the name of the Lord Jesus by killing him as a seducer and an impious man, as it is written of them: [[Jer 11:19|Let us put|Mittamus]] (they say) [[Jer 11:19|wood on his bread, and cut him off from the land of the living|lignum in panem ejus, et eradamus eum de terra viventium]]. But the opposite of this came about, because after the death of Christ his name became known everywhere, and his faith was spread through the whole world. Hence he himself said before his passion: [[John 12:32|if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]].

paras.t: Adstiterunt reges terræ, et principes convenerunt in unum, adversus Dominum et adversus Christum ejus. Qui sunt isti reges, nisi Herodes qui Jesum adhuc infantulum perimere voluit, atque Herodes qui eumdem cum exercitu suo sprevit, ac veste alba illusum ad Pilatum remisit? Et qui sunt principes isti, nisi Annas et Caiphas ac Pilatus? Qui convenerunt adversus Dominum, id est Deum Patrem, et adversus Christum ejus, id est Filium ejus unigenitum ac dilectum. Dicitur autem uterque Herodes adstitisse contra Christum: non quia eodem tempore adstiterunt, quum tempore passionis primus Herodes obierit; sed quoniam pari malitia et infidelitate contra Christum commoti sunt.
paras.en: [[2:2|The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, against the Lord, and against his Christ|Adstiterunt reges terræ, et principes convenerunt in unum, adversus Dominum et adversus Christum ejus]]. Who are these kings but Herod, who sought to kill Jesus while still a little child[[Matt 2:16||]], and the Herod who with his army set him at nought and, mocking him in a white garment, sent him back to Pilate[[Luke 23:11||]]? And who are these princes but Annas and Caiphas and Pilate[[John 11:47||]] [the margin reads Joann. xi, 4… et seq.; the council of the chief priests is at 11:47]? They met together [[2:2|against the Lord|adversus Dominum]], that is, God the Father, [[2:2|and against his Christ|et adversus Christum ejus]], that is, his only-begotten and beloved Son. Both Herods are said to have stood up against Christ, not because they stood up at the same time, since the first Herod had died by the time of the passion, but because they were stirred up against Christ with equal malice and unbelief.

paras.t: Consequenter ponuntur verba regum ac principum horum, dum subditur: Dirumpamus vincula eorum, id est, destruamus legem ac religionem Patris et Filii, occidendo Christum, et ejus doctrinam reprobando. Hoc dixerunt, non quod agnoverint Jesum esse Filium Dei agnitione certa et stabili, vel quia putaverint eum, qui Jesum occideret, Deo resistere: si enim cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent; sed et Jesum tanquam blasphemum et seductorem interfecerunt, arbitrantes obsequium se præstare Deo. Verumtamen ista ignorantia eos nequaquam excusat, quoniam excæcavit eos malitia eorum, nec voluerunt credere divinis miraculis. Quomodo ergo impii isti dixerunt, Dirumpamus vincula eorum, nisi quoniam ille quem ipsi occiderunt tanquam impium, vere Filius Dei erat, cui qui resistit, Patri quoque resistit? Qui enim non honorificat Filium, non honorificat Patrem qui misit illum. Bene autem per vincula intelliguntur lex Dei atque religio, quia per legem refrenantur et constringuntur iniqui, ne peccatis habenas relaxent. Religio etiam a religando vel ligando vocatur, quoniam religat hominem a mundo, et ligat eum sub divino obsequio. Et projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum, id est, non obediamus Dei Patris et Christi præceptis. Noluerunt enim prædicti reges et principes Christi saluberrimis consentire doctrinis.
paras.en: Next the words of these kings and princes are set down, when it is added: [[2:3|Let us break their bonds asunder|Dirumpamus vincula eorum]], that is, let us destroy the law and religion of the Father and the Son, by killing Christ and rejecting his teaching. They said this, not because they acknowledged Jesus to be the Son of God with a sure and settled knowledge, or because they thought that whoever killed Jesus would be resisting God: for [[1 Cor 2:8|if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory|si enim cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent]] [the margin reads I Cor. v, 8; the words are those of 1 Cor 2:8]; but they put Jesus to death as a blasphemer[[Matt 9:3||]] and a seducer[[Matt 27:63||]], thinking that they were doing God a service[[John 16:2||]]. Yet this ignorance in no way excuses them, since [[Wis 2:21|their own malice blinded them|excæcavit eos malitia eorum]] [the margin reads Sap. v, 21; the words are those of Wis 2:21], and they would not believe the divine miracles. How, then, did these wicked men say, [[2:3|Let us break their bonds asunder|Dirumpamus vincula eorum]], unless because he whom they killed as an impious man was truly the Son of God[[Mark 15:39||]], and whoever resists him resists the Father too? For [[John 5:23|He who honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father who hath sent him|Qui enim non honorificat Filium, non honorificat Patrem qui misit illum]]. And by bonds are well understood the law of God and religion, because by the law the wicked are reined in and bound, so that they do not give the rein to sins. And religion is named from binding again, or binding [*religio* from *religare*, *ligare*], since it binds a man back from the world and binds him under the service of God. [[2:3|and let us cast away their yoke from us|Et projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum]], that is, let us not obey the precepts of God the Father and of Christ. For these kings and princes would not consent to Christ's most wholesome teachings.

paras.t: Qui habitat in cœlis irridebit eos. Hic ponitur merces seu præmium malitiæ hominum prædictorum. Qui habitat in cœlis irridebit eos: id est, Deus justus judex, qui habitat in puris sanctisque cordibus, resuscitando Filium suum a mortuis tertia die, ostendet illos irrisione dignos. Item irridebit eos in die finalis judicii. Et Dominus subsannabit eos. Mos est sacræ Scripturæ, secundum Augustinum, ut idem sub aliis verbis resumat, quatenus veritas clarius innotescat, et audientes sive legentes magis attendant. Ita nunc fit. Quod enim prædixit, Qui habitat in cœlis irridebit eos, nunc repetit dicens, Et Dominus subsannabit eos: demonstrando eos omni contemptu dignissimos, quum converterit malignitatem eorum in caput ipsorum, feceritque evenire omnino contrarium machinationi ipsorum. Unde Sapientia ait de impiis: Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo et subsannabo, quum vobis quod timebatis evenerit. Dicitur autem Deus irridere et subsannare, non corporali motu vel modo carnali, sed propter similitudinem operis, seu ratione effectus: videlicet quia talem pœnam infligit, sicut irrisor et subsannator.
paras.en: [[2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them|Qui habitat in cœlis irridebit eos]]. Here the wages or reward of the malice of the men spoken of is set down. [[2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them|Qui habitat in cœlis irridebit eos]]: that is, God the just judge, who dwells in pure and holy hearts, by raising his Son from the dead on the third day, will show them worthy of derision. He will also laugh at them in the day of the final judgment. [[2:4|and the Lord shall deride them|Et Dominus subsannabit eos]]. It is the way of sacred Scripture, according to Augustine, to take up the same thing again in other words, so that the truth may become more clearly known, and hearers or readers may pay closer heed. So it is here. For what it said before, [[2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them|Qui habitat in cœlis irridebit eos]], it now repeats, saying, [[2:4|and the Lord shall deride them|Et Dominus subsannabit eos]]: showing them most worthy of all contempt, when he shall have turned their malice upon their own head[[Ps 7:17||]] and made the very opposite of their scheming come about. Hence Wisdom says of the wicked: [[Prov 1:26|I also will laugh in your destruction, and will mock when that shall come to you which you feared|Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo et subsannabo, quum vobis quod timebatis evenerit]]. God is said to laugh and to deride, not by bodily movement or in a fleshly way, but by a likeness of the work, or by reason of the effect: namely, because he inflicts such a penalty as one who laughs and derides would.

paras.t: Tunc, videlicet quando irridebit eos, loquetur ad eos in ira sua. Hoc in die extremi judicii maxime fiet, quando tota Trinitas judicabit auctoritative, et Christus ut homo ministerialiter et exsecutive. Tunc tota Trinitas dicet reprobis per Christum qui sententiam proferet: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Potest quoque exponi de locutione, qua locutus est malis et reprobis per Apostolos sanctosque prædicatores: per quos loquitur Dominus in ira sua, quando foris facit reprobis prædicari verbum Dei, sed intus non aperit corda ipsorum, nec tangit affectum; sed exigentibus culpis ipsorum, indurat eos, et obstinatos relinquit. Sic loquebatur Judæis incredulis per sanctos Apostolos. Et in furore suo conturbabit eos. Hoc in Judæis Christum occidentibus videmus impletum, quia a tempore destructionis eorum a Tito et Vespasiano, de terra promissionis ejecti sunt, et multis ærumnis oppressi. In die quoque universalis judicii conturbabit eos, quando in ignem projicientur, ubi (ut ait Job) umbra mortis et nullus ordo, sed sempiternus horror inhabitat.
paras.en: [[2:5|Then|Tunc]], namely when he shall laugh at them, [[2:5|shall he speak to them in his anger|loquetur ad eos in ira sua]]. This will be done above all in the day of the last judgment, when the whole Trinity will judge with authority, and Christ as man by ministry and execution. Then the whole Trinity will say to the reprobate, through Christ, who will pronounce the sentence: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]] [Denis reads *Ite*, “Go”, for *Discedite a me*, “Depart from me”]. It can also be expounded of the speech by which he spoke to the wicked and reprobate through the Apostles and holy preachers: through them the Lord speaks in his anger when he has the word of God preached to the reprobate outwardly, but does not open their hearts within or touch their affections; rather, as their sins deserve, he hardens them and leaves them obstinate. So he spoke to the unbelieving Jews through the holy Apostles. [[2:5|and trouble them in his rage|Et in furore suo conturbabit eos]]. This we see fulfilled in the Jews who killed Christ, because from the time of their destruction by Titus and Vespasian they were cast out of the land of promise and oppressed with many miseries. In the day of the universal judgment too he will trouble them, when they shall be cast into the fire, where (as Job says) [[Job 10:22|the shadow of death, and no order, but everlasting horror dwelleth|umbra mortis et nullus ordo, sed sempiternus horror inhabitat]].

paras.t: Consequenter inducit Propheta verba Christi, de se ita dicentis: Ego autem: tanquam dicat, Illi hoc modo peribunt, Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo. Christus in quantum Deus, plenam habet auctoritatem omnium creaturarum: nec sic constituitur rex super aliquid, sed ipse cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto est unus et idem omnium rerum creator ac Dominus, judex et rex; sed prout homo est, sic data est ei omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra, sicut Matthæus scribit. Sic etiam constitutus est rex ab eo, scilicet Deo Patre, imo a tota superbeatissima Trinitate, cujus opera sunt indivisa. Super Sion montem sanctum ejus, id est super populum Israel, illum præsertim qui credidit: qui dicitur mons, propter legis sublimitatem et gratiam electionis. Omnes quippe Prophetæ Messiam appellant regem Israel. Vel per Sion, quod interpretatur speculatio, intelligenda est Ecclesia militans, id est populus christianus Christum contemplans, et ejus lege, fide ac gratia sublimatus præ ceteris gentibus, sicut mons elevatur super circumjacentes terræ partes. Prædicans præceptum ejus, id est, legem evangelicam docens, primo per me ipsum, deinde per Apostolos Spiritu Sancto repletos. In isto versu tactum est de humana Christi natura: in sequenti agitur de ejus divina natura ac generatione æterna, dum dicitur:
paras.en: Next the Prophet brings in the words of Christ, speaking thus of himself: [[2:6|But I|Ego autem]]: as if to say, They will perish in this way, [[2:6|But I am appointed king by him|Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo]]. Christ, as God, has full authority over all creatures: and in that way he is not appointed king over anything, but he himself, with the Father and the Holy Ghost, is one and the same Creator and Lord, judge and king of all things. But as he is man, so all power is given to him in heaven and on earth, as Matthew writes[[Matt 28:18||]]. So too he is appointed king by him, namely by God the Father, nay, by the whole most superblessed Trinity, whose works are undivided. [[2:6|over Sion, his holy mountain|Super Sion montem sanctum ejus]], that is, over the people of Israel, above all that part of it which believed: which is called a mountain because of the loftiness of the law and the grace of election. For all the Prophets call the Messias the king of Israel. Or by Sion, which is interpreted “watch-tower” [*speculatio*: a looking-out, contemplation], is to be understood the Church militant, that is, the Christian people contemplating Christ, and raised by his law, faith and grace above the other nations, as a mountain is raised above the lands that lie round about it. [[2:6|preaching his commandment|Prædicans præceptum ejus]], that is, teaching the law of the Gospel, first through myself, and then through the Apostles filled with the Holy Ghost. In this verse the human nature of Christ is touched on; in the next his divine nature and eternal generation are treated, when it is said:

paras.t: Dominus, scilicet Deus Pater, dixit ad me, scilicet Jesum Christum: Filius meus es tu. Hoc in baptizatione et transfiguratione Christi dictum esse a Patre ad Filium, ex Evangelio constat. Et dicitur Christus Filius Dei, non ut ceteri Sancti per gratiam adoptionis, sed Filius per identitatem naturæ, seu unitatem essentiæ: quoniam ex substantia Patris est genitus ab æterno. Et ideo additur: Ego hodie genui te, id est in die æternitatis: in qua non est prius et posterius, novum vel vetus, mutatio vel vicissitudinis obumbratio; sed dies ista est ipsamet æternitas, quæ est interminabilis vitæ tota simul perfecta possessio. Ista æternitas omne tempus comprehendit, atque per omnem temporis differentiam significatur: quia dicimus, Deus fuit, Deus est, Deus erit; convenientius tamen designatur per præsens tempus, quod habet se per modum quieti et fixi. Volens ergo Propheta æternam Christi generationem subtiliter insinuare, usus est tempore præsenti, dicens, Ego hodie genui te: quæ sunt verba Patris ad Filium. Quidquid enim Pater agit et scit, hoc Filio dicit: et generando dicit, quoniam generando dat Filio divinam essentiam: quam dando, dat omnis veritatis notitiam, quum divina essentia sit ipsa sapientia, cujus non est numerus.
paras.en: [[2:7|The Lord|Dominus]], namely God the Father, [[2:7|hath said to me|dixit ad me]], namely to Jesus Christ: [[2:7|Thou art my son|Filius meus es tu]]. That this was said by the Father to the Son at the baptism[[Matt 3:17||]] and the transfiguration[[Matt 17:5||]] of Christ is clear from the Gospel. And Christ is called the Son of God, not as the other Saints are, by the grace of adoption, but Son by identity of nature, or unity of essence, since he is begotten of the substance of the Father from eternity. And therefore it is added: [[2:7|this day have I begotten thee|Ego hodie genui te]], that is, in the day of eternity, in which there is no before and after, new or old, change or [[Jas 1:17|shadow of alteration|vicissitudinis obumbratio]]; but this day is eternity itself, which is the whole, simultaneous and perfect possession of unending life [Boethius's definition of eternity, *Consolation of Philosophy* V]. This eternity takes in all time, and is signified by every difference of time, for we say, God was, God is, God will be; yet it is more fittingly signified by the present tense, which is in the manner of something at rest and fixed. The Prophet, then, wishing to hint subtly at the eternal generation of Christ, used the present tense [*hodie*, “today”], saying, [[2:7|this day have I begotten thee|Ego hodie genui te]]: which are the words of the Father to the Son. For whatever the Father does and knows, he tells to the Son; and he tells it by begetting, since by begetting he gives the Son the divine essence; and in giving it he gives the knowledge of all truth, since the divine essence is wisdom itself, [[Ps 146:5|of his wisdom there is no number|cujus non est numerus]].

paras.t: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam. Verba sunt Patris ad Christum hominem, cui non competit postulare a Patre secundum quod Deus. Dicit ergo ad Filium incarnatum Deus Pater: O Fili, postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes. Hoc Christus frequenter fecit, quando pro mundi salute rogavit: et passio ejus erat postulatio efficacissima, quia per eam meruit sibi regnum militantis Ecclesiæ. Et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam. Hanc promissionem Pater implevit, quando per prædicationem Christi et Apostolorum ac successorum ipsorum gentiles convertit ad Christum: sicque gentiles, qui ante possidebantur a dæmone, possidentur a Christo; et facti sunt ejus hæreditas, qui olim ad mundi principem pertinebant. Et possessionem tuam terminos terræ: id est, dabo tibi non unam provinciam, unam linguam, unumve regnum, sed terminos terræ, id est fines mundi tuæ legi subjiciam. In omnem namque terram exivit Apostolorum doctrina. Unde inferius dicitur: Et dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad terminos orbis terrarum. De hac regia Christi dignitate et mundi subjectione, Daniel dicit: Antiquus dierum, id est Deus æternus, dedit ei potestatem, et honorem, et regnum: et omnes populi, tribus, et linguæ servient ei.
paras.en: [[2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance|Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam]]. These are the words of the Father to Christ as man, for it does not belong to him to ask of the Father according as he is God. So God the Father says to the incarnate Son: O Son, [[2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles|postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes]]. This Christ often did, when he prayed for the salvation of the world[[John 17:1||]] [the margin reads Joann. xvii, verse unread]; and his passion was a most effective asking, because by it he merited for himself the kingdom of the Church militant. [[2:8|and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance|Et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam]]. The Father fulfilled this promise when, through the preaching of Christ and of the Apostles and their successors, he converted the Gentiles to Christ: and so the Gentiles, who before were possessed by the devil, are possessed by Christ; and those who once belonged to the prince of the world have become his inheritance. [[2:8|and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession|Et possessionem tuam terminos terræ]]: that is, I will give thee not one province, one tongue or one kingdom, but the utmost parts of the earth, that is, I will subject the ends of the world to thy law. For the teaching of the Apostles has gone forth into all the earth[[Ps 18:5||]][[Rom 10:18||]]. Hence it is said further on: [[Ps 71:8|And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth|Et dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad terminos orbis terrarum]]. Of this kingly dignity of Christ and the subjection of the world, Daniel says: [[Dan 7:13|the ancient of days|Antiquus dierum]], that is, the eternal God, [[Dan 7:14|gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom: and all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|dedit ei potestatem, et honorem, et regnum: et omnes populi, tribus, et linguæ servient ei]] [Denis reads *honorem*, “honour”, where the Douay has “glory”].

paras.t: Reges eos in virga ferrea. Christus regit Ecclesiam in virga ferrea, id est in constanti et immobili æquitate. Nam lex christiana et Christi doctrina, quibus reguntur Christifideles a Christo per ejus vicarios seu prælatos, comparantur ferreæ virgæ, propter rigorem justitiæ: quoniam omne malum quantumcumque sit parvum, prohibent et condemnant aliquo modo. Et tanquam vas figuli confringes eos: non utique conterendo naturam, vel corrumpendo exsistentiam naturalem; sed vitia exstirpando, mores corrigendo, propriam voluntatem eorum frangendo.
paras.en: [[2:9|Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron|Reges eos in virga ferrea]]. Christ rules the Church with a rod of iron, that is, with a constant and unmoving equity. For the Christian law and the teaching of Christ, by which the faithful of Christ are ruled by Christ through his vicars or prelates, are compared to a rod of iron because of the rigour of justice, since they forbid and condemn in some way every evil, however small it be. [[2:9|and shalt break them in pieces like a potter's vessel|Et tanquam vas figuli confringes eos]]: not, surely, by crushing their nature or destroying their natural existence, but by rooting out vices, correcting morals and breaking their self-will.

paras.t: Et nunc, reges, intelligite. Hic ponitur salubris doctrina præsidentium, imo et omnium. Et nunc, id est sicut prædictum est de regimine Christi, reges, id est omnes vicarii Christi, qui ejus populo præsidetis, imo et singuli qui reges esse debetis, regendo vos ipsos secundum rationis imperium, intelligite dicta atque dicenda. Erudimini, qui judicatis terram, id est, acquiescite meæ informationi, qui judicatis habitantes in terra.
paras.en: [[2:10|And now, O ye kings, understand|Et nunc, reges, intelligite]]. Here wholesome teaching is set down for those who govern, nay, for all. [[2:10|And now|Et nunc]], that is, as has been said of the rule of Christ, [[2:10|O ye kings|reges]], that is, all you vicars of Christ who govern his people, nay, every one of you who ought to be kings by ruling yourselves according to the command of reason, [[2:10|understand|intelligite]] what has been said and is to be said. [[2:10|receive instruction, you that judge the earth|Erudimini, qui judicatis terram]], that is, yield to my instruction, you who judge those who dwell on the earth.

paras.t: Servite Domino in timore, ut sitis timorati atque solliciti, quomodo digne regatis subjectos, et reverenter ambuletis coram Deo, ne elatione aut vana securitate seducti, negligenter agatis quæ vobis præcepta sunt. Ideo namque scriptum est: Si non in timore Domini tenueris te instanter, cito subvertetur domus tua. Nam timor Dei expellit peccatum. Et exsultate ei cum tremore: id est, o reges terræ et homines universi, exsultate ei, id est, gaudete ad laudem Dei: gaudete, inquam, in exercitiis cultus divini, in laudibus Dei, in omni ejus obsequio, et præsertim in contemplatione ac dilectione ipsius: et hoc, cum tremore, id est cum magno ac reverentiali timore, ne exsultationem vestram dissolutio aliqua consequatur vel incustodia cordis; sicque spiritualis jucunditas in carnalem lætitiam convertatur, quemadmodum accidit his, qui spiritu inchoant, sed carne consummant. Hæc autem non de servili timore, sed initiali aut filiali intelligere congruit.
paras.en: [[2:11|Serve ye the Lord with fear|Servite Domino in timore]], so that you may be God-fearing and careful how you rule your subjects worthily, and walk reverently before God, lest, led astray by pride or vain security, you carry out negligently what has been commanded you. For this is why it is written: [[Ecclus 27:4|Unless thou hold thyself diligently in the fear of the Lord, thy house shall quickly be overthrown|Si non in timore Domini tenueris te instanter, cito subvertetur domus tua]]. For [[Ecclus 1:27|fear of the Lord driveth out sin|timor Dei expellit peccatum]]. [[2:11|and rejoice unto him with trembling|Et exsultate ei cum tremore]]: that is, O kings of the earth and all men, [[2:11|rejoice unto him|exsultate ei]], that is, be glad unto the praise of God: be glad, I say, in the exercises of divine worship, in the praises of God, in all his service, and above all in contemplating and loving him; and this [[2:11|with trembling|cum tremore]], that is, with great and reverent fear, lest any slackness or want of watch over the heart follow on your rejoicing, and so spiritual gladness be turned into carnal mirth, as befalls those who begin in the spirit but end in the flesh[[Gal 3:3||]]. And this is fittingly understood not of servile fear, but of initial or filial fear [initial fear: the fear of beginners, partly of punishment and partly of offending God; filial fear: the fear of a son, of offending the Father].

paras.t: Apprehendite disciplinam, id est, libenter amplectamini informationem fraternam, increpationem caritativam et flagella Dei, et æquanimiter ferte adversa; nequando irascatur Dominus, propter negligentiam vestram et impatientiam; et pereatis de via justa: nam dum Deus irascitur peccatori, tunc eum relinquit; quum vero a Deo homo relinquitur, et gratia ejus privatur, tunc statim perit, cadit, et errat de via justa, id est de observatione præceptorum et de omni meritoria actione.
paras.en: [[2:12|Embrace discipline|Apprehendite disciplinam]], that is, gladly embrace a brother's instruction, charitable rebuke and the scourges of God, and bear adversity with an even mind; [[2:12|lest at any time the Lord be angry|nequando irascatur Dominus]] because of your negligence and impatience, [[2:12|and you perish from the just way|et pereatis de via justa]]: for when God is angry with a sinner, he then leaves him; and when a man is left by God and deprived of his grace, he at once perishes, falls and strays from the just way, that is, from the keeping of the commandments and from every meritorious action.

paras.t: Quum exarserit in brevi ira ejus, id est, quum ira Dei vehementer fuerit inflammata, sicut præcipue erit in die judicii; tunc beati omnes qui confidunt in eo, id est, omnes qui modo sperant in Domino, tunc invenientur beati. Dicitur autem, In brevi, quia finale judicium non diu durabit; vel, In brevi, quia nescimus diem neque horam, qua de præsenti vita migraturi sumus: quando utique juste judicabimur, quoniam secundum opera sua unusquisque recipit, mox quum de corpore exit.
paras.en: [[2:13|When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time|Quum exarserit in brevi ira ejus]], that is, when the wrath of God shall be fiercely kindled, as it will be above all in the day of judgment; then [[2:13|blessed are all they that trust in him|beati omnes qui confidunt in eo]], that is, all who now hope in the Lord will then be found blessed. And it says, [[2:13|in a short time|In brevi]], because the final judgment will not last long; or, [[2:13|in a short time|In brevi]], because [[Matt 25:13|you know not the day nor the hour|nescimus diem neque horam]] in which we are to pass from the present life: when we shall surely be judged justly, since each one receives according to his works[[Rom 2:6||]][[1 Cor 3:8||]] as soon as he leaves the body.

2.title: Expositio ejusdem secundi psalmi tropologica
2.title_en: Tropological exposition of the same second psalm

paras.t: Denique tropologice explanando hunc psalmum, tunc hoc quod dicitur, Quare fremuerunt gentes, sunt verba cujuslibet Christiani, Christi vestigia cruciformiter imitantis, qui cupit pati cum Christo, quatenus postea regnet cum eo.
paras.en: Further, in explaining this psalm tropologically [that is, of the moral life of the soul], what is said, Why have the Gentiles raged, is the word of any Christian who follows the footsteps of Christ in the form of the cross, who longs to suffer with Christ, so that afterwards he may reign with him.

paras.t: Quilibet ergo vere fidelis, malignitatem persequentium homines justos admirans, dicat: Quare fremuerunt gentes, id est homines infideles, Turci, pagani, Judæi, hæretici? et populi, id est mali Christiani, mundi amatores ac carnaliter sapientes, meditati sunt inania? Adstiterunt reges terræ, id est imperatores ac alii reges increduli, persecutores atque tyranni; et principes, id est reliqui omnes judices, et etiam principes, solo nomine christiani, convenerunt in unum, id est, similem malitiam conceperunt, et in idem consilium concordaverunt, adversus Dominum, id est adversus Deum omnipotentem, et adversus Christum ejus, id est contra quemlibet hominem christianum, sacro chrismate unctum, vel gratia Spiritus Sancti spiritualiter unctum ac plenum. Qui enim contra Dei servos insurgit, contra Deum insurgit, quemadmodum Christus testatur: Quod uni minimo ex meis fecistis, mihi fecistis. Et Paulo adhuc persequenti: Quid me, inquit, persequeris?
paras.en: Let every truly faithful man, then, marvelling at the malice of those who persecute just men, say: [[2:1|Why have the Gentiles raged|Quare fremuerunt gentes]], that is, unbelieving men, Turks, pagans, Jews, heretics? [[2:1|and the people|et populi]], that is, bad Christians, lovers of the world and carnally minded, [[2:1|devised vain things?|meditati sunt inania]] [[2:2|The kings of the earth stood up|Adstiterunt reges terræ]], that is, emperors and other unbelieving kings, persecutors and tyrants; [[2:2|and the princes|et principes]], that is, all the other judges, and princes too who are Christian in name only, [[2:2|met together|convenerunt in unum]], that is, conceived a like malice and agreed in the same counsel, [[2:2|against the Lord|adversus Dominum]], that is, against almighty God, [[2:2|and against his Christ|et adversus Christum ejus]], that is, against every Christian man anointed with the holy chrism, or spiritually anointed and filled with the grace of the Holy Ghost [*christus*, "anointed"]. For whoever rises against the servants of God rises against God, as Christ testifies: [[Matt 25:40|as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me|Quod uni minimo ex meis fecistis, mihi fecistis]]. And to Paul, while he was still persecuting: [[Acts 9:4|why persecutest thou me?|Quid me, inquit, persequeris?]] he says.

paras.t: Dirumpamus vincula eorum, id est, destruamus legem ac religionem Christianorum: sicut in præcedenti articulo expositum est. Hoc enim prædicti increduli persecutores intendebant, ut Nero, Domitianus, Diocletianus. Et projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum. Hæc sunt verba Christianorum male viventium, qui se fidem habere fatentur, sed opera fidei aspernantur, atque devotos persequuntur. Hi dicunt: Projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum, id est, repellamus a nobis prædicationem ac comminationem et reprobationem eorum, qui nostræ voluntati contraria prædicant, qui nobis Dei flagella pœnasque æternas minantur, et vitam nostram tanquam injustam et pessimam arbitrantur: docentes verbo vel opere ostendentes, mundum et omnem ejus honorem, et voluptatem ac gloriam esse spernendam, parentes, propinquos, uxorem et agros, propter Christum esse derelinquenda.
paras.en: [[2:3|Let us break their bonds asunder|Dirumpamus vincula eorum]], that is, let us destroy the law and religion of the Christians: as was explained in the preceding article. For this is what the unbelieving persecutors just mentioned intended, such as Nero, Domitian, Diocletian. [[2:3|and let us cast away their yoke from us|Et projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum]]. These are the words of Christians who live badly, who profess that they have faith but despise the works of faith[[Tit 1:16||]], and persecute the devout. These say: [[2:3|let us cast away their yoke from us|Projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum]], that is, let us drive away from us the preaching and threatening and reproof of those who preach things contrary to our will, who threaten us with the scourges of God and eternal punishments, and judge our life to be unjust and most wicked: teaching by word, or showing by deed, that the world and all its honour, pleasure and glory are to be despised, and that parents, kinsfolk, wife and lands are to be left for Christ[[Matt 19:29||]].

paras.t: Qui habitat in cœlis, id est Christus qui sedet ad dexteram Patris, irridebit eos, id est omnes prædictos malignos; et Dominus, id est tota superfelicissima Trinitas, quæ est unus Deus unusque Dominus, subsannabit eos, et hoc propter Christum, qui secundum quod homo, proferet sententiam contra injustos ex totius Trinitatis commissione, quemadmodum in evangelio S. Joannis habetur: Pater omne judicium dedit Filio. Tunc, id est in die judicii, quando prædicta irrisio fiet: tunc, inquam, Christus loquetur ad eos, id est injustos et bonorum persecutores, in ira sua, dicens: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Et in furore suo conturbabit eos, faciens eos absorberi a terra, et cum dæmonibus infernali carcere recludi.
paras.en: [[2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven|Qui habitat in cœlis]], that is, Christ who sits at the right hand of the Father, [[2:4|shall laugh at them|irridebit eos]], that is, at all the wicked just mentioned; [[2:4|and the Lord|et Dominus]], that is, the whole most blessed Trinity, which is one God and one Lord, [[2:4|shall deride them|subsannabit eos]]; and this through Christ, who, as man, will pronounce sentence against the unjust by commission of the whole Trinity, as we have it in the gospel of St John: [[John 5:22|hath given all judgment to the Son|Pater omne judicium dedit Filio]]. [[2:5|Then|Tunc]], that is, on the day of judgment, when the mockery just mentioned will take place: then, I say, [[2:5|shall he speak to them|loquetur ad eos]] (Christ), that is, to the unjust and the persecutors of the good, [[2:5|in his anger|in ira sua]], saying: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. [[2:5|and trouble them in his rage|Et in furore suo conturbabit eos]], making the earth swallow them up and shutting them up with the demons in the prison of hell.

paras.t: Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion. Hoc bonis prælatis ac sanctis episcopis, fidelibusque prædicatoribus maxime convenit. Horum enim quilibet dicere potest: Ego autem, etc., quasi diceret: Illi ita peribunt, sed ego constitutus sum rex, id est prælatus, rector, seu doctor, ab eo, id est a Christo, tanquam ejus vicarius, super Sion montem sanctum ejus, id est super populum christianum divina speculantem, prædicans præceptum ejus, id est docens Christi mandata servari. Potest et hic versus de unoquoque fideli exponi, quoniam unusquisque constitutus est rex, id est dominus operationum suarum, super Sion montem sanctum ejus, scilicet super se ipsum. Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos, ait Apostolus. Quilibet enim terrena despiciens, cœlestia speculans, dici potest Sion et mons sanctus Domini, quia in sublime defigit mentis suæ affectum, estque erectus in Deum. Dicitur autem homo rex super se ipsum, quoniam libere agit, et secundum rationis imperium vivere debet, et juste gubernare se ipsum. Unde in Ecclesiastico: Deus creavit hominem, et reliquit eum in manu consilii sui. Prædicat quoque quilibet præceptum Dei, quando informat et excitat semetipsum, corde revolvens testimonia sacræ Scripturæ.
paras.en: [[2:6|But I am appointed king by him over Sion|Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion]]. This fits good prelates and holy bishops and faithful preachers above all. For any of these can say: [[2:6|But I|Ego autem]], etc., as if to say: They will perish thus, but I [[2:6|am appointed king|constitutus sum rex]], that is, prelate, ruler or teacher, [[2:6|by him|ab eo]], that is, by Christ, as his vicar, [[2:6|over Sion, his holy mountain|super Sion montem sanctum ejus]], that is, over the Christian people who contemplate divine things, [[2:6|preaching his commandment|prædicans præceptum ejus]], that is, teaching that the commandments of Christ be kept. This verse can also be expounded of each of the faithful, since each one is appointed king, that is, lord of his own works, [[2:6|over Sion, his holy mountain|super Sion montem sanctum ejus]], namely over himself. [[1 Cor 3:17|For the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos]], says the Apostle. For whoever despises earthly things and contemplates heavenly ones can be called Sion and the holy mountain of the Lord, since he fixes the affection of his mind on high and is lifted up towards God. And a man is called king over himself because he acts freely, and ought to live by the command of reason and govern himself justly. Hence in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 15:14|God made man|Deus creavit hominem]], [[Ecclus 15:14|and left him in the hand of his own counsel|et reliquit eum in manu consilii sui]]. And each one preaches the commandment of God when he forms and rouses himself, turning over in his heart the testimonies of holy Scripture.

paras.t: Dominus dixit ad me: Filius meus es tu, etc. Hoc est quod ait Apostolus: Ipse Spiritus reddit testimonium spiritui nostro, quod filii Dei sumus. Cuilibet ergo devoto dicit Dominus per inspirationem internam: Filius meus es tu; ego hodie genui te, id est in die qua in fonte Baptismatis regeneravi te. Imo quandocumque infunditur nobis caritas et gratia Spiritus Sancti, tunc Deus spiritualiter generat nos, dans nobis esse spirituale, divinum, atque cœleste.
paras.en: [[2:7|The Lord hath said to me: Thou art my son|Dominus dixit ad me: Filius meus es tu]], etc. This is what the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:16|the Spirit himself giveth testimony to our spirit that we are the sons of God|Ipse Spiritus reddit testimonium spiritui nostro, quod filii Dei sumus]]. To every devout soul, then, the Lord says by inward inspiration: [[2:7|Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee|Filius meus es tu; ego hodie genui te]], that is, on the day on which I regenerated thee in the font of Baptism. Indeed, whenever charity and the grace of the Holy Ghost are poured into us, then God begets us spiritually, giving us a being that is spiritual, divine and heavenly.

paras.t: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam. Hæreditas appellatur, qua aliquis ad libitum utitur, convertens ipsam ad propriam utilitatem. Sic homines justi ac sancti hæreditate possident gentes, scilicet peccatores gentiliter conversantes, quoniam ad libitum suum ipsis utuntur. Nam quidquid gentes hujusmodi agant, hoc totum justi ad utilitatem suam convertunt, sicque omnia cooperantur eis in bonum. Si namque honorentur et laudentur ab impiis, non extolluntur, sed per humilitatem merentur ex hoc. Si vero vilipendantur ac molestentur ab ipsis, non opprimuntur, sed per patientiam manent immobiles. Et possessionem tuam terminos terræ: id est, ego Dominus dabo tibi terminos terræ ad possidendum. Unde Apostolus: Tanquam nihil, inquit, habentes, et omnia possidentes. Justi enim tantum habent de terra quantum desiderant, si fideliter petant, quemadmodum Salvator ait: Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis. Bonis quoque prælatis dat Dominus [gentes] in hæreditatem, quatenus semper eas bene regendo possideant. Denique omnis prælatus et Christi fidelis, dignus Christi vicarius, regit sibi commissos in virga ferrea, id est in constanti justitia, et justa disciplina; et tanquam vas figuli confringit eos, quia facit eos concupiscentias refrenare, mores corrigere, seipsosque frangere.
paras.en: [[2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance|Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam]]. That is called an inheritance which one uses at will, turning it to one's own profit. So just and holy men possess the Gentiles as an inheritance, namely sinners who live like Gentiles, since they use them at will. For whatever such Gentiles do, the just turn it all to their own profit, and so [[Rom 8:28|all things work together unto good|omnia cooperantur eis in bonum]] for them. For if they are honoured and praised by the wicked, they are not puffed up, but gain merit from it through humility. And if they are despised and harassed by them, they are not crushed, but remain unmoved through patience. [[2:8|and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession|Et possessionem tuam terminos terræ]]: that is, I the Lord will give thee the ends of the earth to possess. Hence the Apostle: [[2 Cor 6:10|as having nothing|Tanquam nihil, inquit, habentes]], he says, [[2 Cor 6:10|and possessing all things|et omnia possidentes]]. For the just have as much of the earth as they desire, if they ask faithfully, as the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis]]. To good prelates too the Lord gives [the Gentiles] for an inheritance, so that they may possess them by always ruling them well. Lastly, every prelate and faithful one of Christ, a worthy vicar of Christ, rules those committed to him [[2:9|with a rod of iron|in virga ferrea]], that is, with steadfast justice and just discipline; and breaks them [[2:9|like a potter's vessel|tanquam vas figuli]], since he makes them rein in their desires, correct their ways, and break themselves.

paras.t: Et nunc, reges, intelligite. Ista atque sequentia, exponenda sunt sicut superius factum est. Ponitur hic admonitio optima, rectoribus præcipue opportuna. Prælati namque maxime indigent continuo Dei timore, imo et magno tremore, ne negligentius agant, ne eos principatus delectet, et ne per exteriorem occupationem interius vacui fiant.
paras.en: [[2:10|And now, O ye kings, understand|Et nunc, reges, intelligite]]. These and the following words are to be expounded as was done above. Here is set a most excellent warning, especially fitting for rulers. For prelates most of all need the continual fear of God, and indeed great trembling, lest they act too carelessly, lest their high office delight them, and lest through outward business they become empty within.

paras.t: Moraliter itaque docemur ex psalmo isto, ne deficiamus in adversis, ne frangamur iniquorum persecutionibus; sed considerantes divini judicii ultionem, ac impiorum damnationem æternam, viriliter assequamur Caput nostrum seu Christi vestigia: qui proposito sibi gaudio sustinuit crucem, confusione contempta; qui etiam suis fidelibus clamat, Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam quotidie, et sequatur me. Item ex eo quod dictum est, Dominus dixit ad me, Filius meus es tu, docemur et admonemur considerare eminentiam gratiæ Dei et magnitudinem beneficiorum quæ nobis collata sunt, ut simus Deo grati, et ejus amore ardentes, sicque amplioribus donis impleamur a Domino. Habenti enim dabitur, id est ei qui gratus est Deo, et gloriatur non in se ipso, quasi non acceperit, sed in Domino solum; ei vero qui non habet, id est ingrato, et quod videtur habere, auferetur ab eo.
paras.en: Morally, then, we are taught by this psalm not to fail in adversity, nor to be broken by the persecutions of the wicked; but, considering the vengeance of God's judgment and the eternal damnation of the wicked, manfully to follow our Head, the footsteps of Christ: [[Heb 12:2|who, having joy set before him, endured the cross, despising the shame|qui proposito sibi gaudio sustinuit crucem, confusione contempta]]; who also cries to his faithful: [[Luke 9:23|If any man will come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me|Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam quotidie, et sequatur me]]. Again, from what was said, [[2:7|The Lord hath said to me: Thou art my son|Dominus dixit ad me, Filius meus es tu]], we are taught and warned to consider the greatness of God's grace and the magnitude of the benefits bestowed on us, so that we may be grateful to God and burn with his love, and so be filled by the Lord with ampler gifts. For [[Matt 25:29|to every one that hath shall be given|Habenti enim dabitur]][[Matt 13:12||]], that is, to him who is grateful to God, and glories not in himself, as though he had not received[[1 Cor 4:7||]], but in the Lord alone; [[Matt 25:29|but from him that hath not|ei vero qui non habet]], that is, the ungrateful man, [[Matt 25:29|that also which he seemeth to have shall be taken away|et quod videtur habere, auferetur ab eo]].

2.title: Quod psalmus iste non sit allegorice exponendus, quamvis anagogice possit exponi
2.title_en: That this psalm is not to be expounded allegorically, though it can be expounded anagogically

paras.t: Ex quo autem ostensum est psalmum hunc ad litteram loqui de Christo, certum est quod non sit allegorice exponendus. Tunc namque allegorice Scriptura exponitur, quando id quod ad litteram de aliis scriptum est, de Christo intelligitur. Si vero de David vel de aliis psalmus hic loqueretur, ut putant Judæi, tunc posset de Christo allegorice explanari.
paras.en: Since it has been shown that this psalm speaks literally of Christ, it is certain that it is not to be expounded allegorically. For Scripture is expounded allegorically when what is written literally of others is understood of Christ. But if this psalm spoke of David or of others, as the Jews think, then it could be explained allegorically of Christ.

paras.t: Verum anagogice exponi potest, ut id quod dicitur, Quare fremuerunt gentes, usque ibi, Qui habitat in cælis, sint verba cujuslibet Beati in patria, qui ista dicit ad insinuandum enormitatem peccati eorum qui adversus Deum et Christum ejus, id est contra eos qui nunc Deo fruuntur, convenerunt quando in vita hac fuerunt. Et convenit vox ista præsertim sanctis martyribus, qui se conformando divinæ justitiæ, optant vindictam de impiis, atque ob hanc adipiscendam sic dicunt: Quare fremuerunt, etc. Unde scriptum est: Sub ara Dei, Sancti clamabant, Domine, vindica sanguinem nostrum; et infra: Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam. Interim autem Beati in patria, quasi consolando se ipsos de dilatione divini judicii, dicunt ad invicem: Qui habitat in cælis irridebit eos.
paras.en: But it can be expounded anagogically [that is, of the glory of heaven], so that what is said from [[2:1|Why have the Gentiles raged|Quare fremuerunt gentes]] as far as [[2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven|Qui habitat in cælis]] are the words of any one of the Blessed in the fatherland, who says these things to bring out the enormity of the sin of those who [[2:2|met together|convenerunt]] [[2:2|against the Lord, and against his Christ|adversus Deum et Christum ejus]], that is, against those who now enjoy God, when they were in this life. And this voice befits above all the holy martyrs, who, conforming themselves to the divine justice, desire vengeance on the wicked, and to obtain it say thus: [[2:1|Why have the Gentiles raged|Quare fremuerunt]], etc. Hence it is written: Under the altar of God the saints cried, Lord, [[Apoc 6:10|revenge our blood|vindica sanguinem nostrum]]; and further on: [[Ps 57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam]]. Meanwhile the Blessed in the fatherland, as though consoling themselves for the delay of the divine judgment, say to one another: [[2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them|Qui habitat in cælis irridebit eos]].

paras.t: Denique quilibet Deo jam fruens, dicere potest: Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, id est, in cælo empyreo coronam victoriæ et regium diadema recepi, pro tribulationibus atque laboribus in mundo perpessis; prædicans, id est extollens seu laudans, præceptum ejus, scilicet Domini, quoniam justum est, et quia illud implendo felicitatem adeptus sum.
paras.en: Lastly, anyone who already enjoys God can say: [[2:6|But I am appointed king by him over Sion, his holy mountain|Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus]], that is, in the empyrean heaven I have received the crown of victory and the royal diadem for the tribulations and labours I endured in the world; [[2:6|preaching|prædicans]], that is, extolling or praising, [[2:6|his commandment|præceptum ejus]], that is, the Lord's, because it is just, and because by fulfilling it I have attained happiness.

paras.t: Dominus dicit ad me: Filius meus es tu. Viatores dicuntur filii Dei, propter gratiam adoptionis et similitudinem imperfectam; sed bene in patria nuncupantur filii Dei, propter beatificæ fruitionis gloriam, similitudinemque perfectam, quoniam vident Deum sicuti est. Idcirco unicuique Beatorum optime convenit dicere: Dominus dicit ad me: Filius meus es tu, quia perfecte conjunctus ac assimilatus es mihi. Ego hodie, id est in die qua te mea visione beatificavi, genui te. Tunc enim de viatore seu imperfecto ac misero, facit Deus comprehensorem, et perfectum atque felicem.
paras.en: [[2:7|The Lord hath said to me|Dominus dicit ad me]]: [[2:7|Thou art my son|Filius meus es tu]]. Wayfarers [that is, those still on the road of this life, as against the blessed who have arrived] are called sons of God because of the grace of adoption and an imperfect likeness; but in the fatherland they are rightly called sons of God because of the glory of the beatific enjoyment and a perfect likeness, since they see God as he is. Therefore it befits each of the Blessed most fittingly to say: [[2:7|The Lord hath said to me|Dominus dicit ad me]]: [[2:7|Thou art my son|Filius meus es tu]], because thou art perfectly joined to me and made like me. [[2:7|this day have I|Ego hodie]], that is, on the day on which I beatified thee with the vision of me, [[2:7|begotten thee|genui te]]. For then, out of a wayfarer, imperfect and wretched, God makes a comprehensor [one who has reached and possesses God], perfect and happy.

paras.t: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem, etc. Istud Dominus dixit ad Beatos, quando vivebant in sæculo, secundum intellectum in præcedenti expositione tactum. Vel nunc quoque dicit istud ad ipsos, quoniam Sancti in patria habent sibi subjectos populos mundi hujus, quemadmodum apud Sapientiam legitur: Judicabunt justi nationes, et dominabuntur populis. Reges eos in virga ferrea. Certum est viatores regi ab angelis sanctis in virga ferrea, id est justa ac forti directione. Animæ quoque Beatorum regunt nos, orando pro nobis. Et tanquam vas figuli confringes eos. Sanctis qui judicabunt cum Christo, hoc verbum competit, quia simul cum Christo confringent et conterent impios ab omni esse spirituali, beato, et glorioso.
paras.en: [[2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance|Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem]], etc. The Lord said this to the Blessed when they were living in the world, in the sense touched on in the preceding exposition. Or he says it to them now too, since the Saints in the fatherland have the peoples of this world subject to them, as we read in Wisdom: [[Wis 3:8|They shall judge|Judicabunt]] the just [[Wis 3:8|nations, and rule over people|nationes, et dominabuntur populis]]. [[2:9|Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron|Reges eos in virga ferrea]]. It is certain that wayfarers are ruled by the holy angels [[2:9|with a rod of iron|in virga ferrea]], that is, by a just and strong direction. The souls of the Blessed rule us too, by praying for us. [[2:9|and shalt break them in pieces like a potter's vessel|Et tanquam vas figuli confringes eos]]. This word befits the Saints, who will judge with Christ, because together with Christ they will break and crush the wicked, cutting them off from all spiritual, blessed and glorious being.

paras.t: Porro quæ sequuntur, Et nunc, reges, intelligite, usque ad finem, sunt verba triumphantis Ecclesiæ ad Ecclesiam militantem. Angeli enim qui sunt administratorii spiritus, ex parte Dei ac omnium Beatorum hortantur homines, et eos præcipue qui aliis præsident, dicentes per inspirationem mentalem, quæ est occulta interiorque locutio: Et nunc, reges, intelligite. Et sunt verba hæc exponenda sicut exposita sunt.
paras.en: Further, what follows, from [[2:10|And now, O ye kings, understand|Et nunc, reges, intelligite]] to the end, are the words of the Church triumphant to the Church militant. For the angels, who are [[Heb 1:14|ministering spirits|administratorii spiritus]], exhort men on behalf of God and of all the Blessed, and above all those who are set over others, saying by a mental inspiration, which is a hidden and inward speech: [[2:10|And now, O ye kings, understand|Et nunc, reges, intelligite]]. And these words are to be expounded as they have been expounded already.

paras.t: Itaque ex anagogica expositione psalmi istius, docemur contemplari gloriam Beatorum in patria, quantam videlicet felicitatem sortiti sunt, et quantum præmium receperunt pro temporali et modica tribulatione vitæ præsentis; atque ex hac contemplatione inflammari debemus ad obtinendam hanc felicitatem, et propter ejus amorem fortiter sequi exempla, vitam, mores, ac tribulationes Beatorum, quatenus eorum consortio post præsens exsilium feliciter copulemur.
paras.en: So from the anagogical exposition of this psalm we are taught to contemplate the glory of the Blessed in the fatherland: how great a happiness they have obtained, and how great a reward they have received for the brief and slight tribulation of the present life; and by this contemplation we ought to be inflamed to obtain this happiness, and for love of it to follow bravely the examples, the life, the ways and the tribulations of the Blessed, so that after the present exile we may be happily joined to their company.

paras.t: Precatio. Miserator et piissime Deus, qui tibi famulantes ubique tueris et defendis, dona nobis in Christo Filio tuo fideliter vivere, eique jugiter servire in timore et exsultare cum tremore: ut apprehensa justitiæ disciplina, in ea persistentes beati in perpetuum exsistamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O merciful and most loving God, who everywhere guardest and defendest those who serve thee, grant us to live faithfully in Christ thy Son, and to serve him continually in fear and rejoice in him with trembling: that, having embraced the discipline of justice and persevering in it, we may be blessed for ever.

3.title: Explanatio litteralis psalmi tertii
3.title_en: Literal explanation of the third psalm

paras.t: Hujus psalmi talis est titulus: Psalmus David, quum fugeret a facie Absalon filii sui. Quidam autem hunc psalmum ad litteram exponunt de David, et ita titulus difficultatem non habet. Constat enim scienti Scripturas, quemadmodum narratur Absalon cupidum regni, voluisse patrem suum sanctum David occidere, ut eo occiso ipse regnaret; et congregato exercitu, volebat obsidere Jerusalem. Quo audito, David cum suis fugit; et tandem ejus exercitus vicit atque fugavit exercitum Absalon. Joab quoque princeps militiæ interfecit Absalon de quercu pendentem. In hac ergo persecutione, fecit David hunc psalmum, qui ad litteram de ipso intelligi potest, quamvis verius et efficacius exponatur de Christo.
paras.en: The title of this psalm is this: [[3:1|The psalm of David when he fled from the face of his son Absalom|Psalmus David, quum fugeret a facie Absalon filii sui]]. Now some expound this psalm literally of David, and so the title has no difficulty.
