For as the heat of fire dissolves and destroys wax, so the wrath of divine justice takes sinners away from the present life and drives them back from the blessed life to come: and so they are taken away in both, and are spiritually corrupted. Therefore the Lord says in Osee: [[Osee 13:8|I will meet them as a bear that is robbed of her whelps, and I will rend the inner parts of their liver: and I will devour them there as a lion|Occurram eis quasi ursa raptis catulis, et dirumpam interiora eorum, et consumam eos ut leo]]. For sinners, by sinning, also merit the shortening of the present life, as the Lord said to the avaricious rich man: [[Luke 12:20|Thou fool, this night do they require thy soul of thee|Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetunt a te]]. And Solomon: [[Eccles 8:13|let it not be well|Non sit]], he says, [[Eccles 8:13|with the wicked, neither let his days be prolonged, but as a shadow let them pass away that fear not the face of the Lord|bonum impio, nec prolongentur dies ejus, sed quasi umbra transeant qui non timent faciem Domini]].

paras.t: Supercecidit ignis, et non viderunt solem : id est, ignis infernalis cadet super iniquos, et Deum non videbunt : quia nec sapientia, nec scientia, nec opus, nec ratio erunt apud inferos.
paras.en: [[57:9|fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun|Supercecidit ignis, et non viderunt solem]]: that is, the fire of hell will fall upon the wicked, and they will not see God: because [[Eccles 9:10|neither work, nor reason, nor wisdom, nor knowledge shall be in hell|nec sapientia, nec scientia, nec opus, nec ratio erunt apud inferos]].

paras.t: Vel : Supercecidit ignis, id est, calor libidinis, passionumque fervor, ut sunt inflammatio iræ, æstus avaritiæ, flamma invidiæ, ceciderunt super peccatores, quia facta carnis modo non mortificant, nec sensualitatem rationi subjiciunt ; et non viderunt solem, id est, Christum solem justitiæ, veritatis et sapientiæ, non consideraverunt, nec ejus præceptis obtemperaverunt : quoniam ignis passionum istarum rationem obtenebrat, caritatem exstinguit, et gratiam fugat. Ideo sero fatentur : Erravimus a via veritatis, et justitiæ lumen non luxit nobis, et sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis.
paras.en: Or: [[57:9|fire hath fallen|Supercecidit ignis]], that is, the heat of lust and the fervour of the passions, such as the inflaming of anger, the heat of avarice, the flame of envy, have fallen upon sinners, because they do not now mortify the deeds of the flesh nor subject sensuality to reason; [[57:9|and they shall not see the sun|et non viderunt solem]], that is, they have not considered Christ, the sun of justice, of truth and of wisdom, nor obeyed his precepts: since the fire of these passions darkens the reason, extinguishes charity and puts grace to flight. Therefore they confess too late: [[Wis 5:6|we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of justice hath not shined unto us, and the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us|Erravimus a via veritatis, et justitiæ lumen non luxit nobis, et sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis]].

paras.t: Vel : Supercecidit ignis, id est, tribulatio irruit super malignos in sæculo isto. Peccatori enim dedit Deus afflictionem et curam superfluam. Et non viderunt solem, id est, non pœnituerunt, neque ad Deum conversi sunt, sed impatientes effecti sunt et obstinati, quemadmodum in Apocalypsi legitur : Blasphemaverunt Deum cœli præ doloribus et vulneribus suis, et non egerunt pœnitentiam ex operibus suis ut darent gloriam Deo.
paras.en: Or: [[57:9|fire hath fallen|Supercecidit ignis]], that is, tribulation has rushed upon the wicked in this world. For [[Eccles 2:26|to the sinner he hath given vexation, and superfluous care|Peccatori enim dedit Deus afflictionem et curam superfluam]]. [[57:9|and they shall not see the sun|Et non viderunt solem]], that is, they have not repented, nor been converted to God, but have become impatient and obstinate, as we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 16:11|they blasphemed the God of heaven, because of their pains and wounds: and did not penance for their works|Blasphemaverunt Deum cœli præ doloribus et vulneribus suis, et non egerunt pœnitentiam ex operibus suis]], [[Apoc 16:9|to give him glory|ut darent gloriam Deo]] [the margin gives Apoc. xvi, 9; the words are those of v. 11, with the close of v. 9].

paras.t: Priusquam intelligerent spinæ vestræ rhamnum : id est, antequam vermis conscientiæ vestræ, et punctiones inordinationis internæ pensarent enormitatem peccati, ac gravitatem tormenti vobis in inferno parati ; sicut viventes, sicut in ira absorbet eos, id est, Deus vos subito tollet, opprimet, et damnabit, sicut tolluntur a sæculo isto viventes, qui diu vivere æstimant, sed improvise decedunt. Quamvis enim injusti remorsum conscientiæ habeant, interiorisque inordinationis punctiones persentiant, quoniam animus inordinatus sibi ipsi est pœna ; nolunt tamen ex hoc vitæ suæ pravitatem advertere, neque futura tormenta prospicere : ideo Deus eos imparatos inveniens, subito absorbet eos et damnat, sicut jam patuit. Hic autem versiculus in præcedenti expositione plenius elucidatus est. Cetera quoque jam omissa, illic plene exposita sunt.
paras.en: [[57:10|Before your thorns could know the brier|Priusquam intelligerent spinæ vestræ rhamnum]]: that is, before the worm of your conscience and the prickings of your inward disorder weighed the enormity of sin and the heaviness of the torment prepared for you in hell; [[57:10|he swalloweth them up, as alive, in his wrath|sicut viventes, sicut in ira absorbet eos]], that is, God will suddenly take you away, crush you and condemn you, as the living are taken from this world who think to live long, but die unexpectedly. For although the unjust have remorse of conscience and feel the prickings of inward disorder, since the disordered mind is its own punishment [a saying of Augustine, Confessions I, 12]; yet they will not on that account turn their minds to the depravity of their life, nor look ahead to the torments to come: therefore God, finding them unprepared, suddenly swallows them up and condemns them, as has already been shown. But this little verse has been more fully explained in the preceding exposition. The rest, too, now passed over, has been fully expounded there.

paras.t: Omnino ergo curemus juste judicare, recte discernere, et vitam ac mores justo judicio subjugare, conformare, atque secundum divinæ legis tenorem dirigere, agnoscentes certissime quoniam erit merces operi nostro, nec impii justas pœnas evadent. Unde sapientissimus Salomon in Ecclesiaste contestatur : Peccator ex eo quod centies facit malum, et per patientiam sustentatur, ego cognovi quod erit bonum timentibus Deum, qui quærunt faciem ejus.
paras.en: Let us, then, by all means take care to judge justly, to discern rightly, and to subject our life and conduct to just judgment, to conform it and direct it according to the tenor of the divine law, knowing most certainly that there will be a reward for our work[[Jer 31:16||]], and that the wicked will not escape just punishments. Hence the most wise Solomon testifies in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 8:12|though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and by patience be borne withal, I know from thence that it shall be well with them that fear God, who dread his face|Peccator ex eo quod centies facit malum, et per patientiam sustentatur, ego cognovi quod erit bonum timentibus Deum, qui quærunt faciem ejus]] [Denis has *quærunt*, "seek", where the Vulgate has *verentur*, "dread"].

paras.t: PRECATIO. Da nobis, quæsumus, Domine Deus, vere justitiam tuam semper loqui, diligere et sectari ; et qui vile et reprobum efficis pretiosum, fac nos iniquitates in terra non operari : ut ope miserationis tuæ justificati, salvandis in judicio justis possimus aggregari.
paras.en: Prayer. Grant us, we beseech thee, O Lord God, ever truly to speak thy justice, to love it and to follow it; and thou who makest precious what is vile and reprobate, make us not to work iniquities on the earth: that, justified by the help of thy mercy, we may be gathered to the just who are to be saved in the judgment.

58.title: EXPOSITIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI OCTAVI : ERIPE ME DE INIMICIS MEIS.
58.title_en: Exposition, of Christ, of the fifty-eighth psalm: Deliver me from my enemies.

paras.t: Assignatur præterea psalmo jam explanando hic titulus : In finem, ne disperdas David in tituli inscriptione, quando misit Saul et custodivit domum ejus, ut interficeret eum. Primo libro Regum legitur, quod David coram Saul psallente, nisus est ipse Saul percutere lancea sanctum David, qui fugit ad domum suam. Saul vero satellites suos misit, faciens nocte illa custodiri domum David, quatenus mane facto, David comprehenderetur et occideretur. Sed Michol, filia Saul, annuntiavit hoc viro suo, eumque in sporta deposuit, et ita David evasit. Hujus igitur salvationis occasione edidit David hunc psalmum : quem multi ad litteram exponunt de David, applicando litteram præsentis psalmi ad prædictam historiam. Quod quamvis aliquo modo fieri possit, tamen, ut in processu patebit, multa in hoc psalmo habentur, quæ de David valde improprie exponuntur. Convenientius ergo et verius exponitur de significato per rem gestam, quam de ipsa re. David enim figura est Christi ; domus quoque David, significat Christi sepulcrum ; Saul autem, regnum Judæorum.
paras.en: To the psalm now to be explained this title is further assigned: [[58:1|Unto the end, destroy not, for David for an inscription of a title, when Saul sent and watched his house to kill him|In finem, ne disperdas David in tituli inscriptione, quando misit Saul et custodivit domum ejus, ut interficeret eum]]. In the first book of Kings we read that while David was playing before Saul[[1 Kings 19:9||]], Saul himself tried to strike the holy David with a spear[[1 Kings 19:10||]]; and David fled to his house. But Saul sent his guards and had David's house watched that night, so that when morning came David might be seized and killed. But Michol, the daughter of Saul, told this to her husband[[1 Kings 19:11||]], and let him down in a basket, and so David escaped[[1 Kings 19:12||]]. On the occasion of this deliverance, then, David put out this psalm, which many expound literally of David, applying the letter of the present psalm to the history just told. And although this can be done in some manner, yet, as will appear as we go on, there are many things in this psalm which are very improperly expounded of David. It is therefore expounded more fittingly and more truly of what was signified by the deed than of the deed itself. For David is a figure of Christ; the house of David, too, signifies the sepulchre of Christ; and Saul, the kingdom of the Jews.

paras.t: Est igitur tituli sensus : In finem, id est, iste psalmus in Christum nos erigens, agit vel scriptus est, ne disperdas David, id est, ne Christi honorem aut regnum, quod est Ecclesia, diminuas, in tituli inscriptione, verbis vel actibus malis negando Christum esse verum Salvatorem ; quando misit Saul, id est regnum Judæorum, et custodivit domum ejus : quia Judæi miserunt milites Christi sepulcrum custodientes, signantes lapidem, cum custodibus ; ut interficeret eum : id est, Judæi igitur custodiri fecerunt Christi sepulcrum, quatenus nomen atque memoriam ejus delerent, quemadmodum apud Jeremiam ex eorum persona inducitur : Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra. Unde superius quoque Christus dixit : Inimici mei dixerunt mala mihi : Quando morietur et peribit nomen ejus ?
paras.en: The sense of the title, then, is this: [[58:1|Unto the end|In finem]], that is, this psalm, raising us up to Christ, treats, or was written: [[58:1|destroy not, for David|ne disperdas David]] [Denis takes *David* as the object: "destroy not David"], that is, do not lessen the honour or the kingdom of Christ, which is the Church, [[58:1|for an inscription of a title|in tituli inscriptione]], by denying in evil words or deeds that Christ is the true Saviour; [[58:1|when Saul sent|quando misit Saul]], that is, the kingdom of the Jews, [[58:1|and watched his house|et custodivit domum ejus]]: for the Jews sent soldiers to guard the sepulchre of Christ, [[Matt 27:66|sealing the stone and setting guards|signantes lapidem, cum custodibus]]; [[58:1|to kill him|ut interficeret eum]]: that is, the Jews had Christ's sepulchre guarded so as to blot out his name and memory, as is brought in, in their person, in Jeremias: Let us [[Jer 11:19|cut him off from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more|Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra]]. Hence Christ also said above: [[Ps 40:6|My enemies have spoken evils against me: when shall he die and his name perish?|Inimici mei dixerunt mala mihi : Quando morietur et peribit nomen ejus]]

paras.t: Itaque Christus adhuc passibilis, et passioni jam proximus, ad immortalem vitam resuscitari desiderans, deprecatur : Eripe me de inimicis meis mihi invidentibus, detrahentibus, et mala parantibus, puta Judæis : de quibus in Evangelio dicitur, Jam enim conspiraverant Judæi, ut si quis confiteretur eum esse Christum, extra synagogam fieret ; Deus meus et ab insurgentibus in me, id est a cohorte et tribuno ac ministris Judæorum, qui accesserunt et injecerunt manus in Jesum, et comprehenderunt et ligaverunt eum, libera me, per celerem resurrectionem, ne in morte ultra triduum detinear.
paras.en: And so Christ, still passible and already near his passion, desiring to be raised to immortal life, prays: [[58:2|Deliver me from my enemies|Eripe me de inimicis meis]], who envy me, disparage me and plot evil against me, namely the Jews, of whom it is said in the Gospel: For [[John 9:22|the Jews had already agreed among themselves that if any man should confess him to be Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue|Jam enim conspiraverant Judæi, ut si quis confiteretur eum esse Christum, extra synagogam fieret]]; [[58:2|O my God|Deus meus]], [[58:2|and|et]] [[58:2|from them that rise up against me|ab insurgentibus in me]], that is, from the band and the tribune and the servants of the Jews, who came and laid hands on Jesus, and took him and bound him[[John 18:12||]], [[58:2|defend me|libera me]] by a swift resurrection, so that I be not held in death beyond three days.

paras.t: Eripe me de operantibus iniquitatem, id est a Judæis qui tota nocte me affligebant : ut in Luca habetur, Viri qui tenebant illum, illudebant ei, cædentes eum, et velaverunt eum, et percusserunt faciem ejus, et exspuerunt in eum. Et de viris sanguinum salva me, id est ab his qui in die Parasceves vel lingua vel manu persecuti sunt me usque ad sanguinis effusionem et mortem, corpus meum lacerando flagellis, caput perforando spinis, manus ac pedes confodiendo gravibus clavis. Ab his Christus eripi et salvari precatur, non ut hæc non patiatur, sed ut statim a morte suscitetur, in mundo clarificetur, et corpore glorificetur. Quamobrem ait ad Patrem : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum. Alibi quoque : Pater, inquit, salvifica me ex hac hora.
paras.en: [[58:3|Deliver me from them that work iniquity|Eripe me de operantibus iniquitatem]], that is, from the Jews who afflicted me all night, as is found in Luke: [[Luke 22:63|And the men that held him mocked him and struck him|Viri qui tenebant illum, illudebant ei, cædentes eum]], [[Luke 22:64|And they blindfolded him and smote his face|et velaverunt eum, et percusserunt faciem ejus]], and spat upon him. [[58:3|and save me from bloody men|Et de viris sanguinum salva me]], that is, from those who on the day of the Parasceve [that is, the day of preparation, Good Friday] persecuted me, with tongue or with hand, even to the shedding of my blood and to death, tearing my body with scourges, piercing my head with thorns, and transfixing my hands and feet with heavy nails. Christ prays to be delivered and saved from these, not so as not to suffer these things, but so as to be raised from death at once, made glorious in the world, and glorified in his body. Wherefore he says to the Father: Father, [[John 17:1|the hour is come. Glorify thy Son|venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]]. Elsewhere too: [[John 12:27|Father|Pater]], he says, [[John 12:27|save me from this hour|salvifica me ex hac hora]].

paras.t: Merito autem, o Pater æterne, hæc oro, Quia ecce ceperunt prædicti Judæi, præsidisque ministri, animam meam, id est vitam meam corporalem, ut eam exstinguant ; vel, Animam meam, id est me ipsum, ut me interficiant. Sæpe enim per partem in Scripturis totum signatur, ut ibi : Verbum caro factum est. Ecce istud ad litteram non convenit proprie ipsi David. Nunquam enim a Saul et ejus fautoribus captus fuit, nec capi prævaluit. Irruerunt in me Christum Filium tuum, sanctum et innocentem, fortes in malo, videlicet principes sacerdotum, Pilatus condemnans, et Herodes deridens.
paras.en: And rightly, O eternal Father, do I pray for these things, [[58:4|For behold they have caught|Quia ecce ceperunt]] (the aforesaid Jews and the servants of the governor) [[58:4|my soul|animam meam]], that is, my bodily life, to put it out; or, [[58:4|my soul|Animam meam]], that is, myself, to kill me. For in the Scriptures the whole is often signified by the part, as here: [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh|Verbum caro factum est]]. See, this does not properly fit David himself according to the letter; for he was never caught by Saul and his partisans, nor could they manage to catch him. [[58:4|have rushed in upon me|Irruerunt in me]], Christ thy Son, holy and innocent, [[58:4|the mighty|fortes]] in evil, namely the chief priests, Pilate who condemned, and Herod who mocked.

paras.t: Neque iniquitas mea contra Deum, neque peccatum meum contra proximum, Domine Deus : id est, nulla mea culpa merui ista pati, sed quæ non rapui, exsolvebam, et pro peccato totius mundi hæc pertuli, ut scriptum est : Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Unde Isaias ait : Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Sine iniquitate cucurri, per viam mandatorum tuorum et sæculi hujus campum : sicut superius dictum est, Exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam mandatorum tuorum. Unde Christus testatur : Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio. Et direxi totam conversationem meam humanam in hoc mundo secundum voluntatem divinam, nec unquam in aliquo aberravi. Istud quoque satis improprie convenit David. Quamvis enim a Saule occidi non meruit, non tamen penitus sine iniquitate cucurrit et direxit. Si enim dixerimus quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos seducimus. Et nemo mundus a sorde, nec infans cujus est vita unius diei. Propter quod Salomon asserit : Non est homo super terram qui faciat bonum, et non peccet. Nec videtur quod David in tantum se ipsum justificare præsumpserit ante Deum.
paras.en: [[58:5|Neither is it my iniquity|Neque iniquitas mea]] against God, [[58:5|nor my sin|neque peccatum meum]] against my neighbour, [[58:5|O Lord|Domine]] God: that is, by no fault of mine have I deserved to suffer these things, but [[Ps 68:5|then did I pay that which I took not away|quæ non rapui, exsolvebam]], and I bore these things for the sin of the whole world, as it is written: [[John 10:15|I lay down my life for my sheep|Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]. Hence Isaias says: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. [[58:5|without iniquity have I run|Sine iniquitate cucurri]], along the way of thy commandments and the field of this world, as was said above: [[Ps 18:6|Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way|Exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam]] of thy commandments. Hence Christ testifies: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]. [[58:5|and directed|Et direxi]] my whole human conduct in this world according to the divine will, and never strayed in anything. This too fits David rather improperly. For although he did not deserve to be killed by Saul, yet he did not run and direct his steps wholly without iniquity. For [[1 John 1:8|If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves|Si enim dixerimus quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos seducimus]]. And none is clean from defilement, not even an infant whose life is of one day[[Job 14:4||]] [the margin gives Job xv, 14, "according to the Septuagint"; the words are the Septuagint reading of Job 14:4–5, which the Douay-Rheims renders differently]. Therefore Solomon declares: [[Eccles 7:21|there is no|Non est]] [[Eccles 7:21|man upon earth, that doth good, and sinneth not|homo super terram qui faciat bonum, et non peccet]]. Nor does it seem that David would have presumed to justify himself so far before God.

paras.t: Exsurge in occursum meum : id est, tu, Domine Pater, mihi ad locum Calvariæ exeunti, et propriis humeris crucem bajulanti, occurre, id est, per modum exsurgentis et occurrentis te habe, meæ humanitati in omnibus adsistendo, cooperando, et succurrendo. Tota enim efficacia meriti humanitatis Christi, erat ex virtute divina. Animæ quoque meæ de corpore emigranti, et limbum intranti, et una cum corpore cœlos ascendenti, occurre, eam in omnibus deducendo et amplectendo. Hoc enim Christus oravit, dicendo : Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum. Et vide oculo pietatis atque justitiæ, quanta pro tuo honore ac mundi redemptione sustineo ; hocque videndo, da mihi præmium accidentale, detentis in limbo præmium essentiale, et totum mundum ad rectam fidem converte.
paras.en: [[58:6|Rise up thou to meet me|Exsurge in occursum meum]]: that is, do thou, O Lord the Father, come to meet me as I go out to the place of Calvary carrying the cross on my own shoulders; that is, bear thyself as one who rises up and comes to meet me, assisting, working with and succouring my manhood in all things. For the whole efficacy of the merit of Christ's manhood was from the divine power. Come to meet my soul too as it goes forth from the body and enters limbo, and ascends to heaven together with the body, leading and embracing it in all things. For this Christ prayed when he said: [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]. [[58:6|and behold|Et vide]], with the eye of mercy and of justice, how much I endure for thy honour and the redemption of the world; and, beholding this, give me the accidental reward [that is, the glory added to the essential reward of seeing God, such as the glorifying of his body and of his name], give the essential reward to those held in limbo, and convert the whole world to the right faith.

paras.t: Et tu, Domine universorum, Deus virtutum cœlestium, scilicet angelorum, Deus Israel, id est spiritualium hominum te per fidem contemplantium : qui ad litteram specialiter eras Deus sancti Jacob, qui dictus est Israel, et populi Judæorum, qui sæpe in Scriptura Israel nominatur ; Intende ad visitandas omnes gentes, etc. Visitatio Dei in sacra Scriptura interdum in bono accipitur, scilicet pro miseratione et subventione divina, quemadmodum in Luca habetur : Per viscera misericordiæ Dei nostri, in quibus visitavit nos. Interdum autem accipitur in malo, videlicet pro ultione divina, secundum quod per Sophoniam Dominus ait : Visitabo super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur. Sic quoque accipitur apud Isaiam, ubi legitur de dæmonibus et damnatis : Congregabuntur in congregatione unius fascis in lacum, et claudentur in carcere, et post dies multos visitabuntur. Origenes autem putavit visitationem hoc loco sumi in bono : propterea dixit omnes damnatos tandem salvandos.
paras.en: [[58:6|even thou, O Lord|Et tu, Domine]] of all things, [[58:6|the God of hosts|Deus virtutum]] [*virtutum*, literally "of the powers"] of heaven, that is, of the angels, [[58:6|the God of Israel|Deus Israel]], that is, of spiritual men who contemplate thee by faith: who according to the letter wast in a special way the God of holy Jacob, who was called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]], and of the Jewish people, who are often named Israel in Scripture; [[58:6|Attend to visit all the nations|Intende ad visitandas omnes gentes]], etc. The visitation of God is sometimes taken in sacred Scripture in a good sense, namely for divine mercy and help, as is found in Luke: [[Luke 1:78|Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us|Per viscera misericordiæ Dei nostri, in quibus visitavit nos]]. But sometimes it is taken in an evil sense, namely for divine vengeance, as the Lord says through Sophonias: [[Soph 1:9|I will visit|Visitabo]] [[Soph 1:9|upon every one that entereth arrogantly|super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur]]. So too it is taken in Isaias, where we read of the demons and the damned: [[Is 24:22|they shall be gathered together as in the gathering of one bundle into the pit, and they shall be shut up there in prison: and after many days they shall be visited|Congregabuntur in congregatione unius fascis in lacum, et claudentur in carcere, et post dies multos visitabuntur]]. Origen, however, thought that visitation is taken in a good sense in this place; and for this reason he said that all the damned would at last be saved.

paras.t: Secundum duplicem igitur hanc visitationem, exponi potest dupliciter locus iste. Primo sic : Intende, o Domine, ad visitandas omnes gentes, id est, peccatores gentiliter conversantes justo tuo judicio visita, subtrahendo eis gratiam in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro, atque utrobique debitas eis pœnas infligendo. Ideo sequitur, Non miserearis omnibus qui operantur iniquitatem : quod dicitur magis prænuntiando quam imprecando, nisi intelligatur de perseverantibus in peccato, propriumque affectum conformando divinæ justitiæ. Nec tamen sic intelligi debet, quasi Deus nullo modo misereatur damnatis : quia in præsenti citra condignum relinquuntur, eo quod angeli eorum a multis malis ipsos avertant ; in futuro quoque citra condignum puniuntur. Sed Deus dicitur eis non misereri, quia non salvat eos finaliter, et quoniam magis ac evidentius relucet in eis divina justitia, quam misericordia. Et sic Jacobus ait : Judicium sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam. — Secundo exponitur sic : Intende ad visitandas omnes gentes, ita ut eas per gratiam tuam illumines, ad fidem convertas, super semitas justitiæ ducas, quatenus omnes benedicantur in Christo : secundum quod Abrahæ in Genesi sæpe promittitur, In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes. Non miserearis omnibus qui operantur iniquitatem, id est, in præsenti vita eis non parcas, sed argue et castiga, nuncque ulciscere, ne postmodum gravius ulciscaris.
paras.en: According to this twofold visitation, then, this place can be expounded in two ways. First thus: [[58:6|Attend|Intende]], O Lord, [[58:6|to visit all the nations|ad visitandas omnes gentes]], that is, visit with thy just judgement the sinners who live as the heathen do, withdrawing from them grace in the present and glory in the future, and in both inflicting on them the punishments they are due. Therefore there follows: [[58:6|have no mercy on all them that work iniquity|Non miserearis omnibus qui operantur iniquitatem]]; which is said rather by way of foretelling than of imprecation, unless it be understood of those who persevere in sin, the psalmist conforming his own affection to the divine justice. Yet it must not be understood as though God in no way had mercy on the damned: for in the present they are let off with less than they deserve, in that their angels turn them away from many evils; and in the future too they are punished less than they deserve. But God is said not to have mercy on them because he does not finally save them, and because the divine justice shines out in them more, and more evidently, than mercy. And so James says: [[Jas 2:13|For judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|Judicium sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam]]. Secondly, it is expounded thus: [[58:6|Attend to visit all the nations|Intende ad visitandas omnes gentes]], so as to enlighten them by thy grace, convert them to the faith, and lead them upon the paths of justice, so that all may be blessed in Christ: as is often promised to Abraham in Genesis[[Gen 12:3||]][[Gen 18:18||]]: [[Gen 22:18|in thy seed shall all the nations|In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes]] be blessed. [[58:6|have no mercy on all them that work iniquity|Non miserearis omnibus qui operantur iniquitatem]], that is, spare them not in the present life, but rebuke and chastise them, and take vengeance now, lest thou take vengeance more grievously afterwards.

paras.t: Convertentur ad vesperam, etc. Istud quoque dupliciter explanatur. Primo, de gentibus. Convertentur ad vesperam, id est, gentiles ad Christum convertentur in sexta ætate ac ultima, secundum quod Joannes in sua Canonica ait : Novissima hora est ; et Paulus, Nos sumus in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt. Et famem patientur ut canes, id est, justitiam esurient ac sitient, Deique verbum avide audient, sicut in Actis Apostolorum de Thessalonicensibus Lucas commemorat : Hi sunt qui cum omni aviditate receperunt verbum Dei, quotidie scrutantes Scripturas, si hæc ita se haberent. Et circuibunt civitatem, id est militantem Ecclesiam, quatenus a prædicatoribus audiant verbum salutis quod optant. De hac gentium conversione et fame Amos inquit : Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et mittam famem super terram : non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Dei ; et commovebuntur a mari usque ad mare, id est, circuibunt Ecclesiam, quæ per orbem terrarum longe ac late extenditur.
paras.en: [[58:7|They shall return at evening|Convertentur ad vesperam]], etc. This too is explained in two ways. First, of the Gentiles. [[58:7|They shall return at evening|Convertentur ad vesperam]], that is, the Gentiles shall be converted to Christ in the sixth and last age, as John says in his canonical Epistle: [[1 John 2:18|it is the last hour|Novissima hora est]]; and Paul: We are they [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]]. [[58:7|and shall suffer hunger like dogs|Et famem patientur ut canes]], that is, they shall hunger and thirst after justice, and shall hear the word of God eagerly, as Luke records in the Acts of the Apostles of the Thessalonians [Denis's slip: Acts 17:11 says these were more noble than those of Thessalonica, that is, the Bereans]: These are they [[Acts 17:11|who received the word with all eagerness, daily searching the scriptures, whether these things were so|qui cum omni aviditate receperunt verbum Dei, quotidie scrutantes Scripturas, si hæc ita se haberent]]. [[58:7|and shall go round about the city|Et circuibunt civitatem]], that is, the Church militant, so as to hear from the preachers the word of salvation that they long for. Of this conversion and hunger of the Gentiles Amos says: [[Amos 8:11|Behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will send forth a famine into the land: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst of water, but of hearing the word of the Lord|Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et mittam famem super terram : non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Dei]]; [[Amos 8:12|And they shall move from sea to sea|et commovebuntur a mari usque ad mare]], that is, they shall go round about the Church, which stretches far and wide through the whole world.

paras.t: Ecce loquentur in ore suo : id est, gentes ad fidem conversæ non solum corde, sed etiam ore Christi mirabilia dicent, laudes divinas cantabunt, Deumque verbo et opere audacter et publice confitebuntur : sicut ait Apostolus, Corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem. Et gladius in labiis eorum, id est, prædicatio evangelica erit in ore ipsorum. Hæc enim prædicatio gladius dicitur, juxta illud Apostoli : Et gladium spiritus, quod est verbum Dei. Et in Isaia Christus de Deo Patre loquens : Posuit, inquit, os meum quasi gladium acutum. Prædicatores enim verba instar ensis acuta loquuntur, mundum terribiliter increpando. Quoniam quis audivit ? id est, quoniam pauci sunt qui fide et moribus Evangelio Christi obediunt. Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi. Unde Isaias dicit : Domine, quis credidit auditui nostro ?
paras.en: [[58:8|Behold they shall speak with their mouth|Ecce loquentur in ore suo]]: that is, the nations converted to the faith shall tell the wonders of Christ not only with the heart but also with the mouth, shall sing the divine praises, and shall confess God boldly and openly in word and deed, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 10:10|with the heart, we believe unto justice: but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation|Corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem]]. [[58:8|and a sword is in their lips|Et gladius in labiis eorum]], that is, the preaching of the Gospel shall be in their mouth. For this preaching is called a sword, according to that saying of the Apostle: And [[Eph 6:17|the sword of the Spirit|gladium spiritus]], [[Eph 6:17|which is the word of God|quod est verbum Dei]]. And in Isaias Christ, speaking of God the Father: [[Is 49:2|he hath made|Posuit]], he says, [[Is 49:2|my mouth like a sharp sword|os meum quasi gladium acutum]]. For the preachers speak words sharp as a blade, rebuking the world terribly. [[58:8|for who, say they, hath heard us?|Quoniam quis audivit ?]] that is, because few there are who obey the Gospel of Christ in faith and morals. For [[Matt 20:16|many are called but few chosen|Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi]]. Hence Isaias says: Lord, who [[Is 53:1|hath believed our report|credidit auditui nostro]]?

paras.t: Et tu, Domine, juste judex, Deus omnipotens, sanctus et verax, deridebis eos, id est vocatos et multos, Christi Evan[…] verbo aut opere contradicentes, ad nihilum deduces omnes gentes, id est gentiliter conversantes, omni spirituali et meritorio esse eas privando, finaliterque damnando, atque pro nihilo reputando.
paras.en: [[58:9|But thou, O Lord|Et tu, Domine]], just judge, almighty God, holy and true, [[58:9|shalt laugh at them|deridebis eos]], that is, those called, the many, who gainsay Christ's Gospel […] by word or deed; [[58:9|thou shalt bring all the nations to nothing|ad nihilum deduces omnes gentes]], that is, those who live as the heathen do, depriving them of all spiritual and meritorious being, damning them in the end, and reckoning them as nothing.

paras.t: Secundo exponitur de Judæis hoc modo : Convertentur ad vesperam, id est, in fine mundi et termino hujus ultimæ ætatis convertentur ad Christum, quemadmodum in Osee legitur prophetatum : Dies multos sedebunt filii Israel sine rege, et sine principe, et sine sacrificio, et sine altari, et sine ephod, et sine theraphim : et post hæc convertentur, et quærent Dominum Deum suum et David regem suum (id est Messiam, ut omnes exponunt), et pavebunt ad Dominum, et ad bonum ejus in novissimo dierum. Tunc quippe implebitur quod in Ezechiele prædictum est : Salvabo gregem meum, ait Dominus ; et servus meus David (id est Christus) princeps eorum. Unde ait et Apostolus : Quum plenitudo gentium intraverit, omnis Israel salvus fiet. Nec dissonat quod Christus in Evangelio protestatur, Elias quum venerit, restituet omnia ; et rursus, Fiet unum ovile et unus pastor. Ad prædicationem namque Eliæ convertentur Judæi, secundum quod per Malachiam Dominus ait Judæis : Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam Thesbiten, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis. Et famem patientur ut canes : quoniam tunc Judæi avidissime audient verbum Dei. Et circuibunt civitatem, id est Ecclesiam Christi ex gentibus congregatam, quam modo contemnunt, tunc reverenter atque fideliter visitabunt, quatenus informationem evangelicæ legis acquirant.
paras.en: Secondly, it is expounded of the Jews in this way: [[58:7|They shall return at evening|Convertentur ad vesperam]], that is, at the end of the world and the close of this last age they shall be converted to Christ, as we read prophesied in Osee: [[Osee 3:4|the children of Israel shall sit many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without altar, and without ephod, and without theraphim|Dies multos sedebunt filii Israel sine rege, et sine principe, et sine sacrificio, et sine altari, et sine ephod, et sine theraphim]]; [[Osee 3:5|And after this|et post hæc]] [[Osee 3:5|shall return and shall seek the Lord, their God, and David, their king|convertentur, et quærent Dominum Deum suum et David regem suum]] (that is, the Messias, as all expound it), [[Osee 3:5|and they shall fear the Lord, and his goodness, in the last days|et pavebunt ad Dominum, et ad bonum ejus in novissimo dierum]]. For then shall be fulfilled what was foretold in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:22|I will save my flock|Salvabo gregem meum]], says the Lord; [[Ezech 34:24|and my servant David|et servus meus David]] (that is, Christ) shall be [[Ezech 34:24|the prince|princeps]] of them. Hence the Apostle also says: When [[Rom 11:25|the fulness of the Gentiles should come in|plenitudo gentium intraverit]], [[Rom 11:26|all Israel should be saved|omnis Israel salvus fiet]]. Nor is it out of tune with what Christ declares in the Gospel: [[Mark 9:11|Elias, when he shall come|Elias quum venerit]], [[Mark 9:11|shall restore all things|restituet omnia]]; and again: [[John 10:16|there shall be one fold and one shepherd|Fiet unum ovile et unus pastor]]. For at the preaching of Elias the Jews shall be converted, as the Lord says to the Jews through Malachias: [[Mal 4:5|Behold, I will send you Elias|Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam]] the Thesbite [the Vulgate here reads "the prophet"], [[Mal 4:5|before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord|antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis]]. [[58:7|and shall suffer hunger like dogs|Et famem patientur ut canes]]: for then the Jews shall hear the word of God most eagerly. [[58:7|and shall go round about the city|Et circuibunt civitatem]], that is, the Church of Christ gathered from the Gentiles, which they now despise; then they shall visit it reverently and faithfully, so as to gain instruction in the law of the Gospel.

paras.t: Ecce loquentur in ore suo, etc. Versus iste ita conveniet Judæis tunc convertendis, sicut jam declaratus est convenire gentibus ad fidem conversis. Potest tamen exponi de Judæis qui Christum præsentem spreverunt et occiderunt. Ut sit sensus : Ecce Judæi tempore Christi loquentur in ore suo detractiones et crimina atque blasphemias contra Christum ; et gladius, id est sermo persecutionis et mortis sententiam deprecans, in labiis eorum. Dixerunt enim coram Pilato : Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit. Quoniam quis audivit ? hoc est, Judæi inter se tractabant se velle ista scelera Christo objicere, atque has pœnas ei inferre, quia putabant consilium suum Christum latere, nec aliquem alium ipsorum malignitatem advertere. Volebant enim eum sine præsentia turbæ occidere. Dicebant enim : Non in die festo, ne forte tumultus fieret in populo.
paras.en: [[58:8|Behold they shall speak with their mouth|Ecce loquentur in ore suo]], etc. This verse will fit the Jews who are then to be converted in the same way as it has already been shown to fit the Gentiles converted to the faith. It can, however, be expounded of the Jews who despised and killed Christ when he was present. So that the sense is: [[58:8|Behold|Ecce]], the Jews in the time of Christ [[58:8|shall speak with their mouth|loquentur in ore suo]] slanders and charges and blasphemies against Christ; [[58:8|and a sword|et gladius]], that is, speech of persecution, demanding the sentence of death, [[58:8|is in their lips|in labiis eorum]]. For they said before Pilate: [[John 19:7|We have a law; and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God|Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit]]. [[58:8|for who, say they, hath heard us?|Quoniam quis audivit ?]] That is, the Jews discussed among themselves that they wished to lay these crimes to Christ's charge and to inflict these punishments on him, because they thought that their counsel was hidden from Christ and that no one else noticed their malice. For they wished to kill him without the crowd being present; for they said: [[Matt 26:5|Not on the festival day, lest perhaps there should be a tumult among the people|Non in die festo, ne forte tumultus fieret in populo]].

paras.t: Et tu, Domine, deridebis eos, dando eos in manus Romanorum. Et in hora mortis ipsorum irrisisti eos. In finali quoque judicio ipsos irridebis, ostendendo eos errasse, et irrisione dignos exsistere : sicut superius dictum est, Qui habitat in cœlis, irridebit eos. In libro Proverbiorum quoque legitur : Ego in interitu vestro ridebo et subsannabo, quum vobis quod timebatis evenerit.
paras.en: [[58:9|But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them|Et tu, Domine, deridebis eos]], by giving them into the hands of the Romans. And in the hour of their death thou didst laugh at them. In the final judgement too thou shalt laugh at them, showing that they erred and are worthy of derision, as was said above: [[Ps 2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them|Qui habitat in cœlis, irridebit eos]]. In the book of Proverbs also we read: [[Prov 1:26|I also will laugh in your destruction, and will mock when that shall come to you which you feared|Ego in interitu vestro ridebo et subsannabo, quum vobis quod timebatis evenerit]].

paras.t: Fortitudinem meam ad te custodiam. Hæc sunt verba Christi ad Patrem. Quibus concordat quod ipse in Evangelio testatur : Non potest Filius a se quidquam facere, nisi quod viderit Patrem facientem ; et iterum, Non possum ego a me ipso facere quidquam. Est igitur sensus : Totam meam virtutem, perfectionem atque potentiam ad te, id est ad tuum honorem et laudem, o Pater, custodiam, id est, observabo et ordinabo, ne aliquo modo aberrem, aliquid mihi adscribendo, quum totum a te receperim. Non solum autem refert Christus ad Patrem totam suam virtutem creatam, fortitudinemque humanam, sed etiam divinam et increatam, profitendo se illam quoque recepisse a Patre. Propter quod dicit : Pater quod dedit mihi, majus omnibus est, id est divina essentia quam a Patre accepi. Per hoc enim probat se esse verum Deum : nam subdit, Ego et Pater unum sumus. Increatam autem suam virtutem retulit Christus ad Patrem, tanquam ad originem, non sicut ad finem.
paras.en: [[58:10|I will keep my strength to thee|Fortitudinem meam ad te custodiam]]. These are the words of Christ to the Father. With them agrees what he himself testifies in the Gospel: [[John 5:19|the Son cannot do any thing of himself, but what he seeth the Father doing|Non potest Filius a se quidquam facere, nisi quod viderit Patrem facientem]]; and again: [[John 5:30|I cannot of myself do any thing|Non possum ego a me ipso facere quidquam]]. The sense, then, is: All my power, perfection and might [[58:10|to thee|ad te]], that is, to thy honour and praise, O Father, [[58:10|I will keep|custodiam]], that is, I will observe and order, so as not to stray in any way by ascribing anything to myself, since I have received the whole from thee. And Christ refers to the Father not only all his created power and human strength, but also the divine and uncreated, professing that he received this too from the Father. Wherefore he says: [[John 10:29|That which my Father hath given me is greater than all|Pater quod dedit mihi, majus omnibus est]], that is, the divine essence, which I have received from the Father. For by this he proves that he is true God; for he adds: [[John 10:30|I and the Father are one|Ego et Pater unum sumus]]. But Christ referred his uncreated power to the Father as to its origin, not as to its end.

paras.t: Vel sic : Fortitudinem meam, qua adversarios meos possem subito variisque tormentis destruere, dejicere atque occidere, ad te custodiam, id est, secundum voluntatem tuam, o Deus Pater, restringam et differam, nec statim ulciscar me ipsum, sed tempus pœnitentiæ ipsis concedam. Hinc enim ait Petro : An putas quia non possum rogare Patrem, et exhibebit mihi modo plus quam duodecim legiones angelorum ? Nam et quum solo verbo, passione instante, hostes suos prostravisset dicendo, Ego sum, fortitudinem suam compescuit, eosque surgere fecit.
paras.en: Or thus: [[58:10|my strength|Fortitudinem meam]], by which I could suddenly destroy, cast down and kill my adversaries with various torments, [[58:10|to thee|ad te]] [[58:10|I will keep|custodiam]], that is, according to thy will, O God the Father, I will restrain and put off, and will not at once avenge myself, but will grant them a time for repentance. For hence he says to Peter: [[Matt 26:53|Thinkest thou that I cannot ask my Father, and he will give me presently more than twelve legions of angels?|An putas quia non possum rogare Patrem, et exhibebit mihi modo plus quam duodecim legiones angelorum]] For when, as the passion drew near, he had laid his enemies low by a word alone, saying, [[John 18:5|I am he|Ego sum]], he held back his strength and made them rise again[[John 18:6||]].

paras.t: Quia Deus susceptor meus es : id est, Verbum Dei humanitatem meam ad suam personalitatem assumpsit. Deus quoque Trinitas susceptor est Christi hominis, quoniam omnes ejus preces exaudivit, resurgentem et ascendentem accepit, atque ad dexteram suam collocavit. Unde Deus Pater de Christo per Isaiam ait : Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum.
paras.en: [[58:10|for thou art my protector|Quia Deus susceptor meus es]] [*susceptor*, rendered "protector", means literally "one who takes up"; Denis reads it so]: that is, the Word of God took up my manhood into his own person. God the Trinity too is the one who took up the man Christ, for he heard all his prayers, received him as he rose and ascended, and set him at his right hand. Hence God the Father says of Christ through Isaias: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum]] [*suscipiam*, "I will take him up", the verb of *susceptor*].

paras.t: Deus meus, misericordia ejus præveniet me. Nullam unquam creaturam, imo nec omnes simul Deus tam gratiose misericorditerque prævenit, ut Christum hominem. Sola enim benignitate et gratia Dei, assumpta est Christi humana natura a Verbo : non enim præcesserant merita, sed in eodem instanti est creata et Deo unita.
paras.en: [[58:11|My God, his mercy shall prevent me|Deus meus, misericordia ejus præveniet me]] [that is, shall go before me]. Never did God go before any creature, nay, nor all of them together, so graciously and mercifully as the man Christ. For it was by the sole kindness and grace of God that Christ's human nature was assumed by the Word: for no merits had gone before, but in the same instant it was created and united to God.

paras.t: Deus ostendit mihi super inimicos meos, id est, mihi homini revelavit de ipsis Judæis quod sequitur. Ne occidas eos, id est, noli, o Christe, Fili dilecte, crucifixores tuos eorumque posteros penitus eradicare de terra, sed ora pro eis in bono, dicendo : Pater, ignosce illis. Nec omnes interficiantur, sed quidam eorum remaneant in memoriam ac testimonium evangelicæ veritatis. Ideo subjungit : nequando obliviscantur populi mei, id est, ne aliquando Christiani me et legem meam tradant oblivioni, non credendo quod fuerint aliquando Judæi, qui tantum scelus perpetrare præsumpserint ; sed videndo Judæos inter se commorari, incessabiliter sint memores mei, elicientes etiam fidei suæ argumentum ex repulsa, dispersione ac derelictione Judæorum. Ecce ex his trahitur ratio cur Judæi non sint occidendi, nisi speciali peccato meruerint.
paras.en: [[58:12|God shall let me see over my enemies|Deus ostendit mihi super inimicos meos]] [Denis reads *ostendit*, "hath shewn", for *ostendet*], that is, he hath revealed to me as man, concerning the Jews themselves, what follows. [[58:12|slay them not|Ne occidas eos]], that is: Do not, O Christ, beloved Son, root out from the earth altogether thy crucifiers and their descendants, but pray for them for their good, saying: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them|Pater, ignosce illis]]. Nor let them all be killed, but let some of them remain as a memorial and witness of the truth of the Gospel. Therefore he adds: [[58:12|lest at any time my people forget|nequando obliviscantur populi mei]], that is, lest at any time Christians consign me and my law to oblivion, not believing that there were once Jews who dared to commit so great a crime; but seeing the Jews dwelling among them, let them be unceasingly mindful of me, drawing even an argument for their faith from the rejection, dispersion and abandonment of the Jews. See, from this is drawn the reason why the Jews are not to be killed, unless they have deserved it by some particular sin.

paras.t: Deinde Christus ait ad Patrem : Disperge illos per totum mundum, ut sint vagi in nationibus : sicut per Osee prædictum est ; in virtute tua omnipotente, per quam tibi omnia facilia sunt, per quam etiam contulisti Romanis potentiam dispergendi Judæos. Et depone eos a prosperitate et gloria temporali, a regno, a sacerdotio, omnique honore legis paternæ, protector meus, id est meæ humanitatis, Domine Pater : depone, inquam, non ignoscendo, sed ab effectu impediendo, Delictum oris eorum, hoc est sermonem labiorum ipsorum, quo dixerunt coram Pilato : Si non esset hic malefactor, non tibi tradidissemus eum ; et alibi : Domine, recordati sumus quia seductor ille dixit adhuc vivens, Post tres dies resurgam.
paras.en: Then Christ says to the Father: [[58:12|Scatter them|Disperge illos]] through the whole world, that they may be [[Osee 9:17|wanderers among the nations|vagi in nationibus]], as was foretold through Osee; [[58:12|by thy power|in virtute tua]] almighty, by which all things are easy to thee, by which also thou gavest the Romans the might to scatter the Jews. [[58:12|and bring them down|Et depone eos]] from temporal prosperity and glory, from kingship, from the priesthood, and from all the honour of the law of their fathers, [[58:12|my protector|protector meus]], that is, of my manhood, [[58:12|O Lord|Domine]] the Father: bring down, I say, not by pardoning it but by hindering it from its effect, [[58:13|the sin of their mouth|Delictum oris eorum]] [Denis takes *delictum* as the object of *depone*, "bring down"], that is, [[58:13|the word of their lips|sermonem labiorum ipsorum]], by which they said before Pilate: [[John 18:30|If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up to thee|Si non esset hic malefactor, non tibi tradidissemus eum]]; and elsewhere: [[Matt 27:63|Sir, we have remembered, that that seducer said, while he was yet alive: After three days I will rise again|Domine, recordati sumus quia seductor ille dixit adhuc vivens, Post tres dies resurgam]].

paras.t: Et comprehendantur in superbia sua, id est, in peccato suo moriantur : secundum quod Christus dixit Judæis, In peccato vestro moriemini : quod Christus dicit potius prænuntiando quam imprecando. Vel, Comprehendantur, id est, obsideantur, concludantur, et capiantur in civitate Jerusalem ab exercitu Romanorum, sicut et Christus prædixit. Vel, Comprehendantur in superbia sua, id est, confundantur a Christi Apostolis, verbis atque miraculis Christi resurrectionem docentibus, demonstrantibus, ac palam probantibus.
paras.en: [[58:13|and let them be taken in their pride|Et comprehendantur in superbia sua]], that is, let them die in their sin, as Christ said to the Jews: [[John 8:21|you shall die in your sin|In peccato vestro moriemini]]; which Christ says rather by way of foretelling than of imprecation. Or, [[58:13|let them be taken|Comprehendantur]], that is, let them be besieged, shut in and captured in the city of Jerusalem by the army of the Romans, as Christ also foretold[[Luke 19:43||]][[Luke 19:44||]]. Or, [[58:13|let them be taken in their pride|Comprehendantur in superbia sua]], that is, let them be confounded by the Apostles of Christ, who taught, showed and openly proved the resurrection of Christ by words and miracles.

paras.t: Et de exsecratione, id est abominatione, qua Christo detraxerunt, eumque spreverunt, dicentes, Homo vorax, amicus publicanorum ; et mendacio, quod contra Christum locuti sunt, dicendo, Seducit turbam ; et, quod discipuli furati essent eum de monumento ; annuntiabuntur, id est, redarguentur a judice Christo, in consummatione, id est in fine mundi judicioque finali. De qua consummatione Christus in Evangelio dicit : Sic erit in consummatione sæculi. Tunc enim videbunt in quem pupugerunt. Unde clarius subdit : in ira consummationis, id est in divina ultione et increpatione quæ erit in die judicii, redarguentur a Christo, quia tunc dicet eis : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Et non erunt in numero electorum, neque in gloria : juxta illud, Tollatur impius ne videat gloriam Dei. Tunc enim in æternum peribunt.
paras.en: [[58:13|And for their cursing|Et de exsecratione]], that is, the abomination with which they disparaged Christ and despised him, saying: [[Matt 11:19|a man that is a glutton|Homo vorax]], [[Matt 11:19|a friend of publicans|amicus publicanorum]]; [[58:13|and lying|et mendacio]], which they spoke against Christ, saying: [[John 7:12|he seduceth the people|Seducit turbam]] [the margin gives John viii, 12; the words are at John 7:12]; and that his disciples had stolen him from the tomb[[Matt 28:13||]]; [[58:13|they shall be talked of|annuntiabuntur]] [literally "they shall be announced"], that is, they shall be reproved by Christ the judge, [[58:14|When they are consumed|in consummatione]], that is, at the end of the world and the final judgement. Of which consummation Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 13:40|so shall it be at the end of the world|Sic erit in consummatione sæculi]] [the same word *consummatio*, "consummation, end", that the Psalm uses]. For then [[John 19:37|They shall look on him whom they pierced|videbunt in quem pupugerunt]][[Apoc 1:7||]]. Hence he adds more clearly: [[58:14|when they are consumed by thy wrath|in ira consummationis]], that is, in the divine vengeance and rebuke that shall be on the day of judgement, they shall be reproved by Christ, for then he will say to them: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. [[58:14|and they shall be no more|Et non erunt]] in the number of the elect, nor in glory, according to that saying: Let the wicked be taken away, that he see not the glory of God[[Is 26:10||]] [the margin gives Is. xxvi, 10, "according to the Septuagint"; the Douay-Rheims reads "he shall not see the glory of the Lord"]. For then they shall perish for ever.

paras.t: Et scient, in die novissimo, per experientiam pœnæ, et per corporalem Christi intuitum, quia Deus, id est Christus, dominabitur Jacob, id est vero Israeli, videlicet populo Judæorum in Jesum Christum credenti, et finium terræ, id est omnium gentium in ipsum credentium. Horum enim post finale judicium dominabitur Christus Deus in triumphanti Ecclesia, sicut et nunc dominatur universorum fidelium in Ecclesia militante.
paras.en: [[58:14|And they shall know|Et scient]], on the last day, by the experience of punishment and by the bodily sight of Christ, [[58:14|that God|quia Deus]], that is, Christ, [[58:14|will rule Jacob|dominabitur Jacob]], that is, the true Israel, namely the Jewish people that believes in Jesus Christ, [[58:14|and all the ends of the earth|et finium terræ]], that is, all the nations that believe in him. For over these, after the final judgement, Christ God shall rule in the Church triumphant, as he now also rules over all the faithful in the Church militant.

paras.t: Convertentur ad vesperam, etc. Iste versus jam semel expositus est : quem modo resumit Propheta ad consolandum se ipsum super interitu populi sui. Consolans ergo se ipsum, insinuat quod reliquiæ salvæ fient, quemadmodum Isaias et Paulus testantur : Si fuerit, inquiunt, semen filiorum Israel sicut arena maris, reliquiæ salvabuntur.
paras.en: [[58:15|They shall return at evening|Convertentur ad vesperam]], etc. This verse has already been expounded once; the Prophet takes it up again now to console himself over the ruin of his people. Consoling himself, then, he intimates that a remnant shall be saved, as Isaias and Paul testify: [[Rom 9:27|If|Si fuerit]], they say, [[Rom 9:27|the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved|semen filiorum Israel sicut arena maris, reliquiæ salvabuntur]][[Is 10:22||]] [Denis reads *semen*, "the seed", for "the number"].

paras.t: Ipsi dispergentur ad manducandum : id est, Judæi in fine sæculi convertendi, circumquaque ibunt ad homines virtuosos, ut panem vitæ et intellectus acquirant, cognoscendo et observando Christi doctrinam ; sicque obedientiæ cibum manducent, de quo asserit Christus : Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem Patris mei. Si vero non fuerint saturati pane prædicto, id est justitia quam maxime desiderabunt, tunc et murmurabunt, non contra Deum, sed contra se ipsos, redarguentes se, quod tam sero conversi sunt, nec juxta desiderium suum proficere possunt. Vel : Dispergentur ad manducandum corpus et sanguinem Christi : quæ utique tunc devotissime sument, sicut plenissime credent ; imo devotissime Sacramentum altaris percipient, sicut primitiva Ecclesia, quæ (ut Lucas affirmat) perseveravit in communione fractionis panis. Si vero non fuerint saturati gratia sacramentali, videlicet effectibus hujus superdignissimi Sacramenti, et murmurabunt : secundum intellectum inductum.
paras.en: [[58:16|They shall be scattered abroad to eat|Ipsi dispergentur ad manducandum]]: that is, the Jews who are to be converted at the end of the world shall go about on every side to virtuous men, to gain the bread of life and of understanding by learning and keeping the teaching of Christ; and so they shall eat the food of obedience, of which Christ declares: [[John 4:34|My meat is to do the will|Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem]] of my Father. [[58:16|if they be not filled|Si vero non fuerint saturati]] with the aforesaid bread, that is, with the justice they will most greatly desire, then [[58:16|and shall murmur|et murmurabunt]], not against God but against themselves, reproaching themselves that they were converted so late and cannot make progress as they desire. Or: [[58:16|shall be scattered abroad to eat|Dispergentur ad manducandum]] the body and blood of Christ, which they will then receive most devoutly, as they will believe most fully; nay, they will receive the Sacrament of the altar most devoutly, like the primitive Church, which (as Luke affirms) persevered [[Acts 2:42|in the communication of the breaking of bread|in communione fractionis panis]]. [[58:16|if they be not filled|Si vero non fuerint saturati]] with sacramental grace, namely with the effects of this most worthy Sacrament, [[58:16|and shall murmur|et murmurabunt]], in the sense already given.

paras.t: Ego autem, o Deus, cantabo fortitudinem tuam, id est, laudabo coram discipulis meis tuam potentiam, qua me resuscitasti a mortuis ; et exsultabo, id est, exsultanter gaudioseque proferam et annuntiabo, mane, prima sabbati, quando Mariæ Magdalenæ apparui, misericordiam tuam, id est gratiam qua me tam celeriter resuscitasti, et quam detentis in limbo universoque mundo per me dare dignatus es. Christus enim post resurrectionem, Dei potentiam prædicavit, quando (ut Lucas commemorat) per quadraginta dies apparens discipulis, loquebatur eis de regno Dei : Non est, inquiens, vestrum nosse tempora vel momenta, quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate. Exsultavit quoque mane, id est tempore evangelicæ legis et gratiæ, misericordiam Dei, quando discipulis dixit : Quicumque crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit ; atque iterum : Accipite Spiritum Sanctum ; quorum remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis, etc.
paras.en: [[58:17|But I|Ego autem]], O God, [[58:17|will sing thy strength|cantabo fortitudinem tuam]], that is, I will praise before my disciples thy power, by which thou hast raised me from the dead; [[58:17|and will extol|et exsultabo]], that is, I will proclaim and announce exultantly and joyfully, [[58:17|in the morning|mane]], on the first day of the week, when I appeared to Mary Magdalen[[Mark 16:9||]], [[58:17|thy mercy|misericordiam tuam]], that is, the grace by which thou hast raised me so swiftly, and which thou hast deigned to give through me to those held in limbo and to the whole world. For after the resurrection Christ preached the power of God, when (as Luke records) appearing to the disciples for forty days he spoke to them of the kingdom of God[[Acts 1:3||]]: [[Acts 1:7|It is not|Non est]], he said, [[Acts 1:7|for you to know the time or moments, which the Father hath put in his own power|vestrum nosse tempora vel momenta, quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate]]. He also extolled in the morning, that is, in the time of the law of the Gospel and of grace, the mercy of God, when he said to the disciples: [[Mark 16:16|He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved|Quicumque crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit]]; and again: [[John 20:22|Receive ye the Holy Ghost|Accipite Spiritum Sanctum]]; [[John 20:23|Whose sins you shall forgive, they are forgiven them|quorum remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis]], etc.

paras.t: Quia factus es, o Deus Pater, susceptor meus : secundum sensum jam dictum ; et refugium meum in die tribulationis meæ, id est toto tempore conversationis meæ in mundo, quæ tribulationibus plena fuit. Nam et passione instante, Christus ad Patrem confugit, orans et dicens : Mi Pater, si vis, transfer calicem istum a me. Moriens quoque clamavit : Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum. Et istud conveniebat Christo, in quantum erat passibilis et aliquo modo viator.
paras.en: [[58:17|For thou art become|Quia factus es]], O God the Father, [[58:17|my support|susceptor meus]], in the sense already given; [[58:17|and my refuge, in the day of my trouble|et refugium meum in die tribulationis meæ]], that is, the whole time of my life in the world, which was full of tribulations. For when the passion was at hand, too, Christ took refuge with the Father, praying and saying: My Father, [[Luke 22:42|if thou wilt, remove this chalice from me|si vis, transfer calicem istum a me]]. And dying he cried: [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]. And this befitted Christ insofar as he was passible and in some manner a wayfarer [that is, one still on the way, not yet only a comprehensor, one who already holds the end in glory].

paras.t: Adjutor meus, tibi psallam. Deus Christi hominis adjutor fuit in omnibus, juxta illud Isaiæ prophetæ : Dominus Deus auxiliator meus, ideo non sum confusus. Et in Evangelio dixit : Pater in me manens, ipse facit opera. Huic adjutori Christus per se ipsum et fideles psallit, verbis et operibus ipsum laudando.
paras.en: [[58:18|Unto thee, O my helper, will I sing|Adjutor meus, tibi psallam]]. God was the helper of the man Christ in all things, according to that saying of the prophet Isaias: [[Is 50:7|The Lord God is my helper, therefore am I not confounded|Dominus Deus auxiliator meus, ideo non sum confusus]] [the margin gives Is. i, 7; the words are at Isaias 50:7]. And in the Gospel he said: [[John 14:10|the Father who abideth in me, he doth the works|Pater in me manens, ipse facit opera]]. To this helper Christ sings, by himself and by the faithful, praising him in words and works.

paras.t: Quia Deus susceptor meus es, Deus meus, misericordia mea. Christus ut homo, vocat Deum misericordiam suam, non quia pœnam aut culpam propriam sibi indulsit ; sed quia tam gratiosissime ipsum in omni benedictione dulcedinis prævenit et adimplevit, ac per hoc ab omni peccato præservavit. Incomparabili enim gratia animam ejus implevit, faciens eam divinæ essentiæ contemplatricem per speciem excellentissimo modo, a primo suæ creationis exordio.
paras.en: [[58:18|for thou art God my defence|Quia Deus susceptor meus es]], [[58:18|my God my mercy|Deus meus, misericordia mea]]. Christ as man calls God his mercy, not because God pardoned him any punishment or fault of his own, but because he went before him so very graciously with every blessing of sweetness, and filled him[[Ps 20:4||]], and by this preserved him from all sin. For he filled his soul with incomparable grace, making it a beholder of the divine essence face to face [*per speciem*, that is, by direct vision, not by faith] in the most excellent manner, from the first beginning of its creation.

58.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI OCTAVI.
58.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same fifty-eighth psalm.

paras.t: Moraliter insuper convenit psalmus iste Ecclesiæ Christi tribulatæ, et unicuique Christiano afflicto.
paras.en: Morally, moreover, this psalm fits the Church of Christ in tribulation, and every afflicted Christian.

paras.t: Fidelis ergo tentationibus variisque adversis circumdatus, totis medullis proclamet ad Deum: Eripe me de inimicis meis, Deus meus, id est, ab invidentibus atque occulte et industriose mihi nocere studentibus, erue me. Hoc autem ad invisibiles hostes maxime pertinet. Unde vehementer egemus adjutorio Dei, id est discretione spirituum, seu illuminatione Spiritus Sancti, ad cognoscendum insidias dæmonis, quatenus cum Apostolo dicere valeamus: Non ignoramus cogitationes ejus. Et ab insurgentibus in me, id est a manifestis invasoribus ac persecutoribus, libera me, ne animam meam ad impatientiam aut alia vitia pertrahant, ne damna aut vulnera amplius inferant quam animæ expedit. Hinc enim Apostolus discipulos deprecatur: Orate ut liberemur a malis et importunis hominibus.
paras.en: Let the faithful man, then, beset by temptations and by adversities of many kinds, cry out to God with all his heart [literally "with all his marrow"]: [[58:2|Deliver me from my enemies, O my God|Eripe me de inimicis meis, Deus meus]]; that is, rescue me from those who envy me and who strive secretly and busily to harm me. This applies above all to the invisible enemies. Hence we have great need of the help of God, that is, of the discernment of spirits, or the enlightenment of the Holy Ghost, to recognise the snares of the devil, so that we may be able to say with the Apostle: [[2 Cor 2:11|we are not ignorant of his devices|Non ignoramus cogitationes ejus]]. And [[58:2|from them that rise up against me|ab insurgentibus in me]], that is, from open assailants and persecutors, [[58:2|defend me|libera me]], lest they drag my soul into impatience or other vices, lest they inflict losses or wounds beyond what is good for the soul. For this is why the Apostle begs his disciples: Pray, [[2 Thess 3:2|that we may be delivered from importunate and evil men|ut liberemur a malis et importunis hominibus]].

paras.t: Eripe me de operantibus iniquitatem, id est ab omni male viventi, quamvis non sit æmulus meus: imo a familiaribus, propinquis, vicinis et fratribus malam vitam ducentibus, maxime erui indigemus, ne cum perversis pervertamur, ne ipsis in malo consentiamus, ne propinquitas naturæ, loci et convictus, fiat occasio imitationis perversæ. Et de viris sanguinum, qui affectu et opere proximos suos occidunt in carne aut corde. Qui enim alium ad mortale peccatum inducit, spiritualiter eum occidit. Omnis quoque qui fratrem suum odit, homicida est. Ab his, Domine, salva me, ne sim similis eis.
paras.en: [[58:3|Deliver me from them that work iniquity|Eripe me de operantibus iniquitatem]], that is, from everyone who lives wickedly, even if he is no rival of mine: indeed, it is above all from members of our household, kinsmen, neighbours and brethren who lead a wicked life that we need to be rescued, lest we be perverted with the perverse[[Ps 17:27||]], lest we consent with them in evil, lest nearness of nature, of place and of common life become an occasion of perverse imitation. And [[58:3|from bloody men|de viris sanguinum]], who in desire and in deed slay their neighbours in the flesh or in the heart. For whoever leads another into mortal sin slays him spiritually. Also, [[1 John 3:15|Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer|Omnis quoque qui fratrem suum odit, homicida est]] [the margin reads Joann. iii, 15; the words are from the First Epistle of John]. From these, O Lord, [[58:3|save me|salva me]], lest I be like them.

paras.t: Denique primus versus hoc modo convenienter exponitur: Eripe me de inimicis meis, Deus meus, id est, a malis habitibus seu consuetudinibus vitiosis intus latentibus et quodammodo quiescentibus redime me, per gratiam talia funditus ex corde meo eradicando, oppositosque virtutum habitus inferendo. Et ab insurgentibus in me, id est ab actualibus vitiis, a passionibus impetuosis, a motibus inordinatis, libera me, quatenus per gratiam tuam hujusmodi statim abjiciam, vincam, atque de die in diem minus ac rarius sentiam.
paras.en: Lastly, the first verse is fittingly explained in this way: [[58:2|Deliver me from my enemies, O my God|Eripe me de inimicis meis, Deus meus]]; that is, redeem me from evil habits, or vicious customs, that lie hidden within and are in a manner at rest, by rooting such things out of my heart entirely through grace and putting in their place the opposite habits of virtue. And [[58:2|from them that rise up against me|ab insurgentibus in me]], that is, from actual vices [that is, sins committed in act, as distinct from habits], from violent passions, from disordered movements, [[58:2|defend me|libera me]], so that through Thy grace I may cast off such things at once, overcome them, and feel them less and less often from day to day.

paras.t: Quia ecce, o Domine, prædicti adversarii ceperunt animam meam, id est, vinculis peccatorum eam vinxerunt, in peccati consensum eam trahendo. Vel, Ceperunt, id est, obsederunt, invaserunt, et capere tentaverunt animam meam, insidiantes saluti mentis aut corporis sospitati. Undique namque anima nostra circumvallatur hostibus, id est impugnationibus mundi, carnis et dæmonis. Irruerunt in me fortes adversarii, scilicet dæmones, mundi potentes, aut vitia in me radicata, vel ad quæ ex natura proclivis sum. Hi quotidie irruunt in nos, conantes subvertere animas nostras. Idcirco incessanter clamandum est nobis ad Dominum.
paras.en: [[58:4|For behold|Quia ecce]], O Lord, the aforesaid adversaries [[58:4|have caught my soul|ceperunt animam meam]], that is, they have bound it with the chains of sins, by drawing it into consent to sin. Or, [[58:4|they have caught|Ceperunt]], that is, they have besieged, attacked and tried to catch my soul, lying in wait for the health of the mind or the safety of the body. For our soul is hemmed in by enemies on every side, that is, by the assaults of the world, the flesh and the devil. [[58:4|The mighty have rushed in upon me|Irruerunt in me fortes]]: mighty adversaries, namely the demons, the powerful of the world, or the vices rooted in me, or those to which I am inclined by nature. These rush in upon us daily, trying to overthrow our souls. Therefore we must cry unceasingly to the Lord.

paras.t: Neque iniquitas mea, neque peccatum meum, Domine, id est, nulla culpa merui pati ista flagella. Hoc, proh dolor! paucissimis convenit, illis videlicet qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam: qui dicere possunt cum sancto Job, Hæc passus sum sine iniquitate manus meæ, quum mundas haberem ad Deum preces: his scilicet quibus pro bonis mala redduntur: qui cum Apostolo dicere queunt, Maledicimur, et benedicimus. Talis quoque fuit beatissimus David editor psalmi præsentis: qui quum multa bona fecisset Sauli, gravissimam persecutionem patiebatur ab eo.
paras.en: [[58:5|Neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord|Neque iniquitas mea, neque peccatum meum, Domine]]; that is, by no fault of mine have I deserved to suffer these scourges. This, alas, fits very few: namely those who [[Matt 5:10|suffer persecution for justice' sake|persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam]]; who can say with holy Job, [[Job 16:18|These things have I suffered without the iniquity of my hand, when I offered pure prayers to God|Hæc passus sum sine iniquitate manus meæ, quum mundas haberem ad Deum preces]]; those, that is, to whom evil is returned for good; who can say with the Apostle, [[1 Cor 4:12|We are reviled: and we bless|Maledicimur, et benedicimus]]. Such too was the most blessed David, the author of the present psalm, who, though he had done Saul much good, suffered most grievous persecution from him.

paras.t: Sine iniquitate cucurri, et direxi. Hoc nulli præter Christum ejusque gloriosam Genitricem absolute convenire videtur, nisi taliter exponatur: Sine iniquitate, id est sine peccato mortali, cucurri viam hujus exsilii vel mandatorum; et direxi opera mea, cogitationes ac verba secundum divinæ legis præcepta. Vel, Sine iniquitate cucurri, id est, in peccatis non perseveravi, et de venialibus quotidie satisfeci. Sic enim Apostolus ait: Nihil mihi conscius sum. Et Job: Neque reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea, videlicet quoad peccata mortalia: sine venialibus namque non fuit. Solent autem interdum homines sancti propriam perfectionem sine omni superbia enarrare et confiteri, propter rationabiles causas, scilicet ad honorem Dei, ad proximi ædificationem, aut ut sibi faciant supplicandi fiduciam, vel spiritus pusillanimitatem expellant. Unde piissimus regum Ezechias, pro magna causa oraturus, sic ait: Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et corde perfecto, et quod bonum est in oculis tuis fecerim. Jeremias quoque de se ipso ad nostram informationem ait: Non sedi in consilio ludentium, et diem hominis non concupivi.
paras.en: [[58:5|Without iniquity have I run, and directed my steps|Sine iniquitate cucurri, et direxi]] [the Latin has only *direxi*, "I have directed", with no object]. This seems to fit absolutely no one but Christ and His glorious Mother, unless it is explained thus: [[58:5|without iniquity|Sine iniquitate]], that is, without mortal sin, [[58:5|have I run|cucurri]] the way of this exile, or of the commandments; [[58:5|and directed|et direxi]] my works, thoughts and words according to the precepts of the divine law. Or, [[58:5|without iniquity have I run|Sine iniquitate cucurri]], that is, I have not persevered in sins, and have made satisfaction daily for venial ones. For so the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 4:4|I am not conscious to myself of anything|Nihil mihi conscius sum]]. And Job: [[Job 27:6|my heart doth not reprehend me in all my life|Neque reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea]], namely as regards mortal sins; for he was not without venial ones. Now holy men are sometimes wont to recount and confess their own perfection without any pride, for reasonable causes: namely for the honour of God, for the edification of their neighbour, or to give themselves confidence in praying, or to drive out faintheartedness of spirit. Hence Ezechias, the most devout of kings, being about to pray for a great cause, speaks thus: [[Is 38:3|remember how I have walked before thee in truth, and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in thy sight|Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et corde perfecto, et quod bonum est in oculis tuis fecerim]][[4 Kings 20:3||]] [Denis has "Remember, O Lord, how …"]. Jeremias too says of himself, for our instruction: [[Jer 15:17|I sat not in the assembly of jesters|Non sedi in consilio ludentium]], and [[Jer 17:16|I have not desired the day of man|diem hominis non concupivi]].

paras.t: Exsurge in occursum meum: id est, in omni eventu, causa, opere atque negotio, mihi, o Domine, approxima præsensque esto, ostende te mihi, et suscipe me. Occurre ergo, non locum mutando, quum tu sis incircumscriptibilis atque immobilis; sed opem et gratiam impendendo, quia tu solus servare me potes.
paras.en: [[58:6|Rise up thou to meet me|Exsurge in occursum meum]]: that is, in every event, cause, work and business, draw near to me, O Lord, and be present; show Thyself to me, and take me up. Meet me, then, not by changing place, since Thou art uncircumscribable and immovable, but by bestowing help and grace, for Thou alone canst save me.

paras.t: Occursus autem Dei quandoque in malo accipitur, scilicet pro resistentia et ultione qua Deus peccatoris voluntatem ab opere impedit, punit ac damnat, secundum quod Dominus de peccatoribus protestatur: Occurram eis quasi ursa raptis catulis. Interdum vero in bono accipitur, sicut jam dictum est. Sicque puer Abrahæ: Domine, inquit, obsecro, occurre hodie mihi, et fac misericordiam, etc. Nos igitur, considerantes quia adjutorio Dei indesinenter in omni negotio indigemus, semper dicamus: Exsurge in occursum meum, Domine. Sed ut hujus precis sortiamur effectum, agamus quod Amos scribit: Præparare in occursum Dei tui, id est, fac quod in te est, et para te ipsum, ut dignus efficiaris obviatione divina. Hinc etiam per Jeremiam Dominus ait: Quis est iste qui applicet cor suum ut appropinquet mihi?
paras.en: Now the meeting of God [Latin *occursus*, a coming to meet, which may be friendly or hostile] is sometimes taken in a bad sense, namely for the resistance and vengeance by which God hinders the sinner's will from its work, punishes and condemns it; as the Lord declares of sinners: [[Osee 13:8|I will meet them as a bear that is robbed of her whelps|Occurram eis quasi ursa raptis catulis]]. But sometimes it is taken in a good sense, as has just been said. So Abraham's servant says: [[Gen 24:12|O Lord|Domine]], [[Gen 24:12|meet me today, I beseech thee, and shew kindness|obsecro, occurre hodie mihi, et fac misericordiam]], etc. We therefore, considering that we need the help of God unceasingly in every business, should always say: [[58:6|Rise up thou to meet me|Exsurge in occursum meum]], O Lord. But that we may obtain the effect of this prayer, let us do what Amos writes: [[Amos 4:12|be prepared to meet thy God|Præparare in occursum Dei tui]]; that is, do what is in thee, and prepare thyself, so that thou mayest be made worthy of the divine meeting. Hence also the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 30:21|who is this that setteth his heart to approach to me|Quis est iste qui applicet cor suum ut appropinquet mihi]]?

paras.t: Et vide, id est, o Domine, clementer considera quanta mihi instent discrimina, quantum indigeo gratia tua, quam affectuose et confidenter te invoco.
paras.en: [[58:6|And behold|Et vide]]: that is, O Lord, consider mercifully how great are the dangers that press upon me, how much I need Thy grace, how lovingly and confidently I call upon Thee.

paras.t: Convertentur ad vesperam. Hoc dicere potest mater Ecclesia, de his qui nec in adolescentia, neque in juventute obedire volunt exhortationibus sanctis. De talibus namque desperandum non est, quia fortassis in tertia vigilia seu undecima hora convertentur, et famem justitiæ patientur ut canes, tam cupide proficiendo, ut mane conversos præcedant, fiantque novissimi primi, et primi novissimi.
paras.en: [[58:7|They shall return at evening|Convertentur ad vesperam]]. Mother Church can say this of those who will obey holy exhortations neither in youth nor in early manhood. For one must not despair of such men, since perhaps at the third watch, or at the eleventh hour, they will be converted [Latin *convertentur*, "they shall return" or "be converted"], [[58:7|and shall suffer hunger|et famem]] for justice [[58:7|like dogs|patientur ut canes]], making progress so eagerly that they go before those converted in the morning, and [[Matt 20:16|the last be first and the first last|novissimi primi, et primi novissimi]].
