paras.t: Fortitudinem meam ad te custodiam, id est, totam potestatem, virtutem et gratiam meam tibi attribuam, dicendo cum sancto Job, Ecce non est auxilium mihi in me; et cum Apostolo, Gratia Dei sum id quod sum. Confiteborque verum esse quod tu, Domine, per Prophetam sanctum dicis: Perditio tua, Israel, ex te; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum. Si ergo fortitudinem tibi divinitus præstitam optas servare, non perdere, omne quod es, potes et agis, Deo adscribe, dicque illud: Domine, fortitudo mea et refugium meum et robur meum.
paras.en: [[58:10|I will keep my strength to thee|Fortitudinem meam ad te custodiam]]: that is, I will ascribe to Thee all my power, strength and grace, saying with holy Job, [[Job 6:13|Behold there is no help for me in myself|Ecce non est auxilium mihi in me]]; and with the Apostle, [[1 Cor 15:10|by the grace of God, I am what I am|Gratia Dei sum id quod sum]]. And I will confess to be true what Thou, O Lord, sayest by the holy Prophet: [[Osee 13:9|Destruction is thy own, O Israel: thy help is only in me|Perditio tua, Israel, ex te; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum]]. If then thou wishest to keep, and not to lose, the strength given thee from heaven, ascribe to God all that thou art, canst and doest, and say this: [[Jer 16:19|O Lord, my might, and my strength, and my refuge|Domine, fortitudo mea et refugium meum et robur meum]].

paras.t: Quia Deus susceptor meus es. Deus Dei Filius susceptor est nostræ naturæ in incarnatione; et Deus Trinitas susceptor nostrorum desideriorum in oratione, nostræ pœnitentiæ in justificatione, nostri obsequii in sua pietate, nostræ animæ in glorificatione, nostrique corporis in resuscitatione. Imo benignissimus Dominus Deus noster incessanter paratus est nos in brachiis suæ paternæ dilectionis recipere, confovere, protegere, atque salvare, sicut per Prophetam animæ peccatrici dicit: Tu fornicata es cum amatoribus multis; tamen revertere ad me, et non avertam faciem meam a te; et iterum: Noluisti erubescere; ergo saltem amodo voca me, Pater meus es tu. Et per Ezechielem dicitur: Quacumque hora peccator ingemuerit, omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor amplius.
paras.en: [[58:10|For thou art my protector|Quia Deus susceptor meus es]] [Latin *susceptor*, literally "one who takes up" or "receives": what follows turns on this]. God the Son of God is the One who takes up our nature in the Incarnation; and God the Trinity is the One who receives our desires in prayer, our penance in justification, our service in His goodness, our soul in glorification, and our body in the resurrection. Indeed, the most kind Lord our God is unceasingly ready to receive us in the arms of His fatherly love, to cherish, protect and save us, as He says by the Prophet to the sinful soul: [[Jer 3:1|thou hast prostituted thyself to many lovers: nevertheless return to me|Tu fornicata es cum amatoribus multis; tamen revertere ad me]], and [[Jer 3:12|I will not turn away my face from you|non avertam faciem meam a te]] [the margin gives Jer. iii, 1, 2; these words stand in Jer 3:12]; and again: [[Jer 3:3|thou wouldst not blush|Noluisti erubescere]]; [[Jer 3:4|Therefore at the least from this time call to me|ergo saltem amodo voca me]]: Thou art my father. And by Ezechiel it is said: At whatever hour the sinner shall groan, [[Ezech 18:22|I will not remember all his iniquities|omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor]] any more [no margin reference; the saying is a common form of Ezech 18:21–22].

paras.t: Deus meus, misericordia ejus præveniet me. Hoc est verbum bonæ fiduciæ, estque implicite fervens oratio. Hoc enim dicit fidelis, non præsumendo, sed sperando ac desiderando. Desiderium enim pauperum exaudivit Dominus, etiam antequam in formalem aut vocalem orationem erumpat. Nisi autem misericordia Dei nos præveniret, salvi fieri non possemus, quoniam gratiam primam nullus de condigno meretur: oportet ergo ut gratia Dei nos præveniat, conservet, perducat, perficiat. Ideo enim Christus: Sine me, inquit, nihil potestis facere.
paras.en: [[58:11|My God, his mercy shall prevent me|Deus meus, misericordia ejus præveniet me]] [*prevent* in its old sense: go before]. This is a word of good confidence, and is implicitly a fervent prayer. For the faithful man says this not presuming, but hoping and desiring. For [[Ps 9:38|The Lord hath heard the desire of the poor|Desiderium enim pauperum exaudivit Dominus]] [the margin reads Ps. v, 17 "according to the Hebrew": Ps. x, 17 in the Hebrew numbering, Ps 9:38 in the Vulgate], even before it breaks out into formal or spoken prayer. Unless the mercy of God went before us, we could not be saved, since no one merits the first grace condignly [that is, as something strictly owed in justice]: it is needful, then, that the grace of God go before us, preserve us, lead us on and perfect us. For this is why Christ says: [[John 15:5|without me|Sine me]], he says, [[John 15:5|you can do nothing|nihil potestis facere]].

paras.t: Deus ostendit mihi super inimicos meos: Ne occidas eos, etc. Hoc dicit Ecclesia, sicut et Christus, de Judæis inter Christianos morantibus: quos non occidit propter rationem in præcedenti explanatione expositam.
paras.en: [[58:12|God shall let me see over my enemies|Deus ostendit mihi super inimicos meos]]: [[58:12|slay them not|Ne occidas eos]], etc. The Church says this, as Christ also does, of the Jews dwelling among Christians, whom she does not slay, for the reason set out in the preceding explanation.

paras.t: Potest quoque intelligi de omnibus hostibus, ut sit sensus: Deus ostendit mihi super inimicos meos, id est, Christus præcepit mihi de adversariis meis: Ne occidas eos, nequando obliviscantur populi mei, id est, ne proximi scandalizentur in vestra vindicta, imitenturque opera vestra, et obliviscantur mea præcepta, quibus præcepi: Diligite inimicos vestros, benefacite his qui oderunt vos, et orate pro persequentibus et calumniantibus vos.
paras.en: It can also be understood of all enemies, so that the sense is: [[58:12|God shall let me see over my enemies|Deus ostendit mihi super inimicos meos]] [Latin *ostendit*, "has shown", taken here as "has instructed me"], that is, Christ has commanded me concerning my adversaries: [[58:12|slay them not, lest at any time my people forget|Ne occidas eos, nequando obliviscantur populi mei]]; that is, lest your neighbours be scandalized by your vengeance and imitate your works, and forget My precepts, in which I commanded: [[Matt 5:44|Love your enemies: do good to them that hate you: and pray for them that persecute and calumniate you|Diligite inimicos vestros, benefacite his qui oderunt vos, et orate pro persequentibus et calumniantibus vos]].

paras.t: Hoc ergo agens Ecclesia, orat: Disperge illos in virtute tua, id est, a malitia separa eos, qui solus potes facere mundum de immundo; et depone eos a malo proposito. Depone quoque, id est, indulge et dele, delictum oris eorum, videlicet sermonem illicitum labiorum ipsorum, quo vel in te, vel in proximum peccaverunt; et comprehendantur in superbia sua, id est, per flagella tuæ paternæ correctionis coarctetur ac restringatur eorum superbia, quatenus humiliati per pœnas, cessent a vita superba.
paras.en: Doing this, then, the Church prays: [[58:12|Scatter them by thy power|Disperge illos in virtute tua]]; that is, separate them from malice, Thou who alone canst make clean that which is unclean[[Job 14:4||]]; [[58:12|and bring them down|et depone eos]] from their evil purpose. Bring down also [Latin *depone*, "put down" or "lay aside"], that is, pardon and blot out, [[58:13|the sin of their mouth|delictum oris eorum]], namely the unlawful [[58:13|word of their lips|sermonem illicitum labiorum ipsorum]], by which they have sinned either against Thee or against their neighbour; [[58:13|and let them be taken in their pride|et comprehendantur in superbia sua]]; that is, let their pride be confined and restrained by the scourges of Thy fatherly correction, so that, humbled by punishments, they may cease from a proud life.

paras.t: Et de exsecratione, qua justos abominati sunt, et viam Dei spreverunt, et mendacio annuntiabuntur, id est, accusabuntur et redarguentur a prædicatoribus Christi in sæculo isto quotidie: quorum officium est errantes instruere, peccatores arguere, nulliusque peccata palpare.
paras.en: [[58:13|And for their cursing|Et de exsecratione]], by which they have abhorred the just and despised the way of God, [[58:13|and lying they shall be talked of|et mendacio annuntiabuntur]]; that is, they shall be accused and reproved daily in this world by the preachers of Christ, whose office it is to instruct the erring, to rebuke sinners, and to gloss over no one's sins.

paras.t: Annuntiabuntur autem in consummatione, id est in doctrina eos perficiente, vel ad hoc ut consummentur in bono; in ira consummationis, id est in increpatione caritativa ad consummationem virtuosam tendente. Ex caritate enim procedit ira per zelum, qua prædicatores et justi impios arguunt et castigant, quemadmodum Apostolus ait: Increpa illos dure.
paras.en: And [[58:13|they shall be talked of|Annuntiabuntur]] [[58:14|When they are consumed|in consummatione]] [Latin *in consummatione*, "in the consummation", that is, the completing or perfecting; Denis takes it in a good sense], that is, in teaching that perfects them, or so that they may be perfected in good; [[58:14|when they are consumed by thy wrath|in ira consummationis]] [literally "in the wrath of consummation"], that is, in a charitable rebuke that tends to the perfection of virtue. For from charity proceeds anger through zeal, by which preachers and the just rebuke and chastise the wicked, as the Apostle says: [[Tit 1:13|rebuke them sharply|Increpa illos dure]].

paras.t: Et non erunt, id est, peccatores post annuntiationem et consummationem prædictam, non erunt tales quales ante fuerunt: relinquent enim se ipsos, et vivent jam non ipsi, sed Christus in eis. Unde Salomon admonet: Verte impios, et non erunt. Et scient, per experientiam misericordiæ Dei sibi exhibitæ, quia Deus dominabitur Jacob, id est supplantatoribus vitiorum, videlicet justis, et finium terræ, id est etiam vitiosis, dummodo velint ad ipsum converti. Sic enim regnabit in eis per fidem et gratiam, faciens eos sibi famulos efficaces.
paras.en: [[58:14|And they shall be no more|Et non erunt]]; that is, after the talking of and the perfecting aforesaid, sinners will not be such as they were before: for they will leave themselves, and live, now not they, but Christ in them[[Gal 2:20||]]. Hence Solomon admonishes: [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]]. [[58:14|And they shall know|Et scient]], by experience of the mercy of God shown to them, [[58:14|that God will rule Jacob|quia Deus dominabitur Jacob]], that is, over the supplanters of vices [Jacob means "supplanter"], namely the just, [[58:14|and all the ends of the earth|et finium terræ]], that is, over the vicious as well, provided they are willing to be converted to Him. For so He will reign in them through faith and grace, making them His effective servants.

paras.t: Ego autem, o Deus, cantabo fortitudinem tuam, id est, laudabo potentiam tuam circa me, qua me de ore diaboli eruisti, ex impio justificasti, ad vitam laudabilem perduxisti. Laudabo quoque omnipotentiam tuam, quam parcendo maxime et miserando manifestas; qua cœlum et terram creasti, conservas, gubernas; per quam facis magna et inscrutabilia et mirabilia absque numero. Et exsultabo, id est, hilariter pronuntiabo, mane, id est cito et in principio, scilicet antequam in aliis occuper: secundum quod a Matthæo scriptum est, Primum quærite regnum Dei; vel, Mane, id est gratia tua veniente, ac radiante in me; misericordiam tuam, id est te ipsum misericordem ac misericordiæ tuæ effectum, confitendo beneficia tua mihi clementer collata: quemadmodum Raphael angelus jubet, Benedicite Deum cœli, et coram omnibus viventibus confitemini ei, quia fecit vobiscum misericordiam suam. Quia factus es, sine tui mutatione, susceptor meus, convertendo cor meum ad te. Fit enim Deus susceptor noster, alterando cor nostrum per gratiam suam, non mutando se ipsum. Et refugium meum in die tribulationis meæ, quia dedisti mihi gratiam hanc, per quam in omni necessitate ad tuam pietatem confugio.
paras.en: [[58:17|But I|Ego autem]], O God, [[58:17|will sing thy strength|cantabo fortitudinem tuam]]; that is, I will praise Thy power towards me, by which Thou hast rescued me from the mouth of the devil, made me just from being wicked, and brought me to a praiseworthy life. I will praise also Thy omnipotence, which Thou showest above all by sparing and having mercy; by which Thou didst create heaven and earth, and dost preserve and govern them; through which Thou doest things [[Job 9:10|great and incomprehensible, and wonderful|magna et inscrutabilia et mirabilia]] without number. [[58:17|And will extol|Et exsultabo]], that is, I will proclaim joyfully, [[58:17|in the morning|mane]], that is, quickly and at the beginning, namely before I busy myself with other things: according to what is written by Matthew, [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God|Primum quærite regnum Dei]]; or, [[58:17|in the morning|Mane]], that is, when Thy grace comes and shines in me; [[58:17|thy mercy|misericordiam tuam]], that is, Thyself, merciful, and the effect of Thy mercy, by confessing Thy benefits mercifully bestowed on me: as the angel Raphael bids, [[Tob 12:6|Bless ye the God of heaven, give glory to him in the sight of all that live, because he hath shewn his mercy to you|Benedicite Deum cœli, et coram omnibus viventibus confitemini ei, quia fecit vobiscum misericordiam suam]]. [[58:17|For thou art become|Quia factus es]], without change in Thyself, [[58:17|my support|susceptor meus]], by turning my heart to Thee. For God becomes our support [*susceptor*, "one who takes us up"] by altering our heart through His grace, not by changing Himself. [[58:17|And my refuge, in the day of my trouble|Et refugium meum in die tribulationis meæ]], for Thou hast given me this grace, through which in every need I flee to Thy loving-kindness.

paras.t: Adjutor meus, tibi psallam, id est, laude operosa, scilicet vita et voce, te laudabo, quia Deus susceptor meus es: propterea te satis laudare non valeo. Deus meus, misericordia mea. Cur non potius, Miserator meus? nisi quod tanta tamque inæstimabilis, ineffabilis ac infinita est misericordia Dei super nos, ut aptius dicatur in abstracto, Nostra misericordia, quam in concreto, Miserator noster. Sic enim dicere solemus de eo quem ardenter amamus: Tu es amor meus. Itaque tu, Domine Deus meus, misericordia mea. Definiant seu describant te alii sicut volunt; ego convenientius te describere nequeo, quam, Deus meus, misericordia mea. Dicat Aristoteles: Deus est actus purus; dicat Plato: Deus est per se bonum; dicat Avicenna: Deus est bonitas pura. Ego in æternum dicturus sum: Deus meus, misericordia mea. Tua enim bonitate creatus sum, tua incarnatione deificatus, tua conversatione sanctificatus, tua passione redemptus, tua ascensione glorificatus.
paras.en: [[58:18|Unto thee, O my helper, will I sing|Adjutor meus, tibi psallam]]; that is, I will praise Thee with a praise of deeds, namely with life and voice, [[58:18|for thou art God my defence|quia Deus susceptor meus es]]: therefore I cannot praise Thee enough. [[58:18|My God my mercy|Deus meus, misericordia mea]]. Why not rather "my Merciful One"? Only because the mercy of God towards us is so great, so beyond reckoning, unspeakable and infinite, that it is more fittingly said in the abstract, "our Mercy", than in the concrete, "our Merciful One". For so we are wont to say of one whom we love ardently: Thou art my love. So Thou, O Lord my God, art my mercy. Let others define or describe Thee as they will; I can describe Thee no more fittingly than: [[58:18|My God my mercy|Deus meus, misericordia mea]]. Let Aristotle say: God is pure act; let Plato say: God is the good in itself; let Avicenna say: God is pure goodness. I shall say for ever: [[58:18|My God my mercy|Deus meus, misericordia mea]]. For by Thy goodness I was created, by Thy Incarnation deified, by Thy life among men sanctified, by Thy Passion redeemed, by Thy Ascension glorified.

paras.t: Præterea, quoties in psalmo isto tam inclyto jam dictum est, Deus meus et susceptor meus? Et nonne Deus, omnium cœlestium, terrestrium et infernorum Deus exsistit? Cur ergo, Deus meus? Non est hoc omnium dicere: Deus meus. Deus enim a causalitate et providentia nomen accepit. Nos quoque illud, deum uniuscujusque vocamus, quod summe ab eo amatur et colitur. Ideo enim gulosorum deus venter est, avarorum aurum. Ille igitur vere ac proprie dicere potest, Deus meus, qui ipsum singulariter colit et fervide diligit: de quo etiam Deus specialem providentiam habet, ipsum præservando a malis, et promovendo in bonis. Hinc enim magnus ille atque divinus Areopagita Dionysius absolute dicere non præsumpsit, Deus meus; sed ita in libris suis scripsit: Deus, et si fas est dicere, meus.
paras.en: Moreover, how often has it already been said in this so glorious psalm, "My God" and "my protector"? And is not God the God of all things in heaven, on earth and under the earth? Why then "my God"? It is not for everyone to say this: [[58:18|my God|Deus meus]]. For God has received His name from causality and providence. We too call that each man's god which is loved and worshipped by him above all. So it is that the belly is the god of gluttons[[Phil 3:19||]], gold the god of the avaricious. He, then, can truly and properly say "my God" who worships Him singularly and loves Him fervently, and for whom God also has a special providence, preserving him from evils and advancing him in good things. This is why that great and divine Dionysius the Areopagite did not presume to say "my God" absolutely, but wrote thus in his books: God, and, if it is lawful to say so, mine.

paras.t: Totum igitur affectum nostrum congregemus et stabiliamus in Deo, nil prorsus amantes in creaturis, nisi in ipso et propter ipsum. Ipsum vero finaliter, pure et propter se diligamus, quia in ipso est omnium bonorum, pulchrorum ac desiderabilium plenitudo simpliciter infinita.
paras.en: Let us therefore gather all our affection together and settle it in God, loving nothing whatever in creatures except in Him and for His sake. And let us love Him as our last end, purely and for His own sake, since in Him is the plenitude, simply infinite, of all things good, beautiful and desirable.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Visita nos, Domine, gratuito benignitatis munere, et esto refugium nobis in die tribulationis, eripiens nos ab insurgentibus inimicis nostris: ut ab omnibus subducti hostium incursibus, tibi adjutori modo indefessi psallamus.
paras.en: Prayer. Visit us, O Lord, with the free gift of Thy kindness, and be a refuge to us in the day of tribulation, delivering us from our enemies who rise up against us: that, withdrawn from all the onslaughts of our foes, we may now sing unwearied to Thee, our helper.

59.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI NONI : DEUS, REPULISTI NOS.
59.title_en: Literal exposition of the fifty-ninth psalm: O God, thou hast cast us off.

paras.t: Hujus psalmi titulus est : In finem, pro his qui commutabuntur, in tituli inscriptione ipsi David, in doctrinam, quum succendit Mesopotamiam Syriæ, et Syriam Sobal, et convertit Joab, et percussit Edom in valle Salinarum duodecim millia. Juxta intellectum litteralem, sensus tituli hujus dependet ex historiis librorum Regum et Paralipomenon. Ad litteram enim fecit David hunc psalmum de statu et regno Israel, ejus miserias deplangendo, ejusque reparationem deprecando. Legitur enim secundo Regum libro, quemadmodum Hanon filius Naas regis Ammonitarum, contumeliam intulit servis David : quo facto, timens ipsum David, conduxit sibi in adjutorium quosdam de Mesopotamia, et quosdam de Syria ac aliis locis : qui omnes victi sunt a populo David.
paras.en: The title of this psalm is: [[59:1|Unto the end, for them that shall be changed, for the inscription of a title, to David himself, for doctrine,|In finem, pro his qui commutabuntur, in tituli inscriptione ipsi David, in doctrinam]] [[59:2|When he set fire to Mesopotamia of Syria and Sobal: and Joab returned and slew of Edom, in the vale of the saltpits, twelve thousand men.|quum succendit Mesopotamiam Syriæ, et Syriam Sobal, et convertit Joab, et percussit Edom in valle Salinarum duodecim millia]] According to the literal understanding, the sense of this title depends on the histories of the books of Kings[[2 Kings 10:1||]] and Paralipomenon[[1 Par 19:1||]]. For David made this psalm, to the letter, about the state and kingdom of Israel, lamenting its miseries and praying for its restoration. For we read in the second book of Kings how Hanon, son of Naas king of the Ammonites, did an outrage to the servants of David[[2 Kings 10:4||]]; and when this was done, fearing David, he hired to help him some from Mesopotamia and some from Syria and other places[[2 Kings 10:6||]]: all of whom were overcome by the people of David[[2 Kings 10:13||]][[2 Kings 10:19||]].

paras.t: Est igitur sensus tituli : Psalmus iste in finem, scilicet Christum, nos dirigens, qui est finis totius divinæ Scripturæ, scriptus est ad litteram pro his qui commutabuntur, in tituli inscriptione ipsi David, id est pro populo Israel, qui tenuit David pro rege suo a Deo electo, sicut et titulus dicit : quia Deus per Samuelem prædixit David debere esse et nominari regem Israel. Psalmus, dico, scriptus ea occasione, quum David succendit Mesopotamiam Syriæ, et Syriam Sobal : sicut historiæ prædictæ plenius pandunt ; et convertit Joab, id est, aciem direxit, et percussit Edom, id est Idumæos, in valle Salinarum.
paras.en: The sense of the title, then, is this: this psalm, directing us [[59:1|Unto the end|in finem]], namely unto Christ, who is the end of all divine Scripture, was written, to the letter, [[59:1|for them that shall be changed, for the inscription of a title, to David himself|pro his qui commutabuntur, in tituli inscriptione ipsi David]], that is, for the people of Israel, who held David for their king, chosen by God[[2 Kings 5:3||]], as the title too says: for God foretold through Samuel that David was to be, and to be called, king of Israel[[1 Kings 16:1||]][[1 Kings 16:12||]]. The psalm, I say, was written on this occasion: [[59:2|When|quum]] David [[59:2|set fire to Mesopotamia of Syria and Sobal|succendit Mesopotamiam Syriæ, et Syriam Sobal]], as the histories mentioned above show more fully; [[59:2|and Joab returned|et convertit Joab]], that is, directed his line of battle [convertit, "turned": Denis takes it of Joab turning his army upon the enemy], [[59:2|and slew of Edom|et percussit Edom]], that is, the Idumeans, [[59:2|in the vale of the saltpits|in valle Salinarum]].

paras.t: Loquens igitur David in persona regni Israel, ait : Deus, repulisti nos a tua defensione, et destruxisti nos, permittendo hostes ingredi terminos nostros, et civitates nostras vastare, hominesque occidere. Iratus es adversus nos propter peccata nostra. Regnum enim Israel tempore judicum multipliciter affligebatur. Unde primo libro Regum dicitur, quod faber ferrarius non erat in terra Israel. Caverant namque Philistæi, ne facerent Hebræi lanceam aut gladium, ut pugnare non possent. Et misertus es nobis, non penitus conterendo nos, neque nos affligendo tam vehementer sicut meruimus.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of the kingdom of Israel, David says: [[59:3|O God, thou hast cast us off|Deus, repulisti nos]] from thy defence, [[59:3|and hast destroyed us|et destruxisti nos]], by letting enemies enter our borders, lay waste our cities and slay our men. [[59:3|Thou hast been angry|Iratus es]] against us because of our sins. For the kingdom of Israel was afflicted in many ways in the time of the judges. Hence it is said in the first book of Kings that there was no smith in the land of Israel; for the Philistines had taken care that the Hebrews should not make spear or sword, so that they could not fight[[1 Kings 13:19||]]. [[59:3|and hast had mercy on us|Et misertus es nobis]], not crushing us utterly, nor afflicting us as heavily as we deserved.

paras.t: Commovisti terram, id est inhabitantes in terra nostra, permittendo nos impugnari et eradicari a terra. Expulerunt enim Philistæi Hebræos, et habitabant in civitatibus ipsorum. Et conturbasti eam, id est, terrore adversariorum turbari eos permisisti. Sana contritiones ejus, id est, ruinas ejus et afflictiones recupera, quia commota est, id est, propter prædictas miserias nostras moveatur pietas tua ad miserendum succurrendumque nobis.
paras.en: [[59:4|Thou hast moved the earth|Commovisti terram]], that is, those dwelling in our land, by letting us be assailed and rooted out of the land. For the Philistines drove out the Hebrews and dwelt in their cities[[1 Kings 31:7||]]. [[59:4|and hast troubled it|Et conturbasti eam]], that is, thou hast let them be troubled by terror of their adversaries. [[59:4|heal thou the breaches thereof|Sana contritiones ejus]], that is, repair its ruins and afflictions, [[59:4|for it has been moved|quia commota est]]: that is, because of these miseries of ours, let thy loving-kindness be moved to have mercy on us and to help us.

paras.t: Ostendisti populo tuo dura, id est, diversa flagella super nos induxisti ; potasti nos vino compunctionis, id est, compunctione seu mœrore, et mentis dolore nos implesti, sicut homo vino potatur, et potu impletur : quemadmodum apud Jeremiam legimus, Ecce ego cibabo eos absinthio, et potabo impios felle, dicit Dominus.
paras.en: [[59:5|Thou hast shewn thy people hard things|Ostendisti populo tuo dura]], that is, thou hast brought divers scourges upon us; [[59:5|thou hast made us drink the wine of sorrow|potasti nos vino compunctionis]] [compunctio, "compunction", the pricking of a grieved heart], that is, thou hast filled us with compunction or grief and pain of mind, as a man is given wine to drink and is filled with the drink: as we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 23:15|Behold I will feed them with wormwood|Ecce ego cibabo eos absinthio]], [[Jer 23:15|and will give them gall to drink|et potabo impios felle]] [Denis reads "impios", "the wicked", for Jeremias's "eos", "them"], saith the Lord.

paras.t: Dedisti metuentibus te significationem, id est intellectum, ut fugiant a facie arcus, id est a comminatione divini judicii. Per castigationes enim præsentes illuminat Deus corda humana, ut timeant futura supplicia. Propter quod apud Jeremiam habetur : Castigasti me, et eruditus sum. Hoc autem facis, o Domine, Ut liberentur dilecti tui, videlicet filii Israel quos dilexisti : juxta illud, Puer Israel, et dilexi eum ; et illud, In caritate perpetua dilexi te, ideo attraxi te miserans.
paras.en: [[59:6|Thou hast given a warning to them that fear thee|Dedisti metuentibus te significationem]], that is, understanding [significatio, "a sign" or "warning", which Denis takes for the understanding God gives], [[59:6|that they may flee from before the bow|ut fugiant a facie arcus]], that is, from the threat of the divine judgment. For by present chastisements God enlightens the hearts of men, that they may fear the punishments to come. For which reason it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 31:18|thou hast chastised me, and I was instructed|Castigasti me, et eruditus sum]]. And this thou doest, O Lord, [[59:6|That thy beloved may be delivered|Ut liberentur dilecti tui]], namely the children of Israel, whom thou hast loved: according to that saying, [[Osee 11:1|Israel was a child, and I loved him|Puer Israel, et dilexi eum]]; and that other, [[Jer 31:3|I have loved thee with an everlasting love, therefore have I drawn thee, taking pity on thee|In caritate perpetua dilexi te, ideo attraxi te miserans]].

paras.t: Salvum fac me orantem, et eos pro quibus exoro, dextera tua, id est per dexteram tuam, scilicet per piam tuam adsistentiam, favorabilem præsentiam, et gratiosam clementiam ; et exaudi me ista precantem.
paras.en: [[59:7|Save me|Salvum fac me]] as I pray, and those for whom I pray, [[59:7|with thy right hand|dextera tua]], that is, by thy right hand: namely, by thy loving assistance, thy favouring presence and thy gracious clemency; [[59:7|and hear me|et exaudi me]] as I make this prayer.

paras.t: Deus locutus est in Sancto suo, id est per sanctum suum Prophetam, scilicet Samuelem, seu Nathan, quorum utrique revelavit prosperitatem regno Israel adfuturam tempore David. Locutus est vero Deus quod sequitur : Lætabor, id est, quod ego David in ipso lætarer sicut in Deo salutis meæ ; et partibor Sichimam, id est, spolia terræ Sichem dividam servis et adjutoribus meis, eamque restituam habitatoribus suis : quæ omnia per David completa sunt. Et convallem Tabernaculorum, id est locum juxta Jordanem situm, quem Jacob appellavit Socoth, id est tabernacula, quia de Mesopotamia rediens, et Esau fratrem suum declinans, fixit in eo tentoria. Hanc ergo convallem metibor, id est, filiis Israel dividam secundum debitam uniuscujusque mensuram, expulsis de ea Philistæis, qui eam injuste ad tempus possederant.
paras.en: [[59:8|God hath spoken in his holy place|Deus locutus est in Sancto suo]] [in Sancto suo can mean "in his holy place" or "in his holy one"], that is, by his holy one, the Prophet, namely Samuel[[1 Kings 16:1||]] or Nathan[[2 Kings 7:4||]], to each of whom he revealed the prosperity that would come to the kingdom of Israel in the time of David. And what God spoke is what follows: [[59:8|I will rejoice|Lætabor]], that is, that I, David, should rejoice in him as in the God of my salvation; [[59:8|and I will divide Sichem|et partibor Sichimam]], that is, I will divide the spoils of the land of Sichem among my servants and helpers, and restore it to its inhabitants: all of which was fulfilled through David. And [[59:8|the vale of tabernacles|convallem Tabernaculorum]], that is, a place lying by the Jordan, which Jacob called Socoth, that is, Tabernacles, because, returning from Mesopotamia and turning aside from Esau his brother, he pitched his tents there[[Gen 33:17||]]. This vale, then, I [[59:8|will mete out|metibor]], that is, I will divide it among the children of Israel according to each one's due measure, once the Philistines are driven out of it, who had unjustly held it for a time.

paras.t: Hæc quoque acturus sum adjutorio populi mei, eorum præcipue qui bellicosiores et fortiores fuerunt. De quibus subjungitur : Meus est Galaad, id est populus habens terram Galaad in possessionem trans Jordanem : qui erant nominati in robore propter Jair et Jephthe ; et meus est Manasses, id est populus ex tribu Manasse progenitus : qui erat famosus propter Gedeonem de hac stirpe exortum. Et Ephraim, id est populus ex tribu Ephraim natus, est fortitudo capitis mei, id est potestas regni mei, vel fortitudo principalis quodammodo et capitanea. Habitabat enim hic populus in una extremitatum regni Israel versus aquilonem, sicut et populus Juda in alia extremitate versus austrum. Juda rex meus : quia ex tribu Juda reges sunt orti, eratque populus Juda defensor et custos regni Israel.
paras.en: These things too I am to do with the help of my people, chiefly of those who were the more warlike and the stronger. Of whom it is added: [[59:9|Galaad is mine|Meus est Galaad]], that is, the people that has the land of Galaad for its possession beyond the Jordan, who were renowned for strength because of Jair[[Judg 10:3||]] and Jephte[[Judg 11:1||]]; [[59:9|and Manasses is mine|et meus est Manasses]], that is, the people sprung from the tribe of Manasses, which was famous because of Gedeon, who came of this stock[[Judg 6:1||]]. [[59:9|and Ephraim|Et Ephraim]], that is, the people born of the tribe of Ephraim, [[59:9|is the strength of my head|est fortitudo capitis mei]], that is, the power of my kingdom, or, as it were, its chief and leading strength [capitanea, "chief", from caput, "head"]. For this people dwelt at one end of the kingdom of Israel, towards the north[[Jos 16:1||]], as the people of Juda dwelt at the other end, towards the south[[Jos 15:1||]]. [[59:9|Juda is my king|Juda rex meus]]: because kings arose from the tribe of Juda[[Gen 49:10||]], and the people of Juda was the defender and guardian of the kingdom of Israel[[Deut 33:7||]].

paras.t: Moab, id est terra et populus Moabitarum, est olla spei meæ : id est, per adjutorium spero illam adipisci et possidere, eaque uti tam libere sicut homo paterfamilias utitur olla in suæ domus obsequio. In Idumæam, id est in terram Edom, in qua Esau habitavit, extendam calceamentum meum, id est, pedibus calceatis ibo per illam, faciens eam mihi tributariam. Mihi alienigenæ, scilicet Philistæi et alii in circuitu habitantes, subditi sunt ad obediendum et tributa solvendum.
paras.en: [[59:10|Moab|Moab]], that is, the land and people of the Moabites, [[59:10|is the pot of my hope|est olla spei meæ]]: that is, with help I hope to win and possess it, and to use it as freely as a householder uses a pot in the service of his house. [[59:10|Into Edom|In Idumæam]], that is, into the land of Edom, in which Esau dwelt[[Gen 36:8||]], [[59:10|will I stretch out my shoe|extendam calceamentum meum]], that is, I will go through it with shod feet, making it my tributary. [[59:10|to me the foreigners|Mihi alienigenæ]], namely the Philistines and the others dwelling round about[[2 Kings 8:1||]], [[59:10|are made subject|subditi sunt]], to obey and to pay tribute.

paras.t: Porro, ut David ostendat se ista non præsumere propriis viribus, sed divina virtute, adjungit : Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam muris ac portis ? Quis deducet me usque in Idumæam, ut eam mihi subjiciam ? Et respondet : Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulisti nos quandoque ? sed modo ira tua in misericordiam versa est. Et non egredieris, Deus, in virtutibus nostris ? Interrogatio est, ac si dicat : Imo egredieris in virtutibus nostris, id est in exercitu nostro, erisque dux belli et auxiliator, quemadmodum de nostro exercitu scriptum est : Dominus Deus ejus cum eo est, et clangor victoriæ regis in illo est. Et alibi legitur : In exercitu nostro Deus dux est. Vel : Non egredieris ante nos in virtutibus nostris, sed tuis, quoniam propria potestate nos proteges.
paras.en: Further, to show that he does not presume to do these things by his own strength, but by the power of God, David adds: [[59:11|Who will bring me into the strong city|Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam]], strong with walls and gates? [[59:11|who will lead me into Edom|Quis deducet me usque in Idumæam]], to make it subject to me? And he answers: [[59:12|Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off|Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulisti nos]] once? But now thy wrath is turned into mercy. [[59:12|and wilt not thou, O God, go out with our armies|Et non egredieris, Deus, in virtutibus nostris]]? [Latin "in virtutibus nostris": virtutes means both "hosts" and "powers", and Denis reads it both ways.] It is a question, as if he said: Nay, thou wilt go out with our armies, that is, with our host, and thou wilt be our leader in war and our helper; as it is written of our host: [[Num 23:21|The Lord his God is with him, and the sound of the victory of the king in him|Dominus Deus ejus cum eo est, et clangor victoriæ regis in illo]]. And elsewhere we read: [[2 Par 13:12|God is the leader in our army|In exercitu nostro Deus dux est]]. Or: Thou wilt not go out before us in our powers, but in thine, since thou wilt protect us by thine own power.

paras.t: Da nobis, o Domine, auxilium de tribulatione, id est, quo a persecutione eripiamur ; et vana salus quia hominis. Nam maledictus qui confidit in homine, et ponit carnem brachium suum.
paras.en: [[59:13|Give us|Da nobis]], O Lord, [[59:13|help from trouble|auxilium de tribulatione]], that is, by which we may be rescued from persecution; [[59:13|for vain is the salvation of man|et vana salus quia hominis]] [so the print, with the words of the verse out of their order]. For [[Jer 17:5|Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm|maledictus qui confidit in homine, et ponit carnem brachium suum]].

paras.t: In Deo faciemus virtutem, id est, divina virtute prævalebimus, et opera virtuosa agemus ; et ipse ad nihilum deducet tribulantes nos. Deus enim tempore David contrivit adversarios Israel.
paras.en: [[59:14|Through God we shall do mightily|In Deo faciemus virtutem]], that is, by the power of God we shall prevail, and we shall do works of virtue [virtus is both "might" and "virtue"]; [[59:14|and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us|et ipse ad nihilum deducet tribulantes nos]]. For in the time of David God crushed the adversaries of Israel.

59.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI EJUSDEM QUINQUAGESIMI NONI TROPOLOGICA SEU MORALIS.
59.title_en: Tropological or moral elucidation of the same fifty-ninth psalm.

paras.t: Juxta mysticum vero sensum, exponenda sunt nomina tituli secundum vim interpretationis quam habent, ut sit sensus : In finem, id est, psalmus iste in Christum nos ducens, scriptus est pro his qui commutabuntur, id est, a veteri vita ad christiformem conversationem convertentur, in tituli inscriptione, confitentes verbo et opere Christum esse regem Judæorum, quemadmodum titulus asserit : commutabuntur autem ipsi David, id est ipsi Christo, ut vivant non sibi, sed Domino Salvatori, quum succendit Mesopotamiam Syriæ, id est, dum Christus sua humilitate et sanctitate inflammavit igne divini amoris mundum sua reputatione sublimem. Mesopotamia enim, alta vocatio interpretatur. Et Syriam Sobal, id est sublimitatem vanæ vetustatis. Sobal namque vetustas exponitur. Et convertit Joab, id est, Christus convertit populum Judæorum ; et percussit Edom in valle Salinarum : id est, mundum terrenum et vitiis sanguinolentum percussit sancto timore, ipsum convertendo ad fidem : percussit vero duodecim millia, id est omnes gentes a quatuor finibus mundi. Numerus namque duodenarius est numerus perfectionis, quo totalitas designatur.
paras.en: But according to the mystical sense, the names in the title are to be expounded according to the force of their interpretation, so that the sense is: [[59:1|Unto the end|In finem]], that is, this psalm, leading us unto Christ, was written [[59:1|for them that shall be changed|pro his qui commutabuntur]], that is, who shall be converted from the old life to a Christlike way of life, [[59:1|for the inscription of a title|in tituli inscriptione]], confessing in word and deed that Christ is King of the Jews, as the title declares[[John 19:19||]]; and they shall be changed [[59:1|to David himself|ipsi David]], that is, to Christ himself, so as to live not to themselves but to the Lord the Saviour[[2 Cor 5:15||]]; [[59:2|When he set fire to Mesopotamia of Syria|quum succendit Mesopotamiam Syriæ]], that is, when Christ, by his humility and holiness, set on fire with the fire of divine love a world lofty in its own esteem. For Mesopotamia is interpreted "high calling". [[59:2|and Sobal|Et Syriam Sobal]], that is, the loftiness of vain oldness; for Sobal is expounded "oldness". [[59:2|and Joab returned|Et convertit Joab]], that is, Christ converted the people of the Jews [convertit, "returned" in the Douay-Rheims, also means "converted"]; [[59:2|and slew of Edom, in the vale of the saltpits|et percussit Edom in valle Salinarum]]: that is, he struck with holy fear the earthly world, bloody with vices [Edom means "red"], converting it to the faith; and he struck [[59:2|twelve thousand|duodecim millia]], that is, all the nations from the four ends of the world. For the number twelve is the number of perfection, by which totality is signified.

paras.t: Ait ergo Ecclesia : Deus, repulisti nos, permittendo nos vastari ab hostibus fidei, vel non exaudiendo preces nostras. Quamvis autem ad tempus Deus plebem suam videatur repellere, non tamen finaliter eam relinquit. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Numquid repulit Deus plebem suam ? Absit. Inferius quoque habetur : Quia non repellet Dominus plebem suam. Et destruxisti nos corporaliter, permittendo nos ab injustis occidi : quod in persona martyrum dicere potest Ecclesia ; vel spiritualiter, indurando corda nostra, seu gratiam abstrahendo propter peccata nostra. Sine caritate enim et gratia existentes destruimur, et nihil sumus, juxta Apostolum : Si distribuero in cibos pauperum omnes facultates meas, et si tradidero corpus meum ita ut ardeam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil sum. Caritas enim est animæ vita. Iratus es famulis atque fidelibus tuis, eo modo quo pater filio peccanti irascitur, quem flagellat ne amplius peccet : sic tu afflixisti nos in præsenti variis pœnis in corpore et in anima, intus et foris ; et misertus es nobis, quia per temporales has castigationes peccata nostra dimisisti, gratiam infudisti, nosque de cetero cautiores fecisti.
paras.en: The Church, then, says: [[59:3|O God, thou hast cast us off|Deus, repulisti nos]], by letting us be laid waste by the enemies of the faith, or by not hearing our prayers. But though for a time God seems to cast off his people, yet he does not forsake them in the end. For which reason the Apostle says: [[Rom 11:1|Hath God cast away his people? God forbid!|Numquid repulit Deus plebem suam ? Absit]] And further on it is written: [[Ps 93:14|For the Lord will not cast off his people|Quia non repellet Dominus plebem suam]]. [[59:3|and hast destroyed us|Et destruxisti nos]] bodily, by letting us be slain by the unjust, which the Church can say in the person of the martyrs; or spiritually, by hardening our hearts, or withdrawing grace, because of our sins. For when we are without charity and grace we are destroyed and are nothing, according to the Apostle: [[1 Cor 13:3|And if I should distribute all my goods to feed the poor, and if I should deliver my body to be burned, and have not charity|Si distribuero in cibos pauperum omnes facultates meas, et si tradidero corpus meum ita ut ardeam, caritatem autem non habeam]], [[1 Cor 13:2|I am nothing|nihil sum]] [Denis ends with the words of v. 2, "nihil sum", where v. 3 has "it profiteth me nothing"]. For charity is the life of the soul. [[59:3|Thou hast been angry|Iratus es]] with thy servants and faithful ones, in the way a father is angry with a son who sins, and scourges him so that he may sin no more: so hast thou afflicted us in this present life with various pains in body and in soul, within and without; [[59:3|and hast had mercy on us|et misertus es nobis]], because by these temporal chastisements thou hast forgiven our sins, poured in grace, and made us more careful for the future.

paras.t: Commovisti terram, id est Ecclesiam militantem in terra versantem, quam multipliciter impugnari permittis, multisque inquietudinibus agitari, ita ut pene nunquam in eodem statu permaneat ; et conturbasti eam, propter magnitudinem persecutionum sibi instantium.
paras.en: [[59:4|Thou hast moved the earth|Commovisti terram]], that is, the Church militant dwelling on earth, which thou lettest be assailed in many ways and tossed by many disquiets, so that it almost [[Job 14:2|never continueth in the same state|nunquam in eodem statu permaneat]]; [[59:4|and hast troubled it|et conturbasti eam]], by the greatness of the persecutions pressing upon it.

paras.t: Ostendisti populo tuo dura, ita quod per experientiam didicit quid sit persecutio, et ex his quæ passus est, compassionem. Omnes enim qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur ; et per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cœlorum. Hinc ad Jeremiam Dominus ait : Castigo te in judicio, ne tibi videaris innoxius. Et in Apocalypsi : Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo.
paras.en: [[59:5|Thou hast shewn thy people hard things|Ostendisti populo tuo dura]], so that they learned by experience what persecution is, and, from the things they suffered, compassion. For [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution|Omnes enim qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur]]; and [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God|per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cœlorum]]. Hence the Lord says to Jeremias: [[Jer 30:11|I will chastise thee in judgment, that thou mayst not seem to thyself innocent|Castigo te in judicio, ne tibi videaris innoxius]]. And in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]].

paras.t: Dedisti metuentibus te significationem, id est, per temporalia mala eis inflicta significasti eis, ut fugiant a facie arcus, id est a perpetuis pœnis divinæ ultionis, videlicet ut gaudenter et æquanimiter perferant cuncta præsentis vitæ adversa, quatenus æterna mereantur evadere tormenta. Unde hanc significationem intelligens Jeremias propheta, in hac vita corripi cupit, dum ait : Corripe me, Domine ; verumtamen in judicio, et non in furore tuo, ne forte ad nihilum redigas me. Propter dura ergo quæ nobis Deus ostendit, non murmuremur, sed agamus quod sanctus Dei propheta Michæas ait : Iram Domini portabo, quia peccavi ei.
paras.en: [[59:6|Thou hast given a warning to them that fear thee|Dedisti metuentibus te significationem]], that is, by the temporal evils inflicted on them thou hast given them warning [significatio, from significare, "to signify", "to give a sign"], [[59:6|that they may flee from before the bow|ut fugiant a facie arcus]], that is, from the everlasting pains of the divine vengeance: namely, that they should bear gladly and with an even mind all the adversities of the present life, so as to deserve to escape the eternal torments. Hence the prophet Jeremias, understanding this warning, desires to be corrected in this life, when he says: [[Jer 10:24|Correct me, O Lord, but yet with judgment: and not in thy fury, lest thou bring me to nothing.|Corripe me, Domine ; verumtamen in judicio, et non in furore tuo, ne forte ad nihilum redigas me]] Because of the hard things, then, that God shews us, let us not murmur, but let us do what the holy prophet of God Micheas says: [[Mich 7:9|I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him|Iram Domini portabo, quia peccavi ei]].

paras.t: Ut liberentur dilecti tui, videlicet re et nomine Christiani, de quibus Salvator ait : Ipse Pater amat vos. Et in prima sua Canonica ait Joannes : Carissimi, diligamus Deum, quoniam ipse prior dilexit nos.
paras.en: [[59:6|That thy beloved may be delivered|Ut liberentur dilecti tui]], namely those who are Christians in deed and in name, of whom the Saviour says: [[John 16:27|the Father himself loveth you|Ipse Pater amat vos]]. And John says in his first Canonical Epistle: Dearly beloved, [[1 John 4:19|Let us therefore love God: because God first hath loved us|diligamus Deum, quoniam ipse prior dilexit nos]].

paras.t: Salvum me fac dextera tua, id est in dextera tua, ita ut in dextera tua in cœlo resideam, id est in bonis tuis potioribus atque cœlestibus, prout Christus promisit : Qui vicerit, dabo ei mecum sedere in throno meo, sicut et ego vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus.
paras.en: [[59:7|Save me with thy right hand|Salvum me fac dextera tua]], that is, at thy right hand [Latin "in dextera tua", which can mean "with" or "at thy right hand"]: so that I may sit at thy right hand in heaven, that is, among thy better and heavenly goods, as Christ promised: [[Apoc 3:21|To him that shall overcome, I will give to sit with me in my throne: as I also have overcome and am set down with my Father in his throne.|Qui vicerit, dabo ei mecum sedere in throno meo, sicut et ego vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus]]

paras.t: Deus locutus est in Sancto suo, id est, Pater locutus est nobis in Filio, qui est Sanctus Sanctorum. Porro quæ sequuntur, possunt esse verba Dei Patris, vel Christi, seu Ecclesiæ. Pater igitur ait : Lætabor in vobis, o electi, quum benefecero vobis, quemadmodum spopondi, Dabo (inquiens) eis cor unum, et lætabor super eis quum benefecero eis. Et partibor Sichimam, id est, gentiles dividam, quosdam convertendo, et quosdam deserendo. Non enim est omnium fides. Per Sichimam namque, in qua morabantur pagani, designantur gentiles. Et convallem Tabernaculorum, id est populum Judæorum, metibor, quosdam assumendo, et quosdam relinquendo. Hæc autem conveniunt Christo, sicut et Deo Patri. Unde in Cœna dixit : Non de omnibus vobis dico ; ego scio quos elegerim. Apostolus quoque ad Romanos : Vide, inquit, bonitatem et severitatem Dei : in eos quidem qui ceciderunt, severitatem : in te autem bonitatem, si tamen permanseris in bonitate.
paras.en: [[59:8|God hath spoken in his holy place|Deus locutus est in Sancto suo]] [in Sancto suo can also mean "in his Holy One"], that is, the Father [[Heb 1:2|hath spoken to us by his Son|locutus est nobis in Filio]], who is the Holy of Holies. Now what follows can be the words of God the Father, or of Christ, or of the Church. The Father, then, says: [[59:8|I will rejoice|Lætabor]] in you, O ye elect, when I shall do you good, as I promised, saying: [[Jer 32:39|I will give|Dabo]] [[Jer 32:39|them one heart|eis cor unum]], [[Jer 32:41|And I will rejoice over them, when I shall do them good|et lætabor super eis quum benefecero eis]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxi, 33, 41; the words are Jer 32:39 and 41]. [[59:8|and I will divide Sichem|Et partibor Sichimam]], that is, I will divide the gentiles, converting some and forsaking others. [[2 Thess 3:2|for all men have not faith|Non enim est omnium fides]]. For by Sichem, in which pagans dwelt, the gentiles are signified. And [[59:8|the vale of tabernacles|convallem Tabernaculorum]], that is, the people of the Jews, I [[59:8|will mete out|metibor]], taking up some and leaving others. Now these things befit Christ, as they do God the Father. Hence at the Supper he said: [[John 13:18|I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen|Non de omnibus vobis dico ; ego scio quos elegerim]]. The Apostle too, to the Romans: [[Rom 11:22|See then|Vide]], he says, [[Rom 11:22|the goodness and the severity of God: towards them indeed that are fallen, the severity; but towards thee, the goodness of God, if thou abide in goodness|bonitatem et severitatem Dei : in eos quidem qui ceciderunt, severitatem : in te autem bonitatem, si tamen permanseris in bonitate]].

paras.t: Meus est Galaad, id est congregatio martyrum, qui sanguinis effusione Christo et fidei testimonium præbuerunt. Galaad namque interpretatur, acervus testimonii : per quod martyres designantur. Nam martyr Græce, Latine testis vocatur. Et meus est Manasses : id est, populus priora obliviscens, et in anteriora extendens se ipsum, pertinet ad numerum electorum meorum. Manasses quippe interpretatur oblivio. Debemus autem temporalium, sensibilium et inferiorum oblivisci, atque æternorum ac divinorum jugiter recordari, quatenus, sicut ait Apostolus, revelata facie gloriam Domini speculemur. Et Ephraim, id est populus in bonis operibus copiosus ac fertilis, est fortitudo capitis mei, id est stabilimentum Christi, cujus ego caput sum, et qui est caput Ecclesiæ. Populus autem prædictus dicitur stabilimentum Christi, quia per eum Christus conservat et stabilit alios in fide et gratia. Pater quoque appellat Christum caput suum, quia ipse Pater constituit Christum in caput omnium electorum. Ephraim autem, fertilitas seu crescens interpretatur. Juda, id est populus confessorum, qui vita atque doctrina Domino confitentur, et laudem ejus et prædicationem salubrem annuntiant aliis, tanquam scribæ docti in regno cœlorum ; rex meus : id est, populus iste est rector Ecclesiæ, quia per eum inferiores guberno, quemadmodum per Prophetam testatus sum : Dabo vobis pastores secundum cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina.
paras.en: [[59:9|Galaad is mine|Meus est Galaad]], that is, the assembly of the martyrs, who by the shedding of their blood bore witness to Christ and to the faith. For Galaad is interpreted "heap of witness", by which the martyrs are signified; for one called *martyr* in Greek is called *testis*, "witness", in Latin. [[59:9|and Manasses is mine|Et meus est Manasses]]: that is, the people that forgets the things that were before and stretches itself forth to those ahead[[Phil 3:13||]] belongs to the number of my elect. For Manasses is interpreted "forgetfulness". And we ought to forget temporal, sensible and lower things, and continually remember the eternal and divine, so that, as the Apostle says, we may be [[2 Cor 3:18|beholding the glory of the Lord with open face|revelata facie gloriam Domini speculemur]]. [[59:9|and Ephraim|Et Ephraim]], that is, the people abounding and fruitful in good works, [[59:9|is the strength of my head|est fortitudo capitis mei]], that is, the stay of Christ, whose head I am, and who is the head of the Church[[Eph 1:22||]]. Now this people is called the stay of Christ because through it Christ keeps and establishes others in faith and grace. And the Father calls Christ his head because the Father himself appointed Christ to be head of all the elect. Ephraim, moreover, is interpreted "fruitfulness" or "growing". [[59:9|Juda|Juda]] [the name means "confession" or "praise"], that is, the people of the confessors, who confess the Lord by life and teaching, and proclaim to others his praise and wholesome preaching, like [[Matt 13:52|every scribe instructed in the kingdom of heaven|scribæ docti in regno cœlorum]] [the margin gives Matth. xxiii, 52; the words are Matt 13:52]; [[59:9|is my king|rex meus]]: that is, this people is the ruler of the Church, because through it I govern those below, as I testified through the Prophet: [[Jer 3:15|I will give you pastors according to my own heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine|Dabo vobis pastores secundum cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina]].

paras.t: Moab olla spei meæ. Videtur hoc sic posse intelligi : Nam Ruth de cujus semine ortus est David, et insuper Christus, Moabitis erat ; et ita Moab, id est Christus ortus ex Ruth Moabitide, dicitur olla spei Dei Patris, quia in ipso tanquam in olla seu vase, dedit nobis Deus Pater plenitudinem spei adipiscendi bona divina, secundum quod ait Apostolus : Proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro omnibus nobis tradidit illum : quomodo etiam non omnia nobis cum illo donavit ? Dedit enim omnibus in Christo credentibus potestatem et spem filios Dei fieri. Nec videatur ineptum quod per Moab Christus signetur. Moab enim interpretatur, ex patre : per quod Christus signari potest, qui de se ipso ait, Exivi a Patre. Vel si istud non placet, exponatur hoc modo : Moab, id est Ruth Moabitis, olla spei meæ, quia in utero suo velut in vase portavit Obed avum David, de quo natus est Christus, qui est spes Patris, quia Pater dedit eum nobis ut sit spes nostra atque salvator.
paras.en: [[59:10|Moab is the pot of my hope|Moab olla spei meæ]]. It seems this can be understood thus: Ruth, of whose seed David was born, and Christ besides, was a Moabitess[[Ruth 4:17||]]; and so Moab, that is, Christ born of Ruth the Moabitess, is called the pot of the hope of God the Father, because in him, as in a pot or vessel, God the Father has given us the fulness of hope of obtaining divine goods; according to what the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:32|He that spared not even his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how hath he not also, with him, given us all things?|Proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro omnibus nobis tradidit illum : quomodo etiam non omnia nobis cum illo donavit]] For he gave to all who believe in Christ power and hope [[John 1:12|to be made the sons of God|filios Dei fieri]]. Nor let it seem unfitting that Christ should be signified by Moab. For Moab is interpreted "from the father", by which Christ can be signified, who says of himself: [[John 16:28|I came forth from the Father|Exivi a Patre]]. Or, if that does not please, let it be expounded in this way: [[59:10|Moab|Moab]], that is, Ruth the Moabitess, [[59:10|is the pot of my hope|olla spei meæ]], because in her womb, as in a vessel, she bore Obed, the grandfather of David[[Ruth 4:17||]], of whom Christ was born, who is the hope of the Father, because the Father gave him to us to be our hope and saviour[[Matt 1:21||]][[Luke 2:11||]].

paras.t: Hæc autem possunt esse verba Ecclesiæ, ut sit sensus : Deus locutus est in Sancto, videlicet quod ego Ecclesia lætabor in Deo salutari meo, et partibor Sichimam, et convallem Tabernaculorum metibor. Primitiva enim Ecclesia, puta Apostoli Christi et eorum discipuli, quosdam converterunt ad fidem, tam ex gentibus quam ex Judæis, et quosdam in sua perfidia reliquerunt. Populi quoque designati per Galaad, Manassen, Ephraim et Judam, sunt Ecclesiæ, tanquam membra ejus ac filii.
paras.en: But these can also be the words of the Church, so that the sense is: [[59:8|God hath spoken in his holy place|Deus locutus est in Sancto]], namely, that I the Church [[59:8|will rejoice|lætabor]] in God my Saviour, [[59:8|and I will divide Sichem|et partibor Sichimam]], [[59:8|and will mete out the vale of tabernacles|et convallem Tabernaculorum metibor]]. For the early Church, that is, the Apostles of Christ and their disciples, converted some to the faith, from the gentiles as well as from the Jews, and left others in their unbelief. The peoples, too, signified by Galaad, Manasses, Ephraim and Juda belong to the Church, as its members and children.

paras.t: Deinde Christus ait : In Idumæam, id est in terram ipsam gentilium, extendam calceamentum meum, id est naturam meam humanam, quæ erat quasi calceamentum divinitatis. Dum enim Christus prædicari fecit Evangelium per totum orbem, extendit calceamentum suum in Idumæam, quia incarnationem suam ac humanitatem manifestavit hominibus, sibique subjecit credentes in se. Propter quod subdit : Mihi alienigenæ, id est nationes gentilium, subditi sunt per fidem et obedientiam, sicut superius de eis inductum est : Populus quem non cognovi, servivit mihi ; in auditu auris obedivit mihi. Hinc namque de Christo Balaam prophetavit : Orietur stella ex Jacob, et exsurget homo de Israel, et erit Idumæa possessio ejus. Alia littera habet : Et erit omnis terra possessio ejus.
paras.en: Then Christ says: [[59:10|Into Edom|In Idumæam]], that is, into the very land of the gentiles, [[59:10|will I stretch out my shoe|extendam calceamentum meum]], that is, my human nature, which was as it were the shoe of the Godhead. For when Christ had the Gospel preached through the whole world, he stretched out his shoe into Edom, because he made his incarnation and humanity known to men, and made subject to himself those who believe in him. For which reason he adds: [[59:10|to me the foreigners|Mihi alienigenæ]], that is, the nations of the gentiles, [[59:10|are made subject|subditi sunt]] by faith and obedience, as was said of them above: [[Ps 17:45|A people which I knew not, hath served me: at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me.|Populus quem non cognovi, servivit mihi ; in auditu auris obedivit mihi]] For of Christ Balaam prophesied: [[Num 24:17|A STAR SHALL RISE out of Jacob|Orietur stella ex Jacob]], and a man shall rise up out of Israel [Denis reads "exsurget homo", "a man shall rise up", where the Vulgate has "consurget virga", "a sceptre shall spring up"], [[Num 24:18|And he shall possess Idumea|et erit Idumæa possessio ejus]]. Another reading has: And all the earth shall be his possession.

paras.t: Sed quoniam Christus ut homo ista non fecit, sed divina virtute, ideo subditur : Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam ? Per hanc intelligi potest urbs Roma, quæ tunc erat caput et domina mundi. De qua Isaias prædixit : Civitatem sublimem humiliabit. In hanc urbem Deus Pater induxit Christum per prædicationem Petri et Pauli : quod sine divina virtute fieri nullatenus poterat. Propter quod Christus respondet : Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulisti nos, id est corpus meum mysticum, propter cujus persecutionem dixi Paulo : Quid me persequeris ? Vel, Repulisti nos, id est, corpus meum et animam multis doloribus affici permisisti. Unde clamavi in cruce : Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me ? Et non egredieris, Deus, in virtutibus nostris, id est, prædicta non facies naturali potestate corporis mei vel animæ, sed potestate divina. Dicitur enim Deus egredi, non loco, sed operatione, videlicet quia procedit ad actum.
paras.en: But since Christ did not do these things as man, but by divine power, it is added: [[59:11|Who will bring me into the strong city|Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam]]? By this the city of Rome can be understood, which was then the head and mistress of the world; of which Isaias foretold: [[Is 26:5|the high city he shall lay low|Civitatem sublimem humiliabit]]. Into this city God the Father brought Christ by the preaching of Peter and Paul[[Acts 28:17||]]: which could in no way be done without divine power. For which reason Christ answers: [[59:12|Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off|Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulisti nos]], that is, my mystical body, for whose persecution I said to Paul: [[Acts 9:4|why persecutest thou me|Quid me persequeris]]? Or, [[59:12|hast cast us off|Repulisti nos]], that is, thou hast let my body and soul be afflicted with many sorrows. Hence I cried on the cross: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me]]? [[59:12|and wilt not thou, O God, go out with our armies|Et non egredieris, Deus, in virtutibus nostris]], that is, thou wilt not do the things foretold by the natural power of my body or soul, but by divine power [virtutes, "armies" in the Douay-Rheims, also means "powers"]. For God is said to go out, not in place, but in operation, namely because he proceeds to act.

paras.t: Denique ista convenire possunt Ecclesiæ, quoniam ipsa extendit calceamentum suum in Idumæam, disseminando verbum Dei per totum mundum. Alienigenæ quoque ei subjecti sunt, quia prælatis Ecclesiæ parent gentiles conversi.
paras.en: Lastly, these things can befit the Church, since she stretches out her [[59:10|shoe|calceamentum]] into [[59:10|Edom|Idumæam]], by sowing the word of God through the whole world. The [[59:10|foreigners|Alienigenæ]] too are subject to her, because converted gentiles obey the prelates of the Church.

paras.t: Da nobis auxilium de tribulatione, per quod liberemur ab omni periculo, persecutione et tentatione.
paras.en: [[59:13|Give us help from trouble|Da nobis auxilium de tribulatione]], by which we may be delivered from every danger, persecution and temptation.

paras.t: In Deo faciemus virtutem. Non enim sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Et ipse ad nihilum deducet tribulantes nos: quia nisi pœniteant, æternaliter damnabuntur. Sæpe etiam in præsenti sæculo divina potentia conteruntur: quemadmodum cernimus factum de crudelissimis illis tyrannis, sanctorum martyrum persecutoribus, qui dudum ad nihilum sunt redacti, et ipsa Ecclesia Christi in pace quiescit. Propter quod ei alibi promittitur: Exaltabitur manus tua super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui interibunt.
paras.en: [[59:14|Through God we shall do mightily|In Deo faciemus virtutem]]. For we are not [[2 Cor 3:5|sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God|sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]. [[59:14|and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us|Et ipse ad nihilum deducet tribulantes nos]]: because, unless they repent, they will be damned eternally. Often, too, they are crushed by the power of God in this present world: as we see was done to those most cruel tyrants, the persecutors of the holy martyrs, who were long ago brought to nothing, while the Church of Christ herself rests in peace. For which reason it is promised her elsewhere: [[Mich 5:9|Thy hand shall be lifted up over thy enemies, and all thy enemies shall be cut off.|Exaltabitur manus tua super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui interibunt]]

paras.t: PRECATIO. Solatium afflictorum, Domine, da nobis auxilium in omni tribulatione, et sana contritiones nostras, atque peccata dimitte: ut tribulantibus nos ad nihilum deductis, in te faciamus virtutes pietatis.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, comfort of the afflicted, [[59:13|Give us help|da nobis auxilium]] in every [[59:13|trouble|tribulatione]], and [[59:4|heal thou|sana]] our [[59:4|breaches|contritiones]], and forgive our sins: that, [[59:14|them that afflict us|tribulantibus nos]] being brought [[59:14|to nothing|ad nihilum]], we may in thee [[59:14|do mightily|faciamus virtutes]] in the works of godliness [Latin "faciamus virtutes pietatis", "may do the mighty works (or virtues) of godliness"].

60.title: DECLARATIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI : EXAUDI, DEUS, DEPRECATIONEM MEAM.
60.title_en: Declaration concerning Christ of the sixtieth psalm: Hear, O God, my supplication.

paras.t: Præscribitur insuper præsenti psalmo hic titulus : In finem, in hymnis, psalmus David : id est, psalmus iste a David conscriptus, et Christo per David significato conveniens, dirigit nos in finem, id est in Deum, in hymnis, quatenus Deum laudibus veneremur, hymnumque et gratias Deo referamus pro universis beneficiis Christo homini, et per eum toti generi humano collatis.
paras.en: Moreover, this title is prefixed to the present psalm: [[60:1|Unto the end, in hymns, for David|In finem, in hymnis, psalmus David]] [Denis's title reads "a psalm of David"]: that is, this psalm, written by David and befitting Christ, who was signified by David, directs us unto the end, that is, to God, in hymns, so that we may honour God with praises and render him a hymn and thanks for all the benefits bestowed on Christ as man, and through him on the whole human race.

paras.t: Christus igitur in summæ Deitatis laudem prorumpens propter beneficia suæ humanitati concessa, ab oratione orditur, et ait : Exaudi, Deus Pater, seu Trinitas sancta, deprecationem meam, qua pro me ipso, videlicet corporis mei resuscitatione et glorificatione, oro, dicendo : Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora. Intende orationi meæ, qua oro pro mystico corpore meo, videlicet pro salute Ecclesiæ, dicendo : Pater, sanctifica eos in veritate. Sermo tuus veritas est. Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo.
paras.en: Christ therefore, breaking forth into the praise of the supreme Godhead for the benefits granted to his humanity, begins with prayer, and says: [[60:2|Hear, O God|Exaudi, Deus]] the Father, or holy Trinity, [[60:2|my supplication|deprecationem meam]], with which I pray for myself, namely for the raising up and glorifying of my body, saying: [[John 12:27|Father, save me from this hour|Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora]] [the margin gives John xvii, 27; the words are John 12:27]. [[60:2|Be attentive to my prayer|Intende orationi meæ]], with which I pray for my mystical body, namely for the salvation of the Church, saying[[John 17:1||]]: Father, [[John 17:17|Sanctify them in truth. Thy word is truth|sanctifica eos in veritate. Sermo tuus veritas est]]. [[John 17:11|Holy Father, keep them in thy name|Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo]].

paras.t: A finibus terræ ad te clamavi. Fines terræ non solum dicuntur partes ejus extremæ, sed etiam pars ejus superior atque inferior. Superficies namque corporis, dici potest finis ipsius. Est itaque sensus : A finibus, id est a superioribus partibus seu superficie, terræ Israel, in qua inter homines conversatus sum, ad te Deum Patrem meum clamavi, alto affectu te deprecando atque dicendo : Mi Pater, si fieri potest, transfer a me calicem istum. Dum anxiaretur cor meum, id est, passione instante, dum appetitus meus naturalis et sensitivus mortem naturaliter abhorrebat, quando incepi contristari et pavere, factusque in agonia, prolixius te orabam, et factus est sudor meus sicut guttæ sanguinis. In petra exaltasti me, id est, in te ipso sicut in summo ac fortissimo firmamento, vel in gratia tua seu virtute ac dono fortitudinis, per quam mortis pericula audacter aggressus ac passus sum, sublimasti me ab omni inordinato pavore et animi dejectione. Vel, Exaltasti me, clarificando nomen meum per totum mundum, et dando mihi nomen quod est super omne nomen, ut in nomine meo omne genu flectatur, et omnis lingua confiteatur quia Dominus Jesus Christus in gloria est Dei Patris. De hac enim Christi exaltatione Dominus apud Isaiam ait : Ecce intelliget servus meus, et exaltabitur, et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde ; super ipsum continebunt reges os suum.
paras.en: [[60:3|To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth|A finibus terræ ad te clamavi]]. The ends of the earth are said to be not only its outermost parts but also its upper and lower part; for the surface of a body can be called its end [Latin *finis*: both "end" and "boundary"]. So the sense is: [[60:3|from the ends|A finibus]], that is, from the upper parts or surface, [[60:3|of the earth|terræ]] of Israel, in which I dwelt among men, [[60:3|to thee|ad te]], God my Father, [[60:3|have I cried|clamavi]], beseeching thee with deep affection and saying: [[Matt 26:39|My Father, if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me|Mi Pater, si fieri potest, transfer a me calicem istum]] [no margin reference; Denis's wording joins Matt 26:39 and Mark 14:36, "remove this chalice from me"]. [[60:3|When my heart was in anguish|Dum anxiaretur cor meum]], that is, as the Passion drew near, when my natural and sensitive appetite naturally shrank from death, when I began to grow sorrowful and to fear, and being in an agony I prayed to thee the longer[[Luke 22:43||]], and my sweat became as drops of blood[[Luke 22:44||]]. [[60:3|Thou hast exalted me on a rock|In petra exaltasti me]], that is, in thyself, as in the highest and strongest foundation, or in thy grace, or the virtue and gift of fortitude, by which I boldly went to meet the perils of death and suffered them, thou hast raised me above all inordinate fear and dejection of spirit. Or, [[60:3|thou hast exalted me|Exaltasti me]] by glorifying my name throughout the whole world, and giving me [[Phil 2:9|a name which is above all names|nomen quod est super omne nomen]], that in my name [[Phil 2:10|every knee should bow|omne genu flectatur]], [[Phil 2:11|And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father|et omnis lingua confiteatur quia Dominus Jesus Christus in gloria est Dei Patris]]. For of this exaltation of Christ the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 52:13|Behold my servant shall understand, he shall be exalted, and extolled, and shall be exceeding high|Ecce intelliget servus meus, et exaltabitur, et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde]]; [[Is 52:15|kings shall shut their mouth at him|super ipsum continebunt reges os suum]] [the margin gives Is. iii, 13, 15, for lii].

paras.t: Deduxisti me, quia factus es spes mea. Deus enim Christi humanitatem in cunctis operibus suis direxit, et Christum hominem per viam præsentis sæculi sine omni ruina et labe deduxit. Deduxit eum adhuc infantem in Ægyptum, et inde eum reduxit, sicut per Osee contestatur : Ex Ægypto vocavi Filium meum. Deduxit eum in crucem, quia pro omnibus nobis tradidit illum. Deduxit quoque eum in limbum inferni, et de hoc mundo ad altitudinem cœli. Et hoc fecit Deus, quia fuit spes Christi, id est, quoniam Christus speravit a Deo hoc bonum orando impetrare. Deus autem erat spes Christi, in quantum erat mortalis et nondum corpore glorificatus. Turris fortitudinis a facie inimici : id est, sicut turris fortis protegit exsistentes in se ab hostium jaculis ; sic tu, Deus, in omnibus protexisti me in tuo adjutorio confidentem, atque in te immobiliter habitantem.
paras.en: [[60:3|Thou hast conducted me|Deduxisti me]], [[60:4|for thou hast been my hope|quia factus es spes mea]]. For God directed the humanity of Christ in all his works, and conducted Christ as man along the way of this present world without any fall or stain. He conducted him, still an infant, into Egypt[[Matt 2:14||]], and brought him back thence, as he testifies by Osee: [[Osee 11:1|I called my son out of Egypt|Ex Ægypto vocavi Filium meum]]. He conducted him to the cross, for he [[Rom 8:32|delivered him up for us all|pro omnibus nobis tradidit illum]]. He conducted him also into the limbo of hell, and from this world to the height of heaven. And God did this because he was Christ's hope, that is, because Christ hoped to obtain this good from God by praying. Now God was Christ's hope inasmuch as Christ was mortal and not yet glorified in body. [[60:4|A tower of strength against the face of the enemy|Turris fortitudinis a facie inimici]]: that is, as a strong tower protects those within it from the darts of enemies, so thou, O God, hast protected me in all things, as I trusted in thy help and dwelt immovably in thee.

paras.t: Inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo in sæcula, id est in Ecclesia militanti, secundum quod in Evangelio scriptum est : Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus, usque ad consummationem sæculi. Vel, In tabernaculo tuo, id est in cordibus electorum, per fidem et gratiam commorabor. Electi enim sunt tabernaculum Dei, sicut de eis ait Apostolus : Vos estis templum Dei vivi, sicut dicit Dominus : Quoniam inhabitabo in illis et inambulabo, et ero illorum Deus. Vel, Inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo in sæcula, id est, in triumphanti Ecclesia et cœlo empyreo æternaliter commanebo : quemadmodum testatur Apostolus, Non in manufacta sancta Jesus introiit, sed in ipsum cœlum. Protegar in velamento alarum tuarum, id est, sub defensione tuæ pietatis atque potentiæ ero securus. Hoc est quod apud Isaiam Christus dicit : Pro[…]texit me in umbra manus suæ.
paras.en: [[60:5|In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever|Inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo in sæcula]], that is, in the Church militant, according as it is written in the Gospel: [[Matt 28:20|behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus, usque ad consummationem sæculi]]. Or, [[60:5|in thy tabernacle|In tabernaculo tuo]], that is, in the hearts of the elect, I shall abide by faith and grace. For the elect are the tabernacle of God, as the Apostle says of them: [[2 Cor 6:16|you are the temple of the living God: as God saith: I will dwell in them and walk among them. And I will be their God|Vos estis templum Dei vivi, sicut dicit Dominus : Quoniam inhabitabo in illis et inambulabo, et ero illorum Deus]][[Lev 26:12||]]. Or, [[60:5|In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever|Inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo in sæcula]], that is, I shall abide eternally in the Church triumphant and the empyrean heaven [that is, the highest heaven, the dwelling of God and the blessed], as the Apostle testifies: [[Heb 9:24|Jesus is not entered into the Holies made with hands|Non in manufacta sancta Jesus introiit]], [[Heb 9:24|but into Heaven itself|sed in ipsum cœlum]]. [[60:5|I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings|Protegar in velamento alarum tuarum]], that is, I shall be safe under the defence of thy loving-kindness and might. This is what Christ says in Isaias: […] [[Is 49:2|in the shadow of his hand he hath protected me|texit me in umbra manus suæ]].

paras.t: Quoniam tu, Deus meus, qui es singularissimo modo Deus meus, tanquam summe et unice diligens me, summe quoque dilectus a me, exaudisti orationem meam, quemadmodum fassus sum : Gratias ago tibi, Pater, quoniam audisti me ; ego autem sciebam quoniam semper me audis. Dedisti hereditatem timentibus nomen tuum, id est, merito incarnationis meæ ac passionis præstitisti timentibus te timore filiali et casto, ut sint filii tui adoptivi : si autem filii, ergo et heredes ; heredes quidem Dei, coheredes autem Christi. Hæc autem hereditas est participatio gratiæ et gloriæ Christi, seu vita æterna, quam nobis jam dedit Pater in spe, daturus eam postmodum in re. Nunc quoque dat eam inchoative per infusionem consolationis internæ, conversationis divinæ, et gratiæ quotidianæ. Gratia enim Dei vita æterna, secundum Apostolum. Ait etiam Salvator : Qui verbum meum audit, et credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam. In futuro autem Deus dabit hanc hereditatem consummative, quando videbimus eum per speciem et sicuti est, cognoscentes sicut et cogniti sumus.
paras.en: [[60:6|For thou, my God|Quoniam tu, Deus meus]], who art in a most singular way my God, as loving me supremely and uniquely, and supremely loved by me, [[60:6|hast heard my prayer|exaudisti orationem meam]], as I acknowledged: [[John 11:41|Father, I give thee thanks that thou hast heard me|Gratias ago tibi, Pater, quoniam audisti me]]; [[John 11:42|And I knew that thou hearest me always|ego autem sciebam quoniam semper me audis]]. [[60:6|thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name|Dedisti hereditatem timentibus nomen tuum]], that is, by the merit of my Incarnation and Passion thou hast granted to those who fear thee with a filial and chaste fear [that is, the fear of a son who dreads to offend his father, not the servile fear of punishment] that they should be thy adopted sons: [[Rom 8:17|And if sons, heirs also; heirs indeed of God and joint heirs with Christ|si autem filii, ergo et heredes ; heredes quidem Dei, coheredes autem Christi]]. Now this inheritance is a share in the grace and glory of Christ, or life everlasting, which the Father has already given us in hope, and will give hereafter in reality. Even now he gives it in its beginnings, by pouring in inward consolation, divine converse and daily grace. For [[Rom 6:23|the grace of God, life everlasting|Gratia enim Dei vita æterna]], according to the Apostle. And the Saviour says: [[John 5:24|he who heareth my word and believeth him that sent me hath life everlasting|Qui verbum meum audit, et credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam]]. But in the world to come God will give this inheritance in its fullness, when [[1 John 3:2|we shall see him|videbimus eum]] by sight and [[1 John 3:2|as he is|sicuti est]], knowing even as we are known[[1 Cor 13:12||]].

paras.t: Dies super dies regis adjicies : id est, dies beatæ immortalitatis et securæ æternitatis addes, o Deus Pater, super dies temporales mortalis conversationis meæ Filii tui, qui sum rex Messias, de quo in Zacharia legitur : Jubila, filia Jerusalem ; ecce rex tuus veniet tibi justus et salvator. Et Isaias ait : Dominus judex noster, Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster ; ipse veniet, et salvabit nos. Hos dies æternos adjecit Deus super dies Christi temporales, dum eum ad impassibilem vitam resuscitavit. Ideo subditur : annos ejus usque in diem generationis et generationis : id est, dies æternitatis prædictos adjicies diebus temporalibus Christi, tanquam annos ejus durantes usque in diem generationis et generationis, id est usque in diem æternitatis, omnem generationem includentis et excedentis. Dies ergo quos Deus adjecit Christi diebus, sunt dies æternitatis; qui dici possunt plures dies et anni, non quod successione temporali discurrant ac defluant, sed quoniam omne tempus comprehendunt et ambiunt. Unde de eis ab Isaia dictum est : Erit mensis ex mense, et sabbatum ex sabbato. Verumtamen dies isti magis proprie appellantur unus dies, quam multi dies : non enim interrumpuntur nocte. Propriissime vero vocantur non dies, sed ævum, seu participata æternitas.
paras.en: [[60:7|Thou wilt add days to the days of the king|Dies super dies regis adjicies]]: that is, thou wilt add, O God the Father, days of blessed immortality and secure eternity to the temporal days of the mortal life of me, thy Son, who am the King Messias, of whom we read in Zacharias: [[Zach 9:9|shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem: BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee, the just and saviour|Jubila, filia Jerusalem ; ecce rex tuus veniet tibi justus et salvator]].
