And Isaias says: [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king|Dominus judex noster, Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster]]; he will come, and [[Is 33:22|he will save us|salvabit nos]] [Denis adds "he will come", as in Is 35:4]. These eternal days God added to the temporal days of Christ when he raised him up to a life that cannot suffer. Therefore it is added: [[60:7|his years even to generation and generation|annos ejus usque in diem generationis et generationis]] [the Latin reads "even to the day of generation and generation"]: that is, thou wilt add the aforesaid days of eternity to the temporal days of Christ, as his years lasting even to the day of generation and generation, that is, to the day of eternity, which includes and surpasses every generation. The days, then, that God added to Christ's days are the days of eternity; and these can be called many days and years, not because they run on and flow away in temporal succession, but because they take in and encompass all time. Hence it was said of them by Isaias: [[Is 66:23|there shall be month after month, and sabbath after sabbath|Erit mensis ex mense, et sabbatum ex sabbato]]. Yet these days are more properly called one day than many days, for they are not broken by night. Most properly of all, however, they are called not days but aeviternity [Latin *ævum*: the measure of created beings unchanging in their being, such as the angels and the blessed, which stands between time and eternity], or participated eternity.

paras.t: Et quoniam hi dies æternitatis adjecti sunt Christo, ideo ipse Permanet in æternum in conspectu Dei in cœlo, in quo sedet ad dexteram Patris, interpellans et apparens nunc vultui Dei pro nobis, secundum Apostolum. Misericordiam et veritatem ejus, id est gratiam atque justitiam Jesu Christi, quis requiret in hac vita præsenti, implorando gratiam remissionis, observando Christi mandata, et ejus imitando vestigia? quasi dicat : Pauci sunt qui eas ex corde requirunt. Pauci enim electi, et omnes quæ sua sunt quærunt. Vel : Misericordiam et veritatem ejus quis requiret in vita futura? quasi dicat, Nullus. Misericordia enim miseris necessaria est; veritas autem concernit adimpletionem promissi. In patria vero nemo est miser, et divina promissa in eis impleta sunt, quoniam gaudium sempiternum adepti, amplius pro se ipsis non rogant, saltem pro præmio essentiali. Idcirco Salvator loquens Apostolis : Vos, inquit, nunc quidem tristitiam habetis; iterum autem videbo vos, et gaudebit cor vestrum, et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis; et in illa die me non rogabitis quidquam.
paras.en: And because these days of eternity have been added to Christ, he himself [[60:8|abideth for ever in the sight of God|Permanet in æternum in conspectu Dei]] in heaven, where he sits at the right hand of the Father, interceding[[Rom 8:34||]] and appearing now before the face of God for us[[Heb 9:24||]], according to the Apostle. [[60:8|His mercy and truth|Misericordiam et veritatem ejus]], that is, the grace and justice of Jesus Christ, [[60:8|who shall search|quis requiret]] in this present life, by imploring the grace of forgiveness, keeping Christ's commandments, and following in his footsteps? As if to say: Few there are who seek them from the heart. For there are [[Matt 20:16|few chosen|Pauci enim electi]], and [[Phil 2:21|all seek the things that are their own|omnes quæ sua sunt quærunt]]. Or: [[60:8|his mercy and truth|Misericordiam et veritatem ejus]] [[60:8|who shall search|quis requiret]] in the life to come? As if to say: No one. For mercy is needed by the wretched [*misericordia* and *miseris*: the Latin ties mercy to misery]; truth, on the other hand, concerns the fulfilling of a promise. But in the fatherland [that is, heaven] no one is wretched, and the divine promises are fulfilled in them, since, having gained everlasting joy, they no longer ask anything for themselves, at least as regards the essential reward [that is, the vision of God itself, as distinct from the accidental joys of the blessed]. Therefore the Saviour, speaking to the Apostles: You, he says, [[John 16:22|now indeed have sorrow: but I will see you again and your heart shall rejoice. And your joy no man shall take from you|nunc quidem tristitiam habetis; iterum autem videbo vos, et gaudebit cor vestrum, et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis]]; [[John 16:23|And in that day you shall not ask me any thing|et in illa die me non rogabitis quidquam]].

paras.t: Sic, id est, quoniam ita est, ego Christus psalmum dicam nomini tuo, id est tibi Deo Patri, per me ipsum et meos ministros in cœlo et in terra, in sæculum sæculi, te sine fine laudando; ut reddam vota mea, id est, ut offeram tibi preces meas ac desideria pro militante Ecclesia, pro qua apud te, secundum quod homo, interpello, de die in diem, id est indesinenter usque ad sæculi finem. Christus enim pro nobis repræsentat Patri latus ac vulnera, et ipse est angelus perferens nostra sacrificia in sublime altare Dei, faciens ea Deo accepta. Unde Joannes : Advocatum, ait, habemus apud Patrem, Jesum Christum justum; et ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris.
paras.en: [[60:9|So|Sic]], that is, since this is so, I, Christ, will [[60:9|sing a psalm to thy name|psalmum dicam nomini tuo]], that is, to thee, God the Father, through myself and my ministers in heaven and on earth, [[60:9|for ever and ever|in sæculum sæculi]], praising thee without end; [[60:9|that I may pay my vows|ut reddam vota mea]], that is, that I may offer thee my prayers and desires for the Church militant, for which I intercede with thee as man[[Rom 8:34||]], [[60:9|from day to day|de die in diem]], that is, unceasingly until the end of the world. For Christ shows the Father his side and his wounds on our behalf, and he is the angel who bears our sacrifices to the altar of God on high [an echo of the Roman Canon: "command these to be carried by the hands of thy holy Angel to thine altar on high"], making them acceptable to God. Hence John: [[1 John 2:1|we have an advocate|Advocatum]], he says, [[1 John 2:1|with the Father, Jesus Christ the just|habemus apud Patrem, Jesum Christum justum]]; [[1 John 2:2|And he is the propitiation for our sins|et ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris]].

60.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI SEXAGESIMI.
60.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same sixtieth psalm.

paras.t: Non est negandum quin psalmus iste ad litteram exponi possit de David. Sed quoniam expositio talis parum devotionis atque dulcedinis continet, parumque ab expositione tropologica differt; ideo, ea relicta, tropologicum prosequor sensum, quomodo psalmus iste convenit unicuique Christiano, sive Ecclesiæ Deum oranti, et ei gratias referenti, dicendo : Exaudi, Deus, deprecationem meam, impendendo mihi gratiose et cito precis meæ effectum, qua oro indulgentiam et gratiam in præsenti; intende orationi meæ, qua deprecor consequi gloriam in futuro : id est, considera quanto affectu, quanta fiducia, et quali intentione ac fine te invoco.
paras.en: It is not to be denied that this psalm can be expounded literally of David. But since such an exposition holds little devotion and sweetness, and differs little from the tropological exposition [that is, the moral sense, which applies Scripture to the soul and its conduct], I leave it aside and follow the tropological sense: how this psalm befits every Christian, or the Church, praying to God and giving him thanks, and saying: [[60:2|Hear, O God, my supplication|Exaudi, Deus, deprecationem meam]], by granting me graciously and quickly the effect of my petition, in which I pray for pardon and grace in the present; [[60:2|be attentive to my prayer|intende orationi meæ]], in which I beg to obtain glory in the future: that is, consider with what affection, with what confidence, and with what intention and end I call upon thee.

paras.t: A finibus terræ, id est a cunctis partibus atque climatibus mundi, ad te clamavi in precibus ad te fusis, vel gratiarum actione ac laude, quam tibi obtuli in adversis. Dum anxiaretur cor meum, id est, sollicitaretur et affligeretur timore periculorum sibi imminentium, mœrore quoque propter quotidianos defectus et negligentias suas, videlicet quia secundum quod desiderat non proficit, nec te quantum cupit honorat; vel, Dum anxiaretur tentationibus dæmonum, et persecutionibus hominum ac motibus passionum ; in petra exaltasti me, id est, in Christo sublimasti me de imperfectione naturæ ad celsitudinem gratiæ, et de inferioribus ac terrenis ad cœlestia atque divina. Quilibet quoque nostrum dicere potest : A finibus terræ, id est a superficie, qua terra in qua habito, finitur in altitudine, ad te clamavi : secundum sensum prædictum. Vel, A finibus terræ, id est a terminis corporis mei, in quo velut in terra, habitat anima mea, imo ab omnibus membris et sensibus meis, ad te clamavi : eo modo quo dictum est supra : Omnia ossa mea dicent, Domine, quis similis tibi? Assuescat ergo anima nostra in omni angustia cum omni fiducia ad Deum clamare, quemadmodum Jonas propheta se fecisse affirmat, dicendo : Clamavi ad Dominum de tribulatione mea, et exaudivit me. Quum angustiaretur in me spiritus meus, Domini recordatus sum.
paras.en: [[60:3|From the ends of the earth|A finibus terræ]], that is, from all the parts and regions [Latin *climata*, the zones into which the old geographers divided the world] of the world, [[60:3|to thee have I cried|ad te clamavi]] in prayers poured out to thee, or in the thanksgiving and praise which I offered thee in adversity. [[60:3|When my heart was in anguish|Dum anxiaretur cor meum]], that is, when it was troubled and afflicted with fear of the dangers hanging over it, and with grief too for its daily failings and negligences, namely because it does not advance as it desires, nor honour thee as much as it longs to; or, when it was in anguish through the temptations of the demons, the persecutions of men and the motions of the passions; [[60:3|thou hast exalted me on a rock|in petra exaltasti me]], that is, in Christ thou hast lifted me up from the imperfection of nature to the height of grace, and from things below and earthly to things heavenly and divine. Each of us too can say: [[60:3|From the ends of the earth|A finibus terræ]], that is, from the surface by which the earth I dwell in is bounded in height, [[60:3|to thee have I cried|ad te clamavi]], in the sense given above. Or, [[60:3|from the ends of the earth|A finibus terræ]], that is, from the bounds of my body, in which my soul dwells as in earth, nay from all my members and senses, [[60:3|to thee have I cried|ad te clamavi]], in the way that was said above [that is, earlier in the Psalter]: [[Ps 34:10|All my bones shall say: Lord, who is like to thee?|Omnia ossa mea dicent, Domine, quis similis tibi?]] Let our soul therefore grow used to crying to God with all confidence in every distress, as Jonas the prophet affirms that he did, saying: [[Jon 2:3|I cried out of my affliction to the Lord, and he heard me|Clamavi ad Dominum de tribulatione mea, et exaudivit me]]. [[Jon 2:8|When my soul was in distress within me, I remembered the Lord|Quum angustiaretur in me spiritus meus, Domini recordatus sum]].

paras.t: Deduxisti me in præsenti exilio per viam mandatorum tuorum, ostendendo mihi in lumine gratiæ tuæ viam rectam, in qua ambulem. Nam sine gratia tua cæcus sum mente, et ambulo vias non bonas, vitiosas ac lubricas, in quibus graviter cado, et incessabiliter pecco, nisi tu animam meam deducas de via ad patriam, de labore ad præmium, de creaturis ad Creatorem. Hinc enim apud Isaiam dicis : Ego Dominus Deus tuus, docens te utilia, gubernans te in via in qua ambulas. Et alibi scriptum est : Justum deduxit Dominus per vias rectas, et ostendit illi regnum Dei. Et Tobias ait : Dominus sit in itinere vestro, et angelus ejus comitetur vobiscum.
paras.en: [[60:3|Thou hast conducted me|Deduxisti me]] in this present exile along the way of thy commandments, by showing me in the light of thy grace the right way [[Ps 142:8|wherein I should walk|in qua ambulem]] [the margin gives Ps. cxiii, 8; the words are Ps 142:8]. For without thy grace I am blind in mind, and I walk in ways that are not good[[Is 65:2||]], vicious and slippery, in which I fall grievously and sin unceasingly, unless thou conduct my soul from the way to the fatherland, from labour to reward, from creatures to the Creator. For hence thou sayest in Isaias: [[Is 48:17|I am the Lord thy God that teach thee profitable things, that govern thee in the way that thou walkest|Ego Dominus Deus tuus, docens te utilia, gubernans te in via in qua ambulas]]. And elsewhere it is written: the Lord [[Wis 10:10|conducted the just|Justum deduxit]] [[Wis 10:10|through the right ways, and shewed him the kingdom of God|per vias rectas, et ostendit illi regnum Dei]] [Wisdom 10:10 says this of Wisdom; Denis has "the Lord"]. And Tobias says: [[Tob 5:21|God be with you in your way, and his angel accompany you|Dominus sit in itinere vestro, et angelus ejus comitetur vobiscum]].

paras.t: Deduxisti autem me, Domine, quia factus es spes mea, id est, tu es bonum illud, in quo finaliter spero, et quod finaliter adipisci desidero, atque per cujus auxilium te ipsum adipisci confido. Fit vero Deus spes nostra, quoniam facit nos in ipso sperare. Factus quoque es mihi turris fortitudinis, id est robusta protectio atque sublimis defensor, a facie inimici, quicumque sit ille, id est ab omni incursu hostili, quemadmodum apud Salomonem legitur : Turris fortissima nomen Domini; ad ipsum currit justus, et exaltabitur. Et apud prophetam Habacuc : Deus Dominus fortitudo mea, et ponet pedes meos quasi cervorum. Quid eum dejicere, quid ei nocere poterit, qui in hac summa atque inexpugnabili turre inhabitat? Unde beatus Job ait : Quis mihi tribuat ut cognoscam Deum, et veniam usque ad solium ejus? Nam de habitantibus in hac turre fortitudinis, id est divino auxilio innitentibus, scriptum est : Deus dextera sua tegat eos, et brachio suo defendet eos.
paras.en: And [[60:3|thou hast conducted me|Deduxisti autem me]], O Lord, [[60:4|for thou hast been my hope|quia factus es spes mea]], that is, thou art that good in which I hope as my last end, which I desire to attain as my last end, and by whose help I trust to attain thee thyself. Now God becomes our hope because he makes us hope in him. Thou hast become to me also [[60:4|a tower of strength|turris fortitudinis]], that is, a stout protection and a lofty defender, [[60:4|against the face of the enemy|a facie inimici]], whoever he may be, that is, against every hostile assault; as we read in Solomon: [[Prov 18:10|The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the just runneth to it, and shall be exalted.|Turris fortissima nomen Domini; ad ipsum currit justus, et exaltabitur]] And in the prophet Habacuc: [[Hab 3:19|The Lord God is my strength: and he will make my feet like the feet of harts|Deus Dominus fortitudo mea, et ponet pedes meos quasi cervorum]]. What can cast down or harm him who dwells in this supreme and impregnable tower? Hence blessed Job says: [[Job 23:3|Who will grant me that I might know|Quis mihi tribuat ut cognoscam]] God, [[Job 23:3|and come even to his throne|et veniam usque ad solium ejus]]? [the margin gives Job xxviii, 3; the words are Job 23:3] For of those who dwell in this tower of strength, that is, who lean on God's help, it is written: God [[Wis 5:17|with his right hand he will cover them, and with his holy arm he will defend them|dextera sua tegat eos, et brachio suo defendet eos]].

paras.t: Inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo : id est, ego Ecclesia militans, ad consortium triumphantis Ecclesiæ pertingere spero, et fiducialiter dico quia in ea et in cœlo empyreo post hujus vitæ incolatum morabor in sæcula, id est sine fine, quemadmodum Christus fidelibus repromisit, dicens, Vado parare vobis locum; et, Iterum venio, et accipiam vos ad me ipsum. Vel : Ego Christifidelis inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo, id est in unitate Ecclesiæ, in individua caritate, sancta obedientia et fide catholica. Protegar ab omni periculo animæ, in velamento alarum tuarum, id est in subsidio misericordiæ atque potentiæ tuæ.
paras.en: [[60:5|In thy tabernacle I shall dwell|Inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo]]: that is, I, the Church militant, hope to reach the fellowship of the Church triumphant, and I say with confidence that in it and in the empyrean heaven [that is, the highest heaven, the dwelling of God and the blessed], after the sojourn of this life, I shall abide [[60:5|for ever|in sæcula]], that is, without end, as Christ promised the faithful, saying: [[John 14:2|I go to prepare a place for you|Vado parare vobis locum]]; and: [[John 14:3|I will come again and will take you to myself|Iterum venio, et accipiam vos ad me ipsum]]. Or: I, one of Christ's faithful, [[60:5|in thy tabernacle I shall dwell|inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo]], that is, in the unity of the Church, in undivided charity, holy obedience and the catholic faith. [[60:5|I shall be protected|Protegar]] from every peril of the soul [[60:5|under the covert of thy wings|in velamento alarum tuarum]], that is, in the aid of thy mercy and power.

paras.t: Quoniam tu, Deus meus, in quo solo confido, quem solum desidero, in quo totam salutem meam constituo, exaudisti orationem meam, ut spero. Tu enim dixisti : Quodcumque petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis.
paras.en: [[60:6|For thou, my God|Quoniam tu, Deus meus]], in whom alone I trust, whom alone I desire, in whom I place my whole salvation, [[60:6|hast heard my prayer|exaudisti orationem meam]], as I hope. For thou hast said: [[John 14:13|whatsoever you shall ask the Father in my name|Quodcumque petieritis Patrem in nomine meo]], [[John 16:23|he will give it you|dabit vobis]] [the margin gives John 14:13; the last words are those of John 16:23].

paras.t: Dies super dies regis adjicies, id est, dies æternæ beatitudinis addes post hanc vitam diebus hujus brevis vitæ : diebus dico regis, id est dominatoris atque victoris mundi, carnis ac dæmonis, qui dominatur animo suo, et vincit se ipsum. Unde dicit Apostolus : Id quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ, æternum gloriæ pondus operatur in nobis. Propter quod inferius dicitur : Longitudine dierum replebo eum.
paras.en: [[60:7|Thou wilt add days to the days of the king|Dies super dies regis adjicies]], that is, after this life thou wilt add days of eternal beatitude to the days of this brief life: to the days, I say, [[60:7|of the king|regis]], that is, of the ruler and conqueror of the world, the flesh and the devil, who rules his own spirit and conquers himself. Hence the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 4:17|that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation|Id quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ]] [[2 Cor 4:17|worketh for us|operatur in nobis]] [[2 Cor 4:17|an eternal weight of glory|æternum gloriæ pondus]]. For this reason it is said further on [that is, later in the Psalter]: [[Ps 90:16|I will fill him with length of days|Longitudine dierum replebo eum]].

paras.t: Permanet in æternum in conspectu Dei, id est, Ecclesia usque in finem sæculi in fide persistet, quemadmodum Dominus Petro in persona Ecclesiæ : Ego, inquit, rogavi pro te, ut non deficiat fides tua. Et ista vita decursa, perveniet ad regis sui gloriosum adspectum, quemadmodum in Isaia scriptum est : Regem in decore suo videbunt oculi ejus. Denique homo justus permanet in æternum in conspectu Dei, dicens semper cum sancto Elia, Vivit Dominus, in cujus conspectu sto hodie ; et cum sancto Job, Justificationem meam quam cœpi tenere, non deseram. Nemo enim mittens manum suam ad aratrum, et respiciens retro, aptus est regno Dei ; sed qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit.
paras.en: [[60:8|He abideth for ever in the sight of God|Permanet in æternum in conspectu Dei]], that is, the Church will persist in the faith until the end of the world, as the Lord said to Peter, in the person of the Church: I, he says, [[Luke 22:32|have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not|rogavi pro te, ut non deficiat fides tua]]. And when this life has run its course, she will come to the glorious sight of her king, as it is written in Isaias: [[Is 33:17|His eyes shall see the king in his beauty|Regem in decore suo videbunt oculi ejus]]. Lastly, the just man [[60:8|abideth for ever in the sight of God|permanet in æternum in conspectu Dei]], saying always with holy Elias: [[3 Kings 17:1|As the Lord liveth|Vivit Dominus]], [[3 Kings 17:1|in whose sight I stand|in cujus conspectu sto]] this day; and with holy Job: [[Job 27:6|My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake|Justificationem meam quam cœpi tenere, non deseram]]. For [[Luke 9:62|No man putting his hand to the plough and looking back is fit for the kingdom of God|Nemo enim mittens manum suam ad aratrum, et respiciens retro, aptus est regno Dei]]; but [[Matt 10:22|he that shall persevere unto the end, he shall be saved|qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit]].

paras.t: Sic psalmum dicam nomini tuo in sæculum sæculi, id est, vita et verbis incessanter te laudabo : sicut ab Ecclesiastico dicitur, Confitebor tibi, Domine rex, et collaudabo te Deum salvatorem meum ; et rursus, Laudabit usque ad mortem anima mea Dominum. Ut reddam vota mea de die in diem, id est, quatenus promissiones tibi factas in receptione Baptismi, sacri Ordinis aut religionis, quotidie impleam. Vel, Ut reddam vota mea, id est, desideria mea purificem, tibique ea semper exhibeam : sicut superius dictum est, Domine, ante te omne desiderium meum.
paras.en: [[60:9|So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever|Sic psalmum dicam nomini tuo in sæculum sæculi]], that is, I will praise thee unceasingly in life and in words, as is said by Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 51:1|I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour|Confitebor tibi, Domine rex, et collaudabo te Deum salvatorem meum]] [the margin gives Eccli. ii, 1, for li, 1]; and again: [[Ecclus 51:8|My soul shall praise the Lord even to death|Laudabit usque ad mortem anima mea Dominum]]. [[60:9|that I may pay my vows from day to day|Ut reddam vota mea de die in diem]], that is, so that I may fulfil daily the promises made to thee in receiving Baptism, holy Orders or the religious life. Or, [[60:9|that I may pay my vows|Ut reddam vota mea]], that is, that I may purify my desires and always present them to thee, as was said above [that is, earlier in the Psalter]: [[Ps 37:10|Lord, all my desire is before thee|Domine, ante te omne desiderium meum]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum brevem, pulchrum, delectabilem ac sententiosum audivimus, qui tam Christo quam ejus fidelibus optime convenit : in quo a devota oratione incipitur, post quam salubris doctrina inducitur, deinde divina beneficia fervide recoluntur, postremo per verba bonæ fiduciæ pium propositum inflammatur. Conformemus ergo affectum nostrum psalmi hujus sententiis, ejusque beneficia affectuosissime recolamus, et conemur implere quod dicimus : Sic psalmum dicam nomini tuo in sæculum sæculi. Hoc est enim divinissimum, saluberrimum, atque dulcissimum vitæ præsentis exercitium, Deo psallere, eumque laudare, magnificare, et toto affectu extollere, prout etiam in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Benedicentes Dominum, exaltate illum quantum potestis ; major est enim omni laude.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a short psalm, beautiful, delightful and full of wise sayings, which befits both Christ and his faithful excellently: it begins with devout prayer, after which wholesome teaching is brought in; then the divine benefits are fervently recalled; lastly, through words of good confidence, a devout resolve is kindled. Let us therefore conform our affection to the sayings of this psalm, recall its benefits with the deepest affection, and strive to fulfil what we say: [[60:9|So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever|Sic psalmum dicam nomini tuo in sæculum sæculi]]. For this is the most divine, most wholesome and sweetest exercise of this present life: to sing psalms to God, and to praise him, magnify him and extol him with all our affection, as it is also written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 43:33|Blessing the Lord, exalt him as much as you can; for he is above all praise.|Benedicentes Dominum, exaltate illum quantum potestis ; major est enim omni laude]]

paras.t: PRECATIO. Domine Deus, spes nostra et turris fortitudinis nostræ, protege nos sub umbra alarum tuarum : ut in timore tuo tibi jugiter servientes, et conformes facti gloriæ tuæ, mereamur in spiritualium oblatione votorum psallere nomini tuo in sæcula.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord God, our [[60:4|hope|spes]] and our [[60:4|tower of strength|turris fortitudinis]], protect us under the shadow of [[60:5|thy wings|alarum tuarum]]: that, serving thee continually in thy fear, and made conformable to thy glory, we may deserve, in the offering of spiritual [[60:9|vows|votorum]], to [[60:9|sing a psalm to thy name for ever|psallere nomini tuo in sæcula]].

61.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI PRIMI : NONNE DEO SUBJECTA ERIT ANIMA MEA ?
61.title_en: Exposition of the sixty-first psalm: Shall not my soul be subject to God?

paras.t: Huic præterea psalmo titulus iste præmittitur : In finem, pro Idithun, psalmus David : id est, psalmus iste a David conscriptus, et in finem qui Christus est, nos dirigens, habitus est pro Idithun, id est pro homine omnia terrena transiliente ac parvi pendente, et sola cœlestia finaliter cupiente. Potest quoque titulus ita exponi, quod David fecit hunc psalmum pro Idithun, id est, ut specialiter cantaretur a cantoribus seu Levitis constituti sub Idithun, qui erat unus de principalibus templi cantoribus.
paras.en: To this psalm, moreover, this title is prefixed: [[61:1|Unto the end, for Idithun, a psalm of David|In finem, pro Idithun, psalmus David]]: that is, this psalm, written by David and directing us unto the end, which is Christ, was composed [[61:1|for Idithun|pro Idithun]], that is, for the man who leaps over all earthly things [Idithun is interpreted "one leaping over"] and holds them of little worth, and desires heavenly things alone as his end. The title can also be explained thus: that David made this psalm for Idithun, that is, so that it should be sung especially by the singers or Levites placed under Idithun, who was one of the chief singers of the temple[[1 Par 25:1||]].

paras.t: Homo ergo ad divina se erigens, atque innumerabiles mundi errores, vanitates ac prævaricationes considerans, dicat : Nonne Deo subjecta erit anima mea, ei fideliter adhærendo, et ejus præceptis in omnibus obtemperando ? Utique. Ac si dicat : Subjiciantur alii concupiscentiis carnis, alii mundi principibus, alii dæmonum suggestionibus, variisque peccatis ; ego et anima mea Domino obediemus. Nemo enim potest duobus dominis deservire contraria approbantibus. Quoniam ergo non possumus Deo et sæculo obedire, potius eligo Deo parere quam mundo. Unde de inobediente apud Jeremiam scriptum est : Confregisti jugum meum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam. Quocontra Christus præcipit nobis : Tollite jugum meum super vos. Subjecta igitur erit anima mea Domino. Nam Salomon ait : Mens justi meditabitur obedientiam. Ratio quoque subjectionis subjungitur : ab ipso enim salutare meum, id est, tota mea salus atque felicitas a Deo procedit, dependet, et profectum sortitur. Propter quod per Osee Dominus ait : Populus meus pendebit ad reditum meum. Vel : Ab ipso, id est a Deo Patre, est salutare meum, id est Filius ejus meus salvator. Sic enim Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret.
paras.en: Let a man, then, raising himself to divine things and considering the countless errors, vanities and transgressions of the world, say: [[61:2|Shall not my soul be subject to God|Nonne Deo subjecta erit anima mea]], by cleaving to him faithfully and obeying his precepts in all things? Assuredly. As if he were to say: Let others be subject to the concupiscences of the flesh, others to the princes of the world, others to the suggestions of the demons and to various sins; I and my soul will obey the Lord. For [[Matt 6:24|No man can serve two masters|Nemo enim potest duobus dominis deservire]] who approve contrary things. Since, then, we cannot obey God and the world, I choose rather to obey God than the world. Hence of the disobedient man it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 2:20|thou hast broken my yoke, thou hast burst my bands, and thou saidst: I will not serve|Confregisti jugum meum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam]]. Against this, Christ commands us: [[Matt 11:29|Take up my yoke upon you|Tollite jugum meum super vos]]. My soul therefore shall be subject to the Lord. For Solomon says: [[Prov 15:28|The mind of the just studieth obedience|Mens justi meditabitur obedientiam]]. The reason for this subjection is also added: [[61:2|for from him is my salvation|ab ipso enim salutare meum]]; that is, all my salvation and happiness proceeds from God, depends on him, and from him receives its increase. Wherefore the Lord says through Osee: [[Osee 11:7|my people shall long for my return|Populus meus pendebit ad reditum meum]] [literally "shall hang upon my return": Denis has just said that our salvation "depends", that is, hangs, on God]. Or: [[61:2|from him|Ab ipso]], that is, from God the Father, [[61:2|is my salvation|est salutare meum]], that is, his Son, my Saviour. [[John 3:16|For God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son|Sic enim Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret]].

paras.t: Nam et ipse est Deus meus, id est causa, gubernator et conditor naturæ meæ naturaliumque donorum, et salutaris meus, id est justificator et gratiæ dator; susceptor meus, id est precum mearum auditor, semper paratus me pœnitentem brachiis pietatis amplecti, meque convertentem me, et quod in me est facientem, sibi attrahere et unire : juxta illud, Si direxerit homo ad Deum cor suum, spiritum illius et flatum ad se trahet. Quum ergo sit ita, non movebor amplius ab inchoato virtutis itinere, a bono proposito, a lege divina; nec a Deo meo per mentis aversionem recedam, sed ei immobiliter adhærebo. Hoc autem non præsumptuose aut certo, sed humiliter ac fiducialiter ait viator transiliens, nisi forte ex revelatione divina agnosceret se confirmatum in bono. Vel dicitur hoc ad designandum quid virtuoso conveniat, in quantum hujusmodi. Quemadmodum enim passiones et vitia, instabilitatis, distractionis et aversionis sunt causa; sic virtus seu gratia, interioris stabilitatis ratio perhibetur. Propter quod Salomon protestatur : Justus quasi fundamentum æternum. Et in libro Job : Si iniquitatem quæ est in manu tua, abstuleris, eris stabilis et non timebis.
paras.en: [[61:3|For he is my God|Nam et ipse est Deus meus]], that is, the cause, ruler and maker of my nature and of my natural gifts, [[61:3|and my saviour|et salutaris meus]], that is, the one who justifies me and gives grace; [[61:3|he is my protector|susceptor meus]] [*susceptor*, literally "one who takes up" or "receives": hence Denis's gloss], that is, the hearer of my prayers, ever ready to embrace me in the arms of his mercy when I repent, and, when I turn to him and do what is in me [that is, what lies in my power], to draw me to himself and unite me with him; according to that saying: [[Job 34:14|If he turn his heart to him, he shall draw his spirit and breath unto himself|Si direxerit homo ad Deum cor suum, spiritum illius et flatum ad se trahet]]. Since, then, this is so, [[61:3|I shall be moved no more|non movebor amplius]] from the road of virtue I have begun, from my good purpose, from the divine law; nor shall I depart from my God by turning my mind away, but I shall cleave to him immovably. Yet the wayfarer [that is, one still on the journey of this life, not yet in the fatherland] who leaps over earthly things says this not presumptuously or as a certainty, but humbly and trustfully, unless perhaps he knew by divine revelation that he was confirmed in good. Or it is said to show what befits the virtuous man as such. For as the passions and vices are the cause of instability, distraction and turning away, so virtue or grace is held to be the ground of inward stability. Wherefore Solomon declares: [[Prov 10:25|the just is as an everlasting foundation|Justus quasi fundamentum æternum]] [the margin gives Prov. x, 15; the words are Prov 10:25]. And in the book of Job: [[Job 11:14|If thou wilt put away from thee the iniquity that is in thy hand|Si iniquitatem quæ est in manu tua, abstuleris]], [[Job 11:15|thou shalt be steadfast, and shalt not fear|eris stabilis et non timebis]].

paras.t: Quousque, o maligni, irruitis in hominem justum et innocentem, eum propter justitiam persequendo ? interficitis universi vos, id est, o vos omnes, interficere vultis eum ex odio ? quemadmodum Sapientia inducit : Dixerunt impii : Opprimamus virum justum, quoniam contrarius est operibus nostris. Vel, Interficitis universi vos, id est, omnes occiditis vosmetipsos : quia dum justum affligitis, animas vestras per peccatum occiditis. Unde Joannes : Omnis, inquit, qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est : vel quia animam propriam spiritualiter occidit, vel quia per affectum alium perimit, vel quia coram Deo pœnam homicidæ incurrit. Tanquam parieti inclinato et maceriæ depulsæ. Aliquid subintelligendum est, ut sit sensus : Sic adversamini homini justo, quasi parieti inclinato ad casum, et quasi maceriæ a statu suo depulsæ. Putatis enim quod sicut paries talis fundamento privatur, facileque dejicitur, sic justus Deum conservatorem ac adjutorem non habeat, ideoque a vestra malignitate opprimi possit; et quum eum occideritis, ipsum omnino perisse putatis, non attendentes quid gloriæ Deus illi refundat, et quid pœnæ vobis immineat. Hinc enim scriptum est : Justus perit, et non est qui recogitet in corde suo; et viri misericordiæ tolliuntur, quia non est qui intelligat.
paras.en: [[61:4|How long|Quousque]], O wicked men, [[61:4|do you rush in upon a man|irruitis in hominem]] who is just and innocent, persecuting him for justice' sake? [[61:4|you all kill|interficitis universi vos]]: that is, O all of you, do you wish to kill him out of hatred? As Wisdom brings in: The wicked said: [[Wis 2:10|Let us oppress|Opprimamus]] the just man, because [[Wis 2:12|he is contrary to our doings|contrarius est operibus nostris]]. Or, [[61:4|you all kill|Interficitis universi vos]], that is, you all kill your own selves [the Latin *vos*, "you", can be read as the object: "you all kill yourselves"]: for while you afflict the just man, you kill your own souls by sin. Hence John: [[1 John 3:15|Whosoever|Omnis]], he says, [[1 John 3:15|hateth his brother is a murderer|qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est]]: either because he kills his own soul spiritually, or because in his desire he slays the other, or because before God he incurs the penalty of a murderer. [[61:4|as if you were thrusting down a leaning wall, and a tottering fence|Tanquam parieti inclinato et maceriæ depulsæ]]. Something is to be understood, so that the sense is: You set yourselves against the just man as though against a wall leaning to its fall, and as though against a fence thrust from its place. For you think that, as such a wall is deprived of its foundation and easily thrown down, so the just man has not God for his keeper and helper, and can therefore be crushed by your malice; and when you have killed him, you think he has perished altogether, not considering what glory God pays back to him, and what punishment hangs over you. For hence it is written: [[Is 57:1|The just perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart, and men of mercy are taken away, because there is none that understandeth|Justus perit, et non est qui recogitet in corde suo; et viri misericordiæ tolliuntur, quia non est qui intelligat]].

paras.t: Verumtamen, id est his non obstantibus, pretium meum cogitaverunt repellere, id est, justitiam meam seu opera virtuosa ac vitam laudabilem proposuerunt subvertere, dissipare, et a præmio impedire. Bona enim operatio pretium appellatur, quia per eam vita æterna mercatur. Cucurri in siti, id est, cum magno desiderio ad patriam festinavi : sicut superius dictum est, Sitivit anima mea ad Deum fortem, vivum. Vel sic : Cucurri viam mandatorum Dei in siti perfectionis, videlicet sitiendo justitiam ampliorem, et culmen perfectionis attingere affectuose concupiscens. Ore suo benedicebant, et corde suo maledicebant. Hoc faciunt subversores animarum, adulatores, bilingues, et simulatores : qui eos quos aperte pervertere nequeunt, adulando, et mala sub specie boni proponendo, decipere quaerunt. Propter quod de quolibet tali apud Jeremiam legitur : In ore suo pacem cum amico suo loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias.
paras.en: [[61:5|But|Verumtamen]], that is, notwithstanding these things, [[61:5|they have thought to cast away my price|pretium meum cogitaverunt repellere]]: that is, they purposed to overthrow, scatter and keep from its reward my justice, or my virtuous works and praiseworthy life. For good work is called a price, because by it eternal life is bought. [[61:5|I ran in thirst|Cucurri in siti]]: that is, with great desire I hastened to the fatherland; as was said above: [[Ps 41:3|My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God|Sitivit anima mea ad Deum fortem, vivum]]. Or thus: I ran the way of God's commandments[[Ps 118:32||]] in thirst for perfection, that is, thirsting for greater justice and longing with all my affection to reach the summit of perfection. [[61:5|they blessed with their mouth, but cursed with their heart|Ore suo benedicebant, et corde suo maledicebant]]. This is what the subverters of souls do, the flatterers, the double-tongued and the dissemblers: those whom they cannot pervert openly they seek to deceive by flattery and by setting evil before them under the appearance of good. Wherefore of every such man we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:8|with his mouth one speaketh peace with his friend, and secretly he lieth in wait for him|In ore suo pacem cum amico suo loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias]].

paras.t: Verumtamen Deo subjecta esto, anima mea : id est, propter persecutiones, tentationes, et tribulationes tibi injuste inflictas, noli deficere, noli a Dei lege recedere, noli contra Deum murmurare, sed ei subjicere ; quoniam ab ipso patientia mea, per quam in adversis praevaleo, sine tristitia omnia patiendo. Deus enim patientiam tribuit, sicut et ceteras virtutes infusas. Solet autem interdum homo de ipsa sua, quam in adversis habuit, patientia inaniter gloriari atque extolli, tanquam magnum aliquid fecerit, et Christi vestigia excellenter secutus sit ; sed iste non pensat patientiam suam esse a Deo, quoniam gloriatur in se quasi non acceperit. Sit ergo anima nostra omnino Deo subjecta, videlicet non solum in hoc, quod adversa aequanimiter sustinet, sed etiam in hoc, quod de sua patientia in se ipsa non gaudet, et eam Deo attribuit.
paras.en: [[61:6|But be thou, O my soul, subject to God|Verumtamen Deo subjecta esto, anima mea]]: that is, because of the persecutions, temptations and tribulations unjustly laid upon thee, do not fail, do not depart from the law of God, do not murmur against God, but submit thyself to him; [[61:6|for from him is my patience|quoniam ab ipso patientia mea]], by which I prevail in adversity, suffering all things without sadness. For God gives patience, as he gives the other infused virtues. Now a man is sometimes wont to glory vainly and be puffed up over the very patience he has shown in adversity, as though he had done some great thing and had followed in the footsteps of Christ in an excellent way; but such a man does not consider that his patience is from God, since he glories in himself as if he had not received it[[1 Cor 4:7||]]. Let our soul, then, be wholly subject to God: not only in this, that it bears adversity with an even mind, but also in this, that it does not rejoice in itself over its patience, but attributes it to God.

paras.t: Ideo autem dico patientiam meam esse a Deo, Quia ipse est Deus meus, a quo omne bonum procedit, et tota mea sufficientia fluit, et salvator meus : quia ab eo solo vera beatitudo donatur. Aliter demum convenit Christo esse salvatorem, in quantum Deus ; et aliter, in quantum homo. Nam, ut Deus, vocatur salvator per auctoritatem, tanquam gratiae in praesenti et gloriae in futuro creator et dator; in quantum vero est homo, appellatur salvator quasi instrumentaliter, quum sit satisfactor pro culpa generis humani, reconciliator ac mediator. Deus itaque secundum divinitatem salvator est, quoniam ipse solus peccata dimittit, solus justificat, solus gratiam creat ac influit, beatitudinem quoque solus largitur. Imo hoc modo proprium est Deo esse salvatorem, juxta illud propheticum : Ego Dominus, et salvator non est praeter me. Deus quoque est adjutor meus, in omni opere bono mihi per gratiam cooperans, meque confortans.
paras.en: Now I say that my patience is from God [[61:7|For he is my God|Quia ipse est Deus meus]], from whom all good proceeds and all my sufficiency flows, [[61:7|and my saviour|et salvator meus]], since by him alone true beatitude is given. Further, it belongs to Christ to be Saviour in one way inasmuch as he is God, and in another inasmuch as he is man. For as God he is called Saviour by authority, as the creator and giver of grace in the present and of glory in the future; but inasmuch as he is man he is called Saviour as it were instrumentally, since he is the one who makes satisfaction for the guilt of the human race, the reconciler and mediator. God, therefore, is Saviour according to the Godhead, since he alone forgives sins[[Mark 2:7||]], he alone justifies[[Rom 8:30||]], he alone creates and pours in grace, and he alone bestows beatitude. Indeed, in this way it is proper to God to be Saviour, according to that saying of the prophet: [[Is 43:11|I am the Lord|Ego Dominus]], and [[Osee 13:4|there is no saviour beside me|salvator non est praeter me]] [the margin gives Is. xlv, 11 and Osee xiii, 4; Denis's words are closest to Is 43:11 and Osee 13:4]. God is also [[61:7|my helper|adjutor meus]], working together with me by grace in every good work, and strengthening me.

paras.t: Non emigrabo de unitate Ecclesiae et grege electorum, ad aversos a Deo et societatem pravorum, quoniam In Deo salutare meum, id est, salus mea in hoc consistit, quod non emigrem ab eo, et gloria mea : quia in solo Deo vera et licita habetur gloriatio, quemadmodum Apostolus dicit : Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. Et Habacuc : Ego autem in Domino gaudebo, et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo. Deus auxilii mei, id est, ab eo dependet ac derivatur auxilium meum : sicut per Osee ait : Perditio tua ex te ; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum. Et spes mea in Deo est : quia divinae pietati innititur, Deumque pro immediato objecto et causa sortitur, quum sit virtus theologica et infusa. Ecce quam praeclarus et splendidus suavissimusque versiculus, omni menti devotae super mel et favum dulcis et saporosus.
paras.en: [[61:7|I shall not be moved|Non emigrabo]] [*emigrabo*, literally "I shall not move out", "emigrate": hence Denis's gloss] from the unity of the Church and the flock of the elect to those turned away from God and the company of the wicked, since [[61:8|In God is my salvation|In Deo salutare meum]]: that is, my salvation consists in this, that I do not move away from him; [[61:8|and my glory|et gloria mea]]: for in God alone is true and lawful glorying had, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:31|He that glorieth may glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]]. And Habacuc: [[Hab 3:18|But I will rejoice in the Lord: and I will joy in God my Jesus|Ego autem in Domino gaudebo, et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo]]. [[61:8|the God of my help|Deus auxilii mei]]: that is, my help depends and is derived from him; as he says through Osee: [[Osee 13:9|Destruction is thy own|Perditio tua ex te]]; [[Osee 13:9|thy help is only in me|in me tantummodo auxilium tuum]]. [[61:8|and my hope is in God|Et spes mea in Deo est]]: for it rests upon the divine mercy, and has God for its immediate object and cause, since it is a theological and infused virtue [that is, a virtue that has God himself for its object and is poured in by him, not acquired by practice]. Behold how bright and splendid and most sweet a little verse, to every devout mind sweet and savoury [[Ps 18:11|than honey and the honeycomb|super mel et favum]].

paras.t: Sperate in eo, omnis congregatio populi, id est tota Ecclesia ; effundite coram illo corda vestra, id est, orationes vestras et desideria, necessitates, anxietates, pericula et peccata, et quidquid vestris in mentibus residet, coram Deo exponite, in lucem producite, ei ostendite, coram ipso discutite : sicut Jeremias hortatur, Effunde sicut aquam cor tuum ante conspectum Domini Dei tui. Unde primo Regum sancta Anna testatur : Effudi animam meam coram Domino. Deus adjutor noster in aeternum, id est, quamdiu fuerimus : quoniam in via conservat et juvat per gratiam, in patria quoque per gloriam, quae includit confirmationem in bono.
paras.en: [[61:9|Trust in him, all ye congregation of people|Sperate in eo, omnis congregatio populi]], that is, the whole Church; [[61:9|pour out your hearts before him|effundite coram illo corda vestra]]: that is, set forth before God your prayers and desires, needs, anxieties, dangers and sins, and whatever dwells in your minds; bring it into the light, show it to him, lay it open before him; as Jeremias exhorts: [[Lam 2:19|pour out thy heart like water, before the face of the Lord|Effunde sicut aquam cor tuum ante conspectum Domini]] thy God. Hence in the first book of Kings holy Anna testifies: [[1 Kings 1:15|I have poured out my soul before the Lord|Effudi animam meam coram Domino]]. [[61:9|God is our helper for ever|Deus adjutor noster in aeternum]]: that is, for as long as we shall be; for on the way he keeps and helps us by grace, and in the fatherland by glory, which includes confirmation in good.

paras.t: Verumtamen vani filii hominum, loquendo de filiis hominum eo modo quo de eis loquitur Moyses, dicendo, Videntes filii Dei filias hominum : eorum videlicet qui sine caritate et gratia vivunt. Talium ergo hominum filii vani sunt, quoniam opera sua et vitam præsentem ad debitum finem, videlicet vitam æternam, non referunt, sed in rebus creatis sibi finem constituunt, adhærentes creaturis magis quam Creatori. Mendaces filii hominum in stateris : quia injusta pondera habent, vel mendaciter judicant, præferentes mala ac falsa bonis et veris. Quocirca Dominus per Moysen ait : Nolite facere iniquum aliquid in judicio, in regula, in pondere, in mensura ; statera justa et æqua sint pondera, id est justus modius, æquusque sextarius. Ut decipiant ipsi de vanitate in id ipsum, id est, se invicem fallant in rebus vanis, temporalibus et caducis.
paras.en: [[61:10|But vain are the sons of men|Verumtamen vani filii hominum]], speaking of the sons of men in the way that Moses speaks of them when he says: [[Gen 6:2|The sons of God seeing the daughters of men|Videntes filii Dei filias hominum]]; that is, of those who live without charity and grace. The sons of such men, then, are vain, because they do not refer their works and the present life to their due end, namely eternal life, but set up their end for themselves in created things, cleaving to creatures more than to the Creator. [[61:10|the sons of men are liars in the balances|Mendaces filii hominum in stateris]]: because they have unjust weights, or judge lyingly, preferring evil and false things to good and true. Therefore the Lord says through Moses: [[Lev 19:35|Do not any unjust thing in judgment, in rule, in weight, or in measure|Nolite facere iniquum aliquid in judicio, in regula, in pondere, in mensura]]; [[Lev 19:36|Let the balance be just and the weights equal|statera justa et æqua sint pondera]], that is, [[Lev 19:36|the bushel just, and the sextary equal|justus modius, æquusque sextarius]]. [[61:10|that by vanity they may together deceive|Ut decipiant ipsi de vanitate in id ipsum]]: that is, that they may deceive one another in vain things, temporal and perishable.

paras.t: Hujus proinde oppositum consulens sanctus Propheta : Nolite, inquit, sperare in iniquitate : sicut de impiis scriptum est, Confidunt in nihili. Peccatum enim nihil est : ergo nolite in peccato confidere, quasi per injustitiam atque malitiam possitis salvari aut prosperari. Et rapinas nolite concupiscere : id est, nec manu, nec affectu auferatis alicui sua, neque raptoribus communicetis, quia non solum morte digni sunt qui faciunt, sed etiam qui consentiunt. Divitiæ exteriores si affluant copiose, nolite cor apponere, id est, voluntatem vestram nolite inordinate affigere, nolite inordinate amare, retinere, augere, nolite in eis superflue occupari, videlicet ut cum labore acquirantur, cum timore possideantur, cum dolore perdantur. Non ergo culpantur divitiæ, sed inordinatus affectus. Custodiendæ enim et amandæ seu colligendæ sunt divitiæ, secundum quod ad spiritualia bona sunt necessariæ, quatenus habentes victum et vestitum, contentemur et quiescamus, atque de eo quod superest, eleemosynam faciamus. Verumtamen difficile satis est, circa affluentes divitias cor non apponere, secundum quod Christus in Evangelio asserit : Quam difficile qui divitias habent, intrabunt in regnum cœlorum ! Nihilo minus, sicut Deus potentes non abjicit, quum ipse sit potens, nisi abutantur potentia ; sic ipse divites non repellit, quum ipse sit dives, nisi divitiarum abusi fuerint copia. Sanctus Job divitiis suis cor non apposuit, qui ait : Si lætatus sum super divitiis meis multis. Et alibi, cunctis amissis : Dominus dedit (inquit), Dominus abstulit ; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est : sit nomen Domini benedictum.
paras.en: Counselling, therefore, the opposite of this, the holy Prophet says: [[61:11|Trust not|Nolite]], he says, [[61:11|in iniquity|sperare in iniquitate]]; as it is written of the wicked: [[Is 59:4|they trust in a mere nothing|Confidunt in nihili]]. For sin is nothing [that is, sin is not a thing but a lack of the good that should be there]: therefore do not trust in sin, as though by injustice and malice you could be saved or prosper. [[61:11|and covet not robberies|Et rapinas nolite concupiscere]]: that is, take nothing that is another's, neither with the hand nor in desire, and have no part with robbers; for [[Rom 1:32|not only they that do them, but they also that consent to them|non solum morte digni sunt qui faciunt, sed etiam qui consentiunt]] are worthy of death. [[61:11|if riches|Divitiæ]], outward ones, [[61:11|abound|si affluant]] plentifully, [[61:11|set not your heart upon them|nolite cor apponere]]: that is, do not fix your will on them inordinately, do not inordinately love, keep or increase them, do not busy yourselves with them beyond need, so that they are gained with toil, possessed with fear and lost with grief. It is not riches, then, that are blamed, but inordinate affection. For riches are to be kept and loved or gathered so far as they are necessary for spiritual goods, so that, having food and clothing, we may be content and at rest, and give alms out of what is over. Yet it is hard enough not to set one's heart on riches that abound, as Christ declares in the Gospel: [[Luke 18:24|How hardly shall they that have riches enter|Quam difficile qui divitias habent, intrabunt]] into the kingdom of heaven! [the margin gives "Ibid. xviii, 24", which here can only be Luke 18:24; "kingdom of heaven" is as in Matt 19:23] Nevertheless, just as [[Job 36:5|God doth not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty|Deus potentes non abjicit, quum ipse sit potens]], unless they abuse their power, so he does not repel the rich, since he himself is rich, unless they have abused the abundance of their riches. Holy Job did not set his heart upon his riches, who says: [[Job 31:25|If I have rejoiced over my great riches|Si lætatus sum super divitiis meis multis]]. And elsewhere, when he had lost everything: [[Job 1:21|the Lord gave|Dominus dedit]], he says, [[Job 1:21|the Lord hath taken away: as it hath pleased the Lord, so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord|Dominus abstulit ; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est : sit nomen Domini benedictum]].

paras.t: Semel, id est sine retractatione, ut pote immobiliter, firmiter atque certissime, locutus est Deus, per se ipsum jam incarnatum, et per Prophetas ac Apostolos. Duo hæc audivi, in illa locutione occulta et interna, scilicet in illuminatione supernaturali facta per Spiritum Sanctum. Quæ autem sint duo hæc, subdit : quia potestas Dei est, id est justa potentia ad puniendum iniquos ; et tibi, Domine, misericordia ad coronandum bonos ultra condignum. Et hoc sic esse, constat ex eo, quia tu reddes unicuique juxta opera sua, tanquam justissimus judex. De quo in libro Job legitur : Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas ; opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet eis. Videtur autem hic potestas pro justitia accipi, quia ad exercendum justitiam præcipue est necessaria potestas. Unde de Deo alibi scriptum est : Virtus tua, justitiæ initium est. Attribuuntur itaque hæc duo Deo potissimum, quoniam omnia quæ de Deo affirmat divina Scriptura, præsertim per comparationem ad creaturas, ad ista duo reducuntur. Propter quod ante dictum est : Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas. Porro, ut tactum est, hoc quod dicitur, Semel locutus est Deus, non est referendum ad numerum, quum multifarie multisque modis locutus sit nobis, sed ad firmitatem. Juxta quem sensum in libro beati Job dicitur : Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit.
paras.en: [[61:12|once|Semel]], that is, without retracting, inasmuch as immovably, firmly and most certainly, [[61:12|God hath spoken|locutus est Deus]], through himself, now incarnate, and through the Prophets and Apostles. [[61:12|these two things have I heard|Duo hæc audivi]], in that hidden and inward speaking, namely in the supernatural enlightening wrought by the Holy Ghost. What these two things are, he adds: [[61:12|that power belongeth to God|quia potestas Dei est]], that is, just might for punishing the wicked; [[61:13|And mercy to thee, O Lord|et tibi, Domine, misericordia]], for crowning the good beyond their deserving. And that this is so is plain from this, [[61:13|for thou wilt render to every man according to his works|quia tu reddes unicuique juxta opera sua]], as the most just judge. Of whom we read in the book of Job: [[Job 34:10|far from God be wickedness, and iniquity from the Almighty|Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas]]; [[Job 34:11|For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them|opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet eis]]. Here, however, power seems to be taken for justice, because power is especially needed for exercising justice. Hence it is written elsewhere of God: [[Wis 12:16|thy power is the beginning of justice|Virtus tua, justitiæ initium est]]. These two things, then, are attributed to God above all, since everything that divine Scripture affirms of God, especially by comparison with creatures, comes back to these two. Wherefore it was said before: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]]. Further, as was touched on, the words [[61:12|God hath spoken once|Semel locutus est Deus]] are not to be referred to number, since he has spoken to us [[Heb 1:1|at sundry times and in divers manners|multifarie multisque modis]], but to firmness. In which sense it is said in the book of blessed Job: [[Job 33:14|God speaketh once, and repeateth not the selfsame thing the second time|Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit]].

paras.t: Advertendum quoque quod psalmus iste convenientissime exponi possit de Christo, quoniam anima ejus semper perfectissime fuit Deo subjecta, sicut ipse testatur : Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio ; et alibi, Quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper. Tota enim salus animæ Christi creata fuit a Deo, eratque Deus salutaris, id est beatificator, animæ Christi : propter quod apud Joannem dicitur, Non potest homo accipere quidquam, nisi ei datum fuerit desuper.
paras.en: It is also to be noted that this psalm can most fittingly be expounded of Christ, since his soul was always most perfectly subject to God, as he himself testifies: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]; and elsewhere: [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]]. For the whole salvation of Christ's soul was created by God, and God was the saviour, that is, the beatifier, of Christ's soul; wherefore it is said in John: [[John 3:27|A man cannot receive any thing, unless it be given him|Non potest homo accipere quidquam, nisi ei datum fuerit]] from above.

paras.t: Quod autem adjicitur, Non movebor amplius, sic de Christo exponendum est : Post resurrectionem non patiar magis, sed immobilis a vita (id est impassibilis) ero.
paras.en: And what is added, [[61:3|I shall be moved no more|Non movebor amplius]], is to be expounded of Christ thus: After the resurrection I shall suffer no more, but shall be immovable from life (that is, impassible).

paras.t: Quousque, o Judæi increduli, irruitis in hominem, scilicet in me Filium hominis, quem volebatis occidere? Unde ait Judæis: Vos ex patre diabolo estis, et desideria patris vestri vultis perficere. Et iterum dicit ad eos : Quid me quæritis interficere ? Interficitis universi vos, id est animas vestras, non credendo in me. Hoc ad litteram Christus dixit Judæis : In peccato vestro moriemini.
paras.en: [[61:4|How long|Quousque]], O unbelieving Jews, [[61:4|do you rush in upon a man|irruitis in hominem]], namely upon me, the Son of man, whom you wished to kill? Hence he says to the Jews: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil: and the desires of your father you will do|Vos ex patre diabolo estis, et desideria patris vestri vultis perficere]]. And again he says to them: [[John 7:20|Why seek you to kill me?|Quid me quæritis interficere ?]] [[61:4|you all kill|Interficitis universi vos]], that is, your own souls, by not believing in me. This Christ said to the Jews in so many words: [[John 8:21|you shall die in your sin|In peccato vestro moriemini]].

paras.t: Verumtamen pretium meum cogitaverunt repellere, id est, sanguinem meum voluerunt infructuosum efficere. Volebant enim nomen atque memoriam Christi delere, omnesque homines ab ejus fide avertere, ac per hoc sanguinis effusionem sine fructu statuere. Cucurri in siti, id est, vitam in hoc mundo transegi in magno desiderio humanæ salutis. Propter quod in Cœna dixit : Desiderio desideravi hoc pascha manducare vobiscum, antequam patiar. Et pendens in cruce, Sitio, inquit. Ore suo benedicebant mihi Judæi, dicentes : Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces. Et corde suo maledicebant : talia enim dicebant, ut occasionem mortis ex verbis meis elicerent.
paras.en: [[61:5|But they have thought to cast away my price|Verumtamen pretium meum cogitaverunt repellere]]: that is, they wished to make my blood fruitless. For they wished to blot out the name and memory of Christ, and to turn all men away from faith in him, and by this to make the shedding of his blood without fruit[[John 11:47||]] [the margin gives John xi, 47–50]. [[61:5|I ran in thirst|Cucurri in siti]]: that is, I passed my life in this world in great desire for the salvation of men. Wherefore at the Supper he said: [[Luke 22:15|With desire I have desired to eat this pasch with you, before I suffer|Desiderio desideravi hoc pascha manducare vobiscum, antequam patiar]]. And hanging on the cross, [[John 19:28|I thirst|Sitio]], he said. [[61:5|they blessed with their mouth|Ore suo benedicebant]] me, the Jews, saying: [[Matt 22:16|Master, we know that thou art a true speaker and teachest the way of God in truth|Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces]]. [[61:5|but cursed with their heart|Et corde suo maledicebant]]: for they said such things in order to draw from my words an occasion for my death.

paras.t: Denique Deus dicitur Christi salvator, id est a morte resuscitator ac glorificator, non a peccato redemptor. Quomodo autem cetera Christo conveniant, ex præcedentibus innotescit.
paras.en: Lastly, God is called the saviour of Christ, that is, the one who raised him from death and glorified him, not his redeemer from sin. How the rest fits Christ is clear from what has gone before.

paras.t: Ecce quam ineffabilis et admiranda est pulchritudo atque sentententia hujus psalmi: in quo ignea verba divini amoris, piam mentem totaliter inflammantia, tam copiose includuntur, totiesque repetuntur ; in quo obedientia commendatur, moralissima ac saluberrima documenta proponuntur, impii increpantur, et in ipso fine Deus pulcherrime collaudatur. Sit ergo anima nostra Deo semper subjecta, tamque reverenter ac pure intenta, ut amorosa verba psalmi præsentis ardenter et saporose pronuntiet, cor suum coram Deo confidenter effundat, nec exterioribus rebus cor apponat, sed in Deum se penitus erigat, simplificet, figat.
paras.en: Behold how unspeakable and wonderful is the beauty and meaning of this psalm: in which fiery words of divine love, setting the devout mind wholly aflame, are so abundantly contained and so often repeated; in which obedience is commended, most moral and wholesome teachings are set forth, the wicked are rebuked, and at the very end God is most beautifully praised. Let our soul, then, be ever subject to God, and so reverently and purely intent that it may utter the loving words of the present psalm ardently and with relish, pour out its heart before God with confidence[[Lam 2:19||]], and not set its heart on outward things, but raise itself wholly into God, become simple, and fix itself there.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus virtutum, a quo est omnis virtus Sanctorum, Deus auxilii et spei gloriæ nostræ, corda nostra effundimus coram te ; esto adjutor noster, Deus in æternum pius : ut te cooperante, animas nostras in patientia possideamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O God of hosts [*Deus virtutum*, also "God of powers"], from whom is all the virtue of the Saints, God of our help and of the hope of our glory, we pour out our hearts before thee: be thou our helper, God, merciful for ever; that with thee working with us we may possess our souls in patience[[Luke 21:19||]].

62.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI SECUNDI : DEUS, DEUS MEUS, AD TE DE LUCE VIGILO.
62.title_en: Exposition of the sixty-second psalm: O God, my God, to thee do I watch at break of day.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi est : Psalmus David, quum esset in deserto Idumææ : id est, psalmus iste convenit Ecclesiæ seu fideli per David significato, quum esset ipsa Ecclesia in deserto Idumææ, id est in præsenti exilio et valle hac lacrimarum, vitiis atque ærumnis repleta, a bonis vero deserta seu derelicta.
paras.en: The title of the psalm is: [[62:1|A psalm of David while he was in the desert of Edom|Psalmus David, quum esset in deserto Idumææ]]: that is, this psalm befits the Church, or the faithful soul, signified by David, when the Church herself was [[62:1|in the desert of Edom|in deserto Idumææ]] [Idumæa is the Latin name of Edom], that is, in the present exile and this vale of tears, full of vices and hardships, but bare and bereft of good things.

paras.t: Ecclesia ergo, seu quilibet justus, præsentis sæculi afflictiones expertus, divinamque consolationem efflagitans, dicat : Deus, Deus meus, id est tu, Creator omnipotens, qui es omnium Deus ratione creationis et gubernationis : specialiter vero Deus meus, propter specialem providentiam tuam circa me, qua me a malis protegis, in bonis promoves, atque ad ultimum finem recte perducis ; itemque propter singularem dilectionem et venerationem, qua te solum summe amo et colo ; ad te de luce vigilo, id est, statim quum splendor gratiæ tuæ infulserit animæ meæ, consurgo, ad te cordiali affectu mentem erigendo, ad te contemplandum, diligendum, adorandum, colendum ac promerendum. Ad litteram quoque, de luce, id est summo mane, evigilare et surgere debemus ad Dei cultum ac laudem, quatenus sobrio spiritu Deum laudantes ac invocantes, sic interiores oculi illustrentur lumine gratiæ, sicut oculi exteriores perfunduntur solis splendore. Propterea Isaias : De mane, inquit, vigilabo ad te.
paras.en: Let the Church, then, or any just man, who has known by experience the afflictions of this present world and earnestly begs for God's consolation, say: [[62:2|O God, my God|Deus, Deus meus]], that is, thou, almighty Creator, who art the God of all by reason of creation and government, but especially [[62:2|my God|Deus meus]], because of thy special providence over me, by which thou protectest me from evils, advancest me in good things, and bringest me rightly to my last end; and likewise because of the singular love and veneration with which I love and worship thee alone above all; [[62:2|to thee do I watch at break of day|ad te de luce vigilo]], that is, as soon as the splendour of thy grace has shone into my soul, I rise up, lifting my mind to thee with heartfelt affection, to contemplate, love, adore and worship thee, and to merit thee. Literally too, [[62:2|at break of day|de luce]], that is, very early in the morning, we ought to wake and rise for the worship and praise of God, so that, praising and calling upon God with a sober spirit, our inner eyes may be enlightened by the light of grace, as our outward eyes are flooded with the splendour of the sun. Therefore Isaias: [[Is 26:9|in the morning early|De mane]], he says, [[Is 26:9|I will watch to thee|vigilabo ad te]].

paras.t: Sitivit in te anima mea. Hoc est quod dixit superius, Sitivit anima mea ad Deum fortem, vivum. Sitis etenim animæ, est ingens desiderium boni nondum adepti. Est igitur sensus : Anima mea, id est appetitus meus intellectualis, puta voluntas, sitivit in te, id est, intellectuali ac magno desiderio concupivit te adipisci, consolationem tuam acquirere, a præsentibus malis salvari, atque ad te universæ beatitudinis fontem perduci : sicut Tobias ait, Domine, secundum voluntatem tuam fac mecum, et præcipe in pace recipi spiritum meum. Et Isaias : Nomen, inquit, tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ meæ. Anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritu meo in præcordiis meis, etc. Hac siti ardebat mens Pauli, dicentis : Desiderium habeo dissolvi, et esse cum Christo.
paras.en: [[62:2|For thee my soul hath thirsted|Sitivit in te anima mea]]. This is what he said above: [[Ps 41:3|My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God|Sitivit anima mea ad Deum fortem, vivum]]. For the soul's thirst is a vast desire for a good not yet attained. The sense, then, is this: [[62:2|my soul|Anima mea]], that is, my intellectual appetite, namely the will, [[62:2|hath thirsted|sitivit]] [[62:2|for thee|in te]], that is, has longed with a great intellectual desire to attain thee, to obtain thy consolation, to be saved from present evils, and to be brought to thee, the fountain of all beatitude: as Tobias says: [[Tob 3:6|O Lord, do with me according to thy will, and command my spirit to be received in peace|Domine, secundum voluntatem tuam fac mecum, et præcipe in pace recipi spiritum meum]]. And Isaias: [[Is 26:8|thy name|Nomen]], he says, [[Is 26:8|and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul|tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ meæ]]. [[Is 26:9|My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me|Anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritu meo in præcordiis meis]], etc. With this thirst burned the mind of Paul, who says: [[Phil 1:23|having a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ|Desiderium habeo dissolvi, et esse cum Christo]].

paras.t: Quam multipliciter tibi caro mea ! id est, quam multis suspiriis variisque affectibus sitivit tibi, id est ad gloriam tuam, caro mea, id est appetitus inferior sensitivus ! Insinuat iste versiculus carnem multiplicius affici ad Deum, quam animam : quod sane intelligendum est. Sive enim caro sumatur pro corpore solo, sive pro appetitu sensitivo, non conveniet ei sitire in Deum directe, proprie et immediate. Quoniam namque Deus immaterialis et simplex est, solo immateriali appetitu ad ipsum pertingitur, sicut et solo intellectuali oculo contemplatur. Carni autem secundum se, desiderium non convenit, sed in quantum anima informatur ; ipsumque desiderium potius convenit toti composito et animæ, quam carni.
paras.en: [[62:2|for thee my flesh, O how many ways|Quam multipliciter tibi caro mea]]! that is, with how many sighs and how various affections [[62:2|my flesh|caro mea]], that is, the lower, sensitive appetite, has thirsted [[62:2|for thee|tibi]], that is, for thy glory! This little verse suggests that the flesh is moved towards God in more ways than the soul: which must be rightly understood. For whether flesh be taken for the body alone or for the sensitive appetite, it will not befit it to thirst for God directly, properly and immediately. For since God is immaterial and simple, he is reached only by an immaterial appetite, just as he is beheld only by the eye of the intellect. Desire does not befit the flesh in itself, but only in so far as it is informed by the soul [that is, receives its form and life from the soul]; and desire itself belongs rather to the whole composite, and to the soul, than to the flesh.

paras.t: Quod ergo nunc dicitur caro sitire in Deum, dupliciter intelligi potest. Primo, quoniam ipsa est animæ occasio sitiendi in Deum. Corpus quippe quod corrumpitur, aggravat animam ; multasque necessitudines, sollicitudines, afflictiones ac miserias incidit anima ex unione ad corpus. Nam deprimit terrena inhabitatio sensum multa cogitantem. Hinc ergo dicitur caro multipliciter Deum sitire, etiam multiplicius quam anima : quoniam anima plures causas et incitamenta sitiendi Deum sortitur ex corpore, quam ex se ipsa. Tot enim habet causas Deum concupiscendi, quot se experitur impedimentis ab eo elongari ac retrahi. Ideo ad Romanos exclamat Apostolus : Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus? Simili sensu dicitur caro concupiscere adversus animam, non quod caro secundum se concupiscat, sed quia est animæ occasio concupiscendi adversus se ipsam. Anima enim secundum appetitum sensitivum concupiscit contra se ipsam, quantum ad appetitum intellectualem. Secundo intelligitur sic, quod caro, id est appetitus sensitivus, sitit in Deum, non directe et immediate, quasi Deus sit desiderii sui objectum ; sed quoniam ea quæ desiderat, secundum Deum desiderat, scilicet secundum rationis imperium ac directiones virtutum moralium : sititque multiplicius Deum, quam appetitus superior, quoniam plures pœnas, culpas atque miserias habet homo ex parte appetitus sensitivi, quam intellectivi, præsertim quum passiones animæ, quæ nobis sunt origo peccandi, in appetitu sensitivo fundentur.
paras.en: What is said here, then, that the flesh thirsts for God, can be understood in two ways. First, because the flesh is the soul's occasion of thirsting for God. For [[Wis 9:15|the corruptible body is a load upon the soul|Corpus quippe quod corrumpitur, aggravat animam]]; and the soul falls into many needs, cares, afflictions and miseries from its union with the body. For [[Wis 9:15|the earthly habitation presseth down the mind that museth upon many things|deprimit terrena inhabitatio sensum multa cogitantem]]. Hence the flesh is said to thirst for God in many ways, even in more ways than the soul: because the soul draws more causes and incentives for thirsting for God from the body than from itself. For it has as many causes for longing for God as the hindrances by which it finds itself kept far from him and drawn back. Therefore the Apostle cries out to the Romans: [[Rom 7:24|Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?|Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus?]] In a like sense it is said that [[Gal 5:17|the flesh lusteth against|caro concupiscere adversus]] the soul [the Apostle has "against the spirit"], not that the flesh lusts of itself, but because it is the soul's occasion of lusting against itself. For the soul, by its sensitive appetite, lusts against itself as regards its intellectual appetite. Secondly, it is understood thus: that the flesh, that is, the sensitive appetite, thirsts for God not directly and immediately, as though God were the object of its desire, but because what it desires it desires according to God, namely according to the command of reason and the direction of the moral virtues; and it thirsts for God in more ways than the higher appetite, because man has more pains, faults and miseries on the side of the sensitive appetite than of the intellectual, especially since the passions of the soul, which are for us the origin of sinning, are founded in the sensitive appetite.

paras.t: In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa, id est in corpore isto corruptibili, ab originali justitia derelicto, ad errores proclivi, et secundum se omni gratia destitutus. Caro enim non prodest quidquam. Et Apostolus : Scio, inquit, quia non habitat in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum. In hac igitur terra velut in carcere habitans ego, sic in sancto apparui tibi, id est, in sancto affectu, desiderioque cœlesti repræsentavi me ipsum tuo conspectu, effundendo cor meum coram te, atque perpendens me semper a te inspici. Itaque, non obstante corporis mole, ad cœlestia adspiramus, et mundo corde nos ipsos Deo exhibere conemur, quatenus illud beati Apostoli vere dicamus : In carne ambulantes, non secundum carnem militamus.
paras.en: [[62:3|In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water|In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa]], that is, in this corruptible body, forsaken by original justice, prone to errors, and of itself bereft of all grace. For [[John 6:64|the flesh profiteth nothing|Caro enim non prodest quidquam]]. And the Apostle: [[Rom 7:18|I know|Scio]], he says, [[Rom 7:18|that there dwelleth not in me, that is to say, in my flesh, that which is good|quia non habitat in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum]]. Dwelling, then, in this land as in a prison, [[62:3|so in the sanctuary have I come before thee|sic in sancto apparui tibi]], that is, in holy affection and heavenly desire I have presented myself in thy sight, pouring out my heart before thee and considering that I am always seen by thee [*in sancto*, "in the sanctuary", can also mean "in what is holy"; Denis takes it as "in holy affection"]. Therefore, notwithstanding the weight of the body, let us aspire to heavenly things and strive to present ourselves to God with a clean heart, so that we may truly say that word of the blessed Apostle: [[2 Cor 10:3|though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh|In carne ambulantes, non secundum carnem militamus]].

paras.t: Vel sic : In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa, id est in hoc sæculo nequam, quod est virtutibus destitutum, et lata via ducens ad mortem, inaquosum quoque, id est infructuosum et aridum. De hac terra Christus in Evangelio dicit : Quum immundus spiritus exierit ab homine, ambulat per loca arida et inaquosa. Sic in sancto apparui tibi, quia in mundo isto non sæculariter vixi, nec peccatorum vestigia sum sectatus, sed tibi in sanctitate et justitia ministravi.
paras.en: Or thus: [[62:3|In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water|In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa]], that is, in this wicked world, which is bare of virtues and is the broad way leading to death[[Matt 7:13||]], and waterless too, that is, unfruitful and dry. Of this land Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 11:24|When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through places without water|Quum immundus spiritus exierit ab homine, ambulat per loca arida et inaquosa]] [Denis's "dry and waterless places" joins Matt 12:43, "dry places", to Luke 11:24]. [[62:3|So in the sanctuary have I come before thee|Sic in sancto apparui tibi]], because in this world I have not lived in a worldly way, nor followed in the footsteps of sinners, but have served thee in holiness and justice.

paras.t: Et hoc, ut viderem in patria clare per speciem, virtutem tuam, id est omnipotentiam tuam, qua omnia in cœlo et in terra disponis, omnesque Beatos potentissime in bono confirmas ; et gloriam tuam, id est beatitudinem tuam, quatenus intrem in gaudium Domini mei, et omnem excellentiam ejus in cœlo conspiciam.
paras.en: And this [[62:3|to see|ut viderem]], in the heavenly homeland, clearly and by sight [*per speciem*: by open vision, as opposed to by faith], [[62:3|thy power|virtutem tuam]], that is, thy omnipotence, by which thou orderest all things in heaven and on earth, and most mightily confirmest all the Blessed in good; [[62:3|and thy glory|et gloriam tuam]], that is, thy beatitude, so that I may enter into the joy of my Lord[[Matt 25:23||]], and behold all his excellence in heaven.

paras.t: Vel sic : Ut viderem, o Pater æterne, virtutem tuam et gloriam tuam, id est Christum Filium tuum, qui est virtus et sapientia Patris, secundum Apostolum. Si enim, teste Scriptura, filius sapiens est gloria patris ; quanto magis Christus Dei Unigenitus, qui est ipsa æterna, immensa et increata sapientia Patris, dici potest gloria ejus ? Utroque itaque modo per virtutem et gloriam Dei, intelligitur ipsemet Deus sublimis et gloriosus. Nam propter Dei visionem per speciem, tanquam ob præmium ultimatum, finale et consummatum, omnia quæ agimus operari debemus. Propter quod ait Salvator : Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum. Et Moyses ait ad Dominum : Ostende mihi gloriam tuam.
paras.en: Or thus: [[62:3|To see|Ut viderem]], O eternal Father, [[62:3|thy power and thy glory|virtutem tuam et gloriam tuam]], that is, Christ thy Son, who is the power and wisdom of the Father, according to the Apostle[[1 Cor 1:24||]]. For if, as Scripture witnesses, a wise son is the glory of his father[[Prov 10:1||]] [the margin gives Prov. x, 1, which reads "A wise son maketh the father glad"; Denis gives the sense freely], how much more can Christ, the only-begotten of God, who is the very eternal, immeasurable and uncreated wisdom of the Father, be called his glory? In both ways, then, by the power and glory of God is understood God himself, sublime and glorious. For it is for the sake of the vision of God by sight, as for the ultimate, final and consummate reward, that we ought to do all that we do. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent|Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum]]. And Moyses says to the Lord: [[Ex 33:18|Shew me thy glory|Ostende mihi gloriam tuam]].

paras.t: Hæc autem ideo oro, Quoniam melior est misericordia tua, id est gratiæ tuæ præsentia seu pia conversatio, qua hominem in esse spirituali et gratioso conservas, super vitas, id est super omne genus vitæ naturalis. Præstantiora quippe sunt munera gratiæ donis naturæ ; meliusque exsistit, nec esse nec vivere vita naturali peccatis obnoxia, quam sine caritate et gratia esse, quemadmodum Veritas de Juda protestatur : Bonum ei erat, si natus non fuisset homo ille. Non ergo optemus vivere, nisi ut bene vivamus ; magisque optemus omnino non esse, quam miserationibus Dei carere. Labia mea laudabunt te, propter beneficia mihi ac ceteris a te clementer impensa.
