paras.t: Induti sunt arietes ovium, id est, duces ovium Christi, videlicet prælati, pastores atque doctores, induti sunt fortitudine Spiritus Sancti, sapientia et justitia, quatenus alios fortiter pascant, corripiant, instruant et confirment. Taliter induuntur veri et digni prælati Ecclesiæ, quatenus alios vita, doctrina, et omni perfectione præcedant. De arietibus sic indutis apud Jeremiam ait Dominus: Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina. Et valles, id est subjecti et inferiores, abundabunt frumento, id est, semine verbi quod a suis superioribus audient, diligenter implebuntur, ut fructibus vitæ æternæ ditentur. Clamabunt, affectuose orando, ac Dei beneficia confitendo; etenim hymnum dicent, Domino regratiantes pro universis beneficiis suis, ejusque bonitatem indesinenter laudantes, quemadmodum Dominus per Isaiam ait: Ecce servi mei laudabunt præ exsultatione cordis.
paras.en: [[64:14|The rams of the flock are clothed|Induti sunt arietes ovium]], that is, the leaders of Christ's sheep, namely prelates, pastors and doctors, are clothed with the strength of the Holy Ghost, with wisdom and justice, so that they may strongly feed, correct, instruct and strengthen others. So are the true and worthy prelates of the Church clothed, that they may go before others in life, in doctrine and in all perfection. Of rams so clothed the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 3:15|I will give you pastors according to my own heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine|Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina]]. [[64:14|and the vales|Et valles]], that is, subjects and inferiors, [[64:14|shall abound with corn|abundabunt frumento]], that is, they shall be diligently filled with the seed of the word which they will hear from their superiors, so that they may be enriched with the fruits of eternal life. [[64:14|they shall shout|Clamabunt]], praying with affection and confessing the benefits of God; [[64:14|yea they shall sing a hymn|etenim hymnum dicent]], giving thanks to the Lord for all his benefits and praising his goodness unceasingly, as the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 65:14|behold my servants shall praise for joyfulness of heart|Ecce servi mei laudabunt præ exsultatione cordis]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum mirabili venustate splendentem transcurri: in quo Deus benedictus et sanctus pulchre laudatur, affectuosæ preces comprehenduntur, divina beneficia commemorantur. Conemur ergo totis viribus, tam immaculatam ac sanctam ducere vitam, ut Deum cum omni affectu laudemus, in ejus præconio delectemur, ipsum cordialiter invocemus, beneficiorumque ejus nunquam immemores efficiamur; sed taliter ei in præsenti hymnos cantemus, ut hinc emigrantes, in cœlesti Jerusalem eum continuo collaudemus.
paras.en: See, I have run through a psalm shining with wonderful beauty: in which God, blessed and holy, is beautifully praised, affectionate prayers are contained, and the divine benefits are recalled. Let us strive, then, with all our strength to lead a life so spotless and holy that we may praise God with all our affection, delight in proclaiming him, call upon him from the heart, and never become forgetful of his benefits; but let us so sing hymns to him in the present life that, departing hence, we may praise him without ceasing in the heavenly Jerusalem.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, Pater indulgentiæ, spes omnium finium terræ et in mari longe, impietatibus nostris, quæsumus, propitiare; et ne verba iniquorum super nos in æternum prævaleant, tua nos invicta tuitio non derelinquat.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, Father of forgiveness, [[64:6|the hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off|spes omnium finium terræ et in mari longe]], be merciful, we beseech thee, to our transgressions; and lest the words of the wicked prevail over us for ever, may thy invincible protection never forsake us.

65.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI QUINTI : JUBILATE DEO, OMNIS TERRA ; PSALMUM […] DICITE.
65.title_en: Elucidation of the sixty-fifth psalm: Shout with joy to God, all the earth; sing ye a psalm …

paras.t: Psalmi præsentis titulus talis est : In finem, canticum, psalmus resurrectionis : id est, psalmus iste de spirituali fidelium resurrectione pertractans, et in finem, qui est vita æterna, nos dirigens, est canticum, id est exsultatio magna, de resurrectione prædicta.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is this: [[65:1|Unto the end, a canticle of a psalm of the resurrection|In finem, canticum, psalmus resurrectionis]]: that is, this psalm, which treats of the spiritual resurrection of the faithful and directs us unto the end, which is life everlasting, is a canticle, that is, a great exultation, concerning the aforesaid resurrection.

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta in persona Ecclesiæ, vel cujuslibet fidelis, ait : Jubilate Deo, omnis terra. Jubilus gaudium est, quod propter exuberantiam suam non potest totaliter reprimi, neque totaliter explicari : magis autem jubilatur mente, quam voce. Ait itaque : Jubilate, id est, ineffabiliter exsultate, Deo, id est in Deo et ad gloriam Dei, ex contemplatione bonitatis divinæ et ex consideratione beneficiorum ac promissorum ipsius : et hoc faciat omnis terra, id est totus mundus seu incolæ ejus, non solum Judæa, sed universa gentilitas ad fidem conversa, spemque futuræ resurrectionis per Christum adepta. Cui dicit etiam Isaias, Lauda, sterilis quæ non paris, decanta laudem et hinni, quæ non parturiebas : quod ad plebem gentilium olim sterilem, nunc vero in Christo fecundam dictum esse, docet Apostolus.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of the Church, or of any one of the faithful, the Prophet says: [[65:1|Shout with joy to God, all the earth|Jubilate Deo, omnis terra]]. Jubilation [jubilus: a joy too great for words, uttered without words] is a joy which for its very abundance can neither be wholly held in nor wholly expressed; and one jubilates more with the mind than with the voice. So he says: *Shout with joy*, that is, exult beyond words, *to God*, that is, in God and to the glory of God, from contemplating the divine goodness and considering His benefits and promises: and let *all the earth* do this, that is, the whole world or its inhabitants, not Judea only, but all the Gentiles converted to the faith, who have gained through Christ the hope of the resurrection to come. To whom Isaias also says: [[Is 54:1|Give praise, O thou barren, that bearest not: sing forth praise, and make a joyful noise, thou that didst not travail with child|Lauda, sterilis quæ non paris, decanta laudem et hinni, quæ non parturiebas]]; and the Apostle teaches that this was said to the people of the Gentiles, once barren but now fruitful in Christ[[Gal 4:27||]].

paras.t: Psalmum dicite nomini ejus. Psalmus bonam operationem significat. Quid ergo est Deo psallere, nisi voce et opere ipsum laudare? Qui enim Deum verbis magnificat, et operibus inhonorat, sibimetipsi contradicit : imo, quoniam opera præponderant verbis, magis affirmat Deum inhonorabilem esse, quam honorandum. Date gloriam laudi ejus, id est, clarificate laudem divinam verbis ac factis, docendo seu ostendendo quam excellenter laudandus sit Deus. Gloria quippe dicitur clara cum laude notitia. Dum ergo quis docet quam magnifica atque incomparabilis laus Deo debetur, tunc dat gloriam laudi ejus, id est, laudem Dei glorificat.
paras.en: [[65:2|Sing ye a psalm to his name|Psalmum dicite nomini ejus]]. A psalm signifies good works [psalmus: properly a song sung to the psaltery, an instrument played with the hands, and so taken for deeds]. What, then, is it to sing psalms to God, but to praise Him by voice and by deed? For he who magnifies God with words and dishonours Him by his works contradicts himself: nay, since works weigh more than words, he rather declares God to be unworthy of honour than worthy of it. [[65:2|give glory to his praise|Date gloriam laudi ejus]], that is, make the divine praise bright by words and deeds, teaching or showing how excellently God is to be praised. For glory is defined as clear knowledge joined with praise. When, then, someone teaches how magnificent and incomparable is the praise due to God, he gives glory to His praise, that is, he glorifies the praise of God.

paras.t: Dicite Deo, confitendo magnificentiam ejus, majestatemque ejus laudando : Quam terribilia sunt opera tua, Domine ! Terribilia namque sunt opera divinæ justitiæ quæ a principio mundi fecit, videlicet condemnando totum genus humanum propter primorum parentum peccatum, perdendo mundum diluvio, submergendo Ægyptios in mari Rubro ; et alia quæ sacra Scriptura commemorat. Maxime tamen metuenda sunt opera Dei circa iniquos, quos æternaliter damnat. Unde scriptum est : Horribilis Dominus super impios. Et alibi : Unus est Altissimus, creator omnium omnipotens, rex potens et metuendus nimis.
paras.en: [[65:3|Say unto God|Dicite Deo]], confessing His magnificence and praising His majesty: [[65:3|How terrible are thy works, O Lord!|Quam terribilia sunt opera tua, Domine !]] For terrible are the works of divine justice which He has done from the beginning of the world: namely, condemning the whole human race for the sin of our first parents[[Rom 5:12||]], destroying the world by the flood[[Gen 7:21||]], drowning the Egyptians in the Red Sea[[Ex 14:27||]]; and the others that holy Scripture records. Yet most of all to be feared are the works of God towards the wicked, whom He condemns for ever. Hence it is written: [[Soph 2:11|The Lord shall be terrible upon|Horribilis Dominus super]] the ungodly. And elsewhere: [[Ecclus 1:8|There is one most high Creator Almighty, and a powerful king, and greatly to be feared|Unus est Altissimus, creator omnium omnipotens, rex potens et metuendus nimis]].

paras.t: In multitudine virtutis tuæ mentientur tibi inimici tui, id est, propter multa mirabilia atque miracula tua non convertentur ad te, potentiam tuam humiliter venerando : nam etsi verbis opera tua fatentur, tamen operibus negant. Hoc modo mentiti sunt Christo Judæi, qui miracula ejus adscripserunt diabolo, dicentes, In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia ; et, Non est hic homo a Deo ; et, A Nazareth non surgit Propheta. Sic quoque Deo mentiti sunt Ananias et uxor ipsius, dicente Petro ad Ananiam, Non es mentitus hominibus, sed Deo.
paras.en: [[65:3|in the multitude of thy strength thy enemies shall lie to thee|In multitudine virtutis tuæ mentientur tibi inimici tui]], that is, for all Thy many wonders and miracles they will not be converted to Thee by humbly revering Thy power: for though they confess Thy works in words, yet they deny them in deeds[[Tit 1:16||]]. In this way the Jews lied to Christ, ascribing His miracles to the devil and saying: [[Luke 11:15|He casteth out devils by Beelzebub, the prince of devils|In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia]]; and, [[John 9:16|This man is not of God|Non est hic homo a Deo]]; and, A prophet riseth not out of Nazareth[[John 1:46||]] [the margin gives John 1:46; Denis's wording is closer to John 7:52, out of Galilee a prophet riseth not]. So too Ananias and his wife lied to God, as Peter said to Ananias: [[Acts 5:4|Thou hast not lied to men, but to God|Non es mentitus hominibus, sed Deo]].

paras.t: Omnis terra adoret te, id est, cultum latriæ tibi soli exhibeant omnes homines in terra morantes, falsos deos spernendo, teque in omnibus et super omnia venerando. Adoratio enim proprie sumpta, est cultus latriæ, et soli Deo debetur, tanquam omnium creatori omnipotenti, altissimo principi, Deo vero, vivo, trino ac simplici. Unde Deus sublimis apud Isaiam testatur : Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum ; gloriam meam alteri non dabo, et laudem meam sculptilibus. In hoc quoque quod ait Propheta, Omnis terra adoret te, Deus, prophetavit implicite totum mundum ad unius Dei summi cultum fuisse convertendum, atque ab omnibus adorandum esse, sicut per Christi Apostolos factum est. Propter quod in Isaia habetur : Redemptor tuus, Sanctus Israel, Deus omnis terræ vocabitur ; et apud Zachariam, In die illa erit Dominus rex super omnem terram. Et psallat tibi, mentaliter te laudando : sicut ait Apostolus, Psallentes in cordibus vestris Deo semper. Psalmum dicat nomini tuo, ore seu vocibus te laudando : sicut ait Apostolus, Loquentes vobismetipsis in hymnis, et psalmis, et canticis spiritualibus.
paras.en: [[65:4|Let all the earth adore thee|Omnis terra adoret te]], that is, let all men dwelling on the earth show the worship of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone] to Thee alone, spurning false gods, and revering Thee in all things and above all things. For adoration, taken properly, is the worship of latria, and is due to God alone, as the almighty Creator of all things, the most high Prince, the true and living God, three and simple. Hence God on high declares in Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name: I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to graven things|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum ; gloriam meam alteri non dabo, et laudem meam sculptilibus]]. And in saying, *Let all the earth adore thee*, O God, the Prophet foretold implicitly that the whole world was to be converted to the worship of the one supreme God, and that He was to be adored by all, as was done through the Apostles of Christ. For which reason we have in Isaias: [[Is 54:5|thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, shall be called the God of all the earth|Redemptor tuus, Sanctus Israel, Deus omnis terræ vocabitur]]; and in Zacharias: [[Zach 14:9|in that day|In die illa]] [[Zach 14:9|the Lord shall be king over all the earth|erit Dominus rex super omnem terram]]. [[65:4|and sing to thee|Et psallat tibi]], praising Thee in the mind: as the Apostle says, [[Eph 5:19|making melody in your hearts|Psallentes in cordibus vestris]] to God always. [[65:4|let it sing a psalm to thy name|Psalmum dicat nomini tuo]], praising Thee with the mouth or the voice: as the Apostle says, [[Eph 5:19|Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual canticles|Loquentes vobismetipsis in hymnis, et psalmis, et canticis spiritualibus]].

paras.t: Venite ad audiendum verbum Dei, venite ad ecclesiam, venite non tam corporis gressu, quam fidei passu, contemplationis profectu, interiorique reditu ; et videte per contemplationem internam, per fidei lumen, per Spiritus Sancti irradiationem, opera Dei, qui est terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum. Hæc opera, in quibus Deus tam metuendus ostenditur, maxime sunt effectus prædestinationis ac reprobationis divinæ, quibus nonnulli per misericordiam sunt electi, ceteri vero, justitia exigente, præsciti.
paras.en: [[65:5|Come|Venite]] to hear the word of God, come to the church, come not so much with the step of the body as with the pace of faith, the advance of contemplation and the return within; [[65:5|and see|et videte]], by inward contemplation, by the light of faith, by the shining of the Holy Ghost, [[65:5|the works of God|opera Dei]], who is [[65:5|terrible in his counsels over the sons of men|terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum]]. These works, in which God shows Himself so much to be feared, are above all the effects of divine predestination and reprobation, by which some are chosen through mercy, while the rest, as justice requires, are foreknown [that is, foreknown as lost: the reprobate].

paras.t: Porro, quam terribilis sit Deus in consiliis super filios hominum, advertere possumus, si divinæ Scripturæ testimonia diligenter pensemus. Ecce Dominus apud Ezechielem ait : Revertimini et vivite, quia nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat. Cui concordat quod dicit Apostolus : Deus vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire. Et nihilo minus in Actibus Apostolorum legitur : Vetati sunt (Paulus et sui) a Spiritu Sancto loqui verbum Dei in Asia, et non permisit eos Spiritus Jesu. Quomodo ergo vult Deus omnes converti, quando ipsemet prohibet prædicatores ab instructione quorumdam? Sed forte quis dicet istud non esse multum mirabile, neque Deum ostendi terribilem in consiliis super filios hominum ex isto facto ; asseretque Spiritum Sanctum propterea prohibuisse Paulum ab informatione Asianorum, quia prævidit eos non credituros, et ita ad misericordiam pertinet, quod verbum Dei eis prædicatum non fuit ; vel forte, quoniam digni non erant prædicationem divini verbi audire. Sed nonne aliis multis prædicatum est Evangelium Christi a sanctis Apostolis, qui illud non receperunt, atque omnino indigni fuerunt ? Denique fortius movet quod ad Ezechielem Dominus ait : Fili hominis, vade ad domum Israel. Non enim ad populum profundi sermonis et ignotæ linguæ tu mitteris : et si ad illos mittereris, ipsi audirent te ; domus autem Israel nolunt audire te, quia nolunt audire me. Ecce non misit sanctum Prophetam ad eos quos noverat audituros, si eis missus fuisset Propheta ; et misit eum ad eos quos noverat non audituros. Nonne terribile est hoc consilium justi Dei ? Terribile quoque est illud consilium Dei, quod Paulus ad Romanos, de Jacob et Esau loquens, commemorat : Quum nondum nati fuissent, aut aliquid egissent boni aut mali, ut secundum electionem propositum Dei maneret, non ex operibus, sed ex vocante dictum est, Quia major serviet minori : sicut scriptum est, Quoniam Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui.
paras.en: Further, how [[65:5|terrible|terribilis]] God is [[65:5|in his counsels over the sons of men|in consiliis super filios hominum]], we can see if we weigh the testimonies of holy Scripture carefully. Behold, the Lord says in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 18:32|return ye and live|Revertimini et vivite]], for [[Ezech 33:11|I desire not the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way, and live|nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat]]. With which agrees what the Apostle says: God [[1 Tim 2:4|will have all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth|vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire]]. And nevertheless we read in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 16:6|they were forbidden|Vetati sunt]] (Paul and his companions) [[Acts 16:6|by the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia|a Spiritu Sancto loqui verbum Dei in Asia]], and [[Acts 16:7|the Spirit of Jesus suffered them not|non permisit eos Spiritus Jesu]]. How, then, does God will all to be converted, when He Himself forbids preachers to instruct certain people? But perhaps someone will say that this is not very wonderful, and that God is not shown from this deed to be terrible in His counsels over the sons of men; and he will assert that the Holy Ghost forbade Paul to instruct the people of Asia because He foresaw that they would not believe, and so it belonged to mercy that the word of God was not preached to them; or perhaps because they were not worthy to hear the preaching of the divine word. But was not the Gospel of Christ preached by the holy Apostles to many others who did not receive it and were altogether unworthy? Lastly, what the Lord says to Ezechiel moves us more strongly: [[Ezech 3:4|Son of man, go to the house of Israel|Fili hominis, vade ad domum Israel]]. [[Ezech 3:5|For thou art not sent to a people of a profound speech, and of an unknown tongue|Non enim ad populum profundi sermonis et ignotæ linguæ tu mitteris]]: [[Ezech 3:6|and if thou wert sent to them, they would hearken to thee|et si ad illos mittereris, ipsi audirent te]]; [[Ezech 3:7|But the house of Israel will not hearken to thee: because they will not hearken to me|domus autem Israel nolunt audire te, quia nolunt audire me]]. Behold, He did not send the holy Prophet to those whom He knew would hear, if the Prophet had been sent to them; and He sent him to those whom He knew would not hear. Is not this counsel of the just God terrible? Terrible too is that counsel of God which Paul records to the Romans, speaking of Jacob and Esau: [[Rom 9:11|when the children were not yet born, nor had done any good or evil (that the purpose of God according to election might stand|Quum nondum nati fuissent, aut aliquid egissent boni aut mali, ut secundum electionem propositum Dei maneret]], [[Rom 9:12|Not of works, but of him that calleth, it was said to her: The elder shall serve the younger|non ex operibus, sed ex vocante dictum est, Quia major serviet minori]]: as it is written, [[Mal 1:2|I have loved Jacob|Jacob dilexi]], [[Mal 1:3|But have hated Esau|Esau autem odio habui]].

paras.t: Alia multa sunt in divinis Scripturis, in quibus Deus terribilis esse demonstratur in consiliis suis super filios hominum : quæ investigatione non indigent, sed pia ac sobria fide. Propter quod Salomon protestatur : Sicut qui mel comedit multum, non est ei bonum ; sic qui perscrutator est majestatis, opprimetur a gloria. Verumtamen advertendum quod consilium proprie sumptum, non competit Deo. Consilium namque proprie dicitur inquisitio de faciendis, et ita dubitationem præsupponit. Propterea Damascenus : Consilium, inquit, est ignorantis naturæ. Dum ergo consilium Deo adscribitur, sumitur ipsum consilium pro eo quod perfectionis in ipso est, omni sua imperfectione seclusa.
paras.en: There are many other places in holy Scripture in which God is shown to be terrible in His counsels over the sons of men: and these call not for searching but for a devout and sober faith. For which reason Solomon declares: [[Prov 25:27|As it is not good for a man to eat much honey, so he that is a searcher of majesty shall be overwhelmed by glory|Sicut qui mel comedit multum, non est ei bonum ; sic qui perscrutator est majestatis, opprimetur a gloria]]. Yet it must be noted that counsel, taken properly, does not belong to God. For counsel properly means an inquiry about what is to be done, and so presupposes doubt. Hence Damascene says: Counsel is of a nature that does not know. When, then, counsel is ascribed to God, counsel is taken for what there is of perfection in it, all its imperfection being set aside.

paras.t: Qui convertit mare in aridam. Hoc Deus ad litteram fecit in mari Rubro atque Jordane. Spiritualiter vero per mare intelliguntur peccatores in fluctibus vitiorum submersi : hos Deus convertit in aridam, dum fluctuatione animi vitiosa per gratiam Dei exstincta, incipiunt igne amoris siccari, justitiamque sitire. In flumine, id est in mundo, qui mari magno et flumini comparatur ; vel, In flumine præsentis mortalitatis ; vel, In flumine tentationum et adversitatum ; pertransibunt homines boni, pede sancti desiderii, suspirando ad patriam, et ob æternæ vitæ amorem omnia prospera mundi spernentes, omnia quoque ejus adversa fortiter tolerantes, quemadmodum monet Apostolus : Deponentes omne pondus et circumstans nos peccatum, per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen, adspicientes in auctorem fidei et consummatorem Jesum. Ibi lætabimur in ipso, id est, in prædicta transitione de via ad patriam, de mundo ad cœlum, de fluctibus vitiorum ad quietis securitatisque portum, gaudebimus spirituali lætitia, sicut in omni actu virtuoso gaudendum est in eo, de quo subjungitur :
paras.en: [[65:6|Who turneth the sea into dry land|Qui convertit mare in aridam]]. This God did according to the letter in the Red Sea and the Jordan. Spiritually, by the sea are understood sinners sunk in the waves of vice: these God turns into dry land when, the vicious tossing of the mind being quenched by the grace of God, they begin to be dried by the fire of love and to thirst for justice. [[65:6|in the river|In flumine]], that is, in the world, which is compared to a great sea and to a river; or, in the river of this present mortality; or, in the river of temptations and adversities; good men [[65:6|shall pass|pertransibunt]] [[65:6|on foot|pede]] of holy desire, sighing for the fatherland, and for love of eternal life spurning all the prosperity of the world and bravely bearing all its adversities too, as the Apostle admonishes: [[Heb 12:1|laying aside every weight and sin which surrounds us, let us run by patience to the fight proposed to us|Deponentes omne pondus et circumstans nos peccatum, per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen]], [[Heb 12:2|Looking on Jesus, the author and finisher of faith|adspicientes in auctorem fidei et consummatorem Jesum]]. [[65:6|there shall we rejoice in him|Ibi lætabimur in ipso]], that is, in the aforesaid passing from the way to the fatherland, from the world to heaven, from the waves of vice to the haven of rest and safety, we shall be glad with a spiritual gladness, as in every virtuous act one must rejoice in Him of whom it is added:

paras.t: Qui dominatur, in cœlo et terra omnibusque abyssis, in virtute sua sibi consubstantiali, coæterna ac propria, non aliena aut aliunde adepta, in æternum, sine fine, sicut de Deo conscriptum est : Juxta voluntatem suam facit tam in virtutibus cœli, quam in habitatoribus terræ ; et non est qui resistat manui ejus. Potestas ejus, potestas sempiterna, et regnum ejus in generatione et generationem. Oculi ejus super gentes respiciunt, id est, intellectus divinus omnia opera hominum intuetur ac pensat, ut singulis quod merentur restituat. Unde ipse Dominus dicit : Si occultabitur vir in absconditis, et ego non videbo eum ? Et alibi : Domine Deus, cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes vias filiorum Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas.
paras.en: Who [[65:7|ruleth|dominatur]] in heaven and earth and all the deeps, [[65:7|by his power|in virtute sua]], consubstantial with Him, coeternal and His own, not another's or got from elsewhere, [[65:7|for ever|in æternum]], without end; as is written of God: [[Dan 4:32|he doth according to his will, as well with the powers of heaven, as among the inhabitants of the earth: and there is none that can resist his hand|Juxta voluntatem suam facit tam in virtutibus cœli, quam in habitatoribus terræ ; et non est qui resistat manui ejus]]. [[Dan 4:31|his power is an everlasting power, and his kingdom is to all generations|Potestas ejus, potestas sempiterna, et regnum ejus in generatione et generationem]]. [[65:7|his eyes behold the nations|Oculi ejus super gentes respiciunt]], that is, the divine intellect beholds and weighs all the works of men, to render to each what he deserves. Hence the Lord Himself says: [[Jer 23:24|Shall a man be hid in secret places, and I not see him|Si occultabitur vir in absconditis, et ego non videbo eum]]? And elsewhere: O Lord God, [[Jer 32:19|whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the children of Adam, to render unto every one according to his ways|cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes vias filiorum Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas]].

paras.t: Qui exasperant, id est, Deum ad iracundiam provocant ex pertinacia et elatione peccando, non exaltantur in semetipsis, id est, in interioribus suis nihil proficiant, sed omni gratia destituantur, atque dispereant, sicut ait Scriptura : Anima quæ per superbiam aliquid commiserit, quoniam adversus Dominum rebellis fuit, peribit de populo suo. Hæc autem Propheta non imprecando, sed prænuntiando, aut divinæ se justitiæ conformando locutus est. Et quoniam (ut per Ezechielem Dominus frequentissime asserit) domus Israel exasperans fuit, idcirco exaltati non sunt, sed propter iniquitatem suam in Christum commissam, humiliati sunt, oppressi, dejecti.
paras.en: [[65:7|them that provoke him|Qui exasperant]], that is, who provoke God to anger by sinning out of obstinacy and pride, [[65:7|be exalted in themselves|non exaltantur in semetipsis]] [Denis reads exaltantur, are exalted, for the Vulgate's exaltentur, let them be exalted], that is, let them make no progress within themselves, but be stripped of all grace and perish, as the Scripture says: [[Num 15:30|the soul that committeth any thing through pride|Anima quæ per superbiam aliquid commiserit]], [[Num 15:30|because he hath been rebellious against the Lord|quoniam adversus Dominum rebellis fuit]] [[Num 15:30|shall be cut off from among his people|peribit de populo suo]]. Now the Prophet said this not by way of imprecation, but by foretelling it, or by conforming himself to the divine justice. And since (as the Lord very often declares through Ezechiel) the house of Israel was provoking, therefore they were not exalted, but for their iniquity committed against Christ they were humbled, oppressed, cast down.

paras.t: Benedicite, gentes, Deum nostrum, ipsum laudando, et auditam facite vocem laudis ejus, coram aliis ipsum glorificando, et universos, quantum potestis, ad ejus laudem alliciendo.
paras.en: [[65:8|O bless our God, ye Gentiles|Benedicite, gentes, Deum nostrum]], by praising Him, [[65:8|and make the voice of his praise to be heard|et auditam facite vocem laudis ejus]], by glorifying Him before others, and drawing all, as far as you can, to His praise.

paras.t: Qui posuit animam meam ad vitam spiritualem, a morte peccati eam eripiens, et dono gratiæ eam vivificans : sicut ait Apostolus : Deus qui dives est in misericordia, propter nimiam caritatem suam, qua dilexit nos, quum essemus mortui peccatis, convivificavit nos in Christo, cujus gratia estis salvati. Et non dedit in commotionem pedes meos : id est, desideria mea et opera non permisit esse instabilia, vaga et lubrica ; sed confirmavit ac fixit cor meum in se, ita quod nec propter tentationes diaboli, nec propter blandimenta adversitatesve sæculi, potui ab ejus amore atque obsequio separari : imo perseverantiam contulit mihi. Hoc modo stabiliti erant pedes Apostoli, dicentis : Certus sum quia neque mors, neque vita, neque angeli, neque principatus, neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a caritate Dei.
paras.en: [[65:9|Who hath set my soul to live|Qui posuit animam meam ad vitam]]: to the spiritual life, snatching it from the death of sin and quickening it with the gift of grace: as the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:4|God (who is rich in mercy) for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us|Deus qui dives est in misericordia, propter nimiam caritatem suam, qua dilexit nos]], [[Eph 2:5|when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together in Christ (by whose grace you are saved|quum essemus mortui peccatis, convivificavit nos in Christo, cujus gratia estis salvati]]. [[65:9|and hath not suffered my feet to be moved|Et non dedit in commotionem pedes meos]]: that is, He did not allow my desires and works to be unstable, wandering and slippery; but He strengthened my heart and fixed it in Himself, so that neither through the temptations of the devil nor through the allurements or adversities of the world could I be separated from His love and service: nay, He bestowed perseverance on me. In this way were the feet of the Apostle made firm, who says: [[Rom 8:38|I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities|Certus sum quia neque mors, neque vita, neque angeli, neque principatus]], [[Rom 8:39|nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God|neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a caritate Dei]].

paras.t: Quoniam probasti nos, Deus, per adversa et prospera, per te ipsum quoque effective, et per adversarios nostræ salutis permissive. Probat equidem Deus homines, quatenus innotescat, non ipsi Deo, sed aliis, an veraciter timeant Deum, non recedendo ab ejus præceptis propter ea quæ retrahere solent a bono. Et hoc facit Deus interdum effective, per se vel per suos pios ministros, non statim preces orantium exaudiendo, gratiam suspendendo, penuriam seu aliquam infirmitatem infligendo. Propter quod Moyses : Recordaberis, inquit, cuncti itineris per quod adduxit te Dominus Deus tuus, ut affligeret te atque tentaret, et nota fierent quæ versabantur in corde tuo, utrum custodires mandata illius, an non. Interdum autem probat nos Deus permissive, per tentationes dæmonum persecutionesque hominum, juxta illud : Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit eos Dominus. Igne nos examinasti, id est, acuta tribulatione nos discussisti, si fideliter essemus tibi adhærentes, sicut examinatur argentum, id est, quemadmodum per ignem inquiritur an aliquid sit verum argentum. Hinc enim in libro Job dicitur : Deus scit viam meam, et probavit me quasi aurum quod per ignem transit.
paras.en: [[65:10|For thou, O God, hast proved us|Quoniam probasti nos, Deus]], by adversity and prosperity, by Thyself too effectively [that is, as the one who does it], and permissively [that is, by allowing it] through the enemies of our salvation. God indeed proves men so that it may become known, not to God Himself but to others, whether they truly fear God, not departing from His precepts on account of the things that usually draw men back from good. And God does this sometimes effectively, by Himself or by His devout ministers, by not at once hearing the prayers of those who pray, by withholding grace, by inflicting want or some sickness. For which reason Moses says: [[Deut 8:2|thou shalt remember|Recordaberis]], he says, [[Deut 8:2|all the way through which the Lord thy God hath brought thee|cuncti itineris per quod adduxit te Dominus Deus tuus]], [[Deut 8:2|to afflict thee and to prove thee, and that the things that were known in thy heart might be made known, whether thou wouldst keep his commandments or no|ut affligeret te atque tentaret, et nota fierent quæ versabantur in corde tuo, utrum custodires mandata illius, an non]]. But sometimes God proves us permissively, through the temptations of demons and the persecutions of men, according to that saying: [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace, he hath proved them|Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit eos Dominus]]. [[65:10|thou hast tried us by fire|Igne nos examinasti]], that is, Thou hast searched us with sharp tribulation, whether we were faithfully cleaving to Thee, [[65:10|as silver is tried|sicut examinatur argentum]], that is, as by fire it is tested whether something is true silver. Hence it is said in the book of Job: God [[Job 23:10|knoweth my way, and has tried me as gold that passeth through the fire|scit viam meam, et probavit me quasi aurum quod per ignem transit]].

paras.t: Induxisti nos in laqueum. Quidam est laqueus deceptionis et culpæ ; alius vero est laqueus probationis et pœnæ. In primum laqueum introducit nos Deus permissive, dum nos suo justo judicio tentari, superari, ac falli permittit. In laqueum vero secundum sæpe inducit nos effective, quandoque vero permissive dumtaxat. Posuisti tribulationes in dorso nostro. Per dorsum intelligitur totus homo, qui frequenter anima et corpore tribulatur. Quemadmodum enim super dorsum corporis onera ponuntur et deferuntur, sic super totum hominem variæ tribulationes cadunt ac perferuntur.
paras.en: [[65:11|Thou hast brought us into a net|Induxisti nos in laqueum]]. There is one net [laqueus: a snare or noose] of deception and guilt; another is the net of proving and punishment. Into the first net God leads us permissively, when by His just judgment He allows us to be tempted, overcome and deceived. Into the second He often leads us effectively, but sometimes only permissively. [[65:11|thou hast laid afflictions on our back|Posuisti tribulationes in dorso nostro]]. By the back is understood the whole man, who is often afflicted in soul and body. For as burdens are laid upon the back of the body and carried, so various tribulations fall upon the whole man and are borne.

paras.t: Imposuisti homines super capita nostra, id est super nos ipsos et super propriam nostram libertatem ac rationem : ita quod nec proprium sensum, nec propriam voluntatem sequi præsumimus. Hoc Deus aliquando efficienter agit, sicut dum bonos præsidere facit ; interdum vero permissive, sicut dum impii præferuntur. Unde apud Job habetur : Regnare facit Deus hominem hypocritam propter peccata populi. Et Dominus dicit per Isaiam : Dabo pueros principes eorum, et effeminati dominabuntur eis. Dum ergo indigni et impii præsunt, patienter ferre debemus, a quorum dominio liberari nequimus, cogitantes sic accidisse propter nostra demerita ; nec debemus potestati resistere quantumcumque aperta et magna sit præsidentis iniquitas, dummodo ea præcipiat in quibus ei subjicimur, utpote quæ divino honori et nostræ saluti non opponuntur.
paras.en: [[65:12|Thou hast set men over our heads|Imposuisti homines super capita nostra]], that is, over ourselves and over our own liberty and reason: so that we do not presume to follow our own judgment or our own will. This God sometimes does efficiently, as when He makes the good rule; but sometimes permissively, as when the wicked are set over others. Hence we have in Job: God [[Job 34:30|maketh a man that is a hypocrite to reign for the sins of the people|Regnare facit Deus hominem hypocritam propter peccata populi]]. And the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 3:4|I will give children to be their princes, and the effeminate shall rule over them|Dabo pueros principes eorum, et effeminati dominabuntur eis]] [the margin gives Is. iii, 1; the words are in v. 4]. When, then, the unworthy and the wicked are set over us, from whose rule we cannot be freed, we must bear it patiently, thinking that it has so befallen for our demerits; nor must we resist authority, however open and great the iniquity of the one presiding, so long as he commands those things in which we are subject to him, namely such as are not opposed to the honour of God and our salvation.

paras.t: Transivimus per ignem et aquam, id est per contrarias pœnas, sustinendo afflictiones oppositas, ut sunt abundans aeris seu corporis calor, et intemperata frigiditas. Vel, per ignem et aquam, tanquam per duo extrema, intelligenda sunt omnia genera tribulationum intermedia, quibus electi in hoc mundo purgantur, quemadmodum scriptum est : Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino. Et eduxisti nos in refrigerium. Non enim permittit nos Deus tentari supra id quod possumus, nec solet tribulatio esse continua ; sed Deus vicissim consolatur et relevat suos fideles, quemadmodum scriptum est : Increpationem Domini ne reprobes, quoniam ipse vulnerat, et medetur ; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt. Et alibi : Pro certo habet omnis qui colit te, Domine, quia si in tribulatione fuerit, liberabitur : quia post tempestatem tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis. Denique, si in hac vita refrigerium non præstatur, in futuro utique tanto copiosius dabitur, quanto jam magis negatur.
paras.en: [[65:12|We have passed through fire and water|Transivimus per ignem et aquam]], that is, through contrary pains, bearing opposite afflictions, such as excessive heat of the air or of the body, and immoderate cold. Or, by fire and water, as by two extremes, are to be understood all the kinds of tribulation in between, by which the elect are purged in this world, as it is written: [[Job 5:17|Blessed is the man whom God correcteth|Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino]]. [[65:12|and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment|Et eduxisti nos in refrigerium]]. For God does not allow us to be tempted above that which we are able[[1 Cor 10:13||]], nor is tribulation wont to be continual; but God in turn consoles and relieves His faithful, as it is written: [[Job 5:17|refuse not, therefore, the chastising of the Lord|Increpationem Domini ne reprobes]], [[Job 5:18|For he woundeth, and cureth: he striketh, and his hands shall heal|quoniam ipse vulnerat, et medetur ; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt]]. And elsewhere: [[Tob 3:21|this every one is sure of that worshippeth thee|Pro certo habet omnis qui colit te]], O Lord, that [[Tob 3:21|if it be under tribulation, it shall be delivered|si in tribulatione fuerit, liberabitur]]: [[Tob 3:22|because after a storm thou makest a calm, and after tears and weeping thou pourest in joyfulness|quia post tempestatem tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis]]. Lastly, if refreshment is not granted in this life, it will surely be given in the life to come all the more abundantly, the more it is denied now.

paras.t: Introibo in domum tuam, id est ad animam meam, quæ est domus et templum sui Creatoris, dummodo juste vivat, examinando, dijudicando et exercitando me ipsum : quemadmodum scriptum est, Redite, prævaricatores, ad cor ; et alibi, Considera te ipsum. Vel, Introibo in domum tuam, puta militantem Ecclesiam, fide et opere in ecclesiastica unitate morando. Vel, Introibo, ut confido, post hanc vitam, in domum tuam, id est in regnum cœlorum seu Ecclesiam triumphantem, sicut tu, Domine Jesu, dixisti : Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum. In quamlibet harum domorum introibo in holocaustis, id est in fervida oblatione mei ipsius, me totum tuæ voluntati offerendo et exponendo, nec aliquid mihi proprium retinendo. Holocaustum namque dicebatur sacrificium divinæ majestati oblatum, quod ad ejus honorem totaliter comburebatur, in signum quod homo debet se ipsum omnino relinquere, atque divino honori se penitus mancipare cum ardenti amore. Dum ergo hoc modo nos Deo impendimus, domum ejus ingredimur, Deo unimur, et in ipso manemus.
paras.en: [[65:13|I will go into thy house|Introibo in domum tuam]], that is, into my soul, which is the house and temple of its Creator so long as it lives justly, by examining, judging and exercising myself: as it is written, [[Is 46:8|return, ye transgressors, to the heart|Redite, prævaricatores, ad cor]]; and elsewhere, [[Gal 6:1|considering thyself|Considera te ipsum]] [Denis gives the imperative, consider thyself]. Or, *I will go into thy house*, that is, the Church militant, by abiding in faith and works in the unity of the Church. Or, *I will go*, as I trust, after this life, *into thy house*, that is, into the kingdom of heaven or the Church triumphant, as Thou, Lord Jesus, hast said: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum]]. Into whichever of these houses I will go [[65:13|with burnt offerings|in holocaustis]], that is, in the fervent offering of myself, offering and giving up my whole self to Thy will and keeping nothing of my own. For a holocaust was the name of a sacrifice offered to the divine majesty which was wholly burnt in His honour, in sign that man ought to give himself up entirely and yield himself wholly to the honour of God with burning love. When, then, we spend ourselves on God in this way, we enter His house, we are united to God, and we abide in Him.

paras.t: Reddam tibi vota mea, id est, promissa mea persolvam, quæ vel in Baptismo, vel in Ordinis seu religionis susceptione promisi. Secundum quod Salomon jubet : Si quid vovisti Deo, ne moreris reddere ; displicet enim ei stulta et infidelis promissio. Vel, Reddam tibi vota mea, id est, tibi soli offeram omnia desideria mea, nil desiderando extra te, præter te, contra te, sed totum affectum colligendo in te : sicut superius dictum est, Domine, ante te omne desiderium meum. Quæ promissa seu desideria distinxerunt, id est, distincte et ordinate pronunciaverunt, labia mea. Si enim illicitum aliquid esset promissum, non esset solvendum.
paras.en: [[65:13|I will pay thee my vows|Reddam tibi vota mea]], that is, I will discharge my promises, which I made either in Baptism or in receiving holy Orders or the religious life. According to what Solomon commands: [[Eccles 5:3|If thou hast vowed any thing to God, defer not to pay it: for an unfaithful and foolish promise displeaseth him|Si quid vovisti Deo, ne moreris reddere ; displicet enim ei stulta et infidelis promissio]]. Or, *I will pay thee my vows*, that is, I will offer to Thee alone all my desires, desiring nothing outside Thee, besides Thee, against Thee, but gathering my whole affection into Thee: as was said above, [[Ps 37:10|Lord, all my desire is before thee|Domine, ante te omne desiderium meum]]. [[65:14|Which|Quæ]] promises or desires [[65:14|my lips have uttered|distinxerunt labia mea]] [distinxerunt: literally, have distinguished], that is, have pronounced distinctly and in order. For if something unlawful had been promised, it would not have to be paid.

paras.t: Et locutum est os meum verba promissionis et orationis, in tribulatione mea. Homines enim in tribulatione constituti, orationes atque promissiones facere solent ut liberentur. Quid autem promiserit, subjungit : Holocausta medullata, id est bona ac pinguia, scilicet me ipsum igne amoris inflammatum, et corpore ac anima tuæ voluntati paratum, offeram tibi, o Domine Deus, cum incenso arietum, id est cum oratione ducum gregis dominici, videlicet prælatorum Ecclesiæ, quatenus per intercessionem eorum fiat accepta oblatio mea. Offeram tibi boves, id est doctores ac prædicatores verbi Dei, cum hircis, id est peccatoribus pœnitentibus, ut omnes isti orent pro me. Recte autem per holocausta medullata accipitur proprii corporis et animæ amorosa oblatio : quia medulla, quæ est ossis pinguedo, designat cordis devotionem atque amorem. Arietes vero dicuntur prælati, quoniam sicut aries ductor est ovium, sic ipsi aliorum ductores sunt. Boves quoque (teste Apostolo) prædicatores figurant, eo quod corda audientium vomere prædicationis scindant, et semine verbi fecundent. Hircus etiam, qui est animal vile ac fœtidum, peccatores significat.
paras.en: [[65:14|And my mouth hath spoken|Et locutum est os meum]] words of promise and of prayer, [[65:14|when I was in trouble|in tribulatione mea]]. For men set in tribulation are wont to make prayers and promises in order to be delivered. And what he promised, he adds: [[65:15|holocausts full of marrow|Holocausta medullata]], that is, good and fat ones, namely myself, inflamed with the fire of love and made ready in body and soul for Thy will, [[65:15|I will offer up to thee|offeram tibi]], O Lord God, [[65:15|with burnt offerings of rams|cum incenso arietum]] [incensum: literally, incense], that is, with the prayer of the leaders of the Lord's flock, namely the prelates of the Church, so that through their intercession my offering may be accepted. [[65:15|I will offer to thee bullocks|Offeram tibi boves]], that is, the doctors and preachers of the word of God, [[65:15|with goats|cum hircis]], that is, with penitent sinners, so that all these may pray for me. And rightly by holocausts full of marrow is understood the loving offering of one's own body and soul: for the marrow, which is the fat of the bone, signifies the devotion and love of the heart. The rams are the prelates, because as the ram is the leader of the sheep, so they are the leaders of others. The oxen too (as the Apostle testifies[[1 Cor 9:9||]]) figure the preachers, because they cleave the hearts of their hearers with the ploughshare of preaching and make them fruitful with the seed of the word. The goat also, which is a base and stinking animal, signifies sinners.

paras.t: Venite mentis affectu, et si opus est, etiam corporis gressu, et in domo disciplinæ congregate vos ; audite auribus carnis et cordis, et narrabo vobis, o omnes qui timetis Deum timore casto et filiali. Talibus namque narranda sunt occulta ac specialia dona Creatoris, non impœnitentibus et perversis, juxta illud Salvatoris : Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque margaritas vestras ponatis ante porcos. Quid autem narrare velit, adjungit : quanta fecit animæ meæ, id est, quam multa beneficia pie et dulciter contulit mihi, præservando a malis, conservando in bonis. Debet autem quilibet diligenter pensare specialia beneficia Dei sibi exhibita, quatenus Deo gratus exsistat. Elucescit ex his quoque, quod interdum specialia beneficia Dei, sint aliis enarranda ad gloriam Dei et ædificationem auditorum, sicut in Evangelio Christus ait cuidam : Vade, et narra quanta tibi fecit Deus. Hæc autem enarratio maxime licita est prælatis, et eis qui inanis gloriæ tentationem vicerunt ; ceteris non videtur multum secura, nisi ædificatio proximi id requirat. Propter quod Christus in Evangelio cuidam ait : Vide nemini dixeris. Et Isaias : Secretum, inquit, meum mihi, secretum meum mihi.
paras.en: [[65:16|Come|Venite]] with the affection of the mind, and if need be with the step of the body too, and gather yourselves together in the house of discipline[[Ecclus 51:31||]] [the margin reads Eccli. ii, 31; the words are in Ecclus 51:31]; [[65:16|and hear|audite]] with the ears of the flesh and of the heart, [[65:16|and I will tell|et narrabo]] you, O [[65:16|all ye that fear God|omnes qui timetis Deum]] with a chaste and filial fear. For to such are the hidden and special gifts of the Creator to be told, not to the impenitent and perverse, according to that saying of the Saviour: [[Matt 7:6|Give not that which is holy to dogs; neither cast ye your pearls before swine|Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque margaritas vestras ponatis ante porcos]]. And what he wishes to tell, he adds: [[65:16|what great things he hath done for my soul|quanta fecit animæ meæ]], that is, how many benefits He has bestowed on me, devoutly and sweetly, preserving me from evil and keeping me in good. Now every one ought carefully to weigh the special benefits of God shown to himself, so that he may be grateful to God. It is clear from this too that the special benefits of God are sometimes to be told to others, for the glory of God and the edification of the hearers, as Christ says to someone in the Gospel: Go, and [[Luke 8:39|tell how great things God hath done to thee|narra quanta tibi fecit Deus]]. But such telling is lawful above all to prelates, and to those who have overcome the temptation of vainglory; for others it does not seem very safe, unless the edification of their neighbour requires it. For which reason Christ says to someone in the Gospel: [[Matt 8:4|See thou tell no man|Vide nemini dixeris]]. And Isaias: [[Is 24:16|My secret|Secretum]], he says, [[Is 24:16|to myself, my secret to myself|meum mihi, secretum meum mihi]].

paras.t: Ad ipsum ore meo clamavi, Deum laudando et invocando, et exsultavi sub lingua mea, id est, delectationem quamdam in conscientia sensi ex ipsa laude et invocatione Altissimi. Hæc autem delectatio mentis quandoque tam magna est, ut redundet in corpus, faciatque delectationem seu exsultationem in ore.
paras.en: [[65:17|I cried to him with my mouth|Ad ipsum ore meo clamavi]], praising and calling upon God, [[65:17|and I extolled him with my tongue|et exsultavi sub lingua mea]] [Denis reads exsultavi, I exulted, for the Vulgate's exaltavi; sub lingua, literally under my tongue], that is, I felt a certain delight in my conscience from that very praise and invocation of the Most High. And this delight of the mind is sometimes so great that it overflows into the body and causes delight or exultation in the mouth.

paras.t: Iniquitatem si aspexi in corde meo, per approbationem seu consensum peccati, non exaudiet Dominus. Qui enim sibi de peccato mortali conscius est, in peccandi proposito manens, non exauditur, quemadmodum scriptum est : Deus non projiciet simplicem, nec porriget manum malignis. Et in Evangelio legitur : Scimus quoniam peccatores Deus non audit.
paras.en: [[65:18|If I have looked at iniquity in my heart|Iniquitatem si aspexi in corde meo]], by approving of or consenting to sin, [[65:18|the Lord will not hear me|non exaudiet Dominus]]. For he who is conscious of mortal sin, remaining in the purpose of sinning, is not heard, as it is written: [[Job 8:20|God will not cast away the simple, nor reach out his hand to the evil doer|Deus non projiciet simplicem, nec porriget manum malignis]]. And in the Gospel we read: [[John 9:31|we know that God doth not hear sinners|Scimus quoniam peccatores Deus non audit]].

paras.t: Propterea, id est, quia mihi de peccato mortali conscius non sum, exaudivit Deus, et, pro id est, intendit voci deprecationis meæ. Hoc est quod in libro Job scribitur : Si Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus, si mundus et rectus incesseris, statim evigilabit ad te ; et alibi, Si quis cultor est Dei, et voluntatem ejus facit, hunc exaudit. Oranti autem et in peccandi proposito perseveranti, Dominus per Jeremiam ait : Quid clamas ad me? Insanabilis est dolor tuus. Oportet ergo ut vitam studeamus precibus conformare, proponentes semper ex toto corde emendationem in omnibus.
paras.en: [[65:19|Therefore|Propterea]], that is, because I am not conscious to myself of mortal sin, [[65:19|hath God heard me|exaudivit Deus]], [[65:19|and|et]] (put for *that is*) [[65:19|hath attended to the voice of my supplication|intendit voci deprecationis meæ]] [Denis reads intendit for the Vulgate's attendit; both mean hath attended]. This is what is written in the book of Job: If thou [[Job 8:5|wilt beseech the Almighty|Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus]], [[Job 8:6|If thou wilt walk clean and upright, he will presently awake unto thee|si mundus et rectus incesseris, statim evigilabit ad te]]; and elsewhere: [[John 9:31|if a man be a server of God and doth his, will, him he heareth|Si quis cultor est Dei, et voluntatem ejus facit, hunc exaudit]] [the margin gives Joann. ix, 31 for this, which is the Gospel, not Job]. But to him who prays and perseveres in the purpose of sinning, the Lord says through Jeremias: [[Jer 30:15|Why criest thou|Quid clamas]] to me? [[Jer 30:15|thy sorrow is incurable|Insanabilis est dolor tuus]]. We must therefore strive to make our life agree with our prayers, always purposing with our whole heart amendment in all things.

paras.t: Postremo, vir sanctus gratias refert Deo de beneficiis tantis. Benedictus Deus, id est, benedictus sit et laudetur seu benedicatur ab omnibus, qui non amovit orationem meam, et misericordiam suam a me, sed eam pie accepit, misericorditerque implevit.
paras.en: Lastly, the holy man gives thanks to God for such great benefits. [[65:20|Blessed be God|Benedictus Deus]], that is, may He be blessed and praised, or blessed by all, [[65:20|who hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me|qui non amovit orationem meam, et misericordiam suam a me]], but has devoutly received it and mercifully fulfilled it.

paras.t: Ecce in psalmo isto præclaro accenditur animus noster in laude divina, renovatur in eo divinorum beneficiorum memoria, informatur in eo intellectus noster quanta oporteat pati electos in vita præsenti, roboratur quoque in eo bonum propositum bene agendi. Cum omni ergo hilaritate, fervore, compunctione et puritate decantemus hunc psalmum, in laude divina intime gloriantes, Deumque sublimem ab omnibus benedici ac honorari optantes, ejus beneficia affectuose reminiscentes, ob ejus amorem universa contraria libentissime tolerantes, et sibi in omnibus finaliter regratiantes.
paras.en: Behold, in this glorious psalm our mind is kindled in the praise of God; in it the memory of the divine benefits is renewed; in it our understanding is taught how much the elect must suffer in the present life; in it too our good purpose of acting well is strengthened. With all cheerfulness, then, with fervour, compunction and purity let us sing this psalm, glorying inwardly in the praise of God, desiring that God on high be blessed and honoured by all, lovingly calling to mind His benefits, most willingly bearing all adversities for love of Him, and in all things at the last returning thanks to Him.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus conditor universorum, qui dominaris in virtute tua in æternum, oculis clementiæ, quæsumus, super nos semper respice ; pone animam nostram ad bonæ actionis vitam, et nunquam amoveas a nobis misericordiam tuam.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, maker of all things, who rulest by Thy power [[65:7|for ever|in æternum]], look upon us always, we beseech Thee, with the eyes of Thy clemency[[65:7||]]; set our soul to the life of good action[[65:9||]], and never turn away Thy [[65:20|mercy|misericordiam]] from us.

66.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI SEXTI : DEUS MISEREATUR NOSTRI.
66.title_en: Exposition of the sixty-sixth psalm: May God have mercy on us.

paras.t: Hujus insuper psalmi iste est titulus : In finem, in hymnis, psalmus cantici David : id est, psalmus iste in finem seu Christum nos dirigens, est psalmus cantici, id est spiritualis jucunditatis, et convenit David, id est fideli, in hymnis, id est in laudibus Deo exhibendis. Psalmus iste ad litteram est invocatio et gratiarum actio pro Christi incarnatione olim futura, jamque præterita.
paras.en: Further, the title of this psalm is this: [[66:1|Unto the end, in hymns, a psalm of a canticle for David|In finem, in hymnis, psalmus cantici David]]: that is, this psalm, directing us unto the end, or Christ, is a psalm of a canticle, that is, of spiritual gladness, and it belongs to David, that is, to the faithful man, in hymns, that is, in the praises to be offered to God. According to the letter, this psalm is an invocation and a thanksgiving for the incarnation of Christ, once to come and now past.

paras.t: Ait ergo : Deus misereatur nostri, culpam nostram delendo, et omne impedimentum a Christi adventu impediens removendo, et benedicat nobis, id est, munera gratiæ nobis impendat, eademque in nobis copiose multiplicet. Benedicit autem Creator rationali creaturæ, eam per gratiam sanctificando. Creatura quoque benedicit Creatori, eum laudando et omne bonum ipsi attribuendo. Illuminet vultum suum super nos, id est, intellectum suum faciat radiare super nos : sicut superius dictum est, Illustra faciem tuam super servum tuum. Illuminat igitur Deus vultum suum super nos, dum per sapientiam nobis ab ipso infusam, facit nos contemplatores intellectus divini, dumque precibus nostris et actibus pie arridet. Et misereatur nostri, præservando nos a malis futuris, ne efficiamur adventu ejus indigni, gratiam pristinam amittendo.
paras.en: He says therefore: [[66:2|May God have mercy on us|Deus misereatur nostri]], by blotting out our guilt and removing every hindrance that stands in the way of Christ's coming, [[66:2|and bless us|et benedicat nobis]], that is, bestow on us the gifts of grace and multiply them abundantly in us. Now the Creator blesses the rational creature by sanctifying it through grace; and the creature, too, blesses the Creator by praising him and ascribing every good to him. [[66:2|may he cause the light of his countenance to shine upon us|Illuminet vultum suum super nos]], that is, may he make his understanding shine upon us: as was said above, [[Ps 30:17|Make thy face to shine upon thy servant|Illustra faciem tuam super servum tuum]]. God, then, causes his countenance to shine upon us when, through the wisdom poured into us by him, he makes us contemplators of the divine understanding, and when he smiles graciously upon our prayers and deeds. [[66:2|and may he have mercy on us|Et misereatur nostri]], by preserving us from evils to come, lest we become unworthy of his coming by losing the grace we had before.

paras.t: Ut cognoscamus, o Deus Pater, in terra, id est in præsenti exsilio, viam tuam, ambulando in præceptis legis divinæ; vel, Viam, id est Christum, qui de se ipse ait, Ego sum via, veritas et vita. In omnibus gentibus salutare tuum : id est, ad hoc peto misereri, ut cognoscamus omnes gentes converti ad Christum, qui est salutare tuum : de quo Simeon ait, Quia viderunt oculi mei salutare tuum. Orat ergo fidelis in isto versu pro illuminatione Spiritus Sancti, ne erret in via vitæ præsentis, sed operando cognoscat, et cognoscendo ambulet in via Domini, de qua Salvator in Evangelio dicit : Quam angusta est via quæ ducit ad vitam ! et pauci inveniunt eam. Unde apud Tobiam habetur : Pete a Deo ut viam tuam dirigat. In hoc quoque quod ait, In omnibus gentibus salutare tuum, orat Christum ab omnibus gentibus agnosci et honorari.
paras.en: [[66:3|That we may know|Ut cognoscamus]], O God the Father, [[66:3|upon earth|in terra]], that is, in this present exile, [[66:3|thy way|viam tuam]], by walking in the precepts of the divine law; or else "way", that is, Christ, who says of himself, [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas et vita]]. [[66:3|thy salvation in all nations|In omnibus gentibus salutare tuum]]: that is, I ask thee to have mercy to this end, that we may know all nations to be converted to Christ, who is thy salvation, of whom Simeon says, [[Luke 2:30|Because my eyes have seen thy salvation|Quia viderunt oculi mei salutare tuum]]. In this verse, then, the faithful man prays for the enlightening of the Holy Ghost, that he may not stray in the way of this present life, but may know by doing, and by knowing may walk in the way of the Lord, of which the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:14|How narrow|Quam angusta]] is [[Matt 7:14|the way that leadeth to life: and few there are that find it!|via quæ ducit ad vitam ! et pauci inveniunt eam]] Hence it is said in Tobias: [[Tob 4:20|desire of him to direct thy ways|Pete a Deo ut viam tuam dirigat]]. And in saying, [[66:3|thy salvation in all nations|In omnibus gentibus salutare tuum]], he prays that Christ may be acknowledged and honoured by all nations.

paras.t: Consequenter pro beneficio incarnationis Christi, conversionisque mundi, gratias agit. Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus, confessione laudis tuæ et propriæ culpæ, te glorificando, et se ipsos accusando; confiteantur tibi populi omnes, beneficia tua recolendo ac prædicando, tibique gratias infinitas referendo pro Christi incarnatione et sua conversione : quemadmodum ab Isaia scriptum est, Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis, et quæ largitus est nobis secundum indulgentiam suam.
paras.en: Next he gives thanks for the benefit of Christ's incarnation and of the conversion of the world. [[66:4|Let people confess to thee, O God|Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus]], with the confession of thy praise and of their own guilt, glorifying thee and accusing themselves; [[66:4|let all people give praise to thee|confiteantur tibi populi omnes]] [the Latin has the same word, confiteantur, "let them confess", in both halves of the verse], recalling and proclaiming thy benefits, and returning thee infinite thanks for Christ's incarnation and for their own conversion: as Isaias wrote, [[Is 63:7|I will remember the tender mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all the things that the Lord hath bestowed upon us|Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis]], and [[Is 63:7|which he hath given them according to his kindness|quæ largitus est nobis secundum indulgentiam suam]] [Denis reads "which he hath given us", where the Vulgate has "them"].

paras.t: Lætentur interiori lætitia, et exsultent, forinsecus signa internæ jucunditatis ostendendo, gentes ad fidem Christi vocatæ, quoniam judicas populos in æquitate. Nunc enim quotidie judicat Deus populos in æquitate judicio discretionis : de quo ait Salvator, Nunc judicium est mundi. Nam sine personarum acceptione dat Deus fidem et gratiam cunctis se disponentibus, et quod in se est facientibus, ceteros derelinquens : et ita nunc separat electos a reprobis voto et merito. In morte autem cujuslibet atque in fine sæculi erit judicium remunerationis, quo separabuntur boni a malis loco et præmio. Sed quoniam, teste Apostolo, Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis, mirum apparet cur hortetur Propheta gentes lætari, et non potius formidare, quoniam Deus judicat populos in æquitate, nisi quod illas gentes alloquitur, de quibus prædixit : Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus. Qui enim Deum nunc laudant, seque accusant et corrigunt, futurum judicium securi exspectant, et de ejus adventu gaudere merito possunt, quoniam tunc beatam immortalitatem beatitudinemque completam recipient. Propter quod Christus discipulos exhortatur : His autem fieri incipientibus, levate capita vestra, id est, exhilarate corda, quoniam appropinquat redemptio vestra.
paras.en: Let [[66:5|the nations|gentes]] called to the faith of Christ [[66:5|be glad|Lætentur]] with inward gladness, [[66:5|and rejoice|et exsultent]], showing outward signs of their inward joy, [[66:5|for thou judgest the people with justice|quoniam judicas populos in æquitate]]. For now God daily judges the peoples in equity, by the judgment of discernment, of which the Saviour says, [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world|Nunc judicium est mundi]]. For without respect of persons[[Eph 6:9||]] God gives faith and grace to all who dispose themselves and do what is in them [that is, do what lies in their power: the scholastic axiom that God does not refuse grace to one who does what is in him], leaving the rest; and so he now separates the elect from the reprobate in will and in merit. But at the death of each one, and at the end of the world, there will be the judgment of recompense, in which the good shall be separated from the wicked[[Matt 25:32||]] in place and in reward. But since, as the Apostle witnesses, [[Heb 10:31|It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God|Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis]], it seems strange that the Prophet should exhort the nations to rejoice, and not rather to fear, because God judges the peoples in equity; unless it be that he is speaking to those nations of which he said before, [[66:4|Let people confess to thee, O God|Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus]]. For those who now praise God, and accuse and amend themselves, await the judgment to come without fear, and may rightly rejoice at his coming, since they shall then receive blessed immortality and complete beatitude. Wherefore Christ exhorts his disciples: [[Luke 21:28|But when these things begin to come to pass|His autem fieri incipientibus]], [[Luke 21:28|lift up your heads|levate capita vestra]], that is, gladden your hearts, [[Luke 21:28|because your redemption is at hand|quoniam appropinquat redemptio vestra]].

paras.t: Ideo quoque gentes præsertim lætentur, quia et gentes in terra dirigis, per gratiam tuam atque angelicam opem dirigendo eas in viam salutis æternæ. Hac namque directione maxime indigemus, juxta illud Jeremiæ : Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est ut ambulet, et dirigat gressus suos.
paras.en: The nations are to rejoice especially for this reason too: [[66:5|and directest the nations upon earth|et gentes in terra dirigis]], directing them by thy grace and by the help of the angels into the way of eternal salvation. For of this directing we stand most in need, according to that word of Jeremias: [[Jer 10:23|I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his: neither is it in a man to walk, and to direct his steps|Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est ut ambulet, et dirigat gressus suos]].

paras.t: Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus, confiteantur tibi populi omnes. Resumitur versus iste propter sententiæ suæ jucundam et fructuosam dulcedinem.
paras.en: [[66:6|Let the people, O God, confess to thee: let all the people give praise to thee|Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus, confiteantur tibi populi omnes]]. This verse is taken up again because of the delightful and fruitful sweetness of its meaning.

paras.t: Terra dedit fructum suum, id est, virgo Maria peperit Christum. De qua terra scriptum est : Aperiatur terra et germinet Salvatorem. De fructu etiam hujus terræ apud Isaiam inducitur : In die illa erit germen Domini in magnificentia et gloria, et fructus terræ sublimis. Moraliter vero terra dat fructum, dum sancta Ecclesia filios suos spiritualiter instruit, perficit et conservat, et dum […] animæ in cunctis deserviens.
paras.en: [[66:7|The earth hath yielded her fruit|Terra dedit fructum suum]], that is, the Virgin Mary brought forth Christ. Of this earth it is written: [[Is 45:8|let the earth be opened, and bud forth a saviour|Aperiatur terra et germinet Salvatorem]]. Of the fruit of this earth, too, it is said in Isaias: [[Is 4:2|In that day the bud of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory, and the fruit of the earth shall be high|In die illa erit germen Domini in magnificentia et gloria, et fructus terræ sublimis]]. In the moral sense, the earth yields its fruit when holy Church spiritually instructs, perfects and preserves her children, and when […] serving the soul in all things.

paras.t: Benedicat nos Deus, Deus noster, benedicat nos Deus. Quamvis oratio ista ad totam superbeatissimam Trinitatem, singulasque divinas Personas dirigi possit, tamen ad insinuandum personalem distinctionem in Deo, hoc modo exponi potest : Benedicat nos Deus Pater per Filium suum : quemadmodum ait Apostolus, Benedixit nos in omni benedictione spirituali in cœlestibus in Christo Jesu. Benedicat etiam nos Deus noster, id est Filius Dei incarnatus, qui specialiter dicitur Deus noster, juxta illud, Hoc est nomen quod vocabunt eum, Dominus justus noster ; et illud, Vocabitur nomen ejus Emmanuel, quod interpretatur, nobiscum Deus. Benedicat nos Deus, id est Spiritus Sanctus. Et metuant eum, scilicet Deum unum in essentia, et trinum in personis, omnes fines terræ, id est omnes homines in toto orbe morantes : hi metuant Deum timore sancto ac filiali.
paras.en: [[66:7|May God, our God bless us|Benedicat nos Deus, Deus noster]], [[66:8|May God bless us|benedicat nos Deus]]. Although this prayer may be addressed to the whole most supremely blessed Trinity, and to each of the divine Persons, yet, to suggest the distinction of Persons in God, it can be expounded thus: May God the Father bless us through his Son, as the Apostle says, [[Eph 1:3|hath blessed us with spiritual blessings in heavenly places, in Christ|Benedixit nos in omni benedictione spirituali in cœlestibus in Christo Jesu]]. May our God bless us too, that is, the incarnate Son of God, who is in a special way called our God, according to that word, [[Jer 23:6|this is the name that they shall call him: The Lord our just one|Hoc est nomen quod vocabunt eum, Dominus justus noster]]; and that other, [[Is 7:14|his name shall be called Emmanuel|Vocabitur nomen ejus Emmanuel]], [[Matt 1:23|which being interpreted is, God with us|quod interpretatur, nobiscum Deus]]. May God bless us, that is, the Holy Ghost. And let [[66:8|all the ends of the earth|omnes fines terræ]], that is, all men dwelling throughout the world, [[66:8|fear him|Et metuant eum]], namely God, one in essence and three in Persons: let these fear God with a holy and filial fear.

paras.t: Secundum doctores catholicos, in eo quod ter nominatur hic Deus, et post singulariter repetitur, Eum, innuitur Trinitas in personis, et unitas in natura, quemadmodum de Seraphim per Isaiam dicitur : Clamabant alter ad alterum, Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus. Dominus Deus exercituum. Et Dominus per Zachariam dixit ad Satan : Increpet Dominus in te, Satan, et increpet Dominus in te. Judæi tamen affirmant, quod in talibus locis Scripturæ ter dicitur Deus, propter majorem expressionem, secundum quod apud Jeremiam habetur : Terra, terra, terra, audi verbum Domini.
paras.en: According to the Catholic doctors, in that God is named here three times, and afterwards "him" follows in the singular, the Trinity in Persons and the unity in nature are suggested; as it is said of the Seraphim through Isaias: [[Is 6:3|they cried one to another, and said: Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of hosts|Clamabant alter ad alterum, Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus. Dominus Deus exercituum]]. And the Lord said to Satan through Zacharias: [[Zach 3:2|The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan|Increpet Dominus in te, Satan]], and the Lord rebuke thee. The Jews, however, affirm that in such places of Scripture God is named three times for greater emphasis, as is found in Jeremias: [[Jer 22:29|O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the Lord|Terra, terra, terra, audi verbum Domini]] [the margin gives Jer. xxiii, 29; the words are Jer 22:29].

paras.t: Ecce psalmus brevis, et omni fervore ac devotione plenissimus. Conformemus ergo cordis nostri affectum sacratissimis verbis psalmi præsentis, totisque medullis divinam in omnibus misericordiam imploremus, quatenus vitiis pulsis, benedictionibus Christi ditemur, divinique vultus illustratione erudiamur. Deinde pro omni bono communi et generali universorum salute cordialissime Deum deprecemur, quatenus omnes Domino confiteantur, et eum honorent. In hujuscemodi etenim prece divinæ mentis amori utcumque assimilamur, sequentes Patrem nostrum cœlestem, qui omnes homines vult salvos fieri, et solem suum facit super bonos impiosque oriri. Unde ait divinus Apostolus : Obsecro primum omnium fieri obsecrationes, etc., pro omnibus hominibus, pro regibus, etc., ut quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate.
paras.en: Behold a short psalm, and one most full of all fervour and devotion. Let us therefore conform the affection of our heart to the most sacred words of this psalm, and with our whole inmost being implore the divine mercy in all things, that, our vices driven out, we may be enriched with the blessings of Christ and taught by the shining of the divine countenance. Then let us pray to God most heartily for every common good and for the general salvation of all, that all may confess to the Lord and honour him. For in prayer of this kind we are made in some measure like to the love of the divine mind, following our heavenly Father, [[1 Tim 2:4|Who will have all men to be saved|qui omnes homines vult salvos fieri]], and [[Matt 5:45|maketh his sun to rise upon the good, and bad|solem suum facit super bonos impiosque oriri]]. Hence the divine Apostle says: [[1 Tim 2:1|I desire therefore, first of all, that supplications|Obsecro primum omnium fieri obsecrationes]], etc., [[1 Tim 2:1|for all men|pro omnibus hominibus]], [[1 Tim 2:2|For kings|pro regibus]], etc., [[1 Tim 2:2|that we may lead a quiet and a peaceable life in all piety|ut quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate]].

paras.t: Precatio. Deus miserator omnium, Deus lux lucis et fons luminis, illumina super nos vultum tuæ miserationis, benedic nos, et fac cognoscere in terra viam tuam : ut in hac inoffense ambulantes, lætantes et exsultantes, ad mansionem pertingamus æternam, qui in Trinitate vivis et regnas, Deus.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, who hast mercy on all, God, light of light and fount of light, make the countenance of thy mercy to shine upon us, bless us, and make us to know [[66:3|thy way upon earth|in terra viam tuam]]: that, walking in it without stumbling, glad and rejoicing, we may reach the eternal dwelling; who livest and reignest in Trinity, God.

67.title: EXPLANATIO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI SEPTIMI : EXSURGAT DEUS.
67.title_en: Explanation of the sixty-seventh psalm: Let God arise.

paras.t: Declarandi nunc psalmi titulus est : In finem, psalmus cantici David : id est, psalmus iste in Christum nos erigens, est cantici, id est spiritualis exsultationis, quia de nostræ reparationis mysteriis copiose et clare pertractat : et convenit David prophetæ, tanquam auctori; significato autem per David, videlicet Christo, competit sicut subjecto. Præsens etenim psalmus iste ad litteram loquitur de Christo et ejus mysteriis : quia Apostolus plenus Spiritu Sancto, introducit hujus psalmi scripturam de missione Spiritus Sancti : Unicuique, inquiens, nostrum data est gratia secundum mensuram donationis Christi : propter quod dicit, Ascendens in altum, captivam duxit captivitatem, dedit dona hominibus. Et subjungit : Quod autem ascendit, quid est, nisi quia descendit primum in inferiores partes terræ ? Ecce per hanc scripturam, Christi ascensionem probat Apostolus. Probatio autem non valet, nisi ex sensu litterali, ut Augustinus testatur.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is: [[67:1|Unto the end, a psalm of a canticle for David|In finem, psalmus cantici David]]: that is, this psalm, raising us up to Christ [*in finem*, "unto the end", read as "unto Christ", the end of the law], is *of a canticle*, that is, of spiritual exultation, because it treats copiously and clearly of the mysteries of our restoration; and it belongs to David the prophet as to its author, while to him whom David signifies, namely Christ, it belongs as to its subject. For this present psalm speaks literally of Christ and his mysteries, since the Apostle, full of the Holy Ghost, brings in the scripture of this psalm concerning the sending of the Holy Ghost: [[Eph 4:7|to every one|Unicuique]], he says, [[Eph 4:7|of us is given grace, according to the measure of the giving of Christ|nostrum data est gratia secundum mensuram donationis Christi]]. [[Eph 4:8|Wherefore he saith: Ascending on high, he led captivity captive: he gave gifts to men|propter quod dicit, Ascendens in altum, captivam duxit captivitatem, dedit dona hominibus]]. And he adds: [[Eph 4:9|Now that he ascended, what is it, but because he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?|Quod autem ascendit, quid est, nisi quia descendit primum in inferiores partes terræ]] See how by this scripture the Apostle proves the ascension of Christ. But a proof is not valid except from the literal sense, as Augustine testifies.

paras.t: Ait ergo : Exsurgat Deus, id est, Christus qui est verus Deus, a morte resurgat; et dissipentur inimici ejus, id est, Judæi qui eum occiderunt, vastentur, dispergantur et occidantur. Hoc enim contigit eis a Tito atque Romanis in ultionem sanguinis Christi, quemadmodum apud Danielem prædictum est : Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo. Et fugiant qui oderunt eum, a facie ejus, id est infideles Judæi, de quibus Christus in Evangelio ait, Nunc autem et viderunt et oderunt et me et Patrem meum gratis : hi fugiant a facie ejus, id est ab adspectu seu animadversione vindictæ, quam Christus in eos exercuit per Romanos. De qua vindicta Christus apud Isaiam ait : Dies ultionis in corde meo, annus retributionis meæ venit. Nam ante obsidionem Judææ a Romanis, omnes Judæi confugerant in Jerusalem propter timorem illorum.
paras.en: He says, then: [[67:2|Let God arise|Exsurgat Deus]], that is, let Christ, who is true God, rise again from death; [[67:2|and let his enemies be scattered|et dissipentur inimici ejus]], that is, let the Jews who slew him be laid waste, dispersed and slain. For this befell them at the hands of Titus and the Romans in vengeance for the blood of Christ, as was foretold in Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary|Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo]] [*dissipabit*, "shall destroy", is the verb of the psalm's "be scattered"]. [[67:2|and let them that hate him flee from before his face|Et fugiant qui oderunt eum, a facie ejus]], that is, the unbelieving Jews, of whom Christ says in the Gospel: [[John 15:24|now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father|Nunc autem et viderunt et oderunt et me et Patrem meum]] without cause [Denis adds *gratis*, "without cause", from the next verse, John 15:25]. Let these flee from before his face, that is, from the sight, or the punishment, of the vengeance that Christ wreaked upon them by the Romans. Of which vengeance Christ says in Isaias: [[Is 63:4|the day of vengeance is in my heart, the year of my redemption is come|Dies ultionis in corde meo, annus retributionis meæ venit]] [Denis reads *retributionis*, "of my repayment", where the Vulgate has *redemptionis*, "of my redemption"]. For before the siege of Judea by the Romans all the Jews had fled into Jerusalem for fear of them.

paras.t: Sicut deficit fumus, deficiant. Sicut enim deficit fumus lignis subtractis, ita prædicti Judæi defecerunt victualibus jam consumptis, compulsique sunt se hostibus tradere. Paulatim quoque defecerunt ab illo tempore usque in præsens, non solum numero et merito, sed potestate, regno, sacerdotio, et omni honore legis paternæ. Sicut fluit cera a facie, id est ab adspectu et influentia, ignis, sic pereant peccatores, id est Christicidæ prædicti, a facie Dei, id est ab adspectu et inflictione ultionis divinæ : non ut eorum essentia corrumpatur, sed ut omnis gratia eis subtrahatur, et in præsenti vita multipliciter opprimantur, atque in sæculo futuro æternaliter crucientur.
