paras.en: [[67:3|As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away|Sicut deficit fumus, deficiant]] [*deficere*, "to vanish", also means "to fail" or "to run short", and Denis uses it in both senses]. For as smoke fails when the wood is taken away, so the aforesaid Jews failed when their victuals were spent, and were forced to give themselves up to the enemy. Little by little, too, they have failed from that time until now, not only in number and in merit, but in power, kingdom, priesthood and every honour of their fathers' law. [[67:3|as wax melteth before|Sicut fluit cera a facie]], that is, at the sight and influence of [[67:3|the fire|ignis]], [[67:3|so let the wicked perish|sic pereant peccatores]], that is, the aforesaid slayers of Christ, [[67:3|at the presence of God|a facie Dei]], that is, at the sight and infliction of the divine vengeance: not that their being should be destroyed, but that all grace should be withdrawn from them, that they should be oppressed in many ways in this present life, and tormented eternally in the world to come.

paras.t: Denique locus iste, de invisibilibus Christi hostibus intelligi potest, ut sit sensus : Exsurgat Deus (ut dictum est), et dissipentur inimici ejus : id est, potestas et malignitas dæmonum, quibus hominibus nocuerunt, debilitentur. Christus namque fortem armatum ligavit, et merito suæ passionis dæmonum potestatem maxime minoravit. Et fugiant qui oderunt eum, id est, dæmones a cordibus peccatorum atque corporibus obsessorum ejiciantur, a facie ejus, id est virtute præsentiæ Christi, qui operatur ubique. Unde Christus passione instante, dixit : Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras. Post resurrectionem quoque ait Apostolis : Signa eos qui crediderint, hæc sequentur : In nomine meo dæmonia ejicient. Sicut deficit fumus, deficiant : id est, cultus dæmonum seu idololatria per Christi ministros evacuetur, et ipsi diaboli a Christi Apostolis et eorum successoribus penitus superentur, solusque Christus a sæculo sicut Deus colatur. Unde per Isaiam dicitur : Elevabitur Dominus solus in die illa, et idola penitus conterentur. Hinc etiam ait Salvator : Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi super omnem virtutem inimici, et nihil vobis nocebit. Sicut fluit cera a facie ignis, sic pereant peccatores, id est diaboli in malo obstinati, a facie Dei : quia in fine mundi in infernum retrudentur. Ad litteram quoque, istud impletum fuit in Jesu Christo adhuc in mundo conversante, secundum quod in Evangelio legitur : Quotquot habebant plagas, et spiritus immundi quum Jesum videbant, procidebant ei, dicentes : Tu es Filius Dei. Et iterum : Quid nobis, inquiunt, et tibi, Jesu, fili Dei summi ? Venisti ante tempus perdere nos ?
paras.en: Again, this passage can be understood of Christ's invisible enemies, so that the sense is: [[67:2|Let God arise|Exsurgat Deus]] (as has been said), [[67:2|and let his enemies be scattered|et dissipentur inimici ejus]]: that is, let the power and malice of the demons, with which they have harmed men, be weakened. For Christ bound the strong man armed[[Luke 11:21||]][[Luke 11:22||]], and by the merit of his passion greatly diminished the power of the demons. [[67:2|and let them that hate him flee|Et fugiant qui oderunt eum]], that is, let the demons be cast out of the hearts of sinners and the bodies of the possessed, [[67:2|from before his face|a facie ejus]], that is, by the power of the presence of Christ, who works everywhere. Hence Christ said, as his passion drew near: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]. And after the resurrection he says to the Apostles: [[Mark 16:17|these signs shall follow them that believe: In my name they shall cast out devils|Signa eos qui crediderint, hæc sequentur : In nomine meo dæmonia ejicient]]. [[67:3|As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away|Sicut deficit fumus, deficiant]]: that is, let the worship of demons, or idolatry, be brought to nothing by the ministers of Christ, and the devils themselves be utterly overcome by the Apostles of Christ and their successors, and Christ alone be worshipped by the world as God. Hence it is said through Isaias: [[Is 2:17|the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day|Elevabitur Dominus solus in die illa]], [[Is 2:18|and idols shall be utterly destroyed|et idola penitus conterentur]]. Hence too the Saviour says: [[Luke 10:19|Behold, I have given you power to tread|Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi]] [[Luke 10:19|upon all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall hurt you|super omnem virtutem inimici, et nihil vobis nocebit]]. [[67:3|as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish|Sicut fluit cera a facie ignis, sic pereant peccatores]], that is, the devils obstinate in evil, [[67:3|at the presence of God|a facie Dei]]: because at the end of the world they will be thrust down into hell. Literally, too, this was fulfilled in Jesus Christ while he still went about in the world, according to what we read in the Gospel: [[Mark 3:10|as many as had evils|Quotquot habebant plagas]], [[Mark 3:11|And the unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him|et spiritus immundi quum Jesum videbant, procidebant ei]], saying: [[Mark 3:12|Thou art the Son of God|Tu es Filius Dei]]. And again: [[Matt 8:29|What have we|Quid nobis]], they say, [[Matt 8:29|to do with thee, Jesus Son of God|et tibi, Jesu, fili Dei]] most high? [[Matt 8:29|art thou come hither to torment us before the time|Venisti ante tempus perdere nos]]? [Denis's wording, "Son of the most high God" and "to destroy us" (*perdere nos*), draws on Mark 5:7 and Mark 1:24.]

paras.t: Potest etiam locus iste magis communiter explanari, et de Deo secundum divinam operationem intelligi, hoc modo : Exsurgat Deus, non motu aut loco, sed operatione, quatenus bonis subveniat, impiisque resistat, et ita per modum exsurgentis se habeat, sicut superius dictum est : Exsurge, Domine, adjuva nos. Et dissipentur inimici ejus, qui nolunt converti, videlicet hæretici, schismatici, pagani, Judæi, et indurati. Et fugiant qui oderunt eum, a facie ejus, id est, taliter flagellentur a Deo, ut se abscondere cupiant, nec tamen possint, quoniam Deus ubique est. Unde ait Scriptura : Reges terræ, principes, tribuni, divites et fortes, absconderunt se in speluncis et petris montium, dicentes montibus et petris : Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni. Sicut deficit fumus, deficiant, ne opus malum queant implere, et sanctis nocere. Impii namque indesinenter deficiunt, quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent. Sicut fluit cera a facie ignis, etc. Hoc est quod apud Isaiam scriptum est : Sicut devorat stipulam lingua ignis, sic radix impiorum quasi favilla erit, et germen eorum ut pulvis ascendet.
paras.en: This passage can also be explained more generally and understood of God according to his divine working, in this way: [[67:2|Let God arise|Exsurgat Deus]], not by motion or place, but by working, so as to succour the good and resist the wicked, and so bear himself after the manner of one rising up, as was said above: [[Ps 43:26|Arise, O Lord, help us|Exsurge, Domine, adjuva nos]]. [[67:2|and let his enemies be scattered|Et dissipentur inimici ejus]], those who will not be converted, namely heretics, schismatics, pagans, Jews and the hardened. [[67:2|and let them that hate him flee from before his face|Et fugiant qui oderunt eum, a facie ejus]], that is, let them be so scourged by God that they long to hide themselves and yet cannot, since God is everywhere. Hence the Scripture says: [[Apoc 6:15|the kings of the earth and the princes and tribunes and the rich and the strong|Reges terræ, principes, tribuni, divites et fortes]] [[Apoc 6:15|hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of mountains|absconderunt se in speluncis et petris montium]], saying [[Apoc 6:16|to the mountains and the rocks: Fall upon us and hide us from the face of him that sitteth upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb|montibus et petris : Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni]]. [[67:3|As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away|Sicut deficit fumus, deficiant]], so that they cannot accomplish their evil work and harm the saints. For the wicked fail unceasingly, since [[Ps 36:2|they shall shortly wither away as grass|tanquam fœnum velociter arescent]]. [[67:3|as wax melteth before the fire|Sicut fluit cera a facie ignis]], etc. This is what is written in Isaias: [[Is 5:24|as the tongue of the fire devoureth the stubble|Sicut devorat stipulam lingua ignis]], [[Is 5:24|so shall their root be as ashes, and their bud shall go up as dust|sic radix impiorum quasi favilla erit, et germen eorum ut pulvis ascendet]] [Denis has "the root of the wicked" for "their root"].

paras.t: Hæc autem orat Ecclesia, quilibetque fidelis, non zelo vindictæ, sed amore justitiæ, conformans se æquitati divinæ. Vel orat, ut in præsenti sæculo castigentur, ne æternaliter condemnentur. Possent autem ista, dissipatio, fuga, defectio ac disperitio peccatorum, accipi in bono, videlicet ut oremus in eis dissipari, fugari, deficere atque perire, non naturam aut gratiam, sed malitiam. Unusquisque vero tentatus, versus istos dicere potest pro dissipatione, expulsione atque victoria dæmonum, scilicet ut Deus ad auxilium suum exsurgat, sicque virtute gratiæ Dei dæmones tentatores dissipentur, fugiant, deficiant, pereant.
paras.en: Now the Church, and every one of the faithful, prays for these things not from zeal for vengeance but from love of justice, conforming itself to the divine equity. Or it prays that they may be chastised in this present world, lest they be condemned eternally. These things, too, the scattering, flight, failing and perishing of sinners, could be taken in a good sense: namely, that we pray that in them not their nature or grace, but their malice, be scattered, put to flight, fail and perish. And any one who is tempted can say these verses for the scattering, expulsion and defeat of the demons: that is, that God may arise to his help, and so, by the power of God's grace, the tempting demons may be scattered, flee, vanish and perish.

paras.t: Et justi epulentur et exsultent in conspectu Dei, et delectentur in lætitia. Hoc ad litteram accipi potest de sanctis Apostolis ac primitiva Ecclesia in Jerusalem primo collecta. De quibus scribitur in Actis Apostolorum : Erant perseverantes in doctrina et communicatione fractionis panis; et iterum : Omnes qui credebant, erant pariter, et erant illis omnia communia ; et sumebant cibum cum exsultatione et simplicitate cordis.
paras.en: [[67:4|And let the just feast, and rejoice before God: and be delighted with gladness|Et justi epulentur et exsultent in conspectu Dei, et delectentur in lætitia]]. This can be taken literally of the holy Apostles and the primitive Church first gathered in Jerusalem, of whom it is written in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 2:42|they were persevering in the doctrine|Erant perseverantes in doctrina]] [[Acts 2:42|and in the communication of the breaking of bread|et communicatione fractionis panis]]; and again: [[Acts 2:44|all they that believed were together and had all things common|Omnes qui credebant, erant pariter, et erant illis omnia communia]]; and [[Acts 2:46|they took their meat with gladness and simplicity of heart|sumebant cibum cum exsultatione et simplicitate cordis]].

paras.t: Generaliter vero exponi potest hoc modo : Et justi epulentur, nunc per fidem contemplatione divina, reficiunturque pane vitæ et intellectus, et aqua sapientiæ salutaris, id est caritate et gratia ac donis Spiritus Sancti, præcipue autem Sacramento corporis et sanguinis Christi. In futuro quoque epulentur cum angelis, manducantes panem in regno Dei, id est, ipsa superbeatissima Deitate, quæ est omnium Beatorum refectio, beatifice perfruentes. De hac enim epulatione spirituali ait Salomon in Canticis : Comedite, amici, et bibite ; et inebriamini, carissimi. Et Filius Dei ait ad suos : Ego dispono vobis regnum, ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo. Et exsultent in conspectu Dei, id est, justi gaudeant coram Deo : sicut Apostolus dicit, Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. In præsenti enim vita coram Deo, seu in conspectu divino exsultare, est de his et in his lætari, quæ Deo sunt placita, atque se ipsum coram Deo statuere, et in serenitate sanctæ conscientiæ de actibus virtuosis ac divino honore gaudere. In patria enim Sancti exsultant in conspectu Dei, id est de ipsa visione divinæ essentiæ, quoniam vident eum sicuti est. Propter quod dictum est supra : Adimplebis me lætitia cum vultu tuo. Et delectentur in lætitia, quam Deus præstitit eis. Unde de Christianis primitivæ Ecclesiæ scriptum est : Gavisi sunt super consolatione. Intellectuales namque potentiæ, scilicet ratio et voluntas, reflectuntur super proprium actum : et ita mens ipsa delectari potest de sua lætitia.
paras.en: But it can be expounded generally in this way: [[67:4|And let the just feast|Et justi epulentur]]: now, through faith, on divine contemplation, and they are refreshed with [[Ecclus 15:3|the bread of life and understanding|pane vitæ et intellectus]] and [[Ecclus 15:3|the water of wholesome wisdom|aqua sapientiæ salutaris]], that is, with charity and grace and the gifts of the Holy Ghost, but above all with the Sacrament of the body and blood of Christ. In the time to come, too, let them feast with the angels and [[Luke 14:15|eat bread in the kingdom of God|manducantes panem in regno Dei]], that is, blissfully enjoying the supremely blessed Godhead itself, which is the refreshment of all the Blessed. For of this spiritual feasting Solomon says in the Canticles: [[Cant 5:1|eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved|Comedite, amici, et bibite ; et inebriamini, carissimi]]. And the Son of God says to his own: [[Luke 22:29|I dispose to you|Ego dispono vobis]] [[Luke 22:29|a kingdom|regnum]], [[Luke 22:30|That you may eat and drink at my table, in my kingdom|ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo]]. [[67:4|and rejoice before God|Et exsultent in conspectu Dei]], that is, let the just be glad before God, as the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 10:17|he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]]. For in this present life to rejoice before God, or in the divine sight, is to be glad of and in those things that are pleasing to God, and to set oneself before God, and in the serenity of a holy conscience to rejoice in virtuous acts and in the honour of God. But in the fatherland the Saints rejoice in the sight of God, that is, in the very vision of the divine essence, since they [[1 John 3:2|see him as he is|vident eum sicuti est]]. Wherefore it was said above: [[Ps 15:11|thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance|Adimplebis me lætitia cum vultu tuo]]. [[67:4|and be delighted with gladness|Et delectentur in lætitia]], which God has granted them. Hence it is written of the Christians of the primitive Church: [[Acts 15:31|they rejoiced for the consolation|Gavisi sunt super consolatione]]. For the intellectual powers, namely reason and will, reflect upon their own act, and so the mind itself can take delight in its own gladness.

paras.t: Cantate Deo, corde ac vocibus eum laudando ; psalmum, id est verba ac laudem psalmorum, dicite nomini ejus : quia in psalmis Deus pulcherrime collaudatur. Vel : Psalmum, id est bonam operationem, dicite nomini ejus, non solum verbis, sed etiam actibus eum prædicando, prout Christus hortatus est : Videant, inquiens, bona facta vestra, et glorificent Patrem vestrum qui in cœlis est. Non enim oblivioni tradendum est, quod liber iste idcirco Psalterium nuncupatur, quoniam David in instrumento quod psalterium dicitur, psalmos decantare solebat, ore canens et manibus ludens, sicut nunc agit Ecclesia in organis. Psalmus vero proprie dicebatur ipse sonus seu modulatio instrumenti, quod psalterium dictum est : ideoque cantica hujus libri, psalmi vocantur, quia cum tali modulamine canebantur. Hinc ergo per psalterium intelligi potest operatio bona ad laudem Dei exhibita, vel ipsa laus Deo impensa.
paras.en: [[67:5|Sing ye to God|Cantate Deo]], praising him with heart and voice; [[67:5|sing a psalm|psalmum]], that is, the words and praise of the psalms, [[67:5|to his name|dicite nomini ejus]], because in the psalms God is most beautifully praised. Or: [[67:5|sing a psalm|Psalmum]], that is, good works, [[67:5|to his name|dicite nomini ejus]], proclaiming him not only by words but also by deeds, as Christ exhorted: [[Matt 5:16|that they may see|Videant]], he says, [[Matt 5:16|your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven|bona facta vestra, et glorificent Patrem vestrum qui in cœlis est]]. For it must not be forgotten that this book is called the Psalter because David used to sing the psalms on the instrument called the psaltery, singing with his mouth and playing with his hands, as the Church now does on the organ. A psalm, properly, was the very sound or melody of the instrument called the psaltery, and so the songs of this book are called psalms, because they were sung to such music. Hence, then, by the psaltery can be understood a good work done to the praise of God, or the very praise offered to God.

paras.t: Iter facite ei qui ascendit super occasum, id est, viam Christo parate, qua veniat habitaturus in cordibus vestris, quia deliciæ ejus sunt esse cum filiis hominum. Quid utique est Deo iter facere, nisi se ipsum pro posse ad gratiam Dei disponere, obicem removere, propositum peccandi abjiciendo, de præteritis malis dolendo, atque ad obediendum divinis præceptis se extendendo? Hinc enim Joannes Baptista ait allegans verba Isaiæ : Parate viam Domini, rectas facite in solitudine semitas Dei nostri. Itaque iter Deo parare, aliud nihil est nisi quod jubet Amos propheta, Præparare in occursum Dei tui, Israel. Iter igitur facite ei qui ascendit super occasum, id est Christo, qui omnem mortalitatem, passibilitatem ac defectibilitatem in resurrectione transcendit, quoniam, teste Apostolo, Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur. Verumtamen diligenter advertere congruit, quod loco ejus quod hic dicitur, Super occasum, Hebraica veritas habet, ARABOT, quod secundum Hebræos est nomen proprium unius de septem cœlis. Et ergo secundum eos, ista est vera littera : Iter facite ei qui ascendit in cœlum : quod proprie competit Christo, qui in cœlum empyreum gloriose ascendit, quod sine additamento antonomastice cœlum vocatur. Ad idem quoque reduci potest quod dicitur, Super occasum. Judæi enim versus occidentem adorabant, quatenus a gentilibus distinguerentur, qui omnes versus orientem orabant ad reverentiam solis : et ita per hoc quod Christus asseritur ascendisse super occasum, datur intelligi quod ascendit super locum adorationis humanæ, ad locum habitationis angelicæ, scilicet in cœlum empyreum.
paras.en: [[67:5|make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west|Iter facite ei qui ascendit super occasum]], that is, prepare a way for Christ, by which he may come to dwell in your hearts, since his delights are to be with the children of men[[Prov 8:31||]]. What indeed is it to make a way for God, but to dispose oneself as far as one can for the grace of God, and to remove the obstacle, by casting away the purpose of sinning, sorrowing for past sins, and reaching out to obey the divine commandments? For this is why John the Baptist, alleging the words of Isaias, says[[Luke 3:4||]]: [[Is 40:3|Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the wilderness the paths of our God|Parate viam Domini, rectas facite in solitudine semitas Dei nostri]]. So to prepare a way for God is nothing else than what the prophet Amos bids: [[Amos 4:12|be prepared to meet thy God, O Israel|Præparare in occursum Dei tui, Israel]]. [[67:5|make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west|Iter igitur facite ei qui ascendit super occasum]], then, that is, for Christ, who in the resurrection passed beyond all mortality, passibility and defectibility, since, as the Apostle witnesses, [[Rom 6:9|Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more|Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur]]. Yet it should be carefully noted that in place of what is said here, *upon the west*, the Hebrew verity [that is, the Hebrew original] has ARABOT, which according to the Hebrews is the proper name of one of the seven heavens [the rabbinic tradition counts *'arabot* the highest of seven heavens; the word is now usually taken as "deserts" or "steppes"]. And so according to them the true reading is: *Make a way for him who ascendeth into heaven*: which properly belongs to Christ, who ascended gloriously into the empyrean heaven, which by antonomasia [that is, by way of eminence] is called heaven without anything added. What is said, *upon the west*, can also be brought back to the same meaning. For the Jews worshipped towards the west, so as to be distinguished from the gentiles, who all prayed towards the east in reverence of the sun; and so, by its being said that Christ ascended upon the west, we are given to understand that he ascended above the place of human worship to the place of the angels' dwelling, namely into the empyrean heaven.

paras.t: Dominus nomen illi. Per hoc Propheta demonstrat Christum esse verum Deum, quoniam Dominus est nomen proprium Deo, juxta illud : Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum ; et illud, Qui vocat aquas, et effundit eas super faciem terræ, Dominus nomen illi. Quamvis enim hoc nomen, Dominus, conveniat aliis secundum participationem et imperfecte, tamen Deo est proprium ratione propriæ naturæ, et secundum plenitudinem universalem, quoniam in ditione ejus cuncta sunt posita. Unde in Isaia ait : Ego Dominus, et non est alius. Christo quoque secundum humanam naturam convenit, esse omnium dominatorem ac Dominum, secundum quod ipse ait : Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus ; et alibi, Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra. Sed hoc dominium competit sibi, ut homo est, non per naturam, sed per gratiam.
paras.en: [[67:5|the Lord is his name|Dominus nomen illi]]. By this the Prophet shows that Christ is true God, since *Lord* is the proper name of God, according to that saying: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum]]; and that other: [[Amos 5:8|that calleth the waters|Qui vocat aquas]], [[Amos 5:8|and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name|et effundit eas super faciem terræ, Dominus nomen illi]] [Denis gives the end in the psalm's words, *Dominus nomen illi*, where the Vulgate of Amos has *Dominus nomen est ejus*]. For although this name *Lord* belongs to others by participation and imperfectly, yet it is proper to God by reason of his own nature and according to a universal fullness, since all things are set in his power[[Esth 13:9||]]. Hence he says in Isaias: [[Is 45:18|I am the Lord, and there is no other|Ego Dominus, et non est alius]]. To Christ also, according to his human nature, it belongs to be the ruler and Lord of all, according as he himself says: [[John 3:35|The Father loveth the Son: and he hath given all things into his hand|Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus]]; and elsewhere: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]. But this lordship belongs to him as man not by nature but by grace.

paras.t: Exsultate in conspectu ejus. Hoc est quod superius dixit, Justi epulentur et exsultent in conspectu Dei. Turbabuntur a facie ejus, patris orphanorum et judicis viduarum, id est, infideles Judæi et omnes perversi turbabuntur ab adspectu seu ultione Christi, qui est pater orphanorum et judex viduarum. Judæi enim turbabantur, quando a Romanis vastabantur. In extremo quoque judicio omnes maligni turbandi sunt, sicut in libro Sapientiæ scriptum est : Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili, gementes præ angustia spiritus.
paras.en: [[67:5|Rejoice ye before him|Exsultate in conspectu ejus]]. This is what he said above: Let [[67:4|the just feast, and rejoice before God|Justi epulentur et exsultent in conspectu Dei]]. They [[67:5|shall be troubled at his presence|Turbabuntur a facie ejus]], [[67:6|the father of orphans, and the judge of widows|patris orphanorum et judicis viduarum]], that is, the unbelieving Jews and all the perverse shall be troubled at the sight or the vengeance of Christ, who is the father of orphans and the judge of widows. For the Jews were troubled when they were laid waste by the Romans. At the last judgment, too, all the wicked are to be troubled, as is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:2|seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear|Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili]], [[Wis 5:3|groaning for anguish of spirit|gementes præ angustia spiritus]].

paras.t: Deus in loco sancto suo. Locus sanctus, in quo Deus esse et habitare censetur, est anima pura, quemadmodum scriptum est, Anima justi sedes est Sapientiæ; vel cœlum empyreum, in quo Divinitas eminentius operatur, clariusque refulget : propter quod apud Isaiam dicitur, Cœlum mihi sedes est ; vel ipsa Ecclesia militans ac triumphans, quarum utraque appellatur templum, domus et locus Dei : unde et alibi, Dominus in templo sancto suo ; et rursus Dominus protestatur, Ubi sunt duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi sum in medio eorum.
paras.en: [[67:6|God in his holy place|Deus in loco sancto suo]]. The holy place in which God is held to be and to dwell is the pure soul, as it is written: The soul of the just is the seat of Wisdom[[Wis 7:27||]] [the margin gives Wisdom 7:27, where Wisdom passes into holy souls; the saying itself is not in the Vulgate in these words]; or the empyrean heaven, in which the Godhead works more eminently and shines forth more clearly, wherefore it is said in Isaias, [[Is 66:1|Heaven is my throne|Cœlum mihi sedes est]]; or the Church itself, militant and triumphant, each of which is called the temple, the house and the place of God. Hence elsewhere too: [[Ps 10:5|The Lord is in his holy temple|Dominus in templo sancto suo]]; and again the Lord declares: [[Matt 18:20|where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them|Ubi sunt duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi sum in medio eorum]].

paras.t: Deus qui inhabitare facit unius moris in domo. Per hanc domum intelligi potest Ecclesia militans, et quælibet congregatio devota, vel ipsum habitaculum devotorum. Deus namque per fidem, caritatem, et gratiam efficit servos suos unius voluntatis, ejusdemque ritus et consuetudinis. Unde in Actis Apostolorum legitur de primitiva Ecclesia : Multitudinis credentium erat cor unum et anima una. Propter quod ait Apostolus : Obsecro vos, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ut id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata. Multum ergo vitandum est vitium singularitatis, præsertim in claustralibus, quibus una præfixa est regula. Verumtamen, quoniam (teste Apostolo) unusquisque in suo sensu abundat, non potest esse perfecta conformitas morum in omnibus in vita præsenti, sicut nec perfecta caritas aut gratia. Sed quanto caritas et gratia fuerint ampliores, tanto laudabilium morum major erit conformitas : ideo quod ait, Qui inhabitare facit unius moris in domo, præcipue verum est de civibus triumphantis Ecclesiæ, quia in eis summa concordia est, plena conformitas, gratia consummata, caritasque perfecta.
paras.en: [[67:7|God who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house|Deus qui inhabitare facit unius moris in domo]]. By this house can be understood the Church militant, and any devout community, or the very dwelling-place of the devout. For God, through faith, charity and grace, makes his servants of one will, and of the same rite and custom [*mos*, "manner", means also "custom" or "way of life"]. Hence we read in the Acts of the Apostles of the primitive Church: [[Acts 4:32|the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul|Multitudinis credentium erat cor unum et anima una]]. Wherefore the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:10|I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing and that there be no schisms among you|Obsecro vos, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ut id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata]]. The vice of singularity [that is, affecting to be different from one's brethren], then, is much to be avoided, above all in cloistered religious, for whom one rule has been laid down. Yet since, as the Apostle witnesses, [[Rom 14:5|Let every man abound in his own sense|unusquisque in suo sensu abundat]], there cannot be a perfect conformity of manners in all men in this present life, as neither is there perfect charity or grace. But the fuller charity and grace are, the greater will be the conformity of praiseworthy manners. Therefore what he says, [[67:7|who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house|Qui inhabitare facit unius moris in domo]], is true above all of the citizens of the Church triumphant, since in them there is the highest concord, full conformity, consummate grace and perfect charity.

paras.t: Qui, scilicet Christus, educit vinctos, id est patres et justos omnes antiqui temporis in limbo olim detentos, in fortitudine propria divina. Christus enim statim post resurrectionem, de limbo patrum eduxit sanctos in eo captivos, ut Zacharias ad Christum loquens, ait : Tu quoque in sanguine testamenti tui, emisisti vinctos tuos de lacu in quo non est aqua. Sed quia de ista eductione infra clarius scribitur, ideo verba prædicta convenientius aliter exponuntur, hoc modo : Qui educit vinctos, id est peccatores, vinculis vitiorum irretitos, et dæmonum jugo subjectos, in fortitudine sua omnipotenti atque divina. Nam peccata relaxare, gratiam impertiri, et impium justificare, Deo est proprium : estque majus et fortius opus, impium justificare, quam cœlum et terram creare, secundum Augustinum. Hos vinctos Christus educit de morte ad vitam, de culpa ad gratiam, de statu damnationis ad salutem.
paras.en: [[67:7|Who|Qui]], namely Christ, [[67:7|bringeth out them that were bound|educit vinctos]], that is, the fathers and all the just of the old time once held in limbo, [[67:7|in strength|in fortitudine]], his own divine strength. For Christ, straight after his resurrection, brought out of the limbo of the fathers the saints held captive in it, as Zacharias says, speaking to Christ: [[Zach 9:11|Thou also by the blood of thy testament hast sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit, wherein is no water.|Tu quoque in sanguine testamenti tui, emisisti vinctos tuos de lacu in quo non est aqua]] But since this bringing out is written of more clearly below [at v. 19, *Thou hast led captivity captive*], the words above are more fittingly expounded otherwise, in this way: [[67:7|Who bringeth out them that were bound|Qui educit vinctos]], that is, sinners entangled in the bonds of vices and subject to the yoke of the demons, [[67:7|in strength|in fortitudine]], his own almighty and divine strength. For to remit sins, to bestow grace and to justify the ungodly is proper to God; and it is a greater and mightier work to justify the ungodly than to create heaven and earth, according to Augustine. These bound ones Christ brings out from death to life, from guilt to grace, from the state of damnation to salvation.

paras.t: Similiter eos qui exasperant : id est, illos quoque Deus educit juxta modum expositum, qui non solum peccant, sed etiam fidem impugnant, Deo rebelles sunt, et eum exasperant : qualis erat Saulus, quem allocutus est Christus : Saule, Saule, inquiens, quid me persequeris? Qui habitant in sepulcris. Exasperatores enim divinæ majestatis habitant in sepulcris, id est in pessima consuetudine, in profundissimo miseriæ lacu, sub gravi sarcina habitus vitiosi. Quibus convenit illud Proverbiorum : Impius quum in profundum venerit peccatorum, contemnit. In talium ergo eductione seu conversione major refulget divina potentia, quam in justificatione peccatoris non indurati, nec in vitiis habituati. Quidam vero satis convenienter distinguunt hoc quod dicitur, Similiter eos qui exasperant, ab eo quod subditur, Qui habitant in sepulcris, ita quod non solum Deus educit habituatos in vitiis, sed etiam in mortali peccato defunctos, resuscitans illos ad vitam naturalem ac meritoriam, ut patet de juvene quem suscitavit Joannes evangelista, de mortuo quoque qui se ipsum suspendit, quem suscitavit B. Martinus : et in hoc maxime declaratur omnipotentia Creatoris.
paras.en: [[67:7|in like manner them that provoke|Similiter eos qui exasperant]]: that is, God also brings out, in the manner explained, those who not only sin but also assail the faith, are rebels against God and provoke him [*exasperare*, "to provoke", is literally "to embitter"]; such as was Saul, whom Christ addressed: [[Acts 9:4|Saul, Saul|Saule, Saule]], he said, [[Acts 9:4|why persecutest thou me|quid me persequeris]]? [[67:7|that dwell in sepulchres|Qui habitant in sepulcris]]. For those who provoke the divine majesty dwell in sepulchres, that is, in the worst of customs, in the deepest pit of misery, under the heavy burden of a vicious habit. To them applies that saying of the Proverbs: [[Prov 18:3|The wicked man, when he is come into the depths of sins, contemneth|Impius quum in profundum venerit peccatorum, contemnit]]. In the bringing out, then, or conversion of such men the divine power shines forth more greatly than in the justifying of a sinner who is not hardened nor habituated to vice. Some, however, quite fittingly distinguish what is said, [[67:7|in like manner them that provoke|Similiter eos qui exasperant]], from what follows, [[67:7|that dwell in sepulchres|Qui habitant in sepulcris]], so that God brings out not only those habituated to vices but also those who have died in mortal sin, raising them again to natural and meritorious life, as is plain from the young man whom John the Evangelist raised, and from the dead man who had hanged himself, whom Blessed Martin raised: and in this above all is the omnipotence of the Creator declared.

paras.t: Consequenter ponit Propheta exemplum, vel potius argumentum ab exemplo acceptum. Deus, quum egredereris in conspectu populi tui, educendo filios Israel ex Ægypto ; quum pertransires in deserto, perducendo eos ad montem Sinai. Dicitur autem Deus egredi et pertransire, non locum mutando, quum ipse incircumscriptibilis incommutabilisque consistat ; sed quia in die ostendebat populo suo viam per columnam nubis, et in nocte per columnam ignis. Secundo, ratione protectionis et providentiæ, qua misericorditer eos defendit et gratiose providit. Hinc enim Moyses ait ad Dominum : Si non tu ipse præcedas nos, ne educas nos de loco isto. Tertio dicitur Deus tunc egressus, et pertransisse in conspectu populi sui, quoniam nuntius ejus, videlicet angelus ex persona Dei apparens et loquens, eos præcessit, secundum quod Moysi dixit Dominus : Ecce ego mittam angelum meum, qui præcedat te, et custodiat in via, et introducat in locum quem paravi.
paras.en: Next the Prophet sets down an example, or rather an argument drawn from an example. [[67:8|O God, when thou didst go forth in the sight of thy people|Deus, quum egredereris in conspectu populi tui]], by leading the children of Israel out of Egypt; [[67:8|when thou didst pass through the desert|quum pertransires in deserto]], by bringing them to Mount Sinai. Now God is said to go forth and to pass through, not by changing place, since he abides uncircumscribed and unchangeable [that is, not contained or bounded by any place], but because by day he showed his people the way by the pillar of cloud, and by night by the pillar of fire[[Ex 13:21||]]. Secondly, by reason of the protection and providence with which he mercifully defended them and graciously provided for them. For hence Moses says to the Lord: [[Ex 33:15|If thou thyself dost not go before, bring us not out of this place|Si non tu ipse præcedas nos, ne educas nos de loco isto]]. Thirdly, God is said then to have gone forth and passed through in the sight of his people because his messenger, namely an angel appearing and speaking in the person of God, went before them, according to what the Lord said to Moses: [[Ex 23:20|Behold I will send my angel, who shall go before thee, and keep thee in thy journey, and bring thee into the place that I have prepared.|Ecce ego mittam angelum meum, qui præcedat te, et custodiat in via, et introducat in locum quem paravi]]

paras.t: Terra mota est. Tunc enim mons Sinai videbatur moveri ac tremere. Vel, Terra mota est, id est, habitantes in terra, hominesque terreni commoti sunt, ut in Exodo legitur : Tunc conturbati sunt principes Edom, robustos Moab obtinuit tremor. Etenim cœli distillaverunt a facie Dei Sinai, a facie Dei Israel : id est, cœli aerii tunc pluviam emiserunt a præsentia Dei, apparentis per creaturam subjectam in monte Sinai, et a præsentia Dei Israel, id est populi ex Jacob progeniti. Tunc namque nubes densissima operuit montem Sinai, et ex nube illa pluvia emanabat : et manna de cœlo per modum stillicidiorum descendit.
paras.en: [[67:9|The earth was moved|Terra mota est]]. For then Mount Sinai was seen to move and tremble[[Ex 19:18||]]. Or, [[67:9|The earth was moved|Terra mota est]], that is, those dwelling on the earth, and earthly men, were moved, as we read in Exodus: [[Ex 15:15|Then were the princes of Edom troubled, trembling seized on the stout men of Moab|Tunc conturbati sunt principes Edom, robustos Moab obtinuit tremor]]; [[67:9|and the heavens dropped at the presence of the God of Sina, at the presence of the God of Israel|Etenim cœli distillaverunt a facie Dei Sinai, a facie Dei Israel]]: that is, the heavens of the air then sent forth rain from the presence of God, who appeared on Mount Sinai through a creature made subject to him, and from the presence of the God of Israel, that is, of the people sprung from Jacob. For then a very thick cloud covered Mount Sinai[[Ex 19:16||]], and rain flowed out of that cloud; and the manna came down from heaven in the manner of drops[[Ex 16:14||]].

paras.t: Denique ista mystice exponi possunt, hoc modo : Deus, Dei Unigenite, quum egredereris de secretissimo sinu Dei Patris, apparendo in mundo per carnem assumptam, egrediens in conspectu populi tui, scilicet Apostolorum ac aliorum credentium, inter quos conversari dignatus es ; quum pertransires in deserto, id est in mundo vitiis pleno, et bonis derelicto ; vel, In deserto, mittendo Apostolos ad gentilitatem olim desertam ac sterilem. Terra mota est : id est, homines terreni et peccatores, ad fidem pœnitentiamque conversi sunt ; etenim cœli, id est sancti Apostoli, distillaverunt aquam sapientiæ salutaris, et pluviam gratiæ cœlestis, a facie Dei Sinai, id est a gratiosa præsentia Dei, qui legem dedit in monte Sinai. Hoc modo Apostoli prædicatoresque sancti irrigaverunt ad fidem conversos. Propter quod Apostolus loquitur : Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit.
paras.en: Lastly, these words can be explained mystically, in this way: [[67:8|O God|Deus]], only-begotten of God, [[67:8|when thou didst go forth|quum egredereris]] from the most secret bosom of God the Father, appearing in the world through the flesh thou didst take, going forth [[67:8|in the sight of thy people|in conspectu populi tui]], namely of the Apostles and of the other believers among whom thou didst deign to live; [[67:8|when thou didst pass through the desert|quum pertransires in deserto]], that is, through the world, full of vices and forsaken by good men; or, in [[67:8|the desert|deserto]]: by sending the Apostles to the gentiles, once desert and barren. [[67:9|The earth was moved|Terra mota est]]: that is, earthly men and sinners were converted to faith and penance; [[67:9|and the heavens|etenim cœli]], that is, the holy Apostles, [[67:9|dropped|distillaverunt]] the water of saving wisdom and the rain of heavenly grace [[67:9|at the presence of the God of Sina|a facie Dei Sinai]], that is, from the gracious presence of God, who gave the law on Mount Sinai. In this way the Apostles and holy preachers watered those converted to the faith. Wherefore the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 3:6|I have planted, Apollo watered|Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit]].

paras.t: Ex primo autem et litterali sensu horum duorum versuum Propheta concludit, dicendo : Pluviam voluntariam segregabis, Deus, hereditati tuæ. Quasi dicat : Si tu tantam gratiam contulisti Israelitis in deserto et monte Sinai, dando eis manna et legem per descensum angeli in montem Sinai ; tunc utique multo amplius gratiam magnam dabis populo tuo per ascensionem tuam in cœlum. Ait ergo : Pluviam voluntariam, id est rorem gratiæ tuæ, fluenta doctrinæ, irrigationesque varias Spiritus Sancti gratis ac sponte infusas, segregabis, id est, seorsum ac specialiter dabis, hereditati tuæ, id est populo christiano electo, quem proprio sanguine liberasti. Hoc Christus in die Pentecostes et interim sæpe fecit. Et infirmata est : id est, Ecclesia quæ est hereditas tua, ex se ipsa sibi sufficiens non fuit, nec per naturam salvari aut aliquid promereri valebat. Non enim sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Ideo subdit : tu vero perfecisti eam, conferendo ei per gratiam, quod non habuit per naturam. Hinc namque Christus post resurrectionem dixit discipulis : Sedete in civitate quoadusque induamini virtute ex alto. Ad litteram quoque Ecclesia Dei sæpe infirmata est, refrigescente caritate multorum, et propter varias persecutiones tyrannorum. Deus vero perficit eam, gratiam renovando, et adversarios auferendo.
paras.en: From the first and literal sense of these two verses the Prophet draws his conclusion, saying: [[67:10|Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, O God|Pluviam voluntariam segregabis, Deus, hereditati tuæ]]. As if he were saying: If thou didst bestow so great a grace on the Israelites in the desert and on Mount Sinai, giving them the manna, and the law through the coming down of an angel upon Mount Sinai, then surely thou wilt give far greater grace to thy people through thy ascension into heaven. So he says: [[67:10|a free rain|Pluviam voluntariam]], that is, the dew of thy grace, the streams of doctrine and the various waterings of the Holy Ghost, poured in freely and of thine own will, thou [[67:10|shalt set aside|segregabis]], that is, thou wilt give apart and specially, [[67:10|for thy inheritance|hereditati tuæ]], that is, to the chosen Christian people, whom thou hast set free with thy own blood. This Christ did on the day of Pentecost, and often in the meantime. [[67:10|and it was weakened|Et infirmata est]]: that is, the Church, which is thy inheritance, was not sufficient for itself of itself, and could not be saved, or merit anything, by nature. [[2 Cor 3:5|Not that we are sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God|Non enim sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]. Therefore he adds: [[67:10|but thou hast made it perfect|tu vero perfecisti eam]], by bestowing on it through grace what it did not have by nature. For hence Christ said to the disciples after the resurrection: [[Luke 24:49|stay you in the city till you be endued with power from on high|Sedete in civitate quoadusque induamini virtute ex alto]]. Literally too, the Church of God has often been weakened, as the charity of many grew cold[[Matt 24:12||]], and through the various persecutions of tyrants. But God makes it perfect, by renewing grace and taking away its adversaries.

paras.t: Animalia tua, id est populi christiani, qui sunt oves tuæ, habitabunt in ea, id est in Ecclesia, per fidem et obedientiam manendo in ecclesiastica unitate. Parasti in dulcedine tua, id est dulci bonitate ac pia clementia tua, pauperi, Deus, id est populo christiano pauperi spiritu, qui in primitiva Ecclesia pauper erat atque abjectus : huic populo parasti temporalia bona ad sufficientiam, juxta illud, Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis. Parasti etiam ei cibum ac potum superdignissimum, corpus tuum ac sanguinem, sub sacramentalibus formis contentum. Sed et gratiam, consolationem internam, omniumque divinorum charismatum abundantiam nobis parasti, quibus promisisti : Quodcumque petieritis (inquiens) Patrem in nomine meo, hoc faciam.
paras.en: [[67:11|thy animals|Animalia tua]], that is, the Christian peoples, who are thy sheep, shall [[67:11|dwell|habitabunt]] [[67:11|In it|in ea]], that is, in the Church, by remaining through faith and obedience in the unity of the Church; [[67:11|thou hast provided|Parasti]] [[67:11|in thy sweetness|in dulcedine tua]], that is, in thy sweet goodness and loving clemency, [[67:11|for the poor|pauperi]], [[67:11|O God|Deus]], that is, for the Christian people, poor in spirit, which in the early Church was poor and despised: for this people thou hast provided temporal goods enough, according to that saying: [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis]]. Thou hast provided for it also a most surpassingly worthy food and drink, thy body and blood, contained under the sacramental forms. And thou hast provided for us grace too, inward consolation and an abundance of all the divine gifts, for thou hast promised us: [[John 14:13|whatsoever you shall ask|Quodcumque petieritis]], he says, [[John 14:13|the Father in my name, that will I do|Patrem in nomine meo, hoc faciam]].

paras.t: Dominus dabit verbum, id est sermonem promptum atque prudentiam, evangelizantibus virtute multa, id est sanctis Apostolis et eorum sequacibus, qui potenter prædicaverunt, confirmando doctrinam miraculis atque effusione proprii sanguinis. Illis enim in Evangelio Christus ait : Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri.
paras.en: [[67:12|The Lord shall give the word|Dominus dabit verbum]], that is, ready speech and prudence, [[67:12|to them that preach good tidings with great power|evangelizantibus virtute multa]], that is, to the holy Apostles and their followers, who preached mightily, confirming their doctrine by miracles and by the shedding of their own blood. For to them Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri]].

paras.t: Rex virtutum dilecti dilecti. Versus iste intricatus est atque obscurus. Interdum vero una translatio aliam exponit, et ita utile fuit plures fieri translationes. Translatio autem Hieronymi juxta Hebræum, sic habet : Reges exercituum fœderabuntur. Nam per Apostolorum doctrinam, in Christi amore, fide et cultu unanimes facti sunt multi reges, principes, nobiles et potentes. Sic ergo nunc dicitur : Rex virtutum, id est reges fortes, accipiendo singulare pro plurali, ut in Exodo Dominus ait ad Pharaonem : Adhuc retines filium meum (id est filios Israel) ? Sic ergo, Reges fortes, supplendum est, facti sunt, dilecti, id est amici, dilecti, id est Jesu Christi, de quo ait Pater : Hic est Filius meus dilectus. Vel sic : Rex virtutum, id est Deus Pater qui est rex angelorum, qui dicuntur virtutes cœlestes, et sunt dilecti, id est ipsius Christi, qui est Filius Dei carissimus. Omnes enim angeli sancti, sunt ipsius Christi, sicut servi sunt dominorum suorum. Unde Christus in Evangelio de se ipso asserit : Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos. Repetitur autem, Dilecti, et sequitur, et speciei domus dividere spolia : id est, Christus qui est Dei Patris dilectus, est etiam dilectus in quantum homo, et electus dividere spolia, id est secundum diversos gradus ac status distinguere homines, quos ipse de ore inimici redemit, atque de morte eripuit, dando eis diversa munera gratiarum, quemadmodum Apostolus attestatur : Quosdam, inquiens, posuit in Ecclesia, primo Apostolos, deinde Prophetas, tertio doctores : et hoc fit speciei domus, id est ad ornamentum Ecclesiæ. Talis enim distinctio ecclesiasticarum personarum, cedit in ornamentum Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[67:13|The king of powers is of the beloved, of the beloved|Rex virtutum dilecti dilecti]]. This verse is tangled and obscure. But sometimes one translation explains another, and so it was useful that several translations were made. Now Jerome's translation from the Hebrew has it thus: The kings of armies shall be leagued together. For through the teaching of the Apostles many kings, princes, nobles and mighty men were made of one mind in the love, faith and worship of Christ. So it is said here: [[67:13|The king of powers|Rex virtutum]], that is, strong kings, taking the singular for the plural, as in Exodus the Lord says to Pharao: Dost thou yet hold back my son (that is, the children of Israel)?[[Ex 4:23||]] [the margin gives Exod. iv, 23, where God calls Israel *my son*; the words *Adhuc retines* are those of Exod 9:17, *Dost thou yet hold back my people*]. So, then: strong kings (we must supply "have become") [[67:13|of the beloved|dilecti]], that is, friends, [[67:13|of the beloved|dilecti]], that is, of Jesus Christ, of whom the Father says: [[Matt 3:17|This is my beloved Son|Hic est Filius meus dilectus]]. Or thus: [[67:13|The king of powers|Rex virtutum]], that is, God the Father, who is king of the angels, who are called the heavenly powers [*virtutes*], and they are [[67:13|of the beloved|dilecti]], that is, of Christ himself, who is the most dear Son of God. For all the holy angels belong to Christ himself, as servants belong to their masters. Hence Christ in the Gospel declares of himself: [[Matt 13:41|The Son of man shall send his angels|Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos]]. Now *Of the beloved* is repeated, and there follows: [[67:13|and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils|et speciei domus dividere spolia]]: that is, Christ, who is the beloved of God the Father, is beloved also inasmuch as he is man, and chosen to divide the spoils, that is, to distinguish according to different degrees and states the men whom he himself redeemed from the mouth of the enemy and snatched from death, giving them different gifts of graces, as the Apostle attests: [[1 Cor 12:28|some|Quosdam]], he says, he [[1 Cor 12:28|hath set|posuit]] [[1 Cor 12:28|in the church; first apostles, secondly prophets, thirdly doctors|in Ecclesia, primo Apostolos, deinde Prophetas, tertio doctores]]. And this is done for [[67:13|the beauty of the house|speciei domus]], that is, for the adornment of the Church. For such a distinction of persons in the Church makes for the adornment of the Church.

paras.t: Deinceps alloquitur sanctus David fideles, dicendo : Si dormiatis inter medios cleros, id est, si tranquilla conscientia quiescatis inter duas hereditates, seu inter duo genera bonorum divinitus concessorum, id est inter bona temporalia vitæ præsentis et bona spiritualia vitæ futuræ, sic transeundo per bona temporalia, ut non amittatis æterna ; tunc pennæ columbæ, id est virtutes ac operationes Ecclesiæ, fiunt et sunt deargentatæ, id est puræ et immaculatæ, quando temporalia non appetuntur inordinate, sed solum prout necessaria sive utilia sunt ad adipiscenda bona cœlestia ; et posteriora, id est extrema opera, dorsi ejus, id est scapularum columbæ seu Ecclesiæ, super se portantis jugum Domini, in pallore auri, id est, terminabuntur in fervore caritatis perfectæ, quæ designatur per aurum. Caritas enim non excidit, sed quæ nunc imperfecta est, in patria fit perfecta, dummodo quiescamus inter medios cleros, ut dictum est : quoniam qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit. Per cleros itaque intelliguntur hereditates, quoniam κλῆρος Græce, Latine dicitur sors : sortes autem ex divina promissione, partes hereditatis vocantur. Ecclesia quoque appellatur columba, propter innocentiam atque munditiam vitæ. Aurum vero caritatem significat, juxta illud : Suadeo tibi emere a me aurum ignitum probatum.
paras.en: Next holy David addresses the faithful, saying: [[67:14|If you sleep among the midst of lots|Si dormiatis inter medios cleros]], that is, if with a quiet conscience you rest between two inheritances, or between two kinds of goods granted by God, namely between the temporal goods of the present life and the spiritual goods of the life to come, so passing through temporal goods as not to lose the eternal; then [[67:14|the wings of a dove|pennæ columbæ]], that is, the virtues and works of the Church, become and are [[67:14|covered with silver|deargentatæ]], that is, pure and spotless, when temporal things are not sought inordinately, but only so far as they are necessary or useful for gaining the heavenly goods; [[67:14|and the hinder parts|et posteriora]], that is, the last works, [[67:14|of her back|dorsi ejus]], that is, of the shoulders of the dove, or of the Church, which carries the yoke of the Lord upon herself, [[67:14|with the paleness of gold|in pallore auri]], that is, will end in the fervour of perfect charity, which is signified by gold. For [[1 Cor 13:8|Charity never falleth away|Caritas enim non excidit]], but the charity that is now imperfect is made perfect in our heavenly country, provided we rest among the midst of lots, as has been said: since [[Matt 10:22|he that shall persevere unto the end, he shall be saved|qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit]]. By *cleri*, then, inheritances are understood, since *kleros* in Greek is called *sors* [lot] in Latin; and lots, by God's promise, are called portions of an inheritance. The Church too is called a dove because of the innocence and cleanness of her life. And gold signifies charity, according to that saying: [[Apoc 3:18|I counsel thee to buy of me gold, fire tried|Suadeo tibi emere a me aurum ignitum probatum]].

paras.t: Dum discernit cœlestis reges super eam, id est, dum Christus, qui singulariter vocatur cœlestis, quippe de quo scriptum est, Qui de cœlo venit, super omnes est : dum ergo iste rex cœlestis discernit, id est, discrete ac sapienter disponit, reges super eam, id est rectores, videlicet Apostolos et eorum imitatores, super Ecclesiam, destinando eos per totum mundum ad docendum omnes gentes ; nive dealbabuntur in Selmon, id est, super nivem purificabuntur fideles in umbra gratiæ Dei. Selmon enim uno modo est proprium nomen cujusdam montis ; alio modo est nomen commune, obscuritatem significans, sicque accipitur modo, et potest designare gratiam vitæ, quæ obscura est per comparationem ad gratiam patriæ. Vel potest ita intelligi : Nive dealbabuntur gentes, quæ ante conversionem ad fidem seu gratiam, erant in obscuritate ac tenebris.
paras.en: [[67:15|When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her|Dum discernit cœlestis reges super eam]], that is, when Christ, who is called in a singular way the heavenly one, since it is written of him: [[John 3:31|He that cometh from heaven is above all|Qui de cœlo venit, super omnes est]]; when, then, this heavenly king [[67:15|appointeth|discernit]], that is, discreetly and wisely sets, [[67:15|kings over her|reges super eam]], that is, rulers, namely the Apostles and those who follow their example, over the Church, sending them through the whole world to teach all nations[[Matt 28:19||]]; [[67:15|they shall be whited with snow in Selmon|nive dealbabuntur in Selmon]], that is, the faithful will be made pure beyond snow in the shadow of the grace of God. For Selmon in one way is the proper name of a certain mountain; in another way it is a common noun meaning darkness, and so it is taken here, and it can signify the grace of this life, which is dark in comparison with the grace of our heavenly country. Or it can be understood thus: The gentiles, who before their conversion to the faith, or to grace, were in darkness and shadows, [[67:15|shall be whited with snow|Nive dealbabuntur]].

paras.t: Et quoniam fideles taliter mundabuntur, idcirco mons Dei, id est Ecclesia militans : de qua in Isaia dicitur, Erit præparatus mons domus Domini in vertice montium. Dicitur enim Ecclesia mons propter altitudinem gratiæ Dei, sublimitatemque vitæ fidelium cœlestia contemplantium. Hic itaque mons Dei, est mons pinguis, id est spiritualibus bonis abundans, ex infusione donorum Spiritus Sancti. Est quoque hic, Mons coagulatus, id est per modum casei ex diversis personis compactus, videlicet ex simplicibus, pauperibus, et abjectis collectus ; mons pinguis : quoniam multas elegantes personas intra se habet, sicut sunt viri orthodoxi, id est gloriose fideles, alios verbo atque exemplo spiritualiter impinguantes. Quum ergo sit una Ecclesia, extra quam nullus salvatur, sicut nec extra arcam Noe aliquis salvabatur, ut quid suspicamini montes coagulatos ? id est, cur æstimatis esse separatas ecclesias, seu loca salutis extra catholicam apostolicamque Ecclesiam ?
paras.en: And since the faithful will be cleansed in this way, therefore [[67:16|The mountain of God|mons Dei]], that is, the Church militant, of which it is said in Isaias: [[Is 2:2|the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of mountains|Erit præparatus mons domus Domini in vertice montium]]. For the Church is called a mountain because of the height of the grace of God and the loftiness of the life of the faithful who contemplate heavenly things. This mountain of God, then, [[67:16|is a fat mountain|est mons pinguis]], that is, abounding in spiritual goods, from the pouring in of the gifts of the Holy Ghost. It is also [[67:16|A curdled mountain|Mons coagulatus]], that is, pressed together like cheese out of different persons, namely gathered from the simple, the poor and the despised; [[67:16|a fat mountain|mons pinguis]], since it has within itself many excellent persons, such as orthodox men, that is, gloriously faithful ones, who spiritually fatten others by word and example. Since, then, there is one Church, outside which no one is saved, as no one was saved outside the ark of Noe[[1 Pet 3:20||]], [[67:17|Why suspect, ye curdled mountains|ut quid suspicamini montes coagulatos]]? that is, why do you think that there are separate churches, or places of salvation, outside the Catholic and Apostolic Church?

paras.t: Quæ est Mons, in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo. Hic enim mons est congregatio electorum, de quibus increata Sapientia in Proverbiis ait : Deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum ; et in Apocalypsi, Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis. Etenim Dominus habitabit in finem : non ad horam, seu modicum temporis, sed usque ad finem sæculi, imo in sempiternum habitabit cum Ecclesia electorum, habitando in eis per fidem et gratiam, quemadmodum Christus promisit : Ecce, inquiens, ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi.
paras.en: For it is [[67:17|A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell|Mons, in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo]]. For this mountain is the gathering of the elect, of whom the uncreated Wisdom says in Proverbs: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum]]; and in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:3|Behold the tabernacle of God with men: and he will dwell with them|Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis]]. [[67:17|for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end|Etenim Dominus habitabit in finem]]: not for an hour, or a short time, but to the end of the world, nay, for ever he will dwell with the Church of the elect, dwelling in them through faith and grace, as Christ promised: [[Matt 28:20|behold|Ecce]], he says, [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]].

paras.t: Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex. Versus iste primo de angelis sanctis exponitur. Invitat enim Propheta angelos ad exhibendum Christo ascendenti consortium, quoniam ad magnificentiam regis pertinet comitantium multitudo, juxta illud : In multitudine populi, dignitas regis ; in paucitate vero plebis, ignominia principis. Præmittit autem Propheta ad suum propositum quoddam exemplum de multitudine angelorum adsistentium in datione legis Mosaicæ, secundum quod in Deuteronomio scribitur : Dominus de Sinai venit, et de Seir ortus est nobis ; apparuit de monte Pharan, et cum eo Sanctorum millia, haud dubium quin angelorum sanctorum. Ait ergo : Currus Dei, id est numerus angelorum Deum in se recipientium, deferentium, atque ad humanas mentes Dei notitiam circumducentium, decem millibus multiplex, id est, decem millia angelorum intra se comprehendit : non quod hic exprimatur certus numerus angelorum sanctorum ; sed ponitur finitum pro infinito, seu determinatum pro indeterminato. Nam per millenarium, qui est numerus perfectionis, decies repetitum, insinuatur inæstimabilis multitudo angelorum sanctorum. Quemadmodum enim Dionysius docet, multitudo angelorum sanctorum omnem materialem atque sensibilem multitudinem incomparabiliter excedit. Et juxta hunc sensum apud Danielem scriptum est : Millia millium ministrabant ei. Millia lætantium, id est, multitudo angelorum in Deo gaudentium, indeterminata millia continet, prout Daniel subdit : Decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei. Dominus in eis, id est, associatus fuit ipsis, in Sinai, in sancto, id est in monte Sinai, qui est mons sanctus et locus sacratus. Angelus namque qui Moysi loquebatur, habebat Deum sibi adsistentem ; omnesque angeli dationi legis adsistentes, Deum sibi præsidentem habebant, sicut Moyses ait : Omnes Sancti in manu ejus sunt.
paras.en: [[67:18|The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands|Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex]]. This verse is first explained of the holy angels. For the Prophet invites the angels to give their company to Christ as he ascends, since a multitude of attendants belongs to the magnificence of a king, according to that saying: [[Prov 14:28|In the multitude of people is the dignity of the king: and in the small number of the people the dishonour of the prince.|In multitudine populi, dignitas regis ; in paucitate vero plebis, ignominia principis]] Now the Prophet sets before his purpose an example of the multitude of angels who stood by at the giving of the law of Moses, according to what is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 33:2|The Lord came from Sinai, and from Seir he rose up to us: he hath appeared from mount Pharan, and with him thousands of saints|Dominus de Sinai venit, et de Seir ortus est nobis ; apparuit de monte Pharan, et cum eo Sanctorum millia]], doubtless of holy angels. So he says: [[67:18|The chariot of God|Currus Dei]], that is, the number of the angels who receive God into themselves, bear him, and carry the knowledge of God round to the minds of men, [[67:18|is attended by ten thousands|decem millibus multiplex]], that is, it comprises within itself ten thousand angels [Latin *decem millibus multiplex*, "manifold by ten thousands"]: not that a fixed number of holy angels is expressed here, but the finite is put for the infinite, or the determinate for the indeterminate. For by the thousand, which is the number of perfection, repeated ten times, an inestimable multitude of holy angels is suggested. For, as Dionysius teaches, the multitude of the holy angels beyond compare exceeds every material and sensible multitude. And in this sense it is written in Daniel: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him|Millia millium ministrabant ei]]. [[67:18|thousands of them that rejoice|Millia lætantium]], that is, the multitude of angels rejoicing in God contains thousands without number, as Daniel adds: [[Dan 7:10|ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him|Decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei]]. [[67:18|the Lord is among them|Dominus in eis]], that is, he kept company with them, [[67:18|in Sina, in the holy place|in Sinai, in sancto]], that is, on Mount Sinai, which is a holy mountain and a consecrated place. For the angel who spoke to Moses had God standing by him; and all the angels who stood by at the giving of the law had God presiding over them, as Moses says: [[Deut 33:3|all the saints are in his hand|Omnes Sancti in manu ejus sunt]].

paras.t: Ex his infert Propheta, quod major debuit esse multitudo angelorum associantium se Christo ascendenti, subjungens : Ascendisti, o Christe, in altum, id est in cœlum empyreum ; cepisti captivitatem, id est, in limbo detentos et captos, atque in purgatorio sufficienter mundatos eripuisti antequam ascendebas, eosque tecum ducebas ; accepisti dona in hominibus : id est, tu, Christe, prout homo es, accepisti a Deo Patre seu tota superfelicissima Trinitate, dona seu gratias conferendas hominibus. Hæc dona anima Christi accepit a primo suæ creationis instanti, quia Christus semper plenus fuit gratia et veritate, et de plenitudine ejus omnes accepimus. Erat enim in Christo non solum gratia personalis unionis, gratia quoque beatæ fruitionis, sed etiam gratia capitis, per quam ipse omnibus suis membris, seu toti Ecclesiæ influere potest, et omnes ditare, quemadmodum post resurrectionem dixit, Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra : non quod tunc primo sibi præstita fuit ista potestas, sed quia ex tunc cœpit innotescere omnia esse Christo subjecta. Sic nunc ait Propheta de Christo, Ascendisti in altum, accepisti dona in hominibus : non quod in ascensione primo accepit charismata gratiarum hominibus distribuenda, sed quia ex tunc evidentissime cœpit patere Christum omni beatitudine ac plenitudine Spiritus Sancti esse impletum. Unde in signum perfectæ glorificationis Christi, datus est Spiritus Sanctus post ascensionem in signo visibili. Propter quod apud Joannem scriptum est : Nondum erat Spiritus datus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus. Etenim non credentes inhabitare Dominum Deum : id est, tu, Christe, accepisti hoc donum, videlicet non credentes, id est infideles, inhabitare Dominum. Christo enim merito suæ passionis est datum, ut per eum infideles converterentur ad fidem, sicque in illis habitaret Deus, in quibus ante inhabitabat diabolus.
paras.en: From this the Prophet infers that the multitude of angels keeping company with Christ as he ascended must have been greater, adding: [[67:19|Thou hast ascended|Ascendisti]], O Christ, [[67:19|on high|in altum]], that is, into the empyrean heaven; [[67:19|thou hast led captivity captive|cepisti captivitatem]], that is, thou didst rescue those held captive in limbo, and those sufficiently cleansed in purgatory, before thou didst ascend, and didst lead them with thee; [[67:19|thou hast received gifts in men|accepisti dona in hominibus]]: that is, thou, O Christ, as thou art man, hast received from God the Father, or from the whole most supremely blessed Trinity, gifts or graces to be bestowed on men. These gifts the soul of Christ received from the first instant of its creation, since Christ was always [[John 1:14|full of grace and truth|plenus fuit gratia et veritate]], and [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|de plenitudine ejus omnes accepimus]]. For in Christ there was not only the grace of personal union, and also the grace of blessed fruition [that is, of the beatific vision and enjoyment of God], but also the grace of the head [that is, the grace by which Christ, as head of the Church, pours grace into his members], by which he can flow into all his members, or into the whole Church, and enrich them all; as he said after the resurrection: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]: not that this power was then first granted him, but that from then on it began to be known that all things are subject to Christ. So the Prophet now says of Christ: [[67:19|Thou hast ascended on high|Ascendisti in altum]], [[67:19|thou hast received gifts in men|accepisti dona in hominibus]]: not that at the ascension he first received the gifts of graces to be distributed to men, but that from then on it began to be most evidently plain that Christ was filled with all beatitude and the fulness of the Holy Ghost. Hence, in token of Christ's perfect glorification, the Holy Ghost was given after the ascension in a visible sign[[Acts 2:4||]] [the margin gives Act. ii, 1–4]. Wherefore it is written in John: [[John 7:39|as yet the Spirit was not given, because Jesus was not yet glorified|Nondum erat Spiritus datus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus]]. [[67:19|Yea for those also that do not believe, the dwelling of the Lord God|Etenim non credentes inhabitare Dominum Deum]]: that is, thou, O Christ, hast received this gift, namely that unbelievers, that is, infidels, should have the Lord dwelling in them [Denis reads *non credentes inhabitare Dominum* as "that the Lord should dwell in those who do not believe"]. For it was given to Christ by the merit of his passion that through him infidels should be converted to the faith, and so God should dwell in those in whom the devil dwelt before.

paras.t: Porro Apostolus scripturam istam allegans, sensum magis quam verba inducit. Ait enim : Propter quod dicit : Ascendens in altum, captivam duxit captivitatem, dedit dona hominibus. Solent namque Christus et Evangelistæ atque Apostoli in allegatione Scripturarum veteris Testamenti, magis sententiam quam verba commemorare. Nec mirum, quoniam mentem Prophetarum clarissime cognoverunt, et eam magis quam verba attenderunt.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle, in citing this scripture, brings in the sense rather than the words. For he says: [[Eph 4:8|Wherefore he saith: Ascending on high, he led captivity captive: he gave gifts to men.|Propter quod dicit : Ascendens in altum, captivam duxit captivitatem, dedit dona hominibus]] For Christ and the Evangelists and Apostles are wont, in citing the Scriptures of the Old Testament, to recall the meaning rather than the words. Nor is this surprising, since they knew most clearly the mind of the Prophets, and attended to it more than to the words.

paras.t: Constat ergo ex præinductis, quod hoc loco nomine currus seu curruum, intelliguntur deiferi angeli, qui et sedes Dei dicuntur. Et ita accipiuntur currus, ubi Dominus ait ad Synagogam seu viros Israelitas : Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, in Africam et Lydiam, in Italiam et Græciam ; et adducent omnes fratres vestros in equis et quadrigis, in lecticis et mulis. Hæc namque vehicula spiritualiter exponenda sunt, quia intelliguntur per ea sanctorum angelorum ministeria, quibus cooperabantur Apostolis in Judæorum ac gentium conversione.
paras.en: It is clear, then, from what has been brought forward, that in this place by the name of chariot, or chariots, are understood the God-bearing angels, who are also called the seats of God. And chariots are taken in this way where the Lord says to the Synagogue, or to the men of Israel: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint]], [[Is 66:19|into Africa, and Lydia|in Africam et Lydiam]], [[Is 66:19|into Italy, and Greece|in Italiam et Græciam]]; and [[Is 66:20|they shall bring all your brethren|adducent omnes fratres vestros]] [[Is 66:20|upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and on mules|in equis et quadrigis, in lecticis et mulis]]. For these carriages are to be explained spiritually, since by them are understood the ministries of the holy angels, by which they worked together with the Apostles in the conversion of Jews and gentiles.

paras.t: Secundo autem exponitur quod dictum est, Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex, de sanctis hominibus. Superius namque dixit, Mons in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo : et hunc montem nominat currum, quia fideles Deum intra se portant, sicut ait Apostolus, Glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro ; vel ideo, quoniam Deus eos dirigit, sicut auriga dirigit currum. Unde Eliseus vocat Eliam currum Israel et aurigam ejus. Nam sicut pastor gregem suum portat ac dirigit, sic Elias filios Israel portavit atque direxit. Simili quoque modo rex Israel Eliseo morituro dixit : Pater mi, currus Israel et auriga ejus. Itaque, Currus Dei, id est populus fidelis, decem millibus multiplex, id est ex innumerabilibus populis, linguis ac tribubus constans et congregatus : nam ex omni genere hominum collecta est Christi Ecclesia. Maxime vero per currum Dei, intelliguntur Apostoli et successores eorum, qui nomen Salvatoris per totum mundum vehebant, sicut de Paulo ait Salvator : Vas electionis est mihi iste, ut portet nomen meum coram regibus et gentibus et filiis Israel. Et hic currus est decem millibus multiplex, id est per innumerabilia credentium millia multiplicatus. Dicitur enim aliquis multiplicari, per multiplicationem eorum quos vel spiritualiter vel carnaliter generat. Unde Dominus ait ad Jacob : Augebo et multiplicabo te. Millia lætantium, id est, multa et innumerabilia sunt millia fidelium hominum, qui in præsenti sæculo gloriantur in Domino, ex contemplatione bonitatis beneficiorumque ejus, ex spe quoque futurorum bonorum, et de omni spirituali profectu proximorum. Dominus in eis. Nam per caritatem et gratiam demoratur in ipsis : et hoc, in Sinai, id est in mandato seu observatione mandati in Sinai præstiti. Sinai enim interpretatur mandatum. In sancto, quia mandatum sanctum est ; vel, In sancto, quoniam sanctitas est ratio propter quam Deus in nobis manet. In illis enim Deus est, manet et habitat, qui suis mandatis obediunt, prout asserit Christus : Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit ; et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus.
paras.en: Secondly, what was said, [[67:18|The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands|Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex]], is explained of holy men. For above he said: [[67:17|A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell|Mons in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo]]; and he calls this mountain a chariot because the faithful carry God within themselves, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 6:20|Glorify and bear God in your body|Glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro]]; or else because God guides them, as a charioteer guides a chariot. Hence Eliseus calls Elias the chariot of Israel and its driver[[4 Kings 2:12||]]. For as a shepherd carries and guides his flock, so Elias carried and guided the children of Israel. In like manner the king of Israel said to Eliseus when he was about to die: [[4 Kings 13:14|O my father|Pater mi]], [[4 Kings 13:14|the chariot of Israel, and the guider thereof|currus Israel et auriga ejus]]. So [[67:18|The chariot of God|Currus Dei]], that is, the faithful people, [[67:18|is attended by ten thousands|decem millibus multiplex]], that is, made up and gathered from innumerable peoples, tongues and tribes: for the Church of Christ is gathered from every kind of men. But above all, by the chariot of God are understood the Apostles and their successors, who carried the name of the Saviour through the whole world[[Ps 18:5||]], as the Saviour says of Paul: This man [[Acts 9:15|is to me a vessel of election|Vas electionis est mihi]], [[Acts 9:15|to carry my name|ut portet nomen meum]] before kings and Gentiles and the children of Israel. And this chariot [[67:18|is attended by ten thousands|est decem millibus multiplex]], that is, multiplied by innumerable thousands of believers. For a man is said to be multiplied through the multiplying of those whom he begets, either spiritually or in the flesh. Hence the Lord says to Jacob: [[Gen 48:4|I will cause thee to increase and multiply|Augebo et multiplicabo te]]. [[67:18|thousands of them that rejoice|Millia lætantium]], that is, many and innumerable are the thousands of faithful men who in this present world glory in the Lord, from contemplating his goodness and his benefits, from the hope too of the good things to come, and from every spiritual progress of their neighbours. [[67:18|the Lord is among them|Dominus in eis]]. For by charity and grace he abides in them; and this [[67:18|in Sina|in Sinai]], that is, in the commandment, or in the keeping of the commandment given on Sinai. For Sinai is interpreted *commandment*. [[67:18|in the holy place|In sancto]], because the commandment is holy; or, [[67:18|in the holy place|In sancto]], because holiness is the reason for which God abides in us [*in sancto* can mean both "in the holy place" and "in what is holy"]. For God is in those, abides and dwells in those, who obey his commandments, as Christ declares: [[John 14:23|If any one love me, he will keep my word. And my Father will love him and we will come to him and will make our abode with him|Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit ; et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus]].

paras.t: Ascendisti, Domine Jesu, in altum, quemadmodum de te in Actis dicitur : Videntibus illis, elevatus est, et nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum ; et alio in loco, Elevatis manibus, benedixit eis, et ferebatur in cœlum. Cepisti captivitatem, id est, totum mundum, quantum in te est, eruisti de manu diaboli, qui eum propter reatum peccati tenebat captivum ; sed a te ejectus est foras, qui ais : Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum.
paras.en: [[67:19|Thou hast ascended|Ascendisti]], Lord Jesus, [[67:19|on high|in altum]], as is said of thee in the Acts: [[Acts 1:9|while they looked on, he was raised up: and a cloud received him out of their sight|Videntibus illis, elevatus est, et nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum]]; and in another place [that is, in the Gospel of Luke]: [[Luke 24:50|lifting up his hands, he blessed them|Elevatis manibus, benedixit eis]], and he [[Luke 24:51|was carried up to heaven|ferebatur in cœlum]]. [[67:19|thou hast led captivity captive|Cepisti captivitatem]], that is, thou hast rescued the whole world, as far as lies in thee, from the hand of the devil, who held it captive because of the guilt of sin; but he has been cast out by thee, who sayest: [[John 12:32|I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]].

67.title: PROSECUTIO EXPLANATIONIS PSALMI PRÆSENTIS.
67.title_en: Continuation of the explanation of the present psalm.

paras.t: Benedictus Dominus die quotidie. Hic agit Propheta de profectu Ecclesiæ. Tanquam dicat : Laudatus sit Deus, et glorificetur ab omnibus de die in diem, propter prædicta beneficia nobis collata, et item propter beneficia conferenda. Nam prosperum iter faciet nobis : id est, beatam atque securam viam veniendi ad vitam æternam nobis ostendet, illuminando corda nostra, et dirigendo opera nostra in ultimum finem, quemadmodum ipse ait : Faciam ut in præceptis meis ambuletis, et judicia mea custodiatis et operemini. Non enim potest homo rectam viam incedere sine gratia duce. Propter quod Salomon ait : Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus. Unde Apostolus etiam deprecatur : Ipse Deus dirigat corda vestra et intelligentias vestras, ut integer spiritus vester servetur in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Itaque, Prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum, id est auctor et finis salvationum seu beatitudinum nostrarum. Octo sunt enim beatitudines, quas enumerat Christus apud Matthæum ; totque nobis salvationes largitur, a quantis peccatis atque periculis nos salvare dignatur : et omnis nostra salus ab ipso dependet. Ideo sequitur :
paras.en: [[67:20|Blessed be the Lord day by day|Benedictus Dominus die quotidie]]. Here the Prophet treats of the progress of the Church.
