paras.t: Obscurentur oculi eorum ne videant quanta eis æternæ mortis tormenta parata sint, et quantam felicitatem amittant.
paras.en: [[68:24|Let their eyes be darkened that they see not|Obscurentur oculi eorum ne videant]] how great are the torments of eternal death prepared for them, and how great a happiness they are losing.

paras.t: Effunde super eos iram tuam, derelinquendo eos in suo errore, sicut inferius de reprobis dicis : Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum. De quibus et Job ait : Non est virga Dei super eos ; ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad infernum descendunt. Et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos, damnando eos finaliter, irreparabiliter et æternaliter, quemadmodum alibi legitur : Ulciscens Dominus et habens furorem, ulciscens in hostes suos.
paras.en: [[68:25|Pour out thy indignation upon them|Effunde super eos iram tuam]], by abandoning them in their error, as thou sayest of the reprobate further on: [[Ps 80:13|I let them go according to the desires of their heart|Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum]] [that is, later in the Psalter]. Of whom Job too says: [[Job 21:9|the rod of God is not upon them|Non est virga Dei super eos]]; [[Job 21:13|They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to hell|ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad infernum descendunt]]. [[68:25|and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them|Et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos]], by condemning them finally, irreparably and eternally, as we read elsewhere: [[Nah 1:2|the Lord is a revenger, and hath wrath|Ulciscens Dominus et habens furorem]], [[Nah 1:2|the Lord taketh vengeance on his adversaries|ulciscens in hostes suos]].

paras.t: Fiat habitatio eorum deserta. Civitates et domus infidelium, sæpe a fidelibus destructæ, possessæ et inhabitatæ leguntur : et tunc tabernacula infidelium, proprio inhabitante carebant. Spiritualiter autem habitatio impiorum fit deserta, dum corpora eorum ab animabus ante tempus separantur, ita quod propter sua peccata occiduntur, aut celerius moriuntur ; vel dum animæ eorum, quæ esse deberent sedes sapientiæ, reclinatorium Dei, et domus Christi, a gratia relinquuntur, nec a Deo per fidem formatam inhabitantur : sicut per Ezechielem Dominus ait de peccatrice, Recessit anima mea ab ea ; et de impiis in Osee, Væ eis, quum recessero ab eis.
paras.en: [[68:26|Let their habitation be made desolate|Fiat habitatio eorum deserta]]. We read that the cities and houses of unbelievers were often destroyed, possessed and inhabited by the faithful: and then the tabernacles of the unbelievers lacked their own inhabitant. But spiritually the habitation of the wicked is made desolate when their bodies are separated from their souls before their time, so that for their sins they are slain or die the sooner; or when their souls, which ought to be the seat of wisdom, the resting-place of God and the house of Christ, are forsaken by grace and are not inhabited by God through formed faith [that is, faith informed by charity]: as the Lord says by Ezechiel of the sinful woman, [[Ezech 23:18|my soul was alienated from her|Recessit anima mea ab ea]]; and of the wicked in Osee, [[Osee 9:12|woe to them, when I shall depart from them|Væ eis, quum recessero ab eis]].

paras.t: Quoniam quem tu percussisti permissive, persecuti sunt malitiose, atrociter, et mala intentione. Permittit enim Deus electos ab impiis tribulari, quatenus expurgentur. Impii vero non ideo tribulant eos, ut purgentur, sed invidiose eos affligunt. Idcirco, quemadmodum pater virga corrigit filium, quo correcto, projicit virgam in ignem ; sic Deus per reprobos corrigit electos, quibus emendatis atque salvatis, projicit reprobos in ignem æternum. Et super dolorem vulnerum meorum addiderunt mihi dolorem verborum malorum, irrisiones, maledictiones, blasphemias.
paras.en: [[68:27|Because|Quoniam]] him [[68:27|whom thou hast smitten|quem tu percussisti]] by thy permission [[68:27|they have persecuted|persecuti sunt]] maliciously, cruelly and with evil intent. For God permits the elect to be troubled by the wicked, that they may be purged. But the wicked do not trouble them for this, that they may be purged, but afflict them out of envy. Therefore, as a father corrects his son with the rod, and, when he is corrected, throws the rod into the fire; so God corrects the elect through the reprobate, and, when they are amended and saved, throws the reprobate into the eternal fire. [[68:27|and they have added to the grief of my wounds|Et super dolorem vulnerum meorum addiderunt]] the grief of evil words, mockeries, curses, blasphemies.

paras.t: Deleantur de libro viventium, id est a consortio Beatorum : ad quorum numerum se pertinere existimant etiam infideles et pessimi, quamvis ignorent in quo vera beatitudo consistat.
paras.en: [[68:29|Let them be blotted out of the book of the living|Deleantur de libro viventium]], that is, from the fellowship of the Blessed: to whose number even unbelievers and the very wicked think they belong, though they do not know in what true beatitude consists.

paras.t: Ego sum pauper, præsertim in bonis gratiæ, in donis Spiritus Sancti, in spiritualibus atque internis divitiis ; et convenit mihi quod in Apocalypsi habetur : Tu es miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus. Sum quoque et dolens, propter peccata commissa, et mundi errores, ac tuas injurias. Idcirco salus tua, Deus, suscepit me, id est, gratia tua salvifica mihi infusa est, et tu ipse, qui es vera salus omnium electorum, me misericorditer suscepisti : propterea gratias referam Deo, et laudabo nomen Dei cum cantico psalmodiæ, divinorum hymnorum, devotionisque fervidæ, quia non clamor, sed amor insonat auribus Omnipotentis. Cetera patent ex præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: [[68:30|But I am poor|Ego sum pauper]], above all in the goods of grace, in the gifts of the Holy Ghost, in spiritual and inward riches; and that which is said in the Apocalypse fits me: [[Apoc 3:17|thou art wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|Tu es miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus]]. I am also [[68:30|sorrowful|dolens]], for the sins I have committed, and the errors of the world, and the wrongs done to thee. Therefore [[68:30|thy salvation, O God, hath set me up|salus tua, Deus, suscepit me]] [Latin *suscepit*, "has taken me up", which the next words take as "received"], that is, thy saving grace has been poured into me, and thou thyself, who art the true salvation of all the elect, hast mercifully received me: and so I will give thanks to God, and [[68:31|I will praise the name of God with a canticle|laudabo nomen Dei cum cantico]] of psalmody, of divine hymns and of fervent devotion, for it is not clamour but love that sounds in the ears of the Almighty. The rest is plain from the preceding article.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum præclarum et sanctum audivimus, de Christi passione, Judæorum excæcatione, et ædificatione Ecclesiæ diffuse ac lucide pertractantem. Discamus igitur exemplo Christi, in omni persecutione esse patientes, in omni tentatione constantes, in omni adversitate robusti. Continentur quoque in psalmo præsenti devotissimæ et ardentissimæ orationes, mirabili dulcedine redundantes. Quid enim tam amorosum atque suave, sicut tres versus illi, Exaudi me, Domine, quoniam benigna est misericordia tua, etc. ? Cum multa itaque mentis custodia, munditia et fervore ingenti, canamus semper hunc psalmum.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a glorious and holy psalm, treating fully and clearly of the passion of Christ, the blinding of the Jews, and the building up of the Church. Let us learn therefore by the example of Christ to be patient in every persecution, constant in every temptation, strong in every adversity. There are contained too in the present psalm most devout and most ardent prayers, overflowing with wonderful sweetness. For what is so loving and sweet as those three verses, [[68:17|Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind|Exaudi me, Domine, quoniam benigna est misericordia tua]], etc.? With great watchfulness of mind, then, with purity and with great fervour, let us always sing this psalm.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus, cui est omnis cogitatio manifesta, et a quo delicta nostra non sunt abscondita, respice nos in multitudine misericordiæ tuæ, et maculas te offendentes a nobis absterge ; intende animæ nostræ, et libera eam ab improperio et ab æterna confusione.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, to whom every thought is manifest, and from whom our offences are not hidden, look upon us in the multitude of thy mercy, and wipe away from us the stains that offend thee; attend to our soul, and deliver it from reproach and from everlasting confusion.

69.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI NONI : DEUS, IN ADJUTORIUM, ETC. ; ET DE ADMIRABILI VIRTUTE PRIMI VERSUS PSALMI PRÆSENTIS.
69.title_en: Elucidation of the sixty-ninth psalm: O God, come to my assistance, etc.; and of the wonderful power of the first verse of the present psalm.

paras.t: Habet autem hic psalmus titulum istum : In finem, psalmus David, in rememoratione quod salvum fecit eum Dominus : id est, psalmus iste a David conscriptus, et in finem, qui est Christus, nos dirigens : psalmus, inquam, sancti David, hic in persona hominis justi loquentis, in rememoratione, id est de memoria, quod salvum fecit eum Dominus. Et ita David fecit hunc psalmum ad recolendum beneficia sibi divinitus præstita. Nicolaus de Lyra dicit hunc psalmum in Hebræo taliter intitulatum : Ad victoriam David, ad recordandum ; in translatione quoque Hieronymi juxta Hebræum, sic : Victori, ad recordandum. Quod autem adjungitur, Quod salvum fecit eum Dominus, asserit ab aliquo expositore adjunctum. Propterea ait hic esse prophetiam de futuro, ita ut prævidit in Spiritu Sancto, principium hujus psalmi esse recordandum in omni canonicarum horarum initio, vel juxta initium, sicut jam fit in Ecclesia.
paras.en: Now this psalm has this title: [[69:1|Unto the end|In finem]], [[69:1|a psalm for David|psalmus David]], [[69:1|to bring to remembrance|in rememoratione]] [[69:1|that the Lord saved him|quod salvum fecit eum Dominus]]: that is, this psalm, written by David and directing us [[69:1|unto the end|in finem]], which is Christ; a psalm, I say, of holy David, who speaks here in the person of a just man, [[69:1|to bring to remembrance|in rememoratione]], that is, as a memorial, [[69:1|that the Lord saved him|quod salvum fecit eum Dominus]]. And so David made this psalm to call to mind the benefits granted him by God. Nicholas of Lyra says that in the Hebrew this psalm is entitled thus: For the victory, of David, to bring to remembrance; and in Jerome's translation from the Hebrew thus: To the victor, to bring to remembrance. As for what is added, [[69:1|that the Lord saved him|Quod salvum fecit eum Dominus]], he asserts that it was added by some expositor. Therefore he says that there is here a prophecy of the future, inasmuch as [David] foresaw in the Holy Ghost that the beginning of this psalm was to be recalled at the beginning, or near the beginning, of every one of the canonical hours, as is now done in the Church.

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta in persona viri justi tribulati atque tentati, ait : Deus, in adjutorium meum intende, id est, ad hoc respice in me, ut adjutorium mihi impendas. Intende in adjutorium meum, non in derelictionem, excæcationem, damnationemque meam. Cogita super me cogitationes pacis, non afflictionis, quemadmodum de quibusdam dicis : Ecce ego cogito super familiam istam malum, unde non auferetis colla vestra. Sed quia, o Domine, indesinenter tua ope indigeo, tua conservatione subsisto, idcirco, Domine, ad adjuvandum me festina. Tu enim dixisti : Sine me nihil potestis facere; et per Paulum, Non sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of a just man in tribulation and temptation, the Prophet says: [[69:2|O God, come to my assistance|Deus, in adjutorium meum intende]]; that is, look upon me to this end, that thou mayest bestow thy help upon me. [[69:2|Come to my assistance|Intende in adjutorium meum]], not to my forsaking, my blinding and my damnation. Think over me [[Jer 29:11|thoughts of peace, and not of affliction|cogitationes pacis, non afflictionis]], such as thou speakest of concerning some: [[Mich 2:3|Behold I devise an evil against this family: from which you shall not withdraw your necks|Ecce ego cogito super familiam istam malum, unde non auferetis colla vestra]]. But since, O Lord, I unceasingly need thy aid and subsist by thy keeping, therefore, [[69:2|O Lord, make haste to help me|Domine, ad adjuvandum me festina]]. For thou hast said: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]; and by Paul: [[2 Cor 3:5|Not that we are sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God.|Non sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]

paras.t: Confundantur et revereantur, qui quærunt animam meam, etc. Versus iste, cum duobus sequentibus, exponi potest dupliciter : in bono, et in malo. Primo igitur exponendi sunt versus isti in bono, eritque sensus : Confundantur de suis peccatis, et ex confusione pœniteant, et revereantur, id est, Deum honorent, Deumque judicem expavescant, qui quærunt animam meam, id est hostes mei, qui quærunt vitam meam corporalem lædere sive exstinguere, aut spiritum meum inficere atque subvertere. Est autem duplex confusio, quemadmodum ait Scriptura : Est confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gratiam et gloriam. Confusio adducens peccatum, est verecundari de bono. Unde scriptum est : Non confundaris confiteri peccata tua. Confusio autem adducens gratiam in præsenti, gloriamque in futuro, est verecundari de malo culpæ, sicut de quibusdam ait Apostolus : Quem fructum habuistis tunc in illis, in quibus nunc erubescitis?
paras.en: [[69:3|Let them be confounded and ashamed that seek my soul|Confundantur et revereantur, qui quærunt animam meam]], etc. This verse, with the two that follow, may be expounded in two ways: in a good sense and in a bad. First, then, these verses are to be expounded in the good sense, and the meaning will be: [[69:3|Let them be confounded|Confundantur]] for their sins, and out of their confusion repent; [[69:3|and ashamed|et revereantur]] [Latin revereantur, literally 'let them revere'; Denis takes it here of reverence, and below of shame], that is, let them honour God and stand in dread of God as their judge; [[69:3|that seek my soul|qui quærunt animam meam]], that is, my enemies, who seek to hurt or destroy my bodily life, or to infect and overthrow my spirit. Now shame [Latin confusio, the word behind 'confounded'] is twofold, as the Scripture says: [[Ecclus 4:25|For there is a shame that bringeth sin, and there is a shame that bringeth glory and grace.|Est confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gratiam et gloriam]] The shame that bringeth sin is to be ashamed of what is good. Whence it is written: [[Ecclus 4:31|Be not ashamed to confess thy sins|Non confundaris confiteri peccata tua]]. But the shame that bringeth grace in the present and glory in the future is to be ashamed of the evil of guilt, as the Apostle says of some: [[Rom 6:21|What fruit therefore had you then in those things of which you are now ashamed?|Quem fructum habuistis tunc in illis, in quibus nunc erubescitis?]]

paras.t: Avertantur retrorsum, id est, a malo opere cessent, a proposito pravo desistant, neque in malo procedant et crescant, et erubescant, quod tam inhoneste ac vitiose egerunt aut agere optaverunt; qui volunt mihi mala pœnæ vel culpæ : quod ad invidiam pertinet. Et ita vir justus pro adversariis suis intime deprecatur. Avertantur statim a suo errore, erubescentes de propria iniquitate, quoniam periculosum est eis perseverare in culpa; qui dicunt mihi, Euge, euge, gaudendo de mea miseria, vel de mea prosperitate se gaudere dicentes, non vere, sed adulatorie aut irrisorie. Habet autem homo duplices hostes, invisibiles atque visibiles. Si ergo de invisibilibus hostibus nunc loquamur, tunc ista nullo modo exponenda erunt in bono, præsertim quum hostes hujusmodi sint incorrigibiles et obstinati.
paras.en: [[69:4|Let them be turned backward|Avertantur retrorsum]], that is, let them cease from evil work, desist from their wicked purpose, and not go forward and grow in evil; [[69:4|and blush for shame|et erubescant]] that they have acted, or wished to act, so shamefully and viciously; [[69:4|that desire evils to me|qui volunt mihi mala]], evils of punishment or of guilt, which belongs to envy. And so the just man prays from his heart for his adversaries. [[69:4|Let them be presently turned away|Avertantur statim]] from their error, [[69:4|blushing for shame|erubescentes]] at their own iniquity, since it is dangerous for them to persevere in guilt; [[69:4|that say to me: 'Tis well, 'tis well|qui dicunt mihi, Euge, euge]], rejoicing at my misery, or saying that they rejoice at my prosperity, not truly but in flattery or in mockery. Now man has two kinds of enemies, invisible and visible. If, then, we are speaking now of invisible enemies, these words are by no means to be expounded in the good sense, especially as enemies of that kind are incorrigible and obstinate.

paras.t: Secundo exponuntur in malo, hoc modo : Confundantur iniqui, confusione reprobationis divinæ ac damnationis æternæ, et revereantur, id est, verecundentur in conspectu justi judicii Dei, de peccatis propriæ voluntatis, quemadmodum in Osee scribitur : Confundetur Israel in voluntate sua. Solet enim interdum, Revereri, accipi pro Verecundari, sicut et irreverens dicitur inverecundus, juxta illud : Animæ irreverenti ne tradas me. Qui quærunt animam meam seducere, vel vitam meam destruere. Avertantur retrorsum, id est, a summo bono avertantur, et caducis ac vanis rebus inhæreant : sicut de eis Dominus per Jeremiam ait, Verterunt ad me dorsum, et non faciem ; et alibi, Aversus est populus iste aversione contentiosa. Et erubescant erubescentia damnationis, non confessionis, qui volunt mihi mala, sive suam voluntatem perducant ad actum, sive non. Avertantur statim erubescentes, etc., id est, protinus gratia tua priventur, et nomen tuum confiteri, suaque vitia propalare erubescant. Unde Moyses loquitur : Dominus Deus tuus, ipse est Deus fortis et fidelis, reddens odientibus se statim, ita ut disperdat eos, et ultra non differat, protinus eis restituens quod merentur. In præsenti etenim sæculo statim subtrahit eis gratiam atque protectionem, permittens eos cadere de malo in malum : quod est maxima ultio.
paras.en: Secondly, they are expounded in the bad sense, in this way: [[69:3|Let them be confounded|Confundantur]], the wicked, with the confusion of divine reprobation and eternal damnation; [[69:3|and ashamed|et revereantur]], that is, let them be put to shame in the sight of God's just judgement for the sins of their own will, as is written in Osee: [[Osee 10:6|Israel shall be confounded in his own will|Confundetur Israel in voluntate sua]]. For *revereri* [to revere] is sometimes taken for *verecundari* [to be ashamed], just as one who is *irreverens* [irreverent] is called shameless, according to that saying: [[Ecclus 23:6|give me not over to a shameless and foolish mind|Animæ irreverenti ne tradas me]]. [[69:3|That seek my soul|Qui quærunt animam meam]] to lead it astray, or to destroy my life. [[69:4|Let them be turned backward|Avertantur retrorsum]], that is, let them be turned away from the highest good and cleave to perishable and vain things: as the Lord says of them by Jeremias: [[Jer 2:27|they have turned their back to me, and not their face|Verterunt ad me dorsum, et non faciem]]; and elsewhere: [[Jer 8:5|this people|Aversus est populus iste]] is [[Jer 8:5|turned away with a stubborn revolting|aversione contentiosa]] [in Jeremias the words are a question: Why then is this people turned away …?]. [[69:4|And blush for shame|Et erubescant]] with the blush of damnation, not of confession, [[69:4|that desire evils to me|qui volunt mihi mala]], whether they carry their will into act or not. [[69:4|Let them be presently turned away blushing for shame|Avertantur statim erubescentes]], etc., that is, let them be forthwith deprived of thy grace, and be ashamed to confess thy name and to lay bare their vices. Whence Moses says: [[Deut 7:9|the Lord thy God, he is a strong and faithful God|Dominus Deus tuus, ipse est Deus fortis et fidelis]], [[Deut 7:10|repaying forthwith them that hate him, so as to destroy them, without further delay immediately rendering to them what they deserve|reddens odientibus se statim, ita ut disperdat eos, et ultra non differat, protinus eis restituens quod merentur]]. For in this present world he forthwith withdraws from them his grace and protection, letting them fall from evil into evil: which is the greatest vengeance.

paras.t: Exsultent, id est, signa lætitiæ foris ostendant, et ex interiori hilaritate quasi extra se saltent, et lætentur interiori gaudio, in te, non in vanitatibus mundi, omnes qui quærunt te fide et opere, aut faciendo quod in se est, ut gratiam tuam, contemplationem ac dilectionem bonitatis tuæ acquirant, conservent, possideant. Et dicant : Semper magnificetur Dominus, id est, ab omnibus honoretur ac benedicatur, magnusque esse cognoscatur, qui diligunt salutare tuum, id est salutem gratiæ in præsenti, et beatitudinem gloriæ in futuro ; vel, Salutare tuum, Christum omnium salvatorem.
paras.en: Let them [[69:5|rejoice|Exsultent]] [Latin exsultent, properly 'let them leap for joy'], that is, let them show signs of gladness outwardly, and out of inward cheerfulness leap as it were beside themselves; [[69:5|and be glad|et lætentur]] with inward joy, [[69:5|in thee|in te]], not in the vanities of the world, [[69:5|all that seek thee|omnes qui quærunt te]] by faith and works, or by doing what lies in them [the scholastic 'doing what is in oneself', that is, doing what one can with the help already given], so as to acquire, keep and possess thy grace, and the contemplation and love of thy goodness. And let them [[69:5|say always: The Lord be magnified|dicant : Semper magnificetur Dominus]], that is, let him be honoured and blessed by all, and known to be great; [[69:5|such as love thy salvation|qui diligunt salutare tuum]], that is, the salvation of grace in the present and the bliss of glory in the future; or, [[69:5|thy salvation|Salutare tuum]], that is, Christ the Saviour of all.

paras.t: Ego vero egenus et pauper sum. Egeni sumus, propter imperfectionem naturalem animæ nostræ ac virium ejus. Anima enim rationalis, est infima in ordine intellectualium substantiarum; et intellectus possibilis in principio sui, est tanquam tabula omni carens pictura. Voluntas quoque naturaliter ad malum proclivis est, et memoria labilis. Pauperes vero sumus, propter gratiæ imperfectionem. Nam omnes nostræ justitiæ sunt velut pannus menstruatæ ; et hoc ipsum quod boni in nobis est, aliunde recepimus, nec aliquid ex propriis viribus prævalemus. Propter quod quotidie mendicamus panem a Patre cœlesti, dicentes : Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie. Et ipse David alio loco : Ego, inquit, sum vir pauper et tenuis. Quum ergo sim adeo egenus et pauper, o Deus, adjuva me per gratiæ infusionem, per Christi passionem, per angeli sancti custodiam, per intercessionem Sanctorum, per consilium atque auxilium proximorum et prælatorum meorum. Adjutor meus, in faciendo bono, et liberator meus, in declinando a malo, es tu, et alius nullus, nisi in tua virtute hoc faciat. Deus meus, quem singulariter amo et colo, ne tardaveris preces has implere.
paras.en: [[69:6|But I am needy and poor|Ego vero egenus et pauper sum]]. We are needy because of the natural imperfection of our soul and of its powers. For the rational soul is the lowest in the order of intellectual substances; and the possible intellect [that is, the intellect as able to receive knowledge, which of itself holds none] is at its beginning like a tablet bare of any picture. The will, too, is by nature prone to evil, and the memory apt to slip. And we are poor because of the imperfection of grace. For [[Is 64:6|all our justices|omnes nostræ justitiæ]] are [[Is 64:6|as the rag of a menstruous woman|velut pannus menstruatæ]]; and this very good that is in us we have received from elsewhere, nor can we do anything by our own strength. For this reason we daily beg bread of the heavenly Father, saying: [[Luke 11:3|Give us this day our daily bread|Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie]]. And David himself in another place: [[1 Kings 18:23|I|Ego]], he says, [[1 Kings 18:23|am a poor man, and of small ability|sum vir pauper et tenuis]]. Since, then, I am so needy and poor, [[69:6|O God, help me|o Deus, adjuva me]] by the infusion of grace, by the passion of Christ, by the guardianship of a holy angel, by the intercession of the saints, by the counsel and aid of my neighbours and my prelates. [[69:6|Thou art|es tu]] [[69:6|my helper|Adjutor meus]] in doing good, [[69:6|and my deliverer|et liberator meus]] in turning aside from evil, thou and no other, unless he do it in thy power. My God, whom I singularly love and worship, [[69:6|make no delay|ne tardaveris]] to fulfil these prayers [the Vulgate reads Domine, ne moreris, 'O Lord, make no delay', and the edition prints moreris in the margin; Denis's Deus meus, ne tardaveris is the wording of Ps 39:18].

paras.t: Denique psalmus iste de Christo exponi potest. Nam ipse, ut homo, frequenter petivit adjutorium Dei, ut a morte suscitaretur, in corpore glorificaretur, et per totum orbem clarificaretur. Sed expositio ista ex sæpe inductis atque dicendis clarissime patet. Nam et psalmus iste pro magna parte in psalmo sequenti continetur ; totus vero continetur in psalmo tricesimo nono, cujus exordium est, Exspectans exspectavi Dominum, ab illo loco quo dicitur, Complaceat tibi, Domine, ut eruas me.
paras.en: Lastly, this psalm can be expounded of Christ. For he, as man, often asked the help of God, that he might be raised from death, glorified in his body, and made known in glory throughout the whole world. But this exposition is very clear from what has often been brought forward and is still to be said. For this psalm is also contained for the most part in the following psalm, and the whole of it is contained in the thirty-ninth psalm, which begins [[Ps 39:2|With expectation I have waited for the Lord|Exspectans exspectavi Dominum]], from the place where it says [[Ps 39:14|Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me|Complaceat tibi, Domine, ut eruas me]].

paras.t: Sive autem de Christo, sive de ejus membris exponatur hoc quod dicitur, Confundantur et revereantur, etc., cum duobus sequentibus versibus, quando in malo exponitur, tripliciter intelligi potest : primo, per modum prænuntiationis, non imprecationis, ad designandum quid impiis sit futurum, nisi pœniteant ; secundo, per modum declarationis, ostendentis quid mereantur maligni ; tertio, per modum orationis, qua se homo conformat divinæ justitiæ, cupiens impios justas luere pœnas, vel in præsenti, ne æternaliter pereant, vel in futuro, nisi jam convertantur et Deo ministrent. Si autem intelligantur hi versus de invisibilibus hostibus, tunc simpliciter et absolute accipiuntur in malo.
paras.en: But whether what is said, [[69:3|Let them be confounded and ashamed|Confundantur et revereantur]], etc., with the two following verses, be expounded of Christ or of his members, when it is expounded in the bad sense it can be understood in three ways: first, by way of foretelling, not of cursing, to signify what will befall the wicked unless they repent; secondly, by way of declaration, showing what the wicked deserve; thirdly, by way of prayer, by which a man conforms himself to the divine justice, desiring that the wicked pay just penalties, either in the present, lest they perish eternally, or in the future, unless they are now converted and serve God. But if these verses are understood of invisible enemies, then they are taken simply and absolutely in the bad sense.

paras.t: Magna proinde et admiranda est virtus primi versus psalmi præsentis : propter quod merito mater Ecclesia a Spiritu Sancto instructa, instituit in singularum Horarum principio, vel circa principium, dici hunc versum, quatenus divinæ subventionis clypeo præmuniti, universas evadamus inimici insidias, qui utique tunc nobis fortius insidiatur, nequiusque obsistit, dum divina inchoare curamus.
paras.en: Great, therefore, and wonderful is the power of the first verse of the present psalm. For this reason Mother Church, taught by the Holy Ghost, has rightly ordained that this verse be said at the beginning of each of the Hours, or about the beginning, so that, fortified beforehand by the shield of divine succour, we may escape all the snares of the enemy, who lies in wait for us more strongly and resists us more wickedly at the very time when we set about beginning divine things.

paras.t: Laudem præterea hujus versiculi, illustrissimus pater noster Cassianus libro primo Collationum, pulchre prosequitur, describens ea quæ ex ore sancti anachoretæ abbatis Isaac didicit. Ad perpetuam, inquit, Dei memoriam possidendam, hic versus inseparabiliter proponendus est menti : recipit enim omnes affectus qui inferri possunt humanæ naturæ, et ad omnem statum atque universos incursus proprie et convenienter aptatur. Habet siquidem adversus discrimina invocationem Dei, habet humilitatem piæ confessionis, habet sollicitudinis perpetuique timoris vigilantiam, habet considerationem fragilitatis suæ, exauditionis fiduciam, confidentiam præsentis semperque adstantis præsidii : qui enim jugiter suum invocat protectorem, certus est eum semper esse præsentem. Habet amoris et caritatis ardorem, habet insidiarum contemplationem, inimicorumque formidinem, quibus perspiciens se die noctuque vallatum, confitetur se non posse sine sui defensoris auxilio liberari. Hic versiculus omnibus infestatione dæmonum laborantibus inexpugnabilis murus est, et impenetrabilis lorica ac munitissimus clypeus. Hic versus in acedia et anxietate animi collocatos, seu tristitia vel cogitationibus quibuscumque depressos, salutis remedia desperare non patitur, ostendens illum quem invocant, inspicere jugiter nostra certamina, nec eum suis deesse supplicibus. Admonet nos versus iste, in prosperis successibus spiritualibusque profectibus non extolli, sed sicut in duris ac tristibus, ita in lætis ac prosperis nos semper divino indigere auxilio, quatenus ab illis eruamur, et in istis stabiliter immoremur. Porro quocumque peccato pulsemur, quacumque passione tentemur, quacumque adversitate, evagatione, ariditate, tædioque molestemur, semper nobis clamandum est : Deus, in adjutorium meum intende, etc.
paras.en: Moreover, our most illustrious father Cassian, in the first book of the Conferences [the passage is Conference X, ch. 10, the last conference of the first part], beautifully sets out the praise of this little verse, describing what he learned from the mouth of the holy anchorite Abbot Isaac. “To possess the continual remembrance of God,” he says, “this verse must be set before the mind without ceasing: for it takes in all the affections that can befall human nature, and fits properly and aptly every state and all assaults. For it contains an invocation of God against dangers; it contains the humility of a devout confession; it contains the watchfulness of anxiety and of continual fear; it contains the consideration of one's own frailty, assurance of being heard, and confidence in a protection present and always at hand: for he who continually calls upon his protector is sure that he is always present. It contains the ardour of love and charity; it contains a sight of the snares and a dread of the enemies by whom a man sees himself beset day and night, and so confesses that he cannot be delivered without the help of his defender. This little verse is an impregnable wall, an impenetrable breastplate and a most strong shield for all who labour under the attacks of the demons. This verse does not suffer those who are sunk in acedia [that is, spiritual sloth and weariness] and anxiety of mind, or weighed down by sadness or by any thoughts whatever, to despair of the remedies of salvation, for it shows that he whom they call upon continually beholds our struggles and does not fail his suppliants. This verse warns us not to be lifted up in prosperous successes and spiritual progress, but that, as in hard and sad things, so in glad and prosperous ones, we always need the divine help, that from the former we may be delivered and in the latter we may abide steadfastly. And so, by whatever sin we are struck, by whatever passion we are tempted, by whatever adversity, wandering of mind, dryness and weariness we are troubled, we must always cry out: [[69:2|O God, come to my assistance|Deus, in adjutorium meum intende]], etc.

paras.t: Hujus ergo versiculi meditatio, in tuo pectore indirupta volvatur. Hunc in omni opere, ministerio atque itinere decantare non desinas. Hunc, dormiens et reficiens, et in ultimis naturæ necessitatibus meditare. Hæc enim meditatio, non solum ab omni dæmonum incursione te illæsum custodiet, sed a cunctis quoque vitiis terrenæ te contagionis expurgans, ad illas invisibiles ac cœlestes theorias perducet, atque ad illum ineffabilem ac perpaucis expertum, provehet orationis ardorem. Hunc versiculum meditando obdormi, donec incessabili exercitatione formatus, etiam per soporem eum decantare consuescas. Hic tibi expergefacto primus occurrat, universas quoque cogitationes inanes anticipet, teque omni tempore prosequatur.
paras.en: “Let the meditation of this little verse, then, turn without a break in your breast. Do not cease to sing it in every work, service and journey. Meditate on it when sleeping and when eating, and in the lowest necessities of nature. For this meditation will not only keep you unharmed from every assault of the demons, but, cleansing you also from all the vices of earthly contagion, will lead you to those invisible and heavenly contemplations [Latin theorias, from the Greek theoria, 'contemplation'], and carry you on to that ardour of prayer which is unspeakable and known by experience to very few. Fall asleep meditating this little verse, until, formed by unceasing practice, you grow used to singing it even in your sleep. When you wake, let it be the first thing to come to you; let it forestall all idle thoughts, and go with you at all times.”

paras.t: Precatio. Deus auctor salutis humanæ, contra quærentes animam nostram in adjutorium nostrum intende : ut eorum per te infestatione a nobis cessante, te adjutorem et protectorem nostrum magnificemus sine fine.
paras.en: Prayer. [[69:2|O God|Deus]], author of man's salvation, against those [[69:3|that seek|quærentes]] our soul [[69:2|come to|intende]] our [[69:2|assistance|in adjutorium]]: that, their harassing of us ceasing through thee, we may magnify thee, our [[69:6|helper|adjutorem]] and protector, without end.

70.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI : IN TE, DOMINE, SPERAVI, ETC.
70.title_en: Declaration of the seventieth psalm: In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, etc.

paras.t: Præsentis psalmi titulus est : Psalmus David, filiorum Jonadab, et primorum captivorum. Jeremias narrat, quomodo Jonadab filiis suis præcepit non bibere vinum, neque in domibus residere, sed in tabernaculis habitare. Cui filii fideliter obedierunt : propter quod Dominus improperat filiis Israel, quod verba Jonadab prævaluerunt verbis suis, quibus filii Israel obedire neglexerunt. Psalmus vero jam declarandus, non agit de ista historia, sed de re significata per eam, videlicet de his qui divinæ voluntati sponte obediunt: qui fuerunt primi captivi, id est, antequam ad Deum conversi sunt, subditi erant servituti peccati et jugo diaboli, quemadmodum ait Apostolus : Nos aliquando conversati sumus in desideriis carnis nostræ, et eramus natura filii iræ, sicut et ceteri. Quamdiu enim portamus imaginem prævaricationis Adæ, captivi ducimur in legem peccati ; dum vero imaginem Christi portare incipimus, imitando vestigia ejus, liberamur a misera captivitate culpæ atque diaboli, efficimurque filii gratiæ, et in Domino liberi. Hinc enim dicit Apostolus : Primus homo de terra, terrenus ; secundus homo de cœlo, cœlestis. Qualis terrenus, tales et terreni ; et qualis cœlestis, tales et cœlestes. Igitur, sicut portavimus imaginem terreni, portemus et imaginem cœlestis. Sensus itaque tituli est : Psalmus iste, qui est David prophetæ, sicut auctoris, editus est ad instructionem filiorum Jonadab, id est filiorum obedientiæ, sponte servientium Deo, primorum captivorum, id est filiorum qui erant captivi, secundum modum jam dictum, antequam Domino obedirent, cui servire, est vere regnare.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is: [[70:1|A psalm for David. Of the sons of Jonadab, and the former captives|Psalmus David, filiorum Jonadab, et primorum captivorum]]. Jeremias tells how Jonadab commanded his sons not to drink wine, nor to dwell in houses, but to live in tents[[Jer 35:6||]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxv, 14; the command itself is told at Jer 35:6–7]. His sons obeyed him faithfully: for which the Lord reproaches the children of Israel, that the words of Jonadab had prevailed[[Jer 35:14||]] more than His own words, which the children of Israel neglected to obey[[Jer 35:16||]]. But the psalm now to be explained does not treat of that history, but of the thing signified by it, namely of those who obey the divine will of their own accord: who were the former captives, that is, before they were converted to God they were subject to the bondage of sin and the yoke of the devil, as the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:3|we all conversed in time past, in the desires of our flesh|Nos aliquando conversati sumus in desideriis carnis nostræ]], [[Eph 2:3|and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest|et eramus natura filii iræ, sicut et ceteri]]. For as long as we bear the image of the prevarication of Adam[[Rom 5:14||]], we are led captive into the law of sin; but when we begin to bear the image of Christ, by following in His footsteps, we are set free from the wretched captivity of guilt and of the devil, and are made children of grace, and free in the Lord. For hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 15:47|The first man was of the earth, earthly: the second man, from heaven, heavenly|Primus homo de terra, terrenus ; secundus homo de cœlo, cœlestis]]. [[1 Cor 15:48|Such as is the earthly, such also are the earthly: and such as is the heavenly, such also are they that are heavenly|Qualis terrenus, tales et terreni ; et qualis cœlestis, tales et cœlestes]]. [[1 Cor 15:49|Therefore, as we have borne the image of the earthly, let us bear also the image of the heavenly|Igitur, sicut portavimus imaginem terreni, portemus et imaginem cœlestis]]. The sense of the title, therefore, is: this *psalm*, which is *of David* the prophet as its author, was put forth for the instruction *of the sons of Jonadab*, that is, of the sons of obedience, who serve God of their own accord, *the former captives*, that is, of the sons who were captives in the way just described, before they obeyed the Lord, whom to serve is truly to reign.

paras.t: LOQUENS ergo Propheta in persona hominis vehementer afflicti, et in Domino pure ac integre confidentis, sibique nil boni aut perfectionis attribuentis, ait : In te, Domine, speravi : id est, in tua pietate immensa, in tua bonitate purissima, in merito passionis tuæ, o Christe, non in propriis meritis, vel in incerto divitiarum, aut in aliquo bono creato, caduco et vano, confisus sum. Idcirco oro ut non confundar in æternum, id est, ne æternaliter peream, nec in die judicii, verbum illud æternæ confusionis, cum reprobis audiam : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Quamvis ergo, o Domine, in præsenti vita a malignis confundor, despicior, tribulor, non confundar in æternum, nec spei meæ priver effectu, sed fructum ejus adeptus salvificer, quemadmodum testatus es speranti in te, per Jeremiam : Eruens liberabo te, et erit tibi anima tua in salutem, quia in me habuisti fiduciam.
paras.en: SPEAKING, then, in the person of a man sorely afflicted, who trusts in the Lord purely and wholly and attributes to himself nothing of good or of perfection, the Prophet says: [[70:1|In thee, O Lord, I have hoped|In te, Domine, speravi]]: that is, in Thy boundless pity, in Thy most pure goodness, in the merit of Thy passion, O Christ, and not in my own merits, nor in the uncertainty of riches, nor in any created good, perishable and vain, have I trusted. Therefore I pray that I may [[70:1|never be put to confusion|non confundar in æternum]], that is, that I may not perish eternally, nor at the day of judgment hear with the reprobate that word of eternal confusion: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. Although, then, O Lord, in the present life I am confounded, despised and troubled by the wicked, let me not be confounded for ever, nor be robbed of the effect of my hope, but, having obtained its fruit, may I be saved, as Thou hast testified to him who hopes in Thee, through Jeremias: [[Jer 39:18|But delivering, I will deliver thee|Eruens liberabo te]], [[Jer 39:18|but thy life shall be saved for thee, because thou hast put thy trust in me|et erit tibi anima tua in salutem, quia in me habuisti fiduciam]].

paras.t: In justitia tua libera me, etc. Justitia Dei duplex est, scilicet increata, quæ est ipsemet Deus. In hac justitia liberat Deus viros justos atque perfectos, qui merito suæ conversationis virtuosæ, salvari merentur a Domino. Alia vero est justitia Dei creata, quæ dici potest omnis gratia, virtus et perfectio nobis a Deo concessa. Omnis enim nostra justitia, est Dei, sicut datoris, conservatoris, ac præmiatoris. Specialiter tamen ista justitia dici potest pœnitentia seu forum pœnitentiale, in quo de peccato justitia agitur, dum ipsum corrigitur atque punitur. In hac ergo justitia pœnitentiali, qua homo de propria culpa dolet, seque ad Deum convertit, petit liberari peccator et pœnitens, qui nondum virtutibus plenus est, nec bonis operibus meritisque abundans. Ait ergo : In justitia tua, id est, sicut exigit tua divina justitia, libera me a malo culpæ in sæculo isto, et eripe me a malo pœnæ in sæculo venturo : hoc enim divina justitia tua exigit, ut sperantem in te pœnitentemque liberes. Vel : In tua justitia, mihi a te infusa ac data, videlicet merito actuum virtuosorum, quos virtute gratiæ tuæ feci, libera me. Liberatio enim actui virtutis correspondet. Nec ista petitio repugnat ei quod dictum est : In te, Domine, speravi. Spes enim principaliter innititur Deo, secundario autem innititur proprio merito, quod homo agnoscit sibi a Deo concessum, quia et nostra merita sunt Dei dona.
paras.en: [[70:2|Deliver me in thy justice|In justitia tua libera me]], etc. The justice of God is twofold: the one uncreated, which is God Himself. In this justice God delivers just and perfect men, who by the merit of their virtuous way of life deserve to be saved by the Lord. The other is the created justice of God, by which may be meant every grace, virtue and perfection granted us by God. For all our justice is God's, as its giver, its preserver and its rewarder. Yet in a special way this justice may be called penance, or the court of penance [forum pœnitentiale: the sacrament of penance seen as a tribunal, in which the sinner accuses himself and is judged], in which justice is done upon sin, while sin is corrected and punished. In this penitential justice, then, by which a man grieves for his own guilt and turns to God, the sinner and penitent who is not yet full of virtues, nor abounding in good works and merits, asks to be delivered. He says therefore: [[70:2|in thy justice|In justitia tua]], that is, as Thy divine justice requires, [[70:2|deliver me|libera me]] from the evil of guilt in this world, [[70:2|and rescue me|et eripe me]] from the evil of punishment in the world to come: for this Thy divine justice requires, that Thou deliver him who hopes in Thee and repents. Or: in Thy justice infused and given me by Thee, namely by the merit of the virtuous acts which I have done by the power of Thy grace, deliver me. For deliverance answers to the act of virtue. Nor does this petition conflict with what was said: [[70:1|In thee, O Lord, I have hoped|In te, Domine, speravi]]. For hope rests principally on God, but secondarily on one's own merit, which a man acknowledges to have been granted him by God, since our merits too are gifts of God.

paras.t: Inclina ad me aurem tuam, id est, misericordiam tuam applica mihi, et salva me, nunc per gratiam, per opera virtuosa, per inchoationem felicitatis futuræ, videlicet per contemplationem deiformem et consolationem internam ; in futuro vero me salva per gloriam.
paras.en: [[70:2|Incline thy ear unto me|Inclina ad me aurem tuam]], that is, turn Thy mercy upon me, [[70:2|and save me|et salva me]] now by grace, by virtuous works, by the beginning of the happiness to come, namely by deiform contemplation [that is, contemplation that conforms the soul to God] and by inward consolation; but in the life to come save me by glory.

paras.t: Esto mihi in Deum protectorem, et in locum munitum : id est, tu qui es omnium Deus et conservator, sic sis mihi Deus, ut me protegas et conserves, sicut in loco munito custoditur homo a jaculis atque insidiis inimici : quatenus sicut qui offendit, et iram judicis metuit, ad locum refugii properat, et in eo tutatur ; sic mihi peccatori sit semper recursus ad tuam clementiam, securitasque in ea; ut salvum me facias. Quod ideo deprecor te, Quoniam firmamentum meum, id est causa totius firmitatis stabilitatisque meæ, et refugium meum, id est terminus fugæ meæ, spes mea et summum bonum meum, in quo solo salutem constituo, es tu, Domine.
paras.en: [[70:3|Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength|Esto mihi in Deum protectorem, et in locum munitum]]: that is, Thou who art the God and preserver of all, be so a God to me that Thou protect and preserve me, as a man is kept safe in a fortified place from the darts and ambushes of the enemy: so that, as one who has offended and fears the wrath of the judge hastens to a place of refuge and is safe in it, so I, a sinner, may always have recourse to Thy clemency, and security in it; [[70:3|that thou mayst make me safe|ut salvum me facias]]. And this I beg of Thee [[70:3|For thou art my firmament|Quoniam firmamentum meum]], that is, the cause of all my firmness and stability, [[70:3|and my refuge|et refugium meum]], that is, the goal of my flight, my hope and my highest good, in whom alone I set my salvation: Thou art this, O Lord.

paras.t: Deus meus, eripe me de manu peccatoris, id est de potestate diaboli, ne ejus impugnationi succumbam. De quo in Evangelio scriptum est : Homicida erat ab initio, et in veritate non stetit; et alibi, Diabolus ab initio peccat. Eripe quoque me et de manu contra legem agentis, id est cujuslibet hominis impii justos persequentis, ne ab homine tali inficiar et seducar; et iniqui, qui fraternæ caritatis jura dissolvens, me persequitur sine causa. Maxime tamen, o Domine, eripe me de manu peccatoris, id est a me ipso peccatore, secundum quod impius sum, et de manu mei ipsius contra legem agentis, convertendo me ad te, ne talis sim qualis fui, sed esse desistam injustus : quemadmodum scriptum est, Verte impios, et non erunt.
paras.en: [[70:4|Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the sinner|Deus meus, eripe me de manu peccatoris]], that is, from the power of the devil, lest I give way under his assault. Of him it is written in the Gospel: [[John 8:44|He was a murderer from the beginning: and he stood not in the truth|Homicida erat ab initio, et in veritate non stetit]]; and elsewhere, [[1 John 3:8|the devil sinneth from the beginning|Diabolus ab initio peccat]]. Deliver me also [[70:4|out of the hand of the transgressor of the law|de manu contra legem agentis]], that is, of any wicked man who persecutes the just, lest I be infected and led astray by such a man; [[70:4|and of the unjust|et iniqui]], who, breaking the laws of brotherly charity, persecutes me without cause. Most of all, however, O Lord, deliver me [[70:4|out of the hand of the sinner|de manu peccatoris]], that is, from myself the sinner, inasmuch as I am wicked, and out of the hand of myself, the transgressor of the law, by turning me to Thee, so that I may not be such as I was, but may cease to be unjust: as it is written, [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]].

paras.t: Quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine, id est causa, finis et præmium patientiæ meæ. Unde et sanctus Job ait : Ubi est præstolatio mea et patientia mea? Tu es, Domine, Deus meus. Domine, spes mea a juventute mea : vel corporali, quoniam multi a juventute jugum Domini super se portant, et in Deo confidunt, illi videlicet qui in prima vigilia convertuntur. Propter quod Jeremias testatur : Bonum est viro, quum portaverit jugum Domini ab adolescentia sua; et alius, Laudabo nomen tuum, Domine, assidue, et confitebor tibi quum adhuc junior sum, antequam oberrem. Vel, A juventute mea spirituali, id est ab illo tempore quo cœpi renovari spiritu mentis meæ, exspoliando me veterem hominem cum actibus suis, et induendo novum, qui renovatur in agnitionem Dei, secundum Apostolum. Ab hac juventute est Deus spes hominis, quia sic renovari et taliter conversari nemo potest, nisi in Domino sperans.
paras.en: [[70:5|For thou art my patience, O Lord|Quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine]], that is, the cause, the end and the reward of my patience. Whence holy Job also says: [[Job 17:15|Where is now then my expectation|Ubi est præstolatio mea]], and my patience? [so Denis; the verse itself reads "and who considereth my patience?"] Thou art, O Lord, my God. [[70:5|my hope, O Lord, from my youth|Domine, spes mea a juventute mea]]: either my bodily youth, for many bear the yoke of the Lord upon themselves from their youth and trust in God, namely those who are converted in the first watch [that is, early in life]. For which reason Jeremias testifies: [[Lam 3:27|It is good for a man, when he hath borne the yoke|Bonum est viro, quum portaverit jugum]] of the Lord [[Lam 3:27|from his youth|ab adolescentia sua]]; and another says: [[Ecclus 51:15|I will praise thy name continually|Laudabo nomen tuum, Domine, assidue]], and I will give thanks to Thee[[Ecclus 51:17||]] [[Ecclus 51:18|When I was yet young, before I wandered about|quum adhuc junior sum, antequam oberrem]] [the margin gives Eccli. ii, 15, 17, 18, for li, 15, 17, 18]. Or, from my spiritual youth, that is, from the time when I began to be renewed in the spirit of my mind[[Eph 4:23||]], stripping myself of the old man with his deeds[[Col 3:9||]], and putting on the new, who is renewed unto the knowledge of God[[Col 3:10||]], according to the Apostle. From this youth God is the hope of a man, since no one can be so renewed and live in such a way unless he hopes in the Lord.

paras.t: In te confirmatus sum ex utero, id est, tua virtute sum conservatus in esse naturali in utero matris meæ carnalis, usque ad egressum ex utero, et deinceps. Nisi enim Deus conservaret infantem in utero, esse et permanere non posset, sicut nec aliquid sine manutenentia Dei subsistere valet; et nisi infantem in utero a cunctis præservaret periculis, frequenter facileque moreretur in ventre. Propterea dicit S. Thomas et alii multi, quod infanti adhuc in utero existenti, deputatur angelus bonus qui eum custodiat. De ventre matris meæ tu es protector meus, id est, ab ortu nativitatis meæ usque in præsens, tu protexisti me per te ipsum et angelum tuum sanctum. Quamvis enim justo judicio suo permittat Deus aliquem aliquando cadere, quemlibet tamen electum in tantum defendit, quod non permittit eum in peccato mortali decedere, vel a diabolo finaliter absorberi : imo in quolibet reprobo hoc agit misericordia Creatoris, quod per angelicam custodiam a multis malis retrahitur, atque ad aliqua bona instigatur.
paras.en: [[70:6|By thee have I been confirmed from the womb|In te confirmatus sum ex utero]], that is, by Thy power I was kept in my natural being in the womb of my mother according to the flesh, until I came forth from the womb, and ever since. For unless God preserved the infant in the womb, it could not exist and endure, just as nothing can subsist without God's upholding [manutenentia, literally a "holding in the hand": God's keeping of creatures in being]; and unless He kept the infant in the womb from all dangers, it would often and easily die in the womb. Therefore St. Thomas and many others say that a good angel is assigned to the infant while it is still in the womb, to guard it. [[70:6|from my mother's womb thou art my protector|De ventre matris meæ tu es protector meus]], that is, from my birth until now Thou hast protected me by Thyself and by Thy holy angel. For although God by His just judgment permits someone to fall at times, yet He so defends every one of the elect that He does not let him die in mortal sin, or be finally swallowed up by the devil: indeed, even in every reprobate the mercy of the Creator brings it about that by the guardianship of the angels he is held back from many evils and urged on to some good.

paras.t: Spiritualiter vero ita exponendus est versus iste : In te confirmatus sum, id est, in fide et gratia tua cœpi stabiliri, ex utero, id est ex catechismo, ubi in christiana doctrina instructus sum. De ventre matris meæ, id est de ventre Ecclesiæ, utpote ex sacro Baptismate, in quo spiritualiter regeneratus sum ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto. In Baptismo enim infunditur nobis gratia, fides, spes, caritas. Tu es protector meus, me conservando in donis gratiæ gratum facientis, in Baptismo collatis.
paras.en: Spiritually, however, this verse is to be explained thus: [[70:6|By thee have I been confirmed|In te confirmatus sum]], that is, I began to be made steadfast in Thy faith and grace, [[70:6|from the womb|ex utero]], that is, from the catechism [the instruction in the faith given before baptism], where I was taught Christian doctrine. [[70:6|From my mother's womb|De ventre matris meæ]], that is, from the womb of the Church, namely from holy Baptism, in which I was spiritually born again of water and the Holy Ghost[[John 3:5||]]. For in Baptism grace, faith, hope and charity are infused into us. [[70:6|thou art my protector|Tu es protector meus]], by keeping me in the gifts of sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace "that makes pleasing" to God] bestowed in Baptism.

paras.t: In te cantatio mea semper : id est, laus mea vocalis, exsultatio cordis, et regratiatio animæ meæ, circa tua beneficia versatur, et de tua bonitate concipitur, ita quod incessabiliter te laudare desidero, in omni loco, causa ac tempore. Et si hominem laudo, vel aliquid creatum, hoc ago ad gloriam tuam, tibi omnia bona adscribens, et ad tuum honorem omnia referens. Nec aliquem laudo in malo (sicut superius dictum est, Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ): sed si quem laudo, propter virtutes et gratiæ dona hoc facio. Hoc modo Paulus suos frequenter laudavit discipulos.
paras.en: [[70:6|Of thee I shall continually sing|In te cantatio mea semper]]: that is, the praise of my voice, the exultation of my heart and the thanksgiving of my soul are busied about Thy benefits and are conceived from Thy goodness, so that I desire to praise Thee unceasingly, in every place, cause and time. And if I praise a man, or anything created, I do it to Thy glory, ascribing all good things to Thee and referring all things to Thy honour. Nor do I praise anyone in evil (as was said above, [[Ps 9:24|For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul|Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ]] [the margin gives Ps. x, 3, according to the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate this is Ps 9:24]): but if I praise anyone, I do it for his virtues and the gifts of grace. In this way Paul often praised his disciples[[Rom 1:8||]][[Rom 16:4||]].

paras.t: Tanquam prodigium factus sum multis, id est, velut portentum a multis sum reputatus, irrisus ac spretus, quoniam vita mea vitæ illorum dissimilis invenitur. Temporalia enim, carnalia et delectabilia, quæ ipsi magni pendunt, laudant, acquirunt et diligunt, ego velut stercora arbitror, ut Christo pura ac libera mente adhæream; cœlestia, invisibilia et æterna terrenis, visibilibus et transitoriis præfero; patrem, matrem, fratres, sorores, uxorem, propinquos, agros et cetera universa pro Christi amore relinquo: ideo vitam meam putant insaniam. Unde et ait divinus Apostolus: Spectaculum facti sumus mundo et angelis et hominibus; ad Philippenses quoque, Existimo, inquit, omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Hinc etiam sanctus Ezechiel ait ad populum suum: Ezechiel erit portentum vestrum.
paras.en: [[70:7|I am become unto many as a wonder|Tanquam prodigium factus sum multis]], that is, I am reckoned by many as a portent, mocked and despised, because my life is found to be unlike theirs[[Wis 2:15||]] [the margin gives Wisd. ii, 16; the life unlike other men's is at Wis 2:15]. For the temporal, carnal and pleasant things which they themselves set great store by, praise, acquire and love, I count as dung[[Phil 3:8||]], that I may cleave to Christ with a pure and free mind; things heavenly, invisible and eternal I prefer to things earthly, visible and passing; father, mother, brothers, sisters, wife, kinsfolk, lands and all things else I leave for the love of Christ[[Matt 19:29||]]: therefore they think my life madness[[Wis 5:4||]]. Whence the divine Apostle also says: [[1 Cor 4:9|We are made a spectacle to the world and to angels and to men|Spectaculum facti sumus mundo et angelis et hominibus]]; and to the Philippians too: [[Phil 3:8|I count|Existimo]], he says, [[Phil 3:8|all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge of Jesus Christ, my Lord|omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]. Hence too holy Ezechiel says to his people: [[Ezech 24:24|Ezekiel shall be unto you for a sign of things to come|Ezechiel erit portentum vestrum]] [portentum, "portent", the word Denis has just used to explain the psalm's "wonder"].

paras.t: Et tu adjutor fortis: id est, tu, Domine, fortiter mihi adstitisti, magnamque gratiam ac fortitudinem donasti, ita quod propter improborum irrisiones et persecutiones non recessi a te, nec ab opere bono cessavi, sicut, heu! plurimi facere solent, qui dum se ab aliis aspernari, molestari et vituperari conspiciunt, viam perfectionis arreptam relinquunt. Quocontra exhortatur nos divinus Apostolus: Per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen, adspicientes in auctorem fidei et consummatorem Jesum, qui proposito sibi gaudio, sustinuit crucem, confusione contempta. Recogitate eum, qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversus semetipsum contradictionem, ut non fatigemini animis vestris. Et rursus: Exeamus igitur ad eum extra castra, improperium ejus portantes.
paras.en: [[70:7|but thou art a strong helper|Et tu adjutor fortis]]: that is, Thou, O Lord, hast stood mightily by me and given me great grace and strength, so that for all the mockery and persecutions of the wicked I have not gone back from Thee, nor ceased from good works, as, alas, very many are wont to do, who, when they see themselves scorned, troubled and reviled by others, abandon the way of perfection they had taken up. Against this the divine Apostle exhorts us: [[Heb 12:1|let us run by patience to the fight proposed to us|Per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen]], [[Heb 12:2|Looking on Jesus, the author and finisher of faith, who, having joy set before him, endured the cross, despising the shame|adspicientes in auctorem fidei et consummatorem Jesum, qui proposito sibi gaudio, sustinuit crucem, confusione contempta]]. [[Heb 12:3|think diligently upon him that endured such opposition from sinners against himself that you be not wearied|Recogitate eum, qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversus semetipsum contradictionem, ut non fatigemini]] in your minds. And again: [[Heb 13:13|Let us go forth therefore to him without the camp, bearing his reproach|Exeamus igitur ad eum extra castra, improperium ejus portantes]] [the margin gives Ibid. xii, 3 beside these words; they are Heb 13:13].

paras.t: Deinde vir justus cupiens de tantis beneficiis gratus Domino inveniri, precatur. Repleatur os meum laude: id est, tu, Domine, mentem accende, illumina, quatenus tuam bonitatem et beneficia contemplando, os divina laude repleatur. Ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur. Et nisi tu mentem divino calore succenderis, cito fatigabitur in tua laude os corporis, imo et spiritus meus. Idcirco superius dictum est: Sicut adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea, scilicet divino amore, et labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum. Unde nunc plenius subdit, cur petat os suum laude impleri: ut cantem gloriam tuam, id est, quatenus prædicem famam tuam gloriosam, tamque excellentiam tuam cantando annuntiem, tota die magnitudinem tuam, id est, semper, quantum huic vitæ possibile est, majestatem ac dignitatem tuam decantem. Hoc nempe est divinissimum ac illustrissimum præsentis vitæ exercitium, in divinis laudibus jugiter delectari, hilariter occupari, affectuosissime immorari, cum beatissimo Isaia propheta dicendo: Domine, Deus meus tu es, exaltabo te, et confitebor nomini tuo; et iterum, Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ. Hæc est vere angelica cœliformisque vita, divinæ glorificationis meritoria, sicut et ipse Dominus affirmat: Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum.
paras.en: Then the just man, desiring to be found grateful to the Lord for such great benefits, prays: [[70:8|Let my mouth be filled with praise|Repleatur os meum laude]]: that is, do Thou, O Lord, kindle and enlighten my mind, so that, contemplating Thy goodness and Thy benefits, my mouth may be filled with divine praise. For [[Matt 12:34|out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh|Ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur]]. And unless Thou set my mind alight with divine warmth, the mouth of my body will soon grow weary in Thy praise, and indeed my spirit too. Therefore it was said above: [[Ps 62:6|Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness|Sicut adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea]], namely with divine love, [[Ps 62:6|and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips|et labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxii, 6, for lxii, 6]. Hence he now adds more fully why he asks that his mouth be filled with praise: [[70:8|that I may sing thy glory|ut cantem gloriam tuam]], that is, that I may proclaim Thy glorious fame and announce Thy excellence in song, [[70:8|thy greatness all the day long|tota die magnitudinem tuam]], that is, that I may always, as far as is possible in this life, sing of Thy majesty and dignity. For this indeed is the most divine and most glorious exercise of the present life: to delight continually in the divine praises, to be cheerfully busied in them, to dwell on them with the deepest affection, saying with the most blessed prophet Isaias: [[Is 25:1|O Lord, thou art my God|Domine, Deus meus tu es]], [[Is 25:1|I will exalt O thee, and give glory to thy name|exaltabo te, et confitebor nomini tuo]]; and again, [[Is 26:8|thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul|Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ]]. This is truly the angelic and heaven-like life, which merits being glorified by God, as the Lord Himself affirms: [[1 Kings 2:30|whosoever shall glorify me, him will I glorify|Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum]].

paras.t: Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis. Quemadmodum duplex assignata est nunc juventus, spiritualis et corporalis, sic duplex senectus est: una corporis, dum calor deficit, et corporea virtus occumbere incipit; alia vero est senectus animæ, dum spiritualis calor amoris frigescit, nec anima per gratiarum incrementa renovatur, sed in negligentia sua et vitiis inveteratur, vel tædio persecutionum gravatur, aut minus activa in bonis efficitur. Et de utraque senectute intelligi possunt hæc verba, Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis: id est, ne gratiam tuam auferas mihi, dum corporaliter senesco, aut mente deficio; sed tunc tanto benignius mihi subvenias, quanto me amplius indigere agnoscis. Et ideo, quasi exponendo quod dictum est, addit: Quum deficiet virtus mea corporalis aut spiritualis: quod maxime fieri solet et potest in agone, et tempore magnæ infirmitatis ; ne derelinquas me. In hoc versu S. Thomas singularem præcipuamque devotionem habere solebat, et in dulces lacrimas ac uberem fletum amorose resolvi. Versus enim hic mirabiliter affectuosus, dulcis et efficax est, et salubris : modo eum ita ut decet, consideremus.
paras.en: [[70:9|Cast me not off in the time of old age|Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis]]. Just as a twofold youth has now been set down, spiritual and bodily, so there is a twofold old age: one of the body, when its heat fails and bodily strength begins to sink; the other is the old age of the soul, when the spiritual heat of love grows cold, and the soul is not renewed by increase of graces, but grows old in its negligence and vices, or is weighed down by weariness of persecutions, or becomes less active in good works. And these words can be understood of both old ages, [[70:9|Cast me not off in the time of old age|Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis]]: that is, take not thy grace from me when I grow old in body or fail in mind; but succour me then the more kindly, the more thou seest me to be in need. And so, as though expounding what has been said, he adds: [[70:9|when my strength shall fail|Quum deficiet virtus mea]], bodily or spiritual (which is most wont to happen, and can happen, in the agony [that is, the last struggle before death] and in a time of great sickness), [[70:9|do not thou forsake me|ne derelinquas me]]. St Thomas [that is, Thomas Aquinas] was wont to have a singular and special devotion to this verse, and to melt lovingly into sweet tears and abundant weeping. For this verse is wonderfully full of feeling, sweet and effective, and wholesome, if only we consider it as is fitting.

paras.t: Merito autem, o Domine, peto ista a te, Quia dixerunt inimici mei mihi quidquid excogitare potuerunt ad fallendum et opprimendum me. Dæmones enim honores proponunt, mundus divitias, caro delicias. Et qui custodiebant, id est observabant, animam meam ad decipiendum, consilium fecerunt in unum, id est pari proposito et fine eodem, facti unanimes ad perpetrandum illicita ; Dicentes : Deus dereliquit eum. Quoniam enim factus sum illis prodigium, putant vitam meam Domino non placere, præsertim quum videant se in hoc sæculo prosperari ac prævalere, me vero variis calamitatibus fatigari atque deficere. Hoc namque opinantur maligni, dum justos cernunt affligi, se autem lætari ac dominari. Unde Habacuc : Quia, inquit, impius prævalet adversus justum, propterea egreditur judicium perversum. Et quia me putant a Deo derelictum, arbitrantur se obsequium præstare Deo me persequendo ; et cohortando se, dicunt : Persequimini et comprehendite eum, id est, facite ei quod vultis, quia non est qui eripiat eum de manibus vestris : ipse namque humanum auxilium sprevit, et in Deo confisus est. Non advertunt isti insensati et reprobi, quoniam sicut aurum in fornace, sic Deus probat electos ; et quia per multas tribulationes oportet nos ingredi gloriam Dei, quemadmodum apud sanctum Job inducitur : Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria, et salvabitur innocens.
paras.en: Rightly, then, O Lord, do I ask these things of thee, [[70:10|For my enemies have spoken against me|Quia dixerunt inimici mei mihi]] whatever they could devise to deceive and oppress me. For the demons hold out honours, the world riches, the flesh delights. [[70:10|and they that watched|Et qui custodiebant]], that is, observed, [[70:10|my soul|animam meam]] in order to deceive it, [[70:10|have consulted together|consilium fecerunt in unum]], that is, with like purpose and the same end, made of one mind to commit what is unlawful, [[70:11|Saying: God hath forsaken him|Dicentes : Deus dereliquit eum]]. For since I am become [[70:7|as a wonder|prodigium]] to them, they think that my life does not please the Lord, especially when they see themselves prosper and prevail in this world, but me worn out and failing under various calamities. For this is what the wicked suppose when they see the just afflicted and themselves rejoicing and lording it. Hence Habacuc: [[Hab 1:4|because|Quia]], he says, [[Hab 1:4|the wicked prevaileth against the just, therefore wrong judgment goeth forth|impius prævalet adversus justum, propterea egreditur judicium perversum]]. And because they think me forsaken by God, they suppose that they do God a service by persecuting me; and urging one another on, they say: [[70:11|pursue and take him|Persequimini et comprehendite eum]], that is, do to him what you will, [[70:11|for there is none to deliver him|quia non est qui eripiat eum]] out of your hands: for he has spurned human help and trusted in God. These senseless and reprobate men do not mark that God proves the elect as gold in the furnace, and that through many tribulations we must enter into the glory of God; as is set forth in holy Job: [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]], and [[Job 22:30|The innocent shall be saved|salvabitur innocens]].

paras.t: Deus, ne elongeris a me, auxilium differendo, gratiam subtrahendo, aut eam minorem sinendo ; sed, o Deus meus, in quo summe et plene confido, in auxilium meum respice, tanto gratiosius succurrendo, quanto illi malitiosius me subvertere enituntur : quemadmodum scriptum est, Bonus Dominus et confortans in die tribulationis, et sciens sperantes in se.
paras.en: [[70:12|O God, be not thou far from me|Deus, ne elongeris a me]], by delaying help, withdrawing grace, or letting it grow less; but, [[70:12|O my God|o Deus meus]], in whom I trust supremely and fully, [[70:12|make haste to my help|in auxilium meum respice]] [the Latin *respice* is literally "look": look to my help], succouring me the more graciously, the more maliciously they strive to overthrow me: as it is written, [[Nah 1:7|The Lord is good, and giveth strength in the day of trouble: and knoweth them that hope in him|Bonus Dominus et confortans in die tribulationis, et sciens sperantes in se]].

paras.t: Confundantur de suis sceleribus, et deficiant ab exsecutione operis mali, detrahentes animæ meæ, bonam ejus famam denigrare optantes : quod est mortale peccatum, quoniam bona fama multum pretiosa atque amabilis est, et melior cunctis divitiis, quemadmodum Salomon profitetur : Melius est nomen bonum quam unguenta pretiosa : et Ecclesiasticus : Curam habe de bono nomine ; hoc enim magis proderit tibi, quam mille thesauri. Propterea detractio est majus peccatum quam furtum. Operiantur confusione prædicta, et pudore, qui in confessione peccati maxime cooperatur ad culpæ remissionem, etiam quantum ad pœnam, qui quærunt mala mihi inferre, meque ad peccandum inducere, aut simili modo injuste affligere. De hac bona confusione apud Ezechielem scriptum est : Confundimini et erubescite super viis vestris, ait Dominus. Verumtamen, quomodo ista confusio, pudor et defectio multipliciter accipi queant, in præcedentis psalmi explanatione inductum est.
paras.en: [[70:13|Let them be confounded|Confundantur]] for their crimes, [[70:13|and come to nothing|et deficiant]] [*deficiant*, "let them fail", that is, fall away] from carrying out their evil work, [[70:13|that detract my soul|detrahentes animæ meæ]], wishing to blacken its good name: which is a mortal sin, since a good name is very precious and lovable, and better than all riches, as Solomon declares: [[Eccles 7:2|A good name is better than precious ointments|Melius est nomen bonum quam unguenta pretiosa]]; and Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 41:15|Take care of a good name|Curam habe de bono nomine]]; for this will profit thee more [[Ecclus 41:15|than a thousand treasures|quam mille thesauri]] [Denis reads *proderit*, "will profit", where the Vulgate has *permanebit*, "shall continue"]. Therefore detraction is a greater sin than theft. [[70:13|let them be covered with confusion|Operiantur confusione]], the confusion spoken of, [[70:13|and blame|et pudore]] [*pudor*, shame], which in the confession of sin works together most of all towards the remission of guilt, and even of the punishment, [[70:13|that seek my hurt|qui quærunt mala mihi]] [literally "who seek evils for me"], to bring evils upon me, and to lead me into sin, or in like manner to afflict me unjustly. Of this good confusion it is written in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:32|be confounded, and ashamed at your own ways|Confundimini et erubescite super viis vestris]], saith the Lord. But how this confusion, shame and failing may be taken in many ways has been set out in the explanation of the preceding psalm.

paras.t: Ego autem semper sperabo, id est, quantumcumque illi me persequantur verbis et factis, occulte et publice, ego nihilo minus incessanter in te confidere volo : sicut beatus Job de se fatetur, Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo. Et Salomon : Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo ; et, Exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te. Et adjiciam super omnem laudem tuam : id est, omnem laudem qua te venerari potero, vel ab aliis es laudatus, confitebor esse minorem tua dignitate, et in infinitum deficere a præconio quo tu dignus es, propter tuæ bonitatis plenitudinem prorsus immensam : idcirco, quantum mihi possibile fuerit, semper conabor te novis hymnis laudare, perfectiori laude extollere, et nunquam a tua laude cessare.
paras.en: [[70:14|But I will always hope|Ego autem semper sperabo]]: that is, however much they persecute me in word and deed, secretly and openly, I will nonetheless trust in thee unceasingly: as blessed Job confesses of himself, [[Job 13:15|Although he should kill me, I will trust in him|Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo]]. And Solomon: [[Prov 3:5|Have confidence in the Lord with all thy heart|Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo]]; and, [[Prov 20:22|wait for the Lord, and he will deliver thee|Exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te]]. [[70:14|and will add to all thy praise|Et adjiciam super omnem laudem tuam]] [literally "I will add above all thy praise"]: that is, all the praise with which I shall be able to honour thee, or with which thou hast been praised by others, I will confess to be less than thy dignity, and to fall infinitely short of the praise of which thou art worthy, because of the altogether boundless fullness of thy goodness: therefore, as far as shall be possible to me, I will always strive to praise thee with new hymns, to extol thee with more perfect praise, and never to cease from thy praise.

paras.t: Os meum annuntiabit, apud se te laudando, teque coram aliis prædicando, justitiam tuam, qua unicuique reddis quod meretur, et sine personarum acceptione omnia operaris. Te ergo, o Domine, justificabo, tua judicia approbabo, me vero accusabo et condemnabo. Potest quoque per justitiam Dei sacra Scriptura intelligi, in qua divinæ justitiæ præcepta atque consilia continentur. Unde Sapientia ait : Justi sunt omnes sermones mei, et non est in illis perversum quid neque pravum. Et ita Dei justitiam annuntiare, est sacram Scripturam docere, prædicare, aut legere. Annuntiabit quoque os meum tota die salutare tuum, id est, indesinenter competentibus horis diei, narrabo atque laudabo Dominum Christum omnium salvatorem; vel, Salutare tuum, id est salutem et salvationem quam nobis misericorditer impendisti per Christum, atque in cœlis parasti.
paras.en: [[70:15|My mouth shall shew forth|Os meum annuntiabit]], praising thee inwardly and preaching thee before others, [[70:15|thy justice|justitiam tuam]], by which thou renderest to each what he deserves, and workest all things without respect of persons. Thee, therefore, O Lord, will I justify, thy judgments will I approve, but myself will I accuse and condemn. By the justice of God may also be understood holy Scripture, in which the precepts and counsels of the divine justice are contained. Hence Wisdom says: [[Prov 8:8|All my words are just, there is nothing wicked, nor perverse in them|Justi sunt omnes sermones mei, et non est in illis perversum quid neque pravum]]. And so to shew forth the justice of God is to teach, preach or read holy Scripture. My mouth shall shew forth also, [[70:15|all the day long|tota die]], [[70:15|thy salvation|salutare tuum]] [*salutare*, "salvation", can also be read as "Saviour"]: that is, unceasingly at the fitting hours of the day I will tell of and praise the Lord Christ, the Saviour of all; or, [[70:15|thy salvation|Salutare tuum]], that is, the salvation and saving which thou hast mercifully bestowed on us through Christ, and prepared in heaven.

paras.t: Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam. Istud variis modis exponi potest. Primo sic : Non cognovi litteraturam, id est, non approbavi inanem philosophiam, et omnem scientiam extollentem se adversum scientiam Dei : non quod philosophia sit per se odibilis aut vitanda ; sed quia non debemus in ea quiescere et inaniter gloriari aut inflari, sed ad divinam doctrinam ipsam ordinare. Vel, Non cognovi litteraturam, id est, nihil me scire arbitratus sum, quando in conspectu Dei me ipsum constitui, et ad ejus sapientiam infinitam me comparavi. Vel, Non cognovi litteraturam, id est aliquam scientiam per humanam exercitationem, informationem et studium. Hoc non competit omnibus, sed Petro et Joanni, de quibus legitur, quod erant homines sine litteris et idiotæ. Dicitur etiam convenire sancto David, qui tempore suæ juventutis oves pavisse legitur, non scholas frequentasse, ut aliqui dicunt ; sed non videtur certum, quia et psalmos metro conscripsit.
paras.en: [[70:15|Because I have not known learning|Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam]] [*litteratura*, letters, that is, book-learning]. This can be expounded in various ways. First thus: [[70:15|I have not known learning|Non cognovi litteraturam]], that is, I have not approved vain philosophy, and all knowledge [[2 Cor 10:5|that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God|extollentem se adversum scientiam Dei]]: not that philosophy is hateful in itself or to be shunned, but because we ought not to rest in it, and glory in it vainly or be puffed up, but to direct it to divine doctrine. Or, [[70:15|I have not known learning|Non cognovi litteraturam]], that is, I thought that I knew nothing when I set myself in the sight of God and compared myself with his infinite wisdom. Or, [[70:15|I have not known learning|Non cognovi litteraturam]], that is, any knowledge got by human practice, instruction and study. This does not apply to all, but to Peter and John, of whom we read that they were [[Acts 4:13|illiterate and ignorant men|homines sine litteris et idiotæ]]. It is also said to fit holy David, who is read to have fed sheep in the time of his youth[[1 Kings 16:11||]][[1 Kings 17:15||]], not to have frequented schools, as some say; but this does not seem certain, since he also wrote the psalms in metre.

paras.t: Quoniam ergo his modis vel aliquo horum, non cognovi litteraturam, introibo per contemplationem supernaturalem, in potentias Domini, id est in perfectiones seu veritates divinas, easque cognoscam et alios instruam.
