These words are not to be understood as though sinners did not labour in this life, especially since they themselves say elsewhere: [[Wis 5:7|We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction, and have walked through hard ways|Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis et perditionis, et ambulavimus vias difficiles]]. Ecclesiastes also says: [[Eccles 2:26|God hath given to a man that is good in his sight, wisdom, and knowledge|Bono homini dedit Deus sapientiam et scientiam]], [[Eccles 2:26|but to the sinner he hath given vexation, and superfluous care|peccatori autem afflictionem et curam superfluam]]. There is, then, a twofold labour: the labour of penance, and the labour of wicked working. For as virtue is by its nature delightful, so vice is by its nature bitter, sad, laborious and painful; yet often the contrary happens, as far as we are concerned, because of the corruption of our nature. Sinners, then, are not in the holy labour of penance, since they give themselves neither to sacred vigils, nor to pure prayers, nor to due disciplines [that is, the penitential scourging of oneself], nor to most wholesome fasts, but spend and waste their time in vanity and perversity. And though their life, in truth, is far more laborious and painful than the life of the good, yet because a perverse life pleases them more, they think they live without labour, and they consider the life of the just laborious, and shrink from it and despise it. But the just have true judgement, and have learned by experience how sweet it is to serve God, how great is the delight of a serene conscience, how intense the gladness of a pure soul, how truly sweet is the yoke of Christ and how light His burden[[Matt 11:30||]]. According to Bernard, this verse fits none so properly as the clerics of our time.

paras.t: Quoniam itaque sic prosperantur et otiantur maligni, Ideo tenuit eos superbia, id est, vinculo elationis constricti sunt, et in captivitatem ac servitutem superbiæ ducti : imo servi superbiæ facti, juxta illud, Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati. Operti sunt iniquitate et impietate sua : id est, quemadmodum viri perfecti dicuntur operti atque vestiti justitia, sic isti undique operiuntur malitia, facientes iniquitatem in proximum, et impietatem in Deum. Protulit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum : id est, ex abundantia atque pinguedine seu copia temporalium rerum iniquitas eorum causatur, quoniam temporalium copia rerum, omnis transgressionis est fomentum. Ideo orat vir justus : Tantum victui meo tribue necessaria. Transierunt in affectum cordis, id est, concupiscentiis carnis illicitisque desideriis consenserunt. Quocontra de justis ait Apostolus : Qui autem sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis. Ad quod monemur a principe Apostolorum, dicente : Obsecro vos tanquam advenas et peregrinos, abstinere a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam.
paras.en: Since, then, the wicked so prosper and live at ease, [[72:6|Therefore pride hath held them fast|Ideo tenuit eos superbia]], that is, they are bound by the chain of haughtiness and led into the captivity and slavery of pride: indeed, made slaves of pride, according to that saying: [[John 8:34|whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin|Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati]]. [[72:6|they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness|Operti sunt iniquitate et impietate sua]]: that is, as perfect men are said to be covered and clothed with justice, so these are covered on every side with malice, doing iniquity against their neighbour and wickedness [*impietas*, "impiety"] against God. [[72:7|Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness|Protulit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum]] [Denis reads *Protulit*, "hath brought forth", for the Vulgate's *Prodiit*]: that is, their iniquity is caused by the abundance and fatness, or plenty, of temporal things, since plenty of temporal things is the tinder of every transgression. Therefore the just man prays: [[Prov 30:8|give me only the necessaries of life|Tantum victui meo tribue necessaria]]. [[72:7|they have passed into the affection of the heart|Transierunt in affectum cordis]], that is, they have consented to the concupiscences of the flesh and to unlawful desires. Against which the Apostle says of the just: [[Gal 5:24|And they that are Christ's have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences|Qui autem sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]]. To this we are exhorted by the prince of the Apostles, who says: [[1 Pet 2:11|I beseech you, as strangers and pilgrims, to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul|Obsecro vos tanquam advenas et peregrinos, abstinere a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam]].

paras.t: Cogitaverunt, cum consensu mentali, et locuti sunt, ore corporali, nequitiam, id est fraudulenta et crudelia verba contra virtuosos viros, quos quærunt opprimere : quod in tyrannis, beatorum martyrum homicidis, maxime patet. Unde in Isaia legitur : Fraudulenti vasa pessima sunt ; ipse enim cogitationes concinnabit ad perdendos mites. Iniquitatem, id est verba iniqua, in excelso, id est in sublimi, audacter, alte et publice, locuti sunt : sicut alibi scriptum est, Peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt, et non absconderunt. Posuerunt in cœlum os suum : id est, erecto collo et tumida mente contra Deum locuti sunt verba blasphemiæ, prout in libro Job scribitur : Cucurrit impius adversus Deum erecto collo, et pingui cervice armatus est. Unde et Pharao dixit : Nescio Dominum. Et Sennacherib : Non te decipiat Deus tuus, quia non poterit liberare te. Nero quoque, Domitianus, Diocletianus et alii plures, maximas contra Christum dixerunt blasphemias. Et lingua eorum transivit in terra : id est, sermo eorum rebus terrenis inhæsit, vel in opus processit, atque humanæ fragilitatis mensuram excessit.
paras.en: [[72:8|They have thought|Cogitaverunt]], with the consent of the mind, [[72:8|and spoken|et locuti sunt]], with the bodily mouth, [[72:8|wickedness|nequitiam]], that is, deceitful and cruel words against virtuous men, whom they seek to oppress: which is most plain in the tyrants, the murderers of the blessed martyrs. Hence we read in Isaias: [[Is 32:7|The vessels of the deceitful are most wicked: for he hath framed devices to destroy the meek|Fraudulenti vasa pessima sunt ; ipse enim cogitationes concinnabit ad perdendos mites]]. [[72:8|they have spoken iniquity|Iniquitatem]], that is, wicked words, [[72:8|on high|in excelso]], that is, aloft: boldly, loudly and publicly; as it is written elsewhere: [[Is 3:9|they have proclaimed abroad their sin as Sodom, and they have not hid it|Peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt, et non absconderunt]]. [[72:9|They have set their mouth against heaven|Posuerunt in cœlum os suum]]: that is, with neck raised and swollen mind they have spoken words of blasphemy against God, as is written in the book of Job: [[Job 15:26|He hath run against him with his neck raised up, and is armed with a fat neck|Cucurrit impius adversus Deum erecto collo, et pingui cervice armatus est]] [Denis reads "the wicked man hath run against God"]. Hence Pharao too said: [[Ex 5:2|I know not the Lord|Nescio Dominum]]. And Sennacherib: [[Is 37:10|Let not thy God deceive thee|Non te decipiat Deus tuus]], [[Is 36:14|for he shall not be able to deliver you|quia non poterit liberare te]] [the margin gives Is. xxxvi, 10; Denis's words join Is 37:10 and 36:14 (the same words stand in 4 Kings 18:29 and 19:10)]. Nero too, Domitian, Diocletian and many others spoke the greatest blasphemies against Christ. [[72:9|and their tongue hath passed through the earth|Et lingua eorum transivit in terra]]: that is, their speech has clung to earthly things, or has gone forth into deeds, and has passed beyond the measure of human frailty.

paras.t: Deinde Dominus ait de populo præelecto : Ideo convertetur populus meus hic : id est, quoniam tanta iniquitas atque damnatio concomitantur temporalem prosperitatem impiorum, idcirco populus salvandus convertetur ad me, hic, id est in hac consideratione præsenti : quia perpendet quam periculosa sit mundana prosperitas et carnalis voluptas ; et ita eas abhorrebit et fugiet, nec amplius super iniquos zelabit, sed condolebit, atque ad spiritualem ac arduam conversationem se dabit. Et dies pleni fructibus pœnitentiæ et bonis operibus, invenientur a Deo judice in eis ad Deum conversis. Plenitudinem enim (ait Ambrosius) vita sanctorum habet ; inanes autem sunt dies malorum.
paras.en: Then the Lord says of the chosen people: [[72:10|Therefore will my people return here|Ideo convertetur populus meus hic]]: that is, since such great iniquity and damnation go along with the temporal prosperity of the wicked, therefore the people that is to be saved will turn to me, [[72:10|here|hic]], that is, in this present consideration: for it will weigh how dangerous worldly prosperity and carnal pleasure are; and so it will shrink from them and flee them, and will no longer be zealous on occasion of the wicked, but will grieve for them, and will give itself to a spiritual and arduous way of life. [[72:10|and full days|Et dies pleni]], full of the fruits of penance and of good works, [[72:10|shall be found|invenientur]] by God the judge [[72:10|in them|in eis]] that have turned to God. For the life of the saints (says Ambrose) has fullness; but the days of the wicked are empty.

paras.t: Et dixerunt, prædicti infirmi antequam perfecte essent ad Deum conversi : Quomodo scit Deus ista inferiora, si ista permittit, videlicet ut impii prosperentur ? et, Si est scientia in excelso, id est, si est providentia in Deo sublimi ? Imo videtur quod non : quia si esset, daret Deus malis adversa et pœnas, sicut merentur, justis autem prosperitatem et gaudium. Hoc est quod scribitur apud beatum Job : An cogitas quod Deus excelsior cœlo sit ? Nec nostra considerat, et circa cardines cœli perambulat. Unde de negantibus divinam providentiam alio loco scriptum est : Æstimaverunt lusum esse vitam nostram, et conversationem vitæ ad lucra compositam, et oportere undecumque acquirere. Cur autem infirmi hæc dicant, subjungitur : Ecce ipsi sunt peccatores, et nihilo minus sunt abundantes in sæculo ; obtinuerunt divitias hereditaria possessione.
paras.en: [[72:11|And they said|Et dixerunt]], namely the weak spoken of, before they were perfectly turned to God: [[72:11|How doth God know|Quomodo scit Deus]] these lower things, if He permits them, namely that the wicked should prosper? [[72:11|and is there knowledge in the most High|et, Si est scientia in excelso]], that is, is there providence in God on high? Indeed it seems not: for if there were, God would give adversity and punishments to the wicked, as they deserve, and prosperity and joy to the just. This is what is written in blessed Job: [[Job 22:12|Dost not thou think that God is higher than heaven|An cogitas quod Deus excelsior cœlo sit]]? [[Job 22:14|he doth not consider our things, and he walketh about the poles of heaven|Nec nostra considerat, et circa cardines cœli perambulat]]. Hence of those who deny divine providence it is written in another place: [[Wis 15:12|they have counted our life a pastime and the business of life to be gain, and that we must be getting every way|Æstimaverunt lusum esse vitam nostram, et conversationem vitæ ad lucra compositam, et oportere undecumque acquirere]]. Why the weak say these things is added: [[72:12|Behold these are sinners|Ecce ipsi sunt peccatores]], and nevertheless [[72:12|abounding in the world|sunt abundantes in sæculo]]; [[72:12|they have obtained riches|obtinuerunt divitias]] as an inherited possession.

paras.t: Et dixi, dum adhuc inexercitatos habui sensus : Ergo, id est, quum ita sit, ego sine causa, id est sine fructu et ratione, justificavi cor meum, omni custodia custodiendo cor meum a cogitationibus malis, et sine causa lavi inter innocentes manus meas, id est, opera mea impolluta servavi. Et fui sine causa flagellatus tota die, id est assidue in vigiliis, jejuniis, disciplinis, fletu et precibus, exterioribus quoque laboribus propter Deum assumptis, vel ad spiritualem profectum relatis ; et castigatio mea in matutinis, id est, correctio qua me ipsum correxi, et exercitatio sancta, summo mane arrepta, qua castigavi corpus et spiritum meum, vel a te castigatus sum, fuit inanis.
paras.en: [[72:13|And I said|Et dixi]], while I still had unexercised senses: [[72:13|Then|Ergo]], that is, since it is so, I have [[72:13|in vain|ego sine causa]], that is, without fruit or reason, [[72:13|justified my heart|justificavi cor meum]], keeping my heart [[Prov 4:23|With all watchfulness|omni custodia]] from evil thoughts, [[72:13|and washed my hands among the innocent|et sine causa lavi inter innocentes manus meas]] in vain, that is, I have kept my works undefiled. [[72:14|And I have been scourged all the day|Et fui sine causa flagellatus tota die]] in vain, that is, constantly, in vigils, fasts, disciplines, weeping and prayers, and also in outward labours taken up for God's sake, or directed to spiritual progress; [[72:14|and my chastisement hath been in the mornings|et castigatio mea in matutinis]], that is, the correction by which I corrected myself, and the holy exercise taken up at earliest morning, by which I chastised my body and my spirit, or by which I was chastised by thee, was empty.

paras.t: Consequenter arguit ad oppositum. Si dicebam corde : Narrabo sic, id est, cogitavi ita sentire atque asserere de providentia tua et felicitate malorum ; ecce nationem filiorum tuorum reprobavi, id est, tunc generationem et societatem electorum redarguo, quia vita eorum mercede caret : sicut de quibusdam per Malachiam conqueritur Dominus : Invaluerunt super me verba vestra, dicit Dominus. Et dixistis : Vanus est qui servit Domino ; aut quod emolumentum, quia custodivimus præcepta ejus, et quia ambulavimus tristes coram Domino ?
paras.en: Next he argues to the opposite. [[72:15|If I said|Si dicebam]] in my heart: [[72:15|I will speak thus|Narrabo sic]], that is, I thought to judge and to assert thus of thy providence and of the happiness of the wicked; [[72:15|behold I should condemn the generation of thy children|ecce nationem filiorum tuorum reprobavi]], that is, then I find fault with the generation and company of the elect, since their life lacks its reward: as the Lord complains of some through Malachias: [[Mal 3:13|Your words have been unsufferable to me, saith the Lord|Invaluerunt super me verba vestra, dicit Dominus]]. [[Mal 3:14|And you have said|Et dixistis]]: [[Mal 3:14|He laboureth in vain that serveth God, and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinances, and that we have walked sorrowful before the Lord|Vanus est qui servit Domino ; aut quod emolumentum, quia custodivimus præcepta ejus, et quia ambulavimus tristes coram Domino]]?

paras.t: Existimabam ut cognoscerem : id est, putavi me posse rationem hujus scrutari et invenire, cur impii prosperantur, et sancti multipliciter affliguntur ; hoc labor est ante me, id est, hanc causam cognoscere, laboriosum est mihi.
paras.en: [[72:16|I studied that I might know|Existimabam ut cognoscerem]]: that is, I thought I could search out and find the reason of this, why the wicked prosper and the saints are afflicted in many ways; [[72:16|this thing, it is a labour in my sight|hoc labor est ante me]], that is, to know this cause is laborious to me.

paras.t: Donec intrem in sanctuarium Dei, id est, donec Deus mihi revelet incerta et occulta sapientiæ suæ, in secretum suæ cognitionis me intromittens, et sacram Scripturam, quæ etiam sanctuarium Dei vocatur, mihi aperiat. Per sacram namque Scripturam Deus nobis loquitur et respondet, sicut in sanctuario tabernaculi divina dabantur responsa. Et intelligam in novissimis eorum, id est, considerem quid finaliter instet perversis, quid pœnæ et damnationis eis immineat, quam cito morituri sint, quam districte judicandi, quam irreparabiliter condemnandi. Advertam etiam quid beatitudinis restet electis et justis, quam secure discedent, quam clementer a Judice recipientur, quam gloriose coronabuntur. Dum ista adverto, tunc utique ex prosperitate pravorum non moveor, neque bonorum me turbat adversitas : quoniam scio quod Deus electos hic purgat, quatenus citius copiosiusque glorificentur in cœlis : sicut et ipse in Apocalypsi testatur, Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo. Horum quoque novissimorum præmeditatio sedula, præservat hominem ab omni ruina, juxta illud : In omnibus operibus tuis memorare novissima tua, et in æternum non peccabis. Sed quoniam reprobi ista non pensant, prout de eis in Deuteronomio asseritur, Gens absque consilio est et sine prudentia, utinam saperent et intelligerent, ac novissima providerent ; ideo sine mensura et numero peccant.
paras.en: [[72:17|Until I go into the sanctuary of God|Donec intrem in sanctuarium Dei]]: that is, until God reveal to me [[Ps 50:8|the uncertain and hidden things|incerta et occulta]] of his wisdom [the margin gives Ps. i, 8, a misprint for Ps. l (50), 8], letting me into the secret place of his knowledge, and open to me Holy Scripture, which is also called the sanctuary of God. For through Holy Scripture God speaks to us and answers us, as divine answers were given in the sanctuary of the tabernacle[[Ex 25:22||]]. [[72:17|And understand concerning their last ends|Et intelligam in novissimis eorum]]: that is, let me consider what at the last awaits the perverse, what punishment and damnation hangs over them, how soon they are to die, how strictly they are to be judged, how irreparably condemned. Let me mark also what blessedness remains for the elect and the just, how securely they will depart, how mercifully they will be received by the Judge, how gloriously they will be crowned. While I mark these things, then indeed I am not moved by the prosperity of the wicked, nor does the adversity of the good trouble me: for I know that God purges the elect here, so that they may be glorified the sooner and the more abundantly in heaven, as he himself testifies in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]]. Careful forethought of these last things, too, preserves a man from every fall, according to that saying: [[Ecclus 7:40|In all thy works remember thy last end, and thou shalt never sin.|In omnibus operibus tuis memorare novissima tua, et in æternum non peccabis.]] But since the reprobate do not weigh these things, as is said of them in Deuteronomy, [[Deut 32:28|They are a nation without counsel, and without wisdom|Gens absque consilio est et sine prudentia]], [[Deut 32:29|O that they would be wise and would understand, and would provide for their last end|utinam saperent et intelligerent, ac novissima providerent]], therefore they sin without measure and number.

paras.t: Deinde ponuntur tormenta pravorum. Verumtamen, o Deus, propter dolos, quos impii fecerunt in proximos, posuisti eis, id est impiis, finem vitæ breviorem, quam alias habuissent. Sæpe enim homines propter peccata sua intempestive moriuntur, quando videlicet impletæ sunt iniquitates eorum. Unde de peccatore apud Job scriptum est : Antequam impleantur dies ejus, peribit. Et iterum sanctus Job : Viri, inquit, iniqui ante tempus suum sublati sunt. Dejecisti eos dum allevarentur : id est, dum adhuc florerent et superbirent, humiliasti iniquos, eos occidendo sive damnando. Hinc Abdias disseruit : Superba cordis tui extulit te. Sed si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, inde detraham te, dicit Dominus.
paras.en: Next the torments of the wicked are set out. [[72:18|But indeed|Verumtamen]], O God, [[72:18|for deceits|propter dolos]] which the wicked have practised on their neighbours, [[72:18|thou hast put it to them|posuisti eis]], that is, to the wicked: an end of life shorter than they would otherwise have had. For men often die before their time because of their sins, namely when their iniquities are filled up. Hence it is written in Job of the sinner: [[Job 15:32|Before his days be full he shall perish|Antequam impleantur dies ejus, peribit]]. And again holy Job: [[Job 22:15|wicked men|Viri]], he says, [[Job 22:16|were taken away before their time|iniqui ante tempus suum sublati sunt]] [the margin gives Job xxii, 15, 16; Denis joins the end of v. 15 to v. 16]. [[72:18|when they were lifted up thou hast cast them down|Dejecisti eos dum allevarentur]]: that is, while they still flourished and were proud, thou hast humbled the wicked, by slaying or condemning them. Hence Abdias declared: [[Abd 1:3|The pride of thy heart hath lifted thee up|Superba cordis tui extulit te]]. But [[Abd 1:4|Though thou be exalted as an eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars: thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord|si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, inde detraham te, dicit Dominus]].

paras.t: Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem, perdendo temporalia bona et corporis sanitatem, aut mortem incurrendo, in qua nullus eos valuit adjuvare? Subito defecerunt : sicut dicitur apud Job, Laus impiorum brevis est, et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti. Perierunt, æternaliter condemnati, propter iniquitatem suam : sicut scriptura alia testatur, Ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad inferna descendunt.
paras.en: [[72:19|How are they brought to desolation|Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem]], by losing their temporal goods and the health of the body, or by meeting death, in which no one could help them? [[72:19|they have suddenly ceased to be|Subito defecerunt]]: as is said in Job, [[Job 20:5|the praise of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment|Laus impiorum brevis est, et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti]]. [[72:19|they have perished|Perierunt]], condemned eternally, [[72:19|by reason of their iniquity|propter iniquitatem suam]]: as another scripture testifies, [[Job 21:13|They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to hell.|Ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad inferna descendunt.]]

paras.t: Velut somnium surgentium, Domine, in civitate tua imaginem ipsorum ad nihilum rediges : id est, quemadmodum somnium evigilantium statim evanescit, et fallax fuisse cognoscitur ; sic, o Domine, ad nihilum rediges, id est, condemnabis ac destrues imaginem ipsorum, id est omnem apparentem felicitatem et gloriam reproborum, in civitate tua cœlesti, tollendo eos ab ea, ne videant beatitudinem tuam. Hinc enim dicturi sunt impii in die reprobationis suæ : Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis? Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra, et tanquam nuntius præcurrens. Et iterum scriptum est : Spes impii tanquam lanugo, et tanquam spuma gracilis, et tanquam memoria hospitis unius diei prætereuntis. Ideo in libro Job scriptum est : Si ascenderit usque ad cœlum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit, quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur ; velut somnium avolans non invenietur, transiet quasi visio nocturna.
paras.en: [[72:20|As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing|Velut somnium surgentium, Domine, in civitate tua imaginem ipsorum ad nihilum rediges]]: that is, as the dream of those who wake vanishes at once and is known to have been false, so, O Lord, thou shalt bring to nothing, that is, thou shalt condemn and destroy, their image, that is, all the apparent happiness and glory of the reprobate, in thy heavenly city, by shutting them out of it, so that they may not see thy blessedness. For hence the wicked will say on the day of their rejection: [[Wis 5:8|What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us?|Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis?]] [[Wis 5:9|All those things are passed away like a shadow, and like a post that runneth on|Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra, et tanquam nuntius præcurrens]]. And again it is written: [[Wis 5:15|the hope of the wicked is as dust|Spes impii tanquam lanugo]] [Latin *lanugo*, 'down'], [[Wis 5:15|and as a thin froth|et tanquam spuma gracilis]], [[Wis 5:15|and as the remembrance of a guest of one day that passeth by|et tanquam memoria hospitis unius diei prætereuntis]]. Therefore it is written in the book of Job: [[Job 20:6|If his pride mount up even to heaven, and his head touch the clouds|Si ascenderit usque ad cœlum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit]], [[Job 20:7|In the end he shall be destroyed like a dunghill|quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur]]; [[Job 20:8|As a dream that fleeth away he shall not be found, he shall pass as a vision of the night|velut somnium avolans non invenietur, transiet quasi visio nocturna]].

paras.t: Hæc autem dico, Quia inflammatum est cor meum zelo justitiæ et igne Spiritus Sancti, contigitque mihi quod a Jeremia olim dictum est : Factus est sermo Domini in corde meo quasi ignis exæstuans ; et renes mei, id est motus seu affectus sensitivi appetitus, commutati sunt, id est, rationis imperio subditi sunt, qui dudum secundum impetum concupiscentiæ movebantur : quod non fit sine magna gratia Dei.
paras.en: Now I say these things [[72:21|For my heart hath been inflamed|Quia inflammatum est cor meum]] with zeal for justice and with the fire of the Holy Ghost, and there befell me what was once said by Jeremias: The word of the Lord[[Jer 20:8||]] was made [[Jer 20:9|in my heart as a burning fire|in corde meo quasi ignis exæstuans]] [Denis joins words of Jer 20:8 and 20:9]; [[72:21|and my reins|et renes mei]], that is, the motions or affections of the sensitive appetite, [[72:21|have been changed|commutati sunt]], that is, have been made subject to the rule of reason, which before were moved by the impulse of concupiscence: which does not come about without great grace of God.

paras.t: Et ego ad nihilum redactus sum : id est, quantum ad spirituale esse nihil factus sum, antequam conversi fuerant renes mei, quando peccatis subjacui et concupiscentiis deservivi ; et nescivi me sic annihilatum, propter excæcationem peccati : nam putavi me aliquid esse, quum nihil essem. Vel : Ego ad nihilum redactus sum, propria reputatione ; et nescivi, id est, non sapientem, sed ignorantem me reputavi : eo quod dicat Apostolus, Qui se putat aliquid scire, nondum scit quomodo oportet eum scire : et iterum, Nolite prudentes esse apud vosmetipsos.
paras.en: [[72:22|And I am brought to nothing|Et ego ad nihilum redactus sum]]: that is, as to spiritual being I became nothing, before my reins were turned, when I lay subject to sins and was a slave to concupiscences; [[72:22|and I knew not|et nescivi]] that I was thus brought to nothing, because of the blindness of sin: for I thought myself to be something, when I was nothing[[Gal 6:3||]]. Or: [[72:22|I am brought to nothing|Ego ad nihilum redactus sum]] in my own estimation; [[72:22|and I knew not|et nescivi]], that is, I reckoned myself not wise but ignorant: because the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 8:2|if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he hath not yet known as he ought to know|Qui se putat aliquid scire, nondum scit quomodo oportet eum scire]]; and again, [[Rom 12:16|Be not wise in your own conceits|Nolite prudentes esse apud vosmetipsos]].

paras.t: Ut jumentum factus sum apud te : id est, comparatione tuæ sapientiæ, potius videor esse irrationale animal, quam rationalis creatura. Vel sic : Ut jumentum factus sum apud te, id est, tuo jugo dorsum meum supposui, tuisque præceptis tam prompte obedivi, ut jumentum domino suo obedit, onera ejus portando. Et ego semper tecum. Qui enim se ipsum coram Deo humiliat, eique paret, indesinenter manet in eo per gratiam.
paras.en: [[72:23|I am become as a beast before thee|Ut jumentum factus sum apud te]]: that is, compared with thy wisdom I seem rather an irrational animal than a rational creature. Or thus: [[72:23|I am become as a beast before thee|Ut jumentum factus sum apud te]], that is, I have put my back under thy yoke and obeyed thy commandments as readily as a beast of burden obeys its master, carrying his loads. [[72:23|and I am always with thee|Et ego semper tecum]]. For he who humbles himself before God and obeys him abides in him unceasingly through grace.

paras.t: Tenuisti manum dexteram meam : id est, per gratiam me consolidasti et sustentasti, quemadmodum sustentatur cujus dextera ab amico tenetur ; et in voluntate tua, id est in observatione præceptorum tuorum, vel secundum tuæ voluntatis beneplacitum, deduxisti me in via peregrinationis atque exsilii hujus, ducendo me per rectam viam ad felicitatem æternam ; et cum gloria, id est gloriose atque potenter, suscepisti me, uniendo me tibi per caritatem, quem ex ore diaboli et morte peccati rapuisti. Vel : Cum gloria, id est cœlesti beatitudine, suscepisti me, id est suscipies, transferendo me de via ad patriam, et de corpore mortis hujus ad incorruptibilem statum, præsertim in die judicii, quando mortale hoc induet immortalitatem.
paras.en: [[72:24|Thou hast held me by my right hand|Tenuisti manum dexteram meam]]: that is, by grace thou hast strengthened and upheld me, as one is upheld whose right hand is held by a friend; [[72:24|and by thy will|et in voluntate tua]], that is, in the keeping of thy commandments, or according to the good pleasure of thy will, [[72:24|thou hast conducted me|deduxisti me]] on the way of this pilgrimage and exile, leading me by the right way to eternal happiness; [[72:24|and with thy glory|et cum gloria]], that is, gloriously and mightily, [[72:24|thou hast received me|suscepisti me]], uniting me to thee by charity, whom thou didst snatch from the mouth of the devil and the death of sin. Or: [[72:24|with thy glory|Cum gloria]], that is, with heavenly blessedness, [[72:24|thou hast received me|suscepisti me]], that is, thou wilt receive me, bringing me over from the way to the fatherland [that is, from this life, the road of the pilgrim, to heaven, his true home], and [[Rom 7:24|from the body of this death|de corpore mortis hujus]] to the incorruptible state, above all on the day of judgement, [[1 Cor 15:54|when this mortal hath put on immortality|quando mortale hoc induet immortalitatem]][[1 Cor 15:53||]].

paras.t: Quid enim mihi est in cœlo, et a te quid volui super terram? id est, nihil requiro a te nisi te ipsum, nec in aliqua creatura cœlesti sive terrestri spem meam constituo, aut felicitatem repono ; sed tu mihi objectum et causa es fidei, spei, caritatis, et felicitatis. Omnia arbitror ut stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciam. Insufficiens et angusta est mihi omnis creatura, te Creatorem super omnia diligenti, nec satiare potest affectum meum bonum finitum ; sed tu, Deus æterne, qui es bonitas infinita et veritas incircumscripta, solus quietare, implere et beatificare potes intellectum meum atque affectum.
paras.en: [[72:25|For what have I in heaven? and besides thee what do I desire upon earth?|Quid enim mihi est in cœlo, et a te quid volui super terram?]] That is, I ask nothing of thee but thyself, nor do I set my hope or place my happiness in any creature of heaven or earth; but thou art to me the object and the cause of faith, hope, charity and happiness. I count all things [[Phil 3:8|as dung, that I may gain Christ|ut stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciam]]. Every creature is insufficient and narrow for me, who love thee the Creator above all things, nor can a finite good satisfy my affection; but thou, eternal God, who art infinite goodness and uncircumscribed truth, thou alone canst quiet, fill and make blessed my understanding and my affection.

paras.t: Defecit caro mea, id est appetitus inferior, et cor meum, id est appetitus superior, in contemplatione ac dilectione summi boni, et beatitudinis mihi a Deo meo paratæ, quoniam oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt, quæ præparavit Deus diligentibus se. Deus cordis mei, id est amor animæ meæ, summum bonum ipsius, et Deus totius beatitudinis suæ. Quod enim quis maxime colit ac diligit, hoc est Deus ipsius. Et pars mea Deus in æternum : id est, Deus est illud bonum, quod ego ex omnibus bonis elegi, præ universis rebus dilexi, cui semper adhærere intendo, quoniam ipse solus sufficit mihi, quia in ipso omnium bonorum, pulchrorum, ac desiderabilium plenitudinem invenio. Unde et Isaias hoc bono contentus, ait : Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ. Anima mea desideravit te. Et alia scriptura : Qui diligunt te, Domine, sicut sol in ortu suo splendet, ita rutilent.
paras.en: [[72:26|my flesh|Defecit caro mea]], that is, the lower appetite, [[72:26|and my heart hath fainted away|et cor meum]], that is, the higher appetite, in the contemplation and love of the highest good and of the blessedness prepared for me by my God, since [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man, what things God hath prepared for them that love him|oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt, quæ præparavit Deus diligentibus se]][[Is 64:4||]]. [[72:26|thou art the God of my heart|Deus cordis mei]], that is, the love of my soul, its highest good, and the God of all its blessedness. For what a man most worships and loves, that is his God. [[72:26|and the God that is my portion for ever|Et pars mea Deus in æternum]]: that is, God is that good which I have chosen out of all goods and loved before all things, to which I mean always to cleave, since he alone suffices me, because in him I find the fullness of all good, beautiful and desirable things. Hence Isaias too, content with this good, says: [[Is 26:8|thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul|Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ]]. [[Is 26:9|My soul hath desired thee|Anima mea desideravit te]]. And another scripture: [[Judg 5:31|let them that love thee shine, as the sun shineth in his rising|Qui diligunt te, Domine, sicut sol in ortu suo splendet, ita rutilent]].

paras.t: Quia ecce qui elongant se per peccatum mortale a te, omnium salvatore, peribunt, quoniam ibunt in ignem æternum. Perdidisti omnes qui fornicantur abs te : id est, in præsenti perdis, eis gratiam subtrahendo, et in futuro perdes, a gloria repellendo, omnes qui adulterinis et pessimis cogitationibus a te recedunt, et rebus caducis inhærent. Est enim quædam fornicatio spiritualis, qua anima summæ Trinitatis imagine insignita, quæ esse deberet sui Creatoris filia, Christique sponsa, Deo suo infidelis efficitur, et creaturis potius quam Creatori innititur, delectatur, et fruitur. Sic fornicantes a Deo, conteruntur, sicut scriptum est : Contrivi cor eorum fornicans et recedens a me, dicit Dominus. Et iterum : Noli lætari, Israel, quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo.
paras.en: [[72:27|For behold they that go far|Quia ecce qui elongant se]] by mortal sin [[72:27|from thee|a te]], the Saviour of all, [[72:27|shall perish|peribunt]], since they shall go [[Matt 25:41|into everlasting fire|in ignem æternum]]. [[72:27|thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee|Perdidisti omnes qui fornicantur abs te]] [literally 'who commit fornication away from thee']: that is, in the present thou destroyest them by withdrawing grace from them, and in the future thou wilt destroy them by driving them back from glory, all who depart from thee by adulterous and most wicked thoughts and cleave to perishable things. For there is a kind of spiritual fornication, by which the soul, marked with the image of the most high Trinity, which ought to be the daughter of its Creator and the bride of Christ, becomes unfaithful to its God, and leans on, delights in and enjoys creatures rather than the Creator. Those who thus commit fornication away from God are broken, as it is written: [[Ezech 6:9|I have broken their heart that was faithless, and revolted from me|Contrivi cor eorum fornicans et recedens a me]], saith the Lord. And again: [[Osee 9:1|Rejoice not, O Israel|Noli lætari, Israel]], [[Osee 9:1|for thou hast committed fornication against thy God|quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo]].

paras.t: Mihi autem adhærere Deo per caritatem et humilem servitutem, bonum est, imo optimum, saluberrimum, atque dignissimum. Summa namque nobilitas mentis creatæ, est conversio ejus ad Deum. Ponere in Domino Deo spem meam, bonum est mihi. Hinc etenim Sponsa ait : Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus. Et Christus in Evangelio : Unum, inquit, est necessarium.
paras.en: [[72:28|But it is good for me to adhere to my God|Mihi autem adhærere Deo]] by charity and humble service: [[72:28|good|bonum est]] indeed, nay, best, most wholesome and most worthy. For the highest nobility of a created mind is its turning to God. [[72:28|to put my hope in the Lord God|Ponere in Domino Deo spem meam]] is good for me. For hence the Bride says: [[Cant 7:10|I to my beloved, and his turning is towards me|Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus]] [the margin gives Cant. viii, 10; the words are Cant 7:10]. And Christ in the Gospel: [[Luke 10:42|one thing|Unum]], he says, [[Luke 10:42|is necessary|est necessarium]].

paras.t: Ut annuntiem aliis, vel per me decantem ad gloriam nominis tui, omnes prædicationes tuas in sacra Scriptura contentas, vel mihi divinitus inspiratas, in portis filiæ Sion, id est in Ecclesiis militantibus, quæ sunt filiæ Sion, id est cœlestis Jerusalem, quæ est mater nostra : multæ autem sunt particulares Ecclesiæ, id est congregationes fidelium. Porro secundum venerandum Hugonem, septem sunt genera prædicandorum, quæ designantur hoc versu : Sacra, fides, virtus, vitium, laus, præmia, pœnæ. Prædicanda sunt enim sacra, id est septem sacramenta Ecclesiæ ; fides, id est duodecim articuli fidei ; virtus, id est virtutes theologicæ, morales et intellectuales, quatenus acquirantur ; vitium, id est peccata mortalia, ut vitentur ; laus, id est præconia, exempla, et vita Christi atque Sanctorum ; præmia quoque electorum, et pœnæ reproborum.
paras.en: [[72:28|That I may declare|Ut annuntiem]] to others, or sing by myself to the glory of thy name, [[72:28|all thy praises|omnes prædicationes tuas]] [Latin *prædicationes*, which also means 'preachings'] contained in Holy Scripture or inspired in me by God, [[72:28|in the gates of the daughter of Sion|in portis filiæ Sion]], that is, in the Churches militant, which are daughters of Sion, that is, of the heavenly Jerusalem, which is our mother: for there are many particular Churches, that is, congregations of the faithful. Further, according to the venerable Hugh, there are seven kinds of things to be preached, which are signified by this verse: *Sacra, fides, virtus, vitium, laus, præmia, pœnæ* [holy things, faith, virtue, vice, praise, rewards, punishments]. For there are to be preached holy things, that is, the seven sacraments of the Church; faith, that is, the twelve articles of the faith; virtue, that is, the theological, moral and intellectual virtues, that they may be acquired; vice, that is, mortal sins, that they may be avoided; praise, that is, the praises, the examples and the life of Christ and the Saints; and also the rewards of the elect and the punishments of the reprobate.

paras.t: Ecce completus est psalmus, omni laude dignissimus, qui devotarum est mentium maxime consolativus : in cujus exordio ponitur verbum omni dulcedine plenum, in cujus processu pulchre concionatur Propheta, et tandem concludit, quam vana ac fallax sit impiorum prosperitas, quam contemnenda sit divitiarum superfluitas. Nam (ut ait Hieronymus) continuus temporalium rerum successus, certum indicium est reprobationis æternæ. Et hæc gravissima ira Dei, quum permittit hominem temporaliter prosperari, nec eum castigat, sed in suis adinventionibus voluntatibusque relinquit. Ostendit insuper psalmus iste, quam certam et justam providentiam habeat Deus actuum humanorum. Copiose etiam manifestat, qualis sit vita hominis electi ac justi, videlicet, ut cor suum justificet, manus suas inter innocentes lavet, tota die flagelletur, atque in matutinis castigetur, cor habeat divino amore succensum, carnem mortificatam, et in propriis oculis nihil exsistat, insipientiam suam Domino humillime confiteatur, ejusque imperio instar pii jumenti in omnibus subjiciatur. Deinde beneficia gratiæ Dei commemorantur, et totus spiritualis profectus Deo adscribitur. Postremo anima Deum affectuosissime ac devotissime affatur, affirmans se extra Deum nihil appetere, Deum finaliter desiderare, in ejus dilectione et contemplatione prorsus deficere, vel quia non valet eum tam clare cognoscere, tamque ardenter diligere, sicut ipse cognoscibilis amabilisque consistit, vel quia ex fervidæ dilectionis excessu contemplationisque raptu infirmata sit corpore, et corde alienata a semetipsa. Ultimate etiam eligit, omnibus derelictis, Deo totaliter adhærere, atque in eo pure confidere : et hoc, non ob proprium præmium, cum reflexione ad se, sed ut omnes laudationes Dei pronuntiet. Cum multa igitur attentione pensemus et decantemus psalmum præsentem, quatenus omnis mundana prosperitas nobis vilescat, et illud unum quod solum est necessarium, summe complaceat, ametur, atque delectet.
paras.en: See, the psalm is finished, most worthy of all praise, and most consoling to devout minds: at its beginning is set a word full of all sweetness, in its course the Prophet preaches beautifully, and at length he concludes how vain and deceitful is the prosperity of the wicked, how contemptible the superfluity of riches. For (as Jerome says) an unbroken run of temporal success is a sure sign of eternal reprobation. And this is the heaviest anger of God, when he lets a man prosper in temporal things and does not chastise him, but leaves him in his own inventions and wills[[Ps 80:13||]]. This psalm shows besides how sure and just a providence God has over human acts. It also shows at length what the life of an elect and just man is: namely, that he justify his heart, wash his hands among the innocent, be scourged all the day and chastised in the mornings, have a heart kindled with divine love and the flesh mortified, be nothing in his own eyes, most humbly confess his foolishness to the Lord, and be subject to his rule in all things like a docile beast of burden. Then the benefits of God's grace are recalled, and all spiritual progress is ascribed to God. Lastly the soul speaks to God most affectionately and devoutly, declaring that it desires nothing outside God, that it desires God as its last end, that it altogether faints away in loving and contemplating him: either because it cannot know him as clearly, or love him as ardently, as he is knowable and lovable, or because through the excess of fervent love and the rapture of contemplation it is weakened in body and in heart estranged from itself. Finally too it chooses, leaving all things, to cleave wholly to God and to trust in him purely: and this not for its own reward, with a turning back upon itself, but that it may declare all the praises of God. Let us then weigh and sing the present psalm with great attention, so that all worldly prosperity may grow worthless to us, and that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]] may please, be loved and delight us supremely.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus cordis nostri, Deus pars nostra in æternum, te confortante in bonis agendis non deficiat caro et cor nostrum ; fac nos […]
paras.en: Prayer. God of our heart, God our portion for ever, by thy strengthening let not our flesh and our heart fail in doing good; make us […]

73.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI TERTII : UT QUID, DEUS, REPULISTI IN FINEM ?
73.title_en: Literal exposition of the seventy-third psalm: O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end?

paras.t: Explanandi jam psalmi titulus est : Intellectus Asaph. Asaph interpretatur congregatio : quæ in veteri lege dicebatur Synagoga, nunc vero vocatur Ecclesia. Secundum Hieronymum, psalmus iste ab Asaph compositus est, sicut et alii psalmi ab Asaph intitulati. Augustinus vero aliter sentit. Et ergo, secundum Augustinum, sensus tituli est : Intellectus Asaph : id est, in psalmo hoc agitur, quid Synagoga seu Ecclesia intelligit, scilicet, quod figuræ jam transierunt, atque per Christum impletæ sunt, et quod a Christo exspectare et quærere debemus, non temporalia, sed æterna. Porro secundum doctores catholicos, psalmus iste ad litteram loquitur de captivitate et destructione Judæorum, per Titum et ejus exercitum facta.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is: [[73:1|Understanding for Asaph|Intellectus Asaph]]. Asaph is interpreted *congregation*: which in the old law was called the Synagogue, but now is called the Church. According to Jerome, this psalm was composed by Asaph, as were the other psalms entitled with Asaph's name. Augustine, however, thinks otherwise. And so, according to Augustine, the sense of the title is: [[73:1|Understanding for Asaph|Intellectus Asaph]]: that is, in this psalm is treated what the Synagogue or the Church understands, namely, that the figures have now passed away and have been fulfilled through Christ, and that what we ought to expect and seek from Christ is not temporal things but eternal. Further, according to the Catholic doctors, this psalm speaks literally of the captivity and destruction of the Jews, brought about by Titus and his army.

paras.t: PROPHETA ergo, ut Dei misericordiam citius provocet, causam hujus destructionis regni et populi Hebræorum, per modum admirationis et condolentis inquirit, dicendo : Ut quid, Deus, repulisti terram et populum tuum a te ipso et tua protectione, tradendo eos in manus adversariorum, in finem, id est totaliter et usque ad finem mundi? Quidam vero exponunt hunc psalmum ad litteram de captivitate Babylonica : sed illa non duravit in finem ; imo Deus frequenter per Jeremiam dixit, se non dare eos in consummationem, sed velle reducere eos ad terram suam post septuaginta annos. Non igitur de illa captivitate, magis autem de ea in qua jam sunt, loquitur psalmus hic, quoniam ipsa durat usque in finem : quemadmodum apud Danielem habetur, Usque in finem perseverabit desolatio ; et alibi : Venit finis super populum meum Israel ; non adjiciam ultra ut pertranseam eum.
paras.en: The Prophet therefore, to move God's mercy the sooner, asks the cause of this destruction of the kingdom and people of the Hebrews, in the manner of one wondering and grieving with them, saying: [[73:1|O God, why hast thou cast us off|Ut quid, Deus, repulisti]], that is, thy land and thy people, from thyself and from thy protection, delivering them into the hands of their adversaries, [[73:1|unto the end|in finem]], that is, wholly, and even to the end of the world? Some, however, expound this psalm literally of the Babylonian captivity: but that did not last unto the end; on the contrary, God often said through Jeremias that he would not give them over to utter destruction, but would bring them back to their land after seventy years. It is not, then, of that captivity that this psalm speaks, but rather of the one in which they now are, since it lasts even unto the end: as is found in Daniel, [[Dan 9:27|the desolation shall continue even to the consummation, and to the end|Usque in finem perseverabit desolatio]]; and elsewhere: [[Amos 8:2|The end is come upon my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more|Venit finis super populum meum Israel ; non adjiciam ultra ut pertranseam eum]].

paras.t: Verumtamen quæstio oritur, quomodo Propheta Judæos illos incredulos et perversos, appellet in sequentibus, oves pascuæ Domini, et congregationem Dei. Et respondendum, quod eo modo dicuntur oves et congregatio Dei, quo Christus in Evangelio nuncupat eos filios regni : utpote, quoniam ex semine sanctorum Patriarcharum ac Prophetarum orti fuerunt, specialiterque a Deo vocati : quia Christus in Evangelio, Non sum, inquit, missus, nisi ad oves quæ perierunt, domus Israel. Vel dicuntur, oves pascuæ Dei, quoniam terram promissionis, lacte et melle manantem, præstitit eis, pavitque patres eorum pane cœlesti annis quadraginta in eremo.
paras.en: But a question arises: how can the Prophet, in what follows, call those unbelieving and perverse Jews the sheep of the Lord's pasture and the congregation of God? And the answer is that they are called the sheep and congregation of God in the way in which Christ in the Gospel names them children of the kingdom: namely, because they sprang from the seed of the holy Patriarchs and Prophets, and were specially called by God: for Christ in the Gospel says, [[Matt 15:24|I was not|Non sum]], he says, [[Matt 15:24|sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|missus, nisi ad oves quæ perierunt, domus Israel]] [the margin gives "Ibid. xv, 24", after a note on Amos; the words are those of Matt 15:24]. Or they are called the sheep of God's pasture because he gave them the land of promise, flowing with milk and honey[[Ex 3:8||]], and fed their fathers with bread from heaven for forty years in the desert[[Ex 16:35||]].

paras.t: Sive autem exponatur hic psalmus de captivitate facta per Romanos, sive per Babylonios, constat quod Judæi pro tunc pessimi erant. Tempore enim captivitatis Babylonicæ deos alienos adoraverunt ; tempore vero captivitatis a Tito inductæ, Christum occiderunt, et ob ejus occisionem vastati sunt : quod et Prophetam istum non latuit, quamvis per modum interrogantis exorsus sit. Orat tamen pro liberatione Judæorum a captivitate præsenti, illa potius qua spiritualiter capti sunt a dæmone, et vinculis infidelitatis obstinationisque irretiti, quam illa qua a terra sua expulsi sunt. Agnovit namque sanctus Propheta, tandem fore Judæos ad Christum convertendos. Variis enim temporibus quidam ex eis conversi sunt; sed generaliter non convertentur, nisi in fine sæculi. Quum etenim plenitudo gentium intraverit, tunc omnis Israel salvus erit, secundum Apostolum. De hac quoque vastatione Judæorum a Romanis, pulchre et clare prophetavit Balaam : Venient, inquit, in trieribus de Italia, superabunt Assyrios, vastabuntque Hebræos.
paras.en: Whether this psalm be expounded of the captivity brought about by the Romans or of that by the Babylonians, it is clear that the Jews were at that time very wicked. For at the time of the Babylonian captivity they adored strange gods; and at the time of the captivity brought on by Titus they had slain Christ, and for his slaying were laid waste: which was not hidden from this Prophet either, although he began in the manner of one asking. Yet he prays for the deliverance of the Jews from their present captivity: rather from that in which they have been taken captive spiritually by the devil and entangled in the bonds of unbelief and obstinacy, than from that by which they were driven out of their land. For the holy Prophet knew that the Jews would at length be converted to Christ. At various times, indeed, some of them have been converted; but generally they will not be converted until the end of the world. For when the fulness of the Gentiles has come in, then all Israel will be saved, according to the Apostle[[Rom 11:25||]][[Rom 11:26||]]. Of this laying waste of the Jews by the Romans Balaam also prophesied beautifully and clearly: [[Num 24:24|They shall come|Venient]], he says, [[Num 24:24|in galleys from Italy, they shall overcome the Assyrians, and shall waste the Hebrews|in trieribus de Italia, superabunt Assyrios, vastabuntque Hebræos]].

paras.t: Iratus est furor tuus super oves pascuæ tuæ, id est filios Israel : quia pervenit in eos ira Dei, secundum Apostolum. Et quoniam tam dire atque finaliter derelicti sunt, intus et foris privati omni gratia Dei, et propria terra, idcirco dicitur in eos furor Dei iratus. Adscribit autem divina Scriptura Deo furorem et iram, secundum quod alio loco scriptum habetur, Ulciscens Dominus et habens furorem : non quod in Deo sit aliqua passio aut immutatio recens seu inquietudo, sed propter similitudinem operis, quia per modum irati et furentis se habet, dum peccata nostra ulciscitur per pœnas horribiles. Quod autem Deo non competant vere et proprie passiones hujusmodi, ipse apud Jeremiam testatur : Numquid ad iracundiam me provocant? dicit Dominus; nonne semetipsos in confusione vultus sui?
paras.en: [[73:1|why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?|Iratus est furor tuus super oves pascuæ tuæ]] that is, against the children of Israel: for [[1 Thess 2:16|the wrath of God is come upon them|pervenit in eos ira Dei]], according to the Apostle. And since they have been so dreadfully and so finally forsaken, deprived within and without of all the grace of God and of their own land, therefore God's wrath is said to be enkindled against them. Now divine Scripture ascribes fury and wrath to God, as is written in another place, [[Nah 1:2|the Lord is a revenger, and hath wrath|Ulciscens Dominus et habens furorem]]: not that there is in God any passion, or any fresh change or disquiet, but because of the likeness of the work, since he acts in the manner of one angry and enraged when he avenges our sins with dreadful punishments. And that such passions do not truly and properly belong to God, he himself testifies in Jeremias: [[Jer 7:19|Do they provoke me to anger, saith the Lord? is it not themselves, to the confusion of their own countenance?|Numquid ad iracundiam me provocant? dicit Dominus; nonne semetipsos in confusione vultus sui?]]

paras.t: Memor esto, Domine, misericordiam impendendo, non aliquid cognoscendo de novo, congregationis tuæ, id est Synagogæ, quam possedisti tanquam populum peculiarem et electum, ab initio, quo patres eorum allocutus es, Abraham, Isaac et Jacob, promittens eis quod semen eorum esset populus tuus : prout Moyses ait, Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus, et elegit eos, amavitque semen eorum post eos. Orat ergo Propheta pro illuminatione Judæorum, commemorat quoque industriose pristina beneficia Dei, quatenus Deus reconcilietur facilius. Nam ad magnanimum pertinet, citius indulgere amico se offendenti, propter familiaritatem antiquam amicitiamque priorem. Subdit ergo:
paras.en: [[73:2|Remember|Memor esto]], O Lord, by bestowing mercy, not by coming to know anything anew, [[73:2|thy congregation|congregationis tuæ]], that is, the Synagogue, [[73:2|which thou hast possessed|quam possedisti]] as a peculiar and chosen people, [[73:2|from the beginning|ab initio]], when thou didst speak to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, promising them that their seed should be thy people: as Moyses says, [[Deut 10:15|the Lord hath been closely joined to thy fathers, and loved them and chose their seed after them|Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus, et elegit eos, amavitque semen eorum post eos]]. The Prophet therefore prays for the enlightenment of the Jews, and also carefully recalls God's former benefits, so that God may be the more easily reconciled. For it belongs to a magnanimous man to pardon the sooner a friend who offends him, because of their old familiarity and former friendship. He goes on therefore:

paras.t: Redemisti virgam hereditatis tuæ, id est virgam tuam hereditariam, utpote Israeliticam plebem : quæ dicitur virga, quia per eam correxisti peccatores in terra Chanaan habitantes, et quia ad similitudinem virgæ, recta fuit per justitiam legis, atque ad superiora erecta per fidem et contemplationem futurorum bonorum. Interdum equidem sacra Scriptura per virgam designat singularem personam : secundum quod de incomparabili atque Christifera virgine Maria apud Isaiam scriptum est, Egredietur virga de radice Jesse. Nunc vero per virgam significata est congregatio populi. Hanc Deus redemit de terra Ægypti et Babylonis, aliisque multis pressuris, ut patet in libris Judicum, Machabæorum, Esther et Judith. Quid autem sit virga hæc, subdit : mons Sion, id est Synagoga, ut sumatur locus pro locato, quia in monte Sion constructum erat templum. In quo habitasti in eo. In hoc monte habitavit Deus per gratiam specialem, ostendens in templo mirabilia sua, et in populo illo familiariter habitans, sicut per Moysen ait : Ego sum Dominus qui habito in medio filiorum Israel; et, Dominus Deus tuus ambulat in medio castrorum. Possumus quoque dicere, quod Deus Dei Unigenitus Christus homo, habitavit, id est, frequenter et satis diu aliquando fuit in templo seu monte isto, quemadmodum a Malachia prædictum est : Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator, quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis.
paras.en: [[73:2|thou hast redeemed|Redemisti]] [[73:2|The sceptre of thy inheritance|virgam hereditatis tuæ]] [Latin *virga*, "rod", where the Douay-Rheims has "sceptre"; Denis's gloss turns on the rod], that is, thy hereditary rod, namely the Israelite people: which is called a rod because through it thou didst chastise the sinners dwelling in the land of Chanaan, and because, like a rod, it was straight through the justice of the law, and raised up towards higher things through faith and the contemplation of the good things to come. Sometimes indeed sacred Scripture by a rod denotes a single person: as it is written in Isaias of the incomparable and Christ-bearing Virgin Mary, [[Is 11:1|there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse|Egredietur virga de radice Jesse]]. But here by the rod is signified the congregation of the people. This God redeemed from the land of Egypt and of Babylon, and from many other oppressions, as is plain in the books of Judges, of the Machabees, of Esther and of Judith. And what this rod is, he adds: [[73:2|mount Sion|mons Sion]], that is, the Synagogue, the place being taken for what is in the place, because the temple had been built on mount Sion. [[73:2|in which thou hast dwelt|In quo habitasti in eo]]. On this mountain God dwelt by a special grace, showing his wonders in the temple and dwelling familiarly among that people, as he says through Moyses: I am the Lord who dwell [[Ex 29:45|in the midst of the children of Israel|in medio filiorum Israel]] [Denis's wording, "I am the Lord who dwell", is closer to Num 35:34]; and, [[Deut 23:14|the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp|Dominus Deus tuus ambulat in medio castrorum]]. We can also say that God, the Only-begotten of God, Christ as man, dwelt, that is, was often and for a good while at times, in this temple or mountain, as was foretold by Malachias: [[Mal 3:1|presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple|Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator, quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis]].

paras.t: Leva manus tuas in superbias eorum in finem. Hoc communiter sancti doctores in bono accipiunt, ut sit oratio Prophetæ pro emendatione gentilium, Judæos hoc modo vastantium. Eritque sensus : Extende potentiam tuam in superbias eorum, videlicet Romanorum, exstinguendo in eis culpam, non gratiam; et ita destrue eos in finem, id est salubriter, quatenus per tuam correctionem vitam mereantur æternam. Litteræ tamen potius convenire videtur, ut intelligatur in malo, et sit oratio pro destructione Romani imperii, quantum ad exstinctionem gentilium imperatorum et populi infidelis, non autem in quantum Christo subjecti fuerunt. Et ita completum est tempore Constantini : nam ex tunc regnare cœpit in populo christiano.
paras.en: [[73:3|Lift up thy hands against their pride|Leva manus tuas in superbias eorum]] [[73:3|unto the end|in finem]]. The holy doctors commonly take this in a good sense, so that it is the Prophet's prayer for the amendment of the Gentiles who were laying waste the Jews in this way. And the sense will be: Stretch out thy power against their pride, that is, of the Romans, destroying in them the guilt, not the grace; and so destroy them unto the end, that is, unto salvation, so that through thy correction they may merit eternal life. Yet it seems to suit the letter better that it be understood in an evil sense, as a prayer for the destruction of the Roman empire, as regards the extinction of the heathen emperors and of the unbelieving people, but not in so far as they were subject to Christ. And so it was fulfilled in the time of Constantine: for from then on it [that is, the empire] began to reign among a Christian people.

paras.t: Quanta malignatus est, id est, quam multa opera mala fecit, inimicus, id est quilibet adversarius, seu Titus cum suis militibus, in sancto, id est monte Sion et in civitate sancta Jerusalem, quæ omnia a Romanis vastata sunt! Et dicitur Titus et ejus exercitus malignus seu malignatus, quoniam idololatriæ serviebant, vel quoniam Jerusalem et templum injusta intentione destruxerunt, non in ultionem sanguinis Christi, sed desiderio dominandi.
paras.en: [[73:3|see what things the enemy hath done wickedly|Quanta malignatus est]], that is, how many evil works he has done, [[73:3|the enemy|inimicus]], that is, any adversary, or Titus with his soldiers, [[73:3|in the sanctuary|in sancto]], that is, on mount Sion and in the holy city Jerusalem, all of which were laid waste by the Romans! And Titus and his army are called malignant or wicked-doing, because they served idolatry, or because they destroyed Jerusalem and the temple with an unjust intention, not to avenge the blood of Christ, but from the desire of dominion.

paras.t: Et gloriati sunt in malo et vitiis, qui oderunt te, scilicet prædicti idololatræ, in medio solennitatis tuæ, id est in medio templi, quod ingressi, dejecerunt cum risu et exsultatione. Vel, In medio solennitatis tuæ, id est in medio festivitatis paschalis. Nam quum Judæi in Jerusalem confluxissent ad celebrandum festivitatem paschalem, a Romanorum exercitu et Tito ac Vespasiano obsessi sunt. Posuerunt ipsi Romani signa sua, id est propria signa sive vexilla, quibus utebantur in præliis, utpote aquilas et dracones, signa, id est pro certo indicio victoriæ, expandentes sua vexilla super turres et muros Jerusalem pro signo triumphi ; et non cognoverunt verum Deum neque justitiam ejus, quoniam non pensabant Judæos hæc pati propter peccatum in Filium Dei commissum, sed propria potestate se prævalere opinabantur. Posuerunt autem signa sua, sicut in exitu belli fieri solet, super summum, id est super altiora loca, ut procul apparerent.
paras.en: And [[73:4|have made their boasts|Et gloriati sunt]] in evil and in vices [these words are not in the Vulgate text of the verse], [[73:4|they that hate thee|qui oderunt te]], namely the idolaters already mentioned, [[73:4|in the midst of thy solemnity|in medio solennitatis tuæ]], that is, in the midst of the temple, which they entered and threw down with laughter and exultation. Or, [[73:4|in the midst of thy solemnity|In medio solennitatis tuæ]], that is, in the midst of the paschal feast. For when the Jews had flocked together in Jerusalem to celebrate the paschal feast, they were besieged by the army of the Romans and by Titus and Vespasian. [[73:4|They have set up|Posuerunt]], the Romans themselves, [[73:4|their ensigns|signa sua]], that is, their own standards or banners, which they used in battle, such as eagles and dragons, [[73:4|for signs|signa]], that is, as a sure token of victory, spreading out their banners on the towers and walls of Jerusalem as a sign of triumph; [[73:5|And they knew not|et non cognoverunt]] the true God nor his justice, since they did not consider that the Jews suffered these things for the sin committed against the Son of God, but supposed that they prevailed by their own power. And they set up their ensigns, as is usually done [[73:5|in the going out|in exitu]] of a war, [[73:5|on the highest top|super summum]], that is, on the higher places, so that they might be seen from afar.

paras.t: Quasi in silva lignorum, id est, sicut in silvis ligna præscinduntur, sic ipsi securibus exciderunt et confregerunt januas ejus, scilicet templi et civitatis Jerusalem, in id ipsum, id est pari studio atque unanimi voluntate ; in securi et ascia, id est per talia instrumenta carpentatoria, dejecerunt eam, id est civitatem et domum Dei in ea fundatam. Incenderunt igni sanctuarium tuum, id est templum tibi dicatum, in terra Judææ : quod enim aliter non comminuerunt, flamma voravit. Unde Daniel induxit : Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo, et finis ejus vastitas. Polluerunt tabernaculum nominis tui : quia Romani prædictum templum ingressi sunt cum equis et feminis : quod in lege prohibitum fuit ; imo prohibuit lex gentiles et incircumcisos ingredi templum.
paras.en: As [[73:5|in a wood of trees|in silva lignorum]], that is, as trees are cut down in woods, so they [[73:5|with axes|securibus]] [[73:6|have cut down|exciderunt]] and broken [[73:6|the gates thereof|januas ejus]], that is, of the temple and of the city of Jerusalem, [[73:6|at once|in id ipsum]], that is, with equal zeal and one mind; [[73:6|with axe and hatchet|in securi et ascia]], that is, by such carpenter's tools, [[73:6|they have brought it down|dejecerunt eam]], that is, the city and the house of God founded in it. [[73:7|They have set fire to thy sanctuary|Incenderunt igni sanctuarium tuum]], that is, the temple dedicated to thee, [[73:7|on the earth|in terra]] of Judea: for what they did not break up otherwise, the flame devoured. Hence Daniel brought in: [[Dan 9:26|a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary: and the end thereof shall be waste|Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo, et finis ejus vastitas]]. [[73:7|they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name|Polluerunt tabernaculum nominis tui]]: for the Romans entered the said temple with horses and women: which was forbidden in the law; indeed the law forbade Gentiles and the uncircumcised to enter the temple[[Acts 21:28||]].

paras.t: Dixerunt in corde suo, cognatio eorum simul, id est, ipsi exsistentes generatio prava, cogitaverunt quod sequitur : Quiescere faciamus omnes dies festos Dei a terra, id est, omnem cultum Dei, quem isti colunt, impediamus, homines occidendo, et templum destruendo. Hoc dicebant Romani directe vel æquivalenter. Si enim non dixerunt hoc manifeste, tamen interpretative seu æquivalenter ita locuti sunt : nam ad destructionem civitatis ac templi, destructionemque populi, concomitabatur cessatio dierum festorum : et ergo unum intendendo, aliud quoque, saltem indirecte, intenderunt.
paras.en: [[73:8|They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together|Dixerunt in corde suo, cognatio eorum simul]], that is, being themselves a wicked generation, they thought what follows: [[73:8|Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land|Quiescere faciamus omnes dies festos Dei a terra]], that is, let us hinder all the worship of God which these people practise, by killing the men and destroying the temple. The Romans said this either directly or in effect. For if they did not say it openly, yet by implication, or in effect, they spoke so: for upon the destruction of the city and the temple, and the destruction of the people, there followed the cessation of the festival days: and so in intending the one they also intended the other, at least indirectly.

paras.t: Consequenter ponitur vox Judæorum in prædicta afflictione positorum, qui gemebunde ac querulose dixerunt : Signa nostra non vidimus. Tanquam dicerent : Ubi sunt jam mirabilia illa, quæ Deus fecit cum patribus nostris, quando de terra Ægypti eos eduxit, per mare Rubrum atque desertum deduxit, et in terram promissionis induxit, multotiesque eos redemit de potestate vastantium? Hoc etiam modo Gedeon dixisse scribitur. Nempe quum ei dixisset angelus, Dominus tecum, virorum fortissime, dixit Gedeon : Obsecro, Domine, si Dominus nobiscum est, cur apprehenderunt nos hæc mala? Ubi sunt mirabilia ejus, quæ narraverunt patres nostri? Jam non est Propheta, qui nos consoletur, et pro nobis Dominum deprecetur, nosque erudiat quid facere debeamus. Nam postquam Judæi Christum occiderunt, et ejus discipulos ejecerunt, nullum habuere Prophetam. Ex quo constat, quod psalmus iste non loquitur de captivitate Babylonica. Tunc enim Judæi habuerunt veros ac sanctos Prophetas, quia eodem tempore prophetavit Ezechiel in Babylone, et Jeremias in Judæa, secundum Hieronymum; dixitque uterque eorum Judæis, quid agere expediret, et de liberatione eos consolabantur : quemadmodum certum est intuenti libros Prophetarum istorum. Et nos non cognoscet amplius. Judæi tempore obsidionis a Tito, maximas fecerunt preces, jejunia et hostias, quatenus liberarentur divinitus. Quum autem nullum experirentur Dei auxilium, seque jam capiendos conspicerent, quasi desperantes locuti sunt : Nos non cognoscet amplius, id est, Deus de nobis jam non amplius curat, nec opera nostra acceptat, nec nos per approbationem cognoscit.
paras.en: Next is set down the voice of the Jews placed in the affliction just described, who said, groaning and complaining: [[73:9|Our signs we have not seen|Signa nostra non vidimus]]. As though they said: Where now are those wonders which God did with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt, led them through the Red Sea and the desert, and brought them into the land of promise, and many times redeemed them from the power of those who laid them waste? In this way too Gedeon is written to have spoken. For when the angel had said to him, [[Judg 6:12|The Lord is with thee, O most valiant of men|Dominus tecum, virorum fortissime]], Gedeon said: [[Judg 6:13|I beseech thee, my lord, if the Lord be with us, why have these evils fallen upon us? Where are his miracles, which our fathers have told us of|Obsecro, Domine, si Dominus nobiscum est, cur apprehenderunt nos hæc mala? Ubi sunt mirabilia ejus, quæ narraverunt patres nostri?]] [[73:9|there is now no prophet|Jam non est Propheta]] to comfort us, and to pray to the Lord for us, and to teach us what we ought to do. For after the Jews slew Christ and cast out his disciples, they had no Prophet. From which it is clear that this psalm does not speak of the Babylonian captivity. For then the Jews had true and holy Prophets, since at the same time Ezechiel prophesied in Babylon[[Ezech 1:1||]][[Ezech 1:3||]][[Ezech 3:15||]], and Jeremias in Judea[[Jer 1:2||]][[Jer 1:3||]], according to Jerome; and each of them told the Jews what it was expedient to do, and they comforted them about their deliverance: as is certain to anyone who looks into the books of these Prophets. [[73:9|and he will know us no more|Et nos non cognoscet amplius]]. The Jews, at the time of the siege by Titus, made very great prayers, fasts and sacrifices, that they might be delivered by God. But when they experienced no help from God, and saw that they were now about to be taken, they spoke as though despairing: [[73:9|he will know us no more|Nos non cognoscet amplius]], that is, God no longer cares for us, nor accepts our works, nor knows us with approval.

paras.t: Consequenter Propheta dilationem divinæ subventionis graviter ferens, Deumque ad misericordiam provocare desiderans, lamentabiliter ait : Usquequo, Deus, improperabit inimicus? id est, quamdiu nobis insultabit plebs ista Italiæ, et successores eorum, gloriantes de terræ nostræ destructione, de nostra expulsione et oppressione? Irritat adversarius nomen tuum in finem? id est, quamdiu gens infidelis te irritabit, nomen tuum blasphemans, et majestatem tuam despiciens? In hoc orat Propheta imperium Romanorum a gentilibus tolli, et verorum Israelitarum, id est Christianorum, dominio subjugari. Quidam exponunt hanc ultimam partem hujus versiculi, ut in eo reddatur causa quæstionis, quæ in prima parte præsentis versiculi ponitur. Interrogando enim dixit, Usquequo, Deus, improperabit inimicus? Et respondens, rationem assignat, dicendo : Irritat adversarius, etc. Tanquam dicat : Ideo tamdiu improperat inimicus noster nobis, quia irritat adversarius, id est, populus Judæorum Christo adversans, discredens et obstinatus, offendit et blasphemat nomen tuum, o Christe verax Deus, in finem, id est sine cessatione, et usque in finem mundi : ideo non liberabuntur a Christo, ut verificetur quod scriptum est, Non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est.
paras.en: Next the Prophet, taking the delay of God's help hard, and desiring to move God to mercy, says lamentingly: [[73:10|How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach|Usquequo, Deus, improperabit inimicus]]? that is, how long will this people of Italy, and their successors, insult us, glorying in the destruction of our land, in our expulsion and oppression? [[73:10|is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever|Irritat adversarius nomen tuum in finem]]? that is, how long will an unbelieving nation provoke thee, blaspheming thy name and despising thy majesty? In this the Prophet prays that the empire of the Romans be taken from the heathen and brought under the dominion of the true Israelites, that is, of the Christians. Some expound this last part of the verse so that it gives the reason for the question asked in the first part of the same verse. For asking, he said, [[73:10|How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach|Usquequo, Deus, improperabit inimicus]]? And answering, he gives the reason, saying: [[73:10|the adversary to provoke|Irritat adversarius]], etc. [the Latin can be read either as a question, "is the adversary to provoke…?", or as a statement, "the adversary provokes…"; this reading takes it as a statement]. As though he said: Our enemy reproaches us so long for this reason, because the adversary, that is, the people of the Jews, opposing Christ, unbelieving and obstinate, offends and blasphemes thy name, O Christ, true God, unto the end, that is, without ceasing, and even to the end of the world: therefore they will not be delivered by Christ, that what is written may be fulfilled, [[Dan 9:26|the people that shall deny him shall not be his|Non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est]].

paras.t: Ut quid avertis manum tuam, id est, subtrahis a nobis potestatis tuæ adjutorium, derelinquendo populum Judaicum in captivitate hac duplici, qua et propria terra privati sunt, et a dæmone ligati tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem? Cur etiam, Deus, avertis et dexteram tuam, id est pium ac prosperum tuæ adsistentiæ prospectum, conservationem atque favorem, de medio sinu tuo in finem? Loquitur sanctus Propheta de Deo more humano, quia dum homo non subvenit indigenti, dicitur manum suam in sinu reponere; dum vero auxiliatur, manum extrahere dicitur. Quoniam ergo Propheta intuebatur, Deum Judæos tam finaliter derelinquere, quærit cur in finem, id est in æternum, scilicet usque in terminum sæculi, manum suam ab eorum retrahat ope.
paras.en: [[73:11|Why dost thou turn away thy hand|Ut quid avertis manum tuam]], that is, why dost thou withdraw from us the help of thy power, leaving the Jewish people in this twofold captivity, in which they have both been deprived of their own land and are held bound by the devil at his will? Why also, O God, dost thou turn away [[73:11|and thy right hand|et dexteram tuam]], that is, the kindly and prosperous regard of thy assistance, thy preservation and favour, [[73:11|out of the midst of thy bosom for ever|de medio sinu tuo in finem]]? The holy Prophet speaks of God in human fashion, since when a man does not help one in need he is said to put his hand back in his bosom, but when he helps, he is said to draw out his hand. Since, then, the Prophet saw that God was forsaking the Jews so finally, he asks why he withdraws his hand from helping them unto the end, that is, for ever, namely until the close of the world.

paras.t: Deus autem rex noster ante sæcula, id est Deus verus, unus, æternus, ante omnia sæcula æternaliter manens, operatus est salutem in medio terræ : quia in terra Judææ constituit, conservavit, et salvavit patres nostros.
paras.en: [[73:12|But God is our king before ages|Deus autem rex noster ante sæcula]], that is, the true God, one, eternal, abiding eternally before all ages, [[73:12|he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth|operatus est salutem in medio terræ]]: for in the land of Judea he established, preserved and saved our fathers.

paras.t: Tu confirmasti in virtute tua mare. Ad litteram, Deus confirmavit mare Oceanum in loco suo, ne erumpat, et terram operiat, sicut ait Manasses rex Juda : Domine Deus, signasti mare verbo præcepti tui, qui conclusisti abyssum, et signasti terribili et laudabili nomini tuo, quod omnes pavent. Confirmavit quoque Dominus mare supernaturali firmitate, quando eduxit Israelem per fundum arenam maris Rubri, erantque Hebræis aquæ ex utraque parte pro muro.
paras.en: [[73:13|Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm|Tu confirmasti in virtute tua mare]]. Literally, God made the sea Ocean firm in its place, lest it break out and cover the earth, as Manasses king of Juda says: O Lord God, thou hast sealed the sea by the word of thy command, who hast shut up the deep, and sealed it with thy terrible and praiseworthy name, before which all tremble [the Prayer of Manasses, printed after the books of Paralipomenon in the Vulgate; not in the app's Bible]. The Lord also made the sea firm with a supernatural firmness when he led Israel out through the sandy bottom of the Red Sea, and the waters were to the Hebrews as a wall on either side[[Ex 14:22||]].

paras.t: Contribulasti capita draconum in aquis. Allegat atque commemorat hic Propheta quædam divina miracula antiquitus facta, quatenus manifestet quod Deus nunc quoque redimere possit filios Israel de captivitate præsenti, auferendo velamen de corde eorum, et eos ad christianæ veritatem fidei convertendo. Ad quod ostendendum, Contribulasti, inquit, capita draconum in aquis. Per dracones, intelligit tyrannicos principes ; per aquas autem, tribulationes seu pœnas. Unde Dominus ait ad Pharaonem : Et tu, Pharao, draco magne, qui cubas in medio fluminum tuorum. Est ig[…]
paras.en: [[73:13|thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters|Contribulasti capita draconum in aquis]]. Here the Prophet brings forward and recalls certain divine miracles done of old, to show that God can now also redeem the children of Israel from their present captivity, by taking away the veil from their heart[[2 Cor 3:16||]] and converting them to the truth of the Christian faith. To show this, [[73:13|thou didst crush|Contribulasti]], he says, [[73:13|the heads of the dragons in the waters|capita draconum in aquis]]. By the dragons he understands tyrannical princes; by the waters, tribulations or punishments. Hence the Lord says to Pharao: And thou, Pharao, [[Ezech 29:3|thou great dragon that liest in the midst of thy rivers|draco magne, qui cubas in medio fluminum tuorum]]. It is th[…] [the text breaks off here; the rest of the comment on vv. 13–15 and the beginning of that on v. 16 are missing from the source].

paras.t: […]hilum cœlos, et expandit illos sicut tabernaculum ad inhabitandum. Et omnia astra cœli cum sole, divino nutui parent in omnibus, juxta illud in libro Job : Præcipit soli, et non oritur, et stellas claudit quasi sub signaculo.
paras.en: […] the heavens as nothing, [[Is 40:22|and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in|et expandit illos sicut tabernaculum ad inhabitandum]] [the opening of this sentence is lost; the surviving words are those of Is 40:22]. And all the stars of heaven, with the sun, obey God's bidding in all things, according to that saying in the book of Job: [[Job 9:7|Who commandeth the sun, and it riseth not: and shutteth up the stars, as it were, under a seal|Præcipit soli, et non oritur, et stellas claudit quasi sub signaculo]].

paras.t: Tu fecisti omnes terminos terræ : secundum quod in Isaia scribitur, Deus sempiternus, qui creavit terminos terræ. Unde et ad beatum Job ait Creator omnipotens et sublimis : Ubi eras quando ponebam fundamenta terræ ? Indica mihi, si habes intelligentiam.
