Quis posuit mensuras ejus? aut quis tetendit super eam lineam ? aut super quo bases ejus solidatæ sunt ? Æstatem et ver, id est tempus æstivale atque vernale, tu plasmasti. Tempus enim quum sit causatum a motu primi mobilis, a Deo plasmatum est, sicut et primum mobile. Quatuor namque ponuntur coæquæva, id est simul creata, videlicet : angelus, cœlum, tempus, materia.
paras.en: [[73:17|Thou hast made all the borders of the earth|Tu fecisti omnes terminos terræ]]: as is written in Isaias, [[Is 40:28|the everlasting God, who hath created the ends of the earth|Deus sempiternus, qui creavit terminos terræ]]. Hence also the almighty and most high Creator says to blessed Job: [[Job 38:4|Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? tell me if thou hast understanding|Ubi eras quando ponebam fundamenta terræ ? Indica mihi, si habes intelligentiam]]. [[Job 38:5|Who hath laid the measures thereof|Quis posuit mensuras ejus]]? [[Job 38:5|or who hath stretched the line upon it|aut quis tetendit super eam lineam]]? or [[Job 38:6|upon what are its bases grounded|super quo bases ejus solidatæ sunt]]? [[73:17|the summer and the spring|Æstatem et ver]], that is, the summer season and the spring, [[73:17|were formed by thee|tu plasmasti]]. For since time is caused by the motion of the first movable [that is, the outermost sphere, whose motion medieval cosmology held to measure all time], it was formed by God, as was the first movable itself. For four things are held to be coeval, that is, created together: the angel, the heaven, time, and matter.

paras.t: Memor esto hujus, o Domine : hujus, inquam, quod sequitur. Inimicus improperavit Domino : id est, tuus adversarius Titus idololatra, de quo dictum est supra, Quanta malignatus est inimicus in sancto! hic inimicus improperavit Domino, putans se virtute deorum suorum prævaluisse, nec Deum Israel populum Judæorum potuisse defendere. Hoc forsitan cogitavit, vel dixit. Et populus insipiens, id est exercitus Romanorum, veri Dei notitia carens, et idola colens, incitavit nomen tuum, id est, te offendit in obsidione et destructione Jerusalem, quia non recta intentione fecerunt hoc ; sed erant virga furoris Domini, sicut Assyrii et Babylonii, quorum omnium cor erat non ad corrigendum, sed conterendum, quemadmodum per Isaiam Dominus ait de rege Assyriorum : Væ Assur, virga furoris mei et baculus, ipse est. Ipse autem non sic arbitrabitur.
paras.en: [[73:18|Remember this|Memor esto hujus]], O Lord: this, I say, which follows. [[73:18|the enemy hath reproached the Lord|Inimicus improperavit Domino]]: that is, thy adversary Titus the idolater, of whom it was said above, [[73:3|see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary|Quanta malignatus est inimicus in sancto]]! this enemy reproached the Lord, thinking that he had prevailed by the power of his gods, and that the God of Israel had not been able to defend the people of the Jews. This perhaps he thought, or said. [[73:18|and a foolish people|Et populus insipiens]], that is, the army of the Romans, lacking knowledge of the true God and worshipping idols, [[73:18|hath provoked thy name|incitavit nomen tuum]], that is, offended thee in the siege and destruction of Jerusalem, because they did not do this with a right intention; but they were the rod of the Lord's fury, like the Assyrians and Babylonians, whose heart was set not on correcting but on crushing, as the Lord says through Isaias of the king of the Assyrians: [[Is 10:5|Woe to the Assyrian, he is the rod and the staff of my anger|Væ Assur, virga furoris mei et baculus, ipse est]]. [[Is 10:7|But he shall not take it so|Ipse autem non sic arbitrabitur]].

paras.t: Ne tradas bestiis, id est dæmonibus, tyrannis, crudelibusve hominibus, animam confitentem tibi, id est hominem sua peccata et tua præconia recolentem. Ponit enim partem, scilicet animam, pro toto homine. Et animas pauperum tuorum, id est abjectorum et egenorum, ne obliviscaris in finem, deserendo eos in opportunitate et tribulatione, ac si non pertinerent ad te. Orat ergo ad litteram Propheta pro liberatione populi Israel, ut eruatur a morte peccatis et captivitate diaboli.
paras.en: [[73:19|Deliver not up to beasts|Ne tradas bestiis]], that is, to devils, tyrants, or cruel men, [[73:19|the souls that confess to thee|animam confitentem tibi]] [Denis reads the singular, "the soul that confesseth to thee"], that is, the man who calls to mind his own sins and thy praises. For he puts the part, namely the soul, for the whole man. And [[73:19|the souls of thy poor|Et animas pauperum tuorum]], that is, of the outcast and the needy, [[73:19|forget not to the end|ne obliviscaris in finem]], forsaking them in their need and tribulation, as if they did not belong to thee. The Prophet therefore prays literally for the deliverance of the people of Israel, that it may be rescued from the death of sin and from the captivity of the devil.

paras.t: Respice in testamentum tuum : id est, legem a te datam, et testimonia ejus adverte, quia in ea promittis ignoscere pauperibus tuis ; et ut magis exaudire digneris, attende malignitatem inimicorum tuorum ; quia repleti sunt, qui obscurati sunt, terræ domibus iniquitatum : id est, prædicti Italici, in malis suæ infidelitatis interius obtenebrati, ditati sunt et repleti terræ domibus iniquitatum, id est divitiis terrenis atque injustis : de quibus ait Salvator, Facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis.
paras.en: [[73:20|Have regard to thy covenant|Respice in testamentum tuum]] [Latin *testamentum*, "testament", which Denis takes as the law]: that is, look upon the law given by thee and its testimonies, for in it thou dost promise to pardon thy poor[[Is 66:2||]]; and that thou mayest be the more pleased to hear, consider the malice of thy enemies; [[73:20|for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity|quia repleti sunt, qui obscurati sunt, terræ domibus iniquitatum]]: that is, the said Italians, darkened inwardly in the evils of their unbelief, have been enriched and filled with the dwellings of iniquity of the earth, that is, with earthly and unjust riches: of which the Saviour says, [[Luke 16:9|Make unto you friends of the mammon of iniquity|Facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis]].

paras.t: Ne avertatur a gratia tuæ misericordiæ humilis factus confusus, id est populus Judæorum per captivitatem præsentem multum humiliatus ; pauper et inops spiritu laudabunt nomen tuum cum magno fervore et exsultatione ingenti : quemadmodum Baruch dicit : Non mortui in inferno dabunt honorem Domino ; sed anima quæ tristis est super magnitudine mali, et incedit curva et infirma, dat gloriam et justitiam tibi Domino.
paras.en: [[73:21|Let not the humble be turned away|Ne avertatur]] from the grace of thy mercy, [[73:21|with confusion|humilis factus confusus]] [the Latin runs "let not him who is made humble and confounded be turned away from the grace of thy mercy"], that is, the people of the Jews, greatly humbled through the present captivity; [[73:21|the poor and needy|pauper et inops]] in spirit [[73:21|shall praise thy name|laudabunt nomen tuum]] with great fervour and immense exultation: as Baruch says: [[Bar 2:17|the dead that are in hell|Non mortui in inferno]] [[Bar 2:17|shall not give glory and justice to the Lord|dabunt honorem Domino]] [Denis has "shall not give honour to the Lord"]; [[Bar 2:18|But the soul that is sorrowful for the greatness of evil she hath done, and goeth bowed down, and feeble|sed anima quæ tristis est super magnitudine mali, et incedit curva et infirma]], [[Bar 2:18|giveth glory and justice to thee the Lord|dat gloriam et justitiam tibi Domino]].

paras.t: Exsurge, Deus, non locum mutando, sed fortiter succurrendo, judica causam tuam, quam habes contra adversarios tuos, et ei qui justam habet causam, præsta victoriam ; memor esto improperiorum tuorum, id est famulis tuis inflictorum, vel blasphemiarum nominis tui ; eorum, inquam, improperiorum, quæ ab insipiente sunt tota die : quoniam populus Romanus insipiens, multa dixit contra Deum in obsidione prædicta. Horum improperiorum orat Propheta Deum reminisci, quatenus ponat Judæis hanc pœnam temporalis dejectionis et oppressionis pro peccato eorum, et convertantur ; et non arguat eos secundum rigorem justitiæ suæ, subtrahendo eis gratiam in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro. Propter quod subdit :
paras.en: [[73:22|Arise, O God|Exsurge, Deus]], not by changing place, but by mightily coming to help, [[73:22|judge thy own cause|judica causam tuam]], which thou hast against thy adversaries, and give the victory to him who has the just cause; [[73:22|remember thy reproaches|memor esto improperiorum tuorum]], that is, those inflicted on thy servants, or the blasphemies against thy name; those reproaches, I say, [[73:22|with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day|quæ ab insipiente sunt tota die]]: since the foolish Roman people said many things against God in the said siege. The Prophet prays God to remember these reproaches, so that he may lay upon the Jews this punishment of temporal overthrow and oppression for their sin, and they may be converted; and that he may not rebuke them according to the rigour of his justice, withdrawing from them grace in the present and glory in the future. Wherefore he adds:

paras.t: Ne obliviscaris voces inimicorum tuorum : id est, verba iniqua eorum recordare, quatenus hac occasione pareas populo Israel sic afflicto. Superbia eorum qui te oderunt, ascendit semper : primo, quoniam peccatis peccata adjiciunt, juxta illud, Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum ; et in Apocalypsi, Qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc, et qui justus est, justificetur adhuc. Secundo, quoniam elatio superborum tendit ad alta. Propter quod Isaias dicit : Quum fureres adversum me, superbia tua ascendit in aures meas, dicit Dominus.
paras.en: [[73:23|Forget not the voices of thy enemies|Ne obliviscaris voces inimicorum tuorum]]: that is, remember their wicked words, so that on this occasion thou mayest spare the people of Israel thus afflicted. [[73:23|the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually|Superbia eorum qui te oderunt, ascendit semper]]: first, because they add sins to sins, according to that saying, [[Ecclus 3:29|the sinner will add sin to sin|Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum]] [the margin gives Ecclus. iii, 20; the words are those of Ecclus 3:29]; and in the Apocalypse, [[Apoc 22:11|he that is filthy, let him be filthy still: and he that is just, let him be justified still|Qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc, et qui justus est, justificetur adhuc]]. Secondly, because the haughtiness of the proud tends towards high things. Wherefore Isaias says: [[Is 37:29|When thou wast mad against me, thy pride came up to my ears|Quum fureres adversum me, superbia tua ascendit in aures meas]], saith the Lord [the margin gives Is. xxxvii, 24; the words are those of Is 37:29].

73.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI TERTII.
73.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same seventy-third psalm.

paras.t: Secundum intelligentiam autem moralem, loquitur Propheta in psalmo præsenti in persona Ecclesiæ, seu cujuslibet hominis fraterna caritate ardentis, atque pro reformatione populi christiani orantis. Ecclesia ergo seu homo virtutis, persecutionem, lapsum et dejectionem Christianorum cum magna compassione prospiciens, Dominum affectuosissime alloquatur, deprecetur, et dicat : Ut quid, Deus Trinitas, Deus gloriose, benedicte et felix, ut quid, id est, qua utilitate et causa, repulisti populum christianum, exponendo eum tantis miseriis, tantis impugnationibus hæreticorum, schismaticorum et infidelium, imo et falsorum fratrum, qui fide sunt christiani, sed opere diabolici : et hoc, in finem, id est tam perseveranter? Præcipue autem dicere possumus hæc propter amissionem sepulcri Christi, et Terræ sanctæ ac urbis Jerusalem.
paras.en: Now according to the moral understanding, the Prophet speaks in the present psalm in the person of the Church, or of any man burning with brotherly charity and praying for the reform of the Christian people. Let the Church, then, or a man of virtue, beholding with great compassion the persecution, the fall and the casting down of Christians, address the Lord most lovingly, entreat him, and say: [[73:1|O God, why|Ut quid, Deus]] O Trinity, O glorious God, blessed and happy, why, that is, for what profit and cause, [[73:1|hast thou cast|repulisti]] off the Christian people, exposing it to so many miseries, to so many assaults of heretics, schismatics and unbelievers, and even of false brethren, who are Christians by faith but devilish in deed: and this [[73:1|unto the end|in finem]], that is, so perseveringly? And we can say this above all on account of the loss of Christ's sepulchre, and of the Holy Land and the city of Jerusalem.

paras.t: Iratus est furor tuus super oves pascuæ tuæ : id est, grandem ultionem exerces contra populum tuum christianum, quem ita sinis opprimi, tentari, affligi et fatigari incursu visibilium invisibiliumque inimicorum, ita ut terras Christianorum jam possideant infideles, corda vero seu animas plurimorum peccata et dæmones. Denique industriosum, pulchrum, et efficax genus orationis est, in ipsa prece ea includere, ex quibus rationabile, et quodammodo debitum est, eum qui oratur, mitigari et exaudire. Omnino autem decens videtur, ut Dominus populo sibi peculiari, et multis beneficiis a se honorato faciliter reconcilietur : idcirco Ecclesia seu homo fidelis pro aliis deprecans Christianis, asserit Christianos esse oves pascuæ Dei : quod est verbum amorosum, fiduciale, familiare atque dulcissimum ; et convenit hoc Christianis multo perfectius quam Judæis. Illi enim pasti sunt manna ; nos autem corpore et sanguine Christi, figuratis per manna, quotidie pascimur, multiformi gratia tanti sacramenti reficimur, Christo incorporamur, et nisi in nobis defectus sit, spiritualiter impinguamur, ditamur, perficimur. Corpus enim Christi est vere frumentum electorum, et sanguis ejus est vere vinum germinans virgines, id est animas castas, Christique sponsas. De quo frumento et vino in Zacharia scriptum est : Quid bonum Domini, aut quid pulchrum ejus, nisi frumentum electorum, et vinum germinans virgines?
paras.en: [[73:1|why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?|Iratus est furor tuus super oves pascuæ tuæ]] that is, thou art taking great vengeance on thy Christian people, which thou dost suffer to be so oppressed, tempted, afflicted and wearied by the onset of enemies visible and invisible, that unbelievers now possess the lands of the Christians, and sins and demons the hearts or souls of very many. Further, it is a skilful, beautiful and effective kind of prayer to include in the very petition those things which make it reasonable, and in a manner due, that the one entreated should be appeased and should hear. And it seems altogether fitting that the Lord should be readily reconciled to a people peculiarly his own and honoured by him with many benefits: therefore the Church, or a faithful man praying for other Christians, declares that Christians are the [[73:1|sheep of thy pasture|oves pascuæ]] of God; which is a loving word, trustful, familiar and most sweet; and it fits Christians far more perfectly than the Jews. For they were fed with manna[[Ex 16:15||]][[John 6:49||]] [the margin gives Exod. xvi, 15 and John vi, 48–59]; but we are fed daily with the body and blood of Christ, which the manna prefigured; we are refreshed by the manifold grace of so great a sacrament, we are incorporated into Christ, and, unless the fault be in us, we are spiritually fattened, enriched and made perfect. For the body of Christ is truly the corn of the elect, and his blood is truly the wine springing forth virgins, that is, chaste souls and brides of Christ. Of which corn and wine it is written in Zacharias: [[Zach 9:17|what is the good thing|Quid bonum Domini]] of the Lord, [[Zach 9:17|and what is his beautiful thing, but the corn of the elect, and wine springing forth virgins?|aut quid pulchrum ejus, nisi frumentum electorum, et vinum germinans virgines?]]

paras.t: Memor esto, o rex Christe, mundi Salvator, congregationis tuæ, id est universalis Ecclesiæ, eam ubique terrarum reparando, protegendo, augendo, atque salvando ; quam possedisti per gratiam baptismalem et beatissimam passionem hereditario jure, sicut superius Pater ait ad te : Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam. Hanc autem congregationem possedisti ab initio primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quia ex tunc crediderunt quotquot præordinati erant ad vitam æternam. Et ut ait Apostolus. Firmum fundamentum Dei stat, habens signaculum hoc : Cognovit Dominus qui sunt ejus. Vel dicitur Deus possedisse Ecclesiam ab initio, id est ab æterno, secundum rationem prædestinationis divinæ, secundum quam ab æterno eam dilexit. Christus quoque eam hoc modo ab æterno possedit, in quantum Deus (secundum Apostolum) nos in Christo ab æterno elegit et gratificavit, universaque gratiæ dona in ipso nobis dare decrevit, imo et dedit, secundum Apostolum : Deus (inquit) vocavit nos vocatione sua sancta, non secundum opera nostra, sed secundum propositum suum et gratiam, quæ data est nobis in Christo Jesu ante tempora sæcularia ; manifestata est autem nunc. Verumtamen datio illa ante tempora sæcularia, secundum prædestinationem divinam, non secundum actualem infusionem, sumenda est.
paras.en: [[73:2|Remember|Memor esto]], O Christ the King, Saviour of the world, [[73:2|thy congregation|congregationis tuæ]], that is, the universal Church, restoring it, protecting it, increasing it and saving it in every land; [[73:2|which thou hast possessed|quam possedisti]] by baptismal grace and by thy most blessed passion, by right of inheritance, as the Father said to thee above: [[Ps 2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance|Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam]]. And this congregation thou hast possessed [[73:2|from the beginning|ab initio]] of the primitive Church, because from then on [[Acts 13:48|as many as were ordained to life everlasting believed|crediderunt quotquot præordinati erant ad vitam æternam]]. And as the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:19|the sure foundation of God standeth firm, having this seal: the Lord knoweth who are his|Firmum fundamentum Dei stat, habens signaculum hoc : Cognovit Dominus qui sunt ejus]]. Or God is said to have possessed the Church from the beginning, that is, from eternity, by way of the divine predestination, according to which he loved it from eternity. Christ too possessed it in this way from eternity, inasmuch as God (according to the Apostle) chose us in Christ from eternity and graced us[[Eph 1:4||]][[Eph 1:6||]], and decreed to give us all the gifts of grace in him, nay more, gave them, according to the Apostle: God (he says) [[2 Tim 1:9|called us by his holy calling, not according to our own works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the times of the world|vocavit nos vocatione sua sancta, non secundum opera nostra, sed secundum propositum suum et gratiam, quæ data est nobis in Christo Jesu ante tempora sæcularia]]; [[2 Tim 1:10|But is now made manifest|manifestata est autem nunc]]. Yet that giving before the times of the world is to be understood according to the divine predestination, not according to actual infusion.

paras.t: Redemisti virgam hereditatis tuæ, id est populum christianum ad divina erectum, qui est genus regium et sacerdotale, de spirituali Ægypto, id est de conversatione mundana, vitiosa ac tenebrosa, de multis erroribus, cunctis peccatis, infernique pœnis : et hoc, pretiosissimo pretio, utpote sanguine proprio. Unde in Apocalypsi scriptum est : Dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo, et fecit nos regnum et sacerdotes Deo et Patri suo. Et Petrus in sua Canonica : Non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis, sed pretioso sanguine quasi Agni immaculati. Propter quod ipsemet Christus protestatur : Ego sum pastor bonus, et agnosco oves meas ; et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Hæc autem congregatio tua, est mons Sion, id est Ecclesia militans, Deum fideliter speculans, in quo monte habitasti corporaliter visibiliterque in eo, quando in terris visus es, et inter discipulos conversatus. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Christus tanquam filius in domo sua, quæ domus sumus nos. Nunc quoque et usque in finem mundi habitat Christus in nobis, sicut ipse ait : Ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus ; et rursus, Ubi fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio eorum sum. Sion autem speculatio interpretatur : idcirco per eam Ecclesia designatur, in cujus persona ait Apostolus : Nos revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes.
paras.en: [[73:2|thou hast redeemed|Redemisti]] [[73:2|sceptre of thy inheritance|virgam hereditatis tuæ]] [the Latin *virga* is a rod or staff, here taken as the people raised upright towards divine things], that is, the Christian people raised up towards divine things, which is a kingly and priestly race[[1 Pet 2:9||]], from the spiritual Egypt, that is, from a worldly, vicious and darksome way of life, from many errors, from all sins and from the pains of hell: and this at the most precious price, namely his own blood. Hence it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:5|who hath loved us and washed us from our sins in his own blood|Dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo]], [[Apoc 1:6|And hath made us a kingdom, and priests to God and his Father|et fecit nos regnum et sacerdotes Deo et Patri suo]]. And Peter in his canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 1:18|not redeemed with corruptible things, as gold or silver, from your vain conversation of the tradition of your fathers|Non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis]], [[1 Pet 1:19|But with the precious blood|sed pretioso sanguine]] [[1 Pet 1:19|as of a lamb unspotted|quasi Agni immaculati]]. For which reason Christ himself declares: [[John 10:14|I am the good shepherd: and I know mine|Ego sum pastor bonus, et agnosco oves meas]]; [[John 10:15|and I lay down my life for my sheep|et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]. And this thy congregation is [[73:2|mount Sion|mons Sion]], that is, the Church militant, faithfully contemplating God, [[73:2|in which thou hast dwelt|in quo monte habitasti]], bodily and visibly, when thou wast seen upon earth and didst converse among the disciples[[Bar 3:38||]]. For which reason the Apostle says: [[Heb 3:6|But Christ, as the Son in his own house: which house are we|Christus tanquam filius in domo sua, quæ domus sumus nos]]. Now too, and until the end of the world, Christ dwells in us, as he himself says: [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days|Ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus]]; and again: [[Matt 18:20|where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them|Ubi fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio eorum sum]]. Now Sion is interpreted *contemplation* [*speculatio*, a watching or looking out]: therefore the Church is signified by it, in whose person the Apostle says: we, [[2 Cor 3:18|beholding the glory of the Lord with open face|Nos revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes]].

paras.t: Leva manus tuas in superbias eorum in finem. Ecclesia Dei non est erudita a magistro suo Christo reddere malum pro malo, sed vincere in bono malum, orando pro æmulis. Ideo versus iste in bono exponendus est, ut sit sensus : Leva manus tuas, id est, potentiam tuam extende, in superbias eorum, scilicet inimicorum Ecclesiæ, persequentium justos, destruendo in eis non naturam, sed culpam ; vel in præsenti eos paternaliter ac misericorditer castigando, ne æternaliter pereant, sicut Apostolus tradidit illum Corinthium Satanæ in interitum carnis, quatenus spiritus salvus fieret in die Domini. Illa vero traditio aliud nihil erat, nisi excommunicatio : quam in primitiva Ecclesia concomitari solebat ad fidei confirmationem sensibile signum, scilicet corporalis vexatio excommunicati a dæmone, ad quam sequi sæpe solebat mors corporis ; sed nunc fide firmata, necessarium non est tale sensibile signum. Et quod ista sit expositio apta, liquet ex eo quod subditur, In finem, id est, in vitam æternam ac veram salutem ordina correctionem tuam, qua superbos flagellas.
paras.en: [[73:3|Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end|Leva manus tuas in superbias eorum in finem]]. The Church of God has not been taught by her master Christ to render evil for evil, but to overcome evil by good[[Rom 12:21||]], praying for her rivals[[Matt 5:44||]]. Therefore this verse is to be expounded in a good sense, so that the sense is: [[73:3|Lift up thy hands|Leva manus tuas]], that is, stretch forth thy power, [[73:3|against their pride|in superbias eorum]], namely of the enemies of the Church who persecute the just, destroying in them not their nature but their fault; or chastising them in this present life fatherly and mercifully, lest they perish eternally, as the Apostle delivered that Corinthian [[1 Cor 5:5|to Satan for the destruction of the flesh|Satanæ in interitum carnis]], so that [[1 Cor 5:5|the spirit may be saved in the day of our Lord|spiritus salvus fieret in die Domini]]. Now that delivering was nothing else than excommunication: which in the primitive Church used to be accompanied, for the confirming of the faith, by a sensible sign, namely the bodily harassing of the excommunicated man by a demon, which was often followed by the death of the body; but now that the faith is made firm, such a sensible sign is not needed. And that this is a fitting exposition is plain from what is added, [[73:3|unto the end|In finem]], that is, direct thy correction, with which thou scourgest the proud, to eternal life and true salvation.

paras.t: Quanta malignatus est inimicus in sancto! id est, quam magna mala fecit per suos successores Mahometus in Terra sancta, quæ ejus populo jam est subjecta! quemadmodum Christus in Evangelio prænunciavit : Jerusalem calcabitur a gentibus, donec impleantur tempora nationum. Vel, Quanta malignatus est inimicus, id est quilibet hæresiarcha, tyrannus aut perversus in sancto populo tuo, eum decipiendo, affligendo, aut occidendo! sicut de Arianis maxime patet, qui innumerabiles Christianos jugulaverunt : et imperatores Ariana perfidia intoxicati, innumeros incarceraverunt episcopos, prout in chronicis legitur.
paras.en: [[73:3|see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary|Quanta malignatus est inimicus in sancto!]]: that is, how great are the evils that Mahomet has done through his successors in the Holy Land, which is now subject to his people! as Christ foretold in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:24|Jerusalem shall be trodden down by the Gentiles till the times of the nations be fulfilled|Jerusalem calcabitur a gentibus, donec impleantur tempora nationum]]. Or: [[73:3|see what things the enemy hath done wickedly|Quanta malignatus est inimicus]], that is, any heresiarch, tyrant or wicked man, [[73:3|in the sanctuary|in sancto]], that is, among thy holy people, deceiving, afflicting or slaying them! as is most plain of the Arians, who butchered countless Christians; and emperors poisoned with the Arian perfidy imprisoned innumerable bishops, as we read in the chronicles.

paras.t: Et gloriati sunt, quum malefecerunt, et in rebus pessimis, qui oderunt te, scilicet prædicti maligni, et hoc, in medio solennitatis tuæ, quam ipsi frequenter violaverunt. Sæpe enim perversi in sacratioribus solennioribusque diebus deteriora opera faciunt, secundum quod dæmones corda eorum possidentes, inspirant. Posuerunt signa sua. Ariani hæretici circumferre solebant sua vexilla ad derisionem Catholicorum ; et multi tyranni Ecclesiam devastantes, ubertim erexerunt in signum victoriæ contra Christianos sua vexilla.
paras.en: They [[73:4|have made their boasts|Et gloriati sunt]] [[Prov 2:14|when they have done evil|quum malefecerunt]], and [[Prov 2:14|in the most wicked things|in rebus pessimis]] [these words are taken from Prov 2:14 and worked into the verse], [[73:4|they that hate thee|qui oderunt te]], namely the wicked men already mentioned; and this [[73:4|in the midst of thy solemnity|in medio solennitatis tuæ]], which they themselves have often violated. For wicked men often do worse deeds on the holier and more solemn days, as the demons who possess their hearts inspire them. [[73:4|They have set up their ensigns|Posuerunt signa sua]]. The Arian heretics used to carry their banners about in mockery of the Catholics; and many tyrants laying waste the Church set up their banners in abundance as a sign of victory over the Christians.

paras.t: Porro quod in tribus sequentibus versibus dicitur, tam sæpe ad litteram factum est Ecclesiæ Christi, secundum sensum in præcedenti articulo introductum, ut non sit necesse specialia commemorare exempla : præsertim quum nostris quoque temporibus talia (proh dolor!) abundantissime facta sint Ecclesiis, in regno Bohemiæ et terris ei vicinis, a detestandis ac nefandis regni illius hæreticis : quorum (exigentibus culpis nostris, atque divino permittente judicio) rabies multum nimis ac diu desævit ; sed jam de gratia Dei non parum repressa est, gladioque exstincta.
paras.en: Further, what is said in the three following verses [in the numbering used here, vv. 5–8] has so often been done to the Church of Christ according to the letter, in the sense brought in in the preceding article, that there is no need to recall particular examples: especially since in our own times too (alas!) such things have been done in great abundance to the churches in the kingdom of Bohemia and the lands near it, by the detestable and abominable heretics of that kingdom [that is, the Hussites]: whose fury (our sins requiring it, and the divine judgement permitting it) raged far too much and too long; but now, by the grace of God, it has been not a little checked, and put out by the sword.

paras.t: Sed quum Christifideles tot afficerentur flagellis, persecutionibus, fame, siti, ac mortibus, quid dicerent, nisi quod subditur? Signa nostra non vidimus : id est, tam admirabiles divinæ virtutis protectiones experti non sumus, nec experimur, quales interdum viderunt atque experti sunt patres nostri christianissimi, qui quum pauci essent, maximas infidelium multitudines dejecerunt, auxilio eis desuper condonato : ut patet de Theodosio religiosissimo, Carolo Magno, Godefrido de Bolonia, multisque aliis. Sed et ipsi Apostoli et successores eorum, sæpe angelica ope de carceribus, vinculis, et omni molestia incredulorum erepti noscuntur. Nunc autem nil tale nobis apparet : propterea sola patientia nobis necessaria est cum fide certissima ; dicendumque est nobis illud Machabæorum : Parati sumus magis mori, quam Dei leges prævaricari. Nec ideo frangi debemus, quia in præsenti occidi permittimur, scientes verum esse quod in eodem loco subjungitur : Rex mundi Deus defunctos nos pro suis legibus in æternæ vitæ resurrectione suscitabit. Unde et alibi scriptum est : Si coram hominibus tormenta passi sunt, spes illorum immortalitate plena est. Et rursus : In paucis vexati, in multis bene disponentur. In paucis, inquit, vexati : cur non potius in multis, præsertim quum (teste Apostolo) per multas tribulationes oporteat nos ingredi regnum Dei? nisi quod ait idem Apostolus, Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis.
paras.en: But when the faithful of Christ were struck with so many scourges, persecutions, hunger, thirst and deaths, what should they say but what follows? [[73:9|Our signs we have not seen|Signa nostra non vidimus]]: that is, we have not experienced, nor do we experience, such wonderful protections of the divine power as our most Christian fathers sometimes saw and experienced, who, though they were few, overthrew the greatest multitudes of unbelievers, help being granted them from above: as is plain of the most religious Theodosius, of Charlemagne, of Godfrey of Bouillon, and of many others. And the Apostles themselves too, and their successors, are known to have been often rescued by the help of angels from prisons, chains and every harm done by the unbelievers. But now nothing of the kind appears to us: therefore patience alone is necessary for us, with a most certain faith; and we must say that word of the Machabees: [[2 Mach 7:2|we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of God|Parati sumus magis mori, quam Dei leges prævaricari]] [the margin gives II Mach. vii]. Nor ought we to be broken because we are allowed to be slain in this present life, knowing that what is added in the same place is true: [[2 Mach 7:9|the King of the world will raise us up, who die for his laws, in the resurrection of eternal life|Rex mundi Deus defunctos nos pro suis legibus in æternæ vitæ resurrectione suscitabit]]. Hence it is written elsewhere too: [[Wis 3:4|though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality|Si coram hominibus tormenta passi sunt, spes illorum immortalitate plena est]]. And again: [[Wis 3:5|Afflicted in few things, in many they shall be well rewarded|In paucis vexati, in multis bene disponentur]] [*bene disponentur*, literally "shall be well disposed" or set in order]. *Afflicted in few things*, he says: why not rather in many, especially since (as the Apostle witnesses) [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God|per multas tribulationes oporteat nos ingredi regnum Dei?]]? Only because, as the same Apostle says, [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us|Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis]].

paras.t: Jam non est Propheta. Merito deplangit Ecclesia lapsum suum, quod nunc refriguit caritas plurimorum, nec modo inveniantur in Christianis gratiæ Spiritus Sancti (quas Paulus enumerans : Alii, inquit, datur sermo sapientiæ, alii sermo scientiæ, alii operatio virtutum, alii discretio spirituum, alii prophetia, etc.) tam copiose quemadmodum olim, præcipue tamen in primitiva Ecclesia, in qua multi fuere Prophetæ ; et interim non pauci fulserunt gratia prophetali, sicut Antonius, Hilarion, Joannes eremita, Benedictus, et alii multi. Nunc vero, heu! nimis infirmatur Ecclesia, et jam non est Propheta ; et sic dicere possunt in afflictionibus constituti : et nos non cognoscet amplius Deus noster, approbando opera nostra. Quod dicitur non asserendo, sed dolentis animi gemitum exprimendo, vel quia sic esse videtur.
paras.en: [[73:9|there is now no prophet|Jam non est Propheta]]. Rightly does the Church bewail her fall, in that the charity of many has now grown cold[[Matt 24:12||]], and the graces of the Holy Ghost are not now found in Christians (which Paul enumerates, saying: [[1 Cor 12:8|To one indeed|Alii]], he says, [[1 Cor 12:8|is given the word of wisdom|datur sermo sapientiæ]], [[1 Cor 12:8|to another, the word of knowledge|alii sermo scientiæ]], [[1 Cor 12:10|To another the working of miracles|alii operatio virtutum]], [[1 Cor 12:10|to another, the discerning of spirits|alii discretio spirituum]], [[1 Cor 12:10|to another, prophecy|alii prophetia]], etc.) as abundantly as once they were, and above all in the primitive Church, in which there were many prophets; and meanwhile not a few shone with the grace of prophecy, such as Antony, Hilarion, John the hermit, Benedict and many others. But now, alas, the Church is grown very weak, [[73:9|there is now no prophet|et jam non est Propheta]]; and so those set in afflictions can say: [[73:9|and he will know us no more|et nos non cognoscet amplius]], our God, by approving our works. This is said not as an assertion, but as expressing the groan of a sorrowing soul, or because it seems to be so.

paras.t: Deinde vir justus, seu ipsa Ecclesia improbitate hostium fatigata, ait ad Dominum : Usquequo, Deus, improperabit vel insultabit tibi aut servis tuis inimicus, hæresiarcha, paganus, Judæus aut tyrannus? Qui enim servis Dei improperat, Deo improperat. Propter quod ait Salvator : Qui vos audit, me audit ; et qui vos spernit, me spernit. Et usquequo, Domine Deus, irritat adversarius nomen tuum in finem, te ipsum inhonorando, et tua mandata spernendo, tuosque ministros persequendo?
paras.en: Then the just man, or the Church herself, wearied by the wickedness of her foes, says to the Lord: [[73:10|How long, O God, shall|Usquequo, Deus]] [[73:10|the enemy|inimicus]] [[73:10|reproach|improperabit]], or insult, thee or thy servants: the heresiarch, the pagan, the Jew or the tyrant? For he who reproaches the servants of God reproaches God. For which reason the Saviour says: [[Luke 10:16|He that heareth you heareth me: and he that despiseth you despiseth me|Qui vos audit, me audit ; et qui vos spernit, me spernit]]. And how long, O Lord God, [[73:10|is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever|irritat adversarius nomen tuum in finem]], dishonouring thee thyself, scorning thy commandments and persecuting thy ministers?

paras.t: Deus autem rex noster ante sæcula, id est Christus ante omnia tempora æternaliter genitus a Patre, operatus est salutem in medio terræ, videlicet in Judæa, et in monte Sion, reconcilians nos Deo per passionem suam et sanguinem. Humiliavit enim (ut ait Apostolus) semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. De hac Christi salvatione ait Pater æternus, de Christo loquens apud Zachariam : Ecce adducam servum meum Orientem ; et auferam iniquitatem terræ illius in die una, videlicet in die Parasceves. Tunc enim Christus agnus Dei tulit peccata mundi, sicut et ipse dixit : Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat.
paras.en: [[73:12|But God is our king before ages|Deus autem rex noster ante sæcula]], that is, Christ, eternally begotten of the Father before all times, [[73:12|he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth|operatus est salutem in medio terræ]], namely in Judea and on mount Sion, reconciling us to God through his passion and blood[[Rom 5:10||]]. For he [[Phil 2:8|humbled|Humiliavit]] (as the Apostle says) [[Phil 2:8|himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross|semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis]]. Of this salvation by Christ the eternal Father says, speaking of Christ in Zacharias: [[Zach 3:8|behold, I WILL BRING MY SERVANT THE ORIENT|Ecce adducam servum meum Orientem]]; [[Zach 3:9|and I will take away the iniquity of that land in one day|et auferam iniquitatem terræ illius in die una]], namely on the day of the Parasceve [that is, Good Friday]. For then Christ, the Lamb of God, took away the sins of the world[[John 1:29||]], as he himself also said: [[Luke 19:10|the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost|Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat]].

paras.t: Tu, Domine Christe, confirmasti in virtute tua, id est per divinam tuam potentiam ; vel, In virtute tua, id est in interiori perfectione ac fide catholica ; mare, id est gentiles : qui nomine maris signantur, primo, propter amaritudinem vitiorum gentilitatis ; secundo, quia ad instar aquarum inquieti erant, atque de peccato in peccatum fluxibiles ; tertio, propter multitudinem. Unde et alio loco scriptum est : Aquæ multæ, populi multi sunt. Hoc mare Christus in fide adeo confirmavit, ut pro christianæ fidei veritate mori optarent. Propterea per Isaiam ait Dominus, loquens de Christo : Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus. Et Isaias loquens ad Dominum : Ecce (ait) gentem quam nesciebas, vocabis ; et gentes quæ non cognoverunt te, ad te current. Hinc quoque in Actis Apostolorum scriptum est, quod Spiritus Sanctus cecidit super Cornelium et eos qui erant cum illo, loquebanturque linguis. Quo viso, obstupuerunt qui erant ex circumcisione, dicentes : Ergo et in nationes gratia Dei diffusa est ?
paras.en: [[73:13|Thou|Tu]], O Lord Christ, didst make firm [[73:13|by thy strength|in virtute tua]], that is, by thy divine power; or, [[73:13|by thy strength|In virtute tua]], that is, in inward perfection and the Catholic faith: [[73:13|the sea|mare]], that is, the Gentiles: who are signified by the name of the sea, first, because of the bitterness of the vices of heathendom; secondly, because like the waters they were restless, and flowed from sin to sin; thirdly, because of their multitude. Hence it is written in another place too: Many waters are many peoples[[Apoc 17:1||]][[Apoc 17:15||]] [a loose quotation: the many waters of Apoc 17:1 are explained in 17:15 as peoples]. This sea Christ so made firm in the faith that they longed to die for the truth of the Christian faith. Therefore the Lord says through Isaias, speaking of Christ: [[Is 55:4|Behold I have given him for a witness to the people, for a leader and a master to the Gentiles|Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus]]. And Isaias, speaking to the Lord: [[Is 55:5|Behold|Ecce]] (he says) [[Is 55:5|thou shalt call a nation, which thou knewest not: and the nations that knew not thee shall run to thee|gentem quam nesciebas, vocabis ; et gentes quæ non cognoverunt te, ad te current]]. Hence too it is written in the Acts of the Apostles that the Holy Ghost fell upon Cornelius and those who were with him[[Acts 10:44||]], and they spoke with tongues[[Acts 10:46||]]. Seeing which, those who were of the circumcision were astonished, saying: Is the grace of God then poured out upon the Gentiles too?[[Acts 10:45||]]

paras.t: Contribulasti, Domine Jesu, capita draconum in aquis, id est, spiritus malignos et eorum superbias contrivisti, superasti et exstinxisti in fonte Baptismi : quia in illo efficiuntur homines de filiis iræ filii gratiæ, de filiis perditionis et dæmonis, filii salutis et Creatoris, quoniam in hac aqua cuncta peccata donantur, sicut de ea in Zacharia scriptum est : In die illa erit fons patens domui David in ablutionem peccatoris. Quemadmodum autem per David intelligitur Christus, ita per domum David designatur Ecclesia Christi, quæ nunc purgatur in aquis Baptismi.
paras.en: [[73:13|thou didst crush|Contribulasti]], O Lord Jesus, [[73:13|the heads of the dragons in the waters|capita draconum in aquis]], that is, thou hast crushed, overcome and put out the evil spirits and their pride in the font of Baptism: because in it men are made, from children of wrath, children of grace; from children of perdition and of the devil, children of salvation and of the Creator; since in this water all sins are forgiven, as is written of it in Zacharias: [[Zach 13:1|In that day there shall be a fountain open to the house of David|In die illa erit fons patens domui David]], [[Zach 13:1|for the washing of the sinner|in ablutionem peccatoris]]. And as Christ is understood by David, so by the house of David is signified the Church of Christ, which is now cleansed in the waters of Baptism.

paras.t: Tu confregisti capita draconis. Hoc in præcedenti articulo de principis dæmonum dejectione expositum est. Cui concordat quod in Apocalypsi commemoratur : Factum est prælium in cœlo ; Michael et angeli ejus præliabantur cum dracone, et draco præliabatur et angeli ejus ; et non prævaluerunt, nec inventus est locus eorum amplius in cœlo. Potest quoque exponi de Antichristo, hoc modo : Tu, Christe, confregisti, id est confringes, ponendo præteritum pro futuro, secundum morem propheticæ denuntiationis, propter certitudinem prophetiæ : confringes, inquam, capita, id est principales fautores, seu dominationes atque potentias, draconis, id est Antichristi. De quo in Apocalypsi scriptum est : Vidi de mari ascendentem bestiam, habentem capita septem et cornua decem. Hunc draconem et omnem ejus apparatum, Christus confringet et condemnabit.
paras.en: [[73:14|Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon|Tu confregisti capita draconis]]. This was expounded in the preceding article of the casting down of the prince of the demons. With which agrees what is related in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 12:7|there was a great battle in heaven|Factum est prælium in cœlo]]: [[Apoc 12:7|Michael and his angels fought with the dragon, and the dragon fought, and his angels|Michael et angeli ejus præliabantur cum dracone, et draco præliabatur et angeli ejus]]. [[Apoc 12:8|And they prevailed not: neither was their place found any more in heaven|et non prævaluerunt, nec inventus est locus eorum amplius in cœlo]]. It can also be expounded of Antichrist, in this way: [[73:14|Thou|Tu]], O Christ, [[73:14|hast broken|confregisti]], that is, wilt break, putting the past for the future after the manner of prophetic announcement, because of the certainty of the prophecy: thou wilt break, I say, [[73:14|the heads|capita]], that is, the chief abettors, or the dominions and powers, [[73:14|of the dragon|draconis]], that is, of Antichrist. Of whom it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 13:1|I saw a beast coming up out the sea, having seven heads and ten horns|Vidi de mari ascendentem bestiam, habentem capita septem et cornua decem]]. This dragon and all his array Christ will break and condemn.

paras.t: Tu dirupisti fontes et torrentes : id est, sacram Scripturam, in qua continentur fontes sapientiæ atque torrentes scientiæ, aperuisti, et ejus mysteria revelasti per infusionem Spiritus Sancti. Vel, per fontes et torrentes intelligi possunt Apostoli, qui sunt summi doctores Ecclesiæ, et alii inferiores prædicatores : quorum Deus corda dirupit, dum ex eis fluenta sanctæ prædicationis toti mundo propinavit. Tu siccasti fluvios Ethan. Ethan nomen Hebraicum est, quod interpretatur Robustus. Per fluvios vero hoc loco intelliguntur doctrinæ, quæ de corde unius fluunt in mentem alterius. Est igitur sensus : Tu, Christe salvator mundi, desiccasti, arefecisti, et inutiles ostendisti doctrinas superborum, in sua sapientia gloriantium, seque robustos opinantium, scilicet documenta inanis philosophiæ, variosque errores idololatriæ ac diabolicæ doctrinæ. Propterea Apostolus loquitur : Nonne stultam fecit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi? Et iterum : Quæ stulta sunt mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat sapientes.
paras.en: [[73:15|Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents|Tu dirupisti fontes et torrentes]]: that is, thou hast opened holy Scripture, in which are contained fountains of wisdom and torrents of knowledge, and hast revealed its mysteries by the infusion of the Holy Ghost. Or by the fountains and torrents can be understood the Apostles, who are the highest doctors of the Church, and other lesser preachers: whose hearts God broke open, when from them he gave the streams of holy preaching to the whole world to drink. [[73:15|thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers|Tu siccasti fluvios Ethan]]. *Ethan* is a Hebrew name, which is interpreted *Strong*. And by rivers are understood in this place doctrines, which flow from the heart of one into the mind of another. The sense therefore is: Thou, O Christ, Saviour of the world, hast dried up, withered and shown to be useless the doctrines of the proud, who glory in their own wisdom and think themselves strong, namely the teachings of empty philosophy and the various errors of idolatry and of devilish doctrine. Therefore the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:20|Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?|Nonne stultam fecit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi?]] And again: [[1 Cor 1:27|the foolish things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the wise|Quæ stulta sunt mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat sapientes]].

paras.t: Tuus est dies, id est spirituales viri a sole justitiæ et fonte sapientiæ illuminati, et tua est nox, id est populus carnaliter vivens. Omnia enim genera hominum sunt Dei, jure creationis et universalis dominii. Tu fabricatus es auroram et solem, id est Virginem gloriosam, et Christum hominem Virginis Filium, dando utrique quidquid habent in donis naturæ et gratiæ. Maria quippe, aurora vocatur : quoniam sicut aurora diem præcedit, sic ipsa Christum. Unde de ea in Canticis legitur : Quæ est ista, velut aurora consurgens? Christus quoque, etiam ut homo, sol dicitur : quoniam sicut stellæ omnes a sole lumen recipere æstimantur, sic omnes sancti a Christo lumen fidei, gratiæ et sapientiæ sortiuntur. Nam de plenitudine ejus omnes accepimus. Tu fecisti, id est, spiritualiter reformasti et regenerasti, omnes terminos terræ, id est omnes electos in finibus mundi morantes. Æstatem et ver, id est remunerationem seu præmium ac meritum, tu plasmasti. In vere enim arbores flores, in æstate autem fructus producunt : et ita per æstatem accipitur præmium ; per ver, meritum. Deus autem causat in nobis non solum præmium, sed etiam meritum, juxta illud Isaiæ : Domine, dabis pacem nobis ; omnia enim opera nostra operatus es in nobis. Per æstatem quoque intelligi possunt fervidi amatores Divinitatis ; per ver autem, novelli et incipientes in Dei obsequio.
paras.en: [[73:16|Thine is the day|Tuus est dies]], that is, spiritual men enlightened by the Sun of justice and the fountain of wisdom, [[73:16|and thine is the night|et tua est nox]], that is, the people that lives carnally. For all kinds of men are God's, by right of creation and of universal dominion. [[73:16|thou hast made the morning light and the sun|Tu fabricatus es auroram et solem]], that is, the glorious Virgin, and Christ the man, the Virgin's Son, giving to each whatever they have in the gifts of nature and of grace. For Mary is called the dawn, because as the dawn goes before the day, so she went before Christ. Hence we read of her in the Canticles: [[Cant 6:9|Who is she|Quæ est ista]] [[Cant 6:9|as the morning rising|velut aurora consurgens]]? Christ too, even as man, is called the sun: because as all the stars are thought to receive their light from the sun, so all the saints receive from Christ the light of faith, of grace and of wisdom. For [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|de plenitudine ejus omnes accepimus]]. [[73:17|Thou hast made|Tu fecisti]], that is, hast spiritually reformed and regenerated, [[73:17|all the borders of the earth|omnes terminos terræ]], that is, all the elect dwelling in the ends of the world. [[73:17|the summer and the spring|Æstatem et ver]], that is, the reward or prize, and the merit, [[73:17|were formed by thee|tu plasmasti]] [literally "thou hast formed"]. For in spring the trees bring forth flowers, and in summer fruits: and so by summer is understood the reward, by spring the merit. Now God causes in us not only the reward but also the merit, according to that word of Isaias: [[Is 26:12|Lord, thou wilt give us peace: for thou hast wrought all our works for us|Domine, dabis pacem nobis ; omnia enim opera nostra operatus es in nobis]]. By summer too can be understood the fervent lovers of the Godhead; and by spring, those who are new and beginners in the service of God.

paras.t: Memor esto hujus congregationis ecclesiasticæ : de qua dictum est. Inimicus improperavit Domino, id est, hæretici et perversi vituperaverunt doctrinam Christi atque Ecclesiæ, dicentes : Aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior ; et populus insipiens, id est Deum verum ignorans, vel factis eum se ignorare ostendens, incitavit nomen tuum, id est, te ad iracundiam provocavit : idcirco peribit, sicut de eo inducitur, Populus non intelligens vapulabit. Ne tradas, aut tradi permittas, bestiis, id est dæmonibus vel sævis hominibus, animam confitentem tibi sua peccata et tua præconia. Cetera patent ex elucidatione præhabita.
paras.en: [[73:18|Remember this|Memor esto hujus]] ecclesiastical congregation, of which mention was made[[73:2||]]. [[73:18|the enemy hath reproached the Lord|Inimicus improperavit Domino]], that is, heretics and wicked men have reviled the doctrine of Christ and of the Church, saying: [[Prov 9:17|Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread is more pleasant|Aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior]]; [[73:18|and a foolish people|et populus insipiens]], that is, one ignorant of the true God, or showing by its deeds that it does not know him, [[73:18|hath provoked thy name|incitavit nomen tuum]], that is, has provoked thee to anger: therefore it shall perish, as is said of it: [[Osee 4:14|the people that doth not understand shall be beaten|Populus non intelligens vapulabit]]. [[73:19|Deliver not up|Ne tradas]], or suffer to be delivered up, [[73:19|to beasts|bestiis]], that is, to demons or to cruel men, the soul [[73:19|that confess to thee|confitentem tibi]] [the Douay-Rheims has "the souls that confess"; Denis reads the singular, *animam confitentem*] its sins and thy praises. The rest is plain from the explanation given before.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum sententiosum et affectuosum audivimus : in quo pristina divinæ familiaritatis beneficia recoluntur, malignitas persecutorum Ecclesiæ enarratur, tribulationes justorum scribuntur, pro adversariorum correctione oratur, divina potentia ex suis effectibus demonstratur. Quemadmodum igitur condecens est, devotione congrua præsentem psalmum canamus, et informemur ex eo in omni adversitate ad Deum affectuose converti, confidenter precari, beneficia patribus nostris exhibita commemorare : quatenus consequamur similia, atque ab omni liberemur instabilitate atque angustia.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of weighty sayings and of feeling: in which the former benefits of God's familiar friendship are recalled, the malice of the Church's persecutors is told, the tribulations of the just are written down, prayer is made for the correction of her adversaries, and the divine power is shown from its effects. As it is therefore most fitting, let us sing the present psalm with due devotion, and let us be taught by it, in every adversity, to turn lovingly to God, to pray with confidence, and to recall the benefits shown to our fathers: so that we may obtain the like, and be delivered from all unsteadiness and distress.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, Rex noster ante sæcula, Christe, qui in fine sæculi operatus es salutem in redemptione Ecclesiæ tuæ, quam ab initio tuo possedisti prædestinatione, respice in testamentum sanguine tuo confirmatum, faciendo eamdem Ecclesiam tuam devotam permanere, et in securitate jugi consistere : qui cum Deo Patre et Spiritu Sancto, etc.
paras.en: Prayer. O [[73:12|God|Deus]], [[73:12|our king before ages|Rex noster ante sæcula]], O Christ, who at the end of the age hast [[73:12|wrought salvation|operatus es salutem]] in the redemption of thy Church, [[73:2|which thou hast possessed from the beginning|quam ab initio tuo possedisti]] by thy predestination, [[73:20|Have regard to thy covenant|respice in testamentum]] confirmed by thy blood, making that same Church of thine abide devout and stand in unbroken security: who with God the Father and the Holy Ghost, etc.

74.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI QUARTI : CONFITEBIMUR TIBI, DEUS, CONFITEBIMUR.
74.title_en: Explanation of the seventy-fourth psalm: We will praise thee, O God, we will praise.

paras.t: Denique titulus psalmi præsentis est : In finem, ne corrumpas, psalmus cantici Asaph. Quidam exponunt hunc psalmum ad litteram de populo Judæorum, redeunte a captivitate Babylonis, ut sit gratiarum actio populi inde liberati, et in Judæam reversi. Sicque sensus tituli est iste : Psalmus cantici est ipsius Asaph, ne corrumpas, id est, ne disperdas, o Domine, populum Israel, sicut fecisti in captivitate Babyloniæ. Videtur autem mihi expositio ista parum devotionis includere, modicumque dulcedinis continere : breviter tamen tangi potest hoc modo.
paras.en: Next, the title of the present psalm is: [[74:1|Unto the end, corrupt not, a psalm of a canticle for Asaph|In finem, ne corrumpas, psalmus cantici Asaph]]. Some expound this psalm literally of the Jewish people returning from the captivity of Babylon, so that it is the thanksgiving of the people set free from there and returned to Judea. And so the sense of the title is this: [[74:1|a psalm of a canticle|Psalmus cantici]] is Asaph’s own; [[74:1|corrupt not|ne corrumpas]], that is, destroy not, O Lord, the people of Israel, as thou didst in the captivity of Babylon. But this exposition seems to me to hold little devotion and to contain small sweetness; yet it can be touched on briefly in this way.

paras.t: Confitebimur tibi, Deus, nos de captivitate reversi ex licentia Darii regis Medorum et Cyri regis Persarum, quod juste castigasti nos, quia peccavimus ; confitebimur tibi, quod misericorditer reduxisti nos, imo et juste, quoniam promisisti per Jeremiam, quod post septuaginta annos eripiendi essemus de captivitate; et invocabimus nomen tuum pro gratia vitandi peccata præterita, ne denuo incidamus similia mala. Narrabimus mirabilia tua, quæ in Babylone vidimus aut cognovimus, quomodo scilicet eripuisti tres pueros de camino ardenti, et Danielem de lacu leonum, et Susannam de manibus judicum impiorum : quæ omnia in Daniele leguntur.
paras.en: [[74:2|We will praise thee, O God|Confitebimur tibi, Deus]], we who have returned from captivity by leave of Darius king of the Medes and Cyrus king of the Persians, that thou hast justly chastised us, because we have sinned; [[74:2|we will praise thee|confitebimur tibi]] [the Latin *confitebimur* means both ‘we will praise’ and ‘we will confess’] that thou hast mercifully brought us back, yea, and justly, since thou didst promise by Jeremias that after seventy years we should be delivered from captivity[[Jer 25:11||]]; [[74:2|and we will call upon thy name|et invocabimus nomen tuum]], for grace to shun our past sins, lest we fall again into like evils. [[74:2|We will relate thy wondrous works|Narrabimus mirabilia tua]], which we saw or came to know in Babylon: namely, how thou didst deliver the three children from the burning furnace[[Dan 3:1||]], and Daniel from the lions’ den[[Dan 6:1||]][[Dan 14:1||]], and Susanna from the hands of the wicked judges[[Dan 13:1||]]: all of which are read in Daniel.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta mutans personam, ait in persona Dei : Quum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo, id est, tempore a me præordinato atque disposito, judicabo justitias electorum, liberando eos de manibus injustorum, prout eorum justitiæ exigunt et merentur.
paras.en: Then the Prophet, changing the person, says in the person of God: [[74:3|When I shall take a time, I will judge justices|Quum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo]], that is, at the time foreordained and appointed by me I will judge the justices of the elect [*justitias*, ‘justices’: their just deeds and just causes], delivering them from the hands of the unjust, as their just deeds require and deserve.

paras.t: Liquefacta est terra, id est, Judæa a Chaldæis incensa est et combusta, et omnes qui habitant in ea, id est, qui morabantur in terra hac, timore Chaldæorum dissoluti sunt corde. Ego Deus confirmavi columnas ejus, id est, principes populi hujus stabilivi in bono, et in fortitudine animi inconcussa, videlicet Zorobabel, Jesum filium Josedec sacerdotem magnum, Zachariam, Aggæum, Esdram, Nehemiam.
paras.en: [[74:4|The earth is melted|Liquefacta est terra]], that is, Judea was set on fire and burnt by the Chaldeans, [[74:4|and all that dwell therein|et omnes qui habitant in ea]], that is, those who lived in this land were melted in heart for fear of the Chaldeans. [[74:4|I have established the pillars thereof|Ego Deus confirmavi columnas ejus]], that is, I have made firm in good, and in unshaken strength of soul, the princes of this people: namely Zorobabel[[1 Esd 3:2||]], Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest[[Agg 1:14||]][[Agg 2:3||]], Zacharias, Aggeus[[1 Esd 5:1||]] [the margin gives 1 Esdr. v, 4; Aggeus and Zacharias are named at 1 Esd 5:1], Esdras[[1 Esd 7:6||]], Nehemias[[2 Esd 7:7||]].

paras.t: Dixi, id est, ego Deus, non verbis sed opere, intimavi iniquis, id est superbis Babyloniis : Nolite inique agere, id est, nolite amplius regna et populum alienum opprimere, sicut hucusque fecistis; dixi et delinquentibus, id est prædictis iniquis : Nolite exaltare cornu, id est, nolite diutius regnare seu regiam potestatem exercere. Nolite extollere in altum cornu vestrum, imperando omnibus regnis, et monarchiam tenendo ; nolite loqui adversus Deum iniquitatem, blasphemando Deum Israel, et subsannando populum ejus, quemadmodum diu fecistis. Hæc omnia dixit Deus Chaldæis, non verbo sed opere : quoniam abstulit eis potestatem prosequendi opera mala, transferendo regnum eorum ad Medos ac Persas, ut in Daniele habetur, et ab Isaia et Jeremia evidentissime prænuntiatum conspicitur.
paras.en: [[74:5|I said|Dixi]], that is, I God, not in words but in deed, made known [[74:5|to the wicked|iniquis]], that is, to the proud Babylonians: [[74:5|Do not act wickedly|Nolite inique agere]], that is, oppress no more the kingdoms and a people not your own, as you have done till now; [[74:5|I said|dixi]] also [[74:5|to the sinners|delinquentibus]], that is, to the aforesaid wicked: [[74:5|Lift not up the horn|Nolite exaltare cornu]], that is, reign no longer, nor wield royal power. [[74:6|Lift not up your horn on high|Nolite extollere in altum cornu vestrum]], by ruling over all kingdoms and holding the monarchy; [[74:6|speak not iniquity against God|nolite loqui adversus Deum iniquitatem]], by blaspheming the God of Israel and mocking his people, as you have long done. All this God said to the Chaldeans, not in word but in deed: for he took from them the power to carry on their evil works, by transferring their kingdom to the Medes and Persians, as is found in Daniel[[Dan 5:28||]], and is seen to have been most plainly foretold by Isaias[[Is 13:17||]] and Jeremias[[Jer 51:1||]].

paras.t: Cur autem Deus hæc dixerit eis, subdit Propheta : Quia neque ab oriente, neque ab occidente, neque a desertis montibus, id est, quia ex nulla parte aut latere mundi, poteritis, o Babylonii, judicium divinum effugere : et hoc ideo, quoniam Deus ubique exsistens, omnia cernens, atque omnipotens, judex est. Hunc humiliat, et hunc exaltat, id est, unum deprimit, et alium elevat, secundum quod sibi placet et homines promerentur ; quia calix in manu Domini, id est, pœna seu ultio est in potestate Dei : calix, inquam, vini meri plenus mixto : id est, pœna quam Deus effundere potest in impios, est multum acerba et pungitiva, quemadmodum mixtum ex vino mero. Et inclinavit ex hoc in hoc : id est, Deus pœnam suæ vindictæ effudit de uno populo in alium, puniendo perversos successive, secundum ordinem suæ justissimæ sapientiæ; verumtamen fex ejus non est exinanita : id est, fundus seu amaritudo calicis hujus non est evacuatus, quoniam divina potestas non desinit in ulciscendo. Omnia autem hæc, et quæ restant in psalmo isto, in sequenti articulo latius exponentur.
paras.en: Why God said this to them, the Prophet adds: [[74:7|For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills|Quia neque ab oriente, neque ab occidente, neque a desertis montibus]], that is, because from no part or side of the world, O Babylonians, will you be able to escape the judgment of God; and this because [[74:8|God|Deus]], who is everywhere, sees all things and is almighty, [[74:8|is the judge|judex est]]. [[74:8|One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up|Hunc humiliat, et hunc exaltat]], that is, he lowers one and raises another, as it pleases him and as men deserve; [[74:9|For in the hand of the Lord there is a cup|quia calix in manu Domini]], that is, punishment or vengeance is in the power of God: a cup, I say, [[74:9|of strong wine full of mixture|vini meri plenus mixto]] [*merum*: pure, unmixed wine]: that is, the punishment which God can pour out upon the wicked is very bitter and stinging, like a mixture made from strong wine. [[74:9|And he hath poured it out from this to that|Et inclinavit ex hoc in hoc]]: that is, God has poured out the punishment of his vengeance from one people upon another, punishing the wicked one after another, according to the order of his most just wisdom; [[74:9|but the dregs thereof are not emptied|verumtamen fex ejus non est exinanita]]: that is, the bottom or bitterness of this cup has not been drained, since the divine power does not cease from taking vengeance. But all these things, and what remains in this psalm, will be expounded more fully in the following article.

74.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI QUARTI.
74.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same seventy-fourth psalm.

paras.t: Denique, juxta tropologicum sensum, prædictus titulus ita exponitur : Psalmus cantici, id est spiritualis jucunditatis, quoniam agit de remuneratione justorum, est Asaph, id est, convenit designatis per Asaph, videlicet congregationi fidelium seu Ecclesiæ : Asaph enim congregatio interpretatur. Psalmus (inquam) conscriptus, ne tu fidelis corrumpas te ipsum per superbiam ; et spem tuam, quæ est in finem, id est tendens in Christum seu vitam æternam, evacues. Specialiter autem hic psalmus superbiam detestatur, humilitatem commendat, justum Dei judicium recolit, et omnium justam remunerationem declarat.
paras.en: Next, according to the tropological sense, the aforesaid title is expounded thus: [[74:1|a psalm of a canticle|Psalmus cantici]], that is, of spiritual joy, since it treats of the reward of the just, is Asaph’s, that is, it befits those signified by Asaph, namely the congregation of the faithful, or the Church: for Asaph is interpreted ‘congregation’. A psalm (I say) written so that thou, O faithful soul, [[74:1|corrupt not|corrumpas]] thyself through pride, nor make void thy hope, which is [[74:1|unto the end|in finem]], that is, tending towards Christ, or eternal life. Now this psalm in particular detests pride, commends humility, recalls the just judgment of God, and declares the just reward of all.

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta auctor psalmi præsentis, sive ille fuerit David, sive Asaph, in persona Ecclesiæ ait : Confitebimur tibi, Deus, confitebimur. Repetitio verbi, signum est firmi propositi ardentisque desiderii. Vel, quod primo dicit, Confitebimur, referri potest ad confessionem laudis divinæ, de qua ait Salvator, Confiteor tibi, Pater : et ista confessio manet in patria, sicut inferius dicitur, Confessio et pulchritudo in conspectu ejus. Quod vero secundo repetit, Confitebimur, referri potest ad confessionem propriæ culpæ, de qua Jacobus dicit : Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra, et orate pro invicem, ut salvemini. Itaque, Confitebimur tibi, Deus, id est, te laudabimus, tuam bonitatem æternam, immensam ac puram, ore et opere glorificando, tua beneficia summa ac liberalissima, scilicet dona naturæ et gratiæ recolendo, et tibi attribuendo. Hoc modo confitetur Deo, qui cum B. Jacobo protestatur : Omne datum optimum, et omne donum perfectum desursum est, descendens a Patre luminum. Hoc enim ad commemorationem beneficiorum Dei certum est pertinere, sicut et illud quod Paulus inducit : Quid habes quod non accepisti ? Et iterum : Sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Quod vero Jacobus subdit, Apud quem non est transmutatio nec vicissitudinis obumbratio, pertinet ad recommendationem divinæ naturæ seu bonitatis secundum se. Aut enim laudamus Deum propter se ipsum ac propriam bonitatem, aut propter beneficia sua : et ad hos duos modos confitendi Domino confessione laudis, reducuntur et spectant quæcumque in sacra Scriptura ad laudem Dei dicuntur. Et invocabimus nomen tuum, id est, te ipsum ex interno affectu, ex totis præcordiis intimisque medullis precabimur, quatenus tibi grati inveniamur, in bono conservemur, proficiamus et consummemur. Laudabimus ergo te propter beneficia jam adepta, et invocabimus te propter beneficia adipiscenda, seu propter promissa obtinenda.
paras.en: So the Prophet, the author of the present psalm, whether he was David or Asaph, speaking in the person of the Church, says: [[74:2|We will praise thee, O God: we will praise|Confitebimur tibi, Deus, confitebimur]] [the Latin *confitebimur* means both ‘we will praise’ and ‘we will confess’, and Denis draws on both senses]. The repetition of the word is a sign of firm purpose and ardent desire. Or, what he says the first time, *we will confess*, can be referred to the confession of divine praise, of which the Saviour says, [[Matt 11:25|I confess to thee, O Father|Confiteor tibi, Pater]]: and this confession abides in the fatherland, as is said further on, [[Ps 95:6|Praise and beauty are before him|Confessio et pulchritudo in conspectu ejus]] [in the Latin, *Confessio*]. But what he repeats the second time, *we will confess*, can be referred to the confession of one’s own fault, of which James says: [[Jas 5:16|Confess therefore your sins one to another: and pray one for another, that you may be saved|Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra, et orate pro invicem, ut salvemini]]. Accordingly, [[74:2|We will praise thee, O God|Confitebimur tibi, Deus]], that is, we will praise thee, glorifying by mouth and deed thy goodness, eternal, immense and pure, and recalling thy highest and most liberal benefits, namely the gifts of nature and of grace, and ascribing them to thee. In this way he confesses to God who declares with Blessed James: [[Jas 1:17|Every best gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights|Omne datum optimum, et omne donum perfectum desursum est, descendens a Patre luminum]]. For this certainly belongs to the remembrance of God’s benefits, as does that which Paul brings in: [[1 Cor 4:7|what hast thou that thou hast not received|Quid habes quod non accepisti]]? And again: [[2 Cor 3:5|our sufficiency is from God|Sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]. But what James adds, [[Jas 1:17|with whom there is no change nor shadow of alteration|Apud quem non est transmutatio nec vicissitudinis obumbratio]], belongs to the commendation of the divine nature, or goodness, in itself. For either we praise God for himself and his own goodness, or for his benefits: and to these two ways of confessing to the Lord by the confession of praise is referred, and belongs, whatever is said in holy Scripture in praise of God. [[74:2|and we will call upon thy name|Et invocabimus nomen tuum]], that is, we will pray to thee thyself with inward affection, from our whole heart and inmost marrow, that we may be found pleasing to thee, be kept in good, advance and be made perfect. So we will praise thee for benefits already obtained, and call upon thee for benefits yet to be obtained, or for the promises to be won.

paras.t: Narrabimus mirabilia tua, in veteri ac novo Testamento conscripta, laudando te Deum opificem in tuis effectibus supernaturalibus. Præsertim autem narrare debemus, vel soli coram Deo, vel etiam si ratio exigit, proximis, mirabilia Dei quæ circa unumquemque nostrum operari dignatus est, peccata nostra misericorditer indulgendo, gratiam conversionis præstando, et animas nostras olim peccatrices justificando : quod est magnum mirabile Dei, quoniam (Augustino teste) majus est impium justificare, quam cœlum et terram creare. Unde legitur : Virtutes annuntietis ejus, qui de tenebris vos vocavit in admirabile lumen suum. Maxime vero narrare, incessabiliterque commemorare debemus mirabilia Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quæ ipse pro nostra salute assumpsit, fecit, ac pertulit : utpote mysteria redemptionis humanæ, incarnationem, conversationem, vitam, doctrinam, signa, passionem, resurrectionem, ascensionemque Christi. Hinc enim scriptum est : Nonne Dominus fecit sanctos enarrare omnia mirabilia sua, quæ confirmavit Dominus omnipotens stabilis in gloria sua ?
paras.en: [[74:2|We will relate thy wondrous works|Narrabimus mirabilia tua]], written in the Old and the New Testament, praising thee, God, as the maker, in thy supernatural works. But above all we ought to relate, either alone before God or, if reason requires, to our neighbours also, the wonders of God which he has deigned to work in each one of us, mercifully forgiving our sins, granting the grace of conversion, and justifying our souls, once sinful: which is a great wonder of God, since (as Augustine witnesses) it is a greater thing to justify the ungodly than to create heaven and earth. Hence we read: [[1 Pet 2:9|that you may declare his virtues, who hath called you out of darkness into his marvelous light|Virtutes annuntietis ejus, qui de tenebris vos vocavit in admirabile lumen suum]]. Most of all we ought to relate, and unceasingly call to mind, the wonders of our Lord Jesus Christ, which he took upon himself, did and endured for our salvation: such as the mysteries of man’s redemption, the incarnation, the life among men, the life, teaching, signs, passion, resurrection and ascension of Christ. For hence it is written: [[Ecclus 42:17|Hath not the Lord made the saints to declare all his wonderful works, which the Lord Almighty hath firmly settled to be established for his glory?|Nonne Dominus fecit sanctos enarrare omnia mirabilia sua, quæ confirmavit Dominus omnipotens stabilis in gloria sua]] [the margin gives Ecclus. xliii, 17; the passage is Ecclus 42:17]

paras.t: Deinde vox Christi inducitur. Quum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo : id est, dum tempus ad judicandum Dei sapientia institutum atque præfixum advenerit, ego judicabo justitias. Quod dupliciter explanatur. Primo sic : Justitias, id est opera quæ videntur hominibus justa, ego discutiam, an sint veraciter justa, et recta intentione peracta. Nam tam districte Deus opera justorum discutiet, ut Petrus in sua Canonica dicat : Si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt ? Secundo sic : Justitias judicabo, id est, justas sententias proferam, electos judicando judicio approbationis, et reprobos judicio condemnationis. Propter quod Salomon loquitur : Qui inspector est cordis, ipse intelligit, et servatorem animæ tuæ nihil fallet, reddetque homini juxta opera sua. Oportet autem (secundum Apostolum) nos omnes manifestari ante tribunal Christi; et unumquemque nostrum Christus judicabit sigillatim in hora propriæ mortis, universaliter vero de omnibus judicabit in die novissimo. In primo quoque suo adventu accepit Christus tempus judicandi passive et miserendi, juxta illud : Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat. In secundo autem suo adventu accipiet tempus judicandi active et vindicandi, ut ait Joannes : Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique juxta opera sua. Et Daniel : Judicium sedit, et libri aperti sunt ; et ecce in nubibus cœli quasi Filius hominis veniebat.
paras.en: Then the voice of Christ is brought in: [[74:3|When I shall take a time, I will judge justices|Quum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo]]: that is, when the time for judging, appointed and fixed beforehand by the wisdom of God, shall have come, I will judge justices. This is explained in two ways. First thus: justices, that is, the works that seem just to men, I will examine, whether they be truly just and done with a right intention. For God will examine the works of the just so strictly that Peter says in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 4:18|if the just man shall scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?|Si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt]] Secondly thus: [[74:3|I will judge justices|Justitias judicabo]], that is, I will pronounce just sentences, judging the elect with the judgment of approval and the reprobate with the judgment of condemnation. Wherefore Solomon says: [[Prov 24:12|he that seeth into the heart, he understandeth, and nothing deceiveth the keeper of thy soul, and he shall render to a man according to his works|Qui inspector est cordis, ipse intelligit, et servatorem animæ tuæ nihil fallet, reddetque homini juxta opera sua]]. And (according to the Apostle) [[2 Cor 5:10|we must all be manifested before the judgment seat of Christ|nos omnes manifestari ante tribunal Christi]]; and Christ will judge each one of us singly in the hour of his own death, but all men together on the last day. In his first coming, too, Christ took the time of judging passively [that is, of being judged] and of showing mercy, according to that: [[Luke 19:10|the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost|Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat]]. But in his second coming he will take the time of judging actively and of taking vengeance, as John says: [[Apoc 22:12|Behold, I come quickly: and my reward is with me, to render to every, man according to his works|Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique juxta opera sua]]. And Daniel: [[Dan 7:10|the judgment sat, and the books were opened|Judicium sedit, et libri aperti sunt]]; [[Dan 7:13|and lo, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven|et ecce in nubibus cœli quasi Filius hominis veniebat]].

paras.t: Sed quam terribile erit illud judicium, pandit Propheta, subdendo : Liquefacta est terra, et omnes qui habitant in ea. Nam ante finale judicium terra et aer igne conflagrationis accendentur ac purgabuntur, hominesque tunc viventes, timore ad instar plumbi liquescent et dissolventur, prout Salvator ait : Erunt signa in sole et luna et stellis, et in terris pressura gentium, arescentibus hominibus præ timore et expectatione, quæ supervenient universo orbi. De hac terræ liquefactione futura in die judicii, de qua nunc loquitur Propheta per modum præteriti, secundum consuetudinem prophetiæ, ait beatissimus Petrus : Adveniet dies Domini tanquam fur, in quo cæli (supple, aerii) magno impetu transient, elementa vero calore solventur ; terra autem et quæ in ipsa sunt opera, exurentur. Isaias quoque : Ecce, inquit, dies Domini veniet crudelis et indignationis plenus, et iræ furorisque, ad ponendam terram in solitudinem, et peccatores ejus conterendos de ea. Ego Dominus confirmavi columnas ejus : id est, justos et viros perfectos, qui erunt circa finem mundi, tempore Antichristi, confirmabo et conservabo in gratia, ne in tantis persecutionibus atque terroribus deficiendo frangantur et cadant. Erit enim tunc tribulatio magna, qualis non fuit ab initio mundi usque modo, neque fiet. Et nisi breviati fuissent dies illi, non fieret salva omnis caro ; sed propter electos breviabuntur dies illi. Possunt quoque nomine columnarum intelligi sancti Apostoli, quos Christus post resurrectionem confirmavit in fide. Dicuntur vero viri perfecti, sapientes et sancti, columnæ mundi atque Ecclesiæ, quia per preces, doctrinas et exempla eorum, alii sustentantur.
paras.en: But how terrible that judgment will be, the Prophet shows by adding: [[74:4|The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein|Liquefacta est terra, et omnes qui habitant in ea]]. For before the final judgment the earth and the air will be kindled and purged by the fire of the conflagration, and the men then living will melt and dissolve with fear like lead, as the Saviour says: [[Luke 21:25|there shall be signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations|Erunt signa in sole et luna et stellis, et in terris pressura gentium]], [[Luke 21:26|Men withering away for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world|arescentibus hominibus præ timore et expectatione, quæ supervenient universo orbi]].
