Or: [[75:9|Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven|De cœlo auditum fecisti judicium]], that is, thou wilt cause it to be heard, when [[1 Thess 4:15|the Lord himself shall come down from heaven with commandment and with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God|ipse Dominus in jussu et in voce Archangeli et in tuba Dei descendet de cœlo]], and [[1 Cor 15:52|the trumpet shall sound|tuba canet]], saying: Arise, ye dead, come to judgment [these words are not in Scripture; they are a saying often ascribed to St Jerome]. And also when Christ himself shall pronounce the sentence, saying, [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]; and, [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]]; God the Trinity will cause to be heard the judgment which he has conceived within himself concerning all things, of which judgment Christ as man is the executor or the one who pronounces it.

paras.t: Terra tremuit et quievit, quum exsurgeret in judicium Deus. Hoc diversimode accipi potest. In adventu enim Christi ad judicium, omnes homines in terra exsistentes terrebuntur ; sed boni ab hoc terrore cito quiescent, quoniam Deus judicabit pro eis. Impii quoque quiescent a pristinis vitiis, quoniam amplius deliciari non poterunt. De hac enim quiete apud Isaiam prædictum est : Quiescite agere perverse. Vel ipsum elementum terræ tunc tremet, id est, ad similitudinem trementis se habebit, propter ignem conflagrationis et impetum fluctuum maris ; et quiescet ab hac agitatione, quoniam facto judicio tempus et motus cœli cessabunt, et terra splendebit ut aurum. Sic ergo, Terra tremuit et quievit, id est, contremiscet atque quiescet, quum exsurgeret in judicium Deus, id est, dum Christus ad judicandum veniet cum omnibus incolis cœli, juxta illud Isaiæ : Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senioribus populi sui et principibus ejus ; ut salvos faceret, id est, quatenus ab omni corruptione, mortalitate, molestia salvet, omnes mansuetos terræ, id est homines mites, qui iram refrenant. — Potest quoque exponi de Christo resurgente. Nam, ut dicit Matthæus, Christo resurgente, terræ motus factus est magnus. Angelus enim Domini descendit, etc. Ab hoc autem motu terra quievit, quum exsurgeret Deus Dei Filius, scilicet Christus, a morte in judicium, id est, ut suo tempore judicet mundum, qui est judicatus a mundo, et ut judicaret Judæos.
paras.en: [[75:9|the earth trembled and was still|Terra tremuit et quievit]], [[75:10|When God arose in judgment|quum exsurgeret in judicium Deus]]. This can be taken in various ways. For at the coming of Christ to judgment all men living on the earth will be terrified; but the good will soon be quiet from this terror, since God will judge in their favour. The wicked too will rest from their former vices, since they will be able to take their pleasures no longer. For of this rest it was foretold in Isaias: [[Is 1:16|cease to do perversely|Quiescite agere perverse]]. Or the very element of earth will then tremble, that is, it will behave like one trembling, because of the fire of the conflagration and the onrush of the waves of the sea; and it will be still from this agitation, since once the judgment is done, time and the motion of the heavens will cease, and the earth will shine like gold. So then, [[75:9|the earth trembled and was still|Terra tremuit et quievit]], that is, will tremble and be still, [[75:10|When God arose in judgment|quum exsurgeret in judicium Deus]], that is, when Christ shall come to judge with all the dwellers of heaven, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 3:14|The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and its princes|Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senioribus populi sui et principibus ejus]]; [[75:10|to save|ut salvos faceret]], that is, in order to save from all corruption, mortality and trouble, [[75:10|all the meek of the earth|omnes mansuetos terræ]], that is, gentle men, who curb their anger. It can also be explained of Christ rising again. For, as Matthew says, when Christ rose, [[Matt 28:2|there was a great earthquake|terræ motus factus est magnus]]. [[Matt 28:2|For an angel of the Lord descended|Angelus enim Domini descendit]], etc. And from this motion the earth was still, [[75:10|When God arose|quum exsurgeret Deus]], God the Son of God, namely Christ, from death [[75:10|in judgment|in judicium]], that is, to judge in his own time the world by which he was judged, and to judge the Jews.

paras.t: Quoniam cogitatio hominis confitebitur tibi : id est, prima occupatio seu principalis exercitatio cordis hominis virtuosi, laudabit te, et accusabit se : sicque implebit illud Evangelii, Primum quærite regnum Dei ; et reliquiæ cogitationis, id est ceteræ meditationes ex hac prima occupatione nascentes, diem festum agent tibi, id est, mentem implebunt bonis considerationibus, quibus intenta tibi solenniter vacabit et inhærebit, tempusque festive et fructuose expendet. Dum namque homo Deo primo confitetur sua beneficia, et mox memor efficitur peccatorum suorum : tunc anima ejus impletur splendoribus gratiæ, perpenditque homo quantam beatitudinem peccando amisit, quantam miseriam incidit, pœnamque promeruit, quam viliter tempus expendit, quam grave peccatum sit ingratitudo, quam clemens est Deus qui sibi tam diu pepercit, et gratiam conversionis modo largitus est ; multaque alia considerat anima sic conversa.
paras.en: [[75:11|For the thought of man shall give praise to thee|Quoniam cogitatio hominis confitebitur tibi]]: that is, the first occupation or chief exercise of the heart of the virtuous man will praise thee and accuse itself [*confitebitur* can mean both "shall praise" and "shall confess"]; and so it will fulfil that saying of the Gospel, [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God|Primum quærite regnum Dei]]; [[75:11|and the remainders of the thought|et reliquiæ cogitationis]], that is, the other meditations springing from this first occupation, [[75:11|shall keep holiday to thee|diem festum agent tibi]], that is, they will fill the mind with good considerations, intent on which it will solemnly give itself to thee and cleave to thee, and spend its time festively and fruitfully. For when a man first confesses to God his benefits, and soon becomes mindful of his own sins, then his soul is filled with the splendours of grace, and he weighs how great a beatitude he lost by sinning, into how great a misery he fell and what punishment he deserved, how cheaply he has spent his time, how grave a sin ingratitude is, how merciful God is, who spared him so long and has now bestowed on him the grace of conversion; and many other things does the soul so converted consider.

paras.t: Vovete, id est, consulo vobis ut voveatis, vel in susceptione sacri Ordinis, vel in ingressu religionis, vel aliud aliquid ad Dei honorem agendo vel dando ; et reddite, id est, jubeo ut reddatis Domino Deo vestro. Vovere enim, consilium est, quia ad supererogationem pertinet ; solvere autem vota, præceptum, quemadmodum Moyses asserit, Quod semel egressum est de labiis tuis, observabis, et facies sicut promisisti Domino Deo tuo : imo et cito reddendum est, secundum quod in Ecclesiaste habetur : Si quid vovisti Domino, ne moreris reddere ; displicet enim ei stulta et infidelis promissio. Ideo Thomas affirmat, quod votum plus obligat quam juramentum. Denique multo perfectius est, et magis meritorium, bonum ex voto facere, quam sine voto : sicut et majus est, dare arborem cum fructu, quam fructum tantum. Voluntas namque est veluti arbor, unde fructus boni et mali, id est opera virtuosa ac vitiosa, nascuntur. Qui ergo promittit, voluntatem ipsam Deo offert et obligat ; ostenditur quoque homo talis magis promptus et ardens ad Dei obsequium, quam non promittens. Sed et ipsum votum seu promissio, quum sit actus virtutis quæ latria dicitur, magnum recipit præmium : sicque ex voto operans, dupliciter promeretur, videlicet ratione voti, et item ratione operis boni. Sunt autem quædam vota cunctis communia, sine quibus nemo potest salvari, sicut in fonte Baptismi promittimus credere, et operibus Satanæ renuntiare : et ista cadunt sub præcepto sicut Baptismus. Alia vero sunt specialia vota, quemadmodum votum castitatis, paupertatis, etc. : et ista ante promissionem sunt in consilio ; vota autem emissa, sunt sub præcepto.
paras.en: [[75:12|Vow ye|Vovete]], that is, I counsel you to vow, whether in receiving holy Orders, or in entering religion, or in doing or giving something else to the honour of God; [[75:12|and pay|et reddite]], that is, I command you to pay, [[75:12|to the Lord your God|Domino Deo vestro]]. For to vow is a counsel, since it belongs to supererogation [that is, to doing more than is commanded]; but to pay vows is a precept, as Moses declares: [[Deut 23:23|that which is once gone out of thy lips, thou shalt observe, and shalt do as thou hast promised to the Lord thy God|Quod semel egressum est de labiis tuis, observabis, et facies sicut promisisti Domino Deo tuo]]; indeed it must be paid quickly too, according to what is found in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 5:3|If thou hast vowed any thing to God, defer not to pay it|Si quid vovisti Domino, ne moreris reddere]]: [[Eccles 5:3|for an unfaithful and foolish promise displeaseth him|displicet enim ei stulta et infidelis promissio]]. Therefore Thomas affirms that a vow binds more than an oath. Lastly, it is far more perfect and more meritorious to do good by vow than without a vow, just as it is a greater thing to give the tree with its fruit than the fruit alone. For the will is like a tree, from which spring fruits good and bad, that is, virtuous and vicious works. He then who promises offers and binds the will itself to God; and such a man is shown to be more ready and ardent in God's service than one who does not promise. Moreover the vow or promise itself, since it is an act of the virtue called latria [that is, the worship due to God alone], receives a great reward; and so one who works by vow merits doubly, by reason of the vow and by reason of the good work. Now there are certain vows common to all, without which no one can be saved, as in the font of Baptism we promise to believe and to renounce the works of Satan; and these fall under precept, as Baptism does. Others are special vows, such as the vow of chastity, of poverty, etc.; and these, before they are promised, are matters of counsel, but once made, they are under precept.

paras.t: Sic ergo, vovete et reddite Domino Deo vestro, o omnes fideles, qui in circuitu ejus affertis munera, id est, qui ex omni parte ad Deum confluitis, atque per modum coronæ ad Deum acceditis : qui utique est in medio vestrum ; non tamen sic sunt omnes homines in circuitu Dei, quasi Deum intra se claudant ac terminent, quoniam ipse immensus est. Cetera patent ex precedenti explanatione.
paras.en: So then, [[75:12|Vow ye, and pay to the Lord your God|vovete et reddite Domino Deo vestro]], O [[75:12|all you|omnes]] faithful, [[75:12|that are round about him bring presents|qui in circuitu ejus affertis munera]], that is, who flow together to God from every side and approach God in the manner of a crown, who indeed is in the midst of you[[Matt 18:20||]]; yet all men are not round about God in such a way as if they enclosed and bounded God within themselves, since he is immeasurable. The rest is plain from the preceding explanation.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum jucundum, amoenum, et Dei laudibus plenum audivimus : quem decet nos cum interna dulcedine, cordiali lætitia, et intellectu intento proferre, quatenus nos ipsi et unusquisque nostrum esse queat Judæa, Domino fide et opere confitendo, Israel, gloriam ejus revelata facie speculando : et ita corde pacifico et sincero, præparemus Domino habitationem in nobis.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a pleasant psalm, delightful and full of the praises of God, which it befits us to recite with inward sweetness, heartfelt joy and attentive understanding, so that we ourselves and each one of us may be a *Judea*, confessing the Lord in faith and deed, and an *Israel*, beholding his glory [[2 Cor 3:18|with open face|revelata facie]]; and so, with a peaceful and sincere heart, let us prepare for the Lord a dwelling in us.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus, scrutator renum et cordium, cui omnis confitetur cogitatio hominum, mentium nostrarum infirma benedictionis tuæ virtute corrobora : ut quæ justa et pia sunt, cogitemus, et vota fidelia recte vivendo, tibi Domino Deo nostro reddamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, searcher of reins and hearts, to whom every thought of men gives praise, strengthen the weakness of our minds by the power of thy blessing, that we may think what is just and holy, and, by living rightly, pay our faithful vows to thee, the Lord our God.

76.title: EXPLANATIO PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI SEXTI: VOCE MEA AD DOMINUM CLAMAVI.
76.title_en: Explanation of the seventy-sixth psalm: I cried to the Lord with my voice.

paras.t: Declarandus nunc psalmus, hoc titulo præsignatur: In finem, pro Idithun, psalmus Asaph. Idithun interpretatur transiliens, Asaph autem congregatio. Est igitur sensus: Psalmus Asaph, id est tractatus iste congregationi fidelium, puta Ecclesiæ, competens, atque in finem, qui Christus est et vita æterna, nos dirigens, scriptus ac editus est pro Idithun, id est pro viro perfecto, universa caduca, omnia vana, cuncta transitoria, creata atque finita transiliente, parvi pendente et contemnente, et sola divina, æterna, cœlestia, vel potius ipsum supersimplicem Deum summe et unice concupiscente. Vere equidem, quemadmodum beatissimus Augustinus fatetur, sentire, gustare, seu intellectualiter sapere nequit hujus psalmi virtutem ac sensum, nisi qui hoc modo invenitur transiliens, qui omnia cum Apostolo arbitratur ut stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciat.
paras.en: The psalm now to be explained is headed with this title: [[76:1|Unto the end, for Idithun, a psalm of Asaph|In finem, pro Idithun, psalmus Asaph]]. *Idithun* is interpreted "leaping over", and *Asaph* "congregation". The sense, then, is this: [[76:1|A psalm of Asaph|Psalmus Asaph]], that is, this treatise, which befits the congregation of the faithful, namely the Church, and which directs us [[76:1|unto the end|in finem]], who is Christ and life eternal, was written and published [[76:1|for Idithun|pro Idithun]], that is, for the perfect man, who leaps over all things perishable, all things vain, all things passing, created and finite, makes little of them and despises them, and longs supremely and singly for divine, eternal and heavenly things alone, or rather for the supersimple God himself. Truly indeed, as the most blessed Augustine says, no one can feel, taste, or understand with the mind the power and sense of this psalm, except one who is found leaping over in this way, who with the Apostle counts all things [[Phil 3:8|but as dung, that I may gain Christ|ut stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciat]].

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta in persona viri justi sive Ecclesiæ, ait: Voce mea ad Dominum clamavi, id est, voce cordi meo consentiente, voce attenta et propria, non aliena, ad Dominum clamavi, non tam alto sono, quam magno affectu: nisi quod forte ex desiderio ferventi prorumpit homo in clamorem vocalem. Clamavi ergo ardenter orando, non quasi Deus longe distaret a me, aut suscitandus esset meo clamore, quum ipse ubique exsistat, et omnia distincte agnoscat; sed clamavi, quatenus Deus conspiciens me facere quod in me est, et studii ac desiderii mei impetum cernens, statim mihi attendat: quemadmodum scriptum est, Si Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus, et mundus ac rectus incesseris, statim evigilabit ad te. Voce mea interiori seu exteriori, ad Deum clamavi, ipsum solummodo invocando, in eum sperando, et non aliud ab ipso, nisi ipsum petendo, et ea quibus indigeo, ad hoc quod ad eum pertingam: nec inaniter feci hoc, quia et intendit mihi Deus, considerando clementer precem meam, et eam exaudiendo. Ostendit ergo in me verum esse quod ait Scriptura: Quis invocavit Deum, et despexit illum? Atque in Evangelio: Omnia quæcumque petitis, credite quia accipietis, et evenient vobis. Porro in hoc versu et in sequentibus profitetur vir justus fructum suæ orationis et studium suæ devotionis, quatenus nobis exauditionis fiduciam præstet, nosque ad sanctæ conversationis et intimæ exercitationis exercitia incitet et inflammet.
paras.en: So the Prophet, speaking in the person of the just man or of the Church, says: [[76:2|I cried to the Lord with my voice|Voce mea ad Dominum clamavi]], that is, with a voice in accord with my heart, a voice attentive and my own, not another's, I cried to the Lord, not so much with a loud sound as with great affection; unless perhaps out of fervent desire a man breaks out into a cry of the voice. I cried, then, praying ardently, not as though God were far distant from me, or had to be roused by my cry, since he is everywhere and knows all things distinctly; but I cried so that God, seeing me do what is in me [that is, all that lies in my power], and beholding the force of my zeal and desire, might at once attend to me: as it is written, If thou [[Job 8:5|wilt beseech the Almighty|Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus]], and [[Job 8:6|wilt walk clean and upright, he will presently awake unto thee|mundus ac rectus incesseris, statim evigilabit ad te]]. [[76:2|with my voice|Voce mea]], inward or outward, [[76:2|to God|ad Deum]] I cried, calling upon him alone, hoping in him, and asking of him nothing but himself, and the things I need in order to reach him: nor did I do this in vain, for [[76:2|he gave ear to me|et intendit mihi]], God, that is, considering my prayer mercifully and hearing it. So he showed in me the truth of what the Scripture says: [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath called upon him, and he despised him?|Quis invocavit Deum, et despexit illum?]] And in the Gospel: [[Mark 11:24|all things, whatsoever you ask when ye pray, believe that you shall receive: and they shall come unto you|Omnia quæcumque petitis, credite quia accipietis, et evenient vobis]]. Moreover, in this verse and those that follow the just man declares the fruit of his prayer and the zeal of his devotion, so as to give us confidence of being heard, and to stir us up and inflame us to the exercises of a holy life and of inward discipline.

paras.t: In die tribulationis meæ, id est tempore adversitatis, persecutionis seu tentationis, Deum in adjutorem et salvatorem exquisivi, id est, eximio modo diligentique studio expetivi, manibus meis corporalibus ad cœlos expansis: quemadmodum ait Jeremias in Threnis, Levemus corda nostra cum manibus in cœlum. Vel, Manibus meis, id est operibus bonis, quæ vim sortiuntur orationis, quia non cessat orare, qui non cessat bene agere. Nocte, id est tempore nocturno, quod ad orandum convenientissimum est, propter cessationem exteriorum strepituum, atque vacationem sensuum exteriorum. Propter quod Isaias: Anima mea, inquit, desideravit te in nocte. Et Jeremias: Consurge, lauda in nocte, in principio vigiliarum. Vel, Nocte, id est in vita præsenti, quæ per comparationem ad diem æternitatis vitamque futuram, nox potius appellatur quam dies. Sic vero oravi contra eum, id est, dirigendo oculos meos ad locum mihi ex adverso seu in opposito situm, in quo habitat Deus, videlicet ad cœlum empyreum, quod est contra me, quia est sursum, et ego deorsum. Vel, Contra eum, id est coram eo, constituendo me ipsum in præsentia Dei, eumque velut præsentem precando: secundum quod ait Elias, Vivit Dominus, in cujus conspectu sto hodie. Nam loco ejus quod hic dicitur, Contra eum, alia translatio habet, Coram eo. Et non sum deceptus, id est, fraudatus non sum spei meæ effectu, sed verum esse expertus sum, quod in Evangelio scriptum est: Omnis qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur. Sacra Scriptura neminem fallit, sed possibilius est cœlum et terram transire, quam unum apicem de lege perire, ut ait Salvator. Quoniam ergo divina Scriptura frequenter promittit Deum adesse omnibus invocantibus eum, palam omnino est, nullum invocantium Deum decipi posse, si tamen oret sicut orandum est. Quomodo enim orandum sit, Christus ostendit: Oportet, inquiens, semper orare, et non deficere. Et istud certissime credere atque sperare debemus, et ex tam certa atque fideli fiducia Deum rogare; sicque nequaquam fallemur: quanto enim fiducialius exoramus, tanto libentius liberaliusque exaudit nos.
paras.en: [[76:3|In the days of my trouble|In die tribulationis meæ]], that is, in the time of adversity, persecution or temptation, [[76:3|I sought God|Deum exquisivi]] as helper and saviour, that is, I sought him in an excellent manner and with diligent zeal, [[76:3|with my hands|manibus meis]], my bodily hands, spread out towards the heavens: as Jeremias says in the Lamentations, [[Lam 3:41|Let us lift up our hearts with our hands|Levemus corda nostra cum manibus]] to heaven. Or, *with my hands*, that is, with good works, which take on the force of prayer, for he does not cease to pray who does not cease to do good. [[76:3|in the night|Nocte]], that is, in the night-time, which is most fitting for prayer, because the noises outside cease and the outward senses are at rest. For this reason Isaias says: [[Is 26:9|My soul|Anima mea]], he says, [[Is 26:9|hath desired thee in the night|desideravit te in nocte]]. And Jeremias: [[Lam 2:19|Arise, give praise in the night, in the beginning of the watches|Consurge, lauda in nocte, in principio vigiliarum]]. Or, *in the night*, that is, in the present life, which, compared with the day of eternity and the life to come, is called night rather than day. Thus I prayed [[76:3|lifted up to him|contra eum]] [literally "over against him"; the Douay-Rheims renders the phrase "lifted up to him"], that is, directing my eyes to the place set opposite me, over against me, where God dwells, namely to the empyrean heaven, which is over against me, since it is above and I am below. Or, *over against him*, that is, before him, setting myself in the presence of God and praying to him as present: as Elias says, [[3 Kings 17:1|As the Lord liveth|Vivit Dominus]], [[3 Kings 17:1|in whose sight I stand|in cujus conspectu sto]] this day. For in place of what is said here, *over against him*, another translation has *before him*. [[76:3|and I was not deceived|Et non sum deceptus]], that is, I was not cheated of the fulfilment of my hope, but found by experience the truth of what is written in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:8|every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shall be opened|Omnis qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur]][[Luke 11:10||]]. Holy Scripture deceives no one; rather, as the Saviour says, it is easier for [[Luke 16:17|heaven and earth to pass than one tittle of the law to fall|cœlum et terram transire, quam unum apicem de lege perire]][[Matt 5:18||]]. Since, then, divine Scripture often promises that God is near to all who call upon him, it is altogether plain that none of those who call upon God can be deceived, provided he prays as one ought to pray. For how one ought to pray, Christ shows: [[Luke 18:1|we ought|Oportet]], he says, [[Luke 18:1|always to pray and not to faint|semper orare, et non deficere]]. And this we must most surely believe and hope, and ask God with a confidence so sure and faithful[[Jas 1:6||]] [the margin gives James i, 5–7]; and so we shall by no means be deceived: for the more confidently we entreat him, the more gladly and generously he hears us.

paras.t: Consequenter inducit saluberrimum documentum et institutionem perfectam, qua homo divina exauditione, consolatione et perpetua inhabitatione dignus efficitur. Renuit consolari anima mea, id est, in præsenti sæculo ærumnoso, afflictionibus pleno: in quo ego multipliciter tribulor, temporalia amittendo, corporaliter infirmando, tentationes varias incidendo, pro peccatis meis ac alienis plorando, et maxime quoniam minus quam cupio, in spiritualibus bonis proficio, sæpius cado, gratiæ minorationem sustineo, internæ consolationis atque fervoris suspensionem incurro, menteque durus ac sterilis fio; sed in tantis miseriis nolo consolationem vilem recipere, contemno in temporalibus exsultare, sperno humana solatia, inania verba, gesta scurrilia, atque ob Dei mei super omnia prædilecti amorem, omnem adulterinam lætitiam respuo, confidens et præstolans eum reversurum ad me, et animam meam, ejus amore afflictam et languidam, clementissime consolaturum. Istud autem est signum perfecti atque sinceri amoris, omnem consolationem dilecto contrariam aspernari, ejusque reditum longanimiter præstolari. Unde dilectæ amatrici dicitur per Osee: Dies multos exspectabis me, et non fornicaberis, et non eris viro. Apud eumdem Osee quoque Dominus ait: Populus meus pendebit ad reditum meum. Qui talis est, potest dicere illud Ecclesiastæ: Risum reputavi errorem, et gaudio dixi, Quid frustra deciperis? Ideoque Salomon iterum profitetur: Melius est ire ad domum luctus, quam ad domum convivii. In illa enim finis cunctorum admonetur hominum, et vivens cogitat quid futurum sit. Porro consolationem habentibus in divitiis, deliciis, honoribus, domibus, familiis atque similibus mundi hujus stultitiis, ait Christus: Væ vobis divitibus, qui habetis consolationem vestram. Hæc autem ad religiosos et solitarios tanto amplius pertinent, quanto ipsi ad eminentiorem Divinitatis dilectionem tenentur. Ipsorum enim est, in solo Domino delectari.
paras.en: Next he brings in a most wholesome teaching and a perfect instruction, by which a man is made worthy of being heard by God, of his consolation and of his abiding indwelling. [[76:3|My soul refused to be comforted|Renuit consolari anima mea]], that is, in this present world, full of hardship and afflictions, in which I am troubled in many ways: losing temporal things, falling sick in body, meeting with various temptations, weeping for my own sins and those of others, and above all because I make less progress in spiritual goods than I desire, fall more often, suffer a lessening of grace, and undergo the withdrawal of inward consolation and fervour, and become hard and barren in mind; yet in such great miseries I will not accept a base consolation, I scorn to exult in temporal things, I spurn human comforts, idle words, buffoonish doings, and for love of my God, beloved above all things, I reject every adulterous joy[[Phil 3:8||]] [the margin gives Philipp. iii, 8 here: Denis's thought recalls the Apostle counting all things as dung; no words are quoted], trusting and waiting for him to return to me and most mercifully to comfort my soul, afflicted and languishing with love of him. And this is the sign of a perfect and sincere love: to spurn every consolation contrary to the Beloved, and to wait with long patience for his return. Hence it is said through Osee to the beloved bride: [[Osee 3:3|Thou shalt wait for me many days: thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt be no man's|Dies multos exspectabis me, et non fornicaberis, et non eris viro]]. In the same Osee, too, the Lord says: [[Osee 11:7|my people shall long for my return|Populus meus pendebit ad reditum meum]]. One who is such can say that word of Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 2:2|Laughter I counted error: and to mirth I said: Why art thou vainly deceived?|Risum reputavi errorem, et gaudio dixi, Quid frustra deciperis?]] And so Solomon declares again: [[Eccles 7:3|It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to the house of feasting: for in that we are put in mind of the end of all, and the living thinketh what is to come|Melius est ire ad domum luctus, quam ad domum convivii. In illa enim finis cunctorum admonetur hominum, et vivens cogitat quid futurum sit]]. Moreover, to those who have their consolation in riches, delights, honours, houses, households and the like follies of this world, Christ says: [[Luke 6:24|woe to you that are rich: for you have your consolation|Væ vobis divitibus, qui habetis consolationem vestram]]. These things concern religious and solitaries all the more, the more they are bound to a more eminent love of the Godhead. For it is theirs to delight in the Lord alone.

paras.t: Memor fui Dei, bonitatem ipsius contemplando, beneficia ejus recolendo, promissa ipsius exspectando, et delectatus sum, intellectuali delectatione ex hujusmodi speculatione; et exercitatus sum, id est, occupavi me ipsum in laudibus atque operibus Dei: quoniam caritas otiosa non est; et defecit spiritus meus: vel quoniam Deum digne laudare, sufficienter cognoscere, plene amare, efficaciter honorare non valuit; vel quoniam ex magna atque ecstatica elevatione seu raptu in Deum, a semetipso alienatus est, id est, ab exteriorum sensuum operatione abstractus, et in Deum omnino absorptus, sicut sæpius contingit devotissimis pueris Domini Salvatoris, quibus Deus ostendit divitias gloriæ suæ.
paras.en: [[76:4|I remembered God|Memor fui Dei]], contemplating his goodness, recalling his benefits, awaiting his promises, [[76:4|and was delighted|et delectatus sum]] with an intellectual delight arising from such contemplation; [[76:4|and was exercised|et exercitatus sum]], that is, I occupied myself in the praises and works of God, since charity is not idle; [[76:4|and my spirit swooned away|et defecit spiritus meus]]: either because it was not able to praise God worthily, know him sufficiently, love him fully, honour him effectually; or because, through a great and ecstatic elevation or rapture into God, it was taken out of itself, that is, withdrawn from the working of the outward senses and wholly absorbed in God, as often befalls the most devout children of the Lord the Saviour, to whom God shows [[Rom 9:23|the riches of his glory|divitias gloriæ suæ]].

paras.t: Anticipaverunt vigilias oculi mei: id est, ante lucem surrexi, seu tempus quo alii surgunt, præveni, quatenus Deum orarem, laudarem et contemplarer: quemadmodum in Scriptura habetur, Justus cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum. Hoc in amorosis famulis Christi efficit æstuans amor, qui separationis impatiens est, semperque ad unionem et amplexum Dilecti suspirat. Ignorat siquidem tarda molimina benedicti Creatoris dilectio fervida, quia de ea veraciter scriptum est: Aquæ multæ non poterunt exstinguere caritatem. Lampades ejus, lampades ignis atque flammarum. Turbatus sum ex consideratione peccatorum meorum, quibus intus commaculor, et laqueorum seu periculorum, quibus foris circumdor; et non sum locutus, id est, præ nimia confusione os meum ad Dominum aperire ausus non fui: secundum quod in primo libro Esdræ habetur: Deus meus, confundor et erubesco levare faciem meam ad te, quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt super caput nostrum, et delicta nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum. Similiter tres pueri loquebantur in camino: Et nunc non possumus aperire os; confusio et opprobrium facti sumus. Verumtamen non debet homo in tali formidine diu persistere, ne desperet: talia enim dicuntur ad insinuandum gravitatem nostrorum facinorum. Vel, Non sum locutus, excusando me ipsum, aut aliis mea scelera imponendo, aut humanam refocillationem quærendo. Vel, Non sum locutus, aliis considerationum mearum secreta pandendo; sed feci quod ab alio dictum est, Secretum meum mihi, secretum meum mihi.
paras.en: [[76:5|My eyes prevented the watches|Anticipaverunt vigilias oculi mei]] [*prevented*, that is, went before]: that is, I rose before daylight, or forestalled the time at which others rise, so as to pray to God, praise him and contemplate him: as is found in the Scripture, The just man [[Ecclus 39:6|will give his heart to resort early to the Lord|cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum]]. This is the work of burning love in the loving servants of Christ, which cannot bear separation and ever sighs for union with the Beloved and his embrace. For fervent love of the blessed Creator knows no slow efforts, since of it it is truly written: [[Cant 8:7|Many waters cannot quench charity|Aquæ multæ non poterunt exstinguere caritatem]]. [[Cant 8:6|the lamps thereof are fire and flames|Lampades ejus, lampades ignis atque flammarum]] [these words are from the verse before, Cant. viii, 6]. [[76:5|I was troubled|Turbatus sum]] by considering my sins, with which I am stained within, and the snares or dangers by which I am surrounded without; [[76:5|and I spoke not|et non sum locutus]], that is, out of excessive confusion I did not dare open my mouth to the Lord: according to what is found in the first book of Esdras: [[1 Esd 9:6|My God I am confounded and ashamed to lift up my face to thee: for our iniquities are multiplied over our heads, and our sins are grown up even unto heaven|Deus meus, confundor et erubesco levare faciem meam ad te, quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt super caput nostrum, et delicta nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum]]. Likewise the three children said in the furnace: [[Dan 3:33|And now we cannot open our mouths: we are become a shame, and a reproach|Et nunc non possumus aperire os; confusio et opprobrium facti sumus]]. Yet a man must not persist long in such fear, lest he despair: for such things are said to bring home to us the gravity of our crimes. Or, *I spoke not*, excusing myself, or laying my crimes upon others, or seeking human refreshment. Or, *I spoke not*, revealing to others the secrets of my meditations; but I did what was said by another: [[Is 24:16|My secret to myself, my secret to myself|Secretum meum mihi, secretum meum mihi]].

paras.t: Cogitavi dies antiquos, id est, historias veteres et opera Dei ab exordio mundi, cursumque sæculi usque ad tempus jam instans recolui: juxta quod Ecclesiasticus dicit, Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in Prophetis vacabit. Sed quia inveni omnia quæ sub sole geruntur vanitati subjecta, idcirco et annos æternos in mente habui, id est, statum sæculi futuri, et diem quo vivunt electi cum Deo, reprobique in inferno, corde revolvi, quatenus ex consideratione æternarum lætitiarum in patria, perpetuorumque tormentorum in gehenna, contemnerem universa quæ modo delectant, patienterque ferrem quæcumque temporaliter gravant. O quam salubris est cogitatio talis! Si enim æternorum horum annorum longitudinem perpendamus, momentaneam arbitramur vitam præsentem, quantumcumque protractam; sicque in ejus contemptum atque in futuræ vitæ amorem accendimur: imo si quis a protoplasti parentis tempore usque in præsens vixisset, nonne omne tempus præteritum velut momentum videbitur, præsertim si ad futuræ vitæ æternos annos comparetur? Cordialiter ergo et præcordialissime penitus consideremus præsentis vitæ brevitatem, gaudiorum mundi fallaciam, hujusque status infinita pericula. Habeamus insuper in mente æternos annos qui restant, contemplando solatia electorum, atque supplicia reproborum: hisque pensatis, eligamus quod nobis amplius expedire censemus, vel nunc gaudere cum sæculo, et postmodum æternaliter cruciari cum reprobis in inferno, vel nunc sectari vestigia Christi, et paulo post possidere gaudia cœli. Hinc quippe sapientissimus Salomon loquitur: Si multis annis vixerit homo, et in his omnibus lætatus fuerit, meminisse debet tenebrosi temporis et dierum multorum, qui quum venerint, vanitatis arguentur præterita.
paras.en: [[76:6|I thought upon the days of old|Cogitavi dies antiquos]], that is, I recalled the ancient histories and the works of God from the beginning of the world, and the course of the ages up to the time now present: as Ecclesiasticus says, [[Ecclus 39:1|The wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be occupied in the prophets|Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in Prophetis vacabit]]. But because I found all things that are done under the sun subject to vanity[[Rom 8:20||]], therefore [[76:6|and I had in my mind the eternal years|et annos æternos in mente habui]], that is, I turned over in my heart the state of the world to come, and the day in which the elect live with God and the reprobate in hell, so that by considering the eternal joys in the fatherland and the everlasting torments in Gehenna I might despise all that now delights, and bear patiently whatever weighs upon us in time. O how wholesome is such a thought! For if we weigh the length of these eternal years, we reckon the present life momentary[[2 Cor 4:17||]], however long drawn out; and so we are kindled to despise it and to love the life to come. Indeed, if someone had lived from the time of our first parent until now, would not all the time gone by seem but a moment, especially if compared with the eternal years of the life to come? Let us therefore consider heartily and from our inmost heart the shortness of the present life, the deceitfulness of the joys of the world, and the endless dangers of this state. Let us moreover have in mind the eternal years that remain, contemplating the comforts of the elect and the torments of the reprobate; and having weighed these, let us choose what we judge more profitable for us: either to rejoice now with the world and afterwards to be tormented eternally with the reprobate in hell, or to follow now the footsteps of Christ and shortly after to possess the joys of heaven. Hence the most wise Solomon says: [[Eccles 11:8|If a man live many years, and have rejoiced in them all, he must remember the darksome time, and the many days: which when they shall come, the things past shall be accused of vanity|Si multis annis vixerit homo, et in his omnibus lætatus fuerit, meminisse debet tenebrosi temporis et dierum multorum, qui quum venerint, vanitatis arguentur præterita]].

paras.t: Et meditatus sum nocte cum corde meo: id est, intellectu meo non vana et frivola atque illicita cogitavi, sed in lege Domini versatus sum, discutiendo et intuendo qualiter æternos annos miserorum possem evadere, annosque æternos Beatorum in patria adipisci; et exercitabar, id est, mentaliter ac seriose occupabar in his, et scopebam spiritum meum, id est, animam meam discussi, conscientiam examinavi, et quidquid dignum erat remorsu, ejeci, mundavi, ac vitare decrevi.
paras.en: [[76:7|And I meditated in the night with my own heart|Et meditatus sum nocte cum corde meo]]: that is, with my understanding I thought no vain, frivolous or unlawful things, but busied myself in the law of the Lord, examining and considering how I might escape the eternal years of the wretched and attain the eternal years of the Blessed in the fatherland; [[76:7|and I was exercised|et exercitabar]], that is, I was occupied in these things in mind and in earnest, [[76:7|and I swept my spirit|et scopebam spiritum meum]], that is, I searched my soul, examined my conscience, and whatever deserved remorse I cast out, cleansed, and resolved to avoid.

paras.t: Sed quoniam Deus non semper exaudit hominem tam cito ut cupit, sed vicissim satis diu eum affligi permittit, propterea subditur vox justorum, qui in tali dilatione propter pœnarum ac persecutionum gravitatem, ex humana fragilitate conqueruntur et dicunt: Numquid in æternum projiciet Deus preces meas, ipsas non exaudiendo, nec me ad gratiam desideratam perducendo? Hic enim est modus loquendi afflictorum: quibus duratio modica, videtur longa; longa vero, æterna. Unde beatus Job ait: Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me; sto, et non respicis me. Aut non apponet ut complacitior sit adhuc? id est, numquid Deus semper æque crudelis et durus erit, nec poterit aliquo modo placari? Hæc autem non affirmando, sed negando dicuntur, sicut sequentia: imo Deus non solum dignatur placari, sed etiam occasionem quærit qua mitigetur, propter ineffabilissimam suam clementiam. Propter quod ipse apud Ezechielem testatur: Quæsivi virum qui interponeret sepem, et staret oppositus contra me pro terra, ne disperderem eam. Et Job: Si fuerit angelus pro homine loquens, miserebitur ei Deus, et dicet, Libera eum, inveni in quo ei propitier.
paras.en: But since God does not always hear a man as quickly as he wishes, but at times allows him to be afflicted for quite a long while[[Prov 1:28||]][[Mich 3:4||]], there follows the voice of the just, who in such a delay, because of the heaviness of their pains and persecutions, complain out of human frailty and say: [[76:8|Will God then cast off for ever|Numquid in æternum projiciet Deus]] my prayers, by not hearing them, nor bringing me to the grace I desire? For this is the way the afflicted speak: to them a short duration seems long, and a long one eternal. Hence blessed Job says: [[Job 30:20|I cry to thee, and thou hearest me not: I stand up, and thou dost not regard me|Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me; sto, et non respicis me]]. [[76:8|or will he never be more favourable again|Aut non apponet ut complacitior sit adhuc]]? that is, will God always be equally cruel and hard, and can he in no way be appeased? These things are said not affirming but denying, like those that follow: on the contrary, God not only deigns to be appeased, but even seeks an occasion to be softened, because of his most ineffable clemency. For this reason he himself testifies in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 22:30|I sought among them for a man that might set up a hedge, and stand in the gap before me in favour of the land, that I might not destroy it|Quæsivi virum qui interponeret sepem, et staret oppositus contra me pro terra, ne disperderem eam]]. And Job: [[Job 33:23|If there shall be an angel speaking for him|Si fuerit angelus pro homine loquens]], [[Job 33:24|He shall have mercy on him, and shall say: Deliver him|miserebitur ei Deus, et dicet, Libera eum]], [[Job 33:24|I have found wherein I may be merciful to him|inveni in quo ei propitier]].

paras.t: Aut in finem misericordiam suam abscindet, non subveniendo nobis viatoribus ad ipsum clamantibus? An, inquam, abscindet misericordiam suam, id est, an misericordiæ suæ effectum non impendet, a generatione in generationem, id est, in generationibus sibi succedentibus, visitando seu ulciscendo peccata parentum in posteros sine cessatione?
paras.en: [[76:9|Or will he cut off his mercy for ever|Aut in finem misericordiam suam abscindet]], by not coming to the help of us wayfarers who cry to him? Will he, I say, cut off his mercy, that is, will he not bestow the effect of his mercy, [[76:9|from generation to generation|a generatione in generationem]], that is, in the generations succeeding one another, visiting or avenging the sins of the parents upon their descendants without ceasing?

paras.t: Aut obliviscetur misereri Deus, cui proprium est misereri? aut continebit in ira sua, scilicet exercendo justitiam, seu infligendo vindictam, misericordias suas, non miscendo effectum misericordiæ operi suæ justitiæ, nec ab ultione et indignatione cessando? quasi dicat, Non: quoniam scriptum est de eo, Quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis. Porro nonnulli ex his verbis veritatis ac vitæ, occasionem sumpserunt falsitatis et mortis, dicentes quod pœna inferni quandoque esset terminum habitura, quum tamen manifeste pateat, quod præsens scriptura loquatur de Deo per comparationem ad viatores et pœnitentes.
paras.en: [[76:10|Or will God forget to shew mercy|Aut obliviscetur misereri Deus]], to whom it is proper to show mercy? [[76:10|or will he in his anger shut up|aut continebit in ira sua]], that is, in exercising justice or inflicting vengeance, [[76:10|his mercies|misericordias suas]], not mingling the effect of mercy with the work of his justice, nor ceasing from vengeance and indignation? As if to say: No; for it is written of him, [[Hab 3:2|when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy|Quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis]]. Moreover, some have taken from these words of truth and life an occasion of falsehood and death, saying that the pain of hell would at some time have an end [the error ascribed to Origen and his followers]; whereas it is quite plain that the present scripture speaks of God in relation to wayfarers [that is, those still on the way in this life] and penitents.

paras.t: Et dixi, Nunc cœpi : hæc mutatio dexteræ Excelsi. Hebraica veritas, translatio quoque Hieronymi juxta Hebræum, sic fertur habere : Et dixi, Imbecillitas mea est hæc : id est, secundum rationem asserui, quod prædicta querulatio ex fragilitatis humanæ imbecillitate nascatur. Nostra autem translatio ita exponitur : Et dixi, corde seu ore, Nunc cœpi, id est, jam primitus spiritualiter vivere, sapienter intelligere et vere cognoscere orsus sum, intelligendo præsentis sæculi vanitatem, et futuri sæculi felicitatem, vel totam pristinam meam conversationem, profectum et perfectionem pro nihilo arbitrando, atque cum recenti proposito, cum novo fervore, cum studio vehementi melioris vitæ semitas apprehendendo, spiritualis profectus itinera ingrediendo, imo quotidie quasi de novo incipiendo. Sic enim agendum esse docuerat illustris pater noster Arsenius. Nam et ipse beatus Apostolus ad nostram informationem professus est : Quæ priora sunt obliviscens, ad anteriora autem extendens me ipsum. Christus quoque : Quum feceritis, inquit, omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite : Servi inutiles sumus ; quod debuimus facere, fecimus. Non ergo gloriemur in meritis vitæ prioris, nec aliquid æstimemus nos ipsos ; sed quotidie tam recenter tamque ferventer agamus, ac si eodem die primum inchoaremus, atque morituri essemus, attendentes illud divini Apostoli : Ego non arbitror me apprehendisse ; sequor autem, si quo modo comprehendam.
paras.en: [[76:11|And I said, Now have I begun: this is the change of the right hand of the most High|Et dixi, Nunc cœpi : hæc mutatio dexteræ Excelsi]]. The Hebrew verity, and Jerome's translation from the Hebrew too, is said to read thus: And I said, This is my weakness; that is, I declared according to reason that the complaint made above springs from the weakness of human frailty. But our translation is expounded thus: [[76:11|And I said|Et dixi]] in heart or by mouth, [[76:11|Now have I begun|Nunc cœpi]]: that is, now for the first time I have set out to live spiritually, to understand wisely and to know truly: by understanding the vanity of the present world and the happiness of the world to come; or by counting as nothing all my former way of life, my progress and perfection, and with a fresh resolve, with new fervour, with vehement zeal laying hold of the paths of a better life, entering upon the roads of spiritual progress, nay, beginning every day as it were anew. For so our illustrious father Arsenius had taught that we must do [that is, Abbot Arsenius, one of the Desert Fathers]. And the blessed Apostle himself, for our instruction, professed: [[Phil 3:13|Forgetting the things that are behind and stretching forth myself to those that are before|Quæ priora sunt obliviscens, ad anteriora autem extendens me ipsum]]. Christ too: [[Luke 17:10|when you shall have done|Quum feceritis]], he says, [[Luke 17:10|all these things that are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which we ought to do|omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite : Servi inutiles sumus ; quod debuimus facere, fecimus]]. Let us not glory, then, in the merits of our former life, nor think ourselves anything; but let us act every day as freshly and as fervently as if we were beginning for the first time that very day and were to die, heeding that saying of the divine Apostle: [[Phil 3:13|I do not count myself to have apprehended|Ego non arbitror me apprehendisse]]; [[Phil 3:12|but I follow after, if I may by any means apprehend|sequor autem, si quo modo comprehendam]].

paras.t: Sed quoniam iste profectus non humanæ virtutis est, sed donum gratiæ Dei, ideo subditur : hæc mutatio dexteræ Excelsi : id est, quod ita mutatus sum de tenebris ignorantiæ ad splendorem scientiæ, de vitiis in virtutes, de carnali et animali in spiritualem, adscribendum est pio subsidio seu misericordi præsentiæ Dei sublimis. Non enim sufficientes sumus cogitare aliquid a nobis quasi ex nobis ; sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Unde a Jeremia dictum est : Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est ut ambulet et dirigat gressus suos. Propterea dicit Apostolus : Deus est qui operatur in vobis velle et perficere pro bona voluntate.
paras.en: But since this progress is not of human power but a gift of the grace of God, there is added: [[76:11|this is the change of the right hand of the most High|hæc mutatio dexteræ Excelsi]]: that is, that I have been changed in this way, from the darkness of ignorance to the splendour of knowledge, from vices to virtues, from carnal and animal to spiritual, is to be ascribed to the loving help or merciful presence of God most high. For we are not [[2 Cor 3:5|sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God|sufficientes sumus cogitare aliquid a nobis quasi ex nobis ; sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]. Hence it was said by Jeremias: [[Jer 10:23|I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his: neither is it in a man to walk, and to direct his steps|Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est ut ambulet et dirigat gressus suos]]. Therefore the Apostle says: [[Phil 2:13|it is God who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish, according to his good will|Deus est qui operatur in vobis velle et perficere pro bona voluntate]].

paras.t: Verumtamen omnia jam prædicta ab illo versu, Numquid in æternum projiciet Deus? usque ad versum præsentem, accipi possunt non solum quasi ex infirmitate prolata, sed quasi consolatorie negativeque dicta, videlicet ut sic dicta sumantur, quod Deus in æternum non projicit, nec placari contemnit, neque finaliter misericordiam suam abscindet, etc. ; sicque anima orantis roboratur ex his ad perseveranter fiducialiterque orandum, etiam quamvis Deus longo tempore differat.
paras.en: Nevertheless, all that has been said from the verse [[76:8|Will God then cast off for ever?|Numquid in æternum projiciet Deus?]] up to the present verse can be taken not only as spoken out of infirmity, but as said by way of consolation and in the negative: that is, so that they are taken to mean that God does not cast off for ever, nor scorns to be appeased, nor will finally cut off his mercy, etc. And so the soul of one who prays is strengthened by these words to pray perseveringly and with confidence, even though God delay for a long time.

paras.t: Memor fui operum Domini, id est gratiarum ac misericordiarum suarum, quas mihi ostendit, infudit ac præstitit : quia Apostolus ait, Noli negligere gratiam Dei, quæ data est tibi. Hujus quoque memoriæ meæ signum est, quia memor ero ab initio mirabilium tuorum, quæ fecisti ab origine mundi in cœlo, terra, marique.
paras.en: [[76:12|I remembered the works of the Lord|Memor fui operum Domini]], that is, his graces and mercies, which he has shown me, poured into me and bestowed on me: for the Apostle says, [[1 Tim 4:14|Neglect not the grace|Noli negligere gratiam]] of God, [[1 Tim 4:14|which was given thee|quæ data est tibi]]. And a sign of this remembrance of mine is [[76:12|for I will be mindful of thy wonders from the beginning|quia memor ero ab initio mirabilium tuorum]], which thou hast done from the origin of the world in heaven, on earth and in the sea.

paras.t: Et meditabor in omnibus operibus tuis, quæ in sacra Scriptura lego vel audio, contemplando te Deum operatorem ex tuis operibus : quemadmodum Apostolus asserit, Invisibilia Dei per ea quæ facta sunt, conspiciuntur, sempiterna quoque virtus ejus et divinitas. Et Sapiens : A magnitudine speciei et creaturæ, poterit creator horum cognoscibiliter videri.
paras.en: [[76:13|And I will meditate on all thy works|Et meditabor in omnibus operibus tuis]], which I read or hear of in Holy Scripture, contemplating thee, God, the worker, from thy works: as the Apostle declares, [[Rom 1:20|the invisible things of him|Invisibilia Dei]] [[Rom 1:20|are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made|per ea quæ facta sunt, conspiciuntur]]; [[Rom 1:20|His eternal power also and divinity|sempiterna quoque virtus ejus et divinitas]]. And the Wise Man: [[Wis 13:5|by the greatness of the beauty, and of the creature, the creator of them may be seen, so as to be known thereby|A magnitudine speciei et creaturæ, poterit creator horum cognoscibiliter videri]].

paras.t: Et in adinventionibus tuis, id est in secretissimis illis mysteriis redemptionis humanæ, quæ tu solus ineffabiliter excogitasti, decernens humanum genus esse redimendum per Christi incarnationem, passionem, ac mortem, exercebor, talia cordialiter revolvendo : quemadmodum Jeremias eloquitur, Memoria memor ero, et tabescet in me anima mea ; et subdit, Hæc recolens in corde meo, in Deo sperabo. Verissime namque confidit in Domino, quicumque considerat eum talia adinvenisse atque fecisse seu pertulisse pro genere humano.
paras.en: And [[76:13|in thy inventions|Et in adinventionibus tuis]], that is, in those most secret mysteries of man's redemption which thou alone didst unspeakably devise, decreeing that mankind was to be redeemed through the incarnation, passion and death of Christ, [[76:13|will be employed|exercebor]], turning such things over in my heart: as Jeremias says, [[Lam 3:20|I will be mindful and remember, and my soul shall languish within me|Memoria memor ero, et tabescet in me anima mea]]; and he adds, [[Lam 3:21|These things I shall think over in my heart, therefore will I hope|Hæc recolens in corde meo, in Deo sperabo]] [Denis reads "I will hope in God"]. For whoever considers that he devised and did, or suffered, such things for mankind trusts most truly in the Lord.

paras.t: Vel, In adinventionibus tuis, id est in præceptis et consiliis tuis, quæ pro nostra salute instituisti. Dicitur autem Deus adinvenisse, non utique inquirendo aut proficiendo, sed aliunde non accipiendo. Talis namque locutio atque consimiles, negative sunt exponendæ. Et hoc modo apud alium scriptum est : Qui fecit stellas ; hic est Deus noster, et non æstimabitur alius adversus eum. Hic adinvenit omnem viam disciplinæ. Pensandum tamen, quod hoc dictum est de Filio Dei. Sequitur enim : Post hæc super terram visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est. Quum ergo Filius Dei a Patre acceperit quidquid habet et est, quomodo dicitur omnem viam disciplinæ adinvenisse? præsertim quum ipse evidenter testatus sit, Pater diligit Filium, et omnia demonstrat ei quæ ipse facit ; et alibi, A me ipso non loquor, sed sicut docuit me Pater. Non enim ista dicuntur de Christo dumtaxat propter naturam assumptam, quum de Spiritu Sancto Christus dicat, Non loquetur a semetipso, sed quæcumque audiet, loquetur. Et respondendum, quod Filius Dei dicitur omnem viam disciplinæ invenisse, quoniam non accepit ab aliquo substantialiter a se condistincto : imo ipse et Pater sunt una sapientia, unumque omnis sapientiæ creatæ principium : quia de Filio scriptum est, Fons sapientiæ Verbum Dei in excelsis.
paras.en: Or, [[76:13|in thy inventions|In adinventionibus tuis]], that is, in thy precepts and counsels, which thou didst institute for our salvation. Now God is said to have found out, not indeed by searching or by making progress, but by not receiving from elsewhere: for such expressions and the like are to be expounded negatively. And in this way it is written in another: He who made the stars[[Bar 3:35||]]: [[Bar 3:36|This is our God, and there shall no other be accounted of in comparison of him|hic est Deus noster, et non æstimabitur alius adversus eum]]. [[Bar 3:37|He found out all the way of knowledge|Hic adinvenit omnem viam disciplinæ]] [*disciplina*, "discipline" or "teaching"]. It is to be weighed, however, that this was said of the Son of God; for there follows: [[Bar 3:38|Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|Post hæc super terram visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]]. Since, then, the Son of God received from the Father whatever he has and is, how is he said to have found out all the way of knowledge? especially since he himself plainly testified, [[John 5:20|the Father loveth the Son and sheweth him all things which himself doth|Pater diligit Filium, et omnia demonstrat ei quæ ipse facit]]; and elsewhere, [[John 14:10|I speak not of myself|A me ipso non loquor]], [[John 8:28|But as the Father hath taught me|sed sicut docuit me Pater]]. For these things are not said of Christ only on account of the nature he assumed, since Christ says of the Holy Ghost, [[John 16:13|he shall not speak of himself: but what things soever he shall hear, he shall speak|Non loquetur a semetipso, sed quæcumque audiet, loquetur]]. And the answer is that the Son of God is said to have found out all the way of knowledge because he did not receive it from anyone substantially distinct from himself: nay, he and the Father are one wisdom, and one principle of all created wisdom; for it is written of the Son, [[Ecclus 1:5|The word of God on high is the fountain of wisdom|Fons sapientiæ Verbum Dei in excelsis]].

paras.t: Deus, in sancto via tua : id est, in Christo, Sancto Sanctorum, est via colendi te : quoniam ipse est omnis virtutis ac perfectionis magister, exemplar et causa ; et qui sequitur eum, non ambulat in tenebris, sed ingredietur per fidem et contemplationem, et egredietur per operationem. Ipse quoque est via, veritas et vita. Vel sic : Deus, in sancto, id est in omni corde puro, est via tua, id est observatio mandatorum tuorum. Vel, In sancto via tua, id est, via tua, scilicet lex divina, in vera sanctitate consistit, quemadmodum Daniel commemorat : Benedictus es, Domine, quia justus es in omnibus, et viæ tuæ rectæ, et omnia judicia tua vera. Quis Deus magnus in omni nobilitate, sapientia, pulchritudine, majestate, beatitudine, sanctitate, dulcedine, sicut Deus noster, qui est trinus in Personis, et in essentia simplex? Nullus utique, quoniam Deus sublimis et benedictus omnia alia incomparabiliter seu infinite excedit. Propter quod ait Isaias propheta : Cui similem fecistis Deum? aut quam imaginem ponetis ei?
paras.en: [[76:14|Thy way, O God, is in the holy place|Deus, in sancto via tua]] [*in sancto*, "in the holy", which Denis takes also as "in the Holy One"]: that is, in Christ, the Holy of Holies, is the way of worshipping thee; for he is the master, the exemplar and the cause of all virtue and perfection; and [[John 8:12|He that followeth me walketh not in darkness|qui sequitur eum, non ambulat in tenebris]], but [[John 10:9|he shall go in|ingredietur]] by faith and contemplation, [[John 10:9|and go out|et egredietur]] by working. He too is [[John 14:6|the way, and the truth, and the life|via, veritas et vita]]. Or thus: [[76:14|O God|Deus]], [[76:14|in the holy place|in sancto]], that is, in every pure heart, is [[76:14|Thy way|via tua]], that is, the keeping of thy commandments. Or, [[76:14|Thy way, O God, is in the holy place|In sancto via tua]]: that is, thy way, namely the divine law, consists in true holiness, as Daniel recalls: [[Dan 3:26|Blessed art thou, O Lord|Benedictus es, Domine]], [[Dan 3:27|For thou art just in all|quia justus es in omnibus]], [[Dan 3:27|and thy ways right, and all thy judgments true|et viæ tuæ rectæ, et omnia judicia tua vera]] [the margin gives "Daniel 26. 27", without the chapter: Dan 3:26–27]. [[76:14|who is the great God|Quis Deus magnus]] in all nobility, wisdom, beauty, majesty, blessedness, holiness and sweetness, [[76:14|like our God|sicut Deus noster]], who is three in Persons and simple in essence? None indeed, for God, sublime and blessed, exceeds all other things beyond compare, that is, infinitely. Wherefore Isaias the prophet says: [[Is 40:18|To whom then have you likened God? or what image will you make for him?|Cui similem fecistis Deum? aut quam imaginem ponetis ei?]]

paras.t: Tu es Deus qui facis propria potestate mirabilia, id est supernaturalia opera : de quo in libro Job dicitur, Qui facit magna et inscrutabilia et mirabilia absque numero. Notam fecisti in populis virtutem tuam : id est, in Pharaone et in populo ejus demonstrasti potentiam tuam ; imo in populo universæ terræ notam fecisti virtutem tuam, ad quos fama dejectionis Ægyptiorum pervenit. Unde Deus ait ad Pharaonem : Idcirco posui te, ut ostenderem in te fortitudinem meam, et narretur nomen meum in omni terra. Hinc nempe et Jethro cognatus Moysi, Ægyptiorum dejectione audita, dixit : Nunc cognovi quoniam magnus Dominus super omnes deos.
paras.en: [[76:15|Thou art the God that dost|Tu es Deus qui facis]] by thine own power [[76:15|wonders|mirabilia]], that is, supernatural works: of whom it is said in the book of Job, [[Job 5:9|Who doth great things, and unsearchable and wonderful things without number|Qui facit magna et inscrutabilia et mirabilia absque numero]]. [[76:15|Thou hast made thy power known among the nations|Notam fecisti in populis virtutem tuam]]: that is, thou didst show thy might in Pharao and in his people; nay, thou didst make thy power known among the people of the whole earth, to whom the fame of the overthrow of the Egyptians came. Hence God says to Pharao: [[Ex 9:16|therefore have I raised thee, that I may shew my power in thee, and my name may be spoken of throughout all the earth|Idcirco posui te, ut ostenderem in te fortitudinem meam, et narretur nomen meum in omni terra]]. Hence indeed Jethro too, the kinsman of Moses, having heard of the overthrow of the Egyptians, said: [[Ex 18:11|Now I know, that the Lord is great above all gods|Nunc cognovi quoniam magnus Dominus super omnes deos]].

paras.t: Redemisti in brachio tuo, id est, in fortitudine tua de manu et terra Ægyptiorum eduxisti, populum tuum, filios Jacob et Joseph, id est, tam eos qui nati sunt ex his, qui simul cum Jacob in Ægyptum a terra Chanaan descenderunt, quam eos qui nati sunt ex his, quos genuit Joseph in terra Ægypti, videlicet ex Ephraim et Manasse.
paras.en: [[76:16|With thy arm thou hast redeemed|Redemisti in brachio tuo]], that is, by thy strength thou didst bring out of the hand and land of the Egyptians [[76:16|thy people the children of Jacob and of Joseph|populum tuum, filios Jacob et Joseph]]: that is, both those born of the men who went down into Egypt with Jacob from the land of Chanaan[[Gen 46:8||]], and those born of the sons whom Joseph begot in the land of Egypt, namely of Ephraim and Manasses[[Num 1:1||]] [the margin gives Num. i, the numbering of the tribes].

paras.t: Viderunt te aquæ, Deus : id est, ita tibi obedivit mare Rubrum in sua divisione et consolidatione, ac si fuisset intellectualis naturæ, et tuum imperium cognovisset. Omnia enim ad nutum divino parent imperio per obedientialem potentiam, omni naturæ creatæ ingenitam. Repetitur autem ista sententia ad confirmationem : viderunt te aquæ maris Rubri, et timuerunt, id est, per modum timentis se habuerunt, fugiendo versus ripas, atque in modum muri illic sistendo ; et turbatæ sunt abyssi, id est ambæ partes maris Rubri, eo quod contra, vel potius supra naturam steterunt ex lateribus, neque fluebant in locum inferiorem donec transissent filii Israel, sicut habetur in Exodo : Filii Israel ambulaverunt per medium sicci maris, et aquæ eis erant quasi pro muro a dextris et a sinistris.
paras.en: [[76:17|The waters saw thee, O God|Viderunt te aquæ, Deus]]: that is, the Red Sea so obeyed thee in its dividing and its making firm as if it had been of an intellectual nature and had known thy command[[Ex 14:21||]][[Ex 14:22||]]. For all things obey the divine command at its nod by the obediential power [that is, the capacity, inborn in every creature, to be moved by God beyond its natural powers] inborn in every created nature. And this sentence is repeated for confirmation: [[76:17|the waters saw thee|viderunt te aquæ]] of the Red Sea, [[76:17|and they were afraid|et timuerunt]], that is, they behaved after the manner of one afraid, fleeing towards the banks and standing there like a wall; [[76:17|and the depths were troubled|et turbatæ sunt abyssi]], that is, both parts of the Red Sea, because they stood at the sides against nature, or rather above it, and did not flow into the lower place until the children of Israel had passed over, as we have it in Exodus: [[Ex 14:29|the children of Israel marched through the midst of the sea upon dry land, and the waters were to them as a wall on the right hand and on the left|Filii Israel ambulaverunt per medium sicci maris, et aquæ eis erant quasi pro muro a dextris et a sinistris]].

paras.t: Multitudo sonitus aquarum : id est, magnus sonus seu strepitus erat in aquis maris Rubri, quoniam cum ingenti fragore ac impetu revertebantur aquæ maris Rubri ad locum priorem, et super Ægyptios, ferebanturque Ægyptii in profundum ; vocem dederunt nubes, id est, ex columna ignis ac nubis Deus fecit procedere fulgura atque tonitrua contra Ægyptios. Etenim sagittæ tuæ transeunt : id est, pœnæ tuæ in Ægyptios processerunt, quorum subvertisti currus et equites ; vox tonitrui tui, id est sonus tonitruorum illorum, fuit in rota, id est, ad similitudinem rotæ se habuit : quoniam sicut rotarum simul currentium strepitus magnus est, ita erat vox tonitruorum tuorum, ex nube prædicta egredientium. Illuxerunt coruscationes tuæ orbi terræ : id est, fulgura tua in terra Ægypti fulgere fecisti, quemadmodum scriptum est : Dominus dedit tonitrua et grandinem ac discurrentia fulgura super terram. Vel : Illuxerunt coruscationes tuæ orbi terræ, id est, coruscationes illæ in Ægypto factæ, ad omnium hominum pervenerunt notitiam. Commota est et contremuit terra : id est, Ægyptii ex tantis prodigiis moti sunt, quidam ad admirationem, quidam ad obstinationem, quidam vero ad unius Dei fidem et cultum, sicut vulgus illud promiscuum innumerabile, quod simul ascendit cum filiis Israel ex Ægypto, ut dicitur in Exodo. Contremuit quoque terra, id est, Ægyptii ex illis miraculis territi sunt. Vel, tota terra, id est, homines universi, ad quorum devenit notitiam opus mirabile Dei in Ægypto, commoti sunt et contremuerunt, secundum modum jam dictum.
paras.en: [[76:18|Great was the noise of the waters|Multitudo sonitus aquarum]]: that is, there was a great sound or din in the waters of the Red Sea, since with a huge crash and rush the waters of the Red Sea returned to their former place[[Ex 14:27||]], and over the Egyptians, and the Egyptians were carried into the deep[[Ex 14:25||]]; [[76:18|the clouds sent out a sound|vocem dederunt nubes]], that is, out of the pillar of fire and of the cloud[[Ex 14:24||]] God made lightnings and thunders go forth against the Egyptians. [[76:18|For thy arrows pass|Etenim sagittæ tuæ transeunt]]: that is, thy punishments went forth against the Egyptians, whose chariots and horsemen thou didst overthrow; [[76:19|The voice of thy thunder|vox tonitrui tui]], that is, the sound of those thunders, was [[76:19|in a wheel|in rota]], that is, it was like a wheel: for as the din of wheels running together is great, so was the voice of thy thunders going forth from the cloud just spoken of. [[76:19|Thy lightnings enlightened the world|Illuxerunt coruscationes tuæ orbi terræ]]: that is, thou didst make thy lightnings flash in the land of Egypt, as it is written: [[Ex 9:23|the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightnings running along the ground|Dominus dedit tonitrua et grandinem ac discurrentia fulgura super terram]]. Or: [[76:19|Thy lightnings enlightened the world|Illuxerunt coruscationes tuæ orbi terræ]], that is, those lightnings made in Egypt came to the knowledge of all men. [[76:19|the earth shook and trembled|Commota est et contremuit terra]]: that is, the Egyptians were moved by such great wonders, some to wonder, some to obstinacy, and some to the faith and worship of the one God, like that [[Ex 12:38|mixed multitude, without number|vulgus illud promiscuum innumerabile]] which went up together with the children of Israel out of Egypt, as is said in Exodus. The earth [[76:19|trembled|Contremuit]] too: that is, the Egyptians were terrified by those miracles. Or, the whole earth, that is, all men to whose knowledge the wonderful work of God in Egypt came, were moved and trembled, in the manner already said.

paras.t: In mari via tua, quia in mari Rubro viam parasti populo tuo ; et semitæ tuæ, id est itinera per quæ deduxisti filios Israel, erant in aquis multis, id est in medio aquarum maris Rubri, vel inter partes hujus maris, quoniam aquæ ex utraque parte stabant solidatæ. Et vestigia tua non cognoscentur : id est, nulla apparuerunt indicia pedum seu gressuum populi tui quum pertransissent : statim enim mare ad proprium rediit locum, et intra se ipsum fuit conclusum. Et simili sensu in libro Sapientiæ dicitur : Transierunt omnia illa, scilicet sæculi vanitates, tanquam umbra, et tanquam navis quæ pertransit fluctuantem aquam, cujus, quum præterierit, non est vestigium invenire, neque semitam carinæ illius in fluctibus.
paras.en: [[76:20|Thy way is in the sea|In mari via tua]], because in the Red Sea thou didst prepare a way for thy people; [[76:20|and thy paths|et semitæ tuæ]], that is, the roads by which thou didst lead the children of Israel, were [[76:20|in many waters|in aquis multis]], that is, in the midst of the waters of the Red Sea, or between the parts of this sea, since the waters stood made firm on either side[[Ex 14:29||]]. [[76:20|and thy footsteps shall not be known|Et vestigia tua non cognoscentur]]: that is, no traces of the feet or steps of thy people appeared once they had passed over: for straightway the sea went back to its own place and was closed up within itself. And in a like sense it is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:9|All those things are passed away|Transierunt omnia illa]], namely the vanities of the world, [[Wis 5:9|like a shadow|tanquam umbra]], [[Wis 5:10|And as a ship, that passeth through the waves: whereof when it is gone by, the trace cannot be found. nor the path of its keel in the waters|et tanquam navis quæ pertransit fluctuantem aquam, cujus, quum præterierit, non est vestigium invenire, neque semitam carinæ illius in fluctibus]].

paras.t: Deduxisti sicut oves populum tuum, id est filios Israel per desertum, in quo eos pavisti, protexisti, et custodisti, quemadmodum pastor alit et protegit oves suas : et hoc fecisti in manu Moysis et Aaron, id est per manum et ministerium Moysis ducis populi tui, et Aaron primi ac summi pontificis tui in populo Judæorum.
paras.en: [[76:21|Thou hast conducted thy people like sheep|Deduxisti sicut oves populum tuum]], that is, the children of Israel through the desert, in which thou didst feed them, protect them and keep them, as a shepherd feeds and protects his sheep: and this thou didst [[76:21|by the hand of Moses and Aaron|in manu Moysis et Aaron]][[Num 33:1||]], that is, by the hand and ministry of Moses, the leader of thy people, and of Aaron, thy first and high priest among the people of the Jews.

paras.t: Spiritualiter autem seu mystice exponendus est locus iste hoc modo : Notam fecisti, o Deus Pater, in populis totius mundi virtutem tuam, id est Christum, qui est virtus et sapientia Patris : mittendo enim Filium tuum in mundum per incarnationem, homines illustrasti, et tandem per sanctos Apostolos totum mundum ad Christi notitiam convertisti. Redemisti in brachio tuo populum tuum : id est, in Christo per quem omnia operaris, et qui virtus tua vocatur, liberasti omnes electos de pœnis inferni et morte peccati : utpote filios Jacob, id est Judæos, qui fidem et opera Jacob sequuntur, et Joseph, qui interpretatur augmentum, id est populum ex gentilibus, ex quo augetur Ecclesia. Viderunt te aquæ, Deus, viderunt te aquæ : id est, populi ad fidem conversi tam ex gentilibus quam ex Judæis, oculo contemplationis seu fidei te inspexerunt et cognoverunt.
paras.en: But spiritually, or mystically, this passage is to be expounded thus: [[76:15|Thou hast made thy power known|Notam fecisti]], O God the Father, [[76:15|among the nations|in populis]] of the whole world [[76:15|thy power|virtutem tuam]], that is, Christ, who is the power and the wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]]: for by sending thy Son into the world through the incarnation thou didst enlighten men, and at length through the holy Apostles thou didst turn the whole world to the knowledge of Christ. [[76:16|With thy arm thou hast redeemed thy people|Redemisti in brachio tuo populum tuum]]: that is, in Christ, through whom thou workest all things and who is called thy power[[1 Cor 1:24||]], thou didst set free all the elect from the pains of hell and the death of sin: namely [[76:16|the children of Jacob|filios Jacob]], that is, the Jews who follow the faith and works of Jacob, [[76:16|and of Joseph|et Joseph]], which is interpreted increase, that is, the people from among the gentiles, by whom the Church is increased. [[76:17|The waters saw thee, O God|Viderunt te aquæ, Deus]], [[76:17|the waters saw thee|viderunt te aquæ]]: that is, the peoples converted to the faith, from the gentiles as well as from the Jews, looked upon thee and knew thee with the eye of contemplation, or of faith.

paras.t: Etenim aquæ multæ, sunt populi multi. Et timuerunt jam ad fidem translati tua judicia, tuam majestatem, pœnas inferni, adversitatesque sæculi ; et turbatæ sunt abyssi : id est, corda humana ex prædicatione Evangelii mota sunt, quædam ad indurationem, quædam ad pœnitentiam. Dicitur autem cor humanum abyssus, id est adeo inscrutabile et profundum, ut soli Deo sit cognitum. Propter quod alibi scriptum est : Pravum est cor hominis et inscrutabile. Quis cognoscet illud? Ego Dominus scrutans cor et probans renes.
paras.en: For many waters are many peoples. [[76:17|And they were afraid|Et timuerunt]], once brought over to the faith, of thy judgments, thy majesty, the pains of hell and the adversities of the world; [[76:17|and the depths were troubled|et turbatæ sunt abyssi]]: that is, human hearts were moved by the preaching of the Gospel, some to hardening, some to penance. Now the human heart is called a depth, that is, so unsearchable and deep that it is known to God alone. Wherefore it is written elsewhere: [[Jer 17:9|The heart is perverse above all things, and unsearchable, who can know it?|Pravum est cor hominis et inscrutabile. Quis cognoscet illud?]] [[Jer 17:10|I am the Lord who search the heart, and prove the reins|Ego Dominus scrutans cor et probans renes]].

paras.t: Multitudo sonitus aquarum : id est, varia fuit vox populorum ad fidem catholicam conversorum. Nam quidam benedixerunt Deum in hymnis et confessionibus, quidam deplanxerunt sua peccata in precibus atque gemitibus, alii informaverunt alios doctrinis et prædicationibus sanctis. Hoc vero idcirco fecerunt, quoniam vocem dederunt nubes, id est, quia Apostoli eos sua prædicatione induxerunt ad tam sancta exercitia. Dicuntur autem Apostoli nubes, juxta illud Isaiæ : Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant? Etenim sagittæ tuæ transeunt : id est, acutissima Spiritus Sancti verba in corda electorum infixa sunt ab ore prædicatorum sanctorum. Qui enim ex Deo fuerunt, verba prædicantium receperunt. Vox tonitrui tui in rota : id est, voces tonitruorum tuorum, videlicet sermones Apostolorum, processerunt in omnem mundi circuitum, et in fines orbis terrarum. Dicuntur enim Apostoli tonitrua, propter eminentissimam altitudinem prædicationum suarum. Unde et Christus in Evangelio Joannem et Jacobum filios tonitrui legitur appellasse. Illuxerunt coruscationes tuæ orbi terræ : id est, virtutes et gratiæ atque miracula quæ contulisti Apostolis et reliquis sanctis, manifestata sunt universis hominibus, te Domino sermonem illorum confirmante sequentibus signis. Commota est et contremuit terra : id est, habitantes in terra, ex prædicatione atque prodigiis Apostolorum ac reliquorum apostolicorum virorum diversimode moti sunt et tremefacti, videlicet ad admirationem, ad pœnitentiam, vel etiam ad persecutionem, et item blasphemiam.
paras.en: [[76:18|Great was the noise of the waters|Multitudo sonitus aquarum]]: that is, manifold was the voice of the peoples converted to the Catholic faith. For some blessed God in hymns and thanksgiving[[2 Mach 10:38||]] [the margin gives II Mach. v, 38; the words are those of 2 Mach 10:38], some bewailed their sins in prayers and groans, others instructed others with holy teaching and preaching. And this they did because [[76:18|the clouds sent out a sound|vocem dederunt nubes]], that is, because the Apostles by their preaching led them to such holy exercises. Now the Apostles are called clouds, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant?]]? [[76:18|For thy arrows pass|Etenim sagittæ tuæ transeunt]]: that is, the most piercing words of the Holy Ghost were fixed in the hearts of the elect from the mouth of the holy preachers. For those who were of God received the words of the preachers[[John 8:47||]]. [[76:19|The voice of thy thunder in a wheel|Vox tonitrui tui in rota]]: that is, the voices of thy thunders, namely the discourses of the Apostles, went forth into the whole circuit of the world and to the ends of the earth[[Ps 18:5||]]. For the Apostles are called thunders because of the most eminent loftiness of their preaching. Hence Christ too in the Gospel is read to have called John and James [[Mark 3:17|The sons of thunder|filios tonitrui]]. [[76:19|Thy lightnings enlightened the world|Illuxerunt coruscationes tuæ orbi terræ]]: that is, the powers and graces and miracles that thou didst bestow on the Apostles and the other saints were made manifest to all men, thou, the Lord, [[Mark 16:20|confirming the word with signs that followed|sermonem illorum confirmante sequentibus signis]]. [[76:19|the earth shook and trembled|Commota est et contremuit terra]]: that is, those dwelling on the earth were moved and made to tremble in divers ways by the preaching and wonders of the Apostles and of the other apostolic men: to wonder, to penance, or even to persecution, and to blasphemy as well.

paras.t: In mari via tua, id est, in plebe gentili prædicata est lex evangelica ; et semitæ tuæ, id est præcepta tua et consilia, in aquis multis, id est, in plurimis nationibus manifestata sunt, recepta et adimpleta. Et vestigia tua, o Christe, id est opera tua et exempla, non cognoscentur a populo cui specialiter missus eras, utpote ab incredulis Judæis, qui opera tua adscripserunt Beelzebub. Vel : Vestigia tua non cognoscentur, id est, occultæ impressiones mirabilesque effectus, quos in toto universo exerces, a nullo homine viatore poterunt perscrutari. Unde ad Job dicitur : Forsan vestigia Dei comprehendes, et usque ad perfectum, Omnipotentem reperies?
paras.en: [[76:20|Thy way is in the sea|In mari via tua]], that is, the law of the Gospel was preached among the gentile folk; [[76:20|and thy paths|et semitæ tuæ]], that is, thy precepts and counsels, were made manifest, received and fulfilled [[76:20|in many waters|in aquis multis]], that is, in very many nations. [[76:20|and thy footsteps|Et vestigia tua]], O Christ, that is, thy works and examples, [[76:20|shall not be known|non cognoscentur]] by the people to whom thou wast specially sent[[Matt 15:24||]], namely by the unbelieving Jews, who ascribed thy works to Beelzebub[[Matt 12:24||]]. Or: [[76:20|thy footsteps shall not be known|Vestigia tua non cognoscentur]], that is, the hidden impressions and wonderful effects which thou workest in the whole universe can be searched out by no man still on the way [that is, a wayfarer, one still in this life and not yet in the fatherland]. Hence it is said to Job: [[Job 11:7|Peradventure thou wilt comprehend the steps of God, and wilt find out the Almighty perfectly?|Forsan vestigia Dei comprehendes, et usque ad perfectum, Omnipotentem reperies?]]
