paras.t: Deduxisti, o Deus Trinitas, sicut oves populum tuum, scilicet Christianos, per viam hujus exsilii ad patriam felicitatis æternæ, in manu Moysis et Aaron, id est in virtute et gratia Christi, per Moysen Aaronque præfigurati, quoniam Christus est dux noster atque sacerdos. Unde de eo in Daniele habetur : Ab exitu sermonis usque ad Christum ducem, etc. Et Zacharias ait : Ipse erit sacerdos super solio suo. Et Apostolus : Christus, eo quod maneat in æternum, sempiternum habet sacerdotium.
paras.en: [[76:21|Thou hast conducted|Deduxisti]], O God the Trinity, [[76:21|thy people like sheep|sicut oves populum tuum]], namely Christians, along the way of this exile to the fatherland of eternal happiness, [[76:21|by the hand of Moses and Aaron|in manu Moysis et Aaron]], that is, in the power and grace of Christ, prefigured by Moses and Aaron, since Christ is our leader and priest. Hence we have of him in Daniel: [[Dan 9:25|from the going forth of the word|Ab exitu sermonis]] [[Dan 9:25|unto Christ, the prince|usque ad Christum ducem]], etc. And Zacharias says: [[Zach 6:13|he shall be a priest upon his throne|Ipse erit sacerdos super solio suo]]. And the Apostle: Christ, [[Heb 7:24|for that he continueth for ever, hath an everlasting priesthood|eo quod maneat in æternum, sempiternum habet sacerdotium]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum sententiosum, doctrinalem, et totius spiritualis institutionis dogmata includentem audivimus : in quo primo omnium profitetur se homo transiliens, mundana contemnens, soli Divinitati ardentissime inhians, ad Dominum ingenti proclamasse affectu, eumque in tribulatione sua cordialiter exorasse, nec aliquam consolationem vilem, carnalem, indignam admittere voluisse, sed Dei fuisse recordatum, atque ex hoc mentaliter delectatum. Insuper asserit se prævenisse vigilias causa orandi laudandique Dominum, annos quoque æternos considerans, se propriam conscientiam diligentissime discussisse. Deinde ostendit, quam inæstimabilis sit misericordia Creatoris ; et postmodum Deum laudat ac superexaltat, mirabilia ejus commemorat, beneficia recolit. Omnino ergo conemur tanti psalmi ignea verba fervida mente cantare, tam doctrinalis psalmi documenta implere, universa terrena amore cœlestium aspernari, in solo Salvatore vera solatia adipisci, Dei in omni angustia reminisci, et ex contemplationis lætitia omnem inordinatam tristitiam propulsare.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of sentences, full of teaching, and containing the doctrines of the whole spiritual training: in which, first of all, a man who rises above himself, despising worldly things and longing most ardently for the Godhead alone, professes that he cried out to the Lord with great affection, and besought him from his heart in his tribulation, and would admit no consolation that was base, carnal or unworthy, but remembered God and was delighted in mind by this. Moreover he declares that he prevented the watches [that is, rose before the night watches] in order to pray to and praise the Lord, and that, considering the eternal years, he examined his own conscience most carefully. Then he shows how inestimable is the mercy of the Creator; and afterwards he praises and supremely exalts God, recounts his wonders and recalls his benefits. Let us then strive with all our might to sing the fiery words of so great a psalm with a fervent mind, to fulfil the teachings of so instructive a psalm, to spurn all earthly things for love of heavenly ones, to find true solace in the Saviour alone, to remember God in every distress, and by the joy of contemplation to drive out all inordinate sadness.

paras.t: Precatio. Ineffabilis pietatis Deus, misericors in millibus, non in finem iratus pro peccatis nostris misericordiam tuam abscindas a nobis : non obliviscaris misereri nostri ; sed tua miseratione jube nos æternæ salvationi annumerari.
paras.en: Prayer. O God of unspeakable goodness, merciful unto thousands, do not, in anger for our sins, [[76:9|cut off|abscindas]] thy [[76:9|mercy|misericordiam]] from us [[76:9|for ever|in finem]]; [[76:10|forget|obliviscaris]] not [[76:10|to shew mercy|misereri]] to us; but of thy compassion bid us be numbered among those saved for eternity.

77.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI SEPTIMI: ATTENDITE, POPULE MEUS, LEGEM MEAM.
77.title_en: Explanation of the seventy-seventh psalm: Attend, O my people, to my law.

paras.t: Longus hic psalmus hoc brevi est titulo inscriptus : Intellectus Asaph : id est, in psalmo præsenti datur intelligi, quomodo accipienda sint ea quæ Deus in veteri Testamento populo suo dixit et fecit. Omnia enim in figura contingebant illis, et scripta sunt ad nostram doctrinam. Dum namque titulus psalmi ait, Intellectus Asaph : admonemur ista non simpliciter seu solum historialiter sumere, sed mystice elucidare, præsertim quum in sequenti secundo versu dicatur, Aperiam in parabolis os meum.
paras.en: This long psalm is headed with this short title: [[77:1|Understanding for Asaph|Intellectus Asaph]]: that is, in the present psalm we are given to understand how the things that God said and did to his people in the Old Testament are to be taken. For [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|Omnia enim in figura contingebant illis]], and [[Rom 15:4|were written for our learning|scripta sunt ad nostram doctrinam]]. For when the title of the psalm says, [[77:1|Understanding for Asaph|Intellectus Asaph]], we are reminded not to take these things simply, or only historically, but to unfold them mystically, above all since in the next verse, the second, it is said: [[77:2|I will open my mouth in parables|Aperiam in parabolis os meum]].

paras.t: Parabolica autem eloquia non superficialiter, sed diligenter scrutanda sunt. Porro evangelista Matthæus primum istius psalmi versum allegat de Christo prædictum : Hæc omnia (inquiens) facta sunt, ut impleretur illud quod scriptum est, Aperiam in parabolis os meum, eructabo abscondita a constitutione mundi : quod in hoc psalmo aliis verbis ita exprimitur, Loquar propositiones ab initio. Hinc infert S. Hieronymus, quod evangelista Matthæus hoc intellexerit ex persona Christi. Duos igitur primos psalmi hujus versiculos, qui per modum præfationis seu prologi præmittuntur sequentibus, dicit Propheta, auctor psalmi præsentis, sive ille sit David, sive Asaph, in persona Christi. Verumtamen quæ sequuntur, ad litteram dicta videntur de populo veteris Testamenti, videlicet de mirabilibus Dei circa populum illum, olim sibi peculiarem ; de ingratitudine quoque populi hujus, et digna castigatione ipsius, atque de electione David posteritatisque suæ ad regnum : quæ omnia spiritualiter exponi possunt de populo christiano, sicut aliqualiter tangam in subditis.
paras.en: Now parabolic sayings are to be searched out not superficially but carefully. Further, the evangelist Matthew cites the first verse of this psalm [that is, the first after the opening verse; v. 2 in the numbering used here] as foretold of Christ: [[Matt 13:34|All these things|Hæc omnia]] (he says) were done, [[Matt 13:35|That it might be fulfilled|ut impleretur]] which is written, [[Matt 13:35|I will open my mouth in parables, I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world|Aperiam in parabolis os meum, eructabo abscondita a constitutione mundi]]: which in this psalm is expressed in other words thus: [[77:2|I will utter propositions from the beginning|Loquar propositiones ab initio]]. From this St. Jerome infers that the evangelist Matthew understood this as spoken in the person of Christ. So the first two little verses of this psalm, which are set before what follows by way of a preface or prologue, the Prophet, the author of the present psalm, whether he be David or Asaph, speaks in the person of Christ. But what follows seems to be said, in the letter, of the people of the Old Testament: namely of God's wonders towards that people, once his own peculiar people[[Deut 7:6||]]; of this people's ingratitude too, and of its deserved chastisement; and of the choice of David and his posterity for the kingdom[[1 Kings 16:13||]]: all of which can be expounded spiritually of the Christian people, as I shall touch on in some measure below.

paras.t: Volens ergo Propheta populum cui loquitur, docilem, benevolum et attentum efficere, sic orsus est, loquens (ut dixi) non in sua, sed in Christi persona, qui etiam per os omnium Prophetarum locutus est : Attendite, populus meus, electus a me ad fidem cultumque divinum, legem meam, id est legem decem præceptorum moralium : quæ in veteri Testamento ac novo eadem sunt, quæ primo Moysi in monte Sinai divinitus data noscuntur, atque a Christo in Evangelio approbantur. Inclinate aurem vestram, tam corporis quam cordis, in verba oris mei, id est in verba sacræ Scripturæ ac prædicationis divinæ, ea reverenter auscultando, fideliterque observando.
paras.en: So the Prophet, wishing to make the people he addresses teachable, well disposed and attentive, began thus, speaking (as I said) not in his own person but in the person of Christ, who also spoke by the mouth of all the Prophets[[Luke 1:70||]]: [[77:1|Attend, O my people|Attendite, populus meus]], chosen by me for the faith and for the worship of God, [[77:1|to my law|legem meam]], that is, to the law of the ten moral precepts, which are the same in the Old Testament and in the New: which are known to have been first given by God to Moses on Mount Sinai[[Ex 34:1||]], and are approved by Christ in the Gospel. [[77:1|incline your ears|Inclinate aurem vestram]], both of the body and of the heart, [[77:1|to the words of my mouth|in verba oris mei]], that is, to the words of Holy Scripture and of divine preaching, by listening to them reverently and keeping them faithfully.

paras.t: Aperiam in parabolis os meum. Hoc de Christo ad litteram verum est : propter quod in Evangelio dicitur, Sine parabolis non loquebatur ad turbas. Et ipse ait discipulis : Vobis datum est scire mysterium regni Dei ; illis vero qui foris sunt, omnia in parabolis fiunt. Dicuntur autem parabolæ, quædam rerum similitudines quæ comparantur rebus de quibus tractatur, dum quod de uno asseritur, de alio intelligi datur. Loquar propositiones ab initio. Sicut jam patuit, Matthæus ita allegat : Eructabo abscondita a constitutione mundi. Communiter autem dicunt expositores, quod, Ab initio, in nostra translatione positum, non sit referendum ad mundi exordium, sed ad initium eductionis Israelitarum ex Ægypto. Verumtamen, quoniam Evangelista Spiritu Sancto repletus allegat, A constitutione mundi, dicendum videtur quod in hoc psalmo, saltem implicite et in generali, commemorantur mirabilia Dei ab initio mundi peracta : quia in eo quod sequitur, Quanta audivimus et cognovimus ea, et patres nostri narraverunt nobis : non solum oportet accipere opera Dei a tempore Moysis facta, atque a patribus sibi contemporaneis, seu posterioribus ipso, posteris relata ; sed insuper intelligere possumus magnalia Dei a constitutione mundi facta, sicut erat diluvium, submersio Pentapolis, scilicet Sodomæ, Gomorrhæ, Adamæ, Seboim et Segor, atque similia, quæ Abraham, Melchisedec, Lot, et alii veteres Patriarchæ narraverunt posteris suis, et etiam filiis Israel mediate. Talia vero abscondita Christus in Evangelio narravit, prout studiosis lectoribus constat. Facit namque mentionem de Noe atque diluvio, de submersione quoque Sodomæ, et de primæva quoque matrimonii institutione.
paras.en: [[77:2|I will open my mouth in parables|Aperiam in parabolis os meum]]. This is true of Christ in the letter; for which reason it is said in the Gospel: [[Matt 13:34|without parables he did not speak|Sine parabolis non loquebatur]] to the multitudes. And he himself says to the disciples: [[Mark 4:11|To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but to them that are without, all things are done in parables|Vobis datum est scire mysterium regni Dei ; illis vero qui foris sunt, omnia in parabolis fiunt]]. Now those are called parables which are certain likenesses of things, compared with the things being treated, when what is asserted of one is given to be understood of another. [[77:2|I will utter propositions from the beginning|Loquar propositiones ab initio]]. As has already appeared, Matthew cites it thus: [[Matt 13:35|I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world|Eructabo abscondita a constitutione mundi]]. Now the expositors commonly say that *From the beginning*, as it stands in our translation, is not to be referred to the beginning of the world, but to the beginning of the bringing of the Israelites out of Egypt. Yet since the Evangelist, filled with the Holy Ghost, cites it as *from the foundation of the world*, it seems we must say that in this psalm, at least implicitly and in general, the wonders of God wrought from the beginning of the world are recalled: for in what follows, [[77:3|How great things have we heard and known, and our fathers have told us|Quanta audivimus et cognovimus ea, et patres nostri narraverunt nobis]], we must take not only the works of God done from the time of Moses and told to their descendants by the fathers who were his contemporaries or came after him; but we can also understand the mighty works of God done from the foundation of the world, such as the flood, the overthrow of the Pentapolis, namely of Sodom, Gomorrha, Adama, Seboim and Segor, and the like, which Abraham, Melchisedech, Lot and the other ancient Patriarchs told to their descendants, and so also, at one remove, to the children of Israel. And Christ in the Gospel told such hidden things, as is clear to attentive readers. For he makes mention of Noe and the flood[[Luke 17:26||]][[Matt 24:37||]], of the overthrow of Sodom too[[Luke 17:29||]], and also of the first institution of marriage[[Matt 19:4||]].

paras.t: Quidam vero quod nunc dicitur, Aperiam in parabolis, etc., exponunt de auctore psalmi præsentis, ut sit sensus : Aperiam os meum, id est, dicta et facta veteris Testamenti, quæ sunt figuræ eorum quæ sunt in novo Testamento, narrabo. Loquar propositiones, id est orationes seu quæstiones disputatorias, quæ Græce dicuntur problemata, Hebraice autem ænigmata : propositiones, inquam, loquentes de rebus quæ contigerunt ab initio liberationis Israel de Ægypto.
paras.en: Some, however, expound what is now said, [[77:2|I will open my mouth in parables|Aperiam in parabolis]], etc., of the author of the present psalm, so that the sense is: [[77:2|I will open my mouth|Aperiam os meum]], that is, I will tell the sayings and deeds of the Old Testament, which are figures of what is in the New Testament. [[77:2|I will utter propositions|Loquar propositiones]], that is, discourses or disputed questions, which in Greek are called *problemata*, and in Hebrew *ænigmata* [that is, riddles]: propositions, I say, that speak of the things that happened from the beginning of Israel's deliverance from Egypt.

paras.t: Deinde auctor psalmi in sua ac populi Israelitici loquens persona, subjungit : Quanta mirabilia opera et magnifica beneficia Dei audivimus et cognovimus ea, id est, aure cordis intelligendo percepimus, et patres nostri, scilicet Moyses, Josue, et similes sancti patres, narraverunt nobis mediate, atque per libros quos ediderunt, et nobis reliquerunt.
paras.en: Then the author of the psalm, speaking in his own person and in that of the Israelite people, adds: [[77:3|How great things|Quanta]], wonderful works and magnificent benefits of God, [[77:3|have we heard and known|audivimus et cognovimus ea]], that is, have perceived by understanding with the ear of the heart, [[77:3|and our fathers|et patres nostri]], namely Moses, Josue and like holy fathers, [[77:3|have told us|narraverunt nobis]], at one remove, and through the books which they put forth and left to us.

paras.t: Non sunt occultata illa opera Dei facta in Ægypto, in mari Rubro, in deserto, in terraque Chanaan, a filiis eorum, id est ab eis qui patrum suorum fidem et opera sunt secuti, non obliti beneficiorum Dei altissimi. Non autem innotuerunt omnibus filiis eorum, quoniam in libro Judicum scriptum est : Surrexerunt interea alii qui non cognoverunt Dominum, et opera ejus quæ fecit cum Israel. Tales enim fuerunt solum filii secundum carnem, non secundum fidei imitationem. Non sunt ergo occultata a filiis eorum in generatione altera, id est a filiis qui fuerunt in generatione succedente, quia ad posteros pervenit rerum gestarum memoria.
paras.en: [[77:4|They have not been hidden|Non sunt occultata]], those works of God done in Egypt, in the Red Sea, in the desert and in the land of Chanaan, [[77:4|from their children|a filiis eorum]], that is, from those who followed the faith and works of their fathers, not forgetting the benefits of God most high. But they did not become known to all their children, since it is written in the book of Judges: [[Judg 2:10|there arose others that knew not the Lord and the works which he had done for Israel|Surrexerunt interea alii qui non cognoverunt Dominum, et opera ejus quæ fecit cum Israel]]. For such were sons only according to the flesh, not by imitation of their faith. So [[77:4|They have not been hidden from their children, in another generation|Non sunt ergo occultata a filiis eorum in generatione altera]], that is, from the children who were in the generation that followed, because the memory of the deeds reached their descendants.

paras.t: Quid autem patres narraverunt filiis, subditur : Narrantes laudes Domini, id est laudabilia opera ejus, et verba divinæ laudis contentiva, et virtutes ejus, id est potentias Dei, qui Ægyptum decem principalibus plagis percussit, et mirabilia ejus quæ fecit, mare Rubrum dividendo, et Ægyptios submergendo.
paras.en: What the fathers told their children is added: [[77:4|Declaring the praises of the Lord|Narrantes laudes Domini]], that is, his praiseworthy works, and words that contain God's praise, [[77:4|and his powers|et virtutes ejus]], that is, the mighty acts of God, who struck Egypt with ten chief plagues, [[77:4|and his wonders which he hath done|et mirabilia ejus quæ fecit]], by dividing the Red Sea and drowning the Egyptians[[Ex 14:1||]].

paras.t: Et suscitavit testimonium in Jacob, id est, testamentum quoddam contulit populo Judæorum ex Jacob natorum ; et legem posuit in Israel : quoniam legem dedit per Moysen, et legem hanc scripsit in tabulis lapideis, quatenus servaretur, et esset posteris in testimonium divinæ locutionis et legislationis cœlestis, perversis quoque esset in testimonium damnationis, sicut in Deuteronomio Moyses sæpe testatur. Nam ob hanc causam præcepit Dominus scribi Deuteronomium legis, tabulasque testamenti servari in tabernaculo. Idem sunt ergo testimonium et lex, quemadmodum idem sunt Jacob et Israel ; sed ratione differunt. Lex quippe vocatur, quoniam jubet, coercet, et religat : jubet, inquam, quid agendum, quid evitandum ; coercet a malo per prohibitiones ac pœnas ; religat animam sub Deo per observationem legalem. Testimonium vero vocatur, quoniam probat et convincit.
paras.en: [[77:5|And he set up a testimony in Jacob|Et suscitavit testimonium in Jacob]], that is, he bestowed a certain testament on the people of the Jews, born of Jacob; [[77:5|and made a law in Israel|et legem posuit in Israel]]: for he gave the law through Moses[[John 1:17||]], and wrote this law on tables of stone[[Ex 34:1||]][[Ex 34:29||]], that it might be kept, and be for their descendants a testimony of God's speaking and of the heavenly lawgiving, and for the wicked a testimony of their condemnation, as Moses often witnesses in Deuteronomy. For this reason the Lord commanded the Deuteronomy of the law [that is, its second giving] to be written, and the tables of the testament to be kept in the tabernacle[[Deut 31:10||]][[Deut 31:26||]]. So testimony and law are the same thing, just as Jacob and Israel are the same; but they differ in meaning [*ratione*: that is, in the respect under which each is named]. For it is called law because it commands, restrains and binds: commands, I say, what is to be done and what avoided; restrains from evil by prohibitions and penalties; binds the soul under God by the keeping of the law. And it is called testimony because it proves and convicts.

paras.t: Quanta, id est quam multa et magna facta et verba, mandavit patribus nostris ex Ægypto eductis, nota facere ea filiis suis, narrando aut scribendo quæ fieri conspexerunt, ut cognoscat generatio altera, id est quælibet generatio illis succedens. Filii qui nascentur ex utero, et exsurgent ad perfectionem ætatis, quantitatis et rationis, et narrabunt filiis suis. Hoc in populo Judæorum sæpe impletum est.
paras.en: [[77:5|How great things|Quanta]], that is, how many and how great deeds and words, [[77:5|he commanded our fathers|mandavit patribus nostris]] who were brought out of Egypt, [[77:5|that they should make the same known to their children|nota facere ea filiis suis]], by telling or writing what they had seen done, [[77:6|That another generation might know them|ut cognoscat generatio altera]], that is, any generation that comes after them. [[77:6|The children that should be born|Filii qui nascentur]] from the womb, [[77:6|and should rise up|et exsurgent]] to full growth of age, stature and reason, [[77:6|and declare them to their children|et narrabunt filiis suis]]. This was often fulfilled in the people of the Jews.

paras.t: Ideo autem narrabunt filiis suis, quatenus doceant eos in Deo confidere : ideo sequitur : Ut ponant filii isti in Deo spem suam, non in propriis viribus aut aliqua creatura, et non obliviscantur operum Dei quæ fecit, salvando patres eorum, atque incredulos occidendo, et mandata ejus exquirant, id est, exquisite ac diligenter scire desiderent, quatenus impleant ea.
paras.en: And they will declare them to their children for this reason, to teach them to trust in God; therefore there follows: [[77:7|That they may put their hope in God|Ut ponant filii isti in Deo spem suam]] (these children), not in their own strength or in any creature, [[77:7|and may not forget the works of God|et non obliviscantur operum Dei]] which he did, by saving their fathers and slaying the unbelieving, [[77:7|and may seek his commandments|et mandata ejus exquirant]], that is, may desire to know them searchingly and carefully, so as to fulfil them.

paras.t: Ne fiant sicut patres eorum, ex Ægypto educti, qui erant generatio prava, id est inobediens, et exasperans, id est divinam justitiam ad vindictam inflammans. Unde et Moyses generationi isti locutus est : Ego scio contentionem tuam, et cervicem tuam durissimam. Adhuc vivente me et ingrediente vobiscum, semper contentiose egistis contra Dominum. Pro majori enim parte mali fuerunt : propter quod in deserto prostrati sunt.
paras.en: [[77:8|That they may not become like their fathers|Ne fiant sicut patres eorum]], who were brought out of Egypt, who were a [[77:8|perverse|prava]] generation, that is, disobedient, [[77:8|and exasperating|et exasperans]], that is, inflaming the divine justice to vengeance. Hence Moses too said to this generation: [[Deut 31:27|For I know thy obstinacy, and thy most stiff neck|Ego scio contentionem tuam, et cervicem tuam durissimam]]. [[Deut 31:27|While I am yet living, and going in with you, you have always been rebellious against the Lord|Adhuc vivente me et ingrediente vobiscum, semper contentiose egistis contra Dominum]]. For the greater part of them were wicked, which is why they were laid low in the desert.

paras.t: Generatio quæ non direxit cor suum, id est, quæ Dominum Deum non quæsivit corde perfecto et vero atque sincero. Propterea Moyses ait ad eos : Vos vidistis universa magnalia quæ coram vobis fecit Dominus, et non dedit vobis Dominus cor intelligens usque in præsentem diem. Et non est creditus cum Deo spiritus ejus : id est, spiritus seu anima populi hujus non est Deo per fidem conjunctus, quoniam divinis promissionibus non crediderunt. Unde alia translatio clarior est, dicens : Et non credidit Deo spiritus ejus. Et istud referendum non est ad omnes, sed ad perversos qui erant in populo isto Israelitico, secundum regulam in principio expositionis hujus libri inductam, qua dicitur, quod sacra Scriptura interdum loquitur commixtim de corpore Domini permixto ex bonis et malis : ubi considerandum est quid ad quos referri oporteat. Interdum namque tota congregatio laudatur propter aliquos bonos in ea contentos ; vicissim quoque tota vituperatur propter quosdam malos in ea conclusos, sicut nunc agitur.
paras.en: [[77:8|A generation that set not their heart aright|Generatio quæ non direxit cor suum]], that is, which did not seek the Lord God with a perfect, true and sincere heart. Therefore Moses says to them: [[Deut 29:2|You have seen all the things that the Lord did before you|Vos vidistis universa magnalia quæ coram vobis fecit Dominus]], [[Deut 29:4|And the Lord hath not given you a heart to understand|et non dedit vobis Dominus cor intelligens]] [[Deut 29:4|unto this present day|usque in præsentem diem]] [Denis has *magnalia*, 'mighty works', for 'all the things', and leaves out 'and eyes to see, and ears that may hear']. [[77:8|and whose spirit was not faithful to God|Et non est creditus cum Deo spiritus ejus]]: that is, the spirit or soul of this people was not joined to God by faith, since they did not believe the divine promises. Hence another translation is clearer, saying: *And his spirit did not believe God*. And this is not to be referred to all, but to the wicked who were in this Israelite people, according to the rule set out at the beginning of the exposition of this book, which says that holy Scripture sometimes speaks in a mixed way of the body of the Lord, which is mixed of good and bad [the second of the rules of Tyconius, on the Lord's twofold body]: where we must consider what is to be referred to whom. For sometimes the whole congregation is praised for some good men contained in it; and conversely the whole is blamed for certain wicked men enclosed in it, as is done here.

paras.t: Filii Ephrem, id est aliqui nati ex progenie Ephraim filii Joseph, intendentes et mittentes arcum, id est arcum protendentes, et ex arcu emittentes sagittas, conversi sunt in die belli, id est, terga verterunt atque fugerunt, in die quando contra præceptum Moysis ascenderunt in montem ad præliandum contra Amalecitas et Amorrhæos, ut scribitur in libro Numerorum. A principio namque filii Ephraim præsumptuosi fuerunt et ambitiosi, quoniam pater eorum, scilicet Joseph, dominus erat fratrum suorum ; et quoniam Jacob prætulit Ephraim secundo natum, primogenito Joseph, qui erat Manasses ; et quia Josue minister Moysis et electus ex multis, Ephratæus exstiterat. Unde eorum elatio sæpe patescit in libro Judicum ; ideoque Propheta in psalmo isto singulariter invehitur contra filios Ephraim, ostendens eos non fuisse electos ad regiam dignitatem, sed tribum Juda.
paras.en: [[77:9|The sons of Ephraim|Filii Ephrem]], that is, some born of the stock of Ephraim the son of Joseph[[Gen 41:52||]] [the margin reads Gen. xlix, 32, evidently for xli, 52], [[77:9|who bend and shoot with the bow|intendentes et mittentes arcum]], that is, drawing the bow and shooting arrows from the bow, [[77:9|they have turned back in the day of battle|conversi sunt in die belli]], that is, they turned their backs and fled, on the day when, against the command of Moses, they went up the mountain to fight against the Amalecites and Amorrhites, as is written in the book of Numbers[[Num 14:40||]]. For from the beginning the sons of Ephraim were presumptuous and ambitious, since their father, namely Joseph, was lord of his brethren; and since Jacob preferred Ephraim, the second-born, to Joseph's firstborn, who was Manasses[[Gen 48:14||]][[Gen 48:20||]]; and because Josue, the minister of Moses and chosen out of many, was an Ephraimite[[Deut 31:3||]][[Deut 31:7||]][[Num 13:9||]]. Hence their pride often shows itself in the book of Judges; and therefore the Prophet in this psalm inveighs particularly against the sons of Ephraim, showing that they were not chosen for the royal dignity, but the tribe of Juda.

paras.t: Non custodierunt testamentum Dei : quia transgressi sunt jussionem Dei per Moysen, eundo ad prælium, sicut nunc dictum est ; et in lege ejus noluerunt ambulare, id est, divina præcepta contempserunt implere.
paras.en: [[77:10|They kept not the covenant of God|Non custodierunt testamentum Dei]]: because they transgressed God's command given through Moses, by going to battle, as has just been said; [[77:10|and in his law they would not walk|et in lege ejus noluerunt ambulare]], that is, they scorned to fulfil the divine precepts.

paras.t: Et obliti sunt benefactorum ejus : id est, filii Israel communiter, et non solum filii Ephraim seu Ephrem, quod idem est, beneficiis Dei ingrati fuerunt, vel penitus non recolendo, vel gratias non agendo, nec benefactorem ipsum amando, nec venerando. Sic quoque obliti sunt et mirabilium ejus quæ ostendit eis in terra Ægypti, dicentes ad invicem : Constituamus nobis ducem, et revertamur in Ægyptum.
paras.en: [[77:11|And they forgot his benefits|Et obliti sunt benefactorum ejus]]: that is, the children of Israel in general, and not only the sons of Ephraim or Ephrem, which is the same, were ungrateful for God's benefits, either not recalling them at all, or not giving thanks, nor loving the benefactor himself, nor revering him. So too they forgot [[77:11|his wonders that he had shewn them|mirabilium ejus quæ ostendit eis]] in the land of Egypt, saying to one another: [[Num 14:4|Let us appoint a captain, and let us return into Egypt|Constituamus nobis ducem, et revertamur in Ægyptum]].

paras.t: Coram patribus eorum fecit mirabilia in terra Ægypti : ut patet in Exodo. Et hoc maxime fecit Deus in campo Taneos, id est in planitie civitatis illius. Tanis enim fuit civitas regalis, in qua rex cum suis consiliariis habitare solebat. Propter quod apud Isaiam scriptum est : Stulti principes Taneos, sapientes consiliarii Pharaonis dederunt consilium insipiens. Quoniam ergo rex et consules sui, qui erant principales causæ totius peccati et afflictionis Ægypti, in hac urbe regia demorari solebant, ideo verisimile est quod civitas ista gravius flagellabatur quam reliquæ. Hincque jam dicitur Deus specialiter fecisse mirabilia in loco seu campo urbis istius.
paras.en: [[77:12|Wonderful things did he do in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt|Coram patribus eorum fecit mirabilia in terra Ægypti]]: as is plain in Exodus[[Ex 7:1||]]. And God did this most of all [[77:12|in the field of Tanis|in campo Taneos]], that is, in the plain of that city. For Tanis was the royal city, in which the king used to dwell with his counsellors. For which reason it is written in Isaias: [[Is 19:11|The princes of Tanis are become fools, the wise counsellors of Pharao have given foolish counsel|Stulti principes Taneos, sapientes consiliarii Pharaonis dederunt consilium insipiens]]. Since, then, the king and his counsellors, who were the chief causes of all the sin and affliction of Egypt, used to stay in this royal city, it is likely that this city was scourged more heavily than the rest. And hence it is now said that God did wonders especially in the place or field of that city.

paras.t: Interrupit mare Rubrum, dividens illud, et perduxit eos sicco pede per alveum ejus ; et statuit aquas maris Rubri sic divisas quasi in utre, id est, ita firmavit eas in loco suo ne fluerent, ac si fuissent in vase collectæ.
paras.en: [[77:13|He divided the sea|Interrupit mare]], the Red Sea, cleaving it[[Ex 14:1||]], [[77:13|and brought them through|et perduxit eos]] dry-shod along its bed; [[77:13|and he made the waters to stand|et statuit aquas]] of the Red Sea, thus divided, [[77:13|as in a vessel|quasi in utre]] [*uter*, a leather bottle], that is, he so fixed them in their place that they did not flow, as if they had been gathered in a vessel.

paras.t: Et deduxit eos, scilicet filios Israel ex Ægypto, et per mare Rubrum atque desertum, in nube diei, id est in columna nubis apparentis in die, et tota nocte, id est omnibus noctibus quibus ambulabant, in illuminatione ignis, id est in columna ignis viam ostendentis in tenebris noctis. Quemadmodum enim de die ambulabant sub nube, eos ab ardore solis protegente, ita de nocte sequebantur ductum ignis ; nec unquam defecit columna nubis aut ignis, donec ingressi essent terram promissionis ; nec proficiscebantur diebus aut noctibus, nisi columna nubis aut ignis prius locum mutaret, recedendo a tabernaculo : quæ omnia in Exodo et Numeris frequenter a Moyse describuntur.
paras.en: [[77:14|And he conducted them|Et deduxit eos]], namely the children of Israel, out of Egypt and through the Red Sea and the desert, [[77:14|with a cloud by day|in nube diei]], that is, in the pillar of cloud that appeared by day, [[77:14|and all the night|et tota nocte]], that is, on all the nights on which they journeyed, [[77:14|with a light of fire|in illuminatione ignis]], that is, in the pillar of fire that showed the way in the darkness of the night. For as by day they journeyed under the cloud, which protected them from the heat of the sun, so by night they followed the guidance of the fire; nor did the pillar of cloud or of fire ever fail until they had entered the land of promise; nor did they set out by day or by night unless the pillar of cloud or of fire first changed its place, withdrawing from the tabernacle: all of which Moses often describes in Exodus and Numbers[[Ex 13:1||]][[Ex 14:1||]][[Num 10:1||]].

paras.t: Interrupit petram in eremo. Bis legitur Deus omnipotens eduxisse aquam de petra filiis Israel : semel videlicet de petra Horeb, de qua eductione loquitur iste versiculus, quæ in Exodo plenius invenitur descripta ; secundo, quando Moyses percussit bis silicem, et egressæ sunt aquæ largissimæ, ita ut populus biberet et jumenta, de qua eductione in libro Numerorum habetur. Fueruntque eductiones istæ diversæ, quoniam prima erat ante dationem legis, secunda post eam.
paras.en: [[77:15|He struck the rock in the wilderness|Interrupit petram in eremo]]. We read that God almighty brought water out of the rock for the children of Israel twice: once, namely, from the rock of Horeb, the bringing forth of which this little verse speaks of, and which is found more fully described in Exodus[[Ex 17:6||]]; the second time, when Moses [[Num 20:11|struck the rock twice|percussit bis silicem]], [[Num 20:11|there came forth water in great abundance|et egressæ sunt aquæ largissimæ]], [[Num 20:11|so that the people and their cattle drank|ita ut populus biberet et jumenta]], of which bringing forth we read in the book of Numbers. And these bringings forth were distinct, since the first was before the giving of the law, the second after it.

paras.t: Ait ergo : Interrupit petram in eremo, id est, ita fecit quamdam concavitatem seu divisionem in ea, ac si rupta fuisset, et de petra sic rupta aquas eduxit ; et adaquavit eos, id est, aqua eos potavit, velut in abysso multa, id est tam abundanter, ac si fuissent juxta pelagus magnum, de quo ad libitum aqua hauritur. Quum enim fuerint sexcenta millia virorum in exercitu Hebræorum, præter mulieres et pueros, eos videlicet qui nondum viginti annos attigerant, et item præter vulgus promiscuum Ægyptiacum innumerabile, constat quod maxima copia aquæ fluxit de petra unde universi biberent.
paras.en: So he says: [[77:15|He struck the rock in the wilderness|Interrupit petram in eremo]] [*interrupit*, 'he broke through'], that is, he made a kind of hollow or cleft in it, as if it had been broken, and from the rock so broken he brought out waters; [[77:15|and gave them to drink|et adaquavit eos]], that is, he gave them water to drink, [[77:15|as out of the great deep|velut in abysso multa]], that is, as abundantly as if they had been beside the great sea, from which water is drawn at will. For since there were six hundred thousand men in the army of the Hebrews, besides the women and the boys, namely those who had not yet reached twenty years, and besides the countless mixed crowd of Egyptians, it is clear that a very great quantity of water flowed from the rock, for all of them to drink.

paras.t: Et eduxit aquam de petra, dum Moyses percussit bis petram seu silicem, sicut jam dictum est ; et eduxit ex petra hac, tanquam flumina aquas, id est aquas copiose fluentes instar fluviorum.
paras.en: [[77:16|He brought forth water out of the rock|Et eduxit aquam de petra]], when Moses struck the rock or flint twice, as has just been said; and from this rock he [[77:16|made streams run down as rivers|tanquam flumina aquas]], that is, waters flowing abundantly like rivers.

paras.t: Et apposuerunt adhuc peccare ei : id est, tantis beneficiis Creatoris ingrati fuerunt, reddiderunt malum pro bono, et prioribus suis sceleribus adjecerunt nova peccata : quia et ipsa ingratitudo magnum est peccatum ; in iram excitaverunt Excelsum : id est, ad similitudinem iræ, seu ad effectum iracundiæ, utpote ad justam ultionem atque magnarum inflictionem pœnarum, provocaverunt Deum sublimem suis peccatis : et hoc, in inaquoso, id est in deserto, in quo est naturaliter aquæ penuria.
paras.en: [[77:17|And they added yet more sin against him|Et apposuerunt adhuc peccare ei]]: that is, they were ungrateful for such great benefits of the Creator, returned evil for good, and added new sins to their former crimes: for ingratitude itself is also a great sin; [[77:17|they provoked the most High to wrath|in iram excitaverunt Excelsum]]: that is, to a likeness of wrath, or to the effect of anger, namely to just vengeance and the infliction of great punishments, they provoked God on high by their sins: and this [[77:17|in the place without water|in inaquoso]], that is, in the desert, where there is by nature a lack of water.

paras.t: Et tentaverunt Deum in cordibus suis : id est, ex proposito præmeditatoque cordis experiri volebant providentiam Dei, an scilicet Deus haberet curam eorum, providendo eis de necessariis ad vivendum. Ideo sequitur : ut peterent escas animabus suis, id est alimentum pro sustentatione vitæ. Bis autem escas hoc modo petiisse leguntur. Semel, ante legislationem, quando dixerunt ad Moysen : Cur induxisti nos in desertum istud, ut occideres omnem multitudinem fame ? Et tunc Dominus cœpit pluere manna. Secundo, petebant carnes sibi præstari, dicentes : Anima nostra arida est, nihil vident oculi nostri nisi manna : quemadmodum in libro Numerorum scriptum est.
paras.en: [[77:18|And they tempted God in their hearts|Et tentaverunt Deum in cordibus suis]]: that is, of the set and premeditated purpose of their heart they wished to put God's providence to the test, whether, namely, God had care of them, providing them with what they needed to live. Therefore there follows: [[77:18|by asking meat for their desires|ut peterent escas animabus suis]] [*animabus suis*, literally 'for their souls', that is, for their lives], that is, nourishment for the sustaining of life. Now we read that they asked for food in this way twice. Once, before the giving of the law, when they said to Moses: [[Ex 16:3|Why have you brought us into this desert, that you might destroy all the multitude with famine?|Cur induxisti nos in desertum istud, ut occideres omnem multitudinem fame]] And then the Lord began to rain manna. The second time, they asked for meat to be given them, saying: [[Num 11:6|Our soul is dry, our eyes behold nothing else but manna|Anima nostra arida est, nihil vident oculi nostri nisi manna]]: as is written in the book of Numbers.

paras.t: Et male, videlicet infideliter et perverse, locuti sunt de Deo ; dixerunt quod subditur : Numquid poterit Deus parare mensam in deserto, id est, refectionem pinguem et deliciosam ? Hoc non asserative, sed dubitative dixerunt ; arguebant tamen quod Deus hoc posset.
paras.en: [[77:19|And they spoke ill|Et male]], that is, faithlessly and perversely, [[77:19|of God|de Deo]]; they said what follows: [[77:19|Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?|Numquid poterit Deus parare mensam in deserto]] that is, a rich and delicious meal? They said this not by way of assertion but of doubt; yet they gave proof that God could do it.

paras.t: Quoniam percussit petram, et fluxerunt aquæ ex ea, et torrentes inundaverunt, id est, aquæ copiosæ inde egressæ sunt : sicut nunc patuit.
paras.en: [[77:20|Because he struck the rock, and the waters gushed out, and the streams overflowed|Quoniam percussit petram, et fluxerunt aquæ ex ea, et torrentes inundaverunt]], that is, abundant waters came out from it: as has just appeared.

paras.t: Quum ergo sit ita, Numquid et panem poterit dare ? Per panem (secundum quosdam) non intelligitur hic manna, quoniam Deus hunc panem ante eductionem aquæ prædictam dedit ; sed per panem intelligitur hic quilibet cibus delicatus, ab eis desideratus. Solet quippe Scriptura nomine panis quemcumque cibum significare, sicut et nomine aquæ quemlibet potum. Unde de Saul habetur, quod tota die non comederat panem ; et de Esdra, quod panem non comedit, nec bibit aquam, id est, nihil gustavit. Et legitur Eliseus dixisse regi Israel, ut apponeret exercitui regis Syriæ, quem Eliseus miraculose adduxit, panem et aquam. Et sequitur illic : Apposita est eis magna præparatio ciborum. Sic ergo et nunc per panem intelligi dicunt cibum deliciosum : et ideo additur, aut parare mensam populo suo ? ubi per mensam intelligi volunt refectionem delicatam, præsertim quoniam in Hebræo et in translatione Hieronymi juxta Hebræum, habetur : Aut parare carnem populo suo ? Hæc vero (ut tactum est) non affirmando, sed dubitando dixerunt. Dixerunt enim, ut Moyses scribit : Estne Deus in nobis an non ? Denique de hac infidelissima tentatione eorum in libro Numerorum scribitur : Flagrabant desiderio carnium, et dicebant : Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes ? In mentem nobis veniunt cucumeres et pepones, porri et allia, quæ comedebamus in Ægypto.
paras.en: Since, then, this is so, [[77:20|Can he also give bread|Numquid et panem poterit dare]]? By *bread* (according to some) manna is not understood here, since God had given this bread before the bringing forth of water just mentioned; but by *bread* is understood here any dainty food that they desired. For Scripture is accustomed to signify any food by the name of bread, as also any drink by the name of water. Hence it is said of Saul that [[1 Kings 28:20|he had eaten no bread all that day|tota die non comederat panem]]; and of Esdras that [[1 Esd 10:6|he ate no bread, and drank no water|panem non comedit, nec bibit aquam]], that is, he tasted nothing. And we read that Eliseus told the king of Israel to set bread and water before the army of the king of Syria, which Eliseus had brought there miraculously[[4 Kings 6:22||]]. And there follows there: [[4 Kings 6:23|a great provision of meats was set before them|Apposita est eis magna præparatio ciborum]]. So in the same way here too they say that by *bread* dainty food is understood; and therefore it is added, [[77:20|or provide a table for his people|aut parare mensam populo suo]]? where by *table* they will have a delicate meal understood, especially since in the Hebrew, and in Jerome's translation from the Hebrew, we have: *Or provide flesh for his people?* But these things (as was touched on) they said not affirming but doubting. For they said, as Moses writes: [[Ex 17:7|Is the Lord amongst us or not|Estne Deus in nobis an non]]? [Exodus has *Dominus*, 'the Lord', where Denis writes *Deus*, 'God']. Finally, of this most faithless tempting of theirs it is written in the book of Numbers: they [[Num 11:4|burned with desire|Flagrabant desiderio]] for flesh, and said: [[Num 11:4|Who shall give us flesh to eat|Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes]]? [[Num 11:5|the cucumbers come into our mind, and the melons, and the leeks|In mentem nobis veniunt cucumeres et pepones, porri]], [[Num 11:5|and the garlic|et allia]], [[Num 11:5|that we ate in Egypt|quæ comedebamus in Ægypto]].

paras.t: Ideo, id est, ex quo ista ex infidelitate dixerunt, non habentes pro certo quod Dominus posset implere quod desiderabant, audivit Dominus petitionem ipsorum, non quia ipsi hoc meruerunt, sed ut ipse suam omnipotentiam declararet ; et distulit, id est, non statim ultus est peccatum eorum, sed distulit debitam pœnam, ut postmodum tempore convenienti eam infligeret, et primo ostenderet suam potestatem. Et ignis, id est vehemens furor seu grandis vindicta, accensus est in Jacob, id est, juste inflictus est posteritati Jacob, videlicet filiis Israel : quod consequenter clarius dicitur ; et ira Dei, id est ultio divinæ justitiæ, ascendit in Israel, id est in populum Israeliticum, de semine Jacob, qui dictus est Israel, genitum.
paras.en: [[77:21|Therefore|Ideo]], that is, because they said these things out of unbelief, not holding for certain that the Lord could fulfil what they desired, [[77:21|the Lord heard|audivit Dominus]] their petition, not because they deserved it, but that he might declare his omnipotence; [[77:21|and was angry|et distulit]] [*distulit*, 'he put off'; the Douay-Rheims has 'was angry'], that is, he did not at once avenge their sin, but put off the due punishment, so as to inflict it later at a fitting time, and first to show his power. [[77:21|and a fire|Et ignis]], that is, vehement fury or great vengeance, [[77:21|was kindled against Jacob|accensus est in Jacob]], that is, was justly inflicted on the posterity of Jacob, namely the children of Israel: which is said more clearly next; [[77:21|and wrath|et ira]] of God, that is, the vengeance of divine justice, [[77:21|came up against Israel|ascendit in Israel]], that is, against the Israelite people, begotten of the seed of Jacob, who was called Israel.

paras.t: Hoc modo communiter versus iste explanatur. Sed quoniam in libro Numerorum evidenter habetur : Ortum est murmur populi quasi dolentium pro labore : quod quum audisset Dominus, iratus est ; et accensus in eos ignis Domini, devoravit extremam partem castrorum : quod certum est dici de igne materiali ; ideo potest hic versus de illo igne exponi. Nec obstat quod illius ignis accensio hanc tentationem præcessit, quoniam in divina Scriptura, gesta non semper narrantur eo ordine quo contigerunt ; sed quædam per anticipationem, quædam per recapitulationem, quædam per supplementum dicuntur : quod maxime fit in libris metrice scriptis, qualis est liber Psalmorum.
paras.en: This is how this verse is commonly explained. But since in the book of Numbers it is plainly said: [[Num 11:1|there arose a murmuring of the people|Ortum est murmur populi]] [[Num 11:1|as it were repining at their fatigue|quasi dolentium pro labore]]: [[Num 11:1|And when the Lord heard it he was angry|quod quum audisset Dominus, iratus est]]; [[Num 11:1|And the fire of the Lord being kindled against them, devoured them that were at the uttermost part of the camp|et accensus in eos ignis Domini, devoravit extremam partem castrorum]]: which is certainly said of material fire; therefore this verse can be expounded of that fire. Nor is it an objection that the kindling of that fire came before this tempting, since in divine Scripture deeds are not always told in the order in which they happened; but some are told by anticipation, some by recapitulation, some by way of supplement: which happens most of all in books written in metre, such as the book of Psalms.

paras.t: Ideo autem Deus eos ita punivit, Quia non crediderunt in Deo, qui eis promisit quod induceret eos in terram Chanaan. Dixerunt namque, ut in libro Numerorum habetur : Utinam pereamus, et non inducat nos Dominus in terram hanc, ne cadamus gladio et nos et filii nostri et uxores. Unde Dominus ad Moysen dixit : Usquequo multitudo hæc pessima non credet mihi ? Nec speraverunt in salutari ejus, id est salubri auxilio Dei, quod Deus eis promisit per Moysen, dicens : Dominus pugnabit pro vobis.
paras.en: Now God punished them so for this reason: [[77:22|Because they believed not in God|Quia non crediderunt in Deo]], who promised them that he would bring them into the land of Chanaan. For they said, as is told in the book of Numbers: [[Num 14:3|would God we may die|Utinam pereamus]], [[Num 14:3|and that the Lord may not bring us into this land, lest we fall by the sword|et non inducat nos Dominus in terram hanc, ne cadamus gladio]], both we and our children and wives. Hence the Lord said to Moses: [[Num 14:27|How long doth this wicked multitude|Usquequo multitudo hæc pessima]] [[Num 14:11|not believe me|non credet mihi]]? [Denis joins Num 14:27 and 14:11]. [[77:22|and trusted not in his salvation|Nec speraverunt in salutari ejus]], that is, in the saving help of God, which God promised them through Moses, saying: [[Ex 14:14|The Lord will fight for you|Dominus pugnabit pro vobis]].

paras.t: Et mandavit nubibus desuper : id est, ex divino imperio factum est, ut ex aere, in quo nubes generantur, manna descenderet. Dicitur enim Deus irrationalibus et inanimatis præcipere, quando ex divinæ virtutis nutu aliquid patiuntur et agunt. Propter quod Dominus ait Eliæ : Præcepi corvis ut pascant te. Et januas cœli aperuit, id est, vias fecit in cœlo aerio per quas manna descendit.
paras.en: [[77:23|And he had commanded the clouds from above|Et mandavit nubibus desuper]]: that is, it came about by God's command that the manna came down from the air, in which clouds are formed. For God is said to command irrational and inanimate things when at the bidding of the divine power they undergo or do something. For which reason the Lord said to Elias: [[3 Kings 17:4|I have commanded the ravens to feed thee|Præcepi corvis ut pascant te]]. [[77:23|and had opened the doors of heaven|Et januas cœli aperuit]], that is, he made ways in the heaven of the air, through which the manna came down.

paras.t: Et pluit illis manna ad manducandum, et panem cœli, id est in cœlo aerio ministerio angelorum formatum, dedit eis ad vescendum.
paras.en: [[77:24|And had rained down manna upon them to eat|Et pluit illis manna ad manducandum]], and [[77:24|the bread of heaven|et panem cœli]], that is, formed in the heaven of the air by the ministry of angels, [[77:24|had given them|dedit eis]] to feed on.

paras.t: Propterea subditur : Panem angelorum, id est ministerio angelico productum ac descendentem ; non quod angeli sancti eo vescuntur, quoniam non utuntur cibo corporeo, sicut habetur in libro Tobiæ ; manducavit homo quilibet in exercitu Hebræorum ; cibaria misit eis in abundantia, id est usque ad satietatem.
paras.en: Therefore there is added: [[77:25|the bread of angels|Panem angelorum]], that is, produced and coming down by the ministry of angels; not that the holy angels feed on it, since they do not use bodily food, as we have in the book of Tobias[[Tob 12:19||]]; [[77:25|Man ate|manducavit homo]], any man in the army of the Hebrews; [[77:25|he sent them provisions in abundance|cibaria misit eis in abundantia]], that is, to their fill.

paras.t: Ex isto sequi videtur, quod id quod dictum est supra, Numquid et panem poterit dare ? intelligi poterit de manna, quia tunc dicitur Deus petitionem eorum audivisse, et manna seu panem cœlestem eis dedisse. De hoc pane seu manna, quod simul descendit cum rore, in libro Exodi sic dicitur : Mane ros jacuit per circuitum castrorum, et apparuit in solitudine manna minutum, quasi pilo tusum, in similitudinem pruinæ super terram ; et appellaverunt filii Israel illud Manhu, id est, Quid est hoc ? Quod erat quasi semen coriandri album, gustusque ejus quasi similæ cum melle. Propterea quoque alio loco scriptum est : Angelorum esca nutrivisti populum tuum, et panem de cœlo præstitisti eis, omne delectamentum in se habentem, et omnis saporis suavitatem : deserviens enim uniuscujusque voluntati, ad quod quisque volebat, convertebatur.
paras.en: From this it seems to follow that what was said above, [[77:20|Can he also give bread|Numquid et panem poterit dare]]? can be understood of manna, since it is then said that God heard their petition and gave them manna, or heavenly bread. Of this bread or manna, which came down together with the dew, it is said thus in the book of Exodus: [[Ex 16:13|in the morning a dew lay round about the camp|Mane ros jacuit per circuitum castrorum]], [[Ex 16:14|it appeared in the wilderness small, and as it were beaten with a pestle, like unto the hoar frost on the ground|et apparuit in solitudine manna minutum, quasi pilo tusum, in similitudinem pruinæ super terram]]; and the children of Israel called it [[Ex 16:15|Manhu! which signifieth: What is this!|Manhu, id est, Quid est hoc]] [[Ex 16:31|it was like coriander seed, white, and the taste thereof like to flour with honey|Quod erat quasi semen coriandri album, gustusque ejus quasi similæ cum melle]]. Therefore it is also written in another place: [[Wis 16:20|thou didst feed thy people with the food of angels|Angelorum esca nutrivisti populum tuum]], [[Wis 16:20|and gavest them bread from heaven|et panem de cœlo præstitisti eis]], [[Wis 16:20|having in it all that is delicious, and the sweetness of every taste|omne delectamentum in se habentem, et omnis saporis suavitatem]]: [[Wis 16:21|and serving every man's will, it was turned to what every man liked|deserviens enim uniuscujusque voluntati, ad quod quisque volebat, convertebatur]].

paras.t: Transtulit Austrum de cælo, id est, Deus cessare fecit in aere ventum australem seu meridionalem, et induxit in virtute sua Africum, id est, in potentia sua flare fecit ventum occidentalem, lateralem versus meridiem. Flat enim hic ventus inter meridiem et occidentem. Ideo vero induxit hunc ventum ab Africa flantem, quatenus multitudinem coturnicum ab illa parte exsistentem, suo impetu ultra mare afferret ad locum filiorum Israel, juxta illud libri Numerorum : Ventus autem egrediens a Domino, arreptas trans mare coturnices detulit et demisit in castra.
paras.en: [[77:26|He removed the south wind from heaven|Transtulit Austrum de cælo]], that is, God made the south or meridional wind cease in the air, [[77:26|and by his power brought in the southwest wind|et induxit in virtute sua Africum]], that is, by his might he made the west wind blow, the side wind towards the south. For this wind blows between south and west. And he brought in this wind blowing from Africa so that by its force it might carry the multitude of quails that was in that region across the sea to the place of the children of Israel, according to that passage of the book of Numbers: [[Num 11:31|a wind going out from the Lord, taking quails up beyond the sea brought them, and cast them into the camp|Ventus autem egrediens a Domino, arreptas trans mare coturnices detulit et demisit in castra]].

paras.t: Idcirco subjungitur : Et pluit super eos sicut pulverem carnes, non mortuas, sed vivas : de quibus subjicitur, et sicut arenam maris volatilia pennata. Erant namque coturnices aves circa terram volantes, duobus cubitis in altitudinem super terram. Hæc autem animalia Deus pluit, id est, per modum pluviæ misit de aere tam copiose, quasi arenam maris, secundum quod a Moyse dicitur : Ventus detulit coturnices in castra, itinere quantum uno die confici potest, ex omni parte castrorum per circuitum.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[77:27|And he rained upon them flesh as dust|Et pluit super eos sicut pulverem carnes]], not dead but living: of which is added, [[77:27|and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea|et sicut arenam maris volatilia pennata]]. For the quails were birds flying near the ground, [[Num 11:31|two cubits high above the ground|duobus cubitis in altitudinem super terram]]. And God rained these creatures, that is, sent them down from the air by way of rain, as plentifully as the sand of the sea, according to what Moses says: The wind brought the quails into the camp, [[Num 11:31|for the space of one day's journey, on every side of the camp round about|itinere quantum uno die confici potest, ex omni parte castrorum per circuitum]].

paras.t: Et ceciderunt animalia hæc in medio castrorum eorum, id est intra vel prope castra seu tentoria filiorum Israel, scilicet circa tabernacula seu papiliones eorum, ita quod sine labore capi poterant. Unde dicitur in Numeris : Surgens populus toto die illo et nocte, ac die sequenti, congregavit coturnicum multitudinem, et siccaverunt eas per gyrum castrorum.
paras.en: [[77:28|And they fell|Et ceciderunt]], these creatures, [[77:28|in the midst of their camp|in medio castrorum eorum]], that is, within or near the camp or tents of the children of Israel, namely [[77:28|round about their pavilions|circa tabernacula]] or tents, so that they could be caught without labour. Hence it is said in Numbers: [[Num 11:32|The people therefore rising up all that day, and night, and the next day, gathered together of quails|Surgens populus toto die illo et nocte, ac die sequenti, congregavit coturnicum multitudinem]], [[Num 11:32|and they dried them round about the camp|et siccaverunt eas per gyrum castrorum]].

paras.t: Et manducaverunt filii Israel carnes has, et saturati sunt nimis, usque ad collum et nauseam, et desiderium eorum attulit eis, id est, rem ab eis desideratam contulit ipsis ; non sunt fraudati a desiderio suo, id est, adeptione rei desideratæ non sunt privati, quoniam carnium copiam sunt adepti. Quæ omnia in libro Numerorum clarius inducuntur, hoc modo : Dixit Dominus ad Moysen : Populo dices, Cras comedetis carnes, et comedetis non uno die, neque duobus vel quinque, sed usque ad mensem dierum, donec exeat per nares vestras, et vertatur in nauseam.
paras.en: [[77:29|So they did eat|Et manducaverunt]], the children of Israel, this flesh, [[77:29|and were filled exceedingly|et saturati sunt nimis]], up to the neck and to loathing, [[77:29|and he gave them their desire|et desiderium eorum attulit eis]], that is, he bestowed on them the thing they desired; [[77:30|they were not defrauded of that which they craved|non sunt fraudati a desiderio suo]], that is, they were not deprived of getting the thing desired, since they obtained plenty of meat. All of which is set out more clearly in the book of Numbers, in this way: [[Num 11:16|And the Lord said to Moses|Dixit Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[Num 11:18|And thou shalt say to the people|Populo dices]]: [[Num 11:18|to morrow you shall eat flesh|Cras comedetis carnes]], and you shall eat it [[Num 11:19|Not for one day, nor two, nor five|non uno die, neque duobus vel quinque]], [[Num 11:20|But even for a month of days, till it come out at your nostrils, and become loathsome to you|sed usque ad mensem dierum, donec exeat per nares vestras, et vertatur in nauseam]].

paras.t: Adhuc escæ eorum, scilicet carnes istæ, erant in ore ipsorum, et ira Dei, scilicet ultio sequens, ascendit super eos. Nam et occidit pingues eorum, id est in divitiis abundantes, superbos, carnales; et electos Israel impedivit. Hoc dupliciter accipi potest. Primo sic: Electos Israel, id est bonos et justos Judæos, impedivit, ita quod sua exhortatione aut prece nihil proficere poterant reprobis illis: quoniam exigentibus vitiis reproborum, electi pro eis exauditi non sunt. Secundo sic: Electos Israel, id est elegantes personas populi hujus, ab ingressu terræ promissionis impedivit. Et hoc est quod in Numeris dicitur: Adhuc carnes erant in dentibus eorum, nec defecerat hujusmodi cibus, et ecce furor Domini concitatus in populum, percussit eum plaga magna nimis. Vocatusque est locus ille, sepulcra Concupiscentiæ: ibi enim sepelierunt populum qui desideraverant carnes.
paras.en: [[77:30|As yet their meat|Adhuc escæ eorum]], that is, this flesh-meat, [[77:30|was in their mouth|erant in ore ipsorum]], [[77:31|And the wrath of God|et ira Dei]], that is, the vengeance that followed, [[77:31|came upon them|ascendit super eos]]. For [[77:31|he slew the fat ones amongst them|occidit pingues eorum]], that is, those abounding in riches, the proud, the carnal; [[77:31|and brought down the chosen men of Israel|et electos Israel impedivit]] [*impedivit*, literally "he hindered"; both of Denis's readings take it so]. This can be taken in two ways. First thus: [[77:31|the chosen men of Israel|Electos Israel]], that is, the good and just Jews, he hindered, so that by their exhortation or prayer they could do nothing to profit those reprobates: since, as the vices of the reprobate demanded, the elect were not heard on their behalf. Second thus: [[77:31|the chosen men of Israel|Electos Israel]], that is, the choice persons of this people, he hindered from entering the land of promise. And this is what is said in Numbers: [[Num 11:33|As yet the flesh was between their teeth, neither had that kind of meat failed: when behold the wrath of the Lord being provoked against the people, struck them with an exceeding great plague|Adhuc carnes erant in dentibus eorum, nec defecerat hujusmodi cibus, et ecce furor Domini concitatus in populum, percussit eum plaga magna nimis]]. [[Num 11:34|And that place was called, The graves of lust: for there they buried the people that had lusted|Vocatusque est locus ille, sepulcra Concupiscentiæ: ibi enim sepelierunt populum qui desideraverant carnes]] [Denis adds "for flesh"].

paras.t: In omnibus his jam prædictis non emendati, sed in suis perversitatibus perdurantes, peccaverunt adhuc, videlicet post reditum exploratorum, volentes tunc in Ægyptum reverti; et non crediderunt in mirabilibus ejus: id est, ex consideratione primorum mirabilium quæ Deus fecit coram eis in Ægypto, in mari Rubro, in deserto, nolebant credere quod Deus posset eos in terram Chanaan salvos inducere, propter fortitudinem populi, civitatum atque murorum terræ illius: imo volebant Caleb et Josue lapidare, eo quod dixerant Deum facile posse verbum suum implere, et Chananæos dejicere.
paras.en: [[77:32|In all these things|In omnibus his]] already spoken of, not amended but persisting in their perversities, [[77:32|they sinned still|peccaverunt adhuc]], namely after the return of the spies, when they wished then to go back into Egypt[[Num 14:3||]][[Num 14:4||]]; [[77:32|and they behaved not for his wondrous works|et non crediderunt in mirabilibus ejus]] [literally "they believed not in his wonders", as Denis's gloss takes it]: that is, from considering the first wonders which God had done before them in Egypt, in the Red Sea and in the desert, they would not believe that God could bring them safe into the land of Chanaan, because of the strength of the people, the cities and the walls of that land: nay, they wished to stone Caleb and Josue[[Num 14:10||]], because these had said that God could easily fulfil his word and cast down the Chanaanites.

paras.t: Et defecerunt in vanitate dies eorum, id est, propter peccata sua inanes erant dies ipsorum; et anni eorum cum festinatione defecerunt, id est, cito consumpti sunt, occisi atque prostrati in eremo: quoniam omnes qui tunc numerati erant et murmuraverunt, intra quadraginta annos defuncti sunt in ipso deserto, nec ingredi poterant terram promissam; multi quoque eorum subita morte occisi sunt per serpentes ignitos, et in contradictione Core et propter peccatum Phogor.
paras.en: [[77:33|And their days were consumed in vanity|Et defecerunt in vanitate dies eorum]], that is, because of their sins their days were empty; [[77:33|and their years in haste|et anni eorum cum festinatione defecerunt]] were consumed, that is, they were quickly used up, slain and laid low in the wilderness: for all who were numbered then and murmured died within forty years in that same desert, and could not enter the promised land[[Num 26:64||]][[Num 26:65||]]; many of them also were slain by sudden death through the fiery serpents[[Num 21:6||]], and in the gainsaying of Core[[Num 16:1||]], and because of the sin of Phogor[[Num 25:1||]].

paras.t: Quum occideret eos, quærebant eum, et revertebantur: non quod iidem numero occidebantur et revertebantur; sed secundum regulam in principio positam, loquitur hic Scriptura de diversis, ad eumdem populum pertinentibus, quasi de eisdem suppositis. Itaque, Quum Deus quosdam prævaricatores occideret, aliqui territi sunt ne similia experirentur tormenta: idcirco quærebant eum, id est, misericordiam Dei pro indulgentia invocabant, et revertebantur ad Deum per pœnitentiam. Et diluculo, id est, celeriter ex magno pœnarum timore, veniebant ad eum, non gressibus pedum spatioque locorum, sed mentis immutatione et pœnitentia cordis.
paras.en: [[77:34|When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned|Quum occideret eos, quærebant eum, et revertebantur]]: not that the same men in number were slain and returned; but, according to the rule laid down at the beginning, Scripture here speaks of different men belonging to the same people as if of the same subjects [that is, the same persons]. So: when God slew certain transgressors, some were terrified lest they should suffer like torments; and so they sought him, that is, they called on God's mercy for pardon, and returned to God by penance. And [[77:34|early in the morning|diluculo]], that is, quickly, out of great fear of punishment, [[77:34|came to him|veniebant ad eum]]: not by the steps of their feet and the crossing of places, but by a change of mind and repentance of heart.

paras.t: Et rememorati sunt ex consideratione priorum mirabilium Dei, et occisione eorum qui ita non recoluerunt, quia Deus adjutor est eorum in omnibus bonis, sicut fuit adjutor eorum in Ægypto, et contra Amalec, et Deus excelsus redemptor eorum est, eruens eos a cunctis periculis, sicut eruit eos de manu Pharaonis et ejus exercitu.
paras.en: [[77:35|And they remembered|Et rememorati sunt]], from considering God's earlier wonders and the slaying of those who did not so call them to mind, [[77:35|that God was their helper|quia Deus adjutor est eorum]] in all good things [Denis's text adds these words], as he was their helper in Egypt and against Amalec, [[77:35|and the most high God their redeemer|et Deus excelsus redemptor eorum est]], rescuing them from all dangers, as he rescued them from the hand of Pharao and his army.

paras.t: Verumtamen, quoniam ista reversio non erat ex caritate divina, sed ex timore servili: quo pœna timetur, per cujus imminentiam seu experientiam pensat homo veritatem, juxta illud, Tantummodo sola vexatio dabit intellectum auditui; propterea modo subjungitur: Et dilexerunt eum in ore suo, id est, verbis precatoriis simulabant se Deum amare, et lingua sua mentiti sunt ei, id est, verba eorum falsa fuerunt, neque ex corde sincero prolata sunt. Cor autem eorum non erat rectum cum eo, id est, Deo non placuit, quoniam justum et verum non fuit; nec fideles habiti sunt in testamento ejus, id est, fideliter non egerunt in lege divina, ejus custodiendo præcepta.
paras.en: Yet, since this return was not from divine charity but from servile fear [that is, fear of punishment rather than love of God], by which punishment is feared, and through its nearness or the experience of it a man weighs the truth, according to that saying, [[Is 28:19|vexation alone shall make you understand what you hear|Tantummodo sola vexatio dabit intellectum auditui]], there is added now: [[77:36|And they loved him with their mouth|Et dilexerunt eum in ore suo]], that is, with words of prayer they pretended to love God, [[77:36|and with their tongue they lied unto him|et lingua sua mentiti sunt ei]], that is, their words were false and were not spoken from a sincere heart. [[77:37|But their heart was not right with him|Cor autem eorum non erat rectum cum eo]], that is, it did not please God, since it was not just and true; [[77:37|nor were they counted faithful in his covenant|nec fideles habiti sunt in testamento ejus]], that is, they did not act faithfully in the divine law by keeping its precepts.

paras.t: Ipse autem Deus est misericors, et propitius fiet peccatis eorum, posteritatem eorum non penitus auferendo, et ipsos citra condignum puniendo; et non disperdet eos, id est, non penitus dispersit eos, sed quosdam ad tempus in vita servavit, et eis posteritatem concessit. Et abundavit ut averteret iram suam, id est, copiose paratus fuit vindictam interdum inceptam dimittere, populo parcere, et Moysis preces atque sacrificia Aaron pro peccatis acceptare; et non accendit omnem iram suam, id est, tantum non flagellavit eos ut meruerunt.
paras.en: [[77:38|But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins|Ipse autem Deus est misericors, et propitius fiet peccatis eorum]], not taking away their posterity entirely, and punishing them less than they deserved; [[77:38|and will not destroy them|et non disperdet eos]], that is, he did not wholly destroy them, but kept some alive for a time and granted them posterity. [[77:38|And many a time did he turn away his anger|Et abundavit ut averteret iram suam]] [*abundavit*, literally "he abounded"; hence Denis's gloss], that is, he was abundantly ready to remit a vengeance sometimes already begun, to spare the people, and to accept the prayers of Moses and the sacrifices of Aaron for their sins; [[77:38|and did not kindle all his wrath|et non accendit omnem iram suam]], that is, he did not scourge them as much as they deserved.

paras.t: Et recordatus est, id est, per modum recordantis se habuit, misericorditer ignoscendo, quia caro sunt, spiritus vadens et non rediens. Ponit hic partem pro toto, appellando hominem carnem, deinde spiritum euntem et non redeuntem.
paras.en: [[77:39|And he remembered|Et recordatus est]], that is, he behaved in the manner of one who remembers, mercifully pardoning, [[77:39|that they are flesh: a wind that goeth and returneth not|quia caro sunt, spiritus vadens et non rediens]] [*spiritus*, "breath" or "spirit"; Denis takes it of the soul]. Here he puts the part for the whole, calling man flesh, and then a spirit going and not returning.

paras.t: Est itaque sensus: Recordatus est quia caro sunt, id est, Deus benigne attendit quod corporales et fragiles erant, ac proclives in malum; recordatus est quoque quia spiritus sunt vadens et non rediens, id est, quod animæ hominum sunt multum defectuosæ, tanquam euntes de una dispositione in aliam, vagæ, instabiles, et tandem vadunt de corpore isto mortali ad regionem ignotam, nec redeunt naturali virtute ad pristinum statum. Ex hac autem recordatione inducitur Deus ad indulgendum nobis facile. Unde et ipsemet alibi testatur: Nequaquam ultra maledicam terræ propter homines; sensus enim et cogitatio cordis humani, prona sunt in malum ab adolescentia sua. Propter quod Esdras ait ad Dominum: Quid est enim homo, ut ei indigneris? aut genus corruptibile, ut ita amarus sis de illo?
paras.en: So the sense is: [[77:39|he remembered that they are flesh|Recordatus est quia caro sunt]], that is, God kindly took heed that they were bodily and frail, and prone to evil; he remembered also that they are a spirit [[77:39|that goeth and returneth not|vadens et non rediens]], that is, that the souls of men are very defective, passing as it were from one disposition to another, wandering, unstable, and at last they go out of this mortal body to an unknown region, and do not return by natural power to their former state. And by this remembrance God is moved to pardon us readily. Hence he himself bears witness elsewhere: [[Gen 8:21|I will no more curse the earth for the sake of man: for the imagination and thought of man's heart are prone to evil from his youth|Nequaquam ultra maledicam terræ propter homines; sensus enim et cogitatio cordis humani, prona sunt in malum ab adolescentia sua]]. Therefore Esdras says to the Lord: For what is man, that thou shouldst be angry with him? or a corruptible race, that thou shouldst be so bitter towards it? [4 Esdras 8:34, a book printed in the appendix of the Vulgate and not in the Douay-Rheims; no reference in the margin]

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Deus enormitatem peccati populi hujus, propter multitudinem et recidivum transgressionis ipsorum. Quoties exacerbaverunt eum in deserto, in iram concitaverunt eum in inaquoso? quasi dicat, Multoties. Unde Dominus ad Moysen ait: Tentaverunt me jam per decem vices. Quomodo autem dulcissimus atque incommutabilis Deus, exacerbari et ad iracundiam concitari dicatur, sæpe expositum est.
paras.en: Next God shows the enormity of this people's sin, because of the number and the relapses of their transgressions. [[77:40|How often did they provoke him in the desert: and move him to wrath in the place without water?|Quoties exacerbaverunt eum in deserto, in iram concitaverunt eum in inaquoso?]] As if to say: very many times. Hence the Lord said to Moses that they [[Num 14:22|have tempted me now ten times|Tentaverunt me jam per decem vices]]. How God, who is most sweet and unchangeable, is said to be embittered and roused to anger has often been explained.

paras.t: Et conversi sunt ad se ipsos, ut facerent propriam voluntatem, a Deo aversi, et tentaverunt Deum: sicut nunc sæpius dictum est; et Sanctum Israel, id est Deum omnium verorum Israelitarum sanctificatorem, exacerbaverunt: ita quod propter eorum peccata factus est eis austerus, amarus et durus, ratione effectus seu ultionis, qui in se ipso naturaliter, æternaliter et invariabiliter benignus, suavis et mitis est.
paras.en: [[77:41|And they turned back|Et conversi sunt]] to themselves, to do their own will, turned away from God, [[77:41|and tempted God|et tentaverunt Deum]], as has now been said many times; and [[77:41|the holy one of Israel|Sanctum Israel]], that is, God the sanctifier of all true Israelites, they [[77:41|grieved|exacerbaverunt]] [*exacerbaverunt*, literally "they embittered"; hence what follows]: so that because of their sins he became harsh, bitter and hard towards them, by reason of the effect, that is, of the vengeance, he who in himself is by nature, eternally and unchangeably, kind, sweet and gentle.

paras.t: Non sunt recordati isti ingrati manus ejus, id est potestatis et operationis divinæ ostensæ eis, die qua redemit eos de manu tribulantis, id est de imperio et oppressione regis Ægypti.
paras.en: [[77:42|They remembered not|Non sunt recordati]], these ungrateful men, [[77:42|his hand|manus ejus]], that is, the divine power and working shown to them, [[77:42|in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them|die qua redemit eos de manu tribulantis]], that is, from the rule and oppression of the king of Egypt.

paras.t: Sicut, id est quemadmodum seu qualiter, Deus posuit in Ægypto signa sua, id est decem plagas: secundum quod in Exodo ait, Percutiam Ægyptum in omnibus mirabilibus meis; et prodigia sua in campo Taneos: quod qualiter intelligi debeat, paulo ante satis prolixe monstratum est.
paras.en: [[77:43|How|Sicut]], that is, in what way or in what manner, God [[77:43|wrought his signs in Egypt|posuit in Ægypto signa sua]], that is, the ten plagues: according to what he says in Exodus, I [[Ex 3:20|will strike Egypt with all my wonders|Percutiam Ægyptum in omnibus mirabilibus meis]]; [[77:43|and his wonders in the field of Tanis|et prodigia sua in campo Taneos]]: how this should be understood was shown at some length a little before[[77:12||]].

paras.t: Deinde in speciali tractat de istis prodigiis. Et convertit in sanguinem flumina eorum, scilicet Ægyptiorum, et imbres eorum, id est cisternas seu aquas ex imbre scaturientes, ne biberent. Quemadmodum in Exodo dicitur, prima plaga Ægypti fuit, quod extendente Moyse virgam super fluvios Ægypti, versæ sunt omnes aquæ Ægypti in sanguinem; foderuntque Ægyptii circumquaque, et invenerunt sanguinem pro aqua, nec poterant bibere aquas fluminis propter alienationem saporis.
paras.en: Then he treats of these wonders in particular. [[77:44|And he turned their rivers into blood|Et convertit in sanguinem flumina eorum]], that is, of the Egyptians, [[77:44|and their showers|et imbres eorum]], that is, the cisterns, or the waters gathered from the rain, [[77:44|that they might not drink|ne biberent]]. As is said in Exodus, the first plague of Egypt was that, when Moses stretched out his rod over the rivers of Egypt, all the waters of Egypt were turned into blood[[Ex 7:19||]][[Ex 7:20||]]; and the Egyptians dug round about and found blood instead of water, and could not drink the waters of the river because of the strangeness of their taste[[Ex 7:24||]].

paras.t: Misit Deus in eos, puta Ægyptios, cynomyiam, id est muscam caninam: quia cynomyia dicitur a κυνός, quod est canis, et μυῖα, quod est musca; seu omne genus muscarum; et comedit eos: id est, musca ista punxit momorditque eos; et ranam, et disperdidit eos. Ponuntur autem in versiculo isto singularia pro pluralibus, quia per cynomyiam et ranam intelligenda est multitudo muscarum et ranarum. Missio quoque muscarum erat quarta plaga Ægypti, ut Dominus ait ad Pharaonem: Immittam in te, et in servos tuos, et in populum tuum, et in domos tuas omne genus muscarum. Et sequitur alibi: Venit musca gravissima (id est multitudo muscarum) in domum Pharaonis et in omnem terram ejus; corruptaque est terra ab hujusmodi muscis.
paras.en: God [[77:45|sent amongst them|Misit Deus in eos]], namely the Egyptians, [[77:45|divers sorts of flies|cynomyiam]] [the margin gives the other reading *cœnomyiam*, which is the Vulgate's: "a mixture of flies"], that is, the dog-fly: for *cynomyia* is named from κυνός, which is "dog", and μυῖα, which is "fly"; or else every kind of fly; [[77:45|which devoured them|et comedit eos]]: that is, this fly stung and bit them; [[77:45|and frogs which destroyed them|et ranam, et disperdidit eos]]. In this verse the singular is put for the plural [the Latin has "the dog-fly" and "the frog"], since by the dog-fly and the frog a multitude of flies and of frogs is to be understood. The sending of the flies, moreover, was the fourth plague of Egypt, as the Lord said to Pharao: [[Ex 8:21|I will send in upon thee, and upon thy servants, and upon thy houses, all kind of flies|Immittam in te, et in servos tuos, et in populum tuum, et in domos tuas omne genus muscarum]]. And it follows further on: [[Ex 8:24|there came a very grievous swarm of flies|Venit musca gravissima]] (that is, a multitude of flies) [[Ex 8:24|into the houses of Pharao|in domum Pharaonis]] and [[Ex 8:24|into all the land of Egypt|et in omnem terram ejus]]; [[Ex 8:24|and the land was corrupted by this kind of flies|corruptaque est terra ab hujusmodi muscis]].

paras.t: Missio autem ranarum erat secunda plaga Ægypti. De qua in Exodo scribitur: Dixit Dominus ad Pharaonem: Ecce ego percutiam omnes terminos tuos ranis, et ebulliet fluvius ranas, quæ ingredientur domum tuam, et cubiculum lectuli tui, et super stratum tuum, et in domos servorum tuorum, et in populum tuum, et in furnos tuos, et in reliquias ciborum tuorum.
paras.en: The sending of the frogs was the second plague of Egypt, of which it is written in Exodus: The Lord said to Pharao: [[Ex 8:2|behold I will strike all thy coasts with frogs|Ecce ego percutiam omnes terminos tuos ranis]]. [[Ex 8:3|And the river shall bring forth an abundance of frogs; which shall come up and enter into thy house, and thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the houses of thy servants, and to thy people, and into thy ovens, and into the remains of thy meats|et ebulliet fluvius ranas, quæ ingredientur domum tuam, et cubiculum lectuli tui, et super stratum tuum, et in domos servorum tuorum, et in populum tuum, et in furnos tuos, et in reliquias ciborum tuorum]].

paras.t: Et dedit ærugini, id est vento urenti, segetes corrumpenti; vel, Aurugini, id est auræ noxiæ, sive rubigini; fructus eorum, id est blada terræ, ad destruendum. Hæc plaga non est scripta in Exodo, sicut nec plaga pruinæ, de qua loquitur finis versus sequentis: quia in Exodo non recitantur nisi plagæ principales et notabiles.
