Et labores eorum, id est fructus Ægyptiorum, per eorum laborem productos, dedit Deus locustæ, id est multitudini locustarum, ad devorandum. Hæc fuit plaga Ægypti octava. De qua in Exodo scriptum est: Hæc dicit Dominus ad Pharaonem: Ecce ego inducam locustam in fines tuos, quæ operiet superficiem terræ, ne quidquam ejus appareat. Et venerunt locustæ innumerabiles, omnia devorantes quæ non erant consumpta a grandine.
paras.en: [[77:46|And he gave up|Et dedit]] [[77:46|to the blast|ærugini]], that is, to a burning wind that spoils the crops [*ærugo*, "blight" or "rust"]; or, *Aurugini*, that is, to a noxious air [as if from *aura*, "air"], or to mildew; [[77:46|their fruits|fructus eorum]], that is, the corn of the land, to be destroyed. This plague is not written in Exodus, as neither is the plague of hoarfrost of which the end of the next verse speaks: for in Exodus only the chief and notable plagues are related. [[77:46|And their labours|Et labores eorum]], that is, the fruits of the Egyptians produced by their labour, God gave [[77:46|to the locust|locustæ]], that is, to a multitude of locusts, to be devoured. This was the eighth plague of Egypt, of which it is written in Exodus: [[Ex 10:3|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]] to Pharao: [[Ex 10:4|behold I will bring in|Ecce ego inducam]] [[Ex 10:4|the locusts into thy coasts|locustam in fines tuos]], [[Ex 10:5|To cover the face of the earth, that nothing thereof may appear|quæ operiet superficiem terræ, ne quidquam ejus appareat]]. And the locusts came, innumerable, devouring all that had not been consumed by the hail[[Ex 10:14||]][[Ex 10:15||]].

paras.t: Et occidit in grandine, id est per casum maximæ grandinis, vineas eorum. Hæc erat septima plaga Ægypti. De qua a Moyse dicitur, quod maxima grando cecidit in terra Ægypti; et homines et jumenta super quæ cecidit grando, moriebantur; cunctamque quoque herbam agri percussit, et omne lignum regionis confregit. Et moros eorum Deus destruxit in pruina, id est in frigore congelante atque nocturno, vel in humore moris nocivo.
paras.en: [[77:47|And he destroyed|Et occidit]] [[77:47|with hail|in grandine]], that is, by the fall of very great hail, [[77:47|their vineyards|vineas eorum]]. This was the seventh plague of Egypt, of which Moses says that very great hail fell in the land of Egypt[[Ex 9:23||]]; and men and beasts on which the hail fell died; and that [[Ex 9:25|the hail smote every herb of the field, and it broke every tree of the country|cunctamque quoque herbam agri percussit, et omne lignum regionis confregit]]. [[77:47|And their mulberry trees|Et moros eorum]] God destroyed [[77:47|with hoarfrost|in pruina]], that is, with a freezing cold by night, or with a moisture harmful to mulberries.

paras.t: Et tradidit grandini jumenta eorum: quia omnia bruta in agris reperta grando occidit; dedit et possessionem eorum, scilicet Ægyptiorum, igni ad consumendum: quia ut dicitur in Exodo, Grando et ignis mixta pariter ferebantur.
paras.en: [[77:48|And he gave up their cattle to the hail|Et tradidit grandini jumenta eorum]]: for the hail slew all the beasts found in the fields; he gave also [[77:48|their stock|possessionem eorum]], that is, of the Egyptians, [[77:48|to the fire|igni]] to be consumed: for, as is said in Exodus, [[Ex 9:24|the hail and fire mixt with it drove on together|Grando et ignis mixta pariter ferebantur]].

paras.t: Misit in eos iram indignationis suæ, id est vindictam suæ ulciscentis justitiæ, scilicet indignationem, id est effectum sui contemptus, quo opera eorum indigne ferebat, et iram, id est æquitatis suæ ultionem, et tribulationem multiplicem, hic non expressam; immissiones quoque per angelos malos, id est, pessimas cogitationes, indurationem et obstinationem permisit Deus immitti cordibus Ægyptiorum per suggestionem cooperationemque dæmonum. Mala pœnæ sunt a Deo effective, sed mala culpæ non nisi permissive: quia de malo pœnæ apud Amos prophetam dicitur: Si erit malum in civitate quod Dominus non fecit?
paras.en: [[77:49|And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation|Misit in eos iram indignationis suæ]], that is, the vengeance of his avenging justice, namely [[77:49|indignation|indignationem]], that is, the effect of his contempt, by which he bore their works with indignation, [[77:49|and wrath|et iram]], that is, the vengeance of his equity, [[77:49|and trouble|et tribulationem]] manifold, not expressed here; [[77:49|which he sent by evil angels|immissiones quoque per angelos malos]] [*immissiones*, literally "things sent in"], that is, God permitted the worst thoughts, hardening and obstinacy to be sent into the hearts of the Egyptians through the suggestion and co-operation of the demons. Evils of punishment are from God as their cause, but evils of guilt only by his permission [that is, God inflicts punishment, but only permits sin]: for of the evil of punishment it is said in the prophet Amos: [[Amos 3:6|Shall there be evil in a city, which the Lord hath not done?|Si erit malum in civitate quod Dominus non fecit?]]

paras.t: Viam fecit semitæ iræ suæ: id est, plagas suæ iracundiæ misit versus Ægyptios, non versus Hebræos; sicque angelum vastatorem fecit declinare a terra Ramesses, in qua morabantur Judæi. Unde Dominus ait ad Pharaonem: Ponam divisionem inter populum meum et populum tuum. Non pepercit a morte animarum eorum: id est, Deus sine misericordia occidit Ægyptios magnos et parvos. Et jumenta eorum in morte conclusit, id est, occidit. Hæc vero fuit quinta plaga Ægypti. De qua dixit Dominus ad Pharaonem: Ecce manus mea erit super agros tuos; super equos et asinos et camelos, boves et oves, pestis valde gravis. Mortuaque sunt omnia animantia Ægyptiorum, videlicet in agro per pestilentiam.
paras.en: [[77:50|He made a way for a path to his anger|Viam fecit semitæ iræ suæ]]: that is, he sent the plagues of his wrath towards the Egyptians, not towards the Hebrews; and so he made the destroying angel turn aside from the land of Ramesses, in which the Jews dwelt. Hence the Lord said to Pharao: [[Ex 8:23|I will put a division between my people and thy people|Ponam divisionem inter populum meum et populum tuum]]. [[77:50|He spared not their souls from death|Non pepercit a morte animarum eorum]] [the margin gives the reading *animabus*, which is the Vulgate's]: that is, God slew the Egyptians, great and small, without mercy. [[77:50|And their cattle he shut up in death|Et jumenta eorum in morte conclusit]], that is, he slew them. This was the fifth plague of Egypt, of which the Lord said to Pharao: [[Ex 9:3|Behold my hand shall be upon thy fields|Ecce manus mea erit super agros tuos]]; [[Ex 9:3|a very grievous murrain|pestis valde gravis]] [[Ex 9:3|upon thy horses, and asses, and camels, and oxen, and sheep|super equos et asinos et camelos, boves et oves]]. And [[Ex 9:6|all the beasts of the Egyptians died|Mortuaque sunt omnia animantia Ægyptiorum]], namely in the field, by the pestilence.

paras.t: Et percussit omne primogenitum, tam hominum quam jumentorum, in terra Ægypti: et hæc erat decima plaga Ægypti, ut dicitur in Exodo. Percussit etiam Deus primitias omnis laboris eorum, id est primitiva atque potissima fructuum terræ Ægypti, puta frumenta et cetera, in tabernaculis Cham, id est in locis Ægyptiorum, qui nati erant de semine Cham filii Noe. Mesraim quippe, ut dicitur in Genesi, erat filius Cham, et ab hoc Mesraim Ægyptus nomen sortita est, quia in ea dominabatur: et ideo ubi nostra translatio habet, Ægyptus, in veteri Testamento dicitur, Mesraim.
paras.en: [[77:51|And he killed all the firstborn|Et percussit omne primogenitum]], of men as well as of beasts, [[77:51|in the land of Egypt|in terra Ægypti]]: and this was the tenth plague of Egypt, as is said in Exodus[[Ex 12:29||]] [the margin gives Exod. xii]. God struck also [[77:51|the firstfruits of all their labour|primitias omnis laboris eorum]], that is, the first and best of the fruits of the land of Egypt, such as the corn and the rest, [[77:51|in the tabernacles of Cham|in tabernaculis Cham]], that is, in the places of the Egyptians, who were born of the seed of Cham the son of Noe. For Mesraim, as is said in Genesis[[Gen 10:6||]], was the son of Cham, and Egypt took its name from this Mesraim, because he ruled in it: and so where our translation has *Egypt*, in the Old Testament [that is, in the Hebrew] it is called *Mesraim*.

paras.t: Deinde post descriptionem plagarum Ægypti, recitatur liberatio Hebræorum. Et abstulit sicut oves populum suum: id est, quemadmodum bonus pastor eruit oves suas de invasione luporum; sic Deus de Ægyptiis reprobis et malignis abstulit filios Israel; et perduxit eos tanquam grex in deserto: quia providit eis de bono pastore ac duce, scilicet Moyse, et de cibo ac potu.
paras.en: Then, after the description of the plagues of Egypt, the deliverance of the Hebrews is related. [[77:52|And he took away his own people as sheep|Et abstulit sicut oves populum suum]]: that is, as a good shepherd rescues his sheep from the onslaught of wolves, so God took the children of Israel away from the reprobate and malicious Egyptians; [[77:52|and guided them in the wilderness like a flock|et perduxit eos tanquam grex in deserto]]: for he provided them with a good shepherd and leader, namely Moses, and with food and drink.

paras.t: Et deduxit eos in spe, promittendo quod induceret eos in terram lacte et melle manantem; et non timuerunt ad tempus, quia secuti sunt Moysen per medium maris Rubri; et inimicos eorum operuit mare, videlicet Pharaonem et omnem ejus exercitum.
paras.en: [[77:53|And he brought them out in hope|Et deduxit eos in spe]], promising that he would bring them into a land flowing with milk and honey[[Ex 3:8||]][[Ex 3:17||]]; [[77:53|and they feared not|et non timuerunt]] for the time, since they followed Moses through the midst of the Red Sea[[Ex 14:22||]]; [[77:53|and the sea overwhelmed their enemies|et inimicos eorum operuit mare]], namely Pharao and all his army.

paras.t: Et induxit eos in montem sanctificationis suæ, id est in Jerusalem et montem Sion, in quo postmodum constructum est templum. Huc induxit, non eosdem, qui ex Ægypto egressi fuerant et numerati, præter Caleb et Josue, sed filios illorum, secundum quod Dominus dixit: Omnes qui murmurastis contra me, non intrabitis terram, super quam levavi manum meam ut darem eam vobis, præter Caleb filium Jephone, et Josue filium Nun. Duxit ergo eos in montem sanctificationis suæ, montem quem acquisivit dextera ejus, id est, quem Deus, cujus sunt omnia, de manu indignorum, propria potestate eripuit, et suo populo dedit.
paras.en: [[77:54|And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary|Et induxit eos in montem sanctificationis suæ]], that is, into Jerusalem and mount Sion, on which the temple was afterwards built. He brought there not the same men who had come out of Egypt and been numbered, except Caleb and Josue, but their sons, according to what the Lord said: [[Num 14:29|All you that|Omnes qui]] [[Num 14:29|have murmured against me|murmurastis contra me]], [[Num 14:30|Shall not enter into the land, over which I lifted up my hand|non intrabitis terram, super quam levavi manum meam]] to give it to you [Denis's wording; the Vulgate has "to make you dwell therein"], [[Num 14:30|except Caleb the son of Jephone, and Josue the son of Nun|præter Caleb filium Jephone, et Josue filium Nun]]. He led them, then, into [[77:54|the mountain of his sanctuary|montem sanctificationis suæ]], [[77:54|the mountain which his right hand had purchased|montem quem acquisivit dextera ejus]], that is, which God, whose are all things, snatched by his own power from the hand of the unworthy and gave to his people.

paras.t: Propter quod additur: Et ejecit a facie eorum gentes, id est, a conspectu Israelitarum expulit gentes in terra promissionis habitantes, eas occidendo, effugando, aut subjiciendo populo suo: ut patet de Gabaonitis et ceteris Chananæis, qui sub tributo manebant inter filios Israel, sicut in libro Josue commemoratur. Et sorte divisit eis terram in funiculo distributionis, per manum Eleazari sacerdotis, et Josue, ac principum tribuum Israel, qui ad imperium Domini diviserunt novem tribubus, et dimidiæ tribui Manasse, terram Chanaan, dantes pluribus majorem, paucioribusque minorem. De qua divisione plene tractatur in libro Josue. Tribus namque Ruben et Gad, media quoque tribus Manasse, ante hanc divisionem receperunt possessionem trans Jordanem. Tribus vero Levi non habuit possessionem, nisi ad habitandum, et ad pecora nutrienda; sed Deus Israel fuit eorum hereditas.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[77:54|And he cast out the Gentiles before them|Et ejecit a facie eorum gentes]], that is, from the sight of the Israelites he drove out the nations dwelling in the land of promise, by slaying them, putting them to flight, or subjecting them to his people: as is clear of the Gabaonites[[Jos 9:27||]] and the other Chanaanites, who remained under tribute among the children of Israel, as is recorded in the book of Josue. [[77:54|And by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution|Et sorte divisit eis terram in funiculo distributionis]], by the hand of Eleazar the priest, and of Josue, and of the princes of the tribes of Israel[[Jos 19:51||]], who at the Lord's command divided the land of Chanaan among nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasses, giving to the more a larger share and to the fewer a smaller. Of this division the book of Josue treats fully[[Jos 13:1||]] [the margin gives Jos. xiii–xix]. For the tribes of Ruben and Gad, and the half tribe of Manasses also, received their possession beyond the Jordan before this division[[Num 32:33||]]. But the tribe of Levi had no possession, except for dwelling in and for feeding their cattle; but the God of Israel was their inheritance[[Jos 13:33||]].

paras.t: Et habitare fecit in tabernaculis eorum, id est in civitatibus et villulis Chananæorum, tribus Israel.
paras.en: [[77:55|And he made|Et habitare fecit]] [[77:55|the tribes of Israel|tribus Israel]] [[77:55|to dwell in their tabernacles|in tabernaculis eorum]], that is, in the cities and villages of the Chanaanites.

paras.t: Consequenter narrantur peccata filiorum Israel, commissa in terra promissionis. Et tentaverunt Deum fidelem et verum, de ejus virtute dubitantes, et exacerbaverunt Deum excelsum: secundum sensum præexplanatum; et testimonia ejus non custodierunt. Duæ sunt partes legis divinæ, videlicet testimonia et præcepta. Testimonia pertinent ad credenda, præcepta ad operanda aut omittenda. Quoniam ergo Deum tentaverunt ex infidelitate, constat quod ejus testimonia, id est assertiones sacræ Scripturæ divinitus inspiratæ, non custodierunt, firmiter inviolabiliterque credendo.
paras.en: Next are told the sins of the children of Israel committed in the land of promise. [[77:56|Yet they tempted|Et tentaverunt]] God, faithful and true, doubting his power, [[77:56|and provoked the most high God|et exacerbaverunt Deum excelsum]], in the sense explained before; [[77:56|and they kept not his testimonies|et testimonia ejus non custodierunt]]. There are two parts of the divine law, namely testimonies and precepts. Testimonies belong to what is to be believed, precepts to what is to be done or left undone. Since, then, they tempted God out of unbelief, it is plain that they did not keep his testimonies, that is, the assertions of Holy Scripture, divinely inspired, by believing them firmly and inviolably.

paras.t: Et averterunt se a Deo et ejus imperio, et non servaverunt pactum, quod cum Deo inierunt, dicentes, ut legitur in Exodo: Omnia quæcumque locutus est Dominus, faciemus et erimus obedientes. Sicut patres eorum murmuratores, Deo rebelles, et vituli adoratores, conversi sunt in arcum pravum, id est, similes facti sunt arcui malo: quoniam sicut ex arcu pravo jaciuntur sagittæ non vulnerantes, ita ex ore ipsorum verba mortifera processerunt; et iterum, quoniam sicut arcus pravus extensus, cito laxatur atque remittitur, sic ipsi faciliter a bono proposito et cultu divino aversi sunt, et ad iniquitatem laxati.
paras.en: [[77:57|And they turned away|Et averterunt se]] from God and his command, [[77:57|and kept not the covenant|et non servaverunt pactum]] which they made with God, saying, as we read in Exodus: [[Ex 24:7|All things that the Lord hath spoken, we will do, we will be obedient|Omnia quæcumque locutus est Dominus, faciemus et erimus obedientes]]. [[77:57|Even like their fathers|Sicut patres eorum]], murmurers, rebels against God and worshippers of the calf[[Ex 32:4||]][[Ex 32:6||]], [[77:57|they were turned aside as a crooked bow|conversi sunt in arcum pravum]], that is, they became like a bad bow: for as from a crooked bow arrows are shot that do not wound their mark, so from their mouth deadly words came forth; and again, as a crooked bow when bent is soon slackened and let go, so they were easily turned aside from their good purpose and from the worship of God, and slackened into iniquity.

paras.t: In iram concitaverunt eum in collibus suis, sacrificando in excelsis: quod erat illicitum. Verumtamen advertendum, quod quando arca Domini non habuit certam ac stabilem mansionem, videlicet, antequam posita erat in Silo, et post destructionem Silo usque ad constructionem templi Salomonis, licuit Judæis offerre oblationes sacrificiaque votiva alibi, quam ubi fuerat arca: dum vero erat in Silo et templo Salomonis, istud non licuit. Quoniam ergo Hebræi terram promissionis ingressi, immolabant Deo in locis excelsis seu collibus, etiam tunc quando arca erat in Silo Salomonisque templo, idcirco nunc dicitur, In iram concitaverunt eum in collibus suis.
paras.en: [[77:58|They provoked him to anger on their hills|In iram concitaverunt eum in collibus suis]], by sacrificing on the high places, which was unlawful. Yet it must be noted that when the ark of the Lord had no fixed and settled dwelling, namely before it was placed in Silo[[Jos 18:1||]], and after the destruction of Silo until the building of Solomon's temple, it was lawful for the Jews to offer oblations and votive sacrifices elsewhere than where the ark was; but while it was in Silo and in Solomon's temple, this was not lawful. Since, then, the Hebrews, having entered the land of promise, sacrificed to God on high places or hills even at the times when the ark was in Silo and in Solomon's temple, it is said now: [[77:58|They provoked him to anger on their hills|In iram concitaverunt eum in collibus suis]].

paras.t: Pensandum tamen, quod ex dispensatione divina licuit prædictis temporibus alibi immolare, quam in loco arcæ, quemadmodum tertio Regum libro legitur Elias obtulisse sacrificium in monte Carmeli. Ex his innotescit, quomodo salvatur quod dicitur Salomon obtulisse sacrificium in excelso Gabaon; sed et Samuel in excelso legitur immolasse, quum tamen in libro Regum frequenter imputetur populo in peccatum, quod obtulit in excelsis. Et in sculptilibus suis, id est idola adorando, ad æmulationem, id est indignationem, eum provocaverunt.
paras.en: It must be borne in mind, however, that by divine dispensation it was lawful at the times just mentioned to sacrifice elsewhere than in the place of the ark, as we read in the third book of Kings that Elias offered sacrifice on mount Carmel[[3 Kings 18:30||]][[3 Kings 18:38||]]. From this it becomes clear how what is said may be upheld, that Solomon offered sacrifice on the high place of Gabaon[[3 Kings 3:4||]]; and Samuel too is read to have sacrificed on a high place[[1 Kings 7:9||]], though in the book of Kings it is often imputed to the people as a sin that they offered on the high places. And [[77:58|with their graven things|in sculptilibus suis]], that is, by worshipping idols, they [[77:58|moved him|eum provocaverunt]] [[77:58|to jealousy|ad æmulationem]], that is, to indignation.

paras.t: Audivit Deus, id est, mente cognovit ista eorum peccata; et sprevit tam eos, quam culpas eorum: quoniam sicut Sapiens ait, Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus. Hinc quoque corrigi non valebant, juxta illud sapientissimi Salomonis: Considera opera Dei, quod nemo possit corrigere quem ille despexerit. Et ad nihilum redegit valde Israel. Spiritualiter namque ad nihil eos redegit, quoniam omne esse caritatis et gratiæ eis subtraxit; corporaliter quoque eos ad nihilum redigebat, tradendo iniquos potestati inimicorum suorum, ut patet in libris Regum et Judicum.
paras.en: [[77:59|God heard|Audivit Deus]], that is, knew in his mind these sins of theirs; [[77:59|and despised|et sprevit]] both them and their faults: for, as the Wise Man says, [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful alike|Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]]. Hence also they could not be corrected, according to that saying of the most wise Solomon: [[Eccles 7:14|Consider the works of God, that no man can correct whom he hath despised.|Considera opera Dei, quod nemo possit corrigere quem ille despexerit]] [[77:59|And he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing|Et ad nihilum redegit valde Israel]]. For spiritually he reduced them to nothing, since he withdrew from them all the being of charity and grace; bodily, too, he reduced them to nothing, delivering the wicked into the power of their enemies, as is plain in the books of Kings and of Judges[[Judg 2:14||]].

paras.t: Et repulit tabernaculum Silo: id est, domum in qua erat arca, destrui, arcamque captivari permisit. Repulit ergo tabernaculum Silo, vel potius habitatores tabernaculi ejus, quia non propter locum gentem, sed propter gentem locum Dominus elegit. Similiter non propter locum gentem, sed propter gentem locum Dominus repulit. Tabernaculum, inquam, suum, ubi, id est in quo, habitavit in hominibus, id est inter homines. Deus enim in cordibus hominum bonorum per gratiam habitat, et quamdiu in ipsis hominibus demoratur, in tabernaculis quoque eorum, et maxime in consecratis, habitare censetur. Propter quod ait Scriptura: Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis. Et Moyses dicit: Dominus Deus ambulat in medio castrorum. Et ipse Dominus per Moysen: Ego, inquit, sum qui habito in medio filiorum Israel.
paras.en: [[77:60|And he put away the tabernacle of Silo|Et repulit tabernaculum Silo]]: that is, he allowed the house in which the ark was to be destroyed, and the ark to be taken captive. He put away, then, [[77:60|the tabernacle of Silo|tabernaculum Silo]], or rather the dwellers in its tabernacle, since [[2 Mach 5:19|God did not choose the people for the place's sake, but the place for the people's sake|non propter locum gentem, sed propter gentem locum Dominus elegit]]. In the same way it was not for the place's sake that the Lord rejected the people, but the place for the people's sake. His [[77:60|tabernacle|Tabernaculum]], I say, [[77:60|where|ubi]], that is, in which, [[77:60|he dwelt among men|habitavit in hominibus]], that is, among men [literally "in men"; hence what follows]. For God dwells by grace in the hearts of good men, and as long as he abides in those men, he is held to dwell also in their tabernacles, and above all in those that are consecrated. Therefore Scripture says: [[Apoc 21:3|Behold the tabernacle of God with men: and he will dwell with them|Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis]]. And Moses says: [[Deut 23:14|the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp|Dominus Deus ambulat in medio castrorum]]. And the Lord himself through Moses: I, he says, am he [[Num 35:34|that dwell among the children of Israel|qui habito in medio filiorum Israel]][[Ezech 43:7||]] [the margin gives Num. xxxv, 34 and Ezech. xliii, 7; Denis's words "in the midst of the children of Israel" are those of Ezechiel].

paras.t: Et tradidit Dominus in captivitatem Philistæis, qui alias dicti sunt Palæstini atque Allophyli, virtutem eorum, id est potentiam filiorum Israel: per quam intelligi potest robur exercitus eorum, seu fortes ipsorum; vel ipsa arca, cujus præsentia et virtute prævalere in præliis consueverunt; et pulchritudinem eorum, id est pulchras personas, seu arcam quæ exstitit decor et gloria eorum, in manus inimici, scilicet populi Philistinorum.
paras.en: [[77:61|And he delivered|Et tradidit Dominus]] [[77:61|into captivity|in captivitatem]] to the Philistines, who elsewhere are called Palestines and Allophyli [that is, "foreigners"], [[77:61|their strength|virtutem eorum]], that is, the might of the children of Israel: by which may be understood the force of their army, or their strong men; or else the ark itself, by whose presence and power they were wont to prevail in battle[[1 Kings 4:3||]]; [[77:61|and their beauty|et pulchritudinem eorum]], that is, their beautiful persons, or the ark, which was their adornment and glory, [[77:61|into the hands of the enemy|in manus inimici]], namely of the people of the Philistines.

paras.t: Et conclusit in gladio populum suum, id est, per arma et bella Philistinorum occidi permisit filios Israel; et hereditatem suam sprevit, id est, populum istum, quem sibi elegit et coluit, non protexit. Verumtamen reprobi illi non dicuntur populus atque hereditas Dei, nisi secundum vocationem et nomen, non secundum prædestinationem æternam: quemadmodum et Salvator in Evangelio de Judæis locutus est, Filii autem regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores.
paras.en: [[77:62|And he shut up his people under the sword|Et conclusit in gladio populum suum]], that is, he allowed the children of Israel to be slain by the arms and wars of the Philistines; [[77:62|and he despised his inheritance|et hereditatem suam sprevit]], that is, he did not protect this people, which he had chosen for himself and cherished. Yet those reprobates are called God's people and inheritance only by calling and name, not by eternal predestination: as the Saviour also said of the Jews in the Gospel: [[Matt 8:12|But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into the exterior darkness|Filii autem regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores]].

paras.t: Juvenes eorum, scilicet Judæorum, comedit, id est, devoravit et interfecit, ignis, id est magna impugnatio et vehemens furor Philistinorum; et virgines eorum non sunt lamentatæ: quoniam unusquisque pro sui ipsius evasione tam sollicitus erat, quod aliorum deploratione vacare non potuit.
paras.en: [[77:63|Their young men|Juvenes eorum]], namely of the Jews, [[77:63|fire|ignis]], that is, the great onslaught and vehement fury of the Philistines, [[77:63|consumed|comedit]], that is, devoured and slew; [[77:63|and their maidens were not lamented|et virgines eorum non sunt lamentatæ]]: for each man was so anxious for his own escape that he had no leisure to mourn for others.

paras.t: Sacerdotes eorum, videlicet filii Heli, Ophni et Phinees, in gladio Philistinorum ceciderunt et mortui sunt; et viduæ eorum non plorabantur, propter causam de virginibus assignatam. Nam et uxor Phinees, audito rumore de morte viri sui, mox incurvavit se, et in ipso partu defuncta est, nec potuit propter perturbationem defleri.
paras.en: [[77:64|Their priests|Sacerdotes eorum]], namely the sons of Heli, Ophni and Phinees, [[77:64|fell by the sword|in gladio Philistinorum ceciderunt]] of the Philistines and died; [[77:64|and their widows did not mourn|et viduæ eorum non plorabantur]] [Denis takes *non plorabantur* as "were not wept for"], for the reason given about the maidens. For the wife of Phinees too, on hearing the news of her husband's death, at once bowed herself and died in the very act of childbirth, and because of the confusion she could not be mourned.

paras.t: Deinde ponitur reconciliatio Dei circa populum suum, atque indignatio ejus contra eorum adversarios. Et excitatus est tanquam dormiens Dominus, tanquam potens crapulatus a vino. Quemadmodum homo dormiens et vino inebriatus, propria fortitudine non utitur, nec pro suis præliatur; excitatus autem a somno, et ad sobrietatem reversus, virtutem suam ostendit, et fortiter pugnat, hostesque prosternit: sic Deus omnipotens quamdiu populo suo irascebatur, nec eum tuebatur, erat quasi dormiens, et crapulatus seu inebriatus a vino, quasi non attendens afflictionem populi sui, et captivitatem arcæ testamenti; dum vero Philistæos hos cœpit per Samuelem, Saul ac David dejicere, occidere et vastare, videbatur quasi a somno suscitari, atque ab ebrietate ad usum rationis reverti.
paras.en: Next is set down God's reconciliation with his people, and his indignation against their adversaries. [[77:65|And the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep, and like a mighty man that hath been surfeited with wine|Et excitatus est tanquam dormiens Dominus, tanquam potens crapulatus a vino]]. As a man asleep and drunk with wine does not use his strength nor fight for his own, but when roused from sleep and come back to sobriety shows his strength, fights bravely and lays his enemies low: so almighty God, as long as he was angry with his people and did not defend them, was as one asleep, and surfeited or drunk with wine, as though not heeding the affliction of his people and the captivity of the ark of the covenant; but when he began through Samuel, Saul and David to cast down, slay and lay waste these Philistines, he seemed as it were roused from sleep and brought back from drunkenness to the use of reason.

paras.t: Et percussit inimicos suos Philistæos in posteriora, id est in secretioribus natium partibus, ubi mures rodebant prominentes extales eorum, et computruerunt; opprobrium sempiternum dedit illis: quia in præsenti vita nulla oblivione delebitur memoria tantæ confusionis ipsorum, in inferno quoque sine fine culpa eorum torquebitur.
paras.en: [[77:66|And he smote his enemies|Et percussit inimicos suos]], the Philistines, [[77:66|on the hinder parts|in posteriora]], that is, in the more secret parts of the buttocks, where mice gnawed their protruding fundaments [*extales*, the end of the bowel], and they rotted[[1 Kings 5:6||]][[1 Kings 5:9||]]; [[77:66|he put them to an everlasting reproach|opprobrium sempiternum dedit illis]]: for in the present life the memory of their so great confusion will be blotted out by no forgetting, and in hell too their guilt will be tormented without end.

paras.t: Deinde manifestatur, quod sola tribus Juda erat ad regiam dignitatem electa. Et repulit Deus tabernaculum, id est familiam, Joseph; vel, Tabernaculum Joseph, id est locum et urbem Silo: quæ dicitur tabernaculum Joseph, quoniam erat in sorte Ephraim filii Joseph, eratque in Silo posita arca in tabernaculo Josue Ephraætæi: quæ primo Regum plenius recitantur. Et tribum Ephraim non elegit ad regnandum. Nam quamvis Deus contulit Jeroboam filio Nabat de tribu Ephraim decem tribus Israel, non tamen electus erat ad perseverandum in regno per suam posteritatem, sicut nec Saul de progenie Benjamin; sed uterque assumptus fuit ad tempus.
paras.en: Next it is made plain that the tribe of Juda alone was chosen for the royal dignity. [[77:67|And he rejected the tabernacle|Et repulit Deus tabernaculum]], that is, the family, [[77:67|of Joseph|Joseph]]; or, [[77:67|the tabernacle of Joseph|Tabernaculum Joseph]], that is, the place and city of Silo, which is called the tabernacle of Joseph because it was in the lot of Ephraim the son of Joseph, and the ark was placed in Silo in the tabernacle of Josue the *Ephraætæus* [that is, the Ephraimite]: which things are related more fully in the first book of Kings. [[77:67|And chose not the tribe of Ephraim|Et tribum Ephraim non elegit]] to reign. For although God gave the ten tribes of Israel to Jeroboam the son of Nabat, of the tribe of Ephraim, yet he was not chosen to continue in the kingdom through his posterity, as neither was Saul of the stock of Benjamin; but each was taken up for a time.

paras.t: Denique ad declarandum quod tribus Juda fuit ad regnum electa, merito excludit tribum Joseph, id est Ephraim et Manassen, deinde specialiter tribum Ephraim: Primo, quoniam Joseph sanctior erat fratribus suis, eum injuste vendentibus. Secundo, quia sublimior eis, utpote dominator Ægypti. Tertio, quia primogenita ei data fuerunt, juxta illud: Ruben fuit primogenitus Israel; sed quum violasset torum patris sui, data sunt primogenita filiis Joseph, et hoc a Jacob patriarcha. Sicque progenies Joseph videbatur ad regnandum propinquior: maxime autem tribus Ephraim, quoniam sicut in Genesi dicitur, Jacob præposuit Ephraim ipsi Manassæ.
paras.en: Lastly, to declare that the tribe of Juda was chosen for the kingdom, he fittingly shuts out the tribe of Joseph, that is, Ephraim and Manasses, and then in particular the tribe of Ephraim: first, because Joseph was holier than his brothers, who unjustly sold him; second, because he was higher than they, being ruler of Egypt; third, because the birthright was given to him, according to that saying: Ruben was [[1 Par 5:1|the firstborn of Israel|primogenitus Israel]]; but [[1 Par 5:1|forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his first birthright was given to the sons of Joseph|quum violasset torum patris sui, data sunt primogenita filiis Joseph]]; and this by Jacob the patriarch. And so the offspring of Joseph seemed nearer to reigning: above all the tribe of Ephraim, since, as is said in Genesis, Jacob set Ephraim before Manasses himself[[Gen 48:20||]].

paras.t: Sed elegit tribum Juda ad sceptrum et regnum. Unde et Jacob prædixit: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est. Montem Sion quem dilexit: nam montem sic dictum Deus elegit, ut esset in eo habitatio sua: quoniam David ædificavit in eo altare, et postea Salomon templum.
paras.en: [[77:68|But he chose the tribe of Juda|Sed elegit tribum Juda]] for the sceptre and the kingdom. Hence Jacob also foretold: [[Gen 49:10|The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent|Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est]]. [[77:68|Mount Sion which he loved|Montem Sion quem dilexit]]: for God chose the mount so called, that his dwelling might be on it: since David built an altar on it[[1 Par 21:26||]], and afterwards Solomon the temple[[2 Par 3:1||]].

paras.t: Et ædificavit sicut unicornium sanctificium suum: id est, Deus ædificari fecit templum suum sanctum in monte hoc, sicut unicornium: quod dupliciter accipi potest. Primo sic: Sicut unicornium, id est Judæorum, qui unicornes per similitudinem appellantur: quoniam sicut animal quod unicornis vocatur, unum dumtaxat cornu habet in fronte, sic ipsi unius Dei cultum et fidem habebant. Ædificavit ergo sanctificium suum sicut unicornium, id est, sicut decuit ædificari templum Judæorum, unum verum Deum colentium. Secundo sic: Sicut unicornium, id est, sicut construitur habitaculum animalium quæ unicornes seu rhinocerotes dicuntur: quoniam sicut hoc animal prohibet omnia cetera bruta ab ingressu tabernaculi sui, sic Deus prohibuit alienigenas ab introitu templi. Hinc quoque Balaam comparat Deum rhinoceroti, dicendo: Deus eduxit Israelem de Ægypto, cujus fortitudo similis est rhinocerotis. In terra quam fundavit in sæcula: id est, Deus ædificari fecit templum suum in terra promissionis, quam ad cultum suum consecravit perpetuo, quantum erat in se.
paras.en: [[77:69|And he built his sanctuary as of unicorns|Et ædificavit sicut unicornium sanctificium suum]]: that is, God caused his holy temple to be built on this mount [[77:69|as of unicorns|sicut unicornium]]: which can be taken in two ways. First thus: [[77:69|as of unicorns|Sicut unicornium]], that is, of the Jews, who are called unicorns by a likeness: for as the animal called the unicorn has only one horn on its forehead, so they had the worship of, and faith in, one God. He built [[77:69|his sanctuary|sanctificium suum]], then, [[77:69|as of unicorns|sicut unicornium]], that is, as it was fitting that the temple of the Jews, who worship the one true God, should be built. Second thus: [[77:69|as of unicorns|Sicut unicornium]], that is, as the dwelling of the animals called unicorns or rhinoceroses is built: for as this animal keeps all other beasts from entering its lair, so God kept foreigners from entering the temple. Hence too Balaam compares God to the rhinoceros, saying: [[Num 23:22|God hath brought|Deus eduxit]] Israel [[Num 23:22|out of Egypt, whose strength is like to the rhinoceros|de Ægypto, cujus fortitudo similis est rhinocerotis]] [Denis reads "Israel" for "him", and takes the strength as God's]. [[77:69|In the land which he founded for ever|In terra quam fundavit in sæcula]]: that is, God caused his temple to be built in the land of promise, which he consecrated to his worship for ever, as far as lay in him.

paras.t: Et elegit David servum suum ad stabile regnum, et sustulit eum de gregibus ovium, id est, ab ovibus patris sui quas pavit, eum reduxit; de post fetantes, id est, post oves fetas seu prolem habentes, accepit eum ad gloriam regni;
paras.en: [[77:70|And he chose his servant David|Et elegit David servum suum]] for a lasting kingdom, [[77:70|and took him from the flocks of sheep|et sustulit eum de gregibus ovium]], that is, he brought him back from his father's sheep, which he fed[[1 Kings 16:11||]][[1 Kings 16:12||]]; [[77:70|from following the ewes great with young|de post fetantes]], that is, from behind the ewes that had young or offspring, [[77:70|he brought him|accepit eum]] to the glory of the kingdom;

paras.t: Pascere Jacob servum suum, et Israel hereditatem suam, id est, quatenus bene et digne regeret in spiritualibus ac temporalibus populum Hebræorum, ex Jacob, qui etiam dictus est Israel, natum.
paras.en: [[77:71|To feed Jacob his servant and Israel his inheritance|Pascere Jacob servum suum, et Israel hereditatem suam]], that is, that he might rule well and worthily, in things spiritual and temporal, the people of the Hebrews, born of Jacob, who was also called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]].

paras.t: Et pavit eos David hoc modo, in innocentia cordis sui, id est pura ac simplici intentione; et in intellectibus manuum suarum, id est in prudentia operationum suarum, deduxit eos ad debitum finem, veramque pacem.
paras.en: [[77:72|And he fed them|Et pavit eos]], David did, in this way, [[77:72|in the innocence of his heart|in innocentia cordis sui]], that is, with a pure and simple intention; and [[77:72|by the skilfulness of his hands|in intellectibus manuum suarum]] [*intellectibus*, literally "understandings"], that is, by the prudence of his doings, he [[77:72|conducted them|deduxit eos]] to their due end and true peace.

77.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI EJUSDEM SEPTUAGESIMI SEPTIMI MYSTICA.
77.title_en: Mystical exposition of the same seventy-seventh psalm.
77.note: Part of the Latin (the lower right column of p. 262, in the gloss on vv. 1–3) is missing from the transcription; marked […].

paras.t: Quemadmodum David figura exstitit Christi, sic Synagoga erat figura Ecclesiæ; et regnum ac populus David, typus fuit regni Christi et populi christiani.
paras.en: As David was a figure of Christ, so the Synagogue was a figure of the Church; and the kingdom and people of David were a type of the kingdom of Christ and of the Christian people.

paras.t: Exponendo ergo hunc psalmum de Christo et populo christiano, ipse Salvator et Dominus noster Jesus Christus primo excitat nos ad diligentissimam advertentiam dicendorum, et ait: Attendite toto studio mentis, popule meus, id est plebs christiana, meo sanguine liberata, atque a me […] atque in nomine ejus a suis discipulis facta creduntur; et cognoscimus ea per fidem certissimam. Et quoniam fides est ex auditu, secundum Apostolum, ideo subditur: et patres nostri, Evangelistæ atque Apostoli, narraverunt nobis: quia per totum mundum opera Christi prædicaverunt, et ea ad memoriam sempiternam nostramque informationem, in scriptis reliquerunt.
paras.en: Expounding this psalm, then, of Christ and the Christian people, our Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ himself first rouses us to the most diligent attention to what is to be said, and says: [[77:1|Attend|Attendite]] with all the zeal of your mind, [[77:1|O my people|popule meus]], that is, Christian folk, set free by my blood, and by me […] [text missing in the transcription] and are believed to have been done in his name by his disciples; [[77:3|and known|et cognoscimus ea]] by most certain faith. And since faith [[Rom 10:17|cometh by hearing|est ex auditu]], according to the Apostle, there follows: [[77:3|and our fathers|et patres nostri]], the Evangelists and Apostles, [[77:3|have told us|narraverunt nobis]]: for they preached the works of Christ through the whole world[[Mark 16:15||]][[Mark 16:20||]], and left them in writing for an everlasting remembrance and for our instruction.

paras.t: Non sunt occultata a filiis eorum spiritualibus, scilicet bonis Christianis, qui quoniam ex Deo sunt, verba Dei avide audiunt, in generatione altera, id est in populo christiano, priorum Christifidelium vestigia imitante. Narrantes patres nostri prædicti, laudes Domini, id est præconia Christi, contestando quod ipse sit unigenitus Filius Dei Patris, æterno Patri consubstantialis, coæternus et coæqualis, pro mundi salute veraciter incarnatus et passus, omniumque judex constitutus; et virtutes ejus, id est divinitatis suæ omnipotentiam, et suæ humanitatis potestatem, cui data est omnis potestas in cælo et in terra. Vel, Virtutes ejus, id est conversationis suæ perfectissimam sanctitatem, videlicet ejus caritatem, mansuetudinem, humilitatem, patientiam. Et mirabilia ejus quæ fecit, tres mortuos suscitando, cæcum natum illuminando, cordium secreta propalando. Non tamen omnia mirabilia Christi narraverunt, sicut scriptum est: Multa alia fecit Jesus, quæ si scribantur per singula, nec ipsum mundum arbitror posse capere eos, qui scribendi sunt, libros.
paras.en: [[77:4|They have not been hidden from their children|Non sunt occultata a filiis eorum]], their spiritual children, namely good Christians, who, since they are of God, eagerly hear the words of God[[John 8:47||]], [[77:4|in another generation|in generatione altera]], that is, in the Christian people, which follows in the footsteps of the earlier faithful of Christ. [[77:4|Declaring|Narrantes]], our fathers aforesaid, [[77:4|the praises of the Lord|laudes Domini]], that is, the glories of Christ, bearing witness that he is the only-begotten Son of God the Father, consubstantial with the eternal Father, coeternal and coequal, truly made flesh and suffering for the salvation of the world, and appointed judge of all[[Acts 10:42||]]; [[77:4|and his powers|et virtutes ejus]], that is, the omnipotence of his Godhead and the power of his manhood, to which [[Matt 28:18|All power is given|data est omnis potestas]] [[Matt 28:18|in heaven and in earth|in cælo et in terra]]. Or, his powers [virtutes, which also means 'virtues'], that is, the most perfect holiness of his life, namely his charity, meekness, humility and patience. [[77:4|and his wonders which he hath done|Et mirabilia ejus quæ fecit]]: raising three dead[[Matt 9:25||]][[Luke 7:14||]][[John 11:43||]], giving light to the man born blind[[John 9:6||]], laying bare the secrets of hearts. Yet they did not tell all the wonders of Christ, as it is written: [[John 21:25|many other things which Jesus did which, if they were written every one, the world itself. I think, would not be able to contain the books that should be written|Multa alia fecit Jesus, quæ si scribantur per singula, nec ipsum mundum arbitror posse capere eos, qui scribendi sunt, libros]].

paras.t: Et suscitavit Christus testimonium, id est novum Testamentum, et ea quæ credenda sunt, in Jacob, id est in populo christifideli, contra vitia colluctante, et eadem supplantante; et legem vitæ et gratiæ, posuit in Israel, id est in Ecclesia sancta catholica, Deum spiritualiter contemplante.
paras.en: [[77:5|And he set up|Et suscitavit]] (Christ, that is) [[77:5|a testimony|testimonium]], that is, the New Testament and the things that are to be believed, [[77:5|in Jacob|in Jacob]], that is, in the faithful Christian people, which wrestles against vices and supplants them [Jacob means 'supplanter']; [[77:5|and made a law|et legem]] of life and grace [[77:5|in Israel|posuit in Israel]], that is, in the holy Catholic Church, which beholds God spiritually [Israel is taken to mean 'a man seeing God'].

paras.t: Quanta mandavit patribus nostris, nota facere ea filiis suis, id est, valde multa præcepit Christus suis Apostolis, aliisque nonnullis discipulis, quatenus manifestarent ea his quos ipsi in Christo spiritualiter gignerent: sicut Apostolus ait ad Galatas, Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio donec formetur Christus in vobis; ut cognoscat generatio altera, id est omnes posteri. Filii qui nascentur, id est spiritualiter regenerabuntur ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, exsurgent a somno peccati ad vigilantiam custodiæ cordis, et a terrenis ad amorem cœlestium, et narrabunt filiis suis veraciter christianis, ut sciant et impleant divina præcepta. Ad hanc annuntiationem hortatur nos sanctus Apostolus: Implemini (inquiens) Spiritu Sancto, loquentes vobismetipsis in psalmis et hymnis et canticis spiritualibus. Et rursus: Patres, ait, nolite ad iracundiam provocare filios vestros, sed educate illos in disciplina et correptione Domini.
paras.en: [[77:5|How great things he commanded our fathers, that they should make the same known to their children|Quanta mandavit patribus nostris, nota facere ea filiis suis]]: that is, Christ commanded very many things to his Apostles and to some other disciples, that they should make them manifest to those whom they themselves would beget spiritually in Christ: as the Apostle says to the Galatians, [[Gal 4:19|My little children, of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you|Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio donec formetur Christus in vobis]]; [[77:6|That another generation might know them|ut cognoscat generatio altera]], that is, all who come after. [[77:6|The children that should be born|Filii qui nascentur]], that is, who shall be spiritually born again [[John 3:5|of water and the Holy Ghost|ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto]], [[77:6|and should rise up|exsurgent]] from the sleep of sin to watchful keeping of the heart, and from earthly things to the love of heavenly things, [[77:6|and declare them to their children|et narrabunt filiis suis]], to their truly Christian children, that they may know and fulfil the divine precepts. To this declaring the holy Apostle exhorts us, saying: [[Eph 5:18|be ye filled with the Holy Spirit|Implemini (inquiens) Spiritu Sancto]], [[Eph 5:19|Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual canticles|loquentes vobismetipsis in psalmis et hymnis et canticis spiritualibus]]. And again: [[Eph 6:4|fathers|Patres]], he says, [[Eph 6:4|provoke not your children to anger: but bring them up in the discipline and correction of the Lord|nolite ad iracundiam provocare filios vestros, sed educate illos in disciplina et correptione Domini]].

paras.t: Ut ponant in Deo spem suam, id est, per meritum Christi salvari confidant, ne (quod absit) ignorantes Dei justitiam, et suam quærentes statuere, justitiæ Dei non sint subjecti; et non obliviscantur operum Dei, sed opera Christi incessabiliter recolant, quoniam omnis ejus actio, nostra est instructio. Unde monet Apostolus: Recogitate eum qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversus semetipsum contradictionem. Et Petrus: Christus passus est pro nobis, vobis relinquens exemplum, ut sequamini vestigia ejus. Qui enim opera Christi cordialiter meminit, totius perfectionis documenta invenit, nec faciliter cadere valet aut perire. Et mandata ejus exquirant. Hoc est quod Christus Apostolis dixit: Euntes docete omnes gentes, docentes eos servare quæcumque mandavi vobis. Sine observatione enim mandatorum, nemo potest salvari. Propter quod ait Joannes: Qui se dicit nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est.
paras.en: [[77:7|That they may put their hope in God|Ut ponant in Deo spem suam]]: that is, that they may trust to be saved through the merit of Christ; lest (which God forbid) [[Rom 10:3|not knowing the justice of God and seeking to establish their own|ignorantes Dei justitiam, et suam quærentes statuere]], they should not be subject [[Rom 10:3|to the justice of God|justitiæ Dei]]; [[77:7|and may not forget the works of God|et non obliviscantur operum Dei]], but may recall the works of Christ unceasingly, since his every action is our instruction. Hence the Apostle warns: [[Heb 12:3|think diligently upon him that endured such opposition from sinners against himself|Recogitate eum qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversus semetipsum contradictionem]]. And Peter: [[1 Pet 2:21|Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example that you should follow his steps|Christus passus est pro nobis, vobis relinquens exemplum, ut sequamini vestigia ejus]]. For whoever keeps the works of Christ in his heart finds in them the lessons of all perfection, and cannot easily fall or perish. [[77:7|and may seek his commandments|Et mandata ejus exquirant]]. This is what Christ said to the Apostles: [[Matt 28:19|Going therefore, teach ye all nations|Euntes docete omnes gentes]], [[Matt 28:20|Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you|docentes eos servare quæcumque mandavi vobis]]. For without the keeping of the commandments no one can be saved. Wherefore John says: [[1 John 2:4|He who saith that he knoweth him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar|Qui se dicit nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est]].

paras.t: Ne fiant sicut patres eorum carnales. Filii Ephrem, id est mali et reprobi Christiani, qui multi sunt, et electis ad exercitium apponuntur: Ephraim enim fructificatio interpretatur; intendentes et mittentes arcum oris sui, id est pulchra loquentes et plurima promittentes, sed turpiter operantes et promissa non adimplentes; conversi sunt ad se ipsos et vitia sua, in die belli, id est tempore adversitatis, eis a mundo, carne, dæmonibusve inflictæ. Nam, sicut ait Salvator, Hi radicem non habent, quia ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis recedunt. Contigit quippe eis illud veri proverbii, quod Petrus commemorat, scilicet: Canis reversus ad suum vomitum, et sus lota in volutabro luti. Propter quod Christus iterum loquitur: Quid dicitis mihi, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico?
paras.en: [[77:8|That they may not become like their fathers|Ne fiant sicut patres eorum]] according to the flesh. [[77:9|The sons of Ephraim|Filii Ephrem]]: that is, wicked and reprobate Christians, who are many, and are set beside the elect for their exercise; for Ephraim is interpreted 'fruitfulness'. [[77:9|who bend and shoot with the bow|intendentes et mittentes arcum]] of their mouth, that is, speaking fair words and promising a great deal, but acting basely and not fulfilling their promises; [[77:9|they have turned back|conversi sunt]] to themselves and their vices [[77:9|in the day of battle|in die belli]], that is, in the time of adversity brought on them by the world, the flesh or the devils. For, as the Saviour says, [[Luke 8:13|these have no roots: for they believe for a while and in time of temptation they fall away|Hi radicem non habent, quia ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis recedunt]][[Matt 13:21||]]. For [[2 Pet 2:22|that of the true proverb has happened to them|Contigit quippe eis illud veri proverbii]] which Peter recalls, namely: [[2 Pet 2:22|The dog is returned to his vomit; and: The sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire|Canis reversus ad suum vomitum, et sus lota in volutabro luti]]. Wherefore Christ says again: [[Luke 6:46|why call you me, Lord, Lord; and do not the things which I say?|Quid dicitis mihi, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico?]]

paras.t: Non custodierunt testamentum Dei, dicentes se nosse Deum, et factis negantes; et in lege ejus evangelica noluerunt ambulare: et ita peccabant ex certa malitia, atque ex proposito, non ex infirmitate, aut ex ignorantia: quod quam damnabile sit, Petrus docet: Melius erat illis non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post agnitionem retrorsum converti. Servus namque sciens voluntatem domini sui, et non faciens, vapulabit multis.
paras.en: [[77:10|They kept not the covenant of God|Non custodierunt testamentum Dei]], saying that they know God, and denying him in their deeds[[Tit 1:16||]]; [[77:10|and in his law|et in lege ejus]], the law of the Gospel, [[77:10|they would not walk|noluerunt ambulare]]: and so they sinned out of certain malice and of set purpose, not out of weakness or ignorance [that is, they sinned knowingly and willingly, the gravest kind of sin]. How damnable that is, Peter teaches: [[2 Pet 2:21|it had been better for them not to have known the way of justice than, after they have known it, to turn back|Melius erat illis non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post agnitionem retrorsum converti]]. For the servant [[Luke 12:47|who knew the will of his lord|sciens voluntatem domini sui]], and does it not, [[Luke 12:47|shall be beaten with many stripes|vapulabit multis]].

paras.t: Et obliti sunt benefactorum ejus: id est, mali Christiani oblivioni dederunt beneficia Christi, qui pro eis incarnatus est, conversatus in mundo, suspensus in ligno: qui in tantum eos dilexit, quod animam suam posuit pro eis, et corpus suum ac sanguinem in saluberrimum reliquit viaticum, suæque passionis amarissimæ, ac dilectionis eximiæ memoriale perpetuum. Hoc modo obliviscitur beneficia Christi, quicumque eum non diligit, qui mundi vanitatibus vacat, qui carnis suæ concupiscentiis servit. Qui autem Christo compatitur, qui ejus passionibus, propriam crucem bajulando, quotidie assimilatur, et in labore pœnitentiæ quotidie mortificatur, hic vere memor est beneficiorum Domini sui. Non enim ad veram ac gratam memoriam sufficit nuda et superficialis reminiscentia; sed necessaria est affectuosa quædam recordatio, et operis exhibitio.
paras.en: [[77:11|And they forgot his benefits|Et obliti sunt benefactorum ejus]]: that is, wicked Christians have given over to forgetfulness the benefits of Christ, who for them was made flesh, conversed in the world[[Bar 3:38||]], and hung upon the wood; who loved them so much that he laid down his life for them[[John 10:15||]], and left them his body and blood as a most wholesome viaticum [that is, food for the journey], and an everlasting memorial of his most bitter passion and his surpassing love. In this way whoever does not love him forgets the benefits of Christ: whoever gives himself to the vanities of the world, whoever serves the lusts of his flesh. But he who suffers with Christ, who is daily made like to his sufferings by carrying his own cross, and is daily mortified in the labour of penance, he truly remembers the benefits of his Lord. For a bare and superficial recollection is not enough for a true and grateful remembrance; there must be a remembrance full of affection, and the showing of it in deeds.

paras.t: Obliti quoque sunt et mirabilium ejus, scilicet Christi, quæ ostendit eis per prædicationem famulorum suorum et instructionem sacræ Scripturæ, vel per inspirationem et illuminationem Spiritus Sancti. Mirabilia Christi fuerunt, quod pertransivit benefaciens, sanans omnem languorem et omnem infirmitatem in populo, secundum quod Evangelistæ testantur, omnesque oppressos a diabolo, ut adstruit Petrus. Quos autem sanavit in corpore, justificavit in anima. Horum mirabilium obliviscitur, qui hoc exemplo ad Christum misericordissimum, prudentissimum, ac potentissimum medicum non festinat, qui animæ suæ vulnera ei non detegit, qui fontem omnis salutis et gratiæ, pro oleo pietatis et rivulis gratiarum non deprecatur, præsertim quum ipse proclamet: Venite ad me, omnes, qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos; et alibi, Eum qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras.
paras.en: They forgot also [[77:11|and his wonders|et mirabilium ejus]], that is, Christ's, [[77:11|that he had shewn them|quæ ostendit eis]] through the preaching of his servants and the teaching of Holy Scripture, or through the inspiration and enlightening of the Holy Ghost. The wonders of Christ were that he [[Acts 10:38|went about doing good|pertransivit benefaciens]], [[Matt 4:23|healing all manner of sickness and every infirmity, among the people|sanans omnem languorem et omnem infirmitatem in populo]], as the Evangelists testify, and all [[Acts 10:38|that were oppressed by the devil|oppressos a diabolo]], as Peter affirms. And those whom he healed in body he justified in soul. He forgets these wonders who, taught by this example, does not hasten to Christ, the most merciful, most wise and most mighty physician; who does not uncover to him the wounds of his soul; who does not beg the fountain of all salvation and grace for the oil of mercy and the streams of graces; above all since he himself proclaims: [[Matt 11:28|Come to me all you that labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you|Venite ad me, omnes, qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos]]; and elsewhere: [[John 6:37|him that cometh to me, I will not cast out|Eum qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras]].

paras.t: Coram patribus eorum, id est in conspectu Apostolorum et discipulorum suorum, qui patres sunt omnium Christianorum, fecit Christus mirabilia in terra Ægypti, id est in mundo isto. Ægyptus enim interpretatur caligo seu tribulatio: sicque per eam accipitur sæculum istud nequam, et mundus qui totus in maligno positus est, in quo electi multipliciter tribulantur. In campo Taneos, id est in planitie humilis mandati: quia et Christus ait, Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio. Non enim per jactantiam aliquid fecit, quemadmodum ipsemet rursus dicit: Claritatem ab hominibus non accipio. Christus etiam nobis præceptum humilitatis proposuit, dicens, Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde. Quia etenim Tanis humile mandatum interpretatur, recte per campum Taneos humilis mandati planities designatur. Debemus quoque præcipue humilitatem a Christo discere et sectari.
paras.en: [[77:12|in the sight of their fathers|Coram patribus eorum]], that is, in the sight of his Apostles and disciples, who are the fathers of all Christians, [[77:12|Wonderful things did he do|fecit Christus mirabilia]] (Christ, that is) [[77:12|in the land of Egypt|in terra Ægypti]], that is, in this world. For Egypt is interpreted 'darkness' or 'tribulation': and so by it is understood this wicked age, and the world which wholly [[1 John 5:19|is seated in wickedness|in maligno positus est]] [the margin gives Joann. v, 19; the words are 1 John 5:19], in which the elect are afflicted in many ways. [[77:12|in the field of Tanis|In campo Taneos]], that is, in the plain of the humble commandment: for Christ too says, [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]. For he did nothing out of boasting, as he himself says again: [[John 5:41|I receive not glory from men|Claritatem ab hominibus non accipio]]. Christ also set before us the precept of humility, saying: [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]. For since Tanis is interpreted 'humble commandment', the field of Tanis rightly signifies the plain of the humble commandment. And above all we ought to learn humility from Christ and to follow after it.

paras.t: Interrupit mare et perduxit eos. Per mare (ut sæpius dictum est) intelligi potest gentilitas, vitiorum amaritudine qualificata. Unde conversis gentilibus Paulus clamat: Omnis amaritudo, ira, et indignatio, et clamor tollatur a vobis. Potest quoque per mare designari tribulationum multitudo, sicut in Threnis ait Jeremias: Magna est velut mare contritio tua. Utroque autem modo interrupit Christus mare et perduxit patres nostros sanctos Apostolos et eorum imitatores. Nam per medium mare gentilitatis ipsos perduxit, convertendo paganos ad fidem, gentilitatemque rupit, destruendo ritum gentilium, conterendo etiam peccata et idola paganorum. Perduxit insuper eos per varias tribulationes, et de omnibus illis eripuit eos, quemadmodum Paulus testatur: Benedictus Deus, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra. Et statuit aquas quasi in utre: quia gentiles ad fidem conversos, in divino timore stabilivit, et a fluxu libidinis, sub jugo divinorum præceptorum compescuit; tribulationes etiam fecit cessare, et quasi in utre quiescere.
paras.en: [[77:13|He divided the sea and brought them through|Interrupit mare et perduxit eos]] [interrupit, literally 'broke through': Denis plays on this below with rupit, 'broke']. By the sea (as has often been said) may be understood the Gentile world, marked by the bitterness of vices. Hence Paul cries to the converted Gentiles: [[Eph 4:31|Let all bitterness and anger and indignation and clamour|Omnis amaritudo, ira, et indignatio, et clamor]] [[Eph 4:31|be put away from you|tollatur a vobis]]. By the sea may also be signified the multitude of tribulations, as Jeremias says in the Lamentations: [[Lam 2:13|great as the sea is thy destruction|Magna est velut mare contritio tua]]. In both ways Christ divided the sea and brought through our fathers, the holy Apostles and those who followed them. For he brought them through the midst of the sea of the Gentile world by converting the pagans to the faith; and he broke the Gentile world, destroying the rites of the Gentiles and crushing also the sins and idols of the pagans. He brought them, moreover, through various tribulations, and delivered them from them all, as Paul testifies: [[2 Cor 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], [[2 Cor 1:4|Who comforteth us in all our tribulation|qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra]]. [[77:13|and he made the waters to stand as in a vessel|Et statuit aquas quasi in utre]] [in utre, literally 'in a wineskin']: for he established the Gentiles converted to the faith in the fear of God, and restrained them from the flood of lust under the yoke of the divine precepts; he also made tribulations cease and rest as in a wineskin.

paras.t: Et deduxit eos, videlicet omnes Christifideles, qui voluerunt pie vivere in Christo, et idcirco persecutionem perpessi sunt, in nube diei, id est in refrigerio consolationis divinæ, et sub rore ac stillicidiis gratiæ suæ; et tota nocte, id est in omni adversitate et impugnatione, in illuminatione ignis, id est in splendore sapientiæ Spiritus Sancti, et in radio interioris illuminationis Christi, qui afflictis maxime prope est.
paras.en: [[77:14|And he conducted them|Et deduxit eos]], namely all the faithful of Christ who [[2 Tim 3:12|will live godly in Christ|pie vivere in Christo]], and therefore have suffered persecution, [[77:14|with a cloud by day|in nube diei]], that is, in the refreshment of divine consolation, and under the dew and droppings of his grace; [[77:14|and all the night|et tota nocte]], that is, in every adversity and assault, [[77:14|with a light of fire|in illuminatione ignis]], that is, in the splendour of the wisdom of the Holy Ghost, and in the ray of the inward enlightening of Christ, who is nearest of all to the afflicted.

paras.t: Interrupit Deus Pater, id est, perforari et rumpi permisit, petram, id est Christum, seu latus ipsius, in eremo hujus mundi, seu in cruce, omni humano solatio destituta. Unde Christus clamavit: Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me? In hujus petræ vulneribus, tuti efficimur ab omni invasione hostili, imo et ab iracundia Dei. Propterea dicitur: Ingredere in petram, abscondere in fossa humo a facie timoris Domini. Et adaquavit eos velut in abysso multa: id est, Deus merito sanguinis Christi, Christianos abundanter potavit aqua gratiæ salutaris et donis Spiritus Sancti, et ideo Christus ait: Si quis sitit, veniat ad me, et bibat. Qui credit in me, sicut dicit Scriptura, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ.
paras.en: [[77:15|He struck|Interrupit]] (God the Father, that is: he allowed to be pierced and broken) [[77:15|the rock|petram]], that is, Christ[[1 Cor 10:4||]], or his side[[John 19:34||]], [[77:15|in the wilderness|in eremo]] of this world, or on the cross, bereft of all human comfort. Hence Christ cried: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?]] In the wounds of this rock we are made safe from every attack of the enemy, nay, even from the wrath of God. Therefore it is said: [[Is 2:10|Enter thou into the rock, and hide thee in the pit from the face of the fear of the Lord|Ingredere in petram, abscondere in fossa humo a facie timoris Domini]]. [[77:15|and gave them to drink, as out of the great deep|Et adaquavit eos velut in abysso multa]]: that is, God, by the merit of Christ's blood, gave the Christians abundant drink of the water of saving grace and of the gifts of the Holy Ghost; and therefore Christ says: [[John 7:37|If any man thirst, let him come to me and drink|Si quis sitit, veniat ad me, et bibat]]. [[John 7:38|He that believeth in me, as the scripture saith: Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water|Qui credit in me, sicut dicit Scriptura, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ]].

paras.t: Et eduxit aquam de petra: quia de latere Jesu lancea perforato, exivit sanguis et aqua; et deduxit tanquam flumina aquas: id est, Deus Trinitas de Christo capite nostro deduxit in membra ipsius (id est in nos) copiosa munera gratiarum: quia, ut Joannes ait, De plenitudine ejus accepimus omnes, gratiam pro gratia. Apostolus quoque ad Titum: Secundum suam, inquit, misericordiam salvos nos fecit, per lavacrum regenerationis et renovationis Spiritus Sancti, quem effudit in nos abunde per Jesum Christum. De hac aqua Dominus ait per Ezechielem: Effundam super vos aquam mundam, et mundabimini ab omnibus inquinamentis vestris.
paras.en: [[77:16|He brought forth water out of the rock|Et eduxit aquam de petra]]: for from the side of Jesus, pierced with the lance, [[John 19:34|there came out blood and water|exivit sanguis et aqua]] [the margin gives Judic. xvii, 34, evidently a misprint for Joann. xix, 34]; [[77:16|and made streams run down as rivers|et deduxit tanquam flumina aquas]]: that is, God the Trinity drew down from Christ our head into his members (that is, into us) plentiful gifts of graces: for, as John says, [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received: and grace for grace|De plenitudine ejus accepimus omnes, gratiam pro gratia]]. The Apostle also, to Titus: [[Tit 3:5|according to his mercy|Secundum suam]], he says, [[Tit 3:5|he saved us, by the laver of regeneration and renovation of the Holy Ghost|misericordiam salvos nos fecit, per lavacrum regenerationis et renovationis Spiritus Sancti]], [[Tit 3:6|Whom he hath poured forth upon us abundantly, through Jesus Christ|quem effudit in nos abunde per Jesum Christum]]. Of this water the Lord says by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:25|I will pour upon you clean water, and you shall be cleansed from all your filthiness|Effundam super vos aquam mundam, et mundabimini ab omnibus inquinamentis vestris]].

paras.t: Et apposuerunt adhuc peccare ei. Sic (proh dolor!) multi Christiani post gratiam Baptismi et cetera beneficia Christi, pro gratiarum actione multiplicant offensiones. In iram excitaverunt Excelsum, id est Christum Dei virtutem, in inaquoso, id est in corde suo arenti et infructuoso, omni aqua gratiæ cælestis privato. Et tentaverunt Deum in cordibus suis, ut peterent escas animabus suis. Hoc excessive sollicitos respicit, qui promissionibus Christi increduli sunt, quibus ait: Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis; rursusque: Nolite solliciti esse, dicentes, Quid manducabimus, aut quid bibemus, aut quo operiemur? Hæc enim omnia gentes inquirunt. Scit enim Pater vester quia his omnibus indigetis. Nimis sollicitantur pro temporalibus congregandis, non acquiescentes Paulo qui ait, Habentes alimenta et quibus tegamur, his contenti simus: qui etiam avaritiam nominat idolorum servitutem.
paras.en: [[77:17|And they added yet more sin against him|Et apposuerunt adhuc peccare ei]]. So (alas!) many Christians, after the grace of Baptism and the other benefits of Christ, multiply offences in place of thanksgiving. [[77:17|they provoked the most High to wrath|In iram excitaverunt Excelsum]], that is, Christ, the power of God, [[77:17|in the place without water|in inaquoso]], that is, in their heart, dry and unfruitful, deprived of all the water of heavenly grace. [[77:18|And they tempted God in their hearts, by asking meat for their desires.|Et tentaverunt Deum in cordibus suis, ut peterent escas animabus suis]] [escas animabus suis, literally 'food for their souls']. This regards those who are anxious beyond measure, who do not believe the promises of Christ, to whom he says: [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis]]; and again: [[Matt 6:31|Be not solicitous therefore, saying: What shall we eat: or what shall we drink, or wherewith shall we be clothed?|Nolite solliciti esse, dicentes, Quid manducabimus, aut quid bibemus, aut quo operiemur?]] [[Matt 6:32|For after all these things do the heathens seek. For your Father knoweth that you have need of all these things|Hæc enim omnia gentes inquirunt. Scit enim Pater vester quia his omnibus indigetis]]. They are too anxious about gathering temporal things, not heeding Paul, who says: [[1 Tim 6:8|having food and wherewith to be covered, with these we are content|Habentes alimenta et quibus tegamur, his contenti simus]]; who also calls covetousness [[Col 3:5|the service of idols|idolorum servitutem]].

paras.t: Ideo indignatus est Dominus Jesus ista peccata Christianorum, et distulit, non statim ulciscendo se, sed longanimiter exspectando, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico scribitur: Altissimus est patiens redditor. Et Petrus: Patienter, inquit, agit Dominus propter nos, nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti. Maxime autem appareret patientia Dei tempore novæ legis; nam sicut philosophis innotuit Dei majestas, Judæis autem justitia, sic Christianis innotescit misericordia Creatoris. Propter quod Apostolus asserit: Apparuit benignitas et humanitas Salvatoris nostri Dei. Et ignis iræ Christi, scilicet ultio ejus, accensus est in Jacob, id est in Ecclesia christiana: quia non redeuntes nec pœnitentes Christus tanto horribilius punit, quanto diutius eos exspectavit; et ira Dei ascendit in Israel: quia Ecclesia Christi propter sua peccata variis modis sæpe oppressa est. Nunc quoque opprimitur a Sarracenis, hæreticis et tyrannis, quemadmodum olim Synagoga a Chananæis, Philistæis, Ammonitis et Moabitis.
paras.en: [[77:21|Therefore the Lord|Ideo indignatus est Dominus]] Jesus was indignant at these sins of the Christians [Denis reads indignatus est, 'was indignant', where the Vulgate has audivit, 'heard'], [[77:21|and was angry|et distulit]] [distulit, literally 'and he put off': so Denis takes it here, where the Douay-Rheims has 'was angry'], not avenging himself at once, but waiting with long-suffering, as is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 5:4|the most High is a patient rewarder|Altissimus est patiens redditor]] [the margin gives Eccli. xxxv, 23; the words are Ecclus 5:4]. And Peter: [[2 Pet 3:9|patiently|Patienter]], he says, does the Lord deal for our sake, [[2 Pet 3:9|not willing that any should perish, but that all should return to penance|nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti]]. And the patience of God appeared most of all in the time of the new law; for as the majesty of God became known to the philosophers, and his justice to the Jews, so to the Christians the mercy of the Creator becomes known. Wherefore the Apostle declares: [[Tit 3:4|the goodness and kindness of God our Saviour appeared|Apparuit benignitas et humanitas Salvatoris nostri Dei]]. [[77:21|and a fire|Et ignis]] of the wrath of Christ, namely his vengeance, [[77:21|was kindled against Jacob|accensus est in Jacob]], that is, in the Christian Church: for those who do not return or repent Christ punishes the more terribly, the longer he has waited for them; [[77:21|and wrath came up against Israel|et ira Dei ascendit in Israel]]: for the Church of Christ, because of her sins, has often been oppressed in various ways. Now too she is oppressed by Saracens, heretics and tyrants, as of old the Synagogue was by the Chanaanites, Philistines, Ammonites and Moabites.

paras.t: Quia non crediderunt in Deum, id est in Deum, ejus præceptis obtemperando; nec speraverunt in salutari ejus, id est in Christum; sed potius in vanitatibus suis, aut propriis meritis seu viribus sunt confisi.
paras.en: [[77:22|Because they believed not in God|Quia non crediderunt in Deum]], that is, into God [credere in Deum, to believe in God with a faith that goes out to him], by obeying his precepts; [[77:22|and trusted not in his salvation|nec speraverunt in salutari ejus]] [salutare, 'his saving one'], that is, in Christ; but rather they trusted in their own vanities, or in their own merits or strength.

paras.t: Et mandavit nubibus desuper. Per nubes intelligi possunt angeli sancti, secundum Dionysium; itemque Apostoli, de quibus Isaias interrogat: Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant? Quoniam ergo ministerio archangeli Gabrielis nuntiata est Virgini gloriosæ incarnatio Christi, ministerio quoque angeli nuntiata est pastoribus nativitas Christi jam facta, ministerio quoque angelorum Prophetæ illuminati sunt ad vaticinandum de Christi tunc futura incarnatione; idcirco nunc dicitur Deus mandasse nubibus cœli desuper, id est angelis sanctis, videlicet ut exhiberent obsequium circa Christi descensum in mundum. Porro Apostoli prædicaverunt per mundum incarnationem Christi impletam, mandavitque Apostolis ut circa Christi clarificationem in cordibus hominum famulatum impenderent, juxta illud Petri: Præcepit nobis testificari quia ipse est qui constitutus est a Deo judex vivorum et mortuorum. Utrisque ergo nubibus Deus mandavit. Et januas cœli, id est ora Apostolorum, aperuit ad prædicandum Christi Evangelium. Nam et Christus eis prædixit: Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam. Vel, Januas cœli empyrei aperuit, quantum ad hoc quod ex eo ad nos angelos misit.
paras.en: [[77:23|And he had commanded the clouds from above|Et mandavit nubibus desuper]]. By the clouds may be understood the holy angels, according to Dionysius; and likewise the Apostles, of whom Isaias asks: [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant]]? [the margin gives Is. ix, 8; the words are Is 60:8]. Since, then, the incarnation of Christ was announced to the glorious Virgin by the ministry of the archangel Gabriel[[Luke 1:31||]], and the birth of Christ, now accomplished, was announced to the shepherds by the ministry of an angel[[Luke 2:10||]], and by the ministry of angels the Prophets were enlightened to foretell the incarnation of Christ, then still to come: therefore God is now said to have commanded the clouds of heaven from above, that is, the holy angels, namely that they should render their service about Christ's coming down into the world. Further, the Apostles preached through the world the incarnation of Christ fulfilled, and he commanded the Apostles to give their service to the glorifying of Christ in the hearts of men, according to that saying of Peter: [[Acts 10:42|he commanded us|Præcepit nobis]] [[Acts 10:42|to testify that it is he who was appointed by God to be judge of the living and of the dead|testificari quia ipse est qui constitutus est a Deo judex vivorum et mortuorum]]. God therefore commanded both kinds of clouds. [[77:23|the doors of heaven|Et januas cœli]], that is, the mouths of the Apostles, he [[77:23|had opened|aperuit]] for the preaching of the Gospel of Christ. For Christ also foretold to them: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam]]. Or: he opened the doors of the empyrean heaven [that is, the highest heaven, the dwelling of the blessed], inasmuch as he sent angels to us from it.

paras.t: Et ita pluit illis manna ad manducandum, id est, per hunc modum misit Christum in mundum, et annuntiavit eum gentibus, ut in eum crederent, ejusque corpus in Sacramento comederent. Unde Isaias habet: Rorate, cœli, desuper, et nubes pluant Justum. Christus enim est verum manna, cujus figura erat manna illud patribus datum. Et panem cœli dedit eis, id est, corpus Christi contulit Christianis in salutiferum animæ cibum, secundum quod Christus fatetur: Non Moyses dedit vobis panem de cœlo, sed Pater meus dat vobis panem de cœlo verum; et iterum, Ego sum panis vivus, qui de cœlo descendi.
paras.en: [[77:24|And had rained down manna upon them to eat|Et ita pluit illis manna ad manducandum]]: that is, in this way he sent Christ into the world, and announced him to the nations, that they might believe in him and eat his body in the Sacrament. Hence Isaias has: [[Is 45:8|Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the just|Rorate, cœli, desuper, et nubes pluant Justum]]. For Christ is the true manna, of which the manna given to the fathers was a figure[[Ex 16:14||]]. [[77:24|and had given them the bread of heaven|Et panem cœli dedit eis]]: that is, he bestowed the body of Christ on the Christians as the saving food of the soul, as Christ declares: [[John 6:32|Moses gave you not bread from heaven, but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven|Non Moyses dedit vobis panem de cœlo, sed Pater meus dat vobis panem de cœlo verum]]; and again: [[John 6:51|I am the living bread which came down from heaven|Ego sum panis vivus, qui de cœlo descendi]].

paras.t: Panem angelorum, id est Christum sub formis Sacramenti altaris, manducavit homo quilibet Christianus electus, sacramentaliter vel spiritualiter, seu modo utroque. Christus namque qui est omnium Beatorum refectio in cœlis, ipse quoque est cibus noster in terris, prout ipse testatur: Qui manducat me, et ipse vivet propter me. Estque necessarium omni credenti, hunc panem aliquo prædictorum modorum comedere, sicut ipse affirmat: Nisi manducaveritis carnem Filii hominis, et biberitis ejus sanguinem, non habebitis vitam in vobis. Cibaria misit Deus Pater eis, scilicet Christianis, in abundantia: quoniam omnes Christiani qui volunt, hoc pane cœlesti refici possunt, nec tamen eum consumere aut comminuere queunt.
paras.en: [[77:25|the bread of angels|Panem angelorum]], that is, Christ under the forms of the Sacrament of the altar, [[77:25|Man ate|manducavit homo]], that is, every elect Christian, sacramentally or spiritually, or in both ways [that is, receiving the Sacrament, or by faith and desire without receiving it, or both]. For Christ, who is the refreshment of all the Blessed in heaven, is also our food on earth, as he himself testifies: [[John 6:58|he that eateth me, the same also shall live by me|Qui manducat me, et ipse vivet propter me]]. And it is necessary for every believer to eat this bread in one of the ways named, as he himself affirms: [[John 6:54|except you eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, you shall not have life in you|Nisi manducaveritis carnem Filii hominis, et biberitis ejus sanguinem, non habebitis vitam in vobis]]. God the Father [[77:25|sent them provisions|Cibaria misit]], namely to the Christians, [[77:25|in abundance|in abundantia]]: for all Christians who will can be refreshed with this heavenly bread, and yet they cannot consume it or lessen it.

paras.t: Transtulit Austrum de cœlo: id est, prædicatores angelicæ conversationis, flatu verbi divini corda audientium perflantes, misit per mundum; et induxit Deus Trinitas in virtute sua, divina et propria, Africum, id est prædicatores decliviora dogmata prædicantes.
