Auster enim est ventus meridionalis; Africus autem est ventus occidentalis, et lateralis versus meridiem. Ideo per Austrum designantur sublimiora prædicantes, quemadmodum ait Apostolus, Sapientiam loquimur inter perfectos; per Africum vero, humiliora prædicantes, in quorum persona idem ait, Non judicavi me aliquid scire inter vos, nisi Jesum Christum, et hunc crucifixum.
paras.en: [[77:26|He removed the south wind from heaven|Transtulit Austrum de cœlo]]: that is, he sent through the world preachers of angelic life, who blow through the hearts of their hearers with the breath of the divine word; and God the Trinity, [[77:26|by his power|in virtute sua]], divine and his own, [[77:26|brought in|et induxit]] [[77:26|the southwest wind|Africum]], that is, preachers who preach lower [decliviora, literally 'sloping more downward'] teachings. For Auster is the south wind, and Africus the west wind, lying to the side towards the south. So by Auster are signified those who preach loftier things, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 2:6|we speak wisdom among the perfect|Sapientiam loquimur inter perfectos]]; and by Africus those who preach humbler things, in whose person the same Apostle says: [[1 Cor 2:2|I judged not myself to know anything among you, but Jesus Christ: and him crucified|Non judicavi me aliquid scire inter vos, nisi Jesum Christum, et hunc crucifixum]].

paras.t: Et pluit super eos, id est super omnes ad catholicam fidem conversos, sicut pulverem, id est copiosissime nimis, carnes, id est corpus Christi: quod licet sit unum et idem in omnibus hostiis consecratis, tamen propter multitudinem materiarum seu panum qui convertuntur in ipsum, dictum est Carnes; vel propter partes suas: unde Psalmista ait, Confige timore tuo carnes meas. Quod enim corpus Christi sit caro et cibus quo reficiuntur fideles, ipse de se ostendit, dicens: Caro mea vere est cibus, et sanguis meus vere est potus.
paras.en: [[77:27|And he rained upon them|Et pluit super eos]], that is, upon all converted to the Catholic faith, [[77:27|as dust|sicut pulverem]], that is, most abundantly indeed, [[77:27|flesh|carnes]], that is, the body of Christ: which, though it is one and the same in all the consecrated hosts, is yet called 'fleshes' [the Latin carnes is plural] because of the multitude of the matters, or breads, that are changed into it; or because of its parts: whence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:120|Pierce thou my flesh with thy fear|Confige timore tuo carnes meas]]. For that the body of Christ is flesh, and the food by which the faithful are refreshed, he shows of himself, saying: [[John 6:56|my flesh is meat indeed: and my blood is drink indeed|Caro mea vere est cibus, et sanguis meus vere est potus]].

paras.t: Pluit etiam Deus super Christianos et sicut arenam maris, id est in innumerabili multitudine, volatilia pennata, id est homines contemplativos, Dei amicos: de quibus infra habetur, Dinumerabo eos, et super arenam multiplicabuntur. Hos Deus pluit super Ecclesiam suam, quatenus populum Christi irrigarent et fecundarent pluvia verbi cœlestis, essentque aliorum pastores. Possunt quoque per volatilia pennata intelligi angeli sancti: quoniam Deus singulis Christianis mittit singulos angelos ad custodiam atque subsidium; imo secundum Apostolum, Omnes sunt administratorii spiritus, in ministerium missi propter eos qui hereditatem capiunt salutis. Hos autem misit Deus multo copiosius atque frequentius tempore legis Christi, quam Moysis.
paras.en: God also rained upon the Christians, [[77:27|like as the sand of the sea|et sicut arenam maris]], that is, in a numberless multitude, [[77:27|feathered fowls|volatilia pennata]], that is, contemplative men, the friends of God: of whom it is said further on: [[Ps 138:18|I will number them, and they shall be multiplied above the sand|Dinumerabo eos, et super arenam multiplicabuntur]] [the margin gives Ps. cxxxviii, 14; the words are Ps 138:18]. These God rained upon his Church, that they might water the people of Christ and make it fruitful with the rain of the heavenly word, and be shepherds of others. By the feathered fowls may also be understood the holy angels: since God sends to each Christian an angel of his own for guard and help; nay, according to the Apostle, they are [[Heb 1:14|all ministering spirits, sent to minister for them who shall receive the inheritance of salvation?|Omnes sunt administratorii spiritus, in ministerium missi propter eos qui hereditatem capiunt salutis]] And these God sent far more abundantly and more often in the time of the law of Christ than in that of Moses.

paras.t: Et ceciderunt, id est, descenderunt pastores prædicti et angeli sancti, in medio castrorum eorum, id est Ecclesiarum fidelium, circa tabernacula eorum, id est circa civitates, villas, imo et circa corpora Christianorum. Angeli namque custodiunt corpora hominum a multis læsionibus atque periculis. Unde in Actibus Apostolorum, angelus Dei primo eduxit omnes Apostolos de ergastulo carceris, deinde Petrum eripuit. Deinde legitur et in Evangelio Christus misisse discipulos suos binos et binos, in omnem civitatem et locum quo erat ipse venturus.
paras.en: [[77:28|And they fell|Et ceciderunt]], that is, the aforesaid shepherds and the holy angels came down, [[77:28|in the midst of their camp|in medio castrorum eorum]], that is, of the Churches of the faithful, [[77:28|round about their pavilions|circa tabernacula eorum]], that is, about the cities, the towns, nay even about the bodies of Christians. For the angels guard men's bodies from many hurts and dangers. Hence in the Acts of the Apostles an angel of God first led all the Apostles out of the prison[[Acts 5:19||]], and afterwards rescued Peter[[Acts 12:7||]]. We read too in the Gospel that Christ sent his disciples two and two, [[Luke 10:1|into every city and place whither he himself was to come|in omnem civitatem et locum quo erat ipse venturus]].

paras.t: Et manducaverunt electi Christiani corpus Domini sui, sicut ipse præcepit: Hoc, inquiens, facite in meam commemorationem; et saturati sunt nimis, id est, intus copiose repleti sunt gratia Spiritus Sancti, et spiritualiter impinguati, secundum quod Christus locutus est: Qui manducat meam carnem, et bibit meum sanguinem, in me manet, et ego in eo; et iterum, Qui manducat hunc panem, vivet in æternum. Et desiderium eorum attulit eis, exaudiendo preces eorum.
paras.en: [[77:29|So they did eat|Et manducaverunt]]: the chosen Christians ate the body of their Lord, as he himself commanded, saying: [[Luke 22:19|Do this|Hoc]], he says, [[Luke 22:19|for a commemoration of me|facite in meam commemorationem]]; [[77:29|and were filled exceedingly|et saturati sunt nimis]], that is, they were inwardly filled abundantly with the grace of the Holy Ghost, and spiritually fattened, according to what Christ said: [[John 6:57|He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood abideth in me: and I in him|Qui manducat meam carnem, et bibit meum sanguinem, in me manet, et ego in eo]]; and again, [[John 6:59|He that eateth this bread shall live for ever|Qui manducat hunc panem, vivet in æternum]]. [[77:29|and he gave them their desire|Et desiderium eorum attulit eis]], by hearing their prayers.

paras.t: Adhuc escæ eorum erant in ore ipsorum, non electorum, sed indigne manducantium, et ira Dei ascendit super eos: quoniam Satanas eos ingreditur, sicut et Judam proditorem, quia de eis ait Apostolus: Quicumque manducaverit panem hunc, vel biberit calicem Domini indigne, reus erit corporis et sanguinis Domini. Et occidit Deus pingues eorum: id est, carnaliter Christum sumentes, spiritualiter interfecit, subtrahendo eis caritatem et gratiam. Nam ut ait Apostolus, Qui manducat et bibit indigne, judicium sibi manducat et bibit, non dijudicans corpus Domini, id est non sentiens de illo spiritualiter, nec sumens illud reverenter atque fideliter, sed sicut alios cibos. Et electos Israel, id est, qui videbantur esse magni in Ecclesia, impedivit ab introitu regni cœlestis, propter peccatum indignæ communionis. Electi enim non semper in sacra Scriptura dicuntur prædestinati ad vitam æternam, quoniam Christus in Evangelio Apostolis ait: Nonne ego vos duodecim elegi, et unus ex vobis diabolus est? Et alibi habetur, Erat Saul vir electus: quem tamen multi Sanctorum dicunt damnatum.
paras.en: [[77:30|As yet their meat was in their mouth|Adhuc escæ eorum erant in ore ipsorum]], not of the chosen, but of those who eat unworthily, [[77:31|And the wrath of God came upon them|et ira Dei ascendit super eos]]: for Satan enters into them, as he did into Judas the traitor; since of them the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 11:27|whosoever shall eat this bread, or drink the chalice of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord|Quicumque manducaverit panem hunc, vel biberit calicem Domini indigne, reus erit corporis et sanguinis Domini]]. [[77:31|And he slew the fat ones amongst them|Et occidit Deus pingues eorum]]: that is, those who receive Christ carnally he slew spiritually, by withdrawing charity and grace from them. For, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 11:29|he that eateth and drinketh unworthily eateth and drinketh judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord|Qui manducat et bibit indigne, judicium sibi manducat et bibit, non dijudicans corpus Domini]]: that is, not perceiving it spiritually, nor receiving it with reverence and faith, but as other food. And [[77:31|the chosen men of Israel|Et electos Israel]], that is, those who seemed to be great in the Church, he [[77:31|brought down|impedivit]] [*impedivit*, literally "hindered"] from entrance into the kingdom of heaven, because of the sin of unworthy communion. For in Holy Scripture the chosen are not always those predestined to eternal life, since Christ says to the Apostles in the Gospel: [[John 6:71|Have not I chosen you twelve? And one of you is a devil|Nonne ego vos duodecim elegi, et unus ex vobis diabolus est?]]? And elsewhere we have: Saul was a chosen man[[1 Kings 9:2||]]; and yet many of the Saints say that he was damned.

paras.t: In omnibus his peccaverunt adhuc: id est, non obstantibus tantis beneficiis Christi, ingrati Christiani Christum offenderunt. Et defluxerunt in vanitate dies eorum, id est, sine fructu et merito defluxerunt; et anni eorum cum festinatione: quia sicut in libro Job habetur, Impius, antequam impleantur dies ejus, peribit. Et iterum de peccatoribus Scriptura testatur: Quoniam ante tempus suum sublati sunt. Unde ipsi fatentur: Nos nati continuo desivimus esse, et in malignitate nostra consumpti sumus.
paras.en: [[77:32|In all these things they sinned still|In omnibus his peccaverunt adhuc]]: that is, notwithstanding such great benefits of Christ, ungrateful Christians offended Christ. [[77:33|And their days were consumed in vanity|Et defluxerunt in vanitate dies eorum]] [Denis reads *defluxerunt*, "flowed away", where the Vulgate has *defecerunt*, "were consumed"], that is, they flowed away without fruit and merit; [[77:33|and their years in haste|et anni eorum cum festinatione]]: for, as we have in the book of Job, the wicked man, [[Job 15:32|Before his days be full he shall perish|antequam impleantur dies ejus, peribit]]. And again Scripture testifies of sinners: [[Job 22:16|Who were taken away before their time|Quoniam ante tempus suum sublati sunt]]. Whence they themselves confess: We, [[Wis 5:13|being born, forthwith ceased to be|nati continuo desivimus esse]], and [[Wis 5:13|are consumed in our wickedness|in malignitate nostra consumpti sumus]].

paras.t: Quum occideret eos, quærebant eum et revertebantur. Nam multi perversi, qui tempore securitatis converti contemnunt, dum similes sibi male perire conspiciunt, sibique eadem flagella imminere perpendunt, convertuntur ad Dominum. Tuncque reminisci incipiunt quod Deus adjutor est eorum. Verumtamen quoniam pœnitentia ista potius procedere solet ex humano timore, quam divino amore, idcirco de ipsis mox additur: Et dilexerunt eum in ore suo, dicentes, Domine, Domine; et lingua sua mentiti sunt ei, quia ex ejus reverentia non recesserunt a malo.
paras.en: [[77:34|When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned|Quum occideret eos, quærebant eum et revertebantur]]. For many perverse men, who in time of security disdain to be converted, when they see others like themselves perish miserably, and consider that the same scourges hang over them, are converted to the Lord. And then they begin to remember [[77:35|that God was their helper|Deus adjutor est eorum]]. Yet because this repentance usually proceeds rather from human fear than from divine love, it is straightway added of them: [[77:36|And they loved him with their mouth|Et dilexerunt eum in ore suo]], saying, [[Matt 7:21|Lord, Lord|Domine, Domine]]; [[77:36|and with their tongue they lied unto him|et lingua sua mentiti sunt ei]], because out of reverence for him they did not depart from evil.

paras.t: Ipse autem Christus est misericors ex proprietate naturali, et propitius fiet peccatis eorum, dummodo vere convertantur, et digne pœniteant; et non disperdet eos ab electorum consortio, nec denegabit eis gratiam in præsenti, nec gloriam in futuro: quoniam ipse ait, Gaudium est angelis Dei super uno peccatore pœnitentiam agente; et alibi, Non veni vocare justos, sed peccatores. Et abundavit Christus in se ipso divitiis misericordiæ suæ, ut averteret iram suam ab Ecclesia sua clementissime indulgendo. Nam quum adhuc inimici essemus, ipse pro nobis mortuus est; et quantum in se est, nullum perire permittit. Et non accendit contra nos omnem iram suam, id est justitiæ suæ rigorem, sed effudit super nos copiose misericordiam suam.
paras.en: [[77:38|But he|Ipse autem]], Christ, [[77:38|is merciful|est misericors]] by the property of his nature, [[77:38|and will forgive their sins|et propitius fiet peccatis eorum]], provided that they are truly converted and do worthy penance; [[77:38|and will not destroy them|et non disperdet eos]], cutting them off from the fellowship of the elect, nor will he deny them grace in the present nor glory in the future: for he himself says, There is [[Luke 15:10|joy before the angels of God upon one sinner doing penance|Gaudium est angelis Dei super uno peccatore pœnitentiam agente]]; and elsewhere, [[Matt 9:13|I am not come to call the just, but sinners|Non veni vocare justos, sed peccatores]]. [[77:38|And many a time did he|Et abundavit]] [*abundavit*, literally "he abounded"], Christ, abounding in himself in the riches of his mercy, [[77:38|turn away his anger|ut averteret iram suam]] from his Church, by most graciously forgiving. For when we were as yet enemies, he died for us; and as far as lies in him, he lets no one perish. [[77:38|And did not kindle|Et non accendit]] against us [[77:38|all his wrath|omnem iram suam]], that is, the rigour of his justice, but poured out his mercy upon us abundantly.

paras.t: Sed quanta est ingratitudo Christianorum quorumdam! Nam quoties, id est quam sæpe, quasi dicat, Multoties valde, exacerbaverunt eum, scilicet Salvatorem tam misericordissimum, dulcissimum, atque mitissimum, in deserto, id est in mundo isto a bonis relicto et malis impleto, arescenti et infructuoso! Et quoties in iram concitaverunt eum in inaquoso, videlicet in animo suo indurato et sicco, tanquam aquis gratiæ destituto! Et conversi sunt, post Baptismum et Pœnitentiam, ad pristinam conversationem mundanam; et tentaverunt Deum, quærentes experiri potentiam, providentiam, aut scientiam ejus, tanquam ambigui an Deus omnia possit, cunctorum providentiam habeat, et an universa cognoscat.
paras.en: But how great is the ingratitude of some Christians! For [[77:40|How often|quoties]], that is, how frequently (as if he said, Very many times indeed), [[77:40|did they provoke him|exacerbaverunt eum]], namely a Saviour so most merciful, most sweet and most gentle, [[77:40|in the desert|in deserto]], that is, in this world, forsaken by the good and filled with the wicked, drying up and fruitless! And how often did they [[77:40|move him to wrath in the place without water|in iram concitaverunt eum in inaquoso]], namely in their own mind, hardened and dry, as though bereft of the waters of grace! [[77:41|And they turned back|Et conversi sunt]], after Baptism and Penance, to their former worldly way of life; [[77:41|and tempted God|et tentaverunt Deum]], seeking to test his power, his providence or his knowledge, as though doubtful whether God can do all things, whether he has providence over all, and whether he knows all things.

paras.t: Non sunt recordati Christiani ingrati, manus ejus, id est piæ subventionis Jesu Christi, qua eis subvenit, die qua redemit eos de manu tribulantis, id est de potestate diaboli, de servitute peccati, et morte æterna. Hoc autem Christus fecit in die Parasceves, quando ipse justus pro nobis injustis passus est, ut nos offerret Deo, mortificatos quidem carne, vivificatos autem spiritu, quemadmodum scriptum est. Sicut posuit in Ægypto, id est in mundo isto vitiis involuto, signa sua: quoniam eo in cruce pendente, obscuratus est sol, tempore oppositionis, per suppositionem lunæ sub sole: quod mirabilissimum fuit, sicut in epistola ad Polycarpum magnus Dionysius pulchre prosequitur. Sed et terra tunc mota est, et multi defuncti surrexerunt, non in die passionis, sed resurrectionis.
paras.en: [[77:42|They remembered not|Non sunt recordati]], these ungrateful Christians, [[77:42|his hand|manus ejus]], that is, the loving help of Jesus Christ with which he came to their aid, [[77:42|in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them|die qua redemit eos de manu tribulantis]], that is, from the power of the devil, from the bondage of sin, and from eternal death. This Christ did on the day of the Parasceve [that is, Good Friday, the day of the Preparation], when he, the just, suffered for us the unjust, [[1 Pet 3:18|that he might offer us to God|ut nos offerret Deo]], we being put to death indeed in the flesh, but enlivened in the spirit, as it is written [Denis turns Peter's words about Christ, "put to death in the flesh, enlivened in the spirit", to us]. [[77:43|How he wrought|Sicut posuit]] [[77:43|in Egypt|in Ægypto]], that is, in this world wrapped in vices, [[77:43|his signs|signa sua]]: for while he hung on the cross the sun was darkened, at the time of opposition, by the moon being set beneath the sun [that is, at the full moon of the Pasch, when the moon stands opposite the sun and cannot naturally eclipse it]: which was most wonderful, as the great Dionysius beautifully sets out in his letter to Polycarp. And the earth too was moved then, and many of the dead rose, though not on the day of the passion, but on that of the resurrection.

paras.t: Et convertit in sanguinem flumina eorum. Decem plagæ, quæ Ægyptiis corporaliter contigerunt, perversis fidelibus spiritualiter accidunt. Convertuntur enim flumina eorum in sanguinem, dum sapientia eorum carnalis efficitur, et spiritualia ab eis carnaliter sentiuntur: quoniam, sicut ait Apostolus, Animalis homo non percipit ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei. Misit, et quotidie mittit Christus, non effective, sed permissive, in eos, id est in ingratos Christianos, cynomyiam, id est mores caninos, videlicet rabiem iræ, furorem impatientiæ, irreverentiam circa parentes atque prælatos, et comedit eos, id est, ista tortuositas mox spiritualiter eos annihilat; et ranam, id est incustodiam linguæ, et impudentissimam garrulamque loquacitatem, et disperdidit eos, id est, diversimode perdidit animas eorum loquacitatis peccatum. Unde Salomon dicit: Vidisti hominem velocem ad loquendum? Stultitia magis speranda est, quam illius correptio. Et Jacobus: Universitas iniquitatis, lingua constituitur. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico etiam scriptum est: Qui multis utitur verbis, lædit animam suam. Sit igitur omnis homo velox ad audiendum, tardus autem ad loquendum, et tardus ad iram.
paras.en: [[77:44|And he turned their rivers into blood|Et convertit in sanguinem flumina eorum]]. The ten plagues that befell the Egyptians bodily befall perverse believers spiritually. For their rivers are turned into blood when their wisdom becomes carnal, and spiritual things are understood by them carnally: since, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 2:14|the sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God|Animalis homo non percipit ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei]]. [[77:45|He sent|Misit]], and daily sends, Christ, not by causing it but by permitting it, [[77:45|amongst them|in eos]], that is, among ungrateful Christians, [[77:45|divers sorts of flies|cynomyiam]] [*cynomyia*, "dog-fly", from the Greek for dog and fly: hence Denis's reading], that is, doglike ways, namely the rage of anger, the fury of impatience, irreverence towards parents and prelates; [[77:45|which devoured them|et comedit eos]], that is, this crookedness soon brings them spiritually to nothing; [[77:45|and frogs|et ranam]], that is, an unguarded tongue and a most shameless and chattering talkativeness, [[77:45|which destroyed them|et disperdidit eos]], that is, the sin of talkativeness destroyed their souls in divers ways. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 29:20|Hast thou seen a man hasty to speak? folly is rather to be looked for, than his amendment|Vidisti hominem velocem ad loquendum? Stultitia magis speranda est, quam illius correptio]]. And James: [[Jas 3:6|a world of iniquity|Universitas iniquitatis]], [[Jas 3:6|The tongue is placed|lingua constituitur]] [that is, the tongue is set up as a world of iniquity]. For which reason it is also written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 20:8|He that useth many words shall hurt his own soul|Qui multis utitur verbis, lædit animam suam]] [the margin gives only Ecclus. xx]. Therefore [[Jas 1:19|let every man be swift to hear, but slow to speak and slow to anger|Sit igitur omnis homo velox ad audiendum, tardus autem ad loquendum, et tardus ad iram]].

paras.t: Et dedit ærugini fructus eorum. Per æruginem, quæ est ventus seu aura occulte nocens et fructus inficiens, designatur latens arrogantia cordis: per quam omnium operum bonorum fructus dissipatur, quoniam sola superbia destruit omnia, si comitetur. Nec mirum, quoniam Deus superbis resistit; et certum quoniam non sit tutum aut facile contra Deum pugnare. Et labores eorum locustæ: id est, opera laboriosa et bona prius facta ab ingratis et recidivantibus, Deus permittit evacuari a præmio per vitium detractionis: quia ingrati Deo, hoc vitium detractionis incidere solent: quod valde abominabile est, juxta illud Ecclesiastæ, Si mordeat serpens in silentio, nihil eo minus habet qui occulte detrahit.
paras.en: [[77:46|And he gave up their fruits to the blast|Et dedit ærugini fructus eorum]]. By the blast [*ærugo*, blight or mildew], which is a wind or breeze that does hidden harm and infects the fruits, is meant the hidden arrogance of the heart: by which the fruit of all good works is scattered, since pride alone, if it goes along with them, destroys all. Nor is this any wonder, since [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud|Deus superbis resistit]][[1 Pet 5:5||]]; and it is certain that it is neither safe nor easy to fight against God. [[77:46|and their labours to the locust|Et labores eorum locustæ]]: that is, the laborious and good works done before by the ungrateful and by those who fall back, God permits to be emptied of their reward through the vice of detraction: for those who are ungrateful to God are wont to fall into this vice of detraction; which is very abominable, according to that saying of Ecclesiastes, [[Eccles 10:11|If a serpent bite in silence, he is nothing better that backbiteth secretly|Si mordeat serpens in silentio, nihil eo minus habet qui occulte detrahit]].

paras.t: Et occidit in grandine, id est in iniquitate alios violenter opprimentes, sicut et potestas tyrannica, vineas, id est animas, eorum: quia dum Deo ingrati et arrogantes, alios opprimunt et contristant, semetipsos intus occidunt, et proprio gladio spiritualiter ruunt; et moros eorum, id est opera eorum priora, igne amoris succensa, occidit, id est, occidi permisit Deus, in pruina, id est in nocturno frigore mentis, utpote in rancore et odio: quod est frigus et congelatio spiritus, sicut dilectio est ignis et liquefactio ejus. Qui enim post caritatem receptam, ad interiorem frigiditatem odii ducitur, priorum operum in caritate factorum præmio juste privatur, et variis vitiis implicatur. Propter quod ait Salvator: Abundabit iniquitas, et refrigescet caritas multorum. Hoc frigore tacto ait Joannes, vel potius per Joannem Christus: Habeo adversum te, quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti. Memor esto itaque unde exciderit, et age pœnitentiam.
paras.en: [[77:47|And he destroyed|Et occidit]] [[77:47|with hail|in grandine]], that is, in the iniquity of violently oppressing others, as tyrannical power also does, [[77:47|their vineyards|vineas]], that is, their souls: for while, ungrateful to God and arrogant, they oppress and sadden others, they slay themselves within, and fall spiritually by their own sword; [[77:47|and their mulberry trees|et moros eorum]], that is, their former works, kindled with the fire of love, he destroyed, that is, God allowed them to be destroyed, [[77:47|with hoarfrost|in pruina]], that is, in the nightly cold of the mind, as in rancour and hatred: which is the cold and freezing of the spirit, as love is its fire and its melting. For he who after receiving charity is led to the inner coldness of hatred is justly deprived of the reward of the former works done in charity, and is entangled in various vices. For which reason the Saviour says: [[Matt 24:12|iniquity hath abounded, the charity of many shall grow cold|Abundabit iniquitas, et refrigescet caritas multorum]]. With this cold in view John says, or rather Christ through John: [[Apoc 2:4|I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity|Habeo adversum te, quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti]]. [[Apoc 2:5|Be mindful therefore from whence thou art fallen: and do penance|Memor esto itaque unde exciderit, et age pœnitentiam]].

paras.t: Et tradidit grandini, id est prædictæ iniquitati, jumenta eorum, id est sensitivas eorum potentias, tam cognitivas quam appetitivas, videlicet sensus exteriores et interiores, appetitum quoque concupiscibilem et irascibilem. Dum enim peccator Deo ingratus, toto studio quæret quomodo alios opprimat, lædat, aut eis prævaleat, tunc prædictæ potentiæ grandini dantur, quoniam per operationes earum quærit et satagit quomodo perversum suum propositum exsequatur. Et possessionem eorum, id est statum et perfectiones, seu interiores divitias mentis hominum horum, dat Deus igni, id est avaritiæ æstui: quia dum a spiritualium amore bonorum labuntur, ad terrenarum atque inanium rerum desideria convertuntur; sicque avaritiæ ignis in eis devastat et destruit quidquid perfectionis ante inhæserat. Unde et Paulus ad Timotheum scribit: Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli. Et Ecclesiasticus: Nihil est iniquius quam amare pecuniam. Hic enim (puta avarus) et animam suam venalem habet.
paras.en: [[77:48|And he gave up|Et tradidit]] [[77:48|to the hail|grandini]], that is, to the aforesaid iniquity, [[77:48|their cattle|jumenta eorum]], that is, their powers of sense, both cognitive and appetitive, namely the outer and inner senses, and also the concupiscible and irascible appetite [in the language of the Schoolmen, the powers of desire and of resistance or anger]. For when the sinner, ungrateful to God, seeks with all his zeal how he may oppress or hurt others or prevail over them, then those powers are given up to the hail, since through their workings he seeks and strives to carry out his perverse purpose. [[77:48|And their stock|Et possessionem eorum]], that is, the state and perfections, or the inner riches of mind, of these men, God gives [[77:48|to the fire|igni]], that is, to the heat of avarice: for while they slip away from the love of spiritual goods, they turn to the desire of earthly and empty things; and so the fire of avarice in them lays waste and destroys whatever perfection had clung to them before. Whence Paul also writes to Timothy: [[1 Tim 6:9|they that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli]]. And Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:10|There is not a more wicked thing than to love money|Nihil est iniquius quam amare pecuniam]]: [[Ecclus 10:10|for such a one|Hic enim]] (that is, the covetous man) [[Ecclus 10:10|setteth even his own soul to sale|et animam suam venalem habet]].

paras.t: Viam fecit Deus semitæ iræ suæ, id est effusioni suæ vindictæ. Dum enim peccatorem in suo errore relinquit, viam facit semitæ iræ suæ, quia non tollit impedimentum incurrendi pœnam divinæ justitiæ. Hoc facit Deus in vasis iræ, quæ ad contumeliam facta sunt, puta in reprobis: quos Deus in suis adinventionibus juste relinquit, quia in eis suæ justitiæ distinctionem ostendere cogitavit, sicut in electis misericordiæ suæ divitias. De qua re plenius docet Apostolus. Non pepercit a morte animarum eorum: quoniam caritatem, quæ est vita animæ, Deus protinus subtrahit cunctis hominibus qui mortaliter peccant. Et jumenta eorum, id est carnales eorum affectus et opera carnis, Deus in morte conclusit, id est, æterna morte damnavit: quoniam teste Apostolo, Qui talia agunt, regnum Dei non consequentur; et iterum, Si secundum carnem (inquit) vixeritis, moriemini.
paras.en: [[77:50|He made a way for a path to his anger|Viam fecit Deus semitæ iræ suæ]], that is, for the pouring out of his vengeance. For when he leaves the sinner in his error, he makes a way for the path of his anger, because he does not take away what hinders him from incurring the penalty of divine justice. This God does in the vessels of wrath, which are made unto dishonour, that is, in the reprobate: whom God justly leaves in their own inventions, because he purposed to show in them the severity [reading *districtionem* for the printed *distinctionem*] of his justice, as in the elect the riches of his mercy. On this the Apostle teaches more fully[[Rom 9:22||]] [the margin gives Rom. ix, 21–23]. [[77:50|he spared not their souls from death|Non pepercit a morte animarum eorum]]: since God at once withdraws charity, which is the life of the soul, from all men who sin mortally. [[77:50|and their cattle|Et jumenta eorum]], that is, their carnal affections and the works of the flesh, God [[77:50|shut up in death|in morte conclusit]], that is, condemned to eternal death: since, as the Apostle bears witness, [[Gal 5:21|they who do such things shall not obtain the kingdom of God|Qui talia agunt, regnum Dei non consequentur]]; and again, [[Rom 8:13|if you live according to the flesh|Si secundum carnem]] (he says) [[Rom 8:13|you shall die|vixeritis, moriemini]].

paras.t: Et percussit omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti: id est, in omnibus cordibus in tenebris hujus mundi manentibus, Deus occidit fidem formatam, in quantum formatam, licet in eis fides informis perseveret. Fides namque formata, est in nobis primogenitum, id est primum Dei donum, et omnium operum meritoriorum principium, juxta illud Habacuc: Ecce qui incredulus est, non erit anima ejus recta in semetipso; justus autem meus ex fide vivit. Et Isaias: Qui incredulus est, infideliter agit. Primitias omnis laboris eorum, id est interiores sanctæ caritatis fervores, ex quibus omnis labor Deo placens meritoriusque procedit, Deus occidit, secundum modum prædictum, in ingratis et ad vitia pristina remeantibus, in tabernaculis Cham, id est hominum mundanorum seu dæmonum, qui sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, sed benefacere nescierunt. Cham enim callidus interpretatur. Et Christo testante, Filii hujus sæculi prudentiores in generatione sua sunt filiis lucis.
paras.en: [[77:51|And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt|Et percussit omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti]]: that is, in all hearts that abide in the darkness of this world God slew formed faith [that is, faith given its form by charity, living faith], in so far as it is formed, although unformed faith [faith without charity] remains in them. For formed faith is the firstborn in us, that is, God's first gift and the beginning of all meritorious works, according to that saying of Habacuc: [[Hab 2:4|Behold, he that is unbelieving, his soul shall not be right in himself|Ecce qui incredulus est, non erit anima ejus recta in semetipso]]; [[Heb 10:38|my just man liveth by faith|justus autem meus ex fide vivit]] [Denis gives the end of Hab 2:4 in the words of Heb 10:38]. And Isaias: [[Is 21:2|he that is unfaithful dealeth unfaithfully|Qui incredulus est, infideliter agit]]. [[77:51|the firstfruits of all their labour|Primitias omnis laboris eorum]], that is, the inner fervours of holy charity, from which all labour pleasing to God and meritorious proceeds, God slew, in the way already said, in the ungrateful and in those who go back to their former vices, [[77:51|in the tabernacles of Cham|in tabernaculis Cham]], that is, of worldly men or of demons, who [[Jer 4:22|are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge|sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, sed benefacere nescierunt]]. For Cham is interpreted *crafty*. And, as Christ bears witness, [[Luke 16:8|children of this world are wiser in their generation than the children of light|filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis]].

paras.t: Et abstulit Christus sicut oves populum suum, id est electos, de potestate diaboli, de conversatione sæculari, de societate reproborum, quemadmodum per Osee ait: De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos. Et alibi electis locutus est: De mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo. Hoc agit Salvator, quotiescumque homini gratiam conversionis infundit. Et perduxit eos tanquam gregem in deserto, id est in præsenti exilio, pascendo eos gratiis atque virtutibus. Propter quod de se ait: Ego sum pastor bonus, et cognosco oves meas, et cognoscunt me meæ, et ego vitam æternam do eis. Pascit quoque eas cibo dignissimo, scilicet pretiosissimo corporis sui et sanguinis Sacramento.
paras.en: [[77:52|And he took away|Et abstulit]], Christ did, [[77:52|his own people as sheep|sicut oves populum suum]], that is, the elect, from the power of the devil, from worldly ways, from the company of the reprobate, as he says through Osee: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos]]. And elsewhere he said to the elect: [[John 15:19|you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world|De mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo]]. This the Saviour does whenever he pours into a man the grace of conversion. [[77:52|and guided them in the wilderness like a flock|Et perduxit eos tanquam gregem in deserto]], that is, in this present exile, feeding them with graces and virtues. For which reason he says of himself: [[John 10:14|I am the good shepherd: and I know mine, and mine know me|Ego sum pastor bonus, et cognosco oves meas, et cognoscunt me meæ]], [[John 10:28|And I give them life everlasting|et ego vitam æternam do eis]]. He feeds them also with the worthiest food, namely the most precious Sacrament of his body and blood.

paras.t: Et deduxit eos in spe felicitatis futuræ, et non timuerunt inordinato timore damna temporalia aut diaboli tentamenta, quoniam audierunt quod Salvator ait ad eos: In mundo pressuram habebitis; sed confidite, ego vici mundum. Et alibi: Non turbetur cor vestrum, neque formidet; et, Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt. Et inimicos eorum, id est persecutores justorum, operuit mare, id est iniquitas propria seu damnatio infernalis, vel tumultus occupationum vitæ sæcularis.
paras.en: [[77:53|And he brought them out in hope|Et deduxit eos in spe]] of future happiness, [[77:53|and they feared not|et non timuerunt]] with disordered fear temporal losses or the temptations of the devil, since they had heard what the Saviour said to them: [[John 16:33|In the world you shall have distress. But have confidence. I have overcome the world|In mundo pressuram habebitis; sed confidite, ego vici mundum]]. And elsewhere: [[John 14:27|Let not your heart be troubled: nor let it be afraid|Non turbetur cor vestrum, neque formidet]]; and, [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not them that kill the body|Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt]]. And [[77:53|their enemies|Et inimicos eorum]], that is, the persecutors of the just, [[77:53|the sea overwhelmed|operuit mare]], that is, their own iniquity or the damnation of hell, or the turmoil of the business of worldly life.

paras.t: Et induxit eos in montem sanctificationis suæ, id est in obedientiam sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ, quæ est regnum Christi, in ea per fidem regnantis. Idcirco dicit Apostolus: Gratias agimus Deo et Patri, qui nos transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ. Montem quem acquisivit dextera ejus, scilicet Christi, pro nobis in cruce expansa atque transfixa. Christus namque emit Ecclesiam non corruptibilibus auro et argento, sed sanguine suo pretioso, juxta illud Apostoli: Christus semel oblatus est ad multorum exhaurienda peccata. In Actibus quoque Paulus apertius loquens, et pastores exhortans: Attendite, inquit, vobis et universo gregi, in quo vos posuit Spiritus Sanctus episcopos, regere Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit sanguine suo.
paras.en: [[77:54|And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary|Et induxit eos in montem sanctificationis suæ]], that is, into obedience to holy mother Church, which is the kingdom of Christ, who reigns in her through faith. Therefore the Apostle says: We give thanks to God the Father, who [[Col 1:13|hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love|transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ]]. [[77:54|the mountain which his right hand had purchased|Montem quem acquisivit dextera ejus]], that is, the right hand of Christ, stretched out and pierced for us on the cross. For Christ bought the Church not with corruptible things, gold and silver, but with his own precious blood, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Heb 9:28|Christ was offered once to exhaust the sins of many|Christus semel oblatus est ad multorum exhaurienda peccata]]. In the Acts also Paul, speaking more plainly and exhorting the pastors, says: [[Acts 20:28|Take heed|Attendite]], he says, [[Acts 20:28|to yourselves and to the whole flock, wherein the Holy Ghost hath placed you bishops, to rule the Church of God which he hath purchased with his own blood|vobis et universo gregi, in quo vos posuit Spiritus Sanctus episcopos, regere Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit sanguine suo]].

paras.t: Et ejecit a facie eorum gentes. Hoc in Christianis ad litteram constat impletum, quoniam in universo mundo, ubi olim habitabant gentiles, postmodum habitaverunt Christiani, nuncque morantur: quod utique factum est virtute divina per multa miracula, quibus eradicata est idololatria, et publicata fides catholica. Et sorte divisit eis terram in funiculo distributionis. Per sortem, Dionysius interdum intelligi vult quemdam splendorem seu ordinationem Spiritus Sancti. Quoniam ergo Apostoli, secundum Spiritus Sancti instinctum, mundum sibi partiti sunt, abeuntes singuli in sortem seu partem sibi deputatam, sicut Joannes in Asiam, Petrus in Italiam, Andreas in Achaiam, Thomas in Indiam, etc.; ideo dicitur Deus divisisse eis terram in funiculis distributionis. Unde et Paulus fatetur: Nos non in infinitum gloriabimur, sed secundum mensuram regulæ, qua mensus est nobis Deus mensuram pertingendi usque ad vos.
paras.en: [[77:54|And he cast out the Gentiles before them|Et ejecit a facie eorum gentes]]. This is plainly fulfilled to the letter in the Christians, since throughout the whole world, where once the Gentiles dwelt, Christians afterwards dwelt and dwell now: which was done indeed by divine power through many miracles, by which idolatry was rooted out and the Catholic faith made known. [[77:54|and by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution|Et sorte divisit eis terram in funiculo distributionis]]. By *lot* Dionysius sometimes means a certain splendour or ordering of the Holy Ghost. Since, then, the Apostles, at the prompting of the Holy Ghost, divided the world among themselves, each going off to the lot or share assigned to him, as John to Asia, Peter to Italy, Andrew to Achaia, Thomas to India, etc., God is therefore said to have divided to them the land by lines of distribution. Whence Paul too confesses: [[2 Cor 10:13|we will not glory beyond our measure: but according to the measure of the rule which God hath measured to us, a measure to reach even unto you|Nos non in infinitum gloriabimur, sed secundum mensuram regulæ, qua mensus est nobis Deus mensuram pertingendi usque ad vos]].

paras.t: Et habitare fecit Deus in tabernaculis eorum, id est in locis, terris et urbibus paganorum, tribus Israel, id est populum christianum, qui sunt filii […] Patriarcharum, non carne, sed spiritu.
paras.en: [[77:55|And he made|Et habitare fecit]], God did, [[77:55|to dwell in their tabernacles|in tabernaculis eorum]], that is, in the places, lands and cities of the pagans, [[77:55|the tribes of Israel|tribus Israel]], that is, the Christian people, who are the sons […] of the Patriarchs, not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.

paras.t: Iterum redit Propheta ad describendum peccata Christianorum malorum, qui patrum suorum non sunt imitati vestigia, sed solo nomine et fide informi Christiani exsistunt. De quibus nunc subditur: Et tentaverunt et exacerbaverunt Deum excelsum: secundum modum nunc sæpe expositum.
paras.en: Again the Prophet returns to describing the sins of bad Christians, who have not followed in the footsteps of their fathers, but are Christians only in name and by unformed faith. Of them it is now added: [[77:56|Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God|Et tentaverunt et exacerbaverunt Deum excelsum]], in the way now often explained.

paras.t: In iram concitaverunt eum in collibus suis, id est in tumore superbiæ suæ, transferentes honorem Dei, cui soli debetur omnis honor et gloria, ad semetipsos, quærentes præesse, dominari ac honorari. Talibus equidem a Christo dicitur: Quomodo potestis vos credere, qui gloriam ab invicem accipitis, et gloriam quæ a solo Deo est, non quæritis? Et in sculptilibus suis, id est in idolis seu phantasmatibus imaginationum suarum, et in vanis memoriæ suæ simulacris, ad æmulationem, id est ad indignationem, eum provocaverunt, cogitantes perversa, et vilium rerum recordationibus inhærentes, atque per hoc divinorum obliviscentes, et Deum judicem offendentes: qui per Michæam ait, Væ qui cogitatis inutile; similiter per Isaiam, Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis. De talibus namque dicit Zacharias: Posuerunt cor suum ut adamantem, ne audirent legem.
paras.en: [[77:58|They provoked him to anger on their hills|In iram concitaverunt eum in collibus suis]], that is, in the swelling of their pride, transferring to themselves the honour of God, to whom alone all honour and glory is due[[1 Tim 1:17||]], seeking to be over others, to rule and to be honoured. To such indeed Christ says: [[John 5:44|How can you believe, who receive glory one from another: and the glory which is from God alone, you do not seek?|Quomodo potestis vos credere, qui gloriam ab invicem accipitis, et gloriam quæ a solo Deo est, non quæritis?]] And [[77:58|with their graven things|Et in sculptilibus suis]], that is, in the idols or phantasms of their imaginations, and in the empty images of their memory, [[77:58|to jealousy|ad æmulationem]], that is, to indignation, they [[77:58|moved him|eum provocaverunt]], thinking perverse things, and clinging to the remembrance of base things, and so forgetting divine things, and offending God the judge: who says through Micheas, [[Mich 2:1|Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable|Væ qui cogitatis inutile]]; and likewise through Isaias, [[Is 1:16|take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]]. For of such Zacharias says: [[Zach 7:12|they made their heart as the adamant stone, lest they should hear the law|Posuerunt cor suum ut adamantem, ne audirent legem]].

paras.t: Audivit Deus, id est, omnia ista populi peccata cognovit, quemadmodum Amos testatur: Cognovi multa scelera vestra; et sprevit operantes et opera, sicut inferius dicitur: Sprevisti omnes discedentes a justitiis tuis; et ad nihilum redegit valde Israel, id est plebem fidelium, spoliando eos omni virtute et gratia Spiritus Sancti, propter peccata commissa.
paras.en: [[77:59|God heard|Audivit Deus]], that is, he knew all these sins of the people, as Amos testifies: [[Amos 5:12|I know your manifold crimes|Cognovi multa scelera vestra]]; [[77:59|and despised|et sprevit]] both the workers and the works, as is said further on: [[Ps 118:118|Thou hast despised all them that fall off from thy judgments|Sprevisti omnes discedentes a justitiis tuis]] [Denis has *justitiis*, "justices", where the Vulgate has *judiciis*, "judgments"]; [[77:59|and he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing|et ad nihilum redegit valde Israel]], that is, the people of the faithful, stripping them of all virtue and of the grace of the Holy Ghost, because of the sins they had committed.

paras.t: Et repulit tabernaculum Silo: per quod intelligi potest Ecclesia, quam Deus frequenter vastari permisit a tyrannis et impiis, eo quod legem Christi reliquerit. Potest etiam per hoc accipi corpus nostrum, in quo Deus habitare censetur, sicut ait Apostolus: Glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro; et rursus: Nescitis quia corpora vestra templum sunt Spiritus Sancti? Hoc tabernaculum Deus repellit, dum animam deserit, ab ea offensus propter vitam carnalem. Unde Dominus olim locutus est: Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est.
paras.en: [[77:60|And he put away the tabernacle of Silo|Et repulit tabernaculum Silo]]: by which may be understood the Church, which God has often let be laid waste by tyrants and the wicked, because she forsook the law of Christ. By it may also be taken our body, in which God is held to dwell, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 6:20|Glorify and bear God in your body|Glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro]]; and again: [[1 Cor 6:19|know you not that your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost|Nescitis quia corpora vestra templum sunt Spiritus Sancti?]]? [Denis has *corpora*, "bodies", where the Vulgate has *membra*, "members".] This tabernacle God puts away when he forsakes the soul, offended by it because of its carnal life. Whence the Lord said of old: [[Gen 6:3|My spirit shall not remain in man for ever, because he is flesh|Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est]].

paras.t: Et tradidit in captivitatem virtutem eorum, id est, a tentatore permisit eos superari, et perfectionem eorum exstingui. Superbi enim in se ipsis confidentes, et ingrati, Deo bona sua non adscribentes, divina protectione indigni sunt, ideoque a dæmonibus superantur. Et pulchritudinem eorum in manus inimici: id est, splendorem gratiæ interiora ornantis, permisit obtenebrari et tolli a suggestione et impugnatione carnis, mundi aut dæmonis, in hominibus sibi ingratis. Nam de ingrato ait Salvator in Evangelio: Ei autem qui non habet, et quod videtur habere, auferetur ab eo. Sic ergo captivi sunt, secundum quod Petrus protestatur: Iniqui, servi sunt corruptionis: a quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est.
paras.en: [[77:61|And he delivered their strength into captivity|Et tradidit in captivitatem virtutem eorum]], that is, he let them be overcome by the tempter, and their perfection be extinguished. For the proud, trusting in themselves, and the ungrateful, who do not ascribe their good things to God, are unworthy of divine protection, and so are overcome by the demons. [[77:61|and their beauty into the hands of the enemy|Et pulchritudinem eorum in manus inimici]]: that is, the splendour of grace adorning the inner man he let be darkened and taken away by the suggestion and assault of the flesh, the world or the devil, in men ungrateful to him. For of the ungrateful man the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Matt 25:29|from him that hath not, that also which he seemeth to have shall be taken away|Ei autem qui non habet, et quod videtur habere, auferetur ab eo]]. So then they are captives, as Peter declares: The wicked [[2 Pet 2:19|are the slaves of corruption|servi sunt corruptionis]]: [[2 Pet 2:19|For by whom a man is overcome, of the same also he is the slave|a quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est]].

paras.t: Et conclusit in gladio infidelium populum suum christianum, quem Sarraceni in Terra sancta sæpe occiderunt et expulerunt. Potest quoque nomine gladii intelligi impugnatio tentatoris, seu perversitas animæ se ipsam necantis, imo et totum hominem spiritualiter occidentis gladio consensus illiciti. Et hereditatem suam sprevit: id est, plebem christianam, quæ merito foret hereditas Dei, tanquam ejus sanguine empta, ab infidelibus non protexit, nec a culpa retraxit.
paras.en: [[77:62|And he shut up|Et conclusit]] [[77:62|under the sword|in gladio]] of the infidels [[77:62|his people|populum suum]], the Christian people, whom the Saracens have often slain and driven out in the Holy Land. By the name of *sword* may also be understood the assault of the tempter, or the perversity of the soul that kills itself, nay, that slays the whole man spiritually with the sword of unlawful consent. [[77:62|and he despised his inheritance|Et hereditatem suam sprevit]]: that is, the Christian people, which would rightly be the inheritance of God, as bought with his blood, he did not protect from the infidels, nor draw back from sin.

paras.t: Juvenes eorum comedit ignis concupiscentiæ carnalis: sicut Osee ait, Spiritus fornicationis decepit eos; et virgines eorum vanæ et fatuæ non sunt lamentatæ: quia non est qui earum vanitatem deploret ex compassione caritatis fraternæ, sed laudantur peccatrices in vanitatibus animæ suæ.
paras.en: [[77:63|Fire consumed their young men|Juvenes eorum comedit ignis]], the fire of carnal concupiscence: as Osee says, [[Osee 4:12|the spirit of fornication hath deceived them|Spiritus fornicationis decepit eos]]; [[77:63|and their maidens|et virgines eorum]], vain and foolish, [[77:63|were not lamented|non sunt lamentatæ]]: for there is none to bewail their vanity out of the compassion of brotherly charity, but sinful women are praised in the vanities of their soul[[Ps 9:24||]] [the margin gives Ps. v, 3 and following, in the Hebrew numbering; Denis is adapting Ps 9:24 (Ps 10:3 in the Hebrew), "the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul"].

paras.t: Sacerdotes eorum in gladio ceciderunt. Gladius spiritualis, secundum Apostolum, est verbum Dei. Est igitur sensus: Sacerdotes Christianorum, proprii oris prædicatione occisi sunt intus. Dum enim docent quæ ipsi non implent, mortaliter peccant: et ita se ipsos damnant, spiritualiterque occidunt. Unde Apostolus ait: In quo alium judicas, te ipsum condemnas; eadem enim facis. Et Job dicit: Os tuum condemnabit te, et non ego, et labia tua respondebunt tibi. Et viduæ eorum non plorabantur: sicut ait Apostolus, Vidua quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est. Viduæ ergo non plorantur, dum earum carnales deliciæ non deflentur pio compassionis affectu.
paras.en: [[77:64|Their priests fell by the sword|Sacerdotes eorum in gladio ceciderunt]]. The spiritual sword, according to the Apostle, is [[Eph 6:17|the word of God|verbum Dei]]. The sense, then, is: the priests of the Christians have been slain within by the preaching of their own mouth. For when they teach what they themselves do not fulfil, they sin mortally: and so they condemn themselves and slay themselves spiritually. Whence the Apostle says: [[Rom 2:1|wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself|In quo alium judicas, te ipsum condemnas]]; [[Rom 2:1|For thou dost the same things|eadem enim facis]]. And Job says: [[Job 15:6|Thy own mouth shall condemn thee, and not I: and thy own lips shall answer thee|Os tuum condemnabit te, et non ego, et labia tua respondebunt tibi]]. [[77:64|and their widows did not mourn|Et viduæ eorum non plorabantur]] [Denis takes *non plorabantur* as "were not mourned"]: as the Apostle says, The widow [[1 Tim 5:6|that liveth in pleasures is dead while she is living|quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est]]. Widows, then, are not mourned when their carnal pleasures are not wept for with the loving affection of compassion.

paras.t: Et percussit inimicos suos in posteriora, id est, extrema atque finali pœna eos damnavit, quemadmodum Dominus per Jeremiam ait quibusdam: Dabo vos in opprobrium sempiternum et ignominiam æternam, quæ nunquam oblivione delebitur. Idcirco nunc additur, opprobrium sempiternum dedit illis, projiciendo eos in lacum carceris gehennalis. Propter quod in Jeremia Dominus loquitur: Dabo eos in vexationem et maledictionem et stuporem, et in sibilum, et in opprobrium, eo quod non audierint verba mea.
paras.en: [[77:66|And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts|Et percussit inimicos suos in posteriora]], that is, he condemned them with the last and final punishment, as the Lord says through Jeremias to some: [[Jer 23:40|I will bring an everlasting reproach upon you, and a perpetual shame which shall never be forgotten|Dabo vos in opprobrium sempiternum et ignominiam æternam, quæ nunquam oblivione delebitur]]. Therefore it is now added, [[77:66|he put them to an everlasting reproach|opprobrium sempiternum dedit illis]], casting them into the pit of the prison of hell. For which reason the Lord speaks in Jeremias: [[Jer 29:18|I will give them up unto affliction|Dabo eos in vexationem]], [[Jer 29:18|to be a curse, and an astonishment, and a hissing, and a reproach|et maledictionem et stuporem, et in sibilum, et in opprobrium]], [[Jer 29:19|Because they have not hearkened to my words|eo quod non audierint verba mea]] [the margin gives Jer. xxiv, 9, a like passage; Denis's words are those of Jer 29:18–19].

paras.t: Consequenter agit Propheta, de populo ad regnum Christi veraciter pertinente. Et repulit Deus tabernaculum, id est posteritatem, domum, familiam, Joseph, id est populi Judæorum, in lege sibi finem et sufficientiam constituentis, qui se putat sine gratia Christi per legem posse salvari. Merito quoque per Joseph populus Judæorum signatur. Primo, quoniam Joseph ceteris Patriarchis fratribus suis sanctitate atque imperio eminebat. Secundo, quoniam Joseph interpretatur additamentum: et ita per eum designantur Judæi, quibus temporalium bonorum promittebantur augmenta. Et tribum Ephraim non elegit. Ephraim interpretatur frugifer seu fructificatio: per quem significatur idem populus qui per Joseph, in quantum terrenis fructibus inhiabat. Sed elegit tribum Juda, id est populum christianum, Domino confitentem devote et pure propter bona cœlestia ac divina, videlicet montem Sion, id est militantem Ecclesiam, quem dilexit, juxta illud Apostoli: Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut illam sanctificaret.
paras.en: Next the Prophet treats of the people that truly belongs to the kingdom of Christ. [[77:67|And he rejected the tabernacle|Et repulit Deus tabernaculum]], that is, the posterity, house and family, [[77:67|of Joseph|Joseph]], that is, of the Jewish people, which makes the law its end and sufficiency, and thinks it can be saved by the law without the grace of Christ. And the Jewish people is fittingly signified by Joseph. First, because Joseph stood out above the other Patriarchs, his brothers, in holiness and in rule. Secondly, because Joseph is interpreted *increase*: and so by him are signified the Jews, to whom increase of temporal goods was promised. [[77:67|and chose not the tribe of Ephraim|Et tribum Ephraim non elegit]]. Ephraim is interpreted *fruitful* or *fruit-bearing*: by whom is signified the same people as by Joseph, in so far as it gaped after earthly fruits. [[77:68|But he chose the tribe of Juda|Sed elegit tribum Juda]], that is, the Christian people, confessing the Lord devoutly and purely for the sake of heavenly and divine goods [Juda is interpreted *confession* or *praise*], namely [[77:68|mount Sion|montem Sion]], that is, the Church militant, [[77:68|which he loved|quem dilexit]], according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved the church and delivered himself up for it|Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea]], [[Eph 5:26|That he might sanctify it|ut illam sanctificaret]].

paras.t: Et ædificavit sicut unicornium, id est, sicut ædificari decuit domum Christifidelium, unum verum Deum colentium, sanctificium suum, id est Ecclesiam militantem, seu populum christianum: quem ædificavit, faciendo sibi in cordibus nostris habitaculum aptum per fidem et gratiam Spiritus Sancti. De hac quippe ædificatione ait Christus per Amos: Suscitabo tabernaculum David quod cecidit, et reædificabo aperturas murorum ejus. Hoc sanctificium Deus ædificavit in terra quam fundavit in sæcula, id est in universo mundo, sicut apud Malachiam testatur: Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus; et in omni loco offertur nomini meo oblatio munda, videlicet Sacramentum altaris. Et hæc terra est fundata in sæcula, quoniam, sicut Ecclesiastes ait, Terra in æternum stat.
paras.en: [[77:69|And he built|Et ædificavit]] [[77:69|as of unicorns|sicut unicornium]] [*unicornis*, "one-horned": Denis takes it of those who worship the one God], that is, as it was fitting that the house of Christ's faithful, who worship the one true God, should be built, [[77:69|his sanctuary|sanctificium suum]], that is, the Church militant, or the Christian people: which he built by making for himself in our hearts a fit dwelling through faith and the grace of the Holy Ghost. For of this building Christ says through Amos: [[Amos 9:11|I will raise up the tabernacle of David, that is fallen: and I will close up the breaches of the walls thereof|Suscitabo tabernaculum David quod cecidit, et reædificabo aperturas murorum ejus]]. This sanctuary God built [[77:69|in the land which he founded for ever|in terra quam fundavit in sæcula]], that is, in the whole world, as he testifies in Malachias: [[Mal 1:11|from the rising of the sun even to the going down, my name is great among the Gentiles, and in every place|Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus; et in omni loco]] [[Mal 1:11|there is offered to my name a clean oblation|offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]], namely the Sacrament of the altar. And this land is founded for ever, since, as Ecclesiastes says, [[Eccles 1:4|the earth standeth for ever|Terra in æternum stat]].

paras.t: Et elegit Deus Trinitas David servum suum, id est Christum hominem: qui secundum quod homo est, servus Dei atque electus est, quemadmodum in Isaia Dominus ait: Ecce servus meus, suscipiam illum; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea. Quod evangelista Matthæus de Christo dictum allegat. Christum ergo Deus elegit, ut sit caput et princeps universalis Ecclesiæ, dux, pastor, judex et Dominus omnium electorum. Propter quod Dominus ait: Salvabo gregem meum; et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum qui pascat eum, David servum meum, id est Christum, ut omnes exponunt. Et sustulit eum, scilicet Christum, Deus Trinitas, de gregibus ovium, id est, præ omnibus electis exaltavit glorificavitque eum, quemadmodum Sponsa decantat: Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus. De post fetantes accepit eum: id est, postquam oves suas in hoc mundo spiritualiter fecundavit, redemit, et confirmavit, recepit eum Pater in cœlos ad dexteram suam. Propter quod Christus ait ad Patrem: Opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem; nunc autem ad te venio. Vel, De post fetantes accepit eum, quia Christus primo missus est ad oves perditas domus Israel, quibus reparatis, quoad electos, misit discipulos suos per totum mundum ad oves ex gentibus congregandas, sicut ipse ait: Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere.
paras.en: [[77:70|And he chose|Et elegit]], God the Trinity did, [[77:70|his servant David|David servum suum]], that is, Christ as man: who, according as he is man, is the servant of God and chosen, as the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him: my elect, my soul delighteth in him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam illum; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea]]. This the evangelist Matthew alleges as said of Christ[[Matt 12:18||]]. God therefore chose Christ to be the head and universal prince of the Church, the leader, shepherd, judge and Lord of all the elect. For which reason the Lord says: [[Ezech 34:22|I will save my flock|Salvabo gregem meum]]; [[Ezech 34:23|And I WILL SET UP ONE SHEPHERD OVER THEM, and he shall feed them, even my servant David|et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum qui pascat eum, David servum meum]], that is, Christ, as all expound it. [[77:70|and took him|Et sustulit eum]], namely Christ, God the Trinity did, [[77:70|from the flocks of sheep|de gregibus ovium]], that is, he exalted and glorified him above all the elect, as the Bride sings: [[Cant 5:10|My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands|Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus]]. [[77:70|he brought him from following the ewes great with young|De post fetantes accepit eum]]: that is, after he had made his sheep spiritually fruitful in this world, redeemed them and strengthened them, the Father received him into heaven at his right hand. For which reason Christ says to the Father: [[John 17:4|I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do|Opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem]]; [[John 17:13|And now I come to thee|nunc autem ad te venio]]. Or, [[77:70|he brought him from following the ewes great with young|De post fetantes accepit eum]], because Christ was first sent [[Matt 15:24|to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|ad oves perditas domus Israel]]; and when these had been restored, as regards the elect, he sent his disciples throughout the whole world to gather the sheep from among the Gentiles, as he himself says: [[John 10:16|And other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere]].

paras.t: Accepit autem Deus Christum, pascere, id est ut pasceret, Jacob servum suum, id est populum christianum vitia conculcantem; et Israel hereditatem suam, id est eumdem populum spiritualia contemplantem, et ad vitam æternam electum. Et pavit eos Christus in mundo corporaliter vivens, scientia et doctrina: et hoc, in innocentia cordis sui, quoniam ipse iniquitatem non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus, sicut in Isaia legitur. Et in intellectibus manuum suarum deduxit eos. Ipse nempe est virtus et sapientia Patris, qui de se ipso discipulis dixit: Vos vocatis me, Magister et Domine; et bene dicitis: […] sum etenim. Et iterum: Nolite, ait, vocari Rabbi: unus est enim magister vester, Christus; omnes autem vos fratres estis. Christus ergo deduxit oves suas in intellectibus manuum suarum, id est in doctrina et sanctitate, quoniam cœpit facere et docere. Pascit autem, deducitque Christus oves suas per se ipsum, per vicarios suos, Ecclesiarum prælatos et prædicatores, per angelos sanctos. Ipse enim solus gratiam influit; angeli vero nos ad eam disponunt, nosque illuminant: quod etiam homines facere possunt, quemadmodum Paulus ad Corinthios loquitur: Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit, Deus autem incrementum dedit.
paras.en: And God took Christ [[77:71|To feed|pascere]], that is, that he might feed, [[77:71|Jacob his servant|Jacob servum suum]], that is, the Christian people trampling on vices [Jacob means *supplanter*]; [[77:71|and Israel his inheritance|et Israel hereditatem suam]], that is, the same people contemplating spiritual things [Israel is interpreted *a man seeing God*], and chosen for eternal life. [[77:72|And he fed them|Et pavit eos]], Christ did, living bodily in the world, with knowledge and teaching: and this [[77:72|in the innocence of his heart|in innocentia cordis sui]], since he [[Is 53:9|hath done no iniquity|iniquitatem non fecit]], [[1 Pet 2:22|neither was guile found in his mouth|nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus]], as we read in Isaias [Denis's words are partly those of 1 Pet 2:22, which the margin also gives]. [[77:72|and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands|Et in intellectibus manuum suarum deduxit eos]] [*in intellectibus*, literally "in the understandings"]. For he is the power and the wisdom of the Father, who said of himself to the disciples: [[John 13:13|You call me Master and Lord. And you say well|Vos vocatis me, Magister et Domine; et bene dicitis]]: […] [[John 13:13|for so I am|sum etenim]]. And again: [[Matt 23:8|be not you|Nolite]], he says, [[Matt 23:8|called Rabbi|vocari Rabbi]]: [[Matt 23:8|For one is your master|unus est enim magister vester]], Christ [Denis adds *Christus* from Matt 23:10]; [[Matt 23:8|and all you are brethren|omnes autem vos fratres estis]]. Christ therefore conducted his sheep by the skilfulness of his hands, that is, in teaching and holiness, since he [[Acts 1:1|began to do and to teach|cœpit facere et docere]]. And Christ feeds and conducts his sheep through himself, through his vicars, the prelates and preachers of the Churches, and through the holy angels. For he alone pours in grace; but the angels dispose us to it and enlighten us: which men also can do, as Paul says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 3:6|I have planted, Apollo watered: but God gave the increase|Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit, Deus autem incrementum dedit]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum prolixum audivimus, in superficie planum, in interioribus suis mysteriis plenum: quem expedit prompte intelligere, quoniam compendiose includit quæ in diversis libris Moysis dispendiose tractantur. Ceterum, nunc omissa, præcedenti expositione vel plane omnia patescunt, vel de facili intelligi queunt.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a long psalm, plain on the surface, full of mysteries within: which it profits us to understand readily, since it contains in brief what is treated at length in the various books of Moses. As for what has now been passed over, by the preceding exposition it is all either plain or easily understood.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, qui omnium misereris, et lapsos ad te redeuntes paterna pietate suscipere non desinis: recordare, quæsumus, quia caro sumus, et abunda ut avertas iram, et non accendas contra nos omnem iram tuam; sed mitiga eam, et largire nobis indeficientem gratiam tuam.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, who hast mercy on all, and never ceasest to receive with fatherly kindness the fallen who return to thee: remember, we beseech thee, that we are flesh, and abound so as to turn away thy anger, and kindle not against us all thy wrath; but soften it, and bestow on us thy unfailing grace.

78.title: ELUCIDATIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI OCTAVI : DEUS, VENERUNT GENTES.
78.title_en: Literal explanation of the seventy-eighth psalm: O God, the heathens are come.

paras.t: Sensus tituli psalmi jam declarandi, videlicet, Psalmus Asaph, ex præcedentibus clarus est.
paras.en: The sense of the title of the psalm now to be explained, namely, [[78:1|A psalm for Asaph|Psalmus Asaph]], is clear from what has gone before.

paras.t: Advertendum vero, quod ter leguntur Judæi repulsi, loquendo de repulsione eorum graviori et magis famosa : quarum prima facta est per Chaldæos, secunda per Antiochum regem, tertia per Romanos. Quod autem hic psalmus scriptus non sit de repulsione eorum per Romanos inducta, Augustinus in expositione psalmi hujus satis ostendit. Illis namque non convenit, quod in secundo versu psalmi istius habetur, videlicet, Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum escas volatilibus cœli, carnes sanctorum tuorum bestiis terræ. Erant enim Judæi a Romanis occisi, infideles, obstinati ac reprobi. Cassiodorus ergo et Hugo exponunt hunc psalmum de oppressione Judæorum ab Antiocho introducta. Sed istud Nicolao de Lyra non placet, propter id quod in fine primi versus hujus psalmi habetur, Posuerunt Jerusalem in pomorum custodiam : loco cujus habet Hebraica veritas, Posuerunt Jerusalem in acervum ; translatio quoque Hieronymi, Posuerunt Jerusalem in acervis lapidum. Per quod designari videtur destructio civitatis et templi : quæ ab Antiocho facta non invenitur ; sed polluit templum, statuendo in eo idolum abominandum. Verumtamen ista objectio facillime solvitur. Nam civitas et templum destructa dicuntur, vel propter occisionem populi et sacerdotum, vel propter destructionem quarumdam partium civitatis Jerusalem : quæ tempore Antiochi maxime impugnata est, partimque destructa, ut patet in libris Machabæorum. Ubertim enim in divinis Scripturis per habitatores intelliguntur habitacula, et per partem totum exprimitur. Non ergo oportet hunc psalmum ad litteram dumtaxat intelligi de Judæorum dejectione, et templi ac civitatis destructione, factis tempore Chaldæorum. Mihi quoque videtur, quod de utraque eorum devastatione apte ac litteraliter possit intelligi, quoniam ad utramque littera facile applicatur ; et sicut unam, sic et aliam credere possumus sancto Prophetæ divinitus fuisse revelatam, ac per hoc de utraque simul prophetat. Nam qua ratione dicitur vaticinatus in psalmo præsenti de una, dici potest prophetasse de alia.
paras.en: But it should be noted that the Jews are read to have been cast off three times, speaking of their heavier and more famous casting-off: the first of these was by the Chaldeans, the second by king Antiochus, the third by the Romans. That this psalm was not written of their casting-off brought about by the Romans, Augustine shows well enough in his exposition of this psalm. For what is said in the second verse of this psalm does not fit them, namely: [[78:2|They have given the dead bodies of thy servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: the flesh of thy saints for the beasts of the earth|Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum escas volatilibus cœli, carnes sanctorum tuorum bestiis terræ]]. For the Jews slain by the Romans were unbelievers, obstinate and reprobate. Cassiodorus, therefore, and Hugh expound this psalm of the oppression of the Jews brought about by Antiochus. But this does not please Nicholas of Lyra, because of what is said at the end of the first verse of this psalm, [[78:1|they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit|Posuerunt Jerusalem in pomorum custodiam]]: in place of which the Hebrew truth [that is, the Hebrew original] has, They have made Jerusalem a heap; and Jerome's translation too, They have made Jerusalem into heaps of stones. By this the destruction of the city and of the temple seems to be signified: which is not found to have been done by Antiochus; rather, he defiled the temple, setting up in it the abominable idol[[1 Mach 1:57||]]. Yet this objection is very easily answered. For the city and the temple are said to have been destroyed either because of the slaughter of the people and of the priests, or because of the destruction of certain parts of the city of Jerusalem, which in the time of Antiochus was most fiercely attacked, and in part destroyed, as appears in the books of Machabees. For in the divine Scriptures the dwellings are often meant by the inhabitants, and the whole is expressed by a part. So we need not understand this psalm, according to the letter, solely of the overthrow of the Jews and the destruction of the temple and of the city that came about in the time of the Chaldeans. To me, too, it seems that it can fitly and literally be understood of both their devastations, since the letter is easily applied to either; and as we can believe that the one was revealed by God to the holy Prophet, so we can believe the other was too; and so he prophesies of both at once. For by whatever reason he is said to have foretold the one in the present psalm, he can be said to have prophesied of the other.

paras.t: Ait ergo Propheta in persona congregationis fidelium : Deus, venerunt gentes, videlicet Babylonii et Antiochus cum suis, in hereditatem tuam, id est in Judæam, quæ erat terra divino cultui præelecta, et filiis Israel a Deo specialiter atque hereditarie condonata. Vel, In hereditatem tuam, id est in populum Judæorum. Unde per Isaiam Dominus ait : Benedictus populus meus Ægypti, et opus manuum mearum Assyrius ; hereditas autem mea Israel. Polluerunt templum sanctum tuum. Nam Chaldæi polluerunt et destruxerunt templum a Salomone constructum ; Antiochus vero cum suis, polluit templum a Zorobabel et populo a captivitate Babylonica redeunte ædificatum. Dicuntur autem hi templum polluisse, quia fecerunt in eo quæ erant per legem prohibita, ponendo in eo idola, vel gentes introducendo in ipsum. Unde Jeremias : Vidit (inquit) gentes ingressas in sanctuarium tuum, de quibus præceperas ne ingrederentur in ecclesiam. De hac pollutione templi, primo libro Machabæorum scriptum est : Accepit Antiochus altare aureum et omnia vasa ejus, et comminuit omnia. Rursusque : Ædificavit Antiochus rex abominandum idolum desolationis super altare Dei : nempe (ut alibi dicitur) posuit in templo statuam Jovis.
paras.en: The Prophet therefore says, in the person of the congregation of the faithful: [[78:1|O God, the heathens are come|Deus, venerunt gentes]], namely the Babylonians, and Antiochus with his men, [[78:1|into thy inheritance|in hereditatem tuam]], that is, into Judea, which was the land chosen out for the worship of God, and given by God to the children of Israel in a special way and as an inheritance. Or, [[78:1|into thy inheritance|In hereditatem tuam]], that is, into the Jewish people. Hence the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 19:25|Blessed be my people of Egypt, and the work of my hands to the Assyrian: but Israel is my inheritance|Benedictus populus meus Ægypti, et opus manuum mearum Assyrius ; hereditas autem mea Israel]]. [[78:1|they have defiled thy holy temple|Polluerunt templum sanctum tuum]]. For the Chaldeans defiled and destroyed the temple built by Solomon[[4 Kings 25:9||]]; but Antiochus with his men defiled the temple built by Zorobabel and by the people returning from the Babylonian captivity[[1 Mach 1:57||]]. And these are said to have defiled the temple because they did in it things forbidden by the law, setting up idols in it, or bringing the Gentiles into it. Hence Jeremias: [[Lam 1:10|she hath seen|Vidit]], he says, [[Lam 1:10|the Gentiles enter into her sanctuary, of whom thou gavest commandment that they should not enter into thy church|gentes ingressas in sanctuarium tuum, de quibus præceperas ne ingrederentur in ecclesiam]]. Of this defiling of the temple it is written in the first book of Machabees: Antiochus [[1 Mach 1:23|took away the golden altar|Accepit Antiochus altare aureum]], and [[1 Mach 1:23|all the vessels thereof|omnia vasa ejus]], [[1 Mach 1:23|and he broke them all in pieces|et comminuit omnia]]. And again: [[1 Mach 1:57|king Antiochus set up the abominable idol of desolation upon the altar of God|Ædificavit Antiochus rex abominandum idolum desolationis super altare Dei]]: that is (as is said elsewhere), he set up in the temple a statue of Jupiter[[2 Mach 6:2||]].

paras.t: Posuerunt Jerusalem, id est domos ejus ac templum, in pomorum custodiam, id est, tam vilem eam reputaverunt, sicut reputatur domuncula in qua custodiuntur poma. Vel, In pomorum custodiam : quia sicut custodia pomorum, id est domus in qua poma servantur, relinquitur atque destruitur pomis sublatis, sic isti civitatem Jerusalem destruxerunt, et eam a propriis incolis relinqui fecerunt. Propter quod in primo libro Machabæorum legitur : Misit rex principem tributorum ; et accepit spolia civitatis, et succendit eam igni, et destruxit domos ejus et muros ejus in circuitu. Ex quo constat, objectionem Nicolai prætactam, nullam esse. Et iterum ait Scriptura loco præallegato : Fugerunt habitatores Jerusalem propter eos, et facta est habitatio exterorum. Unde et Isaias : Relinquetur, inquit, filia Sion velut umbraculum in vinea, et sicut tugurium in cucumerario.
paras.en: [[78:1|they have made Jerusalem|Posuerunt Jerusalem]], that is, its houses and the temple, [[78:1|as a place to keep fruit|in pomorum custodiam]]: that is, they held it as cheap as one holds the little hut in which fruit is kept. Or, [[78:1|as a place to keep fruit|In pomorum custodiam]]: because, as the keeping-place of fruit, that is, the house in which fruit is stored, is abandoned and pulled down once the fruit has been taken away, so these men destroyed the city of Jerusalem, and made its own inhabitants abandon it. For which reason we read in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 1:30|the king sent the chief collector of his tributes|Misit rex principem tributorum]]; and [[1 Mach 1:33|he took the spoils of the city, and burnt it with fire, and threw down the houses thereof, and the walls thereof round about|accepit spolia civitatis, et succendit eam igni, et destruxit domos ejus et muros ejus in circuitu]]. From this it is plain that the objection of Nicholas touched on above is of no weight. And again Scripture says in the place cited before: [[1 Mach 1:40|the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled away by reason of them and the city was made the habitation of strangers|Fugerunt habitatores Jerusalem propter eos, et facta est habitatio exterorum]]. Hence Isaias too: [[Is 1:8|shall be left|Relinquetur]], he says, [[Is 1:8|the daughter of Sion|filia Sion]] [[Is 1:8|as a covert in a vineyard, and as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers|velut umbraculum in vinea, et sicut tugurium in cucumerario]].

paras.t: Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum, id est corpora Judæorum occisa, escas volatilibus cœli ; carnes sanctorum tuorum, id est cadavera meliorum ac perfectiorum famulorum tuorum, dederunt in escam bestiis terræ : non enim sepelierunt ea, sed projecerunt ea ad devorandum avibus cœli et bestiis terræ. Propter quod Jeremias ait de valle filii Ennom : Non vocabitur amplius, Vallis filii Ennom, sed, Vallis occisionis.
paras.en: [[78:2|They have given the dead bodies of thy servants|Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum]], that is, the slain bodies of the Jews, [[78:2|to be meat for the fowls of the air|escas volatilibus cœli]]; [[78:2|the flesh of thy saints|carnes sanctorum tuorum]], that is, the corpses of thy better and more perfect servants, they gave as food [[78:2|for the beasts of the earth|bestiis terræ]]: for they did not bury them, but cast them out to be devoured by the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth. For which reason Jeremias says of the valley of the son of Ennom: [[Jer 7:32|it shall no more be called|Non vocabitur amplius]] [[Jer 7:32|the valley of the son of Ennom: but the valley of slaughter|Vallis filii Ennom, sed, Vallis occisionis]].

paras.t: Effuderunt sanguinem eorum tanquam aquam in circuitu Jerusalem, et non erat qui sepeliret. Propter quod libro primo Machabæorum habetur : Effuderunt sanguinem innocentem per circuitum sanctificationis. Et non erat qui sepeliret occisos, præ multitudine corporum occisorum. Nam sicut secundo libro Machabæorum habetur, Erant in toto triduo octoginta millia occisi ab Antiocho.
paras.en: [[78:3|They have poured out their blood as water, round about Jerusalem and there was none to bury them|Effuderunt sanguinem eorum tanquam aquam in circuitu Jerusalem, et non erat qui sepeliret]]. For which reason we have in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 1:39|they shed innocent blood round about the sanctuary|Effuderunt sanguinem innocentem per circuitum sanctificationis]].
