Arbusta sunt, quæ juxta arborem nasci solent : per quæ hoc loco intelliguntur augmenta seu excrementa vineæ, videlicet posteri Patriarcharum patrumque filii, quorum adoptionis gratiæ atque imperii dignitas tanta fuit, ut cedros Dei, id est excellentes valde personas, excellant. Ex Patriarchis enim et populo ex Ægypto translato, orti sunt sanctissimi et maximi reges, Prophetæ, sacerdotes, et alii multi altissimæ gratiæ homines.
paras.en: [[79:11|and the branches thereof the cedars of God|Et arbusta ejus cedros Dei]]. *Arbusta* [shrubs or bushes; the Douay-Rheims has 'branches'] are the plants that usually spring up beside a tree: by them are understood in this place the increase or outgrowth of the vineyard, namely the descendants of the Patriarchs and the sons of the fathers, whose grace of adoption and dignity of rule was so great that they excel [[79:11|the cedars of God|cedros Dei]], that is, very excellent persons. For from the Patriarchs and from the people brought out of Egypt there sprang most holy and very great kings, Prophets, priests, and many other men of the highest grace.

paras.t: Qui autem vineam istam omnino ad litteram vellet exponere, hunc quoque versiculum posset corporaliter explanare. Operuit montes umbra ejus : id est, ædificia, turres, domus et muri populi Judæorum tam alte erant constructa, quod propter eorum sublimitatem montes terræ Israel, quæ montuosa est, radiis solis privabantur, sicque umbram patiebantur. Et prope Jerusalem in gyro montes fuerunt, quos certum est sole oriente umbram sustinuisse ad tempus, ex uno latere urbis, propter altitudinem ædificiorum ipsius. Unde de Josaphat dicitur, quod ædificavit in Jerusalem domos in modum turrium altas. Et arbusta ejus, id est tuguria juxta ædificia sita, vel arborum excrementa, operuerunt propter suam altitudinem cedros Dei, id est cedros terræ promissionis : quæ dicuntur cedri Dei, quia fuerunt cedri terræ divinitus præelectæ.
paras.en: But one who wished to expound this vineyard wholly according to the letter could explain this little verse too in a bodily sense. [[79:11|The shadow of it covered the hills|Operuit montes umbra ejus]]: that is, the buildings, towers, houses and walls of the Jewish people were built so high that because of their height the hills of the land of Israel, which is mountainous, were deprived of the sun's rays, and so lay in shadow. And round about Jerusalem there were hills which, it is certain, lay for a time in shadow at sunrise on one side of the city, because of the height of its buildings. Hence it is said of Josaphat that he built in Jerusalem houses high in the manner of towers[[2 Par 17:12||]] [the text of Paralipomenon has 'in Juda']. [[79:11|and the branches thereof|Et arbusta ejus]], that is, the huts set beside the buildings, or the outgrowths of the trees, because of their height covered [[79:11|the cedars of God|cedros Dei]], that is, the cedars of the land of promise, which are called cedars of God because they were the cedars of a land chosen beforehand by God.

paras.t: Descripta altitudine vineæ hujus, describitur latitudo ipsius dum subditur: Extendit palmites suos usque ad mare : id est, vinea seu populus Judæorum filios genuit, quorum habitatio protensa est usque ad mare Mediterraneum; extendit et usque ad flumen magnum Euphraten propagines, id est generationes suas : et ita possederunt filii Israel omnem terram sibi promissam, multiplicatique sunt in ea a termino uno usque ad terminum alium.
paras.en: Having described the height of this vineyard, he describes its breadth, adding: [[79:12|It stretched forth its branches unto the sea|Extendit palmites suos usque ad mare]]: that is, the vineyard or people of the Jews begot sons whose dwelling reached as far as the Mediterranean Sea; it stretched forth also [[79:12|unto the river|usque ad flumen]], the great Euphrates, [[79:12|its boughs|propagines]], that is, its generations: and so the children of Israel possessed all the land promised them, and were multiplied in it from one border to the other.

paras.t: Quum ergo, o Domine, tanta bona præstiteris olim vineæ huic, Ut quid postmodum destruxisti, id est abstulisti, maceriam ejus, id est sepem, parietem, seu protectionem, subtrahendo ei tuum auxilium, angelicamque defensionem? Quibus destituta, in idololatriam et alia multa facinora lapsa est, promeruitque quod sequitur : et vindemiant, id est, vastant, conculcant et destruunt eam omnes qui prætergrediuntur viam, id est omnes nationes gentilium, in circuitu ejus et procul manentes. Porro hoc modo destructurum se esse maceriam vineæ hujus, per Isaiam Dominus prædixit : Ostendam, inquiens, vobis quid faciam vineæ meæ : auferam sepem ejus, et erit in conculcationem. Quod et factum ostendit apud Jeremiam : Pastores multi demoliti sunt vineam meam. Unde et primo Machabæorum inducitur : Quæ gens non hereditavit regnum ejus, et non obtinuit spolia ejus?
paras.en: Since then, O Lord, thou didst once bestow such great goods on this vineyard, [[79:13|Why|Ut quid]] afterwards [[79:13|hast thou broken down|destruxisti]], that is, taken away, [[79:13|the hedge thereof|maceriam ejus]], that is, its fence, its wall, or its protection, by withdrawing from it thy help and the defence of the angels? Stripped of these, it fell into idolatry and many other crimes, and deserved what follows: [[79:13|do pluck|et vindemiant]], that is, lay waste, trample down and destroy it, [[79:13|all they who pass by the way|omnes qui prætergrediuntur viam]], that is, all the nations of the gentiles, round about it and dwelling far off. Moreover, that he would break down the hedge of this vineyard in this way, the Lord foretold through Isaias: [[Is 5:5|I will shew|Ostendam]], he says, [[Is 5:5|you what I will do to my vineyard. I will take away the hedge thereof|vobis quid faciam vineæ meæ : auferam sepem ejus]], [[Is 5:5|and it shall be trodden down|et erit in conculcationem]]. And that it was done he shows in Jeremias: [[Jer 12:10|Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard|Pastores multi demoliti sunt vineam meam]]. Hence too it is brought in in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 2:10|What nation hath not inherited her kingdom, and gotten of her spoils?|Quæ gens non hereditavit regnum ejus, et non obtinuit spolia ejus?]]

paras.t: Exterminavit eam aper de silva, et singularis ferus depastus est eam. Quidam Cassiodorum imitantes, per aprum intelligunt Vespasianum; per singularem vero ferum, filium ejus Titum : sed non videtur. Nam populus Judæorum tempore devastationis suæ sibi a Vespasiano et Tito inductæ, nullo modo erat vinea Domini, quia nec Deus coluit eam per gratiam, nec ipsa coluit Deum per fidem : sed erat populus ille pro tunc, sicut et nunc, omnino infidelis et reprobus ; habuitque veritatem in eis, quod ait Joannes in Apocalypsi, Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt, sed sunt synagoga Satanæ. Aptius ergo per aprum et singularem ferum, accipimus eumdem tyrannum, sive ille dicatur fuisse Nabuchodonosor, sive Antiochus. Horum namque uterque exterminavit, id est extra proprios terminos posuit, populum istum, ædificia ejus destruendo, et habitatores transferendo seu effugando : sicut de Juda Machabæo et fratribus ejus legitur, quod inter feras in desertis locis morabantur. Et hic singularis ferus depastus est vineam istam, populum hunc terribiliter trucidando. Judæi autem in sua perfidia indurati, per aprum singularemque ferum intelligunt Titum seu Vespasianum.
paras.en: [[79:14|The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste|Exterminavit eam aper de silva]], [[79:14|and a singular wild beast hath devoured it|et singularis ferus depastus est eam]]. Some, following Cassiodorus, understand by the boar Vespasian, and by the singular wild beast his son Titus; but this does not seem right. For at the time of the devastation brought upon it by Vespasian and Titus, the people of the Jews was in no way the vineyard of the Lord, since neither did God tend it by grace, nor did it worship God by faith [the Latin uses one verb, *colere*, for both: to tend a vine and to worship]; but that people was then, as it is now, wholly unbelieving and reprobate, and in them was verified what John says in the Apocalypse of those [[Apoc 2:9|that say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan|Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt, sed sunt synagoga Satanæ]]. It is more fitting, then, to take the boar and the singular wild beast as one and the same tyrant, whether he be said to have been Nabuchodonosor or Antiochus. For each of them laid this people waste, that is, put it outside its own borders [a play on *exterminare*, from *ex* and *terminus*, a border], by destroying its buildings and carrying away or putting to flight its inhabitants; as we read of Judas Machabeus and his brethren, that they lived among wild beasts in desert places[[2 Mach 5:27||]]. And this singular wild beast devoured this vineyard, slaughtering this people terribly. But the Jews, hardened in their unbelief, understand by the boar and the singular wild beast Titus or Vespasian.

paras.t: Hæc vero, quæ de Synagoga sub nomine vineæ dicta sunt, de Ecclesia Christi mystice accipi possunt hoc modo : Vineam, id est militantem Ecclesiam seu populum christianum, de Ægypto, id est de sæculo isto tenebroso, transtulisti in regnum Christi, ut essent Christiani tui heredes, et Christi coheredes. Propter quod ait Apostolus : Deus eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam, et transtulit nos in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ. Ejecisti gentes, id est, gentiles commutasti in melius, convertendo eos ad fidem, et converti nolentes fecisti deficere ; et plantasti eam, id est, populum christianum habitare fecisti in locis et terris, in quibus gentiles olim morati sunt : vel, Plantasti eam in Christo per fidem et caritatem.
paras.en: Now what has been said of the Synagogue under the name of the vineyard may be taken mystically of the Church of Christ, in this way: [[79:9|a vineyard|Vineam]], that is, the Church militant or the Christian people, [[79:9|out of Egypt|de Ægypto]], that is, out of this dark world, [[79:9|thou hast brought|transtulisti]] into the kingdom of Christ, that Christians might be thy heirs and joint heirs of Christ[[Rom 8:17||]]. For this reason the Apostle says that God has snatched us [[Gal 1:4|from this present wicked world|de præsenti sæculo nequam]], and [[Col 1:13|hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love|transtulit nos in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ]]. [[79:9|thou hast cast out the Gentiles|Ejecisti gentes]], that is, thou hast changed the gentiles for the better by converting them to the faith, and those unwilling to be converted thou hast made to fail; [[79:9|and planted it|et plantasti eam]], that is, thou hast made the Christian people dwell in the places and lands where the gentiles once lived: or, Thou hast planted it in Christ through faith and charity.

paras.t: Dux itineris fuisti in conspectu ejus : quia Apostolos per totum mundum duxisti, et omnes electos per gratiam ad te ipsum omnium rerum ultimum finem perducis, quemadmodum protestaris : Ego sum via, veritas, et vita. Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me. Et iterum : Non relinquam vos orphanos ; vado et venio ad vos. Et plantasti radices ejus : id est, primos Ecclesiæ principes, aliorum utique spirituales genitores, videlicet Apostolos et eorum præcipue sectatores, ut erant Dionysius, Polycarpus, Ignatius, in Christo inconcusse corroborasti, ita ut possent ipsi alios in Christo fundare, sicut fundatur palmes in vite. Nam et Christus ait : Ego sum vitis vera, vos palmites. Et implevit terram : quia Ecclesia per universum orbem diffusa est. Unde scriptum est in Isaia : Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebunt faciem orbis semine. Quod exponi non potest de carnali generatione et multiplicatione Judæorum, sed de spirituali generatione Apostolorum, ex populo Israel prodeuntium, et multiplicatione fidelium, qui sunt semen Apostolorum.
paras.en: [[79:10|Thou wast the guide of its journey in its sight|Dux itineris fuisti in conspectu ejus]]: because thou didst lead the Apostles through the whole world, and dost lead all the elect by grace to thyself, the last end of all things, as thou declarest: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me|Ego sum via, veritas, et vita. Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me]]. And again: [[John 14:18|I will not leave you orphans|Non relinquam vos orphanos]]; [[John 14:28|I go away, and I come unto you|vado et venio ad vos]]. [[79:10|thou plantedst the roots thereof|Et plantasti radices ejus]]: that is, the first princes of the Church, the spiritual begetters of the rest, namely the Apostles and above all their followers, such as Dionysius, Polycarp and Ignatius, thou didst make unshakeably strong in Christ, so that they in turn could ground others in Christ, as the branch is grounded in the vine. For Christ too says: [[John 15:1|I am the true vine|Ego sum vitis vera]], [[John 15:5|you the branches|vos palmites]]. [[79:10|and it filled the land|Et implevit terram]]: because the Church is spread throughout the whole world. Hence it is written in Isaias: [[Is 27:6|Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed|Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebunt faciem orbis semine]]. This cannot be expounded of the carnal begetting and multiplying of the Jews, but of the spiritual begetting of the Apostles, who came forth from the people of Israel, and of the multiplying of the faithful, who are the seed of the Apostles.

paras.t: Operuit montes umbra ejus : id est, electio Christianorum omnem altitudinem gratiæ aliis datæ excessit. Nam et Apostoli secure præferuntur Prophetis, et Ecclesia Synagogæ. Et arbusta ejus, cedros Dei: quoniam gratia major effusa est in communem populum christianum, quam olim in homines Dei sublimes.
paras.en: [[79:11|The shadow of it covered the hills|Operuit montes umbra ejus]]: that is, the election of Christians surpassed all the height of grace given to others. For the Apostles are with sure right set above the Prophets, and the Church above the Synagogue. [[79:11|and the branches thereof the cedars of God|Et arbusta ejus, cedros Dei]]: since greater grace has been poured out on the common Christian people than once on the exalted men of God.

paras.t: Extendit Ecclesia palmites suos, id est filios suos, usque ad mare occidentale a mari orientali, quemadmodum de Christo alibi habetur : Potestas ejus a mari usque ad mare. Et usque ad flumen, id est fontem Baptismi, extendit propagines suas : quoniam quotquot gignit Ecclesia, omnes intingit Baptismatis aqua, sicut Salvator præcepit Apostolis : Docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, et Filii, et Spiritus Sancti. Propter quod Petrus propagini, quam in exordio suæ prædicationis in Christo produxit, dixisse scribitur : Baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Christi, in remissionem peccatorum vestrorum.
paras.en: The Church [[79:12|stretched forth|Extendit]] [[79:12|its branches|palmites suos]], that is, its sons, [[79:12|unto the sea|usque ad mare]], the western sea, from the eastern sea, as is said elsewhere of Christ: [[Zach 9:10|his power shall be from sea to sea|Potestas ejus a mari usque ad mare]]. [[79:12|unto the river|Et usque ad flumen]], that is, the font of Baptism, it stretched forth [[79:12|its boughs|propagines]]: since all whom the Church begets she dips in the water of Baptism, as the Saviour commanded the Apostles: [[Matt 28:19|teach ye all nations: baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost|Docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, et Filii, et Spiritus Sancti]]. For this reason Peter is written to have said to the offshoot [*propago*, the psalm's word for 'boughs'] which he brought forth in Christ at the beginning of his preaching: [[Acts 2:38|be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ, for the remission of your sins|Baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Christi, in remissionem peccatorum vestrorum]] [Denis reads 'in the name of Christ'].

paras.t: Ut quid destruxisti maceriam ejus? id est, cur permisisti Ecclesiam ita deficere, tuo auxilio ei subtracto ? Et vindemiant eam, id est, spiritualibus bonis eam spoliant, omnes qui prætergrediuntur viam, id est, qui mandatorum tuorum semitas transgrediuntur, videlicet dæmones, hominesque perversi. Exterminavit eam aper de silva, id est, Mahometus Sarracenorum legislator, cujus populus Ecclesiam Jerosolymorum subvertit. Et singularis ferus depastus est eam. Per hunc singularem ferum, intelligi potest ipse Mahometus, seu quilibet crudelis tyrannus aut hæresiarcha.
paras.en: [[79:13|Why hast thou broken down the hedge thereof|Ut quid destruxisti maceriam ejus]]? that is, why hast thou let the Church fail so, withdrawing thy help from her? [[79:13|do pluck it|Et vindemiant eam]], that is, strip her of spiritual goods, [[79:13|all they who pass by the way|omnes qui prætergrediuntur viam]], that is, those who pass beyond the paths of thy commandments, namely the demons and perverse men. [[79:14|The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste|Exterminavit eam aper de silva]], that is, Mahomet, the lawgiver of the Saracens, whose people overthrew the Church of Jerusalem. [[79:14|and a singular wild beast hath devoured it|Et singularis ferus depastus est eam]]. By this singular wild beast may be understood Mahomet himself, or any cruel tyrant or heresiarch.

paras.t: Deus virtutum, convertere, id est, te ipsum ad nos clementer converte, quemadmodum testatus es : Convertimini ad me, ait Dominus exercituum, et convertar ad vos. Respice de cœlo, oculo pietatis tuæ immensæ, et vide indigentiam nostram; et visita in propria persona vineam istam, id est Ecclesiam tuam ; visita quoque corda humana quotidie per gratiæ infusionem, et spiritualium bonorum augmentum.
paras.en: [[79:15|Turn again, O God of hosts|Deus virtutum, convertere]], that is, turn thyself mercifully to us, as thou hast declared: [[Zach 1:3|Turn ye to me, saith the Lord of hosts: and I will turn to you|Convertimini ad me, ait Dominus exercituum, et convertar ad vos]]. [[79:15|look down from heaven|Respice de cœlo]] with the eye of thy boundless pity, [[79:15|and see|et vide]] our need; [[79:15|and visit|et visita]] in thine own person [[79:15|this vineyard|vineam istam]], that is, thy Church; visit also human hearts daily by the pouring in of grace and the increase of spiritual goods.

paras.t: Et perfice eam, scilicet Ecclesiam, dando ei spiritualem profectum et evangelica consilia, quibus perficiuntur præcepta ; quam plantavit in fide et individua caritate, dextera tua, id est misericordia tua, seu potentia tua benigna. Christus enim stabilivit Ecclesiam suam in terra. Specialiter autem vide et super filium hominis, id est Christum, qui se ipsum in Evangelio sæpe appellat hominis Filium, in cujus figura Ezechiel tam frequenter dictus est filius hominis ; quem Christum confirmasti tibi, id est, inseparabiliter tuæ divinitati conjunxisti, tam secundum unionem personalem, quam secundum unionem fruitivam. Et ita Christus homo peccare non potuit, nec aliquo modo separari a Deo : nam et in triduo mortis, corpus ejus et anima Verbo manserunt unita. Vel, Super Filium tuum dilectum Dominum Jesum, quem confirmasti tibi, id est, quem firmiter testatus es esse Filium tuum, confirmando eum tibi in conspectu hominum, dicendo ad eum tam in baptismo quam in monte sancto, Hic est Filius meus carissimus, in quo mihi complacui.
paras.en: [[79:16|And perfect the same|Et perfice eam]], namely the Church, by giving her spiritual progress and the evangelical counsels, by which the precepts are perfected; [[79:16|which thy right hand hath planted|quam plantavit]] in faith and undivided charity: [[79:16|thy right hand|dextera tua]], that is, thy mercy, or thy kindly power. For Christ established his Church on earth. But in particular look [[79:16|and upon the son of man|et super filium hominis]], that is, Christ, who in the Gospel often calls himself the Son of man[[Matt 8:20||]], in whose figure Ezechiel is so often called son of man[[Ezech 2:1||]][[Ezech 2:3||]]; [[79:16|whom|quem]], Christ, [[79:16|thou hast confirmed for thyself|confirmasti tibi]], that is, hast joined inseparably to thy Godhead, both by the personal union and by the union of fruition [that is, the union by which his soul enjoyed the vision of God]. And so Christ as man could not sin, nor be in any way separated from God: for even in the three days of his death his body and soul remained united to the Word. Or: [[79:16|upon|Super]] thy beloved Son, the Lord Jesus, [[79:16|whom thou hast confirmed for thyself|quem confirmasti tibi]], that is, whom thou hast firmly declared to be thy Son, confirming him to thyself in the sight of men, saying to him both at the baptism and on the holy mount: [[Matt 3:17|This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased|Hic est Filius meus carissimus, in quo mihi complacui]][[Matt 17:5||]].

paras.t: Si autem sic feceris, Incensa igni, id est peccata ex igne concupiscentiæ seu flamma inordinati amoris commissa, et suffossa, id est peccata ex timore malo, deprimente et humiliante, provenientia, ab increpatione vultus tui peribunt, id est, in peccatore pœnitente cessabunt per increpationem tui respectus, dum hominem paternaliter increpas, corrigendoque respicis, illuminas, et convertis. In his vero qui in vitiis perseverant, peribunt ista peccata, id est, æternaliter damnabuntur ab increpatione vultus tui, id est a rigore tuæ divinæ justitiæ, quando peccatoribus dices : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Sciendum vero, quod sicut omnia opera meritoria veniunt ex bono amore, aut bono timore, sic omnia opera mala nascuntur aut ex malo amore, aut malo timore. Timor autem ad amorem, sicut ad causam atque radicem reducitur : non enim timemus, nisi cujus oppositum amamus. Idcirco omnia opera bona originaliter ex amore divino procedunt : nam sine caritate nihil est meritorium. Omnia quoque mala ex inordinato amore nascuntur.
paras.en: If thou dost so, [[79:17|Things set on fire|Incensa igni]], that is, sins committed from the fire of concupiscence or the flame of disordered love, [[79:17|and dug down|et suffossa]], that is, sins that arise from evil fear, which presses down and abases, [[79:17|shall perish at the rebuke of thy countenance|ab increpatione vultus tui peribunt]], that is, they will cease in the penitent sinner through the rebuke of thy look, when thou rebukest a man as a father, and in correcting him dost look upon him, enlighten him and convert him. But in those who persevere in vice these sins [[79:17|shall perish|peribunt]], that is, will be damned eternally, [[79:17|at the rebuke of thy countenance|ab increpatione vultus tui]], that is, by the rigour of thy divine justice, when thou shalt say to sinners: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. Now it should be known that, just as all meritorious works come from good love or good fear, so all evil works are born either of evil love or of evil fear. But fear is reduced to love as to its cause and root: for we fear nothing except that whose opposite we love. Therefore all good works proceed in their origin from divine love, for without charity nothing is meritorious; and all evils, too, are born of disordered love.

paras.t: Fiat manus tua, id est divinitatis tuæ potentia, o Deus Pater, super virum dexteræ tuæ, id est super Christum hominem, ita quod tua divinitas ejus humanitati in omnibus cooperetur, et per eam, nostram salutem finaliter operetur: secundum quod ipse Christus ait, Pater in me manens, ipse facit opera ; et super filium hominis, id est Christum filium Deiferæ Virginis, quem confirmasti tibi. Secundum modum expositum, secunda pars exponit priorem. Dicitur autem Christus vir dexteræ Dei : Primo, quoniam favor, amor, gratia et misericordia, et felix Dei præsentia, in omnibus plene ejus humanitatem prævenit, implevit et beatificavit, prout scriptum est : Vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre, plenum gratiæ et veritatis. Secundo, quoniam secundum divinitatem æqualis est Patri : quæ æqualitas nomine dexteræ designatur. Tertio, quoniam sedet ad dexteram Dei Patris, juxta illud : Dominus Jesus assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei.
paras.en: [[79:18|Let thy hand be|Fiat manus tua]], that is, the power of thy Godhead, O God the Father, [[79:18|upon the man of thy right hand|super virum dexteræ tuæ]], that is, upon Christ as man, so that thy Godhead may work together with his manhood in all things, and through it may in the end work our salvation; according to what Christ himself says: [[John 14:10|the Father who abideth in me, he doth the works|Pater in me manens, ipse facit opera]]; [[79:18|and upon the son of man|et super filium hominis]], that is, Christ, the son of the God-bearing Virgin, [[79:18|whom thou hast confirmed for thyself|quem confirmasti tibi]]. In the way it has been expounded, the second part expounds the first. Now Christ is called the man of God's right hand: first, because the favour, love, grace and mercy and the blissful presence of God went before his manhood in all things fully, filled it and made it blessed, as it is written: [[John 1:14|we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father|Vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre]], [[John 1:14|full of grace and truth|plenum gratiæ et veritatis]]. Secondly, because according to his Godhead he is equal to the Father, which equality is signified by the name of the right hand. Thirdly, because he sits at the right hand of God the Father, according to that saying: [[Mark 16:19|the Lord Jesus|Dominus Jesus]] [[Mark 16:19|was taken up into heaven and sitteth on the right hand of God|assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei]].

paras.t: Et non discedimus a te, id est, non cessamus clamare ad te, et invocare præsentiam Christi : idcirco fiducialiter dico, quia vivificabis nos, vita gratiæ in præsenti, et vita gloriæ in futuro, per meritum incarnationis et passionis Domini Salvatoris. Tu enim per Isaiam tuum dixisti : Ego Dominus, super quo non confundentur omnes qui exspectant eum. Et nomen tuum invocabimus, donec æternam beatitudinem impetremus. Non ergo discedamus a Deo, si differat exaudire, sed dicamus cum Job : Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo.
paras.en: [[79:19|And we depart not from thee|Et non discedimus a te]], that is, we cease not to cry to thee and to call upon the presence of Christ: therefore I say with confidence that [[79:19|thou shalt quicken us|vivificabis nos]] with the life of grace in the present and the life of glory in the future, through the merit of the incarnation and passion of the Lord our Saviour. For thou hast said through thy Isaias: [[Is 49:23|I am the Lord, for they shall not be confounded that wait for him|Ego Dominus, super quo non confundentur omnes qui exspectant eum]]. [[79:19|and we will call upon thy name|Et nomen tuum invocabimus]], until we obtain eternal beatitude. Let us not, then, depart from God if he delays to hear us, but let us say with Job: [[Job 13:15|Although he should kill me, I will trust in him|Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo]].

paras.t: Domine, Deus virtutum, converte nos, etc. Ecce jam trina vice versum hunc repetit : quoniam in summæ Trinitatis visione nostra salus consistit; et item ad designandum affectus sui fervorem, hujusque versiculi utilitatem, dulcedinem et virtutem. Est enim hic versus admirabili potestate refertus, quia in eo petitur quod ad nostram salvationem requiritur, etiam eo ordine quo petendum est. Primo enim a Deo convertimur, quia ab eo est omnis boni principium, deinde divinitus illuminamur, et ita deinceps salvi efficimur.
paras.en: [[79:20|O Lord God of hosts, convert us|Domine, Deus virtutum, converte nos]], etc. See, he now repeats this verse for the third time: because our salvation consists in the vision of the most high Trinity; and also to show the fervour of his affection, and the usefulness, sweetness and power of this little verse. For this verse is filled with a wonderful power, since in it is asked what is required for our salvation, and in the very order in which it is to be asked. For first we are converted by God, since from him is the beginning of all good; then we are enlightened by God; and so, in turn, we are saved.

paras.t: Explicari non potest, quanta sit virtus, dignitas atque sententia hujus versus. In eo namque quod dicitur, Domine, Deus virtutum, tangitur divina majestas, quæ est omnium potestatum fontana origo; excitaturque anima nostra ad reverentialem tanti Dominatoris timorem, de quo a Jeremia scriptum est : Magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine. Quis non timebit te, o rex gentium ? In eo quoque quod additur, converte nos, profitemur totam nostram perfectionem et salutem a Deo penitus dependere inchoative, prosecutive et completive, in tantum ut ipsa primordialis nostra conversio, sit Dei largitio. Quod Salomon innuens, sic orat : Sit Dominus Deus noster nobiscum, et inclinet corda nostra ad se, ut ambulemus in omnibus viis ejus. Quod autem prosecutio seu continuatio boni, sit donum Altissimi, David alio loco professus est, dicens : Domine Deus, custodi in æternum hanc voluntatem eorum, et semper in veneratione tui mens ista permaneat.
paras.en: It cannot be told how great are the power, the dignity and the meaning of this verse. For in the words [[79:20|O Lord God of hosts|Domine, Deus virtutum]], the divine majesty is touched upon, which is the fountain-source of all powers; and our soul is stirred to a reverent fear of so great a Lord, of whom it is written by Jeremias: [[Jer 10:6|thou art great, and great is thy name in might|Magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine]]. [[Jer 10:7|Who shall not fear thee, O king of nations?|Quis non timebit te, o rex gentium]] In the words added, [[79:20|convert us|converte nos]], we profess that our whole perfection and salvation depend entirely on God, in their beginning, their continuance and their completion, so much so that our very first conversion is God's gift. Hinting at this, Solomon prays thus: [[3 Kings 8:57|The Lord our God be with us|Sit Dominus Deus noster nobiscum]], and [[3 Kings 8:58|may he incline our hearts to himself, that we may walk in all his ways|inclinet corda nostra ad se, ut ambulemus in omnibus viis ejus]]. And that the continuance or carrying on of good is a gift of the Most High, David professed in another place, saying: [[1 Par 29:18|O Lord God|Domine Deus]], [[1 Par 29:18|keep for ever this will of their heart, and let this mind remain always for the worship of thee|custodi in æternum hanc voluntatem eorum, et semper in veneratione tui mens ista permaneat]] [the margin gives 1 Par. xvii, 18; the words are from 1 Par 29:18].

paras.t: In eo autem quod sequitur, et ostende faciem tuam, accenditur et certe merito incomparabili flamma amoris æstuare debet in nobis divina dilectio. Quid enim tam bonum, quid tam amabile, dulce, pulchrum, salubre, jucundum et nobile, sicut videre faciem Dei? O facies pulchra, o pulchritudo immensa, o felicitas infinita ! Promittitur nobis adspectus faciei Creatoris nostri : sed quis eam videre dignus habebitur, nisi cujus anima fuerit ab omni immunditia depurata? Propterea, Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt. Ecce si Deum diligimus, affectuose dicamus, Ostende faciem tuam : et tanto affectuosius, quanto frequentius. Non enim decet nos, ex frequenti iteratione et longa consuetudine in bono tepescere, pristinam sollicitudinem perdere, aut remissius agere. Qui enim opus Dei non negligenter, sed reverenter exsolvit, quotidie in gratia crescit : sicque de die in diem divinum obsequium perfectius solvit. Indesinenter igitur Dominum deprecemur ut faciem suam nobis ostendat, nunc quidem per fidem illuminatam et gratiæ claritatem, contemplationemque quotidie sinceriorem, in futuro autem per speciem et gloriæ lumen. Tanto demum faciem Dei clarius jucundiusque conspiciemus in præsenti exsilio, futuroque sæculo, quanto nunc affectuosius exoramus hunc versum, qui veraciter inæstimabili dulcedine superexuberat.
paras.en: And in the words that follow, [[79:20|and shew thy face|et ostende faciem tuam]], divine love is kindled in us, and surely it ought rightly to burn in us with an incomparable flame of love. For what is so good, what so lovable, sweet, beautiful, wholesome, delightful and noble, as to see the face of God? O beautiful face, O boundless beauty, O infinite happiness! The sight of the face of our Creator is promised us: but who shall be held worthy to see it, save he whose soul has been cleansed of all uncleanness? Therefore: [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]]. See, if we love God, let us say with affection, [[79:20|shew thy face|Ostende faciem tuam]]; and the more often, the more affectionately. For it does not become us, through frequent repetition and long habit, to grow lukewarm in good, to lose our first care, or to act more slackly. For he who discharges the work of God not negligently but reverently[[Jer 48:10||]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxiii, 10, which does not fit; Denis seems to have in mind Jer 48:10, 'Cursed be he that doth the work of the Lord deceitfully'] grows daily in grace, and so from day to day renders the divine service more perfectly. Let us therefore pray the Lord without ceasing to shew us his face: now by enlightened faith and the clearness of grace and a contemplation purer day by day, and in the future by sight and the light of glory. In short, the more affectionately we now pray this verse, which truly overflows with a sweetness beyond reckoning, the more clearly and joyfully shall we behold the face of God in this present exile and in the world to come.

paras.t: Sed et totus hic psalmus præclarus est nimis ; et liquet in eo, quam vehementissimo desiderio veteres sancti Christi adventum optabant : et turpe est nobis, si ejus incarnationem jam factam, minori dilectionis fervore amplectimur, quam illi futuram desiderabant.
paras.en: But this whole psalm is exceedingly glorious; and it is plain in it with what most vehement desire the holy men of old longed for the coming of Christ: and it is shameful for us if we embrace his incarnation, now accomplished, with less fervour of love than that with which they desired it while it was yet to come.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, Pater virtutum, esto propitius dux itineris recti in conspectu populi, Filii tui sanguine redempti : ut forti a te plantata radice christianæ professionis, impleat terram æternæ repromissionis.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, Father of hosts, be graciously the guide of the right journey in the sight of the people redeemed by the blood of thy Son: that, planted by thee with the strong root of the Christian profession, it may fill the land of the eternal promise.

80.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI: EXSULTATE DEO ADJUTORI NOSTRO.
80.title_en: Exposition of the eightieth psalm: Rejoice to God our helper.

paras.t: Est autem psalmi jam perscrutandi titulus iste : In finem, pro torcularibus, quinta sabbati, psalmus ipsi Asaph. Titulus hic magis pertinere videtur ad mysticam, quam ad litteralem psalmi præsentis explanationem, præsertim quum multa habeantur verba in eo, quæ nec in Hebræo ponuntur, nec in titulo Hieronymi juxta Hebræum. Idcirco in sequenti explanatione, in qua psalmus iste spiritualiter exponetur, præinductus quoque titulus correspondenter explanabitur. Porro Hieronymus, in translatione sua juxta Hebræum, talem titulum ponit : Victori in torcularibus, Asaph. Pro cujus intellectu habendo, pensandum quod psalmus iste specialiter erat decantandus in festo Tubarum, quod fuit primo die Septembris : circa quod tempus solent esse completæ vindemiæ in terra promissionis, quoniam calida est : idcirco tunc fiebant libamina sacrificiorum in templo. Et ergo hic psalmus titulum sortitur a torcularibus, unde vina exprimuntur, quia in eo redditur Deo gratiarum actio pro fructibus anni collectis.
paras.en: Now the title of the psalm now to be examined is this: [[80:1|Unto the end, for the winepresses|In finem, pro torcularibus]], on the fifth day of the week [these words, from the Septuagint, are not in the Clementine Vulgate or the Douay-Rheims], [[80:1|a psalm for Asaph himself|psalmus ipsi Asaph]]. This title seems to belong more to the mystical than to the literal explanation of the present psalm, especially since it contains many words that are neither in the Hebrew nor in Jerome's title according to the Hebrew. Therefore in the following explanation, in which this psalm will be expounded spiritually, the title given above will also be explained accordingly. Jerome, in his translation according to the Hebrew, gives this title: To the victor, upon the winepresses, of Asaph. To understand this, we must consider that this psalm was to be sung especially on the feast of Trumpets, which was on the first day of September; about that time the vintage is usually finished in the land of promise, since it is a hot land, and so the libations of the sacrifices were then made in the temple. And so this psalm takes its title from the winepresses, in which wine is pressed out, because in it thanks are rendered to God for the fruits of the year that have been gathered in.

paras.t: Ait ergo : Exsultate Deo adjutori nostro : id est, ad gloriam et honorem ac laudem Dei, nos in omni bono adjuvantis per gratiam suam, tam cordialiter ac vehementer gaudete in eo, ut ex abundantia interioris lætitiæ, foris erumpant signa gaudii interioris. Dicitur enim exsultatio, quasi extra se saltatio, puta dum ex plenitudine gaudii interioris, extra manifestantur ejus indicia. Jubilate Deo Jacob, id est, ineffabiliter intus gaudete, et foris affectuosissima laude Deo cantate. Est enim jubilus gaudium animi, quod præ vehementi excessu nec integre valet explicari, nec in toto taceri. Dicitur autem Deus universorum, specialiter Deus Jacob, propter excellentissimam gratiam sibi collatam. Unde de Deo ait Scriptura : Dedit viam disciplinæ Jacob puero suo.
paras.en: He says, then: [[80:2|Rejoice to God our helper|Exsultate Deo adjutori nostro]]: that is, to the glory, honour and praise of God, who helps us in every good thing by his grace, rejoice in him so heartily and so vehemently that from the abundance of the joy within, signs of that inward joy break out without. For *exsultatio* [rejoicing] is so called as being, as it were, *extra se saltatio*, a leaping out of oneself [Denis's play on the Latin *exsultatio*, from *ex* and *saltare*, to leap], that is, when from the fulness of inward joy its tokens are shown outwardly. [[80:2|Sing aloud to the God of Jacob|Jubilate Deo Jacob]]: that is, rejoice inwardly beyond words, and sing to God outwardly with most loving praise. For *jubilus* [jubilation] is a joy of the soul which, from its vehement excess, can neither be fully expressed nor wholly kept silent. And the God of all things is called especially the God of Jacob on account of the most excellent grace bestowed on him. Hence Scripture says of God: He gave the way of discipline [[Bar 3:37|to Jacob his servant|Jacob puero suo]] [Denis gives Baruch shortly; the verse reads: "He found out all the way of knowledge, and gave it to Jacob his servant"].

paras.t: Sumite psalmum, ut eum Deo devote cantetis, et date tympanum : id est, non tantum voce, sed etiam musico instrumento Deum laudate, et simul cum sono tympani psalmos vocibus decantetis. Solebant enim Hebræi instrumentis musicalibus psalmos cantare, sicut nunc in organis cantat Ecclesia. Sic quoque date psalterium jucundum cum cithara, laudando Deum in talibus instrumentis : secundum quod David instituit.
paras.en: [[80:3|Take a psalm|Sumite psalmum]], to sing it devoutly to God, [[80:3|and bring hither the timbrel|et date tympanum]]: that is, praise God not only with the voice but also with a musical instrument, and sing the psalms with your voices together with the sound of the timbrel. For the Hebrews were wont to sing the psalms with musical instruments, as the Church now sings with organs. So too bring hither [[80:3|the pleasant psaltery with the harp|psalterium jucundum cum cithara]], praising God on such instruments, as David ordained[[1 Par 13:8||]].

paras.t: Buccinate in neomenia, id est in die novilunii, tuba, ad buccinandum formata : quoniam Moyses jussit fieri tubam ad hoc. Judæi autem in omnibus noviluniis agebant festum in memoriam gubernationis divinæ. In novilunio vero septimi mensis communiter occurrebat festum Tubarum, apud Hebræos valde solenne, in memoriam redemptionis Isaac ab immolatione, prout in Levitico legitur. Idcirco nunc subditur : in insigni die solennitatis vestræ, id est in solenni festo Tubarum.
paras.en: [[80:4|Blow up|Buccinate]] [[80:4|on the new moon|in neomenia]], that is, on the day of the new moon, [[80:4|the trumpet|tuba]] made for blowing, since Moses commanded a trumpet to be made for this. Now the Jews kept a feast at every new moon in memory of God's governance. And at the new moon of the seventh month there fell, as a rule, the feast of Trumpets, very solemn among the Hebrews, in memory of the redemption of Isaac from being sacrificed, as is read in Leviticus. Therefore it is now added: [[80:4|on the noted day of your solemnity|in insigni die solennitatis vestræ]], that is, on the solemn feast of Trumpets.

paras.t: Cur autem hæc agere debeant, pandit : Quia præceptum in Israel est, quoniam Dominus jussit sic fieri in populo Israelitico, sicut habetur in libro Numerorum. Et judicium Deo Jacob : id est, istud mandatum est a Deo Jacob, qui hoc justum esse dictavit. Vel sic, Judicium Deo Jacob, id est, judicium damnationis erit Jacob, id est populo ex Jacob nato, a Deo omnium justo judice, si populus iste omiserit istud præceptum implere.
paras.en: Why they ought to do these things he shows: [[80:5|For it is a commandment in Israel|Quia præceptum in Israel est]], since the Lord commanded this to be done so among the people of Israel, as is found in the book of Numbers[[Num 29:1||]]. [[80:5|And a judgment to the God of Jacob|Et judicium Deo Jacob]]: that is, this command is from the God of Jacob, who declared it to be just. Or thus: [[80:5|a judgment to the God of Jacob|Judicium Deo Jacob]], that is, there will be a judgment of damnation for Jacob, that is, for the people born of Jacob, from God, the just judge of all, if this people neglect to fulfil this commandment.

paras.t: Testimonium in Joseph posuit illud : id est, Deus istud præceptum cum attestatione proprii testimonii proposuit Joseph, id est populo Judæorum per Joseph designato, propter hoc quod Jacob primogenita contulit ei, et ipse aliis fratribus suis sanctior atque sublimior fuit. Quum exiret Joseph, id est populus Judæorum, de terra Ægypti per manum Moysis. Linguam quam non noverat audivit, id est, legem divinam a Deo per Moysen sumpsit, quam ante nescivit. Vel hoc ideo dicitur, quoniam populus Judæorum, quum accessisset ad montem Sinai, audivit Deum, vel potius angelum Dei sibi loquentem de medio ignis : propter quod territi, dixerunt ad Moysen : Non loquatur nobis Deus, ne forte moriamur ; sed loquere tu nobis. Propter quod Moyses : Ecce, inquit, ostendit nobis Dominus Deus noster majestatem suam ; et probavimus hodie, quod loquente Deo cum homine vixerit homo ; vocem ejus audivimus de medio ignis. Vel quod dicit, Linguam quam non noverat audivit, forsitan ideo dicit, quoniam filii Israel in Ægypto nati et educati, quum venissent ad terras Amorrhæorum, Madianitarum, Moabitarum, Idumæorum, etc., linguas ignotas audierant.
paras.en: [[80:6|He ordained it for a testimony in Joseph|Testimonium in Joseph posuit illud]]: that is, God set forth this commandment, with the attestation of his own testimony, to Joseph, that is, to the Jewish people, signified by Joseph, because Jacob gave him the birthright[[1 Par 5:1||]] and he was holier and loftier than his other brothers. [[80:6|When he came out|Quum exiret]], Joseph, that is, the Jewish people, [[80:6|of the land of Egypt|de terra Ægypti]] by the hand of Moses. [[80:6|He heard a tongue which he knew not|Linguam quam non noverat audivit]]: that is, he received from God through Moses the divine law, which before he did not know. Or else this is said because the Jewish people, when they had come to Mount Sinai, heard God, or rather an angel of God, speaking to them from the midst of the fire; being terrified at this, they said to Moses: [[Ex 20:19|let not the Lord speak to us, lest we die|Non loquatur nobis Deus, ne forte moriamur]]; but [[Ex 20:19|Speak thou to us|loquere tu nobis]]. On which account Moses says: [[Deut 5:24|Behold|Ecce]], he says, [[Deut 5:24|the Lord our God hath shewn us his majesty|ostendit nobis Dominus Deus noster majestatem suam]], and [[Deut 5:24|have proved this day that God speaking with man, man hath lived|probavimus hodie, quod loquente Deo cum homine vixerit homo]]; [[Deut 5:24|we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire|vocem ejus audivimus de medio ignis]]. Or perhaps he says, [[80:6|He heard a tongue which he knew not|Linguam quam non noverat audivit]], because the children of Israel, born and brought up in Egypt, when they came to the lands of the Amorrhites, the Madianites, the Moabites, the Edomites, etc., heard unknown tongues.

paras.t: Divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus : id est, Deus populum Judæorum eripuit a deportatione onerum, quæ portabant in terra Ægypti ex imperio Pharaonis, construentes ei civitates tabernaculorum, ut patet in Exodo ; manus ejus in cophino servierunt. Nam filii Israel in sportis collegerunt et detulerunt lateres, seu alia quæque necessaria ad structuram.
paras.en: [[80:7|He removed his back from the burdens|Divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus]]: that is, God delivered the Jewish people from the carrying of the burdens which they bore in the land of Egypt at Pharao's command, building him cities of tabernacles, as is plain in Exodus[[Ex 1:11||]]; [[80:7|his hands had served in baskets|manus ejus in cophino servierunt]]. For the children of Israel gathered and carried bricks in baskets, or whatever else was needed for the building.

paras.t: Deinde mutat Propheta personam, loquiturque in persona Dei, subdens : In tribulatione invocasti me : id est, o populo Judæorum, dum in Ægypto affligebaris a præpositis operum atque Ægyptiis, vitam vestram ad amaritudinem perducentibus, clamasti ad me pro liberatione; et liberavi te in manu forti et maximis signis. Hinc enim Dominus ait ad Moysen : Clamor filiorum Israel venit ad me, descendeque ut liberem eos. Exaudivi te in abscondito tempestatis, id est in afflictione cordis tui occulta, quando gemebunde suspirabas ad me, non audens manifeste me invocare aut conqueri, propter Ægyptiorum formidinem ; probavi te apud aquam Contradictionis, id est, ibi ostendi tuam ingratitudinem et perversitatem. Unde in libro Numerorum legitur : Hæc est aqua Contradictionis, ubi jurgati sunt filii Israel contra Dominum. Potest quoque istud specialiter ad Moysen Aaronque referri, qui circa hunc locum Deum per incredulitatem offenderunt, propter quod terram promissionis intrare prohibiti sunt, dicente ad eos Domino : Quia non credidistis mihi, ut sanctificaretis me coram filiis Israel, non introducetis hos populos in terram quam dabo eis.
paras.en: Then the Prophet changes the person and speaks in the person of God, adding: [[80:8|Thou calledst upon me in affliction|In tribulatione invocasti me]]: that is, O Jewish people, while thou wast afflicted in Egypt by the overseers of the works and by the Egyptians, who brought your life to bitterness, thou didst cry to me for deliverance[[Ex 2:23||]]; [[80:8|and I delivered thee|et liberavi te]] with a strong hand and very great signs. For hence the Lord says to Moses: [[Ex 3:9|the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me|Clamor filiorum Israel venit ad me]]; and go down, that I may deliver them [these last words are not in Ex 3:9; compare Ex 3:8, "I am come down to deliver them", and 3:10]. [[80:8|I heard thee in the secret place of tempest|Exaudivi te in abscondito tempestatis]]: that is, in the hidden affliction of thy heart, when thou didst sigh to me with groaning, not daring to call upon me or complain openly for fear of the Egyptians; [[80:8|I proved thee at the waters of contradiction|probavi te apud aquam Contradictionis]]: that is, there I showed forth thy ingratitude and perversity. Hence it is read in the book of Numbers: [[Num 20:13|This is the Water of contradiction, where the children of Israel strove with words against the Lord|Hæc est aqua Contradictionis, ubi jurgati sunt filii Israel contra Dominum]]. This can also be referred especially to Moses and Aaron, who at about this place offended God by unbelief, for which they were forbidden to enter the land of promise, the Lord saying to them: [[Num 20:12|Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring these people into the land, which I will give them|Quia non credidistis mihi, ut sanctificaretis me coram filiis Israel, non introducetis hos populos in terram quam dabo eis]] [the margin gives Num. xx and then 13 beside this line; verse 13 is the Water of contradiction, the words quoted here are verse 12].

paras.t: Audi, populus meus peculiaris, verba legis meæ auribus cordis et corporis, et contestabor te, id est, testis ero verborum meorum, operumque tuorum : juxta illud, Ego sum judex et testis, ait Dominus. Israel, id est plebs Israelitica, si audieris me, id est, si præcepta legis meæ impleveris, non erit in te deus recens, quem colas : quia nil temporale aut creatum pro Deo recipies ; neque adorabis deum alienum, sed me solum, verum, æternumque Deum.
paras.en: [[80:9|Hear, O my people|Audi, populus meus]], my own peculiar people, the words of my law with the ears of heart and body, [[80:9|and I will testify to thee|et contestabor te]]: that is, I will be witness of my words and of thy works, according to that saying: [[Jer 29:23|I am the judge and the witness, saith the Lord|Ego sum judex et testis, ait Dominus]] [the margin reads Jer. xxiv, 23; the words are Jer 29:23]. [[80:9|O Israel|Israel]], that is, the people of Israel, [[80:9|if thou wilt hearken to me|si audieris me]], that is, if thou fulfil the precepts of my law, [[80:10|there shall be no new god in thee|non erit in te deus recens]] for thee to worship, because thou wilt take nothing temporal or created for God; [[80:10|neither shalt thou adore a strange god|neque adorabis deum alienum]], but me alone, the true and eternal God[[Ex 20:3||]].

paras.t: Ego enim sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti, et adhuc plura beneficia dare paratus sum. Nam dilata os tuum, id est, desiderium tuum aperi ad recipiendum, et os corporale ad petendum, et implebo illud gratia mea, dando tibi quod postulas.
paras.en: [[80:11|For I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt|Ego enim sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti]][[Ex 20:2||]], and I am ready to give yet more benefits. For [[80:11|open thy mouth wide|dilata os tuum]], that is, open thy desire to receive, and thy bodily mouth to ask, [[80:11|and I will fill it|et implebo illud]] with my grace, giving thee what thou askest.

paras.t: Consequenter ostenditur populi ingratitudo. Et non audivit populus meus aure cordis vocem meam, id est verba præceptorum meorum ; et Israel non intendit mihi, id est, non advertit neque curavit me. Sed mirum apparet, quod Deus populum rebellem et inobedientem appellat populum suum, præsertim quum de tali populo per Osee prophetam dicat : Non populus meus vos, et ego non Deus vester. Et respondendum, sicut nunc sæpius dictum est, quod populus Judæorum (etiam reprobus) dicitur populus Dei, in quantum a Deo præ ceteris gentibus vocati erant, et multis beneficiis ejus honorificati. Ideo namque Dominus apud Jeremiam ait : Sicut adhæret lumbare ad lumbos viri, sic agglutinavi mihi domum Israel, ut esset mihi in populum, et in nomen, et in laudem, et in gloriam ; et non audierunt. Sic quoque dicuntur dilecti a Deo, secundum quod Dominus apud eumdem ait : Quid est, quod dilectus meus in domo mea fecit scelera multa? Non quod vere atque finaliter dilecti erant a Deo, de quo dictum est supra, Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem ; sed quantum ad beneficia eis a Deo exhibita in præsenti, dicuntur dilecti.
paras.en: Next the ingratitude of the people is shown. [[80:12|But my people heard not|Et non audivit populus meus]] with the ear of the heart [[80:12|my voice|vocem meam]], that is, the words of my commandments; [[80:12|and Israel hearkened not to me|et Israel non intendit mihi]], that is, did not heed me nor care for me. But it seems strange that God calls a rebellious and disobedient people his people, especially since he says of such a people through the prophet Osee: [[Osee 1:9|you are not my people, and I will not be yours|Non populus meus vos, et ego non Deus vester]]. We must answer, as has now often been said, that the Jewish people (even the reprobate) is called the people of God inasmuch as they had been called by God before the other nations and honoured with many of his benefits. For this is why the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 13:11|as the girdle sticketh close to the loins of a man|Sicut adhæret lumbare ad lumbos viri]], [[Jer 13:11|so have I brought close to me|sic agglutinavi mihi]] the house of Israel, [[Jer 13:11|that they might be my people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory|ut esset mihi in populum, et in nomen, et in laudem, et in gloriam]]; [[Jer 13:11|but they would not hear|et non audierunt]]. So too they are called beloved of God, as the Lord says in the same prophet: [[Jer 11:15|What is the meaning that my beloved hath wrought much wickedness in my house|Quid est, quod dilectus meus in domo mea fecit scelera multa]]? Not that they were truly and finally beloved of God, of whom it was said above: [[Ps 5:7|Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity|Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem]]; but they are called beloved with regard to the benefits shown them by God in the present life.

paras.t: Hujus autem ingratitudinis gravissima pœna mox subditur : Et dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum : id est, gratiam meam eis subtraxi : qua subtracta, non præservantur a culpa, sed concupiscentias suas sequuntur, et proprias cogitationes et inclinationes sectantur. Propter quod additur : ibunt in adinventionibus suis, id est, in erroribus suis et vitiis a se excogitatis vivent et perdurabunt.
paras.en: And the most grievous punishment of this ingratitude is added at once: [[80:13|So I let them go according to the desires of their heart|Et dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum]]: that is, I withdrew my grace from them; and once it is withdrawn they are not preserved from sin, but follow their concupiscences and pursue their own thoughts and inclinations. For which reason it is added: [[80:13|they shall walk in their own inventions|ibunt in adinventionibus suis]], that is, they will live and continue in their errors and in vices devised by themselves.

paras.t: Si populus meus audisset me, id est legem meam, Israel si in viis meis, id est in observantiis mandatorum meorum, ambulasset ; Pro nihilo, id est tanquam nihil seu gratis, forsitan, id est certitudinaliter, dummodo ipsi in viis meis perseverassent, inimicos eorum humiliassem, id est septem gentes terræ promissionis, et ceteros gentiles eorum hostes dejecissem, atque potestati eorum subjugassem, sicut per Moysen sæpe promisi ; et super tribulantes eos, id est super persecutores eorum, mitissem manum meam, id est, potestatem meam et ultionem justitiæ meæ extendissem.
paras.en: [[80:14|If my people had heard me|Si populus meus audisset me]], that is, my law, [[80:14|if Israel|Israel si]] [[80:14|had walked|ambulasset]] [[80:14|in my ways|in viis meis]], that is, in the keeping of my commandments; [[80:15|soon|Pro nihilo]] [the Latin, *pro nihilo forsitan*, is literally "for nothing, perhaps", and Denis glosses each part], that is, as though for nothing, or freely; *perhaps*, that is, certainly, provided they had persevered in my ways, [[80:15|have humbled their enemies|inimicos eorum humiliassem]], that is, I would have cast down the seven nations of the land of promise and the other gentiles their foes, and subjected them to their power, as I often promised by Moses[[Ex 3:8||]][[Ex 13:5||]][[Ex 23:23||]][[Ex 33:2||]] [the margin adds "and elsewhere"]; [[80:15|and laid my hand|mitissem manum meam]] [[80:15|on them that troubled them|super tribulantes eos]], that is, upon their persecutors, that is, I would have stretched out my power and the vengeance of my justice.

paras.t: Inimici Domini, id est Judæi ingrati : de quibus Moyses loquitur, Audite, rebelles et increduli ; mentiti sunt ei, id est ad injuriam ejus, quia non impleverunt quod spoponderunt dicentes, Omnia quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus. Nam paulo post vitulum aureum adoraverunt. Et erit tempus eorum in sæcula : id est, damnatio et pœna eorum in æternum durabit, quoniam in inferno sine fine cruciabuntur. Unde Dominus dixit ad Moysen : Ego in die ultionis visitabo et hoc peccatum eorum.
paras.en: [[80:16|The enemies of the Lord|Inimici Domini]], that is, the ungrateful Jews, of whom Moses speaks: [[Num 20:10|Hear, ye rebellious and incredulous|Audite, rebelles et increduli]]; [[80:16|have lied to him|mentiti sunt ei]], that is, to his injury, because they did not fulfil what they promised, saying: [[Ex 24:7|All things that the Lord hath spoken, we will do|Omnia quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus]]. For a little after, they worshipped the golden calf. [[80:16|And their time shall be for ever|Et erit tempus eorum in sæcula]]: that is, their damnation and punishment will last for ever, since they will be tormented in hell without end. Hence the Lord said to Moses: [[Ex 32:34|I in the day of revenge will visit this sin also of theirs|Ego in die ultionis visitabo et hoc peccatum eorum]].

paras.t: Et cibavit eos, id est non obstante prædicta ingratitudine Judæorum, Deus cibavit illos ex adipe frumenti, scilicet pane cœlesti seu manna : quod adeo dulce fuit, ac si de simila et adipe factum fuisset. Vel sic : Cibavit eos ex adipe frumenti : quoniam postquam ingressi sunt terram promissionis tritico abundantem, aluit eos pane de simila tritici facto. Et de petra melle saturavit eos, id est melle emanante de petra. Nam terra promissionis dicitur lacte et melle manare. Apes namque in rupibus terræ promissionis mellificant, et ita de locis petrosis mel satis copiose colligitur.
paras.en: [[80:17|And he fed them|Et cibavit eos]], that is, notwithstanding the aforesaid ingratitude of the Jews, God fed them [[80:17|with the fat of wheat|ex adipe frumenti]], namely with the bread of heaven, or manna, which was as sweet as if it had been made of fine flour and fat. Or thus: [[80:17|he fed them with the fat of wheat|Cibavit eos ex adipe frumenti]], because after they had entered the land of promise, abounding in wheat, he nourished them with bread made of fine wheat flour. And [[80:17|filled them with honey out of the rock|Et de petra melle saturavit eos]], that is, with honey flowing from the rock. For the land of promise is said to flow with milk and honey; for bees make honey in the rocks of the land of promise, and so honey is gathered quite plentifully from rocky places.

80.title: EXPLANATIO EJUSDEM PSALMI OCTOGESIMI TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS.
80.title_en: Tropological or moral explanation of the same eightieth psalm.

paras.t: SPIRITUALEM denique intellectum sequendo, titulus psalmi hujus, in principio præcedentis expositionis positus, ita exponitur : Psalmus iste in finem, qui Christus est, nos dirigens, proponitur et cantatur ipsi Asaph, id est congregationi fidelium per Asaph designatæ ; et agit hic psalmus pro torcularibus, id est de tribulationibus, seu Ecclesiis pressura tribulationum afflictis, quibus mali separantur a bonis : quæ separatio designata est quinta sabbati, id est quinta die hebdomadæ : in qua ex aqua producti sunt pisces avesque ; remanseruntque pisces in aqua, et aves conscenderunt in aera. Per quod præfiguratum est, quod in Ecclesia Christi contingit. Omnes enim Christiani in fonte Baptismatis spiritualiter producuntur et regenerantur ; sed quidam eorum manent in terra transitoriis inhærendo, ceteri volant in altum amando cœlestia.
paras.en: Lastly, following the spiritual sense, the title of this psalm, set down at the beginning of the preceding exposition, is explained thus: this psalm is set forth and sung [[80:1|Unto the end|in finem]], who is Christ, directing us, [[80:1|for Asaph himself|ipsi Asaph]], that is, for the congregation of the faithful designated by Asaph; and this psalm treats [[80:1|for the winepresses|pro torcularibus]], that is, of tribulations, or of Churches afflicted by the pressure of tribulations, by which the wicked are separated from the good. This separation is designated by *on the fifth day of the week* [*quinta sabbati*: words of the title as Denis reads it, not in the Douay-Rheims], that is, on the fifth day of the week, on which fishes and birds were brought forth from the water; and the fishes remained in the water, while the birds went up into the air. By this was prefigured what comes to pass in the Church of Christ. For all Christians are spiritually brought forth and born again in the font of Baptism; but some of them remain on the earth by clinging to passing things, while the others fly on high by loving heavenly things.

paras.t: Itaque, o universi filii ecclesiasticæ congregationis, Exsultate Deo adjutori nostro, videlicet summæ Trinitati, simplici Deo, jubilate Deo Jacob, id est supplantantium vitia. Per Jacob namque, qui interpretatur supplantator, conculcatores vitiorum intelliguntur. Versiculus iste spirituali hilaritate redundat. Est enim exhortatio jucundissima, admonitio saluberrima, doctrina prorsus angelica. Quid enim tam cœliforme, angelicum, deiforme ac splendidum, sicut in Deo exsultare et Domino jubilare, congaudendo infinitæ perfectioni Creatoris, infinitæ beatitudini Divinitatis, infinitæ jucunditati supergloriosissimæ Trinitatis? Hoc nempe est præclarissimum exercitium summæ virtutis, videlicet caritatis divinæ, quo esse non potest sublimius in sæculo isto. Quanto enim dignitati et gloriæ Domini Dei nostri cordialius congratulamur, tanto eum ardentius diligere comprobamur; quo autem Deum calidiori mente amamus, eo deiformiores ac nobiliores consistimus, quoniam summa nobilitas mentis creatæ est amor divinus, id est actualis dilectio superbenedictæ Divinitatis.
paras.en: Therefore, O all you sons of the Church's congregation, [[80:2|Rejoice to God our helper|Exsultate Deo adjutori nostro]], namely to the supreme Trinity, the one simple God; [[80:2|sing aloud to the God of Jacob|jubilate Deo Jacob]], that is, of those who supplant vices. For by Jacob, which is interpreted *supplanter*, are understood those who trample vices underfoot. This little verse overflows with spiritual gladness. For it is a most joyful exhortation, a most wholesome admonition, a teaching altogether angelic. For what is so heavenly, angelic, godlike and splendid as to rejoice in God and to sing aloud to the Lord, rejoicing together with the infinite perfection of the Creator, the infinite beatitude of the Godhead, the infinite delight of the most supremely glorious Trinity? This indeed is the most excellent exercise of the highest virtue, namely of divine charity, than which nothing can be more sublime in this world. For the more heartily we rejoice with the dignity and glory of the Lord our God, the more ardently we are shown to love him; and the more fervent the mind with which we love God, the more godlike and noble we become, since the highest nobility of a created mind is divine love, that is, the actual love [that is, love in act, not only as a habit] of the supremely blessed Godhead.

paras.t: Sumite psalmum, id est, bonam operationem a gratia Dei accipite : quam operationem non nisi a Deo habere potestis, quoniam (sicut ait Apostolus) ipse est qui operatur in nobis et velle et perficere pro bona voluntate, id est ex sua voluntate benigna. Ad quem Isaias loquens : Domine, inquit, dabis pacem nobis; omnia enim opera nostra operatus es nobis. Unde et Christus ait discipulis : Sicut palmes a semetipso non potest ferre fructum, nisi manserit in vite; sic nec vos, nisi in me manseritis. Et date tympanum, id est, dulcem reddite sonum, Dei auribus beneplacentem : qui utique non est proprie sonus sensibilis atque exterior, sed intellectualis, videlicet mortificatio carnis, et castitas sancta, quæ etiam est odor bonus. Quemadmodum namque tympanum, id est corium in ligno expansum, non nisi percussum dulciter sonat; sic caro castigationibus pœnitentialium flagellorum lassata et attenuata, Domino placet, et sua operatio coram Altissimo sonat. Sumite quoque psalterium jucundum cum cithara. Psalterium quod a superioribus sonat, et decem chordas habet, designat Decalogum legis divinitus datum. Cithara vero habens sex chordas, et ab inferioribus sonans, significat sex opera misericordiæ. Est igitur sensus : Sumite psalterium jucundum cum cithara, id est, divinæ legis præcepta implete, vacando cœlestibus : sed cum cithara, quatenus simul exerceatis opera misericordiæ, quoniam non debetis sic esse intenti cœlestibus, ut negligatis succurrere proximorum necessitatibus.
paras.en: [[80:3|Take a psalm|Sumite psalmum]], that is, receive good working from the grace of God: a working which you cannot have except from God, since (as the Apostle says) it is he [[Phil 2:13|who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish, according to his good will|qui operatur in nobis et velle et perficere pro bona voluntate]] [the margin reads Philipp. 13; the verse is Phil 2:13; Denis has "in us"], that is, out of his own kindly will. Speaking to him Isaias says: [[Is 26:12|Lord|Domine]], he says, [[Is 26:12|thou wilt give us peace: for thou hast wrought all our works for us|dabis pacem nobis; omnia enim opera nostra operatus es nobis]]. Hence Christ too says to the disciples: [[John 15:4|As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abide in the vine, so neither can you, unless you abide in me|Sicut palmes a semetipso non potest ferre fructum, nisi manserit in vite; sic nec vos, nisi in me manseritis]]. [[80:3|and bring hither the timbrel|Et date tympanum]] [*date tympanum*, literally "give the timbrel"], that is, give back a sweet sound, well pleasing to God's ears: which is not properly a sensible and outward sound, but an intellectual one, namely the mortification of the flesh and holy chastity, which is also a good odour. For as a timbrel, that is, a hide stretched over wood, does not sound sweetly unless it is struck, so the flesh, wearied and worn down by the chastisements of penitential scourges, pleases the Lord, and its working sounds before the Most High. Take also [[80:3|the pleasant psaltery with the harp|psalterium jucundum cum cithara]]. The psaltery, which sounds from its upper part and has ten strings, designates the Decalogue of the law given by God. The harp, having six strings and sounding from its lower part, signifies the six works of mercy. The sense, then, is: Take [[80:3|the pleasant psaltery with the harp|psalterium jucundum cum cithara]], that is, fulfil the precepts of the divine law by giving yourselves to heavenly things; but *with the harp*, so that at the same time you practise the works of mercy, since you ought not to be so intent on heavenly things as to neglect to help the needs of your neighbours.

paras.t: Buccinate, o Christifideles, id est, audacter et amorose sonate Dei præconia, vestra peccata, et proximorum documenta, ita ut Deum laudetis, vos ipsos vituperetis, et proximos instruatis; in neomenia, id est in exordio illuminationis vestræ a Sole justitiæ, scilicet in insigni die solennitatis vestræ interioris, quando videlicet Spiritus Sanctus venit ad vos, et mansionem sibi facit in vobis : tunc enim gratiam vobis concessam, aliis libenter debetis communicare. Sic autem buccinate tuba, id est verbo Dei : quia præceptum in Israel est, id est, Ecclesiæ Christianorum Deum per fidem speculanti, divinitus jussum est taliter facere. Christus enim in Evangelio damnat servum, qui talentum sibi concessum abscondit. Et Paulus vult, ut singuli non quæ nostra sunt quæramus, sed quæ aliorum. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque? Denique excellentissimus apostolici ordinis princeps, evidentius atque præclarius loquens : Unusquisque, inquit, sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei.
paras.en: [[80:4|Blow up the trumpet|Buccinate]], O faithful of Christ, that is, sound boldly and lovingly the praises of God, your own sins, and instruction for your neighbours, so that you praise God, blame yourselves, and teach your neighbours; [[80:4|on the new moon|in neomenia]], that is, at the beginning of your enlightening by the Sun of justice, namely [[80:4|on the noted day of your solemnity|in insigni die solennitatis vestræ]] within you, when, that is, the Holy Ghost comes to you and makes his abode in you[[John 14:23||]]: for then you ought gladly to share with others the grace granted to you. In this way, then, [[80:4|Blow up the trumpet|buccinate tuba]], that is, with the word of God, [[80:5|For it is a commandment in Israel|quia præceptum in Israel est]]: that is, the Church of Christians, which beholds God by faith, has been commanded by God to do so [Israel is taken as "seeing God"]. For Christ in the Gospel condemns the servant who hid the talent granted him[[Matt 25:25||]] [the margin gives Matt. xxv, 24–30]. And Paul wills that each of us seek not the things that are ours, but those that are other men's[[1 Cor 10:24||]] [Denis's wording is closer to Phil 2:4]. For this reason it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 41:17|wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is there in them both?|Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?]][[Ecclus 20:32||]] [the margin gives both places; Denis's *abscondita* is the reading of 41:17]. Lastly the most excellent prince of the apostolic order, speaking more plainly and more clearly: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man|Unusquisque]], he says, [[1 Pet 4:10|hath received grace, ministering the same one to another: as good stewards of the manifold grace of God|sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei]].

paras.t: Testimonium in Joseph posuit illud, id est in populo ex gentilitate ad Christum converso, et Ecclesiæ addito. Joseph enim interpretatur augmentum; sicque per eum signantur ex gentibus Christo per fidem adaucti : et his Deus testatus est præceptum prædictum, ut patet ex auctoritatibus allegatis. Quum exiret de terra Ægypti, id est, quum gentiles in Christum credentes, egrederentur de pristinis suis obscuritatibus, vitiis et ignorantiis. Linguam quam non noverat, audivit, id est, tunc audire cœperunt evangelicam prædicationem, apostolicamque doctrinam, ante ipsis prorsus ignotam. Propter quod Athenienses ad Paulum dixerunt : Volumus scire quæ est hæc nova, quæ a te dicitur, doctrina. Nova enim quædam infers auribus nostris. Tunc quoque quum sic de Ægypto exiit hic populus, Deus divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus, id est a pondere vitiorum, a servitute peccati, a jugo mundi, carnis, atque diaboli. Talibus enim clamat Christus : Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos. Manus ejus, id est operationes populi hujus, antequam converteretur ad Deum, in cophino, id est in vasis immunditiarum ac sordium vitiorum, servierunt legi peccati, imo peccato ac dæmoni. Dum enim peccator vitiis immoratur, manus operationum suarum tenet in vase peccati, id est in actione inordinata, seu voluntate perversa, in quibus culpa fundatur.
paras.en: [[80:6|He ordained it for a testimony in Joseph|Testimonium in Joseph posuit illud]], that is, in the people converted to Christ from the gentiles and added to the Church. For Joseph is interpreted *increase*; and so by him are signified those from among the gentiles who have been added to Christ by faith: and to these God has testified the commandment spoken of, as is plain from the authorities cited. [[80:6|when he came out of the land of Egypt|Quum exiret de terra Ægypti]], that is, when the gentiles who believed in Christ went out of their former darkness, vices and ignorance. [[80:6|he heard a tongue which he knew not|Linguam quam non noverat, audivit]], that is, they then began to hear the preaching of the Gospel and the teaching of the Apostles, wholly unknown to them before. For this reason the Athenians said to Paul: [[Acts 17:19|May we know what this new doctrine is, which thou speakest of?|Volumus scire quæ est hæc nova, quæ a te dicitur, doctrina]] [Denis has *Volumus scire*, "We wish to know"] [[Acts 17:20|For thou bringest in certain new things to our ears|Nova enim quædam infers auribus nostris]]. Then too, when this people thus went out of Egypt, God [[80:7|removed his back from the burdens|divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus]], that is, from the weight of vices, from the bondage of sin, from the yoke of the world, the flesh and the devil. For to such Christ cries: [[Matt 11:28|Come to me all you that labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you|Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos]]. [[80:7|his hands|Manus ejus]], that is, the works of this people before it was converted to God, [[80:7|in baskets|in cophino]], that is, in vessels of uncleanness and of the filth of vices, [[80:7|had served|servierunt]] the law of sin, or rather sin and the devil. For while the sinner lingers in vices, he keeps the hands of his works in the vessel of sin, that is, in disordered action or a perverse will, in which guilt is grounded.

paras.t: Deinde Christus ait Ecclesiæ, cuilibetque devoto : In tribulatione, id est persecutione, tentatione, seu alia quacumque molestia, invocasti me : quod est tutissimum saluberrimumque remedium. Idcirco quandocumque affligimur, sive a dæmone, sive a malis hominibus, sive a propriis passionibus, Deum invocare debemus cum omni fiducia atque constantia, et ita efficiemur securi : nam exaudiemur, sicut subjungitur. Et liberavi te; exaudivi te in abscondito tempestatis, tempore diabolicæ suggestionis seu intimæ afflictionis, quando ad alium nullum confugere poteras. Denique hoc debet esse summa et unica consolatio omni afflicto, quod certissimum est Deum maxime adesse afflictis, quoniam promptus est succurrere eis, sicut superius dictum est : Juxta est Dominus his qui tribulato sunt corde. Inferius quoque ipse testatur : Cum ipso sum in tribulatione. Propterea viri perfecti in tribulationibus gaudent, et in eis libenter exsistunt propter præsentiam Dei, sed pro patientia et fortitudine animi Dominum deprecantur. Probavi te apud aquam Contradictionis, id est apud quamcumque adversitatem et resistentiam, qua tibi in bono resistitur ab hostibus tuæ salutis, videlicet mundo, carne et diabolo. Adversitas enim et resistentia, quam sustinet homo in via Dei ab his qui moliuntur eum a bono opere avertere, declarant an homo vere fideliterque Deo adhæreat. Unde Moyses ait: Adduxit te Dominus, ut affligeret atque tentaret, et notum fieret utrum custodires mandata illius, an non. Et ista est ratio cur Deus permittit famulos suos talia impedimenta pati, videlicet ut probentur, et innotescat utrum sincere quærant justitiam, sicque gratiam ampliorem acquirant, et aliis in exemplum proponantur. Propter quod scriptum est : Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos.
paras.en: Then Christ says to the Church and to every devout soul: [[80:8|in affliction|In tribulatione]], that is, in persecution, temptation, or any other trouble whatever, [[80:8|Thou calledst upon me|invocasti me]]: which is the safest and most wholesome remedy. Therefore whenever we are afflicted, whether by the devil, or by wicked men, or by our own passions, we ought to call upon God with all confidence and constancy, and so we shall be made secure; for we shall be heard, as follows: [[80:8|and I delivered thee|Et liberavi te]]; [[80:8|I heard thee in the secret place of tempest|exaudivi te in abscondito tempestatis]], in the time of the devil's suggestion or of inward affliction, when thou couldst flee to no one else. Indeed this ought to be the highest and only consolation of everyone afflicted: that it is most certain that God is most of all present to the afflicted, since he is ready to help them, as was said above: [[Ps 33:19|The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart|Juxta est Dominus his qui tribulato sunt corde]]. Further on, too, he testifies: [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione]]. Therefore perfect men rejoice in tribulations and willingly remain in them because of the presence of God, but they pray to the Lord for patience and fortitude of soul. [[80:8|I proved thee at the waters of contradiction|Probavi te apud aquam Contradictionis]], that is, at any adversity and resistance by which thou art resisted in good by the enemies of thy salvation, namely the world, the flesh and the devil. For the adversity and resistance which a man endures in the way of God from those who strive to turn him away from good works show whether he truly and faithfully cleaves to God. Hence Moses says: [[Deut 8:2|the Lord thy God hath brought thee|Adduxit te Dominus]] [[Deut 8:2|to afflict thee and to prove thee, and that the things that were known in thy heart might be made known, whether thou wouldst keep his commandments or no|ut affligeret atque tentaret, et notum fieret utrum custodires mandata illius, an non]]. And this is the reason why God permits his servants to suffer such hindrances: that they may be proved, and it may be made known whether they sincerely seek justice, and so may gain more abundant grace and be set forth to others as an example. For this reason it is written: [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace, he hath proved them, and as a victim of a holocaust, he hath received them|Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos]] [Denis reads "the Lord hath proved the elect"].

paras.t: Audi, populus meus, qui a me Christianus vocaris; qui etiam Israel diceris, id est Deum per fidem conspiciens. Tu ergo si audieris me, implendo præcepta mea, ita ut Deum tota anima, toto corde, et tota fortitudine diligas, non erit in te Deus recens, id est, me non derelinques, nec aliis magis quam mihi adhærebis. Non servies creaturæ potius quam Creatori; non magis amabis ventris ingluviem, carnis luxuriam, mundi honorem, temporalia bona sive pecuniam, quam me summum atque incommutabile bonum. Qui enim castitatem relinquit et voluptati deservit, recentem suscipit deum : quoniam luxuriosi deus est sua dilecta, gulosi deus est venter; avari, pecunia. Quod enim quis amplius cogitat, amat et colit, hoc deus ipsius esse convincitur. Ego enim Unigenitus Dei propter te incarnatus, sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti, id est de hoc sæculo nequam, videlicet de caligine culpæ et tenebris ignorantiæ, per mortis meæ meritum et sanguinis pretium, per gratiam baptismalem, per virtutum infusionem, et Spiritus Sancti multiplicem illustrationem.
paras.en: [[80:9|Hear, O my people|Audi, populus meus]], who art called Christian after me; who art also called Israel, that is, beholding God by faith.
