paras.t: Dixerunt isti adversarii tui, o Domine : Venite, et disperdamus eos, scilicet Christianos, de gente : id est, omnes interficiamus, ne quisquam eorum de cetero inter gentes commoretur ; et non memoretur nomen Israel, id est militantis Ecclesiæ, ultra. Multi namque tyranni conati sunt cultum et fidem atque memoriam populi christiani prorsus auferre.
paras.en: [[82:5|They have said|Dixerunt]], these adversaries of thine, O Lord: [[82:5|Come and let us destroy them|Venite, et disperdamus eos]], namely the Christians, [[82:5|so that they be not a nation|de gente]]: that is, let us kill them all, so that none of them may dwell any longer among the nations; [[82:5|and let the name of Israel be remembered|et non memoretur nomen Israel]], that is, of the Church militant, [[82:5|no more|ultra]]. For many tyrants have tried to do away altogether with the worship, the faith and the memory of the Christian people.

paras.t: Simul adversum te testamentum disposuerunt tabernacula Idumæorum et Ismaaelitæ, Moab et Agareni, Gebal et Ammon, etc. Quemadmodum populi isti adversati sunt Synagogæ Judæorum, sic designati per eos adversantur Ecclesiæ Christianorum. Qui autem intelligantur per populos istos, pensare debemus ex interpretationibus nominum horum. Sicut in Genesi legitur, dum natus esset Esau, apparuit totus in modum pellis hispidus atque sanguineus : propterea vocatum est nomen ejus Edom. Idumæi ergo ab Edom nomen sortiti, interpretantur sanguinei seu terreni : per quos designantur avari, terrenarum rerum amatores inordinati. Ismaelitæ interpretantur inobedientes : per quos hoc loco designantur, qui propriam voluntatem sequuntur, non Deo, sed sibimetipsis obtemperantes : per quos significantur gulosi, qui non Christo, sed suo ventri deserviunt. Moab interpretatur, ex patre : per quem designantur perversi, ex Deo secundum naturam exorti, sed propter malitiam ex patre diabolo nati : quibus Christus ait, Vos ex patre diabolo estis. Per quem exprimuntur luxuriosi, quoniam filia major ipsius Lot, genuit Moab ex patre proprio. Agareni interpretantur, alieni seu advenæ : per quos figurantur falsi fratres, qui solo nomine inter electos computantur, sicut Joannes asserit : In nobis erant, sed non erant ex nobis ; nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum. Gebal interpretatur, vallis vana : sicque per eum explicantur fallaciter humiles atque hypocritæ, de quibus in libro Job habetur : Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei. Et in Ecclesiastico : Est qui nequiter se humiliat ; interiora autem ejus plena sunt dolo. Talibus ait Salvator : Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus, Deus autem novit corda vestra ; quia quod hominibus altum est, abominatio est ante Deum. Per Ammon, qui interpretatur, populus turbidus, designati sunt iracundi, quoniam ira rationem perturbat, et hominem stulto assimilat. Propter quod Ecclesiastes dicit : Ne sis velox ad irascendum, quia ira in sinu stulti requiescit ; et Job, Virum stultum interficit iracundia. Per Amalec, quem genuit Eliphaz primogenitus Esau, et interpretatur, populus lingens, significantur adulatores fallaciter blandientes. Quo vitio se caruisse ostendit Apostolus, dicens : Neque aliquando fuimus in sermone adulationis.
paras.en: [[82:6|they have made a covenant together against thee|Simul adversum te testamentum disposuerunt]], [[82:7|The tabernacle of the Edomites, and the Ishmahelites: Moab, and the Agarens|tabernacula Idumæorum et Ismaaelitæ, Moab et Agareni]], [[82:8|Gebal, and Ammon|Gebal et Ammon]], etc. As these peoples opposed the Synagogue of the Jews, so those signified by them oppose the Church of the Christians. And who are to be understood by these peoples we must weigh from the interpretations of their names. As is read in Genesis, when Esau was born he appeared [[Gen 25:25|hairy like a skin|totus in modum pellis hispidus]] all over, and blood-red; and for this reason his name was called Edom [the name Edom is given at Gen 25:30]. The Edomites, then, who take their name from Edom, are interpreted "bloody" or "earthy": by them are signified the covetous, inordinate lovers of earthly things. The Ishmaelites are interpreted "disobedient": by them are signified in this place those who follow their own will, obeying not God but themselves: and by them are signified the gluttons, who [[Rom 16:18|serve not Christ our Lord but their own belly|non Christo, sed suo ventri deserviunt]]. Moab is interpreted "from the father": by him are signified the perverse, who sprang from God according to nature, but through malice are born of their father the devil: to whom Christ says, [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]. By him too the lustful are expressed, since the elder daughter of Lot himself bore Moab by her own father[[Gen 19:33||]][[Gen 19:37||]]. The Agarens are interpreted "strangers" or "newcomers": by them are figured false brethren, who are counted among the elect in name only, as John declares: They were among us, [[1 John 2:19|but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have remained with us|sed non erant ex nobis ; nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum]] [Denis reads "they were among us" where the Vulgate has "they went out from us"]. Gebal is interpreted "vain valley" [that is, a lowliness that is empty]: and so by it are set forth the falsely humble and the hypocrites, of whom it is said in the book of Job: [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God|Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei]]. And in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 19:23|There is one that humbleth himself wickedly, and his interior is full of deceit|Est qui nequiter se humiliat ; interiora autem ejus plena sunt dolo]] [the margin gives Ecclus. xiv, 23; the passage is Ecclus 19:23]. To such the Saviour says: [[Luke 16:15|you are they who justify yourselves before men, but God knoweth your hearts. For that which is high to men is an abomination before God|Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus, Deus autem novit corda vestra ; quia quod hominibus altum est, abominatio est ante Deum]]. By Ammon, which is interpreted "a troubled people", are signified the wrathful, since anger troubles the reason and makes a man like a fool. For this reason Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 7:10|Be not quickly angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of a fool|Ne sis velox ad irascendum, quia ira in sinu stulti requiescit]]; and Job: [[Job 5:2|Anger indeed killeth the foolish|Virum stultum interficit iracundia]] [Denis reads *virum*, "the foolish man", where the Vulgate has *vere*, "indeed"]. By Amalec, whom Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau begot[[Gen 36:12||]], and which is interpreted "a licking people", are signified flatterers, who fawn deceitfully. The Apostle shows that he was free of this vice, saying: [[1 Thess 2:5|neither have we used at any time the speech of flattery|Neque aliquando fuimus in sermone adulationis]].

paras.t: Alienigenæ, id est Philistæi, qui interpretantur, cadentes potione : per quos designantur vitiis atque luxuria ebrii ; cum habitantibus Tyrum, id est cum invidis. Tyrus enim interpretatur angustia : invidi autem in se ipsis torquentur, quasi loco angusto conclusi. Hi utique omnes populo præelecto ad vitam repugnant. Etenim Assur venit cum illis. Per Assur, qui interpretatur deprimens seu elatus, significatur diabolus, qui in profundum peccando prolapsus est, et in mentis tumorem erectus ; qui etiam rex est super omnes filios superbiæ, sicut in libro Job scriptum est. Facti sunt in adjutorium filiis Lot, id est declinantibus. Lot namque interpretatur declinans : quo signantur apostatæ angeli, qui cum principe suo Lucifero declinaverunt a Deo. Dæmonum vero adjutores sunt homines impii jam prædicti, quemadmodum justi adjutores seu cooperatores sunt Dei.
paras.en: [[82:8|the Philistines|Alienigenæ]] [the Latin has *alienigenæ*, "men of another race"], that is, the Philistines, which is interpreted "falling by drink": by them are signified those drunk with vices and with lust; [[82:8|with the inhabitants of Tyre|cum habitantibus Tyrum]], that is, with the envious. For Tyre is interpreted "straitness": and the envious are tormented within themselves, as though shut up in a narrow place. All these, surely, fight against the people chosen beforehand for life. [[82:9|Yea, and the Assyrian also is joined with them|Etenim Assur venit cum illis]] [the Latin has "Assur came with them"]. By Assur, which is interpreted "pressing down" or "lifted up", is signified the devil, who by sinning fell into the depth, and was raised up into swelling of mind; and of whom it is also written in the book of Job: [[Job 41:25|he is king over all the children of pride|rex est super omnes filios superbiæ]]. [[82:9|they are come to the aid of the sons of Lot|Facti sunt in adjutorium filiis Lot]], that is, of those who turn aside. For Lot is interpreted "turning aside": by which are signified the apostate angels, who with their prince Lucifer turned aside from God. And the helpers of the demons are the wicked men already named, just as the just are the helpers, or fellow workers, of God.

paras.t: Deinde orat Ecclesia pro dejectione et justa punitione istorum, potius futura tormenta prædicendo, quam mala imprecando, vel conformando se divinæ justitiæ, vel orando ut in præsenti castigentur, ne æternaliter condemnentur, aut diutius vivendo gravius prævaricentur, et ne bonum commune, atque Ecclesiam diutius persequi permittantur. Fac illis sicut Madian et Sisaræ, etc. Madian, qui erat filius Abrahæ ex Cetura, interpretatur, relinquens judicium : quo figurantur qui se ipsos non judicant, neque Dei futurum judicium metuunt : propter quod salvari non poterunt, secundum quod in libro Job quidam dicit, Numquid qui non amat judicium, sanari potest? Per Sisaram, qui interpretatur, exclusio gaudii, illi signantur qui propter mundi et carnis suæ delicias, æternæ beatitudinis gaudia a se ipsis excludunt, sicut de talibus ait Dominus Jesus : Væ vobis qui nunc ridetis, quia lugebitis et flebitis. Salomon quoque : Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia. Est tamen quædam spiritualis lætitia non abjicienda, de qua dicit Apostolus : Gaudete in Domino semper. Per Jabin, qui interpretatur sapiens, intelliguntur carnaliter sapientes, quibus ab Isaia dicitur : Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris. Per Cison, quod interpretatur duritia, intelliguntur obstinati in malo, seu induratio cordis.
paras.en: Next the Church prays for the casting down and just punishment of these, foretelling torments to come rather than calling down evils; either conforming herself to the divine justice, or praying that they may be chastised in the present, lest they be condemned eternally, or lest by living longer they transgress more grievously, and lest they be allowed to persecute the common good and the Church any longer. [[82:10|Do to them as thou didst to Madian and to Sisara|Fac illis sicut Madian et Sisaræ]], etc. Madian, who was the son of Abraham by Cetura[[Gen 25:2||]], is interpreted "forsaking judgement": by which are figured those who do not judge themselves and do not fear the judgement of God to come: for which reason they cannot be saved, according to what someone says in the book of Job: [[Job 34:17|Can he be healed that loveth not judgment?|Numquid qui non amat judicium, sanari potest?]] By Sisara, which is interpreted "shutting out of joy", are signified those who for the delights of the world and of their flesh shut out from themselves the joys of eternal blessedness, as the Lord Jesus says of such: [[Luke 6:25|Woe to you that now laugh: for you shall mourn and weep|Væ vobis qui nunc ridetis, quia lugebitis et flebitis]]. Solomon too: [[Eccles 7:5|The heart of the wise is where there is mourning, and the heart of fools where there is mirth|Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia]]. Yet there is a certain spiritual joy not to be cast away, of which the Apostle says: [[Phil 4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always|Gaudete in Domino semper]]. By Jabin, which is interpreted "wise", are understood the carnally wise, to whom Isaias says: [[Is 5:21|Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes|Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris]]. By Cison, which is interpreted "hardness", are understood the obstinate in evil, or hardness of heart.

paras.t: Orat ergo Ecclesia, ut persecutoribus suis fiat sicut peccatoribus nunc prædictis sæpius factum est ; præcipue tamen ista petuntur contra exercitum Antichristi. Pone principes eorum, scilicet persecutorum Ecclesiæ, sicut Oreb et Zeb et Zebee, etc. Per Oreb, qui interpretatur siccitas, designantur aridi a gratia Dei : de qua ariditate scriptum est, O pastor et idolum derelinquens gregem, brachium ejus ariditate siccabitur, id est, operatio ejus gratia Dei privabitur. Per Zeb, qui interpretatur lupus, significantur rapaces. Per Zebee, qui interpretatur, victima lupi, figurantur qui peccando facti sunt præda diaboli. Per Salmana, qui interpretatur, umbra commotionis, seu, in pravitate perfectus, signantur instabiles, seu cum diabolo unum corpus effecti, qui simul cum illo projiciendi sunt in caminum ignis æterni.
paras.en: The Church prays, then, that it may be done to her persecutors as was often done to the sinners just named; yet these things are asked above all against the army of Antichrist. [[82:12|Make their princes|Pone principes eorum]], namely of the persecutors of the Church, [[82:12|like Oreb, and Zeb, and Zebee|sicut Oreb et Zeb et Zebee]], etc. By Oreb, which is interpreted "dryness", are signified those dried up from the grace of God: of which dryness it is written: [[Zach 11:17|O shepherd, and idol, that forsaketh the flock|O pastor et idolum derelinquens gregem]], [[Zach 11:17|his arm shall quite wither away|brachium ejus ariditate siccabitur]], that is, his working shall be deprived of the grace of God. By Zeb, which is interpreted "wolf", are signified the rapacious. By Zebee, which is interpreted "the wolf's victim", are figured those who by sinning have become the prey of the devil. By Salmana, which is interpreted "shadow of commotion", or "perfect in wickedness", are signified the unstable, or those made one body with the devil, who are to be cast together with him into the furnace of everlasting fire.

paras.t: Omnes principes eorum, id est, capitaneos peccatorum jam prænominatorum, justos vastantium ; qui principes dixerunt : Hereditate possideamus sanctuarium Dei, id est terram, possessiones, ecclesias Christianorum, vel potius ipsos Christianos, subjiciendo eos nostro imperio, legi et cultui. Populus namque fidelis sanctuarium Dei vocatur, juxta illud Apostoli : Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos. Cetera exponenda sunt sicut in præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: [[82:12|All their princes|Omnes principes eorum]], that is, the captains of the sinners already named, who lay waste the just; the princes [[82:13|Who have said|qui principes dixerunt]]: [[82:13|Let us possess the sanctuary of God for an inheritance|Hereditate possideamus sanctuarium Dei]], that is, the land, the possessions, the churches of the Christians, or rather the Christians themselves, by subjecting them to our rule, law and worship. For the faithful people is called the sanctuary of God, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 3:17|the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos]]. The rest is to be expounded as in the preceding article.

paras.t: Psalmus iste contra iniquos satis terribiliter invehitur ; et quam inæstimabili confusione ac pœna in futuro judicio sint plectendi, qui modo non convertuntur, in ipso ostenditur. Quod vero hic dicitur, Imple facies eorum ignominia, accipi potest de tarda et infructuosa pœnitentia reproborum, non ex amore justitiæ, sed timore pœnarum de peccato dolentium : de quorum pœnitentia in libro Sapientiæ scriptum est : Dicentes intra se, pœnitentiam agentes, et præ angustia spiritus gementes ; et sequitur : Talia dixerunt in inferno. Denique versus iste, Imple facies eorum ignominia, accipi potest in bono ; eritque sensus : Da, Domine, ut in præsenti refutentur et contemnantur ac vituperentur, secundum quod peccatores sunt, quatenus ex ipsa sua ignominia cessent peccare. Quemadmodum enim per adulationem et laudem falsissimam roboratur peccator in culpa, ita per ignominiam sibi illatam, a malo retrahitur, dum se ab omnibus argui contuetur. Et ita salubriter quærent nomen tuum, Domine, per pœnitentiam salutarem et veram compunctionem. Pertinere quippe videtur hoc ad eos, de quibus in Evangelio scriptum est : Compelle intrare.
paras.en: This psalm inveighs against the wicked terribly enough; and it shows with what inestimable confusion and punishment those who do not now turn back are to be struck at the judgement to come. But what is said here, [[82:17|Fill their faces with shame|Imple facies eorum ignominia]], can be taken of the late and fruitless repentance of the reprobate, who grieve over sin not from love of justice but from fear of punishment: of whose repentance it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:3|Saying within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit|Dicentes intra se, pœnitentiam agentes, et præ angustia spiritus gementes]]; and there follows: [[Wis 5:14|Such things as these the sinners said in hell|Talia dixerunt in inferno]]. Lastly, this verse, [[82:17|Fill their faces with shame|Imple facies eorum ignominia]], can be taken in a good sense; and the sense will be: Grant, O Lord, that in the present they may be rebuked, despised and reproached, as the sinners they are, so that through their very shame they may cease to sin. For as a sinner is strengthened in his fault by flattery and most false praise, so by shame brought upon him he is drawn back from evil, when he sees himself reproved by all. [[82:17|and|Et]] so, to their salvation, [[82:17|they shall seek thy name, O Lord|quærent nomen tuum, Domine]], by saving penance and true compunction. For this seems to belong to those of whom it is written in the Gospel: [[Luke 14:23|compel them to come in|Compelle intrare]].

paras.t: Precatio. Deus supernæ majestatis, cui non est similis, propter multitudinem peccatorum non disperdas nos de gente electorum ; sed clementi bonitate facias nomen nostrum memorari in Israel in æternum.
paras.en: Prayer. O God of supernal majesty, to whom none is like: do not for the multitude of our sins [[82:5|destroy|disperdas]] us from the nation of the elect; but in thy merciful goodness cause our [[82:5|name|nomen]] to be [[82:5|remembered|memorari]] in Israel for ever.

83.title: EXPLANATIO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI TERTII: QUAM DILECTA TABERNACULA TUA!
83.title_en: Explanation of the eighty-third psalm: How lovely are thy tabernacles!
83.note: The end of the closing prayer is missing from the transcription; marked […].

paras.t: DECLARANDI nunc psalmi titulus est : In finem, pro torcularibus, filiis Core, psalmus : id est, psalmus iste in finem, id est in Christum, qui est beatitudo nostra ac vita aeterna, nos dirigens, convenit filiis Core, id est imitatoribus Jesu Christi crucifixi ; scriptus pro torcularibus, id est, de tribulationibus atque pressuris Ecclesiarum, seu ipsis Ecclesiis multipliciter tribulatis, agens et tractans. Core enim interpretatur Calvaria. Calvaria autem est locus in quo crucifixus est Dominus. Psalmus iste ad litteram de inaestimabili desiderio ferventium viatorum, ad patriam suspirantium, atque de incomprehensibili beatitudine comprehensorum scriptus videtur.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is: [[83:1|Unto the end|In finem]], [[83:1|for the winepresses|pro torcularibus]], [[83:1|a psalm for the sons of Core|filiis Core, psalmus]]: that is, this psalm, directing us unto the end, that is, unto Christ, who is our beatitude and life everlasting, befits the sons of Core, that is, the imitators of Jesus Christ crucified; written for the winepresses, that is, dealing with and treating of the tribulations and pressures of the Churches, or the Churches themselves, troubled in many ways. For Core is interpreted Calvary; and Calvary is the place in which the Lord was crucified[[John 19:17||]][[John 19:18||]]. According to the letter, this psalm seems to have been written of the inestimable desire of fervent wayfarers, sighing for the fatherland, and of the incomprehensible beatitude of those who have attained [the comprehensores, that is, the blessed who already possess God, as opposed to the viatores, the wayfarers still on the road].

paras.t: AIT ergo : Quam dilecta tabernacula tua ! id est, vehementer dilecta, multum amanda, et incomparabiliter desiderabilia sunt habitacula curiae coelestis, loca et mansiones Beatorum in patria. De quibus tabernaculis etiam ait Salvator : Facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis, ut recipiant vos in aeterna tabernacula ; et rursus : In domo Patris mei mansiones multae sunt. Non quod in coelo empyreo, quod est locus, domus et patria Beatorum, sint habitacula parietibus seu interstitiis opacis divisa ; sed pluraliter dicitur, Tabernacula, et, Mansiones, ad designandum varios gradus praemiorum in patria. Quemadmodum enim alia est claritas solis, alia claritas lunæ, alia claritas stellarum ; sic diversa est quantitas gloriæ Beatorum, secundum exigentiam meritorum eorum. Beatitudo tamen seu vita æterna quam habent, una est ex parte objecti, quæ designatur per denarium, quem singuli operarii receperunt, sicut in Evangelio Veritas docet. Itaque multum dilecta cordi devoto sunt tabernacula tua cœlestia, o Domine virtutum, id est angelorum sanctorum seu omnium potestatum cœlestium, terrestrium et infernorum. Quemadmodum enim omnes angelici spiritus, Angeli appellantur, ita et Virtutes dicuntur, secundum principem theologorum, propter efficaciam quam habent in exsequendo omnem operationem deiformem, eis a Deo præfixam. Hæc superna tabernacula, quantum ad locum corporeum, sunt unum tabernaculum, scilicet cœlum empyreum, de quo ait Apostolus : Scimus quoniam si terrestris domus nostra hujus habitationis dissolvatur, quod ædificationem habemus ex Deo, domum non manufactam, æternam in cœlis. Et ad Hebræos : Non in manufacta sancta Jesus introiit exemplaria verorum, sed in ipsum cœlum. Horum supermundanorum tabernaculorum figuræ erant tentoria filiorum Israel, de quibus ait Balaam propheta verus, sed homo iniquus : Quam pulchra tabernacula tua, Jacob ! tentoria tua, Israel ! ut valles nemorosæ, ut horti juxta fluvios irrigui, ut tabernacula quæ fixit Deus. Hæc tabernacula sibi precabatur ostendi anima Christi amore succensa, ejusque sponsa, dicens in Cantico : Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie.
paras.en: He says, then: [[83:2|How lovely are thy tabernacles|Quam dilecta tabernacula tua]]! that is, exceedingly beloved, much to be loved and incomparably desirable are the dwellings of the heavenly court, the places and mansions of the blessed in the fatherland. Of these tabernacles the Saviour too says: [[Luke 16:9|Make unto you friends of the mammon of iniquity|Facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis]], that [[Luke 16:9|they may receive you into everlasting dwellings|recipiant vos in aeterna tabernacula]]; and again: [[John 14:2|In my Father's house there are many mansions|In domo Patris mei mansiones multae sunt]]. Not that in the empyrean heaven, which is the place, the house and the fatherland of the blessed, there are dwellings divided by walls or by dark partitions; but it says *tabernacles* and *mansions* in the plural to signify the various degrees of reward in the fatherland. For as [[1 Cor 15:41|One is the glory of the sun, another the glory of the moon, and another the glory of the stars|alia est claritas solis, alia claritas lunæ, alia claritas stellarum]], so the measure of the glory of the blessed differs according to the requirement of their merits. Yet the beatitude or life everlasting which they have is one on the part of its object, which is signified by the penny that each of the labourers received[[Matt 20:9||]][[Matt 20:10||]], as the Truth teaches in the Gospel. Therefore thy heavenly tabernacles are much beloved by the devout heart, [[83:2|O Lord of hosts|o Domine virtutum]] [Latin *Domine virtutum*, literally "Lord of the powers" or "virtues", which Denis goes on to explain], that is, of the holy angels, or of all the powers of heaven, earth and hell. For as all the angelic spirits are called Angels, so they are also called Virtues [that is, Powers, the name of one of the nine choirs], according to the prince of theologians [Dionysius the Areopagite], because of the efficacy which they have in carrying out every deiform operation appointed them by God. These supernal tabernacles, as regards their bodily place, are one tabernacle, namely the empyrean heaven, of which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 5:1|we know, if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved, that we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in heaven|Scimus quoniam si terrestris domus nostra hujus habitationis dissolvatur, quod ædificationem habemus ex Deo, domum non manufactam, æternam in cœlis]]. And to the Hebrews: [[Heb 9:24|Jesus is not entered into the Holies made with hands, the patterns of the true: but into Heaven itself|Non in manufacta sancta Jesus introiit exemplaria verorum, sed in ipsum cœlum]]. Figures of these supermundane tabernacles were the tents of the children of Israel, of which Balaam, a true prophet but a wicked man, says: [[Num 24:5|How beautiful are thy tabernacles O Jacob, and thy tents, O Israel!|Quam pulchra tabernacula tua, Jacob ! tentoria tua, Israel]] [[Num 24:6|As woody valleys, as watered gardens near the rivers, as tabernacles which the Lord hath pitched|ut valles nemorosæ, ut horti juxta fluvios irrigui, ut tabernacula quæ fixit Deus]]. These tabernacles the soul on fire with the love of Christ, and his bride, prayed to be shown her, saying in the Canticle: [[Cant 1:6|Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday|Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie]].

paras.t: Verumtamen mirum videtur, cur Propheta non potius commendat amabilitatem regis et habitatoris tabernaculorum istorum, quam ipsa tabernacula : præsertim quum non propter tabernacula hæc amandus sit Rex cœlestis, sed propter Regis decorem amanda sint tabernacula ejus. Et respondendum, quod ideo tabernacula commendantur, ut cognoscamus quæ sit patria nostra, in qua mentis nostræ affectum atque intuitum semper erigere ac stabilire debemus. Nomine quoque tabernaculorum insinuatur decor, gloria et amabilitas Regis ac Creatoris ipsorum. Denique tam dilecta ac diligenda sunt tabernacula ista, quantum sunt bona, jucunda, beata. Quam autem jucunda, itemque beata consistant, inferius tangit.
paras.en: Yet it seems strange that the Prophet does not rather commend the loveliness of the king and dweller of these tabernacles than the tabernacles themselves, especially since the heavenly King is not to be loved for the sake of these tabernacles, but his tabernacles are to be loved for the sake of the King's beauty. And the answer is that the tabernacles are commended so that we may know what our fatherland is, towards which we ought always to raise and fix the affection and gaze of our mind. Moreover, by the name of the tabernacles the beauty, glory and loveliness of their King and Creator is suggested. Finally, these tabernacles are as beloved and as much to be loved as they are good, delightful and blessed; and how delightful and how blessed they are, he touches on below.

paras.t: Concupiscit et deficit anima mea. De duplici concupiscentia loquitur sacra Scriptura, quarum una est sancta et nobilis, alia fœda ac vilis. Concupiscentia sancta et clara, intellectualis vocatur : de qua in libro Sapientiæ dicitur, Concupiscentia sapientiæ deducit ad regnum perpetuum ; et Ecclesiasticus, Auris, inquit, bona cum omni concupiscentia audiet sapientiam. De concupiscentia vero immunda et vili, quæ sensualis dicta est, scribitur apud eumdem : Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere. Nunc autem de intellectuali concupiscentia, quæ est desiderium voluntatis, sermo inducitur. Itaque, Concupiscit, id est, vehementer desiderat, anima mea, cum Creatore suo esse peroptans, et tendens in atria Domini, id est in tabernacula jam prædicta : quæ appellantur tabernacula, propter inhabitationem ; et atria, propter capacitatis suæ latitudinem. Nec solum concupiscit, sed insuper deficit : quod dupliciter accipi potest. Primo sic : Deficit, id est, tantum desiderare atria ista non valet, quantum desiderabilia sunt, quia nec intellectus viatorum digne aut satis cognoscere, neque affectus eorum digne aut satis appetere potest gaudia Beatorum, juxta illud Apostoli : Oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt, quæ præparavit Deus diligentibus se. Et quasi ab eo interrogaremus, Unde hoc nosti ? respondens, Nobis, inquit, revelavit Deus per Spiritum suum. Secundo exponitur sic : Deficit anima mea in atria Domini, id est, ex vehementi affectu in alienationem seu ecstasim cecidit : quoniam ex vehementissima occupatione intellectualium potentiarum in Deo, corporalis natura mirabiliter immutatur, naturalis harmonia constringitur, corpus obrigescit et obstupescit : sicque sensitivæ potentiæ a suis operationibus suspenduntur, et homo a se ipso alienari atque deficere perhibetur.
paras.en: [[83:3|my soul longeth and fainteth|Concupiscit et deficit anima mea]]. Holy Scripture speaks of a twofold concupiscence [Latin *concupiscentia*, desire], one holy and noble, the other foul and base. The holy and glorious concupiscence is called intellectual; of it the book of Wisdom says, [[Wis 6:21|the desire of wisdom bringeth to the everlasting kingdom|Concupiscentia sapientiæ deducit ad regnum perpetuum]]; and Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 3:31|a good ear|Auris]], he says, [[Ecclus 3:31|will hear wisdom with all desire|bona cum omni concupiscentia audiet sapientiam]]. Of the unclean and base concupiscence, which is called sensual, it is written in the same book: [[Ecclus 18:30|Go not after thy lusts, but turn away from thy own will|Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere]]. Here, however, the discourse is of intellectual concupiscence, which is the desire of the will. So: [[83:3|longeth|Concupiscit]], that is, vehemently desires, [[83:3|my soul|anima mea]], longing greatly to be with its Creator, and tending [[83:3|for the courts of the Lord|in atria Domini]], that is, to the tabernacles already spoken of, which are called tabernacles because they are dwelt in, and courts because of the breadth of their capacity. And it not only longs, but also faints, which can be taken in two ways. First thus: it *faints*, that is, it cannot desire these courts as much as they are desirable, since neither can the intellect of wayfarers worthily or sufficiently know, nor can their affection worthily or sufficiently desire, the joys of the blessed, according to that word of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man, what things God hath prepared for them that love him|Oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt, quæ præparavit Deus diligentibus se]][[Is 64:4||]]. And as though we asked him, How dost thou know this? he answers: [[1 Cor 2:10|to us|Nobis]], he says, [[1 Cor 2:10|God hath revealed them by his Spirit|revelavit Deus per Spiritum suum]]. Secondly it is expounded thus: [[83:3|my soul|anima mea]] [[83:3|fainteth|Deficit]] [[83:3|for the courts of the Lord|in atria Domini]], that is, out of vehement affection it has fallen into alienation or ecstasy: for through the most vehement occupation of the intellectual powers in God, the bodily nature is wonderfully changed, the natural harmony is constrained, the body grows stiff and benumbed; and so the sensitive powers are suspended from their operations, and the man is said to be taken out of himself and to faint.

paras.t: Cor meum, id est appetitus intellectualis, et caro mea, id est appetitus sensitivus ; vel, Cor meum, id est anima, et caro mea, scilicet corpus ; exsultaverunt in Deum vivum, id est, cum exsultatione tetenderunt in Deum omnis vitæ principium, et in ipso et de ipso lætati sunt, ita quod Deus est objectum, causa et terminus lætitiæ meæ. Sed non uniformiter convenit exsultatio ista appetitui intellectivo seu voluntati, appetitui quoque sensitivo et carni. In voluntate namque est secundum essentiam ; in appetitu sensitivo, secundum redundantiam ; in carne vero, secundum aliqua signa interioris lætitiæ, sicut est serenitas vultus, risus et refloritio quædam ætatis : quia ut scriptum est, Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit, spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa. Appetitus autem superior, qui est voluntas, appetitum sensitivum movet et secum trahit, quemadmodum sphæra superior inferiorem : propterea magnæ affectiones voluntatis, in appetitum sensitivum redundant, ita quod ipse participat naturam affectionis, quæ in voluntate consistit.
paras.en: [[83:3|My heart|Cor meum]], that is, the intellectual appetite, [[83:3|and my flesh|et caro mea]], that is, the sensitive appetite; or, my heart, that is, the soul, and my flesh, that is, the body, [[83:3|have rejoiced in the living God|exsultaverunt in Deum vivum]], that is, with exultation have tended towards God, the principle of all life, and have rejoiced in him and of him, so that God is the object, cause and term of my joy. But this exultation does not belong in the same way to the intellective appetite or will, to the sensitive appetite, and to the flesh. For in the will it is according to essence; in the sensitive appetite, by overflow; in the flesh, by certain signs of the inward joy, such as serenity of countenance, laughter, and a kind of new flowering of youth: since, as it is written, [[Prov 17:22|A joyful mind maketh age flourishing: a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones|Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit, spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa]]. Now the higher appetite, which is the will, moves the sensitive appetite and draws it along with it, as the higher sphere draws the lower; and so the great affections of the will overflow into the sensitive appetite, so that it shares in the nature of the affection which is in the will.

paras.t: Etenim passer invenit sibi domum, et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos. Versiculus iste diversimode exponitur. Hieronymus enim ad litteram ita exponit, quod Propheta quodammodo probat arguens a majori, quod utique rationalis creatura habeat locum beatum, in quem deveniens quietetur ac requiescat, quoniam passer qui est irrationale animal, post volatum et lassitudinem invenit locum quo quiescat. Turtur quoque nidum habet, in quo pullos proprios collocet : ergo et homo locum sortitur, ubi opera sua reponat, sicut et Christus hortatur : Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in cœlo.
paras.en: [[83:4|For the sparrow hath found herself a house, and the turtle a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones|Etenim passer invenit sibi domum, et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos]]. This little verse is expounded in different ways. Jerome expounds it according to the letter thus: that the Prophet in a manner proves, arguing from the greater, that the rational creature surely has a blessed place, coming to which it may be at rest and repose; since the sparrow, which is an irrational animal, after its flight and weariness finds a place in which to rest, and the turtle too has a nest in which to lay its young: therefore man also is allotted a place where he may lay up his works, as Christ too exhorts: [[Matt 6:20|lay up to yourselves treasures in heaven|Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in cœlo]].

paras.t: Secundo exponitur sic : Etenim passer, id est homo pœnitens : de quo inferius dicitur, Factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto ; invenit sibi domum, id est locum misericordiæ in Ecclesia Christi, qui eum qui venit ad se, non ejicit foras ; et turtur, id est homo perfectus cœlestia speculans, invenit nidum sibi, id est mansionem, haud dubium quin in cœlo, ubi ponat, id est, finaliter statuat, pullos suos, id est opera sua, non quærens mercedem in terra ab homine, sed in cœlo a Deo. Dicitur autem homo pœnitens, passer : primo, quoniam ante conversionem, ad similitudinem passeris, mobilis erat, vagus, libidinosus et petulans ; secundo, quoniam post conversionem, ad similitudinem passeris, in alto ædificat, turrim virtutum construere cupiens, et opera sua ab insidiis dæmonum in Christo abscondens. Vir quoque perfectus, turtur ideo dicitur, quoniam desiderio cœlestium gemit, in petra quæ Christus est, nidificat, pro cantu, id est pro gaudiis mundi, gemitum habet, id est terrenarum rerum contemptum.
paras.en: Secondly it is expounded thus: [[83:4|For the sparrow|Etenim passer]], that is, the penitent man, of whom it is said further on: [[Ps 101:8|am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop|Factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto]]; [[83:4|hath found herself a house|invenit sibi domum]], that is, a place of mercy in the Church of Christ, who does not cast out him that comes to him[[John 6:37||]]; [[83:4|and the turtle|et turtur]], that is, the perfect man who gazes upon heavenly things, has found [[83:4|a nest for herself|nidum sibi]], that is, a mansion, beyond doubt in heaven, [[83:4|where she may lay|ubi ponat]], that is, finally set, [[83:4|her young ones|pullos suos]], that is, her works, seeking a reward not on earth from man but in heaven from God. Now the penitent man is called a sparrow: first, because before his conversion, like a sparrow, he was restless, wandering, lustful and wanton; secondly, because after his conversion, like a sparrow, he builds on high, desiring to build a tower of virtues[[Luke 14:28||]], and hiding his works in Christ from the snares of the demons. The perfect man, too, is called a turtle because he moans with desire for heavenly things, nests in the rock which is Christ[[1 Cor 10:4||]], and in place of song, that is, of the joys of the world, has moaning, that is, contempt of earthly things.

paras.t: Tertio sic : Etenim passer, id est ratio, quæ instar passeris sublimiter volat penna contemplationis atque virtutis, invenit sibi domum nunc in militanti Ecclesia, habitando in ea per fidem et dilectionem, et postea in Ecclesia triumphanti, habitando in ea per speciem, fruitionemque beatam ; et turtur, id est caro mortificata, spiritui prompte obediens, in operibus pœnitentiæ gemens, nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos, quoniam opera sua ponit in loco secure, videlicet non in ore hominum, sed in conscientiæ puritate.
paras.en: Thirdly thus: [[83:4|For the sparrow|Etenim passer]], that is, reason, which like a sparrow flies aloft on the wing of contemplation and of virtue, [[83:4|hath found herself a house|invenit sibi domum]], now in the Church militant, dwelling in it by faith and charity, and afterwards in the Church triumphant, dwelling in it by sight and blessed fruition; [[83:4|and the turtle|et turtur]], that is, the mortified flesh, readily obedient to the spirit and moaning in works of penance, has found [[83:4|a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones|nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos]], since she lays her works in a safe place, namely not in the mouths of men, but in purity of conscience.

paras.t: Altaria tua, Domine virtutum, Rex meus et Deus meus. Versus iste uno modo exponitur, ita ut ad præcedentem versum pertineat, et declaret quæ sit domus, et quis nidus, quem passer et turtur sibi inveniunt, utpote, Altaria tua, id est mansiones cœlestes, de quibus in principio psalmi hujus jam dictum est : quæ idcirco appellantur altaria, quia in eis incessabiliter sacrificia laudum Domino offeruntur ; imo et nostra obsequia, oblationes et vota ibi ab angelis sanctis Deo repræsentantur et immolantur. Hæc ergo altaria tua, Domine, sunt domus et nidus viatorum ad cœlos tendentium, o Domine virtutum : qui licet sis omnium Deus et rex, quoniam cuncta creasti et regis ; specialiter tamen es rex meus, quoniam specialiter provides mihi, præservando me a multis periculis et peccatis, gratiamque recte tendendi ad patriam vitæ æternæ præstando ; es etiam specialiter Deus meus, quia non tantum in naturali esse me produxisti, sed in esse supernaturali, divino atque gratifico me per gratiam reformasti, et ego te præ omnibus rebus singulariter amo et colo. Non est hoc omnium dicere, sed perfectorum dumtaxat, vel etiam ferventer efficaciterque proficientium, qui Deum quotidie fervidorum desideriorum brachiis complectuntur, dicentes : Tenui illum, nec dimittam ; et, Mihi adhærere Deo bonum est.
paras.en: [[83:4|Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, my king and my God|Altaria tua, Domine virtutum, Rex meus et Deus meus]]. In one way this verse is expounded so as to belong to the preceding one and to declare what the house is, and what the nest, which the sparrow and the turtle find for themselves; thus: [[83:4|Thy altars|Altaria tua]], that is, the heavenly mansions, spoken of already at the beginning of this psalm, which are called altars because in them sacrifices of praise are offered to the Lord unceasingly; nay, our services, offerings and vows too are there presented and offered up to God by the holy angels. These altars of thine, then, O Lord, are the house and the nest of wayfarers making for heaven, [[83:4|O Lord of hosts|o Domine virtutum]]: who, though thou art the God and king of all, since thou hast created and rulest all things, art yet in a special way [[83:4|my king|rex meus]], since thou providest specially for me, preserving me from many dangers and sins, and granting me the grace to make my way rightly to the fatherland of life everlasting; thou art also specially [[83:4|my God|Deus meus]], since thou hast brought me forth not only into natural being, but hast also re-formed me by grace into supernatural, divine and grace-giving being, and I love and worship thee singularly before all things. This is not for all to say, but only for the perfect, or for those too who are making fervent and effective progress, who daily embrace God in the arms of fervent desires, saying: [[Cant 3:4|I held him: and I will not let him go|Tenui illum, nec dimittam]]; and, [[Ps 72:28|it is good for me to adhere to my God|Mihi adhærere Deo bonum est]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxvii, 28; the words are Ps 72:28].

paras.t: Secundo exponitur versus iste per se, aliquid tamen subintelligendo, ut sit sensus : Altaria tua, Domine virtutum, sunt illa, in quibus humanus quietatur affectus, videlicet tabernacula illa superna : quæ dicta sunt nidus, propter securitatem; altaria vero, propter oblationem perfectam, praesertim quum in eis etiam Christus interpellet pro nobis.
paras.en: Secondly, this verse is expounded by itself, though something is understood, so that the sense is: [[83:4|Thy altars, O Lord of hosts|Altaria tua, Domine virtutum]], are those in which the human affection is at rest, namely those supernal tabernacles; which are called a nest because of their security, and altars because of the perfect oblation, especially since in them Christ also [[Rom 8:34|maketh intercession for us|interpellet pro nobis]].

paras.t: Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine, id est in regno cœlorum, in patria electorum, in palatio angelorum, in cœlo empyreo, in domo non manufacta, æterna, in triumphanti Ecclesia; in sæcula sæculorum, id est sine fine, laudabunt te : prout in Apocalypsi habetur : Requiem non habebant, die ac nocte dicentia : Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus, Dominus Deus omnipotens. Et alibi : Qui redempti fuerint, venient in Sion laudantes, et lætitia sempiterna super capita eorum ; gaudium et lætitiam obtinebunt, et fugiet dolor et gemitus. Tanta est equidem beatitudo habitantium in domo ista cœlesti, ut omnem defectum, omnem miseriam, omnem displicentiam, omnem insecuritatem ac terminationem excludat, omnem vero sufficientiam, omnem complacentiam comprehendat. Quidquid enim appetitur, præsto est ; quidquid respuitur, longe est. Merito igitur in Evangelio scriptum est : Beatus qui manducabit panem in regno cœlorum. Et Petrus : In Jesum, non videntes, creditis ; videntes autem, exsultabitis lætitia inenarrabili et glorificata. In hoc itaque beatitudinis regno, summa et unica occupatio nostra, totum exercitium nostrum, jucundissimumque nostrum negotium erit Deum laudare, superfelicissimam Trinitatem glorificare, Deo sublimi et benedicto incessabile Alleluia cantare, prout in Isaia scriptum est : Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea, gratiarum actio et vox laudis. Sed quis ad hanc laudem perennem, mansionemque cœlestem perduci merebitur? nisi qui nunc Dominum laudat, nunc in ejus præconiis gaudet, nunc in ejus veneratione lætatur ; qui in carne vivens, non carnaliter conversatur, sed in præsenti sæculo angelicam ac cœlestem conversationem orditur ac imitatur, implere studens quod scriptum est : Timete Dominum, et date illi honorem, et adorate eum qui fecit cœlum et terram, mare et fontes aquarum.
paras.en: [[83:5|Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord|Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine]], that is, in the kingdom of heaven, in the fatherland of the elect, in the palace of the angels, in the empyrean heaven, in [[2 Cor 5:1|a house not made with hands, eternal|domo non manufacta, æterna]], in the Church triumphant; [[83:5|for ever and ever|in sæcula sæculorum]], that is, without end, [[83:5|they shall praise thee|laudabunt te]]: as is found in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 4:8|they rested not day and night, saying: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God Almighty|Requiem non habebant, die ac nocte dicentia : Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus, Dominus Deus omnipotens]][[Is 6:3||]]. And elsewhere: [[Is 51:11|they that are redeemed|Qui redempti fuerint]] [[Is 51:11|shall come into Sion singing praises, and joy everlasting shall be upon their heads, they shall obtain joy and gladness, sorrow and mourning shall flee away|venient in Sion laudantes, et lætitia sempiterna super capita eorum ; gaudium et lætitiam obtinebunt, et fugiet dolor et gemitus]]. So great indeed is the beatitude of those who dwell in this heavenly house that it excludes all defect, all misery, all displeasure, all insecurity and ending, and comprises all sufficiency and all contentment. For whatever is desired is at hand; whatever is rejected is far away. Rightly, then, is it written in the Gospel: [[Luke 14:15|Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom|Beatus qui manducabit panem in regno]] of heaven. And Peter: in Jesus, [[1 Pet 1:8|though you see him not, you believe|non videntes, creditis]]; but seeing [Denis reads *videntes*, "seeing", where the Vulgate has *credentes*, "believing"], you [[1 Pet 1:8|shall rejoice with joy unspeakable and glorified|exsultabitis lætitia inenarrabili et glorificata]]. In this kingdom of beatitude, then, our highest and only occupation, our whole exercise and our most delightful business, will be to praise God, to glorify the more than most blessed Trinity, to sing an unceasing Alleluia to the high and blessed God, as it is written in Isaias: [[Is 51:3|Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of praise|Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea, gratiarum actio et vox laudis]]. But who will deserve to be brought to this everlasting praise and heavenly mansion, but he who now praises the Lord, now rejoices in his praises, now is glad in his worship; who, living in the flesh, does not live carnally[[2 Cor 10:3||]], but in the present world begins and imitates the angelic and heavenly way of life, striving to fulfil what is written: [[Apoc 14:7|Fear the Lord and give him honour|Timete Dominum, et date illi honorem]], [[Apoc 14:7|And adore ye him that made heaven and earth, the sea and the fountains of waters|et adorate eum qui fecit cœlum et terram, mare et fontes aquarum]].

paras.t: Insuper manifestat Propheta, quod non humana et naturali virtute, sed ope gratiæ Dei, homo perveniat ad domum cœlestem. Beatus vir, cujus est auxilium abs te : id est, felix homo nunc in spe, et tandem in re, cui tu, Domine, modo auxilium gratiæ tuæ impendis, ut operetur et adipiscatur per gratiam (quæ est supernaturale donum, omnem naturalem dignitatem et facultatem excedens) quod nec agere neque acquirere sufficit per naturam. In quo error Pelagianorum confunditur, asserentium hominem sine gratia speciali et supernaturali posse mereri atque salvari. Propterea enim ait Apostolus : Deus vivificavit nos in Christo, cujus gratia estis salvati. Et rursus : Gratia, inquit, salvati estis per fidem, et non ex operibus. Dei enim donum est, ne quis glorietur. Dominus quoque per Osee dicit : Perditio tua, Israel, ex te; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum. Igitur, Beatus vir, cujus est auxilium abs te : quia si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos ?
paras.en: Further, the Prophet shows that it is not by human and natural power, but by the help of God's grace, that man comes to the heavenly house. [[83:6|Blessed is the man whose help is from thee|Beatus vir, cujus est auxilium abs te]]: that is, happy the man, now in hope and at last in reality, to whom thou, O Lord, now givest the help of thy grace, so that by grace (which is a supernatural gift, exceeding all natural dignity and ability) he may do and obtain what he is not able to do or acquire by nature. In which the error of the Pelagians is confounded, who assert that man can merit and be saved without special and supernatural grace. For this is why the Apostle says: God [[Eph 2:5|hath quickened us together in Christ|vivificavit nos in Christo]], [[Eph 2:5|by whose grace you are saved|cujus gratia estis salvati]]. And again: [[Eph 2:8|by grace|Gratia]], he says, [[Eph 2:8|you are saved through faith|salvati estis per fidem]], and [[Eph 2:9|not of works|non ex operibus]]; for [[Eph 2:8|it is the gift of God|Dei enim donum est]], [[Eph 2:9|that no man may glory|ne quis glorietur]]. The Lord too says through Osee: [[Osee 13:9|Destruction is thy own, O Israel|Perditio tua, Israel, ex te]]: [[Osee 13:9|thy help is only in me|in me tantummodo auxilium tuum]] [the margin gives Osee viii, 9; the words are Osee 13:9]. Therefore, [[83:6|Blessed is the man whose help is from thee|Beatus vir, cujus est auxilium abs te]]: for [[Rom 8:31|If God be for us, who is against us?|si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos ?]]

paras.t: Ascensiones, id est spiritualium profectuum gradus, virtuosorum processuum incrementa, in corde suo disposuit, proponens fortiter proficere, et gratiæ Dei per liberi usum arbitrii cooperari, in valle lacrimarum, id est in præsentis peregrinationis exsilio, in quo peccata semper plangenda sunt, in loco quem posuit, id est, quem homo sibi ipsi vallem lacrimarum effecit, quoniam peccando, paradiso expulsus est, et in hanc vallem projectus. Vel, In loco quem Deus posuit homini pro valle lacrimarum, quatenus in eo vitia sua deploret, ad patriamque plorans adspiret. Unde Dominus Adæ : Maledicta, inquit, terra in opere tuo. In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo. Verumtamen de hac valle lacrimarum faciunt sibi nonnulli domum lætitiæ, utentes hoc mundo ut patria, non ut via; ut paradiso, non quasi exsilio. Talibus clamat Scriptura : Quicumque voluerit amicus hujus mundi fieri, inimicus Dei constituetur. Nos vero utamur hoc mundo tanquam peregrinatione, via, exsilio, lacrimarumque valle et carcere, et ascensiones spiritualium profectuum intra nos disponamus; consummationem vero et exsecutionem a Domino exspectemus, secundum quod a Salomone scribitur : Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: [[83:6|to ascend by steps|Ascensiones]] [Latin *ascensiones*, ascents], that is, the degrees of spiritual progress, the increments of virtuous advance, [[83:6|in his heart he hath disposed|in corde suo disposuit]], resolving to make strong progress, and to co-operate with the grace of God by the use of free will, [[83:7|In the vale of tears|in valle lacrimarum]], that is, in the exile of this present pilgrimage, in which sins are always to be bewailed, [[83:7|in the place which he hath set|in loco quem posuit]], that is, which man has made a vale of tears for himself, since by sinning he was driven out of paradise[[Gen 3:23||]] and cast into this valley. Or: in the place which God has set for man as a vale of tears, so that in it he may weep over his vices and, weeping, aspire to the fatherland. Hence the Lord says to Adam: [[Gen 3:17|cursed|Maledicta]], he says, [[Gen 3:17|is the earth in thy work|terra in opere tuo]]. [[Gen 3:19|In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread|In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo]]. Yet some make of this vale of tears a house of gladness for themselves, using this world as a fatherland, not as a road; as a paradise, not as an exile. To such the Scripture cries: [[Jas 4:4|Whosoever therefore will be a friend of this world becometh an enemy of God|Quicumque voluerit amicus hujus mundi fieri, inimicus Dei constituetur]] [the margin gives Jac. iv, 5; the words are Jas 4:4]. But let us use this world as a pilgrimage, a road, an exile, a vale of tears and a prison, and dispose within us ascents of spiritual progress; but let us await their completion and accomplishment from the Lord, according to what is written by Solomon: [[Prov 16:9|The heart of man disposeth his way: but the Lord must direct his steps|Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus]]. Therefore he adds:

paras.t: Etenim benedictionem, id est cœlestis gratiæ infusionem ac divinorum donorum multiplicationem, dabit in hac via electis suis legislator, id est Christus, utriusque Testamenti collator, qui per Isaiam admonet : Attendite ad me, populus meus, quia lex a me exiet, et judicium meum in luce populorum requiescet. Ibunt fideles de virtute in virtutem, id est de bono in melius, donec ad optimum perducantur ; ibunt de unius virtutis actu in opus virtutis alterius, nunc orando, nunc aliis succurrendo, nunc propria mala deflendo : et ita post hanc peregrinationem ab eis clare videbitur Deus deorum, id est summus et verus Deus, omnium participative dictorum deorum creator et Dominus, in Sion illa cœlesti, de qua Apostolus loquitur : Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem, et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam. Hic Deus a Sanctis in patria cernitur, quemadmodum in Apocalypsi ostenditur : Videbunt faciem ejus, et nomen ejus in frontibus eorum. Ecce quanta et quam jucunda est merces spiritualis ascensionis, in vera humilitate fundamentum habentis, cui visio Dei promittitur. Propter quod dictum est : Bonorum laborum gloriosus est fructus, videlicet Dei clara cognitio. De qua ait eadem Scriptura : Nosse te, Domine, consummata justitia est; et scire virtutem tuam, radix est immortalitatis.
paras.en: [[83:8|For|Etenim]] [[83:8|a blessing|benedictionem]], that is, the infusion of heavenly grace and the multiplication of divine gifts, [[83:8|shall give|dabit]] on this road to his elect, [[83:8|the lawgiver|legislator]], that is, Christ, the giver of both Testaments, who admonishes through Isaias: [[Is 51:4|Hearken unto me, O my people|Attendite ad me, populus meus]], [[Is 51:4|for a law shall go forth from me, and my judgment shall rest to be a light of the nations|quia lex a me exiet, et judicium meum in luce populorum requiescet]]. The faithful [[83:8|shall go|Ibunt]] [[83:8|from virtue to virtue|de virtute in virtutem]], that is, from good to better, until they are brought to the best; they shall go from the act of one virtue to the work of another, now praying, now helping others, now bewailing their own evils: and so, after this pilgrimage, [[83:8|the God of gods shall be seen|videbitur Deus deorum]] clearly by them, that is, the highest and true God, the creator and Lord of all those who are called gods by participation, [[83:8|in Sion|in Sion]], that heavenly Sion of which the Apostle speaks: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the company of many thousands of angels|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem, et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam]]. Here God is beheld by the saints in the fatherland, as is shown in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:4|And they shall see his face: and his name shall be on their foreheads|Videbunt faciem ejus, et nomen ejus in frontibus eorum]]. Behold how great and how delightful is the reward of spiritual ascent, which has its foundation in true humility, and to which the vision of God is promised. For this reason it is said: [[Wis 3:15|the fruit of good labours is glorious|Bonorum laborum gloriosus est fructus]], namely the clear knowledge of God; of which the same Scripture says: [[Wis 15:3|to know thee|Nosse te]], O Lord, [[Wis 15:3|is perfect justice|consummata justitia est]]; [[Wis 15:3|and to know|et scire]] thy power [[Wis 15:3|is the root of immortality|radix est immortalitatis]].

paras.t: Ut ergo homo hoc Dei auxilium consequi mereatur, devote nunc postulat : Domine, Deus virtutum, exaudi orationem meam, dando quod peto; auribus percipe, id est, per misericordiam et sapientiam tuam demonstra te precem meam acceptasse, Deus Jacob patriarchæ, et populi vitia supplantantis per Jacob designati.
paras.en: So that man may deserve to obtain this help of God, he now devoutly asks: [[83:9|O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer|Domine, Deus virtutum, exaudi orationem meam]], by giving what I ask; [[83:9|give ear|auribus percipe]], that is, by thy mercy and wisdom show that thou hast accepted my prayer, [[83:9|O God of Jacob|Deus Jacob]], the patriarch, and of the people that supplants vices, signified by Jacob [Jacob means "supplanter"].

paras.t: Protector noster in adversis, adspice, Deus, preces, vota, et opera mea ; et respice in faciem Christi tui, Domini Salvatoris, quem habemus advocatum apud te, et est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, secundum Joannem; qui secundum Paulum, ascendit in cœlum ut appareat nunc vultui tuo pro nobis. In hunc respice, et per omnem sanctitatem, dignitatem, ac meritum omnium quæ ipse pro nostra salute assumpsit, fecit ac pertulit, tribue nobis quod nostra opera non merentur, et quidquid in nomine ejus precamur, quatenus verificetur quod Christus tuus ait : Amen, amen dico vobis, si quid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis.
paras.en: [[83:10|O God our protector|Protector noster]] in adversity, [[83:10|Behold, O God|adspice, Deus]], my prayers, vows and works; [[83:10|and look on the face of thy Christ|et respice in faciem Christi tui]], the Lord Saviour, whom we have as advocate with thee[[1 John 2:1||]], and who [[1 John 2:2|is the propitiation for our sins|est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris]], according to John; who, according to Paul, ascended into heaven [[Heb 9:24|that he may appear now in the presence|ut appareat nunc vultui]] of thee [[Heb 9:24|for us|pro nobis]]. Look upon him, and through all the holiness, dignity and merit of all that he took upon himself, did and suffered for our salvation, grant us what our works do not deserve, and whatever we ask in his name, so that what thy Christ said may be verified: [[John 16:23|Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father any thing in my name, he will give it you|Amen, amen dico vobis, si quid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis]].

paras.t: Gratiam hanc perveniendi ad gloriam tuam, o Domine, ideo peto, Quia melior est dies una in atriis tuis, id est in praedictis tabernaculis tuis tam dilectis, mansionibusque coelestibus, super millia, id est ultra quamcumque multitudinem dierum vitae praesentis. Nulla est enim comparatio gaudiorum seu divitiarum regni coelestis, ad bona vitae praesentis ; nobiliusque exsisteret, Deum una die per speciem contemplari, quam multis millibus dierum eum per fidem conspicere. Dicit autem, Melior est dies una, etc., non quod in coelo sint plures dies, quia in coelo dies nocte non rumpitur, nec vicissitudinem temporum patitur ; sed quoniam illa una dies Sanctorum in patria, quae est participata aeternitas appellaturque aevum, multos dies continet et includit. Conjunctio quoque causalis, in principio versus istius posita, ad sequentem versum potest referri : Elegi abjectus esse in domo Dei mei, id est, malui despectus videri, humiliari, subesse, obedire, contemni et castigari in Ecclesia Christi, seu qualibet congregatione fideli, magis quam habitare in tabernaculis peccatorum, id est, quam honorari in mundo, sublimari in saeculo, praesse, dominari, hominibus impiis commisceri, conformari aut complacere. Per humilitatem namque, et non aliter, ad altitudinem pervenitur. Hinc Moyses : Recedite, inquit, a tabernaculis impiorum hominum, et nolite tangere quae ad eos pertinent, ne involvamini in peccatis eorum.
paras.en: This grace of coming to thy glory, O Lord, I ask for this reason: [[83:11|For better is one day in thy courts|Quia melior est dies una in atriis tuis]], that is, in thy tabernacles spoken of above, so beloved, and in the heavenly mansions, [[83:11|above thousands|super millia]], that is, beyond any multitude of the days of the present life. For there is no comparison between the joys or riches of the heavenly kingdom and the goods of the present life; and it would be nobler to contemplate God by sight for one day than to behold him by faith for many thousands of days. He says, *better is one day*, etc., not because there are many days in heaven, since in heaven the day is not broken by night and suffers no succession of times; but because that one day of the saints in the fatherland, which is participated eternity and is called *aevum* [the mode of duration proper to angels and the blessed, between time and God's eternity], contains and includes many days. The causal conjunction placed at the beginning of this verse [*quia*, "for"] can also be referred to what follows: [[83:11|I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God|Elegi abjectus esse in domo Dei mei]], that is, I have preferred to be looked down on, humbled, to be subject, to obey, to be despised and chastised in the Church of Christ, or in any congregation of the faithful, [[83:11|rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners|magis quam habitare in tabernaculis peccatorum]], that is, than to be honoured in the world, raised high in the age, to be over others, to rule, to mingle with wicked men, to conform to them or to please them. For it is by humility, and not otherwise, that height is reached. Hence Moses: [[Num 16:26|Depart|Recedite]], he says, [[Num 16:26|from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be involved in their sins|a tabernaculis impiorum hominum, et nolite tangere quae ad eos pertinent, ne involvamini in peccatis eorum]].

paras.t: Quia misericordiam et veritatem, id est justitiam, diligit Deus in se ipso, et item in nobis, quia per eas Deo placemus, quemadmodum Michaeas commemorat : Indicabo tibi, homo, quid sit bonum, aut quid Dominus requirat a te : utique facere judicium, et diligere misericordiam. Nam et superius dictum est, Universae viae Domini misericordia et veritas : quae etiam in omni opere Deo conveniunt. Et Salomon docet : Misericordia et veritas non te deserant, et invenies gratiam coram Deo et hominibus. Gratiam in praesenti et gloriam in futuro dabit Dominus : ab eo enim descendit omne bonum optimum, et omne donum perfectum.
paras.en: [[83:12|For|Quia]] [[83:12|mercy and truth|misericordiam et veritatem]], that is, justice, [[83:12|God loveth|diligit Deus]] in himself, and likewise in us, since by them we please God, as Michaeas records: [[Mich 6:8|I will shew thee, O man, what is good, and what the Lord requireth of thee: Verily to do judgment, and to love mercy|Indicabo tibi, homo, quid sit bonum, aut quid Dominus requirat a te : utique facere judicium, et diligere misericordiam]]. For it was said above too: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universae viae Domini misericordia et veritas]]; and these too are found together in every work of God. And Solomon teaches: [[Prov 3:3|Let not mercy aud truth leave thee|Misericordia et veritas non te deserant]], [[Prov 3:4|And thou shalt find grace|et invenies gratiam]] [[Prov 3:4|before God and men|coram Deo et hominibus]]. [[83:12|grace|Gratiam]] in the present [[83:12|and glory|et gloriam]] in the future [[83:12|the Lord will give|dabit Dominus]]: for from him comes down: [[Jas 1:17|Every best gift and every perfect gift|omne bonum optimum, et omne donum perfectum]].

paras.t: Non privabit bonis praedictis, videlicet auxilio gratiae, benedictione coelesti, et praemio gloriae, eos qui ambulant in innocentia cordis, id est, qui juste vivunt, nulli nocendo, et divinis mandatis obediendo. De quibus asserit Salomon : Qui justi sunt, habitabunt in terra, et simplices permanebunt in ea. Unde ad sanctum Job quidam dicit : Recordare, obsecro, quis unquam innocens periit? Quin potius vidi iniquos Deo flante perisse. Et alibi : Salvabitur innocens ; salvabitur autem munditia manuum suarum. Domine virtutum, beatus homo qui sperat in te, per spem formatam, prout Isaias fatetur : Deus judicii Dominus ; beati omnes qui exspectant eum. Unde alio loco scriptum est : Respicite, filii, nationes hominum, et scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino et confusus est.
paras.en: [[83:13|He will not deprive of good things|Non privabit bonis]] spoken of above, namely the help of grace, the heavenly blessing and the reward of glory, [[83:13|them that walk in innocence|eos qui ambulant in innocentia]] of heart, that is, who live justly, harming no one and obeying the divine commandments. Of whom Solomon asserts: [[Prov 2:21|they that are upright, shall dwell in the earth; and the simple shall continue in it|Qui justi sunt, habitabunt in terra, et simplices permanebunt in ea]]. Hence one says to holy Job: [[Job 4:7|Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished being innocent?|Recordare, obsecro, quis unquam innocens periit?]] [[Job 4:8|On the contrary, I have seen|Quin potius vidi]] the wicked: [[Job 4:9|Perishing by the blast of God|Deo flante perisse]]. And elsewhere: [[Job 22:30|The innocent shall be saved, and he shall be saved by the cleanness of his hands|Salvabitur innocens ; salvabitur autem munditia manuum suarum]]. [[83:13|O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee|Domine virtutum, beatus homo qui sperat in te]], by formed hope [that is, hope informed by charity, living hope], as Isaias declares: [[Is 30:18|the Lord is the God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him|Deus judicii Dominus ; beati omnes qui exspectant eum]]. Hence it is written in another place: [[Ecclus 2:11|My children behold the generations of men: and know ye that no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded|Respicite, filii, nationes hominum, et scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino et confusus est]].

paras.t: O quam gloriosum, amorosum, et sanctum psalmum audivimus! Qui etiam religiosos et claustrales praecipue consolatur, qui Domino malunt in coenobio, spreto saeculo, in humili abjectaque vita servire, quam in mundo deliciari atque florere. Amemus igitur et incomparabili dilectione praeamemus dilecta tabernacula Domini virtutum, omnia transitoria transcendendo, et velut stercora reputando. Concupiscat, et concupiscendo deficiat anima nostra in atria Dei, scientes et profitentes quoniam non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus, tanquam advenae et peregrini. Exsultemus insuper intus et foris in Domino, ejus dignitatem, bonitatem et beatitudinem contemplando, ejus beneficia recolendo, ejus promissa praestolando, eum in omnibus amando, eum in singulis venerando, intendendo et exquirendo. Conemur quoque incessanter proficere, de actu unius virtutis in operationem alterius transmeare, atque in istis divinis operibus perseverare, quoadusque Deum deorum in Sion per speciem contemplari sinamur.
paras.en: O what a glorious, loving and holy psalm we have heard! It consoles especially religious and cloistered men, who would rather serve the Lord in the monastery, the world despised, in a humble and abject life, than take their delights and flourish in the world. Let us love, then, and with incomparable love love above all else the beloved tabernacles of the Lord of hosts, rising above all things transitory and counting them as dung. Let our soul long, and in longing faint, for the courts of God, knowing and confessing that [[Heb 13:14|we have not here a lasting city: but we seek one that is to come|non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus]], [[1 Pet 2:11|as strangers and pilgrims|tanquam advenae et peregrini]]. Let us exult, moreover, within and without in the Lord, contemplating his dignity, goodness and beatitude, recalling his benefits, awaiting his promises, loving him in all things, revering, intending and seeking him in each. Let us strive also to make progress unceasingly, to pass from the act of one virtue to the working of another, and to persevere in these divine works, until we are granted to contemplate the God of gods in Sion by sight.

paras.t: Precatio. Auxiliator Deus fortis, adsit nobis, quæsumus, virtus tua hac in valle plorationis; […]
paras.en: Prayer. O God, strong helper, may thy power be with us, we beseech thee, in this valley of weeping; […] [the rest of the prayer is missing in the transcription]

84.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI QUARTI: BENEDIXISTI, DOMINE, TERRAM TUAM.
84.title_en: Explanation of the eighty-fourth psalm: Lord, thou hast blessed thy land.

paras.t: Habet præterea psalmus nunc declarandus hunc titulum : In finem, filiis Core, psalmus : id est, psalmus præsens in finem, qui Christus est, nos dirigens, cantatur et convenit filiis Core, atque imitatoribus Christi crucifixi, cujus tota conversatio erat velut quædam continua passio. Psalmus iste ad litteram scriptus est de primo Christi adventu seu incarnatione, variisque beneficiis humano generi per Christi passionem collatis.
paras.en: The psalm now to be explained has, moreover, this title: [[84:1|Unto the end, for the sons of Core, a psalm|In finem, filiis Core, psalmus]]: that is, the present psalm, which directs us unto the end, who is Christ, is sung by and befits the sons of Core, that is, the imitators of Christ crucified, whose whole life was as it were one continual passion. This psalm was written, according to the letter, of the first coming or incarnation of Christ, and of the various benefits bestowed on mankind through the passion of Christ.

paras.t: Sicut sæpe jam præhabitum est, psalmi isti, in quorum titulis ponuntur filii Core, secundum Hieronymum et Hebræos, a filiis Core seu uno eorum conscripti sunt. Secundum Augustinum vero, omnes psalmi a David editi asseruntur, et filii Core spiritualiter exponuntur, sic quod per eos intelligantur filii Domini Jesu pro nobis crucifixi, quoniam Core interpretatur Calvaria, ubi Christus crucifixus est. Hebræi vero (quos imitatur Hieronymus) asserunt, quod dum Core incepit Moysi esse rebellis, quemadmodum Dathan et Abiron et Hon de tribu Ruben, tunc filii Core consenserant patri suo, sed postmodum pœnitebant. Quum vero Moyses jusserat ut omnes recederent a tabernaculis Core et Dathan et Abiron, ne simul cum illis perirent, filii Core non recesserunt, sed cum patre suo in tentorio permanserunt, quatenus eum a sua rebellione averterent. Verum dum ille flecti contempsit, dirupta est terra sub pedibus ejus, et ipse cum tabernaculo suo a terra absorptus est, descenditque in infernum humo opertus. Et factum est grande miraculum, ut eo pereunte, filii ejus non perirent : manserant namque in aere suspensi, quousque reclusa est terra. Quæ omnia in libro Numerorum Moyses adstruit. Quibus gestis et consideratis, filii Core totis præcordiis ad Deum conversi sunt : propter quod spiritum prophetiæ recipere meruerunt, plurimosque psalmos fecerunt. Et dicit Hieronymus : Omne psalterium sagaci mente perlustrans, nihil triste in psalmis filiorum Core invenio : semper enim in psalmis eorum læta sunt omnia et jucunda ac amorosa ; sæcularibusque contemptis, cœlestia et æterna desiderant.
paras.en: As has often been said already, these psalms in whose titles the sons of Core are named were written, according to Jerome and the Hebrews, by the sons of Core or by one of them. According to Augustine, however, all the psalms are held to have been composed by David, and the sons of Core are expounded spiritually, so that by them are understood the sons of the Lord Jesus, who was crucified for us, since Core is interpreted *Calvary*, where Christ was crucified[[John 19:17||]][[John 19:18||]]. The Hebrews, on the other hand (whom Jerome follows), say that when Core began to rebel against Moses, as did Dathan and Abiron and Hon of the tribe of Ruben, the sons of Core at first sided with their father, but afterwards repented. And when Moses had commanded that all should depart from the tents of Core and Dathan and Abiron, lest they perish together with them, the sons of Core did not depart, but stayed with their father in the tent, so as to turn him from his rebellion. But when he scorned to be moved, the earth burst open under his feet, and he with his tent was swallowed up by the earth, and went down into hell covered with earth. And a great miracle took place: while he perished, his sons did not perish, for they remained hanging in the air until the earth had closed again. All this Moses sets down in the book of Numbers[[Num 16:1||]] [the margin gives Num. xvi; the earth swallows Core at Num 16:31–33, and Num 26:11 says that his sons did not perish; that they hung in the air is the Hebrews' tradition, not the text of Numbers]. When these things had happened and they had pondered them, the sons of Core turned to God with their whole heart; and for this they merited to receive the spirit of prophecy, and they composed a great many psalms. And Jerome says: Going through the whole psalter with a careful mind, I find nothing sad in the psalms of the sons of Core; for in their psalms all things are always glad and pleasant and full of love; and despising the things of the world, they long for the heavenly and eternal.

paras.t: Ait itaque sanctus Propheta : Benedixisti, Domine Pater seu Deus Trinitas, per Christi incarnationem, terram tuam, id est omnium electorum Ecclesiam, dando eis salutem et gratiam per Christi adventum. Quod enim facit incarnatio et passio Christi jam facta, hoc fecit antiquis temporibus fienda atque futura, in omnibus Christo tunc futuro per fidem formatam, id est caritati conjunctam, unitis. Unde Joannes in Apocalypsi affirmat, Agnum qui Christus est, ab origine mundi occisum. Benedictio autem Dei vocatur, collatio munerum divinorum. Avertisti captivitatem, id est obligationem ad pœnam damni propter originale peccatum, et spiritualem captivitatem qua a dæmonibus captus tenetur homo, propter jugum iniquitatis et servitutem culpæ ac dæmonis.
paras.en: So the holy Prophet says: [[84:2|Lord, thou hast blessed|Benedixisti, Domine]], O Father, or God the Trinity, through the incarnation of Christ, [[84:2|thy land|terram tuam]], that is, the Church of all the elect, by giving them salvation and grace through the coming of Christ. For what the incarnation and passion of Christ, now accomplished, does, this it did in ancient times as something yet to be done and to come, in all who were then united to Christ who was to come, by formed faith [that is, faith given its form by charity, *fides formata*], that is, faith joined to charity. Hence John in the Apocalypse affirms that [[Apoc 13:8|the Lamb|Agnum]], who is Christ, was [[Apoc 13:8|slain from the beginning of the world|ab origine mundi occisum]]. Now the bestowal of divine gifts is called the blessing of God. [[84:2|thou hast turned away the captivity|Avertisti captivitatem]], that is, the liability to the pain of loss [that is, the loss of the sight of God, the penalty of original sin, as distinct from the pain of sense] on account of original sin, and the spiritual captivity in which man is held captive by the demons, because of the yoke of iniquity and the servitude of guilt and of the devil.

paras.t: Sic igitur, Avertisti captivitatem Jacob, id est populi fidelis, vitia supplantantis, ex Jacob corporaliter vel spiritualiter nati, eripiendo eum a servitute peccati et captivitate diaboli. Christus enim fortem armatum alligavit, et principem hujus mundi foras projecit. De cujus captivitatis aversione per Christum jam facta, Zacharias lætabundus cecinit : Juravit ad Abraham patrem nostrum, daturum se nobis ut sine timore, de manu inimicorum nostrorum liberati, serviamus illi. Jeremias quoque de futura hac liberatione dicit: In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter. Et Dominus apud Isaiam ait ad Christum : Dedi te in fœdus populi, in lucem gentium, ut educeres de conclusione vinctum, de domo carceris sedentes in tenebris. Merito autem per Jacob seu populum Judæorum, intelliguntur ad litteram universi fideles, quoniam eo tempore quo scriptus est psalmus præsens, totus pene mundus ad idololatriam declinavit, præter filios Jacob : sicque per Jacob omnes designantur, qui fidem ejus sequuntur.
paras.en: Thus, then, [[84:2|thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob|Avertisti captivitatem Jacob]], that is, of the faithful people, who supplant vices [*Jacob* means “supplanter”], born of Jacob bodily or spiritually, by rescuing it from the servitude of sin and the captivity of the devil. For Christ bound the strong man armed[[Matt 12:29||]] [the margin gives Matt. xii, 29, where he binds the strong; the words *fortis armatus*, “strong man armed”, are from Luke 11:21], and cast [[John 12:31|the prince of this world|principem hujus mundi]] out. Of this turning away of the captivity, now accomplished through Christ, Zachary sang full of joy: [[Luke 1:73|he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us|Juravit ad Abraham patrem nostrum, daturum se nobis]] [[Luke 1:74|That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear|ut sine timore, de manu inimicorum nostrorum liberati, serviamus illi]]. Jeremias too says of this deliverance to come: [[Jer 23:6|In those days shall Juda be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently|In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter]]. And the Lord says to Christ in Isaias: [[Is 42:6|I have given thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles|Dedi te in fœdus populi, in lucem gentium]], that thou mightest [[Is 42:7|bring forth the prisoner out of prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house|educeres de conclusione vinctum, de domo carceris sedentes in tenebris]]. And rightly by Jacob, or the people of the Jews, all the faithful are understood according to the letter, since at the time when the present psalm was written almost the whole world had turned aside to idolatry, except the sons of Jacob; and so by Jacob all are meant who follow his faith.

paras.t: Remisisti, o Deus Trinitas, iniquitatem plebis tuæ fidelis et electæ, per Christi adventum ac passionem : qui non solum originale peccatum delevit, sed etiam actualia vitia abstulit, satisfaciendo pro totius mundi delictis, quemadmodum scriptum est : Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccata mundi. Et Apostolus : Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi. Isaias quoque : Dominus posuit in eo iniquitates omnium nostrum. Sed si virtus seu meritum incarnationis, conversationis, passionisque Christi nobis proficere debet, oportet ut applicetur nobis : applicatur autem nobis per fidem et caritatem et sacramenta Ecclesiæ. Propter quod Paulus testatur: In hoc omnis qui credit, justificatur.
