Operuisti omnia peccata eorum per Christi mortem ac obedientiam : qui quantum in se est, ita omnia peccata moriendo delevit, ac si nunquam fuissent. Idcirco tu, Deus, de Christo testatus es : Ecce ego adducam servum meum Orientem, et auferam iniquitatem terræ illius in una die, id est in die passionis ipsius.
paras.en: [[84:3|Thou hast forgiven|Remisisti]], O God the Trinity, [[84:3|the iniquity of thy people|iniquitatem plebis tuæ]], the faithful and elect, through the coming and passion of Christ, who not only blotted out original sin but also took away actual sins, making satisfaction for the offences of the whole world, as it is written: [[John 1:29|Behold the Lamb of God. Behold him who taketh away the sin of the world|Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccata mundi]]. And the Apostle: [[2 Cor 5:19|God indeed was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself|Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi]]. Isaias too: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitates omnium nostrum]]. But if the virtue or merit of Christ's incarnation, life and passion is to profit us, it must be applied to us; and it is applied to us by faith and charity and the sacraments of the Church. For this reason Paul testifies: [[Acts 13:39|In him every one that believeth is justified|In hoc omnis qui credit, justificatur]]. [[84:3|thou hast covered all their sins|Operuisti omnia peccata eorum]] through the death and obedience of Christ, who, as far as lay in him, so blotted out all sins by dying, as if they had never been. Therefore thou, O God, didst testify of Christ: [[Zach 3:8|behold I WILL BRING MY SERVANT THE ORIENT|Ecce ego adducam servum meum Orientem]], [[Zach 3:9|and I will take away the iniquity of that land in one day|et auferam iniquitatem terræ illius in una die]], that is, on the day of his passion.

paras.t: Mitigasti omnem iram tuam : id est, vindictam tuæ justitiæ in effectum misericordiæ convertisti, non ulciscendo amplius originale peccatum : quoniam propter illud nullus a beatifica visione differtur post Christi passionem, dummodo aliunde defectum non habeat, scilicet quia meritum Christi sibi applicatum non est; avertisti te ipsum ab ira indignationis tuæ, id est a magna ultione tuæ justitiæ : quoniam usque ad Christi adventum, dimisisti gentes variis erroribus falli multipliciterque damnari, sed Christo adveniente cœpit gentilitas illuminari. Propter quod Paulus: Tempora, inquit, prioris ignorantiæ despiciens Deus, nunc annuntiat hominibus ut omnes ubique pœnitentiam agant. Et Scriptura ait : Nos omnes quasi oves erravimus, unusquisque in viam suam declinavit. Sed Domino Salvatore jam nato, populus qui sedebat in tenebris, vidit lucem magnam ; cœperuntque homines proprias vias deserere, et Christi itinera ambulare, quemadmodum Joannes edocuit : Qui se dicit in Christo manere, debet sicut ille ambulavit, et ipse ambulare. Hæc autem mitigatio etiam ad Judæos extenditur, imo et usque ad patres in limbo : nam et ipsis per Christum indultus est originalis peccati reatus, propter quem retardabantur a gloria. Unde Dominus ait : Sanabo contritiones eorum, diligam eos spontanee, quia aversus est furor meus ab eis. Quod Micheas quoque introducit, dicendo : Non immittet Dominus ultra furorem suum, quia volens misericordiam est. Revertetur et miserebitur nostri ; deponet iniquitates nostras, et projiciet in profundum maris omnia peccata nostra.
paras.en: [[84:4|Thou hast mitigated all thy anger|Mitigasti omnem iram tuam]]: that is, thou hast turned the vengeance of thy justice into the work of mercy, no longer punishing original sin; for after the passion of Christ no one is kept back from the beatific vision on account of it, provided he have no defect from another quarter, namely, that the merit of Christ has not been applied to him. [[84:4|thou hast turned away|avertisti]] thyself [[84:4|from the wrath of thy indignation|ab ira indignationis tuæ]], that is, from the great vengeance of thy justice: for until the coming of Christ thou didst let the nations be deceived by various errors and be damned in many ways, but when Christ came the Gentile world began to be enlightened. For this reason Paul: [[Acts 17:30|the times|Tempora]], he says, [[Acts 17:30|of this ignorance|prioris ignorantiæ]] [[Acts 17:30|God indeed having winked at|despiciens Deus]], [[Acts 17:30|now declareth unto men that all should every where do penance|nunc annuntiat hominibus ut omnes ubique pœnitentiam agant]]. And Scripture says: [[Is 53:6|All we like sheep have gone astray, every one hath turned aside into his own way|Nos omnes quasi oves erravimus, unusquisque in viam suam declinavit]]. But now that the Lord our Saviour is born, [[Is 9:2|The people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light|populus qui sedebat in tenebris, vidit lucem magnam]] [Denis's *sedebat*, “sat”, is the wording of Matt 4:16, where this verse is quoted]; and men began to forsake their own ways and to walk in the paths of Christ, as John taught: [[1 John 2:6|He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also to walk even as he walked|Qui se dicit in Christo manere, debet sicut ille ambulavit, et ipse ambulare]]. And this mitigation extends also to the Jews, and indeed even to the fathers in limbo: for to them too the guilt of original sin, by which they were held back from glory, was forgiven through Christ. Hence the Lord says: [[Osee 14:5|I will heal their breaches, I will love them freely: for my wrath is turned away from them|Sanabo contritiones eorum, diligam eos spontanee, quia aversus est furor meus ab eis]]. Micheas too brings this in, saying: [[Mich 7:18|he will send his fury in no more, because he delighteth in mercy|Non immittet Dominus ultra furorem suum, quia volens misericordiam est]]. [[Mich 7:19|He will turn again, and have mercy on us: he will put away our iniquities: and he will cast all our sins into the bottom of the sea|Revertetur et miserebitur nostri ; deponet iniquitates nostras, et projiciet in profundum maris omnia peccata nostra]].

paras.t: Converte nos, Deus salutaris noster, conversione stabili et perfecta, ita ut toto corde, tota anima, tota virtute tibi adhæreamus per contemplationem sinceram, dilectionem ferventem, devotum et humilem cultum ; et averte iram tuam a nobis, per temetipsum descendendo ad nos, et satisfaciendo pro nobis. Sed quia superius dixit, Mitigasti omnem iram tuam, quid necesse est nunc orare ut iram suam a nobis avertat ? Et respondendum, quod Deus, quantum in se est, omnino placatus est nobis per Christum ; sed si nos Christo ingrati efficimur, gravius quam ante irascitur nobis Deus. Oramus itaque ut iram suam avertat : primo, ne dimittat nos cadere ; secundo, quatenus si ceciderimus, ipse protinus misereatur atque subveniat.
paras.en: [[84:5|Convert us, O God our saviour|Converte nos, Deus salutaris noster]], with a stable and perfect conversion, so that we may cleave to thee with all our heart, all our soul and all our strength, by pure contemplation, fervent love, and devout and humble worship; [[84:5|and turn off thy anger from us|et averte iram tuam a nobis]], by coming down to us thyself and making satisfaction for us. But since he said above, [[84:4|Thou hast mitigated all thy anger|Mitigasti omnem iram tuam]], what need is there now to pray that he turn his anger away from us? The answer is that God, as far as lies in him, is wholly appeased toward us through Christ; but if we become ungrateful to Christ, God is more gravely angry with us than before. We pray, therefore, that he turn away his anger: first, that he let us not fall; secondly, that if we have fallen, he may at once have mercy and come to our help.

paras.t: Numquid in æternum irasceris nobis, subtrahendo opem et gratiam tuam propter nostra demerita, aut extendes iram tuam, id est, continuabis tuam vindictam, a generatione in generationem, id est a qualibet generatione præcedenti in quamlibet generationem sequentem sine fine ? Non utique, quoniam tibi proprium est misereri et parcere : qui locutus es, Ego scio cogitationes quas cogito super vos, cogitationes pacis, et non afflictionis, ut dem vobis finem et patientiam.
paras.en: [[84:6|Wilt thou be angry with us for ever|Numquid in æternum irasceris nobis]], by withdrawing thy help and grace because of our demerits, [[84:6|or wilt thou extend thy wrath|aut extendes iram tuam]], that is, continue thy vengeance, [[84:6|from generation to generation|a generatione in generationem]], that is, from any generation going before to any generation following, without end? Surely not, for it is thine own to have mercy and to spare: thou who hast said, [[Jer 29:11|I know the thoughts that I think towards you|Ego scio cogitationes quas cogito super vos]], [[Jer 29:11|thoughts of peace, and not of affliction, to give you an end and patience|cogitationes pacis, et non afflictionis, ut dem vobis finem et patientiam]].

paras.t: Deus, tu conversus ad nos per tuam incarnationem et corporalem præsentiam, vivificabis nos vita gratiæ in præsenti, et vita gloriæ in futuro. Unde Christus ait : Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant. Alibi quoque : Gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est. Et ipse iterum : Ego, inquit, sum resurrectio et vita ; qui credit in me, non morietur in æternum. Vivificavit autem nos Christus, quoniam a morte peccati et nece inferni nos eruit, atque salutari sua doctrina et gratia corda nostra implevit. Et ideo scriptum est : Tempus inquirendi Dominum, quum venerit qui docebit nos justitiam ; rursusque, De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos.
paras.en: [[84:7|Thou wilt turn, O God|Deus, tu conversus]] to us by thy incarnation and bodily presence, [[84:7|and bring us to life|vivificabis nos]] with the life of grace in the present and the life of glory in the future. Hence Christ says: [[John 10:10|I am come that they may have life and may have it more abundantly|Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant]]. And elsewhere: [[John 1:17|grace and truth came by Jesus Christ|Gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est]]. And again he himself: [[John 11:25|I am the resurrection and the life|sum resurrectio et vita]], he says; [[John 11:25|he that believeth in me|qui credit in me]] [[John 11:26|shall not die for ever|non morietur in æternum]]. Now Christ brought us to life, for he rescued us from the death of sin and the slaughter of hell, and filled our hearts with his saving doctrine and grace. And therefore it is written: [[Osee 10:12|the time to seek the Lord is, when he shall come that shall teach you justice|Tempus inquirendi Dominum, quum venerit qui docebit nos justitiam]]; and again: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos]].

paras.t: Et plebs tua christiana electa et sancta, lætabitur, non in rebus carnalibus, vanis, illicitis, sed in te, tuæ bonitati, perfectioni, et beatitudini congratulando, atque de tuis beneficiis ac promissis cordialiter exsultando. Ad hanc sanctam in Deo lætitiam admonemur a Joele : Exsultate in Domino Deo vestro, quia dedit vobis Doctorem justitiæ. Isaias quoque in persona populi christiani pulcherrime ait : Ecce Deus noster iste ; exspectavimus eum, et salvabit nos. Iste Dominus, sustinuimus eum ; exsultabimus et lætabimur in salutari ejus. Hinc etiam Habacuc ait : Ego autem in Domino gaudebo, et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo.
paras.en: [[84:7|and thy people|Et plebs tua]], Christian, elect and holy, [[84:7|shall rejoice|lætabitur]], not in carnal, vain or unlawful things, but [[84:7|in thee|in te]], rejoicing with thy goodness, perfection and beatitude, and exulting from the heart in thy benefits and promises. To this holy joy in God we are exhorted by Joel: [[Joel 2:23|rejoice, and be joyful in the Lord your God: because he hath given you a teacher of justice|Exsultate in Domino Deo vestro, quia dedit vobis Doctorem justitiæ]]. Isaias too, in the person of the Christian people, says most beautifully: [[Is 25:9|Lo, this is our God, we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the Lord, we have patiently waited for him, we shall rejoice and be joyful in his salvation|Ecce Deus noster iste ; exspectavimus eum, et salvabit nos. Iste Dominus, sustinuimus eum ; exsultabimus et lætabimur in salutari ejus]]. Hence Habacuc too says: [[Hab 3:18|But I will rejoice in the Lord: and I will joy in God my Jesus|Ego autem in Domino gaudebo, et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo]].

paras.t: Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam : id est, Christum Filium tuum misericordiæ fontem, per quem tu nostri summe misertus es, manifesta oculis nostris, quatenus eum oculis mentis et corporis videamus in terra conversari : sicut per Baruch dictum fuit, Post hæc super terram visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est. Orat ergo Propheta ut Christus visibiliter in mundo appareat, assumendo naturam humanam : quod modo impletum est, prout Joannes in exordio primæ suæ Canonicæ pandit : Quod fuit ab initio, quod audivimus, quod vidimus oculis nostris, et manus nostræ contrectaverunt de Verbo vitæ. Alibi quoque : Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis. Et vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre. Et salutare tuum, id est Christum Salvatorem, per quem tu salvas nos, da nobis gratis ex tua caritate et bonitate, non ex nostra justitia, mittendo eum ad nos per nativitatem ex Virgine : quemadmodum per Isaiam prædictum est, Puer natus est nobis, et filius datus est nobis. Et alibi Christus ait : Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret.
paras.en: [[84:8|Shew us, O Lord, thy mercy|Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam]]: that is, make manifest to our eyes Christ thy Son, the fountain of mercy, through whom thou hast had the greatest mercy on us, so that we may see him with the eyes of mind and body living on the earth: as was said by Baruch, [[Bar 3:38|Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|Post hæc super terram visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]]. The Prophet therefore prays that Christ may appear visibly in the world by taking human nature: which has now been fulfilled, as John declares at the beginning of his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 1:1|That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes|Quod fuit ab initio, quod audivimus, quod vidimus oculis nostris]], [[1 John 1:1|and our hands have handled, of the word of life|et manus nostræ contrectaverunt de Verbo vitæ]]. Elsewhere too: [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us|Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis]]. And [[John 1:14|we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father|vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre]]. And [[84:8|thy salvation|Et salutare tuum]], that is, Christ the Saviour, through whom thou savest us, [[84:8|grant us|da nobis]] freely, out of thy charity and goodness, not out of our justice, by sending him to us through his birth of the Virgin: as was foretold by Isaias, [[Is 9:6|a CHILD IS BORN to us, and a son is given to us|Puer natus est nobis, et filius datus est nobis]] [Denis has *Puer* for the Vulgate's *Parvulus*]. And elsewhere Christ says: [[John 3:16|God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son|Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret]].

paras.t: Nos quoque quotidie versum istum congruenter orare debemus ad hunc sensum : Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam, id est, effectum pietatis tuæ evidenter et copiose ostende in nobis ; et salutare tuum, id est salvationem salutarem, da nobis, vel etiam Christum, dando eum nobis quotidie in Sacramento altaris, et per spiritualem adventum ejus in nobis, sicut de ipso sub nomine sapientiæ scriptum est : Da mihi, Domine, sedium tuarum adsistricem sapientiam.
paras.en: We too ought daily to pray this verse fittingly in this sense: [[84:8|Shew us, O Lord, thy mercy|Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam]], that is, show plainly and abundantly in us the effect of thy pity; and [[84:8|thy salvation|et salutare tuum]], that is, saving salvation, [[84:8|grant us|da nobis]]; or even Christ, by giving him to us daily in the Sacrament of the altar, and through his spiritual coming into us, as it is written of him under the name of wisdom: [[Wis 9:4|Give me wisdom, that sitteth by thy throne|Da mihi, Domine, sedium tuarum adsistricem sapientiam]].

paras.t: Audiam auribus mentis cum ingenti advertentia, quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus per inspirationem internam, seu illustrationem angelicam et occultam. Et merito audiam, quoniam loquetur pacem in plebem suam, id est, mihi per allocutionem internam inspirabit ea, quæ spectant ad pacem plebis suæ: quia dum mihi inspirat de Christi adventu, passione et morte, ea in me loquitur per quæ totus mundus veram cœlestemque pacem sortitur. Propterea Christo nato, angelus dixit pastoribus : Annuntio vobis gaudium magnum, quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator. Quo ista loquente, subito facta est multitudo cœlestis exercitus laudantium Deum et dicentium : Gloria in altissimis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis.
paras.en: [[84:9|I will hear|Audiam]] with the ears of the mind, with great attention, [[84:9|what the Lord God will speak in me|quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus]] by inward inspiration, or by hidden illumination through the angels. And rightly will I hear, [[84:9|for he will speak peace unto his people|quoniam loquetur pacem in plebem suam]], that is, by inward speech he will inspire in me the things that concern the peace of his people: for when he inspires me concerning the coming, passion and death of Christ, he speaks in me the things through which the whole world obtains true and heavenly peace. Therefore, when Christ was born, the angel said to the shepherds: [[Luke 2:10|I bring you good tidings of great joy|Annuntio vobis gaudium magnum]], [[Luke 2:11|this day is born to you a Saviour|quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator]]. And as he was saying this, [[Luke 2:13|suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying|subito facta est multitudo cœlestis exercitus laudantium Deum et dicentium]]: [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest: and on earth peace to men of good will|Gloria in altissimis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis]].

paras.t: Et super sanctos suos, et in eos qui convertuntur ad cor : quoniam ista locutio pacis non solum pertingit ac pertinet ad plebem communem, sed etiam ad perfectos, et ad gentiles ac peccatores, qui de idololatria, quæ summa est stultitia et irrationabilissimus error, vel de sensualitate atque perverso judicio, redeunt ad cor, id est ad usum rationis, obediendo legi divinæ, rationique rectæ.
paras.en: [[84:9|And unto his saints: and unto them that are converted to the heart|Et super sanctos suos, et in eos qui convertuntur ad cor]]: for this speaking of peace reaches and belongs not only to the common people, but also to the perfect, and to the Gentiles and sinners who return to the heart, that is, to the use of reason, from idolatry, which is the height of folly and the most irrational of errors, or from sensuality and perverse judgment, by obeying the divine law and right reason.

paras.t: Docemur hoc loco diligenter advertere, quid in nobis Dominus Deus noster loquatur, quatenus ejus inspirationi acquiescamus. Ideo namque Habacuc inquit : Super custodiam meam stabo, et contemplabor ut videam quid dicatur mihi. Sed ad hoc satis necesse est scire, quis sit instinctus divinus, quis angelicus, quis naturalis, quis diabolicus. Verumtamen quidquid menti nostræ secundum Deum et legem Christi occurrit, Deo sine periculo adscribere possumus, illudque implere seu conservare debemus. De ipsa enim increata Sapientia ait Scriptura : Omnibus mobilibus mobilior est sapientia; attingit autem ubique propter suam munditiam. Et quum sit una, omnia potest; et in animas sanctas se transfert, prophetas et amicos Dei constituit. Ideo et Joannes : Unctio, inquit, ejus docet vos de omnibus. Nec dissonat quod Paulus testatur : Dabit tibi Dominus de omnibus intellectum.
paras.en: We are taught in this place to attend carefully to what the Lord our God speaks in us, so that we may yield to his inspiration. For this is why Habacuc says: [[Hab 2:1|I will stand upon my watch|Super custodiam meam stabo]], [[Hab 2:1|and I will watch, to see what will be said to me|et contemplabor ut videam quid dicatur mihi]]. But for this it is very necessary to know which impulse is divine, which angelic, which natural, which diabolical. Yet whatever comes to our mind in accordance with God and the law of Christ we may ascribe to God without danger, and we ought to fulfil or keep it. For of the uncreated Wisdom itself Scripture says: [[Wis 7:24|wisdom is more active than all active things; and reacheth everywhere, by reason of her purity|Omnibus mobilibus mobilior est sapientia; attingit autem ubique propter suam munditiam]]. [[Wis 7:27|And being but one, she can do all things|Et quum sit una, omnia potest]]; [[Wis 7:27|conveyeth herself into holy souls, she maketh the friends of God and prophets|et in animas sanctas se transfert, prophetas et amicos Dei constituit]]. Therefore John too: [[1 John 2:27|his unction|Unctio]], he says, [[1 John 2:27|teacheth you of all things|ejus docet vos de omnibus]]. Nor is it out of tune with what Paul testifies: [[2 Tim 2:7|the Lord will give thee in all things understanding|Dabit tibi Dominus de omnibus intellectum]].

paras.t: Verumtamen prope timentes eum salutare ipsius : id est, Christus, qui est salutare Dei Patris, adest timentibus Deum timore initiali seu filiali. Nam qui Deum timet, declinat a malo : et ita Christus demoratur in corde ipsorum per gratiam. Unde superius dictum est : Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus Deum. Ecclesiasticus quoque : Qui timent Dominum, præparabunt corda sua, et in conspectu illius sanctificabunt animas suas. Ut inhabitet gloria, id est Christus rex gloriæ, qui est imago Dei invisibilis, splendor gloriæ, et figura substantiæ ejus, imo et gloria Patris, prout scriptum est, Gloria patris, filius sapiens; vel, Gloria, id est Christus, qui est honor et gloria nostra; in terra nostra, id est in Judæa, in qua Christus inter homines corporaliter vixit et habitavit, ut Zacharias testatur : Lauda et lætare, filia Sion, quia ecce ego venio, et habitabo in medio tui; et Jeremias : Exspectatio Israel, salvator ejus in tempore tribulationis, quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum?
paras.en: [[84:10|Surely his salvation is near to them that fear him|Verumtamen prope timentes eum salutare ipsius]]: that is, Christ, who is the salvation of God the Father, is near to those who fear God with initial or filial fear [initial fear is the fear of beginners, between servile fear, which dreads punishment, and the filial fear of those who love]. For he who fears God turns away from evil, and so Christ dwells in their heart by grace. Hence it was said above: [[Ps 33:10|Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him|Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus Deum]]. Ecclesiasticus too: [[Ecclus 2:20|They that fear the Lord, will prepare their hearts, and in his sight will sanctify their souls|Qui timent Dominum, præparabunt corda sua, et in conspectu illius sanctificabunt animas suas]]. [[84:10|that glory may dwell|Ut inhabitet gloria]], that is, Christ the king of glory, who is [[Col 1:15|the image of the invisible God|imago Dei invisibilis]], [[Heb 1:3|the brightness of his glory|splendor gloriæ]], and [[Heb 1:3|the figure of his substance|figura substantiæ ejus]], nay, the very glory of the Father, as it is written, The glory of the father is a wise son[[Prov 10:1||]] [so Denis; the Douay-Rheims has “A wise son maketh the father glad”]; or, *glory*, that is, Christ, who is our honour and glory; [[84:10|in our land|in terra nostra]], that is, in Judea, in which Christ lived and dwelt bodily among men, as Zacharias testifies: [[Zach 2:10|Sing praise, and rejoice, O daughter of Sion: for behold I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee|Lauda et lætare, filia Sion, quia ecce ego venio, et habitabo in medio tui]]; and Jeremias: [[Jer 14:8|O expectation of Israel, the Saviour thereof in time of trouble: why wilt thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man turning in to lodge?|Exspectatio Israel, salvator ejus in tempore tribulationis, quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum?]]

paras.t: Misericordia et veritas, id est pietas et justitia Dei, obviaverunt sibi, id est, convenerunt, apparuerunt, et sibi invicem sine discordia occurrerunt in Christo. Misericordia enim Dei in Christi incarnatione apparuit, quoniam ex ineffabili misericordia Dei factum est, ut unigenitus Filius carnem assumeret. Justitia quoque in ea relucet, quoniam Deus in Christi incarnatione implevit quod per Prophetas prædixit ac repromisit. Justitia et pax osculatæ sunt : id est, justa satisfactio, qua Christus pro nobis per viam justitiæ satisfecit, sustinendo pœnam pro culpa nostra, et confœderatio generis humani cum Deo, hanc satisfactionem concomitans, amorose in Christo unitæ sunt. Christus namque (secundum Apostolum) factus est nobis a Deo justitia et redemptio. Ipse quoque est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum. Propter quod ait Apostolus : In ipso complacuit omnem plenitudinem inhabitare, et per ipsum reconciliare omnia, pacificans per sanguinem crucis ejus, sive quæ in cœlis sunt, sive quæ in terris. Hæc quoque justitia et pax osculantur se mutuo in nobis per Christum redemptis, quoniam justificationem nobis per Christum collatam, sequitur statim in nobis pax qua Deo pacificamur.
paras.en: [[84:11|Mercy and truth|Misericordia et veritas]], that is, the pity and the justice of God, [[84:11|have met each other|obviaverunt sibi]], that is, have come together, have appeared, and have run to meet one another without discord in Christ. For the mercy of God appeared in Christ's incarnation, since it came about from the unspeakable mercy of God that the only-begotten Son took flesh. Justice too shines out in it, since in the incarnation of Christ God fulfilled what he had foretold and promised through the Prophets. [[84:11|justice and peace have kissed|Justitia et pax osculatæ sunt]]: that is, the just satisfaction by which Christ made satisfaction for us by the way of justice, bearing the penalty for our guilt, and the covenant of mankind with God which accompanies this satisfaction, were lovingly united in Christ. For Christ (according to the Apostle) [[1 Cor 1:30|of God is made unto us|factus est nobis a Deo]] justice and [[1 Cor 1:30|redemption|redemptio]]. And [[Eph 2:14|he is our peace, who hath made both one|Ipse quoque est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]]. For this reason the Apostle says: [[Col 1:19|in him, it hath well pleased the Father that all fulness should dwell|In ipso complacuit omnem plenitudinem inhabitare]], [[Col 1:20|And through him to reconcile all things unto himself, making peace through the blood of his cross, both as to the things that are on earth and the things that are in heaven|et per ipsum reconciliare omnia, pacificans per sanguinem crucis ejus, sive quæ in cœlis sunt, sive quæ in terris]]. This justice and peace also kiss each other in us who have been redeemed through Christ, since the justification bestowed on us through Christ is at once followed in us by the peace by which we are made at peace with God.

paras.t: Veritas, id est Christus Dei Filius incarnatus : qui de se ipso loquitur, Ego sum via, veritas, et vita ; de terra orta est, id est, de utero Virginis gloriosæ carnem assumpsit, et nascendo processit : sicut de hac terra, videlicet sancta Maria, per Isaiam affectuosissime dicitur, Aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem. Et justitia de cœlo prospexit : id est, æquitas Dei, seu Deus justus hunc Christi ortum approbavit, gratumque habuit, atque per eum genus humanum redemit.
paras.en: [[84:12|Truth|Veritas]], that is, Christ, the incarnate Son of God, who says of himself, [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas, et vita]]; [[84:12|is sprung out of the earth|de terra orta est]], that is, took flesh from the womb of the glorious Virgin, and came forth by being born: as is said most tenderly by Isaias of this earth, namely holy Mary, [[Is 45:8|let the earth be opened, and bud forth a saviour|Aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem]] [the margin gives Is. xliv, 8; the words are Is 45:8]. [[84:12|and justice hath looked down from heaven|Et justitia de cœlo prospexit]]: that is, the equity of God, or the just God, approved this rising of Christ and held it pleasing, and through him redeemed mankind.

paras.t: Moraliter vero, veritas de terra oritur, dum cor peccatoris rebus terrenis involutum, proprias culpas integre confitetur ; dumque Deus omnipotens peccatorem confitentem statim justificat, justitia de cœlo mox prospicit. Unde Joannes ait : Si confiteamur peccata nostra, fidelis et justus est, ut remittat nobis peccata, et emundet nos ab omni iniquitate. Convenienter autem Virgo Mater designatur per terram. Nam ut devotissimus ait Bernardus, Quemadmodum campus seu terra sine omni humano floret adminiculo, non seminatus ab aliquo, non defossus sarculo ; sic Virginis venter floruit, sic inviolata, casta, integra Mariæ viscera, æterni viroris florem protulerunt, cujus pulchritudo et gloria nunquam marcescit.
paras.en: In the moral sense, truth springs out of the earth when the heart of a sinner, wrapped up in earthly things, confesses its own faults wholly; and when almighty God at once justifies the sinner who confesses, justice forthwith looks down from heaven. Hence John says: [[1 John 1:9|If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just, to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all iniquity|Si confiteamur peccata nostra, fidelis et justus est, ut remittat nobis peccata, et emundet nos ab omni iniquitate]]. And the Virgin Mother is fittingly signified by the earth. For, as the most devout Bernard says, Just as a field or the earth flowers without any help from man, not sown by anyone, not dug with the hoe, so the Virgin's womb flowered; so the inviolate, chaste and spotless bowels of Mary brought forth the flower of everlasting greenness, whose beauty and glory never fade.

paras.t: Sed ne alicui impossibile videatur, quod Virgo generet Christum, ostendit modum generationis istius, videlicet quod non sit humana virtute, sed potestate divina. Etenim Dominus, scilicet Trinitas Deus, cujus opera sunt indivisa, dabit benignitatem, id est gratiæ misericordissimam affluentiam, dando per Spiritum Sanctum Virgini præelectæ fecunditatem supernaturalem, et plenitudinem gratiarum : prout Gabriel declaravit, dum Virgini huic locutus est : Ave, inquiens, gratia plena ; Dominus tecum. Et terra nostra, id est Virgo Maria, nostra salvatrix, mater et advocata, dabit fructum suum, Christum gignendo : sicut de ipsa superius dictum est, Terra dedit fructum suum. De quo fructu ait ad eam S. Elisabeth : Benedictus fructus ventris tui.
paras.en: But lest it seem impossible to anyone that a Virgin should bring forth Christ, he shows the manner of this begetting, namely, that it is not by human power but by the might of God. [[84:13|For the Lord|Etenim Dominus]], that is, God the Trinity, whose works are undivided [that is, whatever the Trinity works outside itself is the work of all three Persons together], [[84:13|will give goodness|dabit benignitatem]], that is, a most merciful abundance of grace, by giving through the Holy Ghost to the Virgin chosen beforehand a supernatural fruitfulness and the fulness of graces: as Gabriel declared when he spoke to this Virgin: [[Luke 1:28|Hail|Ave]], he said, [[Luke 1:28|full of grace, the Lord is with thee|gratia plena ; Dominus tecum]]. [[84:13|and our earth|Et terra nostra]], that is, the Virgin Mary, our salvatrix [she who brings us salvation, as Mother of the Saviour], our mother and advocate, [[84:13|shall yield her fruit|dabit fructum suum]], by bringing forth Christ: as was said of her above, [[Ps 66:7|The earth hath yielded her fruit|Terra dedit fructum suum]]. Of which fruit St. Elizabeth says to her: [[Luke 1:42|blessed is the fruit of thy womb|Benedictus fructus ventris tui]].

paras.t: Spiritualiter Dominus dat benignitatem, dum corda nostra implet per gratiam, nostrasque preces exaudit, peccatorem gratis justificat, impium prævenit, justum conservat, proficientemque perficit. Et terra nostra dat fructum suum, dum corpus nostrum obedit spiritui, et in piis exercitiis occupatur; quando implemus illud Apostoli : Obsecro vos, ut exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam viventem, sanctam, Deo placentem.
paras.en: Spiritually, the Lord gives goodness when he fills our hearts by grace, hears our prayers, justifies the sinner freely, goes before the ungodly, keeps the just, and brings to perfection him who is making progress. And our earth yields her fruit when our body obeys the spirit and is busied in pious exercises; when we fulfil that saying of the Apostle: [[Rom 12:1|I beseech you|Obsecro vos]], [[Rom 12:1|that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God|ut exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam viventem, sanctam, Deo placentem]].

paras.t: Justitia ante eum ambulabit : id est, justa doctrina et conversatio sancta Christum in omnibus anteibit, ita quod de corde ac ore ipsius nihil nisi justum et sanctum procedet. Cœpit enim Jesus facere et docere, haud dubium quin justa et vera. Unde Ecclesiasticus ait : Ante omnia opera verbum verax præcedat te, et ante omnem actum consilium stabile. Et ponet in via gressus suos : id est, ipse Christus opere adimplebit quod docebit. In via enim gressus suos doctor ponit, dum doctrinam, quæ est via ad vitam æternam, quam aliis proponit, ipse bene operando veram esse ostendit. Alii ita exponunt : Justitia, id est Joannes Baptista, ante eum ambulabit, quoniam Christi præcursor exstiterat ; et ponet in via gressus suos, quia implevit quod docuit. Sed quod Joannes Baptista appelletur justitia, non invenio in Scriptura canonica : quod tamen de Christo reperio scriptum in Isaia, ubi de Christo ait Pater æternus : Prope est salus mea ut veniat, et justitia mea ut reveletur.
paras.en: [[84:14|Justice shall walk before him|Justitia ante eum ambulabit]]: that is, just teaching and holy conduct will go before Christ in all things, so that nothing will proceed from his heart and mouth but what is just and holy. For [[Acts 1:1|Jesus began to do and to teach|Cœpit enim Jesus facere et docere]], and no doubt what was just and true. Hence Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 37:20|In all thy works let the true word go before thee, and steady counsel before every action|Ante omnia opera verbum verax præcedat te, et ante omnem actum consilium stabile]]. [[84:14|and he shall set his steps in the way|Et ponet in via gressus suos]]: that is, Christ himself will fulfil in deed what he will teach. For a teacher sets his steps in the way when, by doing well himself, he shows that the teaching which he sets before others, which is the way to eternal life, is true. Others explain it thus: *Justice*, that is, John the Baptist, *shall walk before him*, since he was the forerunner of Christ; *and he shall set his steps in the way*, because he fulfilled what he taught. But that John the Baptist is called *justice* I do not find in canonical Scripture; but I do find it written of Christ in Isaias, where the eternal Father says of Christ: [[Is 56:1|my salvation is near to come, and my justice to be revealed|Prope est salus mea ut veniat, et justitia mea ut reveletur]].

paras.t: Moraliter, Justitia ante eum ambulabit : id est, justitia hominis in confessione et pœnitentia culpæ consistens, adventum Christi ad animam hominis talis præcedet. Prima namque justitia hominis est, de malo pœnitere : et hæc præcurrit et præparat viam adventui Christi in animam. Et tunc Christus ponet in via sic sibi parata gressus suos, dando homini gratiam christiformiter conversandi. Sed quoniam tota nostra justitia originaliter Dei donum est, nec posset esse in homine vera justitia, scilicet meritoria et infusa, nisi Deo eum præveniente, fidem gratiamque præstando : idcirco non videtur proprie dictum, quod justitia hominis præcedit Christi spiritualem adventum ; imo per ejus adventum peccator justificatur. Aptior ergo apparet expositio prima.
paras.en: In the moral sense, [[84:14|Justice shall walk before him|Justitia ante eum ambulabit]]: that is, the justice of man, which consists in confession and penance for his guilt, will go before the coming of Christ into the soul of such a man. For the first justice of man is to repent of evil; and this runs before and prepares the way for Christ's coming into the soul. And then Christ [[84:14|shall set his steps in the way|ponet in via gressus suos]] thus prepared for him, by giving the man grace to live in a Christlike way. But since all our justice is in its origin the gift of God, and there could be no true justice in man, that is, meritorious and infused justice, unless God went before him by granting him faith and grace, it does not seem properly said that man's justice goes before Christ's spiritual coming; rather, it is through his coming that the sinner is justified. The first exposition therefore appears more fitting.

paras.t: Postremo, quis intellectus concipere, quæ lingua exprimere possit dignitatem ac laudem psalmi præsentis ? in quo primo Dei beneficia devotissime recoluntur, deinde oratio efficacissima introducitur, scilicet Converte nos, Deus salutaris noster. Et merito versus iste contra noctis insidias, dæmonum tenebras, et hominis infinitas indigentias de sero ante Completorium dicitur, quatenus diurno jam lumine recedente, mens ipsa ad Deum conversa, luce gratiæ perfundatur, atque ab omnibus sensibilibus rebus abstracta, intelligibili, incommutabili, summoque bono firmiter immergatur. Et ne tanta nobis gratia denegetur propter nostra delicta, convenientissime superadditur, et averte iram tuam a nobis. Hunc itaque versum, præsertim in Completorio, cum vehementi affectu et cordis sinceritate dicamus. In versibus quoque sequentibus spes consequendi misericordiam inflammatur, omnisque pusillanimitas ac diffidentia penitus eradicantur. Sed et versiculus iste, Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam, nonne sententiosa dulcedine ac dulci sententia omnem carnalium rerum suavitatem excedit ?
paras.en: Finally, what understanding can conceive, what tongue can express, the dignity and praise of the present psalm? In it, first, the benefits of God are recalled most devoutly; then a most efficacious prayer is brought in, namely, [[84:5|Convert us, O God our saviour|Converte nos, Deus salutaris noster]]. And rightly is this verse said in the evening before Compline, against the snares of the night, the darkness of the demons, and the countless needs of man, so that, as the light of day now withdraws, the mind itself, turned to God, may be flooded with the light of grace, and, drawn away from all things of sense, may be firmly plunged into the intelligible, unchangeable and supreme Good. And lest so great a grace be denied us on account of our sins, there is most fittingly added, [[84:5|and turn off thy anger from us|et averte iram tuam a nobis]]. Let us therefore say this verse, above all at Compline, with vehement affection and sincerity of heart. In the verses that follow, too, the hope of obtaining mercy is kindled, and all faintheartedness and distrust are rooted out entirely. And this little verse, [[84:8|Shew us, O Lord, thy mercy|Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam]]: does it not, by its weighty sweetness and sweet weightiness [*sententiosa dulcedine ac dulci sententia*, a play on words], surpass all the delight of carnal things?

paras.t: Præterea tres primos versiculos hujus psalmi, quidam ad litteram exponunt de terra Judææ, et populo Judæorum a captivitate Babylonica redeunte. Verumtamen melius arbitror, ut totus psalmus de Christo exponatur, et spirituali liberatione Ecclesiæ, secundum sensum inductum, quatenus totus sensus sit sibi connexus et consonus.
paras.en: Moreover, some expound the first three verses of this psalm, according to the letter, of the land of Judea and of the people of the Jews returning from the Babylonian captivity. But I think it better that the whole psalm be expounded of Christ and of the spiritual deliverance of the Church, in the sense set out above, so that the whole sense may hang together and agree with itself.

paras.t: Versiculum insuper illum, Misericordia et veritas obviaverunt sibi, S. Bernardus profundissime atque pulcherrime in quodam sermone pertractat : in quo sic eum exponit, quod circa mysterium redemptionis humanæ videbantur quodammodo sibi invicem contradicere misericordia Dei et veritas : quoniam misericordia exigebat miserum liberari, veritas autem dictabat reum damnari. Sed in hac obviatione justitia et pax osculatæ sunt, quia miser redemptus est, et culpa ejus impunita non fuit. Hanc vero expositionem, quoniam satis communis et prolixa est, derelinquo.
paras.en: Further, the little verse [[84:11|Mercy and truth have met each other|Misericordia et veritas obviaverunt sibi]] St. Bernard treats most profoundly and beautifully in a certain sermon, in which he expounds it thus: that in the mystery of man's redemption the mercy and the truth of God seemed in a way to contradict each other, since mercy required that the wretched be set free, while truth dictated that the guilty be condemned. But in this meeting [[84:11|justice and peace have kissed|justitia et pax osculatæ sunt]], since the wretched man was redeemed and yet his guilt did not go unpunished. This exposition, however, since it is quite common and lengthy, I leave aside.

paras.t: Precatio. Supplices, Domine Deus, clementiam tuam exoramus ; remitte iniquitatem plebis tuæ, averte a nobis iram indignationis tuæ, vivifica nos pia actione, potenti dextera tua : ut plebs tua lætetur in te pace præsenti et sempiterna.
paras.en: Prayer. We humbly entreat thy clemency, O Lord God: forgive the iniquity of thy people, turn away from us the wrath of thy indignation, bring us to life by thy loving action, by thy mighty right hand: that thy people may rejoice in thee in peace, present and everlasting.

85.title: ELUCIDATIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI QUINTI: INCLINA, DOMINE, AUREM TUAM.
85.title_en: Explanation, concerning Christ, of the eighty-fifth psalm: Incline thy ear, O Lord.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi est : Oratio David, id est […] Christi, secundum Hieronymum, in cujus scilicet persona David hic loquitur. Secundum alios, psalmus iste partim convenit Christo, et partim membris ipsius. Secundum quosdam vero, ad litteram de David exponitur.
paras.en: The title of the psalm is: [[85:1|A prayer for David|Oratio David]], that is, […] of Christ, according to Jerome; that is, David speaks here in his person. According to others, this psalm fits partly Christ and partly his members. According to some, however, it is expounded literally of David.

paras.t: Christus itaque secundum quod homo, et passioni jam proximus, ait ad Deum Patrem, seu totam superbeatissimam Trinitatem : Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam, id est, pietatem tuam paternam extende ad me, et exaudi me, dando quod postulo. Loquitur hic Propheta de Deo, quasi de homine, qui dum oratur, primo aurem suam inclinat ad deprecantem, deinde eum exaudit. Quoniam inops et pauper sum ego. Christus inops, id est sine ope alterius erat, præsertim in passione, secundum quod Isaias contestatur : Circumspexi, et non erat auxiliator. Erat etiam pauper, sicut de eo ait Apostolus : Quum dives esset, propter nos pauper factus est.
paras.en: Christ, then, as man, and with his passion now at hand, says to God the Father, or to the whole most blessed Trinity: [[85:1|Incline thy ear, O Lord|Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam]], that is, stretch out thy fatherly kindness to me, [[85:1|and hear me|et exaudi me]], by granting what I ask. The Prophet speaks here of God as of a man who, when he is entreated, first inclines his ear to the one praying and then hears him. [[85:1|for I am needy and poor|Quoniam inops et pauper sum ego]]. Christ was needy [*inops*], that is, without the help [*ops*] of another, above all in his passion, as Isaias testifies: [[Is 63:5|I looked about, and there was none to help|Circumspexi, et non erat auxiliator]]. He was also poor, as the Apostle says of him: [[2 Cor 8:9|being rich he became poor for your sakes|Quum dives esset, propter nos pauper factus est]].

paras.t: Custodi animam meam, id est, vitam corporalem conserva, ne a Judæis, Herode, aut aliunde occidar ante tempus passioni præordinatum. Hoc Christus petere potuit, quando quærebant eum Judæi præcipitare et lapidare. Non autem orabat Christus custodiri a ruina peccati, quoniam comprehensor erat, et confirmatus in bono. Quoniam sanctus sum. Hic Christus meritum suum allegat, cur dignus sit exaudiri : Quoniam, inquit, sanctus sum. Christus enim ut Deus, essentialiter sanctus est, et sanctitas infinita ; in quantum vero […] est homo, omnium creaturarum sanctitatem solus excedit : propter quod, Sanctus Sanctorum vocatur a Daniele : Ungatur Sanctus Sanctorum. Unde et inimicus ejus diabolus compulsus est dicere : Scio quia sis Sanctus Dei.
paras.en: [[85:2|Preserve my soul|Custodi animam meam]], that is, keep my bodily life, so that I be not slain by the Jews, by Herod, or by any other before the time foreordained for my passion. Christ could ask this when the Jews sought to cast him down headlong[[Luke 4:29||]] and to stone him[[John 10:31||]][[John 8:59||]]. But Christ did not pray to be kept from the fall of sin, since he was a comprehensor [that is, one who already enjoys the vision of God, as the blessed in heaven do] and confirmed in good. [[85:2|for I am holy|Quoniam sanctus sum]]. Here Christ puts forward his merit, why he is worthy to be heard: [[85:2|For|Quoniam]], he says, [[85:2|I am holy|sanctus sum]]. For Christ as God is holy by his essence, and is infinite holiness; and inasmuch as he […] is man, he alone surpasses the holiness of all creatures: for which reason he is called the Holy of Holies by Daniel: [[Dan 9:24|the Saint of saints may be anointed|Ungatur Sanctus Sanctorum]]. Hence even his enemy the devil was compelled to say: [[Mark 1:24|I know who thou art, the Holy One of God|Scio quia sis Sanctus Dei]].

paras.t: Salvum fac servum tuum, id est me Christum, qui propter homines redimendos formam servi accepi : de quo tu dicis, Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum ; et qui ad te ait, Hæc dicit Dominus, formans me ex utero servum sibi, ut reducam Jacob ad eum. Itaque, Salvum fac servum tuum, o Deus meus, qui es omnium Deus generaliter, sed meus Deus summe et specialiter, sicut quem incomparabiliter colo et diligo, et a quo incomparabiliter electus atque dilectus sum ; sperantem in te, id est in tua virtute et bonitate. Christus namque, quamvis spem (quæ est theologica virtus) non habuit, nihilo minus in quantum homo passibilis, speravit in Deo per quamdam fiducialem confidentiam, qua exspectavit ab eo adipisci omne bonum quod concupivit. Petit autem Christus salvari a Deo, non utique a peccato, a morte perpetua, quoniam peccatum non habuit ; sed a passibilitate corporis, a rabie Judæorum, a corporis morte per resurrectionem beatam, sicut superius de eo inductum est, Salva me ex ore leonis, etc. Unde et ipse ait : Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora.
paras.en: [[85:2|save thy servant|Salvum fac servum tuum]], that is, me, Christ, who took the form of a servant[[Phil 2:7||]] to redeem men: of whom thou sayest, [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum]]; and who says to thee, [[Is 49:5|saith the Lord, that formed me from the womb to be his servant, that I may bring back Jacob unto him|Hæc dicit Dominus, formans me ex utero servum sibi, ut reducam Jacob ad eum]]. So: [[85:2|save thy servant|Salvum fac servum tuum]], [[85:2|O my God|o Deus meus]], who art the God of all in general, but my God supremely and in a special way, as one whom I worship and love beyond compare, and by whom I am chosen and loved beyond compare; [[85:2|that trusteth in thee|sperantem in te]], that is, in thy power and goodness. For although Christ did not have hope (which is a theological virtue) [that is, since he already saw God, there was nothing left for him to hope for in the strict sense], nevertheless, inasmuch as he was man and able to suffer, he hoped in God with a kind of trusting confidence, by which he expected to obtain from him every good that he desired. And Christ asks to be saved by God, not indeed from sin or from everlasting death, since he had no sin; but from the body's capacity to suffer, from the rage of the Jews, and from the death of the body by a blessed resurrection, as was brought forward of him above: [[Ps 21:22|Save me from the lion's mouth|Salva me ex ore leonis]], etc. Hence he himself says: [[John 12:27|Father, save me from this hour|Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora]].

paras.t: Miserere mei, Domine Pater, liberando me a præsentis vitæ pœnis atque miseriis, quoniam ad te clamavi corde ardenti seu voce sublimi, tota die, id est cunctis diebus quibus vixi in mundo. Christus namque, etiam ut homo, semper in actu divinæ contemplationis dilectionisque fuit : et ita indesinenter oravit, quum oratio (secundum Damascenum) sit ascensus mentis in Deum, nec cesset orare, qui non cessat laudabiliter agere. Oravit ergo Salvator jugiter, et præsertim pro humana salute.
paras.en: [[85:3|Have mercy on me, O Lord|Miserere mei, Domine]] the Father, by freeing me from the pains and miseries of this present life, [[85:3|for I have cried to thee|quoniam ad te clamavi]] with a burning heart or a loud voice, [[85:3|all the day|tota die]], that is, all the days that I lived in the world. For Christ, even as man, was always in the act of divine contemplation and love: and so he prayed without ceasing, since prayer (according to Damascene) is the ascent of the mind to God, and he does not cease to pray who does not cease to act praiseworthily. The Saviour therefore prayed continually, and above all for the salvation of mankind.

paras.t: Lætifica animam servi tui, lætitia accidentalis præmii. Anima namque Christi incessabiliter erat in gaudio beatificæ fruitionis ; sed animam suam, quæ tristis erat in passione, ita ut diceret, Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem, petit lætificari in resurrectione de corporis sui glorificatione, patrum in limbo exsistentium eductione, omnium electorum salute seu justificatione. Mortuus est enim propter delicta nostra, et resurrexit propter justificationem nostram, secundum Apostolum. Quoniam ad te, Domine, animam meam levavi, contemplando, seu intente orando.
paras.en: [[85:4|Give joy to the soul of thy servant|Lætifica animam servi tui]], with the joy of the accidental reward [that is, the joy added to the essential bliss of seeing God, such as the glory of the body]. For the soul of Christ was ceaselessly in the joy of the beatific enjoyment [of God]; but he asks that his soul, which was sorrowful in his passion, so that he said, [[Mark 14:34|My soul is sorrowful even unto death|Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem]], may be gladdened in the resurrection by the glorifying of his body, by the leading forth of the fathers who were in limbo, and by the salvation or justification of all the elect. For he died [[Rom 4:25|for our sins and rose again for our justification|propter delicta nostra, et resurrexit propter justificationem nostram]], according to the Apostle. [[85:4|for to thee, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul|Quoniam ad te, Domine, animam meam levavi]], by contemplating, or by praying intently.

paras.t: Quoniam tu, Domine, Deus Pater, seu Trinitas benedicta, es suavis et mitis. Deus vere, proprie et naturaliter, imo superessentialiter incircumscriptibiliterque suavis est ; et ipsa divina essentia est dulcedo fontana, viva, simplex et infinita, omnem sensum exsuperans, quantum ad suam plenitudinem, omni menti creatæ ignota et inexperta, a qua fluit omnis suavitas, omnis consonantia, omnis fragrantia. Mititas vero seu mansuetudo, Deo non competit proprie, sicut nec cæteræ virtutes morales, circa passionum moderationem versantes : sed sicut Deo adscribitur ira, non propter veritatem affectus, sed propter similitudinem effectus ; sic mititas, quæ proprie appellatur virtus moralis, passionem iræ refrenans, Deo adscribitur transumptive, videlicet quia justam vindictam relaxat. Itaque Deus suavis est justis, ipsum pure et amorose contemplantibus, in quorum affectu divinæ dulcedinis degustatio, omnem mundanæ delectationis fallaciam facit odibilem. Mitis quoque est Deus peccatoribus ad ipsum toto corde redeuntibus, quoniam talibus, per modum hominis mansueti, cito omnem ultionem indulget, quemadmodum Jeremias ait : Revertere ad me, et non avertam faciem meam. Et multæ misericordiæ omnibus invocantibus te : id est, multum misericors es, multiplicemque pietatis effectum impendis cunctis te intime deprecantibus : sicut habetur, Pius et misericors est Deus, et remittit in tempore tribulationis peccata, et protector est omnibus exquirentibus se in veritate ; ibidemque, Quis invocavit illum, et despexit eum?
paras.en: [[85:5|For thou, O Lord|Quoniam tu, Domine]], God the Father, or blessed Trinity, art [[85:5|sweet and mild|suavis et mitis]]. God is sweet truly, properly and by nature, nay, above all being and beyond all bounds; and the divine essence itself is a sweetness that is a fountain, living, simple and infinite, surpassing all sense, unknown and untasted in its fullness by every created mind, from which flows all sweetness, all harmony, all fragrance. Mildness, or gentleness, does not properly belong to God, any more than the other moral virtues, which are concerned with moderating the passions: but as anger is ascribed to God, not because the feeling is truly in him, but because of a likeness in the effect, so mildness, which properly is called a moral virtue that reins in the passion of anger, is ascribed to God by transference [that is, figuratively], namely because he remits just vengeance. So God is sweet to the just, who contemplate him purely and lovingly, in whose affection the tasting of the divine sweetness makes every deceit of worldly delight hateful. God is also mild to sinners who return to him with their whole heart, since, in the manner of a gentle man, he quickly forgoes all punishment of such as these, as Jeremias says: [[Jer 3:1|return to me|Revertere ad me]], and [[Jer 3:12|I will not turn away my face|non avertam faciem meam]]. [[85:5|and plenteous in mercy to all that call upon thee|Et multæ misericordiæ omnibus invocantibus te]]: that is, thou art very merciful, and bestowest manifold effects of thy kindness on all who entreat thee from the heart: as we read, [[Ecclus 2:13|God is compassionate and merciful, and will forgive sins in the day of tribulation: and he is a protector to all that seek him in truth|Pius et misericors est Deus, et remittit in tempore tribulationis peccata, et protector est omnibus exquirentibus se in veritate]]; and in the same place, [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath called upon him, and he despised him|Quis invocavit illum, et despexit eum]]?

paras.t: Auribus percipe, Domine, orationem meam. Superius dixit singulariter, Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam : et ibi per aurem, intellecta est misericordia Creatoris ; nunc vero pluraliter, Auribus percipe. Quid ergo modo per aures Dei, nisi misericordiam et scientiam ejus, intelligendum videtur? Per misericordiam siquidem Deus exaudit, per scientiam vero omnia audit. Interdum autem per aures Dei non designantur misericordia et scientia, sed scientia et justitia, sicut dum Dominus ait : Superbia tua ascendit in aures meas, videlicet ut eam juste ulciscar. His igitur auribus percipe, Domine, orationem meam, ut eam tibimetipsi tenaciter imprimas, non obliviscendo ipsius, id est non tardando ejus effectum seu exauditionem. Ideo subditur : et intende voci deprecationis meæ, id est, orationem meam vocalem diligenter ac pie adverte.
paras.en: [[85:6|Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer|Auribus percipe, Domine, orationem meam]]. Above he said in the singular, [[85:1|Incline thy ear, O Lord|Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam]]: and there by the ear the Creator's mercy was understood; but now in the plural, [[85:6|Give ear|Auribus percipe]] [literally, "perceive with thine ears"]. What, then, seems to be meant here by the ears of God, if not his mercy and his knowledge? For by his mercy God hearkens, and by his knowledge he hears all things. Sometimes, however, the ears of God signify not mercy and knowledge but knowledge and justice, as when the Lord says: [[Is 37:29|thy pride came up to my ears|Superbia tua ascendit in aures meas]], namely so that I may justly punish it. With these ears, therefore, [[85:6|Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer|percipe, Domine, orationem meam]], so that thou mayest imprint it firmly on thyself, not forgetting it, that is, not delaying its effect or its hearing. Therefore it is added: [[85:6|and attend to the voice of my petition|et intende voci deprecationis meæ]], that is, mark my spoken prayer diligently and kindly.

paras.t: In die tribulationis meæ, id est tempore persecutionis et passionis, clamavi ad te, dicendo : Pater, si fieri potest, transeat a me calix iste ; et, Pater, ignosce illis ; et, In manus tuas commendo spiritum meum. Fiducialiter autem et secure te deprecatus sum, quia exaudisti me semper in omnibus ; et ego ipse dixi : Pater, gratias ago tibi, quoniam audisti me. Ego autem sciebam quoniam semper me audis.
paras.en: [[85:7|in the day of my trouble|In die tribulationis meæ]], that is, in the time of persecution and passion, [[85:7|I have called upon thee|clamavi ad te]], saying: Father, [[Matt 26:39|if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me|si fieri potest, transeat a me calix iste]]; and, [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them|Pater, ignosce illis]]; and, [[Luke 23:46|into thy hands I commend my spirit|In manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]. And I besought thee confidently and securely, [[85:7|because thou hast heard me|quia exaudisti me]] always in all things; and I myself said: [[John 11:41|Father, I give thee thanks that thou hast heard me|Pater, gratias ago tibi, quoniam audisti me]]. [[John 11:42|And I knew that thou hearest me always|Ego autem sciebam quoniam semper me audis]].

paras.t: Non est similis tui in diis, Domine : quoniam omnes deos, qui vel mendaciter dii appellantur et veraciter dæmones sunt, vel gratiam divinitatis excellenter participant, per quam efficiuntur divinæ consortes naturæ, et dii dicuntur per participationem, tu, summe veraxque Deus, in infinitum excellis : sicut et Moyses loquitur : Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine? quis similis tui, magnificus in sanctitate, terribilis atque laudabilis, et faciens mirabilia? Sophonias quoque protestatur : Horribilis Dominus, et attenuabit omnes deos terræ. Et non est secundum opera tua, id est, non invenitur qui tibi similia possit efficere. Multa namque sunt opera tibi propria, quæ nulli creaturæ conveniunt, sicut creatio, justificatio, felicitatio, cordium perscrutatio, futurorum pure contingentium certa prænotio, transsubstantiatio, miraculorum operatio. De talibus operibus Christus præcipue ait : Pater meus usquemodo operatur, et ego operor.
paras.en: [[85:8|There is none among the gods like unto thee, O Lord|Non est similis tui in diis, Domine]]: for all the gods, whether those who are falsely called gods and are in truth demons, or those who share in an excellent way in the grace of the Godhead, by which they are made partakers of the divine nature and are called gods by participation, thou, the supreme and true God, infinitely excellest: as Moses too says: [[Ex 15:11|Who is like to thee, among the strong, O Lord? who is like to thee, glorious in holiness, terrible and praise-worthy, doing wonders?|Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine? quis similis tui, magnificus in sanctitate, terribilis atque laudabilis, et faciens mirabilia]] Sophonias also declares: [[Soph 2:11|The Lord shall be terrible|Horribilis Dominus]], [[Soph 2:11|and shall consume all the gods of the earth|et attenuabit omnes deos terræ]]. [[85:8|and there is none according to thy works|Et non est secundum opera tua]], that is, none is found who can do the like of what thou doest. For there are many works proper to thee which belong to no creature, such as creation, justification, the bestowing of beatitude, the searching of hearts, the certain foreknowledge of purely contingent things to come, transubstantiation, the working of miracles. Of such works above all Christ says: [[John 5:17|My Father worketh until now; and I work|Pater meus usquemodo operatur, et ego operor]].

paras.t: Omnes gentes quascumque fecisti, venient et adorabunt coram te, Domine. Hæc est prophetia de gentium illuminatione et vocatione ad fidem : estque distributio ista intelligenda sicut et illa qua dictum est Abrahæ, In semine tuo benedicentur omnes familiæ terræ ; et qua ait Virgo Christifera, Beatam me dicent omnes generationes. Non enim est in istis distributio pro singulis generum, sed pro generibus singulorum. Est igitur sensus : Omnes gentes quascumque fecisti, id est quidam de omni genere hominum a te creatorum, venient ad fidem, et adorabunt coram te, Domine, qui omnia cernis. Adorabunt autem te Deum in spiritu et veritate, sicut apud Sophoniam prædixisti : Quia tunc reddam populis labium electum, ut invocent omnes nomen Domini, et serviant ei humero uno ; et alibi : Ecce levo ad gentes manum meam, et exaltabo ad populos signum meum. Quæ omnia apud Danielem clare tanguntur his verbis : Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei. Et glorificabunt nomen tuum, id est, te gloriosum esse verbis pronuntiabunt, et opere demonstrabunt, sicut per Isaiam pulchre inducitur : In doctrinis glorificate Dominum, in insulis maris nomen Domini Dei Israel. A finibus terræ laudes audivimus, gloriam Justi, scilicet Christi.
paras.en: [[85:9|All the nations thou hast made shall come and adore before thee, O Lord|Omnes gentes quascumque fecisti, venient et adorabunt coram te, Domine]]. This is a prophecy of the enlightening of the Gentiles and their calling to the faith: and this distribution [that is, the word *all*, as the logicians speak of a universal term] is to be understood as is that in which it was said to Abraham, [[Gen 22:18|in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed|In semine tuo benedicentur omnes familiæ terræ]] [Denis's wording, *omnes familiæ terræ*, "all the families of the earth", is that of Acts 3:25], and that in which the Virgin who bore Christ says, [[Luke 1:48|all generations shall call me blessed|Beatam me dicent omnes generationes]]. For in these the distribution is not over every individual of each kind, but over the kinds of individuals [that is, *all* means some of every kind, not every single one]. The sense, then, is: [[85:9|All the nations thou hast made|Omnes gentes quascumque fecisti]], that is, some of every kind of men created by thee, [[85:9|shall come|venient]] to the faith, [[85:9|and adore before thee, O Lord|et adorabunt coram te, Domine]], who seest all things. And they shall adore thee, God, in spirit and in truth, as thou didst foretell in Sophonias: [[Soph 3:9|Because then I will restore to the people a chosen lip, that all may call upon the name of the Lord, and may serve him with one shoulder|Quia tunc reddam populis labium electum, ut invocent omnes nomen Domini, et serviant ei humero uno]]; and elsewhere: [[Is 49:22|Behold I will lift up my hand to the Gentiles, and will set up my standard to the people|Ecce levo ad gentes manum meam, et exaltabo ad populos signum meum]] [the margin gives Is. xix, 22; the words are Is 49:22]. All of this is touched on clearly in Daniel in these words: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]]. [[85:9|and they shall glorify thy name|Et glorificabunt nomen tuum]], that is, they shall proclaim in words that thou art glorious, and show it in deed, as is beautifully set forth through Isaias: [[Is 24:15|glorify ye the Lord in instruction: the name of the Lord God of Israel in the islands of the sea|In doctrinis glorificate Dominum, in insulis maris nomen Domini Dei Israel]]. [[Is 24:16|From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the just one|A finibus terræ laudes audivimus, gloriam Justi]], that is, of Christ.

paras.t: Quoniam magnus es tu : juxta illud : Adonai Domine, magnus es tu, et præclarus in virtute. Denique tam magnus es, ut magnitudinis tuæ nullus sit finis. Et faciens mirabilia in cœlo et in terra. Tu es Deus solus : qui locutus es, Videte quia ego sim solus, et non sit alius Deus præter me : et rursus, Ego sum Dominus faciens omnia, extendens cœlos solus, stabiliens terram, et nullus mecum. Sumitur autem Deus in his locis absolute, et pro Deo Trinitate. Unde Apostolus ait : Unus Deus, una fides, unum Baptisma ; et iterum : Etsi sint qui dicantur dii et domini, nobis tamen unus Deus est ex quo omnia, et unus Dominus per quem omnia.
paras.en: [[85:10|For thou art great|Quoniam magnus es tu]]: according to that: [[Jdt 16:16|O Adonai, Lord, great art thou, and glorious in thy power|Adonai Domine, magnus es tu, et præclarus in virtute]] [the margin gives only Judith xvi]. Indeed, thou art so great that of thy greatness there is no end[[Ps 144:3||]]. [[85:10|and dost wonderful things|Et faciens mirabilia]] in heaven and on earth. [[85:10|thou art God alone|Tu es Deus solus]]: who hast spoken, [[Deut 32:39|See ye that I alone am, and there is no other God besides me|Videte quia ego sim solus, et non sit alius Deus præter me]]: and again, [[Is 44:24|I am the Lord, that make all things, that alone stretch out the heavens, that established the earth, and there is none with me|Ego sum Dominus faciens omnia, extendens cœlos solus, stabiliens terram, et nullus mecum]]. Now *God* is taken in these places absolutely, and for God the Trinity. Hence the Apostle says: One God, [[Eph 4:5|one faith, one baptism|una fides, unum Baptisma]] [the Vulgate has *Unus Dominus*, "One Lord"; "one God" follows in Eph 4:6]; and again: [[1 Cor 8:5|although there be that are called gods|Etsi sint qui dicantur dii]] and lords, [[1 Cor 8:6|Yet to us there is but one God|nobis tamen unus Deus est]], [[1 Cor 8:6|of whom are all things|ex quo omnia]], [[1 Cor 8:6|and one Lord|et unus Dominus]] [[1 Cor 8:6|by whom are all things|per quem omnia]].

paras.t: Deduc me, Domine, in via tua. Secundum expositores, Christus hunc versum dicit, non pro se ipso, sed pro corpore suo mystico : secundum quem modum ait apud Zachariam, Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei ; et in Actibus, Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? Potest tamen hic versus de Christo exponi hoc modo : Deduc me, Domine, in via tua. Via Dei fuit, qua anima Christi in limbum patrum descendit, atque post resurrectionem in cœlos conscendit : et in hac via petiit Christus a Deo deduci, sicut et Sancti in patria orant in corpore glorificari. Omne etenim bonum futurum, nondum adeptum, quod licite desideratur, licenter oratur, secundum Augustinum. Et ingrediar in regnum cœlorum usque ad dexteram tuam, in veritate tua, id est, quemadmodum per sanctos Prophetas veraciter promisisti. Scriptum est enim : Adspiciebam in visione noctis, et ecce in nubibus cœli quasi Filius hominis veniebat, et usque ad Antiquum dierum, id est Deum æternum, pervenit ; et in conspectu ejus obtulerunt eum, et dedit ei potestatem et honorem et regnum. Lætetur cor meum, ut timeat nomen tuum timore filiali ac casto. Hoc Christus dicit, non orando ut sic sit, sed cordialiter exsultando quia sic est, sicut et Sancti in patria dicunt illud in Apocalypsi : Gaudeamus et exsultemus, et demus gloriam Deo. Timuit autem Christus ut homo Deum timore casto, illo præcipue qui est unum septem donorum Spiritus Sancti, secundum quod scriptum est : Replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini.
paras.en: [[85:11|Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way|Deduc me, Domine, in via tua]]. According to the expositors, Christ says this verse not for himself but for his mystical body: in which way he says in Zacharias, [[Zach 2:8|he that toucheth you, toucheth the apple of my eye|Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei]]; and in the Acts, [[Acts 9:4|Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me|Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris]]? Yet this verse can be expounded of Christ in this way: [[85:11|Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way|Deduc me, Domine, in via tua]]. The way of God was that by which the soul of Christ went down into the limbo of the fathers, and after the resurrection went up into heaven: and Christ asked God to be led in this way, just as the Saints in the fatherland pray to be glorified in the body. For every good to come, not yet obtained, that is lawfully desired, may lawfully be prayed for, according to Augustine. [[85:11|and I will walk|Et ingrediar]] into the kingdom of heaven, even to thy right hand, [[85:11|in thy truth|in veritate tua]], that is, as thou hast truly promised through the holy Prophets. For it is written: [[Dan 7:13|I beheld, therefore, in the vision of the night, and lo, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and he came even to the ancient of days|Adspiciebam in visione noctis, et ecce in nubibus cœli quasi Filius hominis veniebat, et usque ad Antiquum dierum]], that is, to the eternal God, [[Dan 7:13|and they presented him before him|et in conspectu ejus obtulerunt eum]], [[Dan 7:14|and he gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom|et dedit ei potestatem et honorem et regnum]]. [[85:11|let my heart rejoice that it may fear thy name|Lætetur cor meum, ut timeat nomen tuum]] with a filial and chaste fear. Christ says this not praying that it may be so, but rejoicing from the heart because it is so, as the Saints in the fatherland also say that word in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:7|Let us be glad and rejoice and give glory to him|Gaudeamus et exsultemus, et demus gloriam Deo]]. Now Christ as man feared God with a chaste fear, above all with that which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, according as it is written: [[Is 11:3|And he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord|Replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini]].

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, Domine Deus meus, id est, laudabo te, in toto corde meo, id est integro, non diviso, nec vago affectu et intellectu. Hoc Christo perfectissime competit, quoniam indesinenter tota anima, tota virtute, tota mente ferebatur in Deum, sicut et Sancti in patria, nec erat cor suum per evagationem aut inordinatum amorem divisum. Hoc modo confessus est Christus Deo, ex toto corde ipsum laudando, prout de ipso in Evangelio scriptum est : Exsultavit Jesus in Spiritu Sancto, et dixit : Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis. Et alibi Christus Patri confitetur confessione laudis, dum eum justum et sanctum appellat, eique ait : Sermo tuus veritas est. Et glorificabo nomen tuum in æternum verbis et factis, per me ipsum et ministros, qui per meam doctrinam et gratiam ad te glorificandum inducuntur. Unde ait Salvator : Ego non quæro gloriam meam, sed honorifico Patrem meum.
paras.en: [[85:12|I will praise thee, O Lord my God|Confitebor tibi, Domine Deus meus]] [*confitebor*, literally "I will confess to thee"], that is, I will praise thee, [[85:12|with my whole heart|in toto corde meo]], that is, with an affection and understanding that is entire, not divided nor wandering. This befits Christ most perfectly, since he was borne towards God unceasingly with all his soul, all his strength, all his mind, as are the Saints in the fatherland, and his heart was not divided by wandering or by disordered love. In this way Christ confessed to God, praising him with his whole heart, as it is written of him in the Gospel: [[Luke 10:21|he rejoiced in the Holy Ghost and said|Exsultavit Jesus in Spiritu Sancto, et dixit]]: [[Matt 11:25|I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of Heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones|Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]. And elsewhere Christ confesses to the Father with the confession of praise, when he calls him just[[John 17:25||]] and holy[[John 17:11||]], and says to him: [[John 17:17|Thy word is truth|Sermo tuus veritas est]]. [[85:12|and I will glorify thy name for ever|Et glorificabo nomen tuum in æternum]], in words and deeds, through myself and through my ministers, who are led by my teaching and grace to glorify thee. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]], but [[John 8:49|I honour my Father|honorifico Patrem meum]].

paras.t: Quia misericordia tua magna est super me, id est super naturam meam humanam quam assumpsi. Misericordia Dei super illum esse asseritur, qui misericordiam consequitur. Multiplex autem est misericordiæ Dei effectus, et secundum hoc diversimode dicitur misericordia Dei esse super homines magna. Unus namque effectus misericordiæ Dei est, peccata dimittere. Alius, gratiam conversionis infundere : sicque misericordia Dei magna est super peccatores pœnitentes et conversos. Propter quod in libro Esdræ ait Scriptura : Tu, Deus, propter nos miseros misericors appellaris. Alter effectus misericordiæ Dei est, hominem per gratiam prævenire, atque in innocentia sine peccato custodire : et ita misericordia Dei magna et incomparabiliter magna in Christo est, quoniam sola gratia natura ejus humana est Dei Verbo unita, a principio suæ creationis beata fruitione dotata, confirmata in bono, et præservata ab omni malo : et ideo ante de eo dictum est Deo Patri, Prævenisti eum in benedictionibus dulcedinis ; et in Evangelio, Non ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum, scilicet homini Christo.
paras.en: [[85:13|For thy mercy is great towards me|Quia misericordia tua magna est super me]], that is, towards my human nature which I took. God's mercy is said to be upon him who obtains mercy. Now the effect of God's mercy is manifold, and accordingly God's mercy is said in different ways to be great upon men. For one effect of God's mercy is to forgive sins. Another is to pour in the grace of conversion: and so God's mercy is great upon sinners who repent and are converted. For which reason Scripture says in the book of Esdras: Thou, O God, art called merciful because of us wretched ones [4 Esdras 8:31, as the margin gives it, a book not in the Douay-Rheims canon; the margin offers *peccatores*, "sinners", as a variant for *miseros*, "wretched ones"]. Another effect of God's mercy is to go before a man by grace, and to keep him in innocence without sin: and in this way God's mercy is great, and great beyond compare, in Christ, since by grace alone his human nature was united to the Word of God, endowed from the beginning of its creation with blessed enjoyment [of God], confirmed in good, and preserved from all evil: and therefore it was said of him before to God the Father, [[Ps 20:4|For thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness|Prævenisti eum in benedictionibus dulcedinis]] [prevented, that is, gone before]; and in the Gospel, [[John 3:34|for God doth not give the Spirit by measure|Non ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum]], namely to the man Christ.

paras.t: Et eruisti, in die resurrectionis, animam meam ex inferno inferiori, id est ex limbo inferni infra terram existentem. De quo limbo Jacob in Genesi : Descendam, inquit, lugens ad filium meum in infernum ; Job etiam : In profundissimum inferni descendent omnia mea : putasne ibi erit requies mihi? Ex hoc inferno eruit Deus animam Christi tertia die, secundum quod Christus superius dixit, Domine, eduxisti ab inferno animam meam ; et, Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno.
paras.en: [[85:13|and thou hast delivered|Et eruisti]], on the day of the resurrection, [[85:13|my soul out of the lower hell|animam meam ex inferno inferiori]], that is, out of the limbo of hell, which is beneath the earth. Of this limbo Jacob speaks in Genesis: [[Gen 37:35|I will go down|Descendam]], he says, [[Gen 37:35|to my son into hell, mourning|lugens ad filium meum in infernum]]; Job too: [[Job 17:16|All that I have shall go down into the deepest pit: thinkest thou that there at least I shall have rest?|In profundissimum inferni descendent omnia mea : putasne ibi erit requies mihi?]] Out of this hell God delivered the soul of Christ on the third day, according as Christ said above, [[Ps 29:4|Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell|Domine, eduxisti ab inferno animam meam]]; and, [[Ps 15:10|Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell|Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno]].

paras.t: Deus Trinitas, iniqui Judæi insurrexerunt super me, id est contra me ; et synagoga potentium, id est principes sacerdotum, Scribæ, Pharisæi, magistratusque templi, quæsierunt animam meam, id est vitam meam, ad occidendum : secundum quod dicitur : Quærebant summi sacerdotes quomodo Jesum tenerent et occiderent. Et Sapiens : Dixerunt impii apud se, cogitantes non recte : Opprimamus virum justum, quoniam contrarius est operibus nostris, et gloriatur se Deum patrem habere, et Filium Dei se nominat. Et non proposuerunt Deum in conspectu suo, id est, divinum judicium non expaverunt in tanto facinore : prout de quibusdam alio loco dictum est, Everterunt sensum suum, ne recordarentur judiciorum justorum.
paras.en: [[85:14|O God|Deus]] the Trinity, [[85:14|the wicked|iniqui]] Jews [[85:14|are risen up against me|insurrexerunt super me]], that is, in opposition to me; [[85:14|and the assembly of the mighty|et synagoga potentium]], that is, the chief priests, the Scribes, the Pharisees and the magistrates of the temple, [[85:14|have sought my soul|quæsierunt animam meam]], that is, my life, to kill me: according as it is said: [[Mark 14:1|the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might by some wile lay hold on him and kill him|Quærebant summi sacerdotes quomodo Jesum tenerent et occiderent]]. And the Wise Man: The wicked [[Wis 2:1|have said, reasoning with themselves, but not right|Dixerunt impii apud se, cogitantes non recte]]: [[Wis 2:10|Let us oppress|Opprimamus]] the just man, because [[Wis 2:12|he is contrary to our doings|contrarius est operibus nostris]], and [[Wis 2:16|glorieth that he hath God for his father|gloriatur se Deum patrem habere]], [[Wis 2:13|and calleth himself the son of God|et Filium Dei se nominat]]. [[85:14|and they have not set thee before their eyes|Et non proposuerunt Deum in conspectu suo]] [Denis reads *Deum*, "God", where the Vulgate has *te*, "thee"], that is, they did not dread the divine judgment in so great a crime: as was said of certain men in another place, [[Dan 13:9|they perverted their own mind|Everterunt sensum suum]], that they might not [[Dan 13:9|remember just judgments|recordarentur judiciorum justorum]].

paras.t: Et tu, Domine Deus, miserator in opere, et misericors in natura, patiens, longanimiter expectando, juxta illud, Altissimus est patiens redditor. Non tamen convenit patientia proprie sumpta Deo, sicut de mititate ostensum est, quoniam patientia proprie est virtus moralis, passionem tristitiæ reprimens. Dicitur ergo Deus patiens propter similitudinem operis, quoniam scilicet peccatorem longanimiter præstolatur ad veniam. Et multæ misericordiæ : sicut expositum est ; et verax in verbis, factis atque promissis.
