paras.en: [[85:15|And thou, O Lord, art a God of compassion|Et tu, Domine Deus, miserator]] in deed, [[85:15|and merciful|et misericors]] in nature [*miserator*, one who shows mercy; *misericors*, one who is merciful], [[85:15|patient|patiens]], by waiting long-sufferingly, according to that word, [[Ecclus 5:4|the most High is a patient rewarder|Altissimus est patiens redditor]]. Yet patience, taken in its proper sense, does not belong to God, as was shown of mildness, since patience is properly a moral virtue that holds down the passion of sorrow. God is therefore called patient because of a likeness in his working, namely because he waits long-sufferingly for the sinner to come to pardon. [[85:15|and of much mercy|Et multæ misericordiæ]]: as has been expounded; [[85:15|and true|et verax]] in words, deeds and promises.

paras.t: Respice in me oculo pietatis paternæ, et miserere mei : secundum sensum jam explanatum ; da imperium tuum puero tuo, id est, regnum militantis Ecclesiæ judiciariamque potestatem da mihi Christo Filio tuo dilecto : quemadmodum alibi prædictum est, Dominus dabit imperium regi suo, et sublimabit cornu Christi sui. Sed quoniam omnis creatura subjecta est Christo, a suæ conceptionis maternæ exordio, quid nunc orat ut sibi detur imperium, nisi ut Deus Pater manifestet hominibus hoc imperium Christo esse collatum? Hoc enim Christus deprecatur, dicendo : Pater, clarifica Filium tuum, ut Filius tuus clarificet te. Et salvum fac a morte per resurrectionem, filium ancillæ tuæ, id est me Christum natum Mariæ, quæ ait, Ecce ancilla Domini.
paras.en: [[85:16|O look upon me|Respice in me]] with the eye of fatherly kindness, [[85:16|and have mercy on me|et miserere mei]]: in the sense already explained; [[85:16|give thy command to thy servant|da imperium tuum puero tuo]] [*puer*, "boy" or "servant"], that is, give the kingdom of the Church militant and the power of judgment to me, Christ, thy beloved Son: as was foretold elsewhere, The Lord [[1 Kings 2:10|shall give empire to his king, and shall exalt the horn of his Christ|dabit imperium regi suo, et sublimabit cornu Christi sui]]. But since every creature has been subject to Christ[[Heb 2:8||]] from the first moment of his conception in his mother, why does he now pray that empire be given him, unless it be that God the Father may make known to men that this empire has been conferred on Christ? For this is what Christ asks when he says: Father, [[John 17:1|Glorify thy Son, that thy Son may glorify thee|clarifica Filium tuum, ut Filius tuus clarificet te]]. [[85:16|and save|Et salvum fac]] from death by the resurrection [[85:16|the son of thy handmaid|filium ancillæ tuæ]], that is, me, Christ, born of Mary, who said, [[Luke 1:38|Behold the handmaid of the Lord|Ecce ancilla Domini]].

paras.t: Fac mecum, o Domine, Deus Pater, signum in bonum, id est, signum resurrectionis ostende in me ad clarificationem nominis mei per mundum, ut videant qui oderunt me, id est Judæi seu custodes sepulcri, qui angelo viso territi ceciderunt, et facti sunt velut mortui : videant, inquam, per certa argumenta atque miracula me resurrexisse, et confundantur de suis peccatis, nunc per pœnitentiam, vel postmodum per condemnationem. Quidam etenim Judæorum, per hæc signa et argumenta Jesum esse verum Christum per fidem viderunt post resurrectionem, qui ante clamaverunt : Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum. De ipsis namque Christus loquebatur : Quum exaltaveritis, inquiens, Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum.
paras.en: [[85:17|Shew me|Fac mecum]], O Lord, God the Father, [[85:17|a token for good|signum in bonum]] [*signum*: "token" in the Douay-Rheims, "sign" below], that is, show forth in me the sign of the resurrection, for the glorifying of my name[[John 17:1||]] throughout the world, [[85:17|that they who hate me may see|ut videant qui oderunt me]], that is, the Jews, or the guards of the sepulchre, who at the sight of the angel fell down in terror [[Matt 28:4|and became as dead men|et facti sunt velut mortui]]: let them see, I say, by sure proofs and miracles that I have risen, [[85:17|and be confounded|et confundantur]] for their sins, now by penance, or later by condemnation. For some of the Jews, by these signs and proofs, saw by faith after the resurrection that Jesus was the true Christ, who before had cried out: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]. For it was of them that Christ spoke, saying: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up|Quum exaltaveritis]], he says, [[John 8:28|the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]].

paras.t: Hoc signum quod Christus hic petit, est signum Jonæ prophetæ, quemadmodum in Evangelio dicit de Judæis Dominus Jesus : Generatio adultera et perversa signum quærit ; et signum non dabitur ei nisi signum Jonæ prophetæ, qui tertio die exivit de piscis ventre. Non ergo datum est Judæis signum descensionis de cruce quod petiebant, dicentes, Si rex Israel est, et, Si hic est Christus Dei electus, descendat nunc de cruce, et credimus ei ; sed signum resurrectionis de monumento. De quo per Sophoniam loquitur Christus, Exspecta me in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum ; de quo alibi ait sermo divinus, Vivificabit nos post duos dies, in die tertia suscitabit nos. Potest quoque per hoc signum intelligi operatio miraculorum, per quod sancti Apostoli in Jerusalem primitus probaverunt Christum resuscitatum. Unde Petrus, claudo nato sanato, dixit Judæis : Deus patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Jesum. Itaque, Fac mecum signum in bonum, ut videant, etc., quoniam tu, Domine, adjuvisti me, cooperando mihi in omnibus, et consolatus es me in resurrectione, liberando me ab omni pœna et passibilitate.
paras.en: This sign which Christ asks for here is the sign of Jonas the prophet, as the Lord Jesus says of the Jews in the Gospel: [[Matt 12:39|An evil and adulterous generation seeketh a sign: and a sign shall not be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet|Generatio adultera et perversa signum quærit ; et signum non dabitur ei nisi signum Jonæ prophetæ]], who on the third day came out of the belly of the fish[[Jon 2:11||]]. So the Jews were not given the sign of the coming down from the cross that they asked for, saying, [[Matt 27:42|If he be the king of Israel|Si rex Israel est]], and, [[Luke 23:35|if he be Christ, the elect of God|Si hic est Christus Dei electus]], [[Matt 27:42|let him now come down from the cross: and we will believe him|descendat nunc de cruce, et credimus ei]]; but the sign of the resurrection from the tomb. Of this Christ speaks through Sophonias, [[Soph 3:8|expect me|Exspecta me]] [[Soph 3:8|in the day of my resurrection that is to come|in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum]]; of this the divine word says elsewhere, [[Osee 6:3|He will revive us after two days: on the third day he will raise us up|Vivificabit nos post duos dies, in die tertia suscitabit nos]]. By this sign may also be understood the working of miracles, by which the holy Apostles first proved in Jerusalem that Christ had risen. Hence Peter, when the man born lame had been healed, said to the Jews: [[Acts 3:13|the God of our fathers, hath glorified his Son Jesus|Deus patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Jesum]]. So: [[85:17|Shew me a token for good|Fac mecum signum in bonum]], that they [[85:17|may see|ut videant]], etc., [[85:17|because thou, O Lord, hast helped me|quoniam tu, Domine, adjuvisti me]], working with me in all things, [[85:17|and hast comforted me|et consolatus es me]] in the resurrection, by freeing me from all pain and from all capacity to suffer.

85.title: EXPLANATIO MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI OCTOGESIMI QUINTI DE QUOLIBET VERE FIDELI.
85.title_en: Moral explanation of the same eighty-fifth psalm, concerning any true believer.

paras.t: Porro quum psalmus iste magna excellentia polleat (continet namque ardentissimas preces viri devoti, pulcherrimas laudes Dei, beneficiorumque divinorum gratam memoriam), ideo plenius pertractandus est, hortando magis quam exponendo : difficultatem enim non habet in sensu ; et si aliqua in eo difficultas consistat, ex præcedenti expositione elucescit. In primis ergo pensandum, quod licet homo Dominum orans, misericordiæ ejus debeat præcipue inniti, dicendo cum publicano, Deus, propitius esto mihi peccatori : nam et alibi scriptum est, Non te justifices coram Deo ; unde et sanctus Job asserit, Si justificare me voluero, os meum condemnabit me : nihilo minus potest homo interdum in oratione aliqua opera sua bona commemorare, non ea sibi ipsi contumaciter, sed Deo humiliter attribuendo, quatenus majorem exauditionis fiduciam inde concipiat. Sic enim Ezechias orans, locutus est : Obsecro, Domine, memento quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et corde perfecto. Judith quoque : Domine, Deus cœli et terræ, intuere superbiam eorum, et respice ad nostram humilitatem, et faciem sanctorum tuorum attende. Sed et sancta ac venerabilis Esther Deum ita precatur : Domine mi rex, adjuva me solitariam, cujus præter te nullus alius auxiliator est. Tu scis necessitatem meam, quod abominer signum superbiæ et gloriæ meæ, quod est super caput meum, quasi pannum menstruatæ, et non portem illud in diebus silentii mei, et quod nunquam lætata sit ancilla tua, ex quo translata sum huc. O quam vere sublimis perfectio ! Ecce ex humili statu facta erat imperatrix, et conjux potentissimi illius regis Assueri, qui regnavit super centum viginti septem provincias : et quum esset in tanta majestate, honore et gloria, nunquam maculavit animam ejus ambitio, nunquam inaniter est lætata, nunquam regis incircumcisi adamavit cubile. Quid ad hæc nos barbati dicemus ?
paras.en: Now since this psalm is of great excellence (for it contains the most ardent prayers of a devout man, the most beautiful praises of God, and a grateful remembrance of the divine benefits), it is to be treated more fully, by exhortation rather than by exposition: for it has no difficulty in its sense, and if there is any difficulty in it, it is made clear by the preceding exposition. First, then, it must be weighed that, although a man praying to the Lord ought to rely chiefly on his mercy, saying with the publican, [[Luke 18:13|O God, be merciful to me a sinner|Deus, propitius esto mihi peccatori]] (for elsewhere too it is written, [[Ecclus 7:5|Justify not thyself before God|Non te justifices coram Deo]]; whence holy Job also declares, [[Job 9:20|If I would justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me|Si justificare me voluero, os meum condemnabit me]]), nevertheless a man may at times in prayer call to mind some of his good works, ascribing them not stubbornly to himself but humbly to God, so that he may conceive from them a greater confidence of being heard. For thus Ezechias, praying, spoke: [[4 Kings 20:3|I beseech thee, O Lord, remember how I have walked before thee in truth, and with a perfect heart|Obsecro, Domine, memento quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et corde perfecto]][[Is 38:3||]]. Judith also: [[Jdt 6:15|O Lord God of heaven and earth, behold their pride, and look on our low condition, and have regard to the face of thy saints|Domine, Deus cœli et terræ, intuere superbiam eorum, et respice ad nostram humilitatem, et faciem sanctorum tuorum attende]] [in the Vulgate these words are the prayer of the people of Bethulia, not of Judith herself]. And the holy and venerable Esther too prays to God thus: [[Esth 14:3|O my Lord|Domine mi]], king, [[Esth 14:3|help me a desolate woman, and who have no other helper but thee|adjuva me solitariam, cujus præter te nullus alius auxiliator est]]. [[Esth 14:16|Thou knowest my necessity, that I abominate the sign of my pride and glory, which is upon my head|Tu scis necessitatem meam, quod abominer signum superbiæ et gloriæ meæ, quod est super caput meum]], [[Esth 14:16|as a menstruous rag, and wear it not in the days of my silence|quasi pannum menstruatæ, et non portem illud in diebus silentii mei]], [[Esth 14:18|and that thy handmaid hath never rejoiced, since I was brought hither|et quod nunquam lætata sit ancilla tua, ex quo translata sum huc]]. O how truly sublime a perfection! Behold, from a lowly state she had been made empress, and wife of that most mighty king Assuerus, [[Esth 1:1|who reigned|qui regnavit]] [[Esth 1:1|over a hundred and twenty seven provinces|super centum viginti septem provincias]]: and though she was in such majesty, honour and glory, ambition never stained her soul, she never rejoiced in vanity, she never loved the bed of the uncircumcised king. What shall we bearded men [that is, we men, who are reckoned the stronger] say to this?

paras.t: Simili itaque modo in psalmo præsenti homo devotus multas causas allegat, cur deceat se exaudiri a Deo, quarum quædam sumuntur ex parte sui, quædam vero ex parte Dei. Earum autem quæ sumuntur ex parte sui, quædam pertinent ad suæ imperfectionis confessionem, quædam vero ad suam perfectionem. Primo igitur allegat causas ex parte sui, quarum prima est propria indigentia et paupertas, de qua modo fatetur : Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam, et exaudi me, quoniam inops et pauper sum ego. Tanquam dicat : Tu, Deus, qui dives es in misericordia, cujus manus non est abbreviata, in cujus manu sunt omnia, in quo sunt infinitæ divitiæ, exaudi me egenum et pauperem. Decet enim liberalem et divitem Dominum, pauperem famulum exaudire, sicut tu ipse apud Prophetam testatus es : Ego Dominus exaudiam egenum et pauperem ; non derelinquam eos. Dicit autem, Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam : non quod in incircumscripto ac simplici Deo sint aures corporeæ aut inclinatio motus localis ; sed secundum sensum præhabitum.
paras.en: In like manner, then, in the present psalm the devout man alleges many reasons why it is fitting that he be heard by God, some of which are taken from his own side, others from God's side. And of those taken from his own side, some belong to the confession of his imperfection, others to his perfection. First, therefore, he alleges reasons on his own side, of which the first is his own need and poverty, which he now confesses: [[85:1|Incline thy ear, O Lord, and hear me: for I am needy and poor|Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam, et exaudi me, quoniam inops et pauper sum ego]]. As if to say: Thou, O God, who art [[Eph 2:4|rich in mercy|dives es in misericordia]], whose hand [[Is 59:1|is not shortened|non est abbreviata]], in whose hand are all things[[Ps 94:4||]] [the margin gives Ps. xciv, 4, where it is "all the ends of the earth"], in whom are infinite riches, hear me, needy and poor. For it befits a generous and rich Lord to hear a poor servant, as thou thyself hast testified in the Prophet: [[Is 41:17|I the Lord will hear|Ego Dominus exaudiam]] the needy and the poor; I [[Is 41:17|will not forsake them|non derelinquam eos]]. Now he says, [[85:1|Incline thy ear, O Lord|Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam]], not that in God, who is uncircumscribed and simple, there are bodily ears, or that inclining is a local motion; but in the sense given before.

paras.t: Secunda ratio exauditionis ex parte hominis, est bonitas vitæ : et istam allegat, subjungens, Custodi animam meam ab omni tentationis et adversitatis periculo, quoniam sanctus sum, id est mundus et innocens. Sanctitas enim (secundum Dionysium) est munditia, ab omni impuritate sejuncta. Sed quis viator audeat hoc dicere, quum asserat Salomon : Quis potest dicere, Mundum est cor meum, purus sum a peccato ? Job quoque : Etiam, inquit, si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea. Et S. Joannes protestatur : Si dixerimus quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos seducimus, et veritas in nobis non est. Videturque prorsus periculosum homini, dicere coram Deo, Sanctus sum, in cujus conspectu cœli mundi non sunt : præsertim quum omnes nostræ justitiæ sint tanquam pannus menstruatæ, secundum Isaiam ; et teste Scriptura, Nescit homo an sit dignus amore vel odio.
paras.en: The second reason for being heard, on man's side, is goodness of life; and this he alleges, adding, [[85:2|Preserve my soul|Custodi animam meam]] from every danger of temptation and adversity, [[85:2|for I am holy|quoniam sanctus sum]], that is, clean and innocent. For holiness (according to Dionysius) is cleanness, separated from all impurity. But what wayfarer [that is, one still on the journey of this life, not yet in the heavenly homeland] would dare to say this, when Solomon declares: [[Prov 20:9|Who can say: My heart is clean, I am pure from sin?|Quis potest dicere, Mundum est cor meum, purus sum a peccato]] Job also: [[Job 9:21|Although|Etiam]], he says, [[Job 9:21|I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of|si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea]]. And St John protests: [[1 John 1:8|If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.|Si dixerimus quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos seducimus, et veritas in nobis non est]] And it seems altogether dangerous for a man to say, I am holy, before God, in whose sight [[Job 15:15|the heavens are not pure|cœli mundi non sunt]]: especially since all our justices are [[Is 64:6|as the rag of a menstruous woman|tanquam pannus menstruatæ]], according to Isaias; and, as Scripture witnesses, [[Eccles 9:1|man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred|Nescit homo an sit dignus amore vel odio]].

paras.t: Hucusque argumentatus sum, quod non sit tutum dicere coram Deo, Custodi animam meam, quoniam sanctus sum. Nunc ex Scriptura argumentandum est ad partem oppositam, quatenus tandem rationabile medium inveniamus et solutionem condignam. Ecce Scriptura testante, in Confessione omnia dimittuntur ; in Baptismo quoque omnia vitia lavantur. Adultus ergo baptizatus, secure atque verissime dicit, Sanctus sum : imo nisi hoc putet, gratiæ Baptismatis derogat, et christianus non est. Similiter in professione vitæ monasticæ et passione martyrii pro Christo, omnia indulgentur peccata, sanctificaturque homo. Et qui ex contritione et bono proposito confitetur, fiducialiter credere potest se esse ab omni peccato mortali immunem. Denique Paulus apostolus se ipsum et coapostolos suos non solum sanctos, sed et sanctissimos et Prophetis sublimiores esse demonstrat, dicendo : Nos ipsi qui primitias Spiritus accepimus. Quid enim est dicere, Primitias Spiritus accepimus, nisi, Primas seu summas gratias Spiritus Sancti adepti sumus ? Jeremias etiam in principio libri visionum suarum fatetur se sanctificatum in utero.
paras.en: Thus far I have argued that it is not safe to say before God, [[85:2|Preserve my soul, for I am holy|Custodi animam meam, quoniam sanctus sum]]. Now we must argue from Scripture for the opposite side, so that at length we may find a reasonable middle way and a fitting solution. Behold, as Scripture witnesses, in Confession all things are forgiven; in Baptism too all vices are washed away. An adult who has been baptized, therefore, says securely and most truly, I am holy: indeed, unless he thinks this, he derogates from the grace of Baptism and is not a Christian. Likewise in the profession of the monastic life and in the passion of martyrdom for Christ all sins are forgiven, and a man is sanctified. And he who confesses with contrition and a good purpose can confidently believe that he is free from every mortal sin. Lastly, Paul the apostle shows that he himself and his fellow apostles are not only holy, but most holy and higher than the Prophets, by saying: We [[Rom 8:23|ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit|Nos ipsi qui primitias Spiritus accepimus]] [Denis reads "who have received the firstfruits"]. For what is it to say, We have received the firstfruits of the Spirit, if not, We have obtained the first or highest graces of the Holy Ghost? Jeremias too, at the beginning of the book of his visions, declares that he was sanctified in the womb[[Jer 1:5||]].

paras.t: Et respondendum, quod de eadem re diversa proferuntur judicia secundum considerationes diversas : quemadmodum Christus ait, Neque me scitis, neque Patrem meum ; et tamen alibi dicit eisdem, Et me scitis, et unde sim scitis. Similiter Job, qui sicut nunc allegatum est, dicit, Etiamsi simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea ; idem ipse loquitur : Donec deficiam, non recedam ab innocentia mea ; justificationem meam quam cœpi tenere, non deseram. In quibus utique verbis testatur se ipsum innocentem esse, justum, constantem et perseverantem. Sed parum est hoc : addit namque, Neque reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea. Hoc Paulus dicere non potuit, qui licet veraciter dixerat, Nihil mihi conscius sum, quantum ad hoc quod de præteritis doluit, et a futuris abstinere peccatis proposuit : reprehendit tamen eum cor suum in multis, propter quod dixit, Non sum dignus vocari Apostolus, quia persecutus sum Ecclesiam Dei ; et rursus, Venit Jesus peccatores salvos facere, quorum primus ego sum. Non tamen præfero sanctum Job Paulo ; imo secure præfero Paulum illi.
paras.en: And the answer is that on one and the same matter different judgements are given according to different considerations: as Christ says, [[John 8:19|Neither me do you know, nor my Father|Neque me scitis, neque Patrem meum]]; and yet elsewhere he says to the same men, [[John 7:28|You both know me, and you know whence I am|Et me scitis, et unde sim scitis]]. Likewise Job, who, as was just alleged, says, [[Job 9:21|Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of|Etiamsi simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea]], himself also says: [[Job 27:5|till I die I will not depart from my innocence|Donec deficiam, non recedam ab innocentia mea]]; [[Job 27:6|My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake|justificationem meam quam cœpi tenere, non deseram]]. In which words he certainly testifies that he himself is innocent, just, constant and persevering. But this is little: for he adds, [[Job 27:6|for my heart doth not reprehend me in all my life|Neque reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea]]. This Paul could not say; for although he had truly said, [[1 Cor 4:4|I am not conscious to myself of anything|Nihil mihi conscius sum]], so far as he had grieved for past sins and purposed to abstain from future ones, yet his heart reproached him in many things, for which reason he said, I [[1 Cor 15:9|am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God|Non sum dignus vocari Apostolus, quia persecutus sum Ecclesiam Dei]]; and again, [[1 Tim 1:15|Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the chief|Venit Jesus peccatores salvos facere, quorum primus ego sum]]. Yet I do not prefer holy Job to Paul; indeed I securely prefer Paul to him.

paras.t: Dicendum ergo, quod nemo dicere potest se sanctum esse simpliciter et absolute, videlicet quasi nullo peccato obnoxius sit : quoniam ut alibi scriptum est, Nemo mundus a sorde, nec infans cujus est unius diei vita super terram : ad minus enim originali peccato fuit obnoxius. Potest tamen homo ad punctum omni peccato carere, quantum ad maculam culpæ et pœnæ reatum : ut patet de evolantibus, qui sine dilatione regnum ingrediuntur cæleste. Sed non potest homo diu in hac vita sine venialibus vivere : quoniam scriptum est, Justus septies in die cadit ; et Job dicit : Quid est homo ut immaculatus sit, et justus appareat natus de muliere ? Dicitur autem viator sanctus, secundum exigentiam et possibilitatem vitæ præsentis, quoniam a mortalibus sollicite abstinet, venialia deflet, in gratia Dei et sancto ejus amore quotidie crescere studet : sicque se ipsum sanctum sine periculo profitetur, qui integro proposito deservire Domino nititur, proponens incessanter proficere, quotidiana mala deplangere, atque in his se ipsum quotidie pro posse exercens.
paras.en: It must be said, therefore, that no one can say that he is holy simply and absolutely, that is, as though he were liable to no sin: since, as is written elsewhere, No one is clean from filth, not even an infant whose life upon earth is of one day[[Job 14:4||]][[Job 14:5||]] [the margin gives Job xiv, 4, 5 "according to the Septuagint"; the Douay-Rheims, following the Vulgate, reads differently there]: for at the least he was liable to original sin. Yet a man can be free of all sin for an instant, as to the stain of guilt and the debt of punishment: as is plain in those who fly up [that is, souls who pass straight from this life to heaven], who enter the heavenly kingdom without delay. But a man cannot live long in this life without venial sins: for it is written, [[Prov 24:16|a just man shall fall seven times|Justus septies in die cadit]] [Denis reads "the just man falls seven times a day"]; and Job says: [[Job 15:14|What is man that he should be without spot, and he that is born of a woman that he should appear just?|Quid est homo ut immaculatus sit, et justus appareat natus de muliere]] Now the wayfarer is called holy according to the demands and the possibility of the present life, since he carefully abstains from mortal sins, weeps over venial ones, and strives daily to grow in the grace of God and in his holy love: and so he professes himself holy without danger who strives with an undivided purpose to serve the Lord, purposing unceasingly to make progress and to bewail his daily faults, and exercising himself daily in these things as far as he can.

paras.t: Dicere ergo, Custodi animam meam, quoniam sanctus sum : non est sermo elati, neque præsumptio hominis vani, sed vox Domino non ingrati, qui sanctitatem suam non suo labori aut viribus, sed gratiæ et misericordiæ Salvatoris cordialiter tribuit. Quod autem Salomon ait, Nescit homo an sit dignus amore an odio, non ideo dictum videtur, quasi nullus ex speciali gratiæ dono hoc sciat : imo multi ex revelatione divina cognoverunt se esse prædestinatos ; multi quoque sciunt se esse in gratia, in quorum persona dicit Apostolus : Ipse spiritus reddit testimonium spiritui nostro, quod filii Dei sumus ; et denuo : Nos non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis. Verum est tamen, quod homo certitudinaliter scire non valet an sit in gratia gratum faciente, sine speciali instinctu Spiritus Sancti seu revelatione divina : idcirco, secundum communem legem loquendo, nescit homo an sit dignus amore an odio. Ex his (ut reor) multa divinæ Scripturæ eloquia, quæ prima fronte dissonare videntur, concordari faciliter possunt. Quod autem non dicat se homo pius sanctum ex elatione, hinc constat, quod in præcedenti versu se inopem pauperemque vocavit ; et nunc se confidere dicit, non in se ipso seu meritis propriis, sed subjungit : salvum fac servum tuum, Deus meus, sperantem in te.
paras.en: To say, then, [[85:2|Preserve my soul, for I am holy|Custodi animam meam, quoniam sanctus sum]], is not the speech of a proud man, nor the presumption of a vain man, but the voice of one not ungrateful to the Lord, who heartily ascribes his holiness not to his own labour or strength but to the grace and mercy of the Saviour. And what Solomon says, [[Eccles 9:1|man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred|Nescit homo an sit dignus amore an odio]], does not seem to have been said as though no one knew this by a special gift of grace: indeed many have known by divine revelation that they were predestined; many also know that they are in grace, in whose person the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:16|the Spirit himself giveth testimony to our spirit that we are the sons of God|Ipse spiritus reddit testimonium spiritui nostro, quod filii Dei sumus]]; and again: [[1 Cor 2:12|we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God: that we may know the things that are given us from God|Nos non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis]]. Yet it is true that a man cannot know with certainty whether he is in sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God] without a special prompting of the Holy Ghost or a divine revelation: and therefore, speaking according to the common law, [[Eccles 9:1|man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred|nescit homo an sit dignus amore an odio]]. From these things (as I think) many sayings of divine Scripture which at first sight seem to disagree can easily be reconciled. And that the devout man does not call himself holy out of pride is clear from this, that in the preceding verse he called himself needy and poor; and now he says that he trusts, not in himself or in his own merits, but he adds: [[85:2|save thy servant, O my God, that trusteth in thee|salvum fac servum tuum, Deus meus, sperantem in te]].

paras.t: Tertia causa, quam allegat pro sua exauditione, est perseverantia in orando. Oportet namque instanter orare, juxta illud Apostoli : Sine intermissione orate. Ideo subditur : Miserere mei, Domine, culpas delendo, pœnas laxando, gratias multiplicando, quoniam ad te clamavi tota die naturali (qui tempus nocturnum includit), id est singulis horis diei ad orandum deputatis aut debitis.
paras.en: The third reason he alleges for his being heard is perseverance in praying. For we must pray instantly, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Thess 5:17|Pray without ceasing|Sine intermissione orate]]. Therefore it is added: [[85:3|Have mercy on me, O Lord|Miserere mei, Domine]], by blotting out my faults, remitting my punishments, multiplying thy graces, [[85:3|for I have cried to thee all the day|quoniam ad te clamavi tota die]], the natural day [the whole day of twenty-four hours, as against the day from sunrise to sunset] (which includes the night-time), that is, at each of the hours of the day appointed for prayer or owed to it.

paras.t: Lætifica animam servi tui, id est, animæ meæ infunde consolationem internam de remissione peccatorum, de infusione divinorum charismatum, de contemplatione et spe futurorum bonorum. Lætifica animam servi tui, ut tibi læto corde deserviam, quoniam hilarem datorem tu diligis : omnem inordinatum mœrorem expelle a me, fac me omni profectui proximorum congaudere, de omni bono eventu lætari. Quoniam ad te, Domine, animam meam levavi per fidem, spem et caritatem, te summum bonum contemplando, exspectando ac diligendo, teque devote invocando.
paras.en: [[85:4|Give joy to the soul of thy servant|Lætifica animam servi tui]], that is, pour into my soul inward consolation from the remission of sins, from the infusion of divine gifts, from the contemplation and hope of the good things to come. [[85:4|Give joy to the soul of thy servant|Lætifica animam servi tui]], that I may serve thee with a glad heart, for thou lovest [[2 Cor 9:7|a cheerful giver|hilarem datorem]]: drive from me all inordinate sorrow, make me rejoice in every progress of my neighbours, and be glad at every good event. [[85:4|For to thee, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul|Quoniam ad te, Domine, animam meam levavi]] by faith, hope and charity, contemplating, awaiting and loving thee, the highest good, and devoutly calling upon thee.

paras.t: In die tribulationis meæ, dum vel a carnis concupiscentiis stimulor, aut a passionibus animæ pulsor, vel a dæmonibus tentor, aut a mundo affligor, aut corpore infirmor, clamavi ad te pro succursu et adsistentia gratiæ tuæ piissimæ, sicut tu ipse alibi admones : Invoca me in die tribulationis, eruam te, et honorificabis me ; et rursus : Salus populi ego sum ; de quacumque tribulatione clamaverint ad me, exaudiam eos. Ideo autem invocavi te, quia exaudisti me : id est, quoniam expertus sum prius me exauditum esse a te, ideo nunc fiduciam habui te invocandi, teque invocavi.
paras.en: [[85:7|In the day of my trouble|In die tribulationis meæ]], when I am either goaded by the concupiscences of the flesh, or buffeted by the passions of the soul, or tempted by the devils, or afflicted by the world, or sick in body, [[85:7|I have called upon thee|clamavi ad te]] for the succour and assistance of thy most loving grace, as thou thyself admonishest elsewhere: [[Ps 49:15|call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me|Invoca me in die tribulationis, eruam te, et honorificabis me]]; and again: I am the salvation of the people; in whatever tribulation they shall cry to me, I will hear them[[Is 43:11||]] [these words are the Introit of the Mass of the nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost, not found word for word in Scripture; the margin compares Is. xliii, 11]. And I have called upon thee for this reason, [[85:7|because thou hast heard me|quia exaudisti me]]: that is, since I have found by experience that I was heard by thee before, I therefore now had confidence to call upon thee, and I called upon thee.

paras.t: Deduc me, Domine, per gratiam tuam angelicamque custodiam, in via tua, id est in lege divina, per quam itur ad te, quatenus illam sine offensione custodiam, digne et sancte ambulando in tua præsentia ; et ingrediar in veritate tua, id est, in hac vita degam, et ad futuram vitam deambulem in veritate tuæ doctrinæ, illi credendo et obediendo, in veritate tuæ justitiæ, illam sequendo : ut impleatur in me, o Domine Christe, quod tu pro electis orasti, Pater, sanctifica eos in veritate : nec in illorum societate inveniar, de quibus apud Jeremiam dicitur, Vere mendacium possederunt patres nostri, vanitatem quæ eis non profuit.
paras.en: [[85:11|Conduct me, O Lord|Deduc me, Domine]], by thy grace and the guardianship of the angels, [[85:11|in thy way|in via tua]], that is, in the divine law, by which one goes to thee, so that I may keep it without offence, walking worthily and holily in thy presence; [[85:11|and I will walk in thy truth|et ingrediar in veritate tua]], that is, may I spend this life, and walk on to the life to come, in the truth of thy teaching, believing and obeying it, and in the truth of thy justice, following it: that there may be fulfilled in me, O Lord Christ, what thou didst pray for the elect, Father, [[John 17:17|Sanctify them in truth|sanctifica eos in veritate]]; and that I may not be found in the company of those of whom it is said in Jeremias, [[Jer 16:19|Surely our fathers have possessed lies, a vanity which hath not profited them|Vere mendacium possederunt patres nostri, vanitatem quæ eis non profuit]].

paras.t: Lætetur cor meum, ut timeat nomen tuum, id est, cum interiori delectatione te timeat sancto et casto timore, qui ex amore procedit. Quum enim timere Deum sit actus virtuosus, delectabiliter fieri debet, quoniam signum virtutis est delectatio operationi annexa. Porro quam necessarius ad salutem sit timor Domini, Moyses ostendit, populo Israelitico loquens : Nisi timueris nomen Domini gloriosum atque terribile, augebit plagas tuas ; et sicut ante lætabatur super vos benefaciens vobis, sic nunc lætabitur vos disperdens atque subvertens. Dominus quoque per Malachiam ait : Filius honorat patrem suum, et servus timet dominum suum. Si ergo pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus ? et si Dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus ? Perfecti igitur timeant Deum timore filiali, ne ab ipso separentur aut eum offendant. De hoc nempe timore ait Scriptura : Ecce timor Domini, ipsa est sapientia. Hic enim timor vere jucundus est, sicut in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Nihil dulcius quam timere Deum. Imperfecti vero timeant Deum, vel potius nomen Domini, quo Judex vocatur, timore partim servili et partim filiali, quia de hoc metuendo nomine Domini scriptum est : Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo ; ardens furor ejus et gravis ad portandum.
paras.en: [[85:11|Let my heart rejoice that it may fear thy name|Lætetur cor meum, ut timeat nomen tuum]], that is, let it fear thee with inward delight, with a holy and chaste fear, which proceeds from love. For since to fear God is a virtuous act, it ought to be done with delight, for delight joined to the operation is a sign of virtue. Further, how necessary to salvation the fear of the Lord is, Moses shows, speaking to the people of Israel: Unless thou [[Deut 28:58|fear his glorious and terrible name|timueris nomen Domini gloriosum atque terribile]], [[Deut 28:59|the Lord shall increase thy plagues|augebit plagas tuas]]; [[Deut 28:63|and as the Lord rejoiced upon you before doing good to you|et sicut ante lætabatur super vos benefaciens vobis]], [[Deut 28:63|so he shall rejoice destroying and bringing you to nought|sic nunc lætabitur vos disperdens atque subvertens]]. The Lord also says by Malachias: [[Mal 1:6|The son honoureth the father, and the servant his master: if then I be a father, where is my honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear|Filius honorat patrem suum, et servus timet dominum suum. Si ergo pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus ? et si Dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus]]? [Denis reads "and the servant feareth his master".] Let the perfect, then, fear God with a filial fear, lest they be separated from him or offend him. Of this fear indeed Scripture says: [[Job 28:28|Behold the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom|Ecce timor Domini, ipsa est sapientia]]. For this fear is truly delightful, as it is written in Ecclesiasticus: Nothing is sweeter than to fear God[[Ecclus 23:37||]] [the margin gives Eccli. xxxvii, 37, which does not exist; the nearest is Ecclus 23:37, "there is nothing better than the fear of God: and … nothing sweeter than to have regard to the commandments of the Lord"]. But let the imperfect fear God, or rather the name of the Lord by which he is called Judge, with a fear partly servile and partly filial, because of this fearful name of the Lord it is written: [[Is 30:27|Behold the name of the Lord cometh from afar, his wrath burneth, and is heavy to bear|Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo ; ardens furor ejus et gravis ad portandum]].

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, Domine Deus meus, in toto corde meo, confessione tuæ laudis et meæ iniquitatis ; confitebor ad gloriam tuam mea peccata et tua præconia. Ex intimis ergo præcordiis, et corde ad Deum pure converso, confiteamur Domino suam bonitatem et beneficia, nostramque pravitatem et ingratitudines plurimas. Et glorificabo nomen tuum in æternum, id est, tuam felicitatem et gloriam verbis fatebor, et opere protestabor, jam per fidem inchoando, et demum in cœlo per speciem sine cessatione complendo. Sanctificatur, magnificatur, et glorificatur creatura a Creatore, et converso, sed dissimiliter valde. Deus namque mentem creatam sanctificat gratiam infundendo ; eamque magnificat spiritualem profectum præstando ; glorificat vero beatitudinem largiendo. Mens autem creata Deum sanctificat, magnificat, glorificatque, non aliquid ei præstando, sed ejus sanctitatem, dignitatem et gloriam verbis et factis testando : quod fit, dum ei in sanctitate et justitia servit, ejusque laudes jugiter resonat. In hac glorificatione qua Deum glorificamus, consistit nostra felicitas, quemadmodum ait Altissimus, Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum ; et rursus, Ego diligentes me diligo.
paras.en: [[85:12|I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart|Confitebor tibi, Domine Deus meus, in toto corde meo]] [the Latin confitebor means both "I will praise" and "I will confess", and Denis takes it both ways], by the confession of thy praise and of my iniquity; I will confess to thy glory my sins and thy praises. From our inmost hearts, then, and with a heart turned purely to God, let us confess to the Lord his goodness and benefits, and our own wickedness and our very many ingratitudes. [[85:12|And I will glorify thy name for ever|Et glorificabo nomen tuum in æternum]], that is, I will acknowledge thy happiness and glory in words and declare it in deed, beginning it now by faith, and at last completing it without ceasing in heaven by sight. The creature is sanctified, magnified and glorified by the Creator, and conversely, but very differently. For God sanctifies the created mind by infusing grace; he magnifies it by granting spiritual progress; and he glorifies it by bestowing beatitude. But the created mind sanctifies, magnifies and glorifies God, not by granting him anything, but by testifying in words and deeds to his holiness, dignity and glory: which is done when it serves him[[Luke 1:74||]] [[Luke 1:75|in holiness and justice|in sanctitate et justitia]], and continually sounds forth his praises. In this glorification by which we glorify God our happiness consists, as the Most High says, [[1 Kings 2:30|whosoever shall glorify me, him will I glorify|Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum]]; and again, [[Prov 8:17|I love them that love me|Ego diligentes me diligo]].

paras.t: Propterea autem hæc faciam, Quia misericordia tua magna est super me, id est, quoniam multiplicem pietatis tuæ effectum mihi largitus es, mittendo Filium tuum pro me, ejus passione me eruendo, per patientiam tuam me longanimiter expectando : ita quod et eruisti animam meam ex inferno inferiori, id est de peccatis mortalibus, quorum demerito pervenitur ad inferiorem infernum, in quo reprobi demorantur, in æternum damnati. Quadruplex autem ponitur infernus, videlicet : locus purgatorii (unde in Missis pro defunctis cantatur : Libera animas fidelium de pœnis inferni) ; secundus infernus, est locus infantium non baptizatorum ; tertius autem, limbus patrum, ad quem infernum Christus descendit ; quartus, est locus reproborum sine fine pereuntium. Creditur quoque infernus esse sub terra, sicut et purgatorium limbusque patrum. Infernus vero reproborum in infimo loco est, in quo sepultus est dives, de quo Christus in Evangelio loquitur.
paras.en: And I will do these things for this reason, [[85:13|For thy mercy is great towards me|Quia misericordia tua magna est super me]], that is, since thou hast bestowed on me the manifold effect of thy goodness, sending thy Son for me, rescuing me by his passion, and waiting for me with long-suffering through thy patience: so that [[85:13|thou hast delivered my soul out of the lower hell|et eruisti animam meam ex inferno inferiori]], that is, from mortal sins, by whose demerit one comes to the lower hell, in which the reprobate dwell, damned for ever. Now hell is reckoned to be fourfold, namely: the place of purgatory (whence in the Masses for the dead it is sung, Deliver the souls of the faithful from the pains of hell); the second hell is the place of unbaptized infants; the third, the limbo of the fathers, to which hell Christ descended; the fourth is the place of the reprobate, who perish without end. Hell is also believed to be under the earth, as are purgatory and the limbo of the fathers. But the hell of the reprobate is in the lowest place, that in which the rich man was buried[[Luke 16:22||]], of whom Christ speaks in the Gospel.

paras.t: Deus, iniqui, id est spiritus maligni, insurrexerunt super me, animam tentando ; et synagoga potentium, id est congregatio tyrannorum hominumque malorum, quæsierunt animam meam malo exemplo subvertere, a tuo itinere elongare, suis perversitatibus conformare.
paras.en: [[85:14|O God, the wicked|Deus, iniqui]], that is, the evil spirits, [[85:14|are risen up against me|insurrexerunt super me]] by tempting my soul; [[85:14|and the assembly of the mighty|et synagoga potentium]], that is, the congregation of tyrants and of evil men, [[85:14|have sought my soul|quæsierunt animam meam]], to overthrow it by bad example, to draw it far from thy road, to conform it to their perversities.

paras.t: Respice in me, vulnera animæ meæ pie sanando, et miserere mei, miserias meas tollendo. Da imperium tuum, id est, præceptum tuum da mihi puero tuo implere et custodire : quemadmodum in Evangelio dictum est, Si vis ingredi ad vitam, serva mandata ; et salvum me fac filium ancillæ tuæ, puta Ecclesiæ, seu feminæ christianæ. Ecce quam dulcis, amorosus atque blandisonus versus.
paras.en: [[85:16|O look upon me|Respice in me]], by tenderly healing the wounds of my soul, [[85:16|and have mercy on me|et miserere mei]], by taking away my miseries. [[85:16|Give thy command|Da imperium tuum]], that is, grant me, [[85:16|thy servant|puero tuo]], to fulfil and keep thy precept: as is said in the Gospel, [[Matt 19:17|if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments|Si vis ingredi ad vitam, serva mandata]] [the margin gives only Matth. xix]; [[85:16|and save the son of thy handmaid|et salvum me fac filium ancillæ tuæ]], that is, of the Church, or of a Christian woman. Behold how sweet, loving and caressing a verse!

paras.t: Fac mecum signum in bonum : id est, talem effectum operare in me, per quem innotescat me esse dilectum ac prædestinatum a te, liberando videlicet me ab omni incursu hostili, et gratiam infundendo, per quam ea agam quæ sunt signa prædestinationis : quæ sunt, verbum Dei libenter audire, vitia abhorrere in quantum sunt vitia, bonum habere propositum ad semper bene vivendum ; ut dæmones hominesque perversi videant signum hoc, qui oderunt me odio iniquo ac pessimo, invidentes non solum temporali meæ prosperitati, sed animæ quoque saluti ; et confundantur, adspicientes se non posse obtinere de me quod cupiunt, imo oppositum sui desiderii in me conspicientes ; quoniam tu, Domine, adjuvisti me, ne illorum tentationi et persecutioni succumberem, et consolatus es me in omni tribulatione atque angustia, ita ut illud Jacobi adimplerem : Omne gaudium existimate, fratres, quum in tentationes varias incideritis ; illud quoque Salvatoris : Gaudete et exsultate in illa hora, quando videlicet exprobrationes et multa adversa patimini, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlo. Unde Apostolus : Gloriamur, inquit, in spe gloriæ filiorum Dei ; non solum autem, sed et gloriamur in tribulationibus, scientes quod tribulatio patientiam operatur, patientia autem probationem, etc. Hoc modo consolatus fuit Deus Apostolum, qui testatur : Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra.
paras.en: [[85:17|Shew me a token for good|Fac mecum signum in bonum]]: that is, work in me such an effect as may make it known that I am loved and predestined by thee, namely by freeing me from every hostile assault and by infusing grace, through which I may do the things that are signs of predestination: and these are, to hear the word of God willingly, to abhor vices inasmuch as they are vices, and to have a good purpose of always living well; [[85:17|that|ut]] the devils and perverse men [[85:17|may see|videant]] this token, [[85:17|they who hate me|qui oderunt me]] with an unjust and most wicked hatred, envying not only my temporal prosperity but also the salvation of my soul; [[85:17|and be confounded|et confundantur]], seeing that they cannot obtain from me what they desire, but rather beholding in me the opposite of their desire; [[85:17|because thou, O Lord, hast helped me|quoniam tu, Domine, adjuvisti me]], so that I should not give way to their temptation and persecution, [[85:17|and hast comforted me|et consolatus es me]] in every tribulation and distress, so that I might fulfil that saying of James: [[Jas 1:2|count it all joy|Omne gaudium existimate]], brethren, [[Jas 1:2|when you shall fall into divers temptations|quum in tentationes varias incideritis]]; and that of the Saviour too: [[Matt 5:12|Be glad and rejoice|Gaudete et exsultate]] in that hour, that is, when you suffer reproaches and many adversities, [[Matt 5:12|for your reward is very great in heaven|quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlo]] [Denis's "in that hour" recalls Luke 6:23, "in that day"]. Whence the Apostle: We [[Rom 5:2|glory|Gloriamur]], he says, [[Rom 5:2|in the hope of the glory of the sons of God|in spe gloriæ filiorum Dei]]; [[Rom 5:3|And not only so: but we glory also in tribulation, knowing that tribulation worketh patience|non solum autem, sed et gloriamur in tribulationibus, scientes quod tribulatio patientiam operatur]]; [[Rom 5:4|and patience trial|patientia autem probationem]], etc. In this way God comforted the Apostle, who testifies: [[2 Cor 1:5|as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]].

paras.t: Ineffabilis plane est virtus hujus versiculi : sed et totus hic psalmus divina dulcedine, sancto fervore, spirituali jucunditate et admiranda devotione redundat : quem condecet nos cum mentali sapore, cum magna lætitia, cum attentione præcipua decantare.
paras.en: Unspeakable indeed is the power of this little verse; but this whole psalm too overflows with divine sweetness, holy fervour, spiritual joy and admirable devotion: and it befits us to sing it with relish of mind, with great gladness, and with special attention.

paras.t: Precatio. Famulantes tibi nos, Domine, deduc in via tua, et ingrediamur in veritate tua : ut magna super nos stillante misericordia tua, animam nostram eruas ab inferno inferiori, atque æternæ gloriæ facias participari.
paras.en: Prayer. [[85:11|Conduct|Deduc]] us who serve thee, O Lord, [[85:11|in thy way|in via tua]], and may we [[85:11|walk in thy truth|ingrediamur in veritate tua]]: that, as thy great mercy drops down upon us, thou mayest deliver our soul [[85:13|out of the lower hell|ab inferno inferiori]], and make it partake of eternal glory.

86.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI SEXTI : FUNDAMENTA EJUS.
86.title_en: Exposition of the eighty-sixth psalm: The foundations thereof.

paras.t: Psalmi jam pertractandi, qui parvus est quantitate et magnus virtute, brevis verbo, sed magnus sententia, iste est titulus: Filiis Core, psalmus cantici: id est, psalmus iste spiritualem lætitiam continens, cantatur et scriptus est filiis Core, id est fidelibus imitatoribus Christi. His enim in hoc psalmo describitur atque laudatur civitas Dei, id est Ecclesia, secundum duplicem ejus statum. Primo namque agit de ea secundum statum suæ militiæ in præsenti: et inde in titulo dicitur, psalmus: per quem operatio designatur, quia operari convenit Ecclesiæ in statu militiæ. Secundo, scilicet in ultimo versu, loquitur de Ecclesia secundum statum sui triumphi, seu in quantum est cum Deo regnans in cœlo. Idcirco in titulo additur, cantici: per quod spiritualis significatur jucunditas, quæ maxime convenit Sanctis in patria.
paras.en: The psalm now to be treated, which is small in size and great in power, brief in words but great in meaning, has this title: [[86:1|For the sons of Core, a psalm of a canticle|Filiis Core, psalmus cantici]]: that is, this psalm, which holds spiritual gladness, is sung and was written for the sons of Core, that is, for the faithful imitators of Christ. For in this psalm the city of God, that is, the Church, is described and praised to them according to her twofold state. First it treats of her according to the state of her warfare in the present life; and therefore the title says [[86:1|a psalm|psalmus]], by which work is signified, since working befits the Church in the state of warfare [that is, the Church militant]. Secondly, namely in the last verse, it speaks of the Church according to the state of her triumph, or in so far as she reigns with God in heaven. Therefore the title adds [[86:1|of a canticle|cantici]], by which spiritual delight is signified, which above all befits the Saints in the fatherland.

paras.t: Ait ergo: Fundamenta ejus. Non exprimit cujus ejus; et quare hoc facit, puto quod ob eamdem causam, ob quam Maria Magdalene dixit ei, quem hortulanum credebat: Domine, si tu sustulisti eum, dicito mihi, etc. Ob vehementem nempe amorem, nullius mentem credidit ab ejus notitia vacuam, cujus fervidus amor mentem suam omnino implevit, occupavit, possedit. Sic nunc Propheta, propter ardentissimam cordis sui dilectionem quam ad Ecclesiam habuit, nomen ejus non explicat: et tamen de ea se loqui, ex verbis sequentibus innotescit. Relatio igitur fit ad id quod corde prædixit. Itaque dicit: Fundamenta ejus, id est Ecclesiæ, collata sunt et stabilita in montibus sanctis, id est in Christo, monte montium, et ejus Apostolis. Hi namque Ecclesiam, id est Christifideles, in fide et gratia fundaverunt. Quamvis enim unum sit principale summum lumen, fundamentum et mons sanctæ Ecclesiæ, sunt tamen alia quædam secundaria et minus principalia lumina, fundamenta et montes Ecclesiæ: et isti sunt sancti Apostoli, quibus Christus in Evangelio ait, Vos estis lux mundi. De quibus in Apocalypsi habetur: Murus civitatis habens fundamenta duodecim, et in ipsis duodecim nomina duodecim Apostolorum et Agni.
paras.en: He says, then: [[86:1|The foundations thereof|Fundamenta ejus]]. He does not state whose *thereof* means; and why he does this, I think, is for the same reason for which Mary Magdalene said to him whom she took for the gardener: [[John 20:15|Sir, if thou hast taken him hence, tell me|Domine, si tu sustulisti eum, dicito mihi]], etc. For out of her vehement love she believed no one's mind to be empty of the knowledge of him with whose fervent love her own mind was wholly filled, taken up and possessed. So now the Prophet, because of the most ardent love of his heart which he had for the Church, does not spell out her name; and yet it becomes plain from the words that follow that he is speaking of her. The reference, then, is to what he had spoken of beforehand in his heart. And so he says: [[86:1|The foundations thereof|Fundamenta ejus]], that is, of the Church, are laid and established in [[86:1|the holy mountains|montibus sanctis]] [the Latin has "in the holy mountains"], that is, in Christ, the mountain of mountains, and in his Apostles. For these founded the Church, that is, the faithful of Christ, in faith and grace. For although there is one principal and supreme light, foundation and mountain of holy Church, there are nevertheless certain other lights, foundations and mountains of the Church, secondary and less principal: and these are the holy Apostles, to whom Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:14|You are the light of the world|Vos estis lux mundi]]. Of whom we have in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:14|the wall of the city had twelve foundations: And in them, the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb|Murus civitatis habens fundamenta duodecim, et in ipsis duodecim nomina duodecim Apostolorum et Agni]].

paras.t: Potest etiam, quamvis minus subtiliter, istud exponi de montibus terræ, in quibus Christus evangelicam legem prædicavit, confirmavit et docuit, ut sit sensus: Fundamenta ejus, id est fundamentalia documenta Ecclesiæ, initiata ac data sunt, et ipsi quoque Apostoli instructi sunt, in montibus sanctis, id est: in monte Sion, in quo situm erat templum in quo sæpe prædicavit, et cœnaculum in quo Sacramentum altaris instituit et Spiritum Sanctum misit; et in monte quem legitur ascendisse, in quo octo beatitudines docuit et evangelicæ legis doctrinam promulgavit; atque in monte Thabor, in quo coram Petro, Joanne et Jacobo transfiguratus est, et fidem futuræ resurrectionis tali experimento probavit.
paras.en: This can also be expounded, though less subtly, of the mountains of the earth on which Christ preached, confirmed and taught the law of the Gospel, so that the sense is: [[86:1|The foundations thereof|Fundamenta ejus]], that is, the fundamental teachings of the Church, were begun and given, and the Apostles themselves were also instructed, on [[86:1|the holy mountains|montibus sanctis]]: that is, on mount Sion, on which stood the temple in which he often preached, and the upper room in which he instituted the Sacrament of the altar and sent the Holy Ghost; and on the mountain which we read that he went up[[Matt 5:1||]], on which he taught the eight beatitudes and proclaimed the doctrine of the law of the Gospel; and on mount Thabor, on which he was transfigured before Peter, John and James[[Matt 17:1||]], and by such a proof made good the faith in the resurrection to come.

paras.t: Diligit Dominus portas Sion, id est, acceptat et approbat sacramenta, virtutes et exorcismum, catechismum atque Baptismum Ecclesiæ, super omnia tabernacula Jacob, id est magis quam cultum veteris Testamenti, qui in diversis tabernaculis exhibebatur, videlicet: in tabernaculo Moysis: secundo, in tabernaculo facto a David; tertio, in templo Salomonis; quarto, in templo Zorobabel. Hoc est quod ait Apostolus: Nihil ad perfectum adduxit lex; introductio vero melioris spei, per quam approximamus ad Deum. Per hoc autem quod præfert portas Sion, id est cultum et sacramenta, et ea per quæ Christiani regnum ingrediuntur cælestem, observantiis veteris Legis, præfert etiam populum christianum seu ipsam Ecclesiam populo Hebræorum ac Synagogæ. Synagoga equidem erat figura Ecclesiæ; et cultus Synagogæ typus exstitit cultus Ecclesiæ, secundum Dionysium. Figuratum vero præfertur figuris. Idcirco ad Synagogam Dominus per Malachiam ait: Non est mihi voluntas in vobis, et munus non suscipiam de manu vestra. Ecce in his verbis Synagogam et ejus sacrificia reprobat. Ecclesiam vero et ejus sacrificium approbans, addit: Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum magnum est nomen meum in gentibus; et in omni loco sacrificatur et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda.
paras.en: [[86:2|The Lord loveth the gates of Sion|Diligit Dominus portas Sion]], that is, accepts and approves the sacraments, virtues and exorcism, the catechism and Baptism of the Church, [[86:2|above all the tabernacles of Jacob|super omnia tabernacula Jacob]], that is, more than the worship of the Old Testament, which was carried on in different tabernacles: namely, in the tabernacle of Moses[[Num 7:1||]]; secondly, in the tabernacle made by David[[2 Kings 6:17||]]; thirdly, in the temple of Solomon[[3 Kings 8:6||]]; fourthly, in the temple of Zorobabel[[1 Esd 6:15||]]. This is what the Apostle says: [[Heb 7:19|the law brought nothing to perfection: but a bringing in of a better hope, by which we draw nigh to God|Nihil ad perfectum adduxit lex; introductio vero melioris spei, per quam approximamus ad Deum]]. Now by preferring the gates of Sion, that is, the worship and sacraments and the things by which Christians enter the heavenly kingdom, to the observances of the old Law, he also prefers the Christian people, or the Church herself, to the people of the Hebrews and to the Synagogue. For the Synagogue was a figure of the Church, and the worship of the Synagogue was a type of the worship of the Church, according to Dionysius. And the thing figured is preferred to its figures. Therefore the Lord says to the Synagogue through Malachias: [[Mal 1:10|I have no pleasure in you|Non est mihi voluntas in vobis]], [[Mal 1:10|and I will not receive a gift of your hand|et munus non suscipiam de manu vestra]]. See how in these words he rejects the Synagogue and her sacrifices. But approving the Church and her sacrifice, he adds: [[Mal 1:11|from the rising of the sun even to the going down, my name is great among the Gentiles, and in every place there is sacrifice, and there is offered to my name a clean oblation|Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum magnum est nomen meum in gentibus; et in omni loco sacrificatur et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]].

paras.t: Moraliter per Sion intelliguntur speculatores cælestium; per Jacob autem, supplantatores vitiorum. Plus ergo diligit Dominus portas Sion, id est virtutes et opera bona hominum contemplativorum, quam tabernacula Jacob, id est habitatores terræ per Jacob signatos: qui licet in gratia Dei exsistant, nondum tamen vitia funditus ejecerunt, sed indigent quotidie contra motus illicitos dimicare. Quamvis isti magis laborant quam speculativi viri perfecti, minus tamen merentur de præmio essentiali quam illi: quoniam actus eorum non prodeunt ex tam sincera, perfecta ac fervida dilectione ut actus illorum, nec tam prompte, tranquille ac delectabiliter operantur ut illi. Quanto autem quis opus Dei promptius, quietius, delectabiliusque exsequitur, tanto absolute loquendo amplius promeretur.
paras.en: Morally, by Sion are understood those who contemplate heavenly things; by Jacob, those who supplant vices [Jacob means "supplanter"]. The Lord, then, [[86:2|loveth the gates of Sion|diligit Dominus portas Sion]], that is, the virtues and good works of contemplative men, more than [[86:2|the tabernacles of Jacob|tabernacula Jacob]], that is, the dwellers on earth signified by Jacob: who, although they are in the grace of God, have not yet cast out their vices root and branch, but need to fight every day against unlawful movements. Although these labour more than perfect contemplative men, they merit less of the essential reward [that is, the vision and enjoyment of God himself, as distinct from the accidental joys of heaven] than they do: because their acts do not proceed from so pure, perfect and fervent a love as the acts of the others, nor do they work so readily, calmly and gladly as they. And the more readily, quietly and gladly anyone carries out the work of God, the more, speaking absolutely, he merits.

paras.t: Deinceps laudat Ecclesiam propter excellentiam suæ famæ. Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, in veteri Testamento, magis autem in novo, civitas Dei, id est, o Ecclesia Christi. Multa namque præclara loquebantur olim Prophetæ de Ecclesia novi Testamenti: quæ tamen in Canticis canticorum copiosius commendatur. De Ecclesia etenim ex gentibus congregata, in Christo fundata, scriptum est: Lauda, sterilis quæ non paris; decanta laudem et hinni, quæ non pariebas: quia multi filii desertæ, magis quam ejus quæ habuit virum. De qua iterum Isaias: Gens et regnum quod non servierit tibi, peribit; rursusque ad Deum: Ecce, inquit, gentem quam nesciebas, vocabis. De hac etiam Christi Ecclesia in Osee dictum est: Erit in loco ubi dicetur eis, Non populus meus vos, dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis. Et Amos: In die illa suscitabo tabernaculum David quod cecidit, ut requirant ceteri hominum Dominum: quod Jacobus exponit de vocatione gentium ad fidem catholicam. Et alibi laudatur Ecclesia Christi hoc modo: Exaltabitur manus tua super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui peribunt. In Scriptura autem novæ legis, multo splendidius laudatur Ecclesia. Unde in Apocalypsi habetur: Veni, et ostendam tibi novam nuptam, sponsam Agni; et: Vidi Jerusalem novam descendentem de cœlo, a Deo paratam tanquam sponsam ornatam viro suo.
paras.en: Next he praises the Church for the excellence of her renown. [[86:3|Glorious things are said of thee|Gloriosa dicta sunt de te]], in the Old Testament, but more in the New, [[86:3|O city of God|civitas Dei]], that is, O Church of Christ. For the Prophets of old said many splendid things of the Church of the New Testament, though she is commended most abundantly in the Canticle of Canticles. For of the Church gathered from the Gentiles and founded in Christ it is written: [[Is 54:1|Give praise, O thou barren, that bearest not: sing forth praise, and make a joyful noise, thou that didst not travail with child: for many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband|Lauda, sterilis quæ non paris; decanta laudem et hinni, quæ non pariebas: quia multi filii desertæ, magis quam ejus quæ habuit virum]]. Of whom Isaias says again: [[Is 60:12|the nation and the kingdom that will not serve thee, shall perish|Gens et regnum quod non servierit tibi, peribit]]; and again, to God: [[Is 55:5|Behold|Ecce]], he says, [[Is 55:5|thou shalt call a nation, which thou knewest not|gentem quam nesciebas, vocabis]]. Of this Church of Christ it was also said in Osee: [[Osee 1:10|it shall be said to them: You are not my people: it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God|Erit in loco ubi dicetur eis, Non populus meus vos, dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis]]. And Amos: [[Amos 9:11|In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David, that is fallen|In die illa suscitabo tabernaculum David quod cecidit]], [[Acts 15:17|That the residue of men may seek after the Lord|ut requirant ceteri hominum Dominum]] [the last words are from St. James's citation of Amos in Acts 15:17]: which James expounds of the calling of the Gentiles to the Catholic faith[[Acts 15:16||]]. And elsewhere the Church of Christ is praised in this way: [[Mich 5:9|Thy hand shall be lifted up over thy enemies, and all thy enemies shall be cut off|Exaltabitur manus tua super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui peribunt]]. But in the Scripture of the new law the Church is praised far more splendidly. Hence we have in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:9|Come and I will shew thee the bride, the wife of the Lamb|Veni, et ostendam tibi novam nuptam, sponsam Agni]] [Denis reads *novam nuptam, sponsam Agni*, "the new bride, the spouse of the Lamb"]; and: I saw [[Apoc 21:2|the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband|Jerusalem novam descendentem de cœlo, a Deo paratam tanquam sponsam ornatam viro suo]].

paras.t: Appellatur vero Ecclesia civitas, quasi civium unitas: quia in ea colliguntur omnes nationes seu tribus terræ per fidem et caritatem, ut sint unus populus Christi: in quo, secundum Apostolum, non est distinctio Judæi et Græci. Et de hac unione fidelium scriptum est, quod Jesus moriturus erat pro gente; et non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum. Unde Christus orat: Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo quos dedisti mihi, ut sint unum, sicut et nos. Paulus quoque: Obsecro (inquit) vos, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ut id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata.
paras.en: Now the Church is called a *city* [*civitas*], as it were a *unity of citizens* [*civium unitas*]: because in her all the nations or tribes of the earth are gathered by faith and charity, so as to be one people of Christ, in whom, according to the Apostle, [[Rom 10:12|there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek|non est distinctio Judæi et Græci]]. And of this union of the faithful it is written [[John 11:51|that Jesus should die for the nation|quod Jesus moriturus erat pro gente]]; [[John 11:52|And not only for the nation, but to gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed|et non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum]]. Hence Christ prays: [[John 17:11|Holy Father, keep them in thy name whom thou hast given me: that they may be one, as we also are|Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo quos dedisti mihi, ut sint unum, sicut et nos]]. Paul too: [[1 Cor 1:10|I beseech you|Obsecro]] (he says) [[1 Cor 1:10|brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing and that there be no schisms among you|fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ut id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata]].

paras.t: Consequenter declaratur conversio gentium ad Christi obsequium, qui ait: Memor ero Rahab et Babylonis, scientium me. Rahab hoc loco non est proprium nomen mulieris illius, ex qua Salmon genuit Booz, quæ legitur recepisse et abscondisse nuntios Josue; sed secundum Hieronymum, Rahab est hic nomen appellativum, designans superbiam seu superbam: per quod designantur pagani idololatriæ dediti, Deo per elationem multum rebelles. Babylon vero interpretatur confusio: et ita per Babylonem intelliguntur perversi vitiis deordinati. Est itaque sensus: Memor ero, misericordiam impendendo, Rahab et Babylonis, id est gentilium superborum, et in peccatorum confusione existentium; scientium me per fidem, postquam eorum recordatus sum. Horum memor fuit Deus, mittendo ad eorum conversionem sanctos Apostolos, per quorum prædicationem corda eorum edocuit, humiliavit et ordinavit, quemadmodum scriptum est: Ecce ego mittam piscatores multos, dicit Dominus, et piscabuntur eos. Ad litteram quoque memor fuit Dominus Babylonis, quoniam per prædicationem Simonis et Judæ, magnam partem terræ illius convertit ad fidem.
paras.en: Next is declared the conversion of the Gentiles to the service of Christ, who says: [[86:4|I will be mindful of Rahab and of Babylon knowing me|Memor ero Rahab et Babylonis, scientium me]]. *Rahab* in this place is not the proper name of that woman of whom Salmon begot Booz[[Matt 1:5||]], who we read received and hid the messengers of Josue; but, according to Jerome, *Rahab* here is a common noun, signifying pride or a proud woman: by which are signified the pagans given over to idolatry, greatly rebellious against God through haughtiness. *Babylon* is interpreted *confusion*: and so by Babylon are understood the perverse, disordered by their vices. The sense, then, is: [[86:4|I will be mindful|Memor ero]], by bestowing mercy, [[86:4|of Rahab and of Babylon|Rahab et Babylonis]], that is, of the proud Gentiles and of those living in the confusion of sins, [[86:4|knowing me|scientium me]] by faith, after I have remembered them. God was mindful of these by sending the holy Apostles to convert them, by whose preaching he taught, humbled and set in order their hearts, as it is written: [[Jer 16:16|Behold I will send many fishers, saith the Lord, and they shall fish them|Ecce ego mittam piscatores multos, dicit Dominus, et piscabuntur eos]]. Literally, too, the Lord was mindful of Babylon, since by the preaching of Simon and Jude he converted a great part of that land to the faith.

paras.t: Ecce alienigenæ, id est olim a fide extranei. In translatione Hieronymi juxta Hebræum habetur, Ecce Palæstina, id est Philistæi. Et Tyrus, id est populus vitiis angustiatus, privatus latitudine caritatis: Tyrus namque interpretatur angustia; et populus Æthiopum, id est pagani vitiis denigrati. Hi fuerunt illic, id est in civitate Christi, quæ est Ecclesia: hujusmodi enim peccatores, facti sunt Ecclesiæ filii. Ad litteram etiam, Palæstina, Tyrus et Æthiopia, ad Christum erant conversæ, viguitque vehementer fides orthodoxa in populis illis: et ita per homines gentiles circa Judæam habitantes, designantur alii infideles, qui in toto mundo ad Ecclesiæ unitatem pervenerunt.
paras.en: [[86:4|Behold the foreigners|Ecce alienigenæ]], that is, those who were once strangers to the faith. In Jerome's translation from the Hebrew we have: *Behold Palestine*, that is, the Philistines. [[86:4|and Tyre|Et Tyrus]], that is, the people straitened by vices, deprived of the breadth of charity: for *Tyre* is interpreted *straitness*; [[86:4|and the people of the Ethiopians|et populus Æthiopum]], that is, the pagans blackened by vices. [[86:4|these were there|Hi fuerunt illic]], that is, in the city of Christ, which is the Church: for sinners of this kind were made sons of the Church. Literally, too, Palestine, Tyre and Ethiopia were converted to Christ, and the orthodox faith flourished mightily among those peoples: and so by the Gentiles dwelling around Judæa are signified the other unbelievers who throughout the whole world came into the unity of the Church.

paras.t: Numquid Sion dicet homo? Et homo natus est in ea, et ipse fundavit eam Altissimus. Versus iste multipliciter exponitur. Sion namque hoc loco est dativi casus, quia in translatione Hieronymi juxta Hebræum ita habetur, Ad Sion dicetur. Sicque hæc dictio, Numquid, non sumitur negative, sed affirmative, ut sit sensus: Numquid? quasi dicat, Imo; ipsi Sion, id est Ecclesiæ per Sion significatæ, dicet homo quæ in hoc psalmo de Christo atque Ecclesia conscribuntur. Possumus autem per hominem accipere Christi præcursorem: de quo in Evangelio scriptum est, Fuit homo missus a Deo. Hic enim primo evangelizavit Sion: de quo in Isaia dicitur, Super montem excelsum ascende, tu qui evangelizas Sion. Quid autem hic dixerit, subditur: Et homo natus est in ea: id est, Christus Deus et homo genitus est in populo Sion, quoniam natus est ex Virgine gloriosa, quæ est dignissimum membrum in ipsa Ecclesia. Unde ad Hebræos ait Apostolus: Quia pueri communicaverunt carni et sanguini, et ipse Christus participavit eisdem. Et ipse Altissimus, id est Christus ex Virgine natus secundum humanitatem, Altissimus vero et æternus secundum divinitatem, fundavit eam, id est, Virginem matrem in omni gratia stabilivit, in tantum quod nunquam a vero fundamento, peccando prolapsa est. Vel, Fundavit eam, id est Ecclesiam, quam a principio in fide et gratia ædificavit, contestante Deo signis et portentis, et variis virtutibus et Spiritus Sancti distributionibus. Propter quod de Christo loquens Zacharias: Ipse, inquit, ædificabit templum Domino.
paras.en: [[86:5|Shall not Sion say: This man and that man is born in her? and the Highest himself hath founded her|Numquid Sion dicet homo? Et homo natus est in ea, et ipse fundavit eam Altissimus]] [Denis's Latin, *Numquid Sion dicet homo? Et homo natus est in ea*, can be read "Shall a man say to Sion? And a man is born in her"; the expositions below turn on this]. This verse is expounded in many ways. For *Sion* in this place is in the dative case, since in Jerome's translation from the Hebrew we have: *To Sion it shall be said*. And so this word *Numquid* ["shall … not?"] is not taken negatively but affirmatively, so that the sense is: *Shall not?* as if to say, Yes indeed: to Sion herself, that is, to the Church signified by Sion, a man shall say the things that are written in this psalm of Christ and of the Church. And by *man* we can take the forerunner of Christ, of whom it is written in the Gospel: [[John 1:6|There was a man sent from God|Fuit homo missus a Deo]]. For he was the first to bring good tidings to Sion, of whom it is said in Isaias: [[Is 40:9|Get thee up upon a high mountain, thou that bringest good tidings to Sion|Super montem excelsum ascende, tu qui evangelizas Sion]]. And what he said is added: [[86:5|man is born in her|homo natus est in ea]]: that is, Christ, God and man, was begotten among the people of Sion, since he was born of the glorious Virgin, who is the most worthy member in the Church herself. Hence the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:14|because the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself in like manner hath been partaker of the same|Quia pueri communicaverunt carni et sanguini, et ipse Christus participavit eisdem]] [Denis adds "Christ" and leaves out "in like manner"]. [[86:5|and the Highest himself|Et ipse Altissimus]], that is, Christ, born of the Virgin according to his humanity, but Most High and eternal according to his divinity, [[86:5|hath founded her|fundavit eam]], that is, established the Virgin mother in all grace, so much so that she never fell away from the true foundation by sinning. Or, [[86:5|hath founded her|Fundavit eam]], that is, the Church, which from the beginning he built up in faith and grace, [[Heb 2:4|God also bearing them witness by signs and wonders and divers miracles and distributions of the Holy Ghost|contestante Deo signis et portentis, et variis virtutibus et Spiritus Sancti distributionibus]]. Wherefore Zacharias, speaking of Christ, says: [[Zach 6:13|he|Ipse]], he says, [[Zach 6:13|shall build a temple to the Lord|ædificabit templum Domino]] [Denis has *ædificabit* where the Vulgate has *exstruet*].

paras.t: In hoc itaque versu evidenter ostenditur in Christo duplex natura et una persona. Dum enim dicitur, Homo natus est in ea, declaratur in Christo natura humana, temporalis, creata; dum vero idem homo demonstratur pronomine Ipse, patet identitas in persona. Postremo quum subditur, Fundavit eam Altissimus, manifestatur divinitas Christi dupliciter: Primo, quum ait, Fundavit. Nullus enim Ecclesiam originaliter fundavit, nec aliquis propriam matrem fecit, nisi Deus. Secundo, dum ait, Altissimus. Nemo enim altissimus, nisi verus unusque Deus, de quo dictum est supra, Tu solus Altissimus in omni terra. Et alia scriptura ait: Unus est Altissimus creator omnium, omnipotens rex, et metuendus nimis.
paras.en: In this verse, then, there is plainly shown in Christ a twofold nature and one person. For when it is said, [[86:5|man is born in her|Homo natus est in ea]], the human nature in Christ, temporal and created, is declared; but when the same man is pointed out by the pronoun *himself*, the identity in person is evident. Lastly, when it is added, [[86:5|the Highest himself hath founded her|Fundavit eam Altissimus]], the divinity of Christ is shown in two ways. First, when it says *hath founded*: for no one founded the Church at her origin, nor did anyone make his own mother, except God. Secondly, when it says *the Highest*: for no one is the most high but the true and only God, of whom it was said above: [[Ps 82:19|thou alone art the most High over all the earth|Tu solus Altissimus in omni terra]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxvii, 19; the words are Ps 82:19]. And another scripture says: [[Ecclus 1:8|There is one most high Creator Almighty, and a powerful king, and greatly to be feared|Unus est Altissimus creator omnium, omnipotens rex, et metuendus nimis]] [Denis's wording differs a little from the Vulgate: "one Most High, creator of all things, almighty king"].

paras.t: Secundo exponitur sic: Numquid Sion, id est Ecclesiæ, dicet homo, id est Christus? quasi dicat, Imo. Nam Christus frequenter dixit Judæis, atque discipulis, primum adventum suum fuisse impletum. Tertio sic: Numquid Sion, id est virgo Maria, de Sion seu populo Judæorum exorta; vel, Sion, id est Ecclesia; dicet corde et ore, Homo (subaudi, purus) est? quasi dicat, Non: quia nec Virgo Christifera, neque Ecclesia dixit seu credidit Christum esse hominem purum, sed Deum et hominem. Et huic sensui consonat littera qua Chrysostomus utitur, qui ita hunc versum allegat: Mater Sion dicet, Homo.
paras.en: Secondly, it is expounded thus: [[86:5|Shall not|Numquid]] a man, that is, Christ, [[86:5|say|dicet]] to [[86:5|Sion|Sion]], that is, to the Church? as if to say, Yes indeed. For Christ often told the Jews and his disciples that his first coming had been fulfilled. Thirdly, thus: Shall Sion, that is, the Virgin Mary, sprung from Sion or the people of the Jews; or Sion, that is, the Church; say with heart and mouth, *He is a man* (understand: a mere man)? as if to say, No: for neither the Virgin who bore Christ nor the Church said or believed Christ to be a mere man, but God and man. And with this sense agrees the reading Chrysostom uses, who cites this verse thus: *Mother Sion shall say, A man* [this is the reading of the Greek Septuagint].

paras.t: Quarto exponitur sic: Numquid Sion dicet homo? id est, numquid aliquis purus homo, humana sapientia et virtute persuadebit seu suggeret Ecclesiæ, ea quæ de Christo tenenda sunt, scilicet quod et homo natus est in ea, et ipse fundavit eam Altissimus? quasi dicat, Non: quia per humanam rationem hoc persuaderi nequivit, quod Christus esset homo natus, et Deus altissimus. Unde dicit Apostolus: Prædicatio mea non fuit in persuasibilibus humanæ sapientiæ verbis, sed in ostensione spiritus et virtutis. Fides quippe catholica divinæ auctoritati innititur, estque Deo comprobante confirmata, juxta illud: Illi autem profecti prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante, et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis. Sed quare de Christo nunc dictum est, Homo natus est in ea, et non potius, Homo conceptus est in ea, nisi ad insinuandum quod Christus ab exordio suæ conceptionis in Virgine, erat homo cunctis virtutibus scientiisque perfectus? Et hoc est novum illud, de quo scriptum est: Novum creavit Dominus super terram, Mulier circumdabit virum. Propterea angelus dixit ad Joseph: Quod natum est in ea, de Spiritu Sancto est.
paras.en: Fourthly, it is expounded thus: Shall a man say to Sion? that is, shall any mere man, by human wisdom and power, persuade or suggest to the Church the things that are to be held about Christ, namely that [[86:5|man is born in her|homo natus est in ea]], [[86:5|and the Highest himself hath founded her|et ipse fundavit eam Altissimus]]? as if to say, No: for it could not be made convincing by human reason that Christ was a man born and the most high God. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 2:4|my preaching was not in the persuasive words of human wisdom. but in shewing of the Spirit and power|Prædicatio mea non fuit in persuasibilibus humanæ sapientiæ verbis, sed in ostensione spiritus et virtutis]].
