For the Catholic faith rests on divine authority, and is confirmed by God's approval, according to the text: [[Mark 16:20|But they going forth preached every where: the Lord working withal, and confirming the word with signs that followed|Illi autem profecti prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante, et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis]]. But why is it said here of Christ, [[86:5|man is born in her|Homo natus est in ea]], and not rather, *A man is conceived in her*, unless to hint that Christ, from the first moment of his conception in the Virgin, was a man perfect in all virtues and knowledge? And this is that new thing of which it is written: [[Jer 31:22|the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Novum creavit Dominus super terram, Mulier circumdabit virum]]. Therefore the angel said to Joseph: [[Matt 1:20|that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost|Quod natum est in ea, de Spiritu Sancto est]] [*natum*, literally "born", which the Douay-Rheims renders "conceived"].

paras.t: Consequenter de christianæ fidei mysteriorumque Christi evangelizatione ac publicatione subjungitur: Dominus Christus, seu Trinitas Deus, narravit in toto mundo, in scripturis populorum, id est, in Scriptura canonica novi Testamenti, videlicet in Evangeliis, Epistolis, et Actibus Apostolorum. Et quoniam istæ Scripturæ ab Apostolis atque Evangelistis, Christianorum principibus, scriptæ sunt, ideo subditur: et principum horum qui fuerunt in ea. De eis namque prædictum est: Constitues eos principes super omnem terram; et, Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham, id est cum Christo omnium vero Deo.
paras.en: Next is added, of the preaching and publishing of the Christian faith and of the mysteries of Christ: [[86:6|The Lord|Dominus]], Christ, or God the Trinity, [[86:6|shall tell|narravit]] [Denis reads *narravit*, "hath told", for the Vulgate's *narrabit*] in the whole world, [[86:6|in his writings of peoples|in scripturis populorum]], that is, in the canonical Scripture of the New Testament, namely in the Gospels, the Epistles and the Acts of the Apostles. And since these Scriptures were written by the Apostles and Evangelists, the princes of Christians, there is added: [[86:6|and of princes, of them that have been in her|et principum horum qui fuerunt in ea]]. For of them it was foretold: [[Ps 44:17|thou shalt make them princes over all the earth|Constitues eos principes super omnem terram]]; and: [[Ps 46:10|The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham|Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham]], that is, with Christ, the true God of all.

paras.t: Deinde describit Ecclesiam secundum statum quo nominatur triumphans. Sicut lætantium omnium habitatio est in te: id est, habitatio tua, o civitas Dei, superna Jerusalem, est sicut lætantium omnium, id est talis, qualis est habitatio eorum qui omnes lætantur: quod proprie Ecclesiæ militanti non competit, in qua omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur. Cui etiam dicitur, Beati qui lugent; et, Mundus gaudebit, vos autem contristabimini; et alibi, Cum metu et timore ac tremore vestram salutem operamini. Sed verissime competit istud Ecclesiæ triumphanti, cujus tota occupatio est jucundissima incessabilisque Dei laudatio. De qua in Apocalypsi scribitur: Absterget Deus omnem lacrimam ab oculis eorum, et mors ultra non erit, neque luctus, sed nec ullus dolor. Itaque hæc dictio, Sicut, hoc loco non similitudinem, sed veritatem designat.
paras.en: Then he describes the Church according to the state in which she is called triumphant. [[86:7|The dwelling in thee is as it were of all rejoicing|Sicut lætantium omnium habitatio est in te]]: that is, thy dwelling, O city of God, Jerusalem on high, is as of all rejoicing, that is, such as is the dwelling of those who all rejoice: which does not properly befit the Church militant, in which [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution|omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur]]. To which it is also said: [[Matt 5:5|Blessed are they that mourn|Beati qui lugent]]; and: [[John 16:20|the world shall rejoice: and you shall be made sorrowful|Mundus gaudebit, vos autem contristabimini]]; and elsewhere: [[Phil 2:12|with fear and trembling work out your salvation|Cum metu et timore ac tremore vestram salutem operamini]] [Denis has "with fear and dread and trembling"]. But it most truly befits the Church triumphant, whose whole occupation is the most joyful and unceasing praise of God. Of which it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:4|God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes: and death shall be no more|Absterget Deus omnem lacrimam ab oculis eorum, et mors ultra non erit]], [[Apoc 21:4|Nor mourning|neque luctus]], nor any sorrow. And so this word *as it were* does not here signify likeness, but reality.

paras.t: Ecce in psalmo hoc compendioso præclare laudatur Ecclesia, Christi continentur mysteria, cœlestis patriæ commendatur lætitia: quem decet nos eo devotius affectuosiusque cantare, quo in eo vocatio gentium clarius prænuntiatur. Et quoniam satis intricatus est, decet ut ejus intellectum studeamus luculenter cognoscere, et limpide intueri, quia nec aliter poterit cum devotione perfecta proferri.
paras.en: See how in this short psalm the Church is splendidly praised, the mysteries of Christ are contained, and the gladness of the heavenly fatherland is commended: and it befits us to sing it the more devoutly and lovingly, the more clearly the calling of the Gentiles is foretold in it. And since it is rather intricate, it befits us to strive to know its meaning clearly and to see into it plainly, for otherwise it cannot be recited with perfect devotion.

paras.t: Precatio. Vivifica nos, Domine, ab operibus mortuis, et fundamenta sinceræ fidei et bonæ operationis in nobis construe: quibus fructum virtutum superædificantes, animas nostras ad te proficiscentes gloriosa civitas tua suscipiat gratulando.
paras.en: Prayer. Quicken us, O Lord, from dead works, and build in us the foundations of sincere faith and good working: so that, building upon them the fruit of the virtues, our souls, as they set out towards thee, may be received with rejoicing by thy glorious city.

87.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI OCTOGESIMI SEPTIMI : DOMINE, DEUS SALUTIS MEÆ.
87.title_en: Literal exposition of the eighty-seventh psalm: O Lord, the God of my salvation.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi nunc explanandi talis est : Canticum, psalmus, filiis Core, in finem, pro Maheleth ad respondendum, intellectus Eman Israelitæ : id est, tractatus præsens qui dicitur canticum, quoniam agit de his per quæ ad spiritualem lætitiam pervenitur, videlicet de Christi passione, quæ est porta ad gloriam : qui tractatus appellatur etiam psalmus, quoniam monet ad bene operandum, scilicet ad imitationem dominicæ passionis ; et dirigit nos psalmus iste in finem, qui Christus est. Proponitur quoque filiis Core, id est sectatoribus Crucifixi, qui carnem suam crucifigunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis. Et scriptus est psalmus iste pro Maheleth, id est pro populo fideli per modum coronæ seu chori ad Christum concurrenti, ad respondendum, id est, ut ei tanquam præcentori respondeant, imitando vestigia ejus : quatenus exsistendo socii tribulationum, socii fiant et consolationis. Et hic psalmus est intellectus Eman Israelitæ, id est, in eo describitur quid frater et consortes Christi intelligere debet : utpote terrenas delectationes esse spernendas, et pro Dei amore dura et aspera sponte et æquanimiter esse toleranda.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is this: [[87:1|A canticle of a psalm for the sons of Core: unto the end, for Maheleth, to answer understanding of Eman|Canticum, psalmus, filiis Core, in finem, pro Maheleth ad respondendum, intellectus Eman]] the Israelite [Denis reads *Israelitæ*, "of the Israelite", where the Vulgate has *Ezrahitæ*, "the Ezrahite", as the Douay-Rheims renders it]: that is, the present treatise, which is called [[87:1|A canticle|canticum]] because it treats of the things through which one comes to spiritual joy, namely of the passion of Christ, which is the gate to glory; and this treatise is also called [[87:1|a psalm|psalmus]], because it urges us to work well, that is, to imitate the Lord's passion; and this psalm directs us [[87:1|unto the end|in finem]], which is Christ. It is also set forth [[87:1|for the sons of Core|filiis Core]], that is, for the followers of the Crucified, who [[Gal 5:24|have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences|carnem suam crucifigunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]]. And this psalm was written [[87:1|for Maheleth|pro Maheleth]], that is, for the faithful people running together to Christ in the manner of a crown or choir, [[87:1|to answer|ad respondendum]], that is, so that they may answer him as their precentor by following in his footsteps: so that, being companions of his tribulations, they may become companions also of his consolation[[2 Cor 1:7||]]. And this psalm is [[87:1|understanding of Eman|intellectus Eman]] the Israelite, that is, in it is described what a brother and fellow of Christ ought to understand: namely, that earthly delights are to be spurned, and that hard and harsh things are to be borne willingly and with an even mind for the love of God.

paras.t: Maheleth interpretatur chorus ; Eman vero, frater fidelis. Ergo concorditer et ex omni latere Christum imitando, sunt Maheleth ; unusquisque quoque eorum Christo se conformando, est Eman, id est frater Christi qui ait in Evangelio, Vade, et dic fratribus meis. Est etiam Israelita, id est Domini speculator. Secundum Hugonem, psalmi in quorum titulis ponitur, Psalmus, agunt de operatione ; in quorum autem titulis ponitur, Canticum, agunt de spirituali lætitia ; sed in quibus utrumque conjungitur, de operatione et lætitia agunt. Denique, secundum Hieronymum, Eman Israelita (vel, ut alii dicunt, Jesraita) exstitit auctor psalmi præsentis, sicut et ceterorum in quorum titulo ponitur.
paras.en: Now *Maheleth* is interpreted "choir", and *Eman* "faithful brother". Those, then, who imitate Christ with one accord and on every side are Maheleth; and each one of them, conforming himself to Christ, is Eman, that is, a brother of Christ, who says in the Gospel: [[John 20:17|go to my brethren and say to them|Vade, et dic fratribus meis]]. He is also an Israelite, that is, one who watches for the Lord [Denis takes *Israel* as "one who sees God"; *speculator* is a watchman or beholder]. According to Hugh, the psalms in whose titles *Psalm* is set treat of working; those in whose titles *Canticle* is set treat of spiritual joy; but those in which both are joined treat of working and of joy. Lastly, according to Jerome, Eman the Israelite (or, as others say, the Jesraite [the edition prints a footnote here giving *Ezrahitæ*, "the Ezrahite", the reading of the Vulgate title]) was the author of the present psalm, as also of the others in whose title he is named.

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta in persona Christi in passione existentis, ait : Domine, Deus salutis meæ. Deus Trinitas seu Deus Pater, est Deus salutis Christi, loquendo de salute Christi creata, quam anima ejus habuit a principio suæ creationis, Deum per speciem intuendo. Hujus namque salutis Pater seu Trinitas dicitur Deus, tanquam dator, conservator et objectum ipsius. Erat autem in Christo etiam salus increata, æterna et infinita, quæ est ipsa divina essentia. Et quamvis Christus Verbum Dei, hanc a Patre suscipit sicut divinam essentiam, non tamen Pater dicitur Deus hujus salutis Christi, quoniam in nomine Dei designatur excellentia super id cujus est Deus. Pater autem non est excellentior Filio, quantum ad increatam ejus salutem.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of Christ in his passion, the Prophet says: [[87:2|O Lord, the God of my salvation|Domine, Deus salutis meæ]]. God the Trinity, or God the Father, is the God of Christ's salvation [*salus*: salvation, health, well-being; here the blessedness of Christ's soul], speaking of the created salvation of Christ, which his soul had from the beginning of its creation, beholding God face to face [*per speciem*, "by sight", as opposed to by faith]. For the Father, or the Trinity, is called the God of this salvation as its giver, preserver and object. But there was in Christ also an uncreated salvation, eternal and infinite, which is the divine essence itself. And although Christ, the Word of God, receives this from the Father, as he receives the divine essence, yet the Father is not called the God of this salvation of Christ, since the name *God* signifies an excellence over that of which he is God; and the Father is not more excellent than the Son as regards his uncreated salvation.

paras.t: In die clamavi et nocte, id est, in prosperis et adversis, atque assidue exoravi, coram te, id est corde non vago et a te distracto, sed coram te constituto, attento ac devoto. Vel, In die passionis seu die Parasceves, et nocte præcedente, clamavi magno affectu te invocando, dicens, Pater, ignosce illis ; et, Si possibile est, transeat a me calix iste. Clamore vocali et exteriori Christus ut homo non oravit Deum nocte ac die, ita quod nunquam cessavit, quamdiu in mundo moratus est ; sed credendum est quod ab interiori clamore nunquam cessavit : imo quemadmodum ardentissime humani generis salutem optavit, sic indesinenter ac affectuosissime pro ea mentaliter Deum deprecabatur.
paras.en: [[87:2|I have cried in the day, and in the night|In die clamavi et nocte]], that is, in prosperity and in adversity, and I have prayed without ceasing, [[87:2|before thee|coram te]], that is, with a heart not wandering and drawn away from thee, but set before thee, attentive and devout. Or: [[87:2|in the day|In die]] of the passion, that is, the day of the Parasceve [that is, the day of Preparation, Good Friday], [[87:2|and in the night|et nocte]] before it, [[87:2|I have cried|clamavi]], calling upon thee with great affection and saying: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them|Pater, ignosce illis]]; and: [[Matt 26:39|if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me|Si possibile est, transeat a me calix iste]]. Christ as man did not pray to God night and day with a vocal and outward cry, in such a way that he never ceased as long as he dwelt in the world; but it is to be believed that he never ceased from the inward cry: indeed, as he most ardently desired the salvation of the human race, so he unceasingly and with the deepest affection besought God for it in his mind.

paras.t: Quid vero orando dixerit subditur : Intret in conspectu tuo, id est, tibi accepta sit, oratio mea ; inclina aurem tuam ad precem meam, eam implendo.
paras.en: What he said in praying is then added: [[87:3|Let my prayer come in before thee|Intret in conspectu tuo]], that is, let [[87:3|my prayer|oratio mea]] be acceptable to thee; [[87:3|incline thy ear to my petition|inclina aurem tuam ad precem meam]], by fulfilling it.

paras.t: Et hoc igitur oro, Quia repleta est malis anima mea. Triplex est malum, videlicet malum naturæ, sicut naturalis defectus, malum pœnæ, et malum culpæ. Malum autem naturæ in Christo non fuit, quia secundum Damascenum, detrahibiles defectus non assumpsit. Malum quoque culpæ longe erat a Christo omnium sanctificatore. Sed malis pœnæ seu pœnis plena erat anima ejus et caro, puta vulneribus, timore, dolore, tristitia. Propter quod dixit : Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem ; et : Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me? Unde in Isaia scriptum est : Vidimus eum despectum et novissimum virorum, virum dolorum, et scientem infirmitatem. Vel, dicitur anima Christi malis repleta, id est peccatis, non propriis, sed eorum pro quibus passus est Christus, eo modo quo per Isaiam dicitur : Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Juxta quem modum Apostolus loquitur : Christus factus est pro nobis maledictum, ut nos de maledicto legis liberaret. Scriptum est enim : Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno. Et vita mea inferno, id est morti per quam ad infernum transitur, et quæ inferno assimilatur, appropinquavit, quia morti exposita est.
paras.en: And this, then, I pray, [[87:4|For my soul is filled with evils|Quia repleta est malis anima mea]]. Evil is threefold: the evil of nature, such as a natural defect; the evil of punishment; and the evil of guilt. The evil of nature was not in Christ, because, according to Damascene, he did not take on the detractable defects [that is, defects that would detract from his perfection, such as ignorance or difficulty in doing good; he took only the blameless ones, such as hunger, weariness and the capacity to suffer]. The evil of guilt, too, was far from Christ, the sanctifier of all. But his soul and his flesh were full of the evils of punishment, that is, of pains: of wounds, fear, pain and sorrow. On account of which he said: [[Matt 26:38|My soul is sorrowful even unto death|Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem]]; and: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?]][[Ps 21:2||]]. Hence it is written in Isaias: [[Is 53:2|we have seen him|Vidimus eum]] [[Is 53:3|Despised, and the most abject of men, a man of sorrows, and acquainted with infirmity|despectum et novissimum virorum, virum dolorum, et scientem infirmitatem]]. Or, the soul of Christ is said to be filled with evils, that is, with sins: not his own, but those of the men for whom Christ suffered, in the way in which it is said through Isaias: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. In the same way the Apostle says: Christ, [[Gal 3:13|being made a curse for us|factus est pro nobis maledictum]], that he might deliver us [[Gal 3:13|from the curse of the law|de maledicto legis]]. For it is written: [[Gal 3:13|Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree|Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno]][[Deut 21:23||]] [the margin gives Deut. xxi, 23, the text the Apostle quotes; Denis's words are those of Gal 3:13]. [[87:4|and my life|Et vita mea]] [[87:4|to hell|inferno]], that is, to death, through which one passes to hell and which is likened to hell, [[87:4|hath drawn nigh|appropinquavit]], because it has been exposed to death.

paras.t: Æstimatus sum a perversis Judæis et infidelibus universis cum descendentibus in lacum, id est talis, quales sunt qui propter sua peccata ad infernum descendunt, et sepulturæ traduntur. Quoniam enim videbant Christum similiter aliis mori, putabant eum cum aliis similem causam mortis habere, ac per hoc corpus ejus in sepulcro debere resolvi, animam quoque ipsius in inferno teneri. Idcirco dictum est : Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo et humiliatum. Et hoc est quod impii dicunt de Christo : Tormentis interrogemus eum, et probemus quæ ventura sunt illi, et sciemus reverentiam ejus. Si enim vere Filius Dei est, liberabit eum de manibus adversariorum, id est, non sinet eum occidi.
paras.en: [[87:5|I am counted|Æstimatus sum]] by the perverse Jews and by all unbelievers [[87:5|among them that go down to the pit|cum descendentibus in lacum]], that is, as one such as those who for their sins go down to hell and are given over to burial. For since they saw Christ die like others, they thought he had a like cause of death with the others, and so that his body must be dissolved in the tomb and his soul held in hell. Therefore it is said: [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God and afflicted|Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo et humiliatum]]. And this is what the wicked say of Christ: [[Wis 2:19|Let us examine him by outrages and tortures|Tormentis interrogemus eum]], [[Wis 2:17|and let us prove what shall happen to him|et probemus quæ ventura sunt illi]], [[Wis 2:19|that we may know his meekness|et sciemus reverentiam ejus]] [Denis has *reverentiam*, "his reverence"]. [[Wis 2:18|For if he be the true son of God|Si enim vere Filius Dei est]], he [[Wis 2:18|will deliver him from the hands of his enemies|liberabit eum de manibus adversariorum]], that is, he will not let him be killed.

paras.t: Factus sum sicut homo sine adjutorio, id est, illis factus sum similis, quibus nullus succurrit, quos Deus non protegit, nec adjuvat homo. Talibus Christus factus est similis : Primo, secundum exteriorem apparentiam, quoniam Deus permisit eum ab impiis cruciari, ac si ad ipsum non pertinuisset. Propter quod Christus dixit Judæis : Hæc est hora vestra et potestas tenebrarum. Tunc nempe Filius hominis (sicut ipse prædixit) traditus est in manus peccatorum, feceruntque in eum quæcumque voluerunt. Secundo, factus dicitur Christus sicut homo sine adjutorio, secundum Judæorum reputationem, qui putabant Deum non esse auxiliatorem ipsius, dicentes : Si rex Israel est, descendat nunc de cruce, et credimus ei. Confidit in Deo; liberet eum nunc, si vult. Et iterum : Alios salvos fecit, se ipsum non potest salvum facere. Tertio, propter solitæ consolationis subtractionem, qua inferior pars animæ Christi impleri, vel aliquid participare solebat a plenitudine beatitudinis superioris partis animæ suæ : et ideo ait, Eloi, Eloi, lamma sabacthani ? Secundum veritatem tamen, absolute loquendo, nunquam erat Christus homo sine adjutorio Dei, sicut per Isaiam testatur : Dominus Deus auxiliator meus, ideo non sum confusus. Per Jeremiam quoque : Dominus mecum est tanquam bellator fortis.
paras.en: [[87:5|I am become as a man without help|Factus sum sicut homo sine adjutorio]], that is, I have become like those whom no one succours, whom God does not protect, nor man help. Christ became like such men: first, in outward appearance, since God allowed him to be tortured by the wicked as though he were no concern of his. On account of which Christ said to the Jews: [[Luke 22:53|this is your hour and the power of darkness|Hæc est hora vestra et potestas tenebrarum]]. For then the Son of man (as he himself foretold) was delivered into the hands of sinners[[Matt 26:45||]], and they [[Matt 17:12|have done unto him whatsoever they had a mind|feceruntque in eum quæcumque voluerunt]] [the margin gives Matt. xxvii, 12; these words are those of Matt 17:12, said of Elias and of the Son of man]. Secondly, Christ is said to have become as a man without help in the reckoning of the Jews, who thought that God was not his helper, saying: [[Matt 27:42|If he be the king of Israel, let him now come down from the cross: and we will believe him|Si rex Israel est, descendat nunc de cruce, et credimus ei]]. [[Matt 27:43|He trusted in God: let him now deliver him if he will have him|Confidit in Deo; liberet eum nunc, si vult]]. And again: [[Matt 27:42|He saved others: himself he cannot save|Alios salvos fecit, se ipsum non potest salvum facere]]. Thirdly, because of the withdrawal of the accustomed consolation, by which the lower part of Christ's soul used to be filled from the fullness of the beatitude of the higher part of his soul, or to have some share in it: and therefore he said: [[Mark 15:34|Eloi, Eloi, lamma sabacthani|Eloi, Eloi, lamma sabacthani]]? Yet in truth, speaking absolutely, Christ was never a man without the help of God, as he testifies through Isaias: [[Is 50:7|The Lord God is my helper, therefore am I not confounded|Dominus Deus auxiliator meus, ideo non sum confusus]] [the margin gives Is. i, 7; the words are Is 50:7]. And through Jeremias also: [[Jer 20:11|the Lord is with me as a strong warrior|Dominus mecum est tanquam bellator fortis]].

paras.t: Itaque, Factus sum sicut homo sine adjutorio ego Christus, qui solus sum inter mortuos liber, id est, inter mortales culpa carens, et liberatore non indigens : qui necessitatem moriendi non habui, neque in morte detineri prævalui ; sed de claustris gehennæ ac fossa sepulturæ propria potestate egressus sum. Merito dicitur Christus inter mortuos (morte peccati seu morte naturali) liber, qui de se ipso loquitur : Venit ad me princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam. De ceteris vero Apostolus asserit : Omnes peccaverunt, et egent gloria Dei. Rursusque : Conclusit Deus omnia sub peccato, ut omnium misereretur.
paras.en: So then: [[87:5|I am become as a man without help|Factus sum sicut homo sine adjutorio]], I, Christ, who alone am [[87:6|Free among the dead|inter mortuos liber]], that is, among mortals free of guilt and needing no deliverer: I who was under no necessity of dying, nor could be held fast in death, but went forth by my own power from the prisons of hell and the pit of the tomb. Rightly is Christ called [[87:6|among the dead|inter mortuos]] (whether by the death of sin or by natural death) [[87:6|free|liber]], who says of himself: [[John 14:30|the prince of this world: cometh|Venit ad me princeps mundi hujus]] to me, [[John 14:30|and in me he hath not any thing|et in me non habet quidquam]]. But of the rest the Apostle declares: [[Rom 3:23|all have sinned and do need the glory of God|Omnes peccaverunt, et egent gloria Dei]]. And again: [[Rom 11:32|God hath concluded all|Conclusit Deus omnia]] [[Gal 3:22|under sin|sub peccato]], [[Rom 11:32|that he may have mercy on all|ut omnium misereretur]].

paras.t: Reputatus insuper a Judæis sum sic periisse, Sicut vulnerati dormientes in sepulcris, id est ex vulnerum inflictione occisi, somno mortis in tumulis quiescentes, quorum non es memor amplius : qui in peccatis mortalibus obierunt, et ideo sempiternæ oblivioni traduntur, quantum ad perceptionem misericordiæ Dei : ideo additur, et ipsi de manu tua repulsi sunt, id est, tua protectione atque salute omnino privati sunt. Talibus sceleratis putabant Judæi Christum consimilem. Unde Pilatum affati sunt : Domine, recordati sumus, quia seductor ille dixit adhuc vivens. Jam ergo opinabantur eum cum fallacibus condemnatum.
paras.en: Moreover, I was reckoned by the Jews to have perished thus: [[87:6|Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres|Sicut vulnerati dormientes in sepulcris]], that is, killed by wounds inflicted, resting in the sleep of death in the tombs, [[87:6|whom thou rememberest no more|quorum non es memor amplius]]: those who died in mortal sins and are therefore given over to everlasting forgetfulness as regards receiving the mercy of God: so it is added, [[87:6|and they are cut off from thy hand|et ipsi de manu tua repulsi sunt]], that is, they are wholly deprived of thy protection and salvation. The Jews thought Christ like such criminals. Hence they said to Pilate: [[Matt 27:63|Sir, we have remembered, that that seducer said, while he was yet alive|Domine, recordati sumus, quia seductor ille dixit adhuc vivens]]. They already held him, then, to be condemned with deceivers.

paras.t: Posuerunt me in lacu inferiori, id est, cum his deputaverunt me, qui ad infima ac pœnalissima loca inferni projiciuntur. Quemadmodum enim maxima scelera Christo adhuc viventi adscripserunt, dicendo, Blasphemavit, etc. ; sic maxima tormenta mortuo inesse arbitrabantur. In tenebrosis et in umbra mortis. Infernus enim, locus tenebrosus est et umbra mortis, juxta illud : Dimitte me, antequam vadam ad terram tenebrosam et opertam mortis caligine : terram miseriæ et tenebrarum, ubi umbra mortis et nullus ordo, sed sempiternus horror inhabitat.
paras.en: [[87:7|They have laid me in the lower pit|Posuerunt me in lacu inferiori]], that is, they reckoned me with those who are cast down into the lowest and most penal places of hell. For as they ascribed the greatest crimes to Christ while he yet lived, saying: [[Matt 26:65|He hath blasphemed|Blasphemavit]], etc., so they judged that the greatest torments were his once dead. [[87:7|in the dark places, and in the shadow of death|In tenebrosis et in umbra mortis]]. For hell is a dark place and the shadow of death, according to that: [[Job 10:20|Suffer me|Dimitte me]], [[Job 10:21|Before I go|antequam vadam]] [[Job 10:21|to a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death|ad terram tenebrosam et opertam mortis caligine]]: [[Job 10:22|A land of misery and darkness, where the shadow of death, and no order, but everlasting horror dwelleth|terram miseriæ et tenebrarum, ubi umbra mortis et nullus ordo, sed sempiternus horror inhabitat]].

paras.t: Super me confirmatus est furor tuus : id est, rigorem justitiæ tuæ, quem demonstrasses in cunctis hominibus, nisi ego pro eis satisfecissem, demonstrasti in me, non parcendo proprio Filio tuo, sed morte amarissima atque turpissima me occidi permittendo : imo pro universis hominibus me tradendo, quemadmodum per Isaiam protestatus es, Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum. Et omnes fluctus tuos, id est omnia genera tormentorum, induxisti, id est, induci permisisti, super me. Passio enim Christi generalissima fuit, quia omnes cruciatus generis humani pertulit, quantum ad genus. In omnibus enim viribus animæ et membris corporis passus est, scilicet captus, vinctus, colaphizatus, consputus, contristatus, ab omnibus derelictus, contemptus, derisus : et sic omnia genera pœnarum, quæ infligi debuerant generi humano pro peccatis, Deus Pater Christo induxit quodammodo. Unde in Isaia dicitur : Disciplina pacis nostræ super eum, cujus livore sanati sumus.
paras.en: [[87:8|Thy wrath is strong over me|Super me confirmatus est furor tuus]]: that is, the rigour of thy justice, which thou wouldst have shown in all men had I not made satisfaction for them, thou hast shown in me, not sparing thine own Son[[Rom 8:32||]], but permitting me to be slain by a most bitter and most shameful death; indeed, delivering me up for all men, as thou didst declare through Isaias: [[Is 53:8|for the wickedness of my people have I struck him|Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum]]. [[87:8|and all thy waves|Et omnes fluctus tuos]], that is, all kinds of torments, [[87:8|thou hast brought in|induxisti]], that is, thou hast permitted to be brought in, [[87:8|upon me|super me]]. For the passion of Christ was most universal, since he bore all the torments of the human race, as to their kinds. For he suffered in all the powers of his soul and in the members of his body: he was taken, bound, buffeted, spat upon, saddened, forsaken by all, despised, mocked; and so God the Father in a manner brought upon Christ all the kinds of pains that were due to be inflicted on the human race for its sins. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 53:5|the chastisement of our peace was upon him|Disciplina pacis nostræ super eum]], [[Is 53:5|by his bruises we are healed|cujus livore sanati sumus]].

paras.t: Longe fecisti notos meos a me, id est, discipulos meos a me fugere permisisti timore Judæorum : quemadmodum apud Matthæum legitur, Tunc discipuli omnes, relicto eo, fugerunt. Vel, Notos meos, id est eos qui me noverunt, et opera mea atque doctrinam approbaverunt, quando prædicabam atque miracula coram eis faciebam : de quibus scriptum est, Omnis plebs ut vidit, dedit laudem Deo. Hos tempore passionis meæ permisisti averti a me. Multi enim Judæorum qui sæpe Christum et ejus opera laudaverunt, a principibus sacerdotum seducti, in die Parasceves Christum occidi petierunt : de quibus dicitur apud Matthæum : Respondens universus populus, dixit, Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros. De quibus subjungitur : posuerunt me abominationem sibi, id est, me contempserunt, et tanquam vilem æstimaverunt : sicut superius dictum est, Omnes videntes me, deriserunt me. Unde in Luca scriptum est : Deridebant eum principes, dicentes : Alios salvos fecit, se ipsum salvum faciat, si hic est Christus Dei electus.
paras.en: [[87:9|Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me|Longe fecisti notos meos a me]], that is, thou hast permitted my disciples to flee from me for fear of the Jews: as is read in Matthew: [[Matt 26:56|Then the disciples, all leaving him, fled|Tunc discipuli omnes, relicto eo, fugerunt]]. Or: [[87:9|my acquaintance|Notos meos]], that is, those who knew me and approved my works and teaching when I preached and worked miracles before them: of whom it is written: [[Luke 18:43|all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God|Omnis plebs ut vidit, dedit laudem Deo]]. These thou hast permitted to be turned away from me in the time of my passion. For many of the Jews who had often praised Christ and his works, led astray by the chief priests, demanded on the day of the Parasceve that Christ be put to death: of whom it is said in Matthew: [[Matt 27:25|the whole people answering, said: His blood be upon us and upon our children|Respondens universus populus, dixit, Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]]. Of whom it is added: [[87:9|they have set me an abomination to themselves|posuerunt me abominationem sibi]], that is, they despised me and esteemed me as worthless: as was said above: [[Ps 21:8|All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn|Omnes videntes me, deriserunt me]]. Hence it is written in Luke: [[Luke 23:35|the rulers with them derided him, saying: He saved others: let him save himself, if he be Christ, the elect of God|Deridebant eum principes, dicentes : Alios salvos fecit, se ipsum salvum faciat, si hic est Christus Dei electus]].

paras.t: Traditus sum et non egrediebar. Christus a Deo Patre traditus legitur, juxta illud Apostoli : Proprio Filio suo non pepercit, sed pro omnibus nobis tradidit illum. Christus quoque se ipsum tradidit in mortem, sicut per Isaiam dictum est : Tradidit in mortem animam suam. Propter quod in Evangelio dixit : Nemo tollit animam meam a me, sed ego pono eam. Traditus quoque est Christus a Juda proditore. Et non egrediebar a voluntate paterna, sed Patri usque ad mortem obediens fui, dicendo : Fiat voluntas tua. Vel, Non egrediebar fugiendo Judæos, sed eis impavide obviavi ac dixi, Quem quæritis? Vel, Non egrediebar, id est, propter passionis meæ horrorem et crucis abjectionem, foris non cognoscebar qualis interius fui, quoniam sub carnis fragilitate abscondebatur divinitas. Propter quod ab Isaia scribitur : Quasi absconditus vultus ejus ; unde nec reputavimus eum.
paras.en: [[87:9|I was delivered up, and came not forth|Traditus sum et non egrediebar]]. Christ is read to have been delivered up by God the Father, according to that of the Apostle: He [[Rom 8:32|spared not even his own Son, but delivered him up for us all|Proprio Filio suo non pepercit, sed pro omnibus nobis tradidit illum]]. Christ also delivered himself up to death, as was said through Isaias: [[Is 53:12|he hath delivered his soul unto death|Tradidit in mortem animam suam]]. On account of which he said in the Gospel: [[John 10:18|No man taketh it away from me: but I lay it down|Nemo tollit animam meam a me, sed ego pono eam]]. Christ was delivered up also by Judas the traitor. [[87:9|and came not forth|Et non egrediebar]] from the Father's will, but was obedient to the Father even unto death, saying: [[Matt 26:42|thy will be done|Fiat voluntas tua]]. Or: I [[87:9|came not forth|Non egrediebar]] by fleeing from the Jews, but went to meet them fearlessly and said: [[John 18:4|Whom seek ye|Quem quæritis]]? Or: I [[87:9|came not forth|Non egrediebar]], that is, because of the horror of my passion and the abjection of the cross I was not known outwardly for what I was within, since the Godhead was hidden under the frailty of the flesh. On account of which it is written by Isaias: [[Is 53:3|his look was as it were hidden|Quasi absconditus vultus ejus]]; [[Is 53:3|whereupon we esteemed him not|unde nec reputavimus eum]].

paras.t: Oculi mei corporales languerunt præ inopia sanitatis. Nam ex velatione et percussionibus Judæorum, ex abundantia etiam lacrimarum, et maxime ex interiori tristitia animæ Christi, oculi ejus exteriores infirmabantur : quoniam dolor interior solet præcipue in oculis apparere. Vel, Oculi mei, id est oculi corporis mei mystici, puta Apostoli, qui inter ceteros cœlesti visione et luce præfulgent, languerunt præ inopia fidei atque constantiæ : nam et princeps eorum me cum juramento negavit. De eis etenim dictum est : Percutiam pastorem, et dispergentur oves gregis.
paras.en: [[87:10|My eyes|Oculi mei]] of the body [[87:10|languished through poverty|languerunt præ inopia]] of health [*inopia*, "poverty", is want of any kind: here, want of health]. For from the veiling of his face and the blows of the Jews, and also from the abundance of his tears, and above all from the inward sorrow of Christ's soul, his outward eyes grew weak: since inward grief is wont to show itself chiefly in the eyes. Or: [[87:10|My eyes|Oculi mei]], that is, the eyes of my mystical body, namely the Apostles, who shine out among the rest by heavenly vision and light, [[87:10|languished through poverty|languerunt præ inopia]] of faith and constancy: for their prince too denied me with an oath[[Matt 26:72||]]. For of them it is said: [[Zach 13:7|strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered|Percutiam pastorem, et dispergentur oves gregis]] [Denis's wording, "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be dispersed", is that of Matt 26:31, where Christ quotes this verse].

paras.t: Clamavi ad te, Domine : sicut in hujus psalmi exordio patuit ; tota die, id est cunctis diebus vitæ meæ, expandi ad te manus meas, id est, ad te direxi, et ad tui nominis honorem ordinavi opera mea, ubique et semper te honorando. Vel : Tota die, id est pro magna parte diei Parasceves, expandi ad te manus meas corporales in cruce, quatenus omnes electos tibi colligerem atque amplecterer.
paras.en: [[87:10|I cried to thee, O Lord|Clamavi ad te, Domine]]: as appeared at the beginning of this psalm; [[87:10|All the day|tota die]], that is, all the days of my life, [[87:10|I stretched out my hands to thee|expandi ad te manus meas]], that is, I directed my works to thee and ordered them to the honour of thy name, honouring thee everywhere and always. Or: [[87:10|All the day|Tota die]], that is, for a great part of the day of the Parasceve, [[87:10|I stretched out my hands to thee|expandi ad te manus meas]], my bodily hands, on the cross[[Is 65:2||]], that I might gather all the elect to thee and embrace them.

paras.t: Deinde Christus argumentando ostendit, quod ex decore divinæ justitiæ decuit se exaudiri pro se ipso et corpore suo mystico, quatenus ipse suscitaretur in corpore, et fideles per gratiam suscitarentur in anima. Decet namque ut Deus hanc admirabilem gratiam aliquibus tribuat : sed non tribuit eam defunctis : ergo sibi ipsi, scilicet Christo et vivis danda est. Ait ergo :
paras.en: Next, Christ shows by argument that it was fitting, by the seemliness of divine justice, that he should be heard for himself and for his mystical body: so that he himself might be raised up in the body, and the faithful raised up in the soul through grace. For it is fitting that God should grant this wonderful grace to some; but he does not grant it to the dead; therefore it is to be given to himself, that is, to Christ, and to the living. He says, then:

paras.t: Numquid mortuis corpore et anima facies mirabilia, resuscitando eos ad pristinam vitam et gratiæ statum? quasi dicat, Non : juxta illud beati Job, Homo quum dormierit, non resurget ; et denuo, Semitam per quam non revertar, ambulo. Quamvis enim quidam defuncti, etiam impii, sint ex speciali gratia resuscitati, tamen de lege communi mortuus non resurgit. Aut medici suscitabunt mortuos, et confitebuntur tibi mortui suscitati ab eis, tua præconia et sua peccata? Non utique, quoniam hoc naturalem artem et potestatem transcendit.
paras.en: [[87:11|Wilt thou shew wonders|facies mirabilia]] [[87:11|to the dead|Numquid mortuis]] in body and soul, raising them up again to their former life and to the state of grace? As if to say: No; according to that of blessed Job: [[Job 14:12|man when he is fallen asleep shall not rise again|Homo quum dormierit, non resurget]]; and again: [[Job 16:23|I am walking in a path by which I shall not return|Semitam per quam non revertar, ambulo]]. For although some of the departed, even of the wicked, have been raised up by a special grace, yet by the common law the dead man does not rise again. [[87:11|or shall physicians raise to life|Aut medici suscitabunt]] the dead, [[87:11|and give praise to thee|et confitebuntur tibi]], the dead raised up by them, confessing thy praises and their own sins [*confitebuntur* means both "give praise" and "confess"]? Not at all, since this goes beyond the art and power of nature.

paras.t: Numquid narrabit aliquis in sepulcro misericordiam tuam? quasi dicat, Non : quia in monumento non jacet nisi corpus exanime. Et, Numquid narrabit aliquis et veritatem tuam in perditione damnationis æternæ? Nequaquam : quoniam in inferno veritas tua non enarratur, juxta illud, Nec sapientia nec scientia erunt apud inferos.
paras.en: [[87:12|Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy|Numquid narrabit aliquis in sepulcro misericordiam tuam?]]? As if to say: No; for in the tomb there lies nothing but a lifeless body. And: Shall any one declare [[87:12|thy truth in destruction|veritatem tuam in perditione]] of eternal damnation? By no means: for in hell thy truth is not declared, according to that: [[Eccles 9:10|nor wisdom, nor knowledge shall be in hell|Nec sapientia nec scientia erunt apud inferos]].

paras.t: Numquid cognoscentur in tenebris, id est in his qui fide et lumine gratiæ carent, mirabilia tua? Non utique. Et numquid cognoscetur justitia tua in terra oblivionis, id est in his qui obstinantur in malo, quorum pietas tua non recordatur, misericordiam impendendo? quasi dicat, Nullatenus : secundum quod apud alium Prophetam habetur, Non mortui qui sunt in inferno, quorum spiritus acceptus est a visceribus eorum, dabunt honorem tibi Domino. Hi ergo exclusi sunt a gratia Dei, quatenus ceteri ostendantur exaudiendi.
paras.en: Shall [[87:13|thy wonders|mirabilia tua]] [[87:13|be known in the dark|Numquid cognoscentur in tenebris]], that is, in those who lack faith and the light of grace? Not at all. And shall [[87:13|thy justice|justitia tua]] be known [[87:13|in the land of forgetfulness|in terra oblivionis]], that is, in those who are obstinate in evil, whom thy loving-kindness does not remember by bestowing mercy? As if to say: In no wise; according to what is had in another Prophet: [[Bar 2:17|the dead that are in hell, whose spirit is taken away from their bowels, shall not give glory|Non mortui qui sunt in inferno, quorum spiritus acceptus est a visceribus eorum, dabunt honorem]] to thee, [[Bar 2:17|the Lord|Domino]]. These, then, are shut out from the grace of God, so that the others may be shown to be worthy of a hearing.

paras.t: Augustinus et alii litteram istam exponunt alio modo. Quoniam enim opera et merita Christi non omnibus, sed solis prædestinatis ad veram salutem proficiunt, ideo dicitur : Numquid mortuis intus in anima morte peccati, facies mirabilia ad utilitatem ipsorum? quasi dicat, Non: quoniam tales indurati in culpa, ex aspectu mirabilium Dei non moventur ad emendationem. Nam ipsis per Jeremiam dicitur : Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, et pardus varietates suas, et vos poteritis benefacere, quum didiceritis malum. Aut medici spirituales, id est prædicatores verbi Dei, qui animarum languoribus medentur, suscitabunt mortuos jam præfatos, et confitebuntur tibi? Non utique : quoniam nisi Deus intus operetur per gratiam, frustra laborat prædicator per linguam. Numquid narrabit aliquis in sepulcro malæ consuetudinis, seu corpore vitioso, quod est animæ ex peccato jam mortuæ monumentum, misericordiam tuam, laudando beneficia pietatis divinæ, et reparationem naturæ humanæ, et veritatem tuam in perditione, id est in vita desperata ac perdita? Non : quia non est speciosa laus in ore peccatoris.
paras.en: Augustine and others expound this text in another way. For since the works and merits of Christ profit not all, but only those predestined to true salvation, it is said: [[87:11|Wilt thou shew wonders|facies mirabilia]] [[87:11|to the dead|Numquid mortuis]] inwardly, in the soul, by the death of sin, to their profit? As if to say: No; since such men, hardened in guilt, are not moved to amendment by the sight of the wonders of God. For to them it is said through Jeremias: [[Jer 13:23|If the Ethiopian can change his skin, or the leopard his spots: you also may do well, when you have learned evil|Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, et pardus varietates suas, et vos poteritis benefacere, quum didiceritis malum]]. [[87:11|or shall physicians|Aut medici]], spiritual physicians, that is, the preachers of the word of God, who heal the sicknesses of souls, [[87:11|raise to life|suscitabunt]] the dead just spoken of, [[87:11|and give praise to thee|et confitebuntur tibi]]? Not at all: for unless God works within by grace, the preacher labours in vain with his tongue. [[87:12|Shall any one in the sepulchre|Numquid narrabit aliquis in sepulcro]] of evil habit, or in a vicious body, which is the tomb of a soul already dead through sin, [[87:12|declare thy mercy|misericordiam tuam]], praising the benefits of the divine goodness and the restoration of human nature, [[87:12|and thy truth in destruction|et veritatem tuam in perditione]], that is, in a life despaired of and lost? No: for [[Ecclus 15:9|Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner|non est speciosa laus in ore peccatoris]].

paras.t: Et ego ad te, Domine, clamavi. Hæc atque sequentia exponunt doctores de corpore Christi mystico, quod est Ecclesia; sed enitendum videtur, ut totus psalmus de Domino Salvatore elucidetur. Christus igitur ait : Ego ad te, Domine Pater, clamavi: quemadmodum ad Hebræos inducit Apostolus : Christus cum clamore valido et lacrimis preces offerens, exauditus est pro sua reverentia. Et mane, id est cito et in splendore gratiæ tuæ, oratio mea prævenit te, id est, orationem meam ad te dirigam antequam alia agam. Vel, Præveniet te, id est ultionem tuæ justitiæ atque horrendum tuum judicium, ita quod in ea oratione te mitigabo, ne genus humanum penitus perdas ac damnes.
paras.en: [[87:14|But I, O Lord, have cried to thee|Et ego ad te, Domine, clamavi]]. The doctors expound this and what follows of the mystical body of Christ, which is the Church; but it seems we should strive to explain the whole psalm of the Lord our Saviour. Christ, then, says: I, O Lord Father, [[87:14|have cried to thee|clamavi]]: as the Apostle sets forth to the Hebrews: Christ, [[Heb 5:7|with a strong cry and tears, offering up prayers|cum clamore valido et lacrimis preces offerens]], [[Heb 5:7|was heard for his reverence|exauditus est pro sua reverentia]]. [[87:14|and in the morning|Et mane]], that is, quickly and in the splendour of thy grace, [[87:14|my prayer shall prevent thee|oratio mea prævenit te]] [that is, shall come before thee], that is, I will direct my prayer to thee before I do anything else. Or: [[87:14|shall prevent thee|Præveniet te]], that is, it shall come before the vengeance of thy justice and thy dreadful judgment[[Heb 10:27||]][[Heb 10:31||]], so that by that prayer I shall appease thee, lest thou utterly destroy and condemn the human race.

paras.t: Ut quid, Domine, repellis orationem meam? Hoc de Christo sumendum est, quemadmodum illud quod dixit superius : Deus meus, clamabo per diem, et non exaudies. Dicitur enim oratio Christi non exaudita seu repulsa : non illa quæ ex deliberata ejus ratione ac rationali voluntate processit : de illa quippe ait, Pater, ego sciebam quoniam semper me audis; sed illa quam secundum naturalem affectum seu sensitivum appetitum effudit, dicendo : Pater, si fieri potest, transeat a me calix iste. Avertis faciem tuam a me? id est, cur, o Pater, consolationis tuæ præsentiam et solitæ pietatis adspectum subtrahis naturæ meæ passibili in cruce vexatæ, ita ut clamare compulsus sim : Deus, Deus meus, respice in me, quare me dereliquisti? Nunquam tamen facies Dei, quæ est ipsemet Deus benedictus, in cujus visione beatitudo consistit, ab anima Christi aversa erat, sed indesinenter eam adspexit visione beata, etiam tempore passionis.
paras.en: [[87:15|Lord, why castest thou off my prayer|Ut quid, Domine, repellis orationem meam?]]? This is to be taken of Christ, as is what he said above: [[Ps 21:3|O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear|Deus meus, clamabo per diem, et non exaudies]]. For the prayer of Christ is said to be unheard, or cast off: not that which proceeded from his deliberate reason and rational will, for of that he says: [[John 11:41|Father|Pater]], [[John 11:42|I knew that thou hearest me always|ego sciebam quoniam semper me audis]]; but that which he poured out according to natural affection, or the sensitive appetite [that is, the desire of the senses, which shrinks by nature from pain and death], saying: [[Matt 26:39|My Father, if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me|Pater, si fieri potest, transeat a me calix iste]]. [[87:15|why turnest thou away thy face from me?|Avertis faciem tuam a me?]] That is: why, O Father, dost thou withdraw the presence of thy consolation and the sight of thy wonted loving-kindness from my passible nature, tormented on the cross, so that I am compelled to cry out: [[Ps 21:2|O God my God, look upon me: why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus, Deus meus, respice in me, quare me dereliquisti?]] Yet the face of God, which is the blessed God himself, in the vision of whom beatitude consists, was never turned away from the soul of Christ, but beheld it unceasingly with the blessed vision, even in the time of the passion.

paras.t: Pauper sum ego, et totius paupertatis exemplar : qui non habui ubi caput reclinarem, et de eleemosynis vixi devotarum feminarum ; et in laboribus a juventute mea : Christus namque nec intus, nec foris exstitit otiosus, sed orando, jejunando, Joseph et Mariæ serviendo, deinde prædicando, discurrendo, esuriendo, sitiendo, patiendo ac moriendo, laboravit. Propter quod protestatur : Servire me fecisti in peccatis tuis ; præbuisti mihi laborem in iniquitatibus tuis. Unde scriptum est : Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur. Et alibi : Jesus fatigatus ex itinere.
paras.en: [[87:16|I am poor|Pauper sum ego]], and the pattern of all poverty: I who had not where to lay my head[[Luke 9:58||]], and lived on the alms of devout women; [[87:16|and in labours from my youth|et in laboribus a juventute mea]]: for Christ was never idle, within or without, but laboured in praying, fasting, serving Joseph and Mary, then in preaching, going about, hungering, thirsting, suffering and dying. On account of which he protests: [[Is 43:24|thou hast made me to serve with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thy iniquities|Servire me fecisti in peccatis tuis ; præbuisti mihi laborem in iniquitatibus tuis]]. Hence it is written: [[Is 53:11|Because his soul hath laboured, he shall see and be filled|Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur]]. And elsewhere: Jesus [[John 4:6|being wearied with his journey|fatigatus ex itinere]].

paras.t: Exaltatus autem, humiliatus sum. Nam sicut Evangelista affirmat, quum voluissent Judæi Christum regem facere, fugit et declinavit a turba ; quum etiam laudaretur a populo conclamante, Omnia bene fecit, et surdos fecit audire, et mutos loqui ; itemque, Nunquam sic apparuit in Israel : nihil sibi ipsi attribuit, sed totum ad Patris retulit gloriam. Dum quoque exaltatus fuisset a Judæis in die Palmarum, clamantibus, Hosanna filio David ! benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini ; paulo post ab eisdem humiliatus fuit, dicentibus, Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum. Et conturbatus, non inordinata passione, sed vehementi affectu impletus, mortem naturaliter metuendo, seu peccatoribus condolendo. Unde legitur : Jesus infremuit spiritu, et turbavit se ipsum.
paras.en: [[87:16|and being exalted have been humbled|Exaltatus autem, humiliatus sum]]. For, as the Evangelist affirms, when the Jews wished to make Christ king, he fled and withdrew from the crowd; and when he was praised by the people crying out together: [[Mark 7:37|He hath done all things well. He hath made both the deaf to hear and the dumb to speak|Omnia bene fecit, et surdos fecit audire, et mutos loqui]]; and again: [[Matt 9:33|Never was the like seen in Israel|Nunquam sic apparuit in Israel]]: he attributed nothing to himself, but referred all to the glory of the Father. And when he had been exalted by the Jews on Palm Sunday, as they cried: [[Matt 21:9|Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord|Hosanna filio David ! benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini]]; a little after he was humbled by the same men, as they said: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]. [[87:16|and troubled|Et conturbatus]]: not by an inordinate passion, but filled with a vehement affection, fearing death by nature, or grieving with sinners. Hence it is read: Jesus [[John 11:33|groaned in the spirit and troubled himself|infremuit spiritu, et turbavit se ipsum]].

paras.t: In me transierunt iræ tuæ, id est, vindictæ tuæ justitiæ, mihi inflictæ sunt pro peccatis hominum quæ super me cepi, et pro quibus debitas pœnas exsolvi : sicut scriptum est, Spiritus oris nostri Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris; et terrores tui, id est terribiles pœnæ quas me pati voluisti, conturbaverunt me, id est, vehementer animam meam affecerunt, ita ut dicerem : Nunc anima mea turbata est. Propter quod scribitur : Cœpit Jesus pavere et tædere.
paras.en: [[87:17|Thy wrath hath come upon me|In me transierunt iræ tuæ]] [Denis has the plural, "thy wraths have passed over me"], that is, the punishments of thy justice have been inflicted on me for the sins of men which I took upon myself, and for which I paid the due penalties: as it is written: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins|Spiritus oris nostri Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris]]; [[87:17|and thy terrors|et terrores tui]], that is, the terrible pains which thou didst will me to suffer, [[87:17|have troubled me|conturbaverunt me]], that is, have vehemently affected my soul, so that I said: [[John 12:27|Now is my soul troubled|Nunc anima mea turbata est]]. On account of which it is written: Jesus [[Mark 14:33|began to fear and to be heavy|Cœpit Jesus pavere et tædere]].

paras.t: Circumdederunt me iræ et pœnæ prædictæ, seu persecutores Judæi, sicut aqua, id est abundanter et copiose, tota die Parasceves ; circumdederunt me simul, in tantum ut a planta pedis usque ad verticem capitis, non esset in me sanitas. Unde in figura Christi sanctus Job ait : Collegit furorem suum in me, et comminans mihi, infremuit dentibus suis. Concidit me vulnere super vulnus ; irruit in me quasi gigas.
paras.en: [[87:18|They have come round about me|Circumdederunt me]], these wraths and pains spoken of, or the Jews my persecutors, [[87:18|like water|sicut aqua]], that is, abundantly and plentifully, [[87:18|all the day|tota die]] of the Parasceve; [[87:18|they have compassed me about together|circumdederunt me simul]], so much so that [[Is 1:6|From the sole of the foot unto the top of the head|a planta pedis usque ad verticem capitis]] there was no soundness in me. Hence holy Job, in the figure of Christ, says: [[Job 16:10|He hath gathered together his fury against me, and threatening me he hath gnashed with his teeth upon me|Collegit furorem suum in me, et comminans mihi, infremuit dentibus suis]]. [[Job 16:15|He hath torn me with wound upon wound, he hath rushed in upon me like a giant.|Concidit me vulnere super vulnus ; irruit in me quasi gigas]]

paras.t: Elongasti a me amicum et proximum, id est, discipulos meos, qui erant mei amici et proximi, a me discedere permisisti, et notos meos elongasti a miseria mea, ita quod mihi non compatiebantur : eo modo quo dictum est supra, Et sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit : quod non de discipulis, sed de ingratis Judæis Dominus ait. De quibus alibi loquitur : Recesserunt a me ; et ego erudivi eos, et in me cogitaverunt malitiam. Translatio Hieronymi sic habet : Et notos meos abstulisti, ita videlicet, quod mihi non possunt auxilium ferre: quemadmodum scriptum est, Circumspexi, et non erat auxiliator; Job quoque, Noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me. Et hoc est quod Christus dixit discipulis : Venit hora, et jam venit, ut dispergamini unusquisque in propria, et me solum relinquatis.
paras.en: [[87:19|Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me|Elongasti a me amicum et proximum]], that is, thou hast permitted my disciples, who were my friends and neighbours, to depart from me; [[87:19|and my acquaintance|et notos meos]] thou hast put far from my misery [Denis takes *a miseria* as "from my misery"; the Douay-Rheims renders it "because of misery"], so that they did not suffer with me: in the way in which it was said above: [[Ps 68:21|And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, but there was none|Et sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit]]: which the Lord says not of the disciples but of the ungrateful Jews. Of whom he speaks elsewhere: [[Osee 7:14|they are departed from me|Recesserunt a me]]; [[Osee 7:15|And I have chastised them|et ego erudivi eos]], [[Osee 7:15|and they have imagined evil against me|et in me cogitaverunt malitiam]]. Jerome's translation has: And my acquaintance thou hast taken away [Jerome's version of the Psalms from the Hebrew]; that is to say, so that they cannot bring me help: as it is written: [[Is 63:5|I looked about, and there was none to help|Circumspexi, et non erat auxiliator]]; and Job also: [[Job 19:13|my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me|Noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me]]. And this is what Christ said to the disciples: [[John 16:32|the hour cometh, and it is now come, that you shall be scattered every man to his own and shall leave me alone|Venit hora, et jam venit, ut dispergamini unusquisque in propria, et me solum relinquatis]].

87.title: DECLARATIO MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI OCTOGESIMI SEPTIMI.
87.title_en: Moral declaration of the same eighty-seventh psalm.

paras.t: Quum dicat Apostolus, Semper mortificationem Jesu in corpore nostro circumferentes, ut et vita Jesu manifestetur in carne nostra mortali, debemus Caput nostrum in passionibus ejus sectari, quatenus conglorificemur eidem. Unde dicit Apostolus : Fidelis sermo : Si commortui sumus, et convivemus ; si sustinemus, et conregnabimus. Hinc igitur mirum non est, si psalmi qui de Christi passione ad litteram loquuntur, de membris ipsius spiritualiter explanentur.
paras.en: Since the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 4:10|Always bearing about in our body the mortification of Jesus|Semper mortificationem Jesu in corpore nostro circumferentes]], [[2 Cor 4:11|that the life also of Jesus may be made manifest in our mortal flesh|ut et vita Jesu manifestetur in carne nostra mortali]], we ought to follow our Head in his sufferings, that we may be glorified together with him. Hence the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:11|A faithful saying|Fidelis sermo]]: [[2 Tim 2:11|if we be dead with him, we shall live also with him|Si commortui sumus, et convivemus]]; [[2 Tim 2:12|If we suffer, we shall also reign with him|si sustinemus, et conregnabimus]]. It is no wonder, then, if the psalms that speak literally of Christ's passion are explained spiritually of his members.

paras.t: Ecclesia ergo seu quilibet Christianus tribulationes expertus, variisque adversitatibus et tentationibus circumvallatus, proclamet hunc psalmum, dicendo : Domine, omnium gubernator, Deus salutis meæ, id est fons, origo et causa totius beatitudinis meæ, a quo tota salus mea dependet, sine cujus misericordia incessabiliter pereo, graviter pecco, in æternum condemnor ; Deus salutis meæ, in via per fidem et gratiam ; Deus quoque salutis meæ, in patria per speciem et gloriæ lumen ; in die clamavi et nocte, id est certis et congruis horis diei ac noctis, coram te omnia conspiciente. Oportet enim sine intermissione orare.
paras.en: Let the Church, then, or any Christian who has known tribulations and is hemmed in by various adversities and temptations, cry out this psalm, saying: [[87:2|O Lord|Domine]], governor of all, [[87:2|the God of my salvation|Deus salutis meæ]], that is, the fount, origin and cause of all my happiness, on whom all my salvation depends, without whose mercy I perish unceasingly, sin grievously and am condemned for ever; [[87:2|the God of my salvation|Deus salutis meæ]] on the way, through faith and grace; [[87:2|the God of my salvation|Deus salutis meæ]] also in the fatherland, through sight and the light of glory [*in via* and *in patria*, "on the way" and "in the fatherland": the theologians' terms for this life and for heaven]; [[87:2|I have cried in the day, and in the night|in die clamavi et nocte]], that is, at fixed and fitting hours of the day and of the night, [[87:2|before thee|coram te]], who seest all things. For we must pray [[1 Thess 5:17|without ceasing|sine intermissione]].

paras.t: Quia repleta est malis pœnæ et culpæ anima mea, videlicet multis afflictionibus, variis vitiis, passionibusque diversis, quæ sunt vulnera animæ. Unde in Ecclesiaste habetur : Cuncti dies hominis doloribus et ærumnis pleni sunt, nec per noctem mente requiescit. Hoc de malis pœnalibus. De malis vero culpæ alibi scriptum est : In multis offendimus omnes. Et vita mea inferno appropinquavit. Anima namque peccando tendit ad inferos ; et quoties peccat, toties inferno propinquior fit. Peccatum vero mortale, est porta inferni ; veniale autem peccatum, est quoddam præambulum et dispositio quædam ad peccatum mortale et pœnam gehennæ. Qui autem mortaliter peccat, statim meretur damnari, quamvis Deus misericorditer præstoletur, sicut Petrus dicit : Patienter agit Dominus propter vos, nolens aliquos perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti.
paras.en: [[87:4|For my soul is filled with evils|Quia repleta est malis]] of punishment and of guilt, that is, with many afflictions, various vices and divers passions, which are the wounds of the soul. Hence it is said in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 2:23|All his days are full of sorrows and miseries, even in the night he doth not rest in mind|Cuncti dies hominis doloribus et ærumnis pleni sunt, nec per noctem mente requiescit]] [the margin gives Eccle. v, 23; the words are Eccles 2:23, where Denis has "all the days of man" for "all his days"]. This is said of the evils of punishment. Of the evils of guilt it is written elsewhere: [[Jas 3:2|in many things we all offend|In multis offendimus omnes]]. [[87:4|and my life hath drawn nigh to hell|Et vita mea inferno appropinquavit]]. For the soul by sinning tends toward hell, and as often as it sins, so often does it come nearer to hell. Mortal sin is the gate of hell; venial sin is a kind of preamble and a certain disposition to mortal sin and to the pain of gehenna. Whoever sins mortally deserves at once to be damned, although God mercifully waits, as Peter says: The Lord [[2 Pet 3:9|dealeth patiently for your sake, not willing that any should perish, but that all should return to penance|Patienter agit Dominus propter vos, nolens aliquos perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti]].

paras.t: Æstimatus sum cum descendentibus in lacum. Hoc omnibus sanctis martyribus convenit, quos tyranni et infideles tanquam sacrilegos occiderunt, in tantum ut arbitrarentur obsequium se præstare Deo, illos occidendo. Justi quoque qui in justitia moriuntur, et a perversis injusti reputantur, æstimantur cum descendentibus in lacum. Factus sum sicut homo sine adjutorio. Hoc convenit his, quibus in Evangelio ait Salvator : Odio eritis omnibus hominibus propter me.
paras.en: [[87:5|I am counted among them that go down to the pit|Æstimatus sum cum descendentibus in lacum]]. This befits all the holy martyrs, whom tyrants and unbelievers slew as sacrilegious men, so much so that they thought they were doing [[John 16:2|a service to God|obsequium se præstare Deo]] by killing them. The just also, who die in justice and are reckoned unjust by the wicked, are counted among those who go down to the pit. [[87:5|I am become as a man without help|Factus sum sicut homo sine adjutorio]]. This befits those to whom the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:17|you shall be hated by all men|Odio eritis omnibus hominibus]] for my sake.

paras.t: Inter mortuos liber. Solus populus christianus inter ceteros homines veraciter liber est. Nam Christi servitus, summa libertas est ; reliqui vero universi, servi sunt iniquitatis ac dæmonis. Unde ait Apostolus : Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum, in quo clamamus, Abba (Pater). Et ad Galatas : Non sumus filii ancillæ, sed liberæ : qua libertate Christus nos liberavit. Sic ergo ab infidelibus et servis peccati, qui spiritualiter mortui sunt, reputatur populus christianus, seu quicumque fidelis ac justus. Reputatur etiam, sicut vulnerati dormientes in sepulcris, etc.
paras.en: [[87:6|Free among the dead|Inter mortuos liber]]. The Christian people alone, among all other men, is truly free. For the service of Christ is the highest freedom, while all the rest are slaves of iniquity and of the devil. Hence the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:15|you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear: but you have received the spirit of adoption of sons, whereby we cry: Abba (Father)|Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum, in quo clamamus, Abba (Pater)]]. And to the Galatians: [[Gal 4:31|we are not the children of the bondwoman but of the free: by the freedom wherewith Christ has made us free|Non sumus filii ancillæ, sed liberæ : qua libertate Christus nos liberavit]]. So, then, is the Christian people, or anyone faithful and just, looked upon by unbelievers and the slaves of sin, who are spiritually dead. He is reckoned also [[87:6|Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres|sicut vulnerati dormientes in sepulcris]], etc.

paras.t: Super me confirmatus est furor tuus, id est rigorosus effectus justitiæ tuæ. Nam quid intelligendum sit per furorem Dei, subjungitur : Et omnes fluctus tuos, id est omnia genera tribulationum sive pœnarum, quæ pro peccatis infliguntur, induxisti super me. Hoc Ecclesiæ Christi atque fidelibus convenit, quoniam Deus in hac vita justos multipliciter et districte castigat, quemadmodum in libro Sapientiæ scriptum est : Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos. Et Judith : Omnes, inquit, qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles. Et Christus discipulis ait : In mundo pressuram habebitis ; sed confidite, ego vici mundum. Hæc autem Deus fecit electis, ut venialia eorum expurgentur, et ipsi ad gratiam ampliorem in præsenti disponantur, aliis quoque in exemplum proponantur, et in futuro gloriam ampliorem consequantur. Hunc furorem super se confirmatum expertus erat Job, qui dixit : Iratus est contra me furor ejus, et sic me habuit quasi hostem suum ; Jeremias etiam, qui profitetur : A facie manus tuæ solus sedebam, quoniam comminatione replesti me.
paras.en: [[87:8|Thy wrath is strong over me|Super me confirmatus est furor tuus]], that is, the rigorous effect of thy justice. For what is to be understood by the wrath of God is added: [[87:8|and all thy waves|Et omnes fluctus tuos]], that is, all kinds of tribulations or punishments that are inflicted for sins, [[87:8|thou hast brought in upon me|induxisti super me]]. This befits the Church of Christ and the faithful, since God in this life chastises the just in many ways and strictly, as it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace|Tanquam aurum in fornace]] the Lord hath proved his elect, [[Wis 3:6|and as a victim of a holocaust, he hath received them|et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos]]. And Judith: [[Jdt 8:23|All|Omnes]], she says, [[Jdt 8:23|that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]]. And Christ says to his disciples: [[John 16:33|In the world you shall have distress. But have confidence. I have overcome the world|In mundo pressuram habebitis ; sed confidite, ego vici mundum]]. These things God has done to his elect, that their venial sins may be purged away, that they themselves may be disposed in this present life for greater grace, that they may be set before others as an example, and that in the life to come they may obtain greater glory. This wrath made strong over him Job had known, who said: [[Job 19:11|His wrath is kindled against me, and he hath counted me as his enemy|Iratus est contra me furor ejus, et sic me habuit quasi hostem suum]]; and Jeremias too, who declares: From [[Jer 15:17|the presence of thy hand|A facie manus tuæ]] [[Jer 15:17|I sat alone, because thou hast filled me with threats|solus sedebam, quoniam comminatione replesti me]] [Denis joins "the presence of thy hand" to "I sat alone"; in the Vulgate it goes with the words before: "I gloried in the presence of thy hand"].

paras.t: Longe fecisti notos meos a me ; posuerunt me abominationem sibi. Hoc est quod Christus in Evangelio suis electis locutus est : Trademini a parentibus et fratribus et amicis et propinquis. Denique Christus venit separare patrem a filiis, fratrem a sororibus, consulendo nobis ut relinquamus omnes propinquos, uxorem atque divitias. Sæpe etiam contigit ut noti a Christianis aufugerent, eosque abominarentur propter vehementissimas persecutiones, adversitates et pœnas sibi illatas, sicut et sanctus Job sibi accidisse fatetur.
paras.en: [[87:9|Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: they have set me an abomination to themselves|Longe fecisti notos meos a me ; posuerunt me abominationem sibi]]. This is what Christ spoke in the Gospel to his elect: [[Luke 21:16|you shall be betrayed by your parents and brethren and kinsmen and friends|Trademini a parentibus et fratribus et amicis et propinquis]]. Indeed, Christ came to part the father from his sons and the brother from his sisters[[Matt 10:35||]], counselling us to leave all our kinsfolk, wife and riches[[Matt 19:29||]]. It has often happened, too, that their acquaintance fled from Christians and held them in abomination because of the most violent persecutions, adversities and punishments brought upon them, as holy Job too confesses happened to him[[Job 19:13||]][[Job 19:19||]] [the margin gives Job xix, 13–17, 19].

paras.t: Traditus sum, vel dæmoni ad tentandum, vel tyranno ad occidendum, vel homini pravo ad persequendum ; et non egrediebar, id est, has pœnas non fugi, sed omnia æquanimiter passus sum, sciens quoniam copiosa est merces mea in cœlo.
paras.en: [[87:9|I was delivered up|Traditus sum]], either to the devil to be tempted, or to the tyrant to be slain, or to a wicked man to be persecuted; [[87:9|and came not forth|et non egrediebar]], that is, I did not flee these punishments but suffered them all with an even mind, knowing that my reward is plentiful in heaven[[Matt 5:12||]].

paras.t: Oculi mei corporales languerunt præ inopia naturalis virtutis, eo quod interior dolor in oculis corporis magis redundat. Unde a beato Job dicitur : Facies mea intumuit a fletu, et oculi mei caligaverunt. Vel, Oculi mei interiores et intellectuales, languerunt præ inopia divinæ illuminationis, et præ abundantia propriæ cæcitatis. Tota die, id est horis competentibus totius diei, expandi ad te, Domine, manus meas, id est desideria mea, seu opera aut manus corporeas : sicut scribitur in Threnis, Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cœlos. Et Apostolus ait : Volo viros orare in omni loco, levantes puras manus sine ira et disceptatione. Plurimum quidem confert ad excitandum mentis fervorem ac devotionem internam, manus corporis in altum erigere, quatenus spiritus dirigatur ad proprium Creatorem, in cœlestibus demorantem.
paras.en: [[87:10|My eyes|Oculi mei]] of the body [[87:10|languished through poverty|languerunt præ inopia]] of natural strength, because inward grief overflows the more into the eyes of the body. Hence it is said by blessed Job: [[Job 16:17|My face is swollen with weeping|Facies mea intumuit a fletu]], and my eyes are dim [the Vulgate has *palpebræ*, "eyelids", where Denis has *oculi*, "eyes"]. Or: [[87:10|My eyes|Oculi mei]], the inward eyes of the understanding, [[87:10|languished through poverty|languerunt præ inopia]] of divine enlightenment, and through the abundance of their own blindness. [[87:10|All the day|Tota die]], that is, at the fitting hours of the whole day, [[87:10|I stretched out my hands to thee|expandi ad te, Domine, manus meas]], O Lord, that is, my desires, or my works, or my bodily hands: as it is written in Lamentations: [[Lam 3:41|Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord in the heavens|Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cœlos]]. And the Apostle says: I will [[1 Tim 2:8|that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands, without anger and contention|viros orare in omni loco, levantes puras manus sine ira et disceptatione]]. Indeed it helps very much to rouse fervour of mind and inward devotion to raise the hands of the body on high, so that the spirit may be directed to its own Creator, who dwells in the heavens.

paras.t: Numquid mortuis facies mirabilia ? etc. Hunc versum cum duobus sequentibus dicere potest Ecclesia seu quicumque fidelis, ad ostendendum quam rationabile sit exaudiri a Domino, sicut in præcedenti expositione a Christo inducti sunt : sensus enim est idem.
paras.en: [[87:11|Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead?|Numquid mortuis facies mirabilia ?]] etc. This verse with the two that follow may be said by the Church or by any of the faithful, to show how reasonable it is to be heard by the Lord, just as in the preceding exposition they were put in the mouth of Christ: for the sense is the same.

paras.t: Et mane, id est in principio infusionis gratiæ tuæ ; vel, Mane, id est in principio lucis solaris ; oratio mea, tibi porrigenda, præveniet te, id est, tibi offeretur antequam alia operer : juxta illud, Quærite primum regnum Dei et justitiam ejus. Vel, Præveniet te, id est tuum judicium, ita quod nunc, quando est tempus acceptabile et dies salutis, conabor te mitigare et tibi placere.
paras.en: [[87:14|and in the morning|Et mane]], that is, at the beginning of the infusion of thy grace; or, [[87:14|in the morning|Mane]], that is, at the beginning of the sun's light, [[87:14|my prayer|oratio mea]], which is to be offered to thee, [[87:14|shall prevent thee|præveniet te]], that is, shall be offered to thee before I do any other work [to *prevent* is, in the old sense, to go before]: according to that saying: Seek ye [[Matt 6:33|first the kingdom of God, and his justice|primum regnum Dei et justitiam ejus]]. Or, [[87:14|shall prevent thee|Præveniet te]], that is, shall go before thy judgement: so that now, while it is [[2 Cor 6:2|the acceptable time|tempus acceptabile]] and the day of salvation, I shall strive to appease thee and to please thee.

paras.t: Ut quid, Domine, repellis orationem meam, non statim eam exaudiendo, seu diutius differendo ? Videtur namque devoto, quod oratio sua repellitur, dum pro suo voto non exauditur. Propter quod Job dixit : Ecce clamabo vim patiens, et nemo exaudiet ; vociferabar, et non est qui judicet. Et Habacuc : Usquequo, Domine, clamabo, et non exaudies ? Interdum quoque oratio omnino repellitur, quia non in nomine Jesu fit, scilicet quum id non postulatur, quod expedit ad salutem. Nam et Paulus ter deprecatus est Dominum, et exauditus non fuit. Quandoque etiam oratio in nomine Jesu oblata, ad tempus repellitur seu differtur, quatenus devotius continuetur, et res optata ardentius appetatur, sicque copiosius obtineatur. Certissime tamen tenere debemus, quod oratio in nomine Jesu formata, si continuetur, et pro ipso orante fiat, semper acceptatur.
paras.en: [[87:15|Lord, why castest thou off my prayer|Ut quid, Domine, repellis orationem meam]], not hearing it at once, or putting it off for a long while? For it seems to the devout man that his prayer is cast off when he is not heard as he wishes. For which reason Job said: [[Job 19:7|Behold I shall cry suffering violence, and no one will hear: I shall cry aloud, and there is none to judge|Ecce clamabo vim patiens, et nemo exaudiet ; vociferabar, et non est qui judicet]]. And Habacuc: [[Hab 1:2|How long, O Lord, shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear?|Usquequo, Domine, clamabo, et non exaudies]] Sometimes, too, a prayer is cast off altogether because it is not made in the name of Jesus: that is, when what is asked is not what is expedient for salvation. For Paul too thrice besought the Lord[[2 Cor 12:8||]], and was not heard[[2 Cor 12:9||]]. Sometimes, again, a prayer offered in the name of Jesus is cast off or put off for a time, so that it may be kept up more devoutly, and the thing desired be sought more ardently, and so be obtained more abundantly. Yet we must hold most certainly that a prayer framed in the name of Jesus, if it is persevered in and is made for the one who prays, is always accepted.

paras.t: Avertis faciem tuam a me, gratiam suspendendo, meque tribulationibus exponendo, nec statim consolando. Ista aversio non est aversio simpliciter dicta, sed similis est aversioni qua mater a parvulo filio suo faciem suam abscondit, tanquam offensa esset, quatenus filius eam cum lacrimis repetat, affectuosiusque adspiciat.
paras.en: [[87:15|turnest thou away thy face from me|Avertis faciem tuam a me]], withholding grace, exposing me to tribulations, and not consoling me at once. This turning away is not a turning away in the plain sense of the word, but is like the turning away by which a mother hides her face from her little son as though she were offended, so that the son may seek her again with tears and look upon her more lovingly.

paras.t: Pauper sum ego, vel rebus sæculi, vel merito et gratia, vel affectu, omnia terrena arbitrando ut stercora ; et in laboribus a juventute mea, id est a principio quo cœperunt esse electi in mundo. Multi namque sunt labores sanctorum, videlicet exercitia pœnitentiæ, vigiliæ, abstinentiæ, orationes, opera exteriora, afflictiones et pœnæ. Propter quod ait Job : Homo nascitur ad laborem, et avis ad volatum. Ideoque de reprobis dictum est supra : In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur. Et secundum Apostolum, Nullus coronatur nisi qui legitime certaverit : quod sine magno labore fieri nequit.
paras.en: [[87:16|I am poor|Pauper sum ego]], either in the goods of this world, or in merit and grace, or in affection, counting all earthly things [[Phil 3:8|as dung|ut stercora]]; [[87:16|and in labours from my youth|et in laboribus a juventute mea]], that is, from the time when the elect began to be in the world. For many are the labours of the saints: the exercises of penance, watchings, fastings, prayers, outward works, afflictions and punishments. For which reason Job says: [[Job 5:7|Man is born to labour, and the bird to fly.|Homo nascitur ad laborem, et avis ad volatum]] And so it was said above of the reprobate: [[Ps 72:5|They are not in the labour of men: neither shall they be scourged like other men|In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur]]. And according to the Apostle, a man [[2 Tim 2:5|is not crowned, except he strive lawfully|Nullus coronatur nisi qui legitime certaverit]]: and this cannot be done without great labour.

paras.t: Exaltatus autem, humiliatus sum. Nam dum boni laudantur et sublimantur ab aliis, in propriis cordibus coram Deo humiliantur : quia non sibi, sed Domino omnia bona attribuunt : et hoc est signum boni virtuosique viri. Propter quod Salomon ait : Quomodo probatur in conflatorio argentum, et in fornace aurum, sic probatur homo ore laudantis.
