Vel : Exaltatus per prospera, humiliatus sum protinus per adversa : quia non permanet homo diu in eodem statu, sed nunc prospera, nunc adversa ei contingunt. Idcirco in Ecclesiastico scribitur : In die bonorum ne immemor sis malorum, et in die malorum ne immemor sis bonorum. Vel : Exaltatus superbe et inobedienter vivendo, humiliatus sum veraciter confitendo, et conturbatus propter enormitatem peccatorum meorum, seu asperitatem pœnarum et persecutionum.
paras.en: [[87:16|and being exalted have been humbled|Exaltatus autem, humiliatus sum]]. For when good men are praised and raised up by others, they are humbled in their own hearts before God, because they ascribe all good things not to themselves but to the Lord: and this is the mark of a good and virtuous man. For which reason Solomon says: [[Prov 27:21|As silver is tried in the fining-pot, and gold in the furnace: so a man is tried by the mouth of him that praiseth|Quomodo probatur in conflatorio argentum, et in fornace aurum, sic probatur homo ore laudantis]]. Or: [[87:16|being exalted|Exaltatus]] by prosperity, I [[87:16|have been humbled|humiliatus sum]] straightway by adversity: because man does not long remain in the same state[[Job 14:2||]], but now prosperity, now adversity befalls him. Therefore it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 11:27|In the day of good things be not unmindful of evils: and in the day of evils be not unmindful of good things|In die bonorum ne immemor sis malorum, et in die malorum ne immemor sis bonorum]]. Or: [[87:16|being exalted|Exaltatus]] by living proudly and disobediently, I [[87:16|have been humbled|humiliatus sum]] by truly confessing, [[87:16|and troubled|et conturbatus]] because of the enormity of my sins, or the harshness of punishments and persecutions.

paras.t: In me transierunt iræ tuæ, id est, effectus tuæ justitiæ seu cogitationes pœnosæ mihi inflictæ sunt : sicut in libro Job habetur : Sagittæ Domini in me sunt, quarum indignatio ebibit spiritum meum, et terrores Domini militant contra me. Ideo subditur : et terrores tui conturbaverunt me, id est, formidines de effectibus tuæ justitiæ, scilicet de futuro judicio, de pœnis inferni, de expulsione a gloria conceptæ, sollicitum me fecerunt, pœnitentem et anxium : juxta illud, A facie Dei turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor.
paras.en: [[87:17|Thy wrath hath come upon me|In me transierunt iræ tuæ]], that is, the effects of thy justice, or painful thoughts, have been inflicted on me [the Latin has "thy wraths have passed into me"]: as is found in the book of Job: [[Job 6:4|the arrows of the Lord are in me, the rage whereof drinketh up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord war against me|Sagittæ Domini in me sunt, quarum indignatio ebibit spiritum meum, et terrores Domini militant contra me]]. Therefore it is added: [[87:17|and thy terrors have troubled me|et terrores tui conturbaverunt me]], that is, the fears conceived of the effects of thy justice, namely of the judgement to come, of the pains of hell, of being shut out from glory, have made me solicitous, penitent and anxious: according to that saying: [[Job 23:15|I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him, I am made pensive with fear|A facie Dei turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor]] [Denis has "at the presence of God" for "at his presence"].

paras.t: Circumdederunt me afflictiones prædictæ, sicut aqua tota die, imo toto tempore vitæ meæ : quia militia est vita hominis super terram. Et secundum Augustinum, […] perseverandum est usque in finem, quia tentatio perseverat usque in finem. Circumdederunt me simul. Multoties namque electi simul et semel a mundo, carne atque diabolo impetuntur ac fatigantur. Cetera ex dictis in præcedenti expositione elucescunt.
paras.en: [[87:18|They have come round about me|Circumdederunt me]], namely the afflictions spoken of, [[87:18|like water all the day|sicut aqua tota die]], nay, the whole time of my life: because [[Job 7:1|The life of man upon earth is a warfare|militia est vita hominis super terram]]. And according to Augustine, […] we must persevere unto the end, because temptation perseveres unto the end. [[87:18|they have compassed me about together|Circumdederunt me simul]]. For many times the elect are assailed and wearied by the world, the flesh and the devil all at once. The rest is clear from what was said in the preceding exposition.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum mysterialem, doctrinalem, et vere devotum audivimus : in quo decet nos Christi passionem intente recolere, eique intime condolere, et ejus vestigia digne sectari, quatenus illud beati Apostoli dicere singuli valeamus : De cetero nemo mihi molestus sit ; ego enim stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto. Illud quoque Sponsæ : Fasciculus myrrhæ dilectus meus mihi, inter ubera mea commorabitur. Et hanc arbitremur summam esse nostram felicitatem dispositive, et in præsenti perfectionem et gratiam, Christi passionibus conformari, ejus abjectiones imitari, ejusque caritati utcumque assimilari. Propterea enim hortatur Apostolus : Estote imitatores Dei sicut filii carissimi ; et ambulate in dilectione, sicut et Christus dilexit nos. Et altissimus ille apostolici ordinis vertex, Communicantes, inquit, Christi passionibus gaudete, ut et in revelatione gloriæ ejus gaudeatis ; rursusque, Si exprobramini, inquit, in nomine Christi, beati eritis. Quid enim gloriosius Christiano, quam esse consimilem Christo ?
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of mystery and of doctrine, and truly devout: in which it befits us to recall Christ's passion attentively, to suffer with him inwardly, and to follow worthily in his footsteps, so that each of us may be able to say that word of the blessed Apostle: [[Gal 6:17|From henceforth let no man be troublesome to me: for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body|De cetero nemo mihi molestus sit ; ego enim stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto]]. And that of the Bride also: [[Cant 1:12|A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall abide between my breasts.|Fasciculus myrrhæ dilectus meus mihi, inter ubera mea commorabitur]] And let us deem this to be our highest happiness by way of disposition [that is, as what disposes us for the happiness to come], and in this present life our perfection and grace: to be conformed to the sufferings of Christ, to imitate his abasements, and to be made like in some measure to his charity. For this is why the Apostle exhorts us: Be ye [[Eph 5:1|followers of God, as most dear children|imitatores Dei sicut filii carissimi]]; [[Eph 5:2|And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us|et ambulate in dilectione, sicut et Christus dilexit nos]]. And that highest summit of the apostolic order [that is, Peter, the head of the Apostles]: [[1 Pet 4:13|if you partake|Communicantes]], he says, [[1 Pet 4:13|of the sufferings of Christ, rejoice that, when his glory shall be revealed, you may also be glad|Christi passionibus gaudete, ut et in revelatione gloriæ ejus gaudeatis]]; and again: [[1 Pet 4:14|If you be reproached|Si exprobramini]], he says, [[1 Pet 4:14|for the name of Christ, you shall be blessed|in nomine Christi, beati eritis]]. For what is more glorious for a Christian than to be made wholly like to Christ?

paras.t: Precatio. Domine, Deus salutis nostræ, nostri pie miserere ; et repletam malis animam nostram, et inferno peccatis appropinquantem vitam nostram, abundantia tuæ propitiationis revoca, et ab omni miseria nunc et semper nos elonga : ut misericordiæ tuæ prærogativa, laudum tibi præconia persolvamus in sæcula.
paras.en: Prayer. [[87:2|O Lord|Domine]], God of our salvation, have loving mercy on us; and by the abundance of thy forgiveness call back our soul [[87:4|filled with evils|repletam malis]], and our life drawing nigh to hell through sins; and remove us far from all misery, now and for ever: that, by the special gift of thy mercy, we may render thee the songs of praise for ever.

88.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI OCTAVI : MISERICORDIAS DOMINI.
88.title_en: Explanation of the eighty-eighth psalm: The mercies of the Lord.

paras.t: Declarandi nunc psalmi titulus est: Intellectus Ethan Israelitæ: id est, in psalmo præsenti continetur, quid homo robustus per gratiam, Deumque contemplans per fidem, de Christo intelligere debet. Ethan namque interpretatur robustus.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is: [[88:1|Of understanding, for Ethan|Intellectus Ethan]] the Israelite [the margin gives the reading *Ezrahitæ*, "the Ezrahite", as in the Vulgate]: that is, the present psalm contains what a man strong through grace, and contemplating God through faith, ought to understand of Christ. For *Ethan* is interpreted "strong".

paras.t: Secundum omnes autem expositores, psalmus hic tractat de stabilitate perpetuitateque regni David: quæ in nullo completa est, nisi in Christo. Propterea psalmus iste ad litteram de Christo pertractat: et quoniam stabilitio ista per gratiam Dei efficitur, ideo sanctus Propheta a fonte omnium gratiarum, videlicet a divina misericordia, orsus est: Misericordias, inquiens, Domini in æternum cantabo. Dulcissimum plane exordium, et omni mundana, carnali et vana voluptate vehementer suavius. Non ait, Misericordiam Domini, sed, Misericordias: quoniam secundum multitudinem miseriarum nostrarum, multiplicatæ sunt super nos misericordiæ Domini. Misericordia autem Dei interdum vocatur ipsa pietas divinæ naturæ, quæ naturaliter clemens est: et ista misericordia non est nisi una, sicut divina essentia. Quandoque vero misericordia Dei nominatur effectus pietatis divinæ, sicut Raphael ait: Benedicite Deum cœli, quia fecit vobiscum misericordiam suam. Et utroque modo accipi potest hoc loco misericordia Domini; sed si primo modo accipiatur, tunc una ac simplex misericordia Dei pluraliter explicatur, propter multiplices suos effectus. Deus enim mille modis novit suis misericorditer auxiliari. Eritque sensus: Misericordias Domini, id est ipsum Deum naturaliter misericordem, seu pietatem divinam multipliciter miserentem, in æternum cantabo, id est, indesinenter laudabo, nunc inchoative, et in futuro completive. Quemadmodum namque, secundum Apostolum, Caritas nunquam excidit, quia nunc incipit et in futuro perficitur; sic actus caritatis, qui sunt, Deum diligere, contemplari, admirari, laudare, ipso frui, in ipso lætari, nunquam deficiunt, sed in præsenti habent exordium, et in patria complementum. Propter quod de Maria Magdalene, his occupata, dixit Salvator: Maria optimam partem elegit, quæ non auferetur ab ea.
paras.en: Now according to all the expositors, this psalm treats of the stability and perpetuity of the kingdom of David, which was fulfilled in no one but in Christ. Therefore this psalm treats literally of Christ; and since that establishment is brought about through the grace of God, the holy Prophet has begun from the fountain of all graces, namely from the divine mercy, saying: [[88:2|The mercies|Misericordias]], [[88:2|of the Lord I will sing for ever|Domini in æternum cantabo]]. A most sweet beginning indeed, and far more delightful than every worldly, carnal and vain pleasure. He does not say, "The mercy of the Lord", but "The mercies": because according to the multitude of our miseries, the mercies of the Lord have been multiplied upon us. Now the mercy of God is sometimes the name given to the very lovingkindness of the divine nature, which is by nature clement; and this mercy is but one, as the divine essence is. But sometimes the mercy of God is the name given to an effect of the divine lovingkindness, as Raphael says: [[Tob 12:6|Bless ye the God of heaven|Benedicite Deum cœli]], [[Tob 12:6|because he hath shewn his mercy to you|quia fecit vobiscum misericordiam suam]]. And the mercy of the Lord can be taken in this place in either way; but if it is taken in the first way, then the one and simple mercy of God is expressed in the plural on account of its manifold effects. For God knows how to help His own mercifully in a thousand ways. And the sense will be: [[88:2|The mercies of the Lord|Misericordias Domini]], that is, God Himself, merciful by nature, or the divine lovingkindness that shows mercy in many ways, [[88:2|I will sing for ever|in æternum cantabo]], that is, I will praise without ceasing, now by way of beginning, and in the future by way of completion. For just as, according to the Apostle, [[1 Cor 13:8|Charity never falleth away|Caritas nunquam excidit]], because it begins now and is perfected in the future, so the acts of charity, which are to love God, to contemplate, to wonder at and praise Him, to enjoy Him and rejoice in Him, never fail, but have their beginning in the present and their completion in the fatherland. Wherefore the Saviour said of Mary Magdalene, when she was taken up with these things: [[Luke 10:42|Mary hath chosen the best part, which shall not be taken away from her|Maria optimam partem elegit, quæ non auferetur ab ea]].

paras.t: Si vero misericordiæ Domini jam dicantur effectus seu opera misericordissimi Creatoris, sensus erit: Misericordias Domini, id est dona gratiæ seu beneficia Dei, et multiplicem suæ bonitatis effectum, tam mihi quam toti generi humano impensum, in æternum cantabo: quemadmodum in Isaia dicitur: Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis, et quæ largitus est nobis secundum indulgentiam suam. Recolat hic unusquisque, ut valet, misericordias Domini, id est beneficia ejus generalia et specialia. Generalia quippe beneficia Dei sunt, creatio, justificatio, et glorificatio; specialia vero beneficia Dei sunt, quæ unicuique singulariter data sunt. Sed utraque vere omnem rationem, linguam numerumque transcendunt. Quis enim omnia beneficia Christi concipiat, eloquatur, aut numeret? Propter nos factus est homo, conversatus in mundo, suspensus in ligno. Nobis dedit se ipsum in Sacramento, promisit pro præmio, in cordibus nostris vult habitare, deliciari, quiescere.
paras.en: But if the mercies of the Lord are here taken to mean the effects or works of the most merciful Creator, the sense will be: [[88:2|The mercies of the Lord|Misericordias Domini]], that is, the gifts of grace or the benefits of God, and the manifold effect of His goodness bestowed both on me and on the whole human race, [[88:2|I will sing for ever|in æternum cantabo]]; as is said in Isaias: [[Is 63:7|I will remember the tender mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all the things that the Lord hath bestowed upon us|Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis]], and [[Is 63:7|which he hath given them according to his kindness|quæ largitus est nobis secundum indulgentiam suam]] [Denis reads *nobis*, "us", where the Vulgate has *eis*, "them"]. Let each one here call to mind, as well as he can, [[88:2|the mercies of the Lord|misericordias Domini]], that is, His benefits, general and special. For the general benefits of God are creation, justification and glorification; the special benefits of God are those given to each one singly. But both kinds truly surpass all reason, tongue and number. For who could conceive, utter or number all the benefits of Christ? For us He was made man, conversed in the world[[Bar 3:38||]], hung upon the tree. To us He gave Himself in the Sacrament, He promised Himself as our reward, He wills to dwell, to take His delight and to rest in our hearts.

paras.t: In generationem et generationem annuntiabo veritatem tuam in ore meo. Propheta auctor psalmi præsentis, sicut prædixit, effecit. Prædixit namque se annuntiaturum Dei veritatem a generatione in generationem, id est a qualibet generatione in quamlibet generationem succedentem, quoniam psalmus ejus usque in finem mundi cantabitur. Solet autem Scriptura per generationem et generationem, designare perpetuam durationem, quemadmodum ait Maria: Et misericordia ejus a progenie in progenies. Quum ergo nos brevi vivamus tempore, et paulo post moriamur, scrutandum est quomodo quilibet nostrum in persona propria hæc dicere queat. Certum est enim, quia in persona Ecclesiæ dici a quolibet possint. Et respondendum, quod quilibet nostrum hæc dicere potest, secundum duplicem sensum. Primo, nam qui bene et exemplariter operatur, imitatores suæ bonæ conversationis relinquit, et ita per suos sequaces veritatem divinam incessanter annuntiat. Secundo exponitur sic: A generatione viæ seu viatorum, in generationem Sanctorum in patria, annuntiabo veritatem tuam: ita quod in generatione sanctorum viatorum hanc annuntiationem incipiam, in generatione vero beatorum comprehensorum eam continuabo atque perficiam. Per veritatem autem Dei, hoc loco accipi potest justitia ejus: quæ ideo annuntiatur ab eo qui misericordiam Domini cantat, quia in omni opere Dei misericordia et justitia commiscentur. Potest quoque per veritatem intelligi promissionum divinarum impletio, qua Deus hominibus per Christum largitus est quod se per illum præstaturum spopondit. Sicque accipitur quum dicitur apud Joannem, Gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est.
paras.en: [[88:2|I will shew forth thy truth with my mouth to generation and generation|In generationem et generationem annuntiabo veritatem tuam in ore meo]]. The Prophet, the author of the present psalm, has done as he foretold. For he foretold that he would shew forth the truth of God from generation to generation, that is, from any generation to any generation that follows it, since his psalm will be sung until the end of the world. Now Scripture is wont to signify perpetual duration by *generation and generation*, as Mary says: [[Luke 1:50|And his mercy is from generation unto generations|Et misericordia ejus a progenie in progenies]]. Since, then, we live for a short time[[Job 14:1||]], and die a little after, it must be asked how any one of us can say these words in his own person. For it is certain that they can be said by anyone in the person of the Church. And the answer is that any one of us can say them in a twofold sense. First, because he who works well and as an example to others leaves behind imitators of his good manner of life, and so through his followers shews forth the divine truth unceasingly. Secondly, it is explained thus: From the generation of the way, or of wayfarers, to the generation of the Saints in the fatherland, [[88:2|I will shew forth thy truth|annuntiabo veritatem tuam]]: so that I shall begin this proclaiming in the generation of the holy wayfarers, and continue and complete it in the generation of the blessed comprehensors [that is, those who already possess God in glory, as opposed to wayfarers still on the road]. Now by the truth of God His justice can be understood in this place: which is shewn forth by him who sings the mercy of the Lord, because in every work of God mercy and justice are mingled. By *truth* can also be understood the fulfilment of the divine promises, by which God has bestowed on men through Christ what He pledged that He would give through Him. And so it is taken when it is said in John: [[John 1:17|grace and truth came by Jesus Christ|Gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est]].

paras.t: Sic ergo Propheta in hoc versu mutans personam, ait ad Dominum: In generationem et generationem annuntiabo veritatem tuam in ore meo, revolvendo stabiliter in ore meo verba divina, et non solum transitorie atque celeriter ea proferendo ex ore.
paras.en: Thus, then, the Prophet, changing the person in this verse, says to the Lord: [[88:2|I will shew forth thy truth with my mouth to generation and generation|In generationem et generationem annuntiabo veritatem tuam in ore meo]], by turning over steadily in my mouth the divine words, and not only uttering them from the mouth in passing and hastily.

paras.t: Propterea autem veritatem tuam annuntiabo, Quoniam dixisti, id est, intra te decrevisti, et multifarie multisque modis locutus es per angelos, per Prophetas, per Filium tuum incarnatum, atque Apostolos, istud scilicet: In æternum misericordia ædificabitur in cœlis: id est, per effectum misericordiæ, ruinæ cœlorum reparabuntur, et muri cœlestis Jerusalem ex vivis lapidibus construentur, dum per Christi incarnationem ac passionem, homines ad sedes apostatarum angelorum transferuntur. Unde superius dictum est, Domine, in cœlo misericordia tua; et, Magnificata est usque ad cœlos misericordia tua. Vel sic: Quoniam dixisti per te ipsum et sanctos Prophetas: In æternum misericordia ædificabitur in cœlis, id est in Apostolis seu per Apostolos, quia per eos fabricata est Ecclesia catholica, operante per eos misericordia tua. Dicitur namque misericordia Dei in æternum ædificari, dum ejus effectus æternaliter perseverat. Ecclesia vero per misericordiam Dei constructa, usque in finem sæculi permanebit. Præparabitur veritas tua in eis: id est, impletio promissionum tuarum et Prophetarum, per Apostolos disponetur, ut per eos ad homines universos perveniat, quatenus per gratiam illis primo concessam ceteri convertantur: quemadmodum ab Ecclesiastico dictum est, Ut Prophetæ tui fideles inveniantur. Vel sic: Præparabitur veritas tua in eis, id est in cœlestibus civibus seu angelis sanctis: quoniam ipsi primitus de divinis mysteriis illustrantur, et ita per eos veritas divinæ illuminationis ad homines sanctos deducitur. Ecclesiastica namque hierarchia, ab hierarchia angelica purgatur, illuminatur et perficitur.
paras.en: And I will [[88:2|shew forth thy truth|veritatem tuam annuntiabo]] for this reason: [[88:3|For thou hast said|Quoniam dixisti]], that is, Thou hast decreed within Thyself, and hast spoken at sundry times and in divers manners through angels, through the Prophets, through Thy incarnate Son and the Apostles, namely this: [[88:3|Mercy shall be built up for ever in the heavens|In æternum misericordia ædificabitur in cœlis]]: that is, through the effect of mercy the ruins of the heavens shall be repaired, and the walls of the heavenly Jerusalem shall be built of living stones, when through the incarnation and passion of Christ men are brought over to the seats of the apostate angels. Hence it was said above: [[Ps 35:6|O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven|Domine, in cœlo misericordia tua]]; and: [[Ps 56:11|thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens|Magnificata est usque ad cœlos misericordia tua]]. Or thus: For Thou hast said through Thyself and the holy Prophets: [[88:3|Mercy shall be built up for ever in the heavens|In æternum misericordia ædificabitur in cœlis]], that is, in the Apostles or through the Apostles, because through them the Catholic Church was built, Thy mercy working through them. For the mercy of God is said to be built up for ever, since its effect endures eternally; and the Church, built through the mercy of God, will last until the end of the world. [[88:3|Thy truth shall be prepared in them|Præparabitur veritas tua in eis]]: that is, the fulfilment of Thy promises and of the Prophets will be ordered through the Apostles, so that through them it may reach all men, inasmuch as through the grace first granted to them the rest may be converted; as was said by Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 36:18|that thy prophets may be found faithful|Ut Prophetæ tui fideles inveniantur]]. Or thus: [[88:3|Thy truth shall be prepared in them|Præparabitur veritas tua in eis]], that is, in the heavenly citizens or holy angels: because they are first enlightened about the divine mysteries, and so through them the truth of the divine illumination is brought down to holy men. For the ecclesiastical hierarchy is purified, enlightened and perfected by the angelic hierarchy.

paras.t: Dixisti quoque, o Domine: Disposui testamentum electis meis, id est, vetus Testamentum seu legem Mosaicam dedi filiis Israel. Quoniam enim lex disponebat ad Christum, juxta illud Apostoli, Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christo; idcirco data non est nisi populo illi ex quo Christus incarnari elegit, videlicet filiis Israel. Juravi David filio Jesse servo meo: Usque in æternum præparabo semen tuum: id est, propagatio filiorum tuorum, usque ad Christum ex eis nasciturum pertinget, et in ipso Christo perpetuabitur. Hoc in Matthæo verum esse probatur, ubi genealogia David usque ad Christum deducitur. Et ædificabo in generationem et generationem, id est per omnem progeniem firmabo et conservabo, sedem tuam, id est regiam potestatem. Primo libro Paralipomenon et alibi Deus promisit regi David, quod non deficeret vir de semine ejus, sedens in throno ipsius, ita dumtaxat, si custodirent filii ejus præcepta divina; sed quia frequenter illa transgressi sunt, ad idolatriam declinantes, propterea tempore Sedeciæ regnum David interruptionem sustinuit, quemadmodum quarto Regum describitur. Quamvis tamen sedes seu regnum David ad tempus cessaverit, nihilo minus in Christo reparatum est, firmatum ac perpetuatum, prout Archangelus ait ad Virginem: Ecce concipies in utero et paries filium, et vocabis nomen ejus Jesum: hic erit magnus, et Filius Altissimi vocabitur; et dabit illi Dominus Deus sedem David patris ejus, et regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum, et regni ejus non erit finis. Quod etiam in Isaia clarissime scriptum est: Super solium David et super regnum ejus sedebit, ut confirmet illud in judicio et justitia, amodo et usque in sempiternum. Ecce quanta concordia evangelicæ narrationis cum sermone prophetico.
paras.en: Thou hast said also, O Lord: [[88:4|I have made a covenant with my elect|Disposui testamentum electis meis]], that is, I gave the Old Testament, or the law of Moses, to the children of Israel. For since the law disposed men towards Christ, according to that saying of the Apostle, [[Gal 3:24|the law was our pedagogue in Christ|Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christo]], therefore it was given only to that people of whom Christ chose to become incarnate, namely the children of Israel. [[88:4|I have sworn to David|Juravi David]], the son of Jesse, [[88:4|my servant|servo meo]]: [[88:5|Thy seed will I settle for ever|Usque in æternum præparabo semen tuum]] [*præparabo*, literally "I will prepare"]: that is, the line of thy sons will reach as far as Christ, who is to be born of them, and in Christ Himself it will be made perpetual. That this is true is proved in Matthew, where the genealogy of David is carried down to Christ. [[88:5|And I will build up|Et ædificabo]] [[88:5|unto generation and generation|in generationem et generationem]], that is, through every generation I will make firm and preserve, [[88:5|thy throne|sedem tuam]], that is, the royal power. In the first book of Paralipomenon and elsewhere God promised King David that there should not fail a man of his seed sitting on his throne, provided only that his sons kept the divine commandments; but because they often transgressed them, turning aside to idolatry, the kingdom of David therefore suffered an interruption in the time of Sedecias, as is described in the fourth book of Kings. Yet although the throne or kingdom of David ceased for a time, it has nonetheless been restored in Christ, made firm and perpetual, as the Archangel says to the Virgin: [[Luke 1:31|Behold thou shalt conceive in thy womb and shalt bring forth a son: and thou shalt call his name Jesus|Ecce concipies in utero et paries filium, et vocabis nomen ejus Jesum]]: [[Luke 1:32|He shall be great and shall be called the Son of the Most High. And the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father: and he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|hic erit magnus, et Filius Altissimi vocabitur; et dabit illi Dominus Deus sedem David patris ejus, et regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum]], [[Luke 1:33|And of his kingdom there shall be no end|et regni ejus non erit finis]]. Which is also written most clearly in Isaias: [[Is 9:7|he shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom; to establish it|Super solium David et super regnum ejus sedebit, ut confirmet illud]] [[Is 9:7|with judgment and with justice, from henceforth and for ever|in judicio et justitia, amodo et usque in sempiternum]]. See how great is the agreement of the Gospel narrative with the prophetic word.

paras.t: Vel sic, et magis secundum doctores catholicos: Disposui, id est, ordinate dedi atque proposui, testamentum novum, id est evangelicam legem, ubi æterna hereditas est promissa: quod etiam testamentum in morte Christi confirmatum est; electis meis, id est re et nomine Christianis: de quibus ait Apostolus: Firmum fundamentum Dei stat, habens signaculum hoc, Cognovit Dominus qui sunt ejus. Petrus quoque: Vos autem genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta. De hoc testamento et dispositione ipsius Paulus testatur: Novi testamenti mediator est Jesus, ut morte intercedente in redemptionem earum prævaricationum quæ erant sub priori testamento, repromissionem accipiant qui vocati sunt æternæ hereditatis. Juravi, id est, certitudinaliter firmiterque promisi, David servo meo, id est Christo, qui ut homo minor est me, et servus meus: Usque in æternum, id est usque in finem sæculi, imo usque in vitam æternam, præparabo semen tuum, id est, per fidem et gratiam formabo et disponam Christianos et fideles. De quo semine apud Isaiam dictum est: Si posuerit (scilicet Christus) animam suam pro peccato, videbit semen longævum. Frequenter in divinis Scripturis per David intelligitur Christus. Unde Dominus per Jeremiam ait: Non dominabuntur Jacob amplius alieni, sed servient Domino Deo suo, et David regi suo, quem suscitabo eis, id est Messiæ, ut omnes exponunt. Non enim suscitavit nec suscitabit Deus defunctum illum David filium Isai, ad regnandum in hoc mundo. Hinc quoque in Osee scriptum est: Post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum.
paras.en: Or thus, and more in keeping with the Catholic doctors: [[88:4|I have made|Disposui]], that is, I have given and set forth in due order, the new [[88:4|covenant|testamentum]], that is, the law of the Gospel, in which an eternal inheritance is promised: which testament was also confirmed in the death of Christ; [[88:4|with my elect|electis meis]], that is, with those who are Christians in deed and in name: of whom the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:19|the sure foundation of God standeth firm, having this seal: the Lord knoweth who are his|Firmum fundamentum Dei stat, habens signaculum hoc, Cognovit Dominus qui sunt ejus]]. And Peter: [[1 Pet 2:9|But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation|Vos autem genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta]]. Of this testament and of its ordering Paul bears witness: Jesus is [[Heb 9:15|the mediator of the new testament|Novi testamenti mediator]]: [[Heb 9:15|that by means of his death for the redemption of those transgressions which were under the former testament, they that are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance|ut morte intercedente in redemptionem earum prævaricationum quæ erant sub priori testamento, repromissionem accipiant qui vocati sunt æternæ hereditatis]]. [[88:4|I have sworn|Juravi]], that is, I have promised with certainty and firmly, [[88:4|to David my servant|David servo meo]], that is, to Christ, who as man is less than I, and My servant: [[88:5|for ever|Usque in æternum]], that is, until the end of the world, nay, unto life eternal, [[88:5|Thy seed will I settle|præparabo semen tuum]], that is, through faith and grace I will form and dispose Christians and the faithful. Of which seed it is said in Isaias: [[Is 53:10|if he shall lay down|Si posuerit]] (namely Christ) [[Is 53:10|his life for sin, he shall see a longlived seed|animam suam pro peccato, videbit semen longævum]]. Often in the divine Scriptures Christ is understood by David. Hence the Lord says through Jeremias: [[Jer 30:8|strangers shall no more rule over him|Non dominabuntur Jacob amplius alieni]] [Denis reads *Jacob*, where the Vulgate has *ei*, "him"], [[Jer 30:9|But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up to them|sed servient Domino Deo suo, et David regi suo, quem suscitabo eis]], that is, the Messias, as all explain it. For God has not raised up, nor will He raise up, that David, the son of Isai, who is dead, to reign in this world. Hence too it is written in Osee: [[Osee 3:5|And after this the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the Lord, their God, and David, their king|Post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum]].

paras.t: Sed ubi juravit Deus Christo, quod in æternum præpararet semen ipsius? Ecce ad Abraham dicitur: Per memetipsum juravi, dicit Dominus: quia non pepercisti filio tuo unigenito propter me, benedicam te; et in semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes terræ. Quid autem per semen hoc intelligere debeamus, Apostolus exponit, ad Galatas dicens: Non dicit, In seminibus, quasi in multis; sed quasi in uno, Et semini tuo, quod est Christus. Daniel etiam dicit: Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei.
paras.en: But where did God swear to Christ that He would settle His seed for ever? See, it is said to Abraham: [[Gen 22:16|By my own self have I sworn, saith the Lord|Per memetipsum juravi, dicit Dominus]]: because thou [[Gen 22:16|hast not spared thy only begotten son for my sake|non pepercisti filio tuo unigenito propter me]], [[Gen 22:17|I will bless thee|benedicam te]]; [[Gen 22:18|And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed|et in semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes terræ]]. And what we ought to understand by this seed the Apostle explains, saying to the Galatians: [[Gal 3:16|He saith not: And to his seeds as of many. But as of one: And to thy seed, which is Christ|Non dicit, In seminibus, quasi in multis; sed quasi in uno, Et semini tuo, quod est Christus]] [Denis reads *In seminibus*, "In seeds", for the Vulgate's *Et seminibus*]. Daniel too says: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]].

paras.t: Et ædificabo, id est stabiliam, in generationem et generationem, id est in æternum, sedem tuam, id est judiciariam tuam potestatem et regiam dignitatem. Unde in Daniele scribitur: Dedit ei potestatem et honorem et regnum. Qualis vero sit ista potestas et regnum, subjungitur: Potestas ejus, potestas æterna, quæ non auferetur, et regnum quod non corrumpetur. Vel: Ædificabo per caritatem et dona Sancti Spiritus, sedem tuam, id est corda fidelium sive Ecclesiam, in quibus tu, Christe, per gratiam habitas. Anima equidem justi, sedes est sapientiæ; et in Ecclesia residet Christus, quemadmodum scriptum est: Ipse sedebit et dominabitur super solio suo. Vel: Ædificabo sedem tuam, non manu factam, sed thronum cœlestem, ut sedeas in cœlo ad dexteram meam in sede, de qua tu, Christe, locutus es: Ego vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus.
paras.en: [[88:5|And I will build up|Et ædificabo]], that is, I will establish, [[88:5|unto generation and generation|in generationem et generationem]], that is, for ever, [[88:5|thy throne|sedem tuam]], that is, thy judicial power and royal dignity. Hence it is written in Daniel: [[Dan 7:14|he gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom|Dedit ei potestatem et honorem et regnum]]. And of what kind that power and kingdom is, is added: [[Dan 7:14|his power is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed|Potestas ejus, potestas æterna, quæ non auferetur, et regnum quod non corrumpetur]]. Or: [[88:5|I will build up|Ædificabo]], through charity and the gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[88:5|thy throne|sedem tuam]], that is, the hearts of the faithful, or the Church, in which Thou, O Christ, dwellest by grace. For the soul of the just is the seat of wisdom[[Wis 7:27||]]; and Christ abides in the Church, as it is written: He [[Zach 6:13|shall sit, and rule upon his throne|sedebit et dominabitur super solio suo]]. Or: [[88:5|I will build up thy throne|Ædificabo sedem tuam]], not one made with hands, but a heavenly throne, so that Thou mayest sit in heaven at My right hand, in the seat of which Thou, O Christ, hast spoken: [[Apoc 3:21|I also have overcome and am set down with my Father in his throne|Ego vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus]].

paras.t: Confitebuntur cœli mirabilia tua, Domine: etenim veritatem tuam in ecclesia sanctorum. Hæc de angelis sanctis et cunctis cœli civibus exponi possunt, qui utique confitentur indesinenter confessione incessabilis laudis mirabilia opera Dei et veritatem ipsius, in Ecclesia triumphanti Sanctorum seu Beatorum in patria, sicut de talibus in Apocalypsi dicitur, Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua, Domine Deus omnipotens, justæ et veræ sunt viæ tuæ, Rex sanctorum: imo secundum divinum et magnum Dionysium, angeli superiores illustrant et docent angelos inferiores de quibusdam mirabilibus Dei effectibus et veritatibus divinorum effectuum. Denique cœli isti confitentur etiam mirabilia Dei et veritatem ipsius, in Ecclesia militanti sanctorum viatorum, quorum mentes illuminant de admirandis Dei operibus et sacris Scripturis. Propter quod angelus scribitur docuisse Joseph de mirabili conceptione Christi; et legitur angelus Apostolos eduxisse de carcere, eisque dixisse: Ite, et stantes loquimini in templo plebi omnia verba hæc. Nihilo minus per cœlos hoc loco convenientius intelliguntur sancti Apostoli, aliique apostolici viri, angelicam atque cœlestem conversationem in terra habentes; eritque sensus:
paras.en: [[88:6|The heavens shall confess thy wonders, O Lord: and thy truth in the church of the saints|Confitebuntur cœli mirabilia tua, Domine: etenim veritatem tuam in ecclesia sanctorum]]. These words can be explained of the holy angels and of all the citizens of heaven, who indeed confess unceasingly, with the confession of never-ending praise, the wonderful works of God and His truth, in the Church triumphant of the Saints, or of the Blessed in the fatherland; as is said of such in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 15:3|Great and wonderful are thy works, O Lord God Almighty. Just and true are thy ways, O King|Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua, Domine Deus omnipotens, justæ et veræ sunt viæ tuæ, Rex]] of saints [Denis reads *Rex sanctorum*, "King of saints", where the Clementine text has *Rex sæculorum*, "King of ages"; the margin marks the place with an asterisk]. Nay more, according to the divine and great Dionysius, the higher angels enlighten and teach the lower angels about certain wonderful effects of God and the truths of the divine effects. Lastly, these heavens confess the wonders of God and His truth also in the Church militant of the holy wayfarers, whose minds they enlighten about the wonderful works of God and the holy Scriptures. Wherefore an angel is written to have taught Joseph about the wonderful conception of Christ[[Matt 1:20||]][[Matt 1:21||]]; and we read that an angel led the Apostles out of prison[[Acts 5:19||]], and said to them: [[Acts 5:20|Go, and standing speak in the temple to the people|Ite, et stantes loquimini in templo plebi]] all these words. Nevertheless by *the heavens* in this place are more fittingly understood the holy Apostles and other apostolic men, who lived an angelic and heavenly life on earth; and the sense will be:

paras.t: Confitebuntur, id est, secure protestabuntur, docebunt et prædicabunt atque laudabunt, cœli, id est Apostoli atque eis consimiles, mirabilia tua, Domine, id est miracula tua, o Christe, et omnia quæ de tuis mysteriis sunt conscripta; etenim, id est, etiam confitebuntur et prædicabunt, veritatem tuam, id est justitiam atque evangelicam legem, omni veritate plenissimam, in ecclesia sanctorum, id est congregationibus fidelium electorum. Istud in Actibus Apostolorum clare docetur impletum, ubi inter cetera scriptum est: Videntes principes sacerdotum, Petri et Joannis constantiam, mirabantur. Quorum constantia patuit quando dicebant: Obedire oportet Deo magis quam hominibus; non enim possumus, quæ audivimus et vidimus, non loqui. Nonne mirabilia Dei et Christi ejus, hoc modo confessi sunt sancti Apostoli, dum Petrus voce omnium dixit Judæis: Jesum Nazarenum, virum approbatum in vobis a Deo virtutibus et prodigiis et signis, interemistis?
paras.en: [[88:6|shall confess|Confitebuntur]], that is, they shall boldly declare, teach, preach and praise, [[88:6|The heavens|cœli]], that is, the Apostles and those like them, [[88:6|thy wonders, O Lord|mirabilia tua, Domine]], that is, Thy miracles, O Christ, and all that has been written of Thy mysteries; [[88:6|and|etenim]], that is, they shall also confess and preach, [[88:6|thy truth|veritatem tuam]], that is, Thy justice and the law of the Gospel, most full of all truth, [[88:6|in the church of the saints|in ecclesia sanctorum]], that is, in the congregations of the elect faithful. This is clearly shewn to have been fulfilled in the Acts of the Apostles, where among other things it is written: The chief priests, [[Acts 4:13|seeing|Videntes]] [[Acts 4:13|the constancy of Peter and of John|Petri et Joannis constantiam]], [[Acts 4:13|they wondered|mirabantur]] [Denis adds *principes sacerdotum*, "the chief priests"]. Their constancy was plain when they said: [[Acts 5:29|We ought to obey God rather than men|Obedire oportet Deo magis quam hominibus]]; [[Acts 4:20|For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard|non enim possumus, quæ audivimus et vidimus, non loqui]]. Did not the holy Apostles in this way confess the wonders of God and of His Christ, when Peter, speaking for all, said to the Jews: [[Acts 2:22|Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs|Jesum Nazarenum, virum approbatum in vobis a Deo virtutibus et prodigiis et signis]], you have [[Acts 2:23|slain|interemistis]]?

paras.t: Ideo autem ista egerunt Apostoli, Quoniam quis: tanquam dicat, Nullus; in nubibus, id est in sublimibus creaturis, quales sunt Apostoli et Prophetæ, æquabitur Domino, Deo trino, uni et benedicto, seu Filio Dei Jesu Christo? de quo Petrus ait, Hic est omnium Dominus. Quamvis enim creatura possit Deo assimilari, non tamen valet ei æquari, sed in infinitum distat ab eo. Propter quod dicitur: Cui adæquastis me? dicit Sanctus. Dicuntur vero Prophetæ et Apostoli nubes, sicut de Apostolis ait Isaias: Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant? Primo, quoniam sicut nubes primo illustrantur a sole, deinde terram illuminant; sic Prophetæ atque Apostoli prius copiosiusque a Sole justitiæ Christo Domino sunt edocti, deinde homines illustraverunt. Unde dicit eis Salvator: Vos estis lux mundi. Secundo, quoniam sicut nubes terram pluendo irrigant et fecundant, sic Apostoli et Prophetæ corda hominum pluvia salutaris doctrinæ et verbo gratiæ perfuderunt, impleverunt, et a damnabili ariditate et sterilitate liberaverunt. Ideo dictum est eis: Vos estis sal terræ. Tertio, propter altitudinem contemplationis, elevationem desideriorum sublimitatemque vitæ.
paras.en: And the Apostles did these things for this reason: [[88:7|For who|Quoniam quis]], as if to say, No one, [[88:7|in the clouds|in nubibus]], that is, among the most exalted creatures, such as are the Apostles and Prophets, [[88:7|can be compared to the Lord|æquabitur Domino]], to God, Three and One and blessed, or to the Son of God, Jesus Christ? of whom Peter says: [[Acts 10:36|He is Lord of all|Hic est omnium Dominus]] [the margin gives "Ibid. v. 35"; the words are in Acts 10:36]. For although a creature can be likened to God, yet it cannot be made equal to Him, but is infinitely distant from Him. Wherefore it is said: [[Is 40:25|to whom|Cui]] have ye [[Is 40:25|made me equal|adæquastis me]]? [[Is 40:25|saith the Holy One|dicit Sanctus]]. Now the Prophets and Apostles are called clouds, as Isaias says of the Apostles: [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant]]? First, because as the clouds are first lit by the sun and then give light to the earth, so the Prophets and Apostles were first and more abundantly taught by the Sun of justice, Christ the Lord, and then enlightened men. Hence the Saviour says to them: [[Matt 5:14|You are the light of the world|Vos estis lux mundi]]. Secondly, because as the clouds water the earth with rain and make it fruitful, so the Apostles and Prophets have drenched and filled the hearts of men with the rain of saving doctrine and with the word of grace, and have freed them from damnable dryness and barrenness. Therefore it was said to them: [[Matt 5:13|You are the salt of the earth|Vos estis sal terræ]]. Thirdly, on account of the height of their contemplation, the lifting up of their desires and the loftiness of their life.

paras.t: Possunt quoque per nubes (secundum Dionysium capitulo quintodecimo Cœlestis hierarchiæ) intelligi angeli sancti. De quibus subjungitur: similis erit Domino in filiis Dei? tanquam dicat, Neque in angelis invenitur aliquis Deo æqualis. Omnes enim (secundum Apostolum) sunt administratorii spiritus. Convenienter vero per filios Dei accipiuntur etiam angeli, quia de eis Dominus apud Job sciscitatur: Ubi eras quum me laudarent astra matutina, et jubilarent omnes filii Dei? De quibus etiam narratur: Quadam die quum venissent filii Dei, et adsisterent coram Domino, adfuit inter eos et Satan.
paras.en: By *the clouds* the holy angels can also be understood (according to Dionysius, in the fifteenth chapter of the *Celestial Hierarchy*). Of whom it is added: [[88:7|who among the sons of God shall be like to God|similis erit Domino in filiis Dei]]? [Denis reads *Domino*, "to the Lord", where the Vulgate has *Deo*] as if to say, Not even among the angels is anyone found equal to God. For all of them (according to the Apostle) are [[Heb 1:14|ministering spirits|administratorii spiritus]]. And the angels too are fittingly understood by *the sons of God*, because the Lord asks about them in Job: [[Job 38:4|Where wast thou|Ubi eras]] [[Job 38:7|When the morning stars praised me together, and all the sons of God made a joyful melody?|quum me laudarent astra matutina, et jubilarent omnes filii Dei?]] Of whom it is also told: [[Job 1:6|on a certain day, when the sons of God came to stand before the Lord, Satan also was present among them|Quadam die quum venissent filii Dei, et adsisterent coram Domino, adfuit inter eos et Satan]].

paras.t: Deus qui glorificatur, id est, gloriosus esse asseritur, honoratur et exaltatur, in consilio sanctorum, id est in diligenti persecutione omnium electorum, in cœlo et terra versantium: quorum unum parque consilium est, ut Deum præ cunctis glorificent corde, ore ac opere; magnus, imo immensus, atque in omni nobilitate simpliciter interminabiliterque perfectus, et terribilis super omnes qui in circuitu ejus sunt, id est venerandus seu metuendus præ cunctis Beatis et Sanctis ei adsistentibus, et ad eum ex omni parte accedentibus. Dicuntur autem electi esse in circuitu Dei, non quod eum intra se claudant ac finiant, quum ipse illocalis incircumscriptibilisque consistat; sed quoniam sic ad eum undique confluunt, ei deserviunt et adsistunt, ac si intra se seu in medio sui eum includerent. Vel, quoniam ipse Deus gloriosus et sanctus omnia penetrat, cunctisque intimus est, et magis vicinus quam aliquid sibimetipsi, seu ipsa essentialia rei principia toti principiato; propterea dicuntur esse in circuitu ejus. Verius tamen ipse est in circuitu eorum, sicut inferius dicitur: Dominus in circuitu populi sui. Unde in Actibus Paulus testatur: Non longe est ab unoquoque nostrum: in ipso enim vivimus, movemur et sumus, sicut et quidam poetarum vestrorum dixerunt, etc. Secundum Thomam, Aratus poeta hoc dixit.
paras.en: [[88:8|God, who is glorified|Deus qui glorificatur]], that is, who is declared to be glorious, is honoured and exalted, [[88:8|in the assembly of the saints|in consilio sanctorum]] [the Latin *consilium* is "counsel", which Denis goes on to explain], that is, in the earnest purpose of all the elect who dwell in heaven and on earth, whose one and equal counsel is to glorify God above all things in heart, in word and in deed: [[88:8|great|magnus]], nay immeasurable, and simply and boundlessly perfect in every nobility, [[88:8|and terrible above all them that are about him|et terribilis super omnes qui in circuitu ejus sunt]], that is, to be revered or feared above all the blessed and the saints who stand by him and draw near to him from every side. Now the elect are said to be round about God, not because they enclose and bound him within themselves, since he is without place and cannot be circumscribed, but because they flow together to him from every side, serve him and stand by him, as though they enclosed him within themselves or in their midst. Or else, because God himself, glorious and holy, penetrates all things and is innermost to all, and is nearer to each thing than it is to itself, or than the essential principles of a thing are to the whole made of them; for that reason they are said to be round about him. More truly, however, he is round about them, as is said further on: [[Ps 124:2|the Lord is round about his people|Dominus in circuitu populi sui]]. Hence Paul testifies in the Acts: [[Acts 17:27|he be not far from every one of us|Non longe est ab unoquoque nostrum]]: [[Acts 17:28|For in him we live and move and are: as some also of your own poets said|in ipso enim vivimus, movemur et sumus, sicut et quidam poetarum vestrorum dixerunt]], etc. According to Thomas, it was the poet Aratus who said this.

paras.t: Domine, Deus virtutum, quis similis tui? Nullus utique, loquendo de similitudine naturali et perfecta. Finiti enim et infiniti nulla exstat proportio: quoniam quotiescumque finitum finito addatur, nunquam exinde infinitum efficitur. Ideoque ad insinuandam infinitam Dei excellentiam super omnia, scriptum est apud Isaiam: Quis mensus est pugillo aquas, et cœlos palma ponderavit? Quis appendit tribus digitis molem terræ, et libravit in pondere montes, et colles in statera? Unde alio in loco dictum est: Tanquam momentum stateræ sic ante te est orbis terræ, et tanquam gutta roris antelucani, quæ descendit in terram. Potens es, Domine, per essentiam, quoniam idem est tibi esse et posse; et sicut tuum esse est infinitum, sic tua potentia est immensa, cui omnia exstant facilia: prout ait Scriptura, Subest tibi, quum volueris, posse. Differt autem potentia Dei ab aliorum potentia: Primo, quoniam Deus ex se ipso seu propria potentia potens est, sicut de eo superius dictum est: Qui dominatur in virtute sua in æternum. Secundo, quoniam Deus universaliter potens est, juxta illud: Misereris omnium, quoniam omnia potes. Tertio, quia potentia Dei est penitus infinita, nec possunt tanta tamve sublimia a Deo produci, quin possint in infinitum plura atque majora ab eo creari seu effici, juxta illud: Numquid manus Domini invalida est? Et alibi: Deus sempiternus Dominus, qui creavit terminos terræ, non deficiet. Potens vero esse Deus designatur, dum dicitur in libro Job: Deus potentes non abjicit, quum et ipse sit potens.
paras.en: [[88:9|O Lord God of hosts, who is like to thee?|Domine, Deus virtutum, quis similis tui?]] No one at all, speaking of a natural and perfect likeness. For between the finite and the infinite there is no proportion, since however often finite is added to finite, the infinite never comes of it. And so, to suggest the infinite excellence of God above all things, it is written in Isaias: [[Is 40:12|Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and weighed the heavens with his palm? who hath poised with three fingers the bulk of the earth, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?|Quis mensus est pugillo aquas, et cœlos palma ponderavit? Quis appendit tribus digitis molem terræ, et libravit in pondere montes, et colles in statera?]] And so it is said in another place: [[Wis 11:23|the whole world before thee is as the least grain of the balance, and as a drop of the morning dew, that falleth down upon tho earth|Tanquam momentum stateræ sic ante te est orbis terræ, et tanquam gutta roris antelucani, quæ descendit in terram]]. [[88:9|thou art mighty, O Lord|Potens es, Domine]], by essence, since for thee to be and to be able are the same; and as thy being is infinite, so thy power is immeasurable, and to it all things are easy; as the Scripture says: [[Wis 12:18|thy power is at hand when thou wilt|Subest tibi, quum volueris, posse]] [the margin gives Ibid. xii, 16; the words are Wis 12:18]. Now the power of God differs from the power of others. First, because God is mighty of himself, or by his own power, as was said of him above: [[Ps 65:7|Who by his power ruleth for ever|Qui dominatur in virtute sua in æternum]]. Secondly, because God is mighty universally, according to the words: [[Wis 11:24|thou hast mercy upon all, because thou canst do all things|Misereris omnium, quoniam omnia potes]]. Thirdly, because the power of God is wholly infinite, and things so many and so high cannot be produced by God but that infinitely more and greater could be created or made by him, according to the words: [[Num 11:23|Is the hand of the Lord unable?|Numquid manus Domini invalida est?]] And elsewhere: [[Is 40:28|the Lord is the everlasting God, who hath created the ends of the earth: he shall not faint|Deus sempiternus Dominus, qui creavit terminos terræ, non deficiet]]. And that God is mighty is shown where it is said in the book of Job: [[Job 36:5|God doth not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty|Deus potentes non abjicit, quum et ipse sit potens]].

paras.t: Et veritas tua divina et increata, resultat, splendet atque apparet in circuitu tuo, id est in omnibus creaturis seu tibi adsistentibus, in quorum tu medio es. Quemadmodum enim divina potentia in rerum creatione relucet, sic sapientia seu veritas Dei in earum ordinibus lucet. Propter quod scriptum est: A magnitudine speciei creaturæ, poterit Creator cognoscibiliter videri; et iterum: Gloria Dei plenum est opus ejus. Vel, Veritas tua, id est vera illuminatio tua, sacra doctrina et sapientialis ordinatio, est in circuitu tuo, id est in corde seu intellectu eorum, de quibus jam dictum est: Magnus et terribilis super omnes qui in circuitu ejus sunt. Nostra quippe veritas et scientia a rebus causantur: sed veritas et scientia Dei, causa est rerum; et uti ab uno vultu diversæ resultant imagines in pluribus speculis, ita quidem ab una ac summa veritate multæ causantur veritates in rebus creatis. Propterea de hac veritate seu sapientia creata, in Ecclesiastico habetur: Deus creavit illam in Spiritu Sancto, et effudit illam super omnia opera sua et super omnem carnem, et præbet eam diligentibus se.
paras.en: [[88:9|and thy truth|Et veritas tua]], divine and uncreated, shines back, glows and appears [[88:9|round about thee|in circuitu tuo]], that is, in all creatures, or in those who stand by thee, in whose midst thou art. For as the divine power shines out in the creation of things, so the wisdom or truth of God shines in their orders. Therefore it is written: [[Wis 13:5|by the greatness of the beauty, and of the creature, the creator of them may be seen, so as to be known thereby|A magnitudine speciei creaturæ, poterit Creator cognoscibiliter videri]]; and again: [[Ecclus 42:16|full of the glory of the Lord is his work|Gloria Dei plenum est opus ejus]] [the margin gives Ecclus. xliii, 16; the words are Ecclus 42:16]. Or: [[88:9|thy truth|Veritas tua]], that is, thy true enlightening, sacred doctrine and wise ordering, is [[88:9|round about thee|in circuitu tuo]], that is, in the heart or understanding of those of whom it has just been said: [[88:8|great and terrible above all them that are about him|Magnus et terribilis super omnes qui in circuitu ejus sunt]]. For our truth and knowledge are caused by things, but the truth and knowledge of God is the cause of things; and as from one face different images are reflected in many mirrors, so from the one supreme truth many truths are caused in created things. Therefore of this created truth or wisdom it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 1:9|He created her in the Holy Ghost|Deus creavit illam in Spiritu Sancto]], [[Ecclus 1:10|And he poured her out upon all his works, and upon all flesh|et effudit illam super omnia opera sua et super omnem carnem]], [[Ecclus 1:10|hath given her to them that love him|præbet eam diligentibus se]].

paras.t: Tu dominaris potestati maris: id est, ipsum mare et omnis naturalis cursus, ordo et virtus ipsius, tibi subjecta sunt. Hoc patuit in divisione maris Rubri. Unde de Christo vero et altissimo Deo scriptum est: Ventus et mare obediunt ei. Job quoque ait: In fortitudine illius repente maria congregata sunt. Per obedientialem namque potentiam omnibus concreatam, universa Creatori suo obediunt. Motum autem fluctuum ejus tu mitigas: id est, impetuosos fluctus abyssi quiescere facis, sedas, atque confringis, quemadmodum ad sanctum Job testatus es: Circumdedi mare terminis meis, et posui vectes et ostia, et dixi: Usque huc venies, et non procedes amplius, et hic confringes tumentes fluctus tuos. Hinc quoque de Christo inducitur: Comminatus est vento, et dixit mari: Tace et obmutesce. Et facta est tranquillitas magna.
paras.en: [[88:10|Thou rulest the power of the sea|Tu dominaris potestati maris]]: that is, the sea itself and all its natural course, order and force are subject to thee. This was made plain in the dividing of the Red Sea[[Ex 14:1||]]. Hence it is written of Christ, true and most high God: [[Matt 8:27|the winds and the sea obey him?|Ventus et mare obediunt ei]] Job too says: [[Job 26:12|By his power the seas are suddenly gathered together|In fortitudine illius repente maria congregata sunt]]. For by the obediential power concreated in all things [that is, the capacity, given to every creature with its being, to be moved by God beyond its natural powers], all things obey their Creator. [[88:10|and appeasest the motion of the waves thereof|Motum autem fluctuum ejus tu mitigas]]: that is, thou makest the raging waves of the deep be still, thou calmest them and breakest them, as thou didst testify to holy Job: [[Job 38:10|I set my bounds around it, and made it bars and doors|Circumdedi mare terminis meis, et posui vectes et ostia]], [[Job 38:11|And I said: Hitherto thou shalt come, and shalt go no further, and here thou shalt break thy swelling waves|et dixi: Usque huc venies, et non procedes amplius, et hic confringes tumentes fluctus tuos]]. Hence too it is brought in of Christ: [[Mark 4:39|he rebuked the wind, and said to the sea: Peace, be still|Comminatus est vento, et dixit mari: Tace et obmutesce]], [[Mark 4:39|and there was made a great calm|Et facta est tranquillitas magna]].

paras.t: Moraliter exponitur sic: Tu dominaris potestati maris, id est potentibus sæculi et principi hujus mundi, videlicet tyrannis et dæmonibus, ne quantum velint, in tuos desæviant: ideo sequitur, motum autem fluctuum ejus, id est impetus tentationum diaboli, persecutionumque mundi, tu mitigas: quia secundum Apostolum, non permittis nos tentari supra id quod possumus, sed facis cum tentatione proventum, ut possimus sustinere. Unde Petrus ait: Novit Dominus pios de tribulatione eripere. Nonne motum fluctuum horum mitigat Deus, de quo asserit Paulus, Benedictus Deus, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra?
paras.en: Morally it is expounded thus: [[88:10|Thou rulest the power of the sea|Tu dominaris potestati maris]], that is, the powerful of the world and the prince of this world, namely tyrants and demons, so that they may not rage against thy own as much as they would. Therefore there follows: [[88:10|the motion of the waves thereof|motum autem fluctuum ejus]], that is, the onsets of the devil's temptations and of the world's persecutions, thou [[88:10|appeasest|tu mitigas]]: because, according to the Apostle, God [[1 Cor 10:13|will not suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able: but will make also with temptation issue, that you may be able to bear it|non permittis nos tentari supra id quod possumus, sed facis cum tentatione proventum, ut possimus sustinere]] [Denis turns the Apostle's words into an address to God: "thou dost not suffer us to be tempted above that which we are able"]. Hence Peter says: [[2 Pet 2:9|The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly from temptation|Novit Dominus pios de tribulatione eripere]] [Denis reads *de tribulatione*, "from tribulation"]. Does not God appease the motion of these waves, he of whom Paul declares: [[2 Cor 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], [[2 Cor 1:4|Who comforteth us in all our tribulation|qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra?]]?

paras.t: Tu humiliasti, sicut vulneratum, superbum: id est, quemcumque elatum, et præcipue primum illum apostatam angelum, qui est pater super omnes filios superbiæ, dejecisti et oppressisti, sicut dejicitur vulneratus: quemadmodum scriptum est, Deus superbis resistit; et rursus, Qui se exaltat, humiliabitur. Ideo ait Salvator: Videbam Satanam sicut fulgur de cœlo cadentem. De cujus humiliatione seu casu scriptum est: Quomodo cecidisti de cœlo, Lucifer, qui mane oriebaris? Unde et alibi habetur: Prudentia Dei percussit superbum. In brachio virtutis tuæ, id est in excelsa et propria tua potestate, dispersisti inimicos tuos, dæmones, hominesque injustos. Hos namque Deus dispergit ab unitate quæ ipse est, et ita convertuntur ad multa caduca et vana, amittentes jam esse gratiæ, et in futuro esse gloriæ. Idcirco in libro Job asseritur: Vidi impios Domino flante perisse.
paras.en: [[88:11|Thou hast humbled the proud one, as one that is slain|Tu humiliasti, sicut vulneratum, superbum]]: that is, whoever is lifted up, and above all that first apostate angel[[Is 14:10||]], who is father over all the children of pride[[Job 41:25||]] [the margin gives Job xxi, 25; the words are close to Job 41:25, "king over all the children of pride"], thou hast cast down and crushed, as one wounded is cast down; as it is written: [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud|Deus superbis resistit]]; and again: [[Luke 14:11|every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled|Qui se exaltat, humiliabitur]]. Therefore the Saviour says: [[Luke 10:18|I saw Satan like lightning falling from heaven|Videbam Satanam sicut fulgur de cœlo cadentem]]. Of whose humbling or fall it is written: [[Is 14:12|How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, who didst rise in the morning?|Quomodo cecidisti de cœlo, Lucifer, qui mane oriebaris?]] Hence it is said elsewhere too: [[Job 26:12|his wisdom has struck the proud one|Prudentia Dei percussit superbum]]. [[88:11|With the arm of thy strength|In brachio virtutis tuæ]], that is, by thy high and proper power, [[88:11|thou hast scattered thy enemies|dispersisti inimicos tuos]], the demons and unjust men. For God scatters these from the unity which he himself is, and so they are turned to many perishable and vain things, losing now the being of grace, and in the future the being of glory. Therefore it is declared in the book of Job: [[Job 4:8|I have seen|Vidi]] the wicked [[Job 4:9|Perishing by the blast of God|Domino flante perisse]].

paras.t: Tui sunt cœli, et tua est terra, id est omnia superiora et inferiora; orbem terræ et plenitudinem ejus, id est universa in eo contenta, tu fundasti, id est, stabiliter collocasti: juxta illud, Dominus sapientia fundavit terram, stabilivit cœlos prudentia.
paras.en: [[88:12|Thine are the heavens, and thine is the earth|Tui sunt cœli, et tua est terra]], that is, all things above and below; [[88:12|the world and the fulness thereof|orbem terræ et plenitudinem ejus]], that is, all that is contained in it, [[88:12|thou hast founded|tu fundasti]], that is, hast set firmly in place; according to the words: [[Prov 3:19|The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth, hath established the heavens by prudence|Dominus sapientia fundavit terram, stabilivit cœlos prudentia]].

paras.t: Aquilonem, id est partem terræ aquilonarem austro oppositam, seu ventum Aquilo dictum, et mare magnum, Oceanum terram cingentem, tu creasti. Unde in libro Job scriptum est, Qui extendit aquilonem super vacuum; et in Apocalypsi: Timete Dominum, et date illi claritatem, et adorate eum qui fecit cœlum et terram, mare et fontes aquarum. Propter quod sanctus Job ait: Quis ignorat quod manus Domini fecit hæc omnia?
paras.en: [[88:13|The north|Aquilonem]], that is, the northern part of the earth, opposite the south, or the wind called Aquilo, [[88:13|and the sea|et mare]], the great sea, the Ocean that girdles the earth, [[88:13|thou hast created|tu creasti]]. Hence it is written in the book of Job: [[Job 26:7|He stretched out the north over the empty space|Qui extendit aquilonem super vacuum]]; and in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 14:7|Fear the Lord and give him honour|Timete Dominum, et date illi claritatem]] [Denis reads *claritatem*, "glory", for *honorem*], [[Apoc 14:7|And adore ye him that made heaven and earth, the sea and the fountains of waters|et adorate eum qui fecit cœlum et terram, mare et fontes aquarum]]. Therefore holy Job says: [[Job 12:9|Who is ignorant that the hand of the Lord hath made all these things?|Quis ignorat quod manus Domini fecit hæc omnia]]

paras.t: Vel: Tui sunt cœli, id est angelicæ mentes, seu sancti prædicatores cœliformiter conversantes, et tua est terra, id est homines terreni, quantum ad id quod sunt: sunt enim tui per naturam. Orbem terræ, id est universalem Ecclesiam, per totum mundum diffusam, et plenitudinem ejus, id est spirituales ejus divitias, scilicet munera gratiarum, sacramenta, virtutes, et cetera spiritualia bona, tu fundasti, quoniam sine te conservari non possunt, sicut nec haberi valent nisi a te. Aquilonem, id est diabolum, aquiloni, id est peccatoribus propter caritatis carentiam frigidis, dominantem: qui dixit: Sedebo in monte testamenti, in lateribus aquilonis; et mare, id est homines ad instar maris instabiles, impetuosos, amaros, tu creasti, dando eis esse naturæ, et naturales proprietates, perfectiones ac vires: non tamen in malitia conditi sunt.
paras.en: Or: [[88:12|Thine are the heavens|Tui sunt cœli]], that is, the angelic minds, or the holy preachers whose life is heavenly, [[88:12|and thine is the earth|et tua est terra]], that is, earthly men, as regards what they are: for they are thine by nature. [[88:12|The world|Orbem terræ]], that is, the universal Church spread through the whole world, [[88:12|and the fulness thereof|et plenitudinem ejus]], that is, its spiritual riches, namely the gifts of graces, the sacraments, the virtues and the other spiritual goods, [[88:12|thou hast founded|tu fundasti]], since without thee they cannot be preserved, as neither can they be had except from thee. [[88:13|The north|Aquilonem]], that is, the devil, who rules over the north, that is, over sinners, who are cold for want of charity; who said: [[Is 14:13|I will sit in the mountain of the covenant, in the sides of the north|Sedebo in monte testamenti, in lateribus aquilonis]]; [[88:13|and the sea|et mare]], that is, men unstable like the sea, impetuous and bitter, [[88:13|thou hast created|tu creasti]], by giving them the being of nature, and natural properties, perfections and powers: yet they were not made in wickedness.

paras.t: Thabor et Hermon in nomine tuo exsultabunt: id est, hi duo montes erunt fidelibus occasio atque materia exsultandi in Deo, propter beneficia Dei in eis ostensa. Thabor enim est mons in Terra sancta, in quo denuntiata fuit victoria Barac de Sisara et ejus exercitu. Hermon vero est mons prope Jordanem, quem transierunt Hebræi arido pede. Sicque montes hi, propter miraculosa opera Dei in eis ostensa, præbuerunt Judæis occasionem lætandi in Deo. Et maxime præbent Christianis materiam exsultandi, quia in monte Thabor transfiguratus est Christus: quem montem Petrus sanctum appellat, Hanc (inquit) vocem audivimus, quum essemus cum ipso in monte sancto. In Jordane vero, juxta quem Hermon mons situs est, baptizatus est Jesus.
paras.en: [[88:13|Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name|Thabor et Hermon in nomine tuo exsultabunt]]: that is, these two mountains will be to the faithful an occasion and matter for rejoicing in God, because of the benefits of God shown in them. For Thabor is a mountain in the Holy Land on which the victory of Barac over Sisara and his army was foretold[[Judg 4:6||]]. Hermon is a mountain near the Jordan, which the Hebrews crossed dry-shod[[Jos 3:17||]]. And so these mountains, because of the miraculous works of God shown in them, gave the Jews occasion to rejoice in God. And they give Christians still greater matter for rejoicing, because on Mount Thabor Christ was transfigured[[Mark 9:1||]]: the mountain which Peter calls holy: [[2 Pet 1:18|this|Hanc]] (he says) [[2 Pet 1:18|voice, we heard|vocem audivimus]], [[2 Pet 1:18|when we were with him in the holy mount|quum essemus cum ipso in monte sancto]]. And in the Jordan, near which Mount Hermon stands, Jesus was baptized[[Matt 3:13||]].

paras.t: Spiritualiter vero per Thabor, quod interpretatur lumen veniens, designantur Judæi, quibus primo data est lex et gratia Dei infusa. Per Hermon autem, quod interpretatur anathema, significantur gentiles, qui tempore suæ perfidiæ erant anathema Deo, et quasi anathematizati ab eo, propter idololatriæ crimen. Est itaque sensus: Thabor et Hermon, id est Judæi et gentiles ad vitam electi, non in se aut propriis viribus, sed in nomine tuo exsultabunt.
paras.en: Spiritually, by Thabor, which is interpreted *light coming*, are signified the Jews, to whom the law was first given and the grace of God poured in. By Hermon, which is interpreted *anathema*, are signified the Gentiles, who in the time of their unbelief were anathema to God, and as it were accursed by him, because of the crime of idolatry. So the sense is: [[88:13|Thabor and Hermon|Thabor et Hermon]], that is, Jews and Gentiles chosen to life, not in themselves or by their own strength, but [[88:13|shall rejoice in thy name|in nomine tuo exsultabunt]].

paras.t: Tuum brachium, id est tua fortitudo, est cum potentia, ita ut nihil ei sit difficile. Firmetur manus tua, id est, virtus tua prævaleat hostibus veritatis, eos dejiciendo, et exaltetur dextera tua. Advertendum quod manus Dei, quæ est virtus ejus operativa, interdum accipitur in bono, sicut quum dicitur, Manus ejus sanabunt; interdum vero in malo, ut quum ait Apostolus, Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis; et Job, Manum tuam longe fac a me. Dum itaque manus Dei in bono accipitur, tunc dextera ejus respicit bona æterna, sinistra vero temporalia bona, secundum quod in Proverbiis legitur: Longitudo dierum in dextera ejus, et in sinistra ejus divitiæ et gloria. Dum vero manus Dei in malo accipitur, scilicet prout concernit malum pœnæ, tunc per sinistram Dei, intelligenda est minor punitio; per dexteram vero, quæ durius percutit, punitio major. Unde superius dictum est: Inveniatur manus tua omnibus inimicis tuis; dextera tua inveniat omnes qui te oderunt. Similiter modo quum dicitur, Firmetur manus tua: per manum, accipitur virtus Dei levius puniens; per dexteram vero, eadem virtus gravius puniens: quam petit exaltari, per depressionem et dejectionem omnimodam hostium pessimorum.
paras.en: [[88:14|Thy arm|Tuum brachium]], that is, thy strength, is [[88:14|with might|cum potentia]], so that nothing is hard to it[[Gen 18:14||]]. [[88:14|Let thy hand be strengthened|Firmetur manus tua]], that is, let thy power prevail over the enemies of the truth by casting them down, [[88:14|and thy right hand exalted|et exaltetur dextera tua]]. It should be noted that the hand of God, which is his working power, is sometimes taken in a good sense, as when it is said: [[Job 5:18|his hands shall heal|Manus ejus sanabunt]]; but sometimes in a bad sense, as when the Apostle says: [[Heb 10:31|It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God|Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis]]; and Job: [[Job 13:21|Withdraw thy hand far from me|Manum tuam longe fac a me]]. When, then, the hand of God is taken in a good sense, his right hand regards eternal goods, and his left temporal goods, according to what is read in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:16|Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and glory|Longitudo dierum in dextera ejus, et in sinistra ejus divitiæ et gloria]]. But when the hand of God is taken in a bad sense, that is, as it concerns the evil of punishment, then by the left hand of God is to be understood the lesser punishment, and by his right hand, which strikes harder, the greater. Hence it was said above: [[Ps 20:9|Let thy hand be found by all thy enemies: let thy right hand find out all them that hate thee|Inveniatur manus tua omnibus inimicis tuis; dextera tua inveniat omnes qui te oderunt]]. In the same way, when it is said, [[88:14|Let thy hand be strengthened|Firmetur manus tua]], by the hand is understood the power of God punishing more lightly, and by the right hand the same power punishing more heavily; and this he asks to be exalted, by the utter overthrow and casting down of the worst enemies.

paras.t: Posset tamen hic versus exponi in bono, hoc modo: Firmetur manus tua, id est, virtus tua firmiter auxilietur famulis tuis, eosque prævalere hostibus faciat; et exaltetur dextera tua, id est, benignitas tua sublimetur, liberaliter communicando dona gratiæ et virtutum.
paras.en: This verse could, however, be expounded in a good sense, thus: [[88:14|Let thy hand be strengthened|Firmetur manus tua]], that is, let thy power firmly help thy servants and make them prevail over their enemies; [[88:14|and thy right hand exalted|et exaltetur dextera tua]], that is, let thy kindness be raised on high, by bountifully imparting the gifts of grace and of the virtues.

paras.t: Justitia et judicium præparatio sedis tuæ: id est, per justitiam atque judicium tu ipse paratus ac dignus es judicare; et sedes tua, id est judiciaria tua potestas, per justitiam atque judicium paratur, aptatur, et idonea redditur ad judicandum. Per justitiam namque, unicuique quod suum est tribuentem, et judicium quod est actus justitiæ, fit judex dignus ad judicandum.
paras.en: [[88:15|Justice and judgment are the preparation of thy throne|Justitia et judicium præparatio sedis tuæ]]: that is, through justice and judgment thou thyself art ready and worthy to judge; and thy throne, that is, thy judicial power, is prepared, fitted and made apt for judging through justice and judgment. For through justice, which renders to each what is his own, and judgment, which is the act of justice, a judge becomes worthy to judge.

paras.t: Vel sic: Justitia et judicium præparatio sedis tuæ, id est, per justam conversationem, et rectum judicium sui ipsius, fit quilibet dignus ut in eo quasi in throno ac thalamo Dominus sedeat, demoretur, et conquiescat. Ideo namque homini tali ait Salvator: Ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus.
paras.en: Or thus: [[88:15|Justice and judgment are the preparation of thy throne|Justitia et judicium præparatio sedis tuæ]], that is, through just living and right judgment of himself, anyone becomes worthy that the Lord should sit, dwell and rest in him as on a throne and in a bridal chamber. For it is to such a man that the Saviour says: [[John 14:23|we will come to him and will make our abode with him|Ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus]].

paras.t: Misericordia, per quam culpam deles et gratiam influis, et veritas, qua sicut promisisti agis: in omni enim opere tuo misericordia veritasque concurrunt; præcedent faciem tuam, id est spiritualem tuam præsentiam, qua quotidie tuis electis per contemplationem appares: secundum illud Apostoli, Nos autem revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes. Non enim adest alicui Deus per contemplationem sinceram, nisi primo per misericordiam suam peccata dimittat, gratiamque concedat: et tunc, sicut promisit, se ipsum per fidem formatam ostendit. Vel: Misericordia et veritas istæ præcedent faciem tuam, id est adventum tuum seu repræsentationem vultus tui, qua apparebis in finali judicio. Tunc quippe erit tempus justitiæ et judicii; interim vero est tempus misericordiæ et veritatis.
paras.en: [[88:15|Mercy|Misericordia]], by which thou blottest out guilt and pourest in grace, [[88:15|and truth|et veritas]], by which thou doest as thou hast promised (for in every work of thine mercy and truth run together), [[88:15|shall go before thy face|præcedent faciem tuam]], that is, thy spiritual presence, in which thou appearest daily to thy elect through contemplation; according to the words of the Apostle: [[2 Cor 3:18|But we all, beholding the glory of the Lord with open face|Nos autem revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes]]. For God is not present to anyone through pure contemplation unless he first forgives his sins by his mercy and grants him grace; and then, as he promised, he shows himself through formed faith [that is, faith given its form, or life, by charity]. Or: these, [[88:15|Mercy and truth|Misericordia et veritas]], [[88:15|shall go before thy face|præcedent faciem tuam]], that is, thy coming, or the showing of thy countenance, in which thou wilt appear at the last judgment. For then will be the time of justice and judgment; meanwhile it is the time of mercy and truth.

paras.t: Beatus populus, nunc in spe, qui scit, per gustum seu experientiam, jubilationem, id est ineffabilem mentis exhilarationem in Deo. Jubilatio nempe seu jubilus, est quædam excessiva atque insolita mentis in Deo jucunditas, adeo æstuans et erumpens ac vehemens, ut nec plene possit exprimi, neque totaliter occultari. Hæc jubilatio ex contemplatione causatur, et interdum procedit ex contemplatione divinæ bonitatis in se, cujus beatitudini congaudemus; interdum vero ex contemplatione beneficiorum divinorum. Et vere modo beatus in spe, qui in horum consideratione tam vehementer lætatur. Est namque talis lætitia, certum, dulce ac ingens præambulum felicitatis futuræ. Sic jubilans Deo, se ipsum non capit præ gaudio; stillant per oculos lacrimæ dulces, miraturque animus quod Deus tantam gratiam sibi præstare dignatur.
paras.en: [[88:16|Blessed is the people|Beatus populus]], now in hope, [[88:16|that knoweth|qui scit]], by taste or experience, [[88:16|jubilation|jubilationem]], that is, an unspeakable gladdening of the mind in God. For jubilation, or the *jubilus*, is a certain overflowing and unwonted joy of the mind in God, so burning, bursting forth and vehement that it can neither be fully expressed nor wholly hidden. This jubilation is caused by contemplation: sometimes it proceeds from the contemplation of the divine goodness in itself, in whose blessedness we rejoice with it; sometimes from the contemplation of the divine benefits. And truly he is blessed now in hope who rejoices so vehemently in considering these things. For such gladness is a sure, sweet and mighty forerunner of the happiness to come. Jubilating thus to God, a man cannot contain himself for joy; sweet tears drop from his eyes, and his soul marvels that God deigns to grant him so great a grace.

paras.t: Domine, in lumine vultus tui naturali et supernaturali ambulabunt de bono in melius, de virtute in virtutem, de via in patriam, de consideratione ad opera bona, fideles. Est enim in nobis naturale lumen, ab intellectu seu vultu divino animæ nostræ impressum, quo inter bonum et malum, verum ac falsum discernit: de quo dictum est supra, Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Domine. In isto ambulamus, dum rationis judicium sequimur. Sed quoniam homo ad supernaturalem beatitudinem ordinatur, quæ est visio Dei per speciem; ideo naturale lumen ad meritoriam vitam non sufficit, sed indiget homo lumine supernaturali, scilicet fide et donis Spiritus Sancti: et ita electi ambulant in lumine naturali, informato ac confortato lumine supernaturali, omnia opera sua ordinando ad Dei honorem ac vitam æternam. Unde Salvator: Ambulate dum lucem habetis, ut non vos tenebræ comprehendant.
