Non in hoc lumine, sed in sensualitatis errore et ignorantia vitiorum ambulant peccatores: de quorum via scriptum est, Via impiorum erit quasi lubricum in tenebris, impellentur et corruent.
paras.en: [[88:16|O Lord, in the light of thy countenance|Domine, in lumine vultus tui]], natural and supernatural, the faithful [[88:16|shall walk|ambulabunt]] from good to better, [[Ps 83:8|from virtue to virtue|de virtute in virtutem]], from the way to the fatherland, from consideration to good works. For there is in us a natural light, impressed on our soul by the divine intellect or countenance, by which it discerns between good and evil, true and false; of which it was said above: [[Ps 4:7|The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us|Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Domine]]. In this we walk when we follow the judgment of reason. But since man is ordained to a supernatural beatitude, which is the vision of God by sight [*per speciem*, as opposed to seeing by faith], the natural light does not suffice for a meritorious life, but man needs a supernatural light, namely faith and the gifts of the Holy Ghost; and so the elect walk in the natural light, informed and strengthened by the supernatural light, ordering all their works to the honour of God and to life everlasting. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 12:35|Walk whilst you have the light, and the darkness overtake you not|Ambulate dum lucem habetis, ut non vos tenebræ comprehendant]]. Not in this light, but in the error of sensuality and the ignorance of vices, do sinners walk, of whose way it is written: [[Jer 23:12|their way shall be as a slippery way in the dark|Via impiorum erit quasi lubricum in tenebris]], [[Jer 23:12|they shall be driven on, and fall|impellentur et corruent]] [Denis reads *Via impiorum*, "the way of the wicked", for *via eorum*, "their way"].

paras.t: Et in nomine tuo, id est in te ipso, exsultabunt tota die, qua in corde eorum lux gratiæ diem spiritualem producit; vel, Tota die, id est assidue, prout præsenti vitæ possibile est; et in virtute tua, id est per adjutorium gratiæ tuæ, non in naturali et propria potestate, exaltabuntur, mundum, carnem, dæmonemque vincendo, et ad regna cælestia pertingendo.
paras.en: [[88:17|And in thy name|Et in nomine tuo]], that is, in thyself, [[88:17|they shall rejoice all the day|exsultabunt tota die]], the day in which the light of grace brings forth a spiritual day in their heart; or, [[88:17|all the day|Tota die]], that is, constantly, as far as is possible in this present life; [[88:17|and in thy justice|et in virtute tua]] [Denis reads *in virtute tua*, "in thy strength", where the Vulgate has *in justitia tua*], that is, by the help of thy grace, not by natural power and their own, [[88:17|they shall be exalted|exaltabuntur]], by overcoming the world, the flesh and the devil, and by reaching the heavenly kingdom.

paras.t: Quoniam gloria virtutis eorum, id est objectum, causa et terminus gloriationis, qua de sua perfectione ac bonis operibus gloriantur, tu es: quoniam non in se, sed in te gaudent, omnia tibi adscribendo: sicut dicit Apostolus, Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. Propter quod Isaias asserit: Erit Dominus exercituum corona gloriæ et sertum exsultationis residuo populi sui. Et in beneplacito tuo, id est pia voluntate tua, seu per effectum voluntatis tuæ, qua tibi in nobis complacuit, scilicet per gratiam tuam, exaltabitur cornu nostrum, id est fortitudo et dignitas nostra, qua dicimur genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta: quia per gratiam tuam fortitudo nostra perseverat, proficit, et coronatur.
paras.en: [[88:18|For|Quoniam]] [[88:18|the glory of their strength|gloria virtutis eorum]], that is, the object, cause and end of the glorying with which they glory in their perfection and good works, [[88:18|thou art|tu es]]: since they rejoice not in themselves but in thee, ascribing all things to thee; as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:31|He that glorieth may glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]]. Therefore Isaias declares: [[Is 28:5|the Lord of hosts shall be a crown of glory, and a garland of joy to the residue of his people|Erit Dominus exercituum corona gloriæ et sertum exsultationis residuo populi sui]]. [[88:18|And in thy good pleasure|Et in beneplacito tuo]], that is, by thy loving will, or by the effect of thy will, by which thou wast well pleased in us, namely by thy grace, [[88:18|shall our horn be exalted|exaltabitur cornu nostrum]], that is, our strength and dignity, by which we are called [[1 Pet 2:9|a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation|genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta]]: because by thy grace our strength perseveres, advances, and is crowned.

paras.t: Cujus ratio est, Quia Domini est assumptio nostra, id est, a Deo misericorditer assumpti sumus: qui nos in suam protectionem gratiamque suscepit, ne ab hostibus devoremur; et, pro id est, ista assumptio est sancti Israel regis nostri, id est Dei sicut auctoris: qui est Sanctus Sanctorum, et sanctificator Israelis et rex noster. Vel: Domini, id est Filii Dei, est assumptio nostra, quoniam ipse in sua incarnatione sanctissima nostram naturam assumpsit.
paras.en: The reason for this is: [[88:19|For our protection is of the Lord|Quia Domini est assumptio nostra]], that is, we have been mercifully taken up by God, who has received us into his protection and grace, lest we be devoured by our enemies; [[88:19|and|et]], put for *that is*: this taking up is [[88:19|of our king the holy one of Israel|sancti Israel regis nostri]], that is, of God as its author, who is the Holy of Holies, and the sanctifier of Israel, and our king. Or: [[88:19|of the Lord|Domini]], that is, of the Son of God, is [[88:19|our protection|assumptio nostra]], since he in his most holy incarnation took up our nature [*assumptio*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "protection", is literally a "taking up"; hence this second reading, of the Son who *assumed*, that is, took up, our nature].

88.title: EXPLANATIO EORUMDEM VERBORUM DE CHRISTO ET MEMBRIS EJUS.
88.title_en: Explanation of the same words concerning Christ and his members.

paras.t: Tunc locutus es in visione sanctis tuis. Tunc, inquit, quando jam prædicta mihi cœlitus revelasti, locutus es in visione sanctis tuis Prophetis, quibus secreta tua, velut familiaribus et amicis revelare consuevisti : quemadmodum Amos dicit, Non faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas. His locutus es in visione, non solum imaginaria, sed etiam intellectuali : quia intelligentia est opus in visione, ut dictum est Danielis decimo. Interdum quidem in somno, juxta illud : Per somnium in visione nocturna aperit Deus aures virorum. Interdum autem in vigilia, ut patet de Daniele : et ita sunt ostensa Moysi divina mysteria, cum quo loquebatur Dominus (id est angelus Domini) facie ad faciem, sicut loqui solet homo ad amicum suum. Et dixisti, in cordibus Prophetarum per inspirationem internam. Quae tamen locutio fit ministerio angelorum, secundum quod Zacharias de se ipso protestatur : Ecce angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur, et alius angelus egrediebatur in occursum ejus, et dixit ad eum : Curre et loquere ad puerum istum. Vel, Dixisti manifeste ad aliquos per os sanctorum, qui a saeculo sunt, Prophetarum tuorum.
paras.en: [[88:20|Then thou spokest in a vision to thy saints|Tunc locutus es in visione sanctis tuis]]. Then, he says, when thou hadst already revealed to me from heaven the things foretold, thou spokest in a vision to thy saints the Prophets, to whom thou wast wont to reveal thy secrets as to thy familiars and friends: as Amos says, [[Amos 3:7|the Lord God doth nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets|Non faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas]]. To these thou spokest in a vision, not only an imaginary one but also an intellectual one [that is, not only through images formed in the imagination, but by a light given to the understanding itself]: for [[Dan 10:1|there is need of understanding in a vision|intelligentia est opus in visione]], as is said in the tenth chapter of Daniel. Sometimes indeed in sleep, according to that saying: [[Job 33:15|By a dream in a vision by night|Per somnium in visione nocturna]] God [[Job 33:16|openeth the ears of men|aperit Deus aures virorum]]. Sometimes, however, in waking, as is plain in the case of Daniel[[Dan 10:4||]]: and so the divine mysteries were shown to Moses, with whom [[Ex 33:11|the Lord spoke|loquebatur Dominus]] (that is, the angel of the Lord) [[Ex 33:11|face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend|facie ad faciem, sicut loqui solet homo ad amicum suum]]. [[88:20|And saidst|Et dixisti]], in the hearts of the Prophets by inward inspiration. Yet this speaking is done by the ministry of angels, as Zacharias testifies of himself: [[Zach 2:3|behold the angel that spoke in me went forth, and another angel went out to meet him|Ecce angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur, et alius angelus egrediebatur in occursum ejus]], [[Zach 2:4|And he said to him: Run, speak to this young man|et dixit ad eum : Curre et loquere ad puerum istum]]. Or, thou saidst openly to some [[Luke 1:70|by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning|per os sanctorum, qui a saeculo sunt, Prophetarum tuorum]] [Denis has "thy prophets", speaking to God].

paras.t: Posui adjutorium meum, scilicet humani generis redemptionem, in potente, id est in Christo, qui est virtus et sapientia Patris : qui (secundum Apostolum) portat omnia verbo virtutis suae, purgationem peccatorum faciens. Et exaltavi electum, id est Christum, qui secundum naturam assumptam appellatur electus et praelectus, sicut de eo in Canticis Sponsa fatetur : Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus. Unde, secundum Apostolum, Praedestinatus est Filius Dei in virtute, secundum spiritum sanctificationis. De plebe mea, id est ex populo Judaeorum, ex quibus Christus ; vel, De plebe mea, quia prae universis hominibus exaltatus est Christus.
paras.en: [[88:20|I have laid help|Posui adjutorium]] (my help, namely the redemption of mankind) [[88:20|upon one that is mighty|in potente]], that is, upon Christ, who is the power and wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]]; who (according to the Apostle) is [[Heb 1:3|upholding all things by the word of his power, making purgation of sins|portat omnia verbo virtutis suae, purgationem peccatorum faciens]]. [[88:20|And have exalted one chosen|Et exaltavi electum]], that is, Christ, who according to the nature he assumed is called chosen and chosen above others [*electus et prælectus*], as the Bride confesses of him in the Canticle: [[Cant 5:10|My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands|Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus]]. Hence, according to the Apostle, he [[Rom 1:4|was predestinated the Son of God in power, according to the spirit of sanctification|Praedestinatus est Filius Dei in virtute, secundum spiritum sanctificationis]]. [[88:20|Out of my people|De plebe mea]], that is, from the people of the Jews, of whom is Christ; or, [[88:20|out of my people|De plebe mea]], because Christ was exalted above all men.

paras.t: Inveni David, id est Christum manufortem et adspectu desiderabilem, servum meum : quia ut homo, minor est Deo et servus ipsius, sicut de eo Dominus per Isaiam ait : Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum. Denique apud Ezechielem, Christus et David et servus Dei vocatur : Salvabo gregem meum, ait Dominus, et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum, qui pascat eum, David servum meum. Oleo sancto meo, id est unctione Spiritus Sancti, plenitudine gratiarum, et omnibus donis Spiritus Sancti, unxi eum : sicut superius praehabitum est, Unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo exsultationis. Propter quod alio loco asserit Christus : Spiritus Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me. Et Evangelista : Non ad mensuram, inquit, dat Deus spiritum, scilicet Christo homini. Tota namque capacitas naturae creatae in Christo, impleta est gratia Dei.
paras.en: [[88:21|I have found David|Inveni David]], that is, Christ, strong of hand and desirable to behold [the two meanings commonly given for the name David], [[88:21|my servant|servum meum]]: for as man he is less than God and his servant, as the Lord says of him by Isaias: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum]]. Again, in Ezechiel Christ is called both David and the servant of God: [[Ezech 34:22|I will save my flock|Salvabo gregem meum]], says the Lord, [[Ezech 34:23|And I WILL SET UP ONE SHEPHERD OVER THEM, and he shall feed them, even my servant David|et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum, qui pascat eum, David servum meum]]. [[88:21|With my holy oil|Oleo sancto meo]], that is, with the anointing of the Holy Ghost, the fulness of graces and all the gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[88:21|I have anointed him|unxi eum]]: as was set down above: [[Ps 44:8|God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness|Unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo exsultationis]] [Denis reads *exsultationis*, "of rejoicing"; the margin gives the Vulgate's *lætitiæ*, "of gladness"]. Hence Christ declares in another place: [[Is 61:1|The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord hath anointed me|Spiritus Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me]]. And the Evangelist says: [[John 3:34|God doth not give the Spirit by measure|Non ad mensuram, inquit, dat Deus spiritum]], namely to Christ as man. For the whole capacity of created nature was filled in Christ with the grace of God.

paras.t: Manus enim mea, id est divinitas mea ei unita, auxiliabitur ei in omnibus. Humanitas enim Christi erat instrumentum animatum, conjunctum et proprium divinae virtutis sibi unitae et operantis per eam, secundum Damascenum : sicut et corpus nostrum est animae nostrae instrumentum conjunctum, animatum ac proprium. Unde Christus apud Isaiam ait : Dominus Deus auxiliator meus; et in Evangelio, Non possum ego a me ipso facere quidquam. Et brachium meum confortabit eum. Quemadmodum digitus Dei est Spiritus Sanctus, quia per eum omnem veritatem nobis ostendit, juxta illud, Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem ; sic brachium Dei est unigenitus Filius ejus, quia per eum omnia operatur. De quo brachio in Isaia scriptum est : Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium. Et alio in loco : Fecit potentiam in brachio suo. Est igitur sensus : Brachium meum, id est Verbum seu Filius meus, confortabit eum, scilicet Christum secundum quod homo est, assumendo ejus humanitatem ad sui ipsius personalem unionem, et confirmando eam in bono per beatificam fruitionem, cooperandoque ei per gratiam singularem.
paras.en: [[88:22|For my hand|Manus enim mea]], that is, my Godhead united to him, [[88:22|shall help him|auxiliabitur ei]] in all things. For the humanity of Christ was a living instrument, conjoined and proper, of the divine power united to it and working through it, according to Damascene [a "conjoined instrument" is one joined to the agent who uses it, as the hand is to the soul, not a separate one like an axe]: just as our body too is the conjoined, living and proper instrument of our soul. Hence Christ says in Isaias: [[Is 50:7|The Lord God is my helper|Dominus Deus auxiliator meus]]; and in the Gospel: [[John 5:30|I cannot of myself do any thing|Non possum ego a me ipso facere quidquam]]. [[88:22|And my arm shall strengthen him|Et brachium meum confortabit eum]]. As the Holy Ghost is the finger of God, because through him God shows us all truth, according to that saying, [[John 16:13|when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth|Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem]], so the arm of God is his only-begotten Son, because through him he works all things. Of this arm it is written in Isaias: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles|Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium]]. And in another place: [[Luke 1:51|He hath shewed might in his arm|Fecit potentiam in brachio suo]]. The sense, then, is: [[88:22|my arm|Brachium meum]], that is, the Word or my Son, [[88:22|shall strengthen him|confortabit eum]], namely Christ as man, by taking his humanity into personal union with himself, by confirming it in good through the beatific enjoyment [*fruitio*: the enjoyment of God possessed as one's last end], and by working together with it through a singular grace.

paras.t: Nihil proficiet inimicus in eo, puta diabolus : quia tentator victus atque confusus recessit a Christo, dicente ad illum, Vade retro, Satana. Et filius iniquitatis, id est Judas, quem Christus in Evangelio diabolum et filium perditionis appellat ; vel, Filius iniquitatis, id est plebs Hebraeorum : quibus Christus ait, Vos ex patre diabolo estis; non apponet nocere ei, id est, non iterabit nocumentum suum in Christo. Quamvis enim ante resurrectionem eum occiderant, postmodum tamen non apposuerunt ei nocere per effectum, quia nec corpus ejus tenere poterant in sepulcro, nec resurgentis gloriam impedire. Nempe et Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur. Vel, Non apponet nocere ei in anima, quoniam spirituale nocumentum Christo non intulerunt : et hoc ipsum nocumentum quod corpori ejus inflixerunt, cessit ad gloriam Christi, totiusque sæculi. Unde per Isaiam loquitur : Quis contradicet mihi? Stemus simul. Quis est adversarius meus? Accedat ad me. Ecce omnes quasi vestimentum conterentur.
paras.en: [[88:23|The enemy shall have no advantage over him|Nihil proficiet inimicus in eo]], namely the devil: for the tempter, vanquished and confounded, departed from Christ when he said to him, [[Matt 4:10|Begone, Satan|Vade retro, Satana]]. [[88:23|Nor the son of iniquity|Et filius iniquitatis]], that is, Judas, whom Christ in the Gospel calls [[John 6:71|a devil|diabolum]][[John 6:72||]] and [[John 17:12|the son of perdition|filium perditionis]] [the margin gives John vi, 70, 71, 72 and xvii, 12; the words are in John 6:71–72 and 17:12]; or, [[88:23|the son of iniquity|Filius iniquitatis]], that is, the Hebrew people, to whom Christ says, [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]; [[88:23|have power to hurt him|non apponet nocere ei]] [literally "shall not add to hurt him"], that is, he shall not repeat his harm against Christ. For although they had killed him before the resurrection, afterwards they did not go on to harm him in effect, because they could neither hold his body in the sepulchre nor hinder the glory of his rising. For truly [[Rom 6:9|Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more|Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur]]. Or, he shall not [[88:23|have power to hurt him|Non apponet nocere ei]] in his soul, since they did Christ no spiritual harm: and the very harm which they inflicted on his body turned to the glory of Christ and of the whole world. Hence he speaks by Isaias: [[Is 50:8|who will contend with me? let us stand together, who is my adversary? let him come near to me|Quis contradicet mihi? Stemus simul. Quis est adversarius meus? Accedat ad me]]. [[Is 50:9|Lo, they shall all be destroyed as a garment|Ecce omnes quasi vestimentum conterentur]] [the margin reads Is. i, 9; the words are Is 50:8–9].

paras.t: Et concidam a facie ipsius inimicos ejus, puta Judæos, qui propter Christi occisionem ab exercitu Romanorum trucidati sunt, venundati, atque per mundum dispersi, quemadmodum scriptum est: Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus; et erunt vagi in nationibus. Et odientes eum in fugam convertam : quia et prædicti Judæi fugerunt a facie Romanorum in Jerusalem, sed non effugerunt. Dæmones quoque frequenter a Christo et ejus ministris fugerunt. Et tandem in die judicii omnes adversarii Salvatoris fugere desiderabunt, secundum illud : Reges terræ, principes et tribuni, divites et fortes absconderunt se in speluncis et petris montium, dicentes montibus et petris : Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie sedentis super thronum.
paras.en: [[88:24|And I will cut down his enemies before his face|Et concidam a facie ipsius inimicos ejus]], namely the Jews, who for the killing of Christ were slaughtered by the army of the Romans, sold, and scattered through the world, as it is written: [[Osee 9:17|My God will cast them away, because they hearkened not to him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations|Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus; et erunt vagi in nationibus]]. [[88:24|and them that hate him I will put to flight|Et odientes eum in fugam convertam]]: for the said Jews also fled from the face of the Romans into Jerusalem, but did not escape. The devils too have often fled from Christ and his ministers. And at last, on the day of judgment, all the adversaries of the Saviour will long to flee, according to that saying: [[Apoc 6:15|the kings of the earth and the princes and tribunes and the rich and the strong|Reges terræ, principes et tribuni, divites et fortes]] [[Apoc 6:15|hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of mountains|absconderunt se in speluncis et petris montium]]; [[Apoc 6:16|And they say to the mountains and the rocks: Fall upon us and hide us from the face of him that sitteth upon the throne|dicentes montibus et petris : Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie sedentis super thronum]].

paras.t: Et veritas mea et misericordia mea cum ipso. Christus enim veritate plenus fuit, sicut scriptum est : Vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre, plenum gratiæ et veritatis. Erat enim veritas Dei cum Christo, quoniam omnia quæ de Christo per Prophetas prædixit, in ipso implevit. Et de Christo filii falsitatis veraciter loquebantur : Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo. Est quoque veritas Dei cum Christo, sicut cum omnium justo et infallibili judice. Sed et misericordia Dei erat cum Christo : quoniam per solam misericordiam Dei, natura ejus humana a Verbo Dei assumpta est, et ab omni culpa præservata, omniumque divinorum charismatum gratia adimpleta ; et misericordiam sibi impensam, Christus paratus est nobis communicare. Et in nomine meo exaltabitur cornu ejus, id est regia dignitas, ita ut omnes populi, tribus ac linguæ ei ministrent. Unde de Christo Pater seu Trinitas per Isaiam ait : Ecce intelliget servus meus, et exaltabitur, et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde.
paras.en: [[88:25|And my truth and my mercy shall be with him|Et veritas mea et misericordia mea cum ipso]]. For Christ was full of truth, as it is written: [[John 1:14|we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father|Vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre]], [[John 1:14|full of grace and truth|plenum gratiæ et veritatis]]. For the truth of God was with Christ, since all that he foretold of Christ by the Prophets he fulfilled in him. And even the sons of falsehood spoke truly of Christ: [[Matt 22:16|Master, we know that thou art a true speaker and teachest the way of God in truth. Neither carest thou for any man|Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo]]. The truth of God is also with Christ as with the just and infallible judge of all. And the mercy of God too was with Christ: since by the mercy of God alone his human nature was assumed by the Word of God, preserved from all fault, and filled with the grace of all the divine gifts; and the mercy bestowed on him Christ is ready to share with us. [[88:25|and in my name shall his horn be exalted|Et in nomine meo exaltabitur cornu ejus]], that is, his kingly dignity, so that all peoples, tribes and tongues serve him[[Dan 7:14||]]. Hence the Father, or the Trinity, says of Christ by Isaias: [[Is 52:13|Behold my servant shall understand, he shall be exalted, and extolled, and shall be exceeding high|Ecce intelliget servus meus, et exaltabitur, et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde]].

paras.t: Et ponam in mari manum ejus, id est, in terris et populis circa mare morantibus dominabitur Christus. Hoc modo videmus impletum in Cypro, Portugallia, et aliis regnis. Et in fluminibus dexteram ejus : id est, fortitudinem Christi ponam in insulis, ita quod populi habitantes in insulis, Christo obedient. Unde apud Isaiam Dominus ait : Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mare, in Africam et Lydiam. Alibi quoque habetur : Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt.
paras.en: [[88:26|And I will set his hand in the sea|Et ponam in mari manum ejus]], that is, Christ shall rule in the lands and peoples dwelling about the sea. We see this fulfilled in Cyprus, Portugal and other kingdoms. [[88:26|And his right hand in the rivers|Et in fluminibus dexteram ejus]]: that is, I will set the strength of Christ in the islands, so that the peoples dwelling in the islands obey Christ. Hence the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles into the sea, into Africa, and Lydia|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mare, in Africam et Lydiam]]. And elsewhere we have: [[Is 42:12|They shall give glory to the Lord, and shall declare his praise in the islands|Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt]].

paras.t: Ipse invocabit me : Pater meus es tu, Deus meus, et susceptor salutis meæ. Nam Christus dixit : Pater, ignosce illis; et, Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum. Ecce quoties invocavit Christus Deum, nominans eum Patrem ? Vocavit eum etiam Deum suum, dicendo : Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me ? Sed et susceptorem suæ salutis (id est, quod eum suscepit ad salutem) vocavit eum, dicendo : Omnia mea abs te sunt.
paras.en: [[88:27|He shall cry out to me: Thou art my father: my God, and the support of my salvation|Ipse invocabit me : Pater meus es tu, Deus meus, et susceptor salutis meæ]]. For Christ said: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them|Pater, ignosce illis]]; and, [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]. See how often Christ called upon God, naming him Father! He also called him his God, saying: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me]][[Ps 21:2||]]. And he also called him the support of his salvation (that is, the one who took him up unto salvation [*susceptor*, from *suscipere*, "to take up"]), saying: All my things are from thee [no margin note; compare John 17:7 and 17:10].

paras.t: Et ego primogenitum ponam illum. Christus ut Deus, est Unigenitus Dei ; ut homo autem, est primogenitus prædestinatione et dignitate, non tempore. Unde Apostolus ait : Quos præscivit, et prædestinavit conformes fieri imaginis Filii sui, ut sit ipse primogenitus in multis fratribus ; et rursus : Qui est imago Dei invisibilis, primogenitus omnis creaturæ. Dicitur quoque Christus primogenitus, quoniam ante omnia creata est genitus. Posuit itaque Deus Christum primogenitum, faciendo eum omnibus electis excellentiorem, et caput Ecclesiæ. Excelsum præ regibus terræ ponam illum : quoniam ipse est rex regum, et Dominus dominantium, et princeps regum terræ. Idcirco supra de eo dictum est : Et adorabunt eum omnes reges terræ.
paras.en: [[88:28|And I will make him my firstborn|Et ego primogenitum ponam illum]]. Christ as God is the Only-begotten of God; but as man he is the firstborn by predestination and dignity, not in time. Hence the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:29|whom he foreknew, he also predestinated to be made conformable to the image of his Son: that he might be the Firstborn amongst many brethren|Quos præscivit, et prædestinavit conformes fieri imaginis Filii sui, ut sit ipse primogenitus in multis fratribus]]; and again: [[Col 1:15|Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature|Qui est imago Dei invisibilis, primogenitus omnis creaturæ]]. Christ is also called the firstborn because he was begotten before all created things. So God made Christ the firstborn by making him more excellent than all the elect, and the head of the Church. [[88:28|High above the kings of the earth|Excelsum præ regibus terræ]] I will make him: since he is [[Apoc 19:16|KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|rex regum, et Dominus dominantium]], and [[Apoc 1:5|the prince of the kings of the earth|princeps regum terræ]]. Therefore it was said of him above: [[Ps 71:11|And all kings of the earth shall adore him|Et adorabunt eum omnes reges terræ]] [the margin reads Ps. lxxxi, 11; the verse is Ps 71:11].

paras.t: In æternum servabo illi misericordiam meam, id est, quidquid misericorditer suæ humanitati donavi, conservabo sine cessatione in ea ; et testamentum meum fidele ipsi, id est, promissionem sibi a me factam, fideliter adimplebo : sicut et ipse ait, Necesse est impleri omnia quæ scripta sunt in lege Moysis et Prophetis et Psalmis de me.
paras.en: [[88:29|I will keep my mercy for him for ever|In æternum servabo illi misericordiam meam]], that is, whatever I have mercifully given to his humanity I will preserve in it without ceasing; [[88:29|and my covenant faithful to him|et testamentum meum fidele ipsi]], that is, the promise I have made to him I will faithfully fulfil: as he himself says, [[Luke 24:44|all things must needs be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses and in the prophets and in the psalms, concerning me|Necesse est impleri omnia quæ scripta sunt in lege Moysis et Prophetis et Psalmis de me]].

paras.t: Et ponam in sæculum sæculi semen ejus, id est, populum christianum ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto in Christo renatum, usque in finem sæculi continuabo. Ecclesia enim in finem mundi persistet, præsertim quum Christus ei promiserit : Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi. De hujus seminis Christi perpetuatione scriptum est : Si posuerit in mortem animam suam, videbit semen longævum. Ponam et thronum ejus, id est sedem et potestatem ejus regalem, sicut dies cæli, ita quod nunquam cessabit ; et regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum, et regni ejus non erit finis.
paras.en: [[88:30|And I will make his seed to endure for evermore|Et ponam in sæculum sæculi semen ejus]], that is, the Christian people, born again in Christ of water and the Holy Ghost, I will continue until the end of the world. For the Church will endure to the end of the world, especially since Christ has promised her: [[Matt 28:20|behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]]. Of the perpetuation of this seed of Christ it is written: [[Is 53:10|if he shall lay down his life for sin, he shall see a longlived seed|Si posuerit in mortem animam suam, videbit semen longævum]] [Denis reads *in mortem*, "unto death", where the Vulgate has *pro peccato*, "for sin"]. [[88:30|And his throne|et thronum ejus]] I will make, that is, his seat and kingly power, [[88:30|as the days of heaven|sicut dies cæli]], so that it shall never cease; [[Luke 1:32|and he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|et regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum]], [[Luke 1:33|And of his kingdom there shall be no end|et regni ejus non erit finis]].

paras.t: Si autem dereliquerint filii ejus per fidem et gratiam baptismalem, videlicet Christiani, legem meam evangelicam, eam non observando : prout de quibusdam in Osee habetur, Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo ; visitabo in virga iniquitates eorum, paternaliter eos corripiendo, non penitus exterminando : quoniam ego quos amo, arguo et castigo. Misericordiam autem meam non dispergam ab eo, id est, gratiam meam non penitus auferam a populo christiano. Et in isto notatur magnitudo misericordiæ Dei tempore evangelicæ legis, quod ideo dicitur tempus gratiæ. Unde scriptum est : Erit, qui offenderit ex eis in die illa, quasi David : cui utique Deus maximam misericordiam fecit.
paras.en: [[88:31|And if his children forsake|Si autem dereliquerint filii ejus]] (his children by faith and baptismal grace, namely Christians) [[88:31|my law|legem meam]] of the Gospel, by not observing it: as is said of some in Osee, [[Osee 4:10|they have forsaken the Lord in not observing|Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo]] [the Douay-Rheims adds "the law"]; [[88:33|I will visit their iniquities with a rod|visitabo in virga iniquitates eorum]], correcting them as a father, not destroying them utterly: for [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]]. [[88:34|But my mercy I will not take away from him|Misericordiam autem meam non dispergam ab eo]], that is, I will not wholly take away my grace from the Christian people. And in this is noted the greatness of God's mercy in the time of the law of the Gospel, which is therefore called the time of grace. Hence it is written: [[Zach 12:8|he that hath offended among them in that day shall be as David|Erit, qui offenderit ex eis in die illa, quasi David]] [the margin reads Zach. xiii, 8; the words are Zach 12:8]: to whom God indeed showed the greatest mercy.

paras.t: Neque profanabo testamentum meum, id est promissionem meam, Christo et semini ejus factam. Semel juravi in sancto meo, id est in me ipso ; si David mentiar, id est, Christo non mentiar : Semen ejus, id est populus christianus, in æternum manebit, nunc in via per fidem et gratiam, deinde in patria per fruitionem et gloriam.
paras.en: [[88:35|Neither will I profane my covenant|Neque profanabo testamentum meum]], that is, my promise made to Christ and to his seed. [[88:36|Once have I sworn by my holiness|Semel juravi in sancto meo]], that is, by myself; [[88:36|I will not lie unto David|si David mentiar]] [literally "if I lie to David", a Hebrew form of oath meaning "I will not lie"], that is, I will not lie to Christ: [[88:37|His seed|Semen ejus]], that is, the Christian people, [[88:37|shall endure for ever|in æternum manebit]], now on the way by faith and grace, afterwards in the fatherland by enjoyment and glory.

paras.t: Tu vero repulisti et despexisti. Hæc et sequentia exponunt doctores catholici de regni et populi David dejectione, sicut in præcedenti expositione patuit. Quæ tamen aliquo modo de statu Ecclesiæ accipi possunt, quoniam populus christianus sæpe similia passus est a paganis atque hæreticis, qualia sustinuerunt Judæi a Chaldæis et aliis gentibus : possetque littera applicari ad hoc.
paras.en: [[88:39|But thou hast rejected and despised|Tu vero repulisti et despexisti]]. These words and those that follow the Catholic doctors expound of the overthrow of the kingdom and people of David, as was made plain in the preceding exposition. Yet they can in some way be taken of the state of the Church, since the Christian people has often suffered from pagans and heretics things like those the Jews endured from the Chaldeans and other nations: and the letter could be applied to this.

paras.t: Postremo, quædam in hoc psalmo contenta, de confessoribus pontificibus cantat Ecclesia, scilicet : Posui adjutorium in potente : posuit namque Deus auxilium gratiæ suæ in illis. Et exaltavi electum de plebe mea : id est, quemlibet sanctum episcopum sublimavi ad statum, gradum ac ordinem episcopalem. Nemo enim assumit sibi honorem, sed qui vocatur a Deo tanquam Aaron. Inveni David servum meum, id est quemlibet sanctum confessorem antistitem, contra mundum, carnem ac dæmonem fortiter dimicantem ; oleo sancto meo unxi eum : quia pontifices oleo sancto unguntur ; et sancti episcopi spiritualiter ungebantur ex infusione gratiarum Spiritus Sancti, cujus unctio docuit eos. Quomodo autem cetera quæ cantantur, eis conveniant, ex præinductis clarissime liquet.
paras.en: Lastly, certain things contained in this psalm the Church sings of confessor bishops [in the Office of the Common of a Confessor Bishop], namely: [[88:20|I have laid help upon one that is mighty|Posui adjutorium in potente]]: for God has laid the help of his grace upon them. [[88:20|and have exalted one chosen out of my people|Et exaltavi electum de plebe mea]]: that is, I have raised each holy bishop to the episcopal state, rank and order. [[Heb 5:4|Neither doth any man take the honour to himself, but he that is called by God, as Aaron was|Nemo enim assumit sibi honorem, sed qui vocatur a Deo tanquam Aaron]]. [[88:21|I have found David my servant|Inveni David servum meum]], that is, each holy confessor bishop, fighting valiantly against the world, the flesh and the devil; [[88:21|with my holy oil I have anointed him|oleo sancto meo unxi eum]]: for bishops are anointed with holy oil; and the holy bishops were anointed spiritually by the infusion of the graces of the Holy Ghost, whose unction taught them. How the other things that are sung fit them is very clear from what was set out before.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum verbis et sensibus magnum, mysteriis plenum, omni laude dignum audivimus : in quo primo omnium misericordia Dei suavissime commendatur, ejus promissa tanguntur, ipsa summa Divinitas pulcherrime præconizatur, Christus secundum utramque naturam mirabiliter describitur, ejus mysteria copiose traduntur ; tandem humanæ naturæ commemoratur fragilitas, divinæ majestatis imploratur benignitas : atque finaliter Deus jucundo laudatur versiculo, quo dicitur : Benedictus Dominus in æternum. Fiat, fiat. Elaboremus igitur cum devotione condigna et sancta hilaritate ac puritate præcipua, tantum psalmum depromere, quatenus nobis conveniat quod in eo cantatur, Beatus populus qui scit jubilationem : et, Domine, in lumine vultus tui ambulabunt, et in nomine tuo exsultabunt tota die, etc. Omnino equidem decet nos in laudibus Dei creatoris et salvatoris nostri cordialiter exsultare et summe laetari, tanquam in summo bono, omnium bonorum nostrorum scaturiente et supermisericordissimo fonte.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm great in words and in meanings, full of mysteries, worthy of all praise: in which, first of all, the mercy of God is most sweetly commended, his promises are touched upon, the supreme Godhead itself is most beautifully proclaimed, Christ is wonderfully described according to both natures, and his mysteries are abundantly set forth; then the frailty of human nature is recalled, and the kindness of the divine majesty implored: and finally God is praised in a joyful little verse, in which it is said: [[88:53|Blessed be the Lord for evermore. So be it. So be it.|Benedictus Dominus in æternum. Fiat, fiat.]] Let us labour, then, with fitting devotion, holy gladness and special purity, to bring forth so great a psalm, that what is sung in it may befit us: [[88:16|Blessed is the people that knoweth jubilation|Beatus populus qui scit jubilationem]]: and, [[88:16|They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance|Domine, in lumine vultus tui ambulabunt]]: [[88:17|And in thy name they shall rejoice all the day|et in nomine tuo exsultabunt tota die]], etc. It altogether befits us indeed to rejoice from the heart and to be supremely glad in the praises of God our creator and saviour, as in the supreme good, the welling and more than most merciful fount of all our goods.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus, gloria virtutis Sanctorum, da nobis semper in lumine vultus tui ambulare, et in nomine tuo exsultare: ut misericordia tua faciem nostram præeunte, perfecto cursu justitiæ ad te valeamus pervenire.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, glory of the strength of the saints[[88:18||]], grant us ever to walk [[88:16|in the light of thy countenance|in lumine vultus tui]], and to rejoice [[88:17|in thy name|in nomine tuo]]: that, with thy mercy going before our face, we may come to thee by a perfect course of justice.

89.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI NONI: DOMINE, REFUGIUM FACTUS ES NOBIS.
89.title_en: Explanation of the eighty-ninth psalm: Lord, thou hast been our refuge.

paras.t: Exponendi nunc psalmi titulus talis est: Oratio Moysis, hominis Dei. Secundum Hebræos atque Hieronymum, Moyses est auctor psalmi præsentis. Secundum Augustinum vero et eum sequentes, David eum composuit, sed intitulatur a Moyse, quia in eo quædam tanguntur ad vetus Testamentum spectantia, et quædam ad novum pertinent Testamentum: sicque congruenter intitulatur a Moyse, qui erat veteris Testamenti legislator, et novi Testamenti propheta. Auctor itaque psalmi præsentis, quicumque sit ille, rogaturus Deum pro beneficiis acquirendis, primo gratias agit de beneficiis jam concessis: quoniam ad impetranda dona futura optimus modus est, gratum exsistere de donis præteritis seu receptis. Habenti enim, id est grato, dabitur; ei autem qui non habet, id est ingrato, et quod videtur habere, auferetur ab eo.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be expounded is this: [[89:1|A prayer of Moses the man of God|Oratio Moysis, hominis Dei]]. According to the Hebrews and Jerome, Moses is the author of the present psalm. But according to Augustine and those who follow him, David composed it, but it is entitled after Moses, because some things are touched on in it that concern the Old Testament, and some that pertain to the New Testament: and so it is fittingly entitled after Moses, who was the lawgiver of the Old Testament and a prophet of the New. The author of the present psalm, then, whoever he may be, being about to ask God for benefits yet to be obtained, first gives thanks for the benefits already granted: since the best way to obtain future gifts is to show oneself grateful for past gifts, that is, for gifts received. [[Matt 25:29|For to every one that hath|Habenti enim]], that is, to the grateful, [[Matt 25:29|shall be given|dabitur]]; [[Matt 25:29|but from him that hath not|ei autem qui non habet]], that is, from the ungrateful, [[Matt 25:29|that also which he seemeth to have shall be taken away|et quod videtur habere, auferetur ab eo]].

paras.t: Itaque ait: Domine, refugium factus es nobis: id est, per beneficia tua nobis collata, dedisti nobis fiduciam plena fide confugiendi ad te in omni necessitate et casu. Ab initio enim fecisti cœlum et omnia sidera, solem ac lunam, in ministerium cunctis gentibus quæ sub cœlo sunt, ut dicitur in Deuteronomio. Deinde fecisti hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem tuam, fecistique eum dominari piscibus maris et bestiis terræ. Habuistique ab exordio specialem providentiam generis humani, in tantum ut dicat Apostolus: Numquid cura est Deo de bobus? Propter hæc atque similia, refugium factus es nobis a generatione in generationem, id est indesinenter per omnium generationum successionem. Verumtamen modo, o Domine, multo amplius refugium factus es nobis, per beneficium tuæ benedictissimæ incarnationis, per meritum tuæ sanctissimæ conversationis et effusionem tui pretiosissimi sanguinis, per missionem Spiritus Sancti, per Sacramentum corporis et sanguinis tui. Idcirco tu dicis: Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos; et iterum: Qui sitit, veniat; et qui vult, accipiat aquam vitæ gratis. Dicitur autem Deus factus refugium nostrum, non per aliquam mutationem seu novitatem ipsius, sed per novam conversionem nostræ mentis ad ipsum: sicut columna fixa stans, fit mihi dextera et sinistra sine sui mutatione, secundum quod ego me diversimode ad eam habeo.
paras.en: And so he says: [[89:1|Lord, thou hast been our refuge|Domine, refugium factus es nobis]]: that is, by thy benefits conferred on us thou hast given us confidence, with full faith, to flee to thee in every need and mishap. For from the beginning thou madest heaven and all the stars[[Gen 1:1||]][[Gen 1:16||]], [[Deut 4:19|the sun and the moon|solem ac lunam]], [[Deut 4:19|for the service of all the nations, that are under heaven|in ministerium cunctis gentibus quæ sub cœlo sunt]], as is said in Deuteronomy. Then thou madest man to thy image and likeness, and madest him to have dominion over the fishes of the sea and the beasts of the earth[[Gen 1:27||]][[Gen 1:28||]] [the margin gives Gen. i, 27, 28; the words "image and likeness" are those of Gen 1:26]. And from the very beginning thou hast had a special providence for the human race, so much so that the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 9:9|Doth God take care for oxen?|Numquid cura est Deo de bobus?]] For these and like reasons thou hast been our refuge [[89:1|from generation to generation|a generatione in generationem]], that is, unceasingly, through the succession of all generations. But now, O Lord, thou hast become our refuge far more fully: through the benefit of thy most blessed Incarnation, through the merit of thy most holy life among us and the shedding of thy most precious blood, through the sending of the Holy Ghost, through the Sacrament of thy Body and Blood. Therefore thou sayest: [[Matt 11:28|Come to me all you that labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you|Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos]]; and again: [[Apoc 22:17|he that thirsteth, let him come. And he that will, let him take the water of life, freely|Qui sitit, veniat; et qui vult, accipiat aquam vitæ gratis]]. Now God is said to have become our refuge, not through any change or newness in himself, but through a new turning of our mind to him: just as a pillar standing fixed comes to be on my right or on my left without any change in itself, according as I place myself differently in relation to it.

paras.t: Priusquam montes fierent, et formaretur terra et orbis, id est totus mundus, scilicet ante omnem creaturam seu totum universum, a sæculo et in sæculum, id est æternaliter, tu es Deus: non quod ante mundi creationem fuerint sæculum et sæculum, sed quia tunc erat ipsa æternitas, omnium sæculorum durationem immobiliter continens. Possunt autem per montes intelligi angeli Dei, vel partes terræ sublimes. Ante omnia ista est Deus, quia creator eorum: creator autem creaturam præcedit natura, dignitate ac tempore. Unde per Isaiam ait: Ego sum Dominus faciens omnia, extendens cœlos solus, stabiliens terram, et nullus mecum. Convenienter quoque dicit, Tu es Deus, et non, Eras: quia in Deo semper est stabile atque invariabile esse: in quo nec præteritum est neque futurum, sed æterna præsentia, ac præsens ac pura æternitas, quæ est interminabilis vitæ tota simul perfecta possessio. Et hoc modo loquendi utitur Christus: Antequam, inquiens, Abraham fieret, ego sum.
paras.en: [[89:2|Before the mountains were made|Priusquam montes fierent]], [[89:2|or the earth and the world was formed|formaretur terra et orbis]], that is, the whole world, namely before every creature or the whole universe, [[89:2|from eternity and to eternity|a sæculo et in sæculum]], that is, eternally, [[89:2|thou art God|tu es Deus]]: not that before the creation of the world there were age and age [sæculum et sæculum: the psalm's "from eternity and to eternity" is literally "from age and unto age"], but because then there was eternity itself, which immovably contains the duration of all ages. Now by the mountains may be understood the angels of God, or the lofty parts of the earth. Before all these is God, because he is their creator: and the creator precedes the creature in nature, dignity and time. Hence he says through Isaias: [[Is 44:24|I am the Lord, that make all things, that alone stretch out the heavens, that established the earth, and there is none with me|Ego sum Dominus faciens omnia, extendens cœlos solus, stabiliens terram, et nullus mecum]]. Fittingly too he says, [[89:2|thou art|Tu es]] God, and not, Thou wast: because in God being is always stable and unchanging: in whom there is neither past nor future, but eternal presence, a present and pure eternity, which is the whole, simultaneous and perfect possession of unending life [Boethius's definition of eternity]. And Christ uses this manner of speaking: [[John 8:58|before|Antequam]], he says, [[John 8:58|Abraham was made, I AM|Abraham fieret, ego sum]].

paras.t: Ne avertas hominem, id est, ne averti permittas hominem a te ipso summo bono, et a bonis spiritualibus atque virtutibus, in humilitatem, id est in vilitatem, ita ut convertatur ad bona temporalia et caduca, et concupiscentias carnis. Hoc age, quia et dixisti, Convertimini, filii hominum: id est, per angelos et homines sanctos exhortatus es homines ad pœnitentiam. Da ergo implere quod mones.
paras.en: [[89:3|Turn not man away|Ne avertas hominem]], that is, do not let man be turned away from thyself, the highest good, and from spiritual goods and virtues, [[89:3|to be brought low|in humilitatem]] [literally "into lowliness"], that is, into vileness, so that he turn to temporal and perishable goods and to the concupiscences of the flesh. Do this, because [[89:3|and thou hast said: Be converted, O ye sons of men|et dixisti, Convertimini, filii hominum]]: that is, through angels and holy men thou hast exhorted men to penance. Grant, then, that we may fulfil what thou urgest.

paras.t: Idcirco autem hortatus es hominem ad conversionem salubrem, Quoniam mille anni ante oculos tuos, id est, quia quælibet duratio temporalis, seu longitudo vitæ humanæ, quantumcumque sit longa, reputatur a te, et brevis est coram te, seu comparatione tuæ æternitatis, tanquam dies hesterna quæ præteriit, id est, nullius momenti est, et velut nihil existit: quia finiti ad infinitum non invenitur proportio. Quemadmodum itaque, secundum Isaiam, Omnes gentes quasi non sint, sic sunt coram eo, et quasi nihilum et inane reputatæ sunt ei (propter quod dictum est supra, Et substantia mea tanquam nihilum ante te); sic omnis duratio vitæ præsentis, sic est tanquam nihil sit, comparatione durationis vitæ futuræ seu felicitatis æternæ. Propterea admonet Deus ut despiciamus præsentia, transitoria et terrena, inquirentes bona futura, æterna atque cœlestia. Propter quod ait Apostolus: Non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus: et iterum, Festinemus ingredi in illam requiem. Hinc quoque Salomon loquitur: Si multis annis vixerit homo, et in his omnibus lætus fuerit, meminisse debet tenebrosi temporis et dierum multorum: qui quum venerint, vanitatis arguentur præterita. Huic autem versiculo consonat quod scriptum est: Unus dies apud Dominum tanquam mille anni, et mille anni sicut unus dies.
paras.en: And thou hast exhorted man to a wholesome conversion for this reason: [[89:4|For a thousand years in thy sight|Quoniam mille anni ante oculos tuos]], that is, because any temporal duration, or the length of human life, however long it may be, is reckoned by thee, and is short before thee, or in comparison with thy eternity, [[89:4|are as yesterday, which is past|tanquam dies hesterna quæ præteriit]], that is, it is of no moment and is as nothing: for between the finite and the infinite there is found no proportion. And so, just as, according to Isaias, [[Is 40:17|All nations are before him as if they had no being at all, and are counted to him as nothing, and vanity|Omnes gentes quasi non sint, sic sunt coram eo, et quasi nihilum et inane reputatæ sunt ei]] (for which reason it was said above, [[Ps 38:6|and my substance is as nothing before thee|Et substantia mea tanquam nihilum ante te]]), so the whole duration of the present life is as though it were nothing, in comparison with the duration of the life to come, or of eternal happiness. Therefore God admonishes us to despise things present, passing and earthly, seeking the goods to come, eternal and heavenly. For which reason the Apostle says: [[Heb 13:14|we have not here a lasting city: but we seek one that is to come|Non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus]]; and again, [[Heb 4:11|Let us hasten therefore to enter into that rest|Festinemus ingredi in illam requiem]]. Hence too Solomon says: [[Eccles 11:8|If a man live many years, and have rejoiced in them all, he must remember the darksome time, and the many days: which when they shall come, the things past shall be accused of vanity|Si multis annis vixerit homo, et in his omnibus lætus fuerit, meminisse debet tenebrosi temporis et dierum multorum: qui quum venerint, vanitatis arguentur præterita]]. And with this verse agrees what is written: [[2 Pet 3:8|one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day|Unus dies apud Dominum tanquam mille anni, et mille anni sicut unus dies]].

paras.t: Et custodia in nocte. Istud sensum versus præcedentis concernit, ut sit sensus: Mille anni ante oculos tuos sunt tanquam dies hesterna quæ præteriit, et custodia in nocte, id est tanquam custodia noctis, quæ est brevior die, quoniam continet tres horas. Ac si dicat: Non solum duratio vitæ humanæ comparatur diei præteritæ, quæ viginti quatuor horas habet, sed etiam custodiæ noctis continenti tres horas. Et convenienter adjungit similitudinem de custodia noctis continente tres horas, quoniam tantum distat ac deficit duratio vitæ hominum post diluvium a duratione vitæ eorum qui ante diluvium erant, quantum integra dies custodiam noctis excedit: idcirco deberent homines nunc præcipue hanc vitam parvi pendere, et futuram inquirere. Sumitur vero jam custodia pro vigilia: quoniam nox in quatuor vigilias dividitur, quibus antiquitus fiebant excubiæ pro custodia exercitus, a militibus sibi invicem succedentibus per quatuor vices, secundum quatuor vigilias noctis. Aptissime insuper comparat vitam humanam custodiæ noctis, in qua omnia sub obscuritate ac trepidatione geruntur: quoniam tota vita nostra in ignorantia est, et periculosissima nimis.
paras.en: [[89:4|And as a watch in the night|Et custodia in nocte]]. This belongs to the sense of the preceding verse, so that the sense is: A thousand years in thy sight are as yesterday which is past, and as a watch in the night, that is, as a watch of the night, which is shorter than a day, since it contains three hours. As if he said: The duration of human life is compared not only to a past day, which has twenty-four hours, but also to a watch of the night, which contains three hours. And fittingly he adds the likeness of the watch of the night containing three hours, since the duration of men's life after the flood is as far removed from, and falls as far short of, the duration of the life of those who were before the flood, as a whole day exceeds a watch of the night: therefore men ought now above all to esteem this life of little worth, and to seek the life to come. Here watch [custodia, literally "guard"] is taken for vigil: for the night is divided into four vigils, in which in ancient times sentries were kept for the guarding of an army, by soldiers succeeding one another four times over, according to the four vigils of the night. Most aptly, moreover, he compares human life to a watch of the night, in which all things are done in darkness and fear: for our whole life is in ignorance, and exceedingly perilous.

paras.t: Quæ pro nihilo habentur, eorum anni erunt: id est, anni seu tempora vitæ hominum, erunt de numero horum quæ pro nihilo computantur, propter nimiam brevitatem vitæ ipsorum. Propter quod Jacobus ait: Quæ enim est vita vestra? Vapor est ad modicum parens, et deinceps exterminabitur.
paras.en: [[89:5|Things that are counted nothing, shall their years be|Quæ pro nihilo habentur, eorum anni erunt]]: that is, the years or times of men's life will be of the number of those things that are counted for nothing, because of the exceeding shortness of their life. For which reason James says: [[Jas 4:15|For what is your life? It is a vapour which appeareth for a little while and afterwards shall vanish away|Quæ enim est vita vestra? Vapor est ad modicum parens, et deinceps exterminabitur]].

paras.t: Et istud consequenter ostenditur clarius. Mane sicut herba transeunt: id est, prima ætas seu pueritia hominis tam cito percurrat, mutetur, et defluat, sicut herba quæ celeriter decidit; mane prædictum floreat: quia in principio sui temporis est homo quasi in flore, et similis fœno virenti; et transeat, non diu in eodem statu manendo: quemadmodum Job dicit, Homo quasi flos egreditur et conteritur, et fugit velut umbra, et nunquam in eodem statu permanet; vespere, id est senectus seu ultima hominis ætas, decidat a pristina fortitudine, induret, id est, siccetur propter consumptionem humidi radicalis, et arescat, propter defectum naturalis caloris, non valentis reparare deperditum. Unde senes naturaliter sunt sicci ac frigidi.
paras.en: And this is next shown more clearly: [[89:6|In the morning man shall grow up like grass|Mane sicut herba transeunt]] [Denis reads transeunt, "they pass", where the Vulgate has transeat], that is, the first age of man, or childhood, runs its course, is changed and flows away as quickly as grass that soon falls; [[89:6|in the morning he shall flourish|mane prædictum floreat]] (the morning just spoken of), because at the beginning of his time man is as it were in flower, and like green grass; [[89:6|and pass away|et transeat]], not remaining long in the same state: as Job says[[Job 14:1||]], Man [[Job 14:2|cometh forth like a flower, and is destroyed, and fleeth as a shadow, and never continueth in the same state|quasi flos egreditur et conteritur, et fugit velut umbra, et nunquam in eodem statu permanet]]; [[89:6|in the evening|vespere]], that is, old age or the last age of man, [[89:6|he shall fall|decidat]] from his former strength, [[89:6|grow dry|induret]] [literally "harden"], that is, be dried up through the consumption of the radical moisture [humidum radicale: in the old physiology, the native moisture on which life depends], [[89:6|and wither|et arescat]], through the failing of natural heat, which can no longer restore what is lost. Hence old men are naturally dry and cold.

paras.t: Cur autem ista nobis contingant, subjungitur: Quia defecimus a primordiali institutione conditionis humanæ, et solita duratione ætatis paternæ, seu patrum nostrorum qui præcesserunt diluvium, et diu vixerunt, videlicet circa nongentos annos, sicut in Genesi legitur; in ira tua, id est in ultione tua seu propter vindictam tuæ justitiæ: nam propter originale peccatum venimus in hunc statum mortalitatis et vallem lacrimarum, qui alias nati essemus in originali justitia, collocati in paradiso terrestri, fuissemusque immortales per obedientiam facti. Vel ira ista intelligi potest diluvium, quod Deus mundo impiorum induxit, atque ex tunc minorati et abbreviati nimis sunt dies nostri, et debilitata humana complexio. Propter quod Dominus ait: Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est: eruntque dies vitæ illius, centum viginti annorum. Et in furore tuo, id est in multiplici pœna, quam nobis propter originale peccatum et per diluvium induxisti, turbati sumus, id est vehementer afflicti, instabiles facti, formidolosi, atque miseriis pleni. In magna namque mentis tranquillitate creati eramus, quoniam per originalem justitiam subjecta erat in homine caro spiritui, sensualitas rationi, et ratio Deo. Sed homine prævaricante, inflictæ sunt nobis pœnæ diversæ gravesque: quia in carne secutæ sunt infirmitates, passibilitates, et mors; in sensualitate autem, timor, dolor, tristitia; in mente vero, ignorantia, instabilitas, et difficultas ad bene agendum: venitque super nos quod dictum est protoplasto nostro parenti: Maledicta terra in opere tuo. In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo, donec revertaris in terram de qua sumptus es: quia pulvis es, et in pulverem reverteris.
paras.en: Why these things befall us is added next: For [[89:7|we have fainted away|Quia defecimus]] from the first institution of the human condition, and from the accustomed duration of our fathers' age, that is, of our fathers who went before the flood and lived long, namely about nine hundred years, as we read in Genesis[[Gen 5:5||]]; [[89:7|in thy wrath|in ira tua]], that is, in thy vengeance, or because of the punishment of thy justice: for on account of original sin we have come into this state of mortality and vale of tears, we who would otherwise have been born in original justice, set in the earthly paradise, and made immortal through obedience. Or by this wrath may be understood the flood, which God brought upon the world of the wicked; and from then on our days were greatly lessened and shortened, and the human constitution weakened. For which reason the Lord says: [[Gen 6:3|My spirit shall not remain in man for ever, because he is flesh, and his days shall be a hundred and twenty years|Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est: eruntque dies vitæ illius, centum viginti annorum]]. And [[89:7|in thy indignation|in furore tuo]], that is, in the manifold punishment which thou hast brought upon us for original sin and through the flood, [[89:7|are troubled|turbati sumus]], that is, grievously afflicted, made unstable, fearful, and full of miseries. For we had been created in great tranquillity of mind, since through original justice the flesh was subject in man to the spirit, sensuality to reason, and reason to God. But when man transgressed, divers and grievous punishments were inflicted on us: for in the flesh there followed infirmities, passibilities [that is, liability to suffering] and death; in sensuality, fear, grief and sadness; and in the mind, ignorance, instability, and difficulty in doing good: and there came upon us what was said to our first-formed parent: [[Gen 3:17|cursed is the earth in thy work|Maledicta terra in opere tuo]]. [[Gen 3:19|In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread till thou return to the earth out of which thou wast taken: for dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return|In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo, donec revertaris in terram de qua sumptus es: quia pulvis es, et in pulverem reverteris]].

paras.t: Posuisti iniquitates nostras in conspectu tuo, id est, eas non indulsisti, sed considerasti, quatenus justam pœnam pro eis infligeres, quemadmodum per Amos dixisti: Cognovi multa scelera vestra, et fortia peccata vestra; et alibi, Adinventiones eorum coram facie mea factæ sunt. Posuisti et sæculum nostrum, id est opera temporis nostri quo vivimus, in illuminatione vultus tui, id est in lucida inspectione intellectus tui, quatenus unicuique tribuas quod meretur: secundum illud Jeremiæ, Fortissime, cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes filios Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas. Et Ecclesiasticus, Oculi, inquit, Domini multo plus lucidiores sunt super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum.
paras.en: [[89:8|Thou hast set our iniquities before thy eyes|Posuisti iniquitates nostras in conspectu tuo]], that is, thou hast not pardoned them, but hast taken account of them, so as to inflict a just punishment for them, as thou saidst through Amos: [[Amos 5:12|I know your manifold crimes, and your grievous sins|Cognovi multa scelera vestra, et fortia peccata vestra]]; and elsewhere, [[Osee 7:2|their own devices|Adinventiones eorum]], [[Osee 7:2|they have been done before my face|coram facie mea factæ sunt]]. Thou hast set also [[89:8|our life|sæculum nostrum]] [literally "our age"], that is, the works of our time in which we live, [[89:8|in the light of thy countenance|in illuminatione vultus tui]], that is, in the clear regard of thy understanding, so as to give to each what he deserves: according to that of Jeremias, [[Jer 32:18|O most mighty|Fortissime]], [[Jer 32:19|whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the children of Adam, to render unto every one according to his ways|cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes filios Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas]]. And Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 23:28|the eyes|Oculi]], he says, [[Ecclus 23:28|of the Lord are far brighter than the sun, beholding round about all the ways of men|Domini multo plus lucidiores sunt super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum]].

paras.t: Quoniam omnes dies nostri, id est duratio seu operatio vitæ nostræ, defecerunt, id est, abbreviati sunt velociterque consumpti: sicut Job dicit: Dies mei velociores fuerunt cursore; transierunt quasi naves poma portantes. Et scriptum est: Dies nostri quasi umbra super terram, et nulla est mora. Et in ira tua defecimus: sicut jam dictum est atque expositum.
paras.en: [[89:9|For all our days|Quoniam omnes dies nostri]], that is, the duration or the activity of our life, [[89:9|are spent|defecerunt]], that is, are shortened and swiftly consumed: as Job says: [[Job 9:25|My days have been swifter than a post|Dies mei velociores fuerunt cursore]]; [[Job 9:26|They have passed by as ships carrying fruits|transierunt quasi naves poma portantes]]. And it is written: [[1 Par 29:15|Our days upon earth are as a shadow, and there is no stay|Dies nostri quasi umbra super terram, et nulla est mora]]. [[89:9|and in thy wrath we have fainted away|Et in ira tua defecimus]]: as has already been said and explained.

paras.t: Anni nostri sicut aranea meditabuntur. Huic simile est quod dictum est ante, Et tabescere fecisti sicut araneam animam ejus. Est itaque sensus: Anni nostri, id est tempora vitæ nostræ, vel nos ipsi in hoc tempore brevi viventes, meditabuntur sicut aranea, id est, similes esse judicabuntur araneæ: quoniam, sicut aranea semetipsam eviscerat et fatigat, telas formando quatenus muscas capiat, cito tamen opus ejus destruitur, modico scilicet vento flante, et labor ejus cassatur, ipsaque perit: sic homines multipliciter occupantur temporalia congregando, honorem et gloriam sæculi hujus quærendo, et alios opprimendo; et tamen ipsi celeriter moriuntur, labores eorum inutiles efficiuntur, imo incessabiliter tendunt ad casum, quemadmodum sanctus Job asserit: Quasi putredo consumendus sum, et quasi vestimentum quod comeditur a tinea. Unde et alibi dicitur: Omnes morimur, et quasi aquæ dilabimur in terram, quæ non revertuntur.
paras.en: [[89:9|Our years shall be considered as a spider|Anni nostri sicut aranea meditabuntur]] [meditabuntur, literally "shall be meditated"]. Like this is what was said earlier: [[Ps 38:12|And thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider|Et tabescere fecisti sicut araneam animam ejus]]. The sense, then, is: Our years, that is, the times of our life, or we ourselves who live in this brief time, shall be considered as a spider, that is, shall be judged to be like a spider: for as the spider disembowels and wears itself out forming webs to catch flies, yet its work is soon destroyed, when a little wind blows, and its labour comes to nothing, and it itself perishes: so men busy themselves in many ways gathering temporal things, seeking the honour and glory of this world, and oppressing others; and yet they themselves die swiftly, their labours are made useless; nay, they tend unceasingly to their fall, as holy Job asserts: I am one [[Job 13:28|to be consumed as rottenness, and as a garment that is motheaten|Quasi putredo consumendus sum, et quasi vestimentum quod comeditur a tinea]]. Hence it is said elsewhere too: [[2 Kings 14:14|We all die, and like waters that return no more, we fall down into the earth|Omnes morimur, et quasi aquæ dilabimur in terram, quæ non revertuntur]].

paras.t: Dies annorum nostrorum, secundum communem cursum, sunt in ipsis hominibus septuaginta anni: quibus homo vivere potest in fortitudine competenti. Si autem in potentatibus, id est fortibus et bene complexionatis hominibus, inveniantur octoginta anni, et amplius eorum, id est tempus ulterius ætatis, erit labor et dolor: quoniam senex plenus est querelis, et ipsa senectus est velut labor continuus. Istud de communi cursu et lege intelligendum est. Nam et multi ante septuaginta annos ærumnosam ac languidam senectutem incurrunt; aliqui vero post octoginta annos satis robuste atque hilariter vivunt.
paras.en: [[89:10|The days of our years|Dies annorum nostrorum]], according to the common course, are, [[89:10|in them|in ipsis]], that is, in men, [[89:10|threescore and ten years|septuaginta anni]]: in which a man can live in fitting strength. [[89:10|But if in the strong|Si autem in potentatibus]], that is, in strong men of sound constitution, there be found [[89:10|fourscore years|octoginta anni]], [[89:10|what is more of them|et amplius eorum]], that is, the further time of their age, will be [[89:10|labour and sorrow|labor et dolor]]: for an old man is full of complaints, and old age itself is as it were a continual labour. This is to be understood of the common course and rule. For many fall into a toilsome and languid old age before seventy years; while some live robustly and cheerfully enough after eighty.

paras.t: Sanctus Thomas allegat hos duos versiculos, ad ostendendum quod vita hominum ante diluvium tam prolixa fuit potius ex divina virtute, seu miraculose, quam ex causa naturali; adducitque ad hoc, illud quod de Berzellai scriptum est: Erat autem Berzellai Galaadites senex valde, id est octogenarius. Et confirmatur idem per hoc, quod de David inducitur: Rex David senuerat, habebatque ætatis plurimos annos: et tamen David septuagenarius obiit. Asserit quoque Thomas, David hos versus de tempore suo scripsisse. Et ita secundum Thomam, David est auctor psalmi præsentis: ex quo sequi videtur, quod Thomas senserit omnes psalmos a David conscriptos.
paras.en: St Thomas cites these two verses [the two halves of v. 10, numbered as two verses in Denis's text] to show that the life of men before the flood was so long rather by divine power, that is, miraculously, than from a natural cause; and he adduces for this what is written of Berzellai: [[2 Kings 19:32|Now Berzellai the Galaadite was of a great age, that is to say, fourscore years old|Erat autem Berzellai Galaadites senex valde, id est octogenarius]]. And the same is confirmed by what is related of David: [[3 Kings 1:1|king David was old, and advanced in years|Rex David senuerat, habebatque ætatis plurimos annos]]: and yet David died at seventy. Thomas also asserts that David wrote these verses about his own time. And so according to Thomas David is the author of the present psalm: from which it seems to follow that Thomas held all the psalms to have been written by David.

paras.t: Hanc autem vitæ abbreviationem et temporalem pœnam nobis induxisti, Quoniam supervenit mansuetudo, id est, quia judicio tuo clementiam addidisti, per quam rigorem tuæ justitiæ temperasti. Meruerunt namque homines penitus destrui ac damnari: sed pro totali destructione inducta est decurtatio vitæ; pro damnatione vero perpetua, temporalis afflictio. Et corripiemur per has tuas castigationes mansuete inflictas, cavendo de cetero a peccatis, ne graviora patiamur flagella.
paras.en: And thou hast brought this shortening of life and this temporal punishment upon us [[89:10|For mildness is come upon us|Quoniam supervenit mansuetudo]], that is, because thou hast added clemency to thy judgment, by which thou hast tempered the rigour of thy justice. For men deserved to be utterly destroyed and damned: but in place of total destruction a cutting short of life was brought in, and in place of perpetual damnation, temporal affliction. [[89:10|and we shall be corrected|Et corripiemur]] by these thy chastisements, mildly inflicted, guarding ourselves henceforth from sins, lest we suffer heavier scourges.

paras.t: Quis novit, sine tua speciali illustratione, potestatem iræ tuæ, id est virtutem justitiæ tuæ, et ultionum tuarum rigorem? et quis novit præ timore tuo, id est præ metuendo tuo judicio, seu præ timore proprii cordis de tua majestate concepto, iram tuam dinumerare, id est omnes pœnas, peccatoribus a tua justitia præparatas, mensurare aut explicare? quasi dicat, Nemo. Incomprehensibilia namque sunt opera divinæ justitiæ, quibus in peccatoribus operatur. Quorumdam enim pœna nunc incipit, et in futuro continuatur: aliorum nunc inchoatur, et in futuro sæculo desinit: aliorum pœna modo differtur, quatenus in æternum continuetur. Quis autem ista discernere valet, et cur singula singulis accidant considerare, nisi quem Deus supernaturaliter mirabiliterque docuerit? Elucescit ex his, quia sancti homines nonnunquam, præ nimio timore majestatis divinæ, deficiunt a contemplatione divinæ justitiæ. Nam et timor vehemens actum rationis locutionemque impedit. Propter quod in libro Job habetur: Pavor ejus non me terreat; neque enim possum metuens respondere. Verumtamen moderata afflictio timoris sive tristitiæ, confert interdum ad veritatis notitiam adipiscendam, in quantum dissolutionem et excessivam libertatem et hilaritatem excludit. Unde Isaias inducit: Domine, in angustia requisierunt te, in tribulatione murmuris doctrina tua eis.
paras.en: [[89:11|Who knoweth|Quis novit]], without thy special enlightenment, [[89:11|the power of thy anger|potestatem iræ tuæ]], that is, the might of thy justice and the rigour of thy vengeances? And who knoweth how, [[89:11|for thy fear|præ timore tuo]], that is, for dread of thy judgment, or for the fear of thy majesty that one's own heart has conceived, to [[89:12|number thy wrath|iram tuam dinumerare]], that is, to measure or set forth all the punishments prepared for sinners by thy justice? As if he said: No one. For incomprehensible are the works of divine justice which it works in sinners[[Rom 11:33||]]. For the punishment of some begins now and is continued in the future[[1 Tim 5:24||]]; that of others is begun now and ends in the world to come [that is, in purgatory]; that of others is put off for the present, so that it may be continued for ever. But who can discern these things, and consider why each befalls each, unless one whom God has taught supernaturally and wonderfully? From this it is clear that holy men sometimes, for exceeding fear of the divine majesty, fail in the contemplation of divine justice[[Job 6:4||]]. For vehement fear hinders the act of reason and speech. For which reason it is said in the book of Job: [[Job 9:34|let not his fear terrify me|Pavor ejus non me terreat]]; [[Job 9:35|for I cannot answer while I am in fear|neque enim possum metuens respondere]]. Yet a moderate affliction of fear or sadness sometimes helps towards attaining knowledge of the truth, inasmuch as it shuts out dissoluteness and excessive freedom and mirth. Hence Isaias brings in: [[Is 26:16|Lord, they have sought after thee in distress, in the tribulation of murmuring thy instruction was with them|Domine, in angustia requisierunt te, in tribulatione murmuris doctrina tua eis]].

paras.t: Insuper pro illuminatione divina orat, dicendo: Dexteram tuam, id est potestatem divinam et ejus correctionem terribilem, sic notam fac nobis jam per fidei contemplationem sinceram, a Spiritu Sancto infusam, quatenus eam veneremur, et ejus iram seu pœnam formidemus, dicentes ex animo illud Apocalypsis: Justæ et veræ sunt viæ tuæ, Rex sæculorum. Quis non timebit te, et magnificabit nomen tuum? Fac quoque nos homines et eruditos corde in sapientia legis divinæ: quoniam, Omnis sapientia a Domino Deo est; et, Beatus homo quem tu erudieris, Domine.
paras.en: Moreover he prays for divine enlightenment, saying: [[89:12|thy right hand|Dexteram tuam]], that is, the divine power and its terrible correction, [[89:12|So make|sic notam fac]] known to us now through a sincere contemplation of faith, infused by the Holy Ghost, so that we may revere it and dread its wrath or punishment, saying from the heart those words of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 15:3|Just and true are thy ways, O King of ages|Justæ et veræ sunt viæ tuæ, Rex sæculorum]]. [[Apoc 15:4|Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and magnify thy name?|Quis non timebit te, et magnificabit nomen tuum?]] Make us also [[89:12|men learned in heart, in wisdom|eruditos corde in sapientia]] of the divine law: for [[Ecclus 1:1|All wisdom is from the Lord God|Omnis sapientia a Domino Deo est]]; and, [[Ps 93:12|Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord|Beatus homo quem tu erudieris, Domine]].

paras.t: Convertere, Domine, sine tui mutatione, convertendo me ad te, et clementer respiciendo in me, usquequo, id est, non cessando ab hac conversione, donec ad ultimum finem pertingam. Vel, Aliquantulum, ut alia translatio habet, id est modicum: quoniam quantumcumque parum de gratia tua præstiteris mihi, ego illud pro magno habebo. Vel, Aliquantulum, id est, tribulationes meas mitiga atque diminue; non penitus tolle, quoniam tribulatio necessaria est electis. Et deprecabilis esto super servos tuos, non differendo nec indignando propter eorum peccata, sed cito ac dulciter succurrendo secundum misericordiam tuam. Versiculus iste efficacissimam, affectuosissimam ac devotissimam continet precem: quem tanto ardentius quanto frequentius dicere, corde attento et affectu vim verborum gustante, debemus.
paras.en: [[89:13|Return, O Lord|Convertere, Domine]], without change in thyself, by turning me to thee and looking mercifully upon me, [[89:13|how long|usquequo]], that is, not ceasing from this turning until I reach my last end. Or, A little while [aliquantulum, in place of usquequo], as another translation has it, that is, a little: for however little of thy grace thou grantest me, I shall hold it for much. Or, A little while, that is, soften and lessen my tribulations; do not take them away altogether, for tribulation is necessary for the elect. [[89:13|and be entreated in favour of thy servants|Et deprecabilis esto super servos tuos]], not delaying, nor being angered because of their sins, but succouring them quickly and sweetly according to thy mercy. This verse contains a most efficacious, most loving and most devout prayer: which we ought to say the more ardently the more often we say it, with an attentive heart and an affection that tastes the force of the words.

paras.t: Repleti sumus mane, id est cito, misericordia tua: quia quam cito corde sincero te invocamus, plus quam meremur recipimus. Vel, Mane, id est in spirituali aurora seu spiritualis diei principio: quando videlicet Sol justitiæ Christus Dominus lucem gratiæ imprimit mentibus nostris. Vel, Mane, id est hora resurrectionis dominicæ, et hora missionis Spiritus Sancti: quia et Christus mane surrexit, et Spiritus Sanctus in die Pentecostes mane super discipulos visibiliter venit: tuncque repleti sumus misericordia Dei, quoniam Christus (secundum Apostolum) resurrexit propter justificationem nostram; et illa Paracleti missio, erat totius mundi illustratio. Et exsultavimus, id est, signa lætitiæ foris ostendimus, et delectati sumus interius. Vel, Exsultavimus secundum intellectualem appetitum, et delectati sumus secundum appetitum sensitivum per redundantiam intellectualis exsultationis in ipsum, sicut superius dictum est: Cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum, id est appetitus superior atque inferior. In omnibus diebus nostris, id est certis horis omnium dierum quibus in gratia viximus: eo modo quo ait Apostolus, Semper gaudete; et, In omnibus gratias agite; et, Cantate et psallite Domino in cordibus vestris semper. Homines namque virtuosi non solum gaudent in prosperis, sed etiam in adversis, quemadmodum Christus hortatur: Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate.
paras.en: [[89:14|We are filled in the morning|Repleti sumus mane]], that is, quickly, [[89:14|with thy mercy|misericordia tua]]: for as soon as we call upon thee with a sincere heart, we receive more than we deserve. Or, In the morning, that is, in the spiritual dawn, or the beginning of the spiritual day: namely when the Sun of justice, Christ the Lord, imprints the light of grace on our minds. Or, In the morning, that is, at the hour of the Lord's resurrection, and the hour of the sending of the Holy Ghost: for Christ rose in the morning[[Mark 16:9||]], and the Holy Ghost came visibly upon the disciples in the morning on the day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:3||]][[Acts 2:15||]]: and then were we filled with the mercy of God, since Christ (according to the Apostle) [[Rom 4:25|rose again for our justification|resurrexit propter justificationem nostram]]; and that sending of the Paraclete was the enlightening of the whole world.
