[[89:14|and we have rejoiced|Et exsultavimus]], that is, we have shown signs of gladness outwardly, [[89:14|and are delighted|et delectati sumus]] inwardly. Or, We have rejoiced according to the intellectual appetite, and are delighted according to the sensitive appetite, through the overflowing of intellectual rejoicing into it, as was said above: [[Ps 83:3|My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God|Cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum]], that is, the higher and the lower appetite. [[89:14|all our days|In omnibus diebus nostris]], that is, at set hours of all the days in which we have lived in grace: in the way in which the Apostle says, [[1 Thess 5:16|Always rejoice|Semper gaudete]]; and, [[1 Thess 5:18|In all things give thanks|In omnibus gratias agite]]; and, [[Eph 5:19|singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord|Cantate et psallite Domino in cordibus vestris semper]] [Denis gives this freely: "Sing and make melody to the Lord in your hearts always"]. For virtuous men rejoice not only in prosperity but also in adversity, as Christ exhorts: [[Luke 6:23|Be glad in that day and rejoice|Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate]] [no reference in the margin; Denis has "in that hour" for "in that day"].

paras.t: Lætati sumus pro diebus quibus nos humiliasti, id est, humiliari, tentari et opprimi permisisti, scilicet pro annis quibus vidimus, id est experti sumus, mala pœnæ. Magna quippe est ratio exsultandi in Deo, sustinuisse patienter adversa et aspera: quoniam hoc est signum prædestinationis æternæ, eo quod Scriptura dicat, Beatus vir qui suffert tentationem; et, Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino; et, Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam; et, Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo.
paras.en: [[89:15|We have rejoiced for the days in which thou hast humbled us|Lætati sumus pro diebus quibus nos humiliasti]], that is, hast permitted us to be humbled, tempted and oppressed: namely [[89:15|for the years in which we have seen|annis quibus vidimus]], that is, experienced, [[89:15|evils|mala]] of punishment. For it is a great reason for rejoicing in God to have patiently borne adversities and hardships: since this is a sign of eternal predestination, because the Scripture says, [[Jas 1:12|Blessed is the man that endureth temptation|Beatus vir qui suffert tentationem]]; and, [[Job 5:17|Blessed is the man whom God correcteth|Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino]]; and, [[Matt 5:10|Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake|Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam]]; and, [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]].

paras.t: Quidam hos versus exponunt de Ecclesia triumphanti, exponendo præteritum pro futuro, et per Mane, intelligentes horam resurrectionis futuræ: nec dubium est, quin hoc modo versiculi isti plenius competant Beatis in patria, quam electis in via. In Beatis namque est misericordia consummata, incessabilisque lætitia, atque jucunda præteritarum tribulationum memoria.
paras.en: Some expound these verses of the Church triumphant, taking the past for the future, and understanding by [[89:14|in the morning|Mane]] the hour of the resurrection to come: and there is no doubt that in this way these verses befit the Blessed in the fatherland more fully than the elect on the way [in patria … in via: those already in heaven, and those still on the journey of this life]. For in the Blessed there is mercy made complete, and unceasing gladness, and the sweet memory of past tribulations.

paras.t: Respice oculo pietatis paternæ in servos tuos et in opera tua, id est in servos tuos qui sunt opera manuum tuarum. Vel, In opera tua, id est operationes tuas, per quas gratiam facis in eis: quemadmodum in Isaia habetur, Omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis. Apostolus quoque: Deus, inquit, est qui operatur in vobis et velle et perficere pro bona voluntate. Hæc opera sunt tua et nostra. Tua sunt, quia a te principaliter procedentia; et nostra, quia per nos facta. Respice, conservando perficiendoque ea in vitam æternam; et dirige, gratia duce, in vitam æternam, filios eorum, videlicet servorum tuorum.
paras.en: [[89:16|Look upon|Respice]] with the eye of fatherly love [[89:16|thy servants and upon their works|in servos tuos et in opera tua]] [the Latin is in opera tua, "upon thy works", and Denis expounds it so], that is, upon thy servants, who are the works of thy hands. Or, Upon thy works, that is, thy operations, by which thou workest grace in them: as is said in Isaias, [[Is 26:12|thou hast wrought all our works for us|Omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis]]. And the Apostle: [[Phil 2:13|For it is God|Deus]], he says, [[Phil 2:13|who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish, according to his good will|est qui operatur in vobis et velle et perficere pro bona voluntate]]. These works are thine and ours: thine, because they proceed from thee as their first source; and ours, because they are done through us. [[89:16|Look|Respice]] upon them, preserving and perfecting them unto life everlasting; [[89:16|and direct|et dirige]], with grace for guide, unto life everlasting, [[89:16|their children|filios eorum]], namely those of thy servants.

paras.t: Ut autem hoc fiat, oro: Et sit splendor Domini Dei nostri super nos, id est, gratia tua semper cordibus nostris effulgeat: sicut Ecclesiasticus dicit, Miserere nostri, Deus omnium, et respice nos, et ostende nobis lucem miserationum tuarum. Et opera manuum nostrarum, id est operationes nostras interiores et exteriores, quæ a viribus operativis causantur, quæ nomine manuum designantur, dirige super nos, id est in finem supernaturalem, in vitam æternam, ad tui ipsius honorem et gloriam: quatenus non hominibus, sed tibi in omnibus complacere optemus, et præmium supercœleste pro nostro labore adipisci curemus et intendamus.
paras.en: And that this may come about, I pray: [[89:17|And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us|Et sit splendor Domini Dei nostri super nos]], that is, may thy grace ever shine forth in our hearts: as Ecclesiasticus says, [[Ecclus 36:1|Have mercy upon us, O God of all, and behold us, and shew us the light of thy mercies|Miserere nostri, Deus omnium, et respice nos, et ostende nobis lucem miserationum tuarum]]. And [[89:17|the works of our hands|opera manuum nostrarum]], that is, our inward and outward operations, which are caused by the operative powers that are signified by the name of hands, [[89:17|direct thou|dirige]] [[89:17|over us|super nos]], that is, to the supernatural end, unto life everlasting, to the honour and glory of thyself: so that we may desire to please not men but thee in all things, and may take care and strive to gain a heavenly reward for our labour.

paras.t: Et opus manuum nostrarum dirige. Postquam pluraliter supplicavit opera sua dirigi, quid necesse jam est singulariter exorare ut opus dirigatur, nisi quod actum caritatis præsertim et summe dirigi cupit? quoniam actu caritatis manente, ceterarum virtutum permanent opera; actu autem caritatis cessante, omnia opera meritoria cessant, quoniam sine actu caritatis, nullius actus virtutis meretur vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[89:17|yea, the work of our hands do thou direct|Et opus manuum nostrarum dirige]]. Since he has already prayed in the plural that his works be directed, what need is there now to pray in the singular that the work be directed, unless that he desires above all, and in the highest degree, that the act of charity be directed? For while the act of charity remains, the works of the other virtues remain; but when the act of charity ceases, all meritorious works cease, since without the act of charity no act of any virtue merits life everlasting.

paras.t: Ecce inclytum psalmum audivimus: cujus primus versiculus, est versus magnæ fiduciæ atque caritatis præcipuæ. Debemus namque ad Dominum Deum nostrum cum omni fiducia ac dilectione confugere, sicut ad patrem et salvatorem. Unde Salvator ait: Si vos quum sitis mali, nostis bona data dare filiis vestris: quanto magis Pater vester cœlestis dabit spiritum bonum petentibus se? Studeamus ergo ex documentis psalmi præsentis, vitæ nostræ brevitatem pensare, æternæ felicitatis indeficientes dies appetere, ab omni sæculari amore atque carnali affectu, vana sollicitudine et inquieta perturbatione corda nostra purgare: quatenus splendoris gratiæ Dei semper capaciores reddamur, moxque finito hujus exsilii incolatu, ad lumen gloriæ intromittamur.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a glorious psalm, whose first verse is a verse of great confidence and of special charity. For we ought to flee to the Lord our God with all confidence and love, as to a father and saviour. Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 11:13|If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father from heaven give the good Spirit to them that ask him?|Si vos quum sitis mali, nostis bona data dare filiis vestris: quanto magis Pater vester cœlestis dabit spiritum bonum petentibus se?]] Let us then strive, from the teachings of the present psalm, to weigh the shortness of our life, to long for the unfailing days of eternal happiness, and to cleanse our hearts of all worldly love and carnal affection, of vain care and restless disturbance: so that we may be made ever more able to receive the splendour of God's grace, and soon, when our sojourn in this exile is ended, may be admitted to the light of glory.

paras.t: Precatio. Sis, Domine, nostrum ubique refugium, qui es Deus a sæculo et usque in sæculum; respice clementer in nos servos tuos, et sit splendor divinitatis tuæ super nos: ut opera nostra a te semper dirigantur, et cœpta per te finiantur.
paras.en: Prayer. Be thou, O Lord, our refuge everywhere, who art God from eternity and unto eternity; look mercifully upon us thy servants, and let the brightness of thy Godhead be upon us: that our works may ever be directed by thee, and what has been begun may be finished through thee.

90.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI NONAGESIMI : QUI HABITAT IN ADJUTORIO ALTISSIMI.
90.title_en: Exposition of the ninetieth psalm: He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High.

paras.t: Adscribitur psalmo jam pertractando hic titulus: Laus cantici, ipsi David: id est, in psalmo hoc continetur laus spiritualis jucunditatis, conveniens ipsi David, et cuilibet fideli per David significato. Agit enim hic psalmus de tentationibus variis generis humani: quarum victor in hoc psalmo laudatur, et de æterna jucunditate per promissionem Dei certus efficitur. Refert autem Nicolaus de Lyra, quod psalmus iste cum psalmis sequentibus usque ad psalmum centesimum, qui incipit, Misericordiam et judicium, etc., in Hebræo titulo caret, et quod titulus iste ab aliquo expositore secundum propriam voluntatem appositus sit. Asserit quoque, quod psalmus iste cum sequentibus usque ad psalmum centesimum, a Moyse factus sit, secundum Hebræos. Hæc autem doctoribus catholicis dissonant. Credendum est namque, titulos psalmorum ab aliquo Sancto ex divina inspiratione formatos: sed et sancti doctores pene omnes, allegando verba horum psalmorum, frequenter sanctum David commemorant tanquam auctorem eorum.
paras.en: To the psalm now to be treated this title is prefixed: [[90:1|The praise of a canticle for David|Laus cantici, ipsi David]]: that is, this psalm contains the praise of spiritual gladness, befitting David himself, and every faithful soul signified by David. For this psalm treats of the various temptations of mankind: the victor over them is praised in this psalm, and is made certain of eternal gladness by the promise of God. Now Nicholas of Lyra relates that this psalm, with the psalms that follow up to the hundredth psalm, which begins [[Ps 100:1|Mercy and judgment|Misericordiam et judicium]], etc., has no title in the Hebrew, and that this title was put to it by some expositor at his own pleasure. He also asserts that this psalm, with those that follow up to the hundredth psalm, was made by Moses, according to the Hebrews. But these things are at variance with the Catholic doctors. For it is to be believed that the titles of the psalms were composed by some saint by divine inspiration; and moreover nearly all the holy doctors, when they allege the words of these psalms, often name holy David as their author.

paras.t: Ait ergo: Qui habitat in adjutorio Altissimi, id est homo mentem suam in Deo stabiliens, innitendo auxilio gratiæ ejus, quemadmodum Isaias dicit: Quis ambulat in tenebris, et non est lumen ei? Speret in nomine Domini, et innitatur super Deum suum. Et Salomon: Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo, et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ. Hic talis in protectione Dei cæli commorabitur, id est, a Deo stabiliter protegetur. Sicut enim in adjutorio Dei habitat sperans ab eo adjuvari; sic in protectione Dei cæli commorabitur effectum spei adipiscendo, quoniam Deus protector est omnium sperantium in se, juxta illud: Respicite, filii, nationes hominum, et scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino et confusus est. Ad hoc itaque ut mereamur a Deo cælorum defendi, non sufficit transitorie seu instabiliter ejus subventioni inniti; sed debemus in adjutorio Altissimi habitare, id est fixo animo permanere, pensantes nos ejus ope incessabiliter indigere, quemadmodum ait Filius Dei: Sine me nihil potestis facere. Nequaquam enim permittimur in nobismetipsis seu propriis meritis viribusque confidere, si verum esse fatemur quod ait divinus Apostolus, Gratia Dei sum id quod sum; et rursus, Non sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Idcirco Christus, Qui manet, inquit, in me, et ego in eo, hic fert fructum multum.
paras.en: He says, then: [[90:1|He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High|Qui habitat in adjutorio Altissimi]], that is, the man who makes his mind steadfast in God, leaning upon the help of his grace; as Isaias says: Who [[Is 50:10|hath walked in darkness, and hath no light? let him hope in the name of the Lord, and lean upon his God|ambulat in tenebris, et non est lumen ei? Speret in nomine Domini, et innitatur super Deum suum]] [the margin gives Is. i, 10; the words are Is 50:10]. And Solomon: [[Prov 3:5|Have confidence in the Lord with all thy heart, and lean not upon thy own prudence.|Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo, et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ]] Such a one [[90:1|shall abide under the protection|in protectione Dei cæli commorabitur]] of the God of heaven [the Vulgate reads *Dei cæli*, "of the God of heaven", where the Douay-Rheims has "of the God of Jacob"], that is, he shall be steadfastly protected by God. For as he dwells in the aid of God who hopes to be helped by him, so he shall abide under the protection of the God of heaven by obtaining the effect of his hope; since God [[Ps 17:31|is the protector of all that trust in him|protector est omnium sperantium in se]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxi, 11; the words are those of Ps 17:31], according to that saying: [[Ecclus 2:11|My children behold the generations of men: and know ye that no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded.|Respicite, filii, nationes hominum, et scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino et confusus est]] And so, that we may deserve to be defended by the God of heaven, it is not enough to lean upon his succour in passing or unsteadily; but we must dwell in the aid of the most High, that is, abide with a fixed mind, considering that we need his help unceasingly, as the Son of God says: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]. For we are by no means allowed to trust in ourselves, or in our own merits and strength, if we confess that what the divine Apostle says is true: [[1 Cor 15:10|by the grace of God, I am what I am|Gratia Dei sum id quod sum]]; and again: [[2 Cor 3:5|Not that we are sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God|Non sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]. Therefore Christ: [[John 15:5|He that abideth|Qui manet]], he says, [[John 15:5|in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruit|in me, et ego in eo, hic fert fructum multum]].

paras.t: Sciendum vero est, quod quidam sunt homines in Deo non sperantes, alii sunt de Deo desperantes, alii autem sunt in Deo frustra sperantes. Qui enim confidunt in vanitatibus suis, in propriis viribus, meritis seu divitiis, non in Deo, sed in se ipsis sperant. Qui autem sine operibus in Deo sperat, inaniter sperat. Habitemus igitur semper, quantumcumque profecerimus, in adjutorio Altissimi, omnem profectum et perfectionem nostram suæ misericordissimæ bonitati, devotione plenissima adscribentes, atque cum Isaia dicentes, A facie tua, Domine, concepimus, et quasi parturivimus et peperimus spiritum; et iterum, Tantum in te recordemur nominis tui. Ad hoc namque inducit nos Deus apertissime per Osee, dicens: Perditio tua, Israel, ex te; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum.
paras.en: But it must be known that some men do not hope in God, others despair of God, and others hope in God in vain. For those who trust in their own vanities, in their own strength, merits or riches, hope not in God but in themselves. And he who hopes in God without works hopes emptily. Let us therefore always dwell, however far we have advanced, in the aid of the most High, ascribing all our progress and perfection with fullest devotion to his most merciful goodness, and saying with Isaias: [[Is 26:17|in thy presence, O Lord|A facie tua, Domine]], [[Is 26:18|We have conceived, and been as it were in labour, and have brought forth wind|concepimus, et quasi parturivimus et peperimus spiritum]] [the Latin *spiritum* is both "wind" and "spirit"; Denis takes it in the second sense]; and again: [[Is 26:13|only in thee let us remember thy name|Tantum in te recordemur nominis tui]]. For to this God leads us most plainly through Osee, saying: [[Osee 13:9|Destruction is thy own, O Israel: thy help is only in me.|Perditio tua, Israel, ex te; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum]]

paras.t: Dicet Domino homo taliter in adjutorio Dei habitans: Susceptor meus es tu, id est orationum mearum pius auditor, meæ infirmitatis clemens curator, mei pœnitentis atque ad te redeuntis clementissimis brachiis misericordiæ amplexator, et refugium meum, quoniam ad te in omni periculo, necessitate et indigentia secure confugio, sicut ad patrem ac salvatorem. Deus meus. Omnium quidem generaliter Deus es, tanquam omnium conditor et provisor, sed specialiter Deus meus: primo, ex parte tui, propter specialem pietatem et gratiam quam mihi impendis; secundo, ex parte mei, propter specialem dilectionem et cultum quibus tibi adhæreo, teque honoro, et summe ac unice colo. Sperabo in eum: non in homine puro, quoniam maledictus vir qui confidit in homine; nec in aliqua pura creatura: sed in te, sperans per opem et gratiam tuam omne malum evadere, omne bonum acquirere. Scriptum est namque: Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino, et erit Dominus fiducia ejus.
paras.en: [[90:2|He shall say to the Lord|Dicet Domino]], the man who thus dwells in the aid of God: [[90:2|Thou art my protector|Susceptor meus es tu]] [*susceptor*: literally "one who takes up" or "receives", which Denis's gloss draws out], that is, the loving hearer of my prayers, the merciful healer of my infirmity, who embraces me, penitent and returning to thee, in the most gentle arms of mercy; [[90:2|and my refuge|et refugium meum]], because in every danger, need and want I flee to thee securely, as to a father and saviour. [[90:2|My God|Deus meus]]. Thou art indeed the God of all in general, as the maker and provider of all, but in a special way my God: first, on thy part, because of the special kindness and grace which thou bestowest on me; secondly, on my part, because of the special love and worship with which I cleave to thee, and honour thee, and worship thee supremely and alone. [[90:2|in him will I trust|Sperabo in eum]]: not in mere man, for [[Jer 17:5|Cursed be the man that trusteth in man|maledictus vir qui confidit in homine]]; nor in any mere creature: but in thee, hoping through thy help and grace to escape every evil and to gain every good. For it is written: [[Jer 17:7|Blessed be the man that trusteth in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his confidence.|Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino, et erit Dominus fiducia ejus]] [the margin's book is unread (Ps. […] 7); the words are Jer 17:7]

paras.t: Sperabo autem in eum, Quoniam ipse per gratiam liberabit me de laqueo, id est a deceptione atque pestifera infectione, venantium, id est iniquorum, ad peccata quibus anima captivatur ac moritur, inducentium. Venatores namque hic appellantur, qui currunt et satagunt fallere animas, easque a Deo avertere, ac per hoc privare gratia in præsenti, et gloria in futuro. Hi vero venatores, non solum sunt dæmones, sed eorum quoque imitatores, homines reprobi: de quibus scriptum est, Invidia diaboli, mors introivit in orbem terrarum. Imitantur autem illum, qui sunt ex parte illius. Unde legitur: Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem. Laqueus vero nunc dicitur id, quo anima dæmonum servituti subjicitur, ab hostibus suæ salutis capitur, vinculisque æternæ mortis ligatur. Hoc autem nihil aliud est, nisi mortale peccatum. Propter quod Apostolus laqueum istum interdum singulariter exprimit, nominans eum avaritiam: Qui, inquit, volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli. Interdum vero exprimit eum pluraliter, intelligendo quæcumque peccata mortalia nomine laqueorum, sicut quum ait: Det illis Deus pœnitentiam, ut resipiscant a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem. Unde de his laqueis, quibus anima miserabiliter irretitur et spiritualiter moritur, in Evangelio asseritur: Ærumnæ sæculi et deceptio divitiarum, et circa reliqua concupiscentiæ, introeuntes in cor, suffocant verbum; et sine fructu efficitur. Quid ergo est, Ipse liberabit me de laqueo venantium, nisi, Ipse per misericordiam suam eripiet me, atque salvabit ab insidiis hostium visibilium et invisibilium? juxta illud: Erit Omnipotens contra hostes tuos.
paras.en: And I will trust in him, [[90:3|For he|Quoniam ipse]] by grace [[90:3|hath delivered me from the snare|liberabit me de laqueo]] [Denis reads *liberabit*, "will deliver", where the Vulgate has *liberavit*, "hath delivered"], that is, from the deceit and pestilent infection [[90:3|of the hunters|venantium]], that is, of the wicked, who lead men on to the sins by which the soul is taken captive and dies. For those are here called hunters who run [a footnote gives the reading *curant*, "take pains"] and busy themselves to deceive souls and turn them away from God, and thereby to deprive them of grace in the present and of glory in the future. And these hunters are not only the demons but also their imitators, reprobate men, of whom it is written: [[Wis 2:24|by the envy of the devil, death came into the world|Invidia diaboli, mors introivit in orbem terrarum]]. [[Wis 2:25|And they follow him that are of his side|Imitantur autem illum, qui sunt ex parte illius]] [*imitantur*: literally "they imitate"]. Hence we read: [[Mich 7:2|every one hunteth his brother to death|Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem]]. Now the snare here means that by which the soul is made subject to the bondage of the demons, is caught by the enemies of its salvation, and is bound with the chains of eternal death. And this is nothing else but mortal sin. For this reason the Apostle sometimes names this snare in the singular, calling it avarice: They, he says, [[1 Tim 6:9|that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli]]. But sometimes he names it in the plural, understanding by the name of snares any mortal sins whatever, as when he says: [[2 Tim 2:25|God may give them repentance|Det illis Deus pœnitentiam]], that [[2 Tim 2:26|they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil by whom they are held captive at his will|ut resipiscant a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem]]. Hence of these snares, by which the soul is wretchedly entangled and dies spiritually, it is said in the Gospel: [[Mark 4:19|the cares of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts after other things entering in choke the word, and it is made fruitless|Ærumnæ sæculi et deceptio divitiarum, et circa reliqua concupiscentiæ, introeuntes in cor, suffocant verbum; et sine fructu efficitur]] [Denis adds "into the heart" after "entering in"]. What then does [[90:3|he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters|Ipse liberabit me de laqueo venantium]] mean, but: He will rescue me by his mercy, and save me from the ambushes of enemies visible and invisible? according to that saying: [[Job 22:25|the Almighty shall be against thy enemies|Erit Omnipotens contra hostes tuos]].

paras.t: Liberabit insuper me et a verbo aspero, id est ab omni sermone nocivo contra me dicto, ita ut non fiam impatiens, dum alii me irrident, calumniantur, vituperant. Deridetur enim justi simplicitas, et vitam justorum perversi sermonibus impii lacerant. Sed gratia Dei juvante non conturbamur in his, imo lætamur, pensantes quod ait Salvator: Beati eritis quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes, propter me. Gloriari namque debemus, dum insurgit in nos imprudentium contumeliosa loquacitas, quoniam conformamur aliqualiter Domino nostro Jesu Christo, qui ait: Opprobria exprobrantium tibi, ceciderunt super me; et, Omnes videntes me, deriserunt me. Cui frequenter dixerunt Judæi: Dæmonium habet et insanit: homo vorax, amicus peccatorum: et, In principe dæmoniorum dæmonia ejicit. Vel, A verbo aspero, id est a sententia judicis, qui dicet in die judicii impiis verbum illud asperrimum: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum.
paras.en: He will deliver me besides [[90:3|from the sharp word|et a verbo aspero]], that is, from every harmful speech spoken against me, so that I do not become impatient while others mock, slander and revile me. For [[Job 12:4|the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn|Deridetur enim justi simplicitas]], and the perverse and wicked tear the life of the just with their words. But with the help of God's grace we are not troubled at these things; rather we rejoice, considering what the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:11|Blessed are ye when they shall revile you, and persecute you, and speak all that is evil against you, untruly, for my sake|Beati eritis quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes, propter me]]. For we ought to glory when the insulting talk of the foolish rises up against us, since we are in some measure conformed to our Lord Jesus Christ, who says: [[Ps 68:10|the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me|Opprobria exprobrantium tibi, ceciderunt super me]]; and: [[Ps 21:8|All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn|Omnes videntes me, deriserunt me]]. To him the Jews often said: [[John 10:20|He hath a devil and is mad|Dæmonium habet et insanit]]; [[Matt 11:19|a man that is a glutton|homo vorax]], a friend of [[Matt 11:19|sinners|peccatorum]]; and: [[Matt 9:34|By the prince of devils he casteth out devils|In principe dæmoniorum dæmonia ejicit]]. Or, [[90:3|from the sharp word|A verbo aspero]], that is, from the sentence of the Judge, who on the day of judgment will say to the wicked that most bitter word: [[Matt 25:41|Depart|Ite]], [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]].

paras.t: Scapulis suis obumbrabit tibi. Per scapulas Dei, intelligit potestatem divinam electos protegentem. Est igitur sensus: Scapulis suis, id est potestate sua benigna, obumbrabit tibi, id est, ab æstu tentationis et igne persecutionis refrigerabit alleviabitque te: sicut infra dicitur, Obumbrasti super caput meum in die belli. Unde Apostolus dicit: Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra. Et sub pennis ejus, id est sub alis ipsius, videlicet sub extensione misericordiæ atque potentiæ Dei, sperabis quod per misericordiam atque potentiam Dei salvaberis.
paras.en: [[90:4|He will overshadow thee with his shoulders|Scapulis suis obumbrabit tibi]]. By the shoulders of God he means the divine power protecting the elect. The sense, then, is: [[90:4|with his shoulders|Scapulis suis]], that is, by his kindly power, [[90:4|He will overshadow thee|obumbrabit tibi]], that is, he will cool and relieve thee from the heat of temptation and the fire of persecution; as is said further on [that is, later in the Psalter]: [[Ps 139:8|thou hast overshadowed my head in the day of battle|Obumbrasti super caput meum in die belli]]. Hence the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 1:5|as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]]. [[90:4|And under his wings|Et sub pennis ejus]], that is, under his very wings [the psalm's *pennis*, literally "feathers", is glossed with *alis*, "wings"], namely under the outspreading of God's mercy and power, [[90:4|thou shalt trust|sperabis]] that thou shalt be saved through the mercy and power of God.

paras.t: Scuto spirituali in anima circumdabit, id est, undique muniet, te veritas ejus, id est sacræ Scripturæ cognitio, seu illustratio Spiritus Sancti. Unde ait Salvator: Si vos manseritis in sermone meo, vere discipuli mei eritis, et cognoscetis veritatem, et veritas liberabit vos. Et Apostolus: Omnis, inquit, Scriptura divinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum, ad arguendum, ad corripiendum, ad erudiendum in justitia, ut perfectus sit homo Dei ad omne opus bonum instructus. Quemadmodum enim scuto materiali defenditur corpus a læsionibus hostis, sic per considerationem sacræ Scripturæ, et commemorationem divinæ doctrinæ, protegitur anima ab impugnationibus tentatoris, rejicitque a suo consensu quidquid divinæ legi conspicit dissonare. Propterea Sapiens dicit: Sermo tuus, Domine, eos qui in te credunt, conservat. Qui enim in omne quod agit vel deserit, sacræ Scripturæ testimonium adhibet, inexpugnabili scuto innitur, nec potest errare.
paras.en: [[90:5|With a shield|Scuto]], a spiritual one, in the soul, [[90:5|shall compass|circumdabit]], that is, shall fortify on every side, [[90:5|thee|te]], [[90:5|His truth|veritas ejus]], that is, the knowledge of Holy Scripture, or the enlightening of the Holy Ghost. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 8:31|If you continue in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed|Si vos manseritis in sermone meo, vere discipuli mei eritis]], [[John 8:32|And you shall know the truth: and the truth shall make you free.|et cognoscetis veritatem, et veritas liberabit vos]] And the Apostle: [[2 Tim 3:16|All|Omnis]], he says, [[2 Tim 3:16|scripture, inspired of God, is profitable to teach, to reprove, to correct, to instruct in justice|Scriptura divinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum, ad arguendum, ad corripiendum, ad erudiendum in justitia]], [[2 Tim 3:17|That the man of God may be perfect, furnished to every good work.|ut perfectus sit homo Dei ad omne opus bonum instructus]] For as the body is defended from the blows of the enemy by a material shield, so by the consideration of Holy Scripture and the remembrance of divine teaching the soul is protected from the assaults of the tempter, and rejects from its consent whatever it sees to be at variance with the divine law. Therefore the Wise Man says: [[Wis 16:26|thy word|Sermo tuus]], O Lord, [[Wis 16:26|preserveth them that believe in thee|eos qui in te credunt, conservat]]. For he who brings the witness of Holy Scripture to all that he does or leaves undone leans upon an unconquerable shield, and cannot go astray.

paras.t: Non timebis a timore nocturno, id est, non formidabis incurrere noctis timorem, neque pavebis ab his quæ solent nocturnis temporibus timorem incutere. Multi enim imbecilles et modicæ spei timent, die adhuc durante, quod in nocte perterrebuntur. Et quidam paululum animo fortiores, hoc non timent; tamen in ipsa nocte de facili perterrentur, ex aliquo strepitu seu imaginatione aut somnio. Hic timor, magnæ imperfectionis indicium est; liberatque ab eo veritas sacræ Scripturæ seu illuminationis supernæ, quæ ait: Ne paveas repentino terrore. Unde Salomon dicit: Fugit impius, nemine persequente; justus autem quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit. Denique contra hunc stultum timorem, quo timemus de nocte propter absentiam hominum, seu propter somniorum aut phantasiarum occursum, quasi Deus et sancti angeli non essent nobiscum de nocte sicut in die, aut quasi dæmon aliquid posset in nos nisi permissus a Deo, scriptum est: Qui timet Deum, nihil trepidabit; et iterum: Quasi qui apprehendit umbram et persequitur ventum, secundum hoc visio somniorum. Qui ista verba æternæ Veritatis perpendit, hoc carebit nocturno timore, quemadmodum Sapientia profitetur: Qui me audierit, absque terrore quiescet. Quod si imaginationes rerum timorem incutientium oriuntur in nobis, videlicet commemorationes jam defunctorum, etc., multum prodest statim in corde describere imaginem Christi in cruce pendentis, et ea quæ ipse pro nobis perpessus est.
paras.en: [[90:5|thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night|Non timebis a timore nocturno]], that is, thou shalt not dread to meet with the fear of the night, nor be afraid of the things that are wont to strike fear in the night-time. For many who are weak and of little hope fear, while it is still day, that they will be terrified in the night. And some, a little stouter of heart, do not fear this; yet in the night itself they are easily terrified by some noise, or imagination, or dream. This fear is a sign of great imperfection; and the truth of Holy Scripture, or of the light from above, frees from it, saying: [[Prov 3:25|Be not afraid of sudden fear|Ne paveas repentino terrore]]. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 28:1|The wicked man fleeth, when no man pursueth: but the just, bold as a lion, shall be without dread.|Fugit impius, nemine persequente; justus autem quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit]] Lastly, against this foolish fear, by which we fear at night because no one is about, or because of dreams or fancies that come upon us, as though God and the holy angels were not with us by night as by day, or as though the devil could do anything against us unless permitted by God, it is written: [[Ecclus 34:16|He that feareth the Lord shall tremble at nothing|Qui timet Deum, nihil trepidabit]]; and again: Like [[Ecclus 34:2|him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind|qui apprehendit umbram et persequitur ventum]], such is [[Ecclus 34:3|the vision of dreams|visio somniorum]] [Denis joins the first half of v. 2 to the last words of v. 3]. Whoever weighs these words of the eternal Truth will be free of this fear of the night, as Wisdom declares: [[Prov 1:33|he that shall hear me, shall rest without terror|Qui me audierit, absque terrore quiescet]]. And if imaginations of things that strike fear arise in us, for instance remembrances of the dead, etc., it is of great profit at once to draw in the heart the image of Christ hanging on the cross, and the things that he suffered for us.

paras.t: Non timebis etiam a sagitta volante in die, id est ab aspera adversitate quæ manifeste infertur, sicut est contumelia, deprædatio, et quæcumque manifesta afflictio: imo adversitas talis tanquam donum Dei recipitur, et jucunde suffertur, juxta illud Apostoli: Vobis datum est a Christo, non solum ut credatis in eum, verum etiam ut patiamini pro eo. Et ad Hebræos: Rapinam, inquit, bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis. Nec timebis a negotio, id est dæmonio, perambulante in tenebris, id est, qui nocturnis temporibus permittitur inquietare homines; neque formidabis ab incursu et dæmonio meridiano, id est dæmone qui in die permittitur desævire.
paras.en: Thou shalt not be afraid, moreover, [[90:6|of the arrow that flieth in the day|a sagitta volante in die]], that is, of harsh adversity that is openly inflicted, such as insult, plundering, and any open affliction whatever: rather, such adversity is received as a gift of God and borne gladly, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Phil 1:29|unto you it is given for Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer for him|Vobis datum est a Christo, non solum ut credatis in eum, verum etiam ut patiamini pro eo]]. And to the Hebrews: You, he says, [[Heb 10:34|took with joy the being stripped of your own goods|bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis]]. Nor shalt thou be afraid [[90:6|of the business|a negotio]], that is, of the devil, [[90:6|that walketh about in the dark|perambulante in tenebris]], that is, who is permitted to disquiet men in the night-time [*negotium*, "business", Denis takes for a demon]; nor shalt thou be in dread [[90:6|of invasion, or of the noonday devil|ab incursu et dæmonio meridiano]], that is, of the devil who is permitted to rage by day.

paras.t: A quatuor ergo tentationibus liberatur, qui in adjutorio Altissimi habitat, scilicet a timore nocturno, a sagitta volante in die, a negotio perambulante in tenebris, et ab incursu et dæmonio meridiano: et ita nullam tentationem, quantumcumque gravem seu undecumque illatam, veretur, dicens cum Apostolo, Omnia possum in eo qui me confortat; et illud Jeremiæ, Domine, fortitudo mea, et refugium meum, et robur meum in die tribulationis meæ. Unde superius dictum est: Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea: quem timebo? etc. Propter quod Petrus protestatur: Quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni æmulatores fueritis? Nempe, Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Igitur nec dæmonem perambulantem in tenebris, nec dæmonium meridianum timebis.
paras.en: So he who dwells in the aid of the most High is delivered from four temptations, namely from [[90:5|the terror of the night|timore nocturno]], from [[90:6|the arrow that flieth in the day|sagitta volante in die]], from [[90:6|the business that walketh about in the dark|negotio perambulante in tenebris]], and from [[90:6|invasion|incursu]] and [[90:6|the noonday devil|dæmonio meridiano]]: and so he fears no temptation, however grave, or from wherever it is brought, saying with the Apostle: [[Phil 4:13|I can do all things in him who strengtheneth me.|Omnia possum in eo qui me confortat]] And that saying of Jeremias: [[Jer 16:19|O Lord, my might, and my strength, and my refuge in the day of tribulation|Domine, fortitudo mea, et refugium meum, et robur meum in die tribulationis meæ]]. Hence it was said above: [[Ps 26:1|The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear?|Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea: quem timebo?]] etc. For this reason Peter declares: [[1 Pet 3:13|who is he that can hurt you, if you be zealous of good?|Quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni æmulatores fueritis?]] Truly, [[Rom 8:31|If God be for us, who is against us?|Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?]] So thou shalt fear neither the devil that walketh about in the dark nor the noonday devil.

paras.t: Cadent a latere tuo sinistro mille ex dæmonibus, et decem millia dæmoniorum cadent a dextris tuis: quia quicumque seu quotcumque ad te tentandum accesserint, divina virtute superabuntur ac fugient, quemadmodum dicit Apostolus: Deus pacis conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter. Ideo Eliseus locutus est: Noli timere; plures enim nobiscum sunt, quam cum illis. Per latus autem sinistrum, a quo mille cadere perhibentur, intelligendus est status animæ in adversis; per dexteram vero, status ejus in prosperis. Dicit ergo, quod mille casuri sint a latere tuo sinistro, quoniam nulla adversitas te dejiciet, si in adjutorio Altissimi habites: imo quantumcumque fuerit spiritus tuus afflictus, nec murmurabit, nec a Deo recedet, neque pusillanimitate victus, tentatori succumbet. Cadent quoque decem millia a dextris tuis, quoniam nulla prosperitas te extollet; et quantumcumque prospere succedat, nunquam in te ipso gaudebis, nec aliquid boni tibi adscribes, nec tentatori blandienti consenties.
paras.en: [[90:7|A thousand shall fall at thy side|Cadent a latere tuo sinistro mille]] [Denis's text reads "at thy left side"] of the demons, [[90:7|and ten thousand|et decem millia]] of the devils shall fall [[90:7|at thy right hand|a dextris tuis]]: because whoever, or however many, approach to tempt thee shall be overcome by the power of God and shall flee, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 16:20|the God of peace crush Satan under your feet speedily|Deus pacis conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter]]. Therefore Eliseus said: [[4 Kings 6:16|Fear not: for there are more with us than with them|Noli timere; plures enim nobiscum sunt, quam cum illis]]. Now by the left side, at which a thousand are said to fall, is to be understood the state of the soul in adversity; and by the right, its state in prosperity. He says, then, that a thousand shall fall at thy left side, because no adversity will cast thee down if thou dwell in the aid of the most High: rather, however much thy spirit be afflicted, it will not murmur, nor depart from God, nor, overcome by faint-heartedness, yield to the tempter. [[90:7|ten thousand at thy right hand|decem millia a dextris tuis]] shall fall too, because no prosperity will lift thee up; and however prosperously things go, thou wilt never rejoice in thyself, nor ascribe any good to thyself, nor consent to the flattering tempter.

paras.t: Sed cur a sinistro latere asserit mille casuros, atque a dextris decem millia? Primo sciendum, quod hic ponitur numerus determinatus pro numero indeterminato, quemadmodum Daniel inquit: Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei. Et in Apocalypsi: Erat numerus angelorum millia millium, dicentium: Dignus est Agnus qui occisus est, accipere virtutem. Est igitur sensus, quod a lateribus tuis cadet multitudo dæmoniorum, quantumcumque fuerit numerosa seu multa. Nam ut in Scriptura habetur, non est Domino difficile salvare vel in multis, vel in paucis; suntque plures ac fortiores pro nobis, videlicet angeli sancti, quam contra nos angeli mali. Verumtamen dicuntur plures casuri a dextris quam a sinistris, quoniam plures homines seducuntur per blandimenta atque illecebras prosperitatis, quam per molestias adversitatis. Delectationem namque omnes naturaliter vehementerque appetunt.
paras.en: But why does he say that a thousand shall fall at the left side, and ten thousand at the right? First it must be known that here a definite number is put for an indefinite one, as Daniel says: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him|Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei]]. And in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 5:11|the number of them was thousands of thousands|Erat numerus angelorum millia millium]] [Denis: "the number of the angels"], [[Apoc 5:12|Saying|dicentium]]: [[Apoc 5:12|The Lamb that was slain is worthy to receive power|Dignus est Agnus qui occisus est, accipere virtutem]]. The sense, then, is that a multitude of demons shall fall at thy sides, however numerous or great it be. For, as is found in Scripture, [[1 Kings 14:6|it is easy for the Lord to save either by many, or by few|non est Domino difficile salvare vel in multis, vel in paucis]]; and there are more and stronger for us, namely the holy angels, than against us, the wicked angels. Yet more are said to fall at the right than at the left, because more men are led astray by the allurements and enticements of prosperity than by the vexations of adversity. For all men naturally and vehemently desire delight.

paras.t: Ad te autem non appropinquabit tentatio dæmonum per consensum, seu multitudo dæmonum a te victa per opem gratiæ Dei. Dæmones namque victi, cessant a tentatione et fugiunt, quemadmodum scriptum est: Resistite diabolo, et fugiet a vobis. Et asserunt aliqui, quod dæmon semel victus ab aliquo, nunquam redeat ad tentandum eumdem. Alii dicunt, quod nunquam redeat ad tentandum eumdem de illo peccato, quo semel ab eo exstitit victus. Sed probabilius reor, quod et S. Thomæ amplius placet, videlicet quod quamvis dæmones victi ad tempus recedant, et a tentatione desistant, redeunt tamen vicissim ad tentandum eumdem de quocumque peccato. Et ad hujus confirmationem, allegat Thomas quod de Christo apud Lucam scriptum est: Consummata omni tentatione, diabolus recessit ab eo usque ad tempus.
paras.en: [[90:7|but it shall not come nigh thee|Ad te autem non appropinquabit]]: namely the temptation of the demons, by way of consent; or the multitude of demons overcome by thee through the help of God's grace. For demons, when overcome, cease from tempting and flee, as it is written: [[Jas 4:7|resist the devil: and he will fly from you|Resistite diabolo, et fugiet a vobis]]. And some assert that a demon once overcome by anyone never returns to tempt the same person. Others say that he never returns to tempt the same person to that sin in which he was once overcome by him. But I think it more probable, and it pleases St. Thomas better, that although the demons, when overcome, withdraw for a time and desist from temptation, yet they return in turn to tempt the same person to any sin whatever. And in confirmation of this Thomas alleges what is written of Christ in Luke: [[Luke 4:13|all the temptation being ended, the devil departed from him for a time|Consummata omni tentatione, diabolus recessit ab eo usque ad tempus]].

paras.t: Verumtamen oculis tuis interioribus considerabis, hanc victoriam tuam tibi divinitus præstitam, ne Deo ingratus exsistas : et ad hanc considerationem requiritur Spiritus Sancti infusio, juxta illud Apostoli : Nos non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed Spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis. Et retributionem peccatorum videbis : id est, justam pœnam reproborum pensabis et cernes, nunc quidem per fidei speculationem, recolendo distinctionem futuri judicii, pœnasque inferni ; in sæculo autem futuro ac finali judicio eam videbis per certissimam manifestationem. Et ut eam evadere queas, dices Deo :
paras.en: [[90:8|But thou shalt consider with thy eyes|Verumtamen oculis tuis interioribus considerabis]], thy inner eyes, this victory of thine as granted thee by God, lest thou be ungrateful to God: and for this consideration the infusion of the Holy Ghost is required, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 2:12|we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God: that we may know the things that are given us from God|Nos non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed Spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis]]. [[90:8|and shalt see the reward of the wicked|Et retributionem peccatorum videbis]]: that is, thou shalt weigh and behold the just punishment of the reprobate, now indeed by the speculation of faith, calling to mind the sorting out of the future judgement and the pains of hell; but in the world to come and at the final judgement thou shalt see it by the most certain manifestation. And that thou mayest escape it, thou shalt say to God:

paras.t: Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea, id est objectum, causa et terminus spei meæ ; vel, Spes mea, id est bonum a me principaliter finaliterque speratum, quia non aliud bonum desidero, nec aliud præmium quæro, nec alium finem exspecto, nisi te ipsum. Altissimum posuisti refugium tuum : id est, in te ipso collocasti terminum nostri refugii, scilicet ut non quiescamus nec stemus citra seu infra te, sed mentem erigamus in tuæ bonitatis contemplationem, sicque ad tui ipsius ineffabilem et superaltissimam confugiamus clementiam. Non accedet ad te malum, id est, peccator non admittetur ad societatem et gloriam tuam. Vel, Malum, id est peccatum, non accedet ad te per approbationem, quia non complacet tibi, sicut prædictum est : Quoniam non Deus volens iniquitatem tu es. Et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernaculo tuo, id est triumphanti Ecclesiæ, seu cœlo empyreo : quia in patria nulla invenitur tristitia, afflictio aut miseria, sed gaudium et lætitia, gratiarum actio et vox laudis.
paras.en: [[90:9|Because thou, O Lord, art my hope|Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea]], that is, the object, cause and term of my hope; or, [[90:9|my hope|Spes mea]], that is, the good hoped for by me principally and finally, for I desire no other good, seek no other reward, and look for no other end, but thyself. [[90:9|thou hast made the most High thy refuge|Altissimum posuisti refugium tuum]]: that is, thou hast placed in thyself the term of our refuge [that is, the end in which our flight for refuge comes to rest], namely, that we should not rest or stand still short of thee or below thee, but should raise our mind to the contemplation of thy goodness, and so take refuge in the ineffable and more than most high clemency of thyself. [[90:10|There shall no evil come to thee|Non accedet ad te malum]], that is, the sinner shall not be admitted to thy fellowship and glory. Or, [[90:10|evil|Malum]], that is, sin, shall not come to thee by approval, because it does not please thee, as was said before: [[Ps 5:5|because thou art not a God that willest iniquity|Quoniam non Deus volens iniquitatem tu es]]. [[90:10|nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling|Et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernaculo tuo]], that is, the Church triumphant, or the empyrean heaven: for in the homeland no sadness, affliction or misery is found, but [[Is 51:3|Joy and gladness|gaudium et lætitia]], [[Is 51:3|thanksgiving, and the voice of praise|gratiarum actio et vox laudis]] [the margin gives Is. lii, 3; the words are those of Is 51:3].

paras.t: Vel sic : Homo justus dicet : Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea : et si hoc Deo veraciter dixeris, o homo, quicumque es ille, tunc utique altissimum posuisti refugium tuum, id est, in Christo universorum conditore, non in rebus creatis et vilibus, statuisti tibi locum refugii. Idcirco non accedet ad te malum pœnæ vel culpæ in sæculo illo, ubi spei tuæ mercedem recipies ; et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernaculo tuo, id est corpori tuo, quod in futura resurrectione resumes, quoniam corpus impassibile, clarum, agile atque subtile habebis. Oportet namque (secundum Apostolum) mortale hoc induere immortalitatem. Unde apud Isaiam Dominus ait : Erit securitas usque in sempiternum ; et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta. Vel : Non accedet ad te malum culpæ mortalis in præsenti per consensum, quoniam sperantem in se Dominus a ruina præservat, secundum quod in secunda Petri Canonica habetur: Satagite ut per bona opera certam vestram vocationem et electionem faciatis ; sic enim facientes, non peccabitis aliquando. Et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernaculo tuo, id est corpori tuo, in detrimentum et nocumentum ipsius : imo tale flagellum potius reputandum est dulce ac prosperum purgamentum et maximum meritum, quam durum tormentum aut aliquod nocumentum : quia, ut ait Apostolus, Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis. Et iterum ait : Id quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ, supra modum in sublimitate æternum gloriæ pondus operatur in nobis.
paras.en: Or thus: the just man shall say: [[90:9|Because thou, O Lord, art my hope|Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea]]; and if thou sayest this truly to God, O man, whoever thou art, then indeed [[90:9|thou hast made the most High thy refuge|altissimum posuisti refugium tuum]], that is, thou hast set up for thyself a place of refuge in Christ, the maker of all things, not in created and base things. Therefore [[90:10|There shall no evil come to thee|non accedet ad te malum]], of punishment or of guilt, in that world where thou shalt receive the reward of thy hope; [[90:10|nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling|et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernaculo tuo]], that is, thy body, which thou shalt take up again in the future resurrection, for thou shalt have a body impassible, bright, agile and subtle [the four endowments of the glorified body: impassibility, clarity, agility and subtlety]. For (according to the Apostle) [[1 Cor 15:53|this mortal must put on immortality|mortale hoc induere immortalitatem]]. Hence the Lord says in Isaias: There shall be [[Is 32:17|security for ever|securitas usque in sempiternum]]; [[Is 32:18|And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta]]. Or: [[90:10|There shall no evil come to thee|Non accedet ad te malum]] of mortal guilt in the present life by consent, since the Lord preserves from ruin him who hopes in him, according to what is found in the second canonical Epistle of Peter: [[2 Pet 1:10|labour the more, that by good works you may make sure your calling and election. For doing these things, you shall not sin at any time|Satagite ut per bona opera certam vestram vocationem et electionem faciatis ; sic enim facientes, non peccabitis aliquando]]. [[90:10|nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling|Et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernaculo tuo]], that is, thy body, to its harm and hurt: nay, such a scourge is rather to be reckoned a sweet and wholesome cleansing and a very great merit than a hard torment or any hurt: for, as the Apostle says, [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us|Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis]]. And again he says: [[2 Cor 4:17|that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation worketh for us above measure, exceedingly an eternal weight of glory|Id quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ, supra modum in sublimitate æternum gloriæ pondus operatur in nobis]].

paras.t: Quoniam angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in omnibus viis tuis. Omnes namque (secundum Apostolum) sunt administratorii spiritus, in ministerium missi propter eos qui hereditatem capiunt salutis. Quod enim angeli deputantur ad custodiam hominum, Christus apud Matthæum insinuat : Angeli, inquit, eorum in cœlis semper vident faciem Patris mei. Ubi Hieronymus dicit : Magna est dignitas animarum, ut unaquæque a nativitatis exordio habeat angelum sanctum, ad sui custodiam deputatum. Sed quum singulis hominibus singuli præsint angeli, cur non ait, Angelo suo mandavit de te, vel, Angelis suis mandavit de vobis? Et respondendum, quod quamvis quilibet homo, in quantum est singularis persona, specialem habeat angelum, tamen sicut unum eumdemque hominem plures tentant diaboli, sic eidem homini adesse atque succurrere possunt angeli plures. Custodiunt autem nos angeli quantum in ipsis est, in omnibus viis, id est operibus nostris. In bonis enim actibus nos custodiunt, ne cessemus a bono, sed semper perseveremus in finem. In malis quoque actibus nos custodiunt, ne statim a dæmone rapiamur, et ne in vitiis persistamus. Custodiunt etiam nos a tentationibus dæmonum, ne quantum desiderant, nos molestent, et a multis periculis mentis et corporis. Unde, secundum Thomam, infantes in utero matrum suarum, angelum specialem pro custodia sortiuntur, quia infanti in utero accidere possunt aliqua nocumenta.
paras.en: [[90:11|For he hath given his angels charge over thee; to keep thee in all thy ways|Quoniam angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in omnibus viis tuis]]. For (according to the Apostle) they are all [[Heb 1:14|ministering spirits, sent to minister for them who shall receive the inheritance of salvation|sunt administratorii spiritus, in ministerium missi propter eos qui hereditatem capiunt salutis]]. That angels are appointed to guard men, Christ gives us to understand in Matthew: [[Matt 18:10|their angels|Angeli]], he says, [[Matt 18:10|in heaven always see the face of my Father|in cœlis semper vident faciem Patris mei]]. On which Jerome says: Great is the dignity of souls, that each one from the beginning of its birth should have a holy angel appointed to guard it. But since single angels are set over single men, why does he not say, *He hath given his angel charge over thee*, or, *He hath given his angels charge over you*? The answer is that, although every man, inasmuch as he is a single person, has a special angel, yet, just as many devils tempt one and the same man, so many angels can stand by the same man and help him. Now the angels guard us, as far as lies in them, [[90:11|in all thy ways|in omnibus viis]], that is, in our works. For in good acts they guard us, lest we cease from good, so that we may always persevere to the end. In evil acts too they guard us, lest we be snatched away at once by the demon, and lest we persist in vices. They guard us also from the temptations of the demons, lest these molest us as much as they desire, and from many dangers of mind and body. Hence, according to Thomas, infants in their mothers' womb are allotted a special angel to guard them, because some harms can befall an infant in the womb.

paras.t: In manibus suis, id est in sua potestate et sapientia, portabunt, id est, dirigent, te de via hujus exilii ad patriam electorum. Adjuvant enim sua virtute nostram infirmitatem, et sua sapientia tenebras cordis nostri illustrant : sicque gradiuntur nobiscum, portantes nos secum, cooperando nobis in omni bono opere. Portabunt igitur te, ne forte offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum, id est, ne aliquid tibi in via obsistat, sed pede inoffenso et calle securo tendas ad patriam. Vel, Ne offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum, id est, ne Christum qui est lapis angularis, peccando offendas. Vel, Ne offendas ad lapidem, id est ad culpam mortalem, ab ingressu patriæ prohibentem, quemadmodum lapis obstruit viam, prohibetque ingressum; pedem tuum, id est affectum tuum, seu operis tui gressum, serviendo ac inhærendo creaturæ potius quam Creatori.
paras.en: [[90:12|In their hands|In manibus suis]], that is, in their power and wisdom, [[90:12|they shall bear thee up|portabunt]], that is, shall guide thee, from the way of this exile to the homeland of the elect. For by their strength they help our weakness, and by their wisdom they enlighten the darkness of our heart: and so they walk with us, carrying us along with them, working together with us in every good work. Therefore [[90:12|they shall bear thee up|Portabunt igitur te]], [[90:12|lest thou dash thy foot against a stone|ne forte offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum]], that is, lest anything stand in thy way, but that with foot unhurt and by a safe path thou mayest make for the homeland. Or, [[90:12|lest thou dash thy foot against a stone|Ne offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum]], that is, lest by sinning thou offend Christ, who is the corner stone[[Is 28:16||]][[Acts 4:11||]][[1 Pet 2:6||]] [the Latin *offendere* means both to strike against and to offend]. Or, [[90:12|lest thou dash|Ne offendas]] [[90:12|against a stone|ad lapidem]], that is, against mortal sin, which bars entry into the homeland, as a stone blocks a road and bars entry; [[90:12|thy foot|pedem tuum]], that is, thy affection, or the step of thy work, by serving and cleaving to the creature rather than the Creator.

paras.t: Hos duos versiculos proposuit Christo diabolus, quasi de Christo prædictos ; sed quum ipse sit mendax, et quum mendacium loquitur, ex proprio loquitur, ideo mendaciter allegavit. Non enim de Christo dicta sunt ista, secundum Hieronymum, sed de membris ejus : quoniam Christus angelorum custodia nullatenus eguit, quippe qui errare non potuit ; ministraverunt tamen ei angeli, non propter necessitatem, sed propter reverentiam atque decentiam.
paras.en: These two verses the devil put before Christ[[Matt 4:6||]], as if foretold of Christ; but since he is a liar, and [[John 8:44|When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own|quum mendacium loquitur, ex proprio loquitur]], he therefore cited them falsely. For these things were not said of Christ, according to Jerome, but of his members: since Christ in no way needed the guarding of angels, as one who could not go astray; yet angels ministered to him[[Matt 4:11||]], not out of need, but out of reverence and fittingness.

paras.t: Super aspidem et basiliscum ambulabis, et conculcabis leonem et draconem. Huic simile est quod Christus ait discipulis : Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi supra serpentes et scorpiones, et super omnem virtutem inimici ; et nihil vobis nocebit. Quæ licet ad litteram accipi possint de irrationalibus venenosisque brutis, quæ multi Sanctorum, præsertim in nova lege, sine læsione calcaverunt, sicut eorum venena sine nocumento biberunt, juxta illud Christi apud Marcum, Si mortiferum quid biberint, non eis nocebit (quod etiam partim contigit filiis Israel ex Ægypto gradientibus per eremum vastam atque horribilem, et venenosis animalibus plenam, quæ nocumentum non intulerunt filiis Israel, quemadmodum Moyses scripsit : Dominus ductor tuus fuit in solitudine magna et terribili, in qua erat serpens flatu adurens, et scorpio, ac dipsas) : convenientius tamen per animalia ista accipimus dæmones, horum animalium proprietatem habentes, vel eumdem dæmonem diversis his proprietatibus vel potius malitiis informatum, seu ipsa vitia taliter nocentia, qualiter nocent animalia ista.
paras.en: [[90:13|Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.|Super aspidem et basiliscum ambulabis, et conculcabis leonem et draconem.]] Like this is what Christ says to the disciples: [[Luke 10:19|Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall hurt you|Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi supra serpentes et scorpiones, et super omnem virtutem inimici ; et nihil vobis nocebit]]. And although these words can be taken literally of irrational and venomous brutes, which many of the Saints, especially under the new law, trod upon without injury, just as they drank their poisons without harm, according to that saying of Christ in Mark, [[Mark 16:18|if they shall drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them|Si mortiferum quid biberint, non eis nocebit]] (which also happened in part to the children of Israel as they went out of Egypt through the vast and horrible desert, full of venomous animals, which did the children of Israel no harm, as Moses wrote: The Lord [[Deut 8:15|was thy leader in the great and terrible wilderness, wherein there was the serpent burning with his breath, and the scorpion and the dipsas|ductor tuus fuit in solitudine magna et terribili, in qua erat serpens flatu adurens, et scorpio, ac dipsas]] [the margin gives Deut. viii, 13; the words are in Deut 8:15]): yet more fittingly we take these animals to mean demons, who have the properties of these animals, or one and the same demon shaped by these different properties, or rather malices; or the vices themselves, which do harm in the way these animals do.

paras.t: Dæmon itaque dicitur aspis, in quantum cordi virus invidiæ ingerit, et occultæ tentationis veneno animam inficit et occidit. Sicque per aspidem intelligi potest invidia, quæ suo veneno caritatem Dei et proximi, omniumque virtutum virorem intoxicat, et penitus demolitur ac destruit : quoniam sicut ait Joannes, Qui non diligit, manet in morte ; et iterum, Qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est. Dæmon quoque dicitur basiliscus, dum sola fraudulenta suggestione animam tentat atque interficit, proponendo ei mala sub specie boni, utpote in angelum lucis se transfigurans, secundum Apostolum. Basiliscus namque solo visu interficit, non quoslibet, sed eos (ut fertur) a quibus ipse primitus non videtur. Nam si homo illum prius conspiciat, non sibi nocet oculus venenosissimi basilisci : imo (ut legitur) si quis speculum basilisco objiciat, repercutitur venenum, rediens ad eum unde manavit, et proprium interimit effusorem, scilicet ipsum basiliscum. Sic plane iste diabolus, qui per basiliscum significatur, et in angelum lucis transformatur, non videntem interimit ; si vero adspiciat homo primitus dæmonem istum, ejus versutiam perpendendo, non læditur, sed redit malignitas dæmonis in caput ipsius. Sicque per basiliscum vana gloria designatur, quæ incautos et mentaliter cæcos prosternit, videnti vero et spiritualiter illustrato nocere non valet. Dicitur etiam dæmon leo, dum contumaciter, violenter ac impetuose hominem, maxime innocentem, persequitur. Propter quod princeps Apostolorum admonet : Sobrii estote et vigilate, quia adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret : cui resistite fortes in fide. Unde per leonem significatur ferocia animi, seu omne peccatum ad violentiam pertinens. Dicitur autem diabolus draco, quum per suarum pestiferarum immissionum abundantiam, hominem prorsus absorbet, sicut de eo scriptum est : Absorbebit fluvium, et non mirabitur. Itaque per draconem obstinatio designatur.
paras.en: The demon, then, is called an [[90:13|asp|aspis]] inasmuch as he pours the venom of envy into the heart, and infects and kills the soul with the poison of hidden temptation. And so by the asp envy can be understood, which with its poison envenoms the charity of God and of neighbour and the green vigour of all the virtues, and utterly pulls it down and destroys it: for as John says, [[1 John 3:14|He that loveth not abideth in death|Qui non diligit, manet in morte]]; and again, [[1 John 3:15|Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer|Qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est]] [the margin gives Joann. iii, 14 and 15; the words are in the First Epistle of John]. The demon is also called a [[90:13|basilisk|basiliscus]] when by deceitful suggestion alone he tempts and kills the soul, putting evils before it under the appearance of good, transforming himself, that is, [[2 Cor 11:14|into an angel of light|in angelum lucis]], according to the Apostle. For the basilisk kills by its look alone, not just anyone, but (as it is said) those by whom it is not seen first. For if a man catches sight of it first, the eye of the most venomous basilisk does him no harm: nay (as one reads), if anyone holds up a mirror to the basilisk, the venom is thrown back, returning to him from whom it flowed, and kills the one who poured it out, namely the basilisk itself. Just so this devil, who is signified by the basilisk and is transformed into an angel of light, kills the man who does not see him; but if a man looks first at this demon, weighing his cunning, he is not harmed, but the demon's malice returns upon his own head. And so by the basilisk vainglory is signified, which lays low the unwary and the mentally blind, but cannot harm one who sees and is spiritually enlightened. The demon is also called a [[90:13|lion|leo]] when he pursues a man, above all an innocent one, stubbornly, violently and furiously. For this reason the prince of the Apostles warns: [[1 Pet 5:8|Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|Sobrii estote et vigilate, quia adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret]]: [[1 Pet 5:9|Whom resist ye, strong in faith|cui resistite fortes in fide]]. Hence by the lion is signified fierceness of mind, or every sin that has to do with violence. And the devil is called a [[90:13|dragon|draco]] when through the abundance of his pestilent promptings he swallows a man up altogether, as is written of him: [[Job 40:18|he will drink up a river, and not wonder|Absorbebit fluvium, et non mirabitur]] [*absorbebit*, literally 'he will swallow up', is the word Denis has just used of the devil swallowing a man]. And so by the dragon obstinacy is signified.

paras.t: Possent quoque per bruta ista intelligi homines impii, propter similitudinem imitationis in malo. Nam perversis incredulisque Judæis ait Joannes Baptista : Progenies viperarum, quis ostendit vobis fugere a ventura ira? Pharaoni quoque per Ezechielem dicitur : Audi, Pharao, draco magne. Si ergo in Deo plena mente confidis, super omnes has aspides et basiliscos ambulabis, omnesque istos leones et dracones calcabis : quoniam in omni tentatione, persecutione, et vitiorum impulsu, a peccato immunis exsistes, juxta illud Apostoli : In omnibus his superamus, propter eum qui dilexit nos.
paras.en: These brutes could also be taken to mean wicked men, because they are like them in imitating evil. For John the Baptist says to the perverse and unbelieving Jews: [[Matt 3:7|Ye brood of vipers, who hath shewed you to flee from the wrath to come?|Progenies viperarum, quis ostendit vobis fugere a ventura ira?]][[Luke 3:7||]] And to Pharao it is said through Ezechiel: Hear, Pharao, [[Ezech 29:3|thou great dragon|draco magne]] [the verse itself begins: Behold, I come against thee, Pharao king of Egypt]. If, then, thou trustest in God with a full mind, thou shalt walk upon all these asps and basilisks, and trample all these lions and dragons: for in every temptation, persecution and onset of the vices thou shalt be kept free of sin, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Rom 8:37|in all these things we overcome, because of him that hath loved us|In omnibus his superamus, propter eum qui dilexit nos]].

paras.t: Deinde sequitur benignissima consolatio Dei promittentis speranti in se multiplicem gratiam in præsenti, plenamque in futuro beatitudinem. Quoniam in me speravit, non spe cassa et vacua, sed operosa atque formata, agens quod sibi possibile fuit, nec tamen viribus suis aliquid tribuens, nec propriæ perfectioni confidens, sed in me principaliter sperans, liberabo eum, jam a vitiis, et in futura resurrectione ab omni pœnalitate ac imperfectione mentis et corporis, quando reformabo corpus humilitatis suæ, configuratum corpori claritatis meæ; protegam eum in omni periculo, quoniam cognovit nomen meum, id est, quoniam scivit et fide ac opere recognovit me esse misericordem in ignoscendo, fidelem in adjuvando, veracem in promittendo. Est autem quædam cognitio Dei, quæ vocatur informis, id est sine decore et ornamento, quoniam non est caritati et bonæ conversationi conjuncta : de qua cognitione dicit Apostolus, Confitentur se nosse Deum, factis autem negant; et ad Romanos, Quum cognovissent Deum, non sicut Deum glorificaverunt, aut gratias egerunt. Alia appellatur cognitio Dei formata, id est dilectioni unita : de qua alio loco scriptum est, Qui dicit se nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non servat, mendax est. Nunc igitur loquitur Propheta de cognitione Dei formata : quæ utique divinam protectionem meretur, quum sit acceptabilior Deo quam holocautomata, quemadmodum Dominus per Osee prophetam ait : Scientiam Dei volo plus quam holocausta. Ecce quam magnum bonum est cognitio Dei. Nempe tam magnum est, ut ipsa dicatur finis adventus Christi et vita æterna. Scriptum est enim: Scimus quoniam Filius Dei venit, et dedit nobis sensum, ut cognoscamus Deum verum. Et iterum: Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum Deum verum.
paras.en: Then follows the most kindly consolation of God, who promises him that hopes in him manifold grace in the present and full beatitude in the future. [[90:14|Because he hoped in me|Quoniam in me speravit]], not with an empty and hollow hope, but with one that is active and formed [that is, informed by charity; hope or knowledge without charity is called *unformed*], doing what was possible for him, yet attributing nothing to his own strength nor trusting in his own perfection, but hoping principally in me, [[90:14|I will deliver him|liberabo eum]], now from vices, and in the future resurrection from all penalty and imperfection of mind and body, when I shall reform the body of his lowness, made like to the body of my glory[[Phil 3:21||]]; [[90:14|I will protect him|protegam eum]] in every danger, [[90:14|because he hath known my name|quoniam cognovit nomen meum]], that is, because he knew, and by faith and work acknowledged, that I am merciful in pardoning, faithful in helping, true in promising. Now there is a certain knowledge of God which is called unformed, that is, without comeliness and adornment, because it is not joined to charity and good conduct: of this knowledge the Apostle says, [[Tit 1:16|They profess that they know God: but in their works they deny|Confitentur se nosse Deum, factis autem negant]]; and to the Romans, [[Rom 1:21|when they knew God, they have not glorified him as God or given thanks|Quum cognovissent Deum, non sicut Deum glorificaverunt, aut gratias egerunt]]. The other is called formed knowledge of God, that is, united to love: of which it is written in another place, [[1 John 2:4|He who saith that he knoweth him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar|Qui dicit se nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non servat, mendax est]]. Here, then, the Prophet speaks of formed knowledge of God, which indeed merits the divine protection, since it is more acceptable to God than holocausts, as the Lord says through the prophet Osee: I desire [[Osee 6:6|the knowledge of God more than holocausts|Scientiam Dei volo plus quam holocausta]]. Behold how great a good is the knowledge of God! So great is it indeed that it is called the end of Christ's coming, and life everlasting. For it is written: [[1 John 5:20|we know that the Son of God is come. And he hath given us understanding that we may know the true God|Scimus quoniam Filius Dei venit, et dedit nobis sensum, ut cognoscamus Deum verum]]. And again: [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God|Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum Deum verum]].

paras.t: Clamavit ad me, ferventer orando et exaudiam eum, dando quod rationabiliter atque stabiliter postulat; cum ipso sum in tribulatione: sicut superius dictum est, Juxta est Dominus his qui tribulato sunt corde. Non ergo formidemus, nec dedignemur tribulationes jugiter sustinere, si cupimus Deum nobis incessanter adesse. Eripiam eum ab adversis, et glorificabo, id est, gloriosum et beatum efficiam, eum in patria, dicendo ad eum: Euge, serve bone, quia supra pauca fuisti fidelis, supra multa te constituam : intra in gaudium Domini tui.
paras.en: [[90:15|He shall cry to me|Clamavit ad me]] [Denis's text reads *clamavit*, he cried, for the Vulgate's *clamabit*], praying fervently, [[90:15|and I will hear him|et exaudiam eum]], granting what he asks reasonably and steadfastly; [[90:15|I am with him in tribulation|cum ipso sum in tribulatione]]: as was said above, [[Ps 33:19|The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart|Juxta est Dominus his qui tribulato sunt corde]] [literally 'of a troubled heart': the Latin *tribulato* is akin to *tribulatione*, 'tribulation']. Let us not, then, be afraid, nor disdain to bear tribulations continually, if we desire God to be with us unceasingly. [[90:15|I will deliver him|Eripiam eum]] from adversities, [[90:15|and I will glorify|et glorificabo]], that is, make glorious and blessed, [[90:15|him|eum]] in the homeland, saying to him: [[Matt 25:21|Well done, good and faithful servant, because thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will place thee over many things. Enter thou into the joy of thy lord|Euge, serve bone, quia supra pauca fuisti fidelis, supra multa te constituam : intra in gaudium Domini tui]][[Matt 25:23||]].

paras.t: Longitudine dierum, id est interminabili duratione vitæ beatæ seu ævo, quod est æternitas participata : quæ est mensura actionis qua Beati in patria beatifice perfruuntur, in qua fruitione nulla est interruptio, vicissitudo aut permutatio ; replebo eum, dando ei æternaliter mecum manere, sicut desiderat appetitus ejus, quatenus nec velit, nec possit, nec timeat separari a me ; et ostendam illi clare per speciem salutare meum, id est Filium meum dilectum, omnium Salvatorem, Verbum æternum, in quo Beati in patria omnia vident : qui cum me Patre suo et Spiritu Sancto, est unum idemque objectum et causa beatitudinis omnium electorum. In hac divinitatis Christi ostensione seu visione tota nostra felicitas, summa jucunditas, præmiumque essentiale consistit. Unde et Christus, in hac ostensione sui felicitatem nostram consistere innuit, dicens: Qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo ; et ego diligam eum, et manifestabo ei me ipsum.
paras.en: [[90:16|With length of days|Longitudine dierum]], that is, with the endless duration of the blessed life, or æviternity, which is eternity participated [*ævum*, the measure of created beings unchangeable in their being, between time and the eternity of God]: it is the measure of the activity by which the Blessed in the homeland enjoy God in bliss, in which enjoyment there is no interruption, alternation or change; [[90:16|I will fill him|replebo eum]], granting him to remain with me eternally, as his desire longs, so that he neither wishes, nor is able, nor fears to be separated from me; [[90:16|and I will shew him|et ostendam illi]] clearly, by sight [that is, by open vision, no longer by faith], [[90:16|my salvation|salutare meum]], that is, my beloved Son, the Saviour of all, the eternal Word, in whom the Blessed in the homeland see all things: who with me his Father and the Holy Ghost is one and the same object and cause of the beatitude of all the elect. In this showing, or vision, of the Godhead of Christ consists our whole happiness, our highest joy, and our essential reward. Hence Christ too gives us to understand that our happiness consists in this showing of himself, saying: [[John 14:21|he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father: and I will love him and will manifest myself to him|Qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo ; et ego diligam eum, et manifestabo ei me ipsum]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum sententiosum, moralem, doctrinalem, et consolativum audivimus : in quo docemur, quam salutare sit in Deo confidere ; quid, sic confidens, debeat Domino dicere, quid ab eo exspectare ; quantis tentationibus plena sit vita ista, quam multiplex adjutorium angelorum sanctorum nobis Deus contra eas donaverit; quam beatos effectus consequantur, spem fixam in Domino habentes. Merito etiam psalmum istum in Completorio dicimus contra insidias noctis, tentationesque multiplices dæmonis. Tunc enim præcipue divina protectione et gratia atque angelica indigemus custodia. Debetque quilibet nostrum speciali veneratione honorare angelum suum, præsertim eum invocando de mane, quatenus tota die nos protegat ac dirigat, et de sero, ut per totam noctem cor nostrum ac corpus custodiat, somnia dura repellat, mentem illustret, resurgentes pie præveniat, indesinenterque nobis adsistat. Et ut promissiones divinas in fine hujus psalmi descriptas mereamur sortiri, satagamus hunc psalmum in Completorio devotissima mente cantare. Quod si egerimus, gustabimus sæpe interiori palato virtutem ac dulcedinem psalmi præsentis, qui vere mirabili suavitate exundat.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of wise sayings, moral, doctrinal and consoling: in which we are taught how wholesome it is to trust in God; what one who so trusts ought to say to the Lord, and what he ought to expect from him; how full of temptations this life is; how manifold a help of the holy angels God has given us against them; and what blessed effects follow for those who have their hope fixed in the Lord. Rightly, too, do we say this psalm at Compline [the night hour of the Divine Office, said before sleep], against the snares of the night and the manifold temptations of the demon. For then above all we need the divine protection and grace, and the guarding of the angels.
