For they were the ministers and executors of the sentence which the tyrants decreed against the Church.

paras.t: Mirabiles elationes maris, id est, mirabiliter magnæ et atroces erant persecutiones sæculi hujus, seu hominum impiorum adversus Christi Ecclesiam. Sed et mirabilis in altis Dominus, id est, Christus qui martyres sanctos confortavit, Ecclesiamque protexit, mirabilis apparebat, et suam omnipotentiam ostendebat tempore persecutionum Ecclesiæ, in altis, id est in magnis miraculis, in sublimibus signis, in prodigiis inauditis : quæ fecit Deus per suos fideles, in tantum ut inter crudelissimas persecutiones Ecclesia non solum non timeret, neque deficeret, sed mirabiliter dilataretur, augeretur, confortaretur, et cum ingenti alacritate universa tormenta perferret, donec tandem tyranni deficerent, ipsumque Romanum imperium fidei Christi collum suum subjiceret.
paras.en: [[92:4|Wonderful are the surges of the sea|Mirabiles elationes maris]], that is, wonderfully great and cruel were the persecutions of this world, or of wicked men, against the Church of Christ. But also [[92:4|wonderful is the Lord on high|mirabilis in altis Dominus]], that is, Christ, who strengthened the holy martyrs and protected the Church, appeared wonderful and showed his almighty power in the time of the Church's persecutions, [[92:4|on high|in altis]] [*in altis*, literally "in high things"], that is, in great miracles, in sublime signs, in unheard-of prodigies, which God wrought through his faithful; so much so that amid the cruellest persecutions the Church not only did not fear nor fail, but was wonderfully spread abroad, increased and strengthened, and bore all torments with great eagerness, until at last the tyrants failed, and the Roman empire itself bowed its neck to the faith of Christ.

paras.t: Propterea Testimonia tua, o Christe, id est, quæcumque sacra Scriptura testatur de te, videlicet vaticinia Prophetarum, verba Evangelistarum, articuli fidei, credibilia facta sunt nimis, propter miracula quibus fidem confirmasti. Duæ sunt partes legis divinæ, utpote testimonia et præcepta. Testimonia pertinent ad credenda ; præcepta, ad operanda. Duo quoque sunt modi probandi veritatem, videlicet naturalis rationis argumentatio, et divinorum miraculorum operatio. Testimonia autem fidei christianæ per naturalem rationem probari non valent, quoniam fides est substantia rerum sperandarum, argumentum non apparentium, secundum Apostolum. Probantur autem per divina miracula, id est per opera talia, quæ fieri nequeunt nisi a Deo dumtaxat : sicut est mortuorum resurrectio, immutatio motus solis et lunæ, quæ fiebat Christo in cruce pendente, quantum ad lunam et supernaturalem solis eclipsim; futurorum pure contingentium certa prænuntiatio, secretorum cordis revelatio : quæ in nomine Christi et a Christo copiosissime facta sunt in lege et plebe christiana. Ex quibus certissime liquet, fidem Ecclesiæ esse veram atque divinam, vel (quod solo auditu horribile est) Deum esse falsitatis confirmatorem, hominumque deceptorem. Idcirco Joannes : Qui non credit (inquit) in Filium Dei, mendacem facit Deum, quoniam non credit in testimonium quod testificatus est Deus de Filio suo. Et iterum : Spiritus testificatur quoniam Christus est veritas. Hinc etiam Christus ait : Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater ut perficiam ea, ipsa opera quæ ego facio, testimonium perhibent de me. Et iterum loquens Judæis : Si non facio, inquit, opera Patris mei, nolite credere mihi. Si autem facio, et si mihi non vultis credere, operibus credite.
paras.en: Therefore [[92:5|Thy testimonies|Testimonia tua]], O Christ, that is, whatever holy Scripture testifies of thee, namely the oracles of the Prophets, the words of the Evangelists, the articles of faith, [[92:5|are become exceedingly credible|credibilia facta sunt nimis]], because of the miracles by which thou hast confirmed the faith. There are two parts of the divine law, namely testimonies and precepts. The testimonies concern what is to be believed; the precepts, what is to be done. There are also two ways of proving the truth, namely the argument of natural reason, and the working of divine miracles. Now the testimonies of the Christian faith cannot be proved by natural reason, since [[Heb 11:1|faith is the substance of things to be hoped for, the evidence of things that appear not|fides est substantia rerum sperandarum, argumentum non apparentium]], according to the Apostle. But they are proved by divine miracles, that is, by such works as cannot be done except by God alone: such as the resurrection of the dead[[Matt 27:52||]]; the change in the motion of the sun and moon which took place while Christ hung on the cross, as regards the moon and the supernatural eclipse of the sun[[Luke 23:45||]] [an eclipse of the sun cannot naturally happen at the full moon of the Pasch, so the moon was held to have left its course]; the certain foretelling of purely contingent future things; the revelation of the secrets of the heart: which have been done most abundantly in the name of Christ and by Christ in the Christian law and people. From these it is most certainly clear that the faith of the Church is true and divine; or else (what is horrible even to hear) that God is a confirmer of falsehood and a deceiver of men. Therefore John: [[1 John 5:10|He that believeth not|Qui non credit]] (he says) in the Son of God [[1 John 5:10|maketh him a liar: because he believeth not in the testimony which God hath testified of his Son|mendacem facit Deum, quoniam non credit in testimonium quod testificatus est Deus de Filio suo]] [Denis has *mendacem facit Deum*, "maketh God a liar"]. And again: [[1 John 5:6|the Spirit which testifieth that Christ is the truth|Spiritus testificatur quoniam Christus est veritas]]. Hence too Christ says: [[John 5:36|the works which the Father hath given me to perfect, the works themselves which I do, give testimony of me|Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater ut perficiam ea, ipsa opera quæ ego facio, testimonium perhibent de me]]. And again, speaking to the Jews: [[John 10:37|If I do not|Si non facio]], he says, [[John 10:37|the works of my Father, believe me not|opera Patris mei, nolite credere mihi]]. [[John 10:38|But if I do, though you will not believe me, believe the works|Si autem facio, et si mihi non vultis credere, operibus credite]].

paras.t: Ineffabiliter quoque roboratur fides nostra per hoc, quod non solum Christus, sed et ministri ejus prædicta signa fecerunt, sicut et Christus ante passionem promisit : Qui credit in me, opera quæ ego facio, et ipse faciet, et majora horum faciet, quia ego ad Patrem vado. Nos insuper evidentissime scimus, quales sint illi, per quos Christus miracula facit : quoniam homines sunt in omni virtute perfecti, qui sui ipsius privatum amorem penitus expulerunt, atque in Dei amore prorsus absorpti sunt, fide immobiles, spe longanimes, humillimi, mitissimi, innocentissimi, in divino obsequio maxime timorati, ferventes, continui.
paras.en: Our faith is also strengthened beyond words by this, that not only Christ but also his ministers have done the aforesaid signs, as Christ too promised before the passion: [[John 14:12|he that believeth in me, the works that I do, he also shall do: and greater than these shall he do|Qui credit in me, opera quæ ego facio, et ipse faciet, et majora horum faciet]], because I go to the Father [these last words end verse 12 in the Vulgate, but begin verse 13 in the Douay-Rheims]. Moreover, we know most evidently what sort of men they are through whom Christ works miracles: for they are men perfect in every virtue, who have wholly driven out the private love of self and are utterly absorbed in the love of God; immovable in faith, long-suffering in hope, most humble, most meek, most innocent, most God-fearing in the divine service, fervent, unceasing.

paras.t: Ecce, his bene pensatis, fiunt nobis testimonia fidei credibilia valde, inconcusse credentibus quoniam possibilius esset cœlum et terram perire, quam unum apicem de lege christiana falsificari. Propter quod monet Apostolus : Abundantius oportet nos observare ea quæ audivimus. Quomodo enim effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem, quæ in nos confirmata est, contestante Deo signis et portentis et variis virtutibus et Spiritus Sancti distributionibus?
paras.en: Behold, when these things are well weighed, the testimonies of the faith become very credible to us, who believe unshakeably that it would be more possible for heaven and earth to perish than for one tittle of the Christian law to be falsified[[Luke 16:17||]]. For this reason the Apostle warns: [[Heb 2:1|ought we more diligently to observe the things which we have heard|Abundantius oportet nos observare ea quæ audivimus]]. [[Heb 2:3|How shall we escape if we neglect so great salvation|Quomodo enim effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem]], which [[Heb 2:3|was confirmed unto us|in nos confirmata est]], [[Heb 2:4|God also bearing them witness by signs and wonders and divers miracles and distributions of the Holy Ghost|contestante Deo signis et portentis et variis virtutibus et Spiritus Sancti distributionibus?]]?

paras.t: Domum tuam, id est Ecclesiam seu populum christianum, juxta illud Apostoli : Scias quomodo oportet te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia ; decet sanctitudo, id est sancta conversatio et cordis munditia, Domine, in longitudinem dierum, id est perseveranter, quamdiu subsistit, ut serviat tibi in sanctitate et justitia omnibus diebus suis, quemadmodum Petrus ait : Secundum eum qui vocavit vos, Sanctum, et ipsi sancti in omni conversatione sitis.
paras.en: [[92:5|thy house|Domum tuam]], that is, the Church or the Christian people, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Tim 3:15|that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church|Scias quomodo oportet te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia]]; [[92:5|holiness becometh|decet sanctitudo]], that is, holy conversation [that is, manner of life] and cleanness of heart, [[92:5|O Lord, unto length of days|Domine, in longitudinem dierum]], that is, perseveringly, as long as it endures, that it may serve thee [[Luke 1:75|In holiness and justice|in sanctitate et justitia]] [[Luke 1:75|all our days|omnibus diebus suis]] [Denis: *omnibus diebus suis*, "all its days"], as Peter says: [[1 Pet 1:15|according to him that hath called you, who is holy, be you also in all manner of conversation holy|Secundum eum qui vocavit vos, Sanctum, et ipsi sancti in omni conversatione sitis]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum brevem verbo, sed sensu uberrimum, veritate conspicuum, mysteriis plenum, præconio Dei dulcissimum, venustissimumque audivimus : in quo anima sancta dulce, fiduciale ac amorosum habet cum Deo colloquium. Non ergo sine devotione præcipua cantetur hic psalmus a nobis. Et ut sic eum mereamur cantare, purgemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis ac spiritus, quatenus corpus nostrum sit templum Spiritus Sancti, et anima nostra sedes sit æternæ Sapientiæ, scilicet Christi : sicque sanctitudo ornet animam nostram et carnem spiritui obedientem, ut impleatur in nobis quod Moyses docet : Perfectus et absque macula eris cum Domino Deo tuo. Unde et Christus ait : Estote et vos perfecti, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est. Omnino enim condecens est, ut domus suo habitatori conformetur et proportionetur. Si ergo esse optamus domus Christi, necesse est ut ejus conversationem sequamur, ejusque sanctitati assimilemur.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm short in words but most rich in meaning, conspicuous in truth, full of mysteries, most sweet and most lovely in its proclaiming of God: in which the holy soul holds sweet, trustful and loving converse with God. Let this psalm, then, not be sung by us without special devotion. And that we may be worthy to sing it so, [[2 Cor 7:1|let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit|purgemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis ac spiritus]] [the margin gives II Cor. viii, 1; the words are at 2 Cor 7:1], so that our body may be [[1 Cor 6:19|the temple of the Holy Ghost|templum Spiritus Sancti]][[2 Cor 6:16||]][[1 Cor 3:16||]], and our soul the seat of the eternal Wisdom[[Wis 7:27||]], namely of Christ: and so let holiness adorn our soul, and our flesh obedient to the spirit, that there may be fulfilled in us what Moses teaches: [[Deut 18:13|Thou shalt be perfect, and without spot before the Lord thy God|Perfectus et absque macula eris cum Domino Deo tuo]]. Hence Christ too says: [[Matt 5:48|Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect|Estote et vos perfecti, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est]]. For it is altogether fitting that a house be conformed and proportioned to its dweller. If, then, we desire to be the house of Christ, we must follow his conversation [that is, his manner of life] and be made like to his holiness.

paras.t: Precatio. Domine, regnator cœli et terræ, indue nos bonorum operum decore et fortitudine gratiæ tuæ, ac præcinge castimoniæ virtute ; daque his nitidis et nuptialibus vestibus tibi venienti obviare, et ornatis lampadibus ad æternitatis nuptias tecum intrare : qui cum Deo Patre vivis et regnas Deus per omnia sæcula sæculorum.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, ruler of heaven and earth, clothe us with the beauty of good works and the strength of thy grace, and gird us with the virtue of chastity; and grant that in these bright and wedding garments we may go out to meet thee as thou comest, and with our lamps trimmed enter with thee into the marriage of eternity: who with God the Father livest and reignest God, for ever and ever.

93.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI NONAGESIMI TERTII : DEUS ULTIONUM DOMINUS.
93.title_en: Explanation of the ninety-third psalm: The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth.

paras.t: Assignatur psalmo præsenti hic titulus: Psalmus David, quarta sabbati: id est, psalmus iste, qui est David prophetæ sicut auctoris, agit de his quæ signantur per opus quartæ diei sabbati seu septimanæ. Quemadmodum enim scriptum est in Genesi, quarta die facta sunt sidera cœli, et duo luminaria magna, videlicet sol et luna: quæ secundum divinum præceptum velocissime currunt, Creatori suo promptissime serviunt, sicut de sole scriptum est: Magnus Dominus qui fecit illum, et in sermonibus ejus festinavit iter. Per sidera vero et luminaria cœli, designantur electi ac justi, quibus ait Apostolus: Omnia facite sine murmuratione, ut sitis irreprehensibiles in medio nationis pravæ et perversæ, inter quos lucetis sicut luminaria in mundo. De horum patientia, obedientia ac zelo justitiæ agit hic psalmus, in primis ostendens errorem ac justam damnationem eorum qui divinam providentiam negant, atque:
paras.en: This title is given to the present psalm: A psalm of David, on the fourth day of the week [in the Latin, *quarta sabbati*, "the fourth of the sabbath", that is, of the week; the Douay-Rheims text in the app leaves out the psalm titles]: that is, this psalm, which is David the prophet's as its author, treats of the things signified by the work of the fourth day of the sabbath or week. For, as is written in Genesis, on the fourth day were made the stars of heaven and [[Gen 1:16|two great lights|duo luminaria magna]], namely the sun and the moon, which at the divine command run most swiftly and serve their Creator most readily; as is written of the sun: [[Ecclus 43:5|Great is the Lord that made him, and at his words he hath hastened his course.|Magnus Dominus qui fecit illum, et in sermonibus ejus festinavit iter.]] By the stars and lights of heaven are signified the elect and the just, to whom the Apostle says: [[Phil 2:14|do ye all things without murmurings|Omnia facite sine murmuratione]], [[Phil 2:15|That you may be blameless|ut sitis irreprehensibiles]] [[Phil 2:15|in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation: among whom you shine as lights in the world|in medio nationis pravæ et perversæ, inter quos lucetis sicut luminaria in mundo]]. Of their patience, obedience and zeal for justice this psalm treats, showing first the error and the just damnation of those who deny divine providence; and so:

paras.t: Deus ultionum, id est justarum punitionum, Dominus: quoniam ex propria potestate ac æquitate ulciscitur de iniquis, quando, ubi, quomodo, et quantum vult. Non est autem qui possit eum in hoc impedire sive arguere: ideo additur, Deus ultionum libere egit, id est secundum quod ei placet. Non enim superioris alicujus legi subjicitur, sed ejus voluntas est causa omnis legis creatæ. Unde ait Apostolus: Omnia operatur secundum consilium voluntatis suæ; et rursus, Cujus vult miseretur; et quem vult indurat. Nec dissonat quod ipse per Moysen ait: Miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit. De justa vero, repentina ac libera ultione Dei, in Deuteronomio scriptum est: Dominus Deus fortis est, reddens odientibus se statim, ita ut disperdat eos, et ultra non differat, protinus eis restituens quod merentur. Et Nahum propheta ait: Deus æmulator et ulciscens Dominus, et habens furorem, ulciscens ipse in hostes suos.
paras.en: [[93:1|The Lord|Dominus]] is [[93:1|the God to whom revenge belongeth|Deus ultionum]], that is, the God of just punishments: since by his own power and equity he takes vengeance on the wicked when, where, how and as much as he will. And there is none who can hinder or reprove him in this; therefore it is added: [[93:1|the God of revenge hath acted freely|Deus ultionum libere egit]], that is, as it pleases him. For he is subject to the law of no superior; rather, his will is the cause of every created law. Hence the Apostle says that it is he [[Eph 1:11|who worketh all things according to the counsel of his will|Omnia operatur secundum consilium voluntatis suæ]]; and again: [[Rom 9:18|he hath mercy on whom he will. And whom he will, he hardeneth|Cujus vult miseretur; et quem vult indurat]]. Nor is this at odds with what he himself says through Moses: [[Ex 33:19|I will have mercy on whom I will, and I will be merciful to whom it shall please me|Miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit]]. Of the just, sudden and free vengeance of God it is written in Deuteronomy: The Lord God is strong, [[Deut 7:10|repaying forthwith them that hate him, so as to destroy them, without further delay immediately rendering to them what they deserve|reddens odientibus se statim, ita ut disperdat eos, et ultra non differat, protinus eis restituens quod merentur]]. And the prophet Nahum says: [[Nah 1:2|The Lord is a jealous God, and a revenger|Deus æmulator et ulciscens Dominus]], [[Nah 1:2|and hath wrath|et habens furorem]]: [[Nah 1:2|the Lord taketh vengeance on his adversaries|ulciscens ipse in hostes suos]].

paras.t: Deinde Propheta conformans suum affectum divinæ justitiæ, orat: Exsurge, id est, justitiam tuam declara, atque te summum esse judicem universorum ostende, qui judicas terram, id est habitantes in terra; redde retributionem, id est justam pœnam, superbis tibi rebellibus, puniendo eos nunc temporalibus pœnis, ne æternaliter pereant. Debemus enim pro omnibus orare in bonum, nec alicujus æternam damnationem appetere, quum jubeamur inimicos diligere, et de nullo desperare. Verumtamen conditionaliter possumus exorare pro impiorum damnatione perpetua, scilicet si converti despiciant, et obstinati permanent: et tunc expedit eis ut cito moriantur et pereant, ne diu vivendo thesaurizent sibi iram in die justi judicii Dei. De talibus enim apud Amos propheta dicitur: Nescierunt facere rectum, thesaurizantes impietatem.
paras.en: Then the Prophet, conforming his own affection to the divine justice, prays: [[93:2|Lift up thyself|Exsurge]] [Denis reads *Exsurge*, "Arise", where the Vulgate has *Exaltare*], that is, declare thy justice and show thyself to be the supreme judge of all, [[93:2|thou that judgest the earth|qui judicas terram]], that is, those who dwell on the earth: [[93:2|render a reward|redde retributionem]], that is, a just punishment, [[93:2|to the proud|superbis]] who rebel against thee, punishing them now with temporal penalties, lest they perish eternally. For we ought to pray for the good of all, and not to desire anyone's eternal damnation, since we are commanded to love our enemies and to despair of no one. Yet we can pray conditionally for the perpetual damnation of the wicked, namely if they scorn to be converted and remain obstinate: and then it is expedient for them to die and perish quickly, lest by living long they treasure up to themselves wrath against the day of the just judgment of God. For of such it is said in the prophet Amos: [[Amos 3:10|they have not known to do the right thing|Nescierunt facere rectum]], [[Amos 3:10|storing up iniquity|thesaurizantes impietatem]].

paras.t: Usquequo, id est quamdiu, peccatores, Domine juste judex, usquequo peccatores gloriabuntur, non vera, sed falsa ac pessima gloriatione, videlicet quum malefecerint, exsultantes in rebus pessimis? De quibus Jacobus: Nunc, ait, exsultatis in superbiis vestris. Omnis exsultatio talis, maligna est. Et usquequo, Domine, effabuntur et loquentur, id est, corde et ore dicent, iniquitatem, id est verba iniqua: loquentur, inquam, talia omnes qui operantur injustitiam, id est opera divinis præceptis contraria?
paras.en: [[93:3|How long|Usquequo]], that is, for how long a time, [[93:3|shall sinners, O Lord|peccatores, Domine]], just judge, [[93:3|how long shall sinners glory|usquequo peccatores gloriabuntur]], not with a true but with a false and most wicked glorying, namely when they have done evil, exulting in the worst of things? Of whom James: [[Jas 4:16|now|Nunc]], he says, [[Jas 4:16|you rejoice in your arrogancies|exsultatis in superbiis vestris]]. [[Jas 4:16|All such rejoicing is wicked|Omnis exsultatio talis, maligna est]]. And how long, O Lord, [[93:4|Shall they utter, and speak|effabuntur et loquentur]], that is, say in heart and mouth, [[93:4|iniquity|iniquitatem]], that is, wicked words: [[93:4|shall all speak|loquentur]], I say, such things, [[93:4|who work injustice|omnes qui operantur injustitiam]], that is, works contrary to the divine precepts?

paras.t: Populum tuum, Domine, tibi obedientem, electum et pium, humiliaverunt, id est, contempserunt ac oppresserunt; et hereditatem tuam, videlicet populum jam prædictum, quem tu hereditarie possides, ipsum colendo, fecundando, conservando, donec eum in vitam æternam promoveas, vexaverunt. Nam viduam solatio viri sui privatam, et advenam, scilicet peregrinum, compatriotarum auxilio destitutum, interfecerunt, et pupillos occiderunt. Isti sunt specialiter populus atque hereditas Dei, et Deus specialiter vindicat eorum injurias, juxta illud: Deus magnus, fortis atque terribilis, facit judicium pupillo et viduæ, amatque peregrinum.
paras.en: [[93:5|Thy people, O Lord|Populum tuum, Domine]], obedient to thee, chosen and devout, [[93:5|they have brought low|humiliaverunt]], that is, they have despised and oppressed; and [[93:5|thy inheritance|hereditatem tuam]], namely the people already mentioned, which thou possessest as thine inheritance, tilling it, making it fruitful and keeping it, until thou bring it forward into life everlasting, [[93:5|they have afflicted|vexaverunt]]. For [[93:6|the widow|viduam]], deprived of the comfort of her husband, [[93:6|and the stranger|et advenam]], namely the foreigner, bereft of the help of his fellow countrymen, [[93:6|they have slain|interfecerunt]], [[93:6|and they have murdered the fatherless|et pupillos occiderunt]]. These are in a special way the people and the inheritance of God, and God in a special way avenges the wrongs done to them, according to that saying: [[Deut 10:17|a great God and mighty and terrible|Deus magnus, fortis atque terribilis]]: [[Deut 10:18|He doth judgment to the fatherless and the widow, loveth the stranger|facit judicium pupillo et viduæ, amatque peregrinum]].

paras.t: Sed quia veraciter scriptum est, Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum; idcirco istis malignis non sufficit peccare hoc modo in proximum, sed insuper peccant in Deum; et sicut Judas apostolus in sua Canonica dicit, Eum qui emit eos, Dominum negant, dominationem contemnunt, majestatem blasphemant. Unde subjungitur: Et dixerunt: Non videt Dominus nos, nec intelliget Deus Jacob patriarchæ, seu populi ex eo nati, opera nostra. Quasi dicant: Deus non habet particularem cognitionem de individuis speciei humanæ, nec distincte intelligit actus humanos, et per consequens non est timendum divinum judicium, nec retributio in alio sæculo exspectanda. Hic est pessimus error negantium providentiam Dei. Ex quorum persona dicitur in libro Job: An cogitas quod Deus circa cardines cœli perambulat, nec nostra considerat? De quibus etiam Dominus ait per Malachiam prophetam: Invaluerunt super me verba vestra; et dixistis: Vanus est qui servit Domino; et quod emolumentum, quia custodivimus præcepta ejus? Contra hos arguit Dominus per Jeremiam, dicens: Si occultabitur vir in absconditis, et ego non videbo eum? Numquid non cœlum et terram ego impleo? dicit Dominus.
paras.en: But since it is truly written, [[Ecclus 3:29|the sinner will add sin to sin|Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum]], it is therefore not enough for these wicked men to sin in this way against their neighbour; they sin against God besides; and, as the apostle Jude says in his Canonical Epistle, they [[2 Pet 2:1|deny the Lord who bought them|Eum qui emit eos, Dominum negant]] [Denis gives these words to Jude; they stand in 2 Pet 2:1, while Jude 4 has "denying our Lord Jesus Christ"], [[Jude 1:8|despise dominion and blaspheme majesty|dominationem contemnunt, majestatem blasphemant]]. Hence there is added: [[93:7|And they have said|Et dixerunt]]: [[93:7|The Lord shall not see|Non videt Dominus nos]] us, [[93:7|neither shall the God of Jacob understand|nec intelliget Deus Jacob]] (Jacob the patriarch, or the people born of him) our works. As if they said: God has no particular knowledge of the individuals of the human species, nor does he understand human acts distinctly; and consequently the divine judgment is not to be feared, nor a retribution to be looked for in another world. This is the very worst error, that of those who deny the providence of God. In the person of such men it is said in the book of Job: Thinkest thou that God [[Job 22:14|walketh about the poles of heaven|circa cardines cœli perambulat]], [[Job 22:14|and he doth not consider our things|nec nostra considerat]]? Of them also the Lord says through the prophet Malachias: [[Mal 3:13|Your words have been unsufferable to me|Invaluerunt super me verba vestra]]; [[Mal 3:14|And you have said|et dixistis]]: [[Mal 3:14|He laboureth in vain that serveth God|Vanus est qui servit Domino]]: [[Mal 3:14|and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinances|et quod emolumentum, quia custodivimus præcepta ejus]]? Against them the Lord argues through Jeremias, saying: [[Jer 23:24|Shall a man be hid in secret places, and I not see him|Si occultabitur vir in absconditis, et ego non videbo eum]]? [[Jer 23:24|do not I fill heaven and earth, saith the Lord|Numquid non cœlum et terram ego impleo? dicit Dominus]]?

paras.t: Nunc vero plenius argumentatur contra eos Propheta: Intelligite quæ sequuntur, insipientes in populo: et stulti, id est vera fide atque notitia divinorum privati, aliquando sapite, id est, cum intellectuali sapore intendite istud: Qui plantavit aurem, non audiet? id est, Deus qui dedit hominibus sensum auditus, et ex fonte propriæ sapientiæ instituit modum, viam ac ordinem, quo alii audiunt, prævidens scilicet quid ad audiendum exigatur, et necessaria ad audiendum donans, non audiet ipse? id est, an ipse intellectualiter non cognoscet quod tu sensibiliter audis? quasi dicat, imo. Nisi enim ipse omnia præcognovisset, scilicet naturam verborum atque sonorum, cetera quoque prædicta, non potuisset organum auditus plantasse. Et simili modo de oculo arguit: aut qui finxit oculum corporalem et interiorem, non considerat? quasi dicat, Utique. Nam quidquid perfectionis reperitur in creaturis, excellentius perfectiusque in Creatore consistit.
paras.en: Now the Prophet argues against them more fully: [[93:8|Understand|Intelligite]] what follows, [[93:8|ye senseless among the people|insipientes in populo]]: [[93:8|and, you fools|et stulti]], that is, you who are deprived of true faith and of the knowledge of divine things, [[93:8|be wise at last|aliquando sapite]], that is, attend to this with an understanding that savours it [*sapite*, "be wise", is from *sapere*, which also means "to taste"; hence Denis's *sapore*, "savour"]: [[93:9|He that planted the ear, shall he not hear|Qui plantavit aurem, non audiet]]? That is: God, who gave men the sense of hearing, and out of the fount of his own wisdom established the manner, way and order by which others hear, foreseeing, that is, what is required for hearing and bestowing what is needed for it, shall he himself not hear? That is, shall he not know by his understanding what thou hearest by sense? As if to say: Indeed he shall. For unless he had known all things beforehand, namely the nature of words and of sounds and the other things mentioned, he could not have planted the organ of hearing. And in like manner he argues of the eye: [[93:9|or he that formed the eye|aut qui finxit oculum]], the bodily eye and the inward, [[93:9|doth he not consider|non considerat]]? As if to say: Assuredly he does. For whatever perfection is found in creatures exists more excellently and more perfectly in the Creator.

paras.t: Qui corripit gentes, id est, qui peccatores in hac vita flagellat pro culpis, ut patet in Pharaone et in populo ejus, quos submersit, et Chananæis, quos per filios Israel interfecit; vel, Qui corripit gentes, id est, peccata earum redarguit per Prophetas et alios Sanctos; non arguet etiam vos? quasi dicat, Imo vos arguet atque damnabit, sicut per Jeremiam frequenter testatur: Numquid super his non visitabo, et in gente hujuscemodi non ulciscetur anima mea? Qui docet hominem scientiam, dando ei legem scriptam et evangelicam, nonne et ipse scientiam providentiamque habebit vitæ humanæ? Qui vellet hæc subtiliter considerare ac prosequi, posset ex eis insolubiles rationes elicere, ad ostendendum providentiam Dei, atque distinctam cognitionem intellectus divini de omnibus rebus creatis.
paras.en: [[93:10|He that chastiseth nations|Qui corripit gentes]] [these words of the lemma are illegible in the transcription and are supplied from the psalm, as Denis repeats them below], that is, he who scourges sinners in this life for their faults, as is plain in Pharao and his people, whom he drowned[[Ex 14:1||]], and in the Chanaanites, whom he slew by the children of Israel; or, [[93:10|He that chastiseth nations|Qui corripit gentes]], that is, who rebukes their sins through the Prophets and other Saints: [[93:10|shall he not rebuke|non arguet]] you also? As if to say: Indeed, he will rebuke you and condemn you, as he often testifies through Jeremias: [[Jer 9:9|Shall I not visit them for these things|Numquid super his non visitabo]], [[Jer 9:9|or shall not my soul be revenged on such a nation|et in gente hujuscemodi non ulciscetur anima mea]]? [the same words stand in Jer 5:9, 5:29 and 9:9; Denis's wording is closest to 9:9] [[93:10|he that teacheth man knowledge|Qui docet hominem scientiam]], by giving him the written law and the law of the Gospel, shall not he too have knowledge and providence of human life? Whoever would consider these things closely and follow them out could draw from them unanswerable arguments to show the providence of God and the distinct knowledge that the divine intellect has of all created things.

paras.t: Dominus scit cogitationes hominum: omnia enim aperta sunt oculis ejus et nuda: quoniam vanæ sunt, id est hoc scit de eis, quod inanes ac fatuæ sunt. Hoc autem probat Dominus in Apocalypsi, increpando mulierem nefariam Jezabel, minando ei pœnam durissimam: unde concludit: Et scient omnes Ecclesiæ, quia ego sum scrutans corda et renes, et dabo unicuique secundum opera sua. Hunc versum allegat Apostolus hoc modo: Dominus scit cogitationes sapientium, quoniam vanæ sunt.
paras.en: [[93:11|The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men|Dominus scit cogitationes hominum]]: for [[Heb 4:13|all things are naked and open to his eyes|omnia enim aperta sunt oculis ejus et nuda]]: [[93:11|that they are vain|quoniam vanæ sunt]], that is, this he knows of them, that they are empty and foolish. And the Lord proves this in the Apocalypse, when he rebukes the wicked woman Jezabel and threatens her with the harshest punishment; whence he concludes: [[Apoc 2:23|and all the churches shall know that I am he that searcheth the reins and hearts|Et scient omnes Ecclesiæ, quia ego sum scrutans corda et renes]]. [[Apoc 2:23|And I will give to every one of you according to your works|et dabo unicuique secundum opera sua]]. The Apostle cites this verse in this way: [[1 Cor 3:20|The Lord knoweth the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain|Dominus scit cogitationes sapientium, quoniam vanæ sunt]].

paras.t: Beatus homo quem erudieris, Domine, per inspirationem internam, per illuminationem occultam, specialem, atque continuam, et de lege tua data per Moysen atque per Christum, docueris eum, dando ei gratiam sane ac lucide intelligendi observandique eam. Propterea ad Colossenses primo, orat Apostolus: Postulamus ut impleamini agnitione voluntatis Dei in omni sapientia et intellectu spirituali, ut ambuletis digne Deo, per omnia crescentes in scientia Dei. Et ad Ephesios: Pater gloriæ det vobis spiritum sapientiæ, ut sciatis quæ sit spes vocationis vestræ. Unde ait sermo divinus: Populus non intelligens vapulabit. Sed quia secundum Scripturam, in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia, nec habitabit in corpore subdito peccatis: idcirco qui hanc beatitudinem divinæ eruditionis consequi cupit, removeat obicem, id est, peccata abhorreat, pœniteat, confiteatur, se corrigat: tuncque pro gratia divinæ illustrationis exoret, et experietur verum esse quod scriptum est: Si quis indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, et dabitur ei.
paras.en: [[93:12|Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord|Beatus homo quem erudieris, Domine]], by inward inspiration, by a hidden, special and continual enlightenment, and [[93:12|shalt teach him|docueris eum]] [[93:12|out of thy law|et de lege tua]], given through Moses and through Christ, by giving him the grace to understand it soundly and clearly and to keep it. Therefore in the first chapter to the Colossians the Apostle prays: We beg [[Col 1:9|that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding|ut impleamini agnitione voluntatis Dei in omni sapientia et intellectu spirituali]], [[Col 1:10|That you may walk worthy of God|ut ambuletis digne Deo]], [[Col 1:10|increasing in the knowledge of God|crescentes in scientia Dei]]. And to the Ephesians: [[Eph 1:17|the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom|Pater gloriæ det vobis spiritum sapientiæ]], [[Eph 1:18|that you may know what the hope is of his calling|ut sciatis quæ sit spes vocationis vestræ]] [Denis reads "of your calling"]. Hence the word of God says: [[Osee 4:14|the people that doth not understand shall be beaten|Populus non intelligens vapulabit]]. But since, according to Scripture, [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins|in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia, nec habitabit in corpore subdito peccatis]], therefore whoever desires to attain this blessedness of divine instruction, let him remove the obstacle: that is, let him abhor his sins, repent, confess and amend himself; and then let him pray for the grace of divine enlightenment, and he will find true what is written: [[Jas 1:5|if any of you want wisdom, let him ask of God|Si quis indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo]], [[Jas 1:5|And it shall be given him|et dabitur ei]].

paras.t: Itaque, Domine, beatus quem ita docueris, ad hoc scilicet, Ut mitiges ei tempus hujus exsilii a diebus malis, in quibus maligni et impii gloriantur et florent, ipse vero tribulatur et plangit: id est, ut pie ac dulciter secum agas, quatenus tribulationes quæ sibi contingunt, æquanimiter patiatur, neque de impiorum prosperitate tristetur, arbitrando eam aliquid esse, aut appetibilem fore. Mitiges, inquam, ei tamdiu, donec fodiatur peccatori fovea monumenti, et lacus inferni ei præstetur, id est, donec peccator moriatur, corpusque ejus in sepulcro, anima vero in inferno locetur: quo facto, ipsum a te eruditum tandem perduces ad gloriam.
paras.en: So then, O Lord, blessed is he whom thou dost so teach, to this end, namely, [[93:13|That thou mayst give him rest|Ut mitiges ei]] (in the time of this exile) [[93:13|from the evil days|a diebus malis]] [*mitiges*, literally "that thou soften" or "lighten"; Denis reads "soften for him the time of this exile"], in which the malicious and the ungodly glory and flourish, while he is afflicted and laments: that is, that thou deal kindly and gently with him, so that he may bear with an even mind the tribulations that befall him, and not be saddened by the prosperity of the wicked, thinking it to be something, or to be desirable. Mayst thou soften it for him, I say, for so long, [[93:13|till a pit be dug for the wicked|donec fodiatur peccatori fovea]], the pit of the tomb, and the lake of hell is made ready for him: that is, until the sinner dies, and his body is laid in the grave and his soul in hell. When this is done, thou wilt at last lead him whom thou hast taught to glory.

paras.t: Hæc autem beneficia dabit Deus petentibus se. Quia non repellet Dominus plebem suam fidelem, id est, preces ejus non spernit, desideria ejus adimplet, obsequiumque acceptat; et hereditatem suam, id est gregem electorum, non derelinquet finaliter. Propter quod ait Apostolus: Non repulit Dominus plebem suam, quam præscivit. Et Salvator: Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Non itaque derelinquet eam, quoadusque justitia ejus convertatur, id est procedat, in judicium, id est in actum seu exsecutionem justitiæ, dando bonis et malis congrua præmia: quod erit in die judicii. Interim ergo Deus suos custodit per gratiam, ne decipiantur et penitus opprimantur ab impiis; post judicium vero eos custodiet per gloriam, ut nihil mali patiantur a malis. Et qui juxta illam? id est, qui homines nunc divinæ justitiæ acquiescunt, et in futuro judicio ei concorditer adhærebunt? Respondet: Omnes qui recto sunt corde, id est omnes justi. Horum namque intentio, affectio et conversatio, divinæ justitiæ placet, adhæret, et æternaliter conjungetur. Nam quum similitudo sit causa amoris ac unionis, Deus justus justos sibi conjungit, eosque diligit. Unde Moyses ait: Notum faciet Dominus qui ad se pertineant, et sanctos applicabit sibi; et quos elegerit, appropinquabunt ei.
paras.en: And God will give these benefits to those who ask him. [[93:14|For the Lord will not cast off his people|Quia non repellet Dominus plebem suam]], his faithful people: that is, he does not spurn their prayers, he fulfils their desires and accepts their service; [[93:14|neither will he forsake|non derelinquet]] [[93:14|his own inheritance|et hereditatem suam]], that is, the flock of the elect, in the end. For this reason the Apostle says: [[Rom 11:2|God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew|Non repulit Dominus plebem suam, quam præscivit]]. And the Saviour: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom.|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum]] He will not then forsake it, [[93:15|Until justice be turned|quoadusque justitia ejus convertatur]] [Denis reads "his justice"], that is, proceed, [[93:15|into judgment|in judicium]], that is, into the act or execution of justice, by giving fitting rewards to the good and to the wicked: which will be on the day of judgment. Meanwhile, then, God guards his own by grace, so that they are not deceived and utterly crushed by the wicked; but after the judgment he will guard them by glory, so that they suffer no evil from the evil. [[93:15|and they that are near it|Et qui juxta illam]]? [Denis takes *qui* as a question: "and who are near it?"] That is, which men now rest content with the divine justice, and at the judgment to come will cleave to it in concord? He answers: [[93:15|all the upright in heart|Omnes qui recto sunt corde]], that is, all the just. For their intention, affection and way of life are pleasing to the divine justice, cleave to it, and will be joined to it for ever. For since likeness is the cause of love and of union, the just God joins the just to himself and loves them. Hence Moses says: [[Num 16:5|the Lord will make known who belong to him, and the holy he will join to himself: and whom he shall choose, they shall approach to him|Notum faciet Dominus qui ad se pertineant, et sanctos applicabit sibi; et quos elegerit, appropinquabunt ei]].

paras.t: Deinde Propheta in persona hominis justi loquens, accensus amore Dei ac proximi, zelo zelatur pro Domino exercituum, atque pro conservatione servorum Dei in bono, et ait: Quis consurget mihi, id est ad salutem meam, adversus malignantes? id est, quis me juvabit, ut malignis resistam, eorumque impia gesta impediam, ne eorum malo exemplo aliquis inficiatur, et Deo a multis irreverentia irrogetur? aut quis stabit mecum, id est, quis mihi constanter adsistet, adversus operantes iniquitatem? ne ipsi quod moliuntur, exsequi valeant, sed justa pœna plectantur. Hoc sancto zelo inflammatum erat cor Moysis, qui dixit, quum fecissent filii Israel vitulum aureum atque conflatilem: Si quis est Domini, jungatur mihi, et ponat vir gladium super femur suum, et occidat unusquisque fratrem et amicum et proximum suum.
paras.en: Then the Prophet, speaking in the person of a just man, kindled with love of God and of his neighbour, is zealous with zeal for the Lord of hosts[[3 Kings 19:10||]] [the margin gives III Kings xxi, 10; the words are Elias's at 3 Kings 19:10 and 14], and for the keeping of God's servants in good, and says: [[93:16|Who shall rise up for me|Quis consurget mihi]], that is, for my salvation, [[93:16|against the evildoers|adversus malignantes]]? That is, who will help me to resist the malignant and to hinder their wicked deeds, lest anyone be infected by their bad example, and irreverence be done to God by many? [[93:16|or who shall stand with me|aut quis stabit mecum]], that is, who will stand by me steadfastly, [[93:16|against the workers of iniquity|adversus operantes iniquitatem]]? so that they may not be able to carry out what they plot, but may be struck with a just punishment. With this holy zeal was the heart of Moses inflamed, who said, when the children of Israel had made the golden and molten calf: [[Ex 32:26|If any man be on the Lord's side, let him join with me|Si quis est Domini, jungatur mihi]]: [[Ex 32:27|Put every man his sword upon his thigh|et ponat vir gladium super femur suum]], [[Ex 32:27|and let every man kill his brother, and friend, and neighbour|et occidat unusquisque fratrem et amicum et proximum suum]].

paras.t: Nisi quia Dominus adjuvit me, id est, si Dominus non adjuvisset me adversus malignos, paulo minus, id est pene, habitasset in inferno anima mea, id est, eorum malis consiliis impiisque exemplis seductus fuissem, mortaliterque peccassem: et ita habitasset anima mea in inferno post terminum vitæ præsentis; et etiam in hac vita habitasset in inferno, faciendo opera quibus ad infernum venitur: quemadmodum viatores sancti dicuntur habitare et conversationem habere in cœlo, quoniam faciunt opera quibus ad regnum cœleste pertingitur. Vel, In inferno, id est in peccato mortali, quod est causa perveniendi ad pœnas inferni. Imo veraciter dicere potest omnis qui mortaliter Deum offendit, et tamen nondum in infernum projectus est: Nisi quia Dominus adjuvit me, id est, nisi pietas Dei misericorditer mecum egisset, totaliter habitasset per damnationem æternam in inferno anima mea. Dum enim homo mortaliter peccat, meretur omnibus beneficiis gratiæ Dei privari, et pœnam æternam incidere: unde quod pœna inferni sibi differtur, misericordiæ Dei adscribere necesse est. Ideoque a Jeremia dicitur: Misericordiæ Domini, quia non sumus consumpti.
paras.en: [[93:17|Unless the Lord had been my helper|Nisi quia Dominus adjuvit me]], that is, if the Lord had not helped me against the malignant, [[93:17|my soul had|anima mea]] [[93:17|almost|paulo minus]], that is, all but, [[93:17|dwelt in hell|habitasset in inferno]]: that is, I should have been led astray by their evil counsels and wicked examples and have sinned mortally; and so my soul would have dwelt in hell after the end of the present life; and even in this life it would have dwelt in hell, by doing the works by which one comes to hell: just as holy wayfarers [*viatores*, those still on the way, in this life] are said to dwell and to have their conversation in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], because they do the works by which the heavenly kingdom is reached. Or, [[93:17|in hell|In inferno]], that is, in mortal sin, which is the cause of coming to the pains of hell. Indeed, everyone who has offended God mortally and yet has not yet been cast into hell can truly say: [[93:17|Unless the Lord had been my helper|Nisi quia Dominus adjuvit me]], that is, unless the loving-kindness of God had dealt mercifully with me, my soul would have dwelt wholly in hell by eternal damnation. For when a man sins mortally, he deserves to be deprived of all the benefits of God's grace and to fall into eternal punishment: hence, that the punishment of hell is put off for him must be ascribed to the mercy of God. And so it is said by Jeremias: [[Lam 3:22|The mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed|Misericordiæ Domini, quia non sumus consumpti]].

paras.t: Quoniam vero ad humilem propriæ infirmitatis confessionem sequitur pia subventio Dei, subjungitur: Si dicebam mente coram te, seu corde in humili confessione: Motus est a rectitudine vitæ et observatione legis divinæ, pes meus, id est affectus cordis mei seu gressus conversationis meæ, misericordia tua, Domine, adjuvit me: id est, tunc misericordia tua statim mihi subvenit, indulgentiam præstitit, gratiamque infudit. Unde Job: Vias, inquit, meas in conspectu ejus arguam: et ipse erit salvator meus. Hoc autem consequenter clarius manifestatur.
paras.en: And since the kindly help of God follows on the humble confession of one's own weakness, there is added: [[93:18|If I said|Si dicebam]] in my mind before thee, or in my heart, in humble confession: [[93:18|My foot|pes meus]], that is, the affection of my heart or the steps of my way of life, [[93:18|is moved|Motus est]] from uprightness of life and from the keeping of the divine law, [[93:18|thy mercy, O Lord, assisted me|misericordia tua, Domine, adjuvit me]] [another reading has *adjuvabat*, "was helping", as the Vulgate does]: that is, then thy mercy came at once to my help, granted me pardon and poured in grace. Hence Job: [[Job 13:15|my ways|Vias]], he says, [[Job 13:15|in his sight|meas in conspectu ejus]] [[Job 13:15|I will reprove|arguam]]: [[Job 13:16|And he shall be my saviour|et ipse erit salvator meus]]. And this is shown more clearly in what follows.

paras.t: Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, id est, secundum quod multipliciter afflictus sum corde pro justis causis, scilicet pro peccatis propriis aut alienis, pro dilatione felicitatis æternæ, pro injuria majestatis divinæ, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam, id est, multiformiter consolatus es me consolatione spirituali, occulta, angelica. Hoc est quod dicit Apostolus: Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra. Et denuo: Benedictus Deus, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra. Hinc quoque alibi scriptum est: Post tempestatem, Domine, tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis. Omnis nempe qui pro causa honesta affligitur, dummodo afflictionem suam æquanimiter toleret, omnemque carnalem ac vilem delectationem despiciat, promeretur consolari a Domino tanto exuberantius, quanto abundantius dolet. Si igitur ad divinarum consolationum, quæ veræ dulcissimæque consistunt, gustum pertingere nitimur, multarum tribulationum afflictionem perpeti non dedignemur, sed gratulemur: quoniam si socii fuerimus passionis, erimus et socii consolationis, secundum Apostolum.
paras.en: [[93:19|According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart|Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo]], that is, according as I have been afflicted in heart in many ways for just causes, namely for my own sins or those of others, for the delay of eternal happiness, for the wrong done to the divine majesty, [[93:19|thy comforts have given joy to my soul|consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam]], that is, thou hast comforted me in manifold ways with a consolation spiritual, hidden and angelic. This is what the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 1:5|as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]]. And again: [[2 Cor 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], [[2 Cor 1:4|Who comforteth us in all our tribulation|qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra]]. Hence also it is written elsewhere: [[Tob 3:22|after a storm|Post tempestatem]], O Lord, [[Tob 3:22|thou makest a calm, and after tears and weeping thou pourest in joyfulness|tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis]]. For everyone who is afflicted for an honourable cause, provided he bears his affliction with an even mind and despises all carnal and base delight, merits to be comforted by the Lord the more richly, the more abundantly he grieves. If then we strive to come to the taste of the divine consolations, which are true and most sweet, let us not disdain to suffer the affliction of many tribulations, but rejoice in it: since, if we are partakers of the sufferings, we shall be partakers also of the consolation, according to the Apostle[[2 Cor 1:7||]].

paras.t: Numquid adhæret tibi sedes iniquitatis, id est anima injusta (quæ est sedes peccati, sicut anima justa est sedes sapientiæ et virtutis): id est, numquid peccator tecum erit, aut tibi placebit, qui fingis laborem in præcepto, id est, qui facis quamdam difficultatem esse in observatione præceptorum tuorum? Non enim sine labore implemus divina mandata. Nam secundum Philosophum, Ars et virtus sunt circa difficilia. Propter quod dictum est supra: Propter verba labiorum tuorum ego custodivi vias duras. Itaque dicit: Numquid adhæret tibi, etc.? quasi dicat, Non: quoniam sicut alibi habetur, Deus fidelis et absque ulla iniquitate, justus et rectus. Idcirco injusti nequaquam ei adhærent, præsertim quum Salomon dicat: Longe est Dominus a peccatoribus. Peccata enim dividunt inter Deum et nos, sicut Isaias asserit. Vel, Qui fingis laborem in præcepto, id est, qui formas, facis et plasmas de ipso labore atque dolore præceptum, quoniam præcipis nos in hac vita laborare atque dolere, dicendo, Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur; et iterum, Regnum cœlorum vim patitur, et violenti rapiunt illud. Propter quod Paulus, Labora, inquit, sicut bonus miles Christi; et Jacobus, Risus vester in luctum convertatur, et gaudium in mærorem.
paras.en: [[93:20|Doth the seat of iniquity stick to thee|Numquid adhæret tibi sedes iniquitatis]], that is, the unjust soul (which is the seat of sin, as the just soul is the seat of wisdom and virtue [the margin gives Wis. vi, 27, which does not fit; cf. Wis 7:27, where wisdom "conveyeth herself into holy souls"]): that is, shall the sinner be with thee, or please thee, [[93:20|who framest labour in commandment|qui fingis laborem in præcepto]], that is, who makest there to be a certain difficulty in the keeping of thy precepts? For we do not fulfil the divine commandments without labour; for according to the Philosopher [Aristotle], art and virtue are concerned with what is difficult. For this reason it was said above: [[Ps 16:4|for the sake of the words of thy lips, I have kept hard ways|Propter verba labiorum tuorum ego custodivi vias duras]]. So he says: [[93:20|Doth the seat of iniquity stick to thee|Numquid adhæret tibi]], etc.? As if to say: No; since, as is found elsewhere, [[Deut 32:4|God is faithful and without any iniquity, he is just and right|Deus fidelis et absque ulla iniquitate, justus et rectus]]. Therefore the unjust in no way cleave to him, especially since Solomon says: [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus a peccatoribus]]. For sins divide between God and us, as Isaias declares[[Is 59:2||]]. Or, [[93:20|who framest labour in commandment|Qui fingis laborem in præcepto]], that is, who formest, makest and fashionest a commandment out of labour and grief itself, since thou commandest us to labour and grieve in this life, saying: [[Matt 5:5|Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted|Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur]]; and again: [[Matt 11:12|the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent bear it away|Regnum cœlorum vim patitur, et violenti rapiunt illud]]. For this reason Paul says: [[2 Tim 2:3|Labour|Labora]], he says, [[2 Tim 2:3|as a good soldier of Christ Jesus|sicut bonus miles Christi]]; and James: [[Jas 4:9|let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow|Risus vester in luctum convertatur, et gaudium in mærorem]].

paras.t: Potest quoque hic versus ad hominem dirigi, et de peccatore exponi; eritque sensus: Numquid, o homo, adhæret tibi sedes iniquitatis, id est, numquid inseparabiliter adhæret tibi iniquitas, seu habituatio in peccato, quæ est cathedra pestilentiæ, qui fingis laborem in præcepto, id est, qui mendaciter dicis te non posse Dei mandata implere? quasi dicat, Non. Potest enim se homo corrigere, quamdiu in via est. Istud dicitur contra eos, qui quum admonentur cessare a peccato, et viam pœnitentiæ introire, respondent: Non possum consuetudinem meam relinquere, nec mundum deserere, nec concupiscentias refrenare; itemque: Non possum jejunare, multum orare, diu vigilare, in solitudine esse. Horum damnatio justa est, quoniam mentiuntur, et Deum indiscretum affirmant, quasi Deus aliquid impossibile jusserit; fatentur quoque suum affectum divinæ voluntati omnino esse contrarium.
paras.en: This verse can also be addressed to man and expounded of the sinner; and the sense will be: [[93:20|Doth the seat of iniquity stick to thee|adhæret tibi sedes iniquitatis]], O man? that is, does iniquity, or a settled habit of sin, which is [[Ps 1:1|the chair of pestilence|cathedra pestilentiæ]], cleave to thee inseparably, [[93:20|who framest labour in commandment|qui fingis laborem in præcepto]], that is, who sayest falsely that thou canst not fulfil God's commandments? As if to say: No. For a man can amend himself as long as he is on the way. This is said against those who, when they are admonished to cease from sin and to enter on the way of penance, answer: I cannot give up my habit, nor leave the world, nor rein in my desires; and again: I cannot fast, pray much, keep long vigils, be in solitude. Their damnation is just, because they lie, and make God out to be without discretion, as though God had commanded something impossible; and they confess too that their affection is wholly contrary to the divine will.

paras.t: Captabunt, id est, frequenter violentiam facient, in animam justi, quatenus falsis persuasionibus, perversis operibus, minis aut blandimentis eam a virtutibus separent, gravent, ac perimant. Unde talibus Dominus ait: Mœrere fecistis cor justi mendaciter, quem ego non contristavi; et confortastis manus impii. Et vir justus ait iniquis: Usquequo affligitis animam meam, et atteritis me sermonibus? En decies confunditis me, et non erubescitis opprimentes me. Et sanguinem innocentem, id est hominem justum ac simplicem, condemnabunt, vitam ejus reprobando, seu ipsum morte dignum asserendo. Ideoque scriptum est: Interfecerunt animas quæ non moriuntur, et vivificabant animas quæ non vivunt.
paras.en: [[93:21|They will hunt after|Captabunt]], that is, they will often do violence against, [[93:21|the soul of the just|in animam justi]], so as to sever it from the virtues, to weigh it down and destroy it by false persuasions, perverse works, threats or flatteries. Hence the Lord says to such men: [[Ezech 13:22|with lies you have made the heart of the just to mourn, whom I have not made sorrowful: and have strengthened the hands of the wicked|Mœrere fecistis cor justi mendaciter, quem ego non contristavi; et confortastis manus impii]]. And the just man says to the wicked: [[Job 19:2|How long do you afflict my soul, and break me in pieces with words?|Usquequo affligitis animam meam, et atteritis me sermonibus?]] [[Job 19:3|Behold, these ten times you confound me, and are not ashamed to oppress me.|En decies confunditis me, et non erubescitis opprimentes me.]] [[93:21|and will condemn|condemnabunt]] [[93:21|innocent blood|Et sanguinem innocentem]], that is, the just and simple man, by condemning his life, or by declaring him worthy of death. And so it is written of them: [[Ezech 13:19|to kill souls which should not die, and to save souls alive which should not live|Interfecerunt animas quæ non moriuntur, et vivificabant animas quæ non vivunt]].

paras.t: Et factus est mihi Dominus in refugium: quoniam dedit mihi caritatem et spem, quibus ad ipsum fiducialiter in omni necessitate confugio; et Deus meus factus est mihi in adjutorium spei meæ, id est, Deus ad effectum perducet spem meam, cooperando mihi per gratiam suam, ita ut non frustrer spe mea, sed omnia possim in eo qui me confortat.
paras.en: [[93:22|But the Lord is my refuge|Et factus est mihi Dominus in refugium]] [literally, "And the Lord has become my refuge"]: for he has given me charity and hope, by which I flee to him with confidence in every need; [[93:22|and my God the help of my hope|et Deus meus factus est mihi in adjutorium spei meæ]], that is, God will bring my hope to its fulfilment, working with me by his grace, so that I am not cheated of my hope, but [[Phil 4:13|I can do all things in him who strengtheneth me|omnia possim in eo qui me confortat]].

paras.t: Et reddet illis, scilicet impiis, iniquitatem ipsorum, id est justa tormenta, quæ eorum peccata merentur, prout apud Joelem asscribitur: Cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem super caput vestrum. Et in malitia cordium, id est propter malam vitam eorum, disperdet, id est, diversimode perdet, eos, prout singuli diversimode promerentur. Dabit enim unicuique tantum de pœna, quantum gloriatur in culpa, juxta illud Joannis in Apocalypsi: Quantum glorificavit se, et in deliciis fuit, tantum date illi tormentum et luctum. Disperdet illos Dominus Deus noster, id est, Christus omnium judex in die judicii dicet ad eos: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum.
paras.en: [[93:23|And he will render them|Et reddet illis]], namely the wicked, [[93:23|their iniquity|iniquitatem ipsorum]], that is, the just torments which their sins deserve, as is set down in Joel: [[Joel 3:4|I will very soon return you a recompense upon your own head|Cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem super caput vestrum]]. [[93:23|and in their malice|Et in malitia cordium]] [Denis reads "in the malice of their hearts"], that is, because of their evil life, [[93:23|he will destroy|disperdet]], that is, will destroy in diverse ways, [[93:23|them|eos]], as each in diverse ways deserves. For he will give to each as much punishment as he glories in his guilt, according to that saying of John in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 18:7|As much as she hath glorified herself and lived in delicacies, so much torment and sorrow give ye to her|Quantum glorificavit se, et in deliciis fuit, tantum date illi tormentum et luctum]]. [[93:23|the Lord our God will destroy them|Disperdet illos Dominus Deus noster]], that is, Christ, the judge of all, will say to them on the day of judgment: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]].

paras.t: Discamus ex psalmo præsenti divinam ultionem metuere, omniaque peccata cordialiter abhorrere, ne, dum psalmum hunc dicimus, os nostrum condemnet nos. Nam sicut in Ecclesiastico legitur, Dum maledicit impius diabolum, maledicit ipse animam suam; sic dum peccator vitia execratur, semetipsum condemnat. Propter quod dicit Apostolus: In quo alium judicas, te ipsum condemnas. Taliter ergo Christo judici ministremus, taliterque divinæ voluntati ipsius nostrum conformemus affectum, ut mente sincera atque secura contra perversos cum ipso loquamur, ejusque providentiam ac rigorosum judicium indesinenter pensemus, dicentes cum sancto Job: Nonne Deus considerat vias meas, et omnes gressus meos dinumerat? Itemque: Verebar omnia opera mea, sciens quod non parceres delinquenti.
paras.en: Let us learn from the present psalm to fear the divine vengeance and to abhor all sins from the heart, lest, while we say this psalm, our own mouth condemn us. For as we read in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 21:30|While the ungodly curseth the devil, he curseth his own soul|Dum maledicit impius diabolum, maledicit ipse animam suam]]: so, when the sinner curses vices, he condemns himself. For this reason the Apostle says: [[Rom 2:1|wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself|In quo alium judicas, te ipsum condemnas]]. Let us then so serve Christ our judge, and so conform our affection to his divine will, that with a sincere and untroubled mind we may speak with him against the perverse, and ponder unceasingly his providence and strict judgment, saying with holy Job: [[Job 31:4|Doth not he consider my ways, and number all my steps?|Nonne Deus considerat vias meas, et omnes gressus meos dinumerat?]] And likewise: [[Job 9:28|I feared all my works, knowing that thou didst not spare the offender.|Verebar omnia opera mea, sciens quod non parceres delinquenti.]]

paras.t: Postremo, quia in psalmis jam explanatis sæpe fit mentio de sabbato, sciendum quod triplex est sabbatum, videlicet: sabbatum temporis, quod est dies hebdomadæ, seu ipsa hebdomada; secundum, est sabbatum mentis, id est quies conscientiæ immaculatæ: tertium vero, est sabbatum æternitatis, de quo agitur in psalmo præsenti.
paras.en: Lastly, since mention is often made of the sabbath in the psalms already explained, it should be known that the sabbath is threefold: the sabbath of time, which is a day of the week, or the week itself; the second is the sabbath of the mind, that is, the rest of a spotless conscience; and the third is the sabbath of eternity, of which the present psalm treats.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, auxilium spei nostræ, in omni necessitate esto refugium familiæ tuæ; mitiga nobis a diebus malis, et semper lætificent animam nostram consolationes tuæ pietatis.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, the help of our hope, be in every need the refuge of thy household; give us rest from the evil days, and may the consolations of thy loving-kindness ever gladden our soul.

94.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI NONAGESIMI QUARTI […] : VENITE, EXULTEMUS DOMINO.
94.title_en: Exposition of the ninety-fourth psalm: Come let us praise the Lord with joy.

paras.t: Hujus psalmi titulus est : Laus cantici ipsi David : id est, psalmus præsens, qui est laus spiritualis exsultationis, de contemplatione Divinitatis concepta, cantatur ipsi David, id est Christo. Dum namque in titulis dicitur, Ipsi David, per David intelligitur Christus communiter. Agit namque hic psalmus de tempore gratiæ, quo per Christi mysteria ad requiem sempiternam deducimur. Loquitur itaque psalmus iste de Christo et ejus adventu, atque introitu cœlestis quietis seu regni cœlorum.
paras.en: The title of this psalm is: Praise of a canticle for David himself [in the Vulgate the title stands at the head of the first verse; the Douay-Rheims text used here does not print it]: that is, the present psalm, which is the praise of a spiritual exultation conceived from the contemplation of the Godhead, is sung for David himself, that is, for Christ. For when the titles say, For David himself, by David is commonly understood Christ. For this psalm treats of the time of grace, in which we are led through the mysteries of Christ to everlasting rest. And so this psalm speaks of Christ and of his coming, and of the entrance into the heavenly rest, or the kingdom of heaven.

paras.t: Nam Paulus apostolus ad Hebræos psalmum istum allegat ab illo versu, Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, usque ad finem, tanquam loquentem de Christo, et ingressu regni cœlestis, nobis per Christum patefacto. Ubi etiam asserit psalmum istum a David compositum, inter cetera sic dicens : Propter quod determinat diem quemdam in David, dicendo : Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, etc.
paras.en: For the apostle Paul, writing to the Hebrews, cites this psalm from the verse [[94:8|To day if you shall hear his voice|Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis]] to the end, as speaking of Christ and of the entrance into the heavenly kingdom, which has been opened to us through Christ. There he also asserts that this psalm was composed by David, saying among other things: Wherefore [[Heb 4:7|he limiteth a certain day|determinat diem quemdam]], [[Heb 4:7|saying in David|in David, dicendo]]: [[Heb 4:7|To day if you shall hear his voice|Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis]], etc.

paras.t: Ex quo absolute concluditur omni Christiano, quod dictum Hebræorum, dicentium undecim psalmos istos, scilicet, Domine, refugium factus es nobis, et eos qui sequuntur, usque ad psalmum qui incipit : Misericordiam et judicium cantabo tibi, Domine, inter quos hic psalmus continetur, editos a Moyse, falsum sit. Et quidam qui Hebræos sequens, affirmat hos psalmos a Moyse factos, isto excepto, fundamento ruinoso innititur. Denique, ubicumque in Scriptura canonica novi Testamenti allegantur verba psalmorum, vel nullus auctor, vel David exprimitur. Unde probabile valde est, omnes psalmos a David conscriptos. Nec valet, si quis dicere velit, ideo interdum non exprimi David, quia non omnes psalmos composuit : quoniam etiam in illorum allegatione psalmorum, quos omnes concorditer dicunt a David factos, non semper exprimitur ipse David in Scriptura novi Testamenti, quemadmodum subtiliter consideranti patescit.
paras.en: From this it follows absolutely, for every Christian, that the saying of the Hebrews is false, who say that these eleven psalms (namely, [[Ps 89:1|Lord, thou hast been our refuge|Domine, refugium factus es nobis]], and those that follow, up to the psalm which begins: [[Ps 100:1|Mercy and judgment I will sing to thee, O Lord|Misericordiam et judicium cantabo tibi, Domine]]), among which this psalm is contained, were put forth by Moses. And a certain writer who, following the Hebrews, affirms that these psalms were made by Moses, this one excepted, leans on a ruinous foundation. Lastly, wherever the words of the psalms are cited in the canonical Scripture of the New Testament, either no author is named, or David is. Hence it is very probable that all the psalms were written by David. Nor does it hold if someone would say that David is sometimes not named because he did not compose all the psalms: for even in citing those psalms which all agree were made by David, David himself is not always named in the Scripture of the New Testament, as is plain to one who considers it carefully.

paras.t: Invitans itaque sanctus Propheta nos omnes ad præcordiale præconium summæ Trinitatis, unius veri ac simplicis Dei seu Christi, qui in unitate Personæ est Deus et homo, ait : Venite, mentis affectu, et si opus est, etiam corporis gressu, quatenus mente et corpore adunati, agamus quæ sequuntur. Venite, qui distatis a Deo per reprobam vitam : venite, inquam, id est, ad ea quæ sequuntur, vos præparate per humilem confessionem et satisfactionem iniquitatum vestrarum. Venite, o omnes devoti ac religiosi, id est, a diversis ac multis rebus, quæ non sunt necessariæ, mentes vestras abstrahite, et ad illud unum, quod solum necessarium est, accedite. Venite, per fidei contemplationem, per spei certissimam præstolationem, per caritatis fervorem. Venite, per puritatem mentalem, per laudem vocalem, per conversationem laudabilem. Venite, cognoscendo, diligendo et operando. Exsultemus Domino, id est, tam vehementer intus in Domino gaudeamus, atque ad gloriam ejus jucundemur, ut interioris lætitiæ signa foris appareant. Exsultemus ergo Domino, id est, de ejus bonitate immensa et beneficiis gloriemur, quemadmodum Habacuc dicit : Ego autem in Domino gaudebo, et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo. Jubilemus Deo salutari nostro, id est, in Christo nostro Salvatore, seu Deo trino, salvatore ac salutari nostro, id est salutis nostræ objecto et causa, tam exuberanter lætemur in anima, ut gaudium illud præ suo excessu nec penitus possit restringi seu occultari, nec integre explicari. Exsultatio namque est exhilaratio mentis, foris ostensa per sensibilia signa : quoniam exsultare, est extra se saltare. Jubilatio autem est tam copiosa mentis in Deo jucunditas, ut nec penitus contineri, nec plene valeat exprimi.
paras.en: And so the holy Prophet, inviting us all to a heartfelt proclaiming of the most high Trinity, the one true and simple God, or of Christ, who in the unity of his Person is God and man, says: [[94:1|Come|Venite]], with the affection of the mind, and if need be, with the steps of the body too, so that, united in mind and body, we may do what follows. Come, you who are far from God by a reprobate life: come, I say, that is, prepare yourselves for what follows by a humble confession of your iniquities and satisfaction for them. Come, all you devout and religious, that is, draw your minds away from the many and various things that are not necessary, and approach that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]]. Come, by the contemplation of faith, by the most certain expectation of hope, by the fervour of charity. Come, by purity of mind, by praise of the voice, by a praiseworthy way of life. Come, by knowing, by loving and by working. [[94:1|let us praise the Lord with joy|Exsultemus Domino]] [Latin *exsultemus*, "let us exult"], that is, let us rejoice so vehemently within, in the Lord, and be so glad for his glory, that the signs of the inward joy appear outwardly. Let us exult in the Lord, then, that is, let us glory in his immense goodness and his benefits, as Habacuc says: [[Hab 3:18|But I will rejoice in the Lord: and I will joy in God my Jesus|Ego autem in Domino gaudebo, et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo]] [the margin gives only Habac. iii]. [[94:1|let us joyfully sing to God our saviour|Jubilemus Deo salutari nostro]], that is, let us be glad in soul in Christ our Saviour, or in the triune God, our saviour and our salvation (that is, the object and cause of our salvation), so overflowingly that this joy, by its very excess, can neither be wholly held in or hidden nor fully expressed. For exultation is a gladdening of the mind shown outwardly by signs the senses perceive: since to exult [*exsultare*] is to leap [*saltare*] outside oneself [*extra se*]. But jubilation is so copious a joy of the mind in God that it can neither be wholly contained nor fully expressed.

paras.t: Præoccupemus faciem ejus, id est, adspectum Dei nostri seu ejus præsentiam præveniamus, ita quod ipsum in primis quæramus, quemadmodum scriptum est : Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus. Præoccupemus, inquam, in confessione jucunda suæ bonitatis, in confessione quoque dolorosa nostræ pravitatis. Vel : Præoccupemus faciem ejus, id est, futurum ejus adventum, quo in judicio præsens videbitur, præveniamus in confessione peccatorum nostrorum, studentes mitigare ejus furorem, ipsumque placatum habere in die judicii : quia tunc hilariter eum sunt visuri, qui modo quotidie satagunt ei reconciliari. Vel : Præoccupemus faciem ejus, id est, omnia divinæ venerationis impedimenta in primis a corde nostro projiciamus, et antequam aliquam cogitationem extraneam aut phantasma inane admittamus, præveniamus, contemplemur, ac honoremus Dei præsentiam. Et in psalmis, id est canticis spiritualibus, carminibusque devotis, jubilemus ei, ipsum ore laudando, quemadmodum docet Apostolus : Implemini Spiritu Sancto, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino semper.
paras.en: [[94:2|Let us come before his presence|Præoccupemus faciem ejus]] [literally "let us forestall his face"], that is, let us go before the sight of our God, or his presence, so that we seek him first of all, as it is written: [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice|Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus]]. Let us come before him, I say, in a joyful confession of his goodness, and also in a sorrowful confession of our wickedness [the Latin *in confessione*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "with thanksgiving", means both praise and the confession of sins]. Or: Let us come before his presence, that is, let us forestall his future coming, when he will be seen present at the judgement, by confessing our sins, striving to soften his wrath and to have him appeased on the day of judgement: for those will then see him gladly who now strive daily to be reconciled to him. Or: Let us come before his presence, that is, let us first of all cast out of our heart every hindrance to the worship of God, and before we admit any stray thought or empty fancy, let us forestall it, contemplate and honour the presence of God. [[94:2|with psalms|Et in psalmis]], that is, with spiritual canticles and devout songs, [[94:2|make a joyful noise to him|jubilemus ei]], praising him with our mouth, as the Apostle teaches: [[Eph 5:18|be ye filled with the Holy Spirit|Implemini Spiritu Sancto]], [[Eph 5:19|singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord|cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino]] always.

paras.t: Hunc psalmum in principio Matutinarum proferimus, quatenus cor nostrum ex verbis igneis psalmi præsentis, divini amoris calore flammescat, divinumque obsequium hilariter, prompte ac fervide inchoet, non pigra, vaga, frigida, indevotaque mente. Sed et quum soli sumus, dicere possumus : Venite, exsultemus Domino, etc., id est, o omnes vires animæ meæ, tota substantia mea, o omnia quæ intra me sunt, et præsertim, o ratio, voluntas, atque memoria, venite : ita quod ratio consideret divina, voluntas eadem appetat, memoria autem stabiliatur in illis : exsultemus concorditer Domino : sicut jam dictum est.
paras.en: We say this psalm at the beginning of Matins, so that our heart may be set aflame with the heat of divine love by the fiery words of the present psalm, and may begin the divine service gladly, readily and fervently, not with a sluggish, wandering, cold and undevout mind. And even when we are alone we can say: [[94:1|Come let us praise the Lord with joy|Venite, exsultemus Domino]], etc., that is: O all you powers of my soul, my whole substance, O all things that are within me, and above all, O reason, will and memory, come: so that reason may consider divine things, the will desire them, and the memory be made steadfast in them: let us exult together in the Lord, as has already been said.

paras.t: Consequenter assignantur variæ causæ, cur ista agere debeamus. Quoniam Deus Trinitas, seu Christus Deus incarnatus, est magnus Dominus : quoniam in ditione ejus universa sunt posita, et non est qui possit ejus voluntati resistere, ut scriptum est in libro Esther. Ipse quoque est et rex magnus, imo immensus atque omnipotens, super omnes deos, qui per gratiam facti sunt divinæ naturæ consortes, videlicet super omnes Sanctos in cœlo terraque viventes. Omnes enim hi dii, sunt creaturæ summi Dei, ab ejus excellentia infinite deficientes ; et solus Deus est universalis Dominus ac generalis rex. Creaturæ vero sortiuntur ab eo aliquod particulare dominium, specialeque regnum, et comparantur ad Deum sicut ministri ad dominum, instrumenta ad principalem agentem, causæ secundæ ad causam primam ac independentem. Unde Apostolus : Non est potestas nisi a Deo ; et : Qui potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit ; minister enim Dei est, scilicet princeps terrenus. Hinc etiam Jethro cognatus Moysis, auditis mirabilibus Dei, dixit : Nunc cognovi quoniam magnus Dominus super omnes deos.
paras.en: Next, various reasons are given why we ought to do these things. [[94:3|For the Lord|Quoniam Deus]], God the Trinity, or Christ, God incarnate, [[94:3|is a great God|est magnus Dominus]] [Latin *Deus magnus Dominus*, "God is a great Lord"]: for all things are placed under his dominion, and there is none that can resist his will, as is written in the book of Esther[[Esth 13:9||]]. He is also [[94:3|and a great King|et rex magnus]], nay, immeasurable and almighty, [[94:3|above all gods|super omnes deos]], those who through grace have been made partakers of the divine nature, that is, above all the Saints living in heaven and on earth. For all these gods are creatures of the most high God, falling infinitely short of his excellence; and God alone is the universal Lord and the king of all. Creatures receive from him some particular lordship and a special kingdom, and are related to God as ministers to their lord, instruments to the principal agent, second causes to the first and independent cause. Hence the Apostle: [[Rom 13:1|there is no power but from God|Non est potestas nisi a Deo]]; and: [[Rom 13:2|he that resisteth the power resisteth the ordinance of God|Qui potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit]]; [[Rom 13:4|For he is God's minister|minister enim Dei est]], namely the earthly prince. So too Jethro, the kinsman of Moses, having heard of the wonders of God, said: [[Ex 18:11|Now I know, that the Lord is great above all gods|Nunc cognovi quoniam magnus Dominus super omnes deos]].

paras.t: Quoniam non repellet Dominus plebem suam. Hoc ad Judæos referri potest, quos Deus non totaliter destruit, quia reliquiæ per electionem salvæ factæ sunt, secundum Apostolum, et in fine sæculi convertentur ad Christum. Propter quod de eis dicit Apostolus : Numquid repulit Dominus plebem suam ? Absit. Melius tamen exponitur de populo christiano, Christi sacratissimo sanguine liberato, quem Christus non repellit, sicut testatur : Eum qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras. Hæc verba in præcedenti psalmo dicta atque exposita sunt, nec pertinent ad psalmum hunc, quamvis quotidiano Officio annectantur.
paras.en: [[Ps 93:14|For the Lord will not cast off his people|Quoniam non repellet Dominus plebem suam]] [these words, from the preceding psalm, are sung after v. 3 in the Invitatory of the daily Office (from the Roman Psalter); they are not in the Vulgate text of this psalm]. This can be referred to the Jews, whom God does not destroy altogether, since a remnant has been saved through election[[Rom 11:5||]], according to the Apostle, and at the end of the world they will be converted to Christ. That is why the Apostle says of them: [[Rom 11:1|Hath God cast away his people? God forbid!|Numquid repulit Dominus plebem suam ? Absit]] It is better explained, however, of the Christian people, set free by the most sacred blood of Christ, whom Christ does not cast off, as he testifies: [[John 6:37|him that cometh to me, I will not cast out|Eum qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras]]. These words were said and expounded in the preceding psalm, and do not belong to this psalm, although they are joined to it in the daily Office.

paras.t: Deus itaque est rex magnus, etc. Quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, id est, in sua potestate consistunt omnia climata mundi, et habitatores eorum, videlicet omnes gentes.
