Omnia enim creavit, conservat, destruere potest ; et de gentibus quas vult, misericorditer salvat, et quas vult, juste relinquit ac damnat. Et altitudines montium, id est virtutes, perfectiones, et gratiæ angelorum sanctorum, hominumque bonorum seu prædicatorum, ipsius sunt, id est Christi, quoniam omnia bona ab ipso originaliter fluunt. Unde Apostolus : Gratia, inquit, Dei sum id quod sum.
paras.en: God, then, is [[94:3|a great King|rex magnus]], etc. [[94:4|For in his hand are all the ends of the earth|Quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ]], that is, all the regions of the world and their inhabitants, namely all the nations, stand in his power. For he created all things, preserves them, and can destroy them; and of the nations he saves in mercy those he wills, and those he wills he justly leaves and condemns. [[94:4|and the heights of the mountains|Et altitudines montium]], that is, the virtues, perfections and graces of the holy angels, and of good men or preachers, [[94:4|are his|ipsius sunt]], that is, Christ's, since all good things flow from him as from their source. Hence the Apostle: [[1 Cor 15:10|by the grace of God|Gratia]], he says, [[1 Cor 15:10|I am what I am|Dei sum id quod sum]].

paras.t: Quoniam ipsius est mare, id est Oceanus terram circumdans, ex quo cetera maria derivantur, et ipse fecit illud, sicut et cetera elementa. Propter quod Jonas loquitur : Deum cœli ego timeo, qui creavit mare et aridam. Et siccam, id est terram, ex sua natura siccam et frigidam, manus ejus fundaverunt, id est omnipotens virtus Dei, seu sapientia atque potentia ejus, juxta illud : Dominus sapientia fundavit terram.
paras.en: [[94:5|For the sea is his|Quoniam ipsius est mare]], that is, the Ocean that surrounds the earth, from which the other seas are drawn, [[94:5|and he made it|et ipse fecit illud]], as he made the other elements too. That is why Jonas says: I fear [[Jon 1:9|the God of heaven, who made both the sea and the dry land|Deum cœli ego timeo, qui creavit mare et aridam]]. [[94:5|the dry land|Et siccam]], that is, the earth, dry and cold by its nature, [[94:5|his hands formed|manus ejus fundaverunt]] [Denis reads *fundaverunt*, "founded", where the Vulgate has *formaverunt*, "formed"; hence the verse of Proverbs that follows], that is, the almighty power of God, or his wisdom and might, according to that saying: [[Prov 3:19|The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth|Dominus sapientia fundavit terram]].

paras.t: Idcirco Venite : secundum modos prætactos ; adoremus adoratione latriæ, soli Deo exhibenda, et procidamus, id est, humiliter prosternamur, et ploremus præ nimio desiderio existendi cum Deo, et propter nostra et aliorum peccata, ante Dominum qui fecit nos, constituendo nos ipsos in ejus præsentia per contemplationem fidelem : dicentes cum Elia, Vivit Dominus, in cujus conspectu adsistimus ; nullam sinistram intentionem habentes, sed Dei in omnibus quærentes honorem, atque illud Apostoli adimplentes, Unanimes, uno ore honorificetis Deum et Patrem.
paras.en: Therefore [[94:6|Come|Venite]], in the ways already touched on; [[94:6|let us adore|adoremus]] with the adoration of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone], which is to be shown to God alone, [[94:6|and fall down|et procidamus]], that is, let us humbly prostrate ourselves, [[94:6|and weep|et ploremus]] for the exceeding desire of being with God, and on account of our own sins and those of others, [[94:6|before the Lord that made us|ante Dominum qui fecit nos]], setting ourselves in his presence by faithful contemplation, saying with Elias: [[3 Kings 17:1|As the Lord liveth|Vivit Dominus]], [[3 Kings 17:1|in whose sight|in cujus conspectu]] we stand; having no crooked intention, but seeking the honour of God in all things, and fulfilling that word of the Apostle: [[Rom 15:6|with one mind and with one mouth you may glorify God and the Father|Unanimes, uno ore honorificetis Deum et Patrem]].

paras.t: Quia ipse est Dominus Deus noster, qui creavit nos, nosque gubernat, pascit, conservat ac perficit. Ideo subditur : Et nos sumus populus pascuæ ejus, id est, pascuis ejus nutrimur mente et corpore, scilicet cibo ac potu corporali, Sacramento altaris, et gratia devotionis, quæ est optima alimonia mentis, quoniam optimum est gratia stabiliri cor, secundum Apostolum. Sumus quoque et oves manus ejus, id est oves potestatis divinæ, seu in potestate Dei constitutæ, quoniam in manu ejus est tota salus nostra.
paras.en: [[94:7|For he is the Lord our God|Quia ipse est Dominus Deus noster]], who created us, and governs, feeds, preserves and perfects us. Therefore it is added: [[94:7|and we are the people of his pasture|Et nos sumus populus pascuæ ejus]], that is, we are nourished in mind and body by his pastures, namely by bodily food and drink, by the Sacrament of the altar, and by the grace of devotion, which is the best nourishment of the mind, since [[Heb 13:9|it is best that the heart be established with grace|optimum est gratia stabiliri cor]], according to the Apostle. We are also [[94:7|the sheep of his hand|et oves manus ejus]], that is, the sheep of the divine power, or set in the power of God, since in his hand is our whole salvation.

paras.t: Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, etc. Secundum expositionem certissimam sancti Apostoli, ista dicuntur specialiter ad Judæos qui erant tempore evangelicæ prædicationis : quos hortatur Propheta, ut tempore gratiæ evangelicam legem recipiant, ne sint rebelles Filio Dei, quemadmodum patres eorum rebelles fuerunt Deo Patri. Ait ergo : Hodie, id est tempore gratiæ, quod dicitur dies, ut Zacharias ait, In die illa applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum ; et Isaias, In die illa erit germen Domini in magnificentia et gloria ; si vocem ejus, id est prædicationem Christi vel discipulorum ipsius, audieritis, o Judæi, nolite obdurare corda vestra, id est, nolite esse increduli et perversi, sicut in irritatione illa contigit, secundum diem tentationis in deserto, id est in die qua ex incredulitate experiri volebant potentiam meam, et veritatem verborum meorum.
paras.en: [[94:8|To day if you shall hear his voice|Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis]], etc. According to the most certain exposition of the holy Apostle[[Heb 4:11||]] [the margin is partly unreadable and ends "iv. 11"; the Apostle expounds these verses in Heb. iii, 7 – iv, 11], these words are said especially to the Jews who lived at the time of the preaching of the Gospel: the Prophet exhorts them to receive the law of the Gospel in the time of grace, lest they be rebels against the Son of God, as their fathers were rebels against God the Father. He says, then: [[94:8|To day|Hodie]], that is, in the time of grace, which is called a day, as Zacharias says: [[Zach 2:11|many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day|In die illa applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum]]; and Isaias: [[Is 4:2|In that day the bud of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory|In die illa erit germen Domini in magnificentia et gloria]]; [[94:8|if you shall hear his voice|si vocem ejus]] (that is, the preaching of Christ or of his disciples), O Jews, [[94:8|harden not your hearts|nolite obdurare corda vestra]], that is, do not be unbelieving and perverse, [[94:9|As in the provocation|sicut in irritatione]] that took place, [[94:9|according to the day of temptation in the wilderness|secundum diem tentationis in deserto]], that is, on the day when out of unbelief they wished to put to the test my power and the truth of my words.

paras.t: Ubi tentaverunt me patres vestri, in deserto dicentes : Estne Deus in nobis, an non ? Hic loquitur Propheta in persona Dei. Probaverunt per experientiam, quid agere possem, et viderunt oculis propriis opera mea mirabilia in Ægypto, in mari Rubro, atque deserto. Sumitur autem hoc loco, si, pro quia : ut sit sensus, Si vocem ejus audieritis, id est, quia eam audietis. Secundum quem etiam modum loquitur Christus Judæis de Antichristo : Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, et non accepistis me : si alius venerit in nomine suo, illum accipietis.
paras.en: [[94:9|where your fathers tempted me|Ubi tentaverunt me patres vestri]], saying in the desert: [[Ex 17:7|Is the Lord amongst us or not?|Estne Deus in nobis, an non ?]] Here the Prophet speaks in the person of God. [[94:9|they proved me|Probaverunt]] by experience what I could do, [[94:9|and saw|et viderunt]] with their own eyes [[94:9|my works|opera mea]], wonderful works, in Egypt, in the Red Sea and in the desert. Now *if* is taken here for *because*: so that the sense is, [[94:8|if you shall hear his voice|Si vocem ejus audieritis]], that is, because you will hear it. In the same way Christ speaks to the Jews of Antichrist: [[John 5:43|I am come in the name of my Father, and you receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him you will receive|Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, et non accepistis me : si alius venerit in nomine suo, illum accipietis]] [the margin, partly unreadable, ends "43": John 5:43].

paras.t: Hortatur ergo nos Spiritus Sanctus, ne obduremus corda nostra, repellendo a nobis evangelica documenta, dum vocem seu doctrinam Salvatoris audimus, sicut populus ille Hebræorum cor suum obduravit, Deum irritans, id est, ad justam ultionem inducens. Quilibet etiam nostrum, verba hæc ad interiora sua dicere potest hoc modo : Hodie, scilicet in die præsenti, si vocem ejus audieritis, o intellectus, memoria, atque voluntas animæ meæ, nolite obdurare corda vestra : id est proposita vestra : sed auscultate diligenter, tenete memoriter, adimplete viriliter quæcumque vobis dicuntur.
paras.en: The Holy Ghost, then, exhorts us not to harden our hearts by thrusting the teachings of the Gospel away from us when we hear the voice or doctrine of the Saviour, as that people of the Hebrews hardened its heart, provoking God, that is, moving him to just vengeance. Each of us, too, can say these words to his own inward self in this way: [[94:8|To day|Hodie]], that is, on this present day, [[94:8|if you shall hear his voice|si vocem ejus audieritis]], O understanding, memory and will of my soul, [[94:8|harden not your hearts|nolite obdurare corda vestra]], that is, your purposes: but listen carefully, hold in memory, and fulfil manfully whatever is said to you.

paras.t: Quadraginta annis offensus fui generationi illi : id est, populo Judæorum me tentantis irascebar, eum juste castigans toto tempore quo ipsum per desertum duxi, quia (sicut in Deuteronomio legitur) semper contentiose egit contra me. Alia littera habet, Proximus fui generationi huic : quoniam Deus non reliquit eos in toto : imo indesinenter pluit illis manna, præcessitque in die per columnam nubis, in nocte autem per columnam ignis. Propter quod Moyses : Non est, inquit, alia natio tam grandis, quæ habeat deos approximantes sibi, sicut adest Dominus Deus noster cunctis obsecrationibus nostris. Et dixi per angelum ad Moysen, per Moysen quoque ad populum, eum reprehendendo : Semper hi, mihi ingrati et murmuratores increduli, errant corde, falsitati credendo, et illicita appetendo.
paras.en: [[94:10|Forty years long was I offended with that generation|Quadraginta annis offensus fui generationi illi]]: that is, I was angry with the people of the Jews who tempted me, chastising it justly through the whole time that I led it through the desert, because (as we read in Deuteronomy) it always dealt contentiously against me[[Deut 31:27||]]. Another reading has: I was near to this generation [*Proximus fui generationi huic*: the reading of the Roman Psalter, sung in the Invitatory]: for God did not forsake them altogether; nay, he rained down manna on them without ceasing, and went before them by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire. That is why Moses says: [[Deut 4:7|Neither is there|Non est]], he says, [[Deut 4:7|any other nation so great, that hath gods so nigh them, as our God is present to all our petitions|alia natio tam grandis, quæ habeat deos approximantes sibi, sicut adest Dominus Deus noster cunctis obsecrationibus nostris]]. [[94:10|and I said|Et dixi]] by an angel to Moses, and by Moses to the people, rebuking it: [[94:10|These always|Semper hi]], ungrateful to me, murmurers and unbelievers, [[94:10|err in heart|errant corde]], by believing what is false and desiring what is forbidden.

paras.t: Et ipsi non cognoverunt vias meas, id est, mandata mea non agnoverunt per approbationem mentis et obedientiam voluntatis : cognoverunt tamen ea per cognitionem informem, quoniam Moyses legem omnibus manifeste proposuit. Vel : Non cognoverunt vias meas, id est, opera mea miraculosa spiritualiter non intellexerunt, neque ex eis consideraverunt quæ merito considerassent. Hinc namque Moyses ait ad eos : Vos vidistis universa magnalia quæ coram vobis Dominus fecit, et non dedit vobis Dominus cor intelligens usque in præsentem diem. Tales quoque fuerunt filii eorum, scilicet Judæi qui erant tempore Christi et Apostolorum. Propter quod Christus ait ad ipsos : Cæci duces cæcorum, implete mensuram patrum vestrorum. Et Augustinus : Murmuratores, ait, filii murmuratorum. Quibus juravi in ira mea, id est, firmiter dixi per Moysen : Si introibunt in requiem meam, id est, non ingredientur terram promissionis, in qua quietam habitationem eis dedissem, nisi inobedientes fuissent, sicut scriptum est : Omnes qui murmurastis contra me, non intrabitis terram, super quam levavi manum meam ut darem eam vobis. Hic sumitur si, pro non : secundum quem modum accipitur, quum per Amos dicitur, Si erit malum in civitate, quod Dominus non fecit.
paras.en: [[94:11|And these men have not known my ways|Et ipsi non cognoverunt vias meas]], that is, they did not acknowledge my commandments by the approval of the mind and the obedience of the will: yet they knew them with an unformed knowledge [that is, a bare knowledge not quickened by charity], since Moses set the law plainly before them all. Or: They have not known my ways, that is, they did not understand my miraculous works spiritually, nor consider from them what they ought rightly to have considered. For this is why Moses says to them: [[Deut 29:2|You have seen all the things|Vos vidistis universa magnalia]] [Latin *magnalia*, "the great works"] [[Deut 29:2|that the Lord did before you|quæ coram vobis Dominus fecit]], [[Deut 29:4|And the Lord hath not given you a heart to understand|et non dedit vobis Dominus cor intelligens]] [[Deut 29:4|unto this present day|usque in præsentem diem]]. Such too were their sons, namely the Jews who lived at the time of Christ and the Apostles. That is why Christ says to them: [[Matt 15:14|blind, and leaders of the blind|Cæci duces cæcorum]]; [[Matt 23:32|Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers|implete mensuram patrum vestrorum]]. And Augustine says: Murmurers, sons of murmurers. To whom [[94:11|I swore in my wrath|juravi in ira mea]], that is, I said firmly through Moses: [[94:11|that they shall not enter into my rest|Si introibunt in requiem meam]], that is, they shall not enter the land of promise, in which I would have given them a quiet dwelling had they not been disobedient, as it is written: [[Num 14:29|All you that|Omnes qui]] [[Num 14:29|have murmured against me|murmurastis contra me]], [[Num 14:30|Shall not enter into the land, over which I lifted up my hand|non intrabitis terram, super quam levavi manum meam]] to give it to you. Here *if* is taken for *not* [Latin *si introibunt*, literally "if they shall enter"]: in which way it is also taken when it is said by Amos: [[Amos 3:6|Shall there be evil in a city, which the Lord hath not done?|Si erit malum in civitate, quod Dominus non fecit]]

paras.t: Denique, quoniam terra promissionis erat figura regni cœlestis seu patriæ, et quies illius figura fuit quietis Beatorum in cœlis ; idcirco intendit David per verba hæc admonere fideles, et maxime populum Hebræorum, ne propter rebellionem ad Christum, impediantur ab introitu patriæ, quæ est terra viventium, in qua est quies perfecta omnium Beatorum. Propter quod monet Apostolus : Videte, fratres, ne forte sit in aliquo vestrum cor malum discedendi a Deo vivo et vero ; sed adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies, ut non obduretur quis ex vobis fallacia peccati. Et alibi : Festinemus ingredi in illam requiem.
paras.en: Lastly, since the land of promise was a figure of the heavenly kingdom, or fatherland, and its rest was a figure of the rest of the Blessed in heaven, David means by these words to admonish the faithful, and above all the people of the Hebrews, not to be kept from entering the fatherland, which is the land of the living, in which is the perfect rest of all the Blessed, by rebellion against Christ. That is why the Apostle warns: [[Heb 3:12|Take heed, brethren, lest perhaps there be in any of you an evil heart|Videte, fratres, ne forte sit in aliquo vestrum cor malum]], [[Heb 3:12|to depart from the living God|discedendi a Deo vivo]] and true; [[Heb 3:13|But exhort one another every day|sed adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies]], [[Heb 3:13|that none of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin|ut non obduretur quis ex vobis fallacia peccati]]. And elsewhere: [[Heb 4:11|Let us hasten therefore to enter into that rest|Festinemus ingredi in illam requiem]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum omni jucunditate plenum audivimus : psalmum utique igne Spiritus Sancti animam piam totaliter inflammantem : quem decet nos præcipue cum omni attentione atque fervore cantare, audire seu legere in exordio matutinalis Officii, quatenus opus Dei ardenter inchoantes, totum diem salubriter expendamus. Agamus igitur ad quod in psalmo præsenti invitamur ; et dum ad matutinale Officium surgimus, strenue inchoemus, omnes cogitationes inanes et phantasmata inutilia procul a corde pellamus, cum solo Deo cor nostrum sollicite occupemus, dicentes ad interiora nostra, vel ad alios si adsint : Venite, exsultemus Domino, etc. ; et omnes hos nobilissimos actus, ad quos psalmus iste nos excitat, mente collecta ac amorosa exsequamur. Hi etenim actus sunt, Domino exsultare, jubilare, faciem ejus in confessione præoccupare, coram eo adorare, procidere atque plorare.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of all joy: a psalm that wholly sets the devout soul on fire with the fire of the Holy Ghost, which it befits us above all to sing, hear or read with all attention and fervour at the beginning of the morning Office, so that, beginning the work of God ardently, we may spend the whole day profitably. Let us do, then, what we are invited to in the present psalm; and when we rise for the morning Office, let us begin it briskly, drive far from our heart all idle thoughts and useless fancies, and busy our heart earnestly with God alone, saying to our inward selves, or to others if they are present: [[94:1|Come let us praise the Lord with joy|Venite, exsultemus Domino]], etc.; and let us carry out, with a recollected and loving mind, all these most noble acts to which this psalm stirs us. For these are the acts: to exult in the Lord, to rejoice in him, to come before his face in confession, to adore before him, to fall down and to weep.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Tuæ largitatis dono, accepto continuæ pacis bono, exsultemus et jubilemus tibi, Deo salutari nostro : præsta nos cognoscere viam tuam, quam perambulantes, te jurante, intremus in requiem tuam.
paras.en: PRAYER. Having received, by the gift of thy bounty, the good of continual peace, may we exult and sing joyfully to thee, God our saviour: grant us to know thy way, that walking in it we may, as thou hast sworn, enter into thy rest.

94.note: Part of the Latin title could not be read in the transcription.

95.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI NONAGESIMI QUINTI : CANTATE DOMINO CANTICUM NOVUM, CANTATE DOMINO, ETC.
95.title_en: Explanation of the ninety-fifth psalm: Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle, sing to the Lord, etc.

paras.t: Psalmi nunc declarandi titulus est : Psalmus David, quando domus ædificabatur post captivitatem. Titulus iste spiritualiter exponendus est, quoniam psalmus præsens nullatenus loquitur de ædificatione templi in Jerusalem post reditum a captivitate Babylonica, sed de re significata per illius ædificationem templi. Sicut enim per captivitatem, qua a Chaldæis capti erant Judæi, figurata est captivitas generis humani, quod per incredulitatem et impiam vitam captivatum a dæmonibus fuit; sic per ædificationem templi in Jerusalem post captivitatem dictam, significata est constructio Ecclesiæ, quæ est domus Dei, non ex insensibilibus saxis constructa, sed vivis lapidibus, scilicet Christifidelibus congregata, atque a Christo fabricata, et in ipso fundata. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : In Christo omnis ædificatio constructa, crescit in templum sanctum in Domino, in quo et vos coædificamini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto. Loquitur ergo psalmus iste ad litteram de Christo et duplici ejus adventu, de constructione quoque et immolatione Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is: A psalm of David, [[95:1|when the house was built after the captivity|quando domus ædificabatur post captivitatem]]. This title is to be expounded spiritually, since the present psalm in no way speaks of the building of the temple in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian captivity, but of the thing signified by that building of the temple. For as the captivity in which the Jews had been taken by the Chaldeans figured the captivity of the human race, which through unbelief and an impious life had been taken captive by the demons, so the building of the temple in Jerusalem after that captivity signified the building of the Church, which is the house of God, built not of senseless stones but gathered together of living stones[[1 Pet 2:5||]], namely the faithful of Christ, and framed by Christ and founded on him. Wherefore the Apostle says: In Christ [[Eph 2:21|all the building, being framed together, groweth up into an holy temple in the Lord|omnis ædificatio constructa, crescit in templum sanctum in Domino]], [[Eph 2:22|In whom you also are built together into an habitation of God in the Spirit|in quo et vos coædificamini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto]]. This psalm, then, speaks literally of Christ and of his twofold coming, and also of the building up and the immolation [that is, the offering of sacrifice] of the Church.

paras.t: Est igitur sensus tituli : Psalmus David, id est, psalmus iste est David prophetæ sicut auctoris, conscriptus pro tempore illo, quando domus ædificabatur : id est, quando Ecclesia Christi cœpit ædificari per prædicationem ipsius et Apostolorum suorum, post captivitatem, id est post liberationem generis humani, quæ facta est per incarnationem et passionem Filii Dei, qui genus humanum redemit de potestate diaboli et servitute peccati, quemadmodum asserit : Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras ; et ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum. Unde Joannes : In hoc, inquit, apparuit Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera diaboli.
paras.en: The sense of the title, then, is this: A psalm of David, that is, this psalm is of David the prophet as its author, written for that time [[95:1|when the house was built|quando domus ædificabatur]]: that is, when the Church of Christ began to be built through the preaching of Christ himself and of his Apostles; [[95:1|after the captivity|post captivitatem]], that is, after the deliverance of the human race, which was wrought through the incarnation and passion of the Son of God, who redeemed the human race from the power of the devil and the bondage of sin, as he declares: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]; [[John 12:32|And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|et ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]]. Whence John: [[1 John 3:8|For this purpose|In hoc]], he says, [[1 John 3:8|the Son of God appeared, that he might destroy the works of the devil|apparuit Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera diaboli]].

paras.t: Ad Christi itaque seu summæ Trinitatis præconium nos invitans sanctus Propheta, ita exorsus est : Cantate Domino canticum novum, id est novi Testamenti Scripturam, evangelicam legem, et maxime hymnum ex consiliis Christi compositum : cujus consilia quædam ante ejus adventum erant ignota ; sed novus magister, doctor cœlestis, et fons sapientiæ Christus Dominus, novam doctrinam novumque canticum secum advexit, et mundo proposuit. Novum canticum est : Porro unum est necessarium ; et, Si vis perfectus esse, vade, et vende omnia quæ habes et da pauperibus. Itemque, Nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum ; et, Patrem nolite vocare vobis super terram, unus est enim Pater vester in cœlo. Et hoc modo novi Testamenti Scriptura, novis est canticis plena, quæ debemus Christo ac summæ Trinitati cantare, per mentis devotionem, per oris laudationem, seu divinorum verborum reverentialem prolationem, atque per operis exsecutionem seu obedientiam sanctam. Peccatori enim dixit Deus : Quare tu enarras justitias meas, et assumis testamentum meum per os tuum? Et Christus in Evangelio : Quid dicitis mihi, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico? Non ergo sufficit cantatio oris, nisi concordet exhibitio honestæ conversationis. Nec sufficit honestas exterior, nisi adfuerit collectio atque sinceritas mentis interior, prout Dominus per Isaiam ait de populo sibi non complacente : Appropinquat populus iste ore suo, et labiis suis glorificat me ; cor autem ejus longe est a me. Cantate Domino, omnis terra, id est incolæ terræ, qui in hoc mundo peregrinos vos esse cognoscitis, et ad futuri sæculi patriam festinatis, dicentes Domino canticum illud dulce ac novum, quod vobis præcinit Apostolus : Propter nimiam caritatem suam qua dilexit nos Deus Pater, Filium suum unigenitum misit in mundum.
paras.en: Inviting us, then, to the praise of Christ, or of the most high Trinity, the holy Prophet begins thus: [[95:1|Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle|Cantate Domino canticum novum]], that is, the Scripture of the New Testament, the law of the Gospel, and above all the hymn composed of the counsels of Christ, some of which were unknown before his coming; but the new master, the heavenly teacher and fountain of wisdom[[Ecclus 1:5||]], Christ the Lord, brought a new doctrine and a new canticle with him and set it before the world. This is a new canticle: [[Luke 10:42|But one thing is necessary|Porro unum est necessarium]]; and, [[Matt 19:21|If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast, and give to the poor|Si vis perfectus esse, vade, et vende omnia quæ habes et da pauperibus]]. And again: [[Matt 5:20|unless your justice abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]]; and, [[Matt 23:9|call none your father upon earth; for one is your father, who is in heaven|Patrem nolite vocare vobis super terram, unus est enim Pater vester in cœlo]]. And in this way the Scripture of the New Testament is full of new canticles, which we ought to sing to Christ and to the most high Trinity by devotion of mind, by praise of the mouth, or the reverent utterance of the divine words, and by carrying them out in deed, that is, by holy obedience. For [[Ps 49:16|to the sinner God hath said: Why dost thou declare my justices, and take my covenant in thy mouth?|Peccatori enim dixit Deus : Quare tu enarras justitias meas, et assumis testamentum meum per os tuum?]] And Christ in the Gospel: [[Luke 6:46|why call you me, Lord, Lord; and do not the things which I say?|Quid dicitis mihi, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico?]] The singing of the mouth, then, is not enough unless the showing of an upright life agrees with it. Nor is outward uprightness enough unless there be also inward recollection and sincerity of mind, as the Lord says through Isaias of a people that did not please him: [[Is 29:13|this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips glorify me, but their heart is far from me|Appropinquat populus iste ore suo, et labiis suis glorificat me ; cor autem ejus longe est a me]]. [[95:1|sing to the Lord, all the earth|Cantate Domino, omnis terra]], that is, ye inhabitants of the earth, who know yourselves to be pilgrims in this world and are hastening to the homeland of the world to come, singing to the Lord that sweet and new canticle which the Apostle sings before you: [[Eph 2:4|for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us|Propter nimiam caritatem suam qua dilexit nos]], God the Father [[1 John 4:9|hath sent his only begotten Son into the world|Filium suum unigenitum misit in mundum]].

paras.t: Cantate Domino, et benedicite nomini ejus, id est, ipsum laudate, beneficia ejus recolite, dicentes cum jubilo : Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus. Dicitur autem canticum novum, non solum propter temporis novitatem, sed etiam propter recentem animi devotionem : et ita debemus ex ferventi nostri Salvatoris amore, semper nova cantica secundum proprii cordis illuminationem reperire, quomodo sæculi amatores nova carmina confingunt et canunt de eo seu ea quam carnaliter amant. Annuntiate de die in diem, id est quotidie, salutare ejus, id est, Christum indesinenter exprimite, collaudate ac prædicate, per quem et in quo Deus Pater nos salvat. De quo salutari loquitur Jacob patriarcha : Salutare tuum exspectabo, Domine.
paras.en: [[95:2|Sing ye to the Lord and bless his name|Cantate Domino, et benedicite nomini ejus]], that is, praise him, call his benefits to mind, saying with jubilation: [[1 John 3:1|Behold what manner of charity the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called and should be the sons of God|Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus]]. Now it is called a new canticle not only because of the newness of the time, but also because of the fresh devotion of the soul; and so, out of fervent love for our Saviour, we ought always to find new canticles according to the enlightening of our own heart, as lovers of the world make up and sing new songs about him or her whom they love carnally. [[95:2|shew forth|Annuntiate]] [[95:2|from day to day|de die in diem]], that is, daily, [[95:2|his salvation|salutare ejus]]: that is, unceasingly express, praise and preach Christ, through whom and in whom God the Father saves us. Of this salvation the patriarch Jacob speaks: [[Gen 49:18|I will look for thy salvation, O Lord|Salutare tuum exspectabo, Domine]].

paras.t: Annuntiate, o prædicatores, et ceteri zelum divini honoris atque fraternæ salutis habentes, inter gentes convertendas ad fidem, ut credant, seu conversas, ut diligant Christum ac laudent, gloriam ejus; in omnibus populis mirabilia ejus, id est gloriosa omnia quæ de eo conscripta sunt : quomodo ab exordio suæ incarnationis usque ad ascensionem angeli sancti sibi ministraverunt, et omnis creatura sibi obediens fuit; quod tertia die a morte surrexit, quadragesima die ascendit, quinquagesima autem Paracletum misit.
paras.en: [[95:3|Declare|Annuntiate]], O ye preachers, and all others who have zeal for God's honour and for the salvation of their brethren, [[95:3|among the Gentiles|inter gentes]] that are to be converted to the faith, that they may believe, or that are converted, that they may love and praise Christ, [[95:3|his glory|gloriam ejus]]; [[95:3|among all people|in omnibus populis]] [[95:3|his wonders|mirabilia ejus]], that is, all the glorious things that are written of him: how from the beginning of his incarnation until his ascension the holy angels ministered to him[[Matt 4:11||]], and every creature obeyed him[[Matt 8:27||]]; how on the third day he rose from death, on the fortieth day ascended, and on the fiftieth sent the Paraclete.

paras.t: Quoniam magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis, imo tantum laudabilis, quantum bonus. Quum ergo sit bonitas ejus immensa, ipse quoque in infinitum laudabilis est, nec valet ab aliqua creatura plene laudari. Propter quod in libro Judith dicitur: Adonai Domine, magnus es tu et præclarus in virtute. In libro quoque Job: Digne eum invenire non possumus, et enarrari non potest. Terribilis est super omnes deos, id est plus quam omnes dii. Vel, Super omnes deos, quoniam omnes deos terribiliter condemnabit et cruciabit. In præcedenti enim psalmo dii vocati sunt, qui gratiam divinæ perfectionis excellenter participant, sicut ad Moysen Dominus ait, Ecce constitui te deum Pharaonis, et Aaron erit propheta tuus; nunc vero dii vocantur, qui a paganis mendaciter dii putantur, inaniterque coluntur. Dicitur autem Deus terribilis præ omnibus creaturis ac diis, propter duas causas: primo, quoniam a nullo est tam malum separari, sicut a Deo; secundo, quoniam nullus tam dira tormenta infligit, ut Deus. Unde scriptum est: Deus, cujus iræ nemo resistere potest, sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem. De his falsis diis subjungitur: Quoniam omnes dii gentium, id est infidelium, sunt dæmonia.
paras.en: [[95:4|For the Lord is great, and exceedingly to be praised|Quoniam magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis]], nay, as much to be praised as he is good. Since, then, his goodness is immeasurable, he too is to be praised without limit, and cannot be fully praised by any creature. Wherefore it is said in the book of Judith: [[Jdt 16:16|O Adonai, Lord, great art thou, and glorious in thy power|Adonai Domine, magnus es tu et præclarus in virtute]]. And in the book of Job: [[Job 37:23|We cannot find him worthily|Digne eum invenire non possumus]], [[Job 37:23|and he is ineffable|et enarrari non potest]]. [[95:4|he is to be feared above all gods|Terribilis est super omnes deos]], that is, more than all gods. Or, *above all gods*, because he will terribly condemn and torment all the gods. For in the preceding psalm[[Ps 94:3||]] those were called gods who share in an excellent way in the grace of the divine perfection, as the Lord said to Moses: [[Ex 7:1|Behold, I have appointed thee the god of Pharao; and Aaron, thy brother, shall be thy prophet|Ecce constitui te deum Pharaonis, et Aaron erit propheta tuus]]; but here those are called gods who are falsely thought to be gods by the pagans and are worshipped in vain. Now God is called terrible [*terribilis*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "to be feared"] above all creatures and gods for two reasons: first, because from no one is it so evil to be separated as from God; secondly, because no one inflicts such dreadful torments as God. Whence it is written: [[Job 9:13|God, whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world|Deus, cujus iræ nemo resistere potest, sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem]]. Of these false gods it is added: [[95:5|For all the gods of the Gentiles|Quoniam omnes dii gentium]], that is, of the unbelievers, [[95:5|are devils|sunt dæmonia]].

paras.t: Occurrit mihi hic dubitatio quædam, quam non vidi ab aliis tactam, unde nec eam libenter tango, ne forte eam insufficienter dissolvam. Ecce multi gentilium coluerunt homines quosdam pro diis, videlicet Saturnum, Jovem, Mercurium, Herculem, Priapum, etc. Alii coluerunt solem, lunam, ac sidera cœli, alii ignem, alii aquam, alii bestias terræ, sicut ad Romanos Apostolus innuit. Quomodo ergo omnes dii gentium, dæmonia? Possem de hominibus impiis, qui tanquam dii colebantur, respondere, quod appellantur dæmonia propter imitationem diabolicæ pravitatis, quemadmodum homines aliqui, angeli nuncupantur propter participationem angelicæ dignitatis: prout Joannes pastores seu episcopos septem Ecclesiarum in Asia angelos nominat, et alibi sacerdos dicitur angelus Domini exercituum. De aliis videtur posse dici, quod licet nullo modo sint dæmones, quoniam tamen cultores ipsorum eo ipso quo ea colunt, dæmonibus serviunt, idcirco omnes dii gentium dæmonia asseruntur. Nam et Apostolus ad Corinthios dicit: Quæ immolant gentes, dæmoniis immolant, et non Deo.
paras.en: Here a certain doubt occurs to me which I have not seen touched on by others, and so I do not touch it willingly either, lest perhaps I resolve it insufficiently. Behold, many of the Gentiles worshipped certain men as gods, namely Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, Hercules, Priapus, etc. Others worshipped the sun, the moon and the stars of heaven, others fire, others water, others the beasts of the earth, as the Apostle intimates to the Romans[[Rom 1:23||]]. How then are [[95:5|all the gods of the Gentiles|omnes dii gentium]] [[95:5|devils|dæmonia]]? Of the impious men who were worshipped as gods I could answer that they are called devils because they imitated the wickedness of the devil, just as some men are called angels because they share in the dignity of the angels: as John names the pastors or bishops of the seven Churches in Asia angels[[Apoc 1:20||]] [the margin gives Apoc. i–iii], and elsewhere the priest is called [[Mal 2:7|the angel of the Lord of hosts|angelus Domini exercituum]]. Of the others it seems it may be said that, although they are in no way demons, yet since their worshippers, by the very fact that they worship them, serve demons, all the gods of the Gentiles are for that reason declared to be devils. For the Apostle too says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 10:20|the things which the heathens sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils and not to God|Quæ immolant gentes, dæmoniis immolant, et non Deo]].

paras.t: Dominus autem cœlos fecit, id est, omnes orbes cœlestes, angelos sanctos, hominesque in terra cœliformiter conversantes creavit, distinxit, ornavit. In principio enim creavit Deus cœlum et terram, ut dicitur in Genesi. Et rursus scriptum est: Tu fortassis cum eo fabricatus es cœlos, qui solidissimi quasi ære fusi sunt.
paras.en: [[95:5|but the Lord made the heavens|Dominus autem cœlos fecit]], that is, he created, distinguished and adorned all the heavenly spheres, the holy angels, and the men who live a heavenly life on earth. For [[Gen 1:1|In the beginning God created heaven, and earth|In principio enim creavit Deus cœlum et terram]], as is said in Genesis. And again it is written: [[Job 37:18|Thou perhaps hast made the heavens with him, which are most strong, as if they were of molten brass|Tu fortassis cum eo fabricatus es cœlos, qui solidissimi quasi ære fusi sunt]].

paras.t: Confessio et pulchritudo in conspectu ejus; sanctimonia et magnificentia in sanctificatione ejus. Versus iste decorus est valde, si lucide intelligatur. Dicitur autem esse seu fieri in conspectu Dei, seu coram Deo, non quia fit et est ipso præsente, sed quoniam approbatur ab eo, et complacet ei, sicut in libro Ruth dicitur: Jesse genuit David, qui ambulavit coram Domino. Et Dominus ait ad Abraham: Ambula coram me. Et quasi quæreres, Quid est ambulare, o Domine, coram te? subdit, Et esto perfectus. Et juxta hunc sensum scriptum est: Non veniet in conspectu Dei omnis hypocrita. Porro confessio est duplex, scilicet confessio laudis divinæ, atque confessio propriæ culpæ. Pulchritudo etiam quædam interior est, quædam exterior. Sed si propter exteriorem pulchritudinem placeret quis Deo, pulcherrimus Absalon tantum ei non displicuisset, neque delirus ille Martinus tantum ei complacuisset. Non ergo corporis, sed mentis pulchritudinem appetamus. Certum est autem, quod confessio culpæ locum non habet in patria. In via autem utraque confessio reperitur; sed confessio laudis divinæ in via, valde est imperfecta.
paras.en: [[95:6|Praise and beauty are before him: holiness and majesty in his sanctuary|Confessio et pulchritudo in conspectu ejus; sanctimonia et magnificentia in sanctificatione ejus]]. This verse is very beautiful if it is clearly understood. A thing is said to be or to be done *in the sight* of God, or before God, not because it is done and exists in his presence, but because it is approved by him and is pleasing to him; as it is said in the book of Ruth: [[Ruth 4:22|Isai begot David|Jesse genuit David]], who walked before the Lord [the margin has "cf."; the words "who walked before the Lord" are not in Ruth]. And the Lord said to Abraham: [[Gen 17:1|walk before me|Ambula coram me]]. And as though you asked, What is it, O Lord, to walk before thee? he adds: [[Gen 17:1|and be perfect|Et esto perfectus]]. And in this sense it is written: [[Job 13:16|no hypocrite shall come before his presence|Non veniet in conspectu Dei omnis hypocrita]]. Now confession [*confessio*, which the Douay-Rheims here renders "praise"] is twofold: the confession of God's praise, and the confession of one's own guilt. Beauty too is partly inward, partly outward. But if anyone pleased God because of outward beauty, the most beautiful Absalom[[2 Kings 14:25||]] would not have displeased him so much, nor would that witless Martin have pleased him so much [Denis does not say who this Martin was]. Let us therefore seek beauty not of body but of mind. Now it is certain that the confession of guilt has no place in the homeland; but on the way [that is, in this life] both confessions are found; yet the confession of God's praise on the way is very imperfect.

paras.t: Primo itaque intendamus, quomodo præsens versiculus exponi debeat de Deo in triumphanti Ecclesia. Sic enim ei plenissime competit hoc modo : Confessio, id est divina laudatio, et pulchritudo, id est decor interior, seu splendor puritatis internæ, est in conspectu ejus, id est coram Deo in patria, ita quod Sancti in patria Deo incessabiliter offerunt confessionem seu laudem suæ infinitæ bonitatis, sicut superius dictum est : Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine; in sæcula sæculorum laudabunt te. Hæc autem confessio maxime complacet Deo, quia in suis ministris ipsum in patria ita laudantibus est pulchritudo interior, id est sanctitas pura, munditia impermixta, et gratia consummata. Nil enim imperfectionis culpabilis reperitur in patria. Propterea confessio Beatorum, quorum tanta est pulchritudo, præcipue grata est Deo. Nostra autem confessio multum est imperfecta, quoniam omnes nostræ justitiæ sunt tanquam pannus menstruatæ. Pulchritudo quoque nostra interior, multis deformitatibus, saltem venialium peccatorum, miscetur et violatur, præsertim quum justus septies in die cadat. Itaque in conspectu Dei in patria, sunt confessio incessabilis laudis, qua jugiter a Beatis Trinitas superbenedicta laudatur; et pulchritudo mundissimæ sanctitatis, quoniam nihil impuritatis aut culpæ esse potest in ministris, Deum hoc modo laudantibus. Propter quod scriptum est : Non intrabit in illam, scilicet patriam Beatorum, aliquid coinquinatum. Dicitur etiam ista confessio et pulchritudo, In conspectu Dei, quoniam complacet ei. — Sanctimonia et magnificentia in sanctificatione ejus : id est, in cultu, laude, seu veneratione qua Deus in patria a Beatis sanctificatur, est sanctimonia, id est sanctitas, scilicet omnis impuritatis exclusio, et magnificentia, id est magna excellentia, seu magna efficientia et honor sublimis. Hoc autem divinæ sanctificationi præcipue competit.
paras.en: Let us first consider, then, how the present verse is to be expounded of God in the Church triumphant; for in this way it fits him most fully, thus: [[95:6|Praise|Confessio]], that is, the praise of God, [[95:6|and beauty|et pulchritudo]], that is, inward comeliness, or the splendour of inward purity, [[95:6|are before him|in conspectu ejus]], that is, before God in the homeland; so that the Saints in the homeland unceasingly offer God confession, or praise, of his infinite goodness, as was said above: [[Ps 83:5|Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: they shall praise thee for ever and ever|Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine; in sæcula sæculorum laudabunt te]]. And this confession is most pleasing to God, because in his ministers who thus praise him in the homeland there is inward beauty, that is, pure holiness, unmixed cleanness and consummate grace; for nothing of culpable imperfection is found in the homeland. Therefore the confession of the Blessed, whose beauty is so great, is especially pleasing to God. But our confession is very imperfect, since [[Is 64:6|all our justices as the rag of a menstruous woman|omnes nostræ justitiæ sunt tanquam pannus menstruatæ]]. Our inward beauty too is mingled with and marred by many deformities, at least of venial sins, especially since [[Prov 24:16|a just man shall fall seven times|justus septies]] a day. So in the sight of God in the homeland there are the confession of unceasing praise, by which the superblessed Trinity is continually praised by the Blessed, and the beauty of most pure holiness, since there can be nothing of impurity or guilt in the ministers who praise God in this way. Wherefore it is written: [[Apoc 21:27|There shall not enter into it|Non intrabit in illam]], namely the homeland of the Blessed, [[Apoc 21:27|any thing defiled|aliquid coinquinatum]]. This confession and beauty are also said to be *in the sight of God*, because they are pleasing to him. — [[95:6|holiness and majesty in his sanctuary|Sanctimonia et magnificentia in sanctificatione ejus]] [*in sanctificatione ejus*, literally "in his sanctification"]: that is, in the worship, praise or veneration by which God is sanctified [that is, acknowledged and honoured as holy] by the Blessed in the homeland, there is *sanctimonia*, that is, holiness, namely the exclusion of all impurity, and *magnificentia*, that is, great excellence, or great efficacy and lofty honour. And this belongs above all to the sanctification of God.

paras.t: Dicitur namque nunc sanctificatio Dei, cultus quo Deus a Beatis sanctus esse perhibetur, et tanquam sanctus laudatur ac honoratur. In hac vero sanctificatione est sanctitas seu sanctimonia, quia quo Deus amplius atque perfectius a suis ministris sanctificatur, eo sanctificatio illa est verior, purior, et ab omni errore immunior : quia Dei laudatio excessum non habet ; sed quo major, eo est sanctior. Unde in Ecclesiastico dicitur : Glorificate Dominum quantumcumque poteritis, supervalebit adhuc : major est enim omni laude. Hoc autem creaturis non competit. Possent namque in tantum sanctificari a nobis, id est tam sanctæ ac magnæ putari, tamque magnifice honorari, quod in sanctificatione hujusmodi non esset sanctimonia, sed idololatria ; non sanctitas, sed falsitas ; non verus honor, sed pessimus error : sicut si alicui puræ creaturæ cultus latriæ impendatur, seu infinita perfectio adscribatur. Hinc patet, quomodo in sanctificatione Dei sit magnificentia. Est enim in ea summa excellentia, quoniam Deus super omnia in infinitum extollitur, omniumque Creator, Salvator, atque immensæ majestatis Dominus appellatur. Est quoque in ea magna quædam efficientia, quoniam nullus effectus seu actus hominis dignior est, quam Deum sanctificare : propter quod in sanctificatione hac est honor sublimis, videlicet adoratio seu latriæ cultus, soli Deo exhibendus.
paras.en: For by the sanctification of God is here meant the worship by which God is declared by the Blessed to be holy, and is praised and honoured as holy. And in this sanctification there is sanctity, or *sanctimonia*, because the more fully and perfectly God is sanctified by his ministers, the truer, the purer and the freer from all error that sanctification is: for the praise of God admits no excess, but the greater it is, the holier it is. Whence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 43:32|Glorify the Lord as much as ever you can, for he will yet far exceed|Glorificate Dominum quantumcumque poteritis, supervalebit adhuc]]: [[Ecclus 43:33|for he is above all praise|major est enim omni laude]]. But this does not hold for creatures. For they could be sanctified by us so far, that is, be thought so holy and great and be honoured so magnificently, that in such sanctification there would be not holiness but idolatry; not sanctity but falsehood; not true honour but the worst error: as if the worship of latria [that is, the adoration due to God alone] were paid to some mere creature, or infinite perfection ascribed to it. Hence it is plain how there is magnificence [*magnificentia*, rendered "majesty" in the Douay-Rheims] in the sanctification of God. For there is in it the highest excellence, since God is extolled infinitely above all things, and is called the Creator of all, the Saviour, and the Lord of immeasurable majesty. There is also in it a great efficacy, since no effect or act of man is worthier than to sanctify God: and therefore in this sanctification there is lofty honour, namely adoration, or the worship of latria, which is to be shown to God alone.

paras.t: Præterea versus iste convenit Deo etiam in militanti Ecclesia, quamvis minus perfecte ac proprie. In militanti ergo Ecclesia est confessio propriæ culpæ, ac laudis divinæ, in conspectu Dei : quoniam talis confessio Deo a fidelibus reverenter offertur, qui se ipsos accusant, et Deum collaudant, atque a Deo misericorditer acceptatur. Per hanc vero confessionem venitur ad interiorem pulchritudinem mentis, quoniam in confessione omnia lavantur, secundum Scripturas. Student quoque fideles Deo in pulchritudine mentis adsistere, id est in sanctitate et cordis puritate adhærere, intendere atque servire, ut sit pulchritudo eorum coram Deo, id est placens et grata coram eo, pensantes verbum sui Salvatoris, dicentis : Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt. In sanctificatione quoque, qua Deum per obedientiam divinorum præceptorum sanctificant, sicut quotidie orant, Sanctificetur nomen tuum, est sanctimonia seu sanctitas secundum modum et possibilitatem vitæ præsentis, videlicet pura ac pia intentio, devotaque laus ac prompta subjectio : et ita invenitur in ea quædam magnificentia, qua Deum præ omnibus mente, ore ac opere superexaltant, dicentes illud Danielis : Benedictus es, Domine, Deus patrum nostrorum, et laudabilis, et superexaltatus in sæcula. Et benedictum nomen gloriæ tuæ sanctum, et superlaudabile, et superexaltatum in omnibus sæculis.
paras.en: Moreover, this verse fits God in the Church militant too, though less perfectly and properly. In the Church militant, then, there is confession of one's own guilt and of God's praise *in the sight of God*: since such confession is reverently offered to God by the faithful, who accuse themselves and praise God, and is mercifully accepted by God. And by this confession one comes to the inward beauty of the mind, since in confession all things are washed, according to the Scriptures[[Ps 31:5||]][[Rom 10:10||]]. The faithful also strive to stand before God in beauty of mind, that is, to cleave to him, attend to him and serve him in holiness and purity of heart, so that their beauty may be *before God*, that is, pleasing and acceptable before him, weighing the word of their Saviour, who says: [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]]. In the sanctification too by which they sanctify God through obedience to the divine commandments, as they pray daily, [[Matt 6:9|hallowed be thy name|Sanctificetur nomen tuum]] [*sanctificetur*, literally "be sanctified"], there is *sanctimonia*, or holiness, according to the measure and possibility of the present life, namely a pure and devout intention, devout praise and ready submission; and so there is found in it a certain magnificence, by which they exalt God above all things in mind, mouth and deed, saying those words of Daniel: [[Dan 3:52|Blessed art thou, O Lord, the God of our fathers; and worthy to be praised, and glorified, and exalted above all for ever: and blessed is the holy name of thy glory: and worthy to be praised and exalted above all, in all ages|Benedictus es, Domine, Deus patrum nostrorum, et laudabilis, et superexaltatus in sæcula. Et benedictum nomen gloriæ tuæ sanctum, et superlaudabile, et superexaltatum in omnibus sæculis]].

paras.t: Afferte, id est exhibete, Domino Salvatori, o patriæ gentium, id est, o homines in patriis gentium habitantes, qui fidem Christi recepistis. Vel : o homines, afferte Domino patriæ gentium, id est Christo, qui est Deus omnium regionum, patriarum, ac nationum. Afferte, inquam, Domino, id est, impendite Deo soli, gloriam et honorem : quemadmodum in Apostolo habetur : Regi sæculorum, immortali, invisibili, soli Deo honor et gloria. Gloria est clara cum laude notitia, secundum Ambrosium. Quid est ergo Deo afferre gloriam, nisi nomen ejus coram aliis clarificare, seu alios ad claram ac laudi conjunctam notitiam Dei introducere, quatenus Deum vere agnoscant, et digne collaudent? Honor autem est exhibitio reverentiæ in signum virtutis. Quid est ergo Deo afferre honorem, nisi Deo humiliter obedire, omne bonum ei adscribere, et ad ejus venerationem omnia ordinare? Afferte Domino non solum exteriora dona, sed gloriam nomini ejus, dicentes : Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam. In exordio psalmi hujus ter dicebatur, Cantate ; nunc vero ter dicitur, Afferte : quatenus utrobique sanctæ Trinitatis mysterium designetur. Tanquam diceret : Cantate Patri, cantate Filio, cantate Spiritui Sancto. Et item : Afferte Patri, afferte Filio, afferte Spiritui Sancto gloriam et honorem.
paras.en: [[95:7|Bring ye|Afferte]], that is, present, [[95:7|to the Lord|Domino]] the Saviour, [[95:7|O ye kindreds of the Gentiles|patriæ gentium]], that is, O ye men dwelling in the countries of the Gentiles, who have received the faith of Christ. Or: O men, bring to the Lord of the kindreds of the Gentiles [*patriæ gentium* read as genitive], that is, to Christ, who is God of all regions, countries and nations. [[95:7|bring ye|Afferte]], I say, [[95:7|to the Lord|Domino]], that is, render to God alone, [[95:7|glory and honour|gloriam et honorem]]: as is found in the Apostle: [[1 Tim 1:17|to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory|Regi sæculorum, immortali, invisibili, soli Deo honor et gloria]]. Glory is clear knowledge together with praise, according to Ambrose. What then is it to bring glory to God, but to make his name known before others, or to lead others to a clear knowledge of God joined with praise, so that they may truly know God and worthily praise him? Honour, again, is the showing of reverence in token of virtue. What then is it to bring honour to God, but to obey God humbly, to ascribe every good to him, and to order all things to his veneration? [[95:8|Bring to the Lord|Afferte Domino]] not only outward gifts but [[95:8|glory unto his name|gloriam nomini ejus]], saying: [[Ps 113:9|Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory|Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam]] [the margin gives Ps. xxv, 1 "according to the Hebrew", evidently for cxv, 1, which is Ps 113:9 in the Vulgate]. At the beginning of this psalm *Sing ye* was said three times; now *Bring ye* is said three times, so that in both places the mystery of the holy Trinity may be signified. As if he said: Sing to the Father, sing to the Son, sing to the Holy Ghost. And again: Bring glory and honour to the Father, bring them to the Son, bring them to the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Tollite hostias, id est, ferte vobiscum dona ac sacrificia Domino immolanda, videlicet : spiritum contribulatum, quoniam sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus ; animum ad obedientiam Dei paratum, quoniam salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, ut dicit Ecclesiasticus ; preces quoque devotas, quæ penetrant cœlos, seu alia quælibet munera Domino offerenda. Et introite mente devota, et corpore rationi subjecto, in atria ejus, id est in Ecclesiam Dei, seu loca sacrata, divino cultui deputata, et maxime in corda propria, redeuntes ad interiora vestra, quatenus Deum intra vos honoretis, contemplando, amando, et omni custodia vitia devitando. Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos.
paras.en: [[95:8|Bring up sacrifices|Tollite hostias]], that is, carry with you gifts and sacrifices to be offered to the Lord, namely: an afflicted spirit, since [[Ps 50:19|A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit|sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus]]; a mind ready to obey God, since [[Ecclus 35:2|It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments|salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis]], as Ecclesiasticus says; devout prayers too, which pierce the heavens[[Ecclus 35:21||]], or any other gifts to be offered to the Lord. [[95:8|and come|Et introite]] with devout mind and with body subject to reason [[95:8|into his courts|in atria ejus]], that is, into the Church of God, or holy places set apart for divine worship, and above all into your own hearts, returning to what is within you, so as to honour God within you by contemplating, by loving, and by shunning vices with all watchfulness. For [[1 Cor 3:17|the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos]].

paras.t: Adorate Dominum in atrio sancto ejus, id est in templo suo materiali, quod est domus orationis ; magis autem in templo ejus immateriali, quod est mens ipsa seu spiritus, ubi per gratiam habitat Deus, ubi et adorare eum oportet, quemadmodum ait Salvator : Spiritus est Deus ; et eos qui adorant eum, in spiritu et veritate oportet adorare. Et alibi : Tu autem quum oraveris, intra in cubiculum tuum ; et clauso ostio, ora Patrem tuum in abscondito, scilicet corde collecto, fixo, non vago. Commoveatur a facie ejus universa terra : id est, universi incolæ terræ ex consideratione præsentiæ majestatisque Christi, motu casti timoris et admirationis ac obedientiæ, convertantur ab iniquitate ad Deum.
paras.en: [[95:9|Adore ye the Lord in his holy court|Adorate Dominum in atrio sancto ejus]], that is, in his material temple, which is [[Is 56:7|the house of prayer|domus orationis]]; but more in his immaterial temple, which is the mind itself or the spirit, where God dwells by grace, and where too he must be adored, as the Saviour says: [[John 4:24|God is a spirit: and they that adore him must adore him in spirit and in truth|Spiritus est Deus ; et eos qui adorant eum, in spiritu et veritate oportet adorare]]. And elsewhere: [[Matt 6:6|But thou when thou shalt pray, enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father in secret|Tu autem quum oraveris, intra in cubiculum tuum ; et clauso ostio, ora Patrem tuum in abscondito]], namely with the heart recollected, fixed, not wandering. [[95:9|Let all the earth be moved at his presence|Commoveatur a facie ejus universa terra]]: that is, let all the inhabitants of the earth, from the consideration of the presence and majesty of Christ, by a movement of chaste fear, of wonder and of obedience, be turned from iniquity to God.

paras.t: Dicite, o sancti Apostoli et successores ac imitatores eorum, in gentibus, ad quarum conversionem seu informationem missi estis, quia Dominus Christus regnavit in toto universo, præsertim tamen in cordibus suorum fidelium per caritatem et fidem. Christus ut Deus, ab initio mundi regnavit ; sed ut homo, cœpit regnare (id est potestatem suam exercere atque ostendere) præcipue post resurrectionem et Spiritus Sancti missionem : quia per mortem vicit eum qui mortis habebat imperium, id est diabolum, secundum Apostolum. Unde post resurrectionem spoliavit infernum, mundumque convertit ad suum obsequium. Et quia hæc facta sunt merito passionis Christi, juxta illud Apostoli, Factus est obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis, propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum; ideo additur, A ligno, id est a crucis patibulo, in quo mundum redemit, secundum quod Apostolus dicit : Christus nos redemit de maledicto legis, factus pro nobis maledictum, quia scriptum est, Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno. Verumtamen istud quod dicitur, A ligno, non est de textu, nec in Hebræo habetur, sed ab aliquo translatore æstimatur appositum. Ex his elucescit, psalmum præsentem factum a David, sicut in hymno Ecclesiæ canitur : Impleta sunt quæ concinit / David fideli carmine, / Dicens : In nationibus / Regnavit a ligno Deus. Et qui aliter dicunt, non videntur satis consonare Ecclesiæ, generaliter atque solenniter hunc hymnum canenti.
paras.en: [[95:10|Say ye|Dicite]], O holy Apostles, and you their successors and imitators, [[95:10|among the Gentiles|in gentibus]] to whose conversion or instruction you have been sent, [[95:10|the Lord|quia Dominus]] Christ [[95:10|hath reigned|regnavit]] in the whole universe, yet especially in the hearts of his faithful through charity and faith. Christ as God has reigned from the beginning of the world; but as man he began to reign (that is, to exercise and show his power) chiefly after the resurrection and the sending of the Holy Ghost: because through death he overcame [[Heb 2:14|him who had the empire of death, that is to say, the devil|eum qui mortis habebat imperium, id est diabolum]], according to the Apostle. Hence after the resurrection he despoiled hell and turned the world to his service. And because these things were done through the merit of Christ's passion, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Phil 2:8|becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross|Factus est obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis]]: [[Phil 2:9|For which cause, God also hath exalted him|propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum]]; therefore it is added, *From the tree* [Denis's text reads *Dominus regnavit a ligno*, "the Lord hath reigned from the tree"; the words are not in the Vulgate or the Douay-Rheims], that is, from the gibbet of the cross, on which he redeemed the world, as the Apostle says: [[Gal 3:13|Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us|Christus nos redemit de maledicto legis, factus pro nobis maledictum]], for it is written, [[Gal 3:13|Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree|Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno]][[Deut 21:23||]]. Yet this *From the tree* is not part of the text, nor is it found in the Hebrew, but is thought to have been added by some translator. From this it is clear that the present psalm was made by David, as is sung in the Church's hymn: Fulfilled are the things that David sang in faithful song, saying: Among the nations God hath reigned from the tree [from the hymn *Vexilla Regis* of Venantius Fortunatus]. And those who say otherwise do not seem to agree well enough with the Church, which sings this hymn everywhere and solemnly.

paras.t: Etenim Christus correxit orbem terræ, id est, homines universos, seu universalem Ecclesiam, toto orbe terrarum diffusam, a vitiis et idololatria convertit, per increpationem et prædicationem servorum suorum. Unde scriptum habetur : Elevabitur Dominus solus in die illa, et idola penitus conterentur. Et Zacharias : In die illa, dicit Dominus, disperdam nomina idolorum de terra. Hinc quoque de Christo dicitur : Percutiet terram virga oris sui. Correxit itaque orbem terræ, qui non commovebitur a fidei veritate in toto, quia Ecclesia usque ad finem sæculi stabilietur in fide, quantum ad aliquos, quantumcumque tribulationibus concutiatur. Judicabit populos in æquitate. Christus in primo suo adventu judicavit populos in æquitate (loquendo de judicio discretionis), quemadmodum ipsemet ait : Nunc judicium est mundi. Et alibi : In judicium, inquit, ego in hunc mundum veni, ut qui non vident, videant; et qui vident, cæci fiant. Per hoc ergo Christus judicavit populos in æquitate judicio discretionis, quod aliquos pie vocavit ad fidem et gratiam, ceteros juste deseruit : quæ discretio omnino justa est, quamvis sit nobis incomprehensibilis et ignota. Non autem judicavit Christus populos in primo suo adventu judicio remunerationis. Propter quod ait : Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum ut judicet mundum. Sed istud judicium Christus acturus est in die novissimo.
paras.en: [[95:10|For he hath corrected the world|Etenim Christus correxit orbem terræ]], Christ, that is: he turned all men, or the universal Church spread throughout the whole world, from vices and idolatry, through the rebuke and preaching of his servants. Whence it is written: [[Is 2:17|the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day|Elevabitur Dominus solus in die illa]], [[Is 2:18|And idols shall be utterly destroyed|et idola penitus conterentur]]. And Zacharias: [[Zach 13:2|in that day, saith the Lord|In die illa, dicit Dominus]], [[Zach 13:2|I will destroy the names of idols out of the earth|disperdam nomina idolorum de terra]]. Hence too it is said of Christ: [[Is 11:4|he shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth|Percutiet terram virga oris sui]]. He corrected the world, then, [[95:10|which shall not be moved|qui non commovebitur]] from the truth of the faith as a whole, because the Church will be kept firm in the faith until the end of the world, as regards some at least, however much it may be shaken by tribulations. [[95:10|he will judge the people with justice|Judicabit populos in æquitate]]. Christ in his first coming judged the peoples in equity (speaking of the judgment of discernment), as he himself says: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world|Nunc judicium est mundi]]. And elsewhere: [[John 9:39|For judgment|In judicium]], he says, [[John 9:39|I am come into this world: that they who see not may see; and they who see may become blind|ego in hunc mundum veni, ut qui non vident, videant; et qui vident, cæci fiant]]. In this way, then, Christ judged the peoples in equity by the judgment of discernment, in that he mercifully called some to faith and grace and justly left the rest: a discernment wholly just, though to us incomprehensible and unknown. But in his first coming Christ did not judge the peoples by the judgment of reward [that is, the judgment that gives each his reward or punishment]. Wherefore he says: [[John 3:17|God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world|Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum ut judicet mundum]]. But that judgment Christ will carry out on the last day.

paras.t: Deinde invitantur creaturæ ad gaudium spirituale ex consideratione primi adventus Christi, qui fuit et est mundo magna ratio exsultandi, quemadmodum angelus dixit pastoribus : Annuntio vobis gaudium magnum quod erit omni populo, quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator. Ait igitur : Lætentur cœli, id est cives cœlorum, seu angeli sancti : nam Christo nato, facta est cum angelo multitudo cœlestis exercitus laudantium Deum. Incarnatio equidem Christi erat angelis materia gaudii, quia per eam reparatur eorum ruina. Et exsultet terra, id est genus humanum in terra exsilium ducens. Commoveatur ad pœnitentiam et gratiarum actionem, mare, id est gentilitas vitiis turbulenta, amara et salsa, et plenitudo ejus, id est viscera ejus interiora, videlicet ratio et voluntas et ceteræ animæ vires. Gaudebunt campi, id est, homines bonis operibus floridi, gratiaque fecundi, in Christi primo adventu et postea spiritualiter exsultabunt, et omnia quæ in eis sunt, id est, interiora eorum in Domino lætabuntur. Tunc exsultabunt omnia ligna silvarum, id est populi nationum ad fidem conversi, a facie Domini, id est ex consideratione præsentiæ Christi, quia venit in mundum per incarnationem. Unde in Actis Apostolorum dicitur : Audientes autem gentes, gavisæ sunt, et glorificaverunt verbum Dei.
paras.en: Next the creatures are invited to spiritual joy from the consideration of Christ's first coming, which was and is a great reason for the world to exult, as the angel said to the shepherds: [[Luke 2:10|I bring you good tidings of great joy that shall be to all the people|Annuntio vobis gaudium magnum quod erit omni populo]], [[Luke 2:11|For, this day is born to you a Saviour|quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator]]. He says, therefore: [[95:11|Let the heavens rejoice|Lætentur cœli]], that is, the citizens of the heavens, or the holy angels: for when Christ was born, [[Luke 2:13|there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God|facta est cum angelo multitudo cœlestis exercitus laudantium Deum]]. For the incarnation of Christ was matter of joy to the angels, because through it their ruin is repaired. [[95:11|and let the earth be glad|Et exsultet terra]], that is, the human race living out its exile on earth. [[95:11|let the sea be moved|Commoveatur]] to penance and thanksgiving: *the sea*, that is, the Gentile world, turbulent with vices, bitter and salt, [[95:11|and the fulness thereof|et plenitudo ejus]], that is, its inward parts, namely reason and will and the other powers of the soul. [[95:12|The fields|campi]] [[95:12|shall be joyful|Gaudebunt]], that is, men flowering with good works and fruitful with grace will exult spiritually at Christ's first coming and afterwards, [[95:12|and all things that are in them|et omnia quæ in eis sunt]], that is, their inward parts will rejoice in the Lord. [[95:12|Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice|Tunc exsultabunt omnia ligna silvarum]], that is, the peoples of the nations converted to the faith, [[95:13|before the face of the Lord|a facie Domini]], that is, from the consideration of Christ's presence, [[95:13|because he cometh|quia venit]] into the world through the incarnation. Whence it is said in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 13:48|And the Gentiles hearing it were glad and glorified the word of the Lord|Audientes autem gentes, gavisæ sunt, et glorificaverunt verbum Dei]].

paras.t: His duobus versiculis consonat quod in Isaia legitur : Laudate, cœli, et exsulta, terra ; jubilate, montes, laudem, quia consolatus est Dominus populum suum. Et quia non solum gaudendum est de primo atque occulto Christi adventu, quo venit judicari, sed etiam de secundo ejus adventu, quo venturus est judicare, secundum quod ipse ait, His autem fieri incipientibus, respicite, et levate capita vestra, id est, exhilarate corda (secundum Gregorium), quia appropinquat redemptio vestra ; ideo subditur : quoniam venit judicare terram, id est, quoniam Christus venturus est judicare vivos et mortuos judicio remunerationis. Ponit enim præteritum pro futuro, more prophetali, propter certitudinem prophetiæ. Per hoc ergo quod bis ait, Venit, innuitur duplex Christi adventus : quorum primus fuit in humilitate et occultus ; secundus erit in majestate ac manifestus, quemadmodum scriptum est in Evangelio : Tunc videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cœli, cum potestate magna et majestate. Judicabit in die extremi judicii orbem terræ, id est homines, in æquitate, dando singulis quod promeruerunt ; et populos in veritate sua, id est, sic eos judicabit, sicut in sanctis Scripturis prædixit. Hoc est quod de Christo apud Isaiam scriptum est : Non secundum visionem oculorum judicabit ; sed judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ. In libro quoque Job quidam ait : Omnipotens causas singulorum intuebitur.
paras.en: With these two verses agrees what is read in Isaias: [[Is 49:13|Give praise, O ye heavens, and rejoice, O earth, ye mountains, give praise with jubilation: because the Lord hath comforted his people|Laudate, cœli, et exsulta, terra ; jubilate, montes, laudem, quia consolatus est Dominus populum suum]]. And because we must rejoice not only over the first and hidden coming of Christ, in which he came to be judged, but also over his second coming, in which he will come to judge, as he himself says: [[Luke 21:28|But when these things begin to come to pass, look up and lift up your heads|His autem fieri incipientibus, respicite, et levate capita vestra]], that is, gladden your hearts (according to Gregory), [[Luke 21:28|because your redemption is at hand|quia appropinquat redemptio vestra]]; therefore it is added: [[95:13|because he cometh to judge the earth|quoniam venit judicare terram]], that is, because Christ will come to judge the living and the dead by the judgment of reward. For he puts the past for the future, in the manner of the prophets, because of the certainty of the prophecy [Denis takes *venit* as a past tense, "he came"; the Douay-Rheims has "he cometh"]. By his saying twice, then, *he cometh*, the twofold coming of Christ is intimated: the first of which was in humility and hidden, the second will be in majesty and manifest, as it is written in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:27|And then they shall see the Son of man coming in a cloud, with great power and majesty|Tunc videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cœli, cum potestate magna et majestate]][[Mark 13:26||]] [Denis's "in the clouds of heaven" is the wording of Matt 24:30; the rest follows Luke]. [[95:13|He shall judge|Judicabit]] on the day of the last judgment [[95:13|the world|orbem terræ]], that is, men, [[95:13|with justice|in æquitate]], giving to each what he has deserved; [[95:13|and the people with his truth|et populos in veritate sua]], that is, he will judge them just as he foretold in the holy Scriptures. This is what is written of Christ in Isaias: [[Is 11:3|He shall not judge according to the sight of the eyes|Non secundum visionem oculorum judicabit]]; [[Is 11:4|But he shall judge the poor with justice, and shall reprove with equity the meek of the earth|sed judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ]]. In the book of Job too someone says: [[Job 35:13|the Almighty will look into the causes of every one|Omnipotens causas singulorum intuebitur]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum cœlesti pulchritudine adornatum audivimus : in quo gentilium prænuntiatur conversio, divina majestas sonoro commendatur oraculo, ad laudem et oblationem fideles invitantur, duplex Christi adventus innuitur, atque divini judicii æquitas collaudatur. Quoniam ergo psalmus præsens Christi laudibus atque mysteriis plenus est, debemus eum cum singulari devotione cantare, nostramque conversationem metu futuri judicii taliter custodire, ut idonei laudatores Domini Salvatoris inveniamur.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm adorned with heavenly beauty: in it the conversion of the Gentiles is foretold, the divine majesty is commended in a resounding oracle, the faithful are invited to praise and offering, the twofold coming of Christ is intimated, and the equity of the divine judgment is extolled. Since, then, the present psalm is full of the praises and mysteries of Christ, we ought to sing it with singular devotion, and so to guard our way of life, for fear of the judgment to come, that we may be found fit to praise the Lord our Saviour.

paras.t: Precatio. Domine, qui fecisti cœlos, et terribilis es super omnes deos, misericordia tua præveniente fac nos confessionis pulchritudine faciem tuam placare : ut expurgati peccatorum colluvionibus, sincera mente et voce tibi Domino jugiter cantemus.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, who madest the heavens, and art to be feared above all gods, grant by thy preventing mercy [that is, mercy that goes before our will and moves it] that we may appease thy face by the beauty of confession: that, cleansed of the defilements of our sins, we may sing continually to thee, the Lord, with sincere mind and voice.

96.title: EXPLANATIO PSALMI NONAGESIMI SEXTI : DOMINUS REGNAVIT, EXSULTET TERRA.
96.title_en: Explanation of the ninety-sixth psalm: The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi nunc pertractandi talis est: Psalmus ipsi David, quando terra ejus restituta est ei: id est, psalmus præsens competit Christo manuforti, desiderabilique adspectu; agens de eo quod accidit, quando terra ejus, id est genus humanum seu Ecclesia electorum, quam per peccatum primi parentis amisit, restituta est ei pretio sanguinis sui. Loquitur namque hic psalmus ad litteram de Christo et secundo ejus adventu, atque judiciaria potestate ipsius, quam Christus homo sua passione promeruit. Eodem enim tempore restituta est Christo terra sua jam dicta, et judiciaria potestas collata, videlicet statim in egressione animæ suæ a corpore. Tunc enim plenissime satisfecit pro genere humano, et tunc dedit ei Pater gentes hereditatem suam, sicut superius dixit: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam: quamvis (ut sæpius patuit) Christo homini ab exordio conceptionis in Virgine, data sit omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra. Quod autem hic psalmus de Christo loquatur, hinc constat, quod Paulus ad Hebræos inducit scripturam hujus psalmi de Christo prænuntiatam, dicendo: Et quum introducit Primogenitum suum in orbem terræ, dicit: Et adorent eum omnes angeli ejus. Hoc quippe inferius ita exprimitur: Adorate eum, omnes angeli ejus.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be treated is this: A psalm for David himself, when his land was restored to him[[96:1||]] [the title of the psalm, which in the Vulgate stands at the head of verse 1; the Douay-Rheims renders it "For the same David, when his land was restored again to him"]: that is, the present psalm belongs to Christ, strong of hand and desirable to look upon [the meanings given to the name David]; and it treats of what came to pass when his land, that is, the human race or the Church of the elect, which was lost through the sin of our first parent, was restored to him at the price of his blood. For this psalm speaks literally of Christ and of his second coming, and of his judicial power, which Christ as man merited by his passion. For at the same time the land just spoken of was restored to Christ and judicial power was conferred on him, namely at once, at the going forth of his soul from the body. For then he made the fullest satisfaction for the human race, and then the Father gave him the Gentiles for his inheritance, as he said above: [[Ps 2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance|Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam]]; although (as has often been shown) all power in heaven and in earth was given to Christ as man from the first moment of his conception in the Virgin[[Matt 28:18||]]. That this psalm speaks of Christ is clear from this, that Paul, writing to the Hebrews, brings forward the words of this psalm as foretold of Christ, saying: [[Heb 1:6|when he bringeth in the first begotten into the world, he saith: And let all the angels of God adore him|quum introducit Primogenitum suum in orbem terræ, dicit: Et adorent eum omnes angeli ejus]] [Denis reads "all his angels", as in the psalm, where the Vulgate of Hebrews has "the angels of God"]. For this is expressed further on thus: [[96:7|Adore him, all you his angels|Adorate eum, omnes angeli ejus]].

paras.t: Ait ergo: Dominus, scilicet Christus, habens in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum: Rex regum et Dominus dominantium; regnavit in militanti Ecclesia, seu cordibus electorum: sicut de eo Abdias dixit propheta, Et erit Domino regnum. De quo in Apocalypsi Sancti hilariter cantant: Regnavit Dominus Deus noster omnipotens; gaudeamus et exsultemus, et demus gloriam ei. Exsultet terra, id est, habitatores terræ Christo Domino suo regnanti congratulentur, et de ejus regno in se ipsis pie lætentur. Lætentur hoc modo in Domino insulæ multæ, ad fidem conversæ, sicut est Anglia, Hibernia, Cyprus, Sicilia: de quibus prædictum est, Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt. Dicuntur enim insulæ, terræ supra mare sitæ. Unde in Isaia habetur: Glorificate Dominum in insulis maris.
paras.en: He says, then: [[96:1|The Lord|Dominus]], that is, Christ, who [[Apoc 19:16|hath on his garment and on his thigh written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|habens in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum: Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]], [[96:1|hath reigned|regnavit]] in the Church militant, or in the hearts of the elect: as the prophet Abdias said of him, [[Abd 1:21|and the kingdom shall be for the Lord|Et erit Domino regnum]]. Of which the saints sing joyfully in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:6|the Lord our God, the Almighty, hath reigned|Regnavit Dominus Deus noster omnipotens]]; [[Apoc 19:7|Let us be glad and rejoice and give glory to him|gaudeamus et exsultemus, et demus gloriam ei]].
