[[96:1|Let the earth rejoice|Exsultet terra]], that is, let the dwellers on the earth rejoice with Christ their Lord as he reigns, and be devoutly glad within themselves of his kingdom. In this way [[96:1|let many islands be glad|lætentur insulæ multæ]] in the Lord, those converted to the faith, such as England, Ireland, Cyprus, Sicily: of which it was foretold, [[Is 42:12|They shall give glory to the Lord, and shall declare his praise in the islands|Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt.]]. For lands set in the sea are called islands. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 24:15|glorify ye the Lord|Glorificate Dominum]] [[Is 24:15|in the islands of the sea|in insulis maris]].

paras.t: Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus: id est, in die judicii erunt et apparebunt in circuitu Christi judicis nubes materiales, quia veniet in nube (Christus namque ascendit in nube, juxta illud, Nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum: venturus est ergo in nube, quoniam sicut illic angeli sancti testati sunt sanctis Apostolis, Sic veniet quemadmodum vidistis eum euntem in cœlum), et caligo, id est obscuritas aeris, quoniam, Dies Domini, tanquam fur in nocte, ita veniet; et, Media nocte clamor factus est, Ecce sponsus venit: quemadmodum ipsemet Sponsus ac Judex testatur. Creditur enim Christus tempore noctis ad judicandum venturus.
paras.en: [[96:2|Clouds and darkness are round about him|Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus]]: that is, at the day of judgement there will be, and there will appear, round about Christ the judge material clouds, since he will come in a cloud[[Luke 21:27||]] (for Christ ascended in a cloud, according to the words, [[Acts 1:9|a cloud received him out of their sight|Nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum]]; so he is to come in a cloud, since, as the holy angels there testified to the holy Apostles, he [[Acts 1:11|shall so come as you have seen him going into heaven|Sic veniet quemadmodum vidistis eum euntem in cœlum]]); and darkness, that is, obscurity of the air, since [[1 Thess 5:2|the day of the Lord shall so come as a thief in the night|Dies Domini, tanquam fur in nocte, ita veniet]][[2 Pet 3:10||]]; and, [[Matt 25:6|at midnight there was a cry made: Behold the bridegroom cometh|Media nocte clamor factus est, Ecce sponsus venit]], as the Bridegroom and Judge himself testifies. For it is believed that Christ will come to judge in the time of night.

paras.t: Sed quæstio est, quomodo tunc erit caligo, præsertim quum totus mundus stabit in igne conflagrationis, qui utique (ut apparet) aerem illustrabit. Possit fortassis responderi ad hoc, quod ignis ille fumosus erit, nec tenebras omnino expellet, sicut nec ignis inferni. Sed quia de necessitate concedere cogimur, quod ipse judex, scilicet Christus, ab universis hominibus etiam corporalibus oculis conspicietur, sicut et Job ait, In novissimo die surrecturus sum, et in carne mea videbo Deum salvatorem meum (imo, secundum Gregorium, omnes angeli tunc corporalibus oculis videbuntur, quanto magis homines?); idcirco non arbitror, quod in die judicii erit caligo in circuitu judicis, ita quod aer omnino tenebrosus erit; sed propter ignis illius fumositatem poterit aliquid tenebrositatis remanere in aere. Potest quoque per caliginem accipi tempestas illa horribilis, quæ erit in die judicii: de qua dictum est supra, Et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida. Unde et Nahum: Dominus in tempestate et turbine viæ ejus.
paras.en: But the question is how there will then be darkness, especially since the whole world will stand in the fire of the conflagration[[2 Pet 3:10||]][[2 Pet 3:12||]], which (as it seems) will certainly light up the air. It might perhaps be answered to this that that fire will be smoky and will not altogether drive out the darkness, just as the fire of hell does not. But since we are compelled of necessity to grant that the judge himself, namely Christ, will be seen by all men even with bodily eyes, as Job too says, [[Job 19:25|in the last day I shall rise|In novissimo die surrecturus sum]], and [[Job 19:26|in my flesh I shall see my God|in carne mea videbo Deum salvatorem meum]] [Denis reads "God my Saviour"] (indeed, according to Gregory, all the angels will then be seen with bodily eyes: how much more men?), I therefore do not think that at the day of judgement there will be darkness round about the judge in such a way that the air will be altogether dark; but on account of the smokiness of that fire some darkness may remain in the air. By the darkness may also be understood that horrible tempest which there will be at the day of judgement, of which it was said above, [[Ps 49:3|and a mighty tempest shall be round about him|Et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida]]. Hence Nahum too: [[Nah 1:3|The Lord's ways are in a tempest, and a whirlwind|Dominus in tempestate et turbine viæ ejus]].

paras.t: Ignis conflagrationis, qui elementa exuret atque purgabit, et tam alte ascendet ut aqua diluvii, ante ipsum præcedet, id est, secundum Christi adventum præveniet: quia quemadmodum mundus primo periit aquis diluvii, sic ultimo peribit igne conflagrationis, qui omnes viventes in mundo occidet. Et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus, scilicet reprobos, quoniam durante hora judicii, ignis conflagrationis, in quo universi tunc stabunt, incendet malignos; electos vero non tanget, nec contristabit, nec aliquid molestiæ inferet: cujus figura præcessit in tribus pueris, quos rex Babylonis misit in fornacem ignis, quos non tetigit ignis, sed Chaldæos combussit, ut dicit Daniel.
paras.en: [[96:3|A fire|Ignis]] of the conflagration, which will burn up and purge the elements, and will rise as high as the water of the flood, [[96:3|shall go before him|ante ipsum præcedet]], that is, will come before the second coming of Christ: for as the world first perished by the waters of the flood[[Gen 7:21||]][[Gen 7:23||]], so at the last it will perish by the fire of the conflagration, which will slay all the living in the world. [[96:3|And shall burn his enemies round about|Et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus]], namely the reprobate: for while the hour of judgement lasts, the fire of the conflagration, in which all will then stand, will burn the wicked; but the elect it will not touch, nor trouble, nor do them any harm [Denis borrows the words of Dan. iii, 50]: a figure of which went before in the three children whom the king of Babylon sent into the furnace of fire, whom the fire did not touch[[Dan 3:50||]], but it burnt up the Chaldeans[[Dan 3:22||]], as Daniel says.

paras.t: Illuxerunt fulgura ejus orbi terræ: id est, magnæ atque terribiles coruscationes circa judicii horam apparebunt, de quibus homines terrebuntur: sicut Lucas dicit, Arescentibus hominibus præ timore et exspectatione quæ supervenient universo orbi. Idcirco subjungitur: vidit et commota est terra, id est, habitantes in terra hæc fulgura cernent, et ad magnum timorem movendi sunt. Propter quod alibi scriptum est: Conturbentur omnes habitatores terræ, quoniam venit dies Domini, dies tenebrarum et caliginis. Similis ei non fuit a principio, et post eum non erit. Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans, et post eum vorax flamma. A facie ejus contremuit terra.
paras.en: [[96:4|His lightnings have shone forth to the world|Illuxerunt fulgura ejus orbi terræ]]: that is, about the hour of judgement great and terrible flashes will appear, by which men will be terrified: as Luke says, [[Luke 21:26|Men withering away for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world|Arescentibus hominibus præ timore et exspectatione quæ supervenient universo orbi]]. Therefore it is added: [[96:4|the earth saw and trembled|vidit et commota est terra]], that is, those who dwell on the earth will see these lightnings, and are to be moved to great fear. On which account it is written elsewhere: [[Joel 2:1|let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: because the day of the Lord cometh|Conturbentur omnes habitatores terræ, quoniam venit dies Domini]], [[Joel 2:2|A day of darkness, and of gloominess|dies tenebrarum et caliginis]]. [[Joel 2:2|the like to it hath not been from the beginning, nor shall be after it|Similis ei non fuit a principio, et post eum non erit]]. [[Joel 2:3|Before the face thereof a devouring fire, and behind it a burning flame|Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans, et post eum vorax flamma]]. [[Joel 2:10|At their presence the earth hath trembled|A facie ejus contremuit terra]].

paras.t: Montes sicut cera fluxerunt a facie Domini: quia in die judicii, seu mox eo peracto, complanabitur terra: sed et ante judicium erunt terræ motus magni per loca. Melius tamen per montes, hoc loco, accipiuntur superbi, non in montem Domini, sed in montem superbiæ ascendentes, sequentes eum qui dixit: Sedebo in monte testamenti, et ascendam super altitudinem nubium. Isti in die judicii, sicut cera fluent, id est, corde dissolventur atque pavebunt, a facie Domini, id est a conspectu judicis; nec ipsi solum, sed a facie Domini, id est a judicis metuenda præsentia, fluet hoc modo omnis terra, id est omnis homo terrenus atque peccator.
paras.en: [[96:5|The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord|Montes sicut cera fluxerunt a facie Domini]]: for at the day of judgement, or soon after it is done, the earth will be made level; and before the judgement too there will be great earthquakes in places[[Matt 24:7||]]. But in this place the mountains are better taken for the proud, who go up not into the mountain of the Lord but into the mountain of pride, following him who said: [[Is 14:13|I will sit in the mountain of the covenant|Sedebo in monte testamenti]], and [[Is 14:14|I will ascend above the height of the clouds|ascendam super altitudinem nubium]]. These at the day of judgement will melt like wax, that is, will be dissolved in heart and will be terrified, [[96:5|at the presence of the Lord|a facie Domini]], that is, at the sight of the judge; and not they alone, but [[96:5|at the presence of the Lord|a facie Domini]], that is, at the dread presence of the judge, so shall melt [[96:5|all the earth|omnis terra]], that is, every earthly man and sinner.

paras.t: Ideo namque ab alio prædictum est: Montes commoti sunt ab eo, et colles desolati sunt, et contremuit terra a facie ejus, orbis et omnes habitantes in eo. Et alibi: Ecce turbo dominicæ indignationis egredietur, et tempestas erumpens super caput impiorum veniet.
paras.en: For this reason it was foretold by another: [[Nah 1:5|The mountains tremble at him, and the hills are made desolate: and the earth hath quaked at his presence, and the world, and all that dwell therein|Montes commoti sunt ab eo, et colles desolati sunt, et contremuit terra a facie ejus, orbis et omnes habitantes in eo]]. And elsewhere: [[Jer 23:19|Behold the whirlwind of the Lord's indignation shall come forth, and a tempest shall break out and come upon the head of the wicked|Ecce turbo Dominicæ indignationis egredietur, et tempestas erumpens super caput impiorum veniet.]].

paras.t: Annuntiaverunt cœli justitiam ejus, id est, per signa in cœlo apparentia, manifestabitur justa ultio Christi in impios. Erunt enim signa in sole et luna et stellis. Unde ait Salvator: Statim post tribulationem dierum illorum sol obscurabitur, et luna non dabit splendorem suum. Per hæc autem patebit, quanta sit Christi justitia ulciscens peccata. Et viderunt omnes populi gloriam ejus, id est, omnes tunc in mundo existentes, conspicient magnalia ista operum divinorum.
paras.en: [[96:6|The heavens declared his justice|Annuntiaverunt cœli justitiam ejus]], that is, by signs appearing in the heaven the just vengeance of Christ upon the wicked will be made manifest. For [[Luke 21:25|there shall be signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars|Erunt enim signa in sole et luna et stellis]]. Hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 24:29|immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun shall be darkened and the moon shall not give her light|Statim post tribulationem dierum illorum sol obscurabitur, et luna non dabit splendorem suum]]. By these it will be plain how great is the justice of Christ avenging sins. [[96:6|And all people saw his glory|Et viderunt omnes populi gloriam ejus]], that is, all then living in the world will behold these mighty works of God.

paras.t: Melius autem exponitur iste versiculus de sanctis Apostolis, quia ne crederetur judicium illud sine præadmonitione et comminatione futurum, adjecit: Annuntiaverunt cœli, id est Apostoli, justitiam ejus: quia in universo mundo prædicaverunt Christum esse omnium justissimum judicem, qui sine personarum acceptione irreprehensibiliter judicabit; et viderunt, id est, per fidem cognoverunt, omnes populi, ad Christum conversi ex annuntiatione horum cœlorum, gloriam ejus, id est majestatem et excellentiam Christi, quæ in Evangelio copiose describitur. Unde et per Isaiam Dominus dicit: Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad insulas longe; et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus.
paras.en: But this verse is better expounded of the holy Apostles: for lest that judgement should be thought to be coming without forewarning and threatening, he added: [[96:6|The heavens declared|Annuntiaverunt cœli]], that is, the Apostles, [[96:6|his justice|justitiam ejus]]: for throughout the whole world they preached that Christ is the most just judge of all, who will judge blamelessly, without respect of persons; and [[96:6|saw|viderunt]], that is, knew by faith, [[96:6|all people|omnes populi]], converted to Christ by the preaching of these heavens, [[96:6|his glory|gloriam ejus]], that is, the majesty and excellence of Christ, which is described at length in the Gospel. Hence the Lord also says through Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint]], [[Is 66:19|to the islands afar off|ad insulas longe]]; [[Is 66:19|And they shall declare my glory to the Gentiles|et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus]].

paras.t: Quum ergo tanta sit gloria Christi, Confundantur, vel modo ad pœnitentiam salutarem, vel si modo non pœnitent, æternaliter erubescant, omnes qui adorant sculptilia, et qui gloriantur in simulacris suis seu idolis, qui serviunt creaturæ potius quam Creatori. Nam quam grave sit hoc peccatum, declarat Sapiens: Initium fornicationis a Deo, est exquisitio idolorum. Infandorum enim idolorum cultura, omnis mali causa est et initium et finis.
paras.en: Since, then, the glory of Christ is so great, [[96:7|Let them be all confounded|Confundantur]], either now, unto saving penance, or, if they do not repent now, let them blush for ever, [[96:7|that adore graven things, and that glory in their idols|omnes qui adorant sculptilia, et qui gloriantur in simulacris suis]] or images, who [[Rom 1:25|served the creature rather than the Creator|serviunt creaturæ potius quam Creatori]]. For how grave this sin is the Wise man declares: [[Wis 14:12|the beginning of fornication is the devising of idols|Initium fornicationis a Deo, est exquisitio idolorum]] [Denis's text adds *a Deo*: the beginning of fornication away from God, that is, of unfaithfulness to him]. [[Wis 14:27|For the worship of abominable idols is the cause, and the beginning and end of all evil|Infandorum enim idolorum cultura, omnis mali causa est et initium et finis]].

paras.t: Adorate eum, scilicet Christum, seu Deum trinum ac simplicem, omnes angeli ejus. De his enim angelis Dominus loquitur Job: Ubi eras quum me laudarent astra matutina, et jubilarent omnes filii Dei?
paras.en: [[96:7|Adore him|Adorate eum]], namely Christ, or God, three and simple [that is, one God in three Persons, without composition], [[96:7|all you his angels|omnes angeli ejus]]. For of these angels the Lord speaks to Job: [[Job 38:4|Where wast thou|Ubi eras]] [[Job 38:7|When the morning stars praised me together, and all the sons of God made a joyful melody?|quum me laudarent astra matutina, et jubilarent omnes filii Dei?]]

paras.t: Audivit, et lætata est Sion: id est, Ecclesia militans, quæ dicitur Sion, id est speculatrix bonorum cœlestium, audivit auribus mentis et corporis annuntiationem seu prædicationem Apostolorum, vel doctrinam eorum, de duplici Christi adventu ac justo judicio; et inde lætata est spirituali lætitia, tanquam se ipsam conformans, favens, atque consentiens voluntati Salvatoris ac Judicis sui. Et exsultaverunt filiæ Judæ, id est animæ Deo veraciter confitentes. Juda enim interpretatur confessio. Unde quum Lia uxor Jacob patriarchæ, peperisset Judam filium suum, dixit: Modo confitebor Domino. Et ob hoc vocavit eum Judam. Hæ itaque filiæ exsultaverunt, propter judicia tua, Domine, id est ex consideratione justorum judiciorum tuorum: quibus nil inordinatum relinquis, nulli injuriam facis, nullius violentiam inultam dimittis: sed eos qui in hoc sæculo contemnuntur, opprimuntur, pro nihilo reputantur, et propter justitiam patiuntur, in æternum exaltas; eos vero qui modo florent, prosperantur, ac deliciantur, sine fine condemnas.
paras.en: [[96:8|Sion heard, and was glad|Audivit, et lætata est Sion]]: that is, the Church militant, which is called Sion, that is, the watcher [*speculatrix*, the usual interpretation of the name Sion, "watch-tower"] of heavenly goods, heard with the ears of mind and body the announcing or preaching of the Apostles, or their teaching, concerning the twofold coming of Christ and the just judgement; and she was glad thereat with a spiritual gladness, as conforming herself to the will of her Saviour and Judge, favouring it and consenting to it. [[96:8|And the daughters of Juda rejoiced|Et exsultaverunt filiæ Judæ]], that is, souls truly confessing God. For Juda is interpreted "confession". Hence when Lia, the wife of the patriarch Jacob, had borne her son Juda, she said: [[Gen 29:35|Now will I praise the Lord: and for this she called him Juda|Modo confitebor Domino. Et ob hoc vocavit eum Judam]] [*confitebor*, "I will praise", also means "I will confess"]. These daughters, then, rejoiced [[96:8|because of thy judgments, O Lord|propter judicia tua, Domine]], that is, from the consideration of thy just judgements: in which thou leavest nothing out of order, doest wrong to no one, leavest no one's violence unpunished; but those who in this world are despised, oppressed, reckoned as nothing, and suffer for justice' sake[[Matt 5:10||]] [the margin gives Matt. v, 10–12], thou exaltest for ever; while those who now flourish, prosper and live in delights thou condemnest without end.

paras.t: Quoniam tu Dominus es altissimus super omnem terram. Omnia namque creasti, et cuncta in infinitum excellis, omniumque omnipotens judex es: idcirco nimis, id est incomparabiliter, incomprehensibiliter, et sine mensura, exaltatus es super omnes deos (de quibus jam dictum est): nam et illorum creator ac judex consistis. Propter quod de te testatur Scriptura: Benedictus es, Domine, in templo sancto gloriæ tuæ, et superlaudabilis et superexaltatus in omnibus sæculis.
paras.en: [[96:9|For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth|Quoniam tu Dominus es altissimus super omnem terram]]. For thou hast created all things, and dost infinitely excel them all, and art the almighty judge of all: therefore [[96:9|thou art exalted exceedingly|nimis]], that is, incomparably, incomprehensibly and without measure, [[96:9|above all gods|exaltatus es super omnes deos]] (of whom mention has just been made): for thou art their creator and judge as well. On which account Scripture testifies of thee: [[Dan 3:53|Blessed art thou|Benedictus es]], O Lord, [[Dan 3:53|in the holy temple of thy glory: and exceedingly to be praised|in templo sancto gloriæ tuæ, et superlaudabilis]] and [[Dan 3:52|exalted above all, in all ages|superexaltatus in omnibus sæculis]].

paras.t: Qui diligitis Dominum, odite malum culpæ, id est, peccatum omne abhorrete, non quia pœnam meretur, sed quia peccatum est displicens Deo. Qui enim diligit Dominum, debet habere affectum divinæ voluntati conformem: ideoque quemadmodum Deus odit peccatum, in quantum peccatum; sic diligens Deum, debet odisse peccatum, in quantum peccatum, seu divinæ voluntati contrarium. Sic autem odio habere peccatum, est evidens signum dilectionis et gratiæ Dei in homine: imo hoc modo societatem ac familiaritatem cum Deo sortimur. Unde Joannes: Societas (inquit) nostra sit cum Patre et Filio ejus Jesu Christo; rursusque, Deus lux est, et tenebræ in eo non sunt ullæ. Si dixerimus quoniam societatem habemus cum illo, et in tenebris ambulamus, mentimur.
paras.en: [[96:10|You that love the Lord, hate evil|Qui diligitis Dominum, odite malum]], the evil of guilt [that is, sin itself, as distinct from the evil of punishment]: that is, abhor every sin, not because it deserves punishment, but because sin is displeasing to God. For he who loves the Lord ought to have an affection conformed to the divine will: and so, as God hates sin inasmuch as it is sin, so he who loves God ought to hate sin inasmuch as it is sin, or contrary to the divine will. Now so to hold sin in hatred is a clear sign of the love and grace of God in a man: indeed, in this way we obtain fellowship and familiarity with God. Hence John: [[1 John 1:3|our fellowship|Societas]], he says, [[1 John 1:3|may be with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ|nostra sit cum Patre et Filio ejus Jesu Christo]]; and again, [[1 John 1:5|God is light and in him there is no darkness|Deus lux est, et tenebræ in eo non sunt ullæ]]. [[1 John 1:6|If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in darkness, we lie|Si dixerimus quoniam societatem habemus cum illo, et in tenebris ambulamus, mentimur]].

paras.t: Custodit Dominus animas sanctorum suorum, in præsenti vita per gratiam angelicamque custodiam, in futuro autem judicio eas custodiet ab omni damnatione atque periculo; de manu peccatoris, id est potestate omnium iniquorum, liberabit eos, scilicet sanctos suos. Nunc enim liberat eos a tentationibus et persecutionibus, ne eis noceant, dando patientiam in adversis, vel ereptionem totalem ab eis; in die quoque judicii perfecte redimet eos. Hinc enim scriptum est: Omnis qui natus est ex Deo, non peccat, quoniam semen Dei manet in eo; et malignus non tangit eum.
paras.en: [[96:10|the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints|Custodit Dominus animas sanctorum suorum]], in the present life by grace and by the guardianship of the angels, and at the judgement to come he will guard them from all damnation and danger; [[96:10|out of the hand of the sinner|de manu peccatoris]], that is, from the power of all the wicked, [[96:10|he will deliver them|liberabit eos]], namely his saints. For now he delivers them from temptations and persecutions, that these may not harm them, giving them patience in adversity, or complete rescue from them; and at the day of judgement he will perfectly redeem them. For hence it is written: [[1 John 3:9|Whosoever is born of God committeth not sin: for his seed abideth in him|Omnis qui natus est ex Deo, non peccat, quoniam semen Dei manet in eo]]; [[1 John 5:18|and the wicked one toucheth him not|et malignus non tangit eum]].

paras.t: Lux, id est splendor gratiæ Dei, seu Christus sol justitiæ, orta est justo, qui Deo ex caritate obedit: quod nemo facere potest, nisi in quo orta est lux gratiæ Christi, qui protestatur, Sine me nihil potestis facere; et rectis corde, id est justis omnibus, orta est lætitia, id est copiosa ratio atque materia spiritualium gaudiorum, ex incarnatione et ceteris beneficiis et promissionibus Christi.
paras.en: [[96:11|Light|Lux]], that is, the splendour of the grace of God, or Christ the sun of justice, [[96:11|is risen to the just|orta est justo]], who obeys God out of charity: which no one can do save he in whom the light of the grace of Christ has risen, who declares, [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]; and [[96:11|to the right of heart|rectis corde]], that is, to all the just, there is risen [[96:11|joy|lætitia]], that is, abundant reason and matter for spiritual joys, from the incarnation and the other benefits and promises of Christ.

paras.t: Propterea Lætamini, o justi, in Domino summo creatore, piissimo redemptore, ac liberalissimo benefactore vestro, et confitemini, confessione laudis, memoriæ sanctificationis ejus, id est recordationi divinæ mentis, seu menti divinæ, quæ clementer memorata est vestri, videlicet sanctificando vos gratis per dona Sancti Spiritus: propter quod gratias agere incessanter debetis, nec oblivisci ejus qui vestri oblitus non est.
paras.en: Therefore [[96:12|Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord|Lætamini, o justi, in Domino]], your supreme creator, most loving redeemer and most bountiful benefactor, [[96:12|and give praise|et confitemini]], with the confession of praise [*confitemini* can mean both "confess" and "give praise"], [[96:12|to the remembrance of his holiness|memoriæ sanctificationis ejus]] [literally "the memory of his sanctifying"], that is, to the remembering of the divine mind, or to the divine mind, which has mercifully remembered you, namely by sanctifying you freely through the gifts of the Holy Ghost: for which you ought to give thanks unceasingly, and not forget him who has not forgotten you.

paras.t: Admonemur ex psalmo præsenti, futuri judicii horrorem districtionemque pensare, cogitando corde tenus quam horrendum tunc erit incidere in manus Dei viventis, Deum judicem summe iratum conspicere, totum mundum incensum videre, universorum angelorum agmina videre armata ad adsistendum Christo judici contra iniquos; coram cœlo et terra de omnibus cogitationibus, verbis et actibus rationem exsolvere, coram universis hominibus, angelis dæmonibusque confundi ac reprobari, audire verbum illud asperrimum, et omni tormento pœnalius, Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum; exspectare incertam seu etiam certam sententiam judicis, intuerique sub se hians chaos carceris infernalis; et tandem ab electorum consortio separari, atque æternæ damnationis sententiam adipisci, in profunda inferni incidere, inexstinguibilibus flammis sine spe unquam evadendi exuri. De hac etenim die convenienter accipitur quod alibi scriptum est: Dies iræ, dies illa, dies tribulationis et angustiæ, dies calamitatis et miseriæ, dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies tubæ et clangoris. Et iterum: Ecce dies Domini veniet crudelis et indignationis plenus, ad conterendos peccatores de terra, quoniam stellæ cœli et splendor earum non expandent lumen suum; obscuratus est sol in ortu suo, et luna non splendebit. Unde altissimus ille Archiapostolus: Adveniet, inquit, dies Domini tanquam fur: in quo cœli magno impetu transient, elementa vero calore solventur; terra autem et quæ in ipsa sunt opera, exurentur. Idcirco dum Christus multa horrenda dixisset, tandem sermonem concludens, ita hortatus est nos: Vigilate omni tempore, orantes, ut digni habeamini fugere ista omnia quæ futura sunt, et stare ante Filium hominis.
paras.en: We are admonished by the present psalm to weigh the horror and the strictness of the judgement to come, pondering in our heart how fearful a thing it will then be [[Heb 10:31|to fall into the hands of the living God|incidere in manus Dei viventis]]; to behold God the judge supremely angered, to see the whole world on fire, to see the hosts of all the angels armed to stand by Christ the judge against the wicked; before heaven and earth to render account for all thoughts, words and deeds; before all men, angels and demons to be confounded and rejected; to hear that most bitter word, more grievous than any torment, Depart, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]] [Denis has *Ite*, "Go", for the Vulgate's *Discedite a me*]; to await the sentence of the judge, uncertain or even certain, and to behold the chaos of the prison of hell yawning beneath one; and at last to be separated from the company of the elect, and to receive the sentence of eternal damnation, to fall into the depths of hell, to burn in unquenchable flames without hope of ever escaping. For of this day is fittingly understood what is written elsewhere: [[Soph 1:15|That day is a day of wrath, a day of tribulation and distress, a day of calamity and misery, a day of darkness and obscurity|Dies iræ, dies illa, dies tribulationis et angustiæ, dies calamitatis et miseriæ, dies tenebrarum et caliginis]], [[Soph 1:16|A day of the trumpet and alarm|dies tubæ et clangoris]]. And again: [[Is 13:9|Behold, the day of the Lord shall come, a cruel day, and full of indignation|Ecce dies Domini veniet crudelis et indignationis plenus]], [[Is 13:9|to destroy the sinners thereof out of it|ad conterendos peccatores de terra]]: [[Is 13:10|For the stars of heaven, and their brightness shall not display their light: the sun shall be darkened in his rising, and the moon shall not shine|quoniam stellæ cœli et splendor earum non expandent lumen suum; obscuratus est sol in ortu suo, et luna non splendebit]]. Hence that most exalted Archapostle: [[2 Pet 3:10|shall come|Adveniet]], he says, [[2 Pet 3:10|the day of the Lord|dies Domini]] [[2 Pet 3:10|as a thief, in which the heavens shall pass away with great violence and the elements shall be melted with heat and the earth and the works which are in it shall be burnt up|tanquam fur: in quo cœli magno impetu transient, elementa vero calore solventur; terra autem et quæ in ipsa sunt opera, exurentur]]. Therefore, when Christ had said many dreadful things, concluding his discourse at last he exhorted us thus: [[Luke 21:36|Watch ye, therefore, praying at all times, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are to come and to stand before the Son of man|Vigilate omni tempore, orantes, ut digni habeamini fugere ista omnia quæ futura sunt, et stare ante Filium hominis]].

paras.t: Precatio. Super omnem terram, altissime Domine Deus, doce nos te tota devotione diligere, et malum odire: custodi in hac vita animas nostras, et hinc migrantes eas, de locis perpetuarum pœnarum eripias.
paras.en: Prayer. Most high Lord God, [[96:9|over all the earth|Super omnem terram]], teach us to love thee with all devotion and to hate evil: keep our souls in this life, and when they depart hence, rescue them from the places of everlasting pains.

97.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI NONAGESIMI SEPTIMI : CANTATE DOMINO CANTICUM NOVUM, QUIA MIRABILIA FECIT.
97.title_en: Exposition of the ninety-seventh psalm: Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: because he hath done wonderful things.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi præsentis est: Psalmus David. Psalmus iste ad litteram competit Christo, quia de ipso ac duplici ejus adventu conscriptus est; specialiter tamen et evidenter loquitur de primo Christi adventu seu incarnatione, et ait:
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is: [[97:1|A psalm for David himself|Psalmus David]]. This psalm applies in the letter to Christ, since it was written of him and of his twofold coming; yet it speaks specially and plainly of Christ's first coming, or incarnation, and says:

paras.t: Cantate Domino Christo canticum novum, videlicet evangelicæ legis præconia, sicut paulo ante plenius exponebatur in psalmo nonagesimo quinto, qui cum isto in verbis atque sententia pro magna parte in idem concurrit. Ideo autem Cantate Domino canticum novum, quia mirabilia fecit: imo superincomprehensibilia fecit, assumendo humanam naturam in unitate suppositali, progrediendo de clauso virgineæ Matris utero, resurgendo et de clauso monumento egrediendo, in cœlos ascendendo, Spiritum Sanctum mittendo. Quanta autem mirabilia Christus in sua prædicatione ac passione molitus sit, Evangelia pandunt; vehementissime tamen mirabile exstitit, quod Deus Pater proprium Filium misit in mundum, quatenus per ejus passionem ac mortem salvaretur genus humanum.
paras.en: [[97:1|Sing ye to the Lord|Cantate Domino]] Christ [[97:1|a new canticle|canticum novum]], that is, the proclamations of the law of the Gospel, as was set out more fully a little before in the ninety-fifth psalm, which for the most part agrees with this one in words and in sense. And the reason why we are to [[97:1|Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle|Cantate Domino canticum novum]] is this: [[97:1|because he hath done wonderful things|quia mirabilia fecit]]; nay, he hath done things beyond all comprehension, by assuming human nature in the unity of the suppositum [that is, into the one subsisting person of the Word], by going forth from the closed womb of the Virgin Mother, by rising again and coming forth from the closed tomb, by ascending into heaven, by sending the Holy Ghost. How great the wonders were that Christ wrought in his preaching and in his passion, the Gospels make known; yet the most exceedingly wonderful thing of all was that God the Father sent his own Son into the world[[Gal 4:4||]], so that through his passion and death the human race might be saved.

paras.t: Salvavit sibi dextera ejus, et brachium sanctum ejus: id est, dextera Christi et brachium ejus, videlicet magna virtus Christi, et fortitudo sua excelsa, salvavit, id est, de morte æterna genus humanum redemit, sibi, id est ad nominis sui honorem. Christus namque propria potestate hominem liberavit. Unde per Isaiam ait: Salvavit mihi brachium meum.
paras.en: [[97:1|His right hand hath wrought for him salvation, and his arm is holy|Salvavit sibi dextera ejus, et brachium sanctum ejus]]: that is, the right hand of Christ and his arm, namely the great power of Christ and his lofty strength, [[97:1|hath wrought|salvavit]], that is, redeemed the human race from eternal death, [[97:1|for him|sibi]], that is, for the honour of his name. For Christ set man free by his own power. Hence he says by Isaias: [[Is 63:5|my own arm hath saved for me|Salvavit mihi brachium meum]].

paras.t: Alii ita exponunt: Dextera ejus et brachium sanctum ejus, id est Christus: qui est virtus seu dextera Dei, juxta illud Apostoli, Prædicamus Christum Dei virtutem et Dei sapientiam; qui etiam dicitur brachium Patris, quia per eum omnia fecit. Sicque per brachium intelligitur Christus, de quo apud Isaiam legitur: Brachium Domini cui revelatum est? Salvavit genus humanum sibi, id est Deo Patri, seu ad gloriam ejus. Hæc enim salvatio fuit opus quod Pater dedit Filio ut faceret: de quo Christus in cruce suspensus, dixit, Consummatum est; et ante passionem, Pater, ego te clarificavi super terram, opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut faciam.
paras.en: Others expound it thus: [[97:1|His right hand|Dextera ejus]] [[97:1|and his arm is holy|et brachium sanctum ejus]], that is, Christ: who is the power or right hand of God, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 1:23|we preach|Prædicamus]] [[1 Cor 1:24|Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God|Christum Dei virtutem et Dei sapientiam]]; who is also called the arm of the Father, because through him he made all things. And so by the arm is understood Christ, of whom we read in Isaias: [[Is 53:1|to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?|Brachium Domini cui revelatum est?]] He [[97:1|hath wrought|Salvavit]] salvation for the human race [[97:1|for him|sibi]], that is, for God the Father, or for his glory. For this salvation was the work which the Father gave the Son to do: of which Christ, hanging on the cross, said: [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]]; and before his passion: Father, [[John 17:4|I have glorified thee on the earth; I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do|ego te clarificavi super terram, opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut faciam]].

paras.t: Deinde Propheta de futuro loquens per modum præteriti, quod tamen jam completum conspicimus, subdit: Notum fecit Dominus, scilicet Deus Pater, salutare suum, id est Christum Filium suum, mundi salvatorem: Primo in Judæa, quia per miracula quæ Christus in nomine Patris operabatur, Pater declaravit Jesum Nazarenum esse Filium suum ac regem Messiam: propter quod Christus ait, Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater, testimonium perhibent de me. Notificavit quoque Pater Filium suum pastoribus per angelum, Zachariæ atque Elisabeth per Spiritum Sanctum, Annæ et Simeoni similiter. Insuper Christo baptizato, et postea transfigurato, Pater de cælo intonuit, Hic est, inquiens, Filius meus dilectus. Secundo notificavit salutare suum gentibus. Unde subjungitur: in conspectu gentium revelavit per prædicationem Apostolorum justitiam suam, id est Christum essentialiter justum atque justitiam: qui appellatur justitia Dei, quia Pater per eum mundum redemit, non per potentiam tantum, sed per modum ac viam justitiæ. Vel, Justitiam suam, id est evangelicæ legis præcepta atque consilia, in quibus continetur plenitudo justitiæ.
paras.en: Then the Prophet, speaking of the future after the manner of the past (though we now see it already fulfilled), adds: [[97:2|The Lord hath made known|Notum fecit Dominus]] (the Lord, that is, God the Father) [[97:2|his salvation|salutare suum]], that is, Christ his Son, the Saviour of the world. First in Judea: for through the miracles which Christ wrought in the name of the Father, the Father declared Jesus of Nazareth to be his Son and the King Messias; wherefore Christ says: [[John 5:36|the works which the Father hath given me|Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater]] [[John 5:36|give testimony of me|testimonium perhibent de me]]. The Father also made his Son known to the shepherds through an angel[[Luke 2:9||]], to Zachary[[Luke 1:67||]] and Elizabeth[[Luke 1:41||]] through the Holy Ghost, and likewise to Anna and Simeon[[Luke 2:25||]]. Moreover, when Christ had been baptized, and afterwards when he was transfigured, the Father thundered from heaven, saying: [[Matt 3:17|This is|Hic est]] [[Matt 3:17|my beloved Son|Filius meus dilectus]][[Matt 17:5||]]. Secondly, he made his salvation known to the Gentiles. Hence it follows: [[97:2|in the sight of the Gentiles|in conspectu gentium]] [[97:2|he hath revealed|revelavit]], through the preaching of the Apostles, [[97:2|his justice|justitiam suam]], that is, Christ, who is essentially just and is justice itself: who is called the justice of God because the Father redeemed the world through him, not by power alone, but by the manner and way of justice. Or, [[97:2|his justice|Justitiam suam]], that is, the precepts and counsels of the law of the Gospel, in which the fullness of justice is contained.

paras.t: Hujus pulchri dulcisque versiculi sensum ac verba, illustrissimus Isaias frequenter in libro visionum suarum deprompsit. Ait enim: Revelabitur gloria Domini, et videbit omnis caro salutare Dei nostri. Et: Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium; et videbunt omnes fines terræ salutare Dei nostri. Et: Prope feci justitiam meam; non elongabitur, et salus mea non morabitur.
paras.en: The sense and the words of this fair and sweet little verse the most illustrious Isaias often brought forth in the book of his visions. For he says: [[Is 40:5|the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see|Revelabitur gloria Domini, et videbit omnis caro]] the salvation of our God [Denis's wording here follows Luke 3:6, where this verse is given as "all flesh shall see the salvation of God"; Isaias has "that the mouth of the Lord hath spoken"]. And: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles: and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God|Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium; et videbunt omnes fines terræ salutare Dei nostri]]. And: I have brought my justice near, it shall not be afar off: and my salvation shall not tarry[[Is 46:13||]].

paras.t: Recordatus est Deus Pater misericordiæ suæ, qua clementer promisit se missurum Filium suum in mundum, et veritatis suæ, qua veraciter adimplevit promissum, mittendo Christum. Dicitur autem Deus recordatus misericordiæ suæ et veritatis suæ, impendendo nobis effectum suæ misericordiæ ac veritatis. Et quia specialiter promisit Patriarchis et Prophetis filiisque eorum de Christi adventu, idcirco nunc dicitur recordatus misericordiæ suæ et veritatis suæ domui Israel, id est populo Judæorum, videlicet ad salutem ipsorum. Unde et Christus in Evangelio: Non sum, inquit, missus, nisi ad oves quæ perierunt, domus Israel. Et Virgo Christifera: Suscepit Israel puerum suum, recordatus misericordiæ suæ, sicut locutus est ad patres nostros, etc.
paras.en: [[97:3|He hath remembered|Recordatus est]] (God the Father, that is) [[97:3|his mercy|misericordiæ suæ]], by which he mercifully promised that he would send his Son into the world, [[97:3|and his truth|et veritatis suæ]], by which he truly fulfilled the promise by sending Christ. Now God is said to have [[97:3|remembered his mercy and his truth|recordatus misericordiæ suæ et veritatis suæ]] in bestowing on us the effect of his mercy and truth. And because he made the promise of Christ's coming specially to the Patriarchs and Prophets and their children, it is therefore said here that he hath [[97:3|remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel|recordatus misericordiæ suæ et veritatis suæ domui Israel]], that is, toward the people of the Jews, namely for their salvation. Hence Christ too says in the Gospel: [[Matt 15:24|I was not|Non sum]], he says, [[Matt 15:24|sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|missus, nisi ad oves quæ perierunt, domus Israel]]. And the Virgin who bore Christ: [[Luke 1:54|He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy|Suscepit Israel puerum suum, recordatus misericordiæ suæ]], [[Luke 1:55|As he spoke to our fathers|sicut locutus est ad patres nostros]], etc.

paras.t: Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri: id est, omnes fines mundi, seu homines universi (ut distributio sit pro generibus singulorum), per fidem cognoverunt salutare Dei nostri, scilicet Christum. Ideo enim Simeon justus ait: Viderunt oculi mei salutare tuum, quod parasti ante faciem omnium populorum. Et Christus dixit Apostolis: Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ.
paras.en: [[97:3|All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God|Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri]]: that is, all the bounds of the world, or all men (so that the distribution is for the kinds of individuals [a term of the logicians: "all" is taken here for men of every kind, not for every single man]), have known by faith [[97:3|the salvation of our God|salutare Dei nostri]], namely Christ. For this is why the just Simeon says: [[Luke 2:30|my eyes have seen thy salvation|Viderunt oculi mei salutare tuum]], [[Luke 2:31|Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples|quod parasti ante faciem omnium populorum]]. And Christ said to the Apostles: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]].

paras.t: Propter tantum autem beneficium, invitantur homines universi ad gratiarum actionem: Jubilate, id est, cum excessivo atque inenarrabili gaudio mentis, laudem dicite Domino Christo seu Deo trino, omnis terra, id est omnes habitantes in terra; cantate, voce laudando, et exsultate, corde gaudendo, et psallite, bene vivendo.
paras.en: Now for so great a benefit all men are invited to give thanks: [[97:4|Sing joyfully|Jubilate]], that is, with an overflowing and unspeakable joy of mind speak praise to the Lord Christ, or to God the Three in One, [[97:4|all the earth|omnis terra]], that is, all who dwell on the earth; [[97:4|make melody|cantate]], praising with the voice; [[97:4|rejoice|et exsultate]], rejoicing in heart; [[97:4|and sing|et psallite]], by living well.

paras.t: Psallite, id est, psalmos devote proferte, Domino, et hoc, in cithara, in cithara et voce psalmi, in tubis ductilibus. Ad literam Hebræi utebantur his musicis instrumentis in laudibus Dei, psallendo ore et organis istis.
paras.en: [[97:5|Sing praise|Psallite]], that is, devoutly utter psalms, [[97:5|to the Lord|Domino]], and this [[97:5|on the harp, on the harp, and with the voice of a psalm|in cithara, in cithara et voce psalmi]], [[97:6|With long trumpets|in tubis ductilibus]]. In the letter, the Hebrews used these musical instruments in the praises of God, singing psalms with the mouth and with these instruments.

paras.t: Spiritualiter autem per citharam intelliguntur misericordiæ opera, seu mortificatio carnis, sicut frequenter ostensum est. Per tubas ductiles, quæ tundendo formantur, designantur tribulationes et adversitates vitæ præsentis, quibus electi tunduntur, ut sint lapides apti in ædificium regni cælestis. Per tubam corneam, id est de cornu corio factam, quod carnem tegit, et eminet, significatur contemplatio divinorum, per quam temporalia transcenduntur. Est itaque sensus: Psallite Domino in cithara, id est cum carnis mortificatione et operibus misericordiæ, ne vita carnalis atque crudelis psalmodiam vestram faciat inacceptam; in cithara, inquam, et voce psalmi, quatenus vita voci concordet. Psallite quoque Domino in tubis ductilibus, id est, in adversis et tribulationibus atque tentationibus vestris, gratias agite Christo: quemadmodum Jacobus monet, Omne gaudium existimate, fratres, quum in diversas tentationes incideritis. Psallite etiam Domino et in voce tubæ corneæ, id est in laude vocali, ex divinorum contemplatione procedente.
paras.en: Spiritually, by the harp are understood the works of mercy, or the mortification of the flesh, as has often been shown. By the long trumpets [*tubæ ductiles*, "drawn" or "beaten" trumpets], which are shaped by hammering, are signified the tribulations and adversities of the present life, by which the elect are hammered, that they may be stones fit for the building of the heavenly kingdom. By the cornet [*tuba cornea*, "trumpet of horn"], that is, one made of horn, a hard covering [*corium*, "hide"] which covers the flesh and stands out from it, is signified the contemplation of divine things, by which temporal things are transcended. This, then, is the sense: [[97:5|Sing praise to the Lord on the harp|Psallite Domino in cithara]], that is, with mortification of the flesh and with works of mercy, lest a carnal and cruel life make your psalmody unacceptable; [[97:5|on the harp|in cithara]], I say, [[97:5|and with the voice of a psalm|et voce psalmi]], so that the life may be in accord with the voice. [[97:5|Sing praise|Psallite]] also [[97:5|to the Lord|Domino]] [[97:6|With long trumpets|in tubis ductilibus]], that is, in your adversities and tribulations and temptations give thanks to Christ, as James admonishes: [[Jas 1:2|count it all joy|Omne gaudium existimate]], brethren, [[Jas 1:2|when you shall fall into divers temptations|quum in diversas tentationes incideritis]]. Sing praise to the Lord also with the [[97:6|sound of cornet|voce tubæ corneæ]], that is, in vocal praise proceeding from the contemplation of divine things.

paras.t: Jubilate in conspectu regis Domini, id est coram Christo omnium rege ac Domino, jubilando ei corde collecto, atque in ejus præsentia constituto: moveatur mare, id est sæculum istud, et plenitudo ejus, id est habitantes in eo, ad fidem et reverentiam Salvatoris. Quod clarius exponendo subjungit: orbis terrarum et qui habitant in eo. Vel per mare et plenitudinem ejus, intelliguntur negotiantes in mari, et habitantes circa ipsum.
paras.en: [[97:6|Make a joyful noise before the Lord our king|Jubilate in conspectu regis Domini]], that is, before Christ, the King and Lord of all, singing joyfully to him with a recollected heart, set in his presence: [[97:7|Let the sea be moved|moveatur mare]], that is, this world, [[97:7|and the fullness thereof|et plenitudo ejus]], that is, those who dwell in it, unto faith in the Saviour and reverence for him. This he sets out more clearly by adding: [[97:7|the world and they that dwell therein|orbis terrarum et qui habitant in eo]]. Or by the sea and the fullness thereof are understood those who trade on the sea and those who dwell about it.

paras.t: Flumina, id est fideles aquis Baptismatis regenerati, et rivis gratiæ pleni, plaudent manu simul, id est, Deum concorditer cum exsultatione cordis ac bonis operibus collaudabunt; montes, id est contemplativi et in omni virtute sublimes, exsultabunt a conspectu Domini, id est ex consideratione adventus atque præsentiæ Christi: quod de utroque ejus adventu et conspectu intelligi potest. Uterque enim justis jucundus est, quoniam venit judicare terram, in primo suo adventu judicio discretionis, increpando vitia ipsorum; in secundo autem adventu veniet judicare mundum judicio retributionis finalis, sicut subjungitur:
paras.en: [[97:8|The rivers|Flumina]], that is, the faithful, born again in the waters of Baptism and full of the streams of grace, [[97:8|shall clap their hands|plaudent manu]] together [Denis takes *simul*, "together", with the clapping of hands; the Douay-Rheims joins it to the mountains], that is, they shall praise God with one accord, with exultation of heart and with good works; [[97:8|the mountains|montes]], that is, the contemplatives, lofty in every virtue, [[97:8|shall rejoice|exsultabunt]] [[97:9|At the presence of the Lord|a conspectu Domini]], that is, from considering the coming and presence of Christ: which may be understood of both his comings and of his presence in each. For each is a joy to the just, [[97:9|because he cometh to judge the earth|quoniam venit judicare terram]]: in his first coming with the judgment of discernment [that is, the judgment that tells good from evil in this life, as distinct from the final judgment of reward and punishment], rebuking their vices; but in his second coming he will come to judge the world with the judgment of final retribution, as follows:

paras.t: Judicabit orbem terrarum in justitia; et quid sit hoc, exponit adjungens, et, pro id est, populos in æquitate. Omnes enim nos oportet stare ante tribunal Christi, ut recipiat unusquisque prout gessit, secundum Apostolum. Est autem judicium discussionis seu retributionis, duplex: videlicet particulare, quo animæ singulorum judicantur, mox dum a corpore exeunt; et universale, quod erit in fine mundi. Et de utroque accipi potest quod scriptum est: Patientes estote usque ad adventum Domini, et confirmate corda vestra, quoniam adventus Domini appropinquabit. Ecce judex ante januam adsistit. De ista materia cito pertranseo, quoniam in expositione duorum psalmorum præcedentium multa de ea commemorata recordor.
paras.en: [[97:9|He shall judge the world with justice|Judicabit orbem terrarum in justitia]]; and what this is he explains by adding: and (here *and* stands for "that is") [[97:9|the people with equity|populos in æquitate]]. For, according to the Apostle, [[2 Cor 5:10|we must all|Omnes enim nos oportet]] stand [[2 Cor 5:10|before the judgment seat of Christ|ante tribunal Christi]], [[2 Cor 5:10|that every one may receive|ut recipiat unusquisque]] [[2 Cor 5:10|according as he hath done|prout gessit]] [Denis reads *stare*, "stand", where the Vulgate has *manifestari*, "be manifested"]. Now the judgment of examination, or of retribution, is twofold: namely the particular, by which the souls of individuals are judged as soon as they leave the body; and the universal, which will be at the end of the world. And of both may be taken what is written: [[Jas 5:7|Be patient|Patientes estote]] [[Jas 5:7|until the coming of the Lord|usque ad adventum Domini]], [[Jas 5:8|and strengthen your hearts: for the coming of the Lord is at hand|et confirmate corda vestra, quoniam adventus Domini appropinquabit]]. [[Jas 5:9|Behold the judge standeth before the door|Ecce judex ante januam adsistit]] [the margin gives James v, 8, 9; the opening words, "Be patient … until the coming of the Lord", are from v. 7]. I pass quickly over this matter, since I remember having set down much about it in the exposition of the two preceding psalms.

paras.t: Denique decet nos psalmum istum dulcifluum ac amœnum, tanto affectuosius devotiusque cantare, atque in ejus decantatione tanto jucundius Domino jubilare, quanto in eo de Christo, et ejus primo adventu ceterisque mysteriis, et gentium vocatione ad fidem et gratiam Salvatoris, evidentius agitur, atque ad Dei præconia persolvenda frequentius invitamur. Nihil enim Christiano dulcius sapere debet, quam sermo divinus in quo de Christi incarnatione ac mundi redemptione tractatur: idcirco psalmi inde loquentes, devotissime sunt cantandi.
paras.en: Finally, it befits us to sing this sweetly flowing and lovely psalm with all the more affection and devotion, and in singing it to rejoice in the Lord with all the more gladness, the more plainly it treats of Christ, of his first coming and his other mysteries, and of the calling of the Gentiles to the faith and grace of the Saviour, and the more often we are invited in it to render the praises of God. For nothing ought to taste sweeter to a Christian than the divine word in which the incarnation of Christ and the redemption of the world are treated; therefore the psalms that speak of these things are to be sung most devoutly.

paras.t: Precatio. Omnipotens, æterne Deus, qui facis mirabilia solus, recordare misericordiæ tuæ, nosque aberrantes corrige, atque tibi perseveranter atque fideliter fac adhærere: ut digni efficiamur tibi Domino cantica placita perpetim decantare.
paras.en: Prayer. Almighty and eternal God, who alone doest wonderful things, remember thy mercy; correct us who go astray, and make us cleave to thee perseveringly and faithfully, that we may be made worthy to sing to thee, our Lord, pleasing canticles for ever.

98.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI NONAGESIMI OCTAVI : DOMINUS REGNAVIT, IRASCANTUR POPULI.
98.title_en: Exposition of the ninety-eighth psalm: The Lord hath reigned, let the people be angry.

paras.t: Porro titulus psalmi nunc exponendi, in verbis ac sensu idem est cum titulo psalmi immediate præhabiti. Loquitur enim hic psalmus ad litteram de Christo, et regia magnificentia atque multiplici laude ipsius. Et qui eum ad litteram exponunt de David et regno ejus, non solum sanctis catholicisque doctoribus superficialiores sunt, sed etiam quibusdam Hebræorum doctoribus, qui ipsum ad litteram exponunt de rege Messia.
paras.en: Now the title of the psalm now to be expounded is the same in words and in sense as the title of the psalm immediately before it [both read *Psalmus ipsi David*, "A psalm for David himself"]. For this psalm speaks literally of Christ, and of his royal magnificence and manifold praise. And those who expound it literally of David and his kingdom are more superficial not only than the holy Catholic doctors, but even than certain doctors of the Hebrews, who expound it literally of the king Messias.

paras.t: De eo igitur loquens David propheta, ait: Dominus Christus, qui primo suo adventu non venit ministrari, sed ministrare, regnavit in Ecclesia militante post resurrectionem et ascensionem; et usque in finem mundi regnabit in ea. Irascantur populi infideles: id est, quantumcumque irati, indignati, reluctatique fuerint regno Christi, illud impedire non poterunt. Vel, Irascantur, id est, irascentur: quia perversi conati sunt regnum Christi destruere, ejusque famam et gloriam exstirpare. Propter quod Paulus: Ostium, inquit, mihi apertum est, et adversarii multi. Vel, Irascantur, id est, ira salubri contra vitia sua insurgant ac vindicent. Qui sedet super Cherubim, id est, Christus, qui ut Deus, omnem plenitudinem creatæ scientiæ superexcedit (de quo in libro Job dicitur, Non audebunt eum contemplari omnes qui sibi videntur sapientes), qui etiam ut homo, elevatus est super omnes ordines angelorum, regnavit; moveatur terra, id est, populus universæ terræ convertatur motu servitutis ac fidei ad Dominum Salvatorem. Vel, Moveatur ad impatientiam quantumcumque voluerit, invidendo gloriæ Christi, sed nihil proficiet. Hoc autem non optando seu imprecando, sed insinuando insuperabilem potestatem Christi, asseritur. Vel, Moveatur, id est, movebitur ad resistendum Christo: quod non optando, sed prænuntiando, intelligi debet. Unde dicit Apostolus: Quemadmodum Jannes et Mambres restiterunt Moysi, ita et hi resistunt veritati; sed ultra non proficient, insipientia enim illorum manifesta erit omnibus.
paras.en: Speaking of him, then, David the prophet says: [[98:1|The Lord|Dominus]] Christ, who at his first coming [[Matt 20:28|is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister|non venit ministrari, sed ministrare]], [[98:1|hath reigned|regnavit]] in the Church militant after the resurrection and ascension; and he will reign in it until the end of the world. [[98:1|let the people be angry|Irascantur populi]], the unbelieving peoples: that is, however angry, indignant and resistant they may be toward the kingdom of Christ, they will not be able to hinder it. Or, [[98:1|let the people be angry|Irascantur]], that is, they will be angry [the wish *irascantur* taken as the future *irascentur*, a foretelling]: for the perverse have striven to destroy the kingdom of Christ and to root out his fame and glory. Hence Paul says: "A [[1 Cor 16:9|door|Ostium]]," he says, "[[1 Cor 16:9|is opened unto me: and many adversaries|mihi apertum est, et adversarii multi]]." Or, [[98:1|let the people be angry|Irascantur]], that is, let them rise up with a wholesome anger against their own vices and punish them. [[98:1|he that sitteth on the cherubims|Qui sedet super Cherubim]] [the name *Cherubim* was taken to mean "fullness of knowledge"], that is, Christ, who as God surpasses all the fullness of created knowledge (of whom it is said in the book of Job: They [[Job 37:24|shall not dare to behold him|Non audebunt eum contemplari]], [[Job 37:24|all that seem to themselves to be wise|omnes qui sibi videntur sapientes]]), and who also as man has been raised above all the orders of angels, hath reigned; [[98:1|let the earth be moved|moveatur terra]], that is, let the people of the whole earth be turned, with a movement of service and of faith, to the Lord the Saviour. Or, [[98:1|let the earth be moved|Moveatur]] to impatience as much as it will, envying the glory of Christ, yet it will gain nothing. This is said not as a wish or a curse, but to make known the unconquerable power of Christ. Or, [[98:1|let the earth be moved|Moveatur]], that is, it will be moved to resist Christ: which is to be understood not as a wish but as a foretelling. Hence the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 3:8|as Jannes and Mambres resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth|Quemadmodum Jannes et Mambres restiterunt Moysi, ita et hi resistunt veritati]]; [[2 Tim 3:9|But they shall proceed no farther: for their folly shall be manifest to all men|sed ultra non proficient, insipientia enim illorum manifesta erit omnibus]].

paras.t: Dominus Christus est in Sion, id est in Ecclesia ipsum fideliter contemplante, magnus: quemadmodum Gabriel Virgini Matri prædixit, Hic erit magnus, et Filius Altissimi vocabitur. Est autem Christus magnus duplici magnitudine. Nam, ut Deus, est magnus magnitudine infinita et increata, quæ est tribus Personis una et indivisa, idemque quod ipsa divina essentia. Unde dicit Apostolus: Sobrie, juste et pie vivamus in hoc sæculo, exspectantes beatam spem et adventum gloriæ magni Dei. Est item Christus magnus magnitudine creata atque finita, non corporali, sed spirituali, id est in omni gratia, sapientia ac virtute perfectus, juxta illud: Puer (Jesus) crescebat et confortabatur, plenus sapientia; et gratia Dei erat in illo. Hac magnitudine magnus erat a principio conceptionis suæ in Virgine; et ob eam dictus est vir, adhuc exsistens in utero matris, secundum quod de ipso apud Jeremiam conscriptum est: Novum creavit Dominus super terram, Mulier circumdabit virum. Et Dominus iste est excelsus loco ac dignitate super omnes populos. Sedet enim ad dexteram Patris, et ut Deus, omnia in infinitum excedit in omni dignitate et perfectione; sed ut homo, perfectior est in omni gratia, quam omnes electi simul in cœlo et terra. Propter quod Isaias inquit: Ecce gentes quasi stilla situlæ, et quasi momentum stateræ reputatæ sunt.
paras.en: [[98:2|The Lord|Dominus]] Christ is [[98:2|in Sion|in Sion]], that is, in the Church that faithfully contemplates him, [[98:2|great|magnus]]: as Gabriel foretold to the Virgin Mother: [[Luke 1:32|He shall be great and shall be called the Son of the Most High|Hic erit magnus, et Filius Altissimi vocabitur]]. Now Christ is great with a twofold greatness. For as God he is great with an infinite and uncreated greatness, which is one and undivided in the three Persons, and the same as the divine essence itself. Hence the Apostle says: [[Tit 2:12|we should live soberly and justly and godly in this world|Sobrie, juste et pie vivamus in hoc sæculo]], [[Tit 2:13|Looking for the blessed hope and coming of the glory of the great God|exspectantes beatam spem et adventum gloriæ magni Dei]]. Christ is likewise great with a created and finite greatness, not bodily but spiritual, that is, perfect in all grace, wisdom and virtue, according to that saying: [[Luke 2:40|the child|Puer]] (Jesus) [[Luke 2:40|grew and waxed strong, full of wisdom: and the grace of God was in him|crescebat et confortabatur, plenus sapientia; et gratia Dei erat in illo]]. With this greatness he was great from the first moment of his conception in the Virgin; and because of it he was called a *man* while still in his mother's womb, according to what is written of him in Jeremias: [[Jer 31:22|the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Novum creavit Dominus super terram, Mulier circumdabit virum]]. And this Lord is [[98:2|high|excelsus]] in place and in dignity [[98:2|above all people|super omnes populos]]. For he sitteth at the right hand of the Father[[Mark 16:19||]], and as God he infinitely surpasses all things in every dignity and perfection; but as man he is more perfect in all grace than all the elect together in heaven and on earth. Wherefore Isaias says: [[Is 40:15|Behold the Gentiles are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the smallest grain of a balance|Ecce gentes quasi stilla situlæ, et quasi momentum stateræ reputatæ sunt]].

paras.t: Confitentur, o Christe, homines universi nomini tuo magno: de quo dicit Apostolus, Donavit illi (scilicet Christo Pater) nomen, quod est super omne nomen. Huic omnes confiteantur, id est tibi ipsi, duplici confessione, videlicet te laudando, et se accusando. quoniam terribile et sanctum est. Est enim terribile, quoniam omnes districtissime judicas; et sanctum, quoniam purum ac bonum, omnisque puritatis fontale principium. Et honor regis, id est regia dignitas Christi, judicium, id est actum justitiæ, diligit. Præcepit namque Christus, rex noster, in veteri ac novo Testamento, judicium fieri, ordinans prælatos ac principes in militanti Ecclesia, quorum est inferioribus judicium facere. Vult quoque, ut ipsi prælati ac judices propria facta discutiant, discernant ac judicent: imo a quolibet nostrum requirit, ut per rationem judicet semetipsum, vitia propria condemnando, ulciscendo ac relinquendo. Propter quod dicit Apostolus: Si nos ipsos dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur. Et alibi habetur: Quærite judicium, subvenite oppresso.
paras.en: [[98:3|Let them give praise|Confitentur]], O Christ, all men, [[98:3|to thy great name|nomini tuo magno]] [the print has *Confitentur*, "they give praise", where the psalm has *Confiteantur*, "let them give praise"]: of which the Apostle says: [[Phil 2:9|hath given him|Donavit illi]] (that is, the Father to Christ) [[Phil 2:9|a name which is above all names|nomen, quod est super omne nomen]]. To this name let all give praise, that is, to thee thyself, with a twofold confession [the Latin *confiteri* means both to praise and to confess], namely by praising thee and by accusing themselves; [[98:3|for it is terrible and holy|quoniam terribile et sanctum est]]. For it is terrible, since thou judgest all men most strictly; and holy, since it is pure and good, and the fountainhead of all purity. [[98:4|And the king's honour|Et honor regis]], that is, the royal dignity of Christ, [[98:4|loveth judgment|judicium diligit]], that is, the doing of justice. For Christ, [[Is 33:22|our king|rex noster]], commanded in the Old and in the New Testament that judgment be done, appointing prelates and princes in the Church militant, whose office it is to do judgment for those beneath them. He wills also that these prelates and judges examine, discern and judge their own deeds; nay, he requires of each one of us that he judge himself by reason, condemning, punishing and forsaking his own vices. Wherefore the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 11:31|if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged|Si nos ipsos dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur]]. And elsewhere it is found: [[Is 1:17|seek judgment, relieve the oppressed|Quærite judicium, subvenite oppresso]].

paras.t: Tu, Christe, legifer noster, parasti directiones, id est, mandata vitæ nobis ostendisti, per quæ dirigitur homo in ultimum finem seu vitam æternam; judicium, id est discretionem inter bonum ac malum, verum ac falsum, et justitiam, id est justitiæ exsecutionem seu boni operationem ac mali evitationem, in Jacob patriarcha et populo Judæorum, seu populo christiano, quorum est vitia supplantare, tu fecisti per gratiam, dando eis virtutem recte judicandi, ac juste agendi. Omnia enim opera nostra operatus es in nobis, secundum Isaiam; et Deus est qui operatur in nobis et velle et perficere, secundum Apostolum.
paras.en: [[98:4|Thou|Tu]], O Christ, [[Is 33:22|our lawgiver|legifer noster]], [[98:4|hast prepared directions|parasti directiones]], that is, thou hast shown us the commandments of life, by which man is directed to his last end, that is, to life everlasting; [[98:4|judgment|judicium]], that is, discernment between good and evil, true and false, [[98:4|and justice|et justitiam]], that is, the carrying out of justice, or the doing of good and the avoiding of evil, [[98:4|in Jacob|in Jacob]] the patriarch and in the Jewish people, or in the Christian people, whose part it is to supplant vices [*Jacob* means "supplanter"], [[98:4|thou hast done|tu fecisti]] by grace, giving them the power to judge rightly and to act justly. For [[Is 26:12|thou hast wrought all our works for us|Omnia enim opera nostra operatus es in nobis]], according to Isaias; and [[Phil 2:13|it is God who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish|Deus est qui operatur in nobis et velle et perficere]], according to the Apostle [in both places Denis reads *in nobis*, "in us"].

paras.t: Idcirco de tantis beneficiis, o fideles, exaltate, id est sublimiter colite, excellentissime honorate, et laude præclara universis præferte, Dominum Deum nostrum, qui solus est verus Deus, dicentes illud Danielis: Oculos meos ad cœlum levo, et Altissimo benedico, et viventem in sempiternum glorifico, et regem cæli laudo atque magnifico. Et adorate scabellum pedum ejus, id est humanam naturam Christi, in qua divinitas Verbi stetit quasi supra scabellum. Hæc humanitas, in quantum est unita Deo in unitate personæ, adoratur adoratione latriæ, non per se, neque seorsum; sed dum Christus Deus et homo adoratur, adoratur et ejus humanitas.
paras.en: Therefore, for such great benefits, O ye faithful, [[98:5|Exalt ye|exaltate]], that is, worship on high, honour most excellently, and with glorious praise set above all things, [[98:5|the Lord our God|Dominum Deum nostrum]], who alone is the true God, saying those words of Daniel: I [[Dan 4:31|lifted up my eyes to heaven|Oculos meos ad cœlum levo]], [[Dan 4:31|and I blessed the most High|et Altissimo benedico]], and [[Dan 4:31|glorified him that liveth for ever|viventem in sempiternum glorifico]], and [[Dan 4:34|praise, and magnify, and glorify the King of heaven|regem cæli laudo atque magnifico]] [Denis puts Nabuchodonosor's words into the present: "I lift up my eyes to heaven, and bless the Most High, and glorify him that liveth for ever, and praise and magnify the King of heaven"]. [[98:5|and adore his footstool|Et adorate scabellum pedum ejus]], that is, the human nature of Christ, on which the divinity of the Word has stood as on a footstool. This humanity, inasmuch as it is united to God in unity of person, is adored with the adoration of latria [that is, the worship owed to God alone], not of itself nor apart; but when Christ, God and man, is adored, his humanity also is adored.

paras.t: Pensandum vero circa præsentem materiam, quæ multis facit difficultatem, dubitationemque anxiam, quod secundum B. Thomam in tertia parte, quæstione 25, duo considerari possunt in eo qui honoratur, videlicet ipsum totum subsistens, et ea quæ in ipso sunt. Honor autem non impenditur proprie et per se, nisi toti subsistenti. Si enim pars alicujus honoretur, videlicet manus aut pes, hoc non est propter se, sed in quantum est aliquid totius: sicque totum honoratur in parte. Causa autem honoris, est excellentia honorati: quoniam honor est exhibitio reverentiæ, alteri impensa in signum seu testimonium perfectionis sive virtutis. Dum ergo in uno supposito sunt plures excellentiæ, scilicet prælatio, sapientia, sanctitas vitæ, erunt plures atque distinctæ honorationes unius, secundum ordinem ad causas honorationis, secundum quod causæ plures sunt et distinctæ; sed ex parte personæ quæ honoratur, erit honoratio una. Denique adoratio in sacra Scriptura non semper accipitur prout est actus latriæ, scilicet pro cultu soli vero Deo impendendo, sed vicissim sumitur pro quacumque excellenti veneratione alterius. Unde scriptum est: Surrexit rex Salomon in occursum matris suæ, adoravitque eam. Et eodem libro legitur Bethsabee capite inclinato David regem adorasse. Similiter in libro Josue scriptum est, quemadmodum Josue angelum adoravit.
paras.en: Now concerning the present matter, which gives many people difficulty and anxious doubt, it is to be weighed that, according to Blessed Thomas in the third part, question 25, two things can be considered in one who is honoured: namely, the whole subsisting thing itself, and the things that are in it. Now honour is not paid properly and of itself except to the whole subsisting thing [that is, the complete individual, the person or *suppositum*]. For if a part of someone is honoured, say a hand or a foot, this is not for its own sake, but inasmuch as it is something of the whole; and so the whole is honoured in the part. Now the cause of honour is the excellence of the one honoured, since honour is a showing of reverence paid to another as a sign or testimony of perfection or virtue. When, therefore, there are several excellences in one suppositum, such as rank, wisdom and holiness of life, there will be several distinct honourings of the one, according to their relation to the causes of honouring, inasmuch as the causes are several and distinct; but on the part of the person who is honoured, the honouring will be one. Lastly, adoration in Holy Scripture is not always taken as an act of latria, that is, for the worship to be paid to the true God alone, but is sometimes used for any excellent veneration of another. Hence it is written: [[3 Kings 2:19|the king arose to meet her, and bowed to her|Surrexit rex Salomon in occursum matris suæ, adoravitque eam]] [Denis: "King Solomon arose to meet his mother, and adored her"; the Douay-Rheims has "bowed to her"]. And in the same book we read that Bethsabee, with head bowed, adored King David[[3 Kings 1:16||]]. Likewise in the book of Josue it is written how Josue adored the angel[[Jos 5:15||]].

paras.t: Quum igitur quæritur, an una atque eadem adoratione sit adoranda humanitas ac divinitas Christi, dicendum quod imo, secundum comparationem seu ordinem ad totum subsistens, quoniam una est adoratio qua totus Christus adoratur propter unitatem personæ. Sed dici possunt plures adorationes, sumendo adorationem communiter secundum diversas causas honorationis, propter quas Christus adoratur. Nam propter sapientiam increatam, adoratur adoratione latriæ proprie sumpta; propter sapientiam vero et sanctitatem et gratiam suam creatam, adoratur adoratione communiter sumpta, quæ dicitur adoratio duliæ, vel potius hyperduliæ, id est excellenti honoratione duliæ. Sicut enim latria est virtus quæ Deo cultum cæremoniamque impendit; sic dulia dicitur virtus quæ creaturis excellentibus debitum affert honorem.
paras.en: When, therefore, it is asked whether the humanity and the divinity of Christ are to be adored with one and the same adoration, the answer is yes, by comparison or relation to the whole subsisting thing, since the adoration by which the whole Christ is adored is one, because of the unity of the person. But several adorations can be spoken of, taking adoration in a broad sense, according to the different causes of honouring for which Christ is adored. For on account of his uncreated wisdom he is adored with the adoration of latria properly so called; but on account of his created wisdom, holiness and grace he is adored with adoration taken in a broad sense, which is called the adoration of dulia, or rather of hyperdulia, that is, an excellent honouring of dulia. For as latria is the virtue that pays worship and ceremony to God, so dulia is the name of the virtue that gives due honour to excellent creatures.

paras.t: Quum insuper quæritur, an adoratio latriæ sit impendenda humanitati Christi, respondendum, sicut nunc tactum est, quod adoratio proprie non competit nisi toti subsistenti seu supposito: idcirco humanitas Christi non dicitur proprie aut directe adoranda seorsum vel per se, sed tamen eo modo quo potest adorari. Dicendum quod adoratio humanitatis Christi dupliciter intelligi potest. Primo, ut adoratio ejus intelligatur esse illius, cujus est ipsa, scilicet Verbi: et ita debetur humanitati Christi adoratio latriæ. Sic namque adorare Christi humanitatem, aliud non est nisi adorare Verbum incarnatum; quemadmodum adorare purpuram regis, est adorare regem purpuratum. Secundo, intelligi potest adoratio humanitatis Christi, ita ut sit ejus secundum se, scilicet ut impendatur ei ratione sui, seu propter plenitudinem gratiæ suæ: sicque non debetur neque impenditur ei adoratio latriæ, sed veneratio duliæ.
paras.en: Further, when it is asked whether the adoration of latria is to be paid to the humanity of Christ, the answer, as was touched on just now, is that adoration properly belongs only to the whole subsisting thing or suppositum: therefore the humanity of Christ is not said to be adored properly or directly, apart or of itself, but yet in the way in which it can be adored. It must be said, then, that the adoration of Christ's humanity can be understood in two ways. First, so that its adoration is understood to be the adoration of him whose humanity it is, namely of the Word: and in this way the adoration of latria is due to the humanity of Christ. For to adore the humanity of Christ in this way is nothing else than to adore the Word incarnate; just as to adore the king's purple is to adore the king clothed in purple. Secondly, the adoration of Christ's humanity can be understood as belonging to it in itself, that is, as paid to it by reason of itself, or on account of the fullness of its grace: and in this way the adoration of latria is neither due nor paid to it, but the veneration of dulia.

paras.t: Christus itaque duplici honoratione adoratur, utpote adoratione latriæ, propter naturam divinam et increatam, et adoratione duliæ, propter naturam humanam.
paras.en: Christ, then, is adored with a twofold honouring: with the adoration of latria, on account of his divine and uncreated nature, and with the adoration of dulia, on account of his human nature.

paras.t: Loquendo ergo de adoratione proprie dicta, nulli debetur proprie et per se, nisi increato supposito. Unde Damascenus tertio libro dicit: Adoratur autem caro Christi in Verbo Dei incarnato, non propter se ipsam, sed propter unitum, secundum hypostasim, Verbum. Cujus simile ponit de purpura regis, quæ honore soli regi debito honoratur, non secundum vel propter se, sed prout est indumentum regis: et sicut rex purpuratus regio veneratur honore, rex quidem proprie et per se, purpura vero, prout est aliquid regi conjunctum; sic Verbum incarnatum adoratur adoratione latriæ propter se proprie et directe, caro vero seu humanitas ejus, prout est aliquid sibi unitum.
paras.en: Speaking, then, of adoration properly so called, it is due properly and of itself to none but an uncreated suppositum. Hence Damascene says in his third book: "The flesh of Christ is adored in the incarnate Word of God, not for its own sake, but on account of the Word united to it according to the hypostasis." He gives a likeness of this in the king's purple, which is honoured with the honour due to the king alone, not according to itself or for its own sake, but as it is the king's garment: and as the king clothed in purple is venerated with royal honour, the king properly and of himself, but the purple as something joined to the king; so the Word incarnate is adored with the adoration of latria for his own sake, properly and directly, but his flesh or humanity as something united to him.

paras.t: Moyses et Aaron in sacerdotibus ejus, id est, de numero sacerdotum Dei fuerunt in veteri Testamento. Aaron namque pontifex erat et summus sacerdos, preces et hostias populi Domino offerens. Moyses vero consecrando seu ordinando Aaron in pontificem, et filios ejus in sacerdotes, prout in Levitico legitur, functus est officio sacerdotis. Et Samuel inter eos qui invocant nomen ejus, id est, de numero fuit eorum qui Deum intime oraverunt in veteri Testamento. Nam et pro adversariis suis precatus est, dicens: Absit a me hoc peccatum in Domino, quominus cessem orare pro vobis. Invocabant Dominum Moyses, Aaron et Samuel pro populi ignorantia, et ipse Dominus exaudiebat eos: quod patet de Moyse et Aaron in libris Exodi et Numerorum, ac alibi. De Samuele etiam scriptum est hoc primo Regum.
paras.en: [[98:6|Moses and Aaron among his priests|Moyses et Aaron in sacerdotibus ejus]], that is, they were of the number of God's priests in the Old Testament. For Aaron was pontiff and high priest, offering the prayers and victims of the people to the Lord. And Moses, in consecrating or ordaining Aaron as pontiff and his sons as priests, as we read in Leviticus[[Lev 8:1||]], performed the office of a priest. [[98:6|and Samuel among them that call upon his name|Et Samuel inter eos qui invocant nomen ejus]], that is, he was of the number of those who prayed to God from the heart in the Old Testament. For he prayed even for his adversaries, saying: [[1 Kings 12:23|far from me be this sin against the Lord, that I should cease to pray for you|Absit a me hoc peccatum in Domino, quominus cessem orare pro vobis]]. Moses, Aaron and Samuel [[98:6|called upon the Lord|Invocabant Dominum]] for the ignorance of the people, [[98:6|and he heard them|et ipse Dominus exaudiebat eos]]: which is plain of Moses and Aaron in the books of Exodus and Numbers, and elsewhere. Of Samuel too this is written, in the first book of Kings.

paras.t: In columna nubis, id est in nube per modum columnæ apparente, loquebatur ad eos Dominus, non in propria persona, sed per angelum ministrantem. De quo Dominus Moysi dixit: Ecce ego mitto angelum meum, qui præcedat te. Quod autem locutus sit hoc modo Dominus Moysi et Aaron in columna nubis, legitur in Exodo; sed de Samuele non legitur hoc in Scriptura canonica manifeste, nisi in psalmo præsenti, propter quod certum est sic esse. Verumtamen primo Regum manifeste describitur, qualiter Dominus orante Samuele dedit voces et pluvias, quæ sine nube non erant. Et forte tunc Dominus loquebatur Samueli in columna nubis, quamvis alii locutionem illam non audierunt: sicut nec ceteri audierunt (ut aliqui asserunt) vocem Patris dicentis de Christo, Hic est Filius meus dilectus: quam tamen audivit Joannes Baptista, Christo baptizato atque orante, ut dicit Lucas.
