Quemadmodum itaque caro talis per ignem arescit, induratur et tabescit ; sic ossa corporis per abstinentiam arefiunt, et per timorem Dei siccantur, secundum illud : Spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa. Ossa quoque animæ, id est virtutes ac vires ipsius, tanquam cremium in frixorio torrefactum arescunt, dum per negligentiam gratia devotionis subtrahitur, et cibus interior (scilicet obedientia sancta) relinquitur. De hoc etenim cibo dicit Christus : Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem Patris mei. Interdum vero ossa ista arescunt igne tentationis ac tribulationis, præsertim in his, in quibus virtus non perficitur in infirmitate : qualis non erat Apostolus. Utroque autem modo intelligi possunt hæc verba de pœnitente. Nam ante conversionem suam ossa animæ infeliciter aruerunt, nulla spirituali pinguedine existente in eis. Post conversionem autem et arreptam pœnitentiam ossa corporis in quibusdam salubriter arefiunt, quibus omnis carnalis voluptas, omnis temporalis jucunditas, omnis etiam alimonia corporis in fastidio sunt, propter intensam mentis occupationem in Deo.
paras.en: [[101:4|and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire|Et ossa mea sicut cremium aruerunt]]. *Cremium* [the word the Douay-Rheims renders "fuel for the fire"] is the name for flesh burnt or fried, what is left when the fat has been drawn out of it by the fire; for *cremium* takes its name from *cremare*, to burn. As such flesh, then, dries up, hardens and wastes away in the fire, so the bones of the body are dried up by abstinence and parched by the fear of God, according to the words: [[Prov 17:22|a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones|Spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa]]. The bones of the soul too, that is, its virtues and powers, dry up like *cremium* roasted in a frying pan, when through negligence the grace of devotion is withdrawn and the inward food (namely holy obedience) is left aside. For of this food Christ says: [[John 4:34|My meat is to do the will|Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem]] of my Father [Denis has "of my Father" for "of him that sent me"]. At times, again, these bones dry up in the fire of temptation and tribulation, above all in those in whom virtue is not made perfect in infirmity[[2 Cor 12:9||]], as the Apostle was not [*virtus* is both "virtue" and "power"; the Douay-Rheims has "power is made perfect in infirmity"]. These words can be understood of the penitent in both ways. For before his conversion the bones of his soul were unhappily dried up, with no spiritual fatness in them; but after his conversion and the taking up of penance the bones of the body are, in some, wholesomely dried up: in those to whom all carnal pleasure, all temporal delight, and even all nourishment of the body are distasteful, because of the intense occupation of their mind with God.

paras.t: Percussus sum virga tentationis ac tribulationis, ut fœnum, quoniam sicut fœnum falce abscinditur, sic ego per tentationem aut adversitatem a gratia excidi : sicut de nonnullis ait Apostolus, Propter incredulitatem excisi sunt. Et aruit cor meum a spirituali gratiarum fomento, quia oblitus sum, ex mea ignavia, comedere panem meum, mihi a Deo semper paratum, dummodo eum instanter requiram, dicendo : Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie. Iste panis, est impletio præceptorum Dei, sicut Christus dicit, Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem ejus qui misit me, ut perficiam opus ejus ; seu studium sacræ Scripturæ et meditatio divinorum, de quibus scriptum est, Cibabit illum pane vitæ et intellectus, et aqua sapientiæ salutaris potabit illum ; vel Sacramentum corporis Christi, in quo est omnium cœlestium deliciarum plenitudo, et vita animæ sempiterna, quemadmodum Veritas ait, Qui manducat hunc panem, vivet in æternum. Qui hos panes spiritualiter edere negligit, corde arescit, et est pauper, cæcus, nudus, miser et miserabilis.
paras.en: [[101:5|I am smitten|Percussus sum]] with the rod of temptation and tribulation [[101:5|as grass|ut fœnum]]: for as grass is cut down by the scythe, so I have been cut off from grace by temptation or adversity, as the Apostle says of some: [[Rom 11:20|because of unbelief they were broken off|Propter incredulitatem excisi sunt]] [Denis has *excisi*, "cut off", where the Vulgate has *fracti*, "broken off"; so the text matches the grass cut down by the scythe]. [[101:5|And my heart is withered|Et aruit cor meum]], for want of the spiritual nourishment of graces, [[101:5|because I forgot|quia oblitus sum]], through my own sloth, [[101:5|to eat my bread|comedere panem meum]], which is always made ready for me by God, provided I seek it earnestly, saying: [[Luke 11:3|Give us this day our daily bread.|Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie]][[Matt 6:11||]]. This bread is the fulfilling of God's commandments, as Christ says: [[John 4:34|My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, that I may perfect his work|Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem ejus qui misit me, ut perficiam opus ejus]]; or the study of holy Scripture and meditation on divine things, of which it is written: [[Ecclus 15:3|With the bread of life and understanding, she shall feed him, and give him the water of wholesome wisdom to drink|Cibabit illum pane vitæ et intellectus, et aqua sapientiæ salutaris potabit illum]]; or the Sacrament of the body of Christ, in which is the fullness of all heavenly delights and the everlasting life of the soul, as the Truth says: [[John 6:59|He that eateth this bread shall live for ever|Qui manducat hunc panem, vivet in æternum]]. He who neglects to eat these breads spiritually withers in heart, and is poor, blind, naked, wretched and miserable[[Apoc 3:17||]].

paras.t: A voce gemitus mei, id est præ nimio gemitu et dolore cordis mei, quem voce oris expressi, adhæsit os meum carni meæ, id est, tantum attenuatus sum corpore, ut ossa mea pelli adhærerent : quemadmodum Job dicit, Pelli meæ, consumptis carnibus, adhæsit os meum. Dolor namque interior de peccatis conceptus, si magnus sit et continuus, carnem vehementer consumit. Sumitur itaque hoc loco caro pro pelle.
paras.en: [[101:6|Through the voice of my groaning|A voce gemitus mei]], that is, by reason of the exceeding groaning and sorrow of my heart, which I uttered with the voice of my mouth, [[101:6|my bone hath cleaved to my flesh|adhæsit os meum carni meæ]], that is, I have become so wasted in body that my bones cleave to my skin, as Job says: [[Job 19:20|The flesh being consumed, my bone hath cleaved to my skin|Pelli meæ, consumptis carnibus, adhæsit os meum]]. For inward sorrow conceived for sins, if it is great and continual, consumes the flesh mightily. *Flesh*, then, is taken here for *skin*.

paras.t: Similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis : id est, sicuti pelecanus est avis solitaria, solitudinem diligens, et naturali quadam macie confecta ; sic ego ut peccata mea liberius possem deflere, homines fugi, in solitudine mansi, atque humanum solatium evitavi : prout superius dictum est, Ecce elongavi fugiens, et mansi in solitudine. Per pelecanum autem designatur primum genus pœnitentium, scilicet ordo eremitarum, qui in eremo carnem suam castigant ac macerant, et sua ac aliorum peccata deplangunt. Ad hoc namque agendum, locus solitarius est aptissimus. Unde quum Jeremias dixisset, Quis dabit capiti meo aquam, et oculis meis fontem lacrimarum, et plorabo die ac nocte interfectos populi mei? insinuans se hoc facere non posse in populo tam bene, solitudinem cupit, dicendo : Quis dabit mihi in solitudine diversorium viatorum, et derelinquam populum meum? Factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio : id est, quemadmodum noctua seu corvus nocturnus in pariete domicilii habitans, ceteris avibus odibilis et abominabilis est, nec in die apparet, sed noctibus cibum quærit ; sic ego nocturno tempore, ceteris quiescentibus, cibum animæ quæro, operibus bonis et luctibus pœnitentiæ insistendo. In die autem dum alii foras vagantur et occupantur, ego domi resideo, nec me dignum arbitror inter homines apparere, propter abominabilem vitam quam duxi. Per nycticoracem ergo significatur secundum genus pœnitentium, eorum videlicet qui humanos adspectus declinant, et domi cum magna contritione ac humilitate animi sedent.
paras.en: [[101:7|I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness|Similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis]]: that is, as the pelican is a solitary bird, loving solitude and worn with a certain natural leanness, so I, that I might bewail my sins more freely, have fled from men, have dwelt in solitude and shunned human comfort, as was said above: [[Ps 54:8|Lo, I have gone far off flying away; and I abode in the wilderness|Ecce elongavi fugiens, et mansi in solitudine]]. By the pelican is signified the first kind of penitents, namely the order of hermits, who in the desert chastise and mortify their flesh and bewail their own sins and those of others. For a solitary place is most fit for doing this. Hence when Jeremias had said, [[Jer 9:1|Who will give water to my head, and a fountain of tears to my eyes? and I will weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people|Quis dabit capiti meo aquam, et oculis meis fontem lacrimarum, et plorabo die ac nocte interfectos populi mei?]]? [Denis has "the slain of my people", without "the daughter of"], hinting that he could not do this so well among the people, he longs for solitude, saying: [[Jer 9:2|Who will give me in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men, and I will leave my people|Quis dabit mihi in solitudine diversorium viatorum, et derelinquam populum meum]]? [[101:7|I am like a night raven in the house|Factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio]]: that is, as the owl or night raven, living in the wall of a house, is hateful and abominable to the other birds, and does not appear by day but seeks its food by night, so I seek the food of the soul in the night-time while others rest, applying myself to good works and to the mourning of penance. But by day, while others wander abroad and are busy, I stay at home, and do not think myself worthy to appear among men, because of the abominable life I have led. By the night raven, then, is signified the second kind of penitents, those namely who shun the sight of men and sit at home in great contrition and humility of mind.

paras.t: Vigilavi : sicut ad Colossenses dicit Apostolus, Orationi instate, vigilantes in ea in gratiarum actione. Vigilavi, id est, a peccato surrexi : juxta illud Apostoli, Tempus est jam nos a somno surgere ; et alibi, Surge qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis. Vigilavi, sanctis operibus inhærendo : secundum quod monet Apostolus, Vigilate, state in fide, viriliter agite, confortamini, et omnia vestra in caritate fiant ; et Christus apud Matthæum, Vigilate et orate, ut non intretis in tentationem. Sic vigilantibus, et non dormientibus, provenit regnum cœlorum. Quapropter Salomon dicit : Noli diligere somnum, ne te egestas opprimat. Vel, Vigilavi, tempore noctis, et illis horis quibus licite dormire poteram, quatenus tempus inutiliter perditum recuperarem, laudibus Creatoris vacando, et corpus sacris vigiliis affligendo. Et ista est magna gratia, dum Deus dat servo suo devoto et studioso, modico contentum reddi somno, quum somnus sit morti similis, et operatori multum odibilis. Unde in Proverbiis Salomon sciscitatur : Usquequo piger dormies? Quando consurges de somno tuo? Verumtamen sicut in abstinentia, sic in vigilia discretionem servare oportet, et proprias vires diligenter metiri, ne efficiatur homo sacrilegii reus, incurratque maledictionem, de qua inquit Jeremias : Quia plus fecit quam potuit, idcirco periit.
paras.en: [[101:8|I have watched|Vigilavi]], as the Apostle says to the Colossians: [[Col 4:2|Be instant in prayer: watching in it with thanksgiving|Orationi instate, vigilantes in ea in gratiarum actione]]. [[101:8|I have watched|Vigilavi]], that is, I have risen from sin, according to the Apostle's words: [[Rom 13:11|it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep|Tempus est jam nos a somno surgere]]; and elsewhere: [[Eph 5:14|Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead|Surge qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis]]. [[101:8|I have watched|Vigilavi]], by holding fast to holy works, as the Apostle admonishes: [[1 Cor 16:13|Watch ye: stand fast in the faith: do manfully and be strengthened.|Vigilate, state in fide, viriliter agite, confortamini]] [[1 Cor 16:14|Let all your things be done in charity|et omnia vestra in caritate fiant]]; and Christ in Matthew: [[Matt 26:41|Watch ye: and pray that ye enter not into temptation|Vigilate et orate, ut non intretis in tentationem]]. Thus to those who watch and do not sleep comes the kingdom of heaven. Wherefore Solomon says: [[Prov 20:13|Love not sleep, lest poverty oppress thee|Noli diligere somnum, ne te egestas opprimat]]. Or: [[101:8|I have watched|Vigilavi]] in the night-time, in the hours in which I might lawfully have slept, so as to recover time uselessly lost, giving myself to the praises of the Creator and afflicting my body with holy vigils. And this is a great grace, when God grants his devout and zealous servant to be made content with a little sleep, since sleep is like death and very hateful to one who would work. Hence in Proverbs Solomon asks: [[Prov 6:9|How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?|Usquequo piger dormies? Quando consurges de somno tuo?]] Yet as in abstinence, so in watching, one must keep discretion and measure one's own strength carefully, lest a man become guilty of sacrilege and incur the curse of which Jeremias says: [[Jer 48:36|because he hath done more than he could, therefore they have perished|Quia plus fecit quam potuit, idcirco periit]] [the margin gives Jer. xlviii, 30; the words are from 48:36].

paras.t: Et factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto : id est, quemadmodum passer in alto ac tuto nidificat, ne vel ipse capiatur, aut pulli ejus vorentur ; sic ego ne a diaboli laqueis irretirer, aut operum bonorum fructibus spoliarer, ad nidum gremiumque Ecclesiæ seu loca monasterii fugi, ut a conventu malignantium separatus, illic conserver atque salvificer. Ecclesia namque signatur per montem de quo angeli dixerunt ad Lot : Noli respicere post tergum, nec stes in omni circa regione, sed in monte salvum te fac. Claustrum vero signatur per civitatem de qua Lot angelo ait : Quæso, Domine mi, est civitas hic juxta, ad quam possum fugere, parva, et salvabor in ea. Per passerem designatur tertium pœnitentium genus, puta eorum qui claustra ingrediuntur.
paras.en: [[101:8|And am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop|Et factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto]]: that is, as the sparrow builds its nest in a high and safe place, lest either it be caught itself or its young be devoured, so I, lest I be entangled in the snares of the devil or robbed of the fruits of good works, have fled to the nest and bosom of the Church, or to the precincts of a monastery, that, separated from the assembly of the malignant, I may be kept and saved there. For the Church is signified by the mountain of which the angels said to Lot: [[Gen 19:17|look not back, neither stay thou in all the country about: but save thy self in the mountain|Noli respicere post tergum, nec stes in omni circa regione, sed in monte salvum te fac]]. And the cloister is signified by the city of which Lot said to the angel: [[Gen 19:18|I beseech thee, my Lord|Quæso, Domine mi]], [[Gen 19:20|There is this city here at hand, to which I may flee, it is a little one, and I shall be saved in it|est civitas hic juxta, ad quam possum fugere, parva, et salvabor in ea]]. By the sparrow is signified the third kind of penitents, namely those who enter cloisters.

paras.t: Deinde pœnitens tribulationes suas commemorat, quatenus Deum ad miserationem inclinet. Tota die, id est quotidie atque assidue, exprobrabant mihi inimici mei, id est amatores hujus mundi, quos ego non odio, sed ipsi me odiunt et mihi insultant : sicut scriptum est, Deridetur justi simplicitas. Et S. Joannes in sua Canonica de quodam superbo testatur : Verbis malignis garriens in nos. Et qui laudabant me in aperto, vel dum eorum conversationi pravæ favebam, adversum me jurabant, id est, nunc postquam eorum vitam abhorreo, atque pœniteo, firmiter statuerunt me persequi verbis aut factis.
paras.en: Next the penitent recounts his tribulations, so as to incline God to mercy. [[101:9|All the day long|Tota die]], that is, daily and continually, [[101:9|my enemies reproached me|exprobrabant mihi inimici mei]], that is, the lovers of this world, whom I do not hate, but they hate me and insult me, as it is written: [[Job 12:4|the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn|Deridetur justi simplicitas]]. And St. John in his Canonical Epistle testifies of a certain proud man: [[3 John 1:10|with malicious words prating against us|Verbis malignis garriens in nos]]. [[101:9|And they that praised me|Et qui laudabant me]] openly, or while I favoured their wicked way of life, [[101:9|did swear against me|adversum me jurabant]], that is, now that I abhor their life and do penance, they have firmly resolved to persecute me by word or deed.

paras.t: Quia cinerem tanquam panem manducabam : id est, ideo ista fecerunt, quoniam ego concupiscentia ventris contempsi, et cibo vili, duro ac modico usus sum ; et poculum meum cum fletu miscebam, id est, potum corporis cum lacrimis sumpsi. Vel, Poculum animæ, scilicet jucunditatem temporalem, cum fletu miscebam, id est, bonæ tristitiæ miscui, ne inaniter gloriando resolverer. Spiritualiter, cinerem sicut panem manducat, qui reliquias cogitationum suarum diligenter examinat, ac peccata minuta quotidie deflet, dicens Deo cum sancto Job : Signasti quasi in sacculo delicta mea ; et, Tu quidem gressus meos dinumerasti.
paras.en: [[101:10|For I did eat ashes like bread|Quia cinerem tanquam panem manducabam]]: that is, they did these things because I despised the cravings of the belly and used food that was poor, hard and scanty; [[101:10|and mingled my drink with weeping|et poculum meum cum fletu miscebam]] [Denis reads *poculum*, "cup", for the Vulgate's *potum*, "drink"], that is, I took the drink of the body with tears. Or: the cup of the soul, namely temporal joy, I [[101:10|mingled|miscebam]] [[101:10|with weeping|cum fletu]], that is, I mixed it with a good sadness, lest I be undone by vain glorying. Spiritually, he eats [[101:10|ashes like bread|cinerem sicut panem]] who carefully examines the remnants of his thoughts and daily bewails his small sins, saying to God with holy Job: [[Job 14:17|Thou hast sealed up my offences as it were in a bag|Signasti quasi in sacculo delicta mea]]; and: [[Job 14:16|Thou indeed hast numbered my steps|Tu quidem gressus meos dinumerasti]].

paras.t: Hæc autem feci, o Domine, A facie iræ indignationis tuæ, id est ex consideratione districti judicii tui, et præ timore justarum pœnarum, quas impiis præparasti. Hoc timore, hacque consideratione, impleta erat anima beatissimi Job, qui ait : Deus solus est, et cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest : idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor. Quia elevans, id est gratia tua adornans, et summæ Trinitatis imagine me consignans, ac omnibus sensibilibus rebus me præferens, allisisti me, id est, cadere me permisisti, et multis miseriis subjacere. Sic Deus allidit nos, ne unquam jactemus nos ipsos, aut de propriis viribus præsumamus: sed dum stamus, timeamus de casu; dum cadimus, resurgere affectemus. Ideo namque Apostolus admonet, Qui stat, videat ne cadat; et iterum, Considerans te ipsum, ne et tu tenteris. Et apud Ecclesiasticum scriptum est: In die bonorum ne immemor sis malorum, et in die malorum ne immemor sis bonorum.
paras.en: And these things I did, O Lord, [[101:11|Because of thy anger and indignation|A facie iræ indignationis tuæ]], that is, from considering thy strict judgment, and for fear of the just punishments which thou hast prepared for the wicked. With this fear and this consideration the soul of most blessed Job was filled, who says: [[Job 23:13|he is alone, and no man can turn away his thought|Deus solus est, et cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest]]: [[Job 23:15|therefore I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him, I am made pensive with fear|idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor]]. [[101:11|For having lifted me up|Quia elevans]], that is, adorning me with thy grace, sealing me with the image of the supreme Trinity, and setting me above all sensible things, [[101:11|thou hast thrown me down|allisisti me]], that is, thou hast let me fall and be subject to many miseries. So God throws us down, that we may never boast of ourselves or presume on our own strength, but that while we stand we may fear a fall, and when we fall we may long to rise again. For this reason the Apostle admonishes: [[1 Cor 10:12|he that thinketh himself to stand, let him take heed lest he fall|Qui stat, videat ne cadat]] [Denis's text is shorter: *Qui stat*, "he that standeth"]; and again: [[Gal 6:1|considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted|Considerans te ipsum, ne et tu tenteris]]. And in Ecclesiasticus it is written: [[Ecclus 11:27|In the day of good things be not unmindful of evils: and in the day of evils be not unmindful of good things|In die bonorum ne immemor sis malorum, et in die malorum ne immemor sis bonorum]].

paras.t: Dies mei sicut umbra, id est velocissime, declinaverunt: quemadmodum in libro primo Paralipomenon habetur: Dies nostri quasi umbra super terram, et nulla est mora. Job quoque ait: Dies mei velocius transierunt, quam a texente tela succiditur. Et ego sicut fœnum, quod hodie est atque virescit, et cras in clibanum mittitur et arescit; arui mente et corpore: mente, ex defectu gratiæ Dei; corpore, propter afflictiones multiplices. Unde apud Isaiam legitur, Vere fœnum est populus; et rursus, Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos fœni.
paras.en: [[101:12|My days|Dies mei]] [[101:12|like a shadow|sicut umbra]], that is, most swiftly, [[101:12|have declined|declinaverunt]], as is said in the first book of Paralipomenon: [[1 Par 29:15|Our days upon earth are as a shadow, and there is no stay|Dies nostri quasi umbra super terram, et nulla est mora]]. Job too says: [[Job 7:6|My days have passed more swiftly than the web is cut by the weaver|Dies mei velocius transierunt, quam a texente tela succiditur]]. [[101:12|And I|Et ego]], [[101:12|like grass|sicut fœnum]], which today is and is green, and tomorrow is cast into the oven and dries up, [[101:12|am withered|arui]] in mind and body: in mind, from want of the grace of God; in body, because of manifold afflictions. Hence we read in Isaias: [[Is 40:7|Indeed the people is grass|Vere fœnum est populus]]; and again: [[Is 40:6|All flesh is grass, and all the glory thereof as the flower of the field|Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos fœni]] [Denis has *flos fœni*, "the flower of the grass", for *flos agri*, "the flower of the field"].

paras.t: Consequenter ponitur efficacia Dei ad liberandum. Tu autem, Domine, in æternum permanes, hoc est, æternaliter invariabiliterque subsistis, quemadmodum in Malachia asseris: Ego Dominus et non mutor. Et memoriale tuum, id est præcipuum opus quod in creatura fecisti, per quod conservatur in nobis memoria nominis tui, permanet in generationem et generationem, id est, præ magnitudine sua non permittit nos sui vel tui oblivisci. Hoc autem memoriale Dei, est miseratio ejus, quam ab exordio mundi hominibus contulit. Unde apud Isaiam inducitur: Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum, Domine, in desiderio animæ. Nunquam enim oblivisci debemus beneficiorum Dei.
paras.en: Next is set forth the power of God to deliver. [[101:13|But thou, O Lord, endurest for ever|Tu autem, Domine, in æternum permanes]], that is, thou dost subsist eternally and unchangeably, as thou declarest in Malachias: [[Mal 3:6|I am the Lord, and I change not|Ego Dominus et non mutor]]. [[101:13|And thy memorial|Et memoriale tuum]], that is, the chief work which thou hast wrought in the creature, by which the memory of thy name is kept in us, endures [[101:13|to all generations|in generationem et generationem]], that is, by its greatness it does not let us forget it or thee. Now this memorial of God is his mercy, which he has bestowed on men from the beginning of the world. Hence in Isaias it is said: [[Is 26:8|thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul|Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum, Domine, in desiderio animæ]]. For we must never forget the benefits of God.

paras.t: Tu, Domine, exsurgens, id est potenter nobis succurrens, et per modum exsurgentis te habens, potentia tua recenter utendo, misereberis Sion, id est Ecclesiæ militanti, te fideliter contemplanti, quia venit tempus miserendi ejus, id est tempus salutis et gratiæ: de quo ait Apostolus, Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis. Hoc tempus incepit præcipue ab incarnatione Christi. Quia venit tempus, id est adventus Christi in mundum: de quo tempore dicit idem Apostolus, Ubi venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum.
paras.en: [[101:14|Thou shalt arise|Tu, Domine, exsurgens]], O Lord, that is, coming mightily to our help, and bearing thyself after the manner of one who rises up, by using thy power anew, [[101:14|and have mercy on Sion|misereberis Sion]], that is, on the Church militant, which faithfully contemplates thee, [[101:14|for it is time to have mercy on it|quia venit tempus miserendi ejus]], that is, the time of salvation and grace, of which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time: behold, now is the day of salvation|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis]]. This time began chiefly from the incarnation of Christ. [[101:14|For the time is come|Quia venit tempus]], that is, the coming of Christ into the world, of which time the same Apostle says: [[Gal 4:4|when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son|Ubi venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum]].

paras.t: Et vere misereberis Sion, Quoniam placuerunt servis tuis lapides ejus, id est angelis tibi semper ministrantibus, lapides ejus, id est ecclesiasticæ personæ, ex quibus tanquam ex vivis lapidibus construitur sancta Ecclesia. Unde in Apocalypsi angelus ait Joanni: Conservus tuus sum et fratrum tuorum. Gaudium quoque est angelis Dei super uno peccatore pœnitentiam agente. Et terræ ejus miserebuntur, id est, angeli pie succurrunt Ecclesiæ, per orbem terrarum diffusæ. Omnes enim sunt administratorii spiritus, preces hominum Domino offerentes, et ejus gratiam reportantes.
paras.en: And truly thou shalt [[101:14|have mercy on Sion|misereberis Sion]], [[101:15|For the stones thereof have pleased thy servants|Quoniam placuerunt servis tuis lapides ejus]], that is, the angels who ever minister to thee; [[101:15|the stones thereof|lapides ejus]], that is, the persons of the Church, of whom, as of living stones, holy Church is built. Hence in the Apocalypse the angel says to John: [[Apoc 19:10|I am thy fellow servant and of thy brethren|Conservus tuus sum et fratrum tuorum]]. There is joy, too, for [[Luke 15:10|the angels of God upon one sinner doing penance|angelis Dei super uno peccatore pœnitentiam agente]]. [[101:15|And they shall have pity on the earth thereof|Et terræ ejus miserebuntur]], that is, the angels lovingly succour the Church spread throughout the world. For they are [[Heb 1:14|all ministering spirits|Omnes enim sunt administratorii spiritus]], offering the prayers of men to the Lord and bringing back his grace.

paras.t: Et timebunt gentes, ab idololatria ad fidem veram conversæ, nomen tuum, Domine, id est te ipsum. Hoc in Christianis ex gentili populo natis, impletum videmus. Quod etiam in Malachia prædictum est: Rex magnus ego sum, dicit Dominus, et nomen meum horribile in gentibus. Et omnes reges terræ, id est aliqui de omni genere regum (ut sit distributio pro generibus singulorum, non pro singulis generum), timebunt gloriam tuam, o Christe, id est majestatem tuam, quam per fidem cognoscent. De omni namque genere regum, sunt quidam ad Christum conversi, eumque cum tremore adoraverunt, quemadmodum Isaias prædixit: Reges videbunt, inquit, et consurgent principes, et adorabunt propter Dominum Deum tuum. Idemque rursus de Christo asserit: Super eum continebunt reges os suum.
paras.en: [[101:16|All the Gentiles shall fear|Et timebunt gentes]], being converted from idolatry to the true faith, [[101:16|thy name, O Lord|nomen tuum, Domine]], that is, thee thyself. This we see fulfilled in the Christians born of the Gentile people. It was foretold also in Malachias: [[Mal 1:14|I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the Gentiles|Rex magnus ego sum, dicit Dominus, et nomen meum horribile in gentibus]]. [[101:16|And all the kings of the earth|Et omnes reges terræ]], that is, some of every kind of king (so that the distribution is for the kinds of individuals, not for the individuals of the kinds [that is, "all" means some of every kind, not every single one]), shall fear [[101:16|thy glory|gloriam tuam]], O Christ, that is, thy majesty, which they will know by faith. For of every kind of king there are some who have been converted to Christ and have adored him with trembling, as Isaias foretold: [[Is 49:7|Kings shall see|Reges videbunt]], he says, [[Is 49:7|and princes shall rise up, and adore for the Lord's sake|et consurgent principes, et adorabunt propter Dominum Deum tuum]] [Denis adds "thy God"]. And again he says of Christ: [[Is 52:15|kings shall shut their mouth at him|Super eum continebunt reges os suum]].

paras.t: Quia ædificabit Dominus Christus Sion, id est Ecclesiam sanctam; et videbitur ipsa Ecclesia in gloria sua, id est in magna excellentia, quoniam Christus confirmavit eam adversus omnes reprobos et perversos. Magnis quoque ac variis gratiis eam decoravit : alii dans sermonem sapientiæ, alii sermonem scientiæ, alii gratiam sanitatum, alii operationem virtutum; ponensque quosdam quidem Apostolos, quosdam autem Evangelistas, quosdam vero doctores, sicut plenius pandit Apostolus. Vel, Videbitur Dominus Christus in gloria sua a filiis Ecclesiæ ipsum per fidem speculantibus, sicut testatur Apostolus : Nos autem revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes. Et Isaias : Regem in decore suo videbunt oculi ejus. In die autem judicii, atque in patria, tam Christus quam Ecclesia electorum, multo clarius videbuntur in gloria sua, quando implebitur illud Apocalypseos : Ecce venit cum nubibus, et videbit eum omnis oculus, et qui eum pupugerunt. Hanc autem Ecclesiam Christus per se ipsum ædificare cœpit, prædicans mundo, congregansque discipulos; deinde per Apostolos, aliosque apostolicos homines, ædificavit eam per totum orbem : prout Zacharias prædixit, Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus, id est Christus, et ædificabit templum Domino.
paras.en: [[101:17|For the Lord hath built up|Quia ædificabit Dominus]] (Christ) [[101:17|Sion|Sion]], that is, holy Church [Denis reads *ædificabit*, "shall build up"]; [[101:17|and he shall be seen|et videbitur]], namely the Church herself, [[101:17|in his glory|in gloria sua]], that is, in great excellence [the Latin *videbitur* can be "he", "she" or "it shall be seen": Denis takes it first of the Church, then of Christ], since Christ has strengthened her against all the reprobate and perverse. He has also adorned her with great and various graces: giving to one the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge[[1 Cor 12:8||]], to another the grace of healings[[1 Cor 12:9||]], to another the working of miracles[[1 Cor 12:10||]]; and setting some as apostles, some as evangelists, some as doctors, as the Apostle sets out more fully[[1 Cor 12:28||]] [the margin gives ibid. 28, that is, 1 Cor. xii, 28; Denis's wording, with the evangelists, is closer to Eph. 4:11]. Or: [[101:17|he shall be seen|Videbitur]], the Lord Christ, [[101:17|in his glory|in gloria sua]] by the children of the Church who behold him by faith, as the Apostle testifies: We, however, [[2 Cor 3:18|beholding the glory of the Lord with open face|revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes]]. And Isaias: [[Is 33:17|His eyes shall see the king in his beauty|Regem in decore suo videbunt oculi ejus]]. But on the day of judgment, and in our heavenly home, both Christ and the Church of the elect will be seen far more clearly in their glory, when that word of the Apocalypse will be fulfilled: [[Apoc 1:7|Behold, he cometh with the clouds, and every eye shall see him: and they also that pierced him|Ecce venit cum nubibus, et videbit eum omnis oculus, et qui eum pupugerunt]]. Now Christ began to build this Church by himself, preaching to the world and gathering disciples; then through the Apostles and other apostolic men he built it throughout the whole world, as Zacharias foretold: [[Zach 6:12|BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME|Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus]], that is, Christ, [[Zach 6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|et ædificabit templum Domino]].

paras.t: Respexit Dominus in orationem humilium, orantium pro Christi adventu et ædificatione Ecclesiæ; et non sprevit precem eorum, sed clementer eam implevit. Exaudivit enim Prophetas et alios Sanctos ista orantes. Quotidie etiam Dominus oculo pietatis in orationem humilium respicit, sicut per Isaiam protestatur : Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos ?
paras.en: [[101:18|He hath had regard to the prayer of the humble|Respexit Dominus in orationem humilium]], who pray for the coming of Christ and the building up of the Church; [[101:18|and he hath not despised their petition|et non sprevit precem eorum]], but has mercifully fulfilled it. For he heard the Prophets and the other Saints when they prayed for these things. Daily, too, the Lord looks with the eye of loving-kindness on the prayer of the humble, as he declares by Isaias: [[Is 66:2|to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit, and that trembleth at my words?|Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos]]

paras.t: Scribantur hæc, quæ dicuntur de Deo ac beneficiis ejus, in generatione altera, id est a posteris usque ad finem sæculi, ne unquam oblivioni tradantur; et populus qui creabitur, id est plebs christiana ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto renata, laudabit Dominum de universis beneficiis suis.
paras.en: [[101:19|Let these things be written|Scribantur hæc]], which are said of God and his benefits, [[101:19|unto another generation|in generatione altera]], that is, by those who come after, until the end of the world, so that they may never be forgotten; [[101:19|and the people that shall be created|et populus qui creabitur]], that is, the Christian people reborn [[John 3:5|of water and the Holy Ghost|ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto]], [[101:19|shall praise the Lord|laudabit Dominum]] for all his benefits.

paras.t: Quia prospexit Dominus de excelso sancto suo, id est, de sancto ac sublimi habitaculo suo clementer genus humanum attendit: Dominus de cælo in terram adspexit oculo pietatis. Sicut enim Deus ubique exsistens, et omnia undique cernens, dicitur specialiter habitare et esse in cælo, quoniam ibi evidentius operatur, clariusque videtur; sic specialiter dicitur de cælo adspicere, non quod inter ipsum et ea quæ respicit, sit distantia aliqua, quum ipse omnia penetret, impleat, circumcludat.
paras.en: [[101:20|Because he hath looked forth from his high sanctuary|Quia prospexit Dominus de excelso sancto suo]], that is, from his holy and lofty dwelling he has mercifully attended to the human race: [[101:20|from heaven the Lord hath looked upon the earth|Dominus de cælo in terram adspexit]] with the eye of loving-kindness. For as God, who exists everywhere and sees all things on every side, is said in a special way to dwell and to be in heaven, because there he works more evidently and is more clearly seen, so he is said in a special way to look from heaven: not that there is any distance between him and the things he looks upon, since he penetrates, fills and encloses all things.

paras.t: Respexit ergo de cælo, Ut audiret gemitus compeditorum, id est, ut gementibus, vinculis vitiorum ligatis, succurreret, ignoscendo eorum sceleribus, sicut in libro Judicum inducitur : Flectebatur Dominus misericordia, et audivit afflictorum gemitus; et liberavit eos de cæde vastantium. Ut solveret, id est, a peccatis absolveret, filios interemptorum, id est homines de parentibus peccatoribus natos (peccatum enim mors animæ est). Omnes autem in primo parente cecidimus. Eramus quoque natura filii iræ : sicque parentes nostri interempti, seu spiritualiter interfecti erant fraude diaboli.
paras.en: He looked from heaven, then, [[101:21|That he might hear the groans of them that are in fetters|Ut audiret gemitus compeditorum]], that is, that he might succour those who groan, bound with the chains of vices, by pardoning their crimes; as is said in the book of Judges: [[Judg 2:18|he was moved to mercy, and heard the groanings of the afflicted, and delivered them from the slaughter of the oppressors|Flectebatur Dominus misericordia, et audivit afflictorum gemitus; et liberavit eos de cæde vastantium]] [the margin gives Judic. xi, 18; the words are from Judg. 2:18]. [[101:21|That he might release|Ut solveret]], that is, absolve from sins, [[101:21|the children of the slain|filios interemptorum]], that is, men born of sinful parents (for sin is the death of the soul). Now we all fell in our first parent. We also [[Eph 2:3|were by nature children of wrath|Eramus quoque natura filii iræ]]: and so our parents were slain, or spiritually killed, by the deceit of the devil.

paras.t: Ideo autem audivit et solvit eos, Ut annuntient in Sion, id est in Ecclesia, nomen Domini, Christum libere prædicando, et fidem catholicam ore ac opere confitendo, et laudem ejus annuntient in Jerusalem, id est in ipsa Ecclesia: quæ dicitur Sion propter speculationem, et Jerusalem propter internæ pacis quietem. Sion quippe interpretatur speculatio; Jerusalem vero, visio pacis. Pax autem interna maxime fuit et est in populo christiano: de quo angeli cecinerunt, In terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis.
paras.en: And he heard and released them for this end, [[101:22|That they may declare|Ut annuntient]] [[101:22|in Sion|in Sion]], that is, in the Church, [[101:22|the name of the Lord|nomen Domini]], by freely preaching Christ and confessing the Catholic faith in word and deed, [[101:22|and his praise|et laudem ejus]] may they declare [[101:22|in Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]], that is, in the Church herself, which is called Sion because of contemplation, and Jerusalem because of the quiet of inward peace. For Sion is interpreted *speculatio* [a watching or looking out, and so contemplation], and Jerusalem *vision of peace*. Now inward peace has been and is above all in the Christian people, of whom the angels sang: [[Luke 2:14|on earth peace to men of good will|In terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis]].

paras.t: Hæc autem annuntiatio fit In conveniendo populos in unum et reges, id est per hoc, quod populi vulgares, et etiam reges ac principes, in unitate fidei congregantur, atque in Christo unum corpus mysticum per caritatem efficiuntur, ut serviant Domino in unitate Ecclesiæ. Ob hanc enim spiritualem electorum congregationem, Christus mori dignatus est, juxta illud : Jesus moriturus erat, etc., ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum.
paras.en: Now this declaring is done [[101:23|when the people assemble together, and kings|In conveniendo populos in unum et reges]], that is, by this: that the common people, and kings and princes as well, are gathered together in the unity of the faith and are made by charity one mystical body in Christ, [[101:23|to serve the Lord|ut serviant Domino]] in the unity of the Church. For it was for the sake of this spiritual gathering of the elect that Christ deigned to die, according to the words: [[John 11:51|Jesus should die|Jesus moriturus erat]], etc., [[John 11:52|to gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed|ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum]].

paras.t: Respondit populus fidelis ei, scilicet Domino suo, in via virtutis suæ, per operationem virtuosam. Quandoque enim respondemus alicui verbo, quandoque opere. Populus autem fidelis Christo respondet bene vivendo, gratias referendo, et ejus imperio obtemperando. De tali namque responso ait sanctus Job Domino: Vocabis me, et ego respondebo tibi. Vocat enim nos Deus per inspirationem internam ad vitam meliorem: et tunc respondemus, quum obedimus. Dum vero negligimus, silemus; sed dum contemnimus, contradicimus. De tali quoque responso ait Jacob: Cras respondebit mihi justitia mea. Et ut populus iste Deo perfecte responderet, oravit: Paucitatem dierum meorum nuntia mihi: id est, da mihi sapienter attendere brevitatem vitæ præsentis, quatenus gaudia temporalia vilipendam, atque ad semper mansuram beatitudinem properem.
paras.en: [[101:24|He answered|Respondit]], that is, the faithful people, [[101:24|him|ei]], namely their Lord, [[101:24|in the way of his strength|in via virtutis suæ]], by virtuous working [*virtus* is both "strength" and "virtue"]. For sometimes we answer someone by a word, sometimes by a deed. And the faithful people answers Christ by living well, by giving thanks, and by obeying his command. Of such an answer holy Job says to the Lord: [[Job 14:15|Thou shalt call me, and I will answer thee|Vocabis me, et ego respondebo tibi]]. For God calls us by inward inspiration to a better life, and then we answer, when we obey. But when we neglect it, we are silent; and when we despise it, we gainsay it. Of such an answer Jacob also says: [[Gen 30:33|my justice shall answer for me tomorrow|Cras respondebit mihi justitia mea]]. And that this people might answer God perfectly, it prayed: [[101:24|Declare unto me the fewness of my days|Paucitatem dierum meorum nuntia mihi]]: that is, grant me to consider wisely the shortness of the present life, so that I may hold temporal joys cheap and hasten to the bliss that will last for ever.

paras.t: Ne revoces me in dimidio dierum meorum: id est, ne me tunc de hac vita egredi jubeas, dum me in dimidio vitæ meæ esse opinor, confidens me diu victurum, ne imparatus decedam; et ne illo tempore moriar, dum vitia magis regnant in me: quod esse solet in dimidio vitæ. In generationem et generationem anni tui, id est, duratio seu æternitas tua per omnem generationem extenditur, nec unquam finitur. Æternitatem nempe creationis annos appellat, quoniam omnem longitudinem temporum seu annorum immutabiliter comprehendit.
paras.en: [[101:25|Call me not away in the midst of my days|Ne revoces me in dimidio dierum meorum]]: that is, do not bid me depart from this life at a time when I think myself in the middle of my life, trusting that I shall live long, lest I die unprepared; nor let me die at that time when vices reign more in me, as is wont to be the case in the middle of life. [[101:25|Thy years are unto generation and generation|In generationem et generationem anni tui]], that is, thy duration or eternity extends through every generation and never ends. For he calls the eternity of the Creator *years* [the print reads *creationis*, "of creation"; *Creatoris*, "of the Creator", seems meant], because it unchangeably comprehends all the length of times or years.

paras.t: Initio temporis et simul cum tempore tu, Domine, terram, id est elementum infimum, fundasti, id est, firmiter in medio universi, tanquam centrum mundi locasti; et opera manuum tuarum, id est creaturæ potestatis tuæ, sunt cœli universi: quemadmodum in Genesi habetur, In principio creavit Deus cœlum et terram; et in Job, Quis ignorat quod manus Domini hæc omnia fecit? Unde per Isaiam Dominus ait: Ego sum Dominus faciens omnia, extendens cœlos solus, stabiliens terram, et nullus mecum. Sed videtur istis contrarium quod in Ecclesiastico habetur: Prior omnium creata est sapientia. Et respondendum, quod sapientia super omnia opera Dei effusa, seu natura angelica, dicitur primo omnium creata, non tempore, sed dignitate.
paras.en: [[101:26|In the beginning|Initio]] of time and together with time, [[101:26|O Lord|tu, Domine]], [[101:26|thou foundedst|fundasti]] [[101:26|the earth|terram]], that is, the lowest element: that is, thou didst set it firmly in the midst of the universe as the centre of the world; and [[101:26|the works of thy hands|opera manuum tuarum]], that is, the creatures of thy power, are [[101:26|the heavens|cœli]], all of them; as is said in Genesis: [[Gen 1:1|In the beginning God created heaven, and earth|In principio creavit Deus cœlum et terram]]; and in Job: [[Job 12:9|Who is ignorant that the hand of the Lord hath made all these things?|Quis ignorat quod manus Domini hæc omnia fecit?]] Hence the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 44:24|I am the Lord, that make all things, that alone stretch out the heavens, that established the earth, and there is none with me|Ego sum Dominus faciens omnia, extendens cœlos solus, stabiliens terram, et nullus mecum]]. But what is said in Ecclesiasticus seems contrary to this: [[Ecclus 1:4|Wisdom hath been created before all things|Prior omnium creata est sapientia]]. And the answer is that wisdom poured out upon all the works of God, that is, the angelic nature, is said to have been created first of all, not in time but in dignity.

paras.t: Ipsi peribunt. Nec cœlum, nec terra peribit substantialiter, sed peribunt in fine mundi, quantum ad esse formæ accidentalis, quoniam alium statum habebunt post judicium, quam modo. Cœlum autem aerium peribit hoc modo per ignem conflagrationis, qui aerem emundabit. Cœli vero supra sphæram ignis existentes, peribunt per cessationem cœlestium motuum. Dum enim generatio et corruptio in inferioribus finiuntur, desinent motus cœlorum. Omnia autem generabilia et corruptibilia et inferiora, ordinantur ad hominem sicut ad finem: idcirco numero electorum completo, cessabit generatio hominum, et per consequens generatio et corruptio ceterorum. Et ita motus et tempus cessabunt in cœlis mobilibus. Quapropter in Apocalypsi scriptum est: Angelus levavit manum ad cœlum, et juravit per Viventem in sæcula sæculorum, quia tempus ultra non erit. Denique, quæcumque ex sua natura habent aliquem ordinem ad semper exsistendum, substantialiter manebunt post diem judicii; cetera corrumpentur. Propterea homines permanebunt, quoniam, licet secundum corpus corruptibiles sint, secundum animam tamen incorruptibiles sunt. Elementa quoque manebunt: nam licet secundum partem corruptibilia sint, tamen secundum se tota corrumpi non possunt. Cœli vero secundum se totos, incorruptibiles sunt, ideo non peribunt, nisi secundum modum essendi, sicut nunc dictum est: et ita intelligenda sunt, quæ in Scripturis sanctis affirmant cœlos corrumpendos, ut est illud, Cœli sicut libri complicabuntur; et quod apud Lucam Dominus ait, Cœlum et terra transibunt; et illud Petri, Cœli qui nunc sunt et terra, igni servati sunt in diem judicii (Petrus tamen de cœlis aeriis loquitur); item illud Apocalypseos, Vidi cœlum novum et terram novam. Primum enim coelum et prima terra abiit, et mare jam non est. Hic autem destruitur opinio philosophorum, qui mundum et generationem atque corruptionem, motus quoque coelestes ac tempus, ab æterno fuisse, et sine fine mansura, ponebant.
paras.en: [[101:27|They shall perish|Ipsi peribunt]]. Neither heaven nor earth will perish in substance; but they will perish at the end of the world as regards the being of their accidental form, since after the judgment they will have another state than now. The aerial heaven will perish in this way through the fire of the conflagration, which will cleanse the air; while the heavens that are above the sphere of fire will perish through the ceasing of the heavenly motions. For when generation and corruption come to an end in the lower things, the motions of the heavens will cease. Now all things that can be generated and corrupted, and all the lower things, are ordered to man as to their end: therefore, when the number of the elect is complete, the generation of men will cease, and in consequence the generation and corruption of the rest. And so motion and time will cease in the movable heavens. Wherefore it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 10:5|The angel|Angelus]] [[Apoc 10:5|lifted up his hand to heaven|levavit manum ad cœlum]], [[Apoc 10:6|and he swore by him that liveth for ever and ever|et juravit per Viventem in sæcula sæculorum]]: [[Apoc 10:6|That time shall be no longer|quia tempus ultra non erit]]. Lastly, whatever things have by their nature some order to existing for ever will remain in substance after the day of judgment; the rest will be corrupted. Hence men will remain, since, although they are corruptible according to the body, yet according to the soul they are incorruptible. The elements also will remain: for although they are corruptible in their parts, yet as wholes they cannot be corrupted. And the heavens, as wholes, are incorruptible; therefore they will not perish except as to their mode of being, as has just been said. And so are to be understood the passages of holy Scripture that affirm the heavens will be corrupted, such as this: [[Is 34:4|the heavens shall be folded together as a book|Cœli sicut libri complicabuntur]]; and what the Lord says in Luke: [[Luke 21:33|Heaven and earth shall pass away|Cœlum et terra transibunt]]; and that of Peter: [[2 Pet 3:7|the heavens and the earth which are now|Cœli qui nunc sunt et terra]], [[2 Pet 3:7|reserved unto fire against the day of judgment|igni servati sunt in diem judicii]] (though Peter is speaking of the aerial heavens); and again that of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:1|I saw a new heaven and a new earth. For the first heaven and the first earth was gone: and the sea is now no more.|Vidi cœlum novum et terram novam. Primum enim coelum et prima terra abiit, et mare jam non est.]] Here is overthrown the opinion of the philosophers who held that the world, and generation and corruption, and also the heavenly motions and time, had been from eternity and would remain without end.

paras.t: Tu autem, o Domine, invariabiliter permanes: quoniam tuum esse, a nullo dependet, ideo vere æternum est, totum simul et semper æque perfectum, in quo nulla vicissitudo concipi potest; et omnes coeli sicut vestimentum veterascent a statu volubili, quem jam sortiuntur. Et sicut opertorium, quod secundum temporis exigentiam induitur et exuitur sive deponitur, mutabis eos a statu præsenti, et mutabuntur in melius: quia lux solis erit septempliciter, et lux lunæ sicut lux solis, ut dicit Isaias. Orbes quoque cœlestes clariori lumine vestientur, quamvis Scriptura quantitatem hujus immutationis non determinet. Tu autem idem ipse es, qui nec substantialiter nec accidentaliter variaris, sed æternaliter in optimo simpliciterque perfecto statu subsistis; et anni tui non deficient, id est, æternitas tua finiri non poterit.
paras.en: [[101:27|But thou|Tu autem]], O Lord, unchangeably [[101:27|remainest|permanes]]: since thy being depends on nothing, it is therefore truly eternal, whole at once and always equally perfect, and in it no change can be conceived; [[101:27|and all of them|et omnes]], the heavens, [[101:27|shall grow old like a garment|sicut vestimentum veterascent]], from the revolving state which they now have. [[101:27|And as a vesture|Et sicut opertorium]], which is put on and taken off or laid aside as the season requires, [[101:27|thou shalt change them|mutabis eos]] from their present state, [[101:27|and they shall be changed|et mutabuntur]] for the better: for [[Is 30:26|the light of the sun shall be sevenfold|lux solis erit septempliciter]], and [[Is 30:26|the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun|lux lunæ sicut lux solis]], as Isaias says. The heavenly spheres too will be clothed with a brighter light, though Scripture does not determine the measure of this change. [[101:28|But thou art always the selfsame|Tu autem idem ipse es]], who dost not vary either in substance or in accident, but subsistest eternally in the best and simply perfect state; [[101:28|and thy years shall not fail|et anni tui non deficient]], that is, thy eternity can never be ended.

paras.t: Filii servorum tuorum, id est posteri Apostolorum, qui sunt spirituales filii ac imitatores ipsorum, juxta illud Apostoli: Filioli, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis; habitabunt, nunc in Ecclesia militante per fidem et gratiam, usque ad sæculi consummationem; postmodum vero in Ecclesia triumphanti per gloriam, usque in sempiternum; et semen eorum, id est bona et fructuosa conversatio ipsorum, in sæculum, id est indesinenter, dirigetur ab ipsis per gratiam tuam, usque in ultimum finem seu vitam æternam; vel, Dirigetur a te, donec perducantur ad patriam.
paras.en: [[101:29|The children of thy servants|Filii servorum tuorum]], that is, the successors of the Apostles, who are their spiritual children and imitators, according to the Apostle's words: [[Gal 4:19|My little children, of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you|Filioli, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis]]; [[101:29|shall continue|habitabunt]] [*habitabunt*, literally "shall dwell"], now in the Church militant by faith and grace until the consummation of the world, and afterwards in the Church triumphant by glory for ever; [[101:29|and their seed|et semen eorum]], that is, their good and fruitful manner of life, [[101:29|for ever|in sæculum]], that is, without ceasing, [[101:29|shall be directed|dirigetur]] by them through thy grace, unto the last end, that is, life everlasting; or, [[101:29|shall be directed|Dirigetur]] by thee until they are brought to the heavenly home.

paras.t: Ecce audivimus vocem veraciter pœnitentis, formamque perfectæ pœnitentiæ. Discamus ergo ex psalmo præsenti, quid ad vere pœnitentem pertineat. Studeamus quoque ea digne implere. Primi etenim versus psalmi istius declarant, quam ardenter et seriose clamare oporteat pœnitentem ad Deum. Deinde docemur nostræ paupertatis ac defectuositatis calamitatem atque miseriam coram Domino lugubriter recitare. Deinceps instruimur, quid nos pœnitendo oporteat vel expediat agere, utpote tam cordialiter, profunde ac dolorose ingemiscere, ut ossa cuti ex maceratione carnis adhæreant. Debemus etiam assimilari pelecano, loca solitaria ingrediendo, in quibus libere nos ipsos in pœnitentiæ luctu mactemus. Debemus et cibo vili contenti esse, potumque planctui commiscere, atque iram Judicis nostri incessabiliter formidare. Postremo docet nos psalmus hic gloriosus, recitationi ac deplorationi nostræ paupertatis, parvitatis ac culpæ miscere divina præconia. Creatoris nostri majestatem laudando, beatitudinem admirando, bonitatem amando, misericordiam ac benevolentiam imitando, ut simus filii Patris nostri qui in cœlis est, quoniam ipse benignus et bonus est, super gratos et ingratos, bonos ac malos, solem suum faciens oriri, pluviamque descendere super omnes.
paras.en: See, we have heard the voice of one who truly repents, and the form of perfect penance. Let us learn, then, from the present psalm what belongs to one who is truly penitent, and let us strive to fulfil it worthily. For the first verses of this psalm declare how ardently and earnestly the penitent must cry to God. Next we are taught to recount mournfully before the Lord the calamity and misery of our poverty and failings. Then we are instructed what we must or should do in doing penance: namely, to groan so heartily, deeply and sorrowfully that our bones cleave to our skin through the wasting of the flesh. We must also be like the pelican, entering solitary places, in which we may freely immolate ourselves in the mourning of penance. We must also be content with poor food, mingle our drink with lamentation, and fear the anger of our Judge without ceasing. Lastly, this glorious psalm teaches us to mingle the praises of God with the recounting and bewailing of our poverty, littleness and guilt: praising the majesty of our Creator, wondering at his blessedness, loving his goodness, imitating his mercy and kindness, that we may be children of our Father who is in heaven, since he is kind and good to the grateful and the ungrateful[[Luke 6:35||]], making his sun to rise on the good and the bad, and the rain to come down upon all[[Matt 5:45||]].

101.title: EXPLANATIO ALLEGORICA EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI PRIMI DE CHRISTO.
101.title_en: Allegorical explanation of the same hundred and first psalm, concerning Christ.

paras.t: Quamvis autem aliquibus visum sit, hunc psalmum non posse convenienter exponi de Christo, præsertim quum sit unus pœnitentialium psalmorum, peccatori conveniens (Christo autem nec pœnitentia competit nec culpa); nihilo minus de Christo multum convenienter exponitur. Primo, quia Apostolus ad Hebræos inducit verba psalmi hujus ab illo loco, Initio tu, Domine, terram fundasti, usque ibi, Et anni tui non deficient, de Christo prædicta, probans ex eis, Filium esse Patri æqualem in potentia et dominatione. Probatio autem, secundum Augustinum, non valet nisi ex sensu litterali. Psalmus igitur iste ad litteram tractat de Domino Salvatore. Secundo, quia Ecclesia in officio Missæ, feria quarta ante Cœnam, assumpsit Tractum de principio hujus psalmi. Unde relinquitur, quod psalmus iste exponi possit de Christo in passione constituto. Totum enim Officium illius diei, imo totius hebdomadæ ante Pascha, est de passione dominica. Tertio, quia secundum Augustinum non est inconveniens, etiam eamdem Scripturam multiplicem sensum habere ad litteram, ita quod sensus litteralis ejusdem Scripturæ multiplex esse possit. Quamvis igitur quædam in hoc psalmo contenta, proprie exponantur de pœnitente; non tamen inconveniens est, ipsa de Christo intelligi secundum alium intellectum.
paras.en: Now although it has seemed to some that this psalm cannot fittingly be expounded of Christ, especially since it is one of the penitential psalms and suited to a sinner (whereas neither penance nor guilt belongs to Christ), it is nonetheless expounded of Christ very fittingly. First, because the Apostle, in the Epistle to the Hebrews, brings in the words of this psalm as foretold of Christ[[Heb 1:10||]][[Heb 1:12||]], from the place [[101:26|In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth|Initio tu, Domine, terram fundasti]] as far as [[101:28|and thy years shall not fail|Et anni tui non deficient]], proving from them that the Son is equal to the Father in power and dominion. But a proof, according to Augustine, holds only from the literal sense. This psalm, therefore, treats literally of the Lord our Saviour. Secondly, because the Church, in the office of the Mass on the fourth feria before the Supper [that is, the Wednesday of Holy Week, the day before Maundy Thursday], has taken its Tract from the beginning of this psalm. Hence it follows that this psalm can be expounded of Christ set in his passion; for the whole Office of that day, indeed of the whole week before Easter, is about the Lord's passion. Thirdly, because, according to Augustine, it is not unfitting that even the same Scripture should have a manifold sense according to the letter, so that the literal sense of the same Scripture can be manifold. Although, then, certain things contained in this psalm are properly expounded of a penitent, it is nevertheless not unfitting that they be understood of Christ in another sense.

paras.t: Elucidando itaque psalmum istum de Christo, præhabitus titulus ita exponitur: Oratio pauperis: id est, psalmus præsens competit Christo propter nos pauperi, qui non habuit ubi caput reclinaret: de quo in Zacharia habetur, Ecce rex tuus venit tibi, ipse pauper et ascendens super asinam; quum anxius fuerit, etc., id est, dum ipse Christus passione jam imminente expavit atque tristatus est, juxta illud Marci: Cœpit Jesus pavere et tædere; et coram Domino Deo Patre effudit precem suam, dicendo: Pater, si fieri potest, transeat a me calix iste.
paras.en: So, in explaining this psalm of Christ, the title given before is expounded thus: [[101:1|The prayer of the poor man|Oratio pauperis]]: that is, the present psalm belongs to Christ, poor for our sake, who [[Matt 8:20|hath not where to lay his head|non habuit ubi caput reclinaret]]; of whom it is said in Zacharias: [[Zach 9:9|BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee|Ecce rex tuus venit tibi]], [[Zach 9:9|he is poor, and riding upon an ass|ipse pauper et ascendens super asinam]]. Then: [[101:1|when he was anxious|quum anxius fuerit]], etc.: that is, when Christ himself, with his passion now at hand, was struck with fear and was sorrowful, according to that of Mark: [[Mark 14:33|he began to fear and to be heavy|Cœpit Jesus pavere et tædere]]; and poured out his prayer before the Lord God the Father, saying: [[Matt 26:39|My Father, if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me|Pater, si fieri potest, transeat a me calix iste]].

paras.t: Christus ergo ut homo passibilis, passioni jam proximus, ait ad Deum Patrem seu totam superbeatissimam Trinitatem, unum verum et simplicissimum Deum: Domine, exaudi orationem meam, qua oro pro corporis mei glorificatione ac celeri resurrectione, dicens illud: Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora; et clamor meus, quo oro pro corpore meo mystico, quod est Ecclesia, ad te veniat, ut facias quod peto apud Joannem: Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo, quos dedisti mihi, ut sint unum sicut et nos.
paras.en: Christ, then, as a man capable of suffering and now close to his passion, says to God the Father, or to the whole most supremely blessed Trinity, the one true and most simple God: [[101:2|Hear, O Lord, my prayer|Domine, exaudi orationem meam]], by which I pray for the glorifying of my body and its swift resurrection, saying that word: [[John 12:27|Father, save me from this hour|Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora]]; [[101:2|and let my cry|et clamor meus]], by which I pray for my mystical body, which is the Church, [[101:2|come to thee|ad te veniat]], so that thou mayest do what I ask in John: [[John 17:11|Holy Father, keep them in thy name whom thou hast given me: that they may be one, as we also are|Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo, quos dedisti mihi, ut sint unum sicut et nos]].

paras.t: Non avertas faciem tuam a me, id est, non habeas te circa me pro aliis exorantem per modum indignantis, ita ut precem meam pro aliis fusam, repellas propter aliorum indignitatem; sed propter me illis ignosce. Christus, qui erat a principio suæ maternæ conceptionis comprehensor perfectus, et in bono immobiliter confirmatus, non oravit ne Pater faciem suam, id est suam cognitionem beatificam, seu piam præsentiam ab ipso averteret (hoc enim scivit nunquam fieri posse); sed oravit ne Pater propter facinora hominum, exauditionem suam averteret a prece Christi pro peccatoribus fusa. In quacumque die tribulor, id est, a Judæis persecutionem sustineo, inclina ad me aurem tuam, ut mihi adsistas, et passionem quam tolero, pro satisfactione vitiorum mundi suscipias. Hoc Christus exoravit: Pater, pro his rogo quos dedisti mihi de mundo, quia tui sunt.
paras.en: [[101:3|Turn not away thy face from me|Non avertas faciem tuam a me]]: that is, do not bear thyself towards me, as I plead for others, in the manner of one who is indignant, so as to thrust back the prayer I pour out for others because of their unworthiness; but for my sake forgive them. Christ, who from the beginning of his conception in his mother was a perfect comprehensor [that is, one already enjoying the vision of God, as the blessed do, not a wayfarer still on the way to it] and immovably confirmed in good, did not pray that the Father should not turn away from him his face, that is, his beatific knowledge or his loving presence (for he knew that this could never happen); but he prayed that the Father should not, because of the crimes of men, turn away his hearing from the prayer that Christ poured out for sinners. [[101:3|in the day when I am in trouble|In quacumque die tribulor]], that is, suffer persecution from the Jews, [[101:3|incline thy ear to me|inclina ad me aurem tuam]], to stand by me, and to accept the passion I endure as satisfaction for the sins of the world. This Christ asked in prayer: Father, I pray [[John 17:9|for them whom thou hast given me: because they are thine|pro his rogo quos dedisti mihi de mundo, quia tui sunt]] [Denis's wording adds "out of the world", from John 17:6].

paras.t: Quia defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei, id est, velociter defluxerunt dies, quibus in mundo conversatus sum. Nam Christus senuit seu antiquior fiebat, id est, ad senium tendebat, sicut et ceteri, diesque ejus in continuo fluxu erant, quemadmodum tempus. Indetrahibiles quippe defectus assumpsit, secundum Damascenum. Propter quod ad Hebræos Apostolus dicit: Debuit per omnia fratribus assimilari. Et ossa mea corporalia, sicut cremium, id est caro cremata, aruerunt in passione: sicut superius dictum est, Aruit tanquam testa virtus mea. Nam in die Parasceves, propter extractionem largissimam sanguinis Christi, et carnis suæ extenuationem, desiccationem et indurationem, ossa sacratissimi corporis sui aruerunt, instar carnis in frixorio usque ad pinguedinis eductionem combustæ. Propter quod de Christo ab Isaia prædictum est: Vidimus eum, et non erat aspectus; et nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum et a Deo percussum.
paras.en: [[101:4|For my days are vanished like smoke|Quia defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei]]: that is, the days in which I lived in the world have swiftly flowed away. For Christ grew old, or became older, that is, he was tending towards old age like other men, and his days were in continual flux, as time is. For he took on the undetractable defects [that is, the natural and blameless weaknesses of human nature, such as hunger, thirst and weariness, which carry no reproach], according to Damascene; wherefore the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:17|it behoved him in all things to be made like unto his brethren|Debuit per omnia fratribus assimilari]]. [[101:4|and my bones|Et ossa mea]], the bones of my body, [[101:4|like fuel for the fire|sicut cremium]], that is, like burnt flesh [the Latin *cremium* is matter for burning; Denis takes it as flesh burnt or fried], [[101:4|are grown dry|aruerunt]] in the passion; as was said above: [[Ps 21:16|My strength is dried up like a potsherd|Aruit tanquam testa virtus mea]]. For on the day of the Parasceve [that is, Good Friday], through the most abundant drawing out of Christ's blood, and the wasting, drying and hardening of his flesh, the bones of his most sacred body grew dry, like flesh burnt in a frying pan until the fat is drawn out. Wherefore it was foretold of Christ by Isaias: [[Is 53:2|we have seen him, and there was no sightliness|Vidimus eum, et non erat aspectus]]; [[Is 53:4|and we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God|et nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum et a Deo percussum]].

paras.t: Unde nunc subditur: Percussus sum ut fœnum: id est, quemadmodum fœnum dum adhuc floret, falce a terra abscinditur; sic ego in juventute mea gladio passionis a societate viventium ablatus sum et occisus: quemadmodum in Jeremia impii aiunt, Eradamus eum de terra viventium; in libro quoque Sapientiæ, Morte turpissima condemnemus eum. Et aruit cor meum corporale, a suo naturali humore, propter totius corporis vehementissimam vulnerationem et sanguinis emanationem. Non autem aruit cor, id est mens Christi, ab humore seu plenitudine gratiæ Dei.
paras.en: Hence it is now added: [[101:5|I am smitten as grass|Percussus sum ut fœnum]]: that is, as grass, while it is still in flower, is cut from the earth by the scythe, so I in my youth was taken away from the company of the living by the sword of the passion, and slain; as the wicked say in Jeremias: Let us [[Jer 11:19|cut him off from the land of the living|Eradamus eum de terra viventium]]; and in the book of Wisdom also: [[Wis 2:20|Let us condemn him to a most shameful death|Morte turpissima condemnemus eum]]. [[101:5|and my heart is withered|Et aruit cor meum]], my bodily heart, of its natural moisture, through the most violent wounding of the whole body and the flowing out of its blood. But the heart, that is, the mind of Christ, did not wither, of the moisture or fulness of the grace of God.

paras.t: Quia oblitus sum comedere panem meum. Hoc videtur Christo non posse competere, et tamen verissime competit ei. Panis enim animæ, est consolatio ejus. In passione vero Christi appetitus sensitivus, atque inferior portio animæ ejus, privata est solita redundantia consolationis divinæ in ipsam, in tantum ut exclamaret: Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me? Et ita oblitus est Christus, id est, per effectum recordatus non est, comedere panem consolationis, quantum ad inferiores animæ suæ potentias. Oblivio autem non semper ignaviam seu negligentiam signat: quia superius dictum est, Obliviscere populum tuum; et in Genesi Joseph fatetur, Oblivisci me fecit Dominus omnium laborum et domus patris mei. Unde interdum dicitur homo oblivisci, quia non operatur, et ita se habet tanquam nesciret: et ita accipitur nunc. Quoniam itaque Christus inferioribus viribus animæ suæ ac corporali naturæ, redundantiam beatitudinis animæ in sua superiori parte existentis, seu consolationem subtraxit; idcirco pati morique potuit. Alias nec pati nec mori potuisset: quia secundum Augustinum in epistola ad Dioscorum, tanta exstitit beatitudo animæ Christi, quod si ipsa redundasset in corpus ipsius, ab omni passibilitate fuisset immune, multo utique magis quam erunt corpora electorum post diem judicii. Sed dispensative suspendebatur redundantia illa, præcipue hora passionis. Idcirco tunc percussus est Christus ut fœnum, et aruit cor ejus.
paras.en: [[101:5|because I forgot to eat my bread|Quia oblitus sum comedere panem meum]]. This seems unable to apply to Christ, and yet it applies to him most truly. For the bread of the soul is its consolation. Now in Christ's passion the sensitive appetite and the lower part of his soul were deprived of the overflow of divine consolation that was usual in them, so much that he cried out: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?]] And so Christ forgot, that is, did not in effect remember, to eat the bread of consolation, as regards the lower powers of his soul. Forgetting does not always signify sloth or neglect; for it was said above: [[Ps 44:11|forget thy people|Obliviscere populum tuum]]; and in Genesis Joseph declares: [[Gen 41:51|God hath made me to forget all my labours, and my father's house|Oblivisci me fecit Dominus omnium laborum et domus patris mei]]. Hence a man is sometimes said to forget because he does not act, and so behaves as though he did not know; and so it is taken here. Since, then, Christ withheld from the lower powers of his soul and from his bodily nature the overflow, or consolation, of the beatitude of his soul that was in its higher part, he was therefore able to suffer and to die. Otherwise he could neither have suffered nor died: for, according to Augustine in the letter to Dioscorus, so great was the beatitude of Christ's soul that, had it overflowed into his body, the body would have been immune from all capacity for suffering, far more indeed than the bodies of the elect will be after the day of judgment. But that overflow was held back by dispensation [that is, by a deliberate ordering of God's providence for our salvation], above all in the hour of the passion. Therefore Christ was then smitten as grass, and his heart was withered.

paras.t: A voce gemitus mei, id est ex magna et gemituosa cordis mei compassione atque dolore, quibus peccatoribus compatiebar, et de propria læsione dolebam, adhæsit os meum carni meæ, id est cuti, quia ex illis pœnis macerata atque exhausta est caro mea tempore passionis: sicque ossa cuti hærebant, in tantum ut dinumerari valuerint. Juxta quod dictum est: Dispersa sunt omnia ossa mea.
paras.en: [[101:6|Through the voice of my groaning|A voce gemitus mei]]: that is, out of the great and groaning compassion and sorrow of my heart, with which I suffered with sinners and grieved over my own hurt, [[101:6|my bone hath cleaved to my flesh|adhæsit os meum carni meæ]], that is, to my skin; because by those pains my flesh was wasted and drained in the time of the passion, and so the bones clung to the skin, so much that they could be numbered. According to what was said: [[Ps 21:15|all my bones are scattered|Dispersa sunt omnia ossa mea]].

paras.t: Et similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis, quia ad loca deserta progressus sum, devitans Judæorum tumultum: quemadmodum apud Joannem dicitur, Jesus jam non in palam ambulabat apud Judæos, sed abiit in regionem juxta desertum. Ductus est quoque a spiritu in desertum, ut tentaretur a diabolo; illicque quadraginta diebus ac noctibus jejunavit, non pro suo, sed pro nostro excessu. Porro, secundum Augustinum, Christus comparatur pelicano, quoniam avis hæc proprio rostro pullos suos fertur occidere, triduoque lugere, et tandem sanguinem suum super pullos rostro effundere, unde illi reviviscunt. Sic Christus occidit in nobis vitia nostra, et sanguine proprio vivificavit nos denuo. Factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio, quoniam tempore noctis in oratione et bonis actibus vigilavi, dum alii somno vacabant. Hinc in Luca habetur: Erat Jesus pernoctans in oratione Dei. Dicitur etiam Christus similis nycticoraci, quoniam sicut avis illa ceteris est odibilis, sic Christus ab omnibus erat despectus, prout superius dixit: Ego autem sum vermis et non homo, opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis. Propter quod Isaias de ipso dicit: Inglorius erit inter viros adspectus ejus.
paras.en: And [[101:7|I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness|similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis]], because I went forth into desert places, avoiding the tumult of the Jews; as it is said in John: [[John 11:54|Jesus walked no more openly among the Jews: but he went into a country near the desert|Jesus jam non in palam ambulabat apud Judæos, sed abiit in regionem juxta desertum]]. He [[Matt 4:1|was led by the spirit into the desert, to be tempted by the devil|Ductus est quoque a spiritu in desertum, ut tentaretur a diabolo]]; and there he fasted forty days and nights[[Matt 4:2||]], not for his own excess but for ours. Further, according to Augustine, Christ is compared to the pelican because this bird is said to kill its young with its own beak, to mourn them for three days, and at last to pour out its own blood over the young with its beak, whereby they come back to life. So Christ slew our vices in us, and with his own blood quickened us anew. [[101:7|I am like a night raven in the house|Factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio]], because in the time of night I kept watch in prayer and good works while others gave themselves to sleep. Hence it is said in Luke: [[Luke 6:12|he passed the whole night in the prayer of God|Erat Jesus pernoctans in oratione Dei]]. Christ is also said to be like the night raven because, as that bird is hateful to the others, so Christ was despised by all, as he said above: [[Ps 21:7|But I am a worm, and no man: the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people|Ego autem sum vermis et non homo, opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis]]. Wherefore Isaias says of him: [[Is 52:14|his visage be inglorious among men|Inglorius erit inter viros adspectus ejus]] [the margin gives Is. liii, 14; the words are Is 52:14].

paras.t: Vigilavi semper in opere bono. Non enim somnus corporis impedivit in Christo operationem interiorem atque vigiliam mentis. Et factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto, quoniam homines dereliqui, et montem ad orandum ascendi: juxta illud, Exiit Jesus in montem orare.
paras.en: [[101:8|I have watched|Vigilavi]] always in good work. For the sleep of the body did not hinder in Christ the inward working and wakefulness of the mind. [[101:8|and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop|Et factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto]], because I left men behind and went up a mountain to pray; according to that word: Jesus [[Luke 6:12|went out into a mountain to pray|Exiit Jesus in montem orare]].

paras.t: Tota die passionis meæ et multis diebus prædicationis meæ, exprobrabant mihi inimici mei Judæi, dicentes illud Matthæi, In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia; et item illud Joannis, Dæmonium habet et insanit, quid eum auditis? Et qui laudabant me, quando eis prædicavi et coram ipsis miracula feci, eosque de quinque panibus saturavi, dicentes, Quia Propheta magnus surrexit in nobis; et, Quia nunquam apparuit sic in Israel; adversum me jurabant, id est, in mortem meam unanimiter conjurabant, in die Parasceves proclamantes, Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum; et, Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros.
paras.en: [[101:9|All the day long|Tota die]] of my passion, and on the many days of my preaching, [[101:9|my enemies reproached me|exprobrabant mihi inimici mei]], the Jews, saying that word of Matthew: He casts out devils [[Matt 12:24|by Beelzebub the prince of the devils|In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum]]; and again that of John: [[John 10:20|He hath a devil and is mad. Why hear you him?|Dæmonium habet et insanit, quid eum auditis?]] [[101:9|and they that praised me|Et qui laudabant me]] when I preached to them and worked miracles before them, and filled them with five loaves[[Matt 14:19||]], saying: [[Luke 7:16|A great prophet is risen up among us|Quia Propheta magnus surrexit in nobis]]; and: [[Matt 9:33|Never was the like seen in Israel|Quia nunquam apparuit sic in Israel]]; [[101:9|did swear against me|adversum me jurabant]], that is, conspired with one accord to bring about my death, crying out on the day of the Parasceve: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]; and: [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]].

paras.t: Vel: Qui laudabant me, ab extra fallaciter, scilicet Pharisæi et Scribæ, dicentes: Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo; adversum me jurabant, occulte proponentes firmissime me occidere. Unde ait Scriptura: Sagitta vulnerans lingua eorum, dolum locuta est. In ore suo pacem cum amico suo loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias.
paras.en: Or: [[101:9|they that praised me|Qui laudabant me]] outwardly and deceitfully, namely the Pharisees and Scribes, saying: [[Matt 22:16|Master, we know that thou art a true speaker and teachest the way of God in truth. Neither carest thou for any man|Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo]], [[101:9|did swear against me|adversum me jurabant]], secretly and most firmly purposing to kill me. Hence Scripture says: [[Jer 9:8|Their tongue is a piercing arrow, it hath spoken deceit: with his mouth one speaketh peace with his friend, and secretly he lieth in wait for him|Sagitta vulnerans lingua eorum, dolum locuta est. In ore suo pacem cum amico suo loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias]].

paras.t: Quia cinerem tanquam panem manducabam. Hoc Christo secundum duplicem convenit sensum. Quia enim cœpit facere et docere, constat quod sicut parcitatem vilitatemque cibi ac potus edocuit, sic eam implevit, et ita cinere, id est non delicato seu exquisito sed simplici cibo, usus est. Et poculum meum corporalem cum fletu oculorum seu cordis miscebam.
