Quando enim Christus cum publicanis et peccatoribus comedebat, dubium non est quin eis toto corde condoluit; et in resuscitatione Lazari, infremuit spiritu, et lacrimatus est. — Spiritualiter vero per cinerem designatur magna humiliatio sive afflictio: et ita Christus cinerem tanquam panem manducavit, id est, in afflictione, derisione, et humiliatione sui, epulabatur mente in adversis lætando, quemadmodum docuit: Exsultate (inquiens) in illa hora, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlo. Se ipsum namque sponte atque hilariter passioni exposuit, sicut ait: Corpus meum dedi percutientibus, et genas meas vellentibus. Et potum meum, id est hilaritatem quam habui de electorum salute, cum fletu miscebam, id est cum tristitia, quam de reproborum damnatione habebam. — Specialiter autem exponi potest hic versus de fellea cibatione, ac acetosa potatione Christi in cruce.
paras.en: [[101:10|For I did eat ashes like bread|Quia cinerem tanquam panem manducabam]]. This fits Christ in a twofold sense. For since he [[Acts 1:1|began to do and to teach|cœpit facere et docere]], it is plain that as he taught sparingness and plainness of food and drink, so he fulfilled it; and so he used ashes, that is, food that was not dainty or choice but simple. [[101:10|and mingled my drink|Et poculum meum]], my bodily cup, [[101:10|with weeping|cum fletu]] of the eyes or of the heart. For when Christ ate with publicans and sinners, there is no doubt that he grieved for them with his whole heart; and at the raising of Lazarus he [[John 11:33|groaned in the spirit|infremuit spiritu]], and [[John 11:35|wept|lacrimatus est]]. — Spiritually, however, ashes signify great humiliation or affliction; and so Christ ate ashes like bread, that is, in his affliction, mockery and humiliation he feasted in mind, rejoicing in adversity, as he taught: [[Matt 5:12|rejoice|Exsultate]] (he says) in that hour, [[Matt 5:12|for your reward is very great in heaven|quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlo]] ["in that hour" is closer to Luke 6:23, "in that day"]. For he exposed himself to the passion willingly and gladly, as he says: [[Is 50:6|I have given my body to the strikers, and my cheeks to them that plucked them|Corpus meum dedi percutientibus, et genas meas vellentibus]]. [[101:10|and mingled my drink|Et potum meum]], that is, the gladness I had over the salvation of the elect, [[101:10|with weeping|cum fletu miscebam]], that is, with the sadness I had over the damnation of the reprobate. — In a special way, however, this verse can be expounded of the feeding of Christ with gall[[Matt 27:34||]] and his drinking of vinegar on the cross[[John 19:30||]].

paras.t: Hæc vero feci ac pertuli a facie iræ indignationis tuæ, id est propter iram tuam mitigandam seu pœnam tollendam, qua irascebaris generi humano propter originale aliaque peccata, quæ super me posuisti, et pro quibus tibi satisfacere volui: prout Isaias dicit, Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum; et ut in Apocalypsi de Christo habetur: Vestitus erat veste aspersa sanguine, et vocabatur nomen ejus, Verbum Dei. Et ipse calcat torcular vini furoris iræ Dei omnipotentis. Hæc autem sustinui, quia tu, o Deus Pater, elevans, id est me omni creaturæ præficiens, allisisti me in mortem, id est, me occidi et opprimi permisisti, quemadmodum apud Isaiam protestaris: Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum.
paras.en: These things I did and bore [[101:11|Because of thy anger and indignation|a facie iræ indignationis tuæ]]: that is, in order to appease thy anger, or take away the punishment, with which thou wast angry with mankind because of original and other sins, which thou hast laid upon me, and for which I willed to make satisfaction to thee; as Isaias says: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]; and as it is said of Christ in the Apocalypse: He was [[Apoc 19:13|clothed with a garment sprinkled with blood. And his name is called: THE WORD OF GOD|Vestitus erat veste aspersa sanguine, et vocabatur nomen ejus, Verbum Dei]]. And [[Apoc 19:15|he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness of the wrath of God the Almighty|ipse calcat torcular vini furoris iræ Dei omnipotentis]][[Is 63:3||]][[Lam 1:15||]]. These things I endured, for thou, O God the Father, [[101:11|having lifted me up|elevans]], that is, setting me over every creature, [[101:11|thou hast thrown me down|allisisti me]] into death, that is, hast permitted me to be slain and crushed, as thou dost declare in Isaias: [[Is 53:8|for the wickedness of my people have I struck him|Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum]].

paras.t: Dies mei temporales, non dies æternitatis, sicut umbra cito pertransiens declinaverunt, id est, fini et morti appropinquaverunt: quoniam circa tricesimum tertium annum finiti sunt. Et ego sicut fœnum arui in passione: sicut nunc patuit. Tu, Deus Pater, exsurgens misereberis Sion, id est Ecclesiæ, quia tempus miserendi ejus est, me incarnato; quia venit tempus liberationis, me passo. Hæc omnia in præcedenti articulo plene exposita sunt, nec modo specialem expositionem recipiunt.
paras.en: [[101:12|My days|Dies mei]], my days in time, not the days of eternity, [[101:12|like a shadow|sicut umbra]] that quickly passes, [[101:12|have declined|declinaverunt]], that is, have drawn near to their end and to death; for they were ended about the thirty-third year. [[101:12|and I am withered like grass|Et ego sicut fœnum arui]] in the passion, as has now been shown. Thou, God the Father, [[101:14|shalt arise and have mercy on Sion|exsurgens misereberis Sion]], that is, on the Church, [[101:14|for it is time to have mercy on it|quia tempus miserendi ejus]], now that I am incarnate; [[101:14|for the time is come|quia venit tempus]] of deliverance, now that I have suffered. All these things were fully expounded in the preceding article, and need no special exposition now.

paras.t: Dominus de cœlo in terram adspexit, etc., ut annuntient fideles in Sion nomen Domini, et laudem ejus in Jerusalem. Hoc ad litteram accipi potest de primitiva Ecclesia, quæ post missionem Paracleti nomen et gloriam Christi constantissime annuntiavit in Sion, id est in templo ædificato in monte Sion (ut scribitur in Actis), et in Jerusalem, civitate sancta, de qua Christus in Evangelio dixit, Non capit Prophetam perire extra Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[101:20|from heaven the Lord hath looked upon the earth|Dominus de cœlo in terram adspexit]], etc., [[101:22|That they may declare|ut annuntient]], the faithful, [[101:22|the name of the Lord in Sion: and his praise in Jerusalem|in Sion nomen Domini, et laudem ejus in Jerusalem]]. This can be taken literally of the early Church, which after the sending of the Paraclete most steadfastly declared the name and glory of Christ in Sion, that is, in the temple built on mount Sion (as is written in the Acts[[Acts 3:1||]]), and in Jerusalem, the holy city, of which Christ said in the Gospel: [[Luke 13:33|it cannot be that a prophet perish, out of Jerusalem|Non capit Prophetam perire extra Jerusalem]].

paras.t: Initio tu, Domine, terram fundasti, etc., sicut ostensum est. Istam scripturam allegat Apostolus de Christo conscriptam. Christus namque secundum quod Deus, est universorum creator, prout ipsemet in Apocalypsi testatur: Ego sum Alpha et Omega, principium et finis. Demum sicut Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti est una essentia, sic eorum est una potentia, unaque actio; et tres personæ sunt unus Deus, unus Creator, unum principium, unus provisor. Cetera ex præinducta expositione clarescunt.
paras.en: [[101:26|In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth|Initio tu, Domine, terram fundasti]], etc., as has been shown. The Apostle alleges this scripture as written of Christ[[Heb 1:10||]]. For Christ, as God, is the creator of all things, as he himself testifies in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:8|I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end|Ego sum Alpha et Omega, principium et finis]][[Apoc 21:6||]][[Apoc 22:13||]]. Finally, as the Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost have one essence, so they have one power and one action; and the three persons are one God, one Creator, one principle, one provider. The rest is made clear by the exposition given before.

101.title: QUALITER ALIQUI EXPONANT HUNC PSALMUM CENTESIMUM PRIMUM AD LITTERAM.
101.title_en: How some expound this hundred and first psalm according to the letter.

paras.t: Præterea quidam expositores catholici affirmant hunc psalmum ad litteram scriptum de populo Judæorum graviter afflicto, vel tempore captivitatis Babylonicæ, vel tempore persecutionis Antiochi, qui graviter nimis Judæos oppressit, sicut in libris Machabæorum narratur. Adjiciunt tamen expositores hi, quod psalmus iste loquitur de populo Judæorum pro tempore Christi, videlicet, quia in persecutionibus illis maxime desiderabant Christi adventum, per quem sciebant se perfecte liberandos, juxta illud Jeremiæ: In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter. Quemadmodum autem hi exponunt hunc psalmum de populo Judæorum qui fuit, sic Judæorum doctores moderni exponunt psalmum istum de populo Judæorum existenti in captivitate præsenti, per Romanos ipsis inflicta, in qua quotidie orant et præstolantur adventum Messiæ, quem scimus venisse. Verum quia prædicta expositio parum devotionis importat, non nisi cursorie tangenda videtur.
paras.en: Further, some Catholic expositors affirm that this psalm was written, according to the letter, of the Jewish people when it was grievously afflicted, either in the time of the Babylonian captivity or in the time of the persecution of Antiochus, who oppressed the Jews exceedingly, as is told in the books of the Machabees[[1 Mach 1:1||]][[2 Mach 5:1||]]. These expositors add, however, that this psalm speaks of the Jewish people with regard to the time of Christ: namely, that in those persecutions they longed above all for the coming of Christ, by whom they knew they would be perfectly set free, according to that word of Jeremias: [[Jer 23:6|In those days shall Juda be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently|In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter]]. And just as these expound this psalm of the Jewish people as it was then, so the modern teachers of the Jews expound it of the Jewish people as it is in its present captivity, inflicted on them by the Romans, in which they pray daily and wait for the coming of the Messias, who we know has come. But since this exposition carries little devotion, it seems that it should be touched on only in passing.

paras.t: Loquens igitur sanctus Propheta in persona populi Judæorum, temporibus Nabuchodonosor seu Antiochi vehementer anxiati ac depauperati, ait: Domine, exaudi orationem meam, etc. Et patet sententia trium versuum horum ex dictis. Deinde psalmus iste dicit: Quia defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei. Chaldæi namque et servi Antiochi Judæos pro magna parte occiderunt. Et ossa mea sicut cremium aruerunt, præ fame, timore, ac multiformi angustia. Vel hoc dicitur ex persona eorum quos Antiochus fecit in sartagine torreri, cremari ac frigi, prout in libro secundo Machabæorum legitur.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of the Jewish people, sorely distressed and impoverished in the times of Nabuchodonosor or of Antiochus, the holy Prophet says: [[101:2|Hear, O Lord, my prayer|Domine, exaudi orationem meam]], etc. And the sense of these three verses is plain from what has been said. Then this psalm says: [[101:4|For my days are vanished like smoke|Quia defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei]]; for the Chaldeans and the servants of Antiochus slew the Jews for the most part. [[101:4|and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire|Et ossa mea sicut cremium aruerunt]], from hunger, fear and anguish of many kinds. Or this is said in the person of those whom Antiochus had roasted, burned and fried in the frying pan, as we read in the second book of the Machabees[[2 Mach 7:3||]][[2 Mach 7:5||]].

paras.t: Percussus sum fervore et igne durissimæ tribulationis, ut fœnum percutitur ardore solis; et aruit cor meum, præ inopia atque dolore, juxta quod in Threnis inducitur: Vide, Domine, quoniam tribulor; conturbatus est venter meus, subversum est cor meum in me. Unde iterum in Threnis de populo isto ait Jeremias: Denigrata est super carbones facies eorum, et non sunt cogniti in plateis. Quia oblitus sum comedere panem meum, id est, quia mandata legis non observavi: quæ faciens homo, vivet in eis, ut Moyses asserit. Vel, Oblitus sum comedere panem meum materialem: quoniam tempore persecutionis Antiochi, multi Judæorum fugerunt subito ad loca deserta, ubi panem habere non poterant. Propter quod dicit Scriptura: Judas Machabæus secessit in desertum locum, ibique inter feras vitam in montibus cum suis agebat, fœni cibo vescentes.
paras.en: [[101:5|I am smitten|Percussus sum]] by the heat and fire of the harshest tribulation, [[101:5|as grass|ut fœnum]] is smitten by the heat of the sun; [[101:5|and my heart is withered|et aruit cor meum]] from want and grief, as is set down in Lamentations: [[Lam 1:20|Behold, O Lord, for I am in distress, my bowels are troubled: my heart is turned within me|Vide, Domine, quoniam tribulor; conturbatus est venter meus, subversum est cor meum in me]]. Hence again Jeremias says of this people in Lamentations: [[Lam 4:8|Their face is now made blacker than coals, and they are not known in the streets|Denigrata est super carbones facies eorum, et non sunt cogniti in plateis]]. [[101:5|Because I forgot to eat my bread|Quia oblitus sum comedere panem meum]]: that is, because I did not keep the commandments of the law, [[Lev 18:5|which if a man do, he shall live in them|quæ faciens homo, vivet in eis]], as Moses declares. Or: I forgot to eat my material bread; for in the time of the persecution of Antiochus many of the Jews fled suddenly to desert places, where they could not have bread. For which reason Scripture says: Judas Machabeus [[2 Mach 5:27|had withdrawn himself into a desert place, and there lived amongst wild beasts in the mountains with his company|secessit in desertum locum, ibique inter feras vitam in montibus cum suis agebat]], [[2 Mach 5:27|feeding on herbs|fœni cibo vescentes]] [*fœnum*, the "grass" of this verse].

paras.t: A voce gemitus mei adhæsit os meum carni meæ, id est cuti: quia in Judæis caro contabuit præ timore, luctu ac gemitu; sicque cuti ossa adhæserant. Similis factus sum pelicano solitudinis, fugiendo ad eremi loca præ pavore adversariorum. Factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio, quia in die apparere ausus non fui. Absconderunt se namque temporibus illis in diversis latibulis, sicut in libris Machabæorum, Jeremiæ, et Regum conscriptum est. Vigilavi etiam noctibus, quia præ sollicitudine ac timore periculorum non valebam quiescere; et factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto, id est a me ipso divisus, atque hinc inde dispersus: sicut fugitivi non vadunt collectim, sed quilibet providet sibi ipsi, si potest, et abscondit se ubi possibile est.
paras.en: [[101:6|Through the voice of my groaning, my bone hath cleaved to my flesh|A voce gemitus mei adhæsit os meum carni meæ]], that is, to my skin: for in the Jews the flesh wasted away from fear, mourning and groaning, and so their bones clung to their skin. [[101:7|I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness|Similis factus sum pelicano solitudinis]], fleeing to the places of the desert for dread of my adversaries. [[101:7|I am like a night raven in the house|Factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio]], because I did not dare to appear by day. For in those times they hid themselves in various hiding places, as is written in the books of the Machabees[[2 Mach 5:27||]], of Jeremias[[Jer 38:6||]] and of Kings[[1 Kings 13:6||]] [the margin gives Reg. viii, 6; the hiding in caves is at 1 Kings 13:6]. [[101:8|I have watched|Vigilavi]] also by night, because for anxiety and fear of dangers I could not rest; [[101:8|and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop|et factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto]]: that is, divided from myself and scattered here and there; as fugitives do not go together, but each one looks out for himself if he can, and hides wherever it is possible.

paras.t: Tota die, id est assidue, exprobrabant mihi inimici mei, Chaldæi et alii blasphemantes Deum Israel et legem ac populum ejus, quemadmodum in Threnis scribitur: Factus sum in derisum omni populo, canticum eorum tota die; et qui laudabant me fraudulenter et simulatorie, adversum me jurabant, proponentes occidere me. Hoc maxime factum est Judæis tempore Machabæorum a Nicanore ceterisque ministris Antiochi, et regum eum sequentium. Sæpe namque loquebantur Judæis verba pacis ac laudis in dolo. Translatio Hieronymi juxta Hebræum sic habet: Exsultantes mihi, per me jurabant, id est, prædicti inimici mei me deridentes, atque de mea calamitate gaudentes, jurabant per me juramento exsecrationis, ponendo miseriam meam pro exemplo, ita ut dicerent, Nisi egero istud seu illud, sic accidat mihi sicut Judæis.
paras.en: [[101:9|All the day long|Tota die]], that is, continually, [[101:9|my enemies reproached me|exprobrabant mihi inimici mei]]: the Chaldeans and others who blasphemed the God of Israel and his law and people, as is written in Lamentations: [[Lam 3:14|I am made a derision to all my people, their song all the day long|Factus sum in derisum omni populo, canticum eorum tota die]]; [[101:9|and they that praised me|et qui laudabant me]] deceitfully and in pretence [[101:9|did swear against me|adversum me jurabant]], purposing to kill me. This was done to the Jews above all in the time of the Machabees by Nicanor and the other ministers of Antiochus and of the kings who followed him[[1 Mach 7:27||]] [the margin gives 1 Mach. vi, 27–30; Nicanor's deceitful words of peace are at 1 Mach 7:27–30]. For they often spoke words of peace and praise to the Jews in guile. Jerome's translation from the Hebrew has: *Exulting over me, they swore by me*: that is, my aforesaid enemies, mocking me and rejoicing at my calamity, swore by me with an oath of cursing, making my misery an example, so that they would say: If I do not do this or that, may it happen to me as it happened to the Jews.

paras.t: Quia cinerem tanquam panem manducabam: fecerunt enim subcinericios panes, in quibus mixti fuerunt cineres pani. Tempore vero obsidionis Jerusalem a Chaldæis, vehementissima fames erat in populo Judæorum, ita ut in Threnis dicatur: Manus mulierum misericordium coxerunt filios suos; et rursus, Qui nutriebantur in croceis, amplexati sunt stercora. Sicque cineres pro panibus sumere poterant. Et poculum meum cum fletu miscebam, id est, potando ploravi propter imminentia mala. A facie iræ indignationis tuæ, id est a justa tua ultione, quia propter peccata mea hæc mihi fecisti, quemadmodum apud Jeremiam testatus es: Dabo vos in vexationem et maledictionem, eo quod non audieritis verba mea; quia elevans, id est aliquando me honorans, dando mihi legem, Prophetas, reges et sacerdotes, allisisti me, temporibus persecutionum istarum: prout primo Machabæorum scriptum est, Facta est ira magna valde super populum Juda; et iterum, Secundum gloriam ejus, sic et ignominia ejus.
paras.en: [[101:10|For I did eat ashes like bread|Quia cinerem tanquam panem manducabam]]: for they made loaves baked under the ashes, in which ashes were mixed with the bread. And in the time of the siege of Jerusalem by the Chaldeans there was a most terrible famine among the Jewish people, so that it is said in Lamentations: [[Lam 4:10|The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children|Manus mulierum misericordium coxerunt filios suos]]; and again, [[Lam 4:5|they that were brought up in scarlet have embraced the dung|Qui nutriebantur in croceis, amplexati sunt stercora]]. And so they might well take ashes for bread. [[101:10|And mingled my drink with weeping|Et poculum meum cum fletu miscebam]]: that is, as I drank I wept because of the evils hanging over me. [[101:11|Because of thy anger and indignation|A facie iræ indignationis tuæ]]: that is, because of thy just vengeance, since thou hast done these things to me for my sins, as thou didst testify through Jeremias: [[Jer 29:18|I will give them up unto affliction|Dabo vos in vexationem]] and [[Jer 29:18|to be a curse|maledictionem]], [[Jer 29:19|Because they have not hearkened to my words|eo quod non audieritis verba mea]]; [[101:11|for having lifted me up|quia elevans]], that is, having once honoured me by giving me the law, the Prophets, kings and priests, [[101:11|thou hast thrown me down|allisisti me]] in the times of these persecutions; as it is written in the first book of the Machabees: [[1 Mach 1:67|And there was very great wrath upon the people|Facta est ira magna valde super populum Juda]]; and again, [[1 Mach 1:42|Her dishonour was increased according to her glory|Secundum gloriam ejus, sic et ignominia ejus]].

paras.t: Deinde ponitur consolatio Judæorum per adventum Christi, qui secundum divinitatem suam æternus est. Unde de eo nunc dicitur: Tu autem, Domine, in æternum permanes. Hoc quoque Judæis innotuisse videtur, qui loquebantur Domino Christo: Nos audivimus ex lege quia Christus manet in æternum. Tu exsurgens, opem præbendo seu per incarnationem veniendo, misereberis Sion, id est populo Judæorum afflicto et capto; vel, Sion, id est templo et civitati Jerusalem a Chaldæis impie demolitis; quia tempus miserendi ejus, scilicet templi et civitatis, ut reædificarentur, consummatis septuaginta annis a Jeremia prædictis; vel, ut repararentur tempore Machabæorum post dignam castigationem populi Judæorum. Unde in libro secundo Machabæorum dicitur: Ira Domini in misericordiam conversa est. Vel, Venit tempus miserendi ejus, id est, tempus tui adventus in mundum, in Daniele prædeterminatum, impletum est: et ita decet te advenire, et populum Sion a spirituali captivitate redimere, sicut in Isaia promisisti: Propter hoc sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ipse qui loquebar, ecce adsum. Quia venit tempus prædictum. Hoc repetitur ad evidentiam ampliorem.
paras.en: Next is set down the consolation of the Jews through the coming of Christ, who according to his divinity is eternal. Hence it is now said of him: [[101:13|But thou, O Lord, endurest for ever|Tu autem, Domine, in æternum permanes]]. This too seems to have been known to the Jews, who said to the Lord Christ: [[John 12:34|We have heard out of the law that Christ abideth for ever|Nos audivimus ex lege quia Christus manet in æternum]]. [[101:14|Thou shalt arise|Tu exsurgens]], bringing help, or coming by the incarnation, [[101:14|and have mercy on Sion|misereberis Sion]]: that is, on the Jewish people, afflicted and captive; or Sion, that is, the temple and the city of Jerusalem, wickedly pulled down by the Chaldeans; [[101:14|for it is time to have mercy on it|quia tempus miserendi ejus]], namely on the temple and the city, that they might be rebuilt when the seventy years foretold by Jeremias were completed[[Jer 29:10||]]; or that they might be restored in the time of the Machabees, after the Jewish people had been chastised as it deserved. Hence it is said in the second book of the Machabees: [[2 Mach 8:5|the wrath of the Lord was turned into mercy|Ira Domini in misericordiam conversa est]]. Or: the time to have mercy on it is come, that is, the time of thy coming into the world, fixed beforehand in Daniel[[Dan 9:24||]], is fulfilled; and so it is fitting that thou come, and redeem the people of Sion from spiritual captivity, as thou didst promise in Isaias: [[Is 52:6|Therefore my people shall know my name in that day: for I myself that spoke, behold I am here|Propter hoc sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ipse qui loquebar, ecce adsum]]. [[101:14|For the time is come|Quia venit tempus]] that was foretold. This is repeated to make it plainer.

paras.t: Quoniam placuerunt servis tuis, Sanctis et Prophetis, lapides ejus, scilicet Sion: quia optabant ex lapidibus reædificare templum et civitatem Jerusalem; et terræ ejus miserebuntur, id est, pro liberatione populi et reædificatione civitatum Judæ orabunt. Pro hac etenim causa multum oraverunt Zacharias, Daniel, Aggæus, et alii Sancti. — Potest autem exponi hic versus de ædificatione Ecclesiæ, intelligendo per lapides, personas seu membra Ecclesiæ; per servos autem, Apostolos qui primo post Christum construxerunt Ecclesiam, convertendo homines ad Christi obsequium; et terræ ejus, id est Judæ, miserebuntur, quia Apostoli primo conabantur Judæos ad Christum convertere, prout in Actibus Paulus fatetur: Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei. Hæc autem expositio superius tacta est.
paras.en: [[101:15|For the stones thereof have pleased thy servants|Quoniam placuerunt servis tuis]], that is, the Saints and Prophets, [[101:15|the stones thereof|lapides ejus]], namely of Sion: for they longed to rebuild the temple and the city of Jerusalem out of its stones; [[101:15|and they shall have pity on the earth thereof|et terræ ejus miserebuntur]]: that is, they will pray for the deliverance of the people and the rebuilding of the cities of Juda. For this cause Zacharias, Daniel, Aggeus and other Saints prayed much. — This verse can also be expounded of the building of the Church, understanding by the stones the persons or members of the Church, and by the servants the Apostles, who first after Christ built up the Church by converting men to the service of Christ; and [[101:15|on the earth thereof|et terræ ejus]], that is, of Juda, [[101:15|they shall have pity|miserebuntur]], because the Apostles first strove to convert the Jews to Christ, as Paul declares in the Acts: [[Acts 13:46|To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God|Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei]]. But this exposition was touched on above.

paras.t: Respondit ei in via virtutis suæ, etc. Hic secundum aliquos describit Propheta tribulationem Ecclesiæ tempore Antichristi futuram, quæ erit durissima, sed non longa. Ait ergo: Respondit ei, id est, Ecclesia Christo tunc respondebit, in via virtutis suæ, id est in observatione patientiæ quæ tunc summe necessaria erit: Paucitatem dierum meorum, id est brevitatem tribulationis meæ, nuntia mihi, quatenus in spe propinquæ liberationis respirem ac roborer. Nisi enim breviati essent dies illi, non fieret salva omnis caro, sed propter electos breviabuntur: ut scribitur in Matthæo. Ne revoces me de hac vita, id est, ne omnino sinas exstirpari Ecclesiam: ne, inquam, revoces me in dimidio dierum meorum, id est intra primum atque secundum tuum adventum; sed usque ad finem mundi conserva me, quemadmodum spopondisti, dicens: Ecce ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi.
paras.en: [[101:24|He answered him in the way of his strength|Respondit ei in via virtutis suæ]], etc. Here, according to some, the Prophet describes the tribulation that will come upon the Church in the time of Antichrist, which will be most severe, but not long. He says, then: [[101:24|He answered him|Respondit ei]]: that is, the Church will then answer Christ, [[101:24|in the way of his strength|in via virtutis suæ]], that is, in the keeping of patience, which will then be supremely necessary: [[101:24|Declare unto me|nuntia mihi]] [[101:24|the fewness of my days|Paucitatem dierum meorum]], that is, the shortness of my tribulation, so that in the hope of a near deliverance I may breathe again and be strengthened. For [[Matt 24:22|unless those days had been shortened, no flesh should be saved|Nisi enim breviati essent dies illi, non fieret salva omnis caro]], [[Matt 24:22|but for the sake of the elect|sed propter electos]] [[Matt 24:22|shall be shortened|breviabuntur]], as is written in Matthew. [[101:25|Call me not away|Ne revoces me]] from this life, that is, do not let the Church be wholly rooted out: do not, I say, call me away [[101:25|in the midst of my days|in dimidio dierum meorum]], that is, between thy first and thy second coming; but preserve me until the end of the world, as thou didst promise, saying: [[Matt 28:20|behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ecce ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]].

paras.t: Quia vero omnia in figura contingebant Hebræis, secundum Apostolum, propterea si ista expositio esset litteralis, posset hic psalmus tropologice explanari de populo christiano vehementer afflicto, sicut superius de quolibet pœnitente expositus est. Postremo, quæ nunc omissa sunt, in primo articulo evidenter patuerunt.
paras.en: But since [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|omnia in figura contingebant]] to the Hebrews, according to the Apostle, therefore, if this exposition were the literal one, this psalm could be explained tropologically [that is, in its moral sense] of the Christian people sorely afflicted, as it was expounded above of any penitent. Lastly, what has been left out now was made plain in the first article.

paras.t: Precatio. Ad te clamantium exaudi orationem nostram, Domine, et de excelso sancto tuo in terram adspice, et mala præsentia et futura a nobis propitiatus averte: ut annuntiemus in Sion gloriam tuam, et in Jerusalem cœlesti laudem tuam.
paras.en: Prayer. Hear the prayer of us who cry to thee, O Lord, and look down upon the earth from thy high sanctuary, and in thy mercy turn away from us evils present and to come: that we may declare thy glory in Sion, and thy praise in the heavenly Jerusalem.

102.title: EXPLANATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI SECUNDI : BENEDIC, ANIMA MEA, DOMINO.
102.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and second psalm: Bless the Lord, O my soul.

paras.t: Assignatur autem psalmo præsenti hic titulus: Psalmus ipsi David: id est, psalmus iste cantandus est Christo per David significato. Agit namque hic psalmus de multiplici beneficio Christi, et hortatur Propheta se ipsum ad gratiarum actionem condignam. Sicut enim in præcedenti psalmo locutus est in persona pœnitentis, suamque miseriam gemituose et anxie commemorantis, sic modo loquitur in persona fervidi amatoris atque gratissimi servitoris: et hoc, congruo ordine, quia post humilem confessionem propriæ imperfectionis, et variam afflictionem contribulati spiritus, sequi solet ex infusione divina, jucunda laudatio divinæ bonitatis, hilarisque memoria beneficiorum Creatoris. Propter quod in Tobia scriptum est: Post tempestatem, Domine, tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis.
paras.en: Now this title is assigned to the present psalm: [[102:1|For David himself|Psalmus ipsi David]]: that is, this psalm is to be sung to Christ, who is signified by David. For this psalm treats of the manifold benefits of Christ, and the Prophet exhorts himself to a worthy thanksgiving. For as in the preceding psalm he spoke in the person of a penitent, recalling his own misery with groaning and anguish, so now he speaks in the person of a fervent lover and a most grateful servant: and this in fitting order, since after the humble confession of one's own imperfection, and the manifold affliction of a troubled spirit, there commonly follows, by divine infusion, a joyful praise of the divine goodness and a glad remembrance of the Creator's benefits. For which reason it is written in Tobias: [[Tob 3:22|after a storm|Post tempestatem]], O Lord, [[Tob 3:22|thou makest a calm, and after|tranquillum facis, et post]] [[Tob 3:22|weeping thou pourest in joyfulness|fletum exsultationem infundis]].

paras.t: Ait itaque: Benedic, anima mea, Domino. Benedicere alteri, est bonum de ipso asserere. Nos autem benedicimus Deo, et Deus benedicit nobis. Sed quia dicere Dei, est causa rerum, juxta illud: Ipse dixit, et facta sunt; nostrum vero dicere, non est causa rerum: idcirco benedictio Dei activa, est causa bonitatis nostræ, et quod benedicti sumus; nostra autem benedictio non est causa alicujus bonitatis in Deo, nec ob eam est Deus benedictus. Et ideo benedictio qua nos Deo benedicimus, est benedictio confessionis seu laudis. De qua in Luca scriptum est: Benedixit Simeon Deum. Et Tobias: Omni, inquit, tempore benedic Deo. Benedictio autem qua Deus benedicit nobis, est benedictio consecrationis seu actionis. Secundum primam benedictionem, minor benedicit majori, ipsum laudando; quantum vero ad benedictionem secundam, major benedicit minori, ipsum sanctificando seu perficiendo, quemadmodum ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus: Sine ulla contradictione quod minus est, a majore benedicitur.
paras.en: He says, then: [[102:1|Bless the Lord, O my soul|Benedic, anima mea, Domino]]. To bless another is to affirm something good of him. Now we bless God, and God blesses us. But since God's saying is the cause of things, according to that verse: [[Ps 148:5|he spoke, and they were made|Ipse dixit, et facta sunt]], while our saying is not the cause of things, therefore God's active blessing is the cause of our goodness and of our being blessed; but our blessing is not the cause of any goodness in God, nor is God blessed on account of it. And so the blessing with which we bless God is a blessing of confession or praise. Of this it is written in Luke: Simeon [[Luke 2:28|blessed God|Benedixit Simeon Deum]]. And Tobias says: [[Tob 4:20|Bless God at all times|Omni, inquit, tempore benedic Deo]]. But the blessing with which God blesses us is a blessing of consecration or of action. According to the first blessing, the lesser blesses the greater by praising him; but as to the second blessing, the greater blesses the lesser by sanctifying or perfecting him, as the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 7:7|without all contradiction, that which is less is blessed by the better|Sine ulla contradictione quod minus est, a majore benedicitur]].

paras.t: Benedic ergo, anima mea, Domino, id est, bona profer de Deo, laudem et gratiarum actionem ei in omnibus impendendo, ipsum in omnibus atque præ omnibus mente, verbo et opere honorando. Et non solum anima mea, quantum ad id quod es, benedic Deo, sed et omnia quæ intra me sunt, id est omnes vires, omnes habitus, omnes actus, omnes virtutes, omnes scientiæ, omnes cogitationes animæ meæ, benedicite nomini sancto ejus, id est ipsi Deo nomen sanctum habenti. Hæc autem benedicunt Deo occasionaliter seu materialiter, quia sunt occasio atque materia benedicendi Deo, dum scilicet perpendimus nos omnia ista a Deo habere: et ita adscribimus ea Deo tanquam primo principio cum laude et gratiarum actione. Vel benedicunt hæc Deo causaliter, quia per ea cognoscimus Deum ac beneficia ejus. Tunc anima nostra et omnia intra eam existentia benedicunt Altissimo, dum ipsa secundum totum suum esse, posse et agere, Deum verbo et vita honorat, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico habetur: Date magnificentiam nomini ejus, et confitemini illi in voce labiorum vestrorum.
paras.en: [[102:1|Bless the Lord, O my soul|Benedic ergo, anima mea, Domino]], therefore, that is, speak good things of God, rendering him praise and thanksgiving in all things, honouring him in all things and above all things in mind, word and deed. And not only do thou, my soul, as to what thou art, bless God, but [[102:1|let all that is within me|et omnia quæ intra me sunt]], that is, all the powers, all the habits, all the acts, all the virtues, all the knowledge, all the thoughts of my soul, [[102:1|bless his holy name|benedicite nomini sancto ejus]], that is, God himself, who has a holy name. Now these bless God occasionally or materially [that is, as the occasion and the matter of the blessing, not as those who utter it], since they are the occasion and matter of blessing God, namely when we consider that we have all these things from God: and so we ascribe them to God as to their first principle, with praise and thanksgiving. Or these things bless God causally, since through them we know God and his benefits. Then our soul and all that exists within it bless the Most High, when the soul honours God by word and life according to its whole being, power and action, as is found in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 39:20|Magnify his name, and give glory to him with the voice of your lips|Date magnificentiam nomini ejus, et confitemini illi in voce labiorum vestrorum]].

paras.t: Benedic, anima mea, Domino: quod tibi iterum dico, quatenus accendaris et penses, quam utile, salubre et justum sit benedicere Creatori; et noli oblivisci per ignaviam et inadvertentiam omnes retributiones ejus, id est dona pietatis divinæ, quæ tibi frequenter collata sunt, et ad minus retributa, id est, rursus tributa sunt tibi semel: quia in primo parente omnes peccavimus, et munera gratiarum Dei perdidimus; sed misericordia Dei per Christum nobis retribuit, quod primus parens abstulit et amisit. Propter quod ad Corinthios Apostolus ait: Sicut in Adam omnes moriuntur, ita et in Christo omnes vivificabuntur. Non ergo obliviscamur misericordiarum Dei nostri, sed attendamus quoties nobis gratiam suam retribuit. Quotiescumque corde ingemiscimus, statim ignoscit, gratiamque refundit: imo legatos ad nos mittit, hortans et per eos deprecans, ut convertamur ad ipsum, quemadmodum profitetur divinus Apostolus: Legatione, inquiens, pro Christo fungimur, tanquam Deo exhortante per nos: Obsecramus pro Christo, reconciliamini Deo. Nunquam igitur obliviscamur viscerum misericordiæ Salvatoris, quia Seneca asserit, Maxima ingratitudo est beneficii collati oblivio. Prima vero gratitudo et gratiæ repensio, est beneficium gratanter recipere. Isaias oblitus non fuit retributionum Dei, qui ait: Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis, et quæ largitus est nobis secundum indulgentiam suam. Unde Ecclesiasticus inquit: Memoratus sum misericordiæ tuæ, Domine, et cooperationis tuæ, quæ a sæculo sunt. Porro quum Deus bonorum nostrorum non egeat, aliquid tamen a nobis requirat, nil dignius, nihilque acceptius ei retribuere possumus, quam benedictionem et laudem. Nam sacrificium laudis honorificat ipsum.
paras.en: [[102:2|Bless the Lord, O my soul|Benedic, anima mea, Domino]]: which I say to thee a second time, that thou mayest be kindled and weigh how profitable, wholesome and just it is to bless the Creator; [[102:2|and never forget|et noli oblivisci]] through sloth and heedlessness [[102:2|all he hath done for thee|omnes retributiones ejus]] [Latin *retributiones*, literally "repayments", which Denis takes up in the next words], that is, the gifts of the divine kindness, which have often been bestowed upon thee, and at the least have been re-tributed, that is, given back to thee again once: for in our first parent we all sinned and lost the gifts of God's graces; but the mercy of God through Christ has given back to us what our first parent took away and lost. For which reason the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 15:22|as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive|Sicut in Adam omnes moriuntur, ita et in Christo omnes vivificabuntur]]. Let us not, then, forget the mercies of our God, but let us mark how often he has given his grace back to us. As often as we groan in heart, he forgives at once and pours his grace in again: nay more, he sends ambassadors to us, exhorting and through them beseeching us to turn to him, as the divine Apostle declares, saying: [[2 Cor 5:20|For Christ therefore we are ambassadors, God as it were exhorting by us, for Christ, we beseech you, be reconciled to God|Legatione, inquiens, pro Christo fungimur, tanquam Deo exhortante per nos: Obsecramus pro Christo, reconciliamini Deo]]. Let us never, therefore, forget the bowels of mercy of the Saviour, since Seneca asserts: The greatest ingratitude is to forget a benefit bestowed. And the first gratitude and return of a favour is to receive the benefit gladly. Isaias did not forget the benefits of God, for he says: [[Is 63:7|I will remember the tender mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all the things that the Lord hath bestowed upon us|Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis]], and [[Is 63:7|which he hath given them according to his kindness|quæ largitus est nobis secundum indulgentiam suam]]. Whence Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 51:11|I remembered thy mercy, O Lord, and thy works, which are from the beginning of the world|Memoratus sum misericordiæ tuæ, Domine, et cooperationis tuæ, quæ a sæculo sunt]]. Moreover, since God has no need of our goods[[Ps 15:2||]], and yet requires something of us, we can render him nothing worthier and nothing more acceptable than blessing and praise. For [[Ps 49:23|The sacrifice of praise shall glorify|sacrificium laudis honorificat]] him.

paras.t: Consequenter commemorantur quædam beneficia Dei, et prius beneficium indulgentiæ. Qui propitiatur omnibus iniquitatibus tuis. Mox enim dum pœnitemus et confitemur, Deus iniquitates omnes nobis dimittit, quantum ad culpam. Non enim dimittitur unum peccatum mortale, quin aliud, si adsit, dimittatur: unum tamen veniale sine alio quandoque dimittitur. Propitiatus est autem Deus piissimus iniquitatibus nostris frequenter, scilicet in Baptismo, in Confessione, quæ est secunda post naufragium tabula, in ingressu seu professione religionis. Qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas, id est interiores languores, qui per gratiæ infusionem sanantur. Vel: Qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas, id est fomitem seu pronitatem ad malum, et quatuor principalia vulnera animæ, quæ sunt, malitia, ignorantia, concupiscentia, infirmitas. Has Deus nunc sanat inchoative, debilitando eas in Baptismo et quotidiano profectu, impediendoque eas per gratiam a consensu ac opere malo. In resurrectione autem futura sanabit eas perfecte, quando mortale hoc induet immortalitatem, secundum Apostolum. Tunc nempe Christus auferet ab electis omnes pœnas pro originali peccato inflictas, quantum ad reatum et exsistentiam; nunc vero aufert eas quoad reatum, non quantum ad exsistentiam. Manet enim in nobis fomes post Baptismum, sed non imputatur ad culpam, nec pro eo pœnam damni incurrimus morientes. Quum autem Christus perfecte sanaverit omnes infirmitates nostras, tunc læti cantabimus illud Apostoli: Ubi est, mors, victoria tua? ubi est, mors, aculeus tuus?
paras.en: Next certain benefits of God are recalled, and first the benefit of pardon. [[102:3|Who forgiveth all thy iniquities|Qui propitiatur omnibus iniquitatibus tuis]]. For as soon as we repent and confess, God remits all our iniquities as to the guilt. For one mortal sin is not remitted without another, if there is one, being remitted too: but one venial sin is sometimes remitted without another. Now the most loving God has often been propitious to our iniquities: namely in Baptism, in Confession, which is the second plank after shipwreck, and at the entrance into religion, that is, at religious profession. [[102:3|who healeth all thy diseases|Qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas]], that is, our inward sicknesses, which are healed by the infusion of grace. Or: [[102:3|who healeth all thy diseases|Qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas]], that is, the tinder [Latin *fomes*: the inclination to sin left in us by original sin] or proneness to evil, and the four chief wounds of the soul, which are malice, ignorance, concupiscence and weakness. These God now heals in a beginning, weakening them in Baptism and by daily progress, and holding them back by grace from consent and evil deed. But in the resurrection to come he will heal them perfectly, when [[1 Cor 15:54|this mortal hath put on immortality|mortale hoc induet immortalitatem]][[1 Cor 15:53||]], according to the Apostle. For then Christ will take away from the elect all the penalties inflicted for original sin, both as to the guilt [Latin *reatus*: liability to punishment] and as to their existence; but now he takes them away as to the guilt, not as to their existence. For the tinder remains in us after Baptism, but it is not imputed as fault, nor do we, dying, incur the penalty of loss [that is, the loss of the vision of God] on its account. And when Christ has perfectly healed all our infirmities, then we shall gladly sing that word of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 15:55|O death, where is thy victory? O death, where is thy sting?|Ubi est, mors, victoria tua? ubi est, mors, aculeus tuus?]][[Osee 13:14||]]

paras.t: Qui redimit de interitu vitam tuam. Interdum redimit Deus vitam nostram corporalem ac naturalem a morte improvisa et corporali, præservando nos a periculis variis. Vitam quoque animæ nostræ spiritualem de interitu spirituali redimit, dum caritatem et gratiam suam in nobis conservat, a peccatis mortalibus nos præservans. Vel: Qui redimit merito suæ passionis de interitu, id est morte inferni seu damnatione æterna, vitam tuam, id est vitam gratiæ tibi in præsenti collatam seu conferendam, et vitam gloriæ tibi in futuro paratam. Vel, Vitam tuam, id est te viventem, quemadmodum dicimus: Rogo dilectionem tuam, id est te dilectum. De hac autem redemptione ait Salvator: Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant; et iterum, Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Qui coronat te in misericordia et miserationibus, id est, qui in sua misericordia et per effectus varios suæ clementiæ nunc coronat te, dando tibi victoriam de mundo, carne ac dæmone, sicut ait Apostolus: Gratias Deo, qui semper triumphat nos in Christo Jesu Domino nostro. Coronat nos etiam Deus in misericordia sua, faciendo animas nostras filias, sponsas atque heredes regni æterni. Propter quod Petrus ait in prima sua Canonica: Vos, inquit, genus electum, regale sacerdotium. In futuro quoque coronabit nos corona felicitatis perfectæ, quemadmodum Paulus affirmat: De reliquo reposita est mihi corona justitiæ, quam reddet mihi Dominus in die illa.
paras.en: [[102:4|Who redeemeth thy life from destruction|Qui redimit de interitu vitam tuam]]. At times God redeems our bodily and natural life from sudden and bodily death, preserving us from various dangers. He also redeems the spiritual life of our soul from spiritual destruction, when he preserves his charity and grace in us, keeping us from mortal sins. Or: [[102:4|Who redeemeth|Qui redimit]] by the merit of his passion [[102:4|from destruction|de interitu]], that is, from the death of hell or eternal damnation, [[102:4|thy life|vitam tuam]], that is, the life of grace bestowed or to be bestowed on thee in the present, and the life of glory prepared for thee in the future. Or: [[102:4|thy life|vitam tuam]], that is, thee, living; as we say: I ask your love, that is, you, beloved [that is, "your love" stands for the person loved, as "thy life" for the person living]. Of this redemption the Saviour says: [[John 10:10|I am come that they may have life and may have it more abundantly|Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant]]; and again: [[John 10:15|I lay down my life for my sheep|Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]. [[102:4|who crowneth thee with mercy and compassion|Qui coronat te in misericordia et miserationibus]], that is, who in his mercy and by the various effects of his clemency now crowns thee, giving thee the victory over the world, the flesh and the devil, as the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 2:14|thanks be to God, who always maketh us to triumph in Christ Jesus|Gratias Deo, qui semper triumphat nos in Christo Jesu]] our Lord. God also crowns us in his mercy by making our souls daughters, brides and heirs of the eternal kingdom. For which reason Peter says in his first Canonical Epistle: But [[1 Pet 2:9|you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood|Vos, inquit, genus electum, regale sacerdotium]]. In the future too he will crown us with the crown of perfect happiness, as Paul affirms: [[2 Tim 4:8|As to the rest, there is laid up for me a crown of justice which the Lord|De reliquo reposita est mihi corona justitiæ, quam reddet mihi Dominus]] [[2 Tim 4:8|will render to me in that day|in die illa]].

paras.t: Qui replet in bonis desiderium tuum, id est, rationabilem tuum affectum seu piam orationem ad actum perducit, dando tibi quod cupis et postulas. Omnis enim qui petit, accipit. Et dictum est supra: Desiderium pauperum exaudivit Dominus; et, Nihil deest timentibus eum. Nunc itaque implet Deus desiderium nostrum gratia atque virtutibus, non simpliciter, nec plene, sed secundum modum vitæ præsentis. In patria vero implebitur simpliciter atque perfecte, juxta quod dictum est: Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua.
paras.en: [[102:5|Who satisfieth thy desire with good things|Qui replet in bonis desiderium tuum]], that is, he brings thy reasonable longing or devout prayer to fulfilment, giving thee what thou desirest and askest. For [[Luke 11:10|every one that asketh receiveth|Omnis enim qui petit, accipit]]. And it has been said above: [[Ps 9:38|The Lord hath heard the desire of the poor|Desiderium pauperum exaudivit Dominus]] [the margin reads "Ps. v, 17, seu Hebr."; the words are Ps 9:38, which is 10:17 in the Hebrew numbering]; and: [[Ps 33:10|there is no want to them that fear him|Nihil deest timentibus eum]] [Denis: "nothing is lacking to them that fear him"]. Now, then, God fills our desire with grace and virtues, not simply nor fully, but according to the measure of the present life. But in our heavenly country it will be filled simply and perfectly, according to what has been said: [[Ps 16:15|I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear|Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua]].

paras.t: Renovabitur ut aquilæ juventus tua: id est, quemadmodum aquila inveterata reparat pristinam juventutem; sic tu, o anima mea, ad pristinam atque deperditam spiritualis juventutis valetudinem reverteris, nunc quidem per gratiam, implendo illud Apostoli, Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ, et induite novum hominem, qui secundum Deum creatus est: in futuro autem per gloriam, quia in die judicii vestieris duplicibus, id est duplici stola immortalitatis, videlicet gloria mentis et corporis; et ultra senectus non erit, sed juventus perpetua, juxta illud Apocalypsis: Dixit qui sedebat in throno, Ecce nova facio omnia. Juventus quoque corporis in die judicii renovabitur, quia in ætate virili resurgent defuncti.
paras.en: [[102:5|thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle's|Renovabitur ut aquilæ juventus tua]]: that is, as the eagle grown old recovers its former youth, so thou, O my soul, returnest to the former and lost vigour of spiritual youth: now, indeed, through grace, fulfilling that word of the Apostle: [[Eph 4:23|And be renewed in spirit of your mind|Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ]], [[Eph 4:24|And put on the new man, who according to God is created|et induite novum hominem, qui secundum Deum creatus est]]; but in the future through glory, since on the day of judgment thou shalt be [[Prov 31:21|clothed with double garments|vestieris duplicibus]], that is, with the double robe of immortality, namely the glory of the mind and of the body; and there will be old age no more, but perpetual youth, according to that verse of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:5|he that sat on the throne, said: Behold, I make all things new|Dixit qui sedebat in throno, Ecce nova facio omnia]]. The youth of the body also will be renewed on the day of judgment, since the dead will rise again at the age of manhood.

paras.t: Demum, sicut refertur, ista aquilæ est natura, quod tempore senectutis suæ superius labium suum per modum unci in tantum excrescit, quod nec os aperire, nec cibum sumere potest. Propter quod tandem fame senioque gravata, ex naturali instinctu labium collidit ad petram, deponitque uncatum, quo sumptio cibi impediebatur: quo facto, reparatur ad valetudinem pristinam per sumptionem escarum. Sic anima, corporis atque terrenæ inhabitationis mole gravata, et a contemplatione cœlestium impedita, nunc quidem quotidie quantum sibi possibile est, a carnis communione se abstrahit, et vitam cœlestem in terra ducere satagit; sicque quotidie renovatur interius, sicut ad Corinthios dicit Apostolus: Licet is qui foris est, noster homo corrumpatur, tamen is qui intus est, renovatur de die in diem. Gratia enim Dei et summæ Trinitatis reformatio in nobis, est renovatio juventutis animæ nostræ. Conversatio autem vitiosa, senectus est animæ. Propter quod scriptum est: Quid est, Israel, quod inveterasti in terra aliena, coinquinatus es cum mortuis, deputatus es cum descendentibus in infernum? Et causam subjungit: Dereliquisti fontem sapientiæ. Nam si in via Dei ambulasses, habitasses utique in pace super terram.
paras.en: Further, as is related, this is the nature of the eagle: in the time of its old age its upper beak grows out so far in the manner of a hook that it can neither open its mouth nor take food. For which reason at length, weighed down by hunger and age, it strikes its beak against a rock by natural instinct and breaks off the hooked part that hindered it from taking food; and when this is done, it is restored to its former vigour by taking food. So the soul, weighed down by the mass of the body and of its earthly dwelling[[Wis 9:15||]] and hindered from the contemplation of heavenly things, now indeed withdraws itself daily, as far as it can, from fellowship with the flesh, and strives to lead a heavenly life on earth; and so it is daily renewed within, as the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 4:16|though our outward man is corrupted, yet the inward man is renewed day by day|Licet is qui foris est, noster homo corrumpatur, tamen is qui intus est, renovatur de die in diem]]. For the grace of God and the reforming of the most high Trinity in us is the renewal of our soul's youth. But a life of vice is the old age of the soul. For which reason it is written: [[Bar 3:10|How happeneth it, O Israel, that|Quid est, Israel, quod]] thou [[Bar 3:11|art grown old in a strange country, thou art defiled with the dead: thou art counted with them that go down into hell|inveterasti in terra aliena, coinquinatus es cum mortuis, deputatus es cum descendentibus in infernum?]]? And he adds the cause: [[Bar 3:12|Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom|Dereliquisti fontem sapientiæ]]. [[Bar 3:13|For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou hadst surely dwelt in peace|Nam si in via Dei ambulasses, habitasses utique in pace]] upon the earth [the Vulgate has "for ever", *sempiterna*, where Denis reads "upon the earth", *super terram*].

paras.t: Quæ autem hucusque inducta sunt ad litteram, exponi possent de specialibus beneficiis sancto David collatis: imo quilibet nostrum hos quinque versus dicendo, beneficia sibi specialiter præstita pensare, et Deo cum omni gratiarum actione debet adscribere, ne propter ingratitudinem et oblivionem animæ nostræ dicatur: Eris deserta, quia oblita es Dei salvatoris tui, et adjutoris tui non es recordata.
paras.en: Now what has been set out so far according to the letter could be expounded of the special benefits bestowed on holy David: nay, each of us, in saying these five verses, ought to weigh the benefits granted to himself in particular and ascribe them to God with all thanksgiving, lest on account of our soul's ingratitude and forgetfulness it be said: [[Is 17:9|thou shalt be desolate|Eris deserta]], [[Is 17:10|Because thou hast forgotten God thy saviour|quia oblita es Dei salvatoris tui]], [[Is 17:10|and hast not remembered|et adjutoris tui non es recordata]] thy helper.

paras.t: Faciens misericordias Dominus : id est, Deus misericorditer agit nobiscum, et misericordias (id est pietatis suæ dona) nobis communicat : et non solum facit misericordias misericordibus, de quibus ait, Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur ; sed etiam impiis et indignis, quos sæpe gratis justificat, quos longanimiter præstolatur, quibus beneficia naturalium donorum largitur, videlicet lumen solis, vestitum et victum, rationem et sensum, corporis sanitatem, ac alia multa. Proprium namque est Deo misereri. Est quoque Dominus faciens et judicium, id est justam ultionem, omnibus injuriam patientibus æquanimiter propter justitiam : quemadmodum alibi ait, Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam. Vult enim Deus sibi reservari vindictam, prout in Levitico hortatur : Non quæras ultionem, nec memor eris injuriæ civium tuorum. Denique, quamvis aliquis impatienter ferat injurias sibi illatas, Deus tamen qui nullum malum inordinatum seu impunitum relinquit, ulciscitur. Præcipue tamen ulciscitur pro patientibus et mansuetis. Unde in Proverbiis : Non dicas, Reddam malum pro malo : exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te.
paras.en: [[102:6|The Lord doth mercies|Faciens misericordias Dominus]]: that is, God deals mercifully with us and imparts his mercies to us (that is, the gifts of his loving-kindness); and he does mercies not only to the merciful, of whom he says, [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]], but also to the wicked and unworthy, whom he often justifies freely, whom he awaits with long patience, and on whom he bestows the benefits of natural gifts: the light of the sun, clothing and food, reason and sense, health of body, and many other things. For it is proper to God to have mercy [an echo of the Church's prayer *Deus, cui proprium est misereri semper et parcere*, "O God, whose property is always to have mercy and to spare"]. The Lord also doth mercies [[102:6|and judgment|et judicium]], that is, just vengeance, [[102:6|for all that suffer wrong|omnibus injuriam patientibus]] with an even mind for justice' sake: as he says elsewhere, [[Deut 32:35|Revenge is mine, and I will repay|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam]] [Denis's wording, *Mihi vindictam*, is that of the Apostle's citations of this verse, Rom 12:19 and Heb 10:30]. For God wills that vengeance be reserved to himself, as he exhorts in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:18|Seek not revenge, nor be mindful of the injury of thy citizens|Non quæras ultionem, nec memor eris injuriæ civium tuorum]]. Finally, though a man may bear impatiently the injuries done to him, yet God, who leaves no evil disordered or unpunished, avenges them. But above all he avenges on behalf of the patient and the meek. Hence in Proverbs: [[Prov 20:22|Say not: I will return evil|Non dicas, Reddam malum pro malo]] [Denis adds *pro malo*, "for evil"]: [[Prov 20:22|wait for the Lord, and he will deliver thee|exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te]].

paras.t: Notas fecit vias suas, id est præcepta moralia, judicialia et cærimonialia, Moysi legislatori in monte Sinai ; et notas fecit per Moysen filiis Israel voluntates suas, id est signa suæ æternæ voluntatis, videlicet jussiones bonorum, prohibitiones malorum. Idem autem significatur per vias Dei, et voluntates ipsius. Hæc autem tunc specialiter notificavit illis. Propter quod Baruch in persona populi Israelitici dicit : Beati sumus nos, quoniam quæ Deo placita sunt, manifesta sunt nobis. Moraliter vero per Moysen intelligitur quilibet sanctus de aquis concupiscentiarum sublatus, cui Deus per Spiritum Sanctum inspirat qualiter sit vivendum, quemadmodum in Joanne habetur : Unctio ejus docet vos de omnibus. Per filios vero Israel intelliguntur omnes fideles, quibus Deus præcepta sua largitus est.
paras.en: [[102:7|He hath made his ways known|Notas fecit vias suas]], that is, the moral, judicial and ceremonial precepts, [[102:7|to Moses|Moysi]] the lawgiver on Mount Sinai; and through Moses he made known [[102:7|his wills to the children of Israel|filiis Israel voluntates suas]], that is, the signs of his eternal will, namely the commanding of good things and the forbidding of evil ones. The same thing is meant by the ways of God and by his wills. And these he then made known to them in a special manner. Wherefore Baruch, in the person of the people of Israel, says: [[Bar 4:4|We are happy|Beati sumus nos]], [[Bar 4:4|because the things that are pleasing to God, are made known to us|quoniam quæ Deo placita sunt, manifesta sunt nobis]]. Morally, by Moses is understood any saint drawn out of the waters of concupiscence [Moses was so named because he was drawn out of the water, Ex 2:10], to whom God by the Holy Ghost breathes how he must live, as we have it in John: [[1 John 2:27|his unction teacheth you of all things|Unctio ejus docet vos de omnibus]]. And by the children of Israel are understood all the faithful, on whom God has bestowed his precepts.

paras.t: Miserator et misericors Dominus. Secundum Damascenum misericors dicitur, quasi cor miserum habens, videlicet quia alterius miseriæ condolet. Deus autem impassibilis immutabilisque consistens, non condolet, neque compatitur. Non ergo misericordia competit Deo, prout compassionem importat, sed in quantum gratuitam subventionem designat : sicque vocatur Deus miserator, actualiter miserendo : misericors autem, propter naturalem proprietatem, qua ad succurrendum paratus est. Longanimis, id est diu exspectans conversionem malorum. Unde in Ecclesiastico scriptum est, Altissimus est patiens redditor ; et in libro Sapientiæ, Misereris omnium, quoniam omnia potes, et dissimulas peccata hominum propter pœnitentiam. Et multum misericors : imo abundantia pietatis suæ, et merita supplicum excedit et vota ; et miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus. Propterea Jacobus asserit : Superexaltat autem misericordia judicium.
paras.en: [[102:8|The Lord is compassionate and merciful|Miserator et misericors Dominus]]. According to Damascene, one is called merciful (*misericors*) as having a sorrowing heart (*cor miserum*), namely because he grieves with another's misery. But God, abiding impassible and unchangeable, neither grieves with anyone nor suffers with him. Mercy, then, does not belong to God in so far as it implies compassion, but in so far as it means freely given relief; and so God is called *compassionate* (*miserator*) from his actually showing mercy, and *merciful* (*misericors*) from the natural property by which he is ready to give help. [[102:8|Longsuffering|Longanimis]], that is, long awaiting the conversion of the wicked. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 5:4|the most High is a patient rewarder|Altissimus est patiens redditor]]; and in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 11:24|thou hast mercy upon all, because thou canst do all things, and overlookest the sins of men for the sake of repentance|Misereris omnium, quoniam omnia potes, et dissimulas peccata hominum propter pœnitentiam]]. [[102:8|And plenteous in mercy|Et multum misericors]]: indeed, in the abundance of his loving-kindness he exceeds both the merits and the desires of those who pray to him [words of a collect of the Church, *qui abundantia pietatis tuæ et merita supplicum excedis et vota*]; and [[Ps 144:9|his tender mercies are over all his works|miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus]]. Therefore James declares: [[Jas 2:13|And mercy exalteth itself above judgment|Superexaltat autem misericordia judicium]].

paras.t: Non in perpetuum irascetur, exercendo vindictam, neque in æternum comminabitur, se pœnas inflicturum. Non absolute intelligenda sunt hæc, ne incidamus eorum insaniam, qui pœnas inferni tandem finiendas dixerunt. Sed non in perpetuum irascetur Dominus electis suis, neque in æternum comminabitur eis : quia licet ad tempus eos flagellet seu deserat, finaliter tamen eis placatur, secundum illud Threnorum : Non repellet in sempiternum Dominus, quia si abjecit, et miserebitur secundum multitudinem misericordiarum suarum.
paras.en: [[102:9|He will not always be angry|Non in perpetuum irascetur]], by exacting vengeance, [[102:9|nor will he threaten for ever|neque in æternum comminabitur]] that he will inflict punishment. These words are not to be understood absolutely, lest we fall into the madness of those who said that the pains of hell will at last come to an end. Rather, the Lord will not always be angry with his elect, nor threaten them for ever: for though for a time he scourges or forsakes them, yet in the end he is appeased towards them, according to that saying of Lamentations: [[Lam 3:31|For the Lord will not cast off for ever|Non repellet in sempiternum Dominus]]: [[Lam 3:32|For if he hath cast off, he will also have mercy, according to the multitude of his mercies|quia si abjecit, et miserebitur secundum multitudinem misericordiarum suarum]].

paras.t: Non secundum peccata nostra fecit nobis : primo, quia citra condignum nos punit ; secundo, quoniam nullus peccator qui est in mortali, gratiam de condigno meretur. Idcirco si gratia ei restituitur, non secundum peccata sua fit sibi. Tertio, quoniam ubi abundavit delictum, superabundat et gratia. Ideo ad Timotheum Apostolus ait : Deus liberavit nos, et vocavit nos vocatione sua sancta, non secundum opera nostra, sed secundum propositum suum et gratiam. Neque secundum iniquitates nostras retribuit nobis : quia frequenter pœnam æternam commutat in pœnam temporalem per gratiam suam.
paras.en: [[102:10|He hath not dealt with us according to our sins|Non secundum peccata nostra fecit nobis]]: first, because he punishes us short of what we deserve; secondly, because no sinner who is in mortal sin merits grace *de condigno* [by condign merit, that is, merit that has a claim in strict justice to its reward]. Therefore, if grace is restored to him, it is not done to him according to his sins. Thirdly, because [[Rom 5:20|where sin abounded, grace did more abound|ubi abundavit delictum, superabundat et gratia]]. Therefore the Apostle says to Timothy: God [[2 Tim 1:9|hath delivered us and called us by his holy calling, not according to our own works, but according to his own purpose and grace|liberavit nos, et vocavit nos vocatione sua sancta, non secundum opera nostra, sed secundum propositum suum et gratiam]]. [[102:10|Nor rewarded us according to our iniquities|Neque secundum iniquitates nostras retribuit nobis]]: because he often commutes eternal punishment into temporal punishment through his grace.

paras.t: Quoniam secundum altitudinem cœli a terra, corroboravit misericordiam suam super timentes se : id est, sicut cœlum super terram maxime elevatur ; sic misericordia Dei elevata est supra nostram malitiam, ita quod incomparabiliter aliter fecit cum timentibus se timore filiali et casto, quam merebantur, juxta illud Apostoli : Commendat autem caritatem suam in nobis Deus, quoniam quum adhuc inimici essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est. Vel sic : Quoniam secundum altitudinem cœli a terra, etc., id est, quemadmodum cœlum ratione altitudinis et excellentiæ suæ terram operit, circuit, fecundat, illuminat ; sic Deus in circuitu populi sui exsistens, eum in bono conservat, intus illustrat, fecunditatem operum bonorum impendit, prout Filius Dei apud Joannem protestatur : Pater meus agricola est.
paras.en: [[102:11|For according to the height of the heaven above the earth: he hath strengthened his mercy towards them that fear him|Quoniam secundum altitudinem cœli a terra, corroboravit misericordiam suam super timentes se]]: that is, as the heaven is raised high above the earth, so the mercy of God is raised above our wickedness, so that he has dealt with them that fear him with a filial and chaste fear incomparably otherwise than they deserved, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Rom 5:8|But God commendeth his charity towards us: because when as yet|Commendat autem caritatem suam in nobis Deus, quoniam quum adhuc]] we were enemies [Denis has *inimici*, "enemies", from the next verse but one, Rom 5:10, where this verse has *peccatores*, "sinners"], [[Rom 5:9|Christ died for us|Christus pro nobis mortuus est]]. Or thus: [[102:11|For according to the height of the heaven above the earth|Quoniam secundum altitudinem cœli a terra]], etc.: that is, as the heaven, by reason of its height and excellence, covers the earth, encircles it, makes it fruitful and gives it light, so God, being round about his people, keeps them in good, enlightens them within, and bestows on them fruitfulness in good works, as the Son of God testifies in John: [[John 15:1|my Father is the husbandman|Pater meus agricola est]].

paras.t: Quantum distat distantia quantitativa atque locali, ortus, id est pars cœli orientalis, ab occidente, id est a parte occidentali : quæ utique tanta est, quanta est distantia inter polum arcticum et antarcticum, quum cœlum sit sphæricum. Vel, Quantum distat distantia qualitatis, ortus, id est lux seu origo diei, ab occidente, id est a tenebris, dieique termino. Longe fecit a nobis iniquitates nostras : quia ita nobis pœnitentibus eas indulget, ac si nunquam fuissent. Unde per Ezechielem testatur : Si impius egerit pœnitentiam, omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor amplius. Et in Michæa habetur : Deponet iniquitates nostras, et projiciet in profundum maris omnia peccata nostra.
paras.en: [[102:12|As far as|Quantum distat]], by a distance of quantity and of place, [[102:12|the east|ortus]], that is, the eastern part of the heaven, [[102:12|is from the west|ab occidente]], that is, from the western part: which is indeed as great as the distance between the arctic and the antarctic pole, since the heaven is a sphere. Or: [[102:12|As far as|Quantum distat]], by a distance of quality, [[102:12|the east|ortus]], that is, the light or beginning of the day, [[102:12|is from the west|ab occidente]], that is, from the darkness and the end of the day. [[102:12|So far hath he removed our iniquities from us|Longe fecit a nobis iniquitates nostras]]: for he so pardons them to us when we repent, as if they had never been. Hence he testifies through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 18:21|if the wicked do penance|Si impius egerit pœnitentiam]], [[Ezech 18:22|I will not remember all his iniquities|omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor]] any more. And in Micheas we have: [[Mich 7:19|he will put away our iniquities: and he will cast all our sins into the bottom of the sea|Deponet iniquitates nostras, et projiciet in profundum maris omnia peccata nostra]].

paras.t: Quomodo miseretur pater carnalis ac indulgentissimus filiorum suorum, misertus est Dominus timentibus se : quoniam sicut pater filium diligit, sive blandiatur, sive comminetur et verberet ; sic Deus timentibus se misericordiam facit, sive eos castiget, sive consolationem infundat. Et hoc est quod in Malachia ait : Parcam timentibus me, sicut parcit vir filio suo servienti sibi. Sive ergo adversa, sive prospera accidant nobis, Domino gratias referamus, scientes quoniam diligentibus atque timentibus Deum, omnia cooperantur in bonum.
paras.en: [[102:13|As a father hath compassion|Quomodo miseretur pater]] (a father in the flesh, and a most indulgent one) [[102:13|on his children|filiorum suorum]], [[102:13|so hath the Lord compassion on them that fear him|misertus est Dominus timentibus se]]: for as a father loves his son, whether he caresses him or threatens and beats him, so God shows mercy to them that fear him, whether he chastises them or pours consolation into them. And this is what he says in Malachias: [[Mal 3:17|I will spare them, as a man spareth his son that serveth him|Parcam timentibus me, sicut parcit vir filio suo servienti sibi]] [Denis has "I will spare them that fear me"; the verse has *parcam eis*, "I will spare them"]. Whether, then, adversity or prosperity befall us, let us give thanks to the Lord, knowing that [[Rom 8:28|to them that love God all things work together unto good|diligentibus atque timentibus Deum, omnia cooperantur in bonum]] [Denis adds "and fear"; the margin's "Item. viii, 28" stands for Rom. viii, 28].

paras.t: Cur autem tam clemens sit nobis Dominus, pandit : Quoniam ipse cognovit figmentum nostrum, id est fragilem nostram substantiam ad mala proclivem, propter fomitem ad vitia inclinantem. Hæc autem fragilitas nostræ substantiæ plenius declaratur, quum subditur : Recordatus est, quoniam pulvis sumus, id est, pie attendit, quoniam pulvis sumus, id est, de limo terræ, quantum ad corpus, formati, atque in pulverem resolvendi, quemadmodum dicit Scriptura : Formavit Dominus Deus hominem de limo terræ ; et : Pulvis es, et in pulverem reverteris.
paras.en: And why the Lord is so gentle towards us, he makes plain: [[102:14|For he knoweth our frame|Quoniam ipse cognovit figmentum nostrum]], that is, our frail substance, prone to evil because of the tinder [*fomes*, the "tinder" of sin: the inclination to sin left in us by original sin] that inclines it to vice. And this frailty of our substance is set out more fully when he adds: [[102:14|He remembereth that we are dust|Recordatus est, quoniam pulvis sumus]], that is, he considers with loving-kindness [[102:14|that we are dust|quoniam pulvis sumus]], that is, formed, as to the body, of the slime of the earth, and to be dissolved into dust, as Scripture says: [[Gen 2:7|the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth|Formavit Dominus Deus hominem de limo terræ]]; and: [[Gen 3:19|dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return|Pulvis es, et in pulverem reverteris]].

paras.t: Homo sicut fœnum dies ejus : quia tam cito arescit et decidit sicut fœnum, prout sanctus Job ait : Dies mei velocius transierunt, quam a texente tela succiditur. Tanquam flos agri, qui hodie est, et cras non reperitur, sic efflorebit, id est, a flore atque vigore primæ ætatis deficiet.
paras.en: [[102:15|Man's days are as grass|Homo sicut fœnum dies ejus]]: for he withers and falls as quickly as grass, as holy Job says: [[Job 7:6|My days have passed more swiftly than the web is cut by the weaver|Dies mei velocius transierunt, quam a texente tela succiditur]]. [[102:15|As the flower of the field|Tanquam flos agri]], which is today and tomorrow is not found, [[102:15|so shall he flourish|sic efflorebit]], that is, he shall fall away from the flower and vigour of his early years [*efflorebit* can mean "shall blossom" or "shall pass out of flower"; Denis takes it in the second sense].

paras.t: Quoniam spiritus, id est anima, pertransibit in illo, id est, temporalem durationem habebit in homine, qua finita, recedit ; et non subsistet homo in hac vita, anima ejus egressa. Hinc enim scriptum est : Breves dies hominis sunt, numerus mensium ejus apud te est ; constituisti terminos ejus, qui præteriri non poterunt. Et in libro Regum : Omnes morimur, et quasi aquæ dilabimur in terram, quæ non revertentur. Hæc autem nostri figmenti fragilitas incitat Deum ad miserendum nobis, quemadmodum in Genesi testatus est : Nequaquam ultra maledicam terræ propter homines. Sensus enim et cogitatio cordis humani, prona sunt in malum ab adolescentia sua. Et non cognoscet anima post separationem amplius locum suum, id est corpus quod reliquit, donec rursus induat illud. Defuncti namque non sciunt in particulari, quid agatur in vita præsenti, nisi ex speciali revelatione, vel propter specialem habitudinem ad ea quæ hic aguntur. Sic enim Sancti in patria in Verbo cognoscunt orationem qua invocantur, atque obsequium quo honorantur. Translatio Hieronymi talis est : Et non cognoscet eum ultra locus ejus. Utrumque autem veritatem sortitur, quia secundum Augustinum in libro de Cura pro mortuis, Sicut viventes in mundo ignorant quid agatur in receptaculis mortuorum, sic defuncti nesciunt quid agatur in locis viventium : quod intelligendum est de lege communi, et de cognitione determinata ac naturali. Unde Isaias ait : Tu, Domine, Pater noster ; et Abraham nescivit nos.
paras.en: [[102:16|For the spirit|Quoniam spiritus]], that is, the soul, [[102:16|shall pass in him|pertransibit in illo]], that is, it shall have a duration in time in man, and when that is ended it departs; [[102:16|and he shall not be|et non subsistet]]: man shall not continue in this life once his soul has gone forth. For hence it is written: [[Job 14:5|The days of man are short, and the number of his months is with thee: thou hast appointed his bounds which cannot be passed|Breves dies hominis sunt, numerus mensium ejus apud te est ; constituisti terminos ejus, qui præteriri non poterunt]]. And in the book of Kings: [[2 Kings 14:14|We all die, and like waters that return no more, we fall down into the earth|Omnes morimur, et quasi aquæ dilabimur in terram, quæ non revertentur]]. Now this frailty of our frame moves God to have mercy on us, as he testified in Genesis: [[Gen 8:21|I will no more curse the earth for the sake of man|Nequaquam ultra maledicam terræ propter homines]]: [[Gen 8:21|for the imagination and thought of man's heart are prone to evil from his youth|Sensus enim et cogitatio cordis humani, prona sunt in malum ab adolescentia sua]]. [[102:16|And he shall know|Et non cognoscet]] (the soul, after its separation) [[102:16|his place no more|amplius locum suum]], that is, the body it has left, until it puts it on again. For the dead do not know in particular what is done in this present life, except by a special revelation, or because of some special relation to the things that are done here. For it is thus that the Saints in the fatherland know in the Word the prayer by which they are invoked and the homage by which they are honoured. Jerome's translation runs thus: And his place shall know him no more. Both are true, for according to Augustine in the book On the Care to be Had for the Dead, as the living in the world do not know what is done in the abodes of the dead, so the dead do not know what is done in the places of the living: which is to be understood of the common law, and of determinate and natural knowledge. Hence Isaias says: [[Is 63:16|thou, O Lord, art our father|Tu, Domine, Pater noster]]; [[Is 63:16|and Abraham hath not known us|et Abraham nescivit nos]].

paras.t: Misericordia autem Domini ab æterno et usque in æternum, id est, sine defectu et termino, et a principio mundi usque in finem nunquam finiendum, expansa est, super timentes eum timore sancto ac filiali. Nunc enim adest eis indesinenter per gratiam, in futuro quoque per gloriam. Sed quum nec mundus ab æterno fuerit, neque peccatum, quomodo misericordia Domini est super timentes se ab æterno ? Et respondendum, quod dicitur ab æterno super eos fuisse, ratione prædestinationis seu præparationis, quemadmodum in Apocalypsi de Christo habetur : Agnus qui occisus est ab origine mundi. Et ad Timotheum : Gratia data est nobis in Christo Jesu ante tempora sæcularia, id est, dari prævisa est.
paras.en: [[102:17|But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity and unto eternity|Misericordia autem Domini ab æterno et usque in æternum]], that is, without failing or end, and from the beginning of the world to an end that shall never end, is spread out [[102:17|upon them that fear him|super timentes eum]] with a holy and filial fear. For now it is with them unceasingly by grace, and in the world to come by glory. But since neither the world nor sin was from eternity, how is the mercy of the Lord upon them that fear him from eternity? The answer is that it is said to have been upon them from eternity by reason of predestination or preparation, as is said of Christ in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 13:8|the Lamb which was slain from the beginning of the world|Agnus qui occisus est ab origine mundi]]. And to Timothy: [[2 Tim 1:9|grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the times of the world|Gratia data est nobis in Christo Jesu ante tempora sæcularia]], that is, it was foreseen that it would be given.

paras.t: Et justitia illius, id est effectus divinæ justitiæ, scilicet justa promissorum impletio et meritorum præmiatio, erit et est in filios filiorum, id est in omnes filios primorum parentum : quod de filiis justis intelligi debet. De quibus annectitur : his qui servant per fidem et obedientiam, testamentum ejus, id est legem divinitus datam.
paras.en: [[102:17|And his justice|Et justitia illius]], that is, the effect of the divine justice, namely the just fulfilment of promises and rewarding of merits, will be and is [[102:17|unto children's children|in filios filiorum]], that is, upon all the children of our first parents: which must be understood of the just children. Of them it is added: [[102:18|To such as keep|his qui servant]], by faith and obedience, [[102:18|his covenant|testamentum ejus]], that is, the law given by God.
