paras.t: Et memores sunt mandatorum ipsius, non qualitercumque, sed ad faciendum ea. Multi enim sunt memores mandatorum Domini, non ut ea adimpleant, sed ut alios doceant quod ipsi non agunt, quod est mortale peccatum ; vel ut docti appareant, quod gloria est vana. Debemus ergo memores esse legis divinæ et mandatorum Altissimi, non ut sciamus, sed ut impleamus. Unde etiam Aristoteles dicit : Quid est virtus, scrutamur, non ut agnoscamus, sed quatenus boni efficiamur. Alias computabimur in Pharisæorum atque Scribarum collegio, de quibus in Matthæo ait Salvator : Omnia quæcumque dixerint vobis, servate et facite ; secundum opera vero illorum nolite facere : dicunt enim et non faciunt. Alligant enim onera gravia et importabilia, et imponunt in humeros hominum ; digito autem suo nolunt ea movere.
paras.en: [[102:18|And are mindful of his commandments|Et memores sunt mandatorum ipsius]], not in any way whatever, but [[102:18|to do them|ad faciendum ea]]. For many are mindful of the commandments of the Lord, not to fulfil them, but to teach others what they themselves do not do, which is a mortal sin; or to appear learned, which is vainglory. We ought, then, to be mindful of the divine law and of the commandments of the Most High, not that we may know them, but that we may fulfil them. Hence Aristotle too says: We inquire what virtue is, not in order to know it, but that we may become good [*Nicomachean Ethics* II, 2]. Otherwise we shall be counted in the company of the Pharisees and Scribes, of whom the Saviour says in Matthew: [[Matt 23:3|All things therefore whatsoever they shall say to you, observe and do: but according to their works do ye not. For they say, and do not|Omnia quæcumque dixerint vobis, servate et facite ; secundum opera vero illorum nolite facere : dicunt enim et non faciunt]]. [[Matt 23:4|For they bind heavy and insupportable burdens and lay them on men's shoulders: but with a finger of their own they will not move them|Alligant enim onera gravia et importabilia, et imponunt in humeros hominum ; digito autem suo nolunt ea movere]].

paras.t: Dominus in cœlo paravit sedem suam. Hoc multipliciter accipi potest. Primo sic : Dominus Deus, Trinitas sancta, in cœlo empyreo paravit sedem suam, id est locum habitationis suæ. Nullus enim corporeus locus tam proprie competit Deo, ut cœlum empyreum. Propter quod Moyses ait : Habitaculum ejus sursum, et subter brachia sempiterna. Vel, In cœlo, id est in civibus regni cœlestis, et maxime in angelis pertinentibus ad infimum ordinem primæ hierarchiæ, qui propter inhabitationem divinam, Throni (id est sedes) Dei vocati sunt. Vel, In cœlo, id est in quolibet homine cœlestem conversationem in terra habente. In tali namque per gratiam demoratur, juxta illud : In eo quasi in thalamo tota die morabitur. Vel : Dominus Christus, homo Deus, in cœlo empyreo paravit a principio mundi sedem suam, id est stabilem mansionem tam sibi, quam suis : quibus ait, Vado parare vobis locum. A principio namque mundi paravit hanc sedem per creationem ; sed post ascensionem suam paravit eam suis per interpellationem, quia secundum Apostolum, Jesus introiit in ipsum cœlum, ut appareat nunc vultui Dei pro nobis. Et regnum ipsius, id est regimen seu regia Christi potestas, omnibus dominabitur. Omnia enim subjecta sunt pedibus ejus, secundum Apostolum. Propter quod scriptum est : Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei. Et in Apocalypsi : Agnus vincet illos, quoniam Dominus dominorum est et Rex regum.
paras.en: [[102:19|The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven|Dominus in cœlo paravit sedem suam]] [*sedes*, "seat" or "throne"]. This can be taken in many ways. First thus: the Lord God, the Holy Trinity, [[102:19|hath prepared his throne|paravit sedem suam]] in the empyrean heaven [the highest heaven, the dwelling of the blessed], that is, the place of his dwelling. For no bodily place belongs so properly to God as the empyrean heaven. Wherefore Moses says: [[Deut 33:27|His dwelling is above, and underneath are the everlasting arms|Habitaculum ejus sursum, et subter brachia sempiterna]]. Or, [[102:19|in heaven|In cœlo]], that is, in the citizens of the heavenly kingdom, and above all in the angels of the lowest order of the first hierarchy, who because of the divine indwelling are called the Thrones (that is, the seats) of God. Or, [[102:19|in heaven|In cœlo]], that is, in any man who has his conversation in heaven while on earth. For in such a one he dwells by grace, according to that saying: [[Deut 33:12|in him: as in a bride chamber shall he abide all the day long|In eo quasi in thalamo tota die morabitur]]. Or: [[102:19|The Lord|Dominus]] Christ, God made man, [[102:19|hath prepared|paravit]] [[102:19|in heaven|in cœlo]], the empyrean, from the beginning of the world, [[102:19|his throne|sedem suam]], that is, a lasting abode both for himself and for his own, to whom he says: [[John 14:2|I go to prepare a place for you|Vado parare vobis locum]]. For from the beginning of the world he prepared this seat by creation; but after his ascension he prepared it for his own by his intercession, since according to the Apostle, Jesus entered [[Heb 9:24|into Heaven itself, that he may appear now in the presence of God for us|in ipsum cœlum, ut appareat nunc vultui Dei pro nobis]]. [[102:19|And his kingdom|Et regnum ipsius]], that is, the rule or royal power of Christ, [[102:19|shall rule over all|omnibus dominabitur]]. For all things are subject under his feet, according to the Apostle[[Heb 2:8||]]. Wherefore it is written: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]]. And in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 17:14|the Lamb shall overcome them because he is Lord of lords and King of kings|Agnus vincet illos, quoniam Dominus dominorum est et Rex regum]].

paras.t: Deinde invitantur creaturæ cœlestes, angelicæ mentes, supermundani intellectus, et animi deiformes ad laudem divinam. Benedicite Domino, angeli ejus, id est nuntii Dei, potentes virtute, id est potestate præcipui, facientes verbum illius, id est, commissionem seu jussionem vobis divinitus factam implentes, ad audiendam vocem sermonum ejus, id est, ut homines audiant per vestram exsecutionem, quid Deus eis mandat et nuntiat. Per angelos namque Deus nobis revelat beneplacitum suum. Quamvis autem per angelos accipi possint angelici spiritus infimi ordinis, quorum est minima nuntiare, secundum Gregorium ; nihilo minus per angelos intelligere possumus omnes spiritus cœlestes, de quibus ait Apostolus, Omnes sunt administratorii spiritus : nam, secundum magni Dionysii dogma, omnes angelicæ mentes, angeli appellantur. Porro potentia angelorum duplex est : scilicet naturalis ; et ista omnem corporalium rerum potestatem vehementer excedit, in tantum ut de diabolo scriptum sit, Non est super terram potestas quæ comparetur ei. Naturalia enim in angelis apostatis integra permanserunt, secundum Dionysium capitulo 4 de Divinis nominibus : et per hanc potestatem competit angelis motus cœlorum, secundum philosophos. Alia vero est potentia angelorum supernaturalis, quæ major et altior est : per quam angelus unus percussit una nocte omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, ut dicitur in Exodo ; et in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia, sicut in Isaia legitur. Hæc tamen angelus facere potuit naturali virtute, ut videtur.
paras.en: Next the heavenly creatures are invited to the praise of God: the angelic minds, the intellects above the world, and the godlike spirits. [[102:20|Bless the Lord|Benedicite Domino]], ye [[102:20|his angels|angeli ejus]], that is, messengers of God [*angelus* means "messenger"], [[102:20|you that are mighty in strength|potentes virtute]], that is, excelling in power, [[102:20|and execute his word|facientes verbum illius]], that is, fulfilling the charge or command given you by God, [[102:20|hearkening to the voice of his orders|ad audiendam vocem sermonum ejus]], that is, so that men may hear, through your carrying it out, what God commands and announces to them [Denis takes *ad audiendam vocem* as "so that the voice may be heard"]. For through the angels God reveals his good pleasure to us. And although by angels may be understood the angelic spirits of the lowest order, whose office is to announce the least things, according to Gregory, nevertheless by angels we can understand all the heavenly spirits, of whom the Apostle says, They are [[Heb 1:14|all ministering spirits|Omnes sunt administratorii spiritus]]: for according to the teaching of the great Dionysius, all the angelic minds are called angels. Further, the power of the angels is twofold. One is natural; and this far exceeds all the power of bodily things, so much so that it is written of the devil: [[Job 41:24|There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him|Non est super terram potestas quæ comparetur ei]]. For their natural gifts remained whole in the apostate angels, according to Dionysius, chapter 4 of On the Divine Names; and by this power the moving of the heavens belongs to the angels, according to the philosophers. The other power of the angels is supernatural, which is greater and higher: by it one angel in one night struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, as is said in Exodus[[Ex 12:29||]], and in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand, as we read in Isaias[[Is 37:36||]]. Yet an angel could have done these things by natural power, it seems.

paras.t: Benedicite Domino, omnes virtutes ejus. Per virtutes accipere possumus angelos pertinentes ad medium ordinem secundæ hierarchiæ, qui speciali nomine appellantur Virtutes, secundum Dionysium ; vel, universas mentes angelicas, quoniam omnes angeli vicissim appellantur Virtutes, propter efficacissimam excellentiam propriæ potestatis. Rabbi Moyses vero per virtutes intelligit naturales vires omnium rerum creatarum. Virtutes, inquam, ministri ejus, qui facitis voluntatem ejus, id est, qui divinæ voluntatis imperio obeditis.
paras.en: [[102:21|Bless the Lord, all ye his hosts|Benedicite Domino, omnes virtutes ejus]] [*virtutes*, "powers", rendered "hosts" in the Douay-Rheims; Denis takes it of the Virtues, an order of angels]. By *virtutes* we may understand the angels of the middle order of the second hierarchy, who are called by the special name of Virtues, according to Dionysius; or all the angelic minds, since all angels are in their turn called Virtues, because of the most effective excellence of their own power. Rabbi Moses [Moses Maimonides], however, understands by *virtutes* the natural powers of all created things. Virtues, I say, [[102:21|you ministers of his that do his will|ministri ejus, qui facitis voluntatem ejus]], that is, who obey the command of the divine will.

paras.t: Benedicite Domino, omnia opera ejus, id est creaturæ universæ, in omni loco dominationis ejus, id est in cœlo ac terra atque intermediis locis. Ubique enim dominatur Creator. Christo quoque data est omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra. Propter quod scriptum est : Domine, Rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita ; tu dominaris omnium. Irrationales autem creaturæ benedicunt et laudant Deum materialiter, quia contemplantibus præbent materiam benedicendi Domino, eo quod in ipsis sapientia, potentia, et bonitas Creatoris resplendeant. Sed quia nil prodest alios exhortari, et proprias exhortationes omittere, prout ait Salvator, Quid prodest homini si mundum universum lucretur, animæ vero suæ detrimentum patiatur ? idcirco revertitur ad se ipsum, dicitque : Benedic, anima mea, Domino : secundum intellectum expositum.
paras.en: [[102:22|Bless the Lord, all his works|Benedicite Domino, omnia opera ejus]], that is, all creatures, [[102:22|in every place of his dominion|in omni loco dominationis ejus]], that is, in heaven and on earth and in the places between. For the Creator has dominion everywhere. To Christ, too, has been given all power in heaven and in earth[[Matt 28:18||]]. Wherefore it is written: O Lord, [[Esth 13:9|almighty king, for all things are in thy power|Rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita]]; [[Esth 13:11|Thou art Lord of all|tu dominaris omnium]]. Now irrational creatures bless and praise God materially, since they furnish those who contemplate them with matter for blessing the Lord, because the wisdom, power and goodness of the Creator shine forth in them. But because it profits nothing to exhort others and to leave off exhorting oneself, as the Saviour says, [[Matt 16:26|what doth it profit a man, if he gain the whole world and suffer the loss of his own soul?|Quid prodest homini si mundum universum lucretur, animæ vero suæ detrimentum patiatur]] therefore he turns back to himself and says: [[102:22|O my soul, bless thou the Lord|Benedic, anima mea, Domino]], in the sense explained above.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum omni laude dignissimum, omni consolatione ac suavitate plenissimum, et nobis peccatoribus ad pœnitentiam sanctam conversis præcipue frequentandum, dulcem ac saporosum audivimus : quem decantando, decet nos ex commemoratione divinorum beneficiorum amore Dei nostri vehementer accendi, in ejus laude cordialiter delectari. Et ut digni inveniamur laudatores, studeamus Christo mundo corde servire, omnia carnalia, sæcularia, temporalia ac vana contemnere, et unum illud, quod solum necessarium est, corde collecto ac stabili contemplari, exquirere, amare, ac honorare tanto intentius atque frequentius, quanto plura ab eo beneficia sumpsimus. Ideo namque in Luca asserit Christus : Cui multum donatum est, multum quæretur ab eo.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm most worthy of all praise, most full of all consolation and sweetness, sweet and savoury, and one to be used especially often by us sinners who have turned to holy penance: in singing it, it befits us to be vehemently kindled with the love of our God by calling to mind his divine benefits, and to delight with all our heart in his praise. And that we may be found worthy to praise him, let us strive to serve Christ with a clean heart, to despise all things carnal, worldly, temporal and vain, and with a recollected and steadfast heart to contemplate, seek, love and honour that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]], so much the more intently and often as we have received the more benefits from him. For this is why Christ declares in Luke: [[Luke 12:48|unto whomsoever much is given, of him much shall be required|Cui multum donatum est, multum quæretur ab eo]].

paras.t: Precatio. Deus salvator viventium, qui non vis mortem peccantium, tu, pie Pater, cognosce figmentum nostrum, et peccatoribus nobis non irascaris in perpetuum ; sed corrobora super nos misericordiam tuam, et redime de æterno interitu vitam nostram.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, Saviour of the living, who willest not the death of sinners, do thou, loving Father, know our frame, and be not angry with us sinners for ever; but strengthen thy mercy over us, and redeem our life from eternal destruction.

103.title: EXPLANATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI TERTII : BENEDIC, ANIMA MEA, DOMINO; DOMINE DEUS MEUS.
103.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and third psalm: Bless the Lord, O my soul: O Lord my God.

paras.t: Brevis autem et planus titulus est psalmi præsentis dum dicitur : Psalmus David. Loquitur vero Propheta in psalmo isto in persona hominis Deum grata mente laudantis.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is short and plain, where it says: [[103:1|For David himself|Psalmus David]] [Denis's text reads *Psalmus David*, "A psalm of David"]. The Prophet speaks in this psalm in the person of a man praising God with a grateful mind.

paras.t: Benedic, anima mea, Domino. Quod qualiter intelligi implerique debeat, in præcedentis psalmi expositione ad longum tractatum est. Domine Deus meus, magnificatus es vehementer : id est, ex operibus tuis mirabilibus in nobis valde magnus effectus es, ita ut excellentia, magnitudo, seu majestas tua nobis clare innotuerit ex consideratione operum tuorum, quamvis tu in te ipso omnino immutabilis et summe perfectus sis.
paras.en: [[103:1|Bless the Lord, O my soul|Benedic, anima mea, Domino]]. How this is to be understood and fulfilled has been treated at length in the exposition of the preceding psalm. [[103:1|O Lord my God, thou art exceedingly great|Domine Deus meus, magnificatus es vehementer]]: that is, by thy wonderful works among us thou hast become very great, so that thy excellence, greatness or majesty has become clearly known to us from the consideration of thy works, although in thyself thou art wholly unchangeable[[Num 23:19||]][[Mal 3:6||]] and supremely perfect.

paras.t: Confessionem et decorem induisti : id est, laude Sanctorum et specioso famulatu eorum circumdatus es, sicut homo circumdatur veste, quia ex omni parte concurrunt ad te omnes Beati. Vel, Decorem induisti, id est, ita in te ipso pulcher, imo pulcherrimus es, ac si pulchritudo esset vestis tua, te undique ornans. Amictus lumine sicut vestimento : id est, sic in te ipso clarus ac fulgidus es, ac si lux esset tibi vestimentum, te omnino operiens, ita quod nihil tenebrositatis in te invenitur : juxta illud, Deus lux est, et tenebræ non sunt in eo ullæ. — Hæc autem de Christo specialiter accipi possunt. Indutus est enim confessionem, quemadmodum ad Philippenses dicit Apostolus : Omnis lingua confiteatur, quia Dominus Jesus Christus in gloria est Dei Patris. Ubique enim electi Christo confitentur. Est quoque indutus decorem, præsertim in resurrectione, quando in forma gloriosa surrexit, cui in passione non erat decor aut species. Surrexit etiam in corpore glorificato, cujus claritas solis splendorem incomparabiliter inæstimabiliterque transcendit : propterea dicitur, Amictus lumine sicut vestimento.
paras.en: [[103:1|Thou hast put on praise and beauty|Confessionem et decorem induisti]] [*confessio*, here "praise", is also "confession" or "acknowledgment"]: that is, thou art surrounded by the praise of the Saints and by their comely service, as a man is surrounded by his garment, for all the Blessed flock to thee from every side. Or, thou hast put on [[103:1|beauty|decorem induisti]]: that is, thou art so beautiful in thyself, nay most beautiful, as if beauty were thy garment, adorning thee on every side. [[103:2|And art clothed with light as with a garment|Amictus lumine sicut vestimento]]: that is, thou art so bright and shining in thyself, as if light were thy garment, covering thee wholly, so that no darkness is found in thee: according to that saying, [[1 John 1:5|God is light and in him there is no darkness|Deus lux est, et tenebræ non sunt in eo ullæ]]. These things can also be taken specially of Christ. For he has put on *confession*, as the Apostle says to the Philippians: [[Phil 2:11|every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father|Omnis lingua confiteatur, quia Dominus Jesus Christus in gloria est Dei Patris]]; for everywhere the elect confess Christ. He has put on beauty too, above all in the resurrection, when he rose in glorious form, he who in his passion had no beauty nor comeliness. He rose, moreover, in a glorified body, whose brightness surpasses the splendour of the sun beyond all comparison and reckoning: therefore it is said, [[103:2|And art clothed with light as with a garment|Amictus lumine sicut vestimento]].

paras.t: Extendens cœlum stellatum seu firmamentum sicut pellem : quia per modum pellis extentæ videtur expansum, quum sit sphæricum, terram tegens atque operiens, et nostrum hemisphærium per modum tentorii circumcludens. Unde Isaias dicit : Extendit velut nihilum cœlos, et expandit illos sicut tabernaculum ad inhabitandum. Qui tegis aquis superiora ejus, id est partes convexas cœli stellati. Scriptum est enim in Genesi : Dixit Deus, Fiat firmamentum in medio aquarum, et dividat aquas ab aquis. Fecitque Deus firmamentum, divisitque aquas quæ erant sub firmamento, ab his quæ erant super firmamentum. Quidam ergo litteram prædictam sequentes, dicunt supra firmamentum esse aquas per modum glaciei congelatas, et cœlum tegentes. Alii vero magis philosophice loquentes, dicunt per aquas has intelligendum esse nonam sphæram, quæ dicitur cœlum crystallinum seu aqueum, sicut cœlum immobile appellatur empyreum, id est igneum : non quasi nona sphæra sit de natura aquæ, vel cœlum empyreum de natura ignis; sed quia cœlum crystallinum cum aqua in diaphaneitate convenit : nam per modum aquæ congelatæ apparet. Cœlum vero empyreum cum igne in claritate communicat. Huic quoque quod nunc ait, Qui tegis aquis superiora ejus, concordat illud Danielis, Benedicite, aquæ omnes quæ super cœlos sunt, Domino. Basilius autem per cœlum hoc loco, et cœlos de quibus Daniel loquitur, atque per firmamentum, de quo in Geneseos libro fit sermo, intelligit cœlum aerium, supra quod nubes feruntur. Et hanc expositionem asserit Augustinus laude dignissimam.
paras.en: [[103:2|Who stretchest out the heaven|Extendens cœlum]], the starry heaven or firmament, [[103:2|like a pavilion|sicut pellem]] [*pellis*, a skin or hide, such as tents were made of]: for it is seen spread out like a stretched skin, though it is spherical, covering and overspreading the earth and enclosing our hemisphere like a tent. Hence Isaias says: He [[Is 40:22|stretcheth out the heavens as nothing, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in|Extendit velut nihilum cœlos, et expandit illos sicut tabernaculum ad inhabitandum]]. [[103:3|Who coverest the higher rooms thereof with water|Qui tegis aquis superiora ejus]], that is, the convex parts of the starry heaven. For it is written in Genesis: [[Gen 1:6|God said: Let there be a firmament made amidst the waters: and let it divide the waters from the waters|Dixit Deus, Fiat firmamentum in medio aquarum, et dividat aquas ab aquis]]. [[Gen 1:7|And God made a firmament, and divided the waters that were under the firmament, from those that were above the firmament|Fecitque Deus firmamentum, divisitque aquas quæ erant sub firmamento, ab his quæ erant super firmamentum]]. Some, then, following the letter just quoted, say that above the firmament there are waters frozen like ice, covering the heaven. Others, speaking more philosophically, say that by these waters is to be understood the ninth sphere, which is called the crystalline or watery heaven, just as the motionless heaven is called the empyrean, that is, the fiery: not as though the ninth sphere were of the nature of water, or the empyrean heaven of the nature of fire, but because the crystalline heaven agrees with water in transparency (for it looks like frozen water), while the empyrean heaven shares brightness with fire. With what is said here, [[103:3|Who coverest the higher rooms thereof with water|Qui tegis aquis superiora ejus]], that saying of Daniel also agrees: [[Dan 3:60|O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord|Benedicite, aquæ omnes quæ super cœlos sunt, Domino]]. But Basil understands by the heaven in this place, and by the heavens of which Daniel speaks, and by the firmament spoken of in the book of Genesis[[Gen 1:6||]][[Gen 1:7||]], the airy heaven, above which the clouds are borne. And Augustine declares this exposition most worthy of praise.

paras.t: Mystice per cœlum designatur Ecclesia, quæ in Canticis canticorum propter pressuram et tribulationem dicit : Nigra sum, sed formosa, sicut pelles Salomonis, id est cœlum, quod est pellis veri Salomonis, scilicet Christi. Extendit ergo Christus cœlum, id est Ecclesiam, sicut pellem, dum eam per omnes partes mundi diffundit, et ad divinorum sublimia per contemplationem exaltat. Hujus autem cœli superiora, id est Apostolos atque Prophetas et efficaces imitatores ipsorum, tegit aquis scientiæ salutaris et gratiæ, seu donis Spiritus Sancti, quemadmodum testatur Salvator : Qui credit in me, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ.
paras.en: Mystically, by the heaven is signified the Church, which in the Canticle of Canticles, because of oppression and tribulation, says: [[Cant 1:4|I am black but beautiful|Nigra sum, sed formosa]], [[Cant 1:4|as the curtains of Solomon|sicut pelles Salomonis]] [*pelles*, "skins", the word used of the heaven in this verse], that is, the heaven, which is the skin of the true Solomon, namely Christ. Christ therefore stretches out the heaven, that is, the Church, like a skin, when he spreads her through all parts of the world and raises her by contemplation to the heights of divine things. And the higher parts of this heaven, that is, the Apostles and Prophets and those who truly imitate them, he covers with the waters of saving knowledge and of grace, or with the gifts of the Holy Ghost, as the Saviour testifies: [[John 7:38|He that believeth in me|Qui credit in me]], [[John 7:38|Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water|flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ]].

paras.t: Qui ponis nubem ascensum tuum, id est, qui efficis ut nubes materialis sit res tua jussione ascendens. Divino enim imperio agitur, ut ex vaporibus nubes generentur, ac sursum feruntur. Unde de Deo scriptum est apud Prophetam : Qui vocat aquas, et effundit eas super faciem terræ; et in Deuteronomio, Magnificentia ejus discurrunt nubes. Qui ambulas super pennas ventorum, id est, qui in operatione tua procedis velocius, quam venti discurrant. Velocitas quippe venti in motu, per pennas significatur. Dominus autem in instanti agit quodcumque voluerit, quum sit virtutis simpliciter infinitæ. Idcirco agit velocius quam venti feruntur. In Job autem vicesimo secundo capite, dicitur Dominus circa cardines cœli perambulare; et alibi de eo legitur, Qui graditur super fluctus maris; et in Deuteronomio legitur, Ascensor cœli auxiliator tuus. Nunc vero super pennas ventorum ambulare censetur. Sed omnium horum est similis sensus. Ambulatio enim Dei est operatio ejus, quemadmodum in Exodo Moyses ait ad Dominum : In quo poterimus scire invenisse nos gratiam in conspectu tuo, nisi ambulaveris nobiscum? Dominus autem propter operationem omnipotentiæ suæ, quam circa cœlos et mare ostendit, ambulare super ea asseritur. Ad litteram quoque exponi hæc possunt de Christo, qui posuit nubem ascensum suum, ambulavitque super pennas ventorum, quando, ut in Actis habetur, Videntibus illis elevatus est, et nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum.
paras.en: [[103:3|Who makest the clouds thy chariot|Qui ponis nubem ascensum tuum]] [literally "who makest the cloud thy ascent"], that is, who bringest it about that the material cloud is a thing that rises at thy command. For it is by God's command that clouds are formed from vapours and are borne upward. Hence it is written of God in the Prophet: [[Amos 9:6|who calleth the waters|Qui vocat aquas]], [[Amos 9:6|and poureth them out upon the face of the earth|et effundit eas super faciem terræ]]; and in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 33:26|By his magnificence the clouds run hither and thither|Magnificentia ejus discurrunt nubes]] [the margin gives Deut. xxxii, 26; the words are in Deut 33:26]. [[103:3|who walkest upon the wings of the winds|Qui ambulas super pennas ventorum]], that is, who goest forth in thy working more swiftly than the winds run. For the swiftness of the wind in its motion is signified by wings. But the Lord does in an instant whatever he wills, since his power is simply infinite; therefore he acts more swiftly than the winds are borne. In the twenty-second chapter of Job it is said of the Lord that [[Job 22:14|he walketh about the poles of heaven|circa cardines cœli perambulare]]; and elsewhere we read of him that he [[Job 9:8|walketh upon the waves of the sea|Qui graditur super fluctus maris]]; and in Deuteronomy we read: [[Deut 33:26|he that is mounted upon the heaven is thy helper|Ascensor cœli auxiliator tuus]]. Here he is held to walk upon the wings of the winds. But all these have a like sense. For God's walking is his working, as Moses says to the Lord in Exodus: [[Ex 33:16|how shall we be able to know|In quo poterimus scire]] [[Ex 33:16|that we have found grace in thy sight, unless thou walk with us|invenisse nos gratiam in conspectu tuo, nisi ambulaveris nobiscum?]]? And the Lord is said to walk upon the heavens and the sea because of the working of his almighty power, which he shows about them. These words can also be expounded literally of Christ, who made a cloud his ascent and walked upon the wings of the winds when, as we have it in the Acts, [[Acts 1:9|while they looked on, he was raised up|Videntibus illis elevatus est]]: [[Acts 1:9|and a cloud received him out of their sight|et nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum]].

paras.t: Mystice ascendit Dominus supra nubem, dum per gratiam suam ascendit cor prædicatoris seu nuntiatoris verbi Dei. Ambulat etiam supra pennas ventorum, id est, operando excedit virtutes et contemplationem animarum sanctarum. Pennæ enim, virtutes seu contemplationes dicuntur, quibus animæ in cœlum vehuntur, quemadmodum Isaias dicit : Qui sperant in Domino assument pennas ut aquilæ. Venti vero sunt animæ, prout per Isaiam Dominus protestatur : Ego Dominus, dans flatum populo qui est super terram.
paras.en: Mystically, the Lord ascends upon a cloud when by his grace he ascends the heart of a preacher or herald of the word of God. He walks also upon the wings of the winds, that is, in his working he surpasses the virtues and the contemplation of holy souls. For virtues or contemplations are called wings, by which souls are carried up to heaven, as Isaias says: [[Is 40:31|they that hope in the Lord|Qui sperant in Domino]] [[Is 40:31|shall take wings as eagles|assument pennas ut aquilæ]]. And the winds are souls, as the Lord declares by Isaias: I the Lord, [[Is 42:5|that giveth breath to the people upon it|dans flatum populo qui est super terram]] [Denis reads *super terram*, "upon the earth"; *flatus*, "breath", is also a blowing of wind].

paras.t: Qui facis angelos tuos spiritus, id est, qui hoc operatus es, ut angeli sancti sint spirituales, non corporales substantiæ; vel, Facis ut spiritus seu spirituales substantiæ sint angeli, id est nuntii tui. Qui enim per creationem facti sunt spiritus, per jussionem et ordinationem divinam facti sunt angeli, id est, nuntii Dei. Spiritus enim est nomen naturæ; angelus autem, officii. Et ministros tuos ignem urentem : id est, servientes tibi zelo ac tanto Divinitatis amore inflammas, ut dici possint ignis urens seu flamma ignis. Nam et Deus (secundum Apostolum) ignis consumens est. Et Daniel scriptum reliquit : Antiquus dierum sedit; thronus ejus flammæ ignis, rotæ ejus ignis accensus. Quid autem per thronum et rotas Dei æterni, nisi angelicas, deiformes, atque deiferas mentes, accipimus? Vel, Facis ignem urentem, id est summam hierarchiam seu angelos de ordine Seraphim, qui summe et ardentissime divino flagrant amore, ministros tuos, quia per eos illuminas alios. Ipsique mitti dicuntur, dum missi ab eis, veniunt ad nos. Propter quod Isaias : Volavit (inquit) ad me unus de Seraphim. Vel dicuntur ministri Dei seu angeli sancti fieri ignis urens, quia frequenter in specie ignis apparuerunt. Unde Matthæus de angelo dicit : Erat adspectus ejus sicut fulgur. Et in Exodo scribitur apparuisse angelus Moysi in rubo ardenti. Elias quoque in curru igneo est translatus ministerio angelorum.
paras.en: [[103:4|Who makest thy angels spirits|Qui facis angelos tuos spiritus]]: that is, who hast wrought this, that the holy angels are spiritual and not bodily substances; or, thou makest spirits, that is, spiritual substances, to be angels, that is, thy messengers. For those who by creation were made spirits were by God's command and ordinance made angels, that is, messengers of God: *spirit* is the name of their nature, *angel* the name of their office. [[103:4|and thy ministers a burning fire|Et ministros tuos ignem urentem]]: that is, thou dost so inflame those who serve thee with zeal and with so great a love of the Godhead that they may be called a burning fire or a flame of fire. For God too, according to the Apostle, is [[Heb 12:29|a consuming fire|ignis consumens]]. And Daniel left in writing: [[Dan 7:9|the ancient of days sat|Antiquus dierum sedit]]: [[Dan 7:9|his throne like flames of fire: the wheels of it like a burning fire|thronus ejus flammæ ignis, rotæ ejus ignis accensus]]. And what do we understand by the throne and wheels of the eternal God but the angelic minds, made like God and bearing God? Or, thou makest *a burning fire*, that is, the highest hierarchy, the angels of the order of the Seraphim, who burn most highly and most ardently with divine love, to be *thy ministers*, since through them thou enlightenest the others. And they are said to be sent when those sent by them come to us. Hence Isaias: [[Is 6:6|one of the seraphims flew|Volavit]], he says, [[Is 6:6|to me|ad me unus de Seraphim]]. Or the ministers of God, the holy angels, are said to become a burning fire because they have often appeared in the form of fire. Hence Matthew says of the angel: [[Matt 28:3|his countenance was as lightning|Erat adspectus ejus sicut fulgur]] [the margin gives Matt. xvii, 2; the words are Matt 28:3]. And in Exodus it is written that an angel appeared to Moses in a burning bush[[Ex 3:2||]]. Elias too was carried away in a fiery chariot by the ministry of angels[[4 Kings 2:11||]].

paras.t: In hominibus insuper facit Deus angelos suos spiritus, dum per religiosos atque devotos aliis nuntiat verbum salutis : et ministros suos ignem urentem, quando per exhortationem, increpationem, […] mationem prædicatorum seu corda audientium ignis Spiritus Sanctus succendit.
paras.en: Among men, moreover, God makes his angels spirits when through religious and devout persons he announces the word of salvation to others; and his ministers a burning fire when, through the exhortation, rebuke and […] of preachers, the fire, the Holy Ghost, kindles the hearts of the hearers.

paras.t: Qui fundasti, id est, firmiter collocasti, terram super stabilitatem suam, id est super immobilem basim suam. Videlicet omnes partes terræ naturaliter tendunt ad centrum ipsius : quoniam omnes partes terræ naturaliter tendunt ad centrum, secundum Philosophum : non inclinabitur in sæculum sæculi, id est nunquam mutabit locum quoad se totam, quemadmodum Ecclesiastes testatur : Terra in æternum stat. Unde et Baruch ait : Fundasti terram in sempiterno tempore. — Spiritualiter, fundavit Deus terram, id est Ecclesiam militantem, super stabilitatem suam, id est super Christum, tanquam super immobile fundamentum, in quo omnes fideles fundari et tendere ac quiescere debent. Non inclinabitur, etc., id est, Ecclesia numquam a fide inclinabitur, nunquam in toto abibit.
paras.en: [[103:5|Who hast founded|Qui fundasti]], that is, hast firmly set, [[103:5|the earth upon its own bases|terram super stabilitatem suam]] [literally "upon its own stability"], that is, upon its immovable base. For all the parts of the earth naturally tend to its centre: since, according to the Philosopher, all the parts of the earth naturally tend to the centre. [[103:5|it shall not be moved for ever and ever|non inclinabitur in sæculum sæculi]]: that is, it will never change its place as a whole, as Ecclesiastes testifies: [[Eccles 1:4|the earth standeth for ever|Terra in æternum stat]]. Hence Baruch too says: [[Bar 3:32|he that prepared the earth for evermore|Fundasti terram in sempiterno tempore]] [Denis reads *Fundasti terram in sempiterno tempore*, "Thou hast founded the earth for all time"]. Spiritually, God has founded the earth, that is, the Church militant, upon its own stability, that is, upon Christ, as upon an immovable foundation, on which all the faithful ought to be founded, and to which they ought to tend and in which to rest. [[103:5|it shall not be moved|non inclinabitur]], etc.: that is, the Church will never be bent away from the faith, never depart from it as a whole.

paras.t: Abyssus sicut vestimentum amictus ejus : id est, mare Oceanum. Quod operitur ab omni parte immensurabilem suam profunditatem, ideo dicitur abyssus, ex omni parte cingit et velut amictus infra terram, sicut vestimentum circumdat hominem, quod operit terram, et in Genesi dicitur : Abyssus operuit illud sicut vestimentum. Quemadmodum enim vestimentum circumdat et operit hominem, sic mare circumdat et operit terram, nisi quod una pars terræ, ex divina dispositione, manet discooperta propter animalium vitam salvandam. Super montes stabunt aquæ pluviales, in nubibus colligatæ. Nubes enim montibus altiores sunt, et in nubibus aquæ servantur, prout in libro Job de Deo scriptum est : Qui ligat aquas in nubibus, ut non erumpant pariter deorsum. Vel, Super montes stabunt aquæ, id est, cacumina montium ascendent Deo jubente, dum ei placuerit, sicut in universali diluvio semel factum cognovimus, atque in particularibus diluviis sæpe contingit.
paras.en: [[103:6|The deep like a garment is its clothing|Abyssus sicut vestimentum amictus ejus]]: that is, the Ocean sea, which, because of its immeasurable depth, is called the deep; on every side it girds the earth and is as it were its clothing, as a garment surrounds a man, for it covers the earth [the Latin of this sentence is disordered in the print; this is its evident sense]; and in Genesis it is said: The deep covered it as a garment [no such words stand in Genesis; they are close to Jerome's version of this verse from the Hebrew]. For as a garment surrounds and covers a man, so the sea surrounds and covers the earth, except that one part of the earth, by divine disposition, remains uncovered to preserve the life of living things. [[103:6|above the mountains shall the waters stand|Super montes stabunt aquæ]]: the rain waters, bound up in the clouds. For the clouds are higher than the mountains, and in the clouds the waters are kept, as is written of God in the book of Job: [[Job 26:8|He bindeth up the waters in his clouds, so that they break not out and fall down together|Qui ligat aquas in nubibus, ut non erumpant pariter deorsum]]. Or, [[103:6|above the mountains shall the waters stand|Super montes stabunt aquæ]], that is, they will rise over the tops of the mountains at God's command, when it pleases him, as we know was done once in the universal flood[[Gen 7:19||]][[Gen 7:20||]], and as often happens in particular floods.

paras.t: Vel, Super montes stabunt aquæ, quoniam aquæ in medio Oceani altiores sunt montibus terræ. Hoc Nicolaus de Lyra refert hoc loco asserere Rabbi Salomonem, et dicit eum falsum dicere. Sed utique Rabbi Salomon in hoc verum asserit, et ideo ratio ipsius Lyræ non procedit, dum ait : Aquæ quum sint graves et fluidæ, æqualiter tendunt ad centrum, et non sunt altiores in medio quam in ripa. Primo destruitur hoc ita : quoniam aqua est corpus homogeneum, id est, ejusdem naturæ in se et in partibus suis. Propterea, sicut quælibet pars aquæ, videlicet gutta, tendit ad rotunditatem, ut patet ad sensum de guttis ; sic tota aqua, quantum potest, ad rotunditatem seu sphæricam tendit figuram. Demum terra est gravior aqua : non tamen partes terræ æqualiter propinquant ad centrum, sed terra in medio sui altior exstat quam alibi : et multo magis aqua. Insuper constat ad sensum stantibus juxta ripam, quod quanto navis in mari longius abscedit, tanto videtur altius sublimari : et illud omnes magni philosophi contestantur.
paras.en: Or, [[103:6|above the mountains shall the waters stand|Super montes stabunt aquæ]], because the waters in the middle of the Ocean are higher than the mountains of the earth. Nicholas of Lyra, on this place, reports that Rabbi Salomon [that is, Rashi, the Jewish commentator] asserts this, and says that he speaks falsely. But Rabbi Salomon certainly speaks the truth in this, and so Lyra's own argument does not hold, when he says: Waters, being heavy and fluid, tend equally to the centre, and are not higher in the middle than at the shore. This is refuted, first, thus: water is a homogeneous body, that is, of the same nature in itself and in its parts. Therefore, just as any part of water, a drop for instance, tends to roundness, as is plain to the senses in the case of drops, so the whole of the water, as far as it can, tends to roundness, that is, to a spherical shape. Next, earth is heavier than water; yet the parts of the earth do not come equally near to the centre, but the earth stands higher in its middle than elsewhere: and much more so water. Moreover, it is plain to the senses of those standing by the shore that the farther a ship goes out to sea, the higher it seems to be raised; and all the great philosophers bear witness to this.

paras.t: Spiritualiter per abyssum intelligitur inundatio tribulationum. Abyssus ergo, id est tribulatio copiosa, est amictus terræ, id est Ecclesiæ, quoniam undique tribulatur Ecclesia, et circumdatur adversis velut amictu, quia per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare regnum cœlorum : id quod in Actibus Pauli sententia docet. Propter quod et Judith contestata est : Omnes qui Deo placuerunt, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles. Sed et super montes, id est perfectos viros, stabunt aquæ tribulationum, quia omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur. Stabunt quoque interdum super hos montes aquæ consolationum divinarum, quoniam juxta Apostolum, sicut pro Christo abundant passiones nostræ, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra. Propter quod alias dicitur de Deo : Quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis.
paras.en: Spiritually, by the deep is understood a flood of tribulations. The deep, then, that is, abundant tribulation, is the clothing of the earth, that is, of the Church, since the Church is afflicted on every side and is surrounded by adversities as by a garment, because [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom|per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare regnum]] of heaven [Denis reads *regnum cœlorum*; the Vulgate has *regnum Dei*, "of God"], as the saying of Paul in the Acts teaches. Hence Judith too bore witness: [[Jdt 8:23|all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|Omnes qui Deo placuerunt, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]]. And above the mountains, that is, perfect men, the waters of tribulations shall stand, for [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ|omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo]] [[2 Tim 3:12|shall suffer persecution|persecutionem patientur]]. Sometimes too the waters of divine consolations will stand upon these mountains, since according to the Apostle, as our sufferings abound for Christ, [[2 Cor 1:5|so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]]. Hence it is said of God elsewhere: [[Hab 3:2|when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy|Quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis]].

paras.t: Ab increpatione tua, id est a te per modum increpantis jubente, fugient aquæ a montibus quos operuerunt ; vel, a loco aeris in quo nubes ante fuerunt ; a voce tonitrui tui, id est a præcepto tuo terribili, formidabunt, id est, per modum formidantis se habebunt, obediendo tuo imperio. Hinc enim Job inquit : In fortitudine illius repente maria congregata sunt. Et Ecclesiasticus : Abyssus et terra et omnia quæ in eis sunt, in conspectu Dei commovebuntur ; et quum conspexerit ea Deus, tremore concutientur. Mystice autem aquæ tribulationum, Deo impios increpante, ab Ecclesia fugiunt atque deficiunt, juxta illud : Deo concedente pacem, quis est qui condemnet ?
paras.en: [[103:7|At thy rebuke|Ab increpatione tua]], that is, at thy commanding in the manner of one who rebukes, [[103:7|they shall flee|fugient]], the waters, from the mountains which they covered; or, from the place in the air where the clouds were before; [[103:7|at the voice of thy thunder|a voce tonitrui tui]], that is, at thy terrible command, [[103:7|they shall fear|formidabunt]], that is, they will behave like one who fears, obeying thy command. Hence Job says: [[Job 26:12|By his power the seas are suddenly gathered together|In fortitudine illius repente maria congregata sunt]]. And Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 16:18|the deep, and all the earth, and the things that are in them, shall be moved in his sight|Abyssus et terra et omnia quæ in eis sunt, in conspectu Dei commovebuntur]]; [[Ecclus 16:19|when God shall look upon them, they shall be shaken with trembling|et quum conspexerit ea Deus, tremore concutientur]]. Mystically, the waters of tribulations, when God rebukes the wicked, flee from the Church and fail, according to that saying: [[Job 34:29|when he granteth peace, who is there that can condemn|Deo concedente pacem, quis est qui condemnet]]?

paras.t: Ascendunt montes et descendunt campi in locum quem fundasti eis : id est, una pars terræ montuosa est, aliaque campestris ; et tam montes quam valles tantum ascendunt seu descendunt, quantum tua sapientia eis præfixit. Spiritualiter montes ascendunt, dum homines virtuosi proficiunt ; et campi descendunt, dum inferiores eorum doctrinæ se ipsos humiliter subdunt : in locum quem fundasti eis, id est in congregationem Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[103:8|The mountains ascend, and the plains descend into the place which thou hast founded for them|Ascendunt montes et descendunt campi in locum quem fundasti eis]]: that is, one part of the earth is mountainous and another level; and both mountains and valleys rise or sink only so far as thy wisdom has fixed for them. Spiritually, the mountains ascend when virtuous men make progress, and the plains descend when those beneath them humbly submit themselves to their teaching: [[103:8|into the place which thou hast founded for them|in locum quem fundasti eis]], that is, into the congregation of the Church.

paras.t: Terminum posuisti aquis Oceani, quem non transgredientur, nec effluent ripas ; neque convertentur, exeundo alveum suum, operire terram animalium habitationi deputatam. Unde Salomon dicit : Certa lege et gyro vallabat abyssos. Job quoque inquit : Terminum circumdedit aquis, usque dum finiantur lux et tenebræ. Et in hoc relucet magna Dei potestas, ob quam metuendus est nimis. Propter quod ipse per Jeremiam locutus est : Audi, popule stulte. Me non timebitis qui posui terminum mari, præceptum sempiternum quod non præteribit?
paras.en: [[103:9|Thou hast set a bound|Terminum posuisti]] for the waters of the Ocean, [[103:9|which they shall not pass over|quem non transgredientur]], nor overflow their shores; [[103:9|neither shall they return|neque convertentur]], going out of their bed, [[103:9|to cover the earth|operire terram]] that is appointed for the dwelling of living things. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 8:27|with a certain law, and compass, he enclosed the depths|Certa lege et gyro vallabat abyssos]]. Job too says: [[Job 26:10|He hath set bounds about the waters, till light and darkness come to an end|Terminum circumdedit aquis, usque dum finiantur lux et tenebræ]]. And in this the great power of God shines out, for which he is greatly to be feared. Therefore he spoke himself by Jeremias: [[Jer 5:21|Hear, O foolish people|Audi, popule stulte]]. [[Jer 5:22|Will not you then fear me|Me non timebitis]], who have set [[Jer 5:22|a bound for the sea, an everlasting ordinance, which it shall not pass over|terminum mari, præceptum sempiternum quod non præteribit?]]?

paras.t: Hoc modo communiter exponitur iste versiculus. Sed quia in versu præcedenti non de aquis, sed de montibus mentio facta est, videtur de montibus posse exponi ; eritque sensus : Terminum posuisti montibus in latitudine et ceteris dimensionibus, quem non transgredientur, ut altius protendantur, seu latius extendantur ; neque convertentur operire terram, id est, cadendo non obruent loca habitationum et homines, nisi te volente, jubente, aut permittente (sicut et sæpius dictum est), prout in libro Job asseritur : Deus transtulit montes, et nescierunt hi quos subvertit.
paras.en: This is how this verse is commonly expounded. But since in the preceding verse mention was made not of waters but of mountains, it seems that it can be expounded of the mountains; and the sense will be: [[103:9|Thou hast set a bound|Terminum posuisti]] for the mountains in breadth and their other dimensions, [[103:9|which they shall not pass over|quem non transgredientur]], so as to stretch higher or extend wider; [[103:9|neither shall they return to cover the earth|neque convertentur operire terram]], that is, by falling they will not overwhelm the places where men dwell, and the men themselves, unless thou willest, commandest or permittest it (as has often been said), as is asserted in the book of Job: God, [[Job 9:5|Who hath removed mountains|transtulit montes]], [[Job 9:5|and they whom he overthrew in his wrath, knew it not|et nescierunt hi quos subvertit]] [Denis omits *in his wrath*].

paras.t: Spiritualiter terminum ponit Deus aquis tribulationum, et montibus elationis, dum non sinit electos tentari seu tribulari supra id quod possunt ferre, sed facit (sicut ait Apostolus) cum tentatione proventum, ut possint sustinere. Neque convertentur aquæ et montes hujusmodi operire terram, id est corda bonorum opprimere, exstinguendo in eis caritatem Dei ac proximi. Propter quod ait Scriptura : Aquæ multæ non poterunt exstinguere caritatem, nec flumina obruent eam.
paras.en: Spiritually, God sets a bound to the waters of tribulations and to the mountains of pride when he does not suffer the elect to be tempted or afflicted above that which they are able to bear, but makes, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 10:13|with temptation issue, that you may be able to bear it|cum tentatione proventum, ut possint sustinere]]. [[103:9|Neither shall they return|Neque convertentur]], such waters and mountains, [[103:9|to cover the earth|operire terram]], that is, to overwhelm the hearts of the good by quenching in them the love of God and of their neighbour. Therefore the Scripture says: [[Cant 8:7|Many waters cannot quench charity, neither can the floods drown it|Aquæ multæ non poterunt exstinguere caritatem, nec flumina obruent eam]].

paras.t: Qui emittis fontes in convallibus, id est, rivos aquarum ex fontibus in montibus ortis manantes, descendere facis ad loca humilia ; inter medium montium, id est inter montes pertransibunt aquæ, id est defluent, nec illic stabunt, sed in locis bassis quiescent. Aqua enim petit locum deorsum. Spiritualiter emittit Deus de cælo fontes, id est dona gratiæ, in convallibus, id est in humilibus mentibus. Inter medium montium pertransibunt aquæ, id est, inter superbos gratia non manebit, quemadmodum Jacobus inquit : Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam. Et Isaias : Omnis vallis exaltabitur, et omnis mons et collis humiliabitur.
paras.en: [[103:10|Thou sendest forth springs in the vales|Qui emittis fontes in convallibus]]: that is, thou makest the streams of water, flowing from springs that rise in the mountains, come down to low places; [[103:10|between the midst of the hills|inter medium montium]], that is, between the mountains, [[103:10|the waters shall pass|pertransibunt aquæ]], that is, shall flow down, and not stand there, but come to rest in low places; for water seeks the place below. Spiritually, God sends forth from heaven springs, that is, the gifts of grace, in the vales, that is, into humble minds. [[103:10|between the midst of the hills the waters shall pass|Inter medium montium pertransibunt aquæ]]: that is, among the proud grace will not remain, as James says: [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble|Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]]. And Isaias: [[Is 40:4|Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low|Omnis vallis exaltabitur, et omnis mons et collis humiliabitur]].

paras.t: Potabunt omnes bestiæ agri de aquis, ex fontibus ad loca bassa venientibus ; expectabunt onagri, id est asini feri, silvestres ac naturaliter calidi, in siti sua potari et refrigerari his aquis. Alii ita exponunt : Expectabunt onagri in siti sua, id est, pluviam cœlestem præstolabuntur. Non enim (ut asserunt hi) onagri bibunt de aqua ex fonte fluente, sed diu expectant pluviam de cœlo, quatenus inde bibant. Mystice de rivis aquarum Christi bibunt omnes bestiæ agri, id est omnes gentiles ad fidem conversi ; exspectabunt usque ad finem mundi, onagri, id est crudeles Judæi, in siti sua, id est in desiderio quo Christum exspectant venturum. Nempe in sua siti durabunt usque ad terminum sæculi : tunc enim convertentur ad Christum.
paras.en: [[103:11|All the beasts of the field shall drink|Potabunt omnes bestiæ agri]] of the waters coming from the springs to low places; [[103:11|the wild asses shall expect|expectabunt onagri]], that is, asses that are wild, living in the woods and naturally hot, [[103:11|in their thirst|in siti sua]], to be given drink and refreshed by these waters. Others expound it thus: [[103:11|the wild asses shall expect in their thirst|Expectabunt onagri in siti sua]], that is, they will wait for the rain from heaven. For (as these assert) wild asses do not drink water flowing from a spring, but wait long for rain from the sky, so as to drink of it. Mystically, all the beasts of the field, that is, all the Gentiles converted to the faith, drink of the streams of the waters of Christ; the wild asses, that is, the cruel Jews, will wait until the end of the world in their thirst, that is, in the longing with which they await Christ as one yet to come. For they will remain in their thirst until the end of the world: then indeed they will be converted to Christ.

paras.t: Super ea, scilicet in cacuminibus montium, et circa undas aquarum, volucres cœli, id est aves in cœlo aerio volitantes, habitabunt, quia in talibus locis nidificant; de medio petrarum, id est de locis petrosis, in quibus sunt avium nidi, dabunt vocem suam, Dominum pro suo modulo collaudantes. Spiritualiter, Super ea jam prædicta, scilicet super montes et aquas, volucres cœli, id est viri sancti et contemplativi, habitabunt, vivendo secundum Christi mandata, atque angelicam vitam in terra ducentes. De medio petrarum dabunt vocem, id est, gratiarum actionem ac laudem tibi offerent de firmissimis locis Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[103:12|Over them|Super ea]], namely on the tops of the mountains and about the waves of the waters, [[103:12|the birds of the air|volucres cœli]], that is, the birds flying in the airy heaven, [[103:12|shall dwell|habitabunt]], for they nest in such places; [[103:12|from the midst of the rocks|de medio petrarum]], that is, from rocky places, where the nests of birds are, [[103:12|they shall give forth their voices|dabunt vocem]], praising the Lord after their fashion. Spiritually, over them, the things already mentioned, that is, over the mountains and waters, the birds of the air, that is, holy and contemplative men, shall dwell, living according to the commandments of Christ and leading an angelic life on earth. [[103:12|from the midst of the rocks they shall give forth their voices|De medio petrarum dabunt vocem]]: that is, they will offer thee thanksgiving and praise from the most secure places of the Church.

paras.t: Rigans montes de superioribus suis : id est, tu, Deus, montes humidos facis de nubibus pluviosis, quæ altiores sunt montibus, vel de fontibus in summitate montium ortis, qui decurrendo loca montis humectant; de fructu operum tuorum, id est de terræ nascentibus, satiabitur terra, id est incolæ terræ. Spiritualiter, rigat Deus montes, id est viros in gratia altos, de superioribus suis, id est de cœlo ministerio angelorum, et de fructu operum Dei, id est prædicatione montium talium, satiabitur terra, id est Ecclesia.
paras.en: [[103:13|Thou waterest the hills from thy upper rooms|Rigans montes de superioribus suis]]: that is, thou, O God, makest the mountains moist from the rainy clouds, which are higher than the mountains, or from springs rising on the summits of the mountains, which as they run down moisten the places of the mountain; [[103:13|with the fruit of thy works|de fructu operum tuorum]], that is, with what springs from the earth, [[103:13|the earth shall be filled|satiabitur terra]], that is, the dwellers on earth. Spiritually, God waters the mountains, that is, men lofty in grace, from his upper rooms, that is, from heaven by the ministry of angels; and with the fruit of God's works, that is, the preaching of such mountains, the earth, that is, the Church, shall be filled.

paras.t: Tu quoque, Domine, es Producens fœnum jumentis ad pabulum, et herbam, id est species varias et medicinales, servituti hominum, id est ad commodum atque obsequium hominum. Quamvis enim hæc fiant per causas secundarias, principaliter tamen fiunt a causa prima, Deo sublimi et benedicto : qui non tantum hominum, sed insuper jumentorum providentiam habet, sicut ex isto clarissime innotescit.
paras.en: And thou, O Lord, art the one [[103:14|Bringing forth grass for cattle|Producens fœnum jumentis]] for fodder, [[103:14|and herb|et herbam]], that is, various kinds of plants, medicinal ones among them, [[103:14|for the service of men|servituti hominum]], that is, for the benefit and use of men. For although these things come about through secondary causes, they come principally from the first cause, God most high and blessed, who has providence not only for men but also for beasts, as is most clearly shown by this.

paras.t: Producis autem fœnum jumentis ad sustentationem vitæ, Ut educas panem, id est bladum, unde fit panis, de terra per jumenta arata et culta, et vinum lætificet cor hominis. Creavit namque Deus vinum, ut moderate sumptum, sumentem ordinate lætificet. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico scribitur : Vinum in jucunditatem creatum est, non in ebrietatem. Est autem cum magna sobrietate potandum, quemadmodum scriptum est : Quam sufficiens est homini erudito vinum exiguum! Si autem immoderate sumatur, intrat quidem suaviter, sed pungit intus ut coluber. Verumtamen quoniam homines in vino difficulter et raro moderamen observant, idcirco Ecclesiasticus monet : In convivio vini non arguas proximum. Spiritualiter, educit Deus panem vitæ et intellectus de terra, id est de corde humano gratia informato, dum facit hominem bonum verbum salutis aliis prædicare, et opera sancta producere. Vinum quoque spirituale, videlicet consolatio fortis Spiritus Sancti, lætificat animam.
paras.en: And thou bringest forth grass for cattle for the sustaining of life [the margin here gives Judith iv, 5, which does not fit this passage], [[103:14|That thou mayst bring bread|Ut educas panem]], that is, grain, from which bread is made, [[103:14|out of the earth|de terra]], ploughed and tilled by beasts, [[103:15|And that wine may cheer the heart of man|et vinum lætificet cor hominis]]. For God created wine so that, taken in moderation, it might cheer the one who takes it in due measure. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 31:35|Wine was created from the beginning to make men joyful, and not to make them drunk|Vinum in jucunditatem creatum est, non in ebrietatem]] [Denis omits *from the beginning*]. But it is to be drunk with great sobriety, as it is written: [[Ecclus 31:22|How sufficient is a little wine for a man well taught|Quam sufficiens est homini erudito vinum exiguum!]]! But if it is taken immoderately, it goes in pleasantly indeed, but stings within like a snake. Yet because men keep moderation in wine with difficulty and seldom, Ecclesiasticus therefore warns: [[Ecclus 31:41|Rebuke not thy neighbour in a banquet of wine|In convivio vini non arguas proximum]]. Spiritually, God brings forth the bread of life and of understanding from the earth, that is, from the human heart formed by grace, when he makes a man preach the good word of salvation to others and bring forth holy works. Spiritual wine too, namely the strong consolation of the Holy Ghost, cheers the soul.

paras.t: Ut exhilaret homo faciem suam in oleo, id est ex condimentis ciborum : non enim sufficit ei panis sine ceteris condimentis; et panis de terra eductus cor hominis confirmet, alendo naturam corpoream. Spiritualiter, exhilaratur facies (id est mens) in oleo, id est in unctione seu gratia Spiritus Sancti, secundum quod in Apocalypsi legitur : Collyrio inunge oculos tuos. Sed et panis ipse cœlestis, videlicet Christus, qui de se ipso ait, Ego sum panis vitæ, summe confirmat cor hominis, quia convertit sumentem in eum qui sumitur, qui utique est virtus et sapientia Patris : ideo dicit, Qui manducat meam carnem et bibit meum sanguinem, in me manet et ego in eo.
paras.en: [[103:15|That he may make the face cheerful with oil|Ut exhilaret homo faciem suam in oleo]] [Denis reads "that man may make his face cheerful"], that is, with the seasonings of food, for bread is not enough for him without other seasonings; [[103:15|and that bread|et panis]], brought out of the earth, [[103:15|may strengthen man's heart|cor hominis confirmet]], by nourishing the bodily nature. Spiritually, the face (that is, the mind) is made cheerful with oil, that is, in the anointing or grace of the Holy Ghost, according to what we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:18|anoint thy eyes with eyesalve|Collyrio inunge oculos tuos]]. And the heavenly bread itself, namely Christ, who says of himself, [[John 6:48|I am the bread of life|Ego sum panis vitæ]], strengthens man's heart supremely, for he changes the one who receives him into him who is received, who is indeed the power and wisdom of the Father: therefore he says, [[John 6:57|He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood abideth in me: and I in him|Qui manducat meam carnem et bibit meum sanguinem, in me manet et ego in eo]].

paras.t: Saturabuntur ligna campi, et cedri Libani quas plantavit Deus principaliter, et homo instrumentaliter : id est, ex humore terræ plenarie nutrientur. Humor namque est arboris alimentum. Nam Christus in Evangelio arborem asserit aruisse quia non habebat humorem. Demum, juxta Philosophum, radices arborum se habent sicut os in animali : per radices ergo alimentum attrahitur.
paras.en: [[103:16|The trees of the field shall be filled, and the cedars of Libanus which he hath planted|Saturabuntur ligna campi, et cedri Libani quas plantavit]], God principally, and man as his instrument: that is, they will be fully nourished from the moisture of the earth. For moisture is the food of a tree: thus Christ in the Gospel says that the plant [[Luke 8:6|withered away, because it had no moisture|aruisse quia non habebat humorem]] [Denis says *arborem*, "a tree"; in the Gospel it is the seed sown upon a rock]. Moreover, according to the Philosopher, the roots of trees are like the mouth in an animal: so it is through the roots that food is drawn in.

paras.t: Illic, puta in cedris, passeres nidificabunt. Invenitur enim quoddam genus passerum, quod nidificare solet in cedris : aliud vero passerum genus in tectis domorum nidificat. Mystice vero ex pane vitæ et vino ac oleo spiritualiter intellecto, saturabuntur in anima ligna campi, id est membra Ecclesiæ, seu inferiores humilesque personæ, et cedri Libani, id est viri perfecti, quos Deus per gratiam in Ecclesia sua plantavit. Illic, scilicet in Ecclesia, passeres, id est pœnitentes per modum passerum in tuto se collocantes, nidificant, id est, sibi thesaurum operum bonorum reponunt. Unde superius a pœnitente dictum est : Factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto. Illic quoque, videlicet in cedris, Herodii domus dux est eorum, id est nidus avis quæ appellatur herodius : quæ est avis rapax, de rapina vivens, ceteris avibus major, quæ etiam aquilam superat atque manducat ; et vocatur dux passerum seu avium, eo modo quo leo nominatur rex animalium.
paras.en: [[103:17|There|Illic]], for instance in the cedars, [[103:17|the sparrows shall make their nests|passeres nidificabunt]]. For there is found a certain kind of sparrow that is wont to nest in cedars, while another kind of sparrow nests on the roofs of houses. Mystically, from the bread of life and from the wine and oil understood spiritually, the trees of the field, that is, the members of the Church, or the lower and humbler persons, shall be filled in soul, and the cedars of Libanus, that is, perfect men, whom God has planted by grace in his Church. There, namely in the Church, the sparrows, that is, penitents who like sparrows settle themselves in safety, make their nests, that is, lay up for themselves a treasure of good works. Hence it was said above by the penitent: I [[Ps 101:8|am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop|Factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto]]. There too, namely in the cedars, [[103:17|The highest of them is the house of the heron|Herodii domus dux est eorum]] [literally "the house of the heron is their leader"], that is, the nest of the bird called the heron, which is a bird of prey, living by plunder, larger than the other birds, which even overcomes and devours the eagle; and it is called the leader of the sparrows, or of the birds, in the way the lion is called the king of beasts.

paras.t: Montes excelsi seu alti, sunt refugia cervis, qui ad talia loca confugiunt ; petra cavernosa, seu subterraneus locus, est refugium herinaciis, id est hericiis. Est autem hericius animal parvum atque spinosum, habitans in cavernis, et vescitur pomis. Quumque adversum quid sentit, per modum globi se contrahit, et intra arma sua se colligit, in tantum ut si eum tangere velis, prius videas tuum sanguinem, quam ejus corpusculum. Per cervos ad montes confugientes, designantur homines virtuosi et contemplativi, qui dum tribulantur, ad contemplanda divina accelerant. Per hericium vero qui dicitur, Noli me tangere, significati sunt peccatores, morbo animæ languentes : qui dum reprehenduntur, remurmurant ; dum aliquid eis negatur, cum indignatione despiciunt ; et unde emendari debebant, inde deteriorantur.
paras.en: [[103:18|The high hills|Montes excelsi]], or lofty, [[103:18|are a refuge for the harts|refugia cervis]], which flee to such places; [[103:18|the rock|petra]], full of caves, or an underground place, is a refuge [[103:18|for the irchins|herinaciis]], that is, hedgehogs. The hedgehog is a small, prickly animal that lives in holes and feeds on fruit. And when it senses anything hostile it draws itself together like a ball and gathers itself within its armour, so that if you try to touch it you will see your own blood before you see its little body. By the harts fleeing to the mountains are signified virtuous and contemplative men, who, when they are afflicted, hasten to the contemplation of divine things. But by the hedgehog, which is called Touch-me-not, are signified sinners sick with disease of soul, who murmur back when they are rebuked, despise with indignation anything that is refused them, and are made worse by what should have amended them.

paras.t: Consequenter laudatur Deus ex ordine temporum, ex vicissitudine lationum cœlestium, ex alternatione actuum naturalium rerum.
paras.en: Next God is praised for the order of the seasons, for the succession of the heavenly motions, and for the alternation of the actions of natural things.

paras.t: Fecit Deus lunam, quæ est infimus planetarum, in tempora, ut per ejus varium motum distinguantur anni lunares et menses. Unde scriptum est : Luna ostensio temporis, et signum ævi ; mensis secundum nomen ejus est, crescens mirabiliter in consummatione ; vas castrorum in excelsis, in firmamento cœli resplendens gloriose. Sol cognovit occasum suum, id est, tam ordinate atque stabiliter fertur in occidentem, ac si intellectualis esset naturæ : quod secundum Augustinum de eo nec affirmari debet, neque negari, donec certius cognoscatur. Mystice, fecit Deus lunam, id est Ecclesiam militantem, lumen suum a Christo sole justitiæ participantem, in tempora, quatenus nunc temporaliter pugnet, tentetur, triumphet, sicque æternaliter coronetur et regnet. Sol, id est Christus Deus noster universa illustrans, cognovit occasum suum, id est, passionem propriam præcognovit.
paras.en: God [[103:19|hath made the moon|Fecit Deus lunam]], which is the lowest of the planets, [[103:19|for seasons|in tempora]], so that by its varying motion the lunar years and months are distinguished. Hence it is written: The moon [[Ecclus 43:6|is for a declaration of times and a sign of the world|ostensio temporis, et signum ævi]]; [[Ecclus 43:8|The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her perfection|mensis secundum nomen ejus est, crescens mirabiliter in consummatione]]; [[Ecclus 43:9|Being an instrument of the armies on high, shining gloriously in the firmament of heaven|vas castrorum in excelsis, in firmamento cœli resplendens gloriose]]. [[103:19|the sun knoweth his going down|Sol cognovit occasum suum]]: that is, it is borne towards the west in so orderly and steady a way, as if it were of an intellectual nature: which, according to Augustine, ought neither to be affirmed nor denied of it until it is known more certainly. Mystically, God hath made the moon, that is, the Church militant, which shares its light from Christ the sun of justice, for seasons, that it may now in time fight, be tempted and triumph, and so be crowned and reign eternally. The sun, that is, Christ our God, who enlightens all things[[John 1:9||]], knoweth his going down, that is, foreknew his own passion.

paras.t: Posuisti tenebras in hemisphærio illo, de quo sol recedit, et facta est nox, sole abeunte ; in ipsa nocte pertransibunt omnes bestiæ silvæ pro victu quærendo. Dicitur autem Deus ponere tenebras : non quod tenebræ sint aliquid positivum, sed sunt privatio tantum, scilicet carentia lucis, quemadmodum cæcitas est carentia visus : dicitur ergo Deus tenebras ponere, quoniam facit lumen recedere, vel cessat illud influere. Sic etiam dicitur aliquos excæcare et obdurare. Spiritualiter, posuit Deus permissive tenebras infidelitatis et culpæ, Christo occiso, et facta est nox, id est veræ fidei defectus ; in ipsa pertransibunt ad animas miseras devorandas, omnes bestiæ silvæ, id est diaboli. Nam ubi fides non adest, nihil boni esse valet.
paras.en: [[103:20|Thou hast appointed darkness|Posuisti tenebras]] in that hemisphere from which the sun withdraws, [[103:20|and it is night|et facta est nox]], when the sun departs; [[103:20|in it shall all the beasts of the woods go about|in ipsa nocte pertransibunt omnes bestiæ silvæ]], to seek their food. God is said to appoint darkness not because darkness is anything positive, for it is only a privation, namely the lack of light, as blindness is the lack of sight: God is said, then, to appoint darkness because he makes the light withdraw, or ceases to pour it in. In the same way he is said to blind and harden some. Spiritually, God appointed, by permission, the darkness of unbelief and of sin when Christ was slain, and it was night, that is, the failing of true faith; in it all the beasts of the woods, that is, the devils, go about to devour wretched souls. For where faith is not present, nothing good can be.

paras.t: Catuli leonum tempore noctis egrediuntur de suis latibulis, rugientes, ut rapiant prædam, et, pro id est, quærant a Deo escam sibi : non quod ipsi Deum agnoscant, sed quia ex naturali instinctu divinitus impresso moventur, atque a Deo, cujus est omnium curam habere, aluntur : quemadmodum de volatilibus cœli Christus ait, Pater vester cœlestis pascit ea. Spiritualiter, dum animæ nostræ occumbit sol lucis æternæ, scilicet Christus, obviant nobis catuli leonum, id est adhæsores atque fautores dæmonum, rugientes, ut spiritualiter devorent quempiam.
paras.en: [[103:21|The young lions|Catuli leonum]] come out of their lairs at night-time, [[103:21|roaring after their prey|rugientes, ut rapiant]] [literally "roaring that they may seize" their prey], and (*and* standing for *that is*) [[103:21|seeking their meat from God|quærant a Deo escam sibi]]: not that they know God, but because they are moved by a natural instinct implanted by God, and are fed by God, whose part it is to care for all things: as Christ says of the birds of the air, [[Matt 6:26|your heavenly Father feedeth them|Pater vester cœlestis pascit ea]]. Spiritually, when the sun of eternal light, namely Christ, sets for our soul, the young lions meet us, that is, the adherents and abettors of the demons, roaring to devour someone spiritually.

paras.t: Ortus est sol, et congregati sunt, id est, sole orto colliguntur hæ bestiæ, et in cubilibus, id est latibulis suis, collocabuntur : statim enim die splendente antra sua introeunt.
paras.en: [[103:22|The sun ariseth, and they are gathered together|Ortus est sol, et congregati sunt]], that is, when the sun has risen these beasts are gathered together, [[103:22|and they shall lie down in their dens|et in cubilibus suis collocabuntur]]: for as soon as the day shines they go into their caves.

paras.t: Exibit in die homo, qui est animal mansuetum et rationale, ad opus suum faciendum infra domum seu muros, et ad operationem suam foris usque ad vesperam : tunc enim cessat, ut comedat et quiescat, atque pericula noctis devitet. Hæc tamen secundum communem legem et solitum cursum dicuntur et fiunt, quamvis interdum ex speciali causa aliter accidat. Spiritualiter, dum oritur nobis sol intelligentiæ Christus nos adjuvans, congregantur et fugiunt dæmones. Et ita exit homo a Christo adjutus ad opus suum intrinsecum, et ad operationem suam extrinsecam peragendam et continuandam, usque ad vesperam, id est perseveranter, quamdiu lux gratiæ sibi refulget, usque ad mortem, advertens quod in Apocalypsi ait Salvator : Esto fidelis usque ad mortem, et dabo tibi coronam vitæ.
paras.en: [[103:23|Man shall go forth|Exibit in die homo]] by day, being a gentle and rational animal, [[103:23|to his work|ad opus suum]], to be done within the house or walls, [[103:23|and to his labour|et ad operationem suam]] out of doors, [[103:23|until the evening|usque ad vesperam]]: for then he stops, to eat and rest and to avoid the dangers of the night. These things, however, are said and come about according to the common law and the usual course, although sometimes for a special cause it happens otherwise. Spiritually, when Christ, the sun of understanding, rises for us and helps us, the demons gather together and flee. And so man, helped by Christ, goes forth to his inward work and to his outward labour, to carry it out and continue it, until the evening, that is, perseveringly, as long as the light of grace shines for him, until death, heeding what the Saviour says in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 2:10|Be thou faithful unto death: and I will give thee the crown of life|Esto fidelis usque ad mortem, et dabo tibi coronam vitæ]].

paras.t: Quoniam autem ex prædictis apparet ineffabilis sapientia summi Regis ac primi Opificis, ideo admirando subjungitur : Quam magnificata sunt opera tua, Domine! id est, valde magnifice facta sunt, valde potenter, sapienter et pie creata, ordinata et conservata. Propter quod in Apocalypsi dicitur : Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua, Domine Deus omnipotens! Sunt enim omnino incomprehensibilia et imperscrutabilia nobis, juxta illud Ecclesiastici : Multa dicimus et deficimus verbis. Rursusque : Multa sunt abscondita majora his ; pauca enim vidimus operum ejus. Et rursus Ecclesiastes dicit : Cunctæ res difficiles ; non potest eas homo explicare sermone. Ecce enim in infimis ac minimis rebus relucet inæstimabilis sapientia Dei : quemadmodum in formica quæ hieme accedente cibum sibi colligit et reponit ; in culice quoque minutissimo, oculos universaque membra habentes sicut et nos. Propterea Ecclesiasticus inducit : Quam desiderabilia sunt omnia opera ejus ! Et quis satiabitur videns gloriam ejus ?
paras.en: And since from what has been said the unspeakable wisdom of the supreme King and first Maker is evident, there follows, in wonder: [[103:24|How great are thy works, O Lord|Quam magnificata sunt opera tua, Domine!]]! that is, they are made most magnificently, most mightily, wisely and lovingly created, ordered and preserved. Hence it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 15:3|Great and wonderful are thy works, O Lord God Almighty|Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua, Domine Deus omnipotens!]]! For they are wholly incomprehensible and unsearchable to us, according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 43:29|We shall say much, and yet shall want words|Multa dicimus et deficimus verbis]]. And again: [[Ecclus 43:36|There are many things hidden from us that are greater than these: for we have seen but a few of his works|Multa sunt abscondita majora his ; pauca enim vidimus operum ejus]]. And again Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 1:8|All things are hard: man cannot explain them by word|Cunctæ res difficiles ; non potest eas homo explicare sermone]]. For see how in the lowest and least things the inestimable wisdom of God shines out: as in the ant, which as winter approaches gathers food for itself and stores it up; and in the tiniest gnat, which has eyes and all its members, as we do. Therefore Ecclesiasticus brings in: [[Ecclus 42:23|O how desirable are all his works|Quam desiderabilia sunt omnia opera ejus]]! [[Ecclus 42:26|And who shall be filled with beholding his glory|Et quis satiabitur videns gloriam ejus]]?

paras.t: Omnia in sapientia fecisti, id est secundum dictamen tuæ æternæ mentis, secundum ideales rationes, secundum ineffabilem gloriam artis divinæ : omnia namque in mensura et numero et pondere constituisti, ut ait Sapientia. Impleta est terra possessione tua, id est hominibus et jumentis ac ceteris creaturis, quæ jure creationis tua sunt. Quamvis autem hæc vera consistant de opere creationis totius universi, veriora tamen sunt de opere recreationis generis humani, ac reparatione ruinæ cœlestis Jerusalem. Hæc namque per Filii Dei incarnationem, passionem, resurrectionem, ascensionem, et Spiritus Sancti missionem magnificentissime facta sunt ; fecitque Deus Pater omnia hæc in Sapientia sua genita, id est per Christum Deum et hominem. Impleta quoque est terra, id est genus humanum seu ipsa Ecclesia, possessione Dei, id est sacramentis Christi, donis Spiritus Sancti, viris catholicis, atque diversis corporalibus ac spiritualibus bonis.
paras.en: [[103:24|thou hast made all things in wisdom|Omnia in sapientia fecisti]]: that is, according to the dictate of thy eternal mind, according to the ideal patterns [*rationes ideales*, the ideas or exemplars of all things in the mind of God], according to the unspeakable glory of the divine art: for thou hast set up all things [[Wis 11:21|in measure, and number, and weight|in mensura et numero et pondere]], as Wisdom says. [[103:24|the earth is filled with thy riches|Impleta est terra possessione tua]] [Denis's Latin is *possessione tua*, "with thy possession"], that is, with men and beasts and the other creatures, which are thine by right of creation. And although these things hold true of the work of the creation of the whole universe, they are truer still of the work of the re-creation of the human race and of the repair of the ruin of the heavenly Jerusalem. For these things were wrought most magnificently through the incarnation, passion, resurrection and ascension of the Son of God, and the sending of the Holy Ghost; and God the Father made all these things in his begotten Wisdom, that is, through Christ, God and man. The earth too, that is, the human race or the Church herself, is filled with the possession of God, that is, with the sacraments of Christ, the gifts of the Holy Ghost, catholic men, and various bodily and spiritual goods.

103.title: PROSECUTIO EXPLANATIONIS HUJUS PSALMI CENTESIMI TERTII.
103.title_en: Continuation of the explanation of this hundred and third psalm.

paras.t: Consequenter denique sanctus Propheta inducit rationem laudis divinæ ex dispositione atque decore maris Oceani. Hoc mare.
