paras.en: God [[104:27|gave them|Posuit Deus in eis]], that is, Moses and Aaron, [[104:27|power to shew them signs|verba signorum suorum]] [literally "he put in them the words of his signs", which is why Denis goes on to speak of God foretelling the signs through them], that is, of the lesser marvels, [[104:27|and his wonders|et prodigiorum]], that is, of the greater miracles, [[104:27|in the land of Cham|in terra Cham]], that is, in Egypt. For through them God foretold to Pharao what signs and wonders were to come the following day, as is often related in Exodus[[Ex 5:1||]][[Ex 7:1||]].

paras.t: Deinde ponuntur plagæ Ægypti, non omnes, sed septem vel octo: quæ tamen non ponuntur hic eo ordine, quo factæ fuerunt.
paras.en: Next the plagues of Egypt are set down: not all of them, but seven or eight; and they are not set down here in the order in which they took place.

paras.t: Misit Deus tenebras in terra ubi morabantur Ægyptii, et obscuravit, id est, lucem solis abstulit. Hæc fuit nona plaga. De qua scribitur in Exodo: Dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Extende manum tuam in cœlum, et sint tenebræ super terram Ægypti tam densæ, ut palpari queant. Et factæ sunt tenebræ horribiles: tribus diebus nemo vidit fratrem suum, nec movit se de loco in quo stetit. Ubicumque autem habitabant filii Israel, lux erat. Hæc autem obscuratio erat valde mirabilis: erat enim per subtractionem radiorum solis ab una parte terræ Ægypti, et non ab altera. Et non exacerbavit, id est, amaros non fecit, sed dulcoravit Deus sermones suos, quibus minabatur Ægyptiis. Pharaone enim pœnitentiam promittente et Moyse exorante, plagæ cessabant, secundum quod in Exodo Moyses Pharaoni locutus est : Egressus de urbe, extendam palmas meas ad Dominum, et cessabunt tonitrua, ut scias quia Domini est terra. Vel, Non exacerbavit, id est, irritos non fecit sermones suos, sed adimplevit.
paras.en: God [[104:28|sent darkness|Misit Deus tenebras]] upon the land where the Egyptians dwelt, [[104:28|and made it obscure|et obscuravit]], that is, took away the light of the sun. This was the ninth plague, of which it is written in Exodus: [[Ex 10:21|the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out thy hand towards heaven: and may there be darkness upon the land of Egypt so thick that it may be felt|Dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Extende manum tuam in cœlum, et sint tenebræ super terram Ægypti tam densæ, ut palpari queant]] And [[Ex 10:22|there came horrible darkness|factæ sunt tenebræ horribiles]]: [[Ex 10:22|for three days|tribus diebus]] no man [[Ex 10:23|saw his brother, nor moved himself out of the place where he was: but wheresoever the children of Israel dwelt, there was light|vidit fratrem suum, nec movit se de loco in quo stetit. Ubicumque autem habitabant filii Israel, lux erat]]. Now this darkening was most wonderful, for it came about by the withdrawing of the sun's rays from one part of the land of Egypt and not from the other. [[104:28|And grieved not|Et non exacerbavit]], that is, did not make bitter, but God sweetened, [[104:28|his words|sermones suos]] with which he threatened the Egyptians [*exacerbare* is "to make bitter", hence Denis's gloss]. For when Pharao promised repentance and Moses prayed, the plagues ceased; according to what Moses said to Pharao in Exodus: [[Ex 9:29|As soon as I am gone out of the city, I will stretch forth my hands to the Lord, and the thunders shall cease|Egressus de urbe, extendam palmas meas ad Dominum, et cessabunt tonitrua]], [[Ex 9:29|that thou mayst know that the earth is the Lord's|ut scias quia Domini est terra]]. Or: [[104:28|grieved not|Non exacerbavit]], that is, did not make his words void, but fulfilled them.

paras.t: Insuper Deus Convertit aquas eorum, id est Ægyptiorum, in sanguinem, et occidit pisces eorum, qui erant ac nutriebantur in aquis. Hæc est prima plaga Ægyptiorum. De qua scriptum est in Exodo : Dixit Dominus ad Moysen : Dic ad Aaron, Tolle virgam tuam, et extende manum tuam super flumina Ægypti, ut vertantur in sanguinem. Et elevans virgam, percussit aquam fluminis coram Pharaone, et pisces mortui sunt.
paras.en: Moreover God [[104:29|turned their waters|Convertit aquas eorum]], that is, the Egyptians', [[104:29|into blood|in sanguinem]], [[104:29|and destroyed their fish|et occidit pisces eorum]], which were and were nourished in the waters. This is the first plague of the Egyptians, of which it is written in Exodus: [[Ex 7:19|The Lord also said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Take thy rod; and stretch forth thy hand upon the waters of Egypt|Dixit Dominus ad Moysen : Dic ad Aaron, Tolle virgam tuam, et extende manum tuam super flumina Ægypti]], [[Ex 7:19|that they may be turned into blood|ut vertantur in sanguinem]]. And [[Ex 7:20|lifting up the rod, he struck the water of the river before Pharao|elevans virgam, percussit aquam fluminis coram Pharaone]], and [[Ex 7:21|the fishes that were in the river died|pisces mortui sunt]].

paras.t: Et edit terra eorum ranas, id est, ex terra Ægypti eruperunt ranæ : quæ ingressæ sunt domos vulgi ac principum Pharaonis, inventæque sunt in penetralibus, id est in locis secretis et thalamo, regum ipsorum, id est principum Ægyptiorum. Hæc est secunda plaga Ægyptiorum. De qua Dominus ait ad Pharaonem : Ebullient ranæ, et ingredientur domum tuam, et cubiculum lecti tui, et super stratum tuum, et in domos servorum tuorum, et in populum tuum.
paras.en: [[104:30|Their land brought forth frogs|Et edit terra eorum ranas]], that is, frogs burst forth from the land of Egypt, which entered the houses of the common people and of Pharao's princes, and were found [[104:30|in the inner chambers|in penetralibus]], that is, in the secret places and the bedchamber, [[104:30|of their kings|regum ipsorum]], that is, of the princes of the Egyptians. This is the second plague of the Egyptians, of which the Lord said to Pharao: [[Ex 8:3|the river shall bring forth an abundance of frogs|Ebullient ranæ]] [Denis has "the frogs shall swarm"], and they shall [[Ex 8:3|enter into thy house, and thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the houses of thy servants, and to thy people|et ingredientur domum tuam, et cubiculum lecti tui, et super stratum tuum, et in domos servorum tuorum, et in populum tuum]].

paras.t: Dixit Deus, id est, esse et fieri jussit, et ex jussione divina venit cynomyia (id est musca canina magna atque gravissima), id est multitudo harum muscarum, cui admixtæ erant aliæ muscæ graves diversi generis. Hæc est quarta plaga Ægypti. De qua Dominus ait per Moysen regi Ægypti : Ecce ego mittam in te et in populum tuum omne genus muscarum. Et corrupta est terra ab hujuscemodi muscis. Dixit quoque Deus, et venerunt scinifes, id est muscæ parvæ atrociterque mordentes. Hæc est autem tertia plaga Ægypti : in qua defecerunt magi Pharaonis. De qua in Exodo habetur : Omnis pulvis terræ versus est in scinifes. Dixeruntque malefici ad Pharaonem : Digitus Dei est hoc. Venit autem et fuit in omnibus finibus eorum, id est in universis terminis populisque regis Ægypti.
paras.en: God [[104:31|spoke|Dixit Deus]], that is, commanded it to be and to come about, and by the divine command [[104:31|there came|venit]] [[104:31|divers sorts of flies|cynomyia]] (that is, the great dog-fly, most grievous) [*cynomyia* is Greek for "dog-fly"], that is, a multitude of these flies, with which other grievous flies of divers kinds were mixed. This is the fourth plague of Egypt, of which the Lord said through Moses to the king of Egypt: [[Ex 8:21|behold I will send in upon thee, and upon thy servants, and upon thy houses, all kind of flies|Ecce ego mittam in te et in populum tuum omne genus muscarum]]. And [[Ex 8:24|the land was corrupted by this kind of flies|corrupta est terra ab hujuscemodi muscis]]. God also [[104:31|spoke|Dixit quoque Deus]], and there came [[104:31|sciniphs|scinifes]], that is, small flies that bite fiercely. This is the third plague of Egypt, in which Pharao's magicians failed. Of it we have in Exodus: [[Ex 8:17|all the dust of the earth was turned into sciniphs|Omnis pulvis terræ versus est in scinifes]]. And [[Ex 8:19|the magicians said to Pharao: This is the finger of God|Dixeruntque malefici ad Pharaonem : Digitus Dei est hoc]]. And it came and was [[104:31|in all their coasts|in omnibus finibus eorum]], that is, in all the borders and peoples of the king of Egypt.

paras.t: Posuit pluvias eorum grandinem, id est, pro pluvia fecit Deus descendere grandinem ; posuit et ignem comburentem, id est fulgura discurrentia, et ignem grandini mixtum, in terra ipsorum. Et percussit Deus grandine, igne ac sulfure vineas eorum et ficulneas eorum ; et contrivit, id est, consumpsit atque destruxit, lignum finium eorum, id est ligna terminorum Ægypti. Hæc est septima plaga Ægypti. De qua dicitur in Exodo : Dominus dedit tonitrua et grandinem, ac discurrentia fulgura ; et grando et ignis mixta pariter ferebantur.
paras.en: [[104:32|He gave them hail for rain|Posuit pluvias eorum grandinem]] [literally "he made their rains hail"], that is, in place of rain God made hail come down; he set also [[104:32|a burning fire|ignem comburentem]], that is, lightnings running about, and fire mixed with the hail, [[104:32|in the land|in terra ipsorum]]. And God [[104:33|destroyed|Et percussit]] with hail, fire and brimstone [[104:33|their vineyards and their fig trees|vineas eorum et ficulneas eorum]]; [[104:33|and he broke in pieces|et contrivit]], that is, consumed and destroyed, [[104:33|the trees of their coasts|lignum finium eorum]], that is, the trees of the borders of Egypt. This is the seventh plague of Egypt, of which it is said in Exodus: [[Ex 9:23|the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightnings running along the ground|Dominus dedit tonitrua et grandinem, ac discurrentia fulgura]]; and [[Ex 9:24|the hail and fire mixt with it drove on together|grando et ignis mixta pariter ferebantur]].

paras.t: Dixit Deus et venit in terram Ægypti locusta, id est multitudo locustarum, et bruchus cujus non erat numerus, id est innumerabiles bruchi : qui sunt animalia brevia, breviterque viventia. Et comedit locusta et bruchus omne fœnum, id est omnem herbam, in terra eorum, et comedit omnem fructum terræ eorum, id est segetes Ægyptiorum. Hæc est octava plaga Ægypti : in qua a bestiolis istis corrosum est, quod remansit igni et grandini : quæ etiam universam terræ superficiem sic operuerunt, quod nihil ejus apparuit, sicut habetur in Exodo.
paras.en: God [[104:34|spoke|Dixit Deus]], and there [[104:34|came|venit]] into the land of Egypt [[104:34|the locust|locusta]], that is, a multitude of locusts, [[104:34|and the bruchus, of which there was no number|et bruchus cujus non erat numerus]], that is, countless bruchi, which are small creatures and short-lived. [[104:35|And they devoured|Et comedit]], the locust and the bruchus, [[104:35|all the grass|omne fœnum]], that is, every herb, [[104:35|in their land|in terra eorum]], [[104:35|and consumed all the fruit of their ground|et comedit omnem fructum terræ eorum]], that is, the crops of the Egyptians. This is the eighth plague of Egypt, in which those little beasts gnawed away what was left by the fire and the hail; and they so covered the whole face of the earth that none of it could be seen, as we have in Exodus[[Ex 10:14||]][[Ex 10:15||]].

paras.t: Et percussit omne primogenitum tam in hominibus, quam in jumentis, in terra eorum ; percussit etiam primitias omnis laboris eorum, id est primitiva fructuum elaboratorum. Hæc est decima plaga Ægypti. De qua in Exodo legitur : Factum est noctis medio, percussit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, a primogenito Pharaonis qui sedebat in solio ejus, usque ad primogenitum captivæ.
paras.en: [[104:36|And he slew all the firstborn|Et percussit omne primogenitum]], both of men and of beasts, [[104:36|in their land|in terra eorum]]; he struck also [[104:36|the firstfruits of all their labour|primitias omnis laboris eorum]], that is, the first of the fruits they had laboured for. This is the tenth plague of Egypt, of which we read in Exodus: [[Ex 12:29|it came to pass at midnight, the Lord slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharao, who sat on his throne, unto the firstborn of the captive woman|Factum est noctis medio, percussit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, a primogenito Pharaonis qui sedebat in solio ejus, usque ad primogenitum captivæ]].

paras.t: Hic itaque omissæ sunt duæ plagæ Ægypti, videlicet quinta et sexta. Quinta enim fuit, quod omnia animantia Ægyptiorum mortua sunt peste ; sexta, quod facta sunt vulnera vesicarum turgentium in hominibus et jumentis.
paras.en: Here, then, two plagues of Egypt are left out, namely the fifth and the sixth. For the fifth was that [[Ex 9:6|all the beasts of the Egyptians died|omnia animantia Ægyptiorum mortua sunt]] of pestilence; the sixth, that [[Ex 9:10|there came boils with swelling blains in men and beasts|facta sunt vulnera vesicarum turgentium in hominibus et jumentis]].

paras.t: Consequenter annumerantur bona Judæis collata. Et eduxit eos Deus de Ægypto cum argento et auro : quia ut in Exodo scriptum est, Dominus jussit Judæis ut peterent ab Ægyptiis vasa aurea atque argentea, vestemque plurimam, et spoliarent Ægyptum : quod etiam factum est, nec tamen injuste, quia Dei sunt omnia, et cui vult, tribuit ea. Ægyptii quoque ingrati erant, ideo injuste possederant. Sed et filii Israel remunerati non erant ab Ægyptiis pro labore gravissimæ servitutis. Et non erat in tribubus eorum, scilicet Hebræorum, infirmus. Omnes enim incolumes Deo disponente fuerunt, quatenus simul egrederentur.
paras.en: Next are reckoned up the good things bestowed on the Jews. And God [[104:37|brought them out|Et eduxit eos]] of Egypt [[104:37|with silver and gold|cum argento et auro]]: for, as is written in Exodus, the Lord commanded the Jews to ask of the Egyptians vessels of gold and silver, and very much raiment, and to strip Egypt[[Ex 11:2||]]. And this was done, yet not unjustly, because all things are God's, and he gives them to whom he will[[1 Par 29:11||]][[1 Par 29:12||]][[1 Par 29:14||]][[1 Par 29:16||]] [the margin gives 1 Par. xxix, 11, 12, 13, 16; v. 13 does not fit, while v. 14 has "all things are thine"]. The Egyptians, too, were ungrateful, and so had held them unjustly. And besides, the children of Israel had not been paid by the Egyptians for the labour of their most grievous bondage. [[104:37|And there was not among their tribes|Et non erat in tribubus eorum]], that is, the Hebrews', [[104:37|one that was feeble|infirmus]]. For by God's ordering all were sound, so that they might go out together.

paras.t: Lætata est Ægyptus in profectione eorum, id est de egressione Hebræorum, quia incubuit timor eorum super eos, id est, pavor invasit Ægyptios, ne propter retentionem Judæorum omnes occiderentur. Unde in Exodo Pharao dixit : Surgite et egredimini de populo meo; et abeuntes benedicite mihi. Urgebantque Ægyptii populum de terra exire velociter, dicentes : Omnes moriemur.
paras.en: [[104:38|Egypt was glad when they departed|Lætata est Ægyptus in profectione eorum]], that is, at the going out of the Hebrews, [[104:38|for the fear of them lay upon them|quia incubuit timor eorum super eos]], that is, dread seized the Egyptians lest they should all be slain because of holding back the Jews. Hence in Exodus Pharao said: [[Ex 12:31|Arise and go forth from among my people|Surgite et egredimini de populo meo]]; and [[Ex 12:32|departing bless me|abeuntes benedicite mihi]]. [[Ex 12:33|And the Egyptians pressed the people to go forth out of the land speedily, saying: We shall all die.|Urgebantque Ægyptii populum de terra exire velociter, dicentes : Omnes moriemur]]

paras.t: Expandit Deus nubem in protectionem eorum, id est in refrigerium populi sui contra æstum diei, et ignem, id est columnam ignis, ut luceret eis per noctem : quemadmodum ait Scriptura : Dominus præcedebat eos ad ostendendum viam per diem in columna nubis, et per noctem in columna ignis.
paras.en: God [[104:39|spread a cloud for their protection|Expandit Deus nubem in protectionem eorum]], that is, to cool his people against the heat of the day, [[104:39|and fire|et ignem]], that is, the pillar of fire, [[104:39|to give them light in the night|ut luceret eis per noctem]]: as the Scripture says: [[Ex 13:21|the Lord went before them to shew the way, by day in a pillar of a cloud, and by night in a pillar of fire|Dominus præcedebat eos ad ostendendum viam per diem in columna nubis, et per noctem in columna ignis]].

paras.t: Deinde recitantur mirabilia Dei facta in deserto : Petierunt Hebræi cibum delicatum, et venit, vento Domini flante, coturnix, id est multitudo coturnicum : quæ sunt aves circa terram volantes ac regiæ. Unde in Numeris dicitur : Flagrabant desiderio carnium, et dicebant : Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes ? Et postea sequitur quomodo per gyrum castrorum volabant coturnices spatio unius diei. Et pane cæli, scilicet manna, saturavit eos quadraginta annis, ut dicitur in Exodo.
paras.en: Next are told the wonders God wrought in the desert. The Hebrews [[104:40|asked|Petierunt]] for dainty food, and there [[104:40|came|et venit]], as the wind of the Lord blew, [[104:40|the quail|coturnix]], that is, a multitude of quails, which are birds that fly close to the ground, and fit for kings. Hence it is said in Numbers: they [[Num 11:4|burned with desire|Flagrabant desiderio]] for flesh, and said: [[Num 11:4|Who shall give us flesh to eat?|Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes]] And afterwards it goes on to tell how the quails flew round about the camp for the space of one day[[Num 11:31||]]. And [[104:40|with the bread of heaven|Et pane cæli]], namely manna, [[104:40|he filled them|saturavit eos]] for forty years, as is said in Exodus[[Ex 16:35||]].

paras.t: Dirupit petram, id est, Moyse percutiente cum virga petram, divino miraculo rupta seu divisa est petra, et fluxerunt aquæ de petra; abierunt in sicco flumina, id est, in deserto currebant ex petra rivi aquarum, ita ut biberet populus et jumenta. Porro hæc petræ diruptio et effluxio aquæ, facta est bis : primo in petra Horeb, ut in Exodo legitur ; secundo in petra deserti Sin, quemadmodum in Numeris scriptum est.
paras.en: [[104:41|He opened the rock|Dirupit petram]], that is, when Moses struck the rock with the rod, the rock was by a divine miracle burst open or split, [[104:41|and waters flowed|et fluxerunt aquæ]] from the rock; [[104:41|rivers ran down in the dry land|abierunt in sicco flumina]], that is, in the desert streams of water ran from the rock, so that the people and the beasts drank. Now this bursting of the rock and flowing out of water happened twice: first at the rock of Horeb, as we read in Exodus[[Ex 17:1||]]; secondly at the rock of the desert of Sin, as is written in Numbers[[Num 20:1||]].

paras.t: Hæc autem beneficia contulit Deus filiis Israel, non propter eorum virtutes aut merita, quum semper rebelles inventi sint, sed propter promissionem Abrahæ factam implendam, et etiam propter Abrahæ merita. Propter quod dicitur : Quoniam memor fuit per effectum verbi sancti sui, id est promissionis divinæ, quod habuit ad Abraham puerum suum, promittens ei quod educeret semen suum ex Ægypto, daretque eis terram Chananæorum.
paras.en: Now God bestowed these benefits on the children of Israel not for their virtues or merits, since they were always found rebellious, but to fulfil the promise made to Abraham, and also for Abraham's merits. Wherefore it is said: [[104:42|Because he remembered|Quoniam memor fuit]], in effect [that is, in deed, by fulfilling it], [[104:42|his holy word|verbi sancti sui]], that is, the divine promise, [[104:42|which he had spoken to his servant Abraham|quod habuit ad Abraham puerum suum]], promising him that he would bring his seed out of Egypt and give them the land of the Chanaanites[[Gen 15:13||]][[Gen 15:14||]].

paras.t: Deinceps scribuntur bona divinitus data filiis Israel tempore Josue. Et eduxit Dominus populum suum post mortem Moysis per Josue, de campestribus Moab per Jordanem in terram promissionis, in exsultatione exteriori, et electos suos, id est populum jam prædictum divinitus præelectum, in lætitia interiori, ut patet in libro Josue.
paras.en: Next are described the good things given by God to the children of Israel in the time of Josue. And the Lord [[104:43|brought forth his people|Et eduxit Dominus populum suum]] after the death of Moses, by Josue, from the plains of Moab across the Jordan into the land of promise, [[104:43|with joy|in exsultatione]] without, [[104:43|and his chosen|et electos suos]], that is, the people already spoken of, chosen beforehand by God, [[104:43|with gladness|in lætitia]] within, as is plain from the book of Josue[[Jos 1:1||]].

paras.t: Et dedit illis regiones gentium, scilicet terram regis Og, terramque regis Sehon, et terras in quibus habitabant septem gentes, videlicet Chananæi, Hethæi, Pherezæi, etc. ; et labores populorum istorum, videlicet urbes, villas atque divitias eorum labore factas seu acquisitas, possederunt filii Israel : sicut in pluribus locis libri Josue legitur.
paras.en: [[104:44|And he gave them the lands of the Gentiles|Et dedit illis regiones gentium]], namely the land of king Og and the land of king Sehon, and the lands in which the seven nations dwelt, that is, the Chanaanites, Hethites, Pherezites, etc.; and the children of Israel [[104:44|possessed|possederunt]] [[104:44|the labours of the people|et labores populorum]], of those peoples, that is, their cities, towns and riches, made or gained by their labour, as we read in many places of the book of Josue[[Jos 12:1||]].

paras.t: Ut custodiant justificationes ejus, id est, observent divina præcepta, hominem justificantia, et legem ejus per Moysen datam requirant, id est, diligentius discant, memoriter teneant, et spiritualiter intelligere studeant.
paras.en: [[104:45|That they might observe his justifications|Ut custodiant justificationes ejus]], that is, keep the divine precepts, which justify a man, [[104:45|and seek after his law|et legem ejus per Moysen datam requirant]], given through Moses: that is, learn it more diligently, hold it in memory, and strive to understand it spiritually.

paras.t: Verumtamen advertendum, quod possessio temporalium rerum non est principale, neque sufficiens præmium observationis legis divinæ seu custodiæ mandatorum : præsertim quum observatio legis sit de genere boni honesti; possessio autem seu remuneratio boni temporalis, de genere boni utilis vel delectabilis. Bonum vero honestum omnino excedit in dignitate bonum utile ac delectabile : ideo non præmiatur finaliter per talia bona, quoniam Deus non præmiat citra, sed ultra condignum. Beatitudo ergo æterna, est principale plenumque præmium vitæ virtuosæ ; remuneratio vero temporalis, est præmium secundarium, et minus principale : quæ tamen populo Israelitico frequenter promissa ac præstita est, propter ruditatem ipsius, quatenus ex perceptione præsentium sperare inciperet futura et spiritualia bona. Et hoc modo multa intelligenda sunt, quæ Moyses scribit, ut est illud Deuteronomii : Dominus est vita tua et longitudo dierum tuorum, ut habites super terram, quam daturus est tibi ; et illud, Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam, ut sis longævus super terram.
paras.en: Yet it should be noted that the possession of temporal things is not the chief nor a sufficient reward for observing the divine law or keeping the commandments: above all since the observance of the law belongs to the kind of the virtuous good, while the possession or reward of a temporal good belongs to the kind of the useful or the pleasant good [the schoolmen's three kinds of good: the *bonum honestum*, good in itself, the useful and the pleasant]. Now the virtuous good wholly surpasses the useful and the pleasant good in dignity; therefore it is not finally rewarded by such goods, since God rewards not short of, but beyond, what is deserved [*condignum*: what is strictly merited]. Eternal beatitude, then, is the chief and full reward of a virtuous life; temporal reward is a secondary and less principal one. Yet this was often promised and granted to the people of Israel because of its rudeness [that is, its want of spiritual understanding], so that from receiving present goods it might begin to hope for goods future and spiritual. And in this way many things that Moses writes are to be understood, such as that of Deuteronomy: The Lord, [[Deut 30:20|he is thy life, and the length of thy days|Dominus est vita tua et longitudo dierum tuorum]], [[Deut 30:20|that thou mayst dwell in the land|ut habites super terram]] which he will give thee; and that saying: [[Ex 20:12|Honour thy father and thy mother, that thou mayst be longlived upon the land|Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam, ut sis longævus super terram]].

104.title: EXPLANATIO MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI QUARTI.
104.title_en: Moral explanation of the same hundred and fourth psalm.

paras.t: Secundum divinum et magnum Dionysium, inter statum veteris Testamenti et patriæ, medius est status evangelicæ legis. Et sicut status Ecclesiæ militantis, est figura status Ecclesiæ triumphantis seu Beatorum; sic status veteris Testamenti erat figura Testamenti novi. Propter quod, secundum Apostolum, omnia in figura contingebant illis. Sicut ergo ad litteram alloquitur Propheta in psalmo isto Synagogam, ita secundum tropologiam seu moralitatem affatur Ecclesiam, et ait:
paras.en: According to the divine and great Dionysius, between the state of the Old Testament and that of the fatherland [that is, heaven, the home of the Blessed] stands, in the middle, the state of the law of the Gospel. And as the state of the Church militant is a figure of the state of the Church triumphant, or of the Blessed, so the state of the Old Testament was a figure of the New. Wherefore, according to the Apostle, [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|omnia in figura contingebant illis]]. As, then, in the literal sense the Prophet in this psalm addresses the Synagogue, so in the tropological or moral sense he speaks to the Church, and says:

paras.t: Confitemini Domino, id est, Christum non solum ut hominem, sed etiam ut verum Deum laudate, et invocate nomen ejus. Annuntiate, o sancti Apostoli et successores ipsorum, inter gentes, id est omnibus paganis, opera ejus, scilicet Christi. Unde in Actibus Paulus: Ecce, inquit, convertimur ad gentes; sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus.
paras.en: [[104:1|Give glory to the Lord|Confitemini Domino]], that is, praise Christ not only as man but also as true God, [[104:1|and call upon his name|et invocate nomen ejus]]. O holy Apostles and your successors, [[104:1|declare|Annuntiate]] [[104:1|his deeds|opera ejus]], namely Christ's, [[104:1|among the Gentiles|inter gentes]], that is, to all the pagans. Hence Paul in the Acts: [[Acts 13:46|behold|Ecce]], he says, [[Acts 13:46|we turn to the Gentiles|convertimur ad gentes]]; [[Acts 13:47|For so the Lord hath commanded us|sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus]].

paras.t: Narrate omnia mirabilia ejus, videlicet Christi, quæ in Evangelio scripta sunt: qualiter ab angelo est nuntiatus, a Virgine conceptus et natus, ab angelis ministratus, et alia ejus magnalia. De ejus annuntiatione Christus per Isaiam dixit: Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes longe, ad eos qui non audierunt de me; et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus.
paras.en: [[104:2|relate all his wondrous works|Narrate omnia mirabilia ejus]], namely Christ's, which are written in the Gospel: how he was announced by an angel, conceived and born of the Virgin, ministered to by angels, and his other great works. Of the proclaiming of him Christ said through Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes]] far off, [[Is 66:19|to them that have not heard of me|ad eos qui non audierunt de me]]; [[Is 66:19|And they shall declare my glory to the Gentiles|et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus]].

paras.t: Mementote, o omnes Christifideles, mirabilium ejus quæ fecit, assumendo pro vobis naturam humanam, conversando in mundo, animam suam ponendo pro impiis, lavando pedes discipulorum, instituendo Sacramentum corporis et sanguinis sui, longanimiter sustinendo ac præstolando peccatores, et vos misericorditer ad pœnitentiam invitando, gratiose justificando. Recolite quoque prodigia ejus: quomodo solo verbo mortuos suscitavit, quinque millia ex quinque panibus et duobus piscibus pavit, cæcum natum illuminavit, cordiumque secreta inspexit, mari, et vento imperavit, tertia die resurrexit, ostiis clausis ad discipulos introivit, cœlos conscendit, Spiritum Sanctum in visibili specie misit; et judicia oris ejus, id est, præceptorum, consiliorum, documentorum, omniumque evangelicorum Christi sermonum memores estote. Hæc namque recordanda sunt semper, eo quod dicat Salvator: Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei, et custodiunt illud. Unde et in Deuteronomio inducitur: Ne obliviscaris verborum Domini, et ne excidant de corde tuo cunctis diebus. Et in Proverbiis: Audi, fili, disciplinam patris tui, et ne dimittas legem matris tuæ, puta Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[104:5|Remember|Mementote]], O all you faithful of Christ, [[104:5|his marvellous works which he hath done|mirabilium ejus quæ fecit]]: in taking human nature for you, in living in the world, in laying down his life for the ungodly, in washing the feet of the disciples[[John 13:5||]], in instituting the Sacrament of his body and blood[[Matt 26:26||]], in patiently bearing with sinners and waiting for them, in mercifully inviting you to penance, in graciously justifying you. Call to mind also [[104:5|his wonders|prodigia ejus]]: how by a word alone he raised the dead[[John 11:43||]][[Luke 8:54||]], fed five thousand with five loaves and two fishes[[Luke 9:14||]], gave light to the man born blind, saw into the secrets of hearts, commanded the sea and the wind, rose again on the third day, came in to the disciples when the doors were shut, ascended into heaven, and sent the Holy Ghost in visible form; [[104:5|and the judgments of his mouth|et judicia oris ejus]]: that is, be mindful of the precepts, counsels and teachings, and of all the gospel sayings of Christ. For these are always to be remembered, since the Saviour says: [[Luke 11:28|blessed are they who hear the word of God and keep it|Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei, et custodiunt illud]]. Hence in Deuteronomy too it is put thus: [[Deut 4:9|Forget not the words|Ne obliviscaris verborum]] of the Lord, [[Deut 4:9|and let them not go out of thy heart all the days|et ne excidant de corde tuo cunctis diebus]]. And in Proverbs: [[Prov 1:8|My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother|Audi, fili, disciplinam patris tui, et ne dimittas legem matris tuæ]], namely the Church.

paras.t: Semen spirituale Abraham, id est, filii fidei et obedientiæ, qui credendo et obediendo sectamini Abraham patrem cunctorum credentium, qui usque ad filii immolationem paruit Deo, ut dicitur in Genesi. Hujus Patriarchæ filii sumus, plenissime immobiliterque credendo, atque nos ipsos Deo per pœnitentiam et obedientiam sacrificando. Filii spirituales Jacob, qui contra vitia colluctando, estis filii Jacob, qui interpretatur supplantator.
paras.en: [[104:6|O ye seed of Abraham|Semen spirituale Abraham]], his spiritual seed, that is, sons of faith and obedience, who by believing and obeying follow Abraham, the father of all believers, who obeyed God even to the sacrifice of his son, as is said in Genesis[[Gen 22:16||]]. We are sons of this Patriarch by believing most fully and unshakeably, and by sacrificing ourselves to God through penance and obedience. [[104:6|ye sons of Jacob|Filii spirituales Jacob]], his spiritual sons, who by wrestling against the vices are sons of Jacob, which is interpreted *supplanter*[[Gen 27:36||]].

paras.t: Ipse Christus est Dominus Deus noster: cui Thomas dixit, Dominus meus et Deus meus; in universa terra judicia ejus, id est, per totum mundum prædicata, scripta et divulgata sunt præcepta, consilia, atque justæ censuræ Domini Salvatoris, secundum quod ait Apostolus: Nunc prædicatum est omni creaturæ quæ sub cœlo est.
paras.en: [[104:7|He|Ipse]], Christ, [[104:7|is the Lord our God|Dominus Deus noster]]: he to whom Thomas said, [[John 20:28|My Lord and my God|Dominus meus et Deus meus]]; [[104:7|his judgments are in all the earth|in universa terra judicia ejus]]: that is, throughout the whole world the precepts, counsels and just sentences of the Lord the Saviour have been preached, written and spread abroad, according to what the Apostle says: Now it [[Col 1:23|is preached in all the creation that is under heaven|prædicatum est omni creaturæ quæ sub cœlo est]].

paras.t: Memor fuit ipse Christus in sæculum, id est in perpetuum, testamenti sui novi, quod in novissima Cœna instituit, in cujus institutione vetus Testamentum implevit et evacuavit. Hujus novi Testamenti memor fuit Christus in sæculum, quoniam fecit ipsum prædicari, sicut usque in finem sæculi permansurum; et talem prædicationem per certa miracula approbavit, quemadmodum scriptum est: Illi autem profecti, prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante, et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis. Verbi quod mandavit in mille, id est in omnes, generationes: ponitur enim hic numerus determinatum pro indeterminato. Jussit autem Christus verbum Evangelii omnibus prædicari, atque ab omnibus usque in finem mundi impleri, quemadmodum apud Matthæum ait Apostolis: Euntes, docete omnes gentes, docentes eos servare omnia quæ mandavi vobis. Propter quod alibi: Quid (inquit) dicitis mihi, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico?
paras.en: [[104:8|He hath remembered|Memor fuit]], Christ himself, [[104:8|for ever|in sæculum]], that is, perpetually, [[104:8|his covenant|testamenti sui]], his new one [the Latin *testamentum* means both covenant and testament], which he instituted at the Last Supper, in the institution of which he fulfilled the Old Testament and made it void. Christ remembered this New Testament for ever, since he caused it to be preached as one that would last until the end of the world; and he approved such preaching by sure miracles, as it is written: [[Mark 16:20|But they going forth preached every where: the Lord working withal, and confirming the word with signs that followed|Illi autem profecti, prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante, et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis]]. [[104:8|the word which he commanded to a thousand|Verbi quod mandavit in mille]], that is, to all, [[104:8|generations|generationes]]: for here a definite number is put for an indefinite one. For Christ ordered the word of the Gospel to be preached to all, and to be fulfilled by all until the end of the world, as he says to the Apostles in Matthew: [[Matt 28:19|Going therefore, teach ye all nations|Euntes, docete omnes gentes]], [[Matt 28:20|Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you|docentes eos servare omnia quæ mandavi vobis]]. Wherefore elsewhere: [[Luke 6:46|why|Quid]], he says, [[Luke 6:46|call you me, Lord, Lord; and do not the things which I say?|dicitis mihi, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico?]]

paras.t: Quod disposuit ad Abraham, id est ad spirituales filios ejus, sicut nunc dictum est. Et juramenti sui, id est firmæ promissionis factæ ad Isaac, id est ad populum christianum, non in se, sed in Domino gloriantem: qui ab Apostolo didicerunt semper gaudere, et in omnibus tribulationibus cordialiter exsultare, lætantes de hoc quod Christo per passionem conformantur, et cum electis in hoc sæculo corriguntur. Ex qua consideratione certissime sperant se filios esse illius, qui in Apocalypsi protestatur: Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo. Isaac quippe, risus vel gaudium interpretatur.
paras.en: [[104:9|Which he made to Abraham|Quod disposuit ad Abraham]], that is, to his spiritual sons, as has just been said. [[104:9|and his oath|Et juramenti sui]], that is, of the firm promise made [[104:9|to Isaac|ad Isaac]], that is, to the Christian people, glorying not in themselves but in the Lord[[2 Cor 10:17||]]: who have learned from the Apostle to rejoice always[[Phil 4:4||]], and in all tribulations to exult from the heart, glad that they are conformed to Christ through his passion, and are chastened with the elect in this world. From which consideration they hope most surely that they are the sons of him who declares in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]]. For Isaac is interpreted *laughter* or *joy*.

paras.t: Et statuit illud testamentum Jacob, id est Christifidelibus vitia conculcantibus, in præceptum fideliter observandum; et Israel, id est populo per fidem cœlestia contemplanti, in testamentum æternum: quatenus non exspectent aliam legem seu aliud testamentum futurum, sed sciant ipsum esse novissimum: propter quod appellatur et Novum, quia post legem Moysis datum est; et Æternum, quoniam alia lex ei nunquam succedet. Lex enim Antichristi erit perversitas atque abusio legis; nec erit a Deo, nec diu durabit, nec in toto legem Christi exstinguet.
paras.en: [[104:10|And he appointed the same|Et statuit illud]] covenant [[104:10|to Jacob|Jacob]], that is, to the faithful of Christ who trample the vices underfoot, [[104:10|for a law|in præceptum]] to be faithfully observed; [[104:10|and to Israel|et Israel]], that is, to the people that contemplates heavenly things by faith, [[104:10|for an everlasting testament|in testamentum æternum]]: so that they may not look for another law or another testament to come, but know that this is the last. For this reason it is called both *New*, because it was given after the law of Moses, and *Everlasting*, because no other law will ever succeed it. For the law of Antichrist will be a perversion and abuse of law; it will not be from God, nor will it last long, nor will it wholly extinguish the law of Christ.

paras.t: Dicens Christus populo in se credenti: Tibi dabo terram Chanaan, id est terram lacte et melle manantem, quæ est omnium terrarum egregia, Moyse contestante: per quam designatur terra viventium, patria Beatorum, ubi inebriantur ab ubertate domus Dei. Unde in Joanne: Vado, inquit, parare vobis locum; et iterum, Veniam et assumam vos ad me ipsum, ut ubi sum ego, et vos sitis. Funiculum hereditatis vestræ, id est partem cuilibet justo tradendam, seu per modum sortis cuilibet evenientem. Sic enim dat Christus electis terram vivorum, quod singulis tribuit certam mansionem in ea secundum exigentiam meritorum suorum. Propter quod ait: In domo Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt. Sicut igitur terra Chanaan data est filiis Israel per partes, secundum exigentiam sortium quas miserunt, sic regio Beatorum dividitur electis per mansiones, secundum congruentiam meritorum.
paras.en: [[104:11|Saying|Dicens]]: Christ, that is, saying to the people that believes in him: [[104:11|To thee will I give the land of Chanaan|Tibi dabo terram Chanaan]], that is, the land flowing with milk and honey, which is the choicest of all lands, as Moses testifies[[Deut 8:7||]]: by which is signified the land of the living, the fatherland of the Blessed, where they are inebriated with the plenty of the house of God[[Ps 35:9||]]. Hence in John: [[John 14:2|I go|Vado]], he says, [[John 14:2|to prepare a place for you|parare vobis locum]]; and again: [[John 14:3|I will come again and will take you to myself: that where I am, you also may be|Veniam et assumam vos ad me ipsum, ut ubi sum ego, et vos sitis]]. [[104:11|the lot of your inheritance|Funiculum hereditatis vestræ]] [*funiculus*, literally a little cord, the measuring line by which land was allotted], that is, the portion to be given to each just man, or falling to each by way of lot. For thus Christ gives the elect the land of the living, in that he assigns to each a certain mansion in it according to what his merits require. Wherefore he says: [[John 14:2|In my Father's house there are many mansions|In domo Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt]]. As, then, the land of Chanaan was given to the children of Israel in portions, according to the lots which they cast[[Jos 14:2||]], so the region of the Blessed is divided among the elect by mansions, according to the fittingness of their merits.

paras.t: Quum essent Christiani in primitiva Ecclesia numero brevi, scilicet centum viginti, ut patet in Actibus Apostolorum, paucissimi et incolæ ejus, id est, quum Christiani valde pauci essent, incolæ exsistentes (ad litteram) terræ Chanaan, quia in Jerusalem et Judæa primo incepit Ecclesia. Vel, Paucissimi incolæ ejus, id est terræ vivorum seu patriæ cœlestis: quia in principio Ecclesiæ paucissimi erant; imo et nunc (proh dolor!) pauci sunt, quibus illud Apostoli competit: Nostra conversatio in cœlis est.
paras.en: [[104:12|When they were|Quum essent]], namely the Christians in the primitive Church, [[104:12|but a small number|numero brevi]], that is, a hundred and twenty, as appears in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 1:15||]], [[104:12|yea very few, and sojourners therein|paucissimi et incolæ ejus]]: that is, when the Christians were very few, being sojourners (in the literal sense) in the land of Chanaan, because the Church began first in Jerusalem and Judæa. Or, [[104:12|very few, and sojourners therein|Paucissimi incolæ ejus]]: that is, of the land of the living, or the heavenly fatherland; for at the beginning of the Church they were very few; nay, even now (alas!) they are few to whom that saying of the Apostle applies: [[Phil 3:20|our conversation is in heaven|Nostra conversatio in cœlis est]].

paras.t: Et pertransierunt ipsi beati Apostoli, aliique discipuli, de gente in gentem, et de regno ad populum alterum. Hoc præcipue patet de Paulo, qui, sicut ipse testatur, perambulabat Macedoniam, Galatiam, Hispaniam, Italiam. Sic et Petrus primo prædicavit in Judæa, deinde in Antiochia, postremo in Italia. In omnem enim terram exivit sonus eorum.
paras.en: [[104:13|And they passed|Et pertransierunt]], namely the blessed Apostles themselves and the other disciples, [[104:13|from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people|de gente in gentem, et de regno ad populum alterum]]. This is especially plain of Paul, who, as he himself testifies, travelled through Macedonia, Galatia, Spain and Italy. So too Peter preached first in Judæa, then in Antioch, and lastly in Italy. For [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem enim terram exivit sonus eorum]].

paras.t: Non reliquit Christus hominem quemquam nocere eis, quantum ad interiorem salutem: quia licet foras corporaliter affligebantur, hoc tamen ad magnum interioris hominis conferebat profectum, sicut ad Romanos ait Apostolus: Scimus quoniam diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum. Propter quod S. Paulus persecutores suos non reputavit adversarios, sed promotores, dicendo: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Hinc quoque scriptum est: Quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni æmulatores fueritis? Ad litteram etiam Christus multos perversos prohibuit a corporali Apostolorum ac reliquorum Sanctorum nocumento, quemadmodum in Actibus Apostolorum leguntur Apostoli a carcere per angelum liberati. Et corripuit pro eis reges. Multos namque reges et principes Deus improvisa atque horribili morte occidit propter persecutionem in Christianos, prout in Actibus Apostolorum de Herode habetur, quem angelus Dei percussit; et in legendis Sanctorum hoc copiose narratur. Corripuit autem eos non solum monendo, sed flagellando; non sermone, sed opere, dicens:
paras.en: [[104:14|He suffered no man to hurt them|Non reliquit Christus hominem quemquam nocere eis]]: Christ, that is, let no one hurt them as regards their inward salvation; for although they were afflicted outwardly in the body, this nonetheless brought great profit to the inner man, as the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 8:28|we know that to them that love God all things work together unto good|Scimus quoniam diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum]]. Wherefore St. Paul reckoned his persecutors not adversaries but promoters, saying: [[Rom 8:31|If God be for us, who is against us?|Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?]] Hence too it is written: [[1 Pet 3:13|who is he that can hurt you, if you be zealous of good?|Quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni æmulatores fueritis?]] In the literal sense also Christ kept many wicked men from doing bodily harm to the Apostles and the other Saints, as we read in the Acts of the Apostles that the Apostles were freed from prison by an angel[[Acts 5:19||]]. [[104:14|and he reproved kings for their sakes|Et corripuit pro eis reges]]. For God slew many kings and princes by a sudden and horrible death because of their persecution of the Christians, as is related in the Acts of the Apostles of Herod, whom the angel of God struck[[Acts 12:23||]]; and this is told at length in the legends of the Saints. And he reproved them not only by warning but by scourging; not by word but by deed, saying:

paras.t: Nolite tangere violenter christos meos, id est Christianos in Baptismate unctos: qui etiam corporaliter unguntur in Confirmatione et Ordinatione. Spiritualiter vero unguntur Spiritu Sancto, juxta illud Apostoli ad Galatas: Misit Deus Spiritum Filii sui in corda nostra, clamantem, Abba (Pater). Et in Prophetis meis, id est in prædicatoribus verbi Dei, qui de futuro judicio, de venturo sæculo Beatorum, de æterna quoque damnatione reproborum aliis sermocinantur, nolite malignari. Talium namque injuriam Deus districte ulciscitur, in tantum ut per Zachariam testetur: Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei.
paras.en: [[104:15|Touch ye not|Nolite tangere]] violently [[104:15|my anointed|christos meos]] [*christos*, literally my christs, that is, my anointed ones], that is, Christians anointed in Baptism, who are also anointed bodily in Confirmation and in Holy Orders. And spiritually they are anointed with the Holy Ghost, according to that saying of the Apostle to the Galatians: [[Gal 4:6|God hath sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying: Abba, Father|Misit Deus Spiritum Filii sui in corda nostra, clamantem, Abba (Pater)]]. And [[104:15|to my prophets|Et in Prophetis meis]], that is, to the preachers of the word of God, who speak to others of the judgment to come, of the world to come of the Blessed, and also of the eternal damnation of the reprobate, [[104:15|do no evil|nolite malignari]]. For God sternly avenges the injury done to such men, so much so that he testifies through Zacharias: [[Zach 2:8|he that toucheth you, toucheth the apple of my eye|Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei]].

paras.t: Et vocavit Deus Trinitas famem super terram. De qua fame scriptum est: Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et mittam famem in terra: non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Dei. Hæc fames præcessit Christi adventum, quoniam tunc multo tempore non erat Propheta usque ad Joannem Baptistam. Idcirco tunc maxima erat penuria spiritualis alimenti, videlicet prædicationis verbi Dei, quam boni semper desideraverunt.
paras.en: [[104:16|And he called|Et vocavit]], namely God the Trinity, [[104:16|a famine upon the land|famem super terram]]. Of which famine it is written: [[Amos 8:11|Behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will send forth a famine into the land: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst of water, but of hearing the word of the Lord|Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et mittam famem in terra: non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Dei]]. This famine went before the coming of Christ, since for a long time then there was no Prophet until John the Baptist. Therefore there was then the greatest dearth of spiritual food, that is, of the preaching of the word of God, which the good always longed for.

paras.t: Unde propter sublevandam hanc famem, misit Deus Pater ante eos hanc famem patientes, virum, scilicet Christum: qui a principio suæ conceptionis vir fuit, juxta illud prophetæ Jeremiæ dictum, Mulier circumdabit virum. Misit enim Pater Filium suum ad homines, ut eos spiritualiter satiaret, secundum quod Christus ait Judæis: Pater meus dat vobis panem de cœlo verum; et denuo, Operamini non cibum qui perit, sed qui permanet in vitam æternam. Hunc enim Pater signavit.
paras.en: Hence, to relieve this famine, God the Father [[104:17|sent|misit]] [[104:17|before them|ante eos]], before those suffering this famine, [[104:17|a man|virum]], namely Christ, who was a man from the first moment of his conception, according to that saying of the prophet Jeremias: [[Jer 31:22|A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Mulier circumdabit virum]]. For the Father sent his Son to men to satisfy them spiritually, according to what Christ says to the Jews: [[John 6:32|my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven|Pater meus dat vobis panem de cœlo verum]]; and again: [[John 6:27|Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that which endureth unto life everlasting|Operamini non cibum qui perit, sed qui permanet in vitam æternam]]. [[John 6:27|For him hath God, the Father, sealed|Hunc enim Pater signavit]].

paras.t: In servum venundatus est Joseph. Amabilis ille sanctusque patriarcha Joseph, in persona, opere ac persecutione, figura exstitit Christi. Nam ejus venditio pro triginta argenteis facta, ut dicitur in Genesi, Christi venditionem præfiguravit pro totidem argenteis factam, ut legitur apud Matthæum. Similiter translatio Joseph in aliam regionem, Christi missionem in mundum; et incarceratio Joseph, Christi captivitatem ac passionem signavit. Itaque, In servum, id est in ministrum voluntatis impiorum, venundatus est Joseph, id est Christus per Joseph signatus. Vendidit namque eum Judas Iscariotes Judæis, ut facerent ei omnia quæ optarent: quod et fecerunt, quemadmodum, Lucæ testante, Christus eis locutus est: Hæc est hora vestra et potestas tenebrarum, id est, jam permittitur vobis dominari in me, et facere mihi quod vultis.
paras.en: [[104:17|Joseph, who was sold for a slave|In servum venundatus est Joseph]]. That lovable and holy patriarch Joseph was a figure of Christ in his person, his work and his persecution. For his sale for thirty pieces of silver, as is said in Genesis[[Gen 37:28||]] [Genesis has twenty pieces of silver], prefigured the sale of Christ for as many pieces of silver, as we read in Matthew[[Matt 26:15||]]. Likewise the removal of Joseph into another country signified the sending of Christ into the world; and the imprisonment of Joseph, Christ's captivity and passion. Thus: [[104:17|for a slave|In servum]], that is, as the minister of the will of the ungodly, [[104:17|Joseph, who was sold|venundatus est Joseph]], that is, Christ, signified by Joseph. For Judas Iscariot sold him to the Jews, that they might do to him all they wished; which they also did, as, on Luke's testimony, Christ said to them: [[Luke 22:53|this is your hour and the power of darkness|Hæc est hora vestra et potestas tenebrarum]]; that is, now it is permitted you to lord it over me, and to do to me what you will.

paras.t: Humiliaverunt Judæi in compedibus, id est in vinculis, pedes ejus, scilicet Christi, id est, ipsum Christum vinculis ligaverunt. Per pedum enim humiliationem, totius corporis ligatio designatur: et forte in nocte, quando erat in domo pontificis, ligati erant sanctissimi Salvatoris pedes. Miserunt quoque Judæi catenam in collum Christi, dum eum comprehenderunt: quæ postea in Jerusalem longo tempore ostendebatur peregrinis cum devotione ingenti. Ferrum, id est dolor sensibilis, compassio magna, vehemensque tristitia, pertransiit animam ejus, scilicet Christi, tempore passionis. Propter quod dixit, Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem; et, Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?
paras.en: [[104:18|They humbled|Humiliaverunt]], namely the Jews, [[104:18|in fetters|in compedibus]], that is, in bonds, [[104:18|his feet|pedes ejus]], namely Christ's: that is, they bound Christ himself with bonds. For by the humbling of the feet the binding of the whole body is signified; and perhaps in the night, when he was in the house of the high priest, the feet of the most holy Saviour were bound. The Jews also put a chain on Christ's neck when they seized him, which was afterwards shown for a long time in Jerusalem to pilgrims, with great devotion. [[104:18|the iron|Ferrum]], that is, sensible pain, great compassion and vehement sorrow, [[104:18|pierced his soul|pertransiit animam ejus]], namely Christ's, in the time of the passion. Wherefore he said: [[Matt 26:38|My soul is sorrowful even unto death|Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem]]; and: [[Mark 15:34|My God, My God, Why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?]]

paras.t: Donec veniret verbum ejus, id est, quousque impleretur sermo ejus quem dixerat, Etenim ea quæ sunt de me, finem habent. Vel, Verbum ejus quod dixit: Consummatum est; et, Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum. Vel, Verbum ejus, id est, donec implerentur omnia quæ de Christi passione prophetata fuerunt. Eloquium Domini inflammavit eum. Quidquid enim Christus ut homo dixit, ex divina inspiratione processit. Inflammavit autem eloquium Dei Christum, quoniam virtuosissima et ignea verba prædicando effudit, eloquentissimus fuit, et quidquid sibi futurum erat, prædixit. Hinc enim apud Matthæum scriptum est, Erat Jesus docens, sicut potestatem habens, non sicut Scribæ et Pharisæi; et apud Joannem, Nunquam sic locutus est homo, sicut hic loquitur.
paras.en: [[104:19|Until his word came|Donec veniret verbum ejus]]: that is, until the saying should be fulfilled which he had spoken: [[Luke 22:37|For the things concerning me have an end|Etenim ea quæ sunt de me, finem habent]]. Or, [[104:19|his word|Verbum ejus]]: the word he spoke, [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]]; and, [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]. Or, [[104:19|his word|Verbum ejus]]: that is, until all things should be fulfilled that had been prophesied of Christ's passion. [[104:19|The word of the Lord inflamed him|Eloquium Domini inflammavit eum]]. For whatever Christ said as man proceeded from divine inspiration. And the word of God inflamed Christ, because in preaching he poured out most powerful and fiery words, he was most eloquent, and he foretold whatever was to befall him. Hence it is written in Matthew: [[Matt 7:29|he was teaching them as one having power, and not as the scribes and Pharisees|Erat Jesus docens, sicut potestatem habens, non sicut Scribæ et Pharisæi]]; and in John: [[John 7:46|Never did man speak like this man|Nunquam sic locutus est homo, sicut hic loquitur]].

paras.t: Misit rex, id est Deus sublimis: de quo in libro Esther dicitur, Domine, Rex omnipotens; et salvavit eum, id est, Christum de morte et monumento ac vinculis passibilitatis eduxit, quemadmodum in Actibus Petrus testatus est: Deus suscitavit Jesum, solutis doloribus inferni. Principes populorum, id est, Deus omnium gentium Dominus misit, virtutem suam exercendo, et dimisit eum, id est, Christum de limbo inferni reduxit, juxta illud Actuum: Neque derelictus est in inferno, neque caro ejus vidit corruptionem.
paras.en: [[104:20|The king sent|Misit rex]], that is, God most high, of whom it is said in the book of Esther: [[Esth 13:9|O Lord, Lord, almighty king|Domine, Rex omnipotens]]; [[104:20|and he released him|et salvavit eum]] [Denis reads *salvavit*, saved, where the Vulgate has *solvit*, released]: that is, he brought Christ out of death and the tomb and the bonds of passibility [that is, of being subject to suffering], as Peter testified in the Acts: [[Acts 2:24|God hath raised up|Deus suscitavit]] Jesus, [[Acts 2:24|having loosed the sorrows of hell|solutis doloribus inferni]]. [[104:20|the ruler of the people|Principes populorum]], that is, God, the Lord of all nations, sent, exercising his power, [[104:20|and he set him at liberty|et dimisit eum]], that is, he brought Christ back from the limbo of hell, according to that saying of the Acts: [[Acts 2:31|neither was he left in hell: neither did his flesh see corruption|Neque derelictus est in inferno, neque caro ejus vidit corruptionem]].

paras.t: Constituit eum dominum domus suæ, id est caput Ecclesiæ, et principem omnis possessionis suæ, id est totius creaturæ. Ideo Joannes de Christo ait: Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus. Et apud Matthæum Christus ait: Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra. Præfecit autem Deus Trinitas Christum hominem non solum militanti, sed etiam triumphanti Ecclesiæ, juxta illud Apostoli ad Ephesios: Deus constituit eum in cœlestibus ad dexteram suam, supra omnem principatum et potestatem et virtutem et dominationem. Hujus quoque figura est, quod Joseph constitutus est dominus universæ terræ Ægypti, et appellatus est, Salvator mundi, ut legitur in Genesi. Sed his obviare videtur quod in libro Job habetur: Quem constituit Deus alium super terram? aut quem posuit super orbem quem fabricatus est? Videtur ergo, quod Deus Christum non præposuit omni creaturæ in principem. Et respondendum, quod illa auctoritas vult tantum, quod Deus non præfecit alium in provisorem ac principem universi, ita quod ipse desierit esse provisor princepsque mundi: et hoc verum est.
paras.en: [[104:21|He made him master of his house|Constituit eum dominum domus suæ]], that is, head of the Church, [[104:21|and ruler of all his possession|et principem omnis possessionis suæ]], that is, of the whole creation. Therefore John says of Christ: [[John 3:35|The Father loveth the Son: and he hath given all things into his hand|Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus]]. And in Matthew Christ says: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]. Now God the Trinity set Christ as man over not only the Church militant but also the Church triumphant, according to that saying of the Apostle to the Ephesians about God [[Eph 1:20|setting him on his right hand in the heavenly places|Deus constituit eum in cœlestibus ad dexteram suam]], [[Eph 1:21|Above all principality and power and virtue and dominion|supra omnem principatum et potestatem et virtutem et dominationem]]. This too has its figure in that Joseph was made lord of the whole land of Egypt[[Gen 41:41||]], and was called the Saviour of the world[[Gen 41:45||]], as we read in Genesis. But against this seems to stand what is found in the book of Job: [[Job 34:13|What other hath he appointed over the earth? or whom hath he set over the world which he made?|Quem constituit Deus alium super terram? aut quem posuit super orbem quem fabricatus est?]] It seems, then, that God did not set Christ over all creation as its ruler. The answer is that that text means only that God did not set another as provider and ruler of the universe in such a way that he himself ceased to be the provider and ruler of the world: and this is true.

paras.t: Sic ergo Deus prætulit Christum Ecclesiæ, ut erudiret principes ejus, id est Apostolos: de quibus dictum est supra, Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham; sicut semetipsum, id est tam fideliter, ac si essent idem cum ipso. Vel, Sicut semetipsum, id est de rebus divinis atque cœlestibus per illustrationem Spiritus Sancti, de quibus ipse per Spiritum Sanctum erat edoctus. Hoc autem Christus eatenus egit, ut diceret: Jam non dicam vos servos, sed amicos meos, quia omnia quæcumque audivi a Patre meo, nota feci vobis. Et senes ejus, id est prædictos principes atque Apostolos et imitatores eorum, qui omnes morum gravitate senes fuerunt, prudentiam, id est notitiam de agendis seu moribus, doceret. Hoc Christus in Evangelio copiosissime fecit: in quo moralissima documenta, optima consilia atque saluberrima mandata proposuit.
paras.en: Thus, then, God set Christ over the Church, [[104:22|That he might instruct his princes|ut erudiret principes ejus]], that is, the Apostles, of whom it was said above: [[Ps 46:10|The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham|Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham]]; [[104:22|as himself|sicut semetipsum]], that is, as faithfully as if they were one with him. Or, [[104:22|as himself|Sicut semetipsum]]: that is, about divine and heavenly things, through the enlightening of the Holy Ghost, in which he himself had been taught by the Holy Ghost. And Christ did this so far as to say: [[John 15:15|I will not now call you servants|Jam non dicam vos servos]], but my friends, [[John 15:15|because all things, whatsoever I have heard of my Father, I have made known to you|quia omnia quæcumque audivi a Patre meo, nota feci vobis]]. [[104:22|and teach his ancients|Et senes ejus]], that is, the aforesaid princes and Apostles and their imitators, who were all ancients in the gravity of their ways, [[104:22|wisdom|prudentiam]] [*prudentia*: prudence, the practical wisdom of conduct], that is, knowledge of what is to be done, or of morals. This Christ did most abundantly in the Gospel, in which he set forth most moral teachings, the best counsels and most wholesome commandments.

paras.t: Et intravit Israel, id est Christus Deum semper per speciem videns, in Ægyptum, id est in mundum, per incarnationem, sicut apud Joannem asserit: Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum. Per Ægyptum namque mundus signatur, prout in Apocalypsi dicitur: Jacebunt corpora eorum in platea civitatis magnæ, quæ spiritualiter vocatur Sodoma et Ægyptus, ubi Dominus eorum crucifixus est. Et Jacob, id est Christus omnium vitiorum supplantator, quia peccatum non fecit, sicut de se ipso profitetur: Venit ad me princeps hujus mundi, et in me non habet quidquam; accola, id est viator et peregrinus, fuit in terra Cham, id est in Ægypto seu mundo, sicut expositum est. Unde Jeremias alloquens Christum: Quare, inquit, quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum?
paras.en: [[104:23|And Israel went|Et intravit Israel]], that is, Christ, who always sees God by sight [*per speciem*, face to face, not by faith], [[104:23|into Egypt|in Ægyptum]], that is, into the world, through the incarnation, as he declares in John: [[John 16:28|I came forth from the Father and am come into the world|Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum]]. For by Egypt the world is signified, as is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 11:8|their bodies shall lie in the streets of the great city which is called spiritually, Sodom and Egypt: where their Lord also was crucified|Jacebunt corpora eorum in platea civitatis magnæ, quæ spiritualiter vocatur Sodoma et Ægyptus, ubi Dominus eorum crucifixus est]]. [[104:23|and Jacob|Et Jacob]], that is, Christ, the supplanter of all vices, because he [[1 Pet 2:22|did no sin|peccatum non fecit]], as he professes of himself: [[John 14:30|the prince of this world|princeps hujus mundi]] cometh to me, [[John 14:30|and in me he hath not any thing|et in me non habet quidquam]]; [[104:23|was a sojourner|accola]], that is, a wayfarer and pilgrim, [[104:23|in the land of Cham|fuit in terra Cham]], that is, in Egypt, or the world, as has been explained. Hence Jeremias, addressing Christ: [[Jer 14:8|why|Quare]], he says, [[Jer 14:8|wilt thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man turning in to lodge?|quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum?]]

paras.t: Et auxit Christus populum suum fidelem vehementer merito et numero, maxime in primitiva Ecclesia per prædicationem Apostolorum, totum pene mundum convertendo ad fidem. Propter quod in Actibus Apostolorum Lucas affirmat: Dominus augebat quotidie qui salvi fierent. Et firmavit eum, scilicet populum christianum, super inimicos ejus, id est mundum, carnem ac dæmonem. Dedit enim ipsis virtutem resistendi atque prævalendi tentationibus dæmonis, concupiscentiis carnis, persecutionibus hominum impiorum; et tandem subjecit Romanum imperium fidei christianæ tempore Constantini. Unde in Michæa dicitur: Exaltabitur manus tua super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui peribunt. Et alibi: Gens et regnum quod non servierit tibi, peribit.
paras.en: [[104:24|And he increased|Et auxit]], namely Christ, [[104:24|his people|populum suum]], his faithful people, [[104:24|exceedingly|vehementer]] in merit and in number, above all in the primitive Church through the preaching of the Apostles, converting almost the whole world to the faith. Wherefore Luke affirms in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 2:47|the Lord increased daily together such as should be saved|Dominus augebat quotidie qui salvi fierent]]. [[104:24|and strengthened them|Et firmavit eum]], namely the Christian people, [[104:24|over their enemies|super inimicos ejus]], that is, the world, the flesh and the devil. For he gave them the power of resisting and overcoming the temptations of the devil, the concupiscences of the flesh and the persecutions of ungodly men[[Matt 10:1||]][[Matt 10:8||]][[Mark 16:17||]]; and at length he subjected the Roman empire to the Christian faith in the time of Constantine. Hence it is said in Micheas: [[Mich 5:9|Thy hand shall be lifted up over thy enemies, and all thy enemies shall be cut off|Exaltabitur manus tua super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui peribunt]]. And elsewhere: [[Is 60:12|the nation and the kingdom that will not serve thee, shall perish|Gens et regnum quod non servierit tibi, peribit]] [the margin gives Is. ix, 12; the words are those of Is 60:12].

paras.t: Convertit cor eorum, ut odirent populum ejus: id est, Christus justo judicio converti permisit corda infidelium et pravorum in odium Christianorum; et dolum facerent in servos ejus, videlicet Christianos. Hoc odium et dolum hunc habuerunt primo Judæi contra primitivam Ecclesiam, ut patet frequenter in Actibus Apostolorum. Deinde imperatores Romani cum satellitibus suis invidiose atque dolose egerunt contra Ecclesiam Christi, multa millia martyrum occidendo. Postremo hæretici falsique fratres hoc faciunt.
paras.en: [[104:25|He turned their heart to hate his people|Convertit cor eorum, ut odirent populum ejus]]: that is, Christ by a just judgment permitted the hearts of the unbelieving and the wicked to be turned to hatred of the Christians; [[104:25|and to deal deceitfully with his servants|et dolum facerent in servos ejus]], namely the Christians. This hatred and this deceit the Jews first had against the primitive Church, as appears often in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 13:50||]][[Acts 14:18||]][[Acts 18:12||]]. Then the Roman emperors with their henchmen acted enviously and deceitfully against the Church of Christ, slaying many thousands of martyrs. Lastly heretics and false brethren do this.

paras.t: Misit Moysen servum suum, Aaron quem elegit ipsum. Per Moysen et Aaron ad filios Israel missos in Ægyptum, designantur Apostoli, in totum orbem destinati ad convertendum populum electorum.
paras.en: [[104:26|He sent Moses his servant: Aaron the man whom he had chosen|Misit Moysen servum suum, Aaron quem elegit ipsum]]. By Moses and Aaron, sent to the children of Israel in Egypt, are signified the Apostles, sent into the whole world to convert the people of the elect.

paras.t: Posuit Christus in eis, id est in Apostolis et eorum successoribus, verba signorum suorum et prodigiorum, quia per eos magna miracula fecit, in terra Cham, id est in toto mundo per terram Cham significato. Unde in Matthæo dixit Apostolis: Infirmos curate, mortuos suscitate, leprosos mundate, dæmones ejicite.
paras.en: [[104:27|He gave them power|Posuit Christus in eis]]: Christ, that is, put into them, the Apostles and their successors, [[104:27|to shew them signs, and his wonders|verba signorum suorum et prodigiorum]] [literally *the words of his signs and wonders*], for through them he worked great miracles, [[104:27|in the land of Cham|in terra Cham]], that is, in the whole world, signified by the land of Cham. Hence in Matthew he said to the Apostles: [[Matt 10:8|Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out devils|Infirmos curate, mortuos suscitate, leprosos mundate, dæmones ejicite]].

paras.t: Misit tenebras, id est cæcitatem mentis in animas reproborum, et obscuravit permissive intellectum eorum; et non exacerbavit sermones suos, id est, benigne illuminavit, ad pœnitentiam quoque recepit credere et obedire volentes, et ita minas suas relaxavit. Hæc est prima plaga hominum mundanorum, ex qua aliæ sex nascuntur sequentes.
paras.en: [[104:28|He sent darkness|Misit tenebras]], that is, blindness of mind, into the souls of the reprobate, [[104:28|and made it obscure|et obscuravit]]: that is, he darkened their understanding, by permitting it; [[104:28|and grieved not his words|et non exacerbavit sermones suos]] [*exacerbavit*, literally made bitter]: that is, he kindly enlightened, and also received to penance, those willing to believe and obey, and so relaxed his threats. This is the first plague of worldly men, from which the six others that follow are born.

paras.t: Convertit aquas eorum in sanguinem: id est, sapientiam eorum fieri permisit carnalem, animalem ac diabolicam, ita ut simplicitatem fidei mente superba contemnerent, sacramque Scripturam perverse exponerent: quod ad hæreticos maxime pertinet. Et occidit pisces eorum: id est, animas discipulorum talium expositorum ac magistrorum, mori seu sine vera fide et gratia esse permisit. Discipulos enim tanquam pisces quosdam colligunt sibi doctores.
paras.en: [[104:29|He turned their waters into blood|Convertit aquas eorum in sanguinem]]: that is, he permitted their wisdom to become carnal, sensual [*animalis*: of the natural man, as opposed to the spiritual] and devilish, so that with proud mind they despised the simplicity of faith and expounded Holy Scripture perversely: which belongs above all to heretics. [[104:29|and destroyed their fish|Et occidit pisces eorum]]: that is, he permitted the souls of the disciples of such expounders and masters to die, or to be without true faith and grace. For teachers gather disciples to themselves like so many fish.

paras.t: Et dedit terra eorum, id est, corda hominum mundanorum, ranas, id est garrulam loquacitatem et strepitum peccatorum, sicut ad Timotheum dicit Apostolus: Sermo eorum ut cancer serpit; in penetralibus regum, id est in domibus atque palatiis principum; ipsorum hominum jam dictorum. Ipsi enim suis adulationibus et fraudulentis sermonibus sibi alliciunt principes et potentes, atque cum eis conversari laborant.
paras.en: [[104:30|Their land brought forth|Et dedit terra eorum]], that is, the hearts of worldly men, [[104:30|frogs|ranas]], that is, the chattering talkativeness and din of sinners, as the Apostle says to Timothy: [[2 Tim 2:17|their speech spreadeth like a canker|Sermo eorum ut cancer serpit]]; [[104:30|in the inner chambers of their kings|in penetralibus regum]], that is, in the houses and palaces of princes; *their* kings, that is, of the men just mentioned. For by their flatteries and deceitful speech they draw princes and the powerful to themselves, and strive to keep company with them.

paras.t: Dixit, et venit cynomyia et scinifes. Per has muscas et bestias dire pungentes, intelliguntur detractores Deo odibiles, et remorsus conscientiæ peccatricis, seu stimuli synderesis, quæ semper inclinatur ad bonum, et remurmurat malo. Quapropter Isaias ait: Vermis eorum non morietur.
paras.en: [[104:31|He spoke, and there came divers sorts of flies and sciniphs|Dixit, et venit cynomyia et scinifes]]. By these flies and beasts that sting cruelly are understood [[Rom 1:30|Detractors, hateful to God|detractores Deo odibiles]], and the remorse of the sinful conscience, or the goads of synderesis [that is, the natural habit of the mind by which it knows the first principles of right action], which always inclines to good and murmurs against evil. Wherefore Isaias says: [[Is 66:24|their worm shall not die|Vermis eorum non morietur]].

paras.t: Posuit pluvias eorum grandinem: id est, pro rore ac refrigerio gratiæ Dei dedit Deus incredulis graves sollicitudines et afflictiones cordis multiplices, juxta illud in libro Job: Angustia vallabit impium sicut regem qui paratur ad prælium. Et iterum: Sonitus terroris semper in auribus impii; et quum pax sit, ille semper insidias suspicatur. Posuit et ignem comburentem in terra ipsorum, id est concupiscentiam malam in corpore impiorum, secundum quod ad Romanos dicit Apostolus: Tradidit illos Deus in passiones ignominiæ, ut contumeliis afficiant corpora sua.
paras.en: [[104:32|He gave them hail for rain|Posuit pluvias eorum grandinem]]: that is, instead of the dew and refreshment of God's grace, God gave the unbelieving heavy cares and manifold afflictions of heart, according to that saying in the book of Job: [[Job 15:24|distress shall surround him, as a king that is prepared for the battle|Angustia vallabit impium sicut regem qui paratur ad prælium]]. And again: [[Job 15:21|The sound of dread is always in his ears: and when there is peace, he always suspecteth treason|Sonitus terroris semper in auribus impii; et quum pax sit, ille semper insidias suspicatur]]. He set also [[104:32|a burning fire in the land|ignem comburentem in terra ipsorum]], that is, evil concupiscence in the body of the ungodly, according to what the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 1:26|God delivered them up to shameful affections|Tradidit illos Deus in passiones ignominiæ]], [[Rom 1:24|to dishonour their own bodies|ut contumeliis afficiant corpora sua]].

paras.t: Dixit, et venit locusta et bruchus, cujus non erat numerus. Per locustam et bruchum (quæ sunt bestiæ parvæ, omnem herbam et fructum terræ vorantes) intelliguntur reiteratores vitiorum deploratorum, seu mentis elatio et gloria vana. Hæc enim omnem mentis virorem et gratiam destruunt, et pristinæ conversationis fructum evacuant.
paras.en: [[104:34|He spoke, and the locust came, and the bruchus, of which there was no number|Dixit, et venit locusta et bruchus, cujus non erat numerus]]. By the locust and the bruchus (which are small beasts that devour every herb and the fruit of the earth) are understood those who fall back into vices they have already bewailed, or loftiness of mind and vainglory. For these destroy all the greenness and grace of the mind, and bring to nothing the fruit of their former way of life.

paras.t: Et percussit omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti: id est, fidem, totius spiritualis ædificationis principium, abstulit Deus ab animo perversorum; sicque percussit primitias omnis laboris eorum, quoniam sine fide nihil acceptum est Deo. Nam qui incredulus est, infideliter agit, ut dicitur in Isaia. Secundum Apostolum quoque, Omne quod non est ex fide, peccatum est.
paras.en: [[104:36|And he slew all the firstborn in their land|Et percussit omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti]] [Denis reads *in terra Ægypti*, in the land of Egypt]: that is, God took away from the mind of the perverse faith, the beginning of the whole spiritual building; and so he struck [[104:36|the firstfruits of all their labour|primitias omnis laboris eorum]], since without faith nothing is acceptable to God[[Heb 11:6||]]. For [[Is 21:2|he that is unfaithful dealeth unfaithfully|qui incredulus est, infideliter agit]], as is said in Isaias. According to the Apostle too, [[Rom 14:23|all that is not of faith is sin|Omne quod non est ex fide, peccatum est]] [the margin gives Rom. xiv, 13].

paras.t: Et eduxit Christus eos, id est fideles et electos de spirituali Ægypto, et communione malorum, ac tenebris ignorantiæ, cum argento, id est cum scientia rerum creatarum, et auro, id est sapientia divinorum. Vel, Cum argento, id est cum fide; et auro, id est cum caritate: de qua in Apocalypsi dicitur, Suadeo tibi emere a me aurum ignitum, probatum. Vel, Cum argento et auro, id est cum naturali philosophia et studio, quæ a philosophis accommodaverunt, et secum tulerunt ad Christum conversi. Datum est enim illis philosophari propter nos, quatenus naturali philosophia utamur ad obsequium fidei christianæ. Et non erat in tribubus eorum, id est in congregationibus Christianorum, infirmus, in anima, quia et Paulus ait: Quum infirmor, tunc potens sum. Nam virtus in infirmitate perficitur.
paras.en: [[104:37|And he brought them out|Et eduxit Christus eos]], namely Christ: that is, the faithful and elect, out of the spiritual Egypt, and the fellowship of the wicked, and the darkness of ignorance, [[104:37|with silver|cum argento]], that is, with the knowledge of created things, [[104:37|and gold|et auro]], that is, the wisdom of divine things. Or, [[104:37|with silver|Cum argento]], that is, with faith; [[104:37|and gold|et auro]], that is, with charity, of which it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:18|I counsel thee to buy of me gold, fire tried|Suadeo tibi emere a me aurum ignitum, probatum]]. Or, [[104:37|with silver and gold|Cum argento et auro]], that is, with natural philosophy and study, which they borrowed from the philosophers and, on being converted to Christ, carried away with them [as Israel borrowed vessels of silver and gold from the Egyptians and took them out of Egypt]. For it was given to the philosophers to philosophize for our sake, so that we might use natural philosophy in the service of the Christian faith. [[104:37|and there was not among their tribes|Et non erat in tribubus eorum]], that is, in the congregations of the Christians, [[104:37|one that was feeble|infirmus]] in soul, for Paul too says: [[2 Cor 12:10|when I am weak, then am I powerful|Quum infirmor, tunc potens sum]]. For [[2 Cor 12:9|power is made perfect in infirmity|virtus in infirmitate perficitur]].

paras.t: Lætata est Ægyptus in profectione eorum: id est, homines sæculares, impii atque increduli, gavisi sunt de separatione Christianorum ab ipsis; quia incubuit, id est cecidit, timor eorum, id est Christianorum, super eos, id est infideles. Hoc interdum ad litteram contigit, quod Christus infideles evidenter percussit, propter persecutiones Christianis illatas, sicut Ambrosius refert in legenda S. Agnetis: et tunc infideles optabant Christianos abire a se, ne durius affligerentur.
paras.en: [[104:38|Egypt was glad when they departed|Lætata est Ægyptus in profectione eorum]]: that is, worldly men, ungodly and unbelieving, rejoiced at the separation of the Christians from them; [[104:38|for the fear of them|timor eorum]], that is, of the Christians, [[104:38|lay|incubuit]], that is, fell, [[104:38|upon them|super eos]], that is, upon the unbelievers. This sometimes happened literally, in that Christ manifestly struck the unbelievers for the persecutions inflicted on the Christians, as Ambrose relates in the legend of St. Agnes; and then the unbelievers wished the Christians to go away from them, lest they should be afflicted more harshly.

paras.t: Expandit Christus nubem, id est gratiam Spiritus Sancti, in protectionem eorum, id est in defensionem et obumbrationem animarum fidelium contra æstus tentationum et concupiscentiarum carnalium; et ignem, id est, radium veritatis et sapientiam salutarem, seu caritatis fervorem expandit, imo infudit cordi eorum, ut luceret eis per noctem, id est in omni adversitate atque periculo, ne errarent in via hujus exsilii, sed gratia duce perducerentur ad patriam, sicut Apostolus loquitur: Deus custodiat corda vestra et intelligentias vestras. Unde et Christus in Evangelio: Ignem, inquit, veni mittere in terram, et quid volo nisi ut ardeat?
