paras.en: [[104:39|He spread a cloud|Expandit Christus nubem]], namely Christ, that is, the grace of the Holy Ghost, [[104:39|for their protection|in protectionem eorum]], that is, for the defence and overshadowing of faithful souls against the heats of temptations and of carnal concupiscences; [[104:39|and fire|et ignem]], that is, the ray of truth and saving wisdom, or the fervour of charity, he spread, nay poured, into their heart, [[104:39|to give them light in the night|ut luceret eis per noctem]], that is, in every adversity and danger, lest they should stray on the way of this exile, but be led through to the fatherland with grace for their guide; as the Apostle says: May God [[Phil 4:7|keep your hearts and minds|custodiat corda vestra et intelligentias vestras]]. Hence Christ too says in the Gospel: [[Luke 12:49|I am come to cast fire on the earth|veni mittere in terram]], [[Luke 12:49|And what will I, but that it be kindled?|et quid volo nisi ut ardeat?]]

paras.t: Petierunt fideles, et venit, Deo mittente, coturnix, id est cogitationum humilitas. Per coturnicem namque, avem circa terram volantem, intelligi potest cogitatio humilis circa discussionem propriæ conscientiæ occupata, non cœlestia inaniter scrutans, nec majestatem comprehendere quærens. Et pane cœli, id est sacramento Eucharistiæ, saturavit eos Salvator, sicut apud Matthæum inducitur: Cœnantibus illis, accepit Jesus panem, et benedixit, deditque discipulis, et ait: Accipite et manducate, hoc est corpus meum.
paras.en: [[104:40|They asked|Petierunt]], namely the faithful, [[104:40|and the quail came|et venit, Deo mittente, coturnix]], God sending it: that is, humility of thoughts. For by the quail, a bird that flies close to the ground, may be understood the humble thought, busied about the examination of one's own conscience, not idly searching into heavenly things, nor seeking to comprehend the majesty. [[104:40|with the bread of heaven|Et pane cœli]], that is, with the sacrament of the Eucharist, the Saviour [[104:40|filled them|saturavit eos]], as is related in Matthew: [[Matt 26:26|whilst they were at supper, Jesus took bread and blessed and broke and gave to his disciples and said: Take ye and eat. This is my body|Cœnantibus illis, accepit Jesus panem, et benedixit, deditque discipulis, et ait: Accipite et manducate, hoc est corpus meum]].

paras.t: Dirupit petram, id est, Deus Pater Christum in passione perforari permisit lancea militari, et fluxerunt aquæ: exivit enim aqua et sanguis, ut dicit Joannes. Abierunt merito passionis Christi in sicco, id est in sterili gentilitate ac arido mundo, flumina sapientiæ et gratiæ multiformis. Hæc enim flumina Spiritus Sanctus infudit credentibus per prædicationem Apostolorum. De quibus fluminibus ait Christus: Qui credit in me, sicut dicit Scriptura, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ. Quod qualiter intelligendum sit, Evangelista subjungit: Hoc autem dixit de Spiritu, quem accepturi erant credentes in eum.
paras.en: [[104:41|He opened the rock|Dirupit petram]]: that is, God the Father permitted Christ in his passion to be pierced with a soldier's lance, [[104:41|and waters flowed|et fluxerunt aquæ]]; for there came out water and blood, as John says[[John 19:34||]]. By the merit of Christ's passion [[104:41|rivers|flumina]] of manifold wisdom and grace [[104:41|ran down|Abierunt]] [[104:41|in the dry land|in sicco]], that is, in barren heathendom and the arid world. For the Holy Ghost poured these rivers into believers through the preaching of the Apostles. Of these rivers Christ says: [[John 7:38|He that believeth in me, as the scripture saith: Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water|Qui credit in me, sicut dicit Scriptura, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ]] [the margin gives Ibid. xii, 38; the words are John 7:38]. How this is to be understood, the Evangelist adds: [[John 7:39|Now this he said of the Spirit which they should receive who believed in him|Hoc autem dixit de Spiritu, quem accepturi erant credentes in eum]].

paras.t: Denique omnia ista dedit Deus populo christiano, quoniam memor fuit verbi sancti sui, quod habuit ad Abraham puerum suum, dicens: In semine tuo benedicentur omnes cognationes terræ. Ad hanc autem promissionem implendam, oportuit Christum incarnari ac pati, dictaque dona Christianis largiri. Simili modo dicit Apostolus: Dico Christum Jesum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis propter promissiones patrum.
paras.en: Finally, God gave all these things to the Christian people, [[104:42|Because he remembered his holy word, which he had spoken to his servant Abraham|quoniam memor fuit verbi sancti sui, quod habuit ad Abraham puerum suum]], saying: [[Gen 22:18|in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed|In semine tuo benedicentur omnes cognationes terræ]][[Gen 12:3||]] [Denis has *cognationes*, kindreds, the word of Gen 12:3]. But to fulfil this promise it behoved Christ to become incarnate and to suffer, and to bestow the said gifts on Christians. In like manner the Apostle says: [[Rom 15:8|I say that Christ Jesus was minister of the circumcision|Dico Christum Jesum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis]], for [[Rom 15:8|the promises made unto the fathers|promissiones patrum]].

paras.t: Et eduxit populum suum christianum de gentilitate ad Christianitatem, de conversatione vitiosa ad vitam angelicam, de via ad patriam, in exsultatione; et electos suos hoc modo eduxit in lætitia.
paras.en: [[104:43|And he brought forth his people|Et eduxit populum suum]], the Christian people, from heathendom to Christianity, from a vicious way of life to the angelic life, from the way to the fatherland, [[104:43|with joy|in exsultatione]]; [[104:43|and his chosen|et electos suos]] he brought forth in this manner [[104:43|with gladness|in lætitia]].

paras.t: Et dedit illis regiones gentium, etc. Terras enim et regna, in quibus olim habitabant pagani, postmodum inhabitaverunt Christiani. Vel, Dedit illis regiones gentium, id est terram vivorum seu regnum cœlorum, cujus largitionis typus erat largitio illa regionum sæculi hujus.
paras.en: [[104:44|And he gave them the lands of the Gentiles|Et dedit illis regiones gentium]], etc. For the lands and kingdoms in which pagans once dwelt, Christians afterwards inhabited. Or, [[104:44|he gave them the lands of the Gentiles|Dedit illis regiones gentium]]: that is, the land of the living, or the kingdom of heaven, of which bestowal that bestowal of the regions of this world was the type.

paras.t: In psalmo præsenti monemur beneficia Dei recolere, providentiam ejus circa genus humanum pensare, atque ex his Deum laudare, magnalia ejus aliis insinuare, incessabiliter quærere Dominum Creatorem, ejus desiderando præsentiam, nec aliud bonum, nisi ipsum æternum, increatum, supergloriosum, immensumque Deum finaliter velle, atque indesinenter pro sanctæ conversationis mercede appetere. Et quamvis hic psalmus juxta superficialem litteræ intellectum, non videatur adeo in quibusdam locis devotus, tamen secundum mysticam expositionem nunc introductam, omni devotione exuberat. Quæ autem omissa sunt, in præcedenti expositione satis patent.
paras.en: In the present psalm we are admonished to call to mind the benefits of God, to weigh his providence towards the human race, and from these to praise God, to make his great works known to others, to seek the Lord the Creator without ceasing, longing for his presence, and to will in the end no other good but the eternal, uncreated, more than glorious and immense God himself, and to seek him unceasingly as the reward of a holy way of life. And although this psalm, according to the surface understanding of the letter, does not seem so devout in certain places, yet according to the mystical exposition now brought forward it overflows with all devotion. What has been left out is plain enough from the preceding exposition.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, qui conspicis te graviter offensum malis nostris, ad impetrandam misericordiam tuam corda nostra, quæsumus, compunge ad pœnitentiam: ut concessa delictorum venia, munda conscientia tibi confiteamur, et nomen tuum invocemus, ac pro acceptis beneficiis mirabilia tua indefessi narremus.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, who seest thyself grievously offended by our evil deeds, pierce our hearts, we beseech thee, to penance, that we may obtain thy mercy: so that, the pardon of our offences being granted, we may with a clean conscience give glory to thee, and call upon thy name, and for the benefits we have received tirelessly relate thy wondrous works.

105.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUINTI : CONFITEMINI DOMINO... QUIS LOQUETUR, ETC.
105.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and fifth psalm: Give glory to the Lord… Who shall declare, etc.

paras.t: Assignatur demum psalmo jam explanando repetitum seu duplex Alleluia, dum dicitur: Alleluia, Alleluia: quod fit vel ad evidentiam seu certitudinem ampliorem, vel ad designandam duplicem laudem Dei, scilicet laudem viæ ac patriæ. Unde in Missa in principio versus cantatur Alleluia, atque in fine repetitur. Simili modo in Apocalypsi ait Joannes: Audivi vocem angelorum in cœlo dicentium, Alleluia. Et iterum dixerunt, Alleluia. Præterea sicut Christus in Evangelio interdum dicit semel, Amen, interdum vero reiterat; sic aliqui psalmi pro titulo habent Alleluia unum, aliqui vero duplex.
paras.en: Lastly, to the psalm now to be explained a repeated or double Alleluia is assigned, when it is said: Alleluia, Alleluia. This is done either for greater evidence or certainty, or to signify a twofold praise of God, namely the praise of the way and that of the fatherland [that is, of this life, in which we are still on the road, and of heaven]. Hence in the Mass Alleluia is sung at the beginning of the verse and repeated at the end. In like manner John says in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:1|I heard|Audivi]] the voice of angels [[Apoc 19:1|in heaven, saying: Alleluia|in cœlo dicentium, Alleluia]]. [[Apoc 19:3|And again they said: Alleluia|Et iterum dixerunt, Alleluia]]. Moreover, just as Christ in the Gospel sometimes says Amen once and sometimes repeats it, so some psalms have a single Alleluia for their title, and others a double one.

paras.t: Invitat autem hic psalmus ad duplicem confessionem, videlicet laudis divinæ ac propriæ culpæ, et ait: Confitemini Domino bono et justo, ipsum laudando, et vos accusando, peccatores variis vitiis sauciati, et ne retrahamini a confessione hac propter vestram ingratitudinem et pravitatem; quoniam bonus est Dominus. Est enim naturaliter, totaliter, et quomodolibet bonus, ejusque natura est bonitas infinita ac pura. Propter quod in Marco scriptum est: Nemo bonus nisi unus Deus. Non ergo desperandum est aliquo modo. Unde secundo Paralipomenon piissimus Ezechias locutus est: Dominus bonus propitiabitur cunctis, qui in toto corde suo requirunt eum. Et iterum: Pius et clemens est Dominus Deus vester, et non avertet faciem suam a vobis, si reversi fueritis ad eum. Quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus: id est, misericordia Dei æterna est, nunquam deficiens, et a principio mundi super electos effusa est; nec cessabit unquam effusio pietatis divinæ, quoniam et in inferno citra condignum miseri affliguntur, in cœlo quoque ultra condignum electi remunerantur.
paras.en: Now this psalm invites to a twofold confession, namely of God's praise and of one's own guilt, and it says: [[105:1|Give glory to the Lord|Confitemini Domino]] [*confitemini* means both "give praise" and "confess": hence the twofold confession], who is good and just, by praising him and accusing yourselves, you sinners wounded by various vices; and do not be held back from this confession by your ingratitude and wickedness, [[105:1|for he is good|quoniam bonus]], the Lord, that is. For he is good by nature, wholly, and in every way, and his nature is infinite and pure goodness. For this reason it is written in Mark: [[Mark 10:18|None is good but one, that is God|Nemo bonus nisi unus Deus]]. So there is no cause for despair in any way. Hence the most devout Ezechias spoke thus in the second book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 30:18|The Lord who is good will shew mercy|Dominus bonus propitiabitur]] [[2 Par 30:19|To all them, who with their whole heart, seek|cunctis, qui in toto corde suo requirunt]] him. And again: [[2 Par 30:9|the Lord your God is merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if you return to him|Pius et clemens est Dominus Deus vester, et non avertet faciem suam a vobis, si reversi fueritis ad eum]]. [[105:1|For his mercy endureth for ever|Quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus]]: that is, the mercy of God is eternal, never failing, and from the beginning of the world it has been poured out upon the elect; nor will the outpouring of God's kindness ever cease, since even in hell the wretched are punished less than they deserve, and in heaven too the elect are rewarded beyond what they deserve.

paras.t: Quis loquetur potentias Domini? id est, quis exprimere poterit, quam potens sit Deus? Et dicit, Potentias, in plurali (quum tamen in Deo non sit nisi una simplex potentia), propter diversos effectus divinæ potentiæ. Vel, per potentias intelliguntur magnalia opera Dei potenter producta. Quum vero sit Deus infinitæ potentiæ atque omnipotens, nulla creatura perfecte comprehendere valet aut explicare potentiam ejus. Propter quod insanissimæ mentis sunt, qui divinam potentiam metiri suo præsumunt ingenio, asserentes Deum non posse supernaturaliter agere, nec aliquid esse credendum quod rationem excedit: quum Deus possit in infinitum plura producere, quam homo consumere. Imo Deus benedictus et sanctus non potest tot tantaque agere, quin possit in infinitum plura atque majora efficere, quantum in se est. Demum impossibile nobis est, intelligere aut exprimere divinæ potestatis effectus. Propter quod Sapiens contestatur: Difficile æstimamus quæ in terra sunt, et quæ in prospectu sunt, invenimus cum labore: quæ autem in cœlis sunt, quis investigabit?
paras.en: [[105:2|Who shall declare the powers of the Lord?|Quis loquetur potentias Domini]] that is, who will be able to express how mighty God is? And he says *powers* in the plural (though in God there is only one simple power) because of the different effects of the divine power. Or, by *powers* are understood the great works of God, mightily brought forth. Since God is of infinite power and almighty, no creature can perfectly comprehend or set forth his power. For this reason they are of a most unsound mind who presume to measure the divine power by their own wit, asserting that God cannot act supernaturally and that nothing is to be believed which exceeds reason: since God can bring forth infinitely more things than man can exhaust. Nay, the blessed and holy God cannot do so many and such great things that he could not, as far as lies in him, do infinitely more and greater. In short, it is impossible for us to understand or express the effects of God's power. For this reason the Wise Man testifies: [[Wis 9:16|hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth: and with labour do we find the things that are before us. But the things that are in heaven, who shall search out?|Difficile æstimamus quæ in terra sunt, et quæ in prospectu sunt, invenimus cum labore: quæ autem in cœlis sunt, quis investigabit?]]

paras.t: Et quis auditas faciet omnes laudes ejus? id est, quis proferre aut aliis annuntiare poterit universa præconia Creatoris, quam laudandus sit ipse? quasi dicat, Nullus. Quum enim Deus laudandus sit propter propriam bonitatem et propter opera sua, quantum a perfecta notitia bonitatis divinæ ac operum ejus deficimus, tantum a plenitudine divinæ laudationis occumbimus. Propterea in libro Job scriptum est: Nos quippe involvimur tenebris. Digne eum invenire non possumus; et enarrari non potest. Et Ecclesiasticus: Exaltantes, inquit, replemini virtute; ne laboretis, non enim pervenietis. Non ergo inaniter gloriemur dum Deum laudamus, quasi magnum seu dignum aliquid operemur, quum nec Cherubim nec Seraphim eum laudare sufficiant; sed cum magno timore atque profunda humilitate ipsum laudemus, sicut superius dictum est: Exsultate ei cum tremore.
paras.en: And [[105:2|who shall set forth all his praises?|quis auditas faciet omnes laudes ejus?]] that is, who will be able to utter or proclaim to others all the praises of the Creator, how worthy of praise he is? As if to say: no one. For since God is to be praised for his own goodness and for his works, the further we fall short of a perfect knowledge of God's goodness and of his works, the further we fall short of the fulness of his praise. Therefore it is written in the book of Job: [[Job 37:19|we are wrapped up in darkness|nos quippe involvimur tenebris]]. [[Job 37:23|We cannot find him worthily|Digne eum invenire non possumus]]; [[Job 37:23|and he is ineffable|et enarrari non potest]]. And Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 43:34|When you exalt him|Exaltantes]], he says, [[Ecclus 43:34|put forth all your strength, and be not weary: for you can never go far enough|replemini virtute; ne laboretis, non enim pervenietis]]. Let us not, then, glory vainly when we praise God, as though we were doing something great or worthy, since neither the Cherubim nor the Seraphim suffice to praise him; but let us praise him with great fear and deep humility, as was said above: [[Ps 2:11|rejoice unto him with trembling|Exsultate ei cum tremore]].

paras.t: Beati sunt jam in spe, qui custodiunt judicium discretionis et retributionis. Prælati namque et judices custodire debent utrumque judicium, quantum ad subditos, discernendo causas eorum, et debitam pœnam infligendo. Quilibet quoque se ipsum judicare debet, discutiendo, accusando, castigando se ipsum, discernendo bonum a malo, et verum a falso: quod singulis nobis necessarium est ad salutem, juxta illud: Numquid qui non amat judicium, sanari potest? Et Apostolus: Si nos ipsos, inquit, dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur. Est autem istud judicium valde acceptum Deo, sicut per Jeremiam protestatur: Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris. Et faciunt justitiam, sequendo et exsequendo quod recta ratio judicat, in omni tempore, id est perseveranter usque in finem, quia qui perseveraverit usque in finem, salvus erit, sicut apud Evangelistam adstruit Christus judex noster.
paras.en: [[105:3|Blessed are they|Beati]], already in hope, [[105:3|that keep judgment|qui custodiunt judicium]]: the judgment of discernment and that of retribution. For prelates and judges must keep both judgments with regard to their subjects, by discerning their causes and inflicting the due penalty. Everyone too must judge himself, by examining, accusing and chastising himself, and by discerning good from evil and the true from the false: which is necessary to each of us for salvation, according to that verse: [[Job 34:17|Can he be healed that loveth not judgment?|Numquid qui non amat judicium, sanari potest?]] [the margin gives Job xxxviii, 17; the words are Job 34:17]. And the Apostle: [[1 Cor 11:31|if we would judge ourselves|Si nos ipsos]], he says, [[1 Cor 11:31|we should not be judged|non utique judicaremur]]. This judgment is very acceptable to God, as he declares through Jeremias: If [[Jer 15:19|thou wilt separate the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth|Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris]]. [[105:3|And do justice|Et faciunt justitiam]], by following and carrying out what right reason judges, [[105:3|at all times|in omni tempore]], that is, perseveringly unto the end, because [[Matt 10:22|he that shall persevere unto the end, he shall be saved|qui perseveraverit usque in finem, salvus erit]], as Christ our judge affirms in the Evangelist.

paras.t: Memento nostri, Domine, in beneplacito populi tui, id est in infusione seu per infusionem gratiæ tuæ, per quam placet tibi populus tuus, quatenus nos tibi placeamus, quemadmodum illi. Omnium quidem memor est Deus, quum Amos propheta dicat: Juravit Dominus, Si oblitus fuero usque in finem opera eorum. Sed orat Propheta ut Deus memor sit nostri, sicut memor fuit electorum suorum. Unde etiam Esdras deprecatur: Memento mei, Deus, in bonum.
paras.en: [[105:4|Remember us, O Lord, in the favour of thy people|Memento nostri, Domine, in beneplacito populi tui]], that is, in the infusion, or by the infusion, of thy grace, through which thy people is pleasing to thee, so that we may please thee as they do. God indeed is mindful of all, since the prophet Amos says: [[Amos 8:7|The Lord hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]]: [[Amos 8:7|surely I will never forget all their works|Si oblitus fuero usque in finem opera eorum]]. But the Prophet prays that God may be mindful of us as he was mindful of his elect. Hence Esdras too entreats: [[2 Esd 5:19|Remember me, O my God, for good|Memento mei, Deus, in bonum]] [the margin gives II Esdr. ix, 19; the words stand at 2 Esd 5:19 and 13:31].

paras.t: Visita nos in salutari tuo, id est in salubri atque benigna salvatione, ita ut visitemur a te per piam præsentiam ad nostram salutem, non per districtam sententiam ad nostram damnationem, quomodo reprobi visitantur. De quibus in Sophonia a te dicitur: Visitabo super viros defixos in fæcibus suis. Sic enim et dæmones visitantur a te, quemadmodum Isaias affirmat: Visitabit Dominus super Leviathan serpentem tortuosum. Vel: Visita nos in salutari tuo, id est in Christo, mittendo illum ad nos. Ipse est enim sapientia tua æterna et increata, quæ ad electos quotidie invisibiliter mittitur, prout in Sapientiæ libro quidam precatur: Da mihi, Domine, sedium tuarum adsistricem sapientiam; et iterum, Mitte illam de cœlis, ut mecum sit et mecum laboret.
paras.en: [[105:4|visit us with thy salvation|Visita nos in salutari tuo]], that is, with a wholesome and kindly saving, so that we may be visited by thee through a loving presence unto our salvation, not through a stern sentence unto our damnation, as the reprobate are visited. Of these thou sayest in Sophonias: I [[Soph 1:12|will visit upon the men that are settled on their lees|Visitabo super viros defixos in fæcibus suis]]. For so the demons too are visited by thee, as Isaias affirms: [[Is 27:1|the Lord|Dominus]] [[Is 27:1|shall visit|Visitabit]] [[Is 27:1|leviathan the crooked serpent|Leviathan serpentem tortuosum]]. Or: [[105:4|visit us with thy salvation|Visita nos in salutari tuo]], that is, in Christ, by sending him to us. For he is thy eternal and uncreated wisdom, which is sent invisibly to the elect every day, as one prays in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 9:4|Give me|Da mihi]], O Lord, [[Wis 9:4|wisdom, that sitteth by thy throne|sedium tuarum adsistricem sapientiam]]; and again: [[Wis 9:10|Send her out of thy holy heaven|Mitte illam de cœlis]], [[Wis 9:10|that she may be with me, and may labour with me|ut mecum sit et mecum laboret]].

paras.t: Hæc autem, o Domine, tribue mihi, Ad videndum, id est, ut spiritualiter videamus et contemplemur nunc per fidem, et in futuro per speciem, in bonitate electorum tuorum, id est bona electis tuis parata. De quibus ait Apostolus: Oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascendit, quæ præparavit Deus his qui diligunt illum. Hæc autem bona aliud nihil sunt, nisi summum bonum, in quo est omnium bonorum et pulchrorum plenitudo immensa, seu ejus visio atque fruitio. Quid ergo orat Propheta, nisi ut Deum videamus, in cujus visione beatitudo et plena merces, præmiumque finale consistit? Vel, In bonitate electorum tuorum, id est in gloria Beatorum seu in supernaturali illuminatione, qua a te illuminantur electi, quoniam sine hac illuminatione omnis nostra visio atque cognitio vanæ informesque sunt.
paras.en: And grant me these things, O Lord, [[105:5|That we may see|Ad videndum]]: that is, that we may see and contemplate spiritually, now by faith and hereafter by sight, [[105:5|the good of thy chosen|in bonitate electorum tuorum]], that is, the good things prepared for thy elect. Of these the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man, what things God hath prepared for them that love him|Oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascendit, quæ præparavit Deus his qui diligunt illum]][[Is 64:4||]]. And these good things are nothing other than the highest good, in which is the boundless fulness of all good and beautiful things, or the vision and enjoyment of it. What then does the Prophet pray for, but that we may see God, in the vision of whom beatitude, full reward and the final prize consist? Or, [[105:5|the good of thy chosen|In bonitate electorum tuorum]], that is, in the glory of the Blessed, or in the supernatural illumination with which the elect are enlightened by thee, since without this illumination all our seeing and knowing is vain and formless.

paras.t: Ad lætandum in lætitia gentis tuæ, id est, ut lætemur spirituali lætitia, qua in te jucundatur plebs tua, nunc in spe futurorum bonorum, in patria vero in adeptione cœlestium præmiorum. Vel, In lætitia gentis tuæ, id est, ut lætemur cum populo tuo, non cum sæculo isto. Et omnia hæc fiant ad nominis tui honorem, videlicet ut lauderis cum hereditate tua, id est cum Ecclesia electorum, ita quod si electi tui de bono laudantur, tu de eodem bono tanquam principalis causa boni lauderis. Vel, Ut lauderis tu in omnibus et præ omnibus, qui per gratiam es cum hereditate tua, id est electis. Vel, Ut lauderis cum hereditate tua, id est ab electis, qui sunt hereditas tua tecum exsistens.
paras.en: [[105:5|that we may rejoice in the joy of thy nation|Ad lætandum in lætitia gentis tuæ]], that is, that we may rejoice with the spiritual joy with which thy people delights in thee: now in the hope of good things to come, but in the fatherland in the attaining of the heavenly rewards. Or, [[105:5|in the joy of thy nation|In lætitia gentis tuæ]], that is, that we may rejoice with thy people, not with this world. And let all this be done for the honour of thy name, namely [[105:5|that thou mayst be praised with thy inheritance|ut lauderis cum hereditate tua]], that is, with the Church of the elect, in such a way that if thy elect are praised for some good, thou art praised for the same good as the principal cause of the good. Or, [[105:5|that thou mayst be praised|Ut lauderis]] in all things and above all things, thou who by grace art [[105:5|with thy inheritance|cum hereditate tua]], that is, with the elect. Or, [[105:5|that thou mayst be praised with thy inheritance|ut lauderis cum hereditate tua]], that is, by the elect, who are thy inheritance, abiding with thee.

paras.t: Peccavimus cum patribus nostris, id est sicut patres nostri, vel pariter cum eis, non declinando, sed imitando eorum delicta. Peccavimus autem præcepta moralia transgrediendo, injuste egimus, transgrediendo præcepta judicialia, iniquitatem fecimus, non servando præcepta cærimonialia. Vel, Peccavimus contra Deum, injuste egimus contra proximum, iniquitatem fecimus contra nos ipsos.
paras.en: [[105:6|We have sinned with our fathers|Peccavimus cum patribus nostris]], that is, as our fathers did, or together with them, not turning away from their offences but imitating them. [[105:6|We have sinned|Peccavimus]] by transgressing the moral precepts; [[105:6|we have acted unjustly|injuste egimus]] by transgressing the judicial precepts; [[105:6|we have wrought iniquity|iniquitatem fecimus]] by not keeping the ceremonial precepts. Or: [[105:6|We have sinned|Peccavimus]] against God, [[105:6|we have acted unjustly|injuste egimus]] against our neighbour, [[105:6|we have wrought iniquity|iniquitatem fecimus]] against ourselves.

paras.t: Patres nostri in Ægypto, id est, qui olim in Ægypto fuerunt, non intellexerunt spiritualiter et prudenter mirabilia tua, quæ per Moysen in Ægypto, in mari Rubro, in deserto fecisti: quia ex talibus mirabilibus non consideraverunt omnipotentiam Dei, et quod Deus qui tanta pro eis fecit in Ægypto, postmodum protegeret eos, atque de facili adimpleret quæcumque eis promisit. Non intellexerunt quoque quid mirabilia illa figurabant. Propter quod in Deuteronomii volumine habetur: Dixit Moyses ad filios Israel: Vos vidistis universa magnalia quæ coram vobis Dominus fecit; et non dedit vobis Dominus cor intelligens et oculos videntes usque in præsentem diem. Unde et rursus Dominus ait per Moysen: Quousque multitudo hæc pessima non credet mihi in omnibus mirabilibus meis? Ecce primum peccatum populi hujus, scilicet peccatum ignorantiæ. Sequitur de ingratitudinis vitio: non fuerunt memores, gratias referendo, multitudinis misericordiæ tuæ, id est multæ ac magnæ miserationis a te eis impensæ, qui propter eos tam graviter afflixisti Ægyptios decem plagis, a quibus eos piissime præservasti.
paras.en: [[105:7|Our fathers|Patres nostri]] [[105:7|in Egypt|in Ægypto]], that is, those who were once in Egypt, [[105:7|understood not|non intellexerunt]] spiritually and wisely [[105:7|thy wonders|mirabilia tua]], which thou didst work through Moses in Egypt, in the Red Sea and in the desert: for from such wonders they did not consider the omnipotence of God, nor that God, who had done such great things for them in Egypt, would protect them afterwards and would easily fulfil whatever he had promised them. Nor did they understand what those wonders prefigured. For this reason it is found in the volume of Deuteronomy: Moses said to the children of Israel: [[Deut 29:2|You have seen all the things that the Lord did before you|Vos vidistis universa magnalia quæ coram vobis Dominus fecit]]; [[Deut 29:4|And the Lord hath not given you a heart to understand, and eyes to see|et non dedit vobis Dominus cor intelligens et oculos videntes]], [[Deut 29:4|unto this present day|usque in præsentem diem]] [the margin gives Deut. xxiv, 2, 4; the words are Deut 29:2, 4]. Hence the Lord says again through Moses: [[Num 14:11|how long|Quousque]] will this most wicked multitude [[Num 14:11|not believe me for all the signs|non credet mihi in omnibus mirabilibus meis?]]? [Denis joins Num 14:11 to the words "this wicked multitude" of Num 14:27.] Behold the first sin of this people, namely the sin of ignorance. There follows the vice of ingratitude: [[105:7|they remembered not|non fuerunt memores]], by giving thanks, [[105:7|the multitude of thy mercies|multitudinis misericordiæ tuæ]], that is, the many and great compassions shown them by thee, who for their sake didst so grievously afflict the Egyptians with ten plagues, from which thou didst most lovingly preserve them[[Ex 7:1||]] [the margin gives Exod. vii–xii].

paras.t: Et irritaverunt Deum et Moysen servum ejus, ascendentes de terra Ægypti in mari, mari, inquam, Rubro: quia videntes Pharaonem ipsos insequentem, antequam ingrederentur alveum maris Rubri, diffidentes de potestate divina, dixerunt ad Moysen: Forsitan non erant sepulcra in Ægypto, ideo tulisti nos, ut moreremur in solitudine. Quid hoc facere voluisti? Sed nec ipsum mare Rubrum, quamvis divisum, ingredi ausi fuerunt, ut alibi legitur, nisi ad monitionem Moysis magnam et longam.
paras.en: [[105:7|And they provoked to wrath|Et irritaverunt]] God and Moses his servant, [[105:7|going up|ascendentes]] from the land of Egypt [[105:7|to the sea|in mari]], to the sea, I say, [[105:7|the Red Sea|Rubro]] [the margin gives the reading *in mare Rubrum*]: for when they saw Pharao pursuing them, before they entered the bed of the Red Sea, distrusting the divine power they said to Moses: [[Ex 14:11|Perhaps there were no graves in Egypt, therefore thou hast brought us to die in the wilderness: why wouldst thou do this|Forsitan non erant sepulcra in Ægypto, ideo tulisti nos, ut moreremur in solitudine. Quid hoc facere voluisti?]]? Nor did they dare to enter the Red Sea itself, though it was divided, as is read elsewhere, except at the great and long urging of Moses.

paras.t: Et salvavit eos Dominus, quamvis ingratos atque incredulos, de manu Ægyptiorum, non propter eorum virtutes aut merita, sed propter nomen suum, id est propter se ipsum et nominis sui glorificationem. Unde in Ezechiele scriptum est: Non propter vos ego faciam, dicit Dominus, notum sit vobis, sed propter nomen sanctum meum. Ut notam faceret cunctis hominibus potentiam suam, qua Ægyptios debellavit, et Israelem salvavit. Ideo in Exodi libro Dominus ait: Glorificabor in Pharaone et in omni exercitu ejus; scientque Ægyptii, quia ego sum Dominus.
paras.en: [[105:8|And he saved them|Et salvavit eos]], the Lord did, ungrateful and unbelieving though they were, from the hand of the Egyptians: not for their virtues or merits, but [[105:8|for his own name's sake|propter nomen suum]], that is, for his own sake and for the glorifying of his name. Hence it is written in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:32|It is not for your sakes that I will do this, saith the Lord God, be it known to you|Non propter vos ego faciam, dicit Dominus, notum sit vobis]], [[Ezech 36:22|but for my holy name's sake|sed propter nomen sanctum meum]]. [[105:8|That he might make his power known|Ut notam faceret cunctis hominibus potentiam suam]] to all men, the power by which he vanquished the Egyptians and saved Israel. Therefore the Lord says in the book of Exodus: [[Ex 14:4|I shall be glorified in Pharao, and in all his army: and the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord|Glorificabor in Pharaone et in omni exercitu ejus; scientque Ægyptii, quia ego sum Dominus]].

paras.t: Et increpuit Dominus, id est, increpavit, seu imperando divisit, mare Rubrum. Mutatio enim maris Rubri a suo naturali statu ac motu, vocatur increpatio ejus. Et exsiccatum est: non mare, quia aqua non exsiccatur manens aqua: inseparabiliter enim connaturale est aquæ, esse humidum; sed dicitur mare exsiccatum, eo quod fundus terræ, ubi currebat, siccatus est, aquis sublatis. Et deduxit eos in abyssis, id est in itinere maris Rubri, non per aquas, sed per iter in quo paulo ante fluxerat aqua, sicut in deserto, id est tam plane et sicco pede, ac si per viam deserti transissent, quemadmodum ibidem plenius recitatur.
paras.en: [[105:9|And he rebuked|Et increpuit]], the Lord, that is, rebuked [Denis explains the rarer form *increpuit* by the usual *increpavit*], or divided by his command, [[105:9|the Red Sea|mare Rubrum]]. For the changing of the Red Sea from its natural state and motion is called its rebuking. [[105:9|And it was dried up|Et exsiccatum est]]: not the sea, for water is not dried up while remaining water, since to be moist is inseparably connatural to water; but the sea is said to be dried up because the bed of earth where it flowed was dried when the waters were taken away. [[105:9|And he led them through the depths|Et deduxit eos in abyssis]], that is, on the way through the Red Sea, not through the waters but along a path where water had flowed a little before, [[105:9|as in a wilderness|sicut in deserto]], that is, as smoothly and dry-shod as if they had passed along a road in the desert, as is told more fully there.

paras.t: Et salvavit eos de manu odientium, scilicet Ægyptiorum eos insequentium cum curribus sexcentis, et redemit eos de manu inimici, id est regis Ægypti. Quod quomodo contigerit, subditur:
paras.en: [[105:10|And he saved them from the hand of them that hated them|Et salvavit eos de manu odientium]], namely of the Egyptians who pursued them with six hundred chariots, [[105:10|and he redeemed them from the hand of the enemy|et redemit eos de manu inimici]], that is, of the king of Egypt. How this came about is told next:

paras.t: Et operuit aqua maris Rubri, revertens ad locum priorem ac proprium, tribulantes eos, id est Ægyptios, qui afflixerunt Israelitas; unus ex eis non remansit: omnes namque submersi sunt. Unde in Exodo legitur: Reversum est mare primo diluculo ad priorem locum, fugientibusque Ægyptiis occurrerunt aquæ, et involvit eos Dominus in mediis fluctibus: ne unus quidem superfuit ex eis.
paras.en: [[105:11|And the water covered|Et operuit aqua]] (the water of the Red Sea, returning to its former and proper place) [[105:11|them that afflicted them|tribulantes eos]], that is, the Egyptians, who had afflicted the Israelites; [[105:11|there was not one of them left|unus ex eis non remansit]]: for all were drowned. Hence it is read in Exodus: The sea [[Ex 14:27|returned at the first break of day to the former place: and as the Egyptians were fleeing away, the waters came upon them, and the Lord shut them up in the middle of the waves|Reversum est mare primo diluculo ad priorem locum, fugientibusque Ægyptiis occurrerunt aquæ, et involvit eos Dominus in mediis fluctibus]]: [[Ex 14:28|neither did there so much as one of them remain|ne unus quidem superfuit ex eis]].

paras.t: Et crediderunt filii Israel verbis ejus, scilicet Dei, viso tanto miraculo. Propter quod illic subjungitur: Timuit populus Dominum, et crediderunt Domino et Moysi servo ejus. Et laudaverunt laudem ejus, id est laudabilia opera atque laudabilem bonitatem Dei hæc facientis, secundum quod ibidem dicitur: Tunc cecinerunt Moyses et filii Israel canticum hoc Domino, et dixerunt: Cantemus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est, equum et ascensorem dejecit in mare. Et infra scriptum est: Sumpsit ergo Maria prophetes, soror Aaron, tympanum in manu sua; egressæque sunt omnes mulieres post eam cum tympanis et choris, quibus præcinebat, dicens: Cantemus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est, etc.
paras.en: [[105:12|And they believed|Et crediderunt]], the children of Israel, [[105:12|his words|verbis ejus]], namely God's, when they had seen so great a miracle. For this reason it is added there: [[Ex 14:31|the people feared the Lord, and they believed the Lord, and Moses his servant|Timuit populus Dominum, et crediderunt Domino et Moysi servo ejus]]. [[105:12|And they sang his praises|Et laudaverunt laudem ejus]], that is, the praiseworthy works and the praiseworthy goodness of God who did these things, according to what is said there: [[Ex 15:1|Then Moses and the children of Israel sung this canticle to the Lord, and said: Let us sing to the Lord: for he is gloriously magnified, the horse and the rider he hath thrown into the sea|Tunc cecinerunt Moyses et filii Israel canticum hoc Domino, et dixerunt: Cantemus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est, equum et ascensorem dejecit in mare]]. And it is written further on: [[Ex 15:20|So Mary the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand: and all the women went forth after her with timbrels and with dances|Sumpsit ergo Maria prophetes, soror Aaron, tympanum in manu sua; egressæque sunt omnes mulieres post eam cum tympanis et choris]], [[Ex 15:21|And she began the song to them, saying: Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnified|quibus præcinebat, dicens: Cantemus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est]], etc.

paras.t: Cito fecerunt, id est, in opere bono non diu perseveraverunt. Vel, Cito, post hanc laudem et gratiarum actionem, fecerunt quæ sequuntur: obliti sunt operum ejus, id est, prædicta miracula Dei non attenderunt mente sagaci grataque. Unde in libro Exodi habetur: Quintadecima die mensis secundi, postquam egressi sunt de Ægypto, murmuraverunt contra Moysen et Aaron in solitudine, dicentes: Utinam mortui essemus in Ægypto. Cur induxistis nos in desertum istud, ut occideretis omnem multitudinem fame? Non sustinuerunt consilium ejus: id est, patienter non exspectaverunt tempus, quo Deus decrevit eis providere de cibo, secundum consilium sapientiæ suæ, qua omnia ordinatissime operatur, juxta illud Apostoli ad Ephesios: Omnia operatur secundum consilium voluntatis suæ. Hujus ergo consilii tempus ex impatientia anticiparunt.
paras.en: [[105:13|They had quickly done|Cito fecerunt]], that is, they did not persevere long in good work. Or, [[105:13|quickly|Cito]], after this praise and thanksgiving, they did the things that follow: [[105:13|they forgot his works|obliti sunt operum ejus]], that is, they did not heed the aforesaid miracles of God with a discerning and grateful mind. Hence it is found in the book of Exodus: [[Ex 16:1|the fifteenth day of the second month, after they came out of the land of Egypt|Quintadecima die mensis secundi, postquam egressi sunt de Ægypto]], they [[Ex 16:2|murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness|murmuraverunt contra Moysen et Aaron in solitudine]], saying: [[Ex 16:3|Would to God we had died|Utinam mortui essemus]] in Egypt. [[Ex 16:3|Why have you brought us into this desert, that you might destroy all the multitude with famine?|Cur induxistis nos in desertum istud, ut occideretis omnem multitudinem fame?]] [[105:13|They waited not for his counsel|Non sustinuerunt consilium ejus]]: that is, they did not wait patiently for the time at which God had decreed to provide them with food, according to the counsel of his wisdom, by which he works all things in perfect order, according to that saying of the Apostle to the Ephesians: He [[Eph 1:11|worketh all things according to the counsel of his will|Omnia operatur secundum consilium voluntatis suæ]]. Out of impatience, then, they ran ahead of the time of this counsel.

paras.t: Et concupierunt concupiscentiam in deserto, id est cibum delicatum, videlicet carnes, secundum quod alibi legitur: Flagrabant desiderio carnium, et dicebant: Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes? Anima nostra arida est, nihil respiciunt oculi nostri nisi manna. Et tentaverunt Deum in inaquoso, id est in deserto (in quo aqua nulla aut modica reperitur), prout in Exodo scriptum est: Tentaverunt Deum, dicentes: Estne Dominus in nobis, an non?
paras.en: [[105:14|And they coveted their desire in the desert|Et concupierunt concupiscentiam in deserto]], that is, dainty food, namely flesh meat, according to what is read elsewhere: They [[Num 11:4|burned with desire|Flagrabant desiderio]] for flesh, and said: [[Num 11:4|Who shall give us flesh to eat?|Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes?]] [[Num 11:6|Our soul is dry, our eyes behold nothing else but manna|Anima nostra arida est, nihil respiciunt oculi nostri nisi manna]]. [[105:14|And they tempted God in the place without water|Et tentaverunt Deum in inaquoso]], that is, in the desert (where little or no water is found), as it is written in Exodus: [[Ex 17:7|they tempted the Lord, saying: Is the Lord amongst us or not?|Tentaverunt Deum, dicentes: Estne Dominus in nobis, an non?]]

paras.t: Et dedit eis Deus petitionem ipsorum, id est rem postulatam, scilicet carnes et aquam, et misit saturitatem in animas eorum, id est animalem vitam, quoniam mense integro dedit eis ad edendum coturnices, donec exibant per nares eorum, et vertebantur in nauseam, sicut in Numerorum libro habetur.
paras.en: [[105:15|And he gave them their request|Et dedit eis Deus petitionem ipsorum]], God did, that is, the thing they asked for, namely flesh and water, [[105:15|and sent fulness into their souls|et misit saturitatem in animas eorum]], that is, into their animal life [that is, the life of the body]: for during a whole month he gave them quails to eat, until they came out at their nostrils and became loathsome to them[[Num 11:20||]], as is found in the book of Numbers.

paras.t: Consequenter autem recitatur seditio ipsius Core atque suorum. Et irritaverunt Core de tribu Levi, et Dathan ac Abiron de tribu Ruben, aliique proceres synagogæ ducentes quinquaginta, qui tempore concilii per nomina vocabantur, ut dicitur in libro Numerorum, Moysen in castris, id est in papilionibus, vel populo habitante in tentoriis, Aaron quoque sanctum Domini, id est Domino consecratum in pontificem. Dathan namque et Abiron, quoniam nati erant de primogenito Jacob, scilicet de Ruben, ambiebant principatum, vel saltem Moyse et Aaron inferiores esse ac obedire spreverunt. Core autem atque Coritæ, quia de tribu Levi erant, sicut et Aaron, purificari volebant et in sacerdotio. Irritaverunt ergo Moysen et Aaron, dicentes illud Numerorum: Sufficiat vobis, quia omnis multitudo sanctorum est, et in ipsis est Dominus. Cur elevamini super populum Domini?
paras.en: Next the sedition of Core and his followers is related. [[105:16|And they provoked|Et irritaverunt]] (Core of the tribe of Levi, and Dathan and Abiron of the tribe of Ruben, and the other [[Num 16:2|leading men of the synagogue|proceres synagogæ]], two hundred and fifty, [[Num 16:2|who in the time of assembly were called by name|qui tempore concilii per nomina vocabantur]], as is said in the book of Numbers) [[105:16|Moses in the camp|Moysen in castris]], that is, in the tents, or the people dwelling in tents; and [[105:16|Aaron|Aaron]] also, [[105:16|the holy one of the Lord|sanctum Domini]], that is, consecrated to the Lord as high priest. For Dathan and Abiron, since they were descended from Jacob's first-born, namely Ruben, coveted the leadership, or at least scorned to be beneath Moses and Aaron and to obey them. Core and the Corites, on the other hand, because they were of the tribe of Levi, as Aaron was, wished to be sanctified for the priesthood as well. So they provoked Moses and Aaron, saying that word of Numbers: [[Num 16:3|Let it be enough for you, that all the multitude consisteth of holy ones, and the Lord is among them: Why lift you up yourselves above the people of the Lord?|Sufficiat vobis, quia omnis multitudo sanctorum est, et in ipsis est Dominus. Cur elevamini super populum Domini?]] [the margin gives "Ibid. 3" after Num. xi; the words are Num 16:3].

paras.t: Propter hanc ergo rebellionem et seditionem, Aperta est terra, et deglutivit Dathan, et operuit super congregationem, id est præ aliis filiis Israel, Abiron similem Dathan in culpa, unde et in pœna ei assimilatus est. Absorbuit etiam terra Core et Hon, tabernacula quoque et omnem possessionem Dathan et Abiron, prout in Numeris scribitur. Non autem absorbuit filios Core, quoniam non consenserant patri suo. Propter quod scriptum est: Factum est grande miraculum, ut Core pereunte, filii ejus non perirent.
paras.en: For this rebellion and sedition, then, [[105:17|The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan|Aperta est terra, et deglutivit Dathan]], [[105:17|and covered|et operuit]] [[105:17|the congregation|super congregationem]] (that is, above the other children of Israel) [Denis takes *super congregationem* as "over and above the congregation"] [[105:17|of Abiron|Abiron]], who was like Dathan in guilt, and so was made like him in punishment too. The earth also swallowed up Core and Hon, and the tents and all the possessions of Dathan and Abiron, as is written in Numbers[[Num 16:31||]]. But it did not swallow up the sons of Core, since they had not consented with their father. For this reason it is written: [[Num 26:10|there was a great miracle wrought|Factum est grande miraculum]], [[Num 26:11|That when Core perished, his sons did not perish.|ut Core pereunte, filii ejus non perirent]]

paras.t: Et exarsit ignis in synagoga eorum, id est in congregatione fautorum Core: flamma ignis hujus combussit peccatores, id est Coritas, quemadmodum liber Numerorum testatur: Ignis egressus a Domino, interfecit ducentos quinquaginta viros, qui offerebant incensum.
paras.en: [[105:18|And a fire was kindled in their congregation|Et exarsit ignis in synagoga eorum]], that is, in the assembly of Core's supporters: [[105:18|the flame|flamma]] of this fire [[105:18|burned the wicked|combussit peccatores]], that is, the Corites, as the book of Numbers testifies: [[Num 16:35|a fire coming out from the Lord, destroyed the two hundred and fifty men that offered the incense|Ignis egressus a Domino, interfecit ducentos quinquaginta viros, qui offerebant incensum]].

paras.t: Et fecerunt filii Israel vitulum in Horeb, id est juxta montem Horeb, qui est pars, scilicet pes, montis Sinai: vertex enim montis dicitur Sinai. Hæc formatio vituli diu præcessit seditionem prædictam. Dicuntur vero filii Israel fecisse hunc vitulum, quia ad eorum instantiam projecit Aaron aureas inaures eorum in ignem, et egressus est opere fusorio vitulus conflatilis, prout in Exodo narratur. Et adoraverunt sculptile. Aliqui dicunt, quod hic ponitur sculptile pro conflatili, eo quod utrumque sit nomen idoli. Nam vitulus ille fusus erat, non sculptus. Alii dicunt, quod primo fusus est; sed quia in fusura non exstitit plene formatus, postmodum sculptus est, perfectiusque formatus. Et ergo interdum vocatur sculptile, interdum conflatile. Hunc itaque vitulum adoraverunt. Immolantes namque ei hostias, dixerunt: Isti sunt dii tui, Israel, qui eduxerunt te de terra Ægypti: ut scribitur in Exodo.
paras.en: [[105:19|They made also a calf in Horeb|Et fecerunt filii Israel vitulum in Horeb]], the children of Israel did, that is, near Mount Horeb, which is a part, namely the foot, of Mount Sinai; for the summit of the mountain is called Sinai. The making of this calf took place long before the sedition just mentioned. The children of Israel are said to have made this calf because at their insistence Aaron threw their golden earrings into the fire, and a molten calf came out by founders' work, as is told in Exodus[[Ex 32:2||]]. [[105:19|And they adored the graven thing|Et adoraverunt sculptile]]. Some say that *graven thing* is put here for *molten thing* [*sculptile*, a carved image; *conflatile*, one cast in metal], because both are names for an idol; for that calf was cast, not carved. Others say that it was first cast, but since it did not come out fully formed in the casting, it was afterwards carved and more perfectly formed; and so it is sometimes called a graven thing and sometimes a molten one. This calf, then, they adored. For [[Ex 32:8|sacrificing victims to it|Immolantes namque ei hostias]], they said: [[Ex 32:8|These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt|Isti sunt dii tui, Israel, qui eduxerunt te de terra Ægypti]], as is written in Exodus [the margin gives Exod. xxxii, 4; Denis's words are those of Ex 32:8].

paras.t: Et mutaverunt gloriam suam, id est honorem et cultum legis divinæ, seu Deum, in quo solo gloriari debebant, in similitudinem vituli comedentis fœnum: quia pro vero Deo adorabant imaginem vituli.
paras.en: [[105:20|And they changed their glory|Et mutaverunt gloriam suam]], that is, the honour and worship of the divine law, or God, in whom alone they ought to have gloried, [[105:20|into the likeness of a calf that eateth grass|in similitudinem vituli comedentis fœnum]]: for in place of the true God they adored the image of a calf.

paras.t: Obliti sunt Deum qui salvavit eos de Ægyptiaca servitute, qui fecit magnalia, id est opera magna, in Ægypto, percutiendo Ægyptios decem principalibus plagis, mirabilia per Moysen in terra Cham, id est in Ægypto, sic dicta propter causam præhabitam, terribilia in mari Rubro, submergendo regem Ægypti cum populo suo.
paras.en: [[105:21|They forgot God, who saved them|Obliti sunt Deum qui salvavit eos]] from the bondage of Egypt, [[105:21|who had done great things|qui fecit magnalia]], that is, great works, [[105:21|in Egypt|in Ægypto]], by striking the Egyptians with ten chief plagues[[Ex 12:1||]] [the margin gives Exod. xii–xiv], [[105:22|Wondrous works|mirabilia]] through Moses [[105:22|in the land of Cham|in terra Cham]], that is, in Egypt, so called for the reason given before [Egypt was peopled by the descendants of Cham, son of Noe], [[105:22|terrible things in the Red Sea|terribilia in mari Rubro]], by drowning the king of Egypt with his people[[Ex 14:28||]].

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus ad Moysen, ut disperderet eos, propter eorum ingratitudinem ac idololatriam, quemadmodum in libro Exodi inducitur: Dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Cerno quod populus iste duræ cervicis sit; dimitte me, ut irascatur furor meus contra eos, et deleam eos. Et hoc utique Dominus fecisset, si non Moyses electus ejus stetisset in confractione, id est in plaga populo imminente, qua erant confringendi, in conspectu ejus, id est coram Deo in monte Sinai, orans indesinenter pro populo, prout in Exodo scriptum est: Moyses autem orabat Deum suum. Et sequitur: Placatusque est Dominus. Demum in tantum objecit se medium pro populo, ut ex ineffabili caritate diceret Domino: Aut dimitte populo hanc noxam, aut si non facis, dele me de libro quem scripsisti. Stetit itaque Moyses in confractione. Ut averteret iram ejus, id est vindictam Dei a populo, ne Deus disperderet eos.
paras.en: [[105:23|And he said|Et dixit]], the Lord, to Moses, [[105:23|that he would destroy them|ut disperderet eos]], for their ingratitude and idolatry, as is set down in the book of Exodus: The Lord said to Moses: [[Ex 32:9|I see that this people is stiffnecked|Cerno quod populus iste duræ cervicis sit]]: [[Ex 32:10|Let me alone, that my wrath may be kindled against them, and that I may destroy them|dimitte me, ut irascatur furor meus contra eos, et deleam eos]]. And the Lord would certainly have done so, [[105:23|had not Moses his chosen stood|si non Moyses electus ejus stetisset]] [[105:23|in the breach|in confractione]] [*confractio*, "breach", is literally a "breaking"], that is, in the blow hanging over the people, by which they were to be broken, [[105:23|before him|in conspectu ejus]], that is, before God on Mount Sinai, praying without ceasing for the people, as it is written in Exodus: [[Ex 32:11|Moses besought the Lord his God|Moyses autem orabat Deum suum]]. And there follows: [[Ex 32:14|the Lord was appeased|Placatusque est Dominus]]. At last he put himself so far between God and the people that out of unspeakable charity he said to the Lord: [[Ex 32:31|either forgive them this trespass|Aut dimitte populo hanc noxam]], [[Ex 32:32|Or if thou do not, strike me out of the book that thou hast written|aut si non facis, dele me de libro quem scripsisti]]. So Moses stood [[105:23|in the breach|in confractione]], [[105:23|To turn away his wrath|Ut averteret iram ejus]], that is, God's vengeance, from the people, [[105:23|lest he should destroy them|ne Deus disperderet eos]].

paras.t: Et pro nihilo habuerunt terram desiderabilem, id est, terram promissionis lacte et melle manantem vilipenderunt, quando territi verbis exploratorum, dixerunt, ut in Numeris habetur: Constituamus nobis ducem, et revertamur in Ægyptum. Non crediderunt verbo ejus, id est promissioni Dei per Moysen, qui dixit eis, quod Dominus pugnaret pro eis, et introduceret eos in terram promissam; sed ipsi econtra dixerunt: Utinam non inducat nos Dominus in terram hanc, ne cadamus gladio.
paras.en: [[105:24|And they set at nought the desirable land|Et pro nihilo habuerunt terram desiderabilem]], that is, they held cheap the land of promise flowing with milk and honey, when, frightened by the words of the spies[[Num 14:1||]], they said, as is found in Numbers: [[Num 14:4|Let us appoint a captain, and let us return into Egypt|Constituamus nobis ducem, et revertamur in Ægyptum]] [the margin gives Num. xiv, 3; the words are Num 14:4]. [[105:24|They believed not his word|Non crediderunt verbo ejus]], that is, the promise of God made through Moses, who told them that the Lord would fight for them and bring them into the promised land; but they on the contrary said: Would God [[Num 14:3|that the Lord may not bring us into this land, lest we fall by the sword|non inducat nos Dominus in terram hanc, ne cadamus gladio]].

paras.t: Et murmuraverunt in tabernaculis suis: quemadmodum in Numeris legitur: Vociferans omnis turba nocte illa flevit, et murmurati sunt contra Moysen et Aaron, dicentes: Utinam mortui essemus in Ægypto, et utinam pereamus. Non exaudierunt vocem Domini, id est, exhortationibus Moysis et Caleb ac Josue, hortantium eos ad bonum, non acquieverunt, sed lapidare eos volebant.
paras.en: [[105:25|And they murmured in their tents|Et murmuraverunt in tabernaculis suis]], as is read in Numbers: [[Num 14:1|the whole multitude crying wept that night|Vociferans omnis turba nocte illa flevit]], and they [[Num 14:2|murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying|murmurati sunt contra Moysen et Aaron, dicentes]]: [[Num 14:3|Would God that we had died in Egypt|Utinam mortui essemus in Ægypto]], [[Num 14:3|and would God we may die|et utinam pereamus]]. [[105:25|They hearkened not to the voice of the Lord|Non exaudierunt vocem Domini]], that is, they did not yield to the exhortations of Moses and of Caleb and Josue, who urged them to good[[Num 14:6||]], but wanted to stone them[[Num 14:10||]].

paras.t: Et elevavit Dominus manum suam, id est virtutis suæ vindictam, super eos, ut prosterneret eos in deserto. Tunc enim Deus absolute dictavit, quod nullus eorum, qui murmuravit, ingrederetur terram promissionis, sed Caleb et Josue soli eam intrarent, de multitudine eorum qui primo numerati fuerunt, prout in libro Numerorum dicitur. Elevavit etiam Dominus manum suam super eos, propter hoc peccatum, ut prosterneret eos statim omnes simul in deserto, secundum quod ait ad Moysen: Usquequo populus iste detrahet mihi? Feriam ergo eos pestilentia atque consumam. Hæc autem pœna per orationem Moysis mitigata est, ita quod per partes atque paulatim mortui sunt in deserto. Sic enim precatus est Moyses pro eis: Domine, patiens et multæ misericordiæ, auferens iniquitatem et scelera, dimitte, obsecro, peccatum populi tui hujus, secundum magnitudinem misericordiæ tuæ, sicut propitius fuisti egredientibus de Ægypto usque ad locum istum. Dixitque Dominus: Dimisi juxta verbum tuum.
paras.en: [[105:26|And he lifted up his hand|Et elevavit Dominus manum suam]], the Lord did, that is, the vengeance of his power, [[105:26|over them|super eos]], [[105:26|to overthrow them in the desert|ut prosterneret eos in deserto]]. For then God decreed absolutely that none of those who had murmured should enter the land of promise, but that Caleb and Josue alone, of the multitude of those who were first numbered, should enter it, as is said in the book of Numbers[[Num 14:22||]]. The Lord also [[105:26|lifted up his hand over them|Elevavit etiam Dominus manum suam super eos]] for this sin, [[105:26|to overthrow them|ut prosterneret eos]] at once, all together, [[105:26|in the desert|in deserto]], according to what he said to Moses: [[Num 14:11|How long will this people detract me?|Usquequo populus iste detrahet mihi?]] [[Num 14:12|I will strike them therefore with pestilence, and will consume them|Feriam ergo eos pestilentia atque consumam]]. But this punishment was softened through the prayer of Moses, so that they died in the desert by parts and little by little. For thus Moses prayed for them: O Lord, [[Num 14:18|patient and full of mercy|patiens et multæ misericordiæ]], [[Num 14:18|taking away iniquity and wickedness|auferens iniquitatem et scelera]], [[Num 14:19|Forgive, I beseech thee, the sins of this people, according to the greatness of thy mercy, as thou hast been merciful to them from their going out of Egypt unto this place|dimitte, obsecro, peccatum populi tui hujus, secundum magnitudinem misericordiæ tuæ, sicut propitius fuisti egredientibus de Ægypto usque ad locum istum]]. [[Num 14:20|And the Lord said: I have forgiven according to thy word.|Dixitque Dominus: Dimisi juxta verbum tuum]]

paras.t: Et ut dejiceret semen, id est filios, eorum in nationibus, faciens eos cadere in terris diversis, et dispergeret eos in regionibus. Istam pœnam Dominus minabatur, sed precibus Moysis omnino ablata est, quoniam filii prostratorum in deserto introducti sunt in terram Chanaan.
paras.en: [[105:27|And to cast down|Et ut dejiceret]] [[105:27|their seed|semen]], that is, their children, [[105:27|among the nations|in nationibus]], making them fall in divers lands, [[105:27|and to scatter them in the countries|et dispergeret eos in regionibus]]. This punishment the Lord threatened, but through the prayers of Moses it was wholly taken away, since the children of those laid low in the desert were brought into the land of Chanaan.

paras.t: Et initiati sunt Beelphegor, id est, cultui idoli sic vocati applicuerunt se ipsos. Istud fuit circa mortem Moysis, quando ad suggestionem Balaam, Balac rex Moabitarum misit puellas pulchras ac nobiles juxta tentoria filiorum Israel, habentes secum idola sua, quatenus facerent filios Israel Deum suum offendere per idololatriam atque luxuriam: quia (ut dicitur) non permiserunt eos secum misceri, nisi primo adorarent idolum Beelphegor. Quod et factum est, quemadmodum in libro Numerorum plenius continetur. Et comederunt sacrificia mortuorum, id est carnes animalium huic idolo immolatas.
paras.en: [[105:28|They also were initiated to Beelphegor|Et initiati sunt Beelphegor]], that is, they gave themselves to the worship of the idol so called. This was about the time of Moses' death, when at the suggestion of Balaam, Balac king of the Moabites sent beautiful and noble girls near the tents of the children of Israel, bringing their idols with them, so as to make the children of Israel offend their God by idolatry and lust: for (as is said) they would not let them lie with them unless they first adored the idol Beelphegor. And this is what happened, as is told more fully in the book of Numbers[[Num 25:1||]][[Num 25:18||]]. [[105:28|And ate the sacrifices of the dead|Et comederunt sacrificia mortuorum]], that is, the flesh of animals sacrificed to this idol.

paras.t: Et irritaverunt eum, id est, Deum offenderunt, in adinventionibus suis, id est in peccatis studiose excogitatis et ex deliberatione patratis, et ob id multiplicata est in eis ruina, id est, multa et magna plaga eis inflicta, propter hæc scelera. Percussa sunt enim viginti quatuor millia hominum. Principes quoque jussi sunt suspendi in patibulis.
paras.en: [[105:29|And they provoked him|Et irritaverunt eum]], that is, they offended God, [[105:29|with their inventions|in adinventionibus suis]], that is, with sins studiously devised and committed of set purpose; and for this [[105:29|destruction was multiplied among them|multiplicata est in eis ruina]], that is, many and great blows were inflicted on them for these crimes. For [[Num 25:9|there were slain four and twenty thousand men|Percussa sunt enim viginti quatuor millia hominum]]. The princes too were ordered to be hanged on gibbets[[Num 25:4||]].

paras.t: Et stetit Phinees filius Eleazari filii Aaron sacerdotis, mente constanti contra idololatras, et placavit Dominum, perfodiendo in locis genitalibus Zambri ducem tribus Simeonis, coeuntem cum Cozbi filia nobilissimi principis Madianitarum; et cessavit quassatio, id est plaga prædictæ persecutionis a populo, propter hoc factum et merito zeli Phinees. Unde in Numeris habetur: Dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Phinees avertit iram meam a filiis Israel, quia zelo meo commotus est contra eos.
paras.en: [[105:30|Then Phinees stood up|Et stetit Phinees]], the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, with a steadfast mind against the idolaters, [[105:30|and pacified him|et placavit Dominum]], by running through the genital parts Zambri, a chief of the tribe of Simeon, as he lay with Cozbi, the daughter of a most noble prince of the Madianites; [[105:30|and the slaughter ceased|et cessavit quassatio]], that is, the blow of the aforesaid persecution was lifted from the people, because of this deed and through the merit of Phinees' zeal. Hence it is found in Numbers: [[Num 25:10|And the Lord said to Moses|Dixit Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[Num 25:11|Phinees|Phinees]] [[Num 25:11|hath turned away my wrath from the children of Israel: because he was moved with my zeal against them|avertit iram meam a filiis Israel, quia zelo meo commotus est contra eos]].

paras.t: Et reputatum est ei a Deo in justitiam, in generationem et generationem usque in sempiternum: quoniam Deus approbavit hoc opus ipsius; et in æternum justus vocabitur propter hanc causam. Meruitque sacerdotio fungi in se et in posteris suis, secundum quod Dominus ait ad Moysen: Loquere ad eum: Ecce do ei pacem fœderis mei; et erit tam sibi, quam semini ejus pactum sacerdotii sempiternum, quia zelatus est pro Deo suo.
paras.en: [[105:31|And it was reputed to him|Et reputatum est ei]] by God [[105:31|unto justice, to generation and generation for evermore|in justitiam, in generationem et generationem usque in sempiternum]]: for God approved this work of his, and he will be called just for ever for this reason. And he merited to exercise the priesthood in himself and in his descendants, according to what the Lord said to Moses: [[Num 25:12|say to him: behold I give him the peace of my covenant|Loquere ad eum: Ecce do ei pacem fœderis mei]]; [[Num 25:13|And the covenant of the priesthood for ever shall be both to him and his seed, because he hath been zealous for his God|et erit tam sibi, quam semini ejus pactum sacerdotii sempiternum, quia zelatus est pro Deo suo]].

105.title: PROSECUTIO EXPOSITIONIS PSALMI CENTESIMI QUINTI. ET EXPOSITIO MYSTICA QUORUMDAM QUÆ IN PSALMO ISTO CONTENTA SUNT.
105.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of the hundred and fifth psalm, and a mystical exposition of some things contained in this psalm.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur jurgatio filiorum Israel contra Deum, facta ad aquas Contradictionis, propter penuriam aquæ. Et irritaverunt eum, scilicet Deum, ad aquas Contradictionis, impatienter loquendo, secundum quod scriptum est : Convenerunt adversus Moysen et Aaron, et versi in seditionem, dixerunt : Utinam perissemus inter fratres nostros coram Domino. Et vexatus, id est animo perturbatus atque lassatus, est Moyses propter eos, id est propter eorum perversitatem, quia exacerbaverunt spiritum ejus, scilicet verbis ingratis et pessimis.
paras.en: Next is described the quarrelling of the children of Israel against God, which took place at the waters of Contradiction for want of water. [[105:32|They provoked him|Et irritaverunt eum]], that is, God, [[105:32|at the waters of contradiction|ad aquas Contradictionis]], by speaking impatiently, according to what is written: They [[Num 20:2|came together against Moses and Aaron|Convenerunt adversus Moysen et Aaron]], [[Num 20:3|and making a sedition, they said: Would God we had perished among our brethren before the Lord|et versi in seditionem, dixerunt : Utinam perissemus inter fratres nostros coram Domino]]. [[105:32|And Moses was afflicted|Et vexatus]], that is, troubled and wearied in mind, [[105:32|for their sakes|est Moyses propter eos]], that is, on account of their perversity, [[105:33|Because they exasperated his spirit|quia exacerbaverunt spiritum ejus]], namely with ungrateful and most wicked words.

paras.t: Et distinxit Moyses in labiis suis : id est, in hac cordis sui perturbatione alium modum loquendi habuit, recitando verba Domini, percutiendoque petram, quam ante habere solebat. Fuit enim incredulus Deo, atque in modo loquendi manifeste declaravit cordis sui hæsitationem. Ut enim in Numerorum libro legitur, quum sibi ac Aaron fratri suo Dominus dixisset, Loquimini ad petram coram eis, et illa dabit aquas ; Moyses percutiendo petram cum virga, protulit sermonem ambiguum, Num de petra hac poterimus vobis aquam ejicere ? Propter quod mox a Domino reprehensus est, et tam ipse quam Aaron ab ingressu terræ promissionis prohibitus est, dicente eis Domino : Quoniam non credidistis mihi, ut sanctificaretis me coram filiis Israel, non introducetis hos populos ad terram quam dabo eis.
paras.en: And Moses [[105:33|distinguished with his lips|distinxit Moyses in labiis suis]]: that is, in this disturbance of his heart he used another manner of speaking, in reciting the words of the Lord and in striking the rock, than he had been wont to use before. For he was unbelieving toward God, and by his manner of speaking he plainly showed the wavering of his heart. For, as we read in the book of Numbers, when the Lord had said to him and to Aaron his brother, [[Num 20:8|speak to the rock before them, and it shall yield waters|Loquimini ad petram coram eis, et illa dabit aquas]], Moses, striking the rock with the rod, uttered a doubtful speech: [[Num 20:10|Can we bring you forth water out of this rock?|Num de petra hac poterimus vobis aquam ejicere ?]] For this he was soon rebuked by the Lord, and both he and Aaron were forbidden to enter the land of promise, the Lord saying to them: [[Num 20:12|Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring these people into the land, which I will give them|Quoniam non credidistis mihi, ut sanctificaretis me coram filiis Israel, non introducetis hos populos ad terram quam dabo eis]].

paras.t: Deinde narrantur peccata filiorum Israel commissa post ingressum terræ Chanaan. Non disperdiderunt gentes, id est, habitatores terræ Chanaan non occiderunt in toto, quas dixit Dominus illis, id est, quas Dominus jussit occidi, earumque aras subverti, neque connubia neque familiaritatem cum eis habere. Hoc frequenter præcepit filiis Israel, ne ex cohabitatione pertraherentur ad idololatriam. Sed filii Israel ex avaritia permiserunt quosdam de gente hac inter se morari, propter tributum quod eis solvebant. Et commixti sunt loco, corpore et opere inter gentes Chananæorum, et didicerunt opera eorum, id est ritum gentilitatis, et servierunt sculptilibus eorum, scilicet Baalim et Astaroth, ut patet in libro Judicum ; et factum est illis hoc idololatriæ scelus in scandalum, id est in magnam ruinam.
paras.en: Then are related the sins of the children of Israel committed after their entry into the land of Chanaan. [[105:34|They did not destroy the nations|Non disperdiderunt gentes]], that is, they did not wholly slay the inhabitants of the land of Chanaan, [[105:34|of which the Lord spoke unto them|quas dixit Dominus illis]], that is, which the Lord commanded to be slain, and their altars to be overthrown, and that they should have neither marriages nor familiarity with them. This he often commanded the children of Israel, lest from living together with them they should be drawn into idolatry. But the children of Israel out of avarice allowed some of this people to dwell among them, for the sake of the tribute which they paid them. [[105:35|And they were mingled|Et commixti sunt]] in place, in body and in deed, [[105:35|among the heathens|inter gentes]] of the Chanaanites, [[105:35|and learned their works|et didicerunt opera eorum]], that is, the rites of heathendom, [[105:36|And served their idols|et servierunt sculptilibus eorum]], namely Baalim and Astaroth, as appears in the book of Judges; and this crime of idolatry [[105:36|became a stumblingblock to them|et factum est illis hoc idololatriæ scelus in scandalum]], that is, a great downfall.

paras.t: Et immolaverunt filios suos et filias suas dæmoniis, quæ in idolis colebantur. Quomodo autem eos immolaverint, subditur : Et effuderunt sanguinem innocentem, videlicet sanguinem filiorum suorum et filiarum suarum, qui propter ætatem infantilem nondum peccaverant, quas sacrificaverunt, id est obtulerunt, sculptilibus Chanaan, id est simulacris Chananæorum. Quamvis alibi in historia canonica non legantur ista fecisse, credendum est tamen Prophetæ hæc recitanti.
paras.en: [[105:37|And they sacrificed their sons, and their daughters to devils|Et immolaverunt filios suos et filias suas dæmoniis]], which were worshipped in the idols. And how they sacrificed them is added: [[105:38|And they shed innocent blood|Et effuderunt sanguinem innocentem]], namely [[105:38|the blood of their sons and of their daughters|sanguinem filiorum suorum et filiarum suarum]], who because of their infant age had not yet sinned, [[105:38|which they sacrificed|quas sacrificaverunt]], that is, offered, [[105:38|to the idols of Chanaan|sculptilibus Chanaan]], that is, to the images of the Chanaanites. Although we do not read elsewhere in the canonical history that they did these things, yet the Prophet who relates them is to be believed.

paras.t: Et interfecta est terra habitationis eorum, id est, habitatores terræ occisi sunt, in sanguinibus quam crudeliter fusis seu impie factis, et contaminata est in operibus eorum tam nefandis. Vel, Interfecta est terra, id est, homines isti terreni effundendo sanguinem innocentem spiritualiter occisi sunt, quoniam animas proprias vita gratiæ spoliaverunt ; et contaminata est in operibus eorum, hoc est, ipsi in suis peccatis polluti sunt. Et fornicati sunt, id est, a Deo per idololatriam recesserunt, in adinventionibus suis, id est in peccatis suis industriose commissis. Merito autem idololatria in sacra Scriptura fornicatio appellatur, quia per eam recedit anima a vero sponso suo, scilicet Deo : cui per fidem et caritatem desponsatur, et a quo per gratiam ac dona Sancti Spiritus fecundatur, quemadmodum Dominus ait : Sponsabo te mihi in fide. Quoniam vero hoc modo fornicati sunt filii Israel, ideo dicitur eis : Noli lætari, Israel, et noli exsultare, quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo.
paras.en: [[105:38|And the land|Et interfecta est terra]] of their dwelling was slain [Denis reads interfecta, "slain", and the margin notes this as a variant; the Clementine Vulgate has infecta, "polluted", which the Douay-Rheims follows], that is, the inhabitants of the land were slain, [[105:38|with blood|in sanguinibus]] so cruelly shed, or so impiously wrought, [[105:39|And was defiled with their works|et contaminata est in operibus eorum]] so abominable. Or: [[105:38|the land|Interfecta est terra]] was slain, that is, these earthly men [terreni, from terra, "land": the land stands for its earthly people], by shedding innocent blood, were slain spiritually, since they robbed their own souls of the life of grace; [[105:39|And was defiled with their works|et contaminata est in operibus eorum]], that is, they themselves were polluted in their sins. [[105:39|and they went aside|Et fornicati sunt]] [the Latin is fornicati sunt, "they committed fornication"], that is, they departed from God by idolatry, [[105:39|after their own inventions|in adinventionibus suis]], that is, in their sins committed with deliberate contrivance. And rightly is idolatry called fornication in holy Scripture, because by it the soul departs from her true spouse, namely God: to whom she is espoused by faith and charity, and by whom she is made fruitful through the grace and gifts of the Holy Ghost, as the Lord says: [[Osee 2:20|I will espouse thee to me in faith|Sponsabo te mihi in fide]]. And because the children of Israel committed fornication in this way, therefore it is said to them: [[Osee 9:1|Rejoice not, O Israel: rejoice not|Noli lætari, Israel, et noli exsultare]], [[Osee 9:1|for thou hast committed fornication against thy God|quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo]].

paras.t: Et iratus est furore Dominus, id est, vehementer iratus est, non per animi commotionem, sed vindictæ gravitatem, in populum suum nomine, et non re ; et abominatus est hereditatem suam, id est filios Israel : quos ipse specialiter invitavit atque vocavit, ut essent hereditas ejus ; sed non obediendo, facti sunt hereditas dæmonis. Et tradidit eos in manus gentium, id est, protectionem et opem divinam eis subtraxit, permittens eos opprimi a Philistæis, Syris, ac aliis multis ; et dominati sunt eorum qui oderunt eos. Nam sicut in libro Judicum scribitur, quibusdam servierunt decem et octo annis, aliquibus longius, aliquibus brevius. Ecce quem Deus relinquit, a quo Deus subsidium tollit, inimicorum suorum servituti subjicitur. Prima quoque pœna culpæ, est subtractio gratiæ; secunda vero, incursio dominationis malignæ.
paras.en: [[105:40|And the Lord was exceedingly angry|Et iratus est furore Dominus]], that is, he was vehemently angry, not by any disturbance of mind but by the severity of his vengeance, [[105:40|with his people|in populum suum]], his in name and not in fact; [[105:40|and he abhorred his inheritance|et abominatus est hereditatem suam]], that is, the children of Israel, whom he had specially invited and called to be his inheritance; but by not obeying they became the inheritance of the devil. [[105:41|And he delivered them into the hands of the nations|Et tradidit eos in manus gentium]], that is, he withdrew from them the divine protection and help, permitting them to be oppressed by the Philistines, the Syrians and many others; [[105:41|and they that hated them had dominion over them|et dominati sunt eorum qui oderunt eos]]. For, as is written in the book of Judges, some of them they served eighteen years[[Judg 3:14||]], others longer[[Judg 4:3||]], others for a shorter time[[Judg 3:8||]]. Behold, he whom God forsakes, from whom God takes away his help, is made subject to the bondage of his enemies. And the first punishment of guilt is the withdrawal of grace; the second, the onset of an evil dominion.

paras.t: Et tribulaverunt eos inimici eorum, imponendo eis graves labores, magna tributa, ingentia damna ; et humiliati sunt filii Israel, id est dejecti, oppressi et victi, sub manibus eorum, id est sub potestate et persecutione adversariorum suorum. Vel, Humiliati sunt coram Deo sub manibus hostium, quia ex gravitate persecutionum confessi sunt sua peccata, veniamque petebant, et emendationem spondebant.
paras.en: [[105:42|And their enemies afflicted them|Et tribulaverunt eos inimici eorum]], laying upon them heavy labours, great tributes, enormous losses; [[105:42|and they were humbled|et humiliati sunt]], the children of Israel, that is, cast down, oppressed and vanquished, [[105:42|under their hands|sub manibus eorum]], that is, under the power and persecution of their adversaries. Or: they were humbled before God under the hands of their foes, because under the weight of the persecutions they confessed their sins, and begged pardon, and promised amendment.

paras.t: Sæpe liberavit eos Deus de potestate infidelium populorum, ut constat ex serie libri Judicum, in quo scriptum habetur : Quumque Dominus judices suscitaret, in diebus eorum flectebatur misericordia, et audiebat afflictorum gemitus, et liberabat eos de cæde vastantium. Ipsi autem exacerbaverunt eum : id est, post liberationem suam a Deo misericorditer factam, rursus reversi sunt ad pristina mala, et Deum offenderunt. Unde in libro Judicum dicitur : Quum mortuus esset judex, fecerunt multo majora quam patres eorum, sequentes deos alienos ; non deseruerunt viam durissimam, per quam ambulare consueverant. Sic autem exacerbaverunt Deum in consilio suo, quia ex malo eorum consilio adinventionibusque vanissimis orta sunt tanta facinora ; et humiliati sunt in iniquitatibus suis, id est, propter peccata sua ab hostibus oppressi et victi sunt, et etiam interdum coram Deo per pœnitentiam humiles facti.
paras.en: [[105:43|Many times did he deliver them|Sæpe liberavit eos]], God did, from the power of unbelieving peoples, as is clear from the course of the book of Judges, in which it is written: [[Judg 2:18|And when the Lord raised them up judges, in their days, he was moved to mercy, and heard the groanings of the afflicted, and delivered them from the slaughter of the oppressors|Quumque Dominus judices suscitaret, in diebus eorum flectebatur misericordia, et audiebat afflictorum gemitus, et liberabat eos de cæde vastantium]]. [[105:43|But they provoked him|Ipsi autem exacerbaverunt eum]]: that is, after their deliverance mercifully wrought by God, they went back again to their former evils, and offended God. Hence it is said in the book of Judges: When [[Judg 2:19|the judge was dead|Quum mortuus esset judex]], they did far greater evils than their fathers, [[Judg 2:19|following strange gods|sequentes deos alienos]]; they forsook not [[Judg 2:19|the stubborn way, by which they were accustomed to walk|viam durissimam, per quam ambulare consueverant]]. Thus they provoked God [[105:43|with their counsel|in consilio suo]], because from their evil counsel and most vain inventions such great crimes arose; [[105:43|and they were brought low by their iniquities|et humiliati sunt in iniquitatibus suis]], that is, on account of their sins they were oppressed and vanquished by their enemies, and also at times made humble before God by penance.
