paras.t: Et vidit quum tribularentur, id est, Deus clementer adspexit eos, dum taliter affligerentur, et audivit orationem eorum, qua petebant ab adversariorum jugo liberari. Et memor fuit per effectum misericordiæ suæ, testamenti sui, id est fœderis seu promissionis, qua prædixit frequenter per Moysen, quod liberaret eos, quandocumque corde integro reverterentur ad Dominum Deum patrum suorum. Unde in Deuteronomio dictum est eis a Moyse : Si ad cardines cœli fueris dissipatus, inde retrahet te Dominus Deus tuus, et assumet ac introducet in terram quam possederunt patres tui. Et in eodem Deuteronomii libro : Quum quæsieris, inquit, Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum, si tamen toto corde quæsieris eum, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ. Et pœnituit eum, id est, per modum pœnitentis se eis exhibuit, quia quos in direptionem captivitatemque dedit, iterum pie eripuit, secundum multitudinem misericordiæ suæ, id est secundum quod ipse multum misericors est, et non propter virtutes eorum. Propter quod rursus in Deuteronomio Moyses ait : Ne dicas in corde tuo, Propter justitiam meam introduxit me Dominus in terram hanc, quum populus durissimæ cervicis sis.
paras.en: [[105:44|And he saw when they were in tribulation|Et vidit quum tribularentur]], that is, God looked mercifully upon them while they were so afflicted, [[105:44|and he heard their prayer|et audivit orationem eorum]], in which they asked to be freed from the yoke of their adversaries. [[105:45|And he was mindful|Et memor fuit]], by the effect of his mercy, [[105:45|of his covenant|testamenti sui]], that is, of the compact or promise by which he often foretold through Moses that he would free them whenever they returned with a whole heart to the Lord, the God of their fathers. Hence in Deuteronomy it was said to them by Moses: [[Deut 30:4|If thou be driven as far as the poles of heaven, the Lord thy God will fetch thee back from hence|Si ad cardines cœli fueris dissipatus, inde retrahet te Dominus Deus tuus]], [[Deut 30:5|And will take thee to himself, and bring thee into the land which thy fathers possessed|et assumet ac introducet in terram quam possederunt patres tui]]. And in the same book of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 4:29|when thou shalt seek|Quum quæsieris]], he says, [[Deut 4:29|the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him: yet so, if thou seek him with all thy heart, and all the affliction of thy soul|Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum, si tamen toto corde quæsieris eum, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ]]. [[105:45|and repented|Et pœnituit eum]], that is, he showed himself toward them after the manner of one who repents, because those whom he had given up to plunder and captivity he lovingly rescued again, [[105:45|according to the multitude of his mercies|secundum multitudinem misericordiæ suæ]], that is, according as he himself is very merciful, and not on account of their virtues. For which reason Moses says again in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 9:4|Say not in thy heart|Ne dicas in corde tuo]]: [[Deut 9:4|For my justice hath the Lord brought me in|Propter justitiam meam introduxit me Dominus]] into this land, [[Deut 9:6|for thou art a very stiffnecked people|quum populus durissimæ cervicis sis]].

paras.t: Et dedit eos in misericordias, id est, suæ divinæ pietatis effectus varios eis impendit, in conspectu omnium qui ceperant eos : quoniam illis videntibus, atque per experientiam pœnæ graviter sæpe luentibus, liberavit filios Israel de potestate eorum.
paras.en: [[105:46|And he gave them unto mercies|Et dedit eos in misericordias]], that is, he bestowed on them the various effects of his divine loving-kindness, [[105:46|in the sight of all those that had made them captives|in conspectu omnium qui ceperant eos]]: since, while these looked on, and often paid heavily for it by the experience of punishment, he freed the children of Israel from their power.

paras.t: Postremo orat Propheta pro populi sui liberatione ac adjuvatione, seu reductione in terram patrum suorum. Et potest esse oratio Ecclesiæ pro conversione et spirituali unione fidelium. Salvos fac nos, Domine Deus noster, ab omni periculo mentis et corporis, et a malis præteritis, præsentibus et futuris, et congrega nos de nationibus, id est, ab infidelibus separa nos atque recollige, loco vel voto, quatenus separati a generatione perversa, tibi fideliter ministremus, nec cum perversis pervertamur. Ut confiteamur nomini sancto tuo nostra mala et tua bona, nos accusando, teque laudando, et ita duplici confessione te venerando, videlicet confessione tuæ laudis, et nostræ iniquitatis ; et gloriemur spirituali jucunditate in laude tua, ita quod te laudemus delectabiliter atque ferventer, non pigre aut somnolenter.
paras.en: Lastly the Prophet prays for the deliverance and help of his people, or for their bringing back into the land of their fathers. And it can be the prayer of the Church for the conversion and spiritual union of the faithful. [[105:47|Save us, O Lord, our God|Salvos fac nos, Domine Deus noster]], from every danger of mind and body, and from evils past, present and to come, [[105:47|and gather us from among the nations|et congrega nos de nationibus]], that is, separate us from the unbelievers and gather us together, in place or in will, so that, separated from a perverse generation, we may serve thee faithfully, and not be perverted with the perverse[[Ps 17:27||]]. [[105:47|That we may give thanks to thy holy name|Ut confiteamur nomini sancto tuo]] [confiteamur: "that we may confess", a word used both of praising God and of confessing sins; Denis takes it in both senses], confessing our evils and thy goods, accusing ourselves and praising thee, and so honouring thee with a twofold confession, namely the confession of thy praise and of our iniquity; [[105:47|and may glory|et gloriemur]] with spiritual gladness [[105:47|in thy praise|in laude tua]], so that we may praise thee with delight and fervour, not sluggishly or drowsily.

paras.t: Benedictus sit, id est, ab omnibus benedicatur, semperque laudatus sit, Dominus Deus Israel, a sæculo et usque in sæculum, id est per omnia sæcula ; et dicet omnis populus, in Christum credens, non tantum Judæi : Fiat, fiat, id est, Amen, amen. In omni enim orbe terrarum consentiunt Christiani huic laudi divinæ, dicentes : Fiat, fiat.
paras.en: [[105:48|Blessed be|Benedictus sit]], that is, may he be blessed by all and ever praised, [[105:48|the Lord the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting|Dominus Deus Israel, a sæculo et usque in sæculum]], that is, through all ages; [[105:48|and let all the people say|et dicet omnis populus]], all that believe in Christ, not the Jews only: [[105:48|So be it, so be it|Fiat, fiat]], that is, Amen, amen. For throughout the whole world Christians agree to this divine praise, saying: So be it, so be it.

paras.t: Porro multa in hoc psalmo contenta, spiritualiter intelligi possunt. Quod enim patres prædicti in Ægypto non intellexerunt mirabilia Dei, nec memores fuerunt multitudinis misericordiæ ejus : significat, quod multi (proh dolor !) Christianorum in sæculo isto non advertunt miracula Christi, nec opera ejus sequuntur, nec recolunt beneficia ejus, nec intelligere student mysteria Salvatoris. Eductio quoque filiorum Israel de Ægypto, præfiguravit conversionem gentium ad Christi fidem et cultum. Hæc namque conversio est spiritualis egressio de veteri vita atque consortio reproborum, de qua ait Apostolus : Exite de medio eorum, et immundum ne tetigeritis. Figuravit etiam ingressum religiosorum ad claustrum. Tunc enim Ægyptum, id est mundum istum, prorsus relinquunt, et dæmonum operibus plene renuntiant.
paras.en: Moreover, many things contained in this psalm can be understood spiritually. For that the aforesaid fathers did not understand the wonders of God in Egypt, nor were mindful of the multitude of his mercy[[105:7||]], signifies that many Christians (alas!) in this world do not heed the miracles of Christ, nor follow his works, nor call to mind his benefits, nor study to understand the mysteries of the Saviour. The leading of the children of Israel out of Egypt, too, prefigured the conversion of the Gentiles to the faith and worship of Christ. For this conversion is a spiritual going out from the old life and from the company of the reprobate, of which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 6:17|Go out from among them|Exite de medio eorum]], [[2 Cor 6:17|and touch not the unclean thing|et immundum ne tetigeritis]]. It figured also the entry of religious into the cloister. For then they wholly leave Egypt, that is, this world, and fully renounce the works of the demons.

paras.t: Demum mare Rubrum signavit Baptismum Christi sanguine consecratum. Et sicut eundo per mare Rubrum, salvati sunt filii Israel de servitute Ægypti ac manu Pharaonis, sic fideles per fontem Baptismatis liberantur a servitute peccati ac potestate diaboli. Et sicut in mari Rubro mergebantur Ægyptii, sic in Baptismo : id est, non suscipiendo Baptismum, spiritualiter pereunt infideles, quia baptizari contemnunt. Nisi enim quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest videre regnum Dei, ut apud Evangelistam Christus testatur. Manna quoque fuit typus Sacramenti corporis et sanguinis Christi. Et sicut filii Israel post transitum maris Rubri manducaverunt manna, sic Christiani post regenerationem Baptismi accipiunt Christi sacramenta. Hinc enim ait Apostolus : Nolo vos ignorare fratres, quoniam patres nostri omnes sub nube fuerunt, et omnes mare transierunt, et omnes in Moyse baptizati sunt in nube et in mari, et omnes eamdem escam spiritualem manducaverunt, et omnes eumdem potum spiritualem biberunt. Biberunt autem de spirituali consequente eos petra : petra autem erat Christus. Hæc autem in figura facta sunt nostri.
paras.en: Further, the Red Sea signified Baptism, consecrated by the blood of Christ. And as the children of Israel, by going through the Red Sea, were saved from the bondage of Egypt and the hand of Pharao, so the faithful through the font of Baptism are freed from the bondage of sin and the power of the devil. And as the Egyptians were drowned in the Red Sea, so in Baptism, that is, by not receiving Baptism, the unbelievers perish spiritually, since they scorn to be baptized. For [[John 3:5|unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot|Nisi enim quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest]] [[John 3:3|see the kingdom of God|videre regnum Dei]], as Christ testifies in the Evangelist [the margin gives John iii, 5; the words see the kingdom of God are those of John 3:3]. The manna, too, was a type of the Sacrament of the body and blood of Christ. And as the children of Israel after the crossing of the Red Sea ate manna[[Ex 16:35||]], so Christians after the regeneration of Baptism receive the sacraments of Christ. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 10:1|I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that our fathers were all under the cloud: and all passed through the sea|Nolo vos ignorare fratres, quoniam patres nostri omnes sub nube fuerunt, et omnes mare transierunt]], [[1 Cor 10:2|And all in Moses were baptized, in the cloud and in the sea|et omnes in Moyse baptizati sunt in nube et in mari]], [[1 Cor 10:3|And did all eat the same spiritual food|et omnes eamdem escam spiritualem manducaverunt]], [[1 Cor 10:4|And all drank the same spiritual drink|et omnes eumdem potum spiritualem biberunt]]. [[1 Cor 10:4|And they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them: and the rock was Christ|Biberunt autem de spirituali consequente eos petra : petra autem erat Christus]]. [[1 Cor 10:6|Now these things were done in a figure of us|Hæc autem in figura facta sunt nostri]].

paras.t: Insuper ex eo quod dictum est, Aperta est terra, et deglutivit Dathan, monemur advertere, quam enorme sit seditionis ac rebellionis peccatum, atque ambitio dominandi. Expavescant igitur ex tam horrenda Dei vindicta, qui superiores suos contemnunt, qui remurmurant, qui obedire despiciunt, qui præesse desiderant. Pensent quid Christus dicat prælatis suis vicariis : Qui vos audit, me audit ; et qui vos spernit, me spernit. Unde et in Exodo Moyses rebellibus dixit : Non contra nos est murmur vestrum, sed contra Dominum. Et alibi : Quid, inquit, est Aaron, ut murmuretis contra eum?
paras.en: Moreover, from what is said, [[105:17|The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan|Aperta est terra, et deglutivit Dathan]], we are warned to consider how monstrous is the sin of sedition and rebellion, and the ambition to rule. Let them therefore tremble at so dreadful a vengeance of God, who despise their superiors, who murmur, who disdain to obey, who desire to be over others. Let them weigh what Christ says to his prelates, his vicars: [[Luke 10:16|He that heareth you heareth me: and he that despiseth you despiseth me|Qui vos audit, me audit ; et qui vos spernit, me spernit]]. Hence also in Exodus Moses said to the rebels: [[Ex 16:8|your murmuring is not against us, but against the Lord|Non contra nos est murmur vestrum, sed contra Dominum]]. And elsewhere: [[Num 16:11|What|Quid]], he says, [[Num 16:11|is Aaron that you murmur against him?|est Aaron, ut murmuretis contra eum?]]

paras.t: Attendant etiam sacerdotes carnaliter et indigne viventes, qualiter flamma combussit peccatores, qui sibi officium sacerdotale indigne usurpaverunt. Nempe, ut ait Apostolus, Quicumque manducaverit panem vel biberit calicem Domini indigne, reus erit corporis et sanguinis Christi. Idcirco æterno igne cremabitur : cujus figura exstitit flamma illa divinitus missa, Coritas consumens.
paras.en: Let priests also who live carnally and unworthily take heed how [[105:18|the flame burned the wicked|flamma combussit peccatores]], who unworthily usurped the priestly office for themselves[[Lev 10:2||]][[Num 16:35||]]. For, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 11:27|whosoever shall eat|Quicumque manducaverit]] bread [[1 Cor 11:27|or drink the chalice of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and of the blood|vel biberit calicem Domini indigne, reus erit corporis et sanguinis]] of Christ. Therefore he shall be burned with everlasting fire: of which that flame sent from God, consuming the Corites, was a figure.

paras.t: Et mutaverunt gloriam suam in similitudinem vituli comedentis fœnum. His assimilantur, qui tota die circa phantasmata sua occupantur, non contemplantes cœlestia, nec meditantes in lege divina. Unde Joannes in prima sua Canonica exhortatur : Filioli, custodite vos a simulacris.
paras.en: [[105:20|And they changed their glory into the likeness of a calf that eateth grass|Et mutaverunt gloriam suam in similitudinem vituli comedentis fœnum]]. To these are likened those who all day long are busied about their own fancies [phantasmata, the images that the imagination forms], not contemplating heavenly things, nor meditating on the divine law. Hence John exhorts in his first Canonical epistle: [[1 John 5:21|Little children, keep yourselves from idols|Filioli, custodite vos a simulacris]].

paras.t: Præterea ex eo quod dictum est, Et dixit ut disperderet eos, si non Moyses electus ejus stetisset in confractione in conspectu ejus, ut averteret iram ejus, discant aliorum rectores, qui inter Deum ac populum constituti sunt mediatores, pro grege sibi commisso instantissime, fidelis[…]ventissime deprecari : nec ali[…] […]tuque zelo contra delinquentes […] compati : nec tamen eos impu[…]quere, sed in præsenti eos dis[…]piant atque flagellent, si fieri possit, et […]desse conspiciunt. Pensent qua[…] dixit : Aut dimitte populo hanc […] si non facis, dele me de libro […]psisti. Hanc ergo boni pastores […] sequantur, et se vita ac prece […] exhibeant inter Deum et sibi co[…] rei fiant damnationis eorum. […]que quod in Ezechiele asseri[…] Quæsivi de eis virum qui inter[…] […] et staret oppositus con[…] terra, ne dissiparem eam ; et […] et effudi super eos indignatio[…] Sed et exemplo Phinees mon[…] amantes, zelare pro Deo suo co[…]sos : quemadmodum tertio l[…]icit Elias. Zelo […] nu[…] exercituum. Omnino namque […] est, delinquentes in hoc sæculo […] ne æternaliter pereant, vel ne i[…]tius perseverent. Et sicut ait […]mus, quamvis pium sit, propria[…] tolerare, impium tamen est D[…] dissimulare. Verumtamen, si[…] Apostolus, Æmulationem Dei […]bent, sed non secundum sci[…] scilicet qui propria vitia negl[…]ri, deplangere, corrigere et […]rum vero peccata amare dij[…]ne compassione condemnant, […] onera caritative supportant. […] autem Phinees sacerdotis hor[…]nymus quemlibet Christi sace[…]orum rectorem, dicendo : Ho[…] ausculta, sacerdos, cui animæ […]tæ sunt. Evagina gladium verb[…]me fornicationem ; insta opp[…]portune ; argue, increpa, obsec[…] patientia et doctrina, ut tibi r[…] justitiam. Unde in Levitico D[…]cerdotibus ait : Habeatis scien[…]nendi inter sanctum et profan[…]tisque filios Israel omnia legit[…]
paras.en: Further, from what is said, [[105:23|And he said that he would destroy them: had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach: To turn away his wrath|Et dixit ut disperderet eos, si non Moyses electus ejus stetisset in confractione in conspectu ejus, ut averteret iram ejus]], let the rulers of others, who are set as mediators between God and the people, learn, for the flock committed to them, [the transcription of the column that begins here is damaged: most of its lines have lost words, and the gaps are marked; only what survives is translated] to pray most urgently, most faithfully […] most fervently; nor […] with […] zeal against offenders […] to have compassion; yet not to leave them unpunished […], but in this present life […] and scourge them, if it can be done, and […] they perceive. Let them weigh how […] said: [[Ex 32:31|either forgive|Aut dimitte]] the people this […] [[Ex 32:32|if thou do not, strike me out of the book|si non facis, dele me de libro]] […] thou hast written. Let good shepherds therefore follow this […], and by life and prayer show themselves […] between God and those committed to them […] become guilty of their damnation. […] what is affirmed in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 22:30|I sought among them for a man that might|Quæsivi de eis virum qui]] […] [[Ezech 22:30|and stand in the gap|et staret oppositus]] […] [[Ezech 22:30|land, that I might not destroy it|terra, ne dissiparem eam]]; and […] [[Ezech 22:31|And I poured out|et effudi]] indignation [[Ezech 22:31|upon them|super eos]] […]. But by the example of Phinees[[Num 25:7||]][[Num 25:8||]] too […] who love […] to be zealous for their God […], as Elias says in the third book […]: [[3 Kings 19:10|With zeal|Zelo]] […] [[3 Kings 19:10|of hosts|exercituum]]. For it is altogether […] offenders in this world […], lest they perish eternally, or lest they […] persevere. And as […] says, though it be a dutiful thing to bear one's own […], yet it is impious to pass over God's […]. Nevertheless, as […] the Apostle, […] have [[Rom 10:2|a zeal of God|Æmulationem Dei]], [[Rom 10:2|but not according to|sed non secundum]] knowledge: namely those who neglect […] to bewail, to correct and […] their own vices, but the sins of […] they judge bitterly […] and condemn without compassion, […] bear burdens charitably. […] of Phinees the priest […] Jerome […] every priest of Christ and ruler of […], saying: […] hearken, O priest, to whom souls […] have been. Unsheathe the sword of the word […] fornication; [[2 Tim 4:2|be instant|insta]] in season, […] out of season; [[2 Tim 4:2|reprove|argue]], [[2 Tim 4:2|rebuke|increpa]], entreat […] [[2 Tim 4:2|patience and doctrine|patientia et doctrina]], that […] to thee […] justice. Hence in Leviticus the Lord says to the priests: [[Lev 10:10|you may have|Habeatis]] knowledge […] to discern [[Lev 10:10|between holy|inter sanctum]] and unholy […] and […] [[Lev 10:11|the children of Israel all|filios Israel omnia]] ordinances […]

paras.t: Præterea ex eo quod dictum est, Pro nihilo habuerunt terram desiderabilem, curandum est nobis, ne Christi promissa parvi pendamus, ne terram viventium, ne regnum cœlorum, ne beatitudinem sempiternam propter hujus mundi amorem, temporalem honorem, vilem carnis delectationem, aut momentaneæ vitæ hujus complacentiam, miserabiliter irrecuperabiliterque perdamus ; sed cum divino Apostolo illud ad Philippenses veraciter proferamus : Omnia arbitror ut stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciam.
paras.en: Further, from what is said, [[105:24|they set at nought the desirable land|Pro nihilo habuerunt terram desiderabilem]], we must take care not to make small account of the promises of Christ, not wretchedly and irrecoverably to lose the land of the living, the kingdom of heaven, everlasting beatitude, for love of this world, for temporal honour, for the base pleasure of the flesh, or for the satisfaction of this momentary life; but with the divine Apostle let us truly say that word of his to the Philippians: [[Phil 3:8|I count all things|Omnia arbitror]] [[Phil 3:8|but as dung|ut stercora]], [[Phil 3:8|that I may gain Christ|ut Christum lucrifaciam]].

paras.t: Postremo ex eo quod dictum est, Et vidit quum tribularetur […]mus inæstimabilia viscera infinitæ clementiæ piissimi Dei, atque in omni angustia ad eum cum plena fiducia recurramus, dicentes : Peccavimus cum patribus nostris, iniquitatem fecimus […] Et tunc utique pœnitebit eum secundum multitudinem misericordiæ suæ, dolebitque […] sicut ait Scriptura super miseriis nostris, et propitius erit.
paras.en: Lastly, from what is said, [[105:44|And he saw when they were in tribulation|Et vidit quum tribularetur]], let us […] the inestimable bowels of the infinite clemency of our most loving God, and in every strait let us run back to him with full confidence, saying: [[105:6|We have sinned with our fathers|Peccavimus cum patribus nostris]], [[105:6|we have wrought iniquity|iniquitatem fecimus]] […] And then surely he will repent [[105:45|according to the multitude of his mercies|secundum multitudinem misericordiæ suæ]], and will grieve […], as Scripture says, over our miseries[[Judg 10:16||]] [the margin gives Jud. ii, 18; the words grieve over miseries are those of Judges 10:16], and will be propitious[[Joel 2:13||]].

paras.t: Ex eo autem quod dictum est, Et […], monemur advertere, quam periculosum atque nocivum sit famulis Christi, et maxime religiosis ac solitariis, cum sæcularibus hominibus conversari, mundi rumores inquirere, facta sæculi recogitare. Hæc namque cordis puritatem inficiunt, stabilitatem animi interrumpunt, divinam caritatem vehementer dirimunt, solitudinem in horrorem ac nauseam vertunt, sæculi falsam dilectionem gignunt ac nutriunt. Summe igitur nobis Cartusiensibus vitanda sunt ista, si digne conversari optamus vocatione, qua nos Spiritus Sanctus vocavit.
paras.en: And from what is said, And […][[105:35||]][[105:36||]] [the rest of the words Denis quotes is lost in the transcription; the margin gives vv. 35, 36, so he probably quoted: And they were mingled among the heathens, and learned their works], we are warned to consider how dangerous and harmful it is for the servants of Christ, and above all for religious and solitaries, to converse with men of the world, to inquire after the rumours of the world, to turn over in mind the doings of the world. For these things infect purity of heart, break up stability of mind, violently sunder divine charity, turn solitude into horror and loathing, and beget and nourish a false love of the world. Supremely, then, are these things to be shunned by us Carthusians, if we desire to live worthy of the vocation with which the Holy Ghost has called us[[Eph 4:1||]].

paras.t: Memento nostri in beneplacito tuo, Domine, et doce nos justitiam facere in omni tempore ; facque nos in laude tua semper gloriari, et a sæculo usque in sæculum, Deus Israel, benedicere tibi.
paras.en: [[105:4|Remember us|Memento nostri]] in thy good pleasure, [[105:4|O Lord|Domine]], and teach us to [[105:3|do justice at all times|justitiam facere in omni tempore]]; and make us ever to [[105:47|glory in thy praise|in laude tua semper gloriari]], and [[105:48|from everlasting to everlasting|a sæculo usque in sæculum]], O [[105:48|God of Israel|Deus Israel]], to bless thee.

105.note: Part of the Latin (the left column of p. 468, in the moral reading of vv. 23 and 30) is damaged in the transcription; lost words are marked […].

106.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI SEXTI : CONFITEMINI DOMINO... DICANT QUI, ETC.
106.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and sixth psalm: Give glory to the Lord… Let them say who, etc.

paras.t: Psalmi insuper jam tractandi titulus, in verbis ac sensu idem est cum titulo psalmi præcedentis. Nam titulus ejus est : Alleluia, alleluia. Materia autem psalmi præsentis, secundum Augustinum, est gratiarum actio pro universali redemptione generis humani, facta per Christum, quam sanctus David Spiritu revelante cognovit. Alii vero grosse procedentes, affirmant quod psalmus iste sit gratiarum actio, seu invitatio ad gratiarum actionem, aliquorum Judæorum a diversis malis liberatorum, et ex omni parte mundi divinitus ereptorum a locis seu periculis in quibus fuerunt. Sed quoniam prima expositio longe convenientior est, subtilior atque devotior, et textui consona, ideo ei prius principaliusque immorandum videtur. Alia vero forsitan tangetur.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be treated is, moreover, the same in words and in sense as the title of the preceding psalm. For its title is: Alleluia, alleluia. The matter of the present psalm, according to Augustine, is a thanksgiving for the universal redemption of the human race wrought by Christ, which holy David knew by the revelation of the Spirit. Others, however, proceeding coarsely [that is, keeping to the bare letter], affirm that this psalm is a thanksgiving, or an invitation to thanksgiving, of certain Jews delivered from various evils and rescued by God from every part of the world, out of the places or dangers in which they were. But since the first exposition is far more fitting, more subtle and more devout, and in keeping with the text, it seems that we should dwell on it first and chiefly. The other will perhaps be touched on.

paras.t: Invitans igitur sanctus Propheta homines omnes ad Christi laudem pro omnibus beneficiis ejus, ait : Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus. Versiculus iste in expositione psalmi præcedentis, qui sic incipit sicut et iste, satis expositus est.
paras.en: Inviting all men, then, to the praise of Christ for all his benefits, the holy Prophet says: [[106:1|Give glory to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.|Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus]] This little verse has been sufficiently explained in the exposition of the preceding psalm, which begins as this one does.

paras.t: Dicant (ad quod versus præcedens hortatur), id est, Dominum laudent, qui redempti sunt a Domino, id est, quos Christus sua incarnatione ac passione redemit, juxta illud ad Ephesios : Christus dilexit nos, et tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem et hostiam Deo, in odorem suavitatis. De quo in Apocalypsi ait Joannes : Christus dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo. Quos redemit de manu inimici, id est de potestate et captivitate diaboli. Propter quod in Evangelio ait, Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras; et apud Osee, De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos. Unde apud Matthæum angelus dixit de Christo : Ipse salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum.
paras.en: [[106:2|Let them say so|Dicant]] (as the preceding verse exhorts them to), that is, let them praise the Lord, [[106:2|that have been redeemed by the Lord|qui redempti sunt a Domino]], that is, whom Christ redeemed by his incarnation and passion, according to that word to the Ephesians: [[Eph 5:2|Christ also hath loved us and hath delivered himself for us, an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness|Christus dilexit nos, et tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem et hostiam Deo, in odorem suavitatis]]. Of him John says in the Apocalypse: Christ, [[Apoc 1:5|who hath loved us and washed us from our sins in his own blood|dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo]]. [[106:2|Whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy|Quos redemit de manu inimici]], that is, from the power and captivity of the devil. For this reason he says in the Gospel: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]; and in Osee: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos]]. Hence in Matthew the angel said of Christ: [[Matt 1:21|he shall save his people from their sins|Ipse salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum]].

paras.t: De regionibus, id est omnibus terminis mundi, seu quatuor plagis terræ, congregavit eos : non motu locali, sed conversione spirituali ; non in eumdem corporeum locum, sed in unam fidem, in unam Ecclesiam, in cultum eumdem. De hac namque spirituali congregatione credentium, per Apostolos atque eorum cooperatores facta, scriptum est in Joanne : Jesus moriturus erat pro gente ; et non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum. Et apud Prophetam : Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, etc.; et adducent omnes fratres vestros ad montem sanctum meum, id est ad Ecclesiam militantem. Congregavit autem eos non solum ab uno latere mundi, sed A solis ortu et occasu, id est ab oriente et ab occidente, ab aquilone et mari, id est a parte aquilonari et australi. Per mare enim Auster exprimitur, quoniam flat versus Oceanum : qui mare vocatur, quia ceteris aquarum congregationibus major est. Christus ergo ex omnibus partibus mundi collegit credentes. Propter quod in Marco Apostolis dicit : Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ. Hoc quoque in Isaia de Christo inducitur : Videbunt gentes justum tuum, et cuncti reges inclytum tuum : quod impleri non poterat, nisi in omnibus regionibus fides Christi annuntiaretur.
paras.en: [[106:2|Out of the countries|De regionibus]], that is, from all the bounds of the world, or the four quarters of the earth, he [[106:2|gathered|congregavit eos]] them: not by local motion but by spiritual conversion; not into the same bodily place, but into one faith, into one Church, into the same worship. For of this spiritual gathering of the believers, made through the Apostles and their fellow-workers, it is written in John: [[John 11:51|that Jesus should die for the nation|Jesus moriturus erat pro gente]]; and [[John 11:52|not only for the nation, but to gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed|non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum]]. And in the Prophet: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint]], etc.; [[Is 66:20|and they shall bring all your brethren|et adducent omnes fratres vestros]] [[Is 66:20|to my holy mountain|ad montem sanctum meum]], that is, to the Church militant. And he gathered them not only from one side of the world, but [[106:3|from the rising and from the setting of the sun|A solis ortu et occasu]], that is, from the east and from the west, [[106:3|from the north and from the sea|ab aquilone et mari]], that is, from the northern and the southern part. For by *the sea* the south is meant [Latin *Auster*, the south wind], since it blows toward the Ocean, which is called the sea because it is greater than the other gatherings of waters. Christ therefore gathered believers from all parts of the world. For this reason in Mark he says to the Apostles: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]. This also is said of Christ in Isaias: [[Is 62:2|The Gentiles shall see thy just one, and all kings thy glorious one|Videbunt gentes justum tuum, et cuncti reges inclytum tuum]]: which could not be fulfilled unless the faith of Christ were proclaimed in all countries.

paras.t: Erraverunt credentes, antequam converterentur ad Dominum, in solitudine, id est in mundo isto a gratia Dei relicto : quod intelligendum est de mundo damnationis, et societate angelorum privato, dicentium illud : Curavimus Babylonem, et non est sanata : derelinquamus eam : in inaquoso, id est in infidelitate seu arido corde, non habente rorem gratiæ salutaris, nec pluviam instructionis cælestis. Viam civitatis habitaculi, id est rectum iter perveniendi ad supernam Jerusalem, ad habitationem Beatorum, ad patriam electorum, non invenerunt potestate humana aut lumine naturali. Hæc enim via est fides catholica, quia secundum Apostolum, accedentem ad Deum oportet credere. Fidem vero homo sine supernaturali adjutorio adipisci, seu invenire non potuit. Potest quoque per viam hanc intelligi conversatio bona seu observatio præceptorum, quæ sine gratia haberi non potest, quemadmodum dum Jeremias hoc clare testatur : Scio, Domine, quia non est in homine via ejus, nec viri est ut dirigat gressus suos. Idcirco semper quærenda est nobis hæc via a Deo, ab angelis sanctis animarum nostrarum custodibus, a doctioribus, melioribus ac superioribus nostris, ne deviemus in isto exsilio. Hinc enim rursus in Jeremia habetur : Interrogate de semitis antiquis quæ sit via bona, et ambulate in ea.
paras.en: [[106:4|They wandered|Erraverunt]], the believers, before they were converted to the Lord, [[106:4|in a wilderness|in solitudine]], that is, in this world forsaken by the grace of God: which is to be understood of the world of damnation, deprived of the fellowship of the angels, who say that word: [[Jer 51:9|We would have cured Babylon, but she is not healed: let us forsake her|Curavimus Babylonem, et non est sanata : derelinquamus eam]]; [[106:4|in a place without water|in inaquoso]], that is, in unbelief, or in a dry heart, that has neither the dew of saving grace nor the rain of heavenly instruction. And [[106:4|the way of a city for their habitation|Viam civitatis habitaculi]], that is, the straight road for reaching the heavenly Jerusalem, the dwelling of the Blessed, the fatherland of the elect, [[106:4|they found not|non invenerunt]] by human power or by natural light. For this way is the Catholic faith, since according to the Apostle, [[Heb 11:6|he that cometh to God must believe|accedentem ad Deum oportet credere]]. But faith man could not obtain or find without supernatural help. By this way may also be understood good conduct, or the keeping of the commandments, which cannot be had without grace, as Jeremias clearly testifies: [[Jer 10:23|I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his|Scio, Domine, quia non est in homine via ejus]]: [[Jer 10:23|neither is it in a man|nec viri est]] [[Jer 10:23|to direct his steps|ut dirigat gressus suos]]. Therefore this way must always be sought by us from God, from the holy angels, the guardians of our souls, and from those more learned, better and higher than ourselves, lest we go astray in this exile. For hence again it is found in Jeremias: [[Jer 6:16|ask for the old paths, which is the good way, and walk ye in it|Interrogate de semitis antiquis quæ sit via bona, et ambulate in ea]].

paras.t: Esurientes et sitientes, id est beatitudinem appetentes, quam omnes naturaliter appetunt. Vel, Esurientes et sitientes justitiam naturalem : quam multi gentilium in tantum optabant, ut se propter eam morti exponerent. Vel, Esurientes et sitientes felicitatem in bonis terrenis, sensibilibus et caducis, in quibus multi summum hominis bonum posuerunt, ut scribit Boetius. Vel, Esurientes et sitientes justitiam legis divinæ, et prædicationem Evangelii postquam fidem receperunt. Anima eorum in ipsis defecit : id est, appetitum hujus famis et sitis ad effectum perducere non valebant propria potestate, sed gratia indigebant. Vel, Anima eorum in ipsis defecit, quoniam licet secundum aliquem modum esuriem suam ac sitim ad actum perduxerunt, acquirendo naturalem justitiam seu temporalium rerum copiam, non tamen suffecit hoc eis ad veram salutem. Propterea vani et vacui permanserunt.
paras.en: [[106:5|They were hungry and thirsty|Esurientes et sitientes]], that is, desiring beatitude, which all men naturally desire. Or, [[106:5|hungry and thirsty|Esurientes et sitientes]] for natural justice, which many of the Gentiles longed for so much that they exposed themselves to death for it. Or, [[106:5|hungry and thirsty|Esurientes et sitientes]] for happiness in earthly, sensible and perishable goods, in which many have placed the highest good of man, as Boethius writes. Or, [[106:5|hungry and thirsty|Esurientes et sitientes]] for the justice of the divine law and the preaching of the Gospel, after they had received the faith. [[106:5|Their soul fainted in them|Anima eorum in ipsis defecit]]: that is, they were not able by their own power to bring the craving of this hunger and thirst to its fulfilment, but stood in need of grace. Or, [[106:5|their soul fainted in them|Anima eorum in ipsis defecit]], because, although in some manner they brought their hunger and thirst to act, by acquiring natural justice or an abundance of temporal things, yet this did not suffice them for true salvation. Therefore they remained vain and empty.

paras.t: Et clamaverunt ad Dominum pro auxilio gratiæ ejus, quum tribularentur, id est, affligerentur in animo, eo quod optatam perfectionem adipisci non possent, sed tentationibus vincerentur, concupiscentiis quoque succumberent : quod est studiosis tanta afflictio mentis, ut ex eorum persona dicat Apostolus ad Romanos : Video aliam legem in membris meis, repugnantem legi mentis meæ, et captivantem me in lege peccati, quæ est in membris meis. Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus? Gratia Dei per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum. Idcirco nunc additur : et de necessitatibus eorum eripuit eos, id est, de malis seu vitiis atque periculis, a quibus propria virtute liberari non poterant, liberati sunt gratia Dei, quæ eos illuminavit ad fidem : sine qua nullus adultus utens ratione, sine mortali peccato vivere potest, quia secundum Apostolum, quidquid non est ex fide, peccatum est. Tamen nec fidem, nec gratiam habere quis potest, nisi a Deo. Gentes ergo, quamdiu luce fidei privabantur, gratiaque carebant, indesinenter seu nimis frequenter peccabant.
paras.en: [[106:6|And they cried to the Lord|Et clamaverunt ad Dominum]] for the help of his grace, [[106:6|in their tribulation|quum tribularentur]], that is, when they were afflicted in mind because they could not attain the perfection they longed for, but were overcome by temptations and gave way to concupiscences as well: which is so great an affliction of mind to the earnest that the Apostle, speaking in their person, says to the Romans: [[Rom 7:23|I see another law in my members, fighting against the law of my mind and captivating me in the law of sin that is in my members|Video aliam legem in membris meis, repugnantem legi mentis meæ, et captivantem me in lege peccati, quæ est in membris meis]]. [[Rom 7:24|Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?|Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus?]] [[Rom 7:25|The grace of God, by Jesus Christ our Lord|Gratia Dei per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]]. Therefore it is now added: [[106:6|and he delivered them out of their distresses|et de necessitatibus eorum eripuit eos]], that is, from evils or vices and dangers, from which they could not be freed by their own strength, they were freed by the grace of God, which enlightened them unto faith: without which no adult who has the use of reason can live without mortal sin, since according to the Apostle, [[Rom 14:23|all that is not of faith is sin|quidquid non est ex fide, peccatum est]]. Yet no one can have either faith or grace except from God. The Gentiles, therefore, as long as they were deprived of the light of faith and lacked grace, sinned unceasingly, or very often.

paras.t: Et deduxit eos in viam rectam : id est, per prædicationem Apostolorum et aliorum doctorum convertit corda eorum ad fidem catholicam, quæ est via ad visionem Dei per speciem. Vel, In viam rectam, id est, in Christum, qui in Evangelio Joannis ait : Ego sum via, veritas, et vita; nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per me. Vel, In viam rectam, id est bonam conversationem seu præceptorum custodiam, sine qua nemo salvatur, juxta illud Matthæi : Si vis ad vitam ingredi, serva mandata. Ut irent in civitatem habitationis, id est in patriam Beatorum : quam debemus quotidie ingredi contemplatione ac voto, quatenus finita hac vita, intremus eam realiter. Unde ad Hebræos Apostolus : Festinemus, inquit, ingredi in illam requiem.
paras.en: [[106:7|And he led them into the right way|Et deduxit eos in viam rectam]]: that is, through the preaching of the Apostles and of other teachers he turned their hearts to the Catholic faith, which is the way to the vision of God by sight [*per speciem*: seeing God openly as he is, as opposed to knowing him by faith]. Or, [[106:7|into the right way|In viam rectam]], that is, into Christ, who says in the Gospel of John: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me|Ego sum via, veritas, et vita; nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per me]]. Or, [[106:7|into the right way|In viam rectam]], that is, into good conduct, or the keeping of the commandments, without which no one is saved, according to that word of Matthew: [[Matt 19:17|if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments|Si vis ad vitam ingredi, serva mandata]]. [[106:7|That they might go to a city of habitation|Ut irent in civitatem habitationis]], that is, to the fatherland of the Blessed: which we ought to enter daily by contemplation and desire, so that when this life is ended we may enter it in reality. Hence the Apostle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 4:11|Let us hasten|Festinemus]], he says, [[Heb 4:11|to enter into that rest|ingredi in illam requiem]].

paras.t: Confitentur Domino misericordiæ ejus: id est, beneficia pietatis divinæ, seu effectus misericordiæ Dei hominibus præstita, inducant eos ad confitendum Domino confessione laudis et gratiarum actionis; et mirabilia ejus filiis hominum, id est hominibus exhibita, seu pro hominibus facta, provocent eos ad confitendum Domino modo jam dicto. Debemus enim omnia bona Deo adscribere, eumque pro cunctis laudare, amare ac venerari. Misericordiæ Dei sunt, quod nos ad fidem vocavit, longanimiter exspectavit, pie convertit, gratis justificavit, proficere fecit, in bono conservavit. Mirabilia ejus sunt, quod propter nos incarnatus est, in mundo conversatus, pro hominibus passus, quod resurrexit, ascendit, Spiritum Sanctum paracletum misit, per se ipsum suosque ministros infinita miracula operari dignatus est.
paras.en: [[106:8|Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him|Confitentur Domino misericordiæ ejus]]: that is, let the benefits of the divine goodness, or the effects of God's mercy bestowed on men, lead them to give glory to the Lord with the confession of praise and thanksgiving [*confiteri*, here "give glory", is literally "to confess"]; [[106:8|and his wonderful works to the children of men|et mirabilia ejus filiis hominum]], that is, shown to men or done for men, let them stir them up to give glory to the Lord in the way just said. For we ought to ascribe all good things to God, and to praise, love and revere him for them all. The mercies of God are these: that he called us to the faith, waited for us with long patience, converted us in his kindness, justified us freely, made us advance, and kept us in good. His wonderful works are these: that for our sake he became incarnate, conversed in the world[[Bar 3:38||]], suffered for men; that he rose again, ascended, sent the Holy Ghost the Paraclete, and deigned to work countless miracles by himself and by his ministers.

paras.t: Quia satiavit animam inanem, et animam esurientem satiavit bonis. Singulare ponit pro plurali. Satiavit enim Christus animas, olim idololatriæ deditas ac per hoc ab omni gratia vacuas, spiritualibus donis, videlicet fide, spe, caritate, donis Spiritus Sancti, gratia multiformi. Sic etiam animas peccatorum, quæ inanes, vanæ ac vacuæ sunt quamdiu vitiis serviunt, satiat Christus dum ad pœnitentiam convertuntur. Et animam esurientem, id est vehementer appetentem Deo conjungi, Deo placere, juste conversari, satiavit bonis optatis, dando ei quotidianum in spiritualibus divitiis incrementum. Habenti enim dabitur, et abundabit. Has animas seu homines tales satiat Christus, nunc inchoative et secundum modum ac statum vitæ præsentis; non tamen satiat eas simpliciter. Sed in patria satiat eas perfecte, plene ac absolute, sicut superius dictum est: Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua. Hinc etiam scriptum est in Matthæo: Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur.
paras.en: [[106:9|For he hath satisfied the empty soul, and hath filled the hungry soul with good things.|Quia satiavit animam inanem, et animam esurientem satiavit bonis]] He puts the singular for the plural. For Christ filled souls once given over to idolatry, and so empty of all grace, with spiritual gifts, namely faith, hope, charity, the gifts of the Holy Ghost, grace in its many forms. So too Christ fills the souls of sinners, which are empty, vain and void as long as they serve vices, when they are converted to penance. And [[106:9|the hungry soul|animam esurientem]], that is, the soul vehemently longing to be joined to God, to please God, to live justly, he [[106:9|hath filled|satiavit]] [[106:9|with good things|bonis]] that it longs for, giving it daily increase in spiritual riches. [[Matt 25:29|For to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall abound|Habenti enim dabitur, et abundabit]]. Such souls, or such men, Christ fills now in a beginning way, according to the manner and state of the present life; yet he does not fill them simply [that is, wholly and without qualification]. But in the fatherland he fills them perfectly, fully and absolutely, as was said above: [[Ps 16:15|I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear|Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua]]. Hence too it is written in Matthew: [[Matt 5:6|Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice: for they shall have their fill.|Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur]]

paras.t: Quantum enim anima esurit, cupit seu vult, tantum recipit a Deo, tam de gratia in præsenti, quam de gloria in futuro, dummodo vere, pure, efficaciter, rationabiliter atque instanter desideret. Deus namque universis infundit secundum quod se præparant, et capaces exsistunt. Præparatio autem seu capacitas ista in voluntate consistit, quoniam desiderium aperit voluntatem ad recipiendum quod amat. Idcirco Deus singulis influit quantum desiderant desiderio puro, efficaci ac stabili. Est autem desiderium purum, quando alieno affectu, scilicet terreno aut carnali amori, non commiscetur; et efficax, dum quidquid valet, pro adeptione boni desiderati exsequitur. Hinc quippe in libro Job inducitur: Si direxerit homo ad Deum cor suum, spiritum illius et flatum ad se trahet. Et apud Jeremiam: Quis est iste qui applicet cor suum, ut appropinquet mihi? ait Dominus. Quod autem animam inanem ac esurientem Deus sic satiet, Isaias fatetur: Deus sempiternus Dominus, etc., dat lasso virtutem, et his qui non sunt, fortitudinem et robur multiplicat.
paras.en: For as much as the soul hungers, desires or wills, so much does it receive from God, both of grace in the present and of glory in the future, provided only that it desires truly, purely, effectually, reasonably and earnestly. For God pours himself into all according as they prepare themselves and are capable. And this preparation or capacity lies in the will, since desire opens the will to receive what it loves. Therefore God flows into each one as much as they desire with a desire that is pure, effectual and steadfast. A desire is pure when it is not mingled with an alien affection, namely with earthly or carnal love; and effectual when it does whatever it can to obtain the good desired. Hence indeed it is said in the book of Job: [[Job 34:14|If he turn his heart to him, he shall draw his spirit and breath unto himself.|Si direxerit homo ad Deum cor suum, spiritum illius et flatum ad se trahet]] [Denis reads: If a man turn his heart to God]. And in Jeremias: [[Jer 30:21|Who is this that setteth his heart to approach to me, saith the Lord?|Quis est iste qui applicet cor suum, ut appropinquet mihi? ait Dominus]] And that God so fills the empty and hungry soul, Isaias declares: [[Is 40:28|The Lord is the everlasting God|Deus sempiternus Dominus]], etc. [[Is 40:29|It is he that giveth strength to the weary, and increaseth force and might to them that are not.|dat lasso virtutem, et his qui non sunt, fortitudinem et robur multiplicat]]

paras.t: Secundum Aurelium Augustinum, in psalmo præsenti tanguntur quatuor tentationes seu quatuor mala, a quibus nos eripit Christus. Primum malum seu prima tentatio est, deviatio in hoc mundo a Deo, spiritualisque fames et mentis inopia: a quibus per Christum eripimur, dum in rectam viam perveniendi ad Deum deducimur et spiritualiter satiamur. Secundum malum seu secunda tentatio est, difficultas superandi concupiscentias, propter consuetudinem malam et impetum passionum. Sic laborantes adjuvat Christus. Tertia est tentatio tædii, torporis seu acediæ, dum homo spiritualem laborem fastidit, et opera bona aggredi differt et horret. Hunc Christus per gratiam excitat et inflammat. Quarta est difficultas in bene agendo propter varia impedimenta occurrentia, quæ sunt velut procellæ ac tempestates atque discrimina hujus maris magni, id est mundi istius, in quo, famulo Christi mille impedimenta inquietudinesque occurrunt, retrahentes a Deo. Ab hoc malo salvat nos Christus, mitigando per gratiam difficul[…]
paras.en: According to Aurelius Augustine, four temptations, or four evils, from which Christ rescues us are touched on in the present psalm. The first evil or first temptation is straying from God in this world, with spiritual hunger and poverty of mind: from these we are rescued through Christ when we are led into the right way of reaching God and are filled spiritually. The second evil or second temptation is the difficulty of overcoming concupiscences, because of evil habit and the onrush of the passions. Those who so labour Christ helps. The third is the temptation of weariness, torpor or acedia [that is, spiritual sloth: a listless distaste for the things of God], when a man loathes spiritual labour, and puts off and shrinks from undertaking good works. Such a man Christ rouses and kindles by grace. The fourth is the difficulty of doing good because of the various hindrances that arise, which are like the squalls and storms and perils of this great sea, that is, of this world, in which a thousand hindrances and disquiets meet the servant of Christ, drawing him back from God. From this evil Christ saves us, easing by grace the difficul[…]

paras.t: […] est, a fidelibus abstulit, ita quod non defendunt se ipsos, sed culpam suam humiliter recognoscunt. Per hæc namque metalla designantur peccata durissima, a quorum vinculis anima difficillime solvitur. Unde in vitiis habituato dicitur per Isaiam : Scivi quia durus es tu, et nervus ferreus cervix tua, et frons tua ærea, dicit Dominus. Sicut autem portæ vecte clauduntur, ne qui intus est, egrediatur ; sic per excusationem peccati, anima claudit os suum a confessione salubri, et peccata intus latentia non aperiuntur neque sanantur.
paras.en: […] he has taken away from the faithful, so that they do not defend themselves, but humbly acknowledge their fault. For by these metals are signified the hardest sins, from whose bonds the soul is loosed with the greatest difficulty. Hence it is said through Isaias to one hardened in vices: [[Is 48:4|I knew that thou art stubborn, and thy neck is as an iron sinew, and thy forehead as brass|Scivi quia durus es tu, et nervus ferreus cervix tua, et frons tua ærea]], saith the Lord. And as gates are shut with a bar, so that he who is within may not go out, so by excusing its sin the soul shuts its mouth against saving confession, and the sins lying hidden within are neither opened nor healed.

paras.t: Suscepit eos ad pœnitentiam salutarem ac pristinam amicitiam de via iniquitatis eorum, id est de via ac vita eorum iniqua, secundum quod per Jeremiam repromittit : Revertere ad me, et non avertam faciem meam. Propter injustitias enim suas humiliati sunt, id est, propter culpas suas puniti sunt. Vel, Propter injustitias suas, id est ex consideratione peccatorum suorum, humiliati sunt coram te, confitentes se omni pœna condignos propter suos excessus.
paras.en: [[106:17|He took them|Suscepit eos]] [*suscepit*: took up, received] to saving penance and their former friendship, [[106:17|out of the way of their iniquity|de via iniquitatis eorum]], that is, from their wicked way and life, as he promises through Jeremias: [[Jer 3:12|Return|Revertere]] to me, [[Jer 3:12|and I will not turn away my face|et non avertam faciem meam]]. [[106:17|For they were brought low for their injustices|Propter injustitias enim suas humiliati sunt]], that is, they were punished for their faults. Or, [[106:17|for their injustices|Propter injustitias suas]], that is, from the consideration of their sins, [[106:17|they were brought low|humiliati sunt]] before thee, confessing themselves worthy of every punishment for their excesses.

paras.t: Deinde describitur tertium malum, quod est fastidium boni. Omnem escam spiritualem, id est omnem bonam operationem, quæ mentem in vita gratiæ conservat, alit, ac perficit, abominata est anima eorum ex tentatione acediæ, ex defectu fervoris in Deo, et torporis ignavia, et appropinquaverunt usque ad portas mortis, id est, pene consenserunt huic fastidio : sicque mortalibus peccatis, quæ sunt portæ mortis atque inferni, appropinquaverunt. Si enim ex tali abominatione operis boni, neglexissent mandata Dei, peccassent mortaliter, et ingressi fuissent portas mortis spiritualis, æternalis ac infernalis ; sed divinitus præservati sunt, ne eas intrarent, nam, Et clamaverunt ad Dominum pro infusione sanctæ devotionis, quum tribularentur, id est, cordialiter affligerentur ex tali torpore ; et de necessitatibus eorum, id est prædictis angustiis, liberavit eos, fortitudinem, caritatisque fervorem excitando in ipsis.
paras.en: Next the third evil is described, which is loathing of good. [[106:18|All manner of meat|Omnem escam]] that is spiritual, that is, every good work, which preserves, nourishes and perfects the mind in the life of grace, [[106:18|their soul abhorred|abominata est anima eorum]] through the temptation of acedia, through want of fervour toward God and the sluggishness of torpor; [[106:18|and they drew nigh even to the gates of death|et appropinquaverunt usque ad portas mortis]], that is, they all but consented to this loathing, and so drew near to mortal sins, which are the gates of death and of hell. For if from such abhorrence of good works they had neglected the commandments of God, they would have sinned mortally, and would have entered the gates of death, spiritual, eternal and infernal; but they were preserved by God from entering them; for: [[106:19|And they cried to the Lord|Et clamaverunt ad Dominum]] for the infusion of holy devotion, [[106:19|in their affliction|quum tribularentur]], that is, when they were afflicted at heart by such torpor; [[106:19|and he delivered them|liberavit eos]] [[106:19|out of their distresses|et de necessitatibus eorum]], that is, out of the straits just spoken of, stirring up in them strength and the fervour of charity.

paras.t: Misit Deus Pater verbum suum, id est Filium suum unigenitum : de quo scriptum est, In principio erat Verbum. Hunc misit per incarnationem in mundum, juxta illud : Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis. Et sanavit eos a vulneribus animæ, et eripuit eos de interitionibus eorum, id est a peccatis quibus moritur anima, prout in Ezechiele asseritur : Anima quæ peccaverit, ipsa morietur. Hinc enim in prima Joannis Canonica ait Scriptura : Pater misit Filium suum salvatorem mundi. Vel, Deus misit verbum suum, id est effectum Verbi sui, videlicet gratiam. Vel, verbum, id est prædicationem verbi cœlestis, qua anima infirma sanatur, quemadmodum in libro Sapientiæ scriptum est : Sermo tuus, Domine, sanat omnia.
paras.en: [[106:20|He sent|Misit]], namely God the Father, [[106:20|his word|verbum suum]], that is, his only-begotten Son, of whom it is written: [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word|In principio erat Verbum]]. Him he sent into the world by the incarnation, according to that word: [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us|Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis]]. [[106:20|And healed them|Et sanavit eos]] of the wounds of the soul, [[106:20|and delivered them from their destructions|et eripuit eos de interitionibus eorum]], that is, from the sins by which the soul dies, as is declared in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 18:20|The soul that sinneth, the same shall die|Anima quæ peccaverit, ipsa morietur]]. For hence Scripture says in the first canonical Epistle of John: [[1 John 4:14|the Father hath sent his Son to be the Saviour of the world|Pater misit Filium suum salvatorem mundi]]. Or, God [[106:20|sent his word|misit verbum suum]], that is, the effect of his Word, namely grace. Or, [[106:20|word|verbum]], that is, the preaching of the heavenly word, by which the sick soul is healed, as is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 16:12|thy word, O Lord, which healeth all things|Sermo tuus, Domine, sanat omnia]].

paras.t: Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus, etc., sicut jam dictum est.
paras.en: [[106:21|Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him|Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus]], etc., as has already been said.

paras.t: Et sacrificent filii hominum sacrificium laudis Domino : qui bonorum nostrorum non eget, sed humili laude et spirituali sacrificio delectatur magis, quam omnibus holocaustis veteris legis. Unde superius dixit : Sacrificium laudis honorificabit me. Et annuntient, id est, aliis prædicent, vel apud se recitent, opera ejus, id est mirabilia Christi, beneficia scilicet et misericordias ejus, in exsultatione, id est cum spirituali lætitia ex divina caritate manante. Qui enim diligit Deum, in annuntiatione operum ejus corde tenus gloriatur, sicut superius dictum est : Exsultabunt labia mea quum cantavero tibi.
paras.en: [[106:22|And let them sacrifice|Et sacrificent]], the children of men, [[106:22|the sacrifice of praise|sacrificium laudis]] to the Lord: who has no need of our goods[[Ps 15:2||]], but is delighted by humble praise and spiritual sacrifice more than by all the holocausts of the old law. Hence he said above: [[Ps 49:23|The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me|Sacrificium laudis honorificabit me]]. [[106:22|And declare|Et annuntient]], that is, let them preach to others, or recount within themselves, [[106:22|his works|opera ejus]], that is, the wonderful works of Christ, namely his benefits and mercies, [[106:22|with joy|in exsultatione]], that is, with spiritual gladness flowing from divine charity. For he who loves God glories from his heart in declaring his works, as was said above: [[Ps 70:23|My lips shall greatly rejoice, when I shall sing to thee|Exsultabunt labia mea quum cantavero tibi]].

paras.t: Qui descendunt mare in navibus, id est, qui ab exercitiis contemplativæ vitæ se deponunt ad opera vitæ activæ, consulendo saluti proximorum, et mare, id est mundum, intrantes, seu homines accedentes, facientes operationem, id est piam exhortationem, diligentem inquisitionem, justam correctionem, in aquis multis, id est in populis plurimis. Aquæ enim multæ, populi multi sunt, secundum Joannem in Apocalypsi. Boni namque pastores et aliorum cultores, multas adhibent operationes subjectis, quatenus eos purgent, illuminent, atque perficiant.
paras.en: [[106:23|They that go down to the sea in ships|Qui descendunt mare in navibus]], that is, those who come down from the exercises of the contemplative life to the works of the active life, providing for the salvation of their neighbours, and, entering the sea, that is, the world, or approaching men, are [[106:23|doing business|facientes operationem]] [*facientes operationem*, literally "doing work"], that is, devout exhortation, careful inquiry, just correction, [[106:23|in the great waters|in aquis multis]] [literally "in many waters"], that is, among very many peoples. For many waters are many peoples, according to John in the Apocalypse[[Apoc 17:1||]][[Apoc 17:15||]]. For good pastors, and those who cultivate others, apply many works to their subjects, that they may purge, enlighten and perfect them.

paras.t: Ipsi prælati et contemplativi sic descendentes, viderunt oculo fidei opera Domini, id est facta Christi in Evangelio clare digesta, seu omnia opera Creatoris in sacris Scripturis expressa; et mirabilia ejus spiritualiter viderunt in profundo, id est in alto intellectu, per quem historialia mystice intellexerunt: sicut quod connubium Salomonis cum filia Pharaonis, significavit desponsationem Ecclesiæ ex gentilibus congregatæ, cum Christo; et venditio Joseph, Christi venditionem; Jonæ quoque in ventre ceti triduana permansio, Christi sepulturam præfiguravit. Vel, Viderunt mirabilia Dei in profundo, id est in secreto cordis humani: quod dicitur profundum, quia est inscrutabile, juxta illud in Jeremia, Pravum est cor hominis et inscrutabile. Et in hoc profundo vident pastores mirabilia Dei, quando ad exhortationem eorum, corda dura in lacrimas resolvuntur, animæ spiritualiter mortuæ ad vitam gratiæ suscitantur, peccatores indurati ad pœnitentiam convertuntur; incontinentes, et qui interdum vix modico tempore poterant continere, tota vita sua continentiam servant; superbi humiles fiunt, iracundi mitescunt. Hæc sunt mirabilia Dei, quia secundum Augustinum, major est impii justificatio quam mundi creatio.
paras.en: [[106:24|These|Ipsi]], the prelates and contemplatives thus going down, [[106:24|have seen|viderunt]] with the eye of faith [[106:24|the works of the Lord|opera Domini]], that is, the deeds of Christ clearly set out in the Gospel, or all the works of the Creator expressed in the sacred Scriptures; [[106:24|and his wonders|et mirabilia ejus]] they have spiritually seen [[106:24|in the deep|in profundo]], that is, in the deep understanding by which they have understood the histories mystically: as that the marriage of Solomon with the daughter of Pharao signified the espousal with Christ of the Church gathered from the Gentiles; and the selling of Joseph, the selling of Christ; and the three days' stay of Jonas in the belly of the whale prefigured the burial of Christ. Or: they [[106:24|have seen|Viderunt]] the wonders of God [[106:24|in the deep|in profundo]], that is, in the secret of the human heart, which is called the deep because it is unsearchable, according to that word in Jeremias: [[Jer 17:9|The heart is perverse above all things, and unsearchable|Pravum est cor hominis et inscrutabile]] [Denis has *cor hominis*, "the heart of man", where the Vulgate has *cor omnium*]. And in this deep pastors see the wonders of God when, at their exhortation, hard hearts melt into tears, souls spiritually dead are raised to the life of grace, hardened sinners are converted to penance; the incontinent, and those who at times could scarcely be continent for a little while, keep continence all their life; the proud become humble, the angry grow meek. These are the wonders of God, for, according to Augustine, the justification of the ungodly is a greater thing than the creation of the world.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur periculum seu tentatio tempestatis. Dixit Deus, cujus dicere est facere, et stetit, id est, stabilis fuit atque invaluit, spiritus procellæ, id est persecutio tyrannica in fideles, seu tentatio gravis. Hanc procellam Deus dixit, id est, permisit esse, ad majus meritum electorum suorum. Et exaltati, id est firmati et aucti, sunt fluctus ejus, id est motus persecutionum istarum: quoniam dum Deus permittit, augentur tribulationes justorum, et invalescit crudelitas perversorum.
paras.en: Next is described the danger, or temptation, of the storm. [[106:25|He said the word|Dixit]], that is, God, whose saying is doing, [[106:25|and there arose|et stetit]] [*stetit*, literally "stood"], that is, became settled and grew strong, [[106:25|a storm of wind|spiritus procellæ]], that is, tyrannical persecution of the faithful, or grievous temptation. This storm God *said*, that is, permitted to be, for the greater merit of his elect. And [[106:25|were lifted up|exaltati]], that is, made firm and increased, [[106:25|the waves thereof|sunt fluctus ejus]], that is, the motions of these persecutions: for while God permits it, the tribulations of the just increase and the cruelty of the wicked grows strong.

paras.t: Ascendunt usque ad cælos: id est, persecutores et tentatores eriguntur in altum contra Deum omnipotentem, crudelitasque eorum atque perversitas propter magnitudinem suam penetrat cælos, quoniam provocat Deum ad vehementem vindictam. Unde secundo Paralipomenon filiis Israel dicitur: Crudelitas vestra usque ad cælos pervenit. Et descendunt usque ad abyssos, id est, turpiter et carnaliter vivunt, et tandem deficiunt, et in infernum labuntur. Vel, Descendunt usque ad abyssos, id est, quantum se contra Deum extollunt, tantum humiliantur a Deo ac pereunt, juxta illud Job: Si ascenderit usque ad cælum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit, quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur. Unde in Isaia dicitur superbo, qui supra astra cœli solium suum exaltare molitus est: Verumtamen in infernum detraheris in profundum laci. Anima eorum in malis tabescebat, id est in propriis peccatis contabuit, aruit et defecit, quemadmodum Jeremias fatetur: Unusquisque in iniquitatibus suis tabescet; et iterum, Omnis qui comederit uvam acerbam, obstupescent dentes ejus. Qui enim alii nocumentum inferre conatur, primo se ipsum interimit, et uniuscujusque malitia in se ipsum redundat. Propter quod in Proverbiorum libro Salomon fassus est: Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur.
paras.en: [[106:26|They mount up to the heavens|Ascendunt usque ad cælos]]: that is, persecutors and tempters are lifted up on high against almighty God, and their cruelty and perversity, by reason of its greatness, pierces the heavens, since it provokes God to vehement vengeance. Hence in the second book of Paralipomenon it is said to the children of Israel: [[2 Par 28:9|your cruelty hath reached up to heaven|Crudelitas vestra usque ad cælos pervenit]]. [[106:26|and they go down to the depths|Et descendunt usque ad abyssos]], that is, they live shamefully and carnally, and at last they fail and slip down into hell. Or: [[106:26|they go down to the depths|Descendunt usque ad abyssos]], that is, as much as they exalt themselves against God, so much are they humbled by God and perish, according to that word of Job: [[Job 20:6|If his pride mount up even to heaven, and his head touch the clouds|Si ascenderit usque ad cælum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit]], [[Job 20:7|In the end he shall be destroyed like a dunghill|quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur]]. Hence in Isaias it is said to the proud one, who strove to exalt his throne above the stars of heaven: [[Is 14:15|But yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, into the depth of the pit|Verumtamen in infernum detraheris in profundum laci]]. [[106:26|their soul pined away with evils|Anima eorum in malis tabescebat]], that is, it wasted away in its own sins, withered and failed, as Jeremias declares: Every one shall [[Ezech 4:17|pine away in their iniquities|in iniquitatibus suis tabescet]] [no margin reference; these words are not in Jeremias: *unusquisque in iniquitate sua* begins Jer 31:30 (quoted next), and the rest is closest to Ezech 4:17, cf. Lev 26:39]; and again: [[Jer 31:30|every man that shall eat the sour grape, his teeth shall be set on edge|Omnis qui comederit uvam acerbam, obstupescent dentes ejus]]. For he who tries to do harm to another first slays himself, and each man's malice recoils upon himself. Wherefore in the book of Proverbs Solomon declared: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur]].

paras.t: Vel: Ascendunt usque ad cælos: id est, fideles tam dire afflicti, orando et contemplando cœlos ascendunt, usque ad Christum, quatenus ex consideratione præmiorum cœlestium facilius omnia patiantur. Nam consideratio præmii minuit vim flagelli. Et descendunt usque ad abyssos: id est, post tantam contemplationem ex gratia acquisitam, iterum ex humana fragilitate cadunt ad cogitationes carnales, ad phantasmata inutilia, ad occupationes indignas. Nam et Paulus post raptum passus est stimulum carnis. Hoc autem Deus permittit, ut homo perpendat quid habeat ex se ipso, quid item ex Deo. Vel, Descendunt usque ad abyssos, considerando tormenta inferni: ex quorum consideratione tolerabilia fiunt omnia mundi supplicia. Anima eorum sic afflictorum, in malis, id est in pœnis et culpis, quibus undique circumdantur homines in hac misera vita, in qua justus septies cadit in die, tabescebat, id est, tædio atque tristitia affecta et languens effecta est, sicut in Threnis ait Jeremias : Propterea in dolore mœstum factum est cor nostrum : ideo contenebrati sunt oculi nostri.
paras.en: Or: [[106:26|They mount up to the heavens|Ascendunt usque ad cælos]]: that is, the faithful, so cruelly afflicted, mount up to the heavens by praying and contemplating, even to Christ, so that from the consideration of the heavenly rewards they may bear all things more easily. For the consideration of the reward lessens the force of the scourge. [[106:26|and they go down to the depths|Et descendunt usque ad abyssos]]: that is, after so great a contemplation, acquired by grace, they fall again through human frailty to carnal thoughts, to useless imaginings, to unworthy occupations. For Paul too, after his rapture, suffered the sting of the flesh. And God permits this so that man may weigh what he has of himself and what he has of God. Or: they [[106:26|go down to the depths|Descendunt usque ad abyssos]] by considering the torments of hell, from the consideration of which all the punishments of the world become bearable. [[106:26|their soul|Anima eorum]], the soul of those thus afflicted, [[106:26|with evils|in malis]], that is, with the pains and faults by which men are surrounded on every side in this wretched life, in which [[Prov 24:16|a just man shall fall seven times|justus septies cadit]] a day, [[106:26|pined away|tabescebat]], that is, was affected with weariness and sadness and made faint, as Jeremias says in Lamentations: [[Lam 5:17|Therefore is our heart sorrowful, therefore are our eyes become dim|Propterea in dolore mœstum factum est cor nostrum : ideo contenebrati sunt oculi nostri]] [Denis adds *in dolore*, "in sorrow"].

paras.t: Turbati sunt animo et moti sunt a recto judicio rationis sicut ebrius, sequendo impetus passionum, atque irrationabiles motus; et omnis sapientia eorum, quam tempore tranquillitatis videbantur habere, devorata est tempore persecutionis seu tentationis, ita quod actus rationis passioni succubuit, et insipientia eorum sapientiæ actum impedivit. Multi namque tempore pacis, quietis, prosperitatis et jucunditatis, virtuosi ac sapientes apparent; sed dum adversitas, inquietudo, et tribulatio eis supervenit, superantur, ratio cadit, sensualitas dominatur, virtus succumbit, et vitia prævalent. Unde et Christus de quibusdam ait in Evangelio : Hi radices non habent, quia ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis recedunt. Et rursus alio in loco ait de eo, qui non facit quod scit esse agendum, sed ex passione aut persecutione cadit a medio rationis : Similis erit viro stulto, qui ædificavit domum suam supra arenam ; et descendit pluvia, et venerunt flumina, et flaverunt venti, et irruerunt in domum illam, et cecidit ; fuitque ruina ejus magna.
paras.en: [[106:27|They were troubled|Turbati sunt]] in mind [[106:27|and reeled|et moti sunt]] [*moti sunt*, literally "were moved"] from the right judgement of reason [[106:27|like a drunken man|sicut ebrius]], following the impulses of the passions and irrational motions; [[106:27|and all their wisdom|et omnis sapientia eorum]], which they seemed to have in time of calm, [[106:27|was swallowed up|devorata est]] in time of persecution or temptation, so that the act of reason gave way to passion and their folly hindered the act of wisdom. For many appear virtuous and wise in time of peace, quiet, prosperity and pleasantness; but when adversity, disquiet and tribulation come upon them, they are overcome: reason falls, sensuality rules, virtue gives way and vices prevail. Hence Christ too says of some in the Gospel: [[Luke 8:13|these have no roots: for they believe for a while and in time of temptation they fall away|Hi radices non habent, quia ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis recedunt]]. And again, in another place, he says of him who does not do what he knows ought to be done, but falls from the mean of reason through passion or persecution: He [[Matt 7:26|shall be like a foolish man that built his house upon the sand|Similis erit viro stulto, qui ædificavit domum suam supra arenam]]; [[Matt 7:27|And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell, and great was the fall thereof|et descendit pluvia, et venerunt flumina, et flaverunt venti, et irruerunt in domum illam, et cecidit ; fuitque ruina ejus magna]].

paras.t: Hæc autem præcipue jam dicuntur de rectoribus aliorum, qui propter varias causas atque negotia subditorumque imperfectionem, cadere solent a fortitudine mentis et recto judicio rationis, iræ et impatientiæ motum admittentes. Talibus ergo præsertim, imo omnibus nobis orandum est ut Deus cor nostrum quotidie in ipso confirmet, ne in adversis, atque turbulentiis aliorum frangatur : quia ut ait Apostolus ad Hebræos, Optimum est gratia stabiliri cor. Inhonestum namque ac turpe est viro erudito, et maxime aliorum rectori, in adversis deficere. Propter quod in libro Job dicitur ei, qui videbatur propter adversa turbatus : Ubi est timor tuus, fortitudo tua, et patientia tua, et perfectio viarum tuarum ?
paras.en: Now these things are said here especially of the rulers of others, who, because of various causes and affairs and the imperfection of their subjects, are apt to fall from fortitude of mind and from the right judgement of reason, admitting the motion of anger and impatience. Such men above all, then, nay all of us, must pray that God may daily strengthen our heart in himself, lest it be broken in adversities and in the disturbances caused by others: because, as the Apostle says to the Hebrews, [[Heb 13:9|it is best that the heart be established with grace|Optimum est gratia stabiliri cor]]. For it is unbecoming and shameful for a learned man, and above all for a ruler of others, to fail in adversity. Wherefore in the book of Job it is said to him who seemed troubled by adversities: [[Job 4:6|Where is thy fear, thy fortitude, thy patience, and the perfection of thy ways?|Ubi est timor tuus, fortitudo tua, et patientia tua, et perfectio viarum tuarum ?]] [the margin gives Job vi; the words are those of Eliphaz, Job 4:6]

paras.t: Et clamaverunt ad Dominum : qui ut propheta Nahum testatur, Increpat mare et exsiccat illud ; quum tribularentur tantis adversis, dicentes cum Petro, Domine, salva nos, perimus. Nec frustra : nam et de necessitatibus eorum, id est prædictis periculis, eduxit eos : non enim sinit nos tentari supra id quod possumus.
paras.en: [[106:28|And they cried to the Lord|Et clamaverunt ad Dominum]], who, as the prophet Nahum testifies, [[Nah 1:4|rebuketh the sea and drieth it up|Increpat mare et exsiccat illud]], [[106:28|in their affliction|quum tribularentur]] [literally "when they were afflicted"] by such great adversities, saying with Peter: [[Matt 8:25|Lord, save us, we perish|Domine, salva nos, perimus]]. And not in vain: for [[106:28|out of their distresses|et de necessitatibus eorum]], that is, out of the perils described, [[106:28|he brought them|eduxit eos]]; for he does not [[1 Cor 10:13|suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able|sinit nos tentari supra id quod possumus]] [Denis has *nos*, "us"].

paras.t: Et statuit procellam ejus, id est, strepitum persecutionis, asperitatem adversitatis, et motum tentationis mutavit in auram, id est ventum leniter flantem : ita quod adversitatem mitigavit, et tranquillitatis serenitatem menti infudit. Non tamen tentationem penitus abstulit : quia, ut ait Augustinus, Persevera usque in finem, quoniam tentatio perseverat usque in finem. Sic ergo petamus unam auferri, ut aliam præstolemur. Et siluerunt fluctus ejus, id est, impugnationes tentationum cessaverunt ad tempus.
paras.en: [[106:29|And he turned the storm|Et statuit procellam ejus]], that is, he changed the din of persecution, the harshness of adversity and the motion of temptation [[106:29|into a breeze|in auram]], that is, a gently blowing wind: so that he softened the adversity and poured the serenity of calm into the mind. Yet he did not take temptation away altogether: because, as Augustine says, Persevere to the end, for temptation perseveres to the end. Let us therefore ask that one be taken away, so as to look out for another. [[106:29|and its waves were still|Et siluerunt fluctus ejus]], that is, the assaults of temptations ceased for a time.

paras.t: Et lætati sunt in Domino homines exonerati a jugo tentationum. Unde in libro Tobiæ scriptum est : Non delectaris, Domine, in perditionibus nostris, quia post tempestatem tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis. Et lætati sunt, gloriantes in Domino de sua liberatione, quia siluerunt fluctus persecutionum istarum. Hinc namque Tobias sanatus ait : Benedico te, Domine, quoniam tu castigasti me, et tu sanasti me. Apostolus quoque : Benedictus Deus, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra. Et deduxit eos in portum voluntatis eorum, id est in pacem omnibus mortalibus desideratam, in perfectionem optatam, ad conscientiæ securitatem, ad tranquillitatem dulcissimam, et post hujus vitæ decursum ad patriam electorum. Qui enim adversa fortiter tolerat, et in tristibus causis Christo fidelis ac stabilis permanet, ad hunc portum pacis ac consolationis perduci meretur. Propter quod dicit Salvator discipulis : Amen, amen dico vobis, quia plorabitis et flebitis vos, mundus autem gaudebit ; sed tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium. Et Apostolus ad Corinthios ait : Scitote, quoniam sicut socii passionum estis, sic eritis et consolationis. Itemque : Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra.
paras.en: [[106:30|And they rejoiced|Et lætati sunt]] in the Lord, men unburdened of the yoke of temptations. Hence it is written in the book of Tobias: [[Tob 3:22|thou art not delighted|Non delectaris]], O Lord, [[Tob 3:22|in our being lost, because after a storm thou makest a calm, and after tears and weeping thou pourest in joyfulness|in perditionibus nostris, quia post tempestatem tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis]]. [[106:30|And they rejoiced|Et lætati sunt]], glorying in the Lord over their deliverance, [[106:30|because they were still|quia siluerunt]], namely the waves of these persecutions.
