For hence Tobias, when he was healed, says: [[Tob 11:17|I bless thee, O Lord|Benedico te, Domine]], [[Tob 11:17|because thou hast chastised me, and thou hast saved me|quoniam tu castigasti me, et tu sanasti me]]. And the Apostle: [[2 Cor 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], [[2 Cor 1:4|who comforteth us in all our tribulation|qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra]] [the margin gives 2 Cor. i, 3; these last words are v. 4]. [[106:30|and he brought them to the haven which they wished for|Et deduxit eos in portum voluntatis eorum]], that is, into the peace desired by all mortals, into the perfection longed for, to security of conscience, to most sweet tranquillity, and, after the course of this life, to the fatherland of the elect. For he who bravely bears adversities, and in sad circumstances remains faithful and steadfast to Christ, deserves to be brought to this haven of peace and consolation. Wherefore the Saviour says to the disciples: [[John 16:20|Amen, amen, I say to you, that you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice|Amen, amen dico vobis, quia plorabitis et flebitis vos, mundus autem gaudebit]]; [[John 16:20|but your sorrow shall be turned into joy|sed tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium]]. And the Apostle says to the Corinthians: Know [[2 Cor 1:7|that as you are partakers of the sufferings, so shall you be also of the consolation|quoniam sicut socii passionum estis, sic eritis et consolationis]]. And again: [[2 Cor 1:5|as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]].

paras.t: Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus, etc., eo quod post tantam persecutionem, tantam pacem largitus sit.
paras.en: [[106:31|Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him|Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus]], etc., because after so great a persecution he has bestowed so great a peace.

paras.t: Et exaltent eum, id est, magnifice verbo et opere eum honorent, in ecclesia plebis, id est in congregatione fidelium ; et in cathedra seniorum, id est in loco ac sede superiorum, laudent eum, qui sedent in cathedra tali. Vult ergo Propheta, ut omnes Deum unanimiter laudent, magni et parvi, superiores et inferiores, quemadmodum in Apocalypsi dicitur : Laudem dicite Deo nostro, omnes servi ejus, et qui timetis eum, pusilli et magni. Et Apostolus ad Romanos : Deus patientiæ et solatii det vobis id ipsum sapere in alterutrum secundum Jesum Christum, ut unanimes uno ore honorificetis Deum.
paras.en: [[106:32|And let them exalt him|Et exaltent eum]], that is, honour him magnificently in word and deed, [[106:32|in the church of the people|in ecclesia plebis]], that is, in the congregation of the faithful; and [[106:32|in the chair of the ancients|in cathedra seniorum]], that is, in the place and seat of superiors, let them [[106:32|praise him|laudent eum]], those who sit in such a chair. The Prophet wills, then, that all should praise God with one accord, great and small, superiors and inferiors, as it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:5|Give praise to our God, all ye his servants: and you that fear him, little and great|Laudem dicite Deo nostro, omnes servi ejus, et qui timetis eum, pusilli et magni]]. And the Apostle to the Romans: [[Rom 15:5|the God of patience and of comfort grant you to be of one mind, one towards another, according to Jesus Christ|Deus patientiæ et solatii det vobis id ipsum sapere in alterutrum secundum Jesum Christum]], [[Rom 15:6|That with one mind and with one mouth you may glorify God|ut unanimes uno ore honorificetis Deum]].

paras.t: Posuit flumina in desertum, id est, Deus fluenta gratiæ atque doctrinæ in corda gentilium derivavit. Gentilitas namque desertum vocatur, juxta illud Isaiæ : Lætabitur deserta et invia, et exsultabit solitudo. Demum, dum Deus mentem nostram cœlitus gratia sua perfundit, flumina ponit in desertum. Et exitus aquarum, id est Synagogam Judæorum, quæ aliis pluviam prædicationis influere consuevit, posuit in sitim, quoniam propter incredulitatem ipsorum privati sunt vera sapientia Christi. Et huic simile est quod Christus testatur : In judicium ego in hunc mundum veni, ut qui non vident, videant ; et qui vident, cæci fiant. In Christi namque adventu cœpit Judæa excæcari, quæ ante videbat ; gentilitas quoque illuminari, quæ ante caligabat. Nam quem Judæi futurum credebant, præsentem non noverant ; gentiles vero per prædicationem Christi et Apostolorum radio sapientiæ illustrati sunt. Ideoque in Isaia habetur : Quibus non est narratum de eo, viderunt ; et qui non audierunt, contemplati sunt.
paras.en: [[106:33|He hath turned rivers into a wilderness|Posuit flumina in desertum]] [the Latin can also mean "he hath put rivers into the wilderness", and so Denis takes it here], that is, God channelled streams of grace and doctrine into the hearts of the Gentiles. For the Gentile world is called a wilderness, according to that word of Isaias: [[Is 35:1|The land that was desolate and impassable shall be glad, and the wilderness shall rejoice|Lætabitur deserta et invia, et exsultabit solitudo]]. Again, when God floods our mind with his grace from heaven, he puts rivers into the wilderness. [[106:33|and the sources of waters|Et exitus aquarum]] [*exitus aquarum*, literally "the outflowings of waters"], that is, the Synagogue of the Jews, which used to pour the rain of preaching upon others, he turned [[106:33|into dry ground|in sitim]] [literally "into thirst"], because through their unbelief they were deprived of the true wisdom of Christ. And like this is what Christ testifies: [[John 9:39|For judgment I am come into this world: that they who see not may see; and they who see may become blind|In judicium ego in hunc mundum veni, ut qui non vident, videant ; et qui vident, cæci fiant]]. For at the coming of Christ, Judea, which before saw, began to be blinded, and the Gentile world, which before was in darkness, to be enlightened. For him whom the Jews believed would come, they did not know when he was present; but the Gentiles, through the preaching of Christ and the Apostles, were enlightened by the ray of wisdom. And therefore it is found in Isaias: [[Is 52:15|they to whom it was not told of him, have seen: and they that heard not, have beheld|Quibus non est narratum de eo, viderunt ; et qui non audierunt, contemplati sunt]] [the margin gives Is. liii, 15; the words are Is 52:15].

paras.t: Posuit etiam Deus terram fructiferam in salsuginem : id est, Judæam seu Synagogam olim doctrina et vita fecundam, fecit siccam et sterilem, abstrahendo a populo Judæorum gratiæ infusionem, quemadmodum in Osee vaticinio inducitur : Radix eorum exsiccata est, fructum nequaquam facient. Hoc autem fecit a malitia inhabitantium in ea, id est propter peccata populi hujus, secundum quod rursus Osee testatur : Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus. Et per Jeremiam Dominus ait : Computrescere faciam superbiam populi hujus pessimi, qui nolunt audire verba mea, et ambulant in pravitate cordis sui.
paras.en: God also turned [[106:34|A fruitful land into barrenness|terram fructiferam in salsuginem]] [*salsugo*, literally "saltness": salt, barren ground]: that is, Judea or the Synagogue, once fruitful in doctrine and life, he made dry and barren, withdrawing from the Jewish people the infusion of grace, as is set forth in the prophecy of Osee: [[Osee 9:16|their root is dried up, they shall yield no fruit|Radix eorum exsiccata est, fructum nequaquam facient]]. And this he did [[106:34|for the wickedness of them that dwell therein|a malitia inhabitantium in ea]], that is, for the sins of this people, as Osee again testifies: [[Osee 9:17|My God will cast them away, because they hearkened not to him|Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus]]. And by Jeremias the Lord says: I will make the pride of this most wicked people to rot[[Jer 13:9||]], [[Jer 13:10|that will not hear my words, and that walk in the perverseness of their heart|qui nolunt audire verba mea, et ambulant in pravitate cordis sui]].

paras.t: Posuit desertum, id est gentilitatem, in stagna aquarum, id est in stabilem exuberantiam spiritualium gratiarum atque cælestium doctrinarum : nam ubi abundavit iniquitas, superabundavit et gratia ; et terram sine aqua, id est gentes quondam sine divina illuminatione et gratia exsistentes, posuit in exitus aquarum, id est, tam copiosam gratiam eis per prædicationem Apostolorum infudit, quod etiam ipsi alios docere atque convertere potuerunt. Unde ad Ephesios Apostolus : Revelatum est, inquit, sanctis Apostolis et Prophetis in spiritu, esse gentes coheredes et concorporales promissionis Dei in Christo Jesu.
paras.en: [[106:35|He hath turned a wilderness|Posuit desertum]], that is, the Gentile world, [[106:35|into pools of waters|in stagna aquarum]] [*stagna*, standing waters, hence "lasting"], that is, into a lasting abundance of spiritual graces and heavenly doctrines: for [[Rom 5:20|where sin abounded, grace did more abound|ubi abundavit iniquitas, superabundavit et gratia]]; [[106:35|and a dry land|et terram sine aqua]], that is, the Gentiles, who were once without divine enlightenment and grace, he turned [[106:35|into water springs|in exitus aquarum]] [literally "into outflowings of waters"], that is, he poured into them so plentiful a grace through the preaching of the Apostles that they themselves too were able to teach and convert others. Hence the Apostle to the Ephesians: It was [[Eph 3:5|revealed|Revelatum est]], he says, [[Eph 3:5|to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit|sanctis Apostolis et Prophetis in spiritu]], [[Eph 3:6|That the Gentiles should be fellow heirs and of the same body|esse gentes coheredes et concorporales]] of the promise of God [[Eph 3:6|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]].

paras.t: Et collocavit Deus illic, id est in prædicta affluentia gratiæ atque doctrinæ cælestis, esurientes justitiam, qui avide receperunt fidem catholicam, et verbi cœlestis prædicationem, quemadmodum in Actibus Apostolorum de Thessalonicensibus scriptum est : Nobiliores ex eis cum omni aviditate susceperunt verbum Domini, quotidie scrutantes Scripturas. Et constituerunt civitatem habitationis, id est Ecclesiam militantem : quæ est civitas Dei et domus Christi, ex fidelibus collecta atque constructa.
paras.en: And God [[106:36|hath placed there|collocavit Deus illic]], that is, in the said abundance of grace and of heavenly doctrine, [[106:36|the hungry|esurientes]] for justice, who eagerly received the Catholic faith and the preaching of the heavenly word, as it is written in the Acts of the Apostles of the Thessalonians: The [[Acts 17:11|more noble|Nobiliores]] of them [[Acts 17:11|received the word|susceperunt verbum]] of the Lord [[Acts 17:11|with all eagerness|cum omni aviditate]], [[Acts 17:11|daily searching the scriptures|quotidie scrutantes Scripturas]] [in Acts these are the Jews of Berea, "more noble than those in Thessalonica"]. [[106:36|and they made a city for their habitation|Et constituerunt civitatem habitationis]], that is, the Church militant, which is the city of God and the house of Christ, gathered and built of the faithful.

paras.t: Et ipsi Apostoli, ac successores et imitatores eorum, seminaverunt agros, id est, homines in mundo morantes fecundaverunt et impleverunt verbo Dei, mittendo in corda ipsorum Evangelium Salvatoris. Ut enim apud Matthæum Christus asseruit, Semen est verbum Dei, ager vero est mundus. Apostoli autem hoc semine mundum impleverunt, quemadmodum in Isaia dictum est : Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebit faciem orbis semine. Hujus seminis fructum non protulerunt Judæi, sed gentes : et ideo Christus apud Matthæum eis locutus est, Auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, et dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus. Et plantaverunt vineas, id est, Ecclesias particulares fundaverunt in Christo. Nam Petrus plantavit vineam Christi in Italia, Joannes in Asia, Thomas in India. Quod autem Ecclesia appelletur vinea, constat ex eo quod in Isaiæ habetur vaticinio : Vinea Domini exercituum, domus Israel est. Et fecerunt fructum nativitatis, id est, multos genuerunt in Christo, quemadmodum ait Apostolus : In Christo Jesu per Evangelium ego vos genui. Tot enim spiritualiter genuerunt, quot ad Christum converterunt.
paras.en: [[106:37|And|Et]] the Apostles themselves, and their successors and imitators, [[106:37|sowed fields|seminaverunt agros]], that is, made fruitful and filled with the word of God the men dwelling in the world, sending the Gospel of the Saviour into their hearts. For, as Christ declared in Matthew, [[Luke 8:11|The seed is the word of God|Semen est verbum Dei]], and [[Matt 13:38|the field is the world|ager vero est mundus]] [as the margin gives, the first words are Luke 8:11, the second Matt 13:38]. And the Apostles filled the world with this seed, as it is said in Isaias: [[Is 27:6|Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed|Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebit faciem orbis semine]]. The fruit of this seed was brought forth not by the Jews but by the Gentiles; and therefore Christ said to them in Matthew: [[Matt 21:43|the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof|Auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, et dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus]]. [[106:37|and planted vineyards|Et plantaverunt vineas]], that is, they founded particular Churches in Christ. For Peter planted the vineyard of Christ in Italy, John in Asia, Thomas in India. And that the Church is called a vineyard is clear from what is found in the prophecy of Isaias: [[Is 5:7|the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel|Vinea Domini exercituum, domus Israel est]]. [[106:37|and they yielded fruit of birth|Et fecerunt fructum nativitatis]], that is, they begot many in Christ, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 4:15|in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you|In Christo Jesu per Evangelium ego vos genui]]. For they begot spiritually as many as they converted to Christ.

paras.t: Et benedixit eis Deus, id est, gratiam copiosam contulit eis, prout in Actibus Apostolorum legitur : Discipuli replebantur gaudio et Spiritu Sancto ; et multiplicati sunt nimis merito et numero, secundum quod Lucas in Actibus dicit : Dominus quotidie augebat qui salvi fierent. Et jumenta eorum, id est idiotas et simplices, jugum Domini super se humiliter bajulantes, non minoravit : nam talium plures a Deo electi sunt, quam nobilium et sapientium. Unde ad Corinthios dicit Apostolus : Videte vocationem vestram, fratres, quia non multi sapientes secundum carnem, non multi potentes, non multi nobiles sunt inter vos; sed quæ stulta et abjecta sunt mundi, elegit Deus, ut confundat sapientes.
paras.en: And God [[106:38|blessed them|benedixit eis]], that is, he bestowed abundant grace on them, as we read in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 13:52|the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Ghost|Discipuli replebantur gaudio et Spiritu Sancto]]; [[106:38|and they were multiplied exceedingly|et multiplicati sunt nimis]] in merit and in number, as Luke says in the Acts: [[Acts 2:47|the Lord increased daily together such as should be saved|Dominus quotidie augebat qui salvi fierent]]. [[106:38|and their cattle|Et jumenta eorum]], that is, the unlettered and simple, humbly carrying the yoke of the Lord upon themselves, [[106:38|he suffered not to decrease|non minoravit]]: for more of such are chosen by God than of the noble and the wise. Hence the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 1:26|see your vocation, brethren, that there are not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble|Videte vocationem vestram, fratres, quia non multi sapientes secundum carnem, non multi potentes, non multi nobiles]] among you; [[1 Cor 1:27|But the foolish things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the wise|sed quæ stulta et abjecta sunt mundi, elegit Deus, ut confundat sapientes]].

paras.t: Et pauci facti sunt fideles in aliquibus locis atque Ecclesiis, per occisionem eorum a tyrannis ac impiis ; et vexati sunt a tribulatione malorum, qui pios affligunt, et dolore eis inflicto a tyrannis et perfidis. Sæpe namque infideles urbes et villas, terras atque Ecclesias Christianorum vastaverunt, destruxerunt, et fideles occiderunt.
paras.en: [[106:39|Then they were brought to be few|Et pauci facti sunt]], the faithful, in some places and Churches, through their being slain by tyrants and the ungodly; [[106:39|and they were afflicted through the trouble of evils|et vexati sunt a tribulatione malorum]] [*malorum*, "of evils", taken here as "of evil men"], who afflict the godly, [[106:39|and sorrow|et dolore]] inflicted on them by tyrants and the faithless. For unbelievers have often laid waste and destroyed the cities and towns, the lands and Churches of Christians, and slain the faithful.

paras.t: Effusa est contentio super principes : id est, majores persequentium Christianos, in contentionem versi sunt, vel contra se invicem, vel contra veritatem fidei christianæ, vel contra principes christianos ; et errare fecit, id est permisit, eos Deus in invio, id est in infidelitate, in qua nulla est via perveniendi ad ultimum finem, et non in via, id est in fide vera, quia nec fidem habuerunt.
paras.en: [[106:40|Contempt was poured forth upon their princes|Effusa est contentio super principes]] [Denis reads *contentio*, "strife", for the Vulgate's *contemptio*, "contempt"]: that is, the chief men among the persecutors of Christians turned to strife, either against one another, or against the truth of the Christian faith, or against Christian princes; [[106:40|and he caused them to wander|et errare fecit]], that is, God permitted them to wander, [[106:40|where there was no passing|in invio]], that is, in unbelief, in which there is no way of reaching the last end, [[106:40|and out of the way|et non in via]] [literally "and not in the way"], that is, not in the true faith, for they did not even have faith.

paras.t: Et adjuvit pauperem de inopia : id est, populum gentilem, spiritualibus divitiis destitutum, sublevavit de ista penuria, ditans eum spiritualibus bonis ; et posuit eos sicut oves familias : id est, sic eos in domo sua (quæ est Ecclesia) collocavit, pavit et custodivit, quemadmodum pastor oves suas custodit, locat et alit. Unde apud Joannem Christus : Alias, inquit, oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere.
paras.en: [[106:41|And he helped the poor out of poverty|Et adjuvit pauperem de inopia]]: that is, the Gentile people, destitute of spiritual riches, he raised up from that penury, enriching it with spiritual goods; [[106:41|and made him families like a flock of sheep|et posuit eos sicut oves familias]]: that is, he so placed them in his house (which is the Church), fed and guarded them, as a shepherd guards, places and nourishes his sheep. Hence Christ in John: [[John 10:16|other sheep|Alias]], he says, [[John 10:16|I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere]].

paras.t: Vel, Adjuvit pauperem, id est humilem, de inopia, exaudiendo precem ipsius. Deus enim superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam. Porro in tantum adjuvat eum de inopia, ut dicat in Evangelio : Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum. Quid ergo hoc paupere ditius, cui promissa est cœlestis regni possessio? Merito igitur ait Tobias : Noli timere, fili mi : pauperem quidem vitam gerimus, sed habebimus multa bona, si timuerimus Deum. Et Apostolus ad Corinthios : Altissima paupertas eorum, abundavit in divitias simplicitatis eorum.
paras.en: Or: [[106:41|he helped the poor|Adjuvit pauperem]], that is, the humble, [[106:41|out of poverty|de inopia]], by hearing his prayer. For [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble|Deus enim superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]]. Indeed, he helps him out of poverty so far as to say in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:3|Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.|Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum]] What, then, is richer than this poor man, to whom the possession of the heavenly kingdom is promised? Rightly, therefore, Tobias says: [[Tob 4:23|Fear not, my son: we lead indeed a poor life, but we shall have many good things if we fear God|Noli timere, fili mi : pauperem quidem vitam gerimus, sed habebimus multa bona, si timuerimus Deum]]. And the Apostle to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 8:2|their very deep poverty hath abounded unto the riches of their simplicity|Altissima paupertas eorum, abundavit in divitias simplicitatis eorum]].

paras.t: Videbunt recti, id est, prædictas misericordias Dei justi intelligent, et lætabuntur in Deo propter beneficia ejus tam copiosa ; et omnis iniquitas, id est omnis iniquus contra veritatem et contra justos impudenter insolenterque garriens, scilicet dæmon, tyrannus, falsus frater, atque hæreticus, oppilabit, id est claudet, os suum, quoniam ab ipsa veritate vincetur, et confundetur, et tandem a Christo reprobabitur atque damnabitur. Propter quod apud Isaiam Dominus ait superbo : Ponam circulum in naribus tuis, et frenum in maxillis tuis. Sæpe etiam impii qui justis detrahunt, dum conversationem eorum sanctam conspiciunt, silent a malo, eosque interdum commendant quibus detrahebant. Hinc enim princeps Apostolorum ait : Hæc est voluntas Dei, ut benefacientes, obmutescere faciatis imprudentium hominum ignorantiam.
paras.en: [[106:42|The just shall see|Videbunt recti]], that is, the just shall understand the aforesaid mercies of God, [[106:42|and shall rejoice|et lætabuntur]] in God for his so plentiful benefits; [[106:42|and all iniquity|et omnis iniquitas]], that is, every wicked one who prates shamelessly and insolently against the truth and against the just, namely the devil, the tyrant, the false brother and the heretic, [[106:42|shall stop|oppilabit]], that is, shall shut, [[106:42|her mouth|os suum]], since he will be overcome by the truth itself and confounded, and at last rejected and condemned by Christ. Wherefore in Isaias the Lord says to the proud one: [[Is 37:29|I will put a ring in thy nose, and a bit between thy lips|Ponam circulum in naribus tuis, et frenum in maxillis tuis]] [Denis has *in maxillis*, "in thy jaws", where the Vulgate has *in labiis*]. Often, too, the ungodly who detract from the just, when they behold their holy manner of life, cease from evil, and sometimes even commend those from whom they used to detract. For hence the prince of the Apostles says: This is [[1 Pet 2:15|the will of God, that by doing well you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men|voluntas Dei, ut benefacientes, obmutescere faciatis imprudentium hominum ignorantiam]].

paras.t: Quis sapiens, et custodiet hæc? id est, qui vere sapiens est, ista memoriter retinebit, spiritualiter sumet, seque inopem reputabit ; et intelliget misericordias Domini? id est, multiplicem gratiam sibi ac ceteris præstitam diligenter pensabit, per experientiamque cognoscet, quam pius et clemens sit Dominus, Pater misericordiarum et Deus totius consolationis. Et huic simile est quod Osee propheta dicit : Quis sapiens, et intelliget ista? intelligens, et sciet hæc? Sed videtur contrarium quod in Evangelio Veritas adstruit : Confiteor, inquiens, tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus. Et respondendum, quod Christus loquitur ibi de sapientibus hujus mundi, quorum sapientiam Deus stultam facit. Nunc autem fit sermo de vere sapientibus, a Spiritu Sancto illuminatis.
paras.en: [[106:43|Who is wise, and will keep these things|Quis sapiens, et custodiet hæc]]? that is, he who is truly wise will keep these things in memory, take them spiritually and count himself needy; [[106:43|and will understand the mercies of the Lord?|et intelliget misericordias Domini]] that is, he will carefully weigh the manifold grace shown to himself and to others, and will know by experience how kind and merciful the Lord is[[2 Par 30:9||]], [[2 Cor 1:3|the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort|Pater misericordiarum et Deus totius consolationis]]. And like this is what the prophet Osee says: [[Osee 14:10|Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know these things?|Quis sapiens, et intelliget ista? intelligens, et sciet hæc]] But what Truth affirms in the Gospel seems contrary: [[Matt 11:25|I confess|Confiteor]], he says, [[Matt 11:25|to thee, O Father, Lord of Heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent|tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus]][[Luke 10:21||]]. And the answer is that Christ is speaking there of the wise of this world, whose wisdom God makes foolish[[1 Cor 1:20||]]. Here, however, the discourse is of the truly wise, enlightened by the Holy Ghost.

106.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI SEXTI.
106.title_en: Literal exposition of the same hundred and sixth psalm.

paras.t: Quidam autem hunc psalmum ad litteram exponunt de solis Judæis, corporalibusque periculis, a quibus divinitus liberati sunt: et est expositio ista satis infructuosa, nec litteræ consonat in quibusdam.
paras.en: Some, however, expound this psalm according to the letter of the Jews alone, and of the bodily dangers from which they were delivered by God: and this exposition is fruitless enough, and in some points does not agree with the letter.

paras.t: Ait itaque: Confitemini Domino, etc., sicut expositum est. Dicant qui redempti sunt a diversis periculis, a Domino Deo Israel, quos redemit de manu inimici et tyranni, eos qualitercumque affligentis. De regionibus in quibus erant dispersi, congregavit eos, reducendo eos in terram patrum suorum, sicut per Ezechielem dixit: Tollam vos de gentibus, et congregabo vos de nationibus, et inducam vos in terram vestram; a solis ortu et occasu, ab aquilone et mari, id est a terris Judææ vicinis ex omni latere ejus, secundum quod quædam terræ respectu ejus sunt orientales, quædam occidentales, etc., in quibus quidam Judæorum fuerunt dispersi, et a quibus reducti sunt.
paras.en: So he says: [[106:1|Give glory to the Lord|Confitemini Domino]], etc., as has been expounded. [[106:2|Let them say so that have been redeemed|Dicant qui redempti sunt]] from various dangers, [[106:2|by the Lord|a Domino]] the God of Israel, [[106:2|whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy|quos redemit de manu inimici]] and tyrant who afflicted them in whatever way. He [[106:2|gathered|congregavit eos]] them [[106:2|out of the countries|De regionibus]] in which they had been scattered, bringing them back into the land of their fathers, as he said by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:24|I will take you from among the Gentiles, and will gather you together out of all the countries, and will bring you into your own land|Tollam vos de gentibus, et congregabo vos de nationibus, et inducam vos in terram vestram]]; [[106:3|From the rising and from the setting of the sun, from the north and from the sea|a solis ortu et occasu, ab aquilone et mari]], that is, from the lands neighbouring Judæa on every side of it, according as some lands lie to the east of it, some to the west, etc., in which some of the Jews had been scattered and from which they were brought back.

paras.t: Erraverunt in solitudine, id est in deserto, in inaquoso, id est in loco sicco, quia in desertis nullæ aut modicæ aquæ reperiuntur. Viam civitatis habitaculi, id est iter tritum ac certum ad civitatem aliquam ducens, in qua secure habitare possent, non invenerunt, quia in locis deserti non inveniuntur itinera strata. Et quia ex tali deviatione sequitur fames ac sitis, ideo subditur: Esurientes et sitientes panem et potum corporeum, anima eorum in ipsis defecit a naturali vigore. Et clamaverunt ad Dominum pro recto meatu. Et deduxit eos in viam rectam, ut irent in civitatem habitationis, in qua tuto manerent. Propterea, Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus, etc. Quia satiavit animam inanem, id est hominem, vacuum ventrem habentem, et animam, id est hominem, esurientem satiavit bonis cibi ac potus.
paras.en: [[106:4|They wandered in a wilderness|Erraverunt in solitudine]], that is, in the desert, [[106:4|in a place without water|in inaquoso]], that is, in a dry place, because in deserts no water, or little, is found. [[106:4|the way of a city for their habitation|Viam civitatis habitaculi]], that is, a beaten and sure road leading to some city in which they might dwell in safety, [[106:4|they found not|non invenerunt]], because in desert places no paved roads are found. And because hunger and thirst follow from such straying, there is added: [[106:5|They were hungry and thirsty|Esurientes et sitientes]] for bodily bread and drink, [[106:5|their soul fainted in them|anima eorum in ipsis defecit]] from its natural vigour. [[106:6|And they cried to the Lord|Et clamaverunt ad Dominum]] for a right course. [[106:7|And he led them into the right way|Et deduxit eos in viam rectam]], [[106:7|that they might go to a city of habitation|ut irent in civitatem habitationis]], in which they might abide in safety. Therefore [[106:8|Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him|Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus]], etc. [[106:9|For he hath satisfied the empty soul|Quia satiavit animam inanem]], that is, the man who has an empty belly, [[106:9|and hath filled the hungry soul|et animam]] (that is, the man) [[106:9|with good things|esurientem satiavit bonis]] of food and drink.

paras.t: Deinde ponitur liberatio a captivitate: Sedentes in tenebris, id est in carceribus tenebrosis, et umbra mortis: nam talia loca sunt morti similia, propter afflictiones gravissimas; vinctos in mendicitate, id est parco victu, et ferro, id est catenis: captis […] enim datur modicus cibus. Hos ergo redemit, qui ideo capti erant, Quia exacerbaverunt eloquia Dei, etc. Et eduxit eos de tenebris, id est prædictis ergastulis, et umbra mortis, id est misera vita captivitatis, quæ morti est similis, et vincula eorum, quibus erant ligati, dirupit, quia contrivit portas æreas, quibus erant conclusi.
paras.en: Next is set down the deliverance from captivity: [[106:10|Such as sat in darkness|Sedentes in tenebris]], that is, in dark prisons, [[106:10|and in the shadow of death|et umbra mortis]]: for such places are like death, because of the most grievous afflictions; [[106:10|bound in want|vinctos in mendicitate]], that is, on scanty fare, [[106:10|and in iron|et ferro]], that is, in chains: for to captives […] little food is given. These, then, he redeemed, who had been taken captive for this reason: [[106:11|Because they had exasperated the words of God|Quia exacerbaverunt eloquia Dei]], etc. [[106:14|And he brought them out of darkness|Et eduxit eos de tenebris]], that is, out of the aforesaid dungeons, [[106:14|and the shadow of death|et umbra mortis]], that is, the wretched life of captivity, which is like death, [[106:14|and broke their bonds|et vincula eorum]], with which they were bound, [[106:14|in sunder|dirupit]], [[106:16|Because he hath broken gates of brass|quia contrivit portas æreas]], within which they were shut up.

paras.t: Omnem escam corporalem abominata est anima eorum, ex gravi corporis infirmitate, et appropinquaverunt usque ad portas mortis, id est ad agonem, quia sanari se posse desperaverunt. Misit verbum suum, id est, dicendo præcepit, et sanavit eos, et eripuit eos de interitionibus eorum, id est de languoribus mortem inducentibus.
paras.en: [[106:18|Their soul abhorred|abominata est anima eorum]] [[106:18|all manner of meat|Omnem escam]] for the body, from grievous sickness of the body, [[106:18|and they drew nigh even to the gates of death|et appropinquaverunt usque ad portas mortis]], that is, to the death-agony, because they despaired of being able to be healed. [[106:20|He sent his word|Misit verbum suum]], that is, he gave command by speaking, [[106:20|and healed them|et sanavit eos]], [[106:20|and delivered them from their destructions|et eripuit eos de interitionibus eorum]], that is, from sicknesses that bring on death.

paras.t: Consequenter agitur de liberatione a tempestatibus atque periculis maris. Qui descendunt mare in navibus, ad navigandum in eo, facientes operationem in aquis multis, id est in mari diversos labores exercentes. Ipsi viderunt opera Domini, quæ natant in mari, scilicet pisces et alia quædam insolita, quæ frequenter apparent in mari. Unde subjungitur, et mirabilia ejus viderunt in profundo maris, videlicet monstra, belluasque marinas. Dixit Deus, et stetit, id est, surrexit atque invaluit, spiritus procellæ, id est ventus et motus tempestatis, et exaltati sunt fluctus ejus, id est, in altum ascenderunt, et intumuerunt gurgites maris. Ascendunt usque ad cœlos, id est, mari sic intumescente, naves et nautæ in eis exsistentes, ascendunt in magnam altitudinem aeris, et descendunt usque ad abyssos, id est in magnam maris profunditatem, secundum quod fluctus descendunt; anima eorum, id est nautarum, in malis pœnæ tabescebat, propter pericula imminentia. Turbati sunt corde, et moti sunt corpore, timore atque tremore, sicut ebrius qui stare et ratione uti non potest perfecte; et omnis sapientia eorum devorata est, quia in tantis periculis nesciunt sibi consulere: quoniam magnæ passiones actum rationis impediunt, eo quod virtutem phantasticam multum deordinent. Et statuit procellam ejus, id est, Deus tempestatem maris convertit, in auram, id est in ventum suavem et statum quietum; et siluerunt fluctus ejus, id est, fluctus maris a suo strepitu cessaverunt. Et lætati sunt nautæ, quia siluerunt hi fluctus; et deduxit eos Deus in portum voluntatis eorum, id est in portum optatum.
paras.en: Next he treats of the deliverance from storms and the dangers of the sea. [[106:23|They that go down to the sea in ships|Qui descendunt mare in navibus]], to sail upon it, [[106:23|doing business in the great waters|facientes operationem in aquis multis]], that is, carrying on various labours on the sea. [[106:24|These have seen the works of the Lord|Ipsi viderunt opera Domini]] that swim in the sea, namely fishes and certain other unusual things which often appear in the sea. Hence there is added: [[106:24|and his wonders|et mirabilia ejus]] they saw [[106:24|in the deep|in profundo]] of the sea, namely monsters and sea beasts. [[106:25|He said the word|Dixit]] (that is, God) [[106:25|and there arose|et stetit]], that is, rose up and grew strong, [[106:25|a storm of wind|spiritus procellæ]], that is, the wind and stirring of the tempest, [[106:25|and the waves thereof were lifted up|et exaltati sunt fluctus ejus]], that is, they rose on high, and the whirling waters of the sea swelled. [[106:26|They mount up to the heavens|Ascendunt usque ad cœlos]], that is, the sea swelling so, the ships and the sailors who are in them rise to a great height of the air, [[106:26|and they go down to the depths|et descendunt usque ad abyssos]], that is, into the great depth of the sea, as the waves go down; [[106:26|their soul|anima eorum]], that is, of the sailors, [[106:26|pined away|tabescebat]] [[106:26|with evils|in malis]] of punishment, because of the dangers that hung over them. [[106:27|They were troubled|Turbati sunt]] in heart, [[106:27|and reeled|et moti sunt]] in body, with fear and trembling, [[106:27|like a drunken man|sicut ebrius]], who cannot stand and use his reason perfectly; [[106:27|and all their wisdom was swallowed up|et omnis sapientia eorum devorata est]], because in such great dangers they know not how to take counsel for themselves: since great passions hinder the act of reason, in that they greatly disorder the imaginative power [*virtus phantastica*: the faculty of imagination, which reason makes use of]. [[106:29|And he turned the storm|Et statuit procellam ejus]], that is, God changed the tempest of the sea, [[106:29|into a breeze|in auram]], that is, into a gentle wind and a quiet state; [[106:29|and its waves were still|et siluerunt fluctus ejus]], that is, the waves of the sea ceased from their roaring. [[106:30|And they rejoiced|Et lætati sunt]], the sailors, [[106:30|because they were still|quia siluerunt]], these waves; [[106:30|and he brought them|et deduxit eos]], God, [[106:30|to the haven which they wished for|in portum voluntatis eorum]], that is, into the haven they longed for.

paras.t: Posuit Deus flumina in desertum, id est, aquas fluviorum fecit deficere, ita quod terra ante aquis irrigua, siccata est tanquam desertum; et exitus aquarum in sitim, id est, terram aquis fluentem, fecit sitibundam et sterilem. Terram fructiferam posuit in salsuginem, id est, sterilem fecit, a malitia inhabitantium in ea, id est propter incolarum ejus peccata. Posuit desertum in stagna aquarum, id est, terram aridam fecit aquosam, et terram sine aqua posuit in exitus aquarum, id est abundantem in aquis. Hæc omnia agit providentia Dei secundum exigentiam divinæ justitiæ et meritorum vitæ humanæ. Et collocavit illic, id est in terra aquosa et uberi, esurientes, id est fructibus terræ indigentes; et constituerunt civitatem habitationis, id est, loca habitabilia construxerunt juxta terram tam fertilem, quatenus eam colere, ejusque fructus percipere possent. Et seminaverunt agros, pro cibo acquirendo, et plantaverunt vineas, pro potu habendo, et fecerunt fructum nativitatis, id est, terram et vineas sic coluerunt, quod fructum convenientem protulerunt. Et benedixit eis, id est, hominibus dona suæ pietatis donavit; et multiplicati sunt nimis, in terra tam bona ex benedictione divina; et jumenta eorum non minoravit, id est, pecora multiplicavit.
paras.en: [[106:33|He hath turned|Posuit Deus]] (God, that is) [[106:33|rivers into a wilderness|flumina in desertum]], that is, he made the waters of the rivers fail, so that land formerly watered was dried up like a desert; [[106:33|and the sources of waters into dry ground|et exitus aquarum in sitim]], that is, land flowing with waters he made thirsty and barren. [[106:34|A fruitful land|Terram fructiferam]] he turned [[106:34|into barrenness|in salsuginem]] [that is, literally, into saltness], that is, made it barren, [[106:34|for the wickedness of them that dwell therein|a malitia inhabitantium in ea]], that is, because of the sins of its inhabitants. [[106:35|He hath turned a wilderness into pools of waters|Posuit desertum in stagna aquarum]], that is, he made dry land watery, [[106:35|and a dry land|et terram sine aqua]] he turned [[106:35|into water springs|in exitus aquarum]], that is, into land abounding in waters. All these things the providence of God does according as divine justice and the deserts of human life require. [[106:36|And hath placed there|Et collocavit illic]], that is, in the watered and fertile land, [[106:36|the hungry|esurientes]], that is, those in need of the fruits of the earth; [[106:36|and they made a city for their habitation|et constituerunt civitatem habitationis]], that is, they built dwelling places beside land so fertile, so that they might till it and gather its fruits. [[106:37|And they sowed fields|Et seminaverunt agros]], to get food, [[106:37|and planted vineyards|et plantaverunt vineas]], to have drink, [[106:37|and they yielded fruit of birth|et fecerunt fructum nativitatis]], that is, they so tilled the land and the vineyards that they brought forth fitting fruit. [[106:38|And he blessed them|Et benedixit eis]], that is, he bestowed on the men the gifts of his loving-kindness; [[106:38|and they were multiplied exceedingly|et multiplicati sunt nimis]], in a land so good, by the divine blessing; [[106:38|and their cattle he suffered not to decrease|et jumenta eorum non minoravit]], that is, he multiplied their flocks.

paras.t: Et iterum propter sua peccata recentia, pauci facti sunt numero, quia partim occisi sunt, aut alias perierunt, eo quod Deum venerati non sunt; et vexati sunt a tribulatione malorum et dolore, ex pœna eis inflicta a pravis hominibus, et propter dolorem intrinsecum, quem conceperunt ex morte propinquorum suorum: per quorum interitum pauci effecti sunt. Effusa est contentio super principes, id est, principes inter se discordes fuerunt; et errare fecit eos in invio, id est, Deus justo judicio permisit eos a recta ratione deficere, et non in via, quia nec in bona via dirigi meruerunt. Et adjuvit pauperem de inopia, ipsum ditando, et posuit sicut oves familias, id est, principibus inter se discordantibus, multiplicavit filios subditorum. Cetera patent in præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: [[106:39|Then they were brought to be few|pauci facti sunt]] again in number, because of their fresh sins: for some were slain or perished otherwise, since they did not worship God; [[106:39|and they were afflicted through the trouble of evils and sorrow|et vexati sunt a tribulatione malorum et dolore]]: by the punishment inflicted on them by wicked men, and because of the inward sorrow which they conceived from the death of their kinsfolk, by whose destruction they were brought to be few. [[106:40|Contempt was poured forth upon their princes|Effusa est contentio super principes]] [Denis reads *contentio*, "strife", where the Vulgate has *contemptio*, "contempt"], that is, the princes were at discord among themselves; [[106:40|and he caused them to wander where there was no passing|et errare fecit eos in invio]], that is, God by a just judgement permitted them to fall away from right reason, [[106:40|and out of the way|et non in via]], because they did not deserve to be directed even in a good way. [[106:41|And he helped the poor out of poverty|Et adjuvit pauperem de inopia]], by making him rich, [[106:41|and made him families like a flock of sheep|et posuit sicut oves familias]], that is, while the princes were at discord among themselves, he multiplied the children of their subjects. The rest is plain from the preceding article.

paras.t: Si autem iste esset sensus a Propheta intentus, nescio cur in fine psalmi præsentis tam specialiter ac noviter diceret, Quis sapiens, et custodiet hæc? In quo utique innuit, psalmum præsentem aliquid singulariter mysticum, fructuosum, atque profundum continere.
paras.en: But if this were the sense intended by the Prophet, I do not know why at the end of the present psalm he should say so particularly and in so new a manner: [[106:43|Who is wise, and will keep these things|Quis sapiens, et custodiet hæc]]? By this he surely hints that the present psalm contains something singularly mystical, fruitful and profound.

paras.t: Idcirco non puto sensum istum tam superficialem ac rudem, a sancto Propheta finaliter aut principaliter fuisse intentum; sed quemadmodum asserit Augustinus, præcedentis articuli expositio vere exprimit sensum litteralem psalmi præsentis.
paras.en: Therefore I do not think that this sense, so superficial and crude, was intended by the holy Prophet as his final or principal meaning; but, as Augustine asserts, the exposition of the preceding article truly expresses the literal sense of the present psalm.

paras.t: Precatio. Te, Domine, præcipiente, sileant fluctus tempestatum vitæ nostræ, et statue procellam nostram in auram tranquillitatis et lætitiæ: ut in portum salutis te gubernatore deducti, nos misericordiæ tuæ opera confiteamur tibi.
paras.en: Prayer. At thy command, O Lord, may the waves of the storms of our life be still; and turn our storm into a breeze of calm and gladness: that, brought into the haven of salvation with thee for our pilot, we may give glory to thee for the works of thy mercy.

107.title: EXPOSITIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI CENTESIMI SEPTIMI : PARATUM COR MEUM, DEUS.
107.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and seventh psalm concerning Christ: My heart is ready, O God.

paras.t: TITULUS psalmi praesentis est : Canticum, psalmus ipsi David : id est, scriptura haec seu iste tractatus, est canticum, quia spiritualem laetitiam continet ; et psalmus, quoniam ad operationem bonam nos admonet : et convenit ipsi David secundum triplicem modum. Convenit enim sancto David prophetae sicut auctori ; et sicut ex circumstantia litterae tangitur, psalmus iste est exsultatio David regis in Domino gloriantis, et ei de suis beneficiis gratias referentis, scilicet de victoria sibi a Deo concessa et restitutione regni Israel in statum bonum. Convenit etiam ipsi David, id est Christo per David significato : et hoc, secundum allegoricum intellectum. Multa namque contigerant sancto David in figura Domini Salvatoris. Convenit quoque David, id est Ecclesiae seu unicuique Christiano pulchro interius ac manuforti in Domino. Sed quoniam expositio illa de Christo dulcior, fructuosior, devotiorque consistit, idcirco eam in primis introducere expedit.
paras.en: The TITLE of the present psalm is: [[107:1|A canticle of a psalm for David himself|Canticum, psalmus ipsi David]] [Denis reads *Canticum, psalmus*, "a canticle, a psalm", and explains the two words in turn]: that is, this writing or treatise is a *canticle*, because it contains spiritual gladness; and a *psalm*, because it admonishes us to good works: and it fits *David himself* in a threefold way. For it fits the holy prophet David as its author; and, as the circumstances of the letter indicate, this psalm is the exultation of King David glorying in the Lord and giving him thanks for his benefits, namely for the victory granted him by God and for the restoring of the kingdom of Israel to a good state. It fits also David himself, that is, Christ, signified by David: and this according to the allegorical sense. For many things had befallen holy David as a figure of the Lord Saviour. It fits David too, that is, the Church, or each Christian who is fair within and strong of hand in the Lord [the name David was taken to mean "strong of hand" and "desirable" or "fair"]. But since the exposition concerning Christ is the sweeter, the more fruitful and the more devout, it is fitting to set it out first.

paras.t: CHRISTUS ergo secundum quod homo, Deo Patri in cunctis obediens, ait ad Patrem seu totam superbeatissimam Trinitatem : Paratum cor meum, id est, voluntas mea tibi parere parata est, Deus Pater. Et resumit ad confirmationem ejus, quod dixit : paratum cor meum : paratum, inquam, ad agenda tibi placentia, paratum ad sustinendum humanae redemptioni necessaria, paratum ad laudem, et paratum ad opus. Hinc enim apud Joannem Christus testatur : Descendi de coelo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed ejus qui misit me. Et apud Matthaeum ait ad Patrem : Non sicut ego volo, sed sicut tu. Cantabo et psallam, id est, verbis atque operibus te laudabo, et tibi gratias agam, in gloria mea, id est in clara notitia laudibus mixta : quam notitiam mihi dedisti de tua bonitate ac majestate. Nisi enim quis Deum cognoscat, eum laudare non valet : propterea, sicut Christus homo seu anima Christi Deum excellentissime noverat in hac vita, sic perfectissime Deo decantavit, psalmumque dixit. Vel, Psallam in gloria mea, id est in omni dignitate gratiæ mihi infusæ, ita quod omnia bona meæ humanitati collata, in tuis præconiis occupabo, nec unquam a tuo honore cessabo, secundum quod apud Evangelistam professus sum, Ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper; et, Ego non quæro gloriam meam, sed honorifico Patrem meum. Vel, In gloria mea, id est in beatitudine animæ meæ et glorificatione corporis mei.
paras.en: CHRIST, then, as man, obedient to God the Father in all things, says to the Father, or to the whole most blessed Trinity: [[107:2|My heart is ready|Paratum cor meum]], that is, my will is ready to obey thee, [[107:2|O God|Deus]] the Father. And he repeats, to confirm what he said, [[107:2|my heart is ready|paratum cor meum]]: ready, I say, to do the things that please thee, ready to bear what is needed for man's redemption, ready for praise, and ready for work. For hence Christ testifies in John: [[John 6:38|I came down from heaven, not to do my own will but the will of him that sent me|Descendi de coelo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed ejus qui misit me]]. And in Matthew he says to the Father: [[Matt 26:39|not as I will but as thou wilt|Non sicut ego volo, sed sicut tu]]. [[107:2|I will sing, and will give praise|Cantabo et psallam]], that is, I will praise thee in words and in works, and give thee thanks, [[107:2|with my glory|in gloria mea]], that is, in a clear knowledge mingled with praises: the knowledge which thou hast given me of thy goodness and majesty. For unless one knows God, one cannot praise him: and so, as Christ as man, or the soul of Christ, knew God most excellently in this life, so he sang to God and said his psalm most perfectly. Or, I [[107:2|will give praise, with my glory|Psallam in gloria mea]], that is, in all the dignity of the grace poured into me, so that I will spend all the good things bestowed on my humanity on thy praises, and will never cease from thy honour, as I professed in the Evangelist: [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]] [the margin gives John xiv, 20; the words are John 8:29]; and, [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]], [[John 8:49|but I honour my Father|sed honorifico Patrem meum]]. Or, [[107:2|with my glory|In gloria mea]], that is, in the beatitude of my soul and the glorification of my body.

paras.t: Exsurge, ad notitiam hominum et ad actum venerationis divinæ, psalterium, id est Evangelium seu doctrina mea evangelica, in qua divinæ majestatis sublimia decantavi, seu docui (quæ doctrina instar psalterii sonat suaviter in auribus Dei), et cithara, id est doctrina mea moralis, vita exemplaris, et passio mortis meæ. Hoc modo exsurge, quatenus hominibus hæc innotescant, eosque ad imitationem inducant. Exsurgam de loco sepulturæ diluculo, id est valde mane, secundum quod Lucas scriptum reliquit: Una sabbati valde diluculo venerunt mulieres, et invenerunt lapidem revolutum ab ostio monumenti; et ingressæ, non invenerunt corpus Domini Jesu. Unde et Marcus refert: Surgens Jesus mane prima sabbati.
paras.en: [[107:3|Arise|Exsurge]], to the knowledge of men and to the act of divine worship, [[107:3|psaltery|psalterium]], that is, my Gospel, or my gospel teaching, in which I have sung, or taught, the sublime things of the divine majesty (which teaching sounds sweetly in the ears of God like a psaltery), [[107:3|and harp|et cithara]], that is, my moral teaching, my exemplary life, and the passion of my death. Arise in this way, so that these things may become known to men and lead them to imitation. [[107:3|I will arise|Exsurgam]] from the place of burial [[107:3|in the morning early|diluculo]], that is, very early, as Luke has left written: [[Luke 24:1|on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came|Una sabbati valde diluculo venerunt]], the women, [[Luke 24:2|and they found the stone rolled back from the sepulchre|et invenerunt lapidem revolutum ab ostio monumenti]]; [[Luke 24:3|and going in, they found not the body of the Lord Jesus|et ingressæ, non invenerunt corpus Domini Jesu]]. Whence Mark too relates of Jesus: [[Mark 16:9|he rising early the first day of the week|Surgens Jesus mane prima sabbati]].

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, id est, laudabo te, in populis Judæorum, Domine Pater: quibus per me ipsum prædicavi, et inter quos te semper laudavi, præcipue inter discipulos meos, qui erant Judæi; et psallam tibi per Apostolos et ceteros meos ministros in nationibus, id est in gentilibus ad fidem per illorum prædicationem conversis. Psallebat Christus in his gentibus Deo, dum misit Apostolos prædicare Evangelium regni inter gentiles. In Evangelio namque Deus summe laudatur. Hinc enim (referente Joanne) ait Patri unigenitus Filius: Ego te clarificavi super terram, opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem, et notum feci hominibus nomen tuum.
paras.en: [[107:4|I will praise thee|Confitebor tibi]], that is, I will laud thee, [[107:4|among the people|in populis]] of the Jews, [[107:4|O Lord|Domine]] the Father: to whom I preached in my own person, and among whom I always praised thee, especially among my disciples, who were Jews; [[107:4|and I will sing unto thee|et psallam tibi]] through the Apostles and my other ministers [[107:4|among the nations|in nationibus]], that is, among the Gentiles converted to the faith by their preaching. Christ sang psalms to God among these nations when he sent the Apostles to preach the gospel of the kingdom among the Gentiles[[Matt 28:19||]][[Matt 28:20||]]. For in the Gospel God is praised supremely. Hence (as John relates) the only-begotten Son says to the Father: [[John 17:4|I have glorified thee on the earth; I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do|Ego te clarificavi super terram, opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem]], and [[John 17:6|I have manifested thy name to the men|notum feci hominibus nomen tuum]] [Denis's *notum feci*, "I have made known", is the wording of John 17:26].

paras.t: Sic autem laudavi te, Quia magna est super cælos misericordia tua, id est, copiose effusa est miseratio tuæ bonitatis super cives cælestes. Et in ipsis refulget pietas tua, quoniam sola gratia sunt præservati a malo, et confirmati in bono. Et usque ad nubes veritas tua, id est, illuminatio evangelicæ veritatis seu infusio sapientiæ salutaris, sanctis Apostolis et prædicatoribus bonis (qui cœli dicuntur) impressa est, quemadmodum in Evangelio promisisti: Quum venerit, inquiens, ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem.
paras.en: And thus I have praised thee, [[107:5|For thy mercy is great above the heavens|Quia magna est super cælos misericordia tua]], that is, the compassion of thy goodness is plentifully poured out upon the citizens of heaven. And thy loving-kindness shines forth in them, since by grace alone they were preserved from evil and confirmed in good. [[107:5|And thy truth even unto the clouds|Et usque ad nubes veritas tua]], that is, the enlightening of gospel truth, or the infusion of saving wisdom, has been imprinted on the holy Apostles and good preachers (who are called heavens [so the text; one might expect "clouds", the word of the verse]), as thou didst promise in the Gospel: [[John 16:13|when he|Quum venerit]], he says, [[John 16:13|the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth|ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem]].

paras.t: Deinde Propheta Christum alloquitur. Exaltare super cælos, Deus: id est, tu, Christe, verus Deus existens, qui in passione tantum conculcatus et humiliatus es, ascende super omnes cælos, et redi unde venisti; et super omnem terram gloria tua: id est, per totum mundum divulgetur excellentia tua, prædicetur divinitas tua, et agnoscatur gloria tua, quemadmodum apud Isaiam prædictum est: Ecce exaltabitur servus meus, et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde. Unde et rursus Isaias dicit: Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt. Hoc etiam Christus commisit implere, post resurrectionem dicens Apostolis: Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ.
paras.en: Then the Prophet addresses Christ. [[107:6|Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens|Exaltare super cælos, Deus]]: that is, thou, O Christ, who art true God, who wast so trodden down and humbled in thy passion, ascend above all the heavens and return whence thou camest; [[107:6|and thy glory over all the earth|et super omnem terram gloria tua]]: that is, let thy excellence be spread abroad through the whole world, let thy divinity be preached and thy glory acknowledged, as was foretold in Isaias: [[Is 52:13|Behold my servant|Ecce exaltabitur servus meus]] [[Is 52:13|shall be exalted, and extolled, and shall be exceeding high|et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde]]. Whence Isaias says again: [[Is 42:12|They shall give glory to the Lord, and shall declare his praise in the islands|Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt]]. This too Christ charged them to fulfil, saying to the Apostles after the resurrection: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]].

paras.t: Ut liberentur per fidem et observantiam legis tuæ dilecti tui, id est omnes a te æterno electi. Ideo enim Christus misit Apostolos prædicare ubique, ut salvarentur electi, juxta illud Apostoli: Omnia propter electos. Salvum me fac dextera tua, id est in dextera tua, ita ut in dextera tua in cœlo resideam in bonis tuis potioribus atque cœlestibus, et exaudi me ista precantem.
paras.en: [[107:7|That thy beloved may be delivered|Ut liberentur]] through faith and the keeping of thy law, [[107:7|thy beloved|dilecti tui]], that is, all chosen by thee from eternity. For this is why Christ sent the Apostles to preach everywhere, that the elect might be saved, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[2 Tim 2:10|all things for the sake of the elect|Omnia propter electos]]. [[107:7|Save|Salvum me fac]] me [[107:7|with thy right hand|dextera tua]] [Denis reads *Salvum me fac*, "save me"], that is, at thy right hand, so that I may sit at thy right hand in heaven among thy better and heavenly goods, [[107:7|and hear me|et exaudi me]] as I pray for these things.

paras.t: Deus locutus est in sancto suo: id est, Pater locutus est nobis in Filio, qui est Sanctus Sanctorum. Quæ autem sequuntur, possunt esse verba Christi seu Dei Patris, vel totius superfelicissimæ Trinitatis.
paras.en: [[107:8|God hath spoken in his holiness|Deus locutus est in sancto suo]] [*in sancto suo* can also mean "in his holy one"]: that is, the Father [[Heb 1:2|hath spoken to us by his Son|locutus est nobis in Filio]], who is the Holy of Holies. What follows may be the words of Christ, or of God the Father, or of the whole most blissful Trinity.

paras.t: Exsultabo, id est, in electis meis lætabor, quia beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo. Et apud Jeremiam testatur: Lætabor super eis quum benefecero eis. Et dividam Sichimam, id est gentilitatem, quosdam gentilium convertendo clementer ad fidem, alios juste relinquendo. Non enim omnium est fides. Et in Actibus Apostolorum legitur Paulus a Spiritu Sancto prohibitus loqui verbum Dei in Asia. Et convallem Tabernaculorum dimetiar, id est, populum Judæorum discernam, quosdam eorum convertendo, et ceteros deserendo. Reliquiæ enim per electionem salvæ factæ sunt, secundum Apostolum. Et apud Joannem dixit Christus : Non de omnibus vobis dico ; ego scio quos elegerim. Per Sichimam autem intelliguntur gentiles, quia in terra Sichimorum morabantur pagani; per convallem vero Tabernaculorum designantur Judæi, quoniam (sicut in Genesi legitur) Jacob de Syria rediens, in hoc loco fixit tentoria, propter quod vocavit eum Socoth, id est tabernacula.
paras.en: [[107:8|I will rejoice|Exsultabo]], that is, I will be glad in my elect, because [[Ps 149:4|the Lord is well pleased with his people|beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo]] [the margin gives only Ps. cxlix]. And he testifies in Jeremias: [[Jer 32:41|I will rejoice over them, when I shall do them good|Lætabor super eis quum benefecero eis]]. [[107:8|and I will divide Sichem|Et dividam Sichimam]], that is, the Gentile world, mercifully converting some of the Gentiles to the faith and justly leaving others; [[2 Thess 3:2|for all men have not faith|Non enim omnium est fides]]. And in the Acts of the Apostles we read that Paul was forbidden by the Holy Ghost to speak the word of God in Asia[[Acts 16:6||]]. [[107:8|and I will mete out the vale of tabernacles|Et convallem Tabernaculorum dimetiar]], that is, I will sift the people of the Jews, converting some of them and forsaking the rest. For, according to the Apostle, [[Rom 11:5|there is a remnant saved according to the election|Reliquiæ enim per electionem salvæ factæ sunt]]. And in John Christ said: [[John 13:18|I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen|Non de omnibus vobis dico ; ego scio quos elegerim]]. By Sichem the Gentiles are meant, because pagans dwelt in the land of the Sichemites; and by the vale of tabernacles the Jews are signified, because (as we read in Genesis) Jacob, returning from Syria, pitched his tents in this place, and therefore called it Socoth, that is, Tabernacles[[Gen 33:17||]].

paras.t: Meus est Galaad, id est congregatio martyrum, qui proprii sanguinis effusione testimonium præbuerunt fidei christianæ. Galaad nempe interpretatur, acervus testimonii. Et meus est Manasses : id est, populus temporalium atque carnalium obliviscens, et divina contemplans ac cœlestia appetens, ad gregem pertinet electorum meorum. Manasses namque interpretatur oblivio. Et Apostolus ait : Quæ posteriora sunt obliviscens, in anteriora extendo me ipsum. Et Ephraim, id est populus in bonis operibus fertilis, est susceptio capitis mei, id est, a me suscipitur, quia acceptus est mihi. Ephraim enim interpretatur fertilitas. Juda rex meus : id est, populus confessorum, est rector corporis mei mystici, puta Ecclesiæ. Per confessores enim, qui vita et verbo Dominum profitentur ac laudant, alii gubernantur. Propter quod Dominus per Jeremiam loquitur : Dabo vobis pastores secundum cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina.
paras.en: [[107:9|Galaad is mine|Meus est Galaad]], that is, the company of the martyrs, who bore witness to the Christian faith by the shedding of their own blood. For Galaad is interpreted "heap of testimony". [[107:9|and Manasses is mine|Et meus est Manasses]]: that is, the people that forgets temporal and carnal things, contemplates divine things and longs for heavenly ones, belongs to the flock of my elect. For Manasses is interpreted "forgetfulness". And the Apostle says: [[Phil 3:13|Forgetting the things that are behind and stretching forth myself to those that are before|Quæ posteriora sunt obliviscens, in anteriora extendo me ipsum]]. [[107:9|and Ephraim|Et Ephraim]], that is, the people fruitful in good works, is [[107:9|the protection of my head|susceptio capitis mei]], that is, it is taken up by me, because it is acceptable to me [*susceptio*, "protection", is literally "a taking up", and Denis reads it so]. For Ephraim is interpreted "fruitfulness". [[107:9|Juda is my king|Juda rex meus]]: that is, the people of the confessors is the ruler of my mystical body, namely the Church. For through the confessors, who profess and praise the Lord by life and word, others are governed. Wherefore the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 3:15|I will give you pastors according to my own heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine|Dabo vobis pastores secundum cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina]].

paras.t: Moab lebes spei meæ. Moab interpretatur, ex patre. Per quod intelliguntur electi, de quibus dicit Evangelista : Non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, etc., sed ex Deo nati sunt. Unde et Christus : Omnis, inquit, plantatio quam non plantavit Pater meus cœlestis, eradicabitur. Hi ergo sunt lebes seu olla spei ipsius Christi, quia per eos impletur illud, propter quod ipse sanguinem proprium fudit. Ipsi namque salvantur, et ita per eos Christus reparat gloriam et glorificationem Patris, per lapsum primorum parentum amissam.
paras.en: [[107:10|Moab the pot of my hope|Moab lebes spei meæ]]. Moab is interpreted "from the father". By this the elect are meant, of whom the Evangelist says that they are born [[John 1:13|not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh|Non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis]], etc., [[John 1:13|but of God|sed ex Deo]]. Whence Christ too: [[Matt 15:13|Every plant|Omnis]], he says, [[Matt 15:13|which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up|plantatio quam non plantavit Pater meus cœlestis, eradicabitur]]. These, then, are the pot, or cauldron, of Christ's own hope, because through them is fulfilled that for which he shed his own blood. For they are saved, and so through them Christ restores the glory and glorification of the Father, lost through the fall of our first parents.

paras.t: In Idumæam, id est in terram gentilium, extendam calceamentum meum, id est naturam meam humanam, quæ erat velut calceamentum divinitatis. Hoc calceamentum Christus in Idumæam extendit, dum per totum orbem se ipsum prædicari, et ad aliorum notitiam ferri fecit, sicut de Paulo in Actibus ait : Vas electionis est mihi iste, ut portet nomen meum coram regibus et principibus. Mihi alienigenæ, id est gentiles olim alieni a Deo et fide, qui aliquando non populus, amici facti sunt, per prædicationem Apostolorum credendo in me. Propter quod ad Ephesios talibus scripsit Apostolus : Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, sed estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei. Et rursus ait : Vos qui eratis longe, nunc facti estis prope in sanguine ejus. Unde et Balaam in Numerorum libro prædixit : Erit Idumæa possessio ejus.
paras.en: [[107:10|Over Edom|In Idumæam]], that is, over the land of the Gentiles, [[107:10|I will stretch out my shoe|extendam calceamentum meum]], that is, my human nature, which was as it were the shoe of the Godhead. Christ stretched out this shoe over Edom when he caused himself to be preached through the whole world and carried to the knowledge of others, as he says of Paul in the Acts: [[Acts 9:15|this man is to me a vessel of election, to carry my name before|Vas electionis est mihi iste, ut portet nomen meum coram]] kings and princes [Denis has "kings and princes" where the Vulgate has "the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel"]. [[107:10|the aliens|Mihi alienigenæ]], that is, the Gentiles, once strangers to God and to the faith, [[1 Pet 2:10|who in times past were not a people|qui aliquando non populus]], [[107:10|are become my friends|amici facti sunt]] by believing in me through the preaching of the Apostles. Wherefore the Apostle wrote to such as these, to the Ephesians: [[Eph 2:19|you are no more strangers and foreigners: but you are fellow citizens with the saints and the domestics of God|Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, sed estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei]]. And again he says: [[Eph 2:13|you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh by the blood|Vos qui eratis longe, nunc facti estis prope in sanguine]] of him. Whence Balaam too foretold in the book of Numbers: [[Num 24:18|he shall possess Idumea|Erit Idumæa possessio ejus]].

paras.t: Sed quoniam ista facta sunt, non virtute humana et naturali, sed divina et supernaturali, ideo Christus ut homo subjungit : Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam ? id est in urbem Romanam (quæ erat caput et domina mundi : de qua per Isaiam prædictum est, Civitatem sublimem humiliabit). Quasi dicat : Hoc humana virtute fieri nequit, ut civitas ista convertatur ad me. Verumtamen divina virtute factum est per prædicationem Petri et Pauli, sicut Isaias disseruit : Conculcabit eam pes pauperis, id est Petri piscatoris, gressus egenorum, id est introitus Petri et Pauli. Quis deducet me usque in Idumæam, ut tota terra recipiat super se jugum meum, et credat in me ?
paras.en: But since these things were done not by human and natural power but by divine and supernatural power, Christ as man adds: [[107:11|Who will bring me into the strong city|Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam]]? That is, into the city of Rome (which was the head and mistress of the world: of which it was foretold by Isaias, [[Is 26:5|the high city he shall lay low|Civitatem sublimem humiliabit]]). As if to say: this cannot be done by human power, that this city should be converted to me. Yet by divine power it was done, through the preaching of Peter and Paul, as Isaias declared: [[Is 26:6|The foot shall tread it down, the feet of the poor|Conculcabit eam pes pauperis]], that is, of Peter the fisherman, [[Is 26:6|the steps of the needy|gressus egenorum]], that is, the entry of Peter and Paul. [[107:11|who will lead me into Edom|Quis deducet me usque in Idumæam]], so that the whole earth may take my yoke upon itself and believe in me?

paras.t: Nonne tu, Deus, hæc facies, qui repulisti nos? id est, qui corpus meum mysticum ex gentibus congregatum, multo tempore deviare permisisti, antequam converterentur, quando et nondum erant corpus mysticum actualiter, sed per prædestinationem : quemadmodum in Actibus Apostolorum asserit Paulus, Prioris ignorantiæ tempora despiciens Deus. Vel, Repulisti nos, id est, corpus meum et animam, quoad vires inferiores, in passione quodammodo dereliquisti, ita ut proclamarem : Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me ? Et non exibis, Deus, in virtutibus nostris : id est, ista non facies in nostra virtute, seu viribus creaturæ, sed potestate divina. Dicitur autem Deus exire, non motu aut loco, sed operatione.
paras.en: [[107:12|Wilt not thou, O God|Nonne tu, Deus]] do these things, [[107:12|who hast cast us off|qui repulisti nos]]? That is, who didst permit my mystical body, gathered from the Gentiles, to go astray for a long time before they were converted, when they were not yet the mystical body in act, but by predestination: as Paul asserts in the Acts of the Apostles, [[Acts 17:30|God indeed having winked at the times of this ignorance|Prioris ignorantiæ tempora despiciens Deus]] [Denis reads "the times of the former ignorance"]. Or, [[107:12|hast cast us off|Repulisti nos]], that is, thou didst in a manner forsake my body and soul, as to the lower powers, in the passion, so that I cried out: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me]]? [[107:12|and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our armies|Et non exibis, Deus, in virtutibus nostris]]? That is, thou wilt do these things not in our strength, or by the powers of a creature, but by divine power [*virtutibus*, "armies", also means "strengths" or "powers", and Denis reads it so]. Now God is said to go forth not by motion or change of place, but by his working.

paras.t: Deinde orat Christus, in quantum passibilis fuit, pro reunione corporis sui ac animæ. Da nobis auxilium de tribulatione, id est, de morte mihi in passione illata resuscita me : quod a te solo petere debeo, quia vana salus hominis, id est, homo purus veram salutem conferre non potest, nec aliquem liberare. Imo qui sperat ab eo salutem, vanus et stultus est.
paras.en: Then Christ, inasmuch as he was passible [that is, capable of suffering], prays for the reuniting of his body and soul. [[107:13|O grant us help from trouble|Da nobis auxilium de tribulatione]], that is, raise me up from the death inflicted on me in the passion: which I ought to ask of thee alone, [[107:13|for vain is the help of man|quia vana salus hominis]] [*salus*, "help", is also "salvation"], that is, a mere man cannot confer true salvation, nor deliver anyone. Nay, he who hopes for salvation from man is vain and foolish[[Jer 17:5||]].

paras.t: In Deo faciemus virtutem, id est, divina potestate iterum uniemur, et de sepulcro egrediemur, atque in cœlos ascendemus, o anima mea et corpus meum ; et ipse Deus ad nihilum deducet inimicos nostros, id est populum Judæorum, privando eum gratia in præsenti, et gloria in futuro, atque per Romanos pro magna parte eum interimendo.
paras.en: [[107:14|Through God we shall do mightily|In Deo faciemus virtutem]], that is, by divine power we shall be united again, and come forth from the sepulchre, and ascend into heaven, O my soul and my body; [[107:14|and he|et ipse]], God, [[107:14|will bring our enemies to nothing|ad nihilum deducet inimicos nostros]], that is, the people of the Jews, depriving it of grace in the present and of glory in the future, and through the Romans destroying it in great part.

107.title: EXPOSITIO EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI SEPTIMI TROPOLOGICA, IN QUA BREVITER TANGITUR LITTERALIS EXPOSITIO EJUS.
107.title_en: Tropological exposition of the same hundred and seventh psalm, in which its literal exposition is briefly touched on.

paras.t: Psalmus iste contextus est ex duorum psalmorum particulis. Prima enim pars psalmi hujus usque ibi, Salvum fac dextera tua, accepta est ex psalmo quinquagesimo sexto, qui incipit: Miserere mei, Deus, miserere mei. Reliqua vero pars ejus accepta est ex psalmo quinquagesimo nono, cujus exordium est: Deus, repulisti nos.
paras.en: This psalm is put together from parts of two psalms. For the first part of this psalm, as far as the words [[107:7|Save with thy right hand|Salvum fac dextera tua]], is taken from the fifty-sixth psalm, which begins: [[Ps 56:2|Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me|Miserere mei, Deus, miserere mei]]. The rest of it is taken from the fifty-ninth psalm, whose opening is: [[Ps 59:3|O God, thou hast cast us off|Deus, repulisti nos]].

paras.t: Moraliter autem competit psalmus iste Ecclesiæ, cuilibetque devoto, grato et fervido amatori, qui ex sanctæ caritatis fervore modum ignorante, et de dilecto plenissime confidente, ait ad Dominum: Paratum est cor meum, Deus, paratum est cor meum, ut agam et patiar omnia tibi placentia. Oro ut fiat voluntas tua in me: quidquid placuerit tibi, hoc erit optimum mihi cunctis diebus, quibus subsisto. Commendo me tibi, tuæ voluntati relinquo et offero me totum. Ecce in isto consistit tota nostra perfectio. Quo enim cor nostrum paratius est ad omnia Deo placentia, tanto Deo similiores carioresque sumus, et omnia quæ postulamus, facillime acquiremus. Hæc namque cordis promptitudo ex fervida dilectione procedit, et tanto sunt opera nostra interiora et exteriora vehementius meritoria, quanto ex corde paratiore seu promptitudine ampliore nascuntur; et tanto est ista præparatio major, quanto fuerit amor privatus minor, atque divina dilectio major. Hinc namque ad Corinthios dicit Apostolus: Non ex tristitia aut necessitate; hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus. Et in libro Paralipomenon David locutus est: Tu autem, fili mi, scito Deum patris tui, et servi ei corde perfecto et animo voluntario.
paras.en: Morally, this psalm fits the Church, and any devout, grateful and fervent lover who, out of a fervour of holy charity that knows no measure and trusts most fully in the Beloved, says to the Lord: [[107:2|My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready|Paratum est cor meum, Deus, paratum est cor meum]], to do and to suffer all things that please thee. I pray that [[Matt 6:10|Thy will be done|fiat voluntas tua]] in me: whatever shall please thee, that will be best for me all the days that I live. I commend myself to thee, I leave myself to thy will and offer myself wholly. Behold, in this consists our whole perfection. For the readier our heart is for all things pleasing to God, the more like to God and the dearer to him we are, and the more easily shall we obtain all that we ask. For this readiness of heart proceeds from fervent love, and our works, inward and outward, are the more strongly meritorious the readier the heart and the greater the promptness from which they spring; and this preparedness is the greater, the less private love [that is, love of self for one's own sake] there is, and the greater the love of God. Hence the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 9:7|not with sadness or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver|Non ex tristitia aut necessitate; hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus]]. And in the book of Paralipomenon David spoke thus: [[1 Par 28:9|And thou my son|Tu autem, fili mi]], [[1 Par 28:9|know the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart, and a willing mind|scito Deum patris tui, et servi ei corde perfecto et animo voluntario]].

paras.t: Cantabo, verba divini præconii proferendo; et psallam, opera sancta prosequendo, in gloria mea, id est in spirituali lætitia. Vel, In gloria mea, id est in conscientia pura. Nam gloria nostra hæc est, testimonium conscientiæ nostræ, secundum Apostolum. Ista ad litteram conveniunt sancto David, qui propter beneficium restitutionis regni sui in bonum statum, gratias agit Deo, offerens se paratum ad universa Deo accepta.
paras.en: [[107:2|I will sing|Cantabo]], by uttering words of divine praise; [[107:2|and will give praise|et psallam]], by carrying out holy works, [[107:2|with my glory|in gloria mea]], that is, in spiritual gladness. Or, [[107:2|with my glory|In gloria mea]], that is, in a pure conscience. For [[2 Cor 1:12|our glory is this: the testimony of our conscience|gloria nostra hæc est, testimonium conscientiæ nostræ]], according to the Apostle. These things fit holy David literally, who, for the benefit of his kingdom being restored to a good state, gives thanks to God[[2 Kings 22:1||]], offering himself ready for all that is acceptable to God.

paras.t: Exsurge, psalterium et cithara. In his enim musicis instrumentis laudavit Deum. Exsurgam diluculo, id est mane consurgam de lecto, ut Domino psallam et obsequar.
paras.en: [[107:3|arise, psaltery and harp|Exsurge, psalterium et cithara]]. For with these musical instruments he praised God. [[107:3|I will arise in the morning early|Exsurgam diluculo]], that is, I will rise from my bed in the morning, to sing to the Lord and to serve him.

paras.t: Spiritualiter vero per psalterium, quod habet decem chordas, atque a superiori parte reddit sonum, intelligitur custodia præceptorum Decalogi, quæ a cælo donata et jussa sunt nobis: quorum utique observatio dulcius sonat in auribus Dei, quam omnia musica instrumenta. Per citharam vero, quæ sex chordas habet vel septem, et ab inferiori parte efficit sonum, intelliguntur opera misericordiæ, quæ circa corporis indigentiam occupantur, atque ad vitam spectant activam. Est igitur sensus: Exsurge, psalterium, id est, observatio præceptorum Altissimi, excitare et esto in me, ut per te Deum collaudem. Sic quoque exsurge, et cithara, id est operum misericordiæ exsecutio. Nam, Benefacit animæ suæ vir misericors; et, Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur. Et ideo in Tobia habetur: Quo modo potueris, ita esto misericors; et in libro Job, Ab infantia crevit mecum miseratio. Exsurgam a lecto, a peccato, ab acedia, diluculo, id est in principio auroræ, in infusione illuminationis divinæ. Hinc enim in Ecclesiastici libro inducitur: Justus cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum. Isaias quoque, De mane, inquit, vigilabo ad te.
paras.en: Spiritually, however, by the psaltery, which has ten strings and gives its sound from the upper part, is understood the keeping of the commandments of the Decalogue[[Ex 20:1||]], which were given and enjoined on us from heaven: and the observance of them sounds sweeter in the ears of God than all musical instruments. By the harp, which has six strings or seven and makes its sound from the lower part, are understood the works of mercy, which are busied about the needs of the body and belong to the active life. So the sense is: [[107:3|arise, psaltery|Exsurge, psalterium]], that is, observance of the commandments of the Most High, be roused and be in me, that through thee I may praise God together with others. So too arise, [[107:3|and harp|et cithara]], that is, the carrying out of the works of mercy. For [[Prov 11:17|A merciful man doth good to his own soul|Benefacit animæ suæ vir misericors]]; and, [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.|Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]] And therefore it is said in Tobias: [[Tob 4:8|According to thy ability be merciful.|Quo modo potueris, ita esto misericors]] And in the book of Job: [[Job 31:18|from my infancy mercy grew up with me|Ab infantia crevit mecum miseratio]]. [[107:3|I will arise|Exsurgam]] from bed, from sin, from sloth, [[107:3|in the morning early|diluculo]], that is, at the beginning of the dawn, at the pouring in of divine light.
