Hence in the book of Ecclesiasticus it is put thus: The just man [[Ecclus 39:6|will give his heart to resort early to the Lord|cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum]]. Isaias too: [[Is 26:9|in the morning early|De mane]], he says, [[Is 26:9|I will watch to thee|vigilabo ad te]].

paras.t: Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine, id est, coram aliis te laudabo, et psallam tibi in nationibus, id est, præsentibus aliis te honorabo. Non erubescam nomen tuum coram hominibus, quoniam tu dixisti: Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo. Et in Matthæo: Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant bona facta vestra, et glorificent Patrem vestrum qui in cœlis est. Interdum etiam debemus Domino confiteri nostra peccata in populis, quando videlicet peccata manifesta sunt.
paras.en: [[107:4|I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people|Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine]], that is, I will praise thee before others, [[107:4|and I will sing unto thee among the nations|et psallam tibi in nationibus]], that is, I will honour thee in the presence of others. I will not be ashamed of thy name before men, since thou hast said: He [[Matt 10:32|that shall confess me before men, I will also confess him before my Father|Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo]][[Luke 12:8||]]. And in Matthew: [[Matt 5:16|So let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven|Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant bona facta vestra, et glorificent Patrem vestrum qui in cœlis est]]. Sometimes also we ought to confess [Latin *confiteri*, the word used in the psalm for praising] our sins to the Lord among the people, namely when the sins are public.

paras.t: Quia magna est super cœlos, id est super omnes qui in terra cœlestem atque angelicam vitam ducunt, quorum conversatio est in cœlis, misericordia tua: quidquid enim boni in eis est, ex tua ordinatione et bonitate manavit, dependet, et conservatur. Vel, Super cœlos, id est Beatos in patria, quoniam ipsi per misericordiam beatitudinem suam adepti sunt. Et usque ad nubes, id est angelos sanctos, veritas tua, id est illuminatio tua, pertingit. Nam secundum Dionysium capitulo 15 Cœlestis hierarchiæ, per nubes sacra Scriptura intelligit angelos, quoniam ipsi primo et immediatius, copiosiusque summæ lucis radios suscipiunt, eosque transfundunt in alios.
paras.en: [[107:5|For thy mercy is great above the heavens|Quia magna est super cœlos]], that is, above all who on earth lead a heavenly and angelic life, whose [[Phil 3:20|conversation is in heaven|conversatio est in cœlis]], [[107:5|thy mercy|misericordia tua]] is great: for whatever good is in them has flowed from thy ordaining and goodness, and depends on it and is kept by it. Or, [[107:5|above the heavens|Super cœlos]], that is, above the Blessed in the fatherland, since they have obtained their beatitude through mercy. [[107:5|even unto the clouds|Et usque ad nubes]], that is, to the holy angels, [[107:5|thy truth|veritas tua]], that is, thine illumination, reaches. For according to Dionysius, in chapter 15 of the *Celestial Hierarchy*, by clouds holy Scripture means the angels, since they receive the rays of the highest light first, more immediately and more abundantly, and pour them on into others.

paras.t: Exaltare super cœlos, Deus, id est, ab omnibus civibus patriæ cœlestis, adoreris, magnificeris, atque laudaris, et super omnem terram, id est in tota militanti Ecclesia, augeatur et semper exsistat gloria tua, id est clara nominis tui notitia, laudatio gloriosa, veneratioque præclara, quatenus omnes convertantur ad te, et tibi obediant, gloriamque persolvant; ut liberentur dilecti tui ab omni periculo. Salvum fac me dextera tua, id est per benignam tuam subventionem ac gratiosam præsentiam, et exaudi me ista precantem.
paras.en: [[107:6|Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens|Exaltare super cœlos, Deus]], that is, be adored, magnified and praised by all the citizens of the heavenly fatherland, [[107:6|over all the earth|et super omnem terram]], that is, in the whole Church militant, may [[107:6|thy glory|gloria tua]] grow and ever abide, that is, the clear knowledge of thy name, glorious praise and illustrious veneration, so that all may be converted to thee, obey thee, and render thee glory; [[107:7|That thy beloved may be delivered|ut liberentur dilecti tui]] from every danger. [[107:7|Save|Salvum fac]] me [[107:7|with thy right hand|dextera tua]], that is, by thy kindly help and gracious presence, [[107:7|and hear me|et exaudi me]] as I pray these things.

paras.t: Deus locutus est per inspirationem internam seu angelicam revelationem, in sancto suo Propheta, scilicet me, seu alio quocumque, hoc quod sequitur: Exsultabo et dividam Sichimam, etc., cujus expositio in præcedenti articulo posita est. Deus enim divisit atque dimensus est Sichimam et convallem Tabernaculorum per prædicationem primitivæ Ecclesiæ, et ita Ecclesia aliquo modo divisionem hanc fecit electorum a reprobis, juxta sensum expositum.
paras.en: [[107:8|God hath spoken|Deus locutus est]] by inward inspiration or angelic revelation, [[107:8|in his holiness|in sancto suo]] [Latin *in sancto suo*, which can also mean "in his holy one"], that is, in his holy Prophet, namely in me or in anyone else, what follows: [[107:8|I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem|Exsultabo et dividam Sichimam]], etc., the exposition of which was given in the preceding article. For God divided and measured out Sichem and [[107:8|the vale of tabernacles|convallem Tabernaculorum]] through the preaching of the early Church, and so the Church in some manner made this division of the elect from the reprobate, according to the sense explained there.

paras.t: Similiter ipsa dicere potest: Meus est Galaad, et meus est Manasses, et Ephraim susceptio capitis mei: quoniam populi sancti et christiani per Galaad et Manassen ac Ephraim designati, prout in præcedenti articulo dictum est, ad unitatem et mysticum corpus Ecclesiæ pertinent, scilicet martyres significati per Galaad, oblitores temporalium rerum figurati per Manassen, operatores idonei per Ephraim denotati. Et de Ephraim ait Ecclesia, quod sit susceptio capitis sui, id est, a Christo capite suo populus fecundus in bono suscipitur. Juda, id est populus Domino confitens verbo ac opere, est rex meus, id est rector membrorum Ecclesiæ, quia a talibus inferiores regendi sunt.
paras.en: In like manner she can say: [[107:9|Galaad is mine: and Manasses is mine and Ephraim the protection of my head|Meus est Galaad, et meus est Manasses, et Ephraim susceptio capitis mei]]: since the holy and Christian peoples signified by Galaad, Manasses and Ephraim, as was said in the preceding article, belong to the unity and mystical body of the Church: namely the martyrs, signified by Galaad; those who forget temporal things, figured by Manasses; and fit workers, denoted by Ephraim. And of Ephraim the Church says that he is the protection of her head [Latin *susceptio capitis*, literally "the taking up of the head"], that is, a people fruitful in good is taken up by Christ her head. [[107:9|Juda|Juda]], that is, the people confessing the Lord in word and deed, [[107:9|is my king|rex meus]], that is, the ruler of the members of the Church, since those below are to be ruled by such.

paras.t: Moab, id est populus ex patre genitus, scilicet filii summi Patris, lebes spei meæ: quia in talibus confidit Ecclesia quod salvabuntur, eo quod scriptum sit in prima Canonica Joannis: Omnis qui natus est ex Deo, non peccat, quoniam semen Dei manet in eo.
paras.en: [[107:10|Moab|Moab]], that is, the people begotten of the father [that is, *Moab* taken to mean "from the father"], namely the sons of the most high Father, is [[107:10|the pot of my hope|lebes spei meæ]]: because the Church trusts that such shall be saved, since it is written in the first canonical Epistle of John: [[1 John 3:9|Whosoever is born of God committeth not sin: for his seed abideth in him|Omnis qui natus est ex Deo, non peccat, quoniam semen Dei manet in eo]].

paras.t: Deinde Ecclesia ait: In Idumæam extendam calceamentum meum, id est, pedes meos ad gentiles extendam, prædicando per totum mundum, quemadmodum dicit Apostolus: Ecce convertimur ad gentes. Mihi alienigenæ amici facti sunt, id est, gentiles per caritatem unum facti sunt mecum in Christo. Omnes namque fideles per caritatem uniuntur in Deo, quia (ut ait Apostolus) Christus est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum. Unde et in Zacharia prædictum est: Consilium pacis erit inter duos illos. In Ecclesia equidem Christi, duo populi caritative adunati sunt, utpote Judæi et gentiles. Et ecce quam amicissimi atque carissimi facti sint conversi ex gentibus, primitivæ Ecclesiæ quæ ex Judæis constabat. Paulus enim Philippensibus scribens: Fratres, inquit, mei carissimi et desideratissimi, gaudium meum et corona; et alibi, Libentissime impendam et superimpendar ipse pro animabus vestris; rursusque, Tunc nos vivimus, si vos statis in Domino.
paras.en: Then the Church says: [[107:10|Over Edom I will stretch out my shoe|In Idumæam extendam calceamentum meum]], that is, I will stretch out my feet to the gentiles, preaching through the whole world, as the Apostle says: [[Acts 13:46|behold we turn to the Gentiles|Ecce convertimur ad gentes]]. [[107:10|the aliens are become my friends|Mihi alienigenæ amici facti sunt]], that is, the gentiles have been made one with me in Christ through charity. For all the faithful are united in God through charity, since (as the Apostle says) Christ [[Eph 2:14|is our peace, who hath made both one|est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]]. Hence it was foretold in Zacharias too: [[Zach 6:13|the counsel of peace shall be between them both|Consilium pacis erit inter duos illos]]. In the Church of Christ, indeed, two peoples have been joined in charity, namely Jews and gentiles. And behold how very friendly and dear the converts from the gentiles became to the early Church, which was made up of Jews. For Paul, writing to the Philippians, says: [[Phil 4:1|my dearly beloved brethren|Fratres]], he says, [[Phil 4:1|and most desired, my joy and my crown|mei carissimi et desideratissimi, gaudium meum et corona]]; and elsewhere: [[2 Cor 12:15|I most gladly will spend and be spent myself for your souls|Libentissime impendam et superimpendar ipse pro animabus vestris]] [the margin gives I Cor. xii, 13; the words are 2 Cor 12:15]; and again: [[1 Thess 3:8|now we live, if you stand in the Lord|Tunc nos vivimus, si vos statis in Domino]].

paras.t: Sed quia ista progressio et prædicatio Ecclesiæ per universum mundum facta est, non virtute humana, sed potestate divina, ideo subdit Ecclesia in persona prædicatorum suorum: Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam? Et patet sententia ex prædictis.
paras.en: But since this advance and preaching of the Church through the whole world was done not by human strength but by divine power, the Church therefore adds, in the person of her preachers: [[107:11|Who will bring me into the strong city?|Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam?]] And the sense is clear from what has been said.

paras.t: Da nobis auxilium de tribulatione, id est adversus omnes persecutiones et adversitates, ne opprimamur a malis, sed patientiam conservemus, atque per eam omnia dura vincamus.
paras.en: [[107:13|O grant us help from trouble|Da nobis auxilium de tribulatione]], that is, against all persecutions and adversities, that we may not be overwhelmed by evils, but may keep patience, and through it overcome all hard things.

paras.t: In Deo, id est per gratiam Dei, faciemus virtutem, resistendo mundo, carni ac dæmoni, atque divina mandata servando. Et ipse ad nihilum deducet, id est, conteret ac deficere faciet, inimicos nostros visibiles et invisibiles: secundum quod ad Romanos scriptum est, Deus conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter.
paras.en: [[107:14|Through God|In Deo]], that is, through the grace of God, [[107:14|we shall do mightily|faciemus virtutem]] [Latin *faciemus virtutem*, "we shall do valour" or "act with strength"], by resisting the world, the flesh and the devil, and by keeping the divine commandments. [[107:14|and he will bring|Et ipse ad nihilum deducet]] to nothing, that is, he will crush them and make them fail, [[107:14|our enemies|inimicos nostros]] visible and invisible: according to what is written to the Romans: God [[Rom 16:20|crush Satan under your feet speedily|conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter]].

paras.t: Demum omnia ista conveniunt sancto David, sicut et ceteris Sanctis, secundum sensum jam explanatum usque ad id, Deus locutus est in sancto suo. Hæc ergo de David litteraliter exponenda sunt.
paras.en: Lastly, all these things fit holy David, as they do the other Saints, according to the sense already explained, as far as the words [[107:8|God hath spoken in his holiness|Deus locutus est in sancto suo]]. These things, then, are to be expounded literally of David.

paras.t: Ait itaque: Deus locutus est in sancto suo: id est per Samuelem et Nathan prophetam. Dixit et promisit mihi, quod ego David exsultabo et dividam, id est, cum lætitia metiar, Sichimam, id est spolia terræ Sichimorum, servis et adjutoribus meis mecum contra illam pugnantibus; et convallem Tabernaculorum, id est locum qui dicitur Socoth juxta Jordanem, dimetiar, id est, filiis Israel restituam, dando unicuique debitam partem. De hac namque convalle expulit David Philistæos, qui eam injuste possederant.
paras.en: So he says: [[107:8|God hath spoken in his holiness|Deus locutus est in sancto suo]]: that is, through Samuel and Nathan the prophet. He told and promised me that I, David, [[107:8|I will rejoice, and I will divide|exsultabo et dividam]], that is, I will measure out with gladness, [[107:8|Sichem|Sichimam]], that is, the spoils of the land of the Sichemites, to my servants and helpers fighting with me against it; and [[107:8|the vale of tabernacles|convallem Tabernaculorum]], that is, the place called Socoth near the Jordan, [[107:8|I will mete out|dimetiar]], that is, I will restore it to the children of Israel, giving each his due share. For from this valley David drove out the Philistines[[2 Kings 8:1||]], who had held it unjustly.

paras.t: Sed quoniam David hæc fecit adjutorio populi sui, eorum præcipue qui magis bellicosi ac fortes fuerunt; idcirco nominat tribus illas, quæ ei adjutorium præbuerunt. Meus est Galaad, id est populus habens terram Galaad in possessionem trans Jordanem: qui erant nominati in robore propter Jair et Jephthe de illa terra exortos; et meus est Manasses, id est populus ex filio Joseph dicto Manasses progenitus: qui populus erat famosus propter Gedeonem ex illa progenie natum. Et Ephraim susceptio capitis mei: id est, populus ex Ephraim genitus, a me principaliter acceptatur: quoniam numerosus atque fortissimus erat, et Josue de hac tribu fuit, prætulitque Jacob Ephraim ipsi Manassæ. Juda rex meus: quia de Juda principes erant; Moab lebes spei meæ: id est, per adjutorium Dei confido Moabitas expugnare ac possidere, quemadmodum possidetur olla a patrefamilias. Hoc etiam factum est: nam Moabitæ servierunt David sub tributo. In Idumæam, id est in terram Edom, in qua moratus est Esau, extendam calceamentum meum, id est, illam intrabo et calceatus per eam meabo, subjiciens eam imperio meo. Mihi alienigenæ, id est gentes in circuitu Judææ manentes, amici facti sunt, id est confœderati, postulantes sibi pacem dari a me.
paras.en: But since David did these things with the help of his people, especially of those who were more warlike and strong, he therefore names those tribes which gave him help. [[107:9|Galaad is mine|Meus est Galaad]], that is, the people holding the land of Galaad as their possession beyond the Jordan, who were renowned for strength because of Jair[[Judg 10:3||]] and Jephthe[[Judg 11:1||]], who sprang from that land; [[107:9|and Manasses is mine|et meus est Manasses]], that is, the people descended from the son of Joseph called Manasses[[Gen 48:5||]], which people was famous because of Gedeon, born of that stock[[Judg 6:15||]]. [[107:9|and Ephraim the protection of my head|Et Ephraim susceptio capitis mei]]: that is, the people born of Ephraim is accepted by me above the rest, since it was numerous and very strong, and Josue was of this tribe[[Num 13:9||]][[Num 13:17||]], and Jacob set Ephraim before Manasses himself[[Gen 48:20||]] [the margin gives Gen. xlviii, 17–20]. [[107:9|Juda is my king|Juda rex meus]]: because the princes came of Juda; [[107:10|Moab the pot of my hope|Moab lebes spei meæ]]: that is, by the help of God I trust to conquer and possess the Moabites, as a pot is possessed by the master of a house. And this was done: for the Moabites served David under tribute[[2 Kings 8:2||]]. [[107:10|Over Edom|In Idumæam]], that is, into the land of Edom, in which Esau dwelt[[Gen 36:8||]], [[107:10|I will stretch out my shoe|extendam calceamentum meum]], that is, I will enter it and walk through it shod, subjecting it to my rule. [[107:10|the aliens|Mihi alienigenæ]], that is, the nations dwelling round about Judæa, [[107:10|are become my friends|amici facti sunt]], that is, allied with me, asking that peace be granted them by me.

paras.t: Quoniam vero David cognovit ista se non posse implere propria potestate, sed adjutorio Dei, ideo subdit: Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam muris ac portis? quis deducet me usque in Idumæam, ut eam mihi subjiciam? Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulisti nos, id est, qui præteritis temporibus permisisti populum Israel graviter multipliciterque affligi? Cetera elucescunt ex præinductis.
paras.en: But since David knew that he could not accomplish these things by his own power, but only by the help of God, he therefore adds: [[107:11|Who will bring me into the strong city|Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam]], strong with walls and gates? [[107:11|who will lead me into Edom|quis deducet me usque in Idumæam]], to subject it to me? [[107:12|Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off|Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulisti nos]], that is, who in times past didst allow the people of Israel to be afflicted grievously and in many ways? The rest is clear from what was brought in before.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum in exordio sui spirituali lætitia plenum, et fervido amatori suavem audivimus. Et omnino conandum est nobis taliter in divino amore succrescere, ut vere dicamus: Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum. Decet namque rationalem creaturam Creatori suo perfecte esse subjectam, et toto desiderio ad ipsius beneplacitum promptam. Debet quoque quilibet nostrum se ipsum hortari, excitare et inflammare ad Dei præconia atque obsequia dicendo: Exsurge, psalterium et cithara. Unde ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus: Adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies, ut non obduretur quis ex vobis fallacia peccati. Debemus insuper omni hora firmum habere propositum indesinenter laudandi ac venerandi Altissimum, dicentes intra nos: Exsurgam diluculo, et, Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine. In omnibus vero et super omnia decet, imo oportet nos Dei honorem intendere, in ejus laudibus exsultare, ejus beatitudini congaudere, secundum quod caritas divina efflagitat.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm that at its opening is full of spiritual gladness and sweet to the fervent lover. And we must strive by all means so to grow in divine love that we may truly say: [[107:2|My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready|Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum]]. For it is fitting that the rational creature be perfectly subject to its Creator, and ready with its whole desire for his good pleasure. Each of us also ought to exhort, rouse and inflame himself to the praises and service of God, saying: [[107:3|arise, psaltery and harp|Exsurge, psalterium et cithara]]. Hence the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 3:13|exhort one another every day|Adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies]], [[Heb 3:13|that none of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin|ut non obduretur quis ex vobis fallacia peccati]]. Moreover we ought at every hour to hold a firm purpose of praising and venerating the Most High without ceasing, saying within ourselves: [[107:3|I will arise in the morning early|Exsurgam diluculo]], and, [[107:4|I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people|Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine]]. In all things, and above all things, it is fitting, nay it is needful, that we aim at the honour of God, exult in his praises, and rejoice with him in his beatitude, as divine charity demands.

paras.t: Demum, ut nos pertineamus ad gregem dominicum, studeamus spiritualiter esse Galaad, Manasses, Ephraim et Judas. Galaad namque efficimur, dum fidem nostram operibus attestamur, in tantum ut nullus dicere possit, quin bona sit fides illa, quæ talem conversationem suggerit et requirit. Manasses autem efficimur temporalia obliviscendo, cœlestiumque bonorum affectuose reminiscendo, quatenus sicut hortatur Apostolus, revelata facie gloriam Domini speculemur, nuncque quotidie in christiana sapientia illustremur, quam in tantum concupivit Apostolus, ut ad Philippenses dixerit: Existimo omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Et omnino decet ut victum et quibus tegamur habentes, temporalium sollicitudinem relinquamus, atque in cœlestibus bonis totaliter occupemur. Efficimur autem et Ephraim in spiritualibus operibus fructificando, et opera spiritus efficaciter exercendo. Judas autem efficimur, Domino ore ac opere confitendo.
paras.en: Lastly, that we may belong to the Lord's flock, let us strive to be spiritually Galaad, Manasses, Ephraim and Juda. For we become Galaad when we bear witness to our faith by works, so that no one can say that the faith is not good which prompts and requires such a way of life. We become Manasses by forgetting temporal things and lovingly remembering heavenly goods, so that, as the Apostle exhorts, we may be [[2 Cor 3:18|beholding the glory of the Lord with open face|revelata facie gloriam Domini speculemur]], and be enlightened now, daily, in Christian wisdom, which the Apostle desired so greatly that he said to the Philippians: [[Phil 3:8|I count all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge of Jesus Christ, my Lord|Existimo omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]. And it is altogether fitting that, [[1 Tim 6:8|having food and wherewith to be covered|victum et quibus tegamur habentes]], we leave aside care for temporal things and be wholly taken up with heavenly goods. We become Ephraim too by bearing fruit in spiritual works and by doing the works of the spirit effectually. And we become Juda by confessing the Lord with mouth and deed.

paras.t: Postremo commemorandum est, quod circa illud, In Deo faciemus virtutem, dicit sanctissimus Hieronymus noster: Non habemus, inquit, spem nisi in Deo tantum. Non dicamus: Si istud aut illud mihi evenerit, unde habeo vivere? Si senuero, si infirmus factus fuero, unde vivo? Christum habes, et times? Si volatilia pascit, dubitas quod possit te pascere? Nos ergo omnem sollicitudinem projiciamus de cordibus nostris, et dicamus, In Deo faciemus virtutem: et ipse erit virtus nostra, et rector noster.
paras.en: Finally it should be recalled that on the words [[107:14|Through God we shall do mightily|In Deo faciemus virtutem]] our most holy Jerome says: We have no hope, he says, except in God alone. Let us not say: If this or that should befall me, how shall I have a living? If I grow old, if I fall sick, how shall I live? Thou hast Christ, and art thou afraid? If he feeds the birds[[Matt 6:26||]], dost thou doubt that he can feed thee? Let us therefore cast all anxiety out of our hearts, and say: [[107:14|Through God we shall do mightily|In Deo faciemus virtutem]]: and he will be our strength [Latin *virtus*, the same word as in the psalm's *faciemus virtutem*] and our ruler.

paras.t: Deus, qui omne quod sincerum et mundum est amas, et castas fidelium mentes inhabitas, benignitatis munificentia ab omni nos contagione expurga: ut et in te semper paratum cor habeamus, et digni in gloria tua tibi cantemus et psallamus.
paras.en: O God, who lovest all that is sincere and clean, and dwellest in the chaste minds of the faithful, by the bounty of thy kindness cleanse us from every contagion: that we may ever have a heart ready in thee, and, being worthy, may sing and give praise to thee in thy glory.

108.title: EXPLANATIO LITTERALIS PSALMI CENTESIMI OCTAVI : DEUS, LAUDEM MEAM NE TACUERIS.
108.title_en: Literal explanation of the hundred and eighth psalm: O God, be not thou silent in my praise.

paras.t: Est autem psalmi præsentis titulus iste : In finem, psalmus David : id est, psalmus iste in finem qui Christus est, nos erigens, quia de eo conscriptus est, est ipsius David tanquam auctoris. Quod enim hic psalmus de Christo ad litteram loquatur, apostolica auctoritate probatur. Nam Petrus, referente Luca in Actibus, allegat scripturam hujus psalmi loquentem de Juda proditore, et pœna sibi inflicta propter peccatum quo tradidit Christum. Sic enim ait in Actibus : Exsurgens Petrus in medio fratrum, dixit : Viri fratres, oportet impleri Scripturam, quam prædixit Spiritus Sanctus per os David, de Juda qui fuit dux eorum qui comprehenderunt Jesum. Et post pauca : Scriptum est, inquit, in libro Psalmorum : Fiat commoratio eorum deserta, et non sit qui habitet in ea ; et episcopatum ejus accipiat alter. Hujus auctoritatis prima pars habita est in psalmo sexagesimo octavo ; alia vero pars ejus continetur in psalmo præsenti. Petrus autem utramque scripturam conjungit, quoniam psalmus uterque de Christi loquitur passione. Prima quoque pars auctoritatis istius explicat pœnam Judæorum, qui ad Christi emptionem et occisionem ex invidia moti sunt ; secunda vero pars ejus exprimit pœnam Judæ, qui ad Christi venditionem ex avaritia motus est. Et sicut verba ementium atque vendentium commixtim narrantur ac describuntur, ita in psalmo hoc verba Judæ proditoris ac Judæorum ementium simul referuntur atque concurrunt.
paras.en: Now the title of the present psalm is this: [[108:1|Unto the end, a psalm for David|In finem, psalmus David]]: that is, this psalm, which tends [[108:1|unto the end|in finem]] who is Christ, raising us up, because it was written about him, is David's own, as its author. For that this psalm speaks of Christ in the literal sense is proved by apostolic authority. For Peter, as Luke relates in the Acts, cites the scripture of this psalm as speaking of Judas the traitor and of the punishment laid on him for the sin by which he betrayed Christ. For thus he says in the Acts: [[Acts 1:15|Peter rising up in the midst of the brethren, said|Exsurgens Petrus in medio fratrum, dixit]]: [[Acts 1:16|Men, brethren, the scripture must needs be fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost spoke before by the mouth of David concerning Judas, who was the leader of them that apprehended Jesus|Viri fratres, oportet impleri Scripturam, quam prædixit Spiritus Sanctus per os David, de Juda qui fuit dux eorum qui comprehenderunt Jesum]]. And a little after: [[Acts 1:20|it is written|Scriptum est]], he says, [[Acts 1:20|in the book of Psalms|in libro Psalmorum]]: [[Acts 1:20|Let their habitation become desolate, and let there be none to dwell therein|Fiat commoratio eorum deserta, et non sit qui habitet in ea]]; [[Acts 1:20|And his bishopric let another take|et episcopatum ejus accipiat alter]]. The first part of this text is found in the sixty-eighth psalm[[Ps 68:26||]]; the other part of it is contained in the present psalm[[108:8||]]. Peter joins the two scriptures together because both psalms speak of the Passion of Christ. The first part of this text, too, sets out the punishment of the Jews, who were moved by envy to buy Christ and put him to death[[Matt 27:18||]]; the second part of it expresses the punishment of Judas, who was moved by avarice to sell Christ[[Matt 26:15||]]. And just as the words of those who bought and of him who sold are told and described together, so in this psalm the words of Judas the traitor and of the Jews who bought are related at once and run together.

paras.t: CHRISTUS igitur, secundum quod aliquo modo viator erat, et passibilis, Patrem orat, dicendo : Deus, laudem meam ne tacueris, id est, eam non celes, neque taceri permittas ; sed tu qui vides me a Judæis vituperari et occidi, nec propriam gloriam quærere, sed omnia ad tuum honorem referre, fac mihi sicut facio tibi, ita ut gloriam meam et laudem atque justitiam aliis manifestes, eosque ad me laudandum convertas. Hoc est quod Christus deprecatur : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum, ut Filius tuus clarificet te. Hæc autem, o Pater, te postulo, quia os peccatoris, id est populi sacerdotalis, et os dolosi, id est Judæ proditoris, super me, id est contra me, apertum est. Sacerdotes enim concitaverunt plebem contra Christum, et multas blasphemias contra Christum locuti sunt ipsi cum suis fautoribus, dicentes : Insanit, quid eum auditis? Et alibi apud eumdem Evangelistam : Nonne bene dicimus nos, quia Samaritanus es tu, et dæmonium habes? Judas quoque contra Christum os suum aperuit : Quid, inquiens, vultis mihi dare, et ego eum vobis tradam? Et quod Marcus refert : Quemcumque osculatus fuero, ipse est, tenete eum, et ducite caute.
paras.en: CHRIST then, inasmuch as he was in some manner a wayfarer [that is, still on the journey of this life, not yet in the glory of the end] and capable of suffering, prays to the Father, saying: [[108:2|O God, be not thou silent in my praise|Deus, laudem meam ne tacueris]], that is, do not hide it nor allow it to be kept silent; but thou who seest me reviled and slain by the Jews, and not seeking my own glory[[John 8:50||]], but referring all things to thy honour, do to me as I do to thee, so that thou make known to others my glory and praise and justice, and turn them to praising me. This is what Christ prays for: Father, [[John 17:1|the hour is come. Glorify thy Son, that thy Son may glorify thee|venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum, ut Filius tuus clarificet te]]. And these things, O Father, I ask of thee, [[108:2|for the mouth of the wicked|quia os peccatoris]], that is, of the priestly people, [[108:2|and the mouth of the deceitful man|et os dolosi]], that is, of Judas the traitor, [[108:2|against me|super me]], that is, in opposition to me, [[108:2|is opened|apertum est]]. For the priests stirred up the common people against Christ, and they themselves with their supporters spoke many blasphemies against Christ, saying: He [[John 10:20|is mad. Why hear you him?|Insanit, quid eum auditis?]] And elsewhere in the same Evangelist: [[John 8:48|Do not we say well that thou art a Samaritan and hast a devil?|Nonne bene dicimus nos, quia Samaritanus es tu, et dæmonium habes?]] Judas too opened his mouth against Christ: [[Matt 26:15|What|Quid]], he said, [[Matt 26:15|will you give me, and I will deliver him unto you?|vultis mihi dare, et ego eum vobis tradam?]] And what Mark relates: [[Mark 14:44|Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he. Lay hold on him: and lead him away carefully|Quemcumque osculatus fuero, ipse est, tenete eum, et ducite caute]].

paras.t: Locuti sunt Judæi et sacerdotes adversum me linguam dolosam, proferendo adulatoria, ut me caperent in sermone. Sic enim apud Matthæum dicunt : Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo. Et sermonibus odii circumdederunt me, dicentes ad me in die Palmarum : Audis quid isti dicunt? Et apud alium Evangelistam : Tu de te ipso testimonium perhibes : testimonium tuum non est verum. Et alibi : Nos scimus quia hic homo peccator est. Unde per Osee ait Salvator : Prævaricati sunt in me, et ego redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia. Et in Jeremia : Audivi contumelias multorum, et terrorem in circuitu : Persequimini et persequamur eum. Et expugnaverunt, id est, usque ad mortem persecuti sunt, me gratis, id est sine rationabili causa. Propter quod Pilatus Judæis dicebat : Nullam causam invenio in homine isto ; sed neque Herodes.
paras.en: [[108:3|They have spoken|Locuti sunt]], the Jews and the priests, [[108:3|against me with deceitful tongues|adversum me linguam dolosam]], uttering flatteries, that they might catch me in my speech. For thus they say in Matthew: [[Matt 22:16|Master, we know that thou art a true speaker and teachest the way of God in truth. Neither carest thou for any man|Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo]]. [[108:3|and they have compassed me about with words of hatred|Et sermonibus odii circumdederunt me]], saying to me on Palm Sunday: [[Matt 21:16|Hearest thou what these say?|Audis quid isti dicunt?]] And in another Evangelist: [[John 8:13|Thou givest testimony of thyself. Thy testimony is not true|Tu de te ipso testimonium perhibes : testimonium tuum non est verum]]. And elsewhere: [[John 9:24|We know that this man is a sinner|Nos scimus quia hic homo peccator est]]. Hence the Saviour says through Osee: [[Osee 7:13|they have transgressed against me: and I redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me|Prævaricati sunt in me, et ego redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia]]. And in Jeremias: [[Jer 20:10|I heard the reproaches of many, and terror on every side: Persecute him, and let us persecute him|Audivi contumelias multorum, et terrorem in circuitu : Persequimini et persequamur eum]]. [[108:3|And have fought against|Et expugnaverunt]], that is, persecuted even unto death, [[108:3|me without cause|me gratis]], that is, without any reasonable cause. For which reason Pilate said to the Jews: I [[Luke 23:14|find no cause in this man|Nullam causam invenio in homine isto]]; [[Luke 23:15|No, nor Herod neither|sed neque Herodes]].

paras.t: Pro eo ut me diligerent, id est pro beneficiis meis a me collatis, propter quæ me tenebantur diligere, detrahebant mihi, dicentes, Seducit turbas ; et, Ecce homo vorax, potator vini, publicanorum et peccatorum amicus ; et, Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit. Ego autem orabam pro conversione eorum. Nam in cruce suspensus, dixit : Pater, ignosce illis. Unde in Isaia scriptum est : Et pro transgressoribus oravit. Christus enim implevit quod docuit, quoniam cœpit facere et docere. Docuit autem pro adversariis esse orandum : Orate, inquiens, pro persequentibus et calumniantibus vos. Ipse igitur pro inimicis suis obtulit precem.
paras.en: [[108:4|Instead of making me a return of love|Pro eo ut me diligerent]], that is, in return for the benefits I bestowed on them, for which they were bound to love me, [[108:4|they detracted me|detrahebant mihi]], saying, [[John 7:12|he seduceth the people|Seducit turbas]]; and, [[Matt 11:19|Behold a man that is a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of publicans and sinners|Ecce homo vorax, potator vini, publicanorum et peccatorum amicus]]; and, [[John 9:16|This man is not of God, who keepeth not the sabbath|Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit]]. [[108:4|But I gave myself to prayer|Ego autem orabam]] for their conversion. For hanging on the cross he said: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them|Pater, ignosce illis]]. Hence it is written in Isaias: [[Is 53:12|and hath prayed for the transgressors|Et pro transgressoribus oravit]]. For Christ fulfilled what he taught, since he [[Acts 1:1|began to do and to teach|cœpit facere et docere]]. And he taught that we must pray for our adversaries: [[Matt 5:44|pray|Orate]], he said, [[Matt 5:44|for them that persecute and calumniate you|pro persequentibus et calumniantibus vos]]. So he himself offered prayer for his enemies.

paras.t: Et posuerunt adversum me mala pro bonis, id est, injurias verborum ac verberum intulerunt mihi, pro informatione qua eis regnum Dei annuntiavi, et multa coram eis miracula feci, ut converterentur ad fidem. Unde locutus sum eis : Multa bona opera ostendi vobis ex Patre meo : propter quod horum me lapidatis? Et per Jeremiam : Numquid redditur pro bono malum, quia foderunt foveam animæ meæ? Et odium pro dilectione mea, id est, pro dilectione mea rependerunt mihi rancorem : quemadmodum in Osee legitur, Ego erudivi eos, et roboravi brachia eorum, et in me cogitaverunt malitiam. Hinc quoque apud Matthæum Christus ait : Jerusalem, Jerusalem, quoties volui congregare filios tuos, quemadmodum gallina congregat pullos suos sub alas, et noluisti?
paras.en: [[108:5|And they repaid me evil for good|Et posuerunt adversum me mala pro bonis]], that is, they inflicted on me injuries of words and of blows, in return for the teaching by which I announced to them the kingdom of God, and the many miracles I worked before them, that they might be converted to the faith. Hence I said to them: [[John 10:32|Many good works I have shewed you from my Father. For which of those works do you stone me?|Multa bona opera ostendi vobis ex Patre meo : propter quod horum me lapidatis?]] And through Jeremias: [[Jer 18:20|Shall evil be rendered for good, because they have digged a pit for my soul?|Numquid redditur pro bono malum, quia foderunt foveam animæ meæ?]] [[108:5|And hatred for my love|Et odium pro dilectione mea]], that is, for my love they paid me back with rancour: as we read in Osee: [[Osee 7:15|I have chastised them, and strengthened their arms: and they have imagined evil against me|Ego erudivi eos, et roboravi brachia eorum, et in me cogitaverunt malitiam]] [*erudivi* means also "I have taught"]. Hence too Christ says in Matthew: [[Matt 23:37|Jerusalem, Jerusalem|Jerusalem, Jerusalem]], [[Matt 23:37|how often would I have gathered together thy children, as the hen doth gather her chickens under her wings, and thou wouldst not?|quoties volui congregare filios tuos, quemadmodum gallina congregat pullos suos sub alas, et noluisti?]]

paras.t: Constitue super eum, id est populum Judæorum, peccatorem, id est principem malum, propter demerita populi hujus : quemadmodum in libro Job habetur, Regnare facit hypocritam propter peccata populi. Hoc impletum est, quando Caiphas pontifex fuit anni illius : qui merito appellatur peccator, quoniam dedit finale consilium de occisione Christi, dicendo : Expedit vobis ut unus moriatur homo pro populo. Ab illo ergo die cogitaverunt interficere eum, ut dicit Joannes.
paras.en: [[108:6|Set thou|Constitue]] [[108:6|over him|super eum]], that is, over the people of the Jews, [[108:6|the sinner|peccatorem]], that is, an evil prince, on account of the demerits of this people: as is found in the book of Job: He [[Job 34:30|maketh a man that is a hypocrite to reign for the sins of the people|Regnare facit hypocritam propter peccata populi]]. This was fulfilled when Caiphas was high priest of that year: who is rightly called a sinner, since he gave the final counsel for the slaying of Christ, saying: [[John 11:50|it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people|Expedit vobis ut unus moriatur homo pro populo]]. [[John 11:53|From that day therefore they devised to put him to death|Ab illo ergo die cogitaverunt interficere eum]], as John says.

paras.t: Vel, Constitue super eum, id est populum istum, et etiam super Judam proditorem, peccatorem, id est diabolum, cujus voluntati deserviant perseverantes in malo. Hinc Christus apud Joannem asseruit : Vos ex patre diabolo estis, et desideria patris vestri vultis perficere. Merentur enim dæmoni subditi, qui nolunt acquiescere Salvatori. Unde de Juda apud Lucam habetur : Intravit Satanas in Judam, qui cognominabatur Iscariotes. Et diabolus stet a dextris ejus, id est, cooperetur et in malo adsistat per suggestionem occultam, tam populo Judæorum quam proditori. Ex dæmonum enim suggestione concitati sunt persequi Christum. Hæc dicuntur non optando, sed prædicendo, et quid illi mereantur ostendendo. Ipsi enim meruerunt sic possideri a dæmone.
paras.en: Or: [[108:6|Set thou|Constitue]] [[108:6|over him|super eum]], that is, over this people, and also over Judas the traitor, [[108:6|the sinner|peccatorem]], that is, the devil, to whose will they may be enslaved, persevering in evil. Hence Christ declared in John: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil: and the desires of your father you will do|Vos ex patre diabolo estis, et desideria patris vestri vultis perficere]]. For those who will not yield to the Saviour deserve to be made subject to the demon. Hence of Judas it is found in Luke: [[Luke 22:3|Satan entered into Judas, who was surnamed Iscariot|Intravit Satanas in Judam, qui cognominabatur Iscariotes]]. [[108:6|And may the devil stand at his right hand|Et diabolus stet a dextris ejus]], that is, may he work with them and stand by them in evil through hidden suggestion, the people of the Jews as much as the traitor. For it was by the suggestion of demons that they were stirred up to persecute Christ. These things are said not by way of wishing, but of foretelling, and of showing what they deserve. For they deserved to be thus possessed by the demon.

paras.t: Quum judicatur ipse Judas a Christo, exeat condemnatus. Hoc fuit impletum in Cœna. Protulit namque Christus judicium contra Judam, dum dixit in Cœna : Væ homini illi, per quem Filius hominis tradetur ; bonum ei esset, si natus non esset homo ille. Hoc autem judicio prolato, dedit Christus Judæ buccellam, qua sumpta, introivit in eum Satanas ; et exivit continuo de felicissimo illo Christi atque Apostolorum collegio ad filios tenebrarum, et tunc damnatus erat sententia Christi. Vel sic : Quum judicatur populus Judæorum seu proditor particulari judicio tempore mortis, vel universali judicio in die novissimo, exeat a conspectu judicis, condemnatus in ignem æternum.
paras.en: [[108:7|When he is judged|Quum judicatur]], Judas himself, by Christ, [[108:7|may he go out condemned|exeat condemnatus]]. This was fulfilled at the Supper. For Christ pronounced judgment against Judas when he said at the Supper: [[Matt 26:24|woe to that man by whom the Son of man shall be betrayed. It were better for him, if that man had not been born|Væ homini illi, per quem Filius hominis tradetur ; bonum ei esset, si natus non esset homo ille]]. And when this judgment had been pronounced, Christ gave Judas the morsel[[John 13:26||]]; and when he had taken it, [[John 13:27|Satan entered into him|introivit in eum Satanas]]; and he [[John 13:30|went out immediately|exivit continuo]] from that most happy company of Christ and the Apostles to the children of darkness, and then he was condemned by the sentence of Christ. Or thus: [[108:7|When he is judged|Quum judicatur]], the people of the Jews or the traitor, at the particular judgment at the time of death, or at the universal judgment on the last day, [[108:7|may he go out|exeat]] from the sight of the judge, [[108:7|condemned|condemnatus]] into everlasting fire.

paras.t: Et oratio ejus, id est sermo Judæ : oratio enim dicitur quasi oris ratio ; fiat in peccatum, id est, imputetur ei in culpam : sicut dum dixit, Ave, Rabbi, et, Quemcumque osculatus fuero, ipse est. Imo pœnitentia ejus versa est ei in desperationis peccatum. Quum enim dixisset, Peccavi, tradens sanguinem justum, desperavit, et laqueo se suspendit : quod fuit peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum. Nam secundum Hieronymum, magis peccavit desperando, et se ipsum occidendo, quam Christum tradendo.
paras.en: [[108:7|And may his prayer|Et oratio ejus]], that is, the speech of Judas (for *oratio* is so called as being *oris ratio* [that is, "the reckoning of the mouth": *oratio* means both "prayer" and "speech"]), [[108:7|be turned to sin|fiat in peccatum]], that is, be imputed to him as guilt: as when he said, [[Matt 26:49|Hail, Rabbi|Ave, Rabbi]], and, [[Matt 26:48|Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he|Quemcumque osculatus fuero, ipse est]]. Nay, his very repentance was turned for him into the sin of despair. For when he had said, [[Matt 27:4|I have sinned in betraying innocent blood|Peccavi, tradens sanguinem justum]], he despaired, and [[Matt 27:5|hanged himself with an halter|laqueo se suspendit]]: which was a sin against the Holy Ghost [despair is reckoned among the sins against the Holy Ghost, which reject the very means of forgiveness]. For according to Jerome he sinned more by despairing and killing himself than by betraying Christ.

paras.t: Vel, Oratio (id est petitio Deo oblata) fiat in peccatum, id est, Deo displiceat, et vitiosa exsistat ; vel saltem occasio fiat culpæ majoris, eo quod contra formam a Christo præfixam oret. Christus namque, in oratione quam docuit, dixit : Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris. Sic autem Judas non fecit : idcirco secundum Cassiodorum peccavit, dicendo, Dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos, etc., quoniam in fraterno fuerat odio.
paras.en: Or: [[108:7|his prayer|Oratio]] (that is, the petition offered to God) [[108:7|be turned to sin|fiat in peccatum]], that is, may it displease God and be faulty; or at least may it become the occasion of greater guilt, because he prays contrary to the form laid down by Christ. For Christ, in the prayer that he taught, said: [[Matt 6:12|And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors|Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris]]. But Judas did not do so: therefore, according to Cassiodorus, he sinned in saying, [[Matt 6:12|forgive us our debts, as we also|Dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos]], etc., since he was in hatred of his brother.

paras.t: Fiant dies ejus, scilicet Judæ, pauci. Nam statim se ipsum peremit ex desperatione, Christo dijudicato. Nam laqueo se suspendit, ut dicitur apud Matthæum ; et suspensus crepuit medius, et diffusa sunt omnia viscera ejus, ut in libro Actuum inducitur. Et episcopatum ejus, id est apostolatum, accipiat alter, puta Matthias, qui pro eo in Apostolum est electus, prout in Actibus Apostolorum plenius recitatur. Unde episcopi dicuntur et sunt successores Apostolorum.
paras.en: [[108:8|May his days|Fiant dies ejus]], namely of Judas, [[108:8|be few|pauci]]. For straightway, once Christ had been sentenced, he made away with himself out of despair. For he [[Matt 27:5|hanged himself with an halter|laqueo se suspendit]], as is said in Matthew; and [[Acts 1:18|being hanged, burst asunder in the midst: and all his bowels gushed out|suspensus crepuit medius, et diffusa sunt omnia viscera ejus]], as is set down in the book of Acts. [[108:8|And his bishopric|Et episcopatum ejus]], that is, his apostleship, [[108:8|let another take|accipiat alter]], namely Matthias, who was chosen an Apostle in his place, as is told more fully in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 1:26||]] [the margin gives Acts i, 23–26]. Hence bishops are called, and are, the successors of the Apostles.

paras.t: Fiant filii ejus orphani, et uxor ejus vidua. Horum utrumque simul factum est, eo suspenso : et merito. Nam, ut fertur, pro filiis et conjuge sustentandis atque ditandis furabatur ea quæ Christo dabantur, cujus ipse procurator fuit. Et huic consonare videtur, quod a Joanne scriptum est, ubi post verba Judæ quibus dixit, Quare unguentum hoc non veniit trecentis denariis, et datum est egenis ? subdit Evangelista : Hoc autem dicebat, non quia de egenis ad eum pertinebat, sed quia fur erat, et loculos habens, ea quæ mittebantur, portabat.
paras.en: [[108:9|May his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow|Fiant filii ejus orphani, et uxor ejus vidua]]. Both of these came about at once, when he had hanged himself: and deservedly. For, as is reported, to support and enrich his children and wife he stole the things that were given to Christ, whose steward he was. And with this what John wrote seems to agree, where, after the words of Judas in which he said, [[John 12:5|Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence and given to the poor?|Quare unguentum hoc non veniit trecentis denariis, et datum est egenis]] the Evangelist adds: [[John 12:6|Now he said this not because he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief and, having the purse, carried the things that were put therein|Hoc autem dicebat, non quia de egenis ad eum pertinebat, sed quia fur erat, et loculos habens, ea quæ mittebantur, portabat]].

paras.t: Deinde describitur pœna populi Judæorum, qui dici possunt filii Judæ, quoniam malitiam ejus imitati sunt. De quibus subjungitur : Nutantes, id est gressu titubantes, et certum locum quo ire debeant, ignorantes, transferantur de propria terra filii ejus, id est Judæi, et mendicent, tanquam ab adversariis suis, scilicet Romanis, spoliati bonis immobilibus atque mobilibus ; et ejiciantur de habitationibus suis ad terras alienas. Hæc omnia facta sunt eis a Tito atque exercitu Romanorum, quemadmodum per Osee prophetam Christus prædixit : Exosos habui eos. Propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum, de domo mea ejiciam eos, et erunt vagi in nationibus.
paras.en: Next is described the punishment of the people of the Jews, who can be called the children of Judas, since they imitated his wickedness. Of whom it is added: [[108:10|vagabonds|Nutantes]], that is, unsteady in their gait and not knowing any sure place to which they should go, [[108:10|be carried about|transferantur]] from their own land, [[108:10|his children|filii ejus]], that is, the Jews, [[108:10|and beg|et mendicent]], as being stripped by their enemies, namely the Romans, of their goods both immovable and movable; [[108:10|and let them be cast out of their dwellings|et ejiciantur de habitationibus suis]] into foreign lands. All these things were done to them by Titus and the army of the Romans, as Christ foretold through Osee the prophet: [[Osee 9:15|I hated them|Exosos habui eos]]. [[Osee 9:15|for the wickedness of their devices I will cast them forth out of my house|Propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum, de domo mea ejiciam eos]], [[Osee 9:17|and they shall be wanderers among the nations|et erunt vagi in nationibus]].

paras.t: Scrutetur fenerator, id est exactor, scilicet Titus, omnem substantiam, id est divitias, ejus, id est populi Judæorum. Titus namque fecit substantiam Judæorum diligenter inquiri ac tolli. Et diripiant alieni, id est Romani ministri Titi, labores ejus, id est divitias Judæorum labore adeptas.
paras.en: [[108:11|May the usurer search|Scrutetur fenerator]], that is, the exactor, namely Titus, [[108:11|all his substance|omnem substantiam]], that is, the riches, *his*, that is, of the people of the Jews. For Titus had the substance of the Jews diligently searched out and taken away. [[108:11|And let strangers plunder|Et diripiant alieni]], that is, the Roman servants of Titus, [[108:11|his labours|labores ejus]], that is, the riches of the Jews gained by labour.

paras.t: Non sit illi, populo Judæorum, adjutor contra Romanos. Nullus enim ausus erat eos juvare : imo, ut Josephus scribit, Agrippa rex quamvis esset Judæus, adhæsit tamen Romanis. Nec sit qui misereatur pupillis ejus, id est filiis Judæorum occisorum. Romani enim sine misericordia eos vel occiderunt, vel vendiderunt, vel graviter afflixerunt.
paras.en: [[108:12|May there be none|Non sit illi]], to the people of the Jews, [[108:12|to help him|adjutor]] against the Romans. For no one dared to help them: nay, as Josephus writes, King Agrippa, though he was a Jew, nevertheless sided with the Romans [the margin gives Josephus, *On the Jewish War*, book II, ch. 16]. [[108:12|Nor none to pity|Nec sit qui misereatur]] [[108:12|his fatherless offspring|pupillis ejus]], that is, the children of the Jews who were slain. For the Romans without mercy either killed them, or sold them, or grievously afflicted them.

paras.t: Fiant nati ejus in interitum, id est, filii populi hujus gladio, fame, et pestilentia pereant : quod factum fuit in obsidione Jerusalem a Romanis. In generatione una deleatur nomen ejus, id est, populus ille cum filiis suis infra tempus unius generationis deficiat. Hoc plane impletum est, quia post quadraginta circiter annos a Christi passione destructa est Jerosolyma, et populus ejus deletus est a principe et exercitu Romanorum, quemadmodum in Daniele prophetatum agnoscimus : Post hebdomadas, inquit, sexaginta duas occidetur Christus, et non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est ; et civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo.
paras.en: [[108:13|May his posterity be cut off|Fiant nati ejus in interitum]], that is, may the children of this people perish by sword, famine and pestilence: which was done in the siege of Jerusalem by the Romans. [[108:13|In one generation may his name be blotted out|In generatione una deleatur nomen ejus]], that is, may that people with its children come to an end within the space of one generation. This was plainly fulfilled, for about forty years after the Passion of Christ Jerusalem was destroyed, and its people blotted out by the prince and army of the Romans, as we know was prophesied in Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|After|Post hebdomadas]], he says, [[Dan 9:26|sixty-two weeks Christ shall be slain: and the people that shall deny him shall not be his|sexaginta duas occidetur Christus, et non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est]]; [[Dan 9:26|And a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary|et civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo]].

paras.t: In memoriam redeat iniquitas patrum ejus, id est, peccatum in Christum commissum a patribus Judæorum, qui erant tempore Titi, recolatur in conspectu Domini, id est coram Deo : ita quod puniatur non solum in patribus qui Christum occiderunt, et tempore Titi pro majori parte defuncti fuerunt, sed etiam in filiis, patrum infidelitatem et culpas sectantibus, quatenus impleatur quod patres horum filiorum coram Pilato clamabant : Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros. Et peccatum matris ejus, id est infidelis Synagogæ, non deleatur. Quoniam ipsa non pœnitet, idcirco in præsenti vita punitur temporaliter, et in inferno æternaliter. Unde Christus de eis ait per Osee : Non addam ut diligam eos.
paras.en: [[108:14|May the iniquity of his fathers be remembered|In memoriam redeat iniquitas patrum ejus]], that is, may the sin committed against Christ by the fathers of the Jews who lived in the time of Titus be recalled [[108:14|in the sight of the Lord|in conspectu Domini]], that is, before God: so that it be punished not only in the fathers who slew Christ, and who for the greater part had died by the time of Titus, but also in the children who follow the unbelief and the faults of their fathers; so that what the fathers of these children cried out before Pilate may be fulfilled: [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]]. [[108:14|And let not the sin of his mother|Et peccatum matris ejus]], that is, of the unbelieving Synagogue, [[108:14|be blotted out|non deleatur]]. Since she does not repent, she is therefore punished temporally in the present life, and eternally in hell. Hence Christ says of them through Osee: [[Osee 9:15|I will love them no more|Non addam ut diligam eos]].

paras.t: Sed quum in Ezechiele Dominus dicat, Non erit vobis istud in proverbium, Patres comederunt uvam acerbam, et dentes filiorum obstupuerunt ; et iterum, Anima quæ peccaverit, ipsa morietur, filius non portabit iniquitatem patris, et pater non portabit iniquitatem filii : quæri potest, quomodo peccatum Judæorum vindicatur in filiis. Et respondendum, quod duplex est pœna, videlicet temporalis et æterna. Iterum, quædam est pœna inferens damnum in spiritualibus bonis, alia vero est pœna damni corporalis. Dum ergo filii non imitantur peccata parentum, non puniuntur pro peccato illorum pœna æternali aut spirituale nocumentum inferenti, videlicet gratiæ subtractionem in præsenti, aut gloriæ in futuro ; dum vero peccatum parentum sequuntur, puniuntur tali, quali et illi, et interdum graviori. Porro dum filii non imitantur peccata parentum, puniuntur quandoque pro peccato parentum pœna temporali et corporale nocumentum inferenti, eo quod filius sit aliquid suorum parentum, tanquam de eorum substantia natus : quemadmodum pomum pendens in arbore, est aliquid arboris. Nec hoc injustum putetur, præsertim quum secundum leges humanas unus hoc modo puniatur pro culpa alterius : sicut propter crimen læsæ majestatis a patre commissum, filius ejus hereditate privatur. Et ex hoc innotescit, quomodo intelligendum sit quod in Exodi libro Dominus ait : Ego sum Dominus Deus tuus, fortis, zelotes, visitans iniquitatem patrum in filios, in tertiam et quartam generationem eorum qui me oderunt. Quod in eodem libro Moyses clarius dicit, loquens ad Dominum : Dominator Domine, nullus apud te per se innocens est, qui reddis iniquitatem patrum filiis ac nepotibus in tertiam et quartam progeniem. Unde et apud Jeremiam inducitur : Domine Deus, tu reddis iniquitatem patrum in sinum filiorum post eos.
paras.en: But since in Ezechiel the Lord says, [[Ezech 18:3|this parable shall be no more to you a proverb|Non erit vobis istud in proverbium]]: [[Ezech 18:2|The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge|Patres comederunt uvam acerbam, et dentes filiorum obstupuerunt]]; and again, [[Ezech 18:20|The soul that sinneth, the same shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, and the father shall not bear the iniquity of the son|Anima quæ peccaverit, ipsa morietur, filius non portabit iniquitatem patris, et pater non portabit iniquitatem filii]]: it may be asked how the sin of the Jews is avenged in their children. And the answer must be that punishment is twofold, namely temporal and eternal. Again, one punishment inflicts loss in spiritual goods, while another is a punishment of bodily loss. So when children do not imitate the sins of their parents, they are not punished for their parents' sin with eternal punishment, or with one that inflicts spiritual harm, namely the withdrawal of grace in the present or of glory in the future; but when they follow the sin of their parents, they are punished with such punishment as they were, and sometimes with heavier. Further, when children do not imitate the sins of their parents, they are sometimes punished for their parents' sin with a temporal punishment, one that inflicts bodily harm, because a son is something of his parents, as born of their substance: just as an apple hanging on a tree is something of the tree. Nor let this be thought unjust, especially since by human laws one man is punished in this way for another's fault: as when, for the crime of high treason [*læsa majestas*, an offence against the sovereign] committed by the father, his son is deprived of his inheritance. And from this it becomes clear how we are to understand what the Lord says in the book of Exodus: [[Ex 20:5|I am the Lord thy God, mighty, jealous, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me|Ego sum Dominus Deus tuus, fortis, zelotes, visitans iniquitatem patrum in filios, in tertiam et quartam generationem eorum qui me oderunt]]. Which Moses says more clearly in the same book, speaking to the Lord: [[Ex 34:6|O the Lord, the Lord|Dominator Domine]], [[Ex 34:7|no man of himself is innocent before thee. Who renderest the iniquity of the fathers to the children, and to the grandchildren unto the third and fourth generation|nullus apud te per se innocens est, qui reddis iniquitatem patrum filiis ac nepotibus in tertiam et quartam progeniem]]. Hence it is also set down in Jeremias: [[Jer 32:17|O Lord God|Domine Deus]], thou [[Jer 32:18|returnest the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them|reddis iniquitatem patrum in sinum filiorum post eos]].

paras.t: Fiant contra Dominum semper, id est, Judæi omni tempore contra Christum, Regem regum et Dominum dominorum, superbiant, et infideles permaneant. Hoc videmus impletum, quoniam pene omnes obstinati sunt. Propter quod Propheta testatur : Domus Israel cecidit, non adjiciet ut resurgat. Et dispereat de terra Ecclesiæ militantis ac triumphantis memoria eorum, scilicet Judæorum, eo modo quo sacra Scriptura multoties perhibet perire memoriam malignorum, videlicet quantum ad bonum et utilitatem. Sic enim perit impiorum memoria, quia non est eorum commemoratio revolvenda in bonum eorum. Nihilo minus quosdam fecit famosos singularis ac summa eorum malitia, sicut Judæos qui Christum occiderunt. Justorum autem memoria manet in bono. Unde in libro Proverbiorum scriptum est : Memoria justi cum laudibus, et nomen impiorum putrescet.
paras.en: [[108:15|May they be before the Lord continually|Fiant contra Dominum semper]] [the Latin *contra Dominum* can mean "before the Lord" or "against the Lord"; Denis takes it in the second sense], that is, may the Jews at all times be proud against Christ, the King of kings and Lord of lords, and remain unbelieving. This we see fulfilled, since almost all of them are obstinate. For which reason the Prophet testifies: [[Amos 5:1|The house of Israel is fallen, and it shall rise no more|Domus Israel cecidit, non adjiciet ut resurgat]]. [[108:15|And let the memory of them perish|Et dispereat]] [[108:15|from the earth|de terra]] of the Church militant and triumphant, the memory, that is, of them, namely of the Jews: in the way in which Holy Scripture often declares that the memory of the wicked perishes, namely as regards good and profit. For thus the memory of the wicked perishes, because their remembrance is not to be recalled to their own good. Nevertheless their singular and supreme wickedness has made some of them famous, as the Jews who slew Christ. But the memory of the just remains in good. Hence it is written in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 10:7|The memory of the just is with praises: and the name of the wicked shall rot|Memoria justi cum laudibus, et nomen impiorum putrescet]].

paras.t: Pro eo quod non est recordatus populus iste et Judas, facere misericordiam cum Domino Salvatore : imo maximam crudelitatem fecerunt in eum, secundum quod sequitur.
paras.en: [[108:16|Because he remembered not|Pro eo quod non est recordatus]], this people and Judas, [[108:16|to shew mercy|facere misericordiam]] to the Lord the Saviour: nay, they did the greatest cruelty to him, as follows.

paras.t: Et persecutus est hominem inopem et mendicum, id est Christum qui duxit in hoc mundo vitam pauperrimam, juxta quod ipsemet ait apud Matthæum : Vulpes foveas habent, et volucres cœli nidos ; Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput suum reclinet. Et sicut Lucas testatur, quædam religiosæ mulieres ministrabant ei de facultatibus suis. Unde Jeremias, Christum in primo suo adventu in omni paupertate fuisse victurum, Spiritu Sancto revelante cognoscens, miratus est valde, alloquens eum his verbis: Quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum? Sic quoque describit eum Zacharias primo fuisse futurum: Exsulta, inquiens, filia Sion, quia rex tuus venit tibi justus et salvator, ipse pauper et ascendens super asinam. Multum igitur errant Judæi, qui præstolantur Messiam in primo suo adventu in tanta majestate venturum, quod totius mundi monarchiam obtineat, universaque regna eis subjiciat.
paras.en: [[108:17|But persecuted the poor man and the beggar|Et persecutus est hominem inopem et mendicum]], that is, Christ, who led a life of the utmost poverty in this world, as he himself says in Matthew: [[Matt 8:20|The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head|Vulpes foveas habent, et volucres cœli nidos ; Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput suum reclinet]]. And as Luke testifies, certain devout women [[Luke 8:3|ministered unto him of their substance|ministrabant ei de facultatibus suis]]. Hence Jeremias, knowing by the revelation of the Holy Ghost that Christ at his first coming would live in all poverty, wondered greatly, and addressed him in these words: [[Jer 14:8|why wilt thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man turning in to lodge?|Quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum?]] So too Zacharias describes what he was to be at first: [[Zach 9:9|Rejoice|Exsulta]], he says, [[Zach 9:9|O daughter of Sion|filia Sion]], for thy king [[Zach 9:9|will come to thee, the just and saviour: he is poor, and riding upon an ass|venit tibi justus et salvator, ipse pauper et ascendens super asinam]]. The Jews, then, are greatly mistaken who wait for the Messias to come at his first coming in such majesty that he will gain the monarchy of the whole world and subject all kingdoms to them.

paras.t: Et compunctum corde mortificare: id est, populus Judæorum persequendo conatus est occidere Christum mente afflictum ex compassione errantium, et propter ingratitudinem Judæorum, ad quorum salutem specialiter missus fuit. Unde apud Joannem dicunt: Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit.
paras.en: [[108:17|and the broken in heart, to put him to death|Et compunctum corde mortificare]]: that is, the people of the Jews, by persecuting him, strove to kill Christ, who was afflicted in mind out of compassion for those in error, and because of the ingratitude of the Jews, for whose salvation especially he was sent[[Matt 15:24||]]. Hence in John they say: [[John 19:7|We have a law; and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God|Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit]].

paras.t: Et dilexit tam Judas quam populus sibi consentiens, maledictionem, non sub ratione maledictionis: nullus enim respiciens ad malum operatur, secundum Dionysium, nec malum sub ratione mali appetitur. Sed dilexit maledictionem, id est causam pro qua maledictio eis superinducta est, scilicet culpam, et facto suo ostendit se id amare, quod vel maledictio est, vel maledictionis origo. Et veniet ei maledictio concupita: nam a Romanis atrocissime opprimebantur. Et noluit populus iste et Judas, benedictionem, id est fidem, doctrinam et gratiam Christi, et elongabitur ab eo, quia non infundetur cordi eorum.
paras.en: [[108:18|And he loved|Et dilexit]], both Judas and the people that consented with him, [[108:18|cursing|maledictionem]]; not under the aspect of a curse [*sub ratione maledictionis*: that is, not loving it precisely as a curse]: for no one acts with his eye on evil, according to Dionysius [the margin gives *On the Divine Names*, ch. 4], nor is evil desired under the aspect of evil. But he loved cursing, that is, the cause for which the curse was brought upon them, namely guilt; and by his deed he showed that he loved what is either a curse or the origin of a curse. [[108:18|and it shall come unto him|Et veniet ei]], the curse he longed for: for they were most cruelly oppressed by the Romans. [[108:18|and he would not have|Et noluit]], this people and Judas, [[108:18|blessing|benedictionem]], that is, the faith, doctrine and grace of Christ, [[108:18|and it shall be far from him|et elongabitur ab eo]], because it will not be poured into their hearts.

paras.t: Et induit maledictionem sicut vestimentum: id est, peccatum pro quo infligitur maledictio, circumdedit populum istum ac Judam, atque operuit eum, sicut vestis circumdat operitque vestitum. Propterea Osee: Circumdederunt, inquit, eos adinventiones suæ, coram facie mea factæ sunt. Et intravit sicut aqua in interiora ejus: id est, peccatum istud per consensum ingressum est corda populi hujus; vel ipsa maledictio, scilicet dolor inflictus, intravit sicut aqua, id est copiose atque faciliter, in interiora ejus, quia non solum corpore, sed etiam mente affligebantur ab æmulis; et sicut oleum in ossibus ejus: id est, sicut oleum ossa corporis refocillat, lenit, atque delectat; sic isti in suo peccato gloriati sunt, et propria malignitate nutriti.
paras.en: [[108:18|And he put on cursing, like a garment|Et induit maledictionem sicut vestimentum]]: that is, the sin for which the curse is inflicted surrounded this people and Judas and covered him, as a garment surrounds and covers the one who wears it. Therefore Osee says: [[Osee 7:2|their own devices|adinventiones suæ]] [[Osee 7:2|have beset them about|Circumdederunt]], [[Osee 7:2|they have been done before my face|coram facie mea factæ sunt]]. [[108:18|and it went in like water into his entrails|Et intravit sicut aqua in interiora ejus]]: that is, that sin entered the hearts of this people by consent; or the curse itself, namely the pain inflicted, went in like water, that is, abundantly and easily, into his entrails, because they were afflicted by their enemies not only in body but also in mind; [[108:18|and like oil in his bones|et sicut oleum in ossibus ejus]]: that is, as oil refreshes, soothes and delights the bones of the body, so these men gloried in their sin and were fed by their own malice.

paras.t: Fiat ei sicut vestimentum quo operitur: id est, undique cadat super eos persecutio dura, et peccatum ipsorum vertatur ipsis in pœnas gravissimas; et sicut zona qua semper præcingitur: id est, maledictione sua capiatur hic populus, et usque in finem sæculi captivitate sua ligetur.
paras.en: [[108:19|May it be unto him like a garment which covereth him|Fiat ei sicut vestimentum quo operitur]]: that is, may harsh persecution fall upon them from every side, and may their sin be turned for them into most grievous punishments; [[108:19|and like a girdle with which he is girded continually|et sicut zona qua semper præcingitur]]: that is, may this people be held fast by its own curse, and be bound by its captivity until the end of the world.

paras.t: Hoc opus eorum, id est, ista est pœna et maledictio Judæorum, qui detrahunt mihi apud Dominum, id est Deo sciente et attendente, quem nil latet; et qui loquuntur mala adversus animam meam, id est, qui mala culpæ mihi imponunt, et mala pœnæ mihi inferre deposcunt, dicentes illud Lucæ, Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram, et prohibentem tributa dari Cæsari, et dicentem se Christum regem esse; illud quoque quod apud Joannem clamant, Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum.
paras.en: [[108:20|This is the work of them|Hoc opus eorum]], that is, this is the punishment and curse of the Jews, [[108:20|who detract me before the Lord|qui detrahunt mihi apud Dominum]], that is, while God, from whom nothing is hidden, knows and gives heed; [[108:20|and who speak evils against my soul|et qui loquuntur mala adversus animam meam]], that is, who lay upon me the evils of guilt and demand that the evils of punishment be brought upon me [the scholastic *malum culpæ* and *malum pœnæ*: the evil of sin and the evil of penalty], saying that of Luke: [[Luke 23:2|We have found this man perverting our nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar and saying that he is Christ the king|Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram, et prohibentem tributa dari Cæsari, et dicentem se Christum regem esse]]; and also what they cry out in John: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]].

paras.t: Deinde Christus orat Patrem. Et tu, Domine, Domine, fac mecum, id est, da mihi quod postulo, propter nomen tuum, id est propter te ipsum et nominis tui honorem, resuscitando me a mortuis; quia suavis est misericordia tua, id est, dulciter sapit electis misericordia tua, qua tot, tanta ac talia pro hominum salute fecisti.
paras.en: Then Christ prays to the Father. [[108:21|But thou, O Lord, do with me|Et tu, Domine, Domine, fac mecum]] [the Latin has *Domine, Domine*, "Lord, Lord", where the Douay-Rheims gives the word once], that is, give me what I ask, [[108:21|for thy name's sake|propter nomen tuum]], that is, for thine own sake and for the honour of thy name, by raising me from the dead; [[108:21|because thy mercy is sweet|quia suavis est misericordia tua]], that is, thy mercy is sweet to the taste of the elect, the mercy by which thou hast done so many, so great and such things for the salvation of men.

paras.t: Ecce quam dulcis, decorus, industriosus ac sententiosus versiculus: in quo nomen Domini iteratur, ut accendatur affectus; in quo Deus rogatur, propter se ipsum agere id pro quo oratur, non propter merita alicujus. Et ad hoc adjicitur ratio: quia suavis est misericordia ejus. Justitia namque ejus terribilis est.
paras.en: See how sweet, comely, skilful and weighty a little verse this is: in it the name of the Lord is repeated, that the affection may be kindled; in it God is asked to do for his own sake what is prayed for, not for anyone's merits. And to this the reason is added: because his mercy is sweet. For his justice is terrible[[2 Mach 1:24||]].

paras.t: Libera me per resurrectionem beatam ab omni corporis passibilitate ac persecutione, quia egenus, id est opem a te requirens, secundum quod homo sum, et pauper ego sum: sicut nunc patuit. Unde Apostolus: Scitis, inquit, gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quia quum dives esset, propter nos pauper factus est, ut nos inopia illius divites essemus.
paras.en: [[108:21|Do thou deliver me|Libera me]] [in the Douay-Rheims these words close v. 21; in the Vulgate they open v. 22] by a blessed resurrection from all passibility [that is, liability to suffering] of the body and from persecution, [[108:22|For I am poor|quia egenus]], that is, seeking help from thee, inasmuch as I am man, [[108:22|and needy|et pauper ego sum]]: as has now been shown. Hence the Apostle: [[2 Cor 8:9|you know|Scitis]], he says, [[2 Cor 8:9|the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that being rich he became poor for your sakes: that through his poverty you might be rich|gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quia quum dives esset, propter nos pauper factus est, ut nos inopia illius divites essemus]] [the margin gives only II Cor. viii].

paras.t: Et cor meum humanum, non mens divina, conturbatum est intra me, id est vehementer affectum dolore, timore, tristitia, ita ut dicerem : Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem. Hinc enim, ut est apud Joannem, dixit : Nunc anima mea turbata est, et quid dicam ? Sed quæri potest, quomodo turbatio Christo conveniat, quum ipse apud eumdem Evangelistam Apostolis dixerit, Non turbetur cor vestrum, neque formidet. Et respondendum, quod turbatio interdum importat deordinationem, seu immoderatam cordis affectionem : et ita in Christo non fuit ; sicque reprobatur ab eo. Interdum vero designat vehementem animi affectionem, ex aliqua præcipua consideratione aut causa : et ita fuit in Christo, tamen sponte assumpta ex prævia ratione, juxta illud Joannis : Jesus infremuit spiritu, et turbavit se ipsum.
paras.en: [[108:22|and my heart|Et cor meum]], my human heart, not the divine mind, [[108:22|is troubled within me|conturbatum est intra me]], that is, vehemently moved with sorrow, fear and sadness, so that I said: [[Matt 26:38|My soul is sorrowful even unto death|Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem]]. For hence, as we read in John, he said: [[John 12:27|Now is my soul troubled. And what shall I say|Nunc anima mea turbata est, et quid dicam]]? But it may be asked how trouble befits Christ, since he himself, in the same Evangelist, said to the Apostles: [[John 14:27|Let not your heart be troubled: nor let it be afraid|Non turbetur cor vestrum, neque formidet]]. The answer is that trouble sometimes implies disorder, that is, an immoderate affection of the heart: in this sense it was not in Christ, and in this sense he condemns it. But sometimes it means a vehement affection of the soul arising from some particular consideration or cause: in this sense it was in Christ, yet taken on freely, with reason going before, according to that of John: Jesus [[John 11:33|groaned in the spirit and troubled himself|infremuit spiritu, et turbavit se ipsum]].

paras.t: Sicut umbra quum declinat ad occasum ac tenebras, cito aufertur ac deficit ; ita ego ablatus sum de vita corporali et consortio discipulorum, affixus cruci, moriensque in ea velociter : prout in Marco scriptum est, Mirabatur Pilatus si jam obiisset. Et excussus sum de manu et persecutionibus Judæorum, in die resurrectionis meæ : quia tunc in corpore immortali surrexi, atque ab omni pœnalitate me ipsum excussi; sicut locustæ, quæ evolant, ne detineantur ab aliquo. Vel, Excussus sum, fugiendo de loco ad locum propter persecutiones adversariorum meorum. Nam in infantia a facie Herodis ingrediebar Ægyptum, Judæorum quoque persecutionem subinde declinavi, sicut locustæ, quæ de loco ad locum transiliunt.
paras.en: [[108:23|like the shadow when it declineth|Sicut umbra quum declinat]] towards its setting and darkness, is quickly taken away and fails, so [[108:23|I am taken away|ablatus sum]] from bodily life and from the company of the disciples, fastened to the cross and dying on it quickly: as it is written in Mark, [[Mark 15:44|Pilate wondered that he should be already dead|Mirabatur Pilatus si jam obiisset]]. [[108:23|and I am shaken off|Et excussus sum]] from the hand and the persecutions of the Jews, on the day of my resurrection: for then I rose in an immortal body and shook myself free of all liability to punishment; [[108:23|as locusts|sicut locustæ]], which fly off so as not to be held by anyone. Or, I am shaken off, by fleeing from place to place because of the persecutions of my adversaries. For in infancy I went into Egypt from the face of Herod[[Matt 2:14||]] [the margin gives Matt. ii, 13–15], and time and again I avoided the persecution of the Jews[[John 8:59||]][[John 11:54||]][[John 12:36||]], as locusts, which leap from place to place.

paras.t: Genua mea infirmata sunt a jejunio. Quamvis quidam existiment, hoc ad litteram non competere Christo, et ideo exponendum esse de membris ejus hoc modo, Genua mea, id est Apostoli qui alios sustentare debuerant suo exemplo, infirmata sunt tempore passionis meæ, a jejunio, id est ex defectu spiritualis refectionis, quoniam donum fortitudinis nondum perfecte gustaverunt aut receperunt, sed omnes (ut Evangelista narrat) dispersi sunt atque fugerunt ; videtur tamen non esse absurdum, si asseramus Christum ex jejunio in genibus proprii corporis infirmatum seu debilitatum. Jejunavit enim continuo quadraginta diebus et noctibus, et postea esuriit, ex attenuatione corporis. Esuries autem fatigationem facit in corpore, quæ sentiri de facili solet in genibus. Denique, cur inconvenientius est, dicere Christum ex jejunio genibus infirmatum, quam ex aliis laboribus corpore fatigatum ? Est autem ex laboribus fatigatus, juxta illud : Jesus fatigatus ex itinere, sedebat super fontem. Assumpsit namque indetrahibiles defectus, secundum Damascenum, quales sunt fames, sitis, fatigatio, timor et dolor naturales atque consimiles.
paras.en: [[108:24|My knees are weakened through fasting|Genua mea infirmata sunt a jejunio]]. Some think that this does not fit Christ literally, and so must be expounded of his members in this way: My knees, that is, the Apostles, who ought to have upheld others by their example, were weakened at the time of my passion, through fasting, that is, through want of spiritual refreshment, since they had not yet perfectly tasted or received the gift of fortitude, but all (as the Evangelist relates) were scattered and fled[[Matt 26:56||]]. Yet it seems not absurd for us to assert that Christ was weakened or enfeebled in the knees of his own body through fasting. For he fasted without a break [[Matt 4:2|forty days and forty nights, afterwards he was hungry|quadraginta diebus et noctibus, et postea esuriit]], from the wasting of his body. And hunger brings weariness on the body, and this is commonly felt most readily in the knees. Lastly, why is it less fitting to say that Christ was weakened in the knees through fasting than that he was wearied in body by other labours?
