And he was wearied by labours, according to that text: [[John 4:6|Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well|Jesus fatigatus ex itinere, sedebat super fontem]]. For he took on the blameless defects [*indetrahibiles*: the natural weaknesses of human nature that imply no sin], according to Damascene, such as hunger, thirst, weariness, natural fear and pain, and the like.

paras.t: Et caro mea immutata est a naturali vigore ad famis defectum, seu maciem quamdam, propter oleum, id est ex defectu cibi conditi. Unde translatio Hieronymi talis est : Caro mea macilenta est absque oleo. Veritas autem Hebraica habet sic : Caro mea macilenta est a pinguedine, id est ex defectu pinguedinis. Christus namque in juventute habuit corpus convenienter carnosum et plenum, quoniam sanguineæ et optimæ fuerat complexionis, tanquam ex purissimis sanguinibus sanctæ Virginis habens corpus sumptum, atque a Spiritu Sancto formatum ; sed postmodum propter diversos labores vigiliarum, jejuniorum, viarum, attenuatum erat in tantum, ut Christus videretur senior quam erat. Propter quod dixerunt ad eum Judæi : Quinquaginta annos nondum habes. Licet enim non haberet ultra triginta tres annos, videbatur tamen satis plus habere de senio. Hæc dicta sint non pertinaciter asserendo, sed pie opinando.
paras.en: [[108:24|and my flesh is changed|Et caro mea immutata est]] from its natural vigour to the faintness of hunger, or a certain leanness, [[108:24|for oil|propter oleum]], that is, through want of seasoned food. Hence Jerome's translation runs thus: My flesh is lean without oil. But the Hebrew truth [that is, the Hebrew original] has it thus: My flesh is lean from fatness, that is, from want of fatness. For in his youth Christ had a body fittingly fleshy and full, since he was of a sanguine and most excellent complexion [that is, temperament, in the medical sense of the balance of the humours], as having a body taken from the most pure blood of the holy Virgin and formed by the Holy Ghost; but afterwards, through his various labours of watchings, fastings and journeys, it was so worn down that Christ seemed older than he was. That is why the Jews said to him: [[John 8:57|Thou art not yet fifty years old|Quinquaginta annos nondum habes]]. For though he was not more than thirty-three years old, he seemed to have a good deal more of age. Let these things be said not by way of stubborn assertion, but as a devout opinion.

paras.t: Et ego factus sum opprobrium illis. Sæpe enim deriserunt Christum Judæi, præsertim in passione, secundum quod dictum est supra : Ego autem sum vermis et non homo, opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis. Viderunt me pendentem in cruce, et moverunt capita sua, congratulantes de mea miseria, sicut scriptum est: Prætereuntes autem blasphemabant eum, moventes capita sua, et dicentes: Vah! qui destruis templum Dei.
paras.en: [[108:25|And I am become a reproach to them|Et ego factus sum opprobrium illis]]. For the Jews often mocked Christ, especially in his passion, according to what was said above: [[Ps 21:7|But I am a worm, and no man: the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people|Ego autem sum vermis et non homo, opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis]]. [[108:25|they saw me|Viderunt me]] hanging on the cross, [[108:25|and they shaked their heads|et moverunt capita sua]], rejoicing together over my misery, as it is written: [[Matt 27:39|And they that passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads|Prætereuntes autem blasphemabant eum, moventes capita sua]], [[Matt 27:40|And saying: Vah, thou that destroyest the temple of God|et dicentes: Vah! qui destruis templum Dei]].

paras.t: Adjuva me: in passione, secundum quod homo sum, et humanitati meæ adsiste, eique in omnibus cooperare. Petiit autem se Christus homo juvari a Deo, non quod timeret se posse peccare, sed ut divina virtute prævaleret in prælio. Propter quod ait: Dominus Deus auxiliator meus; itemque, Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis. Salvum me fac a morte ac mortalitate, secundum misericordiam tuam. Cur non ait, Secundum justitiam tuam? Potuit utique utrumque dicere: sed ut nos suo exemplo doceret nunquam de propria perfectione præsumere, magis autem in Dei pietate incessanter sperare; ideo dixit, Salvum me fac secundum misericordiam tuam; et item, quia in omni opere Dei misericordia commiscetur; itemque, quoniam omnis virtus et gratia Christi sola misericordia Dei concessa est animæ ejus.
paras.en: [[108:26|Help me|Adjuva me]] in my passion, inasmuch as I am man, and stand by my humanity and work together with it in all things. Now Christ as man asked to be helped by God, not because he feared that he could sin, but that he might prevail in the battle by divine power. Wherefore he says: [[Is 50:7|The Lord God is my helper|Dominus Deus auxiliator meus]] [the margin gives Is. i, 7, for l, 7]; and again: [[Jer 20:11|the Lord is with me as a strong warrior|Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis]]. [[108:26|save me|Salvum me fac]] from death and mortality, [[108:26|according to thy mercy|secundum misericordiam tuam]]. Why does he not say, According to thy justice? He could indeed have said either: but he said, [[108:26|save me; according to thy mercy|Salvum me fac secundum misericordiam tuam]], so as to teach us by his example never to presume on our own perfection, but rather to hope unceasingly in the goodness of God; and also because mercy is mingled in every work of God; and again because all the virtue and grace of Christ was granted to his soul by the mercy of God alone.

paras.t: Et sciant adversarii mei per experientiam suæ damnationis; boni quoque per annuntiationem evangelicæ veritatis, quia manus tua hæc, id est, quod ista salvatio ac resurrectio mea, est effectus tuæ divinæ virtutis, quæ sola potest mortuos suscitare, et tu, Domine, fecisti eam, id est prædictum effectum, scilicet resuscitationem meam.
paras.en: [[108:27|And let them know|Et sciant]], my adversaries by the experience of their damnation, and the good too by the preaching of the gospel truth, [[108:27|that this is thy hand|quia manus tua hæc]], that is, that this salvation and resurrection of mine is the effect of thy divine power, which alone can raise the dead, [[108:27|and that thou, O Lord, hast done it|et tu, Domine, fecisti eam]], that is, the effect just named, namely my raising up.

paras.t: Maledicent illi, et tu benedices. Increduli namque Judæi Christum blasphemaverunt ante passionem, in passione, et post passionem. Deus autem benedixit Christo homini, quantum ad præmium accidentale, et quantum ad mysticum corpus ipsius. Qui insurgunt in me, id est persecutores mei, confundantur, vel confusione temporali, erubescendo de suis sceleribus; vel confusione æterna, sentiendo tormenta, si modo non pœnitent. Unde per Jeremiam ait Salvator: Confundantur qui me persequuntur, et non confundar ego. Servus autem tuus lætabitur: id est, ego Filius tuus, qui formam servi accepi, et ut homo servus tuus sum, lætabor in te, erubescentibus atque pereuntibus illis.
paras.en: [[108:28|They will curse and thou wilt bless|Maledicent illi, et tu benedices]]. For the unbelieving Jews blasphemed Christ before his passion, in his passion and after his passion. But God blessed Christ as man as regards his accidental reward [that is, the joys added to his essential beatitude], and as regards his mystical body. [[108:28|let them that rise up against me|Qui insurgunt in me]], that is, my persecutors, [[108:28|be confounded|confundantur]], either with temporal confusion, blushing for their crimes, or with eternal confusion, feeling torments, if they do not repent. Hence the Saviour says by Jeremias: [[Jer 17:18|Let them be confounded that persecute me, and let not me be confounded|Confundantur qui me persequuntur, et non confundar ego]] [the margin gives Jer. xxii, 18; the words are Jer 17:18]. [[108:28|but thy servant shall rejoice|Servus autem tuus lætabitur]]: that is, I thy Son, who took [[Phil 2:7|the form of a servant|formam servi]], and as man am thy servant, shall rejoice in thee, while they blush and perish.

paras.t: Induantur, id est, undique operiantur, qui detrahunt mihi, pudore: ita quod erubescant de sua detractione, vel ad pœnitentiam salutarem, vel per damnationem æternam; et operiantur sicut diploide, id est velut duplici veste, confusione sua: ita quod coram Deo atque hominibus erubescant; imo sic, quod nunc eorum confusio ac pœna incipiant, et in futuro æternaliter durent. Quorumdam enim pœna nunc inchoatur, in futuroque sæculo sine fine continuatur; electorum vero castigatio modo incipit, et postea finem sortitur.
paras.en: [[108:29|Let them that detract me|qui detrahunt mihi]] [[108:29|be clothed|Induantur]], that is, be covered on every side, [[108:29|with shame|pudore]]: so that they may blush for their detraction, either unto saving penance or through eternal damnation; [[108:29|and let them be covered|et operiantur]] [[108:29|as with a double cloak|sicut diploide]], that is, as with a twofold garment, [[108:29|with their confusion|confusione sua]]: so that they may blush before God and men; nay rather, so that their confusion and punishment may begin now and last eternally hereafter. For the punishment of some begins now and is continued without end in the world to come; but the chastisement of the elect begins now and afterwards comes to an end.

paras.t: Hæc autem in Judæis manifeste implentur. Nam a tempore destructionis et expulsionis eorum tempore Titi, usque in præsentem diem, vagi et exules sunt, et adversariorum suorum ditioni subduntur, variisque pœnis ac confusionibus afficiuntur: nec tamen emendantur ex hoc; sed pœna eorum nunc incipit, et postmodum in perpetuum perseverat. Propter quod de eis conscriptum est: Duplici contritione contere eos, Domine Deus noster. Porro prophetia ista de confusione Judæorum tunc summe implebitur, quando videbunt in quem compunxerunt, puta in die judicii. Tunc enim judicabuntur a Christo quem judicaverunt, et conspicient quem occiderunt.
paras.en: Now these things are plainly fulfilled in the Jews. For from the time of their destruction and expulsion in the days of Titus until the present day they are wanderers and exiles, subject to the power of their adversaries, and afflicted with various punishments and confusions: and yet they are not amended by this; but their punishment begins now and afterwards continues for ever. That is why it is written of them: [[Jer 17:18|with a double destruction, destroy them|Duplici contritione contere eos]], O Lord our God. Moreover this prophecy of the confusion of the Jews will be fulfilled to the full when they shall see him whom they pierced[[Apoc 1:7||]] [Denis's words, *videbunt in quem compunxerunt*, are nearest John 19:37, "They shall look on him whom they pierced"], that is, on the day of judgement. For then they will be judged by Christ whom they judged, and will behold him whom they slew.

paras.t: Confitebor Domino nimis, id est devotissime, in ore meo, ipsum laudando de omnibus bonis mihi collatis; et in medio multorum, id est inter fideles seu in Ecclesia, laudabo eum de bonitate ipsius et propria perfectione ejus in semetipso. Hoc Christus post resurrectionem fecit, quando discipulis suis apparuit, stansque in medio eorum dixit: Pax vobis; sicut misit me vivens Pater, et ego mitto vos. Et: Non est vestrum scire tempora vel momenta, quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate. Sed et per se ipsum Christus ut homo, in cœlo empyreo incessabiliter nunc laudat Deum, seu sanctam Trinitatem, cum inexcogitabili reverentia cordis. In Ecclesia quoque militante laudat Deum per suos ministros, quos ad divinam laudem inducit.
paras.en: [[108:30|I will give great thanks to the Lord|Confitebor Domino nimis]], that is, most devoutly, [[108:30|with my mouth|in ore meo]], praising him for all the good things bestowed on me; [[108:30|and in the midst of many|et in medio multorum]], that is, among the faithful, or in the Church, [[108:30|I will praise him|laudabo eum]] for his goodness and for his own perfection in himself. This Christ did after the resurrection, when he appeared to his disciples and, standing in their midst, said: [[John 20:21|Peace be to you|Pax vobis]]; [[John 20:21|As the Father hath sent me, I also send you|sicut misit me vivens Pater, et ego mitto vos]] [Denis's *vivens*, "living", comes from John 6:58, "As the living Father hath sent me"]. And: [[Acts 1:7|It is not for you to know the time or moments, which the Father hath put in his own power|Non est vestrum scire tempora vel momenta, quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate]]. But Christ as man also, in his own person, now praises God, that is, the Holy Trinity, unceasingly in the empyrean heaven, with a reverence of heart beyond all thought. In the Church militant, too, he praises God through his ministers, whom he leads to the praise of God.

paras.t: Quia adstitit a dextris pauperis, id est, mihi pauperi in omni tribulatione paternaliter adfuit, nec unquam me dereliquit, sicut in Evangelio Joannis locutus sum : Non reliquit me Pater solum, quia ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper ; ut salvam faceret a persequentibus animam meam, id est, quatenus me ipsum seu vitam meam corporalem, salvaret de manibus Judæorum et crucifixorum meorum, resuscitando me tertio die a mortuis.
paras.en: [[108:31|Because he hath stood at the right hand of the poor|Quia adstitit a dextris pauperis]], that is, he stood by me, a poor man, like a father in every tribulation, and never forsook me, as I said in the Gospel of John: The Father [[John 8:29|hath not left me alone|Non reliquit me Pater solum]], for [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]]; [[108:31|to save my soul from persecutors|ut salvam faceret a persequentibus animam meam]], that is, to save me myself, or my bodily life, from the hands of the Jews and of those who crucified me, by raising me from the dead on the third day.

paras.t: In expositione psalmi præsentis, S. Hieronymus contra Judæos sic argumentatur : Respondete mihi, o Judæi. Fuistis in Babylonia, habuistis ibi Prophetas, Danielem, Ezechielem; septuaginta annis fuistis in captivitate illa, et postea venistis in propria. Ecce nunc quadringenti anni sunt (computa annos a Christo usque Hieronymum) : quare non est missus ad vos Propheta, et quare dereliquit vos Dominus? Tunc dereliquistis Dominum, et idola colebatis, et miserebatur vestri. Nunc quum non colitis idola, quare dereliquit vos Dominus ? Hucusque Hieronymus.
paras.en: In his exposition of the present psalm St. Jerome argues thus against the Jews: Answer me, O Jews. You were in Babylon; you had Prophets there, Daniel and Ezechiel; for seventy years you were in that captivity, and afterwards you came back to your own land. Behold, it is now four hundred years (reckon the years from Christ to Jerome): why has no Prophet been sent to you, and why has the Lord forsaken you? Then you forsook the Lord and worshipped idols, and he had mercy on you. Now, when you do not worship idols, why has the Lord forsaken you? Thus far Jerome.

paras.t: Sed ecce nunc amplius quam mille et quadringenti anni sunt, ex quo in ista captivitate fuerunt. Nec ad eos invenitur missus Propheta, nec aliquod signum certum, divinum ac evidens eis monstratum est, quo scire possint se pertinere ad populum Dei : imo non obstante quod apertissime demonstramus eis ad oculum hanc esse finalem captivitatem eorum propter peccatum eorum in Christum commissum, quemadmodum per Danielem inducitur : Non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est ; et finis ejus vastitas, et usque in finem perseverabit desolatio. Et per Osee : Dies multos sedebunt filii Israel sine rege, et sine principe, et sine sacrificio, et sine altari, et sine ephod, et sine theraphim ; et post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum (id est Messiam, ut omnes exponunt), et pavebunt ad Dominum, et ad bonum ejus in novissimo dierum. In hoc autem quod sanctus Osee perhibet eos postea reversuros ad Deum, et quæsituros Messiam, dat palam intelligere, quod illis multis diebus de quibus ipse loquitur, sedent sine Deo et Christo, id est sine vera fide et digno cultu Dei atque Messiæ. Vel ergo per dies illos multos, de quibus tractat Osee, intelligendi sunt dies hujus captivitatis, vel non. Si sic, constat quod modo sedeant sine Deo et Christo, tanquam infideles ac reprobi; si non, tunc restat una alia captivitas longior ista, quam nec ipsi exspectant. Quamvis ergo sit ita, non tamen volunt informari, credere, aut converti, quatenus sancti Prophetæ, qui eorum excæcationem et obstinationem prædixerunt, in hoc quoque inveniantur veraces. Vere enim pervenit super eos ira Dei usque in finem, et verificatur in eis quod Salomon dicit : Quem despicit Deus, hunc nullus corrigere potest.
paras.en: But behold, it is now more than fourteen hundred years that they have been in this captivity. And no Prophet is found to have been sent to them, nor has any sure, divine and evident sign been shown them by which they might know that they belong to the people of God: nay, even though we show them most plainly, before their very eyes, that this is their final captivity, on account of the sin they committed against Christ, as is set forth by Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|the people that shall deny him shall not be his|Non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est]]; [[Dan 9:26|and the end thereof shall be waste|et finis ejus vastitas]], [[Dan 9:27|and to the end|et usque in finem]] [[Dan 9:27|the desolation shall continue|perseverabit desolatio]]. And by Osee: [[Osee 3:4|the children of Israel shall sit many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without altar, and without ephod, and without theraphim|Dies multos sedebunt filii Israel sine rege, et sine principe, et sine sacrificio, et sine altari, et sine ephod, et sine theraphim]]; [[Osee 3:5|And after this the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the Lord, their God, and David, their king|et post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum]] (that is, the Messias, as all expound it), [[Osee 3:5|and they shall fear the Lord, and his goodness, in the last days|et pavebunt ad Dominum, et ad bonum ejus in novissimo dierum]]. Now in saying that they will afterwards return to God and seek the Messias, holy Osee gives us plainly to understand that in those many days of which he speaks they sit without God and without Christ, that is, without the true faith and the due worship of God and of the Messias. Either, then, the many days of which Osee treats are to be understood as the days of this captivity, or not. If so, it is plain that they now sit without God and Christ, as unbelievers and reprobates; if not, then there remains yet another captivity, longer than this one, which not even they expect. Yet though this is so, they will not be taught, believe or be converted; so that the holy Prophets, who foretold their blindness and obstinacy, may be found truthful in this too. For truly [[1 Thess 2:16|the wrath of God is come upon them to the end|pervenit super eos ira Dei usque in finem]], and in them is verified what Solomon says: [[Eccles 7:14|no man can correct whom he hath despised|Quem despicit Deus, hunc nullus corrigere potest]].

paras.t: Optime quoque nobilis noster Cassiodorus loquitur : Virgo peperit, Messias venit, Agnus immaculatus occisus est, Redemptor surrexit a mortuis, mundus audita credit : et adhuc Judæus simulat se nescire quod totus mundus agnovit. Præsta, Domine, obstinatis conversionem, obscuris lumen, incredulis fidem, ut pro quibus in cruce orasti, periclitantibus subvenire digneris. Nam quibus suadere justa non possumus, recte pro illis tibi, Domine, supplicamus.
paras.en: Our noble Cassiodorus, too, speaks excellently: The Virgin has given birth, the Messias has come, the immaculate Lamb has been slain, the Redeemer has risen from the dead, the world believes what it has heard: and still the Jew pretends not to know what the whole world has acknowledged. Grant, O Lord, conversion to the obstinate, light to the darkened, faith to the unbelieving, that thou mayest deign to succour in their peril those for whom thou didst pray on the cross[[Luke 23:34||]]. For those whom we cannot persuade to what is right, we rightly entreat thee, O Lord, on their behalf.

108.title_en: Moral exposition of the hundred and eighth psalm
108.note: The heading of this article (its number and title) is missing from the transcription; it awaits a scan of the page. The English title describes the article's contents.

paras.t: Quum Christus dicat, Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam quotidie, et sequatur me: mirum non est, si psalmi qui ad litteram de Christi passione loquuntur, de ejus Ecclesia seu quocumque fideli moraliter exponantur.
paras.en: Since Christ says, [[Luke 9:23|If any man will come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me|Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam quotidie, et sequatur me]], it is no wonder if the psalms which literally speak of Christ's passion are expounded morally of his Church, or of any faithful soul.

paras.t: Ecclesia igitur seu quilibet homo Christi vestigia digne sequens, contemnendo laudes humanas, et sustinendo persecutiones diversas, in propria persona Domino dicere potest: Deus, laudem meam ne tacueris: id est, tu propter quem honores et laudes temporales despicio, atque diversa sustineo, me in judicio approba, lauda et salva, dicendo: Euge, serve bone et fidelis, intra in gaudium Domini tui. Nec permittas ab aliis laudem meam taceri, quando ad ædificationem fit proximi, atque ad gloriam nominis tui. Quia os peccatoris et os dolosi super me apertum est, id est, verba superba et dolosa adversus me dicta sunt.
paras.en: The Church, then, or any man who worthily follows the footsteps of Christ, despising human praise and bearing persecutions of many kinds, can say to the Lord in his own person: [[108:2|O God, be not thou silent in my praise|Deus, laudem meam ne tacueris]]: that is, thou for whose sake I despise temporal honours and praises and bear many things, approve me, praise me and save me at the judgement, saying: [[Matt 25:23|Well done, good and faithful servant|Euge, serve bone et fidelis]], [[Matt 25:23|Enter thou into the joy of thy lord|intra in gaudium Domini tui]] [the margin gives Matth. xxv, 24, 23; the words stand in both Matt 25:21 and 25:23]. Nor suffer my praise to be kept silent by others, when it serves the edification of my neighbour and the glory of thy name; [[108:2|for the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful man is opened against me|Quia os peccatoris et os dolosi super me apertum est]], that is, proud and deceitful words have been spoken against me.

paras.t: Locuti sunt homines pravi adversum me lingua dolosa, proponendo mala sub specie boni, ut quem manifesta malitia fallere nequeunt, palliata æquitate decipiant: quod valde iniquum est, secundum quod per Isaiam inducitur: Fraudulenti vasa (id est verba) pessima sunt; ipse enim cogitationes concinnabat ad perdendos mites in sermone mendacii. Et Malachias: Maledictus, inquit, dolosus. Verumtamen vitium istud, proh dolor! nimis commune est. Propter quod Jeremias ait: Unusquisque se a proximo suo custodiat, et in omni fratre suo non habeat fiduciam, quia omnis frater supplantans supplantabit, et omnis amicus fraudulenter incedet, et vir fratrem suum deridebit. Hinc quoque scriptum est: Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem. Ab ea quæ dormit in sinu tuo, custodi claustra oris tui: quia inimici hominis, domestici ejus. Quum ergo sit ita, merito dicit Scriptura: Ne omni homini cor tuum reveles; et, Beatus qui invenit amicum verum.
paras.en: [[108:3|They have spoken|Locuti sunt]], that is, wicked men, [[108:3|against me with deceitful tongues|adversum me lingua dolosa]], setting forth evil things under the appearance of good, so that those whom open malice cannot mislead they may deceive with a cloak of fairness: which is very wicked, according to what is put forward through Isaias: [[Is 32:7|The vessels of the deceitful|Fraudulenti vasa]] (that is, words) [[Is 32:7|are most wicked: for he hath framed devices to destroy the meek, with lying words|pessima sunt; ipse enim cogitationes concinnabat ad perdendos mites in sermone mendacii]] [the margin gives Is. xxxiii, 7; the words stand in Is 32:7]. And Malachias: [[Mal 1:14|Cursed|Maledictus]], he says, [[Mal 1:14|is the deceitful man|dolosus]]. Yet this vice, alas, is all too common. Wherefore Jeremias says: [[Jer 9:4|Let every man take heed of his neighbour, and let him not trust in any brother of his: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every friend will walk deceitfully|Unusquisque se a proximo suo custodiat, et in omni fratre suo non habeat fiduciam, quia omnis frater supplantans supplantabit, et omnis amicus fraudulenter incedet]], [[Jer 9:5|And a man shall mock his brother|et vir fratrem suum deridebit]]. Hence also it is written: [[Mich 7:2|every one hunteth his brother to death|Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem]]; [[Mich 7:5|keep the doors of thy mouth from her that sleepeth in thy bosom|Ab ea quæ dormit in sinu tuo, custodi claustra oris tui]]: for [[Mich 7:6|a man's enemies are they of his own household|inimici hominis, domestici ejus]]. Since then it is so, rightly does Scripture say: [[Ecclus 8:22|Open not thy heart to every man|Ne omni homini cor tuum reveles]]; and, [[Ecclus 25:12|Blessed is he that findeth a true friend|Beatus qui invenit amicum verum]].

paras.t: Et sermonibus odii circumdederunt me, quærentes me a summo bono avertere: quod est odium pessimum. Sed non est nobis timendum ob hoc, quoniam Christus locutus est: Beati eritis, quum oderint vos homines, et quum separaverint vos, et exprobraverint, et ejecerint nomen vestrum tanquam malum propter Filium hominis. Et expugnaverunt me gratis. Hoc maxime Christi martyribus convenit, qui propter justitiam occidi digni fuerunt: sed et omnis qui propter justitiam patitur atque opprimitur, gratis, id est sine suo demerito, expugnatur.
paras.en: [[108:3|and they have compassed me about with words of hatred|Et sermonibus odii circumdederunt me]], seeking to turn me away from the highest good: which is the worst hatred. But we need not fear on this account, since Christ has said: [[Luke 6:22|Blessed shall you be when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you and shall reproach you and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake|Beati eritis, quum oderint vos homines, et quum separaverint vos, et exprobraverint, et ejecerint nomen vestrum tanquam malum propter Filium hominis]]. [[108:3|and have fought against me without cause|Et expugnaverunt me gratis]]. This fits above all the martyrs of Christ, who were counted worthy to be slain for justice; but also every one who suffers and is oppressed for justice is fought against without cause, that is, through no fault of his own.

paras.t: Pro eo ut me diligerent, detrahebant mihi. Hoc convenit bonis prælatis et fratribus, qui commissos seu proximos caritative ac juste corripiunt: propter quod amari deberent, quemadmodum scriptum est, Argue sapientem, et diliget te. Sed ipsi econtrario ab illis odio habentur, et oblocutiones patiuntur, prout dicit Scriptura: Odio habuerunt corripientem, et loquentem perfecte abominati sunt. Ego autem orabam pro ingratis et æmulis. Hoc est quod dicit Apostolus: Maledicimur, et benedicimus; blasphemamur, et obsecramus. Unde et alibi monet: Noli vinci a malo, sed vince in bono malum. Hoc est scutum patientiæ famulorum Christi, in omni injuriatione ad orationem recurrere: primo, pro semetipsis orando, ne a proprio animo superemur, et ad impatientiam moveamur, sed in omni adversitate constantes reddamur; secundo autem, orando pro adversariis, ut Deus eis ignoscat, gratiamque melioris vitæ infundat. De taliter patientibus Petrus ait: Qui patiuntur, inquit, secundum voluntatem Dei, fideli Creatori commendant animas suas. Unde et Christus ait: Si eos diligitis, qui vos diligunt, quam mercedem habebitis? Nonne et publicani hoc faciunt? Et si salutaveritis fratres vestros tantum, quid amplius facitis? Nonne et ethnici (id est gentiles et infideles) hoc faciunt?
paras.en: [[108:4|Instead of making me a return of love, they detracted me|Pro eo ut me diligerent, detrahebant mihi]]. This fits good prelates and brethren who correct those committed to them, or their neighbours, charitably and justly: for which they ought to be loved, as it is written, [[Prov 9:8|Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee|Argue sapientem, et diliget te]]. But they, on the contrary, are hated by them and suffer their abuse, as Scripture says: [[Amos 5:10|They have hated him that rebuketh|Odio habuerunt corripientem]], [[Amos 5:10|and have abhorred him that speaketh perfectly|et loquentem perfecte abominati sunt]]. [[108:4|but I gave myself to prayer|Ego autem orabam]] for the ungrateful and the envious. This is what the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 4:12|We are reviled: and we bless|Maledicimur, et benedicimus]]. [[1 Cor 4:13|We are blasphemed: and we entreat|blasphemamur, et obsecramus]]. Hence too he warns elsewhere: [[Rom 12:21|Be not overcome by evil: but overcome evil by good|Noli vinci a malo, sed vince in bono malum]]. This is the shield of patience of the servants of Christ: in every injury to have recourse to prayer; first, praying for ourselves, that we be not overcome by our own temper and moved to impatience, but be made steadfast in every adversity; and secondly, praying for our adversaries, that God may forgive them and pour into them the grace of a better life. Of those who suffer in this way Peter says: Let [[1 Pet 4:19|them also that suffer|Qui patiuntur]], he says, [[1 Pet 4:19|according to the will of God|secundum voluntatem Dei]] [[1 Pet 4:19|commend their souls|commendant animas suas]] [[1 Pet 4:19|to the faithful Creator|fideli Creatori]]. Hence Christ too says: [[Matt 5:46|if you love them that love you, what reward shall you have? do not even the publicans this?|Si eos diligitis, qui vos diligunt, quam mercedem habebitis? Nonne et publicani hoc faciunt?]] [[Matt 5:47|And if you salute your brethren only, what do you more? do not also the heathens|Et si salutaveritis fratres vestros tantum, quid amplius facitis? Nonne et ethnici]] (that is, the Gentiles and unbelievers) [[Matt 5:47|this?|hoc faciunt?]]

paras.t: Constitue super eum peccatorem, et diabolus stet a dextris ejus. Quum judicatur, exeat condemnatus, etc. Mirum videtur, quomodo nunc tanta imprecentur adversario justi, ab ipso justo, qui immediate prædixit se orasse pro æmulo. Sciendum ergo, quod verba ista atque similia, quibus videtur malum optari inimico, tripliciter intelliguntur: Primo, per modum propheticæ prænuntiationis, non per modum imprecationis alicujus nocivi. Secundo, per modum demonstrationis, quid impius mereatur. Tertio, per modum zeli, quo se homo conformat divinæ justitiæ, imprecans impiis mala secundum ordinem æquitatis divinæ, nisi pœniteant: et hoc modo Jeremias dicit, Domine, ne propitieris iniquitati eorum, et peccatum eorum non deleatur.
paras.en: [[108:6|Set thou the sinner over him: and may the devil stand at his right hand|Constitue super eum peccatorem, et diabolus stet a dextris ejus]]. [[108:7|When he is judged, may he go out condemned|Quum judicatur, exeat condemnatus]], etc. It seems strange that such great evils should now be called down upon the adversary of the just man by the just man himself, who has just said that he prayed for his rival. It must be known, then, that these words and the like, by which evil seems to be wished upon an enemy, are understood in three ways. First, by way of prophetic foretelling, not by way of an imprecation of some harm. Secondly, by way of showing what the wicked man deserves. Thirdly, by way of zeal, by which a man conforms himself to the divine justice, calling down evils upon the wicked according to the order of divine equity, unless they repent: and in this way Jeremias says, O Lord, forgive [[Jer 18:23|not their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out|ne propitieris iniquitati eorum, et peccatum eorum non deleatur]].

paras.t: Ait ergo Ecclesia seu fidelis: Constitue super eum, id est, super populum prævaricatorem constitues, et constitui decet, et oro ut statuas ad laudem justitiæ tuæ, nisi resipiscat, peccatorem, id est diabolum seu indignum prælatum, quatenus quales servi, tales sint domini; et diabolus stet a dextris ejus, inducendo eum ad omnia opera mala.
paras.en: So the Church, or the faithful soul, says: [[108:6|Set thou|Constitue]] [[108:6|over him|super eum]], that is, over the prevaricating people thou wilt set, and it is fitting that there be set, and I pray that thou set, to the praise of thy justice, unless it repent, [[108:6|the sinner|peccatorem]], that is, the devil or an unworthy prelate, so that as the servants are, such may the masters be; [[108:6|and may the devil stand at his right hand|et diabolus stet a dextris ejus]], leading him on to every evil work.

paras.t: Fiant dies ejus pauci, id est, in vita gratiæ non persistat, vel dies suæ naturalis vitæ brevientur propter peccata ipsius, quemadmodum Ecclesiastes dicit: Non sit bonum impio, nec prolongentur dies ejus. Et episcopatum ejus accipiat alter. Hoc contra indignos prælatos inducitur: qui utinam suo officio privarentur. Sicut enim bono prælato nihil est utilius, sic indigno prælato nihil nocentius.
paras.en: [[108:8|May his days be few|Fiant dies ejus pauci]], that is, may he not persevere in the life of grace; or, may the days of his natural life be shortened because of his sins, as Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 8:13|let it not be well with the wicked, neither let his days be prolonged|Non sit bonum impio, nec prolongentur dies ejus]]. [[108:8|and his bishopric let another take|Et episcopatum ejus accipiat alter]]. This is brought against unworthy prelates: would that they were deprived of their office! For as nothing is more profitable than a good prelate, so nothing is more harmful than an unworthy one.

paras.t: Fiant filii ejus orphani: id est, imitatores populi tam maligni priventur Patre cœlesti, ne sint filii adoptivi Patris æterni, sed servi diaboli, cujus voluntati consentiunt; et uxor ejus, id est ecclesia malignantium, cum qua ipse spiritualiter aut corporaliter fornicatur, fiat vidua, id est, desinat esse Christi sponsa, eo quod fornicetur cum amatoribus multis; nec fecundetur luce et gratia Spiritus Sancti, sed in omnibus bonis sterilis fiat.
paras.en: [[108:9|May his children be fatherless|Fiant filii ejus orphani]]: that is, may the imitators of so malignant a people be deprived of the heavenly Father, so that they be not adopted sons of the eternal Father, but slaves of the devil, to whose will they consent; [[108:9|and his wife|et uxor ejus]], that is, the church of the malignant, with which he commits fornication spiritually or bodily, become [[108:9|a widow|vidua]], that is, cease to be the bride of Christ, because she commits fornication with many lovers[[Jer 3:1||]]; and may she not be made fruitful by the light and grace of the Holy Ghost, but become barren in all good things.

paras.t: Nutantes transferantur filii ejus: id est, imitatores plebis perversæ transferantur de regno Christi ad potestatem diaboli, de statu salutis ad statum damnationis, de morte temporali ad perpetuam mortem inferni: et hoc nutantes, id est instabiles facti, vagi ac dissoluti, sicut supra dictum est: Filii alieni inveterati sunt, et claudicaverunt a semitis suis. Impius namque facit opus instabile, sicut scriptum est. Et mendicent, tanquam omnibus spiritualibus bonis privati eo modo, quo fatuæ virgines mendicabant, dicentes ad sapientes: Date nobis de oleo vestro. Ejiciantur de habitationibus suis, id est de locis Ecclesiæ, tanquam indigna et putrida membra ipsius; vel, De habitationibus suis, id est de cœlestibus mansionibus, eis (si bene vixissent) paratis.
paras.en: [[108:10|Let his children be carried about vagabonds|Nutantes transferantur filii ejus]]: that is, may the imitators of the perverse people be carried over from the kingdom of Christ to the power of the devil, from the state of salvation to the state of damnation, from temporal death to the everlasting death of hell: and this as vagabonds [nutantes, literally “tottering”], that is, made unstable, wandering and dissolute, as was said above [in Ps 17]: [[Ps 17:46|strange children have faded away, and have halted from their paths|Filii alieni inveterati sunt, et claudicaverunt a semitis suis]]. For the [[Prov 11:18|wicked maketh an unsteady work|Impius namque facit opus instabile]], as it is written. [[108:10|and beg|Et mendicent]], as being deprived of all spiritual goods, in the way that the foolish virgins begged, saying to the wise: [[Matt 25:8|Give us of your oil|Date nobis de oleo vestro]]. [[108:10|and let them be cast out of their dwellings|Ejiciantur de habitationibus suis]], that is, from the places of the Church, as unworthy and rotten members of it; or, from their dwellings, that is, from the heavenly mansions which had been prepared for them (had they lived well).

paras.t: Scrutetur fœnerator, id est exactor, scilicet dæmon tentator, a quo peccator peccata velut pecuniam mutuat, dum ejus suggestione et cooperatione concupiscentiis satisfacit, omnem substantiam ejus, id est omnes interiores divitias impii, scilicet dona naturæ et gratiæ sibi collata; et ea suo dominio subdat, auferat aut inficiat. Et diripiant alieni, id est dæmones de particularibus vitiis tentantes, labores, id est virtutes et merita ejus, spoliando eum donis Dei. Quemadmodum enim exactor domum debitoris non potentis debita reddere, percepta licentia, intrat, et bona ejus tollit; sic dæmon cor peccatoris in vitiis persistentis, Deo permittente ingreditur, atque in eo bonis spoliato, dominationem sortitur.
paras.en: [[108:11|May the usurer search|Scrutetur fœnerator]], that is, the exactor, namely the tempting demon, from whom the sinner borrows sins as if money, when by his suggestion and cooperation he satisfies his desires, [[108:11|all his substance|omnem substantiam ejus]], that is, all the inward riches of the wicked man, namely the gifts of nature and of grace bestowed on him; and may he subject them to his dominion, take them away or taint them. [[108:11|and let strangers plunder|Et diripiant alieni]], that is, the demons who tempt to particular vices, [[108:11|his labours|labores]], that is, his virtues and merits, despoiling him of the gifts of God. For as an exactor, having obtained leave, enters the house of a debtor who cannot pay his debts and takes away his goods, so the demon, by God's permission, enters the heart of the sinner who persists in his vices and, when it has been despoiled of its goods, gains dominion in it.

paras.t: Non sit illi adjutor. Qui enim adjutorio Dei juste privatur, ab alio nullo valet salvari, aut salubriter adjuvari. Nec sit qui miseretur pupillis ejus, id est qui prava opera ejus sequuntur, sed justa pœna plectantur, vel in hoc sæculo, aut in futuro, prout scriptum est: Sic pereant inimici tui, Domine; qui autem diligunt te, sicut sol in ortu suo splendet, ita rutilent. Fiant nati ejus in interitum spiritualem, perdendo vitam animæ, scilicet caritatem et gratiam.
paras.en: [[108:12|May there be none to help him|Non sit illi adjutor]]. For he who is justly deprived of God's help can be saved, or helped to salvation, by no one else. [[108:12|nor none to pity his fatherless offspring|Nec sit qui miseretur pupillis ejus]], that is, those who follow his wicked works, but may they be punished with just punishment, either in this world or in the next, as it is written: [[Judg 5:31|So let all thy enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love thee shine, as the sun shineth in his rising|Sic pereant inimici tui, Domine; qui autem diligunt te, sicut sol in ortu suo splendet, ita rutilent]]. [[108:13|May his posterity be cut off|Fiant nati ejus in interitum]], spiritually, by losing the life of the soul, namely charity and grace.

paras.t: Fiant contra Dominum semper, id est, omni tempore Deo displiceant, sicut scriptum est: Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus; et dispereat de terra viatorum ac comprehensorum, id est de præsenti Ecclesia et regione vivorum seu patria, memoria eorum, quantum ad bonum, ita quod nesciantur a Deo per approbationem; pro eo quod non est recordatus conventus eorum, seu ipsi, facere misericordiam cum proximo suo; et persecutus est hominem inopem et mendicum: quod est peccatum clamitans ante Deum; et compunctum corde ex contritione peccati sui et aliorum, conati sunt mortificare. Merito ergo populus tam crudelis æternæ oblivioni traditur, nec ullam misericordiam consequitur, sicut Job ait: Obliviscatur ejus misericordia; et dulcedo illius, vermis. Unde et Christus: Eadem, inquit, mensura qua mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis. Et alibi legitur: Homo in hominem sibi similem non habet misericordiam: et de peccatis suis deprecatur Altissimum? quis exorabit pro peccatis illius? quasi dicat, hoc pene irremissibile esse.
paras.en: [[108:15|May they be before the Lord continually|Fiant contra Dominum semper]] [contra Dominum, literally “against the Lord”], that is, may they displease God at all times, as it is written: [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful|Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]]; and let there [[108:15|perish from the earth|dispereat de terra]] of wayfarers and comprehensors [that is, of those still on the way to God in this life and of the blessed who have reached him], that is, from the present Church and from the land of the living, or homeland, [[108:15|the memory of them|memoria eorum]], as regards good, so that they are not known by God with approval; [[108:16|because he remembered not|pro eo quod non est recordatus]] (their assembly, or they themselves) [[108:16|to shew mercy|facere misericordiam]] to his neighbour; [[108:17|But persecuted the poor man and the beggar|et persecutus est hominem inopem et mendicum]]: which is a sin that cries out before God; [[108:17|and the broken in heart|et compunctum corde]] through contrition for his own sin and that of others, they tried [[108:17|to put him to death|mortificare]]. Rightly then is so cruel a people given over to eternal oblivion, and obtains no mercy, as Job says: [[Job 24:20|Let mercy forget him: may worms be his sweetness|Obliviscatur ejus misericordia; et dulcedo illius, vermis]]. Hence Christ too: [[Luke 6:38|For with the same|Eadem]], he says, [[Luke 6:38|measure that you shall mete withal, it shall be measured to you again|mensura qua mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis]]. And elsewhere we read: Man [[Ecclus 28:4|hath no mercy on a man like himself, and doth he entreat for his own sins?|in hominem sibi similem non habet misericordiam: et de peccatis suis deprecatur Altissimum?]] [[Ecclus 28:5|who shall obtain pardon for his sins?|quis exorabit pro peccatis illius?]] as if to say, this is all but unpardonable.

paras.t: Et dilexit maledictionem, et veniet ei. Maledictionem diligit, qui opera amat propter quæ Christus in fine dicturus est reprobis: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Maledictionem diligit, qui amat quod sibi non expedit, qui lætatur quum malefecerit, et exsultat in rebus pessimis. Maledictionem diligunt, de quibus Job asserit: Dixerunt Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus. Et Isaias: Dicunt videntibus, Nolite videre; et adspicientibus, Nolite adspicere nobis ea quæ recta sunt. Et noluit populus reprobus benedictionem, id est gratiam Dei, quoniam sprevit legem Altissimi, et elongabitur ab eo, quia non dabitur ei. Et induit maledictionem sicut vestimentum, id est, peccato repletus est. Hinc enim Sapientia ait: Quia vocavi, et renuistis; extendi manum meam, et non fuit qui adspiceret; despexistis omne consilium meum, et increpationes meas neglexistis: ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo, et subsannabo, quum vobis id quod timebatis advenerit, quum irruerit repentina calamitas.
paras.en: [[108:18|And he loved cursing, and it shall come unto him|Et dilexit maledictionem, et veniet ei]]. They love cursing who love the works for which Christ at the end will say to the reprobate: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. They love cursing who love what is not good for them, [[Prov 2:14|Who are glad when they have done evil, and rejoice in the most wicked things|qui lætatur quum malefecerit, et exsultat in rebus pessimis]]. They love cursing of whom Job declares: They have [[Job 21:14|said to God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways|Dixerunt Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus]]. And Isaias: They [[Is 30:10|say to the seers: See not: and to them that behold: Behold not for us those things that are right|Dicunt videntibus, Nolite videre; et adspicientibus, Nolite adspicere nobis ea quæ recta sunt]]. And the reprobate people [[108:18|would not have blessing|noluit populus reprobus benedictionem]], that is, the grace of God, since it despised the law of the Most High, [[108:18|and it shall be far from him|et elongabitur ab eo]], because it will not be given him. [[108:18|And he put on cursing, like a garment|Et induit maledictionem sicut vestimentum]], that is, he is filled with sin. For hence Wisdom says: [[Prov 1:24|Because I called, and you refused: I stretched out my hand, and there was none that regarded|Quia vocavi, et renuistis; extendi manum meam, et non fuit qui adspiceret]]: [[Prov 1:25|You have despised all my counsel, and have neglected my reprehensions|despexistis omne consilium meum, et increpationes meas neglexistis]]: [[Prov 1:26|I also will laugh in your destruction, and will mock when that shall come to you which you feared|ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo, et subsannabo, quum vobis id quod timebatis advenerit]], [[Prov 1:27|When sudden calamity shall fall on you|quum irruerit repentina calamitas]].

paras.t: Fiat ei sicut vestimentum quo operitur, id est, maledictio, scilicet culpa et debita pœna, operiat impium, sicut vestis operit veste indutum. Hoc accidit impœnitenti, quemadmodum Isaias dicit: Veniet super te malum atque calamitas, et nescies ortum ejus; et veniet super te miseria repente. In Job quoque legitur: Propter malitiam tuam circumdatus es laqueis, et conturbat te formido subita. Et sicut zona qua semper præcingitur: id est, maledictione perversus ligetur, ne exeat rete diaboli, sicut ligatur corpus cum cingulo. Hoc est quod Salomon fassus est: Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur.
paras.en: [[108:19|May it be unto him like a garment which covereth him|Fiat ei sicut vestimentum quo operitur]], that is, may cursing, namely guilt and the punishment due to it, cover the wicked man, as a garment covers the one clothed in it. This befalls the impenitent, as Isaias says: [[Is 47:11|Evil shall come upon thee, and thou shalt not know the rising thereof|Veniet super te malum atque calamitas, et nescies ortum ejus]]; [[Is 47:11|misery shall come upon thee suddenly|et veniet super te miseria repente]]. In Job too we read: [[Job 22:5|for thy manifold wickedness|Propter malitiam tuam]] [[Job 22:10|art thou surrounded with snares, and sudden fear troubleth thee|circumdatus es laqueis, et conturbat te formido subita]] [Denis joins words of Job 22:5 and 22:10, as the margin notes]. [[108:19|and like a girdle with which he is girded continually|Et sicut zona qua semper præcingitur]]: that is, may the perverse man be bound with cursing, so that he may not get out of the devil's net, as the body is bound with a girdle. This is what Solomon declared: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur]].

paras.t: Deinde Ecclesia, seu quilibet justus subjungit: Hoc opus eorum, id est, ista erit merces illorum, qui detrahunt mihi apud Dominum. Terribile ergo est, detrahere justis.
paras.en: Then the Church, or any just man, adds: [[108:20|This is the work of them|Hoc opus eorum]], that is, this will be the wages of those [[108:20|who detract me before the Lord|qui detrahunt mihi apud Dominum]]. It is a fearful thing, then, to detract the just.

paras.t: Et tu, Domine, Domine, fac mecum misericordiam tuam propter nomen tuum, id est propriam tuam bonitatem et gloriam, non propter justitias meas. Hoc modo Deus propter se ipsum dimittit nobis peccata, et dona gratiæ impertitur. Ait enim per Isaiam: Ego sum qui deleo iniquitates tuas propter me; et alibi, Propter me ego faciam, ut non blasphemer. Quia suavis est nobis misericordia tua. Melior est enim misericordia tua super vitas.
paras.en: [[108:21|But thou, O Lord, do with me|Et tu, Domine, Domine, fac mecum]] thy mercy [Denis reads fac mecum misericordiam tuam, “work thy mercy with me”] [[108:21|for thy name's sake|propter nomen tuum]], that is, for thine own goodness and glory, not for my justices. In this way God forgives us our sins for his own sake, and bestows the gifts of grace. For he says through Isaias: [[Is 43:25|I am he that blot out thy iniquities for my own sake|Ego sum qui deleo iniquitates tuas propter me]]; and elsewhere, [[Is 48:11|for my own sake will I do it, that I may not be blasphemed|Propter me ego faciam, ut non blasphemer]]. [[108:21|because thy mercy is sweet|Quia suavis est nobis misericordia tua]] to us. [[Ps 62:4|For thy mercy is better than lives|Melior est enim misericordia tua super vitas]].

paras.t: Libera me ab omni periculo et malo pœnæ et culpæ, quia egenus, propter imperfectionem naturæ, et pauper, propter carentiam gratiæ, ego sum; et cor meum conturbatum est intra me ex recordatione divini judicii, æterni tormenti, proprii quoque peccati, et propter diversa pericula, quibus expositus sum, ita ut cum sancto Job dicere possim: Antequam comedam, suspiro; et quasi inundantis aquæ, sic rugitus meus.
paras.en: [[108:21|Do thou deliver me|Libera me]] [in the Vulgate these words begin v. 22; the Douay-Rheims puts them at the end of v. 21] from every danger and from the evil of punishment and of guilt, [[108:22|For I am poor|quia egenus]], through the imperfection of nature, [[108:22|and needy|et pauper]], through the want of grace; [[108:22|and my heart is troubled within me|et cor meum conturbatum est intra me]] at the remembrance of the divine judgement, of eternal torment, and of my own sin too, and because of the many dangers to which I am exposed, so that with holy Job I can say: [[Job 3:24|Before I eat I sigh: and as overflowing waters, so is my roaring|Antequam comedam, suspiro; et quasi inundantis aquæ, sic rugitus meus]].

paras.t: Sicut umbra quum declinat, ablatus sum: id est, quemadmodum umbra ad occasum progrediens, statim aufertur ac deficit; sic ego repente defeci et cecidi, vel a pristina gratia, vel a flore juventutis, vel a fortitudine corporis. Et excussus sum a statu perfectionis, stabilitateque mentis, a contemplatione ad phantasmata inutilia corruendo, sicut locustæ excutiuntur de loco suo. Est autem quædam ablatio bona, sicut quum homo aufertur mundo, ut serviat Christo, aufertur diabolo, ut vivat virtutibus. Sic quoque est quædam excussio bona: de qua Isaias, Excutere (inquit) de pulvere, id est, a terrenis ad cœlestia per contemplationem et dilectionem ascende.
paras.en: [[108:23|I am taken away like the shadow when it declineth|Sicut umbra quum declinat, ablatus sum]]: that is, as the shadow moving towards sunset is at once taken away and fails, so I have suddenly failed and fallen, either from former grace, or from the flower of youth, or from bodily strength. [[108:23|and I am shaken off|Et excussus sum]] from the state of perfection and from steadiness of mind, falling from contemplation to useless fancies, [[108:23|as locusts|sicut locustæ]] are shaken off from their place. But there is a good taking away, as when a man is taken away from the world to serve Christ, taken away from the devil to live in the virtues. So too there is a good shaking off, of which Isaias says: [[Is 52:2|Shake thyself|Excutere]] (he says) [[Is 52:2|from the dust|de pulvere]], that is, rise from earthly things to heavenly ones by contemplation and love.

paras.t: Genua mea infirmata sunt a jejunio. Hoc secundum sensum præhabitum competit his, qui cum Apostolo dicere possunt, Castigo corpus meum et in servitutem redigo. Sunt tamen quædam genua cordis: de quibus in sua oratione ait Manasses, Et nunc flecto genua cordis mei. Sic etiam est quoddam spirituale ac malum jejunium, dum a cibo animæ homo jejunat, spirituali scilicet refectione gratiæ Dei privatus. Ab hoc ergo jejunio genua cordis (id est virtutes) infirmantur, quia debiliter et sine fervore procedunt in actum. Gratia namque crescente, omnes virtutes roborantur, et fortius atque ferventius operantur; gratia vero decrescente, infirmantur virtutes. Et caro mea immutata est, id est hilaris facta et roborata, propter oleum, id est propter consolationem internam, et ex promptitudine animi omnia libenter agentis ac sustinentis. Debemus enim in jejunando vitare exteriorem hypocritarum apparentiam. Propter quod Christus locutus est: Tu autem quum jejunas, unge caput tuum, et faciem tuam lava, ne videaris hominibus jejunans.
paras.en: [[108:24|My knees are weakened through fasting|Genua mea infirmata sunt a jejunio]]. In the sense given before, this fits those who can say with the Apostle, [[1 Cor 9:27|I chastise my body and bring it into subjection|Castigo corpus meum et in servitutem redigo]]. Yet there are also certain knees of the heart, of which Manasses speaks in his prayer: And now I bend the knees of my heart [the margin gives Oratio Manassæ: the Prayer of Manasses, which stands outside the canon, in the appendix of the Vulgate]. So too there is a certain spiritual and evil fasting, when a man fasts from the food of the soul, being deprived, that is, of the spiritual refreshment of God's grace. By this fasting, then, the knees of the heart (that is, the virtues) are weakened, because they go forth into act feebly and without fervour. For as grace grows, all the virtues are strengthened and work more strongly and more fervently; but as grace decreases, the virtues are weakened. [[108:24|and my flesh is changed|Et caro mea immutata est]], that is, made cheerful and strengthened, [[108:24|for oil|propter oleum]], that is, because of inward consolation, and out of the readiness of a mind that does and bears all things willingly. For in fasting we ought to avoid the outward show of the hypocrites. Wherefore Christ said: [[Matt 6:17|But thou, when thou fastest anoint thy head, and wash thy face|Tu autem quum jejunas, unge caput tuum, et faciem tuam lava]], [[Matt 6:18|That thou appear not to men to fast|ne videaris hominibus jejunans]].

paras.t: Et ego factus sum opprobrium illis. Justi enim ab impiis deridentur et contemnuntur. Propter quod dicit Salvator: Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur: quia non est servus major domino suo. Viderunt me, et moverunt capita sua, insultando illudendoque mihi: quemadmodum Apostolus dicit, Tanquam purgamentum hujus mundi facti sumus, omnium peripsema usque adhuc; et iterum, Spectaculum facti sumus Deo et angelis et hominibus, et nos stulti propter Christum.
paras.en: [[108:25|And I am become a reproach to them|Et ego factus sum opprobrium illis]]. For the just are mocked and despised by the wicked. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]]: for [[John 15:20|The servant is not greater than his master|non est servus major domino suo]]. [[108:25|they saw me and they shaked their heads|Viderunt me, et moverunt capita sua]], insulting and mocking me: as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 4:13|We are made as the refuse of this world, the offscouring of all, even until now|Tanquam purgamentum hujus mundi facti sumus, omnium peripsema usque adhuc]]; and again, [[1 Cor 4:9|We are made a spectacle|Spectaculum facti sumus]] to God [[1 Cor 4:9|and to angels and to men|et angelis et hominibus]] [Denis reads Deo, “to God”, where the Vulgate has mundo, “to the world”], [[1 Cor 4:10|We are fools for Christs sake|et nos stulti propter Christum]].

paras.t: Adjuva me, Domine Deus meus, ne in tantis adversitatibus per impatientiam vincar. Adjuva me, ut fortiter pro tuo amore cuncta sustineam. Salvum me fac, modo per spem et gratiæ multiplicationem, in futuro autem per rem et gloriæ infusionem, secundum misericordiam tuam, id est cito et copiose, sicut tu copiosus, plenus et velox es in misericordia.
paras.en: [[108:26|Help me, O Lord my God|Adjuva me, Domine Deus meus]], that I be not overcome by impatience in such great adversities. Help me, that I may bravely bear all things for love of thee. [[108:26|save me|Salvum me fac]], now in hope and by the increase of grace, but in the future in reality and by the pouring in of glory, [[108:26|according to thy mercy|secundum misericordiam tuam]], that is, swiftly and abundantly, as thou art abundant, full and swift in mercy.

paras.t: Et sciant, id est, experimentaliter videant hostes mei invisibiles atque visibiles, quia manus tua hæc, id est, quod ista mea confortatio atque salvatio sit effectus seu opus tuæ potestatis divinæ; et tu, Domine, fecisti eam, id est, hoc quoque agnoscant, quod hæc operatio sit in me ex tua virtute, ita quod a te salvata est anima mea.
paras.en: [[108:27|And let them know|Et sciant]], that is, let my enemies, invisible and visible, see by experience, [[108:27|that this is thy hand|quia manus tua hæc]], that is, that this strengthening and saving of mine is the effect or work of thy divine power; [[108:27|and that thou, O Lord, hast done it|et tu, Domine, fecisti eam]], that is, let them acknowledge this too, that this working is in me by thy power, so that my soul has been saved by thee.

paras.t: Maledicent illi mihi ex sua malignitate; et tu benedices, id est, gratiam magnam mihi præstabis pro hac injuria, quam æquanimiter patior. Quanto enim conspexerit Deus fideles suos majora sustinere opprobria et flagella, tanto liberalius eis succurrit, sicut supra dixit: Cum ipso sum in tribulatione. Qui insurgunt in me, confundantur, id est, de sua malitia erubescant, seque victos inveniant; servus autem tuus lætabitur in te: prout Apostolus monet, Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur.
paras.en: [[108:28|They will curse|Maledicent illi]] me out of their malice; [[108:28|and thou wilt bless|et tu benedices]], that is, thou wilt grant me great grace for this injury, which I bear with equanimity. For the more God sees his faithful bear greater reproaches and scourges, the more generously he succours them, as he said above: [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione]]. [[108:28|let them that rise up against me be confounded|Qui insurgunt in me, confundantur]], that is, let them blush for their malice and find themselves vanquished; [[108:28|but thy servant shall rejoice|servus autem tuus lætabitur]] in thee: as the Apostle exhorts, [[2 Cor 10:17|he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]].

paras.t: Deinde sequitur vox gratias Domino referentis: Confitebor Domino benefactori meo nimis, id est toto affectu, devotione præcipua, et ultra naturalium virium potestatem, in ore meo, ipsum laudando: juxta illud, Semper laus ejus in ore meo; et in medio multorum, id est inter alios et in Ecclesia, laudabo eum, propter bonitatem ejus et beneficia mihi concessa. Quia adstitit a dextris pauperis, id est, mihi pauperi favorabiliter adfuit: adstare namque est adjuvantis; ut salvam faceret a persequentibus, id est malis et importunis hominibus atque dæmonibus, animam meam, præservando eam a læsione peccati, conservandoque eam in statu salutis.
paras.en: Then follows the voice of one giving thanks to the Lord: [[108:30|I will give great thanks to the Lord|Confitebor Domino]] my benefactor exceedingly [nimis, which the Douay-Rheims renders with “great”], that is, with all my affection, with special devotion, and beyond the power of my natural strength, [[108:30|with my mouth|in ore meo]], praising him: according to that saying, [[Ps 33:2|his praise shall be always in my mouth|Semper laus ejus in ore meo]]; [[108:30|and in the midst of many|et in medio multorum]], that is, among others and in the Church, [[108:30|I will praise him|laudabo eum]], for his goodness and the benefits granted me. [[108:31|Because he hath stood at the right hand of the poor|Quia adstitit a dextris pauperis]], that is, he stood by me, a poor man, with favour: for to stand by is the part of one who helps; [[108:31|to save|ut salvam faceret]] [[108:31|from persecutors|a persequentibus]], that is, from wicked and troublesome men and from demons, [[108:31|my soul|animam meam]], preserving it from the hurt of sin and keeping it in the state of salvation.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum mysterialem audivimus: in quo Capitis nostri diram persecutionem et admirandam patientiam intuemur. Discamus ergo Christi exemplo pro adversariis et persecutoribus cordialiter exorare, odientibus affectum sanctæ dilectionis rependere, et Christi vestigia in omnibus imitari.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of mystery, in which we see the dire persecution and the wonderful patience of our Head. Let us learn, then, by Christ's example, to pray heartily for our adversaries and persecutors, to repay those who hate us with the affection of holy love, and to follow the footsteps of Christ in all things.

paras.t: Tu, Domine, qui suavis in misericordia, cor nostrum peccatis exigentibus perturbatum intra nos, spiritu tuo bono lætificas, adjuva nos misericorditer et salva: lætentur in te servi tui, et fac nos in perpetuum tibi Domino nimis confiteri.
paras.en: O Lord, who art sweet in mercy, and who gladdenest with thy good spirit our heart, troubled within us as our sins deserve, help us mercifully and save us: let thy servants rejoice in thee, and make us for ever give exceeding thanks to thee, the Lord.

109.title: ELUCIDATIO LITTERALIS PSALMI CENTESIMI NONI : DIXIT DOMINUS DOMINO MEO.
109.title_en: Literal explanation of the hundred and ninth psalm: The Lord said to my Lord.

paras.t: Psalmi nunc declarandi titulus talis est: Psalmus David. Convenit namque hic psalmus David prophetæ tanquam auctoris, et Christo per David significato tanquam materiæ seu subjecto : quia ad litteram loquitur de Christo, quemadmodum ipsemet Christus apud Matthæum testatus est. Alloquens enim Pharisæos : Quid vobis, inquit, videtur de Christo ? Cujus filius est ? Quibus respondentibus, David, adjecit : Quomodo ergo David in spiritu vocat eum Dominum, dicens, Dixit Dominus Domino meo, sede a dextris meis ? Apostolus quoque ex ista scriptura ostendit Christum angelis majorem, et Patri æqualem. Ad quem, inquiens, angelorum dixit aliquando, Sede a dextris meis, quoadusque ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum ? Loquitur itaque psalmus iste de Christo secundum utramque ejus naturam, et de magnificentia ejus in ascensione, de coæternitate ejus, et substantiali identitate cum Patre, de generali ejus dominio, sacerdotioque æterno, atque finali judicio.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is this: [[109:1|A psalm for David|Psalmus David]]. For this psalm belongs to David the prophet as its author, and to Christ, signified by David, as its matter or subject [the Latin Psalmus David can mean both 'a psalm of David' and 'a psalm for David'], because in its literal sense it speaks of Christ, as Christ himself testified in Matthew. For, addressing the Pharisees, he said: [[Matt 22:42|What think you|Quid vobis]], [[Matt 22:42|of Christ? Whose son is he?|videtur de Christo ? Cujus filius est ?]] And when they answered, David's, he added: [[Matt 22:43|How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying|Quomodo ergo David in spiritu vocat eum Dominum, dicens]], [[Matt 22:44|The Lord said to my Lord: Sit on my right hand|Dixit Dominus Domino meo, sede a dextris meis]]? The Apostle too shows from this scripture that Christ is greater than the angels and equal to the Father. [[Heb 1:13|To which|Ad quem]], he says, [[Heb 1:13|of the angels said he at any time: Sit on my right hand, until I make thy enemies thy footstool?|angelorum dixit aliquando, Sede a dextris meis, quoadusque ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum]] This psalm, then, speaks of Christ according to both his natures: of his magnificence in the ascension, of his coeternity and substantial identity with the Father, of his universal dominion and eternal priesthood, and of the final judgment.

paras.t: Ait ergo beatissimus David, cui incerta et occulta sapientiæ suæ revelavit Deus : Dixit Dominus Domino meo : id est, Deus Pater locutus est Filio suo unigenito, vero Deo ac Domino meo : qui est Dominus meus secundum divinitatem, et filius meus secundum humanam, quam ex semine meo suscepit, naturam. Dixit autem non verbo foris sonanti ac transeunti, sed intellectualiter ei innotuit, imo ab æterno ita disposuit. Quid autem dixit, subjungitur : Sede a dextris meis : id est, tu, Fili carissime, qui propter meum honorem, hominumque salutem, sub omnibus creaturis humiliatus es, factus opprobrium hominum, in ascensione tua super omnes creaturas exaltare, et usque ad thronum majestatis ac gloriæ meæ conscende, illicque ad dexteram meam æternaliter reside, habita, et quiesce.
paras.en: Most blessed David, then, to whom God revealed the uncertain and hidden things of his wisdom[[Ps 50:8||]] [the margin reads Ps. i, 8; the words are those of Ps 50:8], says: [[109:1|The Lord said to my Lord|Dixit Dominus Domino meo]]: that is, God the Father spoke to his only-begotten Son, true God and my Lord, who is my Lord according to his divinity, and my son according to the human nature which he took from my seed. He said it, however, not by a word sounding outwardly and passing away, but he made it known to him intellectually; nay, he so disposed it from eternity. What he said is added: [[109:1|Sit thou at my right hand|Sede a dextris meis]]: that is, thou, dearest Son, who for my honour and the salvation of men wast humbled beneath all creatures, made [[Ps 21:7|the reproach of men|opprobrium hominum]], be exalted in thy ascension above all creatures[[Heb 2:7||]][[Heb 2:8||]], and go up even to the throne of my majesty and glory, and there at my right hand reside eternally, dwell, and rest.

paras.t: Donec ponam inimicos tuos, id est omnes incredulos et iniquos, præsertim Judæos, scabellum pedum tuorum, id est sic tuæ potestati ac dominationi subjectos, sicut substernitur scabellum pedibus sedentis. Hæc subjectio jam aliquo modo impleta est. Christus enim post resurrectionem dixit : Data est mihi omnis potestas in cælo et in terra. Imo ante passionem ait de se ad Patrem : Dedisti ei potestatem omnis carnis. Denique qui aliquando Christo repugnabant, post conversionem ad fidem ei subjecti fuerunt. Sed ista subjectio maxime apparebit, et plene implebitur in die finalis judicii, quia tunc Christus omnes adversarios suos dejiciet et damnabit. Nam et tunc implebitur, quod in Isaia de Christo prædictum est : Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei.
paras.en: [[109:1|Until I make thy enemies|Donec ponam inimicos tuos]], that is, all unbelievers and wicked men, especially the Jews, [[109:1|thy footstool|scabellum pedum tuorum]]: that is, so subjected to thy power and dominion as a footstool is set beneath the feet of one who sits. This subjection has already been fulfilled in some manner. For after the resurrection Christ said: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cælo et in terra]]. Nay, before the passion he said of himself to the Father: [[John 17:2|thou hast given him power over all flesh|Dedisti ei potestatem omnis carnis]]. Lastly, those who once resisted Christ became subject to him after their conversion to the faith. But this subjection will appear most of all, and will be fulfilled completely, on the day of the final judgment, because then Christ will cast down and condemn all his adversaries. For then too will be fulfilled what was foretold of Christ in Isaias: [[Is 45:25|they shall come to him, and all that resist him shall be confounded|Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei]].

paras.t: Interim ergo Christus sedebit ad dexteram Patris. Sed numquid postea non sedebit? Sedebit utique postea. In divina enim Scriptura solet hæc dictio, Donec, in oratione affirmativa omnia tempora ponere et includere, sicut dum et infra dicitur : Oculi nostri ad Dominum Deum nostrum donec misereatur nostri. Sicque tenetur hoc loco, quoniam Christus in æternum sedebit ad dexteram Patris. In oratione vero negativa solet omnia tempora abnegare et tollere, sicut in Matthæo de Joseph et Virgine benedicta asseritur : Non cognovit eam donec peperit filium suum primogenitum. Et istud rationabiliter fit. Dum namque Scriptura affirmat aut negat aliquid pro illo tempore quando minus sic esse videtur, tunc certum est quod ipsa velit insinuare illud aliis temporibus sic se habere : sicut dum Matthæus affirmat S. Joseph non cognovisse Mariam donec peperit Christum, certum est quod postmodum eam non cognovit. Quomodo enim Matrem Filii Dei unigeniti tentaret accedere, cui se cohabitare scivit indignum? Simili modo dum Propheta asserit Christum ad dexteram Dei sessurum, donec subjiciantur sibi adversarii sui, certum est quod illis subjectis sedebit.
paras.en: Meanwhile, then, Christ will sit at the right hand of the Father. But will he not sit there afterwards? Assuredly he will sit there afterwards. For in divine Scripture this word 'until', in an affirmative statement, is wont to posit and include all times, as when it is said further on: [[Ps 122:2|our eyes unto the Lord our God, until he have mercy on us|Oculi nostri ad Dominum Deum nostrum donec misereatur nostri]]. And so it is to be taken in this place, since Christ will sit at the right hand of the Father for ever. In a negative statement, on the other hand, it is wont to deny and exclude all times, as is asserted in Matthew of Joseph and the blessed Virgin: [[Matt 1:25|he knew her not, till she brought forth her first born son|Non cognovit eam donec peperit filium suum primogenitum]]. And this is done with reason. For when Scripture affirms or denies something for that time at which it seems less likely to be so, then it is certain that it means to imply that the thing is so at other times as well: thus when Matthew affirms that St. Joseph did not know Mary until she brought forth Christ, it is certain that he did not know her afterwards. For how should he venture to approach the Mother of the only-begotten Son of God, with whom he knew himself unworthy even to dwell? In like manner, when the Prophet asserts that Christ will sit at the right hand of God until his adversaries are subjected to him, it is certain that once they are subjected he will still sit there.

paras.t: Advertendum autem, quod sessio Christi ad dexteram Patris dupliciter intelligi potest. Uno modo secundum divinam ipsius naturam : sicque per dexteram Patris designatur æqualitas ejus, ut sit sensus : Sede a dextris meis, id est, residendo mecum, esto mihi æqualis. Et hoc modo dixit Pater Filio ab æterno, ut ad dexteram suam sederet : imo generando eum, dixit et contulit ei hoc ipsum, quum ipsa generatio non sit nisi Verbi prolatio. Dicitur enim Pater Filio, secundum divinitatem ejus, demonstrare et dicere, quoniam generando Filium, dedit ei divinam essentiam, quæ est ipsa sapientia, quam recipiendo dicitur Filius a Patre audire atque cognoscere. Non est ergo in Patre dextera corporalis; neque in Filio, secundum quod Deus est, sessio situalis. Sed sicut per dexteram Patris designatur ejus æqualitas, ita per sessionem Filii exprimitur summa dominatio ejus. Sedere enim convenit regi ac judici. Secundo intelligitur Christus secundum humanam naturam sedere, id est esse et permanere ad dexteram Patris, id est in summis ac potioribus bonis sui Genitoris, videlicet in summitate cæli empyrei, atque perfecta participatione increatæ beatitudinis Dei Patris. Plus siquidem de beatitudine Dei recepit anima Christi, quam universi simul electi. Et hoc modo dixit Pater Christo homini, Sede a dextris meis, ab exordio creationis animæ Christi, quantum ad intellectualem revelationem. Revelavit etenim sibi, statim ut condita est, quod ipsa cum corpore suo elevanda esset super omnes cælos; sed quantum ad exsecutionem et complementum, dixit Pater Christo, Sede a dextris meis, in ascensione. Tunc enim dicendo, id est intellectualiter causaliterque jubendo, exaltavit Christum, et dedit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen. Et de hac Christi sessione dicit Evangelista : Dominus Jesus postquam locutus est eis, assumptus est in cælum, et sedet a dextris Dei. Unde et scriptum est : Adspiciebam in visione noctis, et ecce in nubibus cæli quasi Filius hominis veniebat, et usque ad Antiquum dierum pervenit; et in conspectu ejus obtulerunt eum.
paras.en: Now it is to be noted that the sitting of Christ at the right hand of the Father can be understood in two ways. In one way, according to his divine nature: and so the right hand of the Father signifies his equality, so that the sense is: [[109:1|Sit thou at my right hand|Sede a dextris meis]], that is, by residing with me, be equal to me. And in this way the Father told the Son from eternity to sit at his right hand: nay, in begetting him he said and conferred on him this very thing, since that generation is nothing else than the utterance of the Word. For the Father is said to show and to speak to the Son, according to his divinity, because in begetting the Son he gave him the divine essence, which is wisdom itself; and in receiving it the Son is said to hear from the Father and to know. There is, then, no bodily right hand in the Father; nor, in the Son as he is God, any sitting in a place. But as the right hand of the Father signifies his equality, so the sitting of the Son expresses his supreme dominion: for sitting befits a king and a judge. In the second way Christ is understood to sit according to his human nature, that is, to be and to abide at the right hand of the Father, that is, in the highest and choicest goods of his Begetter, namely in the summit of the empyrean heaven [that is, the highest heaven, the dwelling of the blessed], and in a perfect sharing of the uncreated beatitude of God the Father. For the soul of Christ received more of the beatitude of God than all the elect together. And in this way the Father said to Christ as man, [[109:1|Sit thou at my right hand|Sede a dextris meis]], from the beginning of the creation of Christ's soul, as regards intellectual revelation: for he revealed to it, as soon as it was created, that it was to be raised with its body above all the heavens; but as regards the carrying out and completion, the Father said to Christ, [[109:1|Sit thou at my right hand|Sede a dextris meis]], in the ascension. For then, by saying it, that is, by commanding it intellectually and causally, he exalted Christ, [[Phil 2:9|and hath given him a name which is above all names|et dedit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen]]. And of this sitting of Christ the Evangelist says: [[Mark 16:19|the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sitteth on the right hand of God|Dominus Jesus postquam locutus est eis, assumptus est in cælum, et sedet a dextris Dei]]. Whence it is also written: [[Dan 7:13|I beheld, therefore, in the vision of the night, and lo, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and he came even to the ancient of days: and they presented him before him|Adspiciebam in visione noctis, et ecce in nubibus cæli quasi Filius hominis veniebat, et usque ad Antiquum dierum pervenit; et in conspectu ejus obtulerunt eum]].

paras.t: Consequenter Propheta alloquitur Christum. Virgam virtutis tuæ, id est evangelicæ legis doctrinam, qua corriguntur injusti, seu dominationis ac regiæ tuæ dignitatis potentiam, o Christe, emittet Dominus Pater seu Deus Trinitas per servos suos Apostolos, ex Sion, id est ex hoc loco sic dicto, in Jerusalem sito. Sion namque mons fuit in Jerusalem, in quo constructum erat templum; itemque conclave vel cœnaculum, in quo Christus Cœnam novissimam celebravit, in quo post resurrectionem discipulis suis apparuit, in quo Apostoli aliique cum eis congregati, Spiritum Sanctum receperunt. Ex hoc ergo cœnaculo et ex templo in monte Sion posito, et ex Jerusalem emisit Deus per Apostolos virgam virtutis Christi, id est evangelicam legem, et Christi magnificentiam per totum mundum. Quum enim Apostoli Spiritum Sanctum recepissent in die Pentecostes, statim omnes cum suo collegio, velut examen apum de conclavi, in quo paulo ante ex timore Judæorum clausi residebant, eruperunt, ingressique templum, Christum prædicare cœperunt. Et exinde derivata est prædicatio eorum in totum orbem, secundum quod Christus eis prædixit : Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ. Quod etiam Isaias prophetavit, dicens : De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Ad hanc autem emissionem et prædicationem, secuta est conversio mundi ad Christum. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: Next the Prophet addresses Christ. [[109:2|the sceptre of thy power|Virgam virtutis tuæ]] [virga, 'rod', where the Douay-Rheims has 'sceptre'], that is, the teaching of the gospel law, by which the unjust are corrected, or the might of thy dominion and royal dignity, O Christ, [[109:2|The Lord will send forth|emittet Dominus]], the Father, or God the Trinity, through his servants the Apostles, [[109:2|out of Sion|ex Sion]], that is, out of the place so called, which lies in Jerusalem. For Sion was a mountain in Jerusalem on which the temple had been built; and on it too was the room or upper chamber in which Christ celebrated the Last Supper[[Mark 14:15||]] [the margin reads Mark xvi, 15, which does not fit; the upper room is in Mark 14:15], in which after the resurrection he appeared to his disciples[[John 20:19||]][[John 20:26||]], in which the Apostles and others gathered with them received the Holy Ghost[[Acts 2:1||]][[Acts 2:4||]]. From this upper room, then, and from the temple standing on mount Sion, and from Jerusalem, God sent forth through the Apostles the sceptre of Christ's power, that is, the gospel law, and the magnificence of Christ through the whole world. For when the Apostles had received the Holy Ghost on the day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:1||]], at once they all, with their company, burst forth like a swarm of bees from the room in which a little before they had been sitting shut in for fear of the Jews[[John 20:19||]], and entering the temple they began to preach Christ. And from there their preaching spread into the whole world, according as Christ had foretold to them: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]]. This Isaias also prophesied, saying: [[Is 2:3|the law shall come forth from Sion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem|De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem]]. And upon this sending forth and preaching there followed the conversion of the world to Christ. Therefore it is added:
