paras.t: Dominare, o Christe, in medio inimicorum tuorum, id est in regnis et populis infidelium : qui tempore infidelitatis inimici tui fuerunt, sed conversi ad fidem, amici effecti sunt ; et tu dominaris in eis per te ipsum ac tuos vicarios Ecclesiarum prælatos. Subjiciuntur etenim tibi per fidem atque divinæ legis custodiam, quoniam quæ præcepisti eis, observant. De hoc Christi dominio dictum est per Michæam : Et nunc magnificabitur in medio universæ terræ. Et item Zacharias : Potestas ejus a mari usque ad mare, et a fluminibus usque ad fines terræ. Unde et in Daniele scriptum est : Dedit ei Antiquus dierum potestatem, honorem et regnum; et omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei.
paras.en: [[109:2|Rule thou|Dominare]], O Christ, [[109:2|in the midst of thy enemies|in medio inimicorum tuorum]], that is, in the kingdoms and peoples of the unbelievers, who in the time of their unbelief were thy enemies, but, converted to the faith, have been made friends; and thou rulest in them through thyself and through thy vicars, the prelates of the Churches. For they are subject to thee through faith and the keeping of the divine law, since they observe what thou hast commanded them. Of this dominion of Christ it was said through Micheas: And [[Mich 5:4|now shall he be magnified|nunc magnificabitur]] in the midst of the whole earth [Denis reads in medio universæ terræ, 'in the midst of the whole earth', where the Vulgate has 'even to the ends of the earth']. And likewise Zacharias: [[Zach 9:10|his power shall be from sea to sea, and from the rivers even to the end of the earth|Potestas ejus a mari usque ad mare, et a fluminibus usque ad fines terræ]]. Whence it is also written in Daniel: [[Dan 7:14|he gave him|Dedit ei]], the Ancient of days, [[Dan 7:14|power, and glory, and a kingdom: and all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|potestatem, honorem et regnum; et omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]].

paras.t: Quæ autem sequuntur, possunt esse verba Prophetæ ad Christum. Tecum principium, id est, cum te, o Christe, est Pater exsistens principium tuum, de quo dicis apud Joannem : Omnia mea abs te sunt. Est enim Pater cum Filio, et Filius cum Patre, quia inseparabiles sunt Pater et Filius. Licet namque personaliter distinguantur, essentialiter tamen identificantur. Propter quod Joannes inquit : In principio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum. Tecum ergo, o Fili, est principium, id est Deus Pater, in die virtutis tuæ, id est in die æternitatis, quæ est ipsa æternitas. In hoc die est tecum Pater, quia æternaliter tecum est, et tu coæternus es ei : et in hoc non est prius neque posterius. Propter quod apud Michæam inducitur : Egressus ejus ab initio, a diebus æternitatis. Et in Proverbiis Sapientia Dei, quæ est Christus Dominus, protestatur : Ab æterno ordinata sum ; necdum erant abyssi, et ego jam concepta eram ; ante colles ego parturiebar. Sic autem est tecum principium in die virtutis tuæ, in splendoribus Sanctorum, id est in splendidis cognitionibus Beatorum in patria, quoniam eis a principio mundi innotescit ista coexistentia et coæternitas tua cum Patre : semper quippe vident faciem Patris, ergo et Filii, quoniam Filius (ut est apud Joannem) ait : Qui videt me, videt et Patrem. Dicitur autem æternitas, dies virtutis, id est potentiæ Christi, quia in eo invariabiliter et omnipotenter subsistit. Et ipsa æternitas proprie sumpta, aliud nihil est, nisi Deus æternus ; nec æternitas est mensura aut dies divinæ durationis, nisi secundum rationem.
paras.en: What follows may be the Prophet's words to Christ. [[109:3|With thee is the principality|Tecum principium]] [principium means both 'beginning' or 'source' and 'rule'; here Denis takes it as the Father, the source of the Son], that is, with thee, O Christ, is the Father, who is thy principle, of whom thou sayest in John: [[John 17:7|all things which thou hast given me are from thee|Omnia mea abs te sunt]] [Denis reads 'all my things are from thee']. For the Father is with the Son, and the Son with the Father, since the Father and the Son are inseparable. For though they are distinguished as persons, yet in essence they are one and the same. Wherefore John says: [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word: and the Word was with God|In principio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum]]. With thee, then, O Son, is the principality, that is, God the Father, [[109:3|in the day of thy strength|in die virtutis tuæ]], that is, in the day of eternity, which is eternity itself. In this day the Father is with thee, because he is with thee eternally, and thou art coeternal with him: and in this there is no before nor after. Wherefore in Micheas it is said: [[Mich 5:2|his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity|Egressus ejus ab initio, a diebus æternitatis]]. And in Proverbs the Wisdom of God, who is Christ the Lord, declares: [[Prov 8:23|I was set up from eternity|Ab æterno ordinata sum]]; [[Prov 8:24|The depths were not as yet, and I was already conceived|necdum erant abyssi, et ego jam concepta eram]]; [[Prov 8:25|before the hills, I was brought forth|ante colles ego parturiebar]]. Thus, then, is the principality with thee in the day of thy strength, [[109:3|in the brightness of the saints|in splendoribus Sanctorum]], that is, in the splendid knowledge of the Blessed in the fatherland, since from the beginning of the world this coexistence and coeternity of thine with the Father is made known to them: for they [[Matt 18:10|always see the face|semper quippe vident faciem]] of the Father, and therefore of the Son too, since the Son (as is found in John) says: [[John 14:9|he that seeth me seeth the Father also|Qui videt me, videt et Patrem]]. Now eternity is called the day of strength, that is, of Christ's power, because in it he subsists unchangeably and almightily. And eternity itself, taken properly, is nothing else than the eternal God; nor is eternity a measure or day of the divine duration, except in our way of conceiving it [secundum rationem: a distinction made by the mind, not one in God himself].

paras.t: Alii exponunt aliter, ut sint verba Patris ad Filium : Tecum principium, id est, una eademque principandi auctoritas est mihi tecum, quoniam ego et tu unum sumus in essentia, unus omnium Conditor, unusque universorum Creator. Hinc enim Christus se dixit esse principium, respondens Judæis : Principium, qui et loquor vobis. Istud vero sic esse innotescit in die virtutis tuæ, id est in claritate patriæ, ubi in lumine tuo vident Beati quomodo una sit auctoritas creandi et gubernandi in me atque in te: in splendoribus Sanctorum, id est in plena illustratione electorum in patria. Nam tunc Sancti ista conspiciunt, quando divino lumine perfunduntur, ita ut fulgeant sicut sol in regno Patris eorum. Nunc enim, secundum Apostolum, videmus per speculum in ænigmate : quia per fidem ambulamus, non per speciem. Tunc vero cognoscemus, sicut et cogniti sumus. Unde Joannes in sua Canonica : Similes, inquit, ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est. In hoc igitur verbo declarantur coæternitas atque æqualitas Patris et Filii.
paras.en: Others explain it otherwise, taking these as the words of the Father to the Son: [[109:3|With thee is the principality|Tecum principium]], that is, one and the same authority to rule [principandi, from principium] is mine with thee, since I and thou are one in essence, one Maker of all things and one Creator of the universe. For hence Christ said that he was the principle, answering the Jews: [[John 8:25|The beginning, who also speak unto you|Principium, qui et loquor vobis]]. That this is so is made known [[109:3|in the day of thy strength|in die virtutis tuæ]], that is, in the brightness of the fatherland, where in thy light the Blessed see how there is one authority of creating and governing in me and in thee: [[109:3|in the brightness of the saints|in splendoribus Sanctorum]], that is, in the full illumination of the elect in the fatherland. For then the Saints behold these things, when they are flooded with the divine light, so that they [[Matt 13:43|shine as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father|fulgeant sicut sol in regno Patris eorum]]. For now, according to the Apostle, we see [[1 Cor 13:12|through a glass in a dark manner|per speculum in ænigmate]]: because [[2 Cor 5:7|we walk by faith and not by sight|per fidem ambulamus, non per speciem]]. But then we shall know, even as we are known[[1 Cor 13:12||]]. Whence John in his Epistle [in sua Canonica, that is, his canonical or catholic epistle]: [[1 John 3:2|we shall be like|Similes]], he says, [[1 John 3:2|to him: because we shall see him as he is|ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est]]. In this verse, therefore, the coeternity and equality of the Father and the Son are declared.

paras.t: Ex utero, id est ex proprio corde, ante luciferum, id est ante productionem omnis lucis creatæ, et ante productionem astrorum, quæ nomine Luciferi designantur, genui te generatione æterna, intellectuali, pura et actualissima. Filius namque ex substantia Patris natus est, ita quod immediate procedit a substantia Patris per intellectum emanatione naturali, sicut procedit splendor a lumine. Ipsa quoque generatio Filii a Patre, aliud non est, nisi processus lucis a luce, actus ab actu, et Dei a Deo. In Patre equidem idem sunt essentia, potentia et operatio. Et ita Pater intelligendo se ipsum, intra se profert Verbum sibi simillimum, in hoc solo ab eo distinctum, quia procedit ab eo. Et sicut Pater se ipsum uno intuitu, et omnia alia creanda et creata et creabilia plene cognoscit: sic æternaliter una conceptione interna unicum Verbum intra se gignit, in quo tota sua natura atque perfectio omnino plenissime continetur ac splendet, et in quo omnia alia comprehenduntur ac lucent. Idcirco hoc Verbum est imago Patris, et omnis creaturæ exemplar, proceditque immediate ab intellectu Patris, secundum Thomam in diversis locis. Christus itaque secundum quod Deus, ab æterno est genitus : sicut si sol ab æterno fuisset, splendor ab æterno ab eo manasset et ortus fuisset. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico testatur : Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam. Et in Sapientiæ libro ait : Sapientia tua, Domine, novit opera tua : quæ et adfuit tunc quum orbem terrarum faceres, et sciebat quid placitum esset oculis tuis. In his verbis evidenter ostenditur duplex esse sapientia in Deo, videlicet genita et ingenita.
paras.en: [[109:3|from the womb|Ex utero]], that is, from my own heart, [[109:3|before the day star|ante luciferum]], that is, before the bringing forth of any created light, and before the bringing forth of the stars, which are signified by the name of Lucifer [lucifer, 'light-bearer', the morning star], [[109:3|I begot thee|genui te]] by a generation eternal, intellectual, pure and most fully in act. For the Son is born of the substance of the Father, in such a way that he proceeds immediately from the substance of the Father through the intellect by a natural emanation, as brightness proceeds from light. And the generation of the Son from the Father is itself nothing else than the procession of light from light, of act from act, and of God from God. For in the Father essence, power and operation are the same. And so the Father, understanding himself, utters within himself a Word most like himself, distinct from him in this alone, that it proceeds from him. And as the Father knows himself, and all other things, those to be created, those created and those that can be created, fully in one gaze, so eternally by one inner conception he begets within himself a single Word, in which his whole nature and perfection is contained and shines forth altogether most fully, and in which all other things are comprehended and shine. Therefore this Word is the image of the Father and the exemplar of every creature, and proceeds immediately from the intellect of the Father, according to Thomas in various places. Christ, then, as he is God, is begotten from eternity: just as, if the sun had existed from eternity, its brightness would have flowed and arisen from it from eternity. Wherefore he testifies in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 24:5|I came out of the mouth of the most High, the firstborn before all creatures|Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam]]. And in the book of Wisdom it says: [[Wis 9:9|thy wisdom|Sapientia tua]], O Lord, [[Wis 9:9|which knoweth thy works, which then also was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was agreeable to thy eyes|novit opera tua : quæ et adfuit tunc quum orbem terrarum faceres, et sciebat quid placitum esset oculis tuis]]. In these words it is plainly shown that wisdom in God is twofold, namely begotten and unbegotten.

paras.t: Insuper agit Propheta de sacerdotio Christi. Juravit Dominus, id est, irretractabiliter affirmavit, firmiterque spopondit, et non pœnitebit eum ita jurasse, quod sequitur: Tu, Christe, in quantum homo, es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech. Christus non obtulit sacrificia legis, quæ sacerdotibus filiis Aaron incumbebat offerre: sed fuit sacerdos offerendo se ipsum Deo, et reconciliando mundum Patri æterno, per crucem dissolvens inimicitias in semetipso, secundum Apostolum ad Ephesios. Qui iterum ait : Christus tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem et hostiam in odorem suavitatis; et ad Hebræos : Christus adsistens pontifex futurorum bonorum, per proprium sanguinem introivit semel in Sancta, æterna redemptione inventa. De excellentia autem sacerdotii Christi dicit Apostolus : Talis decebat ut esset nobis pontifex, sanctus, innocens, impollutus et excelsior cœlis factus. Unde in Zacharia dicitur : Ipse portabit gloriam, et sedebit, et dominabitur, et erit sacerdos super solio suo. Denique, quomodo Christus dicatur sacerdos in æternum, declarat Apostolus ad Hebræos, dicens : Christus eo quod maneat in æternum, sempiternum habet sacerdotium. Unde et salvare potest in perpetuum, accedens per semetipsum ad Deum, semper vivens ad interpellandum pro nobis. Sacerdotis quippe officium est, inter Deum ac populum mediatorem et advocatum existere, preces populi Deo offerre, Deum placare, populo benedicere. Omnia autem hæc congruunt Christo. Propter quod in Canonica Joannis inducitur: Si quis peccaverit, advocatum habemus apud Patrem, Jesum Christum justum; et ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris.
paras.en: Further, the Prophet treats of the priesthood of Christ. [[109:4|The Lord hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]], that is, he has irrevocably affirmed and firmly promised, [[109:4|and he will not repent|et non pœnitebit eum]] of having so sworn what follows: [[109:4|Thou|Tu]], O Christ, as man, [[109:4|art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech|es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech]]. Christ did not offer the sacrifices of the law, which it fell to the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer; but he was a priest by offering himself to God, and by reconciling the world to the eternal Father, [[Eph 2:16|by the cross, killing the enmities in himself|per crucem dissolvens inimicitias in semetipso]], according to the Apostle to the Ephesians. And again he says: Christ [[Eph 5:2|hath delivered himself for us, an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness|tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem et hostiam in odorem suavitatis]]; and to the Hebrews: [[Heb 9:11|Christ, being come an high Priest of the good things to come|Christus adsistens pontifex futurorum bonorum]], [[Heb 9:12|by his own blood, entered once into the Holies, having obtained eternal redemption|per proprium sanguinem introivit semel in Sancta, æterna redemptione inventa]]. And of the excellence of Christ's priesthood the Apostle says: [[Heb 7:26|it was fitting that we should have such a high priest, holy, innocent, undefiled|Talis decebat ut esset nobis pontifex, sanctus, innocens, impollutus]] [[Heb 7:26|and made higher than the heavens|et excelsior cœlis factus]]. Whence it is said in Zacharias: [[Zach 6:13|he shall bear the glory, and shall sit, and rule|Ipse portabit gloriam, et sedebit, et dominabitur]], [[Zach 6:13|and he shall be a priest upon his throne|et erit sacerdos super solio suo]]. Lastly, how Christ is called a priest for ever the Apostle declares to the Hebrews, saying: Christ, [[Heb 7:24|for that he continueth for ever, hath an everlasting priesthood|eo quod maneat in æternum, sempiternum habet sacerdotium]]. [[Heb 7:25|Whereby he is able also to save for ever|Unde et salvare potest in perpetuum]], drawing near through himself to God [Denis reads accedens, 'drawing near', where the Vulgate has 'them that come to God by him'], [[Heb 7:25|always living to make intercession for us|semper vivens ad interpellandum pro nobis]]. For the office of a priest[[Heb 5:1||]] is to stand as mediator and advocate between God and the people, to offer the people's prayers to God, to appease God, and to bless the people. And all these things befit Christ. Wherefore it is said in the Epistle of John: [[1 John 2:1|if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the just|Si quis peccaverit, advocatum habemus apud Patrem, Jesum Christum justum]]; [[1 John 2:2|and he is the propitiation for our sins|et ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris]].

paras.t: Dicitur quoque Christus, sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech: Primo, quoniam sicut Melchisedech obtulit Deo panem et vinum, ut legitur in Genesi; sic Christus sub formis panis et vini, corpus suum et sanguinem obtulit seu dedit discipulis, convertendo panem in corpus, et vinum in sanguinem. Secundo, quoniam sicut Melchisedech sine patre et matre ac genealogia fuisse asseritur, non quia non habuit, sed quia Scriptura propter mysterium ea subticuit; sic Christus sine humanæ generationis naturali ordine natus est, et vere fuit æternus. Hinc namque dicit Apostolus: Præcursor pro nobis introiit Jesus, secundum ordinem Melchisedech pontifex factus in æternum. Et denuo: Melchisedech rex Salem (quod est, rex pacis) sine patre, sine matre, assimilatus Filio Dei.
paras.en: Christ is also called [[109:4|a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech|sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech]]: first, because as Melchisedech offered bread and wine to God, as we read in Genesis[[Gen 14:18||]], so Christ under the forms of bread and wine offered, or gave, his body and blood to his disciples, changing the bread into his body[[Matt 26:26||]] and the wine into his blood[[Matt 26:28||]]. Secondly, because as Melchisedech is said to have been without father and mother and genealogy[[Heb 7:1||]][[Heb 7:3||]], not because he had none, but because Scripture passed them over in silence for the sake of a mystery, so Christ was born without the natural order of human generation, and was truly eternal. For hence the Apostle says: [[Heb 6:20|the forerunner Jesus is entered for us, made a high priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech|Præcursor pro nobis introiit Jesus, secundum ordinem Melchisedech pontifex factus in æternum]] [the margin gives Heb. vii, 20; the words are those of Heb 6:20]. And again: [[Heb 7:1|Melchisedech was king of Salem|Melchisedech rex Salem]] ([[Heb 7:2|that is, king of peace|quod est, rex pacis]]), [[Heb 7:3|Without father, without mother|sine patre, sine matre]], [[Heb 7:3|likened unto the Son of God|assimilatus Filio Dei]].

paras.t: Hæc ergo juravit Deus Christo homini. In ipso enim momento, quo animam ejus creavit, revelavit ei hoc ipsum. Et non pœnitebit eum. Pœnitentia namque proprie dicta, in Deo locum non habet, prout in libro Regum scriptum est: Porro Triumphator in Israel non parcet, et pœnitudine non flectetur: neque enim homo est, ut agat pœnitentiam. Et tamen eodem capitulo Dominus ait ad Samuelem: Pœnitet me quod constituerim Saul regem; sed hoc dicitur propter similitudinem operis, non propter veritatem affectus. Loquitur enim Deus frequenter in Scripturis sanctis more humano.
paras.en: These things, then, God swore to Christ as man: for in the very moment in which he created his soul he revealed this very thing to it. [[109:4|And he will not repent|Et non pœnitebit eum]]. For repentance properly so called has no place in God, as is written in the book of Kings: [[1 Kings 15:29|But the triumpher in Israel will not spare, and will not be moved to repentance: for he is not a man that he should repent|Porro Triumphator in Israel non parcet, et pœnitudine non flectetur: neque enim homo est, ut agat pœnitentiam]]. And yet in the same chapter the Lord says to Samuel: [[1 Kings 15:11|It repenteth me that I have made Saul king|Pœnitet me quod constituerim Saul regem]]; but this is said by reason of a likeness in the work, not of any real affection. For God often speaks in the holy Scriptures after the manner of men.

paras.t: Dominus a dextris tuis. Hoc dupliciter accipi potest. Primo sic: Dominus Pater seu Deus trinus, existens a dextris tuis, o Christe, sicut de te ipso in præcedenti psalmo dixisti, Confitebor Domino nimis in ore meo, quia adstitit a dextris pauperis (quod illic expositum est); supra quoque, Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper, quoniam a dextris est mihi ne commovear. Vel sic: Dominus Christus qui est omnium Dominus, exsistens et residens a dextris tuis, o Deus Pater, sicut paulo ante dixisti, Sede a dextris meis. Confregit in die iræ suæ, id est tempore suæ vindictæ: de quo per Isaiam dicit, Dies ultionis in corde meo; reges infideles, privando eos in hoc mundo vita gratiæ, vel etiam vita corporali, et postmodum æternaliter eos damnando. Potissimum autem loquitur nunc de illorum regum confractione, de quibus supra dictum est: Adstiterunt reges terræ, et principes convenerunt in unum adversus Dominum et adversus Christum ejus. Hi enim reges (sumendo nomen regis communiter pro præsidente), videlicet Herodes, Pilatus, et principes Judæorum, prædicto modo ex divina ultione confracti sunt: quæ confractio adscribi potest cuilibet Personæ in divinis, quoniam effectus superglorissimæ Trinitatis sunt indivisi. Unde per Isaiam Christus testatus est: Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea.
paras.en: [[109:5|The Lord at thy right hand|Dominus a dextris tuis]]. This can be taken in two ways. First thus: the Lord, the Father, or God three in one, being at thy right hand, O Christ, as thou didst say of thyself in the preceding psalm: [[Ps 108:30|I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth|Confitebor Domino nimis in ore meo]], [[Ps 108:31|Because he hath stood at the right hand of the poor|quia adstitit a dextris pauperis]] (as was explained there); and above too: [[Ps 15:8|I set the Lord always in my sight: for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved|Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper, quoniam a dextris est mihi ne commovear]]. Or thus: the Lord Christ ([[Acts 10:36|He is Lord of all|qui est omnium Dominus]]) [the margin sets Acts x, 36 a line lower, beside 'kings'], being and residing at thy right hand, O God the Father, as thou didst say a little before: [[109:1|Sit thou at my right hand|Sede a dextris meis]]. He [[109:5|hath broken|Confregit]] [[109:5|in the day of his wrath|in die iræ suæ]], that is, in the time of his vengeance, of which he says through Isaias: [[Is 63:4|the day of vengeance is in my heart|Dies ultionis in corde meo]]; [[109:5|kings|reges]], unbelieving ones, depriving them in this world of the life of grace, or even of the life of the body, and afterwards condemning them eternally. But he speaks here chiefly of the breaking of those kings of whom it was said above: [[Ps 2:2|The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, against the Lord, and against his Christ|Adstiterunt reges terræ, et principes convenerunt in unum adversus Dominum et adversus Christum ejus]]. For these kings (taking the name of king broadly for anyone who presides), namely Herod, Pilate and the princes of the Jews, were broken in the aforesaid manner by the divine vengeance; and this breaking can be ascribed to any Person in the Godhead, since the works of the supremely glorious Trinity are undivided. Whence Christ testified through Isaias: [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]].

paras.t: Judicabit in nationibus, implebit ruinas. Duplex est Christi adventus. Primus fuit ut judicaretur, secundus erit ut judicet. Propter quod ait Apostolus: Christus semel passus est ad multorum exhaurienda peccata. Secundo autem sine peccato apparebit exspectantibus se in salutem. Secundum hoc duplex est judicium, scilicet judicium discretionis, et judicium remunerationis. Primum judicium fecit Christus in primo suo adventu, et usque ad finem mundi hoc facit, quosdam vocando ad fidem et gratiam, quosdam vero deserendo occulto quidem, sed justo judicio: de quo ante passionem dixit: Nunc judicium est mundi, nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras. Christus ergo in primo suo adventu, et usque in præsens, judicabit in nationibus, id est ipsas nationes, faciendo in gentibus judicium discretionis, quosdam misericorditer adjuvando, ceteras juste derelinquendo. In secundo autem adventu judicabit in nationibus, justas salvando, impiasque damnando, quemadmodum apud Joannem locutus est : Veniet hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem ejus : et procedent qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitæ; qui vero mala, in resurrectionem judicii, id est damnationis. In primo autem adventu et in judicio quod nunc agitur, implet Christus ruinas, id est defectus humanos, gratiam infundendo cordibus vacuis, mentesque inanes ditando spiritualibus bonis. In futuro vero judicio, de his qui salvantur implebit ruinas angelorum, restaurando mansiones cœlestes, angelorum casu evacuatas.
paras.en: [[109:6|He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins|Judicabit in nationibus, implebit ruinas]]. The coming of Christ is twofold: the first was that he might be judged, the second will be that he may judge. Wherefore the Apostle says: Christ suffered [[Heb 9:28|once to exhaust the sins of many|semel passus est ad multorum exhaurienda peccata]] [Denis reads passus est, 'suffered', for the Vulgate's 'was offered']. [[Heb 9:28|The second time he shall appear without sin to them that expect him unto salvation|Secundo autem sine peccato apparebit exspectantibus se in salutem]]. Accordingly the judgment is twofold, namely the judgment of discernment and the judgment of retribution. The first judgment Christ made in his first coming, and he makes it until the end of the world, calling some to faith and grace and forsaking others, by a judgment hidden indeed, but just: of which he said before the passion: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc judicium est mundi, nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]. Christ, then, in his first coming and up to the present, [[109:6|shall judge among nations|judicabit in nationibus]], that is, judges the nations themselves, making among the Gentiles the judgment of discernment, mercifully helping some and justly abandoning the rest. But in his second coming he will judge among the nations by saving the just and condemning the wicked, as he spoke in John: [[John 5:28|the hour cometh wherein all that are in the graves shall hear the voice|Veniet hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem]] of him: [[John 5:29|And they that have done good things shall come forth unto the resurrection of life: but they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment|et procedent qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitæ; qui vero mala, in resurrectionem judicii]], that is, of damnation. In the first coming, then, and in the judgment now going on, Christ [[109:6|shall fill|implet]] [[109:6|ruins|ruinas]], that is, he makes good human failings, pouring grace into empty hearts and enriching empty minds with spiritual goods. But in the judgment to come, out of those who are saved [[109:6|he shall fill|implebit]] the ruins of the angels, restoring the heavenly mansions left empty by the fall of the angels.

paras.t: Conquassabit capita, id est corda humiliabit, in terra multorum, id est in multis locis et habitaculis hominum. In omni enim terra fidelium humiliavit quosdam superbos. In finali autem judicio conquassabit, id est, æternaliter condemnabit, capita in terra multorum, id est capitaneos in multis terris cum elatione regnantes. Unde in Isaia scriptum est : Dominus exercituum cogitavit hoc, ut detraheret superbiam omnis gloriæ, et ad ignominiam deducere universos inclytos terræ. Præterea Christo, secundum quod Deus est, competit judiciaria potestas auctoritative ; sed prout homo est, convenit ei instrumentaliter, et sic meruit eam per suam humiliationem et passionem. Propter quod ait loquens de Patre atque se ipso : Dedit ei potestatem et judicium facere, quia Filius hominis est. Et hoc est, quod modo subjungitur :
paras.en: [[109:6|he shall crush the heads|Conquassabit capita]], that is, he will humble hearts, [[109:6|in the land of many|in terra multorum]], that is, in many places and dwellings of men. For in every land of the faithful he has humbled some proud men. But in the final judgment he will crush, that is, condemn eternally, the heads in the land of many, that is, the chiefs [capitaneos, from caput, 'head'] reigning with pride in many lands. Whence it is written in Isaias: [[Is 23:9|The Lord of hosts hath designed it, to pull down the pride of all glory, and bring to disgrace all the glorious ones of the earth|Dominus exercituum cogitavit hoc, ut detraheret superbiam omnis gloriæ, et ad ignominiam deducere universos inclytos terræ]]. Moreover, judicial power belongs to Christ as God by his own authority; but as man it belongs to him as an instrument, and so he merited it by his humiliation and passion. Wherefore he says, speaking of the Father and of himself: [[John 5:27|he hath given him power to do judgment, because he is the Son of man|Dedit ei potestatem et judicium facere, quia Filius hominis est]]. And this is what is now added:

paras.t: De torrente in via bibet : id est, Christus in hoc mundo pœnas, tribulationes et mortem acerbissimam patietur, sicque de torrente tribulationum bibet, gustando adversa. De hujus torrentis potatione dixit Joanni et Jacobo : Potestis bibere calicem quem ego bibiturus sum? Quod autem nomine torrentis, tribulationis magnitudo designetur, patet per illud Isaiæ : Spiritus ejus velut torrens inundans ad perdendas gentes in nihilum. Propterea, id est merito hujus potationis, exaltabit Christus caput suum, id est, glorificabit et eriget semetipsum, resurgendo in corpore glorioso, et ascendendo ad Patrem, quatenus sedeat secum, tanquam universorum judex ac Dominus. Christus enim ut Deus, suscitavit, exaltavit et glorificavit se ipsum ut homo est. Et ideo apud Joannem profitetur : Potestatem habeo ponendi animam meam, et potestatem habeo iterum sumendi eam. Et quoniam opera sanctæ Trinitatis sunt indivisa, idcirco exaltatio ista attribui potest unicuique divinæ Personæ. Christus namque apud eundem Evangelistam : Quæcumque (inquit) facit Pater, hæc et similiter Filius facit. Et de Spiritu Sancto dicit Apostolus : Hæc omnia operatur unus atque idem Spiritus. Opera igitur superbenedictæ Trinitatis sunt indivisa.
paras.en: [[109:7|He shall drink of the torrent in the way|De torrente in via bibet]]: that is, Christ will suffer in this world pains, tribulations and a most bitter death, and so he will drink of the torrent of tribulations, tasting adversity. Of the drinking of this torrent he said to John and James: [[Matt 20:22|Can you drink the chalice that I shall drink?|Potestis bibere calicem quem ego bibiturus sum?]] That the greatness of tribulation is signified by the name of torrent is clear from that word of Isaias: [[Is 30:28|His breath as a torrent overflowing|Spiritus ejus velut torrens inundans]] [[Is 30:28|to destroy the nations unto nothing|ad perdendas gentes in nihilum]]. [[109:7|therefore|Propterea]], that is, by the merit of this drinking, [[109:7|shall he lift up|exaltabit]] (Christ, that is) his [[109:7|head|caput]], that is, he will glorify and raise up himself, rising again in a glorious body and ascending to the Father, that he may sit with him as Judge and Lord of all. For Christ as God raised up, exalted and glorified himself as he is man. And therefore he professes in John: [[John 10:18|I have power to lay it down|Potestatem habeo ponendi animam meam]]: [[John 10:18|and I have power to take it up again|et potestatem habeo iterum sumendi eam]]. And since the works of the holy Trinity are undivided, this exaltation can be attributed to each divine Person. For Christ says in the same Evangelist: [[John 5:19|what things soever|Quæcumque]] (he says) the Father doth, [[John 5:19|these the Son also doth in like manner|hæc et similiter Filius facit]]. And of the Holy Ghost the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 12:11|all these things, one and the same Spirit worketh|Hæc omnia operatur unus atque idem Spiritus]]. The works of the supremely blessed Trinity, therefore, are undivided.

paras.t: Porro in expositione hujus psalmi circa illud, Juravit Dominus, dicit Hugo, quod Deus legitur tribus locis jurasse : videlicet in Genesi, dicens ad Abraham, Per memetipsum juravi ; item hoc loco ; infra quoque in psalmo centesimo tricesimo primo, ubi scriptum est, Juravit Dominus David veritatem. Sed istud non est intelligendum præcise, quia multo frequentius quam ter, legitur in Scriptura canonica Deus jurasse. In Isaia namque ait Pater : In memetipso juravi, Egredietur de ore meo justitiæ verbum. Et in propheta Amos scriptum est : Juravit Dominus Deus in anima sua, Detestor ego superbiam Jacob. Supra quoque in psalmo octogesimo octavo qui incipit, Misericordias Domini, Dominus loquitur : Juravi David servo meo, Usque in æternum præparabo semen tuum. Et apud Lucam ait Zacharias : Jusjurandum quod juravit ad Abraham patrem nostrum. Et ad Hebræos Apostolus : Deus (inquit) interposuit jusjurandum. Et alibi quoque legitur Deus jurasse.
paras.en: Further, in his exposition of this psalm, on the words [[109:4|The Lord hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]], Hugh [probably Hugh of Saint-Cher, the Dominican cardinal and commentator] says that God is read to have sworn in three places: namely in Genesis, saying to Abraham, [[Gen 22:16|By my own self have I sworn|Per memetipsum juravi]]; again in this place; and further on in the hundred and thirty-first psalm, where it is written: [[Ps 131:11|The Lord hath sworn truth to David|Juravit Dominus David veritatem]]. But this is not to be understood strictly, for God is read in canonical Scripture to have sworn far more often than three times. For in Isaias the Father says: [[Is 45:23|I have sworn by myself, the word of justice shall go out of my mouth|In memetipso juravi, Egredietur de ore meo justitiæ verbum]]. And in the prophet Amos it is written: [[Amos 6:8|The Lord God hath sworn by his own soul|Juravit Dominus Deus in anima sua]], [[Amos 6:8|I detest the pride of Jacob|Detestor ego superbiam Jacob]]. Above also, in the eighty-eighth psalm, which begins Misericordias Domini [The mercies of the Lord], the Lord speaks: [[Ps 88:4|I have sworn to David my servant|Juravi David servo meo]], [[Ps 88:5|Thy seed will I settle for ever|Usque in æternum præparabo semen tuum]]. And in Luke Zachary says: [[Luke 1:73|The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father|Jusjurandum quod juravit ad Abraham patrem nostrum]]. And the Apostle to the Hebrews: God (he says) [[Heb 6:17|interposed an oath|interposuit jusjurandum]]. And elsewhere too God is read to have sworn.

paras.t: Ecce psalmus iste verbo brevis, quam infinitus est sensu. Ostenditur enim in eo duplex Christi natura, simplexque seu una persona. Describitur in eo Christi ad Patrem locatio, inimicorum ejus dejectio, christianæ fidei promulgatio, coæternitas quoque et consubstantialitas Patris ac Filii. Declaratur etiam sacerdotium Christi, et judicialis ejus potestas, ac finale judicium, in psalmo præsenti. Quem decet nos cum multa reverentia, cum devotione præcipua, cum contemplatione profunda proferre, propter dignitatem, dulcedinem, et altitudinem sensuum ejus.
paras.en: Behold how this psalm, brief in words, is boundless in sense. For in it is shown the twofold nature of Christ, and his simple, that is, single, person. In it are described Christ's placing beside the Father, the casting down of his enemies, the publishing of the Christian faith, and also the coeternity and consubstantiality of the Father and the Son. In the present psalm are declared, too, the priesthood of Christ, his judicial power, and the final judgment. It befits us to recite it with great reverence, with special devotion, with deep contemplation, because of the dignity, sweetness and loftiness of its senses.

paras.t: Precatio. Jesu salvator sæculorum, secundum ordinem Melchisedech rex et sacerdos factus in æternum, ineffabili tua miseratione, a dextris tuis in judicio nos constitue ; atque inter benedictos Patris tui deputatos, regnum cœleste fac possidere : qui cum eodem Patre, etc.
paras.en: Prayer. O Jesus, Saviour of the ages, made king and priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech, of thy ineffable mercy set us at thy right hand in the judgment; and, numbered among the blessed of thy Father, make us possess the heavenly kingdom: who with the same Father, etc.

110.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI DECIMI : CONFITEBOR TIBI, DOMINE.
110.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and tenth psalm: I will praise thee, O Lord.

paras.t: Hujus psalmi titulus est : Alleluia, quod significat, Laudate Deum : de cujus præconiis perpulchre atque jucunde tractat hic psalmus, præsertim de admirabilissimo opere Dei in consecratione corporis et sanguinis Christi. Sicut enim psalmus præcedens tractat de sacerdotio Christi, sic iste determinat de institutione sacrificii hujus, et efficacia Sacramenti altaris.
paras.en: The title of this psalm is *Alleluia*, which means, Praise ye God: and of his praises this psalm treats most beautifully and delightfully, above all of the most wonderful work of God in the consecration of the body and blood of Christ. For as the preceding psalm treats of the priesthood of Christ, so this one deals with the institution of this sacrifice, and the efficacy of the Sacrament of the altar.

paras.t: Loquens itaque sanctus Propheta in propria, atque Ecclesiæ omniumque fidelium persona, dicit : Confitebor tibi, id est, laudabo te, Domine, in toto corde meo, id est ex toto intellectu et affectu, mente collecta et fixa. Cor hoc loco non pro organo corporis, sed pro anima ponitur. Anima autem immaterialis est, nec partes habet : quomodo ergo perhibet se Domino confiteri toto corde, tanquam posset ei confiteri pro parte cordis? Et respondendum, quod anima non habet partes quantitativas, quum sit incorporalis ; nec essentiales, quum sit forma simplex ; sed potestativas, id est vires distinctas. Vires autem seu partes potestativæ animæ rationalis, in quantum est rationalis, sunt tres, in quibus summæ Trinitatis imago consistit in anima, scilicet intellectus, memoria, et voluntas. Ad intellectum spectat cognitio, ad voluntatem dilectio, ad memoriam in utroque firma inhæsio. Toto igitur corde Domino confitetur, qui intellectu, voluntate atque memoria eum collaudat : ita quod intellectu advertit, voluntate diligit, memoria retinet verba divina, quibus Domino confessionem laudis sacrificat. Qui autem Deum ore laudat, et mente illicita amat aut cogitat, non toto corde Domino confitetur. Unde de quibusdam animo vagabundis ac vagis scriptum est : Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt. Et in Jeremia Dominus loquitur : Si reverteris, convertere, id est, si tu, o homo, cor tuum ad Deum convertere optas, toto corde ad eum convertere, adhærendo ei perfecte, eique totis viribus ministrando, ne sis tepidus ac divisus. Confitebor autem tibi, o Domine, non inconsulte, indiscrete, aut vana intentione, sed in consilio justorum, id est eo modo quo justorum consilium est, te laudare. Justorum namque consilium est, te laudare corde a vitiis expurgato, quum non sit speciosa laus in ore peccatoris ; et propter nominis tui amorem atque honorem, non propter temporale emolumentum aut laudem humanam. Et congregatione justorum, id est, non in conventiculis hæreticorum, sed in Ecclesia fidelium tibi confitebor.
paras.en: So the holy Prophet, speaking in his own person and in that of the Church and of all the faithful, says: [[110:1|I will praise thee|Confitebor tibi]] [Latin *confitebor*, "I will confess", here in the sense of praising], that is, I will laud thee, [[110:1|O Lord, with my whole heart|Domine, in toto corde meo]], that is, with my whole understanding and affection, with the mind recollected and fixed. *Heart* in this place stands not for the bodily organ but for the soul. But the soul is immaterial and has no parts: how then does he declare that he praises the Lord with his whole heart, as though he could praise him with a part of the heart? The answer is that the soul has no quantitative parts, since it is incorporeal; nor essential parts, since it is a simple form; but potential parts [*partes potestativæ*: the parts of a whole that are distinct powers, not pieces], that is, distinct powers. Now the powers or potential parts of the rational soul, in so far as it is rational, are three, and in them the image of the supreme Trinity in the soul consists: namely understanding, memory and will. To the understanding belongs knowledge, to the will love, to the memory a firm cleaving in both. He therefore praises the Lord with his whole heart who lauds him with understanding, will and memory: so that with the understanding he attends to, with the will he loves, and with the memory he retains the divine words with which he offers the Lord the sacrifice of the confession of praise. But he who praises God with his mouth, and in his mind loves or thinks on unlawful things, does not praise the Lord with his whole heart. Hence it is written of certain men wandering and unsettled in mind: [[Osee 10:2|Their heart is divided: now they shall perish|Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt]]. And in Jeremias the Lord says: [[Jer 4:1|If thou wilt return|Si reverteris]], be converted; that is, if thou, O man, desirest to turn thy heart to God, turn to him with thy whole heart, cleaving to him perfectly and serving him with all thy strength, lest thou be lukewarm[[Apoc 3:16||]] and divided. But I will praise thee, O Lord, not rashly, indiscreetly or with a vain intention, but [[110:1|in the council of the just|in consilio justorum]] [Latin *consilium*, both "council" and "counsel"], that is, in the way in which it is the counsel of the just to praise thee. For the counsel of the just is to praise thee with a heart cleansed of vices, since [[Ecclus 15:9|Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner|non sit speciosa laus in ore peccatoris]]; and for the love and honour of thy name, not for temporal gain or human praise. And [[110:1|in the congregation|congregatione]] of the just, that is, not in the conventicles of heretics but in the Church of the faithful, will I praise thee.

paras.t: Cur autem Domino confiteatur, subjungit : Magna opera Domini, id est, magnifice facta, seu laude admirationeque digna sunt : ut patet de creatione cœli et terræ, de gubernatione universi, de operibus recreationis, glorificationis ac ceteris Dei effectibus. Effectus quippe proportionatur et correspondet suæ causæ. Quum ergo Deus sublimis et benedictus sit infinitæ magnitudinis, sapientiæ et dignitatis, decuit magna ab eo opera fieri. Exquisita, id est exquisite producta, in omnes voluntates ejus, id est secundum omne desiderium seu beneplacitum Creatoris. Singula namque produxit tunc, taliter, ideo, ubi, et secundum quod voluit. Propter quod per Isaiam testatur : Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet. Et Apostolus ait : Deus operatur omnia secundum consilium voluntatis suæ. Sed quum in Deo non sit nisi una, æterna, simplex, invariabilisque voluntas, cur nunc pluraliter dictum est, In omnes voluntates ejus? Et respondendum, quod sicut in Deo dicuntur plures ideæ seu multæ notitiæ, per respectum ad creaturas ; sic dicuntur plures voluntates, secundum rationem nostram, per comparationem ad volita creata, quæ multa sunt.
paras.en: Why he praises the Lord, he adds: [[110:2|Great are the works of the Lord|Magna opera Domini]], that is, they are magnificently done, or worthy of praise and wonder: as is plain from the creation of heaven and earth, from the governance of the universe, from the works of re-creation and of glorification, and from the other effects of God. For an effect is proportioned and corresponds to its cause. Since then God, sublime and blessed, is of infinite greatness, wisdom and dignity, it was fitting that great works should be done by him. [[110:2|sought out|Exquisita]], that is, exquisitely produced, [[110:2|according to all his wills|in omnes voluntates ejus]], that is, according to every desire or good pleasure of the Creator. For he produced each thing at the time, in the manner, for the reason, in the place and according as he willed. Wherefore he testifies through Isaias: [[Is 46:10|My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done|Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet]]. And the Apostle says: God [[Eph 1:11|worketh all things according to the counsel of his will|operatur omnia secundum consilium voluntatis suæ]]. But since in God there is only one will, eternal, simple and unchangeable, why is it said here in the plural, [[110:2|according to all his wills|In omnes voluntates ejus]]? The answer is that, as many ideas or many notions are said to be in God by relation to creatures, so many wills are spoken of, according to our way of understanding, by comparison with the created things willed, which are many.

paras.t: Confessio, id est Dei laudatio, seu propriæ culpæ prolatio, et magnificentia, id est magnifica operatio ad Dei honorem exhibita, sunt opus ejus, id est opera Deo placentia, et nobis ab eo concessa. Omne enim bonum ab ipso procedit, et hæc duo opera Deo præcipue placent, nec nobis insunt nisi ex gratia Dei : ideo Deo magis quam nobis attribuuntur. Et justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi. Justitia namque in Deo exsistens, quæ est ipsemet Deus, æterna est, sicut divina essentia, a qua sola ratione distinguitur. Justitia quoque, quæ est effectus divinæ æquitatis, in perpetuum perseverabit, quoniam electorum gloria et impiorum miseria nunquam cessabunt.
paras.en: [[110:3|praise|Confessio]] [Latin *confessio*: both praise and confession], that is, the praising of God, or the avowal of one's own guilt, [[110:3|and magnificence|et magnificentia]], that is, magnificent work done for the honour of God, are [[110:3|His work|opus ejus]], that is, works pleasing to God and granted to us by him. For every good proceeds from him, and these two works especially please God, and are not in us save by the grace of God: therefore they are attributed to God rather than to us. [[110:3|and his justice continueth for ever and ever|Et justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi]]. For justice as it exists in God, which is God himself, is eternal, like the divine essence, from which it is distinguished only in reason. Justice also, which is the effect of the divine equity, will endure for ever, since the glory of the elect and the misery of the wicked will never cease.

paras.t: Memoriam fecit mirabilium suorum misericors et miserator Dominus, etc. Versiculus iste nec melius nec litteralius valet exponi, quam de institutione ac alimonia Sacramenti altaris, ut sit sensus : Dominus Christus qui est misericors in natura et miserator in actu, fecit memoriam, id est, memoriale instituit, mirabilium suorum, id est incarnationis, dilectionis, conversationis ac passionis suæ. In Cœna enim novissima, recessurus a suis corporali præsentia, volens nos jugiter memores esse eximiæ suæ dilectionis atque amarissimæ passionis, imo omnium quæ pro nostra salute tam dignanter assumpsit, fecit, ac pertulit, Sacramentum corporis ac sanguinis sui instituit, panem convertens in corpus, et vinum in sanguinem. Sicque sub speciebus panis et vini, escam dedit timentibus se, id est, corpus et sanguinem dedit Apostolis, et per eos ac successores eorum dari commisit universis fidelibus : propter quod dixit, Hoc facite in meam commemorationem. Unde Apostolus : Quotiescumque, inquit, manducabitis panem hunc, et calicem bibetis, mortem Domini annuntiabitis donec veniat. De hac etiam esca Christus apud Joannem locutus est : Caro mea vere est cibus, et sanguis meus vere est potus.
paras.en: [[110:4|He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord|Memoriam fecit mirabilium suorum misericors et miserator Dominus]], etc. This verse can be expounded neither better nor more literally than of the institution and nourishment of the Sacrament of the altar, so that the sense is: The Lord Christ, who is merciful in nature and gracious [*miserator*, one who shows mercy] in act, made a remembrance, that is, instituted a memorial, of his wonderful works, that is, of his incarnation, his love, his life among men and his passion. For at the Last Supper, being about to depart from his own in bodily presence, and wishing us to be ever mindful of his surpassing love and most bitter passion, nay, of all that he so condescendingly took upon himself, did and endured for our salvation, he instituted the Sacrament of his body and blood, changing bread into his body and wine into his blood. And so, under the species of bread and wine, [[110:5|He hath given food to them that fear him|escam dedit timentibus se]], that is, he gave his body and blood to the Apostles, and through them and their successors commanded it to be given to all the faithful: wherefore he said, [[Luke 22:19|Do this for a commemoration of me|Hoc facite in meam commemorationem]]. Hence the Apostle: [[1 Cor 11:26|as often as|Quotiescumque]], he says, [[1 Cor 11:26|you shall eat this bread and drink the chalice, you shall shew the death of the Lord, until he come|manducabitis panem hunc, et calicem bibetis, mortem Domini annuntiabitis donec veniat]]. Of this food too Christ spoke in John: [[John 6:56|my flesh is meat indeed: and my blood is drink indeed|Caro mea vere est cibus, et sanguis meus vere est potus]].

paras.t: Memor erit ipse Christus in sæculum, id est indesinenter, testamenti sui, id est hujus Sacramenti, quod dicitur testamentum, juxta illud Apostoli : Hic calix novum testamentum est in meo sanguine. Hujus testamenti seu Sacramenti erit Christus in perpetuum memor, per hoc quod omnibus hoc Sacramentum devote fideliterque sumentibus confert gratiam in præsenti, et vitam æternam in futuro, sicut promisit dicens : Qui manducat meam carnem et bibit meum sanguinem, in me manet et ego in eo ; rursusque, Qui manducat hunc panem, vivet in æternum. Vel dicitur Christus semper memor futurus hujus testamenti, quoniam facit nos memores ejus, conservabitque fidem hujus Sacramenti in cordibus hominum usque ad sæculi consummationem.
paras.en: [[110:5|He will be mindful|Memor erit]] Christ himself [[110:5|for ever|in sæculum]], that is, unceasingly, [[110:5|of his covenant|testamenti sui]] [Latin *testamentum*, both "covenant" and "testament"], that is, of this Sacrament, which is called a testament, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 11:25|This chalice is the new testament in my blood|Hic calix novum testamentum est in meo sanguine]]. Of this testament or Sacrament Christ will be mindful for ever, in that on all who receive this Sacrament devoutly and faithfully he confers grace in the present and eternal life in the future, as he promised, saying: [[John 6:57|He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood abideth in me: and I in him|Qui manducat meam carnem et bibit meum sanguinem, in me manet et ego in eo]]; and again, [[John 6:59|He that eateth this bread shall live for ever|Qui manducat hunc panem, vivet in æternum]]. Or Christ is said to be ever mindful of this testament because he makes us mindful of it, and will preserve the faith of this Sacrament in the hearts of men until the consummation of the world.

paras.t: Virtutem operum suorum, id est fructum et efficaciam hujus Sacramenti, videlicet corporis et sanguinis sui, quæ sunt opera Creatoris ; vel, Virtutem operum suorum, id est potentiam sacramentalium effectuum corporis sui et sanguinis ; annuntiabit Christus populo suo, id est discipulis suis, atque per eorum prædicationem cunctis fidelibus. Horum operum suorum virtutem Christus discipulis annuntiavit, dicendo : Hic est panis de cœlo descendens, ut si quis ex ipso manducaverit, non moriatur in æternum ; et, Qui manducat me, et ipse vivet propter me.
paras.en: [[110:6|the power of his works|Virtutem operum suorum]], that is, the fruit and efficacy of this Sacrament, namely of his body and blood, which are works of the Creator; or, [[110:6|the power of his works|Virtutem operum suorum]], that is, the might of the sacramental effects of his body and blood, [[110:6|He will shew forth|annuntiabit]], that is, Christ, [[110:6|to his people|populo suo]], that is, to his disciples, and through their preaching to all the faithful. The power of these works of his Christ announced to the disciples, saying: [[John 6:50|This is the bread which cometh down from heaven: that if any man eat of it, he may not die|Hic est panis de cœlo descendens, ut si quis ex ipso manducaverit, non moriatur]] for ever; and, [[John 6:58|he that eateth me, the same also shall live by me|Qui manducat me, et ipse vivet propter me]].

paras.t: Possunt quoque hæc generaliter explanari ; eritque sensus : Memoriam fecit mirabilium suorum : quoniam per Spiritum Sanctum edocuit sanctos Prophetas atque Apostolos ad conscribendum et annuntiandum mirabilia sua, quæ utique in veteri ac novo Testamento copiose narrantur, et a fidelibus recoluntur. Escam spiritualem dedit timentibus se, reficiendo mentes eorum pane vitæ et intellectus, et verbo et gratia Spiritus Sancti. De esca quoque corporali providit Deus famulis suis timoratis, quibus apud Matthæum ait : Quærite primo regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis. Propter quod iterum dicit : Ne solliciti sitis animæ vestræ, quid manducetis, neque corpori vestro, quid induamini : scit enim Pater vester cœlestis quia his omnibus indigetis. Memor erit in sæculum testamenti sui, id est novæ atque evangelicæ legis, corroborando conservandoque eam usque ad terminum mundi. Memor etiam erit testamenti sui, id est promissionis suæ factæ in novo Testamento, quoniam eam implebit, dummodo nos agamus quod ipse nobis præcepit. Promissio novi Testamenti est : Fulgebunt justi sicut sol in regno Patris eorum ; et, In futuro sæculo neque nubent neque nubentur, sed erunt sicut angeli Dei. Illud quoque quod Christus clarissime loquitur : Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam, quam dedisti mihi. Hæc omnia implebuntur in nobis, si impleverimus illud quod ad Corinthios ait Apostolus : Has promissiones habentes, carissimi, mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in timore Dei.
paras.en: These things can also be explained generally, and the sense will be: [[110:4|He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works|Memoriam fecit mirabilium suorum]]: for through the Holy Ghost he taught the holy Prophets and Apostles to write down and announce his wonders, which indeed are related at length in the Old and New Testament, and are recalled by the faithful. [[110:5|He hath given food to them that fear him|Escam spiritualem dedit timentibus se]], that is, spiritual food, refreshing their minds with [[Ecclus 15:3|the bread of life and understanding|pane vitæ et intellectus]], and with the word and grace of the Holy Ghost. For bodily food too God has provided for his God-fearing servants, to whom he says in Matthew: [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|Quærite primo regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis]]. Wherefore he says again: [[Matt 6:25|be not solicitous for your life, what you shall eat, nor for your body, what you shall put on|Ne solliciti sitis animæ vestræ, quid manducetis, neque corpori vestro, quid induamini]]: [[Matt 6:32|For your Father knoweth that you have need of all these things|scit enim Pater vester cœlestis quia his omnibus indigetis]]. [[110:5|He will be mindful for ever of his covenant|Memor erit in sæculum testamenti sui]], that is, of the new and evangelical law, strengthening and preserving it until the end of the world. He will also be mindful of his testament, that is, of his promise made in the New Testament, since he will fulfil it, provided that we do what he has commanded us. The promise of the New Testament is: [[Matt 13:43|Then shall the just shine as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father|Fulgebunt justi sicut sol in regno Patris eorum]]; and, In the world to come [[Matt 22:30|they shall neither marry nor be married, but shall be as the angels of God|neque nubent neque nubentur, sed erunt sicut angeli Dei]]. And also what Christ says most clearly: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory which thou hast given me|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam, quam dedisti mihi]]. All these things will be fulfilled in us, if we fulfil what the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 7:1|Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God|Has promissiones habentes, carissimi, mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in timore Dei]].

paras.t: Virtutem operum suorum, id est miraculorum potentiam seu opera sua virtuosa ac sancta, annuntiabit populo suo. Christus enim per se ipsum prædicavit opera Dei Patris, et subinde conversationis suæ innocentiam ac miraculorum suorum excellentiam annuntiavit Judæis : sicut apud Joannem, Quis, inquit, ex vobis arguet me de peccato? et, Ego non quæro gloriam meam ; et alibi, Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater, ut perficiam ea, ipsa opera quæ ego facio, testimonium perhibent de me. Hæc autem opera, id est vita et signa Christi, annuntiata sunt nobis per Apostolos, imo quotidie annuntiantur nobis in Scriptura canonica novi Testamenti, præsertim in Evangeliis.
paras.en: [[110:6|the power of his works|Virtutem operum suorum]], that is, the might of his miracles, or his works of power and holiness, [[110:6|He will shew forth to his people|annuntiabit populo suo]]. For Christ in his own person preached the works of God the Father, and then announced to the Jews the innocence of his life and the excellence of his miracles: as in John, [[John 8:46|Which|Quis]], he says, [[John 8:46|of you shall convince me of sin|ex vobis arguet me de peccato]]? and, [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]]; and elsewhere, [[John 5:36|the works which the Father hath given me to perfect, the works themselves which I do, give testimony of me|Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater, ut perficiam ea, ipsa opera quæ ego facio, testimonium perhibent de me]]. Now these works, that is, the life and signs of Christ, have been announced to us through the Apostles, nay, they are announced to us daily in the canonical Scripture of the New Testament, above all in the Gospels.

paras.t: Omnia autem hæc fecit Deus fidelibus suis, ut det illis hereditatem gentium, id est regnum cœlorum et vitam æternam, hominibus ab origine mundi paratam, quemadmodum apud Matthæum dicit Salvator : Venite, benedicti Patris mei, possidete paratum vobis regnum a constitutione mundi. Specialiter tamen regnum cœlorum appellatur hereditas gentium, quia Judæis propter incredulitatem juste ablatum est, et gentibus humiliter credentibus datum. Propter quod Christus ait : Auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, et dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus. Et denuo ait : Multi ab oriente et occidente venient, et recumbent cum Abraham et Isaac et Jacob in regno Dei ; filii autem regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores. Merito itaque regnum cœlorum nuncupatur hereditas gentium, quibus ait Apostolus : Estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei. Itemque ad Romanos : Filii Dei sumus. Si autem filii, et heredes : heredes quidem Dei, coheredes autem Christi ; si tamen compatimur ei, ut et conglorificemur.
paras.en: All these things God has done for his faithful, [[110:7|That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles|ut det illis hereditatem gentium]], that is, the kingdom of heaven and eternal life, prepared for men from the beginning of the world, as the Saviour says in Matthew: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world|Venite, benedicti Patris mei, possidete paratum vobis regnum a constitutione mundi]]. Yet the kingdom of heaven is called in a special way the inheritance of the Gentiles, because it was justly taken away from the Jews for their unbelief, and given to the Gentiles who humbly believed. Wherefore Christ says: [[Matt 21:43|the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof|Auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, et dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus]]. And again he says: [[Matt 8:11|many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven|Multi ab oriente et occidente venient, et recumbent cum Abraham et Isaac et Jacob in regno Dei]]; [[Matt 8:12|But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into the exterior darkness|filii autem regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores]]. Rightly then is the kingdom of heaven called the inheritance of the Gentiles, to whom the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:19|you are fellow citizens with the saints and the domestics of God|Estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei]]. And likewise to the Romans: [[Rom 8:16|we are the sons of God|Filii Dei sumus]]. [[Rom 8:17|And if sons, heirs also; heirs indeed of God and joint heirs with Christ: yet so, if we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified with him|Si autem filii, et heredes : heredes quidem Dei, coheredes autem Christi ; si tamen compatimur ei, ut et conglorificemur]].

paras.t: Opera manuum ejus, id est effectus divinæ potestatis, sunt veritas et judicium, id est salvatio et damnatio. Veritas enim vocatur, vera impletio promissionis divinæ, factæ de hereditate cœlesti electis donanda, quibus et datur. Hæc impletio est eorum salvatio, et ipsa est opus Christi. Judicium autem frequenter accipitur pro reprobatione malorum. Unde apud Joannem dicitur : Qui credit in Filium Dei, non judicatur ; qui autem non credit, jam judicatus est, id est reprobatus. Et Apostolus : Si nos ipsos, ait, dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur. Hinc quoque Christus apud Joannem clarius loquens : Qui audit (inquit) verbum meum, et credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam, et in judicium non venit. Judicium ergo, id est reproborum justa damnatio, est opus Dei. Vel sic : Veritas et judicium, id est quælibet veritas quodlibetque judicium, est opus Dei. Est enim veritas naturæ, veritas vitæ, et veritas orationis. Est quoque judicium discretionis, et judicium remunerationis. Et omnia hæc opera sunt manuum divinarum. Vel sic : Opera manuum ejus veritas et judicium, id est vera et justa seu discreta. Dum enim aliquid convenit rei excellenter, enuntiatur de eo non solum in concreto, sed etiam in abstracto : sicut ait Christus Apostolis, Vos estis lux mundi ; et Apostolus, Fuistis aliquando tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino, id est, fuistis aliquando vitiis tenebrosi, nunc autem per gratiam lucidi. Unde de homine multum dilecto ac dulci dicimus : Iste est amor meus, et dulcedo seu consolatio mea. Quoniam ergo omnia opera Dei sunt valde justa, vera atque discreta, idcirco non solum vera et justa, sed veritas et judicium nominantur. Potest quoque referri ad Sacramentum altaris, in cujus consecratione opera Dei sunt veritas, quia in hoc Sacramento non solum figuraliter, sed vere ac substantialiter Christus continetur, et judicium mortis sumenti indigne : qui enim manducat indigne, judicium sibi manducat.
paras.en: [[110:7|the works of his hands|Opera manuum ejus]], that is, the effects of the divine power, are [[110:7|truth and judgment|veritas et judicium]], that is, salvation and damnation. For the true fulfilment of the divine promise, made concerning the heavenly inheritance to be given to the elect, to whom it is indeed given, is called truth. This fulfilment is their salvation, and it is the work of Christ. But judgment is often taken for the reprobation of the wicked. Hence it is said in John: [[John 3:18|He that believeth in him is not judged. But he that doth not believe is already judged|Qui credit in Filium Dei, non judicatur ; qui autem non credit, jam judicatus est]], that is, reprobated. And the Apostle: [[1 Cor 11:31|But if we would judge ourselves|Si nos ipsos]], he says, [[1 Cor 11:31|we should not be judged|dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur]]. Hence too Christ, speaking more clearly in John: [[John 5:24|he who heareth|Qui audit]] (he says) [[John 5:24|my word and believeth him that sent me hath life everlasting: and cometh not into judgment|verbum meum, et credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam, et in judicium non venit]]. Judgment, then, that is, the just damnation of the reprobate, is the work of God. Or thus: [[110:7|truth and judgment|Veritas et judicium]], that is, every truth and every judgment, is the work of God. For there is truth of nature, truth of life, and truth of speech. There is also the judgment of discernment and the judgment of reward. And all these are works of the divine hands. Or thus: [[110:7|the works of his hands are truth and judgment|Opera manuum ejus veritas et judicium]], that is, true and just, or discerning. For when something belongs to a thing in an excellent degree, it is predicated of it not only in the concrete but also in the abstract: as Christ says to the Apostles, [[Matt 5:14|You are the light of the world|Vos estis lux mundi]]; and the Apostle, [[Eph 5:8|you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord|Fuistis aliquando tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino]], that is, you were once darkened by vices, but now made bright by grace. Hence of a man much loved and sweet we say: He is my love, and my sweetness or consolation. Since then all the works of God are exceedingly just, true and discerning, they are therefore called not only true and just, but truth and judgment. It may also be referred to the Sacrament of the altar, in whose consecration the works of God are truth, because in this Sacrament Christ is contained not only figuratively but truly and substantially; and judgment of death to him who receives unworthily: [[1 Cor 11:29|For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily eateth and drinketh judgment to himself|qui enim manducat indigne, judicium sibi manducat]].

paras.t: Fidelia omnia mandata ejus : id est, divina præcepta non sunt fallacia, sed firma et certa, ita quod observatores eorum fidelem ac veram mercedem recipient ; confirmata in sæculum sæculi, id est per divina miracula et cetera quibus fides innititur, in æternum roborata, ita quod certum est ista mandata esse a Deo, et per consequens sancta atque salubria ; facta, id est nobis jussa et exhibita, in veritate et æquitate, ita quod ipsa sunt vera et æqua ; vel, In veritate, id est in sapientia, et æquitate, id est justitia præcipientis Dei, qui secundum suam sapientiam atque justitiam seu in sua sapientia et justitia nobis ista mandata fecit et contulit. Vel dicuntur facta seu data in veritate angelicæ illustrationis, et æquitate angelicæ administrationis. Præcepta namque legalia, data sunt Moysi ministerio angelorum, sicut Stephanus ait Judæis : Accepistis legem in dispositione angelorum.
paras.en: [[110:8|All his commandments are faithful|Fidelia omnia mandata ejus]]: that is, the divine precepts are not deceitful, but firm and sure, so that those who keep them will receive a faithful and true reward; [[110:8|confirmed for ever and ever|confirmata in sæculum sæculi]], that is, strengthened for ever by the divine miracles and the other things on which faith rests, so that it is certain that these commandments are from God, and consequently holy and wholesome; [[110:8|made|facta]], that is, enjoined and shown to us, [[110:8|in truth and equity|in veritate et æquitate]], so that they themselves are true and equitable; or, [[110:8|in truth|In veritate]], that is, in the wisdom, [[110:8|and equity|et æquitate]], that is, the justice, of God who commands, who according to his wisdom and justice, or in his wisdom and justice, made these commandments for us and bestowed them on us. Or they are said to be made or given in the truth of angelic enlightenment and the equity of angelic ministry. For the precepts of the law were given to Moses by the ministry of angels, as Stephen says to the Jews: You have [[Acts 7:53|received the law by the disposition of angels|Accepistis legem in dispositione angelorum]].

paras.t: Redemptionem, id est salutem et salvatorem, videlicet Christum, misit Pater, populo suo, id est electis, in hunc mundum Christum transmittens. Non enim misit Deus Filium suum in mundum, ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum, sicut apud Joannem scriptum est. Unde in Isaia Pater dicit ad Christum : Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ. Vel ipse Christus misit, id est, per prædicationem Apostolorum annuntiavit, redemptionem, id est humani generis salvationem sua passione adeptam, populo suo, id est universis fidelibus, secundum quod in Marco dicit ad eos : Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ. Mandavit in æternum testamentum suum, id est, evangelicam legem præcepit usque in finem sæculi custodiri : quod de veteri Testamento non jussit, quoniam illi successit novum Testamentum in illo præfiguratum. Novo autem Testamento aliud non succedet : propterea usque ad sæculi consummationem jubetur servari. Quod tamen de Sacramento altaris præsertim nunc dicitur, quoniam hoc usque in finem mundi frequentandum est.
paras.en: [[110:9|redemption|Redemptionem]], that is, salvation and the Saviour, namely Christ, [[110:9|He hath sent|misit]], that is, the Father, [[110:9|to his people|populo suo]], that is, to the elect, sending Christ into this world. [[John 3:17|For God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world: but that the world may be saved by him|Non enim misit Deus Filium suum in mundum, ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum]], as it is written in John. Hence in Isaias the Father says to Christ: [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]]. Or Christ himself [[110:9|hath sent|misit]], that is, announced through the preaching of the Apostles, [[110:9|redemption|redemptionem]], that is, the salvation of the human race won by his passion, [[110:9|to his people|populo suo]], that is, to all the faithful, according as he says to them in Mark: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]. [[110:9|he hath commanded his covenant for ever|Mandavit in æternum testamentum suum]], that is, he commanded the evangelical law to be kept until the end of the world: which he did not command of the Old Testament, since the New Testament, prefigured in it, succeeded it. But no other will succeed the New Testament: therefore it is commanded to be kept until the consummation of the world. Yet this is said now above all of the Sacrament of the altar, since this is to be frequented until the end of the world.

paras.t: Sanctum et terribile nomen ejus : id est, ipse Deus est sanctus in se ipso, quoniam substantialiter purus atque perfectus est ; et terribilis, ratione sui effectus. Omnibus autem est Deus terribilis, formidandus timore filiali et casto : sic enim Beati in patria timent Deum. Impiis vero terribilis est timore servili, quo Deus timetur non ex amore secum exsistendi, sed ex pavore tormenta sustinendi.
paras.en: [[110:9|Holy and terrible is his name|Sanctum et terribile nomen ejus]]: that is, God himself is holy in himself, since he is substantially pure and perfect; and terrible by reason of his effects[[Deut 10:17||]][[Deut 10:21||]] [the margin reads Deut. v, 17, 21; Deut 5:17 does not fit, Deut 10:17 (a God terrible) and 10:21 (terrible things) do]. To all, indeed, God is terrible, to be feared with a filial and chaste fear [that is, the reverent fear of a son, which comes of love, not of dread of punishment]: for thus the Blessed in the fatherland fear God. But to the wicked he is terrible with a servile fear, by which God is feared not out of love of being with him, but out of dread of suffering torments.

paras.t: Initium sapientiæ timor Domini. Timor enim servilis incipit ad sapientiam recipiendam animam præparare, in quantum facit a malo recedere. Timor vero initialis magis propinque disponit ad sapientiæ infusionem seu potius perfectionem : timor enim initialis, sine caritate et sapientia haberi non potest. Hoc autem quod dictum est, Initium sapientiæ timor Domini, in Ecclesiastico et alibi scriptum est. Sed videtur huic contrarium quod idem Ecclesiasticus testatur : Plenitudo sapientiæ, timere Dominum. Et Job inquit : Ecce timor Domini ipsa est sapientia. Et respondendum, quod ista intelligenda non sunt de timore servili, sed casto et filiali, quem perfecta caritas non expellit, sed exerit et diffundit seu causat. Hoc enim timore Christus exstitit plenus, juxta illud Isaiæ : Replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini. Verumtamen iste timor non est sapientia, aut sapientiæ plenitudo essentialiter, quia realiter ab ea distinguitur ; sed dicitur sapientia secundum resplendentiam quamdam, quia in hoc quod aliquis timet Deum casto timore, maxime liquet eum veraciter esse sapientem. Et hoc modo sapientia de multis virtutibus virtutumque actibus prædicatur, sicut quum dicitur : Nolle præesse, sed velle subesse, est sapientia ; homines fugere, est sapientia ; propter Christum despici velle, est sapientia.
paras.en: [[110:10|The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom|Initium sapientiæ timor Domini]]. For servile fear begins to prepare the soul to receive wisdom, in so far as it makes it depart from evil. But initial fear [that is, the fear of one beginning to love God, between servile fear and the chaste fear of the perfect] disposes it more nearly to the infusion, or rather the perfection, of wisdom: for initial fear cannot be had without charity and wisdom. Now this saying, [[Ecclus 1:16|The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom|Initium sapientiæ timor Domini]], is written in Ecclesiasticus and elsewhere[[Prov 1:7||]][[Prov 9:10||]]. But what the same Ecclesiasticus testifies seems contrary to it: [[Ecclus 1:20|To fear God is the fulness of wisdom|Plenitudo sapientiæ, timere Dominum]]. And Job says: [[Job 28:28|Behold the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom|Ecce timor Domini ipsa est sapientia]]. The answer is that these are to be understood not of servile fear, but of chaste and filial fear, which perfect charity does not cast out, but brings forth and spreads abroad, or causes. For with this fear Christ was full, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 11:3|he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord|Replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini]]. Yet this fear is not wisdom, or the fulness of wisdom, essentially, since it is really distinct from it; but it is called wisdom by a certain shining forth, because in this, that someone fears God with chaste fear, it is most plainly evident that he is truly wise. And in this way wisdom is predicated of many virtues and acts of virtue, as when it is said: Not to wish to be over others, but to wish to be under them, is wisdom; to flee men is wisdom; to wish to be despised for Christ's sake is wisdom[[Acts 5:41||]].

paras.t: Intellectus bonus omnibus facientibus eum : id est, cognitio fructuosa et utilis est his qui agunt quod sciunt agendum. Nam, ut dicitur in secunda Petri, Melius erat non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post agnitionem retrorsum conversi. Et Jacobus affirmat : Scienti bonum et non facienti, peccatum est illi. Unde et Christus in Evangelio : Servus, inquit, qui scit voluntatem domini sui, et non facit, plagis vapulabit multis. Qui ergo putat se eruditum, qui se illuminatum a Deo exsultat, et se sapientem confidit, advertat et impleat quod Jacobus præcipit : Quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiæ. Alioqui audiet a Christo illud Isaiæ : Sapientia tua et scientia tua decipit te. Vel sic : Intellectus bonus, id est vis intellectiva, habitus intellectualis et operatio intellectiva, sunt sana laudeque digna omnibus facientibus eum, scilicet timorem, seu timentibus Deum : qui scilicet vivunt secundum quod suggerit timor, de quo per Ecclesiasticum inducitur, Timor Domini expellit peccatum ; et alibi, Qui timet Deum, nihil negligit. Laudatio ejus qui ita intelligit, et intellecta adimplet, manet in sæculum sæculi : quia et ipse Deum sine fine laudabit, et a Deo æternam laudem pro mercede recipiet, atque cum Sanctis laudabitur, sicut Ecclesiasticus testatur : Collaudabunt multi sapientiam ejus, et usque in sæculum non delebitur.
paras.en: [[110:10|A good understanding to all that do it|Intellectus bonus omnibus facientibus eum]]: that is, knowledge is fruitful and profitable to those who do what they know is to be done. For, as is said in the second Epistle of Peter, [[2 Pet 2:21|it had been better for them not to have known the way of justice than, after they have known it, to turn back|Melius erat non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post agnitionem retrorsum conversi]]. And James affirms: [[Jas 4:17|To him therefore who knoweth to do good and doth it not, to him it is sin|Scienti bonum et non facienti, peccatum est illi]]. Hence Christ too in the Gospel: [[Luke 12:47|that servant|Servus]], he says, [[Luke 12:47|who knew the will of his lord and prepared not himself and did not according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes|qui scit voluntatem domini sui, et non facit, plagis vapulabit multis]]. Let him then who thinks himself learned, who exults that he is enlightened by God, and trusts that he is wise, attend to and fulfil what James commands: [[Jas 3:13|Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge, among you? Let him shew, by a good contestation, his work in the meekness of wisdom|Quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiæ]]. Otherwise he will hear from Christ that word of Isaias: [[Is 47:10|Thy wisdom, and, thy knowledge, this hath deceived thee|Sapientia tua et scientia tua decipit te]].
