Or thus: [[110:10|A good understanding|Intellectus bonus]], that is, the power of understanding, the habit of understanding and the act of understanding, are sound and worthy of praise [[110:10|to all that do it|omnibus facientibus eum]], namely fear, that is, to those who fear God: who live, that is, according as fear suggests, of which it is said through Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 1:27|The fear of the Lord driveth out sin|Timor Domini expellit peccatum]]; and elsewhere, [[Eccles 7:19|he that feareth God, neglecteth nothing|Qui timet Deum, nihil negligit]]. [[110:10|his praise|Laudatio ejus]], the praise of him who so understands and fulfils what he understands, [[110:10|continueth for ever and ever|manet in sæculum sæculi]]: for he himself will praise God without end, and will receive eternal praise from God as his reward, and will be praised with the Saints, as Ecclesiasticus testifies: [[Ecclus 39:12|Many shall praise his wisdom, and it shall never be forgotten|Collaudabunt multi sapientiam ejus, et usque in sæculum non delebitur]].

paras.t: Expositio anagogica. Denique psalmus iste anagogice exponi potest : nam Beatis in patria congruunt, quæ in eo dicuntur. Ecclesia ergo triumphans, seu quilibet Beatorum dicere potest : Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo. Sancti enim in patria Deum sine aliqua interruptione jugiter laudant : et hoc, toto corde, id est in omnibus viribus suis. Sicut enim præceptum caritatis perfectissime implent Deum amando toto corde, tota fortitudine, et omnibus viribus suis, quia totaliter, actualiter et indesinenter feruntur in Deum ; sic Domino confitentur confessione laudis toto corde, quemadmodum per Isaiam Dominus contestatur : Ecce servi mei laudabunt præ exsultatione cordis. In consilio justorum, id est secundum actum prudentiæ electorum in patria. Sancti namque in regno Deum collaudant, secundum quod donum consilii eis a Spiritu Sancto influxum suggerit et suadet. Et congregatione, id est in unione Beatorum seu triumphantis Ecclesiæ. Beati enim Deum concorditer atque generaliter laudant, glorificantes nomen ejus in id ipsum.
paras.en: Anagogical exposition. Finally, this psalm can be expounded anagogically [that is, of the life of the Blessed in heaven]: for the things said in it befit the Blessed in the fatherland. The Church triumphant, then, or any one of the Blessed, can say: [[110:1|I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart|Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo]]. For the Saints in the fatherland praise God continually, without any interruption: and this with the whole heart, that is, with all their powers. For as they fulfil the precept of charity most perfectly, loving God with the whole heart, with the whole strength and with all their powers, because they are borne towards God wholly, actually and unceasingly; so they praise the Lord with the confession of praise with their whole heart, as the Lord testifies through Isaias: [[Is 65:14|behold my servants shall praise for joyfulness of heart|Ecce servi mei laudabunt præ exsultatione cordis]]. [[110:1|in the council of the just|In consilio justorum]], that is, according to the act of prudence of the elect in the fatherland. For the Saints in the kingdom praise God according as the gift of counsel, poured into them by the Holy Ghost, suggests and persuades. And [[110:1|in the congregation|congregatione]], that is, in the union of the Blessed, or of the Church triumphant. For the Blessed praise God with one accord and all together, glorifying his name together.

paras.t: Magna opera Domini, ea præsertim quæ facit in cœlo empyreo circa Beatos : quos sua per speciem visione beatificat, et in quibus mirabilissima efficit opera, nobis prorsus occulta. Confessio, qua Deum incessantissime laudant, et magnificentia, qua ei reverenter obsequuntur ac parent, opus ejus, id est, sunt opera Dei, placita Deo. Memoriam fecit mirabilium suorum. Deus facit in cordibus Beatorum memoriam mirabilium suorum, admittendo eos ad beatificam suæ essentiæ visionem, in qua splendidissime contemplantur, quæ, quanta et qualia fecerit Deus pro eorum salute. Escam dedit timentibus se : id est, nobis Beatis, qui eum timore casto timemus, quantum ad reverentialem subjectionem, non quantum ad affectionem pœnalem, præstitit suæ divinitatis fruitionem, qua feliciter hilariterque intus reficimur, sustentamur, atque perficimur. Memor erit in sæculum testamenti sui, id est, promissionem suam in æternum verificabit, qua nobis promisit pro præmio sui ipsius visionem, ita quod nunquam relabemur ad miserias pristinas, sed cum Deo sine fine manebimus. Virtutem operum suorum annuntiabit populo suo. Deus namque Sanctis in patria revelat suos divinos atque potentes effectus, et per angelos superiores illuminat inferiores de operibus talibus. Cetera ex præinductis faciliter elucescunt.
paras.en: [[110:2|Great are the works of the Lord|Magna opera Domini]], those above all which he does in the empyrean heaven in the Blessed: whom he beatifies by the vision of himself face to face [Latin *per speciem*, that is, by sight and no longer by faith], and in whom he works most wonderful works, wholly hidden from us. [[110:3|praise|Confessio]], with which they praise God most unceasingly, [[110:3|and magnificence|et magnificentia]], with which they reverently serve and obey him, are [[110:3|His work|opus ejus]], that is, are works of God, pleasing to God. [[110:4|He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works|Memoriam fecit mirabilium suorum]]. God makes in the hearts of the Blessed a remembrance of his wonders, admitting them to the beatific vision of his essence, in which they contemplate most splendidly what things, how great and of what kind God has done for their salvation. [[110:5|He hath given food to them that fear him|Escam dedit timentibus se]]: that is, to us the Blessed, who fear him with a chaste fear, as regards reverent subjection, not as regards the feeling of punishment, he has granted the fruition of his divinity, by which we are happily and joyfully refreshed within, sustained and perfected. [[110:5|He will be mindful for ever of his covenant|Memor erit in sæculum testamenti sui]], that is, he will make his promise good for ever, by which he promised us as our reward the vision of himself[[1 John 3:2||]], so that we shall never fall back into our former miseries, but shall abide with God without end. [[110:6|He will shew forth to his people the power of his works|Virtutem operum suorum annuntiabit populo suo]]. For God reveals to the Saints in the fatherland his divine and mighty effects, and through the higher angels enlightens the lower concerning such works. The rest is easily clear from what has been said before.

paras.t: Postremo psalmum præsentem, laudibus Creatoris dulcissime redolentem, affectum psallentis mirabiliter inflammantem, spirituali hilaritate perfusum, quis digne laudare prævaleat? In quo homo fidelis Deum tam fiducialiter, tamque affectuose alloqui orsus est ; in quo Deus in suis effectibus tam præclare extollitur, divina justitia commendatur, sacramenti Eucharistiæ institutio prophetatur, novi Testamenti perpetuitas annuntiatur, vitæ æternæ remuneratio commemoratur, Christi missio tangitur, et alia multa pulcherrima continentur. Si ergo Deum vere diligimus, nequaquam psalmum hunc tam mysterialem ac sententiosum, sine piæ devotionis fervore cantemus. Qui enim Deum veraciter amat, quanto eum ardentiori affectu complectitur, tanto in ejus præconiis atque obsequiis vehementius delectatur. Quod ut nobis quoque conveniat, enitamur semper cor purum Domino repræsentare, in ejus gratia quotidie crescere, et debita nostra officia cum omni diligentia ordinate persolvere. Tunc namque poterimus in spiritualibus gratiis abundare, si conemur opus Dei non negligenter, sed reverenter exsolvere.
paras.en: Lastly, who could worthily praise the present psalm, most sweetly fragrant with the praises of the Creator, wonderfully inflaming the affection of him who sings it, steeped in spiritual gladness? In it the faithful man has begun to address God so trustfully and so affectionately; in it God is so splendidly extolled in his effects, the divine justice is commended, the institution of the sacrament of the Eucharist is prophesied, the perpetuity of the New Testament is announced, the reward of eternal life is recalled, the sending of Christ is touched upon, and many other most beautiful things are contained. If then we truly love God, let us by no means sing this psalm, so full of mystery and of weighty sayings, without the fervour of pious devotion. For he who truly loves God, the more ardent the affection with which he embraces him, the more vehemently he delights in his praises and his service. That this may befit us too, let us strive always to present a pure heart to the Lord[[2 Par 19:3||]][[2 Par 19:9||]][[2 Tim 2:22||]], to grow daily in his grace, and to discharge our due offices with all diligence and in order. For then shall we be able to abound in spiritual graces, if we endeavour to discharge the work of God [*opus Dei*: the Divine Office sung in choir] not negligently but reverently.

paras.t: Precatio. Misericors et miserator Domine, qui diu nobis peccantibus solita pepercisti bonitate, intellectu tandem bono nos reple, et initium sapientiæ timorem tuum mentibus nostris infunde ; atque deinceps fac nos sobrie et juste vivendo tibi placere.
paras.en: Prayer. O merciful and gracious Lord, who with thy wonted goodness hast long spared us in our sins, fill us at last with good understanding, and pour into our minds thy fear, the beginning of wisdom; and henceforth make us please thee by living soberly and justly.

111.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI UNDECIMI : BEATUS VIR QUI TIMET DOMINUM.
111.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and eleventh psalm: Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord.

paras.t: HABET psalmus iste pro titulo, Alleluia. Quod autem adjungitur, Reversionis Aggæi et Zachariæ, non habetur in Hebræo, neque in translatione Hieronymi juxta Hebræum; nec debet ita intelligi, quasi hic psalmus sit editus ab his Prophetis, aut eorum temporibus. Sed hoc ideo additur, quia sicut Aggæus et Zacharias prophetaverunt de ædificatione materialis templi in Jerusalem, post reditum a captivitate Babylonis; sic in psalmo præsenti tractatur de virtutibus, per quas fideles ædificant Christo immateriale templum in cordibus suis, post reditum a misera servitute peccati, seu captivitate diaboli. Specialiter vero loquitur psalmus iste de operibus misericordiæ, de quibus et Christus specialiter perhibet se facturum judicium in die novissimo.
paras.en: This psalm has for its title: *Alleluia*. What is added, *of the return of Aggeus and Zacharias*, is not found in the Hebrew, nor in Jerome's translation from the Hebrew; nor is it to be understood as though this psalm had been composed by these Prophets, or in their times. But it is added for this reason: that as Aggeus and Zacharias prophesied of the building of the material temple in Jerusalem after the return from the captivity of Babylon[[Agg 1:1||]][[Agg 2:1||]][[Zach 2:1||]], so in the present psalm the virtues are treated by which the faithful build for Christ an immaterial temple in their hearts, after the return from the wretched slavery of sin, or the captivity of the devil. But this psalm speaks especially of the works of mercy, on which Christ too declares that he will especially pass judgment on the last day[[Matt 25:31||]] [the margin gives Matt. xxv, 31–46].

paras.t: AIT itaque : Beatus vir, id est, felix homo nunc in spe, et postmodum felix erit in re, qui timet Dominum, timore casto et filiali, vel saltem initiali. Timor namque servilis non est meritorius, quoniam non procedit ex caritate, sine qua nihil est meritorium vitæ æternæ. Hinc enim Ecclesiasticus contestatur : Timenti Deum bene erit in extremis, et in die defunctionis suæ benedicetur ; et alibi, Beatus homo cui donatum est habere timorem Dei. Et Ecclesiastes ait : Finem loquendi pariter omnes audiamus : Deum time, et mandata ejus observa. Denique, quum nihil separet nos a Deo nisi peccatum, eo ipso quo timor peccata expellit, ad omne bonum disponit, omniumque bonorum quodammodo causa est.
paras.en: He says, then: [[111:1|Blessed is the man|Beatus vir]], that is, a happy man, now in hope, and hereafter he will be happy in reality, [[111:1|that feareth the Lord|qui timet Dominum]] with a chaste and filial fear, or at least an initial one [that is, the fear of beginners, in which the fear of punishment is already joined with love]. For servile fear [that is, the fear of punishment alone] is not meritorious, since it does not proceed from charity, without which nothing is meritorious of eternal life. Hence Ecclesiasticus bears witness: [[Ecclus 1:13|With him that feareth the Lord, it shall go well in the latter end, and in the day of his death he shall be blessed|Timenti Deum bene erit in extremis, et in die defunctionis suæ benedicetur]]; and elsewhere, [[Ecclus 25:15|Blessed is the man, to whom it is given to have the fear of God|Beatus homo cui donatum est habere timorem Dei]]. And Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 12:13|Let us all hear together the conclusion of the discourse. Fear God, and keep his commandments|Finem loquendi pariter omnes audiamus : Deum time, et mandata ejus observa]]. Lastly, since nothing separates us from God but sin, by the very fact that fear drives out sins[[Ecclus 1:27||]] it disposes a man to every good, and is in a way the cause of all good things.

paras.t: In mandatis ejus volet nimis, id est, iste Deum timens, valde optabit implere divina mandata. Timor enim filialis, quoniam timet offensam dilecti et separationem ab eo, maxime studet vitare quibus dilectus offenditur et aufertur, videlicet peccata omissionis et commissionis : et per consequens nimis cupit facere quæ placent dilecto, quod est obedire præceptis animo prompto ac fervido. Nam istud nimis, non designat vitiosum excessum, sed ferventem affectum. Insuper timor iste facit nimis velle in præceptis Dei implendis, quia delectat cor, et parit lætitiam, juxta illud in Ecclesiastico : Timor Domini delectabit cor, et dabit lætitiam et gaudium in longitudine dierum.
paras.en: [[111:1|he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments|In mandatis ejus volet nimis]] [literally "in his commandments he will will exceedingly"], that is, this man who fears God will greatly desire to fulfil the divine commandments. For filial fear, since it fears to offend the beloved and to be separated from him, strives above all to avoid the things by which the beloved is offended and taken away, namely sins of omission and of commission; and in consequence it desires *exceedingly* to do what pleases the beloved, which is to obey his precepts with a ready and fervent mind. For this word *exceedingly* does not denote a vicious excess, but a fervent affection. Moreover, this fear makes a man will exceedingly in fulfilling the precepts of God, because it delights the heart and brings forth gladness, according to that saying in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 1:12|The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart, and shall give joy, and gladness|Timor Domini delectabit cor, et dabit lætitiam et gaudium]] in length of days.

paras.t: Potens in terra erit semen ejus : id est, fructus bonæ conversationis hominis timorati, erit fortis ac stabilis in Ecclesia tam militanti quam triumphanti. Nam fructus iste æterno præmio fulcietur, juxta illud : Bonorum laborum gloriosus est fructus. Generatio rectorum, id est populus justus, benedicetur a Deo, recipiendo gratiam ejus, et ab hominibus qui eis bona imprecantur. Scriptum est enim : Benedictio Domini super caput justi ; et, Qui recti sunt, habitabunt in terra, et simplices permanebunt in ea.
paras.en: [[111:2|His seed shall be mighty upon earth|Potens in terra erit semen ejus]]: that is, the fruit of the good life of the God-fearing man will be strong and stable in the Church, militant as well as triumphant. For this fruit will be upheld by an eternal reward, according to that saying: [[Wis 3:15|the fruit of good labours is glorious|Bonorum laborum gloriosus est fructus]]. [[111:2|the generation of the righteous|Generatio rectorum]], that is, the just people, [[111:2|shall be blessed|benedicetur]] by God, in receiving his grace, and by men, who call down good things upon them. For it is written: [[Prov 10:6|The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just|Benedictio Domini super caput justi]]; and, [[Prov 2:21|they that are upright, shall dwell in the earth; and the simple shall continue in it|Qui recti sunt, habitabunt in terra, et simplices permanebunt in ea]].

paras.t: Gloria, id est spiritualis lætitia, bona fama, vitæ excellentia, et divitiæ, id est spiritualium bonorum affluentia, in domo ejus, id est in corde viri Deum timentis : sicut in Ecclesiastico legitur, Nihil melius quam timere Deum. Et justitia, id est justa conversatio, ejus manet in sæculum sæculi. Homo enim timoratus perseverat usque in finem, et tunc æternaliter coronatur. Unde rursus in Ecclesiastico dicitur : Timenti Deum non occurrent mala ; sed Deus in tentatione illum conservabit, et liberabit a malis. Salomon quoque ait : In timore Domini esto tota die, et habebis spem in novissimo.
paras.en: [[111:3|Glory|Gloria]], that is, spiritual gladness, good fame, excellence of life, [[111:3|and wealth|et divitiæ]], that is, an abundance of spiritual goods, [[111:3|shall be in his house|in domo ejus]], that is, in the heart of the man who fears God; as we read in Ecclesiasticus: There is [[Ecclus 23:37|nothing better than the fear of God|Nihil melius quam timere Deum]] [the margin gives Ecclus. x, 27, "there is none greater than he that feareth God"; Denis's words are those of Ecclus 23:37]. [[111:3|and his justice|Et justitia]], that is, his just manner of life, [[111:3|remaineth for ever and ever|ejus manet in sæculum sæculi]]. For the God-fearing man perseveres to the end, and then he is crowned for eternity. Hence again it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 33:1|No evils shall happen to him that feareth the Lord, but in temptation God will keep him and deliver him from evils|Timenti Deum non occurrent mala ; sed Deus in tentatione illum conservabit, et liberabit a malis]]. Solomon also says: [[Prov 23:17|be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long|In timore Domini esto tota die]], and [[Prov 23:18|thou shalt have hope in the latter end|habebis spem in novissimo]].

paras.t: Exortum est in tenebris, id est inter peccatores, seu in hoc sæculo tenebris ignorantiæ atque caligine vitiorum repleto, lumen divinum, æternum et increatum, rectis corde, id est justis hominibus. Et quid sit lumen hoc, subditur : Misericors et miserator et justus, id est Deus qui dicitur misericors in natura, miserator in opere, justus in retributione. Dicitur autem Deus justis oriri per hoc, quod lumen gratiæ ab ipso recipiunt, per quod Creatorem suum contemplantur et diligunt. Propter quod per Malachiam ait : Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum Sol justitiæ.
paras.en: There [[111:4|is risen up in darkness|Exortum est in tenebris]], that is, among sinners, or in this world, filled with the darkness of ignorance and the gloom of vices, [[111:4|a light|lumen]] divine, eternal and uncreated, to [[111:4|the righteous|rectis]] of heart, that is, to just men. And what this light is, is added: [[111:4|merciful, and compassionate and just|Misericors et miserator et justus]], that is, God, who is called merciful in his nature, compassionate in his work, just in his retribution [*misericors* names mercy as it is in him, *miserator* mercy as he shows it]. Now God is said to rise for the just in this, that they receive from him the light of grace, by which they contemplate and love their Creator. Wherefore he says through Malachias: [[Mal 4:2|unto you that fear my name, the Sun of justice shall arise|Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum Sol justitiæ]].

paras.t: Potest quoque hic versus de Christi adventu intelligi, ut sit sensus : Exortum est in tenebris lumen, videlicet Christus, rectis corde. Nam per incarnationem invisibile lumen justis visibiliter apparuit, et ad salutem eorum ipsis exortum est, prout in Isaia ait Scriptura : Populus qui sedebat in tenebris, vidit lucem magnam ; habitantibus in regione umbræ mortis, lux orta est eis. Et apud Joannem ipsemet Christus : Ego, inquit, sum lux mundi ; qui sequitur me, non ambulat in tenebris, sed habebit lumen vitæ.
paras.en: This verse can also be understood of the coming of Christ, so that the sense is: [[111:4|a light is risen up in darkness|Exortum est in tenebris lumen]], namely Christ, to [[111:4|the righteous|rectis]] of heart. For by the incarnation the invisible light appeared visibly to the just, and rose for them, for their salvation; as Scripture says in Isaias: [[Is 9:2|The people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light|Populus qui sedebat in tenebris, vidit lucem magnam]]; [[Is 9:2|to them that dwelt in the region of the shadow of death, light is risen|habitantibus in regione umbræ mortis, lux orta est eis]] [Denis reads *sedebat*, "sat", as in Matt 4:16, where the Vulgate of Isaias has *ambulabat*, "walked"]. And in John, Christ himself: [[John 8:12|I|Ego]], he says, [[John 8:12|am the light of the world|sum lux mundi]]; [[John 8:12|He that followeth me walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life|qui sequitur me, non ambulat in tenebris, sed habebit lumen vitæ]].

paras.t: Jucundus homo, id est spiritualiter in Domino gaudens, aliisque causam lætitiæ præbens, qui miseretur, id est, opera misericordiæ proximis exhibet. Quod non solum de corporalibus eleemosynis, sed de spiritualibus quoque operibus pietatis intelligendum est : sicut sunt ignorantem instruere, peccanti ignoscere, errantem corrigere, etc. Et commodat, id est, de suo aliis mutuat sine usura. Vel, Commodat, id est, aliis temporalia donat, quatenus a Deo æterna recipiat. Unde in Proverbiorum libro dicitur : Fœneratur Domino, qui miseretur pauperis.
paras.en: [[111:5|Acceptable is the man|Jucundus homo]] [*jucundus*, "pleasant, joyful", which Denis explains], that is, one who rejoices spiritually in the Lord and gives others cause for gladness, [[111:5|that sheweth mercy|qui miseretur]], that is, who shows works of mercy to his neighbours. This is to be understood not only of bodily alms, but also of the spiritual works of piety, such as to instruct the ignorant, to pardon one who sins, to correct one who errs, etc. [[111:5|and lendeth|Et commodat]], that is, lends of his own to others without usury. Or, *lendeth*, that is, gives temporal things to others, so as to receive eternal things from God. Hence it is said in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 19:17|He that hath mercy on the poor, lendeth to the Lord|Fœneratur Domino, qui miseretur pauperis]].

paras.t: Disponit sermones suos, id est, verba sua profert, in judicio discretionis, ne loquendo excedat, quemadmodum ad Colossenses monet Apostolus : Sermo vester semper in gratia sale (id est discretione) sit conditus. Nam, ut in Ecclesiastico scriptum est, Qui multis utitur verbis, lædit animam suam ; et alibi, Qui inconsideratus est ad loquendum, sentiet mala. Ideoque in Proverbiis Salomon loquitur : Qui custodit os suum, custodit ab angustiis animam suam. Sic autem disponit in judicio rectæ rationis sermones suos, ut sciat se non posse hoc ipsum implere sine singulari et magno auxilio gratiæ Dei. Nam, ut Jacobus testatur, Si quis in verbo non offendit, hic perfectus est vir. Propterea iterum Salomon dicit : Hominis est animam præparare, et Dei est gubernare linguam.
paras.en: [[111:5|he shall order his words|Disponit sermones suos]], that is, he utters his words, [[111:5|with judgment|in judicio]] of discretion, lest in speaking he go too far; as the Apostle admonishes the Colossians: [[Col 4:6|Let your speech be always in grace seasoned with salt|Sermo vester semper in gratia sale]] (that is, with discretion). For, as is written in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 20:8|He that useth many words shall hurt his own soul|Qui multis utitur verbis, lædit animam suam]]; and elsewhere, [[Prov 13:3|he that hath no guard on his speech shall meet with evils|Qui inconsideratus est ad loquendum, sentiet mala]]. And so Solomon says in Proverbs: [[Prov 21:23|He that keepeth his mouth|Qui custodit os suum]], [[Prov 21:23|keepeth his soul from distress|custodit ab angustiis animam suam]]. And he so orders his words in the judgment of right reason as to know that he cannot accomplish this very thing without a singular and great help of the grace of God. For, as James testifies, [[Jas 3:2|If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man|Si quis in verbo non offendit, hic perfectus est vir]]. Therefore Solomon says again: [[Prov 16:1|It is the part of man to prepare the soul: and of the Lord to govern the tongue|Hominis est animam præparare, et Dei est gubernare linguam]].

paras.t: Quia in æternum non commovebitur a statu salutis et gratiæ, quia ut dictum est, Justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi. Unde in Proverbiorum libro scriptum est : Via justorum absque offendiculo.
paras.en: [[111:6|Because he shall not be moved for ever|Quia in æternum non commovebitur]] from the state of salvation and grace; because, as has been said, [[111:3|his justice remaineth for ever and ever|Justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi]]. Hence it is written in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 15:19|the way of the just is without offence|Via justorum absque offendiculo]].

paras.t: In memoria æterna erit justus : id est, Deus per effectum pietatis suæ et gratiæ, æternaliter memor erit ipsius ; nam scriptus est in libro vitæ, et Deus per approbationem eum cognoscit ; eritque sine fine in conspectu majestatis divinæ in regno felicitatis æternæ. Ab auditione mala malitia pœnæ, non culpæ, videlicet a verbo illo asperrimo, Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum, non timebit in die judicii, quamvis modo eam vehementer formidet. Erunt enim tunc securi, qui modo sunt pavidi ; tuncque pavebunt, qui modo timorem non habent. Dies nempe judicii, judicisque dura sententia, sicut perversis sunt metuendi, sic electis sunt ratio exsultandi. Propter quod Christus dixit : His autem fieri incipientibus, respicite, et levate capita vestra, id est, mentes lætificate, quia appropinquabit redemptio vestra.
paras.en: [[111:7|The just shall be in everlasting remembrance|In memoria æterna erit justus]]: that is, God, by the effect of his goodness and grace, will be mindful of him for ever; for he is written in the book of life, and God knows him with approval [*per approbationem*: the knowledge by which God owns the just as his, not his bare knowledge of all things]; and he will be without end in the sight of the divine majesty, in the kingdom of eternal happiness. [[111:7|the evil hearing|Ab auditione mala]], evil with the evil of punishment, not of guilt (namely that harshest word, Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]] [Denis has *Ite*, "Go", where the Vulgate has *Discedite a me*, "Depart from me"]), [[111:7|he shall not fear|non timebit]] on the day of judgment, though now he dreads it vehemently. For then they will be secure who now are fearful; and then they will tremble who now have no fear. For the day of judgment and the judge's hard sentence, as they are to be feared by the perverse, so are they for the elect a reason to exult. Wherefore Christ said: [[Luke 21:28|But when these things begin to come to pass, look up and lift up your heads|His autem fieri incipientibus, respicite, et levate capita vestra]], that is, gladden your minds, [[Luke 21:28|because your redemption is at hand|quia appropinquabit redemptio vestra]].

paras.t: Paratum cor ejus sperare in Domino : quia per spem in se existentem, quæ est habitus virtuosus, promptus et facilis est, ut actualiter speret in Deo, non in aliquo bono creato, caduco et vano. Unde in Ecclesiastico habetur : Qui timent Dominum, præparabunt corda sua, et in conspectu illius sanctificabunt animas suas.
paras.en: [[111:7|His heart is ready to hope in the Lord|Paratum cor ejus sperare in Domino]]: because, through the hope that is in him, which is a virtuous habit [that is, a settled disposition of the soul], he is ready and quick to hope actually in God, not in any created, perishable and vain good. Hence we find in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 2:20|They that fear the Lord, will prepare their hearts, and in his sight will sanctify their souls|Qui timent Dominum, præparabunt corda sua, et in conspectu illius sanctificabunt animas suas]].

paras.t: Confirmatum est cor ejus in Deo per gratiam, eo modo quo dicit Apostolus ad Hebræos : Optimum est gratia stabiliri cor. Et in Proverbiis scriptum est : Justus quasi fundamentum æternum. Non commovebitur a stabilitate justitiæ, donec despiciat inimicos suos, id est, quousque vitam seu viam hujus exsilii finiat, atque de beatitudine securus existat. Quum enim justus ad Deum pervenerit, omnes adversarios suos visibiles et invisibiles pro nihilo reputabit, non ex superbia, sed ex vera justitia, quia illorum vitia despicit, et eos, in quantum iniqui sunt, pro nihilo æstimat, sicut superius de viro justo inductum est : Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus.
paras.en: [[111:8|His heart is strengthened|Confirmatum est cor ejus]] in God through grace, in the way of which the Apostle speaks to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:9|it is best that the heart be established with grace|Optimum est gratia stabiliri cor]]. And in Proverbs it is written: [[Prov 10:25|the just is as an everlasting foundation|Justus quasi fundamentum æternum]] [the margin gives Prov. v, 25; the verse is Prov 10:25]. [[111:8|he shall not be moved|Non commovebitur]] from the stability of justice, [[111:8|until he look over his enemies|donec despiciat inimicos suos]] [*despiciat*, "look down on", which Denis takes as "despise"], that is, until he ends the life, or the way, of this exile, and is secure of beatitude. For when the just man has come to God, he will count all his adversaries, visible and invisible, as nothing: not out of pride, but out of true justice, because he despises their vices, and esteems them as nothing in so far as they are wicked; as was said above of the just man: [[Ps 14:4|In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing|Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus]].

paras.t: Dispersit, id est, undique diffudit, et dedit pauperibus sua temporalia bona, seu spiritualia dona, sicut in prima sua Canonica Petrus adhortatur : Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes. Justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi. Hoc jam in psalmo isto dictum atque expositum est. Cornu ejus, id est dignitas seu sublimitas gratiæ, quam habuit in præsenti, exaltabitur, id est, perficietur et consummabitur, in gloria Beatorum, quia tunc plenum præmium sortietur, et lumen gratiæ per lumen gloriæ erigetur. Propter quod Salomon dicit : Qui miseretur pauperis, beatus erit.
paras.en: [[111:9|He hath distributed|Dispersit]], that is, he has spread abroad on every side, and [[111:9|he hath given to the poor|dedit pauperibus]] his temporal goods, or his spiritual gifts; as Peter exhorts in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]]. [[111:9|his justice remaineth for ever and ever|Justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi]]: this has already been said and explained in this psalm. [[111:9|his horn|Cornu ejus]], that is, the dignity or loftiness of the grace which he had in the present life, [[111:9|shall be exalted|exaltabitur]], that is, will be perfected and consummated, [[111:9|in glory|in gloria]] of the Blessed, because then he will receive his full reward, and the light of grace will be raised up through the light of glory. Wherefore Solomon says: [[Prov 14:21|he that sheweth mercy to the poor, shall be blessed|Qui miseretur pauperis, beatus erit]].

paras.t: Peccator impœnitens videbit felicitatem justorum, quam modo habent inchoative, et in futuro judicio habebunt perfecte, et irascetur contra eos ex impatientia, vel contra se ipsum, quod tanta tormenta promeruit ; dentibus suis fremet : quia ex interiori furore corpus ejus concutitur, et motu dentium impetum iræ suæ ostendit ; vel, Dentibus suis fremet in inferno, ubi erit fletus et stridor dentium ; et tabescet in se ipso ex invidia.
paras.en: [[111:10|The wicked|Peccator]] [Latin *peccator*, "the sinner"] who is impenitent [[111:10|shall see|videbit]] the happiness of the just, which they have now in its beginning and will have perfectly at the judgment to come, [[111:10|and shall be angry|et irascetur]] against them out of impatience, or against himself, because he has deserved such great torments; [[111:10|he shall gnash with his teeth|dentibus suis fremet]]: because his body is shaken by the fury within, and by the motion of his teeth he shows the violence of his anger. Or, *he shall gnash with his teeth* in hell, where [[Matt 8:12|there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth|erit fletus et stridor dentium]][[Matt 13:42||]][[Matt 13:50||]]; [[111:10|and pine away|et tabescet]] in himself out of envy.

paras.t: Desiderium peccatorum peribit, id est, suo effectu seu re optata privabitur. Quemadmodum enim justi desiderant Deo æternaliter frui, et in hac vita spiritualibus bonis ditari ; sic impii cupiunt rebus temporalibus et caducis jugiter frui, quoniam eis finaliter inhærent. Tale autem desiderium penitus perit post mortem, quia tunc amplius frui non possunt temporalibus rebus, sed pro earum delectationibus compelluntur sentire æterna tormenta. Desiderium vero justorum post hanc vitam impletur. Propter quod in Proverbiis scriptum est : Desiderium suum justis dabitur ; quasi tempestas transiens non erit impius.
paras.en: [[111:10|the desire of the wicked shall perish|Desiderium peccatorum peribit]], that is, it will be deprived of its effect, or of the thing it longed for. For as the just desire to enjoy God eternally, and in this life to be enriched with spiritual goods, so the wicked desire to enjoy temporal and perishable things without end, since they cling to them finally [that is, to the end of life, as to their last end]. But such desire perishes utterly after death, because then they can no longer enjoy temporal things, but instead of the delights of them they are forced to feel eternal torments. The desire of the just, on the other hand, is fulfilled after this life. Wherefore it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 10:24|to the just their desire shall be given|Desiderium suum justis dabitur]]; [[Prov 10:25|As a tempest that passeth, so the wicked shall be no more|quasi tempestas transiens non erit impius]].

111.title: EXPLANATIO ALLEGORICA EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI UNDECIMI DE CHRISTO.
111.title_en: Allegorical explanation of the same hundred and eleventh psalm, concerning Christ.
111.note: The opening words of this article are missing from the transcription; marked […].

paras.t: […]que sensus: Beatus vir, scilicet Christus, qui ab exordio suæ conceptionis in Virgine, et beatus erat, Deum videndo per speciem, et vir, propter omnium virtutum ac sapientiæ perfectionem. Anima enim Christi, a primo suæ creationis instanti Deum per speciem vidit, omnibusque virtutibus (imperfectionem in sua ratione non includentibus) atque scientiis plena fuit. Unde de eo ut nondum nato, sed adhuc infantulo in materno utero consistenti, scriptum est per Jeremiam: Novum creavit Dominus super terram: mulier circumdabit virum. Hic ergo beatus est vir qui timet, in quantum homo, Dominum timore filiali, illo præcipue qui est unum septem donorum Spiritus Sancti, quemadmodum per Isaiam dicitur: Replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini. In mandatis ejus volet nimis. Quanto enim Christus præ ceteris universis Deum amavit ferventius, tanto in ejus mandatis implendis voluit plenius, quoniam ardentissimo appetitu optavit in omnibus Deo parere: nec solum voluit, sed etiam volita plenissime adimplevit, quia præcepta moralia et duo caritatis mandata perfecte implevit. Propter quod apud Joannem ait: Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio; et apud eumdem, Ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper. Imo tam desiderabile, tamque delectabile fuerat Christo homini, Patris præcepta servare, ut dicat: Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem Patris mei, qui misit me, ut perficiam opera ejus.
paras.en: […] [the opening words of the article are lost in the transcription; only “…que sensus” survives] sense: [[111:1|Blessed is the man|Beatus vir]], namely Christ, who from the first beginning of His conception in the Virgin was both *blessed*, seeing God face to face [literally “by sight”, *per speciem*: the clear vision of God enjoyed by the blessed, as opposed to knowledge by faith], and a *man* [*vir*: a grown man, one of manly strength], because of the perfection of all virtues and of wisdom. For the soul of Christ saw God face to face from the first instant of its creation, and was full of all the virtues (those that do not include imperfection in their very notion [such as faith and hope, which of their nature belong to one who does not yet see God]) and of all knowledge. Hence of Him, when He was not yet born but was still a little infant in His mother’s womb, it is written through Jeremias: [[Jer 31:22|the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Novum creavit Dominus super terram: mulier circumdabit virum]]. This, then, is the blessed man [[111:1|that feareth|qui timet]], inasmuch as He is man, [[111:1|the Lord|Dominum]] with filial fear, and above all with that fear which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, as is said through Isaias: [[Is 11:3|he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord|Replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini]]. [[111:1|he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments|In mandatis ejus volet nimis]]. For the more fervently Christ loved God above all others, the more fully He willed the fulfilling of His commandments, since with the most ardent desire He longed to obey God in all things; and not only did He will it, but what He willed He fulfilled most completely, for He perfectly fulfilled the moral precepts and the two commandments of charity. That is why He says in John: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]; and in the same: [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]]. Nay, so desirable, so delightful had it been to Christ as man to keep the Father’s precepts, that He says: [[John 4:34|My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, that I may perfect his work|Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem Patris mei, qui misit me, ut perficiam opera ejus]] [Denis reads “the will of my Father, who sent me … his works”].

paras.t: Potens in terra erit semen ejus. Semen Christi, est populus christianus, de quo apud Isaiam dicitur: Si posuerit pro peccato animam suam, videbit semen longævum. Hoc semen potens est in terra hujus exsilii, quoniam populus christianus magnus, multus, et fortis est in spiritualibus et corporalibus bonis. Potentius tamen est semen istud in patria Beatorum, ubi parificatum est angelis Dei. Potest quoque per semen Christi, intelligi prædicatio evangelicæ legis, quemadmodum Christus ait: Semen est verbum Dei. Hoc autem semen Christi potens fuit, quia ut dicit Marcus, Erat docens sicut potestatem habens, non sicut Scribæ. Generatio rectorum, id est congregatio Christianorum, ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto renata, benedicetur a Deo, secundum quod ait Apostolus: Benedictus Deus, qui benedixit nos in omni benedictione in cœlestibus in Christo Jesu. Et Lucas de Christo dicit: Elevatis manibus, benedixit eis, et ferebatur in cœlum. Unde apud Isaiam Dominus protestatur: Electi mei non laborabunt frustra, quia semen benedictorum Domini est.
paras.en: [[111:2|His seed shall be mighty upon earth|Potens in terra erit semen ejus]]. The seed of Christ is the Christian people, of whom it is said in Isaias: [[Is 53:10|if he shall lay down his life for sin, he shall see a longlived seed|Si posuerit pro peccato animam suam, videbit semen longævum]]. This seed is mighty in the land of this exile, since the Christian people is great, numerous and strong in spiritual and bodily goods. Yet this seed is mightier in the fatherland of the blessed, where it has been made equal to the angels of God. By the seed of Christ may also be understood the preaching of the gospel law, as Christ says: [[Luke 8:11|The seed is the word of God|Semen est verbum Dei]]. And this seed of Christ was mighty, for, as Mark says, [[Mark 1:22|he was teaching them as one having power, and not as the scribes|Erat docens sicut potestatem habens, non sicut Scribæ]]. [[111:2|the generation of the righteous|Generatio rectorum]], that is, the congregation of Christians, [[John 3:5|born again of water and the Holy Ghost|ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto renata]], [[111:2|shall be blessed|benedicetur]] by God, according to what the Apostle says: [[Eph 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], [[Eph 1:3|who hath blessed us with spiritual blessings in heavenly places, in Christ|qui benedixit nos in omni benedictione in cœlestibus in Christo Jesu]]. And Luke says of Christ: [[Luke 24:50|lifting up his hands, he blessed them|Elevatis manibus, benedixit eis]], [[Luke 24:51|and was carried up to heaven|et ferebatur in cœlum]]. Hence the Lord declares in Isaias: [[Is 65:23|My elect shall not labour in vain|Electi mei non laborabunt frustra]], [[Is 65:23|for they are the seed of the blessed of the Lord|quia semen benedictorum Domini est]].

paras.t: Gloria, id est æterna felicitas, et divitiæ, id est omnium bonorum sufficientia, in domo ejus, id est in regno cœlorum, in triumphanti Ecclesia, in patria Beatorum, quæ est domus Christi. Præterea in Ecclesia militanti sunt gloria atque divitiæ, secundum sensum in præcedenti articulo introductum: et ista Ecclesia est domus Christi, juxta illud ad Timotheum: Scias quomodo oportet te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi. Et justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi: divina namque et increata justitia Christi æterna est; creata vero justitia ejus nunquam deficiet. Exortum est in tenebris lumen rectis, etc. Versiculus iste, in præcedenti articulo de Christo expositus est.
paras.en: [[111:3|Glory|Gloria]], that is, eternal happiness, [[111:3|and wealth|et divitiæ]], that is, the sufficiency of all goods, [[111:3|shall be in his house|in domo ejus]], that is, in the kingdom of heaven, in the Church triumphant, in the fatherland of the blessed, which is the house of Christ. Moreover, in the Church militant there are glory and wealth, according to the sense set out in the preceding article; and this Church is the house of Christ, according to that word to Timothy: [[1 Tim 3:15|know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God|Scias quomodo oportet te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi]]. [[111:3|and his justice remaineth for ever and ever|Et justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi]]: for the divine and uncreated justice of Christ is eternal, and His created justice will never fail. [[111:4|To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness|Exortum est in tenebris lumen rectis]], etc. This verse was expounded of Christ in the preceding article.

paras.t: Jucundus homo, videlicet Christus, de quo Isaias asserit: Non erit tristis neque turbulentus. Nam anima Christi semper erat in gaudio beatæ fruitionis. Qui miseretur. Ipse enim in tantum compassus atque misertus est nostri, quod animam suam pro nobis posuit, et proprio sanguine liberavit; omnibus etiam ad se clamantibus miseretur, veniam gratiamque præstando. Et commodat. Omnia quæ a Christo recepimus, ipse nobis quodammodo commodavit, quoniam rationem de eis requiret et fructum, quemadmodum apud Lucam dicitur in parabola de talentis. Disponit sermones suos in judicio veræ prudentiæ. Nam Christus nihil inordinate aut indiscrete locutus est: imo, ut Lucas testatur, Mirabantur omnes in verbis gratiæ, quæ procedebant de ore ejus. Quia in æternum non commovebitur, quia anima Christi a suæ creationis exordio confirmata erat in bono.
paras.en: [[111:5|Acceptable is the man|Jucundus homo]] [*jucundus*: “pleasant, joyful”], namely Christ, of whom Isaias declares: [[Is 42:4|He shall not be sad, nor troublesome|Non erit tristis neque turbulentus]]. For the soul of Christ was always in the joy of blessed fruition [that is, the enjoyment of God possessed by the blessed]. [[111:5|that sheweth mercy|Qui miseretur]]. For He so far took pity and had mercy on us that He laid down His life for us and set us free with His own blood; and He has mercy also on all who cry to Him, granting them pardon and grace. [[111:5|and lendeth|Et commodat]]. All that we have received from Christ He has in a manner lent us, since He will require an account of it and its fruit, as is said in Luke in the parable of the talents[[Luke 19:15||]] [the margin gives Luc. xix, 15 and following]. [[111:5|he shall order his words with judgment|Disponit sermones suos in judicio]] of true prudence. For Christ said nothing disorderly or indiscreet; nay, as Luke testifies, [[Luke 4:22|they wondered at the words of grace that proceeded from his mouth|Mirabantur omnes in verbis gratiæ, quæ procedebant de ore ejus]]. [[111:6|Because he shall not be moved for ever|Quia in æternum non commovebitur]], for the soul of Christ was confirmed in good from the first beginning of its creation.

paras.t: Paratum cor ejus sperare in Domino. In Christo non erat spes, quæ est virtus theologica, quoniam illa est exspectatio futuræ beatitudinis: quam Christus nunquam exspectavit, sed a principio conceptionis fuerat comprehensor tam perfectus, ut modo. Speravit tamen in Deo per quamdam fiduciam, qua certissime confidebat, omne bonum quod cupiebat, se recepturum a Deo. Confirmatum est cor ejus, per gratiam consummatam, ita quod nunquam peccare valebat, sicut nec Sancti in patria.
paras.en: [[111:7|His heart is ready to hope in the Lord|Paratum cor ejus sperare in Domino]]. In Christ there was not hope, the theological virtue, since that is the expectation of future beatitude, which Christ never awaited: from the beginning of His conception He was a comprehensor [that is, one who already possesses the vision of God, as the blessed do, as opposed to a wayfarer still on the way to it] as perfect as He is now. Yet He hoped in God by a kind of trust, by which He confided most surely that He would receive from God every good He desired. [[111:8|His heart is strengthened|Confirmatum est cor ejus]] by consummate grace, so that He was never able to sin, as neither are the saints in the fatherland.

paras.t: Dispersit spiritualia dona Spiritus Sancti, dedit ea pauperibus, id est humilibus. Propter quod Evangelista fatetur: De plenitudine ejus accepimus omnes gratiam pro gratia. Misit enim Spiritum Sanctum Apostolis; et sicut in prima Joannis Canonica dicitur, Quidquid petierimus, accipiemus. Cornu ejus, id est regia Christi potestas, quæ latebat quamdiu inter homines vixit, exaltabitur in gloria resurrectionis, ascensionis, et claritatis cœlestis. In resurrectione namque data est ei omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra, quantum ad manifestationem ac usum; et in patria sedet ad dexteram Patris, tanquam Rex regum et Dominus dominorum.
paras.en: [[111:9|He hath distributed|Dispersit]] the spiritual gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[111:9|he hath given to the poor|dedit ea pauperibus]], that is, to the humble. That is why the Evangelist declares: [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received: and grace for grace|De plenitudine ejus accepimus omnes gratiam pro gratia]]. For He sent the Holy Ghost upon the Apostles; and as is said in the first canonical Epistle of John, [[1 John 3:22|whatsoever we shall ask, we shall receive|Quidquid petierimus, accipiemus]] [the margin gives Joann. iii, 22]. [[111:9|his horn|Cornu ejus]], that is, the kingly power of Christ, which lay hidden as long as He lived among men, [[111:9|shall be exalted in glory|exaltabitur in gloria]]: the glory of the resurrection, of the ascension, and of heavenly brightness. For in the resurrection [[Matt 28:18|All power is given|omnis potestas]] to Him [[Matt 28:18|in heaven and in earth|in cœlo et in terra]], as to its manifestation and exercise; and in the fatherland He sits at the right hand of the Father, as King of kings and Lord of lords.

paras.t: Peccator, id est omnis hæreticus, paganus, Judæus et reprobus Christianus, et maxime Antichristus, videbit in die judicii majestatem et gloriam Christi, et irascetur, id est corde turbabitur, juxta illud: Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili; dentibus suis fremet adversus se ipsum, quod evadendi locus non erit. Cetera ex præcedenti articulo clara sunt.
paras.en: [[111:10|The wicked|Peccator]], that is, every heretic, pagan, Jew and reprobate Christian, and above all Antichrist, [[111:10|shall see|videbit]] on the day of judgment the majesty and glory of Christ, [[111:10|and shall be angry|et irascetur]], that is, shall be troubled in heart, according to that word: [[Wis 5:2|seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear|Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili]]; [[111:10|he shall gnash with his teeth|dentibus suis fremet]] against himself, because there will be no place of escape. The rest is clear from the preceding article.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum doctrinalem ac pulchrum audivimus: in quo ad opera misericordiæ præcipue invitamur, ad quam sacra Scriptura frequenter nos allicit. Unde in Proverbiis Salomon: Misericordia, inquit, et veritas non te deserant, et invenies gratiam coram Deo et hominibus. Et apud Matthæum dicit Judex noster: Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur. Et Ecclesiasticus: Fœnerare proximo tuo in tempore necessitatis; itemque, Perde pecuniam propter amicum et fratrem. Dicit autem Gregorius, quod misericordia aptius potest dici justitia, quam misericordia: quoniam dum pauperibus aliquid erogamus, non nostra largimur, sed quæ eorum sunt, eis præstamus. Et ideo S. Ambrosius atque excellens ille Basilius: Esurientium (inquiunt) panis est quem tu tenes, nudorum vestis quam recludis, captivorum redemptio pecunia quam sub terra tu fodis. Hinc Augustinus quoque disseruit: Quære quantum tibi Deus dederit, et ex eo tolle tibi quod sufficit; cetera quæ superfluunt, pauperum sunt. Res alienæ possidentur, quum superflua non erogantur. Erogari sibi vult Deus ex eo quod dedit. Quid enim das, quod ille non dedit? Quid habes quod non accepisti? Itaque non sunt retinenda superflua, neque divitibus et satis habentibus, sed indigentibus eroganda: alioqui tam retinens, quam recipiens, timeant de rapina.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of teaching and beautiful, in which we are invited above all to the works of mercy, to which Holy Scripture often draws us. Hence Solomon in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:3|Let not mercy|Misericordia]], he says, and [[Prov 3:3|truth leave thee|veritas non te deserant]]: [[Prov 3:4|And thou shalt find grace|et invenies gratiam]] [[Prov 3:4|before God and men|coram Deo et hominibus]]. And in Matthew our Judge says: [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.|Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]] And Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 29:2|Lend to thy neighbour in the time of his need|Fœnerare proximo tuo in tempore necessitatis]] [the margin gives Eccli. xxx, 2; the words are Ecclus 29:2]; and again, [[Ecclus 29:13|Lose thy money for thy brother and thy friend|Perde pecuniam propter amicum et fratrem]] [Denis has “for thy friend and brother”]. And Gregory says that mercy can more fittingly be called justice than mercy, since when we bestow something on the poor we are not giving what is ours, but rendering them what is theirs. And so St Ambrose and that excellent Basil say: “It is the bread of the hungry (they say) that thou holdest, the clothing of the naked that thou lockest away, the ransom of captives, the money that thou buriest in the ground.” Hence Augustine also taught: “Seek how much God has given thee, and take from it what suffices thee; the rest, which is superfluous, belongs to the poor. The goods of others are possessed when superfluities are not given away. God wills that He be given to out of what He gave. For what dost thou give that He did not give? [[1 Cor 4:7|what hast thou that thou hast not received|Quid habes quod non accepisti?]]?” Therefore superfluities are not to be kept back, nor given to the rich and to those who have enough, but given away to the needy: otherwise let both him who keeps them and him who receives them fear the guilt of robbery.

paras.t: Operatione tibi placita effice nos, Domine, potentes in terra, et vivat te præstante in justitia tua anima nostra: tribue nobis, quæsumus, ut in mandatis tuis semper curramus, cujus gratia totum quod rogamus, impetremus.
paras.en: By works pleasing to Thee make us, O Lord, mighty upon earth, and by Thy gift let our soul live in Thy justice: grant us, we beseech Thee, ever to run in Thy commandments, by whose grace we may obtain all that we ask.

112.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI DUODECIMI : LAUDATE, PUERI, DOMINUM.
112.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and twelfth psalm: Praise the Lord, ye children.

paras.t: Assignatur autem psalmo præsenti pro titulo, Alleluia, quia in toto psalmo offertur laus Deo : ad cujus præconia nos invitans sanctus Propheta, ait :
paras.en: Now the title assigned to the present psalm is Alleluia, because in the whole psalm praise is offered to God; and the holy Prophet, inviting us to proclaim his praises, says:

paras.t: LAUDATE, pueri, id est puri et innocentes, Dominum : tales enim pueri digni sunt Deum laudare. Ad quam pueritiam invitamur ab Apostolo : Fratres, nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote, sensibus autem perfecti. Et Christus apud Matthæum : Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum. Sunt vero nonnulli pueri non ætate, sed sensu, juxta illud Isaiæ : Puer centum annorum morietur. Laudate nomen Domini. Frequenter hortatur nos sacra Scriptura laudare et benedicere nomen Domini ; sed hoc de nomine nominato, videlicet de re significata per nomen, et non de nomine nominante, intelligendum est. Semper autem debemus Deum laudare, quoniam hoc est prorsus angelicum opus, quo homo efficitur amicus et filius Dei. Unde apud Isaiam quoque Dominus ait : Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum. Et ad Ephesios dicit Apostolus : Implemini Spiritu Sancto, loquentes vobismetipsis in hymnis et psalmis et canticis spiritualibus, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino, gratias agentes pro omnibus semper.
paras.en: [[112:1|Praise|LAUDATE]], [[112:1|ye children|pueri]], that is, ye pure and innocent, [[112:1|the Lord|Dominum]]: for such children are worthy to praise God. To this childhood we are invited by the Apostle: [[1 Cor 14:20|Brethren, do not become children in sense. But in malice be children: and in sense be perfect|Fratres, nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote, sensibus autem perfecti]]. And Christ in Matthew: [[Matt 18:3|unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]]. But some are children not in age but in understanding, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 65:20|the child shall die a hundred years old|Puer centum annorum morietur]]. [[112:1|praise ye the name of the Lord|Laudate nomen Domini]]. Holy Scripture often exhorts us to praise and bless the name of the Lord; but this is to be understood of the name as what is named, that is, of the thing signified by the name, and not of the name as what names it [that is, of God himself, not of the word that stands for him]. And we ought always to praise God, since this is a wholly angelic work, by which man is made a friend and a son of God. Hence in Isaias too the Lord says: [[Is 43:7|every one that calleth upon my name, I have created him for my glory|Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum]]. And the Apostle says to the Ephesians: [[Eph 5:18|be ye filled with the Holy Spirit|Implemini Spiritu Sancto]], [[Eph 5:19|Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual canticles, singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord|loquentes vobismetipsis in hymnis et psalmis et canticis spiritualibus, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino]]: [[Eph 5:20|Giving thanks always for all things|gratias agentes pro omnibus semper]].

paras.t: Sic autem laudantes dicite : Sit nomen Domini benedictum, id est, ipse Deus ab omnibus laudetur et benedicatur, ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum, id est indesinenter, continue atque perpetue. Qui diligit Deum ferventer, zelo divini honoris frequenter accenditur, Deumque ab omnibus laudari, benedici et omnibus modis honorari desiderat.
paras.en: And praising him thus, say: [[112:2|Blessed be the name of the Lord|Sit nomen Domini benedictum]], that is, may God himself be praised and blessed by all, [[112:2|from henceforth now and for ever|ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum]], that is, unceasingly, continually and perpetually. He who loves God fervently is often kindled with zeal for God's honour, and longs that God be praised, blessed and honoured in every way by all.

paras.t: A solis ortu usque ad occasum, id est de mane usque ad vesperum. Vel, A solis ortu, id est a terra ac populo orientali, usque ad occasum, id est usque ad terram ac populum occidentalem, est laudabile nomen Domini : quia ubique terrarum apparet, operatur ac invenitur bonitas Dei. Propter quod ubique et semper laudandus est, prout per Malachiam testatur : A solis ortu magnum est nomen meum in gentibus.
paras.en: [[112:3|From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same|A solis ortu usque ad occasum]], that is, from morning until evening. Or, [[112:3|From the rising of the sun|A solis ortu]], that is, from the eastern land and people, [[112:3|unto the going down of the same|usque ad occasum]], that is, to the western land and people, [[112:3|the name of the Lord is worthy of praise|est laudabile nomen Domini]]: for everywhere on earth the goodness of God appears, works and is found. For which reason he is to be praised everywhere and always, as he testifies by Malachias: [[Mal 1:11|from the rising of the sun|A solis ortu]] [[Mal 1:11|my name is great among the Gentiles|magnum est nomen meum in gentibus]].

paras.t: Excelsus super omnes gentes Dominus, id est, cunctis hominibus dignior est atque sublimior, juxta illud Isaiæ : Omnes gentes quasi non sint, sic sunt coram illo, et quasi nihilum et inane reputatæ sunt ei. Et in libro Job : Non accipiam personam viri, et Deum homini non æquabo. Sapiens quoque dicit : Tanquam momentum stateræ, sic ante te est orbis terrarum, et tanquam gutta roris antelucani, quæ descendit in terram. Et super cœlos gloria ejus : id est, gaudium Beatorum, quod ipsi a Deo pro mercede recipiunt, est super omnes cælos volubiles, scilicet in cœlo empyreo, quod est locus gloriæ Dei et electorum. Vel, Super cœlos, id est super omnes cives et incolas curiæ cælestis, est gloria ejus, id est excellentia Dei creatoris, quoniam angelicis spiritibus Deus præstantior est, secundum quod in libro Job inducitur: Columnæ cœli contremiscunt et pavent ad nutum ipsius; et alibi, Ecce qui serviunt ei, non sunt stabiles, et in angelis suis reperit pravitatem.
paras.en: [[112:4|The Lord is high above all nations|Excelsus super omnes gentes Dominus]], that is, he is worthier and loftier than all men, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 40:17|All nations are before him as if they had no being at all, and are counted to him as nothing, and vanity|Omnes gentes quasi non sint, sic sunt coram illo, et quasi nihilum et inane reputatæ sunt ei]]. And in the book of Job: [[Job 32:21|I will not accept the person of man, and I will not level God with man|Non accipiam personam viri, et Deum homini non æquabo]] [the margin gives Job xxxi, 21; the words are Job 32:21]. The Wise Man also says: [[Wis 11:23|the whole world before thee is as the least grain of the balance, and as a drop of the morning dew, that falleth down upon tho earth|Tanquam momentum stateræ, sic ante te est orbis terrarum, et tanquam gutta roris antelucani, quæ descendit in terram]]. [[112:4|and his glory above the heavens|Et super cœlos gloria ejus]]: that is, the joy of the Blessed, which they receive from God as their reward, is above all the revolving heavens, namely in the empyrean heaven [that is, the highest heaven, the abode of God and the blessed, beyond the moving spheres], which is the place of the glory of God and of the elect. Or, [[112:4|above the heavens|Super cœlos]], that is, above all the citizens and dwellers of the heavenly court, [[112:4|his glory|gloria ejus]], that is, the excellence of God the Creator, since God surpasses the angelic spirits, as is set forth in the book of Job: [[Job 26:11|The pillars of heaven tremble, and dread at his beck|Columnæ cœli contremiscunt et pavent ad nutum ipsius]]; and elsewhere: [[Job 4:18|Behold, they that serve him are not steadfast, and in his angels he found wickedness|Ecce qui serviunt ei, non sunt stabiles, et in angelis suis reperit pravitatem]].

paras.t: Quis sicut Dominus Deus noster, videlicet Trinitas benedicta? quasi dicat: Nullus ei similis est similitudine æqualitatis, quamvis similitudine imitationis multi sint similes ei. Unde apud Jeremiam habetur : Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me? ait Dominus. Qui in altis habitat, id est in cœlis, de quibus quotidie dicimus, Pater noster qui es in cœlis : ubi per cœlos intelliguntur sanctæ contemplativæque mentes (vel cœlum empyreum, quod pluraliter dicitur, Cœli, quia hoc nomen, cœlum, in Hebræo caret numero singulari, secundum Chrysostomum). In his habitat Deus incircumscriptus per gratiam, et humilia corda respicit per approbationem et conservationem, in cœlo et in terra, imo in omni loco et tempore. Humilibus enim dat gratiam. Et in Isaiæ libro secundum aliam translationem testatur : Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad quietum et humilem, et trementem sermones meos? Qui ergo a Deo respici cupit, spiritum suum humiliet, perpendens illud Virginis gloriosæ : Quia respexit humilitatem ancillæ suæ. Quanto enim se ipsum homo profundius deprimit, tanto a Deo altior judicatur.
paras.en: [[112:5|Who is as the Lord our God|Quis sicut Dominus Deus noster]], namely the blessed Trinity? As if to say: none is like him with a likeness of equality, though by a likeness of imitation many are like him. Hence we have in Jeremias: [[Jer 49:19|who is like to me? and who shall abide me?|Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me?]] saith the Lord [the margin gives Jer. xxiv, 19; the words are Jer 49:19, and again 50:44]. [[112:5|who dwelleth on high|Qui in altis habitat]], that is, in the heavens, of which we say daily: [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven|Pater noster qui es in cœlis]]; where by the heavens are understood holy and contemplative minds (or the empyrean heaven, which is spoken of in the plural, heavens, because this noun, heaven, has no singular number in Hebrew, according to Chrysostom). In these God, who is uncircumscribed [that is, contained by no place], dwells by grace, [[112:6|and looketh down on the low things|et humilia corda respicit]] [Denis reads *humilia corda*, "the humble hearts"] by approving and preserving them, [[112:6|in heaven and in earth|in cœlo et in terra]], nay, in every place and time. For he [[Jas 4:6|giveth grace to the humble|Humilibus enim dat gratiam]]. And in the book of Isaias, according to another translation, he testifies: [[Is 66:2|to whom shall I have respect, but to him|Ad quem respiciam, nisi]] that is quiet and humble, [[Is 66:2|and that trembleth at my words?|et trementem sermones meos?]] [this middle part follows the Greek Septuagint, "the humble and quiet"; the Vulgate has "the poor and little, and of a contrite spirit"]. Whoever then desires to be looked upon by God, let him humble his spirit, pondering that word of the glorious Virgin: [[Luke 1:48|Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid|Quia respexit humilitatem ancillæ suæ]]. For the more deeply a man abases himself, the higher he is judged by God.

paras.t: Suscitans Deus per gratiam suam a terra, id est a vita carnali, ab amore rerum terrenarum, a cogitatione temporalium rerum, inopem, id est in spiritualibus vacuum et egenum, ditans eum donis divinis, amore cælestium, contemplationibus divinorum; et de stercore, id est de habitatione hujus corruptibilis corporis, elevans ad habitationem regni cœlestis, pauperem spiritu, scilicet humilem : quia qui se humiliat, exaltabitur, juxta illud, Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria. Propter quod subditur : Ut collocet eum in patria cum principibus, id est cum angelis sanctis, cum principibus populi sui, id est cum majoribus electorum, videlicet cum Apostolis et Prophetis. Ecclesia namque triumphans una est, ex hominibus bonis et angelis sanctis unita. Vel, Ut collocet eum in die judicii ad dexteram suam, cum principibus, de quibus ab Isaia scriptum est: Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senibus populi sui et principibus ejus. Horum autem duorum versuum sententia in cantico Annæ continetur, primo Regum libro, ubi de Deo sic legitur: Suscitat de pulvere egenum, et de stercore elevat pauperem, ut sedeat cum principibus, et solium gloriæ teneat.
paras.en: [[112:7|Raising up|Suscitans]], God by his grace, [[112:7|from the earth|a terra]], that is, from the carnal life, from the love of earthly things, from thought of temporal things, [[112:7|the needy|inopem]], that is, one empty and destitute in spiritual things, enriching him with divine gifts, with the love of heavenly things, with the contemplation of divine things; and [[112:7|out of the dunghill|de stercore]], that is, from dwelling in this corruptible body, [[112:7|lifting up|elevans]] to the dwelling of the heavenly kingdom [[112:7|the poor|pauperem]] in spirit, that is, the humble one: for [[Luke 14:11|he that humbleth himself shall be exalted|qui se humiliat, exaltabitur]], according to that saying: [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]]. Wherefore it is added: [[112:8|That he may place him|Ut collocet eum]] in the fatherland [[112:8|with princes|cum principibus]], that is, with the holy angels, [[112:8|with the princes of his people|cum principibus populi sui]], that is, with the greatest of the elect, namely with the Apostles and Prophets. For the Church triumphant is one, made one of good men and holy angels. Or, [[112:8|That he may place him|Ut collocet eum]] on the day of judgement at his right hand[[Matt 25:33||]], [[112:8|with princes|cum principibus]], of whom Isaias wrote: [[Is 3:14|The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and its princes|Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senibus populi sui et principibus ejus]]. Now the sense of these two verses is contained in the canticle of Anna, in the first book of Kings, where we read thus of God: [[1 Kings 2:8|He raiseth up the needy from the dust, and lifteth up the poor from the dunghill: that he may sit with princes, and hold the throne of glory|Suscitat de pulvere egenum, et de stercore elevat pauperem, ut sedeat cum principibus, et solium gloriæ teneat]].

paras.t: Qui habitare facit sterilem, id est congregationem gentilium, olim omni spirituali fecunditate carentem, in domo, id est in Ecclesia militanti per gratiam, et postmodum in Ecclesia triumphanti per gloriam. Facit, inquam, eam habitare matrem filiorum lætantem, id est taliter, quod habitando est mater jucunda spiritualium filiorum, quos ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto regenerat, Synagoga Judæorum, quæ quondam erat fecunda, sterili facta. Et ad hunc sensum allegat Apostolus illud Isaiæ: Lætare, sterilis quæ non paris, erumpe et clama, quæ non parturis, quia multi filii desertæ, id est gentilitatis, magis quam ejus quæ habet virum, id est Synagogæ: cujus sponsus et vir fuerat Deus, sed eam propter incredulitatem suam reliquit, quemadmodum per Jeremiam protestatur: Reliqui domum meam, dimisi hereditatem meam; facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva. Appellat autem Propheta gentilitatem seu plebem gentilem, sterilem atque desertam: quoniam diu deserta erat a Deo propter idololatriam, ita quod nullum fructum Spiritus Sancti produxit, nec aliquos filios Christo generavit. Unde primo libro Regum Anna prophetice est locuta: Sterilis peperit plurimos, et quæ multos habebat filios, infirmata est.
paras.en: [[112:9|Who maketh a barren woman to dwell|Qui habitare facit sterilem]], that is, the congregation of the Gentiles, once lacking all spiritual fruitfulness, [[112:9|in a house|in domo]], that is, in the Church militant by grace, and afterwards in the Church triumphant by glory. He makes her dwell, I say, [[112:9|the joyful mother of children|matrem filiorum lætantem]], that is, in such a way that by dwelling there she is the glad mother of spiritual children, whom she regenerates of water and the Holy Ghost, while the Synagogue of the Jews, which was once fruitful, has been made barren. And in this sense the Apostle cites that saying of Isaias[[Is 54:1||]]: [[Gal 4:27|Rejoice, thou barren, that bearest not: break forth and cry thou that travailest not: for many are the children of the desolate|Lætare, sterilis quæ non paris, erumpe et clama, quæ non parturis, quia multi filii desertæ]], that is, of the Gentiles, [[Gal 4:27|more than of her that hath a husband|magis quam ejus quæ habet virum]], that is, of the Synagogue, whose spouse and husband God had been, but who forsook her for her unbelief, as he protests by Jeremias: [[Jer 12:7|I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance|Reliqui domum meam, dimisi hereditatem meam]]; [[Jer 12:8|My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood|facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva]]. Now the Prophet calls the Gentiles, or the Gentile people, barren and desolate, because they had long been forsaken by God for their idolatry, so that they brought forth no fruit of the Holy Ghost, nor bore any children to Christ. Hence in the first book of Kings Anna spoke prophetically: [[1 Kings 2:5|the barren hath borne many: and she that had many children is weakened|Sterilis peperit plurimos, et quæ multos habebat filios, infirmata est]].

paras.t: Ecce hunc psalmum jucundum ac brevem decet nos cum ingenti hilaritate cantare, eo quod totus ad Domini Dei creatorisque nostri laudem pertineat. Et omnino satagendum est nobis, ut tales pueri, id est tam puri, innocentes ac humiles simus, ut Deum digne laudare, atque ab eo pie respici mereamur, quoniam non est speciosa laus in ore hominis vitiosi.
paras.en: Behold, it befits us to sing this joyful and short psalm with great gladness, since the whole of it belongs to the praise of the Lord, our God and Creator. And we must strive in every way to be such children, that is, so pure, innocent and humble, that we may deserve to praise God worthily and to be looked upon by him with kindness; since [[Ecclus 15:9|Praise is not seemly in the mouth|non est speciosa laus in ore]] of a vicious man [the Vulgate has "of a sinner"].

paras.t: Precatio. Deus noster, qui in altis habitas, et de stercore inopem suscitas, nos humiles tuos in terra clementer respice; atque ad sublimia virtutum attolle, in quibus in dies proficientes, in his perseveremus non deficientes.
paras.en: Prayer. O our God, who dwellest on high and raisest up the needy from the dunghill, look mercifully upon us, thy lowly ones on earth; and lift us up to the heights of the virtues, that, advancing in them from day to day, we may persevere in them without failing.

113.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI CENTESIMI TERTIIDECIMI : IN EXITU ISRAEL.
113.title_en: Literal exposition of the hundred and thirteenth psalm: When Israel went out.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi est: Alleluia. Ad litteram enim laudatur Deus in psalmo præsenti, ex consideratione mirabilium quæ fecit circa populum Judæorum in Ægypto, in mari Rubro, atque deserto.
paras.en: The title of the psalm is: *Alleluia*. For in its literal sense God is praised in the present psalm from the consideration of the wonders which he wrought for the people of the Jews in Egypt, in the Red Sea, and in the desert.

paras.t: AIT ergo: In exitu, id est, dum exiret, Israel, id est populus Israeliticus, de Ægypto, domus Jacob, id est in exitu familiæ seu populi hujus, qui dicitur domus Jacob patriarchæ, tanquam natus ex semine ejus, de populo barbaro, id est plebe Ægyptiaca: quæ dicitur populus barbarus, quoniam barbaram linguam habet. Omnia enim idiomata, barbara appellantur, præter Hebræum, Græcum et Latinum: ideoque omnes populi dicti sunt barbari, præter Hebræos, Græcos et Latinos.
paras.en: He says, then: [[113:1|When Israel went out|In exitu]], that is, while there was a going out, [[113:1|Israel|Israel]], that is, the Israelite people, [[113:1|of Egypt, the house of Jacob|de Ægypto, domus Jacob]], that is, at the going out of the family or people of this one, which is called the house of the patriarch Jacob, as being born of his seed, [[113:1|from a barbarous people|de populo barbaro]], that is, the Egyptian people: which is called a barbarous people because it has a barbarous tongue. For all languages are called barbarous except Hebrew, Greek and Latin; and therefore all peoples have been called barbarians except the Hebrews, the Greeks and the Latins.

paras.t: Dum itaque populus iste de Ægypto exiret, secundum quod in Exodo recitatur, tunc. Facta est Judæa, id est populus Judæorum, sanctificatio ejus (videlicet Dei), id est res sanctificata, seu populus sanctificatus a Deo, quia ad unius Dei cultum electus et deputatus est. Sæpe quoque in Exodo et alibi dixit Dominus Moysi: Sanctifica mihi omne primogenitum filiorum Israel. Tunc quoque factus est Israel, id est populus natus ex Jacob, qui alio nomine dictus est Israel, potestas ejus, id est id in quo Deus potestatem suam ostendit, liberando eum de Ægyptiis in manu robusta. Quamvis autem in præcedenti versu non sit nomen Dei expressum, convenienter tamen pronomen relativum, Ejus, refertur ad Deum: quoniam in divinis Scripturis pronomina sæpe demonstrant et referunt, non quod exprimitur, sed quod intelligi datur: quemadmodum apud Lucam angelus dixit de Joanne, Ipse præcedet ante illum in spiritu et virtute Eliæ: ubi per Illum, Christus monstratur, qui ante expressus non fuit. Alii ita exponunt: Facta est Judæa sanctificatio ejus, id est, sanctificatus est populus ille in Judæa, scilicet in terra promissionis; Israel potestas ejus, id est, populus ille potens effectus est in terra prædicta. Sed quoniam ista sanctificatio post quadraginta annos secuta est exitum de Ægypto, secundum hoc aptius dici potuisset: Post exitum Israel de Ægypto. Denique sicut gentilitas significat populum gentilem, sic Judæa populum Judæorum.
paras.en: So while this people was going out of Egypt, as is related in Exodus[[Ex 12:41||]] [the margin gives Exod. xii, 11 and following; xiii, etc.], then [[113:2|Judea was made|Facta est Judæa]], that is, the people of the Jews, [[113:2|his sanctuary|sanctificatio ejus]] (namely God's), that is, a thing sanctified, or a people sanctified by God, because it was chosen and appointed for the worship of the one God [the Latin *sanctificatio* means literally 'sanctification', 'a thing made holy', where the Douay-Rheims has 'sanctuary']. Often, too, in Exodus and elsewhere the Lord said to Moses: [[Ex 13:2|Sanctify unto me every firstborn|Sanctifica mihi omne primogenitum]] [[Ex 13:2|among the children of Israel|filiorum Israel]][[Ex 22:29||]][[Num 3:13||]]. Then too was [[113:2|Israel|Israel]], that is, the people born of Jacob, who by another name was called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]][[Gen 35:10||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxxv, 28; xxxv, 10: the first is evidently Gen 32:28], made [[113:2|his dominion|potestas ejus]], that is, that in which God showed his power [*potestas*, 'power', where the Douay-Rheims has 'dominion'], by delivering him from the Egyptians [[Ex 32:11|with a mighty hand|in manu robusta]]. Now although the name of God is not expressed in the preceding verse, yet the relative pronoun *his* is fittingly referred to God: since in the divine Scriptures pronouns often point to and refer, not to what is expressed, but to what is given to be understood; as in Luke the angel said of John: [[Luke 1:17|And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias|Ipse præcedet ante illum in spiritu et virtute Eliæ]]; where by *him* Christ is pointed out, who had not been expressed before. Others explain it thus: *Judea was made his sanctuary*, that is, that people was sanctified in Judea, namely in the land of promise; *Israel his dominion*, that is, that people was made powerful in the aforesaid land. But since this sanctification followed the going out of Egypt after forty years[[Num 14:34||]], on this view it could more aptly have been said: *After Israel went out of Egypt*. Lastly, as *heathendom* signifies the heathen people, so *Judea* signifies the people of the Jews.

paras.t: Mare vidit et fugit, id est, mare Rubrum, Deo jubente, ita divisum est, sicque Deo obedivit, ac si fuisset intellectualis naturæ. Fuit enim pro muro ex utraque parte filiis Israel, donec sicco pede transirent, ut in Exodo legitur. Jordanis conversus est retrorsum, id est, aliquæ partes aquæ Jordanis redierunt versus suam originem, quia non descenderunt, sed in modum montis intumuerunt, prout in Josue libro dicitur: Ingressis filiis Israel Jordanem, steterunt aquæ descendentes in uno loco, et instar montis intumescentes, apparebant procul; quæ autem inferiores erant, in mare Solitudinis descenderunt, quousque omnino deficerent. Omnisque populus per arentem alveum transibat salvus. Montes exsultaverunt ut arietes, et colles sicut agni ovium.
paras.en: [[113:3|The sea saw and fled|Mare vidit et fugit]], that is, the Red Sea, at God's command, was so divided, and thus obeyed God as if it had been of an intellectual nature. For it was as a wall on either side to the children of Israel until they crossed over dry-shod, as is read in Exodus[[Ex 14:21||]][[Ex 14:22||]]. [[113:3|Jordan was turned back|Jordanis conversus est retrorsum]], that is, some parts of the water of the Jordan went back towards their source, because they did not flow down, but swelled up like a mountain, as is said in the book of Josue: When the children of Israel had come into the Jordan[[Jos 3:15||]], [[Jos 3:16|The waters that came down from above stood in one place, and swelling up like a mountain, were seen afar off|steterunt aquæ descendentes in uno loco, et instar montis intumescentes, apparebant procul]]; [[Jos 3:16|but those that were beneath, ran down into the sea of the wilderness|quæ autem inferiores erant, in mare Solitudinis]] [[Jos 3:16|until they wholly failed|quousque omnino deficerent]]. And [[Jos 3:17|all the people passed over, through the channel that was dried up|Omnisque populus per arentem alveum transibat]] in safety. [[113:4|The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like the lambs of the flock.|Montes exsultaverunt ut arietes, et colles sicut agni ovium.]]

paras.t: Deinde sanctus Propheta, jubilando in Domino de mirabilibus ejus, alloquitur atque interrogat inanimata, non ut illa intelligant et respondeant, sed ut homines in admirationem et Dei præconium excitentur.
