Dicit enim: Quid est tibi, mare, quod fugisti? secundum modum jam dictum. Et tu, Jordanis, quid est tibi, quia conversus es retrorsum? quasi dicat: Unde et qua potestate facta sunt mirabilia ista? Quid etiam vobis est, o Montes, quia exsultastis sicut arietes, qui ex gaudio saltant? Et quid vobis, o colles, quia exsultastis sicut agni ovium, qui ad ubera matrum hilariter currunt? Potest quoque hic versus non interrogative, sed assertive legi atque exponi, et ita est idem cum versu quo dictum est, Montes exsultaverunt ut arietes. Dicuntur autem montes exsultare, quemadmodum terra dicitur Domino benedicere, scilicet metaphorice, materialiter et occasionaliter, in quantum dederunt filiis Israel occasionem gaudendi. Quidam hanc exsultationem montium exponunt de scopulis, id est arduis rupibus, quæ erant juxta fluvium Arnon: quæ (ut asserunt) inclinaverunt se usque ad aliam partem fluvii hujus, præbentes filiis Israel iter per fluvium. Unde in Numerorum libro habetur: Sicut fecit in mari Rubro, sic faciet in torrentibus Arnon: scopuli torrentium inclinati sunt.
paras.en: Then the holy Prophet, rejoicing in the Lord over his wonders, addresses and questions inanimate things, not that they may understand and answer, but that men may be roused to wonder and to the praise of God. For he says: [[113:5|What ailed thee, O thou sea, that thou didst flee|Quid est tibi, mare, quod fugisti?]], in the way already described. [[113:5|And thou, O Jordan|Et tu, Jordanis]], what ailed thee, [[113:5|that thou wast turned back?|quia conversus es retrorsum?]] As if to say: Whence, and by what power, were these wonders done? What ails you too, O [[113:6|Ye mountains, that ye skipped like rams|Montes, quia exsultastis sicut arietes]], which leap for joy? [[113:6|and|Et]] what ails you, O [[113:6|ye hills|colles]], that ye skipped [[113:6|like lambs of the flock|sicut agni ovium]], which run merrily to their mothers' udders? This verse may also be read and explained not as a question but as a statement; and so it is the same as the verse in which it was said: [[113:4|The mountains skipped like rams|Montes exsultaverunt ut arietes]]. Now the mountains are said to leap for joy as the earth is said to bless the Lord: that is, metaphorically, materially and as an occasion, inasmuch as they gave the children of Israel occasion to rejoice. Some explain this leaping of the mountains of the crags, that is, the steep rocks, which were beside the river Arnon: which (so they assert) bent themselves over to the other side of this river, giving the children of Israel a way across the river. Hence it is found in the book of Numbers: [[Num 21:14|As he did in the Red Sea, so will he do in the streams of Arnon|Sicut fecit in mari Rubro, sic faciet in torrentibus Arnon]]: [[Num 21:15|The rocks of the torrents were bowed down|scopuli torrentium inclinati sunt]].

paras.t: Consequenter respondet ad quæstionem factam de exsultatione terræ. A facie Domini mota est terra: id est, ab adspectu divini imperii contigerunt miracula ista, sicut quod terra deglutivit Dathan et Abiron, inclinatique sunt montium scopuli; a facie Dei Jacob patriarchæ, cui tanquam omnipotenti Creatori, omnia animata et inanimata nutu citius parent. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico dicitur: Ecce cælum et cœli cœlorum, abyssus et universa terra, et omnia quæ in eis sunt, in conspectu Dei commovebuntur; et quum conspexerit illa Deus, tremore concutientur.
paras.en: Next he answers the question asked about the leaping of the earth: [[113:7|At the presence of the Lord the earth was moved|A facie Domini mota est terra]]: that is, it was from the regard of the divine command that these miracles came about, such as that the earth swallowed up Dathan and Abiron[[Num 16:31||]][[Num 16:32||]] and the crags of the mountains bowed down[[Num 21:15||]] [the margin gives Num. xvi, 28–33; xxi, 15]; [[113:7|at the presence of the God of Jacob|a facie Dei Jacob]] the patriarch, whom, as the almighty Creator, all things animate and inanimate obey quicker than a nod. Wherefore it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 16:18|Behold the heaven, and the heavens of heavens, the deep, and all the earth, and the things that are in them|Ecce cælum et cœli cœlorum, abyssus et universa terra, et omnia quæ in eis sunt]], [[Ecclus 16:18|shall be moved in his sight|in conspectu Dei commovebuntur]]; [[Ecclus 16:19|when God shall look upon them, they shall be shaken with trembling|et quum conspexerit illa Deus, tremore concutientur]].

paras.t: Qui convertit petram in stagna aquarum, id est, de petra fecit effluere aquas, sicut ex aqua stagnali rivi aquarum erumpunt facto meatu. Hæc erat petra Horeb, quam quum Moyses percussisset, egressæ sunt aquæ largissimæ, prout in Exodi libro scriptum est. Convertit quoque et rupem, id est silicem, in fontes aquarum: quia, ut in Numerorum volumine legitur, quum percussisset Moyses virga bis silicem, aqua copiosa effluxit.
paras.en: [[113:8|Who turned the rock into pools of water|Qui convertit petram in stagna aquarum]], that is, he made waters flow out of the rock, as streams of water break out of standing water when a channel is made. This was the rock Horeb, which when Moses had struck, there came forth water in great abundance, as is written in the book of Exodus[[Ex 17:6||]] [the words are rather those of Num 20:11]. He turned also [[113:8|the stony hill|et rupem]], that is, the flint, [[113:8|into fountains of waters|in fontes aquarum]]: because, as is read in the volume of Numbers, when Moses had [[Num 20:11|struck the rock twice with the rod|percussisset Moyses virga bis silicem]], abundant water flowed out [the margin gives Num. xx, 11].

paras.t: Quoniam igitur ista non nostris meritis aut viribus, sed divina virtute ac miseratione peracta sunt, ideo Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam: id est, fac ut omnes qui ista cognoscunt, non nos, sed te gloriose collaudent, et tibi totum adscribant. Da, inquam, gloriam nomini tuo. Super misericordia tua et veritate tua, id est de istis effectibus ex tua pietate et æquitate productis. Hæc namque prodigia misericorditer facta sunt, quoniam sine meritis hominum præviis agebantur. Sunt etiam juste facta, in quantum Deus promisit Patriarchis sanctis, quod semen eorum ex Ægypto educeret, et sua divina virtute eos protegeret. — Dum ista oramus, divinæ voluntati nostrum affectum conformamus, quoniam Deus per Isaiam testatus est: Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; gloriam meam alteri non dabo. Et Apostolus: Soli (inquit) Deo honor et gloria. Qui autem ista ex corde postulant, a Deo glorificari merentur, qui in libro Regum ait: Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum; qui autem contemnunt me, erunt ignobiles. Quoniam ergo de opere bono soli Deo gloria danda est et debetur, mirum non est, si veris et humilibus famulis Christi molestissimum est, dum ab hominibus gloriam sibi attribui cernunt: quia quod Dei est, usurpare non audent.
paras.en: Since, then, these things were accomplished not by our merits or strength but by the divine power and mercy, therefore: [[113:9|Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory|Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam]]: that is, grant that all who know these things may gloriously praise not us but thee, and ascribe the whole to thee. Give, I say, glory to thy name [[113:10|For thy mercy, and for thy truth's sake|Super misericordia tua et veritate tua]], that is, for these effects brought about by thy kindness and equity. For these prodigies were done mercifully, since they were wrought with no previous merits of men. They were also done justly, inasmuch as God had promised the holy Patriarchs that he would lead their seed out of Egypt[[Gen 50:23||]][[Ex 3:7||]] [the margin gives Gen. i, 23, evidently for l, 23; Exod. iii, 7 and following; and elsewhere] and protect them by his divine power. — When we pray thus, we conform our affection to the divine will, since God has testified through Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name: I will not give my glory to another|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; gloriam meam alteri non dabo]] [the margin gives Is. xliii, 8; the words are Is 42:8]. And the Apostle: [[1 Tim 1:17|the only God|Soli]], he says, [[1 Tim 1:17|be honour and glory|Deo honor et gloria]]. And those who ask for these things from the heart deserve to be glorified by God, who says in the book of Kings: [[1 Kings 2:30|whosoever shall glorify me, him will I glorify: but they that despise me, shall be despised|Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum; qui autem contemnunt me, erunt ignobiles]]. Since, then, for a good work glory is to be given, and is due, to God alone, it is no wonder if it is most irksome to the true and humble servants of Christ when they see glory attributed to themselves by men: for they dare not usurp what is God's.

paras.t: Hæc autem age, o Domine, nequando, id est ne aliquo tempore, dicant gentes idololatriæ deditæ: Ubi est Deus eorum, videlicet Hebræorum? id est, nunc apparet quod non sit verus et omnipotens Deus, quoniam nomen suum non glorificat, demonstrando suam virtutem atque implendo quod spopondit. Hanc causam exauditionis Moyses sæpe commemorat, Deum sic alloquens: Ne, quæso, dicant Ægyptii, Callide eduxit eos, ut interficeret in montibus. Josue quoque dixit: Mi Domine Deus, quid dicam videns Israelem hostibus suis terga vertentem? Et quid facies nomini tuo magno? Ob hanc etiam causam Dominus perhibet se exaudire preces nostras: Propter me (inquiens) ego faciam, ut non blasphemer.
paras.en: Do these things, O Lord, [[113:10|lest|nequando]], that is, lest at any time, [[113:10|the Gentiles should say|dicant gentes]], given over to idolatry: [[113:10|Where is their God?|Ubi est Deus eorum]] namely the God of the Hebrews? That is: now it is plain that he is not the true and almighty God, since he does not glorify his name by showing his power and fulfilling what he promised. This reason for being heard Moses often recalls, addressing God thus: [[Ex 32:12|Let not the Egyptians say, I beseech thee: He craftily brought them out, that he might kill them in the mountains|Ne, quæso, dicant Ægyptii, Callide eduxit eos, ut interficeret in montibus]][[Num 14:13||]] [the margin adds Num. xiv, 13–16]. Josue too said: [[Jos 7:8|My Lord God, what shall I say, seeing Israel turning their backs to their enemies?|Mi Domine Deus, quid dicam videns Israelem hostibus suis terga vertentem?]] [[Jos 7:9|and what wilt thou do to thy great name?|Et quid facies nomini tuo magno?]] For this reason also the Lord declares that he hears our prayers: [[Is 48:11|For my own sake|Propter me]], he says, [[Is 48:11|will I do it, that I may not be blasphemed|ego faciam, ut non blasphemer]].

paras.t: Deus autem noster in cælo est, id est in corde devoto, quod est immateriale cœlum; vel, in cœlo empyreo, in quo specialiter esse censetur, quoniam illic excellentius operatur, clariusque videtur. Omnia quæcumque voluit, fecit, quum sit omnipotens. Et ideo in libro Job legitur: Cogitationem Dei nemo avertere potest, et anima ejus quodcumque voluit, hoc fecit.
paras.en: [[113:11|But our God is in heaven|Deus autem noster in cælo est]], that is, in the devout heart, which is an immaterial heaven; or, in the empyrean heaven, in which he is reckoned to be in a special way, since there he works more excellently and is more clearly seen. [[113:11|he hath done all things whatsoever he would|Omnia quæcumque voluit, fecit]], since he is almighty. And therefore it is read in the book of Job: [[Job 23:13|no man can turn away his thought|Cogitationem Dei nemo avertere potest]]: [[Job 23:13|and whatsoever his soul hath desired, that hath he done|et anima ejus quodcumque voluit, hoc fecit]].

paras.t: Simulacra gentium, id est idola paganorum, substantialiter aliud non sunt, nisi argentum et aurum: quod intelligendum est de pretiosioribus earum simulacris. Habent namque simulacra cuprea, ænea, lignea, in quibus materia est tota substantia: quia secundum Philosophum, in artificialibus tota substantia est materia. Hæc autem simulacra artificialia, sunt, sicut subjungitur, opera manuum hominum. Formata sunt namque manu et arte humana. Os habent, non vere neque univoce, sed similitudinarie, eo modo quo homo defunctus dicitur habere pedes seu oculos; et non loquentur, quia non vivunt, neque intelligunt. Oculos habent, eo modo quo os, et non videbunt per eos. Et simili modo in duobus sequentibus versibus dicuntur habere organa sine officiis, scilicet aures sine auditu, nares sine odoratu, manus sine palpatione, pedes sine ambulatione, guttur sine clamore.
paras.en: [[113:12|The idols of the Gentiles|Simulacra gentium]], that is, the idols of the pagans, are in substance nothing else than [[113:12|silver and gold|argentum et aurum]]: which is to be understood of their more precious idols. For they have idols of copper, of bronze, of wood, in which the matter is the whole substance: because, according to the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle], in things made by art the whole substance is the matter. And these artificial idols are, as is added, [[113:12|the works of the hands of men|opera manuum hominum]]: for they are shaped by human hand and art. [[113:13|They have mouths|Os habent]], not truly nor univocally [that is, not in the same sense of the word as living things have them], but by likeness, in the way in which a dead man is said to have feet or eyes; [[113:13|and speak not|et non loquentur]], because they do not live or understand. [[113:13|they have eyes|Oculos habent]], in the same way as a mouth, [[113:13|and see not|et non videbunt]] with them. And in like manner in the two following verses they are said to have organs without their functions: that is, ears without hearing, noses without smell, hands without touch, feet without walking, a throat without crying out.

paras.t: Sed videtur contrarium: nam idola gentium dant suis cultoribus responsa, imo futura prædicunt. Advertendum ergo, quod sicut Valerius Maximus refert, quidam Romanorum, et præsertim antiqui Romani, non colebant simulacra propter se, tanquam essent viva aut animata, sed in honorem eorum quos repræsentabant. Alii vero Romani coluerunt ea, tanquam per se honoranda, videlicet ut viva, animata et rationalia: quorum insania ex errore Hermetis originem sumpsit. Quemadmodum enim octavo de Civitate Dei Augustinus describit, Hermes Trismegistus asseruit, quod sicut summus Deus est factor deorum cælestium, sic homo fictor est deorum, qui in templis venerantur, et humana proximitate contenti sunt. Statuas enim dixit sensu et spiritu plenas, futurorum præscias, de somniis ac aliis multis prædicentes, hominibus imbecillitatem facientes, eosque curantes, lætitiam atque tristitiam dantes pro meritis. Hæc autem positio non solum theologicæ veritati, sed etiam naturali rationi discordat, sicut in Summa contra gentiles S. Thomas pulchre efficaciterque demonstrat. Contra hunc quoque errorem in libro Sapientiæ plenissime disputatur. Unde etiam Seneca dixit idola nec animata esse, neque colenda: quamvis ipse propter aliquos videretur ea colere foris. De qua tamen simulatione B. Augustinus graviter arguit Senecam.
paras.en: But the contrary seems true: for the idols of the Gentiles give answers to their worshippers, and even foretell the future. It must be noted, then, that, as Valerius Maximus relates, some of the Romans, and especially the ancient Romans, did not worship the images for their own sake, as though they were living or animate, but in honour of those whom they represented. But other Romans worshipped them as to be honoured for themselves, that is, as living, animate and rational: and their madness took its origin from the error of Hermes. For, as Augustine describes in the eighth book of the City of God, Hermes Trismegistus asserted that as the supreme God is the maker of the heavenly gods, so man is the fashioner of the gods who are worshipped in temples and are content to be near to men. For he said that statues are full of sense and spirit, foreknow the future, foretell it through dreams and many other means, cause infirmity in men and cure them, and give joy and sadness according to deserts. But this position is at odds not only with theological truth but even with natural reason, as St Thomas shows finely and forcefully in the *Summa contra Gentiles*. Against this error, too, there is a very full disputation in the book of Wisdom[[Wis 13:10||]][[Is 44:9||]] [the margin gives Wis. xiii, 10–19; Is. xliv, 9–20]. Hence Seneca too said that idols are neither animate nor to be worshipped, although he himself, on account of certain people, seemed to worship them outwardly. For which pretence, however, blessed Augustine severely rebukes Seneca.

paras.t: Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea: id est, omnes qui idola formant aut fieri procurant, similes fiant idolis suis: quatenus sicut illa corporaliter cæca, surda, muta, et sine naturali vita exsistunt, sic isti spiritualiter cæci, surdi, muti, et mortui fiant, carendo vita gratiæ; et omnes qui confidunt in eis, non in Deo vero, similes illis fiant. Hoc autem non optando, sed prænuntiando, et quid illi mereantur ostendendo asseritur, nisi intelligatur de obstinatis.
paras.en: [[113:16|Let them that make them become like unto them|Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea]]: that is, let all who make idols or have them made become like their idols: so that as those are bodily blind, deaf, dumb and without natural life, so these may become spiritually blind, deaf, dumb and dead, lacking the life of grace; [[113:16|and all such as trust in them|et omnes qui confidunt in eis]], not in the true God, let them become like them. But this is said not as a wish but as a foretelling, and to show what they deserve, unless it be understood of the obstinate.

paras.t: Domus Israel, id est populus fidelis ex Jacob ortus, speravit in Domino, non in simulacris. Propter quod Balaam dixit: Non est idolum in Jacob, nec simulacrum in Israel. Dominus Deus ejus cum eo est, et clangor victoriæ regis in illo est. Et hoc est quod subditur: adjutor eorum et protector eorum est, id est, Deus adjuvit eos in bonis, et protexit in adversis. Submersit enim Ægyptios, et Chananæos propter eos occidit.
paras.en: [[113:17|The house of Israel|Domus Israel]], that is, the faithful people sprung from Jacob, [[113:17|hath hoped in the Lord|speravit in Domino]], not in idols. Wherefore Balaam said: [[Num 23:21|There is no idol in Jacob|Non est idolum in Jacob]], [[Num 23:21|neither is there an image god to be seen in Israel|nec simulacrum in Israel]]. [[Num 23:21|The Lord his God is with him, and the sound of the victory of the king in him|Dominus Deus ejus cum eo est, et clangor victoriæ regis in illo]]. And this is what is added: [[113:17|he is their helper and their protector|adjutor eorum et protector eorum est]], that is, God helped them in good things and protected them in adversity. For he drowned the Egyptians[[Ex 14:24||]][[Deut 1:30||]] and slew the Chanaanites for their sake[[Jos 3:10||]][[Jos 12:1||]] [the margin gives Exod. xiv, 24–28; Deut. i, 30; Josue iii, 10; xii].

paras.t: Domus Aaron, id est posteritas ejus, videlicet sacerdotes veteris Testamenti, speravit in Domino. Et quamvis domus Aaron includatur in domo Jacob, ut pars in toto, fit tamen de eis mentio specialis, propter sacerdotii dignitatem. Adjutor eorum et protector eorum est, et fuit, ut patet in libris legis ac Prophetarum.
paras.en: [[113:18|The house of Aaron|Domus Aaron]], that is, his posterity, namely the priests of the Old Testament, [[113:18|hath hoped in the Lord|speravit in Domino]]. And although the house of Aaron is included in the house of Jacob, as a part in the whole, yet special mention is made of them because of the dignity of the priesthood. [[113:18|he is their helper and their protector|Adjutor eorum et protector eorum est]], and was, as is plain in the books of the Law and the Prophets.

paras.t: Qui timent Dominum timore filiali, vel saltem initiali, speraverunt in Domino: alias desperassent. Speraverunt ergo in Domino, quod daret eis virtutem et gratiam omnia mala evadendi, cunctaque bona adipiscendi: nec frustra, quia adjutor eorum et protector eorum est. Unde scriptum est: Respicite, et scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino et confusus est. Et ideo illic monet Scriptura: Qui timetis Dominum, sperate in illo, et in oblectationem vobis veniet misericordia.
paras.en: [[113:19|They that fear the Lord|Qui timent Dominum]] with filial fear, or at least initial fear [that is, the fear of beginners, in which the fear of punishment is already joined with love], [[113:19|have hoped in the Lord|speraverunt in Domino]]: otherwise they would have despaired. They hoped in the Lord, then, that he would give them strength and grace to escape all evils and to obtain all good things: and not in vain, because [[113:19|he is their helper and their protector|adjutor eorum et protector eorum est]]. Hence it is written: [[Ecclus 2:11|behold|Respicite]], [[Ecclus 2:11|and know ye that no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded|et scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino et confusus est]]. And therefore Scripture there admonishes: [[Ecclus 2:9|Ye that fear the Lord hope in him, and mercy shall come to you for your delight|Qui timetis Dominum, sperate in illo, et in oblectationem vobis veniet misericordia]].

paras.t: Dominus memor fuit nostri, scilicet populi Israelitici, ostendendo nobis per effectum, quod curam et dilectionem haberet circa nos; et benedixit nobis, dando nobis abundantiam spiritualium temporaliumque bonorum, quamdiu in ejus cultu permansimus. Quod clarius subditur: Benedixit domui, id est familiæ, Israel; benedixit domui Aaron, id est sacerdotibus. Benedixit omnibus qui timent Dominum, scilicet pusillis, id est parvis et subditis, cum majoribus, id est prælatis. Non enim est personarum acceptor Deus, sed in omni gente, qui timet eum et operatur justitiam, acceptus est illi, ut dicitur in Actis.
paras.en: [[113:20|The Lord hath been mindful of us|Dominus memor fuit nostri]], that is, of the people of Israel, showing us by its effect that he had care and love for us; [[113:20|and hath blessed us|et benedixit nobis]], giving us an abundance of spiritual and temporal goods as long as we remained in his worship. Which is added more clearly: [[113:20|He hath blessed the house|Benedixit domui]], that is, the family, [[113:20|of Israel: he hath blessed the house of Aaron|Israel; benedixit domui Aaron]], that is, the priests. [[113:21|He hath blessed all that fear the Lord|Benedixit omnibus qui timent Dominum]], namely [[113:21|little|pusillis]], that is, the small and the subjects, [[113:21|and great|cum majoribus]], that is, the prelates. For [[Acts 10:34|God is not a respecter of persons|Non enim est personarum acceptor Deus]]: [[Acts 10:35|But in every nation, he that feareth him and worketh justice is acceptable to him|sed in omni gente, qui timet eum et operatur justitiam, acceptus est illi]], as is said in the Acts.

paras.t: Adjiciat Dominus super vos bona majora, quatenus indeficienter proficiatis in spiritualibus: quia non proficere, est deficere. Hoc etiam orat pro nobis Apostolus ad Thessalonicenses: Deus dirigat viam vestram; et abundare faciat caritatem vestram in invicem et in omnes. Et alibi: Oro ut abundetis magis. Super vos et super filios vestros carnales et spirituales, dando vobis et eis quotidianum profectum, ut ambuletis de virtute in virtutem.
paras.en: [[113:22|May the Lord add|Adjiciat Dominus]] [[113:22|upon you|super vos]] greater good things [the Douay-Rheims has 'blessings'; Denis reads *bona majora*, 'greater good things'], so that you may advance unfailingly in spiritual things: for not to advance is to fall back. This too the Apostle prays for us, to the Thessalonians: God [[1 Thess 3:11|direct our way|dirigat viam vestram]] [Denis reads 'your way']; [[1 Thess 3:12|and make you abound in charity towards one another and towards all men|et abundare faciat caritatem vestram in invicem et in omnes]]. And elsewhere: I pray [[1 Thess 4:1|that you may abound the more|ut abundetis magis]]. [[113:22|upon you, and upon your children|Super vos et super filios vestros]], in the flesh and in the spirit, giving to you and to them daily progress, so that you may walk [[Ps 83:8|from virtue to virtue|de virtute in virtutem]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxviii, 8; the words are Ps 83:8].

paras.t: Benedicti estis vos, o patres et filii, Domino, id est a Domino, vel ad honorem et gloriam Dei, qui contulit vobis bona exteriora et interiora, temporalia et æterna, qui fecit cœlum et terram, cum omnibus intermediis.
paras.en: [[113:23|Blessed be you|Benedicti estis vos]], O fathers and sons, [[113:23|of the Lord|Domino]], that is, by the Lord, or to the honour and glory of God [Denis reads *Domino*, 'to the Lord', and takes it either way], who has bestowed on you goods outward and inward, temporal and eternal, [[113:23|who made heaven and earth|qui fecit cœlum et terram]], with all that lies between.

paras.t: Creavit autem Cœlum supremum atque empyreum cœli Domino, id est sibi ipsi pro suo palatio, ut in eo cum Beatis æternaliter demoretur: non quod ipse loco indigeat, sed ad gloriam electorum paravit sibi hanc domum. Terram autem dedit filiis hominum ad inhabitandum atque colendum eam, prout vitæ humanæ necessarium est, sicut per Jeremiam testatur: Ego creavi terram, et dedi eam ei qui placuit in oculis meis.
paras.en: And he created [[113:24|The heaven|Cœlum]], the highest and empyrean heaven, [[113:24|of heaven is the Lord's|cœli Domino]], that is, for himself as his palace, that he may dwell in it with the Blessed for ever: not that he needs a place, but he prepared this house for himself for the glory of the elect. [[113:24|but the earth he has given to the children of men|Terram autem dedit filiis hominum]] to dwell in and to till, as is necessary for human life, as he testifies through Jeremias: [[Jer 27:5|I made the earth|Ego creavi terram]], [[Jer 27:5|and I have given it to whom it seemed good in my eyes|et dedi eam ei qui placuit in oculis meis]].

paras.t: Non mortui in peccatis mortalibus laudabunt te, Domine, laudatione meritoria, quoniam sine caritate et gratia nullus meretur bonum divinum, neque omnes qui descendunt in infernum damnatorum: tales enim Deum blasphemant. Unde Ecclesiastes hortatur: Quodcumque potest manus tua, instanter operare: quia nec opus, nec ratio, nec sapientia, nec scientia erunt apud inferos. Baruch quoque ait: Non mortui qui sunt in inferno, quorum spiritus acceptus est a visceribus eorum, dabunt honorem tibi Domino.
paras.en: [[113:25|The dead|Non mortui]] in mortal sins [[113:25|shall not praise thee, O Lord|laudabunt te, Domine]], with a meritorious praise, since without charity and grace no one merits the divine good; [[113:25|nor any of them that go down to hell|neque omnes qui descendunt in infernum]] of the damned: for such blaspheme God. Hence Ecclesiastes exhorts: [[Eccles 9:10|Whatsoever thy hand is able to do, do it earnestly: for neither work, nor reason, nor wisdom, nor knowledge shall be in hell|Quodcumque potest manus tua, instanter operare: quia nec opus, nec ratio, nec sapientia, nec scientia erunt apud inferos]]. Baruch too says: [[Bar 2:17|the dead that are in hell, whose spirit is taken away from their bowels|Non mortui qui sunt in inferno, quorum spiritus acceptus est a visceribus eorum]], [[Bar 2:17|shall not give glory and justice to the Lord|dabunt honorem tibi Domino]] [Denis reads 'shall not give honour to thee, the Lord'].

paras.t: Sed nos qui vivimus spiritualiter habendo caritatem, quæ est animæ vita, benedicimus Domino, id est, Deum laudamus, ex hoc nunc, id est ex instanti jam præsenti, et usque in sæculum, id est sine fine. Nunc enim laudatio ista incipitur, et usque ad mortem continuatur, atque cum anima a corpore separatur, et simul in ea manet in regno cœlorum in sempiternum, secundum quod per Isaiam Dominus ait: Gaudebitis et exsultabitis usque in æternum.
paras.en: [[113:26|But we that live|Sed nos qui vivimus]] spiritually by having charity, which is the life of the soul, [[113:26|bless the Lord|benedicimus Domino]], that is, we praise God, [[113:26|from this time now|ex hoc nunc]], that is, from the present instant, [[113:26|and for ever|et usque in sæculum]], that is, without end. For this praise is begun now and continued until death, and when the soul is separated from the body it goes with it and remains in it in the kingdom of heaven for ever, as the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 65:18|you shall be glad and rejoice for ever|Gaudebitis et exsultabitis usque in æternum]].

113.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SEU MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI TERTIIDECIMI.
113.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same hundred and thirteenth psalm.

paras.t: QUEMADMODUM ad Corinthios dicit Apostolus: Hæc omnia in figura contingebant illis; scripta sunt autem propter eruditionem nostram, in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt. Debemus ergo prædicta ad nostram moralem instructionem convertere.
paras.en: As the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|Hæc omnia in figura contingebant illis]]: [[1 Cor 10:11|and they are written for our correction, upon whom the ends of the world are come|scripta sunt autem propter eruditionem nostram, in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]] [Denis reads *propter eruditionem nostram*, 'for our instruction', where the Vulgate has *ad correptionem nostram*]. We ought, then, to turn what has been said to our moral instruction.

paras.t: Denique, sicut subinde prætactum est, per Ægyptum intelligitur hoc præsens sæculum seu mundus, qui (secundum Joannem in sua Canonica) totus in maligno positus est. Quapropter Jacobus dicit: Quicumque voluerit amicus hujus mundi fieri, inimicus Dei constituetur. Ubi per mundum non significatur machina mundialis, ex elementis et ceteris irrationalibus constans, sed populus mundanus, sæculariter vivens: de quo ait Apostolus, Si hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem: quia, ut Jacobus scriptum reliquit, Amicitia hujus mundi, inimica est Deo. Per Israel quoque, qui interpretatur, vir videns Deum, intelligitur plebs fidelis, Deum per fidem contemplans. Per Jacob vero, qui dicitur supplantator, intelligitur quilibet contra vitia luctans. Exitus autem filiorum Israel de Ægypto, significat exitum Christianorum de hoc mundo, vel potius de vita mundana ac vitiosa, quoniam mundum egredimur, non motu et loco, sed conversatione et merito.
paras.en: Now, as has been touched on more than once already, by *Egypt* is understood this present age or world, which (according to John in his Canonical Epistle) [[1 John 5:19|the whole world is seated in wickedness|totus in maligno positus est]]. Wherefore James says: [[Jas 4:4|Whosoever therefore will be a friend of this world becometh an enemy of God|Quicumque voluerit amicus hujus mundi fieri, inimicus Dei constituetur]]. Where by *world* is meant not the fabric of the world, made up of the elements and the other irrational things, but the worldly people, living in a worldly way: of whom the Apostle says: [[Gal 1:10|If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ|Si hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem]]: because, as James has left in writing, [[Jas 4:4|the friendship of this world is the enemy of God?|Amicitia hujus mundi, inimica est Deo]] By *Israel* too, which is interpreted *a man seeing God*, is understood the faithful people, contemplating God by faith. And by *Jacob*, which means *supplanter*, is understood anyone who wrestles against vices. And the going out of the children of Israel from Egypt signifies the going out of Christians from this world, or rather from the worldly and vicious life: since we go out of the world not by motion and place, but by our way of life and by merit.

paras.t: Ait ergo: In exitu Israel, id est populi christiani, de Ægypto, id est de conversatione sæculari, domus Jacob, id est ejusdem populi, de populo barbaro, id est congregatione reproborum: qui barbari appellantur, quia ut ait Augustinus, Non nostra lingua est, sed barbara, quæ Deum laudare non novit.
paras.en: He says, then: [[113:1|When Israel went out|In exitu Israel]], that is, the Christian people, [[113:1|of Egypt|de Ægypto]], that is, from a worldly way of life, [[113:1|the house of Jacob|domus Jacob]], that is, of the same people, [[113:1|from a barbarous people|de populo barbaro]], that is, from the congregation of the reprobate: who are called barbarians because, as Augustine says, That tongue is not ours but barbarous which knows not how to praise God.

paras.t: In hoc exitu Facta est Judæa, id est plebs confitens Deo (Judæa namque confessio interpretatur), sanctificatio ejus, id est res seu gens sanctificata a Domino. Dum enim mundum, vitam mutando, egredimur, Dei gratia nobis præstatur, per quam sanctificamur. Israel potestas ejus: id est, in exitu isto, qui aliud non est, nisi aversio mentis a rebus illicitis et conversio ejus ad Deum, homo seu populus contemplativus factus est speculum potestatis divinæ, quia in eo relucet divina potestas, quasi in speculo, quum majus sit peccatorem justificare, quam cœlum creare. Itaque Israel factus est potestas ejus, id est potens Dei effectus. Vel sic: Facta est Judæa sanctificatio ejus, id est, in ipsa confessione qua purgatur, sanctificatur. Israel, id est Deum cognoscens, divina judicia fide contemplans, se ipsum coram Deo ubique constituens atque examinans, factus est potestas ejus, id est potens in Deo, quia per hæc potens efficitur ad resistendum tentationibus universis.
paras.en: In this going out [[113:2|Judea was made|Facta est Judæa]], that is, the people confessing to God (for *Judea* is interpreted *confession*), [[113:2|his sanctuary|sanctificatio ejus]], that is, a thing or nation sanctified by the Lord. For when, by changing our life, we go out of the world, God's grace is given us, by which we are sanctified. [[113:2|Israel his dominion|Israel potestas ejus]]: that is, in this going out, which is nothing else than the turning of the mind away from unlawful things and its turning to God, the contemplative man or people is made a mirror of the divine power, because the divine power shines back in him as in a mirror, since it is a greater thing to justify a sinner than to create heaven. And so Israel was made *his dominion* [Latin *potestas*, 'power'], that is, a mighty one of God. Or thus: *Judea was made his sanctuary*, that is, in the very confession by which he is cleansed he is sanctified. *Israel*, that is, one knowing God, contemplating the divine judgments by faith, setting himself everywhere before God and examining himself, is made *his dominion*, that is, mighty in God, because by these things he is made mighty to resist all temptations.

paras.t: Mare, id est populus inquietus, turbulentus, vitiisque amarus, de quo in Isaia scriptum est: Impii quasi mare fervens, quod quiescere non potest. Hoc igitur mare vidit prædictum exitum electorum de caligine vitiorum, et fugit, id est, imitari eos non voluit. Fugiunt namque et a Deo recedunt, qui converti despiciunt. Propter quod per Jeremiam Dominus: Elongaverunt, inquit, a me, et ambulaverunt post vanitatem, et vani facti sunt. In Proverbiis quoque dicitur: Relinquunt iter rectum, et ambulant per vias tenebrosas. Jordanis, id est homo humilis se ipsum dijudicans: Jordanis quippe interpretatur descensus seu rivus judicii, sicque designatur per eum homo ab alto elationis ad profundum humilitatis descendens, atque se ipsum discutiens. Hic ergo Jordanis vidit sicut et mare, sed non fugit, imo conversus est retrorsum, id est, a cœpto itinere malo se retraxit, a prava consuetudine rediit, et ad fontem suæ salutis, videlicet Deum, reversus est. Ecce quomodo quidam ex bono opere aliorum deteriores fiunt et fugiunt, alii ædificantur atque proficiunt. Ideo namque Apostolus de se et sibi similibus ait: Christi bonus odor sumus Deo in omni loco: aliis quidem odor vitæ ad vitam, aliis vero odor mortis ad mortem.
paras.en: [[113:3|The sea|Mare]], that is, the restless, turbulent people, bitter with vices, of whom it is written in Isaias: [[Is 57:20|the wicked are like the raging sea, which cannot rest|Impii quasi mare fervens, quod quiescere non potest]]. This sea, then, [[113:3|saw|vidit]] the aforesaid going out of the elect from the darkness of vices, [[113:3|and fled|et fugit]], that is, would not imitate them. For those who scorn to be converted flee and depart from God. Wherefore the Lord says through Jeremias: [[Jer 2:5|they are gone far from me|Elongaverunt]], he says, [[Jer 2:5|and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?|a me, et ambulaverunt post vanitatem, et vani facti sunt]] In Proverbs too it is said: [[Prov 2:13|Who leave the right way, and walk by dark ways|Relinquunt iter rectum, et ambulant per vias tenebrosas]]. [[113:3|Jordan|Jordanis]], that is, the humble man who judges himself: for *Jordan* is interpreted *descent* or *stream of judgment*, and so by it is signified the man who comes down from the height of pride to the depth of humility and examines himself. This Jordan, then, saw as the sea did, but did not flee; rather it [[113:3|was turned back|conversus est retrorsum]], that is, drew back from the evil road it had begun, returned from its evil habit, and went back to the source of its salvation, namely God. See how some are made worse by the good work of others and flee, while others are edified and advance. For this is why the Apostle says of himself and those like him: [[2 Cor 2:15|For we are the good odour of Christ unto God|Christi bonus odor sumus Deo]] in every place: to some indeed the odour of life unto life, to others the odour of death unto death[[2 Cor 2:16||]] [Denis gives the two clauses of v. 16 the other way round; 'in every place' is from v. 14].

paras.t: Ex hac autem conversione Jordanis, Montes, id est sancti Apostoli, sanctitate, sapientia, et miraculorum operibus elevati præ ceteris, exsultaverunt in Domino, gratias referendo, ut arietes ducentes ad ovile oviculas. Ideo namque Joannes in sua Canonica profitetur: Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare. Et Paulus sæpe in suis epistolis, de conversione gentium ineffabiliter se gloriari testatur. Et certe sicut bono prælato nihil adeo grave est, sicut perversitas et incorrigibilitas sui gregis; sic nihil ei jucundius est, quam profectus et emendatio subditorum. Et colles, id est inferiores prælati, successores et imitatores Apostolorum, exsultaverunt, ob hanc causam, in Domino, nihil suis viribus tribuentes, sicut agni ovium.
paras.en: And at this turning of the Jordan [[113:4|The mountains|Montes]], that is, the holy Apostles, raised above the rest by holiness, wisdom and works of miracles, [[113:4|skipped|exsultaverunt]] in the Lord, giving thanks, [[113:4|like rams|ut arietes]] leading the little sheep to the fold. For this is why John professes in his Canonical Epistle: [[3 John 1:4|I have no greater grace than this, to hear that my children walk in truth|Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare]]. And Paul often testifies in his epistles that he glories beyond words in the conversion of the Gentiles[[Rom 15:17||]][[2 Cor 1:14||]][[1 Thess 2:19||]][[1 Thess 2:20||]] [the margin gives Rom. xv, 15–19; II Cor. i, 14; I Thess. ii, 19, 20]. And surely, as nothing is so grievous to a good prelate as the perversity and incorrigibility of his flock, so nothing is more delightful to him than the progress and amendment of his subjects. [[113:4|and the hills|et colles]], that is, the lesser prelates, the successors and imitators of the Apostles, leapt for joy for this reason in the Lord, attributing nothing to their own strength, [[113:4|like the lambs of the flock|sicut agni ovium]].

paras.t: Quid est tibi, mare, id est populo sæcularis, quod fugisti a Deo, nolens converti? Et tu, Jordanis, id est populo humilis, quid est tibi, quia conversus es retrorsum, cessans a malo inchoato? de quo, scilicet quod quidam recte conversi sunt, vos, o Montes, exsultastis sicut arietes, etc. Quasi dicat: Quæ est causa hujus discretionis, quod unus corrigitur, alius induratur?
paras.en: [[113:5|What ailed thee, O thou sea|Quid est tibi, mare]], that is, O worldly people, [[113:5|that thou didst flee|quod fugisti]] from God, unwilling to be converted? [[113:5|and thou, O Jordan|Et tu, Jordanis]], that is, O humble people, what ailed thee, [[113:5|that thou wast turned back?|quia conversus es retrorsum]] ceasing from the evil begun? At which, namely that some have been rightly converted, you, [[113:6|Ye mountains, that ye skipped like rams|o Montes, exsultastis sicut arietes]], etc. As if to say: What is the cause of this distinction, that one is corrected and another hardened?

paras.t: Et respondet: A facie Domini mota est terra: id est, ex respectu divinæ præsentiæ ista contingunt, quod unus misericorditer tangitur a Spiritu Sancto et emendatur, alius juste despicitur, et obstinatus efficitur. Propter quod clamat Apostolus: O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei! quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus! Et iterum: Vide bonitatem et severitatem Dei: in eos quidem qui ceciderunt, severitatem; in te autem bonitatem Dei, si tamen permanseris in bonitate.
paras.en: And he answers: [[113:7|At the presence of the Lord the earth was moved|A facie Domini mota est terra]]: that is, these things come about from the regard of the divine presence: that one is mercifully touched by the Holy Spirit and amended, and another is justly disregarded and becomes obstinate. Wherefore the Apostle cries out: [[Rom 11:33|O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments|O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei! quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus!]]! And again: [[Rom 11:22|See then the goodness and the severity of God: towards them indeed that are fallen, the severity; but towards thee, the goodness of God, if thou abide in goodness|Vide bonitatem et severitatem Dei: in eos quidem qui ceciderunt, severitatem; in te autem bonitatem Dei, si tamen permanseris in bonitate]].

paras.t: Qui convertit petram, id est mentes duras, in stagna aquarum, id est lacrimas largas, ut defleant sua et aliorum delicta; qui etiam convertit et rupem, id est cor in malo habituatum, in fontes aquarum, ita quod copiose defluant lacrimæ sanctæ ex eo. Nam sicut Apostolus dicit, Ubi abundavit delictum, superabundat et gratia. Potest quoque exponi de Salvatore, de quo legitur: Petra erat Christus. Ipse est etiam rupes, propter immobilem mentis suæ in Deo constantiam. Hanc petram, istamque rupem convertit Deus in stagna et fontes aquarum, quando pro omnibus nobis tradidit illum, ita ut foderentur manus ejus, pedes ac latus, ex quibus fluxerunt quinque limpidissimi fontes sanguinis sacri: qui aqua dicitur non substantialiter, sed propter effectum, quoniam sicut aqua abluit corpus, sic sanguis Christi abluit corda, secundum quod in Apocalypsi Joannes dicit: Qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo.
paras.en: [[113:8|Who turned the rock|Qui convertit petram]], that is, hard minds, [[113:8|into pools of water|in stagna aquarum]], that is, abundant tears, that they may bewail their own sins and those of others; who turns also [[113:8|the stony hill|et rupem]], that is, the heart grown habituated to evil, [[113:8|into fountains of waters|in fontes aquarum]], so that holy tears flow from it abundantly. For, as the Apostle says, [[Rom 5:20|where sin abounded, grace did more abound|Ubi abundavit delictum, superabundat et gratia]]. It may also be explained of the Saviour, of whom it is read: [[1 Cor 10:4|the rock was Christ|Petra erat Christus]]. He is also the stony hill, because of the immovable constancy of his mind in God. This rock and this stony hill God turned into pools and fountains of waters when he delivered him up for us all, so that his hands, feet and side were dug[[Ps 21:17||]], from which flowed five most limpid fountains of sacred blood: which is called water not in substance but because of its effect, since as water washes the body, so the blood of Christ washes hearts, as John says in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:5|who hath loved us and washed us from our sins in his own blood|Qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo]].

paras.t: De his autem beneficiis tuis, seu nostris profectibus, qui sunt dona tuæ pietatis, Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam. Super misericordia tua, id est de gratia nobis pie indulta, et veritate tua, qua nos pie informas, veraciter corrigis, et de lege tua nos doces. Nequando dicant gentes: Ubi est Deus eorum? id est, nomen tuum in nobis clementer glorifices, nosque magnifice salves, ne blasphemeris ab impiis dicentibus te vel nolle, vel non posse salvare.
paras.en: For these benefits of thine, or our advances, which are gifts of thy kindness, [[113:9|Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory.|Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam]] [[113:10|For thy mercy|Super misericordia tua]], that is, for the grace kindly granted us, [[113:10|and for thy truth's sake|et veritate tua]], by which thou dost kindly shape us, truly correct us, and teach us from thy law. [[113:10|lest the Gentiles should say: Where is their God?|Nequando dicant gentes: Ubi est Deus eorum?]] That is: mayest thou mercifully glorify thy name in us and magnificently save us, lest thou be blasphemed by the wicked, who say that thou art either unwilling or unable to save.

paras.t: Simulacra, id est dii et idola, gentium, id est bestialiter criminaliterque viventium, sunt argentum et aurum, opera manuum hominum, id est humano artificio ad formam deducta. Avari enim pecuniam colunt pro deo. Propter quod dicit Apostolus, quod avaritia est idolorum servitus. Uniuscujusque equidem deus est quod amplius cogitat, amat et colit, secundum Augustinum. Et ergo luxuriosi deus atque simulacrum est femina; gulosi, venter. Sed hæc longe ab eo sunt, qui cum sancto Job dicere potest: Si putavi aurum robur meum, et obryzo dixi, Fiducia mea. Unde Apostolus in prima ad Timotheum ait: Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe non sublime sapere, nec sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in Deo vivo, qui præstat omnia nobis abunde. Quidam etiam in phantasmatibus suis atque vanissimis phantasiis, Deo relicto, occupantur.
paras.en: [[113:12|The idols|Simulacra]], that is, the gods and images, [[113:12|of the Gentiles|gentium]], that is, of those living like beasts and in crime, [[113:12|are silver and gold, the works of the hands of men|sunt argentum et aurum, opera manuum hominum]], that is, brought into shape by human craft. For the covetous worship money as a god. Wherefore the Apostle says that [[Col 3:5|covetousness, which is the service of idols|avaritia est idolorum servitus]]. Indeed, according to Augustine, each man's god is what he most thinks of, loves and worships. And so the lustful man's god and idol is a woman; the glutton's, his belly. But these things are far from him who can say with holy Job: [[Job 31:24|If I have thought gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence|Si putavi aurum robur meum, et obryzo dixi, Fiducia mea]]. Hence the Apostle says in the first Epistle to Timothy: [[1 Tim 6:17|Charge the rich of this world not to be highminded nor to trust in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God|Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe non sublime sapere, nec sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in Deo vivo]] [[1 Tim 6:17|who giveth us abundantly all things|qui præstat omnia nobis abunde]]. Some too, forsaking God, are taken up with their own phantasms and most vain fancies.

paras.t: Homines autem, quorum sunt ista simulacra, dii et opera, Os habent, et non loquuntur salubria, Deum laudando, et propria vitia confitendo; oculos habent apertos ad vana et sæcularia, et non videbunt bona æterna atque cœlestia. Aures habent ad inutilia verba intentas, et non audient per obedientiam divina eloquia; nares habent ad discernendum, et non odorabunt bonæ vitæ fragrantiam et virtutum dulcedinem. Manus habent extentas ad opera vitiosa, et non palpabunt, id est, digitis suis non tangent quæ dicunt, ut bona quæ docent aut sciunt exsequantur; pedes habent currentes ad mala, et non ambulabunt viam mandatorum Dei; non clamabunt in gutture suo, personando devote præconia Creatoris. Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea: id est, qui illos ad idola facienda aut veneranda inducunt, illis assimilentur in malis culpæ et pœnæ: quia non solum qui faciunt, sed etiam qui consentiunt, aut cooperantur facientibus, digni sunt morte, secundum Apostolum.
paras.en: And the men whose idols, gods and works these are, [[113:13|They have mouths and speak not|Os habent, et non loquuntur]] wholesome things, by praising God and confessing their own vices; [[113:13|they have eyes|oculos habent]] open to vain and worldly things, [[113:13|and see not|et non videbunt]] the eternal and heavenly goods. [[113:14|They have ears|Aures habent]] intent on useless words, [[113:14|and hear not|et non audient]] the divine sayings by obedience; [[113:14|they have noses|nares habent]] for discerning, [[113:14|and smell not|et non odorabunt]] the fragrance of a good life and the sweetness of the virtues. [[113:15|They have hands|Manus habent]] stretched out to vicious works, [[113:15|and feel not|et non palpabunt]], that is, they do not touch with their fingers what they say, so as to carry out the good things they teach or know; [[113:15|they have feet|pedes habent]] running to evil, [[113:15|and walk not|et non ambulabunt]] in the way of God's commandments; [[113:15|neither shall they cry out through their throat|non clamabunt in gutture suo]], by devoutly sounding forth the praises of the Creator. [[113:16|Let them that make them become like unto them|Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea]]: that is, let those who lead them to make or worship idols be made like them in the evils of guilt and of punishment: because, according to the Apostle, not only they that do them, but also they that consent to or co-operate with them that do them, are worthy of death[[Rom 1:32||]].

paras.t: Ecce qualiter peccatores impii et ingrati, omnibus donis Dei, videlicet membris corporis et viribus animæ abutuntur. Nam quibus uti debuerant in Dei obsequio, utuntur in operibus tenebrarum; talenta sibi commissa non solum abscondunt, sed inique dilapidant. Propter hoc Romanos hortatur Apostolus: Sicut exhibuistis membra vestra servire immunditiæ et iniquitati ad iniquitatem, ita nunc exhibete membra vestra servire justitiæ in sanctificationem.
paras.en: See how wicked and ungrateful sinners abuse all the gifts of God, namely the members of the body and the powers of the soul. For what they ought to have used in the service of God they use in the works of darkness; the talents entrusted to them they not only hide[[Matt 25:18||]] but wickedly squander. For this reason the Apostle exhorts the Romans: [[Rom 6:19|as you have yielded your members to serve uncleanness and iniquity, unto iniquity: so now yield your members to serve justice, unto sanctification|Sicut exhibuistis membra vestra servire immunditiæ et iniquitati ad iniquitatem, ita nunc exhibete membra vestra servire justitiæ in sanctificationem]].

paras.t: Domus Israel, id est Ecclesia Christi, Deum per fidem amorose contemplans: de qua domo dicit Apostolus ad Hebræos: Christus tanquam filius in domo sua, quæ domus sumus nos; speravit in Domino, sciens scriptum esse, Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino. Huic enim domui ait Christus apud Lucam: Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quoniam complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Adjutor eorum et protector eorum est. Christus namque, ut in Matthæo legitur, promittit Ecclesiæ: Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi.
paras.en: [[113:17|The house of Israel|Domus Israel]], that is, the Church of Christ, lovingly contemplating God by faith: of which house the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 3:6|Christ, as the Son in his own house: which house are we|Christus tanquam filius in domo sua, quæ domus sumus nos]]; [[113:17|hath hoped in the Lord|speravit in Domino]], knowing that it is written: [[Jer 17:7|Blessed be the man that trusteth in the Lord|Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino]]. For to this house Christ says in Luke: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quoniam complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum]]. [[113:17|he is their helper and their protector|Adjutor eorum et protector eorum est]]. For Christ, as is read in Matthew, promises the Church: [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]].

paras.t: Domus Aaron, id est congregatio fidelium sacerdotum: de quibus Apostolus loquitur, Qui bene præsunt presbyteri, duplici honore digni sunt. Quibus apud Isaiam dicitur: Vos Sacerdotes Domini vocabimini; Ministri Dei nostri dicetur vobis. Speravit in Domino, quod ejus auxilio sacerdotaliter vivat, et aliis digne præsit. Quanto enim ad perfectiorem vitam tenentur, et graviori periculo subjiciuntur, si indigne se habeant, tanto indigent firmius pleniusque sperare in Domino. Sed, proh dolor! multi jam sacerdotes inveniuntur, non in Domino confidentes, nec sacerdotaliter conversantes, sed thesaurizantes sibi argentum et aurum, in quo confidunt homines, Veneremque colentes. Quibus convenit illud Jeremiæ: Sacerdotes non dixerunt, Ubi est Dominus? Et tenentes legem, nescierunt me, et pastores prævaricati sunt in me. Illud quoque Ezechielis: Sacerdotes inter mundum et pollutum non intellexerunt. Impletumque cernimus, quod per prophetas Isaiam et Osee prædictum est: Erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos. Cetera patent ex præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: [[113:18|The house of Aaron|Domus Aaron]], that is, the congregation of faithful priests: of whom the Apostle speaks: [[1 Tim 5:17|Let the priests that rule well be esteemed worthy of double honour|Qui bene præsunt presbyteri, duplici honore digni sunt]]. To whom it is said in Isaias: [[Is 61:6|you shall be called the priests of the Lord|Vos Sacerdotes Domini vocabimini]]; [[Is 61:6|Ye ministers of our God|Ministri Dei nostri]], [[Is 61:6|to you it shall be said|dicetur vobis]]. [[113:18|hath hoped in the Lord|Speravit in Domino]], that by his help it may live as befits priests and worthily preside over others. For the more they are bound to a more perfect life, and the graver the danger they are exposed to if they behave unworthily, the more firmly and fully they need to hope in the Lord. But, alas! many priests are now found not trusting in the Lord, nor living as priests, but [[Bar 3:18|That hoard up silver and gold, wherein men trust|thesaurizantes sibi argentum et aurum, in quo confidunt homines]], and worshipping Venus. To them applies that saying of Jeremias: [[Jer 2:8|The priests did not say: Where is the Lord? and they that held the law knew me not, and the pastors transgressed against me|Sacerdotes non dixerunt, Ubi est Dominus? Et tenentes legem, nescierunt me, et pastores prævaricati sunt in me]]. That too of Ezechiel: [[Ezech 22:26|Her priests|Sacerdotes]] [[Ezech 22:26|nor have distinguished between the polluted and the clean|inter mundum et pollutum non intellexerunt]] [no reference in the margin here]. And we see fulfilled what was foretold by the prophets Isaias and Osee: [[Is 24:2|And it shall be as with the people, so with the priest|Erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos]][[Osee 4:9||]] [no reference in the margin here; the words stand in both Is 24:2 and Osee 4:9]. The rest is plain from the preceding article.

paras.t: Egrediamur itaque spiritualiter ex Ægypto, festinando ad patriam, et odientes (secundum monita Judæ apostoli) eam quæ carnalis est, maculatam tunicam. Nam, ut scribit Corinthiis Paulus, Quæ societas luci ad tenebras? Quæ autem conventio Christi ad Belial? aut quæ pars fideli cum infideli? Denique non compingamus animas nostras simulacris sensibilium rerum aut imaginibus transitoriorum bonorum; sed mundo corde et mente theoricis contemplationibus adornata, Domino ministrare, placere, et semper adsistere enitamur, implentes illud Judæ: Superædificantes vosmetipsos sanctissimæ fidei vestræ, in Spiritu Sancto orantes, vosmetipsos in dilectione Dei servate, exspectantes misericordiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi in vitam æternam.
paras.en: Let us therefore go out spiritually from Egypt, hastening to our fatherland, and [[Jude 1:23|hating|odientes]] (according to the admonitions of Jude the apostle) [[Jude 1:23|the spotted garment which is carnal|eam quæ carnalis est, maculatam tunicam]]. For, as Paul writes to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 6:14|what fellowship hath light with darkness?|Quæ societas luci ad tenebras?]] [[2 Cor 6:15|And what concord hath Christ with Belial? Or what part hath the faithful with the unbeliever?|Quæ autem conventio Christi ad Belial? aut quæ pars fideli cum infideli?]] Lastly, let us not fasten our souls to the images of sensible things or the likenesses of passing goods; but with a clean heart and a mind adorned with speculative contemplations let us strive to serve the Lord, to please him and to stand ever before him, fulfilling that saying of Jude: [[Jude 1:20|building yourselves upon your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost|Superædificantes vosmetipsos sanctissimæ fidei vestræ, in Spiritu Sancto orantes]], [[Jude 1:21|Keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, unto life everlasting.|vosmetipsos in dilectione Dei servate, exspectantes misericordiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi in vitam æternam]] [no references in the margin here].

paras.t: Precatio. Fortissime Deus creaturarum, qui convertis petram in stagna aquarum, a facie tua ad pœnitentiam moveatur corporis nostri terra, unde sit nomini tuo gloria pro nobis misericorditer salvandis in beatitudine perpetua.
paras.en: Prayer. O most mighty God of creatures, who [[113:8|turned the rock into pools of water|convertis petram in stagna aquarum]], at thy presence may the earth of our body be moved to repentance, that thence there may be glory to thy name for our being mercifully saved in everlasting beatitude.

114.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUARTADECIMI : DILEXI, QUONIAM EXAUDIET DOMINUS.
114.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and fourteenth psalm: I have loved, because the Lord will hear.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi est : Alleluia. Loquitur autem Propheta in psalmo hoc in persona cujuscumque fidelis, peregrinantis a Domino in hoc sæculo nequam, quod est regio vitiorum.
paras.en: The title of the psalm is: Alleluia. In this psalm the Prophet speaks in the person of any of the faithful who is a pilgrim away from the Lord[[2 Cor 5:6||]] in this wicked world, which is the region of vices.

paras.t: TALIS igitur homo gratias agens Deo de sua liberatione, partim jam facta seu inchoata, postmodum vero complenda, ita exorsus est: Dilexi summum bonum, quod solum in se et propter se summe amandum est. Et non dixit quid diligeret, ad insinuandum quod Deus solus propter se amandus sit, et alia tantum in eo. Quoniam exaudiet Dominus vocem orationis meæ. Hoc est verbum bonæ spei. Omnino enim sperare debemus, quod Deus preces nostras inanes esse non sustinet, dummodo postulemus sicut petendum est ; alias convenit nobis quod Jacobus asserit : Petitis, et non accipitis, eo quod male petatis. Talis autem petitio nec vere, nec proprie dici potest oratio, quoniam oratio (secundum Damascenum) est petitio decentium a Deo. Hic autem dicit se diligere Deum propter beneficium exauditionis. Nam propter beneficia sua Deus amandus est, et tanto plus ceteris, quanto plura atque majora dona ab eo recepimus. Magis tamen amandus est Deus propter se ipsum ac propriam bonitatem, quæ vere pura et infinita est. Debemus autem Deum propter utramque causam simul ac summe amare : ad quod pertinet, quod in Canonica Joannis scriptum est, Nos ergo diligamus Deum, quoniam ipse prior dilexit nos.
paras.en: Such a man, then, giving thanks to God for his deliverance, partly already accomplished or begun, but to be completed hereafter, began thus: [[114:1|I have loved|Dilexi]] the highest good, which alone is to be loved supremely in itself and for its own sake. And he did not say what he loved, to suggest that God alone is to be loved for his own sake, and other things only in him. [[114:1|because the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer|Quoniam exaudiet Dominus vocem orationis meæ]]. This is a word of good hope. For we ought to hope wholeheartedly that God does not suffer our prayers to be in vain, provided we ask as we ought to ask; otherwise there applies to us what James declares: [[Jas 4:3|You ask and receive not: because you ask amiss|Petitis, et non accipitis, eo quod male petatis]]. But such a petition can be called prayer neither truly nor properly, since prayer (according to Damascene) is the asking of fitting things from God. Here, then, he says that he loves God for the benefit of being heard. For God is to be loved for his benefits, and the more beyond others, the more and the greater the gifts we have received from him. Yet God is to be loved more for his own sake and for his own goodness, which is truly pure and infinite. And we ought to love God for both reasons together, and supremely; to which belongs what is written in the Canonical Epistle of John: [[1 John 4:19|Let us therefore love God: because God first hath loved us|Nos ergo diligamus Deum, quoniam ipse prior dilexit nos]].

paras.t: Quod autem Dominus exauditurus sit me, hinc confido, Quia inclinavit aurem suam mihi, id est, misericordiam suam obtulit mihi, asserens se paratum infirmanti succurrere, miserum exaudire, periclitantem salvare. Propterea et in diebus meis, id est cunctis diebus quibus subsisto, et non solum ad horam seu modico tempore, invocabo, id est, ex intimo cordis affectu Deum orabo : secundum quod apud Lucam Christus testatur, Oportet semper orare, et non deficere.
paras.en: And that the Lord will hear me, I trust from this: [[114:2|Because he hath inclined his ear unto me|Quia inclinavit aurem suam mihi]], that is, he has offered me his mercy, declaring himself ready to succour the weak, to hear the wretched, to save him who is in peril. Therefore [[114:2|and in my days|et in diebus meis]], that is, all the days that I live, and not only for an hour or a short time, [[114:2|I will call upon him|invocabo]], that is, I will pray to God from the inmost affection of my heart; as Christ testifies in Luke: [[Luke 18:1|we ought always to pray and not to faint|Oportet semper orare, et non deficere]].

paras.t: Circumdederunt, id est, copiose et undique invaserunt, me in medio laqueorum positum, dolores mortis, id est pœnæ mortales, vehementes tentationes, inordinatæ affectiones, quæ mortem perpetuam animæ ingerunt, nisi pietas Dei succurrat ; et pericula inferni, id est peccata mortalia, vel saltem via facile incidendi ea, invenerunt me, quando gratiam perdidi, consentiendo malignis affectibus. Dicuntur autem peccata mortalia, inferni pericula : quia per ea perit anima in æternum, projicienda in infernum. Possumus quoque per dolores mortis accipere pœnas ex originali peccato secutas, et propter illud nobis inflictas, sicut sunt languores et moriendi necessitas, rebellio sensualitatis et reliqua vulnera animæ. Pericula vero inferni, sunt omnia illa quæ hominem trahunt ad spiritualem interitum. Hos dolores, hæque pericula, non ignorabat beatus Job, qui ait : Sagittæ Domini in me sunt, quarum indignatio ebibit spiritum meum, et terrores Domini militant contra me.
paras.en: [[114:3|have compassed me|Circumdederunt]], that is, have assailed me in abundance and on every side, set as I am in the midst of snares, [[114:3|The sorrows of death|dolores mortis]], that is, deadly pains, violent temptations, disordered affections, which bring everlasting death upon the soul unless God's kindness come to its aid; [[114:3|and the perils of hell|et pericula inferni]], that is, mortal sins, or at least the way of falling easily into them, [[114:3|have found me|invenerunt me]], when I lost grace by consenting to evil affections. Mortal sins are called perils of hell because through them the soul perishes for ever, to be cast into hell. We may also take the sorrows of death to be the penalties that followed from original sin and were inflicted on us because of it, such as sicknesses and the necessity of dying, the rebellion of sensuality and the other wounds of the soul. And the perils of hell are all those things that draw a man to spiritual ruin. These sorrows and these perils were not unknown to blessed Job, who says: [[Job 6:4|the arrows of the Lord are in me, the rage whereof drinketh up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord war against me|Sagittæ Domini in me sunt, quarum indignatio ebibit spiritum meum, et terrores Domini militant contra me]].

paras.t: Tribulationem in corpore et dolorem in anima inveni per experientiam earumdem. Quemadmodum dicit Apostolus : Nullam requiem habuit caro nostra, sed omnem tribulationem passi sumus : foris pugnæ, intus timores ; et : Supra modum gravati sumus. Ecce quomodo præelecti Dei viventis, flagellis præsentis vitæ purgantur, circumciduntur, et poliuntur, ut fiant lapides apti, ex quibus ædificentur muri Jerusalem. Ideoque in Proverbiis scriptum est : Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, et ne deficias quum ab illo corriperis : quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi. Hinc quoque angelus Raphael dixit Tobiæ : Quia acceptus eras Deo, necesse fuit ut tentatio probaret te. Non ergo frangamur adversis ; sed quo pluribus malis vallamur, eo fiducialius pleniusque speremus nos ad electorum ac filiorum numerum pertinere. Sed pro gratia inconcussæ patientiæ indesinenter oremus, sicut subjungitur : et nomen Domini invocavi, ut mecum esset per gratiam, meque erueret, si utile esset animæ meæ. Unde scriptum est : Clamavi ad Dominum de tribulatione mea, et exaudivit me. Quum angustiaretur in me spiritus meus, Domini recordatus sum.
paras.en: [[114:3|I met with trouble|Tribulationem]] in the body [[114:3|and sorrow|et dolorem]] in the soul, by experiencing them. As the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 7:5|our flesh had no rest: but we suffered all tribulation. Combats without: fears within|Nullam requiem habuit caro nostra, sed omnem tribulationem passi sumus : foris pugnæ, intus timores]]; and: [[2 Cor 1:8|we were pressed out of measure|Supra modum gravati sumus]]. Behold how the chosen of the living God are purged, circumcised and polished by the scourges of this present life, that they may become fit stones, of which the walls of Jerusalem are built. And therefore it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:11|My son, reject not the correction of the Lord: and do not faint when thou art chastised by him|Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, et ne deficias quum ab illo corriperis]]: [[Prov 3:12|For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth: and as a father in the son he pleaseth himself|quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi]]. Hence too the angel Raphael said to Tobias: [[Tob 12:13|because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove thee|Quia acceptus eras Deo, necesse fuit ut tentatio probaret te]]. Let us not then be broken by adversity; but the more evils hem us in, the more confidently and fully let us hope that we belong to the number of the elect and of the sons. But let us pray unceasingly for the grace of unshaken patience, as is added: [[114:4|And I called upon the name of the Lord|et nomen Domini invocavi]], that he might be with me by grace and deliver me, if it were profitable to my soul. Hence it is written: [[Jon 2:3|I cried out of my affliction to the Lord, and he heard me|Clamavi ad Dominum de tribulatione mea, et exaudivit me]]. [[Jon 2:8|When my soul was in distress within me, I remembered the Lord|Quum angustiaretur in me spiritus meus, Domini recordatus sum]].

paras.t: O Domine, libera animam meam ab omni periculo, qui es misericors Dominus, quoniam peccatori pœnitenti statim indulges ; et justus, quoniam nullum malum impunitum relinquis, et me propter peccata mea in hac vita tantis castigationibus percussisti. Unde Job ait : Deus inultum abire non patitur. Et Deus noster miseretur : prout liber Sapientiæ testatur : Misereris omnium, quoniam omnia potes, et dissimulas peccata hominum propter pœnitentiam ; et in Joele : Convertimini ad Dominum, quia benignus et misericors est, patiens et multæ misericordiæ, et præstabilis super malitia.
paras.en: [[114:4|O Lord, deliver my soul|O Domine, libera animam meam]] from every peril, thou who art the [[114:5|merciful|misericors]] Lord, since thou forgivest the penitent sinner at once; [[114:5|and just|et justus]], since thou leavest no evil unpunished, and hast struck me in this life with such great chastisements for my sins. Hence Job says: [[Job 24:12|God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged|Deus inultum abire non patitur]]. [[114:5|and our God sheweth mercy|Et Deus noster miseretur]]: as the book of Wisdom testifies: [[Wis 11:24|thou hast mercy upon all, because thou canst do all things, and overlookest the sins of men for the sake of repentance|Misereris omnium, quoniam omnia potes, et dissimulas peccata hominum propter pœnitentiam]]; and in Joel: [[Joel 2:13|turn to the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, patient and rich in mercy, and ready to repent of the evil|Convertimini ad Dominum, quia benignus et misericors est, patiens et multæ misericordiæ, et præstabilis super malitia]].

paras.t: Custodiens parvulos, id est humiles a peccatis gratiose præservans, est Dominus. Superbis enim resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam. Quapropter in Proverbiis legitur : Sapientia protegit gradientes simpliciter, id est humiliter ; et apud Isaiam : Dominus excelsus et sublimis, habitans æternitatem, et sanctum nomen ejus, in excelso et in sancto habitans, et cum contrito ac humili spiritu : ut vivificet spiritum humilium, et vivificet cor contritorum. Humiliatus sum, descendens a monte superbiæ, et agens quod Ecclesiasticus consulit : Quanto magnus es, humilia te in omnibus ; et liberavit me a malis pœnarum multarum ac variis vitiis. Propter quod in prima Petri monet sermo divinus : Humiliamini sub potenti manu Dei, ut vos exaltet in tempore visitationis.
paras.en: [[114:6|The Lord is the keeper of little ones|Custodiens parvulos]], that is, he graciously preserves the humble from sins. For he [[Jas 4:6|resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble|Superbis enim resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]]. Wherefore we read in Proverbs: Wisdom protecteth [[Prov 2:7|them that walk in simplicity|gradientes simpliciter]], that is, humbly; and in Isaias, of the Lord: the [[Is 57:15|High and the Eminent that inhabiteth eternity: and his name is Holy, who dwelleth in the high and holy place, and with a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite|Dominus excelsus et sublimis, habitans æternitatem, et sanctum nomen ejus, in excelso et in sancto habitans, et cum contrito ac humili spiritu : ut vivificet spiritum humilium, et vivificet cor contritorum]]. [[114:6|I was humbled|Humiliatus sum]], coming down from the mountain of pride, and doing what Ecclesiasticus counsels: [[Ecclus 3:20|The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things|Quanto magnus es, humilia te in omnibus]]; [[114:6|and he delivered me|et liberavit me]] from the evils of many punishments and from various vices. For which reason the divine word warns in the first Epistle of Peter: [[1 Pet 5:6|Be you humbled therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in the time of visitation|Humiliamini sub potenti manu Dei, ut vos exaltet in tempore visitationis]].

paras.t: Convertere, anima mea, a turbulentis cogitationibus, a supervacuis sollicitudinibus, ab impetuosis inordinatisque motibus passionum atque facinorum, in requiem tuam, id est ad pacem internam, ad contemplationem quietam, ad stabilitatem mentalem, ad tui ipsius vacationem, ad conscientiæ securitatem. Et quoniam ista reperiri non valent nisi in Deo, idcirco convertere, o anima mea, a multis in requiem tuam, videlicet ad unum quod solum necessarium est, a creaturis ad Creatorem, de quo in Isaia scriptum est : Requiem dabit tibi Dominus semper, et implebit splendoribus animam tuam. Quia Dominus benefecit tibi : id est, merito in Deum converti debes, quiescendo in eo, sicut in ultimo fine summoque bono, propter beneficia ejus, quibus te a malis eripuit, a periculis præservavit, gratiaque implevit. Hæc autem beneficia specificantur, dum subditur :
paras.en: [[114:7|Turn, O my soul|Convertere, anima mea]], from turbulent thoughts, from needless cares, from the violent and disordered motions of passions and of evil deeds, [[114:7|into thy rest|in requiem tuam]], that is, to inward peace, to quiet contemplation, to steadiness of mind, to leisure for thyself [that is, being free and at rest within oneself], to security of conscience. And since these cannot be found except in God, therefore turn, O my soul, from many things into thy rest, namely to the one thing that alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]], from creatures to the Creator, of whom it is written in Isaias: [[Is 58:11|the Lord will give thee rest continually, and will fill thy soul with brightness|Requiem dabit tibi Dominus semper, et implebit splendoribus animam tuam]]. [[114:7|for the Lord hath been bountiful to thee|Quia Dominus benefecit tibi]]: that is, thou oughtest rightly to turn to God, resting in him as in thy last end and highest good, because of his benefits, by which he has snatched thee from evils, preserved thee from perils and filled thee with grace. And these benefits are specified when it is added:

paras.t: Quia eripuit animam meam de morte peccati, in qua fuit ; de morte quoque inferni, in qua nisi Deus misericorditer pepercisset, fuisset ; oculos meos a lacrimis, id est a causa plangendi : quia enim de peccato eum eripuit, abstulit ei causam lacrimandi. Vel, A lacrimis, quas pro peccatis effudi, dando mihi consolationem internam de spe remissionis, et ita mitigavit in me dolorem ac fletum. Vel sic, et melius, ut videtur : Eripuit oculos meos a lacrimis, quæ solent venire ex pusillanimitate, seu inordinata tristitia, aut alia qualibet irrationabili causa. Has lacrimas expedit nobis auferri, non autem lacrimas ex recordatione peccati, seu desiderio Dei ac patriæ emanantes, nisi forte ad tempus, quum ipsæ sint maximum donum Spiritus Sancti. De illarum vero cessatione lacrimarum Dominus ait per Jeremiam : Quiescat vox tua a ploratu, et oculi tui a lacrimis, quia est merces operi tuo. De his autem lacrimis Dominus ait apud Matthæum : Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur. Pedes meos, id est affectus meos, cogitationes et opera, eripuit a lapsu, id est a ruina peccati.
paras.en: [[114:8|For he hath delivered my soul from death|Quia eripuit animam meam de morte]] of sin, in which it was; and also from the death of hell, in which it would have been had not God mercifully spared it; [[114:8|my eyes from tears|oculos meos a lacrimis]], that is, from cause for lamenting: for since he snatched him from sin, he took away from him the cause of weeping. Or, [[114:8|from tears|A lacrimis]] which I shed for my sins, by giving me inward consolation from the hope of forgiveness, and so he softened grief and weeping in me. Or thus, and better, as it seems: he [[114:8|hath delivered|Eripuit]] [[114:8|my eyes from tears|oculos meos a lacrimis]] that are wont to come from faint-heartedness, or disordered sadness, or any other unreasonable cause. It is good for us that these tears be taken away, but not the tears that flow from the remembrance of sin or from longing for God and the fatherland, except perhaps for a time, since they are a very great gift of the Holy Ghost. Of the ceasing of those former tears the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 31:16|Let thy voice cease from weeping, and thy eyes tears: for there is a reward for thy work|Quiescat vox tua a ploratu, et oculi tui a lacrimis, quia est merces operi tuo]]. But of these latter tears the Lord says in Matthew: [[Matt 5:5|Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted|Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur]]. [[114:8|my feet|Pedes meos]], that is, my affections, thoughts and works, he hath delivered [[114:8|from falling|a lapsu]], that is, from the ruin of sin.

paras.t: Hinc ergo, ut spero, Placebo Domino plene atque perfecte, in regione vivorum, id est in patria Beatorum qui veraciter vivunt, in tantum, ut nostra vita, illorum vitæ comparata, mors sit potius dicenda, quam vita. In hac vita, in qua justus septies cadit in die, in qua omnes nostræ justitiæ sunt quasi pannus menstruatæ, Deo perfecte placere non possumus, quoniam videt in nobis venialia mala, quæ sibi nullatenus placent, et aliqualiter displicent. In patria vero perfecte ei placebimus, quoniam nihil impuritatis inerit nobis, sed erimus ei, ratione perfectæ munditiæ, similes.
paras.en: Hence then, as I hope, [[114:9|I will please the Lord|Placebo Domino]] fully and perfectly [[114:9|in the land of the living|in regione vivorum]], that is, in the fatherland of the Blessed, who truly live; so much so that our life, compared with theirs, should rather be called death than life. In this life, in which the just man falls seven times a day[[Prov 24:16||]], in which [[Is 64:6|all our justices as the rag of a menstruous woman|omnes nostræ justitiæ sunt quasi pannus menstruatæ]], we cannot please God perfectly, since he sees in us venial evils, which in no way please him and in some measure displease him. But in the fatherland we shall please him perfectly, since there will be no impurity in us, but we shall be like him by reason of perfect cleanness[[1 John 3:2||]].

paras.t: Specialiter autem convenire possunt tres isti versiculi viro devoto in extremis agenti, qui videns mortem sibi jam esse propinquam, alloqui potest animam suam, dicendo : Convertere, anima mea, de corpore mortis hujus, de præsentibus istis pressuris, de gravi isto exsilio, in requiem tuam, id est in paradisum cœlestem, in vitam æternam, quia Dominus benefecit tibi in vita ista per gratiam. Idcirco redi ad Creatorem tuum, per ferventem amorem, ut benefaciat tibi per gloriam. De hac etenim requie accipi potest quod Dominus per Isaiam testatur : Erit, inquiens, securitas usque in sempiternum ; et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta.
paras.en: These three verses can also apply in particular to a devout man at the point of death, who, seeing death now near him, can address his soul, saying: [[114:7|Turn, O my soul|Convertere, anima mea]], [[Rom 7:24|from the body of this death|de corpore mortis hujus]] [the margin gives Rom. xi, 24; the words are Rom 7:24], from these present afflictions, from this grievous exile, [[114:7|into thy rest|in requiem tuam]], that is, into the heavenly paradise, into life everlasting, [[114:7|for the Lord hath been bountiful to thee|quia Dominus benefecit tibi]] in this life by grace. Therefore return to thy Creator by fervent love, that he may be bountiful to thee by glory.
