For of this rest may be taken what the Lord testifies by Isaias: There shall be, he says, [[Is 32:17|security for ever|securitas usque in sempiternum]]; [[Is 32:18|And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta]].

paras.t: Quia eripuit animam meam de morte : sicut expositum est. Vel ideo ista dicuntur, quoniam sanguine suo eripuit Christus animas nostras a morte æterna, de qua in Apocalypsi scriptum est : Qui vicerit, non lædetur a morte secunda. Oculos meos a lacrimis, quas in inferno habuissem, in quo erit fletus stridorque dentium, nisi Christus me liberasset; pedes meos a lapsu, quia in se stabilivit vota et opera mea.
paras.en: [[114:8|For he hath delivered my soul from death|Quia eripuit animam meam de morte]]: as has been explained. Or these things are said because Christ by his blood has delivered our souls from eternal death, of which it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 2:11|He that shall overcome shall not be hurt by the second death|Qui vicerit, non lædetur a morte secunda]]. [[114:8|my eyes from tears|Oculos meos a lacrimis]] which I should have had in hell, where there shall be [[Luke 13:28|weeping and gnashing of teeth|fletus stridorque dentium]] [the margin adds "and elsewhere"], had not Christ set me free; [[114:8|my feet from falling|pedes meos a lapsu]], because he has made my desires and works steadfast in himself.

paras.t: Ecce psalmus hic brevis sententiarum plenitudine decoratur : in quo pulchre instruimur, quid nobis in adversis agendum sit, ubi intentionem ac desideria nostra figere debeamus, et beneficia Dei in ipso compendiose recolimus. Merito etiam psalmus iste in defunctorum Officio caput est, quia in eo multa dicuntur, quæ vel in persona defunctorum vel pro ipsis defunctis dici possunt. Defuncti enim (pro quibus oramus) qui sunt in purgatorio, diligunt Deum, et sciunt se a tormentis liberandos : pro qua tamen liberatione ipsi orare non possunt oratione meritoria, quamvis eam inæstimabiliter cupiant. Denique certi sunt se nunquam damnandos : de quo, proh dolor ! nos certi non sumus. Propter quod necesse est nos timorate atque sollicite ambulare cum Deo nostro, illudque Apostoli adimplere : Cum metu, timore et tremore vestram salutem operamini. Ob hanc etiam causam sanctus Job dixit : Semper quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum. Nec mirum, quum nemo nostrum sciat, an amore dignus sit an odio.
paras.en: Behold, this short psalm is adorned with a fullness of meaning: in it we are finely taught what we must do in adversity, and where we ought to fix our intention and desires, and in it we briefly recall the benefits of God. Rightly too this psalm stands at the head of the Office of the Dead, for many things are said in it that can be said either in the person of the dead or for the dead themselves. For the dead (for whom we pray) who are in purgatory love God and know that they will be freed from their torments; yet they cannot pray for that deliverance with meritorious prayer, though they desire it beyond all reckoning. Lastly, they are certain that they will never be damned: of which, alas, we are not certain. Wherefore we must walk fearfully and solicitously with our God[[Mich 6:8||]], and fulfil that saying of the Apostle: [[Phil 2:12|with fear and trembling work out your salvation|Cum metu, timore et tremore vestram salutem operamini]] [Denis reads "with fear, dread and trembling"]. For this reason too holy Job said: [[Job 31:23|I have always feared God as waves swelling over me|Semper quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum]]. Nor is it any wonder, since none of us knows whether he is worthy of love or of hatred[[Eccles 9:1||]].

paras.t: Precatio. Deus cœli et terræ, vocem orationis te diligentium benignus admitte, aurem clementiæ precibus te invocantium inclina : ab omni tribulatione et dolore nos libera, et ab hac transeuntibus vita, redde nobis bona sempiterna.
paras.en: Prayer. God of heaven and earth, graciously receive the voice of the prayer of those who love thee; incline the ear of thy clemency to the prayers of those who call upon thee; deliver us from all trouble and sorrow, and when we pass from this life, render to us the goods everlasting.

115.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUINTIDECIMI : CREDIDI, PROPTER QUOD.
115.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and fifteenth psalm: I have believed, therefore.

paras.t: Hujus quoque psalmi, sicut præcedentium, titulus est : Alleluia. Et sicut præcedentem psalmum quidam exponunt ad litteram de David constituto in persecutione Saulis, ita quod in psalmo illo petit liberari ab illa persecutione injusta; sic psalmum præsentem exponunt ad litteram de David constituto in persecutione Absalonis filii sui, ut sit sensus primi versiculi : Credidi Sibæ dicenti mihi de domino suo Miphiboseth verba mendacia ; propter quod locutus sum ad Sibam : Omnia quæ erant domini tui, tua sint ; ego autem humiliatus, id est contemptus et exprobratus, sum nimis, quia propter Absalonem fugam. Secundum hanc expositionem loquitur David hic de sua credulitate mala et levi atque decepta (nam credidit pessimo detractori, sine debita inquisitione), et de locutione sua injusta, qua ex falsa credulitate contulit Sibæ omnia bona pii viri, puta Miphiboseth.
paras.en: The title of this psalm too, as of the preceding ones, is: Alleluia. And just as some expound the preceding psalm literally of David set in the persecution of Saul, so that in that psalm he asks to be delivered from that unjust persecution, so they expound the present psalm literally of David set in the persecution of Absalom his son, so that the sense of the first verse is: [[115:1|I have believed|Credidi]] Siba, who spoke lying words to me about his master Miphiboseth[[2 Kings 16:3||]]; [[115:1|therefore have I spoken|propter quod locutus sum]] to Siba: All that was thy master's, let it be thine[[2 Kings 16:4||]]; [[115:1|but I have been humbled|ego autem humiliatus]], that is, despised and reproached, [[115:1|exceedingly|sum nimis]], because on account of Absalom I took flight[[2 Kings 15:14||]] [the Latin has only *quia propter Absalonem fugam*, "because on account of Absalom … flight": a verb seems to have dropped out]. According to this exposition David speaks here of his own credulity, wrong, light and deceived (for he believed a most wicked slanderer without due inquiry), and of his unjust speech, by which, out of a false belief, he bestowed on Siba all the goods of a good man, namely Miphiboseth.

paras.t: Hæc autem expositio non videtur consonare expositioni seu allegationi Pauli apostoli, qui Sancto Spiritu plenus, et mentem David plenissime sciens, allegat hæc verba in secunda epistola ad Corinthios, tanquam dicta de bona credulitate fidei sanctæ, et sancta confessione veritatis creditæ, de quibus ad Romanos ait : Corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem. Sic enim allegat versum præsentem : Sicut scriptum est : Credidi, propter quod locutus sum ; et nos credimus, propter quod et loquimur. Unde certum est, quod Apostolus innuit istam scripturam ad litteram loqui de bona credulitate atque salubri locutione. Et ita David non fecit hunc psalmum de se ipso ad sensum prætactum. Dicendum itaque, quod materia psalmi istius, est constantia fidelium, et maxime sanctorum martyrum, in fide et fidei publica professione. In quorum persona ait Propheta :
paras.en: But this exposition does not seem to agree with the exposition, or citation, of Paul the Apostle, who, being full of the Holy Ghost and knowing David's mind most fully, cites these words in the second epistle to the Corinthians as spoken of the good belief of holy faith and of the holy confession of the truth believed, of which he says to the Romans: [[Rom 10:10|with the heart, we believe unto justice: but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation|Corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem]]. For thus he cites the present verse: [[2 Cor 4:13|as it is written: I believed, for which cause I have spoken; we also believe. For which cause we speak also|Sicut scriptum est : Credidi, propter quod locutus sum ; et nos credimus, propter quod et loquimur]]. Hence it is certain that the Apostle intimates that this scripture speaks, in the literal sense, of good belief and wholesome speech. And so David did not make this psalm about himself in the sense touched on above. It must be said, therefore, that the matter of this psalm is the constancy of the faithful, and above all of the holy martyrs, in the faith and in the public profession of the faith. In their person the Prophet says:

paras.t: Credidi quæcumque fides catholica exigit esse credenda ; propter quod locutus sum, publice confitendo coram infidelibus et tyrannis, seu aliis quibuscumque, ea quæ credo. Primo autem creditur, deinde vera confessio sequitur, quæ ex fide originatur : nec sufficit unum sine alio in certo casu. Quod enim sine fide non sufficiat locutio seu confessio, certum est, quum justus ex fide vivat. Quod vero necesse sit fidem confiteri coram hominibus, quando rationabilis causa occurrit, videlicet ne alii scandalizentur, vel Deus blasphemetur, liquet ex eo quod Christus ait : Qui me erubuerit et meos sermones, hunc Filius hominis erubescet, quum venerit in regno suo. Et ad Timotheum ait Apostolus: Noli erubescere testimonium Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Hoc martyres sancti eminentissime impleverunt. Nos quoque in pace Ecclesiæ credimus, et proximis nostris credita loquimur et confitemur. Ego autem propter veram fidem et sanctam confessionem, humiliatus, id est vexatus, contemptus et passus, sum nimis ab adversariis veritatis : quemadmodum Christus in Evangelio ait, In mundo pressuram habebitis ; et iterum, Odio eritis omnibus hominibus propter nomen meum. Vel, Ego humiliatus sum nimis, id est, de vera fide et confessione constanti non superbivi, nec aliquid boni viribus meis adscripsi, sed me ipsum coram Deo profundissime humiliavi, idcirco ab eo merui conservari.
paras.en: [[115:1|I have believed|Credidi]] whatever the Catholic faith requires to be believed; [[115:1|therefore have I spoken|propter quod locutus sum]], confessing publicly before unbelievers and tyrants, or any others whatever, the things that I believe. Now first one believes, and then true confession follows, which springs from faith; nor, in a given case, is the one enough without the other. For that speech or confession is not enough without faith is certain, since the [[Rom 1:17|just man liveth by faith|justus ex fide vivat]]. And that it is necessary to confess the faith before men when a reasonable cause arises, namely lest others be scandalized or God be blasphemed, is plain from Christ's saying: [[Luke 9:26|he that shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of man shall be ashamed|Qui me erubuerit et meos sermones, hunc Filius hominis erubescet]], when he shall come in his kingdom [Denis reads *in regno suo*, "in his kingdom", where the Vulgate has "in his majesty"]. And the Apostle says to Timothy: [[2 Tim 1:8|Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord|Noli erubescere testimonium Domini nostri]] Jesus Christ. This the holy martyrs fulfilled most eminently. We too, in the peace of the Church, believe, and speak and confess to our neighbours what we believe. [[115:1|but I|Ego autem]], on account of the true faith and holy confession, [[115:1|have been humbled|humiliatus]], that is, harassed, despised and made to suffer, [[115:1|exceedingly|sum nimis]] by the adversaries of the truth: as Christ says in the Gospel, [[John 16:33|In the world you shall have distress|In mundo pressuram habebitis]]; and again, [[Matt 10:22|you shall be hated by all men for my name's sake|Odio eritis omnibus hominibus propter nomen meum]]. Or, [[115:1|I have been humbled exceedingly|Ego humiliatus sum nimis]]: that is, I was not proud of the true faith and of my constant confession, nor did I ascribe any good to my own strength, but humbled myself most deeply before God; therefore I deserved to be preserved by him.

paras.t: Ego dixi in excessu meo, id est in sublimi consideratione seu contemplatione ecstatica, qua speculatus sum distinctionem inter divinam essentiam atque humanam naturam : Omnis homo mendax, id est, quilibet homo per comparationem ejus ad Deum, et consideratus secundum se ipsum, est mendax, verbo vel opere, vel patientia, vel comparatione: ita quod sicut Deus est ens et veritas, sic homo est nihil et mendax, si referatur ad veritatem, essentiamque divinam. Dicitur ergo omnis homo mendax, non ab habitu falsitatis, sed quia interdum mentitus est verbo vel actu, loquendo aut operando non recte, non juste, non vere, et per consequens mendaciter et oblique. Unde ad Romanos scribit Apostolus : Est autem Deus verax, omnis autem homo mendax. Et apud Jeremiam dicitur Deo : Ad te gentes venient ab extremis terræ, et dicent : Vere mendacium possederunt patres nostri, vanitatem quæ eis non profuit. Quemadmodum namque verum multipliciter dicitur, ita et mendax. Nam alia est veritas vitæ, alia veritas entis, alia veritas propositionis. Iterum alia est veritas vitæ, alia veritas doctrinæ, alia justitiæ. Similiter aliud est mendacium vitæ, quod simulatio appellari posse videtur, vel injustitia ; aliud est mendacium entis, sicut dicimus, Istud est falsum et sophisticatum aurum ; aliud vero est mendacium orationis. Et certum est, quod omnis homo viator, sit aliquo horum modorum mendax, quum non sit homo super terram, qui faciat bonum et non peccet, ut dicit Ecclesiastes. Imo Jacobo teste, In multis offendimus omnes. Vel dicitur omnis homo secundum se mendax, id est instabilis, fragilis, ad peccata proclivus.
paras.en: [[115:2|I said in my excess|Ego dixi in excessu meo]], that is, in a lofty consideration or ecstatic contemplation, in which I beheld the distinction between the divine essence and human nature: [[115:2|Every man is a liar|Omnis homo mendax]]; that is, any man whatever, in comparison with God and considered in himself, is a liar, in word or deed, or in suffering, or by comparison: so that, as God is being and truth, so man is nothing and a liar, if he is set against the truth and the divine essence. Every man, then, is called a liar, not from a habit of falsehood, but because at times he has lied in word or act, speaking or acting not rightly, not justly, not truly, and consequently falsely and crookedly. Hence the Apostle writes to the Romans: [[Rom 3:4|God is true and every man a liar|Est autem Deus verax, omnis autem homo mendax]]. And in Jeremias it is said to God: [[Jer 16:19|to thee the Gentiles shall come from the ends of the earth, and shall say: Surely our fathers have possessed lies, a vanity which hath not profited them|Ad te gentes venient ab extremis terræ, et dicent : Vere mendacium possederunt patres nostri, vanitatem quæ eis non profuit]]. For as *true* is said in many ways, so too is *liar*. For the truth of life is one thing, the truth of being another, the truth of a proposition another. Again, the truth of life is one thing, the truth of doctrine another, that of justice another. Likewise the lie of life, which it seems may be called pretence, or injustice, is one thing; the lie of being another, as when we say, This is false and counterfeit gold; and the lie of speech yet another. And it is certain that every man still on the way [that is, a *viator*, one still journeying in this life, not yet in the homeland] is a liar in some one of these ways, since [[Eccles 7:21|there is no just man upon earth, that doth good, and sinneth not|non sit homo super terram, qui faciat bonum et non peccet]], as Ecclesiastes says. Indeed, as James bears witness, [[Jas 3:2|in many things we all offend|In multis offendimus omnes]]. Or every man is called a liar in himself, that is, unstable, frail, prone to sins.

paras.t: Quum ergo omnis homo ex se sit mendax, ego autem ex gratia Dei verax sum, ideo Quid retribuam Domino, id est, quid dignum restituam ei, et quam ei vicissitudinem reddam, pro omnibus quae retribuit mihi, id est pro omnibus donis gratiae suae, quae saepe contulit mihi? quia in primo parente dedit ea mihi, et peccavi in illo amisique ea. Rursus dedit mihi ea in Baptismo, sed iterum peccans, perdidi dona gratiae Dei; ipse vero in sacramento Poenitentiae ea mihi retribuit. Quis autem omnia beneficia Dei generalia et specialia, naturalia atque gratuita, numerare vel exprimere poterit? Omnia condidit propter nos, ad nostram custodiam deputat atque transmittit angelos sanctos. Tandem ipsemet venit ad nos, et in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est, corpore suo et sanguine alit nos, propter nos mori dignatus est. Versiculus iste cum ingenti devotione dicendus est, quatenus tota mente optemus Deo esse grati, ejus beneficia memoriter atque frequenter recolendo, eaque Domino humiliter confitendo, ipsum pro eis ferventer amando, reverenter colendo. Sed quoniam Deus bonorum nostrorum non eget, sicut primo Paralipomenon Scriptura affirmat, Tua, Domine, sunt omnia, et quae de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi; idcirco nil dignius ei rependere possum, nisi ut sequar vestigia ejus, et offeram ei me ipsum, passionem ac mortem seu alia dura sustinendo libenter pro ejus amore: sicut subjungitur.
paras.en: Since, then, every man of himself is a liar, but I by the grace of God am truthful, therefore: [[115:3|What shall I render to the Lord|Quid retribuam Domino]], that is, what worthy return shall I make him, and what requital shall I give him, [[115:3|for all the things that he hath rendered to me|pro omnibus quae retribuit mihi]], that is, for all the gifts of his grace which he has often bestowed on me? For in our first parent he gave them to me, and I sinned in him and lost them. Again he gave them to me in Baptism, but sinning once more I lost the gifts of God's grace; and he gave them back to me in the sacrament of Penance. Yet who could number or tell all God's benefits, general and special, natural and gratuitous? He made all things for our sake; he appoints and sends the holy angels to guard us. At last he came to us himself, and [[Bar 3:38|was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]]; he feeds us with his own body and blood; he deigned to die for us. This verse is to be said with great devotion, so that with our whole mind we may desire to be grateful to God, recalling his benefits from memory and often, humbly confessing them to the Lord, loving him fervently for them, and reverently worshipping him. But since God has no need of our goods[[Ps 15:2||]], as Scripture affirms in the first book of Paralipomenon, [[1 Par 29:14|all things are thine: and we have given thee what we received of thy hand|Tua, Domine, sunt omnia, et quae de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi]], I can repay him with nothing worthier than to follow in his footsteps and offer myself to him, willingly bearing suffering and death or other hard things for love of him: as follows.

paras.t: Calicem salutaris, id est passionem, persecutionem, seu mortem salutis, id est per quam ad salutem pertingitur : per calicem namque venitur ad gloriam ; accipiam, id est, æquanimiter feram. Vel : Calicem salutaris, id est vitam poenitentialem, mei ipsius districtam castigationem, quotidianamque mortificationem, accipiam, bajulando crucem meam quotidie, et Christum sectando. Nam, ut ait Apostolus ad Romanos, si spiritu facta carnis mortificaverimus, vivemus. Et nomen Domini invocabo, ne in adversis deficiam, aut in propriis meritis sperare incipiam, aut mihi aliquid tribuam.
paras.en: [[115:4|the chalice of salvation|Calicem salutaris]], that is, the passion, persecution or death of salvation, that is, by which salvation is reached: for through the chalice one comes to glory; [[115:4|I will take|accipiam]], that is, I will bear it with an even mind. Or: [[115:4|the chalice of salvation|Calicem salutaris]], that is, a life of penance, strict chastisement of myself and daily mortification, [[115:4|I will take|accipiam]], carrying my cross daily and following Christ. For, as the Apostle says to the Romans, [[Rom 8:13|if by the Spirit you mortify the deeds of the flesh, you shall live|si spiritu facta carnis mortificaverimus, vivemus]]. [[115:4|and I will call upon the name of the Lord|Et nomen Domini invocabo]], lest I fail in adversity, or begin to hope in my own merits, or ascribe anything to myself.

paras.t: Vota mea, id est desideria mea, Domino reddam, nihil inordinatum aut Deo contrarium cupiendo, sed cœlestia acquirendo, atque pro eis rogando, coram omni populo ejus fideli præsente, ut ipsi quoque desideria sua Domino reddant, et meo exemplo cœlestia appetant. Vel : Vota mea Domino reddam, id est, promissiones meas ad laudem Domini adimplebo: juxta illud Ecclesiastæ : Si quid vovisti Deo, ne moreris reddere; displicet enim ei infidelis et stulta promissio. Et Jonas: Quæcumque (inquit) vovi, reddam Domino pro salute. In Baptismo promisimus abrenuntiare omnibus pompis et actibus Satanæ; in religionis professione spopondimus paupertatem, castitatem et obedientiam: et utinam vota ista Domino persolvamus! Reddam ergo Domino vota hæc non solum in occulto, sed coram omni populo, non propter inanem gloriam, sed ad Dei honorem et proximorum ædificationem, quatenus illud Matthæi perficiam : Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant bona facta vestra, et glorificent Patrem.
paras.en: [[115:5|I will pay my vows|Vota mea]], that is, my desires, [[115:5|to the Lord|Domino reddam]], coveting nothing disordered or contrary to God, but seeking heavenly things and praying for them, [[115:5|before all his people|coram omni populo ejus]], the faithful being present, so that they too may pay their desires to the Lord and by my example seek heavenly things. Or: [[115:5|I will pay my vows to the Lord|Vota mea Domino reddam]], that is, I will fulfil my promises to the praise of the Lord: according to that saying of Ecclesiastes, [[Eccles 5:3|If thou hast vowed any thing to God, defer not to pay it: for an unfaithful and foolish promise displeaseth him|Si quid vovisti Deo, ne moreris reddere; displicet enim ei infidelis et stulta promissio]] [the margin gives Eccles. v, 1; the words are Eccles 5:3]. And Jonas says: [[Jon 2:10|I will pay whatsoever I have vowed for my salvation to the Lord|Quæcumque (inquit) vovi, reddam Domino pro salute]]. In Baptism we promised to renounce all the pomps and works of Satan; in the profession of religion we vowed poverty, chastity and obedience: and would that we paid those vows to the Lord! I will pay these vows to the Lord, then, not only in secret, but before all the people, not for vain glory, but for the honour of God and the edification of my neighbours, so as to fulfil that word of Matthew: [[Matt 5:16|So let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father|Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant bona facta vestra, et glorificent Patrem]].

paras.t: Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum ejus : id est, coram Deo digna atque accepta est decessio hominum perfectorum, quoniam mors hæc, janua est vitæ æternæ. Homines autem ubertim parvi pendunt mortem vel occisionem Sanctorum; sed Deus judicat eam æterno præmio munerandam. Hinc nempe ab Isaia dicitur : Justus perit, et non est qui recogitet in corde suo; et viri misericordiæ tolluntur, et non est qui intelligat. Et in libro Sapientiæ : Justus si morte præoccupatus fuerit, in refrigerio erit.
paras.en: [[115:6|Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints|Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum ejus]]: that is, before God the departure of perfect men is worthy and acceptable, since this death is the gate of eternal life. Men, for their part, commonly make little of the death or slaying of the Saints; but God judges that it is to be rewarded with an eternal prize. Hence indeed it is said by Isaias: [[Is 57:1|The just perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart, and men of mercy are taken away, because there is none that understandeth|Justus perit, et non est qui recogitet in corde suo; et viri misericordiæ tolluntur, et non est qui intelligat]]. And in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 4:7|the just man, if he be prevented with death, shall be in rest|Justus si morte præoccupatus fuerit, in refrigerio erit]].

paras.t: O Domine, id est, merito te Dominum voco, quia ego servus tuus, tibi obediens in credendo, ego servus tuus operando, et filius ancillæ tuæ, id est natus de matre fideli te colente ; vel, Filius ancillæ tuæ, id est Ecclesiæ tibi ministrantis.
paras.en: [[115:7|O Lord|O Domine]], that is, rightly do I call thee Lord, [[115:7|for I am thy servant|quia ego servus tuus]], obeying thee in believing; [[115:7|I am thy servant|ego servus tuus]] in working, [[115:7|and the son of thy handmaid|et filius ancillæ tuæ]], that is, born of a faithful mother who worships thee; or, [[115:7|the son of thy handmaid|Filius ancillæ tuæ]], that is, of the Church that serves thee.

paras.t: Dirupisti vincula mea, id est consuetudines malas et opera vitiosa, quæ hominem stringunt, ne ad Dei obsequium libere vadat. Hæc enim ligant, captumque tenent peccatorem sub potestate diaboli. Hæc vincula rumpit in nobis Deus, dum peccata dimittit, gratiam influit, et de servis peccati efficit filios adoptionis. Propter quod ait Apostolus : Misit Deus Spiritum Filii sui in corda nostra, clamantem, Abba (Pater). Vel, Dirupisti vincula mea, id est omnia impedimenta, quibus a tua contemplatione impedior, scilicet pœnalitates et obligationes pœnarum. Hoc Deus non facit perfecte, nisi in morte hominum perfectorum qui evolant, quales præsertim sunt martyres. Alii enim quamvis sint sancti, et miracula maxima operati, non tamen vadunt ad Dominum securi, sed horrescit eorum conscientia, secundum Hieronymum : quod secundum communem legem accipi potest. Aliqui tamen ex speciali gratiæ dono certificati fuerunt de sua salvatione, imo et evolatione, qui martyres non fuerunt.
paras.en: [[115:7|Thou hast broken my bonds|Dirupisti vincula mea]], that is, evil habits and vicious works, which bind a man so that he cannot go freely to the service of God. For these tie the sinner and hold him captive under the power of the devil. These bonds God breaks in us when he forgives sins, pours in grace, and makes of the servants of sin sons of adoption. For which reason the Apostle says: [[Gal 4:6|God hath sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying: Abba, Father|Misit Deus Spiritum Filii sui in corda nostra, clamantem, Abba (Pater)]]. Or, [[115:7|Thou hast broken my bonds|Dirupisti vincula mea]], that is, all the hindrances by which I am kept from the contemplation of thee, namely the penalties and the debts of punishment [that is, the temporal punishment still owed for sins already forgiven]. This God does not do perfectly except in the death of perfect men who fly away [to heaven at once], such as the martyrs above all. For others, though they be saints and have worked the greatest miracles, yet do not go to the Lord free of fear, but their conscience shudders, according to Jerome: which may be taken as said of the common law. Some, however, who were not martyrs, were by a special gift of grace made certain of their salvation, and indeed of their flying away to heaven.

paras.t: Tibi sacrificabo hostiam laudis : id est, pro istis beneficiis te laudabo, et me ipsum seu alia quælibet munera tibi cum laudibus immolabo : quemadmodum scriptum est : Ego autem in voce laudis immolabo tibi; et rursus : Quid dignum offeram Domino? Curvabo genu Deo excelso. Et nomen Domini invocabo, pro conservatione atque profectu in omni bono. O quanta est virtus hujus versiculi!
paras.en: [[115:8|I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise|Tibi sacrificabo hostiam laudis]]: that is, for these benefits I will praise thee, and will offer to thee with praises myself or any other gifts whatever: as it is written, [[Jon 2:10|But I with the voice of praise will sacrifice to thee|Ego autem in voce laudis immolabo tibi]]; and again, [[Mich 6:6|What shall I offer to the Lord that is worthy? wherewith shall I kneel before the high God?|Quid dignum offeram Domino? Curvabo genu Deo excelso]] [Denis reads *Curvabo genu*, "I will bend the knee", as a statement]. [[115:8|and I will call upon the name of the Lord|Et nomen Domini invocabo]], for preservation and progress in all good. O how great is the power of this verse!

paras.t: Vota mea Domino reddam in conspectu omnis populi ejus : sicut nunc dictum atque expositum est; in atriis domus Domini, id est in locis Ecclesiæ, quæ est domus orationis, in medio tui, Jerusalem, id est in medio universalis Ecclesiæ, per totum mundum diffusæ, ita quod perseverabo in ecclesiastica unitate atque catholica fide, scissuras hæreticorum devitans. Interdum enim per Jerusalem significatur anima fidelis, et Ecclesia militans.
paras.en: [[115:9|I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all his people|Vota mea Domino reddam in conspectu omnis populi ejus]]: as has just been said and expounded; [[115:10|In the courts of the house of the Lord|in atriis domus Domini]], that is, in the places of the Church, which is the [[Matt 21:13|house of prayer|domus orationis]], [[115:10|in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem|in medio tui, Jerusalem]], that is, in the midst of the universal Church spread throughout the whole world, so that I will persevere in the unity of the Church and in the Catholic faith, shunning the schisms of heretics. For at times Jerusalem signifies the faithful soul, and the Church militant.

115.title: EXPOSITIO EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI QUINTIDECIMI DE CHRISTO, ET QUOMODO A SACERDOTE CELEBRATURO DICENDUS SIT.
115.title_en: Exposition of the same hundred and fifteenth psalm concerning Christ, and how it is to be said by a priest about to celebrate.

paras.t: Omnia insuper verba psalmi istius, de Christo convenienter satis intelligi possunt, excepto primo verbo, quo dicitur, Credidi. Quum enim Christus a principio creationis suæ animæ, fuerit comprehensor, non convenit ei fides, quæ est theologica virtus : sed sicut in superioribus frequenter attributum est Christo sperare seu spes, non prout spes est virtus theologica, sed in quantum accipitur pro quadam præstolatione boni futuri ; sic Christo attribui potest actus credendi, sumendo hunc actum pro quacumque cognitione fideli. Sicut enim interdum accipit Scriptura Scire pro Credere, ut quum sanctus Job dicit, Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum (futuram namque resurrectionem non scivit nisi per fidem); ita econtra quandoque sumit Scriptura Credere pro Scire. Sicque convenit Christo, de quo psalmus iste exponi potest hoc modo :
paras.en: Moreover, all the words of this psalm can be understood quite fittingly of Christ, except the first word, where it says, [[115:1|I have believed|Credidi]]. For since Christ was a comprehensor [that is, one already enjoying the vision of God, as the blessed do in heaven] from the beginning of the creation of his soul, faith, which is a theological virtue, does not befit him. But just as, in what went before, hoping or hope has often been attributed to Christ, not as hope is a theological virtue, but in so far as it is taken for a certain awaiting of a future good, so the act of believing can be attributed to Christ, taking this act for any faithful knowledge whatever. For as Scripture sometimes takes *knowing* for *believing*, as when holy Job says, [[Job 19:25|I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]] (for he knew the future resurrection only by faith), so conversely Scripture sometimes takes *believing* for *knowing*. And in this way it befits Christ, of whom this psalm can be expounded thus:

paras.t: Credidi, id est, de veritate eorum quæ Deus mihi (ut homo sum) revelavit, non dubitavi ; propter quod locutus sum doctrinam evangelicæ legis, asserendo me esse Christum, et veritati testimonium exhibendo : sicut in Evangelio dixi, Ego in hoc natus sum, et ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimonium perhibeam veritati. Ego autem humiliatus sum nimis a Judæis, qui me contempserunt, blasphemaverunt, et turpissima atque amarissima morte occiderunt. Unde in Isaia scriptum est : Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo, et humiliatum. Vel, Humiliatus sum nimis, id est, in proprio corde humillimus fui : secundum quod dixi apud Matthæum, Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde; et alibi, Ego non quæro gloriam meam.
paras.en: [[115:1|I have believed|Credidi]], that is, I did not doubt the truth of the things which God revealed to me (as I am man); [[115:1|therefore have I spoken|propter quod locutus sum]] the doctrine of the gospel law, declaring myself to be the Christ and bearing witness to the truth, as I said in the Gospel: [[John 18:37|For this was I born, and for this came I into the world; that I should give testimony to the truth|Ego in hoc natus sum, et ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimonium perhibeam veritati]]. [[115:1|But I have been humbled exceedingly|Ego autem humiliatus sum nimis]] by the Jews, who despised me, blasphemed me, and killed me by a most shameful and most bitter death. Whence it is written in Isaias: [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God and afflicted|Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo, et humiliatum]]. Or, [[115:1|I have been humbled exceedingly|Humiliatus sum nimis]], that is, I was most humble in my own heart, according to what I said in Matthew: [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]; and elsewhere: [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]].

paras.t: Ego dixi in excessu meo, id est in contemplatione qua Deum vidi per speciem : Omnis homo, præter me, mendax : sicut in præcedenti articulo plenius est dictum. Et quia hoc dixi, cognovi quod omnes indigerent liberari per me, sicut fatetur Apostolus : Omnes peccaverunt, et egent gloria Dei. Et hoc modo in Michæa dicitur : Periit sanctus de terra, et rectus in hominibus non est.
paras.en: [[115:2|I said in my excess|Ego dixi in excessu meo]], that is, in the contemplation in which I saw God by sight [*per speciem*: openly, face to face, as opposed to by faith]: [[115:2|Every man|Omnis homo]], except me, [[115:2|is a liar|mendax]], as was said more fully in the preceding article. And because I said this, I knew that all needed to be set free through me, as the Apostle declares: [[Rom 3:23|all have sinned and do need the glory of God|Omnes peccaverunt, et egent gloria Dei]]. And in this way it is said in Micheas: [[Mich 7:2|The holy man is perished out of the earth, and there is none upright among men|Periit sanctus de terra, et rectus in hominibus non est]].

paras.t: Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi, id est pro incomparabilibus gratiis mihi concessis? quia non ad mensuram dedit mihi Deus spiritum, et sine præviis meritis assumpsit meam humanitatem ad suum esse divinum Dei Verbum, imo plus dedit mihi, quam toti universo. Sicut Christus Deo gratissimus fuit, sic ista affectuosissime dixit.
paras.en: [[115:3|What shall I render to the Lord, for all the things that he hath rendered to me|Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi]], that is, for the incomparable graces granted to me? For God gave me the Spirit not by measure[[John 3:34||]], and without any merits going before, God the Word took up my humanity into his own divine being; indeed he gave more to me than to the whole universe. As Christ was most grateful to God, so he said these words with the deepest affection.

paras.t: Et respondet : Calicem salutaris accipiam : id est, passionem salvificam, et mortem qua mundus vivificetur, sustinebo, quatenus Dei honorem recuperem, moriendo pro omnibus, ut reducantur ad Deum. Hoc est quod Christus passione instante dixit : Calicem quem dedit mihi Pater, non bibam illum? Et alibi : Pater, si non potest hic calix transire a me, nisi bibam illum, fiat voluntas tua. Et filiis Zebedæi : Potestis, inquit, bibere calicem quem ego bibiturus sum? Et nomen Domini invocabo. Frequenter Christus Patrem invocavit. Unde scriptum est : Erat Jesus pernoctans in oratione Dei. Passione quoque instante oravit, quemadmodum ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus : Jesus cum clamore valido et lacrimis preces supplicationesque fundens ad eum, qui possit illum a morte salvum facere, exauditus est pro sua reverentia.
paras.en: And he answers: [[115:4|I will take the chalice of salvation|Calicem salutaris accipiam]], that is, I will undergo the saving passion, and the death by which the world is to be given life, so as to recover the honour of God by dying for all, that they may be brought back to God. This is what Christ said when his passion was at hand: [[John 18:11|The chalice which my father hath given me, shall I not drink it?|Calicem quem dedit mihi Pater, non bibam illum?]] And elsewhere: Father, [[Matt 26:42|if this chalice may not pass away, but I must drink it, thy will be done|si non potest hic calix transire a me, nisi bibam illum, fiat voluntas tua]]. And to the sons of Zebedee: [[Matt 20:22|Can you|Potestis]], he says, [[Matt 20:22|drink the chalice that I shall drink?|bibere calicem quem ego bibiturus sum?]] [[115:4|And I will call upon the name of the Lord|Et nomen Domini invocabo]]. Christ often called upon the Father. Hence it is written of Jesus: [[Luke 6:12|he passed the whole night in the prayer of God|Erat Jesus pernoctans in oratione Dei]]. When his passion was at hand he also prayed, as the Apostle says to the Hebrews: Jesus, [[Heb 5:7|with a strong cry and tears, offering up prayers and supplications to him that was able to save him from death, was heard for his reverence|cum clamore valido et lacrimis preces supplicationesque fundens ad eum, qui possit illum a morte salvum facere, exauditus est pro sua reverentia]].

paras.t: Vota mea Domino reddam, id est, desideria mea Deo offeram, orando atque docendo pro ejus honore et mundi salute, coram omni populo ejus præsente. Nam apud Joannem Christus dixit coram discipulis atque Judæis : Ego honorifico Patrem meum. Et in cruce suspensus, oravit : Pater, ignosce illis.
paras.en: [[115:5|I will pay my vows to the Lord|Vota mea Domino reddam]], that is, I will offer my desires to God, praying and teaching for his honour and the salvation of the world, [[115:5|before all his people|coram omni populo ejus]] there present. For in John, Christ said before the disciples and the Jews: [[John 8:49|I honour my Father|Ego honorifico Patrem meum]]. And hanging on the cross he prayed: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them|Pater, ignosce illis]].

paras.t: Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum ejus. Hoc est quod Christus in Evangelio ait : Capillus de capite vestro non peribit; et rursus, Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt. Quasi dicat : Tam pretiosa erit mors vestra Domino, quam pro nomine ejus suffertis, ut merito debeatis appetere eam.
paras.en: [[115:6|Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints|Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum ejus]]. This is what Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:18|a hair of your head shall not perish|Capillus de capite vestro non peribit]]; and again: [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not them that kill the body|Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt]]. As if he said: so precious to the Lord will be your death, which you suffer for his name, that you may rightly long for it.

paras.t: O Domine, quia ego servus tuus, in quantum homo. Unde dixi : Pater major me est; et : Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio; in Isaia quoque : Dominus formans me ex utero servum sibi. Et ipse Dominus ait de me : Ecce ego adducam servum meum Orientem. Ego servus tuus et filius ancillæ tuæ, videlicet Virginis benedictæ, quæ ait : Ecce ancilla Domini. Dirupisti vincula mea : id est, passibilitatem et omnes naturales defectus, quos sponte assumpsi, abstulisti a me, resuscitans me in corpore glorioso. Vel, Dirupisti vincula mea : id est, corpus meum et corporis membra tempore passionis rumpi, vulnerari ac lacerari permisisti, ita ut a planta pedis usque ad verticem capitis non esset in me sanitas.
paras.en: [[115:7|O Lord, for I am thy servant|O Domine, quia ego servus tuus]], in so far as I am man. Hence I said: [[John 14:28|the Father is greater than I|Pater major me est]]; and: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]; and in Isaias too: [[Is 49:5|the Lord, that formed me from the womb to be his servant|Dominus formans me ex utero servum sibi]]. And the Lord himself says of me: [[Zach 3:8|behold, I WILL BRING MY SERVANT THE ORIENT|Ecce ego adducam servum meum Orientem]]. [[115:7|I am thy servant, and the son of thy handmaid|Ego servus tuus et filius ancillæ tuæ]], namely of the blessed Virgin, who says: [[Luke 1:38|Behold the handmaid of the Lord|Ecce ancilla Domini]]. [[115:7|Thou hast broken my bonds|Dirupisti vincula mea]], that is, thou hast taken from me passibility [that is, the capacity to suffer and die] and all the natural defects which I took on of my own will, raising me again in a glorious body. Or, [[115:7|Thou hast broken my bonds|Dirupisti vincula mea]], that is, thou hast permitted my body and the members of my body to be broken, wounded and torn at the time of the passion, so that [[Is 1:6|from the sole of the foot unto the top of the head|a planta pedis usque ad verticem capitis]] there was no soundness in me.

paras.t: Tibi sacrificabo hostiam laudis, id est, me ipsum in cruce offeram ad gloriam tuam pro redemptione humana : quemadmodum ad Hebræos ait Apostolus : Christus per Spiritum Sanctum semetipsum obtulit immaculatum Deo.
paras.en: [[115:8|I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise|Tibi sacrificabo hostiam laudis]] [the Latin *hostia* is a sacrificial victim], that is, I will offer myself on the cross to thy glory for the redemption of mankind, as the Apostle says to the Hebrews: Christ, [[Heb 9:14|who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God|per Spiritum Sanctum semetipsum obtulit immaculatum Deo]].

paras.t: Vota mea Domino reddam in conspectu omnis populi ejus : sicut jam patuit; in atriis domus Domini, in medio tui, Jerusalem. Ad litteram Christus oravit et prædicavit in templo Dei quod erat in Jerusalem, prout per Malachiam fuit prædictum : Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator, quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti, quem vos vultis.
paras.en: [[115:9|I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all his people|Vota mea Domino reddam in conspectu omnis populi ejus]], as has already been shown; [[115:10|in the courts of the house of the Lord, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem|in atriis domus Domini, in medio tui, Jerusalem]]. According to the letter, Christ prayed and preached in the temple of God which was in Jerusalem, as was foretold by Malachias: [[Mal 3:1|presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple|Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator, quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti, quem vos vultis]].

paras.t: Porro quum psalmus iste sit unus eorum qui a sacerdotibus ante celebrationem dici solent, tangendum est breviter, qualiter ab eis applicandus sit sensus psalmi istius ad sacrosanctum officium Missæ, Sacramentumque altaris. Dicat ergo fidelis ac devotissimus Christi sacerdos :
paras.en: Further, since this psalm is one of those which priests are accustomed to say before celebrating, we must touch briefly on how they should apply the sense of this psalm to the most holy office of the Mass and to the Sacrament of the altar. Let the faithful and most devout priest of Christ, then, say:

paras.t: Credidi, id est, firmissime tenui et tenebo ac teneo, quod in hoc Sacramento sit totus Christus, eo modo quo ipse testatur, et ipsa Ecclesia profitetur ; propter quod locutus sum confessionem meam, et sermonem ad populum, seu alia quælibet bona ad hanc fidem spectantia, meique præparatoria ad tantum officium. Ego autem humiliatus sum nimis, id est, omnino indignum me reputavi ac reputo ad accedendum Christi altare, et immolandum sacrificium tam divinum : ad quod dignus non essem, considerata dignitate Sacramenti, quamvis totius mundi virtutes ac merita possiderem.
paras.en: [[115:1|I have believed|Credidi]], that is, I have held, and shall hold, and do hold most firmly that the whole Christ is in this Sacrament, in the way that he himself testifies and the Church herself professes; [[115:1|therefore have I spoken|propter quod locutus sum]] my confession, and the sermon to the people, or any other good things that bear on this faith and prepare me for so great an office. [[115:1|But I have been humbled exceedingly|Ego autem humiliatus sum nimis]], that is, I have reckoned and do reckon myself altogether unworthy to approach the altar of Christ and to offer so divine a sacrifice: of which I should not be worthy, considering the dignity of the Sacrament, even if I possessed the virtues and merits of the whole world.

paras.t: Ego dixi in excessu meo, id est in alta consideratione eorum quæ circa hoc Sacramentum pensanda sunt : Omnis homo mendax, id est, nullus vere dignus est ipsum consecrare aut sumere, quoniam omnes fragiles sunt et caduci.
paras.en: [[115:2|I said in my excess|Ego dixi in excessu meo]], that is, in deep consideration of the things to be weighed concerning this Sacrament: [[115:2|Every man is a liar|Omnis homo mendax]], that is, no one is truly worthy to consecrate or to receive it, since all are frail and perishable.

paras.t: Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi, præsertim pro sacrosancta communione corporis et sanguinis sui ? Calicem salutaris, id est calicem Salvatoris, in quo sanguis ejus consecratur et accipiam manibus meis in altari ; et nomen Domini invocabo, orando pro me ipso ac aliis, pro vivis et mortuis, atque pro omnibus causis pro quibus Ecclesia statuit, aut mihi incumbit.
paras.en: [[115:3|What shall I render to the Lord, for all the things that he hath rendered to me|Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi]], especially for the most holy communion of his body and blood? [[115:4|The chalice of salvation|Calicem salutaris]], that is, the chalice of the Saviour [*salutaris*, "of salvation", is here taken as *Salvatoris*, "of the Saviour"], in which his blood is consecrated, and [[115:4|I will take|accipiam]] it in my hands at the altar; [[115:4|and I will call upon the name of the Lord|et nomen Domini invocabo]], praying for myself and for others, for the living and the dead, and for all the causes for which the Church has ordained it, or which fall to me.

paras.t: Vota mea, id est desideria mea, Domino reddam coram omni populo ejus, id est coram universis adstantibus, offerendo, eis præsentibus, vota et preces Deo.
paras.en: [[115:5|I will pay my vows|Vota mea]], that is, my desires, [[115:5|to the Lord before all his people|Domino reddam coram omni populo ejus]], that is, before all who stand by, offering vows and prayers to God in their presence.

paras.t: Dirupisti vincula mea, o Christe, id est, tuo pretiosissimo sanguine abstulisti peccata mea : imo quotidie rumpis vincula vitiorum meorum, per saluberrimam hostiam corporis tui et sanguinis ; tibi, o Deus Pater, seu Trinitas superbenedicta, sacrificabo hostiam laudis, offerendo ad laudem tuam corpus et sanguinem Salvatoris : per quam oblationem, laus, honor, et gloria tibi impenditur. Cetera patent.
paras.en: [[115:7|Thou hast broken my bonds|Dirupisti vincula mea]], O Christ, that is, by thy most precious blood thou hast taken away my sins; indeed, daily thou breakest the bonds of my vices by the most wholesome victim of thy body and blood. [[115:8|To thee|tibi]], O God the Father, or Trinity supremely blessed, [[115:8|I will sacrifice|sacrificabo]] [[115:8|the sacrifice of praise|hostiam laudis]], offering for thy praise the body and blood of the Saviour: through which offering praise, honour and glory are rendered to thee. The rest is plain.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum vere ineffabili laude dignum audivimus : in cujus principio fidem veram et sanctam confessionem homo devotus et martyr invictus fatetur ; deinde, respectu divinæ veritatis, ceteros omnes arbitratur mendaces ; insuper sollicitatur ne Deo inveniatur ingratus, perhibens se multa opera bona acturum ad gloriam Creatoris, ne ingratus exsistat. Cum præcipua igitur devotione decet nos psalmum tam dulcem, decorum, et sententiosum cantare, quatenus vim ejus mereamur gustare.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm truly worthy of unspeakable praise: at its beginning the devout man and unconquered martyr professes true faith and holy confession; then, in respect of the divine truth, he judges all others to be liars; moreover he is anxious not to be found ungrateful to God, declaring that he will do many good works to the glory of the Creator, lest he prove ungrateful. It befits us, therefore, to sing with special devotion a psalm so sweet, so beautiful and so full of meaning, that we may deserve to taste its power.

paras.t: Precatio. Preces populi in te credentis, Domine, suscipe, et concede nos sacrificium laudis tibi semper offerre : dirumpe peccatorum nostrorum vincula, ut tibi digne reddamus fidei christianæ vota.
paras.en: Prayer. Receive, O Lord, the prayers of the people that believes in thee, and grant us ever to offer thee the sacrifice of praise; break the bonds of our sins, that we may worthily pay thee the vows of the Christian faith.

116.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI SEXTIDECIMI : LAUDATE DOMINUM, OMNES GENTES.
116.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and sixteenth psalm: O praise the Lord, all ye nations.

paras.t: Est autem titulus psalmi præsentis, Alleluia, quia Propheta in hoc psalmo omnes gentes omnesque populos, id est homines universos, Judæos videlicet atque gentiles, invitat ad laudem Dei pro beneficio incarnationis Christi, et pro adimpletione eorum quæ prophetata erant de Christo gentiumque conversione. Et quod iste sit litteralis sensus psalmi hujus, constat ex eo quod Apostolus ad Romanos allegat scripturam psalmi istius, tanquam de gentium conversione prædictam : Dico, inquiens, Jesum Christum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis ; gentes autem super misericordia honorare Deum, sicut scriptum est, Propterea confitebor tibi in gentibus ; et iterum, Laudate, omnes gentes, Dominum, et magnificate eum, omnes populi. Christus enim est lapis angularis, in quo gentes et Judæi conjuncti sunt : unam constituens ex utrisque Ecclesiam, in qua non est distinctio Judæi et Græci. Nam, sicut ait Apostolus, In Christo Jesu neque circumcisio est aliquid, neque præputium, sed nova creatura.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is *Alleluia*, because in this psalm the Prophet invites all nations and all peoples, that is, all men, Jews namely and Gentiles, to the praise of God for the benefit of Christ's incarnation, and for the fulfilment of the things that had been prophesied of Christ and of the conversion of the Gentiles. And that this is the literal sense of this psalm is clear from the fact that the Apostle, in the Epistle to the Romans, cites the scripture of this psalm as foretold of the conversion of the Gentiles. [[Rom 15:8|For I say|Dico]], he says, [[Rom 15:8|that Christ Jesus was minister of the circumcision|Jesum Christum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis]]; [[Rom 15:9|But that the Gentiles are to glorify God for his mercy, as it is written|gentes autem super misericordia honorare Deum, sicut scriptum est]]: [[Rom 15:9|Therefore will I confess to thee, O Lord, among the Gentiles|Propterea confitebor tibi in gentibus]][[Ps 17:50||]]; [[Rom 15:11|And again: praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles: and magnify him, all ye people|et iterum, Laudate, omnes gentes, Dominum, et magnificate eum, omnes populi]]. For Christ is the corner stone[[Is 28:16||]][[Eph 2:20||]], in whom Gentiles and Jews are joined together, making of both one Church, in which [[Rom 10:12|there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek|non est distinctio Judæi et Græci]]. For, as the Apostle says, [[Gal 6:15|in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision: but a new creature|In Christo Jesu neque circumcisio est aliquid, neque præputium, sed nova creatura]][[Gal 5:6||]] [Denis reads *est aliquid*, "is anything", where the Vulgate has *aliquid valet*, "availeth any thing"].

paras.t: Quoniam vero plures de gentibus quam de Judæis ad Christum conversi sunt, idcirco Propheta hoc prævidens, primo invitat gentes, dicendo : Laudate Dominum, omnes gentes, ad fidem vocatæ. De quibus Christus ait : Oportebat Christum pati et resurgere a mortuis tertia die, et prædicari in nomine ejus pœnitentiam et remissionem peccatorum in omnes gentes. Laudate eum, omnes populi, ex judaismo conversi. Causa autem hujus invitationis annectitur.
paras.en: But since more of the Gentiles than of the Jews were converted to Christ, the Prophet, foreseeing this, first invites the Gentiles, saying: [[116:1|O Praise the Lord, all ye nations|Laudate Dominum, omnes gentes]], called to the faith; of whom Christ says: [[Luke 24:46|it behoved Christ to suffer and to rise again from the dead, the third day|Oportebat Christum pati et resurgere a mortuis tertia die]], [[Luke 24:47|And that penance and remission of sins should be preached in his name, unto all nations|et prædicari in nomine ejus pœnitentiam et remissionem peccatorum in omnes gentes]]. [[116:1|praise him, all ye people|Laudate eum, omnes populi]], converted from Judaism. Then the reason for this invitation is added.

paras.t: Quoniam confirmata est super nos misericordia ejus : id est, effectus pietatis divinæ, seu gratia Dei copiose et plenius quam ante, effusa et roborata est super totum genus humanum, videlicet super gentes et populos omnes. Quando utique, nisi in Christi adventu ? Tunc enim (sicut Joannes testatur) gratia per Christum facta est. Loquebatur ergo Propheta de futuro per modum præteriti, propter certitudinem prophetiæ. De hac confirmatione misericordiæ Dei super nos, quæ facta est in Christi adventu, non ante, dicit Apostolus : Tempora prioris ignorantiæ despiciens Deus, nunc annuntiat hominibus, ut omnes ubique pœnitentiam agant. Et veritas Domini, id est impletio divinarum promissionum mysteriorumque Christi, manet in æternum, quantum ad fructum ex ea consecutum, qui est liberatio generis humani. De hac veritate habetur apud Joannem : Veritas per Christum facta est. Ipse namque omnia de se prædicta implevit. Unde pendens in cruce, dixit : Consummatum est. Vel, Veritas Domini, id est doctrina et prædicatio Christi atque evangelicæ legis, manet in æternum, quemadmodum Christus testatur : Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt. Vel, Veritas Domini, id est Christus Filius Dei qui ait, Ego sum via, veritas et vita ; manet in æternum : quod Judæi quoque confessi sunt, dicentes ad Salvatorem, Nos audivimus ex lege, quia Christus manet in æternum.
paras.en: [[116:2|For his mercy is confirmed upon us|Quoniam confirmata est super nos misericordia ejus]]: that is, the effect of the divine goodness, or the grace of God, has been poured out abundantly, and more fully than before, and made strong upon the whole human race, namely upon all nations and peoples. When, indeed, but at the coming of Christ? For then (as John testifies) grace came by Christ[[John 1:17||]]. The Prophet therefore was speaking of the future in the manner of the past, because of the certainty of the prophecy. Of this confirming of God's mercy upon us, which was done at the coming of Christ and not before, the Apostle says: God, overlooking the times of former ignorance, [[Acts 17:30|now declareth unto men that all should every where do penance|nunc annuntiat hominibus, ut omnes ubique pœnitentiam agant]] [Denis reads *prioris ignorantiæ*, "of former ignorance", where the Vulgate has *hujus ignorantiæ*, "of this ignorance"; the words are Paul's at Athens]. [[116:2|and the truth of the Lord|Et veritas Domini]], that is, the fulfilment of the divine promises and of the mysteries of Christ, [[116:2|remaineth for ever|manet in æternum]], as to the fruit that followed from it, which is the deliverance of the human race. Of this truth we have in John: Truth came by Christ[[John 1:17||]]. For He fulfilled all that had been foretold of Him; and so, hanging on the cross, He said: [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]]. Or, *the truth of the Lord*, that is, the teaching and preaching of Christ and of the law of the Gospel, *remaineth for ever*, as Christ testifies: [[Luke 21:33|Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away|Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt]]. Or, *the truth of the Lord*, that is, Christ the Son of God, who says, [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas et vita]], *remaineth for ever*: which the Jews too confessed, saying to the Saviour, [[John 12:34|We have heard out of the law that Christ abideth for ever|Nos audivimus ex lege, quia Christus manet in æternum]].

paras.t: Psalmum hunc verbis permodicum, et sensibus plenum ac magnum, sancti doctores vehementer commendant. Continet enim summatim, quod in aliis psalmis sparsim tractatur. Denique, quid desperatis gentibus jucundius, quid miseris, cæcis et perditis dulcius dici potuit, quam quod super eas confirmata esset misericordia Dei, atque ob hoc Deum laudarent ? Cum quadam igitur flamma sanctæ devotionis pronuntietur a nobis hic psalmus.
paras.en: This psalm, very short in words but full and great in meaning, the holy doctors warmly commend; for it contains in sum what is treated here and there in the other psalms. Indeed, what more joyful thing could be said to the despairing Gentiles, what sweeter to the wretched, the blind and the lost, than that the mercy of God had been confirmed upon them, and that for this they should praise God? Let this psalm, then, be said by us with a certain flame of holy devotion.

paras.t: Precatio. Omnipotens Pater Domine, condignas majestati tuæ laudes fac nos tibi semper offerre ; confirma super nos misericordiam tuam, ne aliqua corruptela criminum inficiat animam nostram : ut Veritas tua tibi consubstantialis, nobiscum maneat in æternum.
paras.en: Prayer. Almighty Father, O Lord, make us ever offer to Thee praises worthy of Thy majesty; confirm Thy mercy upon us, that no corruption of sins may infect our soul: so that Thy Truth, consubstantial with Thee, may remain with us for ever.

117.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI SEPTIMIDECIMI : CONFITEMINI DOMINO QUONIAM BONUS.
117.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and seventeenth psalm: Give praise to the Lord, for he is good.

paras.t: Assignatur psalmo huic pro titulo, Alleluia. Invitatur enim populus electorum ad laudem divinam in hoc psalmo. Secundum Hieronymum, psalmus iste de Christi primo adventu manifeste conscriptus est, sicut in processu patebit. Quod enim inferius dicitur, Lapidem quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, etc., dixit Christus Judæis de se ipso prædictum : Nunquam, inquiens, legistis in Scripturis, Lapidem quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, hic factus est in caput anguli, etc. ? Petrus quoque loquens principibus sacerdotum de Christo, probansque eis Christi glorificationem, ait : Hic est lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus, qui factus est in caput anguli ; et non est in alio aliquo salus. Probatio autem non valet, nisi ex sensu litterali, præsertim Judæis, qui (ut fertur) non recipiunt nisi sensum litteralem.
paras.en: This psalm is given the title Alleluia. For in this psalm the people of the elect is invited to the praise of God. According to Jerome, this psalm was plainly written of the first coming of Christ, as will appear as we go on. For what is said further on, [[117:22|The stone which the builders rejected|Lapidem quem reprobaverunt ædificantes]], etc., Christ told the Jews had been foretold of himself: [[Matt 21:42|Have you never|Nunquam]], he says, [[Matt 21:42|read in the Scriptures: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?|legistis in Scripturis, Lapidem quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, hic factus est in caput anguli]] etc.? Peter too, speaking to the chief priests about Christ and proving to them Christ's glorification, says: [[Acts 4:11|This is the stone which was rejected by you the builders, which is become the head of the corner|Hic est lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus, qui factus est in caput anguli]]; [[Acts 4:12|Neither is there salvation in any other|et non est in alio aliquo salus]]. But the proof holds only from the literal sense, especially for the Jews, who (as is said) accept only the literal sense.

paras.t: Multi ergo dicunt hunc psalmum ab illo loco, Aperite mihi portas justitiæ, usque ad finem, loqui de Christo. Ceteri vero dicunt eum loqui de invitatione Judæorum ad laudem Dei, propter liberationem David a multis periculis, ita quod David usque in illum locum, loquitur in propria persona de suis periculis. Hæc autem non videntur congruere. Petrus namque in Actibus Apostolorum allegat illum versiculum, Dextera Domini exaltavit me, dextera Domini fecit virtutem, de exaltatione Christi divinitus facta : et tamen ille versiculus præcedit versum, Aperite mihi portas justitiæ. Totus ergo hic psalmus, quantum fieri potest, de Christo exponendus videtur.
paras.en: Many, then, say that this psalm speaks of Christ from the place [[117:19|Open ye to me the gates of justice|Aperite mihi portas justitiæ]] to the end. Others say that it speaks of the Jews being invited to the praise of God for the deliverance of David from many dangers, so that up to that place David speaks in his own person of his own dangers. But these views do not seem to fit. For Peter in the Acts of the Apostles cites the verse [[117:16|the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me|Dextera Domini exaltavit me]], [[117:16|the right hand of the Lord hath wrought strength|dextera Domini fecit virtutem]], of the exaltation of Christ wrought by God[[Acts 2:33||]] [Peter's words there are "Being exalted therefore by the right hand of God"]; and yet that verse comes before the verse [[117:19|Open ye to me the gates of justice|Aperite mihi portas justitiæ]]. The whole of this psalm, then, seems to be expounded of Christ, as far as can be done.

paras.t: Loquens ergo sanctus David in persona Christi sive Ecclesiæ, ait : Confitemini Domino confessione laudis, id est, Deum laudate, quoniam bonus, id est propter se ipsum, quoniam naturaliter, quomodolibet, incircumscriptibiliter et superessentialiter bonus est, in tantum ut in Marco Christus affirmet, Nemo bonus nisi unus Deus : quod apud Lucam ita disseruit, Nemo bonus nisi solus Deus. Et non solum debetis Domino confiteri quoniam bonus in se ipso, sed etiam quoniam bonus per comparationem ad vos, sicut subjungitur : quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus, id est, semper paratus est vobis misereri, et ejus misericordia æterna est, sicut et ipse, quum idem sit ei esse, et misericordem esse. Effectus quoque divinæ misericordiæ manet in sæculum, quoniam indesinenter dat gratiam saltem aliquibus in præsenti, et in omni opere Dei misericordia admiscetur : imo, Miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus. Propter quod apud Jacobum scriptum est : Superexaltat autem misericordia judicium. — Sed repugnare videtur quod ab eodem dicitur, Judicium sine misericordia ei qui non fecerit misericordiam : cui concordat illud Job, Obliviscatur ejus misericordia.
paras.en: Holy David, then, speaking in the person of Christ or of the Church, says: [[117:1|Give praise to the Lord|Confitemini Domino]] with the confession of praise, that is, praise God, [[117:1|for he is good|quoniam bonus]], that is, for his own sake, because he is good by nature, in every way, without limit and above all being, so much so that in Mark Christ affirms: [[Mark 10:18|None is good but one, that is God|Nemo bonus nisi unus Deus]]; which in Luke he put thus: [[Luke 18:19|None is good but God alone|Nemo bonus nisi solus Deus]]. And you ought to give praise to the Lord not only because he is good in himself, but also because he is good in relation to you, as is added: [[117:1|for his mercy endureth for ever|quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus]]; that is, he is always ready to have mercy on you, and his mercy is eternal, as he himself is, since for him to be and to be merciful are the same. The effect of God's mercy, too, endures for ever, since he unceasingly gives grace, at least to some, in the present, and mercy is mingled in every work of God; indeed, [[Ps 144:9|his tender mercies are over all his works|Miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlv, 9, the Hebrew numbering]. Therefore it is written in James: [[Jas 2:13|And mercy exalteth itself above judgment|Superexaltat autem misericordia judicium]]. But what the same writer says seems to conflict with this: [[Jas 2:13|judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|Judicium sine misericordia ei qui non fecerit misericordiam]]; and with this agrees that saying of Job: [[Job 24:20|Let mercy forget him|Obliviscatur ejus misericordia]].

paras.t: Et respondendum, quod in aliquibus operibus Dei, justitia præponderat, clariusque refulget, ut in damnatione æterna malorum. Idcirco dicitur eis fieri judicium sine misericordia, et quod misericordia Dei eorum non meminit : non quod omnino nulla misericordia eis impendatur, quum citra condignum patiantur ; sed quia misericordiam evidentem non consequuntur, eo quod æternaliter puniantur.
paras.en: The answer is that in some of God's works justice outweighs mercy and shines out more clearly, as in the eternal damnation of the wicked. Therefore judgment without mercy is said to be done to them, and God's mercy is said not to remember them: not that no mercy at all is bestowed on them, since they suffer less than they deserve; but because they obtain no evident mercy, in that they are punished eternally.

paras.t: Dicat nunc, id est in Christi adventu præcipue, Israel: Quoniam bonus est Deus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus : dat enim gratiam in præsenti, gloriamque æternam in futuro. Dicat nunc domus Aaron : Quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus. Ista intelligi possunt tam de populo Israelitico ex Jacob patriarcha orto, et sacerdotibus ex semine Aaron natis, quam de populo christiano, et sacerdotibus Christi per illos significatis. Populus enim christianus dicitur Israel, id est Deum fide per dilectionem operante contemplans. Domus autem seu familia Aaron, figuraliter est congregatio sacerdotum Ecclesiæ : qui sunt filii sacerdotis magni, videlicet Christi, qui est sacerdos et pontifex noster, quemadmodum Petrus in prima sua Canonica protestatur : Eratis aliquando sicut oves errantes, sed conversi estis ad pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum.
paras.en: [[117:2|Let Israel now say|Dicat nunc]], that is, chiefly at the coming of Christ, [[117:2|that he is good|Quoniam bonus]] (God, that is), [[117:2|that his mercy endureth for ever|quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus]]: for he gives grace in the present, and eternal glory in the future. [[117:3|Let the house of Aaron now say|Dicat nunc domus Aaron]], [[117:3|that his mercy endureth for ever|Quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus]]. These words can be understood both of the people of Israel sprung from the patriarch Jacob and of the priests born of the seed of Aaron, and of the Christian people and of the priests of Christ, whom those signified. For the Christian people is called Israel, that is, one who beholds God by faith that worketh through charity [Israel was commonly taken to mean "seeing God"]. And the house or family of Aaron is, figuratively, the congregation of the priests of the Church, who are the sons of the great priest, namely Christ, who is our priest and pontiff, as Peter declares in his first canonical epistle: [[1 Pet 2:25|you were as sheep going astray: but you are now converted to the shepherd and bishop of your souls|Eratis aliquando sicut oves errantes, sed conversi estis ad pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum]].

paras.t: Dicant nunc qui timent Dominum timore sancto et filiali : Quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus : sicut etiam ait Virgo beata, Et misericordia ejus a progenie in progenies timentibus eum. Unde in Exodo Dominus ait : Ego sum Dominus Deus, faciens misericordiam in millia, his qui diligunt me, et custodiunt præcepta mea.
paras.en: [[117:4|Let them that fear the Lord now say|Dicant nunc qui timent Dominum]], with a holy and filial fear, [[117:4|that his mercy endureth for ever|Quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus]]: as the blessed Virgin also says: [[Luke 1:50|And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him|Et misericordia ejus a progenie in progenies timentibus eum]]. Hence the Lord says in Exodus: I am the Lord God, [[Ex 20:6|shewing mercy unto thousands to them that love me, and keep my commandments|faciens misericordiam in millia, his qui diligunt me, et custodiunt præcepta mea]].

paras.t: Deinde Christus de se ipso testatur : De tribulatione invocavi Dominum. Hoc est quod nunc ex verbis Apostoli commemoratum est, quia Christus passione instante cum clamore valido et lacrimis preces fecit ad Deum. Propter quod Lucas dicit, quod factus in agonia, prolixius orabat. Et exaudivit me in latitudine suæ dilectionis et pietatis, Dominus Pater omnipotens. Ideo Apostolus addidit, quod exauditus est pro sua reverentia. Et ipse ait ad Patrem : Gratias ago tibi, Pater, quoniam audisti me ; ego autem sciebam quoniam semper me audis.
paras.en: Then Christ testifies of himself: [[117:5|In my trouble I called upon the Lord|De tribulatione invocavi Dominum]]. This is what has now been recalled from the words of the Apostle: that Christ, when his passion was at hand, offered prayers to God with a strong cry and tears[[Heb 5:7||]]. Therefore Luke says that [[Luke 22:43|being in an agony, he prayed the longer|factus in agonia, prolixius orabat]]. [[117:5|and the Lord heard me|Et exaudivit me]], [[117:5|and enlarged me|in latitudine]] [literally "in breadth"], in the breadth of his love and kindness, the Lord the Father almighty. Therefore the Apostle added that he [[Heb 5:7|was heard for his reverence|exauditus est pro sua reverentia]]. And he himself says to the Father: [[John 11:41|Father, I give thee thanks that thou hast heard me|Gratias ago tibi, Pater, quoniam audisti me]]; [[John 11:42|And I knew that thou hearest me always|ego autem sciebam quoniam semper me audis]].

paras.t: Dominus mihi, secundum quod homo sum, adjutor fuit et est, cooperando mihi, et protegendo me semper dum eram in via, quemadmodum apud Jeremiam ait de me sermo divinus : Dominus mecum est tanquam bellator fortis. Idcirco non timebo timore inordinato, quid faciat mihi homo perversus, quicumque sit ille : juxta quod in Isaia scriptum est de me : Quis est adversarius meus ? Accedat ad me. Dominus mihi adjutor : quemadmodum idem Isaias ait : Dominus Deus auxiliator meus ; et ego despiciam inimicos meos me persequentes, non despiciendo eorum naturam, sed malitiam, ita quod eorum malignitatem non formidabo, nec eos aliquid esse reputabo, in quantum iniqui sunt.
paras.en: [[117:6|The Lord is my|Dominus mihi]], as I am man, [[117:6|helper|adjutor]]: he was and is, working with me and protecting me always while I was on the way [in via: in this life, as a wayfarer], as the divine word says of me in Jeremias: [[Jer 20:11|the Lord is with me as a strong warrior|Dominus mecum est tanquam bellator fortis]]. Therefore [[117:6|I will not fear|non timebo]] with an inordinate fear [[117:6|what man can do unto me|quid faciat mihi homo]], a perverse man, whoever he be; as it is written of me in Isaias: [[Is 50:8|who is my adversary? let him come near to me|Quis est adversarius meus ? Accedat ad me]]. [[117:7|The Lord is my helper|Dominus mihi adjutor]], as the same Isaias says: [[Is 50:9|the Lord God is my helper|Dominus Deus auxiliator meus]]; [[117:7|and I will look over my enemies|et ego despiciam inimicos meos]] [despiciam, "look over" in the Douay-Rheims, also means "look down on, despise", and Denis takes it so] who persecute me, despising not their nature but their malice, so that I shall not dread their malignity, nor reckon them to be anything, inasmuch as they are wicked.

paras.t: Præterea quilibet Christianus de se ipso hæc dicere potest. Debemus enim de tribulatione clamare ad Dominum, sicut superius dictum est : Invoca me in die tribulationis. Et tunc utique si perseveranter clamemus, exaudiet nos Deus noster in latitudine, id est late et copiose : prout ipse pius et bonus est, et nostra merita exigunt. Quis enim invocavit eum, et despexit illum ? Cuilibet quoque fideli adjutor est Dominus, quia non sumus sufficientes aliquid cogitare ex nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Ideo non timet veraciter Christianus, quid faciat sibi homo perversus : imo in adversis lætatur, et propter amorem Christi præmiique cœlestis paratus est mori, quoniam scriptum est : Nolite timere opprobrium hominum ; et blasphemias eorum ne metuatis. Quis tu ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis, qui quasi fœnum arescit ? Propterea Salomon protestatur : Qui timet hominem, cito corruet ; qui autem sperat in Domino, sublevabitur. Dominus mihi adjutor, per gratiam suam in prosperis atque adversis conservans me ; et ego despiciam inimicos meos, visibiles et invisibiles, confidendo in adjutorio Dei, non innitendo viribus meis. Certus sum enim, quod mihi Domino adhærenti nocere non poterunt.
paras.en: Moreover, any Christian can say these things of himself. For we ought to cry to the Lord out of trouble, as was said above: [[Ps 49:15|call upon me in the day of trouble|Invoca me in die tribulationis]]. And then, surely, if we cry perseveringly, our God will hear us "in breadth" [in latitudine, the "enlarged me" of the Douay-Rheims], that is, broadly and abundantly, as he himself is kind and good, and as our merits require. For [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath called upon him, and he despised him|Quis enim invocavit eum, et despexit illum]]? To every believer, too, the Lord is a helper, because we are not [[2 Cor 3:5|sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God|sufficientes aliquid cogitare ex nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]. Therefore a Christian truly does not fear what a perverse man can do to him: rather, he rejoices in adversity, and for love of Christ and of the heavenly reward he is ready to die, since it is written: [[Is 51:7|fear ye not the reproach of men, and be not afraid of their blasphemies|Nolite timere opprobrium hominum ; et blasphemias eorum ne metuatis]]. [[Is 51:12|who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a mortal man, and of the son of man, who shall wither away like grass?|Quis tu ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis, qui quasi fœnum arescit]] Therefore Solomon declares: [[Prov 29:25|He that feareth man shall quickly fall: he that trusteth in the Lord, shall be set on high|Qui timet hominem, cito corruet ; qui autem sperat in Domino, sublevabitur]]. [[117:7|The Lord is my helper|Dominus mihi adjutor]], keeping me by his grace in prosperity and adversity; [[117:7|and I will look over my enemies|et ego despiciam inimicos meos]], visible and invisible, trusting in the help of God, not leaning on my own strength. For I am certain that they will not be able to harm me while I cleave to the Lord.

paras.t: Ex quo sequitur, quod Bonum, id est melius, est confidere in Domino, quam confidere in homine. Nam benedictus homo qui confidit in Domino; maledictus vero qui confidit in homine, et ponit carnem brachium suum, et a Domino recedit cor ejus. Bonum, id est melius, est sperare in Domino, qui solus potest salvare, quam sperare in principibus, qui neque se ipsos, nec alios valent salvare.
paras.en: From this it follows that [[117:8|It is good|Bonum]], that is, better, [[117:8|to confide in the Lord, rather than to have confidence in man|est confidere in Domino, quam confidere in homine]]. For [[Jer 17:7|Blessed be the man that trusteth in the Lord|benedictus homo qui confidit in Domino]]; but [[Jer 17:5|Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord|maledictus vero qui confidit in homine, et ponit carnem brachium suum, et a Domino recedit cor ejus]]. [[117:9|It is good|Bonum]], that is, better, [[117:9|to trust in the Lord|est sperare in Domino]], who alone can save, [[117:9|rather than to trust in princes|quam sperare in principibus]], who can save neither themselves nor others.

paras.t: Insuper Christus ait : Omnes gentes, id est aliqui de omni genere hominum, scilicet viri et mulieres, superiores et subditi, antiqui et juniores, Judæi atque gentiles, circumierunt me, tempore passionis, consentientes in mortem meam. Nec mirum si propter hos Christus universaliter dicat, Omnes gentes, quum Lucas scripserit : Erant autem in Jerusalem habitantes viri religiosi, ex omni natione quæ sub cœlo est. Et alibi legitur : Exclamans universus populus, dixit, Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros. Ecce qualiter omnes gentes circumierunt Christum in malo. Interdum quoque omnes gentes circumierunt eum in bono, eo modo quo Pharisæi et principes Judæorum dixerunt: Videtis quia nihil proficimus? Ecce totus mundus post eum abiit. Et in nomine Domini, id est ad gloriam Dei, factum sit istud, quia ultus sum in eos ex zelo justitiæ, non ex impatientia aliqua. Unde Christus loquitur : Dies ultionis in corde meo. Ultus quippe est Christus in Judæos, excæcando cor eorum, auferendo eis gratiam in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro, tradendo etiam eos in manus Romanorum, atque in hac captivitate gravissima eos tenendo, in qua jam ultra mille et trecentos annos fuerunt. Hanc ultionem fecit Christus ut Deus, sed ut homo oravit pro ea, apud Jeremiam dicens : Tu autem, Domine Sabaoth, qui judicas juste, et probas corda et renes, videam ultionem tuam ex eis; tibi enim revelavi causam meam.
paras.en: Further, Christ says: [[117:10|All nations|Omnes gentes]], that is, some of every kind of men, namely men and women, superiors and subjects, old and young, Jews and Gentiles, [[117:10|compassed me about|circumierunt me]] at the time of the passion, consenting to my death. Nor is it surprising if on their account Christ says universally "All nations", since Luke wrote: [[Acts 2:5|Now there were dwelling at Jerusalem, Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven|Erant autem in Jerusalem habitantes viri religiosi, ex omni natione quæ sub cœlo est]]. And elsewhere we read: [[Matt 27:25|And the whole people answering, said|Exclamans universus populus, dixit]] [Denis has exclamans, "crying out", where the Gospel has "answering"], [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]]. See how all nations compassed Christ about for evil. Sometimes, too, all nations compassed him about for good, in the way in which the Pharisees and chief men of the Jews said: [[John 12:19|Do you see that we prevail nothing? Behold, the whole world is gone after him|Videtis quia nihil proficimus? Ecce totus mundus post eum abiit]] [the margin gives John xi, 19; the words are John 12:19]. [[117:10|and, in the name of the Lord|Et in nomine Domini]], that is, to the glory of God, let this be done, [[117:10|I have been revenged on them|quia ultus sum in eos]] out of zeal for justice, not out of any impatience.
