Hence Christ says: [[Is 63:4|the day of vengeance is in my heart|Dies ultionis in corde meo]]. For Christ took vengeance on the Jews by blinding their heart, by taking away from them grace in the present and glory in the future, and also by delivering them into the hands of the Romans and holding them in this most grievous captivity, in which they have now been for more than thirteen hundred years. This vengeance Christ wrought as God, but as man he prayed for it, saying in Jeremias: [[Jer 11:20|But thou, O Lord of Sabaoth, who judgest justly, and triest the reins and the hearts, let me see thy revenge on them: for to thee have I revealed my cause|Tu autem, Domine Sabaoth, qui judicas juste, et probas corda et renes, videam ultionem tuam ex eis; tibi enim revelavi causam meam]].

paras.t: Circumdantes circumdederunt me, id est, cum magno malignitatis affectu ambierunt me, coram Pilato clamantes : Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum. Et in nomine Domini, quia ultus sum in eos. Istud in versu præcedenti exponitur et in versu sequenti repetitur, et est sensus idem. Terque ponuntur hæc verba, ad designandum magnitudinem zeli justitiæ, quem habuit Christus, qui semper erat divinæ justitiæ unitus et conformatus.
paras.en: [[117:11|Surrounding me they compassed me about|Circumdantes circumdederunt me]], that is, they beset me with a great disposition of malice, crying out before Pilate: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]. [[117:11|and in the name of the Lord I have been revenged on them|Et in nomine Domini, quia ultus sum in eos]]. This is expounded in the preceding verse and repeated in the following one, and the sense is the same. And these words are set down three times to show the greatness of the zeal for justice that Christ had, who was always united and conformed to the divine justice.

paras.t: Circumdederunt me sicut apes, quæ pungunt aculeo : sic Judæi verbis et ictibus me pungebant, dicendo contra me verba blasphemiæ plena. Unde et scriptum est : Videbunt in quem compunxerunt. Et exarserunt sicut ignis in spinis, etc., id est, igne furoris et vehementissima iracundiæ flamma accensi sunt contra me, sicut in spinis ignis accenditur. Quapropter ex eorum persona scriptum est : Circumveniamus virum justum, quoniam contrarius est operibus nostris; gravis est nobis etiam ad videndum.
paras.en: [[117:12|They surrounded me like bees|Circumdederunt me sicut apes]], which sting with their sting: so the Jews stung me with words and blows, speaking words full of blasphemy against me. Hence also it is written: [[John 19:37|They shall look on him whom they pierced|Videbunt in quem compunxerunt]][[Zach 12:10||]][[Apoc 1:7||]] [Denis's compunxerunt, "pricked", fits the bees' sting]. [[117:12|and they burned like fire among thorns|Et exarserunt sicut ignis in spinis]], etc., that is, they were kindled against me with the fire of fury and the most vehement flame of wrath, as fire is kindled among thorns. Therefore it is written in their person: Let us [[Wis 2:12|lie in wait for the just|Circumveniamus virum justum]], because [[Wis 2:12|he is contrary to our doings|contrarius est operibus nostris]]; [[Wis 2:15|He is grievous unto us, even to behold|gravis est nobis etiam ad videndum]].

paras.t: Impulsus, id est a Judæis captus, et usque ad locum Calvariæ crucem bajulans ductus, eversus sum a vita corporali, ut caderem, id est, omnino mortuus remanerem, nec amplius memoria esset nominis mei in terra, prout scriptum est : Dicunt adversarii de me, Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra. Et Dominus suscepit me : id est, ab ista ruina præservavit me; imo ejus oppositum fecit, quoniam ipsi penitus perierunt, et ego resuscitatus sum, et ubique glorificatus. Propter quod ait Pater de me : Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum. Potest etiam istud intelligi de impulsione illa Christi, de qua in Luca dicitur : Duxerunt eum ad supercilium montis, ut præcipitarent eum; ipse autem transiens per medium illorum, ibat.
paras.en: [[117:13|Being pushed|Impulsus]], that is, seized by the Jews and led, carrying the cross, to the place of Calvary[[John 19:17||]], [[117:13|I was overturned|eversus sum]] from bodily life, [[117:13|that I might fall|ut caderem]], that is, that I might remain wholly dead, and the memory of my name be no more on earth, as it is written: My adversaries say of me: Let us [[Jer 11:19|cut him off from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more|Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra]]. [[117:13|but the Lord supported me|Et Dominus suscepit me]]: that is, he preserved me from that ruin; indeed he did the opposite of it, since they utterly perished, while I was raised up and glorified everywhere. Therefore the Father says of me: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum]] [suscipiam is the verb of the psalm's suscepit, "supported"]. This can also be understood of that thrusting of Christ of which Luke says: [[Luke 4:29|they brought him to the brow of the hill|Duxerunt eum ad supercilium montis]], [[Luke 4:29|that they might cast him down headlong|ut præcipitarent eum]]; [[Luke 4:30|But he passing through the midst of them, went his way|ipse autem transiens per medium illorum, ibat]].

paras.t: Quoniam ergo Dominus ita suscepit me, ideo Fortitudo mea, id est causa totius fortitudinis meæ creatæ, et laus mea, id est quem laudo, videlicet res laudata a me, est Dominus Pater seu Deus Trinitas. Hinc enim ait Salvator : Non potest Filius a se facere quidquam ; et alibi, Ego non quæro gloriam meam, sed honorifico Patrem meum. Et factus est mihi in salutem, id est in causam totius salutis animæ meæ et corporis, quia ab eo est glorificatio mea in mente et corpore.
paras.en: Since, then, the Lord has so supported me, therefore [[117:14|my strength|Fortitudo mea]], that is, the cause of all my created strength, [[117:14|and my praise|et laus mea]], that is, he whom I praise, namely the one praised by me, is [[117:14|The Lord|Dominus]], the Father, or God the Trinity. For hence the Saviour says: [[John 5:19|the Son cannot do any thing of himself|Non potest Filius a se facere quidquam]]; and elsewhere: [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]], [[John 8:49|but I honour my Father|sed honorifico Patrem meum]]. [[117:14|and he is become my salvation|Et factus est mihi in salutem]], that is, the cause of all the salvation of my soul and body, since from him comes my glorification in mind and body.

paras.t: Vox exsultationis, id est laudatio spiritualis lætitiæ, et salutis, id est laudatio beata et salutaris, videlicet laus jucunda atque salubris, atque ex interiori jucunditate ac salute procedens, est in tabernaculis justorum, id est in patria Beatorum, in cordibus electorum, in Ecclesiis Christifidelium : juxta illud, Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea, gratiarum actio et vox laudis. Unde supra dictum est : Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine ; in sæcula sæculorum laudabunt te.
paras.en: [[117:15|The voice of rejoicing|Vox exsultationis]], that is, the praise of spiritual gladness, [[117:15|and of salvation|et salutis]], that is, blessed and saving praise, namely joyful and wholesome praise, proceeding from inward joy and salvation, [[117:15|is in the tabernacles of the just|in tabernaculis justorum]], that is, in the fatherland of the Blessed, in the hearts of the elect, in the churches of Christ's faithful: according to that saying: [[Is 51:3|Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of praise|Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea, gratiarum actio et vox laudis]] [the margin gives Is. lii, 3; the words are Is 51:3]. Hence it was said above: [[Ps 83:5|Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: they shall praise thee for ever and ever|Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine ; in sæcula sæculorum laudabunt te]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxviii, 5; the words are Ps 83:5].

paras.t: Dextera Domini, id est pia et gratiosa adsistentia seu magna potentia Patris æterni, fecit virtutem in me, conservando me tempore passionis, et faciendo mirabilia quæ tunc fiebant in sole et luna, in terra et templo, cujus scissum est velum ; me quoque ac alios multos resuscitando tertia die a mortuis : sicut habetur apud Matthæum. Dextera Domini exaltavit me in die ascensionis super omnes cœlos ; exaltavit etiam me, clarificando me in toto mundo per doctrinam et signa Apostolorum, sicut rogavi passione instante : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum. De hac enim exaltatione prædixit Deus : Ecce intelliget servus meus, et exaltabitur et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde. Dextera Domini fecit virtutem in corpore meo mystico, quod est Ecclesia, mittendo ei in die Pentecostes Spiritum Sanctum, dansque gratiam miraculorum discipulis meis. Unde legitur : Virtutes non modicas faciebat Deus per manus Pauli.
paras.en: [[117:16|The right hand of the Lord|Dextera Domini]], that is, the kind and gracious assistance, or the great power, of the eternal Father, [[117:16|hath wrought strength|fecit virtutem]] in me, preserving me at the time of the passion, and working the wonders that were done then in the sun and moon[[Matt 27:45||]], in the earth and in the temple, whose veil was rent[[Matt 27:51||]]; raising me too, and many others, from the dead on the third day[[Matt 27:52||]][[Matt 27:53||]][[Matt 28:6||]], as is found in Matthew. [[117:16|the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me|Dextera Domini exaltavit me]] on the day of the ascension above all the heavens; it exalted me also by glorifying me in all the world through the teaching and signs of the Apostles, as I prayed when the passion was at hand: Father, [[John 17:1|the hour is come. Glorify thy Son|venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]]. For of this exaltation God foretold: [[Is 52:13|Behold my servant shall understand, he shall be exalted, and extolled, and shall be exceeding high|Ecce intelliget servus meus, et exaltabitur et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde]]. [[117:16|the right hand of the Lord hath wrought strength|Dextera Domini fecit virtutem]] in my mystical body, which is the Church, by sending it the Holy Ghost on the day of Pentecost, and giving the grace of miracles to my disciples. Hence we read: [[Acts 19:11|God wrought by the hand of Paul more than common miracles|Virtutes non modicas faciebat Deus per manus Pauli]].

paras.t: Non moriar eo modo sicut vos, o Judæi, putastis, quia nec spiritualiter moriar, quasi blasphemus et impius, neque imperio corporalis mortis subjiciar : quin imo mox ad immortalem vitam resurgam, sicut in Evangelio sæpe prædixi. Ideo sequitur : sed vivam, factus impassibilis, et narrabo opera Domini. Nam, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum et in omnibus Evangelistis narratur, Christus post passionem et resurrectionem discipulis suis frequenter apparuit per dies quadraginta, intrans et exiens atque manducans cum eis, et disputans de regno Dei. Tunc ergo narravit eis opera Domini, scilicet suam resurrectionem, futurum judicium, et vaticinia Prophetarum, multaque alia quæ scripta non sunt, quia, ut dicitur in Evangelio Joannis, Multa alia fecit Jesus, quæ si scribantur per singula, nec ipsum arbitror mundum capere posse eos qui scribendi sunt, libros.
paras.en: [[117:17|I shall not die|Non moriar]] in the way that you, O Jews, thought, for I shall neither die spiritually, as a blasphemer and an impious man, nor be made subject to the dominion of bodily death; but rather I shall soon rise again to immortal life, as I often foretold in the Gospel. Therefore there follows: [[117:17|but live|sed vivam]], made impassible [that is, no longer able to suffer], [[117:17|and shall declare the works of the Lord|et narrabo opera Domini]]. For, as is told in the Acts of the Apostles and in all the Evangelists[[Acts 1:3||]][[Matt 28:17||]][[Matt 28:18||]][[Mark 16:9||]][[Luke 24:1||]][[John 20:1||]][[John 21:1||]] [the margin gives Mark xvi, 9 and following, and Luke xxiv, John xx and xxi as whole chapters], Christ after his passion and resurrection often appeared to his disciples for forty days, going in and out and eating with them, and discoursing of the kingdom of God. Then, therefore, he declared to them the works of the Lord, namely his resurrection, the judgment to come, and the prophecies of the Prophets, and many other things that are not written; for, as is said in the Gospel of John: [[John 21:25|many other things which Jesus did which, if they were written every one, the world itself. I think, would not be able to contain the books that should be written|Multa alia fecit Jesus, quæ si scribantur per singula, nec ipsum arbitror mundum capere posse eos qui scribendi sunt, libros]].

paras.t: Castigans castigavit me Dominus, non propter proprias culpas, sed propter delicta eorum, pro quibus mori me voluit : sicut scriptum est : Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum ; ipse autem vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra. Et alibi : Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris. Et morti non tradidit me, ita quod mortis imperio subjacerem, sed statim ad vitam corporalem reduxit me, sicut supra dictum est : Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno, nec dabis Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem.
paras.en: [[117:18|The Lord chastising hath chastised me|Castigans castigavit me Dominus]], not for my own faults, but for the sins of those for whom he willed me to die; as it is written: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]; [[Is 53:5|he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins|ipse autem vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra]]. And elsewhere: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins|Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris]]. [[117:18|but he hath not delivered me over to death|Et morti non tradidit me]], so that I should lie under the dominion of death, but at once he brought me back to bodily life, as was said above: [[Ps 15:10|Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption|Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno, nec dabis Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem]].

paras.t: Aperite mihi portas justitiæ. Hæc sunt verba Christi ascendentis ad cœlos, imperantis angelis sanctis : Aperite mihi ascendenti et venientibus mecum, portas justitiæ, id est aditus regni cœlestis. Has portas angeli sancti aperire dicuntur propter duplicem causam. Prima est, quoniam tollunt impedimenta ingrediendi regnum cœleste, per hoc quod ad eorum officium spectat aerias potestates coercere, quæ semper nituntur ascendentes impedire ; secunda, per hoc quod se ipsos disponunt ad recipiendum devote ascendentes ad societatem angelicam. Et ita nunc Christus jubet ut se ipsos disponant ad occurrendum sibi reverenter, et ut eum cum debita servitute, laude ac veneratione, introducant in regnum suum cœleste. Ingressus in eas, videlicet portas ac mansiones regni cœlestis, confitebor Domino confessione laudationis perfectæ. Christus enim sedens ad dexteram Patris, incessabiliter Dominum laudat per se ipsum, secundum quod homo est, et per alios, quos ad hoc induxit.
paras.en: [[117:19|Open ye to me the gates of justice|Aperite mihi portas justitiæ]]. These are the words of Christ ascending to heaven and commanding the holy angels: [[117:19|Open ye to me|Aperite mihi]] as I ascend, and to those coming with me, [[117:19|the gates of justice|portas justitiæ]], that is, the entrances of the heavenly kingdom. The holy angels are said to open these gates for a twofold reason. The first is that they remove the hindrances to entering the heavenly kingdom, in that it belongs to their office to restrain the powers of the air, which always strive to hinder those who ascend; the second, in that they dispose themselves to receive devoutly into the company of the angels those who ascend. And so Christ now commands them to dispose themselves to meet him reverently, and to bring him with due service, praise and veneration into their heavenly kingdom. [[117:19|I will go in to them|Ingressus in eas]], namely the gates and mansions of the heavenly kingdom, [[117:19|and give praise to the Lord|confitebor Domino]] with the confession of perfect praise. For Christ, sitting at the right hand of the Father, unceasingly praises the Lord by himself, according as he is man, and through others, whom he has led to do so.

paras.t: Hæc porta Domini, justi intrabunt in eam. Ante dixit pluraliter, Portas ; nunc singulariter ait, Hæc porta: quoniam quamvis tot sint portæ justitiæ quot virtutes, nulla tamen portarum introducere potest, nisi per caritatem ; et ideo caritas porta est, virtualiter omnes portas comprehendens. Justi intrabunt in eam, quemadmodum monet Apostolus : Ambulate in dilectione, sicut et Christus dilexit nos.
paras.en: [[117:20|This is the gate of the Lord|Hæc porta Domini]], [[117:20|the just shall enter into it|justi intrabunt in eam]]. Before, he said in the plural, "gates"; now he says in the singular, "This is the gate": because, though there are as many gates of justice as there are virtues, yet none of the gates can lead in except through charity; and therefore charity is the gate, containing all the gates virtually [that is, in its power, as a cause contains its effects]. [[117:20|the just shall enter into it|Justi intrabunt in eam]], as the Apostle admonishes: [[Eph 5:2|walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us|Ambulate in dilectione, sicut et Christus dilexit nos]].

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, id est, laudabo te, Domine Pater, quoniam exaudisti me, et factus es mihi in salutem: sicut nunc dictum est.
paras.en: [[117:21|I will give glory to thee|Confitebor tibi]], that is, I will praise thee, O Lord Father, [[117:21|because thou hast heard me: and art become my salvation|quoniam exaudisti me, et factus es mihi in salutem]]: as has just been said.

paras.t: Præterea ista jam de Christo exposita, exponi etiam possunt de Ecclesia seu fideli, quorum est sequi vestigia Christi. Omnes gentes circumierunt me: id est, aliqui de omni genere hominum persecuti sunt me, vel blandimentis aut minis me tentaverunt, et fallere nisi sunt. Unde et Christus loquitur: Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur, quia non est servus major domino suo; et alibi, Odio eritis omnibus hominibus propter me. Et in nomine Domini, quia ultus sum in eos, secundum ordinem justitiæ. Vel, Ultus sum in eos, a Domino, qui ait: Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam. De quo in Deuteronomio inducitur: Quia sanguinem servorum suorum ulciscetur, et vindictam retribuet in hostes eorum. Circumdantes circumdederunt me, quatenus suis peccatis animam meam inficiant et occidant. Circumdederunt me sicut apes, quæ gerunt mel in ore, aculeum vero in cauda. Sic isti blandiuntur ut fallant, quemadmodum scriptum est: Sagitta vulnerans lingua eorum. In ore suo pacem cum amico suo loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias. Et exarserunt igne libidinis, flamma rancoris, fervore iræ fumantis, quatenus me aliquo modo subvertant, sicut exardescere solet ignis materialis in spinis siccis, quæ facillime inflammantur.
paras.en: Moreover, these things, which have now been expounded of Christ, can also be expounded of the Church or of the faithful soul, whose part it is to follow in the footsteps of Christ. [[117:10|All nations compassed me about|Omnes gentes circumierunt me]]: that is, some out of every kind of men have persecuted me, or have tempted me with flatteries or threats, and have striven to deceive me. Hence Christ too says: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]], because [[John 15:20|The servant is not greater than his master|non est servus major domino suo]]; and elsewhere: [[Matt 10:22|you shall be hated by all men|Odio eritis omnibus hominibus]] for my sake. [[117:10|and, in the name of the Lord I have been revenged on them|Et in nomine Domini, quia ultus sum in eos]], according to the order of justice. Or: [[117:10|I have been revenged on them|Ultus sum in eos]] by the Lord, who says: [[Heb 10:30|Vengeance belongeth to me, and I will repay|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam]]. Of whom it is said in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:43|for he will revenge the blood of his servants: and will render vengeance to their enemies|Quia sanguinem servorum suorum ulciscetur, et vindictam retribuet in hostes eorum]]. [[117:11|Surrounding me they compassed me about|Circumdantes circumdederunt me]], so as to infect and slay my soul with their sins. [[117:12|They surrounded me like bees|Circumdederunt me sicut apes]], which carry honey in their mouth but a sting in their tail. So these men flatter that they may deceive, as it is written: [[Jer 9:8|Their tongue is a piercing arrow|Sagitta vulnerans lingua eorum]]... [[Jer 9:8|with his mouth one speaketh peace with his friend, and secretly he lieth in wait for him|In ore suo pacem cum amico suo loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias]]. [[117:12|and they burned|Et exarserunt]] with the fire of lust, the flame of rancour, the heat of smouldering anger, so as somehow to overthrow me, as material fire is wont to blaze up [[117:12|among thorns|in spinis]] that are dry, which very easily catch fire.

paras.t: Impulsus tentatione seu persecutione, eversus sum a rectitudine perfectionis, ut caderem, id est, omnino deficerem, peccato mortali consentiendo, aut perseverando in malo; et Dominus suscepit me in ulnis misericordiæ suæ, non sinens me tentari ultra vires, sed faciens cum tentatione proventum. Quamvis enim Deus sanctus et benedictus, cujus judicia prorsus imperscrutabilia sunt, permittat interdum electos suos graviter tribulari, dire impelli, venialiter peccare, aut etiam mortaliter, non tamen sinit eos penitus cadere. Unde dictum est supra: Quum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam. Et apud Michæam: Ne læteris, inimica mea, super me, quia cecidi: consurgam. Quum sedero in tenebris, Dominus lux mea est.
paras.en: [[117:13|Being pushed|Impulsus]] by temptation or persecution, [[117:13|I was overturned|eversus sum]] from the uprightness of perfection, [[117:13|that I might fall|ut caderem]], that is, might fail altogether, by consenting to mortal sin or by persevering in evil; [[117:13|but the Lord supported me|et Dominus suscepit me]] in the arms of his mercy, not suffering me to be tempted beyond my strength, but making with temptation issue[[1 Cor 10:13||]]. For although the holy and blessed God, whose judgments are altogether unsearchable, sometimes permits his elect to be grievously troubled, fiercely pushed, to sin venially or even mortally, yet he does not suffer them to fall utterly. Hence it was said above: [[Ps 36:24|When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, for the Lord putteth his hand under him|Quum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam]]. And in Micheas: [[Mich 7:8|Rejoice not, thou my enemy, over me, because I am fallen: I shall arise|Ne læteris, inimica mea, super me, quia cecidi: consurgam]]. [[Mich 7:8|when I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light|Quum sedero in tenebris, Dominus lux mea est]].

paras.t: Quod ergo tentationi resistimus, quod a peccato resurgimus, quod non penitus disperimus, non nisi Domino adscribamus, dicentes corde sincero quod sequitur: Fortitudo mea, id est causa et dator totius firmitatis meæ atque victoriæ, et laus mea, est Dominus, cui in omnibus gratias ago, omneque bonum adscribo. Unde scriptum est: Dominus fortitudo mea et refugium meum, et robur meum in die tribulationis. Et factus est mihi in salutem, id est, salvator effectus est mihi, dando mihi constantiam in adversis, et humilitatem in prosperis. Propter quod Moyses dicit: Ne dicas in corde tuo, Fortitudo mea et robur manus meæ hæc omnia præstiterunt mihi; sed recordare Domini Dei tui, quod ipse vires tibi præbuerit. Quicumque hoc modo totam spem suam ponit in Deo, eum appellans fortitudinem suam et laudem, illi fit Deus in salutem.
paras.en: That we resist temptation, then, that we rise again from sin, that we do not perish utterly, let us ascribe to none but the Lord, saying with a sincere heart what follows: [[117:14|my strength|Fortitudo mea]], that is, the cause and giver of all my firmness and victory, [[117:14|and my praise|et laus mea]], is [[117:14|The Lord|Dominus]], to whom I give thanks in all things, and to whom I ascribe every good. Hence it is written: [[Jer 16:19|O Lord, my might, and my strength, and my refuge in the day of tribulation|Dominus fortitudo mea et refugium meum, et robur meum in die tribulationis]]. [[117:14|and he is become my salvation|Et factus est mihi in salutem]], that is, he has been made my saviour, by giving me constancy in adversity and humility in prosperity. For this reason Moses says: [[Deut 8:17|Lest thou shouldst say in thy heart: My own might, and the strength of my own hand have achieved all these things for me|Ne dicas in corde tuo, Fortitudo mea et robur manus meæ hæc omnia præstiterunt mihi]]; [[Deut 8:18|But remember the Lord thy God, that he hath given thee strength|sed recordare Domini Dei tui, quod ipse vires tibi præbuerit]]. Whoever in this way puts all his hope in God, calling him his strength and his praise, for him God is become salvation.

paras.t: Dextera Domini, id est Christus Filius Dei: qui dicitur brachium, dextera et virtus Dei Patris, sicut de eo scriptum est: Brachium Domini cui revelatum est? Et rursum clarius dicitur: Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium. Cui concordat quod Simeon cecinit: Viderunt oculi mei salutare tuum, quod parasti ante faciem omnium populorum. Vel, Dextera, id est potentia, Domini fecit virtutem, faciendo de impio justum: quod est majus quam creatio hominis. Dextera Domini exaltavit me de vita ignobili, vitiosa, carnali, ad vitam nobilem, virtuosam, spiritualem ac humilem; dextera Domini fecit virtutem, conservando me in bono, et pugnando ac expugnando pro me adversarios meos. Huic consonat quod in Exodo legitur: Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine; dextera tua, Domine, percussit inimicum; et in multitudine gloriæ tuæ deposuisti adversarios meos.
paras.en: [[117:16|The right hand of the Lord|Dextera Domini]], that is, Christ the Son of God, who is called the arm, the right hand and the power of God the Father, as it is written of him: [[Is 53:1|to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?|Brachium Domini cui revelatum est?]] And again it is said more clearly: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles|Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium]] [the margin gives Is. liii, 10; the words are Is 52:10]. With this agrees what Simeon sang: [[Luke 2:30|my eyes have seen thy salvation|Viderunt oculi mei salutare tuum]], [[Luke 2:31|Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples|quod parasti ante faciem omnium populorum]]. Or: [[117:16|The right hand|Dextera]], that is, the power, [[117:16|of the Lord hath wrought strength|Domini fecit virtutem]] by making a just man out of an ungodly one, which is a greater thing than the creation of man. [[117:16|the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me|Dextera Domini exaltavit me]] from a life ignoble, vicious and carnal to a life noble, virtuous, spiritual and humble; [[117:16|the right hand of the Lord hath wrought strength|dextera Domini fecit virtutem]] by keeping me in good, and by fighting for me and overcoming my adversaries. With this agrees what is read in Exodus: [[Ex 15:6|Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength: thy right hand, O Lord, hath slain the enemy|Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine; dextera tua, Domine, percussit inimicum]]; [[Ex 15:7|And in the multitude of thy glory thou hast put down thy adversaries|et in multitudine gloriæ tuæ deposuisti adversarios meos]] [Denis reads *adversarios meos*, "my adversaries"; the Vulgate has *tuos*, "thy"].

paras.t: Quoniam igitur tanta bona largitus est mihi Creator, fiducialiter dicere possum: Non moriar morte peccati et damnationis æternæ, sed vivam vita gratiæ in præsenti, vitaque gloriæ in futuro. Et juxta hunc sensum ait Christus: Si quis sermonem meum servaverit, mortem non videbit in æternum. Et narrabo opera Domini, id est, beneficia Dei mihi collata, apud me commemorabo, et aliis intimabo, ad gloriam largitoris, sicut et Christus in Evangelio dixit cuidam: Vade, et narra quanta tibi fecit Deus.
paras.en: Since, then, the Creator has bestowed such great goods on me, I can say with confidence: [[117:17|I shall not die|Non moriar]] the death of sin and of eternal damnation, [[117:17|but live|sed vivam]] the life of grace in the present and the life of glory in the future. And in this sense Christ says: [[John 8:51|If any man keep my word, he shall not see death for ever|Si quis sermonem meum servaverit, mortem non videbit in æternum]]. [[117:17|and shall declare the works of the Lord|Et narrabo opera Domini]], that is, I will call to mind within myself the benefits God has bestowed on me, and make them known to others, to the glory of the giver; as Christ too said to a certain man in the Gospel: Go, and [[Luke 8:39|tell how great things God hath done to thee|narra quanta tibi fecit Deus]].

paras.t: Castigans castigavit me Dominus, id est, propter peccata mea paternaliter me corripuit atque afflixit in sæculo isto, ne peream in æternum. Ideo additur: et morti æternæ non tradidit me. Unde dicit Apostolus: Quis filius quem non corripit pater? Quod si extra disciplinam estis, ergo adulteri et non filii estis. Et Salomon loquitur: Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, et non deficias quum ab eo corriperis; quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit. Quidquid igitur adversitatis et pœnæ accidit nobis, nostris adscribamus demeritis, illudque patienter, imo hilariter toleremus, pensantes illud Judith: Non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur; sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse, flagella Domini, quasi servi qui corripimur, ad emendationem et non ad perditionem nostram, evenisse credamus. Hinc namque scriptum est: Filii, patienter sustinete iram quæ supervenit vobis, etc. Qui enim induxit vobis mala, ipse rursus adducet vobis sempiternam jucunditatem cum vestra salute.
paras.en: [[117:18|The Lord chastising hath chastised me|Castigans castigavit me Dominus]], that is, for my sins he has corrected and afflicted me like a father in this world, lest I perish for ever. Therefore it is added: [[117:18|but he hath not delivered me over to death|et morti æternæ non tradidit me]] [Denis reads *morti æternæ*, "to eternal death"]. Hence the Apostle says: [[Heb 12:7|For what son is there whom the father doth not correct?|Quis filius quem non corripit pater?]] [[Heb 12:8|But if you be without chastisement|Quod si extra disciplinam estis]], [[Heb 12:8|then are you bastards and not sons|ergo adulteri et non filii estis]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 3:11|My son, reject not the correction of the Lord: and do not faint when thou art chastised by him|Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, et non deficias quum ab eo corriperis]]; [[Prov 3:12|For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth|quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit]]. Whatever adversity and punishment befalls us, then, let us ascribe to our own demerits, and bear it patiently, nay cheerfully, weighing that saying of Judith: [[Jdt 8:26|let us not revenge ourselves for these things which we suffer|Non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur]]. [[Jdt 8:27|But esteeming these very punishments to be less than our sins deserve, let us believe that these scourges of the Lord, with which like servants we are chastised, have happened for our amendment, and not for our destruction|sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse, flagella Domini, quasi servi qui corripimur, ad emendationem et non ad perditionem nostram, evenisse credamus]]. For hence it is written: [[Bar 4:25|My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you|Filii, patienter sustinete iram quæ supervenit vobis]], etc. [[Bar 4:29|For he that hath brought evils upon you, shall bring you everlasting joy again with your salvation|Qui enim induxit vobis mala, ipse rursus adducet vobis sempiternam jucunditatem cum vestra salute]].

paras.t: Deinde David in persona Ecclesiæ seu cujuscumque fidelis ait: Aperite mihi portas justitiæ: id est, o vos, Apostoli Christi et prædicatores sancti, per vestram doctrinam ostendite mihi mandata Christi, sacramenta novæ legis, evangelica consilia, operationes virtutum: quæ omnia appellantur portæ justitiæ, quia per ea intratur ad vitam justam. Ingressus in eas, confitebor Domino. Qui enim has portas ingreditur, laudabiliter conversatur, et ita dignus efficitur Deum laudare. Propter quod non ingredientibus portas has, Dominus ait: Quid dicitis mihi, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico? Hæc, id est confessio ista, est porta Domini, quia per eam itur ad Deum; justi intrabunt in eam, id est, confessionem istam laudis divinæ assument.
paras.en: Then David, in the person of the Church or of any of the faithful, says: [[117:19|Open ye to me the gates of justice|Aperite mihi portas justitiæ]]: that is, O you Apostles of Christ and holy preachers, by your teaching show me the commandments of Christ, the sacraments of the new law, the evangelical counsels, the works of the virtues: all of which are called gates of justice, because through them one enters into a just life. [[117:19|I will go in to them, and give praise to the Lord|Ingressus in eas, confitebor Domino]]. For whoever goes in at these gates lives praiseworthily, and so is made worthy to praise God. For this reason the Lord says to those who do not go in at these gates: [[Luke 6:46|And why call you me, Lord, Lord; and do not the things which I say?|Quid dicitis mihi, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico?]] [[117:20|This is|Hæc]], that is, this praise [*confessio*: the praise of the *confitebor*, "I will give praise", just before], [[117:20|the gate of the Lord|est porta Domini]], because through it one goes to God; [[117:20|the just shall enter into it|justi intrabunt in eam]], that is, they will take up this praise of God[[Jer 7:16||]] [the margin gives Jer. vii, 16, where the words *assumere laudem* also stand: "nor take to thee praise" for this people].

paras.t: Lapidem, id est Christum, de quo scriptum est: Lapis qui abscissus est de monte sine manibus. De quo Petrus testatur: Ecce pono in Sion lapidem summum, angularem, electum, pretiosum, in fundamento fundatum; et qui crediderit in eum, non confundetur. Hic igitur lapis, videlicet Christus, quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, id est principes sacerdotum, Scribæ et Pharisæi, quorum erat alios in fide et moribus prædicando et bene vivendo ædificare, hic factus est in caput anguli: ita quod in ipsum concurrunt duo populi, sicut duo parietes concurrunt in lapidem angularem. Christus enim ex Judæis atque gentilibus constituit unam Ecclesiam, cujus ipse est caput, influens eis motum virtutum et vitam gratiæ. Propterea Christus dixit: Alias oves habeo quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere, et fiet unum ovile et unus pastor.
paras.en: [[117:22|The stone|Lapidem]], that is, Christ, of whom it is written: [[Dan 2:45|the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands|Lapis qui abscissus est de monte sine manibus]]. Of whom Peter testifies: [[1 Pet 2:6|Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious|Ecce pono in Sion lapidem summum, angularem, electum, pretiosum]], [[Is 28:16|founded in the foundation|in fundamento fundatum]]; [[1 Pet 2:6|And he that shall believe in him shall not be confounded|et qui crediderit in eum, non confundetur]]. This stone, then, namely Christ, [[117:22|which the builders rejected|quem reprobaverunt ædificantes]], that is, the chief priests, the Scribes and Pharisees, whose part it was to build others up in faith and morals by preaching and by living well, [[117:22|the same is become the head of the corner|hic factus est in caput anguli]]: so that in him the two peoples meet, as two walls meet in the corner stone. For out of Jews and Gentiles Christ has formed one Church, of which he himself is the head, pouring into them the movement of the virtues and the life of grace. Hence Christ said: [[John 10:16|And other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias oves habeo quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere]]... [[John 10:16|And there shall be one fold and one shepherd|et fiet unum ovile et unus pastor]].

paras.t: A Domino factum est istud: id est, non humana aut naturali, sed divina ac supernaturali virtute facta est ista conjunctio lapidis angularis seu Christi, et utriusque populi inter se atque cum Christo. Tota enim Ecclesia Christo unitur ut capiti per fidem, caritatem et gratiam, quæ sunt supernaturalia dona Dei. Unde ait Apostolus: Deus qui dives est in misericordia, propter nimiam caritatem suam qua dilexit nos, quum essemus mortui peccatis, convivificavit nos in Christo: cujus gratia estis salvati. Et est mirabile in oculis nostris: id est, in consideratione fidelium, multum miranda est ista conversio atque conjunctio hominum cum Christo. Nullus enim satis valet mirari tam ineffabilem misericordiam Creatoris, qua misertus est mundo, mittens Unigenitum suum, atque pro omnibus nobis tradens illum, et nos unum cum illo efficiens. Unde rursus dicit Apostolus: Aliis generationibus non est agnitum filiis hominum, sicut nunc revelatum est sanctis Apostolis ejus et Prophetis in Spiritu, esse gentes coheredes et concorporales et comparticipes promissionis in Christo Jesu. Et alibi: Gratias, inquit, Deo super inenarrabili dono ejus. Præcipue autem mirabilis fuit ista conversio gentium primitivæ Ecclesiæ ex Judæis collectæ, juxta illud: Obstupuerunt ex circumcisione fideles, quia in nationes Spiritus Sancti gratia effusa est.
paras.en: [[117:23|This is the Lord's doing|A Domino factum est istud]]: that is, not by human or natural power but by divine and supernatural power has this joining been made, of the corner stone, that is, of Christ, and of both peoples with each other and with Christ. For the whole Church is united to Christ as to its head by faith, charity and grace, which are supernatural gifts of God. Hence the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:4|But God (who is rich in mercy) for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us|Deus qui dives est in misericordia, propter nimiam caritatem suam qua dilexit nos]], [[Eph 2:5|Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together in Christ (by whose grace you are saved)|quum essemus mortui peccatis, convivificavit nos in Christo: cujus gratia estis salvati]]. [[117:23|and it is wonderful in our eyes|Et est mirabile in oculis nostris]]: that is, in the consideration of the faithful, this conversion and joining of men with Christ is greatly to be wondered at. For no one can wonder enough at the so unspeakable mercy of the Creator, with which he had pity on the world, sending his Only-begotten, and delivering him up for us all[[Rom 8:32||]], and making us one with him. Hence the Apostle says again: [[Eph 3:5|in other generations was not known to the sons of men, as it is now revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit|Aliis generationibus non est agnitum filiis hominum, sicut nunc revelatum est sanctis Apostolis ejus et Prophetis in Spiritu]]: [[Eph 3:6|That the Gentiles should be fellow heirs and of the same body: and copartners of his promise in Christ Jesus|esse gentes coheredes et concorporales et comparticipes promissionis in Christo Jesu]]. And elsewhere: [[2 Cor 9:15|Thanks|Gratias]], he says, [[2 Cor 9:15|be to God for his unspeakable gift|Deo super inenarrabili dono ejus]]. But this conversion of the Gentiles was wonderful above all to the primitive Church gathered out of the Jews, according to that word: [[Acts 10:45|the faithful of the circumcision|ex circumcisione fideles]]... [[Acts 10:45|were astonished|Obstupuerunt]], [[Acts 10:45|for that the grace of the Holy Ghost was poured out upon the Gentiles|quia in nationes Spiritus Sancti gratia effusa est]] [the margin gives Act. x, 43; the words are Acts 10:45].

paras.t: Vel sic: A Domino trino in personis et uno in natura, factum est istud, videlicet quod lapis ab ædificantibus reprobatus, factus est in caput anguli; et est mirabile in oculis nostris mentalibus. Vehementer namque mirandum est, quod ille qui tempore passionis in tantum humiliatus fuit, paulo post in tantum glorificaretur a Deo, ut ex omni genere hominum multi converterentur ad ipsum: inter quos erant nonnulli, qui ejus occisioni consenserunt, et eam procuraverunt, quibus dixit ante passionem: Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum.
paras.en: Or thus: [[117:23|This is the Lord's doing|A Domino trino in personis et uno in natura, factum est istud]] (the Lord, that is, three in Persons and one in nature), namely, that the stone rejected by the builders is become the head of the corner; [[117:23|and it is wonderful in our eyes|et est mirabile in oculis nostris]], the eyes of the mind. For it is greatly to be wondered at that he who in the time of his passion was so deeply humbled should a little after be so glorified by God that out of every kind of men many were converted to him: among whom were some who had consented to his killing and had brought it about, to whom he said before his passion: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]].

paras.t: Hæc dies, in qua Deus hæc fecit, est dies quam fecit Dominus: id est, tempus Christi, tempus evangelicæ legis et gratiæ, in quo utique constituta est ex utroque populo Ecclesia una in Christo, est tempus a Deo specialiter factum. Nam licet omnium dierum ac temporum Deus sit factor, illius tamen diei et temporis dicitur Deus specialiter factor, in quo ipse præcipua et specialia opera fecit. Quoniam ergo in Christi adventu et interim majorem benignitatem et gratiam impendit hominibus quam ante, merito tempus seu dies Christi dicitur factus a Deo. Sæpe enim in sacra Scriptura, tempus novi Testamenti, dies vocatur: quia in eo veritas, in veteri Testamento figuris occultata, clare revelata cognoscitur; et quia in novo Testamento splendor gratiæ Dei clarius copiosiusque refulsit hominibus, quam tempore veteris legis. Exsultemus et lætemur in ea, id est, mente et corpore gaudeamus in Domino tempore isto, de beneficiis ejus gratias ipsi agendo. Unde quum Apostolus dixisset, Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis, adjecit: Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes.
paras.en: [[117:24|This is the day|Hæc dies]], in which God has done these things, is the day [[117:24|which the Lord hath made|quam fecit Dominus]]: that is, the time of Christ, the time of the gospel law and of grace, in which the one Church in Christ was established out of both peoples, is a time specially made by God. For though God is the maker of all days and times, yet he is said to be in a special way the maker of that day and time in which he did his chief and special works. Since, then, at the coming of Christ and in the time since, he has bestowed greater kindness and grace on men than before, the time or day of Christ is rightly said to be made by God. For in sacred Scripture the time of the New Testament is often called day: because in it the truth that was hidden under figures in the Old Testament is known, clearly revealed; and because in the New Testament the splendour of God's grace has shone upon men more clearly and more abundantly than in the time of the old law. [[117:24|let us be glad and rejoice therein|Exsultemus et lætemur in ea]], that is, let us rejoice in the Lord in mind and body in this time, giving him thanks for his benefits. Hence when the Apostle had said, [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time: behold, now is the day of salvation|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis]], he added: [[2 Cor 6:10|As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing|Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes]].

paras.t: Merito autem cantatur hic versus in die Paschæ tam frequenter, quoniam Christus, sol justitiæ, candor lucis æternæ, lux lucis et fons luminis, qui erat in die Parasceves passionis caligine obscuratus, atque in monumento lapideo, tanquam densissima nube absconditus, in die Paschæ de sepulcro glorificatus, candidus et rubicundus processit, illuminans mundum, noctem infidelitatis et tenebras ignorantiæ de cordibus discipulorum ejiciens.
paras.en: And this verse is rightly sung so often on Easter day, since Christ, the sun of justice, [[Wis 7:26|the brightness of eternal light|candor lucis æternæ]], light of light and fount of brightness, who on the day of the Parasceve [that is, Good Friday] had been darkened by the gloom of his passion, and hidden in the monument of stone as in a very dense cloud[[Matt 27:60||]], on Easter day came forth glorified from the sepulchre[[Matt 28:6||]] [the margin gives only Matth. xxvii, xxviii], [[Cant 5:10|white and ruddy|candidus et rubicundus]], enlightening the world, and casting the night of unbelief and the darkness of ignorance out of the hearts of his disciples.

paras.t: Et ut per temporalia festa et gaudia mereamur venire ad præmia sempiterna, orandum est nobis quod subditur: O Domine, salvum me fac de pœnis et vitiis vitæ præsentis; o Domine, bene prosperare: id est, prospera dona concede, augendo Ecclesiam numero et merito, perducendoque nos per gratiæ tuæ ducatum ad tui ipsius beatificam visionem: sicut supra dictum est, Prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum.
paras.en: And that through temporal feasts and joys we may deserve to come to the everlasting rewards, we must pray what follows: [[117:25|O Lord, save me|O Domine, salvum me fac]] from the pains and vices of the present life; [[117:25|O Lord, give good success|o Domine, bene prosperare]]: that is, grant prosperous gifts, increasing the Church in number and in merit, and leading us under the guidance of thy grace to the beatific vision of thyself: as was said above: [[Ps 67:20|the God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous to us|Prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum]].

paras.t: Benedictus est qui venit in nomine Domini, id est Christus, qui ait: Ego veni in nomine Patris mei. Secundum Hieronymum, canticum istud puerorum, quo Christo in die Palmarum cantabant: Hosanna filio David, Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, Hosanna in excelsis, ex isto versiculo sumptum est. Et ita David prophetavit hoc loco de laude illa.
paras.en: [[117:26|Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the Lord|Benedictus est qui venit in nomine Domini]], that is, Christ, who says: [[John 5:43|I am come in the name of my Father|Ego veni in nomine Patris mei]]. According to Jerome, that song of the children which they sang to Christ on Palm Sunday, [[Matt 21:9|Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest|Hosanna filio David, Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, Hosanna in excelsis]], was taken from this verse. And so David in this place prophesied of that praise.

paras.t: Deinde in persona Apostolorum et succedentium eis, videlicet pastorum et sacerdotum Ecclesiæ, subditur: Benediximus, nos episcopi et prælati, vobis, o subditi, de domo Domini, id est de Ecclesia Christi, prædicando vobis verbum salutis, ministrando vobis sacramenta novæ legis, orando quoque pro vobis, et gratiam nobis divinitus datam, vobis (sicut caritas exigit) communicando. Benedictio proprie dicitur collatio gratiæ Dei. Gratiam autem non confert nisi Deus. Quomodo ergo unus nostrum alteri benedicere, seu gratiam communicare potest, nisi instrumentaliter, non principaliter? Ideo subditur: Deus Dominus, et illuxit nobis: id est, Deus, qui est Dominus noster, ipse et illuxit nobis, illuminando corda nostra Spiritu Sancto, et gratiam splendidam nostris mentibus infundendo, dando quoque nobis auctoritatem ligandi atque solvendi, ministrandi sacramenta, prædicandi evangelica verba, consecrandi et benedicendi: ex quibus idonei sumus ad benedicendum vobis. Quapropter Joannes testatur: De plenitudine ejus accepimus omnes.
paras.en: Then, in the person of the Apostles and of those who succeed them, namely the pastors and priests of the Church, it is added: [[117:26|We have blessed|Benediximus]], we bishops and prelates, [[117:26|you|vobis]], O subjects, [[117:26|out of the house of the Lord|de domo Domini]], that is, out of the Church of Christ, by preaching to you the word of salvation, ministering to you the sacraments of the new law, praying also for you, and sharing with you (as charity requires) the grace given us from God. Blessing, properly speaking, is the bestowal of God's grace. But none but God bestows grace. How then can one of us bless another, or share grace with him, except as an instrument and not as the principal cause? Therefore it is added: [[117:27|The Lord is God, and he hath shone upon us|Deus Dominus, et illuxit nobis]]: that is, God, who is our Lord[[Ps 8:2||]] [the margin gives Ps. viii, 2, which begins *Domine, Dominus noster*, "O Lord, our Lord"], has himself shone upon us, enlightening our hearts with the Holy Ghost and pouring shining grace into our minds, and giving us also the authority of binding and loosing, of ministering the sacraments, of preaching the words of the gospel, of consecrating and of blessing: by which we are fit to bless you. Wherefore John testifies: [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|De plenitudine ejus accepimus omnes]].

paras.t: Constituite, o vos antistites Christi, diem solennem, id est celebre festum, seu dies festivos, in commemorationem incarnationis, resurrectionis, ascensionisque Christi, videlicet festum Nativitatis, solennitatem Resurrectionis, etc.; et de hoc agite in condensis, id est in populis adunatis, ita quod Christifideles in magna densitate et copia ad festa ista conveniant. Alia translatio habet, In congregationibus; alia vero, In frequentationibus: ex quo claret, quod iste sit sensus litteralis. Quod etiam patet ex eo quod subditur: usque ad cornu altaris, id est, tam copiose ac dense fideles concurrant, quod ipsa ecclesia usque ad altaris angulum impleatur.
paras.en: [[117:27|Appoint|Constituite]], O you bishops of Christ, [[117:27|a solemn day|diem solennem]], that is, a thronged feast, or feast days, in commemoration of the incarnation, resurrection and ascension of Christ, namely the feast of the Nativity, the solemnity of the Resurrection, etc.; and do this [[117:27|with shady boughs|in condensis]], that is, among the people gathered together, so that the faithful of Christ come to these feasts in great density and numbers [*in condensis*, literally "in thick places": the Douay-Rheims takes it of thick boughs, Denis of thronging crowds]. Another translation has *In congregations*; another, *In frequentations* [that is, in throngs]: from which it is plain that this is the literal sense. This is clear also from what follows: [[117:27|even to the horn of the altar|usque ad cornu altaris]], that is, let the faithful flock together so abundantly and densely that the church itself is filled even to the corner of the altar.

paras.t: Moraliter vero ita exponitur: Constituite, o universi fideles, diem solennem, id est sabbatum mentis, videlicet interioris hominis tranquillam quietem, in condensis, id est in cumulo gratiarum divinarum, in abundantia sanctarum cogitationum, in densitate divinorum charismatum, ita quod Deo intra vos exhibeatis solennitatem decoram, ab exterioribus quiescendo, cœlestibus inhiando, Deumque ardenter amando; usque ad cornu altaris, id est perseveranter, donec pertingatis ad sublime Dei altare in cœlo paratum, in quo offerunt Deo omnes Beati hymnum incessabilis laudis.
paras.en: Morally, however, it is expounded thus: [[117:27|Appoint|Constituite]], O all you faithful, [[117:27|a solemn day|diem solennem]], that is, the sabbath of the mind, namely the tranquil quiet of the inner man, [[117:27|with shady boughs|in condensis]], that is, in a heap of divine graces, in an abundance of holy thoughts, in a thickness of divine gifts, so that within yourselves you show God a comely solemnity, resting from outward things, longing for heavenly things, and loving God ardently; [[117:27|even to the horn of the altar|usque ad cornu altaris]], that is, perseveringly, until you reach the high altar of God prepared in heaven, at which all the Blessed offer to God a hymn of unceasing praise.

paras.t: Postremo Ecclesia seu fidelis de prædictis beneficiis gratias referens ait: Deus meus es tu, Domine Christe: cui Thomas ait, Dominus meus, et Deus meus; et confitebor tibi, id est, te laudabo. Deus meus es tu, Jesu, Fili Dei summi, prout de te scriptum est: Hic est verus Deus et vita æterna; et exaltabo te: non quod ego te altum efficiam, sed quoniam tuam dignitatem et altitudinem verbis et actibus profitebor et prædicabo; atque per hoc te, qui in te ipso semper altus et magnus es, altum et magnum efficiam in corde meo et proximorum, quibus tua magnalia recitabo. Confitebor tibi quoniam exaudisti me, id est, de mea exauditione gratias tibi agam, et quoniam factus es mihi in salutem: sicut expositum est.
paras.en: Lastly the Church, or the faithful soul, giving thanks for the benefits spoken of, says: [[117:28|Thou art my God|Deus meus es tu]], O Lord Christ, to whom Thomas said: [[John 20:28|My Lord and my God|Dominus meus, et Deus meus]]; [[117:28|and I will praise thee|et confitebor tibi]], that is, I will praise thee [Denis glosses *confitebor*, "I will confess", by *laudabo*, "I will praise"]. [[117:28|thou art my God|Deus meus es tu]], Jesus, Son of God most high, as it is written of thee: [[1 John 5:20|This is the true God and life eternal|Hic est verus Deus et vita æterna]]; [[117:28|and I will exalt thee|et exaltabo te]]: not that I make thee high, but because I will profess and proclaim thy dignity and height in words and deeds; and in this way I shall make thee, who in thyself art ever high and great, high and great in my heart and in the hearts of my neighbours, to whom I shall tell thy great works. [[117:28|I will praise thee, because thou hast heard me|Confitebor tibi quoniam exaudisti me]], that is, I will give thee thanks for my being heard, [[117:28|and art become my salvation|et quoniam factus es mihi in salutem]]: as has been expounded.

paras.t: Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus. Ecce versiculum in exordio psalmi præhabitum jam resumit, ad insinuandum quod omnis operatio perfectorum, a laude Dei sit inchoanda, atque in laudibus terminanda, quemadmodum docet divinus Apostolus: Sive manducatis, sive bibitis, sive aliud aliquid facitis, omnia in gloriam Dei facite.
paras.en: [[117:29|O praise ye the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.|Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.]] See, he now takes up again the verse that stood at the beginning of the psalm, to suggest that every work of the perfect is to be begun with the praise of God and ended in praises, as the divine Apostle teaches: [[1 Cor 10:31|whether you eat or drink, or whatsoever else you do, do all to the glory of God|Sive manducatis, sive bibitis, sive aliud aliquid facitis, omnia in gloriam Dei facite]].

paras.t: En psalmum dulcem ac speciosum, sensu atque mysteriis plenum audivimus: in cujus principio ad Dei præconia repetitis vicibus invitamur. In quo moraliter edocemur de tribulatione ad Dominum exclamare, non frangi, tristari, aut desperare, sperantes secure quod late exaudiet nos, prout alibi inducitur: Animæquiores estote, filii, clamate ad Dominum, et eripiet vos de manu inimicorum. Docemur insuper ex psalmo præsenti, in solo Deo confidere, ejusque gratiæ semper inniti. Describuntur etiam beneficia Dei in psalmo isto lucifluo, et Christi mysteria recitantur in eo. Cum multa igitur devotione et jucunditate præcipua, decantemus hunc splendidissimum psalmum: cujus utique suavitatem copiosissime experiemur, si corde intento et puro eum cantemus. Non enim mens vaga, intimorata, carnalis sive mundana, experiri valet virtutem psalmorum.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a sweet and beautiful psalm, full of meaning and of mysteries, at the beginning of which we are invited again and again to the praises of God. In it we are taught morally to cry out to the Lord from tribulation, and not to be broken, saddened or despairing, hoping securely that he will hear us abundantly, as is said elsewhere: [[Bar 4:21|Be of good comfort, my children, cry to the Lord, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the princes your enemies|Animæquiores estote, filii, clamate ad Dominum, et eripiet vos de manu inimicorum]]. We are taught besides by this present psalm to trust in God alone and to lean always on his grace. The benefits of God are also described in this light-streaming psalm, and the mysteries of Christ are recounted in it. With much devotion, then, and with especial gladness, let us sing this most splendid psalm: whose sweetness we shall surely taste most abundantly if we sing it with an attentive and pure heart. For a wandering mind, one without the fear of God, carnal or worldly, cannot taste the power of the psalms.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, fortitudo et laus fidelium, spesque cunctorum in te confidentium, da nobis in salute tua pietatis profectum, dextera tua in bonis nos exalta: ut te aperiente, portas justitiæ ingressi, perenniter cum justis confiteamur tibi.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, the strength and praise of the faithful, and the hope of all who trust in thee, grant us in thy salvation an increase of godliness; exalt us in good things by thy right hand: that, thou opening to us, we may enter the gates of justice and praise thee for ever with the just.

118.title: EXPLANATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI OCTAVIDECIMI : BEATI IMMACULATI.
118.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and eighteenth psalm: Blessed are the undefiled.

paras.t: Habet psalmus nunc declarandus pro titulo, Alleluia. Nec mirum, quum psalmus iste plenus sit laudibus Dei : in quo edocemur, Deum verbis et bonis laudare operibus. Denique psalmus præsens alphabeticus est, tot habentes octonarios quot sunt litteras in alphabeto Hebræo, videlicet viginti duo. Incipiuntque octonarii secundum ordinem litterarum alphabeti Hebraici, ita quod singuli versus ejusdem octonarii, inchoantur a littera quæ eis præponitur : propter quod singulis octonariis singulæ litteræ præscribuntur. — Est autem hic psalmus in superficie satis planus, sed bene examinatus, sensuum profunditate præcipuus est. Loquitur vero de ipsa beatitudine, et iis per quæ ad beatitudinem pervenitur. Beatitudo vero duplex est, scilicet viæ et patriæ. Nunc autem de beatitudine viæ fit sermo : et est psalmus iste omni morali doctrina conspicuus, præfulgens et summus. In quo sanctus Propheta ex æstuanti et exuberantis cordis sui amore divino, Deum familiariter suaviterque affatur, atque eamdem sententiam frequenter resumit, sub aliis tamen verbis, ut tædium evitetur. Moris namque est ferventis et impatientis desiderii, idem frequenter repetere, quia cum dilecto loquendo nescit lassescere. — Secundum eos quoque, qui asserunt non omnes psalmos a David compositos, ignoratur auctor psalmi præsentis, quia in titulo auctor non explicatur ; sed secundum omnes pene sanctos ac magnos doctores catholicos, David edidit eum, qui tanquam amantissimus Domini in Deo habitans confidenter, per totum psalmi hujus processum cum admirabili caritatis fervore et sanctæ exercitationis devotione eloquitur. In quo omnis fidelis plenissime eruditur, quid agendum, quid vitandum, quid appetendum. Laudantque doctores psalmum præsentem eminenter et mirabiliter. A beatitudine igitur, quam omnes naturaliter appetunt, orsus loqui Psalmographus, ait :
paras.en: The psalm now to be explained has for its title: Alleluia. And no wonder, since this psalm is full of the praises of God: in it we are taught to praise God with words and with good works. Further, the present psalm is alphabetical, having as many octonaries [that is, sections of eight verses] as there are letters in the Hebrew alphabet, namely twenty-two. And the octonaries begin in the order of the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, in such a way that each verse of the same octonary begins with the letter set before it: which is why a letter is written before each octonary. — Now this psalm is plain enough on the surface, but when well examined it is outstanding for the depth of its senses. It speaks of beatitude itself, and of the things by which beatitude is reached. Beatitude is twofold, namely of the way and of the fatherland [that is, the happiness possible to us as wayfarers in this life, and that of heaven]. Here the discourse is of the beatitude of the way; and this psalm is conspicuous, resplendent and supreme in all moral doctrine. In it the holy Prophet, out of the burning and overflowing divine love of his heart, addresses God familiarly and sweetly, and often takes up the same thought again, though in other words, so that weariness may be avoided. For it is the way of fervent and impatient desire to repeat the same thing often, since in speaking with the beloved it does not know how to grow weary. — According to those, too, who assert that not all the psalms were composed by David, the author of the present psalm is unknown, since the author is not stated in the title; but according to nearly all the holy and great Catholic doctors, David composed it, who, as one most beloved of the Lord dwelling confidently in God, speaks throughout the whole course of this psalm with an admirable fervour of charity and devotion of holy exercise. In it every one of the faithful is most fully instructed in what is to be done, what avoided, what desired. And the doctors praise the present psalm eminently and wonderfully. Beginning, then, to speak of beatitude, which all men naturally desire, the Psalmist says:

paras.t: Aleph. Beati sunt jam in spe, postmodum beatificandi in re, immaculati, id est sine labe mortalis peccati, in via, id est vita præsenti, quæ est via ad futuram, veram, æternamque vitam; qui ambulant in lege Domini, id est, qui conversantur in observatione legis divinæ seu præceptorum Decalogi. Non enim sufficit declinare a malo, nisi quod bonum est, fiat. Propter quod Christus ait : Omnem palmitem in me non ferentem fructum, tollet eum. Et alibi dicitur : Omnis arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur, et in ignem mittetur. Verumtamen immaculatio non solum concernit peccata commissionis, sed etiam peccata omissionis. Frequenter quoque testatur Scriptura, neminem posse immaculatum vocari, juxta illud : Quis potest dicere, Mundum est cor meum, purus sum a peccato? Et alibi : Nemo mundus a sorde, nec infans cujus est unius diei vita super terram.
paras.en: Aleph. [[118:1|Blessed|Beati]] are they, now in hope, and hereafter to be made blessed in reality, [[118:1|the undefiled|immaculati]], that is, without the stain of mortal sin, [[118:1|in the way|in via]], that is, in the present life, which is the way to the future, true and eternal life; [[118:1|who walk in the law of the Lord|qui ambulant in lege Domini]], that is, who live in the observance of the divine law, or of the commandments of the Decalogue. For it is not enough to turn aside from evil unless what is good is done. That is why Christ says: [[John 15:2|Every branch in me that beareth not fruit, he will take away|Omnem palmitem in me non ferentem fructum, tollet eum]]. And elsewhere it is said: [[Matt 3:10|Every tree therefore that doth not yield good fruit, shall be cut down, and cast into the fire|Omnis arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur, et in ignem mittetur]]. Yet undefilement concerns not only sins of commission, but also sins of omission. Scripture also often testifies that no one can be called undefiled, according to that saying: [[Prov 20:9|Who can say: My heart is clean, I am pure from sin?|Quis potest dicere, Mundum est cor meum, purus sum a peccato?]] And elsewhere: No one is clean from filth, not even the infant whose life upon the earth is of one day[[Job 14:4||]] [the margin gives Job xiv, 4, 5, according to the Septuagint; the Vulgate wording differs].

paras.t: Pensandum itaque quod aliquis dicitur immaculatus variis modis : Primo, quoniam nunquam peccato subjacere potuit, nec originali, nec mortali, nec veniali : et ita Christus homo immaculatus censetur. Secundo, quoniam nec mortali, nec veniali peccato fuscatus est : et hoc modo Virgo beata immaculata est. Quod ei soli convenit, quantum ad adultos : nam ante annos discretionis seu usum rationis, ceteri quoque hoc modo immaculati sunt ; qui tamen maculati et sorde infecti dicuntur propter originale, quod habent aut habuerunt : a quo Virgo beata, per prævenientem Filii sui gratiam creditur præservata. Tertio, quoniam mortali peccato pollutus non est, vel si fuit, per pœnitentiam exstat purgatus : sicque de gratia Dei multi immaculati existunt, quamvis nullus viator sine speciali revelatione certo scire queat, an sic immaculatus sit. Potest tamen conjecturaliter et probabiliter scire : ideoque scriptum est, Etiam si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea. Ad hanc autem immaculationem hortatur nos sermo divinus : Exhibete vos sanctos et immaculatos et irreprehensibiles coram Deo. Hæc autem immaculatio est beatitudo viæ, quæ aliud non est, nisi observatio præceptorum Altissimi, loquendo de beatitudine vitæ activæ, de qua loquitur Christus apud Matthæum, et David in isto versiculo. Hæc namque beatitudo est actus virtutum quæ ordinantur ad opus. Porro alia est beatitudo vitæ contemplativæ, quæ est actus sapientiæ, ad quam disponit beatitudo prædicta, consistens in operatione virtutum moralium. Quum enim ad contemplationem requiratur ordinatio appetitus sensitivi, seu refrenatio passionum, necesse est beatitudinem vitæ activæ præcedere beatitudinem vitæ contemplativæ, eo quod virtutes morales refrenent ac ordinent passiones, ne rationem in consideratione veritatis, aut voluntatem in dilectione bonitatis impediant.
paras.en: It is to be considered, then, that someone is called undefiled in various ways. First, because he never could be subject to sin, neither original, nor mortal, nor venial: and in this way Christ as man is held to be undefiled. Secondly, because he has been darkened by neither mortal nor venial sin: and in this way the Blessed Virgin is undefiled. This belongs to her alone, as far as adults are concerned; for before the years of discretion, or the use of reason, others too are undefiled in this way; and yet they are said to be stained and infected with filth on account of original sin, which they have or have had: from which the Blessed Virgin is believed to have been preserved by the prevenient grace of her Son. Thirdly, because he has not been polluted by mortal sin, or, if he was, he has been cleansed by penance: and so by the grace of God many are undefiled, although no wayfarer [that is, no one still on the way of this life] can know for certain without a special revelation whether he is undefiled in this way. He can, however, know it by conjecture and with probability: and therefore it is written: [[Job 9:21|Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of|Etiam si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea]]. Now to this undefilement the divine word exhorts us: [[Col 1:22|to present you holy and unspotted and blameless before him|Exhibete vos sanctos et immaculatos et irreprehensibiles coram Deo]] [Denis has *coram Deo*, "before God"]. This undefilement is the beatitude of the way, which is nothing other than the observance of the commandments of the Most High, speaking of the beatitude of the active life, of which Christ speaks in Matthew[[Matt 5:3||]] [the margin gives Matth. v, 3–12, the eight beatitudes], and David in this verse. For this beatitude is the act of the virtues that are ordered to action. There is besides another beatitude, of the contemplative life, which is the act of wisdom, to which the beatitude just named disposes, consisting in the exercise of the moral virtues. For since contemplation requires the ordering of the sensitive appetite, or the curbing of the passions, the beatitude of the active life must precede the beatitude of the contemplative life, because the moral virtues curb and order the passions, so that they do not hinder the reason in the consideration of truth, or the will in the love of goodness.

paras.t: De beatitudine itaque vitæ contemplativæ subjungitur : Beati sunt jam in spe qui scrutantur, non præsumptuose aut curiose, sed diligenter atque humiliter, testimonia ejus, id est attestationes sacræ Scripturæ seu ipsas divinas Scripturas, in quibus Deus nobis testatur quid credere debeamus. Duæ sunt partes legis divinæ, videlicet mandata et testimonia. Mandata pertinent ad agenda, testimonia ad credenda. Idcirco in observatione mandatorum sita est beatitudo vitæ activæ ; in contemplatione autem testimoniorum, beatitudo vitæ contemplativæ. Quapropter ait Salvator, loquens ad Patrem : Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum. Et Apostolus : Existimo, inquit, omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Debemus igitur, si beatitudinem vere optamus, scrutari sacras Scripturas, in studio divinorum librorum continuo exerceri, et sacra eloquia tanquam epistolas Spiritus Sancti ad nos missas, cum omni reverentia speculari. Quum enim studemus, Spiritus Sanctus loquitur nobis. Et sicut fatetur studiosissimus ille Hieronymus, Qui diligit studia Scripturarum, ventris ingluviem atque delicias abominatur. Hinc enim in Ecclesiastico dicitur : Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in Prophetis vacabit. Quæ utique occupatio valde delectabilis est et salubris, prout legitur : Nos autem solatio habentes sanctos libros, qui in manibus nostris sunt.
paras.en: Of the beatitude of the contemplative life, then, there follows: [[118:2|Blessed|Beati]] are they now in hope [[118:2|that search|qui scrutantur]], not presumptuously or out of curiosity, but diligently and humbly, [[118:2|his testimonies|testimonia ejus]], that is, the attestations of sacred Scripture, or the divine Scriptures themselves, in which God testifies to us what we ought to believe. There are two parts of the divine law, namely commandments and testimonies. The commandments concern what is to be done, the testimonies what is to be believed. Therefore the beatitude of the active life lies in the observance of the commandments, and the beatitude of the contemplative life in the contemplation of the testimonies. Hence the Saviour says, speaking to the Father: [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent|Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum]]. And the Apostle: [[Phil 3:8|I count|Existimo]], he says, [[Phil 3:8|all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge|omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam]] of our Lord Jesus Christ. If, then, we truly desire beatitude, we must search the sacred Scriptures, be continually exercised in the study of the divine books, and gaze with all reverence upon the sacred words as letters sent to us by the Holy Ghost. For when we study, the Holy Ghost speaks to us. And as that most studious man Jerome declares: He who loves the study of the Scriptures abhors gluttony and the pleasures of the belly. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 39:1|The wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be occupied in the prophets.|Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in Prophetis vacabit]] And this occupation is indeed most delightful and wholesome, as we read: [[1 Mach 12:9|We|Nos]] for our part [[1 Mach 12:9|having for our comfort the holy books that are in our hands|solatio habentes sanctos libros, qui in manibus nostris sunt]].

paras.t: Sed omnino cavere oportet, ne in tantum occupemus intellectum in consideratione veritatis, quod infrigidetur aut tepescat affectus in dilectione summæ bonitatis, et igne sanctæ devotionis. Imo frequentius, principalius, et si possibile est, diutius immorari debemus circa exercitationem et inflammationem affectus, quam circa studium intellectus. Cujus (proh dolor !) oppositum multi agunt : propter quod nunquam ad veram perfectionem pertingunt. Idcirco adjicitur : in toto corde exquirunt eum : id est, hanc scrutationem testimoniorum Dei referunt prorsus ad Deum, quatenus ex contemplatione sincera in ejus amore proficiant, eumque in omnibus intellectu atque affectu honorent. Et in hoc differunt contemplatio sanctorum a contemplatione vanorum, contemplatio quoque theologorum a contemplatione philosophorum, quod sancti et veri theologi non sistunt in nuda speculatione, sed ad Dei actualem fervidumque amorem referunt eam ; philosophi vero et vani fideles, in consideratione quiescunt, vel etiam, quod pejus est, eam interdum ad vanam gloriam, seu lucrum temporaleque bonum coordinant.
paras.en: But we must take great care not to occupy the intellect so much in the consideration of truth that the affection grows cold or lukewarm in the love of the supreme goodness and in the fire of holy devotion. Rather, we ought to dwell more often, more principally and, if possible, longer on the exercise and kindling of the affection than on the study of the intellect. Many (alas!) do the opposite: and that is why they never reach true perfection. Therefore it is added: [[118:2|that seek him with their whole heart|in toto corde exquirunt eum]]: that is, they refer this searching of God's testimonies wholly to God, so that from sincere contemplation they may advance in his love, and honour him in all things with intellect and affection. And in this the contemplation of the saints differs from the contemplation of the vain, and the contemplation of theologians from the contemplation of philosophers: that the saints and true theologians do not stop at bare speculation, but refer it to an actual and fervent love of God; whereas philosophers and vain believers rest in the consideration itself, or even, what is worse, sometimes direct it to vainglory, or to gain and temporal good.

paras.t: Hi ergo immaculati et studiosi, beati sunt, non vitiosi et pigri : cujus ratio est, vel potius signum : Non enim qui operantur iniquitatem, id est peccatum mortale, quod nunquam committitur sine rationis consensu, in viis ejus ambulaverunt, id est, in divinis præceptis conversati non sunt in eo tempore quo iniquitatem fecerunt : imo in viis diaboli ambulant tales. De quibus scriptum est : Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis et perditionis, et ambulavimus vias difficiles ; viam autem Domini ignoravimus. Hæc est via spatiosa et lata, quæ ducit ad mortem, per quam ambulant multi. Hinc enim legitur : Rectæ sunt viæ Domini, et justi ambulabunt in eis; prævaricatores vero corruent in eis. Denique viæ quas ambulant impii, tenebrosæ et turpes atque obliquæ sunt. Non ergo ambulant vias Domini, de quibus dicitur : Viæ ejus viæ pulchræ, et omnes semitæ ejus pacificæ. De pulchritudine autem viæ justorum, qua Deo in sanctitate deserviunt, scriptum est : Justorum semita quasi lux splendens, procedit et crescit usque ad perfectam diem.
paras.en: These, then, the undefiled and the studious, are blessed, not the vicious and the slothful: and the reason for this, or rather the sign of it, is: [[118:3|For they that work iniquity|Non enim qui operantur iniquitatem]], that is, mortal sin, which is never committed without the consent of reason, [[118:3|have not walked in his ways|in viis ejus ambulaverunt]], that is, they have not lived in the divine commandments at the time when they did iniquity: rather, such men walk in the ways of the devil. Of them it is written: [[Wis 5:7|We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction, and have walked through hard ways, but the way of the Lord we have not known.|Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis et perditionis, et ambulavimus vias difficiles ; viam autem Domini ignoravimus]] This is the wide and broad way that leads to death, by which many walk[[Matt 7:13||]]. Hence we read: [[Osee 14:10|the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall in them|Rectæ sunt viæ Domini, et justi ambulabunt in eis; prævaricatores vero corruent in eis]]. In short, the ways in which the wicked walk are dark and foul and crooked. They do not, then, walk the ways of the Lord, of which it is said: [[Prov 3:17|Her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are peaceable.|Viæ ejus viæ pulchræ, et omnes semitæ ejus pacificæ]] And of the beauty of the way of the just, by which they serve God in holiness, it is written: [[Prov 4:18|the path of the just, as a shining light, goeth forwards, and increaseth even to perfect day|Justorum semita quasi lux splendens, procedit et crescit usque ad perfectam diem]].

paras.t: Tu, Domine, mandasti mandata tua custodiri nimis, id est multum diligenter. Magno enim, summo et infinito Domino cum incomparabili reverentia, amore, atque timore ministrare oportet. Et ideo apud Jeremiam inducitur : Maledictus qui facit opus Dei fraudulenter. Et alibi : Nunc quia tepidus es, incipiam te evomere de ore meo. Hinc quoque Moyses scripsit : Custodi te ipsum et animam tuam sollicite ; et ne obliviscaris verborum Domini, et ne excidant de corde tuo omnibus diebus vitæ tuæ. Si autem scire volumus quam nimis præceperit Christus impleri mandata sua, audiamus quid de præceptis caritatis asserat : Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota anima tua, et ex tota mente tua, et ex tota virtute tua. Ecce tam nimis præcepit, ut nullus in hac vita implere totaliter possit. Timorate ergo et sollicite ambulemus coram Domino Deo nostro, pensantes illud : Tempus est ut incipiat judicium a domo Dei. Si autem primum a nobis, quis finis eorum qui non credunt Evangelio? Et si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt ?
paras.en: [[118:4|Thou|Tu]], O Lord, [[118:4|hast commanded thy commandments to be kept most diligently|mandasti mandata tua custodiri nimis]] [*nimis*, literally "exceedingly"], that is, with great diligence. For a great, supreme and infinite Lord must be served with incomparable reverence, love and fear. And therefore in Jeremias it is said: [[Jer 48:10|Cursed be he that doth the work of the Lord deceitfully|Maledictus qui facit opus Dei fraudulenter]]. And elsewhere: Now [[Apoc 3:16|because thou art lukewarm|quia tepidus es]], [[Apoc 3:16|I will begin to vomit thee out of my mouth|incipiam te evomere de ore meo]]. Hence too Moses wrote: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully|Custodi te ipsum et animam tuam sollicite]]; and [[Deut 4:9|Forget not the words|ne obliviscaris verborum]] of the Lord, [[Deut 4:9|and let them not go out of thy heart all the days of thy life|et ne excidant de corde tuo omnibus diebus vitæ tuæ]]. And if we wish to know how exceedingly Christ commanded his commandments to be fulfilled, let us hear what he declares of the precepts of charity: [[Mark 12:30|thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart and with thy whole soul and with thy whole mind and with thy whole strength|Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota anima tua, et ex tota mente tua, et ex tota virtute tua]]. See, he commanded so exceedingly that no one in this life can fulfil it entirely.
