Let us therefore walk fearfully and carefully before the Lord our God[[Mich 6:8||]], pondering that saying: [[1 Pet 4:17|the time is, that judgment should begin at the house of God. And if at first at us, what shall be the end of them that believe not the gospel of God?|Tempus est ut incipiat judicium a domo Dei. Si autem primum a nobis, quis finis eorum qui non credunt Evangelio?]] [[1 Pet 4:18|And if the just man shall scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?|Et si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt]]

paras.t: Utinam, Domine, dirigantur a te et angelo sancto per gratiam tuam viæ meæ, id est desideria, verba et opera quibus ad patriam tendit homo, ad custodiendas justificationes tuas, id est taliter tamque directe, ut tua mandata justa et justificantia observentur a me. Hoc, o Domine, vehementer cupio a te fieri, quoniam naturali potestate id nequeo adimplere, quum (teste Apostolo) non sit volentis neque currentis, sed Dei miserentis. Unde et sanctus Jeremias ait : Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri ut ambulet et dirigat gressus suos. Et Salomon : Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus. Erubescat igitur inimicus gratiæ Dei Pelagius, qui dixit hominem sine gratia posse mereri, justificari, itemque salvari, non obstante quod ait Apostolus : Non sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis quasi ex nobis. Et Christus profitetur : Sicut palmes a semetipso non potest ferre fructum, nisi manserit in vite ; sic nec vos, nisi in me manseritis.
paras.en: [[118:5|O! that my ways may be directed|Utinam, Domine, dirigantur]], O Lord, by thee and by the holy angel through thy grace, [[118:5|my ways|viæ meæ]], that is, the desires, words and works by which man makes his way to the fatherland, [[118:5|to keep thy justifications|ad custodiendas justificationes tuas]], that is, so well and so straightly that thy just and justifying commandments may be observed by me. This, O Lord, I vehemently desire to be done by thee, since I cannot accomplish it by natural power, for (as the Apostle testifies) [[Rom 9:16|it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy|non sit volentis neque currentis, sed Dei miserentis]]. Hence holy Jeremias too says: [[Jer 10:23|I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his: neither is it in a man to walk, and to direct his steps|Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri ut ambulet et dirigat gressus suos]]. And Solomon: [[Prov 16:9|The heart of man disposeth his way: but the Lord must direct his steps|Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus]]. Let Pelagius, then, the enemy of the grace of God, blush for shame, who said that man can merit, be justified and also be saved without grace, notwithstanding what the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 3:5|we are sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves|Non sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid a nobis quasi ex nobis]]. And Christ declares: [[John 15:4|As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abide in the vine, so neither can you, unless you abide in me|Sicut palmes a semetipso non potest ferre fructum, nisi manserit in vite ; sic nec vos, nisi in me manseritis]].

paras.t: Tunc non confundar de negligentia, quum perspexero in omnibus mandatis tuis, id est, quum omnia divina præcepta penetrative lustravero, profunde pensavero, efficaciterque implevero : quia, ut Jacobus in sua testatur Canonica, Qui perspexerit in lege perfectæ libertatis, hic beatus in facto suo erit. Et congrue ait, In omnibus mandatis, quia quicumque totam legem impleverit, offendat autem in uno, factus est omnium reus. Ad quod pertinere videtur illud Ecclesiastæ : Qui in uno peccaverit, multa bona perdet. Ex quo constat, quod in uno delinquens, efficitur omnium reus quantum ad pœnam damni.
paras.en: [[118:6|Then shall I not be confounded|Tunc non confundar]] for negligence, [[118:6|when I shall look into all thy commandments|quum perspexero in omnibus mandatis tuis]], that is, when I shall have searched all the divine precepts penetratingly, weighed them deeply, and fulfilled them effectually: for, as James testifies in his Canonical Epistle, [[Jas 1:25|he that hath looked into the perfect law of liberty|Qui perspexerit in lege perfectæ libertatis]] [[Jas 1:25|this man shall be blessed in his deed|hic beatus in facto suo erit]]. And he fittingly says, [[118:6|all thy commandments|omnibus mandatis]], because [[Jas 2:10|whosoever shall keep the whole law, but offend in one point, is become guilty of all|quicumque totam legem impleverit, offendat autem in uno, factus est omnium reus]]. To this seems to belong that saying of Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 9:18|he that shall offend in one, shall lose many good things|Qui in uno peccaverit, multa bona perdet]]. From which it is clear that he who offends in one point is made guilty of all as regards the pain of loss [that is, the loss of the vision of God, as distinct from the pain of sense].

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, id est, laudabo te, et accusabo me, geminam tibi confessionem, videlicet laudis et culpæ, offerens, in directione cordis, id est, dum tu cor meum ad te ipsum direxeris, vel ego illud ad te per gratiam tuam direxero, in eo, id est per id, quod didici ex revelatione divina, informatione humana, considerationeve propria, judicia justitiæ tuæ, id est justas sententias in Scripturis contentas, secundum quas judicas bonos et malos, reddens singulis quod merentur. Hæc judicia sunt: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum ; et, Venite, benedicti Patris mei ; et, Væ mundo a scandalis. Hæc autem dicendo, gratias agimus Deo pro suæ illuminationis beneficio; compungimur quoque et perterremur de nostris excessibus: sicque confitemur Deo, non solum confessione laudis, sed etiam confessione propriæ iniquitatis.
paras.en: [[118:7|I will praise thee|Confitebor tibi]] [*confitebor*, which means both "I will praise" and "I will confess"], that is, I will praise thee and accuse myself, offering thee a twofold confession, namely of praise and of guilt, [[118:7|with uprightness of heart|in directione cordis]] [*in directione cordis*, literally "in the directing of the heart"], that is, when thou shalt have directed my heart to thyself, or I shall have directed it to thee by thy grace, [[118:7|when|in eo]], that is, by this, [[118:7|I shall have learned|quod didici]] by divine revelation, human instruction or my own consideration, [[118:7|the judgments of thy justice|judicia justitiæ tuæ]], that is, the just sentences contained in the Scriptures, according to which thou judgest the good and the wicked, rendering to each what he deserves. These judgments are: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]]; and: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]]; and: [[Matt 18:7|Woe to the world because of scandals|Væ mundo a scandalis]]. In saying these things we give thanks to God for the benefit of his enlightenment; we are also pricked with compunction and terrified at our own excesses: and so we confess to God, not only by the confession of praise, but also by the confession of our own iniquity.

paras.t: Sed quia utraque confessio exigit obedientiam mandatorum cœlestium, ideo fixe propono, quod Justificationes tuas, id est præcepta tua, custodiam : sicut scriptum est, Qui custodit mandatum, custodit animam suam. Et ut hoc facere valeam, non me derelinquas usquequaque, id est, gratiam tui subsidii non auferas mihi in toto, nec diu suspendas solitam pietatem tuam a me. Imo rogare debemus, ut Deus nullo unquam momento subtrahat nobis habitum caritatis et gratiæ, quia tunc essemus in statu damnationis. Expedit autem nobis quandoque, ut Deus relinquat nos ad tempus, quantum ad aliquos gratiæ actus, auferendo videlicet seu suspendendo consolationem internam, experimentalem devotionem ; quatenus virtus probetur, meritum per patientiam augeatur, anima ab omni superbia præservetur, et propriam fragilitatem homo per experientiam discat; sicque ad Deum recurrat, atque de cetero cautior fiat. Verumtamen nullo momento possumus meritorie operari, aut in bono perseverare sine auxilio Dei.
paras.en: But since each confession demands obedience to the heavenly commandments, I therefore firmly resolve that [[118:8|thy justifications|Justificationes tuas]], that is, thy precepts, [[118:8|I will keep|custodiam]]: as it is written, [[Prov 19:16|He that keepeth the commandment, keepeth his own soul|Qui custodit mandatum, custodit animam suam]]. And that I may be able to do this, [[118:8|O! do not thou utterly forsake me|non me derelinquas usquequaque]], that is, do not take away from me altogether the grace of thy help, nor withhold from me long thy wonted kindness. Indeed we ought to pray that God may never for a single moment withdraw from us the habit of charity and grace, for then we should be in the state of damnation. But it is sometimes expedient for us that God should leave us for a time as regards certain acts of grace, namely by taking away or suspending inward consolation and felt devotion; so that virtue may be proved, merit increased through patience, the soul preserved from all pride, and man may learn his own frailty by experience; and so run back to God, and be more cautious thereafter. Yet at no moment can we act meritoriously, or persevere in good, without the help of God.

paras.t: Precatio. In hujus, Domine, sæculi via fac nos sanctos et immaculatos ambulare in lege tua, mandata tua nimis custodire, et in justificationum tuarum custodia non nos derelinquas usquequaque.
paras.en: Prayer. In the way of this world, O Lord, make us walk holy and undefiled in thy law, and keep thy commandments most diligently; and in the keeping of thy justifications do not thou utterly forsake us.

paras.t: Beth. In quo corrigit adolescentior viam suam? id est, per quid homo juvenis ad passiones proclivus, abstinet ab operatione passionum, ad quas naturaliter inclinatur? Præsertim enim ad iram et concupiscentiam inclinantur adolescentes. Et respondet : In custodiendo sermones tuos, id est, in obediendo sacræ Scripturæ, quæ mala prohibet, damnat et punit; bona vero jubet, laudat atque remunerat. Vere enim a concupiscentia carnis corrigitur adolescens, qui illud Salvatoris bene perpendit: Qui viderit mulierem ad concupiscendum eam, jam mœchatus est eam in corde suo; et, Qui non odit patrem et matrem et uxorem, etc., non potest meus esse discipulus; itemque, Videte ne graventur corda vestra crapula vel ebrietate. Qui etiam audit et sequitur illud sancti Job, Pepigi fœdus cum oculis meis ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine, a concupiscentia emendatur. Similiter sermo Christi ab ira refrenat, dum ait: Qui irascitur fratri suo reus erit judicio; et, Discite a me, quia mitis sum. Hinc etiam Petrus in sua Canonica, Obsecro, inquit, vos tanquam advenas et peregrinos, abstinere vos a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam. Qui autem ista non implet, non putet se pertinere ad Christum, quum Paulus dicat: Qui enim sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis. Et in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Si præstiteris animæ tuæ concupiscentias ejus, facient te in gaudium inimicis tuis.
paras.en: Beth. [[118:9|By what doth a young man correct his way?|In quo corrigit adolescentior viam suam?]] that is, by what means does a young man, prone to the passions, abstain from acting on the passions to which he is naturally inclined? For the young are inclined above all to anger and concupiscence. And he answers: [[118:9|by observing thy words|In custodiendo sermones tuos]], that is, by obeying sacred Scripture, which forbids, condemns and punishes evil things, but commands, praises and rewards good things. For truly the young man is corrected from the concupiscence of the flesh who weighs well that saying of the Saviour: [[Matt 5:28|whosoever shall look on a woman to lust after her, hath already committed adultery with her in his heart|Qui viderit mulierem ad concupiscendum eam, jam mœchatus est eam in corde suo]]; and: [[Luke 14:26|hate not his father and mother and wife|Qui non odit patrem et matrem et uxorem]], etc., [[Luke 14:26|he cannot be my disciple|non potest meus esse discipulus]]; and again: Take heed [[Luke 21:34|lest perhaps your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness|ne graventur corda vestra crapula vel ebrietate]]. He too is amended from concupiscence who hears and follows that saying of holy Job: [[Job 31:1|I made a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin.|Pepigi fœdus cum oculis meis ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine]] Likewise the word of Christ restrains from anger, when he says: [[Matt 5:22|whosoever is angry with his brother, shall be in danger of the judgment|Qui irascitur fratri suo reus erit judicio]]; and: [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek|Discite a me, quia mitis sum]]. Hence also Peter in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 2:11|I beseech you|Obsecro]], he says, [[1 Pet 2:11|as strangers and pilgrims, to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul|vos tanquam advenas et peregrinos, abstinere vos a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam]]. And let him who does not fulfil these things not think that he belongs to Christ, since Paul says: [[Gal 5:24|And they that are Christ's have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences.|Qui enim sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]] And in Ecclesiasticus it is written: [[Ecclus 18:31|If thou give to thy soul her desires, she will make thee a joy to thy enemies.|Si præstiteris animæ tuæ concupiscentias ejus, facient te in gaudium inimicis tuis]]

paras.t: Quum ergo sit ita, idcirco ut ego viam meam per tuorum sermonum custodiam corrigere possim, In toto corde meo, id est intellectu et voluntate; vel, In toto corde meo, id est corde totaliter ad te converso, ita quod a rebus illicitis prorsus aversum est; exquisivi te tanquam summum bonum, cui finaliter adhærere intendo et cupio. Non ergo quæramus Deum corde diviso aut duplici, quia pro quanta parte aliud quærimus, Deum non quærimus. Unde de quibusdam scriptum est: Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt; et, Ne accesseris ad Deum duplici corde. Ne repellas me a mandatis tuis, id est, ne dimittas me a propriis vitiis et passionibus superari, ac per hoc a tuorum observatione mandatorum elongari, sed precem meam admitte, meque divina jussa adimplere concede. Hoc est quod oramus: Domine, noli me reprobare a pueris tuis; et, Domine, pater et dominator vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in cogitatu et consilio malorum.
paras.en: Since this is so, therefore, that I may be able to correct my way by keeping thy words, [[118:10|With my whole heart|In toto corde meo]], that is, with intellect and will; or, [[118:10|With my whole heart|In toto corde meo]], that is, with a heart wholly turned to thee, so that it is utterly turned away from unlawful things, [[118:10|have I sought after thee|exquisivi te]] as the supreme good, to whom I intend and desire to cleave finally. Let us not, then, seek God with a divided or double heart, for in so far as we seek something else, we do not seek God. Hence it is written of some: [[Osee 10:2|Their heart is divided: now they shall perish|Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt]]; and: [[Ecclus 1:36|come not to him with a double heart|Ne accesseris ad Deum duplici corde]] [Denis has "to God"; the margin gives no reference for this]. [[118:10|let me not stray from thy commandments|Ne repellas me a mandatis tuis]] [literally "do not thrust me away from thy commandments"], that is, do not let me be overcome by my own vices and passions, and thereby be taken far from the observance of thy commandments, but admit my prayer, and grant me to fulfil the divine commands. This is what we pray: Lord, [[Wis 9:4|cast me not off from among thy children|noli me reprobare a pueris tuis]]; and: [[Ecclus 23:1|O Lord, father, and sovereign ruler of my life|Domine, pater et dominator vitæ meæ]], leave me not in the thought and counsel of the wicked.

paras.t: In corde meo abscondi, id est, memoriter tenui, eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi, id est ad injuriam tuam. Sacra enim eloquia edocent quid agendum, quid omittendum, ne Dominus offendatur. Et ideo Christus ait: Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei, et custodiunt illud. Sed videtur contrarium quod dictum est ante: Non abscondi misericordiam tuam et veritatem tuam a concilio multo. Et respondendum, quod absconsio sacri eloquii duplex est. Una, per quam non communicatur proximo fraterna instructio: et ista est vitiosa, juxta illud: Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque? Alia ergo est absconsio, quæ oblivionem excludit: et de illa nunc loquitur.
paras.en: [[118:11|have I hidden in my heart|In corde meo abscondi]], that is, I have held in memory, [[118:11|Thy words|eloquia tua]], [[118:11|that I may not sin against thee|ut non peccem tibi]], that is, to thy injury. For the sacred words teach what is to be done and what left undone, lest the Lord be offended. And therefore Christ says: [[Luke 11:28|blessed are they who hear the word of God and keep it|Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei, et custodiunt illud]]. But what was said earlier [in Psalm 39] seems contrary: [[Ps 39:11|I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth from a great council|Non abscondi misericordiam tuam et veritatem tuam a concilio multo]]. The answer is that the hiding of the sacred word is twofold. One, by which brotherly instruction is not shared with one's neighbour: and this is vicious, according to that saying: [[Ecclus 41:17|wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is there in them both?|Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?]] [the same words stand in Ecclus 20:32]. The other is the hiding that shuts out forgetfulness: and of that he is speaking here.

paras.t: Benedictus es, Domine, in te ipso propter sanctitatem tuæ naturæ, doce me justificationes tuas, id est mandata divina: quatenus ea non solum habitualiter, sed etiam actualiter sciam et impleam.
paras.en: [[118:12|Blessed art thou, O Lord|Benedictus es, Domine]], in thyself, because of the holiness of thy nature: [[118:12|teach me thy justifications|doce me justificationes tuas]], that is, the divine commandments, so that I may know and fulfil them not only habitually but also actually.

paras.t: In labiis meis pronuntiavi, aliis prædicando, vel apud me proferendo, omnia judicia oris tui, id est omnes sermones justitiæ tuæ in Scripturis contentos: omnia, inquam, in genere aut in specie, commemorando sententias tuas, quibus impii condemnantur, et boni salvantur. Et quamvis (secundum Apostolum) judicia Dei incomprehensibilia sint, illa præsertim, quibus nonnulli ab æterno electi sunt et alii reprobati; possunt tamen pronuntiari, sicut quum illud mirabile Dei judicium proferimus conscriptum: Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui.
paras.en: [[118:13|With my lips I have pronounced|In labiis meis pronuntiavi]], by preaching to others, or by uttering them to myself, [[118:13|all the judgments of thy mouth|omnia judicia oris tui]], that is, all the words of thy justice contained in the Scriptures: *all*, I say, in general or in particular, by recalling thy sentences by which the wicked are condemned and the good are saved. And although (according to the Apostle) the judgments of God are incomprehensible[[Rom 11:33||]], those above all by which some have been chosen from eternity and others reprobated, yet they can be pronounced, as when we utter that wonderful judgment of God that is written: [[Rom 9:13|Jacob I have loved: but Esau I have hated|Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui]].

paras.t: In via, id est in observatione et contemplatione, testimoniorum tuorum, id est sermonum sacræ Scripturæ, delectatus sum, sicut in omnibus divitiis, id est tam cordialiter et exuberanter, sicut avari in temporalibus bonis lætantur, ita quod corde jucundo et amoroso legi, audivi seu protuli verba sacræ Scripturæ : ut sunt, Beati pauperes spiritu, Beati misericordes, Beati mites, Beati qui lugent ; et, Qui se humiliat, exaltabitur.
paras.en: [[118:14|in the way|In via]], that is, in the observance and contemplation, [[118:14|of thy testimonies|testimoniorum tuorum]], that is, of the words of sacred Scripture, [[118:14|I have been delighted|delectatus sum]], [[118:14|as in all riches|sicut in omnibus divitiis]], that is, as heartily and abundantly as the avaricious rejoice in temporal goods; so that with a joyful and loving heart I have read, heard or uttered the words of sacred Scripture, such as: [[Matt 5:3|Blessed are the poor in spirit|Beati pauperes spiritu]], [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful|Beati misericordes]], [[Matt 5:4|Blessed are the meek|Beati mites]], [[Matt 5:5|Blessed are they that mourn|Beati qui lugent]]; and: [[Luke 14:11|he that humbleth himself shall be exalted|Qui se humiliat, exaltabitur]].

paras.t: In mandatis tuis exercebor, frequenter ea recogitando, atque fideliter exsequendo ; et considerabo vias tuas, id est opera et exempla eorum qui tibi placuerunt, per quæ venitur ad te ; vel, Vias tuas, id est operationes tuas quas exerces in nobis, quatenus sicut tu pluis super justos et impios, sic adversariis meis benefacere discam ; vel, Vias tuas, id est æquitatem atque clementiam tuam : de quibus prædictum est, Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas.
paras.en: [[118:15|I will meditate on thy commandments|In mandatis tuis exercebor]] [*exercebor*, literally "I will be exercised"], by often thinking them over and faithfully carrying them out; [[118:15|and I will consider thy ways|et considerabo vias tuas]], that is, the works and examples of those who have pleased thee, by which one comes to thee; or, [[118:15|thy ways|Vias tuas]], that is, thy works which thou workest in us, so that, as thou rainest upon the just and the wicked[[Matt 5:45||]] [the margin gives Matth. v, 15], so I may learn to do good to my adversaries; or, [[118:15|thy ways|Vias tuas]], that is, thy equity and clemency: of which it was said before: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]].

paras.t: In justificationibus tuis, id est in præceptis tuis justificantibus observantes, meditabor : prout in exordio libri habetur, In lege Domini voluntas ejus, et in lege ejus meditabitur die ac nocte: non obliviscar sermones tuos, sed implere conabor illud Moysis : Erunt verba Domini in corde tuo, et narrabis ea filiis tuis, et meditaberis sedens in domo tua et ambulans in itinere, et dormiens atque consurgens ; et ligabis ea quasi signum in manu tua, eruntque et movebuntur inter oculos tuos; scribesque ea in limine et ostiis domus tuæ. Unde ut incessanter recolerent filii Israel divina præcepta, jussit eis Deus, ut facerent sibi fimbrias quatuor, per quatuor angulos palliorum, ponentes in eis vittas hyacinthinas, quas quum viderent, recordarentur omnium mandatorum Dei, nec sequerentur cogitationes et oculos per res varias fornicantes.
paras.en: [[118:16|thy justifications|In justificationibus tuis]], that is, in thy justifying precepts, observing them, [[118:16|I will think of|meditabor]] [*meditabor*, literally "I will meditate"]: as is found at the opening of the book: [[Ps 1:2|his will is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he shall meditate day and night|In lege Domini voluntas ejus, et in lege ejus meditabitur die ac nocte]]: [[118:16|I will not forget thy words|non obliviscar sermones tuos]], but will endeavour to fulfil that saying of Moses: The words of the Lord [[Deut 6:6|shall be in thy heart|Erunt verba Domini in corde tuo]], [[Deut 6:7|thou shalt tell them to thy children, and thou shalt meditate upon them sitting in thy house, and walking on thy journey, sleeping and rising|narrabis ea filiis tuis, et meditaberis sedens in domo tua et ambulans in itinere, et dormiens atque consurgens]]; [[Deut 6:8|thou shalt bind them as a sign on thy hand, and they shall be and shall move between thy eyes|ligabis ea quasi signum in manu tua, eruntque et movebuntur inter oculos tuos]]; [[Deut 6:9|thou shalt write them in the entry, and on the doors of thy house|scribesque ea in limine et ostiis domus tuæ]]. Hence, so that the children of Israel might unceasingly call the divine precepts to mind, God commanded them to make themselves four fringes at the four corners of their cloaks, putting in them ribands of blue[[Num 15:38||]], so that when they saw them they might remember all the commandments of God, and not follow their thoughts and eyes going astray after divers things[[Num 15:39||]].

paras.t: Precatio. In servitio tuo constitutos, Domine, fac nos te toto corde exquirere, et in mandatis tuis viriliter exerceri : ut consideratis viis tuis, et te docente intellectis, semper sicut in omnibus divitiis delectemur in illis.
paras.en: Prayer. Make us, O Lord, who are set in thy service, seek thee with our whole heart, and be manfully exercised in thy commandments: that, having considered thy ways and understood them by thy teaching, we may ever delight in them as in all riches.

paras.t: Ghimel. Retribue servo tuo, videlicet mihi atque universo Christianorum conventui, quod peccando amisi, vel per omissionem promereri neglexi, videlicet gratiam ; vivifica me spiritualiter vita gratiæ: nam sicut anima vivificat carnem, sic gratia animam ; et custodiam sermones tuos, id est, jussa tua implebo, confortatus ope luceque gratiæ, quæ sine hac gratia meritorie nequeo adimplere.
paras.en: Ghimel. [[118:17|Give bountifully to thy servant|Retribue servo tuo]], that is, to me and to the whole assembly of Christians, what I lost by sinning or neglected to merit by omission, namely grace [the Latin *retribue* means "give back", "repay": Denis takes it as restoring what was lost]; [[118:17|enliven me|vivifica me]] spiritually with the life of grace: for as the soul gives life to the flesh, so grace gives life to the soul; [[118:17|and I shall keep thy words|et custodiam sermones tuos]], that is, I shall fulfil thy commands, strengthened by the help and light of grace: commands which without this grace I cannot fulfil meritoriously.

paras.t: Revela oculos meos (haud dubium quin interiores), id est, intellectum meum speculativum et practicum, rationem superiorem et inferiorem, doce atque clarifica per dona sapientiæ, scientiæ, intellectus atque consilii, per illuminationem quoque angelicam et instructionem humanam ; et considerabo, illuminatus a te, mirabilia de lege tua, id est incomprehensibilia testimonia, supernaturales articulos fidei, alia quoque in utroque Testamento contenta mysteria : quæ sine illuminatione divina considerari sincere non valent ; imo multi infelices hæretici præsumentes talia naturali lumine considerare ac mensurare, sectas æternæ perditionis introduxerunt. Hos oculos revelari optabat Apostolus suis discipulis, dum ait : Pater gloriæ det vobis spiritum sapientiæ in agnitione ejus, illuminatos oculos cordis vestri, ut sciatis quæ sit spes vocationis vestræ.
paras.en: [[118:18|Open thou my eyes|Revela oculos meos]] (the inward eyes, no doubt), that is, teach and enlighten my understanding, speculative and practical, my higher and lower reason [the higher reason looks to eternal things, the lower to temporal ones], through the gifts of wisdom, knowledge, understanding and counsel, and also through the enlightening of the angels and the teaching of men; [[118:18|and I will consider|et considerabo]], enlightened by thee, [[118:18|the wondrous things of thy law|mirabilia de lege tua]], that is, the incomprehensible testimonies, the supernatural articles of faith, and the other mysteries contained in both Testaments, which cannot be rightly considered without divine enlightenment; indeed many unhappy heretics, presuming to consider and measure such things by natural light, have brought in sects of eternal perdition. The Apostle wished these eyes to be opened for his disciples when he says: [[Eph 1:17|the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom|Pater gloriæ det vobis spiritum sapientiæ]] [[Eph 1:17|in the knowledge of him|in agnitione ejus]], [[Eph 1:18|The eyes of your heart enlightened that you may know what the hope is|illuminatos oculos cordis vestri, ut sciatis quæ sit spes]] of your calling [Denis reads *vocationis vestræ*, "your calling"; the Vulgate has "his calling"].

paras.t: Indigeo autem, o Domine, revelatione prædicta : nam Incola ego sum in terra, id est viator, non comprehensor sicut incolæ cœli, sed peregrinus et advena. Idcirco per fidem, non per speciem, ambulo : quoniam (teste Apostolo) quamdiu sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino ; videmusque per speculum in ænigmate, cognoscentes ex parte. Propterea indesinenter divina illustratione indigeo, quia corpus quod corrumpitur, aggravat animam, et cogitationes mortalium sunt timidæ, et incertæ providentiæ nostræ. Non abscondas a me mandata tua, sed doce me ea, vitiorum caliginem, mandatorum agnitionem obtenebrantem, auferendo a me, et gratiæ lumen ita augendo in anima mea, ut nulla occupatio eam impediat a divinorum memoria mandatorum.
paras.en: But I need, O Lord, the revelation spoken of: for [[118:19|I am a sojourner on the earth|Incola ego sum in terra]], that is, a wayfarer, not a comprehensor [that is, one who already possesses God in the vision of glory] like the dwellers of heaven, but a pilgrim and a stranger [*incola* means both "sojourner" and "dweller": hence the contrast with the *incolæ cœli*, the dwellers of heaven]. Therefore I walk by faith, not by sight: since (as the Apostle testifies) [[2 Cor 5:6|while we are in the body we are absent from the Lord|quamdiu sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino]]; and [[1 Cor 13:12|We see now through a glass in a dark manner|videmusque per speculum in ænigmate]], [[1 Cor 13:12|know in part|cognoscentes ex parte]]. Therefore I need divine enlightening without ceasing, because [[Wis 9:15|the corruptible body is a load upon the soul|corpus quod corrumpitur, aggravat animam]], and [[Wis 9:14|the thoughts of mortal men are fearful, and our counsels uncertain|cogitationes mortalium sunt timidæ, et incertæ providentiæ nostræ]]; [[118:19|hide not thy commandments from me|Non abscondas a me mandata tua]], but teach them to me, taking from me the darkness of vices that clouds the knowledge of the commandments, and so increasing the light of grace in my soul that no business may keep it from the remembrance of the divine commandments.

paras.t: Concupivit anima mea desiderare justificationes tuas : id est, anima mea, quæ adhuc imperfecte ac tepide concupiscit tua mandata, seu mandatorum operationes, desiderat ea ardenter atque perfecte concupiscere. Sicut enim intellectus, sic et voluntas supra proprium actum reflectitur. Ideo, sicut anima per intellectum intelligit se intelligere, actusque sui imperfectionem cognoscit, atque perfectiorem notitiam cupit ; sic anima per voluntatem suam intellectualem concupiscentiam cupit et vult, ejusque incomplementum experitur, et desiderium magis completum adipisci molitur : quoniam tam intellectus quam voluntas, ex imperfecto ad perfectionem progreditur. Concupiscit autem anima mea desiderare justificationes divinas, id est opera justa quibus justificetur, non qualitercumque, sed in omni tempore, quatenus perseveret in sancto affectu : non quod singulis horis valeat actualiter desiderare hujusmodi, sed ut debitis, certis et congruis horis omnium temporum, eas desideret : juxta quem modum dicit Apostolus, Sine intermissione orate. Debemus tamen indesinenter hæc bona desiderare actu vel habitu.
paras.en: [[118:20|My soul hath coveted to long for thy justifications|Concupivit anima mea desiderare justificationes tuas]]: that is, my soul, which as yet covets thy commandments, or the doing of the commandments, imperfectly and lukewarmly, longs to covet them ardently and perfectly. For the will, like the understanding, turns back upon its own act. So, just as the soul through the understanding understands that it understands, knows the imperfection of its act, and desires a more perfect knowledge, so the soul through its will desires and wills its intellectual desire [that is, the desire of the will, the appetite that follows the intellect], feels its incompleteness, and strives to attain a more complete desire: since both understanding and will progress from the imperfect to perfection. Now my soul covets to long for the divine justifications, that is, the just works by which it may be justified, not in any way whatever, but [[118:20|at all times|in omni tempore]], so that it may persevere in holy affection: not that it can actually long for such things every single hour, but that it may long for them at the due, fixed and fitting hours of all times; in the way in which the Apostle says, [[1 Thess 5:17|Pray without ceasing|Sine intermissione orate]]. Yet we ought to long for these goods without ceasing, in act or in habit.

paras.t: Increpasti superbos. In sacra Scriptura frequenter reprehenduntur omnes superbi : sicut quum in Ecclesiastico dicitur : Quid superbit terra et cinis? et alibi : Omnis qui se exaltat, humiliabitur ; et, Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam. Denique angelos superbientes in cælo Deus increpavit, dum eos e cælo in aerem caliginosum dejecit ac inferum, quemadmodum scriptum est : Angelos qui non servaverunt suum principatum, sed dereliquerunt suum domicilium, in judicium magni diei, vinculis æternis sub caligine reservavit. Et Petrus ait : Deus angelis peccantibus non pepercit, sed rudentibus inferni detractos in tartarum, tradidit in judicium cruciandos reservari. Protoplastos quoque nostros parentes, in paradiso superbientes, Deus increpavit et expulit.
paras.en: [[118:21|Thou hast rebuked the proud|Increpasti superbos]]. In sacred Scripture all the proud are often reproved: as when it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:9|Why is earth, and ashes proud?|Quid superbit terra et cinis?]] and elsewhere: [[Luke 18:14|every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled|Omnis qui se exaltat, humiliabitur]]; and, [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble|Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]]. Lastly, God rebuked the angels who grew proud in heaven, when he cast them down from heaven into the dark air and into hell, as it is written: [[Jude 1:6|the angels who kept not their principality but forsook their own habitation, he hath reserved under darkness in everlasting chains, unto the judgment of the great day|Angelos qui non servaverunt suum principatum, sed dereliquerunt suum domicilium, in judicium magni diei, vinculis æternis sub caligine reservavit]]. And Peter says: [[2 Pet 2:4|God spared not the angels that sinned, but delivered them, drawn down by infernal ropes to the lower hell, unto torments, to be reserved unto judgment|Deus angelis peccantibus non pepercit, sed rudentibus inferni detractos in tartarum, tradidit in judicium cruciandos reservari]]. Our first-formed parents too, when they grew proud in paradise, God rebuked[[Gen 3:9||]] and drove out[[Gen 3:24||]].

paras.t: Maledicti, id est, a Deo vituperati, æternaliterque damnati sunt, qui declinant finaliter a mandatis tuis, ea non observando : non enim quis potest salvari aut benedici, nisi custodiendo præcepta Dei excelsi. Angeli quoque superbi æternaliter maledicti sunt, prout Dominus ait principi eorum : Repleta sunt interiora tua iniquitate, et ejeci te de monte sancto Dei, et perdidi te, o Cherub protegens, de medio lapidum ignitorum. Primi quoque parentes temporaliter maledicti fuerunt, certis pœnis atque miseriis in præsenti vita adjudicati, quemadmodum in Genesi legitur.
paras.en: [[118:21|they are cursed|Maledicti]], that is, reproved by God and eternally damned, [[118:21|who decline|qui declinant]] finally [[118:21|from thy commandments|a mandatis tuis]], by not keeping them: for no one can be saved or blessed except by keeping the precepts of God most high. The proud angels too are eternally cursed, as the Lord says to their prince: [[Ezech 28:16|thy inner parts were filled with iniquity|Repleta sunt interiora tua iniquitate]], [[Ezech 28:16|and I cast thee out from the mountain of God, and destroyed thee, O covering cherub, out of the midst of the stones of fire|et ejeci te de monte sancto Dei, et perdidi te, o Cherub protegens, de medio lapidum ignitorum]]. Our first parents too were cursed in time, being sentenced to certain pains and miseries in this present life, as we read in Genesis[[Gen 3:16||]].

paras.t: Aufer a me opprobrium et contemptum. Hoc tripliciter intelligi potest : Primo, de opprobrio et contemptu activis, ut sit sensus : Da ut ego nulli opprobrium inferam, nec aliquem spernam : quoniam magnum malum est hoc, et æternæ damnationis meritorium, juxta illud : Væ qui prædaris, nonne et ipse prædaberis? et qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris? quum fatigatus desieris contemnere, contemneris. Et : Numquid non pater unus est omnium nostrum? numquid non Deus unus creavit nos? Quare ergo despicit unusquisque nostrum fratrem suum, violans pactum patrum nostrorum? Secundo exponitur de opprobrio et contemptu passivis, quæ petimus nobis auferri : [non quidem] ut non exprobremur et contemnamur ab aliquo, præsertim dum promeremur, aut propter justitiam, quum sanctus Petrus dicat, Si exprobramini in nomine Christi, beati eritis ; sed ne per impatientiam superemur in talibus. Dum enim patienter sustinemus, auferuntur a nobis, quantum ad nocumentum, imo tunc multum proficiunt ad coronam. Tertio sic : Aufer a me opprobrium maledictionis, qua maledicuntur superbi et inobedientes, et contemptum transgressionis, ne mihi dicatur quod dictum est Sauli, Quare contempsisti verbum Domini? Quia testimonia tua, id est sacra eloquia a te testificata, et multipliciter confirmata, exquisivi ad cognoscendum et operandum. Idcirco congruit te exaudire me.
paras.en: [[118:22|Remove from me reproach and contempt|Aufer a me opprobrium et contemptum]]. This can be understood in three ways. First, of reproach and contempt in the active sense, so that the sense is: Grant that I may bring reproach on no one and despise no one: for this is a great evil and deserves eternal damnation, according to that saying: [[Is 33:1|Woe to thee that spoilest, shalt not thou thyself also be spoiled? and thou that despisest, shalt not thyself also be despised?|Væ qui prædaris, nonne et ipse prædaberis? et qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris?]] [[Is 33:1|when being wearied thou shalt cease to despise, thou shalt be despised|quum fatigatus desieris contemnere, contemneris]]. And: [[Mal 2:10|Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us? why then doth every one of us despise his brother, violating the covenant of our fathers?|Numquid non pater unus est omnium nostrum? numquid non Deus unus creavit nos? Quare ergo despicit unusquisque nostrum fratrem suum, violans pactum patrum nostrorum?]] Secondly it is explained of reproach and contempt in the passive sense, which we ask to have taken from us: not indeed that we should not be reproached and despised by anyone, especially when we deserve it, or for justice' sake, since Saint Peter says, [[1 Pet 4:14|If you be reproached for the name of Christ, you shall be blessed|Si exprobramini in nomine Christi, beati eritis]]; but that we may not be overcome by impatience in such things. For while we bear them patiently, they are taken from us as far as harm goes; indeed they then do much toward the crown. Thirdly thus: Remove from me the reproach of the curse with which the proud and disobedient are cursed, and the contempt of transgression, lest there be said to me what was said to Saul [so the text; the margin corrects it to David, to whom Nathan spoke these words], [[2 Kings 12:9|Why therefore hast thou despised the word of the Lord|Quare contempsisti verbum Domini]]? [[118:22|Because|Quia]] [[118:22|thy testimonies|testimonia tua]], that is, the sacred words testified by thee and confirmed in many ways, [[118:22|I have sought after|exquisivi]], so as to know and do them. Therefore it is fitting that thou hear me.

paras.t: Etenim sederunt principes, et adversum me loquebantur. Contra martyres Christi et alios justos, sæpe sederunt ac sedent principes mundi, homines impii, in conciliis atque judiciis adversus eos loquentes, et de eorum morte aut persecutione tractantes. Denique contra nos omnes sedent, id est, parati manent principes, hoc est dæmones. De quibus dicit Apostolus : Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates, contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus. Et adversum me loquebantur. Nam inter se tractant, et suo modo loquuntur, quo genere tentationis unumquemque dejiciant. Singulorum namque mores et studia curiose explorant, et ibi quærunt nocumentum inferre, ubi quempiam viderint studiosius occupari ; de his quoque vitiis unumquemque tentare conantur, ad quæ viderint eum procliviorem. Nec mirum si contra nos taliter sedent et machinantur, quum Christus de uno horum professus sit : Venit enim princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam. Servus autem tuus in tali oppugnatione exercebatur, id est, mente et opere occupabatur, in justificationibus tuis, id est in divinis præceptis. Una enim occupatio expellit aut minuit aliam, maxime si intendatur. Idcirco debemus tanto vehementius in divinis occupari, meditando, orando, psallendo, scribendo, aut alia opera bona patrando, quanto videmus nos gravius tentari : sic enim tentatio minus sentitur. Otium vero maxime roborat adversarii potestatem.
paras.en: [[118:23|For princes sat, and spoke against me|Etenim sederunt principes, et adversum me loquebantur]]. Against the martyrs of Christ and other just men the princes of the world, ungodly men, have often sat and still sit in councils and courts, speaking against them and debating their death or persecution. Lastly, against all of us the princes sit, that is, stand ready: the princes, that is, the demons. Of these the Apostle says: [[Eph 6:12|our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and powers|Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates]], [[Eph 6:12|against the spirits of wickedness in the high places|contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus]]. [[118:23|And spoke against me|Et adversum me loquebantur]]: for they discuss among themselves, and speak in their own way, by what kind of temptation they may cast down each one. For they inquisitively search out the habits and pursuits of each, and seek to do harm where they see someone more eagerly occupied; and they try to tempt each one with those vices to which they see him more inclined. No wonder if they sit and plot against us in this way, since Christ declared of one of them: [[John 14:30|For the prince of this world: cometh: and in me he hath not any thing|Venit enim princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam]]. [[118:23|But thy servant|Servus autem tuus]], in such an assault, [[118:23|was employed|exercebatur]], that is, was busied in mind and work, [[118:23|in thy justifications|in justificationibus tuis]], that is, in the divine precepts. For one occupation drives out or lessens another, especially if it is pursued intently. Therefore we ought to busy ourselves in divine things, meditating, praying, singing psalms, writing, or doing other good works, the more earnestly the more heavily we see ourselves tempted: for so the temptation is felt less. But idleness most of all strengthens the adversary's power.

paras.t: Nam et testimonia tua meditatio mea est, non essentialiter, sed materialiter, quia testimonia tua continue meditor, aliaque cogitare detestor ; et consilium meum sunt justificationes tuæ, id est mandata, ita quod totum consilium meum versatur et ordinatur ad hoc, ut præcepta tua observem. Talis erat venerabilis illa Sara, quæ ait : Nunquam cum ludentibus miscui me, neque cum his qui in levitate ambulant, participem me præbui.
paras.en: [[118:24|For thy testimonies are my meditation|Nam et testimonia tua meditatio mea est]], not in essence but in matter [that is, the testimonies are not the act of meditating itself but what it is about], since I meditate continually on thy testimonies and loathe to think of other things; [[118:24|and thy justifications my counsel|et consilium meum sunt justificationes tuæ]], that is, thy commandments, so that all my counsel turns on this and is ordered to it, that I may keep thy precepts. Such was that venerable Sara, who says: [[Tob 3:17|Never have I joined myself with them that play: neither have I made myself partaker with them that walk in lightness.|Nunquam cum ludentibus miscui me, neque cum his qui in levitate ambulant, participem me præbui]]

paras.t: Precatio. Bonorum omnium largitor, Domine, fac nos desiderare justificationes tuas in omni tempore, et in eis bene operando perseverare ; aufer a nobis opprobrium inimici et contemptum, et da nos perpetim de manu tua accipere decoris et honoris regnum.
paras.en: Prayer. Giver of all good things, O Lord, make us long for thy justifications at all times, and persevere in them by working well; take from us the reproach and contempt of the enemy, and grant us to receive for ever from thy hand the kingdom of beauty and honour.

paras.t: Daleth. Adhæsit pavimento anima mea, id est, corpori gravi, terreno et corruptibili conjuncta est anima mea tanquam forma substantialis atque intrinseca : idcirco frequenter a bonis operibus impeditur, quoniam deprimit terrena inhabitatio sensum multa cogitantem. Frequenter quoque adhæsit anima mea per consensum illicitum pavimento huic, sequendo concupiscentias ejus. Contra quod in Ecclesiastico dicitur : Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere. Itaque captiva ducta est anima mea in legem peccati, quæ regnat in membris meis. De qua dicit Apostolus : Video aliam legem in membris meis, repugnantem legi mentis meæ. Unde cum sancto Apostolo exclamare compellor : Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus, id est de vitiis, defectibus, et concupiscentiis, seu impedimentis hujus mortalis corporis? Et respondet : Gratia Dei per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum. Nunc enim per gratiam Dei minuuntur et alleviantur prædicta mala, quæ animæ accidunt ex corporis conjunctione. In resurrectione vero futura penitus auferentur, quia tunc corpora erunt omnino animabus sanctis subjecta, proportionata, et assimilata, secundum quod ad Romanos inducitur : Ipsa creatura liberabitur a servitute corruptionis, in libertatem gloriæ filiorum Dei.
paras.en: Daleth. [[118:25|My soul hath cleaved to the pavement|Adhæsit pavimento anima mea]], that is, my soul is joined to a heavy, earthly and corruptible body as its substantial and intrinsic form [that is, the soul is not merely lodged in the body but is what makes it a living human body]: therefore it is often hindered from good works, since [[Wis 9:15|the earthly habitation presseth down the mind that museth upon many things|deprimit terrena inhabitatio sensum multa cogitantem]]. Often too my soul has cleaved to this pavement by unlawful consent, following its lusts. Against which it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 18:30|Go not after thy lusts, but turn away from thy own will.|Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere]] And so my soul has been led captive into the law of sin which reigns in my members. Of this the Apostle says: [[Rom 7:23|I see another law in my members, fighting against the law of my mind|Video aliam legem in membris meis, repugnantem legi mentis meæ]]. Whence I am driven to cry out with the holy Apostle: [[Rom 7:24|Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me|Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit]] [[Rom 7:24|from the body of this death|de corpore mortis hujus]], that is, from the vices, defects and lusts, or hindrances, of this mortal body? And he answers: [[Rom 7:25|The grace of God, by Jesus Christ our Lord|Gratia Dei per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]]. For now through the grace of God the evils spoken of, which befall the soul from its union with the body, are lessened and lightened; but in the resurrection to come they will be wholly taken away, since then bodies will be altogether subject, proportioned and likened to holy souls, as is brought forward in Romans: [[Rom 8:21|the creature also itself shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption, into the liberty of the glory of the children of God|Ipsa creatura liberabitur a servitute corruptionis, in libertatem gloriæ filiorum Dei]].

paras.t: Idcirco nunc subditur : vivifica me per gratiæ infusionem, operumque bonorum promptam ac vividam exsecutionem, ne inferioribus istis adhæream, sed toto affectu cœlestia quæram, et in carne vivens, non secundum carnem ambulem, quatenus cum Apostolo valeam profiteri: Nostra autem conversatio in cœlis est. Vivifica autem me secundum verbum tuum, quo in sacra Scriptura promittis te exauditurum precantem, et ei gratiam omnem quam postulat, infusurum, prout scriptum est: Omnia quæcumque orantes petitis, credite quia accipietis, et evenient vobis. Vel, Secundum verbum tuum, quod in Deuteronomio conscriptum est, quo dicitur: Non in solo pane vivit homo, sed in omni verbo quod egreditur de ore Domini.
paras.en: Therefore it now adds: [[118:25|quicken thou me|vivifica me]] by the infusion of grace and by a ready and lively doing of good works, that I may not cleave to these lower things, but seek heavenly things with all my affection, and, living in the flesh, may not walk according to the flesh, so that with the Apostle I may be able to profess: [[Phil 3:20|But our conversation is in heaven|Nostra autem conversatio in cœlis est]]. Now [[118:25|quicken thou me|Vivifica autem me]] [[118:25|according to thy word|secundum verbum tuum]], by which in sacred Scripture thou promisest to hear the one who prays and to pour into him every grace he asks, as it is written: [[Mark 11:24|all things, whatsoever you ask when ye pray, believe that you shall receive: and they shall come unto you|Omnia quæcumque orantes petitis, credite quia accipietis, et evenient vobis]]. Or, [[118:25|according to thy word|Secundum verbum tuum]] which is written in Deuteronomy, where it is said: [[Deut 8:3|not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God|Non in solo pane vivit homo, sed in omni verbo quod egreditur de ore Domini]][[Matt 4:4||]].

paras.t: Vias meas, id est operationes meas interiores et exteriores, enuntiavi tibi omnia cognoscenti, vel tuo vicario sacerdoti, confitendo humiliter imperfectum meum et culpas, omneque bonum tibi totaliter adscribendo, et exaudisti me, indulgentiam largiendo, gratiamque præstando. Unde de Job dicit: Vias meas in conspectu ejus arguam, et ipse erit salvator meus. Superius quoque: Revela Domino viam tuam, et spera in eo, et ipse faciet. Doce me justificationes tuas, id est mandata, ut ea salubriter, non inaniter, sciam et impleam.
paras.en: [[118:26|My ways|Vias meas]], that is, my inward and outward workings, [[118:26|I have declared|enuntiavi]] to thee who knowest all things, or to thy vicar the priest, humbly confessing my imperfection and my faults, and ascribing every good wholly to thee; [[118:26|and thou hast heard me|et exaudisti me]], granting pardon and bestowing grace. Hence Job says: [[Job 13:15|I will reprove my ways in his sight|Vias meas in conspectu ejus arguam]], [[Job 13:16|and he shall be my saviour|et ipse erit salvator meus]]. And above: [[Ps 36:5|Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, and he will do it.|Revela Domino viam tuam, et spera in eo, et ipse faciet]] [*Revela*: literally "reveal", "lay open", the same verb as in "Open thou my eyes", v. 18] [[118:26|Teach me thy justifications|Doce me justificationes tuas]], that is, thy commandments, so that I may know and fulfil them to my salvation, not in vain.

paras.t: Viam, id est processum et ordinem, justificationum tuarum instrue me, ut sciam quæ mandata sint prima atque præcipua, quæ necesse est primo principaliterque impleri. Hæc enim sunt duo caritatis præcepta, in quibus alia virtualiter continentur. Et exercebor in mirabilibus tuis. Hoc est quod paulo ante induxit: Considerabo mirabilia de lege tua. Quid itaque est, in mirabilibus Dei exerceri? nisi oculo illuminato contemplari humiliter atque subtiliter incomprehensibilia testimonia fidei christianæ, videlicet qualiter Deus sanctus et gloriosus, quamvis sit unus summeque simplex in essentia, verissime tamen trinus est in personis; et quod ex ineffabili Trinitatis consilio incarnatus est Filius Dei propter nostram reparandam salutem, quod Mater ejus virgo permansit, cetera quoque Christi mysteria contemplari; considerare etiam, quam terribilis sit Deus in consiliis super filios hominum, quanta suavitas ejus circa electos, quanta severitas ad reprobos.
paras.en: [[118:27|Make me to understand|instrue me]] [[118:27|the way|Viam]], that is, the course and order, [[118:27|of thy justifications|justificationum tuarum]], so that I may know which commandments are first and chief, which must be fulfilled first and principally. For these are the two precepts of charity, in which the others are virtually contained [that is, contained in their power, as conclusions in their principles]. [[118:27|And I shall be exercised in thy wondrous works|Et exercebor in mirabilibus tuis]]. This is what he brought in a little before: [[118:18|I will consider the wondrous things of thy law|Considerabo mirabilia de lege tua]]. What then is it to be exercised in the wonders of God, but with enlightened eye to contemplate humbly and keenly the incomprehensible testimonies of the Christian faith: namely how God, holy and glorious, though he is one and supremely simple in essence, is yet most truly three in persons; and that by the ineffable counsel of the Trinity the Son of God became incarnate to restore our salvation; that his Mother remained a virgin; and to contemplate the other mysteries of Christ too; and also to consider how God is [[Ps 65:5|terrible in his counsels over the sons of men|terribilis sit Deus in consiliis super filios hominum]], how great is his sweetness toward the elect, how great his severity toward the reprobate?

paras.t: Dormitavit anima mea præ tædio. Dormire, proprie convenit pigro, juxta illud: Pigredo immittit soporem. Et iterum Salomon ait: Usquequo, piger, dormies? Dormitare autem, convenit fatigato seu lasso. Anima vero gravatur atque lassatur sarcina corporis, propter varias necessitudines ejus. Anima ergo dormitat præ tædio, dum fatigata onere corporis, ad spiritualia minus affectuose afficitur, ipsaque difficultate proficiendi, seu dilatione consolationis internæ quodammodo frangitur: ideo indiget divinitus confortari. Pro quo orat, subdendo: confirma me in verbis tuis, id est, da mihi ex lectione, auditione, vel commemoratione sacræ Scripturæ cordialiter roborari, sicut dum audio, lego aut recolo: Quia non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam; et, Vigilate, state in fide, viriliter agite, confortamini. Nam teste Apostolo, Omnis Scriptura divinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum, etc., ut perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum instructus. Et scriptum est: Sermo Dei clypeus est omnibus sperantibus in se.
paras.en: [[118:28|My soul hath slumbered through heaviness|Dormitavit anima mea præ tædio]]. To sleep belongs properly to the sluggard, according to that saying: [[Prov 19:15|Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep|Pigredo immittit soporem]]. And again Solomon says: [[Prov 6:9|How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard?|Usquequo, piger, dormies?]] But to slumber belongs to one who is tired or weary [Denis distinguishes *dormire*, "to sleep", from *dormitare*, "to doze"]. Now the soul is weighed down and wearied by the burden of the body, because of its various needs. So the soul slumbers through heaviness [*præ tædio*: from weariness] when, tired by the load of the body, it is drawn with less affection to spiritual things, and is in a way broken by the very difficulty of making progress, or by the delay of inward consolation: therefore it needs to be strengthened by God. For this he prays, adding: [[118:28|strengthen thou me in thy words|confirma me in verbis tuis]], that is, grant me to be strengthened at heart by the reading, hearing or recalling of sacred Scripture, as when I hear, read or call to mind that [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come|non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam]]; and, [[1 Cor 16:13|Watch ye: stand fast in the faith: do manfully and be strengthened.|Vigilate, state in fide, viriliter agite, confortamini]] For, as the Apostle testifies, [[2 Tim 3:16|All scripture, inspired of God, is profitable to teach|Omnis Scriptura divinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum]], etc., [[2 Tim 3:17|That the man of God may be perfect, furnished to every good work.|ut perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum instructus]] And it is written: The [[Prov 30:5|word of God|Sermo Dei]] [[Prov 30:5|is a buckler to them that hope in him|clypeus est omnibus sperantibus in se]].

paras.t: Viam iniquitatis, id est viam iniquam; vel, Viam iniquitatis, id est præambulum, dispositionem, seu occasionem peccandi; amove a me: non enim possibile est vitare peccatum, nisi peccandi occasio vitetur: quam si non possumus semper humana virtute cavere, precamur ut Deus eam amoveat, præveniendo nos gratia sua, et præservando ab omni ruina. Et de lege tua, id est secundum decretum misericordiæ tuæ, qua proprium tibi est misereri et parcere, miserere mei, dimittendo peccata, et dona gratiæ multiplicando in me. Vel, Lege tua, id est in lege divina nobis proposita, miserere mei, ignoscendo quod contra eam committo sive omitto.
paras.en: [[118:29|The way of iniquity|Viam iniquitatis]], that is, the wicked way; or, [[118:29|the way of iniquity|Viam iniquitatis]], that is, the preamble, disposition or occasion of sinning: [[118:29|remove from me|amove a me]]. For it is not possible to avoid sin unless the occasion of sinning is avoided; and since we cannot always guard against it by human strength, we pray that God may remove it, going before us with his grace and preserving us from every fall. [[118:29|And out of thy law|Et de lege tua]], that is, according to the decree of thy mercy, by which it is proper to thee to have mercy and to spare, [[118:29|have mercy on me|miserere mei]], by forgiving sins and multiplying the gifts of grace in me. Or, [[118:29|thy law|Lege tua]], that is, in the divine law set before us, [[118:29|have mercy on me|miserere mei]], by pardoning what I commit or omit against it.

paras.t: Viam veritatis, id est fidem catholicam conversationemque justam, elegi, contemptis erroribus peccatisque pristinis. Unde dicit Apostolus: Condelector legi Dei secundum interiorem hominem. Judicia tua, id est justas sententias atque vindictas, quibus a principio mundi injustos reprobasti et afflixisti, bonos vero salvasti : ut patet in diluvio, in submersione Pentapolis, in occisione Pharaonis ac populi ejus ; non sum oblitus, quia eorum memoria salutarem mihi timorem incutit, spemque confortat.
paras.en: [[118:30|The way of truth|Viam veritatis]], that is, the Catholic faith and a just way of life, [[118:30|I have chosen|elegi]], having despised my former errors and sins. Whence the Apostle says: [[Rom 7:22|I am delighted with the law of God, according to the inward man|Condelector legi Dei secundum interiorem hominem]]. [[118:30|Thy judgments|Judicia tua]], that is, the just sentences and punishments by which from the beginning of the world thou hast rejected and afflicted the unjust but saved the good, as is plain in the flood[[Gen 7:1||]], in the sinking of the Pentapolis [the five cities of the plain, Sodom and its neighbours][[Gen 19:1||]], and in the slaying of Pharao and his people[[Ex 14:28||]]: [[118:30|I have not forgotten|non sum oblitus]], because the remembrance of them strikes a wholesome fear into me and strengthens my hope.

paras.t: Adhæsi testimoniis tuis, Domine, fide et opere, faciendo quæ novi tibi placere : propterea noli me confundere, frustrando me spe mea, repellendo precem meam, aut permittendo ut cadam et confusione dignus efficiar.
paras.en: [[118:31|I have stuck to thy testimonies, O Lord|Adhæsi testimoniis tuis, Domine]], by faith and work, doing what I know to be pleasing to thee: therefore [[118:31|put me not to shame|noli me confundere]], by frustrating my hope, by rejecting my prayer, or by letting me fall and become worthy of confusion.

paras.t: Viam, id est operationem, mandatorum tuorum cucurri, id est, festinanter implevi, ardenter exsecutus sum, quum dilatasti cor meum, infundendo ei desiderium fervidum, quo cor aperitur ad consentiendum omnibus dilecto placentibus. Cor enim caritate spiritualiter dilatatur, exhilaratur, et ampliatur in Deo et bonis operibus. Amanti autem nihil difficile est. Ideo talis currit magis, quam vadat aut ambulet, in lege divina. Experiturque verum esse quod scriptum est : Mandata ejus gravia non sunt ; et, Jugum meum suave est et onus meum leve. Dum ergo sentimus nos ferventes et alacres in divinis, non gloriemur in nobis inaniter, sed in Deo, humiliter gratias agendo caritati et gratiæ ejus ; simusque cauti ac providi contra gloriam vanam, aliorum contemptum, futuramque ruinam.
paras.en: [[118:32|The way|Viam]], that is, the working, [[118:32|of thy commandments|mandatorum tuorum]] [[118:32|I have run|cucurri]], that is, I have fulfilled them speedily, carried them out ardently, [[118:32|when thou didst enlarge my heart|quum dilatasti cor meum]], pouring into it a fervent desire by which the heart is opened to consent to all that pleases the Beloved. For the heart is spiritually enlarged by charity, gladdened and widened in God and in good works; and to one who loves nothing is difficult. So such a one runs, rather than goes or walks, in the divine law, and finds true what is written: [[1 John 5:3|his commandments are not heavy|Mandata ejus gravia non sunt]]; and, [[Matt 11:30|my yoke is sweet and my burden light|Jugum meum suave est et onus meum leve]]. When therefore we feel ourselves fervent and eager in divine things, let us not glory in ourselves in vain, but in God, humbly giving thanks to his charity and grace; and let us be wary and watchful against vainglory, contempt of others, and a fall to come.

paras.t: Precatio. Iniquitatis vias amove a nobis, Domine, et tuo gratuito munere viam mandatorum tuorum dilatato corde da nos percurrere : ut exuti corpore, per te cives constituamur cœlestis patriæ.
paras.en: Prayer. Remove from us the ways of iniquity, O Lord, and by thy free gift grant us to run through the way of thy commandments with enlarged heart: that, stripped of the body, we may through thee be made citizens of the heavenly fatherland.

paras.t: He. Legem pone mihi, Domine, viam justificationum tuarum, id est legem divinam omnibus generaliter positam, quæ est via justificationum tuarum, quia per legem justificationem tuam acquirimus. Hanc legem pone mihi singulariter in corde, et ante oculos mentis, quatenus die ac nocte cogitem eam. Hæc autem positio fit per hoc, quod Deus animæ influit lucem gratiæ copiose : per quam frequenter, faciliter et perseveranter meditatur ea quæ scripta sunt in lege divina, nova ac veteri. Ideo subditur : et exquiram, id est, exquisite quæram, eam semper, perseverando in ea quamdiu sum.
paras.en: He. [[118:33|Set before me for a law the way of thy justifications, O Lord|Legem pone mihi, Domine, viam justificationum tuarum]], that is, the divine law laid down for all in general, which is the way of thy justifications, because through the law we acquire thy justification. Set this law before me in particular, in my heart and before the eyes of my mind, so that I may think upon it day and night. This setting before is done in this way: God pours into the soul the light of grace in abundance, by which it meditates often, readily and perseveringly on what is written in the divine law, the New and the Old. Therefore it is added: [[118:33|and I will always seek after it|et exquiram]], that is, I will seek it out with care [Latin *exquisite quæram*, a play on *exquiram*], [[118:33|always|eam semper]], persevering in it as long as I live.

paras.t: Da mihi intellectum, id est donum Spiritus Sancti quod dicitur intellectus ; vel, Intellectum, id est intelligentiam actualem ex gratia procedentem ; et scrutabor, id est, diligenter considerabo et investigabo, legem tuam, pensando quid in ea proponatur credendum, quid sperandum, quid amandum, quid formidandum, quid agendum, quid præcavendum, quid etiam dicat jubendo, quid consulendo ; et custodiam illam, scilicet legem divinam, in toto corde meo, eam videlicet recolendo, contemplando, diligendo, et exsequendo.
paras.en: [[118:34|Give me understanding|Da mihi intellectum]], that is, the gift of the Holy Ghost which is called understanding[[Is 11:2||]]; or, *understanding*, that is, actual understanding [that is, an act of understanding, as distinct from the abiding gift] proceeding from grace; [[118:34|and I will search|et scrutabor]], that is, I will diligently consider and investigate, [[118:34|thy law|legem tuam]], weighing what it sets forth to be believed, what to be hoped for, what to be loved, what to be feared, what to be done, what to be guarded against, and also what it says by way of command and what by way of counsel; [[118:34|and I will keep it|et custodiam illam]], namely the divine law, [[118:34|with my whole heart|in toto corde meo]], that is, by recalling it, contemplating it, loving it and carrying it out.

paras.t: Deduc me, per gratiæ claritatem angelicamque directionem, in semita, id est in processu et executione, mandatorum tuorum moralium (mandata autem cærimonialia cessarunt), ne aberrem ; quia ipsam volui, id est, quia hanc semitam concupivi, et ita feci quod in me est, præparando videlicet me ad gratiam tuæ deductionis. Decet igitur te, ut me exaudias atque deducas.
paras.en: [[118:35|Lead me|Deduc me]], by the brightness of grace and the guidance of the angels, [[118:35|into the path|in semita]], that is, into the following and carrying out, [[118:35|of thy commandments|mandatorum tuorum]], the moral ones (for the ceremonial commandments have ceased), lest I go astray; [[118:35|for this same I have desired|quia ipsam volui]], that is, because I have longed for this path, and so have done what is in me [that is, what lies in one's own power, the scholastic *facere quod in se est*], namely by preparing myself for the grace of thy leading. It is fitting, then, that thou hear me and lead me.

paras.t: Inclina cor meum in testimonia tua : id est, intellectum et voluntatem animæ meæ per gratiam tuam converte ad sacra eloquia, et inchoa bonum in me, quoniam tu es qui operaris in nobis et velle et perficere, pro bona voluntate, id est ex tua benignitate, secundum Apostolum. Omnia quoque opera nostra operatus es in nobis. Et non in avaritiam : quia qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationes et laqueum diaboli. Inclina itaque cor meum ad bona divina, in tantum ut ab inordinato amore terrenarum rerum penitus avertatur.
paras.en: [[118:36|Incline my heart into thy testimonies|Inclina cor meum in testimonia tua]]: that is, by thy grace turn the understanding and will of my soul to the sacred words, and begin good in me; since, according to the Apostle, it is thou [[Phil 2:13|who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish|qui operaris in nobis et velle et perficere]] [Denis adapts the words: "thou who workest in us"], [[Phil 2:13|according to his good will|pro bona voluntate]], that is, out of thy kindness. And [[Is 26:12|thou hast wrought all our works for us|Omnia quoque opera nostra operatus es in nobis]]. [[118:36|And not to covetousness|Et non in avaritiam]]: for [[1 Tim 6:9|they that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationes et laqueum diaboli]]. Incline my heart, then, to the things of God, so far that it be wholly turned away from the inordinate love of earthly things.

paras.t: Averte oculos meos exteriores et interiores, ne videant aut videre desiderent vanitatem, id est mundi spectaculum, speciem mulieris ornatæ, etc., quorum consideratio nocet. Plurimum enim nocet inconsideratio visus, et ad magnam ruinam disponit. Mors quippe per fenestram ingreditur, mens ipsa distrahitur, concupiscentia provocatur, affectionesque variæ ac nocivæ inde nascuntur. Propter quod scriptum est : Noli circumspicere in vicis civitatis; averte faciem tuam a muliere compta; propter speciem mulieris multi perierunt. Et Ezechiel : Unusquisque offensiones oculorum suorum abjiciat, ait Dominus. In via tua, id est in observatione legis divinæ, vivifica me vita gratiæ, ut opera mea meritoria sint vitæ gloriæ, scilicet vitæ æternæ.
paras.en: [[118:37|Turn away my eyes|Averte oculos meos]], outward and inward, [[118:37|that they may not behold|ne videant]] or desire to behold [[118:37|vanity|vanitatem]], that is, the spectacle of the world, the beauty of a woman adorned, etc., the regarding of which does harm. For unguarded looking does very great harm, and disposes to a great fall: for death enters by the window[[Jer 9:21||]], the mind itself is distracted, concupiscence is stirred up, and various harmful affections are born of it. For this reason it is written: [[Ecclus 9:7|Look not round about thee in the ways of the city|Noli circumspicere in vicis civitatis]]; [[Ecclus 9:8|turn away thy face from a woman dressed up|averte faciem tuam a muliere compta]]; [[Ecclus 9:9|many have perished by the beauty of a woman|propter speciem mulieris multi perierunt]]. And Ezechiel: [[Ezech 20:7|Let every man cast away the scandals of his eyes|Unusquisque offensiones oculorum suorum abjiciat]], saith the Lord. [[118:37|In thy way|In via tua]], that is, in the observance of the divine law, [[118:37|quicken me|vivifica me]] with the life of grace, so that my works may be meritorious of the life of glory, that is, of eternal life.

paras.t: Statue servo tuo eloquium tuum in timore tuo : id est, fac ut servus tuus sacram Scripturam reverenter ac timorate recogitet, non ob gloriam vanam, sed ut ex ea a vitiis retrahatur, atque in omnibus secundum divinum eloquium gubernetur. Amputa opprobrium meum quod suspicatus sum : id est, aufer a me malum omne quod aliis ex suspicione imposui, ne aliquem temerarie judicem, ne alteri detraham; quia judicia tua jucunda, id est, justa, vera et sancta, et per consequens ex sua natura jucunda sunt : imo bonis jucunda sunt judicia quibus damnantur perversi; electis vero jucundum erit judicium quod de eis Dominus faciet, Venite, inquiens, benedicti Patris mei.
paras.en: [[118:38|Establish thy word to thy servant, in thy fear|Statue servo tuo eloquium tuum in timore tuo]]: that is, make thy servant ponder the sacred Scripture with reverence and fear, not for vainglory, but that by it he may be drawn back from vices, and be governed in all things according to the divine word. [[118:39|Turn away my reproach, which I have apprehended|Amputa opprobrium meum quod suspicatus sum]] [Latin *quod suspicatus sum*, "which I have suspected", whence Denis's reading]: that is, take away from me every evil that I have laid upon others out of suspicion, lest I judge anyone rashly, lest I detract from another; [[118:39|for thy judgments are delightful|quia judicia tua jucunda]], that is, they are just, true and holy, and consequently delightful by their own nature: nay, to the good even the judgments by which the wicked are condemned are delightful; and to the elect the judgment which the Lord will pass on them will be delightful, when he says: [[Matt 25:34|Come|Venite]], [[Matt 25:34|ye blessed of my Father|benedicti Patris mei]].

paras.t: Ecce concupivi mandata tua plus quam omnia bona terrena; in æquitate tua, id est in justa conversatione, quæ dicitur æquitas tua, tanquam a te data, et tibi accepta, vivifica me, gratiam confortando in anima mea, quatenus semper vigil, vivens et agilis sim in vita decenti, ne mihi dicatur illud Apocalypsis : Nomen habes quod vivas, sed mortuus es.
paras.en: [[118:40|Behold I have longed after thy precepts|Ecce concupivi mandata tua]] more than all earthly goods; [[118:40|in thy justice|in æquitate tua]] [Latin *in æquitate tua*, "in thy equity"], that is, in a just way of life, which is called thy equity as being given by thee and acceptable to thee, [[118:40|quicken me|vivifica me]], by strengthening grace in my soul, so that I may be ever watchful, living and active in a seemly life, lest that word of the Apocalypse be said to me: [[Apoc 3:1|thou hast the name of being alive. And thou art dead|Nomen habes quod vivas, sed mortuus es]].

paras.t: Precatio. Expiatos a sordibus peccatorum deduc nos, Domine, in semita mandatorum tuorum : corda nostra ab omni avaritia, et a noxiæ delectationis vanitate oculos cordis nostri averte : ut recte vivendi studium semper dirigamus ad te Creatorem nostrum.
paras.en: Prayer. [[118:35|Lead|deduc]] us, O Lord, cleansed from the filth of sins, [[118:35|into the path of thy commandments|in semita mandatorum tuorum]]: turn away our hearts from all [[118:36|covetousness|avaritia]], and the eyes of our heart from the [[118:37|vanity|vanitate]] of harmful delight: that we may ever direct our zeal for right living to thee, our Creator.

paras.t: Vau. Et veniat super me misericordia tua, Domine. Secundum doctores sanctos, hic Propheta loquitur in persona gentilium vel totius generis humani, orans pro Christi adventu, et redemptione facta per eum, ut sit sensus : Et veniat super me per incarnationem misericordia tua, Domine, id est Filius tuus, o Deus Pater, per quem misertus es nostri, et qui est fons omnis pietatis et gratiæ. Unde quid per misericordiam istam intelligendum sit, planius pandit : salutare tuum, id est Christus Salvator : de quo in Isaia habetur, Videbunt omnes fines terræ salutare Dei nostri ; secundum eloquium tuum : id est, Christum mitte ad nos, quemadmodum per Prophetas locutus atque pollicitus es. — Potest quoque unusquisque pro se ista orare. Et veniat super me misericordia tua, Domine, id est, effectum pietatis tuæ mihi infunde ; salutare tuum, id est salvatio tua, veniat super me secundum eloquium tuum, quo in Scripturis gratiam deprecanti promittis, dicendo : Pater cœlestis dabit spiritum bonum petentibus se.
paras.en: Vau. [[118:41|Let thy mercy also come upon me, O Lord|Et veniat super me misericordia tua, Domine]]. According to the holy doctors, the Prophet here speaks in the person of the Gentiles, or of the whole human race, praying for the coming of Christ and for the redemption wrought by him; so that the sense is: [[118:41|Let thy mercy also come upon me|Et veniat super me]] through the Incarnation (thy [[118:41|mercy|misericordia tua]], [[118:41|O Lord|Domine]]), that is, thy Son, O God the Father, through whom thou hast had mercy on us, and who is the fount of all kindness and grace. Then he shows more plainly what is to be understood by this mercy: [[118:41|thy salvation|salutare tuum]], that is, Christ the Saviour, of whom it is said in Isaias: [[Is 52:10|all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God|Videbunt omnes fines terræ salutare Dei nostri]]; [[118:41|according to thy word|secundum eloquium tuum]]: that is, send Christ to us, as thou hast spoken and promised through the Prophets. Each one may also pray these words for himself: [[118:41|Let thy mercy also come upon me, O Lord|Et veniat super me misericordia tua, Domine]], that is, pour into me the effect of thy kindness; may [[118:41|thy salvation|salutare tuum]], that is, thy saving help, come upon me [[118:41|according to thy word|secundum eloquium tuum]], by which in the Scriptures thou promisest grace to him who prays for it, saying: [[Luke 11:13|your Father from heaven|Pater cœlestis]] will [[Luke 11:13|give the good Spirit to them that ask him|dabit spiritum bonum petentibus se]].

paras.t: Et ego ita adjutus gratia tua, respondebo, inspirante Spiritu Sancto, exprobrantibus, id est opprobriose loquentibus, mihi, verbum bonum et efficax, secundum quod materia exigit. Respondebo enim dæmonibus verbum cordis, negando consensum; hæreticis, verbum sapientiæ, defendendo fidem; injuriantibus, verbum patientiæ, vincendo in bono malum; detractoribus, verbum operis, bene vivendo. Sicque implebo verbum Apostoli : Sciatis quomodo oporteat vos unicuique respondere. Porro tam efficaciter respondebo, quia speravi in sermonibus tuis, id est, verum esse credidi atque in me implendum speravi, quod in Evangelio dicis : Non vos estis qui loquimini, sed Spiritus Patris vestri qui loquitur in vobis ; et iterum, Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri.
paras.en: And I, thus helped by thy grace, shall [[118:42|answer|respondebo]], by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost, [[118:42|them that reproach me|exprobrantibus]], that is, those who speak reproachfully to me, [[118:42|in any thing|mihi, verbum]] [Latin *verbum*, "a word": I shall answer them a word], a good and effective word, as the matter requires. For I shall answer the devils with the word of the heart, by refusing consent; heretics with the word of wisdom, by defending the faith; those who wrong me with the word of patience, as I [[Rom 12:21|overcome evil by good|vincendo in bono malum]]; detractors with the word of deed, by living well. And so I shall fulfil the word of the Apostle: [[Col 4:6|that you may know how you ought to answer every man|Sciatis quomodo oporteat vos unicuique respondere]]. Moreover, I shall answer so effectively because [[118:42|I have trusted in thy words|quia speravi in sermonibus tuis]], that is, I have believed to be true, and hoped to see fulfilled in me, what thou sayest in the Gospel: [[Matt 10:20|it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you|Non vos estis qui loquimini, sed Spiritus Patris vestri qui loquitur in vobis]]; and again: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri]].

paras.t: Vel sic : Et respondebo exprobrantibus mihi verbum istud quod sequitur : Quia speravi in sermonibus tuis : id est, quidquid illi mihi improperent, non curabo, nec verbis contendam, sed dicam eis : Ego spero in sermonibus Dei mei, quibus prædixit beatos qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam ; et, Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam. Spero ergo quod Dominus tempore suo respondebit et judicabit pro me : prout scriptum est : Ne dicas, Reddam malum pro malo ; exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te.
paras.en: Or thus: [[118:42|So shall I answer them that reproach me in any thing|Et respondebo exprobrantibus mihi verbum]], namely this word which follows: [[118:42|that I have trusted in thy words|Quia speravi in sermonibus tuis]]; that is, whatever they cast in my teeth, I will not care, nor contend in words, but will say to them: I hope in the words of my God, in which he foretold: [[Matt 5:10|Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake|beatos qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam]]; and: [[Heb 10:30|Vengeance belongeth to me, and I will repay|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam]][[Rom 12:19||]]. I hope, then, that the Lord in his own time will answer and judge for me, as it is written: [[Prov 20:22|Say not: I will return evil: wait for the Lord, and he will deliver thee|Ne dicas, Reddam malum pro malo ; exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te]].
