paras.t: Et ne auferas de ore meo verbum veritatis usquequaque, id est, propter peccata mea non tollas a me verbum laudis divinæ, instructionis fraternæ, prædicationis catholicæ, responsionis condignæ. Sed tu, Domine, sis mihi motor doctorque linguæ, sicut in Ecclesiastico dicitur : Dominus dedit mihi linguam mercedem meam ; et per Isaiam : Dominus dedit mihi linguam eruditam, ut sciam sustentare eum, qui lassus est, verbo. Hæc ergo, Domine, tribue mihi, quia in judiciis tuis, quibus juste judicas, justeque agis, ut abscondas verbum hujusmodi a sapientibus et prudentibus, et reveles ipsum parvulis ; in judiciis quoque, quibus abjecta et infirma mundi eligis, ut fortes et sapientes confundas ; supersperavi, id est, vehementer speravi. Ex hac namque consideratione roboratur spes mea, hisque pensatis desperare non valeo, quamvis sim vilis, abjectus et modicus. Et custodiam legem tuam semper, videlicet in sæculum et in sæculum sæculi, id est quamdiu sum, eam mente revolvendo, et opere adimplendo.
paras.en: [[118:43|And take not thou the word of truth utterly out of my mouth|Et ne auferas de ore meo verbum veritatis usquequaque]], that is, for my sins take not from me the word of divine praise, of brotherly instruction, of catholic preaching, of fitting answer. But be thou, O Lord, the mover and teacher of my tongue, as is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 51:30|The Lord hath given me a tongue for my reward|Dominus dedit mihi linguam mercedem meam]]; and through Isaias: [[Is 50:4|The Lord hath given me a learned tongue, that I should know how to uphold by word him that is weary|Dominus dedit mihi linguam eruditam, ut sciam sustentare eum, qui lassus est, verbo]]. Grant me these things, then, O Lord, [[118:43|for in thy words|quia in judiciis tuis]] [Latin *in judiciis tuis*, "in thy judgments", which Denis explains], by which thou judgest justly and dealest justly in hiding such a word from the wise and prudent and revealing it to little ones, and in the judgments also by which thou choosest the abject and weak things of the world to confound the strong and the wise, [[118:43|I have hoped exceedingly|supersperavi]], that is, I have hoped vehemently. For by this consideration my hope is strengthened, and when I weigh these things I cannot despair, though I be vile, abject and of small account. [[118:44|So shall I always keep thy law|Et custodiam legem tuam semper]], namely [[118:44|for ever and ever|in sæculum et in sæculum sæculi]], that is, as long as I live, turning it over in my mind and fulfilling it in deed.

paras.t: Et ambulabam, id est, conversatus sum, in latitudine caritatis Dei et proximi : quæ caritas adeo lata est, ut se ubique communicet, nil sibi proprium servans, sed usque ad æmulos se extendens : quia (ut ait Apostolus) caritas non æmulatur, non agit perperam, non irritatur, non quærit quæ sua sunt ; quia mandata tua, quibus præcipis etiam adversarios diligi, exquisivi scire et agere.
paras.en: [[118:45|And I walked|Et ambulabam]], that is, I have lived, [[118:45|at large|in latitudine]], in the breadth of the charity of God and of neighbour: which charity is so broad that it shares itself everywhere, keeping nothing as its own, but reaching even to rivals; for (as the Apostle says) [[1 Cor 13:4|charity envieth not, dealeth not perversely|caritas non æmulatur, non agit perperam]], [[1 Cor 13:5|is not provoked to anger|non irritatur]], [[1 Cor 13:5|seeketh not her own|non quærit quæ sua sunt]]; [[118:45|because|quia]] thy [[118:45|commandments|mandata tua]], by which thou commandest that even adversaries be loved[[Luke 6:27||]], [[118:45|I have sought after|exquisivi]], to know them and to do them.

paras.t: Sed quum Christus dicat, Contendite intrare per angustam portam ; et, Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam : quomodo potest aliquis justus in latitudine ambulare, præsertim quum lata sit via quæ ducit ad mortem ? Et respondendum, quod via Domini et porta ducens ad vitam, appellatur angusta et arcta ; via vero seu porta perditionis, spatiosa et lata : quoniam sicut testatur princeps theologorum sacratissimus Dionysius (et idem ait Aristoteles), virtus seu bonum est ex integra causa, videlicet concurrentibus omnibus circumstantiis ad virtutem requisitis ; peccatum vero est ex singulis circumstantiis omissis. Et ergo contingit multis modis peccare, errare, deficere ; sed benefacere non contingit, nisi uno modo. Virtus enim consistit in medio ; peccatum vero, in recessu a medio. Medium autem uno modo atque cum difficultate attingitur ; multis vero modis et faciliter a medio isto receditur : idcirco facilius est peccare, quam virtuose agere, sicut facilius est non tangere signum ad quod sagittantes sagittant, quam illud contingere. Sed huic angustiæ non obviat latitudo dilectionis, quæ omnia arcta efficit ampla, et universa difficilia prope nulla : quoniam nulla forma operatur tam prompte tamque jucunde ut caritas.
paras.en: But since Christ says: [[Luke 13:24|Strive to enter by the narrow gate|Contendite intrare per angustam portam]]; and: [[Matt 7:14|strait is the way that leadeth to life|Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam]]: how can any just man walk at large, especially since broad is the way that leads to death[[Matt 7:13||]]? The answer is that the way of the Lord and the gate leading to life are called narrow and strait, and the way or gate of perdition spacious and broad, because, as the most holy Dionysius, prince of theologians, testifies (and Aristotle says the same) [Dionysius, *On the Divine Names*, ch. 4; Aristotle, *Ethics* II, 6], virtue or good comes from an entire cause, that is, when all the circumstances required for virtue concur, but sin comes from any single circumstance left out. And so one may sin, err and fall short in many ways, but one may do well in only one way. For virtue consists in the mean, and sin in departing from the mean. Now the mean is reached in one way only and with difficulty, but one departs from it in many ways and easily: hence it is easier to sin than to act virtuously, just as it is easier to miss the mark at which archers shoot than to hit it. But the breadth of love is not at odds with this narrowness, for it makes all strait things wide and all difficult things almost nothing: since no form [that is, no inward principle of action] works so promptly and so gladly as charity.

paras.t: Et loquebar in testimoniis tuis in conspectu regum, et non confundebar. Hic versus præcipue competit sanctis martyribus, quibus Christus in Evangelio ait : Ante reges et præsides ducemini propter me. Illic ipsi confessi sunt nomen, fidem, documentaque Christi, et non sunt confusi. Imo adversarios fidei confuderunt, quia non poterant resistere sapientiæ et spiritui qui per martyres loquebatur, sicut de Stephano scriptum est. Eratque supermirabile et omni pene miraculo mirabilius, quod tenerrimæ virgines et adolescentulæ illustrissimæ, tam constanter tamque insuperabiliter responderunt regibus, judicibus, philosophis, et tyrannis, ut patet de beatissimis Ursula, Barbara, Catharina, Agatha, Agnete et aliis infinitis. Debemus autem et nos coram omnibus Christum libere confiteri, et ejus testimonia fideliter eloqui, quoniam ipse ait : Qui me erubuerit et meos sermones, hunc Filius hominis erubescet quum venerit in regno suo.
paras.en: [[118:46|And I spoke of thy testimonies before kings: and I was not ashamed|Et loquebar in testimoniis tuis in conspectu regum, et non confundebar]]. This verse applies above all to the holy martyrs, to whom Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 10:18|you shall be brought before governors, and before kings for my sake|Ante reges et præsides ducemini propter me]]. There they confessed the name, the faith and the teachings of Christ, and were not confounded. Nay, they confounded the adversaries of the faith, because [[Acts 6:10|they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit|non poterant resistere sapientiæ et spiritui]] which spoke through the martyrs, as is written of Stephen. And it was a marvel beyond marvels, more wonderful than almost any miracle, that most tender virgins and most noble young maidens answered kings, judges, philosophers and tyrants so steadfastly and so invincibly, as is plain from the most blessed Ursula, Barbara, Catherine, Agatha, Agnes and countless others. We too ought to confess Christ freely before all[[Tob 12:6||]], and to speak his testimonies faithfully, since he himself says: [[Luke 9:26|he that shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of man shall be ashamed, when he shall come|Qui me erubuerit et meos sermones, hunc Filius hominis erubescet quum venerit]] in his kingdom [the Vulgate has "in his majesty"].

paras.t: Et meditabar in mandatis tuis quæ dilexi. Quod enim ardentius amatur, frequentius cogitatur ; et ipsa meditatio formata, est fructus mandati. Et levavi, id est extendi, manus meas, id est potentias operativas, desideria cordis et corporis membra, ad mandata tua quæ dilexi, quatenus ea actu implerem : quoniam ipsa meditatio sine opere non sufficit, si operandi adsit facultas ; et exercebar, secundum modum jam dictum, videlicet meditando, loquendo et operando, in justificationibus tuis, id est in divinis mandatis obedientem justificantibus.
paras.en: [[118:47|I meditated also on thy commandments, which I loved|Et meditabar in mandatis tuis quæ dilexi]]. For what is loved more ardently is thought of more often; and meditation itself, when formed [that is, given its form by charity], is the fruit of the commandment. [[118:48|And I lifted up|Et levavi]], that is, stretched out, [[118:48|my hands|manus meas]], that is, my powers of action, the desires of the heart and the members of the body, [[118:48|to thy commandments, which I loved|ad mandata tua quæ dilexi]], so as to fulfil them in act: for meditation without work is not enough, if there is the means to work; [[118:48|and I was exercised|et exercebar]], in the way already said, namely by meditating, speaking and working, [[118:48|in thy justifications|in justificationibus tuis]], that is, in the divine commandments, which justify the one who obeys them.

paras.t: Precatio. Veniat super nos misericordia tua, Domine, et spe bona fac nos in te vigere, daque vigilare in geminæ caritatis latitudine ; et ut in custodia legis tuæ devoti simus, semper in ea gloriose vivamus.
paras.en: Prayer. Let [[118:41|thy mercy|misericordia tua]] come upon us, O Lord, and make us flourish in thee with good hope; and grant us to keep watch in the breadth of twofold charity [that is, love of God and of neighbour]; and that, being devout in the keeping of thy law, we may ever live gloriously in it.

paras.t: Zain. Memor esto verbi tui servo tuo : id est, ad salutem famuli tui fac sicut locutus es, scilicet ne propter nostram malitiam desinas facere quod aliter faceres. Dixisti enim, o Domine : Omnis qui petit, accipit ; et qui quærit, invenit ; et pulsanti aperietur. Dixisti etiam, Beati qui non viderunt, et crediderunt ; et alibi, Ubi sum ego, illic et minister meus erit. Omnia verba hæc impleantur in me, et singulis nobis. In quo verbo mihi spem dedisti. Hæc namque atque similia verba conferunt spem indulgentiæ, spem gratiæ, atque fiduciam gloriæ acquirendæ. Huic simile est quod Salomon orat : Et nunc, Domine, Deus Israel, firmentur verba tua quæ locutus es David servo tuo patri meo ; et, Fac sicut locutus es, ut magnificetur nomen tuum.
paras.en: Zain. [[118:49|Be thou mindful of thy word to thy servant|Memor esto verbi tui servo tuo]]: that is, for the salvation of thy servant do as thou hast spoken; namely, do not, because of our wickedness, cease to do what thou wouldst otherwise do. For thou hast said, O Lord: [[Matt 7:8|every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shall be opened|Omnis qui petit, accipit ; et qui quærit, invenit ; et pulsanti aperietur]]. Thou hast said also: [[John 20:29|blessed are they that have not seen and have believed|Beati qui non viderunt, et crediderunt]]; and elsewhere: [[John 12:26|where I am, there also shall my minister be|Ubi sum ego, illic et minister meus erit]]. May all these words be fulfilled in me, and in each one of us. [[118:49|In which thou hast given me hope|In quo verbo mihi spem dedisti]]. For these and like words give hope of pardon, hope of grace, and confidence of attaining glory. Like this is what Solomon prays: [[3 Kings 8:26|And now, Lord God of Israel, let thy words be established, which thou hast spoken to thy servant David, my father|Et nunc, Domine, Deus Israel, firmentur verba tua quæ locutus es David servo tuo patri meo]]; and: [[2 Kings 7:25|do as thou hast spoken|Fac sicut locutus es]], [[2 Kings 7:26|That thy name may be magnified|ut magnificetur nomen tuum]] [these last words are David's prayer in 2 Kings 7:25–26].

paras.t: Hæc spes concepta ex verbo Dei, me consolata est in humilitate mea, id est in omni oppressione et afflictione vitæ præsentis, atque in humiliatione qua me propter peccata mea contempsi. Nam ex hac spe desperationem exclusi, remissionisque gratiam exspectavi, quia eloquium tuum prædictum consolatorium, vivificavit me, id est, animavit et inflammavit animam meam ad bonum.
paras.en: [[118:50|This|Hæc]] hope, conceived from the word of God, [[118:50|hath comforted me in my humiliation|me consolata est in humilitate mea]], that is, in every oppression and affliction of the present life, and in the humiliation in which I have despised myself for my sins. For by this hope I shut out despair and looked for the grace of forgiveness, [[118:50|because thy word|quia eloquium tuum]], the word of comfort spoken before, [[118:50|hath enlivened me|vivificavit me]], that is, has quickened and kindled my soul to good.

paras.t: Superbi iniquè agebant usquequaque, quoniam Deum offendunt cogitando, loquendo et operando, se ipsos excusando et alios inficiendo. Ideo scriptum est : Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum ; et, Impius quum in profundum peccatorum venerit, contemnit. Ecclesiastes quoque ait : Peccator centies facit malum, et per patientiam sustentatur. Peccatum namque, præsertim mortale, quod per pœnitentiam non deletur, suo mox pondere trahit ad aliud. Unde ait Apostolus : Omnia munda mundis ; coinquinatis autem et infidelibus nihil est mundum ; sed inquinatæ sunt eorum mens et conscientia, quum sint abominati et reprobi. A lege autem tua non declinavi : vel quia nunquam eam transgressus sum : quod competit his qui non peccaverunt mortaliter ; vel quia ad tempus et nunc usque servavi eam : quod pœnitentibus convenit. Loquitur enim David in psalmo hoc in persona generalis justi : idcirco non omnia verba psalmi hujus singulis justis conveniunt.
paras.en: [[118:51|The proud did iniquitously altogether|Superbi iniquè agebant usquequaque]], for they offend God in thought, word and deed, excusing themselves and infecting others. Therefore it is written: [[Ecclus 3:29|the sinner will add sin to sin|Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum]]; and: [[Prov 18:3|The wicked man, when he is come into the depths of sins, contemneth|Impius quum in profundum peccatorum venerit, contemnit]]. Ecclesiastes also says: [[Eccles 8:12|though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and by patience be borne withal|Peccator centies facit malum, et per patientiam sustentatur]]. For sin, especially mortal sin, when it is not blotted out by penance, soon drags a man by its own weight to another. Hence the Apostle says: [[Tit 1:15|All things are clean to the clean: but to them that are defiled and to unbelievers, nothing is clean: but both their mind and their conscience are defiled|Omnia munda mundis ; coinquinatis autem et infidelibus nihil est mundum ; sed inquinatæ sunt eorum mens et conscientia]], [[Tit 1:16|being abominable|sint abominati]] and [[Tit 1:16|reprobate|reprobi]]. [[118:51|But I declined not from thy law|A lege autem tua non declinavi]]: either because I have never transgressed it, which befits those who have not sinned mortally; or because for a time, and up to now, I have kept it, which suits penitents. For David speaks in this psalm in the person of the just man in general: therefore not all the words of this psalm fit each just man.

paras.t: Memor fui judiciorum tuorum quæ facta sunt a sæculo, id est ab origine mundi, o Domine, considerando quomodo a principio mundi rebelles et animosos reprobasti ; mites vero, obedientes et humiles liberasti, quoad vitam æternam, quamvis interdum permisisti eos temporaliter tribulari corporaliterque occidi, propter purgationem culparum et augmentum meritorum ac præmiorum : quomodo etiam semper electi tui in hac vita afflicti sunt, reprobi vero hic floruerunt. Et consolatus sum ex ista memoria, sperans me ad sortem electorum pertinere, eo quod ego tantis tribulationibus tentationibusque afficiar.
paras.en: [[118:52|I remembered|Memor fui]] [[118:52|thy judgments|judiciorum tuorum]] which were done [[118:52|of old|a sæculo]], that is, from the beginning of the world, [[118:52|O Lord|Domine]], considering how from the beginning of the world thou hast rejected the rebellious and the proud-spirited, and delivered the meek, the obedient and the humble, as regards eternal life, though thou hast sometimes permitted them to be afflicted in time and slain in the body, for the cleansing of their faults and the increase of their merits and rewards; and how thy elect have always been afflicted in this life, while the reprobate have flourished here. [[118:52|And I was comforted|Et consolatus sum]] by this remembrance, hoping that I belong to the lot of the elect, since I am visited with so many tribulations and temptations.

paras.t: Defectio tenuit me, id est, magnus timor invasit me, pro peccatoribus derelinquentibus legem tuam, id est ex consideratione hominum perversorum : quia dum me eis in natura similem video, vehementer formido, ne ex humana fragilitate incidam vitia atque pericula, quæ eos incidisse conspicio. Quantumcumque enim sit homo perfectus, debet tamen esse cautus et metuens, ne illis assimiletur in culpa, quibus conformatur in natura. Ideo namque Salomon ait : Beatus homo qui semper est pavidus. Et dicit Apostolus : Considerans te ipsum, ne et tu tenteris ; et alibi, Itaque qui se existimat stare, videat ne cadat. Vel sic : Defectio, id est ingens compassio seu mœror deficere faciens, tenuit me pro peccatoribus, etc., in tantum eorum errorum et cæcitati compassus sum, sicut ait Apostolus de se ipso : Tristitia mihi est magna et continuus dolor cordi meo pro fratribus meis Judæis. Ex hac etiam defectione, ex vera caritate ortum habente, dixit Michæas : Utinam non essem vir spiritum habens, et mendacium potius loquerer. Tanta enim est pietas hominum perfectorum, ut amplius doleant de aliena culpa et miseria, quam de propria pœna atque injuria, sicut et indulgentissimus pater tanto plus condolet filio suo phrenetico, quanto pluribus ab eo ictibus injuriisque pulsatur.
paras.en: [[118:53|A fainting hath taken hold of me|Defectio tenuit me]], that is, a great fear has seized me, [[118:53|because of the wicked that forsake thy law|pro peccatoribus derelinquentibus legem tuam]], that is, from considering perverse men: for when I see that I am like them in nature, I am vehemently afraid lest through human frailty I fall into the vices and perils into which I see they have fallen. For however perfect a man may be, he must still be wary and fearful lest he become like in fault to those to whom he is conformed in nature. For this reason Solomon says: [[Prov 28:14|Blessed is the man that is always fearful|Beatus homo qui semper est pavidus]]. And the Apostle says: [[Gal 6:1|considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted|Considerans te ipsum, ne et tu tenteris]]; and elsewhere: [[1 Cor 10:12|Wherefore, he that thinketh himself to stand, let him take heed lest he fall|Itaque qui se existimat stare, videat ne cadat]]. Or thus: [[118:53|A fainting|Defectio]], that is, an immense compassion or grief that makes one faint, [[118:53|hath taken hold of me, because of the wicked|tenuit me pro peccatoribus]], etc.: so much have I suffered with them in their errors and blindness; as the Apostle says of himself: [[Rom 9:2|I have great sadness and continual sorrow in my heart|Tristitia mihi est magna et continuus dolor cordi meo]] [[Rom 9:3|for my brethren|pro fratribus meis]] the Jews. From this fainting too, springing from true charity, Micheas said: [[Mich 2:11|Would God I were not a man that hath the spirit, and that I rather spoke a lie|Utinam non essem vir spiritum habens, et mendacium potius loquerer]]. For so great is the tender love of perfect men that they grieve more over another's fault and misery than over their own punishment and injury; as a most indulgent father feels the more for his frenzied son the more blows and injuries he receives from him.

paras.t: Cantabiles mihi erant, imo semper cantandæ, et delectabiliter proferendæ sunt, justificationes tuæ, id est dona divina quibus justificamur a te, scilicet laudes divinæ, mandata, flagella, et cetera quibus salubriter exercemur ; in loco peregrinationis meæ, id est in Ecclesia militanti, in via exsilii, in hoc corpore corruptibili, sicut scriptum est : Lauda, filia Sion ; jubila, Israel ; exsulta in corde tuo, filia Jerusalem. Et Apostolus : Cantantes, inquit, et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino semper.
paras.en: [[118:54|Thy justifications|justificationes tuæ]] [[118:54|were the subject of my song|Cantabiles mihi erant]] (nay, they are always to be sung and uttered with delight), that is, the divine gifts by which we are justified by thee, namely the divine praises, the commandments, the scourges and the other things by which we are wholesomely exercised; [[118:54|in the place of my pilgrimage|in loco peregrinationis meæ]], that is, in the Church militant, on the way of exile, in this corruptible body; as it is written: [[Soph 3:14|Give praise, O daughter of Sion: shout, O Israel|Lauda, filia Sion ; jubila, Israel]]: [[Soph 3:14|rejoice with all thy heart, O daughter of Jerusalem|exsulta in corde tuo, filia Jerusalem]]. And the Apostle: [[Eph 5:19|singing|Cantantes]], he says, [[Eph 5:19|and making melody in your hearts to the Lord|et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino]] always.

paras.t: Memor fui nocte nominis tui, Domine : sicut in Threnis habetur : Consurge, lauda in nocte, in principio vigiliarum. Vel, In nocte, id est tempore adversitatis et tentationis. Et custodivi legem tuam. Nam memoria, scientia, seu contemplatio Dei, sine observantia legis, vana atque informis est, prout Paulus de reprobis fatetur : Confitentur se nosse Deum, factis autem negant. Hæc custodia legis facta est mihi, id est, gratia custodiendi legem data est mihi, quia justificationes tuas, id est præcepta, exquisivi, ut ea implerem. Idcirco dedit mihi Creator omnipotens gratiam implendi. Nam, ut scriptum est, Omnis qui petit, accipit, et qui quærit, invenit.
paras.en: [[118:55|In the night I have remembered thy name, O Lord|Memor fui nocte nominis tui, Domine]]: as is said in Lamentations: [[Lam 2:19|Arise, give praise in the night, in the beginning of the watches|Consurge, lauda in nocte, in principio vigiliarum]]. Or, *in the night*, that is, in the time of adversity and temptation. [[118:55|And have kept thy law|Et custodivi legem tuam]]. For the remembrance, knowledge or contemplation of God without the observance of the law is vain and unformed [that is, lacking the form that charity gives], as Paul declares of the reprobate: [[Tit 1:16|They profess that they know God: but in their works they deny him|Confitentur se nosse Deum, factis autem negant]]. [[118:56|This|Hæc]] keeping of the law [[118:56|happened to me|facta est mihi]], that is, the grace of keeping the law was given to me, [[118:56|because|quia]] thy [[118:56|justifications|justificationes tuas]], that is, the precepts, [[118:56|I sought after|exquisivi]], in order to fulfil them. Therefore the almighty Creator gave me the grace to fulfil them. For, as it is written: [[Matt 7:8|every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth|Omnis qui petit, accipit, et qui quærit, invenit]].

paras.t: Precatio. Pro obtentu cælestis patriæ, Domine, justificationes tuæ sunt nobis cantabiles in locis peregrinationis nostræ : quibus suaviter modulatis, æternæ misericordiæ mercedem a te percipiamus.
paras.en: Prayer. For the winning of our heavenly fatherland, O Lord, [[118:54|thy justifications|justificationes tuæ]] are the subject of our song in the places of our [[118:54|pilgrimage|peregrinationis]]: grant that, having sweetly sung them, we may receive from thee the reward of eternal mercy.

paras.t: Heth. Portio mea, Domine, dixi custodire legem tuam : hoc est, o Domine, ego dixi, id est, apud me statui, quod custodirem legem tuam : id est, custodia legis divinæ est portio mea, id est bonum quod ego ex omnibus atque præ omnibus temporalibus bonis elegi, ita quod aliis exteriora et sensibilia bona eligentibus, ego pro meliori elegi tibi in omnibus obedire, hoc est legem tuam servare. Lex enim divina esse debet Christiano locupletatio maxima, ita ut dicere possit illud : Præposui illam regnis et sedibus, et divitias nihil esse duxi in comparatione illius. Nec mirum, quia subjungitur, Venerunt mihi omnia bona pariter cum illa. Vel sic : O Domine, qui es portio mea, id est unicum bonum quod præ omnibus amo, quod solum adipisci desidero; dixi, id est, fortiter apud me ordinavi, custodire legem tuam, sine cujus custodia non salvatur adultus.
paras.en: Heth. [[118:57|O Lord, my portion, I have said, I would keep thy law|Portio mea, Domine, dixi custodire legem tuam]]: that is, O Lord, I have said, that is, I have resolved within myself, that I would keep thy law: that is, the keeping of the divine law is my portion, that is, the good which I have chosen out of all temporal goods and before them all; so that, while others choose outward and sensible goods, I have chosen as the better part to obey thee in all things, that is, to keep thy law. For the divine law ought to be the Christian's greatest wealth, so that he can say that word: [[Wis 7:8|I preferred her before kingdoms and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her|Præposui illam regnis et sedibus, et divitias nihil esse duxi in comparatione illius]]. Nor is this any wonder, since it is added: [[Wis 7:11|all good things came to me together with her|Venerunt mihi omnia bona pariter cum illa]]. Or thus: O Lord, who art my portion, that is, the one good which I love above all things and which alone I desire to obtain, [[118:57|I have said|dixi]], that is, I have firmly determined within myself, [[118:57|I would keep thy law|custodire legem tuam]], without the keeping of which no adult is saved.

paras.t: Deprecatus sum faciem tuam [in toto corde meo], id est, te ubique præsentem et omnia conspectantem, vel pium adspectum tuum et adsistentiam gratiæ tuæ : hanc faciem tuam precatus sum tanquam bonum finale, ut eam aliquando per speciem videam, sicut et Moyses deprecabatur : Si inveni gratiam in conspectu tuo, ostende mihi faciem tuam, ut sciam te. In hac nempe visione beatitudo mea reposita est. Vel, Deprecatus sum faciem tuam illud quod subditur : Miserere mei, veniam gratiamque præstando, secundum eloquium tuum, quo locutus es : Si impius egerit pœnitentiam, omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor amplius.
paras.en: [[118:58|I entreated thy face|Deprecatus sum faciem tuam]] [[118:58|with all my heart|in toto corde meo]], that is, thee, who art present everywhere and beholdest all things; or thy loving regard and the assistance of thy grace: this thy face I have entreated as the final good, that I may one day see it by sight [*per speciem*: seeing face to face, as opposed to knowing by faith], as Moses also entreated: [[Ex 33:13|If therefore I have found favour in thy sight, shew me thy face, that I may know thee|Si inveni gratiam in conspectu tuo, ostende mihi faciem tuam, ut sciam te]]. For in this vision my beatitude is laid up. Or: [[118:58|I entreated thy face|Deprecatus sum faciem tuam]] for that which follows: [[118:58|have mercy on me|Miserere mei]], by granting pardon and grace, [[118:58|according to thy word|secundum eloquium tuum]], in which thou hast said: [[Ezech 18:21|if the wicked do penance|Si impius egerit pœnitentiam]], [[Ezech 18:22|I will not remember all his iniquities|omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor]] any more.

paras.t: Cogitavi vias meas, id est, vitam et opera mea discussi, et de bonis tibi, o Domine, gratias retuli, de malis vero pœnitui. Sicque et converti pedes meos, id est desideria mea, opera mea, et corporis plantas, in testimonia tua, id est in verba sacri eloquii, quatenus secundum tua præcepta, exempla atque consilia gubernem in omnibus memetipsum. Unde in Aggæo habetur : Ponite corda vestra super vias vestras.
paras.en: [[118:59|I have thought on my ways|Cogitavi vias meas]], that is, I have examined my life and my works, and for the good I have given thanks to thee, O Lord, and for the evil I have repented. And so I [[118:59|turned my feet|converti pedes meos]], that is, my desires, my works and the feet of my body, [[118:59|unto thy testimonies|in testimonia tua]], that is, to the words of the sacred utterance, so that I may govern myself in all things according to thy precepts, examples and counsels. Hence it is said in Aggeus: [[Agg 1:7|Set your hearts upon your ways|Ponite corda vestra super vias vestras]].

paras.t: Paratus sum ex caritate ferventi, gratia habituali, habitibusque virtutum, et non sum turbatus ex passione inordinata, ut custodiam mandata tua : nam habitus virtuosus efficit hominem ad divina paratum. Propter quod in Jeremia legitur : Ego non sum turbatus, te pastorem sequens. Et Apostolus monet : Quodcumque facitis, ex animo facite. Beatus plane qui ita paratus est, qui non turbatur circa plurima ; sed unum illud quod solum necessarium est, summe et unice quærit, cupit ac diligit.
paras.en: [[118:60|I am ready|Paratus sum]] through fervent charity, habitual grace [that is, the sanctifying grace that abides in the soul as a habit] and the habits of the virtues, [[118:60|and am not troubled|et non sum turbatus]] by disordered passion, [[118:60|that I may keep thy commandments|ut custodiam mandata tua]]: for a virtuous habit makes a man ready for divine things. Wherefore we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 17:16|I am not troubled, following thee for my pastor|Ego non sum turbatus, te pastorem sequens]]. And the Apostle admonishes: [[Col 3:23|Whatsoever you do, do it from the heart|Quodcumque facitis, ex animo facite]]. Blessed indeed is he who is so ready, who is not troubled about many things, but seeks, desires and loves supremely and solely that one thing which alone is necessary.

paras.t: Talis dicere potest : Funes peccatorum, id est impugnationes hostium visibilium et invisibilium, circumplexi sunt me, qui in medio laqueorum ambulo. Undique enim conantur nos dæmones pravique homines a Deo avertere, et suæ voluntati nos conformare. Propter quod scriptum est : Adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret : cui resistite fortes in fide, scientes eamdem passionem ei quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitati fieri. Et legem tuam non sum oblitus, id est, propter tentationem et adversitatem nequaquam recessi a te, nec legem tuam transgressus sum.
paras.en: Such a one can say: [[118:61|The cords of the wicked|Funes peccatorum]] [*peccatorum*, literally 'of sinners'], that is, the assaults of enemies visible and invisible, [[118:61|have encompassed me|circumplexi sunt me]], who walk in the midst of snares. For on every side the demons and wicked men strive to turn us away from God and to conform us to their own will. Wherefore it is written: [[1 Pet 5:8|your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|Adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret]]: [[1 Pet 5:9|Whom resist ye, strong in faith: knowing that the same affliction befalls, your brethren who are in the world.|cui resistite fortes in fide, scientes eamdem passionem ei quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitati fieri]] And [[118:61|I have not forgotten thy law|legem tuam non sum oblitus]], that is, on account of temptation and adversity I have in no way gone back from thee, nor transgressed thy law.

paras.t: Media nocte surgebam ad confitendum tibi duplici confessione, videlicet laudis tuæ et propriæ culpæ. Hora enim mediæ noctis sicut dormientibus pigris solet esse periculosior, sic surgentibus religiosis esse consuevit salubrior. Tunc nempe, ut ait Ambrosius, fervet carnis illecebra, tunc mens somnolenta est, tunc tentator adsistit, retia jacit quibus turbet mentem improvidam, tunc varias deceptiones pectori dormientis infundit. Denique hora ista ad devotionem confert maximam occasionem, quoniam tunc cessant strepitus exteriores, neque objiciunt se sensibus corporis rerum imagines, sicut in die. Surgebam itaque media nocte ad confitendum tibi super judicia justificationis tuæ, id est de judiciis tuæ justitiæ, quæ circa me exercuisti, quibus justificasti me, videlicet de omni misericordia quam mihi dedisti, de castigationibus quibus me afflixisti, ceterisque operibus, ex tuo judicio circa me factis.
paras.en: [[118:62|I rose at midnight to give praise to thee|Media nocte surgebam ad confitendum tibi]] [*ad confitendum*, literally 'to confess', which covers both praising God and owning one's sin] with a twofold confession, namely of thy praise and of my own fault. For as the hour of midnight is wont to be the more dangerous for the slothful who sleep, so it is wont to be the more wholesome for religious who rise. For then, as Ambrose says, the allurement of the flesh is hot, then the mind is drowsy, then the tempter stands by and casts the nets with which to trouble the unwary mind, then he pours manifold deceits into the breast of the sleeper. Lastly, that hour gives the greatest occasion for devotion, since then the noises outside cease, and the images of things do not thrust themselves upon the bodily senses as they do by day. So, [[118:62|I rose at midnight to give praise to thee|Surgebam itaque media nocte ad confitendum tibi]] [[118:62|for the judgments of thy justification|super judicia justificationis tuæ]], that is, for the judgments of thy justice which thou hast exercised upon me, by which thou hast justified me: namely for all the mercy thou hast shown me, for the chastisements with which thou hast afflicted me, and for thy other works done towards me by thy judgment.

paras.t: Particeps ego sum omnium timentium te timore casto et filiali, et custodientium mandata tua. Omnes enim in gratia existentes, sunt unum in Christo propter vinculum caritatis, qua connectuntur, nec quæ sua sunt quærunt, sed quæ aliorum. Idcirco meritum unius redundat in alium, in quantum se mutuo juvant, et unum per dilectionem existunt. Hinc enim indulgentiæ efficaciam sortiuntur, quoniam propter unitatem capitis atque membrorum, videlicet Christi et Christianorum, et membrorum (id est fidelium) inter se, communicatur et cooperatur nobis meritum Christi atque Sanctorum. Ob hanc enim participationem, communionem et unitatem mysticam electorum in Christo, Apostolus admonet : Nemo quod suum est quærat, sed quod alterius ; et rursus, Unus panis et unum corpus multi sumus. Hinc etiam Christus orat: Rogo, Pater, ut omnes unum sint, sicut tu, Pater, in me et ego in te, ut sint consummati in unum; et item: Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo quos dedisti mihi, ut sint unum sicut et nos.
paras.en: [[118:63|I am a partaker with all them that fear thee|Particeps ego sum omnium timentium te]] with a chaste and filial fear, [[118:63|and that keep thy commandments|et custodientium mandata tua]]. For all who are in grace are one in Christ through the bond of charity by which they are joined together, and they seek not the things that are their own, but those of others[[1 Cor 10:24||]]. Therefore the merit of one overflows into another, inasmuch as they help one another and are one through love. From this indeed indulgences have their efficacy [an indulgence: the remission, granted by the Church from the merits of Christ and the Saints, of the temporal punishment still due for sins already forgiven], since through the unity of the head and the members, namely of Christ and Christians, and of the members (that is, the faithful) among themselves, the merit of Christ and of the Saints is shared with us and works together with us. For on account of this participation, communion and mystical unity of the elect in Christ, the Apostle admonishes: [[1 Cor 10:24|Let no man seek his own, but that which is another's|Nemo quod suum est quærat, sed quod alterius]]; and again: [[1 Cor 10:17|we, being many, are one bread, one body|Unus panis et unum corpus multi sumus]]. Hence too Christ prays: [[John 17:20|I pray|Rogo]], Father, [[John 17:21|That they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee|ut omnes unum sint, sicut tu, Pater, in me et ego in te]], [[John 17:23|that they may be made perfect in one|ut sint consummati in unum]]; and again: [[John 17:11|Holy Father, keep them in thy name whom thou hast given me: that they may be one, as we also are|Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo quos dedisti mihi, ut sint unum sicut et nos]].

paras.t: Misericordia tua, Domine, id est effectibus pietatis divinæ, plena est terra, id est homines viatores. Aut enim misericorditer convertuntur, aut longanimiter tolerantur, aut paternaliter corriguntur, aut citra condignum patiuntur; omnesque generaliter communibus beneficiis Dei utuntur, videlicet donis naturæ; et omnibus offert Deus gratiam, sicut Apostolus ait: Legatione pro Christo fungimur, tanquam Deo exhortante per nos. Obsecramus pro Christo, reconciliamini Deo. Justificationes tuas, id est mandata vitæ, doce me, quatenus ea clarius semper cognoscam, atque perfectius impleam.
paras.en: [[118:64|The earth|terra]], that is, men who are wayfarers [*viatores*: men still on the way in this life, not yet in the heavenly homeland], [[118:64|is full|plena est]] [[118:64|of thy mercy|Misericordia tua]], [[118:64|O Lord|Domine]], that is, of the effects of the divine goodness. For either they are mercifully converted, or patiently borne with, or corrected as by a father, or suffer less than they deserve; and all in general enjoy the common benefits of God, namely the gifts of nature; and to all God offers grace, as the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 5:20|For Christ therefore we are ambassadors, God as it were exhorting by us, for Christ, we beseech you, be reconciled to God|Legatione pro Christo fungimur, tanquam Deo exhortante per nos. Obsecramus pro Christo, reconciliamini Deo]]. [[118:64|Teach me|doce me]] [[118:64|thy justifications|Justificationes tuas]], that is, the commandments of life, so that I may ever know them more clearly and fulfil them more perfectly.

paras.t: Precatio. Fac nos participes, Domine, timentium te, et da nobis legem tuam in beneplacito custodire; et in necessitatibus in toto corde deprecantes faciem tuam, miserere secundum misericordiam tuam.
paras.en: Prayer. Make us partakers, O Lord, with them that fear thee, and grant us to keep thy law in thy good pleasure; and when in our needs we entreat thy face with all our heart, have mercy on us according to thy mercy.

paras.t: Teth. Bonitatem fecisti cum servo tuo, Domine, id est, tuam bonitatem mihi communicasti, dando mihi pietatem et gratiam, dona naturæ et munera gratiæ, secundum verbum tuum, id est, sicut jubes nos facere. Dicis enim et præcipis nobis bonitatem facere aliis prompte ac large, quemadmodum legitur: Omni petenti te tribue. Et in Actibus Apostolorum Paulus: Oportet, inquit, reminisci verbi Domini Jesu, qui dixit, Beatius est magis dare quam accipere. Vel, Secundum verbum tuum, id est, sicut locutus es te bonitatem facturum nobiscum. Scriptum est namque: Bonus est Dominus sperantibus in eum, animæ quærenti illum.
paras.en: Teth. [[118:65|Thou hast done well with thy servant, O Lord|Bonitatem fecisti cum servo tuo, Domine]] [*bonitatem fecisti*, literally 'thou hast done goodness'], that is, thou hast shared thy goodness with me, giving me loving-kindness and grace, the gifts of nature and the gifts of grace, [[118:65|according to thy word|secundum verbum tuum]], that is, as thou biddest us do. For thou tellest and commandest us to do goodness to others readily and generously, as we read: [[Luke 6:30|Give to every one that asketh thee|Omni petenti te tribue]]. And Paul in the Acts of the Apostles: We ought, he says, [[Acts 20:35|to remember the word of the Lord Jesus, how he said: It is a more blessed thing to give, rather than to receive|reminisci verbi Domini Jesu, qui dixit, Beatius est magis dare quam accipere]]. Or: [[118:65|according to thy word|Secundum verbum tuum]], that is, as thou hast said that thou wouldst do goodness with us. For it is written: [[Lam 3:25|The Lord is good to them that hope in him, to the soul that seeketh him|Bonus est Dominus sperantibus in eum, animæ quærenti illum]].

paras.t: Bonitatem, id est pietatem seu misericordiam, et disciplinam, id est rigorem justitiæ, et scientiam, id est discretionem utendi bonitate ac disciplina, doce me, quatenus me ipsum seu mihi commissos efficaciter regam, ut sit rationabile obsequium meum. Hæc tria præcipue pertinent ad prælatos et principes. Nec sufficit eis unum istorum sine aliis, ne sit pietas laxa, vel justitia crudelis, vel scientia sine opere. Necessaria ergo est prælato pietas disciplinaris seu justa, et disciplina benigna: quod esse non potest, nisi adsit essentialis discretio, qua discernatur quando et quomodo uti oporteat pietate et disciplina, commiscendo utrasque ad invicem secundum verum rationis judicium. Pertinet autem bonitas ad rectorem, juxta illud, Roboratur clementia thronus regis; justitia quoque seu disciplina, juxta illud, Rex qui judicat in veritate pauperes, thronus ejus in æternum firmabitur. Maxime quoque spectat ad eum scientia, quatenus inter verum et falsum, bonum et malum discernere queat. Unde conqueritur apud Isaiam Dominus: Ipsi pastores ignoraverunt intelligentiam. Et per Osee testatur: Quia tu scientiam repulisti, repellam te ego, ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi. Nam ut Christus per se ipsum disseruit, Cæcus si cæco ducatum præstet, ambo in foveam cadunt. Hinc etiam Moyses, insinuans qui essent ad prælationem et regimen aliorum digni atque idonei: Date, inquit, ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribubus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes.
paras.en: [[118:66|Teach me|doce me]] [[118:66|goodness|Bonitatem]], that is, kindness or mercy, [[118:66|and discipline|et disciplinam]], that is, the rigour of justice, [[118:66|and knowledge|et scientiam]], that is, the discernment to use goodness and discipline, so that I may rule myself, or those committed to me, to good effect, and that it may be my [[Rom 12:1|reasonable service|rationabile obsequium]]. These three belong chiefly to prelates and princes. Nor is one of them enough for them without the others, lest kindness be slack, or justice cruel, or knowledge without works. A prelate therefore needs a kindness that keeps discipline, that is, a just kindness, and a kindly discipline: which cannot be unless there is present an essential discernment, by which it is discerned when and how kindness and discipline are to be used, mixing the two with each other according to the true judgment of reason. Now goodness belongs to a ruler, according to that word: [[Prov 20:28|his throne is strengthened by clemency|Roboratur clementia thronus regis]] [Denis has *thronus regis*, 'the king's throne', for *thronus ejus*]; justice also, or discipline, according to that word: [[Prov 29:14|The king that judgeth the poor in truth, his throne shall be established for ever|Rex qui judicat in veritate pauperes, thronus ejus in æternum firmabitur]]. And knowledge too concerns him above all, so that he may be able to discern between true and false, good and evil. Hence the Lord complains in Isaias: [[Is 56:11|the shepherds themselves knew no understanding|Ipsi pastores ignoraverunt intelligentiam]]. And by Osee he testifies: [[Osee 4:6|because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will reject thee, that thou shalt not do the office of priesthood to me|Quia tu scientiam repulisti, repellam te ego, ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi]]. For, as Christ himself declared, [[Matt 15:14|if the blind lead the blind, both fall into the pit|Cæcus si cæco ducatum præstet, ambo in foveam cadunt]]. Hence also Moses, showing who were worthy and fit for prelacy and the government of others: [[Deut 1:13|Let me have|Date]], he says, [[Deut 1:13|from among you wise and understanding men, and such whose conversation is approved among your tribes, that I may appoint them your rulers|ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribubus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes]].

paras.t: Hæc tribue mihi, o Domine, quia mandatis tuis credidi, id est, operando consensi, credidique eis non verbo solo aut lingua, sed opere et veritate. Oportet namque, secundum Philosophum, credere addiscentem. Nec dissonat Isaias qui ait: Si non credideritis, non intelligetis. Qui igitur cupit divinitus illustrari, firmiter credat.
paras.en: Grant me these things, O Lord, [[118:66|for I have believed thy commandments|quia mandatis tuis credidi]], that is, I have consented to them by doing them, and I have believed them not [[1 John 3:18|in word nor in tongue, but in deed and in truth|verbo solo aut lingua, sed opere et veritate]] [the margin gives Joann. iii, 18: the words are those of 1 John 3:18; Denis has 'not in word alone or tongue']. For, according to the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle], the learner must believe. Nor does Isaias disagree, who says: [[Is 7:9|If you will not believe|Si non credideritis]], you shall not understand [Denis follows the old reading *non intelligetis*, 'you shall not understand', often cited by Augustine; the Vulgate has *non permanebitis*, 'you shall not continue']. Whoever therefore desires to be enlightened by God, let him believe firmly.

paras.t: Priusquam humiliarer per flagella, diffortunia et adversa, ego deliqui. Multi enim tempore prosperitatis multipliciter peccant, qui dum a statu suæ prosperitatis dejiciuntur atque divinitus castigantur, retrahuntur a malo, et flagellis edocti, convertuntur ad Deum. Ideo subditur : propterea, id est propter humiliationem istam, eloquium tuum custodivi, obediendo de cetero sermonibus tuis. Ideo per Jeremiam inducitur : Castigasti me, Domine, et eruditus sum. Et alibi Dominus ait : Ego sepiam viam tuam spinis, et sepiam eam maceria. Ex correctione ergo divina experitur homo, quam bonum sit Domino obedire : ad quod pertinet illud, Tantummodo sola vexatio dabit intellectum auditui.
paras.en: [[118:67|Before I was humbled|Priusquam humiliarer]] by scourges, misfortunes and adversities, [[118:67|I offended|ego deliqui]]. For many sin in many ways in the time of prosperity who, when they are cast down from their prosperous state and chastised by God, are drawn back from evil and, taught by the scourges, are converted to God. Therefore it is added: [[118:67|therefore|propterea]], that is, on account of this humbling, [[118:67|have I kept thy word|eloquium tuum custodivi]], by obeying thy words thenceforward. Therefore in Jeremias one is brought in saying: [[Jer 31:18|Thou hast chastised me|Castigasti me]], O Lord, [[Jer 31:18|and I was instructed|et eruditus sum]]. And elsewhere the Lord says: [[Osee 2:6|I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will stop it up with a wall|Ego sepiam viam tuam spinis, et sepiam eam maceria]]. From the divine correction, then, man learns by experience how good it is to obey the Lord; to which belongs that word: [[Is 28:19|vexation alone shall make you understand what you hear|Tantummodo sola vexatio dabit intellectum auditui]].

paras.t: Vel sic : Priusquam humiliarer, id est, antequam humiliarem me ipsum, considerando miserias meas innumeras, ego deliqui, quoniam superbia mater est omnis peccati. Unde qui se non humiliat, infinita vitia incidit. Propterea, ne sic delinquam, eloquium tuum quo dicis, Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde, custodivi, humiliando me ipsum : quia odibilis coram Deo et hominibus est superbia. Propter quod in Tobia habetur : Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu aut in verbo tuo dominari permittas. In ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio.
paras.en: Or thus: [[118:67|Before I was humbled|Priusquam humiliarer]], that is, before I humbled myself by considering my numberless miseries, [[118:67|I offended|ego deliqui]], since pride is the mother of all sin. Hence he who does not humble himself falls into countless vices. [[118:67|Therefore|Propterea]], that I may not so offend, [[118:67|have I kept|custodivi]] [[118:67|thy word|eloquium tuum]], in which thou sayest: [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde]], humbling myself; for [[Ecclus 10:7|Pride is hateful before God and men|odibilis coram Deo et hominibus est superbia]] [the margin gives Eccli. v, 7; the words are those of Ecclus 10:7]. Wherefore we have in Tobias: [[Tob 4:14|Never suffer pride to reign in thy mind, or in thy words: for from it all perdition took its beginning.|Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu aut in verbo tuo dominari permittas. In ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio]]

paras.t: Bonus es tu naturaliter, quomodolibet atque totaliter. Unde Scriptura affirmat : Nemo bonus nisi solus Deus. Et in bonitate tua, id est secundum quod tu bonus et clemens es, doce me justificationes tuas, id est mandata. Beatus enim quem tu erudieris, Domine : quoniam omnis qui audivit a Patre et didicit, venit ad Christum, ut ipse ait.
paras.en: [[118:68|Thou art good|Bonus es tu]] by nature, in every way and wholly. Hence Scripture affirms: [[Luke 18:19|None is good but God alone|Nemo bonus nisi solus Deus]]. [[118:68|And in thy goodness|Et in bonitate tua]], that is, according as thou art good and merciful, [[118:68|teach me thy justifications|doce me justificationes tuas]], that is, thy commandments. For [[Ps 93:12|blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord|Beatus enim quem tu erudieris, Domine]] [the margin gives Ps. xcii, 12; the verse is Ps 93:12]: since [[John 6:45|every one that hath heard of the Father and hath learned|omnis qui audivit a Patre et didicit]] cometh to Christ, as he himself says.

paras.t: Multiplicata est super me iniquitas superborum : id est, superbi diaboli, hominesque elati, quorum pater diabolus est, multipliciter conati sunt me ad malum inducere, minando, blandiendo, persequendo; ego autem in toto corde meo scrutabor mandata tua, ut sciam quid tibi acceptum sit, cui tanto studiosius placere adhærereque volo, quanto illi multiplicius me impellunt ad malum. Hoc non convenit eis qui radices non habent, sed tempore tentationis labuntur. Ideo Ecclesiasticus docet : Esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui.
paras.en: [[118:69|The iniquity of the proud hath been multiplied over me|Multiplicata est super me iniquitas superborum]]: that is, the proud devils, and puffed-up men whose father is the devil[[John 8:44||]], have tried in many ways to lead me into evil, by threats, by flatteries, by persecution; [[118:69|but I will seek thy commandments with my whole heart|ego autem in toto corde meo scrutabor mandata tua]] [*scrutabor*, 'I will search out'], [[Wis 9:10|that I may know what is acceptable with thee|ut sciam quid tibi acceptum sit]], whom I wish to please and to cleave to the more zealously, the more manifoldly they drive me towards evil. This does not befit those who [[Luke 8:13|have no roots|radices non habent]], but fall away [[Luke 8:13|in time of temptation|tempore tentationis]]. Therefore Ecclesiasticus teaches: [[Ecclus 5:12|Be steadfast in the way of the Lord, and in the truth of thy judgment|Esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui]].

paras.t: Coagulatum est sicut lac cor eorum, id est in malitia induratum ; ego vero legem tuam meditatus sum, cujus meditatio clypeus est contra omnem malignitatem tentantium.
paras.en: [[118:70|Their heart is curdled like milk|Coagulatum est sicut lac cor eorum]], that is, hardened in malice; [[118:70|but I have meditated on thy law|ego vero legem tuam meditatus sum]], the meditation of which is a shield against all the malice of those who tempt.

paras.t: Bonum mihi quoniam humiliasti me per flagella et tentamenta, seu privando me honore et gloria mundi, seu dando animæ meæ humilitatis virtutem, ut discam justificationes tuas : quas superbus discere nequit, quoniam Spiritus Sanctus abominatur superbum.
paras.en: [[118:71|It is good for me that thou hast humbled me|Bonum mihi quoniam humiliasti me]] by scourges and trials, either by depriving me of the honour and glory of the world, or by giving my soul the virtue of humility, [[118:71|that I may learn thy justifications|ut discam justificationes tuas]]: which the proud man cannot learn, since the Holy Ghost abhors the proud.

paras.t: Bonum mihi lex oris tui, id est lex decem præceptorum moralium, et lex evangelica, quam Christus proprio ore edocuit, super millia auri et argenti, id est præ omnibus divitiis sæculi. Ponit namque determinatum pro indeterminato, quia incomparabiliter melior nobis est lex divina, quam quæcumque temporalia bona, secundum illud : Melior est acquisitio ejus negotiatione auri et argenti. Propterea obligamur Deo maximas reddere grates, quod legem divinam nobis largitus est; et tanto gravius peccamus legem transgrediendo, quanto legislatori Deo gratiores esse tenemur de legis suæ sanctissimæ dono.
paras.en: [[118:72|The law of thy mouth is good to me|Bonum mihi lex oris tui]], that is, the law of the ten moral precepts, and the law of the Gospel, which Christ taught with his own mouth, [[118:72|above thousands of gold and silver|super millia auri et argenti]], that is, above all the riches of the world. For he puts a definite number for an indefinite one, since the divine law is incomparably better for us than any temporal goods whatever, according to that word: [[Prov 3:14|The purchasing thereof is better than the merchandise of silver|Melior est acquisitio ejus negotiatione auri et argenti]] [Denis has 'of gold and silver']. Therefore we are bound to render the greatest thanks to God for having bestowed the divine law upon us; and we sin the more gravely by transgressing the law, the more grateful we are bound to be to God the lawgiver for the gift of his most holy law.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, qui naturaliter es bonus, in bonitate tua instrue nos cœlesti disciplina et scientia; fac nos accepta eloquia tua fideliter custodire, et toto corde legem tuam meditari et adimplere, et in justificationibus tuis immaculatum cor semper possidere.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, who art good by nature, in thy goodness instruct us with heavenly discipline and knowledge; make us keep faithfully the words of thine that we have received, and with our whole heart meditate on thy law and fulfil it, and ever possess a heart undefiled in thy justifications.

paras.t: Iod. Manus tuæ fecerunt me, et plasmaverunt me. Eadem verba scripta sunt in libro Job; et est sensus : O Creator sublimis et benedicte, incorporalis et incircumscripte, Manus tuæ, id est potentia et sapientia tua, fecerunt me, animam meam producendo de nihilo, et plasmaverunt me, formando corpus meum ex semine. Unde ad Job dicitur : Ecce et me, sicut et te, fecit Deus, et de eadem luto formatus sum. Sicut autem anima rationalis omnium formarum hujus mundi dignissima est, sic corpus humanum præ cunctis mixtis et elementis præstantius est, nobilioremque figuram sortitur, puta erectam ad contemplanda cœlestia. Formæ enim proportionatur materia, sicut actui potentia. Ideo sicut anima rationalis cœlestium contemplativa est, sic corpus ejus ad cœlum erigitur, quatenus anima per sensum visus, cœlestium notitiam adipiscatur.
paras.en: Iod. [[118:73|Thy hands have made me and formed me|Manus tuæ fecerunt me, et plasmaverunt me]]. The same words are written in the book of Job[[Job 10:8||]]; and the sense is: O Creator most high and blessed, incorporeal and uncircumscribed, [[118:73|Thy hands|Manus tuæ]], that is, thy power and wisdom, [[118:73|have made me|fecerunt me]], bringing forth my soul from nothing, [[118:73|and formed me|et plasmaverunt me]], fashioning my body from seed. Hence it is said to Job: [[Job 33:6|Behold God hath made me as well as thee, and of the same clay I also was formed|Ecce et me, sicut et te, fecit Deus, et de eadem luto formatus sum]]. And as the rational soul is the most noble of all the forms of this world, so the human body is more excellent than all mixed bodies and the elements [*mixta*: bodies compounded of the elements], and is given a nobler shape, namely upright, for contemplating heavenly things. For matter is proportioned to form, as potency to act. Therefore, as the rational soul is contemplative of heavenly things, so its body is raised up towards heaven, so that the soul, through the sense of sight, may gain knowledge of heavenly things.

paras.t: Da mihi intellectum, id est intellectualem illuminationem, ut discam mandata tua, ad intelligendum ea sincerius, meditandum frequentius, exsequendum perfectius. Quia enim, o Domine, a te habeo quidquid sum et habeo : ideo teneor tibi me ipsum ; me autem tibi reddere nequeo, nisi te amando et honorando. Idcirco postulo intellectum, quo discam tua mandata, quoniam amor tuus exigit tua mandata impleri, prout asseritur : In hoc scimus quoniam cognovimus Deum, si mandata ejus servamus. Advertendum quoque quod intellectus interdum sumitur pro intellectuali substantia, interdum pro potentia intellectiva, quandoque pro habitu intellectuali naturali, aliquando pro dono intellectus, qui est habitus intellectualis supernaturalis a Spiritu Sancto infusus, aliquando pro actu intellectivæ potentiæ, seu illustratione ipsius, sicque accipitur modo.
paras.en: [[118:73|give me understanding|Da mihi intellectum]], that is, intellectual enlightenment, [[118:73|and I will learn thy commandments|ut discam mandata tua]] [Denis reads *ut discam*, 'that I may learn', for the Vulgate's *et discam*], so as to understand them more purely, meditate on them more often and carry them out more perfectly. For since, O Lord, I have from thee whatever I am and have, I am therefore bound to give thee my very self; but I cannot give myself back to thee except by loving and honouring thee. Therefore I ask for understanding, by which I may learn thy commandments, since love of thee requires that thy commandments be fulfilled, as it is declared: [[1 John 2:3|And by this we know that we have known him, if we keep his commandments|In hoc scimus quoniam cognovimus Deum, si mandata ejus servamus]]. It is to be noted also that *understanding* (*intellectus*) is sometimes taken for an intellectual substance, sometimes for the intellective power, at times for the natural intellectual habit, at times for the gift of understanding, which is a supernatural intellectual habit infused by the Holy Ghost, and at times for the act of the intellective power, or its enlightenment; and so it is taken here.

paras.t: Qui timent te timore amicali et filiali, videbunt me, id est, opera mea virtuosa considerabunt, et lætabuntur in te, congratulando meo profectui, et tuæ majestatis venerationi. Quemadmodum enim perversi lætantur et congratulantur de malo, sic justi et timorati ex fraterna caritate de proximorum profectu quasi de propria gaudent salute : præcipue tamen lætantur de hoc, quod Deum honorari conspiciunt. Propter quod Paulus inquit : Caritas non gaudet super iniquitate, congaudet autem veritati. Videbunt ergo et lætabuntur, nec opera mea interpretabuntur sinistre, quia in verba tua supersperavi, id est, ultra modum magnam spem habui in verbis divinis, quibus gratiam promittis in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro. Unde et sanctus Job ait : Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo. Debemus enim omnino in verba Dei supersperare, tanquam certissimi quod cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem divinæ legis perseverabunt.
paras.en: [[118:74|They that fear thee|Qui timent te]] with the fear of a friend and of a son [*timore amicali et filiali*: the fear of one who loves and dreads to offend, not the servile fear of punishment], [[118:74|shall see me|videbunt me]], that is, shall consider my virtuous works, [[118:74|and shall be glad|et lætabuntur]] in thee, rejoicing with me at my progress and at the honour paid to thy majesty. For as the perverse are glad and rejoice together over evil[[Prov 2:14||]] [the margin gives Prov. xi, 14, which does not fit; the sense is that of Prov 2:14], so the just and God-fearing, out of brotherly charity, rejoice at their neighbours' progress as at their own salvation; but they are glad above all at this, that they see God honoured. Wherefore Paul says: Charity [[1 Cor 13:6|rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth with the truth|non gaudet super iniquitate, congaudet autem veritati]]. They shall see, then, and be glad, and shall not interpret my works amiss, [[118:74|because I have greatly hoped in thy words|quia in verba tua supersperavi]], that is, I have had a hope great beyond measure in the divine words, in which thou promisest grace in the present and glory in the future. Hence holy Job too says: [[Job 13:15|Although he should kill me, I will trust in him|Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo]]. For we ought altogether to hope exceedingly in the words of God, as being most certain that [[Matt 24:35|heaven and earth shall pass|cœlum et terra transibunt]], but the words of the divine law shall endure.

paras.t: Cognovi, Domine, ex fide et revelatione divina, quia æquitas judicia tua, id est, quod divina judicia, scilicet sententiæ et remunerationes ex divina justitia procedentes, adeo justa et vera sunt, ut aptius asserantur æquitas, quam æqua, quamvis rationem et modum justitiæ horum judiciorum nullus viator comprehendere valet. Hinc enim in Apocalypsi dicitur : Etiam, Domine Deus omnipotens, justa et vera judicia tua ; et in Daniele : Omnia quæ fecisti nobis, Domine, in vero judicio fecisti. Et Dominus dixit ad Job : Numquid irritum facies judicium meum, et condemnabis me ut tu justificeris?
paras.en: [[118:75|I know, O Lord|Cognovi, Domine]], by faith and divine revelation, [[118:75|that thy judgments are equity|quia æquitas judicia tua]], that is, that the divine judgments, namely the sentences and rewards proceeding from the divine justice, are so just and true that they are more fitly called equity than equitable, although no wayfarer can comprehend the reason and manner of the justice of these judgments. Hence it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 16:7|Yea, O Lord God Almighty, true and just are thy judgments|Etiam, Domine Deus omnipotens, justa et vera judicia tua]]; and in Daniel: [[Dan 3:31|every thing that thou hast done to us, thou hast done in true judgment|Omnia quæ fecisti nobis, Domine, in vero judicio fecisti]]. And the Lord said to Job: [[Job 40:3|Wilt thou make void my judgment: and condemn me, that thou mayst be justified?|Numquid irritum facies judicium meum, et condemnabis me ut tu justificeris]]

paras.t: Et in veritate tua, id est consideratione divinæ veritatis, humiliasti me, id est, contulisti mihi humiliationem, qua humiliavi me ipsum. Considerando enim quæ in sacra Scriptura dicuntur de majestate divina et vilitate humana, humiliamus nos ipsos. Vel : In veritate tua, id est in tua justitia, seu justo judicio, humiliasti me, deponendo me a statu sublimi, a gloria temporali, a prosperitate fallaci, prout sanctus Job ait : Ego ille quondam opulentus, repente contritus sum. Non ergo in humiliatione hujusmodi impatientes seu murmurantes inveniamur; sed dicamus cum sancto Job : Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
paras.en: [[118:75|And in thy truth|Et in veritate tua]], that is, by the consideration of the divine truth, [[118:75|thou hast humbled me|humiliasti me]], that is, thou hast bestowed on me the humility by which I have humbled myself. For by considering what is said in sacred Scripture of the divine majesty and of human vileness, we humble ourselves. Or: [[118:75|in thy truth|In veritate tua]], that is, in thy justice, or just judgment, [[118:75|thou hast humbled me|humiliasti me]], putting me down from a high estate, from temporal glory, from deceitful prosperity, as holy Job says: [[Job 16:13|I that was formerly so wealthy, am all on a sudden broken to pieces|Ego ille quondam opulentus, repente contritus sum]]. Let us not then be found impatient or murmuring in such humiliation, but let us say with holy Job: [[Job 1:21|the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away: as it hath pleased the Lord, so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord|Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est. Sit nomen Domini benedictum]].

paras.t: Fiat misericordia tua ut consoletur me, id est, sic mihi effectum misericordiæ tuæ infundas, quod ex hoc in omni adversitate respirem de spe veniæ beatitudinisque futuræ, secundum eloquium tuum servo tuo : id est, mihi famulo tuo impendatur misericordia tua, quemadmodum promisisti in Scripturis, te miserturum omnibus invocantibus te. Nam per Isaiam dicis : Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum. Consolationem quoque afflictis promittis, dicente Propheta : Bonus Dominus, et confortans in die tribulationis. Et alibi : Salus populi ego sum, de quacumque tribulatione clamaverint ad me, exaudiam eos.
paras.en: [[118:76|Let thy mercy be for my comfort|Fiat misericordia tua ut consoletur me]], that is, pour the effect of thy mercy into me in such a way that by it I may breathe again in every adversity, in the hope of pardon and of the beatitude to come, [[118:76|according to thy word unto thy servant|secundum eloquium tuum servo tuo]]: that is, let thy mercy be bestowed on me, thy servant, as thou hast promised in the Scriptures that thou wilt have mercy on all who call upon thee. For thou sayest by Isaias: [[Is 43:7|every one that calleth upon my name, I have created him for my glory|Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum]]. Thou promisest consolation also to the afflicted, as the Prophet says: [[Nah 1:7|The Lord is good, and giveth strength in the day of trouble|Bonus Dominus, et confortans in die tribulationis]]. And elsewhere: I am the salvation of the people; out of whatever tribulation they shall cry to me, I will hear them[[Is 43:2||]] [the margin gives only 'cf. Is. xliii'; these words are not found as such in Scripture: they are the Introit of the Mass of the nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost, drawn from such promises as Is 43:2 and Ps 36:39–40].

paras.t: Veniant mihi miserationes tuæ, id est effectus pietatis divinæ, et vivam vita gratiæ in præsenti, vitaque gloriæ in futuro ; quia lex tua meditatio mea est materialiter, id est, de lege tua meditor, sicque miserationes tuas, scilicet indulgentiam perseverantiamque, promereor.
paras.en: [[118:77|Let thy tender mercies come unto me|Veniant mihi miserationes tuæ]], that is, the effects of the divine goodness, [[118:77|and I shall live|et vivam]] the life of grace in the present and the life of glory in the future; [[118:77|for thy law is my meditation|quia lex tua meditatio mea est]] as its matter [*materialiter*: thy law is what my meditation is about], that is, I meditate on thy law, and so I merit thy tender mercies, namely pardon and perseverance.

paras.t: Confundantur superbi, id est homines animosi, confusione pœnitentiam adducentes, verecundantes de sua malitia ; vel, Confundantur superbi, id est diaboli propter superbiam e cœlo projecti, confusione perpetua ; quia injuste, id est mala intentione et sine meo demerito, iniquitatem fecerunt in me, tentando et persequendo animam meam. Ego autem exercebor in mandatis tuis, occupando me ipsum in eis mente et opere tanto instantius, quanto illi adversantur mihi injustius, quatenus exercitatio sancta atque intensa, exercitationem inimicorum iniquam expellat. Uni namque operationi anima vehementer intenta, alia parum aut nihil advertit.
paras.en: [[118:78|Let the proud be ashamed|Confundantur superbi]], that is, haughty men, with a shame that brings repentance, so that they blush for their malice; or, [[118:78|Let the proud be ashamed|Confundantur superbi]], that is, the devils cast out of heaven for their pride, with everlasting shame; [[118:78|because they have done unjustly|quia injuste]], that is, with an evil intention and through no fault of mine, [[118:78|towards me|iniquitatem fecerunt in me]], by tempting and persecuting my soul. [[118:78|But I will be employed in thy commandments|Ego autem exercebor in mandatis tuis]] [*exercebor*, literally 'I will be exercised', which leads to his *exercitatio*, 'exercise', below], occupying myself in them in mind and deed the more earnestly, the more unjustly they oppose me, so that a holy and intense exercise may drive out the wicked exercise of the enemies. For the soul that is earnestly intent on one activity notices other things little or not at all.

paras.t: Convertantur mihi, id est ad me, quatenus auxilium præbeant mihi, timentes te timore sancto et casto, qui caritate urgente, miserentur afflictis, sicut scribit Apostolus : Confirmate in illum caritatem, id est, peccatori illi succurrite. Et qui noverunt testimonia tua.
paras.en: Let [[118:79|them that fear thee|timentes te]] with a holy and chaste fear [[118:79|turn to me|Convertantur mihi]], that is, towards me, so that they may give me help: those who, urged by charity, have pity on the afflicted, as the Apostle writes: [[2 Cor 2:8|confirm your charity towards him|Confirmate in illum caritatem]], that is, succour that sinner. [[118:79|And they that know thy testimonies|Et qui noverunt testimonia tua]].

paras.t: Fiat cor meum, id est anima mea, immaculatum in justificationibus tuis, id est mandatis, ita ut ea tam perfecte observet, ne tanquam prævaricatrix, macula culpæ deformetur, ut non confundar a te, o Judex metuende, tanquam neglector ac transgressor legis divinæ. Nam sicut habetur secundo Machabæorum libro, In leges divinas agere impie, impune non cedit.
paras.en: [[118:80|Let my heart|Fiat cor meum]], that is, my soul, [[118:80|be undefiled in thy justifications|immaculatum in justificationibus tuis]], that is, thy commandments, so that it may keep them so perfectly as not to be disfigured, like a transgressor, by the stain of guilt, [[118:80|that I may not be confounded|ut non confundar]] by thee, O dread Judge, as a neglecter and transgressor of the divine law. For, as we have it in the second book of Machabees, [[2 Mach 4:17|acting wickedly against the laws of God doth not pass unpunished|In leges divinas agere impie, impune non cedit]].

paras.t: Totum hunc psalmum, in quo virtutes justorum tam diligenter enumerantur, cantamus et dicimus non in nostra, sed in viri justi persona, quatenus agnoscamus quid nobis de perfectione justitiæ desit, illudque adipisci nitamur. Verumtamen si quis gratia largiente adeo justus est, ut verba psalmi hujus sibi conveniant, poterit omnia verba hæc in propria persona depromere ad gloriam Dei, ædificationemque proximi, sicut et Paulus in suis epistolis bona sua frequenter describit.
paras.en: This whole psalm, in which the virtues of the just are so carefully enumerated, we sing and say not in our own person but in the person of a just man, so that we may recognize what we lack of the perfection of justice, and strive to attain it. Yet if anyone, by the gift of grace, is so just that the words of this psalm befit him, he may utter all these words in his own person, to the glory of God and the edification of his neighbour, as Paul too often describes his own good works in his epistles.

paras.t: Precatio. Vitæ dator, Deus, veniant nobis miserationes tuæ, ut juste vivamus ; da nobis intellectum ut mandata tua discamus, ut vigilanter observantes tibi veraciter placeamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, giver of life, let thy tender mercies come to us, that we may live justly; give us understanding, that we may learn thy commandments, so that, keeping them watchfully, we may truly please thee.

paras.t: Caph. Deficit in salutare tuum anima mea. Hucusque egit Propheta de beatitudine, prout in operibus vitæ activæ consistit; deinceps usque ad finem psalmi agit de ea, prout in actibus vitæ contemplativæ reponitur, et ait : Defecit in salutare tuum, id est in dilectione et contemplatione salutaris tui, videlicet Christi; vel salutaris tui, id est salutis æternæ nobis promissæ ; vel tui ipsius, qui es salutare nostrum altissimum ; anima mea. Iste defectus intelligi potest tripliciter. Primo sic: Defecit in salutare tuum anima mea, id est, satis et plene amare et contemplari non potuit anima mea salutare tuum : quia ut ait Apostolus, Oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt, quæ præparavit Deus diligentibus se. Et hæc bona præparata, sunt salus æterna et salutare nostrum. Quid enim aliud præparavit Deus amatoribus suis, nisi se ipsum ? Nemo autem Deum, seu vitam æternam, tam clare cognoscere tamque ardenter diligere potest, præsertim in vita præsenti, quantum ipse cognoscibilis amabilisque consistit. Ideo deficit anima mea in salutare divinum. Secundo exponitur sic : Defecit in salutare tuum anima mea, id est, præ elevata contemplatione ac fervidissima dilectione salutaris tui, defecit anima mea ab operationibus virium sensitivarum, corporaliterque infirmatus sum. Quanto enim contemplatio purior atque sublimior fuerit, et amor Divinitatis ferventior, tanto amplius deficiunt naturales et sensitivæ potentiæ ab actibus suis. Unde quum anima ad raptum et ecstasim venit, quasi omnino suspenditur vita corporalis ac sensitiva, nec vivit homo ut homo. Quidam vero ita exponunt : Defecit in salutare tuum anima mea, id est, præ nimia exspectatione atque dilatione salutis divinæ seu gloriæ sempiternæ defecit, id est, tædio fracta est, fatigata, et infirmata, anima mea. Nam ut Salomon ait : Spes quæ differtur, affligit animam ; lignum vitæ, desiderium veniens. Et in verbum tuum, quo opem et gratiam in præsenti, securitatem vero et gloriam in futuro promittis, supersperavi, id est, vehementer confisus sum.
paras.en: Caph. [[118:81|My soul hath fainted after thy salvation|Deficit in salutare tuum anima mea]]. Up to this point the Prophet has treated of beatitude as it consists in the works of the active life; from here to the end of the psalm he treats of it as it lies in the acts of the contemplative life, and he says: [[118:81|My soul hath fainted after thy salvation|Defecit in salutare tuum]], that is, in the love and contemplation of thy Saviour, namely Christ[[Luke 1:47||]][[Luke 2:30||]] [*salutare tuum*: literally "thy saving one", which can mean either the Saviour or salvation]; or of thy salvation, that is, the eternal salvation promised us; or of thyself, who art our highest salvation. This fainting can be understood in three ways. First thus: [[118:81|My soul hath fainted after thy salvation|Defecit in salutare tuum anima mea]], that is, my soul could not love and contemplate thy salvation enough and fully: for, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man, what things God hath prepared for them that love him|Oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt, quæ præparavit Deus diligentibus se]]. And these good things prepared are eternal salvation and our Saviour. For what else has God prepared for those who love him but himself? But no one, above all in the present life, can know God, or eternal life, so clearly and love him so ardently as he is knowable and lovable. Therefore my soul faints after the divine salvation. Secondly it is expounded thus: [[118:81|My soul hath fainted after thy salvation|Defecit in salutare tuum anima mea]], that is, through lofty contemplation and most fervent love of thy salvation, my soul has fainted away from the operations of the sensitive powers, and I have grown weak in body. For the purer and more sublime contemplation is, and the more fervent the love of the Godhead, the more do the natural and sensitive powers fail from their acts. Hence, when the soul comes to rapture and ecstasy, the bodily and sensitive life is as it were wholly suspended, and man does not live as man. Some, however, expound it thus: [[118:81|My soul hath fainted after thy salvation|Defecit in salutare tuum anima mea]], that is, through too long waiting for and delay of the divine salvation, or of everlasting glory, my soul has fainted, that is, is broken with weariness, wearied out and enfeebled. For, as Solomon says, [[Prov 13:12|Hope that is deferred afflicteth the soul: desire when it cometh, is a tree of life|Spes quæ differtur, affligit animam ; lignum vitæ, desiderium veniens]]. [[118:81|and in thy word|Et in verbum tuum]], by which thou promisest help and grace in the present, and security and glory in the future, [[118:81|I have very much hoped|supersperavi]], that is, I have trusted vehemently.

paras.t: Defecerunt oculi mei interiores in eloquium tuum, id est in verba sacræ Scripturæ, videlicet in promissa et testimonia atque mandata divina. Et iste defectus tripliciter accipi potest, sicut præcedens : quia nec plene comprehendere possumus eloquium Dei ; et interdum ex contemplatione hujus eloquii deficit anima sancta ab exterioribus et sensibilibus rebus, tanquam omnino rapta atque suspensa ad Deum. Denique nimio desiderio consequendi promissiones divini eloquii, interdum deficiunt oculi nostri interni, dicentes ad Dominum : Quando consolaberis me, dando mihi quod præstolor, scilicet tui ipsius optatam præsentiam atque beatificam fruitionem ? De hoc defectu divini eloquii ait Jeremias : Factus est sermo Domini in corde meo quasi ignis exæstuans, et defeci, ferre non sustinens.
paras.en: [[118:82|My eyes have failed|Defecerunt oculi mei]], my inward eyes, [[118:82|for thy word|in eloquium tuum]], that is, for the words of sacred Scripture, namely for the divine promises, testimonies and commandments. And this failing can be taken in three ways, like the one before: because we cannot fully comprehend the word of God; and at times, from the contemplation of this word, the holy soul faints away from outward and sensible things, as though wholly rapt and held up to God. Lastly, through too great desire to obtain the promises of the divine word, our inward eyes at times fail, saying to the Lord: [[118:82|When wilt thou comfort me?|Quando consolaberis me]] by giving me what I wait for, namely the longed-for presence of thyself and the fruition that makes blessed? Of this failing for the divine word Jeremias says: The word of the Lord [[Jer 20:9|came in my heart as a burning fire|in corde meo quasi ignis exæstuans]], [[Jer 20:9|and I was wearied, not being able to bear it|et defeci, ferre non sustinens]].

paras.t: Merito autem consolationem istam requiro, Quia factus sum sicut uter in pruina : id est, quemadmodum vas de corio factum in pruina relictum, contractum, et madefactum seu congelatum, ineptum videtur ad omnem usum humanum ; sic ego ab hominibus sæcularibus circa exteriora versantibus, reputatus sum quasi omnino vilis atque inutilis in conversatione politica et humana. Homines namque eminenter speculativi, efficiuntur quodammodo insensibiles circa exteriora : propterea reputantur in agibilibus et exterioribus velut inepti et stolidi, imo quandoque reputantur simpliciter stulti a prudentibus hujus sæculi.
