Unde legitur quod principes qui erant cum Jehu filio Namsi, quum vidissent filium prophetarum, quem misit Eliseus ut ungeret Jehu in regem, dixerunt ad Jehu : Quid venit insanus iste ad te ? Vel sic : Quia factus sum sicut uter in pruina, id est, sicut uter impletur liquore pruinæ, sic ego impletus sum desiderio patriæ, seu afflictionibus hujus vitæ, ideo cupio consolari. Justificationes tuas, id est mandata, non sum oblitus. Quin potius illud implere curavi : Deum time, et mandata ejus observa : hoc est omnis homo ; illud quoque Apostoli : Serva mandatum sine macula, irreprehensibile, usque ad adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi.
paras.en: And rightly do I ask for this comfort, [[118:83|For I am become like a bottle in the frost|Quia factus sum sicut uter in pruina]]: that is, just as a vessel made of leather, left out in the frost, shrunken and soaked or frozen, seems unfit for any human use, so I, by worldly men busied about outward things, am reckoned as altogether worthless and useless in civil and human dealings. For men eminently given to contemplation become in a manner insensible to outward things: therefore in practical and outward affairs they are reckoned as unfit and dull, nay, sometimes they are reckoned simply fools by the prudent of this world. Hence we read that the captains who were with Jehu the son of Namsi, when they had seen the son of the prophets whom Eliseus sent to anoint Jehu king, said to Jehu: [[4 Kings 9:11|why came this madman to thee?|Quid venit insanus iste ad te]] Or thus: [[118:83|For I am become like a bottle in the frost|Quia factus sum sicut uter in pruina]], that is, as a bottle is filled with the moisture of the frost, so I am filled with desire for the fatherland, or with the afflictions of this life; therefore I long to be comforted. [[118:83|thy justifications|Justificationes tuas]], that is, thy commandments, [[118:83|I have not forgotten|non sum oblitus]]. Nay rather, I have taken care to fulfil this: [[Eccles 12:13|Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is all man|Deum time, et mandata ejus observa : hoc est omnis homo]]; and this too of the Apostle: [[1 Tim 6:14|keep the commandment without spot, blameless, unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ|Serva mandatum sine macula, irreprehensibile, usque ad adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi]].

paras.t: Quot sunt dies servi tui? id est, utinam tempus hujus exsilii, quo peregrinor a te, celeriter finiatur, ne retarder diutius a felicitate cœlesti. Sic Paulus locutus est : Cupio dissolvi et esse cum Christo. Unde supra dictum est : Locutus sum in lingua mea, Notum fac mihi, Domine, finem meum, et numerum dierum meorum, quis est. Quando facies de persequentibus me judicium ? id est, utinam dies finalis judicii veniat, quando persecutores meos diabolos juste damnabis. Hæc dies a justis et contemplativis desideratur, sicut ab aliis formidatur. Propter quod ait Salvator : His autem fieri incipientibus, respicite, et levate capita vestra, id est, hilariter respirate.
paras.en: [[118:84|How many are the days of thy servant|Quot sunt dies servi tui]]? that is, would that the time of this exile, in which I am absent from thee[[2 Cor 5:6||]], may quickly be ended, that I be not held back any longer from heavenly happiness. So Paul spoke: [[Phil 1:23|having a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ|Cupio dissolvi et esse cum Christo]]. Hence it was said above: [[Ps 38:5|I spoke with my tongue: O Lord, make me know my end. And what is the number of my days|Locutus sum in lingua mea, Notum fac mihi, Domine, finem meum, et numerum dierum meorum, quis est]]. [[118:84|when wilt thou execute judgment on them that persecute me?|Quando facies de persequentibus me judicium]] that is, would that the day of the final judgment may come, when thou wilt justly condemn my persecutors, the devils. This day is longed for by the just and the contemplative, as it is dreaded by others. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[Luke 21:28|when these things begin to come to pass, look up and lift up your heads|His autem fieri incipientibus, respicite, et levate capita vestra]], that is, breathe again joyfully.

paras.t: Narraverunt mihi iniqui, scilicet dæmones pravique homines, fabulationes, id est falsas suggestiones, documenta perversa, sermones inutiles ; sed non ut lex tua, id est, istæ fabulationes et vanæ narrationes spiritualiter seu corporaliter factæ, non consonant legi divinæ. Unde ait Apostolus : Stultas et sine disciplina quæstiones devita, sciens quia generant lites.
paras.en: [[118:85|The wicked have told me|Narraverunt mihi iniqui]], namely the demons and wicked men, [[118:85|fables|fabulationes]], that is, false suggestions, perverse teachings, useless talk; [[118:85|but not as thy law|sed non ut lex tua]], that is, these fables and vain tales, told spiritually or bodily, do not accord with the divine law. Hence the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:23|avoid foolish and unlearned questions, knowing that they beget strifes|Stultas et sine disciplina quæstiones devita, sciens quia generant lites]].

paras.t: Omnia mandata tua veritas, id est, adeo vera sunt, ut melius nominentur in abstracto veritas, quam vera in concreto. Iniqui, hæretici, schismatici, falsi fratres, dæmones vel infideles, persecuti sunt me verbis et ictibus ; adjuva me, ne succumbam, quia sine tuo auxilio nequeo repugnare.
paras.en: [[118:86|All thy statutes are truth|Omnia mandata tua veritas]], that is, they are so true that they are better named *truth* in the abstract than *true* in the concrete. The wicked [*Iniqui*: Denis reads "the wicked" where the Vulgate has *inique*, "unjustly"], heretics, schismatics, false brethren, demons or unbelievers, [[118:86|they have persecuted me|persecuti sunt me]] with words and blows; [[118:86|do thou help me|adjuva me]], lest I give way, for without thy help I cannot resist.

paras.t: Paulo minus, id est quasi, seu fere, consummaverunt, id est, perfecte oppresserunt seu dejecerunt, me in terra : sicut Apostolus, Supra modum, inquit, gravati sumus ; ego autem non dereliqui mandata tua, quibus fortitudinem atque perseverantiam præcipis, dicens : Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt ; et alibi : Pro justitia agonizare pro anima tua, et usque ad mortem certa pro justitia ; et : Ecce præcipio tibi, confortare et esto robustus ; noli timere, quoniam tecum est Dominus Deus tuus. Quantumcumque ergo hostis desæviat et tribulatio crescat, recordari debemus præcepta divina, neque lassari, prout monet Apostolus : Non fatigemini animis vestris.
paras.en: [[118:87|They had almost|Paulo minus]], that is, all but, or nearly, [[118:87|made an end of me|consummaverunt]], that is, completely crushed or cast down, [[118:87|me upon earth|me in terra]]: as the Apostle says, [[2 Cor 1:8|out of measure|Supra modum]], he says, [[2 Cor 1:8|we were pressed|gravati sumus]]; [[118:87|but I have not forsaken thy commandments|ego autem non dereliqui mandata tua]], in which thou commandest fortitude and perseverance, saying: [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not them that kill the body|Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt]]; and elsewhere: [[Ecclus 4:33|Strive for justice for thy soul, and even unto death fight for justice|Pro justitia agonizare pro anima tua, et usque ad mortem certa pro justitia]]; and: [[Jos 1:9|Behold I command thee, take courage, and be strong|Ecce præcipio tibi, confortare et esto robustus]]; [[Jos 1:9|Fear not|noli timere]], [[Jos 1:9|because the Lord thy God is with thee|quoniam tecum est Dominus Deus tuus]]. However much, then, the enemy may rage and tribulation grow, we must remember the divine precepts and not grow weary, as the Apostle warns: [[Heb 12:3|be not wearied|Non fatigemini]] [[Heb 12:3|in your minds|animis vestris]].

paras.t: Secundum misericordiam tuam vivifica me, gratiam multiplicando in anima mea, et custodiam fide et opere testimonia oris tui, id est sacri eloquii verba, præsertim articulos fidei atque præcepta Decalogi.
paras.en: [[118:88|Quicken thou me according to thy mercy|Secundum misericordiam tuam vivifica me]], by multiplying grace in my soul, [[118:88|and I shall keep|et custodiam]] by faith and deed [[118:88|the testimonies of thy mouth|testimonia oris tui]], that is, the words of the sacred Scripture, above all the articles of faith and the precepts of the Decalogue.

paras.t: Precatio. Tua, Domine, larga clementia sanctissimi nominis tui amore corda nostra confirma, ne derelinquamus mandata tua; vivificet nos misericordiæ tuæ opus, ut testimonia oris tui proficiendo custodiamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, of thy bountiful clemency strengthen our hearts with the love of thy most holy name, that we may not forsake thy commandments; may the work of thy mercy quicken us, that by going forward we may keep the testimonies of thy mouth.

paras.t: Lamed. In æternum, Domine, verbum tuum, id est jussio tua, illuminatio tua et opus tuum, permanet in cœlo, id est in triumphanti Ecclesia : quoniam omnes angeli sancti atque Beati tibi ad nutum obediunt, tuamque illuminationem incessanter recipiunt. Unde oramus quotidie, ut voluntas tua (id est præceptum tuum) fiat sicut in cœlo et in terra, videlicet ut homines tibi obediant, sicut et angeli. Potest quoque exponi de Filio Dei : de quo scriptum est, In principio erat Verbum. Hoc Verbum in æternum permanet in cœlo, quia licet ad homines venit, non tamen cœlum reliquit, imo simul et semel erat totus in utero Virginis atque in sinu Patris. Propter quod in terra consistens, Nicodemoque loquens, dixit : Nemo ascendit in cœlum, nisi qui descendit de cœlo, Filius hominis qui est in cœlo.
paras.en: Lamed. [[118:89|For ever, O Lord, thy word|In æternum, Domine, verbum tuum]], that is, thy command, thy illumination and thy work, [[118:89|standeth firm in heaven|permanet in cœlo]], that is, in the Church triumphant: for all the holy angels and the Blessed obey thee at thy nod, and receive thy illumination unceasingly. Hence we pray daily that [[Matt 6:10|Thy will|voluntas tua]] (that is, thy command) [[Matt 6:10|be done on earth as it is in heaven|fiat sicut in cœlo et in terra]], namely that men may obey thee as the angels do. It can also be expounded of the Son of God, of whom it is written: [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word|In principio erat Verbum]]. This Word standeth firm in heaven for ever, because, though he came to men, he did not leave heaven; nay, at one and the same time he was wholly in the Virgin's womb and in the bosom of the Father. Wherefore, while he stood on earth and spoke to Nicodemus, he said: [[John 3:13|no man hath ascended into heaven, but he that descended from heaven, the Son of man who is in heaven|Nemo ascendit in cœlum, nisi qui descendit de cœlo, Filius hominis qui est in cœlo]].

paras.t: In generationem et generationem, id est per omnes generationes sibi in sæculo succedentes, veritas tua, id est fides catholica, lex christiana, doctrina evangelica, permanet in militanti Ecclesia. Fundasti, id est, firmiter collocasti, terram in medio mundi, et permanet, sicut in Ecclesiaste inducitur : Generatio præterit et generatio advenit ; terra vero in æternum stat. Spiritualiter vero, Fundasti terram, id est Ecclesiam, in fide et veritate divina, quemadmodum dicis : Super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam ; et permanet stabilis in fide usque ad terminum mundi.
paras.en: [[118:90|unto all generations|In generationem et generationem]], that is, through all the generations that follow one another in the world, [[118:90|Thy truth|veritas tua]], that is, the catholic faith, the Christian law, the teaching of the Gospel, abides in the Church militant. [[118:90|thou hast founded|Fundasti]], that is, thou hast firmly set, [[118:90|the earth|terram]] in the midst of the world, [[118:90|and it continueth|et permanet]], as is set down in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 1:4|One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth standeth for ever|Generatio præterit et generatio advenit ; terra vero in æternum stat]]. Spiritually, [[118:90|thou hast founded the earth|Fundasti terram]], that is, the Church, in faith and divine truth, as thou sayest: [[Matt 16:18|upon this rock I will build my church|Super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam]]; and it continueth steadfast in the faith to the end of the world.

paras.t: Ordinatione tua perseverat dies, qui ex motu et lumine solis causatur. Nam ex ordinatione sapientiæ tuæ superiora et inferiora universaque tempora moderantur. Propter quod alibi habetur : Hæc dicit Dominus, qui dat solem in lumine diei, ordinem lunæ atque stellarum in lumine noctis; et faciens Arcturum et Orionem, et diem nocte mutans. Vel, Ordinatione tua perseverat dies æternitatis creatæ, scilicet ævum, quo Sancti in patria te fruuntur ; vel, dies spiritualis, id est illuminatio Beatorum. Quoniam omnia serviunt tibi : quemadmodum dictum est : Domine, Rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita, et non est qui possit resistere voluntati tuæ. Omni enim naturæ creatæ inest obedientialis potentia, qua suo Creatori in omnibus paret. Sed si omnia serviunt Deo, quid est quod homines Deo non serviunt ? Et respondendum, quod omnia dicuntur Deo servire, ita quod nihil possit resistere ordinationi divinæ.
paras.en: [[118:91|By thy ordinance the day goeth on|Ordinatione tua perseverat dies]], the day which is caused by the motion and light of the sun. For by the ordinance of thy wisdom things above and things below, and all the seasons, are governed. Wherefore it is said elsewhere: [[Jer 31:35|Thus saith the Lord, who giveth the sun for the light of the day, the order of the moon and of the stars, for the light of the night|Hæc dicit Dominus, qui dat solem in lumine diei, ordinem lunæ atque stellarum in lumine noctis]]; and: [[Amos 5:8|that maketh Arcturus, and Orion|faciens Arcturum et Orionem]], [[Amos 5:8|and that changeth day into night|et diem nocte mutans]]. Or: [[118:91|By thy ordinance the day goeth on|Ordinatione tua perseverat dies]], the day of created eternity, namely the *aevum* [that is, the measure of the duration of angels and of the blessed, between time and God's eternity], in which the Saints enjoy thee in the fatherland; or the spiritual day, that is, the illumination of the Blessed. [[118:91|for all things serve thee|Quoniam omnia serviunt tibi]]: as it is said: [[Esth 13:9|O Lord, Lord, almighty king, for all things are in thy power, and there is none that can resist thy will|Domine, Rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita, et non est qui possit resistere voluntati tuæ]]. For in every created nature there is an obediential potency [that is, a capacity to be acted on by God beyond its natural powers], by which it obeys its Creator in all things. But if all things serve God, how is it that men do not serve God? The answer is that all things are said to serve God in the sense that nothing can resist the divine ordinance.

paras.t: Nisi quod lex tua meditatio mea est, id est, nisi legis tuæ testimonia præ oculis habuissem, tunc forte perissem, id est, victus fuissem seu desperassem, in humilitate mea, id est in tribulatione et tentatione quas passus sum ; vel in consideratione qua meam imperfectionem atque miseriam consideravi. Nisi enim in tribulatione et consideratione hujusmodi, cogitaremus quanta esset felicitas eorum qui propter justitiam patiuntur, et Christi vestigia imitantur, atque in tentationibus manent constantes, quanta etiam esset misericordia Dei circa miseros pœnitentes, tunc utique possemus perire in prædicta humilitate.
paras.en: [[118:92|Unless thy law had been my meditation|Nisi quod lex tua meditatio mea est]], that is, had I not kept the testimonies of thy law before my eyes, [[118:92|I had then perhaps perished|tunc forte perissem]], that is, I should have been overcome or have despaired, [[118:92|in my abjection|in humilitate mea]] [*humilitas*: lowliness, here affliction], that is, in the tribulation and temptation that I have suffered; or in the consideration in which I considered my imperfection and misery. For unless, in such tribulation and consideration, we thought how great is the happiness of those who suffer for justice' sake, follow in the footsteps of Christ and remain constant in temptations, and how great also is God's mercy towards wretched penitents, then we might indeed perish in that abjection.

paras.t: Ne ergo peream unquam, In æternum non obliviscar justificationes tuas, id est, nunquam negligam divina mandata recolere et servare ; quia in ipsis vivificasti me vita gratiæ ac spirituali profectu : quemadmodum ait Salvator : Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit ; et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus. Et scriptum est : Hic liber mandatorum Dei, et lex quæ est in æternum : omnes qui tenent eam, pervenient ad vitam ; qui autem derelinquunt eam, ad mortem.
paras.en: So then, that I may never perish, [[118:93|Thy justifications I will never forget|In æternum non obliviscar justificationes tuas]], that is, I will never neglect to call to mind and to keep the divine commandments; [[118:93|for by them thou hast given me life|quia in ipsis vivificasti me]] with the life of grace and spiritual progress: as the Saviour says: [[John 14:23|If any one love me, he will keep my word. And my Father will love him and we will come to him and will make our abode with him|Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit ; et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus]]. And it is written: [[Bar 4:1|This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law, that is for ever: all they that keep it, shall come to life: but they that have forsaken it, to death|Hic liber mandatorum Dei, et lex quæ est in æternum : omnes qui tenent eam, pervenient ad vitam ; qui autem derelinquunt eam, ad mortem]].

paras.t: Tuus sum ego conditione et cultu, fide et opere, salvum me fac in præsenti per gratiam, et in futuro per gloriam, quoniam justificationes tuas exquisivi, id est, mandata implere curavi, ideo salus mihi ex tua promissione debetur : quoniam scriptum est, Si vis ad vitam ingredi, serva mandata ; et iterum, Dirige cor tuum in viam rectam, ut salvus fias.
paras.en: [[118:94|I am thine|Tuus sum ego]] by creation and by worship, by faith and by deed: [[118:94|save thou me|salvum me fac]] in the present by grace and in the future by glory, [[118:94|for I have sought thy justifications|quoniam justificationes tuas exquisivi]], that is, I have taken care to fulfil the commandments; therefore salvation is owed me by thy promise: for it is written, [[Matt 19:17|if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments|Si vis ad vitam ingredi, serva mandata]]; and again, [[Jer 31:21|direct thy heart into the right way|Dirige cor tuum in viam rectam]], that thou mayest be saved [the words "that thou mayest be saved" are not in Jer 31:21].

paras.t: Me exspectaverunt peccatores, id est visibiles atque invisibiles hostes, ut perderent me, inducendo animam meam ad ruinam peccati, vel corpus ad mortem seu læsionem. Hoc sanctis martyribus maxime competit, quos tyranni exspectabant ad interficiendum spiritualiter vel corporaliter. Testimonia tua, id est verba Spiritus Sancti in Scripturis contenta, intellexi, id est, clare perspexi, considerando impiorum fallaciam, hujus vitæ brevitatem, et futuræ gloriæ immensitatem : quibus pensatis, omnia fortiter pertuli, eorumque impugnationes evasi, aut per patientiam vici.
paras.en: [[118:95|The wicked have waited for me|Me exspectaverunt peccatores]], that is, enemies visible and invisible, [[118:95|to destroy me|ut perderent me]], by leading my soul to the ruin of sin, or my body to death or injury. This applies above all to the holy martyrs, whom tyrants lay in wait for, to slay them spiritually or bodily. [[118:95|thy testimonies|Testimonia tua]], that is, the words of the Holy Ghost contained in the Scriptures, [[118:95|I have understood|intellexi]], that is, I have seen them clearly, considering the deceit of the wicked, the shortness of this life and the immensity of the glory to come: weighing these, I have borne all things bravely, and have escaped their assaults, or overcome them by patience.

paras.t: Omnis consummationis, id est omnis humanæ perfectionis, vidi, id est consideravi, finem : ad quem esset referenda omnis virtus humana. Hic autem finis est vita æterna, quæ est finis omnium actuum atque virtutum. Potest etiam finis iste dici caritas, quoniam ipsa est summa virtus, virtutum omnium origo et finis. Quapropter ait Apostolus : Plenitudo legis est dilectio ; et iterum, Finis præcepti est caritas de corde puro. Omnes namque virtutes et actus earum, ad caritatis fervorem et perfectionem ordinandi sunt. Et ita quod sequitur, latum mandatum tuum nimis, exponit quid dixerit, Finem omnis consummationis, ut sit sensus : Omnis consummationis vidi finem, utique latum mandatum tuum nimis, id est, vidi quod caritatis præceptum, quod est valde latum, esset finis et perfectio universæ consummationis, quia ad ipsum cetera referuntur præcepta. Dicitur autem præceptum caritatis latum nimis, quoniam ad omnes se extendit : nam adversarios diligere facit. Secundo, quoniam omnia mandata virtualiter continet, juxta illud : In his duobus præceptis, scilicet caritatis Dei et proximi, tota lex pendet et Prophetæ. Tertio, quia ut legitur, Universa delicta operit caritas.
paras.en: [[118:96|of all perfection|Omnis consummationis]], that is, of all human perfection, [[118:96|I have seen|vidi]], that is, I have considered, [[118:96|an end|finem]]: the end to which all human virtue is to be referred. Now this end is eternal life, which is the end of all acts and virtues. This end can also be called charity, since it is the highest virtue, the origin and end of all the virtues. Wherefore the Apostle says: [[Rom 13:10|Love therefore is the fulfilling of the law|Plenitudo legis est dilectio]]; and again, [[1 Tim 1:5|the end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart|Finis præcepti est caritas de corde puro]]. For all the virtues and their acts are to be ordered to the fervour and perfection of charity. And so what follows, [[118:96|thy commandment is exceeding broad|latum mandatum tuum nimis]], explains what he meant by *the end of all perfection*, so that the sense is: [[118:96|I have seen an end of all perfection|Omnis consummationis vidi finem]], namely [[118:96|thy commandment is exceeding broad|latum mandatum tuum nimis]], that is, I have seen that the commandment of charity, which is very broad, is the end and perfection of all perfection, because the other commandments are referred to it. The commandment of charity is called exceeding broad, first, because it extends to all men, for it makes us love our adversaries. Secondly, because it contains all the commandments virtually, according to that saying: [[Matt 22:40|On these two commandments|In his duobus præceptis]], namely of the love of God and of neighbour, [[Matt 22:40|dependeth the whole law and the prophets|tota lex pendet et Prophetæ]]. Thirdly, because, as we read, [[Prov 10:12|charity covereth all sins|Universa delicta operit caritas]].

paras.t: Potestque litteraliter exponi : Omnis consummationis, id est omnis terrenæ possessionis, omnis ambitionis et gloriæ temporalis, vidi finem, id est terminum. Cito enim deficiunt ista, prout per Joannem inducitur : Et mundus transit, et concupiscentia ejus ; latum mandatum tuum nimis, id est in perpetuum durans, et ad latitudinem cœli perducens.
paras.en: It can also be expounded literally: [[118:96|of all perfection|Omnis consummationis]], that is, of all earthly possession, of all ambition and temporal glory, [[118:96|I have seen an end|vidi finem]], that is, a limit. For these things soon fail, as is set down by John: [[1 John 2:17|And the world passeth away and the concupiscence thereof|Et mundus transit, et concupiscentia ejus]]; [[118:96|thy commandment is exceeding broad|latum mandatum tuum nimis]], that is, lasting for ever, and leading to the breadth of heaven.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, cui omnia serviunt creata, da nos servire tibi fide, spe, et caritate perfecta : ut in æternum justificationes tuas non obliviscamur, sed in ipsis tua propitiatione bonis operibus insistendo vivificemur.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, whom all created things serve, grant us to serve thee with faith, hope and perfect charity, that we may never forget thy justifications, but by thy favour may be quickened in them by persevering in good works.

paras.t: Mem. Quomodo dilexi legem tuam, Domine? Quæritur Propheta in persona Ecclesiæ Deum, quomodo legem ejus diligat. Et ipsemet respondet : Tota die meditatio mea est. Quæritur enim et respondet, ut omnes qui audiunt, informentur. In hoc autem, quod asserit se tota die legem Domini meditari, declarat se ardentissime Deum amare, quia in tantum diligitur, in quantum honoratur, quemadmodum alibi habetur : Qui servat verbum Christi, vere in eo caritas Dei perfecta est. Quod autem magis amatur, hoc sæpius cogitatur. Qui igitur tota die naturali, qui noctem includit, et viginti quatuor horas habet, in lege Domini meditatur, maxime diligit eam, et per consequens legislatorem, utique Deum. Quomodo autem aliquis possit tota die in lege divina meditari, frequenter ostensum est.
paras.en: Mem. [[118:97|O how have I loved thy law, O Lord!|Quomodo dilexi legem tuam, Domine]] The Prophet, in the person of the Church, asks God how he loves his law. And he himself answers: [[118:97|it is my meditation all the day|Tota die meditatio mea est]]. For he asks and answers so that all who hear may be instructed. Now in saying that he meditates on the law of the Lord all the day, he declares that he loves God most ardently, for God is loved in so far as he is honoured, as is said elsewhere: [[1 John 2:5|he that keepeth his word|Qui servat verbum Christi]] [Denis: "the word of Christ"], [[1 John 2:5|in him in very deed the charity of God is perfected|vere in eo caritas Dei perfecta est]]. And what is more loved is more often thought of. He, then, who meditates on the law of the Lord all the natural day, which includes the night and has twenty-four hours, loves it most of all, and consequently the lawgiver, that is, God. How anyone can meditate all the day on the divine law has often been shown.

paras.t: Super inimicos meos prudentem me fecisti, id est, prudentiorem seu sapientiorem me fecisti inimicis meis, puta Judæis et infidelibus, imo omnibus Deo rebellibus : quos perfecto odio odi, non in quantum sunt homines felicitatis capaces, sed in quantum sunt Deo inobedientes, et dæmoni consentientes ; mandato tuo : id est, per hoc quod, illis mandatum tuum non observantibus, dedisti mihi gratiam illud servandi, fecisti me illis prudentiorem. Nam sine observatione præcepti nullus veraciter prudens est ; et summa prudentia est, Deo servire. Unde scriptum est : Quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiæ. Sic autem prudentem me fecisti mandato tuo, quia in æternum mihi est, id est, quoniam perseveranter ac jugiter ei adhærere intendo.
paras.en: [[118:98|thou hast made me wiser than my enemies|Super inimicos meos prudentem me fecisti]], that is, thou hast made me more prudent or wiser than my enemies, for instance the Jews and unbelievers, nay, all who rebel against God, whom I hate [[Ps 138:22|with a perfect hatred|perfecto odio]], not in so far as they are men capable of happiness, but in so far as they disobey God and consent to the devil; [[118:98|Through thy commandment|mandato tuo]]: that is, by this, that while they do not keep thy commandment, thou hast given me the grace to keep it, thou hast made me more prudent than they. For without keeping the commandment no one is truly prudent; and the highest prudence is to serve God. Hence it is written: [[Jas 3:13|Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge, among you? Let him shew, by a good contestation, his work in the meekness of wisdom|Quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiæ]]. And thus hast thou made me wise through thy commandment, [[118:98|for it is ever with me|quia in æternum mihi est]], that is, because I mean to cleave to it perseveringly and continually.

paras.t: Super omnes docentes me intellexi, quia testimonia tua meditatio mea est. Non loquitur absolute de omnibus suis doctoribus : quoniam Christo testante, Non est discipulus supra magistrum ; præsumptuosumque esset se præferre doctoribus. De quibus ergo doctoribus loquitur, nisi de iis qui dicunt et non faciunt, vel qui philosophicam scientiam aut sæcularem prudentiam docent ? His Deo obediens intelligentior est, quia testimonia Dei sunt meditatio ejus : quoniam cogitat verba divina, quatenus secundum doctrinam præceptaque Christi, cogitationes, sermones et actus suos gubernet.
paras.en: [[118:99|I have understood more than all my teachers: because thy testimonies are my meditation|Super omnes docentes me intellexi, quia testimonia tua meditatio mea est]]. He does not speak absolutely of all his teachers, since, as Christ bears witness, [[Matt 10:24|The disciple is not above the master|Non est discipulus supra magistrum]]; and it would be presumptuous to set oneself above one's teachers. Of what teachers, then, does he speak, but of those who say and do not[[Matt 23:3||]], or who teach philosophical knowledge or worldly prudence? He who obeys God has more understanding than these, because the testimonies of God are his meditation: for he ponders the divine words in order to govern his thoughts, words and acts according to the teaching and precepts of Christ.

paras.t: Super senes intellexi, id est senibus doctior fui, quia mandata tua quæsivi scire et adimplere. Ex quo constat, quod non loquitur nisi de senibus illis, qui non quærunt divina mandata, quales fuerunt de quibus apud Danielem dicitur : Iniquitas egressa est de Babylone, a senioribus qui videbantur regere populum.
paras.en: [[118:100|I have had understanding above ancients|Super senes intellexi]], that is, I have been more learned than the old, [[118:100|because I have sought thy commandments|quia mandata tua quæsivi]] to know and fulfil them. From this it is clear that he speaks only of those old men who do not seek the divine commandments, such as those of whom it is said in Daniel: [[Dan 13:5|That iniquity came out from Babylon, from the ancient judges, that seemed to govern the people|Iniquitas egressa est de Babylone, a senioribus qui videbantur regere populum]] [Denis omits "judges"].

paras.t: Ab omni via mala, id est peccato mortali, doctrina pestifera, et ceteris quibus itur ad mortem æternam, prohibui per imperium rationis, pedes meos, id est affectus, cogitationes et opera, vel etiam corporis pedes, vitando loca in quibus puto me debere peccare ; ut custodiam verba tua, quibus jussisti me vitare itinera mala.
paras.en: [[118:101|from every evil way|Ab omni via mala]], that is, from mortal sin, pestilent doctrine and the other things by which one goes to eternal death, [[118:101|I have restrained|prohibui]] by the command of reason [[118:101|my feet|pedes meos]], that is, my affections, thoughts and works, or even the feet of the body, by shunning the places in which I think I should be bound to sin; [[118:101|that I may keep thy words|ut custodiam verba tua]], by which thou hast bidden me shun evil paths.

paras.t: A judiciis tuis non declinavi, id est, ab his quæ bona judicas et approbas tu, non recessi, quia tu legem posuisti mihi, id est præceptum consentiendi vero et bono, et resistendi malo ac falso, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico scribitur : Lege vitæ hereditavit illos (scilicet homines Deus); justitiam et judicia sua ostendit eis, et dixit : Attendite ab omni iniquo.
paras.en: [[118:102|I have not declined from thy judgments|A judiciis tuis non declinavi]], that is, I have not departed from the things which thou judgest good and approvest, [[118:102|because thou hast set me a law|quia tu legem posuisti mihi]], that is, the precept of assenting to what is true and good and resisting what is evil and false, as is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 17:9|the law of life for an inheritance|Lege vitæ hereditavit illos]] (namely, God gave men); [[Ecclus 17:10|he shewed them his justice and judgments|justitiam et judicia sua ostendit eis]], [[Ecclus 17:11|and he said to them: Beware of all iniquity|et dixit : Attendite ab omni iniquo]].

paras.t: Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua! id est, valde suavia sunt verba divina interiori cordis mei palato, videlicet rationi et voluntati, quibus spiritualis dulcedo gustatur, cibus animæ masticatur, et cælestis lætitia prælibatur. Super mel ori meo, id est, dulciora sunt interiori ori meo, utpote menti, qua verbum cordis profert, quam sit mel gustui meo corporeo. Verbum enim Dei cibus est animæ, cujus refectio dulcior est ex sua natura omni cibo corporeo : quamvis interdum ex parte nostri contingat oppositum, quia videlicet appetitus noster nondum purgatus est a vitiis et concupiscentiis. Hinc enim de sapientia scriptum est : Scio quoniam mecum communicabit de bonis, et erit allocutio cogitationis et tædii mei. Intrans in domum meam, conquiescam cum illa : non enim habet amaritudinem conversatio illius, nec tædium convictus ejus, sed lætitiam et gaudium. Et quid mirum si sacra doctrina seu divina et christiana sapientia tam suavis est homini contemplativo ? quum Aristoteles dicat, quod philosophia admirabiles habet delectationes admixtas ; et rursus, quod vita nostra quandoque ad modicum talis est, qualis est vita primi principii semper ; itemque, quod vir contemplativus non quærit delectationes externas, quoniam intra se plenus est jucundis theorematibus.
paras.en: [[118:103|How sweet are thy words to my palate!|Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua!]] that is, the divine words are very sweet to the inner palate of my heart, namely to reason and will, by which spiritual sweetness is tasted, the food of the soul is chewed, and heavenly joy is foretasted. [[118:103|more than honey to my mouth|Super mel ori meo]], that is, they are sweeter to my inner mouth, namely the mind, by which it utters the word of the heart, than honey is to my bodily taste. For the word of God is the food of the soul, and its refreshment is by its nature sweeter than any bodily food, though at times the opposite happens on our part, namely because our appetite is not yet cleansed of vices and concupiscences. Hence it is written of wisdom: [[Wis 8:9|knowing that she will communicate to me of her good things, and will be a comfort in my cares and grief|Scio quoniam mecum communicabit de bonis, et erit allocutio cogitationis et tædii mei]] [Denis: "I know that"]. [[Wis 8:16|When I go into my house, I shall repose myself with her: for her conversation hath no bitterness, nor her company any tediousness, but joy and gladness|Intrans in domum meam, conquiescam cum illa : non enim habet amaritudinem conversatio illius, nec tædium convictus ejus, sed lætitiam et gaudium]]. And what wonder if sacred doctrine, or divine and Christian wisdom, is so sweet to the contemplative man, when Aristotle says that philosophy has wonderful delights mingled with it; and again, that our life at times, for a little while, is such as the life of the first principle is always; and likewise, that the contemplative man does not seek outward delights, since within himself he is full of delightful theorems?

paras.t: A mandatis tuis intellexi, id est, ex consideratione præceptorum cognovi distantiam inter virtutes et vitia. Vel, A mandatis tuis intellexi, id est, intelligentiam veram adeptus sum servando mandata : sicut scriptum est, Fili, concupiscens sapientiam, serva mandata, et Deus præbebit illam tibi. Ait quoque prophetica Scriptura : Quem docebit Dominus sapientiam, et quem intelligere faciet auditum ? Et respondet Propheta : Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere, id est eos qui carnis voluptates contemnunt, et secundum divina præcepta spiritualiter atque pœnitentialiter vivunt. Propterea odivi omnem viam iniquitatis : quam si non odirem, ex certa scientia, non ex ignorantia, peccarem ; conveniretque mihi illud, Servus qui scit voluntatem domini sui, et non facit, plagis vapulabit multis.
paras.en: [[118:104|By thy commandments I have had understanding|A mandatis tuis intellexi]], that is, from considering the precepts I have known the distance between virtues and vices. Or: [[118:104|By thy commandments I have had understanding|A mandatis tuis intellexi]], that is, I have gained true understanding by keeping the commandments: as it is written, [[Ecclus 1:33|Son, if thou desire wisdom|Fili, concupiscens sapientiam]], keep the commandments, [[Ecclus 1:33|and God will give her to thee|et Deus præbebit illam tibi]] [the Vulgate has "keep justice"; Denis reads "keep the commandments"]. The prophetic Scripture also says: [[Is 28:9|Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the hearing?|Quem docebit Dominus sapientiam, et quem intelligere faciet auditum]] And the Prophet answers: [[Is 28:9|them that are weaned from the milk, that are drawn away from the breasts|Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere]], that is, those who despise the pleasures of the flesh, and live spiritually and penitentially according to the divine precepts. [[118:104|therefore have I hated every way of iniquity|Propterea odivi omnem viam iniquitatis]]: for if I did not hate it, I should sin from sure knowledge, not from ignorance, and that saying would fit me: [[Luke 12:47|that servant, who knew the will of his lord|Servus qui scit voluntatem domini sui]], and doeth it not, [[Luke 12:47|shall be beaten with many stripes|plagis vapulabit multis]].

paras.t: Precatio. Totius boni largitor, Domine, da nobis legem tuam sanctam diligere, et ejus meditationi pervigili mente inservire ; fac nos mandata tua recte intelligere, atque ab omni via mala te adjuvante nostræ pravitatis pedes prohibere.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, giver of all good, grant us to love thy holy law, and to give ourselves to meditating on it with watchful mind; make us rightly understand thy commandments, and, with thy help, restrain the feet of our perversity from every evil way.

paras.t: Nun. Lucerna pedibus meis verbum tuum: id est, sacra Scriptura est intellectui meo atque affectui et cunctis operibus meis lucerna, quia illuminat me ne ambulem in tenebris vitiorum; et verbum istud est lumen semitis meis, id est directio mea in observationibus consiliorum Christi: quæ dicuntur semitæ, quia sunt strictiores compendiosioresque viæ perveniendi ad Deum, quam præcepta. Hoc est quod Salomon asserit: Mandatum lucerna est, et lex lux, et via vitæ increpatio disciplinæ. Et alibi: Apprehende legem, et ambula per viam ad splendorem ejus.
paras.en: Nun. [[118:105|Thy word is a lamp to my feet|Lucerna pedibus meis verbum tuum]]: that is, Holy Scripture is a lamp to my understanding and my affections and all my works, because it enlightens me so that I may not walk in the darkness of vices; and this word is [[118:105|a light to my paths|lumen semitis meis]], that is, my guidance in keeping the counsels of Christ, which are called paths because they are narrower and shorter ways of coming to God than the precepts. This is what Solomon asserts: [[Prov 6:23|the commandment is a lamp, and the law a light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life|Mandatum lucerna est, et lex lux, et via vitæ increpatio disciplinæ]]. And elsewhere: Take hold of the law [[Bar 4:2|walk in the way by its brightness|et ambula per viam ad splendorem ejus]] [Baruch has "take hold of it"; Denis reads "the law"].

paras.t: Juravi, id est, irrevocabiliter affirmavi, et statui, id est, proposui, custodire judicia justitiæ tuæ, id est præcepta quæ tua justitia judicat esse recta atque servanda. Jurare itaque licet, quando materia exigit: imo jurare debite circumstantionatum, est actus virtutis, quæ dicitur latria; sicque Scriptura admittit, laudat aut jubet juramentum, juxta illud, Dominum Deum tuum timebis, et per nomen ejus jurabis; et, In omni corde suo juraverunt Domino, et in tota voluntate sua quæsierunt eum, et invenerunt. Quod vero Christus in Evangelio ait, Ego dico vobis non jurare omnino, non dicitur præceptive simpliciter, sed ne sine necessitate juremus, quatenus occasionem perjurii et usum jurandi vitemus.
paras.en: [[118:106|I have sworn|Juravi]], that is, I have affirmed irrevocably, [[118:106|and am determined|et statui]], that is, I have resolved, [[118:106|to keep the judgments of thy justice|custodire judicia justitiæ tuæ]], that is, the precepts which thy justice judges to be right and to be kept. It is lawful, then, to swear when the matter requires it; indeed, to swear with the due circumstances [that is, attended by the right circumstances] is an act of the virtue called latria [that is, the worship due to God alone]. And so Scripture admits, praises or commands the oath, according to the words: [[Deut 6:13|Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God|Dominum Deum tuum timebis]], [[Deut 6:13|and thou shalt swear by his name|et per nomen ejus jurabis]]; and: [[2 Par 15:15|with all their heart they swore|In omni corde suo juraverunt]] to the Lord, [[2 Par 15:15|and with all their will they sought him, and they found him|et in tota voluntate sua quæsierunt eum, et invenerunt]]. But what Christ says in the Gospel, [[Matt 5:34|I say to you not to swear at all|Ego dico vobis non jurare omnino]], is not said as a precept simply, but that we should not swear without necessity, so as to avoid the occasion of perjury and the habit of swearing.

paras.t: Humiliatus sum usquequaque, id est, multum afflictus, dejectus et spretus sum; vel me ipsum vehementer humiliavi, contemnendo me propter negligentias et infinitos meos defectus. Idcirco, Domine, vivifica me secundum verbum tuum, id est, gratiam præsta mihi, qua vivam secundum verbum doctrinæ tuæ. Vel, Vivifica me, per gratiæ infusionem, secundum verbum tuum, id est, sicut pollicitus es te gratiam donaturum afflictis et humiliatis. Scriptum enim est: Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria; et alibi: Miserans miserebitur tui; ad vocem clamoris tui, statim ut audierit, respondebit tibi.
paras.en: [[118:107|I have been humbled, O Lord, exceedingly|Humiliatus sum usquequaque]], that is, I have been much afflicted, cast down and despised; or, I have humbled myself greatly, despising myself for my negligences and my numberless failings. Therefore, O Lord, [[118:107|quicken thou me according to thy word|vivifica me secundum verbum tuum]], that is, grant me grace by which I may live according to the word of thy teaching. Or: [[118:107|quicken thou me|Vivifica me]] by the infusion of grace, [[118:107|according to thy word|secundum verbum tuum]], that is, as thou hast promised that thou wilt give grace to the afflicted and the humbled. For it is written: [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]]; and elsewhere: [[Is 30:19|he will surely have pity on thee: at the voice of thy cry, as soon as he shall hear, he will answer thee|Miserans miserebitur tui; ad vocem clamoris tui, statim ut audierit, respondebit tibi]].

paras.t: Voluntaria oris mei, id est preces meas et cuncta quæ cupio, seu voluntarie tibi offero, beneplacita fac, Domine, id est, da gratiam illa taliter ordinare seu exhibere, ut tibi complaceant. Nam quid oremus sicut oportet, nescimus; sed ipse Spiritus postulat pro nobis, id est, infundit nobis quid postulandum sit. Unde orat Apostolus: Deus meus impleat omne desiderium vestrum secundum divitias suas in Christo Jesu. Et judicia tua, id est mandata a te approbata, doce me. Vel, Judicia tua doce me, id est, da mihi gratiam contemplandi divina judicia, quibus unicuique datur quod meruit, ut sciam quam horrendum sit incidere in manus Dei viventis.
paras.en: [[118:108|The free offerings of my mouth|Voluntaria oris mei]], that is, my prayers and all that I desire or offer thee freely, [[118:108|make acceptable, O Lord|beneplacita fac, Domine]], that is, give me grace to order or present them in such a way that they may please thee. For [[Rom 8:26|we know not what we should pray for as we ought|quid oremus sicut oportet, nescimus]]: [[Rom 8:26|but the Spirit himself asketh for us|sed ipse Spiritus postulat pro nobis]], that is, he pours into us what is to be asked. Hence the Apostle prays: [[Phil 4:19|may my God supply all your want, according to his riches|Deus meus impleat omne desiderium vestrum secundum divitias suas]] [[Phil 4:19|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]] [*desiderium*, "desire", where the Douay-Rheims has "want"]. And [[118:108|thy judgments|Et judicia tua]], that is, the commandments approved by thee, [[118:108|teach me|doce me]]. Or: [[118:108|teach me thy judgments|Judicia tua doce me]], that is, give me the grace of contemplating the divine judgments, by which each is given what he has deserved, that I may know it to be [[Heb 10:31|a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God|horrendum sit incidere in manus Dei viventis]].

paras.t: Anima mea in manibus meis semper: id est, in continuo periculo incidendi peccata, et per consequens æternam damnationem, exsisto, propter insidias dæmonum, concupiscentias carnis, et cetera mundi ac corporis impedimenta, quibus a Deo retrahor, atque ad vitia trahor. Per hoc enim quod dicitur anima esse in manibus, designat Scriptura aliquod manifestum periculum, quemadmodum Jonathas dixit de David: Ipse posuit animam suam in manibus suis, et occidit Philistæum. Et idem dixit Jephthe reversus de bello contra Ammonitas. Idem etiam dixit mulier pythonissa ad Saul. Si ergo est anima nostra semper in manibus nostris, id est in tanto periculo, mirum est quod tam intimorati, leves et securi exsistimus. Idcirco veraciter scriptum est: Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia. Et legem tuam non sum oblitus, sed per memoriam et obedientiam eam servavi.
paras.en: [[118:109|My soul is continually in my hands|Anima mea in manibus meis semper]]: that is, I stand in continual danger of falling into sins, and in consequence into eternal damnation, because of the snares of the demons, the lusts of the flesh, and the other hindrances of the world and the body, by which I am drawn back from God and drawn to vices. For by saying that the soul is in the hands, Scripture signifies some open danger, as Jonathas said of David: He [[1 Kings 19:5|put his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine|posuit animam suam in manibus suis, et occidit Philistæum]] [Denis reads "in his hands" and "slew" (*occidit*) for *percussit*]. And Jephte said the same on returning from the war against the Ammonites[[Judg 12:3||]]. The woman with the divining spirit said the same to Saul[[1 Kings 28:21||]]. If, then, our soul is always in our hands, that is, in so great a danger, it is a wonder that we live so fearless, light-minded and secure. Therefore it is truly written: [[Eccles 7:5|The heart of the wise is where there is mourning, and the heart of fools where there is mirth|Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia]]. [[118:109|and I have not forgotten thy law|Et legem tuam non sum oblitus]], but have kept it by remembering and obeying it.

paras.t: Posuerunt peccatores, videlicet dæmones injustique homines, laqueum, id est occasionem ruinæ ac deceptionis, mihi, quatenus me aliquo modo a via Dei averterent. Laquei enim istorum quibus incautos decipiunt, sunt adulatio, laudatio, comminatio, sæculi vanitates, divitiæ temporales, et cetera in quibus maculatur affectus. Et de mandatis tuis non erravi: quia illorum tentationibus et suggestionibus non consensi, prout Salomon monet: Fili mi, si te lactaverint peccatores, ne acquiescas illis.
paras.en: [[118:110|Sinners have laid|Posuerunt peccatores]], namely the demons and unjust men, [[118:110|a snare|laqueum]], that is, an occasion of ruin and deception, [[118:110|for me|mihi]], so as to turn me in some way from the way of God. For the snares with which they deceive the unwary are flattery, praise, threats, the vanities of the world, temporal riches, and the other things by which the affections are stained. [[118:110|but I have not erred from thy precepts|Et de mandatis tuis non erravi]], because I did not consent to their temptations and suggestions, as Solomon warns: [[Prov 1:10|My son, if sinners shall entice thee, consent not to them|Fili mi, si te lactaverint peccatores, ne acquiescas illis]].

paras.t: Hereditate, id est stabili possessione, acquisivi testimonia tua, id est divina præcepta, et cetera verba divino testimonio approbata, utpote omnia sacræ Scripturæ eloquia, in æternum, ita quod eis æternaliter adhærebo; quia exsultatio cordis mei sunt, id est, de eorum possessione atque notitia gaudeo magis, quam de omnibus temporalibus bonis.
paras.en: [[118:111|for an inheritance|Hereditate]], that is, as a lasting possession, [[118:111|I have purchased thy testimonies|acquisivi testimonia tua]], that is, the divine precepts and the other words approved by divine testimony, namely all the utterances of Holy Scripture, [[118:111|for ever|in æternum]], so that I shall cleave to them eternally; [[118:111|because they are the joy of my heart|quia exsultatio cordis mei sunt]], that is, I rejoice more in possessing and knowing them than in all temporal goods.

paras.t: Inclinavi cor meum ad faciendas justificationes tuas, id est tua mandata seu opera quæque, propter quæ justificatur homo a te: et hoc, in æternum, id est jugiter quamdiu sum. Nam et aliqua præcepta implentur in patria magis perfecte quam in via, sicut præceptum caritatis. Propter retributionem æternam, non temporalem, videlicet propter felicitatem cœlestem, ut eam obtineam.
paras.en: [[118:112|I have inclined my heart to do thy justifications|Inclinavi cor meum ad faciendas justificationes tuas]], that is, thy commandments, or all the works for which man is justified by thee; and this [[118:112|for ever|in æternum]], that is, continually as long as I live. For some precepts too are fulfilled more perfectly in the fatherland than on the way, as the precept of charity [that is, in heaven (*patria*) than in this life (*via*)]. [[118:112|for the reward|Propter retributionem]] that is eternal, not temporal, namely for heavenly happiness, that I may obtain it.

paras.t: Sed quum propter mercedem operari, sit opus mercenarii, non filii aut amici, quomodo ait se propter retributionem inclinasse cor suum ad opera bona? Et respondendum, quod sicut timor pure servilis nihil meretur; sic propter solam retributionem operari, nihil meretur, quia utrumque istorum procedit ex privato amore. Sed quemadmodum timor initialis meritorius est, in quantum aliquid habet de caritate adjunctum; sic propter retributionem operari, meritorium est, quando intentio ultima fertur ad Dei honorem seu Deum, quem necesse est principaliter intendi in omni meritorio actu. Postremo, quemadmodum timor filialis maxime complacet Deo; sic tota mente Dei honorem intendere, et propter purum Dei amorem bona agere, maxime sanctum et meritorium est, quoniam hoc ex divino amore causatur. Nihilo minus homo talis implicite agit propter mercedem, eamque aliquo modo intendit, non ex privato amore, sed ex amore divino, in quantum videlicet Deus vult ut operemur propter præmium felicitatis æternæ.
paras.en: But since to work for wages is the work of a hireling, not of a son or a friend, how does he say that he inclined his heart to good works for the reward? The answer is that, just as purely servile fear merits nothing, so working for the reward alone merits nothing, because both proceed from private love [that is, love of self for one's own sake]. But just as initial fear [that is, the fear of beginners, partly servile and partly filial] is meritorious in so far as it has something of charity joined to it, so working for the reward is meritorious when the final intention is borne to God's honour, or to God, who must be chiefly intended in every meritorious act. Lastly, just as filial fear is most pleasing to God, so to intend God's honour with the whole mind and to do good out of pure love of God is most holy and meritorious, since this is caused by divine love. Nevertheless such a man acts implicitly for the reward and in some way intends it, not out of private love but out of divine love, inasmuch as God wills that we work for the prize of eternal happiness.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, recte viventium semita, et splendor animarum. Verbum tuum Christus sit lucerna pedibus nostris et lumen semitis nostris: ut ejus ductu, a mandatis ejus recta intelligamus, et omnem viam iniquitatis semper odio habeamus et declinemus.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, the path of those who live rightly and the brightness of souls: may thy Word, Christ, be a lamp to our feet and a light to our paths, that under his guidance we may understand what is right from his commandments, and may always hate and turn aside from every way of iniquity.

paras.t: Samech. Iniquos odio habui, in quantum iniqui sunt: sic enim et Deo odibiles sunt, juxta illud, Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus. Non autem odio eos secundum quod homines sunt, quum scriptum sit, Diligite inimicos vestros. Amare vero, secundum Philosophum, est alicui bonum velle; odire vero, est velle alteri malum. Iniquis itaque, in quantum sunt homines, debemus velle seu appetere bona, scilicet gratiam modo, et gloriam postmodum. In quantum vero sunt impii, non appetimus eis bonum; hoc enim esset contra justitiam: imo appetimus eis malum pœnæ in præsenti sæculo vel futuro, nisi pœniteant.
paras.en: Samech. [[118:113|I have hated the unjust|Iniquos odio habui]], in so far as they are unjust; for so they are hateful to God too, according to the words: [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful|Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]]. But I do not hate them as they are men, since it is written: [[Matt 5:44|Love your enemies|Diligite inimicos vestros]]. Now to love, according to the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle], is to will good to someone; to hate is to will evil to another. To the unjust, then, in so far as they are men, we ought to will or desire good things, namely grace now and glory afterwards. But in so far as they are wicked we do not desire good for them, for that would be against justice; rather we desire for them the evil of punishment, in this world or the next, unless they repent.

paras.t: Verumtamen circa odium inimicorum et impiorum erraverunt et errant Judæi, arbitrantes secundum legem simpliciter fore odiendos iniquos ac æmulos, eo quod Moyses dicat: Diliges amicum tuum, et odio habebis inimicum tuum. Sed hoc penitus falsum est; et non solum ex Scriptura canonica veteris Testamenti, sed etiam ex gestis antiquorum Sanctorum hujus oppositum comprobatur. Constat enim quod David dilexit Saulem, cui tam frequenter pepercit, quem tam benigne patrem vocavit; qui etiam eum occidit qui se, licet falso, asseruit occidisse Saulem. Similiter filium ejus Isboseth dilexisse ostenditur. Nam eo occiso, dixit latronibus qui eum interfecerunt: Quum homines impii interfecerunt virum innoxium in domo sua, super lectum suum, non quæram sanguinem ejus de manu vestra, et auferam vos de terra? Et idem constat de aliis multis in veteri Testamento. Denique Moyses ait: Ne oderis fratrem tuum in corde tuo, sed publice argue eum, ne habeas super illo peccatum; et iterum, Non quæras ultionem, nec memor eris injuriæ civium tuorum. Salomon quoque loquitur: Ne dicas, Quomodo fecit mihi, sic et faciam ei; et iterum, Quum ceciderit inimicus tuus, ne gaudeas, et in ruina illius ne exsultet cor tuum. Cui concordat sanctus Job, dicens: Si gavisus sum ad ruinam ejus qui me oderat, et exsultavi quod invenisset eum malum. Sed et alibi habetur: Si esurierit inimicus tuus, ciba illum; si sitit, da ei aquam: et Dominus reddet tibi. Et hæc verba inducit Apostolus, probans ex eis inimicos esse amandos.
paras.en: However, the Jews have erred and still err about hatred of enemies and of the wicked, thinking that according to the law the unjust and their rivals are simply to be hated, because Moses says: Thou shalt love thy friend[[Lev 19:18||]], [[Matt 5:43|and hate thy enemy|et odio habebis inimicum tuum]] [the margin gives Lev. xix, 18 and Matth. v, 43: the first half is in Leviticus, the second only in the saying Christ reports]. But this is altogether false, and the opposite is proved not only from the canonical Scripture of the Old Testament but also from the deeds of the ancient saints. For it is plain that David loved Saul, whom he spared so often[[1 Kings 26:12||]] and called father so kindly [as at 1 Kings 24:12]; who even slew the man who claimed, though falsely, to have slain Saul[[2 Kings 1:15||]]. He is likewise shown to have loved Saul's son Isboseth. For when he had been killed, David said to the robbers who slew him: [[2 Kings 4:11|when wicked men have slain an innocent man in his own house, upon his bed, shall I not require his blood at your hand, and take you away from the earth?|Quum homines impii interfecerunt virum innoxium in domo sua, super lectum suum, non quæram sanguinem ejus de manu vestra, et auferam vos de terra]] [the margin gives "Ibid. v, 11"; the words are at 2 Kings 4:11.] And the same is plain of many others in the Old Testament. Finally Moses says: [[Lev 19:17|Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thy heart: But reprove him openly, lest thou incur sin through him|Ne oderis fratrem tuum in corde tuo, sed publice argue eum, ne habeas super illo peccatum]]; and again: [[Lev 19:18|Seek not revenge, nor be mindful of the injury of thy citizens|Non quæras ultionem, nec memor eris injuriæ civium tuorum]]. Solomon too says: [[Prov 24:29|Say not: I will do to him as he hath done to me|Ne dicas, Quomodo fecit mihi, sic et faciam ei]]; and again: [[Prov 24:17|When thy enemy shall fall, be not glad, and in his ruin let not thy heart rejoice|Quum ceciderit inimicus tuus, ne gaudeas, et in ruina illius ne exsultet cor tuum]]. With which holy Job agrees, saying: [[Job 31:29|If I have been glad at the downfall of him that hated me, and have rejoiced that evil had found him|Si gavisus sum ad ruinam ejus qui me oderat, et exsultavi quod invenisset eum malum]]. And it is said elsewhere too: [[Prov 25:21|If thy enemy be hungry, give him to eat: if he thirst, give him water to drink|Si esurierit inimicus tuus, ciba illum; si sitit, da ei aquam]]: [[Prov 25:22|and the Lord will reward thee|et Dominus reddet tibi]]. And the Apostle brings in these words, proving from them that enemies are to be loved[[Rom 12:20||]].

paras.t: Et legem tuam dilexi, sicut nunc dictum est, super millia auri et argenti. Propter quod scriptum est: Parati sumus magis mori, quam patrias Dei leges prævaricari. Si autem diligo legem tuam, ergo et observatores ipsius, videlicet justos.
paras.en: [[118:113|and have loved thy law|Et legem tuam dilexi]], as was said just now, [[118:72|above thousands of gold and silver|super millia auri et argenti]]. Because of this it is written: [[2 Mach 7:2|we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of God, received from our fathers|Parati sumus magis mori, quam patrias Dei leges prævaricari]]. And if I love thy law, then I love those who keep it too, namely the just.

paras.t: Adjutor meus, cooperando mihi per gratiam: sicut dicit Apostolus, Non autem ego, sed gratia Dei mecum; et susceptor meus, id est precum mearum auditor, meique ad te confugientis misericors amplexator: quemadmodum testatus es, Eum qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras; es tu, et in verbum tuum quo misericordiam promisisti, supersperavi, sciens infallibiliter verum esse quod spondes.
paras.en: [[118:114|Thou art my helper|Adjutor meus]], working with me by grace, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 15:10|Yet not I, but the grace of God with me|Non autem ego, sed gratia Dei mecum]]; [[118:114|and my protector|et susceptor meus]] [*susceptor*, "one who takes up", which Denis goes on to explain], that is, the hearer of my prayers and the merciful embracer of me as I flee to thee, as thou hast testified: [[John 6:37|him that cometh to me, I will not cast out|Eum qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras]]; [[118:114|thou art|es tu]]; [[118:114|and in thy word|et in verbum tuum]], by which thou hast promised mercy, [[118:114|I have greatly hoped|supersperavi]], knowing infallibly that what thou pledgest is true.

paras.t: Idcirco ut benignitatem æternam promerear, Declinate a me, maligni, quicumque sint illi, et o vos, cogitationes inanes et malæ, abite a me, nihilque mihi propinquet, quo a Deo elonger. Dicit autem et optat malignos a se recedere, non quod tentationes diaboli persecutionesque mundi absolute abhorreat, quum scriptum sit, Per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum Dei; sed dicit, Declinate a me, maligni, causa animandi se ipsum contra malignos, quatenus consensum deneget eis, eosque detestetur et vilipendat, in quantum sibi in via Dei resistere moliuntur. Et scrutabor mandata Dei mei diligenter atque humiliter, ut sciam ea luculenter, impleamque reverenter.
paras.en: Therefore, that I may merit the eternal kindness: [[118:115|Depart from me, ye malignant|Declinate a me, maligni]], whoever they be; and you, empty and evil thoughts, go away from me, and let nothing come near me by which I might be drawn far from God. He says this and wishes the malignant to depart from him, not because he shrinks absolutely from the temptations of the devil and the persecutions of the world, since it is written: [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God|Per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum Dei]]; but he says [[118:115|Depart from me, ye malignant|Declinate a me, maligni]] in order to rouse himself against the malignant, that he may refuse them consent and detest and despise them, in so far as they strive to withstand him on the way of God. [[118:115|and I will search the commandments of my God|Et scrutabor mandata Dei mei]] diligently and humbly, that I may know them clearly and fulfil them reverently.

paras.t: Suscipe me brachiis pietatis immensæ, secundum eloquium tuum, quo dixisti, Convertimini ad me, et convertar ad vos, et vivam per gratiam multo felicius, quam vivo per naturam seu animam; et non confundas me, nec confundi permittas, ab exspectatione mea, id est a bono exspectato a te, quod est gratia in præsenti, atque æterna beatitudo in cœlo. Exspectatio autem ista, est idem quod spes: quoniam spes est certa exspectatio futuræ felicitatis. Orat ergo ne frustretur spe sua, sed effectum et fructum spei mereatur sortiri. Nam et hoc Dominus per Isaiam promisit: Ego (inquiens) Dominus, super quo non confundentur omnes qui exspectant eum. Unde apud eumdem dicitur: Deus judicii Dominus; beati omnes qui exspectant eum. Hinc in Ecclesiastico habetur: Nullus speravit in Domino, et confusus est.
paras.en: [[118:116|Uphold me|Suscipe me]] [*suscipe*, "take me up"] with the arms of thy boundless love, [[118:116|according to thy word|secundum eloquium tuum]], in which thou saidst: [[Zach 1:3|Turn ye to me|Convertimini ad me]], [[Zach 1:3|and I will turn to you|et convertar ad vos]]; [[118:116|and I shall live|et vivam]] by grace far more happily than I live by nature, or by the soul; [[118:116|and let me not be confounded|et non confundas me]] [literally "and do not confound me"], nor allow me to be confounded, [[118:116|in my expectation|ab exspectatione mea]], that is, away from the good I expect from thee, which is grace in the present and eternal beatitude in heaven. Now this expectation is the same as hope, since hope is the sure expectation of future happiness. He prays, then, that he may not be cheated of his hope, but may merit to obtain the effect and fruit of hope. For the Lord promised this too through Isaias: [[Is 49:23|I am the Lord|Ego (inquiens) Dominus]] (he says), [[Is 49:23|for they shall not be confounded that wait for him|super quo non confundentur omnes qui exspectant eum]] [the margin gives Is. xliv, 23; the words are at Is 49:23]. Hence it is said in the same prophet: [[Is 30:18|the Lord is the God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him|Deus judicii Dominus; beati omnes qui exspectant eum]]. So it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 2:11|no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded|Nullus speravit in Domino, et confusus est]].

paras.t: Adjuva me per gratiam incessantem, et salvus ero ab omni periculo. Nempe si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Propterea sanctus Job Domino ait: Pone me juxta te, et cujusvis manus pugnet contra me. Nemo enim omnipotenti Deo resistere valet. Et ideo in libro Esther dicitur: Si decreveris salvare nos, continuo liberabimur. Et meditabor in justificationibus tuis, id est mandatis, semper, id est omni tempore apto ac debito. Dicitur enim res semper fieri, dum nunquam omittitur quando fieri debet.
paras.en: [[118:117|Help me|Adjuva me]] by unceasing grace, [[118:117|and I shall be saved|et salvus ero]] from every danger. For indeed, [[Rom 8:31|If God be for us, who is against us|si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos]]? Therefore holy Job says to the Lord: [[Job 17:3|set me beside thee, and let any man's hand fight against me|Pone me juxta te, et cujusvis manus pugnet contra me]]. For no one can resist almighty God [the margin gives Gen. i, 19, which does not fit; compare Esth 13:9, 11]. And so it is said in the book of Esther: If thou determine to save us, we shall be delivered at once[[Esth 13:9||]] [Denis's wording; the verse reads "if thou determine to save Israel"]. [[118:117|and I will meditate|Et meditabor]] [[118:117|on thy justifications|in justificationibus tuis]], that is, thy commandments, [[118:117|always|semper]], that is, at every fitting and due time. For a thing is said to be done always when it is never left undone when it ought to be done.

paras.t: Sprevisti, o Domine, omnes discedentes a justitiis tuis, id est omnes in malo perseverantes, tua mandata non observantes. Sicut enim Deus hos odit, sic eos contemnit. Unde scriptum est: Abominatio est Domino via impii. Rursusque Sapientia ait: Arrogantiam et superbiam, et viam pravam, et os bilingue detestor. Quia injusta cogitatio eorum. Nam divinæ justitiæ contrariatur, juxta illud Michææ: Væ qui cogitatis inutile, etc., quoniam contra Deum est manus eorum.
paras.en: [[118:118|Thou hast despised|Sprevisti]], O Lord, [[118:118|all them that fall off|omnes discedentes]] from thy justices [the margin notes the reading *judiciis*, "judgments", as in the Vulgate; Denis reads *justitiis*], that is, all who persevere in evil and do not keep thy commandments. For as God hates these, so he despises them. Hence it is written: [[Prov 15:9|The way of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord|Abominatio est Domino via impii]]. And again Wisdom says: [[Prov 8:13|I hate arrogance, and pride, and every wicked way, and a mouth with a double tongue|Arrogantiam et superbiam, et viam pravam, et os bilingue detestor]]. [[118:118|for their thought is unjust|Quia injusta cogitatio eorum]]: for it is contrary to the divine justice, according to the words of Micheas: [[Mich 2:1|Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable|Væ qui cogitatis inutile]], etc., [[Mich 2:1|because their hand is against God|quoniam contra Deum est manus eorum]].

paras.t: Prævaricatores, id est legem Altissimi transgredientes, reputavi omnes peccatores terræ: de quibus scriptum est: Domine, omnes qui te derelinquunt, confundentur; recedentes a te, in terra scribentur; ideo dilexi testimonia tua interiori affectu, et exsecutione fideli, ne ego illis compar efficiar.
paras.en: [[118:119|prevaricators|Prævaricatores]], that is, transgressors of the law of the Most High, [[118:119|I have accounted all the sinners of the earth|reputavi omnes peccatores terræ]], of whom it is written: [[Jer 17:13|O Lord|Domine]], [[Jer 17:13|all that forsake thee shall be confounded: they that depart from thee, shall be written in the earth|omnes qui te derelinquunt, confundentur; recedentes a te, in terra scribentur]]; [[118:119|therefore have I loved thy testimonies|ideo dilexi testimonia tua]] with inward affection and faithful performance, lest I be made like them.

paras.t: Confige timore tuo carnes meas, id est, carnales motus existentes in me refrena atque mortifica timore futuri judicii æternarumque pœnarum; a judiciis enim tuis timui: id est, ex consideratione particularis judicii, quo statim dum moriar a te judicabor, ex consideratione quoque extremi judicii, et propter judicia tua jam facta, quibus luxuriosos atque carnales destruxisti, sicut in diluvio factum est quando omnis caro corrupit viam suam, perterritus sum ne condemner. Vehementer quippe metuenda sunt ista judicia. Imo qui ea diligenter perpendit, sancto timore configitur, atque carnalibus motibus reluctatur.
paras.en: [[118:120|Pierce thou my flesh with thy fear|Confige timore tuo carnes meas]], that is, restrain and mortify the carnal motions that are in me by the fear of the judgment to come and of the eternal pains; [[118:120|for I am afraid of thy judgments|a judiciis enim tuis timui]]: that is, from considering the particular judgment, by which I shall be judged by thee as soon as I die, and from considering the last judgment too, and because of thy judgments already carried out, by which thou hast destroyed the lustful and the carnal, as was done in the flood when [[Gen 6:12|all flesh had corrupted its way|omnis caro corrupit viam suam]], I am terrified lest I be condemned. For these judgments are greatly to be feared; indeed, whoever weighs them carefully is pierced with holy fear and struggles against carnal motions.

paras.t: Precatio. Suscipe nos in gratiam tuam, Domine Deus, et non confundas nos ab æternæ salutis benedictione, quam a te exspectamus; tribue, quæsumus, nos in justificationibus tuis perseveranter meditari, et te adjuvante, cum integra fide præsenti vita dissolvi.
paras.en: Prayer. Take us up into thy grace, O Lord God, and let us not be confounded in our expectation of the blessing of eternal salvation, which we await from thee; grant, we beseech thee, that we may meditate perseveringly on thy justifications, and, with thy help, be released from this present life with faith unbroken.

paras.t: Ain. Feci judicium, diligenter discutiendo et dijudicando me ipsum, discernendo bonum a malo, verum a falso, purum a polluto; vel, Feci judicium subditis, quibus præfectus sum; et justitiam, dando unicuique quod suum est, me ipsum juste corrigendo, Deum in omnibus atque præ omnibus venerando, proximis quoque faciendo sicut mihi fieri cupio. Hæc duo Deus præcipue quærit a nobis, prout habetur apud Michæam: Indicabo tibi, o homo, quid sit bonum, et quid Dominus requirat a te: utique facere judicium, etc. Non tradas, nec tradi permittas me calumniantibus me, id est voluntati et potestati eorum qui mihi calumniam inferunt, quærentes decipere, inficere, subvertere animam meam. Non ergo, o Domine, permittas me vinci, aut dæmonibus subdi. Hinc in Ecclesiastico dicitur: Dominator vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in cogitatu et consilio eorum, etc., et incidam in conspectu adversariorum meorum; et animæ irreverenti ne tradas me.
paras.en: Ain. [[118:121|I have done judgment|Feci judicium]], carefully examining and judging myself, discerning good from evil, the true from the false, the pure from the defiled; or, [[118:121|I have done judgment|Feci judicium]] for the subjects over whom I am set; [[118:121|and justice|et justitiam]], giving to each what is his: correcting myself justly, honouring God in all things and above all things, and doing to my neighbours as I wish to be done to me. These two things God chiefly asks of us, as is said in Micheas: [[Mich 6:8|I will shew thee, O man, what is good, and what the Lord requireth of thee: Verily to do judgment|Indicabo tibi, o homo, quid sit bonum, et quid Dominus requirat a te: utique facere judicium]], etc. [[118:121|give me not up|Non tradas]], nor allow me to be given up, [[118:121|to them that slander me|me calumniantibus me]], that is, to the will and power of those who bring calumny against me, seeking to deceive, infect and overthrow my soul. Do not, then, O Lord, let me be overcome or made subject to the demons. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 23:1|sovereign ruler of my life, leave me not|Dominator vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me]] in the thought and [[Ecclus 23:1|to their counsel|consilio eorum]] [Denis adds "in the thought", from v. 2], etc., [[Ecclus 23:3|and I fall before my adversaries|et incidam in conspectu adversariorum meorum]]; and [[Ecclus 23:6|give me not over to a shameless and foolish mind|animæ irreverenti ne tradas me]].

paras.t: Suscipe servum tuum in bonum, benigne ignoscendo imperfectionibus ejus, et ejus obsequium clementer acceptando, eique gratiam refundendo, qua semper proficiat; non calumnientur me superbi, id est, justam causam calumniandi me non inveniant dæmones in superbia obstinati, et homines eorum vestigia secuti.
paras.en: [[118:122|Uphold thy servant unto good|Suscipe servum tuum in bonum]], kindly pardoning his imperfections, mercifully accepting his service, and pouring grace back into him, by which he may always advance; [[118:122|let not the proud calumniate me|non calumnientur me superbi]], that is, let not the demons hardened in pride, and the men who have followed in their steps, find just cause to calumniate me.

paras.t: Oculi mei defecerunt in salutare tuum, et in eloquium justitiæ tuæ. Hoc est quod paulo ante dictum ac variis modis expositum est: Defecit in salutare tuum anima mea; Defecerunt oculi mei in eloquium tuum. Sicut enim anima, sic oculi interiores, de quibus nunc agitur, deficere asseruntur in salutare Dei: quod qualiter intelligendum sit, illic quæratur.
paras.en: [[118:123|My eyes have fainted after thy salvation: and for the word of thy justice|Oculi mei defecerunt in salutare tuum, et in eloquium justitiæ tuæ]]. This is what was said a little before and explained in various ways: [[118:81|My soul hath fainted after thy salvation|Defecit in salutare tuum anima mea]]; [[118:82|My eyes have failed for thy word|Defecerunt oculi mei in eloquium tuum]]. For as the soul, so the inner eyes, which are spoken of here, are said to faint after the salvation of God; how this is to be understood may be looked for there.

paras.t: Fac cum servo tuo, videlicet mecum et unoquoque fideli, secundum misericordiam tuam, quæ vere immensa est, et non secundum malitiam meam innumeram; sed pietatis tuæ abyssum declara in me, et sicut me conspicis indigere, sic subvenire dignare: quemadmodum a Daniele supplicatur: Non confundas nos, sed fac nobiscum juxta mansuetudinem tuam, et secundum multitudinem misericordiæ tuæ. Neque enim in justificationibus nostris prosternimus preces ante faciem tuam, sed in miserationibus tuis multis. Et justificationes tuas, id est mandata tua justificantia, doce me.
paras.en: [[118:124|Deal with thy servant|Fac cum servo tuo]], namely with me and with each of the faithful, [[118:124|according to thy mercy|secundum misericordiam tuam]], which is truly boundless, and not according to my numberless wickedness; but show forth in me the abyss of thy loving-kindness, and as thou seest me in need, so deign to come to my help, as Daniel prays: [[Dan 3:42|Put us not to confusion, but deal with us according to thy meekness, and according to the multitude of thy mercies|Non confundas nos, sed fac nobiscum juxta mansuetudinem tuam, et secundum multitudinem misericordiæ tuæ]] [the prayer of Azarias in the furnace; no margin note here, the next note reads "Ibid. ix, 18"]. [[Dan 9:18|for it is not for our justifications that we present our prayers before thy face, but for the multitude of thy tender mercies|Neque enim in justificationibus nostris prosternimus preces ante faciem tuam, sed in miserationibus tuis multis]]. And [[118:124|thy justifications|Et justificationes tuas]], that is, thy commandments that justify, [[118:124|teach me|doce me]].

paras.t: Et decet te, nam Servus tuus sum ego: idcirco da mihi intellectum divinitus illuminatum seu intelligentiam puram, ut sciam testimonia tua, id est credenda et operanda.
paras.en: And it becomes thee, for [[118:125|I am thy servant|Servus tuus sum ego]]: therefore [[118:125|give me understanding|da mihi intellectum]], divinely enlightened, or pure intelligence, [[118:125|that I may know thy testimonies|ut sciam testimonia tua]], that is, what is to be believed and what is to be done.

paras.t: Tempus faciendi, Domine, id est, hora est ut mihi concedas, propter pericula imminentia. Nam dissipaverunt legem tuam: id est, hæretici, doctores perversi, Judæi, et ceteri reprobi legem evangelicam et divinam perverterunt, et quantum in se est, annihilaverunt, eam mendaciter exponendo, impie blasphemando, contumaciter transgrediendo.
paras.en: [[118:126|It is time, O Lord, to do|Tempus faciendi, Domine]], that is, it is the hour for thee to grant it to me, because of the dangers that threaten. For [[118:126|they have dissipated thy law|dissipaverunt legem tuam]]: that is, heretics, perverse teachers, Jews and the other reprobate have perverted the gospel and divine law and, as far as in them lies, have brought it to nothing, expounding it falsely, blaspheming it impiously and transgressing it obstinately.

paras.t: Ideo dilexi mandata tua: id est, quanto legem tuam conspicio amplius dissipari ab illis, tanto ardentiori zelo inflammor, ut eam recuperem, confirmem, observem. Unde dilexi mandata tua super aurum et topazion, id est plus quam omne aurum aut lapidem pretiosissimum nomine topazion. In hac enim lege divina consistit sapientia vera: idcirco de amore legis et mandatorum Dei verissime dici potest illud: Pretiosior est cunctis opibus; et omnia quæ desiderantur, huic non valent comparari. Et alibi: Non dabitur aurum obryzum pro ea, nec appendetur argentum in commutatione ejus; non conferetur tinctis Indiæ coloribus, nec lapidi sardonycho pretiosissimo, vel sapphiro, etc.; non adæquabitur ei topazius de Æthiopia. Est autem topazion lapis pretiosissimus, duplicem habens colorem, videlicet auri purissimi, et alium ætherea claritate splendentem, cujus aspectus oculis intuentium jucundissimus fertur. Hic lapis adeo carus est, ut reges nil eo locupletius arbitrentur in suis thesauris.
paras.en: [[118:127|Therefore have I loved thy commandments|Ideo dilexi mandata tua]]: that is, the more I see thy law dissipated by them, the more ardent the zeal with which I am inflamed to recover it, strengthen it and keep it. Hence [[118:127|have I loved thy commandments above gold and the topaz|dilexi mandata tua super aurum et topazion]], that is, more than all gold, or the most precious stone called topaz. For true wisdom consists in this divine law; therefore of the love of the law and commandments of God it can most truly be said: [[Prov 3:15|She is more precious than all riches: and all the things that are desired, are not to be compared to her|Pretiosior est cunctis opibus; et omnia quæ desiderantur, huic non valent comparari]]. And elsewhere: [[Job 28:15|The finest gold shall not purchase it, neither shall silver be weighed in exchange for it|Non dabitur aurum obryzum pro ea, nec appendetur argentum in commutatione ejus]]; [[Job 28:16|It shall not be compared with the dyed colours of India, or with the most precious stone sardonyx, or the sapphire|non conferetur tinctis Indiæ coloribus, nec lapidi sardonycho pretiosissimo, vel sapphiro]], etc.; [[Job 28:19|The topaz of Ethiopia shall not be equal to it|non adæquabitur ei topazius de Æthiopia]]. Now the topaz is a most precious stone, having two colours, namely that of the purest gold and another shining with the clearness of the sky, and its look is said to be most delightful to the eyes of those who gaze on it.
