This stone is so dear that kings think they have nothing richer in their treasuries.

paras.t: Propterea, scilicet propter causam qua tua mandata dilexi, ad omnia mandata tua dirigebar, mente, ore et opere, quoniam unum observari non potest, si aliud negligatur; omnem viam iniquam, id est omne peccatum, odio habui, non solum propter pœnam sequentem, sed propter ipsam deformitatem peccati, et maxime quia displicet Creatori sublimi et benedicto.
paras.en: [[118:128|Therefore|Propterea]], namely for the reason for which I loved thy commandments, [[118:128|was I directed to all thy commandments|ad omnia mandata tua dirigebar]], in mind, word and deed, since one cannot be kept if another is neglected; [[118:128|all wicked ways|omnem viam iniquam]] [literally "every wicked way"], that is, every sin, [[118:128|I have hated|odio habui]], not only because of the punishment that follows, but because of the very ugliness of sin, and above all because it displeases the most high and blessed Creator.

paras.t: Ecce quam ardentissimæ preces, quam saluberrima documenta, quam perfectissima opera continentur ac describuntur in psalmo præsenti. Qui ergo hæc opera habet, Deo gratus exsistat, et alios instruat. Qui vero non habet, studeat ea habere, studeat documenta ista implere, studeat preces istas tam ardenter Salvatori offerre, quod gratiam sortiatur tam perfecte vivendi, ut omnia ista sibi conveniant, et ea in propria persona decantet ad gloriam Dei mente jucunda atque gratissima, dicens cum sancto Apostolo: Gratia Dei sum id quod sum; cum Virgine quoque beata, incomparabiliter excellentissima: Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus.
paras.en: See what most ardent prayers, what most wholesome teachings, what most perfect works are contained and described in the present psalm. Let him, then, who has these works be grateful to God and instruct others. And let him who has them not strive to have them, strive to fulfil these teachings, strive to offer these prayers so ardently to the Saviour that he may obtain the grace of living so perfectly that all these things may fit him, and he may sing them in his own person to the glory of God with a joyful and most grateful mind, saying with the holy Apostle: [[1 Cor 15:10|by the grace of God, I am what I am|Gratia Dei sum id quod sum]]; and also with the blessed Virgin, beyond compare most excellent: [[Luke 1:49|Because he that is mighty hath done great things to me: and holy is his name|Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus]].

paras.t: Precatio. Dona nobis, omnipotens Pater, mandata tua super aurum et topazion diligere, et omnem viam iniquam odio habere, et ab ea declinare: ut tua protectione defensi, a calumnia superborum valeamus liberari.
paras.en: Prayer. Grant us, almighty Father, to love thy commandments above gold and the topaz, and to hate every wicked way and turn aside from it, that, defended by thy protection, we may be delivered from the calumny of the proud.

paras.t: Phe. Mirabilia testimonia tua. Sicut prædictum est, divinæ legis duæ sunt partes, videlicet mandata, quæ pertinent ad agenda, et testimonia, quæ pertinent ad credenda. Quamvis autem miranda et mirabilia sint quæ præcipimur agere, seu mandata, multo tamen mirabiliora sunt quæ jubemur credere. Nam præcepta moralia non excedunt naturalis rationis dictamen : aliqua tamen jubemur agere quæ naturalem rationem excedunt, secundum quosdam doctores, sicut inimicum diligere, et adversantibus bona impendere. Sicut enim naturale est amantem amare, et benefacienti benefacere ; sic naturale videtur odientem odio habere, et mala inferenti mala rependere. Porro ea quæ nobis credenda proponuntur, omnem prorsus rationem transcendunt, sicut sunt trinitas Personarum, incarnatio Verbi, integritas Matris, existentia Christi sub formis Sacramenti. Quum ergo tam mirabilia sint testimonia tua, o Domine, ideo scrutata est ea anima mea, optans ac satagens ea utcumque intelligere. Perscrutatio namque ex admiratione procedit. Et sicut philosophi ex admiratione cœperunt philosophari, quia videntes effectus mirabiles, ut sunt eclipsis solis, terræ motus et alia, et causam ignorantes, mirati sunt, et causam horum scrutari cœperunt ; sic sancti doctores inspicientes sacram Scripturam, et mirabilia Dei testimonia in ipsa videntes, mirati sunt ; cœperuntque intellectum eorum scrutari, et Deo illustrante profecerunt, quamvis perfecte ea comprehendere nequierunt.
paras.en: Phe. [[118:129|Thy testimonies are wonderful|Mirabilia testimonia tua]]. As was said before, the divine law has two parts: the commandments, which concern what is to be done, and the testimonies, which concern what is to be believed. Now although the things we are commanded to do, that is, the commandments, are wondrous and wonderful, yet far more wonderful are the things we are bidden to believe. For the moral precepts do not exceed the dictate of natural reason; yet, according to certain doctors, we are bidden to do some things that exceed natural reason, such as to love an enemy and to do good to those who oppose us[[Luke 6:27||]]. For as it is natural to love one who loves, and to do good to one who does good, so it seems natural to hate one who hates, and to repay evil to one who inflicts evil. But the things put before us to be believed transcend all reason altogether, such as the Trinity of Persons, the Incarnation of the Word, the integrity of the Mother [that is, her virginity kept intact], the existence of Christ under the forms of the Sacrament. Since, then, thy testimonies, O Lord, are so wonderful, [[118:129|therefore my soul hath sought them|ideo scrutata est ea anima mea]] [*scrutata est*, "hath searched them out"], desiring and striving to understand them in some measure. For searching proceeds from wonder. And as the philosophers began to philosophize from wonder, because, seeing wonderful effects, such as an eclipse of the sun, earthquakes and the like, and not knowing the cause, they wondered, and began to search out the cause of these things; so the holy doctors, looking into Sacred Scripture and seeing in it the wonderful testimonies of God, wondered, and began to search out their meaning, and by God's enlightening made progress, although they could not comprehend them perfectly.

paras.t: Sed quum Salomon asserat, Sicut qui mel comedit multum, non est ei bonum, sic qui perscrutator est majestatis, opprimetur a gloria ; et Paulus, Non plus sapere quam oportet, sed sapere ad sobrietatem ; et rursus, Noli (inquit) altum sapere, sed time ; et iterum scriptum est, Altiora te ne quæsieris, et fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris : quid est quod Propheta et quilibet justus in psalmo isto dicit se divina velle scrutari, dicendo, Considerabo mirabilia de lege tua ; et, Exercebor in mirabilibus tuis ; nunc quoque, Mirabilia testimonia tua, ideo scrutata est ea anima mea ? Et respondendum, quod quædam est perscrutatio curiosa et animosa, dum homo proprio innitens ingenio, quærit divina comprehendere seu cognoscere ultra suæ capacitatis mensuram. Et ista culpabilis atque vitanda est. Unde ab Ecclesiastico dicitur : In pluribus operibus Dei ne fueris curiosus. Non est enim tibi necessarium, ea quæ abscondita sunt, oculis tuis videre. Alia vero est perscrutatio pia et humilis, dum homo divino innitens subsidio, studet divina cognoscere, quatenus in Dei amore proficiat, Beatorumque contemplationi, quantum possibile est, appropinquet. Et hæc bona et sancta est, ad quam hortabatur Christus Judæos : Scrutamini, inquiens, Scripturas, quia illæ sunt quæ testimonium perhibent de me. Et Thessalonicenses laudat beatissimus Lucas, dicens quod quotidie perscrutabantur Scripturas.
paras.en: But since Solomon asserts: [[Prov 25:27|As it is not good for a man to eat much honey, so he that is a searcher of majesty shall be overwhelmed by glory|Sicut qui mel comedit multum, non est ei bonum, sic qui perscrutator est majestatis, opprimetur a gloria]]; and Paul: [[Rom 12:3|not to be more wise than it behoveth to be wise, but to be wise unto sobriety|Non plus sapere quam oportet, sed sapere ad sobrietatem]]; and again: [[Rom 11:20|Be not|Noli]] (he says) [[Rom 11:20|highminded, but fear|altum sapere, sed time]]; and once more it is written: [[Ecclus 3:22|Seek not the things that are too high for thee, and search not into things above thy ability|Altiora te ne quæsieris, et fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris]]: how is it that the Prophet, and every just man, says in this psalm that he wishes to search into divine things, saying: [[118:18|I will consider the wondrous things of thy law|Considerabo mirabilia de lege tua]]; and: [[118:27|I shall be exercised in thy wondrous works|Exercebor in mirabilibus tuis]]; and now also: [[118:129|Thy testimonies are wonderful|Mirabilia testimonia tua]], [[118:129|therefore my soul hath sought them|ideo scrutata est ea anima mea]]? The answer is that there is one kind of searching that is curious and presumptuous, when a man, relying on his own wit, seeks to comprehend or know divine things beyond the measure of his capacity. And this is blameworthy and to be avoided. Hence it is said by Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 3:22|In many of his works be not curious|In pluribus operibus Dei ne fueris curiosus]]. [[Ecclus 3:23|For it is not necessary for thee to see with thy eyes those things that are hid.|Non est enim tibi necessarium, ea quæ abscondita sunt, oculis tuis videre]] But there is another searching, devout and humble, when a man, relying on divine help, strives to know divine things, so that he may advance in the love of God and draw near, as far as is possible, to the contemplation of the Blessed. And this is good and holy, and to it Christ exhorted the Jews, saying: [[John 5:39|Search|Scrutamini]], he said, [[John 5:39|the scriptures|Scripturas]], for [[John 5:39|the same are they that give testimony of me|illæ sunt quæ testimonium perhibent de me]]. And the most blessed Luke praises the Thessalonians, saying that they were [[Acts 17:11|daily searching the scriptures|quotidie perscrutabantur Scripturas]] [in Acts it is the Jews of Berea who are praised as nobler than those of Thessalonica].

paras.t: Declaratio sermonum tuorum, id est elucidatio sacræ Scripturæ a Spiritu Sancto infusa, sive per homines divinitus illustratos aliis facta, illuminat mentem humanam ad recte intelligendum ac juste vivendum. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Sacras litteras nosti, quæ te possunt instruere. Et intellectum, id est formatam atque salubrem notitiam, dat parvulis, id est humilibus. Propter quod Christus ait : Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis. Et Sapientia ait : Si quis est parvulus, veniat ad me. Superborum enim cognitio informis, vana, atque damnosa est, quum non sit caritati virtuosæque vitæ unita.
paras.en: [[118:130|The declaration of thy words|Declaratio sermonum tuorum]], that is, the elucidation of Sacred Scripture infused by the Holy Ghost, or given to others by men divinely enlightened, [[118:130|giveth light|illuminat]] to the human mind, for understanding rightly and living justly. For which reason the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 3:15|thou hast known the holy scriptures which can instruct thee|Sacras litteras nosti, quæ te possunt instruere]]. [[118:130|And giveth understanding|Et intellectum]], that is, formed and wholesome knowledge [*formata*, "formed", that is, informed by charity], [[118:130|to little ones|dat parvulis]], that is, to the humble. For which reason Christ says: [[Luke 10:21|I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent and hast revealed them to little ones|Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]. And Wisdom says: [[Prov 9:4|Whosoever is a little one, let him come to me|Si quis est parvulus, veniat ad me]]. For the knowledge of the proud is unformed, vain and harmful, since it is not united to charity and a virtuous life.

paras.t: Os meum corporale aperui orando, psallendo, quærendo, gemendo, et attraxi spiritum, id est aerem, sine cujus attractione vox oris formari non potest. Vel sic : Os meum intellectuale, videlicet intellectum, quo verbum mentis profertur, aperui, id est, ad gratiam Dei recipiendam affectuose disposui, juxta illud, Os suum aperuit sapientiæ ; et attraxi spiritum, id est, merito hujus sanctæ affectionis seu apertionis hausi atque recepi spiritum sapientiæ et intelligentiæ, imo Spiritum Sanctum, qui in corde desiderantium suum adventum descendere non abhorret. Hinc namque in libro Sapientiæ dicitur : Optavi, et datus est mihi sensus; invocavi, et venit in me spiritus sapientiæ. Sic ergo os aperui, spiritumque attraxi, quia mandata tua, o Domine, desiderabam affectuosissime, quatenus ea clare cognoscerem, semperque perfectius observarem : quoniam non proficere in via mandatorum tuorum, est deficere. Ex ardenti autem desiderio causatur utraque ista apertio, ac bina attractio : nam vehementer cupiens, frequenter suspirat ac gemit.
paras.en: [[118:131|I opened|aperui]] [[118:131|my mouth|Os meum]], my bodily mouth, in praying, singing psalms, seeking, groaning, [[118:131|and panted|et attraxi spiritum]] [*attraxi spiritum*, literally "I drew in breath (spirit)", which Denis takes in both senses], that is, I drew in air, without the drawing in of which the voice of the mouth cannot be formed. Or thus: [[118:131|I opened|aperui]] [[118:131|my mouth|Os meum]] of the intellect, namely the understanding, by which the word of the mind is uttered: that is, I disposed it with affection to receive the grace of God, according to that saying: [[Prov 31:26|She hath opened her mouth to wisdom|Os suum aperuit sapientiæ]] [the margin gives "Ibid. xxvi" (that is, Proverbs); the words are Prov 31:26]; [[118:131|and panted|et attraxi spiritum]], that is, by the merit of this holy affection or opening I drew in and received the spirit of wisdom and understanding, nay, the Holy Ghost, who does not disdain to descend into the heart of those who desire his coming. For hence it is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 7:7|I wished, and understanding was given me: and I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came upon me|Optavi, et datus est mihi sensus; invocavi, et venit in me spiritus sapientiæ]]. So, then, I opened my mouth and drew in breath, [[118:131|because I longed for thy commandments|quia mandata tua, o Domine, desiderabam]], O Lord, most affectionately, that I might know them clearly and keep them ever more perfectly: for not to advance in the way of thy commandments is to fall back. Both this opening and the twofold drawing in are caused by ardent desire: for one who desires vehemently sighs and groans often.

paras.t: Adspice in me, non oculo districtæ ultionis, sed paternæ pietatis, et miserere mei, dando mihi gratiam contemplationis purissimæ, secundum judicium diligentium nomen tuum, id est, sicut diligentes te judicant sibi necessarium aut salubre. Vel, Secundum judicium diligentium nomen tuum, id est secundum judicium tuæ discretionis, quod fecisti in tuos dilectores, quos tua sapientia judicavit esse implendos misericordia tua. Vel, Secundum judicium diligentium nomen tuum, id est, sicut decrevisti facere diligentibus te : quibus tanta ac talia bona dare disposuisti, quod oculus ea non vidit, nec auris audivit, secundum Apostolum.
paras.en: [[118:132|Look thou upon me|Adspice in me]], not with the eye of strict vengeance, but of fatherly kindness, [[118:132|and have mercy on me|et miserere mei]], giving me the grace of most pure contemplation, [[118:132|according to the judgment of them that love thy name|secundum judicium diligentium nomen tuum]], that is, as those who love thee judge to be needful or wholesome for them. Or, [[118:132|according to the judgment of them that love thy name|Secundum judicium diligentium nomen tuum]], that is, according to the judgment of thy discernment, which thou hast passed upon those who love thee, whom thy wisdom has judged are to be filled with thy mercy. Or, [[118:132|according to the judgment of them that love thy name|Secundum judicium diligentium nomen tuum]], that is, as thou hast decreed to do to those who love thee: to whom thou hast purposed to give goods so great and such that [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|oculus ea non vidit, nec auris audivit]], according to the Apostle.

paras.t: Gressus meos, id est affectus, cogitationes, verba et opera, dirige secundum eloquium tuum, id est secundum doctrinam sacræ Scripturæ, ut mandata observem, consilia quoque adimpleam ; et non dominetur mei omnis injustitia, id est, nulla culpa aut passio ratione meæ prævaleat, ne sim servus peccati et carni subjectus, imo omni suggestioni perversæ et passioni immoderatæ efficaciter repugnem ac dominer. Hinc enim Dominus loquitur : Si male egeris, statim peccatum in foribus aderit ; sed sub te erit appetitus ejus, et tu dominaberis illius. Ratio igitur nostra jugiter dominetur appetitui sensitivo, qui in concupiscibilem, irascibilemque partitur.
paras.en: [[118:133|Direct|dirige]] [[118:133|my steps|Gressus meos]], that is, my affections, thoughts, words and works, [[118:133|according to thy word|secundum eloquium tuum]], that is, according to the teaching of Sacred Scripture, that I may keep the commandments and fulfil the counsels also [that is, the evangelical counsels, which go beyond what is commanded]; [[118:133|and let no iniquity have dominion over me|et non dominetur mei omnis injustitia]], that is, let no fault or passion prevail over my reason, lest I be the slave of sin and subject to the flesh; rather, let me resist effectually and master every perverse suggestion and immoderate passion. For hence the Lord says: [[Gen 4:7|if ill, shall not sin forthwith be present at the door? but the lust thereof shall be under thee, and thou shalt have dominion over it|Si male egeris, statim peccatum in foribus aderit ; sed sub te erit appetitus ejus, et tu dominaberis illius]]. Let our reason, therefore, continually have dominion over the sensitive appetite, which is divided into the concupiscible and the irascible [the two powers of the sense appetite: the one desires what is pleasant, the other strives against what is hard].

paras.t: Redime me a calumniis, id est falsis accusationibus, hominum malignorum : non ut nunquam calumnias patiar, quas Christus toties passus est, cujus vestigia sequi oportet ; sed ne per impatientiam vincar, ne remurmurem, atque in talibus occuper : sed potius da mihi eas non curare, nec eis immorari, ut custodiam mandata tua corde quieto ac libero, quæ ab impatientibus litigantibusque nequeunt custodiri.
paras.en: [[118:134|Redeem me from the calumnies|Redime me a calumniis]], that is, from the false accusations, [[118:134|of men|hominum]] who are malicious: not that I may never suffer calumnies, which Christ suffered so often, whose footsteps we must follow; but that I may not be overcome through impatience, nor murmur back, nor be taken up with such things: rather, grant me not to care about them nor to dwell on them, [[118:134|that I may keep thy commandments|ut custodiam mandata tua]] with a quiet and free heart, for they cannot be kept by the impatient and the quarrelsome.

paras.t: Faciem tuam illumina super servum tuum, id est, lumen vultus tui signatum super me clarifica, tui ipsius notitiam mihi infunde, fac me te modo contemplari per fidem et gratiam, postea quoque per speciem ; quoniam hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum ; et vani sunt omnes quibus non subest scientia Dei. Et doce me justificationes tuas, id est mandata. Quam ubertim repetit hoc, ad insinuandum cordis sui ardentissimum appetitum, et observantiæ præceptorum necessitatem ! Propter quod scriptum est : Quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper, et in supervacuis rebus noli scrutari multipliciter. Neque enim sufficit illuminatio veritatis, sine operatione virtutis : quoniam ex operibus innotescit, quantum homo in sancta Scriptura profecerit.
paras.en: [[118:135|Make thy face to shine upon thy servant|Faciem tuam illumina super servum tuum]], that is, make bright [[Ps 4:7|The light of thy countenance|lumen vultus tui]] signed upon me, pour into me the knowledge of thyself, make me contemplate thee now by faith and grace, and afterwards by sight also; for [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God|hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum]]; and [[Wis 13:1|all men are vain, in whom there is not the knowledge of God|vani sunt omnes quibus non subest scientia Dei]]. [[118:135|And teach me thy justifications|Et doce me justificationes tuas]], that is, thy commandments. How abundantly he repeats this, to convey the most ardent longing of his heart and the necessity of keeping the precepts! For which reason it is written: [[Ecclus 3:22|the things that God hath commanded thee, think on them always|Quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper]], and [[Ecclus 3:24|In unnecessary matters be not over curious|in supervacuis rebus noli scrutari multipliciter]]. For the illumination of truth does not suffice without the working of virtue: since it is from his works that it becomes known how far a man has advanced in Holy Scripture.

paras.t: Exitus aquarum, id est rivos lacrimarum seu lacrimas copiosas, deduxerunt oculi mei exteriores, quia non custodierunt legem tuam, id est, quia per eos non custodivi legem divinam, quoniam usus sum eis ad vanitates, non ad spirituales profectus. Ecce docet nos sacratissimus ille versiculus, quid agere debeamus, videlicet ut uberrime nostra deploremus peccata, vehementissime dolentes quod Deum creatorem nostrum, naturaliter bonum et superpiissimum, unquam offendimus. Qui autem ita non plangit, ut versiculum istum de se ipso canere possit, non se putet efficaciter pœnitentem. Unde Jeremias hortatur : Deduc quasi torrentem lacrimas per diem et noctem, et non des requiem tibi, neque taceat pupilla oculi tui.
paras.en: [[118:136|Springs of water|Exitus aquarum]], that is, streams of tears or abundant tears, [[118:136|My eyes have sent forth|deduxerunt oculi mei]], my outward eyes, [[118:136|because they have not kept thy law|quia non custodierunt legem tuam]], that is, because through them I have not kept the divine law, since I used them for vanities, not for spiritual progress. Behold, this most sacred little verse teaches us what we ought to do: namely, that we bewail our sins most abundantly, grieving most vehemently that we ever offended God our Creator, who is good by nature and loving beyond all measure. But let him who does not so lament that he can sing this little verse of himself not think himself effectually penitent. Hence Jeremias exhorts: [[Lam 2:18|Let tears run down like a torrent day and night: give thyself no rest, and let not the apple of thy eye cease|Deduc quasi torrentem lacrimas per diem et noctem, et non des requiem tibi, neque taceat pupilla oculi tui]].

paras.t: Postremo, quis mortalium digne aut plene laudare valebit octonarium istum, cujus quatuor versus efficacissimas et omnino devotissimas preces includunt et continent?
paras.en: Lastly, which of mortals will be able worthily or fully to praise this octonary [that is, this group of eight verses under one Hebrew letter], four of whose verses enclose and contain most efficacious and altogether most devout prayers?

paras.t: Precatio. Faciem misericordiæ tuæ illumina super nos, Domine, et doce nos justificationum tuarum opera peragere : ut qui tenebris peccatorum deprimimur, ab his declaratione sermonum tuorum illuminati exuamur.
paras.en: Prayer. Make the face of thy mercy shine upon us, O Lord, and teach us to perform the works of thy justifications: that we who are weighed down by the darkness of sins may, enlightened by the declaration of thy words, be set free from it.

paras.t: Sade. Justus es, Domine, et rectum judicium tuum. Hoc est quod dicitur in libro Sapientiæ : Quum sis justus, omnia juste disponis; virtus enim tua, justitiæ initium est. Et alibi : Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas; opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet.
paras.en: Sade. [[118:137|Thou art just, O Lord: and thy judgment is right|Justus es, Domine, et rectum judicium tuum]]. This is what is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 12:15|as thou art just, thou orderest all things justly|Quum sis justus, omnia juste disponis]]; [[Wis 12:16|For thy power is the beginning of justice|virtus enim tua, justitiæ initium est]]. And elsewhere: [[Job 34:10|far from God be wickedness, and iniquity from the Almighty|Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas]]; [[Job 34:11|For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them|opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet]].

paras.t: Mandasti justitiam, scilicet testimonia tua, id est mandata, impleri. Jussit enim Deus ut fideles justam habeant conversationem, quæ consistit in hoc quod divina testimonia servant. Et veritatem tuam, id est fidem, nimis custodiri jussisti : quoniam nisi quisque articulos fidei firmiter immobiliterque servaverit, salvus esse non poterit. Decet namque omnino, ut tam magno legislatori ac Domino cum omni reverentia ministretur, fidelissime quoque credatur. Propterea scriptum est : Maledictus qui facit opus Dei fraudulenter.
paras.en: [[118:138|Thou hast commanded justice|Mandasti justitiam]], namely [[118:138|thy testimonies|testimonia tua]], that is, the commandments, to be fulfilled. For God has ordered that the faithful should have a just manner of life, which consists in keeping the divine testimonies. [[118:138|And thy truth|Et veritatem tuam]], that is, the faith, thou hast commanded to be kept [[118:138|exceedingly|nimis]]: since unless each one keeps the articles of faith firmly and immovably, he cannot be saved. For it is altogether fitting that so great a Lawgiver and Lord be served with all reverence, and also believed most faithfully. Therefore it is written: [[Jer 48:10|Cursed be he that doth the work of the Lord deceitfully|Maledictus qui facit opus Dei fraudulenter]].

paras.t: Tabescere, id est ex magna tristitia deficere et liquefieri, me fecit zelus meus, id est zelus animæ meæ, ex divino amore procedens ; quia obliti sunt adimplere et operabiliter credere verba tua, id est divina præcepta, inimici mei, qui contra præcepta operantur, et Deum ac justos odio habent. Hic zelus tabefecit Eliam, qui ait : Zelo zelatus sum pro Domino exercituum. Denique quicumque Deum fervide diligit, quanto eum ferventius amat, tanto de ejus inhonoratione magis affligitur, et sancto zelo resolvitur.
paras.en: [[118:139|Pine away|Tabescere]], that is, to fail and melt away from great sorrow, [[118:139|My zeal hath made me|me fecit zelus meus]]: that is, the zeal of my soul, proceeding from divine love; [[118:139|because my enemies forgot|quia obliti sunt]] to fulfil and to believe in deed [[118:139|thy words|verba tua]], that is, the divine precepts: [[118:139|my enemies|inimici mei]], who act against the precepts and hold God and the just in hatred. This zeal made Elias pine away, who says: [[3 Kings 19:10|With zeal have I been zealous for the Lord God of hosts|Zelo zelatus sum pro Domino exercituum]]. In short, whoever loves God fervently is the more afflicted at his being dishonoured the more fervently he loves him, and is melted by holy zeal.

paras.t: Ignitum eloquium tuum vehementer : id est, sermo divinus, sacra Scriptura, verbum Christi multum ignitum et igneum est, utpote igne Spiritus Sancti repletum, omnem mentem devotam inflammans divino amore, peccata comburens, frigida corda accendens. Dicitur ergo Dei eloquium ignitum, id est affectuosum. Propter quod Christus : Ignem, inquit, veni mittere in terram, et quid volo nisi ut ardeat? Hic ignis erat ardentissima prædicatio ejus, seu gratia Spiritus Sancti, sicut et in Proverbiis dicitur : Omnis sermo Dei ignitus est. Et servus tuus dilexit illud eloquium.
paras.en: [[118:140|Thy word is exceedingly refined|Ignitum eloquium tuum vehementer]] [*ignitum*, literally "fiery", "set on fire", the sense Denis follows; the Douay-Rheims has "refined"]: that is, the divine discourse, Sacred Scripture, the word of Christ, is very fiery and full of fire, being filled with the fire of the Holy Ghost, inflaming every devout mind with divine love, burning up sins, kindling cold hearts. God's word, then, is called fiery, that is, full of affection. For which reason Christ: [[Luke 12:49|I am come to cast fire|Ignem]], he says, [[Luke 12:49|on the earth. And what will I, but that it be kindled?|veni mittere in terram, et quid volo nisi ut ardeat]] This fire was his most ardent preaching, or the grace of the Holy Ghost, as it is also said in Proverbs: [[Prov 30:5|Every word of God is fire tried|Omnis sermo Dei ignitus est]]. [[118:140|And thy servant hath loved it|Et servus tuus dilexit illud]], that word.

paras.t: Adolescentulus sum ego, id est per gratiam novus seu recens : prout Apostolus monet, Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ. Et iterum ait : Interior noster homo renovatur de die in diem. De iis enim qui hanc adolescentiam habent, scriptum est : Adolescentulæ dilexerunt te. Qui enim quotidie proficit, quotidie renovatur, adolescentiorque efficitur. Et contemptus. Hoc est quod dixit superius. Factus sum sicut uter in pruina. Devotos enim et mundo ac vitiis mortificatos odit, contemnit, persequitur mundus. Propter quod Christus ait : Si de mundo essetis, mundus quod suum est diligeret. Unde ad Ezechielem Dominus ait : Portentum te dedi domui Israel. Dic, Ego portentum vestrum. Et Apostolus : Si adhuc hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem. Ecce docemur ex isto versiculo, tanto cordialius exsultare, quanto amplius aspernamur. Justificationes tuas non sum oblitus : id est, propter istam afflictionem contemptus mei, non neglexi implere mandata, nec recessi ab incepto salutis itinere. Talis erat sanctissimus Job, qui quum dixisset, Probavit me Dominus quasi aurum quod per ignem transit, adjecit : A mandatis labiorum ejus non recessi, et in sinu meo abscondi verba ejus.
paras.en: [[118:141|I am very young|Adolescentulus sum ego]], that is, new or fresh through grace: as the Apostle admonishes, [[Eph 4:23|Be renewed in spirit of your mind|Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ]]. And again he says: [[2 Cor 4:16|The inward man is renewed day by day|Interior noster homo renovatur de die in diem]]. For of those who have this youth it is written: [[Cant 1:2|young maidens have loved thee|Adolescentulæ dilexerunt te]]. For he who advances daily is renewed daily, and becomes younger. [[118:141|And despised|Et contemptus]]. This is what he said above: [[118:83|I am become like a bottle in the frost|Factus sum sicut uter in pruina]]. For the world hates, despises and persecutes the devout and those who are dead to the world and to vices. For which reason Christ says: [[John 15:19|If you had been of the world, the world would love its own|Si de mundo essetis, mundus quod suum est diligeret]]. Hence the Lord says to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 12:6|I have set thee for a sign of things to come to the house of Israel|Portentum te dedi domui Israel]] [*portentum*, "a portent", "a sign of wonder"]. [[Ezech 12:11|Say: I am a sign of things to come to you|Dic, Ego portentum vestrum]]. And the Apostle: [[Gal 1:10|If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ|Si adhuc hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem]]. Behold, we are taught by this little verse to exult the more heartily the more we are scorned. [[118:141|But I forget not thy justifications|Justificationes tuas non sum oblitus]]: that is, because of this affliction of being despised I have not neglected to fulfil the commandments, nor turned back from the road of salvation once begun. Such was the most holy Job, who, having said, [[Job 23:10|has tried me as gold that passeth through the fire|Probavit me Dominus quasi aurum quod per ignem transit]], added: [[Job 23:12|I have not departed from the commandments of his lips, and the words of his mouth I have hid in my bosom|A mandatis labiorum ejus non recessi, et in sinu meo abscondi verba ejus]].

paras.t: Justitia tua, justitia in æternum : nam increata Dei justitia est æterna. Effectus quoque divinæ justitiæ æternaliter manet in reprobis. Similiter justitia, id est justa lex fidesque Christi, nunquam deficiet mundo isto durante ; nec ei succedet alia lex, sicut successit justitiæ veteris legis, quæ æterna non fuit, sed Christo veniente et passo, cessavit. Et lex tua veritas : quoniam adeo vera est, ut convenientius veritas nominetur, quam vera. Nil enim dubietatis, nil falsitatis ei miscetur.
paras.en: [[118:142|Thy justice is justice for ever|Justitia tua, justitia in æternum]]: for the uncreated justice of God is eternal. The effect of divine justice also remains eternally in the reprobate. Likewise justice, that is, the just law and faith of Christ, will never fail while this world lasts; nor will another law succeed it, as it succeeded the justice of the old law, which was not eternal, but ceased when Christ came and suffered. [[118:142|And thy law is the truth|Et lex tua veritas]]: for it is so true that it is more fittingly named truth than true. For nothing of doubt, nothing of falsehood, is mingled with it.

paras.t: Tribulatio et angustia, id est dolor exterior atque interior, invenerunt me : id est, persecutio, languor, tentatio invenerunt me in hac miserabili vita, pœnis et vitiis plena ; sed quod est remedium in tanta ærumna, adjecit : mandata tua, meditatio mea est, id est, ad hoc ordinatur omne exercitium et universa occupatio animæ meæ, ne propter adversa aliquo modo recedat a te. Meditatio ista constantiam causat in animo.
paras.en: [[118:143|Trouble and anguish|Tribulatio et angustia]], that is, sorrow outward and inward, [[118:143|have found me|invenerunt me]]: that is, persecution, sickness, temptation have found me in this wretched life, full of pains and vices; but what the remedy is in so great a hardship he has added: [[118:143|thy commandments are my meditation|mandata tua, meditatio mea est]], that is, to this is ordered all the exercise and the whole occupation of my soul, that it may not in any way withdraw from thee because of adversity. This meditation causes constancy in the mind.

paras.t: Æquitas testimonia tua in æternum : id est, verba sacræ Scripturæ propter nimiam suam æquitatem, dicuntur non solum æqua, sed æquitas sine fine. Unde Sapientia ait : Justi sunt omnes sermones mei, et non est in eis pravum quid neque perversum. Intellectum, id est supernaturalem et gratiosam illustrationem mentis, da mihi, et vivam per gratiam, fidem formatam, caritatem divinam, operationemque justam.
paras.en: [[118:144|Thy testimonies are justice for ever|Æquitas testimonia tua in æternum]] [*æquitas*, "equity"]: that is, the words of Sacred Scripture, because of their exceeding equity, are called not only equitable but equity without end. Hence Wisdom says: [[Prov 8:8|All my words are just, there is nothing wicked, nor perverse in them|Justi sunt omnes sermones mei, et non est in eis pravum quid neque perversum]]. [[118:144|Understanding|Intellectum]], that is, a supernatural and gracious enlightening of the mind, [[118:144|give me|da mihi]], [[118:144|and I shall live|et vivam]] through grace, formed faith [that is, faith informed by charity], divine charity, and just working.

paras.t: Precatio. Spiritus tui igne accensos, Domine, ignitum eloquium tuum fac nos servos tuos diligere, et operibus bonis adimplere : ut eodem Spiritu tribuente, intellectum capiamus, quo in æternum vivamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, make us thy servants, kindled with the fire of thy Spirit, love thy fiery word and fulfil it with good works: that, by the gift of the same Spirit, we may receive understanding by which we may live for ever.

paras.t: Coph. Clamavi in toto corde meo, id est corde omnino converso ad te, non vago, neque per amorem temporalium rerum diviso, sed collecto et fixo in te. Iste clamor cordis interior, est desiderium vehemens, quo tendit ad Deum anima amorosa. Vel, Clamavi ad te, o Domine, te exorando in toto corde, id est ex toto corde, videlicet ex intellectu, diligenter sensum verborum pensante, et voluntate, id quod postulo, ardenter concupiente. Exaudi me, Domine, taliter deprecantem ; justificationes tuas requiram : id est, quatenus me promptius pleniusque exaudire digneris, propono firmissime mandata tua requirere.
paras.en: Coph. [[118:145|I cried with my whole heart|Clamavi in toto corde meo]], that is, with a heart wholly turned to thee, not wandering, nor divided by love of temporal things, but gathered and fixed in thee. This inward cry of the heart is the vehement desire by which the loving soul tends to God. Or: [[118:145|I cried|Clamavi]] to thee, O Lord, entreating thee [[118:145|with my whole heart|in toto corde]], that is, from my whole heart, namely from the intellect, carefully weighing the sense of the words, and from the will, ardently desiring what I ask. [[118:145|Hear me, O Lord|Exaudi me, Domine]], as I thus pray; [[118:145|I will seek thy justifications|justificationes tuas requiram]]: that is, so that thou mayest deign to hear me more readily and more fully, I most firmly purpose to seek thy commandments.

paras.t: Clamavi ad te dicens : Salvum me fac, amovendo a me mala pœnæ et culpæ, atque præstando bona gratiæ et gloriæ, ut custodiam mandata tua, id est, ad hoc libera me a malis perturbationum præsentium, ut tibi semper obediam corde quieto ac libero.
paras.en: [[118:146|I cried unto thee|Clamavi ad te]], saying: [[118:146|Save me|Salvum me fac]], by removing from me the evils of punishment and of guilt, and bestowing the goods of grace and of glory, [[118:146|that I may keep thy commandments|ut custodiam mandata tua]]: that is, free me from the evils of present disturbances to this end, that I may always obey thee with a quiet and free heart.

paras.t: Præveni, id est, antequam transirem ad alia, veni ad te, in maturitate sensus mei, ex deliberatione videlicet ordinata, non ex præcipitatione importuna, primo quærendo regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et clamavi psallendo sive orando devote ; in verba tua, quibus promittis exauditionem benignam, gratiam piam, et gloriam sempiternam, supersperavi.
paras.en: [[118:147|I prevented|Præveni]] [that is, "I came before"], that is, before I passed to other things, I came to thee, [[118:147|the dawning of the day|in maturitate]] [*in maturitate*, which Denis takes as "in ripeness"], in the ripeness, that is, of my judgment, from ordered deliberation, not from rash haste, first seeking the kingdom of God and his justice[[Matt 6:33||]], [[118:147|and cried|et clamavi]], singing psalms or praying devoutly; [[118:147|in thy words|in verba tua]] [the margin gives the reading *quia in*, "because in"], by which thou promisest a kindly hearing, loving grace and everlasting glory, [[118:147|I very much hoped|supersperavi]].

paras.t: Prævenerunt oculi mei ad te diluculo : id est, oculos cordis mei direxi ad te, antequam temporalia ista attenderem, aut in exterioribus occuparer, videlicet diluculo, id est mane incipiente aurora : quemadmodum Isaias ait, De mane vigilabo ad te. Et in Ecclesiastico de viro justo inducitur : Cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum qui fecit illum, et in conspectu Altissimi deprecabitur. Vel, Diluculo, id est in principio spiritualis diei, scilicet radiante gratia tua in anima mea, quoniam sine ejus splendore oculi mei ad te pervenire aut dirigi nequeunt. Sic itaque prævenerunt oculi mei ad te, ut meditarer eloquia tua : in quibus continentur aliqua ad tuæ majestatis contemplationem spectantia, aliqua vero ad meæ fragilitatis notitiam, quædam autem ad mandatorum cognitionem respicientia : et omnia ista diligenter ac jugiter meditanda sunt.
paras.en: [[118:148|My eyes to thee have prevented the morning|Prævenerunt oculi mei ad te diluculo]]: that is, I directed the eyes of my heart to thee before I attended to these temporal things or was busied with outward things; namely in [[118:148|the morning|diluculo]], that is, early, as the dawn begins: as Isaias says, [[Is 26:9|in the morning early I will watch to thee|De mane vigilabo ad te]]. And in Ecclesiasticus it is said of the just man: [[Ecclus 39:6|He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High|Cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum qui fecit illum, et in conspectu Altissimi deprecabitur]]. Or, [[118:148|the morning|Diluculo]], that is, at the beginning of the spiritual day, namely when thy grace shines in my soul, since without its splendour my eyes cannot reach thee or be directed to thee. Thus, then, [[118:148|My eyes to thee have prevented|prævenerunt oculi mei ad te]], [[118:148|that I might meditate on thy words|ut meditarer eloquia tua]]: in which are contained some things that look to the contemplation of thy majesty, some to the knowledge of my frailty, and some to the knowledge of the commandments: and all these are to be meditated on diligently and continually.

paras.t: Vocem meam, id est orationem meam, audi secundum misericordiam tuam, Domine. Ecce qui tantis perfectionibus se ornatum disserit, postulat exaudiri secundum misericordiam Dei, non secundum justitiam suam aut propria merita : quatenus advertamus non nobis sufficere merita nostra, nisi misericordia Dei subveniat, imperfecto nostro indulgens, nosque clementer salvificans. Secundum judicium tuum, id est, sicut tu vides atque discernis te decere et me indigere, sicut tu bonum judicas, sicut tua sapientia dictat, vivifica me gratia, caritate et opere consummato. Nunc enim judicium sumitur pro actu exsistente in eo qui judicat, non pro reprobatione, remuneratione, aut effectu justitiæ. Sicque frequenter leguntur fideles orasse, ut Deus secundum judicium suum faceret eis, quemadmodum Joab ait : Dominus quod bonum est in conspectu suo faciet.
paras.en: [[118:149|Hear thou|audi]] [[118:149|my voice|Vocem meam]], that is, my prayer, [[118:149|O Lord, according to thy mercy|secundum misericordiam tuam, Domine]]. Behold, he who sets forth that he is adorned with such great perfections asks to be heard according to the mercy of God, not according to his own justice or his own merits: so that we may take note that our merits do not suffice for us unless the mercy of God comes to our aid, pardoning our imperfection and mercifully saving us. [[118:149|According to thy judgment|Secundum judicium tuum]], that is, as thou seest and discernest it to befit thee and me to need it, as thou judgest good, as thy wisdom dictates, [[118:149|quicken me|vivifica me]] by grace, by charity and by finished work. For here *judgment* is taken for the act existing in him who judges, not for reprobation, reward, or the effect of justice. And so the faithful are often read to have prayed that God would do to them according to his judgment, as Joab says: [[2 Kings 10:12|the Lord will do what is good in his sight|Dominus quod bonum est in conspectu suo faciet]].

paras.t: Appropinquaverunt persequentes me iniquitati, id est, persequendo me, inique fecerunt ; a lege autem tua longe facti sunt, id est, affectus et opus eorum divinæ legi atque justitiæ multum contraria exstiterunt, eo quod innocentem et justum malitiose ac impie persecuti sunt. Quanto enim quis gravius peccat, tanto a Deo ac lege divina longius distat et abit. Propter quod apud Osee habetur : Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo.
paras.en: [[118:150|They that persecute me have drawn nigh to iniquity|Appropinquaverunt persequentes me iniquitati]], that is, in persecuting me they have acted wickedly; [[118:150|but they are gone far off from thy law|a lege autem tua longe facti sunt]], that is, their affection and work have proved very contrary to the divine law and justice, in that they have persecuted the innocent and just man maliciously and impiously. For the more gravely one sins, the farther one stands and departs from God and the divine law. For which reason it is found in Osee: [[Osee 4:10|they have forsaken the Lord in not observing|Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo]].

paras.t: Prope esto, Domine, id est, per gratiam opemque perennem mihi adsistas, et omnes viæ tuæ veritas, id est, vera et justa sunt omnia opera tua, verba et jussa. Quamvis enim universæ viæ Domini sint misericordia et veritas, nihilo minus omnes viæ ejus sunt veritas, et iterum omnes viæ ejus sunt misericordia, secundum aliquem modum. Dum enim peccatorem gratis justificat, justum est ex parte bonitatis suæ, quæ tanta est, ut justum sit eam etiam indignis misereri. Est quoque justificatio illa misericors, eo quod Deus sine meritis misereatur iniquo.
paras.en: [[118:151|Thou art near, O Lord|Prope esto, Domine]] [Denis reads *Prope esto*, "Be thou near"; the margin gives the other reading, *Prope es tu*, "Thou art near", which the Douay-Rheims follows], that is, mayest thou assist me with grace and help without end; [[118:151|and all thy ways are truth|et omnes viæ tuæ veritas]], that is, [[Apoc 19:2|true and just|vera et justa]] are all thy works, words and commands. For although [[Ps 24:10|all the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|universæ viæ Domini sint misericordia et veritas]], nevertheless all his ways are truth, and again all his ways are mercy, in some manner. For when he justifies the sinner freely, it is just on the part of his goodness, which is so great that it is just for it to have mercy even on the unworthy. That justification is also merciful, in that God has mercy on the wicked man without any merits.

paras.t: Initio, id est primo omnium, et ab exordio considerationis meæ, cognovi de testimoniis tuis, id est verbis sacræ Scripturæ, quia in æternum fundasti ea, id est, taliter ea confirmasti et stabilisti, quod nunquam falsificabuntur, nec ab aliquo infirmabuntur. Hoc est quod Christus ait : Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt. Et Isaias testatur : Verbum Dei nostri stabit in æternum.
paras.en: [[118:152|From the beginning|Initio]], that is, first of all, and from the outset of my reflection, [[118:152|I have known|cognovi]] [[118:152|concerning thy testimonies|de testimoniis tuis]], that is, the words of Sacred Scripture, [[118:152|that thou hast founded them for ever|quia in æternum fundasti ea]], that is, thou hast so confirmed and established them that they will never be falsified nor weakened by anyone. This is what Christ says: [[Luke 21:33|Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.|Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt]] And Isaias testifies: [[Is 40:8|the word of our Lord endureth for ever|Verbum Dei nostri stabit in æternum]].

paras.t: Precatio. Prope esto nobis, Domine, et appropinquantes et persequentes nos in iniquitate a nobis repelle; ad te nos clamantes salva: ut per te securi custodiamus mandata tua.
paras.en: Prayer. Be near us, O Lord, and drive away from us those who draw near and persecute us in iniquity; save us who cry to thee: that, made secure by thee, we may keep thy commandments.

paras.t: Res. Vide humilitatem meam, id est, clementer, o Domine, intuere quantum affligor, contemnor, qualiter etiam ego me ipsum humilio, vilipendo et reprobo; et eripe me ab omni miseria. Scriptum est enim : Qui se humiliat, exaltabitur. Job quoque ait : Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria. Unde et alibi dicitur : Gloriam præcedit humilitas. Quia legem tuam non sum oblitus, sed mente et opere eam servavi.
paras.en: Res. [[118:153|See my humiliation|Vide humilitatem meam]], that is, look mercifully, O Lord, upon how greatly I am afflicted and despised, and also how I humble, belittle and reprove myself; [[118:153|and deliver me|et eripe me]] from all misery. For it is written: [[Luke 14:11|he that humbleth himself shall be exalted|Qui se humiliat, exaltabitur]]. Job also says: [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]]. Whence it is said elsewhere too: [[Prov 15:33|humility goeth before glory|Gloriam præcedit humilitas]]. [[118:153|For I have not forgotten thy law|Quia legem tuam non sum oblitus]], but have kept it in mind and in deed.

paras.t: Judica judicium meum, id est, profer sententiam pro me, et discerne atque determina causam meam, quam habeo contra iniquos, qui me conantur elongare a te. Judica ergo ut angelus sanctus me protegat, nec illi prævaleant, et redime me ab omni malo præterito, præsenti et futuro. Propter eloquium tuum vivifica me gratia Spiritus Sancti. Hoc autem quod ait, Propter eloquium tuum, exponi potest tripliciter. Primo sic : Propter eloquium tuum, id est, ut sermo tuus quo gratiam deprecantibus promisisti, impleatur, vivifica me. Secundo sic : Propter eloquium tuum, id est ad honorem legis divinæ, ut promulgetur et observetur, vivifica me. Tertio sic : Propter eloquium tuum, id est propter bonitatem et gratiam tuam, qua dignatus es loqui nobiscum, et dare nobis divinam Scripturam ac legem, vivifica me, ne sim in morte peccati : de qua dicit Apostolus, Vidua quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est ; et Christus in Evangelio, Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos.
paras.en: [[118:154|Judge my judgment|Judica judicium meum]], that is, give sentence for me, and decide and determine my cause, which I have against the wicked who try to draw me far from thee. Judge, then, so that the holy angel may protect me and they may not prevail, [[118:154|and redeem me|et redime me]] from every evil, past, present and to come. [[118:154|For thy word's sake|Propter eloquium tuum]] [[118:154|quicken thou me|vivifica me]] by the grace of the Holy Ghost. Now this that he says, [[118:154|for thy word's sake|Propter eloquium tuum]], can be expounded in three ways. First thus: [[118:154|for thy word's sake|Propter eloquium tuum]], that is, that thy word, by which thou hast promised grace to those who pray for it, may be fulfilled, quicken me. Secondly thus: [[118:154|for thy word's sake|Propter eloquium tuum]], that is, for the honour of the divine law, that it may be proclaimed and kept, quicken me. Thirdly thus: [[118:154|for thy word's sake|Propter eloquium tuum]], that is, for the sake of thy goodness and grace, by which thou hast deigned to speak with us and to give us the divine Scripture and law, quicken me, that I may not be in the death of sin; of which the Apostle says: The widow [[1 Tim 5:6|that liveth in pleasures is dead while she is living|quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est]]; and Christ in the Gospel: [[Matt 8:22|let the dead bury their dead|Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos]].

paras.t: Longe a peccatoribus impœnitentibus salus, eo quod gratia careant, nec Deus cum eis sit, juxta illud, Longe est Dominus ab impiis ; et iterum, Abominabile est Domino cor pravum ; et alibi, Miseros facit populos peccatum. Salus autem et felicitas idem sunt. Sicut ergo una est felicitas viæ, consistens dispositive in operatione virtutum moralium, essentialiter autem in contemplatione Dei per fidem formatam, sic salus duplex est : et ab utraque tam longe exstat peccator, quantum a virtutibus distat. Quia justificationes tuas non exquisierunt, id est, mandata non quæsierunt diligenter implere. Idcirco eis continget quod apud Prophetam inducitur : Disperdam eos qui avertuntur de post tergum Domini, et qui non exquisierunt Dominum, nec investigaverunt eum.
paras.en: [[118:155|Salvation|salus]] is [[118:155|far from sinners|Longe a peccatoribus]] who do not repent, because they lack grace and God is not with them, according to that saying: [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus ab impiis]]; and again: [[Prov 11:20|A perverse heart is abominable to the Lord|Abominabile est Domino cor pravum]] [the margin gives Ibid. xv, 29; the words are Prov 11:20]; and elsewhere: [[Prov 14:34|sin maketh nations miserable|Miseros facit populos peccatum]]. Now salvation and happiness are the same. As, then, one happiness is that of the way [that is, of this present life, as distinct from that of the heavenly fatherland], consisting dispositively in the exercise of the moral virtues but essentially in the contemplation of God through formed faith [that is, faith given life by charity], so salvation is twofold; and the sinner stands as far from each as he is distant from the virtues. [[118:155|Because they have not sought thy justifications|Quia justificationes tuas non exquisierunt]], that is, they have not sought diligently to fulfil the commandments. Therefore there will befall them what is set down in the Prophet: [[Soph 1:4|I will destroy|Disperdam]] [[Soph 1:6|them that turn away from following after the Lord, and that have not sought the Lord, nor searched after him|eos qui avertuntur de post tergum Domini, et qui non exquisierunt Dominum, nec investigaverunt eum]].

paras.t: Misericordiæ tuæ multæ, Domine : id est, effectus divinæ pietatis multi et varii sunt, multipliciterque misertus es nobis, imo mille et innumerabilibus modis nosti succurrere miseris, sicut scriptum est : Misericordiæ Domini, quia non sumus consumpti, quia non defecerunt miserationes ejus. Vel ipsa una ac simplex misericordia Dei, vocata est pluraliter misericordiæ, propter multiplicem actum suum. Secundum judicium tuum vivifica me.
paras.en: [[118:156|Many, O Lord, are thy mercies|Misericordiæ tuæ multæ, Domine]]: that is, the effects of the divine goodness are many and various, and in many ways hast thou had mercy on us; nay, in a thousand and countless ways thou knowest how to succour the wretched, as it is written: [[Lam 3:22|The mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed: because his commiserations have not failed|Misericordiæ Domini, quia non sumus consumpti, quia non defecerunt miserationes ejus]]. Or else the one and simple mercy of God is itself called *mercies* in the plural, because of its manifold working. [[118:156|Quicken me according to thy judgment|Secundum judicium tuum vivifica me]].

paras.t: Multi qui persequuntur me, et tribulant me, videlicet dæmon cum angelis suis, mundus cum amatoribus suis, caro cum concupiscentiis suis. Verumtamen desperandum nobis non est, quoniam Eliseus hortatus est : Noli timere ; plures enim nobiscum sunt, quam cum illis. Et sicut Jonathas ait : Non est Domino difficile salvare in multis vel in paucis. Hinc etiam Christus ait electis : In mundo pressuram habebitis ; sed confidite, ego vici mundum. Denique, juxta Apostolum, Sicut abundant Christi passiones in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra. A testimoniis tuis non declinavi, sed fide et opere mansi fidelis. Ecce quanta constantia ! Magnum enim est non deficere in adversis. Unde Dominus loquitur : Esto fidelis usque ad mortem, et dabo tibi coronam vitæ.
paras.en: [[118:157|Many are they that persecute me and afflict me|Multi qui persequuntur me, et tribulant me]], namely the devil with his angels, the world with its lovers, the flesh with its concupiscences. Yet we must not despair, since Eliseus exhorted: [[4 Kings 6:16|Fear not: for there are more with us than with them|Noli timere ; plures enim nobiscum sunt, quam cum illis]]. And as Jonathas says: [[1 Kings 14:6|it is easy for the Lord to save either by many, or by few|Non est Domino difficile salvare in multis vel in paucis]]. Hence too Christ says to the elect: [[John 16:33|In the world you shall have distress. But have confidence. I have overcome the world|In mundo pressuram habebitis ; sed confidite, ego vici mundum]]. Lastly, according to the Apostle: [[2 Cor 1:5|as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|Sicut abundant Christi passiones in nobis, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]]. [[118:157|I have not declined from thy testimonies|A testimoniis tuis non declinavi]], but by faith and work I have remained faithful. See what constancy! For it is a great thing not to give way in adversity. Whence the Lord says: [[Apoc 2:10|Be thou faithful unto death: and I will give thee the crown of life|Esto fidelis usque ad mortem, et dabo tibi coronam vitæ]].

paras.t: Vidi prævaricantes, et tabescebam, quia eloquia tua non custodierunt. Hoc est quod paulo ante dixit atque expositum est : Tabescere me fecit zelus meus, quia obliti sunt verba tua inimici mei. Illic ergo sensum require.
paras.en: [[118:158|I beheld the transgressors, and pined away; because they kept not thy word|Vidi prævaricantes, et tabescebam, quia eloquia tua non custodierunt]]. This is what he said a little before, and it has been expounded: [[118:139|My zeal hath made me pine away: because my enemies forgot thy words|Tabescere me fecit zelus meus, quia obliti sunt verba tua inimici mei]]. Look for the sense there, then.

paras.t: Vide quoniam mandata tua dilexi : id est, pietatem affectus mei clementer attende, approba et accepta. Et sicut me cernis zelari pro te, sic mihi repende, et dilige atque glorifica me, prout dixisti : Ego diligentes me diligo ; et iterum, Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum. Domine, in misericordia tua vivifica me, dando mihi incessantem ac evidentem spiritualis vitæ profectum, ita ut impleam illud Apostoli : Profectus tuus manifestus sit omnibus ; et, Noli negligere gratiam quæ data est tibi.
paras.en: [[118:159|Behold I have loved thy commandments|Vide quoniam mandata tua dilexi]]: that is, look mercifully upon the devotion of my affection, approve it and accept it. And as thou seest me zealous for thee, so repay me, and love and glorify me, as thou hast said: [[Prov 8:17|I love them that love me|Ego diligentes me diligo]]; and again: [[1 Kings 2:30|whosoever shall glorify me, him will I glorify|Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum]]. [[118:159|O Lord|Domine]], [[118:159|quicken me thou in thy mercy|in misericordia tua vivifica me]], by giving me unceasing and evident progress in the spiritual life, so that I may fulfil that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Tim 4:15|thy profiting may be manifest to all|Profectus tuus manifestus sit omnibus]]; and: [[1 Tim 4:14|Neglect not the grace|Noli negligere gratiam]] [[1 Tim 4:14|which was given thee|quæ data est tibi]].

paras.t: Principium verborum tuorum veritas: id est, primum quod convenit sacro eloquio, est veritas, quoniam mere verissima sunt omnia verba sacræ Scripturæ. Propterea Christus Patri suo ait : Sermo tuus veritas est. In æternum omnia judicia justitiæ tuæ : id est, quæcumque tua justitia approbat, causat et asserit, æternaliter justa sunt, semperque manebunt. Vel sic : Principium, id est origo seu causa, verborum tuorum, id est sermonum sacræ Scripturæ, est veritas increata, a qua procedit sacra doctrina, et cui immediate innititur tanquam immobili fundamento. Propter quod tanta est certitudo et firmitas evangelicæ legis, imo universæ Scripturæ canonicæ, ut dicat Apostolus : Licet angelus de cœlo evangelizet vobis, præterquam quod evangelizavimus vobis, anathema sit. Imo quum fides christiana æternæ veritati directe innitatur, nil falsius esse potest, nisi quod fidei benedictæ repugnet. In æternum omnia judicia justitiæ tuæ : id est, judicia quæ facturus es in die novissimo, sine termino permanebunt, quantum ad præmium singulorum : quia ut in Evangelio dicitur, Ibunt hi in ignem æternum, justi autem in vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[118:160|The beginning of thy words is truth|Principium verborum tuorum veritas]]: that is, the first thing that belongs to the sacred word is truth, since all the words of holy Scripture are purely and wholly true. Therefore Christ says to his Father: [[John 17:17|Thy word is truth|Sermo tuus veritas est]]. [[118:160|All the judgments of thy justice are for ever|In æternum omnia judicia justitiæ tuæ]]: that is, whatever thy justice approves, causes and affirms is eternally just, and will abide for ever. Or thus: [[118:160|The beginning|Principium]], that is, the origin or cause, [[118:160|of thy words|verborum tuorum]], that is, of the discourses of holy Scripture, is the uncreated truth, from which sacred doctrine proceeds, and on which it rests immediately as on an immovable foundation. For this reason so great is the certainty and firmness of the law of the Gospel, nay of the whole canonical Scripture, that the Apostle says: Though [[Gal 1:8|an angel from heaven, preach a gospel to you besides that which we have preached to you, let him be anathema|angelus de cœlo evangelizet vobis, præterquam quod evangelizavimus vobis, anathema sit]]. Indeed, since the Christian faith rests directly on the eternal truth, nothing can be more false than what is contrary to the blessed faith. [[118:160|All the judgments of thy justice are for ever|In æternum omnia judicia justitiæ tuæ]]: that is, the judgments which thou wilt make on the last day will abide without end, as to the reward of each one; for, as is said in the Gospel, [[Matt 25:46|these shall go|Ibunt hi]] into everlasting fire [Denis's wording, *in ignem æternum*, is that of Matt 25:41; v. 46 reads "into everlasting punishment"], [[Matt 25:46|but the just, into life everlasting|justi autem in vitam æternam]].

paras.t: Precatio. Vide humilitatem plebis tuæ, Domine, et ab omnibus malis obstrepentibus nos redime ; vivifica nos pro tua pietate, in omni bona actione, ut semper custodiamus judicia justitiæ tuæ.
paras.en: Prayer. See the humiliation of thy people, O Lord, and redeem us from all the evils that clamour against us; quicken us in thy goodness in every good action, that we may ever keep the judgments of thy justice.

paras.t: Sin. Principes hujus mundi, videlicet dæmones, qui peccatoribus principantur, persecuti sunt, id est tentaverunt, me gratis, id est sine meis demeritis ; vel, Gratis, id est frustra, quia non prævaluerunt. Vel : Principes, id est homines impii, ceteris dominantes, persecuti sunt me gratis, sicut scriptum est : Nonne divites per potentiam opprimunt vos, et blasphemant bonum nomen, quod invocatum est super vos? De illis autem invisibilibus principibus, multum potentibus et astutis, ait Apostolus : Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates, contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cælestibus. Et a verbis tuis formidavit cor meum, id est, timui et expavi ne verbis mandatorum tuorum inobediens fierem. Quanto enim persecutio major est, tanto fit homo facilius transgressor legis divinæ : quia non cadere in adversis, difficile est. Ideo tempore persecutionis indiget homo specialiter formidare ne peccet, et verbum Dei relinquat. Imo quilibet nostrum quantumcumque perfectus, habet timere a verbis Dei, si velit Spiritum Sanctum habere in se, quum Dominus dicat : Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos? Vel, A verbis tuis, quibus comminaris tormenta gravissima his qui vincuntur, formidavit cor meum : idcirco ne pœnas incidam, mansi fidelis et constans.
paras.en: Sin. [[118:161|Princes|Principes]] of this world, namely the demons, who hold princely rule over sinners, [[118:161|have persecuted|persecuti sunt]], that is, tempted, [[118:161|me without cause|me gratis]], that is, without any deserving of mine; or, [[118:161|without cause|Gratis]], that is, in vain, because they did not prevail [the Latin *gratis* means both "without cause" and "to no purpose"]. Or: [[118:161|Princes|Principes]], that is, wicked men who lord it over the rest, [[118:161|have persecuted me without cause|persecuti sunt me gratis]], as it is written: [[Jas 2:6|Do not the rich oppress you by might|Nonne divites per potentiam opprimunt vos]], and [[Jas 2:7|blaspheme the good name that is invoked upon you?|blasphemant bonum nomen, quod invocatum est super vos?]] And of those invisible princes, very powerful and cunning, the Apostle says: [[Eph 6:12|our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and powers|Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates]] [*principes*, the same word as the psalm's *Princes*], [[Eph 6:12|against the spirits of wickedness in the high places|contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cælestibus]]. [[118:161|And my heart hath been in awe of thy words|Et a verbis tuis formidavit cor meum]], that is, I feared and dreaded lest I should become disobedient to the words of thy commandments. For the greater the persecution, the more easily does a man become a transgressor of the divine law, since not to fall in adversity is hard. Therefore in time of persecution a man has special need to fear lest he sin and forsake the word of God. Nay, every one of us, however perfect, must stand in awe of the words of God if he wishes to have the Holy Ghost in him, since the Lord says: [[Is 66:2|to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit, and that trembleth at my words?|Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos?]] Or: [[118:161|of thy words|A verbis tuis]], by which thou threatenest most grievous torments to those who are overcome, [[118:161|my heart hath been in awe|formidavit cor meum]]: and so, lest I fall into punishment, I have remained faithful and constant.

paras.t: Lætabor ego super eloquia tua, id est de hoc quod divina Scriptura mihi et aliis data ac revelata est : sicut a Propheta inducitur, Beati sumus nos, quoniam quæ Deo placita sunt, manifesta sunt nobis. Vel, Lætabor ego super eloquia tua, meditando, contemplando, observandoque ea. Sicut qui invenit spolia multa: qui utique multum gaudet. Unde a Jeremia dicitur : Factum est mihi verbum tuum in gaudium et in lætitiam cordis mei. Et Isaias ait : Lætabuntur coram te, sicut qui lætantur in messe, sicut exsultant victores capta præda, quando dividunt spolia. Utroque modo lætari debemus super eloquia Dei. Maximum enim beneficium Dei est, quod sacro eloquio illustravit Ecclesiam ; et qui diligit Deum, delectari debet in sermonibus ejus.
paras.en: [[118:162|I will rejoice at thy words|Lætabor ego super eloquia tua]], that is, because the divine Scripture has been given and revealed to me and to others: as is set down by the Prophet, [[Bar 4:4|We are happy|Beati sumus nos]], [[Bar 4:4|because the things that are pleasing to God, are made known to us|quoniam quæ Deo placita sunt, manifesta sunt nobis]]. Or: [[118:162|I will rejoice at thy words|Lætabor ego super eloquia tua]] by meditating on them, contemplating them and keeping them. [[118:162|As one that hath found great spoil|Sicut qui invenit spolia multa]], who indeed rejoices greatly. Whence it is said by Jeremias: [[Jer 15:16|thy word was to me a joy and gladness of my heart|Factum est mihi verbum tuum in gaudium et in lætitiam cordis mei]]. And Isaias says: [[Is 9:3|They shall rejoice before thee, as they that rejoice in the harvest, as conquerors rejoice after taking a prey, when they divide the spoils|Lætabuntur coram te, sicut qui lætantur in messe, sicut exsultant victores capta præda, quando dividunt spolia]]. In both ways we ought to rejoice at the words of God. For it is a very great benefit of God that he has enlightened the Church with the sacred word; and he who loves God ought to delight in his words.

paras.t: Iniquitatem odio habui et abominatus sum. Aliqui odiunt iniquitatem, non propter se ipsam, sed propter pœnam sequentem. Et isti sunt imperfecti. Operantur enim bonum ex timore servili, qui non est meritorius, quamvis disponat ad gratiam secundum quod timor. Aliqui autem odiunt iniquitatem propter deformitatem et turpitudinem ejus. Quidam vero ex Dei amore odiunt eam, videlicet quoniam displicet Deo, et quia per eam inhonoratur atque offenditur Deus. Et istud est perfectius quam secundum : præsertim quum aliqui gentiles et infideles tantæ perfectionis fuisse legantur, ut peccatum propter suam deformitatem oderint, quemadmodum Seneca ait : Quamvis scirem deos mihi ignoscituros, non peccarem propter ipsam vilitatem peccati. Studeamus ergo tertio modo iniquitatem odio habere, quoniam hoc est amicorum filiorumque Dei, et evidens signum gratiæ. Amicorum quippe est proprium, eadem velle et nolle. Et honorare Deum spectat ad filios adoptivos, prout asserit Dominus : Filius honorat patrem suum, et servus timet dominum suum. Si ergo Pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus ? et si Dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus? Legem autem tuam dilexi magis quam omnia temporalia, vana atque caduca.
paras.en: [[118:163|I have hated and abhorred iniquity|Iniquitatem odio habui et abominatus sum]]. Some hate iniquity not for its own sake but for the punishment that follows; and these are the imperfect. For they do good out of servile fear [that is, fear of punishment rather than of offending God], which is not meritorious, although, in so far as it is fear, it disposes to grace. Others hate iniquity for its deformity and foulness. But some hate it out of the love of God, namely because it displeases God, and because by it God is dishonoured and offended. And this is more perfect than the second way, especially since some gentiles and unbelievers are read to have been of such perfection that they hated sin for its deformity, as Seneca says: Even if I knew that the gods would pardon me, I would not sin, because of the very vileness of sin. Let us strive, then, to hate iniquity in the third way, since this belongs to the friends and sons of God, and is a clear sign of grace. For it is the property of friends to will and not to will the same things; and to honour God belongs to adopted sons, as the Lord declares: [[Mal 1:6|The son honoureth the father|Filius honorat patrem suum]], [[Mal 1:6|and the servant|et servus]] feareth [[Mal 1:6|his master|dominum suum]]: [[Mal 1:6|if then I be a father, where is my honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear|Si ergo Pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus ? et si Dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus?]]? [[118:163|But I have loved thy law|Legem autem tuam dilexi]] more than all things temporal, vain and perishable.

paras.t: Septies in die laudem dixi tibi, id est, septem Horis seu vicibus canonicis quotidie te laudavi, super judicia justitiæ tuæ, id est de operibus, sermonibus, mandatis, ac ceteris a tua justitia procedentibus, et judicialiter approbatis. Hunc numerum ad litteram non observabant Judæi, quoniam Nehemias ait : Quater in die, et quater in nocte confitebantur Judæi, et adorabant Dominum Deum. Hæc ergo dixit Propheta in persona populi christiani, qui omni die naturali Deum septies laudat et invocat.
paras.en: [[118:164|Seven times a day I have given praise to thee|Septies in die laudem dixi tibi]], that is, I have praised thee daily at seven canonical Hours or times [the Hours of the Divine Office: Matins with Lauds, Prime, Terce, Sext, None, Vespers and Compline], [[118:164|for the judgments of thy justice|super judicia justitiæ tuæ]], that is, for the works, words, commandments and all else that proceeds from thy justice and is judicially approved. The Jews did not keep this number to the letter, since Nehemias says: [[2 Esd 9:3|four times in the day, and four times|Quater in die, et quater]] in the night [Denis's text adds *in nocte*, "in the night"] the Jews [[2 Esd 9:3|confessed, and adored the Lord their God|confitebantur Judæi, et adorabant Dominum Deum]]. So the Prophet said this in the person of the Christian people, who every natural day [that is, the whole day of twenty-four hours] praise and call upon God seven times.

paras.t: Pax multa, id est interna et copiosa, est diligentibus opere et veritate legem tuam. Qui enim diligit legem Dei, in omnibus ordinate se habet. Pax autem est tranquillitas mentis, secundum Augustinum ; tranquillitas vero ordinationem consequitur. Dilectio ergo legis divinæ, est causa pacis internæ. Et quanto legem Dei perfectius amamus et observamus, tanto pleniorem in nobis pacem sortimur : quæ omni Christiano maxime appetenda est. Nam et Christus post resurrectionem discipulos suos taliter salutavit : Pax vobis. Ait quoque Apostolus : Si fieri potest, quod in vobis est, cum omnibus hominibus pacem habentes ; et iterum, Pax Domini quæ exsuperat omnem sensum, custodiat corda vestra et intelligentias vestras ; et iterum, Pax Christi exsultet semper in cordibus vestris ; rursusque, Pacem sequimini cum omnibus et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit. Ecce quam frequenter nos hortatur noster Doctor ad pacis custodiam. Et non est illis scandalum, quia ut ait Hieronymus, qui scandalizatur parvulus est. Majores enim scandala non recipiunt. Unde perfecti qui Deum seu legem ejus efficaciter diligunt, nec activum neque passivum scandalum habent, id est, nec scandalizantur, nec scandalizant. Et si quis ex dictis seu factis eorum scandalizetur, hoc erit Pharisæorum Scribarumque scandalum, vel ex infirmitate scandalizati.
paras.en: [[118:165|Much peace|Pax multa]], that is, inward and abundant, [[118:165|have they that love|est diligentibus]] in deed and in truth [[118:165|thy law|legem tuam]]. For he who loves the law of God bears himself in an ordered way in all things. Now peace is tranquillity of mind, according to Augustine; and tranquillity follows upon order. The love of the divine law, then, is the cause of inward peace; and the more perfectly we love and keep the law of God, the fuller the peace we obtain within us: a peace which every Christian should desire above all. For Christ too after his resurrection greeted his disciples thus: [[John 20:19|Peace be to you|Pax vobis]][[John 20:21||]][[John 20:26||]]. The Apostle also says: [[Rom 12:18|If it be possible, as much as is in you, have peace with all men|Si fieri potest, quod in vobis est, cum omnibus hominibus pacem habentes]]; and again: The peace of the Lord, [[Phil 4:7|which surpasseth all understanding, keep your hearts and minds|quæ exsuperat omnem sensum, custodiat corda vestra et intelligentias vestras]]; and again: [[Col 3:15|let the peace of Christ rejoice|Pax Christi exsultet]] always [[Col 3:15|in your hearts|in cordibus vestris]]; and once more: [[Heb 12:14|Follow peace with all men and holiness: without which no man shall see God|Pacem sequimini cum omnibus et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit]]. See how often our Doctor [that is, the Apostle] exhorts us to keep peace. [[118:165|And to them there is no stumbling block|Et non est illis scandalum]] [*scandalum*, the Douay-Rheims "stumbling block", is "scandal" in what follows], because, as Jerome says, he who is scandalized is a little one; for the greater do not take scandal. Whence the perfect, who love God or his law effectually, have neither active nor passive scandal [active scandal is giving another occasion of sin; passive, taking it], that is, they are neither scandalized nor give scandal. And if anyone is scandalized by their words or deeds, this will be the scandal of the Pharisees and Scribes, or of those scandalized through weakness.

paras.t: Exspectabam spe certa atque longanimi salutare tuum, Domine, id est salutem a te, salvationem salubrem, gratiam salutarem. Debemus enim in omni adversitate exspectare salubre auxilium Dei. Vel, Exspectabam, quamdiu in ista peregrinatione fui et vixi, salutare tuum, Domine, id est Christum mundi salvatorem : quemadmodum Jacob ait, Salutare tuum exspectabo, Domine ; et Habacuc, Si moram fecerit, exspecta eum, quia veniens veniet, et non tardabit. Et mandata tua dilexi, quatenus per eorum caritativam custodiam, merear adipisci in patria salutare Dei, quod præstolor.
paras.en: [[118:166|I looked for|Exspectabam]], with sure and long-suffering hope, [[118:166|thy salvation, O Lord|salutare tuum, Domine]], that is, salvation from thee, saving deliverance, saving grace. For in every adversity we ought to look for the saving help of God. Or: [[118:166|I looked for|Exspectabam]], as long as I was and lived in this pilgrimage, [[118:166|thy salvation, O Lord|salutare tuum, Domine]], that is, Christ the Saviour of the world [the Latin *salutare*, "that which saves", can name the Saviour himself]: as Jacob says, [[Gen 49:18|I will look for thy salvation, O Lord|Salutare tuum exspectabo, Domine]]; and Habacuc: [[Hab 2:3|if it make any delay, wait for it: for it shall surely come, and it shall not be slack|Si moram fecerit, exspecta eum, quia veniens veniet, et non tardabit]] [Denis reads *eum*, "him", taking it of Christ]. [[118:166|And I loved thy commandments|Et mandata tua dilexi]], so that by keeping them in charity I may merit to obtain in the fatherland the salvation of God for which I wait.

paras.t: Custodivit anima mea tenaci memoria atque laudabili vita testimonia tua, id est verba sacræ Scripturæ, quæ tu per multa mirabilia vera esse testatus es, testimonium exhibens eis : prout dicitur de Apostolis, Prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis. Et dicit Apostolus : Abundantius oportet nos observare ea quæ audivimus, contestante Deo signis et portentis, et variis virtutibus, et Spiritus Sancti distributionibus. Ecce quam inviolata et inconcussa est certitudo fidei christianæ atque catholicæ. Et dilexit ea vehementer, sicut decet magnum bonum ardenter amari.
paras.en: [[118:167|My soul hath kept|Custodivit anima mea]], by a tenacious memory and a praiseworthy life, [[118:167|thy testimonies|testimonia tua]], that is, the words of holy Scripture, which thou hast testified by many wonders to be true, bearing witness to them: as is said of the Apostles, they [[Mark 16:20|preached every where: the Lord working withal, and confirming the word with signs that followed|Prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis]]. And the Apostle says: [[Heb 2:1|ought we more diligently to observe the things which we have heard|Abundantius oportet nos observare ea quæ audivimus]], [[Heb 2:4|God also bearing them witness by signs and wonders and divers miracles and distributions of the Holy Ghost|contestante Deo signis et portentis, et variis virtutibus, et Spiritus Sancti distributionibus]]. See how inviolate and unshaken is the certainty of the Christian and Catholic faith. [[118:167|And hath loved them exceedingly|Et dilexit ea vehementer]], as it befits a great good to be ardently loved.

paras.t: Servavi mandata tua per obedientiam, et testimonia tua per fidem formatam, id est caritati unitam, quia omnes viæ meæ in conspectu tuo, id est, universa quæ cogito, cupio, loquor et ago, videntur et judicantur a te. Hinc enim sanctus Job ait : Nonne Deus scit viam meam, et cunctos gressus meos dinumerat? Et iterum, Signasti quasi in sacculo delicta mea ; itemque, Observasti omnes semitas meas, et vestigia pedum meorum considerasti. O quanta est nobis causa sollicite ac timorate ambulandi coram Deo judice nostro ! Nam et maximam injuriam facit judici, qui eo præsente et prohibente, male agit. Sic nos qui scimus Deum omnia nostra opera intueri, vehementissime inhonoramus eum, quod sine diligenti custodia cordis coram eo conversamur. Idcirco Boetius optime dixit : Magna est vobis indicta necessitas probitatis, si dissimulare non vultis, quoniam omnia agitis ante oculos Judicis cuncta cernentis. Semper igitur divinæ majestatis præsentiam cogitemus, dicentes cum Elia, Vivit Dominus, in cujus conspectu sto hodie : sicque vivamus tanquam mox judicandi ab eo. Et utique si ista pensemus, incipiemus Deum vehementer timere, in tantum ut cum beato Job dicere poterimus : Considerans Deum, timore sollicitor ; et rursus, Semper quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum, et pondus ejus ferre non potui. Hic autem timor præclarus facit vitare peccata, et observari mandata, quemadmodum Salomon profitetur : Timor Domini fons vitæ, ut declinet a ruina mortis.
