Hoc dicit nobis Apostolus: Scimus quoniam si terrestris domus nostra hujus habitationis dissolvatur, quod ædificationem habemus ex Deo, domum non manufactam, æternam in cœlo. Et iterum: Ingrediemur illam requiem nos qui credidimus. Christus quoque: Vado, inquit, parare vobis locum; et si abiero, et præparavero vobis locum, iterum venio et accipiam vos ad me ipsum, ut ubi sum ego, et vos sitis. Et iterum Dominus ait: Ecce ego creo cælos novos et terram novam: et exsultabitis et gaudebitis usque in æternum in his quæ ego creo. Hoc autem quod dicitur, In domum Domini ibimus, est verbum bonæ spei. Non enim certitudinaliter scimus hoc, nisi dicantur hæc verba in persona Ecclesiæ. Denique, quam vehementer, ineffabiliter, incomparabiliterque gaudendum est nobis de hoc, quod in hanc domum Domini sumus ituri, in qua Deus sublimis et benedictus facie ad faciem sine fine videtur, in qua invenitur æterna securitas et plena jucunditas, in qua erimus sicut angeli Dei, satiabiturque in bonis desiderium nostrum! Hujus domus ingressu dignus non est, qui in carnalibus jucundatur, qui in sensibilibus detinetur, qui non contemplatur cœlestia, qui non servit Deo in sanctitate atque justitia: quia ut asseritur, non intrabit in illam aliquid coinquinatum.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of a man who holds all present things cheap and longs from his heart for the heavenly dwelling, the Prophet says: [[121:1|I rejoiced|Lætatus sum]] in the Lord, with spiritual joy, [[121:1|at the things|in his]], that is, at the consideration of the things [[121:1|that were said to me|quæ dicta sunt mihi]] by the Prophets and Apostles and their successors, or by the revelation of angels, or by inward inspiration. And what was said, he adds: [[121:1|We shall go into the house of the Lord|In domum Domini ibimus]]: that is, into the Church triumphant, into the fatherland of the Blessed, into the kingdom of heaven, we shall go after our sojourn in this life, when we have been cleansed of all guilt. This the Apostle tells us: For [[2 Cor 5:1|we know, if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved, that we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in heaven|Scimus quoniam si terrestris domus nostra hujus habitationis dissolvatur, quod ædificationem habemus ex Deo, domum non manufactam, æternam in cœlo]]. And again: [[Heb 4:3|we, who have believed, shall enter into rest|Ingrediemur illam requiem nos qui credidimus]]. Christ also says: [[John 14:2|I go|Vado]], he says, [[John 14:2|to prepare a place for you|parare vobis locum]]: [[John 14:3|And if I shall go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will take you to myself: that where I am, you also may be|et si abiero, et præparavero vobis locum, iterum venio et accipiam vos ad me ipsum, ut ubi sum ego, et vos sitis]]. And again the Lord says: [[Is 65:17|behold I create new heavens, and a new earth|Ecce ego creo cælos novos et terram novam]]: [[Is 65:18|you shall be glad and rejoice for ever in these things, which I create|et exsultabitis et gaudebitis usque in æternum in his quæ ego creo]] [Denis's text has “rejoice and be glad” in the reverse order of the Vulgate]. Now this saying, [[121:1|We shall go into the house of the Lord|In domum Domini ibimus]], is a word of good hope. For we do not know this with certainty, unless these words are said in the person of the Church. And so how vehemently, how ineffably, how incomparably ought we to rejoice at this, that we are to go into this house of the Lord, in which God, exalted and blessed, is seen [[1 Cor 13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]] without end; in which is found eternal security and full delight; in which we shall be [[Matt 22:30|as the angels of God|sicut angeli Dei]], and our desire shall be filled with good things[[Ps 102:5||]]! He is not worthy to enter this house who takes delight in carnal things, who is held fast by the things of sense, who does not contemplate heavenly things, who does not serve God in [[Luke 1:75|holiness and justice|sanctitate atque justitia]]: for, as is declared, [[Apoc 21:27|There shall not enter into it any thing defiled|non intrabit in illam aliquid coinquinatum]].

paras.t: Signum autem et causa sperandi, quod ibimus in domum Domini, est, quia jam Stantes erant pedes nostri, id est, desideria nostra et contemplationes nostræ, fixa et stabilita fuerunt in atriis tuis, Jerusalem, id est in mansionibus regni cœlestis: ita quod conversatio nostra fuit in cœlis, et omnia opera nostra ordinavimus ad vitam æternam, quam summe atque finaliter desideramus. Hoc est quod ait Apostolus: Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem, et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam, et Ecclesiam primitivorum, qui conscripti sunt in cœlis. Alibi quoque: Nos, inquit, revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes, in eamdem imaginem transformamur, de claritate in claritatem.
paras.en: And the sign and cause of our hope that [[121:1|We shall go into the house of the Lord|In domum Domini ibimus]] is that already [[121:2|Our feet were standing|Stantes erant pedes nostri]], that is, our desires and our contemplations were fixed and settled [[121:2|in thy courts, O Jerusalem|in atriis tuis, Jerusalem]], that is, in the mansions of the heavenly kingdom: so that [[Phil 3:20|our conversation is in heaven|conversatio nostra fuit in cœlis]], and we have ordered all our works to eternal life, which we desire supremely and as our last end. This is what the Apostle says: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the company of many thousands of angels|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem, et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam]], [[Heb 12:23|And to the church of the firstborn who are written in the heavens|et Ecclesiam primitivorum, qui conscripti sunt in cœlis]]. And elsewhere: We, he says, [[2 Cor 3:18|beholding the glory of the Lord with open face, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory|revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes, in eamdem imaginem transformamur, de claritate in claritatem]].

paras.t: Jerusalem ista cœlestis, est quæ ædificatur quotidie usque ad consummationem sæculi ex vivis lapidibus, id est sanctis animabus ad patriam pervenientibus, ut civitas summa atque perfecta, taliter videlicet qualiter decet ædificari civitatem Regis æterni. Ædificatur enim ex pretiosis, politis, rationalibus ac sanctis lapidibus, scilicet angelis atque hominibus, quomodo Paulus testatur: In Christo omnis ædificatio constructa, crescit in templum sanctum in Domino, in quo et vos coædificamini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto. Civitas autem dicitur quasi civium unitas. Tanto igitur cœlestis Jerusalem verius civitas appellatur, quam aliqua mansio viæ; quanto cœlestium civium major concordia est, quam aliquorum in via. Cujus participatio ejus in id ipsum: id est, omnes cives hujus civitatis idem bonum participant, quoniam eodem summo bono omnes fruuntur: magis tamen et minus, secundum quod magis ac minus dilexerunt. Deus ergo est id ipsum ejus, id est invariabile indivisumque bonum supernæ Jerusalem: cujus participatio, id est fruitio, beatitudo, deificatio, qua divinam bonitatem participat, est uniformis et sempiterna, quemadmodum scriptum est: Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum Deum verum; et iterum, Similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est. Vel, Cujus participatio ejus in id ipsum, id est, bonum omnium est bonum singulorum, et econverso, in civitate cœlesti. Quum enim amor sit sui diffusivus et communicativus, sicut in patria est perfectissimus mutuus amor omnium Beatorum; sic ibi est plenissima communio beatitudinis singulorum. Nam de felicitate unius, alius gaudet sicut de propria: imo singuli singulis congratulantur, et superiores inferioribus tradunt de perfectionibus sibi divinitus datis, secundum magnum Dionysium. Hæc autem nulli civitati terrenæ proprie competunt.
paras.en: This heavenly [[121:3|Jerusalem|Jerusalem]] is the one [[121:3|which is built|quæ ædificatur]] daily until the consummation of the world out of living stones[[1 Pet 2:5||]], that is, out of holy souls arriving at the fatherland, [[121:3|as a city|ut civitas]], supreme and perfect, built, that is, as befits the city of the eternal King to be built. For it is built of precious, polished, rational and holy stones, namely of angels and men, as Paul testifies: In Christ [[Eph 2:21|all the building, being framed together, groweth up into an holy temple in the Lord|omnis ædificatio constructa, crescit in templum sanctum in Domino]], [[Eph 2:22|In whom you also are built together into an habitation of God in the Spirit|in quo et vos coædificamini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto]]. Now a city (*civitas*) is so called as being a unity of citizens (*civium unitas*). So the heavenly Jerusalem is called a city more truly than any dwelling on the way, by as much as the concord of the heavenly citizens is greater than that of any on the way. [[121:3|which is compact together|Cujus participatio ejus in id ipsum]] [literally, “whose sharing is in the selfsame”; Denis expounds the Latin words]: that is, all the citizens of this city share the same good, since they all enjoy the same supreme good: yet more and less, according as they have loved more and less. God, then, is its *selfsame*, that is, the unchanging and undivided good of the Jerusalem above: and its *sharing*, that is, the enjoyment, beatitude and deification by which it shares in the divine goodness, is uniform and everlasting, as it is written: [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God|Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum Deum verum]]; and again, [[1 John 3:2|we shall be like to him: because we shall see him as he is|Similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est]]. Or, [[121:3|which is compact together|Cujus participatio ejus in id ipsum]]: that is, in the heavenly city the good of all is the good of each, and conversely. For since love pours itself out and communicates itself, just as in the fatherland there is the most perfect mutual love of all the Blessed, so there is there the fullest communion of the beatitude of each. For one rejoices at the happiness of another as at his own: indeed each congratulates each, and the higher hand on to the lower something of the perfections given them by God, according to the great Dionysius. But none of this properly befits any earthly city.

paras.t: Illuc enim, id est ad supernam Jerusalem, ascenderunt, quantum ad animam, tribus, non qualescumque, sed tribus Domini, id est populus ex Deo per gratiam natus, videlicet omnes electi jam defuncti, et ab omni macula depurati. Multi enim eorum simul cum Christo ascenderunt, et alii interim sunt secuti. Præcesseruntque nos, ut præparent nobis locum, ut orent pro nobis, ut eorum imitemur vestigia, prout monet Apostolus: Ideo et nos tantam habentes impositam nobis nubem testium, deponentes omne pondus et circumstans nos peccatum, per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen. Testimonium Israel: id est, ascensus iste est testimonium Israel, id est populi fidelis Deum contemplantis. Nam huic populo Deus testatus est, quod ascenderent ad domum suam cœlestem. Imo Jacob, sicut et Abrahæ, promisit hoc Deus. Ad confitendum nomini Domini, confessione laudis æternæ, quemadmodum in Apocalypsi legitur: Requiem non habebant die ac nocte, dicentia: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus, ... Dominus Deus omnipotens.
paras.en: [[121:4|For thither|Illuc enim]], that is, to the Jerusalem above, did [[121:4|go up|ascenderunt]], as to the soul, [[121:4|the tribes|tribus]], not any whatever, but [[121:4|the tribes of the Lord|tribus Domini]], that is, the people born of God through grace, namely all the elect already departed and cleansed of every stain. For many of them went up together with Christ, and others have followed in the meantime. And they have gone before us to prepare a place for us, to pray for us, and that we may follow in their footsteps, as the Apostle admonishes: And therefore [[Heb 12:1|we also having so great a cloud of witnesses over our head, laying aside every weight and sin which surrounds us, let us run by patience to the fight proposed to us|et nos tantam habentes impositam nobis nubem testium, deponentes omne pondus et circumstans nos peccatum, per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen]]. [[121:4|the testimony of Israel|Testimonium Israel]]: that is, this ascent is the testimony of Israel, that is, of the faithful people that contemplates God. For to this people God testified that they would go up to his heavenly house. Indeed God promised this to Jacob, as also to Abraham. [[121:4|to praise the name of the Lord|Ad confitendum nomini Domini]], with the confession of eternal praise, as we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 4:8|they rested not day and night, saying: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God Almighty|Requiem non habebant die ac nocte, dicentia: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus, ... Dominus Deus omnipotens]].

paras.t: Quia illic, id est in civitate cœlesti, sederunt, sedent, atque sedebunt, sedes, id est sancti Apostoli et apostolici viri, in quibus Deus per gratiam requiescit. Nam et anima justi, sedes est Sapientiæ increatæ, quæ Deus est. Sedes in judicio, id est, isti sedent in regno cœlesti cum Christo, ut in die judicii judicent cum Christo, quemadmodum ipse in Evangelio ait: Vos qui secuti estis me, in regeneratione quum sederit Filius hominis in sede majestatis suæ, sedebitis et vos super duodecim thronos, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel. Unde alibi dicitur: Judicabunt nationes, et dominabuntur populis. Sedes super domum David, id est super populum Christi, cui prælati sunt et judices constituti. Denique solus Christus judicabit, proferendo sententiam. Trinitas vero superbenedicta judicabit per auctoritatem. Sancti vero et apostolici viri, qui propter Christi amorem omnia reliquerunt, et se ipsos abnegarunt, judicabunt per approbationem et assessionem.
paras.en: [[121:5|Because|Quia]] there, that is, in the heavenly city, [[121:5|their seats have sat|sederunt]], sit and shall sit: the *seats*, that is, the holy Apostles and apostolic men, in whom God rests through grace. For the soul of the just man too is the seat of uncreated Wisdom, which is God[[Prov 14:33||]][[Wis 7:27||]]. [[121:5|in judgment|in judicio]]: that is, these sit in the heavenly kingdom with Christ, so that on the day of judgment they may judge with Christ, as he himself says in the Gospel: [[Matt 19:28|you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel|Vos qui secuti estis me, in regeneratione quum sederit Filius hominis in sede majestatis suæ, sedebitis et vos super duodecim thronos, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel]]. Hence it is said elsewhere: [[Wis 3:8|They shall judge nations, and rule over people|Judicabunt nationes, et dominabuntur populis]]. [[121:5|seats upon the house of David|Sedes super domum David]], that is, over the people of Christ, over whom they have been set as prelates and judges. Now Christ alone will judge by pronouncing the sentence; the superblessed Trinity will judge by authority; and the saints and apostolic men who for the love of Christ left all things and denied themselves will judge by approval and by sitting beside him [*assessio*, sitting as assessors to the judge].

paras.t: Quum ergo sit tanta beatitudo civitatis supernæ, o universi fideles, Rogate quæ ad pacem sunt Jerusalem: id est, Deum invocate pro his bonis, videlicet pro donis Spiritus Sancti, per quæ mereamini ad cœlestis Jerusalem pacem perduci. Moxque convertens Propheta sermonem ad triumphantem Ecclesiam, ait: Et abundantia divinorum charismatum seu spiritualium gratiarum detur divinitus per tuam intercessionem, diligentibus te, id est nobis viatoribus, qui ad tuam societatem perduci optamus.
paras.en: Since, then, the beatitude of the city above is so great, O all ye faithful, [[121:6|Pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem|Rogate quæ ad pacem sunt Jerusalem]]: that is, call upon God for these good things, namely for the gifts of the Holy Ghost, through which you may deserve to be brought to the peace of the heavenly Jerusalem. And presently, turning his words to the Church triumphant, the Prophet says: [[121:6|and abundance|Et abundantia]] of divine charisms, or of spiritual graces, be given from God through thy intercession [[121:6|for them that love thee|diligentibus te]], that is, to us wayfarers, who long to be brought into thy company.

paras.t: Verum quoniam Petrus in sua Canonica ait, ut quilibet sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administraret; idcirco Propter fratres meos et proximos meos loquebar pacem de te, id est, felicitatem et gaudia tua, o superna Jerusalem, aliis prædicavi, quatenus fratres et proximos meos, id est fideles atque propinquos, erudirem, tuo amore accenderem, atque ad tuam unionem salvificam seu vitam æternam adducere possem. Propter domum Domini Dei nostri, id est, ut Ecclesiam militantem hoc modo ædificarem, quæsivi bona tibi, id est ad honorem et gloriam tuam: id est, orando et prædicando quæsivi spiritualia bona viatoribus ad gloriam Beatorum, videlicet ut ipsi amplius jucundentur, quantum ad præmium accidentale, pervenientibus viatoribus ad eorum consortium. Vel, Quæsivi bona tibi, Ecclesiæ triumphanti, laborando pro viribus, ut impleatur numerus electorum, et ædificentur muri tui per complementum.
paras.en: But since Peter says in his canonical epistle that [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administraret]], therefore: [[121:8|For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours, I spoke peace of thee|Propter fratres meos et proximos meos loquebar pacem de te]]: that is, I have preached thy happiness and thy joys, O Jerusalem above, to others, so that I might instruct my brethren and neighbours, that is, the faithful and those near me, kindle them with thy love, and lead them to saving union with thee, that is, to eternal life. [[121:9|Because of the house of the Lord our God|Propter domum Domini Dei nostri]], that is, that in this way I might build up the Church militant, [[121:9|I have sought good things for thee|quæsivi bona tibi]], that is, for thy honour and glory: that is, by praying and preaching I have sought spiritual goods for wayfarers, to the glory of the Blessed, namely that they may rejoice the more, as to their accidental reward [that is, the joy added to the essential reward of seeing God], when wayfarers come into their fellowship. Or, [[121:9|I have sought good things for thee|Quæsivi bona tibi]], the Church triumphant, by labouring with all my strength that the number of the elect may be filled up and thy walls be built up to their completion.

paras.t: Præterea, quia per Jerusalem allegorice significatur Ecclesia militans, ideo potest hic psalmus de Ecclesia militanti exponi. Sicque loquens Propheta in persona populi gentilis, ait: Lætatus sum in his quæ dicta sunt mihi ab Apostolis, scilicet quod in domum Domini, id est in Ecclesiam Christi, ibimus, ita quod pertinebimus ad societatem ac numerum Christianorum. Hoc est quod in Actibus recitatur. Quum enim Paulus Judæis blasphemantibus respondisset: Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quoniam repulistis illud, et indignos vos judicastis æternæ vitæ, ecce convertimur ad gentes: sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus, Posui te in lucem Gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ (quæ sunt verba Dei, de Christo loquentis per Isaiam); subjungitur: Audientes autem gentes, gavisæ sunt, et glorificaverunt verbum Domini, videlicet quia reprobatis Judæis, ipsi illuminandi essent a Christo.
paras.en: Moreover, since Jerusalem allegorically signifies the Church militant, this psalm can therefore be expounded of the Church militant. And so, speaking in the person of the gentile people, the Prophet says: [[121:1|I rejoiced at the things that were said to me|Lætatus sum in his quæ dicta sunt mihi]] by the Apostles, namely that [[121:1|We shall go into the house of the Lord|In domum Domini ibimus]], that is, into the Church of Christ, so that we shall belong to the fellowship and number of Christians. This is what is related in the Acts. For when Paul had answered the blaspheming Jews: [[Acts 13:46|To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God: but because you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold we turn to the Gentiles|Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quoniam repulistis illud, et indignos vos judicastis æternæ vitæ, ecce convertimur ad gentes]]: [[Acts 13:47|For so the Lord hath commanded us: I have set thee to be the light of the Gentiles: that thou mayest be for salvation unto the utmost part of the earth|sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus, Posui te in lucem Gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]] (which are the words of God speaking of Christ through Isaias[[Is 49:6||]]), it is added: [[Acts 13:48|the Gentiles hearing it were glad and glorified the word of the Lord|Audientes autem gentes, gavisæ sunt, et glorificaverunt verbum Domini]], namely because, the Jews being rejected, they were to be enlightened by Christ.

paras.t: Stantes erant, id est, erunt: sæpe enim Prophetæ loquuntur de futuro per modum præteriti, propter certitudinem prophetiæ; pedes nostri corporales et spirituales in atriis tuis, Jerusalem, id est in locis Ecclesiæ. Atria enim dicuntur introitus, seu loca per quæ in domum intratur. Unde spiritualia atria sunt fides, spes, caritas, per quas itur ad unitatem Ecclesiæ, cultumque divinum. In spiritualibus itaque atriis stant pedes spirituales, videlicet boni affectus et sanctæ cogitationes, quibus ad Deum graditur anima; in corporalibus vero atriis stant corporis pedes.
paras.en: [[121:2|were standing|Stantes erant]], that is, will be: for the Prophets often speak of the future in the manner of the past, because of the certainty of prophecy; [[121:2|Our feet|pedes nostri]], bodily and spiritual, [[121:2|in thy courts, O Jerusalem|in atriis tuis, Jerusalem]], that is, in the places of the Church. For *courts* are the name for entrances, the places through which one goes into a house. Hence the spiritual courts are faith, hope and charity, through which one goes to the unity of the Church and to the worship of God. So in the spiritual courts stand the spiritual feet, namely good affections and holy thoughts, by which the soul walks to God; and in the bodily courts stand the feet of the body.

paras.t: Jerusalem, id est Ecclesia militans, est quæ ædificatur ex Christifidelibus tanquam ex vivis lapidibus, ut civitas Dei, quoniam ipsa est civitas Salvatoris; cujus participatio ejus in id ipsum, id est, bona spiritualia civitatis hujus quodammodo exstant communia: quoniam unus fidelium alii impertitur quod ipse recepit; imo alteri cupit providere atque succurrere tanquam sibi ipsi, quemadmodum ait Apostolus: Non quæro quod mihi utile est, sed quod multis, ut salvi fiant; et alibi, Non quæ sua sunt singuli quærentes, sed quæ aliorum. Et quid mirum, si participatio Ecclesiæ est in id ipsum, quum affirmet Apostolus, Omnes vos unum estis in Christo Jesu?
paras.en: [[121:3|Jerusalem|Jerusalem]], that is, the Church militant, is the one [[121:3|which is built|quæ ædificatur]] of the faithful of Christ as of living stones[[1 Pet 2:5||]], [[121:3|as a city|ut civitas]] of God, since she is the city of the Saviour; [[121:3|which is compact together|cujus participatio ejus in id ipsum]]: that is, the spiritual goods of this city are in a manner common: for one of the faithful imparts to another what he himself has received; indeed he desires to provide for and help another as himself, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 10:33|not seeking that which is profitable to myself but to many|Non quæro quod mihi utile est, sed quod multis]], [[1 Cor 10:33|that they may be saved|ut salvi fiant]]; and elsewhere, [[Phil 2:4|not considering the things that are his own, but those that are other men's|Non quæ sua sunt singuli quærentes, sed quæ aliorum]]. And what wonder if the sharing of the Church is *in the selfsame*, when the Apostle affirms: [[Gal 3:28|you are all one in Christ Jesus|Omnes vos unum estis in Christo Jesu]]?

paras.t: Illuc enim, id est ad Ecclesiam militantem, ascenderunt tribus, tribus Domini, id est familiæ atque progenies electorum ad fidem et gratiam, scilicet Christiani; de quibus in Actibus dicitur, Crediderunt quotquot præordinati erant ad vitam æternam. Nam et ad ecclesiam materialem Christiani corporali motu conveniunt; ad Ecclesiam autem spiritualem, id est congregationem fidelium seu ecclesiasticam unitatem, conveniunt affectu, fide et opere, idem credendo, idem sperando, idem amando, eademque præcepta servando.
paras.en: [[121:4|For thither|Illuc enim]], that is, to the Church militant, [[121:4|did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord|ascenderunt tribus, tribus Domini]], that is, the families and offspring of those elected to faith and grace, namely Christians; of whom it is said in the Acts: [[Acts 13:48|as many as were ordained to life everlasting|Crediderunt quotquot præordinati erant ad vitam æternam]] [the margin reads Act. viii, 48; the words are Acts 13:48] believed. For Christians come together to the material church by bodily movement; but to the spiritual Church, that is, the congregation of the faithful, or the unity of the Church, they come by affection, faith and works: believing the same things, hoping the same, loving the same, and keeping the same commandments.

paras.t: Quia illic sederunt sedes in judicio. In Ecclesia namque constituti sunt judices, tam spirituales quam sæculares: et isti sunt sedes, id est in sede sedentes, super domum David, id est præsidentes populo Christi, qui significatur per David.
paras.en: [[121:5|Because their seats have sat in judgment|Quia illic sederunt sedes in judicio]]. For in the Church judges have been set, both spiritual and secular: and these are the [[121:5|seats|sedes]], that is, those sitting on a seat, [[121:5|upon the house of David|super domum David]], that is, presiding over the people of Christ, who is signified by David.

paras.t: Rogate, o Sancti in patria, et o omnes devoti in via, quæ ad pacem sunt Jerusalem, id est, illa vestris precibus procurate Ecclesiæ, quæ sunt pro spirituali pace et statu pacifico ejus. Hoc enim oravit Apostolus: Obsecro, inquiens, fieri orationes pro omnibus hominibus, pro regibus et omnibus qui in sublimitate constituti sunt, ut quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate. Et abundantia gratiæ et virtutum sit, o Ecclesia, diligentibus te, id est universis qui zelum pium et amorosum habent pro bono statu ac spirituali profectu totius Ecclesiæ militantis: qualis exstitit Paulus, quem sollicitudo omnium Ecclesiarum afflixit.
paras.en: [[121:6|Pray ye|Rogate]], O Saints in the fatherland, and O all ye devout on the way, [[121:6|for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem|quæ ad pacem sunt Jerusalem]], that is, obtain by your prayers for the Church those things that make for her spiritual peace and peaceful state. For this the Apostle prayed: [[1 Tim 2:1|I desire|Obsecro]], he says, [[1 Tim 2:1|that supplications, prayers, intercessions and thanksgivings be made for all men|fieri orationes pro omnibus hominibus]], [[1 Tim 2:2|For kings and for all that are in high station: that we may lead a quiet and a peaceable life in all piety|pro regibus et omnibus qui in sublimitate constituti sunt, ut quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate]]. [[121:6|and abundance|Et abundantia]] of grace and virtues be, O Church, [[121:6|for them that love thee|diligentibus te]], that is, for all who have a devout and loving zeal for the good state and spiritual progress of the whole Church militant: such as Paul was, whom the solicitude for all the churches afflicted[[2 Cor 11:28||]].

paras.t: Propter fratres meos et proximos meos, id est propter salutem et informationem fratrum ac proximorum meorum, loquebar in oratione mea ad Deum bona de te, rogando Deum, ut bona spiritualia tibi conferret.
paras.en: [[121:8|For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours|Propter fratres meos et proximos meos]], that is, for the salvation and instruction of my brethren and neighbours, [[121:8|I spoke|loquebar]] in my prayer to God good things [the margin notes that other copies read *pacem*, “peace”, as the Vulgate does] [[121:8|of thee|de te]], asking God to bestow spiritual goods on thee.

paras.t: Propter domum Domini Dei nostri, id est, ut Ecclesia Christi modo proficeret in gratia, et postmodum esset in gloria, quæsivi bona tibi, id est, dona Dei tibi acquirere laboravi, o Ecclesia Christi nunc militans. Ac si dicat: Propter tuam salutem, non propter meam commoditatem, studui tibi auxiliari.
paras.en: [[121:9|Because of the house of the Lord our God|Propter domum Domini Dei nostri]], that is, that the Church of Christ might now advance in grace and afterwards be in glory, [[121:9|I have sought good things for thee|quæsivi bona tibi]], that is, I have laboured to gain the gifts of God for thee, O Church of Christ, now militant. As if he were saying: For thy salvation, not for my own advantage, have I striven to help thee.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum spirituali hilaritate perfusum, animamque devotam spiritualiter lætificantem audivimus: quem decet nos cum præcordiali gaudio decantare, nec primum psalmi hujus versiculum sine caritatis fervore ac spiritualis jucunditatis excessu depromere. Et quia ad hanc cœlestem Jerusalem, in qua est ineffabilis concordia caritasque plenissima, nemo pertingit, nisi caritatis et pacis amator et observator; conemur in vera Dei ac proximi dilectione vivere atque proficere, perpendentes et adimplentes illud beatissimi Apostoli: Obsecro vos ego vinctus in Domino, ut digne ambuletis vocatione qua vocati estis, cum omni humilitate et mansuetudine, cum patientia supportantes invicem in caritate, solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis. Sic itaque conversantes in militanti Ecclesia, digni habebuntur ingredi Ecclesiam triumphantem, cœlestem Jerusalem, quoniam vitam civium ejus imitantur in terra. Hanc enim civitatem supernam eleganter describens Isaias, in Dei persona ait: Ponam visionem tuam pacem, et præpositos tuos justitiam; occupabit salus muros tuos. Non erit tibi amplius sol ad lucendum per diem, nec splendor lunæ illuminabit te; sed erit tibi Dominus in lucem sempiternam, et Deus tuus in gloriam tuam. Populus autem tuus, omnes justi. Ecce quam appetenda decoraque civitas! Ad quam duobus pedibus caritatis, videlicet Dei et proximi, itur et pervenitur. Spiritualium etenim gressuum pedem movet dilectio: quæ etiam intrat ubi scientia foris stat, sicut venerabilis Hugo testatur.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm steeped in spiritual gladness, and spiritually gladdening the devout soul: which it befits us to sing with heartfelt joy, and not to utter even the first verse of this psalm without the fervour of charity and an overflowing of spiritual delight. And since no one reaches this heavenly Jerusalem, in which there is ineffable concord and the fullest charity, unless he is a lover and keeper of charity and peace, let us strive to live and to advance in true love of God and of our neighbour, weighing and fulfilling that saying of the most blessed Apostle: [[Eph 4:1|I therefore, a prisoner in the Lord, beseech you that you walk worthy of the vocation in which you are called|Obsecro vos ego vinctus in Domino, ut digne ambuletis vocatione qua vocati estis]], [[Eph 4:2|With all humility and mildness, with patience, supporting one another in charity|cum omni humilitate et mansuetudine, cum patientia supportantes invicem in caritate]], [[Eph 4:3|Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace|solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis]]. Living thus in the Church militant, they will be held worthy to enter the Church triumphant, the heavenly Jerusalem, since they imitate on earth the life of its citizens. For Isaias, describing this city above with elegance, says in the person of God: [[Is 60:17|I will make thy visitation peace, and thy overseers justice|Ponam visionem tuam pacem, et præpositos tuos justitiam]] [Denis reads *visionem*, “vision”, where the Vulgate has *visitationem*, “visitation”]; [[Is 60:18|salvation shall possess thy walls|occupabit salus muros tuos]]. [[Is 60:19|Thou shalt no more have the sun for thy light by day, neither shall the brightness of the moon enlighten thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee for an everlasting light, and thy God for thy glory|Non erit tibi amplius sol ad lucendum per diem, nec splendor lunæ illuminabit te; sed erit tibi Dominus in lucem sempiternam, et Deus tuus in gloriam tuam]]. [[Is 60:21|And thy people shall be all just|Populus autem tuus, omnes justi]]. Behold how desirable and how fair a city! To which one goes and arrives on the two feet of charity, namely love of God and of neighbour. For it is love that moves the foot of spiritual steps: love, which enters even where knowledge stands outside, as the venerable Hugh testifies.

paras.t: Precatio. Omnium existentium opifex, Domine, statue pedes nostros in atriis tuis, et ædifica Jerusalem supernam in nobis; fiat nobis pax continua in virtute tua: ut et ejusdem semper civitatis bona devoti quæramus, et te præstante inveniamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, maker of all that exists, set our feet in thy courts, and build up the Jerusalem above within us; let there be continual peace for us in thy strength: that we may ever devoutly seek the good things of that same city, and by thy gift find them.

122.title: EXPLANATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI SECUNDI : AD TE LEVAVI OCULOS MEOS.
122.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and twenty-second psalm: To thee have I lifted up my eyes.

paras.t: Insuper titulus psalmi jam declarandi est : Canticum graduum : cujus intellectus liquet ex dictis. In hoc autem quarto psalmo graduali agitur de quarto gradu spiritualis ascensionis, qui est, inter omnes adversitates atque angustias inconcussam habere fiduciam de miseratione divina, sicut Job ait : Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo.
paras.en: Further, the title of the psalm now to be explained is: *A gradual canticle*[[122:1||]]; its meaning is clear from what has been said. In this fourth gradual psalm, then, the fourth degree of the spiritual ascent is treated, which is to have, amid all adversities and straits, an unshaken trust in the divine mercy, as Job says: [[Job 13:15|Although he should kill me, I will trust in him|Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo]].

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta in persona hominis graviter tribulati, et tamen de Domino immobiliter confidentis, ait : Ad te levavi, credendo, sperando, amando, contemplando, patienter ferendo, fideliter operando, oculos meos, præsertim intellectuales, et etiam corporales : quemadmodum Jeremias ait, Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cœlos ; qui habitas in cœlis materialibus et immaterialibus. Deus enim æternus et incircumscriptus, in nullo ente creato habitat, ita quod includatur aut comprehendatur seu limitetur ; in omnibus tamen est per essentiam, præsentiam atque potentiam. Ibi vero præcipue esse et habitare censetur, ubi gratiosius et evidentius operatur : idcirco in angelis sanctis hominibusque devotis, qui sunt cœli spirituales, specialiter esse et habitare asseritur. In cœlis quoque, et præsertim in cœlo empyreo, est et habitat Deus, quoniam ibi videtur sicuti est. Verumtamen, quoniam omnes Beati in cœlo materiali habitant, et nunc per hoc quod dicitur, Qui habitas in cœlis, intelligitur Deus, videtur de immaterialibus cœlis loqui, quia in illis Deo habitare est proprium.
paras.en: So the Prophet, speaking in the person of a man grievously afflicted and yet trusting immovably in the Lord, says: [[122:1|To thee have I lifted up|Ad te levavi]], by believing, hoping, loving, contemplating, bearing patiently, working faithfully, [[122:1|my eyes|oculos meos]], above all the eyes of the understanding, and the bodily ones as well; as Jeremias says: [[Lam 3:41|Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord in the heavens|Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cœlos]]; [[122:1|who dwellest in heaven|qui habitas in cœlis]], the material heavens and the immaterial. For God, eternal and uncircumscribed, dwells in no created being in such a way as to be enclosed, comprehended or limited by it; yet He is in all things by essence, presence and power. But He is held to be and to dwell chiefly there where He works more graciously and more manifestly: and so He is said to be and to dwell in a special way in the holy angels and in devout men, who are spiritual heavens. In the heavens also, and above all in the empyrean heaven, God is and dwells, since there He is seen [[1 John 3:2|as he is|sicuti est]]. Yet since all the Blessed dwell in the material heaven, and here by the words [[122:1|Who dwellest in heaven|Qui habitas in cœlis]] God is meant, he seems to be speaking of the immaterial heavens, because to dwell in them is proper to God.

paras.t: Ecce sicut oculi servorum sunt in manibus, id est potestate et voluntate, dominorum suorum, ita quod diriguntur ad eos, postulando veniam, si offenderunt ; vel præmium, si laboraverunt ; vel informationem, si ignorent quid agere debeant ; Sicut oculi ancillæ sunt in manibus dominæ suæ : secundum modum jam dictum ; ita oculi nostri diriguntur ad Dominum Deum nostrum, auxilium, indulgentiam, gratiamque precantes, donec misereatur nostri, faciendo quod postulamus, vel certe dando quod ipse novit nobis esse utilius. Et quia tamdiu indigemus misericordia Dei, quamdiu versamur in sæculo isto ; ideo quamdiu hic vivimus, debemus indesinenter oculos nostros ad Deum dirigere, præcipue tamen dum graviter tentamur sive affligimur. Sciendum quoque, quod hoc loco vox ista, Donec, est affirmativa et inclusiva omnium temporum, sicut habetur de Joseph : Non cognovit eam (puta Mariam) donec peperit filium suum primogenitum. Non enim sic dicuntur oculi nostri ad Dominum dirigi donec misereatur nostri, quasi quum misertus fuerit nostri, non amplius dirigentur ad eum.
paras.en: [[122:2|Behold as the eyes of servants are on the hands|Ecce sicut oculi servorum sunt in manibus]], that is, the power and will, [[122:2|of their masters|dominorum suorum]], so that they are directed towards them, asking pardon if they have offended, or reward if they have laboured, or instruction if they do not know what they ought to do; [[122:2|As the eyes of the handmaid are on the hands of her mistress|Sicut oculi ancillæ sunt in manibus dominæ suæ]], in the manner just described: [[122:2|so are our eyes|ita oculi nostri]] directed [[122:2|unto the Lord our God|ad Dominum Deum nostrum]], praying for help, pardon and grace, [[122:2|until he have mercy on us|donec misereatur nostri]], by doing what we ask, or at least by giving what He knows to be more profitable for us. And since we need God's mercy for as long as we live in this world, therefore as long as we live here we ought to direct our eyes to God unceasingly, above all when we are grievously tempted or afflicted. It should be known too that here the word *until* is affirmative and takes in all times, as is said of Joseph: [[Matt 1:25|he knew her not|Non cognovit eam]] (that is, Mary) [[Matt 1:25|till she brought forth her first born son|donec peperit filium suum primogenitum]]. For our eyes are not said to be directed to the Lord [[122:2|until he have mercy on us|donec misereatur nostri]], as though, once He has had mercy on us, they would no longer be directed to Him.

paras.t: Miserere nostri, Domine, mala culpæ et pœnæ tollendo, miserere nostri, gratiam et gloriam conferendo, quia multum repleti sumus despectione, id est, ab iniquis multum despecti sumus. Deridetur enim justi simplicitas, sicut Job ait. Et Paulus : Nos, inquit, stulti propter Christum. Electi namque a reprobis contemnuntur, religiosi a sæcularibus, humiles a superbis, egeni a divitibus. Ideo subditur : Quia multum repleta est anima nostra miseriis variis, in tantum ut facta sit opprobrium abundantibus, id est divitibus, et despectio superbis.
paras.en: [[122:3|Have mercy on us, O Lord|Miserere nostri, Domine]], by taking away the evils of guilt and of punishment; [[122:3|have mercy on us|miserere nostri]], by bestowing grace and glory; [[122:3|for we are greatly filled with contempt|quia multum repleti sumus despectione]], that is, we are much despised by the wicked. For [[Job 12:4|the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn|Deridetur enim justi simplicitas]], as Job says. And Paul: [[1 Cor 4:10|We are|Nos]], he says, [[1 Cor 4:10|fools for Christs sake|stulti propter Christum]]. For the elect are scorned by the reprobate, religious by men of the world, the humble by the proud, the needy by the rich. Therefore it is added: [[122:4|For our soul is greatly filled|Quia multum repleta est anima nostra]] with manifold miseries, so much that [[122:4|we are a reproach to the rich|facta sit opprobrium abundantibus]] [the Latin *abundantibus* is literally "those who abound"], that is, to the wealthy, [[122:4|and contempt to the proud|et despectio superbis]].

paras.t: Psalmus iste instruit nos oculum cordis ad Deum in omni necessitate erigere, neque recedere donec misericordiam consequamur. Oportet enim semper orare, et non deficere. Præterea ad istam fiducialem sanctamque elevationem inducit nos Christus suo exemplo. De quo scriptum est : Sublevatis Jesus oculis in cœlum, dixit : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum. Et iterum : Jesus elevatis sursum oculis, dixit : Pater, gratias ago tibi. Ad quid enim elevatio corporalium oculorum sibi necessaria fuit, cujus interior oculus Deum incessanter per speciem vidit, et cujus voluntas in divino amore semper æqualiter arsit ? Non ergo ob aliud fecit hæc, nisi ut nos eadem faciamus. Fecit autem ideo, ut ostenderet se omnia a Patre habere ; sed et hoc fecit, quatenus nos jugiter fateamur a Deo esse, quidquid in nobis boni exstiterit, juxta illud : Non potest homo accipere quidquam, nisi datum fuerit ei de cœlo.
paras.en: This psalm teaches us to raise the eye of the heart to God in every need, and not to draw back until we obtain mercy. For [[Luke 18:1|we ought always to pray and not to faint|Oportet enim semper orare, et non deficere]]. Moreover Christ leads us by His example to this trustful and holy lifting up. Of Him it is written: Jesus, [[John 17:1|lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said|Sublevatis Jesus oculis in cœlum, dixit]]: Father, [[John 17:1|the hour is come. Glorify thy Son|venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]]. And again: [[John 11:41|Jesus lifting up his eyes, said: Father, I give thee thanks|Jesus elevatis sursum oculis, dixit : Pater, gratias ago tibi]]. For what need had He to lift up His bodily eyes, whose inward eye saw God unceasingly face to face [*per speciem*, that is, by direct vision, not by faith], and whose will burned always with equal ardour in divine love? He did these things, then, for no other reason than that we should do the same. He did it, too, to show that He has all things from the Father; and He did it also so that we may always confess that whatever good is found in us is from God, according to the words: [[John 3:27|A man cannot receive any thing, unless it be given him from heaven|Non potest homo accipere quidquam, nisi datum fuerit ei de cœlo]].

paras.t: Precatio. Nos tui servi oculos nostros ad te levamus, qui habitas in cœlestibus, Domine Deus, nostri miserere, et de opprobrio et æterna superborum eripe despectione.
paras.en: Prayer. We Thy servants lift up our eyes to Thee, who dwellest in the heavenly places, O Lord God: have mercy on us, and deliver us from the reproach and the eternal contempt of the proud.

123.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI TERTII : NISI QUIA DOMINUS ERAT IN NOBIS.
123.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and twenty-third psalm: If it had not been that the Lord was with us.

paras.t: Hujus insuper psalmi titulus idem est cum titulo psalmi præcedentis. Quamvis autem psalmus iste convenientissime exponitur in persona martyrum jam cum Christo triumphantium, seu aliorum Beatorum in patria, qui per multas tribulationes ingressi sunt regnum cœlorum ; potest tamen viatoribus convenire, qui a tentationibus, passionibus, persecutionibusque divinitus liberati, gratias referunt de sua evasione. Et rite ponitur psalmus hic quintus in ordine psalmorum gradualium. Tractat enim de quinto gradu spiritualis ascensionis, qui est, non propriis viribus, sed gratiæ Dei suam liberationem adscribere. Unde Dominus in libro Judicum ait : Ne glorietur contra me Israel, et dicat, Meis viribus liberatus sum.
paras.en: The title of this psalm, moreover, is the same as the title of the preceding psalm. And although this psalm is most fittingly expounded in the person of the martyrs now triumphing with Christ, or of the other Blessed in the fatherland, who [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations|per multas tribulationes]] have entered into the kingdom of heaven, it can nevertheless suit wayfarers [that is, those still on the way in this life, as opposed to the Blessed who have reached the fatherland], who, delivered by God from temptations, sufferings and persecutions, give thanks for their escape. And this psalm is rightly placed fifth in the order of the gradual psalms. For it treats of the fifth degree of spiritual ascent, which is to ascribe one's deliverance not to one's own strength but to the grace of God. Hence the Lord says in the book of Judges: [[Judg 7:2|lest Israel should glory against me, and say: I was delivered by my own strength|Ne glorietur contra me Israel, et dicat, Meis viribus liberatus sum]].

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta de homine seu populo, a multis tentationibus atque periculis liberato, ait : Nisi quia Dominus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israel : id est, populus fidelis, Deum fideliter speculans, profiteatur jam corde devoto ac grato, quod nisi Deus gratiose fuisset nobiscum : quod iteratur pro majori certitudine, pro ampliori gratitudine, pro exhortatione ferventiore, dum subditur, nisi quia Dominus erat in nobis, id est, per gratiam suæ defensionis nos protexisset ; Quum exsurgerent homines infideles, hæretici, tyranni, maligni, in nos, id est contra nos, mala pœnalia nobis inferentes, nosque ad mala culpæ inducere satagentes, forte vivos deglutissent nos, id est, ita nos occidissent, sicut occiditur quod a bestia vivum glutitur. Proprie autem convenit vox ista sanctis martyribus, quia tyranni conati sunt eos ad idololatriam seu Christi negationem inducere : quo facto, absorpta esset anima eorum, non caro : et ita vivi absorpti fuissent. Nam viventes in corpore, mortui fuissent in anima ; habentesque vitam naturæ, perdidissent vitam gratiæ et gloriæ.
paras.en: Speaking therefore of a man or a people delivered from many temptations and dangers, the Prophet says: [[123:1|If it had not been that the Lord was with us, let Israel now say|Nisi quia Dominus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israel]]: that is, let the faithful people, who faithfully contemplates God [*Israel* was taken to mean "one who sees God"], now confess with a devout and grateful heart that, had not God been graciously with us (which is repeated for greater certainty, for fuller gratitude, for more fervent exhortation, when it is added, [[123:2|If it had not been that the Lord was with us|nisi quia Dominus erat in nobis]]: that is, had he not protected us by the grace of his defence), [[123:2|When men rose up|Quum exsurgerent homines]], unbelievers, heretics, tyrants, the wicked, [[123:2|against us|in nos]], that is, in opposition to us, bringing penal evils upon us [that is, evils of punishment, as distinct from evils of guilt] and striving to lead us into evils of guilt, [[123:3|Perhaps they had swallowed us up alive|forte vivos deglutissent nos]]: that is, they would have slain us as that is slain which a beast swallows alive. Now this utterance properly suits the holy martyrs, because the tyrants tried to lead them to idolatry or to the denial of Christ; had this been done, their soul, not their flesh, would have been swallowed up, and so they would have been swallowed up alive. For, living in the body, they would have been dead in the soul; and having the life of nature, they would have lost the life of grace and of glory.

paras.t: Quum irasceretur furor eorum in nos, forsitan aquæ tribulationum, id est vehementes persecutiones, absorbuissent nos, id est, prævaluissent contra nos, ita quod mortui fuissemus morte peccati, consentiendo malignis, vel per impatientiam superati. Nisi enim Deus patientiam atque constantiam daret, quis in tantis tribulationibus inconcussus persisteret? Unde Moyses loquitur : Ne dicas in corde tuo, Fortitudo mea et robur manus meæ hæc omnia mihi præstiterunt ; sed recordare Domini Dei tui, quod ipse vires tibi præbuerit. Significatur autem per aquam tribulatio magna, juxta illud : Adducet super eos aquas multas et fortes, regem Assyriorum. Et alibi : Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum ; dixi, Perii.
paras.en: [[123:3|When their fury was enkindled against us|Quum irasceretur furor eorum in nos]], [[123:4|Perhaps the waters|forsitan aquæ]] of tribulations, that is, vehement persecutions, [[123:4|had swallowed us up|absorbuissent nos]]: that is, had prevailed against us, so that we should have died the death of sin, by consenting to the wicked or by being overcome through impatience. For unless God gave patience and constancy, who would stand unshaken in such great tribulations? Hence Moses says: [[Deut 8:17|Lest thou shouldst say in thy heart: My own might, and the strength of my own hand have achieved all these things for me|Ne dicas in corde tuo, Fortitudo mea et robur manus meæ hæc omnia mihi præstiterunt]]; [[Deut 8:18|But remember the Lord thy God, that he hath given thee strength|sed recordare Domini Dei tui, quod ipse vires tibi præbuerit]]. Now by water is signified great tribulation, according to that saying: [[Is 8:7|will bring upon them the waters of the river strong and many, the king of the Assyrians|Adducet super eos aquas multas et fortes, regem Assyriorum]]. And elsewhere: [[Lam 3:54|Waters have flowed over my head: I said: I am cut off|Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum ; dixi, Perii]].

paras.t: Torrentem, id est copiosam et magnam tribulationem et tentationem, pertransivit anima nostra, æquanimiter sustinendo adversa, neque consentiens suggestioni perversæ ; forsitan pertransisset anima nostra aquam intolerabilem : id est, nisi Dominus succurrisset, supra vires gravati atque tentati essemus, et compulsa fuisset anima nostra pertransire, id est pati, aquam intolerabilem, id est persecutionem, cui resistere nullatenus potuisset. Sed fidelis Dominus, qui non est passus nos tentari supra id quod ferre potuimus : imo fecit cum tentatione proventum, dan[…] Nequaquam etenim posset homo invisibilibus hostibus suis resistere, nisi angelus sanctus succurreret, et Deus per se ipsum seu per angelum opem impenderet. Nam de potestate diaboli scriptum est : Non est super terram potestas quæ comparetur ei. Sunt enim incomparabiliter astutiores, agiliores, expertioresque nobis.
paras.en: [[123:5|a torrent|Torrentem]], that is, an abundant and great tribulation and temptation, [[123:5|Our soul hath passed through|pertransivit anima nostra]], bearing adversities with an even mind and not consenting to perverse suggestion; [[123:5|perhaps our soul had passed through a water insupportable|forsitan pertransisset anima nostra aquam intolerabilem]]: that is, had the Lord not come to our aid, we should have been weighed down and tempted above our strength[[2 Cor 1:8||]], and our soul would have been compelled to pass through, that is, to suffer, the insupportable water, that is, a persecution which it could in no way have resisted. But the Lord is faithful, [[1 Cor 10:13|who will not suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able: but will make also with temptation issue|qui non est passus nos tentari supra id quod ferre potuimus : imo fecit cum tentatione proventum]] [Denis has: "who has not suffered us to be tempted above what we could bear, but has made with the temptation an issue"], giving […] [the text breaks off here in the source]. For man could by no means resist his invisible enemies, unless a holy angel came to his aid and God gave help, either by himself or through an angel. For of the power of the devil it is written: [[Job 41:24|There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him|Non est super terram potestas quæ comparetur ei]]. For they [the demons] are incomparably more cunning, more nimble and more experienced than we.

paras.t: Idcirco : Benedictus Dominus, id est, ab omnibus benedicatur, laudetur, et æternaliter benedictus exsistat, qui non dedit nos effective vel permissive in captionem dentibus, id est crudelitati ac malignitati, eorum, id est invisibilium visibiliumque inimicorum : id est, qui non permisit nos capi seu vinci ab hostibus, quantum ad animam, quamvis corporaliter ab eis vincti, afflicti, occisive simus.
paras.en: Therefore: [[123:6|Blessed be the Lord|Benedictus Dominus]], that is, may he be blessed and praised by all, and be blessed eternally, [[123:6|who hath not given us|qui non dedit nos]], effectively or permissively, [[123:6|to be a prey to their teeth|in captionem dentibus]], that is, to the cruelty and malice of them, that is, of our invisible and visible enemies: that is, who has not permitted us to be taken or overcome by our foes as regards the soul, although in the body we be bound, afflicted or slain by them.

paras.t: Anima nostra sicut passer erepta est de laqueo venantium : id est, quemadmodum passer evadit rete sibi extensum, ne capiatur ; sic anima nostra per gratiam Dei erepta est de impugnatione inimicorum suæ salutis, videlicet hominum impiorum ac dæmonum : qui vocantur venantes, quoniam animam insequuntur ut canes, quatenus eam occidant, fallant, vinculo miseræ servitutis ligent, et potestati diaboli subdant. Quod enim non solum dæmon, sed etiam homo malignus dicatur hoc modo venator, liquet ex eo quod scriptum est: Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem. Et de indignis pastoribus ab Osee inducitur : Ad iniquitatem eorum sublevabunt animas eorum. Laqueus vero vocatur, omne quo anima ad peccandum inducitur, vel potestati dæmonis subjecta efficitur. Unde in Osee habetur : Attendite hoc, sacerdotes, quoniam laqueus facti estis speculationi, et sicut rete expansum super montem Thabor. Similiter laqueus diaboli, species meretricis. Et de avaritia ait Apostolus : Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli. Porro, quod omnia vitia dici possint laquei dæmonis, patet per illud Apostoli : Det Deus illis pœnitentiam ad cognoscendum veritatem, et resipiscant a diaboli laqueis, a quo captivi tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem. Laqueus ergo venantium est omnis tentatio, omnis carnis voluptas, omnis inordinata lætitia.
paras.en: [[123:7|Our soul hath been delivered as a sparrow out of the snare of the fowlers|Anima nostra sicut passer erepta est de laqueo venantium]]: that is, as a sparrow escapes the net stretched out for it, so as not to be caught, so our soul by the grace of God has been delivered from the assault of the enemies of its salvation, namely wicked men and demons. These are called fowlers [Latin *venantes*, hunters in general, hence the dogs that follow], because they pursue the soul like dogs, to slay it, deceive it, bind it with the chain of wretched servitude and subject it to the power of the devil. For that not only the demon but also a wicked man is called a hunter in this way is clear from what is written: [[Mich 7:2|every one hunteth his brother to death|Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem]]. And of unworthy pastors it is said by Osee: [[Osee 4:8|shall lift up their souls to their iniquity|Ad iniquitatem eorum sublevabunt animas eorum]]. And a snare is the name for everything by which the soul is led into sin or is made subject to the power of the demon. Hence it is said in Osee: [[Osee 5:1|Hear ye this, O priests|Attendite hoc, sacerdotes]], [[Osee 5:1|because you have been a snare to them whom you should have watched over and a net spread upon Thabor|quoniam laqueus facti estis speculationi, et sicut rete expansum super montem Thabor]]. Likewise the beauty of a harlot is a snare of the devil. And of avarice the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 6:9|they that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli]]. Further, that all vices can be called snares of the demon is plain from that saying of the Apostle: [[2 Tim 2:25|God may give them repentance to know the truth|Det Deus illis pœnitentiam ad cognoscendum veritatem]], [[2 Tim 2:26|And they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil by whom they are held captive at his will.|et resipiscant a diaboli laqueis, a quo captivi tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem.]] The snare of the fowlers, then, is every temptation, every pleasure of the flesh, every inordinate gladness.

paras.t: Laqueus contritus est, id est, dæmon superatus est, peccato consensus negatus est, adversitas nocere non potuit, et nos liberati sumus a laqueis præinductis. Istud in hac vita perfecte cantare non possumus, quoniam tentatio durat usque ad finem, imo interdum in fine vitæ durius instat. Quando ergo cantabimus istud perfecte? nisi in vita futura, quando dicemus mente jucunda illud Apostoli : Ubi est, mors, victoria tua? ubi est, mors, stimulus tuus? Possumus tamen istud in hac vita aliquo modo cantare, quando videlicet tentationi alicui prævalemus, aut quæcumque adversa Deo auxiliante evadimus. Nam et Apostolus dicit : Deo gratias qui dedit nobis victoriam per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum. Et de contritione diaboli ejusque laqueis ait : Dominus conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter.
paras.en: [[123:7|The snare is broken|Laqueus contritus est]]: that is, the demon has been overcome, consent to sin has been refused, adversity could do no harm; [[123:7|and we are delivered|et nos liberati sumus]] from the snares laid before us. This we cannot sing perfectly in this life, since temptation lasts until the end, and indeed sometimes presses harder at the end of life. When, then, shall we sing it perfectly, if not in the life to come, when with joyful mind we shall say that word of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 15:55|O death, where is thy victory? O death, where is thy sting?|Ubi est, mors, victoria tua? ubi est, mors, stimulus tuus]] Yet we can sing it in some manner in this life, namely when we prevail over some temptation, or escape any adversities with God's help. For the Apostle too says: [[1 Cor 15:57|thanks be to God, who hath given us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ|Deo gratias qui dedit nobis victoriam per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]]. And of the crushing of the devil and his snares he says: The Lord shall [[Rom 16:20|crush Satan under your feet speedily|conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter]].

paras.t: Adjutorium nostrum consistit in nomine Domini, id est in potestate Creatoris, non in viribus nostris, quoniam scriptum est : Domine, omnia opera nostra operatus es nobis, et tantum in te recordemur nominis tui. In Domino itaque situm est adjutorium nostrum, qui fecit cœlum et terram.
paras.en: [[123:8|Our help|Adjutorium nostrum]] consists [[123:8|in the name of the Lord|in nomine Domini]], that is, in the power of the Creator, not in our own strength; for it is written: [[Is 26:12|Lord|Domine]], [[Is 26:12|thou hast wrought all our works for us|omnia opera nostra operatus es nobis]]; and [[Is 26:13|only in thee let us remember thy name|tantum in te recordemur nominis tui]]. In the Lord, then, our help is placed, [[123:8|who made heaven and earth|qui fecit cœlum et terram]].

paras.t: Docet nos psalmus præsens omnem triumphum, profectum et gratiam Deo cum vera humilitate adscribere, divina beneficia devote recolere, atque de eis Domino gratias immolare.
paras.en: The present psalm teaches us to ascribe every triumph, every progress and every grace to God with true humility, to call to mind the divine benefits devoutly, and to offer the Lord thanks for them.

paras.t: Postremo, secundum Hugonem, dæmones invadunt homines per suggestionem, tangunt per malam cogitationem, mordent per pravam delectationem, masticant per deliberationem, transglutiunt per consensum, trajiciunt in stomachum per operationem, decoquunt per consuetudinem, et egerunt in mortem per damnationem. His autem gradibus descenditur in infernum.
paras.en: Lastly, according to Hugh, the demons attack men by suggestion, touch them by evil thought, bite them by depraved delight, chew them by deliberation, swallow them down by consent, pass them into the stomach by the deed, digest them by habit, and void them into death by damnation. And by these steps one goes down into hell.

paras.t: Precatio. Torrentem vitiorum, Domine, fac animam nostram pertransire : ut tua fortitudine laqueo diabolicæ fraudis contrito, tuo in perpetuum liberemur adjutorio.
paras.en: Prayer. Make our soul, O Lord, pass through the torrent of vices: that, the snare of the devil's fraud being broken by thy strength, we may be delivered for ever by thy help.

124.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI QUARTI : QUI CONFIDUNT IN DOMINO.
124.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and twenty-fourth psalm: They that trust in the Lord.

paras.t: Est autem titulus psalmi nunc declarandi : Canticum graduum. Est enim hic psalmus inter psalmos graduales sextus, agitque de sexto spiritualis ascensionis gradu, qui est immobilis quædam in Deo fiducia, ex præteritis beneficiis roborata. Quanto enim quis frequentius pietatem et gratiam Dei circa se experitur, tanto ejus fiducia in Deo certius stabilitur, et ita ex perceptione præsentium munerum certa fit exspectatio futurorum.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is: [[124:1|A gradual canticle|Canticum graduum]]. For this psalm is the sixth among the gradual psalms, and it treats of the sixth step of the spiritual ascent, which is an immovable trust in God, strengthened by past benefits. For the more often a man experiences God's kindness and grace towards him, the more surely his trust in God is established; and so from receiving present gifts comes a sure expectation of those to come.

paras.t: Ait itaque sanctus Propheta : Qui confidunt in Domino, non in rebus creatis, caducis et vanis, tales erunt et sunt sicut mons Sion : sive per montem Sion intelligatur mons ille terrenus, in quo templum Salomonis erat constructum, sive homo speculativus, qui alios per gratiam contemplationis transcendit. Nam, sicut mons ille terrenus erat immobilis, vel quia nullo modo, vel quia difficulter mobilis erat ; sic confidentes in Domino, aut nullo modo, aut difficulter moventur a rectitudine fidei atque justitia vitæ. Iterum, sicut vir contemplativus, qui est mons speculationis, in Domino stabilitur per gratiam ; sic qui confidunt in Domino, in eo roborantur per spei certissimam longanimitatem. Unde ait Scriptura : Qui sperant in Domino, mutabunt fortitudinem, assument pennas ut aquilæ, ambulabunt et non deficient. Et iterum : Turris fortissima nomen Domini ; ad ipsum currit justus, et salvabitur.
paras.en: So the holy Prophet says: [[124:1|They that trust in the Lord|Qui confidunt in Domino]], not in created things, perishable and vain, such men will be, and are, [[124:1|as mount Sion|sicut mons Sion]]: whether by mount Sion we understand that earthly mountain on which Solomon's temple was built, or the speculative man, who rises above others by the grace of contemplation. For as that earthly mountain was immovable, either because it could not be moved at all or because it could be moved only with difficulty, so those who trust in the Lord are moved not at all, or only with difficulty, from the rightness of faith and the justice of life. Again, as the contemplative man, who is a mountain of speculation, is established in the Lord by grace, so they that trust in the Lord are strengthened in him by the most certain long-suffering of hope. Hence the Scripture says: [[Is 40:31|they that hope in the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall take wings as eagles|Qui sperant in Domino, mutabunt fortitudinem, assument pennas ut aquilæ]], [[Is 40:31|they shall walk and not faint|ambulabunt et non deficient]] [the margin gives Is. vi, 31, a misreading of Is. xl, 31]. And again: [[Prov 18:10|The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the just runneth to it|Turris fortissima nomen Domini ; ad ipsum currit justus]], and shall be saved [Denis reads *salvabitur*, "shall be saved", where the Vulgate has *exaltabitur*, "shall be exalted"].

paras.t: Non movebitur in æternum qui habitat in Jerusalem. Jerusalem illa terrena, quæ erat civitas in Judæa, sæpe mota atque destructa est. Bis enim totaliter est destructa, videlicet semel a rege Babylonis, et semel a Tito principe Romanorum. Frequenter quoque partim destructa est ; sed et habitatores ipsius sæpe vastati sunt. Non ergo de illa Jerusalem loquitur jam Propheta, sed de cœlesti Jerusalem, cujus habitatores confirmati sunt in bono et statu beato, ita ut amplius nequeant commoveri. Potest quoque exponi de militanti Ecclesia, quæ per Jerusalem designatur, ut sit sensus : Non movebitur in æternum a fide catholica, a vita fideli, a gratia, quamdiu in præsenti sæculo degit, qui habitat in Jerusalem, id est in militanti Ecclesia, per fidem caritate et gratia adornatam. Non quod talis nunquam possit peccare, vel quod omnis in Ecclesia taliter habitans, sit electus, æternaliterque servandus ; sed hoc dicitur ad insinuandum quid conveniat habitatori ac filio Ecclesiæ, seu homini justo, in quantum hujusmodi. Quamdiu enim manet membrum et filius Ecclesiæ, a Christo defenditur ; sed non confirmatur in bono de lege communi, nisi hujus viæ cursu finito, vel potius in termino ejus. Nihilo minus ex gratia speciali aliqui Sancti ausi fuerunt asserere, in hac vita se nunquam movendos a statu salutis, quemadmodum sanctus Job ait : Donec deficiam, non recedam ab innocentia mea ; et Paulus : Certus sum quod neque mors, neque vita, neque angeli, neque principatus, neque creatura aliqua poterit nos separare a caritate Dei.
paras.en: [[124:1|he shall not be moved for ever that dwelleth|Non movebitur in æternum qui habitat]] [[124:2|In Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]]. That earthly Jerusalem, which was a city in Judea, was often shaken and destroyed. For it was twice destroyed entirely: once by the king of Babylon[[4 Kings 25:9||]][[4 Kings 25:10||]], and once by Titus, the Roman commander. Often too it was partly destroyed, and its inhabitants were often laid waste. So the Prophet is not speaking here of that Jerusalem, but of the heavenly Jerusalem, whose inhabitants are confirmed in good and in the state of bliss, so that they can no longer be moved. It can also be explained of the Church militant, which is signified by Jerusalem, so that the sense is: [[124:1|he shall not be moved for ever|Non movebitur in æternum]] from the catholic faith, from a faithful life, from grace, as long as he lives in the present world, [[124:1|that dwelleth|qui habitat]] [[124:2|In Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]], that is, in the Church militant, by faith adorned with charity and grace. Not that such a man can never sin, or that everyone who dwells thus in the Church is elect and to be saved for ever; but this is said to suggest what befits a dweller in the Church and a son of the Church, or a just man, as such. For as long as he remains a member and a son of the Church, he is defended by Christ; but by the common law he is not confirmed in good until the course of this way is finished, or rather at its end. Nevertheless, by a special grace some Saints have dared to assert that in this life they would never be moved from the state of salvation, as holy Job says: [[Job 27:5|till I die I will not depart from my innocence|Donec deficiam, non recedam ab innocentia mea]]; and Paul: [[Rom 8:38|I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities|Certus sum quod neque mors, neque vita, neque angeli, neque principatus]], [[Rom 8:39|nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God|neque creatura aliqua poterit nos separare a caritate Dei]].

paras.t: Hujus vero stabilitatis causa subjungitur. Montes in circuitu ejus : id est, Beati in patria, scilicet angeli sancti et homines jam salvati, sunt in circuitu ejus, id est in gyro cœlestis Jerusalem, ideo civitas illa turbari non potest. Vel sic : Montes, id est angeli Dei, qui propter naturæ et gratiæ excellentiam montes vocantur, sunt in circuitu ejus, id est militantis Ecclesiæ, tanquam ad custodiam hominum ordinati ac missi. Sed ne quis hoc sufficere putet, vel in illis finaliter speret, adjungitur : et Dominus in circuitu populi sui : quemadmodum in Evangelio ait, Non relinquam vos orphanos ; et, Ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi. Propterea sequitur : ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum. Superius dictum est Domino, Synagoga populorum circumdabit te : quod illic expositum est ; nunc dicitur, Dominus in circuitu populi sui : quod magis proprie dicitur quam illud. Proprie namque nihil esse potest in circuitu immensi et incircumscriptibilis Dei ; sed Deus æternus ac infinitus, universa includit, omnia continet, ambit, conservat, suosque electos gratiose defendit.
paras.en: Then the cause of this stability is added: [[124:2|Mountains are round about it|Montes in circuitu ejus]]: that is, the Blessed in the fatherland, namely the holy angels and the men already saved, are round about it, that is, in the circuit of the heavenly Jerusalem; and therefore that city cannot be disturbed. Or thus: Mountains, that is, the angels of God, who are called mountains for the excellence of their nature and grace, are round about it, that is, round the Church militant, as appointed and sent to guard men. But lest anyone think this enough, or put his final hope in them, there is added: [[124:2|so the Lord is round about his people|et Dominus in circuitu populi sui]]: as he says in the Gospel, [[John 14:18|I will not leave you orphans|Non relinquam vos orphanos]]; and, [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]]. Therefore there follows: [[124:2|from henceforth now and for ever|ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum]]. Earlier it was said to the Lord, [[Ps 7:8|a congregation of people shall surround thee|Synagoga populorum circumdabit te]], which was explained there; now it is said, [[124:2|the Lord is round about his people|Dominus in circuitu populi sui]], which is said more properly than that. For properly nothing can be round about the immense God, whom nothing can circumscribe; but God, eternal and infinite, encloses all things, contains, encompasses and preserves them all, and graciously defends his elect.

paras.t: Quia non relinquet Dominus finaliter virgam peccatorum, id est potestatem, persecutionem, tyrannidem reproborum, super sortem, id est partem, justorum, seu super justos, qui sunt portio atque hereditas Dei : et hoc ideo, ut non extendant justi ad iniquitatem manus suas, id est, ne ipsi superentur et peccent. Quamvis Deus ad tempus relinquat electos a perversis affligi, ut purgentur et gloriam mereantur, non tamen relinquit eos finaliter, sed salvat æternaliter. Denique dum videt eos supra vires tentari ac tribulari, et casui appropinquare, mox subvenit, et cum tentatione dispensat, ne justi iniquitatem incurrant.
paras.en: [[124:3|For the Lord will not leave|Quia non relinquet Dominus]] finally [[124:3|the rod of sinners|virgam peccatorum]], that is, the power, the persecution, the tyranny of the reprobate, [[124:3|upon the lot|super sortem]], that is, the portion, [[124:3|of the just|justorum]], or upon the just, who are the portion and inheritance of God[[Ps 15:5||]][[Ps 15:6||]]; and this [[124:3|that the just may not stretch forth their hands to iniquity|ut non extendant justi ad iniquitatem manus suas]], that is, lest they be overcome and sin. Though God for a time leaves his elect to be afflicted by the wicked, that they may be purified and merit glory, yet he does not leave them finally, but saves them eternally. Indeed, when he sees them tempted and troubled beyond their strength and drawing near to a fall, he soon comes to their help, and with the temptation makes provision, lest the just fall into iniquity.

paras.t: Benefac, Domine, bonis in opere, et rectis corde, id est intentione, dando eis gratiæ incrementa in via, et beatitudinis largitatem in patria. Recti corde sunt, quorum affectio Deo atque justitiæ consonat, quorum oculus simplex est, quorum intentio tendit in Deum.
paras.en: [[124:4|Do good, O Lord, to those that are good|Benefac, Domine, bonis]] in work, [[124:4|and to the upright of heart|et rectis corde]], that is, in intention, by giving them increase of grace on the way, and the bounty of bliss in the fatherland. The upright of heart are those whose affection accords with God and with justice, whose eye is single[[Matt 6:22||]], whose intention tends towards God.

paras.t: Declinantes autem a bono et via justa in obligationes, id est ad peccata, hominem ad pœnam obligantia, adducet Dominus in die judicii ad sinistram, et postea vel etiam ante, in infernum, cum operantibus iniquitatem, id est cum dæmonibus, quorum superbia ascendit semper, qui a principio peccant, qui quum cecidissent, non adjecerunt ut resurgerent, sed in malo obstinati manserunt. Hoc est quod apud Evangelistam inducitur : Tunc dicet rex his qui a sinistris erunt : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum, qui paratus est diabolo et angelis ejus. Et Dominus alio loco ait injustis : Cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem super caput vestrum. Et scriptum est : Ecce dies veniet succensa quasi ignis ; et erunt omnes superbi et omnes facientes impietatem, stipula, et inflammabit eos dies veniens. Pax vera sit super Israel, id est populum fidelem, quemadmodum angeli cecinerunt : Gloria in altissimis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis. Et Christus ait : Pacem relinquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis. Quam utique pacem optavit Isaias, dicens : Domine, dabis pacem nobis.
paras.en: [[124:5|But such as turn aside|Declinantes autem]] from good and from the just way [[124:5|into bonds|in obligationes]], that is, into sins, which bind a man to punishment [*obligationes*: things that bind, obligations], [[124:5|the Lord shall lead out|adducet Dominus]] on the day of judgment to the left hand, and afterwards, or even before, into hell, [[124:5|with the workers of iniquity|cum operantibus iniquitatem]], that is, with the demons, whose pride [[Ps 73:23|ascendeth continually|ascendit semper]], who sin from the beginning[[1 John 3:8||]], who, when they had fallen, did not rise again[[Ps 40:9||]], but remained obstinate in evil. This is what is set down in the Evangelist: [[Matt 25:41|Then he shall say|Tunc dicet]] the King to them [[Matt 25:41|that shall be on his left hand|qui a sinistris erunt]]: [[Matt 25:41|Depart|Ite]], [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels|maledicti, in ignem æternum, qui paratus est diabolo et angelis ejus]]. And the Lord says in another place to the unjust: [[Joel 3:4|I will very soon return you a recompense upon your own head|Cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem super caput vestrum]]. And it is written: [[Mal 4:1|behold the day shall come kindled as a furnace: and all the proud, and all that do wickedly shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall set them on fire|Ecce dies veniet succensa quasi ignis ; et erunt omnes superbi et omnes facientes impietatem, stipula, et inflammabit eos dies veniens]] [Denis reads *quasi ignis*, "as fire", where the Vulgate has *quasi caminus*, "as a furnace"]. Let true [[124:5|peace|Pax]] be [[124:5|upon Israel|super Israel]], that is, upon the faithful people, as the angels sang: [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest: and on earth peace to men of good will.|Gloria in altissimis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis.]] And Christ says: [[John 14:27|Peace I leave with you: my peace I give unto you|Pacem relinquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis]]. This is the peace that Isaias longed for, saying: [[Is 26:12|Lord, thou wilt give us peace|Domine, dabis pacem nobis]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum compendiosum et vere fructuosissimum, lætum et nimis sententiosum audivimus : in cujus exordio edocemur quam beatum sit in Deo confidere. Unde et Jeremias testatur : Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino ; et Salomon, Habe, inquit, fiduciam in Domino toto corde tuo, et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ. Docet quoque nos psalmus iste, quam potentes sint defensores Ecclesiæ, scilicet angeli, montes vocati, qui in circuitu Christianorum sunt discurrentes, velut apes negotiosæ, ut nostræ saluti provideant, dæmones coercendo, bona suggerendo, nostro profectui congaudendo, pro nobis orando, gratiam reportando. Unde Dominus per Isaiam contestatur : Super muros tuos, Jerusalem, constitui custodes ; tota die et tota nocte in perpetuum non tacebunt. Promittit insuper nobis hic psalmus, quod Dominus non relinquet virgam impiorum super sortem justorum, quatenus in omni afflictione hujusmodi confidamus nos tandem divinitus eruendos, interimque patientiam veram servemus : quia qui perseveraverit usque in finem, salvus erit, sicut Salvator disseruit.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm that is brief and truly most fruitful, joyful and full of meaning: at its beginning we are taught how blessed it is to trust in God. Hence Jeremias too bears witness: [[Jer 17:7|Blessed be the man that trusteth in the Lord|Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino]]; and Solomon: [[Prov 3:5|Have|Habe]], he says, [[Prov 3:5|confidence in the Lord with all thy heart, and lean not upon thy own prudence|fiduciam in Domino toto corde tuo, et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ]]. This psalm also teaches us how mighty are the defenders of the Church, namely the angels, called mountains, who are round about Christians, hurrying to and fro like busy bees to provide for our salvation: restraining the demons, suggesting good things, rejoicing in our progress, praying for us, bringing back grace. Hence the Lord declares through Isaias: [[Is 62:6|Upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen all the day, and all the night, they shall never hold their peace|Super muros tuos, Jerusalem, constitui custodes ; tota die et tota nocte in perpetuum non tacebunt]]. Moreover, this psalm promises us that the Lord [[124:3|will not leave the rod|non relinquet virgam]] of the ungodly [[124:3|upon the lot of the just|super sortem justorum]], so that in every such affliction we may trust that we shall at last be delivered by God, and meanwhile keep true patience: for [[Matt 10:22|he that shall persevere unto the end|qui perseveraverit usque in finem]], [[Matt 10:22|he shall be saved|salvus erit]], as the Saviour taught.

paras.t: Precatio. Mons, Christe, fortitudinis, tuis nos (quæsumus) ubique tuere præsidiis, esto in circuitu populi tui, et non derelinquas virgam peccatorum dominari super sortem famulantium tibi ; bene fac nobis, et indulge tempora prosperitatis et pacis.
paras.en: Prayer. O Christ, Mountain of strength, protect us everywhere (we beseech thee) with thy defences; be round about thy people, and do not let the rod of sinners rule over the lot of those who serve thee; do good to us, and grant us times of prosperity and peace.
