125.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS AC MYSTICA IN PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI QUINTI : IN CONVERTENDO DOMINUS.
125.title_en: Literal and mystical exposition of the hundred and twenty-fifth psalm: When the Lord brought back.

paras.t: Hujus quoque psalmi titulus est : Canticum graduum : quoniam psalmus iste spiritualiter explanatus, tractat de septimo gradu spiritualis ascensionis ad Deum : qui gradus consistit in exsultatione et gratiarum actione de spirituali liberatione a vinculis peccatorum et servitute diaboli. Verumtamen, sicut ex littera patere potest, psalmus iste ad litteram scriptus est de reditu Judæorum a captivitate Babylonis, in qua septuaginta annis fuerunt, quemadmodum Jeremias prædixit. Et est psalmus præsens gratiarum actio, et gaudium de liberatione captivitatis tam longæ. Breviter ergo tangenda est expositio litteralis.
paras.en: The title of this psalm also is: [[125:1|A gradual canticle|Canticum graduum]]; for this psalm, explained spiritually, treats of the seventh step of the spiritual ascent to God: and this step consists in exultation and thanksgiving for spiritual deliverance from the bonds of sins and from the servitude of the devil. Yet, as can be seen from the letter, this psalm was written in its literal sense of the return of the Jews from the captivity of Babylon, in which they were for seventy years, as Jeremias foretold[[Jer 25:11||]]. And the present psalm is a thanksgiving, and a rejoicing over deliverance from so long a captivity. The literal exposition, then, is to be touched on briefly.

paras.t: Unde Propheta loquens in persona populi, de captivitate hac redeuntis, ait: In convertendo Dominus captivitatem Sion : id est, dum Dominus converteret captivitatem populi Judæorum, reducendo eos de Babylone in Judæam ; facti sumus nos inde redeuntes, sicut consolati de beneficio liberationis. Sicut, hoc loco significat non solum similitudinem, sed veritatem, quoniam multum gaudebant quod revertebantur ad locum cultus divini, ut patet in libro Esdræ. Per Sion autem significatur populus Judæorum, quoniam Sion mons erat in Jerusalem, in quo situm erat templum et regis palatium.
paras.en: Hence the Prophet, speaking in the person of the people returning from this captivity, says: [[125:1|When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion|In convertendo Dominus captivitatem Sion]]: that is, when the Lord turned back the captivity of the people of the Jews, leading them back from Babylon into Judæa, [[125:1|we became|facti sumus]], we who were returning from there, [[125:1|like men comforted|sicut consolati]] by the benefit of deliverance. *Like* [Latin *sicut*, which can mean "as" in the sense of "truly as"] here signifies not only likeness but reality, since they rejoiced greatly that they were returning to the place of divine worship, as is clear in the book of Esdras[[1 Esd 3:11||]] [the margin gives 1 Esd. iii, 11–13]. By Sion is signified the people of the Jews, since Sion was a mountain in Jerusalem on which the temple and the king's palace stood.

paras.t: Tunc repletum est gaudio os nostrum, et lingua nostra exsultatione, id est, laudes divinas læto ore et animo cantabamus, Domino gratias referendo. Tunc dicent inter gentes, id est, subjecti imperio Cyri tunc dixerunt : Magnificavit Dominus facere cum eis, id est, Deus Israel magnifice fecit cum populo suo : quia Cyrus rex Persarum in universo suo regno publicavit edictum, quod Judæi libere possent reverti ad terram patrum suorum. Quo audito, gentes miratæ sunt atque dixerunt, quod Dominus magnificavit facere cum populo suo, præsertim quoniam Cyrus in sua epistola ita scripsit: Omnia regna terræ dedit mihi Deus cœli, et ipse præcepit mihi ut ædificarem ei domum in Jerusalem. Propter quod etiam quidam gentilium convertebantur ad Judaismum.
paras.en: [[125:2|Then was our mouth filled with gladness; and our tongue with joy|Tunc repletum est gaudio os nostrum, et lingua nostra exsultatione]]: that is, we sang the divine praises with glad mouth and heart, giving thanks to the Lord. [[125:2|Then shall they say among the Gentiles|Tunc dicent inter gentes]]: that is, those subject to the rule of Cyrus then said: [[125:2|The Lord hath done great things for them|Magnificavit Dominus facere cum eis]]; that is, the God of Israel has dealt magnificently with his people: for Cyrus king of the Persians published an edict throughout all his kingdom, that the Jews might freely return to the land of their fathers[[1 Esd 1:1||]]. Hearing this, the Gentiles marvelled and said that the Lord had done great things for his people, especially since Cyrus wrote thus in his letter: [[1 Esd 1:2|The Lord the God of heaven hath given to me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he hath charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem|Omnia regna terræ dedit mihi Deus cœli, et ipse præcepit mihi ut ædificarem ei domum in Jerusalem]]. For this reason, too, some of the Gentiles were converted to Judaism.

paras.t: Hinc Propheta in persona Judæorum adjecit: Magnificavit Dominus facere nobiscum, id est, multum gratiose, pie, atque potenter fecit nobiscum. Unde Esdras dicebat: Benedictus Dominus qui dedit hoc in corde regis. Facti sumus lætantes in Domino de beneficiis tantis.
paras.en: Hence the Prophet added, in the person of the Jews: [[125:3|The Lord hath done great things for us|Magnificavit Dominus facere nobiscum]]: that is, he has dealt with us most graciously, lovingly and mightily. Whence Esdras said: [[1 Esd 7:27|Blessed be the Lord|Benedictus Dominus]] [[1 Esd 7:27|who hath put this in the king's heart|qui dedit hoc in corde regis]]. [[125:3|We are become joyful|Facti sumus lætantes]] in the Lord over such great benefits.

paras.t: Sed quoniam temporibus Esdræ in principio hujus reversionis populus modicus erat, et nec civitas nec templum fuerant reparata, idcirco pro conversione perfecta captivitatis prædictæ orans Propheta, adjungit: Converte, Domine, captivitatem nostram, sicut torrens in Austro convertitur : id est, quemadmodum torrens siccatus rursus impletur flante vento australi, qui pluviam causat, et ita torrentes siccatos facit aquosos ; sic populum tuum numero minoratum auge et repara, civitatesque Judæ et templum restaura.
paras.en: But since in the times of Esdras, at the beginning of this return, the people were few, and neither the city nor the temple had been rebuilt, the Prophet therefore, praying for the complete turning back of the said captivity, adds: [[125:4|Turn again our captivity, O Lord, as a stream in the south|Converte, Domine, captivitatem nostram, sicut torrens in Austro]] is turned: that is, as a dried-up stream is filled again when the south wind blows, which brings rain and so makes the dried-up streams full of water, so do thou increase and restore thy people, diminished in number, and rebuild the cities of Juda and the temple.

paras.t: Et decet sic fieri, quoniam Qui seminant in lacrimis, id est, qui opera pœnitentiæ faciunt, lacrimasque compunctionis ac devotionis effundunt pro præteritorum malorum indulgentia et futurorum bonorum gratia impetranda, in exsultatione metent, id est, jucunde impetrabunt quod postulant, præmiumque gloriosum recipient, juxta illud : Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur.
paras.en: And it is fitting that it be so, since [[125:5|They that sow in tears|Qui seminant in lacrimis]], that is, those who do works of penance and shed tears of compunction and devotion to obtain pardon for past evils and the grace of good things to come, [[125:5|shall reap in joy|in exsultatione metent]]: that is, they shall joyfully obtain what they ask, and receive a glorious reward, according to that saying: [[Matt 5:5|Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted|Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur]].

paras.t: Sic autem Judæi fecerunt, nam Euntes a Jerusalem et Judæa in Babylonem, ibant et flebant ex compunctione atque tristitia, quod locum divini cultus relinquere et terram idololatriæ deditam ingredi cogebantur, mittentes semina sua, id est, opera bona agentes, ex quibus tempore apto fructum consolationis et gratiæ sortirentur. Venientes autem de Babylone ad Judæam, venient cum exsultatione, portantes manipulos suos, id est fructum seminis jam prædicti.
paras.en: And so the Jews did; for [[125:6|Going|Euntes]] from Jerusalem and Judæa into Babylon, [[125:6|they went and wept|ibant et flebant]] out of compunction and sorrow, because they were forced to leave the place of divine worship and to enter a land given over to idolatry, [[125:6|casting their seeds|mittentes semina sua]]: that is, doing good works, from which in due time they would obtain the fruit of consolation and grace. [[125:7|But coming|Venientes autem]] from Babylon to Judæa, [[125:7|they shall come with joyfulness, carrying their sheaves|venient cum exsultatione, portantes manipulos suos]], that is, the fruit of the seed already mentioned.

paras.t: Mystice insuper explanatur hic psalmus de Ecclesia, seu unoquoque fideli, a vitiis seu spiritualis Babylone, id est scelerum confusione, erepto. Eritque sensus: In convertendo Dominus captivitatem Sion : id est, quum Ecclesiam militantem, seu quemlibet fidelem converteret a vita confusa, a peccato mortali, a præsenti miseria, ad vitam ordinatam, ad gratiæ statum, ad gloriæ locum; facti sumus sicut consolati. De hac enim conversione vehementissime gloriandum est omni Christiano. Propter quod ait Apostolus: Multa mihi fiducia est apud vos, multa mihi gloriatio pro vobis ; repletus sum consolatione, superabundo gaudio in omni tribulatione nostra. Præcipue vero gaudendum est prælatis, dum eorum subditi convertuntur ad meliora, exemplo B. Joannis, qui in sua Canonica profitetur : Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare.
paras.en: Mystically, moreover, this psalm is explained of the Church, or of each of the faithful, rescued from vices, or from the spiritual Babylon, that is, the confusion of sins [Babylon is taken to mean "confusion"]. And the sense will be: [[125:1|When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion|In convertendo Dominus captivitatem Sion]]: that is, when he turned the Church militant, or any one of the faithful, from a disordered life, from mortal sin, from present misery, to an ordered life, to the state of grace, to the place of glory, [[125:1|we became like men comforted|facti sumus sicut consolati]]. For every Christian ought to glory most vehemently in this turning back. Hence the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 7:4|Great is my confidence for you: great is my glorying for you. I am filled with comfort: I exceedingly abound with joy in all our tribulation|Multa mihi fiducia est apud vos, multa mihi gloriatio pro vobis ; repletus sum consolatione, superabundo gaudio in omni tribulatione nostra]]. And prelates especially ought to rejoice when those subject to them are turned to better things, after the example of blessed John, who professes in his Canonical Epistle: [[3 John 1:4|I have no greater grace than this, to hear that my children walk in truth|Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare]].

paras.t: Tunc, id est in conversione hujus spiritualis captivitatis atque internæ consolationis, repletum est gaudio spirituali et laude jucunda os nostrum mentale et corporale. Est enim os spirituale, intellectuale sive mentale, quo verbum cordis profertur, quo angeli colloquuntur. De quo Sapientia dicit : Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam. Hoc os impletur gaudio Spiritus Sancti, ex consideratione gratiæ beneficiorumque Dei. Et lingua nostra impleta est exsultatione, id est laude vocali et jubilo exuberanti. Ex abundantia enim cordis loquitur lingua. Similiter plenitudo interioris lætitiæ redundat atque apparet in ore et lingua corporis. Tunc dicent inter gentes : Magnificavit Dominus facere cum eis : id est, quidam sæcularium hominum, seu quicumque alii populi, videntes gratiam Dei nobis collatam, mirabuntur et dicent : Magnifice fecit Deus cum eis. Frequenter enim homines mundum amantes, laudant in aliis quod imitari non volunt; videntesque quosdam converti ad Christum, ingredi claustrum, subito immutari, mirantur, et Deum in suis effectibus laudant, nec tamen eamdem gratiam sibi elargiri precantur.
paras.en: [[125:2|Then|Tunc]], that is, in the turning back of this spiritual captivity and of inward consolation, [[125:2|was our mouth|os nostrum]], both of the mind and of the body, [[125:2|filled with gladness|repletum est gaudio]], spiritual gladness and joyful praise. For there is a spiritual mouth, intellectual or mental, by which the word of the heart is uttered, by which the angels speak with one another. Of this Wisdom says: [[Ecclus 24:5|I came out of the mouth of the most High, the firstborn before all creatures|Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam]]. This mouth is filled with the joy of the Holy Ghost from considering the grace and the benefits of God. [[125:2|And our tongue|Et lingua nostra]] is filled [[125:2|with joy|exsultatione]], that is, with spoken praise and overflowing jubilation. [[Matt 12:34|For out of the abundance of the heart|Ex abundantia enim cordis]] the tongue speaketh [Denis has *lingua*, "tongue", where the Gospel has *os*, "mouth"]. In like manner the fullness of inward gladness overflows and shows itself in the mouth and tongue of the body. [[125:2|Then shall they say among the Gentiles|Tunc dicent inter gentes]]: [[125:2|The Lord hath done great things for them|Magnificavit Dominus facere cum eis]]: that is, some worldly men, or any other peoples, seeing the grace of God bestowed on us, will marvel and say: God has dealt magnificently with them. For men who love the world often praise in others what they will not imitate; and seeing some converted to Christ, entering the cloister, suddenly changed, they marvel and praise God in his works, yet do not pray that the same grace be granted to themselves.

paras.t: Magnificavit Dominus facere nobiscum. Hoc est quod ait dignissima Virgo : Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est. Magnificavit enim Dominus Christus facere nobiscum, nostram naturam assumendo, nostram captivitatem primam ac generalem convertendo, pro originali peccato satisfaciendo, inter homines conversando, nos sibi per gratiam uniendo, ex nobis Ecclesiam congregando, corpus suum et sanguinem nobis tradendo, Spiritum Sanctum mittendo, et innumerabilia beneficia conferendo : idcirco facti sumus lætantes, et gratias referentes, atque hilariter ministrantes. Hinc enim Judith misericordiam Dei experta, ait : Laudate Dominum Deum nostrum, qui non deseruit sperantes in se, et in me adimplevit misericordiam suam.
paras.en: [[125:3|The Lord hath done great things for us|Magnificavit Dominus facere nobiscum]]. This is what the most worthy Virgin says: [[Luke 1:49|Because he that is mighty hath done great things to me|Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est]]. For the Lord Christ has done great things for us: by taking our nature, by turning back our first and general captivity, by making satisfaction for original sin, by dwelling among men[[Bar 3:38||]], by uniting us to himself through grace, by gathering the Church out of us, by giving us his body and blood, by sending the Holy Ghost, and by bestowing innumerable benefits. Therefore [[125:3|we are become joyful|facti sumus lætantes]], and give thanks, and serve him gladly. Hence Judith, having experienced the mercy of God, says: [[Jdt 13:17|Praise ye the Lord our God, who hath not forsaken them that hope in him|Laudate Dominum Deum nostrum, qui non deseruit sperantes in se]], [[Jdt 13:18|And by me|et in me]] [[Jdt 13:18|he hath fulfilled his mercy|adimplevit misericordiam suam]].

paras.t: Converte, Domine, captivitatem nostram perfecte : id est, nos propter originale peccatum infectos vulneribus animæ, erue ab omni corruptione peccati, in libertatem filiorum Dei; et peccata quibus quotidie ligamur et capimur, aufer a nobis; sicut torrens in Austro convertitur, quatenus sic impleamur donis et gratiis Spiritus Sancti, sicut torrens siccatus impletur humoribus aquæ Austro flante.
paras.en: [[125:4|Turn again our captivity, O Lord|Converte, Domine, captivitatem nostram]] perfectly: that is, rescue us, who because of original sin are infected with wounds of the soul, from all corruption of sin, [[Rom 8:21|into the liberty|in libertatem]] [[Rom 8:21|of the children of God|filiorum Dei]]; and take away from us the sins by which we are daily bound and taken captive, [[125:4|as a stream in the south|sicut torrens in Austro]] is turned, so that we may be filled with the gifts and graces of the Holy Ghost as a dried-up stream is filled with waters when the south wind blows.

paras.t: Qui seminant in lacrimis, id est, qui modo in luctu pœnitentiæ seu lacrimis devotionis se ipsos exercent, qui temporales delectationes contemnunt, et corde contrito et humiliato Deo ministrant : isti in exsultatione metent bona gratiæ in præsenti, et fructum gloriæ in futuro. Bonorum enim laborum gloriosus est fructus. Et Apostolus ait : Qui parce seminat, parce et metet ; et qui seminat in benedictionibus, de benedictionibus et metet vitam æternam. Propterea apud Jeremiam consulitur nobis : Novate vobis novale, et nolite serere super spinas. Porro quinque sunt genera lacrimarum. Primæ lacrimæ sunt pro indulgentia propriæ culpæ : et hæ mundant a sorde peccati. Secundæ sunt pro timore futuri judicii et gehennæ : et istæ refrigerant ab ardore concupiscentiæ, retrahuntque ab omni iniquitate. Tertiæ sunt pro incolatu præsentis exsilii : quæ potant animam sitientem. Quartæ, pro defectibus proximorum : et istæ impinguant plangentem. Quintæ sunt pro desiderio patriæ : quæ animam omni bono fecundant.
paras.en: [[125:5|They that sow in tears|Qui seminant in lacrimis]]: that is, those who now exercise themselves in the mourning of penance or in tears of devotion, who despise temporal delights, and serve God with a contrite and humbled heart: these [[125:5|shall reap in joy|in exsultatione metent]] the good things of grace in the present, and the fruit of glory in the future. [[Wis 3:15|For the fruit of good labours is glorious|Bonorum enim laborum gloriosus est fructus]]. And the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 9:6|He who soweth sparingly shall also reap sparingly: and he who soweth in blessings shall also reap blessings|Qui parce seminat, parce et metet ; et qui seminat in benedictionibus, de benedictionibus et metet]], life everlasting. Therefore we are counselled in Jeremias: [[Jer 4:3|Break up anew your fallow ground, and sow not upon thorns|Novate vobis novale, et nolite serere super spinas]]. Now there are five kinds of tears. The first tears are for the pardon of one's own guilt: and these cleanse from the filth of sin. The second are from fear of the judgement to come and of hell: and these cool the heat of concupiscence and draw back from all iniquity. The third are for our sojourning in this present exile: and these give drink to the thirsting soul. The fourth, for the failings of our neighbours: and these make fat him who mourns. The fifth are from longing for the fatherland: and these make the soul fruitful in every good.

paras.t: Euntes electi Dei per viam vitæ præsentis, ibant per viam mandatorum Altissimi, et flebant, secundum aliquem modum prædictorum generum lacrimandi, mittentes semina sua, id est opera meritoria facientes : quæ opera dicta sunt semina, quoniam sicut ex semine nascitur fructus, sic ex operibus bonis oritur fructus vitæ æternæ, infusio consolationis divinæ. Mittunt igitur semina sua, id est, opera bona ante se mittunt, cumulum meritorum colligunt, quem in Christo abscondunt, quemadmodum ipse hortatur : Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in cœlo. Et Apostolus : Nolite, inquit, deficere benefacientes ; tempore enim suo metemus non deficientes. Venientes autem ad Christi tribunal, venient cum exsultatione, id est cum secura et læta conscientia, portantes manipulos suos, id est opera virtuosa quæ collegerunt. Opera enim illorum sequuntur illos.
paras.en: [[125:6|Going|Euntes]], the elect of God, along the way of the present life, [[125:6|they went|ibant]] along the way of the commandments of the Most High, [[125:6|and wept|et flebant]] in one or other of the kinds of weeping just described, [[125:6|casting their seeds|mittentes semina sua]], that is, doing meritorious works: and these works are called seeds because, as fruit springs from seed, so from good works arises the fruit of eternal life, the inpouring of divine consolation. They cast their seeds, then, that is, they send good works on before them, they gather a store of merits, which they hide in Christ, as he himself exhorts: [[Matt 6:20|lay up to yourselves treasures in heaven|Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in cœlo]]. And the Apostle: [[Gal 6:9|let us not fail|Nolite]], he says, [[Gal 6:9|in doing good|deficere benefacientes]]; [[Gal 6:9|For in due time we shall reap, not failing|tempore enim suo metemus non deficientes]]. [[125:7|But coming|Venientes autem]] to the judgement-seat of Christ, [[125:7|they shall come with joyfulness|venient cum exsultatione]], that is, with a secure and glad conscience, [[125:7|carrying their sheaves|portantes manipulos suos]], that is, the virtuous works they have gathered. [[Apoc 14:13|For their works follow them|Opera enim illorum sequuntur illos]].

paras.t: Admonemur ex psalmo præsenti redemptionem nostram a Christo factam recolere, atque in Salvatore de suis beneficiis exsultare, eum laudando, contemplando, incomparabiliterque amando. Denique docet nos scriptura psalmi istius, quid inter electos et reprobos distet : quia electi eundo in bono, proficiunt lacrimando ; reprobi vero in isto exsilio quasi in patria gloriantur, et de carcere captivitatis faciunt sibi paradisum voluptatis : idcirco venientes ad Christi judicium, venient cum mœrore, nihil portantes nisi damnationis suæ chirographum. Unde in Evangelio dicitur eis : Væ vobis qui habetis consolationem vestram ; et, Væ vobis qui ridetis nunc, quia plorabitis et flebitis. Hinc enim Abraham diviti dixit : Fili, recordare quia recepisti bona in vita tua, et Lazarus similiter mala : nunc autem hic consolatur, tu vero cruciaris. Despiciamus igitur omnem mundi pompam, vanitatem et gloriam, corporisque desideria reprimamus, et in lacrimis sanctis occupemur, scientes non posse nos modo cum mundo gaudere, et postmodum cum Christo regnare.
paras.en: We are admonished by the present psalm to call to mind our redemption wrought by Christ, and to exult in the Saviour over his benefits, praising him, contemplating him, and loving him beyond compare. Finally, the text of this psalm teaches us what difference there is between the elect and the reprobate: for the elect, going on in good, advance by weeping; but the reprobate glory in this exile as though in their fatherland, and make of the prison of their captivity a paradise of pleasure: therefore, coming to the judgement of Christ, they shall come with grief, carrying nothing but the bond of their damnation [*chirographum*, a handwritten bond or note of debt; compare Col. ii, 14]. Hence it is said to them in the Gospel: [[Luke 6:24|Woe to you|Væ vobis]] who [[Luke 6:24|have your consolation|habetis consolationem vestram]]; and: [[Luke 6:25|Woe to you that now laugh: for you shall mourn and weep|Væ vobis qui ridetis nunc, quia plorabitis et flebitis]]. Hence Abraham said to the rich man: [[Luke 16:25|Son, remember that thou didst receive good things in thy lifetime, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted and thou art tormented|Fili, recordare quia recepisti bona in vita tua, et Lazarus similiter mala : nunc autem hic consolatur, tu vero cruciaris]]. Let us therefore despise all the pomp, vanity and glory of the world, and restrain the desires of the body, and busy ourselves with holy tears, knowing that we cannot rejoice with the world now and afterwards reign with Christ.

paras.t: Precatio. Expurga nos, Domine, a peccatis ; ædifica tibi in nobis domum mansionis : ut tu in nobis, et nos in te manentes, quum deleris nobis somnum mortis, cum dilectis tuis simus heredes regni cœlestis.
paras.en: Prayer. Cleanse us, O Lord, from our sins; build thyself in us a house to dwell in: that, thou abiding in us and we in thee, when thou hast done away for us the sleep of death, we may be heirs of the heavenly kingdom with thy beloved.

126.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI SEXTI : NISI DOMINUS ÆDIFICAVERIT DOMUM.
126.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and twenty-sixth psalm: Unless the Lord build the house.

paras.t: Habet præterea psalmus jam declarandus hunc titulum : Canticum graduum Salomonis. Secundum eos autem, qui psalmum hunc litteraliter exponunt de ædificatione templi materialis in Jerusalem, additur in titulo, Salomonis : vel quoniam David fecit hunc psalmum pro filio suo Salomone ; vel quia Salomon eum conscripsit, ad insinuandum quod sine speciali adjutorio Dei, ædificatio templi consummari non posset. Est autem expositio hæc multum grossa et rudis, quæ tamen breviter tangi potest, ut sit sensus :
paras.en: The psalm now to be explained has, moreover, this title: [[126:1|A gradual canticle of Solomon|Canticum graduum Salomonis]]. Now according to those who expound this psalm literally of the building of the material temple in Jerusalem[[3 Kings 6:1||]], *of Solomon* is added in the title: either because David made this psalm for his son Solomon, or because Solomon wrote it, to convey that without God's special help the building of the temple could not be completed. This exposition, however, is very gross and crude [that is, it keeps to the bare outward letter]; yet it may be touched on briefly, so that the sense is this:

paras.t: Nisi Dominus ædificaverit domum, principaliter operando, et artificibus efficaciam operandi præstando, in vanum laboraverunt qui ædificant eam : quoniam sine ejus adjutorio eam perficere nequeunt. Et hujus signum et simile est, quia Nisi Dominus custodierit civitatem ab inimicorum incursu, ceterisque periculis, frustra vigilat qui custodit eam, eo quod urbem sua potestate nequeat custodire.
paras.en: [[126:1|Unless the Lord build the house|Nisi Dominus ædificaverit domum]], working as the principal cause and giving the craftsmen the power to work to effect, [[126:1|they labour in vain that build it|in vanum laboraverunt qui ædificant eam]]: since without his help they cannot complete it[[John 15:5||]]. And a sign and likeness of this is that [[126:1|Unless the Lord keep the city|Nisi Dominus custodierit civitatem]] from the onset of enemies and from other dangers, [[126:1|he watcheth in vain that keepeth it|frustra vigilat qui custodit eam]], because he cannot guard the city by his own power.

paras.t: Deinde Psalmista affatur artifices : Vanum est vobis ante lucem diei surgere ad operandum, quasi vestra potestate et festinatione possitis templum perficere. Idcirco surgite ad operandum postquam sederitis, id est nocte et somno completis, qui manducatis panem doloris, id est, qui vescimini cibo vestro labore acquisito, cui labori miscetur pœna et fatigatio corporis.
paras.en: Then the Psalmist addresses the craftsmen: [[126:2|It is vain for you|Vanum est vobis]] [[126:2|before light|ante lucem]] of day [[126:2|to rise|surgere]] to work, as though by your own power and haste you could complete the temple. Therefore [[126:2|rise ye|surgite]] to work [[126:2|after you have sitten|postquam sederitis]], that is, when the night and your sleep are finished, [[126:2|you that eat the bread of sorrow|qui manducatis panem doloris]], that is, who feed on food gotten by your labour, a labour mingled with pain and weariness of body.

paras.t: Quum dederit Dominus dilectis suis, scilicet filiis Israel, somnum, id est quietem beatæ mortis, ecce hereditas Domini, filii, id est, tunc filii ab eis instructi, sunt hereditas Domini Dei : quia populus fidelis appellatur hereditas Dei. Et per Isaiam Dominus ait : Hereditas mea Israel. Et ista hereditas, seu filii boni atque fideles, sunt merces fructus ventris, id est præmium meriti Christi, qui est fructus ventris virginei. Christus enim sua passione eos redemit et emit, et Pater dedit eos Filio suo.
paras.en: [[126:2|When he shall give|Quum dederit Dominus]] [[126:2|to his beloved|dilectis suis]], namely the children of Israel, [[126:2|sleep|somnum]], that is, the rest of a blessed death, [[126:3|Behold the inheritance of the Lord are children|ecce hereditas Domini, filii]]: that is, then the children instructed by them are the inheritance of the Lord God, for the faithful people is called the inheritance of God. And the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 19:25|Israel is my inheritance|Hereditas mea Israel]]. And this inheritance, that is, the good and faithful children, are [[126:3|the reward, the fruit of the womb|merces fructus ventris]], that is, the reward of the merit of Christ, who is the fruit of the virginal womb. For Christ redeemed and bought them by his passion, and the Father gave them to his Son.

paras.t: Sicut sagittæ in manu potentis, id est fortis sagittatoris, exsistentes, sunt acutæ et paratæ ad resistendum adversariis ; ita filii excussorum, id est, sic discipuli et imitatores dilectorum Domini, videlicet sanctorum doctorum, antiquorumque patrum, parati sunt ad resistendum hostibus veritatis. Dicuntur autem doctores sancti et patres antiqui, excussi : quoniam de hac vita ablati et quasi excussi sunt ; vel quia a carnalibus concupiscentiis, et ceteris impedimentis serviendi vacandique Deo, erant abstracti, et ad spirituale præmium expediti.
paras.en: [[126:4|As arrows in the hand of the mighty|Sicut sagittæ in manu potentis]], that is, of a strong archer, are sharp and ready to withstand adversaries, [[126:4|so the children of them that have been shaken|ita filii excussorum]]: that is, so the disciples and imitators of the Lord's beloved, namely of the holy doctors and the ancient fathers, are ready to withstand the enemies of the truth. Now the holy doctors and ancient fathers are called *shaken* [*excussi*, also "shaken off" or "set free"], because they have been taken away and as it were shaken out of this life; or because they had been drawn away from fleshly desires and the other hindrances to serving God and giving themselves to him, and were set free for the spiritual reward.

paras.t: Beatus vir qui implevit desiderium suum ex ipsis filiis excussorum : id est, beatus est doctor seu pastor, qui cupit tales habere discipulos, qui diligenter observent quæ audiunt, et pro veritate efficaciter pugnent. Vel : Beatus vir qui implevit desiderium suum ex ipsis excussis, id est, qui doctrinam et vitam sanctorum patrum atque doctorum digne assequitur. Hic vir beatus non confundetur nec reprobabitur quum loquetur inimicis suis, id est hostibus veritatis, in porta, id est in publico. Nam verus et justus apparebit, tam in præsenti, quam in futuro judicio, dum causa ejus cœperit discuti contra adversarios suos.
paras.en: [[126:5|Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire|Beatus vir qui implevit desiderium suum]] [[126:5|with them|ex ipsis]], the children of them that have been shaken: that is, blessed is the doctor or pastor who desires to have such disciples as diligently keep what they hear and fight effectively for the truth. Or: [[126:5|Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire|Beatus vir qui implevit desiderium suum]] [[126:5|with them|ex ipsis]], the shaken themselves, that is, who worthily attains to the teaching and life of the holy fathers and doctors. This blessed man [[126:5|shall not be confounded|non confundetur]] nor rejected [[126:5|when he shall speak to his enemies|quum loquetur inimicis suis]], that is, to the enemies of the truth, [[126:5|in the gate|in porta]], that is, in public. For he will appear true and just, both in the present judgment and in the judgment to come, when his cause begins to be tried against his adversaries.

paras.t: Denique moraliter per Salomonem intelligitur Christus, qui est verus pacificus, ædificavitque domum, id est Ecclesiam Deo Patri ex vivis lapidibus. Et de hujus domus ædificatione verissime dicitur : Nisi Dominus Jesus Christus, seu Trinitas Deus, ædificaverit intus per fidem, caritatem et gratiam, domum, id est Ecclesiam, seu quamlibet personam ecclesiasticam, in qua Deus per fidem moratur : quemadmodum ait Salvator, Ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus ; in vanum, id est frustra et sine profectu, laboraverunt et laborabunt, qui ædificant, id est, ædificare nituntur eam, videlicet Prophetæ, Apostoli et successores eorum : qui prædicando, docendo, exemplariter conversando, miracula faciendo, conati sunt convertere homines, informare fideles, ædificare Ecclesiam ; sed nisi Deus intus illuminet, inanis est prædicatio foris adhibita. Propter quod Paulus testatur : Neque qui plantat, est aliquid, neque qui rigat, sed qui incrementum dat, Deus.
paras.en: Lastly, in the moral sense, Solomon is understood as Christ, who is the true peaceable one [*Salomon* means "peaceable"], and who built a house, that is, the Church, to God the Father out of living stones. And of the building of this house it is most truly said: [[126:1|Unless the Lord|Nisi Dominus]] Jesus Christ, or God the Trinity, [[126:1|build|ædificaverit]] within, through faith, charity and grace, [[126:1|the house|domum]], that is, the Church, or any member of the Church, in whom God dwells by faith, as the Saviour says, [[John 14:23|we will come to him and will make our abode with him|Ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus]]; [[126:1|in vain|in vanum]], that is, to no purpose and without profit, [[126:1|they labour|laboraverunt]] and shall labour [[126:1|that build it|qui ædificant]], that is, who strive to build it, namely the Prophets, the Apostles and their successors, who by preaching, teaching, living as examples and working miracles have endeavoured to convert men, to form the faithful and to build up the Church; but unless God enlightens within, preaching applied from without is empty. For which reason Paul testifies: [[1 Cor 3:7|neither he that planteth is any thing, nor he that watereth: but God that giveth the increase|Neque qui plantat, est aliquid, neque qui rigat, sed qui incrementum dat, Deus]].

paras.t: Nisi Dominus custodierit civitatem, id est Ecclesiam : quæ dicitur civitas, propter caritativam unionem fidelium ; frustra vigilat omnis doctor, pastor, prælatus, qui custodit eam. A Deo enim est non solum inchoatio boni, sed etiam conservatio, protectio atque perfectio. Et ideo, sicut solus Deus Ecclesiam intus ædificat, caritatem, fidem, spem, et dona Spiritus Sancti per creationem infundendo hominibus : ad quam infusionem homines sancti Deo subservientes disponunt mentes humanas ; sic solus Deus custodit Ecclesiam seu corda fidelium per se ipsum, conservando in esse dona quæ creando infudit. Angeli vero et homines ceteris præsidentes, custodiunt instrumentaliter, dispositive atque forinsecus, hortando ad bonum, et impedimenta bene vivendi tollendo. Hinc scriptum habetur : A facie tua, Domine, concepimus, et quasi parturivimus et peperimus spiritum.
paras.en: [[126:1|Unless the Lord keep the city|Nisi Dominus custodierit civitatem]], that is, the Church, which is called a city because of the union of the faithful in charity, [[126:1|he watcheth in vain|frustra vigilat]], every doctor, pastor and prelate [[126:1|that keepeth it|qui custodit eam]]. For from God is not only the beginning of good but also its preservation, protection and perfection. And therefore, just as God alone builds the Church within, pouring charity, faith, hope and the gifts of the Holy Ghost into men by creating them [that is, these gifts are created in the soul by God, not produced by man], while holy men, serving God, dispose human minds for that infusion; so God alone keeps the Church, or the hearts of the faithful, by himself, preserving in being the gifts which he poured in by creating them. But angels, and men set over others, keep it instrumentally, by way of disposing, and from without, by exhorting to good and removing the hindrances to living well. Hence it is written: [[Is 26:17|in thy presence, O Lord|A facie tua, Domine]], we [[Is 26:18|have conceived, and been as it were in labour, and have brought forth wind|concepimus, et quasi parturivimus et peperimus spiritum]] [*spiritum*, "wind" in the Douay-Rheims, is here taken as "spirit"].

paras.t: Deinde ædificatoribus domus Dei, id est prælatis Ecclesiæ, ait : Vanum est vobis ante lucem, id est ante gratiæ infusionem, ante divini auxilii irradiationem seu receptionem, surgere ad instruendum seu ædificandum Ecclesiam. Tanquam dicat : Nihil proficiet labor vester, nisi gratia Dei adfuerit tam vobis quam auditoribus vestris. Idcirco surgite ad exsequendum officium vobis commissum, postquam sederitis, id est, gratiam Dei humiliter imploraveritis, atque ab exterioribus quiescendo, paulisper ad pedes Crucifixi sederitis, meditando, contemplando, orando, quatenus intromittamini in cellam vinariam Spiritus Sancti, et in thesauros sapientiæ Dei ; illicque spiritualiter inebriati ardore sancti amoris et lumine veritatis, surgatis et procedatis ad alios instruendos, eructando et communicando eis de plenitudine vestra. Qui manducatis panem doloris, id est, quibus lacrimæ compassionis fraternæ, panes sunt die ac nocte : quoniam semper oportet vos condolere subditis vestris ; nec solum vestra, sed eorum quoque peccata deplangere, prout Apostolus ait : Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor ? Quis scandalizatur, et ego non uror ? Et Job loquitur : Flebam super eo qui afflictus erat, et compatiebatur anima mea pauperi. Et Ezechieli præcepit Dominus, ut portet iniquitatem populi Judæorum.
paras.en: Then to the builders of God's house, that is, the prelates of the Church, he says: [[126:2|It is vain for you|Vanum est vobis]] [[126:2|before light|ante lucem]], that is, before the infusion of grace, before the shining forth or the receiving of divine help, [[126:2|to rise|surgere]] to instruct or build up the Church. As if to say: your labour will profit nothing unless the grace of God be present both to you and to your hearers[[John 15:4||]][[John 15:5||]]. Therefore [[126:2|rise ye|surgite]] to carry out the office committed to you [[126:2|after you have sitten|postquam sederitis]], that is, when you have humbly implored the grace of God and, resting from outward things, have sat a while at the feet of the Crucified, meditating, contemplating and praying, so that you may be brought into the [[Cant 2:4|cellar of wine|cellam vinariam]] of the Holy Ghost and into the treasuries of the wisdom of God; and there, spiritually inebriated with the ardour of holy love and the light of truth, may rise and go forth to instruct others, pouring out and imparting to them of your fullness. [[126:2|You that eat the bread of sorrow|Qui manducatis panem doloris]], that is, for whom the tears of brotherly compassion are [[Ps 41:4|bread day and night|panes sunt die ac nocte]] [the margin gives Ps. xii, 4; the words are those of Ps 41:4]: since you must always suffer with those under you, and bewail not only your own sins but theirs too, as the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 11:29|Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is scandalized, and I am not on fire?|Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor? quis scandalizatur, et ego non uror?]] And Job says: [[Job 30:25|I wept|Flebam]] [[Job 30:25|for him that was afflicted, and my soul had compassion on the poor|super eo qui afflictus erat, et compatiebatur anima mea pauperi]] [the margin gives Job xxxi, 25; the words are from Job 30:25]. And the Lord commanded Ezechiel to bear the iniquity of the people of the Jews[[Ezech 4:4||]].

paras.t: Potest etiam versus iste exponi ad omnes. Vanum est vobis, o universi viatores, ante lucem surgere, id est, ante caritatem gratiæ gratificantis, aliquid velle meritorie agere. Vel, Ante lucem surgere, id est, antequam veniatis ad caritatem patriæ, vos ipsos velle erigere, exaltare, aut aliquid reputare, vel quasi ex securitate gaudere. Propterea surgite, id est, exaltari satagite, postquam sederitis, id est, humiliati fueritis, atque in hac vita nil nisi humilitatem in omnibus desideraveritis, qui manducatis panem doloris, id est lacrimarum, exercentes opera pœnitentiæ, illisque reficientes animas vestras : quemadmodum Christus ait : Meus cibus est ut faciam voluntatem ejus qui misit me.
paras.en: This verse can also be expounded of all men. [[126:2|It is vain for you|Vanum est vobis]], O all ye wayfarers [that is, those still on the way, in this life], [[126:2|to rise before light|ante lucem surgere]], that is, to will to do anything meritoriously before the charity of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratificans*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God]. Or, [[126:2|to rise before light|Ante lucem surgere]], that is, before you come to the charity of the fatherland, to will to raise yourselves up, to exalt yourselves, or to think yourselves anything, or to rejoice as though in security. Therefore [[126:2|rise ye|surgite]], that is, strive to be exalted, [[126:2|after you have sitten|postquam sederitis]], that is, after you have been humbled, and in this life have desired nothing in all things but humility, [[126:2|you that eat the bread of sorrow|qui manducatis panem doloris]], that is, of tears, practising the works of penance and refreshing your souls with them, as Christ says: [[John 4:34|My meat is to do the will of him that sent me|Meus cibus est ut faciam voluntatem ejus qui misit me]].

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit quando surgendum sit plene atque perfecte. Quum dederit Dominus dilectis suis, id est electis, somnum, id est felicem quietem post hanc laboriosissimam vitam, ecce hereditas Domini, id est, tunc populus electus, existens hereditas Dei, præsens præstoque erit, atque in gloria apparebit : hereditas, inquam, exsistens, filii, merces fructus ventris, id est Christi filii Dei, qui Christus est fructus ventris generosi Virginis benedictæ. Cur autem homines asserantur merces Christi, jam dictum est. Sed et Christus est merces eorum : nam ipse est præmium nostrum, et objectalis nostra felicitas. Propter quod ait : Manifestabo ei (scilicet diligenti) me ipsum.
paras.en: Next he shows when one is to rise fully and perfectly. [[126:2|When he shall give|Quum dederit Dominus]] [[126:2|to his beloved|dilectis suis]], that is, to the elect, [[126:2|sleep|somnum]], that is, happy rest after this most toilsome life, [[126:3|Behold the inheritance of the Lord|ecce hereditas Domini]], that is, then the elect people, being the inheritance of God, will be present and at hand and will appear in glory: an inheritance, I say, being [[126:3|children|filii]], [[126:3|the reward, the fruit of the womb|merces fructus ventris]], that is, of Christ the Son of God, for Christ is the fruit of the noble womb of the blessed Virgin. Why men are said to be the reward of Christ has already been told. But Christ too is their reward: for he is our prize and our felicity as its object [that is, the good whose possession is our happiness]. For which reason he says: I [[John 14:21|will manifest myself to him|Manifestabo ei (scilicet diligenti) me ipsum]] (namely, to him that loveth).

paras.t: Deinde ostenditur quomodo Ecclesia sit collecta, et quomodo hereditas hæc sit Domino acquisita. Sicut sagittæ in manu potentis se habent, ita filii excussorum, id est, sic sancti Apostoli et cooperatores atque successores eorum, qui sunt filii Prophetarum : qui nominantur excussi propter causas præhabitas. Nam sicut sagittæ de manu viri potentis cito in longinquum jaciuntur, ita Apostoli et eorum discipuli velociter per universum orbem transmissi sunt, prædicantes ubique, et omnes electos ad fidem congregantes in una Ecclesia Christi, quemadmodum Isaias prædixit : Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mare, in Africam et Lydiam, tenentes sagittam, in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe : et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus, et adducent omnes fratres vestros. Beatus vir, jam in spe, qui implevit desiderium suum, id est, qui mentem suam spirituali desiderio implevit, ex ipsis filiis excussorum atque excussis : id est, qui tam ardenti affectu audit, tenet et implet verba Apostolorum et Prophetarum, quod nullum illicitum desiderium, nulla inordinata affectio locum invenit in anima ejus. Cetera ex dictis innotescunt.
paras.en: Next it is shown how the Church was gathered, and how this inheritance was acquired for the Lord. [[126:4|As arrows in the hand of the mighty|Sicut sagittæ in manu potentis]] are, [[126:4|so the children of them that have been shaken|ita filii excussorum]], that is, so are the holy Apostles and their fellow workers and successors, who are the children of the Prophets, and these are called *shaken* for the reasons given before. For as arrows are swiftly shot far off from the hand of a mighty man, so the Apostles and their disciples were swiftly sent through the whole world, preaching everywhere and gathering all the elect to the faith in the one Church of Christ, as Isaias foretold: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles into the sea|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mare]], [[Is 66:19|into Africa, and Lydia them that draw the bow: into Italy, and Greece, to the islands afar off|in Africam et Lydiam, tenentes sagittam, in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe]]: [[Is 66:19|And they shall declare my glory to the Gentiles|et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus]], [[Is 66:20|And they shall bring all your brethren|et adducent omnes fratres vestros]]. [[126:5|Blessed is the man|Beatus vir]], already in hope, [[126:5|that hath filled the desire|qui implevit desiderium suum]], that is, who has filled his mind with spiritual desire, [[126:5|with them|ex ipsis]], the children of them that have been shaken and the shaken themselves: that is, who hears, holds and fulfils the words of the Apostles and Prophets with such ardent affection that no unlawful desire, no disordered affection, finds place in his soul. The rest is clear from what has been said.

paras.t: Ecce psalmus iste morali documento saluberrime plenus, et de octavo gradu spiritualis ascensus pertractans, videlicet de modo, hora et ordine surgendi ad summum ac ultimum omnium entium finem, Deum æternum et adorandum. Docet nos evidenter, ut nunquam nisi in solo Deo speremus, omne bonum, id est initium, conservationem, processum et consummationem operum bonorum ei attribuamus, sicut Deo nostræ salutis, quemadmodum a Jeremia dicitur : Vere in Domino Deo nostro salus Israel. Docet enim nos canticum istud omnem superbiam funditus exstirpare, humilitatem amplecti, talique ordine ad somnum electorum procedere.
paras.en: Behold, this psalm is most wholesomely full of moral teaching, and treats of the eighth degree of the spiritual ascent, namely of the manner, the hour and the order of rising to the highest and last end of all beings, God, eternal and adorable. It teaches us plainly never to hope save in God alone, and to ascribe to him all good, that is, the beginning, preservation, progress and completion of good works, as to the God of our salvation[[Ps 17:47||]], as is said by Jeremias: [[Jer 3:23|truly in the Lord our God is the salvation of Israel|Vere in Domino Deo nostro salus Israel]]. For this canticle teaches us to root out all pride utterly, to embrace humility, and in such order to go forward to the sleep of the elect.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, spiritualium domorum ædificator, ut nos custodias precamur : imple in te desiderium nostrum, et electis tuis nos conjunge pro meritis.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, builder of spiritual houses, we pray thee to keep us: fill our desire in thee, and join us to thy elect according to their merits.

127.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI SEPTIMI : BEATI OMNES QUI TIMENT DOMINUM.
127.title_en: Declaration of the hundred and twenty-seventh psalm: Blessed are all they that fear the Lord.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi præsentis est: Canticum graduum. Agit enim hic psalmus de filiali timore, qui est nonus gradus spiritualis ascensus. Hic enim gradus præcipue necessarius est ascendere atque proficere cupienti: quoniam in Ecclesiastico habetur, Qui sine timore est, non potest justificari. Est tamen quidam timor servilis quo pœna timetur, nec malum vitatur amore boni, sed pavore tormenti. De quo Apostolus ait: Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum; et iterum, Non dedit nobis Deus spiritum timoris, sed dilectionis. Unde beatus Antonius dixit: Ego jam non timeo Deum. Pensandum namque quod objectum timoris, est malum. Nam timor est quidam recessus, quo appetitus aliquid refugit. Deus ergo, secundum quod Deus, et in quantum naturaliter bonus est, timeri non potest directe et per se, secundum Thomam. Objectum autem timoris servilis, est malum pœnæ; objectum vero timoris filialis, est malum culpæ. In quantum igitur Deus pro culpa pœnam infligit, timetur timore servili; in quantum vero separatio a Deo, malum aliquod est, timetur timore filiali castoque.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is: [[127:1|A gradual canticle|Canticum graduum]]. For this psalm treats of filial fear, which is the ninth step of the spiritual ascent. This step is especially necessary for one who wishes to ascend and make progress, since it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 1:28|he that is without fear, cannot be justified|Qui sine timore est, non potest justificari]]. There is, however, a certain servile fear, by which punishment is feared, and evil is shunned not out of love of the good but out of dread of torment. Of this the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:15|you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear: but you have received the spirit of adoption of sons|Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum]]; and again, [[2 Tim 1:7|God hath not given us the spirit of fear|Non dedit nobis Deus spiritum timoris]], but [[2 Tim 1:7|of love|dilectionis]]. Hence blessed Antony said: I no longer fear God. For it must be considered that the object of fear is evil, since fear is a kind of drawing back, by which the appetite flees from something. God, therefore, as God and inasmuch as He is good by nature, cannot be feared directly and of Himself, according to Thomas. The object of servile fear is the evil of punishment; the object of filial fear is the evil of guilt. Inasmuch, then, as God inflicts punishment for guilt, He is feared with servile fear; but inasmuch as separation from God is an evil, He is feared with filial and chaste fear.

paras.t: Ait ergo sanctus Propheta: Beati omnes sunt jam in spe, qui timent Dominum filiali et casto timore. Non enim est personarum acceptor Deus; sed in omni gente, qui timet Deum et operatur justitiam, acceptus est illi. Qui ambulant in viis ejus, id est in divinis præceptis, non in propriis adinventionibus, et post pravitatem proprii cordis, sicut de impio scriptum est: Abiit vagus in via cordis sui; et alibi: Quam vilis facta es, iterans vias tuas!
paras.en: The holy Prophet says, then: [[127:1|Blessed are all|Beati omnes]] (that is, they are blessed already in hope) [[127:1|they that fear the Lord|qui timent Dominum]] with a filial and chaste fear. For [[Acts 10:34|God is not a respecter of persons|Non enim est personarum acceptor Deus]]; [[Acts 10:35|But in every nation, he that feareth him and worketh justice is acceptable to him|sed in omni gente, qui timet Deum et operatur justitiam, acceptus est illi]]. [[127:1|that walk in his ways|Qui ambulant in viis ejus]], that is, in the divine commandments, not in their own inventions and after the perversity of their own heart, as is written of the wicked man: [[Is 57:17|he went away wandering in his own heart|Abiit vagus in via cordis sui]]; and elsewhere: [[Jer 2:36|How exceeding base art thou become, going the same ways over again!|Quam vilis facta es, iterans vias tuas]]

paras.t: Labores manuum tuarum quia manducabis, id est, quoniam præmio operum tuorum bonorum in cœlo vesceris, et fructus studiorum actuumque meritoriorum tuorum percipies in patria seu visione divina: juxta illud, Anima operantium impinguabitur; beatus es nunc in spe, et bene tibi erit illic in re. Unde in Evangelio dicitur: Beatus qui manducabit panem in regno cœlorum.
paras.en: [[127:2|For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands|Labores manuum tuarum quia manducabis]]: that is, because thou shalt feed in heaven on the reward of thy good works, and shalt gather the fruits of thy meritorious endeavours and acts in the fatherland, or in the vision of God; according to that saying, [[Prov 13:4|the soul of them that work, shall be made fat|Anima operantium impinguabitur]]. [[127:2|blessed art thou|beatus es]] now in hope, [[127:2|and it shall be well with thee|et bene tibi erit]] there in reality. Hence it is said in the Gospel: [[Luke 14:15|Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom|Beatus qui manducabit panem in regno]] of heaven.

paras.t: Vel sic: Labores manuum tuarum quia manducabis, id est, quia de labore proprio vives, victum et necessaria tibi laboribus piis procurando; beatus es et bene tibi erit, quoniam talis labor multum meritorius est. Propter quod de se ipso ait Apostolus: Laboramus manibus nostris; et, Ad ea quæ mihi necessaria fuerunt, ministraverunt manus istæ; itemque, Qui non laborat, non manducet. Et Salomon ait: Qui sectatur otium, stultissimus est.
paras.en: Or thus: [[127:2|For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands|Labores manuum tuarum quia manducabis]]: that is, because thou shalt live by thine own labour, providing thy food and necessities for thyself by devout labours; [[127:2|blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee|beatus es et bene tibi erit]], since such labour is very meritorious. For this reason the Apostle says of himself: [[1 Cor 4:12|we labour|Laboramus]] [[1 Cor 4:12|with our own hands|manibus nostris]]; and, [[Acts 20:34|For such things as were needful for me|Ad ea quæ mihi necessaria fuerunt]], [[Acts 20:34|these hands have furnished|ministraverunt manus istæ]]; and likewise, [[2 Thess 3:10|if any man will not work, neither let him eat|Qui non laborat, non manducet]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 12:11|he that pursueth idleness is very foolish|Qui sectatur otium, stultissimus est]].

paras.t: Deinde describitur plenius beatitudo timentis Deum. Primo per bona spiritualia vitæ præsentis, dum subditur: Uxor tua, id est sapientia tibi divinitus data, erit sicut vitis abundans, id est, opera sancta producet, in lateribus domus tuæ, id est in interioribus viribus animæ tuæ: juxta quod alibi dicitur: Quæ desursum est sapientia, primo quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suasibilis, bonis consentiens, plena misericordia et fructibus bonis. Sapientia est cognitio divinorum. Qui autem dicit se nosse Deum et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est. Idcirco vera sapientia fructuosa est tanquam vitis abundans, quæ plurimos generat botros. Dicitur autem sapientia uxor et sponsa hominis timorati, juxta illud: Hanc amavi et exquisivi a juventute mea, et quæsivi sponsam eam mihi assumere, et amator factus sum formæ illius. Salomon quoque monet: Dic sapientiæ, Soror mea es; et prudentiam voca amicam. Unde per uxorem intelligi potest Sapientia æterna et increata, quæ utique sponsa est cordis devoti, et in eo fructificat tanquam vitis fructifera. Hinc nempe ista Sapientia: Ego, inquit, quasi terebinthus extendi ramos meos, et rami mei honoris et gratiæ; rursusque, Ego quasi vitis fructificavi suavitatem odoris.
paras.en: Next, the blessedness of him who fears God is described more fully: first, by the spiritual goods of the present life, when it is added: [[127:3|Thy wife|Uxor tua]], that is, the wisdom given thee from God, shall be [[127:3|as a fruitful vine|sicut vitis abundans]], that is, it shall bring forth holy works, [[127:3|on the sides of thy house|in lateribus domus tuæ]], that is, in the inner powers of thy soul; according to what is said elsewhere: [[Jas 3:17|the wisdom that is from above, first indeed is chaste, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good, full of mercy and good fruits|Quæ desursum est sapientia, primo quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suasibilis, bonis consentiens, plena misericordia et fructibus bonis]]. Wisdom is the knowledge of divine things. But [[1 John 2:4|He who saith that he knoweth him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar|Qui autem dicit se nosse Deum et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est]]. Therefore true wisdom is fruitful, like an abounding vine that bears very many clusters. Now wisdom is called the wife and spouse of the God-fearing man, according to that saying: [[Wis 8:2|Her have I loved, and have sought her out from my youth, and have desired to take for my spouse, and I became a lover of her beauty|Hanc amavi et exquisivi a juventute mea, et quæsivi sponsam eam mihi assumere, et amator factus sum formæ illius]]. Solomon too admonishes: [[Prov 7:4|Say to wisdom: Thou art my sister: and call prudence thy friend|Dic sapientiæ, Soror mea es; et prudentiam voca amicam]]. Hence by the wife may be understood the eternal and uncreated Wisdom, who is indeed the spouse of the devout heart and bears fruit in it like a fruitful vine. Thus this Wisdom says: [[Ecclus 24:22|I have stretched out my branches as the turpentine tree, and my branches are of honour and grace|quasi terebinthus extendi ramos meos, et rami mei honoris et gratiæ]]; and again, [[Ecclus 24:23|As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odour|Ego quasi vitis fructificavi suavitatem odoris]].

paras.t: Filii tui, id est actus ex sapientia orti, erunt sicut novellæ olivarum, id est, virescent et augebuntur, ita quod multi et magni, decori et validi erunt, quoniam indesinenter proficies, in circuitu mensæ tuæ, id est in gyro fidei cordis tui. Sicut enim super mensam cibi ponuntur et sustentantur, sic omnia opera bona supra fidem fundantur, firmantur et radicantur. Fides autem sine dono sapientiæ opera bona non profert, neque econtra. Idcirco ex fide per sapientiam illustrata, causantur et effluunt opera Deo accepta, in circuitu fidei, id est undique in interioribus animæ.
paras.en: [[127:3|Thy children|Filii tui]], that is, the acts that spring from wisdom, shall be [[127:3|as olive plants|sicut novellæ olivarum]], that is, they shall flourish and increase, so that they will be many and great, comely and strong, since thou shalt make progress without ceasing, [[127:3|round about thy table|in circuitu mensæ tuæ]], that is, all around the faith of thy heart. For as food is set on a table and held up by it, so all good works are founded, made firm and rooted upon faith. But faith without the gift of wisdom does not bring forth good works, nor the other way about. Therefore from faith enlightened by wisdom are caused, and flow forth, works acceptable to God, round about faith, that is, on every side within the soul.

paras.t: Vel sic: Uxor tua, id est sapientia, sicut vitis abundans in lateribus domus tuæ, id est in spiritualibus filiis tuis: quia per sapientiam generantur filii spirituales in Christo, juxta illud Apostoli: Per Evangelium Christi ego vos genui. Filii tui spirituales a te sapienter instructi, sicut novellæ olivarum, id est, uncti erunt gratia spirituali, et in Christo florentes atque fecundi, in circuitu mensæ tuæ, id est in gyro spiritualis doctrinæ, qua eos pane vitæ et aqua sapientiæ reficis.
paras.en: Or thus: [[127:3|Thy wife|Uxor tua]], that is, wisdom, [[127:3|as a fruitful vine, on the sides of thy house|sicut vitis abundans in lateribus domus tuæ]], that is, in thy spiritual children; for through wisdom spiritual children are begotten in Christ, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 4:15|by the gospel|Per Evangelium]] of Christ [[1 Cor 4:15|I have begotten you|ego vos genui]]. [[127:3|Thy children|Filii tui]], thy spiritual children wisely instructed by thee, [[127:3|as olive plants|sicut novellæ olivarum]], that is, they shall be anointed with spiritual grace, and flourishing and fruitful in Christ, [[127:3|round about thy table|in circuitu mensæ tuæ]], that is, all around the spiritual teaching with which thou dost refresh them with the bread of life and the water of wisdom[[Ecclus 15:3||]].

paras.t: Ecce sic benedicetur, id est, talia munera gratiæ desuper sortietur, homo qui timet Dominum timore casto et amicali. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico habetur: Timenti Deum bene erit in extremis, et in die defunctionis benedicetur. Quum enim nihil dividat nos a Deo, nisi peccatum, nilque impediat infusionem gratiæ Dei in nos, nisi negligentia nostra, eo ipso quo timor negligentiam excutit, a vitiis retrahit, et peccata expellit, disponit cor nostrum ad omne bonum, omnisque boni quodammodo causa est. Ideo et alibi inducitur: Plenitudo sapientiæ, timere Deum.
paras.en: [[127:4|Behold, thus shall the man be blessed|Ecce sic benedicetur]], that is, he shall obtain such gifts of grace from above, [[127:4|that feareth the Lord|homo qui timet Dominum]] with a chaste and friendly fear. For this reason it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 1:13|With him that feareth the Lord, it shall go well in the latter end, and in the day of his death he shall be blessed|Timenti Deum bene erit in extremis, et in die defunctionis benedicetur]]. For since nothing divides us from God but sin, and nothing hinders the pouring of God's grace into us but our own negligence, by the very fact that fear shakes off negligence, draws us back from vices and drives out sins, it disposes our heart to every good, and is in a manner the cause of every good. Therefore it is said elsewhere too: [[Ecclus 1:20|To fear God is the fulness of wisdom|Plenitudo sapientiæ, timere Deum]].

paras.t: Benedicat tibi Dominus ex Sion, id est ex Ecclesia militanti, benedicendo tibi per ministros et prælatos Ecclesiæ; et videas bona, id est bonum statum, continuumque profectum, Jerusalem, id est Ecclesiæ peregrinantis a Domino, scilicet militantis, præliantis, laborantis, tamen in pace Christi pausantis, omnibus diebus vitæ tuæ. Quantum enim bonum commune totius Ecclesiæ diligis, tantum de ejus conservatione ac profectu exsultas. Unde et vere devotus frequenter ac ferventer orare habet pro bono statu Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[127:5|May the Lord bless thee out of Sion|Benedicat tibi Dominus ex Sion]], that is, out of the Church militant, blessing thee through the ministers and prelates of the Church; [[127:5|and mayst thou see the good things|et videas bona]], that is, the good state and continual progress, [[127:5|of Jerusalem|Jerusalem]], that is, of the Church that is a pilgrim [[2 Cor 5:6|absent from the Lord|peregrinantis a Domino]], namely the Church militant, fighting and toiling, yet resting in the peace of Christ, [[127:5|all the days of thy life|omnibus diebus vitæ tuæ]]. For as much as thou lovest the common good of the whole Church, so much dost thou rejoice in its preservation and progress. Hence the truly devout man ought to pray often and fervently for the good state of the Church.

paras.t: Et videas filios filiorum tuorum, id est, cernas quod illi quos tu spiritualiter genuisti, alios spiritualiter generent, quatenus merito et numero augeatur Ecclesia: sicque conspicias pacem Christi seu Christum, qui est pax nostra, secundum Apostolum, super Israel, id est super te ipsum, et alium quemlibet Christianum, Deum fideliter contemplantem.
paras.en: [[127:6|And mayst thou see thy children's children|Et videas filios filiorum tuorum]], that is, mayst thou behold those whom thou hast spiritually begotten spiritually begetting others, so that the Church may be increased in merit and in number; and so mayst thou behold the [[127:6|peace|pacem]] of Christ, or Christ Himself, who is [[Eph 2:14|our peace|pax nostra]], according to the Apostle, [[127:6|upon Israel|super Israel]], that is, upon thyself and upon every other Christian who faithfully contemplates God.

paras.t: Vel sic: Benedicat tibi, id est, dona cœlestis gratiæ mittat et conferat tibi Dominus Deus omnipotens, ex Sion, id est ex triumphanti Ecclesia, in qua Sancti Deum sicut est speculantur. Sion namque speculatio interpretatur. Et videas, post hujus exsilii terminum, bona Jerusalem cœlestis, quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec mens comprehendere sufficit, omnibus diebus vitæ tuæ gloriosæ, quæ erit æterna.
paras.en: Or thus: [[127:5|May the Lord bless thee|Benedicat tibi]], that is, may the [[127:5|Lord|Dominus]] God almighty send and bestow on thee the gifts of heavenly grace, [[127:5|out of Sion|ex Sion]], that is, out of the Church triumphant, in which the Saints behold God [[1 John 3:2|as he is|sicut est]]. For Sion is interpreted *speculatio* [that is, a looking out or watching, the beholding of contemplation]. [[127:5|and mayst thou see|Et videas]], after the end of this exile, [[127:5|the good things of Jerusalem|bona Jerusalem]], the heavenly Jerusalem, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit]][[Is 64:4||]], nor can the mind suffice to comprehend, [[127:5|all the days of thy life|omnibus diebus vitæ tuæ]] in glory, which will be eternal.

paras.t: Et videas filios filiorum tuorum, quatenus illi tecum in patria gaudeant, qui a filiis tuis spiritualibus spiritualiter geniti sunt. Sed quoniam forsitan non omnes electi spirituales filios habent, et si habeant, forte quod illi non habent; idcirco sicut per filios intelliguntur opera gratiosa, sic per filios filiorum istorum intelligi possunt opera gloriosa, sicut sunt Deo frui, et cetera gaudia ac merita Beatorum, quæ ex præviis meritis seu bonis operibus quodammodo oriuntur. Sic etiam videas pacem cœlestem, quæ omnem sensum exsuperat, super Israel, id est quemlibet Beatum, Deum per speciem contuentem.
paras.en: [[127:6|And mayst thou see thy children's children|Et videas filios filiorum tuorum]], so that those who have been spiritually begotten by thy spiritual children may rejoice with thee in the fatherland. But since perhaps not all the elect have spiritual children, and if they have, perhaps those children have none; therefore, as by the children are understood works of grace, so by the children of those children may be understood works of glory, such as the enjoyment of God, and the other joys and merits of the Blessed, which in a manner spring from the merits or good works that went before. So also mayst thou see heavenly [[127:6|peace|pacem]], [[Phil 4:7|which surpasseth all understanding|quæ omnem sensum exsuperat]], [[127:6|upon Israel|super Israel]], that is, upon each of the Blessed, who beholds God face to face [*per speciem*, by sight, as opposed to by faith].

paras.t: Expositio litteralis. Præterea exponentes psalmum istum ad litteram de populo Judæorum, asserunt quod Psalmista invitat eos ad timorem Dei per temporalium bonorum promissa, quemadmodum moris est in lege ac Prophetis invitare eos ad obedientiam Dei per temporalium prosperitatum promissiones. Unde Dominus ait populo huic: Si volueritis et audieritis me, bona terræ comedetis. Sed advertendum quod sicut hujusmodi bona non sunt sufficiens præmium actus virtuosi, præsertim dilectionis divinæ quam præcipit lex; ita non omnibus observantibus legem dabantur, sed spiritualia et meliora data sunt eis, tanquam magis perfectis. Infirmiores vero per temporalia alliciendi erant promissa. Sic ergo quod modo timenti Deum promittitur, quod labores manuum suarum manducabit, id est, temporalium divitiarum abundantia perfruetur, et quod uxor ejus esset fecunda velut vitis abundans; item quod filii ejus carnales sederent seu starent sicut novellæ olivarum in circuitu mensæ suæ: non omnibus, sed multis in veteri Testamento concessum est. Nec enim Eliæ, nec Jeremiæ data sunt hæc, quorum uterque virgo permansit.
paras.en: Literal exposition. Moreover, those who expound this psalm literally of the Jewish people assert that the Psalmist invites them to the fear of God by promises of temporal goods, as it is the custom in the Law and the Prophets to invite them to obedience to God by promises of temporal prosperity. Hence the Lord says to this people: [[Is 1:19|If you be willing, and will hearken to me, you shall eat the good things of the land|Si volueritis et audieritis me, bona terræ comedetis]]. But it must be noted that, as goods of this kind are not a sufficient reward for a virtuous act, especially for the love of God which the Law commands, so they were not given to all who kept the Law; rather, spiritual and better things were given to these, as to the more perfect, while the weaker had to be drawn by promises of temporal things. So what is here promised to him who fears God, namely that he shall eat the labours of his hands, that is, shall enjoy an abundance of temporal riches, and that his wife shall be fruitful [[127:3|as a fruitful vine|velut vitis abundans]], and likewise that his children according to the flesh shall sit or stand [[127:3|as olive plants|sicut novellæ olivarum]] round about his table: this was granted not to all, but to many, in the Old Testament. For these things were not given to Elias or to Jeremias, both of whom remained virgins.

paras.t: Litteralem igitur sequendo sensum, quod ait, Ecce sic benedicetur homo qui timet Dominum, intelligendum est, quod sic vel melius benedicetur. Vel, Sic benedicetur, id est, ita laudabitur. Deinde loquens Propheta populo Synagogæ, subdit: Benedicat tibi Dominus ex Sion, id est ex templo sito in monte Sion, in quo ministri templi benedicebant Judæis; et videas bona Jerusalem, id est bonum statum civitatis regiæ in Judæa, ex cujus bono regimine totius regni salus pendebat. Et videas filios filiorum tuorum, id est, diu vivas, ut tuos nepotes conspicias, videasque pacem super Israel, id est super universum Israeliticum populum.
paras.en: Following, then, the literal sense: where he says, [[127:4|Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord|Ecce sic benedicetur homo qui timet Dominum]], it is to be understood that he shall be blessed thus or better. Or, [[127:4|thus shall the man be blessed|Sic benedicetur]], that is, thus shall he be praised [the Latin *benedicere* means both to bless and to speak well of]. Then the Prophet, speaking to the people of the Synagogue, adds: [[127:5|May the Lord bless thee out of Sion|Benedicat tibi Dominus ex Sion]], that is, out of the temple built on mount Sion, in which the ministers of the temple used to bless the Jews; [[127:5|and mayst thou see the good things of Jerusalem|et videas bona Jerusalem]], that is, the good state of the royal city in Judæa, on whose good government the welfare of the whole kingdom depended. [[127:6|And mayst thou see thy children's children|Et videas filios filiorum tuorum]], that is, mayst thou live long, so as to behold thy grandchildren, and mayst thou see [[127:6|peace upon Israel|pacem super Israel]], that is, upon the whole Israelite people.

paras.t: Precatio. Timentes te beatifica nos, Domine, et fac in viis tuis perseveranter ambulare: benedic nos benedictione tua sancta, ut videamus bona Jerusalem sine fine mansura.
paras.en: Prayer. Make us blessed, O Lord, as those who fear thee, and make us walk perseveringly in thy ways: bless us with thy holy blessing, that we may see the good things of Jerusalem that shall abide without end.

128.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI OCTAVI : SÆPE EXPUGNAVERUNT ME.
128.title_en: Tropological exposition of the hundred and twenty-eighth psalm: Often have they fought against me.

paras.t: Assignatur insuper psalmo jam declarando pro titulo : Canticum graduum : id est, psalmus qui canticum dicitur, tractat de gradu proficiendi ad Deum apicemque virtutum. Iste enim est decimus psalmus gradualis, de patientia loquens, quæ est decimus gradus spiritualis ascensus : et convenienter ponitur post timorem, quoniam metuentem Deum decet omnia æquanimiter tolerare propter justitiam, ne Deus per impatientiam offendatur. Tanta autem est virtus patientiæ, ut Christus dicat : In patientia vestra possidebitis animas vestras.
paras.en: Furthermore, the psalm now to be explained is given as its title: [[128:1|A gradual canticle|Canticum graduum]]: that is, the psalm which is called a canticle treats of a step [that is, a degree; *gradus*, whence "gradual"] in advancing towards God and towards the summit of the virtues. For this is the tenth gradual psalm, speaking of patience, which is the tenth step of the spiritual ascent; and it is fittingly placed after fear [that is, after the preceding psalm, on the fear of the Lord], since it befits one who fears God to bear all things with an even mind for justice' sake, lest God be offended by impatience. And so great is the virtue of patience that Christ says: [[Luke 21:19|In your patience you shall possess your souls|In patientia vestra possidebitis animas vestras]].

paras.t: Propheta igitur volens nos ad patientiam animare, hortatur Ecclesiam, dicens : Sæpe expugnaverunt, id est impugnaverunt, me hostes invisibiles, scilicet dæmones me tentantes, atque visibiles, puta hæretici et tyranni, aliique perversi, a juventute mea, id est ab exordio durationis meæ, et a principio temporis mei. Nam et in paradiso tentatus est primus parens cum conjuge sua a dæmone, et postmodum Abel justus a Cain occisus est. Dicat nunc Israel, id est Ecclesia Deum per fidem contemplans. Quemadmodum enim Gregorius dicit, Omnium electorum qui a principio mundi fuerunt, et usque ad sæculi consummationem futuri sunt, est una Ecclesia, cujus caput est Christus. Semper autem perversi ac reprobi molesti fuerunt electis, nec unquam defuit, deest, aut deerit malignitas persequens et æquitas patiens ; semperque verum fuit, quod per multas tribulationes oportet nos fieri salvos. Unde in historia Judith dicitur : Abraham pater noster tentatus est, et per multas tribulationes probatus, amicus Dei effectus est. Sic Isaac, sic Jacob, sic Moyses et omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles.
paras.en: The Prophet, then, wishing to hearten us to patience, exhorts the Church, saying: [[128:1|Often have they fought against|Sæpe expugnaverunt]], that is, assailed, me: the invisible enemies, namely the demons who tempt me, and the visible ones, such as heretics and tyrants and other perverse men; [[128:1|from my youth|a juventute mea]], that is, from the outset of my existence and from the beginning of my time. For in paradise the first parent was tempted by the devil together with his wife[[Gen 3:1||]], and afterwards Abel the just was slain by Cain[[Gen 4:8||]]. [[128:1|let Israel now say|Dicat nunc Israel]], that is, the Church, contemplating God by faith. For, as Gregory says, of all the elect who have been from the beginning of the world and who shall be until the consummation of the age there is one Church, whose head is Christ[[Eph 5:23||]][[Col 1:18||]]. And the perverse and reprobate have always been troublesome to the elect; never has there been, nor is there, nor will there be, a lack of malice that persecutes and of justice that suffers; and it has always been true that [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must|per multas tribulationes oportet nos]] be saved [Denis's wording; the Douay-Rheims goes on "enter into the kingdom of God"]. Hence it is said in the history of Judith: [[Jdt 8:22|our father Abraham was tempted, and being proved by many tribulations, was made the friend of God|Abraham pater noster tentatus est, et per multas tribulationes probatus, amicus Dei effectus est]]. [[Jdt 8:23|So Isaac, so Jacob, so Moses, and all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|Sic Isaac, sic Jacob, sic Moyses et omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]].

paras.t: Sæpe expugnaverunt me isti a juventute mea : sicut nunc dictum est ; sed frustra : etenim, id est quia, non potuerunt mihi finaliter prævalere, aut interius lædere, seu nocere. Imo omnia cooperantur mihi in bonum ; et eorum malignitas facta est eis causa damnationis æternæ, mihi vero occasio facta est sempiternæ lætitiæ. Hinc enim altissimus apostolici agminis princeps in sua Canonica fatetur : Quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni æmulatores fueritis? Paulus quoque ait : Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Quamvis ergo hostes Ecclesiæ corpus occidant aut animam ad tempus decipiant, non tamen finaliter neque simpliciter prævalent. Imo tempore persecutionis tyrannicæ augebatur Ecclesia merito sanctitatis, et numero conversorum ad fidem, magis quam tempore pacis : sicut Hieronymus testatur, dolens et conquerens, quod postquam Ecclesia temporale imperium acquisivit, pristinam gratiam pro magna parte amisit.
paras.en: [[128:2|Often have they fought against me from my youth|Sæpe expugnaverunt me isti a juventute mea]], as has just been said; but in vain: [[128:2|but|etenim]] (that is, because) [[128:2|they could not prevail over me|non potuerunt mihi]] in the end, nor hurt me inwardly, nor do me harm. Nay rather, [[Rom 8:28|all things work together|omnia cooperantur]] for me [[Rom 8:28|unto good|in bonum]]; and their malice has become for them the cause of eternal damnation, but for me the occasion of everlasting joy. For hence the most exalted prince of the apostolic band declares in his canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 3:13|who is he that can hurt you, if you be zealous of good?|Quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni æmulatores fueritis?]] Paul too says: [[Rom 8:31|If God be for us, who is against us?|Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?]] Although, then, the enemies of the Church may kill the body, or deceive the soul for a time[[Matt 10:28||]], yet they do not prevail in the end, nor absolutely. Nay rather, in the time of the tyrants' persecution the Church grew in the merit of holiness and in the number of converts to the faith more than in time of peace; as Jerome testifies, grieving and lamenting that after the Church acquired temporal power it lost its former grace in great part.

paras.t: Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt peccatores, id est, ita me sibi subjecerunt, conculcaverunt, et afflixerunt, sicut fabricantes sibi subjiciunt atque conculcant fundamentum, supra quod ædificium fundant. Vel, Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt, id est, me pro suo libito persecuti sunt. Vel, Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt, id est, machinam iniquitatis supra me construxerunt, accumulantes sibi sarcinam vitiorum, seu pondus ac multitudinem scelerum, dum me tam injuste molestaverunt. Per dorsum autem designatur totum, eo quod patientes verba, soleant dorsum ad percutientem convertere, vel quoniam patientes mentem convertunt ad Deum, et corpus exponunt ictibus impiorum. Prolongaverunt, id est, longam et perseverantem fecerunt, iniquitatem suam adversum me. Unde ait Scriptura : Væ qui trahitis iniquitatem in funiculis vanitatis, et quasi vinculum plaustri peccatum.
paras.en: [[128:3|The wicked have wrought upon my back|Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt peccatores]]: that is, they so subjected me to themselves, trampled on me and afflicted me, as builders subject to themselves and tread upon the foundation on which they found the building. Or, [[128:3|have wrought upon my back|Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt]]: that is, they persecuted me at their own pleasure. Or, [[128:3|have wrought upon my back|Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt]]: that is, they built up a structure of iniquity upon me, heaping up for themselves a burden of vices, or a weight and multitude of crimes, while they so unjustly molested me. And by the back the whole [person] is signified, because those who suffer words are wont to turn their back to the one who strikes them; or because the patient turn their mind to God and expose their body to the blows of the wicked.
