[[128:3|they have lengthened|Prolongaverunt]], that is, made long and persevering, [[128:3|their iniquity|iniquitatem suam]] against me. Whence the Scripture says: [[Is 5:18|Woe to you that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as the rope of a cart|Væ qui trahitis iniquitatem in funiculis vanitatis, et quasi vinculum plaustri peccatum]].

paras.t: Dominus justus, nihil irremuneratum relinquens, concidet cervices, id est, damnabit et destruet superbias, peccatorum : quemadmodum testatur : Omnium excellentium et sublimium colla calcavi. Et apud Isaiam scriptum est : Dominus exercituum cogitavit hoc, ut detraheret superbiam omnis gloriæ.
paras.en: [[128:4|The Lord who is just|Dominus justus]], leaving nothing unrequited, [[128:4|will cut the necks|concidet cervices]], that is, will condemn and destroy the prides, [[128:4|of sinners|peccatorum]]: as [Wisdom] testifies: I have trodden upon the necks of all the high and lofty[[Ecclus 24:11||]] [Denis's wording; the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have "the hearts of all the high and low"]. And in Isaias it is written: [[Is 23:9|The Lord of hosts hath designed it, to pull down the pride of all glory|Dominus exercituum cogitavit hoc, ut detraheret superbiam omnis gloriæ]] [the margin gives Is. xxxiii, 9; the words are Is 23:9].

paras.t: Confundantur confusione damnationis æternæ ac reprobationis divinæ, et convertantur retrorsum, id est, cadant, deficiant, et repellantur a Deo, omnes qui oderunt Sion, id est Ecclesiam Christi in monte, qui Christus est, sitam, atque cœlestia speculantem.
paras.en: Let them [[128:5|be confounded|Confundantur]] with the confusion of eternal damnation and of divine reprobation, [[128:5|and turned back|et convertantur retrorsum]], that is, let them fall, fail, and be driven back from God, all [[128:5|that hate Sion|qui oderunt Sion]], that is, the Church of Christ, set upon the mountain which is Christ, and gazing upon heavenly things.

paras.t: Fiant sicut fœnum tectorum, quod priusquam evellatur, exaruit : id est, quemadmodum fœnum in tectis domorum nascens, celerrime (sole desuper decoquente) siccatur et cadit ; sic potestas, gloria atque prosperitas inimicorum Ecclesiæ, Christo ulciscente, cito dispereant, ne et ipsi diu vivendo gravius peccent, et Ecclesia supra modum gravetur.
paras.en: [[128:6|Let them be as grass upon the tops of houses: which withereth before it be plucked up|Fiant sicut fœnum tectorum, quod priusquam evellatur, exaruit]]: that is, as grass growing on the roofs of houses very quickly dries up and falls (the sun scorching it from above), so may the power, glory and prosperity of the enemies of the Church quickly perish, Christ avenging, lest they themselves by living long sin more grievously, and the Church be burdened beyond measure.

paras.t: De quo fœno in tectis orto, non implebit manum suam qui metet, id est, messor tale fœnum non colliget, eo quod ante tempus dissipetur et dispergitur ; et propter eamdem causam de eo non implebit sinum suum qui manipulos colliget alibi, quam supra tectum, videlicet ubi terræ nascentia fructuose nascuntur. Et sicut de illo fœno non implet manum suam messor humanus ; sic in die judicii quando separabuntur boni a malis, angeli sancti qui sunt messores Dei, colligentes triticum (id est electos et opera bona eorum) in horreum cœli, non implebunt manum suam de operibus perversorum, quia nil boni in eis conspicient, nec deferent eos ad horreum Christi.
paras.en: Of which grass grown on the roofs [[128:7|the mower|qui metet]] [[128:7|filleth not his hand|non implebit manum suam]], that is, the reaper will not gather such grass, because it is scattered and dispersed before its time; and for the same reason [[128:7|he that gathereth sheaves|qui manipulos colliget]] elsewhere than on the roof (namely where the growth of the earth springs up fruitfully) will not fill [[128:7|his bosom|sinum suum]] with it. And as the human reaper does not fill his hand with that grass, so on the day of judgement, when the good shall be separated from the wicked[[Matt 13:49||]], the holy angels, who are the reapers of God[[Matt 13:39||]], gathering the wheat (that is, the elect and their good works) into the barn of heaven[[Matt 13:30||]], will not fill their hand with the works of the perverse, because they will see nothing good in them, and will not carry them to the barn of Christ [the margin gives Matt. xiii, 49, 30; that the reapers are the angels is v. 39].

paras.t: Et non dixerunt qui præteribant, id est, in mundo isto velut in exsilio ambulabant, festinantes ad patriam, scilicet sancti Prophetæ, Patriarchæ, Apostoli : Benedictio Domini sit super vos, o inimici Ecclesiæ : id est, Sancti non optaverunt reprobis, in quantum hujusmodi sunt, bona gratiæ, quoniam noverant eos ad corpus Antichristi atque diaboli pertinere. Unde Apostolus de talibus ait : Quos tradidi Satanæ, ut discant non blasphemare. Et Salomon loquitur : Non sit bonum impio, nec prolongentur dies ejus ; sed quasi umbra prætereant, qui non timent faciem Dei. Secundum Augustinum, consuetudo erat Hebræis ut prætereuntes benedicerent operantibus in agro, quemadmodum Booz legitur dixisse messoribus, Dominus vobiscum : qui responderunt, Benedicat tibi Dominus. Justi autem comparantur agro fecundo, impii vero sterili terræ. Innuit ergo Propheta, quod sicut prætereuntes benedicunt agro fecundo et operariis ejus, non autem sterili terræ et operantibus eam, sed potius increpant eos, quoniam stulto labore se ipsos fatigant ; sic Sancti hanc vitam spernentes, et velut locum peregrinationis hunc mundum prætereuntes, impiis non benedixerunt, sed bonis, sicut subjungitur. Benediximus vobis, o justi amatores ecclesiasticæ unitatis, id est catholicæ fidei atque individuæ caritatis, imprecantes vobis bona gratiæ in præsenti, et bona gloriæ in futuro, in nomine Domini.
paras.en: [[128:8|And they that passed by have not said|Et non dixerunt qui præteribant]], that is, those who walked in this world as in exile, hastening to the fatherland, namely the holy Prophets, Patriarchs and Apostles: [[128:8|The blessing of the Lord be upon you|Benedictio Domini sit super vos]], O enemies of the Church: that is, the Saints did not wish the goods of grace to the reprobate, in so far as they are such, since they knew them to belong to the body of Antichrist and of the devil. Whence the Apostle says of such men: [[1 Tim 1:20|whom I have delivered up to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme|Quos tradidi Satanæ, ut discant non blasphemare]]. And Solomon says: [[Eccles 8:13|let it not be well with the wicked, neither let his days be prolonged, but as a shadow let them pass away that fear not the face of the Lord|Non sit bonum impio, nec prolongentur dies ejus ; sed quasi umbra prætereant, qui non timent faciem Dei]]. According to Augustine, it was the custom among the Hebrews that passers-by should bless those working in the field, as Booz is read to have said to the reapers, [[Ruth 2:4|The Lord be with you|Dominus vobiscum]]; and they answered, [[Ruth 2:4|The Lord bless thee|Benedicat tibi Dominus]]. Now the just are compared to a fruitful field, and the wicked to barren ground. The Prophet therefore hints that, as passers-by bless a fruitful field and its labourers, but not barren ground and those who work it (rather they chide them, because they weary themselves with foolish labour), so the Saints, despising this life and passing through this world as a place of pilgrimage, did not bless the wicked, but the good, as follows: [[128:8|we have blessed you|Benediximus vobis]], O ye just, lovers of the unity of the Church, that is, of the Catholic faith and of undivided charity, wishing you the goods of grace in the present and the goods of glory in the future, [[128:8|in the name of the Lord|in nomine Domini]].

paras.t: Postremo quæ hic dicuntur contra iniquos, dicuntur zelo justitiæ, non affectu invidiæ ; magisque dicuntur prænuntiando quam imprecando, et conditionaliter magis quam simpliciter, scilicet, si non pœnitent.
paras.en: Lastly, what is said here against the wicked is said out of zeal for justice, not from a feeling of ill will; and it is said by way of foretelling rather than of imprecation, and conditionally rather than absolutely: namely, if they do not repent.

128.title: EXPOSITIO ALLEGORICA ET LITTERALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI OCTAVI.
128.title_en: Allegorical and literal exposition of the same hundred and twenty-eighth psalm.

paras.t: Convenientissime autem exponitur psalmus iste de Christo, qui est verus et purus Israelita. Eritque sensus: Sæpe expugnaverunt me Judæi a juventute mea, dicat nunc Israel, id est Christus, qui erat a principio suæ conceptionis in Virgine, vir videns Deum, non per fidem, ut ceteri; neque per subjectam creaturam, ut Jacob, qui eo quod vidit angelum, dixit, Vidi Dominum facie ad faciem (propter quod etiam Israel ab angelo dictus est): neque per imaginariam formam, ut Isaias, qui dixit, Vidi Dominum sedentem super solium excelsum; et Daniel, qui dixit, Adspiciebam donec throni positi sunt, et Antiquus dierum sedit: sed sicut comprehensores in patria vident, imo incomparabiliter clarius atque beatius. Anima etenim Christi a principio suæ creationis, semper æque perfecte vidit Deum: et ipsa sola clarius vidit Deum, quam omnes simul Beati. Idcirco Christus verissime Israel appellatur. Christum autem ab infantia persecuti sunt Judæi saltem proselyti, puta Herodes, qui erat ad Judaismum conversus, et Christum infantem occidere nisus est: cui (secundum Hieronymum) multi sacerdotum ac Judæorum consenserunt. Sumitur autem hoc loco juventus communiter, prout adolescentiam includit. Si vero proprie accipiatur, tunc Christum persecuti sunt Judæi a juventute sua, id est ab anno tricesimo suæ ætatis. Tunc nempe prædicare exorsus est; et statim ex tunc impugnaverunt eum Judæi, nunc verbis, nunc actibus, sicut Evangelistæ testantur.
paras.en: Now this psalm is most fittingly expounded of Christ, who is the true and pure Israelite. And the sense will be: [[128:1|Often have they fought against me|Sæpe expugnaverunt me]], namely the Jews, [[128:1|from my youth, let Israel now say|a juventute mea, dicat nunc Israel]]: that is, Christ, who from the beginning of his conception in the Virgin was a man seeing God [the name Israel was commonly interpreted "a man seeing God"]: not by faith, as the rest are; nor through a created thing set before him, like Jacob, who, because he had seen an angel, said, [[Gen 32:30|I have seen God face to face|Vidi Dominum facie ad faciem]] (which is also why he was called Israel by the angel[[Gen 32:28||]]); nor through an imagined form, like Isaias, who said, [[Is 6:1|I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high|Vidi Dominum sedentem super solium excelsum]], and Daniel, who said, [[Dan 7:9|I beheld till thrones were placed, and the ancient of days sat|Adspiciebam donec throni positi sunt, et Antiquus dierum sedit]]: but as the comprehensors [that is, the blessed who already possess God in glory] see him in the fatherland, nay, incomparably more clearly and more blessedly. For the soul of Christ, from the beginning of its creation, always saw God with equal perfection; and it alone saw God more clearly than all the Blessed together. Therefore Christ is most truly called Israel. Now the Jews persecuted Christ from his infancy, at least the proselytes among them, for instance Herod, who had been converted to Judaism and tried to kill the infant Christ[[Matt 2:16||]]; and with him (according to Jerome) many of the priests and Jews consented. Youth is taken here in the common way, as including adolescence. But if it is taken strictly, then the Jews persecuted Christ from his youth, that is, from the thirtieth year of his age. For then he began to preach; and from that moment the Jews fought against him, now with words, now with deeds, as the Evangelists testify.

paras.t: Etenim non potuerunt mihi prævalere. Nam quum Christum vellent præcipitare, et postmodum lapidare, exivit de manibus eorum, et transiens per medium illorum ibat. Denique, dum eum capere vellent, et ipse respondisset, Ego sum: abierunt retrorsum, et ceciderunt in terram; nec aliquid facere poterant Christo, nisi eo volente. Propter quod ait: Nemo tollit animam meam a me, sed ego pono eam. Et per Jeremiam ait: Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis: idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent et infirmi erunt.
paras.en: [[128:2|but they could not prevail over me|Etenim non potuerunt mihi prævalere]]. For when they wished to cast Christ down headlong[[Luke 4:29||]], and afterwards to stone him[[John 10:31||]], [[John 10:39|he escaped out of their hands|exivit de manibus eorum]], and [[Luke 4:30|passing through the midst of them, went his way|transiens per medium illorum ibat]]. Lastly, when they wished to seize him and he had answered, [[John 18:6|I am he; they went backward and fell to the ground|Ego sum: abierunt retrorsum, et ceciderunt in terram]]; nor could they do anything to Christ except by his will. Wherefore he says: [[John 10:18|No man taketh it away from me: but I lay it down|Nemo tollit animam meam a me, sed ego pono eam]] [Denis reads "my soul" (*animam meam*) for "it"]. And by Jeremias he says: [[Jer 20:11|the Lord is with me as a strong warrior: therefore they that persecute me shall fall, and shall be weak|Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis: idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent et infirmi erunt]].

paras.t: Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt peccatores. Hoc plane fecerunt sacrilegi impiissimique Judæi et servi Pilati, dum Christum flagellis laceraverunt, ad mortem crucem sibi bajulantem duxerunt, et duro crucis ligno dorsum ejus tenerrimum crudelissime appenderunt. Prolongaverunt iniquitatem suam: quia non cessaverunt clamare, Tolle, et, Crucifige, donec me occiderunt; imo a principio prædicationis meæ mihi insidiari cœperunt usque ad mortem, dicentes: Homo vorax, potator vini; seducit turbas; insanit, dæmonium habet; blasphemat.
paras.en: [[128:3|The wicked have wrought upon my back|Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt peccatores]]. This the sacrilegious and most impious Jews and the servants of Pilate plainly did, when they tore Christ with scourges, led him to death carrying his cross for himself, and most cruelly hung his most tender back upon the hard wood of the cross. [[128:3|they have lengthened their iniquity|Prolongaverunt iniquitatem suam]]: for they did not cease to cry out, [[John 19:15|Away with him|Tolle]], and, [[John 19:15|Crucify him|Crucifige]], until they had slain me; nay, from the beginning of my preaching they began to lie in wait for me even unto death, saying: [[Matt 11:19|a man that is a glutton and a wine drinker|Homo vorax, potator vini]]; [[John 7:12|he seduceth the people|seducit turbas]]; he [[John 10:20|is mad|insanit]], [[John 10:20|He hath a devil|dæmonium habet]]; [[Matt 9:3|He blasphemeth|blasphemat]].

paras.t: Dominus justus concidet cervices peccatorum, id est, Judæos istos destruet et occidet. Hoc fecit Deus per Titum et Romanos, quemadmodum prædictum est: Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo; et alibi, Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus.
paras.en: [[128:4|The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners|Dominus justus concidet cervices peccatorum]], that is, he will destroy and slay these Jews. This God did through Titus and the Romans, as was foretold: [[Dan 9:26|a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary|Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo]]; and elsewhere, [[Osee 9:17|My God will cast them away, because they hearkened not to him|Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus]].

paras.t: Confundantur et convertantur retrorsum, secundum sensum expositum, omnes qui oderunt Sion, id est Christum divina incessabiliter speculantem; vel, Sion, id est primitivam Christi Ecclesiam, quam maxime oderunt Judæi, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum habetur.
paras.en: [[128:5|Let them all be confounded and turned back|Confundantur et convertantur retrorsum]], in the sense expounded, [[128:5|that hate Sion|omnes qui oderunt Sion]]: that is, Christ, who unceasingly contemplates divine things [Sion was commonly interpreted "watch-tower" or "contemplation"]; or, Sion, that is, the primitive Church of Christ, which the Jews hated exceedingly, as is related in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 4:1||]] [the margin gives Act. iv, v, vi, etc.: the persecutions in Acts 4–6].

paras.t: Fiant Judæi Christum negantes, sicut fenum tectorum, etc. Hoc in eis impletum est: nam multi eorum in adolescentia et juventute a Romanis occisi sunt.
paras.en: [[128:6|Let them be|Fiant]], the Jews who deny Christ, [[128:6|as grass upon the tops of houses|sicut fenum tectorum]], etc. This was fulfilled in them: for many of them were slain by the Romans in their adolescence and youth.

paras.t: Et non dixerunt qui præteribant, id est Prophetæ: Benedictio Domini super vos: id est, Prophetæ nil boni dixerunt de Judæis qui Christum occiderunt, sed multa mala, quemadmodum patescit, ubi de eis sic dicitur: Non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est, id est Judæi qui dixerunt: Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem; et, Hunc nescimus unde est. Et: Exosos habui eos propter malitiam adinventionum eorum; et rursus: Negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt, Non est ipse. Per Isaiam quoque Dominus ait: Excæcatum est cor populi hujus. Sed nos Prophetæ qui istis incredulis maledixìmus, benedixìmus vobis, o Christiani, in nomine Domini, scilicet Christi prophetando de vestra salute et gratia. Hinc enim beatissimus Petrus in sua Canonica alloquens Christianos, disseruit: De vestra salute exquisierunt atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui de futura in vobis gratia prophetaverunt.
paras.en: [[128:8|And they that passed by have not said|Et non dixerunt qui præteribant]], that is, the Prophets: [[128:8|The blessing of the Lord be upon you|Benedictio Domini super vos]]: that is, the Prophets said nothing good of the Jews who slew Christ, but many evil things, as is plain where it is said of them thus: [[Dan 9:26|the people that shall deny him shall not be his|Non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est]]; that is, the Jews who said: [[John 19:15|We have no king but Caesar|Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem]] [the margin gives Joann. xi, 15, evidently for xix, 15]; and, [[John 9:29|as to this man, we know not from whence he is|Hunc nescimus unde est]]. And: [[Osee 9:15|there I hated them: for the wickedness of their devices|Exosos habui eos propter malitiam adinventionum eorum]]; and again: [[Jer 5:12|They have denied the Lord, and said, It is not he|Negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt, Non est ipse]] [no margin reference; the words are Jer 5:12]. By Isaias also the Lord says: [[Is 6:10|Blind the heart of this people|Excæcatum est cor populi hujus]] [Denis has "the heart of this people has been blinded"; no margin reference]. But we Prophets, who have cursed these unbelievers, [[128:8|we have blessed you|benedixìmus vobis]], O Christians, [[128:8|in the name of the Lord|in nomine Domini]], that is, of Christ, by prophesying of your salvation and grace. Hence the most blessed Peter, addressing Christians in his canonical Epistle, declared: [[1 Pet 1:10|Of which salvation the prophets have inquired and diligently searched, who prophesied of the grace to come in you|De vestra salute exquisierunt atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui de futura in vobis gratia prophetaverunt]] [Denis reads "Of your salvation"].

paras.t: Præterea, quamvis sensus litteralis in primo ponendus sit, propter rationabilem tamen causam, videlicet propter prolixitatem vitandam, interdum pono eum posterius. Itaque ad litteram videtur psalmus præsens loqui de frequenti tribulatione ac liberatione Israeliticæ plebis, ut sit sensus: Sæpe expugnaverunt me a juventute mea, dicat nunc Israel: id est, populus Israel dictus, eo quod natus sit ex Jacob, alias alio nomine Israel, fateatur cum gratiarum actione quod sæpe expugnaverunt me gentiles a juventute mea, id est a tempore quo fui in Ægypto: quod dicitur juventus populi hujus, secundum quod Dominus ait apud Jeremiam ad Synagogam: Recordatus sum tui, miserans adolescentiam tuam, quando secuta es me in deserto.
paras.en: Moreover, although the literal sense ought to be set first, yet for a reasonable cause, namely to avoid prolixity, I sometimes place it afterwards. So, according to the letter, the present psalm seems to speak of the frequent tribulation and deliverance of the Israelite people, so that the sense is: [[128:1|Often have they fought against me from my youth, let Israel now say|Sæpe expugnaverunt me a juventute mea, dicat nunc Israel]]: that is, the people called Israel, because it was born of Jacob, otherwise named Israel[[Gen 32:28||]], let it acknowledge with thanksgiving that the gentiles have often fought against me from my youth, that is, from the time when I was in Egypt: which is called the youth of this people, as the Lord says to the Synagogue in Jeremias: [[Jer 2:2|I have remembered thee, pitying thy youth|Recordatus sum tui, miserans adolescentiam tuam]], [[Jer 2:2|when thou followedst me in the desert|quando secuta es me in deserto]].

paras.t: Etenim non potuerunt mihi prævalere. Nam Ægyptii qui eos impugnaverunt, succubuerunt, dicentes: Fugiamus Israelem; Dominus enim pugnat pro eis contra nos.
paras.en: [[128:2|but they could not prevail over me|Etenim non potuerunt mihi prævalere]]. For the Egyptians who fought against them gave way, saying: [[Ex 14:25|Let us flee from Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against us|Fugiamus Israelem; Dominus enim pugnat pro eis contra nos]].

paras.t: Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt peccatores, puta Ægyptii, imponentes mihi onera gravissima ad portandum. Babylonii quoque et alii multi fabricaverunt super dorsum eorum, secundum sensum prætactum.
paras.en: [[128:3|The wicked have wrought upon my back|Supra dorsum meum fabricaverunt peccatores]], for instance the Egyptians, laying most heavy burdens upon me to carry[[Ex 1:11||]][[Ex 1:14||]]. The Babylonians also, and many others, wrought upon their back, in the sense touched on before.

paras.t: Dominus justus concidet cervices peccatorum. Nam Ægyptios superbissimos, aliosque Israelem persequentes, graviter interfecit, atque in die judicii penitus eos damnabit et dissipabit.
paras.en: [[128:4|The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners|Dominus justus concidet cervices peccatorum]]. For he grievously slew the most proud Egyptians[[Ex 14:27||]][[Ex 14:28||]], and others who persecuted Israel, and in the day of judgment he will utterly damn and scatter them.

paras.t: Confundantur et convertantur retrorsum, quasi debellati et victi a Deo, omnes qui oderunt Sion, id est populum Judæorum per Sion significatum; vel, Sion, id est sanctuarium Dei constructum in monte Sion.
paras.en: [[128:5|Let them all be confounded and turned back|Confundantur et convertantur retrorsum]], as though vanquished and conquered by God, [[128:5|that hate Sion|omnes qui oderunt Sion]]: that is, the people of the Jews signified by Sion; or, Sion, that is, the sanctuary of God built on mount Sion.

paras.t: Et non dixerunt qui præteribant, id est sancti viri hunc mundum perambulantes: Benedictio Domini super vos: id est, odientibus Sion non sunt imprecati benedictionem, sed futuram eorum damnationem prælocuti sunt. Unde nec eis dixerunt: benedixìmus vobis in nomine Domini. Cetera patent ex dictis.
paras.en: [[128:8|And they that passed by have not said|Et non dixerunt qui præteribant]], that is, holy men walking through this world: [[128:8|The blessing of the Lord be upon you|Benedictio Domini super vos]]: that is, they did not call down a blessing on those who hate Sion, but foretold their future damnation. Hence neither did they say to them: [[128:8|we have blessed you in the name of the Lord|benedixìmus vobis in nomine Domini]]. The rest is plain from what has been said.

paras.t: Precatio. Bello et terrore spiritualis nequitiæ a juventute sua impugnatam Ecclesiam, Domine, fac de inimicis potenter triumphare: ut humiliatis cervicibus eorum, gaudium et lætitiam per te obtineat in sempiternum.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, make thy Church, assailed from her youth by the war and terror of spiritual wickedness, to triumph mightily over her enemies: that, their necks being humbled, she may obtain through thee joy and gladness for evermore.

129.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI VICESIMI NONI : DE PROFUNDIS CLAMAVI.
129.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and twenty-ninth psalm: Out of the depths I have cried.

paras.t: Psalmi præsentis titulus est: Canticum graduum. Hic enim psalmus est undecimus in ordine gradualium psalmorum, tractans de undecimo gradu spiritualis ascensionis, videlicet de pœnitentiali prece ad Dominum: quoniam omnis homo, quantumcumque sit justus et patiens, indiget divinam misericordiam quotidie implorare pro quotidianis excessibus, seu malis præteritis.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is: [[129:1|A gradual canticle|Canticum graduum]]. For this psalm is the eleventh in the order of the gradual psalms, and treats of the eleventh step of the spiritual ascent, namely of penitential prayer to the Lord: since every man, however just and patient he may be, needs to implore the divine mercy daily for his daily excesses, or for his past evils.

paras.t: Ait ergo Propheta in persona hominis pœnitentis: De profundis, id est de hac valle lacrimarum, de corpore isto mortali, de intimo cordis affectu, de tribulationibus multis et magna voragine vitiorum, clamavi ad te, Domine, tuam misericordiam implorando; Domine, exaudi vocem meam, dando quod postulo. Fiant aures tuæ intendentes in vocem deprecationis meæ, id est, misericordia et sapientia tua pie attendant quæ deprecor. Sæpe resumit eumdem sensum sub aliis verbis, ad insinuandum cordis sui æstuantem affectum, et ut ex iteratione desiderii mens accendatur.
paras.en: The Prophet therefore says, in the person of a penitent man: [[129:1|Out of the depths|De profundis]], that is, out of this vale of tears, out of this mortal body, out of the inmost affection of the heart, out of many tribulations and the great whirlpool of vices, [[129:1|I have cried to thee, O Lord|clamavi ad te, Domine]], imploring thy mercy; [[129:2|Lord, hear my voice|Domine, exaudi vocem meam]], by granting what I ask. [[129:2|Let thy ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication|Fiant aures tuæ intendentes in vocem deprecationis meæ]], that is, let thy mercy and wisdom kindly attend to what I pray for. He often takes up the same sense again in other words, to convey the burning affection of his heart, and so that the mind may be kindled by the repetition of its desire.

paras.t: Si iniquitates observaveris, Domine, id est, si peccatorum nostrorum oblivisci nolueris, si eorum enormitatem perpenderis, si ea secundum justitiam tuam ulcisci volueris, Domine, quis sustinebit? id est, quis poterit tantum rigorem sufferre? quis poterit coram te stare, salvusque fieri? tanquam dicat, Nullus. Unde primo Regum habetur: Quis poterit stare ante conspectum Domini Dei hujus?
paras.en: [[129:3|If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities|Si iniquitates observaveris, Domine]], that is, if thou wilt not forget our sins, if thou weigh their enormity, if thou wilt avenge them according to thy justice, [[129:3|Lord, who shall stand it|Domine, quis sustinebit]]? that is, who will be able to bear so great a rigour? who will be able to stand before thee, and be saved? as if to say, No one. Hence it is found in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 6:20|Who shall be able to stand before the Lord|Quis poterit stare ante conspectum Domini]] this God?

paras.t: Quia apud te propitiatio est, id est, in te misericordia et miseratio magna est, et miserationes tuæ super omnia opera tua: quemadmodum alibi dicitur: Convertimini ad Dominum Deum vestrum, quia benignus et misericors est, patiens et multæ misericordiæ, et præstabilis super malitia. Et propter legem tuam, id est propter testimonia sacræ Scripturæ, tuam misericordiam pœnitentibus promittentis, sicut quum dicis: Convertimini ad me, et convertar ad vos; et iterum, Si fuerint peccata vestra ut coccinum, quasi nix dealbabuntur; sustinui te, Domine, id est, tua flagella æquanimiter pertuli, tuæ exauditionis dilationem longanimiter et fiducialiter præstolabar, tuam clementiam exspectavi: quemadmodum apud Isaiam legitur: Ecce Deus noster; exspectavimus eum, et salvabit nos; sustinuimus eum, et lætabimur in salutari ejus.
paras.en: [[129:4|For with thee there is merciful forgiveness|Quia apud te propitiatio est]], that is, in thee is mercy and great compassion, and [[Ps 144:9|his tender mercies are over all his works|miserationes tuæ super omnia opera tua]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlv, 9; the words are those of Ps 144:9, here turned to the second person, “thy tender mercies … thy works”]: as it is said elsewhere: [[Joel 2:13|turn to the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, patient and rich in mercy, and ready to repent of the evil|Convertimini ad Dominum Deum vestrum, quia benignus et misericors est, patiens et multæ misericordiæ, et præstabilis super malitia]]. [[129:4|and by reason of thy law|Et propter legem tuam]], that is, by reason of the testimonies of Sacred Scripture, which promises thy mercy to penitents, as when thou sayest: [[Zach 1:3|Turn ye to me|Convertimini ad me]], [[Zach 1:3|and I will turn to you|et convertar ad vos]]; and again, [[Is 1:18|if your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made as white as snow|Si fuerint peccata vestra ut coccinum, quasi nix dealbabuntur]]; [[129:4|I have waited for thee, O Lord|sustinui te, Domine]], that is, I have borne thy scourges with an even mind, I have looked for the delay of thy hearing me with long-suffering and with trust, I have awaited thy clemency: as we read in Isaias: [[Is 25:9|Lo, this is our God, we have waited for him, and he will save us|Ecce Deus noster; exspectavimus eum, et salvabit nos]]; [[Is 25:9|we have patiently waited for him, we shall rejoice and be joyful in his salvation|sustinuimus eum, et lætabimur in salutari ejus]].

paras.t: Sustinuit anima mea in verbo ejus: id est, ex sacra Scriptura recepit anima mea fiduciam sustinendi Deum, et in verbo divinæ promissionis confisa est, plenissime sciens, quoniam quod promisit, potens est adimplere; speravit anima mea in Domino, non in meritis propriis aut rebus creatis.
paras.en: [[129:4|My soul hath relied on his word|Sustinuit anima mea in verbo ejus]]: that is, from Sacred Scripture my soul has received the confidence to wait for God, and has trusted in the word of the divine promise, [[Rom 4:21|Most fully knowing that whatsoever he has promised, he is able also to perform|plenissime sciens, quoniam quod promisit, potens est adimplere]]; [[129:5|my soul hath hoped in the Lord|speravit anima mea in Domino]], not in its own merits or in created things.

paras.t: A custodia matutina usque ad noctem, id est de mane usque ad vesperam, a principio usque ad finem, a juventute usque ad mortis occasum, speret Israel, id est homo fidelis, seu populus christianus Deum fide pura contemplans, in Domino.
paras.en: [[129:6|From the morning watch even until night|A custodia matutina usque ad noctem]], that is, from morning until evening, from the beginning to the end, from youth until the setting of death, [[129:6|let Israel hope|speret Israel]], that is, the faithful man, or the Christian people, contemplating God with pure faith, [[129:6|in the Lord|in Domino]].

paras.t: Quia apud Dominum misericordia, id est, in Deo est pietas magna, quippe cui proprium est misereri et parcere; et copiosa apud eum redemptio est: quoniam ipse valde potens et clemens est ad indulgendum, subveniendum, atque salvandum; nec deficit ejus virtus in redimendo. Propter quod Moyses ait: Dominator Domine, misericors et clemens, patiens et multæ misericordiæ ac verus, qui custodis misericordiam in millia, qui aufers iniquitatem et scelera atque peccata. Et iterum dicit Scriptura: Ecce non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare nequeat; neque aggravata est auris ejus, ut non exaudiat. Est ergo apud Dominum, in Domino, et a Domino, copiosa redemptio, id est magna virtus ad liberandum, quæ est activa redemptio, causans in nobis redemptionem passivam qua liberamur.
paras.en: [[129:7|Because with the Lord there is mercy|Quia apud Dominum misericordia]], that is, in God there is great pity, since it is proper to him to have mercy and to spare; [[129:7|and with him plentiful redemption|et copiosa apud eum redemptio]]: for he is exceedingly mighty and merciful to pardon, to succour and to save; nor does his power fail in redeeming. Wherefore Moses says: [[Ex 34:6|O the Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient and of much compassion, and true|Dominator Domine, misericors et clemens, patiens et multæ misericordiæ ac verus]], [[Ex 34:7|Who keepest mercy unto thousands: who takest away iniquity, and wickedness, and sin|qui custodis misericordiam in millia, qui aufers iniquitatem et scelera atque peccata]]. And again Scripture says: [[Is 59:1|Behold the hand of the Lord is not shortened that it cannot save, neither is his ear heavy that it cannot hear|Ecce non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare nequeat; neque aggravata est auris ejus, ut non exaudiat]]. There is therefore with the Lord, in the Lord, and from the Lord, plentiful redemption, that is, great power to set free, which is active redemption, causing in us the passive redemption by which we are set free [that is, redemption as God works it, and redemption as we receive it].

paras.t: Et ipse redimet Israel in se sperantem: de quo jam dictum est; ex omnibus iniquitatibus ejus, dimittendo ei universa peccata per gratiam suam. Vel dicitur apud Dominum Christum copiosa redemptio, id est efficacissimum atque plenissimum meritum redimendi: nam sua passione meruit copiosam redimendi efficaciam; et ipse redemit Israel ex omnibus iniquitatibus ejus, satisfaciendo in cruce pro nostris peccatis, nosque proprio sanguine redimendo: sicut in Evangelio loquitur, Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis; et in Isaia scriptum est, Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et dolores nostros ipse portavit.
paras.en: [[129:8|And he shall redeem Israel|Et ipse redimet Israel]], hoping in him, of whom it has just been spoken, [[129:8|from all his iniquities|ex omnibus iniquitatibus ejus]], forgiving him all his sins through his grace. Or, plentiful redemption is said to be with the Lord Christ, that is, a most efficacious and most full merit of redeeming: for by his passion he merited a plentiful efficacy of redeeming; and he redeemed Israel from all his iniquities, making satisfaction on the cross for our sins, and redeeming us with his own blood: as he says in the Gospel, [[John 10:15|I lay down my life for my sheep|Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]; and in Isaias it is written, [[Is 53:4|Surely he hath borne our infirmities and carried our sorrows|Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et dolores nostros ipse portavit]].

paras.t: Ecce hic psalmus qui pœnitentialium psalmorum sextus est, pia devotione plenus exsistens, tanto attentius affectuosiusque cantandus est quanto nobis misericordiam Dei peculiarius recolit et commendat, et quanto personæ pœnitentium congruentius competit. Clamemus de profundo nostræ cæcitatis ad sublimitatem divinæ lucis. Invocet abyssus nostræ miseriæ abyssum pietatis divinæ. Cognoscamus nos in judicio cum Deo non posse contendere, juxta illud: Non justificabitur homo compositus Deo; et si voluerit cum eo contendere, non poterit respondere unum pro mille. Iterum ergo conemur placare Deum creatorem, salvatorem ac judicem nostrum, orando, meditando, legendo, sacrificium laudis offerendo: et quod super omnia est, in divino atque fraterno amore proficiendo, quoniam caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum.
paras.en: Behold, this psalm, which is the sixth of the penitential psalms, being full of loving devotion, is to be sung the more attentively and affectionately, the more particularly it recalls and commends to us the mercy of God, and the more fittingly it suits the person of penitents. Let us cry out of the depth of our blindness to the height of the divine light. Let the abyss of our misery call upon the abyss of the divine pity[[Ps 41:8||]]. Let us acknowledge that we cannot contend with God in judgment, according to that saying: [[Job 9:2|man cannot be justified, compared with God|Non justificabitur homo compositus Deo]]; and [[Job 9:3|If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one for a thousand|si voluerit cum eo contendere, non poterit respondere unum pro mille]]. Let us therefore strive again to appease God, our creator, saviour and judge, by praying, meditating, reading, offering the sacrifice of praise; and, what is above all, by advancing in the love of God and of our brethren, because [[1 Pet 4:8|charity covereth a multitude of sins|caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum]].

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, apud quem est misericordia et redemptio copiosa, redime nos ab iniquitatibus nostris, et in plenitudine sanctæ devotionis, fac nos tuis semper deservire præceptis.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, with whom is mercy and plentiful redemption, redeem us from our iniquities, and make us ever to serve thy commandments in the fulness of holy devotion.

130.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI : DOMINE, NON EST EXALTATUM COR MEUM.
130.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and thirtieth psalm: Lord, my heart is not exalted.

paras.t: Præscribitur psalmo jam declarando: Canticum graduum, ipsi David. Loquitur enim psalmus iste de duodecimo gradu spiritualis ascensus, videlicet de humilitate, sine qua nulla virtus habetur aut conservatur. Nam et pœnitentia sine ea non prodest. Quamvis autem humilitas sit basis et fundamentum spiritualis profectus, tamen humilitas talis ac tanta, qualis et quanta in hoc psalmo describitur, merito ponitur gradus duodecimus. Loquitur ergo Propheta in persona hominis virtuosi, qui suam perfectionem non jactanter, sed ad gloriam Dei ædificationemque Christi profitetur. Secundum quem modum Sancti frequenter propria bona describunt, ut Paulus qui ait, Plus omnibus laboravi; et Job qui dicit, Neque reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea; et Ezechias qui loquitur, Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te corde perfecto. Quod sancti viri interdum faciunt, quatenus citius exaudiantur; non tamen in suis virtutibus principaliter sperant, præsertim quum sciant sua merita esse dona divina.
paras.en: The psalm now to be explained has the title: [[130:1|A gradual canticle of David|Canticum graduum, ipsi David]]. For this psalm speaks of the twelfth step of the spiritual ascent, namely of humility, without which no virtue is had or kept. For even penance is of no profit without it. And although humility is the base and foundation of spiritual progress, yet humility such and so great as is described in this psalm is rightly placed as the twelfth step. The Prophet therefore speaks in the person of a virtuous man, who professes his own perfection not boastfully, but to the glory of God and the edification of Christ [that is, the building up of Christ's body, the Church]. In which manner the Saints often describe their own good things: as Paul, who says, [[1 Cor 15:10|I have laboured more abundantly than all they|Plus omnibus laboravi]]; and Job, who says, [[Job 27:6|my heart doth not reprehend me in all my life|Neque reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea]]; and Ezechias, who says, [[Is 38:3|remember how I have walked before thee|Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te]] [[Is 38:3|with a perfect heart|corde perfecto]]. Holy men sometimes do this so that they may be heard the sooner; yet they do not hope chiefly in their own virtues, especially since they know that their merits are divine gifts.

paras.t: In talis itaque hominis persona loquens Propheta, ait: Domine, inquit, non est exaltatum cor meum tumore superbiæ, gloriando in se, aut sibi adscribendo quod tibi attribuendum est, aut præferendo se aliis. Unde David alibi testatur: Vilior fiam plus quam factus sum, et ero humilis in oculis meis. Neque elati sunt oculi mei, id est, interior cordis elatio non ascendit neque apparuit in oculis corporis: ubi maxime apparere consuevit. Sic ergo nec intus nec foris, nec vere nec apparenter, superbivit. Hinc quippe scriptum est: Quid te elevat cor tuum, et quasi magna cogitans, attonitos habes oculos? Quid tumet contra Deum spiritus tuus? Contra Deum enim tumet omnis superbus. Propter quod dicitur in Proverbiis: Abominatio est Domino omnis arrogans.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of such a man, the Prophet says: [[130:1|Lord|Domine]], he says, [[130:1|my heart is not exalted|non est exaltatum cor meum]] with the swelling of pride, by glorying in itself, or ascribing to itself what is to be attributed to thee, or preferring itself to others. Hence David testifies elsewhere: I will [[2 Kings 6:22|make myself meaner than I have done|Vilior fiam plus quam factus sum]], [[2 Kings 6:22|and I will be little in my own eyes|et ero humilis in oculis meis]]. [[130:1|nor are my eyes lofty|Neque elati sunt oculi mei]], that is, the inward elation of the heart has not risen up nor appeared in the eyes of the body, where it is most wont to appear. So, then, neither within nor without, neither in truth nor in appearance, was he proud. For hence it is written: [[Job 15:12|Why doth thy heart elevate thee, and why dost thou stare with thy eyes, as if they were thinking great things?|Quid te elevat cor tuum, et quasi magna cogitans, attonitos habes oculos?]] [[Job 15:13|Why doth thy spirit swell against God|Quid tumet contra Deum spiritus tuus]]? For every proud man swells against God. Wherefore it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 16:5|Every proud man is an abomination to the Lord|Abominatio est Domino omnis arrogans]].

paras.t: Neque ambulavi in magnis, faciendo opera meam mensuram transcendentia, seu inter proximos superbe vivendo, aut me inaniter ostendendo; neque in mirabilibus super me: id est, non quæsivi facere opera rara, miranda; nec ea optavi, per quæ hominibus mirabilis apparerem. Sed nec præsumpsi esse scrutator majestatis, aut supernaturalia fidei testimonia meo ingenio mensurare: quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico legitur: Altiora te ne quæsieris, et fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris; sed quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper. Et Apostolus dicit: Non alta sapientes, sed humilibus consentientes. Hæc tamen atque similia quædam ignavi et derisores studiosorum, multum perverse intelligunt, putantes hæc ideo dici, quasi non debeamus mysteria fidei perscrutari, et conari quantum possibile est, intelligere alta de fide: quum tamen Apostolus dicat, Crescite in scientia Dei; et Christus, Scrutamini (ait) Scripturas. Denique sanctissimi patres nostri, Hieronymus, Augustinus, Hilarius, Thomas, nonne difficillima loca Scripturæ conati sunt explanare, supernaturalia utcumque cognoscere?
paras.en: [[130:1|Neither have I walked in great matters|Neque ambulavi in magnis]], by doing works that go beyond my measure, or by living proudly among my neighbours, or by vainly showing myself off; [[130:1|nor in wonderful things above me|neque in mirabilibus super me]]: that is, I have not sought to do rare and marvellous works, nor have I desired those things by which I might appear marvellous to men. Nor have I presumed to be a searcher of majesty [that is, one who pries into the majesty of God], or to measure the supernatural testimonies of faith by my own wit: as we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 3:22|Seek not the things that are too high for thee, and search not into things above thy ability: but the things that God hath commanded thee, think on them always|Altiora te ne quæsieris, et fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris; sed quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper]]. And the Apostle says: [[Rom 12:16|Not minding high things, but consenting to the humble|Non alta sapientes, sed humilibus consentientes]]. Yet these and some similar sayings the slothful, and those who mock the studious, understand very perversely, thinking that they are said as though we ought not to search into the mysteries of the faith, and to try, as far as is possible, to understand high things of the faith: whereas the Apostle says, [[Col 1:10|increasing in the knowledge of God|Crescite in scientia Dei]] [Denis has crescite, “grow”, where Col 1:10 has crescentes, “increasing”; compare 2 Pet 3:18]; and Christ, [[John 5:39|Search the scriptures|Scrutamini (ait) Scripturas]], he says. Lastly, our most holy fathers, Jerome, Augustine, Hilary, Thomas, did they not strive to explain the most difficult passages of Scripture, and to know supernatural things as far as they could?

paras.t: Si non humiliter sentiebam, humiliando me intus et foris, et coram Deo atque hominibus, sed exaltari animam meam, reputando me aliquid esse, quum nihil sim; Sicut ablactatus supra matrem suam, ita retributio in animam meam: id est, tunc retribuatur et fiat animæ meæ a te, sicut fit puero ablactato, incumbenti supra ubera matris suæ: quatenus, sicut puer talis quærit ubera sugere, et non potest, sed dolet, plangitque atque repellitur; sic ego a te internam consolationem non acquiram, nec ubera æternæ Sapientiæ sugam, sed tanquam indignus abjiciar. Hæc autem dicit potius prænuntiando quid futurum sit, si intumescat, quam sibi ipsi mala imprecando.
paras.en: [[130:2|If I was not humbly minded|Si non humiliter sentiebam]], humbling myself within and without, both before God and before men, [[130:2|but exalted my soul|sed exaltari animam meam]], reckoning myself to be something, whereas I am nothing[[Gal 6:3||]]; [[130:2|As a child that is weaned is towards his mother, so reward in my soul|Sicut ablactatus supra matrem suam, ita retributio in animam meam]]: that is, then let it be repaid and done to my soul by thee as it is done to a weaned child lying upon his mother's breasts: so that, as such a child seeks to suck the breasts and cannot, but grieves and wails and is pushed away; so may I not obtain inward consolation from thee, nor suck the breasts of the eternal Wisdom, but be cast off as unworthy. Yet he says this rather by foretelling what would happen if he were to swell with pride, than by calling down evils upon himself.

paras.t: Speret Israel, id est fidelis, in Domino, ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum, id est indesinenter, quamdiu in isto exsilio degit. Non enim in patria sperat aliquis in Deo, quia nec fides nec spes permanent in Beatis.
paras.en: [[130:3|Let Israel hope|Speret Israel]], that is, the faithful man, [[130:3|in the Lord, from henceforth now and for ever|in Domino, ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum]], that is, unceasingly, as long as he lives in this exile. For in the fatherland no one hopes in God, since neither faith nor hope remains in the Blessed.

paras.t: Ecce dum psalmum hunc cantamus, de nostra superbia erubescamus, quid humilitatis nobis desit pensemus, atque ad veræ humilitatis amorem accendamur, eamque adipisci fideliter jugiterque conemur. Nam et Christus inter beatitudines gradum humilitatis primum locavit, dicens: Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum. Et iterum ait: Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde. Et Apostolus: Honore, inquit, invicem prævenientes. Et iterum: Subjecti estote invicem in timore Dei. Ad Philippenses quoque saluberrime exhortatur: Nihil agite per contentionem, neque per inanem gloriam, sed in humilitate superiores invicem arbitrantes.
paras.en: Behold, while we sing this psalm, let us blush for our pride, let us weigh what humility we lack, and be kindled to the love of true humility, and strive faithfully and constantly to attain it. For Christ too placed the step of humility first among the beatitudes, saying: [[Matt 5:3|Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven|Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum]]. And again he says: [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]. And the Apostle: [[Rom 12:10|with honour preventing one another|Honore, inquit, invicem prævenientes]], he says. And again: [[Eph 5:21|Being subject one to another|Subjecti estote invicem]], in the fear of God. To the Philippians too he most wholesomely exhorts: [[Phil 2:3|Let nothing be done through contention: neither by vain glory. But in humility, let each esteem others better than themselves:|Nihil agite per contentionem, neque per inanem gloriam, sed in humilitate superiores invicem arbitrantes]]

paras.t: Precatio. Virtute fulti, Domine, sanctæ majestatis tuæ, non sit exaltatum cor nostrum, oculi nostri non elati; non in magnis neque in mirabilibus super nos ambulemus, sed semper humilia sentiamus: quo perpetim sæculorum tempore tibi placeamus.
paras.en: Prayer. Upheld, O Lord, by the power of thy holy majesty, let not our heart be exalted, nor our eyes lofty; let us not walk in great matters nor in wonderful things above us, but let us ever be humbly minded: that through all the ages of eternity we may please thee.

131.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and thirty-first psalm: O Lord, remember David.
131.note: The heading of this article (its Latin title) is missing from the transcription; the English title is supplied.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi præsentis est : Canticum graduum. Loquitur jam psalmus iste de tertiodecimo gradu spiritualis ascensionis, videlicet de spirituali ædificatione domus interioris, quæ est anima sancta : quæ dum virtutibus adornatur, domus Christi efficitur. Quamvis autem quidam doctores magni atque catholici videantur prætendere, quod psalmus iste non loquatur ad litteram de rege David filio Jesse, sed Christo per David significato ; tamen ex verbis Hieronymi elucescit, quod psalmus iste ad litteram loquatur de David. Ait enim in quadam homilia, quod ad Abraham et David specialiter facta est de Christo repromissio : Ad David, De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam : quæ sunt verba psalmi præsentis. Alii quoque doctores catholici ita exponunt hunc psalmum, quos verum dicere reor. Loquitur autem David in psalmo isto, præcipue de duobus, videlicet de affectu seu devotione sui ad ædificandum Domino templum, et de promissione sibi facta, de successione suæ posteritatis, quantum ad regnum.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is: [[131:1|A gradual canticle|Canticum graduum]]. This psalm now speaks of the thirteenth step of the spiritual ascent, namely of the spiritual building of the inner house, which is the holy soul: for when it is adorned with virtues, it becomes the house of Christ. And although certain great and catholic doctors seem to maintain that this psalm does not speak literally of King David, the son of Jesse, but of Christ signified by David, yet it is clear from the words of Jerome that this psalm speaks literally of David. For he says in a certain homily that the promise of Christ was made in a special way to Abraham and to David: to David, [[131:11|of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne|De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam]]; and these are words of the present psalm. Other catholic doctors also expound this psalm in this way, and I judge that they say what is true. Now in this psalm David speaks chiefly of two things: namely, of his affection or devotion toward building a temple to the Lord, and of the promise made to him concerning the succession of his posterity in the kingdom.

paras.t: Ait ergo, orans pro semetipso : Memento, Domine, David, miserendo sibi in omnibus : prout ab Esdra dicitur, Memento mei, Deus meus, in bonum. Non quod in Deo cadat oblivio, aut recens memoria, sicut ubertim præhabitum est. Et omnis mansuetudinis ejus : id est, mititatem ejus habe acceptam, et propter eam exaudi famulum tuum David. Erat namque David multum mansuetus : quod constat ex eo, quod adversariis suis tam pie pepercit, puta Sauli et Semei ; pro Absalone quoque præcepit ne occideretur : quæ patent primo et secundo libris Regum. Unde Dionysius in epistola ad Demophilum monachum, asserit David merito suæ mansuetudinis maximam apud Deum gratiam invenisse.
paras.en: He says, then, praying for himself: [[131:1|O Lord, remember David|Memento, Domine, David]], by having mercy on him in all things; as is said by Esdras [in the second book of Esdras, which other Bibles call Nehemias]: [[2 Esd 5:19|Remember me, O my God, for good|Memento mei, Deus meus, in bonum]]. Not that forgetfulness, or a fresh remembering, can befall God, as has been fully shown before. [[131:1|and all his meekness|Et omnis mansuetudinis ejus]]: that is, hold his mildness acceptable, and for its sake hear thy servant David. For David was very meek: which is plain from his having spared his adversaries so tenderly, Saul for instance[[1 Kings 24:8||]][[1 Kings 26:9||]] and Semei[[2 Kings 16:10||]]; and for Absalom too he gave orders that he should not be slain[[2 Kings 18:5||]]: all of which is plain in the first and second books of Kings. Hence Dionysius, in his letter to the monk Demophilus, affirms that by the merit of his meekness David found the greatest grace with God.

paras.t: Ad hoc autem memento ejus, o Domine, ut impleat, Sicut juravit Domino, et sicut votum vovit Deo Jacob patriarchæ. Qualiter autem juravit et vovit, subjungitur. Si introiero in tabernaculum domus meæ, id est, non ingrediar domum meam, ut in ea repausem, et a proposito meo desistam ; si ascendero, id est, non ascendam, in lectum strati mei, ut in eo dormiam, quiescens et cessans ab exsecutione voti et juramenti. Sicut autem domus et tabernaculum domus idem sunt ; sic stratum et lectus strati idem significant. Juxta quem modum dicit Apostolus : Corporis carnis. Si dedero, id est, non dabo, somnum oculis meis, et palpebris meis dormitationem non dabo, quasi desinens a proposito ; Et requiem temporibus meis non dabo, id est, non quiescam toto tempore vitæ meæ ; donec inveniam locum Domino. In isto versiculo tangitur, quid vovit atque juravit : et est sensus, Donec inveniam locum Domino, id est ad Dei honorem, in quo sibi templum ædificem. Ideo additur : tabernaculum Deo Jacob, id est, donec construam templum Deo patris nostri, sancti Jacob ; sicque illo constructo, inveniam illud ad libitum, ad colendum Deum in ipso.
paras.en: And remember him, O Lord, to this end, that he may fulfil it, [[131:2|How he swore to the Lord|Sicut juravit Domino]], and how [[131:2|he vowed a vow to the God of Jacob|votum vovit Deo Jacob]] the patriarch. And how he swore and vowed is added: [[131:3|If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house|Si introiero in tabernaculum domus meæ]], that is, I will not go into my house to rest in it and give up my purpose; [[131:3|if I shall go up|si ascendero]], that is, I will not go up, [[131:3|into the bed wherein I lie|in lectum strati mei]], to sleep in it, resting and ceasing from the carrying out of my vow and oath. And as *house* and *tabernacle of the house* are the same, so *couch* and *bed of the couch* mean the same [Latin *stratum* and *lectus strati*; the Douay-Rheims renders the phrase "the bed wherein I lie"]. In the same way the Apostle says: [[Col 2:11|the body of the flesh|Corporis carnis]][[Col 1:22||]]. [[131:4|If I shall give|Si dedero]], that is, I will not give, [[131:4|sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids|somnum oculis meis, et palpebris meis dormitationem]] I will not give, as though leaving off my purpose; [[131:5|Or rest to my temples|Et requiem temporibus meis]] I will not give, that is, I will not rest the whole time of my life; [[131:5|until I find out a place for the Lord|donec inveniam locum Domino]]. In this verse is touched what he vowed and swore; and the sense is: [[131:5|until I find out a place for the Lord|Donec inveniam locum Domino]], that is, for the honour of God, in which I may build him a temple. Therefore it is added: [[131:5|a tabernacle for the God of Jacob|tabernaculum Deo Jacob]], that is, until I build a temple to the God of our father, holy Jacob; and so, once it is built, I may find it at will, to worship God in it.

paras.t: Sed quoniam David ædificare non potuit templum, eo quod multum sanguinem fudit, numquid perjurus est ? Et respondendum, quod David hæc vovit atque juravit, supposita voluntate divina : et ergo bona voluntas sibi pro opere reputabatur. Filio autem ejus concessum est implere quod ipse proposuit. Unde Dominus ait : Quod cogitasti in corde tuo ædificare domum nomini meo, bene fecisti, hoc ipsum mente pertractans ; verumtamen tu non ædificabis mihi domum, sed filius tuus.
paras.en: But since David could not build the temple[[1 Par 22:7||]], because he had shed much blood[[1 Par 22:8||]], was he then forsworn? The answer is that David vowed and swore these things on the supposition of the divine will; and so his good will was reckoned to him for the deed. And to his son it was granted to fulfil what he himself had purposed. Hence the Lord says: [[3 Kings 8:18|thou hast thought in thy heart to build a house to my name, thou hast done well in having this same thing in thy mind|Quod cogitasti in corde tuo ædificare domum nomini meo, bene fecisti, hoc ipsum mente pertractans]]; [[3 Kings 8:19|Nevertheless, thou shalt not build me a house, but thy son|verumtamen tu non ædificabis mihi domum, sed filius tuus]].

paras.t: Ecce audivimus eam in Ephrata. Secundum quosdam, in hoc loco ostenditur devotio David in translatione arcæ, quæ primo stabilem habuit mansionem in Silo, ubi Josue eam locavit, eratque ibi donec tempore Heli capta est a Philistæis. Ex tunc autem non habuit fixum locum, donec in templo Salomonis locata est. Quum enim remisissent eam Philistæi in Judæam, posita fuit in Cariathiarim, deinde in Maspha, et postea in Gabaa, in domum Abinadab ; deinde transtulit eam David in domum Obededom Gethæi, ut legitur secundo libro Regum. Postremo posuit eam David in tabernaculo quod ipse ei tetenderat. Sic ergo litteram istam exponunt : Ecce audivimus eam, id est arcam, positam fuisse in Ephrata, id est in Silo, quæ dicitur Ephrata, quoniam erat in sorte Ephraim ; invenimus eam in campis silvæ, id est in Gabaa, quæ est in territorio Cariathiarim, quæ dicitur, urbs Silvarum. Introibimus, ego David et populus meus, in tabernaculum ejus, id est in tabernaculum quod ego tetendi arcæ in civitate mea Jerusalem ; adorabimus Deum in loco ubi steterunt pedes ejus. Deus enim dicebatur sedere super propitiatorium, quod erat super arcam tanquam operculum ejus, et ita pedes Dei dicebantur stare in loco ubi exstitit arca.
paras.en: [[131:6|Behold we have heard of it in Ephrata|Ecce audivimus eam in Ephrata]]. According to some, this place shows the devotion of David in the translation of the ark, which first had a settled abode in Silo, where Josue placed it; and it was there until in the time of Heli it was taken by the Philistines. From then on it had no fixed place until it was set in the temple of Solomon. For when the Philistines had sent it back into Judæa, it was placed in Cariathiarim, then in Maspha, and afterwards in Gabaa, in the house of Abinadab; then David moved it into the house of Obededom the Gethite, as we read in the second book of Kings. Lastly David put it in the tabernacle which he himself had pitched for it. So they expound this text thus: [[131:6|Behold we have heard of it|Ecce audivimus eam]], that is, of the ark, that it had been placed [[131:6|in Ephrata|in Ephrata]], that is, in Silo, which is called Ephrata because it lay in the lot of Ephraim; [[131:6|we have found it in the fields of the wood|invenimus eam in campis silvæ]], that is, in Gabaa, which is in the territory of Cariathiarim, which is called the City of Woods [the Hebrew name Cariathiarim means "city of forests"]. [[131:7|We will go|Introibimus]], I David and my people, [[131:7|into his tabernacle|in tabernaculum ejus]], that is, into the tabernacle which I pitched for the ark in my city Jerusalem; [[131:7|we will adore|adorabimus]] God [[131:7|in the place where his feet stood|in loco ubi steterunt pedes ejus]]. For God was said to sit upon the propitiatory, which was over the ark as its lid; and so the feet of God were said to stand in the place where the ark was.

paras.t: Hæc autem expositio videtur extranea. Quum enim nulla mentio facta sit in psalmo præsenti usque ad hunc versum de arca, non apparet cur hoc relativum, eam, referat arcam. Item quod per Ephrata intelligatur Silo, extraneum esse videtur. Nam in Genesi habetur : Bethleem dicta est Ephrata. Unde et Michæas ait : Et tu, Bethleem Ephrata, parvulus es in millibus Juda. Si dixisset Propheta, Ecce audivimus eam in Ephraim, vel in Ephrem, apparentiam haberet majorem expositio ista. Denique quod per campos silvæ intelligitur Gabaa, quæ erat civitas populosa, non videtur conveniens. Quidam etiam libri, qui creduntur correcti, non habent, Ecce invenimus eam, sed, eum. Aptius ergo puto, ut exponantur ista de Christo atque Ecclesia, de quibus David hoc loco prophetice loquitur, sicut in sequenti patebit articulo.
paras.en: But this exposition seems far-fetched. For since no mention of the ark has been made in the present psalm up to this verse, it does not appear why this relative, *it* [Latin *eam*], should refer to the ark. Again, that Silo should be understood by Ephrata seems far-fetched. For in Genesis we have: Bethlehem was called Ephrata [see Gen 35:19 and 48:7]. Whence Micheas too says: [[Mich 5:2|And thou Bethlehem Ephrata, art a little one among the thousands of Juda|Et tu, Bethleem Ephrata, parvulus es in millibus Juda]]. Had the Prophet said, [[131:6|Behold we have heard of it|Ecce audivimus eam]] in Ephraim, or in Ephrem, this exposition would have more likelihood. Lastly, that by [[131:6|the fields of the wood|campos silvæ]] Gabaa should be understood, which was a populous city, does not seem fitting. Some books too, which are held to be corrected, do not have: Behold, [[131:6|we have found it|invenimus eam]], but *him* [Latin *eum* in place of *eam*: a masculine pronoun, which suits Christ rather than the ark]. I think it more fitting, therefore, that these words be expounded of Christ and the Church, of whom David here speaks prophetically, as will be clear in the following article.

paras.t: Deinde David orat Dominum ut dignanter descendat, et habitet in templo Salomonis. Surge, Domine, in requiem tuam, id est in templum a filio meo Salomone ædificandum, in quo tibi stabilem habitationem elegisti. Surge, inquam, tu, ingrediendo non motu locali, sed operatione gratuita, templum hoc, et arca sanctificationis tuæ, id est arca Moysis sanctificata a te, et continens sancta, duas videlicet tabulas digito Dei scriptas, virgamque Aaron quæ fronduerat, et urnam auream continentem manna. Hæc arca surgat, id est transferatur, in requiem tuam, id est in templum Salomonis. Itaque orat David ut arca transferretur in templum Salomonis: quod factum esse tertio Regum ostenditur.
paras.en: Then David prays the Lord to deign to come down and dwell in the temple of Solomon: [[131:8|Arise, O Lord, into thy resting place|Surge, Domine, in requiem tuam]], that is, into the temple to be built by my son Solomon, in which thou hast chosen for thyself a settled dwelling. Arise, I say, [[131:8|thou|tu]], entering this temple not by local motion but by the working of grace, [[131:8|and the ark, which thou hast sanctified|et arca sanctificationis tuæ]] [literally "the ark of thy sanctification"], that is, the ark of Moses, sanctified by thee and holding holy things: namely the two tables written by the finger of God, the rod of Aaron which had blossomed, and the golden urn holding the manna. Let this ark arise, that is, be carried over, into thy resting place, that is, into the temple of Solomon. So David prays that the ark be carried over into the temple of Solomon: which is shown in the third book of Kings to have been done.

paras.t: Sacerdotes tui, videlicet filii Aaron, ministri altaris ac templi, induantur justitiam, id est, taliter adornentur et operiantur justa vita atque virtutibus, sicut corpus vestimento ornatur ac tegitur. Propter quod Moyses dixit : Sacerdotes qui accedunt ad Dominum, sanctificentur, ne percutiat eos. Et sancti tui exsultent spirituali jucunditate in te.
paras.en: [[131:9|Let thy priests|Sacerdotes tui]], namely the sons of Aaron, ministers of the altar and of the temple, [[131:9|be clothed with justice|induantur justitiam]]: that is, let them be so adorned and covered with a just life and with virtues, as the body is adorned and covered with a garment. For this reason Moses said: [[Ex 19:22|The priests also that come to the Lord, let them be sanctified, lest he strike them|Sacerdotes qui accedunt ad Dominum, sanctificentur, ne percutiat eos]]. [[131:9|and let thy saints rejoice|Et sancti tui exsultent]] with spiritual gladness in thee.

paras.t: Propter David servum tuum, id est propter preces et merita ejus, non avertas faciem christi tui, id est, non differas mittere Christum mundi Salvatorem, sed ostende nobis faciem atque præsentiam ejus. Nicolaus de Lyra, per christum hoc loco intelligit Salomonem. Et dicit quod secundum Judæos, portæ templi Salomonis clauserunt se contra sacerdotes atque Levitas, arcam portantes ut eam transferrent in templum. Quumque Dominum pro apertione portarum orarent, psalmumque præsentem cantarent, statim dum istum versiculum canebant, portæ templi aperuerunt se. Quo facto, universi qui aderant, cognoverunt quod David erat acceptus Deo : cujus oppositum multi tenebant usque ad illud tempus, propter occisionem Uriæ et adulterium Bethsabee.
paras.en: [[131:10|For thy servant David's sake|Propter David servum tuum]], that is, for the sake of his prayers and merits, [[131:10|turn not away the face of thy anointed|non avertas faciem christi tui]] [Latin *christi tui*, "of thy christ", that is, of thy anointed one]: that is, do not delay to send Christ, the Saviour of the world, but show us his face and presence. Nicholas of Lyra understands by *anointed* in this place Solomon. And he says that, according to the Jews, the gates of Solomon's temple shut themselves against the priests and Levites who were carrying the ark to bring it into the temple; and when they prayed the Lord for the opening of the gates and sang the present psalm, at once, while they were singing this verse, the gates of the temple opened themselves. When this happened, all who were present knew that David was acceptable to God: the opposite of which many had held until that time, because of the killing of Urias[[2 Kings 11:16||]][[2 Kings 11:17||]] and the adultery with Bethsabee[[2 Kings 11:4||]].

paras.t: Juravit Dominus David servo suo veritatem, id est quod verum est, et non frustrabitur eum (alias eam), id est, non omittet implere quod ei juravit. Quid autem juravit, adjecit. De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam, id est, dabo tibi filium regni successorem. Istud, secundum Hieronymum, intelligendum est de Christo, qui dicitur filius David secundum carnem, et in eo perpetuatum est regnum David, sicut angelus dixit Virgini gloriosæ : Dabit illi Dominus Deus sedem David patris ejus, et regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum. Unde ab Isaia prædictum est : Super solium David et super regnum ejus sedebit, ut confirmet illud, et corroboret in judicio et justitia, amodo et usque in sempiternum. Quidam tamen exponunt de Salomone, qui erat filius et successor David in regno, sicut per Nathan Dominus promiserat David.
paras.en: [[131:11|The Lord hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]] to David his servant [[131:11|truth|veritatem]], that is, what is true, [[131:11|and he will not make it void|et non frustrabitur eum]] [the print reads *eum*, "him" (he will not disappoint him), with the note "otherwise *eam*", "it", the reading of the Vulgate]: that is, he will not fail to fulfil what he swore to him. And what he swore, he added: [[131:11|of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne|De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam]], that is, I will give thee a son to succeed to the kingdom. This, according to Jerome, is to be understood of Christ, who is called the son of David according to the flesh; and in him the kingdom of David was made everlasting, as the angel said to the glorious Virgin: [[Luke 1:32|the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father: and he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|Dabit illi Dominus Deus sedem David patris ejus, et regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum]]. Whence it was foretold by Isaias: [[Is 9:7|he shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom; to establish it and strengthen it with judgment and with justice, from henceforth and for ever|Super solium David et super regnum ejus sedebit, ut confirmet illud, et corroboret in judicio et justitia, amodo et usque in sempiternum]]. Some, however, expound it of Solomon, who was David's son and successor in the kingdom, as the Lord had promised David through Nathan[[2 Kings 7:12||]][[2 Kings 7:13||]].

paras.t: Si custodierint filii tui, o David, testamentum meum, id est legem Mosaicam, et testimonia mea, id est cetera quæ in lege contenta sunt, hæc quæ docebo eos, id est, tunc illuminabo corda ipsorum, ut plenius veriusque ea cognoscant. Et filii eorum usque in sæculum, id est, quamdiu duraverit cursus veteris Testamenti, sedebunt super sedem tuam, regnantes in regno tuo, et patribus suis succedentes. Sic plane factum fuisset, si non peccassent adeo graviter. Unde propter eorum gravissima crimina regalis successio desiit tempore captivitatis Babylonicæ.
paras.en: [[131:12|If thy children will keep|Si custodierint filii tui]], O David, [[131:12|my covenant|testamentum meum]], that is, the law of Moses, and [[131:12|my testimonies|testimonia mea]], that is, the other things contained in the law, these [[131:12|which I shall teach them|quæ docebo eos]]: that is, I will then enlighten their hearts, so that they may know them more fully and more truly. [[131:12|Their children also for evermore|Et filii eorum usque in sæculum]], that is, as long as the course of the Old Testament should last, [[131:12|shall sit upon thy throne|sedebunt super sedem tuam]], reigning in thy kingdom and succeeding their fathers. So indeed it would have come about, had they not sinned so grievously. Hence, because of their most grievous crimes, the royal succession ceased at the time of the Babylonian captivity.

paras.t: Quoniam elegit Dominus Sion, id est montem in quo ædificatum est templum ; elegit eam in habitationem sibi. Nam in templo dicebatur Deus specialiter esse et habitare, propter evidentem operationem suam in eo : in templo namque dabantur divina responsa de propitiatorio. Sciendum autem quod mons Sion, qui etiam dictus est mons Moria, erat locus in quo David vidit angelum Domini percutientem populum propter numerationem populi. Hunc autem locum Deus ostendit se elegisse, quando misit Gad prophetam ad David, præcipiens ei ut in monte seu loco hoc ædificaret altare, hostiasque offerret in eo. Quod quum fecisset, exaudivit eum Deus in igne cœlitus descendente. Propter quod David locutus est, dum ista vidisset : Hæc est domus Dei, et hoc altare in holocaustum Israel. In hoc itaque monte præcepit David Salomoni construere templum.
paras.en: [[131:13|For the Lord hath chosen Sion|Quoniam elegit Dominus Sion]], that is, the mountain on which the temple was built; [[131:13|he hath chosen it for his dwelling|elegit eam in habitationem sibi]]. For God was said to be and to dwell in the temple in a special way, because of his evident working in it: for in the temple divine answers were given from the propitiatory. Now it should be known that Mount Sion, which was also called Mount Moria[[2 Par 3:1||]], was the place in which David saw the angel of the Lord striking the people because of the numbering of the people[[1 Par 21:15||]][[1 Par 21:16||]]. And God showed that he had chosen this place when he sent Gad the prophet to David, bidding him build an altar on this mountain or place and offer victims on it[[1 Par 21:18||]]. And when he had done so, God heard him by fire coming down from heaven[[1 Par 21:26||]]. For this reason David, when he had seen these things, said: [[1 Par 22:1|This is the house of God, And this is the altar for the holocaust of Israel|Hæc est domus Dei, et hoc altare in holocaustum Israel]]. On this mountain, then, David commanded Solomon to build the temple.

paras.t: Hæc requies mea in sæculum sæculi, id est, in templo ædificato in hoc monte requiescam cum filiis Israel; hic, id est in monte isto, habitabo cum populo meo, quoniam elegi eam, scilicet Sion. Unde Dominus dixit Salomoni : Sanctificavi mihi domum istam, et habitabo cum filiis Israel.
paras.en: [[131:14|This is my rest for ever and ever|Hæc requies mea in sæculum sæculi]], that is, in the temple built on this mountain I will rest with the children of Israel; [[131:14|here|hic]], that is, on this mountain, [[131:14|will I dwell|habitabo]] with my people, [[131:14|for I have chosen it|quoniam elegi eam]], namely Sion. Hence the Lord said to Solomon: [[3 Kings 9:3|I have sanctified this house|Sanctificavi mihi domum istam]], [[3 Kings 6:13|And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel|et habitabo cum filiis Israel]] [the margin gives 3 Kings 9:3; the second half is closer to 3 Kings 6:13].

paras.t: Viduam ejus benedicens benedicam, id est, in spiritualibus et temporalibus dabo sufficientiam viduis Sion ; pauperes ejus saturabo panibus mentis et corporis, dummodo legem meam custodire sategerint. Sacerdotes ejus, scilicet templi, induam salutari, id est salute et gratia ; et sancti ejus exsultatione spirituali exsultabunt de bonis Domini, eique hilariter ministrabunt.
paras.en: [[131:15|Blessing I will bless her widow|Viduam ejus benedicens benedicam]], that is, I will give sufficiency in spiritual and temporal things to the widows of Sion; [[131:15|I will satisfy her poor with bread|pauperes ejus saturabo panibus]] of mind and of body, provided they take care to keep my law. [[131:16|her priests|Sacerdotes ejus]], namely those of the temple, [[131:16|I will clothe|induam]] [[131:16|with salvation|salutari]], that is, with salvation and grace; [[131:16|and her saints shall rejoice with exceeding great joy|et sancti ejus exsultatione spirituali exsultabunt]] [Denis's text has *exsultatione spirituali*, "with spiritual exultation"] in the good things of the Lord, and serve him cheerfully.

paras.t: Illic, videlicet in Sion, producam, id est, procreabo et prolongabo, cornu, id est regiam potestatem, David, dando ei regni successores ; paravi lucernam, id est claram memoriam, christo meo, id est regi David, non penitus auferendo regnum a posteris ejus usque ad longum tempus. Hinc enim Dominus ait Ahiæ prophetæ, cui loquebatur de divisione regni Israelitici : Filio autem ejus, videlicet Roboam filio Salomonis, dabo tribum unam, ut remaneat lucerna David servo meo. Et simile sæpius dicitur de aliis regibus Juda, qui suis peccatis meruerunt regno atque successore privari ; sed propter David factum est ut maneret ei lucerna.
paras.en: [[131:17|There|Illic]], namely in Sion, [[131:17|will I bring forth|producam]], that is, beget and prolong, [[131:17|a horn|cornu]], that is, royal power, [[131:17|to David|David]], by giving him successors in the kingdom; [[131:17|I have prepared a lamp|paravi lucernam]], that is, a bright memory, [[131:17|for my anointed|christo meo]], that is, for King David, by not wholly taking the kingdom away from his posterity for a long time. For hence the Lord said to Ahias the prophet, to whom he was speaking of the division of the kingdom of Israel: [[3 Kings 11:36|And to his son|Filio autem ejus]], namely to Roboam the son of Solomon, [[3 Kings 11:36|I will give one tribe, that there may remain a lamp for my servant, David|dabo tribum unam, ut remaneat lucerna David servo meo]]. And the like is often said of other kings of Juda, who by their sins deserved to be deprived of the kingdom and of a successor; but for David's sake it came about that a lamp remained to him.

paras.t: Inimicos ejus induam confusione. Sæpe enim dejecit Deus adversarios David filiorumque ejus, et tunc confusione replevit æmulos ejus ; super ipsum autem David et posteritatem ipsius efflorebit sanctificatio mea, id est unctio sancta, qua reges ungi solebant.
paras.en: [[131:18|His enemies I will clothe with confusion|Inimicos ejus induam confusione]]. For God often cast down the adversaries of David and of his sons, and then filled his rivals with confusion; [[131:18|but upon him|super ipsum autem]], David, and upon his posterity, [[131:18|shall my sanctification flourish|efflorebit sanctificatio mea]], that is, the holy anointing with which kings were wont to be anointed.

paras.t: Verumtamen ista de Christo multo convenientius exponuntur, sicut jam elucescet.
paras.en: Yet these things are expounded far more fittingly of Christ, as will now be made clear.

131.title: ELUCIDATIO EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI PRIMI DE CHRISTO.
131.title_en: Explanation of the same hundred and thirty-first psalm, concerning Christ.
131.note: Part of the text (the rest of v. 5 and all of v. 6) is missing from the transcription of p. 616 and is marked […].

paras.t: Convenientissime autem exponitur psalmus iste de Christo: qui in scripturis veteris Testamenti frequenter David vocatur, sicut dum Dominus per Ezechielem ait: Salvabo gregem meum, et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum, qui pascat eum, David servum meum; et per Osee: Revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum. David enim interpretatur, manu fortis, seu desiderabilis adspectu. Et quis adeo fortis, ut Christus, Dei virtus, qui fortem armatum alligavit, id est, diabolum vicit, et vasa ejus diripuit, id est, peccatores redemit? Præterea quis tam desiderabilis adspectu, ut Christus, speciosus forma præ filiis hominum, qui est candor lucis æternæ, in quem desiderant angeli sancti prospicere?
paras.en: Now this psalm is most fittingly expounded of Christ, who in the scriptures of the Old Testament is often called David: as when the Lord says by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:22|I will save my flock|Salvabo gregem meum]], [[Ezech 34:23|And I WILL SET UP ONE SHEPHERD OVER THEM, and he shall feed them, even my servant David|et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum, qui pascat eum, David servum meum]]; and by Osee: [[Osee 3:5|the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the Lord, their God, and David, their king|Revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum]]. For David is interpreted *strong of hand*, or *desirable to behold*. And who is so strong as Christ, the power of God, who bound the strong man armed[[Luke 11:21||]], that is, overcame the devil, and plundered his goods[[Luke 11:22||]] [literally *vessels*], that is, redeemed sinners? Moreover, who is so desirable to behold as Christ, [[Ps 44:3|beautiful above the sons of men|speciosus forma præ filiis hominum]], who is [[Wis 7:26|the brightness of eternal light|candor lucis æternæ]], [[1 Pet 1:12|on whom the angels desire to look|in quem desiderant angeli sancti prospicere]]?

paras.t: De Christo itaque loquens Propheta, ait: Memento, Domine, Pater æterne, David, id est Christi, et omnis mansuetudinis ejus. Christus enim mitis, imo mitissimus erat. Propter quod ait: Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam; et iterum, Discite a me quia mitis sum. De ejus quoque mansuetudine scriptum est: Non clamabit, nec audietur foris vox ejus; et, Non erit tristis neque turbulentus.
paras.en: Speaking of Christ, then, the Prophet says: [[131:1|O Lord, remember|Memento, Domine]], eternal Father, [[131:1|David|David]], that is, Christ, [[131:1|and all his meekness|et omnis mansuetudinis ejus]]. For Christ was meek, nay, most meek.
