For which reason he says: [[Jer 11:19|I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim|Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam]]; and again, [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek|Discite a me quia mitis sum]]. Of his meekness too it is written: [[Is 42:2|He shall not cry|Non clamabit]], [[Is 42:2|neither shall his voice be heard abroad|nec audietur foris vox ejus]]; and, [[Is 42:4|He shall not be sad, nor troublesome|Non erit tristis neque turbulentus]].

paras.t: Sed multa sunt quæ circa hoc movere possunt studiosum lectorem. Primo enim videtur mirabile, quod Propheta oret pro Christo et mansuetudine ejus. Secundo, mirum apparet cur oret ut Deus meminerit Christi, quum certum sit quod nunquam oblivisci potuit Filii sui dilecti, aut ejus mansuetudinem reprobare, in quo sibi bene complacuit. Tertio, mirum est cur oret pro Christo, quum Christus omnipotens sit, et per se ipsum omnia possit. Et respondendum ad primum istorum, quod Propheta orat pro Christo, non tamen pro propria Christi persona. Orat enim ut Deus meminerit Christi, non quantum ad ipsum Christum, sed quantum ad corpus suum mysticum, quod est Ecclesia, scilicet ut per Christum et merito ejus misereatur omnibus nobis. Et hoc modo Moyses sæpe precatus est Deum ut recordaretur Abrahæ et Isaac et Jacob: non quod pro Sanctis illis defunctis oravit; sed hoc deprecabatur ut Deus meritis eorum misereretur filiis Israel. Vel dici potest, quod Propheta orat pro Christo, non propter Christi indigentiam, sed ad ostendendum cordis sui affectum quem habebat ad Christum. Sicut enim Christus pro se ipso oravit, sic membra ejus pro eo hoc modo poterant exorare: et ex hoc patet responsio ad secundum. Non enim sic orat Propheta ut Deus Pater memor sit Christi et mansuetudinis ejus, quasi eorum oblivisci potuerit, sed ut recordando Christi et mansuetudinis ejus, memor sit misereaturque nostri, dando nobis per ipsum, quod ipsi non promeremur. Denique, licet Christus secundum quod Deus, omnipotens sit, orat tamen Propheta ut Pater ei cooperetur, quoniam Christus ut homo, indesinenter adjuvabatur a Patre, et quidquid fuit ac habuit, a Patre recepit. Unde ipse testatur: Non potest Filius a se facere quidquam, nisi quod viderit Patrem facientem.
paras.en: But there are many things here that may trouble the studious reader. First, it seems strange that the Prophet should pray for Christ and for his meekness. Secondly, it seems strange why he should pray that God remember Christ, since it is certain that he could never forget his beloved Son, or reject the meekness of him in whom he was well pleased[[Matt 3:17||]][[Matt 17:5||]]. Thirdly, it is strange why he should pray for Christ, since Christ is almighty and can do all things of himself. To the first of these the answer is that the Prophet prays for Christ, yet not for Christ's own person. For he prays that God may remember Christ, not as regards Christ himself, but as regards his mystical body, which is the Church: namely, that through Christ and by his merit he may have mercy on us all. And in this way Moses often besought God to remember Abraham and Isaac and Jacob[[Ex 32:13||]]: not that he was praying for those holy men who were dead, but he asked this, that God by their merits might have mercy on the children of Israel. Or it can be said that the Prophet prays for Christ, not because of any need in Christ, but to show the affection of his heart which he had towards Christ. For just as Christ prayed for himself[[Matt 26:39||]][[John 17:1||]][[John 17:5||]], so his members could pray for him in this way: and from this the answer to the second is plain. For the Prophet does not pray that God the Father be mindful of Christ and his meekness as though he could have forgotten them, but that, remembering Christ and his meekness, he may be mindful of us and have mercy on us, giving us through him what we ourselves do not deserve. Lastly, although Christ, inasmuch as he is God, is almighty, the Prophet nevertheless prays that the Father work together with him, because Christ as man was unceasingly helped by the Father, and whatever he was and had he received from the Father. Hence he himself testifies: [[John 5:19|the Son cannot do any thing of himself, but what he seeth the Father doing|Non potest Filius a se facere quidquam, nisi quod viderit Patrem facientem]].

paras.t: Itaque, Domine, memento David, id est Christi, ad hoc ut impleatur sicut Christus juravit Domino Deo Patri, et sicut votum vovit Deo Jacob. Sed ubi in Scriptura canonica legitur Christus jurasse, vovisseque Domino? Ad hoc responderi potest dupliciter: Primo, quod per juramentum Christi, intelligatur firmum propositum ejus. Per votum vero ipsius, intelligitur voluntas ejus promptissima, et firma assertio qua se dixit facturum quod sequitur. Secundo (ut arbitror) dici potest, quod Christus homo vere juravit atque promisit Deo illud quod subditur, quamvis fortassis hoc alibi non legatur. Quum enim Christus plenus fuerit omni virtute, plenus utique fuit omni actu ac perfectione virtutum. Quum ergo juramentum et votum sint actus religionis seu latriæ, quemadmodum in Secunda secundæ Thomas declarat, probabile est quod in Christo fuerunt, præsertim quum opera ex voto procedentia, sint perfectiora magisque meritoria quam alia. Unde et Virgo benedicta virginitatem creditur promisisse.
paras.en: Therefore, [[131:1|O Lord, remember David|Domine, memento David]], that is, Christ, to this end, that it may be fulfilled as Christ [[131:2|swore to the Lord|juravit Domino]], God the Father, and as he [[131:2|vowed a vow to the God of Jacob|votum vovit Deo Jacob]]. But where in canonical Scripture do we read that Christ swore and vowed to the Lord? To this one may answer in two ways. First, that by Christ's oath is to be understood his firm purpose, and by his vow his most ready will, and the firm assertion by which he said that he would do what follows. Secondly (as I think) it can be said that Christ as man truly swore and promised to God what is added next, although perhaps this is not read anywhere else. For since Christ was full of every virtue, he was surely full of every act and perfection of the virtues. Since, then, the oath and the vow are acts of religion or latria [that is, the worship owed to God alone], as Thomas declares in the Secunda secundæ [the margin gives Summa theologiae II-II, q. 88, a. 5, and q. 89, a. 1], it is probable that they were in Christ; all the more since works that proceed from a vow are more perfect and more meritorious than others. Hence the blessed Virgin too is believed to have vowed her virginity.

paras.t: Juravit autem et vovit Christus hoc modo: Si introiero, id est, non intrabo, in tabernaculum domus meæ, id est in cœlum, unde descendi; si ascendero, id est, non ascendam, in lectum strati mei, id est ad thronum gloriæ, ut requiescam ad dexteram Dei Patris. De quo throno scriptum est: Ego vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus. Si dedero, id est, non dabo, somnum, id est triduanæ sepulturæ quietem, oculis meis corporeis: quæ tunc sine vigilia actionis fuerunt. Et hoc idem repetit aliis verbis, dicendo: et palpebris meis dormitationem. Et requiem temporibus meis non dabo, id est, quamdiu in mundo isto conversor, non quiescam, neque cessabo discurrere, prædicare, miracula facere, injurias sustinere. Donec inveniam locum Domino. Hic ponitur, quid Christus juravit et vovit, ut sit sensus: Donec inveniam, id est, parem et faciam locum Domino in cordibus electorum, convertendo eos ad fidem et gratiam Dei; et donec hoc modo inveniam tabernaculum, id est Ecclesiam, Deo Jacob, congregando electos in unum, id est in unam catholicam fidem atque individuam caritatem: sicque exsistant tabernaculum Dei, in quo ipse per gratiam habitet: sicut Apostol[…]
paras.en: Now Christ swore and vowed in this way: [[131:3|If I shall enter|Si introiero]], that is, I will not enter [in an oath, "if I shall …" stands for "I will not …", as Denis's gloss shows], [[131:3|into the tabernacle of my house|in tabernaculum domus meæ]], that is, into heaven, whence I came down; [[131:3|if I shall go up|si ascendero]], that is, I will not go up, [[131:3|into the bed wherein I lie|in lectum strati mei]], that is, to the throne of glory, to rest at the right hand of God the Father. Of which throne it is written: [[Apoc 3:21|I also have overcome and am set down with my Father in his throne|Ego vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus]]. [[131:4|If I shall give|Si dedero]], that is, I will not give, [[131:4|sleep|somnum]], that is, the rest of the three days' burial, [[131:4|to my eyes|oculis meis]] of the body, which were then without the watchfulness of action. And he repeats the same thing in other words, saying: [[131:4|or slumber to my eyelids|et palpebris meis dormitationem]]. [[131:5|Or rest to my temples|Et requiem temporibus meis]] I will not give: that is, as long as I live in this world I will not rest, nor cease to go about, to preach, to work miracles, to bear wrongs, [[131:5|until I find out a place for the Lord|Donec inveniam locum Domino]]. Here is set down what Christ swore and vowed, so that the sense is: [[131:5|until I find out|Donec inveniam]], that is, prepare and make, [[131:5|a place for the Lord|locum Domino]] in the hearts of the elect, converting them to faith and to the grace of God; and until in this way I find [[131:5|a tabernacle|tabernaculum]], that is, the Church, [[131:5|for the God of Jacob|Deo Jacob]], gathering the elect into one, that is, into one catholic faith and undivided charity; and so they become the tabernacle of God, in which he dwells by grace: as the Apostle […]

paras.t: […] qui non interrogabant de me. Ad quod etiam pertinet illud Osee: Erit in loco ubi dicetur eis, Non populus meus vos; dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis.
paras.en: […] who [[Is 65:1|asked not for me|non interrogabant]] [a column of the text is lost here in the transcription, with the end of the comment on v. 5 and the comment on v. 6; these last words are those of Isaias 65:1, also quoted by the Apostle at Rom 10:20]. To this also belongs that saying of Osee: [[Osee 1:10|it shall be in the place where it shall be said to them: You are not my people: it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God|Erit in loco ubi dicetur eis, Non populus meus vos; dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis]].

paras.t: Introibimus, nos in Christum credentes, in tabernaculum ejus, id est locum Ecclesiæ; adorabimus Deum cultu latriæ, in loco ubi steterunt pedes ejus, id est in gentilitate conversa seu ipsa Ecclesia, ubi steterunt sancti Apostoli, et eorum prædicationes auditæ sunt. Qui Apostoli sunt pedes Ecclesiæ, quoniam corpus ejus sustentant et bajulant. De eis namque et eorum doctrinis Isaias ait: O quam pulchri super montes pedes evangelizantium pacem, annuntiantium bona! Vel sic: Introibimus in tabernaculum ejus, videlicet Christi; adorabimus in loco ubi steterunt pedes ejus. Hoc ad litteram convenientissime accipitur de templo in Jerusalem ædificato post reditum a Babylone. In hoc enim tabernaculo pedes Christi frequenter steterunt, sicut dum ejecit de eo omnes ementes et vendentes. Unde dictum erat: Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis.
paras.en: [[131:7|We will go|Introibimus]], we who believe in Christ, [[131:7|into his tabernacle|in tabernaculum ejus]], that is, the place of the Church; [[131:7|we will adore|adorabimus]] God with the worship of latria [that is, the worship owed to God alone], [[131:7|in the place where his feet stood|in loco ubi steterunt pedes ejus]], that is, among the converted gentiles, or in the Church itself, where the holy Apostles stood and their preaching was heard. These Apostles are the feet of the Church, because they hold up and carry its body. For of them and of their teaching Isaias says: [[Is 52:7|How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet|O quam pulchri super montes pedes]] of them that preach the gospel of peace, that bring good things! [the margin gives Is. liii, 7; the words are from Is 52:7, which Denis gives in a form close to Rom 10:15]. Or thus: [[131:7|We will go into his tabernacle|Introibimus in tabernaculum ejus]], namely Christ's; [[131:7|we will adore in the place where his feet stood|adorabimus in loco ubi steterunt pedes ejus]]. This is most fittingly taken, according to the letter, of the temple in Jerusalem built after the return from Babylon. For in this tabernacle the feet of Christ often stood, as when he cast out of it all that bought and sold[[Luke 19:45||]][[John 2:15||]]. Hence it had been said: [[Mal 3:1|And presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple|Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis]].

paras.t: Surge, Domine Christe, in requiem tuam, id est, surge a mortuis, et assume corpus gloriosum, et redi ad cœlum. Jam enim juramentum tuum implesti, votum solvisti, invenisti Domino locum, fundasti Ecclesiam. Tu et arca sanctificationis tuæ, id est, non solum tu surge, sed et Ecclesia tecum resurgat. Ita impletum est. Nam Christo resurgente, multi Sanctorum qui dormierant, surrexerunt. Christo quoque resurgente in re, omnes Christiani surrexerunt in spe: capitis enim præcessio, spes exstat membrorum. Propterea dicit Apostolus: Si enim credimus quod Jesus mortuus est et resurrexit, ita et Deus eos qui dormierunt, adducet cum eo. Dicitur autem Ecclesia, arca sanctificationis Christi, quoniam sicut arca Moysis continebat quædam præcipua sancta, in præcedenti articulo nominata; ita Ecclesia Christi continet electos, qui sunt vasa misericordiæ. Dicitur quoque, arca sanctificationis, id est sanctificata adspersione sanguinis Agni immaculati, quemadmodum scriptum est: Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut illam sanctificaret, mundans illam lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ. Lavacrum autem aquæ, puta Baptismus, operatur virtute sanguinis Christi. Omnia namque sacramenta sunt quasi vasa medicinalia, per quæ nobis applicatur virtus seu meritum passionis et sanguinis Christi.
paras.en: [[131:8|Arise, O Lord|Surge, Domine]] Christ, [[131:8|into thy resting place|in requiem tuam]]: that is, arise from the dead, and take up a glorious body, and return to heaven. For now thou hast fulfilled thy oath, paid thy vow, found a place for the Lord, founded the Church. [[131:8|thou and the ark, which thou hast sanctified|Tu et arca sanctificationis tuæ]]: that is, not only do thou arise, but let the Church also rise again with thee. And so it was fulfilled. For when Christ rose, many of the saints who had slept arose. And when Christ rose in fact, all Christians rose in hope: for the going before of the head is the hope of the members. Therefore the Apostle says: [[1 Thess 4:13|For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again: even so them who have slept through Jesus, will God bring with him|Si enim credimus quod Jesus mortuus est et resurrexit, ita et Deus eos qui dormierunt, adducet cum eo]]. Now the Church is called the ark of Christ's sanctification [literally "the ark of thy sanctification", where the Douay-Rheims has "the ark, which thou hast sanctified"], because, just as the ark of Moses contained certain chief holy things, named in the preceding article, so the Church of Christ contains the elect, who are vessels of mercy. It is called the ark of sanctification also as sanctified by the sprinkling of the blood of the spotless Lamb, as it is written: [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved the church and delivered himself up for it|Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea]], [[Eph 5:26|That he might sanctify it, cleansing it by the laver of water in the word of life|ut illam sanctificaret, mundans illam lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ]]. Now the laver of water, that is, Baptism, works by the power of Christ's blood. For all the sacraments are like vessels of medicine, through which the power or merit of Christ's passion and blood is applied to us.

paras.t: Deinde Christus vel Propheta pro sacerdotibus novi Testamenti deprecans, subdit: Sacerdotes tui induantur justitiam. Maxima enim puritas christianos condecet sacerdotes, qui hostiam illam supermundissimam superdignissimamque conficiunt, tractant et sumunt.
paras.en: Then Christ, or the Prophet, praying for the priests of the New Testament, adds: [[131:9|Let thy priests be clothed with justice|Sacerdotes tui induantur justitiam]]. For the greatest purity befits Christian priests, who consecrate, handle and receive that Victim, clean and worthy beyond all others [Latin *supermundissimam superdignissimamque*, "more than most clean and more than most worthy"].

paras.t: Propter David servum tuum, id est Christum: qui secundum quod formam servi accepit, servus vocatur; non avertas, id est, non repellas a te, o Deus Pater, faciem christi tui, id est vultum seu mentem hominis christiani: qui christus nominatur, tanquam spiritualiter unctus Spiritu Sancto; sed merito passionis, orationis, conversationisque Christi, suscipe faciem Christiani, sicut de Job dicis: Faciem ejus, videlicet Job, suscipiam. Unde Malachias: Deprecamini, inquit, vultum Domini, ut misereatur vestri, si quo modo suscipiat facies vestras. Vel sic: Non avertas faciem christi tui, id est, propter ipsum Christum non avertas piam præsentiam, claram notitiam, gratiosam inhabitationem Christi a nobis.
paras.en: [[131:10|For thy servant David's sake|Propter David servum tuum]], that is, Christ, who is called a servant inasmuch as he took the form of a servant, [[131:10|turn not away|non avertas]], that is, do not thrust away from thee, O God the Father, [[131:10|the face of thy anointed|faciem christi tui]], that is, the countenance or the mind of the Christian man, who is called *christus* [that is, anointed], as being spiritually anointed with the Holy Ghost; but by the merit of Christ's passion, prayer and manner of life, receive the face of the Christian, as thou sayest of Job: [[Job 42:8|his face|Faciem ejus]], namely Job's, [[Job 42:8|I will accept|suscipiam]]. Hence Malachias: [[Mal 1:9|beseech ye|Deprecamini]], he says, [[Mal 1:9|the face of God, that he may have mercy on you|vultum Domini, ut misereatur vestri]], [[Mal 1:9|if by any means he will receive your faces|si quo modo suscipiat facies vestras]]. Or thus: [[131:10|turn not away the face of thy anointed|Non avertas faciem christi tui]]: that is, for the sake of Christ himself, turn not away from us the loving presence, the clear knowledge, the gracious indwelling of Christ.

paras.t: Juravit, id est, inviolabiliter affirmavit, immobiliterque promisit, Dominus Pater, David, id est Christo, veritatem, et non frustrabitur eum, id est, juramentum suum non faciet irritum. Quid autem juravit, subjungitur. De fructu, id est de filiis spiritualibus, ventris tui, id est cordis tui, quos scilicet per sapientiam tuæ mentis spiritualiter generasti: prout Jacobus ait, Voluntarie genuit nos verbo veritatis suæ; ponam super sedem tuam, id est in cathedra Ecclesiæ, faciendo ex eis pastores, prælatos, doctores: sicut supra de Apostolis dictum est, Constitues eos principes super omnem terram. Hinc enim dicit Apostolus: Quosdam posuit Deus in Ecclesia, primo Apostolos, deinde Prophetas, tertio doctores. Sæpe autem in Scriptura divina ponitur venter, pro corde seu mente. Nam supra dictum est, Ex utero ante luciferum genui te, id est, ex corde: non enim in Deo Patre est venter corporeus. Salomon quoque ait: Appone cor tuum ad doctrinam meam, quæ pulchra erit tibi quum servaveris eam in ventre tuo, id est in mente tua.
paras.en: [[131:11|The Lord|Dominus]] the Father [[131:11|hath sworn|Juravit]], that is, has inviolably affirmed and immovably promised, [[131:11|truth|veritatem]] [[131:11|to David|David]], that is, to Christ, [[131:11|and he will not make it void|et non frustrabitur eum]] [Denis reads *eum*, "him", for the Vulgate's *eam*, "it": he will not disappoint him], that is, he will not make his oath of no effect. What he swore is added next: [[131:11|of the fruit|De fructu]], that is, of the spiritual children, [[131:11|of thy womb|ventris tui]], that is, of thy heart, whom thou hast spiritually begotten through the wisdom of thy mind, as James says: [[Jas 1:18|of his own will hath he begotten us by the word of truth|Voluntarie genuit nos verbo veritatis suæ]]; [[131:11|I will set upon thy throne|ponam super sedem tuam]], that is, in the chair of the Church, making of them pastors, prelates, doctors: as was said above of the Apostles, [[Ps 44:17|thou shalt make them princes over all the earth|Constitues eos principes super omnem terram]]. For hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 12:28|God indeed hath set some in the church; first apostles, secondly prophets, thirdly doctors|Quosdam posuit Deus in Ecclesia, primo Apostolos, deinde Prophetas, tertio doctores]]. Now in divine Scripture the womb [Latin *venter*, "belly" or "womb"] is often put for the heart or mind. For it was said above: [[Ps 109:3|from the womb before the day star I begot thee|Ex utero ante luciferum genui te]], that is, from the heart: for there is no bodily womb in God the Father. Solomon also says: [[Prov 22:17|apply thy heart to my doctrine|Appone cor tuum ad doctrinam meam]], [[Prov 22:18|Which shall be beautiful for thee, if thou keep it in thy bowels|quæ pulchra erit tibi quum servaveris eam in ventre tuo]] [here the Douay-Rheims has "bowels" for *venter*], that is, in thy mind.

paras.t: Si custodierint, o Christe, filii tui, id est Christiani, testamentum meum, id est Decalogum, et testimonia mea in Evangelio tradita, hæc quæ docebo eos, ut clarius ea cognoscant et certius comprehendant, imo certissime sciant ea esse a Deo. Hanc beatissimam illuminationem meretur conversatio virtuosa. Ideoque Salvator locutus est: Si quis voluerit voluntatem Dei facere, cognoscet de doctrina, an ex Deo sit. Et iterum: Numquid vestrum est scire judicium, qui odio habetis bonum? Et filii eorum, id est spiritualiter enutriti sana doctrina et moribus ab illis qui præcesserunt, usque in sæculum, id est, quamdiu Ecclesia steterit, scilicet usque ad terminum mundi, sedebunt super sedem tuam, tanquam successores Apostolorum, regentes Ecclesiam tuam. Hoc autem fiet non eorum meritis, sed gratia Dei. Propter quod sequitur:
paras.en: [[131:12|If|Si]], O Christ, [[131:12|thy children|filii tui]], that is, Christians, [[131:12|will keep|custodierint]] [[131:12|my covenant|testamentum meum]], that is, the Decalogue, [[131:12|and these my testimonies|et testimonia mea]] handed down in the Gospel, [[131:12|which I shall teach them|hæc quæ docebo eos]], so that they may know them more clearly and grasp them more surely, nay, know most certainly that they are from God. A virtuous life merits this most blessed enlightenment. And therefore the Saviour said: [[John 7:17|If any man will do the will of him, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God|Si quis voluerit voluntatem Dei facere, cognoscet de doctrina, an ex Deo sit]]. And again: [[Mich 3:1|Is it not your part to know judgment|Numquid vestrum est scire judicium]], [[Mich 3:2|You that hate good|qui odio habetis bonum]]? [the margin gives Mich. iii, 1, 2: these words are Micheas's, not the Saviour's; Denis reads them without *non*, "Is it your part to know judgment, you that hate good?"] [[131:12|Their children also|Et filii eorum]], that is, those spiritually nourished in sound doctrine and morals by those who went before, [[131:12|for evermore|usque in sæculum]], that is, as long as the Church shall stand, namely until the end of the world, [[131:12|shall sit upon thy throne|sedebunt super sedem tuam]], as successors of the Apostles, ruling thy Church. But this will come about not by their merits but by the grace of God. For which reason there follows:

paras.t: Quoniam elegit Dominus Sion, id est Ecclesiam militantem, quemadmodum in Evangelio dicit: Non vos me elegistis, sed ego elegi vos. Et Apostolus protestatur: Deus elegit nos in Christo ante mundi constitutionem, ut essemus sancti et immaculati in conspectu ejus. Elegit eam in habitationem sibi, id est, ut in ea per gratiam habitaret, sicut per Salomonem asseruit: Deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum. Unde Apostolus dicit: Vos estis templum Dei vivi, sicut dicit Dominus: Quoniam inhabitabo in illis et inambulabo, et ero illorum Deus.
paras.en: [[131:13|For the Lord hath chosen Sion|Quoniam elegit Dominus Sion]], that is, the Church militant, as he says in the Gospel: [[John 15:16|You have not chosen me: but I have chosen you|Non vos me elegistis, sed ego elegi vos]]. And the Apostle declares: [[Eph 1:4|he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and unspotted in his sight|Deus elegit nos in Christo ante mundi constitutionem, ut essemus sancti et immaculati in conspectu ejus]]. [[131:13|he hath chosen it for his dwelling|Elegit eam in habitationem sibi]], that is, that he might dwell in it by grace, as he declared through Solomon: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum]]. Hence the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 6:16|you are the temple of the living God: as God saith: I will dwell in them and walk among them. And I will be their God|Vos estis templum Dei vivi, sicut dicit Dominus: Quoniam inhabitabo in illis et inambulabo, et ero illorum Deus]][[Lev 26:12||]].

paras.t: Hæc, id est Ecclesia seu anima munda, devota et studiosa, requies mea in sæculum sæculi: sicut dixi, Ecce ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus. Dicitur autem Deus immobilem requiem habere in nobis, non quod ipse unquam turbetur aut moveatur, sed quoniam facit corda nostra in ipso quiescere. Hic habitabo per gratiam, quoniam elegi eam mea bonitate, non ejus virtute.
paras.en: [[131:14|This|Hæc]], that is, the Church, or the soul that is pure, devout and zealous, [[131:14|is my rest for ever and ever|requies mea in sæculum sæculi]]: as I said, [[Matt 28:20|behold I am with you all days|Ecce ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus]]. Now God is said to have an unmoving rest in us, not because he is ever troubled or moved, but because he makes our hearts rest in him. [[131:14|here will I dwell|Hic habitabo]] by grace, [[131:14|for I have chosen it|quoniam elegi eam]] of my goodness, not for its own virtue.

paras.t: Viduam ejus, scilicet Ecclesiæ, id est feminam viri solatio destitutam, et de cetero propter me continentem, nec in deliciis viventem, benedicens benedicam, dando ei necessaria vitæ, gratiamque in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro. Unde de talibus viduis scribens Apostolus: Viduas, inquit, honora, quæ vere viduæ sunt. Vel: Viduam, id est animam fidelem humano solatio destitutam, et vana gaudia contemnentem, benedicens benedicam. Pauperes ejus, id est egenos Ecclesiæ, scilicet pauperes spiritu, quorum est regnum cœlorum, saturabo panibus vitæ et intellectus, pane sacramentali, pane lacrimarum, pane operum bonorum.
paras.en: [[131:15|her widow|Viduam ejus]], namely the Church's, that is, a woman bereft of a husband's comfort, and for the rest living continently for my sake and not living in delights, [[131:15|Blessing I will bless|benedicens benedicam]], giving her the necessaries of life, and grace in the present and glory in the future. Hence the Apostle, writing of such widows: [[1 Tim 5:3|Honour widows|Viduas]], he says, [[1 Tim 5:3|that are widows indeed|honora, quæ vere viduæ sunt]]. Or: [[131:15|her widow|Viduam]], that is, the faithful soul, bereft of human comfort and despising vain joys, [[131:15|Blessing I will bless|benedicens benedicam]]. [[131:15|her poor|Pauperes ejus]], that is, the needy of the Church, namely [[Matt 5:3|the poor in spirit|pauperes spiritu]], [[Matt 5:3|for theirs is the kingdom of heaven|quorum est regnum cœlorum]], [[131:15|I will satisfy|saturabo]] [[131:15|with bread|panibus]] [[Ecclus 15:3|of life and understanding|vitæ et intellectus]], with the bread of the sacrament, [[Ps 79:6|the bread of tears|pane lacrimarum]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxix, 6; the words are from Ps 79:6], the bread of good works.

paras.t: Illic, id est in Ecclesia, producam, id est, formabo, conservabo et prolongabo, cornu David, id est dignitatem atque potentiam Christi, dando Ecclesiæ magnam dignitatem ac potestatem in nomine Christi. Vel: Illic, id est in futuro judicio atque in patria, producam, id est, proferam et ostendam, cornu David, id est regiam seu judiciariam potestatem Christi, quæ illic præcipue apparebit, ubi videbitur in majestate gloriæ suæ. Paravi lucernam, id est claram ac sempiternam memoriam, Christo meo: quoniam nomen Christi ubique gloriosum et notum est. Vel, Lucernam, id est vasa gratiæ, scilicet homines bonos, in quibus Christus per gratiam splendet, quemadmodum in lucerna lucet candela. Vel, Lucernam, id est Joannem præcursorem, qui paravit viam Domino: de quo dicitur, Ille erat lucerna ardens et lucens.
paras.en: [[131:17|There|Illic]], that is, in the Church, [[131:17|will I bring forth|producam]], that is, will form, preserve and prolong, [[131:17|a horn to David|cornu David]], that is, the dignity and power of Christ, by giving the Church great dignity and power in the name of Christ. Or: [[131:17|There|Illic]], that is, at the judgment to come and in our heavenly fatherland, [[131:17|will I bring forth|producam]], that is, will bring out and show, [[131:17|a horn to David|cornu David]], that is, the royal or judicial power of Christ, which will appear there above all, where he will be seen in the majesty of his glory. [[131:17|I have prepared a lamp|Paravi lucernam]], that is, a bright and everlasting memory, [[131:17|for my anointed|Christo meo]]: because the name of Christ is glorious and known everywhere. Or, [[131:17|a lamp|Lucernam]], that is, vessels of grace, namely good men, in whom Christ shines by grace as a candle gives light in a lantern. Or, [[131:17|a lamp|Lucernam]], that is, John the forerunner, who prepared the way for the Lord, of whom it is said: [[John 5:35|He was a burning and a shining light|Ille erat lucerna ardens et lucens]] [Latin *lucerna*, "lamp", as in the psalm].

paras.t: Inimicos ejus, id est adversarios Christi, induam confusione, præsertim in die judicii, quando videbunt Filium hominis in majestate sua: quando illud Isaiæ implebitur: Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei. Super ipsum autem, id est super Christum, efflorebit, id est, affluenter seu copiose florebit, sanctificatio mea: quia et ejus naturam humanam præ omnibus Sanctis sanctificavi, implens eam Spiritu Sancto sine mensura, et omnes Ecclesiæ filios sanctificabo per eum. Unde dicit Apostolus: Reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem Filii ejus. Hoc etiam Christus oravit: Pater, sanctifica eos in veritate.
paras.en: [[131:18|His enemies|Inimicos ejus]], that is, the adversaries of Christ, [[131:18|I will clothe with confusion|induam confusione]], especially on the day of judgment, when they shall see the Son of man in his majesty: when that saying of Isaias shall be fulfilled: [[Is 45:25|they shall come to him, and all that resist him shall be confounded|Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei]] [the margin gives Is. xlv, 23; the words are from Is 45:25]. [[131:18|but upon him|Super ipsum autem]], that is, upon Christ, shall [[131:18|flourish|efflorebit]], that is, flower abundantly or copiously, [[131:18|my sanctification|sanctificatio mea]]: because I have both sanctified his human nature above all the saints, filling it with the Holy Ghost without measure[[John 3:34||]], and I will sanctify all the children of the Church through him. Hence the Apostle says: [[Rom 5:10|we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son|Reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem Filii ejus]]. This too Christ prayed: Father[[John 17:11||]], [[John 17:17|Sanctify them in truth|sanctifica eos in veritate]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum gloriosum ac mysterialem audivimus: in quo Christi incarnatio et Ecclesiæ institutio pulchre signantur.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a glorious psalm, full of mysteries, in which the incarnation of Christ and the founding of the Church are beautifully signified.

paras.t: Tropologice quoque monet nos psalmus iste, ut juremus et promittamus non ingressuros nos tabernaculum domus nostræ, etc., donec in nobis ipsis inveniamus locum Domino, emundantes cor nostrum ab occupatione superflua, ab inordinato affectu, ab omni torpore.
paras.en: Tropologically [that is, in the moral sense] too this psalm admonishes us to swear and promise that we will not enter the tabernacle of our house, etc., until we find in ourselves [[131:5|a place for the Lord|locum Domino]], cleansing our heart from superfluous occupation, from disordered affection, from all sluggishness.

paras.t: Precatio. Pro tua pietate, Domine, da nobis, quæsumus, bonæ operationis studiis sic jugiter invigilare, quo nos tibi Domino locum inveniamus in corde nostro: sit tua præsentia nostra ubique defensio, et nostris confusis inimicis, tua super nos semper floreat sanctificatio.
paras.en: Prayer. Of thy loving kindness, O Lord, grant us, we beseech thee, so to keep watch continually in the pursuit of good works that we may find in our heart a place for thee, the Lord: may thy presence be our defence everywhere, and, our enemies being confounded, may thy sanctification ever flourish upon us.

132.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI SECUNDI : ECCE QUAM BONUM.
132.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and thirty-second psalm: Behold how good.
132.note: The beginning of this article (the title of the psalm and Denis's first exposition of v. 1) is missing from the transcription and is marked […].

paras.t: […] [Si] quis velit exponere tam extense, ut omnibus in gratia exsistentibus congruat, sensus erit: Ecce quam bonum, etc., in unum, id est, concorditer habitando in Ecclesia Christi sub una fide, spe et caritate, ut sint omnes unum in Christo, quemadmodum Apostolus loquitur: Etenim in uno Spiritu in unum corpus baptizati sumus, sive Judæi, sive gentiles, sive servi, sive liberi; et omnes uno Spiritu potati sumus.
paras.en: […] [the opening of the article, with the title of the psalm and Denis's first exposition of v. 1, is missing from the transcription] if anyone wishes to expound it so widely that it fits all who are in grace, the sense will be: [[132:1|Behold how good|Ecce quam bonum]], etc., [[132:1|in unity|in unum]], that is, dwelling in concord in the Church of Christ under one faith, hope and charity, so that all may be one in Christ, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 12:13|For in one Spirit were we all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Gentiles, whether bond or free: and in one Spirit we have all been made to drink.|Etenim in uno Spiritu in unum corpus baptizati sumus, sive Judæi, sive gentiles, sive servi, sive liberi; et omnes uno Spiritu potati sumus]]

paras.t: Secundum primam autem expositionem convenit psalmus iste præsertim claustralibus: quorum esse debet major concordia, quam aliorum, ita ut multitudinis fratrum sit cor unum et anima una, sicut Dominus alibi ait: Dabo eis cor unum et animam unam. Summa nihilo minus est anachoretarum perfectio: quæ est magis divina, quam humana. Nam homo solus, est, aut deus, aut bestia; non essentialiter, sed participative.
paras.en: But according to the first exposition this psalm especially suits those who live in the cloister, among whom there ought to be greater concord than among others, so that the multitude of the brethren [[Acts 4:32|had but one heart and one soul|sit cor unum et anima una]]; as the Lord says elsewhere: [[Jer 32:39|I will give them one heart|Dabo eis cor unum]], and one soul [the Douay-Rheims, following the Vulgate, has “and one way”; Denis reads et animam unam]. None the less, the perfection of anchorites is the highest, being more divine than human. For man alone is either a god or a beast [the saying is Aristotle's, Politics I, 2]: not in essence, but by participation.

paras.t: Deinde ponit exemplum bipartitum, seu duplex de isto. Sicut unguentum in capite, quod descendit in barbam, barbam Aaron: id est, sicut unguentum seu oleum, quo in veteri Testamento consecrabatur summus sacerdos, erat valde pretiosum, dulce, et optime redolens; sic vehementer virtuosum, suave, et Deo placitum est, habitare fratres in unum per caritatem. Caritas enim omnium virtutum altissima est, et nulla virtus tam dulciter, prompte ac delectabiliter operatur ut ipsa, secundum quod in Canticis scribitur: Fortis est ut mors dilectio; et, Aquæ multæ non poterunt exstinguere caritatem. Ait ergo: Sicut unguentum in capite summi sacerdotis legalis, quod descendit a capite uncto in barbam, non cujuslibet, sed barbam Aaron, primi pontificis legalis, per quem alii designantur. Soli enim summi sacerdotes ungebantur hoc oleo, quantum ad sacerdotes. Ungebantur autem et reges atque Prophetæ eo modo, quo Dominus dixit Eliæ: Eliseum unges prophetam pro te. Quod unguentum descendit a barba, fluendo in oram superiorem vestimenti ejus, id est summi sacerdotis. Fluxit enim oleum istud, dum ungebatur summus sacerdos, a capite per barbam usque ad superiorem oram tunicæ hyacinthinæ et superhumeralis.
paras.en: Then he gives a twofold, or double, example of this. [[132:2|Like the precious ointment on the head, that ran down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron|Sicut unguentum in capite, quod descendit in barbam, barbam Aaron]]: that is, as the ointment or oil with which the high priest was consecrated in the Old Testament[[Ex 30:23||]] was very precious, sweet, and most fragrant, so it is exceedingly virtuous, sweet, and pleasing to God [[132:1|for brethren to dwell together in unity|habitare fratres in unum]] through charity. For charity is the highest of all the virtues, and no virtue works so sweetly, readily and delightfully as it does, according to what is written in the Canticle: [[Cant 8:6|love is strong as death|Fortis est ut mors dilectio]]; and, [[Cant 8:7|Many waters cannot quench charity|Aquæ multæ non poterunt exstinguere caritatem]]. He says, then: [[132:2|Like the precious ointment on the head|Sicut unguentum in capite]] of the high priest of the Law, [[132:2|that ran down|quod descendit]] from the anointed head [[132:2|upon the beard|in barbam]], not of anyone at all, but [[132:2|the beard of Aaron|barbam Aaron]], the first high priest of the Law, by whom the others are signified. For of priests, only the high priests were anointed with this oil. But kings and Prophets were also anointed, in the way in which the Lord said to Elias: [[3 Kings 19:16|Eliseus, the son of Saphat, of Abelmeula, thou shalt anoint to be prophet in thy room|Eliseum unges prophetam pro te]]. [[132:2|Which|Quod]] ointment [[132:2|ran down|descendit]] from the beard, flowing [[132:2|to the skirt|in oram]], the upper edge, [[132:2|of his garment|vestimenti ejus]], that is, of the high priest's. For this oil, when the high priest was anointed, flowed from the head through the beard down to the upper edge of the violet tunic and of the ephod[[Ex 29:7||]][[Lev 8:12||]].

paras.t: Sicut ros Hermon, qui descendit in montem Sion. Hic ponit secundum exemplum; et est sensus: Sicut ros montis qui dicitur Hermon, est bonus et causa lætitiæ, quoniam efficit montem illum fructuosum; sic bonum atque jucundum est habitare fratres in unum. Qui ros descendit in montem Sion: id est, ros similis in specie rori montis Hermon, descendit in montem Sion, in quo fuerat templum.
paras.en: [[132:3|As the dew of Hermon, which descendeth upon mount Sion|Sicut ros Hermon, qui descendit in montem Sion]]. Here he gives the second example; and the sense is: as the dew of the mountain called Hermon is good and a cause of gladness, since it makes that mountain fruitful, so it is good and pleasant [[132:1|for brethren to dwell together in unity|habitare fratres in unum]]. [[132:3|which descendeth upon mount Sion|Qui ros descendit in montem Sion]]: that is, a dew like in kind to the dew of mount Hermon comes down upon mount Sion, on which the temple had stood.

paras.t: Moraliter ita exponitur: Bonum et jucundum est fratres habitare in unum, sicut unguentum in capite, id est, sicut bona est gratia existens in Christo, qui est caput Ecclesiæ: quod descendit in barbam, barbam Aaron, id est, quæ gratia descendit a Christo in Apostolos ejus: qui significantur per barbam, eo quod barba sit signum virilitatis, et ipsi in bello pro fide fortissimi perstiterunt. Per Aaron ergo intelligitur Christus, summus sacerdos Ecclesiæ, qui per Spiritum Sanctum semetipsum obtulit immaculatum Deo. Quod descendit in oram vestimenti ejus, id est, quæ gratia Spiritus Sancti descendit a Christo per Apostolos in Ecclesiam: quæ significatur per oram vestimenti Christi, quoniam, sicut vestimentum est ornamentum vestiti, ita Ecclesia est decor quodammodo Christi, tanquam sponsa ipsius. Insuper bonum et item jucundum est fratres habitare in unum, sicut bonus est ros Hermon, id est spiritualis fecunditatio Christi. Hermon namque interpretatur, lumen exaltatum: sicque significat Christum, qui est lumen verum super omnes cœlos exaltatum. Qui descendit in montem Sion, id est, quæ fecunditas diffusa est in animam speculativam, bonis operibus plenam.
paras.en: Morally it is expounded thus: it is good and pleasant [[132:1|for brethren to dwell together in unity|fratres habitare in unum]], [[132:2|Like the precious ointment on the head|sicut unguentum in capite]], that is, as good as is the grace that is in Christ, who is the head of the Church[[Eph 5:23||]]: [[132:2|that ran down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron|quod descendit in barbam, barbam Aaron]], that is, which grace came down from Christ upon his Apostles, who are signified by the beard, because the beard is a sign of manhood, and they stood most valiant in the war for the faith. By Aaron, then, is understood Christ, the high priest of the Church, [[Heb 9:14|who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God|qui per Spiritum Sanctum semetipsum obtulit immaculatum Deo]]. [[132:2|Which ran down to the skirt of his garment|Quod descendit in oram vestimenti ejus]], that is, which grace of the Holy Ghost came down from Christ through the Apostles upon the Church, which is signified by the skirt of Christ's garment, since, as a garment is the adornment of the one who wears it, so the Church is in a manner the beauty of Christ, as being his bride. Moreover, it is good and likewise pleasant for brethren to dwell together in unity, as good as is [[132:3|the dew of Hermon|ros Hermon]], that is, the spiritual making fruitful that comes from Christ. For Hermon is interpreted “light exalted”, and so it signifies Christ, who is the true light, exalted above all the heavens. [[132:3|which descendeth upon mount Sion|Qui descendit in montem Sion]], that is, which fruitfulness is poured out upon the contemplative soul, full of good works.

paras.t: Quoniam illic, id est ad concordem fratrum cohabitationem, mandavit, id est misit, Dominus benedictionem, id est gratiarum cœlestium collationem, et vitam spiritualem usque in sæculum: quoniam taliter cohabitantes nunc vivunt per gratiam, in æternum victuri in cœlo per gloriam. Vel: Quoniam illic mandavit, id est præcepit, Dominus benedictionem, id est, in tali congregatione præcepit se benedici, qui a discordibus non dignatur laudari.
paras.en: [[132:3|For there|Quoniam illic]], that is, to the concordant dwelling together of brethren, [[132:3|the Lord hath commanded|mandavit Dominus]], that is, has sent, [[132:3|blessing|benedictionem]], that is, the bestowal of heavenly graces, [[132:3|and life|et vitam]], spiritual life, [[132:3|for evermore|usque in sæculum]]: since those who dwell together in this way live now by grace, and will live for ever in heaven by glory. Or: [[132:3|For there the Lord hath commanded blessing|Quoniam illic mandavit Dominus benedictionem]] [here taking mandavit as “commanded” rather than “sent”], that is, in such a congregation he has commanded that he be blessed, he who does not deign to be praised by those who are at discord.

paras.t: Hortatur nos divinus sermo psalmi præsentis ad inviolabilem fraternæ caritatis tenorem, ad pacificam cohabitationem, ad mutuam communicationem. Sine caritate namque nulla virtus meritoria est. Ipsa est omnis spiritualis profectus principium, medium et finis. Ipsa de claustro efficit paradisum, de monachis angelos. Odium vero, de claustro facit infernum, de religiosis diabolos. Qui in caritate non proficit, nil proficit; sine caritatis profectu corporalis exercitatio sterilis est. Solitudo, silentium, abstinentia, disciplina, cilicium, clausura, vigilia, duritia strati, nil prosunt ad vitam æternam sine præsentia caritatis. Idcirco Apostolus: Excellentiorem, inquit, vobis viam demonstro. Si linguis angelorum loquar et hominum, caritatem autem non habeam, factus sum velut æs sonans aut cymbalum tinniens. Unde in Petri Canonica scriptum est: Omnes unanimes, fraternitatis amatores, compatientes, misericordes, modesti, humiles, non reddentes malum pro malo; sed econtrario benedicentes, quia in hoc vocati estis.
paras.en: The divine word of the present psalm exhorts us to an unbroken course of brotherly charity, to peaceful dwelling together, to mutual sharing. For without charity no virtue is meritorious. It is the beginning, middle and end of all spiritual progress. It makes of a cloister a paradise, and of monks angels. But hatred makes of a cloister a hell, and of religious devils. He who does not advance in charity advances in nothing; without advance in charity bodily exercise is barren. Solitude, silence, abstinence, the discipline, the hair shirt, enclosure, vigils, a hard bed, profit nothing for eternal life without the presence of charity. Therefore the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 12:31|I shew unto you yet a more excellent way|Excellentiorem, inquit, vobis viam demonstro]]. [[1 Cor 13:1|If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.|Si linguis angelorum loquar et hominum, caritatem autem non habeam, factus sum velut æs sonans aut cymbalum tinniens]] Hence it is written in the Epistle of Peter: [[1 Pet 3:8|be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, being lovers of the brotherhood, merciful, modest, humble|Omnes unanimes, fraternitatis amatores, compatientes, misericordes, modesti, humiles]], [[1 Pet 3:9|Not rendering evil for evil|non reddentes malum pro malo]], [[1 Pet 3:9|but contrariwise, blessing: for unto this are you called|sed econtrario benedicentes, quia in hoc vocati estis]].

paras.t: Precatio. Largire nobis, Domine, gratiæ tuæ donum, ut in caritate concordes habitemus in unum: per quod suaviter apud te redolentes, benedictionem tuam et vitam consequamur in sæculum.
paras.en: Prayer. Grant us, O Lord, the gift of thy grace, that we may dwell together in unity, of one accord in charity: that thereby, being of sweet savour before thee, we may obtain thy blessing and life for evermore.

133.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI TRIGESIMI TERTII : ECCE NUNC BENEDICITE DOMINO.
133.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and thirty-third psalm: Behold now bless ye the Lord.

paras.t: Insuper titulus psalmi nunc exponendi talis est: Canticum graduum. Nam, sicut psalmus præcedens locutus est de caritate fraterna; sic iste de caritate divina eloquitur, quæ est quintusdecimus, summus et ultimus gradus spiritualis ascensionis. Realiter tamen idem sunt caritas Dei et proximi, quia virtutes distinguuntur per rationes formales. Ratio autem amandi proximum, Deus est. Porro psalmus iste ad litteram est invitatio sacerdotum ac Levitarum veteris Testamenti ad laudem divinam: et sic per domum Domini, designatur templum Jerusalem, in quo stabant sacerdotes et Levitæ ad orandum et immolandum.
paras.en: Further, the title of the psalm now to be expounded is this: [[133:1|A gradual canticle|Canticum graduum]]. For as the preceding psalm spoke of brotherly charity, so this one speaks of divine charity, which is the fifteenth, the highest and last step of the spiritual ascent. Yet in reality the charity of God and of our neighbour are the same, since virtues are distinguished by their formal reasons [that is, by the aspect under which they reach their object]; and the reason for loving our neighbour is God. Now according to the letter this psalm is an invitation to the priests and Levites of the Old Testament to the praise of God: and so by the house of the Lord is meant the temple of Jerusalem, in which the priests and Levites stood to pray and to offer sacrifice.

paras.t: Spiritualiter vero exponitur de universis fidelibus, et est sensus: Ecce nunc, id est tempore isto, de quo dicit Apostolus: Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis. De quo in Isaia habetur: Quærite Dominum dum inveniri potest, invocate eum dum prope est. Vel, Nunc, id est, ascensis gradibus præinductis. Benedicite Domino, id est, Deum laudate ex caritate ardente, omnes servi Domini, qui fide et opere Christiani estis. Qui enim prædictos virtutum gradus ascenderunt atque sortiti sunt, digni habentur benedicere Domino benedictione laudis et gratiarum actionis: quæ utique benedictio non est speciosa in ore peccatoris.
paras.en: But spiritually it is expounded of all the faithful, and the sense is: [[133:1|Behold now|Ecce nunc]], that is, in this time, of which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time: behold, now is the day of salvation|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis]]. Of which we have in Isaias: [[Is 55:6|Seek ye the Lord, while he may be found: call upon him, while he is near.|Quærite Dominum dum inveniri potest, invocate eum dum prope est]] Or, [[133:1|now|Nunc]], that is, when the steps set out before have been climbed. [[133:1|bless ye the Lord|Benedicite Domino]], that is, praise God out of burning charity, [[133:1|all ye servants of the Lord|omnes servi Domini]], who are Christians in faith and in deed. For those who have climbed and attained the steps of virtue spoken of are held worthy to bless the Lord with the blessing of praise and thanksgiving: which blessing indeed [[Ecclus 15:9|is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner|non est speciosa in ore peccatoris]].

paras.t: Qui statis in domo Domini, id est, qui stabiliter estis Ecclesiæ filii, perseverantes constanter in ecclesiastica unitate, id est in vera fide et caritate; et qui statis in atriis domus Dei nostri, id est in primis seu amplioribus locis Ecclesiæ, quæ sunt materialia atria ejus. Vel: In atriis, id est in latitudine caritatis, domus Dei nostri, id est fidelis animæ, quæ est domus et sedes Sapientiæ increatæ.
paras.en: [[133:1|Who stand in the house of the Lord|Qui statis in domo Domini]], that is, who are steadfastly sons of the Church, persevering constantly in the unity of the Church, that is, in true faith and charity; and who stand [[133:1|in the courts of the house of our God|in atriis domus Dei nostri]], that is, in the first or more spacious parts of the church, which are its material courts. Or: [[133:1|in the courts|In atriis]], that is, in the breadth of charity, [[133:1|of the house of our God|domus Dei nostri]], that is, of the faithful soul, which is the house and seat of the uncreated Wisdom[[Wis 7:27||]].

paras.t: In noctibus, id est tempore nocturno, juxta illud: Consurge, lauda in nocte; vel, In noctibus, id est tempore adversitatis; vel, In noctibus, id est toto tempore vitæ præsentis, quod innumerabilibus vitiorum tenebris, tribulationumque pressuris obtenebratur. Propter quod in tenebris et in umbra mortis sedere perhibemur. Extollite manus vestras corporales ac spirituales, quæ sunt desideria ad superna tendentia, in sancta, id est in cœlestia, quatenus ea adipisci et ingredi valeatis. De quibus ait Apostolus: Christus per proprium sanguinem introivit semel in Sancta. Debemus autem utrasque manus cum ferventissimo semper affectu extollere, juxta illud Apostoli: Volo viros orare in omni loco, levantes puras manus, etc. Et benedicite Domino indesinenter.
paras.en: [[133:2|In the nights|In noctibus]], that is, in the night-time, according to that saying: [[Lam 2:19|Arise, give praise in the night|Consurge, lauda in nocte]]; or, [[133:2|In the nights|In noctibus]], that is, in the time of adversity; or, [[133:2|In the nights|In noctibus]], that is, in the whole time of this present life, which is darkened by the countless darknesses of vices and the pressures of tribulations. For which reason we are said to [[Luke 1:79|sit in darkness and in the shadow of death|in tenebris et in umbra mortis sedere]]. [[133:2|lift up your hands|Extollite manus vestras]], bodily and spiritual, which are desires reaching up to the things above, [[133:2|to the holy places|in sancta]], that is, to heavenly things, so that you may be able to attain and enter them. Of which the Apostle says: Christ [[Heb 9:12|by his own blood, entered once into the Holies|per proprium sanguinem introivit semel in Sancta]]. And we ought always to lift up both hands with the most fervent affection, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Tim 2:8|I will therefore that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands|Volo viros orare in omni loco, levantes puras manus]], etc. [[133:2|and bless ye the Lord|Et benedicite Domino]] unceasingly.

paras.t: Et ut hoc queas perficere, o serve atque Ecclesia Dei, Benedicat te Dominus, id est, gratiæ dona tibi infundat, ex Sion, id est ex cœlesti Jerusalem, ubi ipse specialiter habitat, qui fecit cœlum et terram ex nihilo, tanquam Creator omnipotens: cui subest, quum voluerit, posse; cui non est difficile omne verbum; qui in infinitum plura atque majora potest efficere, quam possit mens humana concipere.
paras.en: And that thou mayest be able to accomplish this, O servant and Church of God, may the Lord [[133:3|bless thee|Benedicat te Dominus]], that is, pour into thee the gifts of grace, [[133:3|out of Sion|ex Sion]], that is, out of the heavenly Jerusalem, where he especially dwells, [[133:3|he that made heaven and earth|qui fecit cœlum et terram]] out of nothing, as the almighty Creator: [[Wis 12:18|thy power is at hand when thou wilt|cui subest, quum voluerit, posse]] [Denis turns the words of Wis 12:18, “for thy power is at hand when thou wilt”, to the third person]; to whom [[Jer 32:17|no word shall be hard|non est difficile omne verbum]]; who can do infinitely more and greater things than the human mind can conceive.

paras.t: Sed quid est quod in principio psalmi hortatur nos sanctus Propheta benedicere Domino, nunc vero precatur ut Dominus nos benedicat? Et respondendum, quod duplex est benedictio, scilicet consecrationis et laudis. De benedictione consecrationis dicit Apostolus: Sine ulla contradictione, quod minus est, a majore benedicitur. Hac ergo benedictione benedicit nos Deus. Benedictione vero laudis minor benedicit majori, et creatura Creatorem.
paras.en: But how is it that at the beginning of the psalm the holy Prophet exhorts us to bless the Lord, and now prays that the Lord may bless us? The answer is that blessing is twofold, namely of consecration and of praise. Of the blessing of consecration the Apostle says: [[Heb 7:7|And without all contradiction, that which is less is blessed by the better.|Sine ulla contradictione, quod minus est, a majore benedicitur]] With this blessing, then, God blesses us. But with the blessing of praise the lesser blesses the greater, and the creature the Creator.

paras.t: Postremo psalmum istum affectuosum ac dulcem decet nos hora Completorii cum speciali devotione cantare, dirigendo mentem ad Creatorem, atque in ejus præconiis diem concludere, obdormiendo in meditationibus divinorum.
paras.en: Lastly, it befits us to sing this tender and sweet psalm at the hour of Compline with special devotion, directing the mind to the Creator, and to close the day in his praises, falling asleep in meditation on divine things.

paras.t: Precatio. In sancta devotione in noctibus hujus sæculi, Domine, in domo tua et in atriis tuis stantes, fac nos tibi servientes benedicere; teque nobis benedicentibus, tu, Domine, benedicas nos ex Sion propitius.
paras.en: Prayer. Grant, O Lord, that standing in holy devotion in the nights of this world, in thy house and in thy courts, we may serve thee and bless thee; and as we bless thee, do thou, O Lord, graciously bless us out of Sion.

134.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI QUARTI : LAUDATE NOMEN DOMINI.
134.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and thirty-fourth psalm: Praise ye the name of the Lord.

paras.t: Præterea psalmi præsentis titulus est : Alleluia : cujus interpretatio est, Laudate Dominum. Merito autem post psalmos graduales ponitur psalmus, Alleluia pro titulo habens : quoniam gradus spiritualis ascensionis perambulans, sicque ad veram perfectionem pertingens, dignus est Deum laudare.
paras.en: Further, the title of the present psalm is: [[134:1|Alleluia|Alleluia]], which is interpreted, Praise ye the Lord. And fittingly a psalm having Alleluia for its title is placed after the gradual psalms [that is, the fifteen "gradual canticles", Ps 119–133, sung as the people went up to Jerusalem]: for he who walks the steps of the spiritual ascent, and so attains to true perfection, is worthy to praise God.

paras.t: Psalmus vero iste hortatur nos ad laudem divinam propter multiplicem rationem, et ait : Laudate, o universi fideles, nomen Domini, id est Dominum nomine designatum, seu rem significatam per nomen ; laudate, servi justitiæ, non servi peccati, Dominum. Qui statis fide constanti et opere efficaci in domo Domini, id est in ecclesia materiali, quæ est domus orationis et laudis ; vel, In domo Domini, id est in Ecclesia militante et spirituali, seu congregatione fidelium, qui omnes sunt unum mysticum corpus Christi, recipientes ab eo motum virtutum et vitam gratiæ ; et qui statis in atriis domus Dei nostri. Versiculus iste in præcedenti psalmo expositus est.
paras.en: This psalm exhorts us to the praise of God for many reasons, and says: [[134:1|Praise ye|Laudate]], O all ye faithful, [[134:1|the name of the Lord|nomen Domini]], that is, the Lord designated by the name, or the thing signified by the name; [[134:1|O you his servants, praise the Lord|laudate, servi, Dominum]]: servants of justice, that is, not servants of sin. [[134:2|You that stand|Qui statis]] with constant faith and effective works [[134:2|in the house of the Lord|in domo Domini]], that is, in the material church, which is a house of prayer and praise; or, [[134:2|In the house of the Lord|In domo Domini]], that is, in the Church militant and spiritual, or the congregation of the faithful, who are all one mystical body of Christ, receiving from him the movement of the virtues and the life of grace; and you that stand [[134:2|in the courts of the house of our God|in atriis domus Dei nostri]]. This verse has been explained in the preceding psalm[[Ps 133:1||]].

paras.t: Laudate Dominum, quoniam bonus Dominus. Deus enim sanctus et benedictus, essentialiter, incircumscriptibiliter et quomodolibet bonus est, et ipse est omnis boni principium, quem omnia naturaliter appetunt tanquam ultimum finem, sine cujus incessabili conservatione nec in momento subsistere possent. Ideo ait Salvator : Quid me dicis bonum? Nemo bonus nisi solus Deus. Psallite nomini ejus, quoniam suave. Proprium nomen Domini Creatoris, est Deus : et quid dulcius Deo? imo quid vel in minimo comparari poterit dulcedini Dei? Cujus est tanta dulcedo, quanta bonitas ; qui in se ipso infinita dulcedine æternaliter fruitur, omnesque Beatos in patria inexcogitabili suavitate perfundit, nos quoque in hac valle lacrimarum subinde dulciter visitat, pie lætificat, excessive exhilarat, supernaturaliterque reficit.
paras.en: [[134:3|Praise ye the Lord, for the Lord is good|Laudate Dominum, quoniam bonus Dominus]]. For God, holy and blessed, is good essentially, without circumscription [that is, without any limit that could bound or contain his goodness], and in every way; and he is himself the principle of all good, whom all things naturally desire as their last end, and without whose unceasing preservation they could not subsist even for a moment. Therefore the Saviour says: [[Luke 18:19|Why dost thou call me good? None is good but God alone|Quid me dicis bonum? Nemo bonus nisi solus Deus]] [no reference in the margin; the words are as in Luke 18:19, nearly so in Mark 10:18]. [[134:3|sing ye to his name, for it is sweet|Psallite nomini ejus, quoniam suave]]. The proper name of the Lord the Creator is God: and what is sweeter than God? Nay, what could be compared, even in the least degree, to the sweetness of God? His sweetness is as great as his goodness; he enjoys infinite sweetness in himself eternally, and floods all the Blessed in the fatherland with a sweetness past all imagining; us too, in this vale of tears, he visits sweetly from time to time, gladdens lovingly, cheers beyond measure, and refreshes supernaturally.

paras.t: Psallendum est etiam Domino propter beneficia ejus, videlicet, Quoniam Jacob elegit sibi Dominus, Israel in possessionem sibi. Jacob qui interpretatur supplantator, alio nomine dictus est Israel, quod interpretatur, vir videns Deum. Sive autem per Jacob et Israel intelligatur persona Jacob, sive populus ab eo descendens, certum est quod Deus eum elegit, quemadmodum Moyses profitetur populo huic : Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus, et elegit eos, amavitque semen eorum post eos. Et iterum : Te elegit Dominus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram. Et ideo dicitur elegisse Israel in possessionem, id est in hereditatem seu hereditarium populum, sicut per Isaiam loquitur : Hereditas mea Israel. Et Samuel dixit ad Saul : Ecce unxit te Dominus super hereditatem suam in principem. Spiritualiter vero per Jacob intelligitur quilibet contra vitia luctans; per Israel vero, omnis Deum fideliter speculans : quod maxime competit veris Christianis, seu Ecclesiæ Christi; et hos Deus elegit in possessionem æternam, possidens eos in via per gratiam, in patria autem per gloriam. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Deus prædestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum per Jesum Christum, secundum propositum voluntatis suæ.
paras.en: We must sing to the Lord also because of his benefits, namely, [[134:4|For the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself: Israel for his own possession|Quoniam Jacob elegit sibi Dominus, Israel in possessionem sibi]]. Jacob, which is interpreted supplanter[[Gen 27:36||]], was by another name called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]] [the margin gives "Ibid. xxvii, 28"; the renaming is at Gen 32:28], which is interpreted, a man seeing God. Now whether by Jacob and Israel is understood the person of Jacob, or the people descended from him, it is certain that God chose him, as Moses declares to this people: [[Deut 10:15|the Lord hath been closely joined to thy fathers|Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus]], and chose them, and loved [[Deut 10:15|their seed after them|semen eorum post eos]] [the margin gives Deut. v, 15; the words are Deut 10:15, where they run "and loved them and chose their seed after them"]. And again: [[Deut 7:6|The Lord thy God hath chosen thee, to be his peculiar people of all peoples that are upon the earth|Te elegit Dominus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram]]. And therefore he is said to have chosen Israel for a possession, that is, for an inheritance or an inherited people, as he speaks by Isaias: [[Is 19:25|Israel is my inheritance|Hereditas mea Israel]] [the margin gives Is. xlix, 25; the words are Is 19:25]. And Samuel said to Saul: [[1 Kings 10:1|Behold, the Lord hath anointed thee to be prince over his inheritance|Ecce unxit te Dominus super hereditatem suam in principem]]. Spiritually, however, by Jacob is understood anyone who wrestles against vices; and by Israel, everyone who faithfully contemplates God: which belongs above all to true Christians, or the Church of Christ; and these God has chosen for an eternal possession, possessing them on the way through grace, and in the fatherland through glory. Wherefore the Apostle says: God [[Eph 1:5|hath predestinated us unto the adoption of children through Jesus Christ|prædestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum per Jesum Christum]], [[Eph 1:5|according to the purpose of his will|secundum propositum voluntatis suæ]].

paras.t: Quia ego cognovi per fidem, per rationem naturalem, per experientiam, per divinæ dulcedinis gustum, quod magnus est Dominus, non magnitudine molis, sed dignitatis : imo vere infinitus est Dominus, et perfectionis ejus nullus est terminus ; et Deus noster, videlicet Trinitas superbenedicta, quæ est Deitas simplex et adoranda, præ omnibus diis magnus est, quia in infinitum omnes excedit : sive per deos intelligantur excellentes creaturæ, videlicet angeli sancti et homines summi, qui dii vocantur; sive per deos intelligantur dii seu idola gentium, qui mendaciter dii dicuntur. Hoc modo Jethro cognatus Moysis novit magnitudinem Domini, dicens : Nunc cognovi quoniam magnus Dominus super omnes deos. Hinc etiam scriptum est : Excelsior cœlo est, et quid facies? profundior inferno, et unde cognosces? Longior terra mensura ejus, et latior mari.
paras.en: [[134:5|For I have known|Quia ego cognovi]], by faith, by natural reason, by experience, by the taste of the divine sweetness, [[134:5|that the Lord is great|quod magnus est Dominus]], not in greatness of bulk but of dignity: nay, the Lord is truly infinite, and of his perfection there is no bound; [[134:5|and our God|et Deus noster]], namely the superblessed Trinity, which is the simple and adorable Godhead, is great [[134:5|above all gods|præ omnibus diis]], because he exceeds them all infinitely: whether by gods are understood excellent creatures, namely the holy angels and the highest men, who are called gods; or by gods are understood the gods or idols of the Gentiles, who are falsely called gods. In this way Jethro, Moses' kinsman, knew the greatness of the Lord, saying: [[Ex 18:11|Now I know, that the Lord is great above all gods|Nunc cognovi quoniam magnus Dominus super omnes deos]]. Hence too it is written: [[Job 11:8|He is higher than heaven, and what wilt thou do? he is deeper than hell, and how wilt thou know?|Excelsior cœlo est, et quid facies? profundior inferno, et unde cognosces?]] [[Job 11:9|The measure of him is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea|Longior terra mensura ejus, et latior mari]].

paras.t: Omnia quæcumque voluit Dominus, fecit in cœlo et in terra, tam in operibus naturæ, quam in operibus gratiæ. Deo enim nihil difficile est, ut dicit Jeremias. Et ipse testatur : Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet. In cœlo namque condidit angelos atque angelicos ordines tot, quando, et quomodo voluit. Denique quos voluit, præservavit a ruina, et quos voluit, permisit peccare. Similiter fecit in terra, in hominibus, in mari Oceano et in omnibus abyssis particularibus. In his enim magna fecit opera, tam in navigantibus, quorum quosdam mirabiliter liberavit, ut Jonam; quam in piscibus, quorum diversa mirandaque genera inveniuntur in abyssis.
paras.en: [[134:6|Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done, in heaven, in earth|Omnia quæcumque voluit Dominus, fecit in cœlo et in terra]], both in the works of nature and in the works of grace. For nothing is hard for God, as Jeremias says[[Jer 32:17||]][[Jer 32:27||]]. And he himself testifies: [[Is 46:10|My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done|Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet]]. For in heaven he made the angels, and as many orders of angels as he willed, when and how he willed. Then, those whom he willed he preserved from the fall, and those whom he willed he permitted to sin. Likewise he did in the earth, among men, [[134:6|in the sea|in mari]], the Ocean, [[134:6|and in all the deeps|et in omnibus abyssis]] in particular. For in these he has done great works, both among seafarers, some of whom he has wonderfully delivered, as Jonas[[Jon 2:1||]][[Jon 2:11||]]; and among the fishes, of which diverse and wonderful kinds are found in the deeps.

paras.t: Educens ipse Dominus motu et calore solis, vel supernaturaliter, nubes ab extremo terræ, elevando videlicet vapores ex quibus nubes causantur, a mari Oceano, unde (ut sæpius) nubes ascendunt. Propter quod ad Job Dominus ait : Quum ponerem nubem vestimentum ejus, scilicet maris. Fulgura in pluviam fecit, id est, terminavit. In nubibus enim fieri solent tonitrua, ex quibus coruscationes et fulgura prodeunt; terminanturque fulgura ista per hoc, quod nubes resolvuntur in pluviam. Unde alibi dicitur : Qui vocat aquas et effundit eas super faciem terræ. In quo apparet infinita sapientia Dei. Cur enim in nubes condenset aquas, ostenditur apud Job : Qui ligat aquas in nubibus, ut non erumpant pariter deorsum. Si enim simul erumperent, omnia subverterentur, sicut idem fatetur : Si continuerit aquas, omnia siccabuntur ; si emiserit eas, subvertent terram. Producit igitur nubes, et ordinatissime irrigat mundum. Qui producit ventos de thesauris suis. Thesauri appellantur divitiæ occultatæ. Per thesauros ergo intelliguntur divitiæ bonitatis divinæ, id est omnipotentia Dei, qua sufficit omnia agere prout vult; vel causæ creatæ, ex quibus virtus divina ventos producit, sicut ex thesauro proferuntur denarii. Ait itaque : Qui producit ventos de thesauris suis, id est de plenitudine propriæ voluntatis ; vel, De thesauris suis, id est de causis creatis, videlicet de materia copiosa ac diviti ad hoc ut ex ea producantur venti. Alii sic exponunt, De thesauris suis, id est de locis ignotis, sicut thesauri ponuntur in loco occulto. Sunt ergo thesauri venti ; sunt quoque thesauri nivis et grandinis : de quibus Dominus ait ad Job, Numquid ingressus es thesauros nivis, aut thesauros grandinis adspexisti?
paras.en: [[134:7|He bringeth up|Educens]], that is, the Lord himself, by the motion and heat of the sun, or supernaturally, [[134:7|clouds from the end of the earth|nubes ab extremo terræ]], namely by raising up the vapours from which clouds are caused, from the Ocean sea, whence (as is most often the case) the clouds rise. Wherefore the Lord says to Job: [[Job 38:9|When I made a cloud the garment thereof|Quum ponerem nubem vestimentum ejus]], that is, of the sea. [[134:7|he hath made lightnings for the rain|Fulgura in pluviam fecit]], that is, he has ended them in rain [Denis reads *fecit* here as *terminavit*, "brought to an end"]. For thunders commonly arise in the clouds, and from them come forth flashes and lightnings; and these lightnings are ended by the clouds' dissolving into rain. Hence it is said elsewhere: [[Amos 5:8|that calleth the waters|Qui vocat aquas]] [[Amos 5:8|and poureth them out upon the face of the earth|et effundit eas super faciem terræ]]. In this the infinite wisdom of God appears. For why he thickens the waters into clouds is shown in Job: [[Job 26:8|He bindeth up the waters in his clouds, so that they break not out and fall down together|Qui ligat aquas in nubibus, ut non erumpant pariter deorsum]]. For if they broke out all at once, all things would be overturned, as the same book declares: [[Job 12:15|If he withhold the waters, all things shall be dried up: and if he send them out, they shall overturn the earth|Si continuerit aquas, omnia siccabuntur ; si emiserit eas, subvertent terram]]. He brings up the clouds, then, and waters the world in the most ordered way. [[134:7|He bringeth forth winds out of his stores|Qui producit ventos de thesauris suis]] [*thesauri*, "treasures"; the Douay-Rheims has "stores"]. Hidden riches are called treasures. By the treasures, therefore, are understood the riches of the divine goodness, that is, the omnipotence of God, by which he suffices to do all things as he wills; or created causes, from which the divine power brings forth the winds, as coins are brought out of a treasury. So he says: [[134:7|He bringeth forth winds out of his stores|Qui producit ventos de thesauris suis]], that is, from the fulness of his own will; or, [[134:7|out of his stores|De thesauris suis]], that is, from created causes, namely from matter abundant and rich enough for winds to be brought forth from it. Others expound it thus: [[134:7|out of his stores|De thesauris suis]], that is, from unknown places, as treasures are put in a hidden place. So there are treasures of the wind; there are also treasures of snow and hail, of which the Lord says to Job: [[Job 38:22|Hast thou entered into the storehouses of the snow, or hast thou beheld the treasures of the hail|Numquid ingressus es thesauros nivis, aut thesauros grandinis adspexisti?]]?

paras.t: Qui percussit primogenita Ægypti ab homine usque ad pecus inclusive, quemadmodum scriptum est : Decima plaga terræ Ægypti erat, quod Deus percussit in ea omne primogenitum, tam in hominibus quam in pecoribus. Et ista percussio facta est media nocte ab angelo Dei. Emisit Deus signa et prodigia, scilicet decem horribiles plagas, in medio tui, Ægypte; et non solum in terra, sed in habitatoribus ejus, sicut subjungitur : in Pharaonem regem Ægypti, et in omnes servos ejus, quorum multos tandem submersit in mari Rubro.
paras.en: [[134:8|He slew the firstborn of Egypt from man even unto beast|Qui percussit primogenita Ægypti ab homine usque ad pecus]], the beast included, as it is written: the tenth plague of the land of Egypt was that God slew in it every firstborn, both of men and of cattle. And this slaying was done at midnight by the angel of God[[Ex 12:29||]]. [[134:9|He sent forth|Emisit]], that is, God, [[134:9|signs and wonders|signa et prodigia]], namely the ten dreadful plagues, [[134:9|in the midst of thee, O Egypt|in medio tui, Ægypte]]; and not only on the land but on its inhabitants, as is added: [[134:9|upon Pharao|in Pharaonem]], king of Egypt, [[134:9|and upon all his servants|et in omnes servos ejus]], many of whom he at length drowned in the Red Sea[[Ex 14:27||]][[Ex 14:28||]].

paras.t: Qui percussit gentes multas in conspectu filiorum Israel, scilicet Amalecitas et alias multas. Nam quum elevaret Moyses manus, vincebat Israel; si autem paululum remisisset, vincebat Amalec. Et occidit reges fortes : quia virtute divina occiderunt eos filii Israel, videlicet, Sehon regem Amorrhæorum, et Og regem Basan, quorum terram possederunt filii Ruben, et Gad, et dimidia tribus Manasse, et omnia regna Chanaan, scilicet trans Jordanem, ubi Josue et filii Israel, Deo auxiliante, interfecerunt triginta unum reges. Et dedit terram eorum hereditatem, non quibuscumque, sed hereditatem Israel populo suo, videlicet novem tribubus et dimidiæ tribui Manasse, quibus Josue divisit terram per sortem, prout in diversis capitulis libri Josue recitatur.
paras.en: [[134:10|He smote many nations|Qui percussit gentes multas]] in the sight of the children of Israel, namely the Amalecites and many others. For [[Ex 17:11|when Moses lifted up his hands, Israel overcame|quum elevaret Moyses manus, vincebat Israel]]; [[Ex 17:11|but if he let them down a little, Amalec overcame|si autem paululum remisisset, vincebat Amalec]] [the margin gives Exod. xvii, 9–13]. [[134:10|and slew mighty kings|Et occidit reges fortes]]: because by divine power the children of Israel slew them, namely, [[134:11|Sehon king of the Amorrhites, and Og king of Basan|Sehon regem Amorrhæorum, et Og regem Basan]][[Num 21:24||]][[Num 21:35||]], whose land the sons of Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses possessed[[Num 32:33||]], [[134:11|and all the kingdoms of Chanaan|et omnia regna Chanaan]], namely across the Jordan, where Josue and the children of Israel, with God's help, slew thirty-one kings[[Jos 12:7||]][[Jos 12:24||]]. [[134:12|And gave their land for an inheritance|Et dedit terram eorum hereditatem]], not to just anyone, but [[134:12|for an inheritance to his people Israel|hereditatem Israel populo suo]], namely to the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasses, among whom Josue divided the land by lot[[Jos 13:7||]] [the margin gives Jos. xiii–xxi], as is related in various chapters of the book of Josue.

paras.t: Denique ista quæ ad litteram plana sunt, mystice intelligi possunt hoc modo : Educens Deus nubes ab extremo terræ, id est prædicatores sanctos a finibus mundi. Nam in omnibus terris gentilium ad fidem conversorum, fecit Deus ex gentilibus aliquos eximios prædicatores: qui nubes dicuntur, quoniam pluunt docendo, tonant comminando, coruscant miracula peragendo. Ideo quoque nubes dicuntur, quoniam supra ceteros penna contemplationis volant, terrena transiliunt, lumen veritatis a fonte sapientiæ prius copiosiusque participant. Unde de talibus scriptum est : Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant, et quasi columbæ ad fenestras suas? Fulgura in pluviam fecit, id est, terribiles comminationes de futuro judicio et pœnis inferni in dulces consolationes de futura felicitate Sanctorum mutavit. Prædicatores etenim terrent, comminando supplicia; et refrigerant, promittendo gaudia sempiterna. Qui producit ventos, id est inspirationes seu motiones ad bona, de thesauris suis, id est de divitiis suæ liberalissimæ Deitatis. Qui percussit primogenita Ægypti, id est, capitalia vitia hominum terrenorum destruxit, convertendo eos ad gratiam, ab homine usque ad pecus, id est a philosopho seu docto usque ad laicum seu indoctum. Emisit signa et prodigia in medio tui, Ægypte, id est per universum mundum : quemadmodum in Evangelio dicitur, Illi profecti prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante, et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis; et, Misit Jesus discipulos, dicens, Infirmos curate, mortuos suscitate, leprosos mundate, dæmones ejicite. In Pharaonem et in omnes servos ejus, id est principes hujus mundi et eorum satellites.
paras.en: Lastly, these things, which are plain according to the letter, can be understood mystically in this way: [[134:7|He bringeth up|Educens]], that is, God, [[134:7|clouds from the end of the earth|nubes ab extremo terræ]], that is, holy preachers from the ends of the world. For in all the lands of the Gentiles converted to the faith, God made some outstanding preachers out of the Gentiles; and they are called clouds because they rain by teaching, thunder by threatening, and flash by working miracles. They are called clouds also because they fly above the rest on the wing of contemplation, leap over earthly things, and share first and more abundantly in the light of truth from the fountain of wisdom. Hence it is written of such men: [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds, and as doves to their windows?|Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant, et quasi columbæ ad fenestras suas?]] [[134:7|he hath made lightnings for the rain|Fulgura in pluviam fecit]], that is, he has changed the terrible threats of the judgment to come and of the pains of hell into sweet consolations of the future happiness of the Saints. For preachers terrify by threatening punishments, and refresh by promising everlasting joys. [[134:7|He bringeth forth winds|Qui producit ventos]], that is, inspirations or movements towards good, [[134:7|out of his stores|de thesauris suis]], that is, from the riches of his most bountiful Godhead. [[134:8|He slew the firstborn of Egypt|Qui percussit primogenita Ægypti]], that is, he destroyed the capital vices of earthly men by converting them to grace, [[134:8|from man even unto beast|ab homine usque ad pecus]], that is, from the philosopher or learned man to the layman or unlearned.
