[[134:9|He sent forth signs and wonders in the midst of thee, O Egypt|Emisit signa et prodigia in medio tui, Ægypte]], that is, throughout the whole world: as is said in the Gospel, [[Mark 16:20|they going forth preached every where: the Lord working withal, and confirming the word with signs that followed|Illi profecti prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante, et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis]]; and, Jesus sent his disciples, saying[[Matt 10:5||]], [[Matt 10:8|Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out devils|Infirmos curate, mortuos suscitate, leprosos mundate, dæmones ejicite]]. [[134:9|upon Pharao, and upon all his servants|In Pharaonem et in omnes servos ejus]], that is, the princes of this world and their henchmen.

paras.t: Qui percussit gentes multas, et occidit reges fortes. Hoc accipi potest in bono atque in malo. Gentes enim et reges ad æternam vitam præordinatos, percussit et occidit Deus, non quantum ad esse naturæ, sed quantum ad esse culpæ. De qua occisione Christus testatur : Qui voluerit animam suam salvam facere, perdet eam. Sicque gentes et reges desierunt esse eo modo, quo in Proverbiis dicitur : Verte impios, et non erunt. Desierunt enim esse, non quod fuerunt, sed quales fuerunt. Secundo accipitur in malo, videlicet de gentibus et regibus reprobis, quos Deus percussit et occidit spiritualiter, deserendo eos in morte infidelitatis et culpæ : qualiter etiam dicitur indurasse Pharaonem. Sehon regem Amorrhæorum, etc. Sehon interpretatur, tentatio oculorum : unde significat luxuriosum. Og vero interpretatur congregans, et designat avarum. Talibus autem vitiis implicatos Deus occidit secundum modum prædictum. Et omnia regna Chanaan, id est superborum. Chanaan enim interpretatur possidens ; significatque superbos, quia superbi alios possidere præsidendo et dominando nituntur. Et dedit terram eorum, id est regnum cœlorum, quod est terra viventium : in qua dæmones superbi creati sunt, et ad quam possidendam universi homines facti sunt ; sed multi peccando se ipsos impediunt. Hanc autem terram dedit Deus in hereditatem populo suo christiano, electo et pauco, cui ait : Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum.
paras.en: [[134:10|He smote many nations, and slew mighty kings|Qui percussit gentes multas, et occidit reges fortes]]. This can be taken in a good sense and in a bad. For the nations and kings foreordained to eternal life God smote and slew, not as to their being in nature but as to their being in guilt. Of this slaying Christ testifies: [[Luke 9:24|whosoever will save his life shall lose it|Qui voluerit animam suam salvam facere, perdet eam]] [*animam*, "soul" or "life"]. And so the nations and kings ceased to be, in the way that is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]]. For they ceased to be, not what they were, but such as they were. Secondly, it is taken in the bad sense, namely of reprobate nations and kings, whom God smote and slew spiritually, by abandoning them in the death of unbelief and guilt: in the way in which he is also said to have hardened Pharao. [[134:11|Sehon king of the Amorrhites|Sehon regem Amorrhæorum]], etc. Sehon is interpreted, temptation of the eyes: hence he signifies the lustful man. Og is interpreted, gathering, and designates the covetous man. Those entangled in such vices God slays in the way already described. [[134:11|and all the kingdoms of Chanaan|Et omnia regna Chanaan]], that is, of the proud. For Chanaan is interpreted possessing; and it signifies the proud, because the proud strive to possess others by presiding and lording it over them. [[134:12|And gave their land|Et dedit terram eorum]], that is, the kingdom of heaven, which is the land of the living: in which the proud demons were created, and for the possession of which all men were made; but many hinder themselves by sinning. And this land God has given for an inheritance to his Christian people, chosen and few, to whom he says: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum]].

paras.t: Domine, nomen tuum in æternum permanebit, id est, æternaliter nominaberis ab adorantibus atque laudantibus te, præsertim in patria. Domine, memoriale tuum, id est gloriosa et memorabilis operatio tua, videlicet magna miseratio tua, recoletur et perseverabit in generationem et generationem, id est per omnium generationum successionem usque ad mundi consummationem. Hoc enim memoriale Dei in Evangelio Christi conscriptum est, nec tradetur oblivioni quamdiu Evangelium legitur, et Ecclesia durat.
paras.en: [[134:13|Thy name, O Lord, is for ever|Domine, nomen tuum in æternum]]: it will abide, that is, thou wilt be named eternally by those who adore and praise thee, above all in the fatherland. [[134:13|thy memorial, O Lord|Domine, memoriale tuum]], that is, thy glorious and memorable working, namely thy great mercy, will be recalled and will endure [[134:13|unto all generations|in generationem et generationem]], that is, through the succession of all generations until the consummation of the world. For this memorial of God is written in the Gospel of Christ, and it will not be given over to oblivion as long as the Gospel is read and the Church endures.

paras.t: Quia judicabit Dominus populum suum, et in servis suis deprecabitur. Istum versiculum, quantum ad verba et sensum, ponit Moyses, nisi quod ibi dicitur in fine versiculi, Miserebitur. Itaque, Judicabit Dominus populum suum, in præsenti vita judicio piæ discretionis, discernendo eos ab impiis voto, conversatione, et merito. Unde de hoc judicio ait : Nunc judicium est mundi. In die vero novissimo, vel in hora mortis eorum, judicaturus est eos judicio beatæ remunerationis, dando sententiam judicialem pro eis, sicut legitur in Apocalypsi : Exsultate, cœli et sancti Apostoli et Prophetæ, quoniam judicavit Deus judicium vestrum. Et in servis suis, qui sibi fide et opere parent, deprecabitur, exaudiendo preces eorum, juxta illud : Peccatores Deus non audit ; sed si quis est cultor Dei, et voluntatem ejus facit, hunc exaudit. Et in libro Job dicitur : Si Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus, si mundus et rectus incesseris, statim evigilabit ad te.
paras.en: [[134:14|For the Lord will judge his people, and will be entreated in favour of his servants|Quia judicabit Dominus populum suum, et in servis suis deprecabitur]]. Moses sets down this verse, as to its words and sense, except that there it says at the end of the verse, [[Deut 32:36|will have mercy|Miserebitur]]. So then, [[134:14|the Lord will judge his people|Judicabit Dominus populum suum]] in the present life by the judgment of loving discernment, distinguishing them from the wicked in desire, in manner of life, and in merit[[Ps 42:1||]] [the margin gives Ps. xli, 1; the verse that fits is Ps 42:1, "Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy"]. Hence of this judgment he says: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world|Nunc judicium est mundi]]. But on the last day, or in the hour of their death, he will judge them with the judgment of blessed reward, giving judicial sentence in their favour, as we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 18:20|Rejoice over her, thou heaven and ye holy apostles and prophets. For God hath judged your judgment|Exsultate, cœli et sancti Apostoli et Prophetæ, quoniam judicavit Deus judicium vestrum]] [Denis leaves out "over her"]. [[134:14|and will be entreated in favour of his servants|et in servis suis deprecabitur]], who obey him in faith and works, by hearing their prayers, according to that saying: [[John 9:31|God doth not hear sinners: but if a man be a server of God and doth his, will, him he heareth|Peccatores Deus non audit ; sed si quis est cultor Dei, et voluntatem ejus facit, hunc exaudit]]. And in the book of Job it is said: If thou [[Job 8:5|wilt beseech the Almighty|Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus]], [[Job 8:6|If thou wilt walk clean and upright, he will presently awake unto thee|si mundus et rectus incesseris, statim evigilabit ad te]].

paras.t: Simulacra gentium, quantum ad materiam, imo quoad totam substantiam, sunt argentum et aurum, seu simile aliquid : nam quædam ex ære, quædam ex stanno conflantur. Tota autem substantia artificialium, est eorum materia, secundum Philosophum. Sunt vero simulacra hæc opera manuum hominum, quantum ad formam accidentalem : nam artifices ea formant et faciunt. Os habent non verum, sed similitudinarium, et non loquentur : quamvis interdum dæmones per ipsa loquantur. Simili modo oculos habent, et non videbunt. Aures habent, et non audient. Cujus ratio est : neque enim est spiritus, id est forma vitalis, anima rationalis, aut certe anhelitus, in ore ipsorum : idcirco habere non valent opera vitæ, qualia sunt, loqui, videre, audire, etc. Similes illis simulacris fiant qui faciunt ea, puta artifices, et omnes qui confidunt in eis, videlicet homines vani, et maxime illi qui faciunt talia fieri : quatenus sicut simulacra illa non loquuntur, nec vident, nec audiunt, nec spiritum habent ; sic isti nec vera neque salubria proferant, intelligant, audiant, sed nec spiritum gratiæ sortiantur : quod non imprecando, sed prænuntiando dici putemus. De horum autem versuum litterali ac mystica explanatione plenius dictum est in expositione psalmi cujus exordium est, In exitu Israel de Ægypto.
paras.en: [[134:15|The idols of the Gentiles|Simulacra gentium]], as to their matter, nay, as to their whole substance, [[134:15|are silver and gold|sunt argentum et aurum]], or something like it: for some are cast of bronze, some of tin. Now the whole substance of artificial things is their matter, according to the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle]. But these idols are [[134:15|the works of men's hands|opera manuum hominum]] as to their accidental form: for craftsmen shape and make them. [[134:16|They have a mouth|Os habent]], not a true one but a likeness of one, [[134:16|but they speak not|et non loquentur]]: although sometimes demons speak through them. In like manner [[134:16|they have eyes, but they see not|oculos habent, et non videbunt]]. [[134:17|They have ears, but they hear not|Aures habent, et non audient]]. The reason for which is this: [[134:17|neither is there any breath|neque enim est spiritus]] [*spiritus*, "spirit" or "breath"], that is, a living form, a rational soul, or at any rate breathing, [[134:17|in their mouths|in ore ipsorum]]: and so they cannot have the works of life, such as speaking, seeing, hearing, etc. [[134:18|Let them that make them be like to them|Similes illis simulacris fiant qui faciunt ea]] (to those idols, that is): for instance, the craftsmen; [[134:18|and every one that trusteth in them|et omnes qui confidunt in eis]], namely vain men, and above all those who have such things made: so that, as those idols do not speak, nor see, nor hear, nor have breath, so these may neither utter, understand nor hear what is true or wholesome, nor yet obtain the spirit of grace: which let us take as said not by way of imprecation but of foretelling. Of the literal and mystical explanation of these verses more has been said in the exposition of the psalm whose beginning is, [[Ps 113:1|When Israel went out of Egypt|In exitu Israel de Ægypto]][[Ps 113:12||]] [the margin gives Ps. cxiii, 4–8 (Hebr.), that is, Ps 115:4–8 in the Hebrew numbering, Ps 113:12–16 in the Vulgate].

paras.t: Domus Israel, benedicite Domino. Ad litteram David hortatur Judæos ad laudem divinam, dicendo : Domus, id est populus, Israel, benedicite Domino, ipsum laudando : quod referendum est ad undecim tribus. Nam de Levi fit mentio specialis, dum subditur : Domus Aaron, id est sacerdotes legales ex Aaron nati, benedicite Domino. Domus Levi, id est familia, populus, seu congregatio Levitarum, benedicite Domino. Tamen domus Aaron etiam ex Levi descendit, quoniam (sicut scriptum est) Levi genuit Gerson, Caath et Merari. Caath vero genuit Ammam, de quo nati sunt Moyses, Aaron et Maria. Sed nunc accipiuntur Levitæ, prout a sacerdotibus distinguuntur, utpote pro inferioribus templi ministris. Spiritualiter per domum Israel, intelligenda est Ecclesia Christi ; per domum Levi, ministri altaris ; per domum Aaron, sacerdotes atque prælati Ecclesiæ militantis. Qui timetis Dominum timore filiali, vel saltem initiali (qui timores non differunt realiter, sed gradualiter, scilicet secundum perfectum et imperfectum), benedicite Domino. Tales quippe digni sunt Deum laudare, implentque quod dictum est supra : Servite Domino in timore, et exsultate ei cum tremore.
paras.en: [[134:19|Bless the Lord, O house of Israel|Domus Israel, benedicite Domino]]. According to the letter David exhorts the Jews to the praise of God, saying: O house, that is, people, of Israel, bless the Lord by praising him: which is to be referred to the eleven tribes. For special mention is made of Levi when it is added: [[134:19|O house of Aaron|Domus Aaron]], that is, the priests of the Law born of Aaron, [[134:19|bless the Lord|benedicite Domino]]. [[134:20|O house of Levi|Domus Levi]], that is, the family, people, or congregation of the Levites, [[134:20|Bless the Lord|benedicite Domino]]. Yet the house of Aaron also descends from Levi, since (as it is written) Levi begot Gerson, Caath and Merari[[Ex 6:16||]][[Num 26:57||]]. And Caath begot Ammam [the Douay-Rheims has Amram][[Ex 6:18||]], of whom were born Moses, Aaron and Mary[[Ex 6:20||]][[Num 26:59||]]. But here the Levites are taken as distinguished from the priests, that is, for the lower ministers of the temple. Spiritually, by the house of Israel is to be understood the Church of Christ; by the house of Levi, the ministers of the altar; by the house of Aaron, the priests and prelates of the Church militant. [[134:20|you that fear the Lord|Qui timetis Dominum]] with filial fear, or at least with initial fear (which fears differ not really but in degree, namely as perfect and imperfect) [that is, the fear of a son, which dreads offending God out of love, and the beginner's fear, which still has some dread of punishment mixed with it], [[134:20|bless the Lord|benedicite Domino]]. For such are worthy to praise God, and they fulfil what was said above: [[Ps 2:11|Serve ye the Lord with fear: and rejoice unto him with trembling|Servite Domino in timore, et exsultate ei cum tremore]].

paras.t: Benedictus Dominus ex Sion, id est, ex templo constructo in monte Sion benedicatur Deus, seu benedictus esse noscatur per hoc, quod in templo illo solenniter celebrantur laudes divinæ, qui habitat in Jerusalem, civitate metropoli in Judæa. Hanc enim Deus elegit, ut in ea templum ædificaretur : ad quod omnes Judæi certis temporibus confluebant, atque in eo sacrificia offerebant, quæ non licuit eis offerre nisi in uno loco, templo constructo. Unde in libro Regum sæpe redarguuntur, quoniam immolabant in excelsis, id est in locis sublimibus. Hinc Moyses loquens populo huic : Cave, inquit, ne offeras holocausta tua in omni loco quem videris, sed in eo quem elegerit Dominus in una tribuum tuarum. Hic autem locus fuit Jerusalem, prout Dominus loquitur : Elegi Jerusalem, ut sit nomen meum ibi. — Tropologice vero, Benedictus sit Dominus ex Sion, id est, ab Ecclesia militanti, divina contemplante, laudetur Deus omnium Dominus, qui habitat in Jerusalem cœlesti, scilicet in Ecclesia triumphanti, divinæ pacis dulcedine perfruente.
paras.en: [[134:21|Blessed be the Lord out of Sion|Benedictus Dominus ex Sion]], that is, let God be blessed out of the temple built on mount Sion, or be known to be blessed through this, that in that temple the divine praises are solemnly celebrated; [[134:21|who dwelleth in Jerusalem|qui habitat in Jerusalem]], the chief city in Judea. For God chose this city, that the temple might be built in it: to which all the Jews flocked at set times[[Deut 16:16||]], and in it they offered sacrifices, which it was not lawful for them to offer except in one place, once the temple was built. Hence in the book of Kings they are often rebuked because they sacrificed in the high places[[3 Kings 3:2||]], that is, in lofty places. Hence Moses, speaking to this people: [[Deut 12:13|Beware|Cave]], he says, [[Deut 12:13|lest thou offer thy holocausts in every place that thou shalt see|ne offeras holocausta tua in omni loco quem videris]]: [[Deut 12:14|But in the place which the Lord shall choose in one of thy tribes|sed in eo quem elegerit Dominus in una tribuum tuarum]]. And this place was Jerusalem, as the Lord says: [[2 Par 6:6|I chose Jerusalem, that my name might be there|Elegi Jerusalem, ut sit nomen meum ibi]]. Tropologically [that is, in the moral sense], [[134:21|Blessed be the Lord out of Sion|Benedictus sit Dominus ex Sion]], that is, let God, the Lord of all, be praised by the Church militant, which contemplates divine things, [[134:21|who dwelleth in Jerusalem|qui habitat in Jerusalem]], the heavenly one, namely in the Church triumphant, which enjoys the sweetness of the divine peace.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum decorum atque jucundum audivimus : in cujus principio invitamur ad benedicendum Domino Deo nostro, eo quod ipse bonus et dulcis existat, et nos gratis elegerit, atque universa potenter et libere condiderit. Igitur bono Domino, mente ab omni malitia purificata, reverenter ministremus ; suavique Domino sine zelo amaro, sine ira et disceptatione, sine omni perturbatione et amaritudine psallamus, benedicamus, obsequamur ac uniamur, pensantes illud Jacobi : Si zelum amarum habetis, et contentiones sunt inter vos, nolite gloriari, et mendaces esse adversus veritatem. Unde a Moyse dicitur : Non sit inter vos radix germinans fel et amaritudinem. Hinc quoque Apostolus exhortatur : Pacem sequimini cum omnibus, et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit ; contemplantes ne qua radix amaritudinis sursum germinans impediat, et per illam inquinentur multi.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a comely and delightful psalm: at its beginning we are invited to bless the Lord our God, because he is good and sweet, and has chosen us freely, and has made all things mightily and freely. Let us therefore serve the good Lord reverently, with a mind cleansed of all malice; and to the sweet Lord let us sing, let us bless him, obey him and be united to him, without bitter zeal, [[1 Tim 2:8|without anger and contention|sine ira et disceptatione]], without any disturbance or bitterness, weighing that saying of James: [[Jas 3:14|if you have bitter zeal, and there be contention|Si zelum amarum habetis, et contentiones sunt]] among you, [[Jas 3:14|glory not and be not liars against the truth|nolite gloriari, et mendaces esse adversus veritatem]]. Hence it is said by Moses: Let there not be among you [[Deut 29:18|a root bringing forth gall and bitterness|radix germinans fel et amaritudinem]]. Hence too the Apostle exhorts: [[Heb 12:14|Follow peace with all men and holiness: without which no man shall see God|Pacem sequimini cum omnibus, et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit]]; [[Heb 12:15|Looking diligently|contemplantes]], [[Heb 12:15|lest any root of bitterness springing up do hinder and by it many be defiled|ne qua radix amaritudinis sursum germinans impediat, et per illam inquinentur multi]].

paras.t: Precatio. Nos in Israel, Domine, nos tibi in possessionem elige, et post luctas hostium in pace constitue, et libere deservire concede ; et ut hac potiti libertate, nomini tuo, quod suave est, læti psallamus, teque Dominum semper benedicamus et laudemus.
paras.en: Prayer. Choose us, O Lord, into Israel; choose us for thy possession, and after our wrestlings with the enemy set us in peace, and grant us to serve thee freely; and that, having gained this freedom, we may joyfully sing to thy name, which is sweet, and ever bless and praise thee, the Lord.

135.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI QUINTI : CONFITEMINI DOMINO QUONIAM BONUS.
135.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and thirty-fifth psalm: Praise the Lord, for he is good.

paras.t: Est quoque titulus psalmi præsentis: Alleluia. Nam ad laudem divinam psalmus nos iste invitat; et in materia plurimum convenit cum psalmo immediate præhabito. Merito etiam additur in fine cujuslibet versus ista particula, Quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus: nam miserationes Dei sunt super omnia opera sua, imo quidquid boni in nobis est, ex misericordia Dei profluxit; incessabiliterque egemus misericordia Creatoris.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is also [[135:1|Alleluia|Alleluia]]. For this psalm invites us to the praise of God, and in its matter it agrees very closely with the psalm immediately before it. Fittingly, too, this little phrase is added at the end of each verse, [[135:1|for his mercy endureth for ever|Quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus]]: for [[Ps 144:9|his tender mercies are over all his works|miserationes Dei sunt super omnia opera sua]] [the margin gives Ps. cxiv, 9; the words are Ps 144:9]; indeed, whatever good is in us has flowed from the mercy of God, and we stand unceasingly in need of the Creator's mercy.

paras.t: Ait igitur: Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus, quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus. Versiculus iste in hac tertia quinquagena frequenter expositus est. Plures etenim psalmi ab hoc versu (ut patuit) inchoantur.
paras.en: He says, then: [[135:1|Praise the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever|Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus, quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus]]. This little verse has often been expounded in this third fifty [that is, the third group of fifty psalms, Pss. 101–150]. For several psalms (as has been seen) begin with this verse[[Ps 105:1||]][[Ps 106:1||]][[Ps 117:1||]].

paras.t: Confitemini laudando ac benedicendo, Deo deorum, id est Deo sancto et benedicto, vero, vivo, atque æterno, qui est Deus deorum, id est universorum qui vel participative, ut angeli sancti hominesque præcipui, vel mendaciter, ut dii gentilium idololatrarum, appellati sunt dii. Omnium enim horum Deus immensus et adorandus creator est: et eos qui participative dii dicuntur, salvavit per gratiam; eos vero qui mendaciter dii vocantur, et intellectuales creaturæ sunt, æternaliter condemnavit per æquitatis censuram, sicut sunt Jupiter, Mercurius, Saturnus, Mars, Hercules, atque consimiles.
paras.en: [[135:2|Praise ye|Confitemini]], by praising and blessing, [[135:2|the God of gods|Deo deorum]], that is, the God holy and blessed, true, living and eternal, who is [[Ps 49:1|The God of gods|Deus deorum]] [the margin gives Ps. xliv, 1; the words are Ps 49:1], that is, the God of all those who are called gods, whether by participation [that is, by a share in God's own life given through grace], as the holy angels and eminent men, or falsely, as the gods of the heathen idolaters. For of all these the immeasurable and adorable God is the creator; and those who are called gods by participation he has saved through grace, while those who are falsely called gods, and are intellectual creatures [that is, the demons worshipped under those names], he has condemned eternally by the sentence of his equity: such as Jupiter, Mercury, Saturn, Mars, Hercules and the like.

paras.t: Confitemini Domino dominorum, id est Deo qui omnibus universaliter dominatur, qui est Rex regum et Dominus dominantium, ad quem comparatur omnis creatura sicut minister ad dominum. De quo scriptum est: Deus cœlorum, Creator aquarum, et Dominus totius creaturæ; et iterum: Domine, Rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta posita sunt, et non est qui tuæ possit resistere voluntati.
paras.en: [[135:3|Praise ye the Lord of lords|Confitemini Domino dominorum]], that is, the God who rules over all things universally, who is [[Apoc 19:16|KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]], to whom every creature stands as a servant to his lord. Of him it is written: [[Jdt 9:17|O God of the heavens, creator of the waters, and Lord of the whole creation|Deus cœlorum, Creator aquarum, et Dominus totius creaturæ]]; and again: [[Esth 13:9|O Lord, Lord, almighty king, for all things are in thy power, and there is none that can resist thy will|Domine, Rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta posita sunt, et non est qui tuæ possit resistere voluntati]].

paras.t: Qui facit mirabilia magna solus. Superius dictum est, Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, qui facit mirabilia solus; nunc vero de eo asseritur, Qui facit mirabilia magna solus. Sed utrique dicto obviare videtur quod Apostolus de Antichristo ait: Revelabitur, inquit, ille iniquus, cujus erit adventus secundum operationem Satanæ, in omni virtute et signis et prodigiis mendacibus. Ubi doctores edisserunt, quod licet miracula Antichristi erunt mendacia, quantum ad finem, quoniam ordinabuntur ad hominum seductionem, erunt tamen realiter vera miracula. Unde scriptum est: Habebat bestia, scilicet Antichristus, cornua duo similia Agni. Et fecit signa magna, ut etiam ignem faceret de cœlo descendere in conspectu hominum; et seduxit habitantes in terra propter signa quæ data sunt illi. Et respondendum, quod aliquid dicitur esse mirabile dupliciter: scilicet respective seu quantum ad aliquem: sicut eclipsis solis illi mirabilis est, qui causam ejus ignorat; non est tamen absolute mirabilis. Taliter vero mirabilia asseruntur, quæcumque excedunt cognitionem alicujus, seu modum, virtutem ac ordinem causalitatis quarumdam causarum naturalium creatarum. Talia tamen fieri possunt arte magica, atque a dæmone: et maxime fient tempore Antichristi. Alia vero dicuntur mirabilia simpliciter et absolute, videlicet quæ totius creaturæ facultatem, et omnium causarum naturalium potestatem transcendunt: sicut sunt statio solis, illuminatio cæci nati, resurrectio mortui, penetratio dimensionum, transsubstantiatio naturarum. Et de istis loquitur Propheta. Fiuntque a Deo dumtaxat: nam etsi homo fidelis talia facere perhibeatur, non facit ea nisi instrumentaliter, vel potius dispositive seu occasionaliter.
paras.en: [[135:4|Who alone doth great wonders|Qui facit mirabilia magna solus]]. Above it was said: [[Ps 71:18|Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone doth wonderful things|Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, qui facit mirabilia solus]]; but now it is asserted of him: [[135:4|Who alone doth great wonders|Qui facit mirabilia magna solus]]. Yet both sayings seem to be contradicted by what the Apostle says of Antichrist: [[2 Thess 2:8|shall be revealed|Revelabitur]], he says, [[2 Thess 2:8|that wicked one|ille iniquus]], [[2 Thess 2:9|Whose coming is according to the working of Satan, in all power and signs and lying wonders|cujus erit adventus secundum operationem Satanæ, in omni virtute et signis et prodigiis mendacibus]]. Here the doctors explain that although the miracles of Antichrist will be lying as regards their end, since they will be directed to the seduction of men, they will nevertheless really be true miracles. Whence it is written: the beast, namely Antichrist, [[Apoc 13:11|had two horns, like a lamb|cornua duo similia Agni]]. [[Apoc 13:13|And he did great signs, so that he made also fire to come down from heaven unto the earth, in the sight of men|Et fecit signa magna, ut etiam ignem faceret de cœlo descendere in conspectu hominum]]; [[Apoc 13:14|And he seduced them that dwell on the earth, for the signs which were given him|et seduxit habitantes in terra propter signa quæ data sunt illi]]. And the answer must be that a thing is called wonderful in two ways. First, relatively, or with respect to someone: as an eclipse of the sun is wonderful to one who does not know its cause, yet it is not wonderful absolutely. In this way whatever exceeds someone's knowledge, or the mode, power and order of causality of certain created natural causes, is said to be wonderful. Such things can be done by magic art and by a demon, and they will be done above all in the time of Antichrist. Other things are called wonders simply and absolutely, namely those that transcend the capacity of the whole of creation and the power of all natural causes: such as the standing still of the sun, the giving of sight to the man born blind, the raising of the dead, the interpenetration of dimensions [that is, one body occupying the same place as another, as Christ's risen body passed through closed doors], the transubstantiation of natures. And it is of these that the Prophet speaks. These are done by God alone: for even if a faithful man is said to do such things, he does them only as an instrument, or rather dispositively or as an occasion [that is, by preparing for or occasioning an effect which God alone produces].

paras.t: Qui fecit cœlos in intellectu, id est intellectualiter, scilicet secundum ordinem suæ æternæ sapientiæ, secundum idealem rationem mentis divinæ, secundum dictamen intellectus; et libere, non ex necessitate naturæ, ut quidam philosophorum opinati sunt. Unde in Proverbiis dicitur: Dominus sapientia fundavit terram, stabilivit cœlos prudentia.
paras.en: [[135:5|Who made the heavens in understanding|Qui fecit cœlos in intellectu]], that is, with understanding: namely according to the order of his eternal wisdom, according to the ideal pattern of the divine mind [that is, the exemplar ideas of all things in the mind of God], according to the dictate of his intellect; and freely, not by necessity of nature, as some of the philosophers have held. Hence it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:19|The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth, hath established the heavens by prudence|Dominus sapientia fundavit terram, stabilivit cœlos prudentia]].

paras.t: Qui firmavit, id est, firmiter collocavit, terram super aquas maris Oceani, seu ceterorum fluviorum: non quod terra operiat aquas, vel omnibus partibus earum superior sit; sed quoniam ripæ terræ supereminent aquis. Vel dicitur terra firmata super aquas, id est juxta aquas, quemadmodum dicimus: Colonia sita est super Rhenum. Sicque (ut ait Cassiodorus) Jesus fatigatus ex itinere, sedit super puteum. Porro in omnibus versibus istis subintelligendum est, Confitemini Domino, ut sit sensus: Qui firmavit terram super aquas, id est, Confitemini Domino qui firmavit terram super aquas, et ita in aliis.
paras.en: [[135:6|Who established|Qui firmavit]], that is, set firmly in place, [[135:6|the earth above the waters|terram super aquas]] of the Ocean sea, or of the other rivers: not that the earth covers the waters, or is higher than them in all their parts, but because the banks of the earth rise above the waters. Or the earth is said to be established *above* the waters [Latin *super*, which can mean both "above" and "by"], that is, beside the waters, as we say: Cologne lies upon the Rhine. And thus (as Cassiodorus says) [[John 4:6|Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well|Jesus fatigatus ex itinere, sedit super puteum]] [Latin *super puteum*, "upon", that is, beside, the well]. Further, in all these verses *Praise ye the Lord* is to be understood, so that the sense is: *Who established the earth above the waters*, that is, Praise ye the Lord who established the earth above the waters; and so in the others.

paras.t: Qui fecit luminaria magna, quemadmodum in Genesi dicitur: Fecit Deus duo luminaria magna: luminare majus, ut præesset diei; et luminare minus, ut præesset nocti. Et hoc est quod modo subjungitur: Solem in potestatem diei, id est, ut suo splendore ac motu diem causaret; Lunam et stellas fecit in potestatem noctis, id est, ut nocti præessent, aerem aliqualiter illustrando, ne sint omnimodæ atque palpabiles tenebræ tempore noctis. Omnia hæc fecit Deus in intellectu.
paras.en: [[135:7|Who made the great lights|Qui fecit luminaria magna]], as it is said in Genesis: [[Gen 1:16|God made two great lights: a greater light to rule the day; and a lesser light to rule the night|Fecit Deus duo luminaria magna: luminare majus, ut præesset diei; et luminare minus, ut præesset nocti]]. And this is what is now added: [[135:8|The sun to rule the day|Solem in potestatem diei]] [Latin *in potestatem diei*, "for the power of the day"], that is, to cause the day by its brightness and motion; [[135:9|The moon and the stars|Lunam et stellas]] he made [[135:9|to rule the night|in potestatem noctis]], that is, to preside over the night, lighting the air in some measure, so that there may not be utter and palpable darkness in the night-time[[Ex 10:21||]]. All these God made in understanding.

paras.t: Denique juxta intelligentiam spiritualem, fecit Deus cœlos, id est cives cœlestes et homines spirituales, conversationem in cœlo habentes, in intellectu, dando eis cognitionem supernaturalem ac mysticam. Qui firmavit terram, id est Ecclesiam, super aquas, id est fidem lavacrumque Baptismi, in quo peccata donantur, et virtutum firmitas baptizato infunditur. Qui fecit luminaria magna: scilicet solem, id est Christum secundum quod homo est, in potestatem diei, id est, ut homines virtuosos, perfectos, atque præclaros illustret, sine advocato intercedente ac mediante. Propter quod Dominus ait: Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum Sol justitiæ, scilicet Christus. Lunam, id est Virginem gloriosam, sanctam Mariam, de qua dicitur in Canticis: Quæ est ista quæ progreditur quasi aurora consurgens, pulchra ut luna? et stellas, id est Apostolos atque doctores, de quibus dictum est: Qui multos erudiunt ad justitiam, quasi stellæ fulgebunt in perpetuas æternitates; in potestatem noctis, id est ad intercedendum pro peccatoribus, ut sint intercessores et advocati miserorum: quod maxime competit Virgini benedictæ, Reginæ ac Matri misericordiæ. Vel sic: Qui fecit solem in potestatem diei, id est, qui donum sapientiæ dedit perfectis; lunam et stellas, id est inferiora dona Spiritus Sancti, in potestatem noctis, id est, imperfectioribus ea infudit: non quod dona Spiritus Sancti sint diversa (imo qui unum sortitus est, omnia septem adeptus est), sed quia in viris perfectis donum sapientiæ magis abundat.
paras.en: Lastly, according to the spiritual understanding, God [[135:5|made the heavens|fecit Deus cœlos]], that is, the citizens of heaven and spiritual men whose conversation is in heaven, [[135:5|in understanding|in intellectu]], by giving them a supernatural and mystical knowledge. [[135:6|Who established the earth|Qui firmavit terram]], that is, the Church, [[135:6|above the waters|super aquas]], that is, faith and the laver of Baptism, in which sins are forgiven and firmness in the virtues is poured into the baptized. [[135:7|Who made the great lights|Qui fecit luminaria magna]]: namely [[135:8|The sun|solem]], that is, Christ as man, [[135:8|to rule the day|in potestatem diei]], that is, to enlighten men who are virtuous, perfect and illustrious, with no advocate interceding or mediating. For this reason the Lord says: [[Mal 4:2|unto you that fear my name, the Sun of justice shall arise|Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum Sol justitiæ]], namely Christ. [[135:9|The moon|Lunam]], that is, the glorious Virgin, holy Mary, of whom it is said in the Canticles: [[Cant 6:9|Who is she that cometh forth as the morning rising, fair as the moon|Quæ est ista quæ progreditur quasi aurora consurgens, pulchra ut luna?]]? [[135:9|and the stars|et stellas]], that is, the Apostles and doctors, of whom it is said: [[Dan 12:3|they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity|Qui multos erudiunt ad justitiam, quasi stellæ fulgebunt in perpetuas æternitates]]; [[135:9|to rule the night|in potestatem noctis]], that is, to intercede for sinners, that they may be the intercessors and advocates of the wretched: which belongs above all to the blessed Virgin, Queen and Mother of mercy. Or thus: *Who made the sun to rule the day*, that is, who gave the gift of wisdom to the perfect; *the moon and the stars*, that is, the lower gifts of the Holy Ghost, *to rule the night*, that is, he poured them into the less perfect: not that the gifts of the Holy Ghost are found apart (indeed, whoever has received one has obtained all seven), but because in perfect men the gift of wisdom abounds more.

paras.t: Qui percussit Ægyptum, id est habitatores Ægypti, cum primogenitis eorum, occidendo omne primogenitum in hominibus atque pecoribus. Qui eduxit Israel de medio eorum, videlicet Ægyptiorum: cujus eductionis forma subjungitur: In manu potenti, id est operatione virtuosa, quantum ad minora miracula, quæ magi quoque Pharaonis fecerunt, et brachio excelso, id est operatione supernaturali atque terribili, quantum ad majora miracula, quæ illi facere non valebant. Quæ omnia in libro Exodi plenius continentur.
paras.en: [[135:10|Who smote Egypt|Qui percussit Ægyptum]], that is, the inhabitants of Egypt, [[135:10|with their firstborn|cum primogenitis eorum]], by slaying every firstborn among men and cattle[[Ex 12:29||]]. [[135:11|Who brought out Israel from among them|Qui eduxit Israel de medio eorum]], that is, from among the Egyptians; and the manner of this bringing out is added: [[135:12|With a mighty hand|In manu potenti]], that is, by a powerful working, as regards the lesser miracles, which the magicians of Pharao also did[[Ex 7:11||]][[Ex 7:22||]][[Ex 8:7||]], [[135:12|and with a stretched out arm|et brachio excelso]] [Latin *brachio excelso*, "with a lofty arm"], that is, by a working supernatural and terrible, as regards the greater miracles, which they could not do[[Ex 8:18||]][[Ex 8:19||]]. All of which is contained more fully in the book of Exodus.

paras.t: Spiritualiter autem educit Deus Israel, id est electos, de medio eorum, id est de hoc mundo fallaci, et societate ac vita hominum mundanorum, sicut superius dictum est: Protexisti me a conventu malignantium. Ad quam eductionem hortatur nos Apostolus: Deponite vos secundum pristinam conversationem, veterem hominem, qui corrumpitur secundum desideria erroris: et renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ. Unde iterum ait: Exite de medio eorum, et immundum ne tetigeritis, scilicet per consensum. Sic autem Deus educit electos in manu potenti et brachio excelso. Nam et quosdam compellit intrare, et quosdam convertit per miracula, quosdam per inspirationem occultam, quosdam per alias supernaturales ac admirabiles vias, prout multi nostrum vere experti sunt.
paras.en: Spiritually, God brings out [[135:11|Israel|Israel]], that is, the elect, [[135:11|from among them|de medio eorum]], that is, from this deceitful world, and from the company and life of worldly men, as was said above: [[Ps 63:3|Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant|Protexisti me a conventu malignantium]]. To this bringing out the Apostle exhorts us: [[Eph 4:22|To put off, according to former conversation, the old man, who is corrupted according to the desire of error|Deponite vos secundum pristinam conversationem, veterem hominem, qui corrumpitur secundum desideria erroris]]; [[Eph 4:23|And be renewed in spirit of your mind|renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ]]. Hence he says again: [[2 Cor 6:17|Go out from among them|Exite de medio eorum]], [[2 Cor 6:17|and touch not the unclean thing|et immundum ne tetigeritis]], namely by consent. And God brings out his elect [[135:12|With a mighty hand and with a stretched out arm|in manu potenti et brachio excelso]]. For some he compels to come in, some he converts by miracles, some by a hidden inspiration, some by other supernatural and wonderful ways, as many of us have truly experienced.

paras.t: Qui divisit mare Rubrum in divisiones, id est in partes a se invicem distantes atque partitas, sicut in Exodo legitur: Dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Tolle virgam tuam, et extende manum tuam super mare, et divide illud. Et post pauca: Abstulit Deus illud, flante vento vehementissimo. Quidam autem, eo quod nunc dictum est pluraliter, In divisiones, asserunt mare Rubrum fuisse divisum in duodecim partes, secundum numerum tribuum Israel, ita quod quælibet tribus ivit per viam specialem. Sed hoc aliis non videtur: propter quod dicunt sic esse intelligendum, quod nunc dicitur mare divisum fuisse in divisiones, id est in partes duas, ita quod aquæ a se divisæ et consolidatæ, erant filiis Israel pro muro a dextris et a sinistris.
paras.en: [[135:13|Who divided the Red Sea into parts|Qui divisit mare Rubrum in divisiones]], that is, into portions standing apart from one another and separated, as we read in Exodus: [[Ex 14:15|And the Lord said to Moses|Dixit Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[Ex 14:16|lift thou up thy rod, and stretch forth thy hand over the sea, and divide it|Tolle virgam tuam, et extende manum tuam super mare, et divide illud]]. And a little after: [[Ex 14:21|the Lord took it away by a strong and burning wind|Abstulit Deus illud, flante vento vehementissimo]]. But some, because it is said here in the plural, *into parts* [Latin *in divisiones*, "into divisions"], assert that the Red Sea was divided into twelve parts, according to the number of the tribes of Israel, so that each tribe went by a path of its own. But others do not think so; and so they say it is to be understood thus: that the sea is here said to have been divided *into parts*, that is, into two parts, so that the waters, divided from one another and made firm, were to the children of Israel as a wall on the right hand and on the left.

paras.t: Et eduxit Israel, id est populum Judæorum, per medium ejus, videlicet maris Rubri: non quod ibant per ipsam aquam, sed per locum arentem, in quo paulo ante aqua maris currebat. Unde in Exodo legitur: Filii Israel ambulaverunt per medium sicci maris. Dicitur autem mare hoc Rubrum, non quod aquæ sint rubræ, sed quoniam rubræ apparent propter terram rubram super quam fluunt.
paras.en: [[135:14|And brought out Israel|Et eduxit Israel]], that is, the Jewish people, [[135:14|through the midst thereof|per medium ejus]], that is, of the Red Sea: not that they went through the water itself, but through a dry place where the water of the sea had been running a little before. Hence we read in Exodus: [[Ex 14:22|the children of Israel went in through the midst of the sea dried up|Filii Israel ambulaverunt per medium sicci maris]]. Now this sea is called Red, not because its waters are red, but because they look red on account of the red earth over which they flow.

paras.t: Et excussit, id est, submersit et interfecit, Pharaonem regem Ægypti, et virtutem, id est exercitum, ejus in mari Rubro, dum persequebantur filios Israel, prout in Exodo scriptum est: Involvit eos Dominus in mediis fluctibus: et subvertit rotas curruum, ferebanturque in profundum.
paras.en: [[135:15|And overthrew|Et excussit]], that is, drowned and slew, [[135:15|Pharao|Pharaonem]] king of Egypt, [[135:15|and his host|et virtutem]], that is, his army, [[135:15|in the Red Sea|in mari Rubro]], while they were pursuing the children of Israel, as it is written in Exodus: [[Ex 14:27|the Lord shut them up in the middle of the waves|Involvit eos Dominus in mediis fluctibus]]; [[Ex 14:25|And overthrew the wheels of the chariots, and they were carried into the deep|et subvertit rotas curruum, ferebanturque in profundum]] [the margin gives Exod. xiv, 27, 28; these last words are Ex 14:25].

paras.t: Qui traduxit populum suum Israeliticum per desertum annis quadraginta, quoadusque consumeretur omnis generatio quæ murmuravit contra Dominum.
paras.en: [[135:16|Who led his people|Qui traduxit populum suum]] of Israel [[135:16|through the desert|per desertum]] for forty years, until the whole generation that murmured against the Lord was consumed[[Num 32:13||]].

paras.t: Spiritualiter dividit Deus mare Rubrum, id est sæculum istud, amaritudine vitiorum et fluxu luxuriæ plenum, in divisiones, dum per varias vias electos suos educit ad vitam religiosam seu patriam Beatorum. Excutitque Pharaonem, id est diabolum, et virtutem ejus, videlicet angelos Satanæ, in mari Rubro, id est in fonte Baptismatis, Christi sanguine rubricati: quia virtute Baptismi superatur potestas diaboli, et vasa sua sibi tolluntur, Christo quoque incorporantur. Traducit etiam Deus populum suum fidelem per desertum, id est mundum istum virtutibus destitutum, illuminando corda eorum, ne errent in via.
paras.en: Spiritually, God divides [[135:13|the Red Sea|mare Rubrum]], that is, this world, full of the bitterness of vices and the flood of lust, [[135:13|into parts|in divisiones]], when he leads his elect by various ways to the religious life or to the fatherland of the Blessed. And he overthrows [[135:15|Pharao|Pharaonem]], that is, the devil, [[135:15|and his host|et virtutem ejus]], namely the angels of Satan, [[135:15|in the Red Sea|in mari Rubro]], that is, in the font of Baptism, reddened with the blood of Christ: for by the power of Baptism the might of the devil is overcome, and his vessels [that is, the souls he held as his goods] are taken from him and are incorporated into Christ. God also leads [[135:16|his people|populum suum]], his faithful people, [[135:16|through the desert|per desertum]], that is, this world bare of virtues, enlightening their hearts so that they may not stray on the way.

paras.t: Qui percussit reges magnos, etc. Hic locus usque ad id, Quia in humilitate nostra memor fuit nostri, etc., in præcedenti psalmo litteraliter ac spiritualiter expositus est.
paras.en: [[135:17|Who smote great kings|Qui percussit reges magnos]], etc. This passage, up to the words [[135:23|For he was mindful of us in our affliction|Quia in humilitate nostra memor fuit nostri]], etc., has been expounded literally and spiritually in the preceding psalm[[Ps 134:10||]][[Ps 134:11||]][[Ps 134:12||]].

paras.t: In persona itaque Israeliticæ plebis loquens Propheta, adjecit: Quia in humilitate nostra, id est in afflictione qua ab Ægyptiis opprimebamur, et in humili prece qua ad Deum pro liberatione clamavimus, memor fuit nostri, id est, per effectum misericordiæ suæ ostendit se memorem nostri fuisse, eruendo nos, sicut subjungitur: Et redemit nos ab inimicis nostris Ægyptiis.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of the people of Israel, the Prophet added: For [[135:23|in our affliction|in humilitate nostra]] [Latin *humilitas*, both "lowliness" or "affliction" and "humility": Denis takes it both ways], that is, in the affliction with which we were oppressed by the Egyptians, and in the humble prayer with which we cried to God for deliverance, [[135:23|he was mindful of us|memor fuit nostri]], that is, by the effect of his mercy he showed that he had been mindful of us, by rescuing us, as is added: [[135:24|And he redeemed us from our enemies|Et redemit nos ab inimicis nostris]], the Egyptians.

paras.t: Moraliter quoque, memor fuit et est Deus Ecclesiæ suæ, omnisque Christiani in sua humilitate: sive per humilitatem intelligatur oppressio tribulationis, sive interior humiliatio mentis, de qua Petrus nos admonet: Humiliamini sub potenti manu Dei. Et redemit nos ab inimicis nostris invisibilibus, puta dæmonibus, pretio proprii sanguinis, sicut ait Apostolus: In fide vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me; et Petrus inducit: Non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis, sed pretioso sanguine Christi.
paras.en: Morally, too, God was and is mindful of his Church and of every Christian in their lowliness: whether by lowliness we understand the oppression of tribulation, or the inward humbling of the mind, to which Peter exhorts us: [[1 Pet 5:6|Be you humbled therefore under the mighty hand of God|Humiliamini sub potenti manu Dei]]. [[135:24|And he redeemed us from our enemies|Et redemit nos ab inimicis nostris]] invisible, that is, the demons, at the price of his own blood, as the Apostle says: [[Gal 2:20|I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and delivered himself for me|In fide vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me]]; and Peter adds: [[1 Pet 1:18|you were not redeemed with corruptible things, as gold or silver|Non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis]], [[1 Pet 1:19|But with the precious blood of Christ|sed pretioso sanguine Christi]].

paras.t: Qui dat escam omni carni, id est omni animali: ponit enim partem pro toto. Omnibus autem viventibus vita sensitiva, providit Deus per se ipsum vel causas secundas de necessariis ad vivendum, quemadmodum dicit Salvator: Respicite volatilia cœli, quia non serunt, neque metunt; et Pater vester cœlestis pascit ea. Et iterum: Nonne quinque passeres veneunt dipondio, et unus ex illis non est in oblivione coram Deo? Maledictus est ergo error eorum, qui omniscientiam aut providentiam Dei negaverunt aut negant.
paras.en: [[135:25|Who giveth food to all flesh|Qui dat escam omni carni]], that is, to every animal: for he puts the part for the whole [that is, *flesh*, a part of the animal, for the whole living creature]. For to all that live with sensitive life [that is, the life of sense, which animals share with men] God has provided, by himself or through secondary causes, what they need for living, as the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:26|Behold the birds of the air, for they neither sow, nor do they reap|Respicite volatilia cœli, quia non serunt, neque metunt]]; [[Matt 6:26|and your heavenly Father feedeth them|et Pater vester cœlestis pascit ea]]. And again: [[Luke 12:6|Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?|Nonne quinque passeres veneunt dipondio, et unus ex illis non est in oblivione coram Deo?]] Accursed, therefore, is the error of those who have denied, or deny, the omniscience or the providence of God.

paras.t: Confitemini Deo cœli. Specialiter Deus vocatus est Deus cœli: primo, quoniam inter corporales creaturas cœlum excellit; secundo, quoniam Dominus testatus est, Cœlum mihi sedes est; tertio, quoniam in cœlo Deus excellentius operatur, clariusque conspicitur. Confitemini Domino dominorum, quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus.
paras.en: [[135:26|Give glory to the God of heaven|Confitemini Deo cœli]]. God is called the God of heaven in a special way: first, because among bodily creatures heaven excels; secondly, because the Lord has testified: [[Is 66:1|Heaven is my throne|Cœlum mihi sedes est]]; thirdly, because in heaven God works more excellently and is more clearly seen. [[135:27|Give glory to the Lord of lords: for his mercy endureth for ever|Confitemini Domino dominorum, quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum incomparabili jucunditate plenum audivimus: qui utique Deum amantibus, ejusque misericordiam cognoscentibus et expertis, dulciter sapit. Et quid miseris nobis esse aut dici potest suavius, nisi, Quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus? Propter quod decet nos toties spiritualiter exhilarari, atque divino amore succendi, quoties canimus, Quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus. Invitat autem nos psalmus iste ad reverentiam Creatoris, dum eum appellat Deum deorum et Dominum dominorum, dum insuper magnalia ejus describit, et ipsius justitiam tam evidenter commendat. Misericordiæ igitur Dei semper memores simus, et Deo altissimo grati ac reverenter subjecti esse curemus. Et quidquid boni in nobis est, quidquid mali evasimus, quidquid boni peregimus, totum misericordiæ Dei cordialissime adscribamus, dicentes ex animo illud Jeremiæ: Misericordiæ Domini, quia non sumus consumpti, quia non defecerunt miserationes ejus; illud quoque Isaiæ: Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis Dominus, et quæ largitus est nobis secundum indulgentiam suam.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of incomparable delight, which tastes sweet indeed to those who love God and who know and have experienced his mercy. And what sweeter thing can there be, or be said, for us wretches than [[135:1|for his mercy endureth for ever|Quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus]]? Therefore it befits us to be spiritually gladdened and kindled with divine love as often as we sing [[135:1|for his mercy endureth for ever|Quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus]]. This psalm also invites us to reverence for the Creator, when it calls him the God of gods and the Lord of lords, when moreover it describes his great works, and commends his justice so plainly. Let us therefore be ever mindful of the mercy of God, and take care to be grateful to God most high and reverently subject to him. And whatever good is in us, whatever evil we have escaped, whatever good we have done, let us ascribe it all most heartily to the mercy of God, saying from the heart that word of Jeremias: [[Lam 3:22|The mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed: because his commiserations have not failed|Misericordiæ Domini, quia non sumus consumpti, quia non defecerunt miserationes ejus]]; and that of Isaias also: [[Is 63:7|I will remember the tender mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all the things that the Lord hath bestowed upon us|Miserationum Domini recordabor, laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis Dominus]], [[Is 63:7|which he hath given them according to his kindness|quæ largitus est nobis secundum indulgentiam suam]] [Denis reads *nobis*, "to us", where the Vulgate has *eis*, "to them"].

paras.t: Precatio. Tibi Domino dominorum toto mentis affectu confitentibus, ac mirabilia tua decantantibus, hilaritatem tui vultus nobis impertiri dignare, et ab omni plaga Ægyptiorum nos clementer tuere, et misericordiam tuam nobis in æternum concede.
paras.en: Prayer. Vouchsafe, O Lord of lords, to bestow the gladness of thy countenance on us who give praise to thee with all the affection of our mind and sing of thy wonders; mercifully protect us from every plague of the Egyptians, and grant us thy mercy for ever.

136.title: DECLARATIO LITTERALIS PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI SEXTI : SUPER FLUMINA BABYLONIS.
136.title_en: Literal explanation of the hundred and thirty-sixth psalm: Upon the rivers of Babylon.

paras.t: Assignatur autem psalmo huic pro titulo: Psalmus David propter Jeremiam: quia in psalmo præsenti tractat David de his, de quibus Jeremias copiosius prophetavit et scripsit. Loquitur enim de templi destructione atque Judaici populi captivitate, quas Jeremias in Threnis abundanter describit ac plangit.
paras.en: This psalm is given for its title: A psalm of David, for Jeremias [the Vulgate's title is Psalmus David, Jeremiæ; the Douay-Rheims gives the psalm no title]: because in the present psalm David treats of the things of which Jeremias prophesied and wrote more fully. For it speaks of the destruction of the temple and of the captivity of the Jewish people, which Jeremias describes and laments at length in the Lamentations.

paras.t: In persona itaque populi Judæorum captivi loquens Propheta, Super flumina, inquit, Babylonis, id est juxta aquas Chaldææ, in qua flumina multa decurrunt, illic sedimus, id est, habitavimus septuaginta annis, sicut Jeremias prædixit. Unde communiter dicimus: Ille sedit ibi annos tres, id est, habitavit. Et juxta talem modum loquendi ait Moyses: Sedistis in Cadesbarne multo tempore. Et flevimus, propter nostram captivitatem, magis tamen propter templi destructionem, sicut subjungitur: dum recordaremur tui, o Sion, id est templi a Salomone constructi, a Babyloniis vero destructi, in monte Sion.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of the captive people of the Jews, the Prophet says: [[136:1|Upon the rivers|Super flumina]], he says, [[136:1|of Babylon|Babylonis]], that is, beside the waters of Chaldea, through which many rivers run, [[136:1|there we sat|illic sedimus]], that is, we dwelt for seventy years, as Jeremias foretold[[Jer 25:11||]][[Jer 25:12||]]. So we commonly say: He sat there three years, that is, he dwelt there. And in this manner of speaking Moses says: [[Deut 1:46|you abode in Cadesbarne a long time|Sedistis in Cadesbarne multo tempore]] [the Latin has sedistis, “you sat”]. [[136:1|and wept|Et flevimus]], because of our captivity, but more because of the destruction of the temple, as is added: [[136:1|when we remembered|dum recordaremur]] thee, O [[136:1|Sion|Sion]], that is, the temple built by Solomon, but destroyed by the Babylonians[[4 Kings 25:9||]], on mount Sion [the margin gives IV Reg. xxv, without a verse; the burning of the temple is told at 4 Kings 25:9].

paras.t: In salicibus, id est inter arbores infructuosas et aridas, in medio ejus, id est, quæ fuerunt in medio Babylonis, suspendimus organa nostra, id est, ab omni cantico jucunditatis cessavimus: non solum propter recordationem Sion, sed etiam Quia illic interrogaverunt nos, qui captivos duxerunt nos, verba cantionum, scilicet Babylonii seu Chaldæi; Et qui abduxerunt nos a terra patrum nostrorum in Babylonem, dicentes: Hymnum cantate nobis de canticis Sion, quæ canere solebatis in templo Jerusalem. Hoc dixerunt irridendo, et nostro planctui congaudendo, nostramque tristitiam exaggerando. Nos autem respondimus eis: Quomodo cantabimus canticum Domini, id est laudes divinas, in terra aliena, id est, in Chaldæa idololatriæ dedita? Hoc nempe non decet, ne videamur non curantes de nostra translatione, templique destructione.
paras.en: [[136:2|On the willows|In salicibus]], that is, among barren and dry trees, [[136:2|in the midst thereof|in medio ejus]], that is, which were in the midst of Babylon, [[136:2|we hung up our instruments|suspendimus organa nostra]], that is, we ceased from every song of gladness: not only because of the remembrance of Sion, but also [[136:3|For there they that led us into captivity required of us the words of songs|Quia illic interrogaverunt nos, qui captivos duxerunt nos, verba cantionum]], namely the Babylonians or Chaldeans; [[136:3|And they that carried us away|Et qui abduxerunt nos]] from the land of our fathers into Babylon, [[136:3|said|dicentes]]: [[136:3|Sing ye to us a hymn of the songs of Sion|Hymnum cantate nobis de canticis Sion]], which you used to sing in the temple of Jerusalem. This they said in mockery, rejoicing at our lamentation and heaping up our sorrow. But we answered them: [[136:4|How shall we sing the song of the Lord|Quomodo cantabimus canticum Domini]], that is, the divine praises, [[136:4|in a strange land|in terra aliena]], that is, in Chaldea, given over to idolatry? For this is not fitting, lest we seem not to care about our being carried away, and the destruction of the temple.

paras.t: Idcirco cum juramento affirmo: Si oblitus fuero tui, Jerusalem, ego populus inde translatus, id est, si desiero tuam devastationem deflere, vel pro tua reparatione orare, oblivioni detur dextera mea, id est, ego ipse seu tota virtus mea oblivioni tradatur a Deo, ita quod pereat. Adhæreat lingua mea faucibus meis, in tantum quod loqui non possim, si non meminero tui, orando ut reædificeris; Si non proposuero Jerusalem in principio lætitiæ meæ, id est, nisi ipsa Jerusalem fuerit mihi prima causa seu principium quoddam lætitiæ, non in quantum destructa est, sed prout concipio eam ut reædificandam: ita quod in spe reparationis ejus prius lætor, quam in aliis inferioribus rebus. Vel sic: Si non proposuero, etc., id est, si eveniente mihi causa lætandi, non prius meminero Jerusalem, dolendo de ejus destructione, atque orando pro ipsius restauratione; tunc prædicta mala quæ imprecatus sum, mihi contingant.
paras.en: Therefore I affirm with an oath: [[136:5|If I forget thee, O Jerusalem|Si oblitus fuero tui, Jerusalem]], I, the people carried away from there, that is, if I cease to bewail thy devastation, or to pray for thy restoration, [[136:5|let my right hand be forgotten|oblivioni detur dextera mea]], that is, let I myself, or all my strength, be given over to forgetfulness by God, so that it perish. [[136:6|Let my tongue cleave to my jaws|Adhæreat lingua mea faucibus meis]], so much that I cannot speak, [[136:6|if I do not remember thee|si non meminero tui]], praying that thou be rebuilt; [[136:6|If I make not Jerusalem the beginning of my joy|Si non proposuero Jerusalem in principio lætitiæ meæ]], that is, unless Jerusalem itself be to me the first cause or a kind of beginning of joy, not inasmuch as she is destroyed, but as I conceive her as to be rebuilt: so that I rejoice in the hope of her restoration before I rejoice in other, lesser things. Or thus: [[136:6|If I make not|Si non proposuero]], etc., that is, if, when a cause of rejoicing comes to me, I do not first remember Jerusalem, grieving over her destruction and praying for her restoration, then let the evils I have called down upon myself befall me.

paras.t: Memor esto, Domine, ad ulciscendum filiorum Edom, id est Idumæorum descendentium ab Esau fratre Jacob: qui Esau alio nomine dictus est Edom; in die Jerusalem: id est, memor esto, o Domine, iniquitatis eorum quam fecerunt in die, id est tempore, destructionis Jerusalem, quod fuit tempus vindictæ ipsius. Qui filii Edom dicunt, id est, locuti sunt Babyloniis: Exinanite, exinanite, id est, humiliate atque destruite Jerusalem, usque ad fundamentum in ea, id est, funditus eam dejicite. Sicut enim Esau persecutus est Jacob, sic Idumæi pene semper molesti fuerunt Judæis. Unde Abdias ait ad populum Idumæorum: Propter iniquitatem in fratrem tuum Jacob, operiet te confusio, et peribis in æternum. In his ergo versiculis oravit Propheta pro justa ultione Idumæorum, qui consilio auxilioque fuerunt Chaldæis contra Judæos.
paras.en: [[136:7|Remember, O Lord|Memor esto, Domine]], so as to take vengeance, [[136:7|the children of Edom|filiorum Edom]], that is, the Idumeans descended from Esau the brother of Jacob, which Esau was called by another name Edom[[Gen 25:30||]]; [[136:7|in the day of Jerusalem|in die Jerusalem]]: that is, remember, O Lord, the iniquity they did in the day, that is, the time, of the destruction of Jerusalem, which was the time of her punishment. [[136:7|Who say|Qui filii Edom dicunt]], the children of Edom, that is, who spoke to the Babylonians: [[136:7|Rase it, rase it|Exinanite, exinanite]], that is, humble and destroy Jerusalem, [[136:7|even to the foundation thereof|usque ad fundamentum in ea]], that is, cast her down utterly. For as Esau persecuted Jacob[[Gen 27:41||]], so the Idumeans were almost always troublesome to the Jews. Hence Abdias says to the people of the Idumeans: [[Abd 1:10|for the iniquity against thy brother Jacob, confusion shall cover thee, and thou shalt perish for ever|Propter iniquitatem in fratrem tuum Jacob, operiet te confusio, et peribis in æternum]]. In these verses, then, the Prophet prayed for the just punishment of the Idumeans, who were with the Chaldeans against the Jews with counsel and help.

paras.t: Nunc prophetat de Chaldæorum dejectione. Filia Babylonis misera, id est, o infelix gens Babylonis, beatus est ipse Deus, qui retribuet tibi per Cyrum regem Medorum, et Darium regem Persarum, retributionem tuam, id est justam vindictam pro tuis sceleribus, quam, id est cui similem, retribuisti nobis, exigentibus nostris peccatis. Sicut enim Chaldæi destruxerunt Jerusalem, et populum ejus interfecerunt, sic Persæ ac Medi everterunt funditus Babylonem, et habitatores ejus peremerunt.
paras.en: Now he prophesies of the overthrow of the Chaldeans. [[136:8|O daughter of Babylon, miserable|Filia Babylonis misera]], that is, O unhappy nation of Babylon, [[136:8|blessed shall he be who shall repay thee|beatus est ipse Deus, qui retribuet tibi]], that is, God himself, by Cyrus king of the Medes and Darius king of the Persians [Denis reads “blessed is God himself, who shall repay thee”], [[136:8|thy payment|retributionem tuam]], that is, just vengeance for thy crimes, [[136:8|which|quam]], that is, like that which, [[136:8|thou hast paid us|retribuisti nobis]], as our sins required. For as the Chaldeans destroyed Jerusalem and slew her people[[4 Kings 25:9||]][[4 Kings 25:21||]] [the margin gives IV Reg. xxv, without a verse], so the Persians and Medes overthrew Babylon utterly, and slew its inhabitants.

paras.t: Beatus qui tenebit et allidet parvulos suos ad petram: id est, vere felix est Deus, qui per Medos ac Persas tenebit per pedes, et allidet, id est, confringet, occidet et conteret, parvulos suos, id est pueros et infantes Babyloniorum (qui dicuntur parvuli Dei, quia ab eo creati), ad petram, id est parietem saxeum. Persæ enim et Medi ex nimia crudelitate tenuerunt et alliserunt hoc modo parvulos Babylonis. Quod Dominus apud Isaiam ita prædixit: Suscitabo super vos Medos, qui argentum non quærant, nec aurum; et lactantibus non miserebuntur. Rursusque: Infantes eorum allidentur in oculis eorum. Hanc autem ultionem petit Propheta zelo justitiæ, conformando cor suum æquitati divinæ; petitque ut in præsenti puniantur, ne pluribus noceant, gravius peccent, et damnabilius pereant.
paras.en: [[136:9|Blessed be he that shall take and dash|Beatus qui tenebit et allidet]] his [[136:9|little ones against the rock|parvulos suos ad petram]] [Denis reads parvulos suos, “his little ones”; a footnote of the edition gives the variant tuos, “thy”, as in the Vulgate]: that is, truly happy is God, who by the Medes and Persians shall take them by the feet and [[136:9|dash|allidet]], that is, shall break, kill and crush, his [[136:9|little ones|parvulos]], that is, the boys and infants of the Babylonians (who are called God's little ones because they were created by him), [[136:9|against the rock|ad petram]], that is, against a wall of stone. For the Persians and Medes, out of exceeding cruelty, took and dashed the little ones of Babylon in this way. Which the Lord foretold thus in Isaias: [[Is 13:17|I will stir up the Medes|Suscitabo super vos Medos]] against you, [[Is 13:17|who shall not seek silver, nor desire gold|qui argentum non quærant, nec aurum]]; and [[Is 13:18|shall have no pity upon the sucklings|lactantibus non miserebuntur]]. And again: their infants [[Is 13:16|shall be dashed in pieces before their eyes|allidentur in oculis eorum]] [the Douay-Rheims reads “their inhabitants”; the Vulgate has infantes, “infants”]. Now the Prophet asks for this vengeance out of zeal for justice, conforming his heart to the divine equity; and he asks that they be punished in this present life, lest they harm more people, sin more grievously, and perish with greater damnation.

136.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA EJUSDEM I[…] PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI SEXTI.
136.title_en: Tropological exposition of the same hundred and thirty-sixth psalm.
136.note: One word of the Latin title is unreadable in the transcription.

paras.t: Mystice vero per Babylonem significatur sæculum præsens, confusione vitiorum repletum. Babylon namque interpretatur confusio. Unde Petrus, in fine primæ suæ Canonicæ, Romam nominat Babylonem, dicendo : Salutat vos Ecclesia, quæ est in Babylone collecta.
paras.en: In the mystical sense, Babylon signifies the present world, filled with the confusion of vices. For *Babylon* is interpreted "confusion". Hence Peter, at the end of his first canonical Epistle, names Rome Babylon, saying: [[1 Pet 5:13|The church that is in Babylon, elected together with you, saluteth you|Salutat vos Ecclesia, quæ est in Babylone collecta]] [Denis reads *collecta*, "gathered", where the Vulgate has *coelecta*, "elected together"].

paras.t: Sancti itaque, qui hoc mundo tanquam exsilio quodam utuntur, non habentes hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirentes, hujus miserrimæ vitæ incolatum deplangunt, et dicunt : Super flumina Babylonis, id est juxta divitias atque delicias hujus mundi, quæ tanquam flumina currunt ac defluunt, illic sedimus, tanquam exsules in humilitate præcipua, et flevimus, præ desiderio patriæ cœlestis, dum recordaremur Sion, id est, dum contemplaremur gaudia triumphantis Ecclesiæ, Deum facie ad faciem speculantis. Hoc convenit his qui cum Apostolo cupiunt dissolvi et esse cum Christo, qui promissiones cœlestes a longe adspiciunt et salutant, confitentes quoniam peregrini et hospites sunt super terram. Possunt quoque per flumina Babylonis intelligi tentationes, persecutionesque mundi : de quibus fluminibus dicitur in Threnis, Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum. Super hæc flumina sedent electi, dum in sæculo isto plurimas sustinent adversitates, persecutiones, pœnas ac tentationes ; et flent, dum recordantur paradisi unde ejecti sunt, et patriæ ad quam tendunt, dicentes illud : Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus ?
paras.en: The saints, therefore, who use this world as a kind of exile, not having here a lasting city but seeking one that is to come[[Heb 13:14||]], bewail their sojourn in this most wretched life, and say: [[136:1|Upon the rivers of Babylon|Super flumina Babylonis]], that is, beside the riches and delights of this world, which run and flow away like rivers, [[136:1|there we sat|illic sedimus]], as exiles, in singular lowliness, [[136:1|and wept|et flevimus]] for longing for the heavenly fatherland, [[136:1|when we remembered Sion|dum recordaremur Sion]], that is, while we contemplated the joys of the Church triumphant, which beholds God face to face. This befits those who with the Apostle desire [[Phil 1:23|to be dissolved and to be with Christ|dissolvi et esse cum Christo]], who behold the heavenly promises from afar and salute them, [[Heb 11:13|confessing that they are pilgrims and strangers on the earth|confitentes quoniam peregrini et hospites sunt super terram]] [the margin gives Hebr. vi, 13; the passage is Heb 11:13]. By [[136:1|the rivers of Babylon|flumina Babylonis]] may also be understood the temptations and persecutions of the world, of which rivers it is said in Lamentations: [[Lam 3:54|Waters have flowed over my head|Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum]]. Upon these rivers the elect sit, while in this world they endure very many adversities, persecutions, pains and temptations; and they weep when they remember the paradise from which they were cast out, and the fatherland towards which they are making their way, saying: [[Rom 7:24|Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?|Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus ?]]

paras.t: In salicibus, id est inter homines infructuosos, vitiosos et sæculares : qui significantur per salices, quæ sunt arbores infructuosæ et aridæ ; in medio ejus, id est in medio hujus mundi conversantes ac positi, suspendimus organa nostra, id est, a prædicatione regni cœlestis, et documentis sacræ Scripturæ, quæ est organum nostrum, cessavimus, quoniam spes nulla fuit proficiendi. Unde scriptum est : Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem ; et alibi : In auribus insipientium ne loquaris, ne forte despiciant doctrinam eloquii tui. Hinc Dominus ait Ezechieli : Linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo, et non eris quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est. Vel : Suspendimus organa nostra, id est, interdum ad tempus cessavimus a laude Dei jucunda, et contemplatione cœlestium, propter dolorem propriorum defectuum, compassionemque proximorum, quos ire conspeximus per abrupta et devia vitiorum. Nam et Apostolus ait, Flere cum flentibus. Et, Beati qui lugent.
paras.en: [[136:2|On the willows|In salicibus]], that is, among men who are fruitless, vicious and worldly, who are signified by willows, which are fruitless and dry trees; [[136:2|in the midst thereof|in medio ejus]], that is, living and set in the midst of this world, [[136:2|we hung up our instruments|suspendimus organa nostra]], that is, we ceased from preaching the kingdom of heaven and from the teachings of Holy Scripture, which is our instrument, since there was no hope of doing any good. Hence it is written: [[Ecclus 32:6|Where there is no hearing, pour not out words|Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem]]; and elsewhere: [[Prov 23:9|Speak not in the ears of fools: because they will despise the instruction of thy speech|In auribus insipientium ne loquaris, ne forte despiciant doctrinam eloquii tui]]. Hence the Lord says to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 3:26|I will make thy tongue stick fast to the roof of thy mouth|Linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo]], [[Ezech 3:26|and not as a man that reproveth: because they are a provoking house|et non eris quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est]]. Or: [[136:2|we hung up our instruments|Suspendimus organa nostra]], that is, at times we have ceased for a while from the joyful praise of God and from the contemplation of heavenly things, for sorrow at our own failings and for compassion on our neighbours, whom we saw going over the steep and pathless ways of the vices. For the Apostle too says: [[Rom 12:15|weep with them that weep|Flere cum flentibus]]. And: [[Matt 5:5|Blessed are they that mourn|Beati qui lugent]].

paras.t: Quia illic, id est in Babylonia, scilicet in mundi vanitate, interrogaverunt nos, qui captivos duxerunt nos, id est homines pestilentes, qui suo exemplo pestifero conati sunt nos inducere in servitutem peccati et captivitatem diaboli, verba cantionum spiritualium ex derisione, vel cantionum sæcularium, quatenus cum ipsis cantaremus, gauderemus, et epularemur. Et qui abduxerunt nos, affectu vel effectu, a Deo, a justitia, a recta ratione : Hymnum cantate nobis de canticis Sion : id est, ostendite nobis vera esse quæ prædicatis de invisibilibus bonis ; rationem reddite nobis, quid sit anima, quid vita futura, quid infernus, quid paradisus. Hoc dicunt illi, de quibus alio loco dictum est: Non est qui agnitus sit reversus ab inferis; quia ex nihilo nati sumus, et post hæc erimus tanquam non fuerimus. Venite ergo et fruamur bonis quæ sunt, et utamur creatura tanquam in juventute celeriter. Et illud : Comedamus et bibamus ; cras enim moriemur.
paras.en: [[136:3|For there|Quia illic]], that is, in Babylonia, namely in the vanity of the world, [[136:3|they that led us into captivity|qui captivos duxerunt nos]], that is, pestilent men, who by their pestilential example tried to bring us into the slavery of sin and the captivity of the devil, [[136:3|required of us|interrogaverunt nos]] [[136:3|the words of songs|verba cantionum]]: spiritual songs, in mockery, or worldly songs, so that we might sing and make merry and feast with them. [[136:3|And they that carried us away|Et qui abduxerunt nos]], in desire or in deed, from God, from justice, from right reason, said: [[136:3|Sing ye to us a hymn of the songs of Sion|Hymnum cantate nobis de canticis Sion]]; that is, show us that what you preach about invisible goods is true; give us an account of what the soul is, what the life to come, what hell, what paradise. This is said by those of whom it is said in another place: [[Wis 2:1|no man hath been known to have returned from hell|Non est qui agnitus sit reversus ab inferis]]; [[Wis 2:2|For we are born of nothing, and after this we shall be as if we had not been|quia ex nihilo nati sumus, et post hæc erimus tanquam non fuerimus]]. [[Wis 2:6|Come, therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that are present, and let us speedily use the creatures as in youth|Venite ergo et fruamur bonis quæ sunt, et utamur creatura tanquam in juventute celeriter]]. And that other saying: [[Is 22:13|Let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die|Comedamus et bibamus ; cras enim moriemur]].

paras.t: Istis igitur respondent electi : Quomodo cantabimus canticum Domini in terra aliena ? id est, qualiter loqui poterimus verbum Dei hominibus vanis, illud spernentibus ? qui sunt terra aliena, quoniam non coluntur a Deo per gratiam, sed a dæmonibus per suggestionem malignam. Hinc namque ait Salvator : Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque mittatis margaritas vestras ante porcos, ne forte conculcent eas pedibus suis.
paras.en: To these, then, the elect reply: [[136:4|How shall we sing the song of the Lord in a strange land?|Quomodo cantabimus canticum Domini in terra aliena ?]] That is, how shall we be able to speak the word of God to vain men who scorn it? They are the strange land, since they are not tilled by God through grace, but by the demons through malignant suggestion [*coluntur*: "are tilled", as land is, and also "are tended, worshipped"]. For hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 7:6|Give not that which is holy to dogs; neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet|Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque mittatis margaritas vestras ante porcos, ne forte conculcent eas pedibus suis]].

paras.t: Denique, licet homo fidelis ita organa sua suspendat fortiter, tamen semetipsum adstringit et obligat, quod nequaquam velit oblivisci cœlestis Jerusalem. Dicit enim: Si oblitus fuero tui, o Jerusalem, civitas Dei summi, non manufacta, sed æterna in cœlo parata, non quærendo te cogitatu, verbo et opere ; oblivioni detur dextera mea, id est, salus mea dispereat, et virtus mea deficiat. Adhæreat lingua mea faucibus meis, ut sim spiritualiter mutus, non loquendo verba utilia, si non meminero tui, sed rebus terrenis inhæsero ; si non proposuero Jerusalem cœlestem in principio lætitiæ meæ, ita quod ipsa sit mihi præcipua causa gaudendi in hoc mundo : quemadmodum ait Apostolus, Spe gaudentes ; et item, Gloriamur in spe gloriæ filiorum Dei. Vel, In principio lætitiæ meæ, ita quod propter nullam carnalem aut sæcularem delectationem mihi occurrentem, omittam plorare desiderio hujus Jerusalem, vel de ejus exspectatione spiritualiter exsultare. Hæc autem dicuntur, non imprecando malum, sed prænuntiando quale malum futurum sit ei qui obliviscitur supernæ Jerusalem.
paras.en: Lastly, although the faithful man thus hangs up his instruments resolutely, yet he binds and pledges himself never to consent to forget the heavenly Jerusalem. For he says: [[136:5|If I forget thee, O Jerusalem|Si oblitus fuero tui, o Jerusalem]], city of the most high God, not made with hands, but eternal, prepared in heaven[[2 Cor 5:1||]], by not seeking thee in thought, word and deed, [[136:5|let my right hand be forgotten|oblivioni detur dextera mea]], that is, let my salvation perish and my strength fail. [[136:6|Let my tongue cleave to my jaws|Adhæreat lingua mea faucibus meis]], so that I be spiritually dumb, not speaking profitable words, [[136:6|if I do not remember thee|si non meminero tui]], but cling to earthly things; [[136:6|If I make not Jerusalem|si non proposuero Jerusalem]], the heavenly one, [[136:6|the beginning of my joy|in principio lætitiæ meæ]], so that she be for me the chief cause of rejoicing in this world: as the Apostle says, [[Rom 12:12|Rejoicing in hope|Spe gaudentes]]; and again, we [[Rom 5:2|glory in the hope of the glory of the sons of God|Gloriamur in spe gloriæ filiorum Dei]]. Or, [[136:6|the beginning of my joy|In principio lætitiæ meæ]]: so that for no carnal or worldly delight that comes my way do I leave off weeping with longing for this Jerusalem, or exulting spiritually in the expectation of her. These things are said, however, not as calling down evil, but as foretelling what evil is to come upon him who forgets the Jerusalem above.

paras.t: Deinde loquitur contra hostes Ecclesiæ. Memor esto, Domine, filiorum Edom, id est hominum terrenorum, in die Jerusalem, id est tempore quo persequuntur Ecclesiam militantem. Edom enim interpretatur sanguinea seu terrena. Vel, In die Jerusalem, id est tempore generalis judicii, quando electi separabuntur a reprobis, separatione æterna atque perfecta. Orat itaque ut impiorum malignitas reprimatur, et Ecclesia liberetur. Qui dicunt : Exinanite, exinanite, id est, Ecclesiam dejicite, fideles subvertite, usque ad fundamentum, id est fidem exsistentem in ea, id est in Ecclesia. Conantur enim nonnulli non solum opera bona, sed etiam fidem electorum evacuare ac dissipare.
paras.en: Next he speaks against the enemies of the Church. [[136:7|Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom|Memor esto, Domine, filiorum Edom]], that is, of earthly men, [[136:7|in the day of Jerusalem|in die Jerusalem]], that is, at the time when they persecute the Church militant. For *Edom* is interpreted "bloody" or "earthy". Or, [[136:7|in the day of Jerusalem|In die Jerusalem]], that is, at the time of the general judgement, when the elect shall be separated from the reprobate with an eternal and perfect separation[[Matt 25:32||]].
