He prays, then, that the malice of the wicked be checked and the Church set free. [[136:7|Who say: Rase it, rase it|Qui dicunt : Exinanite, exinanite]], that is, cast down the Church, overthrow the faithful, [[136:7|even to the foundation|usque ad fundamentum]], that is, the faith existing in it; [[136:7|thereof|in ea]], that is, in the Church. For some strive to bring to nothing and scatter not only the good works but even the faith of the elect.

paras.t: Filia Babylonis, id est gens mundana, civitas impiorum, urbs synagogaque Satanæ, misera, beatus est justus Judex, Deus omnipotens, qui retribuet tibi retributionem tuam, id est justam pœnam, quam retribuisti, id est inflixisti, nobis, injuste persequendo populum Dei. Eadem enim mensura qua mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis. Unde apud Joelem Dominus ait : Cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem super caput vestrum. Solet autem Scriptura per filiam, totum populum designare, sicut dum per Isaiam dicitur : Descende, sede in pulvere, filia Babylon.
paras.en: [[136:8|O daughter of Babylon|Filia Babylonis]], that is, worldly people, the city of the wicked, the town and synagogue of Satan, [[136:8|miserable|misera]]: [[136:8|blessed|beatus]] is the just Judge, God almighty, [[136:8|who shall repay thee thy payment|qui retribuet tibi retributionem tuam]], that is, a just punishment, [[136:8|which thou hast paid|quam retribuisti]], that is, inflicted on, [[136:8|us|nobis]], by unjustly persecuting the people of God. [[Luke 6:38|For with the same measure that you shall mete withal, it shall be measured to you again|Eadem enim mensura qua mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis]][[Matt 7:2||]]. Hence the Lord says in Joel: [[Joel 3:4|I will very soon return you a recompense upon your own head|Cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem super caput vestrum]]. Now Scripture is wont to signify the whole people by *daughter*, as when it is said by Isaias: [[Is 47:1|Come down, sit in the dust|Descende, sede in pulvere]], O [[Is 47:1|daughter of Babylon|filia Babylon]].

paras.t: Beatus est Deus judex, qui tenebit, id est comprehendet, et allidet parvulos suos, id est invidos, Ecclesiæ invidentes et ceteros impios : qui sunt parvuli sensibus atque virtutibus. Sunt etiam parvuli, viles, et indigni divino judicio, quamvis propria æstimatione magni exsistant. Proprie vero invidi dicti sunt parvuli, juxta illud : Parvulum occidit invidia. Hi autem sunt parvuli Dei, quantum ad esse naturæ, seu ratione creationis ; sunt tamen parvuli dæmonum, quantum ad culpam et operationem. A quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est. Allidet itaque, id est, destruet et damnabit, parvulos istos, id est vagos, fluctuantes, spirituali magnitudine carentes, ad petram, id est Christum, qui (teste Scriptura) est reprobis lapis offensionis et petra scandali; vel, Ad petram, id est ad fundum inferni, quando dicturus est eis : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum.
paras.en: [[136:9|Blessed|Beatus]] is God the judge, [[136:9|that shall take|qui tenebit]], that is, seize, [[136:9|and dash|et allidet]] his [[136:9|little ones|parvulos]] [the print reads *suos*, "his", with a footnote giving the other reading *tuos*, "thy", as in the Vulgate], that is, the envious, who envy the Church, and the other wicked: who are little ones in understanding and in virtues. They are also little, that is, vile and worthless in the judgement of God, though great in their own estimation. But it is the envious who are properly called little ones, according to that saying: [[Job 5:2|envy slayeth the little one|Parvulum occidit invidia]]. These are God's little ones as to the being of their nature, or by reason of their creation; yet they are the devils' little ones as to guilt and works. For [[2 Pet 2:19|by whom a man is overcome, of the same also he is the slave|A quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est]]. He shall [[136:9|dash|Allidet]], then, that is, destroy and damn, these [[136:9|little ones|parvulos]], that is, the wandering and wavering, who lack spiritual greatness, [[136:9|against the rock|ad petram]], that is, Christ, who (as Scripture bears witness) is to the reprobate [[1 Pet 2:8|a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal|lapis offensionis et petra scandali]][[Is 8:14||]][[Rom 9:33||]] [the margin gives Is. viii, 14; I Petr. ii, 6; Rom. ix, 33: Denis's words are those of 1 Pet 2:8]; or, [[136:9|against the rock|Ad petram]], that is, to the bottom of hell, when he shall say to them: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]] [Denis reads *Ite*, "Go", where the Vulgate has *Discedite a me*].

paras.t: Hortatur nos Spiritus Sanctus in psalmo præsenti hunc mundum despicere; omnem florem ac prosperitatem ipsius, vanitatem, fallaciamque putare; sæcularem lætitiam, consolationem carnalem, et omnem mundanum amorem funditus exstirpare; ad cœlestia quoque cum ardenti affectu ac lacrimis suspirare; æterna divinaque bona incessabiliter contemplari; gaudiorum cœlestium et invisibilium promissorum nullatenus oblivisci : quoniam Deum amare et ista appetere, est ad patriam tendere : et tanto amplius festinamus, tanto celerius ad supernam Jerusalem imus, quanto ista ferventius desideramus. Quæ utique nequeunt fervide diligi, nisi mundus spernatur. Ideo namque admonemur : Nolite diligere mundum, neque ea quæ in mundo sunt. Si quis autem diligit mundum, non est caritas Patris in eo. Et quid clarius dici potuit a beato Apostolo ?
paras.en: In the present psalm the Holy Ghost exhorts us to despise this world; to count all its flower and prosperity as vanity and deceit; to root out utterly worldly gladness, carnal consolation and all love of the world; to sigh also for heavenly things with ardent affection and with tears; to contemplate unceasingly the eternal and divine goods; never to forget the heavenly joys and the invisible things promised: for to love God and to long for these is to make one's way to the fatherland; and the more fervently we desire them, the more we hasten, the more swiftly we go to the Jerusalem above. And these assuredly cannot be loved fervently unless the world is spurned. For this is why we are admonished: [[1 John 2:15|Love not the world, nor the things which are in the world. If any man love the world, the charity of the Father is not in him|Nolite diligere mundum, neque ea quæ in mundo sunt. Si quis autem diligit mundum, non est caritas Patris in eo]] [the margin gives Joann. ii, 15, that is, the First Epistle of John]. And what could have been said more plainly by the blessed Apostle?

paras.t: Precatio. Te miserante, Domine, redeuntes de Babylone, id est peccatorum confusione, ut pater benignus nos suscipe; teque inspirante, excessus nostros fac ad petram Christum confitendo plenius allidere : ut de cœlesti Sion canticis dignis tibi cantemus hymnum jubilationis.
paras.en: Prayer. In thy mercy, O Lord, receive us like a kindly father as we return from Babylon, that is, from the confusion of sins; and by thy inspiration make us dash our transgressions more fully against the rock, Christ, by confessing them: that with worthy songs of the heavenly Sion we may sing to thee a hymn of jubilation.

137.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI SEPTIMI : CONFITEBOR TIBI, DOMINE, IN TOTO CORDE MEO.
137.title_en: Explanation of the hundred and thirty-seventh psalm: I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart.

paras.t: Habet autem psalmus iste nunc declaratus hunc titulum, Psalmus ipsi David: id est, psalmus iste a David conscriptus, convenit ipsi David, id est omni fideli ac devoto, vel toti Ecclesiæ: in cujus persona loquens beatus Propheta, ait:
paras.en: This psalm, now to be explained, has this title: A psalm [[137:1|For David himself|ipsi David]]: that is, this psalm, written by David, befits David himself, that is, every faithful and devout soul, or the whole Church: speaking in whose person the blessed Prophet says:

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, Domine, confessione laudis et gratiarum actionis, in toto corde meo, id est cunctis viribus animæ meæ, loquendo de viribus ejus superioribus ac divinis, videlicet intellectu et voluntate: id est, attente et affectuose, fideliter et ardenter te laudabo. Vel, In toto corde meo, id est corde omnino converso ad te, adhærenteque tibi: ita quod pro nulla parte erit conversum ad terrena, vana atque carnalia; sed amor tuus illud totaliter possidebit. Sicque affectu puro, ingenti ac integro tibi, o Domine, confitebor, quoniam audisti verba oris mei, id est, preces meas implesti. Beati qui taliter Domino confitentur, qui in illo summo uno, quod solum necessarium est, omne desiderium cordis sui stabiliunt, qui omnem affectionem circa creata ad Dei amorem perordinant, quorum animas nulla turpis affectio maculat.
paras.en: [[137:1|I will praise thee, O Lord|Confitebor tibi, Domine]] [confitebor means both “I will confess” and “I will praise”], with the confession of praise and of thanksgiving, [[137:1|with my whole heart|in toto corde meo]], that is, with all the powers of my soul, speaking of its higher and divine powers, namely the intellect and the will: that is, I will praise thee attentively and lovingly, faithfully and ardently. Or, [[137:1|with my whole heart|In toto corde meo]], that is, with a heart wholly turned to thee and cleaving to thee: so that in no part will it be turned to earthly, vain and carnal things, but thy love will possess it wholly. And so with a pure, mighty and undivided affection I will praise thee, O Lord, [[137:1|for thou hast heard the words of my mouth|quoniam audisti verba oris mei]], that is, thou hast fulfilled my prayers. Blessed are they who so praise the Lord, who fix all the desire of their heart on that one highest good which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]], who order every affection toward created things to the love of God, whose souls no base affection stains.

paras.t: In conspectu angelorum psallam tibi: id est, dum psallo tibi, considerabo angelorum venerandam præsentiam, qua vel tibi adsistunt, vel mihi præsentes sunt: et ita in eorum conspectu me ipsum constituendo, psallam tibi cum reverentia magna, quippe cui angeli sancti cum tremore adsistunt.
paras.en: [[137:1|I will sing praise to thee in the sight of the angels|In conspectu angelorum psallam tibi]]: that is, while I sing psalms to thee, I will consider the venerable presence of the angels, by which they either stand before thee or are present to me: and so, setting myself in their sight, I will sing praise to thee with great reverence, since the holy angels stand before thee with trembling.

paras.t: Adorabo ad templum sanctum tuum: id est, te adorando dirigam oculum mentis meæ ad templum illud altissimum, id est cœlum empyreum, seu triumphantem Ecclesiam, in qua per gloriam habitas. De quo templo Moyses ait: Habitaculum ejus sursum. Sed obviare videtur quod dicit Joannes: Templum non vidi in ea (videlicet in civitate superna, Jerusalem illa cœlesti); Dominus enim Deus omnipotens, templum illius est et Agnus. Et respondendum, quod in ea non est templum, prout templum est domus orationis pro propria salute. Non enim Beati pro sua salute precantur. Unde Salvator ait: In die illo me non rogabitis quidquam. Dicitur autem Deus et Agnus, scilicet Christus, templum illius, quia triumphans Ecclesia habitat in Deo et Christo per beatificam fruitionem. Nihilo minus cœlum empyreum, templum Dei dici potest, quoniam incessanter offertur sibi in eo sacrificium laudis: similiter Ecclesia triumphans, quia in ea habitat Deus per gratiam consummatam.
paras.en: [[137:2|I will worship towards thy holy temple|Adorabo ad templum sanctum tuum]]: that is, in adoring thee I will direct the eye of my mind to that most high temple, that is, the empyrean heaven [the highest heaven, the dwelling of the blessed], or the Church triumphant, in which thou dwellest by glory. Of this temple Moses says: [[Deut 33:27|His dwelling is above|Habitaculum ejus sursum]]. But what John says seems to stand against this: [[Apoc 21:22|I saw no temple therein|Templum non vidi in ea]] (namely in the city above, that heavenly Jerusalem); [[Apoc 21:22|For the Lord God Almighty is the temple thereof, and the Lamb|Dominus enim Deus omnipotens, templum illius est et Agnus]]. And the answer must be that in it there is no temple in so far as a temple is a house of prayer for one’s own salvation; for the blessed do not pray for their own salvation. Whence the Saviour says: [[John 16:23|in that day you shall not ask me any thing|In die illo me non rogabitis quidquam]]. But God and the Lamb, that is, Christ, are called its temple because the Church triumphant dwells in God and in Christ by beatific fruition [that is, the enjoyment of God in the vision of glory]. None the less the empyrean heaven can be called the temple of God, since in it the sacrifice of praise is offered to him without ceasing; and likewise the Church triumphant, because God dwells in it by consummated grace.

paras.t: Et confitebor nomini tuo, id est tibi, Super misericordia tua, id est de gratia et beneficiis mihi et aliis a te clementer collatis, et veritate tua, id est vera impletione qua nobis misertus es, sicut dixisti ac promisisti; vel, Veritate tua, id est de tua justitia, qua impios dereliquisti et condemnasti, bonos autem coronasti, et tibi feliciter conjunxisti. Quoniam magnificasti super omne, id est, omnibus rebus majus et excellentius ostendisti, nomen sanctum tuum, id est te ipsum, faciendo mirabilia quæ nulla valeat agere creatura. Vel: Magnificasti, id est exaltasti, super omne nomen cœlestium, terrestrium, et infernorum, sanctum tuum, id est Christum, de quo dictum est ante, Non dabis Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem. De quo et alibi habetur: Ungatur Sanctus Sanctorum. De quo ipse quoque diabolus, a veritate convictus, compulsus est dicere: Scio quia sis Sanctus Dei. Sicut enim dicit Apostolus, Deus exaltavit illum, et dedit ei nomen quod est super omne nomen, ut in nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur.
paras.en: [[137:2|and I will give glory to thy name|Et confitebor nomini tuo]], that is, to thee, [[137:2|For thy mercy|Super misericordia tua]], that is, for the grace and benefits mercifully bestowed by thee on me and on others, [[137:2|and for thy truth|et veritate tua]], that is, for the true fulfilment by which thou hast had mercy on us[[Amos 7:3||]], as thou didst say and promise [the margin gives Amos vii, 3, where the Lord has pity and revokes a threatened punishment; it fits only loosely]; or, [[137:2|for thy truth|Veritate tua]], that is, for thy justice, by which thou hast forsaken and condemned the wicked, but crowned the good and happily joined them to thyself. [[137:2|for thou hast magnified|Quoniam magnificasti]] [[137:2|above all|super omne]], that is, thou hast shewn it to be greater and more excellent than all things, [[137:2|thy holy name|nomen sanctum tuum]], that is, thyself, by doing wonders that no creature could work. Or: [[137:2|thou hast magnified|Magnificasti]], that is, exalted, [[137:2|above all|super omne]] the name of those in heaven, on earth and under the earth [here Denis takes super omne nomen together, “above every name”], [[137:2|thy holy|sanctum tuum]] one [sanctum tuum can also mean “thy Holy One”], that is, Christ, of whom it was said earlier: [[Ps 15:10|nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption|Non dabis Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem]]. Of whom it is also said elsewhere: [[Dan 9:24|the Saint of saints may be anointed|Ungatur Sanctus Sanctorum]]. Of whom the devil himself too, overcome by the truth, was compelled to say: [[Mark 1:24|I know who thou art, the Holy One of God|Scio quia sis Sanctus Dei]][[Luke 4:34||]]. For, as the Apostle says, [[Phil 2:9|God also hath exalted him and hath given him a name which is above all names|Deus exaltavit illum, et dedit ei nomen quod est super omne nomen]], [[Phil 2:10|That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow|ut in nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur]].

paras.t: In quacumque die naturali, quæ noctem includit, id est quacumque hora, imo quocumque momento hujus diei, invocavero te, exaudi me. Quod si exaudieris me, multiplicabis in anima mea virtutem, id est spiritualem perfectionem. Nam et virtutes connexæ sunt; et dum Deus unam infundit, omnes largitur. Dum autem existentem in gratia exaudit, virtutem gratiæ quæ habetur multiplicat, eam confortando atque augendo.
paras.en: [[137:3|In what day soever|In quacumque die]], that is, in any natural day, which includes the night [the full day of twenty-four hours], that is, in whatever hour, nay, in whatever moment of this day, [[137:3|I shall call upon thee, hear me|invocavero te, exaudi me]]. And if thou hearest me, [[137:3|thou shalt multiply strength in my soul|multiplicabis in anima mea virtutem]] [virtus is both “strength” and “virtue”], that is, spiritual perfection. For the virtues are connected with one another; and when God infuses one, he bestows them all. And when he hears one who is in grace, he multiplies the strength of the grace already possessed, strengthening and increasing it.

paras.t: Confitentur tibi, Domine, confessione duplici, scilicet laudis et culpæ, videlicet te laudando, et se accusando, omnes reges, id est principes, terræ, seu omnes reges, id est universi qui per rationis imperium regunt se ipsos, subjiciendo carnem spiritui, sensualitatem rationi, rationemque Deo; quia audierunt ex ore prædicatorum omnia verba oris tui, quæ in sacra continentur Scriptura. Distributio autem horum nominum, Omnes, et, Omnia, intelligenda est hic pro generibus singulorum, non pro singulis generum: quia nec absolute omnes reges ad fidem conversi sunt, nec omnes conversi omnia verba Dei simpliciter audierunt; sed quidam de omni genere regum conversi sunt, et omnes quædam de omni genere verborum Dei audierunt.
paras.en: They [[137:4|give glory to thee|Confitentur tibi, Domine]], O Lord [Denis reads Confitentur, “they give glory”, where the Vulgate has Confiteantur, “may they give glory”], with a twofold confession, namely of praise and of fault, that is, by praising thee and accusing themselves, [[137:4|all the kings|omnes reges]], that is, the princes, [[137:4|of the earth|terræ]]; or all kings, that is, all those who by the command of reason rule themselves, subjecting the flesh to the spirit, sensuality to reason, and reason to God; [[137:4|for they have heard|quia audierunt]] from the mouth of preachers [[137:4|all the words of thy mouth|omnia verba oris tui]], which are contained in holy Scripture. Now the distribution of these words, All and All [a term of logic: the range of things a universal word such as “all” covers], is to be understood here of the kinds of individuals, not of the individuals of the kinds [that is, some of every kind, not every one of each kind]: for neither have absolutely all kings been converted to the faith, nor have all the converted heard absolutely all the words of God; but some of every kind of kings have been converted, and all have heard some of every kind of the words of God.

paras.t: Et cantent in viis Domini, id est in observationibus præceptorum divinorum, cantandoque dicant: Quoniam magna, imo immensa, est gloria Domini, id est excellentia, beatitudo, lætitia Dei. Plena namque est omnis terra gloria Dei: ubi per gloriam possumus intelligere gloriosa opera Creatoris. Unde in libris Moysis sæpius legitur: Apparuit filiis Israel gloria Domini; et, Implebitur omnis terra gloria Domini.
paras.en: [[137:5|And let them sing in the ways of the Lord|Et cantent in viis Domini]], that is, in keeping the divine commandments, and singing let them say: [[137:5|for great|Quoniam magna]], nay, boundless, [[137:5|is the glory of the Lord|est gloria Domini]], that is, the excellence, blessedness and joy of God. For [[Is 6:3|all the earth is full of his glory|Plena namque est omnis terra gloria Dei]]: where by glory we can understand the glorious works of the Creator. Whence in the books of Moses we often read: [[Ex 16:10|the glory of the Lord appeared|Apparuit filiis Israel gloria Domini]] to the children of Israel[[Ex 24:16||]][[Ex 40:32||]]; and, [[Num 14:21|the whole earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord|Implebitur omnis terra gloria Domini]].

paras.t: Quoniam excelsus Dominus. Est enim laudabilis et supergloriosus et superexaltatus in omnibus sæculis. Et ait Scriptura: Dominus excelsus et sublimis, habitans æternitatem, et sanctum nomen ejus. Est autem Deus excelsus, non loco, sed dignitate. Nihilo minus ipse est super omnia, non elatus; sicut est infra omnia, non oppressus. Et humilia corda respicit oculo pietatis per approbationem, quemadmodum per Isaiam dicit: Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu? Et alta, id est corda superba, a longe, id est per reprobationem, cognoscit: non enim adest eis per gratiam. Propter quod Salomon: Longe, inquit, est Dominus a peccatoribus. Cognoscit itaque alta, juxta illud: Cognovi multa scelera vestra. Et alibi scriptum est: In omni loco oculi Domini contemplantur bonos et malos. Sed hoc interest, quod humiles respicit de prope, superbos autem a longe.
paras.en: [[137:6|For the Lord is high|Quoniam excelsus Dominus]]. For he is [[Dan 3:52|worthy to be praised and exalted above all, in all ages|laudabilis et supergloriosus et superexaltatus in omnibus sæculis]] [Denis’s words, “praiseworthy and glorious above all and exalted above all in all ages”, join phrases from both halves of the verse]. And Scripture says: [[Is 57:15|the High and the Eminent that inhabiteth eternity: and his name is Holy|Dominus excelsus et sublimis, habitans æternitatem, et sanctum nomen ejus]]. Now God is high not in place but in dignity. None the less he is above all things, not lifted up; as he is beneath all things, not weighed down. [[137:6|and looketh on the low|Et humilia corda respicit]] hearts [Denis reads humilia corda, “the low hearts”] with the eye of mercy, by approving them, as he says by Isaias: [[Is 66:2|to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit|Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu]]? [[137:6|and the high|Et alta]], that is, proud hearts, [[137:6|he knoweth|cognoscit]] [[137:6|afar off|a longe]], that is, by reproving them [per reprobationem, the opposite of the approval just mentioned]: for he is not present to them by grace. Wherefore Solomon says: [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe, inquit, est Dominus a peccatoribus]] [Denis has a peccatoribus, “from sinners”]. So he knows the high, according to that saying: [[Amos 5:12|I know your manifold crimes|Cognovi multa scelera vestra]]. And elsewhere it is written: [[Prov 15:3|The eyes of the Lord in every place behold the good and the evil|In omni loco oculi Domini contemplantur bonos et malos]]. But there is this difference, that he looks on the humble from near at hand, but on the proud from afar.

paras.t: Si ambulavero, id est, conversatus fuero et afflictus, in medio tribulationis, a mundo seu dæmone mihi inflictæ, vivificabis me per gratiam, ne spiritualiter moriar aut succumbam. Hoc est verbum bonæ spei, ex magna ad Deum caritate fiduciaque procedens. Et super, id est contra, iram inimicorum meorum visibilium ac invisibilium extendisti, et, ut spero, extendes manum tuam, id est potentiam tuam divinam, reprimendo eorum malignitatem; et salvum me fecit a tentationibus atque periculis dextera tua, id est gratiosa tua præsentia, seu potestas divina, non sinens me ultra vires tentari, sed faciens cum tentatione proventum, videlicet præstans requiem pro labore, coronam pro pugna, gratiam pro mercede.
paras.en: [[137:7|If I shall walk|Si ambulavero]], that is, if I shall have lived and been afflicted, [[137:7|in the midst of tribulation|in medio tribulationis]] brought on me by the world or the devil, [[137:7|thou wilt quicken me|vivificabis me]] by grace, lest I die spiritually or give way. This is a word of good hope, proceeding from great charity and trust toward God. And [[137:7|against|super]] [the Latin super, “over”; Denis glosses it “that is, against”, as the Douay-Rheims renders it] [[137:7|the wrath of my enemies|iram inimicorum meorum]], visible and invisible, [[137:7|thou hast stretched forth|extendisti]], and, as I hope, wilt stretch forth, [[137:7|thy hand|manum tuam]], that is, thy divine power, by checking their malice; [[137:7|and thy right hand|dextera tua]], that is, thy gracious presence, or divine power, [[137:7|hath saved me|et salvum me fecit]] from temptations and dangers, not suffering me to be tempted beyond my strength, but making [[1 Cor 10:13|with temptation issue|cum tentatione proventum]] [proventus, “a way out” or “a good outcome”], that is, granting rest for labour, a crown for the fight, grace as a reward.

paras.t: Dominus retribuet pro me, omnia æquanimiter patiente, dando adversariis debitam pœnam damni ac sensus, pro peccato commisso in me: sicut et alibi ait, Apostolusque allegat, Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam. Et ne hoc videatur dictum ex crudelitate seu zelo vindictæ, sed potius ex pura intentione, subjungit: Domine, misericordia tua in sæculum, id est, æternaliter permanet, nec deficere potest miserendo: juxta illud, Non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare nequeat. Ideo, Domine, opera manuum tuarum, id est creaturas rationales, a tua sapientia atque potentia conditas, ne despicias juste, sed salva benigne. In hoc igitur verbo etiam pro adversariis deprecatur, ne a Deo spernantur: quoniam quem ille despexerit, nullus corrigere potest.
paras.en: [[137:8|The Lord will repay for me|Dominus retribuet pro me]], who suffer all things with an even mind, by giving my adversaries the due penalty of loss and of sense [that is, the loss of God and the pain that is felt] for the sin committed against me: as he also says elsewhere[[Deut 32:35||]], and the Apostle cites it: [[Rom 12:19|Revenge is mine, I will repay|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam]]. And lest this seem said out of cruelty or zeal for vengeance, rather than out of a pure intention, he adds: [[137:8|thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever|Domine, misericordia tua in sæculum]], that is, it abides eternally and cannot fail in showing mercy: according to that saying, [[Is 59:1|the hand of the Lord is not shortened that it cannot save|Non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare nequeat]] [the margin gives Is. lx, 1; the words are Is 59:1]. Therefore, O Lord, [[137:8|the works of thy hands|opera manuum tuarum]], that is, the rational creatures made by thy wisdom and power, [[137:8|despise not|ne despicias]] in justice, but save them in kindness. In this word, then, he prays also for his adversaries, that they be not spurned by God: since [[Eccles 7:14|no man can correct whom he hath despised|quem ille despexerit, nullus corrigere potest]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmus iste spirituali lætitia plenus, laudibus Dei redundat. Et ut eum digne atque devote mereamur cantare, conandum est nobis ut omnes affectiones nostræ ordinentur ad Deum, ita quod amor Dei totaliter cor nostrum possideat: sicque Domino angelorum reverenter psallamus, memores semper Dei ac angelorum præsentiæ.
paras.en: See how this psalm, full of spiritual gladness, overflows with the praises of God. And that we may be found worthy to sing it worthily and devoutly, we must strive that all our affections be ordered to God, so that the love of God may possess our heart wholly: and so let us sing reverently to the Lord of the angels, ever mindful of the presence of God and of the angels.

paras.t: Precatio. Ambulantes in medio tribulationis nos, Domine, vivificare digneris, suspirantes ad te et te invocantes: opera manuum tuarum ne despicias, sed tua nos miseratione salvos facias.
paras.en: Prayer. Vouchsafe, O Lord, to quicken us as we walk in the midst of tribulation, sighing to thee and calling upon thee: despise not the works of thy hands, but in thy mercy make us safe.

138.title: EXPOSITIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI OCTAVI : DOMINE, PROBASTI ME.
138.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and thirty-eighth psalm, of Christ: Lord, thou hast proved me.

paras.t: Præponitur insuper psalmo nunc elucidando titulus talis : In finem, psalmus David : id est, psalmus iste in finem, qui Christus est, nos dirigens, convenit prophetæ David, sicut et ceteris justis. Et adscribitur ei tanquam auctori, sed Christo significato per David, vere et proprie congruit. Sancti enim doctores Hilarius et Augustinus, et viri catholici Cassiodorus ac Hugo, exponunt hunc psalmum de Christo, partim de ipso ratione suæ personæ, partim vero ratione corporis sui mystici. Laborandum tamen videtur, ut quantum fieri potest, totus exponatur de Christo, et totus de membris ipsius.
paras.en: Moreover, this title is set before the psalm now to be explained: [[138:1|Unto the end, a psalm of David|In finem, psalmus David]]: that is, this psalm, which directs us unto the end, who is Christ, befits the prophet David, as it also befits the other just. And it is ascribed to him as its author; but to Christ, who is signified by David, it belongs truly and properly. For the holy doctors Hilary and Augustine, and the catholic men Cassiodorus and Hugh, expound this psalm of Christ, partly of him by reason of his own person, and partly by reason of his mystical body. Yet it seems worth the labour that, as far as can be done, the whole of it be expounded of Christ, and the whole of it of his members.

paras.t: In persona igitur Christi hominis loquens Propheta, ita exorsus est: Domine Pater, seu Deus Trinitas, probasti me, id est, probatum, fidelem et constantem me aliis ostendisti, per hoc quod permisisti me a diabolo tentari, a Judæis irrideri, tandemque turpissima morte occidi: in quibus omnibus firmus et stabilis permansi, propter quod omnibus probatus innotui. Unde ait de Christo Apostolus: Non habemus pontificem, qui non possit compati infirmitatibus nostris; tentatum autem per omnia. Et cognovisti me per approbationem, dicendo tempore baptizationis, transfigurationisque meæ: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo mihi complacui, ipsum audite: sicut Evangelistæ testantur. Tu cognovisti, id est approbasti, sessionem meam, id est humiliationem meam, qua factus sum opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis: prout Apostolus dicit: Christus nos redemit de maledicto, factus pro nobis maledictum; et resurrectionem meam, factam tertio die post passionem, seu glorificationem ac exaltationem meam. Horum enim utrumque summe complacuit Deo.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of Christ as man, the Prophet began thus: [[138:1|Lord|Domine]], Father, or God the Trinity, [[138:1|thou hast proved me|probasti me]], that is, thou hast shewn me to others as proved, faithful and constant, by permitting me to be tempted by the devil[[Matt 4:1||]], mocked by the Jews, and at last slain by a most shameful death[[Matt 27:1||]]: in all of which I remained firm and steadfast, and so became known to all as proved. Hence the Apostle says of Christ: [[Heb 4:15|we have not a high priest who cannot have compassion on our infirmities: but one tempted in all things|Non habemus pontificem, qui non possit compati infirmitatibus nostris; tentatum autem per omnia]]. [[138:1|And known me|Et cognovisti me]], by approving me, saying at the time of my baptism[[Matt 3:17||]] and of my transfiguration: [[Matt 17:5|This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him|Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo mihi complacui, ipsum audite]], as the Evangelists bear witness. [[138:2|Thou hast known|Tu cognovisti]], that is, thou hast approved, [[138:2|my sitting down|sessionem meam]], that is, my humiliation, by which I was made [[Ps 21:7|the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people|opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis]], as the Apostle says: [[Gal 3:13|Christ hath redeemed us from the curse|Christus nos redemit de maledicto]], [[Gal 3:13|being made a curse for us|factus pro nobis maledictum]]; [[138:2|and my rising up|et resurrectionem meam]] [Latin *resurrectio*, "rising up", is also the word for the resurrection], which took place on the third day after the passion[[Matt 28:6||]], or my glorification and exaltation. For both of these were supremely pleasing to God.

paras.t: Intellexisti cogitationes meas humanas de longe, id est de cœlo seu ab æterno; semitam meam, id est evangelicam prædicationem, seu conversationem meam, et funiculum meum, id est partem seu sortem hereditatis meæ, seu terminum operis mei, investigasti, id est, tam diligenter ac intime attendisti, sicut ea quæ investigantur. Investigatio autem proprie sumpta, prout importat discursum a noto ad ignotum, Deo non competit. Quod autem Deus taliter investigavit semitam et funiculum Christi, constat ex eo, quod tam frequenter ac evidenter, per signa et verba, confirmavit ejus doctrinam. Et omnes vias meas, quas ambulavi, et alios docui, scilicet præcepta atque consilia, prævidisti ab æterno; quia non est sermo in lingua mea, id est, respectu tuæ infinitæ sapientiæ et præcognitionis æternæ, sum tanquam non valens eam plene exprimere.
paras.en: [[138:3|Thou hast understood my thoughts|Intellexisti cogitationes meas]], my human thoughts, [[138:3|afar off|de longe]], that is, from heaven, or from eternity; [[138:3|my path|semitam meam]], that is, my preaching of the gospel, or my manner of life, [[138:3|and my line|et funiculum meum]] [Latin *funiculus*, a little cord, the measuring line by which land was allotted], that is, the portion or lot of my inheritance, or the bound of my work, [[138:3|thou hast searched out|investigasti]], that is, thou hast attended to them as diligently and as inwardly as to things that are searched out. But searching out, taken properly, in so far as it implies reasoning from the known to the unknown, does not belong to God. And that God so searched out the path and the line of Christ is plain from this, that he so often and so evidently confirmed his doctrine by signs and words. And [[138:4|all my ways|omnes vias meas]], in which I walked and taught others to walk, namely the precepts and the counsels, [[138:4|thou hast foreseen|prævidisti]] from eternity; [[138:4|for there is no speech in my tongue|quia non est sermo in lingua mea]], that is, with respect to thy infinite wisdom and eternal foreknowledge, I am as one not able to express it fully.

paras.t: Ecce, Domine, tu cognovisti omnia novissima, id est universa quæ mihi in hac ultima mundi ætate acciderunt, videlicet incarnationem, prædicationem, persecutionem, passionem, ac cetera humanitatis meæ mysteria, et antiqua, id est omnia quæ a principio mundi de me dicta, scripta et præsignata sunt; tu formasti me in utero Virginis, quoad formam servilem, seu corporis formationem, quod a Spiritu Sancto supernaturaliter et instantanee organizatum est et formatum. Unde apud Zachariam legitur: Ego cælabo sculpturam ejus, ait Dominus. Et posuisti super me manum tuam, id est potentiam tuam, confirmando me in te, mihique in omnibus cooperando. Horum autem utrumque insinuatur, ubi Christus ait: Dominus in umbra manus suæ protexit me, formans me ex utero servum sibi.
paras.en: [[138:5|Behold, O Lord, thou hast known all things, the last|Ecce, Domine, tu cognovisti omnia novissima]], that is, all that has befallen me in this last age of the world, namely the incarnation, the preaching, the persecution, the passion, and the other mysteries of my humanity, [[138:5|and those of old|et antiqua]], that is, all things that were spoken, written and foreshadowed of me from the beginning of the world; [[138:5|thou hast formed me|tu formasti me]] in the womb of the Virgin, as to the form of a servant, or the forming of the body, which was organized and formed by the Holy Ghost supernaturally and in an instant. Hence we read in Zacharias: [[Zach 3:9|I will grave the graving thereof, saith the Lord|Ego cælabo sculpturam ejus, ait Dominus]]. [[138:5|And hast laid thy hand upon me|Et posuisti super me manum tuam]], that is, thy power, by confirming me in thee and working together with me in all things. Both of these are hinted at where Christ says: The Lord [[Is 49:2|in the shadow of his hand he hath protected me|in umbra manus suæ protexit me]], [[Is 49:5|that formed me from the womb to be his servant|formans me ex utero servum sibi]][[Is 49:1||]].

paras.t: Mirabilis facta est scientia tua ex me: id est, increata tua scientia in anima mea, facta est mirabilis mihi; et per me, id est ex prædicatione mea et Apostolorum meorum, mirabilis facta est per mundum universum, ita quod omnes fideles eam mirantur, quum sit infinita, dicentes illud Apostoli: O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei! Maxime vero apparet et facta est scientia Dei mirabilis ex Christo, id est ex eis quæ de eo scribuntur, videlicet ex hoc, quod ipse unigenitus Filius Dei incarnatus, passus et mortuus est, quod Deus per talem modum genus humanum redimere voluit, quod Christus tanta pro nostra salute assumpsit, fecit ac pertulit. De hac mirabili scientia Dei apud Isaiam scriptum est: Cum quo iniit consilium, et instruxit eum, et docuit eum semitam justitiæ, et erudivit eum scientia? Confortata est, id est, capacitatem meam transcendit, et non potero ad eam, ut ipsam perfecte comprehendam. Quamvis enim anima Christi Deum præ omnibus Sanctis plene et incomparabiliter clarius videat, tamen in infinitum distat a perfectione intellectus divini, qui solus divinam scientiam plene cognoscit. Nullus vero intellectus finitus seu creatus, infinitam essentiam seu scientiam Dei comprehendere valet comprehensione proprie dicta, qua aliquid cognoscitur quoad se totum tam perfecte, sicut ex sua natura cognoscibile est.
paras.en: [[138:6|Thy knowledge is become wonderful to me|Mirabilis facta est scientia tua ex me]] [Latin *ex me*, literally "from me" or "out of me": Denis reads it as "in me" and "through me", and below as "from Christ"]: that is, thy uncreated knowledge has become wonderful to me in my soul; and through me, that is, by my preaching and that of my Apostles, it has become wonderful throughout the whole world, so that all the faithful wonder at it, since it is infinite, saying that word of the Apostle: [[Rom 11:33|O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God!|O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei!]] But most of all the knowledge of God appears, and has become wonderful, from Christ, that is, from the things that are written of him: namely from this, that the only-begotten Son of God himself was made flesh, suffered and died; that God willed to redeem mankind in such a way; that Christ took upon himself, did and bore such great things for our salvation. Of this wonderful knowledge of God it is written in Isaias: [[Is 40:14|With whom hath he consulted, and who hath instructed him, and taught him the path of justice, and taught him knowledge|Cum quo iniit consilium, et instruxit eum, et docuit eum semitam justitiæ, et erudivit eum scientia?]]? [[138:6|it is high|Confortata est]] [Latin *confortata est*, literally "it is grown strong"], that is, it surpasses my capacity, [[138:6|and I cannot reach to it|et non potero ad eam]], so as to comprehend it perfectly. For though the soul of Christ sees God fully, and incomparably more clearly than all the Saints, yet it is infinitely distant from the perfection of the divine intellect, which alone knows the divine knowledge fully. And no finite or created intellect can comprehend the infinite essence or knowledge of God with comprehension properly so called, by which a thing is known in its whole self as perfectly as it is knowable by its nature.

paras.t: Quo ibo a spiritu tuo? et quo a facie tua fugiam? Hæc ait Christus, non quod unquam Deum servili timore timuerit, ex quo procedit fugiendi affectus, quemadmodum mulier adultera virum serviliter timens, quum fornicata fuerit, et hoc viro constiterit, appetit fugere ; sed hoc dicit Christus : primo, ut instruat nos Deum semper timere, eo quod ejus præsentiam nequeamus effugere ; secundo, ut ostendat se omnino paratum ad omnia Patris mandata implenda usque ad crucis patibulum, prout ad Philippenses habetur, Humiliavit semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem. Tanquam dicat : O Deus, quo ibo a spiritu tuo, id est a te ipso qui spiritus es? Et quo a facie, id est præsentia seu cognitione, tua fugiam? quasi dicat : Fugere nequeo ; et si possem, tamen non vellem. Ideo dico : Ecce venio ut faciam voluntatem tuam, Deus. Et passione instante locutus sum : Pater, fiat voluntas tua. Quod autem fugere nequeo, patet : nam Si ascendero in cœlum, tu illic es : quoniam illic facie ad faciem videris, et ibi es, Domine, in templo tuo per resplendentiam gloriæ tuæ ; si descendero in infernum, ades, non solum per essentiam, præsentiam, atque potentiam, sicut in ceteris, sed per ultionis effectum seu justitiæ exsecutionem.
paras.en: [[138:7|Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy face?|Quo ibo a spiritu tuo? et quo a facie tua fugiam?]] Christ says this, not because he ever feared God with servile fear, from which the impulse to flee proceeds, as an adulterous wife who fears her husband servilely longs to flee when she has committed fornication and her husband has learned of it; but Christ says this, first, to teach us always to fear God, since we cannot escape his presence; secondly, to show that he is wholly ready to fulfil all the Father's commands, even to the gibbet of the cross, as we have it in the Epistle to the Philippians: [[Phil 2:8|He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death|Humiliavit semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem]]. As if he said: O God, [[138:7|whither shall I go from thy spirit|quo ibo a spiritu tuo]], that is, from thee thyself, who art spirit[[John 4:24||]]? [[138:7|or whither|Et quo]] [[138:7|from thy face|a facie]], that is, from thy presence or knowledge, [[138:7|shall I flee?|tua fugiam?]] As if he said: I cannot flee; and if I could, yet I would not. Therefore I say: [[Ps 39:8|Behold I come|Ecce venio]] [[Ps 39:9|That I should do thy will|ut faciam voluntatem tuam]], O God. And when the passion was at hand I said: [[Matt 26:42|My Father|Pater]], [[Matt 26:42|thy will be done|fiat voluntas tua]]. And that I cannot flee is plain: for [[138:8|If I ascend into heaven, thou art there|Si ascendero in cœlum, tu illic es]]: since there thou art seen face to face, and there thou art, O Lord, in thy temple, by the shining forth of thy glory; [[138:8|if I descend into hell, thou art present|si descendero in infernum, ades]], not only by essence, presence and power, as in other things, but by the effect of vengeance, or the carrying out of justice.

paras.t: Si sumpsero pennas meas, id est vires divinæ potestatis, ad resurgendum diluculo, id est valde mane in die Paschæ, et habitavero, post resurrectionem, in extremis maris, id est in paradiso terrestri, juxta finem mundi sito. Ibi enim Christus per dies quadraginta cum electis de limbo eductis moratus est, scilicet a die Paschæ usque ad diem ascensionis. Interdum vero discipulis suis apparuit, moxque ad paradisum reversus est. Ideo subditur : Etenim illuc, scilicet ad paradisum, manus tua, id est virtus divina, deducet me, secundum quod homo sum, per dotem agilitatis corpori meo concessam in die resurrectionis, quia tunc corpus glorificatum resumpsi ; et tenebit me, id est, in bono immobiliter conservabit, dextera tua, id est favorabilis, gloriosa atque omnipotens tua præsentia, scilicet tumetipse. Vel : Tenebit me, inseparabiliter in unione personali ac naturali, dextera tua, id est unicum Verbum tuum, seu Filius tuus existens verus Deus. Christi enim humanitatem tenuit Verbum seu Filius Dei, vel ipsemet Christus, secundum quod Deus est. Sicut enim suscitavit semetipsum, sic tenuit naturam assumptam. Porro ante passionem tenuit Verbum humanam Christi naturam inseparabiliter, quantum ad se (quoniam nunquam separata est anima Christi aut corpus ipsius a Verbo, ex quo primo assumpta sunt) ; non autem, quantum ad essentiales partes ipsius ad invicem : nam in triduo mortis, anima caroque Christi a se erant disjunctæ. Post resurrectionem vero tenuit Verbum naturam humanam Christi tam inseparabiliter, quod nec partes ejus a se invicem poterant separari. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur. Dicitur autem Filius Dei, dextera et brachium Dei, juxta illud Isaiæ : Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium. Ipse enim est virtus Dei ; et, Per ipsum facta sunt omnia.
paras.en: [[138:9|If I take my wings|Si sumpsero pennas meas]], that is, the strength of the divine power, to rise again [[138:9|early in the morning|diluculo]], that is, very early on Easter day, [[138:9|and dwell|et habitavero]], after the resurrection, [[138:9|in the uttermost parts of the sea|in extremis maris]], that is, in the earthly paradise, which lies near the end of the world. For there Christ stayed for forty days with the elect led out of limbo, namely from Easter day until the day of the ascension; and from time to time he appeared to his disciples, and soon returned to paradise. Therefore it is added: [[138:10|Even there also|Etenim illuc]], namely to paradise, [[138:10|shall thy hand|manus tua]], that is, the divine power, [[138:10|lead me|deducet me]], in so far as I am man, by the gift of agility [one of the four gifts of the glorified body] granted to my body on the day of the resurrection, since then I took up again my body glorified; and [[138:10|shall hold me|tenebit me]], that is, shall keep me immovably in good, [[138:10|thy right hand|dextera tua]], that is, thy favourable, glorious and almighty presence, namely thou thyself. Or: [[138:10|shall hold me|Tenebit me]], inseparably, in the personal and natural union, [[138:10|thy right hand|dextera tua]], that is, thy only Word, or thy Son, who is true God. For the Word, or Son of God, held the humanity of Christ; or Christ himself, in so far as he is God. For as he raised himself up, so he held the nature he had taken. Before the passion, the Word held the human nature of Christ inseparably as regards himself (since neither the soul of Christ nor his body was ever separated from the Word, from the time they were first assumed); but not as regards its essential parts with one another: for in the three days of his death the soul and the flesh of Christ were parted from each other. But after the resurrection the Word held the human nature of Christ so inseparably that not even its parts could be separated from one another. Therefore the Apostle says: [[Rom 6:9|Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more|Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur]]. Now the Son of God is called the right hand and the arm of God, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles|Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium]]. For he is [[1 Cor 1:24|the power of God|virtus Dei]]; and, [[John 1:3|All things were made by him|Per ipsum facta sunt omnia]].

paras.t: Et dixi, non assertive aut dubitative, sed ironice, ad derisionem eorum qui me putabant detinendum in morte, et igne gehennæ, ut seductorem, urendum : Forsitan tenebræ mortis, sepulturæ ac inferni, conculcabunt me. Hoc autem continuo removet, subdens : et nox, id est mors corporalis, vel sepultura, seu limbus patrum, est illuminatio mea, id est causa et porta glorificationis meæ ; vel, Illuminatio mea, id est res illuminata a me : in deliciis meis spiritualibus. Christus enim sua passione meruit tertia die resuscitari et glorificari : quæ resuscitatio seu glorificatio apte vocatur illuminatio Christi, non interior seu mentalis, sed corporalis. Anima enim Christi semper æque clare Deum conspexit; corpus vero ipsius illuminatum est, animam resumendo, et dotem claritatis adipiscendo. Sic igitur nox, id est mors, fuit Christo homini causa, id est meritum, et porta, id est ingressus, ad illuminationem prædictam : et hoc, in deliciis Christi, quoniam ista illuminatio deliciosa fuerat ei, tanquam accidentale præmium ejus. Limbus vero inferni, seu sancti in eo contenti, qui dicti sunt nox, propter carentiam gloriæ, et quia in tenebris erant, facti sunt illuminatio Christi, id est res illuminata a Christo. Statim enim ut anima ejus a corpore suo recessit, limbum patrum ingressa est, et suo adventu omnes illic spiritualiter illustravit; imo Christus tunc eos visione Dei per speciem beatificavit, quoniam pro originali peccato pœna fuit soluta : et totum istud fuit in deliciis Christi, quoniam de plenitudine suarum deliciarum alios lætificavit. Vel, nox ista fuit illuminatio Christi in deliciis ejus, id est, recipiendo illuminationem prædictam a Christo, positæ sunt in deliciis ejus perfruendo gaudiis Salvatoris.
paras.en: [[138:11|And I said|Et dixi]], not asserting or doubting, but in irony, in mockery of those who thought I would be held fast in death, and burned in the fire of hell as a seducer: [[138:11|Perhaps darkness|Forsitan tenebræ]] of death, of the grave and of hell [[138:11|shall cover me|conculcabunt me]] [Latin *conculcabunt*, literally "shall trample upon"]. But this he at once sets aside, adding: [[138:11|and night|et nox]], that is, bodily death, or the grave, or the limbo of the fathers, is [[138:11|my light|illuminatio mea]], that is, the cause and the gate of my glorification; or, [[138:11|my light|Illuminatio mea]], that is, a thing enlightened by me: [[138:11|in my pleasures|in deliciis meis]], spiritual ones. For Christ by his passion merited to be raised up and glorified on the third day: and this raising up or glorification is fitly called Christ's enlightening, not an inward one, of the mind, but a bodily one. For the soul of Christ always beheld God with equal clearness; but his body was enlightened by taking up the soul again and receiving the gift of brightness. Thus, then, night, that is death, was for Christ as man the cause, that is the merit, and the gate, that is the entrance, to the enlightening spoken of: and this in Christ's pleasures, since this enlightening was delightful to him, as his accidental reward [that is, a joy added to the essential reward, which is the vision of God]. But the limbo of hell, or the saints held in it, who are called night because they lacked glory and were in darkness, became Christ's light, that is, a thing enlightened by Christ. For as soon as his soul departed from his body it entered the limbo of the fathers, and by its coming enlightened all there spiritually; nay, Christ then beatified them with the vision of God by sight [Latin *per speciem*: seeing God as he is, no longer by faith], since the penalty for original sin had been paid: and all this was in Christ's pleasures, since out of the fullness of his own delights he gladdened others. Or, this night was Christ's light in his pleasures, that is, by receiving the said enlightening from Christ they were set in his pleasures, enjoying the joys of the Saviour.

paras.t: Hæc autem omnia vera esse, hinc liquet : Quia tenebræ (de quibus jam dictum est, Forsitan tenebræ conculcabunt me), id est caligo mortis et tenebræ corruptionis, non obscurabuntur a te, id est, lumine tuæ revivificationis et claritate tuæ visitationis non privabuntur ; sed me occisum resuscitabis, et de tenebris sepulturæ reduces. Et nox, de qua dixi, Nox illuminatio mea, sicut dies illuminabitur : id est, mors corporis mei per resuscitationem ad lumen vitæ redibit. Nox etiam sepulturæ ad diem manifestæ apparitionis ducetur. Et nox, id est caligo limbi, sicut dies illuminabitur, me ad inferos descendente. Sicut tenebræ ejus, ita et lumen ejus. Hæc sunt verba Prophetæ, quodammodo rationem reddentis prædictorum, ut sit sensus : Sicut tenebræ ejus, id est sicut mors Christi, ita et lumen, id est vita ejus : id est, utrumque æqualiter in divina potestate constitutum est. Potest etiam accipi de tenebris limbi et lumine ejus, quod a Christo recepit.
paras.en: That all this is true is clear from this: [[138:12|But darkness|Quia tenebræ]] (of which it was said just now, [[138:11|Perhaps darkness shall cover me|Forsitan tenebræ conculcabunt me]]), that is, the gloom of death and the darkness of corruption, [[138:12|shall not be dark to thee|non obscurabuntur a te]], that is, shall not be deprived of the light of thy bringing back to life and of the brightness of thy visitation; but thou wilt raise me up when I have been slain, and bring me back from the darkness of the grave. [[138:12|and night|Et nox]], of which I said, [[138:11|night shall be my light|Nox illuminatio mea]], [[138:12|shall be light all the day|sicut dies illuminabitur]] [Latin *sicut dies illuminabitur*, "shall be lit up as the day"]: that is, the death of my body will return to the light of life by being raised up. The night of the grave also shall be brought to the day of open appearing. And night, that is, the gloom of limbo, shall be lit up as the day when I go down to those below. [[138:12|the darkness thereof, and the light thereof are alike to thee|Sicut tenebræ ejus, ita et lumen ejus]] [literally "as its darkness, so also its light"]: these are the words of the Prophet, giving in some sort the reason of what has been said, so that the sense is: As his darkness, that is, as Christ's death, so also his light, that is, his life: that is, both are set equally within the divine power. It can also be taken of the darkness of limbo, and of its light, which it received from Christ.

paras.t: Quia tu, Domine Pater, possedisti renes meos, id est, carnem meam seu corporalem naturam, vel interiorem sensitivum appetitum ab omni macula culpæ præservasti, faciendo conceptionem meam ac nativitatem ab omni peccato originali actualique liberam, nec permittendo ut unquam inordinatus aliquis motus in anima mea seu renibus esset. Suscepisti me de utero matris meæ, id est, a puncto seu hora qua uterum Virginis sum egressus, tu indesinenter conservasti et protexisti me, prout alibi testatus es : Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum. Vel, Suscepisti me de utero matris meæ, id est, miraculose eduxisti me de clauso utero Matris meæ benedictæ.
paras.en: [[138:13|For thou|Quia tu]], O Lord Father, [[138:13|hast possessed my reins|possedisti renes meos]], that is, thou hast kept my flesh, or bodily nature, or the inner sensitive appetite [the reins were held to be the seat of the sensual desires], from every stain of sin, making my conception and birth free from all original and actual sin, and never allowing any disordered movement to be in my soul or in my reins. [[138:13|thou hast protected me from my mother's womb|Suscepisti me de utero matris meæ]] [Latin *suscepisti*, "thou hast taken me up" or "received me"], that is, from the moment or hour in which I came forth from the Virgin's womb thou hast unceasingly kept and protected me, as thou hast testified elsewhere: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum]]. Or, [[138:13|thou hast protected me from my mother's womb|Suscepisti me de utero matris meæ]], that is, thou didst miraculously bring me forth from the closed womb of my blessed Mother.

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, confessione laudis devotæ, quia terribiliter magnificatus es, id est, per horribilia opera tuam magnitudinem demonstrasti, te magnum esse probasti, in cordibus fidelium magnus et honorandus effectus es. Quamvis hæc opera horribilia, quibus Deus magnificavit se ipsum, intelligi possint destructio mundi per aquas diluvii, submersio Pharaonis, devoratio Dathan et Abiron, ac similia; tamen hoc loco specialiter designantur ea, quæ circa Christum contigerunt. Terribiliter enim magnificatus est Deus, quando in ultionem sanguinis Christi, Judæos tam horribiliter devastavit per Romanos, occidit, et nunc usque affligit. Denique terribiliter magnificatus est in passione Christi, quando a sexta hora usque ad nonam, tenebræ factæ sunt super universam terram, et petræ scissæ sunt, et terra mota est, et monumenta aperta sunt, multique Sanctorum resurrexerunt a mortuis. Mirabilia sunt opera tua, jam prædicta, et cetera quæ fecisti circa me; vel, quæ ego feci in nomine tuo, sicut sunt incarnatio, resurrectio de clauso sepulcro, ingressus ad discipulos januis clausis, ascensio quoque ad cœlos, et reliqua in sacro Evangelio copiose descripta ; et anima mea cognoscet opera ista nimis, id est valde eminenter et clare præ omnibus angelis atque hominibus. Neque enim angeli sancti prædicta Dei opera comprehendere valent, præsertim incarnationem. Anima autem Christi valde excedit omnes Beatos in cognitione istorum : imo de istis illuminat summos ordines supernorum spirituum, secundum Dionysium.
paras.en: [[138:14|I will praise thee|Confitebor tibi]], with the confession of devout praise, [[138:14|for thou art fearfully magnified|quia terribiliter magnificatus es]], that is, thou hast shown thy greatness by fearful works, hast proved thyself to be great, and hast been made great and worthy of honour in the hearts of the faithful. Although these fearful works, by which God magnified himself, may be understood as the destruction of the world by the waters of the flood[[Gen 7:1||]], the drowning of Pharao[[Ex 14:1||]], the swallowing up of Dathan and Abiron[[Num 16:1||]], and the like, yet in this place those things are specially meant which came to pass concerning Christ. For God was fearfully magnified when, in vengeance for the blood of Christ, he so fearfully laid waste the Jews by the Romans, slew them, and afflicts them even to this day. Lastly, he was fearfully magnified in the passion of Christ, when from the sixth hour until the ninth there was darkness over the whole earth[[Matt 27:45||]], and the rocks were rent, and the earth quaked[[Matt 27:51||]], and the graves were opened, and many of the Saints rose from the dead[[Matt 27:52||]]. [[138:14|wonderful are thy works|Mirabilia sunt opera tua]], those already spoken of, and the others that thou hast done concerning me; or those that I have done in thy name, such as the incarnation[[Luke 1:1||]], the resurrection from the closed sepulchre[[Mark 16:1||]], the coming in to the disciples when the doors were shut[[John 20:1||]], the ascension also into heaven, and the rest copiously described in the holy Gospel; [[138:14|and my soul knoweth|et anima mea cognoscet opera ista]] [Denis reads *cognoscet opera ista*, "shall know these works"] [[138:14|right well|nimis]], that is, very eminently and clearly, beyond all angels and men. For not even the holy angels can comprehend the said works of God, especially the incarnation. But the soul of Christ far exceeds all the Blessed in the knowledge of these things: nay, it enlightens the highest orders of the heavenly spirits about them, according to Dionysius.

paras.t: Non est occultatum os meum a te, id est, ori meo non occultasti, neque ab intellectu meo abscondisti, quod fecisti in occulto : id est, opera quæ in abscondito perpetrasti, imo occultissima quæque, quæ aliis abscondisti, mihi clarissime revelasti. Omnia enim præterita, præsentia et futura, universa quoque mysteria gratiæ, anima Christi cognovit. Potest autem per os intelligi intellectus animæ Christi, quo verbum cordis profertur ; vel, os ejus corporale, quoniam Christus ore proprio prædicavit occulta opera Dei. Et substantia mea in inferioribus terræ. Hoc est quod dixit supra, Infixus sum in limo profundi. Est igitur sensus : Substantia mea, id est humana natura a me assumpta, in inferioribus terræ, id est, in mundo isto apparuit, vixit et fuit. Vel, Substantia mea, id est divinitas mea, seu ego ipse, in inferioribus terræ, id est in hoc mundo, conversatus sum, et divinitas mea ad hæc infima se inclinavit per incarnationem. Hinc Apostolus loquens de Christo, ait : Quod autem ascendit, quid est nisi quia primum descendit in inferiores partes terræ? Unde legitur apud Baruch : Post hæc super terram visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est. Vel sic : Substantia mea, id est, corpus et anima fuerunt in inferioribus terræ : nam anima fuit in limbo, et corpus in monumento.
paras.en: [[138:15|My bone is not hidden from thee|Non est occultatum os meum a te]] [Latin *os* may be "bone" (*ossis*) or "mouth" (*oris*); Denis takes it here as "mouth"], that is, thou hast not hidden from my mouth, nor concealed from my intellect, [[138:15|which thou hast made in secret|quod fecisti in occulto]]: that is, the works that thou hast wrought in hiding, nay, all the most hidden things that thou hast hidden from others, thou hast most clearly revealed to me. For the soul of Christ knew all things past, present and to come, and all the mysteries of grace as well. Now by the mouth may be understood the intellect of Christ's soul, by which the word of the heart is uttered; or his bodily mouth, since Christ with his own mouth preached the hidden works of God. [[138:15|and my substance in the lower parts of the earth|Et substantia mea in inferioribus terræ]]. This is what he said above: [[Ps 68:3|I stick fast in the mire of the deep|Infixus sum in limo profundi]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxviii, 3; the words are those of Ps 68:3]. The sense, then, is: My substance, that is, the human nature I assumed, in the lower parts of the earth, that is, appeared, lived and was in this world. Or, My substance, that is, my Godhead, or I myself, dwelt in the lower parts of the earth, that is, in this world, and my Godhead bowed itself down to these lowest things by the incarnation. Hence the Apostle, speaking of Christ, says: [[Eph 4:9|Now that he ascended, what is it, but because he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?|Quod autem ascendit, quid est nisi quia primum descendit in inferiores partes terræ?]] And so we read in Baruch: [[Bar 3:38|Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|Post hæc super terram visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]]. Or thus: My substance, that is, my body and soul, were in the lower parts of the earth: for the soul was in limbo, and the body in the tomb.

paras.t: Imperfectum meum, id est naturales defectus quos assumpsi, viderunt oculi tui, id est, sapientia tua cognovit cur eos assumpsi. Non enim habuit Christus imperfectum aliquod virtutis aut vitæ, sed indetrahibiles assumpsit defectus seu mala pœnæ, ut nos ab eis erueret. Et in libro tuo omnes scribentur, id est, boni ac mali a te cognoscentur. Per librum namque intelligitur Dei cognitio : in qua omnes firmiter continentur, sicut scriptura in libro. Quamvis autem in libro seu notitia prædestinationis divinæ soli electi conscripti sint, tamen in libro divinæ cognitionis universi scribuntur, imo et opera singulorum, sicut beatus Job dicit : Scribis enim contra me amaritudines. Et Ecclesiasticus : Oculi (ait) Domini multo plus lucidiores super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum. Dies, id est homines spirituales, præsertim Apostoli : de quibus præhabitum est, Dies diei eructat verbum; formabuntur per gratiam Spiritus Sancti, exuendo veterem hominem cum actibus suis, et deserendo opera tenebrarum, ut sint filii lucis. Talibus namque diebus Paulus : Eratis, inquit, aliquando tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino. Et nemo in eis, id est, nullus homo in istis diebus sistere aut confidere debet, ita quod nemo in eis formabitur, ut perfectionem aut nomen ab eis sortiatur. Hoc est quod dicit Apostolus : Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit, Deus autem incrementum dedit. Neque ergo qui plantat est aliquid, neque qui rigat; sed qui incrementum dat, Deus. Et item : Quum alius dicit, Ego quidem sum Pauli, ego autem Apollo, ego vero Cephas, nonne homines estis? Numquid in nomine Pauli baptizati estis? Hinc quoque, ut in Actibus legitur, quum quidam voluissent sacrificare Paulo et Barnabæ tanquam diis, eo quod Paulus a nativitate claudum sanasset, Apostoli scissis vestibus suis, responderunt : Viri, quid facitis? Et nos mortales sumus, similes vobis homines. Nemo ergo formabitur in eis : nam, Maledictus homo qui confidit in homine.
paras.en: [[138:16|my imperfect being|Imperfectum meum]], that is, the natural defects which I assumed, [[138:16|Thy eyes did see|viderunt oculi tui]], that is, thy wisdom knew why I assumed them. For Christ had no imperfection of virtue or of life; but he assumed the blameless defects [Latin *indetrahibiles*, Damascene's term for natural weaknesses that carry no reproach, such as hunger, thirst and death], or the evils of punishment, that he might deliver us from them. [[138:16|and in thy book all shall be written|Et in libro tuo omnes scribentur]], that is, good and bad shall be known by thee. For by the book is understood the knowledge of God, in which all are firmly contained, as writing is in a book. And though in the book, or knowledge, of divine predestination only the elect are written, yet in the book of divine knowledge all are written, nay, and the works of each, as blessed Job says: [[Job 13:26|For thou writest bitter things against me|Scribis enim contra me amaritudines]]. And Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 23:28|the eyes|Oculi]] (he says) [[Ecclus 23:28|of the Lord are far brighter than the sun, beholding round about all the ways of men|Domini multo plus lucidiores super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum]]. [[138:16|days|Dies]], that is, spiritual men, especially the Apostles, of whom it was said before, [[Ps 18:3|Day to day uttereth speech|Dies diei eructat verbum]], [[138:16|shall be formed|formabuntur]] by the grace of the Holy Ghost, putting off the old man with his deeds and forsaking the works of darkness, that they may be children of the light. For to such days Paul says: [[Eph 5:8|you were|Eratis]], he says, [[Eph 5:8|heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord|aliquando tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino]]. [[138:16|and no one in them|Et nemo in eis]], that is, no man ought to rest or trust in these days, so that no one shall be formed in them, so as to take his perfection or his name from them. This is what the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 3:6|I have planted, Apollo watered: but God gave the increase|Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit, Deus autem incrementum dedit]]. [[1 Cor 3:7|Therefore, neither he that planteth is any thing, nor he that watereth: but God that giveth the increase|Neque ergo qui plantat est aliquid, neque qui rigat; sed qui incrementum dat, Deus]]. And again: [[1 Cor 3:4|while one saith: I indeed am of Paul|Quum alius dicit, Ego quidem sum Pauli]], [[1 Cor 1:12|and I am of Apollo; and I of Cephas|ego autem Apollo, ego vero Cephas]], [[1 Cor 3:4|are you not men?|nonne homines estis?]] [[1 Cor 1:13|Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?|Numquid in nomine Pauli baptizati estis?]] [Denis joins 1 Cor 3:4 with 1 Cor 1:12–13]. Hence also, as we read in the Acts, when certain men wished to offer sacrifice to Paul and Barnabas as to gods, because Paul had healed a man lame from his birth, the Apostles rent their garments and answered: [[Acts 14:14|Ye men, why do ye these things? We also are mortals, men like unto you|Viri, quid facitis? Et nos mortales sumus, similes vobis homines]]. No one, then, shall be formed in them: for, [[Jer 17:5|Cursed be the man that trusteth in man|Maledictus homo qui confidit in homine]].

paras.t: Deinde Christus ad Deum Patrem, seu totam superbeatissimam Trinitatem, unum verum simplicissimum Deum, ait : Mihi autem, id est ad honorem meum, nimis honorati sunt amici tui, Deus, id est Apostoli et apostolici viri, qui omnia relinquentes, mea sunt assecuti vestigia, propter quod digni facti sunt amicitia tua. Hos enim Deus multipliciter honoravit, dando eis varias gratias Spiritus Sancti, videlicet sapientiam, omnium linguarum notitiam, gratiam curationum, spiritum prophetiæ, sanctimoniam vitæ. Nimis confortatus est principatus eorum. Nam constituti sunt principes super omnem terram, prævalueruntque mundo, carni, ac dæmoni ; et adeo confortati sunt in gratia Dei, ut occidi possent, flecti non possent, sicut et Paulus ex eorum persona testatur : Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi ? Tribulatio ? an angustia ? an fames ? an nuditas ? an periculum ? an persecutio? an gladius ? Et iterum ait de principatu antiquorum Dei sanctorum et amicorum : Per fidem vicerunt regna, operati sunt justitiam, adepti sunt repromissiones ; obturaverunt ora leonum, exstinxerunt impetum ignis, etc. Dinumerabo eos. Christus enim nomina prædestinatorum determinate cognoscit. Unde Moysi Dominus ait : Te ipsum novi ex nomine. Et super arenam multiplicabuntur prædicti amici tui, videlicet viri spirituales et sancti : vel quia excedunt numerum arenæ maris; vel quia eorum multitudo aptius exprimi nequit, nisi ut dicantur plures arena maris. Unde de electis et Dei amicis ait Joannes : Vidi turbam magnam quam nemo dinumerare poterat, ex omnibus tribubus et linguis et populis, stantes ante thronum Dei.
paras.en: Then Christ says to God the Father, or to the whole most blessed Trinity, the one true and most simple God: [[138:17|But to me|Mihi autem]], that is, to my honour, [[138:17|thy friends, O God, are made exceedingly honourable|nimis honorati sunt amici tui, Deus]] [the margin gives the reading *honorificati*, that of the Vulgate, for Denis's *honorati*], that is, the Apostles and apostolic men, who, leaving all things, have followed in my footsteps[[Matt 19:27||]] [the margin gives Matth. xx, 27; the passage is Matt 19:27], and so have been made worthy of thy friendship. For God honoured these in many ways, giving them various graces of the Holy Ghost, namely wisdom, knowledge of all tongues[[Acts 2:4||]], the grace of healings[[Matt 10:1||]], the spirit of prophecy, holiness of life. [[138:17|their principality is exceedingly strengthened|Nimis confortatus est principatus eorum]]. For they were made [[Ps 44:17|princes over all the earth|principes super omnem terram]] [the margin gives Ps. xvii, 17; the words are those of Ps 44:17], and prevailed over the world, the flesh and the devil; and they were so strengthened in the grace of God that they could be slain but could not be bent, as Paul too testifies in their person: [[Rom 8:35|Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation? Or distress? Or famine? Or nakedness? Or danger? Or persecution? Or the sword?|Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi ? Tribulatio ? an angustia ? an fames ? an nuditas ? an periculum ? an persecutio? an gladius]] And again he says of the principality of the ancient saints and friends of God: [[Heb 11:33|by faith conquered kingdoms, wrought justice, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions|Per fidem vicerunt regna, operati sunt justitiam, adepti sunt repromissiones ; obturaverunt ora leonum]]; [[Heb 11:34|Quenched the violence of fire|exstinxerunt impetum ignis]], etc. [[138:18|I will number them|Dinumerabo eos]]. For Christ knows the names of the predestined distinctly. Hence the Lord says to Moses: [[Ex 33:17|thee I have known by name|Te ipsum novi ex nomine]]. [[138:18|and they shall be multiplied above the sand|Et super arenam multiplicabuntur]], these thy friends of whom we have spoken, namely spiritual and holy men: either because they exceed the number of the sand of the sea, or because their multitude cannot be more fitly expressed than by saying that they are more than the sand of the sea. Hence John says of the elect and the friends of God: [[Apoc 7:9|I saw a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations and tribes and peoples and tongues, standing before the throne|Vidi turbam magnam quam nemo dinumerare poterat, ex omnibus tribubus et linguis et populis, stantes ante thronum]] of God.

paras.t: Præterea quidam exponunt hos duos versiculos de angelis sanctis, qui appellantur amici Dei : qui utique valde honorati sunt, et nimis confortatus est principatus eorum, quia ab eis regitur corporalis creatura atque ecclesiastica hierarchia ; qui etiam super arenam multiplicantur, prout de eis apud Job dicitur : Numquid est numerus militum ejus ? Et Daniel ait : Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei. Hæ vero expositiones, quantum ad numerum amicorum Dei, in idem redeunt, dummodo omnes homines prædestinati dicantur amici Dei : quia, secundum Gregorium, tot homines salvabuntur, quot angeli permanserunt stantes.
paras.en: Moreover, some expound these two verses of the holy angels, who are called the friends of God: who indeed are greatly honoured, and [[138:17|their principality is exceedingly strengthened|confortatus est principatus eorum]], since by them the bodily creation and the ecclesiastical hierarchy are ruled; and who are also multiplied above the sand, as is said of them in Job: [[Job 25:3|Is there any numbering of his soldiers?|Numquid est numerus militum ejus]] And Daniel says: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him|Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei]]. But these expositions come to the same thing as regards the number of God's friends, provided that all predestined men are called friends of God: since, according to Gregory, as many men will be saved as there are angels who remained standing.

paras.t: Exsurrexi ego Christus a mortuis, sicut prædixi, et adhuc sum tecum, id est, usque ad secundum meum adventum tecum invisibiliter ero, quantum ad viatores. Interim enim sedebo ad dexteram tuam in cœlo, nec hominibus generaliter visibiliterque apparebo, donec adveniat dies judicii, in quo omnibus manifestus ostendar. Unde dicit Apostolus : Præcipio tibi coram Deo, etc., ut serves mandatum sine macula irreprehensibile usque in adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quem suis temporibus ostendet beatus et solus potens, Rex regum, etc.
paras.en: [[138:18|I rose up|Exsurrexi]], I, Christ, from the dead, as I foretold[[Mark 16:7||]] [the margin gives Marc. xvi, 19 and Ibid. xvi; Mark 16:7, "as he told you", fits here], [[138:18|and am still with thee|et adhuc sum tecum]], that is, until my second coming I shall be with thee invisibly, as regards wayfarers [that is, men still on the way, in this life]. For in the meantime I shall sit at thy right hand in heaven[[Mark 16:19||]], and shall not appear to men generally and visibly until the day of judgment comes, in which I shall be shown openly to all. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 6:13|I charge thee before God|Præcipio tibi coram Deo]], etc., [[1 Tim 6:14|That thou keep the commandment without spot, blameless, unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ|ut serves mandatum sine macula irreprehensibile usque in adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], [[1 Tim 6:15|Which in his times he shall shew, who is the Blessed and only Mighty, the King of kings|quem suis temporibus ostendet beatus et solus potens, Rex regum]], etc.

paras.t: Si occideris, Deus, id est, quia æternaliter condemnabis, et nunc spiritualiter occides per gratiæ subtractionem, peccatores, impœnitentes et reprobos, viri sanguinum, id est odiosi, carnales et vitiosi, declinate a me in die judicii, quando dicturus sum vobis : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Hoc est quod Christus ait : Multi dicent mihi in die illo, Domine, Domine. Et tunc confitebor illis : Nescio vos unde sitis ; discedite a me, omnes operarii iniquitatis.
paras.en: [[138:19|If thou wilt kill|Si occideris]], [[138:19|O God|Deus]], that is, since thou wilt condemn eternally, and now dost kill spiritually by withdrawing grace, [[138:19|the wicked|peccatores]], the impenitent and the reprobate: [[138:19|ye men of blood|viri sanguinum]], that is, hateful, carnal and vicious men, [[138:19|depart from me|declinate a me]] on the day of judgment, when I shall say to you: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]] [Denis has *Ite*, "Go", for *Discedite a me*]. This is what Christ says: [[Matt 7:22|Many will say to me in that day: Lord, Lord|Multi dicent mihi in die illo, Domine, Domine]]. [[Matt 7:23|And then will I profess unto them|Et tunc confitebor illis]]: [[Luke 13:27|I know you not, whence you are. Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity|Nescio vos unde sitis ; discedite a me, omnes operarii iniquitatis]] [the margin gives Matth. vii, 22, 23; these last words are those of Luke 13:27].

paras.t: Quia dicitis intra vos, in cogitatione perversa et pessima : Accipiant in vanitate civitates suas, id est, injusti in sua vanitate ac malignitate prævaleant, et civitates suas, id est bona et loca seu habitacula quæ desiderant, quamvis ad justos pertineant, ipsi acquirant. Vel sic : Quia dicitis, o viri sanguinum, in cogitatione contra justos : Accipiant justi seu religiosi, in vanitate, id est frustra atque in vanum, civitates suas, id est particulares Ecclesias, congregationes seu claustra, ita quod nihil proficiat eorum saluti, quod se a nobis separant et elongant.
paras.en: [[138:20|Because you say|Quia dicitis]] within yourselves, [[138:20|in thought|in cogitatione]] perverse and most wicked: [[138:20|They shall receive|Accipiant]] [[138:20|in vain|in vanitate]] their cities [Denis reads *Accipiant in vanitate civitates suas*, "Let them receive their cities in vanity", where the Douay-Rheims, with the Clementine text, has "They shall receive thy cities in vain"], that is, let the unjust prevail in their vanity and malice, and let them acquire their cities, that is, the goods and places or dwellings which they desire, though these belong to the just. Or thus: [[138:20|Because you say|Quia dicitis]], O men of blood, [[138:20|in thought|in cogitatione]] against the just: Let the just, or religious, receive [[138:20|in vain|in vanitate]], that is, to no purpose and in vain, their cities, that is, their particular churches, congregations or cloisters, so that their separating and withdrawing themselves from us may profit their salvation nothing.

paras.t: Nonne qui oderunt te, Domine, oderam ? quasi dicat, Imo. Oderat enim Christus homo inimicos Dei, non quantum ad naturam, sed per respectum ad culpam. Amare namque, secundum Philosophum, est alicui bonum velle ; odire vero, est alicui malum optare. Quemadmodum autem justo debetur gloria, et bono dilectio (objectum enim appetitus est, bonum), sic injusto debetur miseria, et odium malo. Peccatorem ergo, in quantum peccator est, debemus odire, id est pœnam atque miseriam ejus velle, ut scilicet corrigatur in præsenti, ne pereat in æternum sicut justitia exigit ; in quantum vero est homo et creatura, seu conversionis et beatitudinis capax, amandus est, quemadmodum præcepit Christus : Diligite inimicos vestros. Hæc autem agendo, conformamus nos Deo, qui omnia amat quantum ad id quod sunt et a Creatore receperunt, juxta illud : Diligis omnia quæ sunt, et nihil odisti eorum quæ fecisti. Verumtamen rationales creaturas in vitiis deordinatas, a rectitudine obliquatas, a Deo aversas odit Deus secundum quod tales sunt : juxta illud, Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus. Sic autem Christus præcipue oderat impios, de quo subditur : et super inimicos tuos tabescebam, id est, magno zelo contra eorum pravitatem zelatus sum : sicut patebat, dum ementes et vendentes de templo ejeci. Tunc enim zelus domus Dei comedit me.
paras.en: [[138:21|Have I not hated them, O Lord, that hated thee|Nonne qui oderunt te, Domine, oderam]]? as if he said: Yes indeed. For Christ as man hated the enemies of God, not as to their nature, but with respect to their guilt. For to love, according to the Philosopher, is to will good to someone; and to hate is to wish evil to someone. Now as glory is due to the just, and love to the good (for the object of the appetite is the good), so misery is due to the unjust, and hatred to the bad.
