The sinner, then, in so far as he is a sinner, we ought to hate, that is, to will his punishment and misery, namely that he may be corrected in this present life, lest he perish for ever, as justice demands; but in so far as he is a man and a creature, or capable of conversion and of beatitude, he is to be loved, as Christ commanded: [[Matt 5:44|Love your enemies|Diligite inimicos vestros]]. By doing this we conform ourselves to God, who loves all things as to what they are and have received from the Creator, according to that saying: [[Wis 11:25|thou lovest all things that are, and hatest none of the things which thou hast made|Diligis omnia quæ sunt, et nihil odisti eorum quæ fecisti]]. Yet rational creatures that are disordered in vices, bent away from rectitude and turned away from God, God hates in so far as they are such: according to that saying, [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful|Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]]. In this way, then, Christ especially hated the wicked; and of this it is added: [[138:21|and pined away because of thy enemies|et super inimicos tuos tabescebam]], that is, I was zealous with great zeal against their wickedness: as was plain when I cast out of the temple those who bought and sold[[Matt 21:12||]][[John 2:15||]]. For then [[Ps 68:10|the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up|zelus domus Dei comedit me]] [Denis has *domus Dei*, "the house of God", for *domus tuæ*, "thy house"].

paras.t: Perfecto odio, id est odio virtuoso et justo, oderam illos, et inimici facti sunt mihi, propter eorum malitiam. Est itaque quoddam odium malum, vitiosum et imperfectum, quod est mortale peccatum, quo natura alterius oditur, vel gratiæ fraternæ invidetur. Hoc odium Christo et membris ejus non convenit. Odium vero perfectum, quo oditur culpa et auctor culpæ in quantum hujusmodi, est de quo loquitur nunc psalmus.
paras.en: [[138:22|with a perfect hatred|Perfecto odio]], that is, with a virtuous and just hatred, [[138:22|I have hated them|oderam illos]], [[138:22|and they are become enemies to me|et inimici facti sunt mihi]], because of their malice. There is, then, a certain hatred that is evil, vicious and imperfect, which is a mortal sin, by which the nature of another is hated, or a brother's grace is envied. This hatred does not befit Christ and his members. But the perfect hatred, by which guilt and the author of guilt are hated as such, is the one of which the psalm now speaks.

paras.t: Deinde Christus ait : Proba me, Deus, id est, per tormenta passionis probatum ostende me : sicut in principio psalmi inductum est, Domine, probasti me. Et scito cor meum per approbationem. Hoc Christus non dicit orando, quoniam a principio suæ conceptionis in Virgine, confirmatum erat cor ejus in Deo, sed potius congratulando. Interroga me per flagella, et cognosce semitas meas, id est, opera mea attende. Hoc Christus orat non pro se, sed pro nobis. Non enim oravit ut Deo placerent opera sua, quoniam scivit se non posse peccare ; oravit autem ut Deus attenderet opera sua, indulgendo propter meritum eorum universæ Ecclesiæ. Sic enim interpellat pro nobis, secundum Apostolum, ostendens Patri latus et vulnera, secundum Bernardum.
paras.en: Then Christ says: [[138:23|Prove me, O God|Proba me, Deus]], that is, show me proved through the torments of the passion, as was set down at the beginning of the psalm, [[138:1|Lord, thou hast proved me|Domine, probasti me]]. [[138:23|and know my heart|Et scito cor meum]], by approving it. Christ does not say this by way of prayer, since from the beginning of his conception in the Virgin his heart was confirmed in God, but rather by way of rejoicing. [[138:23|examine me|Interroga me]] [Latin *interroga*, literally "question me"] by scourges, [[138:23|and know my paths|et cognosce semitas meas]], that is, attend to my works. This Christ prays not for himself, but for us. For he did not pray that his works might please God, since he knew that he could not sin; but he prayed that God would attend to his works, granting pardon for their merit to the whole Church. For so he [[Rom 8:34|maketh intercession for us|interpellat pro nobis]][[Heb 7:25||]], according to the Apostle, showing the Father his side and his wounds, according to Bernard.

paras.t: Et vide si via iniquitatis in me est, id est, falsa doctrina, seu simile aliquod in me exsistat. Hoc Christus dicit, non dubitando an aliquid mali in se habeat locum, sed ex magna securitate, ut ostendat se ab omni culpa penitus alienum, nec adversariorum suorum, sibi multa scelera imponentium, se timere calumniam. Et deduc me in via æterna, id est in via ad æternam gloriam perducente, videlicet in ascensione, per quam ivi ad felicitatem æternam. Orat igitur Christus ut Deus in ascensione ipsum perducat ad cœlum. Non enim humana et pure naturali, sed divina virtute ascendit. Et sicut oravit pro gloria resurrectionis, sic quoque oravit pro deductione ascensionis. Pro iis enim quæ ad accidentale præmium pertinent, Christus oravit etiam pro se ipso ; pro præmio autem essentiali precatus non est, nisi pro nobis.
paras.en: [[138:24|And see if there be in me the way of iniquity|Et vide si via iniquitatis in me est]], that is, whether false doctrine, or anything like it, is in me. Christ says this, not doubting whether anything evil has place in him, but out of great assurance, to show that he is wholly a stranger to all guilt, and does not fear the calumny of his adversaries, who laid many crimes to his charge. [[138:24|and lead me in the eternal way|Et deduc me in via æterna]], that is, in the way that leads to eternal glory, namely in the ascension, by which I went to eternal happiness. Christ prays, then, that God may lead him up to heaven in the ascension. For he ascended not by a human and purely natural power, but by divine power. And as he prayed for the glory of the resurrection, so too he prayed for being led up in the ascension. For Christ prayed even for himself for the things that belong to his accidental reward; but for the essential reward he did not pray, except for us.

138.title: EXPOSITIO EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI OCTAVI, DE MEMBRIS CHRISTI SEU QUOCUMQUE FIDELI.
138.title_en: Exposition of the same hundred and thirty-eighth psalm, of the members of Christ or any one of the faithful.

paras.t: Denique psalmus iste exponi potest de homine justo. Qui ait : Domine, probasti me, id est, per prospera et adversa inquisisti et examinasti me, qualis essem ; et cognovisti me, id est, fidelem atque constantem me invenisti, ex tali probatione, eo quod nec in prosperis, nec in adversis a recta via abierim.
paras.en: Lastly, this psalm can be expounded of the just man, who says: [[138:1|Lord, thou hast proved me|Domine, probasti me]], that is, thou hast searched and examined me through prosperity and adversity, to see what manner of man I was; [[138:1|and known me|et cognovisti me]], that is, from such a proving thou hast found me faithful and constant, because I have not gone aside from the right way either in prosperity or in adversity.

paras.t: Dicitur autem Deus probare et tentare, non ut ipse cognitionem recipiat, sed ut homo se ipsum cognoscat, et ab aliis cognoscatur qualis sit; vel, quia per modum probantis se habet. Sic enim ait ad Abraham quem tentavit : Nunc cognovi quod timeas Deum, et non peperceris filio tuo unigenito propter me. Utrumque enim cognovit, antequam eum tentaret ; sed dicitur tunc cognovisse, quia tunc fecit alios illud cognoscere per tam solennem obedientiam Abrahæ. Sic quoque Dominus loquitur filiis Israel, qui vitulum aureum adoraverunt : Jam nunc depone ornatum tuum, ut sciam quid faciam tibi. Numquid ante non scivit quid faceret eis ? Dicitur itaque Deus probare et tentare, sicque cognoscere homines, quoniam probando facit homines cognosci, ostendendo eos ex probatione fideles aut inconstantes : quod evidenter patet ex eo, quod Moyses ait populo Judæorum : Recordaberis cuncti itineris, per quod adduxit te Dominus Deus tuus, ut affligeret te atque tentaret, et nota fierent quæ versabantur in corde tuo, utrum custodires mandata illius, an non. Ita a Deo probatus est Job, et probus inventus est, qui ait : Probavit me Dominus quasi aurum quod per ignem transit. Et legitur apud Salomonem : Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus.
paras.en: Now God is said to prove and to try, not that he himself may come to know, but that man may know himself and be known by others for what he is; or because he acts after the manner of one who proves. For thus he said to Abraham, whom he tried: [[Gen 22:12|now I know that thou fearest God, and hast not spared thy only begotten son for my sake|Nunc cognovi quod timeas Deum, et non peperceris filio tuo unigenito propter me]]. For he knew both before he tried him; but he is said to have known then because he then made others know it, through so solemn an obedience of Abraham. So too the Lord speaks to the children of Israel, who had adored the golden calf: [[Ex 33:5|Now presently lay aside thy ornaments, that I may know what to do to thee|Jam nunc depone ornatum tuum, ut sciam quid faciam tibi]]. Did he not know beforehand what he would do with them? God, then, is said to prove and to try, and so to know men, because by proving them he makes men known, showing them by the proof to be faithful or inconstant. This is plain from what Moses says to the people of the Jews: [[Deut 8:2|thou shalt remember all the way through which the Lord thy God hath brought thee|Recordaberis cuncti itineris, per quod adduxit te Dominus Deus tuus]], [[Deut 8:2|to afflict thee and to prove thee, and that the things that were known in thy heart might be made known, whether thou wouldst keep his commandments or no|ut affligeret te atque tentaret, et nota fierent quæ versabantur in corde tuo, utrum custodires mandata illius, an non]]. So was Job proved by God and found upright, who says: The Lord [[Job 23:10|has tried me as gold that passeth through the fire|Probavit me Dominus quasi aurum quod per ignem transit]]. And we read in Solomon of the Lord: [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace, he hath proved|Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit]] his elect [Denis reads *electos*, the elect, where the Vulgate has *illos*, them].

paras.t: Nequaquam ergo deficiamus, dum a Deo corripimur, dum per adversa probamur, dum injurias patimur, sed nec prosperis extollamur : imo prædicta mala patiendo lætemur, sperantes nos pertinere ad numerum electorum, de quibus Dominus ait : Deducam eos per ignem, et uram eos sicut uritur argentum, et probabo eos sicut probatur aurum. Et exaudiam eos et dicam : Populus meus tu es.
paras.en: Let us by no means faint, then, when we are chastised by God[[Prov 3:11||]], when we are proved by adversity, when we suffer wrongs; nor yet let us be puffed up by prosperity. Rather, let us rejoice in suffering the evils just named, hoping that we belong to the number of the elect, of whom the Lord says: I will lead them through the fire, and [[Zach 13:9|will refine them as silver is refined: and I will try them as gold is tried|uram eos sicut uritur argentum, et probabo eos sicut probatur aurum]]. And [[Zach 13:9|I will hear them|exaudiam eos]], and [[Zach 13:9|I will say: Thou art my people|dicam : Populus meus tu es]].

paras.t: Tu cognovisti sessionem, id est humiliationem, contritionem, seu dejectionem, meam, et resurrectionem meam, qua a somno peccati resurgo, et justus de injusto (Deo operante) efficior. Unde Apostolus clamat : Hora est nos jam de somno surgere ; et iterum, Surge, qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis.
paras.en: [[138:2|Thou hast known my sitting down|Tu cognovisti sessionem]], that is, my humbling, contrition or casting down, [[138:2|and my rising up|et resurrectionem meam]], by which I rise from the sleep of sin and am made just from unjust (God working it). Hence the Apostle cries out: [[Rom 13:11|it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep|Hora est nos jam de somno surgere]]; and again: [[Eph 5:14|Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead|Surge, qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis]].

paras.t: Intellexisti cogitationes meas de longe, id est, in te ipso ab æterno eas vidisti : quoniam in divina essentia universa resplendent, sicut in prima causa et exemplari principio. Propter quod Dominus in Apocalypsi testatur : Scient omnes Ecclesiæ quia ego sum scrutans renes et corda. Semitam meam, id est actionem seu conversationem meam, et funiculum meum, id est vitæ meæ mensuram, modum seu limitem, investigasti, id est, diligenter pensasti, considerando quousque pervenero, quidve profecero. Unde a beato Job dicitur : Observasti omnes semitas meas, et vestigia pedum meorum considerasti.
paras.en: [[138:3|Thou hast understood my thoughts afar off|Intellexisti cogitationes meas de longe]], that is, thou hast seen them in thyself from eternity: for in the divine essence all things shine forth, as in their first cause and exemplar principle. Wherefore the Lord testifies in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 2:23|all the churches shall know that I am he that searcheth the reins and hearts|Scient omnes Ecclesiæ quia ego sum scrutans renes et corda]]. [[138:3|my path|Semitam meam]], that is, my action or way of life, [[138:3|and my line|et funiculum meum]] [*funiculus*, a small cord, used for a measuring line], that is, the measure, manner or limit of my life, [[138:3|thou hast searched out|investigasti]], that is, thou hast carefully weighed, considering how far I shall come and what progress I shall make. Hence blessed Job says: [[Job 13:27|hast observed all my paths, and hast considered the steps of my feet|Observasti omnes semitas meas, et vestigia pedum meorum considerasti]].

paras.t: Et omnes vias meas, id est cogitationes, verba et opera : quæ viæ dicuntur, quia per ea tendo ad ultimum finem ; prævidisti ab æterno antequam sint : juxta illud, Domino Deo, antequam crearentur, omnia sunt cognita ; quia non est sermo in lingua mea, quo tibi respondere sufficiam, rationem reddendo pro singulis quæ commisi aut omisi : secundum quod alibi scriptum est : Non justificatur homo compositus Deo; et si voluerit cum eo contendere, non poterit respondere unum pro mille. Hinc rursus sanctus Job ait : Deus, cujus iræ nemo resistere potest, sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem. Quantus ergo ego sum ut respondeam ei, et loquar verbis meis cum eo ?
paras.en: And [[138:4|all my ways|Et omnes vias meas]], that is, my thoughts, words and works, which are called ways because through them I tend to my last end, [[138:4|thou hast foreseen|prævidisti]] from eternity, before they are: according to that saying, [[Ecclus 23:29|all things were known to the Lord God, before they were created|Domino Deo, antequam crearentur, omnia sunt cognita]]; [[138:4|for there is no speech in my tongue|quia non est sermo in lingua mea]] with which I could answer thee, rendering an account for each thing I have done or left undone; as it is written elsewhere: [[Job 9:2|man cannot be justified, compared with God|Non justificatur homo compositus Deo]]; [[Job 9:3|If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one for a thousand|et si voluerit cum eo contendere, non poterit respondere unum pro mille]] [the margin gives Job ii, 2, 3; the passage is Job 9:2–3]. Hence holy Job says again: [[Job 9:13|God, whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world|Deus, cujus iræ nemo resistere potest, sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem]]. [[Job 9:14|What am I then, that I should answer him, and have words with him?|Quantus ergo ego sum ut respondeam ei, et loquar verbis meis cum eo]]

paras.t: Ecce, Domine, tu cognovisti omnia novissima, id est ultima, et antiqua, id est prima, videlicet omnia quæ sunt, erunt vel fuerunt. Tu formasti me in utero, corpus organizando et animam infundendo. Vel, Formasti, id est, perfecisti me, gratiam tribuendo, secundum quod protestaris : Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum. Hinc quoque dicitur : Pater noster tu es, nos vero lutum; et fictor noster tu, et opera manuum tuarum omnes nos. Et posuisti super me manum tuam, id est potentiam tuam, conservando me in esse. Vel, Posuisti super me manum tuam, castigando me quando peccavi : quemadmodum in Apocalypsi dicis, Ego, quos amo, arguo et castigo. Vel, Posuisti super me manum tuam, id est, pie et gratiose sustentasti, et confortasti me in spiritualis conversationis processu.
paras.en: [[138:5|Behold, O Lord, thou hast known all things, the last|Ecce, Domine, tu cognovisti omnia novissima]], that is, the final things, [[138:5|and those of old|et antiqua]], that is, the first: namely, all things that are, will be or have been. [[138:5|thou hast formed me|Tu formasti me]] in the womb, fashioning the body and infusing the soul. Or, [[138:5|thou hast formed|Formasti]], that is, thou hast perfected me, by bestowing grace, as thou dost declare: [[Is 43:7|every one that calleth upon my name, I have created him for my glory|Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum]]. Hence too it is said: [[Is 64:8|thou art our father, and we are clay: and thou art our maker, and we all are the works of thy hands|Pater noster tu es, nos vero lutum; et fictor noster tu, et opera manuum tuarum omnes nos]]. [[138:5|and hast laid thy hand upon me|Et posuisti super me manum tuam]], that is, thy power, preserving me in being. Or, [[138:5|hast laid thy hand upon me|Posuisti super me manum tuam]] by chastising me when I sinned, as thou sayest in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego, quos amo, arguo et castigo]]. Or, [[138:5|hast laid thy hand upon me|Posuisti super me manum tuam]], that is, thou hast lovingly and graciously upheld me and strengthened me in my progress in the spiritual life.

paras.t: Mirabilis facta est omni menti creatæ scientia tua, o Deus, ex me, id est ex consideratione mea. Scientia enim Creatoris, in creaturis relucet; et ex earum consideratione mirabilis apparet consideranti tanto amplius, quanto creaturæ fuerint digniores, seu mirabilius institutæ. Quum igitur homo sit creatura excellens, et valde mirabiliter instituta, scilicet ex corruptibili carne et immortali spiritu constans, mirabilis facta est scientia Creatoris ex consideratione hominis, ita quod consideranti miranda apparet. Confortata est, et non potero ad eam. Hoc est quod in libro Job dicitur : Ecce Deus magnus, vincens scientiam nostram.
paras.en: [[138:6|Thy knowledge is become wonderful|Mirabilis facta est]] to every created mind, O God, [[138:6|to me|ex me]] [*ex me*, literally "from me"], that is, from the consideration of me. For the knowledge of the Creator shines forth in creatures, and from the consideration of them it appears the more wonderful to one who considers them, the nobler or the more wonderfully fashioned the creatures are. Since, then, man is an excellent creature and very wonderfully fashioned, made up as he is of corruptible flesh and immortal spirit, the knowledge of the Creator has become wonderful from the consideration of man, so that it appears marvellous to whoever considers it. [[138:6|it is high, and I cannot reach to it|Confortata est, et non potero ad eam]] [*confortata est*, literally "it is made strong"]. This is what is said in the book of Job: [[Job 36:26|Behold, God is great, exceeding our knowledge|Ecce Deus magnus, vincens scientiam nostram]].

paras.t: Quo ibo a spiritu tuo? qui omnia perscrutatur, secundum Apostolum. De quo scriptum est : Spiritus Domini replevit orbem terrarum. Et quo a facie tua fugiam? tanquam dicat : Tuum conspectum fugere nequeo. Unde in libro Sapientiæ dicitur : Effugere manum tuam, Domine, impossibile est.
paras.en: [[138:7|Whither shall I go from thy spirit|Quo ibo a spiritu tuo]]? which, according to the Apostle, [[1 Cor 2:10|searcheth all things|omnia perscrutatur]]; of which it is written: [[Wis 1:7|the Spirit of the Lord hath filled the whole world|Spiritus Domini replevit orbem terrarum]]. [[138:7|or whither shall I flee from thy face|Et quo a facie tua fugiam]]? as if to say: I cannot flee thy sight. Hence it is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 16:15|it is impossible to escape thy hand|Effugere manum tuam, Domine, impossibile est]], O Lord.

paras.t: Si ascendero in cœlum, id est, si per mentis elationem me ipsum erexero, justum putavero, ceterisque prætulero, tu illic es, ut superbum humilies : sicut Abdias propheta testatur, Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, inde te detraham, dicit Dominus. Vel, Si ascendero in cœlum, per contemplationem et desiderium bonorum cœlestium, tu illic es, qui dicis : Numquid non cœlum et terram ego impleo? Si descendero in infernum, id est in profundum vitiorum, ita ut vel desperem, vel divinam providentiam negem, ades tanquam inspector et ultor. Vel, Si descendero in infernum, considerando ipsius tormenta, ades.
paras.en: [[138:8|If I ascend into heaven|Si ascendero in cœlum]], that is, if by pride of mind I lift myself up, think myself just and set myself above others, [[138:8|thou art there|tu illic es]] to humble the proud: as the prophet Abdias testifies, [[Abd 1:4|Though thou be exalted as an eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars: thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord|Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, inde te detraham, dicit Dominus]]. Or, [[138:8|If I ascend into heaven|Si ascendero in cœlum]] by contemplation and desire of heavenly goods, [[138:8|thou art there|tu illic es]], who sayest: [[Jer 23:24|do not I fill heaven and earth|Numquid non cœlum et terram ego impleo]]? [[138:8|if I descend into hell|Si descendero in infernum]], that is, into the depth of vices, so that I either despair or deny divine providence, [[138:8|thou art present|ades]] as watcher and avenger. Or, [[138:8|if I descend into hell|Si descendero in infernum]] by considering its torments, [[138:8|thou art present|ades]].

paras.t: Si sumpsero pennas meas, id est alas contemplationum, diluculo, id est in principio diei sensibilis seu spiritualis, et habitavero in extremis maris, id est in ultimis finibus pelagi, seu in quocumque termino mundi : etenim illuc manus tua deducet me, quocumque tibi placuerit, nec potero illinc evadere, sed comprehendar a te : sicut subjungitur, et tenebit me dextera tua, id est omnipotens virtus tua.
paras.en: [[138:9|If I take my wings|Si sumpsero pennas meas]], that is, the wings of contemplation, [[138:9|early in the morning|diluculo]], that is, at the beginning of the day, whether of the senses or of the spirit, [[138:9|and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea|et habitavero in extremis maris]], that is, in the farthest bounds of the deep, or at any end of the world whatever: [[138:10|Even there also shall thy hand lead me|etenim illuc manus tua deducet me]], wherever it pleases thee, nor shall I be able to escape from there, but I shall be laid hold of by thee; as is added: [[138:10|and thy right hand shall hold me|et tenebit me dextera tua]], that is, thy almighty power.

paras.t: Et dixi: Forsitan tenebræ conculcabunt me, id est, operient atque abscondent me, sicut absconditur quod conculcatur. Hoc dicitur derisorie, secundum opinionem eorum qui existimant Deum illa conspicere, quæ fiunt in die seu luce, non autem quæ fiunt in nocte seu tenebris. Contra quos Dominus per Jeremiam loquitur : Putasne Deus e vicino ego sum, et non Deus de longe? Si occultabitur vir in absconditis suis, et ego non videbo eum? Dixi etiam : Forsitan et nox illuminatio mea, id est, tempus nocturnum et tenebrosum erit exsultatio mea, quia tunc libere faciam quæ delectant, tanquam a Deo videri non potens. in deliciis meis, id est delectationibus vitiorum. Sæpe autem accipitur illuminatio pro exsultatione.
paras.en: [[138:11|And I said: Perhaps darkness shall cover me|Et dixi: Forsitan tenebræ conculcabunt me]] [*conculcabunt*, literally "shall tread underfoot"], that is, shall cover and hide me, as what is trodden underfoot is hidden. This is said in mockery, after the opinion of those who think that God sees what is done by day or in the light, but not what is done by night or in darkness. Against them the Lord speaks through Jeremias: [[Jer 23:23|Am I, think ye, a God at hand|Putasne Deus e vicino ego sum]], [[Jer 23:23|and not a God afar off|et non Deus de longe]]? [[Jer 23:24|Shall a man be hid in secret places, and I not see him|Si occultabitur vir in absconditis suis, et ego non videbo eum?]]? I said also: [[138:11|and night shall be my light|Forsitan et nox illuminatio mea]] [Denis repeats *Forsitan*, perhaps], that is, the time of night and darkness shall be my exultation, because then I shall freely do what delights me, as though I could not be seen by God, [[138:11|in my pleasures|in deliciis meis]], that is, in the delights of vice. Now *illuminatio* [light] is often taken for exultation.

paras.t: Deinde reprobatur opinio talis. Quia tenebræ non obscurabuntur a te, id est, opera tenebrosa seu tempus nocturnum te nequaquam latebunt; et nox sicut dies illuminabitur, id est, tam evidenter a divina luce videbitur opus noctis et nox, sicut opus diei et dies. Sicut tenebræ ejus, id est, sicut tenebræ noctis cognoscuntur a Deo, ita et lumen ejus, id est, sic lumen diei videbitur ab eo. Omnia namque æque clare Deo patescunt.
paras.en: Then such an opinion is refuted: [[138:12|But darkness shall not be dark to thee|Quia tenebræ non obscurabuntur a te]], that is, works of darkness or the time of night shall in no way be hidden from thee; [[138:12|and night shall be light all the day|et nox sicut dies illuminabitur]] [the Latin reads "and night shall be lit up like the day"], that is, the work of the night and the night itself shall be seen by the divine light as plainly as the work of the day and the day itself. [[138:12|the darkness thereof|Sicut tenebræ ejus]], that is, as the darkness of the night is known by God, [[138:12|and the light thereof|ita et lumen ejus]], that is, so shall the light of the day be seen by him. For all things lie open to God with equal clearness[[Heb 4:13||]].

paras.t: Quia tu possedisti renes meos, id est, appetitum sensitivum animæ meæ per gratiam possedisti, exstinguendo in me inordinatos concupiscentiæ motus. In renibus enim viget luxuria: quos Deus dicitur possidere, dum eos dignatur per gratiam gubernare. Suscepisti me de utero matris meæ, id est, ab hora nativitatis meæ usque in præsens conservasti me, et a diversis periculis protexisti me, et tanquam pius pater custodisti me.
paras.en: [[138:13|For thou hast possessed my reins|Quia tu possedisti renes meos]], that is, thou hast possessed by grace the sensitive appetite of my soul, quenching in me the disordered motions of concupiscence. For lust thrives in the reins, and God is said to possess them when he deigns to govern them by grace. [[138:13|thou hast protected me from my mother's womb|Suscepisti me de utero matris meæ]], that is, from the hour of my birth until now thou hast preserved me, protected me from various dangers, and guarded me like a loving father.

paras.t: Mirabilia opera tua, et anima mea cognoscet ea nimis, id est multum præclare, secundum quod eam illuminare dignaberis.
paras.en: [[138:14|wonderful are thy works|Mirabilia opera tua]], [[138:14|and my soul knoweth right well|et anima mea cognoscet ea nimis]] [Denis reads *cognoscet ea*, shall know them], that is, very clearly, according as thou shalt deign to enlighten it.

paras.t: Non est occultatum os meum a te quod fecisti in occulto. Hoc, secundum expositionem in præcedenti articulo positam, convenit eis qui dicere possunt Deo: Incerta et occulta sapientiæ tuæ manifestasti mihi. Quibus Deus ostendit opera sua occulta tanquam filiis et amicis ac familiaribus suis, sicut Salvator ait discipulis suis: Jam non dicam vos servos, sed amicos meos, quia omnia quæcumque audivi a Patre meo, nota feci vobis. Et apud Amos legitur: Non faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas. Quidam vero exponunt de osse corporis, quod non est occultatum a Deo, sed notum est ei: quod dicitur factum in occulto, quia latet sub carne. Alii autem de osse spirituali, videlicet de firmitate seu fortitudine animæ: quæ nota est Deo, et dicitur facta in occulto, quoniam Deus facit eam per creationem in interioribus animæ viribus. Et substantia, id est natura mea, quæ ex anima rationali et corpore constat, in inferioribus terræ, id est, in hoc inferiori mundo versatur, terrenis inquietudinibus occupatur, multisque modis distrahitur.
paras.en: [[138:15|My bone is not hidden from thee, which thou hast made in secret|Non est occultatum os meum a te quod fecisti in occulto]]. This, according to the exposition given in the preceding article, befits those who can say to God: [[Ps 50:8|the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me|Incerta et occulta sapientiæ tuæ manifestasti mihi]]. To them God shows his hidden works as to his sons, friends and intimates, as the Saviour says to his disciples: [[John 15:15|I will not now call you servants|Jam non dicam vos servos]], but my [[John 15:15|friends|amicos]], [[John 15:15|because all things, whatsoever I have heard of my Father, I have made known to you|quia omnia quæcumque audivi a Patre meo, nota feci vobis]]. And we read in Amos: [[Amos 3:7|the Lord God doth nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets|Non faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas]]. Some, however, expound it of the bone of the body, which is not hidden from God but known to him; and it is said to be made in secret because it lies hidden under the flesh. Others, of the spiritual bone, namely the firmness or strength of the soul, which is known to God and is said to be made in secret because God makes it by creation in the inner powers of the soul. [[138:15|and my substance|Et substantia]], that is, my nature, which consists of a rational soul and a body, [[138:15|in the lower parts of the earth|in inferioribus terræ]], that is, dwells in this lower world, is taken up with earthly disquiet, and is distracted in many ways.

paras.t: Unde tibi confiteri et dicere cogor: Imperfectum meum, id est non solum excessum vitiorum, verum etiam defectum operum meorum bonorum, viderunt oculi tui. Mala etenim mea, omnino et pure mala sunt. Bona autem quæ facio, non sunt pure bona, sed imperfectionibus multis admixta, sicut apud Isaiam legitur: Ut immundi omnes nos, et quasi pannus menstruatæ universæ justitiæ nostræ. Semper ergo cum omni humilitate confiteamur Domino, et cognoscamus ex corde imperfectum nostrum, scientes quoniam quidquid boni in nobis et actibus nostris invenitur, divinitus nobis præstatur, et Deo adscribendum est; quidquid vero mali in nobis et nostris operibus reperitur, ex nobis oritur, nobisque attribuendum est. Dies formabuntur, id est, dies futuri a te producentur, et nemo in eis, id est, nullus eorum qui nunc est, in eis erit, sed interim morientur qui nunc sunt. Hoc certius dici poterat tempore veteris Testamenti, quam modo. Tunc namque certum erat, mundum diutissime duraturum: quod modo incertum est; imo nescimus an per tempus naturalis periodi unius hominis mundus durabit.
paras.en: Hence I am compelled to confess to thee and say: [[138:16|my imperfect being|Imperfectum meum]], that is, not only the excess of my vices but also the defect of my good works, [[138:16|Thy eyes did see|viderunt oculi tui]]. For my evils are wholly and purely evil; but the good things I do are not purely good, but mixed with many imperfections, as we read in Isaias: [[Is 64:6|we are all become as one unclean, and all our justices as the rag of a menstruous woman|Ut immundi omnes nos, et quasi pannus menstruatæ universæ justitiæ nostræ]]. Let us therefore always confess to the Lord with all humility and acknowledge from the heart our imperfection, knowing that whatever good is found in us and in our acts is given us from God and must be ascribed to God, while whatever evil is found in us and in our works arises from us and must be attributed to us. [[138:16|days shall be formed|Dies formabuntur]], that is, days to come shall be brought forth by thee, [[138:16|and no one in them|et nemo in eis]], that is, none of those who are now shall be in them, but those who are now shall die in the meantime. This could be said with more certainty in the time of the Old Testament than now. For then it was certain that the world would last a very long time, which is now uncertain; indeed, we do not know whether the world will last for the natural span of one man's life.

paras.t: Exsurrexi per gratiam tuam a morte peccati, a consuetudine prava, a somno pigritiæ, et adhuc sum tecum, per caritatem tibi fideliter adhærendo. Hoc est verbum bonæ spei. Non enim hoc scire possumus certitudinaliter, sed conjecturaliter, nisi ex speciali instinctu.
paras.en: [[138:18|I rose up|Exsurrexi]] by thy grace from the death of sin, from evil habit, from the sleep of sloth, [[138:18|and am still with thee|et adhuc sum tecum]], cleaving faithfully to thee by charity. This is a word of good hope. For we cannot know this with certainty, but only by conjecture, unless by a special inspiration.

paras.t: Si occideris, id est, quia occides occisione æternæ mortis, o Deus, peccatores, idcirco, viri sanguinum, declinate a me, loco vel opere, ne vobis communicem, et vobiscum occidar ac peream. Qui enim tetigerit picem, inquinabitur ab ea. Apostolus quoque: Nolite, inquit, communicare infructuosis operibus eorum: nam morte digni sunt non solum qui faciunt ea, sed etiam qui consentiunt facientibus. Vitanda est ergo impiorum societas, familiaritas, atque communio ; appetenda vero familiaritas virtuosi ac docti, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico inducitur: Quum videris sensatum, evigila ad illum ; et, Cum viro sancto assiduus esto, quemcumque cognoveris observantem timorem Dei, cujus anima est secundum animam tuam.
paras.en: [[138:19|If thou wilt kill|Si occideris]], that is, since thou wilt kill with the slaying of eternal death, [[138:19|O God|o Deus]], [[138:19|the wicked|peccatores]], therefore, [[138:19|ye men of blood, depart from me|viri sanguinum, declinate a me]], in place or in deed, lest I have fellowship with you and be slain and perish with you. For [[Ecclus 13:1|He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled with it|Qui enim tetigerit picem, inquinabitur ab ea]]. The Apostle too says: [[Eph 5:11|have no|Nolite]], he says, [[Eph 5:11|fellowship with the unfruitful works|communicare infructuosis operibus]] of theirs; for they [[Rom 1:32|are worthy of death: and not only they that do them, but they also that consent to them that do them|morte digni sunt non solum qui faciunt ea, sed etiam qui consentiunt facientibus]]. The company, familiarity and fellowship of the wicked, then, must be shunned, and the familiarity of a virtuous and learned man [a variant noted in the margin reads *devoti*, devout, for *docti*, learned] sought, as is set forth in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 6:36|if thou see a man of understanding, go to him early in the morning|Quum videris sensatum, evigila ad illum]]; and: [[Ecclus 37:15|be continually with a holy man, whomsoever thou shalt know to observe the fear of God|Cum viro sancto assiduus esto, quemcumque cognoveris observantem timorem Dei]], [[Ecclus 37:16|Whose soul is according to thy own soul|cujus anima est secundum animam tuam]].

paras.t: Proba me, Deus, adhuc ea probatione, de qua in exordio psalmi præsentis locutus sum : Domine, probasti me. Itaque, Proba me sicut probantur electi, quos corrigis et emendas, non ut tu cognoscas, sed ut illi salubriter se ipsos noscant, ne eis dicatur illud Apostoli : Annon cognoscitis vosmetipsos, quia Jesus Christus in vobis est? nisi forte reprobi estis. Et scito cor meum, cognitione approbationis, de qua dicit Apostolus : Si quis diligit Deum, hic cognitus est ab eo. Interroga me, id est, per adversa inquire, et vide an vere te diligam, an tibi constanter fidelis sim. Sic velle a Deo probari et interrogari, non pertinet ad imperfectos, sed fortes, qui pro consuetudine exercitatos habent sensus, qui cum Apostolo dicere possunt illud : Ego didici, in quibus sum, sufficiens esse. Scio et humiliari, scio et abundare ; ubique et in omnibus institutus sum. Et cognosce, per acceptationem, approbationem, seu complacentiam, semitas meas, id est desideria, cogitationes, verba et actus ;
paras.en: [[138:23|Prove me, O God|Proba me, Deus]], still with that proving of which I spoke at the beginning of the present psalm: [[138:1|Lord, thou hast proved me|Domine, probasti me]]. So, [[138:23|Prove me|Proba me]] as the elect are proved, whom thou correctest and amendest, not that thou mayest know, but that they may know themselves to their salvation, lest that saying of the Apostle be said to them: [[2 Cor 13:5|Know you not your own selves, that Christ Jesus is in you, unless perhaps you be reprobates?|Annon cognoscitis vosmetipsos, quia Jesus Christus in vobis est? nisi forte reprobi estis]] [[138:23|and know my heart|Et scito cor meum]] with the knowledge of approval, of which the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 8:3|if any man love God, the same is known by him|Si quis diligit Deum, hic cognitus est ab eo]] [the margin gives I Cor. xiii, 3; the passage is 1 Cor 8:3]. [[138:23|examine me|Interroga me]] [*interroga*, literally "question"], that is, search me out through adversity, and see whether I truly love thee and whether I am constantly faithful to thee. To wish thus to be proved and questioned by God does not belong to the imperfect but to the strong, [[Heb 5:14|who by custom have their senses exercised|qui pro consuetudine exercitatos habent sensus]], who can say with the Apostle: [[Phil 4:11|I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, to be content therewith|Ego didici, in quibus sum, sufficiens esse]]. [[Phil 4:12|I know both how to be brought low, and I know how to abound|Scio et humiliari, scio et abundare]]; [[Phil 4:12|every where and in all things I am instructed|ubique et in omnibus institutus sum]]. [[138:23|and know|Et cognosce]] by accepting, approving and being well pleased with them, [[138:23|my paths|semitas meas]], that is, my desires, thoughts, words and acts;

paras.t: et vide, more pii, diligentis, expertique medici, si via iniquitatis, id est malum propositum seu latens peccatum, in me est, quatenus ab occultis meis mundes me, Domine, et a vulneribus animæ salves me: sicut Jeremias ait : Sana me, Domine, et sanabor ; salvum me fac, et salvus ero. Denique quum ignoremus qualiter interiora nostra cum Deo se habeant, an pura exsistant, indigemus semper clamare ad Deum : Vide si via iniquitatis in me est. Mihi quoque concede ut interiora mea diligenter discutiam, vere cognoscam, caute custodiam. Et deduc me in via æterna, id est in fide catholica, in lege divina, in observatione præcepti : quorum unumquodque dicitur via æterna, quia ad vitam perducit æternam seu patriam supercœlestem, nunquam electis auferendam.
paras.en: [[138:24|And see|et vide]], after the manner of a kind, careful and experienced physician, if [[138:24|the way of iniquity|via iniquitatis]], that is, an evil purpose or hidden sin, [[138:24|be in me|in me est]], so that thou mayest [[Ps 18:13|from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord|ab occultis meis mundes me, Domine]], and save me from the wounds of the soul; as Jeremias says: [[Jer 17:14|Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed: save me, and I shall be saved|Sana me, Domine, et sanabor ; salvum me fac, et salvus ero]]. Lastly, since we do not know how our inward parts stand with God, whether they are pure, we need always to cry to God: [[138:24|See if there be in me the way of iniquity|Vide si via iniquitatis in me est]]. Grant me also to examine my inward parts diligently, to know them truly, to guard them carefully. [[138:24|and lead me in the eternal way|Et deduc me in via æterna]], that is, in the Catholic faith, in the divine law, in the keeping of the commandment: each of which is called the eternal way because it leads to eternal life, or to the fatherland above the heavens, which shall never be taken from the elect.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum mirabilem, difficilem, et omni laude dignum, divinis præconiis plenum, sacris mysteriis altum audivimus : in quo de Christi mysteriis copiose tractatur ; ex cujus doctrina admonemur divinam providentiam considerare, divinam præsentiam honorare, immensam Creatoris majestatem timere. Estque psalmus iste cum ingenti attentione cantandus, quia pene in singulis versibus dirigitur sermo ad Deum, et ubique est sensus sublimis. Ostendit enim hic psalmus incomprehensibilem esse Dei scientiam, infinitam ejus exsistere essentiam, metuendam quoque esse ipsius magnificentiam.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm wonderful, difficult and worthy of all praise, full of divine praises, lofty in sacred mysteries, in which the mysteries of Christ are treated at length; by whose teaching we are admonished to consider divine providence, to honour the divine presence, to fear the immense majesty of the Creator. And this psalm is to be sung with very great attention, because in almost every verse the speech is directed to God, and everywhere the sense is sublime. For this psalm shows that the knowledge of God is incomprehensible, that his essence is infinite, and that his magnificence is to be feared.

paras.t: Precatio. Cœli terræque conditor Deus, precamur immensæ majestatis tuæ excellentem virtutem : ut nos in viam directos æternam, illo tuearis brachio, quo amici tui nimis honorificati apud te, felicissime gloriantur in cœlis.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, maker of heaven and earth, we beseech the surpassing power of thy immense majesty, that thou wouldst guard us, set straight in [[138:24|the eternal way|viam directos æternam]], with that arm by which [[138:17|thy friends|amici tui]], [[138:17|exceedingly honourable|nimis honorificati]] with thee, most happily glory in heaven.

139.title: EXPOSITIO DE CHRISTO, PSALMI CENTESIMI TRICESIMI NONI : ERIPE ME, DOMINE, AB HOMINE MALO.
139.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and thirty-ninth psalm, of Christ: Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man.

paras.t: Assignatur insuper psalmo nunc declarando titulus talis : In finem, psalmus David : id est, psalmus iste a sancto David conscriptus ac editus, dirigit nos in finem, qui Christus est : qui testatur, Ego sum Alpha et Omega, principium et finis; de quo etiam dicit Apostolus, Finis legis est Christus omni credenti.
paras.en: Further, the psalm now to be explained is given this title: [[139:1|Unto the end, a psalm of David|In finem, psalmus David]]: that is, this psalm, written and set forth by holy David, directs us to the end, who is Christ, who testifies, [[Apoc 1:8|I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end|Ego sum Alpha et Omega, principium et finis]][[Apoc 21:6||]][[Apoc 22:13||]]; of whom the Apostle also says, [[Rom 10:4|the end of the law is Christ|Finis legis est Christus]] [[Rom 10:4|to everyone that believeth|omni credenti]].

paras.t: Doctores autem catholici exponunt hunc psalmum de Ecclesia in tribulationibus constituta, ad Deum clamante. Quidam tamen exponunt eum ad litteram de David : quæ expositio insipida est. Imo quum multi psalmi exponantur ad litteram de Christo, eo quod in Scriptura canonica novæ legis allegentur de Christo, qui tamen minus conveniunt Christo quam psalmus iste : ut patet de psalmo tricesimo nono, qui incipit, Expectans exspectavi Dominum. Cujus scripturam de Christo prædictam allegat Apostolus : in quo tamen psalmo inter cetera dicitur, Comprehenderunt me iniquitates meæ, et non potui ut viderem : quod certum est Christo non convenire ratione propriæ personæ, aut naturæ suæ divinitati unitæ. Idem patet de psalmo immediate sequenti, qui incipit, Beatus qui intelligit. Cujus scripturam allegat Christus de se prædictam, videlicet illum versiculum, Etenim homo pacis meæ, in quo speravi, qui edebat panes meos. Hoc enim inducit de Juda proditore vaticinatum : et tamen in psalmo illo inter alia scribitur, Sana animam meam, quia peccavi tibi : quod Christo non convenit. Idem etiam patet de illo psalmo, cujus exordium est, Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam. Cujus scripturam allegant Joannes et Paulus de […] hoc scriptum est, Delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita. Quum ergo singula verba hujus psalmi proprie congruant Christo, sicut patebit in prosequendo, videtur quod de ipso proprie debeat explanari : quod etiam inde probatur, quia Ecclesia in die Parasceves in officio Missæ canit hunc psalmum pro Tractu. De Christi igitur passione conscriptus est psalmus præsens.
paras.en: Now the Catholic doctors expound this psalm of the Church set amid tribulations and crying out to God. Some, however, expound it literally of David, and that exposition is insipid. Indeed many psalms are expounded literally of Christ, because they are cited of Christ in the canonical Scripture of the New Law, and yet they fit Christ less well than this psalm: as is plain of the thirty-ninth psalm, which begins, [[Ps 39:2|With expectation I have waited for the Lord|Expectans exspectavi Dominum]]. Its scripture the Apostle cites as foretold of Christ[[Heb 10:5||]]; and yet in that psalm, among other things, it is said, [[Ps 39:13|my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see|Comprehenderunt me iniquitates meæ, et non potui ut viderem]]: which, it is certain, does not fit Christ by reason of his own person, or of his nature united to the Godhead. The same is plain of the psalm immediately following, which begins, [[Ps 40:2|Blessed is he that understandeth|Beatus qui intelligit]]. Its scripture Christ cites as foretold of himself, namely that little verse, [[Ps 40:10|For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread|Etenim homo pacis meæ, in quo speravi, qui edebat panes meos]]. For he brings this in as prophesied of Judas the traitor[[John 13:18||]]; and yet in that psalm, among other things, it is written, [[Ps 40:5|heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee|Sana animam meam, quia peccavi tibi]]: which does not fit Christ. The same again is plain of that psalm whose opening is, [[Ps 68:2|Save me, O God: for the waters are come in even unto my soul|Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam]]. Its scripture John and Paul cite[[John 2:17||]][[Rom 15:3||]] concerning […] this is written: [[Ps 68:6|my offences are not hidden from thee|Delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita]]. Since, then, every single word of this psalm properly fits Christ, as will be plain as we go on, it seems that it ought properly to be explained of him; and this is proved also from the fact that the Church on the day of the Parasceve [that is, Good Friday] sings this psalm as the Tract in the office of the Mass. The present psalm, therefore, was written of the Passion of Christ.

paras.t: Unde Christus, ut homo passibilis passionique proximus, ait ad Patrem : Eripe me, Domine, ab homine malo. Non ita oravit Christus ab iniquis hominibus eripi, ut non traderetur in manus eorum : imo quum Petrus ei dixisset, Non erit tibi hoc, respondit ei : Vade retro me, satana, quoniam non sapis ea quæ Dei sunt, etc. Nec sic oravit ab eis eripi, ne per eos induceretur ad malum culpæ, quia sciebat se non posse peccare ; sed oravit eripi, ne detineretur in morte, et ut tertia die resurgeret, et glorificaretur in corpore. Sic igitur ait : Eripe me, Domine, Pater æterne, ab homine malo me persequente, puta Judæo quocumque, qui me lingua crucifixit, dicendo : Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum. A viro iniquo me actualiter crucifigente, qui Judæi clamorem ad opus perduxit, videlicet a gentili quocumque Pilati ministro, eripe me.
paras.en: Hence Christ, as a man able to suffer and near to his Passion, says to the Father: [[139:2|Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man|Eripe me, Domine, ab homine malo]]. Christ did not pray to be delivered from wicked men in such a way that he would not be handed over into their hands: nay, when Peter had said to him, [[Matt 16:22|this shall not be unto thee|Non erit tibi hoc]], he answered him, [[Mark 8:33|Go behind me, Satan, because thou savourest not the things that are of God|Vade retro me, satana, quoniam non sapis ea quæ Dei sunt]], etc. [Peter's words are those of Matt 16:22; the reply is in the wording of Mark 8:33]. Nor did he pray to be delivered from them lest they should lead him into the evil of guilt [that is, into sin, as distinct from the evil of punishment], for he knew that he could not sin; but he prayed to be delivered so that he should not be held in death, and that he might rise again on the third day and be glorified in the body. So then he says: [[139:2|Deliver me, O Lord|Eripe me, Domine]], eternal Father, [[139:2|from the evil man|ab homine malo]] who persecutes me, any Jew, say, who crucified me with his tongue, saying, [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]. [[139:2|from the unjust man|A viro iniquo]] who crucifies me in deed, who carried the Jew's clamour into effect, that is, from any Gentile servant of Pilate, [[139:2|rescue me|eripe me]].

paras.t: Qui, homo malus et vir iniquus, cogitaverunt iniquitates in corde, proponentes me persequi atque occidere. Unde ab Evangelista dicitur : Ab illo die cogitaverunt interficere eum. Tota die, non solum in die Parasceves, sed multis diebus præcedentibus, constituebant prælia, id est, inter se ordinabant qualiter mihi resisterent, repugnarent et prævalerent : secundum quod apud Matthæum habetur, Congregati sunt principes sacerdotum et seniores, ut Jesum dolo tenerent et occiderent.
paras.en: [[139:3|Who|Qui]], the evil man and the unjust man, [[139:3|have devised iniquities in their hearts|cogitaverunt iniquitates in corde]], purposing to persecute and kill me. Hence the Evangelist says, [[John 11:53|From that day therefore they devised to put him to death|Ab illo die cogitaverunt interficere eum]]. [[139:3|all the day long|Tota die]], not only on the day of the Parasceve but on many days before, [[139:3|they designed battles|constituebant prælia]], that is, they arranged among themselves how they might resist me, oppose me and prevail against me: according to what is had in Matthew, [[Matt 26:3|were gathered together the chief priests and ancients|Congregati sunt principes sacerdotum et seniores]], [[Matt 26:4|that by subtilty they might apprehend Jesus and put him to death|ut Jesum dolo tenerent et occiderent]].

paras.t: Acuerunt linguas suas sicut serpentes, id est, verba acuta, pungitiva et aspera contra me protulerunt, conantes mihi nocere, sicut nocent serpentes. Acuerunt plane Judæi linguas suas, quando Pilato, tot occasiones liberandi Jesum quærenti, dixerunt : Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris ; et, Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros. Venenum aspidum, id est sermo letalis, venenosus, invidiosus et pestifer, sub labiis eorum, id est, paratus est in ore ipsorum, ut illum effundant. Hoc venenum aspidum effuderunt Judæi in Christum, dicentes : Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit. Unde Christus per Osee ait : Ego redemi eos, et ipsi contra me locuti sunt mendacium ; et apud Jeremiam : Facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva ; dedit contra me vocem suam, ideo odivi eam.
paras.en: [[139:4|They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent|Acuerunt linguas suas sicut serpentes]], that is, they uttered sharp, stinging and harsh words against me, trying to harm me as serpents harm. The Jews plainly sharpened their tongues when they said to Pilate, who was seeking so many occasions of releasing Jesus, [[John 19:12|If thou release this man, thou art not Caesar's friend|Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris]]; and, [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]]. [[139:4|the venom of asps|Venenum aspidum]], that is, deadly, venomous, envious and pestilent speech, [[139:4|is under their lips|sub labiis eorum]], that is, is ready in their mouth for them to pour it out. This venom of asps the Jews poured out against Christ, saying, [[John 19:7|We have a law; and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God|Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit]]. Hence Christ says through Osee, [[Osee 7:13|I redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me|Ego redemi eos, et ipsi contra me locuti sunt mendacium]]; and in Jeremias, [[Jer 12:8|My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: it hath cried out against me, therefore have I hated it|Facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva ; dedit contra me vocem suam, ideo odivi eam]].

paras.t: Custodi me, Domine, de manu peccatoris, id est de potestate principis sacerdotum, et ab hominibus iniquis, id est ejus fautoribus, eripe me, ne mihi eveniat quod mihi conati sunt facere, dicentes illud Jeremiæ : Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra. Idcirco namque fecerunt custodiri sepulcrum, ut corpus Christi in eo teneretur et corrumperetur, sicque memoria ejus omnino periret, nullo in ipsum credente. Nunc igitur orat Christus homo custodiri et eripi, ne hoc fiat.
paras.en: [[139:5|Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the wicked|Custodi me, Domine, de manu peccatoris]], that is, from the power of the high priest, [[139:5|and from unjust men|et ab hominibus iniquis]], that is, his abettors, [[139:5|deliver me|eripe me]], lest there befall me what they tried to do to me, saying that word of Jeremias, [[Jer 11:19|cut him off from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more|Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra]]. For this is why they had the sepulchre guarded[[Matt 27:66||]]: that the body of Christ might be held in it and corrupt, and so his memory might perish altogether, with no one believing in him. Now therefore Christ as man prays to be kept and delivered, lest this come to pass.

paras.t: Qui cogitaverunt supplantare, id est a via justitiæ retrahere, gressus meos, id est opera mea. Nitebantur enim Judæi Christum a veritate abducere, nunc terrendo, nunc blandiendo. Propter quod dixerunt : Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo. Dic ergo nobis : Licet tributum dare Cæsari, an non? Vel, Cogitaverunt supplantare, id est reprobare et malos ostendere, gressus meos, dicentes : Tu de te ipso testimonium perhibes; testimonium tuum non est verum. Et iterum : Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit. In passione quoque coram Pilato : Si non esset hic malefactor, non tibi tradidissemus eum.
paras.en: [[139:5|Who have proposed to supplant|Qui cogitaverunt supplantare]], that is, to draw back from the way of justice, [[139:5|my steps|gressus meos]], that is, my works. For the Jews strove to lead Christ away from the truth, now by terrifying him, now by flattering him. That is why they said, [[Matt 22:16|Master, we know that thou art a true speaker and teachest the way of God in truth. Neither carest thou for any man|Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo]]. [[Matt 22:17|Tell us therefore|Dic ergo nobis]]: [[Matt 22:17|Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?|Licet tributum dare Cæsari, an non?]] Or: they [[139:5|have proposed to supplant|Cogitaverunt supplantare]], that is, to condemn and show to be evil, [[139:5|my steps|gressus meos]], saying, [[John 8:13|Thou givest testimony of thyself. Thy testimony is not true|Tu de te ipso testimonium perhibes; testimonium tuum non est verum]]. And again, [[John 9:16|This man is not of God, who keepeth not the sabbath|Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit]]. In the Passion also, before Pilate, [[John 18:30|If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up to thee|Si non esset hic malefactor, non tibi tradidissemus eum]].

paras.t: Absconderunt superbi, id est principes Judæorum et Pharisæi, de generis nobilitate et falsa justitia præsumentes, laqueum, id est fraudulentas insidias, mihi, id est contra me et ad injuriam meam. Multipliciter enim studuerunt aliquam occasionem invenire, qua Christum reprehendere et accusare valerent, sicut ab Evangelista dicitur : Observabant Judæi si sabbatis curaret, ut accusarent eum. Ideo etiam obtulerunt ei mulierem in adulterio deprehensam. Unde per Jeremiam dicit Salvator : Tu, Domine, scis omne consilium eorum adversum me.
paras.en: [[139:6|The proud have hidden|Absconderunt superbi]], that is, the princes of the Jews and the Pharisees, presuming on the nobility of their race and on a false justice, [[139:6|a net|laqueum]], that is, deceitful snares, [[139:6|for me|mihi]], that is, against me and to my injury. For in many ways they strove to find some occasion by which they might reprehend and accuse Christ, as the Evangelist says: the Jews [[Mark 3:2|watched him whether he would heal on the sabbath days, that they might accuse him|Observabant Judæi si sabbatis curaret, ut accusarent eum]]. For this reason too they brought before him the woman taken in adultery. Hence the Saviour says through Jeremias, [[Jer 18:23|But thou, O Lord, knowest all their counsel against me|Tu, Domine, scis omne consilium eorum adversum me]].

paras.t: Et funes, id est multas et longas astutias fallendique machinas, extenderunt in laqueum, id est ad hoc, ut me funibus suarum insidiarum capere et reprehendere possent. Longo enim tempore sequebantur perfidi Pharisæi ac Scribæ Dominum Salvatorem, ut aliquid reprehensionis invenire possent in ejus doctrina aut vita. Hinc quippe Christus loquitur per Osee : Exosos habui eos propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum. Juxta iter, id est juxta conversationem hujus viæ, vel juxta legem seu observationem præceptorum, scandalum posuerunt mihi, id est verba et opera quibus me scandalizare quærebant, quamvis non profecerunt.
paras.en: And [[139:6|cords|funes]], that is, many and long-drawn wiles and contrivances of deceit, [[139:6|they have stretched out|extenderunt]] [[139:6|for a snare|in laqueum]], that is, to this end, that they might catch and reprehend me with the cords of their plots. For a long time the faithless Pharisees and Scribes followed the Lord and Saviour, to find something to reprehend in his teaching or his life. Hence indeed Christ speaks through Osee: [[Osee 9:15|I hated them|Exosos habui eos]] [[Osee 9:15|for the wickedness of their devices|propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum]]. [[139:6|by the wayside|Juxta iter]], that is, beside the conduct of this way [that is, of his life as a wayfarer in this world], or beside the law or the observance of the commandments, [[139:6|they have laid for me a stumblingblock|scandalum posuerunt mihi]], that is, words and deeds by which they sought to make me stumble, though they did not succeed.

paras.t: Dixi Domino : Deus meus es tu. Certum est quod Christus frequenter vocavit Deum omnium, Deum suum. Singulariter etenim erat Deus suus, secundum quod homo, quia præelectus ab eo, et quia ipse præcipue Deum amavit et coluit, sicut ipse testatur : Ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper. Hinc etiam post resurrectionem dicebat : Ascendo ad Deum meum et Deum vestrum. Exaudi, Domine, vocem deprecationis meæ, quam nunc coram te fudi.
paras.en: [[139:7|I said to the Lord: Thou art my God|Dixi Domino : Deus meus es tu]]. It is certain that Christ often called the God of all things his God. For he was his God in a singular way, inasmuch as he was man, because he was chosen beforehand by him, and because he himself loved and worshipped God above all, as he himself testifies, [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]]. Hence too after the resurrection he said, [[John 20:17|I ascend|Ascendo]] [[John 20:17|to my God and to your God|ad Deum meum et Deum vestrum]]. [[139:7|hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication|Exaudi, Domine, vocem deprecationis meæ]], which I have now poured out before thee.

paras.t: Domine, Domine, virtus, id est causa et conservator, salutis meæ creatæ. Beatitudo enim creata animæ Christi, a Deo manavit et dependebat. Obumbrasti super caput meum, id est super cor meum; vel, Super me, tuam defensionem, cooperationem seu opem extendisti; in die belli, id est tempore passionis, quando dæmones expugnavi et exspoliavi. Contulit enim Deus Christo in passione inconcussam constantiam : propter quod factus est potens in prælio. Unde per Jeremiam prædixit : Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis; idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent.
paras.en: [[139:8|O Lord, Lord, the strength|Domine, Domine, virtus]], that is, the cause and preserver, [[139:8|of my salvation|salutis meæ]], my created salvation [that is, the salvation and well-being of Christ's human soul, which is a created thing, as distinct from his uncreated Godhead]. For the created beatitude of Christ's soul flowed from God and depended on him. [[139:8|thou hast overshadowed my head|Obumbrasti super caput meum]], that is, over my heart; or, over me thou hast stretched out thy defence, thy co-operation or help; [[139:8|in the day of battle|in die belli]], that is, in the time of the Passion, when I overcame and despoiled the demons[[Col 2:15||]]. For God gave Christ in his Passion an unshaken constancy, and therefore he was made [[Ps 23:8|mighty in battle|potens in prælio]] [the margin gives Ps. xviii, 8; the words are those of Ps 23:8]. Hence he foretold through Jeremias, [[Jer 20:11|the Lord is with me as a strong warrior: therefore they that persecute me shall fall|Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis; idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent]].

paras.t: Non tradas me, Domine, a desiderio meo, id est contra seu extra desiderium meum, peccatori, videlicet populo Judæorum. Aliquo enim modo desideravit Christus eis tradi, videlicet ut pro mundo moreretur; et aliquo modo desideravit eis non tradi, videlicet ne in morte detineretur. Et ideo nunc orat, ne extra tale desiderium eis tradatur. Cogitaverunt contra me, sicut apud Jeremiam dicitur : Super me cogitaverunt consilia, dicentes, Mittamus lignum in panem ejus. Ne derelinquas me, quantum ad animam, in limbo; et quantum ad corpus, in tumulo; sed statim me suscita, ne forte exaltentur, id est, prævaluisse videantur, atque inaniter glorientur.
paras.en: [[139:9|Give me not up, O Lord, from my desire|Non tradas me, Domine, a desiderio meo]], that is, against or beyond my desire [Denis takes a, 'from', in the sense of 'apart from'], [[139:9|to the wicked|peccatori]], namely to the people of the Jews. For in one way Christ desired to be handed over to them, namely that he might die for the world; and in another way he desired not to be handed over to them, namely that he might not be held in death. And so he now prays not to be handed over to them beyond such a desire. [[139:9|they have plotted against me|Cogitaverunt contra me]], as is said in Jeremias, [[Jer 11:19|they had devised counsels against me, saying: Let us put wood on his bread|Super me cogitaverunt consilia, dicentes, Mittamus lignum in panem ejus]]. [[139:9|do not thou forsake me|Ne derelinquas me]], as to the soul, in limbo, and as to the body, in the tomb, but raise me up at once, [[139:9|lest they should triumph|ne forte exaltentur]], that is, seem to have prevailed, and glory in vain.

paras.t: Deinde describitur Judæorum dejectio. Caput, id est princeps sacerdotum, qui erat caput seu princeps circuitus eorum, id est exercitus Judæorum, me tempore passionis circumdantium. Quid autem huic capiti et subditis suis futurum fuerit, subditur : labor labiorum ipsorum, id est laboriosus et gravis sermo, quem contra me loquebantur, dicentes : Blasphemavit; et, Reus est mortis; et, Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem; operiet eos, id est, faciet eos debita pœna operiri atque torqueri. Hoc in Judæis impletum videmus. Voluerunt enim Christum regno et fama omnino privari, et ecce ipsi privati sunt regno et fama honesta; Christo autem data est omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra. Ipsi quoque nitebantur conculcare atque conterere Christum; et Christus eos conculcavit et contrivit, sicut asserit : Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea. Itaque in præsenti vita operuit Judæos labor labiorum ipsorum, quando per Titum et exercitum Romanorum tam horribiliter vastabantur. Idcirco scriptum est : Circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ.
paras.en: Next the overthrow of the Jews is described. [[139:10|The head|Caput]], that is, the high priest, who was the head or prince [[139:10|of them compassing me about|circuitus eorum]], that is, of the host of the Jews surrounding me in the time of the Passion. And what was to befall this head and his subjects is added: [[139:10|the labour of their lips|labor labiorum ipsorum]], that is, the toilsome and grievous speech which they spoke against me, saying, [[Matt 26:65|He hath blasphemed|Blasphemavit]]; and, [[Matt 26:66|He is guilty of death|Reus est mortis]]; and, [[John 19:15|We have no king but Caesar|Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem]]; [[139:10|shall overwhelm them|operiet eos]], that is, shall cause them to be covered over and tormented with due punishment [operiet, literally 'shall cover']. This we see fulfilled in the Jews. For they wished Christ to be wholly deprived of kingdom and of fame, and behold, they themselves have been deprived of kingdom and of good fame; but to Christ [[Matt 28:18|All power is given|data est omnis potestas]] [[Matt 28:18|in heaven and in earth|in cœlo et in terra]]. They too strove to trample and crush Christ; and Christ has trampled and crushed them, as he declares, [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]]. Thus in the present life [[139:10|the labour of their lips|labor labiorum ipsorum]] overwhelmed the Jews, when they were so horribly laid waste by Titus and the army of the Romans. Therefore it is written, [[Osee 7:2|their own devices now have beset them about|Circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ]].

paras.t: Cadent super eos carbones, id est materia flammæ infernalis; in ignem gehennæ dejicies eos, quantum ad animam statim dum moriuntur; quantum vero ad corpus et animam, in die judicii, quando dicturus es, Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum; in miseriis, id est in pœnis inferni, non subsistent : non quod illic esse cessabunt, sed quia de uno tormento transibunt ad aliud, vel quia intolerabiles pœnas tolerare cogentur.
paras.en: [[139:11|Burning coals shall fall upon them|Cadent super eos carbones]], that is, the fuel of the flame of hell; [[139:11|into the fire|in ignem]] of gehenna [[139:11|thou wilt cast them down|dejicies eos]], as to the soul at once when they die, and as to body and soul on the day of judgement, when thou wilt say, Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]] [Denis has Ite, 'Go', for the Gospel's 'Depart from me']; [[139:11|in miseries|in miseriis]], that is, in the pains of hell, [[139:11|they shall not be able to stand|non subsistent]]: not that they will cease to be there, but because they will pass from one torment to another, or because they will be forced to bear unbearable pains.

paras.t: Vir linguosus, id est Judas proditor, non dirigetur in terra : nam abiens laqueo se suspendit. Vel : Vir linguosus, id est Judæus Christo detrahens, eumque blasphemans, et multis vanis rationibus demonstrare laborans Jesum Nazarenum non esse Christum in lege promissum, non dirigetur a Deo in terra, id est in vita præsenti, ut salubriter vivat; sed excæcatus manebit et peribit. Virum injustum Christo repugnantem, mala pœnæ et culpæ capient, id est comprehendent, in interitu, id est, dum morietur. Tunc enim opera ejus eum sequentur, et de morte temporali ibit ad mortem æternam.
paras.en: [[139:12|A man full of tongue|Vir linguosus]], that is, Judas the traitor, [[139:12|shall not be established in the earth|non dirigetur in terra]] [dirigetur, literally 'shall be set straight' or 'guided'], for he [[Matt 27:5|went and hanged himself with an halter|abiens laqueo se suspendit]]. Or: [[139:12|A man full of tongue|Vir linguosus]], that is, the Jew who disparages Christ and blasphemes him, and labours with many vain arguments to show that Jesus of Nazareth is not the Christ promised in the law, [[139:12|shall not be established|non dirigetur]] by God [[139:12|in the earth|in terra]], that is, in the present life, so as to live a saving life; but he will remain blinded and will perish. [[139:12|evil|mala]] of punishment and of guilt [[139:12|shall catch|capient]], that is, shall seize, [[139:12|the unjust man|Virum injustum]] who resists Christ, [[139:12|unto destruction|in interitu]], that is, when he dies. For then his works shall follow him[[Apoc 14:13||]], and from temporal death he will go to eternal death.

paras.t: Cognovi quia faciet Dominus justus judex : qui alias affirmat, Ego sum judex et testis; judicium inopis, id est justum judicium pro Christo paupere contra adversarios ejus, ipsos juste damnando. Recte quidem nomine inopis Christum designat, qui de se ipso loquitur : Filius hominis non habet ubi caput reclinet. De quo etiam a Zacharia inducitur : Ipse pauper et ascendens super asinam. Et vindictam pauperum, id est Apostolorum ac primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quibus Judæi multas intulerunt injurias, ut patet in Actibus Apostolorum. Sed Deus fecit vindictam eorum, id est, debitam ultionem inflixit Judæis propter peccata commissa in Christi discipulos, qui valde pauperes erant, postquam exposita erant bona illa, quæ vendiderunt primo ad fidem conversi. Illis namque bonis durantibus, non erat quisquam egens inter eos, ut scribitur in Actibus. Hoc autem judicium inopis Christi, et vindicta pauperum ejus, erat illa devastatio Judæorum a Romanis, quando dirissime occisi sunt, in ultionem sanguinis Christi et discipulorum ipsius, quam Christus prædixisse cognoscitur.
paras.en: [[139:13|I know that the Lord will do|Cognovi quia faciet Dominus]], [[2 Tim 4:8|the just judge|justus judex]], who elsewhere affirms, [[Jer 29:23|I am the judge and the witness|Ego sum judex et testis]], [[139:13|justice to the needy|judicium inopis]] [literally 'the judgement of the needy'], that is, just judgement on behalf of Christ the poor man against his adversaries, by justly condemning them. Rightly indeed does he signify Christ by the name of the needy, for Christ says of himself, [[Luke 9:58|the Son of man hath not where to lay his head|Filius hominis non habet ubi caput reclinet]]. Of him too Zacharias says, [[Zach 9:9|he is poor, and riding upon an ass|Ipse pauper et ascendens super asinam]]. [[139:13|and will revenge the poor|Et vindictam pauperum]], that is, the Apostles and the primitive Church, on whom the Jews inflicted many injuries, as is plain in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 4:1||]]. But God took vengeance for them, that is, he inflicted due retribution on the Jews for the sins committed against Christ's disciples, who were very poor once those goods had been spent which they sold when first converted to the faith. For while those goods lasted, [[Acts 4:34|neither was there any one needy among them|non erat quisquam egens inter eos]], as is written in the Acts. Now this judgement of Christ the needy, and the vengeance of his poor, was that devastation of the Jews by the Romans, when they were most cruelly slain in vengeance for the blood of Christ and of his disciples, which Christ is known to have foretold[[Luke 21:24||]].

paras.t: Verumtamen justi, videlicet in Christum credentes, confitebuntur nomini tuo, te laudando. Christiani namque in Judæa exsistentes, instante adventu Romanorum, admoniti sunt ab angelo sancto egredi Judæam, et introire regnum Agrippæ, qui erat confœderatus Romanis : quod et fecerunt ; et illic salvati sunt, propter quod Deum laudabant. Et habitabunt recti, id est justi Christum sequentes fide et opere, cum vultu tuo, id est tecum in tua præsentia, nunc equidem per gratiam, postmodum vero per gloriam.
paras.en: [[139:14|But as for the just|Verumtamen justi]], namely those who believe in Christ, [[139:14|they shall give glory to thy name|confitebuntur nomini tuo]], by praising thee. For the Christians who were in Judea, when the coming of the Romans was at hand, were warned by a holy angel to go out of Judea and enter the kingdom of Agrippa, who was allied with the Romans; and this they did, and there they were saved, for which they praised God. [[139:14|and the upright shall dwell|Et habitabunt recti]], that is, the just who follow Christ in faith and in works, [[139:14|with thy countenance|cum vultu tuo]], that is, with thee in thy presence: now indeed by grace, but hereafter by glory.

paras.t: Ecce psalmus iste quam vere et proprie competit Christo, quam evidenter Judæorum malitiam exprimit, quam veraciter eorumdem punitionem describit.
paras.en: See how truly and properly this psalm befits Christ, how plainly it expresses the malice of the Jews, how truthfully it describes their punishment.

139.title: EXPOSITIO EJUSDEM PSALMI CENTESIMI TRIGESIMI NONI, DE ECCLESIA, SEU QUOLIBET FIDELI.
139.title_en: Exposition of the same hundred and thirty-ninth psalm, of the Church or any one of the faithful.

paras.t: Ecclesia itaque, seu anima religiosa, adversitatibus tentationibusque pulsata, proclamet ad Dominum, dicens : Eripe me, Domine, ab homine malo, ne cum perverso pervertar, ne ultra quam ferre possum, molester, ne per impatientiam vincar. Martyres sancti hominesque perfecti, qui in adversis exsultant, in tribulationibus gaudent, non sic petunt ab homine malo eripi, ne persecutionem ejus sustineant, sed ne in adversis deficiant, vel ne plus quam expedit eorum saluti seu bono communi, graventur. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Orate, ut liberemur a malis et importunis hominibus.
paras.en: Let the Church, then, or the religious soul, buffeted by adversities and temptations, cry out to the Lord, saying: [[139:2|Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man|Eripe me, Domine, ab homine malo]], lest with the perverse I be perverted[[Ps 17:27||]], lest I be troubled beyond what I can bear, lest I be overcome through impatience. The holy martyrs and perfect men, who exult in adversities and rejoice in tribulations, do not ask to be delivered from the evil man in such a way as not to bear his persecution, but that they may not fail in adversities, or be weighed down more than is expedient for their salvation or for the common good. For which reason the Apostle says: [[2 Thess 3:1|pray|Orate]], [[2 Thess 3:2|that we may be delivered from importunate and evil men|ut liberemur a malis et importunis hominibus]].

paras.t: A viro iniquo eripe me. Quod prædixit, resumit. Vel per hominem malum intelligit eum cujus malitia non est adeo magna ; per virum vero iniquum, eum qui omnino induratus atque subversus est. Qui autem se impatientem et ad mala proclivem cognoscit, orare potest ne persecutionem malorum patiatur, ne per impatientiam gravius prolabatur. Ego, dum versum hunc dico, per hominem malum et virum iniquum, me ipsum intelligo. Neminem enim tam secure, certe atque salubriter malum et iniquum voco ac judico, sicut me ipsum, præsertim quum dicat Apostolus : Quis scit quid agatur in homine, nisi spiritus ejus? Peto igitur eripi a me ipso, ut desinam esse malus et impius, sicque abnegem et relinquam me ipsum, non quantum ad id quod sum per naturam et gratiam, sed quoad id quod sum per propriam voluntatem et culpam.
paras.en: [[139:2|rescue me from the unjust man|A viro iniquo eripe me]]. He takes up again what he said before. Or by the evil man he means one whose malice is not so very great, but by the unjust man one who is wholly hardened and overthrown. But one who knows himself to be impatient and prone to evil may pray not to suffer the persecution of the wicked, lest through impatience he fall more gravely. When I say this verse, I understand myself by the evil man and the unjust man. For there is no one whom I call and judge evil and unjust so safely, so surely and so wholesomely as myself, especially since the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 2:11|what man knoweth the things of a man, but the spirit of a man that is in him?|Quis scit quid agatur in homine, nisi spiritus ejus?]] [Denis quotes loosely: "Who knows what goes on in a man, but his spirit?"] I ask, then, to be delivered from myself, that I may cease to be evil and impious, and so deny and forsake myself[[Luke 9:23||]]: not as to what I am by nature and grace, but as to what I am by my own will and fault.

paras.t: Qui cogitaverunt iniquitates in corde, qualiter mihi possint nocere, et ex cogitationibus talibus tota die, id est indesinenter et quasi continue, constituebant prælia, id est contentiones et rixas, seu impugnationem a manu. Acuerunt linguas suas sicut serpentes, proferendo verba adulatoria et fraudulenta more serpentium, qui blandiuntur lingua ut mordeant. Sic injusti interdum amicitiam ostendunt in verbis, sed venenum abscondunt interius. De quibus apud Jeremiam inducitur : Sagitta vulnerans est lingua eorum. In ore pacem cum amico loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias. Vel, Acuerunt linguas suas sicut serpentes, loquendo verba subtilia, acuta, mordacia et nociva, sicut de quibusdam dicit Apostolus : Sermo eorum ut cancer serpit. Venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum. Hoc et cetera quæ nunc transiliuntur, in præcedenti articulo satis exposita sunt.
paras.en: [[139:3|Who have devised iniquities in their hearts|Qui cogitaverunt iniquitates in corde]], how they might harm me, and out of such thoughts [[139:3|all the day long|tota die]], that is, unceasingly and as it were continually, [[139:3|they designed battles|constituebant prælia]], that is, contentions and quarrels, or assault by force of hand. [[139:4|They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent|Acuerunt linguas suas sicut serpentes]], by uttering flattering and deceitful words after the manner of serpents, which fawn with the tongue in order to bite. So the unjust sometimes show friendship in their words, but hide poison within. Of whom it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:8|Their tongue is a piercing arrow|Sagitta vulnerans est lingua eorum]]. [[Jer 9:8|with his mouth one speaketh peace with his friend, and secretly he lieth in wait for him|In ore pacem cum amico loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias]]. Or, [[139:4|They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent|Acuerunt linguas suas sicut serpentes]], by speaking subtle words, sharp, biting and harmful, as the Apostle says of certain men: [[2 Tim 2:17|their speech spreadeth like a canker|Sermo eorum ut cancer serpit]]. [[139:4|the venom of asps is under their lips|Venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum]]. This, and the rest that is now passed over, has been sufficiently expounded in the preceding article.

paras.t: Custodi me, Domine, de manu, id est de potestate, peccatoris, id est diaboli, qui (sicut apud Joannem habetur) a principio peccat. Ab ejus tentationibus me tuere, quoniam naturali virtute nullo modo valeo ei resistere, quum sit invisibilis hostis me incomparabiliter astutior, experientior, agilior, atque robustior. Non est enim potestas super terram quæ comparetur ei. Ideo, Domine, custodi me per te ipsum et angelum sanctum meæ custodiæ deputatum. Etenim nisi tu, Domine, custodieris civitatem, id est animam virtutum concordia circumvallatam, munitam et plenam, frustra vigilat qui custodit eam. Et ab hominibus iniquis, qui sunt instrumentum et corpus atque ministri diaboli, eripe me, ne illis conformer, et dæmonis ditioni subjiciar.
