paras.en: [[139:5|Keep me, O Lord, from the hand|Custodi me, Domine, de manu]], that is, from the power, [[139:5|of the wicked|peccatoris]] [Latin *peccatoris*, "of the sinner"], that is, of the devil, who (as we have it in John) [[1 John 3:8|sinneth from the beginning|a principio peccat]]. Protect me from his temptations, since by natural strength I can in no way resist him, for he is an invisible enemy incomparably more cunning than I, more experienced, more agile and stronger: [[Job 41:24|There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him|Non est enim potestas super terram quæ comparetur ei]]. Therefore, O Lord, keep me by thyself and by the holy angel appointed to guard me. For unless thou, O Lord, [[Ps 126:1|keep the city|custodieris civitatem]], that is, the soul walled about, fortified and filled with the harmony of the virtues, [[Ps 126:1|he watcheth in vain that keepeth it|frustra vigilat qui custodit eam]] [the margin gives Ps. xxvi, 1, a misreading of Ps. cxxvi, 1]. [[139:5|and from unjust men|Et ab hominibus iniquis]], who are the instrument and body and ministers of the devil, [[139:5|deliver me|eripe me]], lest I be conformed to them and subjected to the dominion of the demon.

paras.t: Qui cogitaverunt supplantare, id est impedire, conterere, annihilare, gressus meos, id est opera bona, quibus ad te proficiscitur anima mea ; absconderunt superbi laqueum mihi : id est, dæmones, Dei similitudinem inordinate appetentes, et homines excæcati qui eorum pompam sequuntur, non solum aperte, sed et occulte ac insidiose mihi nocere disposuerunt, proponendo mala sub specie boni, loquendo sophistice, agendo pestiliter. Et funes, id est mala exempla seu vitia, quibus anima dire ligatur ne Deum prompte ac libere imitetur, extenderunt, id est prolongaverunt, trahendo peccata velut longam restem, in laqueum, id est in deceptionem, videlicet ad hoc ut funibus istis anima mea capiatur, et vitiis substernatur. Juxta iter quo ambulo, id est juxta viam Dei, seu observantiam præceptorum, scandalum activum, id est occasionem ruinæ seu offendiculum, posuerunt mihi. Maligni equidem spiritus iter nostrum velut quidam latrunculi obsident, teste Gregorio.
paras.en: [[139:5|Who have proposed to supplant|Qui cogitaverunt supplantare]], that is, to hinder, crush and bring to nothing, [[139:5|my steps|gressus meos]], that is, the good works by which my soul journeys to thee; [[139:6|The proud have hidden a net for me|absconderunt superbi laqueum mihi]]: that is, the demons, who inordinately desire likeness to God, and blinded men who follow their pomp, have set themselves to harm me not only openly but also secretly and treacherously, by proposing evil under the appearance of good, by speaking sophistically[[Ecclus 37:23||]], by acting balefully. And the [[139:6|cords|funes]], that is, evil examples or vices, by which the soul is cruelly bound so that it may not imitate God readily and freely, [[139:6|they have stretched out|extenderunt]], that is, drawn out at length, dragging sins along like a long rope, [[139:6|for a snare|in laqueum]], that is, for deception: namely, so that by these cords my soul may be caught and laid low under the vices. [[139:6|by the wayside|Juxta iter]] by which I walk, that is, beside the way of God, or the keeping of the commandments, [[139:6|they have laid for me|posuerunt mihi]] [[139:6|a stumblingblock|scandalum]] [Denis says *scandalum activum*, "active scandal": a word or deed that gives another occasion of falling, as distinct from passive scandal, the fall of the one who takes it], that is, an occasion of ruin or a stumbling-block. For the evil spirits beset our way like highwaymen, as Gregory witnesses.

paras.t: Quoniam ergo viribus meis evadere aut prævalere non potui, ad misericordiam opemque Creatoris confugi. Dixi Domino : Deus meus es tu, non alius aliquis : nam tu solus potes me liberare atque salvare. Propterea in te solo confido, ad te confidenter recurro. Domine, Domine, virtus salutis meæ, id est fons, origo et conservator totius perfectionis, felicitatis et gratiæ meæ, sine cujus manutenentia nec ad momentum subsistere, aut salvus exsistere queo ; obumbrasti super caput meum, id est, protexisti, confirmasti et consolatus es me, in die belli, id est tempore adversitatis et tentationis : aliter succubuissem.
paras.en: Since, then, I could not escape or prevail by my own strength, I fled to the mercy and help of the Creator. [[139:7|I said to the Lord: Thou art my God|Dixi Domino : Deus meus es tu]], and no other: for thou alone canst deliver and save me. Therefore I trust in thee alone, and to thee I run back with confidence. [[139:8|O Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation|Domine, Domine, virtus salutis meæ]], that is, the fount, origin and preserver of all my perfection, happiness and grace, without whose upholding [Latin *manutenentia*, literally "holding by the hand"] I cannot stand even for a moment, nor be saved; [[139:8|thou hast overshadowed my head|obumbrasti super caput meum]], that is, thou hast protected, strengthened and consoled me, [[139:8|in the day of battle|in die belli]], that is, in the time of adversity and temptation: otherwise I should have succumbed.

paras.t: Non tradas me, Domine, a desiderio meo, id est contra desiderium meum rationale et ordinatum, quo cupio tibi semper subesse et adhærere, peccatori, dæmoni seu impio homini, ne ei assimiler, cui desidero dispar esse.
paras.en: [[139:9|Give me not up, O Lord|Non tradas me, Domine]], [[139:9|from my desire|a desiderio meo]], that is, against my rational and ordered desire, by which I long ever to be subject to thee and to cleave to thee, [[139:9|to the wicked|peccatori]], to the demon or the impious man, lest I become like him to whom I desire to be unlike.

paras.t: Vel sic : Non tradas me, Domine, id est, non me tradi permittas, a desiderio meo, id est ab hoste intrinseco, a concupiscentia carnis, ab inordinato affectu seu fomite, peccatori, videlicet ne a me ipso seducar et vincar, et potestati dæmonis subdar : quemadmodum de quibusdam ait Apostolus, Tradidit illos Deus in desideria cordis eorum, in immunditiam et reprobum sensum.
paras.en: Or thus: [[139:9|Give me not up, O Lord|Non tradas me, Domine]], that is, do not permit me to be given up, [[139:9|from my desire|a desiderio meo]], that is, by the enemy within, by the concupiscence of the flesh, by inordinate affection or the *fomes* [that is, the tinder of sin: the inclination to evil left in us by original sin], [[139:9|to the wicked|peccatori]]: namely, lest I be led astray and overcome by myself, and made subject to the power of the demon; as the Apostle says of certain men: [[Rom 1:24|God gave them up to the desires of their heart, unto uncleanness|Tradidit illos Deus in desideria cordis eorum, in immunditiam]], and [[Rom 1:28|to a reprobate sense|reprobum sensum]]. [In this second reading *a desiderio meo* is taken as "by my desire": it is desire itself that hands one over to the sinner.]

paras.t: Cogitaverunt contra me dæmon et mundus, ut a tuo me obsequio retrahant ; ne derelinquas me vinci ab eis, ne forte exaltentur, id est, triumphent et gaudeant. Nempe qui tribulant me, exsultabunt si motus fuero. Derisores enim patimur, a quibus ad illicita instigamur. Unde in Ecclesiastico dicitur : Domine, pater et dominator vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in cogitatu et consilio eorum, et incidam in conspectu adversariorum meorum, et gaudeat inimicus meus.
paras.en: [[139:9|they have plotted against me|Cogitaverunt contra me]], the demon and the world, to draw me back from thy service; [[139:9|do not thou forsake me|ne derelinquas me]] to be overcome by them, [[139:9|lest they should triumph|ne forte exaltentur]], that is, triumph and rejoice. For indeed [[Ps 12:5|They that trouble me, will rejoice when I am moved|qui tribulant me, exsultabunt si motus fuero]]. For we suffer mockers when we are urged by them to unlawful things. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 23:1|O Lord, father, and sovereign ruler of my life|Domine, pater et dominator vitæ meæ]], leave me not in their thought and counsel [the words *in cogitatu*, "in their thought", come from Ecclus 23:4], [[Ecclus 23:3|and I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice|et incidam in conspectu adversariorum meorum, et gaudeat inimicus meus]].

paras.t: Caput, videlicet dæmon, qui est princeps hujus mundi, id est reproborum, circuitus, id est exercitus seu turba, eorum, videlicet iniquorum. Istud non regitur, sed præmittitur propter relationem sequentem. Huic itaque capiti et circuitui continget quod subditur : Labor labiorum ipsorum, id est sermo eorum iniquus, quo laboraverunt subvertere innocentes, operiet eos, id est, in eos redundabit, eis nocebit, et tormentis æternis eos involvet, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico scribitur : Facienti nequissimum consilium, super ipsum devolvetur, et non cognoscet unde illi adveniat illusio. Uniuscujusque etenim malum in proprium redundat auctorem ; et qui alteri quærit nocere, primo propria iniquitate occidit aut lædit se ipsum, secundum quod Salomon profitetur : In impietate sua corruet impius, et in insidiis suis capientur iniqui.
paras.en: [[139:10|The head|Caput]], namely the devil, who is [[John 12:31|the prince of this world|princeps hujus mundi]], that is, of the reprobate; [[139:10|compassing me about|circuitus]] [Latin *circuitus*, "circle"], that is, the army or throng, [[139:10|of them|eorum]], namely of the wicked. This word is not governed by anything, but is put first for the sake of the reference that follows [that is, *caput* stands at the head of the sentence, and *eos*, "them", later takes it up]. So to this head and this circle shall befall what is added: [[139:10|the labour of their lips|Labor labiorum ipsorum]], that is, their wicked speech, by which they laboured to overthrow the innocent, [[139:10|shall overwhelm them|operiet eos]], that is, shall rebound upon them, shall harm them, and shall wrap them in eternal torments; as it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 27:30|A mischievous counsel shall be rolled back upon the author, and he shall not know from whence it cometh to him|Facienti nequissimum consilium, super ipsum devolvetur, et non cognoscet unde illi adveniat illusio]] [the margin reads Eccli. xxxii, 30, 31: the passage is Ecclus 27:30, and Denis's last word, *illusio*, "mockery", opens 27:31]. For each man's evil rebounds upon its own author; and he who seeks to harm another first slays or wounds himself by his own iniquity, as Solomon declares: [[Prov 11:5|the wicked man shall fall by his own wickedness|In impietate sua corruet impius]], [[Prov 11:6|and the unjust shall be caught in their own snares|et in insidiis suis capientur iniqui]].

paras.t: Vir linguosus, id est verbosus et garrulus, procax ad fabulandum, non dirigetur ad debitum finem a gratia Dei, in terra habitationis vitæ præsentis. Non enim tendit ad ultimum finem, qui est Deus et vita æterna, sed inferno quotidie appropinquat. Unde in Proverbiis habetur : Vidisti aliquem velocem ad loquendum ? Stultitia magis speranda est, quam illius correctio ; et, Qui multis utitur verbis, lædit animam suam. Faciamus ergo quod Jacobus consulit : Sit omnis homo velox ad audiendum, tardus autem ad loquendum. Alibi enim scriptum est : Totum spiritum suum profert stultus; sapiens autem differt in posterum. Maxime vero oportet nos solitarios, esse in verbis cautos et circumspectos, si volumus Deo in stabili puritate et pace servire.
paras.en: [[139:12|A man full of tongue|Vir linguosus]], that is, wordy and garrulous, forward in chattering, [[139:12|shall not be established|non dirigetur]] [Latin *dirigetur*, "shall be directed"] by the grace of God to his due end [[139:12|in the earth|in terra]] of our dwelling in this present life. For he does not tend to the last end, which is God and eternal life, but daily draws nearer to hell. Hence we have in Proverbs: [[Prov 29:20|Hast thou seen a man hasty to speak? folly is rather to be looked for, than his amendment|Vidisti aliquem velocem ad loquendum ? Stultitia magis speranda est, quam illius correctio]] [the margin reads "Ibid. xxx, 20": the verse is Prov 29:20]; and: [[Ecclus 20:8|He that useth many words shall hurt his own soul|Qui multis utitur verbis, lædit animam suam]] [this is Ecclesiasticus, as the margin says, not Proverbs]. Let us therefore do as James counsels: [[Jas 1:19|let every man be swift to hear, but slow to speak|Sit omnis homo velox ad audiendum, tardus autem ad loquendum]]. For it is written elsewhere: [[Prov 29:11|A fool uttereth all his mind: a wise man deferreth, and keepeth it till afterwards|Totum spiritum suum profert stultus; sapiens autem differt in posterum]]. But above all it behoves us solitaries to be cautious and circumspect in our words, if we wish to serve God in stable purity and peace.

paras.t: Cognovi ex sacra Scriptura, ex revelatione divina, imo ex ratione naturali, quia faciet Dominus judicium inopis. Qui vere et sponte inops ac humilis est, hujus judicium Dominus faciet, justo judicio eum salvando, ejusque persecutores damnando. Ideo additur : et vindictam pauperum : sicut et alibi ait, Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam. Quamvis enim omnium injuriam Dominus ulciscatur, atque pro omnibus electis judicium faciat, maxime tamen ulciscitur injuriam pauperum spiritu, atque pro inopibus judicat. Ei enim derelictus est pauper. Propter quod per Isaiam : Egenum, inquit, et pauperem non derelinquam.
paras.en: [[139:13|I know|Cognovi]] from holy Scripture, from divine revelation, nay, from natural reason, [[139:13|that the Lord will do justice to the needy|quia faciet Dominus judicium inopis]]. He who is truly and willingly needy and lowly, the Lord will do his justice [Latin *judicium*, "judgment": the Lord will judge his cause], by saving him with a just judgment and condemning his persecutors. Therefore it is added: [[139:13|and will revenge the poor|et vindictam pauperum]]; as he also says elsewhere: [[Heb 10:30|Vengeance belongeth to me, and I will repay|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam]]. For though the Lord avenges the wrong done to all, and does justice for all the elect, yet he avenges above all the wrong done to the poor in spirit, and judges for the needy. For to him [[Ps 9:35|is the poor man left|derelictus est pauper]] [the margin gives Ps. x, 14 "according to the Hebrew", which is Ps 9:35 in the Vulgate]. For which reason he says through Isaias: [[Is 41:17|The needy|Egenum]], he says, [[Is 41:17|and the poor|et pauperem]] I [[Is 41:17|will not forsake|non derelinquam]].

paras.t: Verumtamen justi confitebuntur in prosperis et adversis nomini tuo, duplici confessione, videlicet confessione laudis divinæ, ac propriæ culpæ. Bona enim tibi, mala vero sibi ipsis adscribent ; et quidquid eis acciderit, te in omnibus justificabunt, dicentes : Sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est. Sit nomen Domini benedictum. Et habitabunt recti cum vultu tuo, id est, tibi unientur, teque fruentur, te facie ad faciem in patria contemplabuntur. Porro in isto exilio justi confitentur Domino duplici confessione, sed confessio laudis eorum est imperfecta. In patria vero non nisi confessione laudis Domino confitentur, sed illa confessio perfecta est atque perpetua. Nunc etiam habitant cum vultu divino, conversando sincere coram Deo, eumque fideliter contemplando. Hæc tamen habitatio non est fixa et proprie dicta : Non enim habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus. In patria autem vere, fixe et proprie habitare dicuntur cum vultu divino.
paras.en: [[139:14|But as for the just, they shall give glory|Verumtamen justi confitebuntur]] in prosperity and adversity [[139:14|to thy name|nomini tuo]] [Latin *confitebuntur*, which means both "they shall praise" and "they shall confess"], with a twofold confession, namely the confession of God's praise and of their own fault. For they will ascribe the good to thee and the evil to themselves; and whatever befalls them, they will justify thee in all things, saying: [[Job 1:21|as it hath pleased the Lord, so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord|Sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est. Sit nomen Domini benedictum]]. [[139:14|and the upright shall dwell with thy countenance|Et habitabunt recti cum vultu tuo]], that is, they shall be united to thee and enjoy thee, and shall contemplate thee [[1 Cor 13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]] in the fatherland. Now in this exile the just confess to the Lord with a twofold confession, but their confession of praise is imperfect. In the fatherland, however, they confess to the Lord only with the confession of praise, but that confession is perfect and everlasting. Even now they dwell with the divine countenance, by living sincerely before God and faithfully contemplating him. Yet this dwelling is not fixed nor dwelling in the proper sense: [[Heb 13:14|For, we have not here a lasting city: but we seek one that is to come|Non enim habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus]]. But in the fatherland they are said to dwell with the divine countenance truly, fixedly and properly.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum fervidis orationibus plenum, et morali instructione ornatum audivimus : quem decet nos ardenti affectu proferre, atque ex ejus doctrina discere quod incessanter ad Deum recurrere indigemus, eo quod ipse sit virtus nostræ salutis. Propterea semper ex corde ei dicamus : Salus nostra in manu tua est ; respiciat nos Dominus noster, et læti serviemus regi. Hæc enim fuerunt verba Ægyptiorum ad Joseph. Per Ægyptios autem signantur peccatores ; per Joseph, Christus.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of fervent prayers and adorned with moral instruction: which it befits us to utter with ardent affection, and to learn from its teaching that we need to run back to God unceasingly, since he is the strength of our salvation. Therefore let us always say to him from the heart: [[Gen 47:25|our life is in thy hand; only let my lord look favourably upon us, and we will gladly serve the king|Salus nostra in manu tua est ; respiciat nos Dominus noster, et læti serviemus regi]] [Latin *salus*, "life" or "safety", but also "salvation", the word of the psalm's *virtus salutis*]. For these were the words of the Egyptians to Joseph; and by the Egyptians are signified sinners, by Joseph, Christ.

paras.t: Precatio. Domine, virtus salutis nostræ, exaudi vocem orationis plebis tuæ, et in miseriis quibus affligimur, nobis adsiste : ut ab omni malo, te protegente, erepti, secure serviamus tibi.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, strength of our salvation, hear the voice of the prayer of thy people, and stand by us in the miseries with which we are afflicted: that, delivered from all evil under thy protection, we may serve thee without fear.

140.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUADRAGESIMI : DOMINE, CLAMAVI AD TE.
140.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and fortieth psalm: I have cried to thee, O Lord.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi est: Psalmus David. Ipse enim beatus David auctor est psalmi præsentis, loquens in eo in persona hominis studiosi, perfectionem attingere laborantis: quam quia sine custodia linguæ adipisci non valet, precatur sibi a Domino gratiam condonari, qua linguam refrenet ac regat, et ait:
paras.en: The title of the psalm is: A psalm of David [Psalmus David; in the Vulgate the title is part of v. 1, which the Douay-Rheims prints without it]. For blessed David himself is the author of the present psalm, speaking in it in the person of a zealous man who labours to attain perfection: and because he cannot reach it without guarding his tongue, he prays that the Lord grant him the grace to bridle and rule his tongue, and says:

paras.t: Domine, clamavi ad te, non tam alta voce, quam vehementi ac præcordiali affectu. Non enim remisse aut pigre invocandus est Deus, sed animo timorato, affectuoso, atque pervigili, imo et incessanti, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico inducitur: Non impediaris semper orare; et, Ante orationem præpara animam tuam, et noli esse quasi homo tentans Deum. Idcirco quum dixisset, Domine, clamavi ad te, scilicet tempore præterito, profitetur se in præsenti clamare, et in futuro clamaturum esse, ut pandat se nunquam a prece velle cessare. Sequitur enim: exaudi me nunc in præsenti; intende voci meæ, dum clamavero ad te, id est, quocumque tempore futuro te invocavero, ostende te mihi intendere, ita ut vocem meam, id est orationem meam, diligenter consideres, et pie exaudias.
paras.en: [[140:1|I have cried to thee, O Lord|Domine, clamavi ad te]], not so much with a loud voice as with vehement and heartfelt affection. For God is not to be called upon slackly or sluggishly, but with a God-fearing, loving and wakeful mind, nay, an unceasing one, as is set down in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 18:22|Let nothing hinder thee from praying always|Non impediaris semper orare]]; and, [[Ecclus 18:23|Before prayer prepare thy soul: and be not as a man that tempteth God|Ante orationem præpara animam tuam, et noli esse quasi homo tentans Deum]]. Therefore, having said, [[140:1|I have cried to thee, O Lord|Domine, clamavi ad te]], that is, in time past, he professes that he cries in the present and will cry in the future, to show that he will never cease from prayer. For there follows: [[140:1|hear me|exaudi me]] now in the present; [[140:1|hearken to my voice, when I cry to thee|intende voci meæ, dum clamavero ad te]], that is, at whatever time to come I shall call upon thee, show that thou hearkenest to me, so that thou mayest diligently consider my voice, that is, my prayer, and graciously hear it.

paras.t: Dirigatur oratio mea, id est, ascendat, cœlos penetret, tibi perfecte complaceat, sicut incensum in lege dirigebatur ad te, et fumando ascendit, ac tibi præ ceteris sacrificiis placuit: non propter se ipsum, sed ex devotione offerentis. Quod autem subjungitur, in conspectu tuo, referri potest ad utrumque horum: videlicet ut oratio dirigatur in conspectu Dei sicut incensum; vel ut oratio dirigatur ad Deum, sicut incensum dirigebatur in conspectu divino. Dicebatur autem incensum, oblatio quæ tota incendebatur et comburebatur ad Dei honorem: per quod designatur obsequium perfectorum, qui se totos mancipant Deo, seque totaliter abnegant et relinquunt. Petitur ergo, ut sicut incensum coram Deo ascendit, et placuit propter devotionem fervidam offerentis, sic oratio nostra coram Deo ascendat atque complaceat. Unde in Ecclesiastico habetur: Oratio humiliantis se penetrabit nubes; et alias, Oratio justi penetrat cœlos. Elevatio manuum mearum, id est exaltatio desideriorum meorum ad superna, directio operum meorum ad divina, erectio manuum mearum corporalium ex cordis elevatione procedens, seu ordinata ad illam, virtualiter sit coram te, Domine, sacrificium vespertinum: quatenus ita placeat tibi, sicut placebat sacrificium vespertinum seu ultimum quolibet die, quando videlicet offerebatur agnus ad vesperam: cujus immolatio erat figura immolationis Agni Dei, scilicet Christi in cruce. Unde Christus in cruce pendens, dicere poterat: Elevatio manuum mearum sacrificium vespertinum.
paras.en: [[140:2|Let my prayer be directed|Dirigatur oratio mea]], that is, let it ascend, pierce the heavens, and be perfectly pleasing to thee, [[140:2|as incense|sicut incensum]] under the law was directed to thee, and rose up in smoke, and pleased thee above the other sacrifices: not for its own sake, but for the devotion of the offerer. What is added, [[140:2|in thy sight|in conspectu tuo]], can be referred to either of these: namely, that the prayer be directed in God's sight as incense; or that the prayer be directed to God, as the incense was directed in the divine sight. Now that oblation was called incense [incensum, literally "a thing set alight"] which was wholly set alight and burnt to the honour of God[[Ex 29:18||]] [the Vulgate there has in incensum, where the Douay-Rheims reads "for a burnt offering"]: by which is signified the service of the perfect, who give themselves over wholly to God, and utterly deny and forsake themselves. It is asked, then, that as incense rose up before God and was pleasing for the fervent devotion of the offerer, so our prayer may rise up before God and be pleasing to him. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 35:21|The prayer of him that humbleth himself, shall pierce the clouds|Oratio humiliantis se penetrabit nubes]]; and elsewhere, The prayer of the just pierces the heavens. [[140:2|the lifting up of my hands|Elevatio manuum mearum]], that is, the raising of my desires to the things above, the directing of my works to divine things, the lifting of my bodily hands which proceeds from the uplifting of the heart or is ordered to it, be in effect before thee, O Lord, [[140:2|as evening sacrifice|sacrificium vespertinum]]: so that it may please thee as the evening sacrifice pleased thee, that is, the last one of each day, when a lamb was offered in the evening[[Ex 29:41||]] [the margin gives Exod. xxix, 38–41]: whose immolation was a figure of the immolation of the Lamb of God, namely of Christ on the cross. Hence Christ, hanging on the cross, could say: [[140:2|the lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice|Elevatio manuum mearum sacrificium vespertinum]].

paras.t: Pone, Domine, custodiam ori meo, id est, da mihi gratiam custodiendi os meum, ne loquar vel taceam inordinate: sed dum tempus est loquendi, prudenter atque utiliter loquar; dum vero tempus tacendi adfuerit, moderate ac laudabiliter taceam. Pone quoque et ostium circumstantiæ, id est clausuram discretam, labiis meis: videlicet ut tunc, ibi, et taliter labia mea ad loquendum aperiam, et ad tacendum recludam, quando, quo loco, et qualiter oportet aut expedit, ut sim in utroque discretus et fructuosus. Hoc est quod ab Ecclesiastico inducitur: Quis dabit ori meo custodiam, et super labia mea signaculum certum, ut non cadam ab ipsis, et lingua mea me perdat?
paras.en: [[140:3|Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth|Pone, Domine, custodiam ori meo]], that is, give me the grace of guarding my mouth, that I may not speak or keep silence inordinately: but when it is the time to speak, may speak prudently and profitably, and when the time to keep silence is come, may keep silence with moderation and to good purpose[[Eccles 3:7||]]. Set also [[140:3|a door round about|ostium circumstantiæ]] [ostium circumstantiæ, literally "a door of circumstance": Denis takes it of the circumstances of when, where and how], that is, a discreet enclosure, [[140:3|my lips|labiis meis]]: namely, that I may open my lips to speak and close them to keep silence at the time, in the place and in the manner that is fitting or expedient, so as to be discreet and fruitful in both. This is what is set down in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 22:33|Who will set a guard before my mouth, and a sure seal upon my lips, that I fall not by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?|Quis dabit ori meo custodiam, et super labia mea signaculum certum, ut non cadam ab ipsis, et lingua mea me perdat?]] [the margin gives Eccli. xxxiii, 33; the verse is Ecclus 22:33]

paras.t: Non declines, id est, non inclinari seu moveri permittas, cor meum in verba malitiæ, ut verba maligna effundat, videlicet ad excusandas, id est excusatorie proferendas, excusationes in peccatis mihi objectis, et a me perpetratis, Cum hominibus operantibus iniquitatem, id est, sicut agunt homines assueti seu habituati in malo; et non communicabo, per consensum seu imitationem hujuscemodi excusationis, cum electis, id est præcipuis, eorum qui se excusant. Electi enim eorum sunt, qui in modo et arte excusandi propria vitia, aliis eminent: quales sunt simulatores et callidi, qui (sicut asseritur) provocant iram Dei. Hoc est miserandissimum genus pravorum, qui propria delicta excusant. Hi enim obicem ponunt remedio, vulnus suum abscondunt, manus divini judicii incidunt, insanabilesque consistunt. Multipliciter vero excusat quis sua peccata: Primo, dicendo id quod malum est, non esse malum. Contra quos per Isaiam dicitur: Væ qui dicitis malum bonum, et bonum malum. Et Amos ait: Væ qui convertistis in amaritudinem judicium, et fructum justitiæ in absinthium. Secundo, negando se peccasse, quum tamen peccaverit. Quod quam damnabile sit, Dominus manifestat, dum ait: Ecce ego judicio contendam tecum, eo quod dixeris, Non peccavi. Tertio, alleviando propriam culpam, dicendo: Non adverto, non pondero, habeo a natura. Quarto, imputando alteri proprium malum, dicendo: Ille me induxit; ille est causa peccati mei. Hinc enim in Proverbiis dicitur: Qui odit increpationes, insipiens est; et, Non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit. Et Salomon iterum loquitur: Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis. Propterea, quantum distat cœlum a terra, et ortus ab occidente, tam remote abjiciamus semper a nobis tam pessimum vitium.
paras.en: [[140:4|Incline not|Non declines]], that is, do not suffer to be inclined or moved, [[140:4|my heart to evil words|cor meum in verba malitiæ]], so that it pours out malicious words, namely [[140:4|to make excuses|ad excusandas]], that is, to put forward by way of excuse, [[140:4|in sins|excusationes in peccatis]] [ad excusandas excusationes, literally "to excuse excuses"] laid to my charge and committed by me, [[140:4|With men that work iniquity|Cum hominibus operantibus iniquitatem]], that is, as men do who are accustomed or habituated to evil; [[140:4|and I will not communicate|et non communicabo]], by consent to or imitation of such excusing, [[140:4|with the choicest|cum electis]], that is, the foremost, [[140:4|of them|eorum]] who excuse themselves. For the choicest of them are those who excel others in the manner and art of excusing their own vices: such are [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men|simulatores et callidi]], who (as is asserted) [[Job 36:13|prove the wrath of God|provocant iram Dei]] [prove, that is, provoke]. This is the most pitiable kind of the wicked, those who excuse their own faults. For they set an obstacle to the remedy, hide their wound, fall into the hands of the divine judgment, and remain incurable. Now a man excuses his sins in many ways. First, by saying that what is evil is not evil. Against such it is said through Isaias: [[Is 5:20|Woe to you that call evil good, and good evil|Væ qui dicitis malum bonum, et bonum malum]]. And Amos says: Woe[[Amos 6:1||]] to you that [[Amos 6:13|have turned judgment into bitterness, and the fruit of justice into wormwood|convertistis in amaritudinem judicium, et fructum justitiæ in absinthium]] [the margin gives Amos vi, 1, 13: the Woe stands at 6:1, the words that follow at 6:13]. Secondly, by denying that he has sinned, when in fact he has sinned. How damnable this is the Lord shows when he says: [[Jer 2:35|Behold, I will contend with thee in judgment, because thou hast said: I have not sinned|Ecce ego judicio contendam tecum, eo quod dixeris, Non peccavi]]. Thirdly, by lightening his own fault, saying: I do not notice it, I do not weigh it, I have it from nature. Fourthly, by imputing his own evil to another, saying: He led me into it; he is the cause of my sin. Hence it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 12:1|he that hateth reproof, is foolish|Qui odit increpationes, insipiens est]]; and, [[Prov 15:12|A corrupt man loveth not one that reproveth him|Non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit]]. And Solomon says again: [[Prov 15:32|He that rejecteth instruction, despiseth his own soul|Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam]]; [[Prov 15:32|but he that yieldeth to reproof, possesseth understanding|qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis]] [possessor est cordis, literally "is the possessor of a heart"]. Therefore, as far as heaven is from earth, and the east from the west[[Ps 102:12||]], so far let us always cast so very wicked a vice from us.

paras.t: Corripiet me justus, qui neminem palpat, nulli blanditur, in misericordia, id est pie et caritative, non crudeliter et invidiose; et increpabit me propter meos excessus, sicut dilectio fraterna expostulat. Oleum autem, id est adulatio, simulata dilectio, falsa laudatio peccatoris, non impinguet caput meum, id est, non delectet mentem meam, non me demulceat, non mihi complaceat, nec ad consensum illicitum pertrahat. Unde scriptum est: Attende tibi a pestifero. Quoniam adhuc et oratio mea versatur in beneplacitis eorum, id est in his quæ peccatoribus istis placent, quatenus ipsi a suis peccatis desistant, et ne ego ab eis seducar. Hoc igitur continuo oro, ut ipsi convertantur, et ego custodiar.
paras.en: [[140:5|The just man shall correct me|Corripiet me justus]], he who coaxes no one and flatters none, [[140:5|in mercy|in misericordia]], that is, kindly and charitably, not cruelly and enviously; [[140:5|and shall reprove me|et increpabit me]] for my excesses, as brotherly love demands. [[140:5|but let not the oil|Oleum autem]], that is, flattery, feigned love, the false praise [[140:5|of the sinner|peccatoris]], [[140:5|fatten my head|non impinguet caput meum]], that is, let it not delight my mind, nor soothe me, nor please me, nor draw me to unlawful consent. Hence it is written: [[Ecclus 11:35|Take heed to thyself of a mischievous man|Attende tibi a pestifero]]. [[140:5|For my prayer shall still be|Quoniam adhuc et oratio mea]] busied [[140:5|against the things with which they are well pleased|in beneplacitis eorum]] [in beneplacitis eorum, literally "in their good pleasures"], that is, in the things that please these sinners, to the end that they may desist from their sins, and that I may not be led astray by them. This, then, I pray continually: that they may be converted, and I be kept safe.

paras.t: Absorpti sunt juncti petræ judices eorum: id est, principales et magistri istorum juncti petræ, id est Deo seu divinæ justitiæ comparati, absorpti sunt, id est, omnino defecerunt, ita quod nihil veræ justitiæ habent, præsertim quum careant fide per dilectionem operante. Bene autem per petram intelligitur Christus, juxta illud: Dominus petra mea et robur meum. Vel, per petram accipitur Christus, qui stultam fecit sapientiam hujus mundi, damnabilemque probavit justitiam confidentium propriis viribus, et philosophorum, qui in suis cogitationibus evanuerunt.
paras.en: [[140:6|Their judges falling upon the rock have been swallowed up|Absorpti sunt juncti petræ judices eorum]]: that is, the chief men and masters of these, [[140:6|falling upon the rock|juncti petræ]] [juncti petræ, literally "joined to the rock"], that is, set beside God or the divine justice, [[140:6|have been swallowed up|absorpti sunt]], that is, have utterly failed, so that they have nothing of true justice, especially since they lack the faith that works through charity. And well is Christ understood by the rock, according to that saying: [[2 Kings 22:2|The Lord is my rock, and my strength|Dominus petra mea et robur meum]]. Or, by the rock is understood Christ, who [[1 Cor 1:20|made foolish the wisdom of this world|stultam fecit sapientiam hujus mundi]], and showed to be damnable the justice of those who trust in their own strength, and of the philosophers, who [[Rom 1:21|became vain in their thoughts|in suis cogitationibus evanuerunt]].

paras.t: Audient, id est, audiant peccatores ad suam correctionem, verba mea informatoria atque salubria, quoniam potuerunt, id est, quoniam verba mea efficacia sive potentia sunt ad instruendum iniquos; vel, Quoniam potuerunt ipsi audire verba mea, quum non sint incorrigibiles penitus. Sicut crassitudo terræ, id est pinguedo latens sub terra, erupta est, id est ascendit et apparuit, super terram, quum terra vomere scinderetur, sic verba mea potuerunt eos corrigere. Tanquam dicat: Quemadmodum crassitudo terræ egreditur, terramque fecundat, sic verba mea spiritualiter fecundare possunt corda infructuosa et mala. Melius tamen videtur, ut istud referatur ad versum sequentem, præsertim quoniam in Hebræo hic incipit versus. Eritque sensus: Sicut crassitudo terræ erupta est, id est erupit, super terram aratam, sic Dissipata sunt ossa nostra, id est, virtutes animæ nostræ debilitatæ, dispersæ, seu corruptæ sunt, secus infernum, id est juxta peccata, quæ sunt portæ inferni. Peccando namque virtus animæ dissipatur, atque inferno appropinquat. Mortali enim peccato corrumpitur, veniali vero debilitatur; et dum una amittitur, cæteræ quoque perduntur. Dicuntur autem ossa virtutes, quoniam sicut ossa sunt robur et firmitas corporis, sic virtutes stabilimentum sunt animæ.
paras.en: [[140:6|They shall hear|Audient]], that is, let sinners hear, for their correction, [[140:6|my words|verba mea]] of instruction and healing, [[140:6|for they have prevailed|quoniam potuerunt]] [potuerunt, literally "they have been able"], that is, because my words are effectual or powerful to instruct the wicked; or, Because they themselves have been able to hear my words, since they are not wholly incorrigible. [[140:7|As when the thickness of the earth|Sicut crassitudo terræ]] [crassitudo, "thickness" or "fatness"], that is, the fatness hidden beneath the earth, [[140:7|is broken up|erupta est]], that is, has risen and appeared, [[140:7|upon the ground|super terram]], when the earth was cut by the ploughshare, so my words were able to correct them. As though he said: As the thickness of the earth comes forth and makes the earth fruitful, so my words can spiritually make fruitful hearts that are barren and evil. It seems better, however, that this be referred to the following verse, especially since in the Hebrew the verse begins here. And the sense will be: [[140:7|As when the thickness of the earth is broken up|Sicut crassitudo terræ erupta est]], that is, has burst forth, [[140:7|upon the ground|super terram]] that has been ploughed, so [[140:7|Our bones are scattered|Dissipata sunt ossa nostra]], that is, the virtues of our soul are weakened, dispersed or corrupted, [[140:7|by the side of hell|secus infernum]], that is, close to sins, which are the gates of hell. For by sinning the virtue of the soul is scattered and draws near to hell. For by mortal sin it is corrupted, and by venial sin weakened; and when one is lost, the others too are lost. And the virtues are called bones because, as the bones are the strength and firmness of the body, so the virtues are the support of the soul.

paras.t: Quia ad te, Domine, Domine, oculi mei, id est, ex quo o Domine, Domine, oculi cordis mei diriguntur ad te, idcirco in te speravi, qui non despicis confugientes ad tuam clementiam: non auferas animam meam a consortio electorum, nec eam auferri permittas a te per culpam; sed quando fuerit a te aversa, digneris eam convertere, et tibi inseparabiliter copulare. Custodi me a laqueo, id est deceptione, quem statuerunt mihi dæmon et mundus, ne incidam illum et capiar, et a scandalis operantium iniquitatem, id est a vitiis impiorum scandalizantibus pusillos, videlicet ne ex dicto aut facto inordinato alterius scandalizer, sed in via Dei fortis solidusque persistam. Nam qui scandalizatur, pusillus est. Perfecti vero nec scandalizantur, nec scandalizant active.
paras.en: [[140:8|But to thee, O Lord, Lord, are my eyes|Quia ad te, Domine, Domine, oculi mei]] [Quia, "since" or "because"], that is, since, O Lord, Lord, the eyes of my heart are directed to thee, therefore [[140:8|in thee have I put my trust|in te speravi]], who dost not despise those who take refuge in thy clemency: [[140:8|take not away my soul|non auferas animam meam]] from the fellowship of the elect, nor suffer it to be taken away from thee by sin; but when it has turned away from thee, vouchsafe to convert it and join it to thyself inseparably. [[140:9|Keep me from the snare|Custodi me a laqueo]], that is, from the deception, [[140:9|which they have laid for me|quem statuerunt mihi]], the devil and the world, that I may not fall into it and be caught, [[140:9|and from the stumblingblocks of them that work iniquity|et a scandalis operantium iniquitatem]], that is, from the vices of the wicked which scandalize the little ones: namely, that I may not be scandalized by another's inordinate word or deed, but may persist strong and firm in the way of God. For he who is scandalized is little. But the perfect are neither scandalized nor actively give scandal.

paras.t: Cadent in retiaculo, id est in muscipula seu deceptione, ejus (scandali, vel iniquitatis, seu dæmonis) peccatores. Ipsi enim ruunt ad culpam ex deceptione scandali, ex fraude diaboli, ex attractione peccati. Singulariter sum ego, id est, ab impiis sequestratus subsisto, et soli portioni seu societati justorum adhæreo, donec transeam de via ad patriam.
paras.en: [[140:10|The wicked|peccatores]] [[140:10|shall fall in his net|Cadent in retiaculo]], that is, into the trap or deception; [[140:10|his|ejus]], that is, of the scandal, or of the iniquity, or of the devil. For they rush into sin through the deception of scandal, through the fraud of the devil, through the attraction of sin. [[140:10|I am alone|Singulariter sum ego]], that is, I stand apart, separated from the wicked, and cleave only to the portion or company of the just, [[140:10|until I pass|donec transeam]] from the way to the fatherland.

paras.t: Psalmus iste devotissimis precibus adornatus, nos admonet vigilare circa linguæ custodiam. Magna nempe perfectio est custodia linguæ: imo divina Scriptura beatitudinem in ea aliquo modo constituit. Scriptum est enim: Si quis in verbo non offendit, hic perfectus est vir; et iterum, Beatus vir qui non est lapsus in verbo ex ore suo. Ad custodiendam autem linguam, primo oportet pensare qualitatem ejus cui loquimur, quatenus verba nostra aptemus capacitati et dispositioni ejus cui loquimur. Secundo, observandum est debitum tempus loquendi, videlicet ut non loquamur, nisi fructus sperari possit ex locutione profuturus. Tertio, considerare oportet ubi et inter quos loquendum sit. Non enim in ecclesia fabulari debemus. Et in Ecclesiastico habetur: Loqui in medio magnatorum non præsumas; et, Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem. Quarto servanda est quantitas in loquendo, ne plura verba proferamus quam oportet aut expedit. Propter quod a Salomone dicitur: Qui moderatur labia sua, prudentissimus est; et rursus, In multiloquio non deerit peccatum. Quinto, pensandum est qualiter sit loquendum, videlicet modeste, mansuete, suaviter. Scriptum est enim: Verbum dulce multiplicat amicos, et mitigat inimicos; et iterum, Responsio mollis frangit iram. Sexto, consideremus cur seu propter quem finem loqui intendimus, scilicet ad Dei honorem, et propter rationabilem causam.
paras.en: This psalm, adorned with most devout prayers, admonishes us to keep watch over the guarding of the tongue. For the guarding of the tongue is a great perfection: nay, divine Scripture in some way places blessedness in it. For it is written: [[Jas 3:2|If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man|Si quis in verbo non offendit, hic perfectus est vir]]; and again, [[Ecclus 14:1|Blessed is the man that hath not slipped by a word out of his mouth|Beatus vir qui non est lapsus in verbo ex ore suo]]. Now to guard the tongue, we must first weigh the condition of the one to whom we speak, so as to fit our words to the capacity and disposition of the one to whom we speak. Secondly, the due time for speaking must be observed: namely, that we speak only when some profitable fruit can be hoped for from the speaking. Thirdly, we must consider where and among whom one is to speak. For we ought not to chatter in church. And in Ecclesiasticus it is said: [[Ecclus 32:13|In the company of great men take not upon thee|Loqui in medio magnatorum non præsumas]] [Denis reads Loqui in medio magnatorum non præsumas, "Presume not to speak in the midst of great men"]; and, [[Ecclus 32:6|Where there is no hearing, pour not out words|Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem]]. Fourthly, measure must be kept in speaking, that we may not utter more words than is fitting or expedient. For which reason it is said by Solomon: [[Prov 10:19|he that refraineth his lips, is most wise|Qui moderatur labia sua, prudentissimus est]]; and again, [[Prov 10:19|In the multitude of words there shall not want sin|In multiloquio non deerit peccatum]]. Fifthly, we must weigh how one should speak: namely, modestly, gently, sweetly. For it is written: [[Ecclus 6:5|A sweet word multiplieth friends, and appeaseth enemies|Verbum dulce multiplicat amicos, et mitigat inimicos]]; and again, [[Prov 15:1|A mild answer breaketh wrath|Responsio mollis frangit iram]]. Sixthly, let us consider why, or for what end, we mean to speak: namely, for the honour of God, and for a reasonable cause.

paras.t: Precatio. Clamantium ad te, Domine, intende vocem; peccantes nos, non in ira, sed in misericordia increpa: pone custodiam ori nostro, et non declines cor nostrum in verba peccati et malitiæ; sed linguam nostram fac semper exsultare in laude gloriæ tuæ.
paras.en: Prayer. Hearken, O Lord, to the voice of us who cry to thee; reprove us sinners not in anger but in mercy; set a watch before our mouth, and incline not our heart to words of sin and malice; but make our tongue ever exult in the praise of thy glory.

141.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS, TROPOLOGICA ET ALLEGORICA PSALMI CENTESIMI QUADRAGESIMI PRIMI : VOCE MEA AD DOMINUM CLAMAVI.
141.title_en: Literal, tropological and allegorical exposition of the hundred and forty-first psalm: I cried to the Lord with my voice.

paras.t: Prænotatur autem psalmus præsens hoc titulo : Intellectus David, quum esset in spelunca; oratio. Ad litteram, sanctus David fugiens regem Saulem, fecit hunc Psalmum, quum lateret in spelunca Odollam, suppliciter petens liberari divinitus a persecutoribus suis. Et est sensus tituli talis : Intellectus David, id est, psalmus iste est eruditio David, qui et ipse a Spiritu Sancto edoctus est ad scribendum hunc psalmum, quum esset in spelunca prædicta absconditus : qua etiam ipse David nos erudivit. Suo enim exemplo docet nos clamare ferventer fiducialiterque ad Dominum. Expositio autem litteralis psalmi præsentis, difficultatem non habet. Petit enim David a Saule ejusque fautoribus erui, qui sibi varios laqueos paraverunt.
paras.en: Now the present psalm has this title prefixed to it: [[141:1|Of understanding for David|Intellectus David]], [[141:1|when he was in the cave|quum esset in spelunca]]; [[141:1|A prayer|oratio]]. According to the letter, holy David, fleeing from King Saul, made this Psalm while he lay hidden in the cave of Odollam[[1 Kings 22:1||]], humbly asking to be delivered by God from his persecutors. And the sense of the title is this: [[141:1|Of understanding for David|Intellectus David]] [Latin *Intellectus David*, literally "the understanding of David"], that is, this psalm is the instruction of David, who was himself taught by the Holy Ghost to write this psalm while he was hidden in the aforesaid cave; and by it David has also instructed us. For by his own example he teaches us to cry to the Lord fervently and with confidence. The literal exposition of the present psalm has no difficulty. For David asks to be rescued from Saul and his supporters, who had laid various snares for him.

paras.t: Sed quoniam in principio tituli dicitur, Intellectus David, videtur ipse David scripsisse hunc psalmum magis de re significata, quam de figura significante. Quamvis enim David aliquos psalmos ediderit occasione persecutionis suæ, quam sustinuit a Saule et Absalone ac aliis ; tamen, quum esset Propheta, de Christi mysteriis præ universis Prophetis illuminatus, credendum est quod in talibus psalmis potius vaticinetur de Christo, quam orationem sive historiam texat de semetipso : præsertim quum David non ignoraverit se esse figuram Christi, et in Christi figura sibi contingere multa eorum quæ sibi accidisse noscuntur. Sic in præsenti credendum est. David enim est figura Christi ; Saul vero cum populo suo sibi consentiente, typus est principis sacerdotum ac Judæorum persequentium Salvatorem. Spelunca vero significat præsens sæculum, seu corpus passibile. Est itaque tituli sensus : Psalmus iste est intellectus David, id est Christi per David figurati : quem intellectum Christus habuit, quum esset in mundo inferiore seu corpore suo mortali ; et est oratio ejus. Christus ergo ut homo passibilis, in passione constitutus, ait Ecclesiæ se clamasse ad Dominum, ut doceat eam etiam sic agere dum tribulatur.
paras.en: But since at the beginning of the title it is said, [[141:1|Of understanding for David|Intellectus David]], David himself seems to have written this psalm rather about the thing signified than about the figure that signifies it. For although David composed some psalms on the occasion of the persecution which he suffered from Saul, from Absalom and from others, yet, since he was a Prophet, enlightened about the mysteries of Christ beyond all the Prophets, we must believe that in such psalms he prophesies of Christ rather than weaves a prayer or a history about himself: especially since David was not unaware that he was a figure of Christ, and that many of the things known to have befallen him happened to him as a figure of Christ. So we must believe in the present case. For David is a figure of Christ; while Saul, with his people consenting to him, is a type of the chief of the priests and of the Jews who persecuted the Saviour. The cave, again, signifies the present world, or the passible body [that is, the body capable of suffering]. So the sense of the title is this: This psalm is the understanding of David, that is, of Christ prefigured by David: an understanding which Christ had [[141:1|when he was in|quum esset in]] the lower world, or in his mortal body; and it is his [[141:1|prayer|oratio]]. Christ, then, as a man capable of suffering, set in his passion, tells the Church that he cried to the Lord, to teach her also to do likewise when she is in tribulation.

paras.t: VOCE mea ad Dominum clamavi, orando pro celeri resurrectione, pro corporis mei glorificatione, pro transgressorum conversione. Voce mea ad Dominum deprecatus sum. Repetit quod prædixit, propter expressionem majorem, et exhortationem efficaciorem. Effundo in conspectu ejus orationem meam, orando eum intente, ejusque præsentiam cogitando sollicite, et tribulationem meam corporalem seu exteriorem, et spiritualem seu interiorem, videlicet tristitiam et timorem : quam tribulationem mihi intulerunt Judæi, vel quam sponte assumpsi, et quam ex compassione errantium habui ; ante ipsum pronuntio, id est, coram Deo Patre exposui. Hæc omnia Christum fecisse, Evangelistæ testantur. Quomodo enim passione instante ter Patrem oravit, Matthæus refert ; et quomodo tunc factus sit sudor ejus sicut guttæ sanguinis, factusque in agonia, prolixius oraverit, in Luca scriptum est.
paras.en: [[141:2|I cried to the Lord with my voice|VOCE mea ad Dominum clamavi]], praying for a speedy resurrection, for the glorification of my body, for the conversion of transgressors. [[141:2|with my voice I made supplication to the Lord|Voce mea ad Dominum deprecatus sum]]. He repeats what he said before, for greater expression and more effective exhortation. [[141:3|In his sight I pour out my prayer|Effundo in conspectu ejus orationem meam]], praying to him intently and thinking anxiously on his presence; and [[141:3|my trouble|tribulationem meam]], bodily or outward, and spiritual or inward, namely sadness and fear: a trouble which the Jews brought upon me, or which I took upon myself of my own will, and which I had out of compassion for those who go astray; [[141:3|before him I declare|ante ipsum pronuntio]], that is, I have set it forth before God the Father. That Christ did all these things the Evangelists bear witness. For how, when his passion was at hand, he prayed to the Father three times, Matthew relates[[Matt 26:39||]][[Matt 26:42||]][[Matt 26:44||]]; and how his sweat then became as drops of blood, and how, being in an agony, he prayed the longer, is written in Luke.

paras.t: In deficiendo ex me spiritum meum, id est, quum spiritus meus creatus, videlicet anima rationalis in me exsistens, deficeret ex se seu sua conditione, non defectu culpæ, sed pœnæ : quando videlicet cœpi pavere et tædere, et quando in agonia factus sum, vel quando inclinato capite tradidi spiritum ; et tu cognovisti semitas meas, id est, tunc tu, o Pater, per approbationem novisti doctrinam conversationemque meam, et omnia quæ pro humana salute assumpsi, feci, atque perpessus sum. In via hac qua ambulabam, id est in sæculo isto, in via virtutum qua incessi in tota conversatione mea, absconderunt Judæi laqueum mihi, id est contra me, insidiantes mihi occulte, loquentes adulatorie, variisque fraudulentiis quærentes nocere.
paras.en: [[141:4|When my spirit failed me|In deficiendo ex me spiritum meum]], that is, when my created spirit, namely the rational soul existing in me, failed of itself or by its own condition, not by a failing of guilt but of punishment: namely when I began to fear and to be heavy, and when I was in an agony, or when, bowing my head, I gave up the ghost; [[141:4|then thou knewest my paths|et tu cognovisti semitas meas]], that is, then thou, O Father, didst know with approval my teaching and my manner of life, and all that I took upon me, did and suffered for the salvation of mankind. [[141:4|In this way wherein I walked|In via hac qua ambulabam]], that is, in this world, in the way of the virtues in which I went throughout my whole life, the Jews [[141:4|have hidden|absconderunt]] [[141:4|a snare for me|laqueum mihi]], that is, against me, lying in wait for me secretly, speaking flatteringly, and seeking to harm me by various deceits.

paras.t: Considerabam ad dexteram, id est ad partem mihi favorabilem, videlicet ad notos atque discipulos meos, et videbam, an aliquem mihi constanter cohærentem invenirem ; et non erat aliquis vir qui cognosceret me cognitione publicæ confessionis. Tempore enim quo captus est Christus, discipuli omnes relicto eo fugerunt ; et paulo post princeps eorum cœpit anathematizare, detestari et jurare : Quia nescio hominem istum. Periit fuga a me, quoniam fugere nolui : sicut supra dictum est, Traditus sum, et non egrediebar. Vel, Periit fuga a me, id est, ita ligatus sum vinculis, et circumdatus hostibus, quod, humano modo loquendo, fugere nequeo, quamvis vellem. Non enim nisi supernaturali virtute fugere potuisset, dum erat ligatus, hostibusque vallatus. Et non est qui requirat animam meam, id est, nemo erat qui conaretur me de manu hostium liberare constanter. Quamvis enim Pilatus ad tempus studuerit me eripere, tandem tamen dedit sententiam contra me : qua data, nemo contradixit. Unde Christus testatur : Circumspexi, et non erat auxiliator ; itemque, Torcular calcavi solus, et de gentibus non est vir mecum. Supra quoque prædictum est : Et sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit.
paras.en: [[141:5|I looked on my right hand|Considerabam ad dexteram]], that is, to the side favourable to me, namely to my acquaintances and my disciples, [[141:5|and beheld|et videbam]], whether I might find anyone who clung to me steadfastly; [[141:5|and there was no one|et non erat]], no man, [[141:5|that would know me|qui cognosceret me]] with the knowledge of open confession. For at the time when Christ was taken, [[Matt 26:56|the disciples, all leaving him, fled|discipuli omnes relicto eo fugerunt]]; and a little after, their chief began to curse, to detest and to swear[[Matt 26:74||]]: [[Mark 14:71|I know not this man|Quia nescio hominem istum]]. [[141:5|Flight hath failed me|Periit fuga a me]], because I would not flee: as was said above, [[Ps 87:9|I was delivered up, and came not forth|Traditus sum, et non egrediebar]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxvii, 9; the words are Ps 87:9]. Or, [[141:5|Flight hath failed me|Periit fuga a me]], that is, I am so bound with chains and so surrounded by enemies that, speaking after the manner of men, I cannot flee, even if I would. For he could not have fled, except by supernatural power, while he was bound and hemmed in by enemies. [[141:5|And there is no one that hath regard to my soul|Et non est qui requirat animam meam]], that is, there was no one who would steadfastly try to deliver me from the hand of my enemies. For although Pilate for a time tried to rescue me, yet in the end he gave sentence against me[[Matt 27:24||]] [the margin gives Matth. xxvii, 15–26]; and once it was given, no one spoke against it. Hence Christ testifies: [[Is 63:5|I looked about, and there was none to help|Circumspexi, et non erat auxiliator]]; and again, [[Is 63:3|I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the Gentiles there is not a man with me|Torcular calcavi solus, et de gentibus non est vir mecum]]. It was also foretold above: [[Ps 68:21|And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, but there was none|Et sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit]].

paras.t: Clamavi ad te, Domine : dicendo in cruce : Eli, Eli, id est, Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me? Et : Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum. Dixi : Tu es spes mea, id est in quo spero, secundum quod homo sum, et aliquo modo viator. Speravit autem Christus in Deo, non per spem quæ est virtus theologica, quæ in comprehensoribus locum non habet, sed per quamdam præstolationem sive fiduciam, qua omne bonum quod nondum habuit, a Deo longanimiter expectavit. Portio mea, id est bonum quod ego requiro, intendo et diligo, est in terra viventium, id est in regno cœlorum. Et potest nomine portionis intelligi Deus, de quo dictum est supra, Dominus pars hereditatis meæ ; vel, retributio gloriæ quæ conferetur electis. Vel sic : Portio mea, id est Ecclesia electorum, quæ est pars mea, ex multis mihi proveniens, electa ac data, in terra viventium, id est, mecum erit in regione paradisi cœlestis, sicut dixi : Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem quam dedisti mihi.
paras.en: [[141:6|I cried to thee, O Lord|Clamavi ad te, Domine]]: saying on the cross, [[Matt 27:46|Eli, Eli|Eli, Eli]], that is, [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?]] And: [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]. [[141:6|I said: Thou art my hope|Dixi : Tu es spes mea]], that is, he in whom I hope, inasmuch as I am man, and in some manner a wayfarer. Now Christ hoped in God, not by the hope that is a theological virtue, which has no place in comprehensors [that is, the blessed who already possess God, as against wayfarers still on the way], but by a certain awaiting or confidence, by which he patiently expected from God every good which he did not yet have. [[141:6|My portion|Portio mea]], that is, the good which I seek, aim at and love, is [[141:6|in the land of the living|in terra viventium]], that is, in the kingdom of heaven. And by the name of portion may be understood God, of whom it was said above, [[Ps 15:5|The Lord is the portion of my inheritance|Dominus pars hereditatis meæ]]; or the reward of glory which will be bestowed on the elect. Or thus: [[141:6|My portion|Portio mea]], that is, the Church of the elect, which is my part, coming to me from many, chosen and given, [[141:6|in the land of the living|in terra viventium]], that is, will be with me in the region of the heavenly paradise, as I said: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory which thou hast given me|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem quam dedisti mihi]].

paras.t: Intende ad deprecationem meam, quia humiliatus, id est contemptus, abjectus, blasphematus, imo turpissima passione afflictus, sum nimis a Judæis : quemadmodum scriptum est, Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo et humiliatum. Libera me, suscitando me tertia die, a persequentibus me, id est Judæis, atque Pilati ministris me crucifigentibus ; quia confortati sunt super me, secundum apparentiam, quia permissi sunt mihi prævalere, quantum ad hoc quod me occidere potuerunt. Interdum enim Christus aliquid dicit, quia sic esse videbatur, quemadmodum apud Jeremiam ait : Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam ; et non cognovi quia super me cogitaverunt consilia.
paras.en: [[141:7|Attend to my supplication: for|Intende ad deprecationem meam, quia]] I am brought low [Latin *humiliatus*, "humbled"], that is, despised, cast off, blasphemed, nay afflicted with a most shameful passion, and that [[141:7|very|sum nimis]] greatly, by the Jews: as it is written, [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God and afflicted|Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo et humiliatum]] [Latin *humiliatum*, "humbled", the word of the verse]. [[141:7|Deliver me|Libera me]], by raising me up on the third day, [[141:7|from my persecutors|a persequentibus me]], that is, from the Jews and the servants of Pilate who crucified me; [[141:7|for they are stronger than I|quia confortati sunt super me]], in appearance, since they were allowed to prevail over me so far as to be able to kill me. For Christ sometimes says a thing because it seemed so, as he says in Jeremias: [[Jer 11:19|I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim: and I knew not that they had devised counsels against me|Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam ; et non cognovi quia super me cogitaverunt consilia]].

paras.t: Educ de custodia, id est de clausura seu carcere limbi infernalis : qui alibi vocatur lacus sine aqua ; animam meam : quæ ibi fuit quousque corpori reunita est ; ad confitendum nomini tuo, id est, ut te laudet novo modo et coram aliis, tam in Ecclesia militanti quam triumphanti, tibique gratias agat de gloria resurrectionis, de eductione patrum ex limbo, de omni præmio accidentali sibi recenter collato. Me exspectant justi existentes in limbo, donec retribuas mihi præmium accidentale quod patiendo promerui, videlicet resurrectionem beatam. Non enim educi potuerunt, donec Christus a morte surrexit. Propterea, quamvis anima Christi in limbum venit ante resurrectionem, exspectabant tamen adventum Christi usque ad horam resurrectionis, in qua suos inde captivos eduxit, prout Zacharias ait : Tu quoque in sanguine testamenti tui eduxisti vinctos tuos de lacu, in quo non est aqua.
paras.en: [[141:8|Bring|Educ]] [[141:8|out of prison|de custodia]], that is, out of the enclosure or gaol of the infernal limbo, which elsewhere is called a pit without water[[Zach 9:11||]], [[141:8|my soul|animam meam]], which was there until it was reunited with the body; [[141:8|that I may praise thy name|ad confitendum nomini tuo]], that is, that it may praise thee in a new manner and before others, in the Church militant as well as in the Church triumphant, and give thee thanks for the glory of the resurrection, for the bringing of the fathers out of limbo, for every accidental reward [that is, joy added to the essential reward of the vision of God] lately bestowed on it. [[141:8|the just wait for me|Me exspectant justi]], those in limbo, [[141:8|until thou reward me|donec retribuas mihi]] with the accidental reward which I merited by suffering, namely a blessed resurrection. For they could not be brought out until Christ rose from the dead. Therefore, although the soul of Christ came into limbo before the resurrection, they still awaited the coming of Christ until the hour of the resurrection, in which he led his captives out of it, as Zacharias says: [[Zach 9:11|Thou also by the blood of thy testament hast sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit, wherein is no water|Tu quoque in sanguine testamenti tui eduxisti vinctos tuos de lacu, in quo non est aqua]].

paras.t: Porro allegorice exponi potest hic psalmus de quolibet fideli, in magnis tribulationibus constituto. Qui dicere potest : Voce mea, id est voce propria, voce interioris hominis, non per intermediam vocem, ad Dominum clamavi, qui solus me eripere potest atque salvare. Sunt autem nonnulli, qui negligunt propria voce clamare ad Dominum, sed aliis dicunt : Ora pro me.
paras.en: Further, this psalm may be expounded allegorically of any one of the faithful set in great tribulations, who can say: [[141:2|with my voice|Voce mea]], that is, with my own voice, the voice of the inner man, not through a voice between, [[141:2|I cried to the Lord|ad Dominum clamavi]], who alone can rescue and save me. For there are some who neglect to cry to the Lord with their own voice, but say to others: Pray for me.

paras.t: Effundo in conspectu ejus, id est eo præsente et attendente, orationem meam : sicut in Threnis dicitur, Effunde sicut aquam cor tuum ante conspectum Domini Dei tui. Et mater Samuelis : Effudi, inquit, animam meam in conspectu Domini. Debemus autem effundere cor nostrum ac preces coram Deo cum omni fiducia, devotione ac perseverantia, sicut coram benignissimo patre, piissimo salvatore, fidelissimo et omnipotenti adjutore : sicque procul dubio suscipiemur ab eo. Et tribulationem meam, quam patior a dæmone, mundo et carne, ante ipsum pronuntio, ut ipse me consoletur et liberet. Dico ergo et conqueror ei quanta sustineo, non ut ipse sciat, sed ut confessio miseriæ meæ ejus misericordiam provocet. Unde supra dictum est : Revela Domino viam tuam, et ipse faciet.
paras.en: [[141:3|In his sight I pour out|Effundo in conspectu ejus]], that is, while he is present and attending, [[141:3|my prayer|orationem meam]]: as it is said in Lamentations, [[Lam 2:19|pour out thy heart like water, before the face of the Lord|Effunde sicut aquam cor tuum ante conspectum Domini]] thy God. And the mother of Samuel: [[1 Kings 1:15|I have poured out|Effudi]], she says, [[1 Kings 1:15|my soul before the Lord|animam meam in conspectu Domini]]. Now we ought to pour out our heart and our prayers before God with all confidence, devotion and perseverance, as before a most kind father, a most loving saviour, a most faithful and almighty helper: and so without doubt we shall be received by him. And [[141:3|my trouble|tribulationem meam]], which I suffer from the devil, the world and the flesh, [[141:3|before him I declare|ante ipsum pronuntio]], that he may comfort and deliver me. I tell him, then, and complain to him of how much I endure, not so that he may know it, but so that the confession of my misery may call forth his mercy. Hence it was said above: [[Ps 36:5|Commit thy way to the Lord|Revela Domino viam tuam]], [[Ps 36:5|and he will do it|et ipse faciet]].

paras.t: In deficiendo ex me spiritum meum, id est, dum anima mea ex sua fragilitate deficeret, cadendo in vitia vel patiendo adversa, nec sufficienter valendo prosequi quæ requiruntur ad obtinendam salutem : dum ita deficeret anima mea, effundo in conspectu tuo orationem meam, et tribulationem meam ante te pronuntio. Vel refertur ad sequentem partem hujus versus, quo dicitur : Et tu cognovisti semitas meas, quidquid ago et patior, quidquid cogito, appeto, loquor aut facio : juxta illud, Respicit Dominus viam hominis, et omnes gressus illius considerat. In via hac qua ambulabam, id est in conversatione qua præcepta Dei custodire disposui, absconderunt hostes animæ meæ laqueum mihi, quærentes me in peccati consensum pertrahere.
paras.en: [[141:4|When my spirit failed me|In deficiendo ex me spiritum meum]], that is, while my soul failed through its own frailty, falling into vices or suffering adversities, and not being strong enough to pursue what is required for obtaining salvation: while my soul thus failed, [[141:3|I pour out|effundo]] [[141:3|my prayer|orationem meam]] in thy sight, and [[141:3|I declare my trouble|tribulationem meam ante te pronuntio]] before thee. Or it is referred to the following part of this verse, where it is said: [[141:4|then thou knewest my paths|Et tu cognovisti semitas meas]], whatever I do and suffer, whatever I think, desire, speak or do: according to that saying, [[Prov 5:21|The Lord beholdeth the ways of man, and considereth all his steps|Respicit Dominus viam hominis, et omnes gressus illius considerat]] [Denis has *viam*, "the way"]. [[141:4|In this way wherein I walked|In via hac qua ambulabam]], that is, in the manner of life in which I resolved to keep the commandments of God, the enemies of my soul [[141:4|have hidden|absconderunt]] [[141:4|a snare for me|laqueum mihi]], seeking to draw me into consent to sin.

paras.t: Considerabam ad dexteram, id est ad eos a quibus speravi me amplius adjuvandum, et videbam, si quis mihi succurreret ; et non erat qui cognosceret me, id est, qui signa dilectionis mihi ostenderet ; sed velut alieni recesserunt a me : sicut Job ait, Fratres mei elongaverunt a me, et noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me. Periit fuga a me : id est, tot laqueis, tot malis atque periculis circumdatus atque repletus sum, quod ea propria potestate evadere nequeo ; et non est qui requirat animam meam, ut eam salvet, nisi tu, Deus meus : non enim est alius qui pugnet pro me. Hæc atque similia dicit afflictus ex vehementi dolore : vel quia simpliciter nullus est qui eum cognoscat, et vitam ejus requirat ; vel quoniam adeo pauci sunt et impotentes, ut pro nihilo reputentur.
paras.en: [[141:5|I looked on my right hand|Considerabam ad dexteram]], that is, to those by whom I hoped to be helped the most, [[141:5|and beheld|et videbam]], whether anyone would succour me; [[141:5|and there was no one that would know me|et non erat qui cognosceret me]], that is, who would show me signs of love; but like strangers they departed from me: as Job says, [[Job 19:13|He hath put my brethren far from me, and my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me|Fratres mei elongaverunt a me, et noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me]] [Denis has "My brethren have gone far from me"]. [[141:5|Flight hath failed me|Periit fuga a me]]: that is, I am surrounded and filled with so many snares, so many evils and dangers, that I cannot escape them by my own power; [[141:5|and there is no one that hath regard to my soul|et non est qui requirat animam meam]], to save it, but thou, my God: for there is no other that fighteth for me. The afflicted man says these and like things out of vehement grief: either because there is simply no one who knows him and has regard for his life, or because they are so few and so powerless that they are counted as nothing.

paras.t: Idcirco, Clamavi ad te, Domine, qui solus potes me liberare ; clamandoque dixi : Tu es spes mea, id est objectum, causa et finis spei meæ ; in te confido, te exspecto, teque finaliter adipisci spero ; portio mea, id est, hereditas mea, præmium meum atque divitiæ sint in terra viventium, sicut tu, Domine, jubes : Thesaurizate, inquiens, vobis thesauros in cœlo.
paras.en: Therefore, [[141:6|I cried to thee, O Lord|Clamavi ad te, Domine]], who alone canst deliver me; and crying [[141:6|I said: Thou art my hope|dixi : Tu es spes mea]], that is, the object, cause and end of my hope; in thee I trust, thee I await, and thee I hope at the last to attain; [[141:6|my portion|portio mea]], that is, may my inheritance, my reward and my riches be [[141:6|in the land of the living|in terra viventium]], as thou, O Lord, dost command, saying: [[Matt 6:20|lay up|Thesaurizate]], he says, [[Matt 6:20|to yourselves treasures in heaven|vobis thesauros in cœlo]].

paras.t: Intende ad deprecationem meam, eam celeriter exaudiendo, quia humiliatus sum nimis, id est, multum afflictus, tentatus, oppressus sum : sed et ego valde humiliavi me ipsum, ut misericordiam invenirem. Unde in Ecclesiastico dicitur : Humilia valde spiritum tuum, quia vindicta carnis impii, ignis et vermis. Libera me a persequentibus me, scilicet invisibilibus ac visibilibus hostibus, quia confortati sunt super me. Non enim resistere possum eorum dolis atque insidiis, nisi per gratiæ tuæ subsidium.
paras.en: [[141:7|Attend to my supplication|Intende ad deprecationem meam]], by hearing it speedily, [[141:7|for I am brought very low|quia humiliatus sum nimis]] [Latin *humiliatus*, "humbled"], that is, I am much afflicted, tempted, oppressed: but I too have greatly humbled myself, that I might find mercy. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 7:19|Humble thy spirit very much: for the vengeance on the flesh of the ungodly is fire and worms|Humilia valde spiritum tuum, quia vindicta carnis impii, ignis et vermis]]. [[141:7|Deliver me from my persecutors|Libera me a persequentibus me]], namely from enemies invisible and visible, [[141:7|for they are stronger than I|quia confortati sunt super me]]. For I cannot resist their wiles and snares except by the help of thy grace.

paras.t: Educ de custodia animam meam. In Hebræo habetur, Educ de carcere. Sensus vero permanet idem, qui talis est : Educ de custodia, id est de isto exsilio, de corpore mortis hujus, de valle hac lacrimarum, animam meam, transferendo eam de via ad patriam, ad confitendum nomini tuo, confessione incessabilis hymni cum Sanctis in regno cœlesti. Hoc dicere pertinet ad perfectos qui bona conscientia cupiunt dissolvi et esse cum Christo. Ceteri vero dicere possunt : Educ de custodia animam meam quotidie per vitam spiritualem, per contemplationem cœlestium, per desiderium æternorum, ut anima mea carnem transcendat, mundum relinquat, in cœlis conversationem habere laboret; sicque ad illos pertineat quibus ait Apostolus : Vos autem in carne non estis, sed in spiritu ; et, Nos revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes.
paras.en: [[141:8|Bring my soul out of prison|Educ de custodia animam meam]]. In the Hebrew it reads, Bring out of the gaol [Latin *carcere*]. But the sense remains the same, which is this: [[141:8|Bring|Educ]] [[141:8|out of prison|de custodia]], that is, out of this exile, out of [[Rom 7:24|the body of this death|corpore mortis hujus]], out of this valley of tears, [[141:8|my soul|animam meam]], carrying it over from the way to the fatherland, [[141:8|that I may praise thy name|ad confitendum nomini tuo]], by the praise of an unceasing hymn with the Saints in the kingdom of heaven. To say this belongs to the perfect, who with a good conscience desire [[Phil 1:23|to be dissolved and to be with Christ|dissolvi et esse cum Christo]]. But the rest can say: Bring my soul out of prison daily, by the spiritual life, by the contemplation of heavenly things, by the desire of things eternal, that my soul may rise above the flesh, leave the world, and strive to have its conversation in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]] [the margin gives "Ibid. iii, 20" after Rom. vii, 24; the passage is Phil 3:20]; and so may belong to those to whom the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:9|But you are not in the flesh, but the spirit|Vos autem in carne non estis, sed in spiritu]]; and, [[2 Cor 3:18|beholding the glory of the Lord with open face|revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes]].

paras.t: Me exspectant justi in patria, quatenus me in suam recipiant domum, societatem et gloriam, donec retribuas mihi vitam æternam pro mercede obsequii tibi impensi ; videlicet usque ad horam mortis meæ, vel usque ad horam eductionis de purgatorio, vel usque ad diem universalis judicii, quo electi anima et corpore præmiabuntur. Cum magno desiderio præstolantur Beati nostrum adventum, tanquam vere amantes nos : propter quod merito festinaremus occurrere eis, et eorum jucundissimæ societati uniri, ne nobis dicatur illud : Usquequo marcetis ignavia, et non intratis ad possidendam terram quam Dominus dedit vobis?
paras.en: [[141:8|the just wait for me|Me exspectant justi]] in the fatherland, to receive me into their house, their company and their glory, [[141:8|until thou reward me|donec retribuas mihi]] with eternal life as the wage of the service rendered to thee; that is, until the hour of my death, or until the hour of my being brought out of purgatory, or until the day of the general judgement, on which the elect will be rewarded in soul and body. With great desire the Blessed await our coming, as those who truly love us: for which reason we should rightly hasten to go to meet them and to be united to their most delightful company, lest that word be said to us: [[Jos 18:3|How long are you indolent and slack, and go not in to possess the land which the Lord the God of your fathers hath given you?|Usquequo marcetis ignavia, et non intratis ad possidendam terram quam Dominus dedit vobis?]] [Denis omits "the God of your fathers"]

paras.t: Psalmum istum ignitis affectibus redolentem, et fervidis precibus plenum, decet nos corde devotissimo decantare, et quasi proprii cordis affectu omnia verba ejus formare.
paras.en: This psalm, fragrant with fiery affections and full of fervent prayers, it befits us to sing with a most devout heart, and to form all its words as if with the affection of our own heart.

paras.t: PRECATIO. In via præsentis vitæ, qua ambulamus, Domine, laqueos hostium absconditos fac nos declinare : ut nos persequentes non prævaleant, sed procul a nobis, te jubente, recedant.
paras.en: Prayer. In the way of this present life in which we walk, O Lord, make us avoid the hidden snares of our enemies: that those who persecute us may not prevail, but at thy command may depart far from us.

142.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUADRAGESIMI SECUNDI : DOMINE, EXAUDI ORATIONEM MEAM.
142.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and forty-second psalm: Hear, O Lord, my prayer.

paras.t: Habet hic psalmus nunc exponendus, pro titulo : Psalmus David, quando persequebatur eum filius suus Absalon. Ad litteram enim edidit David hunc psalmum, dum fugeret a facie Absalon filii sui. De qua persecutione habetur in secundo libro Regum. Et quamvis littera psalmi hujus possit applicari ad hoc, sicut et breviter tangetur, aptius tamen est ut exponatur hic psalmus in persona cujuslibet pœnitentis.
paras.en: This psalm, now to be expounded, has for its title: [[142:1|A psalm of David, when his son Absalom pursued him|Psalmus David, quando persequebatur eum filius suus Absalon]]. For literally David composed this psalm while he was fleeing from the face of Absalom his son; of which persecution we read in the second book of Kings[[2 Kings 15:1||]] [the margin gives II Reg. xv–xviii]. And although the letter of this psalm can be applied to this, as will also be touched on briefly, it is more fitting that this psalm be expounded in the person of any penitent.

paras.t: Adloquens igitur David in persona pœnitentis, ait : Domine, exaudi orationem meam; auribus tuæ immensæ pietatis percipe obsecrationem meam. Aures Dei aliud non sunt, nisi misericordia et sapientia ejus, sicut frequenter inductum est. Sæpe autem loquitur Scriptura de Deo more humano. Dicitur ergo Deus auribus percipere, non quod aliquid de novo cognoscat, sed quia gratiam largiendo, ostendit se scire atque attendere preces nostras.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of a penitent, David says: [[142:1|Hear, O Lord, my prayer|Domine, exaudi orationem meam]]; with the ears of thy boundless loving-kindness [[142:1|give ear to my supplication|percipe obsecrationem meam]]. The ears of God are nothing other than his mercy and his wisdom, as has often been set out. For Scripture often speaks of God after the manner of men. God is said, then, to give ear, not because he comes to know anything anew, but because in bestowing grace he shows that he knows and attends to our prayers.

paras.t: Quamvis autem inter orationem et obsecrationem possit poni distinctio, quoniam obsecratio proprie dicitur, dum aliquid postulamus a Deo per aliquod sacrum, sicut quum dicimus, Per nativitatem tuam libera nos, Domine ; vel, Propter misericordiam seu bonitatem tuam exaudi me, Domine : tamen hoc loco accipi possunt pro eodem.
