In cujus exordio Deum pro suis beneficiis devote laudamus, eumque nominibus amorosis exprimimus, appellantes eum, Misericordiam nostram, et Refugium nostrum, etc., quæ sunt verba affectuosissima: quæ nullatenus proferre debemus, nisi ardenti affectu. Docet nos etiam psalmus iste veram atque præcipuam humilitatem, dum hominem divina illuminatione indignum, vanitatique similem et tanquam umbram præterire testatur. Multaque alia tanguntur et edocentur in psalmo hoc ipso.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm truly glorious and splendid: a psalm full of praises and shining with moral teaching. At its beginning we devoutly praise God for his benefits and express him by loving names, calling him our Mercy and our Refuge, etc., which are most affectionate words, and which we ought never to utter except with burning affection. This psalm also teaches us true and principal humility, when it testifies that man is unworthy of the divine illumination, like to vanity, and passes away like a shadow. And many other things are touched on and taught in this very psalm.

paras.t: Emitte, quæsumus, Domine, manum tuam de alto cælorum, et erue nos de manu visibilium et invisibilium inimicorum et de omnibus periculis malorum: ut cunctis sopitis adversitatibus, canticum victoriæ tibi Domino Deo exsultantes cantemus.
paras.en: Prayer. Put forth, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy hand from the height of the heavens, and rescue us from the hand of our enemies visible and invisible, and from all the perils of evils: that, all adversities being laid to rest, we may sing with exultation the canticle of victory to thee, the Lord God.

144.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUADRAGESIMI QUARTI : EXALTABO TE, DEUS MEUS REX.
144.title_en: Elucidation of the hundred and forty-fourth psalm: I will extol thee, O God my king.

paras.t: Explanandi nunc psalmi iste est titulus : Laudatio ipsi David : id est, psalmus iste qui dicitur laudatio, quoniam totus pertinet ad Dei præconium, convenit seu attribuitur ipsi David prophetæ tanquam auctori, Christo autem significato per David, sicut objecto quod laudatur. Christus namque seu tota supersancta Trinitas, in psalmo præsenti pulcherrime collaudatur. Unde etiam huic psalmo pro titulo appropriatur laudatio Dei, quamvis in aliis multis psalmis Deus laudetur. Est autem hic psalmus mirabiliter delectabilis et suavis, pulcher et sententiosus.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is this: [[144:1|Praise, for David himself|Laudatio ipsi David]]: that is, this psalm, which is called a praise because it belongs wholly to the proclaiming of God, befits or is ascribed to David himself, the prophet, as to its author, but to Christ, signified by David, as to the object that is praised. For Christ, or rather the whole most holy Trinity, is most beautifully praised in the present psalm. Hence too *the praise of God* is given to this psalm as its own title, although God is praised in many other psalms. And this psalm is wonderfully delightful and sweet, beautiful and full of meaning.

paras.t: In persona ergo Ecclesiæ seu fidelis Deum laudantis, loquens Propheta, ita exorsus est : Exaltabo te, Deus meus rex. Quum Deus in summo sit, imo altissimus et infinitus exsistat, quomodo valet ab homine exaltari ? Numquid creatura aliquid poterit conferre aut addere Creatori ? Non utique ; sed ita dicimur Deum exaltare, quomodo dicimus eum magnificare, glorificare et sanctificare, videlicet quoniam ejus magnitudinem, gloriam, sanctitatem agnoscimus, profitemur, prædicamus et veneramur. Itaque, Exaltabo, id est, sublimiter laudabo, reverentialiter colam, magnifice prædicabo, et cunctis incomparabiliter præferam, te, Domine, Deus meus rex : qui es omnium Dominus per generalem præsidentiam, Deus meus per singularem devotionem, et rex meus per indesinentem et gratiosissimam providentiam. Et benedicam nomini tuo, id est tibi, benedictione gratiarum actionis et laudis, non benedictione consecrationis, in sæculum et in sæculum sæculi, id est indesinenter, scilicet in via atque in patria. Quemadmodum enim caritas nunquam excidit, secundum Apostolum : sic benedictio seu Dei laudatio nunquam cessat ; imo jam inchoatur, et in futuro perficitur.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of the Church, or of a faithful soul praising God, the Prophet begins thus: [[144:1|I will extol thee, O God my king|Exaltabo te, Deus meus rex]]. Since God is in the highest, nay, is most high and infinite, how can He be extolled by man? Can a creature confer or add anything to the Creator? Surely not; but we are said to extol God in the way that we are said to magnify, glorify and hallow Him: namely because we acknowledge, profess, proclaim and venerate His greatness, glory and holiness. And so, [[144:1|I will extol|Exaltabo]], that is, I will praise loftily, worship reverently, proclaim magnificently, and set above all things beyond compare, [[144:1|thee|te]], O Lord, [[144:1|O God my king|Deus meus rex]]: who art Lord of all by Thy universal rule, my God by singular devotion, and my king by Thy unceasing and most gracious providence. [[144:1|And I will bless thy name|Et benedicam nomini tuo]], that is, Thee, with the blessing of thanksgiving and praise, not with the blessing of consecration, [[144:1|for ever; yea, for ever and ever|in sæculum et in sæculum sæculi]], that is, unceasingly, namely on the way and in the fatherland. For as [[1 Cor 13:8|charity never falleth away|caritas nunquam excidit]], according to the Apostle, so the blessing or praise of God never ceases; rather, it is begun now and is perfected in the world to come.

paras.t: Per singulos dies, id est quotidie, imo die ac nocte, videlicet per singulos dies naturales, qui noctem includunt, benedicam tibi in adversis et prosperis, in omni eventu, pro beneficiis quæ mihi aut aliis contulisti ; et de omni bono quod fieri video aut percipio, tibi benedicturus sum, a quo omne bonum procedit. Et laudabo nomen tuum in sæculum, et in sæculum sæculi : quemadmodum et alibi scriptum est, Laudabit usque ad mortem anima mea Dominum. Ecce quam sanctum ac bonum propositum. Asserit Propheta se die et nocte jugiter atque perpetue Domino benedicturum. Nos ergo agamus quod psallimus, impleamus quod dicimus, persequamur quod proponimus ; Deum exaltemus, benedicamus, laudemus ubique et semper. Si spernimur, si tentamur, si reprobamur, et quidquid nobis acciderit, non recedat a corde, non cesset ab ore divina laudatio, gratiarum actio, benedictio ; non frangatur animi fortitudo, nec desistat mentis ad Deum erectio ; non fatigetur patientia, neque deficiat tranquillitas interna.
paras.en: [[144:2|Every day|Per singulos dies]], that is, daily, nay, day and night, namely through each natural day, which includes the night, [[144:2|will I bless thee|benedicam tibi]] in adversity and prosperity, in every event, for the benefits Thou hast bestowed on me or on others; and for every good that I see done or perceive, I will bless Thee, from whom every good proceeds. [[144:2|and I will praise thy name for ever; yea, for ever and ever|Et laudabo nomen tuum in sæculum, et in sæculum sæculi]]: as it is written elsewhere also, [[Ecclus 51:8|My soul shall praise the Lord even to death|Laudabit usque ad mortem anima mea Dominum]] [the margin gives Ecclus. ii, 8; the words are Ecclus 51:8]. See how holy and good a resolve! The Prophet declares that he will bless the Lord day and night, continually and for ever. Let us then do what we sing, fulfil what we say, carry out what we resolve; let us extol, bless and praise God everywhere and always. If we are scorned, if we are tempted, if we are rejected, and whatever befalls us, let not the praise of God, thanksgiving and blessing depart from the heart or cease from the mouth; let not the strength of the soul be broken, nor the mind's lifting up to God give way; let not patience grow weary, nor inward tranquillity fail.

paras.t: Deinde subjungitur ratio, cur Deus taliter benedicendus atque laudandus sit. Magnus Dominus, non magnitudine molis, sed perfectionis. In omni enim perfectione summus consistit. Propter quod alio loco dictum est : Magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine. Quis non timebit te, o Rex gentium ? Et laudabilis nimis. In tantum namque laudabilis est Deus omnipotens, quantum bonus exsistit. Unde, sicut bonitas ejus omnium creaturarum bonitatem incomparabiliter vincit atque transcendit, sic incomparabiliter laudabilior, majorque laude dignus est, quam ab aliqua creatura possit laudari. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico legitur : Magnus Dominus vehementer. Glorificate eum quantumcumque poteritis, supervalebit adhuc : major est enim omni laude. Et magnitudinis ejus non est finis. Divina enim essentia, divina potentia, divina sapientia, omnisque perfectio Dei, vere et absolute seu intensive infinita est, ita quod totum universum est velut minutissima arena, respectu majestatis divinæ. Idcirco cum omni reverentia, cum omni diligentia, cum omni affectu ministrandum est Domino tam excelso. Hinc quoque verissime dictum est, quod Deus est ante omnia non solus, post omnia non præventus, supra omnia non elatus, infra omnia non oppressus, intra omnia non inclusus, extra omnia non exclusus ; manens in sua superessentiali simplicitate, æternaliter, incircumscriptibiliterque subsistens ; et ejus lætitia, ejus dulcedo et pax, ejusque felicitas omnino et omnimode est immensa.
paras.en: Then is added the reason why God is to be so blessed and praised. [[144:3|Great is the Lord|Magnus Dominus]]: not with a greatness of bulk, but of perfection. For He is supreme in every perfection. That is why it is said in another place: [[Jer 10:6|thou art great, and great is thy name in might|Magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine]]. [[Jer 10:7|Who shall not fear thee, O king of nations?|Quis non timebit te, o Rex gentium?]] [[144:3|And greatly to be praised|Et laudabilis nimis]]. For almighty God is as worthy of praise as He is good. Hence, as His goodness surpasses and transcends beyond compare the goodness of all creatures, so He is beyond compare more praiseworthy, and worthy of greater praise than any creature could give Him. That is why we read in Ecclesiasticus: The Lord is [[Ecclus 43:31|exceeding great|Magnus Dominus vehementer]]. [[Ecclus 43:32|Glorify the Lord as much as ever you can, for he will yet far exceed|Glorificate eum quantumcumque poteritis, supervalebit adhuc]]: [[Ecclus 43:33|for he is above all praise|major est enim omni laude]]. [[144:3|And of his greatness there is no end|Et magnitudinis ejus non est finis]]. For the divine essence, the divine power, the divine wisdom, and every perfection of God is truly and absolutely, that is, intensively, infinite, so that the whole universe is as the smallest grain of sand compared with the divine majesty[[Is 40:15||]] [the margin gives Is. x, 15; the image is that of Is 40:15, compare Wis 11:23]. Therefore the Lord, so exalted, is to be served with all reverence, all diligence and all affection. Hence too it is most truly said that God is before all things, not alone; after all things, not forestalled; above all things, not lifted up; beneath all things, not weighed down; within all things, not shut in; outside all things, not shut out; abiding in His superessential simplicity, subsisting eternally and without bounds; and His joy, His sweetness and peace, and His happiness are altogether and in every way immeasurable.

paras.t: Generatio et generatio, id est quælibet fidelium natio seu congregatio, laudabit opera tua, videlicet opera naturæ, opera gratiæ, opera gloriæ. Quis enim non laudet gubernationem mundi, motum cœli, vicissitudinem temporum, ordinem specierum ? Et cetera opera sapientissimi Creatoris omni laude dignissima sunt : sic tamen, ut Deus in eis laudetur, lausque eorum ad præconium Creatoris referatur. Universa equidem propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus, et cuncta fecit Deus ut timeatur. Et potentiam tuam pronuntiabunt, id est, divinam potestatem prædicabunt, teque omnipotentem esse dicent, commemorantes illud Machabæorum : Deus potest universum mundum uno nutu delere.
paras.en: [[144:4|Generation and generation|Generatio et generatio]], that is, every nation or gathering of the faithful, [[144:4|shall praise thy works|laudabit opera tua]], namely the works of nature, the works of grace, the works of glory. For who would not praise the governance of the world, the motion of the heavens, the succession of the seasons, the order of species? And the other works of the most wise Creator are most worthy of all praise: yet so that God be praised in them, and their praise be referred to the glory of the Creator. For [[Prov 16:4|The Lord hath made all things for himself|Universa equidem propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus]], and all things [[Eccles 3:14|God hath made that he may be feared|fecit Deus ut timeatur]]. [[144:4|And they shall declare thy power|Et potentiam tuam pronuntiabunt]], that is, they shall proclaim the divine power and say that Thou art almighty, recalling the words of the Machabees: God [[2 Mach 8:18|at a beck can utterly destroy|uno nutu delere]] [[2 Mach 8:18|the whole world|universum mundum]].

paras.t: Magnificentiam, id est magnam efficientiam seu magnificam exsistentiam, gloriæ, id est gloriosi effectus (vel, Gloriæ, id est excellentiæ seu claræ notitiæ), sanctitatis tuæ, id est tui ipsius qui Sanctus Sanctorum es, loquentur, dicentes : Non est Deus, ut Deus rectissimus ; magnificentia ejus discurrunt nubes. Illud Job quoque : Quum vix parvam stillam sermonum ejus audierimus, quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis ejus intueri ? Et item illud : Benedicta gloria Domini de loco suo. Et mirabilia tua, id est opera supernaturalia, seu naturalia humanæ rationis investigationem excedentia, narrabunt. Sic enim Evangelistæ in Evangeliis narrant mirabilia opera Christi. Unde ab Ecclesiastico inducitur : Nonne Dominus fecit Sanctos enarrare omnia mirabilia sua, quæ confirmavit Dominus omnipotens, stabilis in gloria sua ?
paras.en: Of [[144:5|the magnificence|Magnificentiam]], that is, the great working or magnificent existence, [[144:5|of the glory|gloriæ]], that is, of the glorious effect (or, *of the glory*, that is, of the excellence or bright knowledge), [[144:5|of thy holiness|sanctitatis tuæ]], that is, of Thyself, who art the Holy of Holies, [[144:5|They shall speak|loquentur]], saying: [[Deut 33:26|There is no other god like the God of the rightest|Non est Deus, ut Deus rectissimus]]; [[Deut 33:26|By his magnificence the clouds run hither and thither|magnificentia ejus discurrunt nubes]] [the margin gives Deut. xxxii, 26; the words are Deut 33:26]. And that of Job too: [[Job 26:14|seeing we have heard scarce a little drop of his word, who shall be able to behold the thunder of his greatness?|Quum vix parvam stillam sermonum ejus audierimus, quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis ejus intueri]] And again that: [[Ezech 3:12|Blessed be the glory of the Lord, from his place|Benedicta gloria Domini de loco suo]]. And [[144:5|thy wondrous works|Et mirabilia tua]], that is, works above nature, or natural works that pass the searching of human reason, [[144:5|shall tell|narrabunt]]. For so the Evangelists in the Gospels tell the wonderful works of Christ. Hence Ecclesiasticus brings in: [[Ecclus 42:17|Hath not the Lord made the saints to declare all his wonderful works, which the Lord Almighty hath firmly settled to be established for his glory?|Nonne Dominus fecit Sanctos enarrare omnia mirabilia sua, quæ confirmavit Dominus omnipotens, stabilis in gloria sua]] [the margin gives Ecclus. xliii, 17; the words are Ecclus 42:17]

paras.t: Et virtutem, id est potentiam, terribilium tuorum, videlicet justorum judiciorum, ac districtissimarum ultionum, dicent, recolendo futurum judicium, inferique tormentum ; et magnitudinem tuam, id est magnam tuam perfectionem, narrabunt : ut te collaudent, aliosque informent.
paras.en: And [[144:6|the might|Et virtutem]], that is, the power, [[144:6|of thy terrible acts|terribilium tuorum]], namely of Thy just judgments and most strict vengeances, [[144:6|they shall speak|dicent]], calling to mind the judgment to come and the torment of hell; and [[144:6|thy greatness|et magnitudinem tuam]], that is, Thy great perfection, [[144:6|shall declare|narrabunt]], so as to praise Thee and instruct others.

paras.t: Memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis tuæ eructabunt, id est, recordationem copiosæ dulcedinis tuæ ex cordis plenitudine et experientia proferent atque effundent. Ructus enim non nisi de plenitudine fluit. Sancti igitur, qui ex singulari gratia Salvatoris introduci merentur in cellam vinariam : quibus Sapientia ait, Comedite, amici, et bibite, et inebriamini, carissimi ; dum isti de secreto contemplationis divinæ et consolationis internæ, in quo gustaverunt quam suavis est Dominus, egrediuntur, memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis Dei eructant, clamantes illud quod dictum est ante : Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine ! et illud Sapientiæ : O quam bonus et suavis est, Domine, spiritus tuus in omnibus ! De istis enim per Isaiam Dominus ait : Ecce ego declinabo in eos ut flumen pacis. Hæc autem perfectio seu eructatio, secundum Gregorium, maxime convenire debet prælatis, quos oportet præ cunctis contemplatione esse suspensos, et actione præcipuos, quatenus gregi sibi commisso semper aliquid salubre eructent, eosque ad divinæ suavitatis gustum alliciant.
paras.en: [[144:7|They shall publish the memory of the abundance of thy sweetness|Memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis tuæ eructabunt]] [*eructabunt*, literally "they shall belch forth", "utter abundantly"], that is, they shall bring forth and pour out the remembrance of Thy plentiful sweetness from the fullness and experience of the heart. For belching flows only from fullness. The saints, then, who by the singular grace of the Saviour are found worthy to be brought into [[Cant 2:4|the cellar of wine|cellam vinariam]], to whom Wisdom says: [[Cant 5:1|eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved|Comedite, amici, et bibite, et inebriamini, carissimi]]: when they come forth from the secret place of divine contemplation and inward consolation, in which they have tasted how [[Ps 33:9|the Lord is sweet|suavis est Dominus]], they publish the memory of the abundance of God's sweetness, crying out what was said before: [[Ps 30:20|O how great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord|Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine]]! and that of Wisdom: [[Wis 12:1|O how good and sweet is thy Spirit, O Lord, in all things!|O quam bonus et suavis est, Domine, spiritus tuus in omnibus]] For of these the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 66:12|Behold I will bring upon her as it were a river of peace|Ecce ego declinabo in eos ut flumen pacis]] [Denis has *in eos*, "upon them"; the Vulgate has "upon her"]. Now this perfection or outpouring, according to Gregory, should belong above all to prelates, who ought to be raised up in contemplation and foremost in action beyond all others, so that they may always pour forth something wholesome to the flock committed to them, and draw them to the taste of the divine sweetness.

paras.t: Et justitia tua exsultabunt, id est, in tua æquitate divina seu justa vindicta spiritualiter lætabuntur, quemadmodum supra dictum est : Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam. De hoc enim quod Dominus justus est, et omnia juste disponit, singulisque sine personarum acceptione quod merentur largitur, gaudent electi et sancti : imo mallent se ipsos non esse seu perire, quam ita non esse, eo quod Deum plus ament quam se. Propterea superius habetur : Videbunt justi et lætabuntur, videlicet de sublatione impiorum.
paras.en: [[144:7|and shall rejoice in thy justice|Et justitia tua exsultabunt]], that is, they shall rejoice spiritually in Thy divine equity or just vengeance, as was said above: [[Ps 57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam]]. For the elect and the saints rejoice that the Lord is just, and [[Wis 12:15|thou art just, thou orderest all things justly|Dominus justus est, et omnia juste disponit]] [the margin gives Sap. xii, 13; the words are Wis 12:15], and gives each one what he deserves without respect of persons: nay, they would rather not be themselves, or perish, than that it should not be so, because they love God more than themselves. That is why we have above: [[Ps 106:42|The just shall see, and shall rejoice|Videbunt justi et lætabuntur]], namely at the taking away of the wicked.

paras.t: Miserator in opere et misericors in natura est Dominus ; patiens, longanimiter expectando, juxta illud, Omnipotens est patiens redditor ; et multum, id est inæstimabiliter, misericors : imo infinitæ misericordiæ est Deus, quum ei sit proprium misereri et parcere. Abundantia enim pietatis suæ et merita supplicum excedit et vota. Ideo Moyses dixit : Dominator Domine, misericors et clemens, patiens et multæ misericordiæ et verax. Apostolus quoque : Deus, inquit, qui dives est in misericordia, etc.
paras.en: [[144:8|The Lord is gracious|Miserator]] in His work [[144:8|and merciful|et misericors]] in His nature; [[144:8|patient|patiens]], waiting long-sufferingly, according to that saying: The Almighty [[Ecclus 5:4|is a patient rewarder|est patiens redditor]] [no margin reference; the words are Ecclus 5:4, where the Vulgate reads "the most High" for Denis's "the Almighty"]; [[144:8|and plenteous in mercy|et multum misericors]], that is, beyond reckoning: nay, God is of infinite mercy, since it is proper to Him to have mercy and to spare. For the abundance of His loving kindness exceeds both the merits and the desires of those who pray to Him. Therefore Moses said: [[Ex 34:6|O the Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient and of much compassion, and true|Dominator Domine, misericors et clemens, patiens et multæ misericordiæ et verax]]. The Apostle also: [[Eph 2:4|God (who is rich in mercy)|Deus, inquit, qui dives est in misericordia]], he says, etc.

paras.t: Suavis Dominus universis. Numquid reprobis in inferno Deus suavis est, qui præ dolore et vulneribus linguas suas manducant, mortem desiderant, Deumque blasphemant, sicut in Apocalypsi ait Joannes ? Et respondendum, quod Deus, quantum in se est, omnibus exstat suavis. Denique universis dicitur Deus esse suavis, quantum ad naturalem appetitum eorum. Sic enim dat omnibus esse et vivere, cunctisque providet, et necessaria tribuit. Quod autem quibusdam (teste Apostolo) severus esse censetur, contingit ex corruptione et vitio appetitus, sicut et febricitanti dulcia videntur amara. Unde, secundum Philosophum, omnium rerum naturalia desideria tendunt ad primum principium, quatenus ab eo gubernentur et conserventur. Hinc etiam Sapientia dicitur omnia disponere suaviter, id est secundum naturalem inclinationem eorum, nisi obicem ponant. Propter culpam namque disponuntur amaritudinaliter, juxta illud : Cor nequam gravabitur doloribus, et cor durum male habebit in novissimo.
paras.en: [[144:9|The Lord is sweet to all|Suavis Dominus universis]]. Is God sweet to the reprobate in hell, who for pain and wounds gnaw their tongues[[Apoc 16:10||]], desire death[[Apoc 9:6||]], and blaspheme God[[Apoc 16:11||]], as John says in the Apocalypse? It must be answered that God, as far as lies in Him, is sweet to all. Moreover God is said to be sweet to all as regards their natural appetite. For thus He gives to all being and life, provides for all, and bestows what is needful. That He is held to be severe to some (as the Apostle witnesses)[[Rom 11:22||]] comes from the corruption and vice of the appetite, as to one in a fever sweet things seem bitter. Hence, according to the Philosopher, the natural desires of all things tend to the first principle, that they may be governed and preserved by it. Hence too Wisdom is said to order [[Wis 8:1|all things sweetly|omnia disponere suaviter]], that is, according to their natural inclination, unless they put an obstacle in the way. For because of sin they are ordered bitterly, according to that saying: [[Ecclus 3:29|A wicked heart shall be laden with sorrows|Cor nequam gravabitur doloribus]], and [[Ecclus 3:27|A hard heart shall fear evil at the last|cor durum male habebit in novissimo]].

paras.t: Et miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus. Quum multi sint vocati seu reprobi, pauci vero electi ; in reprobis autem præcipue in inferno existentibus, magis appareat justitia quam misericordia Dei (nam licet in omni effectu divino misceantur misericordia et justitia, tamen in damnatis justitia eminet, maxime quum de impio dictum sit, Obliviscatur ejus misericordia) : quæri potest, quomodo miserationes Dei sunt super omnia opera ejus. Et respondendum, quod istud dupliciter intelligi potest. Primo sic : Miserationes ejus, id est divinæ pietatis effectus, super omnia opera ejus, id est, ad omnem se creaturam extendunt, omnibus communicantur et insunt. Hoc autem simpliciter et generaliter verum est. Nil enim divinæ bonitatis participatione expers consistit : sed effusio liberalitatis divinæ ad omnia venit, quantum ad naturalia dona ; in damnatis etiam miseris invenitur, dum citra condignum torquentur. Hinc Christus testatur : Eritis filii Altissimi, quia ipse benignus est super ingratos et malos ; quia solem suum facit oriri super bonos et malos, et pluit super justos et injustos. Secundo intelligitur sic : Miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus : id est, effectus divinæ misericordiæ, majores et evidentiores sunt ceteris Dei operibus, utpote quod plus abundant in creaturis, quam effectus divinæ justitiæ, juxta illud Jacobi : Superexaltat misericordia judicium. Si autem hoc modo intelligatur, non videtur verum esse, nisi quantum ad viatores. Si enim justi sunt, hoc per solam gratiam et misericordiam Dei habent : si vero injusti sunt, per misericordiam tolerantur ; et quamdiu expectantur a Deo, miseratio Dei in eis præfulget.
paras.en: [[144:9|and his tender mercies are over all his works|Et miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus]]. Since [[Matt 20:16|many are called|multi sint vocati]], that is, the reprobate, but [[Matt 20:16|few chosen|pauci vero electi]], and in the reprobate, above all those who are in hell, God's justice appears more than His mercy (for although mercy and justice are mingled in every divine effect, yet in the damned justice stands out, especially since it is said of the wicked man: [[Job 24:20|Let mercy forget him|Obliviscatur ejus misericordia]]), it may be asked how God's tender mercies are over all His works. It must be answered that this can be understood in two ways. First thus: [[144:9|his tender mercies|Miserationes ejus]], that is, the effects of the divine loving kindness, [[144:9|are over all his works|super omnia opera ejus]], that is, extend themselves to every creature, are shared with all and are in all. And this is true simply and universally. For nothing is without a share in the divine goodness: but the outpouring of the divine liberality reaches all things as to natural gifts; it is found even in the wretched damned, inasmuch as they are tormented less than they deserve. Hence Christ testifies: [[Luke 6:35|you shall be the sons of the Highest. For he is kind to the unthankful and to the evil|Eritis filii Altissimi, quia ipse benignus est super ingratos et malos]]; for He [[Matt 5:45|maketh his sun to rise upon the good, and bad, and raineth upon the just and the unjust|solem suum facit oriri super bonos et malos, et pluit super justos et injustos]]. Secondly it is understood thus: *His tender mercies are over all his works*: that is, the effects of the divine mercy are greater and more evident than God's other works, inasmuch as they abound more in creatures than the effects of the divine justice, according to that saying of James: [[Jas 2:13|mercy exalteth itself above judgment|Superexaltat misericordia judicium]]. But if it is understood in this way, it does not seem to be true except as regards wayfarers [that is, those still in this life, on the way to the fatherland]. For if they are just, they have this by the grace and mercy of God alone; and if they are unjust, they are borne with by mercy; and as long as they are waited for by God, God's mercy shines forth in them.

paras.t: Insuper sanctus Propheta seu quilibet justus, zelo zelans pro Domino exercituum, ejusque honorem vehementer affectans, invitat universa creata ad laudem Dei, dicendo : Confiteantur confessione laudis tibi, Domine, omnia opera tua, id est cuncta creata, visibilia et invisibilia, spiritualia et corporalia, animata et inanimata, rationalia et irrationalia. Rationales autem seu intellectuales creaturæ confitentur Domino creatori directe et cognitive. Cetera vero non nisi materialiter, secundario seu indirecte, in quantum occasionem præbent intellectualibus creaturis confitendi Domino. Relucet quippe in ipsis bonitas, sapientia, atque potentia Dei : sicque ex consideratione eorum inducitur homo ad summi Opificis laudem. Et hoc modo dicuntur Deum laudare, benedicere, timere, et similes actus vitales habere. Et sancti tui, id est homines virtuosi et perfecti, quales fuerunt Apostoli, et successores eorum, benedicant tibi, te in omnibus, tam in te ipso quam in operibus tuis, laudando.
paras.en: Further, the holy Prophet, or any just man, zealous with zeal for the Lord of hosts[[3 Kings 19:10||]] and vehemently desiring His honour, invites all created things to the praise of God, saying: [[144:10|Let all thy works, O Lord, praise thee|Confiteantur confessione laudis tibi, Domine, omnia opera tua]], that is, let them confess Thee with the confession of praise [*confiteantur*, "let them confess", here rendered "praise"]; *all thy works*, that is, all created things, visible and invisible, spiritual and bodily, animate and inanimate, rational and irrational. Now rational or intellectual creatures confess the Lord their Creator directly and knowingly; the others only materially, secondarily or indirectly, inasmuch as they give intellectual creatures occasion to confess the Lord. For the goodness, wisdom and power of God shine out in them, and so by considering them man is led to the praise of the supreme Maker. And in this way they are said to praise God, to bless Him, to fear Him, and to have like acts of life. [[144:10|and let thy saints|Et sancti tui]], that is, virtuous and perfect men, such as were the Apostles and their successors, [[144:10|bless thee|benedicant tibi]], praising Thee in all things, both in Thyself and in Thy works.

paras.t: Gloriam regni tui dicent, id est, excellentiam et beatitudinem regni cœlestis prædicabunt. Hoc fecerunt Apostoli, quibus Christus dixit : Euntes prædicate, dicentes, Quia appropinquavit regnum cœlorum. Hoc fecit Paulus : Non sunt, inquiens, condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis. Unde et Petrus in sua Canonica loquitur : Videntes Jesum Christum, exsultabitis lætitia inenarrabili et glorificata. Istud quoque quotidie faciunt boni prælati et prædicatores devoti. Et potentiam tuam loquentur, dicentes : Quia non erit impossibile apud Deum omne verbum.
paras.en: [[144:11|They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom|Gloriam regni tui dicent]], that is, they shall proclaim the excellence and blessedness of the heavenly kingdom. This the Apostles did, to whom Christ said: [[Matt 10:7|going, preach, saying: The kingdom of heaven is at hand|Euntes prædicate, dicentes, Quia appropinquavit regnum cœlorum]]. This Paul did, saying: [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us|Non sunt, inquiens, condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis]]. Hence Peter too says in his Canonical Epistle: Seeing Jesus Christ, you [[1 Pet 1:8|shall rejoice with joy unspeakable and glorified|exsultabitis lætitia inenarrabili et glorificata]] [Denis reads *Videntes*, "seeing"; the Vulgate has "though you see him not"]. This too good prelates and devout preachers do daily. [[144:11|and shall tell of thy power|Et potentiam tuam loquentur]], saying: [[Luke 1:37|Because no word shall be impossible with God|Quia non erit impossibile apud Deum omne verbum]].

paras.t: Ut notam faciant filiis hominum, scilicet fratribus et proximis suis, potentiam tuam : cui nullus resistere potest ; cujus in ditione cuncta sunt posita ; quæ omnes superbos et impios congregabit congregatione unius fascis, et projiciet humiliabitque eos usque ad lacum gehennæ, humiles vero exaltabit. Et gloriam magnificentiæ regni tui dicent, id est magnificam gloriam regni cœlestis. De quo subditur :
paras.en: [[144:12|To make thy might known to the sons of men|Ut notam faciant filiis hominum]], namely to their brethren and neighbours, [[144:12|thy might|potentiam tuam]]: which none can resist, [[Esth 13:9|for all things are in thy power|in ditione cuncta sunt posita]] [Denis: "in whose power all things are set"]; which shall gather all the proud and wicked together [[Is 24:22|in the gathering of one bundle|congregatione unius fascis]], and shall cast them down and humble them even to the pit of hell, but shall exalt the humble. [[144:12|and the glory of the magnificence of thy kingdom|Et gloriam magnificentiæ regni tui]] they shall speak of, that is, the magnificent glory of the heavenly kingdom. Of which it is added:

paras.t: Regnum tuum, regnum omnium sæculorum, id est, per omnia sæcula durat. In Ecclesia namque triumphanti sine fine regnabis. Vel sic : Regnum tuum, regnum omnium sæculorum, id est, omnibus regnis, quæ unquam fuerunt, sunt, vel erunt, excellentius est. Hoc autem exponi etiam posset de regno Christi, quo regnat in Ecclesia militanti, quod juxta vaticinia Danielis, majus et fortius fuit omnibus regnis aliorum regum et principum. Et dominatio tua in omni generatione et generatione, id est, tuæ dominationi omnes generationes subduntur. Omnibus enim imperas, et in bonis dominaris in hac vita per gratiam, in Beatis vero per gloriam. Hæc autem etiam apud Danielem habentur : Potestas ejus potestas sempiterna, et regnum ejus in generationem et generationem. Specialiter vero de Christo apud eumdem dicitur : Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei. Potestas ejus potestas æterna quæ non auferetur, et regnum ejus quod non corrumpetur. Cui concordat illud : Regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum, et regni ejus non erit finis. Quod de præsenti regno Christi accipi potest, quoniam usque in finem sæculi Ecclesia stabit, et Christus in ea regnabit ; quumque finitum fuerit regnum hoc, quoad statum hujus viæ, perficietur, et sine fine durabit in patria.
paras.en: [[144:13|Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages|Regnum tuum, regnum omnium sæculorum]], that is, it lasts through all ages. For in the Church triumphant Thou shalt reign without end. Or thus: *Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages*, that is, it is more excellent than all the kingdoms that ever were, are, or shall be. This could also be explained of the kingdom of Christ, by which He reigns in the Church militant, which, according to the prophecies of Daniel[[Dan 2:44||]][[Dan 2:45||]], was greater and stronger than all the kingdoms of other kings and princes. [[144:13|and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations|Et dominatio tua in omni generatione et generatione]], that is, all generations are subject to Thy dominion. For Thou commandest all things, and rulest in the good in this life by grace, and in the Blessed by glory. And these things are found in Daniel too: [[Dan 4:31|his power is an everlasting power, and his kingdom is to all generations|Potestas ejus potestas sempiterna, et regnum ejus in generationem et generationem]]. And of Christ in particular it is said in the same: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]]. [[Dan 7:14|his power is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed|Potestas ejus potestas æterna quæ non auferetur, et regnum ejus quod non corrumpetur]]. With which agrees that saying: [[Luke 1:32|he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|Regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum]]. [[Luke 1:33|And of his kingdom there shall be no end|et regni ejus non erit finis]]. This can be taken of Christ's present kingdom, since the Church will stand until the end of the world and Christ will reign in it; and when this kingdom has ended as to the state of this way [that is, of this present life], it will be perfected and will last without end in the fatherland.

paras.t: Fidelis Dominus in omnibus verbis suis, quoniam quidquid dicit aut spondet, verum est atque impletur, dummodo absolute dicatur. Quædam namque dicuntur a Deo comminative seu conditionaliter, quæ non semper implentur, sicut de morte Ezechiæ : et tamen in talibus verbis Deus fidelis est, quoniam eo modo quo ipse ea dicit, vera sunt atque implentur. Hinc Christus testatur : Unus apex non præteribit de lege, donec omnia fiant. Et iterum dicit : Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt. Dicitur autem Deus fidelis, non a fide, quæ est virtus theologica, Deo non competens, imo nec Christo homini, sed a quadam fidelitate qua neminem decipit. Sicque Apostolus nominat eum fidelem, Fidelis est, inquiens, qui repromisit ; et alibi, Fidelis autem Deus, qui non patietur vos tentari, etc. Et sanctus in omnibus operibus suis. Omnia enim juste fecit, nec reprehendi potest in aliquo, sicut ait Scriptura : Quis ei dicere potest, Operatus es iniquitatem ? Et Apostolus dicit : Quæ a Deo sunt, ordinata sunt.
paras.en: [[144:13|The Lord is faithful in all his words|Fidelis Dominus in omnibus verbis suis]], since whatever He says or promises is true and is fulfilled, provided it is said absolutely. For some things are said by God by way of threat or conditionally, which are not always fulfilled, as concerning the death of Ezechias[[Is 38:1||]][[Is 38:5||]]; and yet in such words God is faithful, since in the way in which He says them they are true and are fulfilled. Hence Christ testifies: [[Matt 5:18|one tittle shall not pass of the law, till all be fulfilled|Unus apex non præteribit de lege, donec omnia fiant]]. And again He says: [[Luke 21:33|Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.|Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt]] Now God is called faithful, not from faith, which is a theological virtue not befitting God, nor even Christ as man, but from a certain faithfulness by which He deceives no one. And so the Apostle names Him faithful: [[Heb 10:23|he is faithful that hath promised|Fidelis est, inquiens, qui repromisit]], he says; and elsewhere: [[1 Cor 10:13|God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted|Fidelis autem Deus, qui non patietur vos tentari]], etc. [[144:13|and holy in all his works|Et sanctus in omnibus operibus suis]]. For He has done all things justly, and cannot be blamed in anything, as Scripture says: [[Job 36:23|who can say to him: Thou hast wrought iniquity?|Quis ei dicere potest, Operatus es iniquitatem]] And the Apostle says: [[Rom 13:1|those that are ordained of God|Quæ a Deo sunt, ordinata sunt]].

paras.t: Allevat Dominus omnes qui corruunt. Quam multi corruunt, quos Deus non allevat ! ut patet de reprobis qui manent in culpa et pœna æterna. Quid ergo est quod ait, Allevat Dominus omnes qui corruunt, nisi, Omnes corruentes in culpam, qui allevantur, a Domino allevantur ? Solus enim Deus lapsum in peccatum, per gratiam allevat. Simili modo dicitur de Christo : Erat lux vera quæ illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum ; non quod omnes homines a Christo illuminentur, quum statim sequatur, Tenebræ eam non comprehenderunt, et, Sui eum non receperunt : nisi intelligatur de lumine naturali. Et erigit per gratiam omnes elisos, id est in malum prolapsos. Idem est hoc cum eo quod dixit, Allevat Dominus omnes qui corruunt. Propter quod idem est modus intelligendi.
paras.en: [[144:14|The Lord lifteth up all that fall|Allevat Dominus omnes qui corruunt]]. How many fall whom God does not lift up! as is plain in the reprobate, who remain in sin and in everlasting punishment. What then does he mean by *The Lord lifteth up all that fall*, unless this: all who fall into sin and are lifted up are lifted up by the Lord? For God alone lifts up by grace one fallen into sin. In like manner it is said of Christ: [[John 1:9|That was the true light, which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world|Erat lux vera quæ illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum]]; not that all men are enlightened by Christ, since there follows straight after: [[John 1:5|the darkness did not comprehend it|Tenebræ eam non comprehenderunt]], and: [[John 1:11|his own received him not|Sui eum non receperunt]]; unless it be understood of the natural light. [[144:14|And setteth up|Et erigit]] by grace [[144:14|all that are cast down|omnes elisos]], that is, those who have slipped into evil. This is the same as what he said: *The Lord lifteth up all that fall*. So it is to be understood in the same way.

paras.t: Oculi omnium in te sperant, Domine. Si spes proprie accipiatur, tunc istud non convenit nisi homini viatori in Deo speranti, ut sit sensus : Oculi interiores omnium fidelium et bonorum, in te sperant, Domine, omne bonum præstolando a te ; et tu das escam illorum spiritualem et corporalem, videlicet panem quotidianum, sacramentalem, pœnitentialem, in tempore opportuno, id est hora convenienti. Si autem sumatur spes metaphorice atque communiter pro quacumque exspectatione, seu naturali affectione boni futuri ; tunc oculi omnium animantium, rationalium et irrationalium, sperant in Domino, id est, bonum suæ sustentationi atque naturæ necessarium, exspectant ab eo, naturali motu, quia habere non possunt escam nisi a Deo, cui cura est de omnibus.
paras.en: [[144:15|The eyes of all hope in thee, O Lord|Oculi omnium in te sperant, Domine]]. If hope be taken properly, then this befits only man, the wayfarer, hoping in God, so that the sense is: [[144:15|The eyes|Oculi]] within [[144:15|of all|omnium]] the faithful and good [[144:15|hope in thee, O Lord|in te sperant, Domine]], awaiting every good from Thee; [[144:15|and thou givest them meat|et tu das escam illorum]], spiritual and bodily, namely daily bread, sacramental bread, the bread of penance, [[144:15|in due season|in tempore opportuno]], that is, at a fitting hour. But if hope be taken metaphorically and broadly for any kind of expectation, or natural longing for a good to come, then the eyes of all living things, rational and irrational, hope in the Lord: that is, they await from Him, by a natural movement, the good needful for their sustenance and nature, because they can have food only from God, [[Wis 12:13|who hast care of all|cui cura est de omnibus]][[1 Pet 5:7||]].

paras.t: Aperis tu manum tuam, id est, bonitatem tuam effundis, et imples omne animal benedictione, id est dono sibi necessario, scilicet cibo. Si autem per omne animal intelligatur omnis homo, qui etiam nominatur omnis creatura, tunc sensus est : Imples omne animal, id est omnem hominem, cujus oculi sperant in te, benedictione, id est gratiæ tuæ collatione ; quemadmodum ait Apostolus, Benedictus Deus, qui benedixit nos in omni benedictione in cœlestibus in Christo Jesu. Et Dominus per Isaiam, Effundam, inquit, benedictionem meam super stirpem tuam.
paras.en: [[144:16|Thou openest thy hand|Aperis tu manum tuam]], that is, Thou pourest out Thy goodness, [[144:16|and fillest with blessing every living creature|et imples omne animal benedictione]], that is, with the gift it needs, namely food. But if by *every living creature* [*omne animal*, "every animal", "every living thing"] every man is understood, who is also called *every creature*[[Mark 16:15||]], then the sense is: *Thou fillest every living creature*, that is, every man whose eyes hope in Thee, *with blessing*, that is, with the bestowal of Thy grace; as the Apostle says: [[Eph 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], [[Eph 1:3|who hath blessed us with spiritual blessings in heavenly places, in Christ|qui benedixit nos in omni benedictione in cœlestibus in Christo Jesu]] [Denis: "with every blessing"]. And the Lord says by Isaias: I will pour out, He says, [[Is 44:3|my blessing upon thy stock|benedictionem meam super stirpem tuam]].

paras.t: Justus Dominus in omnibus viis suis, id est in cunctis quæ agit, in omni dispositione, in omni processu, in se ipso atque in suis effectibus : secundum quod scriptum est, Justæ et veræ sunt omnes viæ tuæ, Rex sæculorum ; et iterum, Non injustus est Deus, ut obliviscatur operis vestri. Verumtamen, sicut prædictum est, Universæ viæ Domini, misericordia et veritas, seu æquitas. Quum enim in omni opere Dei misericordia atque justitia inveniantur, utrumque verissime dicitur, scilicet, Justus Dominus in omnibus viis suis ; et, Misericors Dominus in omnibus viis suis. Hoc autem superius sæpe declaratum recordor. Et sanctus in omnibus operibus suis. Hoc paulo ante expositum est.
paras.en: [[144:17|The Lord is just in all his ways|Justus Dominus in omnibus viis suis]], that is, in all that He does, in every ordering, in every proceeding, in Himself and in His effects; as it is written: [[Apoc 15:3|Just and true are thy ways, O King of ages|Justæ et veræ sunt omnes viæ tuæ, Rex sæculorum]]; and again: [[Heb 6:10|God is not unjust, that he should forget your work|Non injustus est Deus, ut obliviscatur operis vestri]]. And yet, as was said before: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini, misericordia et veritas]], or equity. For since mercy and justice are found in every work of God, both are most truly said, namely *The Lord is just in all his ways*, and *The Lord is merciful in all his ways*. And I recall that this has often been declared above. [[144:17|and holy in all his works|Et sanctus in omnibus operibus suis]]. This was explained a little before.

paras.t: Prope est Dominus per gratiam omnibus invocantibus eum, id est intus seu ex intimo affectu vocantibus eum, qui ejus misericordiam pie implorant. Ideo subditur : omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate, id est in vera fide. Accedentem enim ad Deum oportet credere quia est, et quia inquirentibus se remunerator sit, prout dicitur ad Hebræos. Vel, In veritate, id est in veritate vitæ, videlicet in conversatione divinæ æquitati placens. Peccatores enim Deus non audit ; sed si quis cultor est Dei, et voluntatem ejus facit, hunc exaudit. Cui consonat illud Job : Deus non porriget manum malignis. Ad hoc ergo quod aliquis meritorie oret, aut de condigno exaudiatur, oportet ut coram Deo in veritate, id est in justa conversatione, ambulet. Ideo scriptum est : Si mundus et rectus incesseris, statim evigilabit ad te. Vel, In veritate, id est vera et pia intentione, ordinando orationem et bonum optatum ad Dei honorem et sui ipsius veram salutem. Secundum Augustinum, invocare Deum in veritate, est invocare Patrem per Filium, quoniam Filius Dei est veritas Patris æterni.
paras.en: [[144:18|The Lord is nigh|Prope est Dominus]] by grace [[144:18|unto all them that call upon him|omnibus invocantibus eum]] [*invocantibus*, "calling within"], that is, calling upon Him inwardly or from their inmost affection, who devoutly implore His mercy. Therefore it is added: [[144:18|to all that call upon him in truth|omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate]], that is, in true faith. For [[Heb 11:6|he that cometh to God must believe that he is: and is a rewarder to them that seek him|Accedentem enim ad Deum oportet credere quia est, et quia inquirentibus se remunerator sit]], as is said to the Hebrews. Or, *in truth*, that is, in truth of life, namely in a manner of living pleasing to the divine equity. For [[John 9:31|God doth not hear sinners: but if a man be a server of God and doth his, will, him he heareth|Peccatores enim Deus non audit ; sed si quis cultor est Dei, et voluntatem ejus facit, hunc exaudit]]. With which agrees that saying of Job: God will not [[Job 8:20|reach out his hand to the evil doer|porriget manum malignis]]. In order, then, that one may pray meritoriously, or be heard as one who deserves it, he must walk before God in truth[[3 Kings 2:4||]], that is, in a just manner of living. Therefore it is written: [[Job 8:6|If thou wilt walk clean and upright, he will presently awake unto thee|Si mundus et rectus incesseris, statim evigilabit ad te]]. Or, *in truth*, that is, with a true and devout intention, directing the prayer and the good desired to the honour of God and to one's own true salvation. According to Augustine, to call upon God in truth is to call upon the Father through the Son, since the Son of God is the truth[[John 14:6||]] of the eternal Father.

paras.t: Voluntatem timentium se faciet, id est, actum voluntatis, seu desiderium timentium se filiali timore, ad effectum perducet tempore apto et sibi placenti ; et deprecationem eorum exaudiet, dummodo orent instanter, salubriter, et pro se ipsis. Pro aliis enim non semper exaudiuntur, propter obicem quem opponunt. Et salvos faciet eos, tollendo ab ipsis mala culpæ et pœnæ, tribuendoque eis in præsenti bona gratiæ, in patria vero bona gloriæ. Propter quod Salomon monet : In timore Domini esto tota die, quia habebis spem in novissimo.
paras.en: [[144:19|He will do the will of them that fear him|Voluntatem timentium se faciet]], that is, the act of will, or the desire, of those who fear Him with filial fear He will bring to effect at a fitting time pleasing to Himself; [[144:19|and he will hear their prayer|et deprecationem eorum exaudiet]], provided they pray earnestly, for what is wholesome, and for themselves. For they are not always heard for others, because of the obstacle those others put in the way. [[144:19|and save them|Et salvos faciet eos]], taking from them the evils of sin and punishment, and giving them in the present the goods of grace, and in the fatherland the goods of glory. That is why Solomon warns: [[Prov 23:17|be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long|In timore Domini esto tota die]]: [[Prov 23:18|Because thou shalt have hope in the latter end|quia habebis spem in novissimo]].

paras.t: Custodit Dominus omnes diligentes se, præservando eos ab universis periculis, ne finaliter pereant. Scimus enim quoniam diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum. Et cur hoc ? nisi quia æterna Sapientia protestatur : Ego diligentes me diligo. Qui autem alium diligit, eum utique secundum quantitatem dilectionis pro posse custodit. Et omnes peccatores in vitiis perseverantes disperdet, dicendo : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum.
paras.en: [[144:20|The Lord keepeth all them that love him|Custodit Dominus omnes diligentes se]], preserving them from all dangers, lest they perish in the end. For [[Rom 8:28|we know that to them that love God all things work together unto good|Scimus enim quoniam diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum]]. And why this? but because the eternal Wisdom declares: [[Prov 8:17|I love them that love me|Ego diligentes me diligo]]. And he who loves another surely guards him as far as he can, according to the measure of his love. [[144:20|but all the wicked|Et omnes peccatores]] who persevere in their vices [[144:20|he will destroy|disperdet]], saying: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]].

paras.t: Laudationem Domini loquetur os meum, non verba scurrilia, nociva, infructuosa et vana. Et quoniam ego in laude ejus deficio, ideo et benedicat omnis caro, id est omnis homo, nomini sancto ejus, id est ipsi sancto Deo, in sæculum et in sæculum sæculi, id est æternaliter, scilicet nunc inchoando, atque in patria sine fine continuando. Magnum est, desiderare ut Deus ab omnibus benedicatur. Hoc namque procedit ex amore Dei et proximi.
paras.en: [[144:21|My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord|Laudationem Domini loquetur os meum]], not scurrilous, harmful, unfruitful and vain words. And since I fall short in His praise, therefore [[144:21|and let all flesh bless|et benedicat omnis caro]], that is, every man, [[144:21|his holy name|nomini sancto ejus]], that is, the holy God Himself, [[144:21|forever; yea, for ever and ever|in sæculum et in sæculum sæculi]], that is, eternally, namely beginning now and continuing without end in the fatherland. It is a great thing to desire that God be blessed by all; for this proceeds from the love of God and of neighbour.

paras.t: Ecce gloriosissimum atque dulcissimum psalmum audivimus : qui utique aliud nihil est, nisi angelicum canticum cœlesteque carmen, in quo nihil triste vel minus deificum continetur. Imo totus hic psalmus de Beatis in patria exponi posset, eisque sublimius convenit, quam viatoribus. Quid ergo finaliter nobis incumbit ? nisi ut (juxta Apostolicam admonitionem) mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus : quatenus corde mundo et vere devoto psalmum præsentem cum omni alacritate Domino decantemus, summumque nostrum in hac peregrinatione solatium sit, in laudibus Dei jugiter occupari.
paras.en: See, we have heard a most glorious and most sweet psalm, which is indeed nothing other than an angelic canticle and a heavenly song, in which nothing sad or less than godlike is contained. Nay, this whole psalm could be explained of the Blessed in the fatherland, and befits them more sublimely than wayfarers. What then is incumbent on us in the end, but that (according to the Apostle's admonition) [[2 Cor 7:1|let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit|mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus]], so that with a clean and truly devout heart we may sing the present psalm to the Lord with all eagerness, and that our highest solace in this pilgrimage may be to be continually occupied in the praises of God?

paras.t: Patiens et multæ misericordiæ Deus, nobis peccare cessantibus, ac indulgentiam postulantibus, esto propitius : ut correctis actibus nostris, conferri nobis gratulemur gaudia perpetuitatis.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, patient and of great mercy, be propitious to us who cease from sinning and ask for pardon: that, our deeds being amended, we may rejoice that the joys of eternity are bestowed on us.

145.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUADRAGESIMI QUINTI : LAUDA, ANIMA MEA, DOMINUM.
145.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and forty-fifth psalm: Praise the Lord, O my soul.

paras.t: Habet insuper psalmus jam pertractandus, pro titulo, Alleluia : cujus interpretatio est, Laudate Dominum. Est enim hic psalmus laus Dei, præcipue admonens in Deo esse finaliter confidendum, et ait :
paras.en: The psalm now to be treated has, moreover, for its title [[145:1|Alleluia|Alleluia]], which is interpreted, Praise ye the Lord. For this psalm is a praise of God, chiefly admonishing us that we must trust in God finally [that is, in him as our last end, and not merely as a means], and it says:

paras.t: Lauda, anima mea, Dominum. Quidam philosophorum atque theologorum etiam magni, asseruerunt hominem non esse nisi animam. Unde Plato dixit, quod homo est anima utens corpore. Secundum hos igitur, dum dicitur, Lauda, anima mea, Dominum, alloquitur anima semetipsam. Secundum veritatem autem, homo ex anima et corpore constat, tanquam essentialibus partibus. Et quoniam omnium operationum vitalium, præsertim intellectualium, radix principiumque est anima, ideo totus homo se ipsum ad laudem Dei accendere volens, animam suam affatur. Hæc tamen allocutio convenit homini ex parte animæ. Sæpe alloquitur homo se ipsum tanquam alium. Interdum vero loquitur de se ipso et anima sua, tanquam essent distincta, quum tamen proprie loquendo, nec idem sint neque distincta, sed unum est aliquid alterius. Unde in Tobia dicitur : Ego autem et anima mea in Deo lætabimur.
paras.en: [[145:2|Praise the Lord, O my soul|Lauda, anima mea, Dominum]]. Certain of the philosophers, and great ones among the theologians too, have asserted that man is nothing but the soul. Hence Plato said that man is a soul using a body. According to these, then, when it is said, [[145:2|Praise the Lord, O my soul|Lauda, anima mea, Dominum]], the soul addresses itself. But according to the truth, man is made up of soul and body, as of his essential parts. And since the soul is the root and principle of all the vital operations, especially the intellectual ones, the whole man, wishing to kindle himself to the praise of God, addresses his soul. Yet this address befits man on the side of the soul. Often a man addresses himself as though he were another. Sometimes, again, he speaks of himself and of his soul as though they were distinct, though, properly speaking, they are neither the same nor distinct, but the one is something of the other. Hence it is said in Tobias: [[Tob 13:9|And I and my soul will rejoice in him|Ego autem et anima mea in Deo lætabimur]].

paras.t: Devotus itaque ad Dei præconium se excitans : Lauda, inquit, anima mea, Dominum, tanquam summum bonum et omnis boni fontanum principium. Soli Deo da honorem et gloriam, quia etsi alium interdum laudas sive honoras, quam Deum, hoc tamen non facis, nisi propter aliquod divinum in illo consistens; nec alium laudas et honoras, nisi propter Deum, ad quem etiam refers quidquid honoris et laudis alteri exhibes. Propterea, alios laudando et honorando, magis honoras et laudas Deum, quam illos. Lauda ergo, anima mea, Dominum creatorem, salvatorem ac judicem tuum, quoniam hoc est inter omnia opera tua dignissimum. Lauda autem eum non solum voce oris, sed interioribus verbis cordis : imo mente, ore et opere eum collauda, secundum illud Ecclesiastici : Et nunc in omni corde et ore collaudate, et benedicite nomen Domini. Deinde anima huic admonitioni acquiescens, respondet : Laudabo Dominum in vita mea, id est tempore vitæ meæ; vel, In vita mea, id est bene vivendo, sicque laudabo eum in vita gratiæ et gloriæ. Laudare autem Deum in nuda vita naturæ, non est meritorium. Psallam Deo meo, id est summo et vero Deo, quem summe et unice colo ac diligo, quamdiu fuero, scilicet in præsenti et in futuro. Quam dulce verbum est hoc, Psallam Deo meo quamdiu fuero ! Deum enim universorum, nominat Deum suum : quod utique nemo in propria persona veraciter dicit, nisi qui toto corde ad Deum conversus est, ei totaliter stabiliterque inhærens.
paras.en: So the devout man, rousing himself to the praise of God: [[145:2|Praise|Lauda]], he says, [[145:2|the Lord, O my soul|anima mea, Dominum]], as the highest good and the fountain-head and principle of all good. To God alone give honour and glory[[1 Tim 1:17||]]; for even if thou sometimes praisest or honourest another than God, thou dost this only on account of something divine abiding in him; nor dost thou praise and honour another except for God's sake, to whom thou also referest whatever honour and praise thou showest to another. Therefore, in praising and honouring others, thou honourest and praisest God more than them. Praise, then, O my soul, the Lord thy creator, saviour and judge, since this is the worthiest of all thy works. And praise him not only with the voice of the mouth, but with the inward words of the heart: nay, praise him with mind, mouth and deed together, according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 39:41|Now therefore with the whole heart and mouth praise ye him, and bless the name of the Lord|Et nunc in omni corde et ore collaudate, et benedicite nomen Domini]]. Then the soul, assenting to this admonition, replies: [[145:2|in my life I will praise the Lord|Laudabo Dominum in vita mea]], that is, in the time of my life; or, [[145:2|in my life|In vita mea]], that is, by living well, and so I will praise him in the life of grace and of glory. For to praise God in the bare life of nature is not meritorious. [[145:2|I will sing to my God|Psallam Deo meo]], that is, to the highest and true God, whom I worship and love supremely and alone, [[145:2|as long as I shall be|quamdiu fuero]], namely in the present life and in the life to come. How sweet a word is this: [[145:2|I will sing to my God as long as I shall be|Psallam Deo meo quamdiu fuero]]! For he names the God of all things his own God: which surely no one says truly in his own person except one who is turned to God with his whole heart, cleaving to him wholly and steadfastly.

paras.t: Nolite confidere in principibus. Advertendum, quod homo dicitur in aliquo confidere seu sperare dupliciter : scilicet principaliter seu directe ; sicque in Deum dumtaxat sperandum est, quoniam ipse est principalis omnis boni largitor. Secundo dicitur homo sperare in aliquo secundario et minus principaliter, in quantum videlicet ejus auxilio potest juvari ut adipiscatur bonum optatum : et ita speramus in Sanctis, qui orant pro nobis, quorum patrocinio confidimus liberari. Sic enim Virginem gloriosam vocamus spem nostram. Præterea agnoscendum, quod primum et proprium spei objectum, est Deus seu beatitudo æterna et increata; secundarium vero spei objectum, est omne id quo indigemus et adjuvamur ad summi boni adeptionem, ut est gratia, virtus, scientia, remissio culpæ. Quantum ergo ad principale seu primum ac proprium spei objectum, in solo Deo speramus. Non enim adipisci valemus hoc bonum infinitum, nisi virtute divina immensa, cui spes directe innititur. Quantum vero ad secundarium spei objectum, confidimus in sanctis angelis atque hominibus, quorum intercessione, virtute ac meritis ea a Deo consequimur, per quæ ad ipsum pertingere promeremur.
paras.en: [[145:2|Put not your trust in princes|Nolite confidere in principibus]]. It is to be noted that a man is said to trust or hope in something in two ways. First, principally or directly; and in this way hope is to be placed in God alone, since he is the principal giver of every good. Secondly, a man is said to hope in something secondarily and less principally, inasmuch, namely, as he can be helped by its aid to obtain the good he desires; and in this way we hope in the Saints, who pray for us, and by whose patronage we trust to be delivered. For thus we call the glorious Virgin our hope. It is further to be recognised that the first and proper object of hope [that is, what hope is chiefly directed to] is God, or eternal and uncreated beatitude; while the secondary object of hope is everything that we need and that helps us toward the attainment of the highest good, such as grace, virtue, knowledge, the remission of guilt. As to the principal, or first and proper, object of hope, then, we hope in God alone; for we cannot obtain this infinite good except by the immense divine power, on which hope directly rests. But as to the secondary object of hope, we trust in the holy angels and men, by whose intercession, power and merits we obtain from God those things by which we merit to reach him.

paras.t: Ait ergo: Nolite confidere, id est spem ponere, in principibus, id est in regibus, ducibus, judicibus, et ceteris inter homines principatum habentibus, ita quod finaliter in eis speretis, seu eorum potestati principaliter innitamini, quum ipsi nihil possint nisi virtute divina. Potestis tamen eorum auxilio instrumentaliter uti, Deo semper principaliter innitendo. Propter quod apud Osee dicitur: Convertimini ad Dominum, et dicite ei: Assur non salvabit nos, super equum non ascendemus. Non quod super equum ascendere sit peccatum, sed ne in velocitate equi potius quam in Deo speretur, qui ait: In me tantummodo auxilium tuum. Unde sperantibus in equis atque equitibus potius quam in Deo, in Isaia dicitur: Dixistis, Ad equos fugiemus: ideo fugietis. Et super veloces ascendemus: ideo veloces erunt qui persequentur vos. Non est ergo in principibus confidendum, quoniam de iniquo principe dicitur: Gloria ejus stercus et vermis; hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur. Unde scriptum est: Omnis potentatus brevis vita; sic et rex hodie est, et cras morietur. Etenim mane præcedit eum exercitus, et vespere jacet in tumulo. Noli quoque confidere in filiis hominum, id est in ceteris qui principibus sunt subjecti, in quibus non est salus vera et spiritualis: imo nec se ipsos possunt salvare. Et ideo apud Jeremiam legitur: Vere in Domino Deo nostro salus. De electis quoque et bonis atque fidelibus filiis, ex perversis parentibus natis, scriptum est: Ad te, Domine, gentes venient ab extremis terræ, et dicent: Vere mendacium possederunt patres nostri, vanitatem quæ eis non profuit.
paras.en: He says, then: [[145:2|Put not your trust|Nolite confidere]], that is, do not place your hope, [[145:2|in princes|in principibus]], that is, in kings, captains, judges and the others who hold rule among men, so as to hope in them as your end, or to lean principally on their power, since they can do nothing except by the divine power. You may, however, make use of their help as instruments, while always leaning principally on God. For which reason it is said in Osee: [[Osee 14:3|return to the Lord, and say to him|Convertimini ad Dominum, et dicite ei]]: [[Osee 14:4|Assyria shall not save us, we will not ride upon horses|Assur non salvabit nos, super equum non ascendemus]]. Not that to ride upon a horse is a sin, but lest hope be placed in the swiftness of the horse rather than in God, who says: [[Osee 13:9|thy help is only in me|In me tantummodo auxilium tuum]]. Hence to those who hope in horses and horsemen rather than in God it is said in Isaias: You [[Is 30:16|have said|Dixistis]]: [[Is 30:16|we will flee to horses: therefore shall you flee. And we will mount upon swift ones: therefore shall they be swifter that shall pursue after you|Ad equos fugiemus: ideo fugietis. Et super veloces ascendemus: ideo veloces erunt qui persequentur vos]]. Therefore we must not trust in princes, since of the wicked prince it is said: [[1 Mach 2:62|his glory is dung and worms|Gloria ejus stercus et vermis]]: [[1 Mach 2:63|Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow he shall not be found|hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur]]. Hence it is written: [[Ecclus 10:11|All power is of short life|Omnis potentatus brevis vita]]; [[Ecclus 10:12|so also a king is to day, and to morrow he shall die|sic et rex hodie est, et cras morietur]]. For in the morning an army goes before him, and in the evening he lies in the tomb [this last sentence is not in Ecclesiasticus; its source has not been found]. Do not trust, either, [[145:3|in the children of men|in filiis hominum]], that is, in the rest, who are subject to princes, [[145:3|in whom there is no salvation|in quibus non est salus]], true and spiritual: nay, they cannot even save themselves. And therefore we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 3:23|truly in the Lord our God is the salvation|Vere in Domino Deo nostro salus]]. Of the elect also, the good and faithful children born of perverse parents, it is written: [[Jer 16:19|to thee the Gentiles shall come from the ends of the earth, and shall say: Surely our fathers have possessed lies, a vanity which hath not profited them|Ad te, Domine, gentes venient ab extremis terræ, et dicent: Vere mendacium possederunt patres nostri, vanitatem quæ eis non profuit]].

paras.t: Quod autem in homine salus non consistat, consequenter ostenditur. Exibit spiritus, id est anima, ejus de corpore hora mortis, et revertetur homo, quantum ad corpus mortale, in terram suam, id est in præjacentem materiam, de qua erat formatum, quemadmodum Deus prædixit: Pulvis es, et in pulverem reverteris. In illa die, id est tempore mortis, peribunt omnes cogitationes eorum, id est, effectu et fine intento frustrabuntur cogitationes hominum impiorum, quemadmodum alibi inducitur: Peccator conversus est in terram suam, et cogitatio ejus periit. Unde sera pœnitentia ducti testantur: Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis? Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra.
paras.en: That salvation does not lie in man is shown next. [[145:4|His spirit shall go forth|Exibit spiritus]], that is, his soul, from the body at the hour of death, [[145:4|and he shall return|et revertetur]], that is, man, as to his mortal body, [[145:4|into his earth|in terram suam]], that is, into the pre-existing matter [that is, the matter which was there before, out of which the body was made] of which it was formed, as God foretold: [[Gen 3:19|dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return|Pulvis es, et in pulverem reverteris]]. [[145:4|in that day|In illa die]], that is, at the time of death, [[145:4|all their thoughts shall perish|peribunt omnes cogitationes eorum]], that is, the thoughts of wicked men shall be cheated of their effect and of the end they aimed at; as is brought in elsewhere: The sinner [[1 Mach 2:63|is returned into his earth and his thought is come to nothing|conversus est in terram suam, et cogitatio ejus periit]]. Hence, moved by a late repentance, they testify: [[Wis 5:8|What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us?|Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis?]] [[Wis 5:9|All those things are passed away like a shadow|Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra]].

paras.t: Beatus est jam in spe, cujus est Deus Jacob patriarchæ, scilicet Deus verus atque omnipotens, adjutor ejus. Si enim Deus pro eo, quis contra eum? Spes ejus, id est talis hominis quem adjuvat Deus, est in Domino Deo ipsius, non in aliquo transitorio ente, sed in summo bono, Deo altissimo, qui fecit ex nihilo cœlum et terram, mare Oceanum, et omnia quæ in eis sunt. Omnia enim fecit mediate vel immediate, quemadmodum in alio loco dicitur: Domine, Rex omnipotens, tu fecisti cœlum et terram, et quidquid cœli ambitu continetur.
paras.en: [[145:5|Blessed|Beatus]] already in hope is he [[145:5|who hath the God of Jacob|cujus est Deus Jacob]], the patriarch, that is, the true and almighty God, [[145:5|for his helper|adjutor ejus]]. For if God be for him, who is against him?[[Rom 8:31||]] [[145:5|whose hope|Spes ejus]], that is, the hope of such a man as God helps, is [[145:5|in the Lord his God|in Domino Deo ipsius]]: not in any passing being, but in the highest good, God most high, [[145:6|Who made|qui fecit]] out of nothing [[145:6|heaven and earth, the sea|cœlum et terram, mare]], the Ocean, [[145:6|and all things that are in them|et omnia quæ in eis sunt]][[Gen 1:1||]]. For he made all things, mediately or immediately, as is said in another place: O Lord, [[Esth 13:9|almighty king|Rex omnipotens]], [[Esth 13:10|Thou hast made heaven and earth and all things that are under the cope of heaven|tu fecisti cœlum et terram, et quidquid cœli ambitu continetur]].

paras.t: Qui custodit veritatem, eam conservando in esse: ipse namque est causa, conservator et finis omnis veritatis; in sæculum, id est perpetuo. Facit judicium injuriam patientibus, ulciscendo injuriam eis illatam, quemadmodum Scriptura ait: Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam; et iterum: Deus inultum abire non patitur. Dat escam esurientibus. De hoc præcedenti psalmo dictum est plenius in expositione illius versiculi, Oculi omnium in te sperant, Domine, et tu das escam illorum. Denique esurientes et sitientes justitiam, saturabuntur ab eo.
paras.en: [[145:7|Who keepeth truth|Qui custodit veritatem]], preserving it in being: for he is the cause, preserver and end of all truth; [[145:7|for ever|in sæculum]], that is, perpetually. He [[145:7|executeth judgment for them that suffer wrong|Facit judicium injuriam patientibus]], avenging the wrong done to them, as the Scripture says: [[Rom 12:19|Revenge is mine, I will repay|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam]]; and again: [[Job 24:12|God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged|Deus inultum abire non patitur]]. He [[145:7|giveth food to the hungry|Dat escam esurientibus]]. Of this more was said in the preceding psalm, in the exposition of the little verse, [[Ps 144:15|The eyes of all hope in thee, O Lord: and thou givest them meat|Oculi omnium in te sperant, Domine, et tu das escam illorum]] [the margin gives Ps. cxliv, 13; the verse is 144:15]. And lastly, those who hunger and thirst after justice shall be filled by him.

paras.t: Dominus solvit compeditos; Dominus illuminat cæcos. Dominus erigit elisos. Hæc omnia corporaliter et spiritualiter sæpius facta a Deo sunt. Compeditos enim vinculis corporis, sæpe a carceribus liberavit; compeditos quoque vinculis peccatorum, per gratiam misericorditer solvit. Corporales insuper oculos hominum excæcatorum, sæpe ad visum corporalem reduxit; peccatores quoque tenebris ignorantiæ, passionum caligine, vitiorumque nebula spiritualiter excæcatos, frequenter misericordissime illustravit, dando eis gratiæ lumen, sapientiæ claritatem, veritatis notitiam. Quorum utrumque in Manasse rege Juda, mirabiliter factum describitur in libro Paralipomenon. Quomodo autem Dominus erigat elisos, in præcedenti psalmo ostensum est in illo versiculo, Allevat Dominus omnes qui corruunt, et erigit omnes elisos. Maxime vero omnia ista in Christi adventu impleta sunt, quemadmodum beatissimus Isaias prædixit: Ecce Deus vester; ipse veniet, et salvabit vos. Tunc aperientur oculi cæcorum, et aures surdorum patebunt; tunc saliet sicut cervus claudus, et aperta erit lingua mutorum.
paras.en: [[145:7|The Lord looseth them that are fettered|Dominus solvit compeditos]]; [[145:8|The Lord enlighteneth the blind|Dominus illuminat cæcos]]. [[145:8|The Lord lifteth up them that are cast down|Dominus erigit elisos]]. All these things have often been done by God, both bodily and spiritually. For those fettered with the bonds of the body he has often freed from prisons; and those fettered with the bonds of sins he has mercifully loosed by grace. Moreover, he has often brought back the bodily eyes of blinded men to bodily sight; and sinners spiritually blinded by the darkness of ignorance, the fog of the passions and the cloud of the vices he has very often most mercifully enlightened, giving them the light of grace, the brightness of wisdom, the knowledge of the truth. Both of these are described in the book of Paralipomenon as wonderfully done in Manasses king of Juda[[2 Par 33:1||]] [the margin gives II Par. xxxiii; his fetters and his return to the Lord are told in vv. 11–13]. And how the Lord lifts up them that are cast down was shown in the preceding psalm, at the little verse, [[Ps 144:14|The Lord lifteth up all that fall: and setteth up all that are cast down|Allevat Dominus omnes qui corruunt, et erigit omnes elisos]]. But above all, all these things were fulfilled at the coming of Christ, as the most blessed Isaias foretold: [[Is 35:4|behold your God|Ecce Deus vester]]: he [[Is 35:4|himself will come and will save you|ipse veniet, et salvabit vos]]. [[Is 35:5|Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped|Tunc aperientur oculi cæcorum, et aures surdorum patebunt]]; [[Is 35:6|Then shall the lame man leap as a hart, and the tongue of the dumb shall be free|tunc saliet sicut cervus claudus, et aperta erit lingua mutorum]].

paras.t: Dominus diligit justos. Similitudo enim est causa amoris, idcirco justus Dominus diligit justos. Et sicut odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus, sic amori sunt ei justus et justitia ejus. Justus autem vocatur, qui divina præcepta observat. Unde de eo qui præcepta se observasse veraciter dixit, scriptum est: Jesus intuitus eum, dilexit eum.
paras.en: [[145:8|the Lord loveth the just|Dominus diligit justos]]. For likeness is the cause of love; therefore the just Lord loves the just. And as [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful|odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]], so the just man and his justice are lovable to him. Now he is called just who keeps the divine commandments. Hence of him who said truly that he had kept the commandments it is written: [[Mark 10:21|Jesus, looking on him, loved him|Jesus intuitus eum, dilexit eum]].

paras.t: Dominus custodit advenas; pupillum et viduam suscipiet. Pater misericordiarum et Deus totius consolationis, illorum præcipue Deus et Dominus, pater et custos est, qui aliunde non habent subsidium. Tales vero sunt peregrini, id est a propria terra elongati; pupilli, id est parentibus orbati; et viduæ. Horum ergo Deus custos atque susceptor est. Propter quod scriptum est: Dominus facit judicium pupillo et viduæ, amatque peregrinum. Et iterum per Moysen jubet Dominus: Peregrinum et advenam non contristabis.
paras.en: [[145:9|The Lord keepeth the strangers|Dominus custodit advenas]], [[145:9|he will support the fatherless and the widow|pupillum et viduam suscipiet]]. The [[2 Cor 1:3|Father of mercies and the God of all comfort|Pater misericordiarum et Deus totius consolationis]] is in a special way the God and Lord, the father and keeper, of those who have no help from elsewhere. And such are strangers, that is, those far from their own land; the fatherless, that is, those bereft of parents; and widows. Of these, then, God is the keeper and the supporter. For which reason it is written: The Lord [[Deut 10:18|doth judgment to the fatherless and the widow, loveth the stranger|facit judicium pupillo et viduæ, amatque peregrinum]]. And again the Lord commands through Moses: [[Ex 22:21|Thou shalt not molest a stranger|Peregrinum et advenam non contristabis]][[Ex 23:9||]] [Denis's words, "thou shalt not grieve the sojourner and the stranger", join the two verses].

paras.t: Verumtamen quoniam multos corporaliter advenas, pupillos et viduas conspicimus relinqui a Deo, æternaliterque perire (quoniam, teste Apostolo, vidua quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est); ideo melius est, ista spiritualiter explanari hoc modo: Dominus custodit per gratiam a ruina peccati et mortis æternæ advenas, id est exsules a patria cœlesti, qui hoc mundo velut exsilio utuntur, patriamque cœlestem inquirunt, scientes se hic non habere manentem civitatem. Pupillum, id est omnem carnalem affectum spernentem, qui illud evangelicum implet, Patrem nolite vocare super terram; qui veraciter dicit, Pater noster qui es in cœlis; et viduam, id est animam omni sæculari solatio destitutam, et solum cœlestis Sponsi amplexibus perfrui cupientem, suscipiet in suam providentiam singularem ac paternalem. Et vias peccatorum disperdet, id est peccata eorum damnabit, operationes eorum malas et delectabiles dissipabit. Jam namque prædictum est, quod in illa die peribunt omnes cogitationes eorum; et in psalmo primo habetur, Iter impiorum peribit.
paras.en: Yet since we see many who are strangers, fatherless and widows in the bodily sense forsaken by God and perishing eternally (for, as the Apostle witnesses, the widow [[1 Tim 5:6|that liveth in pleasures is dead while she is living|quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est]]), it is therefore better to explain these words spiritually, in this way: [[145:9|The Lord keepeth|Dominus custodit]] by grace from the ruin of sin and of eternal death [[145:9|the strangers|advenas]], that is, the exiles from the heavenly fatherland, who use this world as a place of exile and seek the heavenly country[[Heb 11:14||]], knowing that they [[Heb 13:14|have not here a lasting city|hic non habere manentem civitatem]]; [[145:9|the fatherless|Pupillum]], that is, everyone who spurns all carnal affection, who fulfils that saying of the Gospel, [[Matt 23:9|call none your father upon earth|Patrem nolite vocare super terram]], and who says truly, [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven|Pater noster qui es in cœlis]]; [[145:9|and the widow|et viduam]], that is, the soul bereft of all worldly comfort and desiring to enjoy only the embraces of the heavenly Bridegroom: these [[145:9|he will support|suscipiet]] [the Latin *suscipiet* is "he will take up" or "receive"] into his singular and fatherly providence. [[145:9|and the ways of sinners he will destroy|Et vias peccatorum disperdet]], that is, he will condemn their sins, he will scatter their evil and pleasurable works.
