What is to be understood by these waters the doctors assign in different ways. For the ancient doctors, except Augustine, say that above the firmament or starry heaven there are true waters, which Bede asserts are suspended above the firmament with an icy solidity, after the manner of crystal; and so they would be of the same nature as elemental water. But the modern doctors, following Augustine, commonly say that there are by no means true waters above the heavens, but that by these waters is to be understood the ninth movable sphere, which is called the crystalline or watery heaven, not because it is of the nature of water, but because it agrees with water in transparency; just as the empyrean heaven is called fiery, not as being of the nature of fire, but as agreeing with fire in brightness or clearness. Yet according to Thomas on the Second Book of the Sentences, the empyrean heaven is not called bright because it sends out sensible rays, since it is not compact (for the cause of such brightness is the gathering or compacting of the parts of a transparent body, as Avicenna and Averroes say, which is why fire in its own sphere does not shine); but it is called bright because it has the nature of light in itself, since it is supremely formal [that is, most fully actual, having the least of matter's potentiality]. To the ninth sphere, or watery heaven, the astronomers ascribe the motion of the starry heaven from west to east. And some of them posit also a tenth movable sphere, which they say is the cause of the daily motion of the firmament or starry heaven from east to west.

paras.t: Consequenter ponitur ratio cur omnia Deum teneantur laudare. Quia ipse dixit, id est, intellectualiter intra se protulit practico intellectu, ut crearentur, et facta sunt ex nihilo; ipse mandavit, id est, per voluntatem imperialiter jussit, et creata sunt. Vocat enim ea quæ non sunt, tanquam sint. Unde in Genesi habetur: Dixit Deus, Fiat lux, Fiat firmamentum: et ita omnia dicendo creata sunt. Deus quippe est causa rerum per intellectum, juxta illud, Omnia in sapientia fecisti; et per voluntatem, quemadmodum dictum est, Omnia quæcumque voluit Dominus, fecit.
paras.en: Next is given the reason why all things are bound to praise God. [[148:5|For he spoke|Quia ipse dixit]], that is, he uttered intellectually within himself, by his practical intellect, that they should be created, [[148:5|and they were made|et facta sunt]] out of nothing; [[148:5|he commanded|ipse mandavit]], that is, he bade by his will as with authority, [[148:5|and they were created|et creata sunt]]. For he [[Rom 4:17|calleth those things that are not, as those that are|Vocat enim ea quæ non sunt, tanquam sint]]. Hence it is said in Genesis: [[Gen 1:3|And God said: Be light made|Dixit Deus, Fiat lux]], [[Gen 1:6|Let there be a firmament made|Fiat firmamentum]]; and so all things were created by his saying. For God is the cause of things through his intellect, according to that saying, [[Ps 103:24|thou hast made all things in wisdom|Omnia in sapientia fecisti]]; and through his will, as it is said, [[Ps 134:6|Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done|Omnia quæcumque voluit Dominus, fecit]].

paras.t: Statuit, id est, firmiter collocavit, ea jam prædicta, videlicet angelos, virtutes, solem, lunam, stellas, lumen, cœlos cœlorum, et aquas quæ super cœlos sunt, in sæculum sæculi, id est perpetuo. Dedit enim eis incorruptibile esse, quamvis cœli et luminaria, quantum ad formam accidentalem, mutanda atque in melius commutanda credantur. Præceptum posuit, id est, certam legem operandi eis præfixit, et non præteribit, id est, præceptum istud non desinet. Unde Hieronymus ait: Præceptum posuit soli ut luceret per diem: et ecce per tantos annos nunquam præceptum ejus præterivit. Lunæ præceptum posuit ut per triginta dies crescat et decrescat: nunquam cursus ejus mutatur. Mari præceptum posuit ut littora sua non egrediatur: venit Oceanus tumens fluctibus, et ipse redit, et præceptum observat. Grandis hominis honor, et grandis miseria; sol tibi currit, et elementa tibi serviunt: et tu ignoras Creatorem tuum! Totus mundus Deo servit, et præcepti ejus meminit: solus homo illud contemnit aut negligit! O infelix hominum genus! descendit ad te Deus, quoniam tu ad cœlum non vis ascendere: non tibi sufficit quod ipsum non suscipis, sed crucifigis, blasphemas, flagellas, nec tamen pœnitentiam agis!
paras.en: [[148:6|He hath established them|Statuit]], that is, he has firmly set them, the things already named, namely the angels, virtues, sun, moon, stars, light, heavens of heavens, and the waters that are above the heavens, [[148:6|for ages of ages|in sæculum sæculi]], that is, perpetually. For he gave them incorruptible being, although the heavens and the luminaries are believed to be due to change, and to be changed for the better, as regards their accidental form. [[148:6|he hath made a decree|Præceptum posuit]], that is, he has appointed for them a fixed law of working, [[148:6|and it shall not pass away|et non præteribit]], that is, that decree shall not cease. Hence Jerome says: He set a decree for the sun, that it should shine by day: and behold, through so many years it has never passed beyond his decree. He set a decree for the moon, that over thirty days it should wax and wane: its course is never changed. He set a decree for the sea, that it should not go beyond its shores: the Ocean comes swelling with its waves, and it goes back again, and keeps the decree. Great is the honour of man, and great his misery: the sun runs for thee, and the elements serve thee, and thou knowest not thy Creator! The whole world serves God and is mindful of his decree: man alone despises or neglects it! O unhappy race of men! God came down to thee, since thou wilt not ascend to heaven: it is not enough for thee that thou dost not receive him, but thou crucifiest, blasphemest, scourgest him, and yet thou dost not do penance!

paras.t: Laudate Dominum universorum de terra, id est, o terrena et inferiora, videlicet dracones, id est serpentes squamosi et magni: qui habitant in cavernis seu speluncis aquosis, in temperamentum sui naturalis caloris, qui non repunt in terra, sed volant in aere, et cetera animantia terræ in quantitate excedunt. Aliqui per dracones intelligunt cete grandia, quoniam in Genesi, ubi nos habemus, Creavit Deus cete grandia, in Hebræo dicitur, Dracones magnos. Et omnes abyssi, id est particularia profundaque maria, seu profunda loca Oceani, in quibus habitant cete; Ignis, id est elementum supremum, grando, nix, glacies, spiritus procellarum, id est venti tempestuosi, concitantes procellas in mari, quæ faciunt verbum ejus, id est, divino præcepto obediunt, idque operantur ad quod divinitus ordinantur; Montes et omnes colles, id est magni et parvi montes, ligna fructifera habentia sementem generis sui in se ipsis, et omnes cedri, quæ sunt arbores altæ; Bestiæ silvestres atque indomitæ, et universa pecora domestica, serpentes, id est animalia repentia, et volucres pennatæ. Omnia hæc laudent Deum, unumquodque secundum modum suum. Sed quid est quod inanimata et irrationalia et bruta alloquimur? Et respondendum, quod ea alloquimur, non ut ipsa intelligant verba nostra, sed ut nos ipsi ea nominando et considerando, inducamur ad Creatoris admirationem ac laudem. Nam, sicut in libro Sapientiæ dicitur, A magnitudine speciei creaturæ poterit Creator horum cognoscibiliter videri. Invisibilia quoque Dei, per ea quæ facta sunt, cognoscuntur, testante Apostolo.
paras.en: [[148:7|Praise the Lord|Laudate Dominum]] of all things [[148:7|from the earth|de terra]], that is, O earthly and lower things, namely [[148:7|ye dragons|dracones]], that is, great scaly serpents, which live in caverns or watery caves to temper their natural heat, which do not creep on the earth but fly in the air, and exceed the other animals of the earth in size. Some understand by dragons the great whales, since in Genesis, where we have, [[Gen 1:21|And God created the great whales|Creavit Deus cete grandia]], in the Hebrew it says, Great dragons. [[148:7|and all ye deeps|Et omnes abyssi]], that is, the particular and deep seas, or the deep places of the Ocean in which the whales live; [[148:8|Fire|Ignis]], that is, the highest element, [[148:8|hail, snow, ice, stormy winds|grando, nix, glacies, spiritus procellarum]], that is, tempestuous winds stirring up storms on the sea, [[148:8|which fulfil his word|quæ faciunt verbum ejus]], that is, they obey the divine command, and do that to which they are divinely ordained; [[148:9|Mountains and all hills|Montes et omnes colles]], that is, great and small mountains, [[148:9|fruitful trees|ligna fructifera]] having seed of their own kind in themselves, [[148:9|and all cedars|et omnes cedri]], which are tall trees; [[148:10|Beasts|Bestiæ]] wild and untamed, [[148:10|and all cattle|et universa pecora]] that are domestic, [[148:10|serpents|serpentes]], that is, creeping animals, [[148:10|and feathered fowls|et volucres pennatæ]]. Let all these praise God, each after its own manner. But why is it that we address inanimate, irrational and brute things? The answer is that we address them, not that they may understand our words, but that we ourselves, by naming and considering them, may be led to the admiration and praise of the Creator. For, as is said in the book of Wisdom, [[Wis 13:5|by the greatness of the beauty, and of the creature, the creator of them may be seen, so as to be known thereby|A magnitudine speciei creaturæ poterit Creator horum cognoscibiliter videri]]. And the [[Rom 1:20|invisible things of him|Invisibilia quoque Dei]], [[Rom 1:20|being understood by the things that are made|per ea quæ facta sunt, cognoscuntur]], as the Apostle testifies.

paras.t: Deinceps invitatur et excitatur ad laudem Dei ipse homo, propter quem facta sunt omnia ista terrena. Reges terræ, id est regnorum et insularum, et omnes populi eis subjecti, principes, regibus inferiores, et omnes judices terræ, id est habitantes in terra, seu hominum in terra manentium, Juvenes et virgines, senes cum junioribus: id est omnis conditio, omnis sexus, ætas et status humanæ creaturæ, laudent nomen Domini, id est Dominum nomine designatum; quia exaltatum, id est cunctis prælatum, est nomen ejus solius: id est, ipse solus universis sublimior est, imo omnia in infinitum excedit in omni nobilitate et perfectione. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico inducitur: Unus est Altissimus creator omnium, omnipotens Rex et metuendus nimis. Et Moyses ait: Non est alius deus in cœlo vel in terra, qui possit facere opera tua, et comparari fortitudini tuæ.
paras.en: Next man himself is invited and roused to the praise of God, for whose sake all these earthly things were made. [[148:11|Kings of the earth|Reges terræ]], that is, of kingdoms and islands, [[148:11|and all people|et omnes populi]] subject to them, [[148:11|princes|principes]], who are lower than kings, [[148:11|and all judges of the earth|et omnes judices terræ]], that is, dwelling on the earth, or of the men who abide on the earth; [[148:12|Young men and maidens|Juvenes et virgines]]: [[148:12|let the old with the younger|senes cum junioribus]], that is, every condition, every sex, age and state of human creatures, [[148:12|praise the name of the Lord|laudent nomen Domini]], that is, the Lord signified by the name; [[148:13|For his name alone is exalted|quia exaltatum]]: *exalted*, that is, set before all things; [[148:13|his name alone|est nomen ejus solius]]: that is, he alone is higher than all things, nay, exceeds all things infinitely in all nobility and perfection. For which reason it is set down in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 1:8|There is one most high Creator Almighty, and a powerful king, and greatly to be feared|Unus est Altissimus creator omnium, omnipotens Rex et metuendus nimis]]. And Moses says: [[Deut 3:24|there is no other God either in heaven or earth, that is able to do thy works, or to be compared to thy strength|Non est alius deus in cœlo vel in terra, qui possit facere opera tua, et comparari fortitudini tuæ]].

paras.t: Confessio ejus, id est laus Dei, est super cœlum et terram, id est in Ecclesia triumphanti ac militanti, in patria atque in via. Unde alibi legitur: Operuit cœlos gloria ejus, et laudis ejus plena est terra. Et exaltabit in præsenti vita per gratiam, et in futura per gloriam, cornu populi sui, id est virtutem et dignitatem fidelium atque humilium. Humiles enim exaltat quotidie, dando eis spiritualem profectum. In die autem judicii collocabit eos ad dexteram suam; deinde ponet eos cum corpore et anima in regno majestatis paternæ, quatenus ubi ipse fuerit, et illi sint secum. De qua exaltatione electorum impii mirabuntur in die judicii, dicentes: Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam, et finem illorum sine honore: ecce quomodo computati sunt inter filios Dei, et inter Sanctos sors illorum est.
paras.en: [[148:14|The praise of him|Confessio ejus]], that is, the praise of God, is [[148:14|above heaven and earth|super cœlum et terram]], that is, in the Church triumphant and militant, in the fatherland and on the way. Hence it is read elsewhere: [[Hab 3:3|His glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise|Operuit cœlos gloria ejus, et laudis ejus plena est terra]]. [[148:14|and he hath exalted|Et exaltabit]] [Denis reads *exaltabit*, "he shall exalt"; the Vulgate has *exaltavit*], in the present life by grace and in the life to come by glory, [[148:14|the horn of his people|cornu populi sui]], that is, the strength and dignity of the faithful and the humble. For he exalts the humble daily[[Luke 18:14||]], giving them spiritual progress. And on the day of judgment he will set them at his right hand[[Matt 25:33||]]; then he will place them, body and soul, in the kingdom of the Father's majesty, so that where he is, they too may be with him[[John 17:24||]]. At which exaltation of the elect the wicked will marvel on the day of judgment, saying: [[Wis 5:4|We fools esteemed their life madness, and their end without honour|Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam, et finem illorum sine honore]]: [[Wis 5:5|Behold, how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints|ecce quomodo computati sunt inter filios Dei, et inter Sanctos sors illorum est]].

paras.t: Hymnus, id est laus Dei cum cantico, est atque debetur omnibus sanctis ejus in cœlo et in terra. Nam et ipsi laude digni sunt, et Deum incessabiliter laudant. Qui autem sint sancti ejus, exemplificat: filiis Israel, populo appropinquanti sibi. Ad litteram Psalmista vocavit filios Israel seu Jacob patriarchæ, sanctos Dei, quoniam tempore illo pene totus mundus declinavit ad idololatriam præter eos. Unde Moyses sæpe ait ad eos: Populus sanctus es Domino Deo tuo. Et hi filii Israel erant populus appropinquans Deo, bene vivendo. Sicut enim a Deo receditur per peccatum, sic ei appropinquatur per virtutes. Fides namque ostendit viam et finem seu terminum; spes vero incipit tendere; caritas autem unit nos Deo; et ceteræ virtutes, in quantum per caritatem informantur, Deo nos copulant. — Spiritualiter vero, per filios Israel intelliguntur omnes fideles seu Christiani Deum per fidem contemplantes: et istis est aut debetur hymnus, quemadmodum dicit Apostolus: Loquimini vobismetipsis in psalmis et hymnis et canticis spiritualibus, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino.
paras.en: [[148:14|A hymn|Hymnus]], that is, the praise of God with song, is, and is owed, [[148:14|to all his saints|omnibus sanctis ejus]] in heaven and on earth. For they too are worthy of praise, and they praise God unceasingly. And who his saints are, he shows by example: [[148:14|to the children of Israel, a people approaching to him|filiis Israel, populo appropinquanti sibi]]. Literally, the Psalmist called the children of Israel, or of the patriarch Jacob, the saints of God, since at that time almost the whole world had turned aside to idolatry except them. Hence Moses often says to them: [[Deut 7:6|thou art a holy people to the Lord thy God|Populus sanctus es Domino Deo tuo]][[Deut 14:2||]]. And these children of Israel were a people approaching to God by living well. For as one goes away from God by sin, so one draws near to him by the virtues. For faith shows the way and the end or goal; hope begins to tend towards it; charity unites us to God; and the other virtues, in so far as they are informed by charity [that is, given their form and their merit by charity], join us to God. Spiritually, however, by the children of Israel are understood all the faithful, or Christians, who contemplate God by faith; and to these the hymn is, or is owed, as the Apostle says: [[Eph 5:19|Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual canticles, singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord|Loquimini vobismetipsis in psalmis et hymnis et canticis spiritualibus, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum cœlicæ amœnitatis decore fulcitum, et sancti amoris zelo refertum, audivimus: in quo devotissimus Dei cultor totam universitatis machinam, paucis creaturis nominatim expressis, ad summæ Trinitatis laudem hortatur: quatenus quod ipse per se implere non valet, ab illis impleatur. Dum ergo psalmum hunc canimus, mentem nostram ab omni distractione revocemus, zelo divini amoris accendamus, et omni custodia præservemus. Contemplemur insuper in universis creaturis, præsertim in cœlestibus, excellentiam Creatoris, in ejus contemplatione epulemur, in ejus præconio delectemur, ejus beatitudini affectuosissime congratulemur. Denique id personaliter impleamus, ad quod cetera omnia exhortamur, videlicet Deum laudantes et glorificantes, ad cujus laudem et gloriam omnia facta sunt. Vere etenim possibilius esset, cœlum et terram annihilari, quam hominem in laudibus Dei gloriantem non salvari.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm adorned with the beauty of heavenly delight and filled with the zeal of holy love, in which the most devout worshipper of God exhorts the whole fabric of the universe, a few creatures being expressly named, to the praise of the most high Trinity, so that what he cannot fulfil by himself may be fulfilled by them. While we sing this psalm, then, let us call our mind back from all distraction, kindle it with the zeal of divine love, and guard it with all watchfulness. Let us contemplate, moreover, in all creatures, especially in the heavenly ones, the excellence of the Creator; let us feast on the contemplation of him, delight in his praise, and rejoice most affectionately with him in his blessedness. Finally, let us ourselves fulfil in person that to which we exhort all other things, namely praising and glorifying God, for whose praise and glory all things were made. For truly it would be more possible for heaven and earth to be brought to nothing than for a man who glories in the praises of God not to be saved.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Laudabilis Domine et gloriose, fac nos, precamur, cum angelis tuis et omni creatura te digne laudare: ut devotas tibi laudes jugiter proclamantibus cœtibus angelicis in gloria æternitatis nos associes.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, worthy of praise and glorious, grant us, we pray, to praise thee worthily with thy angels and with every creature: that thou mayest join us, in the glory of eternity, to the angelic hosts, who unceasingly proclaim devout praises to thee.

149.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUADRAGESIMI NONI : CANTATE DOMINO CANTICUM NOVUM.
149.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and forty-ninth psalm: Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle.

paras.t: Porro titulus huic psalmo præscriptus est : Alleluia. Est namque hic psalmus laus Domini Salvatoris, atque totius supergloriosissimæ Trinitatis : præsertim pro beneficio perfectæ victoriæ atque finalis triumphi, quem per Christi virtutem adepturi sunt fideles in secundo ejus adventu, quando omnes adversarii electorum æternaliter damnabuntur, et ipsi electi ab omni malo pœnæ et culpæ liberabuntur, resumentes corpora glorificata.
paras.en: Further, the title prefixed to this psalm is: Alleluia [in the Vulgate this word opens the psalm; the Douay-Rheims text used here prints it at the end of the psalm before]. For this psalm is a praise of the Lord the Saviour, and of the whole most supremely glorious Trinity: above all for the benefit of the perfect victory and final triumph which the faithful are to obtain through the power of Christ at his second coming, when all the adversaries of the elect shall be damned eternally, and the elect themselves shall be freed from every evil of punishment and of guilt, taking up again their glorified bodies.

paras.t: Ait ergo sanctus Propheta : Cantate Domino canticum novum, id est, recens carmen et novam laudem Deo offerte, in qua nova ejus beneficia contineantur. Dicitur autem canticum novum, non propter temporis novitatem, sed propter materiæ atque devotionis spiritualem innovationem. Itaque monemur Deum laudare pro beneficiis ejus, nobis in fine sæculorum per Christum collatis, videlicet de Christi incarnatione, prædicatione, passione, Spiritus Sancti missione ; de ejus quoque futuris beneficiis, quibus reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ, configuratum corpori claritatis suæ, et vindicabit perfecte injuriam servorum suorum humilium. Laus ejus, scilicet Dei, est in ecclesia sanctorum, id est in congregationibus devotorum, in Ecclesia militante ac triumphanti, quemadmodum apud Isaiam recolitur : Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea, gratiarum actio, et vox laudis.
paras.en: The holy Prophet says, then: [[149:1|Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle|Cantate Domino canticum novum]], that is, offer to God a fresh song and a new praise, in which his new benefits are contained. And it is called a *new canticle* not because of newness in time, but because of the spiritual renewal of its matter and of devotion. And so we are admonished to praise God for his benefits bestowed on us through Christ at the end of the ages: namely, for Christ's incarnation, preaching and passion, and the sending of the Holy Ghost; and also for his benefits to come, by which he [[Phil 3:21|will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory|reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ, configuratum corpori claritatis suæ]], and will perfectly avenge the wrong done to his lowly servants[[Apoc 19:2||]]. [[149:1|his praise|Laus ejus]], that is, God's, is [[149:1|in the church of the saints|in ecclesia sanctorum]], that is, in the gatherings of the devout, in the Church militant and triumphant, as is recalled in Isaias: [[Is 51:3|Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of praise|Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea, gratiarum actio, et vox laudis]].

paras.t: Lætetur Israel, id est populus fidelis seu christianus, qui per fidem et vitam reputatur in semine Patriarcharum, multo amplius quam filii carnis, prout Apostolus memorat : Non qui in manifesto, Judæus; neque quæ in manifesto in carne est circumcisio : sed qui in abscondito, Judæus est; et circumcisio cordis in spiritu, non littera. Unde de filiis carnalibus carnaliter circumcisis, sed Christum negantibus, ait Joannes : Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt, sed mentiuntur. Unde rursus Paulus testatur : Qui ex fide sunt, hi filii sunt Abrahæ. Itaque iste verus Israel lætetur spirituali lætitia in eo qui fecit eum, id est in suo Creatore ac Salvatore, in ejus contemplatione, dilectione et cultu cordialiter gloriando, sicut Apostolus monet : Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur.
paras.en: [[149:2|Let Israel rejoice|Lætetur Israel]], that is, the faithful or Christian people, which through faith and life is reckoned among the seed of the Patriarchs far more than the children of the flesh, as the Apostle relates: [[Rom 2:28|it is not he is a Jew, who is so outwardly: nor is that circumcision which is outwardly in the flesh|Non qui in manifesto, Judæus; neque quæ in manifesto in carne est circumcisio]]. [[Rom 2:29|But he is a Jew that is one inwardly and the circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter|sed qui in abscondito, Judæus est; et circumcisio cordis in spiritu, non littera]]. Hence John says of the children of the flesh, circumcised in the flesh but denying Christ: [[Apoc 3:9|who say they are Jews and are not, but do lie|Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt, sed mentiuntur]]. Hence again Paul bears witness: [[Gal 3:7|they who are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham|Qui ex fide sunt, hi filii sunt Abrahæ]]. Let this true Israel, then, rejoice with a spiritual joy [[149:2|in him that made him|in eo qui fecit eum]], that is, in his Creator and Saviour, glorying from the heart in contemplating, loving and worshipping him, as the Apostle admonishes: [[1 Cor 1:31|He that glorieth may glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]].

paras.t: Et filiæ Sion, id est particulares Ecclesiæ cœlestia speculantes, vel animæ devotæ, quæ sunt filiæ Ecclesiæ per Sion designatæ, exsultent in rege suo, Sponso cœlesti. De quo in Canticis canticorum habetur : Egredimini, filiæ Sion, et videte regem Salomonem; et iterum, Introduxit me rex in cellam vinariam. Iste rex noster est Christus, de quo scriptum est : Dominus judex noster, Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster; ipse veniet et salvabit nos. In hoc rege animæ piæ modo gaudent spiritualiter.
paras.en: [[149:2|and let the children of Sion|Et filiæ Sion]] [Denis reads *filiæ*, "daughters", where the Vulgate has *filii*, "sons" or "children"], that is, the particular Churches that contemplate heavenly things, or devout souls, which are daughters of the Church signified by Sion, [[149:2|be joyful in their king|exsultent in rege suo]], the heavenly Bridegroom. Of him we have in the Canticle of Canticles: [[Cant 3:11|Go forth, ye daughters of Sion, and see king Solomon|Egredimini, filiæ Sion, et videte regem Salomonem]]; and again, [[Cant 2:4|He brought me|Introduxit me]] (the king) [[Cant 2:4|into the cellar of wine|in cellam vinariam]]. This our king is Christ, of whom it is written: [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king|Dominus judex noster, Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster]]; he will come and [[Is 33:22|save us|salvabit nos]]. In this king pious souls now rejoice spiritually.

paras.t: Laudent nomen ejus in choro corporali, videlicet societate per caritatem concordi; et item in choro spirituali, id est in concordia morum, in consonantia operum bonorum, in connexione virtutum. In tympano et psalterio psallant ei. Utitur enim interdum Ecclesia in laude divina his musicis instrumentis. — Spiritualiter vero per tympanum, carnis mortificatio significatur, quia in tympano corium extenditur. Per psalterium vero, in quo chordæ extenduntur, bona operatio figuratur. Itaque, Filiæ Sion in tympano, id est in carnis castigatione, in concupiscentiarum refrenatione, in propria mortificatione, et psalterio, id est vita laudabili, psallant, id est, laudem annuntient, ei, id est regi suo, Domino Salvatori : quatenus vita et mores consonent verbis, et talis sit vita, quæ reddat animam ad laudandum Deum idoneam.
paras.en: [[149:3|Let them praise his name in choir|Laudent nomen ejus in choro]], a bodily choir, namely a company made of one heart by charity; and likewise in a spiritual choir, that is, in harmony of conduct, in the concord of good works, in the linking together of the virtues. [[149:3|with the timbrel and the psaltery|In tympano et psalterio]] [[149:3|let them sing to him|psallant ei]]. For the Church sometimes uses these musical instruments in the divine praise. — Spiritually, however, the timbrel signifies the mortification of the flesh, because in the timbrel a skin is stretched; and the psaltery, in which strings are stretched, figures good works. And so let the daughters of Sion, *with the timbrel*, that is, in chastising the flesh, in reining in the concupiscences, in mortifying themselves, *and the psaltery*, that is, with a praiseworthy life, *sing*, that is, proclaim praise, *to him*, that is, to their king, the Lord the Saviour: so that life and conduct may accord with words, and the life be such as to make the soul fit to praise God.

paras.t: Quia beneplacitum est Domino Christo in populo suo christiano, æternaliter præelecto, quemadmodum fatetur : Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum; et iterum, Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos. Et exaltabit in die judicii mansuetos, id est veraciter Christianos, qui didicerunt ab eo illam lectionem quam omnibus nobis proponit : Discite, inquiens, a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde. Hos ergo mansuetos exaltabit in salutem mentis et corporis, dando eis duplicem stolam, beatitudinem plenam, vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[149:4|For the Lord is well pleased|Quia beneplacitum est Domino]], Christ, [[149:4|with his people|in populo suo]], the Christian people, chosen beforehand from eternity, as he declares: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum]]; and again, [[John 15:9|As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you|Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos]]. [[149:4|and he will exalt|Et exaltabit]] on the day of judgment [[149:4|the meek|mansuetos]], that is, those who are truly Christians, who have learned from him the lesson he sets before us all: [[Matt 11:29|learn|Discite]], he says, [[Matt 11:29|of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]. These meek ones, then, he will exalt [[149:4|unto salvation|in salutem]] of mind and body, giving them the double stole [that is, the glory of soul and of body], full beatitude, life everlasting.

paras.t: Propterea subditur : Exsultabunt Sancti in gloria beatificæ visionis in patria, prout Dominus ait : Exsultabitis et gaudebitis usque in æternum; lætabuntur in cubilibus suis, id est in cœlestibus mansionibus, in quibus dulciter requiescunt, atque in Deo feliciter somno sincerissimæ contemplationis obdormiunt. De his cubilibus ait Salvator : Vado parare vobis locum ; et rursus, In domo Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[149:5|The saints shall rejoice in glory|Exsultabunt Sancti in gloria]], the glory of the beatific vision in the fatherland, as the Lord says: [[Is 65:18|shall be glad and rejoice for ever|Exsultabitis et gaudebitis usque in æternum]] [Denis's wording differs a little from the Vulgate's *gaudebitis et exsultabitis usque in sempiternum*]; [[149:5|they shall be joyful in their beds|lætabuntur in cubilibus suis]], that is, in the heavenly mansions, in which they rest sweetly and fall happily asleep in God in the slumber of the purest contemplation. Of these beds the Saviour says: [[John 14:2|I go to prepare a place for you|Vado parare vobis locum]]; and again, [[John 14:2|In my Father's house there are many mansions|In domo Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt]].

paras.t: Exsultationes Dei, id est exsultationes spirituales atque divinæ, laudes perpetuæ, erunt in gutture eorum. Si hoc de gutture corporali intelligatur, sequi videtur quod in patria erit laus vocalis : quod ego probabilius reor quam aliud. Potest tamen exponi de gutture spirituali : de quo Sponsa ait in Canticis, Fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo; et Salomon, Veritatem meditabitur guttur meum. Hoc est guttur per quod verbum cordis profertur, quo spiritualis dulcedo gustatur. Itaque, Exsultationes Dei, id est divinæ, et ad Deum ordinatæ, erunt in gutture Beatorum, ita quod in eorum gutture spirituali erunt exsultationes seu delectationes internæ et spirituales; in gutture autem eorum corporali erunt exsultationes seu laudes exteriores atque sensibiles. Qualiter vero voces et soni laudum vocalium in cœlo empyreo formabuntur, difficultatem habet, quæ hoc loco discutienda non est.
paras.en: [[149:6|The high praises of God|Exsultationes Dei]] [Denis reads *exsultationes*, "rejoicings", where the Vulgate has *exaltationes*, "high praises"], that is, spiritual and divine rejoicings, perpetual praises, shall be [[149:6|in their mouth|in gutture eorum]] [*guttur*, "throat", which the Douay-Rheims renders "mouth"]. If this is understood of the bodily throat, it seems to follow that in the fatherland there will be vocal praise: and this I think more probable than the other view. Yet it can also be expounded of the spiritual throat, of which the Bride says in the Canticle, [[Cant 2:3|his fruit was sweet to my palate|Fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo]]; and Solomon, [[Prov 8:7|My mouth shall meditate truth|Veritatem meditabitur guttur meum]] [here too the Latin has *guttur*, "throat"]. This is the throat through which the word of the heart is uttered, by which spiritual sweetness is tasted. And so *the rejoicings of God*, that is, divine ones and ordered to God, shall be in the throat of the Blessed, in such wise that in their spiritual throat there shall be inward and spiritual rejoicings or delights, while in their bodily throat there shall be outward and sensible rejoicings or praises. But how the voices and sounds of vocal praise will be formed in the empyrean heaven [that is, the highest heaven, the dwelling of the Blessed] is a difficult matter, which is not to be discussed in this place.

paras.t: Et gladii ancipites in manibus eorum. In Apocalypsi de Christo inducitur : De ore ejus gladius ex utraque parte acutus exibat. Et palam quod ibi per gladium intelligatur districta sententia judicis contra injustos. Similiter nunc ait Scriptura de Sanctis cum Christo judicaturis (quibus ipse loquitur : Quum sederit Filius hominis in sede majestatis suæ, sedebitis et vos super sedes duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel) : Gladii ancipites, id est sententia judicis contra iniquos, in manibus, id est in potestate eorum. Simul enim cum Christo judicabunt.
paras.en: [[149:6|and two-edged swords in their hands|Et gladii ancipites in manibus eorum]]. In the Apocalypse it is said of Christ: [[Apoc 1:16|from his mouth came out a sharp two-edged sword|De ore ejus gladius ex utraque parte acutus exibat]]. And it is plain that there the sword is understood as the strict sentence of the judge against the unjust. So now Scripture says likewise of the Saints who are to judge with Christ (to whom he himself says: [[Matt 19:28|when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel|Quum sederit Filius hominis in sede majestatis suæ, sedebitis et vos super sedes duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel]]): [[149:6|two-edged swords|Gladii ancipites]], that is, the judge's sentence against the wicked, [[149:6|in their hands|in manibus]], that is, in their power. For they will judge together with Christ[[1 Cor 6:2||]].

paras.t: Ad faciendam vindictam in nationibus, id est, ut simul cum Christo ulciscantur in nationibus perversorum peccata atque injurias Deo et sibi illatas ; et ad faciendas increpationes, id est justas reprobationes et pœnas, in populis reprobis. Dicuntur autem Sancti ista facturi, quoniam Christo ista agenti consentient et adstabunt.
paras.en: [[149:7|To execute vengeance upon the nations|Ad faciendam vindictam in nationibus]], that is, that together with Christ they may avenge among the nations the sins of the perverse and the wrongs done to God and to themselves; and to execute [[149:7|chastisements|increpationes]], that is, just condemnations and punishments, [[149:7|among the people|in populis]] that are reprobate. And the Saints are said to be going to do these things because they will consent to Christ as he does them, and will stand by him.

paras.t: Ad alligandos reges injustos eorum, scilicet impiorum, in compedibus, id est in vinculis æternæ damnationis, a quibus nunquam erui poterunt, et nobiles eorum superbos in manicis, id est ligaminibus, ferreis. Per hoc enim quod Sancti impios cum Christo damnabunt, reges nobilesque eorum, puta tyrannos injustosque præsides, ligabunt in compedibus et manicis ferreis, secundum quod Christus locutus est : Ligatis manibus et pedibus, projicite eum in tenebras exteriores.
paras.en: [[149:8|To bind their kings|Ad alligandos reges]], their unjust kings (*their*, that is, the wicked's), [[149:8|with fetters|in compedibus]], that is, in the chains of eternal damnation, from which they will never be able to be delivered, [[149:8|and their nobles|et nobiles eorum]], their proud nobles, [[149:8|with manacles|in manicis]], that is, bonds, [[149:8|of iron|ferreis]]. For by the fact that the Saints will condemn the wicked together with Christ, they will bind their kings and nobles, that is to say, tyrants and unjust governors, with fetters and manacles of iron, according to what Christ said: [[Matt 22:13|Bind his hands and feet, and cast him into the exterior darkness|Ligatis manibus et pedibus, projicite eum in tenebras exteriores]] [the margin gives Matth. xxv, 13; the words are those of Matt 22:13, compare Matt 25:30].

paras.t: Ut faciant in eis judicium conscriptum, id est, ut sic judicent impios, sicut in divina præscientia scriptum, atque in sacris Scripturis digestum est. Unde Dominus alio loco justis promittit : Egrediemini et salietis quasi vituli de armento, et calcabitis impios in die qua ego facio, dicit Dominus.
paras.en: [[149:9|To execute upon them the judgment that is written|Ut faciant in eis judicium conscriptum]], that is, that they may judge the wicked as it is written in the divine foreknowledge and set down in the sacred Scriptures. Hence the Lord promises the just in another place: [[Mal 4:2|you shall go forth, and shall leap like calves of the herd|Egrediemini et salietis quasi vituli de armento]], [[Mal 4:3|And you shall tread down the wicked|et calcabitis impios]] [[Mal 4:3|in the day that I do this, saith the Lord|in die qua ego facio, dicit Dominus]].

paras.t: Gloria hæc est omnibus Sanctis ejus, id est, universis electis cedet ad gloriam præinducta ultio Beatorum, quemadmodum scriptum est : Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam. Vel, Gloria hæc est omnibus Sanctis ejus, id est, omnes electi tunc vindicabunt in nationibus, sicut jam patuit. Omnes enim cum Christo per approbationem judicabunt, et fortiter, imperterrite et constantissime contra reprobos stabunt, et maxime martyres contra tyrannos, juxta illud : Tunc stabunt justi in magna constantia adversus eos qui se angustiaverunt, et qui abstulerunt labores eorum. Videntes (impii) turbabuntur timore horribili, etc., gementes præ angustia spiritus, dicentes : Hi sunt quos aliquando habuimus in derisum, et in similitudinem improperii. In libro quoque Sapientiæ iterum legitur : Judicabunt justi nationes, et dominabuntur populis. Hæc sunt incomprehensibilia Dei justi judicia : ut taliter exaltentur in die judicii, qui nunc propter justitiam patiuntur, veraciter humiliantur, et Deo humiliter obsequuntur. Sic quoque tunc humiliabuntur, qui modo justos affligunt, contra justitiam tument, et temporaliter prævalent.
paras.en: [[149:9|this glory is to all his saints|Gloria hæc est omnibus Sanctis ejus]], that is, the vengeance of the Blessed described above will turn to the glory of all the elect, as it is written: [[Ps 57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam]] [the margin gives Ps. lxvii, 11; the words are those of Ps 57:11]. Or, [[149:9|this glory is to all his saints|Gloria hæc est omnibus Sanctis ejus]], that is, all the elect will then take vengeance among the nations, as has already been shown. For all will judge together with Christ by approving his sentence, and will stand bravely, fearlessly and most steadfastly against the reprobate, and above all the martyrs against the tyrants, according to that saying: [[Wis 5:1|Then shall the just stand with great constancy against those that have afflicted them, and taken away their labours|Tunc stabunt justi in magna constantia adversus eos qui se angustiaverunt, et qui abstulerunt labores eorum]]. [[Wis 5:2|These seeing it|Videntes]] (the wicked) [[Wis 5:2|shall be troubled with terrible fear|turbabuntur timore horribili]], etc., [[Wis 5:3|groaning for anguish of spirit|gementes præ angustia spiritus]], saying: [[Wis 5:3|These are they, whom we had sometime in derision, and for a parable of reproach|Hi sunt quos aliquando habuimus in derisum, et in similitudinem improperii]]. And again in the book of Wisdom we read: The just [[Wis 3:8|shall judge nations, and rule over people|Judicabunt justi nationes, et dominabuntur populis]]. These are the incomprehensible just judgments of God: that those who now suffer for justice' sake, are truly humbled, and humbly obey God, should be so exalted on the day of judgment. So too those shall then be humbled who now afflict the just, swell with pride against justice, and prevail for a time.

paras.t: Denique movere non debet, quod primo dicit Sanctos exsultaturos in gloria, et lætaturos in cubilibus suis ; et postea subdit, Gladii ancipites in manibus eorum, ad faciendam vindictam in nationibus, etc., quod tamen præcedet. Sacra namque Scriptura non semper enumerat dona Dei eo ordine quo præstantur. Sed et Christus talem ordinem ponit in verbis, sicut nunc psalmus præsens. Ait namque discipulis : Ego dispono vobis regnum, ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo, et sedeatis super thronos, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel.
paras.en: Lastly, it should not trouble anyone that the psalm first says that the Saints [[149:5|shall rejoice in glory|exsultaturos in gloria]] and [[149:5|shall be joyful in their beds|lætaturos in cubilibus suis]], and afterwards adds, [[149:6|two-edged swords in their hands|Gladii ancipites in manibus eorum]], [[149:7|To execute vengeance upon the nations|ad faciendam vindictam in nationibus]], etc., which nevertheless will come first. For sacred Scripture does not always list the gifts of God in the order in which they are bestowed. Indeed Christ too puts his words in such an order, just as the present psalm does now. For he says to the disciples: [[Luke 22:29|I dispose to you|Ego dispono vobis]] [[Luke 22:29|a kingdom|regnum]]; [[Luke 22:30|That you may eat and drink at my table, in my kingdom: and may sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel|ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo, et sedeatis super thronos, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel]].

paras.t: Ecce hic psalmus ad laudem divinam et spiritualem lætitiam hilariter nos invitat, beatitudinem electorum jucunde describit, reproborumque pœnas salubriter pandit : quatenus ad Sanctorum societatem pertingere satagamus, impiorumque opera atque tormenta abhorrere et fugere laboremus.
paras.en: See how this psalm gladly invites us to the divine praise and to spiritual joy, delightfully describes the beatitude of the elect, and for our good lays open the punishments of the reprobate: so that we may strive to attain to the company of the Saints, and labour to abhor and flee the works and the torments of the wicked.

paras.t: Precatio. Qui nos fecisti, Domine, præsta nobis te diligendo lætari et exsultare in te ; et beneplacitum tibi sit in nobis, et exaltes nos in salutem æternæ beatitudinis.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, who hast made us, grant us, by loving thee, to be glad and to rejoice in thee; and may it be well pleasing to thee in us, and mayest thou exalt us unto the salvation of everlasting beatitude.

150.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI CENTESIMI QUINQUAGESIMI : LAUDATE DOMINUM IN SANCTIS EJUS.
150.title_en: Exposition of the hundred and fiftieth psalm: Praise ye the Lord in his holy places.

paras.t: Titulus hujus novissimi psalmi est : Alleluia. Præsens enim psalmus Ecclesiam triumphantem invitat ad laudandum suæ fontem beatitudinis, suæ salutis auctorem. Quia enim psalmus immediate præcedens, translationem Sanctorum ad patriam reseravit, merito nunc Psalmista hortatur eamdem Sanctorum societatem, ut Domino Deo pro tantis beneficiis laudes et gratias referat.
paras.en: The title of this last psalm is: Alleluia. For the present psalm invites the Church triumphant to praise the fount of her beatitude, the author of her salvation. For since the psalm immediately preceding disclosed the passage of the saints to the fatherland, the Psalmist now rightly exhorts that same company of the saints to render praise and thanks to the Lord God for such great benefits.

paras.t: Itaque dicit : Laudate, o vos cives cœlestes, Dominum, vestræ felicitatis objectum et causam, in Sanctis ejus, id est in universis comprehensoribus et Beatis, gratias ei agendo pro omnibus bonis quæ largitus est eis, et quidquid felicitatis et gloriæ in ipsis est, ei principaliter adscribendo. Vere enim mirabilis est Deus in Sanctis illis. Laudate eum in firmamento virtutis ejus, id est in stabilitate fortitudinis, quam dedit Beatis, confirmando eos in bono. Hanc ergo beneficentiam Deo adscribite, atque pro ea ipsum laudate. Vel, In firmamento virtutis ejus, id est in cœlo empyreo a divina virtute causato. Sicut enim Deus in hoc cœlo esse censetur, ita in eo laudandus perhibetur. De hoc enim firmamento scriptum est : Respice, Domine, de sanctuario tuo, de excelso cœlorum habitaculo.
paras.en: So he says: [[150:1|Praise ye|Laudate]], O ye citizens of heaven, [[150:1|the Lord|Dominum]], the object and cause of your happiness, [[150:1|in his holy places|in Sanctis ejus]] [the Latin *in sanctis ejus* can also mean "in his saints", and so Denis takes it], that is, in all the comprehensors [those who already see God in glory, as against wayfarers still on the road] and the blessed: giving him thanks for all the good things he has bestowed on them, and ascribing to him first of all whatever happiness and glory there is in them. For truly [[Ps 67:36|God is wonderful in his saints|mirabilis est Deus in Sanctis illis]]. [[150:1|Praise ye him in the firmament of his power|Laudate eum in firmamento virtutis ejus]], that is, in the steadfastness of strength which he has given to the blessed, confirming them in good. Ascribe this kindness, then, to God, and praise him for it. Or, [[150:1|in the firmament of his power|In firmamento virtutis ejus]], that is, in the empyrean heaven, caused by the divine power. For as God is held to be in this heaven, so he is said to be praised in it; for of this firmament it is written: [[Deut 26:15|Look from thy sanctuary, and thy high habitation of heaven|Respice, Domine, de sanctuario tuo, de excelso cœlorum habitaculo]] [Denis adds *Domine*, "O Lord"].

paras.t: Laudate eum in virtutibus ejus, id est in angelis sanctis, qui virtutes dicuntur, ut in præcedentibus dictum est ; vel, In virtutibus ejus, id est magnis atque potentibus ejus effectibus, scilicet quod tanta pro hominibus fecit et passus est, quod Sanctos suos tam mirabiliter exaltavit in judicio, in patria, in corpore et anima. Laudate eum secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus, id est secundum quod ipse Deus multipliciter magnus est in se ipso et suis operibus. Est enim magnus in sapientia, quia sapientiæ ejus non est numerus ; magnus in potentia, quia non est difficile ei omne verbum : magnus in misericordia, magnus in justitia, magnus, imo immensus in omni perfectione.
paras.en: [[150:2|Praise ye him for his mighty acts|Laudate eum in virtutibus ejus]], that is, in the holy angels, who are called Virtues [*virtutes*, "powers", the name of one of the choirs of angels; the Douay-Rheims has "mighty acts"], as was said above; or, [[150:2|for his mighty acts|In virtutibus ejus]], that is, for his great and mighty works: namely, that he did and suffered such great things for men, and that he has so wonderfully exalted his saints, at the judgement, in the fatherland, in body and soul. [[150:2|Praise ye him according to the multitude of his greatness|Laudate eum secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus]], that is, according as God himself is great in many ways, in himself and in his works. For he is great in wisdom, since [[Ps 146:5|of his wisdom there is no number|sapientiæ ejus non est numerus]]; great in power, since [[Jer 32:17|no word shall be hard to thee|non est difficile ei omne verbum]] [Denis puts it in the third person: "no word is hard to him"]; great in mercy, great in justice, great, nay immense, in every perfection.

paras.t: Sed quum Deus in infinitum major et dignior sit omni laude, quam sibi offerre potest omnis creatura, quomodo aliquis potest Deum laudare secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus? Et respondendum, quod hoc est Deum laudare secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus : laudare eum totis viribus, et tamen profiteri se nihil dignum agere, neque sufficere ad ejus præconia persolvenda, et nihilo minus reverenter atque humiliter facere ad gloriam Dei quidquid possibile fuerit.
paras.en: But since God is infinitely greater and worthier than all the praise[[Ecclus 43:33||]] that every creature can offer him, how can anyone praise God [[150:2|according to the multitude of his greatness|secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus]]? The answer must be that this is to praise God [[150:2|according to the multitude of his greatness|secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus]]: to praise him with all one's strength, and yet to confess that one does nothing worthy of him and is not equal to paying him his due praises, and none the less to do, reverently and humbly, whatever is possible for the glory of God.

paras.t: Laudate eum in sono tubæ, etc. Per hæc septem musica instrumenta quæ hic nominantur, designatur ineffabilis et multiformis seu multiplex Beatorum jucunditas in Dei laudatione consistens : suntque instrumenta hæc spiritualiter intelligenda. Itaque, Laudate eum in sono tubæ, id est laude magnifica et summo præconio, tanquam regem regum et omnis triumphi datorem. Laudate eum in psalterio, id est in gratiarum actione, de hoc quod præstitit vobis gratiam custodiendi mandata : quorum observatio per psalterium designatur, ut dictum est sæpe ; et citharæ, id est in gratiarum actione de hoc, quod contulit vobis carnis mortificationem in sæculo isto : quæ significatur per citharam.
paras.en: [[150:3|Praise him with the sound of trumpet|Laudate eum in sono tubæ]], etc. By these seven musical instruments which are named here is signified the ineffable, manifold or many-sided joy of the blessed, which consists in the praise of God; and these instruments are to be understood spiritually. So: [[150:3|Praise him with the sound of trumpet|Laudate eum in sono tubæ]], that is, with magnificent praise and the highest proclamation, as the King of kings and the giver of every triumph. [[150:3|Praise him with psaltery|Laudate eum in psalterio]], that is, with thanksgiving for this, that he granted you the grace of keeping the commandments, the observance of which is signified by the psaltery, as has often been said; [[150:3|and harp|et citharæ]], that is, with thanksgiving for this, that he bestowed on you the mortification of the flesh in this world, which is signified by the harp.

paras.t: Laudate eum in tympano, id est pro dono immortalitatis, vestræ carni olim mortali collato. De spirituali autem significatione tympani, dictum est in psalmo præcedenti. Et choro, id est, in choro seu ordine angelorum, cui adunati estis, Deum laudate qui vos fecit angelis pares. Laudate eum in chordis, id est in virtutum consonantiis, in longitudine quoque, latitudine et profunditate caritatis, et organo, id est in dulci modulamine omnium ad divinam laudem spectantium. Per organa enim, quorum usus manet in Christi militanti Ecclesia, generalitas laudis divinæ exprimitur.
paras.en: [[150:4|Praise him with timbrel|Laudate eum in tympano]], that is, for the gift of immortality bestowed on your flesh, once mortal. Of the spiritual meaning of the timbrel, something was said in the preceding psalm. [[150:4|and choir|Et choro]], that is, in the choir or order of the angels, to which you have been joined, praise God, who has made you equal to the angels. [[150:4|Praise him with strings|Laudate eum in chordis]], that is, with the harmonies of the virtues, and also with the length, breadth and depth of charity, [[150:4|and organs|et organo]], that is, with the sweet melody of all things that belong to the divine praise. For by organs, whose use continues in the Church militant of Christ, the universality of the divine praise is expressed.

paras.t: Laudate eum in cymbalis benesonantibus. Cymbala benesonantia sunt labia oris et cordis, Deum devote laudantia. In istis laudant Deum Beati. Unde quod de istis cymbalis animatis loquatur Propheta, sequentia verba ostendunt : laudate eum in cymbalis jubilationis, id est in cymbalis talibus, de quibus jubilatio, id est jucundissima atque inenarrabilis quædam Dei laudatio, oritur, scilicet in labiis cordis seu oris. Labia vero cordis aliud prorsus non sunt, nisi intellectus, quo verbum mentale profertur, vel habitus intellectualis et vis intellectiva. Cupit ergo Propheta, ut Sancti in patria Deum tota mente collaudent, et oris quoque præconiis eum, ut decet, attollant : quod utique incessabiliter agunt, sicut apud Isaiam Dominus protestatur : Ecce servi mei laudabunt præ exsultatione cordis. Neque enim idcirco invitantur et admonentur a nobis ad laudem divinam, quasi nostra exhortatione indigeant, sed ut nos eis congratulemur, et propria invitatione accendamur.
paras.en: [[150:5|Praise him on high sounding cymbals|Laudate eum in cymbalis benesonantibus]]. The well-sounding cymbals [*cymbala benesonantia*; the Douay-Rheims has "high sounding cymbals"] are the lips of the mouth and of the heart, praising God devoutly. With these the blessed praise God. And that the Prophet is speaking of these living cymbals the words that follow show: [[150:5|praise him on cymbals of joy|laudate eum in cymbalis jubilationis]] [*jubilatio*, "jubilation", where the Douay-Rheims has "joy"], that is, on such cymbals as give rise to jubilation, that is, a certain most joyful and unspeakable praise of God: namely, on the lips of the heart or of the mouth. Now the lips of the heart are nothing else at all than the intellect, by which the mental word is uttered, or the intellectual habit and the intellective power. The Prophet desires, then, that the saints in the fatherland should praise God together with their whole mind, and extol him with the praises of their mouth as well, as is fitting: which indeed they do unceasingly, as the Lord testifies in Isaias: [[Is 65:14|Behold my servants shall praise for joyfulness of heart|Ecce servi mei laudabunt præ exsultatione cordis]]. For they are not invited and exhorted by us to the divine praise as though they needed our exhortation, but so that we may rejoice with them, and be kindled by our own invitation.

paras.t: Denique quoniam nostra perfectio ab operatione morali inchoatur, et in laude divina finitur; idcirco sicut exordium libri præsentis admonet ad bene agendum, sic finis ejus hortatur ad Dei præconium, dum subditur : Omnis spiritus intellectualis, bene dispositus, utpote angelus et anima rationalis, laudet Dominum omnipotentem, æternum, immensum, in substantia unum et simplicem, in personis trinum : a quo tanquam a Patre luminum, descendit omne donum optimum, et omne datum perfectum.
paras.en: Lastly, since our perfection begins with moral action and ends in the divine praise, therefore, as the opening of this book admonishes us to do well, so its end exhorts us to the praise of God, when it adds: [[150:5|let every spirit|Omnis spiritus]] that is intellectual and well disposed, such as an angel and a rational soul, [[150:5|praise the Lord|laudet Dominum]], almighty, eternal, immense, one and simple in substance, three in persons: from whom, as from [[Jas 1:17|the Father of lights|Patre luminum]], comes down every [[Jas 1:17|best gift and every perfect gift|donum optimum, et omne datum perfectum]]. [In the Vulgate "Every spirit…" is verse 6; the Douay-Rheims joins it to verse 5.]

paras.t: Præcatio. Spiritualibus vitiis cunctis a nobis expulsis, infunde sensibus nostris, Domine, unctionem Spiritus Sancti : cujus nobis habitaculum factis, omnis spiritus noster laudet te Dominum cœli.
paras.en: Prayer. Drive out from us all spiritual vices, O Lord, and pour into our senses the unction of the Holy Ghost: that when we have been made his dwelling, every spirit of ours may praise thee, the Lord of heaven.

paras.t: Ecce ad laudem, honorem et gloriam superbenedictæ et superessentialis et supergloriosissimæ Trinitatis, unius simplicissimæ atque purissimæ Deitatis, utcumque finita est expositio libri Psalmorum, prout Dominus dare dignatus est, juxta formam a principio conceptam, videlicet simplici planoque stilo, imo et sensu perfacili, sed tamen frequenter multiplici, utpote litterali, allegorico, tropologico, et anagogico.
paras.en: Behold, to the praise, honour and glory of the superblessed and superessential and most superglorious Trinity [words formed with *super-*, after Dionysius the Areopagite, to say that God is above all blessing, being and glory], the one most simple and most pure Godhead, the exposition of the book of Psalms has been finished after a fashion, as the Lord has deigned to grant, according to the plan conceived from the beginning: that is, in a simple and plain style, and indeed with a very easy sense, yet often a manifold one, namely literal, allegorical, tropological and anagogical [the four senses of Scripture: the literal, the allegorical (of Christ and the Church), the tropological or moral, and the anagogical (of the life to come)].

paras.t: Saluberrima demum scientia est, intelligere librum Psalmorum, quoniam (contestante magno itemque divino Dionysio) quidquid in sacra Scriptura describitur, continetur et clauditur, hoc liber Psalmorum per modum laudis divinæ complectitur. Incessabiliter ergo et infatigabiliter in psalmorum cantibus occupemur; jugiter fluant ex corde per ora sacratissima verba psalmorum. In hoc exercitio habituetur anima nostra, donec perfecte habituata, sine labore delectabilissime psallat; et omnem occupationem, statum et curam ab hoc exercitio cœliformi atque angelico impedientem, fastidiat, vitet, et quantum licet seu expedit, deserat. Hoc est in terra angelicam vitam ducere, conversationem in cœlis habere, ad futuram beatitudinem disponi et appropinquare. Tanto equidem Deum in patria jucundius beatiusque laudabimus, quanto nunc Deum devotius, frequentius delectabiliusque laudamus, qui est super omnia Deus fortis et gloriosus : cui gloria, magnificentia, imperium et potestas, quoniam ipse est universorum superfelix creator, omnipotens gubernator, misericordissimus quoque salvator, Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: Finally, it is a most wholesome knowledge to understand the book of Psalms, since (as the great and likewise divine Dionysius testifies) [Dionysius the Areopagite, *On the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy*, ch. 3] whatever is described, contained and enclosed in sacred Scripture, the book of Psalms embraces by way of divine praise. Let us therefore be occupied unceasingly and untiringly in the singing of the psalms; let the most sacred words of the psalms flow continually from the heart through the mouth. Let our soul grow accustomed to this exercise, until, perfectly accustomed, it sings the psalms without labour and with the greatest delight; and let it loathe, shun, and, so far as is lawful or expedient, forsake every occupation, state and care that keeps it from this heavenly and angelic exercise. This is to lead the angelic life on earth, to have our conversation in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]] [*conversatio*, way of life], to be made ready for the beatitude to come and to draw near to it. For we shall praise God in the fatherland the more joyfully and blessedly, the more devoutly, frequently and delightfully we praise God now, who is above all things God strong and glorious: to whom be glory, magnificence, empire and power, since he is the superhappy creator of all things, the almighty governor, and also the most merciful saviour, God sublime and blessed. Amen.
